description: Acourtiae venturae R. L. Cabrera similis, sed tantum in pagina folii inferna pubescentia glandulosa, inflorescentia terminali et atque laterali, involucro anguste campanulato, altiore (usque 9-10 mm), floribus pluri- bus per capitulum (14) differt.
bibliographicCitation: Cabrera, L. 2001. Six new species of Acourtia (Asteraceae) and a historical account of Acourtia mexicana. Brittonia. 53: 416-429.

description: Erect, herbaceous plants, to 1.5 m tall. Stems striate, the younger curly-pubescent, the older glabrescent. Leaves broadly ovate to oblong-ovate, 2-15 X 2-11 cm, the apex rounded to obtuse, the base auriculate, the margin spinulose-denticulate, coriaceous, stiff, scabrid, curly-puberulent on the veins of both surfaces, glandular-punctate on the lower surfaces, those associated with the inflorescence minutely spinulose-denticulate. Inflorescence lateral or terminal; capitula glomerulate, forming a small corymbiform panicle at the end of the branches, sessile; involucres 3-4-seriate, narrowly campanulate, 9-10 mm long, the phyllaries obtuse and abruptly mucronulate, dorsally lustrous, but with scattered glandular hairs, the outermost ovate to lanceolate, 2-3 x ca. 2 mm, arachnoid and glandular-ciliate on the margins, glandular-ciliolate with long arachnoid hairs scattered toward the apex, oblong to oblong- oblanceolate, 4 X ca. 2 mm, the innermost oblong to oblanceolate, 5.5-8 X 1-2 mm, glandular-ciliolate and with few scattered long curly hairs on the margins. Florets ca. 14; corollas glandular-puberulent, 11-12 mm long, the tubes 6.5-7 mm long, the lips ca. 5 mm long; stamens ca. 8 mm long, the apical appendages ca. 2 mm long, the anther thecae ca. 3 mm long, the tails ca. 2.5 mm long, the filaments ca. 2.5 mm long; styles 10-13 mm long, including the ca. 1 mm long branches. Achenes fusiform, glandular-punctate throughout; pappus ca. 11 mm long, whitish, biseriate.
bibliographicCitation: Cabrera, L. 2001. Six new species of Acourtia (Asteraceae) and a historical account of Acourtia mexicana. Brittonia. 53: 416-429.

description: Plants perennial, 40-95 cm high, roots with one-several woody, tuberous thickenings; stems erect or subdecumbent, sparsely to densely hirsute or hispid; leaves narrowly lanceolate, elliptic-lanceolate, to ovate-lanceolate, rarely ovate, (2.5-)3-8 cm long, 1-3.5 cm wide, sparsely to densely hirsute, attenuate to cuneate at the base, obtuse to acute at the apex, subentire or toothed, varying to deeply serratedentate or lobed, the lobes acute; short petiolate, heads campanulate, (8-) 10-15 mm in diameter; peduncles 4-12 cm long, short-pubescent, interspersed with spreading, glandular-capitate trichomes, especially near the heads; receptacle conical, 2-4 mm across, 2-4 mm high; chaff persistent, scarious, glabrous, (5-)7-10 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, tapering to an awn-like (beaked) apex, the lower margins incised; involucre 4-5-seriate, outer bracts green, oblong-elliptic, 1.5-3 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, glabrous to puberulent, margins and rounded apex ciliate; inner bracts progressively longer, oblong-elliptic, nearly boat-shaped, the longest 9-12 mm long, glabrous to puberulent, the margins and rounded apex scarious, ciliate, partially purple; ray flowers absent; disc corollas greenish-yellow, 7-9 mm long, the tube (2-)3-3.5 mm long, densely pilose, the throat broadly tubular, 3-4(-4.5) mm long, pilose at the base, lobes acute, ca 1.5 mm long, involute at the apex, pubescent on the margins; style branches rather flattened, 1.5-2 mm long, pubescent with stiff, black hairs, the tips subulate and long-pubescent; achenes blackish, subobconical to turbinate, sometinmes pentagonal, (3-)3.5-4 mm long, densely short-pilose; pappus of 12-20 unequal, linear-lanceolate, fimbriate scales and slender bristles, 1-1.5(-2) mm long, the shorter bristles alternating with longer scales; anthers 3.5-4 mm long, sagittate at the base.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, William L. & Zamuco, Isidro T. 1965. Identify of 'Tinong' (Dipterocarpaceae). Brittonia. 17: 35-46.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Perennial, reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes; stems erect, puberulent to pubescent below and more densely so above, simple to the inflorescence, up to 35 dm high; leaves cauline, numerous, 6-30 cm long, 1.0-7.5 cm wide, basally attenuate, elliptic to linear-lanceolate or oblanceolate, serrate, acuminate, with uniseriate hairs above, L-shaped trichomes mainly along leaf veins, with bilobed trichomes on upper and lower leaf surfaces, and with awl-shaped glandular trichomes on the leaf blade below; inflorescence usually large, loose to irregular, center head opening first; heads 9-30 flowered; involucre cylindric to hemispheric, 2.3-7.0 mm high, 2.0-5.5 mm wide; inner bracts lanceolate to ovate, 2.2-5.6 mm long, 0.9-3.1 mm wide, with acute to obtuse and often mucronate tips; outer bracts deltoid, with acute outer bract tips; bracts green to purple, pubescent along the edges and outer surfaces; achenes pubescent on the ribs, ca. 3.5 mm long; pappus tan to brown, sometimes with a purple tinge, very light colored in white flowered forms, bristles ca. 6 mm long, scales irregular, 0.2-0.8 mm long; flowers from late June to October. Vernonia gigantea grows in low, wet places along streams, ditches, roadsides, and in pastures, sometimes spreading to drier, upland areas.
bibliographicCitation: Urbatsch, Lowell E. 1972. Systematic study of the Altissimae and Giganteae species groups of the genus Vernonia (Compositae). Brittonia. 24: 229-238.

description: Coarse, robust subshrubs 1.5-2 m tall. Leaves opposite; petioles 4.5 cm long; blades 8-1 6 x 3-8.5 cm, submembranous, ovate, obtuse to rounded then shortly or very shortly attenuate at the base, acuminate at the apex, margins serrulate, adaxial surface sparsely scabridulous, the abaxial sparsely to densely strigillose or subtomentose, both surfaces with larger trichomes on veins. Outer phyllaries 8-20x2.5-6 mm, oblong to narrowly oblong or elliptic, slightly indurate at the base; inner phyllaries 5-8 x 2-5 mm, oblong-obovate, indurate at the base and more scarious. Paleae 7-8 x ca. 1.2 mm when folded, with subulate tip. Ray florets fertile, tube 1-1.5 mm, lamina 10.3-25x5-6 mm, oblong to elliptic or oblanceolate. Disc florets 4.5-6 mm long, lobes sparsely setulose abaxially. Cypselae 2.5-4.5x1.2-1.5 mm, the peripheral ones usually trigonous, awnless and wingless, the inner thickened, subquadrangular to slightly flattened, wingless or with wings up to 1mm wide; pappus mostly 1- awned, with the one awn, with the one awn on the opposite side of pale up to 2 mm long or awnless, crown 0.2 -1 mm high, partially fused to the body (less than 1/3) with laciniate to fimbroilate margins.
bibliographicCitation: Moraes, M. D. & Semir, J. 2009. A revision of Brazilian Dimerostemma (Asteraceae, Heliantheae, Ecliptinae), with a new species and taxonomic adjustments. Brittonia. 61 (4): 341-365.

description: Involucre, peduncles, stem (at least the upper part), and commonly also the leaves finely and copiously stipitate-glandular, or the involuere merely atomiferous-glandular; peduncular hairs apparently always spreading. Approximately the range of the subspecies.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herba annua, erecta, 5-8 dm. alta, tenerrima, supra ramosa ramis gracillimis suberectis acriter alato-tetragonis faciebus sulculatis viridibusque sparsim adpresso vel patenti-hispidulis sub 1 mm crassis; caule brunneo, sub 4 mm crasso, obscuire tetragono, sulculato, obscure adpresso-setuloso. Folia opposita, petiolata petiolo tenui 8-15 mm longo et patenti-setuloso setulis interdum antrorsum spectantibus; lamina pro principalibus bi vel vix subtripinnati, 4-6 cm longa et ca 3 cm lata, foliolis plerumque 3, supra obscure irregulariterque papillatis sed non nigro-punctulatis, faciebus marginibusque albido-setulosis, lateralibus imperfecte petiolulatis petiolulo alato sub 4 mm longo, incise pinnulatis pinnulis acriter lobulatis apice acerrime mucronatis, facie superiore conspicue elevato-venulatis, unico lobulo varie lineari-oblongo usque ad anguste oblongo-lanceolato ea 2.5 nmm lato; terminali simili sed moderate majore, rhachi antrorsum alata. Infloreseentia corymbosa, pedunculis capillaribus saepius 3-6 em longis pluri- pedicellatis, pedicellis summe capilliformibus 0.5-4 cm longis patenti-hispidulis basi anoguste lineari-bracteatis apice monocephalicis. Capitulum radiatum, pansa ad anthesin tantum ea 8-10 mm latum et 5-6 mm altum; bracteis exterioribus 6-8, anguste linearibus, ea 2-4 mm longis, utrinque paulo dilatatis, apice acutis, extus glabratis, margine paucisetulosis; interioribus ovato-oblongis vel late lanceolatis, longitudillaliter medianeque atro-striatis, ea 3-4.5 mm longis. Flores ligulati 4 vel 5, albi, steriles, ligula supra oiato-oblonga infra attenuata, longi- tudinaliter ea 4-7 striata, apiee plerumque 2-denticulata, tantum ca 4 mm longa. Palae quam braetea exteriores angustiores et paulo longiores acutioresque. Flores tubulosi pauci (ca 10-15), viridi-flavidi, fertiles, corolla atro-striata, 4-5 mm longa. Achaenia obeompressa, supra ineurvata; corpore faciebus sub- glabrato nigroque, oblongo-lineari, 3-4.5 mm longo et ca 1 mm lato, apice calvo, marginibus anguste crassiusculeque ineurvato-alato alis pectinatim incisis et parce 0.2 mm latis, tergo subobseure unicostato et apicem versus saepe minutissime adpresso-setuloso.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1964. A new species of Coreocarpus [C. cronquistii] (Compositae: Coreopsidinae) from Guerrero, Mexico. Brittonia. 16: 433, 434.

description: Herba perennis subglabra caudice crasso ramoso, caulibus circa 3-7 cm. altis, foliis imis oblanceolatis usque ad 6 cm. longis 6 mm. latis, caulinis reductis linearibus vel lineari-oblongis, capitulis solitariis disco 8-10 mm. lato, involuero 4-5 mm. alto bracteis duris leviter imbricatis, ligulis circa 25-35 purpureis vel caeruleis 6-9 mm. longis 1.3-2.3 mm. latis, corollis disci circa 2.9-3.6 mm. longis, pappo duplici, achaeniis 2-nervis moderate hirsutis.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Perennial herb with a stout branched caudex and a taproot; herbage nearly glabrous throughout, the leaf-margins obscurely hirsute-ciliate with appressedascending hairs; stem about 3-7 cm. high; basal leaves numerous, oblanceolate, up to about 6 cm. long and 6 mm. wide, the blade tapering very gradually to the petiole; cauline leaves several, reduced, linear or linear-oblong; head solitary, the disk 8-10 mm. wide; involuere 4-5 mm. high; phyllaries slightly imbricate, firm, olive-green, the inner and sometimes the outer purplish toward the tip; ligules about 25-35, rose-purple to deep blue, about 6-9 mm. long, 1.3-2.3 mm. wide; diskcorollas about 2.9-3.6 mm. long, the poorly marked tube about 0.5-0.8 mm. long, the lobes about 0.6-0.8 mm., the lower part of the limb somewhat contracted; style-appendages ovate or ovate-lanceolate, obtuse to acute, 0.2-0.3 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 10-16 fragile sordid bristles evidently shorter than the disk-corollas, the outer setose; akenes 2-nerved, somewhat hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Rhizome slender, 1.0-2.0 mm. in diam., the internodes 1-several cm. long, densely clothed with fine roots, branched, each axis producing a single stem, the hair tufts in axils of old leaves scant or mostly absent; innovations infre- quently produced; sterns moderately slender, 2.0-3.0 mm. in diam., 3.0(1.0) - 5.0 (6.0) dm. high, striate, scabrid-villous and glandular-puberulent below, increasingly so upwards; cauline leaves 4(5) pairs, 1.0(0.3)-2.0(3.0) cm. broad, 8.0(5.0)-12(15) cm. long, the lower two (or three) pairs sub-basal, narrowly or broadly oblanceolate, obtuse, with narrowly winged petioles which equal or are somewhat shorter than the blades, connate-sheathing at the base, strongly 3-5-parallel-nerved, margins entire or remotely dentieu- late or crenulate, both surfaces conspicuously short-stipitate-glandular and scabrid-villous, the upper two pairs of leaves usually remote, reduced, sessile, lanceolate, similar in pubescence, peduncles 5.0-15 cm. long, usually shorter when more than one is present, slender, densely glandular and scabrid- villous; heads broadly hemispheric, 1.5 (1.2)-2.0 (2.2) cm. high; perieliniuni densely short, or sometimes long-stipitate-glandular and densely scabrid- subpilose; involueral bracts 14-18(20), biseriate, 9.0-14 mm. long, narrowly lanceolate, the apex acute or acutish, similarly but less pubescent than the perielinium, sparingly so at the apex; ray flowers 11-18(23), ligules 4.0-8.0 mm. broad, elliptic-oblong, the teeth short, rounded or acutish, 0.5-1.5 mm. long; disc corolla 8.0 (6.0)-9.0 (11) mm. long, goblet-shaped, the tube 3.5(3.3)-4.0(5.4) mm. long, uniformly stipitate-glandular, with few or mostly no septate hairs, the limb similarly pubescent at base, the corolla lobes acutish, ca. 0.8 mm. long, sparingly hispidulous; achenes 4.0(3.5)- 5.0(5.5) mm. long, striate, uniformly appressed-hispid with double hairs, only occasionally sparingly short-stipitate-glandular, plump, slightly tapered at both ends, bronze-black; alnulus well developed, ca. 0.5 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Camp, Wendell H. & Gilly, Charles L. 1943. Part II: Systematic Treatment, [Arnica alpina-Arnica discoidea]. Brittonia. 4 (3): 405-457.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herba 30 cm alta tota flavido-albo-lanata rhizomate inclinato apice fasciculato-folioso. Folia basilaria crassiuscula subspathulato-oblonga vel oblonga apice obtusissimo basim versus in petiolum attenuata margine iutegerrimo, 10-12 cm longa, limnbo 6-8 cm longo 1.5-2 cm lato, petiolo 4-6 cm longo 0.6 cm lato, utrinque erassiuscule crispulo-lauata pallescenti-albida tantum costa subtus emineuiti reliqua nervis inconspicuis; basi in vaginam seariosam subglabram nervato-striolatam 4.5-5 cm longam ad 1.8 cm latam ampliata. Caulis florifer singulus erectus robustus crasse albido-lanatus 5-7 foliatus circa 25 cm longus, foliis cum basilaribus similibus sed breviter petiolatis vel sessilibus basi amplectente apice magis rotundatis, 5-10 cm longis 1-1.8 cm latis. Capitula homnogama discoidea semiglobosa 4-5-racemosa cernua ad extremum scapi. Pedicelli 1.5-2 cmn longi crassi recurvati crasse lanati, apicem versus et basi capituli bracteolis pluribus subulatis circa 12 mm longis 0.6 mm latis longe lalnatis calycultim, involuerum vix attingentem, formantibus. Inlvolucrum cupularebracteis viridi-purpuraceis circa 30 subbiseriatis anguste laneeolatis acutis 12-14 mm longis 1-1.5 mm latis subolabris tantum apice ciliato-penicillatis. Flores omnes hermaphroditi ultra 200 in capitulo, corolla flava glabra 9 mm lonoa tubulo 4 mm longo basi dilatato, limbo tubuloso apice 5 dentibus anguste triangularibus crassiusculis 1 mm longis; antherae 2 mm longae basi obtusae. Stylus rainis crassis apice truneato papilloso-penicillato. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus albus 8 mm longus pilis biseriatis strigulosis. Achaenia oblonga striata glabra 3 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1960. Studies on Andean Compositae--IV. Brittonia. 12: 182-195.

description: Stem stout, 2-3 m tall, simnple, with scattered short hairs, becoming scabrous toward the top, mottled light-green, light-red, or purple; leaves lanceolate-ovate, acuminate at the apex, alternate, usually rounded to the base, 11.5-16.5 cm long, 2-4.1 cm wide; petioles short, variable, often 2-3 cm long, with scattered cilia near base; leaf undersurfaces with abundant short white hairs; phyllaries with rather long, white, spreading marginal cilia, the surfaces with scattered pulbescene the pubescence sometimes abundant, especially in the central portion; inflorescence paniculate; disk 1.5-2.8 cm in diameter; ligules 2.7-3.6 cm long, 0.9-1.2 cm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Long, Robert W. 1961. Biosystematics of two perennial species of Helianthus (Compositae), II. Natural populations and taxonomy. Brittonia. 13: 129-141.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Perennial herb with a taproot, the caudex with a few slender branches, or perhaps sometimes simple; stems generally decumbent at the base, then erect or ascending, slender and somewhat flexuous, sparsely or moderately strigose, also more or less glandular under the heads, and the hairs there spreading; leaves linear or linear-oblanceolate, sparsely or moderately strigose, 1-nerved or the lowermost occasionally obscurely 3-nerved, the lower ones evidently petioled, up to 8 cm. long and 3 mm. wide, but not forming a conspicuous basal tuft, the cauline ones less petiolate, gradually reduced upwards; heads several on leafy branches, the disk 5-10 mm. wide; involuere 4-5 mm. high, finely and evidently glandular, commonly also with some spreading hairs; phyllaries equal or slightly imbricate, rays about 12-20, pink, about 5-7 mm. long, 1.4-2.0 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 2.7-3.5 mm. long, the tube obscure, the lobes about 0.5 min.; style-appendages deltoid or broader, acutish, about 0.1-0.2 mm. long; pappus of about 15-25 fragile bristles shorter than the corollas, commonly with a few slender and inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herba perennis, caulibus strigosis flexuosis usque ad 25 cm. altis subaequabiliter foliosis, foliis linlearibus vel lineari-oblanceolatis plerunique uninervis, imisusque ad 8 cm. longis 3 mm. latis, capitulis aliquot.disco 5-10 mm. lato involuero 4-5 mm. alto bracteis glandulosis et plerumque sparse hirsutis, ligulis 12-20, roseis, 5-7 mm. longis 1.4-2.0 mm. latis, corollis disco 2.7-3.3 mm. longis, pappo obscure duplici, achaeniis hirsutis 2-nervis.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Stems "in clumps from caudex," glabrate below, appressed-pilose and some- what glandular above; leaves opposite below, alternate above; petioles about 0.5 mm long; blades linear-lanceolate or linear, 4.0 cm long, 6 mm wide, acumi- nate with obtuse apex, cuneate at base, somewhat falcate, entire or subentire, revolute-margined, above dull green, densely strigose to sparsely hispidulous, somewhat glabrescent, beneath densely and loosely white-tomentose; heads 1-3 on peduncles 3-12 cm long; disk 1.5-2.7 cm in diameter; phyllaries oblong or oblong lanceolate, 8 mm long, 3 mm wide, obtuse to acutish, densely appressed pilose or somewhat hirsute, the outer subherbaceous, the inner indurate and blackish below; rays about 9, 15 mm long, 5 mm wide; disk corollas 7 mm long, yellow with blackish teeth, puberulous; anthers black; pales acuminate, blackish above, hispidulous and ciliolate above along keel; achenes 4 mm long, glabrous, dark-speckled; pappus of two linear-lanceolate awns about 2 mm long; pappus of ray achenes of one or two awns or lacking.
bibliographicCitation: Heiser, Charles B. 1957. A revision of the South American Species of Helianthus. Brittonia. 8: 283-285.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Aromatic annual or perennial herbs to 3 m tall angled, hispid or pilose; leaves sessile or with a winged petiole, perfoliate, to 40 cm long and 34 cm wide, scabrous or strigose above, puberulent to pilose below, often resin-dotted; upper ovate-lan- ceolate, serrate or dentate; lower leaves triangular, acuminate, the bases hastate or truncate, abruptly tapering to the lower winged portion, the lobes coarsely and finely dentate, peduncles densely glandular-pilose, glandular, or pilose; phyllaries ca 5, ovate to lanceolate, basally connate, glandular or pilose below; ray flowers in 2 series of ca 20 flowers each, corollas yellow, to 8 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, the pilose tube ca 2 mm long; disc flowers 5 mm long, ca 80 or more, upper portion of corolla often dark-purple when dried, pilose outside; ray paleae concave, lanceolate, pilose below, glabrous above, ca 7 mm long, acuminate to long-acuminate; disc paleae membranaceous, to 7 mm long, lanceolate, the margins pilose; achene dark brown, compressed-obovoid, striate, to 7 mm long and 5 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Wells, James R. 1965. A taxonomic study of Polymnia (Compositae). Brittonia. 17: 144-159.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Shrubs, 2-3 m tall; stems subangulate, branches densely strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades 7-14 X 2-4 cm, lanceolate, apices long-acuminate, bases truncate, attenuate, 3-nerved, margins crenate-serrate, adaxially dark-green, scabrous, abaxially pilose, hairs 1-1.5 mm long; petioles 0.5-1 cm long, densely strigose-hispidulous, hairs 1.5 mm long. Capitulescences thyrsoid, with dense axillary or terminal clusters of capitula, on peduncles 3-6 cm long, 2 bracts at base, glomerules 1-1.5 cm diam. (including =<20 aggregated capitula). Capitula 6 mm high, 4 mm diam.; phyllaries 3, oblongo-ovate, 5 X 4.5 mm, apices acute, densely strigose, hairs 1 mm long, distal one-third ciliate, 4-5 nerved. Pistillate fiorets 5-7, subtended by ovate paleae, 4.5 X 3.5 mm wide, 3-veined, strigose, hairs 1 mm long; corollas 4 mm long, 1.5 mm diam., white, tubulate, 2-lobed, lobes irregularly deltoid, scarcely pilose toward apex, hairs 0.5 mm long. Staminate fiorets (7)-10, subtended by lanceolate paleae, 4 X 2 mm, 1-veined, slightly ciliate toward apex margin; corollas 3 mm long, 1 mm diam., white, tubulate, 5-lobed, lobes regularly deltoid, 0.5 mm long, scarcely ciliate toward apex; anthers black; styles undivided, 2.5 mm long; ovaries 2 mm long, 1 mm diam., pilose toward, hairs 0.8 mm long. Cypselae 2.5 X 1.8-2 mm, with fleshy exocarp, brown-black, apex pilose, hairs 1 mm long. Chromosome numbers unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Arriagada, J. E. 2003. Revision of the genus Clibadium (Asteraceae, Heliantheae). Brittonia. 55: 245-301.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Trees exceeding 12 m in height, the stems to 20 cm in diameter; bark at least sometimes very dark, becoming rough on older stems; leaves ovate to broadly ovate, dentate or denticulate, sessile or petiole winged to base or distinctly petiolate, to 25 cm wide and 42 cm long, the lower surface tomentose especially along veins, the upper surface glabrous or sparingly strigose; peduncles villous to hispid; phyllaries ca 6, to 1 cm long and 7 mm wide, ovate, uniseriate, glabrous or with few pilose hairs, the margins pilose; ray flowers ca 20, the corollas yellow, to 1 cm long and ca 4 mm wide; disc flowers ca 3 mm long, the corollas yellow, puberulent outside; ray paleae concave, obovate, to 5 mm long; disc paleae oblanceolate, ca 3 mm long, the margin denticulate, midvein prominent; achene black, flattened-obovoid, to 4 mm long and 3 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Wells, James R. 1965. A taxonomic study of Polymnia (Compositae). Brittonia. 17: 144-159.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Cormo circa 1 cm. crasso, e-aule gracili, subtus glabro, 4-5 dm. alto; foliis rariter hirsutulis vel glabreseentibus; inferioribus anguste oblanceolatis, 1-1.5 dm. longis, 1-2 cm. latis; superioribus linearis; inflorentia laxa, 1-1.5 dim. longa, capitulis. 8-10, breviter peduneulatis; involuero turbinato, 1 cm. alto et lato; bracteis exterioribus ellipticis; interioribus oblongis, leviter erosis; pappo purpureoapiculato.
bibliographicCitation: Rydberg, Per A. 1934. Taxonomic notes on the flora of the prairies and plains of central North America. Brittonia. 1: 79-104.

description: Dioecious shrubs, much-branched from the base, 20-50 cm tall, branches densely albo-tomentose, glabrescent. Leaves with petioles 1-4 mm long; blades ovate to orbiculate, 3-14 mm long, 4-8 mm wide, base cuneate, apex obtuse, the margins 2-3-dentate, revolute, albo-tomentose to glabrescent. Capitulescences of solitary capitula or 2-3 capitula on distal branchlets; peduncles 2-5 mm long. Capitula with invo- lucres campanulate, 5-6 mm tall, ca. 4 mm wide, subtended by 1-2-bracteoles, ca. 2 mm long, linear; phyllaries 8-10, the inner ovate, ca. 4 mm long, ca. 1.5 mm wide, apically obtuse, hyaline-margined, dorsally tomentose, the outer oblong-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, apically acute. Functionally staminate individuals with capitula containing 15-20 florets, the corollas yellow or violet, campanulate, 5.5-6 mm long, the tube ca. 2 mm long, the throat ca. 3 mm long, the lobes lanceolate, 0.7 mm long, ca. 0.3 mm wide; anthers ca. 2 mm long; style branches ca. 1 mm long, apically obtuse; ovaries sterile; pappus bristles ca. 6 mm long, yellow to violet, apical cells slender, acute. Pistillate individuals with capitula containing 15-20 florets, the corollas narrowly tubular, ca. 6 mm long, the tube ca. 2 mm long, the throat ca. 3 mm long, the lobes linear, ca. 1 mm long, ca. 0.2 mm wide; anthers nonfunctional; style branches linear, ca. 1 mm long, apically obtuse, dorsally glabrous. Achenes cylindrical, ca. 3 mm long, costate, glabrous; pappus 6-8 mm long, rose to violet, apical cells slender, acute.

description: Perennial herb with a branched caudex; stem 1-4 dm. high, sparsely or moderately villous-hirsute with spreading hairs; leaves sparsely hirsute or essentially glabrous, the margins evidently hirsute-ciliate, all narrow, elongate, and acuminate or attenuate, the basal and lowermost cauline ones linear-oblanceolate, up to 16 cm. long and 8 mm. wide; middle cauline leaves linear-lanceolate or narrowly lanceolate, up to 10 ecn. long and 7 mm. wide; upper leaves scattered, reduced, linear; heads about 1-4, the disk 11-17 mm. broad; involuere 7-10 mm. high, equaling or surpassing the disk, sparsely or moderately woolly-villous with multicellular hairs, usually more densely so toward the base, phyllaries equal, thin, narrow, attenuate, the purplish tips loose and often reflexed; ligules about 45-75, pink or pink-purple, about 10-15 mm. long, 1.5-2.2 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.2-5.2 mm. long, the tube 1.0-1.5 mm., the lobes 0.6-0.7 mm.; style-appendages a little narrower than deltoid, acute, 0.2-0.3 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of 15-20 bristles, the outer of narrow squamellae or coarse bristles; akenes 2-nerved, hairy. Known from White Horse, Yukon Territory, to Richards Island, at the mouth of the Mackenzie River.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Basally woody herbs or subshrubs 1 - 1.5 mm tall. Leaves opposite; petioles up to 2 cm long; blades 7.5-11 x 3.5-5.5 cm, sub- membranous, ovate, obtuse to subtruncate then shortly attenuate at the base, acuminate at the apex, margins serrulate, adaxial surface scabridulous, the abaxial paler, strigillose, both surfaces with longer trichomes on the veins. Outer phyllaries 13-37x5-11 mm, lanceolate to oblong-elliptic, slightly indurate at the base; inner phyllaries 5-9 x 2.5-4 mm, oblong-elliptic, constricted and indurate at the base to oblong-obovate and more scarious. Paleae 7-8 xca. 1.5 mm when folded, deltate (ca. 1 x 1 mm) at the tip. Ray florets fertile, tube 2 mm long, lamina 18-20 x 7-8 mm, oblong to elliptic, abaxial surface sparsely setulose toward the base. Disc florets with the corolla 4-5 mm long, lobes abaxially gla- brous or with a few trichomes. Cypselae 3.5- 4.5 x 1.2-1.5 mm, the peripheral ones thickened, subquadrangular or trigonous with much reduced wings to wingless, densely tuberculate, the inner laterally flattened, sparsely tuberculate, wings up to 1.2 mm wide; pappus with awns mostly reduced to tooth-like projections or sometimes awnless, crown 0.5-0.8 mm high, almost totally fused to the body (mostly more than 2/3), with erose to fimbriolate margins.
bibliographicCitation: Moraes, M. D. & Semir, J. 2009. A revision of Brazilian Dimerostemma (Asteraceae, Heliantheae, Ecliptinae), with a new species and taxonomic adjustments. Brittonia. 61 (4): 341-365.

description: Perennial herb with a stout taproot and a stout usually branched caudex; stems several, curved or decumbent at the base, then erect, densely hirtellous or caneseent with short spreading hairs, 5-30 cm. high; leaves hairy like the stem, often grayish with pubescence, the basal ones more or less triple-nerved (some- times obseurely so), oblanceolate or spatulate, usually rounded or obtuse at the apex, usually aeute, tapering to a short or moderately long petiole, up to 12 cm. long and 15 mm. wide, usually considerably smaller; cauline leaves several or rather many, varying from oblong-ovate and only slightly smaller than the basal ones to occasionally linear and much red-uced; heads solitary or few, u-p to about 10, the disk 9-18 mm. wide; involueres 4-7 mm. high, more or less caneseent with white hairs, and sparsely to rather densely glandular; phyllaries slightly to strongly imbricate, appressed, firm, evidently thickened on the back, scarcely herbaceous; ligules about 30-100, blue, white, or sometimes pink, 5-15 mm. long, about 1.0-2.5 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.2-4.4 mm. long, the tube about 0.8-1.2 mm., the lobes 0.4-0.8 mm.; style-appendages ovate or broadly triangular, rounded or obtuse at the apex, about 0.1-0.15 or occasionally 0.2 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 15-25 firm bristles, the outer setulose-squamel- late, evident; akenes 2-nerved, hairy.

description: Frutex ramis terminalibus foliosis dense lanato-tomentosis, exfoliatis tuberculato-cicatricosis. Folia alterna coriacea rigida sessilia anguste linearia apice acutiuscula basi vaginato-amplectentia, supra laevia viridia glabra vel glabrata glanduloso- viscosa, margine valde revoluta, subtus crasse denseque tomentosa, 8-14 mm longa 1-1.5 mm lata. Capitula lata solitaria terminalia breviter pedunculata. Involucrum turbinato- campanulatum circiter 14 mm altum bracteis numerosis 7-8 seriatis paleaceis lineari-subulatis acutissimis interioribus 12 mm longis ad basim 1.5-2 mm latis ceteris gradatim brevioribus, extus parce araneosis sed externis lanuginosis. Flores-radii feminei numerosi ligulati corolla violacea 12 mm longa glabra, tubulo 2 mm longo lamina 1.5 mm lata. Flores disci hernaphroditi tubulosi corolla 5.5 mm longa glabra tubulo 1.8 mm longo, dentibus oblongis 1 mm longis, antheris 2 mm longis, stylo bifido ramis hirsutulis lanceolatis 2 mm longis. Ovarium dense hirsutoovillosum. Pappus ochraceo-rubescens 6 mm longus pilis externis palea- ceis acutis 0.8 mm longis.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1956. Studies on Andean Compositae - III. Brittonia. 8 (3): 179-193.

description: Shrubs or small trees, to 5 m tall; stems woody at base, branches and twigs densely pubescent, hairs 1 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades broad-ovate to ovate-oblong, membraneous, 8-25 X 8-12 cm, 3-veined, bases attenuate, apices shortly acuminate, margins erose, coarsely and finely incised and serrate, larger teeth to 8 mm long, deltoid, acute, densely strigose in both faces, hairs 1 mm long; petioles 3-6 cm long. Capitulescences thyrsoid, 8-15 cm long. Capitula subglobose, 5 mm high, nearly sessile or shortly pedicellate; involucres cupulate, 4 mm diam.; phyllaries (3)-4, ovate, 4 X 3 mm, 5-7 veined, strigose, hairs 0.1 mm long, apices obtuse, distal one-third ciliate, bases fleshy at maturity. Pistillate florets 12(-24), subtended by ovate paleae, 4 X 3 mm wide, arranged in 3-5 series, 3-veined, abaxially strigose, distal one-third ciliate, bases fleshy at maturity; corollas white or purple, 2.5 mm long, glabrous, 3-lobed, lobes deltoid, 0.5 mm long, shortly ciliate at margins; styles 4 mm long, branches 1 mm long. Staminate florets 8-(14), subtended by ovate-lanceolate paleae, 3 mm long, 3-veined, margins distal one-third ciliate; corollas tubulate, 3 mm long, 4-lobed, lobes 0.5 mm long, apices hispidulous; anthers black, 1.5 mm long; ovaries, 2.5 mm long, apices pilose, styles undivided, 3 mm long. Cypselae, drupaceous, obovate, 2.5 X 1.5 mm, rounded at base, distal one-third hirsute, hairs 0.5 mm long. Chromosome number, n = 16 (Stuessy & Arriagada, 1993).
bibliographicCitation: Arriagada, J. E. 2003. Revision of the genus Clibadium (Asteraceae, Heliantheae). Brittonia. 55: 245-301.

description: Plant perennial from a stout caudex, which is simple or somewhat branched with relatively stout usually short branches; herbage and involuere more or less glandular, and always with at least a few hispid-hirsute spreading hairs, sometimes densely pubescent, sometimes almost smooth; leaves crowded at the base, ternately lobed or dissected; cauline leaves few and reduced, mostly entire; stem scapiform, up to 25 cm. high, usually much shorter; heads solitary, the disk 8-20 mm. wide; involuere 5-10 mm. high, with thin subequal phyllaries which are purplish at least at the tips; pistillate flowers about 20-60, with white, pink, or blue ligules up to as much as 12 mm. long and 2 mm. wide, usually narrower, or shorter, or both, often more or less reduced and inconspicuous or essentially absent; disk-corollas 3-5 mm. long, the tube 0.5-1.0 mm., the lobes likewise; styleappendages deltoid or deltoid-ovate, acute or acutish, about 0.2 mm. long or a little less; pappus simple, of about 12-20 coarse bristles equaling or usually a little shorter than the corolla; akenes shortly villous-hirsute, 2-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Perennial herb arising from a simple or slightly branched caudex, commonly bearing tufts of radical leaves at the ends of short rhizomes; stems 1 or several, 1.5-6 dm. high, glabrous below, glandular in the infloreseence; leaves more or less triple-nerved, few, commonly shorter than or barely exceeding the internodes, obtuse or acute, apiculate, entire, or some, especially the lower, denticulate or crenulate, not ciliate on the margins, or the lowermost but slightly so toward the bases of the petioles; basal and lowermost cauline leaves glabrous, persistent, ob- lanceolate to oval, rather abruptly narrowed to winged petioles, the blade and petiole 3-15 cm. long and 10-33 mm. wide; middle cauline leaves smaller than or equaling those below, lanceolate to ovate or oblong, glandular; heads mostly 1-7, rarely as many as 16, commonly borne on nearly naked peduncles, the disks 11-19 mm. wide; involucre 7-9 mm. high, equaling or surpassing the disk; phyl- laries equal, glandular, occasionally with a few long hairs, the outer ones broad, mostly 0.8-1.3 mm. wide, acuminate, the tips appressed or a little loose; ligules comparatively few, mostly 40-80, 1-2 mm. wide and 12-20 mm. long, blue or rose- purple, rarely white, disk-corollas 4.5-6 mm. long, the tube up to 1.5 mm. long, the sharply pointed lobes 0.6-1.0 mm. long; style-appendages triangular-lance- olate to deltoid-ovate, sharply acute or sometimes merely acutish, about 0.2 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 25 reddish or tawny bristles, the outer setulose and sometimes very scanty; akenes hairy, 2-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Resembling S. agrestis but readily distinguished by the very short tube of its ray florets (ca 0.2 mm), short, outer bracts which are prominently pilose-ciliate, out-numbering two or more to one the short glandular-capitate trichomes, inner involucral bracts glabrous or nearly so (except for glandular trichomes); disc florets with nearly glabrous tube and smaller dimorphic achenes.

description: Dioecious (or rarely polygamo-dioecious) shrubs, much-branched from the base, 10-40 cm tall, erect, the branches densely albo-tomentose, glabrescent. Leaves with petioles 1-3 mm long; blades elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, 5-20 mm long, 1.5-5(7) mm wide, the bases cuneate, the apices obtuse, the margins 1-2-dentate, revolute, albo-tomentose to glabrescent. Capitulescences solitary on distal branchlets; peduncles 1-1.5 cm long. Capitula with involucres campanulate, 3-6 mm tall, 3-4 mm wide, bracteoles ca. 2 mm long, linear; phyllaries 8, the inner oblong, ca. 6 mm long, ca. 1.8 mm wide, hyaline-mar- gined, apically acute, ciliolate, dorsally to- mentose, the outer lanceolate, ca. 6 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, apically acute, cili- olate. Functionally staminate individuals with capitula containing 12-15 florets, the corollas yellow, narrowly campanulate, ca. 7 mm long, the tube 3.5 mm long, the throat 4.5-5 mm long, the lobes lanceolate, 0.7-1 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm wide; anthers basally caudate; style branches 0.5 mm long, apically rounded to broadly triangular, dorsally papillose; ovaries sterile or rarely fertile; pappus bristles ca. 7 mm long, violet, apical cells slender, acute. Pistillate individuals with capitula containing 10-20 florets, the corollas yellow, narrowly tubular, ca. 6 mm long, the tube 2.5-3 mm long, the throat ca. 5.5 mm long, the lobes (0.75)1-1.5 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm wide; anthers nonfunctional; style branches linear, 0.8 mm long, apically rounded, dorsally papillose. Achenes cylindrical, 2.5 mm long, costate, glabrous; pappus 6.5-7.5 mm long, rose to yellow, apical cells slender, acute.
bibliographicCitation: Dillon, Michael O. & Sagástegui Alva, Abundio. 1996. Revision of the dioecious genus Chersodoma Phil. (Senecioneae, Asteraceae), including a new species and status change. Brittonia. 48: 582-604.

description: Herba annua ad 25 cm alta. Radices paucae graciles albae non suberosae, non ex rhizomate exorientes. Caulis unicus purpureus vel pallide brunneus teres erectus, supra trichomatibus crassis articulatis instructus. Folia opposita lanceolata vel linearia obscure crenata purpurascentia glanduloso-punctata subsessilia vel sessilia, apice acuta, basi anguste cuneata, 5-10 mm longa 1-4 mm lata; superficies parce crispo-puberula; pagina inferior crispo-pilosa secus venas; venatio inconspicua, venis 3 in foliis majoribus, 1 in foliis minoribus. Inflorescentia paniculata; pedunculi ad 12 mm longi. Involucra cylindrica, phyllariis 4-5 mm longis, atropurpureis acutis vel acuminatis, glandulis stipitatis obsitis, non erosis ad marginem. Corollae 5 mm longae per anthesin, zygomorphae, trichomatibus albis vel purpureis glandulosis vel non glandulosis obsitae; lobi 0.8-1.0 mm longi pallide lavanduli aut 1.5-2.2 mm longi albidi; fauces tubusque purpurei sine limitibus inter se. Achenia heteromorpha nigra hispida 3 mm longa pappo excluso; pappus adelphocarpiorum ex 2-3 aristis corollas aequantibus et 2-4 squamellis obtriangularibus firmis descretis 0.7 mm longis constans. Basibus aristarum non alatis; pappus idiocarpii ex 1-3 squamellis et aliquot aristis minutis squamellas aequantibus constans.

description: Plants perennial, 40-65 cm high, procumbent or decumbent, with adventitious roots arising at the nodes (sometimes trailing in dense vegetation), with elongated internodes and slender, pliable stems, sparsely to rather densely hirsute; leaves 2.9-8.5(-11) cm long, 1.5-4.5(-5.5) mm wide, ovate below, becoming ovate-lanceolate above, serrate, acute to attenuate at the apex, cuneate at the base, evenly hirsute; petioles slender, 0.4-1.5(-2.5) mm long; heads campanulate, 6-8 mm in diameter, solitary on peduncles which branch from the axis in a modified cymose fashion; peduncles 2.5-5(-7.5) mm long, slender, rather densely spreading-hirsute, with glandular trichomes interspersed; receptacle convex, ca 2.0 mm across, 1-1.5 mm high; chaff persistent, membranous, oblong, 5-6 mm long, ca 1.5 mm wide, pilose toward the acuminate apex; involucre subuniseriate, the outer bracts 4-5.5(-6) mm long, 2-4 mm wide, elongate, slightly oval, green to purplishgreen, leaf-like in texture, acuminafe-attenuate to attenuate at the apex, hirsute, often densely so, with glandular trichomes copiously intermingled, the margins often scarious, ciliate; inner bracts essentially like the outer, oblongish, narrower than the outer, becoming membranous, lighter green to greenlish-yellow, purple-tinged toward the cuspidate to attenuate apex, at least the upper half pubescent; ray flowers ca 8, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 2.5-3 mm, the tube with glandular trichomes; ray corollas with orange or golden yellow ligules, these 2-4 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, broadly oblong (squarish) and three-lobed at the apex, the inner lobelets merely vestigial; achenes of the ray florets rather densely pilose, tangentially compressed, with a pappus like that of the disc; disc corollas yellow, 5-6 mm long, the tube 1.2-1.5 mm long, sparsely short-pubescent, gradually passing into a narrowly funnelform throat, ca 2.5 mm long, short pubescent near the base, the lobes narrowly lanceolate, 1.2-1.5 mm long, pilose at the apex; style branches slender, flattened, recurved, ca 1.1 mm long, glabrous except for the finely pubescent, short subulate tip; achenes black, very narrowly obconical, ca 2 mm long, obscurely to obviously 5-ridged, glabrous to minutely pubescent near the base; pappus of 10 unequal, ciliate scales, 1-1.5 mm long, brownish, to often rose-colored, shorter than the achene; anthers ca 2 mm long, dark brown or purplish, obscurely sagittate at the base; chromosome number, n =9, determined in the 2 populations indicated below with an asterisk.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and short branched caudex; stem and leaves sparsely to very densely hispid-hirsute, obscurely to conspicuously glandular; stem mostly 15 cm. high or less, in large forms sometimes to 30 cm. high; basal leaves linear-oblanceolate to spatulate, up to 8 cm. long and 12 mm. wide, tufted and persistent in small forms, fewer and deciduous in large forms; cauline leaves few, linear, and reduced, in small forms, to numerous.and as Large as the basal ones in larger forms; heads solitary, or in large forms occasionally several, hemispherical, the disk 9-20 mm. broad; involuere 5-9 mm. high, sparsely to very densely hispid-hirsute with long white hairs, and obscurely to conspicuously glandular; phyllaries equal or nearly so, green, sometimes with light brown midrib and narrow searious margins, relatively broad, the outer mostly 0.5-0.8 mm. wide; ligules about 15-45, pink or purple to deep blue or violet, 5-14 mm. long, 1.3-3.6 mm. wide, or occasionally very reduced and inconspicuous, or absent; disk-corollas mostly 4.0-5.5 mm. long, in depauperate forms sometimes onily 3.5 mm., in very robust forms sometimes as much as 6.5 mm., the tube 0.6-1.3 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.9 mm.; style-appendages from broadly triangular and obtuse to narrower than deltoid and acute, 0.15-0.4 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 20-30 firm bristles, the outer-of well developed setae somewhat intermingled with the bristles; akenes 2-nerved, very densely long-silky with appressed or ascending hairs, these sometimes obscuring the outer pappus.

description: Biennial or short-lived perennial from a short simple caudex, occasionally annual, or at least blooming the first season, very rarely with a short stoloniform rhizome; herbage more or less villous-hirsute with spreading hairs that are usually shorter than in E. philadelphicus; stem slender, 1-6 dm. high; basal leaves oblanceolate to obovate, sinuately lobed to subentire, rounded at the tip, tapering to the short petiole or petioliform base, 1-14 cm. long, 5-40 mm. wide; cauline leaves usually denticulate, mostly oblong or lanceolate, sometimes ovate, often clasping at the base but usually not so conspicuously so as in E. philadelphicus, usually reduced and scattered upwards; heads 1-50 in an often long and subnaked inflorescence; involuere 2.5-4 mm. high; phyllaries subequal, or the outer slightly shorter, viscid-villous, darker than in E. philadelphicus; disk 4.5-10 mm. broad; ligules about 100-150, 0.5 mm. wide or less, up to 5 mm. or rarely 6 mm. long, blue, occasionally white or pinkish; disk-corollas about 1.5-2.8 mm. long, the clearly marked tube about 0.4-0.8 mm. long, the lobes about 0.3-0.4 mm. long; styleappendages broadly ovate, obtuse, about 0.1 mm. long; pappus of about 10-15 very fragile bristles, occasionally with a short setulose outer series; akenes sparsely hairy, 2-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Rhizomes short, (1) 2-4 cm. in length, mostly unbranched, clothed with the base of previous leaves, 2-4 mm. thick; innovations rarely produced (seen only once), the leaves narrowly oblanceolate, obtuse, 14-17 cm. long, 2 cm. broad, narrowed to slender petioles 2-3 cm. long; stems simple, rarely branched, 1.5-6.0 dm. high, glabrate or puberulent and pubescent with coarse moniliform hairs (multiple at the base), and also long-stipitate-glandular, becoming more densely pubescent upwards; cauline leaves 3(2-4) pairs, mostly crowded near the base, rarely equally distributed upwards, ovarcte, obovate or elliptical-oblong, not infrequently lanceolate or oblanceolate, 2-5 cm. broad, 4-18 cm. long, obtuse, pale and glabrate or sparingly pubescent beneath, sparingly to moderately puberulent and coarsely moniliform-strigose and stipitate-glandular above, broadly ciliolate, entire or remotely and inconspicuously callous denticulate, connate-sheathing at the base, infrequently narrowed into a perceptible petiole; peduncles 10-30 cm. long, frequently with alternately disposed bracteoles; heads 1-3(7), hemispheric-turbinate, 18 (15)-22 mm. high; perielinium short, compact-white-puberulent and long-stipitate-glandular; involueral bracts 16-22(26), lanceolate, acute, 14(12)-17 mm. long, 2-3 mm. broad, puberulent and more or less pilose with coarse moniliform hairs and- sometimes also stipitate-glandular, ciliolate, pilose at the tip; ray flowers mostly 11-15, the ligules yellow, strigose, 5 (4)-8 mm. broad, 1.8-2.5(3) cm. long, 7-9 nerved, tridentate, the teeth acute, 2(1)-3 mm. long; disc flowers 9(8.4)-11(11.3) mm. long, narrowly to broadly goblet-shaped, the tube 3.6 (3.0)-4.5 (4.8) mm. long, the limb 5.5(5)-6.3 (6.6) mm. long, the collar conspicuous, the slender tube and the base of the limb thinly to densely pilose with somewhat coarse septate hairs; achenes tapering toward the base, 6.5 (6.0)-9 (10) mm. long, uniformly and sometimes densely hirsute with short double hairs, and stipitate-glandular; annulus 0.1-0.2 mm. long, insconspicuous, pappus ? length of corolla, stramineous, occasionally darker, barbellate, the setae 0.1-0.15(0.2) mm. long.

description: Herbacea exylopodio ca 25 cm alta; caules puberuli, striati, intemodiis ca 1-2 cm longis; folia opposita, sessilia; lamina chartacea, lineari-lanceolata, 1.3-3.2 cm longa, 0.8-3.8 mm lata, plerumque univenosa, integra, revoluta, glandulosa, glabriuscula; capitulescentia monocephala; pedunculi 13-16 cm longi; capitula heterogama, paleacea; involucrum hemisphericum, ca 8 mm longum, ca 12 mm latum; phyllaria subaequalia, 2-3-seriata; receptaculi paleae linearae, ca 3.5 mm longae, ca 0.3 mm latae; flosculi radiati ca 9, corolla ca 9.5-10 mm longa, luteola, tubo ca 1.5 mm longo, limbo 7-nervio, ca 8-8.5 mm longo, glandulifero; flosculi disci ca 21, corolla campanulata, ca 4.6-5 mm longa, glabra, luteola, lobis 1.7-2 mm longis; achaenia turbinata, prismatica, glabra, ca 2.7-2.9 mm longa; pappi squamae ca 15, ellipticae vel elliptico-lanceolatae, ca 0.6-1.3 mm longae.

description: Functionally herbaceous subshrubs to ca 25 cm tall with clumped stems arising annually from a subterranean xylopodium; stems erect, subterete, striate, puberulent, branching from near base, internodes about 1-2 cm long, usually much shorter than the subtending leaves. Leaves opposite, sessile; blade chartaceous, linear-lanceolate, 1.3-3.2 cm long, 0.8-3.8 mm wide, basally cuneate or clasping, apically acute or attenuate, margins entire and revolute, secondary veins generally absent, when present venation trinervate, upper surface green, smooth, hirtellous, especially when young; with uniseriate, multicellular, arcuate trichomes or glabrous, lower surface paler green, glandular with multicellular, biseriate, globular trichomes (glands), often puberulent especially along midrib with hairs as on upper surface. Capitulescence terminal, monocephalous, peduncle 13-16 cm long, puberulent to pubescent especially distally. Capitulum radiate, ca 30-flowered; in volucre hemispheric, ca 8 mm high, ca 12 mm broad, 2-3-seriate; phyllaries ca 12, imbricate, subequal, 7-8.5 mm long, 4.5-6 mm wide, 5- or 7-nerved, glabrous to abaxially puberulent on the nerves, apically acute to rounded, margins entire, outer ca 4 scabrous below, herbaceous-tipped, inner ones scarious; receptacle paleaceous, the paleae linear, ca 3.5 mm long, ca 0.3 mm wide, flat, entire. Ray florets ca 9; corolla ca 9.5-10 mm long, yellow, the tube ca 1.5 mm long, glabrous, the ligule 7-nerved, ca 8-8.5 mm long, ca 4-5 mm wide, apically 3-toothed, abaxially lightly glandular; style ca 4-4.5 mm long, branches only slightly recurved, ca 1.3 mm long. Disc florets ca 21; corolla campanulate, ca 4.6-5 mm long, glabrous, yellow to golden-yellow, tube ca 1.7 mm long, throat ca 1-1.2 mm long, lobes 5, erect to spreading, elliptic-lanceolate, ca 1.7-2 mm long, broadly acute apically; anthers partially exserted, pale yellow, ca 2 mm long, apical appendage deltoid, very lightly glandular abaxially; style ca 5.5 mm long, branches recurved, ca 1.1 mm long. Achenes (immature) of ray and disc florets similar, turbinate prismatic, ca 2.7-2.9 mm long, brown, glabrous; carpopodium tan, non-sculp- tured; pappus of ca 15, elliptic to elliptic lanceolate, apically acuminate to attenuate, marginally serrate, stramineous scales, ca 0.6-1.3 mm long. Pollen helian theous, ca 31-35 ,um diam. Chromosome number unknown.

description: Taprooted annual, probably scented but nature of scent unknown. Stems erect or ascending, solitary or 2-5-branched from near base, 5-20 cm long, stramineous or purplish, puberulent with retrorsely curved, multicellular trichomes ca 0.1 mm long. Leaves linear, 2-4 cm long, 2-3 mm broad, mucronate or setose-tipped, proximally ciliate to about the middle with bristles ca 2 mm long, sparsely pu- berulent abaxially on the midrib with trichomes ca 0.1 mm long, minutely scaberulous along margins, otherwise glabrous, densely punctate on the undersurface with round glands 0.1-0.3 mm diameter. Heads short-peduncled from the forks of the stems and at stem apices, solitary or becoming cymose-clustered in age. Peduncles 1-32 mm long, puberulent, bearing 1 or 2 alternate, scale-like to foliaceous setose-tipped bractlets 2-4 mm long. Involucres cylindric to narrowly cam- panulate; phyllaries 5-7, oblong-oblanceolate, 5-6 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, obtuse to subacute, on abaxial surface convex, keeled to above the middle, dotted or streaked with numerous scattered elliptical to linear glands 0.2-0.6 mm long, near apex and streaked with linear glands proximally, thin-margined, minutely glandular-ciliolate, otherwise glabrous. Ray florets 5-7; corollas yellow or red- dening in age, 4-5 mm long with tubes 1.5-1.8 mm long and ligules 2.5-3.2 mm long. Diskflorets 10-15; corollas yellow, 2.5-3 mm long, 4- or 5-lobed, weakly bilabiate, with the anterior lip 0.6-0.7 mm long, ca 2-3 x the length of the lobes on the posterior lip; style about equalling the corolla; anthers ca 0.6-0.7 mm long; pollen grains 34-40 µm diameter. Achenes 3-4 mm long, uniformly strigose with bifurcate 2-celled trichomes 0.15-0.25 mm long and just below insertion of pappus bearing multicellular gland-tipped trichomes ca 0.1 mm long. Ray pappus of 2 or 3 paleaceous-based awns 3-4 mm long, often with several short bristles or scales 0. 5-1 mm long inserted abaxially between the awns; disk pappus of 15-20 unequal antrorsely barbed bristles 2-4 mm long, these sometimes paleaceous based. Chro- mosome number: unknown.

description: Plants perennial, 2.5-14.0 dm tall, one to several stems originating from the root- stock, unbranched above or rarely with one or two branches. Stems weakly winged, usually glabrous below, sparsely to moderately pubescent above. Peduncles (5-) 10-30(-50) cm long, usually densely pubescent, usually tomentose beneath the receptacle but sometimes only moderately pubescent, ca. 2-6 times as wide at the top as at the base. Leaves variable in shape, entire, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, midrib prominent and lateral veins apparent in most; basal and lower leaves spatulate with clasping bases and rounded apices; middle and upper leaves sessile to petioliform, ovate to oblanceolate or oblong-elliptic with clasping and sometimes subauriculate bases and obtuse to acuminate apices. Heads usually one but rarely two or three, globoid to depressed hemispherical, 14-24 mm high, 18-34 mm wide (excluding rays). Receptacle hemispherical to globoid or ovoid. Involucral bracts united at the base, spreading to reflexed at anthesis, usually tomentose. Ray florets 15-30, ligules (12.0-) 16.5-28.0(-37.1) mm long, 6.0-13.6(-25.3) mm wide, yellow, densely pubescent on the undersurface. Disc corollas 5-lobed, cylindrical to cylindric-campanulate, 4.0- 5.0(-5.2) mm long, 1.0-1.5 mm wide, yellow with yellow to brown or purple lobes. Achenes 1.5-2.5 mm long, 0.6-1.1 mm wide, moderately to densely pubescent with relatively long hairs. Pappus scales 6-8, (2.5-)3.0-4.5 mm long, including the terminal awn, 0.2-0.4 mm wide, from 3/4 as long as to often exceeding the disc corolla. Chromosome number, n = 16.

description: Perennial herb with more or less branched woody caudex; stem 1.5-8 dm. high, glabrous, or sometimes slightly hairy or glandular in the infloreseence, usually with a few hairs just under each head; leaves commonly but not always triple-nerved, entire. but with ciliate margins, the cilia sometimes very few or present only along part of the margin, glabrous or sometimes with a few hairs along the main veins, the basal and lowermost cauline ones oblanceolate to broadly spatulate, narrowed to winged petioles, the blade and petiole mostly 5-15 cm. long and 4-20 mm. wide, usually deciduous or withered by flowering time; middle cauline leaves as large as the lower, or commonly larger, narrowly lanceolate to oblong or broadly oval, acute or sometimes obtuse, apiculate, sessile, 3-11 cm. long and 5-28 mm. wide; upper leaves usually not markedly reduced, narrowly lanceo- late to broadly ovate, occasionally minutely glandular; head 1-13, the disk about 11-22 mm. broad; involuere mostly 6-9 mm. high, glandular and sometimes with a few long hairs; phyllaries equal, narrow, acuminate or attenuate, the tips loose; ligules numerous, about 75-150, rarely fewer, about 9-18 mm. long and 1 mm. wide, blue, rarely white; pappus double, the inner of about 20-30 bristles, the outer commonly setulose; disk-corollas about 4.0-5.0 mm. long, the tube about 0.7-1.0 mm., the lobes about 0.6-0.9 mm., style-appendages triangular-lanceolate, acute, about 0.15-0.2 mm. long; akeines hairy, 2-4-nerved.

description: Probably an erect perennial herb; stem sulcate with spreading pilose hairs, becoming stipitate-glandular above; leaves sessile or winged to base, 3-nerved, the lower broadly ovate, the upper ovate, to 35 cm long and 32 cm wide, the lobes short and sinuses shallow and broad, obsolete near the apex; margins irregularly dentate, the teeth callous-tipped; upper surface short-pilose, especially along the main veins, the lower surface densely pubescent; peduncles stipitate-glandular; phyllaries ca 5, basally united, lanceolate, callous-tipped, to 9 mm wide and 2.5 cm long, stipitate-glandular and pilose below, the margins pilose, sparsely glandular to glabrous above; ray flowers ca 10, the corollas yellow, tridentate, ca 2 cm long and 5 mm wide, short-pilose on the veins below; disc flowers ca 6 mm long; ray paleae ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, ca 11 mm long and 4 mm wide; disc paleae lanceolate-ovate, ca 7 mm long and 2 mm wide; immature achene black, not noticably striate.

description: Roots mostly 0.8-1.0 mm thick; stems erect, up to ca. 1 m long, minutely pilose; leaves opposite, subcoriaceous, glabrous (except for a few hairs on the larger veins beneath), deltoid, narrowly deltoid or rhombic, the larger blades up to 2-6 (-7) cm long, apices acute or attenuate, bases of the larger leaves slightly subcordate, truncate, or cuneate, margins subentire to crenate (each crenation being somewhat asymmetrical and sometimes inconspicuously mucro-tipped), or, more commonly, coarsely serrate or incised with sharp or rounded teeth, petioles long, the larger blades mostly 1-4 times longer than their petioles, the upper leaves distinctly petiolate; involucres comprised of 8-12 (-14) phyllaries, imbricated towards the base (except sometimes in fruit), and arranged in 2 or 3 series: the outer series often wanting but when present comprised of a single, short phyllary, the inner two series of 8-11 (-13) subequal phyllaries, the longest being 2-4 mm long, (narrowly) oblong, glabrous or sparingly and minutely pubescent, herbaceous, margins sometimes narrowly scarious, often ciliate, apices acute or obtuse, sometimes fimbriate, nerveless or weakly 2- nerved; heads bearing ca. 12 (7-18) flowers; corollas white, funnelform, 2.5-3.5 mm long, the lobes ca. 1/3-1/4 as long as the tube, sparsely pubescent (best seen in bud) or rarely glabrous beneath; achenes 2-3 mm long, pubescent, at least with short, fine hairs near the apex, rarely glabrous; 2n = 34.

description: Herba suffruticosa ramis tortuosis nodosis prostratis basilaribus sterilibus fasciculato-foliosis. Folia herbacea crassiuscula, inferiora et fascicularia oblanceolata apice subite acutata basim versus attenuata in petiolum longum angustata basi longe vaginata amplexicaule, margine integerrima vel remotis minutis dentibus praedita, limbo 4-9 cm longo 1.1-1.8 cm lato, costa tantum conspicua reliquis venis inconspicuis utrinque subglabra parcis floccis areneosis deciduis ad costam et vaginam munitis, petiolo 1-2 cm longo, vagina subseariosa amplexicaule ad 2 cm longa. Folia superiora sessilia sublanceolato-oblonga basi cordata amplectentia, 5-8 cm longa 1.2-1.8 cm lata, vix sparsissime lana araneosa decidua. Inflorescentia paucicapitata terminalis corymbosa vel laxe paniculata, peduneulis vel ramis elongatis tenuibus flexuosis 2-5 cm longis glabris vel sparsis pilis munitis. Calyculus 8-10 bracteolis lanceolato-subulatis tenuibus 4-5 mm longis circa 1 mm latis parce araneosis vel parce ciliatis vel glabris ad basim capituli et secundum pedunculum descendentibus. Capitula homogama discoidea subglobosa nutantia vel cernua. Involucrum subcampanulatum 12 bracteis herbaceis lanceolatis acutis apice ciliato-penicillatis dorso glabris vel sparse araneosis circa 9 mm longis exterioribus 1.5 mm latis interioribus 2.5 mm latis margine seariosis. Flores omnes hermaphroditi isomorphi circa 50 in capitulo, corolla lutea glabra 8-10 mm longa tubulo 5-6 mm longo capillari (basi inerassata excepta) limbo campanulato dentibus deltoideis acutis 1 mm longis. Antherae 2 mm longae basi obtusae. Rami styli crassiusculi recurvati apice truneati papilloso-penicillati. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus albus 6 mm longus pilis biseriatis sericeis breviter scabrosis.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1960. Studies on Andean Compositae--IV. Brittonia. 12: 182-195.

description: Arbor 12 m alta ramis terminalibus fuscis subteretibus cicatricoso-tuberculatis parce puberulis. Folia chartacea simplicia alterna. Petiolus 2-3 cm longus flexuosus dense brunneo-tomentosus. Lamina elliptico-lanceolata basi acute vel obtuse cuneata apice angustata acuta vel acuminata margine integra, 8-12 cm longa 2.5-4.8 cm lata; supra viridis copiose minuteque resinoso-granulata, costa tomentella notata cetera glabra nervis secundariis parum conspicuis; subtus dense subferrugineo- tomentosa pilis furcatis ramosisque intricatis munita, costa bene elevata nervis secundariis 13-14 utroque latere prominentibus subpatulis marginem versus furcato-anastomosantibus, reliquis nervulis reticulum prominulum plus minusve conspicuum formantibus. Inflorescentia terminalis paniculata multiflora folia non attingens, axi ramu- lisque dense brunnescenti-tomentosis. Pedicelli tenues pallido-tomentosi flex- uosi 2-4 mm longi. Capitula biflora involucro stramineo pluriseriato disticho-complanato 7-8 mm longo 2.5-3 mm lato bracteis involucralibus scariosis ovatis acutis gradatim imbricatis inferioribus brevibus puberulisque superioribus subglabris longioribus duobus intimis fertilibus basi connatis 6-6.5 mm longis 3 mm latis amplectente navicularibus apice indurato-acutis. Corolla late tubulosa 5 mm longa glabra lobulis anguste linearibus 2 mm longis. Antherae 2.2 mm longae, basi sagittatae lobis obtusis. Styli ramis validis hirsutisque. Ovarium glabrum sursum parce glandulosum 1.5 mm longum. Pappus 2-4 paleis ensiformibus acu- tiusculis rigidis planis margine ciliatis nervo medio crassiusculo conspicuo, 3.5-4 mm longis 0.4 mm latis; alteris paleis squamosis valde brevibus irregulariter laceratis liberis vel coalitis 0.3-0.5 mm longis.

description: Herb 4-20 cm tall, sparingly branched from the base and above or rarely simple; glabrous or moderately pubescent throughout; lower leaves 2-4 cm long, simple, the middle and upper cauline leaves gradually reduced and pinnately parted with 1-3 pairs of short lobes; upper leaves much reduced; involuere 2-4.5 mm high, the 5-8 narrowly to broadly ovate phyllaries curved over the disk after flowering and slightly reflexed when achenes are ripe; ray florets 4-7 (-12), equal to or slightly exceeding the phyllaries, yellow, with yellow stigmas; disk florets 2-16, 3-5-merous, yellow, their stigmas and pollen yellow; achenes 2-3 mm long, obscurely angled; n = 16; self-compatible.

description: Rhizomes generously rooting, mostly short, thick, 3-5 mm. in diam., dark brown, much branched, forming a dense crown; innovations numerous, leafy, short, the plant thus forming large dlense clumips, by laid-summer bearing numerous conspicuous buds at the ends of the caudex branches; stems 4-6 dm. high, subglabrate below, becoming sparsely granular and viscid scabrid-puberulent above, simple below, branched at the middle and above, late in the season producing slender branchlets below the middle, these bearing slender petiolate leaves; cauline leaves 5-7 pairs, diminishing but little upwards, 5-12(15) cm. long, 1.5-2(3.5) cm. broad, laneeolate to lance-elliptic, the apex long-acute or muerely acutish, the base narrow, connate-sheathing, the margins entire or minutely denticulate, sparsely scabrid-puberulelnt and glandular-punctate, more sparingly so and greener on the upper surface; peduncles slender, 3-5(7) cm. long; infloreseenee cynmose, paniculately or corymbosely so wheni heads numerous; heads 7-20(35), rarely as few as 3 (as in the type), 10-15 (17) mm. high, turbinate-campanulate; perielinium prominent, scantily to moderately puberulent and somewhat densely shortstipitate-glandular, or also sparsely pilose with coarse nmoniliform hairs; involueral bracts 11-15(20), 7 (6)-1 (12) mm. high, becoming less pubescent above, the apex subglabrous, narrowly or somewhat broadly lanceolate, acute to accuminate; ray flowers 8-11, the ligules deep or mostly pale yellow, linear-oblong or elliptic, 1-2 cm. long, 4-6 nim. broad, 3- or rarely irregularly toothed, the teeth acute 0.5-1.5 mm. long; disc corollas 7.5 (6.9)-8.5(9.6) mnm. long, the tube 2(1.8)-2.5(2.9) mmi. lonig, the limb 5.4(5.0)-6.5(7.2) mm. long, slender, the tube and the base of the limb moderately short-hirsute and short-stipitate-glandular; achenes 4.5-5.5 mm. long, tapering toward the base, subglabrate, or uniformly and moderately short-stipitate-glandular, occasionally also with sparse double strigose hairs; annulus poorly developed; pappus stramineous to tawny, ? the length of the corolla, barbellate to subplumose, the setae 0.15-0.3 mm. long.

description: Frutex 1.5 m altus, dense hispidulus. Folia opposita, sub 3.5 cm longa et sub 3 cm lata, petiolata petiolo angusto sub 5-6 mm longo, lamina membranacea, pin- natim 3- vel 5-partita, foliolis segmentisve ovatis usque ad lanceolatis 3-13 mm latis, apice acriter mucronulatis; rhachi inferne tenui superne marginato. Rami terminaliter corymboseque ramulosi, terminaliter ca 8 capitula subtendentes. Pedunculi graciles, dense hispiduli, ca 1-4 cm longi. Capitula radiata pansa ad anthesin (unicum cum radiis visum) ca 1 cm lata et alta. Involucri bracteae exteriores ca 8-10, lineares, ca 3-4 mm longae extus hispidulae, dense ciliatae, quam oblongae interiores dimidio breviores. Flores liguldati (3 pro uiico capitulo manci visi) rosacei, ligula late obovata apice obtuse lobulata ca 7-8 mm lata. Paleae lanceolato-oblongae apicaliter attenuatae, sub 7 mm longae. Achaenia linearia, obcompressa, exteriora circumambitu fere oblanceolata, ca 5.5 mm longa et 1.5 mm lata, atra, mediane costata marginibus brunneo-pectinata deiitulis ir- regfulariter connatis, apice calva; interiora angustiora, vix longiora.

description: Shrub 1.5 m tall, densely hispidulous. Leaves opposite, under 3.5 cm long alnd unlder 3 cm wide, petiolate with a petiole narrow and uLnder 5-6 mm long; blade membranaceous, pinnately 3- or 5-parted, the leaflets or segments ovate to lanceolate and 3-13 mm wide, sharply mucronulate at apex; rhachis proximally slender distally margined. Branches terminally and corymbosely ramulose, ter- minally bearing ca 8 heads. Peduncles slender, densely hispidulous, ca 1-4 cm long. Heads radiate, expanded at flowering (a single one observed with rays) ea 1 cm wide and tall. Outer phyllaries ca 8-10, linear, ca 3-4 mm long, outwardly hispidulous, densely ciliate, a half shorter than the oblong inner ones. Ray florets (3 fragmented ones seen on a single head), rosaceous; ray widely obovate, ca 7-8 mm wide, obtusely lobulate at apex. Chaff-scales lanceolate-ob- long, attenuate at tip, under 7 mm long. Achenes linear, obcompressed, outer ones almost oblanceolate in outline, ca 5.5 mm long and 1.5 mm wide, black, medianly costate, on margins brown-pectinate with irregularly connate little teeth, apically exaristate; inner ones uarrower, scarcely longer.

description: Perennial 2-5(0.8-8) dm tall, glabrous or lightly pubescent on the outside of the involucral bracts, and sometimes on the undersides of the leaves; stems arising singly or very loosely clustered from well developed fibrous-rooted creeping rhyzomes. Basal leaves cordate to subcordate, frequently with 1-3 pairs of lateral lobes on the well developed petiole, making the leaf lyrate, the margins shallowly to rather deeply incised, with the sinuses rounded, 8-15(5-25) cm long, including the petiole and 3-7(1.5-12) cm wide; petiole usually about twice as long as the blade. Cauline leaves only about 3-6 but conspicuous and well developed, 2/3-3/4 as long as the basal leaves, pinnatifid to sublyrate, the midrib usually winged. Inflorescence a corymbose or subumbellate cyme of (4)8-15+ heads; principal involucral bracts ca. (8)13 or 21, 5-8 mm long; calyculate bracts few but sometimes prominent; ray florets ca. (5)8 or 13, the ligule 10-15(20) mm long. Achenes 3-5 mm long, glabrous.

description:
Frutex 2-3 m altus ramosus ramis foliosis griseis resinoso-viscosis araneo- sisque. Folia alterna coriacea sessilia anguste linearia basim versus paulo attenuata basi vaginata amplectentia supra basim saepe geniculata patula, margine valde revoluta apice subspinuloso-acuta; supra viridia nitidissima resinoso-viscosa glabra; subtus costa crassa eminentissima glabra et viscosa reliqua dense albo- lanata, 2-3 cm longa 1.5-2.5 mm lata.

Capitula lata subterminalia pedicellata 5-6 in pseudo-umbella disposita folia suprema attingentia vel superantia. Pedicelli mediocres 10-18 mm longi resinosi et tenuiter albo-arachnoideo-lanuginosi. Capitula radiata expansa 4 cm lata vel ultra. Involucrum subhemisphaericum 12-14 mm altum bracteis crebris plurise- riatis rigide paleaceis lineari-lanceolatis acutissimis margine plu3 minusve eroso-laceratis dorso araneosis albo-lanatis, intimis 11-12 mm longis 1.5 mm latis ceteris gradatim brevioribus. Flores-radii feminei ligulati conspicuissimi circa 30, corolla azurea glabra 22-23 mm longa tubulo angusto 6 mm longo, lamina 2 mm lata apice breviter 3-dentata; stylo 2 ramis subulatis 2 mm longis exsertis; ovario compresso subglabro sparse glanduloso; pappo stramineo 7 mm longo setis externis valde brevis. Flores disci hermaphroditi crebrissimi corolla tubulosa lutea 10-11 mm longa glabra tubulo 3 mm longo dentibus papillosis 1 mm longis; antheris 4 mm longis basi sagittatis; stylo ramis lanceolatis crassius- culis papilloso-hirsutulis 2 mm longis; ovario 3.5 mm longo costato sparsis glandulis et setis brevibus munito; pappo stramineo 8 mm longo, setis extemis brevibus paleaceis acutissimis.

description: Frutex vel arbor, caulibus tomentosis. Folia alterna 3-8 x 1-2.5 cm (ca 3-plo longiora guam latiora), anguste elliptica, supra glanduloso-punctata et strigosa, infra glanduloso-punctata et pannosa et hirsuta, apice acuta vel acuminata, basi cuneata, marginibus denticulata et revoluta; petioli 0.5-1.2 cm longi. Inflorescentiae terminales paniculatae 5-10 cm diametro. Capitula uniflora, sessilia vel brevipedunculata, arcte fasciculata. Involucra tubulosa, 5-7 x 1.4-1.9 mm. Phyllaria glabra vel tomentulosa, imbricata, interiora anguste oblonga, ca 5 x 1-1.5 mm, externa ovata, ca 1.5 x 1.2-1.7 mm, apice acuta. Corolla (6.5) 7 (8) mm longa, tubulo 3-3.5 mm longo glanduloso, lobis 3.6-4 mm longis ad apicem glandulosis. Antherae ca 2.7 mm longae. Achaenia (imperfecte matura) 2 mm longa, ca 8- nervia, glandulosa. Pappi setae 25-35 albae, 6 mm longae.

description: Rhizome slender, short, with slender roots, bearing a tuft of half a dozen leaves and 1 or 2 elongate flexuous remotely rooting flowering stems; basal leaves with an obovate or elliptic blade 1.5-2.3 cm. long, 7-8 mm. wide, narrowly long-decurrent on the petiole (this 2-3.5 cm. long), the blade somewhat yellowish green, papery, obtuse or rounded and often bluntly apiculate, obscurely serrulate with 1 or 2 pairs of usually minute mucronulate teeth or subentire, feather-veined (veins 2 or 3 pairs) or somewhat triplinerved, evenly but not densely spreading-pilose with several-celled white hairs on both sides, the petiole similarly pubescent; stems about 3-5.5 dm. long, slender, about 1 mm. thick, apparently arching, greenish, striatul ate, sometimes throwing out a strong tuft of roots once or twice in their length and there devel- oping a tuft of leaves like those at base of stem, evenly leafy nearly to tip, their leaves alternate, mostly 5-18 mm. apart, obovate, 1-2 cm. long, 3.5-5.5 mm. wide, obtuse or rounded, bluntly apiculate, narrowed to a sessile base, the 3 or 4 uppermost smaller, elliptic, subremote; pedunc]e 3.5-6 cm. long, thickened below the head and there more densely spreading-pilose; head 1.8-2.3 cm. wide; disk broadly rounded, 4.5 mm. high, 8-9 mm. thick (as pressed); involuere hemispheric, 2-seriate, subequal, 5 mm. high, the phyllaries lanceolate (1-1.2 mm. wide), acuminate, submembranous with very narrow thinner paler margin, greenish with somewhat loose purplish tips, not evidently ciliate except at apex, rather densely spreading-pilose on back, 3-vittate; receptacle foveolate, slightly convex, broadly rounded; rays about 60-70, white, pistillate, 3-seriate, the tube glabrous, 1.3 mm. long, the lamina linear- oblanceolate, 8 mm. long, 1.2 mm. wide, 2-3-denticulate, 3-4-nerved, glabrous except for a few short hairs on back near base; disk flowers very numerous, fertile, their corollas yellow, slender-funnelf orm, sparsely pilosulous near middle with several-celled mostly blunt hairs, 3 mm. long (tube 0.8 mm., throat 1.7 mm., teeth ovate, slightly papil- lose, 0.5 mm. long); ray achenes ellipsoid-oblong, compressed, 1.5-1.7 mm. long, 0.6 mm. wide, whitish, thick-margined, sparsely hispidulous toward the rounded apex, their pappus of 2 or 3 hispidulous hairs 0.25 mm. long or less; disk achenes similar, even more obscurely hispidulous, epappose, subtruneate at apex.

description: Plants perennial, 15-40 cm high, procumbent and subscapose to erect or suberect with leafy stemis, sparsely to densely hirsute; leaves ovate or narrowly to broadly lanceolate, 2-6.5 cm long, 0.5-2 cm iwide, deeply serrate to pinnately lobed, acute to attenuate at the apex, attenuate at the base, sparsely to densely hirsute on both surfaces; heads campanulate, 9-13 mm in diameter, solitary on rather slender peduncles; peduncles 6-23 cm long (often with 2-3 originating from the same node), with spreading or irregularly appressed (rarely antrorsely appressed) trichomes; receptacle short-conical, 4-6 mm across, 1.5-2.5 mm high; chaff persistent, membranous, 6-9 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, pubescent near dentate-obtuse or mucronate apex; involucre 2-3-seriate, the outer bracts alternately broader and longer, ovate to obovate, purple-tinged, 3.5-6(-7) mm long, 2-6.5 mm wide, densely hirsute, attenuate at the apex; inner bracts oblong to sub-oblong, 3-7.5 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, hirsute and purple at the apex; ray flowers 6-8, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 4-5 mm, with conspicuous, bright yellow ligules, these 5-7 mm long, 4-7 mm wide, broadly oblong to obovate, with 3(-4) obtuse or acute lobes at the apex; pappus of the ray florets reduced, 1-2 mm long; disc corollas yellow, (6-)6.5-9 mm long, the tube finely pilose, 1-1.5 mm long, the throat tubular to narrowly funnelform, 4-6 mm long, with fine, appressed pilose hairs, the lobes acute, reflexed, 1-1.5 mm long, slightly pubescent at the apex; style branches rather slender and flattened, 1.5-2.5 mm long, with a subulate tip, pubescent only half the length, mostly at the apex; achenes black, narrowly turbinate or narrowly obconical and truncate at the apex, densely pilose, 2-2.5 mm long; pappus of 20 plumose bristles, shorter than the corollas, the bristles alternately long and short, the longest (4-)6-7.5 mm long, the shortest 34 the length of the longest, the cilia ca 1.0 mm long; anthers 2.5-3.5 mm long, minutely sagittate at the base; chromosome number, n = 9, determined in the 3 populations indicated below with an asterisk.

description: Frutex; rami teretes, squamis multiradiatis adpressis pallide rufescentibus obsiti; folia alterna, petiolis 2-4 mm longis supra sulcatis 1-1.5 mm crassis suffulta, elliptica vel oblongo-elliptica, basi rotundata vel obtusa, apice obtusa vel acuta, 3.5-4 cm longa, 1.5-3 cm lata, nervo medio supra impresso, subtus prominente, nervis lateralibus utroque latere 4-5 supra leviter impressis, subtus prominentibus non anastomosantibus, supra glabra, aureo-glanduloso-punctata, subtus lepidibus multiradiatis adpressis, rufescentibus obtecta, margine minute 3-4-dentata, chartacea; inflorescentiae terminales, capitulis glomeratis sessilibus; bracteae euphylloideae sed minores; capitula 5-6 mm longa, 5-8-flora; involucri squamae 3-5-seriatae, exteriores anguste ovatae, interiores lineari-oblongae, margine plus minus ciliatae vel scariosae, apice obtusae vel rotundatae, sub apice macula rotunda viridi notatae, usque 4 mm longae; corollae 5 mm longae, cylindraceae, apice parum ampliatae; lobi lineares, 1.5 mm longi; antherae 2.5 mm longae, ligula lineari-lanceolata, 0.75 mm longa; stylus 7 mm longus, ramis 1.5 mm longis, brevissime antrorse pilosis; pappi setae interiores 10-15 lineares, minutissime denticellatae, 4-4.5 mm longae, exteriores 0.5-0.7 mm longae inter sese liberae; achaenia linearia, immatura 2 mm longa, glabra, 4-costata.
bibliographicCitation: Liogier, Alain H. 1968. Novitates Antillanae. III. Brittonia. 20: 148-161.

description: Giant herbaceous perennial (Fig. 1A) with commonly 1 but up to 5 or more aerial stems from a rootstock of stubby rhizomes with hairy buds (Fig. 1B); stems 1.5-4.7 m tall and 1.5-4 cm in diam at base; upper portion of stem with pith solid and white, sometimes gelatinous, in smaller stems or chambered in larger stems; basal portion of stem fistulose, sometimes filled with a cylinder of gelatinous material or a liquid containing gelatinous blobs; lower leaves deciduous, leaving prominent U-shaped leaf scars; central leaves with petioles 1-4 dm long and blades 1.2-3.8 dm long and 1.6-5.7 dm wide, sub-rotund with (7) 9-11 (17) lobes, sub-palmately veined and cordate at base (Fig. lD), the margin callose-denticulate (Fig. 1 E); upper leaves smaller and more oblong in outline (Fig. 2A); inflorescence a terminal panicle up to 1 m long with branches bearing small subsessile foliaceous bracts (Fig. 2A); heads numerous on filiform peduncles; involucres cylindrical, 3.5-6.6 mm long with 1-8 tiny calyculate bracts at base (Fig. 2B); phyllaries 7- 13, glabrous except at tip, 0.28-0.94 mm broad; ray florets 3-8 with deep yellow rays 3.5-6.4 mm long and 0.8-2.1 mm wide (Fig. 2C); disk florets 4-14, with deep yellow to orange-yellow corollas 5.5-7.7 mm long with cups 3.2-4.3 mm long (Fig. 2D); tube of both ray and disk florets and base of cup sparsely hairy; anthers with appendages 0.32-0.48 mm long, anther sacs 1.4-2.3 mm long, and tails 0.11-0.35 mm long (Fig. 2E); achenes glabrous, 2-2.5 mm long; pappus 3.3- 6.2 mm long; receptacle alveolate.

description: Central cauline leaves tending to have elongate lobes; phyllaries shorter, 3.2-4.6 mm long, narrower, 0.28-0.71 mm wide, and more numerous, (8) 11-13; heads with more ray and disk florets, the total number of florets 14-21; ray and disk florets smaller, with shorter ovaries, corollas, lobes on disk corollas, and anther tails (Table II).
