description: Stout herb, the caudex subterranean (?); leaves somewhat papyraceous, elliptic-oblong, 15-30 cm. long, 4-5 cm. broad, narrowed proximally to about 5 mm., acute at apex, sinuate-denticulate at margins, glabreseent above, closely einereous tomentose beneath, the costa prominent, the secondary nerves 8-12 per centimeter, spreading nearly at right angles, the veinlets obscure; flowering branches erect, subligneous, glabreseent, bearing cauline leaves proximally, corymbosepaniculate, the branches subtended by foliaceous bracts; heads at maturity 20-25 cm. in diameter; phyllaries about 20, 2- or 3-seriate, papyraceous, broadly ovate, cuspidate, the outer ones 7-9 mm. long, 5-7 mm. broad, sparsely short hispid without; ray florets 40-60, about 2-seriate, the corolla about 8 mm. long, the tube 1 mm. long, densely viscid-glandular-hispid, the lamina oblong, 2.5-3 mm. broad, usually 2-lobed at apex, sparsely pilose without, the style and stigmas 3-4 mm. long, the achene about 3 mm. long; disk florets 5-6 mm. long, the tube and lobes glandular-hispid, the tube and limb subequal, the lobes deltoid, the stamens 3.5-4 mm. long; paleae imembranaceous, obovate, 5-6 mm. long, 3-3.5 mm. broad, acute, densely atropurpureous glandular- viscid distally without.

description: Roots mostly 0.8-1.0 mm thick and usually some up to 1.2-1.5 mm thick; stems erect, up to ca. 1 m long, minutely pilose; leaves opposite, membranous or usually subcoriaceous, minutely pilose on one or both surfaces or, uncommonly, glabrous, mostly narrowly deltoid, sometimes nearly ovate or lanceolate, the larger ones up to 2-7 (-9) cm long, apices acute, bases of the larger leaves slightly sub- cordate, truncate, or broadly cuneate, margins commonly crenate, each crenation being somewhat asymmetrical and occasionally inconspicuously mucro-tipped, less commonly dentate or subentire, petioles short, the larger blades at least 3 and mostly 5 or more times longer than their petioles, the upper leaves mostly subsessile; involucres comprised of 8-14 phyllaries, imbricated towards the base (except some- times in fruit) and arranged in 3 series: the outer series being comprised of 1 or 2 short phyllaries or wanting, the inner two series of 8-12 subequal phyllaries, the longest 3.5-4.5 (3-5.5) mm long, usually pubescent, (narrowly) oblong or slightly spatulate, the margins scarious or herbaceous, sometimes ciliate, the apices acute or obtuse, occasionally fimbriate, weakly 2-nerved or appearing nerveless; heads bearing 10-19 flowers; corollas white, funnelform, 3-4 mm long, the lobes 1/3-1/4 as long as the tube, conspicuously long-pubescent beneath; achenes 2-3 mm long, rarely longer, glabrous or rarely finely pubescent near the apex; n = 17, 2n = 34

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and branching caudex, the primary branches usually again branched; stem 5 cm. high or less, finely hirsute or villous, especially upwards, with spreading or sometimes appressed hairs; leaves oblanceolate or linear-oblanceolate, tufted, all or nearly all in a basal cluster, up to 2 cm. long and 2.5 mm. wide, the surfaces glabrous or sparsely and finely hairy, the margins finely more or less ciliate; cauline leaves 2 or 3, reduced and linear, more hairy than the basal ones, or absent; head solitary, the disk about 7-10 mm. wide; involucre about 5 mm. high, viscid and finely villous with short hairs; phyllaries relatively broad, narrowly lanceolate or lance-oblong, green or greenish, slightly imbricate, or subequal; ligules about 20-50, white, 5-8 mm. long, 1.9-2.2 mm. wide, disk-corollas about 2.3-3.0 mm. long, the tube 0.5-0.7 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.6 mm.; style-appendages deltoid, acute or acutish, 0.2-0.3 mm. long; pappus double, the outer of fine and not very conspicuous squamellae or setae, the inner of about 6-12 fragile bristles; akenes 2-nerved, hairy. Rocky Mountiins of southern Alberta and presumably British Columbia; also in the Cypress Hills, Saskatchewan.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Trees to 7 m, terminal branches densely tomentose. Leaves with petioles of 2-15 cm long, tomentose, blade obovate-elliptic-oblong, 10-45 X 4-21.5 cm, coriaceous, base cuneate, apex subacute, rounded or obtuse, abaxial surface tomentose, adaxial surface glabrous, reticulate veined with 9-10 secondary veins on each side of midrib, margins entire, slightly revolute. Capitulescences thyrsoid-paniculate. Capitula homogamous, discoid; involucre cylindrical, phyllaries 5, weakly biseriate, subcoriaceous, outer phyllaries oblong, 6-8 X 1.5-2.5 mm, tomentose, apex acute, inner phyllaries elliptic-oblong, 6-7.5 X 2-3 mm, medially tomentose, apex obtuse, margins scarious. Florets 5, hermaphroditic, corolla 7.5-9.5 mm long, tube 3.5-4 mm long, limb 4-5.5 mm, lobes linear, ca. S mm long, apex acute; an- thers ca. 3 mm long, base sagittate, caudate, terminal appendage lanceolate, slightly acute; style branches with the apex slightly obtuse, dorsally pilose. Achenes oblong, ca. 3 mm long; pappus 8-10 mm long.

description: Branching shrub 2-4 m. high, the branches and branchlets woody, stout, subterete, pale yellow or white lanate, at length glabrous; leaves aggregated near ends of branchlets, coriaceous, oblong or obovate-oblong, 15-50 cm. long, 3-17 cm. broad, narrowed towards the base to 2-5 mm., acute or callose-apieulate at apex, entire or crenulate at margins, glabrous above, covered with copious pale yellow or white tomentum beneath, the costa prominent, the secondary nerves up to 70 per side, parallel, straight, spreading, the veinlets obscurely reticulate; inflorescence axillary near ends of branchlets, broadly corymbose-paniculate, many-headed; branches of the inflorescence white lanate, subtended by bracts resembling minute leaves; heads at maturity 7-15 mm. in diameter; involucre 3- or 4-seriate, the phyllaries 20-30, ovate, 3-3.5 mm. long, about 2 mm. broad, acute, sparsely pilose without; ray florets 15-20, in 1 or 2 series, the corolla 5-5.5 mm. long, the tube setose with translucent hairs about 0.5 mm. long, the lamina oblong or obovate, 3 mm. broad, usually 3-lobed at apex, the style and stigmas 1.5-2 mm. long, the achene 2-3 mm. long; disk florets sparsely hispid, about 4 mm. long, the limb equaling the tube, the lobes deltoid, the stamens about 2 mm. long, the anthers longer than the filaments; paleae oblong-obovate, 3-4 mm. long, 1.3-1.5 mm. broad, subacute at apex, densely pilose without.

description: Herba perennis, ut videtur subscandens, infloreseentiis exceptis glaber, ramis teretibus flexilibus, pallidis, laevis, eirciter 1.2 mm. diametro, internodiis plerumque 3.5-5 cm. longis; foliis membranaceis, oblongo-ovatis vel late oblongo-lanceolatis, in sieco subolivaceis, utrinque subconcoloribus nitidisque, 8-13 cm. longis, 3.5-5 cm. latis, distanter (5-10 mm.) breviter apiculato-serratis, dentibus angustis, inerassatis, patulis, vix 0.5 mm. longis, nervis primariis utrinque eirciter 7, gracilibus, subtus elevatis, distinctis, curvatoadscendentibus, laxe arcuato-anastomosantibus, reticulis ultimis gracilibus, utrinque elevatis, distinctis; petiolo gracili, 1-1.5 cm. longo; cymis terminalibus axillaribusque, graciliter (1.5-4 cm.) pedunculatis, 3-5 cm. diametro, submultifloris, breviter pubeseentibus; capitulis angustis, 6-7 mm. longis, eirciter 2 mm. diametro, plerumque 5-floris, pedunculis 1-2.5 mm. longis, dense pubeseentibus, bracteis linearibus, 1-1.2 mm. longis; involueri bracteis paucis, binis exterioribus lanceolatis, acuminatis, eirciter 1 mm. longis, interioribus 5, anguste oblongis vel oblongo-ellipticis, eirciter 3.5 mm. longis, 0.6-1.2 mm. latis, obscurissime consperseque pubeseentibus vel glabris, obtusis; floribus plerumque 5, ut videtur flavidis, 3 interioribus, [Mercury symbol], 2 exterioribus 9; floribus Q corolla eirciter 5 mm. longa, tubo glabro, cylindrico, eirciter 3 mm. longo, deorsum gracili, sursum ampliato, lobis oblongis, acutis vel acuminatis, recurvatis, 2 mm. longis, 0.25 mm. latis; antheris 2.5 mm. longis, leviter apiculatis, basi sagittatis, lobis angustissimis; stylus glabris stigmatibus 1 mm. longis, truneatis, minutissime penicillatis; floribus [female] reductis, ligula anguste oblongis, obtusis, vix 0.5 mm. longis, staminibus 0; archeniis subeylindraceis, anguste oblongis, glabris, 1.2 mm. longis (immaturis), setis albidis, scaberulis, 3.5 mm. longis.
bibliographicCitation: Merrill, Elmer D. 1941. Plants Collected on the Vernay-Cutting Expedition. Brittonia. 4 (1): 23-68.

description: Plants short-lived perennials but often flowering the first year; stems 1-several from a branching, subterranean caudex, 3-6 dm tall, the indumentum of the stems predominantly glandular; leaves of the basal rosette spatulate to, oblanceolate, repand- dentate, glandular, 1-6 cm long, 5-16 mm wide, with a broad petiole, the margins conspicuously villous, the upper leaves not markedly reduced, the uppermost entire; inflorescence cymose or racemose; involucre 10-16 mm broad, 10-12 mm high, the involucral bracts lanceolate, acuminate, viscid-villous, often reddish at the tips, 8-10 mm long, 1-3 mm wide; ray corollas yellow, 10-23, retuse; disk corollas campanulate, 5-7 mm long; achenes linear, 6-8 long, the pappus pairs conspicuously dimorphic, the shorter pair 1-2 mm long, the longer pair 2-3 mm long, often tinged reddish.

description: Coarse, robust subshrubs 1.5-2 m tall, from a xylopodium. Leaves opposite; petioles 2-10 mm long; blades 2-7.5x1-3.8 cm, subchartaceous, ovate to elliptic, shortly to very shortly attenuate at the base, acute to shortly acuminate at the apex, margins serru- late to serrate, the adaxial surface búllate, strigose, the abaxial paler, densely tomentose to villous, sparsely so along the veins, 3- nerved, reticulate and pinnately netted distal- ly. Outer phyllaries 6-20 x 2-8 mm, mostly much longer than the inner, spreading, elliptic to narrowly oblong or lanceolate, sometimes slightly indurate and constricted at the base, obtuse, sometimes acute and mucronulate at the apex; inner phyllaries 5-7x2-3 mm, ovate to slightly obovate, obtuse to acute, mucronulate at the apex. Paleae 7-9 xca. 1.2 mm when folded, stramineous, rounded to obtuse or sometimes deltate (1:1 length/ width) at the tip. Ray florets sterile, tube 1- 2 mm long, lamina 8-17x3-6 mm, mostly yellow, rarely purplish along the veins, elliptic to obovate, mostly with deeply cut lobes, sparsely setulose abaxially. Disc florets with corollas 4-5 mm long, sometimes sparsely setulose along the veins and on the abaxial side of lobes. Cypselae 4-4.8*1.5- 2 mm, slightly thickened, subquadrangular, with a tendency for being densely tuberculate, wings 0.5-1 mm wide; pappus with awns reduced to tooth-like projections or less than one half of the cypsela length, crown 0.2- 0.8 mm high, partially fused (usually less than 1/3) with laciniate to fimbriolate or lacerate margins.
bibliographicCitation: Moraes, M. D. & Semir, J. 2009. A revision of Brazilian Dimerostemma (Asteraceae, Heliantheae, Ecliptinae), with a new species and taxonomic adjustments. Brittonia. 61 (4): 341-365.

description: Perennial herb with a stout taproot and branching caudex, the old leaf-bases persistent and becoming fibrous; stem 5-35 cm. high, usually erect or nearly so, grayish-strigose with appressed white hairs; leaves grayish, rather densely strigose, the basal ones tufted, oblanceolate, usually narrowly so, up to 10 cm. long and 7 mm. wide, usually much smaller; cauline leaves reduced and mostly linear, usually not more than 3 cm. long, sometimes few, sometimes rather numerous; heads usually solitary, sometimes as many as 4, the disk 9-16 mm. wide; involuere 5-7 mm. high, caneseently hirtellous with short straight spreading white hairs, sometimes also obscurely glandular; phyllaries strongly imbricate, narrow, sharply acute, with dark midrib, the inner with light-colored margins, the outer usually with a greenish strip on each side of the midrib, with or without strawcolored margins; ligules mostly 30-40, blue or white, 7-12 mm. long, 0.8-1.4 mm. wide; disk-corollas narrow, 3.7-5.6 mm. long, the tube 0.9-1.5 mm., the lobes 0.4-0.5 mm.; style-appendages broadly triangular, obtuse, 0.1-0.15 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 20-25 slender white bristles, the outer of short setae; akenes glabrous, about 8-14-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Perennial herb with an apparently brittle rhizome; stem 2-5 dm. high, glabrous below, rather scantily short-villous under the heads; foliage equable, the cauline leaves ample though sometimes few; basal and lowermost cauline leaves with elliptical or suborbicular blades 2-8 cm. lonig and 1.5-4.5 cm. wide, mostly rather abruptly contracted to the petioles which are 2-12 em. long; middle cauline leaves ovate to cordate, strongly clasping at the base, 2.5-6 cm. long. 1.2-4 cm. wide; upper leaves like the middle ones, but smaller; leaves all quite glabrous except for the ciliate margins, rather thin and membranaceous, entire or with a few irregular teeth, mucronate at the apex; heads apparently always solitary, the disk 6-8 mm. high and 12-20 mm. wide; phyllaries linear, acuminate or attenuate, loose, somewhat herbaceous, 0.7-1.1 mm. wide, glandular, equal, often surpassing the disk and as much as 1 cm. long; ligules about 30-50, 13-25 mm. long, 2-4 mm. wide, white; disk-corollas 4-5 mm. long, narrow and tubular for about a millimeter, distinctly flared above, the lobes about 1 mm. loing; style-appendages or lance-ovate, acute, mostly 0.3-0.4 mm. long; akenes short-hairy, asymmetrically 5-nerved, rarely 4- or 6-nerved; pappus simple, of about 20-30 bristles.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Frutex ad 40 cm. altus valde ramosus ramis vetustis griseis cicatricosis ceteris cum vaginibus foliorum dense imbricatis subsquamosis obtectis. Ramuli terminales erecti valde foliosi congesti, intra axillas foliorum parcissima lana muniti. Folia alterna integra linearia coriacea nitida. acuta 7-9 mm. longa petiolis planis vaginatis ad caulem adpressis imbricatis 2-3 mm. longis 1.2-1.8 mm. latis margine parce ciliato-lanatis supra parcissime indumento lanato deciduo munitis ceteris glabris nitidis, persistentibus. Lamina articulata patentis, subtus dense crasseque lanata sed margines laterales valde plicato-revoluti indumentum cancellantes, aspectu aciculata acuta supra plana utrinque glabra nitida margine (angulo plicaturae) ciliata excepto. Capitula radiata terminalia sessilia mediocria. Involucrum campanulatum circa 7 mm. altum et 5 mm. diam. bracteis viridi-palleaceis 4-5 seriatis lanceolato- linearibus acutissimis dorso uninervis parce arachnoideo-pubescentibus margine scariosis lacerato-ciliatis, interioribus anguste linearibus 6-6.5 mm. longis ad 1 mm. latis. Receptaculum 2 mm. latum alveolatum marginibus alveolorum mem- branaceis dentatis 0.3-0.5 mm. altis. Flores radii feminei ligulati circa 30 corolla alba 10 mm. longa glabra tubulo 2 mm. longo lamina oblonga 1.5 mm. lata, ramis stigmaticis linearibus 0.8 mm. longis glabris, ovario 1.3 mm. longo hispido- villoso sed basim versus glabrato et subapice parce glanduloso, pappo rubello 5 mm. longo pilis hispidulis apice dilatatis sed exterioribus brevioribus (0.5 mm. longis) subpaleaceis. Flores centrales hermaphroditi tubulosi circa 25, corolla 5.5 mm. longa parcissime puberula tubulo 2 mm. longo dentibus oblongis 1 mm. longis apice crasse ciliatis, antheris 2.2 mm. longis basi breviter sagittatis, ramis stigmaticis linearibus semiteretibus extus papilloso.hispidis 1.2 mm. longis, ovario 1.7 mm. longo pappoque cum feminorum floribus similibus. Azuay- Oriente border: Eastern cordillera between Ofia and rio Yacuambi, crest, 10.000-11.200 ft. Shrubs reaching a maximum of 0.4 met. high. Lvs. dark-green. Ray fls. white, disc fls. yellow. Pappus deep salmon red. Collected under the direction of W. H. Camp, F. Prieto P-284 (F, holotype).
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1954. New species of Compositae from Ecuador, collected by W. H. Camp. Brittonia. 8: 39-79.

description: Perennial herb with a loosely branched caudex and a long taproot, the taproot sometimes not preserved in herbarium specimens when the branches of the caudex are very long; stem 2-10 cm. high, glabrous or sparsely strigose, the hairs under the heads longer and sometimes spreading; leaves essentially glabrous, the basal broadly oblanceolate or spatulate, rounded at the apex, up to about 4 cm. long and 7 mm. wide; cauline leaves absent, or represented by two or three mere linear bracts; head solitary, the disk 7-13 mm. wide; involuere 5-8 mm. high, hirsute villous with spreading slightly viscid hairs; phyllaries green below, usually strongly purple above, the inner with broad thin margins, the outer a little shorter than the inner, less purplish, and with narrow or no thin margins; ligules about 15-40, white, about 6-10 mm. long, 1.7-2.7 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.6-4.5 mm. long, the poorly marked tube about 0.9-1.4 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm.; style appendages a little narrower than deltoid, acute, 0.25-0.35 mm. long; pappus of about 25-35 bristles of greatly unequal length and thickness; akenes 2-nerved, short-hairy.

description: Plants annual, 15-35(-58) cm high, divaricate with lower branches decumbent to scarcely branched and suberect, sparsely to densely hirsute, and densely beset with glandular-capitate trichomes; leaves subsessile to petiolate, linear or lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.2-9(-11) cm long, 0.5-1.5 (-3) cm wide, trilobed to pinnately lobed to merely toothed, long-attenuate at the base, sparsely hirsute on both surfaces, occasionally with glandular trichomes, the petioles 0.7-3 cm long; heads campanulate, 1-1.5(-2) cm in diameter, solitary on stout peduncles; peduncles 4-8(-13) cm long, sparsely hirsute, densely pubescent with glandular trichomes, especially near the heads, inflorescence single or sub-cymose, with 2-3 peduncles branching from a node, often secondarily dichotomous above; receptacle convex conical, 2-4 mm across, 2-3 mm high; chaff persistent, scarious, glabrous, 5-6.5(-7) mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, tapering to an attenuate, usually awn-like beak at the apex; involucre 4,(-5)-seriate, outer bracts oblong, green, purple-tinged, 1-3 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, rounded at the apex, glabrate or with short glandular trichomes near the apex; inner bracts progressively longer, the longest oblong, usually obovate, becoming membranous, 6-8(-10) mm long, 3.5-4(-5) mm wide, almost entirely to only partially purple, rounded at the apex, with scarious, purple margins and apex, glabrous, or with glandular trichomes near the apex; ray flowers 6-8, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 3.5-4(-4.5) mm, with conspicuous orange-yellow ligules, these 5.5-8 mm long, 4.5-7 mm wide, reflexed, broadly oblong to suborbicular, 3-loped at the apex; ray corollas with 1-3 linear inner lobelets, these 1-2 mm long; pappus of the ray florets like that of the disc; disc corollas yellow, 4.5-5.5 (-6) mm long, the tube 1.2-1.8(-2) mm long, glabrous to sparsely pilose, the throat narrowly funnelform, 2.5-2.8 mm long, pilose at the base, lobes acute, 0.5-1(-1.5) mm long; description: Shrub or shrublet 1.5-2 m high. Stems terete, densely tawny hirsute. Achenes ca 2 mm long, glabrous or sparsely hispid at or near the apex; pappus of 40-50 sparsely ciliate setae, 3-4 mm long. Chromosome number, 2n = 10 pairs, from the type.

description: Perennial herbs, 2.5-5.8 dm tall, from a stout, woody taproot-like structure, remains of previous stems often visible; stems with strigose to hirsute, golden-brown trichomes. Inflorescences compact to branched scorpioid cymes. Heads 10-21-flowered, sessile. Involucre narrowly campanulate, 5-10 mm high, 4.7-9 mm wide. Phyllaries loosely imbricated in 2 or 3 series, arachnoid to slightly strigose, reddish-purple to brown, the inner ones linear-lanceolate, acute to acu- minate, 4.7-8 mm long, 0.9-1.8 mm wide, the outer ones lanceolate, 1.5-2.8 mm long, 0.4-1 mm wide. Pappus white, the inner bristles 5-10 mm long, the outer scale-like ones 0.7-1.8 mm long. Corollas 7-12.5 mm long, reddish-purple, gla- brous. Anthers 2.5-4.5 mm long. description: Shinners (1947) treated the above two taxa as species and mentioned that K. gracilis "differs [from K. oppositifolia] in little but its more robust appearance, much larger flowering heads (which make it easily dis- tinguishable in the field when both species are found together), and generally deeper color of the corollas." He further noted that the two do not intergrade even when growing together. However, many intermediate populations were observed in eastern Texas and many intermediate forms are also apparent from a wide range of herbarium specimens. Furthermore, several K. gracilis-like specimens also occur in collections from Oklahoma and Louisiana, in spite of Shinners' belief that K. gracilis was confined to central Texas. The characters used by Shinners to distinguish between the two forms are often correlated with microhabitats, such as soil type and water availability. We have extensively surveyed cpDNA and nrDNA variation from 16 populations of this species complex, including five populations of f. gracilis, three intermediate populations, and eight populations of f. cespitosa. DNA data could not segregate any meaningful populational units from this complex (Kim et al., in press, a; Kim & Mabry, 1991). On the other hand, the K. cespitosa species complex was clearly distinguished from its sister species, K. occidentalis, by a large number of mutations (Figs. 20-26). As a result, the two specific taxa recognized by Shinners are reduced to the status of forma. All populations of Krigia cespitosa have a chromosome number of n = 8. The species is widely distributed from southern Virginia to Florida, westward to central Texas, and Nebraska. It is especially abundant in the Gulf Coastal States. A single collection is known from northeastern Mexico (Nuevo Leon, near San Carlos, Nesom 6293, TEX!). The gracilis form occurs mainly in eastern Texas and adjacent Oklahoma, Arkansas, and Louisiana.

description: Spreading shrubs, 2.5 m tall; stems with branches slender, striate, glabrous to strigose, hairs 1 mm long, internodes 3-12 cm long. Capitulescences paniculiform, on terminal branches. Capitula sessile or short-pedicellate, subglobose, 3.5-4.5 mm high, 3-3.5 mm diam.; phyllaries 4, 3.5-4 X 3-3.5 mm, ovate-suborbicular, 5-veined, apices obtuse, distal half strigose, hairs 0.6 mm long, margins ciliate on distal one-third. Staminate fiorets 8-11, subtended by ovate-lanceolate paleae, 3-3.5 X 1.5-2 mm, apices scarcely ciliate, 2-veined; corollas 3 mm long, 0.5 mm diam., white, 5-lobed, lobes deltoid, 0.4 mm long, apices scarcely pubescent; anthers 1.5 mm long, black; ovaries 2 mm long, 1.5 mm diam., pilose toward apex. Cypselae obovoid, with short ring-shaped apical projection, bases rounded, pilose at distal one-third, hairs 1.1-5 mm long. Chromosome number, n = 16 (Stuessy & Arriagada, 1993).

description: Basally woody perennial herbs or subshrubs 40-90 cm tall, mostly caespitose from a xylopodium. description: Cormo circa 1.5 cm. crasso, caule 5-10 cm. alto, subtus glabro, superne crispati-pubeseente; foliis inferioribus anguste lineari- oblanceolatis, 1-1.5 dm. longis, 4-5 mm. latis, glabris; spica 1.5-2 dm. longa, densissima; capitulis circa 1 cm. altis, 7-10-floris; bracteis pur- puraseentibus, puberulis atque ciliatis, acutis; exterioribus ovatis, vix squarrosis; interioribus lanceolati-oblongis, crispatis apicibus paten- tibus; corollis roseo-purpureis; acheniis 4 mm. longis, hirsutulis; pappo barbellato, fusco, 6-7 mm. longo.

description: Herbaceous perennial having a woody caudex and tuberously thickened rhizomes; stems erect to 60 cm, pubescent with white uniseriate hairs and sometimes with black capitate trichomes interspersed; leaves distinctly petiolate, petioles to 8 mm long, blades lanceolate to ovate, 2.5-8 cm long, 0.7-5 cm wide, apex acute, base attenuate, cuneate to nearly truncate; inflorescence a compact cyme, peduncles to 3 cm long; heads radiate; involucres turbinate to campanulate 4.5-6 mm high, 3.5-5 mm wide, phyllaries imbricate, 2-3 seriate, elliptic to ovate, apex obtuse, subequal, striate; receptacle sub- conical; palea spatulate or gradually ampliate upward, entire or with 1-2 short lateral lobes; rays 1-7, corolla tube pubescent with ascending 2-5-celled uniseriate trichomes, ligules white, quadrate to obovate, ca. 9 mm long and ca. 6 mm wide, 3-lobed; disk florets ca. 20, corolla yellow, tube flaring into a tubular throat, pubescent with 2-5-celled uniseriate ascending hairs, ray and disk achenes similar, obconical, ca. 2 mm long, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Urbatsch, Lowell E. & Turner, Billie L. 1976. New species and combinations in Sabazia (Heliautheae, Galinoginae). Brittonia. 27: 348-354.

description: Plants perennial (?), 35-65 cm high; stems erect, 1 to several from a suffruticose base, glabrous, striate, minutely glandular-punctate; leaves alternate, pinnately dissected into linear-filiform divisions 0.5-1 mm wide, glabrous, glandular-punctate; upper leaves few-parted and often simple; petioles 10-30 mm long; inflorescence a loose-flowered cyme of 3-8 heads; heads turbinate, discoid, 5-6 mm across, 9-10 mm hiah (including the projecting florets), 10- to 20-flowered, on slender, glabrous peduncles 20-50 mm long; principal involueral bracts 4-6, obovate, 6-7 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, glandular-punctate and glabrous, with white or rose-tinged membranous margins, broadly obtuse or rounded at the apex; florets "white," according to data from labels (Heiser described the florets as "yellow"), zygomorphic; corolla 4-5 mm long (including the lobes), the tube glandular-pubescent, 1.5 mm long, the throat funnelform, the lobes 0.5-1 mm long, unequal; style branches flattened, recurved, 1-1.2 mm long, stigmatose from the base, abruptly terminated at the apex with a somewhat swollen, acute appendage; achenes obpyramidal, 4-sided, 3-4 mm long, sparsely pubeseent, especially below; pappus of 7-10 lanceolate, paleaceous scales 3-4 mm long, the mid-nerve of each extending into a fine awn.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1962. Taxonomy of Hymenothriz (Helenicae, Compositae). Brittonia. 14: 101-120.

description: Perennial herb from a branched caudex densely clothed with the remnants of previous years' leaves, forming loose mats to 3 dm across, spreading-pubescent nearly throughout with a mixture of short, brownish-glandular and longer, whitish non glandular hairs; lower leaves spreading to erect, oblanceolate to spatulate, 1.6-4.0 cm long, 0.6-1.2 cm wide, mostly dentate above the middle with up to 6 pairs of coarse lateral teeth, strongly 1-nerved with 2 faint lateral veins from the base to near the tip; cauline leaves gradually reduced upward, sessile, appressed to slightly spreading, oblanceolate to oblong with some small lateral dentations; stems numerous, erect or ascending, 0.8-1.9 (2.3) dm high; heads up to 11 per stem, narrowly campanulate, discoid, subtended by 1 or 2 reduced leaves; phyllaries 22-26, more or less in 3 unequal series, 1-nerved, oblong, the outer ones acute, green, glandular-pubescent, 2.2-4.0 mm long, the inner obtuse to submucronate, green-tipped, glandular-pubescent only toward the tip, with hyaline minutely fimbriate margins, to 6 mm long; receptacle convex, naked; disc florets (13) 15-16 (19), (3.9) 4.2-5.0 mm long, slenderly funnelform, with a few hairs below the middle, fertile; style branches deeply cleft, 1.5-2.0 mm long, the appendages about equaling the stigmatic portion; pappus bristles in a single series, white, short-barbellate, slightly surpassing the corolla lobes; achenes fusiform, 2.0-2.9 mm long, white-hairy, 3-angled, compressed.
bibliographicCitation: Tiehm, Arnold G. & Shultz, Leila M. 1985. A new Haplopappus (Asteraceae: Astereae) from Nevada. Brittonia. 37: 165-168.

description: Perennial herb with a much-branched moderately slender caudex; stem slender, 3-15 cm. high, sparsely strigose, the base conspicuously smooth, shining, somewhat enlarged and indurated, and usually straw-colored; leaves, except for some scattered small ones in tall forms, all in a basal cluster, narrowly linear, mostly 1.5-6 cm. long, 0.5-1.0 mm. wide, sparsely to moderately strigose, the lowermost ones with the bases enlarged, shining, and somewhat membranous or indurated; head solitary, small, the disk 6-11 mm. wide; involuere 3.5-5 mm. high, equaling or usually shorter than the disk, sparsely or moderately strigose and somewhat glutinous; phyllaries imbricate, the short outer ones narrow, rather thick or firm, the inner ones broader, with searious and usually erose margins, merely acute or abruptly acuminate; ligules about 15-20, blue or pink, about 6-9 mm. long and 1.3-1.8 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.4-5.0 mm. long, the tube 0.6-1.0 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.6 mm.; style-appendages deltoid, acute or acutish, about 0.15-0.25 mm. long; pappus of about 20-30 slender but firm obscurely barbellate bristles, occasionally with a few slender outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely strigose, sometimes glabrous below or throughout.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Rhizomatous perennial. Stems erect, slender, to 80 cm tall, terete, lanulose, green, sometimes tinged brown; upper part branches forming a large loose compound corymb. Leaves opposite; lamina herbaceous, narrowly deltoid, trinerved, 30-50 X 20-35 mm in the middle part of stems, acute at apex, truncate at base, crenate with ca. 10 pairs of teeth along margin, sparsely hispidulous and punctate-glandular (yellow) on both surfaces, sometimes having stipitate red-purple glands, whitish green below; petioles winged, 15-25 mm long. Heads many, 8-10 X 5-6 mm, shortly pedunculate, in many small corymbs; each corymb 5-15 mm wide consisting of a few to ca. 10 heads. Inflorescence branches and peduncles stipitate-glandular mixed with some short woolly hairs. Phyllaries ca. 5 mm long, acuminate at apex, pale green, stipitate-glandular (yellow or red-purple) with a few sessile yellow glands outside. Corolla white, sometimes pale pink, sparsely puberulous and with a few yellow glands scattered outside; tubes ca. 5 mm long; lobes ca. 2 mm long. Achenes ca. 2.5 mm long, hispid. Pappus scales membranous, almost completely united into a crown of fine-pectinate margin, ca. 0.3 mm high, not awned.
bibliographicCitation: Soejima, A., et al. 2001. Thirteen new species and two new combinations of Stevia (Asteraceae: Eupatorieae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 53: 377-395.

description: Planta ad 3 m alta; caule dense et molliter piloso; pilis appressis vel dis- tentis, ad 3 mm longis; foliis alternis; petiolis 4 cm longis; laminis ovatis, 10 cm longis, 7 cm latis, cuneatis vel subcordatis, longo-acuminatis apice, crenato- serratis, supra dense brevi-pilosis, infra dense molliter piloso-tomentosis, pilis flexuosis, distentis; capitulis 3-5; pedunculis 1.5-12.0 cm longis; disco 1.5- 2.0 cm in diam.; phyllariis ovatis vel ovato-lanceolatis, 1.5 cm longis, 4 mm latis, acutiusculis, nigro-viridibus, in margine ciliolatis, sparse pilosis vel prope glabris; radiis ca. 21, 2.5 cm longis, 1.0 cm latis; corollis disci flaviis, 7 mm longis, dentibus nigrescentibus, sparse hispidulis vel pilosiusculis; colum- nis antheris nigris; receptaculi paleis acutis, prope glabris, apice nigro-viridibus; achaeniis 3.5 mm longis cum maculiatris; pappi aristis 2 vel 3, lineari-lanceolatis, 3-4 mm longis, squamella una vel pluribus; pappo radiotum ca. 10 squa- mellis laceratis.
bibliographicCitation: Heiser, Charles B. 1957. A revision of the South American Species of Helianthus. Brittonia. 8: 283-285.

description: Herb 3-25 cm tall, diffusely branched from the base and above or rarely simple; glabrous or sparsely pubescent throughout, especially on the peduncle and involucre; lower leaves 3-6 cm long, pinnately parted with 4-5 pairs of short lobes or rarely simple; upper leaves gradually reduced; involucre 5-6 mm high, the 6-10 ovate phyllaries curved over the disk after flowering and reflexed when achenes are ripe; ray florets 6-13, much exceeding the phyllaries, yellow (rarely white) with yellow stigmas; disk florets 20-70, 5-merous, yellow, their stigmas and pollen white or rarely yellow; achenes 2.5-3 mm long, angled; n = 7; self-incompatible.
bibliographicCitation: Ornduff, Robert. 1964. Biosystematics of Blennosperma (Composiatae). Brittonia. 16: 289-295.

description: Herba ad 60 cm. alta, caudice subterraneo; foliis densissimis tenuiter coriaceis oblongo-spathulatis, 15-23 cm. longis, 8-15 mm. latis, basin versus ad 3 mm. angustatis, ad vaginam coriaceam eirciter 1 cm. latain dilatatis, apice acutis vel subacutis, margine integris et planis, utrinque dense argenteo-sericeis, nervis obscuratis; ramis floriferis 20-30-capitulatis e caudice erectis ad 60 cm. longis argenteosericeis vel tomentosis, copiose ramosis, ramis gracilibus alternatis vel suboppositis, bracteis oblongo-linearibus 3-6 cm. longis et eirciter 3 mm. latis subtentis; capitulis maturitate 15-20 mm. diametro corymboso- paniculatis, pedunculis gracilibus maturitate 3-7 cm. longis; involuero eirciter 2-seriato, phyllaribus 15-20 oblongis vel oblongolanceolatis, 6-8 mm. longis, 2-3 mm. latis, apice subacutis, extra pilis 1.5-2 mm. longis dense ferrugineo- vel aureo-sericeis; floribus radii 40-60, 2- vel 3-seriatis, lamina oblonga, eirciter 7 mm. longa et 1.8 mm. lata, basi pilos pallidos delicatulos eirciter 0.3 mm. longos gerente, achenio trigono eirciter 2 mm. longo; floribus disci stramineis glabris eirciter 6 mm. longis, tubo quam limbo breviore, lobis deltoideis eirciter 0.8 mm. longis; staininibus leviter exsertis, filamentis antheras subaequantibus; stylo exserto; paleis submembranaceis oblongis velobovatis eirciter 5 mm. longis et 2 mm. latis, apice obtusis, apicem versus extra hispidulis, pilis eirciter 0.5 mm. longis.

description: Folia submembranacea sessilia obovato-oblonga basim versus attenuata apice angustata acutissime cuspidata, margine argute serrata, supra sparse piloso-scabrida nervis paulo conspicuis, subtus tenuiter arachnoidea costa crassa pubescenti-tomentella, nervis secundariis patulis extremo arcuatis pubes- centibus, venulis discoloribus minute reticulatis. Capitula radiata pedicellata in magnis paniculis floribundis dispositia. Pedicelli 10-30 mm longi valde graciles flexuosi sparse glanduloso-puberuli et araneosi, bracteolis capillaribus flexuosis brevibus praediti, 3-5 ad basim involucri ad modum calyculi. Involucrum hemisphaericum 4-5 mm altum 13 bracteis ovatis acuminatis 4 mm longis 1.5-2mm latis apice ciliatis margine scariosis dorso parce glandulosis araneosisque. Flores-radii feminei ligulati 9-10, corolla glabra lutea 8-9 mm longa tubulo 2.5-3 mm longo lamina elliptico-oblonga 2.5-3 mm lata. Flores disci hermaphroditi circa 40, corolla lutea 6 mm longa, antheris 2 mm basi obtusis, ramis styli truncatis. Ovarium glabrum pappus albo-sericeus 5-6 mm longus.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1956. Studies on Andean Compositae - III. Brittonia. 8 (3): 179-193.

description: Perennial herb with a branched caudex, these branches moderately slender and usually fairly long, arising from a definite central axis or taproot; stem mostly 1 dm. high or less, rarely up to 1.5 dm., glabrous or usually sparsely strigose, a little more densely strigose under the solitary head; mature leaves glabrous or nearly so, sometimes with a few very fine and inconspicuous short strigose hairs; basal leaves spatulate or obovate to merely oblanceolate, rounded or retuse at the tip, usually more or less abruptly contracted to the petiole, sometimes gradually tapering, up to 7 cm. long and 15 mm. wide, usually considerably less, the base enlarged, membranous, light-colored or rarely a little purplish; cauline leaves reduced, usually several, the lower commonly oblanceolate and obtuse or rounded at the tip, the upper linear and acutish; head solitary, the disk about 7-13 mm. wide; involucre 4-6 mm. high, finely glandular; phyllaries slightly or moderately imbricate, purple or purplish at the tips or more commonly throughout, the outer, at least, mostly linear-oblong and with nearly parallel sides to above the middle; ligules about 15-60, deep blue or occasionally nearly white, about 6-11 mm. long and 1.5-2.5 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.2-4.4 mm. long, the tube obscure, 0.7-1.0 mm. long, the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm.; style-appendages ovate to a little narrower than deltoid, acute or acutish, 0.15-0.3 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 15-25 fragile bristles, evidently shorter than the corolla, the outer of inconspicuous short setae; akenes 2-nerved, short-hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herba annua 4 cm alta. Folia opposita, ovata vel elliptica rhomboidea, mlargiine crenulata vel undulata; lamina 1.5-4 mm lata, 1.5-4 mm longa; petiolo tenui 0.5-1.5 mm longo. Capitulae in cyinibus paniculatis interdum axillaribus aggregatae; pedunculis monocephalis 1.5-3 mm longis. Capitula discoidea, campanulata, 1-2 mm lata, 1.5-2 mm alta. Flores hermaphroditi, 3-7, fertiles, regulares. Corolla 4-lobata, alba. Achaenia 0.3-0.4 mm lata, 0.6-0.8 mm longa, nigra, 8-10-costata.
bibliographicCitation: King, Robert M. 1965. Piqueriopsis, a new genus of Compositae from southwestern Mexico. Brittonia. 17: 352, 353.

description: Delicate annuals, to 4 cm high; taproots minute, few branched, glabrate to sparingly short-pilose, 0.3-0.5 mm thick; stems single, erect, strict or few branched, striate, 0.3-0.5 mm thick, glabrate to sparingly short-pilose, the basal portioin reddish, paniculately branched above; leaves thin, glabrate to sparingly shortpilose, opposite, ovate to elliptic-rhombic, the margins crenulate to undulate; blades 1.5-4 mm broad, 1.5-4 mm long; petioles 0.5-1.5 mm long; heads arranged in compound cymes, these paniculate or sometimes axillary; peduncles monocephalic, 1.5-3.0 mm long, heads discoid, campanulate, 1-2 mm broad, 1.5-2 mm high, 3-7-flowered, receptacle convex to hemispherical, naked; phyllaries (4-) 5-6, in 2 series, striate, thin, obovate to oblanceolate, the apex obtuse to acute, slightly fimbriate, 1-1.5 mm broad, 1-1.5 mm long; florets perfect, fertile, regular, 4-lobed, white, the throat campanulate, the tubular portion with multicellular glands, the base with numerous short tapered bristles ca 25 µ wide, 125-175 µ long; stamens 4, the anthers obtuse, 50-60 µ long, the filaments 40-50 µ wide, 450-500 µ long; style branches 2, spathulate, papillate on the inner surface, 0.25-0.3 mm long, 65-140 µ in diameter, the style tube 750-800 µ long, 75-90 µ in diameter; pappus lacking; achenes narrowly ellipsoid, 0.3-0.4 mm thick, 0.6-0.8 min long, dark brown to black, 8-10-ribbed.
bibliographicCitation: King, Robert M. 1965. Piqueriopsis, a new genus of Compositae from southwestern Mexico. Brittonia. 17: 352, 353.

description: Branched shrub, 2 m tall; stems with branches striate, pilose hairs 0.5-1 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate to ovate-lanceolate, membraneous, 8-15 X 4- 8 cm, apices largely acuminate, bases attenuate, margins shortly serrate to serrulate; adaxial surface glabrous to shortly strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long, abaxial surface glabrous; petioles 1-2.5 cm long, strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Capitulescences thyrsoid, trichotomously divided, branches slightly striate, strigose. Capitula subglobose, 3 mm high, 2 mm diam., sessile or shortly pedicellated; phyllaries 3, ovate to suborbicular, 3 X 2-2.5 mm, apices acute, abaxially short pilose, hairs 0.3 mm long, margin shortly ciliate on distal one-third, 7-veined. Pistillate florets 10-14, subtended by ovate to oblong-ovate paleae, 3 X 2 mm, 7-veined, shortly pilose, hairs 0.4 mm long, margins shortly ciliate on distal one-third; corollas white, glabrous, 1.5 mm long, 0.5 mm diam., 3-lobed, lobes 0.3 mm long, glabrous; styles 1.5 mm long, branches 0.5 mm long. Staminate florets 10-11, subtended by lanceolate paleae, 2.5 X 1-1.5 mm, 3-veined; corollas tubulate, white, 1.5 mm long, 0.5 mm diam., 3-lobed, lobes irregularly deltoid, 0.4 mm long, glabrous; anthers black, 1 mm long; ovaries 1.5 mm long, 0.5 mm diam., glabrous. Cypselae obovoid, 1.5-2 X 1-1.4 mm, rounded at base, glabrous (exceptionally scarcely pilose at apex). Chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Arriagada, J. E. 2003. Revision of the genus Clibadium (Asteraceae, Heliantheae). Brittonia. 55: 245-301.

description: Herbaceous perennial to 20 cm tall; stems slim 3-4 cm long, sparsely pubescent, unwinged. Leaves basal, alternate; blades obovate to spatulate, tapering narrowly to the stem, to 8.5 cm long and 1 .5 cm wide, margins entire or irregularly serrulate, ciliate, apex rounded or apiculate, pubescence sparse above and below with long delicate hairs, denser on the main veins. Capitula 3.5-4 mm in diam, fewer than 12 per plant, solitary on slender, hispidulous pedicels to 10 cm long. Involucre 1-2-seriate; outer bracts linear-lanceolate, 1.7-2.1 mm long, 0.4-0.5 mm wide, pubescent, margins ciliate, apex broadly acute, base indurate; inner bracts longer, grading into the pales. Paleae linear-oblanceolate, 2.1-2.2 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm wide, keeled, pubescent on upper 1/3, apex acute, herbaceous. Receptacle hemispheric. Ray florets 11-13, ligules yellow, glabrous, 2.6-2.9 mm long, 0.9-1.1 mm wide, apex 2-dentate, tube glabrous, 0.4-0.6 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide. Disc florets ca 25, corolla yellow, glabrous, funnelform, 1-1.3 mm long, 0.7-1 mm wide, tube glabrous, 0.5-0.6 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, anthers black, apical appendages acute, style branches acute. Ray and disc achenes similar, brown to black, 1.6-1.9 mm long, 0.8-0.9 mm wide, sparsely pubescent to glabrous, wings narrow, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, ciliate, pappus usually of 2 unequal awns, the longer always present, 1.9-2.3 mm long, strongly recurved at the tip, a second awn occasionally absent but generally present and very reduced, 0.1-0.2 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Olsen, John S. 1986. Revision of Verbesina section Verbesina (Asteraceae: Heliantheae). Brittonia. 38: 362-368.

description: Coarse, robust subshrubs up to 1.5 m tall, from a xylopodium. Leaves opposite; petioles 5-13 mm long; blades 5-9x3.5-6.5 cm ovate to broadly ovate, rounded to truncate or subcordate at the base, very shortly acuminate to acute at the apex, margins minutely serrulate, adaxial surface sparsely pillóse, the abaxial paler, more densely pillóse to subvelutinous. Outer phyllaries 10-25x5-14 mm, elliptic; inner phyllaries 6-8x3-5 mm, elliptic to obovate or oblong, sometimes constricted at the base. Paleae 6-7 x ca. 1 mm when folded, with an obtuse to acute tip up to 1 mm long. Ray florets sterile, tube 0.5-1 mm long, lamina 15-17x5-7 mm, elliptic to oblong or obovate, sparsely setullose abaxially. Disc florets with corollas 3.5- 4.5 mm long, lobes glabrous or with a few trichomes abaxially. Cypselae ca. 3 x 1.3 mm, thickened, subquadrangular, tuberculate at maturity, wingless or wings much reduced to a narrow margin; pappus awnless or sometimes with awns much reduced to tooth- like projections ca. 0.2 mm long, crown reduced to a minutely erose margin.

description: Caulis (basi inflorescentiae) subteres multistriatus nigreseenti-olivaceus glaber; folia (basi infloreseentiae) ovata petiolata obtusa basi late rotundata v. vix cordata remote crenata submarginata plana coriacea 5-plinervia supra saturate viridia glaberrima lucida subtus obscure viridia subtilissime stipitato-glandulosa pilis paueis longioribus multiloculatis intermixtis; panicula oblonga ca. 20 cm. longa 7 cm. lata crispe brunneo-pilosula usque medium foliaceo-bracteata, ramis erectiusculis, pedicellis saepius 4-5 mm. longis bracteolam linearem 3 mm. longam gerentibus; capitula fructifera 7-8 mm. alta; involueri ca. 5 mm. longi phyllaria oblonga obtusa substraminea pilosula; corolla ca. 3.9 mm. longa, tubo 1.5 mm., fauce anguste campanulata 1.1 mm., delitibus 1.3 mm. longis; achenia inter costas dense sessili-glandulosa in costis sparse crispe puberula.

description: Stem (at base of infloreseence) 3 mm. in diameter, with lnearly or quite solid white pith, glabrous and shining; leaves opposite; petioles (of leaves at base of inflorescence) essentially glabrous, suleate above, 6 mm. long; blades 3.2 cm. long, 2.3 cm. wide, remotely crenate (teeth about 3 pairs), 5-plinerved within 2 mm. of base, the upper pair of nerves much the stronger and reaching practically to tip of leaf, the principal veins prominulous on both sides, the secondaries impressed on upper surface, scarcely prominulous beneath, translucent, the lower surface of leaf appearing glabrous to the eye but rather densely stipitate-glandular (the glands set in little pits) and with sparse longer several-celled hairs; heads eymose-panicled on the branches of the essentially isodiametric panicle, this crisp-pilosulous with many-celled eglandular hairs; pedicels 2-6 mm. long, usually bearing a little below the head an obtuse linear-spatulate bractlet about 3 mm. long; phyllaries few-nerved, thinly pilosulous with many-celled brownish hairs over most of their exposed surface, thickened at base but not calearate; achenes 3 mm. long, olivaceous, 5-ribbed, sometimes with a weak additional rib on one face; corollas sessile-glandular toward apex of tube, otherwise glabrous; pappus somewhat yellowish-white, 3.8 mm. long, equaling the corolla, the bristles about 45, hispidulous except toward the not obviously enlarged apex.

description: Annual erect to spreading herb up to 1.5 dm high; stems hirsute-hispid, especially on younger branches, reddish-brown, striated, mostly terete but sometimes somewhat flattened; leaves opposite, sessile or subsessile with connate bases sheathing the stem, variably shaped, generally entire, but sometimes minutely toothed, variably pubescent but mostly hispid on both surfaces, up to ca. 2.5 cm long and 1 cm wide but variable; peduncles hispid, slender, of variable length, slightly flaring at apex, heads solitary, terminal, campanulate to subhemispherical, generally less than 4 mm wide; phyllaries uniseriate, inconstant in number but generally 5-11, lance-linear, more hispid on the basal half, up to ca. 3.5 mm long, hyaline alae up to ca. 2.0 mm long with erose apices; ray flowers about equalling or slightly exceeding the phyllaries in length, the corolla pale yellow to orange, 2-lobed, glabrous, ca. 1.5 mm long with a 0.5 mm tube, ray style bifid, branches recurved, apices acute; ray achene slightly shorter than the corolla, glabrous, slightly compressed, minutely striate, black when mature, narrowly obovate; disk flowers numerous, corollas yellow, 5- or rarely 4-lobed, with a pubescent basal constriction, ca. 1.3 mm long; disk achene ca. 1 mm long, glabrous, obovate to turbinate, minutely striate, shiny black when mature; paleae broadly obovate or oblanceolate to linear, hyaline, more or less persistent on the receptacle, glabrous except for the ciliated margins, apices acute to subacuminate; receptacle conical; 2n = 36.

description: Shrub or small tree; stems unwinged, reddish, densely pilose with spreading hairs. Leaves alternate; blades ovate-lanceolate to ovate elliptic, 6-12 cm long, 2.5-4.0 cm wide, apex acuminate, base abaxially revolute, tapering to a thinly winged petiole, margin serrate to serratulate, teeth sometimes glandular-tipped, hirsutellous with appressed hairs above, spreading pilose below, hairs on principal veins distinctly reddish; petiole 1-2.5 cm long. Capitulescence cymose to paniculate with 4-12 heads borne on tomentose peduncles to 5 cm long (mostly less than 3 cm). Involucre hemispheric, 2 seriate; outer bracts ovate lanceolate, pubescent, 3.8-4.7 mm long, 1.7-2.3 mm wide, apex broadly acute, base not indurate; inner bracts longer, grading into the pales. Pales 5.6-7.5 mm long, 1.4-2.4 mm wide, distinctly keeled, pubescent along the keel and upper 1/3, apex acute, subherbaceous. Ray florets 13-18, ligule white or cream, unlobed, 8.5-9.6 mm long, 3.0-4.1 mm wide, tube pubescent, 1.3-2.5 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm wide. Disc florets ca 75, corolla cream colored, cylindric, 3.5-4.0 mm long, 0.8-1.0 mm wide, glabrous, tube 0.7-1.1 mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm wide, pubescent. Ray achenes immature, black, 4-angled, to 3.1 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, glabrous or with a few hairs on the ribs, winged by 2 narrow, ciliate wings to 0.2 mm broad; pappus of 2 (1) unequal awns to 4.1 mm long with thickened bases. Disc achenes immature, black, 4-angled, to 3.8 mm long, 1.2 mm wide, glabrous, ciliate along the ribs, wings not developed; pappus of 2 unequal awns to 4.2 mm long with thickened bases.
bibliographicCitation: Olsen, John S. 1982. Two new species of Verbesina section Ochractinia (Asteraceae) from South America. Brittonia. 34: 282-284.

description: Rhizomes horizontal, slender, 1.5-2.5 mm. thick, dark brown, with conspicuous slender roots; innovations frequent, the leaves similar to the lower cauline ones; stems occurring singly, 3-5(2-6) dm. high, unbranched below, occasionally red tinged, lanate-villous (sometimes sparingly so) toward the base, overeovering short-stipitate glands, becoming less pilose and more conspicuously long-stipitate-glandular and scabrid-puberulent above; cauline leaves 2-3 (4) pairs, much reduced upwards, the lowermost largest, with blades 5-20 cm. long, 2-4 cm. broad, lanceolate, acutely or abruptly drawn to a narrowly winged petiole, evenly callous denticulate or entire, sparingly to densely villous on both surfaces, short-stipitate-glandular on the upper surface; inflorescence cymose, the lateral peduncles upwardly arcuate; heads 3(1)-9(16), turbinate-campanulate, nodding in the bud; periclinium longand short-stipitate-glandular, and coarsely and moderately pilose; involuere 2-ranked, the bracts 12-20, lanceolate, acute, sparingly glandular, puberulent and ciliolate towards the tip; rays wanting or rarely well developed, normally present in one subspecies; disc flowers yellow, 7.5-9 mm. long, vaseshaped the tube 2.5(2.1)-3.0(3.5) mm. long, the limb 5.5(5.0)-6.0(6.2) mm. long, the tube and the base of the limb pilose, the collar conspicuous; achelles 4.5 (4.2) -5.5 (6.0) mm. long, strongly angled aind striate, bronze-black, glabrous, hirsute onily above, or uniformly hirsute with double hairs, frequently also sparsely short-stipitate-glandular; annulus short; pappus usually exceeding the corolla, stramineous or mostly tawny, barbellate to subplumose, the setae 0.15-0.25(0.3) mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Camp, Wendell H. & Gilly, Charles L. 1943. Part II: Systematic Treatment, [Arnica alpina-Arnica discoidea]. Brittonia. 4 (3): 405-457.

description: Perennial herb with a stout taproot and superficial or nearly superficial rootcrown; stems erect or nearly so, often a little woody at the base, 1-10 dm. high, usually unbranched at the base, except in var. con fiis and sometimes var. hartwegi, the base occasionally somewhat rhizomatous, but if so, then either very short, or relatively stout and more than 1.5 mm. thick, or both; stem varying from glabrous to commonly coarsely strigose or appressed-hirsute, to spreading-puberulent or spreading-hirtellous, or even spreading-hirsute; leaves numerous, more or less crowded, generally several times longer than the internodes, all nearly alike, without a conspicuous basal tuft, and only very gradually reduced upwards, varying from linear-filiform and less than 1 mm. wide to narrowly oblong and 5-6 mm. wide, rarely as much as 10 mm. wide, and from about 1 cm. to 8 cm. long, the base only slightly narrowed and not at all chaffy, the surfaces varying from essentially glabrous to more or less strigose, or loosely hirsute, or spreading-hirtellous, the margins often with stout subconical hairs; heads generally several or numerous in a corymbiform leafy or subnaked infloreseence, often solitary in var. confinis; disk about 10-18 mm. wide; involuere 4-7 mm. high, varying from nearly glabrous to more or less densely hirtellous or short-hirsute, often also more or less glandular, or merely glandular and not hairy; phyllaries evidently imbricate, narrow, linear-subulate, acuminate, greenish, or the inner somewhat straw-colored, with brown midrib; ligules about 15-65, generally blue, about 5-15 mm. long, 1.0-2.7 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.0-6.5 mm. long, the tube about 0.9-1.5 mm., the lobes about 0.5-0.8 mm.; style-appendages varying from truncate to broadly triangular and obtuse, or sometimes deltoid and acute, 0.05-0.2 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 20-33 sordid barbellate bristles, the outer of a few inconspicuous setae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely hairy or sometimes glabrous. Dry, often rocky places, or in waste land; from southwestern Oregon, through California, to Baja California; common.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Shrubs, 20-25 cm high, much branched from a crown, stems herbaceous, foliose, ending in a bracteose peduncle. Leaves alternate, spathulate, glabrous; with petioles 2-3 cm long; blades obovate, 2.5-4 X 1.5-2 cm, glands spherical and multicellular on both surfaces, margins denticulate and slightly undulated. Heads radiate, 3-4 cm diam.; ray florets ca. 36, disk florets 115. Peduncles 12-13 cm long, bracts 4-5. Involucre 13 mm high, bracts in 7 series; bracts glabrous, glandular; external bracts triangular, 3 mm X 1.5 mm; internal bracts elliptic, 10 mm X 3 mm. Rayflorets pistillate, yellow, fertile; corolla 18 mm long, limb 4.5 mm wide. Disk florets perfect, yellow, corolla 4.5 mm long. Pappus of disk and ray florets of 5-6 awns, caducous, 4 mm long, white. Achenes elliptic, winged, flattened, glabrous, 4-5 mm long, straw colored.

description: Perennial herbs 0.2-0.5 m high. Stems terete, striate, tawny lanose to glabrate, mostly single and unbranched, arising from slender rhizomes. Leaves mostly basal, 10-20 cm long, 5-10 cm wide; petiole 2-8 cm long, densely but loosely tawny lanose; blade cordate to broadly elliptic, palmately to pinnately veined, tomentose on both surfaces, more so below, the margins weakly 6-13 lobed to undulate or seemingly entire with remote apiculations. Capitulescences a terminal, nearly naked, corymbose-panicle of 5-50 heads borne above the leaves. Heads broadly turbinate, radiate; involucre biseriate, 5-6 mm long; bracts 8, glabrous, equal, lanceolate to elliptic-ovate, somewhat thickened, the inner series broader and with scarious margins; calyculus of 1-4 loose bracts 1-2 mm long. Receptacle planar, ca 0.8 mm across, alveolate. Ray florets 3 or 5, pistillate, fertile; corollas yellow; tube 4-4.5 mm long, glabrous; ligule 6-10 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, 2-4 nervate. Disk florets 10-25; corolla yellow, glabrous; tube 2.5-3 mm long; limb funnelform, 3.5-4 mm long, the throat ca 1.5 mm long, the lobes 2-2.8 mm long, 2-3 times as long as wide. Achenes columnar, 3-4 mm long, glabrous or sparsely hispid above; pappus of numerous white, ciliate setae, 5-6 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1985. TWO new species of Senecio section Palmatinervii (Asteraceae) from northeastern Mexico. Brittonia. 37: 117-120.

description: Rhizomes dark brown, 2.5 (2)-4 (5) mm. thick, short, branched, conspicuously clothed with coarse rootlets, the whole forming a loose approximate crown, each branch producing a single stem; innovations frequently and vigorously developed, the leaves oblanceolate, petiolate; stems unbranched, 3(2)-4(5) mm. thick, striate, 2(1.5)-5(6.5) dm. high, scantily scabridpuberulent to rather conspicuously pilose with weak septate and sometimes moniliform hairs, and also frequently more or less conspicuously long- and short-stipitate-glandular; eauiline leaves 3(2-4) pairs (excluding the occasional pair of much reduced spathulate leaves at the stem base), the lowermost usually largest, all sessile or the lower abruptly or gradually narrowed into a well defined petiole, the blades ovate (rarely suborbicular) elliptic, lanceolate to oblanceolate or obovate, acute or obtuse, the margins irregularly and inconspicuously denticulate, occasionally conspicuously serrate, or subentire, the lower surface glabrate and the upper sparsely granular-glalldular, or generally both sides obviously stipitate-glandular and frequently also sparsely or moderately pilose with weak septate hairs; peduncles coarse, 5-10(20) cm. long, more or less pubescent with septate hairs and short- and long-stipitate-glandular, sometimes scantily so, rarely only scabrid-glandular and puberulent; heads 1-3 (5), hemispheric-campanulate frequently broader than high, 15(13)-18(20) mm. high; perielinium broad, short, sparsely to moderately pilose with septate or moniliform white hairs and also long-stipitate-glandular, rarely only scabrid-glandular and puberulent; involueral bracts 18-22, lanceolate to obanceolate, 12-14 mm. long, 2(1.5)-3 mm. broad, usually conspicuously acuminate, red-tinged towards the apex, sparsely or conspicuously moniliform pilose at the base, stipitate-glandular, and sometimes glandular-ciliolate above; ray corollas 14-18 (22), the ligules yellow, sometimes deeply so, 6 (4)-9 mm. broad, 18 (14)-24 mm. long, tridentate, the teeth blunt or acute, 0.5-1.5 mm. long; disc corollas numerous (usually 90-120), goblet-shaped or rarely tubular, 8(7.4)-9.5(10.5) mm. long, the tube 3(2.5)-4(4.8) mm. and the limb 5.0(4.5)-5.5(6.0) mm. long, the limb and the base of the tube sparingly short hispid-pilose to moderately pilose with septate hairs, sometimes also glandular, the collar evident to conspicuous; achenes 6 (5)-7 (8) mm. long, uniformly and sparsely to conspicuously hirsute with double hairs exceeding W the diam. of the achene, mostly also stipitate-glandular; annulus short; pappus tawny, -+ length of corolla, nmostly plumose, the setae 0.3 (0.24)-0.45 (0.6) mm. long.

description: "Shrub 8 ft. (2.4 m.) high"; upper part of stem (or branch) terete, striatulate, pale brown, glabrous, herbaceous, pithy, 5 mm. thick, with erect branches; upper internodes 4.5-7 cm. long; leaves opposite, connate at base for 1-2 mm.; blades elliptic-oblong, 17.5-26 cm. long, 5.5-8 cm. wide, broadest near the middle, gradually narrowed to both ends, closely and subequally serrulate from the upper part of the cuneate lower portion nearly to the apex (teeth about 60 on each side, about 1 mm. high, obtusely callous-mucronulate), above glabrous and deep green, beneath equally green, somewhat shinilig, and sparsely pilosulous along costa and chief veins with crisped, brownish, many- celled hairs, thin, feather-veined, the costa corky-thickened especially at base and prominent beneath, 1-suleate beneath above the base, 3-suleate at base, the chief lateral veins about 8-10 pairs, prominulous, the pair at about the middle of blade usually somewhat stronger than the others, the veinlets translucent-reticulate; panicle terminal, corn- pound, many-headed, flattish, about 21 cm. wide, the pedicels slender, 1-2.5 cm. long, sordid-pilosulous with in part subglalldular-tipped hairs, the bracts small, elliptic or lanceolate, 2 cm. long or less; heads (moistened) 3 cm. wide; disk subglobose, 6-8 mm. high and thick; involuere double, the outer phyllaries 5, obovate, in flower about 4 mm. long, in fruit 5-6 mmn. long, 2-3.8 mm. wide, obtuse or rounded, thin- herbaceous, glabrous or obscurely ciliolate at apex, 1-ribbed and with 2 or 3 branehing lateral veins, the inner (subtending and half-enclosing the ray achenes) 10, lanceolate, acuminate, incurved, sparsely pilose and pilosulous and densely covered especially on back with yellowish tack-shaped glands; rays 10, fertile, the tube 2.5 mm. long, densely spreading-pilose ancd somewhat stipitate-glandular, the lamina oval.- oblong, bluntly 3-toothed, 11-12 mm. long, 5.5 mm. wide, 11-nerved; disk flowers about 55, fertile, their corollas densely spreading-pilose and sparsely stipitate-glandular on tube, otherwise glabrous, 4.8 mm. long (tube becoming conic in age, 1.5 mm., throat cylindric-campanulate, 2.5 mm., teeth ovate, 0.8 mm. long); pales of disk similar to the inner phyllaries; achenes of ray and disk similar, obovoid, somewhat compressed, 2-2.3 mm. long, 1.4 mm. wide, gibbous, blackish, striate, glabrous, epappose.

description: Low, much branched annual herbs ea. 1.7 dm tall; stems slender, strigose, brownish red to yellowish red; leaves linear to lance-oblong, very variable, up to 2.5 cm long and 7 mm wide, -gland-dotted, hispid, sessile or short-petioled; peduncles up to 1.7 cm long, sericeous; heads broadly campanulate to hemi- spheric, ea 7 mm high; phyllaries yellowish brown to purplish brown, nearly glabrous to sericeous, their apices rounded, the summit bands often indistinct; rays 5-6, pale yellow to white, suborbicular, 5 mm long to very small, smooth above, with two prominent ciliated veins below, the tube cartilaginous, 0.5 nmi long; ray achenes linear-elliptic, 3-angled, 5 mm long, striate, slightly pubescent, becoming tuberculate, the pappus horns completely fused to the corolla tube or only scarcely free; disk corollas 4.5 mm long, yellow below, orange above outside, the lobes yellow inside; disk achenes oblanceloate, 3.5 mm long, apically emargi- nate, smooth at first with marginal ciliary tufts, later crenate-crustose with upwardly projecting hairs on the cartilaginous projections; pappus of a single, slender, eaducous awn; chaff generally orange-tipped, yellow below, glabrous or with a few fine hairs, the apex acute, erose; receptacle conical.

description: Herbae annuae, 16-40 cm altae. Caules erecti, hispidulo-strigillosi, pilis 0.5 mm longis. Pedunculi 5.5-6.5 cm longi. Folia petiolata, petiolis contractis 1-3 cm longis, laminis ovatis vel rhombeis, 4-5 cm longis, 2-4 cm latis, apice acuminatis, basi attenuatis, ambabus paginis strigosis pilis 0.5 mm longis; marginibus subintegris vel serratis, ciliatis, pilis 0.3 mm longis. Capitula 5-7 mm alta, 9-16 mm diametro. Involucrum extimum patens, 8-14 mm diametro; bracteae 3 (raro 4), ovatae vel anguste ovatae, basi leviter connatae, 4-7 mm longae, 2.5-4 mm latae, apice acutae, extus strigosae, pilis 0.3 mm longis (basalibus longioribus), marginibus opacis, ciliatis, pilis 0.4 mm longis. Bracteae intimae involucri extendentes sursum in brevi crasso cucullo, apice muticae vel cirrhosae, lateribus costatis reticulatisque; fructus 1.8-2.1 mm longi. Flosculi radii 5-7; ligulae flavo-aurantiacae, orbiculatae, 2-4 mm longae, 2-4 mm latae, apice trilobatae, marginibus imbricatis. Flosculi disci 40-80; corollae flavo-aurantiacae, lobis apice comosis. Paleae flavae apicem versus, anguste obovatae, 2 mm longae, apice obtusae, marginibus laciniatis, costa debili, leviter puberula, pilis 0.1 mm longis. Chromosomatum numerus, n = 11.

description: Plants 3-8 dm high. Stems usually lanate in upper 3/4. Upper leaves lanceolate to often deeply 3-toothed, moderately to usually densely pubescent; middle leaves oblong-elliptic to occasionally deeply 3-toothed, sparsely to densely pubescent; lower and radical leaves oblanceolate to spatulate, glabrous to moderately pubescent. Peduncles 2.5-10.0 cm long, lanate. Heads 1-6 per plant, 13-20 mm high, 20-30 mm wide. Involucre of 3-4 series of lanceolate bracts, not united, the inner bracts only slightly shorter and narrower than the outer. The outer bracts usually lanate at the base and moderately pubescent at the apex; the inner bracts sparsely to moderately pubescent. Ray florets 25-35 (-60); ligules usually deeply 3-4-lobed. Disc corollas 5.0-5.5 mm long, 1.1-1.4 mm wide. Achenes ca. 3.5 mm long, ca. 1.0 mm wide, moderately to densely pubescent. Pappus scales 2.6-4.5 mm long, 0.4-0.8 mm wide.

description: Suffrutex 70-90 cm altus, erectus, basi ramosus, ramis simplicibus, teretibus. Folia alterna, sessilia; folia infera 4-5 cm long., 2-2.5 cm lata, obovata, glabra; folia caulina 1.5-4.5 cm longa, 1-2.5 cm lata, ovata, base dilatata auriculata, amplexicaulia. Capitula discoidea, pedunculata, in cymis corymbiformibus 3-8-cephalis disposita, pedicellis bracteolatis 1-4 cm longis. Involucrum campanulatum, calyculatum, 7-8 mm altum, 7-9 mm crassum, bracteis involucralibus 12-14, lineari-ellipticis, 1-2-nervibus. Flores lutei. Achaenia 3-3.4 mm longa, teretia, 5-costata. Pappus albus.

description: Suffruticose herbs 0.70-0.90 m tall, glabrous, branched at the base. Stems erect, ribbed, reddish at the base. Leaves alternate, sessile, margin irregularly and strongly dentate, midvein and lateral veins prominent on both surfaces; basal leaves sessile 4.0-5.0 x 2.0-2.5 cm, obovate, base auriculate, apex obtuse; cauline leaves sessile,1.5-4.5 x 1.0-2.5 cm, ovate, base broad and auriculate, apex acute. Corymbiform capitulescenses, bracts 0.3-2.5 x 0.3-1.5 cm, ovate, base auriculate, apex acute, margin entire or dentate, peduncles 1-4 cm long, heads 3-8, homogamous. Involucre 7-8 x 7-9 mm, campanulate, calyculated. Calycular bracts 1-3, ca. 1 mm long. Phyllaries 12-14, 7-8 x 0.8-1.5 mm, linear-elliptic, apex acute, reddish with a tuft of short trichomes, dorsally 1-2 veined. Florets perfect, corolla tubular, glabrous, yel- low, tube 5.5-6.0 mm long, lobes 5, 0.1-0.2 x 0.2-0.4 mm, triangular. Anthers 2.8-3.0 mm long, base minutely sagitate, apical appendage 0.6-0.7 mm long, ovate-lanceolate. Style ca. 1 mm long, branches 0.8-1.0 mm long, truncate, broadened apically and penicillate. Cypselae 3.0-3.4 mm long, cylindric, fusiform at the base and truncate at the apex, 5-ribbed, brown reddish, strigose. Pappus bristles 4.0-6.0 mm long, white, straight and rough.

description: Trees, to 15 m. Leaves with petioles 11-13 cm long, densely tomentose; blade ovate-elliptic, 30-40 X 20-21 cm, coriaceous, base cordate, apex attenuate, obtuse, lower surface densely woolly-tomentose, upper surface glabrous except for the woolly-tomentose midrib, reticulate veined, 15-17 secondary veins in each side of the mid- rib, margins entire. Cap itulescences cor- ymbose-paniculate. Capitula homogamous, discoid; involucre cylindric-campanulate; phyllaries 5-6, uniseriate, coriaceous, ovate-oblong, ca. 8 X 3 mm, densely tomentose, apex acute. Florets 7-9, hermaphroditic, corolla ca. 12 mm long, tube ca. 6 mm long, limb ca. 5.5 mm long, lobes linear, ca. 5 mm long, apex acute; anthers ca. 4 mm, base appendiculate, terminal appendage lanceolate, acute; style branches with the apex obtuse, dorsally penicillate-appendiculate. Achenes oblong, ca. 3 mm long; pappus, 9 mm long.

description: Pulvinate-cespitose perennial herb with a branched caudex and a long stout taproot; leaves essentially all basal, linear, 4-20 mm. long, 0.7-1.4 mm. wide, densely and finely strigose; scape 3-10 cm. high, finely strigose, often with two or three much reduce leaves or bracts; head solitary, the disk 11-22 mm. wide; involucre 6-8.5 mm. high, hispidulous with short spreading hairs; phyllaries imbricate, yellowish-straw-colored or greenish-brown, with darker midrib, the outer ones a little thickened, acute, the inner thinner and sometimes broader, somewhat acuminate, sometimes purplish at the tips; ligules mostly 30-55, white or pinkish, 7-11 mm. long, 1.4-2.5 mm. wide; disk-corollas 4.3-6.0 mm. long, the tube about 0.9-1.1 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm., the narrow limb constricted in the lower half, slightly flaring above; style-appendages deltoid, acutish, 0.15-0.25 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of 15-25 or sometimes 35 slender, fragile, and slightly sordid bristles, the outer of long slender setae; akenes 2-nerved, conspicuously long-ciliate on the nerves, otherwise glabrous.

description: Annual, biennial, or short-lived perennial with a short slightly branched caLidex; stem slender, 1-4 dm. high, moderately to diffusely branched, stiffly hirsute, the hairs near the base spreading, those near the top usually appressed or ascending, but not always so; leaves hirsute, the lowermost ones oblanceolate, petiolate, entire or occasionally with a few large teeth, the blade 1-2 cm. long and 3-5 mm. (rarely 7 mm.) wide, tapering to a short petiole up to 2 cm. long; middle and upper leaves linear or linear-oblanceolate, sessile, 1-2.5 cm. long, 1-3 mm. wide; heads several or numerous, the disk 5-10 mm. wide; involuere moderately hispid-hirsute with curved hairs, 3-5 mm. high; phyllaries usually with dark midrib and lighter margins, the outer a little shorter and narrower than the inner and often wholly dark greenish-brown; ligules mostly 30-65, but occasionally as many as 100 or more, mostly 4-6 mm. long and 0.7-0.9 mm. wide, white or pink; disk-corollas similar to those of E. divergens, about 2.0-2.6 mm. long, the tube 0.3-0.6 mm., the lobes about 0.4 mm.; style-appendages broad, obtuse, about 0.1 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about a dozen fragile bristles, the outer of short setae or narrow squamellae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely hairy. Texas; a single collection in New Mexico, and an outlying station in Maricopa County, Arizona.

description: Plant perennial from a relatively slender rhizome which is sometimes shortened into a branching caudex; stem 1-6 dm. high, leafy, more or less spreadinghirsute, especially above, often nearly glabrous except under the heads; leaves sparsely to fairly densely hirsute, some of them, especiallv the lower, more or less dentate or denticulate; basal and lowermost cauline leaves broadly oblanceolate to elliptic, acute or obtuse, tapering to the petioles, mostly not over 15 cm. long and 25 mm. wide, usually smaller, occasionally much larger, the basal ones sometimes withered or deciduous before flowering time; middle and upper cauline leaves broadly lanceolate to oblong or ovate, usually more or less clasping at the base, not over about 9 cm. long and 3 cm. wide, usually smaller, reduced upwards; heads solitary, or occasionally 2 or 3, usually borne on long naked peduncles; disk 10-15 mm. wide; involuere 7-10 mm. high, equaling or surpassing the disk, glandular and more or less villous-hirsute with long spreading hairs which have black cross-walls near their bases; phyllaries equal, attenuate, the outer a little over a millimeter wide, thin and green, often purple-tipped, sometimes 3-nerved, the inner similar, but less green, partly or wholly searious; ligules 50-100, white, 9-24 mm. long, 1.2-1.7 mm. wide; disk-corollas 3.0-4.4 mm. long, with a usually ill-defined tube about 0.8-1.0 mm. long, the lobes about 0.6-0.9 mm.; style-appendages deltoid or triangular-ovate, about 0.2-0.35 mm. long; pappus of about 20-25 bristles, rarely with a few inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, hairy at least on the nerves and near the top.

description: Basally woody perennial herbs or subshrubs 0.5 - 1.70m tall, xylopodium not seen. Leaves alterante; petioles up to 5 mm long; blades 4.5 - 8 x 2.5 -3.5 cm, coriaceous, elliptic to oblong - elliptic or sometimes ovate, cuneate at the base, obtuse or sometimes rounded and mucronate at the apex, margins minutely toothed distally, both surfaces grayish - green, appressed and densely scabridulous, sparsely so along the veins, prominently reticulate. Peduncles stout; heads campanulate; outer phyllaries 9-15 x 3-5.5 mm, oblong to ellpitic or obovate, constricted and indurate at the base to oblong- obvate and more scarious. Paleae 6-8 x ca. 1.2mm when folded, tip obtuse to rounded, reflexed, up to ca. 1mm long. Ray florets absent. Disc florets with corollas 4-5 mm long, lobes glabrous. Cypselae 5-6 x 2-2.5 mm, those peripheral trigonous, 3 -winged, 3-awned, the inner laterally flattened, wings 1-1.5 mm wide; pappus with awns 2-3.5 mm long, broad to very broad at the base, the longest awn one half or less than % of the cypsela length, crown 0.5- 1(- 1.8) mm high, partially fused to the cypsela body (less than 1/3) with lacerate margins.

description: Plantae annuae, 30-40 cm altae; caules erecti, simplices aut supra manifeste ramosi, trichomatibLis 0.5-1 mm longis, tenuibus, patentibus glandularibus dense pubescentes (trichomatibus pilis brevioribus sine glandibus saepe interspersis); folia trifoliata, 3-6 cm longa, pilis sparsis appressis pubescentia; folia medio in caule petiolos 1-2 cm long. habentia; foliola ambiter triangulari-ovata ad obovata, perspicue irregulariter lobata (raro folia infima foliolis integris praedita); infloreseentia e cyma subeorymnbosa laxe florifera, 5 ad multa capitula habente constans; capitula subturbinata, 4-6 mm diametro, 6-7 mm alta, ca. 18-20-flora, in pedunculis 3-10 mm longis dense pubeseentibus portata; bracteae involucrales principales 10-11, 4.5-6 mm longae, 1.5-2.5 mm latae, marginibus subalbis membranaceis praeditae, ad apicem late obtusae ad acutas, glabrae aut subglabrae; flosculi albi, manifeste zygomorphici; corolla 2-3 mm longa, tubus ca. 1 mm longo, iugulo expandente, ca. 1 mm longo, lobis imparibus 1-1.5 mm longis; rami styli complanati, ca. 1 mm longi, appendicula penicillata cuspidata manifesta ad apicem praediti; achaenia 3-4 mm longa, obpyramidalia, quadrilateralia, pilis brevibus aseendentibus aequaliter pubeseentia, superficiebus perspicue 3-nervatis; pappus ex 8 squamis paleaceis ca. 1 mm longis, ad apicem truneatis, costam basalem manifestam inerassatam habentibus, per aristam mucronemive, autem, non terminatis constans; chromosomata 10on visa.

description: Ascending slender to stout herbs ca 1.2-2 dm tall; stems reddish brown, obscurely striate, hispid; leaves linear to elliptic, up to 2 cm long and 6 mm wide, but variable, sessile or short-petioled, scabrous-hispid; peduncles of varying length, ca 2.5 cm long, hispid; heads mostly hemispheric, ca 8 mm wide; phyl- laries obovate, spreading,, yellow with a dark purple summit band, hispid, especially at the rounded apices; rays 6-8, white, fading to pale yellow, oblong, 5.2 mm long or less, the tube slender, ea 0.8 mm long, essentially glabrous; ray achenes elliptic, 3-angled, 2.8 min long, concave at the apex, tuberculate at maturity, ciliate on the horns; disk corollas ea 4.7 mm long, the tube yellow, the lobes orange outside, yellow inside, the throat on the outer surface pubescent; disk achenes broadly oblanceolate, the margins smooth or ciliate, black, ea 2.3 mm long, the pappus of a single slender eaducous awn; chaff yellow, sometimes purplish below the obtuse, erose apices, sometimes ciliate along the keel; receptacle conical.

description: Herbs to 2 m tall; stems round, erect, sparingly hirsute to densely pilose, often purple-striped; leaves opposite, sessile or with winged petioles, the bases auriculate, 20 cm or more long, to 16 cm wide, pinnate to pinnatifid, the lobes 5-7, acuminate, dentate, dark green above, pale green beneath, both surfaces sparingly pubescent or upper surface scabrous; upper leaves with small lobes separated by shallow sinuses or entire; peduncles puberulous to glandular-pilose; phyllaries 5, uniseriate, basally united, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, sparsely or densely pilose below, glabrous above; ray flowers ca 10, corollas yellow to reddish-purple, to 7 mm wide and 15 mm long; disc flowers numerous, corollas ca 6 mm long, styles becoming long-exserted at maturity and exceeding the corolla by ca 2 mm; ray paleae ovate-lanceolate, ca 5 mm long; disc paleae ca 4 mm long or less, with prominent midvein; achenes dark brown or black, asymmetrically obovoid, somewhat flattened, ca 3 mm long, 2.5 mm broad.

description: Plant perennial, the caudex with several long slender branches; stem 1-10 cm. high, usually leafy at the base, naked above when well developed, finely glandular and more or less villous with loosely spreading hairs; leaves villous at least when young, later more or less glabrate, sometimes a little glandular, oblanceolate or spatulate, up to 3 cm. lolig and 5 mm. wide, a few of the earliest ones 3-toothed or -lobed at the summit, the rest entire; heads solitary, the disk 10-15 mm. wide; involuere 7-10 mm. high, viscid-villous, especially near the base, with long multicellular hairs, some of these usually with purplish cross-walls; phyllaries subequal, narrow, acuminate, purple at least near the, tips, sometimes throughout; ligules about 60-90, pink (at least when dry), short and erect, about 4-6 mm. long and 0.5-0.9 mm. wide, the margins usually inrolled, making them appear narrower; disk-corollas about 4-5 mm. long, the tube 1.3-1.5 mm., the lobes about 0.5 mm.; style-appendages deltoid-ovate, acutish, about 0.25-0.3 mm. long; pappus simple, of about 35-40 bristles, these, especially the barbellules, more or less tinted with reddish purple; akenes 2-nerved, short-hairy. Sandy river banks and gravelly soil; Yukon Territory, Alaska, and northern British Columbia.

description: Perennial herb with a simple or slightly branching caudex; stems solitary or few, usually erect, 2-20 cm. high, more or less viscid-villous with spreading hairs; leaves glabrous or not infrequently somewhat hirsute, with ciliate margins, the basal ones tufted and conspicuous, oblanceolate to spatulate, up to 8 cm. long and 13 mm. wide, but usually much smaller, the blade obtuse or rounded at the apex and tapering to the petiole; cauline leaves few and reduced; head solitary, the disk 8-20 mm. wide; involucre 5-8 mm. high, equaling or surpassing the disk, somewhat viscid and moderately to densely white-villous with flattened multicellular hairs, the cross-walls clear or occasionally the basal ones bright reddish purple; phyllaries thin, equal, green, or more or less purple, especially upwards, appressed, or some of the outer ones reflexed; ligules 50-125, blue or pink, rarely white, 7-11 mm. long, 1.2-2.5 mm. wide; disk-corollas 3.0-3.6 mm. long, the tube 0.7-1.0 mm., the lobes 0.4-0.7 mm.; style-appendages lanceolate to deltoid, acute, about 0.2 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about a dozen (rarely 15) firm obscurely barbellate bristles, the outer conspicuous, setose-squLamellate; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely hirsute. High moLntains; Montana and northern Oregon to northeastern Nevada, Utah, Colorado, and nqorthern New Mexico and Arizona.
