description: Perennial herbs with fibrous roots, without a well-defined central axis, caespitose from many, crowded, short (ca. 0.5 cm), erect, perennating branches, or these branches up to 4 cm long, rhizome- or caudex-like, slender and woody, thicker at their apices with old leaf bases attached; basal leaves and one to several erect stems borne at the tops of the caudex branches. Stems 4.5-16.0 cm high, rarely with a single primary branch, very sparsely strigose, loosely appressed to sparsely spreading-hirsute with often flattened and twisted Type A trichomes (Fig. 2), more dense and spreading just under the heads, very small Type B trichomes (Fig. 3) also present on the stems but inconspicuous. Basal leaves conspicuously but often rather sparsely long-ciliate on the margins with sparsely strigose-hirsute lamina, Type B trichomes common but inconspicuous; lower cauline leaves similar in pubescence to the basal ones, the upper cauline leaves ciliate, sparsely strigose or hirsute to almost glabrous except for Type B trichomes; basal leaves up to 6.8 cm long and 7 mm wide, usually somewhat smaller, the blades oblanceolate to elliptic, entire or with a pair of very small, serrate teeth near the top, apex acute or sharply acuminate, blades about 1/3 to 1/2 the -length of the leaf, tapering to a winged, ciliate petiole 0.5-0.8 mm wide, widening slightly at the base but not membranaceous, sometimes with a slight purple tinge at the base; cauline leaves 5-11 in number, alternate, clasping on the lower 1/3 of the stem, sessile above, entire, mostly oblanceolate with acute apices, much reduced in size on the upper half of the stem, linear and about 5 mm long just under the heads. Heads solitary at the ends of erect stems or occasional branches; peduncles 3-21 mm long; involucres 8-13 mm wide, 5-6 mm high, composed of phyllaries in about 3 subequal series; the outer phyllaries lanceolate, the inner elliptic-lanceolate with erect or sometimes loose and reflexed, acuminate tips, 3-6 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm wide, purple over the whole surface or only at the tips, the inner sometimes with a purple midrib, usually thick, sometimes with a very narrow chartaceous margin, finely punctate-glandular with Type C trichomes (Fig. 4) but sometimes sparsely or inconspicuously so, strigose along the midrib with thick, flattened and twisted Type A trichomes (Fig. 5); receptacle very shallowly convex. Ray flowers pistillate, fertile, about 44-75 in number, in a single series, ligules white, drying white or sometimes with a slight purplish tinge, 3-4(5)-nerved, truncate, acute, or cleft at the apex, ray corollas about 8-11 mm long and 1.2-1.8 mm wide, the tubular portion 1.2-1.8 mm long, the tube sparsely pubescent with long Type C trichomes. Disc flowers perfect, fertile, yellowish, corollas 2.6-3.1 mm high and 0.4-0.6 mm wide, narrowly funnel- form, without a prominent constriction or indurated region, sparsely pubescent with long Type C trichomes, the 5 erect lobes 0.5-0.6 mm long and often purplish; anthers with thecae 0.8-1.1 mm long with a lanceolate apical appendage about 0.2 mm long; style with branches 0.5-0.6 mm long including the triangular or widely deltate collecting appendages, 0.15-0.20 mm long. Achenes laterally compressed, oblong-ovate, conspicuously strigose, 1.1-1.3 mm long and about 0.5 mm wide, ribs and achene surface olive-brown; carpopodia cartilaginous, about 0.05 mm high; pappus composed of about 13-18 sordid-white barbellate bristles, the longest 1.9-2.8 mm long, some- times with a few, very short outer setae, less than 0.1 mm high, pappus of the ray flowers not exceeding the involucre, pappus of the disc flowers from 2/3 to equal the length of the corollas. Chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Nesom, Guy L. 1978. Erigeron hessii sp. nov. and Erigeron kuschei Eastwood (Compositae), two closely related narrow endemics from the southwestern United States. Brittonia. 30: 440-446.

description: Stems densely white-lanate; leaves opposite, subsessile; blades linear-lanceolate, 2.0 cm long, 0.4 cm wide, entire, obtuse, revolute, above dark green, rugose, pilose or strigose with scattered hairs, beneath white-lanate; monocephalous; disk 1.5 cm in diameter; phyllaries broadly linear to oblong-lanceolate, obtuse, 1 cm long; 2 mm wide, densely white-tomentose; pales lanceolate, acute, villous on keel; rays 10-12, 1.0-1.5 cm long, 5 mm broad; disk corollas 5 mm long, yellow, short-villous on throat and tube; anthers black; immature achenes 2.5 mm long; pappus of 2 subulate awns.
bibliographicCitation: Heiser, Charles B. 1957. A revision of the South American Species of Helianthus. Brittonia. 8: 283-285.

description: Dioecious perennial herbs from a thick, woody caudex; stems stoloniferous, 5-20 cm long, erect to decumbent, proximal portion densely lanate-tomentose, especially at the nodes. Leaves with petioles 10-50 mm long; blades ovate or orbicular to spathulate, 15-25(35) mm long, 10-20 mm wide, prominently 3-nerved, the base rounded to long-attenuate, prolonged into the petiole, the apex obtuse to rounded, the abaxial surfaces lanate-tomentose or glabrous, the ad- axial surfaces usually glabrous or rarely lanate-tomentose, the margins irregularly dentate or repand, revolute. Capitulescences of solitary capitula on distal branchlets; peduncles 1-5 cm long, densely lanate- tomentose or glabrous, 1-2-bracteolate, the bracts linear, 5-10 mm long. Capitula with involucres campanulate, 8-10 mm tall, 10- 12 mm wide; phyllaries ca. 18, the outer linear-lanceolate, 7.5-9 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, apically acute, purple, dorsally tomentose or glabrous, the inner ovate-lanceolate, ca. 9 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, apically acute, purple hyaline-margined, dorsally tomentose or glabrous. Functionally staminate individuals with capitula containing ca. 50-100 florets, the corollas yellow, narrowly campanulate, 7.5-8 mm long, the tube ca. 3.5 mm long, the throat ca. 3 mm long, the lobes lanceolate, ca. 1.25 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm wide; anthers ca. 2.5 mm long; styles branches ca. 1 mm long, apically rounded, dorsally papillose; ovaries sterile; pappus bristles ca. 6.5-7 mm long, white, apical cells slender, acute. Pistillate individuals with capitula contain- ing 50-75 florets, the corollas yellow, narrowly campanulate, 8-8.5 mm long, the tube ca. 4 mm long, the throat ca. 3 mm long, the lobes lanceolate, ca. 1.5 mm long, ca. 0.4 mm wide; style branches linear, ca. 1 mm long, apically rounded, dorsally papillose. Achenes cylindrical, 3.5-4 mm long, costate, glabrous or rarely with a few uniseriate trichomes near the carpopodium, pappus 6-8 mm long, white, apical cells slender, acute.

description: Perennial subshrub, forming rounded clumps, from a stout taproot; stems numerous, whitish, ca 30 cm tall, villous at nodes, almost glabrous along internodes; leaves 2.5-5 cm long, 2.5-5 mm wide, longest near middle, reduced above and below, linear-lanceolate, sparingly dentate to entire, sparsely villous, ciliate, the midrib prominent; heads solitary; involucres 10-12.5 mm high, 13-19 mm wide, the bracts imbricate in 3-4 series, oblanceolate, acute to acuminate, herbaceous above the middle, chartaceous below, short villous on back; rays white, 14-16, 20-25 mm long; achenes compressed, villous; pappus bristles barbellate.

description: Perennial, herb with a slender taproot and a simple or branched somewhat slender caudex; stem and leaves pubescent throughout with short spreading hairs, the stem 2-20 cm. high, spreading or loosely ascending to nearly erect, usually curved near the base; basal leaves up to 8 cm. long and 13 mm. wide, usually much smaller, commonly with well-marked obovate or elliptical to subrotund blades contracted rather abruptly to long petioles, but very variable in shape and sometimes merely oblanceolate; cauline leaves several, reduced, linear or nearly so, acute; heads solitary or sometimes 2, relatively narrow, usually distinctly turbinate, the disk 7-14 mm. wide; involuere 5-9 mm. high, finely glandular and more or less spreading-hirsute; phyllaries few, imbricate, green, with usually dark often purplish midrib, the inner commonly purple-tinged on the margins and tips; ligules about 10-25, usually deep blue or violet, sometimes bright rosepurple, 5-10 mm. long, 1.3-2.4 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.2-6.3 mm. long, the tube poorly marked, 1.0-3.0 mm. long, the lobes about 0.5-0.8 mm.; styleappendages deltoid, acute or acutish, 0.25-0.35 mm. long; pappus of 20-30 relatively coarse and firm white bristles, rarely with a few inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, hairy. Rocky or gravelly slopes and ridges, at moderate or high elevations in the mountains; central Idaho and northeastern Nevada.

description: Plantae annuae. Caules usque ad 15 cm longi, ramosissimi, saepe pseudodichotomi, 6-angulosi, glabri, plerumque glandibus oleosis ellipticis vel ovatis in seriebus vertical- ibus punctati. Folia linearia vel anguste oblanceolata, 0.5-2.5 cm longa, 1-2.5 mm lata, uninervia, mucronata, prope bases 2-4 paribus ciliorum usque ad 2 mm longorum ciliata, margine scaberula vel glabrata, in superficiebus ambabus glabra, supra atro- virentia, subtus pallentia, glandibus oleosis circularibus 0.2-0.3 mm diametro in seriebus submarginalibus (interdum cum aliquot glandibus additis dispersis) punctata. Pedunculi filiformes, 8-15 mm longi, interdum glandibus oleosis ovatis vel ellipticis punctati, bracteolati; bracteolae 3-6, alternae, lanceolatae, 0.5-2 mm longae, atten- uatae, hyalinae, interdum margine purpurascentes, saepe 1-2 glandibus oleosis punctatae. Capitula solitaria vel pauca, terminalia aut axillaria, campanulata, 2.5 mm alta, 1.5-2.5 mm diametro. Phyllaria 5, uniserialia, obovata, 2 mm longa, 1 mm lata, marginibus imbricatis, ad apices hyalinis, purpurascentibus, ciliolatis, costis in- crassatis, basi gibbosis, in costis et prope apices 3-6 glandibus oleosis ellipticis punctata. Flosculi radii 5; corollae flavae, 1.2 mm longae, tubis 0.5 mm longis et ligulis 0.7 mm longis, glabrae, ad apices tridenticulatae; styli cum stigmatibus lineari- bus usque ad 1.2 mm longi. Flosculi disci 14-19; corollae flavae, 1-1.2 mm longae, glabrae, sub-bilabiatae, lobis erectis 0.05-0.15 mm longis; stigmata minute bifida, vix exserta. Achenia cylindrica vel anguste clavata, 1.2-1.3 mm longa, glabra vel strigillosa. Pappus fimbriato-coroniformis vel absens. Chromosomatum numerus ignotus.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and short branched caudex; stems decumbent at the base, then ascending or suberect, 15-40 cm. long, sparsely to moderately spreading-hirsute or -villous with long multicellular hairs, sometimes more densely so near the top, often also finlely and sparsely glandular; leaves more or less conspicuously ciliate on the margins, otherwise subglabrous to sparsely or moderately villous-hirsute, relatively numerous and crowded, but evidenitly reduced upwards, scarcely or not at all tufted at the base, the basal and lowermost cauline ones oblanceolate, petiolate, up to 6 cm. long and 7 mm. wide, those above similar, but progressively reduced, becoming sessile and linear-lanceolate or narrowly oblong; head solitary, borne on a subnaked peduncle about 2-10 cm. long, the disk 14-20 mm. wide, very broad in shape, often becoming nearly circular in pressed specimens; involucre about 7-11 mm. high, sparsely to densely villous-hirsute with long spreading white hairs, also viscid or finely glandular; phyllaries nearly equal, green, somewhat leafy-textured, with thin yellow-green margins, the tips thin, attenuate or acuminate; pistillate flowers absent; disk-corollas bright orange-yellow, 4.7-7.0 mm. long, the tube 1.2-2.0 mm., the lobes 0.8-1.2 mm.; styleappendages broadly ovate, obtuse, 0.2-0.25 mm. long; pappus of about 17-30 firm white or sordid bristles, with a few short and inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely hairy. Near the seacoast in Mendocino and Humboldt Counties, California.

description: Plants annual (?), 30-75 cm high, erect, sparsely to densely hispid with spreading or antrorsely appressed hairs; lower leaves broadly ovate, (5-)8-15 cm long (2-)6-10 cm wide, becoming progressively smaller and ovate-lanceolate upward, acuminate to attenuate at the apex, long attenuate at the base, unevenly serratedentate, with trichomes evenly distributed and appressed on upper surfaces, sparsely so on lower surfaces, the hairs tuberculate at the base; heads solitary on rather stout peduncles, campanulate to elongate-campanulate, 5-10 mm in diameter; inflorescence subeymose, with usually 3 peduncles arising from a node but sometimes further modified with peduncular dichotomy; peduncles 2-11 cm long, with trichomes tending to be antrorsely appressed, occasionally sparsely interspersed with glandular trichomes; receptacle convex, 2.5-4 mm across, 1.5-2 mm high; chaff persistent, membranous, glabrous, oblong and acuminate or cuspidateto lanceolate and attenuate, 5-9.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide; involucre obscurely 2-seriate, the outer bracts lanceolate to broadly ovate, striate, 5-9(-10) mm long, 2-5 mm wide, acute to attenuate at the apex, corasely hispid-tuberculate; inner bracts subequal to the outer, becoming thinner, membranous, purple-tinged; ray flowers ca 5, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 3-4.5 mm, with conspicuous whitish to pale yellow ligules, these 4-7 mm long, 4-7 mm wide, broadly oblong to suborbicular, 3-lobed at the apex; ray corollas with inner lobelets vestigial to ca 1.5 mm long; pappus of the ray florets reduced, 1-3 mm long; disc corollas pale yellow, 6-8 mm long, the tube 1.2-2 mm long, glabrous, the throat tubular, 3-4 mm long, glabrous, the lobes linear, (1.2-)1.5-2 mm long, erect or reflexed, finely pubescent at the apex; style branches revolute, slender, slightly flattened, ca 2 mm long, pubescent near the conspicuously subulate tip; achenes blackish, narrowly turbinate, 2-2.5(-3) mm long, slightly flattened and incurved near periphery of heads, densely long pilose; pappus of 20 alternately longer and shorter plumose bristles (the shorter rarely broadened at the base), 2-6.5 mm long, the shortest ca 1/2 to 3/4 the length of the longest, the cilia short, becoming minute upwards; anthers 3-3.5 mm long, obscurely sagittate at the base; chromosome number, n = 9, determined in the 2 populations indicated below with an asterisk.

description: Erect perennial herbs, (5) 7-12 (20) dm tall, from a stout rootstock; stems variable in pubescence, strigose, hirsute, thinly tomentose, pilose to thinly tomentose, thickly hirsute or glabrate. Leaves cauline, moderately spaced, reduced upwards, the sessile blades (4) 6-10 (14) cm long, (1.1) 1.4-3 (4) cm wide, elliptic, oblanceolate or linear-elliptic, widest above the middle, apically acute to acuminate, basally cuneate, margins revolute and remotely toothed, strigose to slightly scabrous above, densely to thinly pilose to pilose-hirsute especially on veins, and often glandular beneath. Inflorescences cymose-paniculate slightly scorpioid, sometimes with well-developed bracteal leaves. Heads (10) 18-24 (27)-flowered; peduncles wanting to short, thinly tomentose to pilose-hirsute or even densely tomentose. Involucre campanulate, 5.5-7 (9) mm high, (4.6) 6-7 (9) mm wide. Phyllaries loosely imbricate in 3-4 series, variably strigose, arachnoid, pilose, densely tomentose, or hirsute-villous, sometimes glandular, often slightly scarious along the margins, greenish tinged with purple, the inner ones lanceolate, (4) 5-6 (7.5) mm long, (0.8) 1-1.2 (1.8) mm wide, acuminate to long acuminate, the outer ones ovate-lanceolate (1.3) 2-3 (4) mm long, (0.3) 0.5-0.7 (1.2) mm wide. Pappus straw-colored, the inner bristles (5.5) 6-7.5 (9.2) mm long, the outer scale-like (0.5) 1.1-1.5 (2.2) mm long. Corollas (5.3) 8-9 (11.5) mm long, reddish-purple, the tips of lobes often glandular, sometimes with 1 or 2 trichomes. Anthers (2.5) 2.8-3.5 (4.2) mm long, often glandular at the tips. Achenes (1.2) 2-2.8 (3) mm long, strigose, usually glandular at the base. Chromosome number n = 17, 34. Flowering and fruiting generally from November to April or very rarely throughout the year.

description: Plants perennial from a rhizomatous base, 35-60 cm high, hirsute; leaves lanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic, 4-9 cm long, 0.7-2.5 cm wide, acute at the appex, the margins of the blade entire to denticulate, attenuate-decurrent at the base, hirsute on both surfaces, subsessile to petiolate, the petioles 1-15 mm long; heads campanulate, 0.9-1.5 cm in diameter; peduncles 1-15 cm long, densely hirsute, interspersed with glandular trichomes, especially near the heads; receptacle conical; chaff ca 3 mm across, ca 5 mm high, persistent, scarious, glabrous, 8.5-10 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, light greenish-yellow, abruptly forming a slender awn-like beak, ca 13 the length of the body, or merely attenuate to acuminate at the often purple-colored apex; involucre 4-5-seriate, the outer bracts oblong to suboval, the shortest 3-5 mm long, 2-3.2 mm wide, rounded at the apex, light green and purple-tinged, dark purple near the apices, finely ciliate on the margins and apices, sparsely to densely short-pubescent and with short glandular trichomes; inner bracts progressively longer, oblong to suboval or obovate, the longest 9-12 mm long, 3.5-4 mm wide, becoming membranous, light green and purple-tinged or dark purple near the apices, sparsely to densely pubescent and with short glandular trichomes, rounded (rarely obtuse or emarginate) at the apices, the margins finely ciliate; ray flowers 5-8, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 6-6.5 mm, with conspicuous lavender-pink ligules, 12-20 mm long, 9-14 mm wide, broadly obovate to suborbicular, with 3 short, broadly rounded lobes at the apex; ray corollas with inner lobelets absent or rarely 1-2, the lobelets ca 1 mm long, and with 3-5 staminodia; pappus of the ray florets reduced to less than 2 mm, or absent; disc corollas greenishyellow, 6-8.5 mm long, the tube 2.5-3.5 mm long, entirely pubescent or only so near the throat, throat tubular to narrowly funnelform, 2.7-4.1 mm long, pubescent at the base, lobes obtuse-acute, ca 1 mm long, slightly involute at the apex; style branches brownish, flattened, (1.3-)2-2.2 mm long, minutely pubescent beneath, with subulate appendages at the apices; achenes black, narrowly turbinate, terete or tangentially compressed, 3-3.9 mm long, densely pilose, the hairs 0.2-0.8 mm long; pappus of 20 light brown, unequal, linear-lanceolate, plumose scales or scale-like bristles, (3.5-)4-5.5(-6) mm long, alternately longer and shorter, the shortest, usually slender, bristles, 1/2 to 3/4 the length of the longest; anthers nigrescent, 3-3.5(-3.8) mm long, obscurely sagittate at the base.

description: Herbaceous perennial 2.5-5(7) dm tall, glabrous, or sometimes floccose-tomentose in and near the axils of the leaves, sometimes lightly pubescent at and near the base of the receptacle and at the points of attachment of the involucral bracts; stems arising singly or several loosely clustered from a weakly creeping, branching, fibrous-rooted caudex. Basal leaves ovate to narrowly ovate in gross outline but 2 or 3 times pinnately dissected, the segments broadly linear to linear or even filiform; 10-15(6-30) cm long overall, including petiole, 3-5(2-8) cm wide; petiole about as long as the blade. Cauline leaves few, about 2-5 in number, half as long as the basal leaves or less, pinnately dissected, petiole indistinct. Inflorescence an open, subcorymbose cyme of 8-20(5-60) heads; principal involucral bracts com- monly between 13 and 21 (most often 21), 4-5(6) mm long, green or sometimes slightly pink-tipped, the apex often with a minute tuft of floccose hairs; calyculate bracts few and inconspicuous. Ray florets 8-10(13), the ligules 8-12 mm long. Achenes pubescent, at least along the angles, 2-3 mm long.

description: Plants up to 1.1 m tall; stems glabrous, inconspicuously striated, brown to red, black gland-dotted; leaves petiolate, blades trullate, 3-5-nerved, glabrous, up to 7-8 cm long, petioles ca. 2.5 cm long; peduncles striate, up to 4 cm long, lightly pubescent at apex; heads 1 cm wide; phyllaries 2-3-seriate, subulate, strongly convex, ca. 6 mm long, marginally ciliate, apices reflexed and acute, sometimes foliaceous; rays 15-22, oblong, minutely 2-3-lobed, ca. 9 mm long, glabrous except for a few fine apical cilia, style branches ca. 1 mm long, recurved; ray achene obpyramidal, ca. 4 mm long, the single awn at the inner angle ca. 3 mm long; disk flower lobes marginally vein-thickened, ca. 0.7 mm long, glabrous throughout, corolla ca. 4 mm long of uniform width, anthers ca. 2 mm long; disk achenes 2-4-angled, obpyramidal to flattened, up to 3.5 mm long, ciliate along the angles and on the 1-4 (mostly 2) unequal, up to 2.5-3 mm long awns; palea yellow, becoming indurate, exceeding the disk flowers giving a burlike appearance, apices acuminate often with uncinate tips; n = 28, 2n = 56.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1970. Revision of the genus Philactis (Compositae). Brittonia. 21: 322-331.

description: Pulvinate-cespitose perennial herb with a stout taproot and a stout branching caudex; stem about 6 cm. high or usually less, more or less pubescent with short spreading hairs, usually also viscid or finely glandular, sometimes nearly smooth near the base; leaves copiously hirtellous or coarsely strigose with short appressed or spreading hairs, the basal ones oblanceolate or linear-oblanceolate, not over about 2.5 cm. long and 2.5 mm. wide, usually less; cauline leaves absent, or sometimes a few reduced linear ones present near the base; head solitary, the disk 6-13 mm. wide, turbinate; involuere 4-7 mm. high, glandular and more or less spreading-hirsute; phyllaries slender, subequal to moderately imbricate, usually all deep blackish-purple, sometimes purple only at the tips, the rest greenish; ligules about 15-35, blue or purple, about 4-7 mm. long, 1.1-1.8 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.7-5.3 mm. long, the tube 0.6-1.2 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm.; style-appendages lanceolate, acute, 0.3-0.5 mm. long; pappus of about 15-25 firm bristles, nearly simple, bearing only a few intermingled short setae; akenes 2-nerved, hairy. .

description: Herbae annuae, 15-35 cm altae. Caules erecti vel decumbentes, plerumque glabri. Pedunculi 0.5-7 (saepe 1-2) cm longi. Folia petiolata, petiolis 0.4-2.5 cm longis, laminis ovato-rhombeis (juvenilibus lanceolatis), 2.5-7 cm longis, 1.5-5.5 cm latis, apice acuminatis vel obtusis, basi attenuato-obtusis, supra strigosis, pilis 0.6 mm longis, subtus glabris; marginibus obscure vel grosse serratis in superibus 3/4 laminae, integri in inferiore 1/4 laminae, saepe ciliatis. Capitula 4-5 mm alta, 6-7 (10) mm diametro. Involucrum extimum cupulatum, 5-10 mm diametro; bracteae 5, im- bricatae, ovato-orbiculatae, connatae 1/41/3 longitudinis, 2.2-5 mm longae, 2-5 mm latae, apice obtusae, extus glabrae, marginibus opacis, ciliatis, pilis 0.3 mm longis. Bracteae intirmae involucri omnes includentes achenia, lateribus amplificatis marginibus et diagonaliter prominente cristatae; fructus 2.9-3.1 mm longi. Flosculi radii 5-8; ligulae flavo-aurantiacae, ellipticae, 1-1.5 mm longae, 0.5-1 mm latae, apice minute bidentatae. Flosculi disci 15-25; corollae flavae, lobis apice acutis. Paleae flavae apicem versus, oblongo-ellipticae, 2.5 mm longae, apice acutae, marginibus erosis, costa debili, glabra. Chromosomatum numerus, n = 25 +/- 1.
bibliographicCitation: Stuessy, Tod F. 1970. Six new species of Melampodium (Compositae: Heliantheae) from Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 22: 112-124.

description: Frutex, ramis quadrangularibus strigillosis; folia ovata mediocria v. parva acuta basi rotundata petiolata crenato-serrata supra viridia hispidula et minute tuberculata subtus densissime caneseenti-strigillosa triplinervia; capitula parva radiata aurea in apicibus ramorum et ramulorum per 3-5 eymosa, pedicellis capitulis multo longioribus; involueri 4-5.5 mm. alti ca. 4-seriati gradati phyllaria ovata acuta dense strigillosa vix ciliata; radii 8-10, ca. 8.5 mm. longi.

description: Stems sparingly lanate or strigose with long hairs; leaves alternate; petioles 0.8 mm long; blades, 5.0 cm long, 1.5 cm wide, lanceolate, acuminate, cuneate at base, entire or obscurely serrulate, slightly revolute, above densely appressed-pilose with long hairs, below densely griseous-lanate; heads 3-7 on peduncles 1-3 cm long; disks 0.8 cm in diameter; phyllaries oblong-ovate, 5 mm long, 2 mm wide, obtuse, lanate-pilose or tomentulose, the inner with the lower half nearly glabrous and indurated, shorter than disk; rays about 10, 7 mm long, 3 mm wide; disk corollas 3 mm long, yellow, puberulent; anthers yellow; pales obtuse, straw colored with dark mid-area and tip, glabrous, or with a few scattered hairs on keel; achenes glabrous, 2-3 mm long; pappus of 2 slender unequal awas, to 2 mm long, 1 or 2 short squamellae sometime present; pappus of ray achenes of several lacerate squamellae.
bibliographicCitation: Heiser, Charles B. 1957. A revision of the South American Species of Helianthus. Brittonia. 8: 283-285.

description: Frutex ligneus 2-3 m altus. Caules cani. Folia 6-10 cm x 2-3 cm. Capitula 6-7-flora. Corollae albae, 4.3-8 mm longae, glandulosae. Achaenia glandulosa, ca 6-nervia, 2.3-2.5 mm longa.

description: Shrubs 2-3 m high; stems canescent. Leaves cauline, spaced 1.5 to 2 cm apart, the petioles 2-4 mm long, canescent, the blades 6-10 x 2-3 cm, elliptic-lanceolate, widest at or below the middle, apically acute to acuminate, basally cuneate, marginally revolute, pubescent above, canescent below. Inflorescences corymbose, composed of tight globular clusters of heads. Heads 6-7-flowered; peduncles 0.3-1 mm long, canescent. Involucre campanulate, 4.5-5 x 2-3 mm. Phyllaries imbricate in ca 6 series, greenish, arachnoid apically, the inner ones ovate-rounded, 3-3.5 x 1.3-1.5 mm, the outer ones ovate, 0.6-0.8 x 0.5-0.7 mm. Pappus white, the inner bristles 4.6-5 mm, the outer ones 1.2-1.7 mm long. Corollas 4.3-4.8 mm long, white, sparsely glandular. Anthers 3.7-4 mm long. Achenes 2.3-2.5 mm long, ca 6-ribbed, thinly strigose. Pollen type A (Keeley & Jones, 1979). Flowering and fruiting from January to March.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and stout branched caudex; stem decumbent or spreading at the base, 5-15 cm. long, strigose; leaves finely strigose or the basal sometimes loosely hirtellous, the basal ones oblanceolate, usually rather narrowly so, up to 6 cm. long and 5 mm. wide; cauline leaves several, fairly well developed, linear to usually linear-oblong or narrowly lance-oblong, mostly 1-2.5 cm. long, 1.5-4 mm. wide; head solitary, the disk mostly 10-11 mm. wide; involuere finely hispidulous or hirtellous to occasionally rather looselv strigose, also obscurely viscid; phyllaries subequal or only slightly imbricate, firm, somewhat thickened on the back, relatively broad, greenish brown, often with tan margins, usually somewhat purplish toward the tip; ligules about 40-60, blue, or sometimes white, 3-8 mm. long, 1.0-1.8 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.0-4.0 um. long, the tube 0.7-1.0 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm.; style-appendages deltoid or usually a little narrower, acute, 0.2-0.3 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of 12-20 bristles, the outer of more or less evident setae or setiform squamellae; akenes 2-nerved, short-hairy. High altitudes in the Abajo Mts. of southeastern Utah.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herba perennis radice maximo et caudice ramoso, caulibus decumbentibus strigosis 5-15 cm. longis, foliis strigosis vel imis hirtellis, imis oblanceolatis usque ad 6 cm. longis 5 mm. latis, caulinis reductis linearibus vel lineari-oblongis vel oblongo-lanceolatis circa 1-2.5 cm. longis 1.5-4 mm. latis; capitulo solitario disco 10-11 mm. lato, involuero hispidulo vel hirtello, bracteis subaequalibus, ligulis 40-60 caeruleis vel albis 3-8 mm. longis 1.0-1.8 mm. fatis, corollis disci circa 3.0-4.0 mm. longis, pappo duplici, achaeniis pubeseentibus 2-nervis.

description: Perennial herbs with erect to decumbent, branched, leafy stems to 12 dm tall, rising from a basal rosette or a cluster of shortened leafy branches. Leaves velvety, lower ones long petiolate. Peduncles long, scabrous to subscabrous. Heads 1.3-1.7 cm wide. Ray ligules deep yellow to orange-yellow, 10-14 mm long, 5.5-8 mm wide, with red to maroon veins beneath (sometimes entire lower surfaces so colored). Achenes small, elongate, 4.5-6 mm long, 2.7-3.7 mm wide, quick maturing. Dry, rocky lime- stone soils, roadsides.
bibliographicCitation: Pinkava, Donald J. 1967. Biosystematic study of Berlandiera (Compositae). Brittonia. 19: 285-298.

description: Plants up to 6 dm tall; stems slelider, strigose-pilose, becoming purplish; leaves variable, lanceolate, sessile, 3.5 cm long, 0.7 cm wide, 3-nerved, hispid; peduncles strigose, intensely so above, up to 6 cm long, not inflated; heads broadly campanulate to hemispheric, ea 1.1. cm wide or less; phyllaries obovate, the upper ones subsquarrose, glabrous with a wide dark summit band which may be ciliate; rays 8-9, bright orange and velvety above (drying yellow), dull orange to yellow and hirsute beneath, oblong, up to 1.7 cm long, the densely pubescent tube 9.9 mm long; ray styles 2 mm long, the branches 1 mm long with a few spreading hairs; ray achenes dorsally compressed to 3-angled, oblanceolate, ea 5 mm lono, striate, awnless; disk flowers numerous, the lobes orange inside and outside, becoming darker below, outside having upwardly directed appressed hairs; disk achenes obovate, 4-angled but flattened laterally, ernarginate, ea 3.5 mm long, glabrous with ciliate margins; pappus of two unequal awns, the longer borne medially, ea 4 mm long, the shorter reduced or wanting; chaff searious, acute, entire, yellow with a black tip, becomingr euspidate, exceeding the disk flowers; receptacle conical.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1963. Taxonomy of Zinnia. Brittonia. 15: 1-25.

description: Annual herbs with one or several stems originating at the base, paniculately branched above, 3-15 dm tall. Stems sparsely pubescent below becoming moderately pubescent above with short crisped hairs, narrowly to rather broadly winged. Peduncles 3.0-13.0 cm long, ca. 2-4 times as wide at the top as at the base, usually quite densely pubescent, especially just beneath the receptacle. Leaves glabrous to sparsely pubescent, 5-15 times as long as wide, apices acute to narrowly acuminate, midrib prominent and lateral veins often apparent in larger leaves; lower leaves linear- lanceolate, entire to occasionally toothed or occasionally irregularly laciniate; middle and upper leaves linear-lanceolate, entire. Heads few to many, globose to ovoid, 5-13 mm high, 6-14 mm wide (excluding rays). Receptacle globoid to ovoid, 3-9 mm high, 3-10 mm wide. Involucral bracts united at the base (sometimes strongly so), reflexed at anthesis, moderately to densely pubescent. Ray florets 11-17; ligules 6.8-15.5 mm long, 5.6-9.5 mm wide, yellow, glabrous on the upper surface and moderately to densely pubescent on the under surface. Disc corollas 5-lobed, cylindrical to cylindric-campanulate, 1.5-2.5 mm long, 0.6-1.0 mm wide, yellow with brownish to purple lobes. Achenes 1.0-1.5 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm wide, pubescent. Pappus scales usua.lly 6, 0.5-1.2 mm long, including the usually present terminal awn that is ca. 1/4-1/2 the length of the body, 0.3-0.5 mm wide. Chromosome number, n = 13.
bibliographicCitation: Bierner, Mark W. 1972. Taxonomy of Helenium sect. Tetrodus and a conspectus of North American Helenium (Compositae). Brittonia. 24: 331-355.

description: Acaulescent, perennial herbs 30-60 cm tall, 1.5-2 m tall if flowering shoot included. Leaves alternate, peltate; the petiole joining blade off-center, rarely at center; blades 13.5-23 cm diam., round, or suborbicular to obovate, adaxial surfaces glabrous, bluish green, abaxial surfaces glabrous, creamy white, veins shallowly out- lined against whitish background, margin with 5-7 obdeltate to obovate lobes, each lobe with 2 smaller lobes at approximately 450 from main axis, blades associated with capitulescence smaller than cauline leaves, not peltate and with lobes more deeply dis- sected, suborbicular to deltate in outline; petioles 4.5-23 cm long, glabrous, petioles of leaves associated with capitulescence completely winged, wings 2.5-5 cm wide. Capitulescence of 30-100+ heads, arranged in open paniculiform cymes, nodding; peduncles 0.5-2 cm long, glabrous, green-blue. Heads discoid, narrowly campanulate, nodding, 14-18 mm long, 3-5 mm wide; receptacle epaleate. Phyllaries 6 in 1 series, 8-13 mm long, 2-3.7 mm wide, appressed, herbaceous, narrowly lanceolate to oblong, glabrous, blue-green. Flowers 5, perfect, the corollas salverform, glabrous, deep purple or burgundy; tubes 5-7 mm long, 0.7-0.9 mm wide, deep purple; throats ca. 1 mm long, ca. 1.3 mm wide at base, 2-2.6 mm wide at top; lobes 1-1.2 mm long, lanceolate, revolute; anthers 2.5- 3 mm long, black, the appendages 0.5 mm long, lanceolate, stramineous; styles 8-10 mm long, stramineous, the branches 1.4-2 mm long, apices truncate, without append- ages, stramineous. Cypselae ca. 9 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, oval to fusiform, sometimes constricted at neck, terete, glabrous, light green to stramineous; pappus of 110-125 bristles of various lengths, 0.6-0.9 mm long, white, easily caducous.
bibliographicCitation: Panero, José L. & Villaseñor, José L. 1996. New taxa of Asteraceae from southern Mexico. Brittonia. 48: 566-573.

description: Plant perennial; stem erect, leafy, 10-15 cm. high, freely branching, finely glandular and conspicuously hispid-hirsute with coarse spreading hairs; leaves conspicuously hispid-hirsute like the stem and sometimes also finely glandular, all about alike, the basal slightly larger but not forming a conspicuous tuft, up to 3 cm. long, most of them 3-cleft, with linear or oblong lobes, these sometimes again cleft; heads several or numerous, the disk 6-9 mm. wide; involuere 4-5 mm. high; phyllaries conspicuously glandular and sparsely hispid-hirsute; ligules about 25-40, white, drying pink, 3-6 mm. long, about 1 mm. wide; disk-corollas narrow, about 2.5-3.2 mm. long, with a conspicuous short tube about 0.2-0.4 mm. long, this abruptly surmounted by the limb, the lower part of which is white, almost nerveless, and a little inflated; lobes of the disk-corollas about 0.3-0.4 mm. long; pappus of about 12-20 very fragile and readily deciduous bristles, apparently without an outer series; akenes 2-nerved, finely and inconspicuously strigose. Known only from Shell Creek Canyon, Wyoming, where it was recollected in 1946 by Ripley & Barneby.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Plants perennial, 30-40 cm high, decumbent and rooting at the nodes, glabrate or sparsely pubescent; leaves sessile, lance-linear, entire to dentate, 5-8 cm long, 4-7 mm wide, the margins pubescent, attenuate at the base, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces; heads elongate-campanulate, 1-1.5 cm in diameter; peduncles 3-8 cm long, spreading-hirsute and with glandular trichomes, especially near the heads; receptacle conical; chaff persistent, glabrous, scarious, 11-13 mm long, ca 2 mm wide with an attenuate to acuminate-mucronate, purple-tinged apex; involucre 4-5-seriate, outer bracts lanceolate-acute, the shortest ca 5 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, subsquarrose, light green, and purple at the apex to almost entirely purple, pubescent especially toward the apex, margins ciliate; inner bracts progressively longer, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, pubescent, often with short glandular trichomes especially near the apex, the longest 10-13 mm long, ca 2.5 mm wide, striate, light green with purple, acute apices, and membranous, ciliate margins; ray flowers ca 6, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for (6-)6.5-8 mm, with conspicuous white to purple-tinged obovate ligules, 8-10 mm long, 3.5-5 mm wide; pappus of the ray florets like that of the disc; disc corollas greenish, glabrous, 7.5-8 mm long, the tube ca 2.5 mm long, the throat tubular to narrowly funnelform, 4-4.5 mm long, the lobes acute to obtuse, ca 1 mm long; style branches recurved, dark brown, slightly broadened and flattened, ca 2.5 mm long, with subulate tips, minutely pubescent beneath and at the apex, with obscure stigmatic lines on the inner margins; achenes black, very narrowly turbinate, 3.5-4 mm long, often compressed, obscurely ridged, densely hirsute-pilose, the hairs ca 1 mm long; pappus of 20 brownish, unequal, silky-plumose bristles, 7-7.5 mm long, some of the bristles slightly broadened at the base, readily deciduous, alternately longer and shorter, the shortest ca 4 the length of the longest; anthers 3-3.5 mm long, obscurely sagittate at the base.

description: Plant biennial or short-lived perennial, with a short subsimple caudex and rosulate offsets; stem 15-50 cm. high, sparsely hirsute with appressed or ascending hairs, especially upwards, or nearly glabrous; basal leaves thick, conspicuous, resembling in aspect those of some species of Saxifraga, essentially glabrous, oblanceolate to suborbicular, obtuse or more commonly rounded at the apex, gradually or abruptly contracted to short winged petioles or petioliform bases, 2-10 cm. long (rarely 15 cm.), 4-25 mm. wide, denticulate; cauline leaves very few and small, mostly reduced to mere bracts, the stem appearing scapose; heads usually several (rarely as many as 35) in an open infloreseence, rarely solitary; disk 5-11 mm. wide; involuere 3-4 mm. high; phyllaries glutinous, sometimes sparsely hairy, with broad brown midrib, otherwise light tan, except for the sometimes purplish tips; outer phyllaries often wholly brown, shorter and usually narrower than the others, the conspicuously scarious margins of which mostly do not extend to the acuminate tips; ligules white, 25-40, 0.5-1.3 mm. wide, 4-8 mm. long; disk-corollas about 2.5-3.8 mm. long, the tube about 0.9-1.0 mm., the lobes 0.6 mm., the limb rather narrow for 0.6-1.2 mm., then flaring; style-appendages lanceolate, sharply acute, about 0.25-0.3 mm. long; akenes hairy, 4-nerved; pappus simple, of about 20 bristles.

description: Perennial herb with a slender taproot and a short branched eaudex; stem slender, 3-10 cm. high, usually only slightly exceeding the leaves, hirsute or hirsute-strigose with appressed or loosely ascending hairs, or the hairs sometimes spreading below; leaves numerous, not all basal, linear or very narrowly linearoblanceolate, lax and usually more or less curved, up to 4 cm. long and 1.5 mm. wide, hispid-ciliate on the margins, especially near the base, and more or less appressed-hirsute on the surfaces, the lower ones with conspicuously enlarged whitish indurated bases which sheath the somewhat bony-textured and lightcolored base of the stem; heads solitary, or the stem occasionally branching below the middle and several-headed; disk 5-10 mm. wide; involuere 3-5 mm. high, more or less spreading-hirsute with long white hairs, and often somewhat glutinous or viscid; phyllaries green or greenish, with darker thickened midrib, and often somewhat keeled, subequal or somewhat imbricate, the acuminate tips sometimes slightly scarious; ligules 25-40, yellow, 4-9 mm. long, 1.0-1.8 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 2.8-4.2 mm. long, the tube 0.4-0.7 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm.; style-appendages deltoid, acutish, about 0.15-0.25 mm. long; pappus of 15-25 slender white bristles, often with some evident outer or interminigled setae; akenes 2-nerved, more or less hairy.

description: Paniculately branched annual, 3-10 dm tall. Stems moderately to strongly winged,glabrous to sparsely pubescent with short antrorse hairs. Peduncles 3-13 cm long,ca. 2 times as wide at the top as at the base, sparsely to moderately pubescent withantrorse hairs. Leaves linear-lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, entire, apices variable from rounded to narrowly acuminate, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, midrib promi- nent and lateral veins often apparent in larger leaves; lower leaves occasionally pinnately lobed. Heads few to many but not numerous, ovoid to conical, 7-11 (-14) mm high, 6-11 mm wide (excluding rays). Receptacle ovoid to narrowly conical, (3.2-) 5.0-8.0 mm high, 2.0-6.0(-8.0) mm wide. Involucral bracts united at the base, re- flexed at anthesis, sparsely to densely pubescent. Ray florets 10-15; ligules 7.0-12.4 mm long, 4.0-8.8 mm wide, yellow, glabrous to sparsely pubescent. Disc corollas 4-lobed, cylindrical to cylindric-campanulate, 1.1-1.8 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm wide, yellow with yellow to brown or reddish brown lobes. Achenes 0.6-1.2 mm long, 0.3- 0.5 mm wide, pubescent with short hairs. Pappus scales usually 6, 0.1-0.3 mm long, 0.1-0.2 mm wide. Chromosome number, n = 13.

description: To 3 m tall; stems terete, smooth or sparingly puberulent; leaves lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate to 30 cm long and 8 mm wide, serrate, some teeth ca 1 mm long and callous-tipped, others smaller; some lower leaves with short lobes separated by shallow sinuses, glabrous to scabrous above, sordid-pilose in axils of main veins or puberulent along the veins below, the base oblique or attenuate, the apex acuminate to very long-acuminate; peduncles glabrous or sparsely puberulent; heads few or solitary; phyllaries broadly lanceolate to round-ovate, to 1.7 cm wide and 2 cm long; ray flowers 7-15, the corollas yellow, to 3 cm long and 9 mm wide; disc flowers ca 1 cm long, the corollas yellow; ray paleae broadly lanceolate, to 13 mm long and 8 mm wide; disc paleae linear, ca 7-8 mmnn long and 1.5 imm wide; achenle black, spherical, 5-6 mm in diameter.

description: Spinescent shrubs, densely and rigidly branched, to ca. 2 m tall. Old stems gray- black streaked with reddish brown; younger stems unevenly pannose with glabrescent streaks on the internodes below the spines. Primary leaves forming rigid, ascending, straight or slightly upturned spines; mostly 1-2 (-3 ) cm long; canescent or glabrescent. Secondary leaves filiform to clavate; 6-8 (3-20) mm long, sca-rcely 1 mm thick; glabrous or nearly so. Capitula borne in corymbose clusters of 2-5 at the ends of branches. Peduncles mostly 1-4 mm long; silvery-pannose; ebracteate. Involucres narrowly turbinate; ca. 7 mm high. Phyllaries 5; narrowly oval-elliptic; obtuse to acute; equal; pannose to canescent. Florets 5 per capitulum. Corollas  slender, pale yellow, ca. 9 mm long; throat slightly dilated, ca. 1 mm long; lobes narrowly lanceolate, ca. 3 mm long. Achenes slender, subcylindrical, 2.5-3.5 mm long; tawny with 5 reddish brown ribs; glabrous. Pappus of ca. 75-100 fine, penicil- late bristles; ca. 8 mm long. Style branches ca. 1.5 mm long; truncate or obtuse. Anthers ca. 3.5 mm long; sagittate; sterile tips narrow, obtuse. Pollen grains 41-45 ,um in diameter.

description: Shrubs ca. 1 m tall; stems terete, moderately hirsute to scabrous, stramineous-green. Leaves alternate; blades 30-62 X 18-30 mm, smaller distally toward the capitulescence, ovate to elliptical, uninerved with pinnate venation, adaxial surfaces moderately scabrous, bright green, abaxial surfaces sparsely scabrous to strigose, vein reticulum conspicuously outlined against green background, slightly lighter in color than adaxial surfaces, bases round, margins entire or with 2-3 minute mucros on each side, apices acute; petiole 1-2 mm long. Capitulescence of 3-30+ heads, arranged in compact simple cymes, terminal head of each main flowering branch nearly sessile, overtopped by flanking simple cymes with 3 heads each; peduncles 7-25 mm long, moderately to densely strigose, green. Heads discoid, involucres hemispherical, 10-12 mm high, ca. 12 mm wide; receptacle ca. 2.5 mm high, ca. 3.6 mm diam., shallowly convex, paleate. Phyllaries 7-9 in a single series; phyllaries 4.5-7 X 2.7-4 mm, ovate or oval to obovate, moderately to densely strigose, appressed, slightly indurate at base and along central vein, greenish yellow, distal third somewhat herbaceous, appressed, margin minutely fimbriate, green with a few blackish or dark green markings. Pales 8-9 X 3.7-4 mm, obtrullate in outline, conduplicate, apices acute, sparsely to moderately strigose, basal half stramineous-yellow, distal half greenish yellow with dark green markings, margin minutely fimbriate. Disk flowers 19-27, perfect, the corollas tubular, sparsely to moderately strigose, greenish yellow; tubes ca. 1.3 X ca. 0.5 mm, moderately strigose, stramineous-yellow; throats ca. 4 mm long, ca. 1.2 mm wide at base, ca. 1.6 mm wide at top, sparsely strigose; lobes ca. 1.2 mm long, deltate, sparsely strigose; anthers ca. 2.5 mm long, black, the appendages ca. 0.4 mm long, ovate, black; styles ca. 4.2 mm long, yellow, the branches ca. 2 mm long, tapered, with small appendage, yellow. Cypselae ca. 4.5 X ca. 2.3 mm, wings ca. 1 mm wide, obovate, stramineous, flatly biconvex, glabrous except for a few appressed trichomes on center of cypsela, black, epappose.

description: Herbacea vel basi sublignosa, caule abbreviato; folia pauca basalia sessilia alterna, ambitu oblongo-lanceolata vel oblanceolata, ad apicem versus latissima, 8-14 cm longa, 3-4 cm lata, ad basin versus angustata, apice rotundata, plus minus profunde pinnatiloba, lobis oblongis 6-8 mm latis, usque 15 mm longis, apice in 215 superioribus minus profunde lobata vel subintegra et minute mucronata, nervo medio et nervis late areolatis, lamina sparse punctata minute et sparse pilosa; pedunculi usque 23 cm longi valde exserti, capitulum unicum gerentes; involucri squamae 2-3-seriatae, lanceolato-lineares, apice acutae vel subrotundatae, 3-3.5 mm longae extus et intus pilosae; paleae lineares, 3.5-4 mm longae, 0.4 mm latae, margine uno ciliatae et virides caeterum stramineae; corollae flavae (croceae ex Ekman), radii ca. 5 mm longae, tubo 2 mm longo, glabro, limbo oblongo apice emarginato, 3-3.5 mm longo, 1 mm lato, 2-4-nervoso; corollae disci 2-3 mm longae, tubo cylindraceo superne parum usque dimidio ampliato, lobis triangularibus 0.5 mm longis; antherae 1.2 mm longae, ligula elliptica loculis tertio longiore; stylus 2 mm longus, ramis 0.3 mm longis; achaenia elliptico-obovata 3 mm longa, 2 mm lata, nigrescentia pilosa et verrucosa, alis 0.3 mm latis ciliatis stramineis; pappi setae subulatae inaequales apice recurvatae, alterae 2.5 mm longae, alterae 1.5 mm longae.

description: Annua pusilla semiuncialis; caulis simplex v. dichotomus erectohirsutus et glandulari-pilosus; folia opposita petiolata tripartita, segmentis linearibus v. lineari-oblanceolatis integris v. tripartitis glandulari- pilosis et patenti-hispidis; capitula parva minute radiata apice caulis et ramorum solitaria v. bina; involueri glandulari-pilosi et pareissime hirsuti phyllaria 4 obovata obtusa flaveseenti-viridia; radii 2 flavi minimi vix exserti, laminis erectis ca. 0.6 mm. longis; corollae disci 6 flavi, limbo late campanulato; achenia obovoidea trigona, facie exteriore glabra, faciebus' interioribus hispidulis; pappi squamellae obovato-suborbiculares obtusae ca. 0.2 mm. longae, tubo corollae duplo breviores.

description: Small, perennial herbs, 1.5-10.5 cm tall; base of stems often branching to form very short, horizontal, woody, stoloniferous branches up to 3.5 cm long, each of which bears a tuft of basal leaves at its tip, forming clones of plants which remain interconnected by these short stems; leafy stems erect to decumbent, herbaceous, usually branched, 1.5-13.5 cm long, basal portion often conspicuously ribbed and tinged with purple, the lower part glabrous or nearly so but becoming appressed pubescent toward the top, trichomes spreading just under the heads, Type A trichomes 185-770 ,u long, Type C trichomes glandular-appearing and dense just under the heads; roots woody, with one to a few branches. Basal leaves simple, oblanceolate, sometimes entire but usually pinnately 3, 4, or 5-lobed, with the sinuses reaching almost to the midvein, 5-34 mm long, the blade length slightly less than 1/2 the leaf length, blade 1-11 mm wide, sparsely strigose, lengths of the Type A trichomes similar to those of the stem trichomes, glabrous or less pubescent below; cauline leaves entire, linear, 4-16 mm long, becoming reduced in size upwards, pubescence similar to that of the basal leaves. Heads several, the first solitary at the ends of erect stems, later on peduncles developing from axils of cauline leaves; disks 5-7 mm wide; involucres 2-3 mm high, moderately hirtellous, with Type C trichomes which impart a finely glandular appearance, the outer phyllaries with a brown midrib, sometimes with a purplish tint, slightly shorter, narrower, and thicker than the inner, the inner green with chartaceous margins; ligules 23-38, white above and below with a lilac midstripe below, 3.9-6.1 mm long, 1.0-1.6 mm wide, with 3 or 4 veins; disk corollas 1.6-2.8 mm long, glabrous or with a few inconspicuous biseriate trichomes, the tube well-defined, 0.2-0.3 mm long, the lower part of the limb white, slightly indurated and slightly inflated, corolla lobes about 0.4 mm long; style ap- pendages broadly triangular, 0.4-0.5 mm long; pappus double, the inner of 7-13 bristles, the outer of slender setae up to 0.6 mm long. Achenes 2-nerved, 1.0-1.4 mm long, sparsely pubescent; n = 18. Locally abundant in crevices of Navajo Sandstone and in shallow accumulations of sand at the junctures between bedding planes. Known only from Zion National Park, Washington and Kane cos., Utah. June- September.
bibliographicCitation: Nesom, Guy L. 1976. A new species of Erigeron [E. proselyticus] (Asteraceae) and its relatives in southwestern Utah. Brittonia. 28: 263-272.

description: Short-lived perennial with leafy stolons that root at the end; stem weak, curved, very slender, about 10-20 cm. long, glabrous, or bearing an occasional appressed hair; leaves glabrous, or sparsely and finely strigose, the basal ones pinnately few-lobed, 2 cm. long or less; cauline leaves scattered, linear, 1 cm. long or less; heads solitary at the ends of several long branches, the disk about 3-5 mm. wide; involucre about 3 mm. high, glutinous or finely glandular, and sparsely spreading-hirsute with short hairs; phyllaries slightly imbricate, greenish or greenish-brownish, with brown midrib; ligules about 20, white, 3-4 mm. long, 0.8-1.2 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 2.3-2.5 mm. long, the tube 0.5 mm., the lobes 0.4-0.5 mm.; style-appendages broadly triangular, obtuse, 0.05-0.1 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 10-12 slender white bristles, the outer of distinct small setose squamellae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely hairy.

description: Planta stolonifera, vix tandem perennis, caule tenui laxo subglabro 10-20 cm. alto, foliis glabris vel sparse strigulosis, imis pinnatilobis usque ad 2 cm. longis, caulinis paucis linearibus usque ad 1 cm. longis, capitulis paucis vel solitariis, disco 3-5 mm. lato, involucro circa 3 mm. alto bracteis leviter imbricatis et leviter hirsutis, subglutinosis vel subtiliter glandulosis, ligulis circa 20 albis 3-4 mm. longis circa 1 mm. latis, corollis disci usque ad 2.5 mm. longis, pappo duplici, achaeniis leviter hirsutis 2-nervis.

description: Herba suffruticosa 40 cm alta basi prostrata ramis fertilibus tenuibus subflexuosis erectis violascentibus primum parce lanuginosis deinde glabris. Folia alterna sessilia linearia apice calloso-mucronulata basi leviter amplectentia margine valde revoluta, 2.5-3.5 cm longa 2-4 mm lata, pallide viridia; supra nervo medio tantum impresso pilis arachnoideo-lanuginosis deinde deciduis; subtus nervo medio crasso pilis longis patulis sparsis munitis et alteris arachnoideis laxis plus minusve deciduis. Capitula radiata grandia nutantia pauca (1-5) in corymbis terminalibus, pedicellis crassiusculis flexuosis 1-2 cm longis crasse tomentosis, paucis bracteis oblongis acutis pilosis circa 10 mm longis. Calyculum 12-14 bracteolis oblongis subacutis margine nigricantibus hirsutulis 5-6 mm longis 1.5 mm latis. Involucrum sub-campanulatum circa 15-17 bracteis herbaceis linearibus subacutis apice parce ciliatis, dorso pilis longis flexuosis atratis copiosis deciduis vel glabris, circa 11 mm longis 1.5-2 mm latis. Flores radii feminei ligulati 15-17, corolla flava 25-26 mm longa tubulo angusto 4 mm longo limbo 2.5 mm lato 4-5-nervato apice breviter tridentato, ovario glabro stylo bifureato exserto, pappo sericeo 6-7 mm longo. Flores disci hermaphroditi circa 100, corolla tubulosa lutea glabra 8-9 mm longa tubulo 1.5 mm longo limbo tubuloso apice 5 dentibus circa 0.6 mm longis apice papillosulis; antherae 2 mm longae saccis basi attenuatis subacutis; stylus crassiusculus ramis curvatis apice truneato-penicillatis; ovarium glabrum; pappus albo-sericeus 9-10 mm longus pilis triseriatis gracilibus leviter sparseque strigulosis.

description: Vine; stems terete, gray-brown, striate, glabrous to sparsely pubescent. Leaves alternate, borne singly or in clusters on short axillary shoots; petiole 10-15 mm long, sparsely pubescent; blade elliptic, 4-8 cm long, 1.5-2.5 cm wide, glabrous and dark green above, paler with sparse tomentum below, apically acute to nar- rowly acuminate, basally cuneate, tapering to the petiole, margins repand. Ca- pitulescences of loosely arrayed axillary or terminal panicles. Capitula borne on slender glabrous peduncles 5-15 mm long; involucres campanulate, 5.5-6.5 mm long, 6-8 mm wide; phyllaries persistent, imbricate, 4-6-seriate, the outermost extending onto peduncle, gold-brown, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, margins entire, sometimes ciliate; innermost phyllaries loosely appressed, oblong, apices blunt, often split and darker than the body, 5-5.5 mm long, 1.1-1.5 mm wide; outer phyllaries strongly appressed, persistent, deltoid to oblong, 1.5-3 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide. Florets 10-11; corollas white, glabrous, 5.5-7 mm long, lobes ca 2.8 mm long; anthers 2-3 mm long, base sagittate; styles 8.5-9 mm long, branches ca 2.5 mm long, with acute trichomes on outer surface. Achenes dark brown, ribbed and sparsely pilose, ca 2 mm long; pappus uniseriate of slender straw-colored bristles, 5-7 mm long.

description: Shrubs, to 5 m tall, woody at base; stems with branches slender, striate, strigose to densely strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate to ovate-lanceolate; membraneous; 6-20 X 3-1 0 cm; 3-5-veined at base, apices acuminate to largely acuminate, bases acute or attenuate, margins serrate, pauciserrate, serrulate or crenate-serrate, teeth usually mucronate; adaxially dark green, slightly strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long, abaxially pale green, scarcely pilose or shortly pilose mostly on the main veins, hairs 1 mm long; petioles slender, 1.5 to 5 cm long, strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Capitulescences thyrsoid, trichotomously branched. Capitula subglobose, 4-5 mm high, 3-4 mm diam., sessile or shortly pedicellate; phyllaries 3, suborbicular-orbicular, 3-4 X 2.5-3.5 mm, 7-veined, apices acute, abaxially greenish, strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long, margins shortly ciliate at distal one-third. Pistillate florets 4-6, subtended by ovate paleae, 3.5 X 2.5 mm, 7-veined, apices acute, strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long, margins scarcely ciliate at distal one-third; corollas white, 3 mm long, 1 mm diam., glabrous, 3-lobed, lobes irregularly deltoid, 0.4 mm long, scarcely pilose at apex; styles 1.5 mm long, branches 1 mm long. Staminate fiorets 5-10, subtended by lanceolate paleae (occasionally few central florets without paleae), 3 X 1-1.5 mm, glabrous, margins distal one-third shortly ciliate, 3-veined; corollas white, tubulate, 3 mm long, 1 mm diam., 5-lobed, lobed deltoid, 0.5 mm long, scarcely pilose at apex; anthers black, 1 mm long; ovaries 1.5 mm long, 0.8 mm diam., scarcely pilose at distal apex. Cypselae obovoid, rounded at base, 2 X 1.7 mm, pilose at distal one-third, hairs 1 mm long. Chromosome number unknown.

description: Perennial herbs 3-9 dm high, unbranched or corymbosely branched above. Stems sulcate below becoming striate above, glabrous to lanate. Peduncles 2.5-16.0 cm long, striate, moderately pubescent to lanate. Leaves dotted with few to numerous impressed glands, the margins entire to deeply 3-toothed, the midrib and lateral veins prominent; upper leaves lanceolate to elliptic to ovate, glabrous to densely pubescent; middle leaves ovate, elliptic, oblong or oblanceolate, glabrous to densely pubescent; lower and radical leaves oblanceolate to spatulate with broadened, clasp- ing bases, glabrous to moderately pubescent. Heads 1-15 per plant, hemispherical to globoid, 12-20 mm high, 19-30 mm wide. Receptacle ovoid to globoid, alveolate. Involucre of 2-4 series of bracts, dotted with few to numerous impressed glands, spreading but not reflexed at anthesis. Ray florets 14-35 (-60), styliferous and fertile; ligules 3-4-lobed, orange-yellow to yellow, glabrous. Disc florets bisexual and fertile; disc corollas 5-lobed, yellow, cylindrical to cylindric-campanulate, 4.2-5.5 mm long, 0.8-1.5 mm wide. Achenes 3.5-4.5 mm long, 1.0-1.7 mm wide, moderately to densely pubescent with straight hairs forked at their apices. Pappus scales 5-7, lanceolate to acuminate, 2.6-4.5 mm long, 0.4-0.8 mm wide. Chromosome number: n= 15.

description: Plants 3-9 dm high. Stems glabrous to rather densely pubescent. Leaf margins entire; upper leaves usually lanceolate, glabrous to moderately pubescent; middle leaves oblong to elliptic, glabrous to sparsely pubescent; lower and radical leaves oblanceolate to spatulate, glabrous. Peduncles 3-16 cm long, moderately pubescent, becoming lanate beneath the receptacle. Heads 2-15 per plant, 12-17 mm high, 19-26 mm wide. Involucre of 2 series of bracts. The outer bracts ovate to lanceolate, strongly united at their bases, sparsely to densely pubescent; the inner bracts some- what smaller than the outer, elliptic with acuminate apices, not united, glabrous. Occasionally a few very small, lanceolate bracts form a third series inside the inner bracts. Ray florets 14-26; ligules shallowly 3-4-lobed, orange-yellow, becoming yellow with age. Disc corollas 4.2-5.4 mm long, 0.8-1.5 mm wide. Achenes 3.5-4.5 mm long, 1.0-1.7 mm wide, densely pubescent. Pappus scales 2.9-4.1 mm long, 0.4- 0.8 mm wide.

description: Annual herbs to 2 m tall; stems often orange-yellow when dried, glabrous below, stipitate-glandular or glandular and pilose above; leaves sessile or with winged peioles, the lower basally connate, deltoid, acuminate, the base cuneate, puberulent or strigose above, sparsely puberulent below; peduncles stipitate-glandular or glandular and pilose; phyllaries usually 5, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, ca 7 mm long, to 5 mm wide, glandular, glandular-puberulent, or glabrous below; ray flowers ca 15, in 1 series, the corollas yellow, 5-7 mm long, to 2 mm wide; disc flowers about as many as or fewer than the ray flowers, 5-6 mm long; ray paleae ovate, long-acuminate, concave, ca 5 mm long, stipitate-glandular below, glabrous above, the margins of the long-acuminate tip inrolled; disc paleae lanceolate, ca 5 mm long; achene dark brown to black, obovoid, longitudinally striate, to 3 mm wide and 4 mm long.

description: Frutex ramosissimus. Caules dense pilosi. Folia versus apicem ramorum congesta, spiraliter disposita, obovata vel oblanceolata, subtus dense pilosa, margine integra revoluta. Synflorescentia congesta, capitulis brevipedunculatis; involucra campanulata, receptaculum conicum, epaleaceum. Corollae glandulis stipitatis praeditae. Cypselae unaequaeque in carpopodio asymmetrico annuliformi insidentes, epapposae.

description: Shrub to 80 cm tall. Stems terete, much-branched, covered by multicellular trichomes, conic, thick, stiff and usually not glandular. Leaves short-petiolate (petiole 0.2-0.5 mm long), arranged spirally, aggregated at the apex of the branches; lamina thick, narrowly obovate to broadly oblanceolate, 5-7 X 2-4 mm, acute at apex, entire and revolute at margins, glabrous above and with sparse, translucent trichomes beneath, 3-nerved, venation prominent beneath. Capitula arranged in tight-clustered subumbels, main axes 2.5-3 mm long, tomentose; peduncles 1.5-2.5 mm long, to- mentose, with 2 bracteoles, 2.3-3.7 X 0.3- 0.7 mm. Heads with ca. 48 flowers, involucre campanulate, phyllaries ca. 25, 2-seriate, 3.5-5.5 X 0.5-1 mm, the outermost commonly with trichomes on the lower half and margins sparsely ciliate; receptacle conspicuously conic, naked. Corolla tubular, white, 1.9-2.5 mm long; tube 1.6-2 X 0.4-0.5 mm, externally covered by small glands, these more abundant on the proximal half; lobes 0.3-0.5 mm long, acute at apex, externally papillate, internally papillate at margins only. Apical appendages of the anthers wider than long, emarginate. Style 4.5-5.7 mm long; branches 1.5-1.9 mm long, clavate, papillate except at apex. Cypselae 1.5-1.8 x 0.5-0.8 mm, prismatic, slightly curved, 5-ribbed, with a ring of non-carbonized cells at the apex, with trichomes on the upper part and rare, usually deciduous, glands; carpopodium asymmetrical, ring-like, well-developed, cells ca. 50 pm long, rectangular, in numerous series; pappus lacking.

description: Haec species Lessingiantho reitzicmo (Cabrera) H. Rob. similis sed foliis brevioribus, phyllariis pluriser-iatis et caulibus omnibus foliosis differt. Herba erecta 30-70 cm alta, caulibus simplicibus rotundatis dense villosis ad inflorescentiam sparse foliatis. Folia lanceo-lata, 2.5-3.5 cm longa 0.8-13 cm lata, utrinque glabrata, infeme glanduloso-punctata. Capitula longe pedunculata, hemisphaerica, solitaria vel ad inflorescentiam cymosam 2-5-cephala. Phyllaria 4-5(-6)-seriata, oblonga vel lanceolata. Flores 100-110, viola-cei. Corolla glabrata 13-14 mm longa.

description: Perennial herb, 30-70 cm tall. Stems 1-3, single, rounded, 2-3 mm in diam., villous, regularly leafy to the inflorescence, internodes 3- 10(-15) mm long. Leaves alternate to subopposite, ascending, subsessile, chartaceous, concolorous. Leaf blades lanceolate, 2.5-3.5(-5.5) cm long, 0.8-1.5 cm wide, entire, subrevolute at the margin, apically acute and mucronate, cuneate at base, glabrous on both faces, glandular dotted beneath, pinnatinerved, secondary veins 4-6, almost straight, not strongly evident. Capitula terminal, solitary at the stem apex or eventually in broad corymbose cymes. Involucres widely campanulate to hemispherical, 12-14 mm high, 15-20 mm wide. Phyllaries disposed in 4-5(-6) series, loosely imbricate, appressed, acuminate, brownish to blackish, villous at apex, inner phyllaries lanceolate to linear, 9-11 mm long, 1.1-1.6 mm wide, middle phyllaries oblong to lanceolate, 78 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, the outer ones ovate, 4-6 mm long, 1.5-2 mm long. Florets violet, 100-110 per head. Corollas glabrous, 13-14 mm long, lobes lanceolate, 4-A.6 mm long. Anthers basally calcarate, thecae 3.84 mm long, apical appendages ovate, 0.40.5 mm long. Style 15-16 mm long, branches linear, 3.5 x 1 mm long. Cypselas cylindrical, ribbed, densely sericeous, 4-5 mm long. Pappus biseriate, dark grayish, inner bristles 8-9 mm long, outer scales linear to lanceolate, fimbriate, 0.6-0.8 mm long. Pollen grains spheroidal to prolate spheroidal, echi-nolophate, 38x 5 pm in diam., tricolporate, exine semitectate, regularly areolate, spiculate (type B).
bibliographicCitation: Borges, R. & Dematteis, Massimiliano. 2008. A new species of Lessingianthus (Asteraceae: Vernonieae) from Minas Gerais, Brazil. Brittonia. 60 (4): 377-381.

description: Shrubs, 2-3 m tall; stems striate, purplish with green spotting, branches densely strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate-lanceolate to ovate, 8-10 X 3- 7 cm; apices acute, bases attenuate (round- cuneate), margins finely irregularly serrate, 3-veined, veins yellowish, strigose-pubescent on both surfaces, hairs 0.5-1 mm long; petioles 1-3 cm long, strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Capitulescence paniculiform, terminal, with capitula short-pedicellate. Capitulum subglobose, 5 mm high, 4 mm diam.; phyllaries 3, broadly ovate, 4.5-5 X 3.5-4 mm, apices acute, 7-veined, margins ciliate on distal one-third, strigose-pubescent on abaxial side, hairs 0.5 mm long, light-green with fine green dark lines. Pistillate florets 5, subtended by ovate paleae, 4-4.5 X 3.5- 4 mm, 5-veined, apices acute, strigose, hairs 0.5 mm, margins distal half ciliate; corollas white, tubulate, 3 mm long, 1 mm diam., 3- lobed, lobes deltoid, 0.5 mm long, apices scarcely ciliate; styles 2 mm long, branches 1 mm long. Staminate florets 19, epaleaceous; corollas tubulate, white, 3 mm long, 1 mm diam., 5-lobed, lobes 0.5 mm long, scarcely ciliate at apex; anthers black, 1.5 mm long; style 1 mm long, undivided, ovaries 1.5-2 mm long, 1-1.5 mm diam., glabrous to scarcely pubescent at apex, hairs 0.2-0.5 mm long. Cypselae subglobose, black, 2 X 1.5 mm, glabrous, slightly papillose on distal one-third. Chromosome number unknown.

description: Small ascending shrubs 30-50 cm tall. Young branches lanulose, later glabrous, light brown. Leaves opposite; lamina lustrous, oval to ovate, 5-7 X 2-3 cm, acute at apex, cuneate to attenuate at base, crenate with 5-8 pairs of teeth along margin or sometimes subentire, hispidulous and punctate glandular (yellow) on both surfaces; veins triplinerved and raised below; petioles 5-10 mm long. Lateral shoots from leaf axils sometimes shortly developed, bearing a few pairs of small lance-elliptic entire leaves. Heads many, 7-8 X ca. 3 mm, very shortly pedunculate, in several dense corymbs, each corymb 20-50 mm wide consisting of 20-60 heads. Inflorescence branches and peduncles lanulose and sessile-glandular (yellow). Phyllaries ca. 5 mm long, acuminate at apex, pale green, bearing sparse transparent or yellow sessile-glands and puberulous outside. Corolla white to pale pink; outside sparsely puberulous above and bearing some transparent, sessile- or sometimes sparsely stipitate-glandular below; tubes ca. 4 mm long; lobes ca. 0.8 mm long. Achenes ca. 3.5 mm long, brown-black, hispid on the ribs. Pappus scales membranous, united into a crown, ca. 0.5 mm high, fine-pectinate margin.

description: Perennial herbs, 5-10 dm tall; stems gray- to slightly brown-tomentose. Leaves cauline, crowded basally, remote and reduced upwards, sessile, the basal ones (9) 13-22 cm long, 4-7 cm wide, the rest 5.5-11.5 cm long, (0.9) 2-3.5 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, widest at or below the middle, apically acute, basally attenuate, marginally slightly revolute, slightly crenate to remotely callous- toothed, slightly scabrous, occasionally slightly villous above, whitish- to grayish-tomentose and darkly reticulate-veined beneath. Inflorescences paniculate-cymose, with (1) 5-10 (24) large heads. Heads ca 42-110-flowered; peduncles 2-30 mm long, tomentose. Involucre campanulate-urceolate, 14-21 mm high, 12-19 mm wide; phyllaries very tightly imbricated in ca 6-7 series, dark reddish-purple, rarely greenish, the inner ones ovate-oblong, acute, 10.5-13 mm long, 3-5.2 mm wide, the outer ones ovate, 3-4 (5) mm long, 2.2-3.5 mm wide. Pappus brown, the inner bristles 9-13 mm long and outer scales (1.5) 2-2.7 mm long. Corollas (13) 16-20 mm long, reddish-purple, slightly hairy at tip of the lobes. Anthers 5.2-7 mm long. Achenes (3.2) 4-5 (6) mm long, 9-10 ribbed, brownish-hirsute. Flowering and fruiting from November to March.

description: Frutex scandens ramis ramulisque cylindricis striatis glaberrimis. Folia alterna petiolata coriacea. Petiolus 2-2.5 cm. longus rectus vel flexuosus semiteres supra sulcatus glaber. Lamina oblongo-ovata utrinque at- tenuata basi longe cuneata apice angustato-cuspidata margine integra 10-12 cm. longa 4-6 cm. lata; utrinque glaberrima nitidoque, costa supra paulo impressa subtus crassiuscule eminenti, nervis lateralibus prominulis arcuato-ascendentibus ceteris nervulis plus-minusve prominulis anastomosato-reticulatis. Inflorescentiae axillare s thyrsoideo-paniculatae floribundae circa 25 cm. longae, in specimine, pedunculo robusto striato glabro 8 cm. longo, axi tomentuloso, ramulis ascendentibus tomentulosis bracteis lanceolatis vel late ovatis acutis glabris vel paulo ciliatis praeditis. Capitula heterogama discoidea sessilia vel subsessilia congeste glomerata. Calyculus plerumque 3 bracteolis, una media ovata acuminata 5-7 mm. longa 2.5-4 mm. lata membranacea margine scarioso- lacerata ciliataque reliqua subglabra, 2 bracteolis lateralibus linearibus brevioribus. Involucrum campanulatum 12 bracteis oblongis 7 mm. longis 1.8-2.4 mm. latis subglabris apice acutis parce ciliolatis margine anguste scariosis. Re- ceptaculum alveolatum 1.8,-2 mm. latum, margine alveolarum breviter fimbriati. Flores marginales feminei 6-7 tubulosi, corolla 5-7 mm. longa lutea glabra tubulo angusto 2.5 mm. longo limbo infundibuliforme 3-5 dentato dentibus aequilongis vel irregularibus. Flores disci hermaphroditi circa 18 tubulosi corolla glabra lutea 7 mm. longa tubulo 3 mm. longo limbo ampliato profunde 5-dentato. Antherae 2 mm. longae basi obtusae. Rami stigmatici truncati. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus albus 5-6 mm. longus.

description: Coarse vine, branches 1-2.5 cm. diam. rooting where touching soil, or climbing trees. Lvs. leathery deep green nitid above, pale green, subnitid below. Bracts pale green, tipped with brown. Corollas pale yellow. Anthers reddish brown. Style branches pale yellow. W. H. Camp E-4323 (F, holotype).

description: Fibrous rooted annual. Stems erect, to 30 cm tall, terete, simply branched, lanulose below, sparsely pilose and stipitate-glandular above, red-purple. Leaves opposite, sessile; lamina trifid near the base; segments linear to filamentous, sometimes divided again and bifid or trifid, the lobes entire. In leaves of the lower part of stems, the lateral segments trifid at base and each lobe shallowly divided again bifidly or trifidly, the middle segment also trifid in upper part and each lobe shallowly bifid or trifid. Leaf blades herbaceous, 1-2.5 cm long, sparsely pilose and punctate-glandular, and stipitate-glandular on the margin of young leaves. Heads a few on the top of diffuse panicle branches, ca. 7 X ca. 4.5 mm. Inflorescence branches and peduncles stipitate-glandular (red-purple); peduncles gracile, 2-12 mm long. Phyllaries ca. 4.5 mm long, acuminate at apex, pale green, sometimes red-purplish at apex, puberulous with short hairs, stipitate-glandular (red- purple) and sessile-glandular (yellow) outside. Corolla sparsely puberulous outside; tubes deep red-purple, ca. 3.5 mm long; lobes white, ca. 2 mm long. Achenes ca. 3 mm long, dark black-brown, hispidulous. Pappus awns 3(-4), almost as long as corolla, deep red-purple, covered with minute spines; scales between awns membranous.

description: Rhizomatous perennial. Stems erect, 30- 60 cm tall, terete, minutely puberulous, usually purplish brown, branched in upper part; branches elongate, ascending, bearing a few pairs of small elliptic leaves. Leaves opposite, nearly sessile, thick and lustrous above, oval, 30-45 X 10-18 mm in the middle part of stems, smaller in the lower part, subacute at apex, shortly attenuate at base, serrate with a few to 7 pairs of teeth along margin, punctate-glandular and nearly glabrous on both surfaces, light green, sometimes purplish, trinerved, usually having conspicuous small veins. Lateral shoots from lower leaf axils sometimes developed shortly, bearing a few pairs of small leaves. Heads many, ca. 10 X 3-4 mm, nearly sessile, in many compound dense corymbs; each corymb 10-20 mm wide consisting of 5-20 heads. Inflorescence branches puberulous and sessile-glandular. Phyllaries 6-7 mm long, acuminate at apex, pale green, tinged with red-purple near apex, bearing sessile yellow glands and sparsely puberulous outside. Corolla pale pink, sparsely puberulous and sparsely sessile-glandular out- side; tubes ca. 5.5 mm long; lobes ca. 2 mm long. Achenes 4.5-5 mm long, black- brown, hispid above. Pappus scales membranous, incompletely united to a crown, 0.5-1 mm high, fine-pectinate margin.

description: Apomictica morphologice inter Eupatorium sessilifolium et E. rotundifolium, ab E. sessilifolio differt pube magis copiosa et foliis latioribus, ab E. rotundifolio differt pube leviter minore et foliis acutius serratis, plane pinnatim venosis (nec triplinervis); caulibus praesertim distaliter laxe puberulentis vel villoso-puberulentis; foliis plerumque 4-11 x 1.5-4.5 cm, 2-3 (3.5)-plo longioribus quam latis, atomifero-glandulosis et subsparse puberulentis; pollinis granis abortivis.

description: Plants 6-12+ dm tall, the stems clustered on a short rhizome or crown; stems loosely puberulent or villous-puberulent, especially upwards, becoming copiously and often viscidly so in the inflorescence; leaves opposite, sessile, mostly lance-ovate or rather narrowly ovate, 4-11 x 1.5-4.5 cm, 2-3 (3.5) times as long as wide, pinnately veined (not at all trinerved nor triplinerved), rather broadly round- ed or somewhat tapering at the base, acute or acuminate at the tip, fairly coarsely serrate, atomiferous-glandular and rather sparsely puberulent; lower leaves smaller and deciduous; inflorescence terminal, cymose-corymbiform, with numerous heads; involucre 4.5-6 mm high, its bracts rather few but well imbricate, atomiferous-glandular and rather roughly villous-puberulent, longitudinally few-striate, light green with pale, thin margins, only slightly paler distally, the outer blunt, the inner more acute or shortly acuminate, or mucronate-acuminate; flowers 5; corolla white, about 3 mm long; anthers without pollen; achenes 3-4 mm long, promi- nently atomiferous-glandular. Presumably an apomictic triploid reflecting hybridization between E. sessilifolium and E. rotundifolium, but now a widespread, stable, self-perpetuating population.
bibliographicCitation: Vovides, Andres P. 1985. Systematic studies on Mexican Zamiaceae II. Additional notes on Ceratozamia kuesteriana from Tamaulipas, Mexico. Brittonia. 37: 226-231.

description: Herba annua, erecta, gracilis, usque ad supra medium simplex; caule basim versus ca 3 mm crasso supra 1-2 mm crasso, demum brunneo-purpurascenti, hispidulo, aegre sulculato. Folia opposita, tenerrime petiolata petiolis 2-3 cm longis et numerosissime papillatis, hispidulis et conspicue vestitis capillis elongatis tenuibus squarrosis albis basaliter cylindraceo-incrassatis et interdum stellate ramosis ca 5 mm longis; lamina circuinambitu deltoidea vel ovata, 5-6 cm longa et lata, bipinnata vel bipinnatisecta, segmentis lineari-oblongis vel oblonga-lanceolatis, creberrime minutissimeque papillatis, marginibus setulosis, ad venulas irregulariter vestitis capillis elongatis albidis, ultimis ca 1 cm longis apice acutis et 2-6 mm latis. Capitula radiata pansa ad anthesin 2.5-3 cm lata et ea 1.4 cm alta. Involucri bracteae exteriores ca 10, lineares, conspicue elongateque albido-capillatae, 7-10 mm longae; interiores lineari-lanceolatae superne attenuatae apice irregulariter pubescentes, quam exteriores breviores. Flores ligulati ca 10, ligula subangusti forsitan lineari-oblongi, sicci (vivi ignoti) atro-purpurei, apice minute denticulati. Paleae diaphanae, oblongo-lanceolatae, superne acerrimae et longe ciliatae. Flores tubulosi ad summam basimque purpurei, alibi flavido-stra- minei, corollae tubo puberuli. Achaenia matura absentia; ovariis planis, oblanceo- latis vel anguste obovatis, faciebus marginibusque dense sursum adpresseque setulosis; apice biaristata aristis gracillimis rectis subrectisve minute antrorso- setulosis ca 6 mm longis.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1964. Some new or otherwise noteworthy Coreopsidinae (Compositae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 18: 58-73.

description: Annual herb, erect, slender, simple to above the middle; stem ca 3 mm thick toward base, 1-2 mm thick above, finally brownsh-purple, hispidulous, weakly sulculate. Leaves opposite, very slenderly petiolate with petioles 2-3 cm long and most abundantly papillate, hispidulous and conspicuously clothed with hairs, these elongate, slender, squarrose, white, ca 5 mm long, basally cylindric-thick- ened and at times stellate-branched; blade deltoid or ovate in outline, bipinnate or bipinnatisect, segments linear-oblong or oblong-lanceolate, very thickly and minutely papillate, setulose at the margins, along the veinlets irregularly invested with elongate whitish hairs, ultimate segments ca 1 cm long and 2-6 mm wide, with acute tip. Heads radiate, expanded at flowering 2.5-3 cm wide and ca 1.4 cm tall. Outer phyllaries ca 10, linear, conspicuously and elongately whitish- haired, 7-10 mm long; inner ones linear-lanceolate, upwardly attenuate, at apex irregularly pubescent, shorter than outer ones. Ligulate florets ca 10; ligule narrow, perhaps linear-oblong, in dry state (not known in living state) dark-purple, at apex minutely denticulate. Chaff-scales diaphanous, oblong-lanceolate, toward top very acute and elongately ciliate. Tubular florets purplish at top and base, elsewhere yellowish-stramineous, corolla's tube puberulous. Mature achenes absent; ovaries flat, oblanceolate or narrowly obovate, the faces and edges densely and appressedly antrorse-setulose; apex biaristate with very slender aristae, these straight or nearly so, minutely antrorse-setulose and ca 6 mm long.

description: Perennial herb with a slender upright subterranean stem having the form of a creeping rhizome, this giving off at intervals arcuate-ascending slender branches which, on reaching the surface, become erect aerial stems; stems sparsely or moderately strigose, the flowering ones sparsely leafy, the sterile ones, which arise as branches near the base of the flowering stems, densely leafy, the leaves longer than the internodes, these leafy stems perhaps later floriferous; leaves glabrous or nearly so except for the hirsute-ciliate margins, mostly about 1 cm. long or less, the lower narrowly oblong, up to 3 mm. wide, the middle and upper linear, 1.5 mm. wide or less; heads solitary, the disk 13-16 mm. wide; involuere about 6 mm. high, obscurely glutinous and sparsely strigose; phyllaries imbricate in several series, firm, long-acuminate, yellowish-green, with slightly darker midrib; ligules abouit 25-45, blue or white, 6-7 mm. long, 1.3-1.5 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.8-5.6 mm. long, the tube 1.4-2.0 mm., the limb but little wider than the tube, the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm. long; style-appendages triangular-lanceolate to lance-ovate, acute, 0.25-0.3 mm. long; pappus of about 25-35 fragile bristles, with a few short outer setae; akenes 5-6-nerved, neatly or quite glabrous. Known only from the type collection, McKinley County, New Mexico.

description: Herba perennis, caudice subterraneo erecto gracili ramis arcuati-aseendentibus, caulibus erectis sparse vel moderate strigosis ad basin ramosis, foliis subglabris margine hirsuto-ciliatis usque ad 1 cm. longis imis anguste oblongis usque ad 3 mm. latis, mediis et supremis linearibus usque ad 1.5 mm. latis, capitulis solitariis, disco 13-16 mm. lato, involuero 6 mm. alto sparse strigoso, bracteis duris perspicue imbricatis, ligulis 25-45 caertileis vel albis 6-7 longis 1.3-1.5 mm. latis, corollis disci 4.8-5.6 mm. longis, stylorum appendicibus acutis 0.25-0.3 mm. longis, pappo obscure duplici, achaeniis subglabris 5-6-nervis.
