description: Shrubs; stems canescent, becoming dark with age. Leaves cauline, crowded, the sessile blades 0.7-1.1 x 0.1-0.2 cm wide, linear-lanceolate, widest below the middle, apically acuminate, basally cuneate to rounded, marginally entire and strongly revolute, glabrous above, canescent-tomentose below. Inflorescences terminal, of loosely syncephalous glomerules. Heads 3-4-flowered. Phyllaries loosely imbricate in several series, the inner ca 5 x ca 1 mm wide, tips acute. Pappus straw-colored; inner paleas flattened ca 4 mm long, outer scales minute, ca 0.5 mm long. Corollas ca 5 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers ca 2.2 mm long. Achenes (immature) unribbed, glabrous. Pollen type: A. Information is not available on flowering and fruiting dates nor on habitat.

description: Perennial herbs, hemicryptophytes, tubers elongate, cylindrical, diameter, stems 30-45 cm tall, branched or with only one branch, the branches long. Leaves densely disposed, alternate, spirally arranged, 15-35 x 1- 3 mm, narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, sessile, apex sub-acute, base attenuate, glandular (vesicular biseriate trichomes, notably sunken on epidermis) and woolly-villous (flagellate-septate trichomes) on both surfaces, margins entire, the basal leaves with one or two pair of lobes. Capitula solitary (rarely grouped in 2- or 3-headed capitulescences), terminal, sessile, heterogamous, radiate. Involucres 12-20 x 20-25 mm, hemispheric to globose; phyllaries in 5 or 6 series, tips reddish, outer phyllaries 7-9 x 0.7-1.1 mm, narrowly elliptic to linear, subulate, margin membranous, glandular and woolly-villous on both surfaces; inner phyllaries 10-13 x 1-1.2 mm, linear, apex subulate, margin membranous, glandular and woolly-villous on abaxial surface, glabrous or with little glandularvillous pubescence towards the apex on adaxial surface. Receptacles epaleate, with short scales. Ray florets arranged in 3 or 4 series, 100-150, pistillate, corollas white, true ray, tube ca. 4 mm long, limb ca. 17 x 1 mm, linear, minutely 2- or 3-lobed; style ca. 4.5 mm long, style branches 2-2.2 mm long, linear. Disk Jflorets ca. 150, bisexual (functionally male), corolla yellow, actinomorphic, 5-lobed, subcampanulate, tube ca. 2 mm long, throat 3.5-4 mm long, tube and throat laxly glandular (biseriate glandular trichomes), lobes ca. 1 x 0.5-0.6 mm, triangular, glandular (vesicular biseriate glandular trichomes) towards the apex; anthers ca. 2 mm long, antheropodium present ca. 0.6 mm long, anther base slightly sagittate, apical connectival appendages ca. 0.6 x 0.3 mm, ovate, style ca. 5mm long, style branches ca. 2mm long, narrowly triangular to oblong, whole abaxial surface covered by sweeping hairs. Cypselae 4-4.5 mm long, elliptic, flattened, strongly 2- nerved, gradually attenuated towards the apex, glandular throughout its surface, and villous mainly on the margins. Pappus ca. 7 mm long, of 2 or 3 series of scabrid, subequal bristles, sometimes with some outermost bristles very short, 1 mm long, all bristles tapering, somewhat flattened at the base.

description: Dioecious dwarf shrub, 0.2-0.5 m tall. Stems erect, shoots with abortive apex,  proliferating after flowering from subapical axils in dichotomous branches; young shoots reddish, resinous like leaves, with 5-7 basal and deciduous scale-like leaves; older shoots brownish or blackish, grooved or fissured, with petiole scars and resinous exudates along leaf scars; trichomes blackish emerging from bark grooves. Leaves spirally alternate, crowded at apex of branches, sessile; blades 0.9-1.5x0.3-0.6 cm, fleshy, appearing coria- ceous in dried material, obovate to spathulate, base cunéate, apex obtuse, margins entire, flat or slightly revolute, resinous, 1 -veined; both surfaces appearing glabrous, but covered with small tufts of trichomes and solitary biseriate trichomes, abaxial surface with resinous dots, adaxial surface vernicose, strongly resinous. Capitula 1-2 per shoot apex, axillary, solitary, subapical, peduncles 1.3-3 mm long, with longitudinal slightly spiralled ribs. Male capitula 5-6.2 mm long, involucre 4- 4.4 mm long, 3^-. 3 mm diam., cylindrical to campanulate; phyllaries 4- or 5 -seriate, outer and median ovate, inner linear to ovate, apex dentate, margins pale-yellow, narrowly scarious; clinanthium flat, glabrous, alveolate; paleae absent. Male florets 25-44; corolla 3- 3.3 mm long, apex 5-lobed, tubular, tube 2.2- 2.5 mm long, with sparse uniseriate trichomes in lower 2/3, slightly expanded and with several biseriate trichomes in apical 1/3, throat 0-0.2 mm long, cup-shaped, lobes 0.8-1 mm long, apex not revolute; anthers not exceeding corolla; styles 3.3-3.6 mm long, apex appearing rhomboidal by sweep- ing hairs of unequal size, slightly divided into connivent branches; sterile ovaries 0.7-1 mm long, light brown, nearly obconical, narrowed in proximal extremity, with 6-8 longitudinal ribs, sparse uniseriate trichomes near base and dense near apex; pappus 4-4.5 mm long, white, uniseriate, bristle apex dilated, with erect, shortly protruding cell ends. Female capitula poorly preserved, involucre 3.7- 5.2 mm long, 4.8-6.8 mm diam., campanu- late; phyllaries like those of male capitulum; clinanthium slightly convex, glabrous, alveo- late, paleae absent. Female florets filiform; corollas 2.7-3.1 mm long, with 5 apical teeth, with sparse trichomes throughout length; styles 3-3.9 mm long, branches ca. 0.2 mm long. Cypselae 1.9-2.2 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm wide, light brown, cylindrical, narrowed at base, with 8-10 strong longitudinal ribs, without papillae, glabrous; pappus 3-3.6 mm long, white, slightly shorter than style, multiseriate, bristle apex dilated, with erect, shortly proturding cell ends, deciduous, not accrescent at maturity.
bibliographicCitation: Heiden, Gustavo & Meireles, L. D. 2010. A new dwarf shrubby species of Baccharis subg. Baccharis (Asteraceae, Astereae) from southeastern Brazil. Brittonia. 62 (3): 215-218.

description: Herba circa 40 cm alta robusta erecta glaberrima. Folia alterna sessilia crasse herbacea elliptico-lanceolata acutissima basi cordata auriculato-amplexicaulia margine leviter revoluta grosse dentata dentibus triangularibus acutis, 5-7 cm longa 2-2.5 cm lata, supra viridia sublaevia nervis paulo conspicuis, subtus costa crassiuscula nervis secundariis 12-14 utroque latere aseendentibus tenuibus prominulis venulis laxe reticulatis conspicuis. Capitula radiata in paniculis oligocephalis foliosis terminalibus. Pedunculi 20-30 cm longi erecti crassiusculi sursum paucis bracteis foliaceis 1.5-2 X 0.5-0.6 cm aliquando involucrum superantibus; bracteolis aliquis 8-10 oblongis subite acutatis apice penicillatis reliqua glaberrima 8-10 mm longis 1.5-2 mm latis calyculo instructis. Involucrum late cupulare 17-21 bracteis herbaceis lanceolatis apice ciliatis reliquum glabris circa 11 mm longis exterioribus 1.8 mm latis interioribus marginibus scariosis 3 mm latis. Flores radii feminei ligulati 17-21 corolla lutea glabra circa 17 mm longa tubulo subeapillari 5 mm longo lamina elliptico-oblonga 4-nervia apice minute denticulata circa 12 mm longa 4.5 mm lata; rami styli paulo exserti tenues apice truneato brevi-papilloso-penicillato. Flores disci hermaphroditi numerosi, corolla lutea glabra 7-7.5 mm longa tubulo 2 mm longo limbo tubuloso apice 5 dentibus oblongis obtusiusculis circa 0.6 mm longis; antherae 2 mm longae basi obtusiuseulae. Rami styli apice truneato papilloso-penicillato. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus albus sericeus 6-7 mm longus pilis biseriatis strictis breviter strigulosis.

description: Herba perennis suffrutescens decumbens; ramis 3-4 dm. longis, fragilibus; petiolo 2-3 cm. longo; foliis dense alternantibus, 3-5 cm. long, adscendentibus, 3-5-foliolatis; petiolulis 4-6 mm. longis; lobis ovatis vel lneari-lanceolatis 8-16 mm. longis, sparse hispidulosis; capitulis longe pedunculatis, multifloris, campanulatis, 7-8 mm. altis; phyllariis ca. 60, aculeatissimis glabris; corolla viridi-alba 3.4 mm. longa; achaeniis nigris 1.5 mm. longis, 5-angulatis, strigosis; setis pappi 5 puniceis, 3.5 mm. longis, antrorse barbatis.

description: Suffrutescent, decumbent, cespitose herb forming, an irregular spreading clump 3-4 dm. high; branches sagging, brittle, brownish; diffusely branched distally, leafy, the older wood glabrous, the younger white-pubescent. Leaves closely alternate, 3-5 cm. long including petiole 2-3 cm. long, ascending, pinnately dissected into three or rarely 5 petioluled, variously lobed, thin, acutish leaflets finely, sparsely, and shortly hispid above and below; peduncles slender, 7-9 cm. long, sparingly, finely hispid; heads many-flowered, broadly campanulate, 7-8 mm. high, 6-7 mm. wide; bracts about 60, glabrous, lucid, finely acute, 5-striate, with a median brown streak; corolla greenish-white, narrowly tubular, 3.5 mm. long, lobes minute, blunt; pappus of 5 pinkish awns, finely antrorsely barbed, as long as or slightly longer than the corolla, and with alternating simple or laciniate paleae; achenes black, 1.5 mm. long with 5 angles sparsely and finely strigillose and basal disk-like callous.

description: Subshrub to 2 m. high, branches 5 mm. thick, subsucculent, strongly and sharply angled (at least when dry), internodes 1.0-2.5 cm. long, pith brown; leaves opposite, sessile, subsucculent 5-10 cm. long, 2-4 cm. broad, obovate-cuneate or elliptic-cuneate, the apex acute, serrate, the teeth low and blunt, pinnately veined, the midrib prominent, lateral veins prominulous, the surfaces drying somewhat reticulate; inflorescence compactly corymbose, rounded, 3-4 cm. long, 3-6 cm. broad, the branches glabrous, sharply angled, bracteoles linear; heads 8-10 flowered, peduncles about 1 mm. long, receptacle convex, glabrous, 0.5-0.75 mm. high; involucre 3-4-ranked, 5-6 mm. long, the bracts subequal, linear-oblong or linear-lanceolate, 4-5 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide, obtuse, cucullate, glabrous, subcrassulous, 3-4 nerved, corolla 4 mm. long, glabrous except for the five 0.2-0.3 mm. long, hispidulous teeth; anther appendages slightly exserted; achenes 2 mm. long, dark ash-brown, sharply angled, glabrous, or the angles slightly hispid- ulous, callous oblique, pappus capillary, 3-4 mm. long, the bristles slender, essentially free to the base, neither connate nor deciduous in a ring.

description: Basally woody perennial herbs or subshrubs to ca. 1m tall, xylopodium not seen. Leaves opposite throughout; petioles up to 1 cm long; blades 6-8x3-3.5 cm, coriaceous, rigid, oblong or oblong-elliptic, obtuse to very shortly attenuate at the base, very shortly acuminate to acute at the apex, margins toothed, adaxial surface scabrous, asperous, búllate, the abaxial pilose, prominently reticulate. Outer phyllaries 7-9 (16) x 6-10 mm, mostly smaller than the inner, erect, not surpassing the disc, elliptic to obovate, constricted at the base, rounded and mucronulate at the apex; inner phyllaries 9-12 x 3-6 mm, spatulate to oblong-obovate and more scari- ous. Paleae ll-12 x ca. 1 mm when folded, with rounded tip up to 2 mm long. Ray florets sterile, tube 1.5-2 mm long, lamina 16-19x 5-7 mm, oblong to elliptic, sparsely setulose abaxially. Disc florets with corollas 5.5-6 mm long, lobes with a few trichomes abaxially. Cypselae 6-6.5 x ca. 3 mm, laterally flattened, wings up to ca. 2 mm wide; pappus with awns 4-5 mm long, broad at the base, the longest awns mostly ca. one half or less than 3/4 of the cypsela length, crown ca. 1.5 mm high, partially fused to the cypsela body (less than 1/3), with laciniate margins.

description: Plantae suffruticosae, glabrae, aliquando glaucae, punctis disipatis parvulis albis; caulibus erectis, purpureo-viridibus vel maturitate purpurescentibus, teretis, striatis; foliis alternis vel oppositis, sessilibus, 2-6 cm longis, filiformis, glandibus magnis rubro-fuscatis; capitulis solis in pedunculis ca 1-2 cm longis vel in corymbis laxis; phyllariis 5, viridibus vel purpurescentibus, 11.7-14.4 mm longis, 1.7-2.1 mrn latis, linearibus, glandibus linearibus 1-2-ordinatis, apicibus acutis; flosculis 20-25; corollis 6.8-8.4 mm longis, hispidulosis, puniciis albisque; pappis 6-7.8 mm longis, setis breve hispidis; achaeniis linearibus, nigris, 6.3-7.9 mm longis scabrescentibus.

description: Frutex scandens, ramis cinereo-lepidotis. Folia alterna, subcoriacea, oblonga, (3.5) 4.5-9 x 1.5-3 cm, supra glabra, infra cinereo-lepidota; petioli 7-14 mm longi. Inflorescentiae axillares dense cor- ymbosae glomeratae. Capitula 3-flosculosa, solitaria vel bina vel tria aggregata, pedunculis ramosis; involucrum ovoideum vel cylindricum 7-8 x 2-3 mm; phyllaria irregulatim imbricata 5-7-seriata, flavo-brunnea, purpurea ad apicem vadatim tridentata. Corollae rubro-purpuratae, tubo (5.5) 6-7 (7.5) mm longo, lobis 2.5-3 (3.5) mm longis; antherae (3.6) 4-4.5 mm longae, basi auriculis 0.3-0.4 mm et longis subelongatis subacutis praeditae. Pappi albi biseriati setae interiores filiformes (8) 9-9.5 mm longae, exteriores lineares vel filiformes, inaequales, interdum deciduae 0.5-2.5 mm longae. description: Scandent to subscandent shrubs; branches widely spreading, terete, finely striate, cinereous-lepidote, lateral flowering branchlets numerous, short. Leaves somewhat crowded towards the end of lateral branchlets; petioles slightly furrowed, cinereous-lepidote 7-14 mm long; blades subcoriaceous, oblong, (3.5) 4.5-9 x 1.5-3 cm, obtuse or subacute, rarely acute at apex, narrowly rounded to slightly oblique at base, margins often conspicuously dentate, glabrous above, cinereous scales with resinous dots in center beneath, 4-8 lateral veins on each side. Inflorescences axillary, dense corymbose clusters of (5) 10-30 heads. Heads of 3 florets, solitary or in groups of two or three at end of branching peduncles; involucre ovoid to cylindrical 7-8 x 2-3 mm; phyllaries irregularly imbricate in 5-7 series, yellow-brown, maroon at shallowly trident apex; tomentulose-glandular below tip, marginally sparsely arachnoid to ciliate, outer ones oval to elliptic, inner ones narrowly elliptic, curling. Corollas red-purple, tube sparsely pilose and white gland-dotted (5.5) 6-7 (7.5) mm long, the lobes 2.5-3 (3.5) mm, outer surface densely glandular at apex, anthers white (3.6) 4-4.5 mm long, basal auricles 0.3-0.4 mm long, slightly elongated and tapered, subacute at tip. Pappus white, biseriate, inner bristles filiform (8) 9-9.5 mm long, outer bristles linear or filiform, unequal, often deciduous 0.5-2.5 mm long. Achenes ca 5 mm long, 10-costate, minutely gland-dotted.

description: Perennial reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes. Stems erect to spreading, usually more than 15 per plant, densely tomentose, usually simple to the inflorescence, some- times branched, 6-9 dm high. Leaves cauline, numerous and crowded, 6-12 cm long, 3-6 mm wide, linear-lanceolate, narrowed to a sessile base, densely tomentose above and below, with dense "longhorn" trichomes and bilobed glands on both surfaces, numerous awl-shaped trichomes below, not revolute or only slightly so, the tips acute, the margins entire. Inflorescence compact, sometimes branching and spreading, with few to many heads. Heads 40-60-flowered. Involucre broadly campanulate, 7-12 mm high, 7-11 mm wide; phyllaries spreading, greenish with purple margins; inner phyllaries sparsely pubescent, often glabrous along the margins, lanceo- late, 6-9 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, the tips attenuate; outer phyllaries tomentose, ovate with acuminate tips. Achenes deeply to slightly ribbed, usually glabrous or rarely bearing a few glands in the furrows, straw colored, ca. 4 mm long. Pappus white, the bristles ca. 7 mm long, the scales white, irregular, 0.5-2 mm long. Flowering from mid-July to September.

description: Perennial herb with a much-branched moderately slender caudex; stem 5-1l cm. high, finely strigose, lax or curved at the conspicuously smooth and shining somewhat indurated usually purplish base, leafy below, the leaves forming part of the basal tuft, otherwise essentially scapose; leaves numerous, finely strigose, oblanceolate, usually obtuse or rounded at the apex, occasionally acute, mostly 1.5-4 cm. long and 1.5-5 mm. wide, the petioles of the lowermost ones enlarged, shining, and indurated at the base; head solitary, the disk 13-18 mm. broad; involuere 5.5-9 mm. high, sparsely or moderately hirsute-villous or looselv strigose, and somewhat glutinous; phyllaries subequal or slightly imbricate, lolig-acuminate, usually slightly thickened on the back; ligules about 15-35, blue or purple, varying to white, 7-12 mm. long, 1.5-2.8 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.4-7.0 mm. long, the tube 0.9-1.5 mm. long, the lobes 0.7-1.0 mm.; style-appendages deltoid, acutish, about 0.2-0.25 mm. long; pappus of about 30-40 (rarely 50) slender but firm obscurely barbellate bristles, occasiolnally with a few slender obscure outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely strigose, sometimes glabrous below.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Plant mostly 1-4 dm. high, erect; leaves tending to be narrower and sparser than in the other varieties; heads solitary or few, the involuere and peduncle more or less hirsute, not or scarcely glandular; peduncles commonly less spreading and more nearly erect than in the other varieties; ligules generally narrower and often shorter than in var. debilis, white or sometimes pinkish; eligulate pistillate flowers generally few and inconspicuous.

description: Perennial herbs, 6-8 dm tall; stems whitish- to brownish-pilose-tomentose, becoming glabrate. Leaves cauline, somewhat remote; petioles 2-4 mm long; blades 12-15 cm long, 3.5-4 cm wide, oblong-elliptic to elliptic, widest at the middle, apically acute, basally cuneate, marginally revolute and minutely callous-toothed, glabrous above, whitish- or brownish-felted beneath. Inflorescences of a solitary head or racemose-cymose. Heads ca 70-110-flowered; peduncles 0.4-4 cm long, pilose-tomentose. Involucre broadly campanulate, 17-21 mm high, 15-25 mm wide; phyllaries imbricate in several series, whitish-floccose-tomentose, the inner ones oblong, acute to acuminate, 12-16 mm long, 2.2-3.6 mm wide, the outer ones oblong-lanceolate, 2.5-9 mm long, 2-3.5 mm wide. Pappus straw-colored, the inner bristles 11-13 mm long and outer scale-like bristles 2-3.5 mm long. Corollas 17-20 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers 6.1-6.3 mm long. Achenes 3.1-4.9 mm long, 8-10-ribbed, slightly pubescent to strigose on ribs. Flowering and fruiting from December to March.
bibliographicCitation: Jones, Jr., Samuel B. 1982. A revision of Vernonia series Buddleiifoliae (Compositae: Vernonieae). Brittonia. 34: 102-117.

description: Perennial herb with a short taproot and branching caudex, the primary branches usually branched again; stem up to 8 cm. high, finely spreading-hirsute, scapose or nearly so, the leaves all in a basal eluster, except for sometimes 1 or 2 linear and inconspicuous mere bracts; leaves linear-oblanceolate, tufted and erect, up to 4 cm. long and 2 mm. wide, the surfaces short-hirsute, sometimes sparsely so, or even glabrate, the margills coarsely ciliate toward the base with spreading hairs mostly 1 mm. long or more; leaf bases more or less conspicuously enlarged and chaffy, white; head solitary, turbinate, the disk 7-13 mm. wide; involuere 5-8 mm. high, finely glandular or viscid and more or less hirsute with long hairs, the longer ones usually well over 1 mm. long; phyllaries subequal, firm with brown or purplish brown midstripe and greenish borders, or more or less purplish throughout; ligules about 15-35, violet or purple, 5-10 mm. long, 1.3-2.5 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.9-5.5 mm. long, the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm., the tube poorly marked, but the whole lower half of the corolla slender; style-appendages deltoid and acute to ovate and obtuse, 0.2-0.25 mm. long; pappus of about 15-23 firm white bristles, commonly with some slender and inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, hirsute.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Shrubs to small trees, 2-6 m tall; stems 3 cm diam. toward base, striate, strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades 20-40 X 10-30 cm, broadly ovate, apices acute to acuminate, bases obtuse to shortly attenuate, sometimes decurrens on distal third of petiole; margins serrate, adaxial surface glabrate to strigose, abaxial surface strigose, hairs 0.6-0.8 mm long; petioles 4-19 cm long, 3-4 mm diam., glabrate to strigillose, hairs 0.5 mm long. Capitulescences paniculiform, with 400-600(-819) clustered capitula in terminal open branches, peduncles 0.5 mm long. Capitula globose to subglobose, (3) 4-6 mm high, 3-5 mm diam.; involucres cupulate; phyllaries 3, light green, ovate to suborbicular-ovate, 3-5 X 3-4 mm, 5-veined, abaxially glabrate to strigillose, hairs 1 mm long, margins ciliate on distal one-third. Pistillate forets 6- 8(-10), subtended by ovate paleae, 3-4 X 2-2.6 mm, strigillose toward apex, hairs 0.5 mm long, margins ciliate on distal one-third, 4-veined; corollas 3 mm long, 0.5 mm diam., white, 3-lobed, lobes deltoid, 0.4 mm long, scarcely pubescent at apex; styles 2.5 mm long, branches 1.2 mm long. Staminate fiorets 8-12(-14), epaleate (exceptionally, 1-2 disc florets subtended by narrowly lanceolate paleae); corollas 3-4 mm long, throats 2.5 mm long, 1 mm diam., white, 5-lobed, lobes 0.5 mm long, scarcely pubescent at apex; anthers 2 mm long, black; styles 3 mm long, ovaries 1.5 mm long, villose at apex. Cypselae 2.5 X 1.7 mm, pilose on upper one-third, hairs 0.5 mm long. Chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Arriagada, J. E. 2003. Revision of the genus Clibadium (Asteraceae, Heliantheae). Brittonia. 55: 245-301.

description: Shrubs, 2-3 m tall; stems branched, 2-3 cm diam., often strigose, hairs 0.1-0.5 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 5-16 X 4-10 cm, 3-veined, apices acuminate, bases attenuate, margins serrate, faces weakly to densely strigose, hairs 0.5-1 mm long; petioles 2-5 cm long, to 1 mm diam., strigose, hairs 0.1- 0.5 mm long. Capitulescences thyrsoid, 10- 25 capitula; peduncles 1 mm long. Capitula 5 mm high, 4 mm diam.; involucres cupulate; phyllaries 2, ovate, 3-3.5 X 2-2.5 mm, 5-7-veined, strigose, hairs 0.1 mm long, the distal one-third ciliate, apices acute, bases fleshy at maturity. Pistillate florets 30-40, in 5-7 series, subtended by ovate, 5-veined paleae, 2-3 X 1.5-2 mm, paleae strigillose toward apex, hairs 0.1 mm long, margins ciliate on distal one-third, bases fleshy at maturity; corollas white, 1 mm long, tubes 0.6 mm long, 0.4 mm diam., lobes 4, del- toid, shortly ciliate at margins; styles 1.5 mm long, branches 0.5 mm long. Staminate florets 8-9, subtended by lanceolate paleae, paleae 2 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, 3-veined; corollas 1.5 mm long, (4)-5-lobed, with deltoid lobes 0.5 mm long scarcely pubescent at apex; throats 1 mm long, 0.5 mm diam.; anthers 1.5 mm long, black; styles 2.5 mm long, branches 1.5 mm long; ovaries 1.5 mm long, 0.6 mm diam., pilose distally, hairs 0.5 mm long. Cypselae drupaceous, 2 X 1.6 mm, hirsute on distal one-third, hairs 0.5 mm long. Chromosome number, n = 16 (Stuessy & Arriagada, 1993).
bibliographicCitation: Arriagada, J. E. 2003. Revision of the genus Clibadium (Asteraceae, Heliantheae). Brittonia. 55: 245-301.

description: Basally woody perennial herbs or subshrubs 0.5-1 m tall, caespitose from a xylopodium. Leaves opposite throughout or sometimes alternate distally on the peduncles; petioles up to 7 mm long; blades 3-5*2.2- 5.5 cm, subchartaceous, broadly ovate to orbicular, rounded to truncate to subcordate at the base, rounded to obtuse at the apex, margins crenate-serrulate or sometimes serru- late, adaxial surface subtomentose or sometimes pilose-strigillose, mostly soft to the touch, the abaxial surface tomentose, grayish 3 -nerved from near to well above the base, mostly reticulate. Peduncles mostly slender or somewhat stout; heads subglobose; Outer phyllaries 7-13x5-10 mm, broadly ovate to elliptic; inner phyllaries 6-10x3-5 mm, elliptic, constricted at the base to obovate. Paleae 9-llxca. 2 mm when folded, with triangular to subulate tip 1-1.5 mm long. Ray florets absent or heads with a few small rays in transition to a tubulate shape, less than 10 mm long, rarely with deeply cleft linear laminas. Disc florets with corollas 4.5-6 mm long, lobes with a few trichomes abaxially. Cypselae 3.5-4.5x1.2-2 mm, slightly flat- tened, smooth or rarely sparsely and finely ruberculate, wings 0.5-1.2 mm wide, ciliate on the margin opposite the palea; pappus with awns 3-5.5 mm long, of the same length, longer or not less than % of the cypsela body, very broad and sometimes decurrent at base, crown up to 1.5 mm high, mostly laterally parted with squamelloid processes between the awns.

description: Rhizomes rather extensive, coarse, 2-3 mm. in diam., strongly beset with roots, the crown loose, frequently producing several stems in the manner of A. latifolia, or producing only a single stem; innovations occasionally produced, the leaves with petioles exceeding the blades; stems simple, 1.5-4.0 dm. high, green or occasionally red-tinged, subglabrate or short scabridgranular, frequently short-stipitate-glandular and puberulent toward the summit; herbage usually pale green; cauline leaves 3 pairs (occasionally 4), the blades ovate to elliptic, obtuse to truncate or subcordate at the base, minutely short-stipitate-glandular above and glabrate beneath, inconspicuously to strongly and irregularly serrate-dentate, -scabrid-ciliolate, the middle stem leaves the largest, with blades 4-8 cm. long, 2.5-6 cm. broad, mostly with winged petioles shorter than the blades, sometimes sessile, the upper leaves not greatly reduced, the lower most spathulate and reduced, occasionally petiolate; peduncles 5-8 cm. long; heads 3-5, rarely 1 or 7, campanulate-turbinate, 12-15(18) mm. high; perielinium strongly short-stipitate-glandular and scantily to moderately short-pilose; involueral bracts obscurely 2-ranked, the bracts 10-14 mm. long and ca. 2.5 mm. broad, lanceolate, acute to acuminate, uniformly short-stipitate-glandular; ray flowers 12-15, the ligules pale yellow, 18-20 mm. long, 4-6 mm. broad, tridentate, the teeth 1-1.5 mm. long, acutish; disc flowers broadly tubular, 7-9 (10.5) mm. long, the tube 3.5-4.0 mm. long, the limb 4.5-6.0 mm. long, the lobes acutish, the tube and the base of the limb sparsely short-pilose; achenes 5.5-6.5 mm. long, strongly angled at maturity, scantily short-hispidulous or hispid, sometimes also short-stipitate-glandular; annulus short; pappus -+ length of corolla, not copious, stramineous to tawny, subplumose, the setae 0.2-0.3 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Camp, Wendell H. & Gilly, Charles L. 1943. Part II: Systematic Treatment, [Arnica alpina-Arnica discoidea]. Brittonia. 4 (3): 405-457.

description: Herbacea vel suffruticosa; caules erecti, puberuli, striati, internodiis ca 1.5-6 cm longis; folia op- posita, sessilia vel brevipetiolata; lamina subcoriacea, elliptica, (1) 1.5-2 cm longa, (0.5) 0.9-1.3 cm lata, serrulata, undulata, subtriplinervis, glandulosa vel puberula; capitulescentia terminalis, cymosa; pedunculi nulli vel 2.5 mm longi; capitula homogama, paleacea; involucrum cylindricum, 10-12 mm longum, 3.5-4.5 mm latum; phyllaria gradata, 4-5-seriata, scariosa, sed dua externa herbacea adja- centibus multo longiora; receptaculi paleae elliptico-lanceolatae, 8.5-10 mm longae, integrae; flosculi radiati nulli; flosculi disci ca 16-18, corolla campanulata, ca 7 mm longa, glabra, luteola, lobis ca 2 mm longis; achaenia turbinata, valde angulata, pubescentia, 4-4.6 mm longa, stipitata; pappi squamae ca 12, distinctae, lanceolatae, 1.5-2.5 mm longae.

description: Annual, probably scented but nature of scent unknown. Stems several from the base, 10-15 cm long, densely puberulent with retrorsely curled trichomes, stramin- eous to purplish. Leaves lance-linear, 1-2.5 cm long, 1-2.2 mm broad, acute, mucronate or bristle-tipped, proximally ciliate to about the middle with bristles 2-4 mm long, glabrous or sparsely puberulent abaxially on the midrib with nu- merous round glands ca 0.2 mm diameter. Heads solitary at branch-tips, becoming cymosely clustered with age. Peduncles 3.5-4.5 mm long, puberulent, with 4-7 scattered setiform bractlets or the lowermost somewhat foliaceous. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 5, narrowly obovate, 6-7 mm long, 2-2.5 mm broad, acute with the abaxial surface strongly convex, keeled nearly to the apex, narrowly hyaline margined, sparsely puberulent near the apex, otherwise glabrous, streaked longitudinally with numerous linear glands. Rayflorets 5; corollas yellow, 7 mm long, with the tube 2 mm long, and ligule 5 mm long, glabrous. Disk florets ca 20; corollas 4 mm long, yellow, bilabiate with the anterior lip 1 mm long, ca 2 x the length of the lobes of the posterior lip, glabrous; anthers 1.2-1.5 mm long; pollen grains ca 32 gm diameter. Achenes of ray and disk similar, 4-4.5 mm long, strigillose or pilosulous with blunt-tipped bicellular trichomes 0.25-0.3 mm long. Pappus of ray and disk similar, of 30-40 antrorsely barbed bristles 3-4.5 mm long. Chromosome number: unknown.

description: Erect shrub 0.5-1 m heigh, stems striate, purple, white-tomentose, densely leafy at the inflorescence, internodes 0.5-2 cm long. Leaves alternate, sessile to subsessile, coriaceous. Leaf blades 3.5-5.5 x 1.2-1.7 cm, elliptic to lanceolate, denticulate, revolute at the margin, acute at the apex, basally cuneate, hispid above, sparsely lanate beneath, glandular dotted on both faces, pinnatinervate, secondary veins 10-13, slightly curved, prominent beneath. Inflorescence 10-15 cm long, terminal, paniculiform, individual branches corymbose, bracts greatly reduced or absent. Capitula shortly pedicellate, disposed in pedicellate glomerules or rarely solitary. Pedicels 2-6 mm long, densely tomentose. Involucre campanulate, 6-7 mm high, 6-8 mm diam. Phyllaries 6 or 7 seriate, loosely imbricate, mucronate, purple at the apex, outer phyllaries 1.8-3.5 x 1-1.5 mm, triangular to ovate, sparsely tomentose, often extending down the pedicel, the inner ones 5-7 x 1-1.8 mm, ovate-lanceolate, acute. Florets 15-20. Corollas 6-7 mm long, violet, glabrous, lobes lanceolate, 1.5-1.8 mm long. Anthers 3-3.5 mm long, basally sagittate. Stylus 8-9 mm long, densely pilose, branches linear, 2.4-2.7 mm long. Cypselas 1.6-2 mm long, ribbed, sparsely sericeous- pubescent. Pappus yellowish, biseriate, outer scales 0.6-0.9 mm long, linear-lanceolate, fimbriate, inner bristles 4-5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Dematteis, Massimiliano. 2006. Vernonanthura warmingiana (Asteraceae: Vernonieae), a new species from Brazil. Brittonia. 58 (2): 182-188.

description: Perennial herb with a branched caudex to which the fibrous or long-chaffy leafbases of several seasons adhere; stem moderately strigose to almost glabrous, 4-15 cm. high; leaves linear or narrowly linear-oblanceolate, sparsely strigose to essentially glabrose, the basal ones numerous, tufted, 2-8 cm. long, 1.5-2.2 mm. wide, the margins commonly ciliate toward the base, which is enlarged, somewhat sheathing, purplish or light straw-colored, and membranous or slightly chartaceous; cauline leaves few and reduced, mostly below the middle of the stem, often not exceeding the basal cluster; heads solitary, turbinate or sub-hemispherical, the disk 6-12 mm. wide; involuere 4-6.5 mm. high, more or less imbricate, moderately strigose or hirsute-strigose; phyllaries green or greenish brown, with darker midrib, the outer narrow, firm, and slightly thickened,, the inner broader and thinner, often with searious margins and purplish tips; ligules 15-55, white or pink, 4-8 mm. long, 1.3-2.3 mm. wide; disk-corollas 3.5-4.3 mm. long, the tube 0.7-1.1 mm. long, the lobes 0.6-0.8 mm., the limb contracted in the lower half, slightly flaring above; style-appendages deltoid or usually a little narrower, acute, 0.2-0.3 mm. long; pappus of about 15-25 very slender and fragile sordid bristles, sometimes with a few intermingled short setae; akenes 2-nerved, shortly villous-hirsute with ascending hairs, the hairs commonly denser and more spreading on the nerves.

description: Basally woody perennial herbs or subshrubs to ca. 1 m tall, branches stramineous, xylopodium not seen. Leaves opposite; petioles up to 1  mm long; blades 2-8.5 x 0.6 - 1.9 cm, length mostly 3-5 times width, submembranous, lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, shortly attenuate at the base, acuminate at apex, margins remotely serrulate, adaxial surface strigillose, the abaxial densely villous, with larger trichomes along the veins. Outer phyllaries 9 x 3.5 mm, oblong- ovate, indurate at the base; inner phyllaries 5 x2 mm, oblong - ovate, indurate and constricted at the base to oblong- obovate and more scarious. Ray florets sterile, tube ca. 1 mm long, lamina 15x3mm. Disc floret corollas ca. 4mm long. Paleae 6.5 -7 x ca. 1mm when folded, with rigid acute linear tip up to 2mm long. Cypselae 3- 3.5 x ca. 1.5 mm, thickened, subquadrangular, slightly tuberculate at maturity, wings much reduced, up to 0.5 mm wide, slightly asymmetrical, being wider on teh opposite side of the paleae; pappus awnless, crown reduced to a minutely ciliated margin.

description: Perennial herb with a stout caudex, about 1 dm. high or less; leaves, stem, and involuere densely gnaphalioid-lanate; basal leaves oblanceolate or spatulate, 1.5-3 cm. long, 5-7 mm. wide, rounded or obtuse at the apex; cauline leaves several, oblong or linear-oblong, about 2-3 cm. long and 5 mm. wide, acute or obtuse; head solitary, the disk 12-20 mm. wide; involuere about 8-9 mm. high, exceeding the disk, the phyllaries purple under the long dense tomentum, equal, loose, some of the outer sometimes reflexed above the middle; ligules about 75-100, 8-13 mm. long, a little over 1 mm. wide, white ( ?); disk-corollas about 3.5-4.0 mm. long, the tube 0.7-0.8 mm. the lobes 0.6-0.7 mm.; style-appendages triangular-ovate, acutish, about 0.3 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of 15-20 coarse bristles, the outer of conspicuous setose squamellae; akenes villous-hirsute, 2-nerved.

description: Suffrutescent herbs up to 12 dm tall, often much branched. Peduncles short, densely long hirsute, bearing heads 1.8-2.7 cm wide. Central cauline leaves sessile or short petioled, about 1/2 to %/n as broad as long, the wider leaves found on plants toward eastern portion of range; triangulate to ovate with serrate to partially doubly serrate to dentate margins; stiffly hirsute to subscabrous. Leaves well dis- tributed or crowded near summit; no persistent basal rosette. Ray-flower ligules 10.5-17 mm long, 6.5-9 mm wide, deep yellow to orange-yellow, with green veins beneath. Disk-flower corollas red to maroon. Achenes large, ovate, 4.5-6 mm long, 3-4.8 mm wide. Plants commonly of sandy soils, at woodland margins or of open or grazed woodlots, on hillsides or along lightly shaded river banks.

description: Viscid, spreading shrubs to about 6 dm high from a thick, woody taproot; branching at the root apex and above. Stems and branches usually white; main stems to 6 mm in diameter; upper branches 1-3 mm in diameter, glandular-hispid with short, stout trichomes, occasionally with a few longer, soft hairs in addition. Leaves oblanceolate to orbicular, 1.2-3.6 cm long, 0.4-2.5 cm wide, glabrous to scabrous with glandular trichomes; apex obtuse to acuminate, spinulose or mucronate; base cuneate to auriculate and subclasping, the auricles obtuse to acute; margins spinulose-dentate to subentire, 2-20 teeth per leaf; lower leaves largest, gradually reduced upwards. Heads solitary at the ends of branches, sessile or nearly so, campanulate or hemispherical, 1.2-2.4 cm wide. Involucre loosely imbricated; phyllaries in 4-6 series; outermost phyllaries linear- lanceolate, herbaceous for 1/2 to 3/4 of their length, scarious below, basally keeled or not, 3.4-8 mm long, 0.6-1.1 mm wide, glabrate to scabrous, usually glandular, entire or with thin, fimbriate, hyaline margins, the apex attenuate to acuminate; innermost phyllaries equal to or shorter than the immediately preceding series, largely scarious with a herbaceous splotch at the apex, keeled basally, 8.5-12.5 mm long, 0.7-1.2 mm wide, the apex acute to acuminate. Ray flowers 24-44 per head; tube slender, 3.7-5 mm long; ligule light blue, oblong, 7.4-12 mm long, 1.8-2.4 mm wide, obscurely to distinctly 3-toothed. Disc flowers 32-77 per head; corolla 6.5-8.5 mm long, narrowed below into a slender tube, 4-5 mm long, and expanded above into a narrowly funnel- form throat; style branches linear, 1-1.8 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, the appendages acute, 0.2-0.4 mm long, shorter than the stigmatic lines. Pappus of 32-40 stout, unequal bristles, the largest up to 6.5 mm long. Achenes fusiform, slightly compressed, with several strong costae, velutinous with long, silky, subappressed hairs. Chromo- some number n = 6.

description: Herbae annuae 10-20 cm altae, caulibus erectis tenuibus maculatis, maculis purpureis vulgo ad bases trichomatum limitatis; folia opposita; laminae ovatae 1.5-4 cm longae minute dentatae ad basem angustatae nervis 3 prominulis divaricatis, petioli alati 2-5 mm longi, folia vetustiora maculata maculis remotis ut in S. agresti; capitula parva 3-4 mm longa turbinata solitaria pedunculis brevibus 2-10 mm longis vel in cymulas 3-5 capitatas conferta; phyllaria exteriora 4 argute reflexa ca 1.6-2.0 mm longa linearia prominenter ciliata trichomatibus ad 0.75 mm longis; phyllaria interiora 3-4 ad basem gibbosa, 5-nervata 3.0-3.4 mm longa; receptaculum breviconicum paleaceum; flores radiati 3, pistillati seminiferi epapposi, ligulis albis 3-lobatis ca 1 mm longis, tubulis brevibus ca 2 mm longis dense pubescentibus; flores disci 6-8 ut videtur bisexuales sed steriles 5-lobati, antheris cum appendiculibus vestigialibus ca 0.6 mm longis; styli bifidi rami breves angusti acuti. Achaenia abovoidea striata glabra nigra ca 2 mm longa. Chromosomatum numerus n = ca 45.

description: Annual herb 10-20 cm tall; stems erect, delicate, spotted purple (the colored area mostly confined to the base of trichomes). Leaves opposite; blades ovate, 1.5-4.0 cm long, minutely dentate with 3 prominent nerves diverging from the base, narrowing into a winged petiole, 2-5 mm long, the older leaves with scattered resinous dots as in S. agrestis. Heads small, 3-4 mm long, turbinate, borne singly on short pedicels 2-10 mm long, or 3-5 in clustered cymules. Outer involucral bracts 4, sharply reflexed, ca 1.6-2.0 mm long, linear, prominently ciliate, the trichomes up to 0.75 mm long. Inner bracts 3-4, gibbous at the base, 5-nerved, 3.0-3.4 mm long. Receptacle short-conical, chaffy. Ray florets 3, pistillate and fertile, epappose; ligules white, 3-lobed, ca 1 mm long; the tube short, ca 0.2 mm long, densely pubescent. Disk florets 6-8, perfect but sterile, 5-lobed, the anthers short, ca 0.6 mm long, including the vestigial appendages; style bifid, the branches short, narrow, and acute at the apex. Achenes obovoid, striate, glabrous, black, ca 2 mm long. Chromosome number, n = ca 45 pairs.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1978. New Taxa from the Avila and Naiguata Mountains, Venezuela. Brittonia. 30 (1): 39-49.

description: Herba elata, caulibus erectis, pluricostatis, glabris, usque ad inflorescentiam foliosis. Folia densa, alterna (internodiis superioribus 1.5-2 cm. longis), breviter petiolata, petiolo tomentuloso 5-10 mm. longo, lamina elliptica, pinnativenosa, apice acuta, basi breviter attenuata, margine serrata (dentibus utroque latere 20-25) nonnunquam revoluta, superne glabra, inferne persistenter denseque griseo vel ochraceo-tomentosa, 9-10 cm. longa, 2.5-3 cm. lata. Capitula multa, radiata, in paniculis corymbis definitis disposita. Pedicelli lanosi, 2-6 mm. longi. Involu- crum campanulatum, calyculatum, 6-7 mm. altum, 5-6 mm. crassum, quam floribus disci breviore; bracteolis calyculi paucis, brevibus, lanuginosis; bracteis involucri ca. 10, aliis oblongis, angustis, acutis, aliis latioribus, sub-obtusis, scarioso-marginatis, utrisque apice ciliatis, dorso glabrescentibus. Flores lutei, dimorphi: marginales ca. 5, feminei, ligulati: tubulo ca. 3 mm. longo, ligula 7 mm. longa, 2.2-2.5 mm. lata, apice profunde tridentata. Flores disci ca. 18, hermaphroditi, corolla tubulosa 10 mm. longa, apice profunde pentadentata: tubulo 4 mm. longo, limbo 10-nervato 6 mm. longoo, dentibus acutis 1.6 mm. longis. Antherae basi rotundatae. Styli rami apice truncati, cum corona pilis et penicillo longiori in medio nascente muniti. Achaenia cylindracea, costata, glabra. Pappus albus, ca. 10 mm. longus.
bibliographicCitation: Cabrera, Ángel L. 1950. Notes on the Brazilian Senecioneae. Brittonia. 7: 53-74.

description: Perennial herb with a branehed eaudex to which the chaffy leaf bases of many seasons adhere; stems wiry, ascending or erect, 5-30 cm. high, finely glandular under the heads, otherwise essentially glabrous; leaves glabrous or sparsely strigose, the basal ones linear or narrowly linear-oblanceolate, about 1-8 cm. long and 1-2 mm. wide, rarely 5 mm. wide, with broad firm light-colored bases suggestive of those of E. linearis; eauline leaves linear, 5-25 mm. long; heads solitary or sometimes 2 or 3, rarely up to 9, the disk 6-10 mm. wide; involucre 4-6 mm. high, finely and copiously glandular; phyllaries imbricate in several series, firm, greenish brown, with brown midrib and often purplish tips, the innler sometimes with scarious margins; ligules 10-25, blue, 4-8 mm. long, 1.0-1.8 mm. wide; diskcorollas about 2.5-4.2 mm. long, the tube 0.5-0.8 mm. long, the lobes 0.6-0.7 mm.; style-appendages varying from narrowly triangular-lanceolate to almost deltoid, sharply acute, 0.2-0.25 mm. long; pappus of about 10-16 slender and fragile slightly sordid bristles, with a few short setae intermingled; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely strigose or somewhat hirtellous.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herba perennis decumbens; caules pauci subsimplices sparse pilosi, pilis adscendentibus v. subappressis; folia inferiora rhombico-ovata media et superiora lanceolata obtusiuscula v. acuta basi cuneata pauci serrata utrinque sparse hirsuta; capitula solitaria longe pedunculata; involueri phyllaria ovata obtusa dorso glabra basi sparse ciliata apice minute subglandulari-erosa; radii 7 vel 8 albi; achenia radii et disci glabra epapposa.
bibliographicCitation: Blake, Sidney F. 1937. New Asteraceae from Guatemala and Costa Rica Collected by A. F. Skutch. Brittonia. 2 (4): 329 -361.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herbae annuae, 15-22 cm altae. Caules erecti vel decumbentes, basi subglabri, supra basin pilosi, pilis usque ad 1 mm longis. Pedunculi 1.3-1.7 cm longi. Folia sessilia, lanceolata, 2-3.3 cm longa, 0.4-0.7 cm lata, apice obtusa, basi obtuso- subauriculata, ambabus paginis parce strigosis, pilis usque ad 1 mm longis, marginibus integris (raro bilobatis), irregulariter ciliatis, pilis 0.3 mm longis (basalibus longiori- bus). Capitula 5-6 mm alta, 6-9 mm diametro. Involucrum extimum cupulatum, 7-8 mm diametro; bracteae 5, elliptico-orbiculatae, basi leviter connatae, 3-4 mm longae, 2.4-3.2 mm latae, apice rotundatae, extus glabrae, marginibus anguste scariosis, ciliatis pilis usque ad 0.6 mm longis. Bracteae intimae involucri extendentes sursum in cucullo, apice cirrhosae; lateribus verrucatis vel tuberculatis; fructus 3 mm longi. Flosculi radii 6-8; ligulae luteaibus, ovato-oblongae, 3-3.5 mm longae, 2-2.5 mm latae, apice bidentatae. Flosculi disci circa 30; corollae flavae, lobis apice comosis. Paleae flavae apicem versus, oblanceolatae, 3.3 mm longae, apice rotundatae, marginibus apicum leviter erosis; costis conspicuis, glabris. Chromosomatum numerus ignotus.
bibliographicCitation: Stuessy, Tod F. 1970. Six new species of Melampodium (Compositae: Heliantheae) from Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 22: 112-124.

description: Perennial herb with a short caudex aind fibrous root system; stem erect, 2-20 cm. high, moderately villous-hirsute with spreading or retrorse hairs; leaves more or less hairy like the stem, the lower ones often glabrate by flowering time; basal leaves oblanceolate or occasionally spatulate, up to about 8 em. long and 10 mm. wide, rounded and sometimes mucronulate at the apex; cauline leaves generally several, more or less reduced, mostly broadly linear or narrowly lance-oblong, acute or acuminate; heads solitary, or rarely 3-4, the disk 12-20 mm. widee; involuere 6-8 mm. high, moderately villous, often more densely so toward the base, the cross-walls of the hairs clear, or rarely some of them lightly tinted with reddish purple; phyllaries suibequal, somewhat leafy-textured, the outer about 1 mm. broad or more, with purplish usually erect sharply acute or acuminate tips, rarely purplish throughout; ligules about 100-200, white to pink-purple, about 4-6 mm. long, 0.4-0.8 mm. wide, the tube usually with a few hairs over 1 mm. long near the junction with the ligule; disk-corollas 3.7-4.7 mm. long, the tube 1.4-2.2 mm., the lobes 0.4-0.6 mm.; style-appendages broadly triangular and obtuse to deltoid and acutish, 0.1-0.2 mm. long; pappus of about 20-30 brittle bristles, about equaling or sometimes slightly surpassing the disk-corollas, with a few short and inconspicuous outer setae; akenies 2-nerved, somewhat hirsute. East and west Greenland, as far north as about 70 degrees.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herba perennis usque ad 20 cm. alta, eaulibus moderate hirsuto-villosis pilis patentibus, foliis hirsuto-villosis imis plerumque plus minusve glabratis oblanceolatis usque ad 8 cm. longis 10 mm. latis, eaulinis reductis late linearibus vel anguste oblongo-lanceolatis, capitulis plerumque solitariis, disco 12-20 mm. lato, involuero 6-8 mm. alto moderate villoso, bracteis plerumque viridibus, ad apices purpureis non atteftuatis, ligulis circa 100-200, 4-6 mm. longis, 0.4-0.8 mm. latis, corollis disci 3.7-4.7 mm. longis, pappo subduplici plerumque corollas disci haud vel vix superante, achaeniis hirsutis 2-nervis.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and short branching caudex; stem erect, 6-40 cm. high, finely strigose and more or less silvery or grayish; leaves silvery-strigose, sometimes becoming greener at maturity, the basal ones tufted, oblanceolate or linear-oblanceolate, up to about 7 cm. long and 6 mm. wide, the blade ill-defined and mostly shorter than the petiole; cauline leaves reduced, scattered, linear or linear-oblanceolate, the lower ones sometimes as much as 6 cm. long and 3 mm. wide, usually smaller; heads solitary, the disk 10-18 mm. wide; involucre 5.5-9 mm. high; phyllaries strongly imbricate, the outer silvery-strigose, the inner sparsely strigose and often finely glandular, thinner than the outer and usually with straw-colored margins, all sharply acute or acuminate; ligules about 20-50, blue, or sometimes lavender, pink or perhaps white, 9-15 mm. long, 1.6-2.8 mm. wide; disk-corollas 3.8-5.6 mm. long, slender, the tube 0.9-1.3 mm. long, the lobes 0.3-0.5 mm.; style-appendages deltoid or usually broader, obtuse, 0.1-0.15 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 25-40 fine white bristles, the outer of well-developed but inconspicuous short bristles; akenes pilose, with 6, 7, or most commonly 8 prominent nerves, reputedly sometimes 10-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Perennial herb with a branched woody caudex; stem more or less strigose, densely so at the base, 10-50 cm. high; leaves more or less strigose, linear or linear-filiform, 1-8 cm. long, 0.3-2.5 or rarely 3.5 mmn. wide, well distributed along the stem, but the basal ones commonly longer, or more numerous, or both; heads solitary or several, the disk 5-18 mm. wide; involuere 4-7 mm. high, closely villous-strigose or finely glandular, or both; phyllaries firm, somewhat thickened on the back, subequal or more or less imbricate, usually greenish, often with darker midrib; ligules 15-125, blue, sometimes pink or white, 3-13 mm. long, 1.1-2.0 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 2.5-5.4 mm. long, the tube 0.6-1.1 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm.; style-appendages deltoid or narrower, acute or acutish, 0.1-0.3 mm. long; pappus of about 20-30 slender but firm white bristles, sometimes with a few very slender and inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, more or less hairy, or sometimes nearly glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herba robusta vel suffrutex ramis foliosis viridibus nitidis striatis sparse puberulis. Folia alterna tenuiter membranacea sessilia. Lamina late triangulari-lanceolata apice acute acuminata, infra medium abrupte in pseudopetiolum contracta basi in auriculas latas rotundatas amplexicaules dilatata margine acute dentata, 2.5-6 cm longa 9.8-2.5 cm lata (pseudopetiolo 1-8 mm longo 1-4 mm lato, auri- culis ad 15 mm latis), utrinque sparse puberula margine parce ciliolata, nervo medio notato subtus prominulo, nervis secundariis 7-8 utroque latere ascendenti- bus paulo conspicuis ceteris nervulis laxe reticulatis subobsoletis. Inflorescentiae in paniculis corymbosis oligocephalis terminalibus folia valde superantibus, axi ramulisque striatis erectis vel subpatulis hirsutulis. Pedicelli 5-20 mm longi teneres hirsutuli parce bracteati, bracteolis anguste linearibus flexuosis 10-5 mm longis. Calyculus 8-10 bracteolis subulatis 2-5 mm longis flexuosis parce hirsutulis. Capitula radiata. Involucrum campanulatum 21 bracteis anguste linearibus acutis 8 mm longis 1 mm latis pallide viridibus apice maculatis dorso breviter hirsutis. Flores marginales feminei ligulati 9. corolla lutea 11 mm longa tubulo capillari breviter puberulo 4 mm longo lamina elliptico- oblonga 7 mm longa 3 mm lata, 4-nervata apice minute 3-dentata. Flores centrales hermaphroditi tubulosi 51, corolla lutea subglabra 6.5-7.5 mm longa tubulo 2.5-3 mm longo limbo infundibuliformi dentibus triangularibus 0.6 mm longis. Antherae 2.5 mm longae basi obtusiusculae. Rami styli truncati paulo penicillati. Achaenia linearia 3 mm longa sed albo-villosa pilis strigosis tecta. Pappus 7-8 mm longus albus pilis capillaribus minute sparseque strigosis.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1956. Studies on Andean Compositae - III. Brittonia. 8 (3): 179-193.

description: A speciebus aliis omnibus Ambrosiae foliis 1-2-pinnatifidis segmentis lineari-filiformibus, involucris [male] profunde 5-8-fidis, capitulis [female] solitariis in axillis superioribus sessilibus 2-floris, spinis rectis conicis confertis differt.
bibliographicCitation: Henrickson, James. 1980. Ambrosia johnstoniorum (Asteraceae) a new species of ragweed from the Chihuahuan Desert. Brittonia. 32: 340-342.

description: Erect colonial perennials 2-5.5 dm high; stems woody and branched near base, sulcate, puberulent-strigulose above. Leaves opposite below, alternate above, obovate in outline, (1.5) 3.6-6 cm long, 1.5-4 cm wide, 1-2-pinnatifid into 5-9 linear-filiform, acute divisions (0.5) 0.7-0.8 mm wide, the lowermost divisions reduced, often opposite, distal divisions more alternate along midrib, strigulose, trichomes 0.2 mm long with broad pustulate bases and very slender antrorsely, appressed tips; midrib somewhat winged; upper leaves often with 1-2 reduced axillary leaves. Staminate heads in terminal racemes 1.5-5 cm long; peduncles 0.8-2 mm long, puberulent-strigulose; staminate involucres 4-5 mm broad at anthesis, deeply parted into 5-8 acute, subequal lobes (1) 1.5-2.7 mm long, sometimes the 2 adaxial smaller, surface strigulose-puberulent to strigulose; staminate flowers (9) 15-20; corollas 1.2-2.1 mm long, tuberculate-glandular outside; anthers with deltoid, inflexed distal appendages; receptacle with irregular lanceolate to spathulate glandular-ciliate squamae 0.6-1.5 mm long. Pistillate heads sessile or shortly pedunculate, solitary at upper nodes below staminate racemes; fruiting involucres (probably immature) ovoid, 3-5 mm long, 4-6 mm wide with 22-30 imbricate, erect, straight, broadly conical spines 1-2 mm long in 2-4 series, the outer ones longer, more flattened to concave adaxially at base and usually arcuate; pistillate flowers 2, style lobes 1.3-1.7 mm long; terminal beaks larger than lower ones at anthesis, 1-2 toothed.
bibliographicCitation: Henrickson, James. 1980. Ambrosia johnstoniorum (Asteraceae) a new species of ragweed from the Chihuahuan Desert. Brittonia. 32: 340-342.

description: Shrubs 0.3-1.5 m tall, branching from the base; stems unbranched or angularly so, gray-brown or brownish green below, brown or dark green above, usually with prominent leaf-scars; leaves dispersed evenly on stems or clustered at branch tips, spreading, ascendant-erect to appressed, narrowly obovate-spatulate to obovate or ovate, 1.0-8.0 cm long, 5.0-11.0 mm wide, dark green, bases truncate or cuneate, apices obtuse, acute, or apiculate, margins entire or minutely denticulate, glabrous to sca- brate. Capitulescences densely rounded- corymbose, occasionally flat-topped or somewhat paniculate, more or less bracteate; peduncles 0-2.5 mm long, extremely minutely scabrate-scabridulous; clusters of capitula borne in corymbs, these in turn borne corymbosely; involucres cylindric- turbinate, 3.7-6.0 mm high, 2.0-4.0 mm wide, phyllaries 13-25 in 3-5 series, often appearing 4-ranked, ovate, 1.0-3.0 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm wide, apices (to ¼ - 1/3 the total length) herbaceous, acute to acuminate, margins hyaline-winged in upper 1/4- 1/3; ray florets 3-8, corollas 3.2-6.5 mm long, tubes 1.8-3.2 mm long, limbs 2.0-3.5 mm long, 1.3-2.0 mm wide; disk florets 3- 10, corollas glabrous or minutely hispid-pi- lose at juncture of tube and throat, 4.0-5.0 mm high, tubes 1.0-2.2 mm long; styles to 6.0 mm long at full anthesis, branches 0.9- 1.4 mm long, appendages 0.5-0.6 mm long, narrowly triangular. Cypselas cylindric, 1.0-2.0 mm high, 0.3-0.6 mm diam., gray brown to bronze, trichomes 0.4-0.5 mm long; pappus of 30-70 fine, minutely barbellate bristles in 1(2) series, 3.5-5.0 mm high, yellowish white to whitish tan. Chromosome number: 2n = 9II (Anderson et al., 1974; Keil et al., 1988).
bibliographicCitation: Lane, Meredith A. 1996. Taxonomy of Gundlachia (Compositae: Astereae). Brittonia. 48: 532-541.

description: Plants annual or biennial, 1-8 stems from the base, 4-12 dm tall; leaves, of the basal rosette spatulate to oblanceolate, densely villous to woolly, undulate, entire, tapering at the base, 6-10 cm long, 2-4 cm wide, the upper gradually reduced, less villous, obovate to ovate, entire, sessile; inflorescence cymose or paniculate of cymose branches; involucre 12-18 mm high, 1-2 cm broad, the involucral bracts 9-14 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, attenuate, glandular and sparsely villous; ray flowers 22-40, yellow; disk corollas yellow; achenes 4-6 mm long, pappus paleae sub- equal, 1-2 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Wilken, Dieter H. 1975. A systematic study of the genus Hulsea (Asteraceae). Brittonia. 27: 228-244.

description: To about 1.5 m, stems many from the base (plants as large in diameter as tall), glabrous or rarely sparsely pilose; leaves 3-15 cm long, 2-8 cm wide, ovate to broadly lanceolate, 2-3 times pinnately divided, the ultimate segments variable, usually linear, oblong, or lanceolate, 1.5-5 mm wide, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, with punctate glands, petioles 0.5-5 cm long; heads 12 or fewer cymosely disposed, peduncles 2- 15 cm long, sparsely pilose; heads 2.5-5 cm wide at anthesis; outer involucral bracts 8, linear, 5-9 mm long, glabrous or sparsely hispid at the base; inner involucral bracts 8, 6-10 mm long, oblong, elliptic, or narrowly ovate, ciliate at the apex; chaff narrowly oblong to oblanceolate, 1-3 lobed at the apex, villous on the outer surface and at the apical margins, 5-6 mm long at anthesis; ray florets 7-9; disk florets 50- 75; achenes oblanceolate to linear, 4-7 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, aristae 3-5 mm long. 2n = 26 (Hartman & Crawford, 1971).
bibliographicCitation: Crawford, Daniel J. 1976. Taxonomy of Coreposis sect. Pseudo-Agarista (Compositae) in Mexico with additional comments on sectional relationships in Mexican Coreopsis. Brittonia. 28: 329-336.

description: Gracilis, aquatica annua, caule usque ad 80 cm alto; folia aeria cum basibus amplectentibus, margines eorum vel ilitegri vel diverse dentibus cuspidatis serrati; infloreseentia aliquot pauciramosa; involuera 1-1.5 cm lata, 0.4-0.7 cm alta; phyllaria herbacea vel scarioso-marginata oblongo- ad lineari-lanceo- lata, aliquantum resinosa, capitato-glandulosa; flores radii circa 35-50, 6.5- 9.5 mm longi, 2.0-2.5 mm lati, flavi; flores disci circa 125-140, 3-3.8 mm longi, flavi; rami styli disci appendiculis anguste lanceolatis, circa duplo ad quad- ruplo longioribus quam lineae stigmaticae instructis; setae pappi radii 2-5, disci 2-5; achaenia radii et disci similia, binervata, oblanceolata, glabra, luteo-oleagina.
bibliographicCitation: De Jong, D. D. D. & Beaman, John H. 1963. The genus Olivaea (Compositae-Astereae). Brittonia. 15: 86-92.

description: Slender herbs, up to 80 cm high, the stem few-branched above, irregularly furrowed with longitudinal grooves; submerged leaves not seen, deciduous; aerial leaves linear to linear-oblong or broader at base and apex than at middle, clasping, basally and distally serrate and entire about the middle or entire, rarely serrate throughout, the teeth cuspidate with often incurved apices; lower aerial leaves 2.8-4.1 cm long, 2.5-5 mm wide, the upper reduced, 0.8-2.3 cm long, 1-2.5 mm wide; heads medium-sized, few; receptacle alveolate; involuere 1-1.5 cm wide, 0.4-0.7 cm high; outer phyllaries widely spaced, oblong-lanceolate, cuspidate, 3-4 mm long, chartaceous, with herbaceous tips, abaxially capitate-glandular toward the base, and marginally so throughout; inner phyllaries lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, acute, 4.5-5 mm long, chartaceous, with herbaceous tips and searious margins, abaxially and marginally capitate-glandular; ray florets 35-50, 6.5-9.5 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, yellow, sometimes orange when dried, the ligule shriveling along the long axis upon drying, the apex 3-toothed; disk florets style branches of the disk florets with narrowly lanceolate appendages about 2-4 times the length of the stigmatic lines; pappus of both ray and disk florets of 2-5 unequal bristles, the longest bristles of the ray florets about equal to the length of the corolla throat, the longest of the disk florets about as long as the tube; achenes of ray- and disk florets similar, oblanceolate, 2-nerved, 3-3.6 mm long, 0.7-1 mm wide, buffy-olive; chromosome number n 6 (Fig. 17), deter- mined from PMC squashes (voucher, De Jong & Longpre 971, MSC).
bibliographicCitation: De Jong, D. D. D. & Beaman, John H. 1963. The genus Olivaea (Compositae-Astereae). Brittonia. 15: 86-92.

description: Frutices; inflorescentiis paniculatis; pedunculi 5-20 mm longi, bracteis minutis; involucrum campanulatum, phyllaria 5-6-seriatis; capitula 19-21-flosculosa; pappus duplex; exterior brevissimus, squamis crebris; interior pilosus, pilis albidis.
bibliographicCitation: Keeley, Sterling C. 1987. Two new species of Vernonia (Asteraceae: Vernonieae) from Panama. Brittonia. 39: 44-48.

description: Shrub to 1 m tall; stems green to brown, terete, striate, glabrous to strigose-hispid. Leaves alternate; petiole 6-8 mm long, strigose; blade narrowly elliptic, 6-15 cm long, 1-3 cm wide, shiny, glabrous to sparsely hispid on both surfaces with persistent trichome bases, paler below, apically acuminate, basally cuneate and tapering onto the petiole, margins entire, sometimes revolute. Capitulescences terminal paniculate cymes. Capitula on peduncles 5-20 mm long, some with minute bracts; involucre campanulate, 8-10 mm long, 8-10 mm wide; phyllaries persistent, imbricate, 5-6-seriate, brown with darker tips, lanceolate to oblong, sericeous to sparsely villous, margins entire, sometimes ciliate; innermost phyl- laries linear-oblong, apices acute to obtuse some with a short mucro, 6-7 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide; outer phyllaries elliptic to lance-elliptic, with prominently ciliate margins on the lower half, 1.2-2 mm long, 0.3-1 mm wide. Florets 19-21; corollas pinkish, sparsely glandular on tube, 6-7 mm long, lobes 2.5-3 mm long; anthers ca 3 mm long, base sagittate; styles ca 8 mm long, branches 2.5-3 mm long, slender with long sharply acute trichomes on outer surface. Achenes tawny to dark brown, ribbed, sericeous, ca 2 mm long; pappus white, biseriate, the inner of slender bristles, 6-7 mm long, the outer of somewhat flattened fimbriate scales, ca 1 mm long.

description: Plants annual (or biennial?), 30-60 cm high; stems erect, striate and commonly reddish, single from a relatively small tap root (stems often several following injury of primary shoot), the lowermost portion often conspicuously pubescent, becoming glabrous upwards; leaves alternate, the lower ones triternately dissected pubescent with spreading hairs, (the lowermost apparently forming a rosette but these soon deciduous); later leaves biternately compound to merely pinnate; mid-stem leaves glabrous with petioles 1-4 cm long, dissected, the ultimate divisions 5-30 mm long, 0.5-1.5(-2) mm wide; infloreseence of primary stem a relatively congested corymbose eyme with 5-30 heads; heads hemispheric, 8-10 mm across, about 8 mm high, 25- to 40-flowered, on glabrous peduncles 5-20 mm long; principal involueral bracts 8-12, ovate to obovate, 5-6 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, glabrous, with yellowish, membranous margins, obtuse or rounded at the apex; florets "yellow," distinctly zygomorphic; corollas 4-5 mm long (including the lobes), the tube cylindric, glandular-pubescent, 1.6-1.9 mm long; throat deeply 5 lobed, 3 lobes lanceolate-deltoid, the remaining 2 lobes united for 2/3 their length; style branches flattened, 1 mm long, stigmatic from the base, the apex terminated by an obtuse somewhat swollen appendage; achenes obpyramidal, 4-sided, 3-4 mm long, glabrous and nerveless on the faces, pubescent on the angles; pappus of 12-15 broadly oblanceolate to narrowly oblong-obovate, paleaceous scales 1-3 mm long, the mid-nerve of each scale extending to the apex and usually forming a short awn or mucro; chromosome number not determined.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1962. Taxonomy of Hymenothriz (Helenicae, Compositae). Brittonia. 14: 101-120.

description: Annual herbs usually with several stems originating at the base and then sparingly branched above, 1-4 or more dm tall. Stems narrowly winged by the decurrent leaves that do not extend from node to node, sparsely pubescent below, moderately to densely pubescent above with short, crisped hairs. Peduncles 2-12 cm long, ca. 2 times as wide at the top as at the base. Leaves moderately to densely pubescent, margins toothed or occasionally entire, apices acute to narrowly acuminate, midrib prominent but lateral veins obscure; lower leaves irregularly laciniate; middle and upper leaves irregularly laciniate or occasionally linear-lanceolate. Heads few to many, ovoid to globoid, 9-14 mm high, 9-13 mm wide (excluding rays). Receptacle ovoid, 5-6 mm high, 3-5 mm wide. Involucral bracts united at the base, reflexed at anthesis, densely pubescent. Ray florets ca. 10, ligules 8-10 mm long, 5-8 mm wide, yellow to yellow- brown, densely pubescent on the undersurface. Disc corollas 5-lobed, cylindrical to cylindric-campanulate or somewhat urceolate, 2.0-2.4 mm long, 0.7-1.3 mm wide, yellow-green with yellow-brown to purple lobes. Achenes 1.3-1.6 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm wide, pubescent with many relatively long, straight hairs. Pappus scales 6-7, 1.4-1.9 mm long, including the terminal awn which is ca. ?/, the length of the body, 0.5-0.7 mm wide. Chromosome number, n = 13.

description: Suffrutex caule basi prostrato ramis aseendelntibus dense lanatis copiose foliosis. Folia crassiuscula alterna oblanceolato-elliptica apice acutata calloso-mueronulata basi attenuata in petiolum ad 7 mm longum attenuata, margine integra, limbo 10-20 mm longo, 3-7 mm lata superiora sessilia; omnia supra viridia parce araneosa rugulosa tantum costa visibili, subtus dense subadpresseque albo-lanata tantum costa prominula. Capitula discoidea homogama solitaria terminalia, subcampanulata nutalntia. Ad apicem scapi pluribus bracteolis adscendentibus lanceolatis acutissimis extremo violaceo reliquo viridulis plus minusve lanuginosis 6-7 mm longis 1-1.2 mm latis involuero breviores ad modum calyculi subimbricatis instructis. Involuerum subcampanulatum 21 bracteis subbiseriatis lanceolatis acutis extremo apieeque ciliatis dorso violaceis sparse arachnoideis margine seariosis circa 9 mm longis, externis 1.5 mm latis internis 2 mm latis. Receptaculum alveolatum circa 4 mm diamitens marginibus al-veolorum dentatis. Flores omnes hermaphroditi circa 75 in capitulo, corolla tubulosa glabra 7.5 mm longa tubulo angusto 4 mm longo, limbo tubuloso-campanulato apice 5 dentibus oblongis recurvis rubescentibus instructa; antherae circa 2 mm longae lobis basi minute apiculatis. Stylus crassiusculus ramulis apice truncato papilloso-penicillato. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus albus 7-8 mm longis pilis biseriatis strictis minute strigulosis.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1960. Studies on Andean Compositae--IV. Brittonia. 12: 182-195.

description: Perennial herb to 1.5 m tall; leaves opposite, sessile or with a petiole less than 3 mm long, petioles clasping the stem, blades lanceolate, oblanceolate or elliptic, 3-10 cm long, 0.5-2.5 cm wide, sparsely pubescent to hirsute above and below with white arcuate-appressed, uniseriate trichomes; inflorescence a loose cyme, peduncles 1-12 cm; heads radiate, involucres hemispherical, 3.5-6 mm high, 5-9 mm wide; phyllaries subequal, 2-6 mm long; herbaceous, usually with scarious margins, striated, glabrous or pubescent on the lower, outer surface and margins with uniseriate trichomes; palea scarious, concave, lanceolate, 3-5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, entire or with 1 or 2 shallow lateral lobes; ray florets 5-12, the corolla tube 1.5-3 mm long, sparsely to densely pubescent with ascending 2-5-celled uniseriate hairs, the ligules quadrate to obovate, 5-9 mm long, 3-lobed; disk florets 35-65, 3.5-4 mm long, the corolla tube abruptly flaring into a tubular throat, pubescent with 2-5-celled uni- seriate, ascending trichomes, ray and disk achenes similar, obconical, 1.5-2.2 mm long, black at maturity, pubescent, ray achenes occasionally glabrous; pappus of 10-20 spinulose-fimbriate, linear-lanceolate scales, 1-4 mm long, ray achenes occasion- ally epappose; x = 8.
bibliographicCitation: Urbatsch, Lowell E. & Turner, Billie L. 1976. New species and combinations in Sabazia (Heliautheae, Galinoginae). Brittonia. 27: 348-354.

description: Arbuscula erecta 1.5-3.5 m caulibus ochraceo-lanatis. Folia (1.7) 3.5-6.1 x (0.3) 0.5-1 cm. lineari-lanceolata. marginibus valde revoluta. subtus cinereo-coacta, apiculata. Glomeruli subglobosi. capitulis 5-12-floris dense aggregatis. bracteis imbricatis suffulti. Pappi paleae biseriatae, internae 7.5-9 mm longae. externae 1.9-2.8 (4) mm longae. Achaeniorum costae ad apicem strigosae.

description: Shrubs to slender trees (Fig. 3), 1.5-3.5 m tall; stems lanate, ochroleucous, darkening with age. Leaves cauline, crowded, the sessile blades (1.7) 3.5-6.1 x (0.3) 0.5-1 cm, linear to lanceolate, widest at or below the middle, acute and mucronate, basally subcordate to rounded, marginally entire and strongly revo- lute sometimes glaucous, glabrous except pilose basally along the usually sunken midvein above, conspicuously cinereous-felted below, midvein prominent or obscured by pubescence below. Inflorescences terminal, of large, subglobose glom- erules with densely packed heads, subtended by overlapping clasping bracts. Heads 5-12-flowered. Phyllaries 6.2-9.5 x ca 1.6-2.8 mm, obtuse, slightly arachnoid dorsally. Pappus straw-colored; inner paleas flattened, slightly twisted, 7.5-9 mm long, outer scales separate, 1.9-2.8 (4) mm long. Corollas 9-10.2 mm long, whitish, glabrous. Anthers 4-5 mm long. Achenes 3.8-4.5 mm long, 10-11-ribbed, 4-sided, strigose apically on the angles. Chromosome number: n = 17 IIs, Smith 1013 (GA). Pollen type: A-B. Flowering and fruiting from November to January.

description: Slender, annual herbs up to 60 cm tall. Leaves opposite, subsessile or with petioles up to 5 mm long; blades 4.5-6.5x0.3-0.5 cm, submembranous, linear to very narrowly oblong-elliptic, attenuate at the base, acute to shortly acuminate at the apex, margins entire or obscurely toothed, adaxial surface with small, appressed and sparse trichomes, appearing subglabrate to the naked eye, the abaxial surface sparsely and appressed strigillose, 1- nerved. Outer phyllaries 6-22x1.5-3 mm, linear to lanceolate; inner phyllaries 4-5 x 3- 3.5 mm, broadly ovate, shortly acuminate to acute at the apex. Paleae 4-5 x ca. 0.5 mm when folded, slightly conduplicate, not cari- nate-alate, with subulate or triangular tip up to ca. 0.5 mm long. Ray florets sterile, tube 0.5-1 mm long, lamina 7.5-16 x 3.5-6 mm, oblong to obovate, glabrous. Disc florets with corollas 2.8-3 mm long, lobes glabrous. Cypselae 2.2- 2.8x1-1.3 mm, thickened, subquadrangular, wings up to 0.8 mm wide, those of the peripheral flowers wingless, densely tuberculate at maturity; pappus with awns reduced to tooth-like projections or less than one half of the cypsela body or awnless, crown 0.2-0.4 mm tall, partially fused to the body (less than 1/3), with minutely erose margins.

description: Rhizomes slender, 1.5-2.0 mm. in diam., brown, extensive, the scales soon disintegrating, producing one, or sometimes 2-3, approximate shoots; innovations occasionally developed, bearing ovate cordate blades on long petioles; stems simple, or branched below, 1.0(0.7)-3.0 din. high, slender, glabrate or sparingly strigose-pilosulose, becoming scabrid-pilosulose and stipitate-glandular above; cauline leaves 3-4 pairs, uniformly distributed on the stems or crowded toward the base, petiolate, only the uppermost sessile, reduced, and lanceolate, the lower leaves lanceolate-ovate to obovate, sometimes subcordate, coarsely crenate, somewhat sharply dentate or sometimes lobed, seldom finely toothed, the surfaces glabrous or minutely or coarsely scabrid-puberulent, the margins sparingly or densely scabrid; peduncles 3.0-10 cm. long; head solitary, 12-18(24) mm. high, campanulate-turbinate; perielinium sparingly scabrid-puberulent and stipitate-glandular to moderately pilose and glandular; involueral bracts 8-12, 11 (9) -18 mm. long, 2.5-4.0(5.0) mm. broad, oblanceolate, short acute to acuminate, sparsely pilosulose to pilose toward base, becoming only puberulent above, also frequently short-stipitate-glandular, ciliolate, the tips pilosulose within; ray flowers 7-10, the ligules 15-24 mm. long, 4.0-6.0 mm. broad, yellow, strigose on the back and also frequently on the upper surface, the lobes 1.0(0.5)-2.0(3.0) mm. long; disc corollas yellow, 8.7(8.1)-10.5(11.6) mm. long, the tube 3.0 (2.7)-4.3 (4.8) mm. long, broadly tubular, the limb and tube deilsely short-villous, the collar inconspicuous, the lobes sharply acute, 1.5-2.5 mm. long, pilosulose; achenes 6.0-7.5(8.2) mm. long, hirsute above the middle with double hairs ca. I as long as the diam. of the achene, becoming densely hirsute at the summit, glabrous below; annulus ca. 0.3 mm. long; pappus creamy-white, -+ length of the corolla, the setae not uniform, 0.15-0.25 (0.30) mm. long.

description: Plants 1-2 m tall; stem densely and softly cinerous-pilosulous to somewhat arachnose; leaves alternate; petioles-vl.5-5.0 cm long; blades ovate to lance- ovate, 11-15 cm long, 7-8 cm wide, acuminate, cuneate, crenate-serrate, above dull greenish, cinerescent-pilosulous, beneath densely and softly argenteous- pilose; heads 3-5 on peduncles 1-3.5 cm long; disk about 1.5 cm in diameter; phyllaries lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 9-11 mm long, 2.5-4.5 mm broad, with dark, striate, indurate sparsely pubescent or glabrous bases and acute, dark green, densely pilosulous, reflexed or spreading tips; rays 12-15, 7-13 mm long, 3.0-5.5 mm wide; disk corollas about 3.5 mm long, yellow, hirsutulous at base of throat, otherwise glabrous; pales acute, straw-colored with scattered black areas, hirsutulous at apex; achenes dark-speckled, about 3 mm long; pappus of 2 linear' lanceolate awns, 1.5 to rarely 2.5 mm long, squamellae sometimes present; pappus of ray flowers of lacerate squamellae. Chromosome number: n=17.
bibliographicCitation: Heiser, Charles B. 1957. A revision of the South American Species of Helianthus. Brittonia. 8: 283-285.

description: Perennial herbs to more than 3 m tall; roots fibrous but often partly tuberous; stems furrowed, purple-spotted, glabrous to densely pilose, to ca 3 cm thick; leaves to 39 cm wide, 68 cm long, sessile or winged to base, palmately 3-5-lobed and veined, ovate to deltoid, scabrous to nearly glabrous above, glabrous or resin-dotted and puberulous below, the hairs larger on main veins, the base abruptly cuneate to the winged portion; upper leaves sparsely dentate, often not lobed; peduncles glabrous, densely pilose, stipitate-glandular, or glandular-pilose; phyllaries 4-6, to 12 mm wide and 20 mm long, broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, glabrous above, glabrous or with sparse pubescence or greenish-yellow sessile glands below; ray flowers 7-13, the corollas yellow, to 3 cm long, ca 1 cm wide, the tube 2 mm long, pilose or glandular-pilose outside; disc flowers 45-80, yellow, ca 1 cm long, the corolla sparsely pilose outside; ray paleae broadly ovate, acuminate; disc paleae lanceolate, chartaceous; achene 6 mm long, 4 mm wide, longitudinally multistriate, ovoid and somewhat lat- erally compressed, first white, then red, then purple, and finally black.
bibliographicCitation: Wells, James R. 1965. A taxonomic study of Polymnia (Compositae). Brittonia. 17: 144-159.

description: Erect herb or shrub to 4 meters tall; sparingly branched; leaves, phyllaries, corollas, and styles bearing short stalked glands. Stems rounded, faintly striate, brown. Leaves alternate; petioles 3-7 cm long, not winged; blades broadly ovate, with a large dentation on each side, up to 17 cm long, and to 15 cm wide, lower leaves as much as 25 cm long and 24 cm wide, rather palmately veined; margin serrate, apex acuminate. Inflorescence a thyrsoid panicle, up to 25 cm long, and to 10 cm wide. Heads numerous, 5-6 mm high, ca. 25-flowered. Phyllaries ca. 15, oblong-lanceolate, with few striae, apex usually obtusely pointed, pubescent. Receptacle convex, chaffy. Corollas white, narrowly tubular, 3.5 mm long. Pappus of 25-30 white setae, ca. 3 mm long, not dilated apically. Achenes dark brown, 2 mm long, 4-5-ribbed, ribs setose. Carpopodium well developed. Pollen tricolpate, spherical, minutely papillose, ca. 20 µ in diameter.

description: Frutex satis ramosus ramis terminalibus dense adpresseque ochraceo-lanato-tomentosis valde foliatis, foliis patulis internodiis brevibus. Folia alterna rigide coriacea. Petiolus crassiusculus 1-2 mm longus lanato- tomentosus basi amplectens. Lamina anguste elliptico-oblonga vel elliptico-lanceolata utrinque subite attenuata subacuta, margine crasse revoluta, 6-12 mm longa 2.4 mm lata; supra nitida glabra et sparse minuteque spinuloso-tuberculata costa tantum conspicua impressa; subtus dense crasseque ochraceo-tomentoso-lanata costa parum conspicua. Capitula grandia solitaria ad terminationem ramulorum foliosorum sessilia. Involucrum turbinato-carnpanulatum 18 mm altum, bracteis crebris multiseriatis subpaleaceis anguste linearibus acutissimis, extus praecipue deorsum tomentellis, interioribus 14 mm longis 1 mm latis, ceteris gradatim brevioribus. Flores- radii feminei numerosi ligulati corolla 12 mm longa lamina 2 mm lata, ovario glabro pappo 7 mm longo. Flores disci hermaphroditi numerosi corolla tubulosa glabra 3 mm longa, stylo bifido ramis lanceolatis 2 mm longis, ovario glabro pappo pallide roseo 7 mm longo.

description: Suifruticose annual (or biennial?) from a well developed taproot, 30-40 cm high, very leafy throughout, the stems and leaves densely glandular-puberulent; stems stout, 3-5 mm in diameter at the lower internodes; leaves sessile, linear-oblong, the lower ones 20-30 mm long, 5-20 mm wide, irregularly and incisely dentate, the whole leaf crisped; heads on primary shoots 1-4, borne on short lateral shoots of the uppermost stem; involuere hemispheric, 6-8 mm high, 10-15 mm wide, enclosing 75-100 florets, erect at anthesis, later becoming reflexed; peduncles 4-15 mm long, densely covered with short-stipitate glands; involucral bracts imbricate, ea 35 in 3-5 series, linear-lanceolate, with green, spreading tips and searious margins, 3-8 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, densely glandular-furfuraceous, white and chartaceous below; receptacle flat; ray florets 30-40, the ligules 6-8 mm long, 0.8-1.0 mm wide, "purple" or "pink," only weakly enrolling on drying, tube 3-4 mm long; disk corollas yellow, 4-6 mm long, the lobes erect, 0.3-0.6 mm long; style-branches ea 1 mm long, with an acute ciliate appendage; anthers ca 1.5 mm long; achenes of disk florets, 2-2.4 mm long, oval or faintly 4-sided in cross section, sparsely pubescent throughout with closely appressed, ascending hairs; pappus composed of a single whorl of ea 30 bristles, 2.8-3.4 mm long; ray achenes sonmewhat shorter than those of the disk florets; chromosome number, 2n = 10.

description: Annual to perennial herb 8-40 cm high, aromatic; stems erect and often the basal branches decumbent, usually purple, glabrous; leaves opposite below, most of the upper ones subopposite; blades 15-30 X 8-26 mm, elliptic-obovate in outline, pinnately dissected into 5-9 obovate-oblanceolate segments, 4-10 X 3-5 mm, obtuse, slightly tapering at the base, sharply dentate, each tooth often bristle-tipped, with a circular gland near each tooth; heads solitary, terminal and in the upper axils; peduncles thick, naked, slightly dilated beneath the heads, 4-8 cm long, 1-2 mm thick, as wide as the branches; involucres fusiform to urceolate, 12-14 X 4-7 mm, with a basal annular enlargement; phyllaries 5(-8), connate, green or purplish toward the apex, with 1-2 rows of linear glands on each phyllary; ray flowers 5-6(-8), the ligules elliptic, 2-3 mm or 13-15 mm long, yellow-orange; disk flowers 10-20(-50), tubular, 8-10 mm long, yellow; achenes linear, 6-8 mm long, glabrous, striate, black; pappus biseriate, the first series of 5 scales with erose apices, 0.4-0.5 mm long and a second series of 3 scales with erose apices, 1.5-2 mm long plus 2 lanceolate scales, 4-6 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Villarreal-Quintanilla, José Á. & de la Rosa-I, M. 2002. A new variety of Tagetes moorei (Asteraceae), a poorly known species from central Mexico. Brittonia. 54: 164-167.
