description: Frutex scandens ramis volubilis leviter striatis lana arachnoidea ochracea decidua praeditis. Folia alterna petiolata coriacea. Petiolus 10-15 mm. longus ochraceo-lanato- tomentosus supra sulcatus. Lamina oblongo-ovata basi rotundata apice angustata cuspidata margine leviter revoluta repando minute dentata dentibus callosulis mucroniformibus brevissimis; 610.5 cm. longa, 2.8-5.5 cm. lata; supra valde junior indumento arachnoideo tecta mox glabra nitidula atroviridis minutissime prominuleque reticulato-venosa costa angusta impressa nervis secundariis fili- formibus impressis vel prominulis plus minusve notatis; subtus in sicco ferrugineo-ochracea dense pulverulento-lanato-tomentosa costa crassiuscula eminenti nervis secundariis angustis prominentibus 11-12 utroque latere valde patulis parallelis, remote distantia marginis arcuato anastomosatis, nervulis reticulum prominulum cum indumento subvelatum formantibus. Inflorescentiae axillares thyrsoideo-paniculatae folia longitudine sub- aequantes pedunculo valde flexuoso robusto striolato lanuginoso tomentello axi ramulisque araneoso-tomentulosis bracteis brevibus munitis. Capitula discoidea sessilia in glomerulis ad apicem et secundum ramusculos congesta. Calyculus 3-5 bracteolis angustis acutis lanuginosis circa 2 mm. longis 0.5 mm. latis. Involucrum cupuliforme extus crispo-lanatus ochraceus 8 bracteis ovato-oblongis acutis 3 mm. longis 1-1.5 mm. latis margine scariosis apicem ciliolatis dorso lanuginosis. Flores omnes hermaphroditi 13, corolla lutea 4-5 mm. longa glabra tubulo 1 mm. crassiusculo limbo campanulato subinflato plus minusve superne gibboso subapicem contracto apice dentibus oblongis 1 mm. longis. Antherae 1.5 mm. longae basi sagittatae. Rami stigmatici truncati. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus stranmineus 4.5 mm. longus.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1954. New species of Compositae from Ecuador, collected by W. H. Camp. Brittonia. 8: 39-79.

description: Vine. Lvs. subcoriaceous; deep green dull above, ochraceous pubescent below. Bracts pale green under the pubescence. Corolla tube notably gibbous, very pale greenish yellow. Anthers brown. Style branches deep yellow. Pappus white. W. H. Camp E-4580 (F, holotype).
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1954. New species of Compositae from Ecuador, collected by W. H. Camp. Brittonia. 8: 39-79.

description: The two varieties of T. pringlei are vegetatively very similar but differ in the structure of the head. In var. oligantha the heads are subtended by 1-5 instead of 5-7 accessory bracts, have only 5 instead of 8 phyllaries and 4-6 instead of 11-13 flowers. The corollas of all flowers of var. oligantha have revolute outer lips while the outer corollas of var. pringlei have spreading outer lips. In general, all of the parts of the head are smaller in var. oligantha. It seems likely that var. oligantha is derived from var. pringlei by reduction. Intermediates between the two varieties have been found in the vicinity of the Puebla-Oaxaca border where the ranges of the two varieties overlap (Anderson & Anderson 5368, 5381, 5649, all MICH).
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, Christiane. 1971. New names and combinations in Trixis (Compositae). Brittonia. 23: 347-353.

description: Caulis herbaceus, tomentosus. Inflorescentia terminalis, racemosa. Capitula ca 55-flosculosa. In- volucrum 12-13 mm longum. Phyllariorum apices acuminati. Achenia pilosa-strigosa.
bibliographicCitation: Jones, Jr., Samuel B. 1982. A revision of Vernonia series Buddleiifoliae (Compositae: Vernonieae). Brittonia. 34: 102-117.

description: Perennial herbs, ca 5 dm tall; stems tomentose. Leaves cauline, gradually re- duced upwards; petioles ca 2 mm long; basal leaves 7.5-9.5 cm long, 1.2-1.5 cm wide; cauline ones 4.5-4.7 cm long, 0.5-0.6 cm wide, oblong-elliptic to linear-elliptic, widest at or above the middle, apically rounded to acute, basally cuneate, marginally revolute and remotely toothed, slightly scabrous above, lanate be- neath. Inflorescences a single terminal raceme of ca 4-6 heads. Heads ca 55- flowered; peduncles 2-8 mm long. Involucre campanulate-cylindrical, 12-13 mm high, 9-10 mm wide; phyllaries tightly imbricated in ca 6 series, hispid, blackish, with a prominent midrib, the inner ones narrowly elliptic-lanceolate, acuminate, ca 10 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, the outer ones ovate-lanceolate, ca 3.5 mm long, ca 1.2 mm wide. Pappus straw-colored, the inner bristles 6.2-6.7 mm long and outer scales ca 1.2 mm long. Corollas 8.5-11 mm long, reddish-purple, hispid at tip of the lobes. Anthers 3.5-3.7 mm long. Achenes (immature) ca 2 mm long, ribbed, pilose-strigose. Flowering and fruiting from January to February.
bibliographicCitation: Jones, Jr., Samuel B. 1982. A revision of Vernonia series Buddleiifoliae (Compositae: Vernonieae). Brittonia. 34: 102-117.

description: Perennial herbs from a highly branched caudex atop a thick, woody taproot; often forming small colonies from lateral root branches; aerial branching confined to lower 1/3 of plant. Stems erect, (5.5) 9-15 (23) cm long, 1-2 mm in diameter, glabrate to sparsely pilose with longer, spreading hairs and with a sparse to dense additional vestiture of sessile or minutely stipitate glands. Leaves linear or slightly broader apically, (1.5) 2.5-3.5 (4.5) cm long, 1-2.5 mm wide, glabrate to densely pilose and usually moderately glandular; apex acute, mucronate; lowermost leaves with a slightly expanded and clasping base; margins entire, commonly involute. Heads solitary at the ends of the stems, campanulate or hemispherical, 1-2.5 cm wide, pedunculate, the peduncles (1.8) 3-6 (14) cm long. Involucre loosely imbricated; phyllaries in 3 or 4 series; outermost phyllaries oblong, elliptic or broadly lanceolate, herbaceous for 1/2 to entire length, scarious below, usually keeled basally, 2-4.8 mm long, 0.7-2 mm wide, usually moderately pilose with long, spreading hairs and with a sparse to dense additional vestiture of short, glandular trichomes, occasionally glabrate, with entire or thin, fimbriate, hyaline margins, the apex acute to acuminate; innermost phyllaries similar to the outer phyllaries, but usually larger, more scarious, and less pubescent, keeled basally, the apex acute to acuminate. Ray flowers 4-12 per head; tube 3.5-4.5 mm long; ligule white, oblong or narrowly elliptic, 0.9-1.8 cm long, 2-4 mm wide, obscurely to distinctly 3-toothed. Disc flowers 29-45 per head; corolla 6-9 mm long, gradually ampliate or narrowed below into a slender tube, 2-3 mm long and expanded above into a narrowly funnelform throat, style branches linear-subulate, 1.4-1.9 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, the appendages attenuate to acute, 0.8-0.9 mm long, longer to shorter than the stigmatic lines. Pappus of about 30-50 stout, unequal bristles, the largest up to 6.5 mm long. Achenes linear to clavate, 3.5-6 mm long, laterally compressed, velutinous with long, silky, subappressed hairs. Chromosome number n = 6.
bibliographicCitation: Watson, Thomas J., Jr. 1977. The taxonomy of Xylorhiza (Asteraceae-Astereae). Brittonia. 29: 199-216.

description: Perennial herb with a stout branching caudex; stem decumbent at the base or essentially erect, 5-15 cm. high, densely hirsute with spreading hairs; leaves densely hirsute like the stem, the basal ones oblanceolate to obovate or even sometimes broadly elliptic, rounded or obtuse and sometimes mucronulate at the apex, gradually or abruptly contracted to the petiole, more or less triple-nerved, especially toward the base, up to 7 cm. long and 13 mm. wide, usually smaller; cauline leaves several, reduced, oblanceolate to linear; head solitary, turbinate to hemi- spherical, the disk 7-14 mm. wide; involuere shorter than the disk, 6-8 mm. high, densely glandular and sometimes also sparsely hirsute with coarse spreading hairs; phyllaries imbricate, thickened on the back, the inner often strongly purplish at the loose and searious acuminate tips; pistillate flowers wanting; disk-corollas 4.0-5.8 mm. long, the tube 0.8-1.4 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm.; style- appendages ovate or broadly triangular, obtuse or acutish, 0.1-0.15 mm. long; pappus tawny or sordid, double, the inner of 15-25 firm bristles, the outer setulose and- sometimes obscure; akenes hirsute, 2-nerved. Rocky places in the mountains; known from Lincoln and Clark Counties, Nevada; possibly also in southern Utah.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Paniculately branched annual, 2-12 dm tall. Stems moderately to strongly winged, glabrous to moderately pubescent with short, antrorse hairs. Peduncles 2-14 cm long, moderately to densely pubescent with antrorse hairs, ca. 2-4 times as wide at the top as at the base. Leaves glabrous to sparsely pubescent, midrib prominent but lateral veins obscure except in some of the larger leaves, apices rounded to narrowly acuminate; lower and middle leaves lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, entire to serrate or irregularly toothed or lobed; upper leaves linear to lanceolate, entire. Heads few to numerous, globoid, 5-11 mm high, 5-12(-13) mm wide (excluding rays). Receptacle globoid to ovoid, 1.5-4.5 mm high, 1.5-6.0 mm wide. Involucral bracts united at the base, reflexed at anthesis, moderately to densely pubescent. Ray florets 10-17; ligules 5.5-15.0(-19.0) mm long, 2.2-5.5(-8.7) mm wide, yellow or usually yellow with a red or red-brown base, sparsely pubescent on the undersurface. Disc corollas 5-lobed, cylindrical to cylindric-campanulate, 1.5-2.3(-2.5) mm long, (0.4-)0.5-0.7 mm wide, yellow with yellow to brown or usually reddish brown lobes. Achenes 0.6-1.0 mm long, 0.3-0.4(-0.5) mm wide, pubescent with short hairs. Pappus scales 6-7, 0.05-0.3 (-0.4) mm long, 0.1-0.2 mm wide. Chromosome number, n = 13.

description: This species has a pappus of five scales and five bristles, similar to that found in K. virginica. However, bristle length in K. occidentalis is much shorter than that of the latter (0.8-1.8 mm vs 4.0-7.0 mm). Occasional individuals of K occidentalis have a reduced pappus and may be confused with K. cespitosa and K. wrightii. Both reduced and normal pappus forms have been observed within a single population. The chromosome number of n = 6 for K. occidentalis is unique in the genus. Krigia occidentalis groups with K. cespitosa of sect. Cymbia in phylogenies generated using both morphological and DNA data (Figs. 20-26). Krigia occidentalis occurs on sandy open habitats in eastern Texas, Oklahoma and adjacent Missouri, Kansas, Arkansas, and Louisiana (Fig. 28).

description: Short, talus-inhabiting perennial; 3-7 (2-10) cm tall, lightly lanate to arachnoid tomentose or becoming glabrate, especially in age, lower parts and often the in- volucral bracts purplish; stems arising singly from the upturned ends of creeping rhizomes, sometimes loosely clustered and giving the plant a subcaespitose aspect. Basal leaves petiolate, usually obovate in outline but deeply dissected, especially the lower half, making the blade lyrate or sublyrate, the midrib distinctly winged between the lobes, or the blade oval-orbicular and only shallowly toothed, overall dimensions (0.5)1-2 cm wide and (2)3-5+ cm long. Cauline leaves reduced to mere bracts or sometimes short, 1-2 cm long, and pinnatifid. Inflorescence a single head or 2-6 heads in a compact cluster; involucral bracts about 13 or 21 in number, 6-9 mm long, often purplish toward the tip; ray florets about 8-13, the ligule only 5-10 mm long making it conspicuously small for the rather large heads. Achene glabrous, at least 2 and probably 5 mm long at maturity.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, T. M. 1968. Taxonomy of Senecio multilobaius and its allies. Brittonia. 20: 267-284.

description: Subshrubs 1-2 m tall; stems erect, sub- terete, densely pubescent, few-branched; internodes 1-3 cm long, as long as or more commonly shorter than the leaves. Leaves simple, opposite, petiolate; blade subcor- iaceous to coriaceous, elliptic-lanceolate, 1.5-4 cm long, 1-1.6 cm wide, basally cunate, narrowly acute at apex, margins entire or weakly serrulate, revolute, 3-veined from near base, veins arching toward apex, upper surface dark green, rugose, glabrous or weakly puberulent toward base of the impressed veins, lower surface pale green, puberulent, especially so on veins, densely glandular, reticulate; petiole stout, pubescent, canaliculate, 1-5 mm long. Capitulescence terminal, corymbiform, to 8 cm tall and 11 cm broad; capitula temate or occasionally in 5's, sessile or central 3 heads of capitulescence occasionally shortly pe- dunculate, 8.5-9.5 mm tall, 2.6-3.4 mm broad, homogamous, 10-16-flowered, subtended by branches 1-2.5 cm long; involucre broadly cylindric; phyllaries deciduous, 29- 33, ca 7-seriate, imbricate, graduate, glabrous or outer 1-3 lightly glandular, 3-{5) nerved, scarious, stramineous proximally, reddish distally, the ca 8-10 outer ones ovate, 3.5-4 x 1.5-2.2 mm, apex rounded, the inner series narrowly elliptic, 5.8-7.1 x 1-1.6 mm, apex obtuse to rounded; recep- tacleconvex, 1.5-2.6 x 0.6-0.9 mm, naked, glabrous. Corollas discoid, cylindric, shallowly 5-lobed, 4.1-4.5 mm long, white; tube narrow and not much expanded above, thereby not distinct from throat, occasion- ally glandular; lobes triangular, glandular, 0.4-0.5 mm long, erect or slightly reflexed; anthers included, ca 1.3 mm long, anther collar obviously swollen, cream-colored, ca 0.3 mm long; style exserted, to ca 7 mm long, base glabrous, not expanded, style branches linear, ca 3.5 mm long, lower half with weakly discernible paired stigmatic lines. Achenes prismatic, 5-ribbed, brown, 2.8-3.2 mm long, glabrous or angles weakly hispidulous; carpopodium distinct, sym- metric, tan; pappus persistent, uniseriate, stramineous, of many bristles 3.7-4 mm long, about as long as the corolla and longer than the achene.

description: Herba crassa, caudice ad 2 m. alto et 25 cm. diametro, foliis vetustis dense induto; foliis summo densissimis coriaceis oblongo-spathulatis, 25-30 cm. longis, 3-4.5 cm. latis, ad basin sensim angustatis (loco angustissimo 7-11 mm. latis), ad vaginam rigide coriaceam 3-4 cm. latam dilatatis, apice obtusis vel subacutis, margine integris ubiqne arete ferrugineo-lanatis, nervis obscuratis, costa crassa; ramis floriferis axillaribns gracilibns ad 60 cm. longis dense lanatis, 3-5-capitulatis; capitnlis maturitate 30-40 mm. diametro, dense conglom-eratis (pedunculis ad 1 cm. longis), bracteis oblongo-deltoideis sub-tentis (bracteis 4-5 cm. longis, 1.5 cm. latis, apice subacutis); in-volucro 1-2-seriato, phyllaribus tenniter coriaceis 7-9, extra dense lanatis intns glabris, deltoideo-oblongis, circiter 15 mm. longis et 8 mm. latis (interioribns minoribns), apice acutis; floribus radii circiter 150 circiter 3-seriatis, lamina oblonga, 10-11 mm. longa, 1.5-2 mm. lata, prope basin pilis fnscis crassis 0.5 mm. longis pilosa; achenio obovato-trigono 3-4 mm. longo; floribus disci medio parce hispidulis, circiter 7 mm. longis, tubo quam limbo breviore, lobis deltoideis subacutis circiter 0.8 mm. longis; staminibus longe exsertis, circiter 7 mm. longis, filamentis quam antheris longioribus; stylo 8-9 mm. longo; paleis stramineis membranaceis oblongis, 7-9 mm. longis, circiter 2 mm. latis, apice subacutis, extra apicem versus dense ferrugineo-hispidis, pilis 0.5 mm. longis.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and crown or slightly branched caudex; stem decumbent and often purplish at the base, sparsely to moderately strigose, 1.5-7 dm. high; leaves numerous, sparsely or moderately strigose, linear or linear lanceolate, the basal and some or most of the cauline ones triple-nerved; basal leaves up to 25 cm. long and 1 cm. wide, including the long petiole, usually smaller; cauline leaves gradually reduced upwards; heads 1-20, the disk 8-15 mm. wide,; involuere 3.5-8 mm. high, sparsely or moderately hirsute and usually obscurely viscid; phyllaries subequal or slightly imbricate, often dark green or brownish, sometimes light green; rays about 20-50, blue, 6-20 mm. long and 1-3 mm. wide; disk-corollas 2.5-5.0 mm. long, the tube 0.6-1.5 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm.; style-appendages broadly triangular-ovate and obtuse to deltoid and acutish, 0.1-0.2 mm. long; pappus of about 12-16 slender and fragile bristles, occasionally with a few very slender and inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, finely hairy. Open places; western Oregon and northern California.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Frutex ad 1 m altus ramis erectis vel ascendentibus striatis glabris glanduloso-glutinosis. Folia alterna subeoriacea rigidula subtrinervia. Petiolus 2-3 mm longus basi vaginato-dilatatus glaber vel marginibus parce ciliatus glandulosus. Lamina elliptica vel ovato-elliptica vel oblongo-elliptica basi attenuato-cuneata apice paulo angustata obtusa mucronulataque margine inferiori parte excepta acute serrata. 1-2.8 cm longa 1-1.5 cm lata, utrinque laeteviridis glabra eopioqe glanduloso-punctata, costa supra lineari subtus bene elevata, nervis seeundariis (Ullnoutroque latere) basilaribus prominulis aseendentibus eum marginibus subparallelis, parcis venulis transversis paulo prominulis laxe reticulatis plus minusve conspicuis. Inflorescentiae thyrsoideo-paniculatae terminales basi foliosac ramis ramulisque gracilibus ascendentibus angulosis glabris vel minute sparse-pilosulis dense glandulosis glutinosis, foliis sursum gradatim minoribus usque ad bracteoliformes. Pedicelli 1-4 mm longi teneri minutissime puberuli glandulosi. Bracteolae 1-3 mm longae anguste lineares. Capitula feminea tubulosa 6-7 mm longa pedicellata; involucrum 4-5.5 mm altum stramineum 20-30 bracteis 5-6-seriatis imbricatis exterioribus oblongo-ovatis 1-1.5 mm longis, interioribus linearibus 4-4.5 mm longis 0.6-1 mm latis omnibus apice subacutis marginibus seariosis ciliatisque dorso glandulosis. Flores feminei 14-20 in capitulo, corolla capillari glabra apice denticulato-lacinata circa 3.5 mm longa; stylus valde exsertus ramuli oblongi subacuti sublaeves minutissime papillosuli; pappus 4.5-5 mm longus stramineus pilis biseriatis strietis rigidis acutis minute strigulosis; ovarium glabrum striatum. Capitula maselLLa subeampaniulata circa 4.5 mm longa; involucrum circa 3.5 mm altum 29-25 bracteis 4-5-seriatis exterioribus ovatis circa 1 mm longis interioribus oblongis obtusiuseulis circa 3 mm loncis 0.7-1 mm latis margine seariosis ciliatisque. Flores masculi 10-12 in capitulo, corolla 3.5 mm longa glabra tubulo angusto 1.5-1.6 mm longo limbo campanulato 5-lobato lobis linearibus circa 1.2 mm longis recurvatis; antherae 1.3 mm longae basi obtusae; stylo ramulis sublanceolatis inerassatis villosulis 0.7 mm longis; ovarium abortivum glabrum; pappus 3 mm longus stramineus pilis biseriatis strigosis apice dilatatis.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1960. Studies on Andean Compositae--IV. Brittonia. 12: 182-195.

description: Plants annual; 2-8 dm, stems square and pubescent; leaves opposite, 3-11 cm long, 1-9 cm wide, 2 to 3 times pinnate-pinnatifid, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, petiolate; "inflorescence" cymose with mostly 5-26 heads; involucre glabrous, outer involucral bracts 5-10, subulate, 2-4 mm long, inner involucral bracts 7-8, oblan- ceolate, 6-8 mm long, pubescent on both surfaces; paleae 22-45, linear-lanceolate, yellow, 6-9 mm long at anthesis; ray-florets 5 (7), ligule obovate, 1-2 cm long, lemon yellow; disc-florets 22-45, yellow, stamen "appendages" lanceolate-ovate with no gland and yellow pigmented, style branches 2-3 mm, linear-acuminate; achenes 22-45, dimorphic, awnless, outer ones 4-7 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm wide, subulate, rubro-castaneous, innermost ones 7-12 mm long, 0.25-1.0 mm wide, linear-cuneate, black, chromosome number n 12.

description: Plants 1.0-3.0 m tall; stems densely soft-pilose with spreading or appressed hairs to 2 mm long; leaves alternate; petioles to 3 cm long; blades ovate to ovate-lanceolatt, 9 cm long, 7 cm wide, acuminate, cuneate at base, serrate, above appressed-pilose, beneath villous-tomentose or sericeous-tomentose with long hairs; heads 1-3 on peduncles 3-15 cm long; disk 1.5-3.0 cm in diam.; phyllaries broadly lanceolate, long attenuate, 15-23 mm long, 3-4 mm broad, dark green, suffused with black, long-sericeous-pilose; rays 13-18, 1.5-2.0 cm long, 0.5 cm wide; disk flowers 6-7 mm long, yellow with nigrescent tips, puberulent or nearly glabrous; anthers black; pales obtuse to acute, black, glabrous; achenes 4 mm long, with a few hairs near apex, otherwise glabrous; pappus of 3-4 linear= lanceolate, unequal awns; squamellae occasionally present; pappus of ray flowers of 2 linear-lanceolate awns, with or without lacerate squamellae.
bibliographicCitation: Heiser, Charles B. 1957. A revision of the South American Species of Helianthus. Brittonia. 8: 283-285.

description: Plants to 4 m tall; stems densely and finely sericeous-lanate; leaves alter- nate; petioles 5 mm long; blades lanceolate, 4.0 cm long, 0.7 cm wide, acuminate, above sericeous-pilose, below white-tomentose; peduncles 1-2 cm long; disk about 1.5-1.7 cm in diameter; phyllaries oblong-lanceolate, sericeous-lanate, equaling the disk in length; rays about 15, about 1.5 cm long; disk corollas yellow, the teeth pubescent or glabrous; pales lanceolate, acutish, with pubescent tip and keel; achene compressed, submarginate; pappus of 2 long, slender awns.

description: Plant perennial; caudex diffuse, slenderly branching; leaves villous, more or less glandular, oblanceolate or spathulate, to 2 cm long and 4 mm wide, mostly smaller, early leaves sometimes shallowly 3-lobed at apex; peduncles scapiform, to ca. 3.5 cm long, densely villous with long, spreading hairs, glandular; heads solitary; disc 9-12 mm wide; involucre (4-) 5-7 mm high, densely viscid-villous with long (to ca. 3 mm), spreading, multicellular, flattened hairs, these on some heads with mostly dark-purple cross-walls; phyllaries 22-24, narrow, subequal, acuminate and often recurved at apex, purple, or on some heads purple only towards apex; ligules ca. 30-40, white or laven- der, 4-6 mm long, 1-2 mm wide; disc corollas ca. 4 mm long, lobes ca. 0.7 mm long; style-appendages triangular, acute, 0.25-0.3 mm long; pappus simple, usually more or less strongly purple-red tinged, especially on the barbellules, bristles ca. 20-25, nearly equal in length to disc corollas or generally somewhat shorter; achene 2-nerved, short-hairy.

description: Herbae perenes, rosulatae-pulvinato, caudicibus ramosis, pro parte subterraneis e radice gracili, ramulis superioribus saepe foliorum basibus vestitis, vulgo pilis longis albis ferentibus; plantae 2-6 cm latae, minus quam 2.5 cm altae; folia spathulata vel oblanceolata, integra, apice acuta et minute mucronata, paene uniformiter strigosa supra et subtus, minute glandulosa, basi 1-1.3 mm lata, supra fere glabra, subtus et secus marginem strigosa, ad laminam contracta, puncto angustissimo 3-6 mm supra basin, 7-13 (16) mm longa, 1.5-3 (1-3.5) mm lata; pedunculi nulli; involucra 4-8 mm alta, 7-13 mm lata, obconica; phyllaria 3-(raro 4-) seriata, lanceolata, apice acuta, fimbriata, rubri-scariosi-marginata, ciliis hyalinis numerosis, supra glabra, serie extima subinde externe sparsim strigosa, aliter glabra, 5-7 mm longa, 0.9-1.8 mm lata, intima longioria; corollae radii ca. 13-21, ligulis 4-7 mm longis 0.8-2.2 mm latis supra flavis vel aureis et glabris, subtus rubellis vel rubiginosis, margine flavis, aliquantum ubique dense glanduliferis, tubo 1.8-2.9 mm longo, viridulo vel rubiginoso, glandulifero; corollae disci flavae, apice purpurascenti-tinctae, 3.7-4.5 mm longae; achenia angusti-oblanceolata, 2-2.5 mm longa, 0.5-0.7 mm lata, compressa, in costis glabra, in lateribus compressis, dense pubescentia, pilis longis, adscendentibus, hyalinis, apice bifurcatis, furcibus 2, minutis, recurvatis; pappus flosculorum radiorum 0.7-1.0 mm longus (vel setis paucis tantum 0.3 mm longis), setis ca. 15, barbellatis, plus minusve basaliter conjunctis; pappus flosculorum discorum 4-5 mm longus, setis basaliter liberis.

description: Perennial herbs to subshrubs; stems canescent becoming glabrate. Leaves cauline, sometimes slightly crowded near the inflorescence, sessile, 2.8-4.2 cm long, 1.8-3 cm wide, ovate or ovate-oblong, apically rounded to acute, usually apiculate with a small callous tooth, basally cordate to rounded, marginally revolute and remotely callous-toothed, tomentose above, canescent beneath. Inflorescences greatly reduced or bracteate and cymose-paniculate. Heads (10) 12-14-flowered; peduncles 1-4 cm long, canescent. Involucre campanulate, 8.5-13 mm high, 5-8.5 (10) mm wide; phyllaries loosely imbricate in ca 4 series, tomentose, the inner ones lanceolate, long-acuminate, 8.2-11 mm long, 1.7-2.1 mm wide, the outer ones ovate-lanceolate, 2.6-3.3 mm long, 0.8-1.2 mm wide. Pappus brownish, the inner bristles 6-7.5 mm long and outer bristles 1.3-3 mm long. Corollas 6.5-11 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers 2.2-3.9 mm long. Achenes 2.3-3 mm long, strigose-pilose. Flowering and fruiting from November to March.

description: Shrubs to 1.5 m tall, branching from base; stems branched only from base except at capitulescence, tan-brown below, yellow green above, striate; leaves fascicled above or not, but tending to cluster at branch tips, ascendant-erect (occasionally appressed), broadly linear, linear-lanceolate, or narrowly spatulate, 1.5-6.0 cm long, 2.0-7.5 mm wide, dark yellow-green, bases cuneate, apices obtuse, acute, or apiculate, margins entire, glabrous. Capitulescences densely paniculate, not bracteate; peduncles 1-4 mm long, glabrous; clusters of capitula borne in racemes, these in turn borne paniculately; involucres turbinate to narrowly obconic, 4.0-6.0 mm high, 2.0-3.0 mm wide, phyllaries 14-17 in 3-5 series, linear- lanceolate, 2.0-4.5 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm wide, apices (to 1/8-l/4 the total length) herbaceous, acute, margins hyaline-winged throughout; ray florets 3-5, corollas ca. 5.0 mm long, tubes ca. 3.0 mm long, limbs ca. 2.5 mm long, 1.3-1.5 mm wide; disk florets 3-4, corollas glabrous at juncture of tube and throat, 4.5-5.5 mm high, tubes 2.0-2.2 mm long; styles 7.0-7.5 mm long at full anthesis, branches 1.0-1.5 mm long, ap- pendages 0.5-0.8 mm long, lanceolate. Cypselas cylindric, 1.4-2.5 mm high, 0.3- 0.5 mm diam., grayish or coppery-bronze, trichomes 0.2-0.4 mm long, white; pappus of 30-60 bristles in 1 series, 4.2-5.0 mm high, yellowish white to pinkish coppery.

description: Shrubby tree ca 2 m tall; branches sulcate-angled, villous, hairs jointed, rust-colored, ca 4 mm long; lower leaves cordate-ovate, some cuneate, petiole winged and narrowly decurrent, acuminate, membranaceous, 3-nerved, thickly pubescent below chiefly on veins; petiole with a wing ca 3 mm wide on both sides, ca 8 cm long; leaves to 4.7 dm long and 2.5 dm wide, the upper ones smaller, subessile, ovate, long-acuminate; inflorescence corymbose, many-headed, the heads small; peduncles 1-3 cm long, ca lmm thick; bracts ovate, to 8 mm long and 3 mm wide, short-acum- inate or almost blunt; involucral scales ovate, 5-6 mm long, 3.5-4 mm wide, 11-13-nerved, the margins ciliate, the inner several boat-shaped; ray flowers 10-12, the corollas biligulate; outer ligules quadrate-ovate, ca 2.5 mm long, 1.25 mm wide, the apex tridentate, 7-nerved; inner ligule 1.25 mm long, 0.75 mm wide, 1-nerved, the tube ca 1 mm long, villous; disc flowers ca 30, the corollas ca 3 mm long; achene glabrous, dark brown, compressed, obovoid, 4-angled, the outer angles narrowly winged.

description: Perennial herbs, 30-70 cm tall, stems te- rete, densely pubescent with tapered trichomes on basal third, interspersed with stipitate glandular trichomes distally, dark green-purple. Leaves opposite; petioles 13- 30 mm long; blades 15-55 mm long, 5-45 mm wide, smaller distally, leaves associated with capitulescence 5-30 mm long, 5-18 mm wide, cordate or ovate to trullate, triplinerved, bases cordate, truncate or obtuse and shallowly attenuate onto petiole, margins crenate to serrulate, apices acute to obtuse, adaxial surfaces light green to green purple, moderately pubescent, trichomes variously multicellular, tapered, monili- form, or stipitate-glandular, moniliform and glandular trichomes mostly on veins, abaxial surface green or purple-green, mod- erately pubescent, trichomes variously multicellular, tapered, moniliform, sessile or stipitate-glandular, the sessile-glandular tri- chomes numerous and scattered throughout the surface, other trichomes mainly on veins, veins clearly outlined as a whitish to light brown reticulum against purplish green background. Capitulescences of 15- 45+ heads arranged in loose, paniculiform, somewhat nodding cymes; peduncles 12-35 mm long, green, sparsely to moderately pu- bescent. Heads discoid, campanulate, nodding, 10-15 mm high, 7-8 mm wide; re- ceptacle epaleate, ca. 2.5 mm diam. Phyllaries 14-17 in 2 subequal series, 5.5-6.5 mm long, 0.6-1 mm wide, lanceolate, appressed, herbaceous, green-purple, moderately to densely puberulous with stipitate- glandular trichomes, pubescence denser on basal half of each phyllary. Flowers 24-33, corollas narrowly funnelform, white, essentially glabrous; tubes 2.3-2.5 mm long throats 2.5-3 mm long, 0.5-0.6 mm wide at base, ca. 1.5 mm wide at distal end, essentially glabrous; lobes ca. 0.7 mm long; anthers ca. 1.7 mm long, white, anther appendages ca. 0.2 mm long; styles ca. 4.5 mm long, white, the branches 3-4 mm long, white. Cypselae ca. 4 mm long, cylindrical, with 8-10 ribs, sparsely puberulent pubescence slightly denser along ribs and at base and neck, pappi of 29-35 subequal bristles, these 6-6.5 mm long. Chromosome number 2n = 28.

description: Perennial herbs ca. 1 m tall; stems terete, moderately hirsute to scabrous, purplish green. Leaves alternate, uninerved; blades linear, 8-12 cm long, 5-13 mm wide, smaller distally toward the capitulescence, adaxial surface moderately scabrous, bright green, abaxial surface moderately scabrous to strigose, trichomes slightly more appressed and longer than on adaxial surface, pubescence denser along the main vein, with a few appressed trichomes, slightly lighter in color than adaxial surface, bases attenuate, margins involute, entire, apices acute to acuminate; petiole ca. 2 mm long. Capitulescence of 3-30+ heads, arranged in open paniculiform cymes; peduncles 2- 9 cm long, moderately strigose, purplish green. Heads radiate, hemispherical, 10-12 mm long, ca. 1 cm wide (excluding ligules); receptacle ca. 2.5 mm high, ca. 2 mm diam., convex, paleate. Phyllaries 17-23 in 2 subequal series, 3.2-3.5 mm long, 0.7-1 mm wide, ovate to narrowly lanceolate, sparsely strigose, appressed, slightly indurate at base, yellow-green, distal third herbaceous, slightly reflexed, green. Pales 4-4.2 mm long, 1.5-1.7 mm wide, obovate to oblanceolate in outline, conduplicate, apex acute, essentially glabrous, basal half stramineous, distal half yellow with dark green markings. Ray flowers 13-15, pistillate, the corollas glabrous, golden yellow; tubes ca. 1.4 mm long, 0.4-0.5 mm wide, yellow- stramineous; ligules 50-5.5 mm long, ca. 2.2 mm wide, oval, apices trifid; styles 1.6- 1.8 mm long, the branches ca. 0.7 mm long, tapered with a small appendage. Ray cypselae ca. 4 mm long, 1.2-1.4 mm wide, wings ca. 1 mm wide, stramineous; body obovate, flatly biconvex, glabrous except for a few appressed trichomes on center of achene, shiny black; pappus of 2 awns, 2.1- 2.3 mm long, stramineous. Disk flowers 85-120, perfect, the corollas tubular, essentially glabrous, yellow; tubes 0.5-0.6 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm wide, yellow-stramineous; throats ca. 2.4 mm long, ca. 0.7-0.8 mm wide at base, 1 mm wide at top; lobes 0.7- 0.8 mm long, narrowly ovate to lanceolate; anthers ca. 1.7 mm long, black, the appendages ca. 0.25 mm long, lanceolate, strami- neous; styles ca. 3 mm long, yellow, the branches 1.5 mm long, tapered, with small appendage, yellow. Disk cypselae like those of the rays.

description: Herba perennis caulibus ad 8 cm. altis laxis erectis villosulis pilis patentibus, foliis glabris vel sparse villosulis marginibus glabris vel ciliatis pilis minus quam 1 mm. longis, folis imis anguste oblanceolatis usque ad 5 cm. longis 3 mm. latis; caulinis reductis linearibus, capitulis solitariis turbinatis disco 7-12 mm. lato, involuero 5-6 mm. alto subglutinoso villosulo pilis millus quam 1 mm. longis, bracteis subaequalibus vel leviter imbricatis, ligulis circa 15-35 violaceis 6-9 mm. longis 1.4-2.0 mm. latis, corollis disci 3.7-5.0 mm. longis, pappo obscure duplici, achaeniis hirsutis 2-nervis.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and moderately branched caudex; stem about 8 cm. high or usually less, erect but lax, finely villous with short spreading hairs; leaf surfaces sparsely and finely hairy, or glabrous, the margins smooth, or finely ciliate with short hairs less than 1 mm. long; basal leaves narrowly oblanceolate, up to 5 cm. long and 3 mm. wide; cauline leaves reduced and linear, usually several, commonly more hairy than the basal ones; head solitary, turbinate, the disk 7-12 mm. wide; involuere 5-6 mm. high, glutinous or obscurely viscid and finely villous, sometimes sparsely so, with short hairs less than 1 mm. long; phyllaries subequal or slightlv imbricate, greenish or greenish-brownish, with purplish tips, usually linear-subulate and attenuate-acuminate, sometimes broader; ligules about 15-35, violet, 6-9 mm. long, 1.4-2.0 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.7-5.0 mm. long, the tube 0.7-1.2 mm., the lobes 0.6-0.9 mm.; style-appendages lanceolate to deltoid, acute or acutish, 0.15-0.35 mm. long; pappus of about 15-20 fairly firm bristles, commonly with some slender and inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, hairy.

description: Rhizome freely branching; stems 15-30 em. high, sparingly villous and glandular, inereasinigly so above; leaves mostly 3 pairs, occasionally 2 or 4, 1.0-3.5 cm. broad, 5.0 (3.0)-10 em. long, regularly and conspicuously dentate, infrequently merely denticulate, 3-5-nerved, sparingly villous and short- stipitate-glandular, rarely glabrate; peduncles denselv stipitate-glandular and conspicuously scaberulous-puberulent and pilose above; heads 1-3(4), 15-18 mm. high, campanulate-turbinate; perielinium pilose and obviously glandular; involuere obviously biseriate, the bracts 10-15, 10-12 mm. lonig, 1.5-3.0 mm. broad, acute, lanceolate, rarely somewhat oblanceolate, sparingly pilose toward the base, obviously short-stipitate-glandular to the tip, red-tinged; ray flowers 8-12(15), the ligules 10-15 mm. long, 4.0-6.0 mm. broad, linear-oblong, the teeth obtusish, 0.5-1.0 (2.0) mm. long; disc corolla 6.5(6.0)-8.5(10.4) mm. long, the tube 3.3-3.9(4.8) mm. long, the tube and the base of the limb densely and somewhat coarsely long-pilose, the collar conspicuous, the corolla lobes acutish, 0.6-0.8 mnm. long; achenes 4.5-5.6(6.5) mm. long, sparingly short-aseending-hispid with double hairs which in length equal 2 the diamu. of the achene, intermixed sparingly with long sep- tate hairs, not at all glandular.

description: Trees or shrubs to 5 m tall; stems puberulent above; leaves sessile or with a winged petiole, the basal portion of the expanded blade cuneate to attenuate, acuminate, to 35 cm long and 18 cm wide, dentate, the teeth blunt and rounded, the lower surface puberulent to tomentose especially on main veins; peduncles puberulent; phyllaries obovate to ovate, glabrous, ca 3 mm long and 2 mm wide; ray flowers 10-15, the corolla yellow, ca 3 mm wide and to 6 mm long; disc flowers ca 25, to 4 mm long, the corollas glabrous; ray paleae obovate, glabrous, ca 4 mm long and 2 mm wide; disc paleae ca 3 mm long, lanceolate, chartaceous, their upper margins denticulate, the midvein prominent; achene black, ca 3 mm long and 2 mm wide, obovoid and flattened or obpyramidal.

description: Stem usually stout, 1-3 mn. high, simple to inflorescence, rarely with laterals near the top; scabrous, or with abundant, short, white hairs, usually light yellow in color; leaves lanceolate, gradually aculmiinate to both apex and base, mostly 14-30 cm long, 2-5.5 cm wide, the margins entire, sometimes obscurely serrate, the surfaces with many short hairs imparting grayish-green color, characteristically strongly conduplicate and falcate, sessile; phyllaries 1-1.5 cm long, densely pubescent and margins strongly ciliate, spreading; heads in simple terminal raceme, sometimes panicles, the peduncles scabrous, often with dense white pubescence towards top, variable in length, 5-7.5 cm in diameter; florets of disk 1-1.2 cm long, the base of corolla puberulent; ligules bright yellow, 2.5-3.5 cm long, concave; chaff linear-acuminate, obscurely 3-cuspidate, pubescent at tip.

description: Plants annual, 10-50 cm high; sterns erect, the lower portion densely pubescent with spreading, glandular trichomes (0.3-) 0.5-1.5 mm long (breaking off with age, but the bases persisting), the upper portion anid the inflorescence becoming sparsely glandular-pubescent to merely strigose or rarely glabrate; lower leaves simple to 3-foliate anid opposite, the upper ones 3-parted and/or 5-parted and alternate (new growth on secondary stems following drought or injury frequently shows simple leaves throughout), pubescent with scattered appressed hairs; mid-sten- leaves with petioles 1-2 cm long; leaflets or leaf segments usually lanceolate to oblanceolate, 0.2-1 cm wide, 2-5 cm long, 3-20 timnes as long as wide, acute at the apex, entire (rarely a few leaflets irregularly lobed but not consistently so) ; inflorescence a subcorymbose cyme, with 5 to numerous heads; heads subturbinate, 3 5 mm across, 4-6 mm high; prilncipal inlvolucral bracts 8-12, 4-6 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, with white and/or conspicuously red-tinged marginis, broadly obtuse or rounded at the apex, ciliate to sparsely pubescent on the back or less often glabrous; florets white or sometimes purplish in the throat, distinctly zygomorphic; corolla 3-4 mm long, tube 0.75-1 mm long, glabrous to sparsely glandular-pubescent; throat (including the lobes) about 2 mm long, the lobes of different lengths, 0.5-2 mim long; style branches as in F. tripteris; aehenes 3-4 (-5) mm lono, obpyramidal, 4-sided, finely pubescent with ascendinig hairs to niearly glabrous; pappus of 8-10 paleaceous scales, 0.5-1.5 mm long, broadly rounded at the apex, without terminal awns or mucros; chromosome number, n = 10.

description: Perennial herb with a branching caudex; stem 1-3 dm. high, glabrous except immediately under the heads, where usually finely glandular; leaves glabrous, the basal broadly oblanceolate to elliptical or obovate, up to 12 cm. long and 15 mm. wide, the rounded apex usually mucronate; cauline leaves several, scattered, somewhat reduced but still fairly well developed, broadly oblanceolate to oblong or lanceolate, obtuse or acute; heads solitary or sometimes 3 or 4, the disk about 10-15 mm. wide; involuere finely and sometimes obscurely glandular, 5-7 mm. high; phyllaries subequal, green, herbaceous, purple-tipped, the outer acute, the inner acuminate; ligules about 20-45, blue or sometimes pink-purple, 7-10 mm. long; 1.3-2.7 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.5-4.9 mm. long, the tube 0.8-1.7 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm., the limb slightly or moderately puberulent, at least below the middle; style-appendages ovate to deltoid or a little narrower, rounded or obtuse to sometimes acute, 0.2-0.25 mm. long; pappus of about a dozen or 15 bristles, with a few outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, moderately white-hairy. Meadows and open places in the Siskiyou Mountains of northwestern California and adjacent Oregon.

description: Plant relatively low and slender, mostly 1-6 cm. high, rarely 10 cm.; basal leaves about 1-6 cm. long, 1-3 mm. wide, their bases more obviously enlarged than in var. typicus; dead basal leaves often persisting from one year to the next; cauline leaves few and small, not over 3 cm. long, usually smaller; heads solitary, the disk mnostly 6-15 mm. wide; involuere rarely exceeding 7 mm. high; phyllaries greener and more herbaceous than in var. typicus, and their hairs more frequently with purple cross-walls; ligules mostly 20-60, 4-8 mm. long; akenes tending to be appressed-hirsute.

description: Basally woody perennial herbs or sub shrubs up to 1 m tall, mostly caespitose, from a xylopodium. Leaves mostly alternate, opposite at the base, sometimes a few shoots or all of them may become opposite leaved throughout; petioles up to 4 mm long or subsessile; blades 3-7 (-9) x 0.5-3 cm, submembranous, ovate to lanceolate, sometimes elliptic to obovate or narrowly lanceolate to rarely linear, very shortly attenuate to cunéate at the base, acuminate to acute or sometimes obtuse and mucronulate at the apex, margins sparsely and obscurely serrulate to serrate, strigillose to velutinous to densely sericeous on both surfaces, abaxially paler, 3 nerved from near to well above the base, subpinnately netted distally or sometimes throughout. Outer phyllaries 8-20(30) x (1.5)2-8 mm, oblong to narrowly oblong, slightly constricted and indurate at the base or elliptic beyond a short, narrow oblong base, rarely linear; inner phyllaries 8-11 x 2-2.5 mm, narrowly oblong to oblong, indurate at the base, constricted and foliaceous at the apex to completely scarious. Paleae 9-11 x ca. 1 mm when folded, obtuse and mucronulate to shortly acuminate or sometimes subulate at the tips. Ray florets fertile, tube 2-4 mm long, lamina 11-23 x 3 - 7 mm, oblong to elliptic to oblanceolate, abaxially glabrous or with a few trichomes. Disc florets with corolla 4-5 mm long, lobes abaxially glabrous or with a few trichomes. Cypselae 3.5-5.5 x 1.5-2 mm, smooth to finely and sparsely tuberculate, peripheral ones trigonous, 3- winged, 3 awned, the inner laterally flattened, the wings 1-2 mm wide, obscurely ciliate expecially on the side opposite the paleae; pappus with awns 1.5 - 5 mm long, mostly subequal, the longest shorter but not less than 3/4 of the cypsela body length, broad to very  broad at the base, crown 0.5 - 1 mm high, very fragile, easily broken, partially fused to the cypsela body (mostly less than 1/3), with lacerate or entire margins.

description: Low plant. with numerous slender erect or suberect stems and very crowded linear-filiform to linear-oblanceolate leaves about 0.5-2.5 mm. wide and less than 4 cm. long; stem and leaves varying from subglabrous (in forms approaching var. hartwegi) to usually more or less strigose-hirsute, to sometimes coarsely spreading-hirsute; heads solitary or few; ligules tending to be longer and more conspicuous than in some of the other varieties; akenes sparsely hairy.

description: Shrubs, 3-4 m tall; stems with branches terete, scabrid-hispid, hairs 1 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades broadly ovate, edges recurved, 4-7 X 3-5 cm, subcoriaceous, apices acuminate and mucronate, bases rounded or sometimes cordate, margins mucronate serrate, pinni-nerved, 5-7-veined at the base, pale green on both faces, hispidulous, hairs 1 mm long; petioles 3-10 mm long, scabrid-hispid, hairs 1 mm long. Capitulescences thyrsoid. Capitula ovoid, sessile, 5-6 mm high, 4 mm diam.; phyllaries 3, coriaceous, concave, broadly ovate, 4.5 X 3.5-4 mm; 5-veined; whitish green, apices shortly acuminate to mucronate; strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Pistillate florets 4, subtended by broadly ovate paleae, 4 X 3.5 mm; 5-veined; apices short-acuminate; strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long; corollas white, tubular, 3.5 mm long, 1.5 mm diam., 3-lobed, lobes irregularly deltoid, 0.3 mm long, apices scarcely ciliate. Staminate florets 5-8, epaleaceous, corollas white, tubular, 4.5 mm long, 2 mm diam., 5-lobed, lobes deltoid, 0.8-1 mm long, apices scarcely ciliate; ovaries 2 mm long, 1-1.5 mm diam., hirsute, hairs 1 mm long. Cypselae broadly obovoid, 3 X 2-2.5 mm, apices hirsute, hairs 1 mm long. Chromosome number, n = 16 (Robinson et al., 1981).

description: Folia coriacea subobovato-oblonga, basi attenuata acute cuneata longe petio. lata, apice obtusa vel subacuta margine repando dentata revolutaque; supra glabra, subtus dense tomentosa costa crassa nervis lateralibus patulis bene elevatis reticulo obsoleto. Lamina 3-4.5 cm longa 0.8-2 cm lata. Petiolus flex. uosus tenuis subglaber 8.14 mm longus. Inflorescentia corymboso-paniculata folia non excedens ramis tomentosis. Involucrum ochraceum 6-7 mm altum leviter tomentosum. Flores marginales feminei circa 20, corolla alba ligulata 6 mm longa glabra tubulo 3 mm lamina oblonga 3 mm longa. Flores disci circa 34 corolla tubulosa glabra 4 mm longa dentibus linearibus 1 mm longis. Stylus florum centralium bifidus ramis lanceolatis papillosis. Ovarium sparsissime pilosulum glandulosumque. Pappus 4 mm longus roseo-ochraceus pilis rigidis strigosis in floribus marginalibus acutis in disco ad apicem incrassatis.

description: Plants annual or biennial; stems 1-several from the base, 2-10 dm tall, the indumentum of the stems predominantly glandular; leaves of the basal rosette spatulate to oblanceolate, dentate, glandular, with villous trichomes on the upper surface, 5-15 cm long, 1-3 cm wide, the upper leaves not markedly reduced, ovate to lanceolate, the uppermost entire; inflorescence cymose to paniculate; involucre 10-18 mm high, 15-20 mm broad, the involucral bracts linear-lanceolate, narrowly acuminate, viscid-villous, often reddish at the tips, 8-12 mm long, 1-2 mm wide; ray corollas yellow, 20-35; disk corollas yellow, 6-7 mm long; achenes linear, 4-6 mm long, pappus pairs unequal, 1-2 mm long.

description: Small trees 3-5 m high; branchlets slender, terete, cinereous-stellate-tomentose, alternate but upper ones becoming subopposite to opposite with glomerules in leaf axils. Leaves alternate but upper ones becoming subopposite to opposite, decussate, somewhat crowded towards end of branchlets; petioles slightly furrowed, cinereous-tomentose (7) 10-15 (18) mm long; blades coriaceous, elliptic to obovate, 3.5-8 x 1.5-3.5 cm, acute to subacute at apex, slightly oblique to cuneate at base, glabrous, lustrous above, on midvein tomentose, cinereous-to- mentose with stellate trichomes beneath, 6-8 lateral veins on each side, margins remotely denticulate. Inflorescences axillary clusters of 4-7 heads, the inflorescence of each subopposite leaf pair often appearing as one dense cluster. Heads of 5-7 florets on short tomentose peduncles; involucre turbinate 6.5-7.5 x 3.5- 4.5 mm; phyllaries imbricate in 4-5 series, deciduous, rusty-brown, marginally arachnoid, outer ones triangular-ovate, subobtuse, tomentulose at apex, inner ones lanceolate to oblong, obtuse, densely tomentose at apex. Corollas white, glabrate, tube ca 4 mm long, lobes 1.5-3 mm long; anthers purple ca 3.5 mm long, the basal auricles ca 0.5 mm long, elongated, papillate at tip. Pappus white to straw-colored, biseriate, inner bristles filiform, 5-6 mm long, outer ones linear or filiform, unequal 0.5-2 mm long. Achenes 3-3.5 long, somewhat 3-4- angled, 10-costate, gland-dotted.

description: Biennial herb with a taproot; stem green, slender, lax, 5-25 cm. long, branched, finely and rather sparsely appressed-hairy, finely glandular just under the heads, and the hairs there spreading; leaves finely strigose, the basal ones oblanceolate to spatulate, up to 5 cm. long and 6 mm. wide, or with elliptic blade up to 1.5 cm. long and 6 mm. wide, borne on a petiole of about the same length; cauline leaves linear or oblanceolate, reduced upwards, the upper ones mere bracts 5 mm. long or less; heads several, the disk about 4-7 mm. wide; involuere about 3-4 mm. high, finely glandular and sparsely or moderately spreading-hirtellous; phyllaries green, with brown midrib, the outer narrower and shorter than the inner; ligules about 20-70, white or perhaps blue, about 3.5-4 mm. long and 1.2-1.4 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 1.8-2.3 mm. long, the tube 0.3-0.4 mm., the lobes likewise, the lower part of the limb somewhat inflated and whitish, as in E. divergens; style appendages ovate or broadly triangular, obtuse, about 0.05-0.1 mm. long; pappus of about 6-12 fragile white bristles and some small and inconspicuous squamellae; akenes 2-nerved, more or less hairy.

description: Herba biennis radice maximo caulibus laxis ramosis usque ad 25 cm. altis sparse vel moderate strigosis pilis sub capitulis patentibus, foliis strigosis imis oblanceolatis vel spathulatis usque ad 5 cm. longis 6 mm. latis, caulinis reductis linearibus vel oblanceolatis, capitulis nonnullis disco 4-7 mm. lato involuero circa 3-4 mm. alto, bracteis leviter imbricatis, glandulosis et sparse vel moderate patenti-hirtellis, ligulis circa 20-70 albis vel caeruleis 3.5-4 mm. longis 1.2-1.4 mm. latis, corollis disci 1.8-2.3 mm. latis, pappo duplici, achaeniis 2-nervis.

description: Biennial or sometimes short-lived perennial herbs, 6-26 cm tall, with a slender, woody taproot; caudex simple, often producing several groups of basal leaves, or with several short, slender, vertical or oblique caudex branches, each branch bearing a single tuft of leaves; usually several flowering stems from the base, erect or arching upward, sparsely strigose, Type A trichomes 135-500 u long, mostly appressed or closely ascending, but spreading just under the heads and sometimes at the base of the stem, glandular-appearing Type C trichomes dense just under the heads. Basal leaves oblanceolate to spatulate, mostly entire but sometimes pinnately lobed, the sinuses varying from shallow notches to cleavages extending almost to the midvein near the base of blade, 1.0-7.0 cm long, length of the blade slightly less than 1/2 the leaf length, blade width 2-8(-13) mm, strigose, Type A trichome lengths similar to those of the stem; cauline leaves entire, linear to oblanceolate, 3-25 mm long, up to 3.5 mm wide, gradually reduced upwards, pubescence similar to that of the basal leaves. Heads numerous, the first at the ends of long branches, usually overtopped by later heads on peduncles from the axils of cauline leaves; disks 6.0-7.5 mm wide; involucres 2.0-3.5 mm high, sparsely to moderately hirtellous, appearing finely glandular, phyllaries with a brown midrib, the outer slightly shorter and narrower than the inner, the inner light green with chartaceous margins; ligules 37-83, white above and below with a lilac midstripe below, drying white or sometimes light blue, 3.4-6.8 mm long, 0.5-1.4 mm wide, with 4 or 5 veins; disk corollas 1.6-2.4 mm long, glabrous or with a few inconspicuous biseriate trichomes, the tube well-defined, about 0.3 mm long, the lower part of the limb white, slightly indurated and slightly in- flated, corolla lobes 0.2-0.3 mm long; style appendages broadly triangular, 0.3-0.5 mm long; pappus double, the inner of 6-12 bristles, the outer of slender setae up to 0.1 mm high. Achenes 2-nerved, 0.8-1.2 mm long, sparsely pubescent; n = 9. Locally abundant in the Clear Creek drainage of Zion National Park in deep sand derived from Navajo Sandstone, Washington and Kane cos., Utah, and a single population in the Coral Pink Sand Dunes, west of Kanab, Kane Co., Utah. June- September.
bibliographicCitation: Nesom, Guy L. 1976. A new species of Erigeron [E. proselyticus] (Asteraceae) and its relatives in southwestern Utah. Brittonia. 28: 263-272.

description: Herba perennis spithamaea stolonifera; eaulis florifer suberectus paucifoliatus simplex v. pauciramosus 1-3-cepbalus pilosus et stipitato- glandulosus, foliis inferioribus oblanceolatis obtusis, ceteris oblongis v. lanceolatis subintegris; stolones repentes, foliis obovatis apice rotundatis quoque latere 1-dentatis; capitula pedunculata, radiis 16-21 albis 2- seriatis; involueri 2-seriati vix gradati phyllaria ovalia apice rotundata ciliata et sparse pilosula pilis glandulosis subrnembranacea 5-9-vittata flavo-viridia apice nigro-purpurea; achenia glabra epapposa.

description: Rootstock short, with slender roots, bearing 1 or 2 flowering stems and 2 or 3 creeping stolons; flowering stems erectish or ascending, 15-18 cm. high, sometimes bearing a stolon from near base, siinple or with a couple of branches near base, slender, striate, pilose with lax several- celled whitish hairs intermixed with shorter stipitate glands, bearing only 3-4 pairs of leaves, these much shorter than the internodes; lowest 1-2 pairs of leaves oblanceolate, 2.2-2.8 cm. long, 6 mm. wide, obtuse, sessile, tapering into a petioliform base, entire or with a minute mucronulate tooth on each side toward apex, membranous, triplinerved, rather evenly but not denfsely pilose on both sides with several-celled, yellowish, mostly gland-tipped hairs; middle and upper leaves oblong to lanceo- late, 7-17 mm. long, 1.5-5 mm. wide, obtuse, sessile, entire or with 1-2 pairs of small teeth, yellowish green, triplinerved, pubescent like the lower leaves, the uppermost braeteiform; peduncles solitary at apex cf stem and branches, pubescent like the stem, densely so toward apex, inonocephalous, slender, 3.5-10 cm. long; heads 1.5-1.8 cm. wide; stolons about as long as steni, with shorter internodes (3-30 mm. long), denudate below, bearing 3-7 unwithered pairs of leaves toward tip, sparsely stipitate-glandular and very sparsely pilose, glabreseent below, the leaves obovate, 11-23 mm. long, 5-10 mm. wide, rounded at apex, sessile but narrowed into a petioliform base, bearing, usually a pair of darkened obtusely mucronulate teeth toward apex, thin, triplinerved, pubescent like the stem leaves; involuere hemispheric-campanulate, 4.5- 5 mm. high, the phyllaries few (about 13), appressed, oval (1.8-3 mm. wide), rounded, often minutely apiculate, sometimes erose at apex, ciliate and sparsely pilosulous chiefly below the apex with gland-tipped hairs, thin, 5-9-nerved; rays about 16-21, 2-seriate, white, fertile, the tube spreading-pilose with several-celled eglandular hairs, the lamina cuneate, 4.8 mm. long, 3.2-3.6 mm. wide, 3-toothed, 5-6-nerved; disk corollas numerous, greenish yellow, 2.8 mm. long (tube densely spreading-pilose with several-celled eglandular hairs, 1.3 mm., throat broadly campanulate, glabrous or with single hairs in the sinuses, 0.8 mm., teeth ovate, glabrous, 0.7 mm. long); receptacle convex; pales narrowly linear, flat, acuminate, glabrous, 3-vittate, 3.5 mm. long, 0.2 mm. wide; ray achenes obovoid, plumpish, somewhat obcornpressed (the outer) or laterally compressed (the inner), bluntly about 5-angled, blackish, glabrous, epappose, 1.6 mm. long; disk achenes obovoid, slightly com- pressed, bluntly about 5-angled, blackish, epappose, glabrous, striatu- late, 1.4 mm. long.

description: Shrubs or small trees, to 6 m tall; stems densely branched, branches densely pilose, hairs 1 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate to broadly ovate, 10-20 X 8-18 cm, membranaceous, apices acuminate or long acuminate, bases more or less rounded and then cuneate, 3-veined far above the base, margins serrate; adaxial surface scabrous, abaxial surface densely short pilose, hairs 0.5 mm long. Capitulescences paniculiform, with small or large cluster of capitula, leafly at base. Capitula subglobose, sessile or shortly pedicellate, 5 mm high, 3.5 mm diam.; phyllaries 3(-4), broadly ovate, striate, 5 X 4-5 mm, 5-7 veined, apices acute or slightly obtuse to obtusely pointed, strigose, hairs 1 mm long, margins ciliate on distal one-third. Pistillate florets 3-6, subtended by broadly ovate paleae, 4.5 X 4 mm wide, 5-veined, strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long, apices obtuse, scarcely ciliate; corollas white, 2.5 mm long, 1 mm diam., 4- lobed, lobes 0.2 mm long, apices scarcely pubescent; styles 2 mm long, branches 1.5 mm long, tips recurved. Staminate florets 4-10, epaleaceous; corollas white, 2-3 mm long, tubes 1 mm long, expanded into a campanulate throat, 0.5 mm diam., 5-lobed, lobes deltoid, 1 mm long, apices scarcely hirsute; ovaries 1.5 mm long, 0.5 mm diam., hirsute at distal one-third, hairs 0.5 mm long. Cypselae blackish, obovoid, 2 X 1.5 mm, hirsute at apex, hairs 0.5 mm long. Chromosome number, n = 16 (Stuessy & Arriagada, 1993).
bibliographicCitation: Arriagada, J. E. 2003. Revision of the genus Clibadium (Asteraceae, Heliantheae). Brittonia. 55: 245-301.

description: Plant perennial; stem arising from a slender rhizome, or less commonly from a short slightly branched caudex, mostly 2-5 dm. high (in depauperate forms sometimes only 6 cm. high, with leaves correspondingly reduced), hirsute with spreading hairs, the hairs sometimes appressed on the upper part of the stem; leaves sparsely to densely hirsute, numerous, equably distributed, the cauline ones lanceolate or lance-oblong to ovate, mostly acute, up to 8 cm. long and 25 mm. wide, usually smaller, the basal ones oblanceolate or elliptic, obtuse or rounded at the apex, tapering to the petiole, the blades usually smaller than those of the cauline leaves; heads usually solitary, occasionally 2 or 3, rarely more; disk 9-13 mm. wide; involuere mostly 5-8 mm. high, the phyllaries somewhat glandular or viscid, and sparsely to densely hirsute, the outer ones mostly 0.4-0.9 mm. wide, acute or acuminate, appressed, the inner ones usually attenuate into thin scarious flexuous tips; ligules 50-100, white or pink, 1-1.5 mm. wide, 7-14 mm: long; diskcorollas 3.0-4.0 mm. long, the tube about 0.7-0.9 mm. long, usually not sharply defined, the lobes about 0.5 mm.; style-appendages triangular-lanceolate, clearly acute, about 0.15-0.2 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of 15-25 bristles, the outer obscure, scanty, and setulose, rarely apparently wanting; akenes hairy,2-nerved. Mountains of central and southern Arizona and New Mexico, at 7000-10,000 feet; in Arizona, known from Coconino, Graham, Cochise, and Pima Counties, on the Mogollon Plateau, and in the Pinaleno, Chiricahua, Huachuca, and Santa Catalina Mountains; in New Mexico, known from Lincoln and Otero Counties, in the White and Sacramento Mountains.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Plants annual (stems sometimes appearing perennial and rhizomnatous when covered with drifting dune sand), 30-60 cm high; stems erect, sparingly branched, pubescent with short, white appressed hairs and densely covered throughout with short stipitate glands, the latter 0.2-0.4 mm long; lower leaves simple and opposite, the upper ones trifoliate or irregularly lobed, all pubescent with coarse appressed hairs; mid-stem leaves with petioles 1.5-2.5 cm long; blades (or leaflets) broadly to narrowly ovate, 0.6-2 cm wide, 3-4 cm long, 1.5-4 times as long as wide, acute at the apex; inflorescence a subcorymbose cyme, with 10 to numerous heads; heads turbinate, 4-6 mm across, 5-8 mm high, 10- to 16-flowered, on peduncles 3-15 mm. long; principal involueral bracts 8-10, 4-6 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, obovate or spatulate with white membranous margins, rounded at the apex, glabrous or with a scattered short pubescence; florets white, distinctly zygomorphic; corollas 4 mm long, the throat about 1 mm long, the lobes 1-2 mm long; style branches flattened, 1-1.5 mm long, with well-defined stigmatic lines, abruptly terminated by a penicillate, cuspidate appendage, otherwise glabrous; achenes 4-4.5 mm long, obpyramidal, 4-sided, rather sparsely strigose to nearly glabrous; pappus of 8-10 obovate scales, 1.5-2 mm long, broadly rounded at the apex and without terminal awns or mucros; chromosome number, n = 10.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1963. Taxonomy of Forestina (Helenleae, Compositae). Brittonia. 15: 27-46.

description: Herba perennis erecta ca. 3 m. alta, caulibus costatis, lanuginosis. Folia papyracea, alterna, petiolata, late ovata, apice acuminata, basi rotundata vel paulum cordata, margine dentata: dentibus triangularibus acuminatis, superne glabra, inferne lanuginosa, nervo primario subtus exsculpto, secundariis utroque latere ca. 20, 20-35 cm. longa, 11-20 cm. lata; petiolo lanuginoso, longitudine limbo fere aequante. Capitula permulta, radiata, in paniculis definitis amplis disposita; pedicellis lanuginosis 6-12 mm. longis. Involucrum campanulatum, calyculatum, 7-8 mm. altum, 7 mm. crassum; bracteolis calyculi multis, brevissimis; bracteis involucri ca. 13, oblongo-linearibus, acutis, dorso glabris vel leviter pilosis. Flores dimorphi: marginales 810 feminei, ligulati, tubulo 5 mm. longo, ligula elliptica 4 mm. longa, 1.5 mm. lata; flores disci ca. 25, hermaphro-. diti, corolla tubulosa 7 mm. longa, limbo dilatata pentalobataque: lobulis lanceo- latis, acutis, 1 mm. longis, ad medium nervatis. Antherae appendicibus angustis, basi sub-sagittatae. Styli rami apice truncati. Achaenia (valde inmatura) cylindra- cea, costata, glabra, 2 mm. longa. Pappus exasperatus, albus, circa 7 mm. longus.
bibliographicCitation: Cabrera, Ángel L. 1950. Notes on the Brazilian Senecioneae. Brittonia. 7: 53-74.

description: Perennial herbs, (2.4) 3-5 (7.5) dm tall, from a stout woody caudex; stems strigose to strigose-hirsute becoming glabrate with age. Leaves mainly on lower 2/3 of stems, greatly reduced upwards, sometimes basally clustered, the sessile blades (1.4) 3-5 (6.5) cm long, (0.2) 0.4-0.8 (1.3) cm wide, the basal ones wider and oblanceolate, those at middle stem linear-elliptic, widest at the middle, acu- minate, basally cuneate, the margins revolute, sparsely (sometimes densely) strigose-hispid above, densely (sometimes sparsely) strigose-hispid and sparsely glandular below. Inflorescences paniculate-cymose, the branches forming a zig-zag pattern. Heads (17) 35-58 (65)-flowered; peduncles 1-4 cm long, strigose- villous. Involucre broadly campanulate, (4) 6-10 (11) mm high, (7) 8-11 (14) mm wide. Phyllaries loosely imbricated in 3-4 series, arachnoid to slightly villous, the inner ones lanceolate (4) 6-8 (9) mm long, (1) 1.3-1.8 (2) mm wide, long- acuminate, the outer ones lanceolate (2) 3-5 (5.5) mm long, (0.5) 0.9-1.4 mm wide. Pappus whitish to straw-colored, the inner bristles (5.5) 6-8.5 (10) mm long, the outer scale-like ones (0.8) 1.6-2 (2.8) mm long. Corollas (6) 10-11 (13) mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers (2.2) 3.3-3.8 (5) mm long. Achenes (1.5) 1.8-2 (2.4) mm long, strigose, glandular. Chromosome number n = ca 17. Flowering and fruiting from (September) November to February (June).

description: Plants annual, 10-45(-60) cm high, simply branched to divaricate, the outer branches decumbent, the inner ones suberect, hirsute; leaves pinnately lobed or divided, the lobes subfiliform to linear and acute, 1.7-8 cm long, cuneate to attenuate at the base, evenly hirsute on both surfaces; petioles 0.4-2 cm long; heads broadly campanulate, 1-2 cm in diameter, solitary on long, slender peduncles; peduncles 5-12(-24) cm long, sparsely to densely short-hirsute, the trichomes appressed, sparsely interspersed with glandular trichomes, especially near the heads; receptacle conical, 4-5 mm across, 5-6 mm high; chaff persistent, scarious, glabrous, (6.5-)8.5-10 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, obovate below, tapering to an attenuate, awn-like beak at the apex; involucre 4-5-seriate, the outer bracts green oblong (subovate), puberulent to glabrous, rounded at the apex, with scarious, usually purple margins and apex; inner bracts progressively longer, oblong to subovate, puberulent to glabrous, the longest 7-10(-12) mm long, 3.5-5 mm wide, becoming membranous, with conspicuous, scarious, usually purple margins, rounded to obtuse at the apex; ray flowers 8, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 6.5-7(-8) mm, with conspicuous white to roseate ligules, (7-)8-12 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, obovate, reflexed, 3-lobed at the apex; ray corollas with 2 linear lobelets, ca 1 mm long; pappus of the ray florets like that of the discs; disc corollas yellow, (5-)6-7.5 mm long, the tube 2-3 mm long, sparsely pilose to glabrous near the throat, throat tubular, often broadly so, 3-3.5 mm long, sparsely pilose to glabrous near the base, lobes acute 1-1.5 mm long, minutely pubescent on the margins; style branches recurved, slender, rather flattened, ca 1.5 mm long, with a subulate tip, scarcely pubescent except near the apex, the stigmatic lines obscure, on the inner margins; achenes black, turbinate to subturbinate, (2-) 2.5-3 mm long, often obscurely 4-5-ridged, with long, silky-pilose hairs, those often concentrated on the ridges, the hairs 2-3 mm long; pappus of 35-45 unequal, plumose bristles, (4,5-) 5.5-7 mm long, the shortest 12 to almost as long as the longest, cilia silky, 1-1.5 mm long; anthers 3-3.5 mm long, sagittate at the base; chromosome number, n = 10, determined in the 2 populations indicated below with an asterisk.

description: Rhizomatous perennial. Stems erect, 40- 60 cm tall, terete, sparsely lanulose, reddish in upper part; upper branches sparse, elongate, bearing a few pairs of small leaves. Lower leaves withered at anthesis. Cauline leaves opposite; lamina thick, deltoid to round-ovate, ca. 20 X 17-20 mm, subequal in size below branches, subacute at apex, truncate or sometimes cuneate at base, crenulate along margin, sparsely hispidulous above, manicate beneath, punctate-glandular (yellow) on both surfaces; veins not conspicuous; petioles ca. 6 mm long. Lateral shoots from leaf axils often developed shortly, bearing 1 or 2 pairs of small leaves. Heads many, ca. 12 X 6-7 mm, nearly sessile, in several compound dense corymbs; each corymb 10-30 mm wide, consisting of 10-20 heads. Inflorescence branches and peduncles puberulous with short woolly hairs and stipitate-glandular. Phyllaries ca. 7 mm long, acuminate at apex, pale green, tinged with red-purple near apex, covered with glandular red-purple hairs, short woolly hairs and sessile yellow glands outside. Corolla sparsely puberulous and sparsely sessile-glandular outside; tubes dark pink, 6-7 mm long; lobes white, ca. 2 mm long. Achenes ca. 4.5 mm long, dark brown, hispidulous. Pappus awns 5-7, as long as corolla, covered with minute spines, red-purple above.

description: Perennial herbs with simple or branched caudex and stout taproot, the caudex branches short, clothed with persistent leaf bases, the stems arising directly from the caudex, 2-4.2 dm tall, villous; leaves of sterile basal rosettes mostly 8-21 cm long, twice to thrice pinnately divided, the segments lance-attenuate to acute, villous on both sides; cauline leaves similar to the basal, the lower ones longer than the lowermost, becoming smaller upwards, often with stipule-like divisions near the base; inflorescence paniculate or racemose; heads several to numerous, nodding, sessile or on peduncles to 5 cm long; involucres 3.5-5 mm high, 6-11 mm wide, the bracts villous-pilose, with broad brownish-scarious margins; marginal flowers pistillate, fertile; central flowers pistillate, fertile, the corollas long-hairy, cream to pale yellow; receptacle and achenes glabrous.

description: Rhizomes extensively branched, frequently forming an approximate crown, the short shoots often clothed at the summit with imbricated scales; stem simple, 3.0-6.0 dm. tall, 2.0-4.0 mm. thick, variously but seldom densely pubeseent with septate hairs and stipitate glands, occasionally red-tinged; cauline leaves 3-4(5) pairs, the lower leaves and those of the innovationls more or less pilose and short-stipitate-glandular; petioles sometimes wingmargined, shorter than or exceeding the lanceolate to cordate blades which are 3.0-6.0 cmn. broad and 5.0-10 cm. long, obtuse or acute, irregularly moderately or sharply dentate, more or less villous and short-stipitate-glandular; middle cauline leaves spathulate or broadly sessile, reduced; infloreseence extensive, the branches sometimes alternate by disjunction of the nodes, the bracts smiall, narrow; peduncle 2.0-15 cm. long; heads 3-15(20), 12-25 mm. high, turbinate to campanulate; periclinium more or less densely villous and short-stipitate-glandular; involueral bracts 10-14, 10-15 mm. long, narrowly to broadly lanceolate, obtusish to acute, scantily or obviously villous and short- or long-stipitate-glandular, the upper margins moderately or densely villous-ciliate, the tips conspicuously pilose within; ray flowers none, but occasionally the inarginal flowers becoming ampliate, the normal disc corollas 8.0-12 mm. long, goblet-shaped, frequently narrowly so, the tube and the base of the limb moderately to densely villous, the limb sometimes pubescent to the summit, the collar inconspicuous to prominent; tube 3.6-5.4 mm. long, the eorolla lobes 0.8-1.2 mm. long, sparingly short-stipitate-glandular or hirsutulose; achenes 6.0 (5.5)-8.0 (8.5) mm. long, variously glandular or hirsute, with double hairs; annulus 0.2-0.3 mm. long; pappus white, -+ the length of the corolla, barbellate to subplumose, the setae 0.1-0.3 imm. long.

description: Arbuscula ad 8 met. alta ramulis terminalibus plus minusve flexuosis anguloso- striatis ferrugineo-tomentulosis. Folia opposita petiolata coriacea. Petiolus 2-3 cm. longus striatus ferrugineo- tomentosus supra sulcatus. Lamina elliptico-oblonga vel lanceolato-oblonga, basi cordata vel subcordata apicem versus angustata apice obtusa vel acutiuscula, margine integra, 7-17 cm. longa, 3.5-6.5 cm. lata; supra juvenilis stellato- pilosa denique nervo medio conspicuo pilosiusculo excepto glabra, nervis secundariis pallidis visibilibus reticulo nervulorum paulo conspicuo; subtus ferrugineo-tomentulosa costa crassa prominenti striata nervis secundariis 9-10 utroque latere paulo ascendentibus prominentibus nervulis laxe reticulatis plus minusve conspicuis. Inflorescentiae terminales cymoso-paniculatae basi foliosae folia non vel parum excedentes, axi ramulisque striolatis rufo-tomentosis plus minusve flexuosis bracteolis linearibus brevibus munitis. Pedicelli teneres 4-20 mm. longi tomentelli sparsis bracteolis linearibus minutis ad apicem vix calyculum formantibus. Capitula radiata. Involucrum subconicum 8 bracteis submembranaceis oblongis subacutis 4.5 mm. longis, exterioribus 1 mm. latis extus tomentellis, interioribus 2-2.2 mm. latis margine late scariosis dorso tomentellis. Flores marginales feminei ligulati circa 5, corolla 10.5-11 mm. longa glabra tubulo 3.5 mm. longo lamina tridentata 2 mm. lata. Flores disci hermaphroditi tubulosi 10-11, corolla 7 mm. longa glabra tubulo 3 mm. longo dentibus oblongis 2 mm. longis. Antherae 2 mm. longae basi apiculatae. Stigmata conica. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus 6.5 mm. longus pilis apice incrassatis.

description:
Ex affinitate Steviae monardifoliae H.B.K. foliis breviter petiolatis triangulatis a congeneri diversa

Herba (?) perennis ramosissima, basi mihi incognita. Caules erecti ad 6 dm alti purpurei vel brunnei breviter pilosi, inferne lignescentes; rami inferiores oppositi, superiores alterni; internodia laminis foliorum 1-2-plo longiora. Folia opposita (praeter ea inflorescentiae), crassomembranacea vel chartacea, breviter petiolata; laminae triangulares subtriplinerviae 2.5-3.0 cm longae 1.5-2.2 cm latae (rameales minores) crenatae vel crenulatae, apice acutae vel obtusae (infimae rotundatae), basi truncatae vel cordatae vel subhastatae, supra dense minuteque puberulae, infra puberulae et pilosae et glandulis pellucidis sessilibus obsitae; petioli graciles ca. 3-6 mm longi non alati; venae saepe rufae, infra elevatae reticulataeque, supra eae majores depressae eae minores minute reticulatae. Inflorescentia corymbosa gregibus capitulorum aggregatissimorum bracteatis; ramuli pro parte maxima alterni, pilosi plerumque stipitato-glandulosi; bracteae foliaceae conspicuae. Capitula ca. 8 mm longa per anthesin; involucra 5-6 mm longa, phyllariis oblongis, apice breviter acuminatis, integris purpurascentibus puberulis, glandulis stipitatis minutis paucis vel multis obsitis. Corollae ca. 8 mm longae per anthesin, pallide roseae in lobis et basi tubi hirsutae; lobi ca. 1 mm longi; fauces cum tubo 5 mm longi. Achenia (immatura) 2 mm longa sparsim minuteque hispida brunnea aliquantum vernicosa; pappus coroniformis integer 0.1 mm vel minus altus.

description: Suffrutex 3.5 m. alt. ramis atriatis glabris ramulis striolulatis indumento lanuginoso crispo deciduo vestitis. Folia alterna membranacea crassiuscula in ramis adultis sterilibusque petiolata in ramulis floriferis superiora sessilia. Petiolus 2-3 cm. longus tomentoso-lanatus supra sulcatus, subtus rotundato-carinatus denique glaber, basi ample vaginato-dilatatus. Lamina ovato-oblonga basi rotundata inaequilatera apice acuta margine anguste revoluta denticulata, dentibus callosis subacutis, 7-10 cm. longa, 2.5-4.5 cm. lata; supra primum indumento tenue lanuginoso deciduo vestita deinde glabrescens costa nervisque secundariis notatis nervulis obsoletis sed aspectu superficie rugulosa; subtus crassiuscule lanato-tomentosa costa elevata nervis secundariis circa 10 utroque latere prominulis ascendentibus marginem versus evanescentibus venulis obsoletis. Folia superiora in ramulis fertilibus sessilia basi profunde cordato-amplexic aulia. Inflorescentiae terminale s corymboso-paniculatae basi foliosae ramulis lanuginosis. Capitula discoidea pedicellata. Pedicelli 3-10 mm. longi mediocres flexuosi lanuginosi paulis bracteolis angustis 3,mm. longis praediti, apice 6-7 bracteolis acutis 2-3 mm. longis lanuginosis brevem calyculum formantibus. Involucrum hemisphaerico-campanulatum 17-19 bracteis linearibus acuminatis 5.5 mm. longis 1-1.5 mm. latis margine scariosis dorso herbaceis crassis parce puberulis vel glabratis, apice ciliatis. Receptaculum planum 3.5 mm. diam. foveo- latum. Flores omnes hermaphroditi circa 60 tubulosi corolla flava glabra 6 mm. longa tubulo 3 mm. Antherae 2 mm. longae basi obtusae. Stigmata incrassata conica. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus albidus.

description: Foliis uniformibus parvis (minus quam 2 cm longis) lanceolatis, ramis numerosis gracilibus ascendentibus, internodiis subaequalibus ex congeneris distinguitur. Herba perennis. Rhizoma breve. Caules plures graciles ad 45 cm alti minute puberuli vel glabri vel subglabri rufi; internodia subaequalia 2-3 cm longa; rami oppositi (superne alterni) graciles ad angulum ca. 450 ex axe patentes. Folia infime opposita superne alterna oblanceolata vel raro elliptica sessilia membranacea, apice acuta, basi cuneata, ea caulium principalium et ramorum majorum 13-17 mm longa 5-7 mm lata, ea ramorum lateralium 9-12 mm longa 2.5-4.0 mm lata, supra infraque puberula et glanduloso-punctata; venae praeter nervum medium plerumque inconspicuae. Inflorescentiae corymbosae plus minusve planae ad apicem, in caule principali et in aliquibus ramis lateralibus portatae. Capitula brevissime pedunculata, 9-10 mm alta per anthesin; involucra 4-5 mm longa, phyllariis purpureis (minimum ad apicem) oblongis integris, apice acuta submucronata. Corollae 5-6 mm longae per anthesin purpureae extus sparsim puberulae; lobi pallidiores 1.0-1.3 mm longi; fauces cum tubo 4.5-5.0 mm longae. Achenia (immatura) 3-4 mm longa pappo excluso brunnea costis pallidis, hispida, aut semper exaristata corona squamellarum 0.5 mm longarum praedita aut semper aristata aristis 3-4 necnon aliquot squamellis discretis parvis praedita aut semper aristata aristis 5 necnon squamellis 5 sublaceratis 0.4 mm altis alternantibus praedita.

description: Rhizomes short branching, 2-3 mm. in diam., frequently becoming knotted, dark brown, scales dark and imbricate toward summit of branches; stems 2-4 mm. in diam., 1.5-4.0(5.0) dm. tall, frequently reddish, pilose toward the base with septate hairs, long-stipitate-glandular, becoming less conspicuously so above, the hairs frequently red pigmented; cauline leaves 3-4(5) pairs, frequently crowded toward the stem base, the lower leaves and those of the innovations with broad winged petioles equaling or shorter than the blades, the leaves thus oblanceolate or spathulate, the blades 2-3 cm. broad and about 4-6 cm. long, sharply and sometimes irregularly doubly dentate, more or less densely villous, the middle leaves broadly wing petioled or sessile, the uppermost reduced; peduncles 8-10(20) cm. long, more or less villous or pilose, and conspicuously long-stipitate-glaildular; heads 3-15, seldom only 1 or as many as 20, 18-20 mm. high, campanulate-turbinate; perielinium pilose and glandular; involueral bracts 10-12, lanceolate to lance-oblong, acute, seldom obtusish, pilose and glandular toward the base, less densely pubescent above, the tips pilose on the margins and within; ray flowers none; disc corollas 9(8) -10.5 (11.5) mm. long more or less coarsely villous and pilose, and frequently short-stipitate-glaildular, the limb glabrous above, the collar conspicuous, the corolla lobes acutish, ca. 1.0 mm. long, hirsutulose; pappus white, barbellate, the setae 1.5-1.8 mm. long; achenes 7(6)-8(10) mm. long. sparsely short-stipitate-glandular, frequently with a few double hairs above the middle; anlulus ca. 0.36 mm. long.

description: Plant perennial from a stout usually branched caudex; stem mostly 5-10 cm. long, occasionally a little more or less, somewhat glandular and sparsely spreading-hairy, subnaked, usually bearing two or three reduced linear leaves; leaves clustered at the base, pinnatifid, the lobes linear or nearly so; sometimes with one or two sublobes, bristly-ciliate on the petioles, otherwise usually nearly glabrous, commonly with a few glands or appressed hairs, or both, occasionally conspicuously glandular; heads solitary, the disk about 9-13 mm. wide,; involuere 5.5-8 mm. high, glandular and usually sparsely or moderately hirsute, the phyllaries subequal, usually purple or purplish at least at the margins and tips, sometimes throughout; ligules 40-70, uniformly blue or purplish, 7-12 mm. long, a little over 1 mm. (sometimes nearly 2 mm.) wide; disk-corollas about 3.8-4.5 mm. long, the lobes about 0.6-0.8 mm., the tube very ill-defined and about 0.8-1.2 mm. long; style-appendages narrowly to broadly lanceolate or triangular-lanceolate, acute, often very sharply so, about 0.25-0.35 mm. long; pappus simple or nearly so, of about 25-30 bristles, usually unequal in length and often much shorter than the corolla, sometimes with a few short setae intermingled; akenes hairy, 2-nerved. Alpine and occasionally upper subalpine stations; Colorado, extending into southern Wyoming and northern New Mexico.

description: Perennial herb with a stout taproot and rootcrown or short caudex; stems numerous, ascending, mostly 5-15 (rarely 25) cm. high, more or less densely spreading-villous with long white hairs, sometimes also finely and obscurely glandular; leaves pubescent like the stem, oblanceolate or broadly linear, all nearly alike, without a basal tuft, only slightly reduced upwards, the lower ones sometimes with more evident distinction into blade and petiole than the others, the larger ones mostly 1-2 em. long, 2-3 mm. wide; heads solitary or few, the disk 7-14 mm. wide; involucre4-6 mm. high, glandular; phyllaries evidently imbricate, firm, acuminate, green or greenish, especially the outer, occasionally a little purplish near the tips; pistillate flowers absent; disk-corollas about 3.7-5.0 mm. long, the tube 0.7-1.3 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm.; style-appendages broadly triangular, obtuse, 0.1 mm. long; pappus double, tlfe inner of about 12-25(28) white or brownish bristles, the outer of evident setae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely hairy.
