description: Perennial herb with a stout taproot and rooterown; stems 10-35 cm. high, moderately to densely spreading-villous or -villosulous, often also more or less glandular, the hairs averaging shorter and often coarser than those of E. miser; leaves numerous, longer than the internodes, all nearly alike, without a basal tuft, only gradually reduced upwards, mostly bi:oadly linear or narrowly oblanceolate, the larger ones mostly 2-4 cm. long, 2-5 mm. wide, more or less hairy like the stem, and sometimes also strongly glanidular, apt to be less hairy when more glandular, sometimes conspicuously long-ciliate on the margins; heads several or sometimes solitary, the disk about 9-15 mm. wide; involucre 5-9 mm. high, densely glandular; phyllaries strongly imbricate, firm, acuminate, greenish,t sometimes with a brown midrib, often strongly purplish above the middle, and sometimes with fairly well developed Aster-like green areas near the tips; pistillate flowers absent; disk-corollas 4.5-6.5 mm. long, the tube obscure, 1.0-1.3 mm. long, the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm. long and usually pink or reddish, sometimes merely yellow; style-appendages 0.15-0.2 mm. long, broadly triangular to nearly deltoid, obtuse or acutish; pappus of about 25-40 (rarely only 20) firm white or sonetimes sordid bristles, generally with a few short and inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely hairy.

description: Plants annual, from a well developed taproot, 30-110 cm high, glabrate below, becoming sparsely glandular-pubescent above; basal rosette absent or weakly defined and soon deciduous; stems terete, stout, to 6 mm in diameter, leafy throughout, single at first but often developing basal branches so that the whole plant becomes relatively large and rank; lower leaves of primary shoots variable, from linear-oblanceolate to linear-lanceolate, mostly entire to irregularly lobed, 1-8 cm long, 0.4-1.5 cm wide, rather evenly short-pubescent with appressed hairs, gradually tapering into a narrow, winged, semi-clasping petiole, the upper leaves becoming successively reduced and entire, gradually passing into the short, subulate, frequently glabrate leaves of the inflorescence; heads on primary shoot 5-50, becoming numerous after secondary branching; involuere hemispheric, with 75-100 florets (fewer in late-flowering heads), 5-10 mm across, 3-5 mm high, erect at anthesis but usually reflexing in age; peduncle 1-4 cm long, sparsely to conspicuously glandular-pubescent; involueral bracts ca 40, in 2-3 series, imbricated, subulate, green and herbaceous above, searious below; principal involueral bracts linear-lanceolate, 3-5 mm long, 0.75-1 mrm wide, nearly glabrous to densely glandular-pubescent; receptacle flat; ray florets 32-50, the ligules (4-)5-7 mm long, 0.75 mm wide, light blue or blue-violet to white, enrolling or drying, the tube 1.2-1.5 mm long; disk corollas pale yellow, rarely with purple lobes, 4-5 mm long the lobes, erect, 0.5-0.8 mm long; style branches 0.75 mm long, with an acute ciliate appendage; anthers ea 1.5 mm long, scarcely exserted; achenes of disk florets 2-2.4 mm long, with 5-7 indistinct ribs, thinly pubescent throughout with short aseending hairs; pappus of 30-40 bristles 2.5-4.0 mm long; ray achenes somewhat shorter than but essentially like the disk achenes; chromosome number, n = 4.

description: Perennial; herbage spreading-hirsute and finely glandular; stems several from a taproot, sprawling or pendant, branched, the lower part resembling the caudex of E. vagtus, leafy, especially near the tip; leaves cuneate to obovate, up to about 4 cm. long and 1.5 cm. wide, more or less deeply and often irregularly trilobed, the lobes broad, often slightly lobed again; lower leaves soon withering and sometimes deciduous; heads terminating the leafy branches; disk about 8-12 mm. wide; involuere 5-6 mm. high, densely and finely glandular, the outer phyllaries sometimes with a few stiff hairs on the margins; phyllaries subequal or the outer shorter, green, the slender acuminate tips commonly purplish; ligules about 25-30, pink or pink-purple, about 5-7 mm. long, 1.4-1.6 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.2-3.9 mm. long, the tube 0.8-1.0 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.6 mm.; style-appendages triangular-ovate, obtusish, about 0.1-0.15 mm. long; pappus of about 10-15 bristles, with some inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, hairy.

description: Perennial, precumbent, suffrutescent herbs up to 1.4 dm high; stems strigose, reddish brown to yellow, obscurely striate, densely strigose at the nodes; leaves sessile to short-petioled, elliptic-oblong to elliptic-linear, 2.5 cm long, 1.2 cm wide; peduncles densely strigose, usually less than 5 mm long but occasionally up to 3 cm; heads hemispheric, up to 8 mm wide, rarely 10 mhm wide; phyllaries obovate, becoming searious, finely and sparsely strigose, with purplish or dark brown summit bands, erect or subsquarrose at the apex; rays ca 7, yellow, suborbicular, ca 7 mm long with a 1 mm tube, flaring at the base and adnate to the inside of the horns, velvety above, minutely hirsute beneath and at the throat; ray achenes 3-angled, oblanceolate to cuneate, 3.2 mm long, tuberculate when mature, depressed at apex, the pappus of two erect or ilnwardly directed hoins; disk corollas sparsely pubescent on lobes and throat outside, yellow below, the lobes yellow-tipped inside, orange below, orange outside; disk achenes laterally compressed, oblanceolate, emarginate, the margins ciliate, the pappus of a single, long, slender eaducous awn; chaff entire to minutely erose at apex, yellow or with scattered purple areas, becoming cuspidate, exceeding the disk flowers; receptacle convex.

description: Erect herb or shrub to 2 m tall, sparingly branched; leaves, phyllaries, corollas, and styles bearing glandular hairs. Stems striate, often deeply grooved, light brown. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petioles up to 5 cm long, not winged; blades ovate, cuneate to rounded at base, blades of basal leaves broadly ovate, rounded to subcordate at base, blades 5-16 cm long, 3-12 cm wide, rather palmately veined; margin crenulate- serrulate; apex acuminate. Inflorescence a thyrsoid panicle, up to 30 cm long, and to 15 cm wide. Heads numerous, ca. 5-6 mm high, ca. 7-12(10)-flowered. Phyllaries ca. 10, narrowly oblong, apex rather acute, with few or no striae, green, pubescent with densely fringed margin. Receptacle slightly to strongly convex, chaffy. Corollas white, funnelform, ca. 2.5 mm long. Pappus of 22-30 white setae ca. 2.5 mm long, not dilated at tips. Achenes dark brown or black, ca. 1.5 mm long, 4-5-ribbed; ribs setose; carpopodium well developed. Pollen tricolpate, spherical, minutely papillose, ca. 20 µ in diameter.

description: Shrubs, 4 m tall; stems sometimes prostrate, glabrous to strigose, hairs 1 mm long. Leaves sessile; blades 8-20 X 5-11 cm, broadest near the middle; narrowly ovate; apices acuminate, bases cuneate, margins serrate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially strigillose, hairs 0.5-1 mm long; petioles 2-6 cm long, 2 mm diam., winged, wings decreasing toward nodes to become subauriculate at base. Capitula radiate, 3.5-4.5 mm high; involucres cupulate, 3-4 mm diam.; phyllaries 3, 3-4 X 2.5-3 mm, ovate to obovate, 7-12-veined, abaxially glabrous, apices obtuse, margins ciliate on distal one-third. description: Plants 3-12 dm tall. Stems moderately to strongly winged, glabrous to occasionally very sparsely pubescent above. description: Stout herb, the caudex erect, 1-3 m. high at maturity, clothed with loosely deflexed old leaves; leaves coriaceous, elliptic-oblong or obovate-spatulate, 30-50 cm. long, 4-8 cm. broad, conspicuously narrowed proximally to 7-15 mm., acute at apex, entire at margins, copiously appressed ferruginous or cinereous lanate on both sides, the costa stout, the secondary nerves 1 or 2 per centimeter, ascending, parallel, usually visible beneath and obscure above; flowering branches exceeding the leaves, copiously ferruginous tomentose, corymbose-paniculate, 6-15-headed, the lower branches often short, opposite, subtended by foliaceous bracts; heads at maturity 25-40 mm. in diameter; phyllaries 15-25, 2- or 3-seriate, papyraceous, oblong or oblong-ovate, obtuse, the outer ones 15-18 mm. long, 10-15 mm. broad, ferruginous lanate without, the inner ones narrowed; ray florets very numerous, the corolla 16-19 mm. long, the tube 2-3 mm. long, hispid, the lamina oblong, 2.5-3 mm. broad, 2- or 3-lobed at apex, the style and stigmas 5-7 mm. long, the achene 2-3 mm. long; disk florets 6-8 mm. long, the tube hispidulous, shorter than the limb, the lobes ovate-deltoid, the stamens 5-7 mm. long, the filaments frequently longer than the anthers; paleae membranaceous, oblong or obovate-oblong, 5-6 mm. long, about 2 mm. broad, densely pilose distally without with crisp brown hairs.

description: Trees to 4 m tall; stems striate, ferruginous-villous. Leaves alternate, petiole 2.3-3 cm long, ferruginous-villous, blade oblong-elliptic to obovate, 10-18 cm long, 5-6 cm wide, basally obtuse, apically obtuse to rounded, lower surface prominent-reticulate, tomentose to lanate, upper surface bullate, villosulous especially along midvein, margin entire, secondary veins remotely mucronate. Capitulescences terminal and axillary, corymbose-paniculate, congested, peduncles 2-8 cm long, cinereous-villous, secondary peduncles 1-2 cm long, cinereousvillous. Capitula with 6-7 florets, sessile or subsessile; involucre campanulate, ca 8 mm high, ca 4 mm wide; phyllaries 4-5-seriate, imbricate, graduate, the outer ovate, 3-5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, apically obtuse, densely tomentose, gray-brown, indurate, ciliate, the inner ovate to lanceolate, 5-5.7 mm long, 1-2.5 mm wide, apically acute to attenuate, occasionally bi- or trifid, tomentose, stramineous, cartilaginous, deciduous with mature achenes; receptacle convex; corolla lavender, tube cylindric, ca 7.5 mm long, limb narrowly campanulate, lobes 2-2.5 mm long, ca 0.5 mm wide, strongly reflexed, apically glandular, spiculiferous, anthers ca 2.5 mm long, basally sagittate, auricles truncate, terminal appendages obtuse, style branches filiform-subulate, ca 2 mm long, abaxial surface hispidulose. Achenes turbinate, ca 2 mm long, ca 10-ribbed, sparsely glandular at base; pappus white, biseriate, filiform, outer bristles 1-3 mm long, inner bristles ca 6 mm long.

description: Robust, herbaceous perennial from tuberous rootstock, to 2.4 m tall, with 1 to several erect stems. Stems glaucous, nearly terete to slightly angled, the internodes hollow, the lower nodes hollow but upper nodes solid. Median leaves 27-35 cm (including petioles) long, twice compound with stipels frequently at the first and/or second rachis node, primary leaflets 5-7, pinnules opposite on rachilla; margins of ultimate leaf segments eciliolate; petioles 7-11 cm, solid. Capitulum to 14.5 cm diam. on terminal or axillary stems; the peduncle 14-32 cm; disk florets fertile, tubular, yellow; ray florets sterile, ligules 7 or 8, 5.8- 7 X 2.1-3.2 cm, light lavender with darker longitudinal veins on the abaxial surface. Inner involucral bracts 7 or 8, 9-16 X 4- 7.5 mm; outer involucral bracts 5 or 6, narrowly spatulate to oblong, 9-14 X 2-3 mm, reflexed at anthesis. Achenes black, 10.2-13.1 X 1.7-2 mm. Plants glabrous. Flowering from August through at least October.

description: Perennial herbs, 1.2-1.6 m tall; stems canescent. Leaves chiefly basal and greatly reduced upwards; petioles 7-20 mm long, canescent; basal blades 14-21 cm long, 2.5-4.5 cm wide; middle stem blades 3.5-11 cm long, 0.4-1.6 cm wide, oblong-elliptic, widest at the middle, apically acute, basally cuneate, marginally revolute with remote callous teeth, glabrate and prominently reticulate veined above, canescent beneath. Inflorescences branched and somewhat scorpioid- to paniculate-cymose. Heads 32-51-flowered; peduncles 2-5 cm long, canescent. Involucre broadly campanulate, 7.5-9.5 mm high, 9.5-11 mm wide; phyllaries imbricate in ca 5 series, canescent, the inner ones oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, 5.9-7 mm long, 1.3-1.6 mm wide, the outer ones ovate, 1.2-1.5 mm long, 0.7-1.1 mm wide. Pappus brownish, the inner bristles 5.5-6.5 mm long and outer scales 2-2.5 mm long. Corollas 7.5-8 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers 4.5-5 mm long. Achenes 2.5-2.8 mm long, pilose. Flowering and fruiting from April to May.

description: Plants from a simple caudex or very slender rhizome up to 1.5 cm long. Leaves obovate to obovate-elliptic, 1.7-19 (26) cm long, epetiolate or attenuate to a petiolar region 1/10-1/8 (1/3) as long as the leaf, the blade 7-24 (28) mm wide, densely gray-white to tawny pubescent below, thinly villous and glabrescent above, eventually glabrate, the margins retrorsely serrulate- to denticulate-apiculate, sometimes so minutely as to appear nearly entire, relatively straight (to prominently sinuate), slightly revolute. Stems 6-15 cm tall at anthesis, elongating to 30 (37) cm at fruit release, densely white webby-tomentose, glabrescent, ebracteate, prom- inently dilated immediately beneath the head. Heads 1-4 per plant, erect in bud and fruit; involucre campanulate-cylindrical, 6-10 mm wide (pressed); phyllaries in (3) 4-6 strongly imbricated series, lanceolate with acute to acuminate, often apiculate or mucronulate apices, herbaceous, yellow-green, densely tawny-white villous but often glabrous along the midregion, inner 8.5-12 mm long and 1-1.8 mm wide, to 20 mm in fruit, often with narrow, chartaceous margins, innermost often glabrous and translucent, outermost 1/3-1/4 as long as the inner. Flowers trimorphic, all fertile; outer pistillate flowers 13-23 in 1 (2) series, the corollas 8.6-11 mm long, slightly exceeding the involucre at anthesis, without an inner lip, the ligules 0.2-0.3 mm wide, 1-3 veined, creamy-white, rarely purple-tinged, the apex acute or shallowly notched, the tubular portion 5-6.5 mm long, ca 3/5 as long as the corolla, the style 6.5-8.5 mm long with filiform branches 0.8-1.3 mm long; inner pistillate flowers nearly as numerous as the outer, eligulate or with a minute, ligulate extension ca 0.1 mm long, the tubular portion of corolla 2.4-3.8 mm long; hermaphroditic corollas creamy-white, 6.8-7.5 mm long, weakly bi- labiate, the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm long, erect; anthers with thecae 1.4-1.7 mm long, the apical appendages 0.5-0.6 mm long, truncate; style branches 0.5-0.8 mm long. Achenes 8.4-11.2 mm long, the body 0.5-0.7 mm wide, fusiform, slightly flattened, narrowly elliptic-lanceolate or oblanceolate in outline, with a whitish, fil- iform beak 1/2-2/3 as long as the achene, with (4) 5 (6) light-colored ribs, the surface tan to brown, glabrous to sparsely and inconspicuously glandular-pubescent with minute, usually capitate, thin-walled, biseriate trichomes, these often present only on the ribs; carpopodium very narrow, whitish; pappus bristles tawny-white, 7.8-10.5 mm long at maturity, longer than the disc corollas. Chromosome number 2n = 48, ca 58 (Torres & Liogier, 1970, reported as C. leiocarpa).

description: Perennial, reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes; stems erect, nearly glabrous above and below, glaucous, simple to the inflorescence, up to 20 dm high; leaves cauline, numerous, 10-25 cm long, 2-7 cm wide, basally attenuate, serrate, elliptic to linear-lanceolate, acuminate, with sparse, uniseriate hairs above, and with L-shaped glandular trichomes varying from sparse to dense below; inflorescence loose to irregular, center head opening first; heads 16-26 flowered, involucre cylindric hemispheric, 3.5-5.0 mm high, 3.5-5.5 mm wide; inner bracts lanceolate to ovate, 3-5 mm long, 1.3-3.0 mm wide; outer bracts deltoid; inner bract tips acute to obtuse, often mucronate; outer bract tips acute; bracts green to purple, glabrous to pubescent along margins and outer surface; achenes pubescent on ribs, ca 3.5 mm long; pappus pale straw color, bristles ca. 6 mm long, scales irregular, 0.2-0.8 mm long; flowers from June to August.

description: Rhizomatous perennial. Stems erect, 30- 80 cm tall, terete, puberulous, sometimes almost glabrous, green to reddish, scarcely branched in upper part. Basal leaves withered at anthesis. Leaves opposite; lamina somewhat thick, deltoid to round-ovate, 20-35 X 17-30 mm in the middle part of stems, acute to subacute at apex, round to cuneate at base, crenate along margin, nearly glabrous or sparsely hispid and punctate-glandular on both surfaces, whitish beneath; veins trinerved, conspicuous below; petioles 7-25 mm long. Lateral shoots from leaf axils sometimes shortly developed, bearing a few pairs of small leaves. Heads many, 6-8 X ca. 4 mm, in several compound corymbs; each corymb ca. 5-20 mm wide, consisting of 10-20 heads. Peduncles lanate or sometimes nearly glabrous, sessile-glandular (yellow); peduncles short. Phyllaries ca. 5 mm long, acuminate at apex, pale green, sometimes red-purple at apex, sparsely puberulous and sessile-glandular outside. Corolla white, sparsely sessile-glandular (yellow) outside above; tubes 3.5-4 mm long; lobes 1-1.5 mm long. Achenes 2.5-3 mm long, black, hispid. Pappus scales united to a crown, membranous, whitish, often having 1-5 red-purple awns covered with minute spines as long as corolla. Usually 2 or 3 florets in a head pos- sessing 1-5 awns and the other florets lacking awns, but some plants entirely awnless.

description: Shrubs or subshrubs, infrequently up to 9 dm tall, much branched from the base; stems green, becoming yellow-green to reddish, striate, tomentose; leaves linear to very narrowly lanceeolate, up to 6.5 cm long and 2.3 mm wide, strigose on margins and nerves; peduncles up to 6.5 cm long, tomentose; heads broadly campanulate, 8-11 mm high; phyllaries oblong, rounded at the summit, erose-ciliate with a dark purple summit band, the upper phyllaries squarrose; rays 5-11, deep orange above, dull orange beneath, oblong, up to 15 mm long, the tube 1.0 mm long; ray style ea 4.5 mm long with branches 1 mm long, filiform, glabrous; ray achenes dark brown, oblance-linear, 3-angled, 5-8 mm lolng, striate, minutely ciliate, awnless; disk flowers numerous, orange, 6.8 mm long with lobes ca 1 mm. long, glabrous without; style of the disk flower ca 7 mm long with exserted branches ca 1.6 mm long; disk achenes oblanceolate, compressed or 3- or 4-angled with 2 or 3 unequal awns; chaff orange-tipped, the apex obtuse; receptacle broadly conical.

description: Rhizomes ca. 2 mm. in diam., light brown, branching, the nodes usually 1.0-2.0 cm. apart, the scales 3.0-8.0 mm. long, light brown, sometimes densely imbricate at apex; stems 1.5 (1.0)-3.0 (3.5) dm. high, striate, slender, shortstipitate-glandular and puberulent below, becoming more prominently so and intermixed with septate hairs above; description: Rhizomes short, mostly ascending; stems solitary, simple, 0.5-2.0 dm. high, conspicuously villose, increasingly so upwards; leaves of the infrequent innovatiolls like the lower stem leaves; caulin-e leaves (3)4-5 pairs, 3-15 cm. long, 5-15 mm. broad, the lowermost narrowly lanceolate to oblaileeolate, acute, with short-winged petioles, entire or rarely remotely callous-denticu- late, 3-5-nerved, loosely and mostly densely villous on both surfaces, the over-covering a uniform, obviously stipitate-glandular pubescence, the upper leaves similar, sessile, reduced; head solitary, large, campanulate, 15-20 mm. high; perielinium densely white-lanate-pilose and conspicuously long-stipitate-glandular; involueral bracts 9-14, 2.0-3.5 mm. broad, 10-14 mm. long, broadly lanceolate-oblanceolate, long-villous toward base, less densely so above; ray flowers 9-12, the ligules pale or deep yellow, the teeth 1.0-2.5 (rarely 5) mm. long; disc corollas 8.5(8.0)-10.5(11.1) mm. long, goblet- shaped; tubes 3.5(3.3)-4.5 mm. long, the base of the limb and the tube softly pilose, the collar conspicuous, the collar lobes acute, hirsutulose; achenes 6.0 (5.4)-7.5 (8.4) mm. long, densely hirsute with double hairs which in length exceed 1/2 diam. of the achenes, intermixed with fewer septate hairs.

description: Plants from a simple caudex or slender rhizome up to 2 cm long. Leaves obovate to obovate-elliptic or widely oblanceolate, 2.5-10.5 cm long, epetiolate or attenuate to a petiolar region 1/10-1/8 as long as the leaf, the blade 6-30 mm wide, densely silvery-white pubescent below, tardily glabrescent above and usually remaining thinly white-villous, the margins retrorsely serrulate- to denticulate-apiculate, sometimes so minutely as to appear nearly entire, relatively straight to prominently sinuate, usually slightly revolute. Stems (4) 6-11.5 cm tall at anthesis, elongating to 9.5-38 cm at fruit release, densely white webby-tomentose, glabrescent, ebrac- teate, prominently dilated immediately beneath the head. Heads 1-5 per plant, erect in bud and fruit; involucre turbinate to campanulate-cylindrical, 5-10 mm wide (pressed); phyllaries in 3-5 strongly imbricated series, lanceolate with acute, often apiculate apices, herbaceous, yellow-green, densely white-villous, less so along the midregion, inner 7-12.5 mm long, 0.8-1.7 mm wide, elongating in fruit to 12.5-17.5 mm, the margins chartaceous, sometimes purplish, eglandular, outermost 1/3-1/4 as long as the inner. Flowers trimorphic, all fertile; outer pistillate flowers 1 1-16 (29) in one series, the corollas (6) 7. 1-10 mm long, slightly exceeding the involucre at anthesis, without an inner lip, the ligules (0.2) 0.4-0.7 mm wide, 2-4 veined, greenish to white, very rarely purplish, the apex rounded, acute, or shallowly notched, tubular portion 4-5.5 mm long, ca half as long as the corolla, the style 5.8-7.2 mm long with filiform branches (0.5) 0.7-0.9 mm long and often greenish; inner pistillate flowers nearly as numerous as the outer to ca twice as numerous, with a minute, ligulate extension 0.1-1 mm long, weakly bilabiate, tubular portion of corolla 3.8-4.8 mm long; hermaphroditic corollas creamy- white, sometimes greenish, 5.5-7.5 mm long, weakly bilabiate, the lobes 0.5-1 mm long, erect, the anthers with thecae 1.2-1.5 mm long, the apical appendages 0.5-0.6 mm long, truncate to acutish, the style branches 0.4-0.7 mm long. Achenes 5.5-7.5 (8.5) mm long, the body 0.4-0.6 mm wide, fusiform, slightly flattened, narrowly elliptic to lanceolate or oblanceolate in outline, with a whitish, filiform beak 2/5-3/5 as long as the achene, with 5-6 light-colored ribs, surface tan to brown, prominently pubescent with short, whitish, papillate trichomes, these sometimes sparse or absent on the beak but the beak often glandular-pubescent with minute, often capitate, thin-walled, biseriate trichomes; carpopodium narrow, orange; pappus bristles white to slightly tawny, 5.8-8.5 mm long at maturity, longer than the disc corollas. Chromosome number 2n = 48 (Torres & Liogier, 1970).

description: Perennial herb with a stout branching caudex, the leaf bases of the previous years commonly persistent and conspicuous; stem 5-20 cm. high, lax, decumbent at the base or erect, sparsely strigose with ascending hairs, or nearly glabrous; leaves glabrous or sparsely strigose; basal leaves with petioles 1-7 cm. long, the blades 5-25 mm. long, some or all of them either 3-lobed at the apex or with 3-5 pairs of pinnately disposed acute lobes, or in reduced forms the basal leaves entire, linear-oblanceolate, 2 cm. long or less, not much over 1 mm. wide; cauline leaves linear or linear-oblanceolate, 1-4 cm. long, 1-3 mm. wide, shorter when depauperate; heads solitary or few, the disk about 7-9 mm. wide; involuere 4-5 mm. high, glabrous or sparsely strigose; phyllaries commonly purple or purplish, at least at the tips, clearly imbricate; liguhles few, only about 20-35, pink, 6-8 mm. long, about 1-1.5 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 2.9-3.7 mm. long, the tube 0.6-0.8 mm. long, the lobes 0.5-0.6 mm.; style-appendages distinctly ovate, acute, about 0.3-0.35 mm. long; pappus of about 12-16 slender bristles, sometimes with a few outer setae; akenes sparsely hairy, 2-nerved. Rock crevices and ledges; central and southern Arizona.

description:
Planta fruticosa, parva. description: Trees, to 5 m; terminal branches thick, densely woolly-tomentose. Leaves with petioles ca. 5 cm long, tomentose, thick, rigid, blade oblong-elliptic or elliptic, 15-25 X 8- 12 cm, coriaceous, base rounded-truncate or obtuse, apex rounded, abaxial surface woolly-tomentose, adaxial surface slightly scabrous, reticulate veined with 7-10 secondary veins in each side of the midrib, margins unequal but entire, narrowly revolute. Capitulescences thyrsoid-paniculate. Capi- tula homogamous, discoid; involucre subcylindrical; phyllaries 5, weakly biseriate, subcoriaceous, outer phyllaries oblong, 6-8 X 2-2.2 mm, densely tomentose, apex acute, inner phyllaries oblong-elliptic, 6-8 X 2.5-4 mm, medially tomentose, apex obtuse, margins scarious. Florets 5, hermaphroditic, corolla 8-10 mm long, tube 3-4.5 mm long, limb 5-5.5 mm long, lobes linear, ca. 5 mm long, apex acute; anthers ca. 3.5 mm long, base sagittate, caudate, terminal appendage lanceolate, acute; style branches with the apex slightly acute, dorsally papillose-pilose. Achenes oblong, ca. 3.5 mm; pappus 8-10 mm long.

description: Trees, to 18 m. Leaves with petioles 1.5- 7 cm long, densely tomentose; blade oblanceolate, 11.5-53 X 3.5-23 cm, coriaceous, base subcordate or auriculate, apex acute, abaxial surface glabrous except the villose reticule, adaxial surface glabrescent, reticulate veined with 18-22 secondary veins on each side of the midrib, margins subrepand-dentate, teeth callous-triangular. Capitules-cences paniculate. Capitula homogamous, discoid; involucre turbinate; phyllaries 5, uniseriate, coriaceous, elliptic or oblanceolate, 6-7 X 2.5-3 mm, villose, apex acute. Florets 5, hermaphroditic, corolla 9-12 mm long, tube ca. 4.5 mm long, limb ca. 5.5 mm long, lobes oblong or subelliptic-oblong, ca. 4 mm long, apex acute; anthers ca. 2 mm long, base sagittate, caudate, terminal appendage lanceolate, acute; style branches with the apex ovate-deltoid, dorsally puberulent-papillose. Achenes turbinate, ca. 2 mm; pappus 5-7.5 mm long.

description: Shrubs, 1.5 m tall; stems branched, shortly strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades 28-28.5 X 20-21.5 cm, ovate, membraneous, apices acuminate, bases cordate, slightly truncate and decurrent; margins twice serrate; adaxial surface sparsely strigose, main veins conspicuous and shortly pubescent; abaxial surface light green, scarcely strigose, hairs 0.5-1 mm long, main veins thick, secondary veins 6- 7 each side, minor veins reticulated; petioles 8-10 cm long, shortly strigose, hairs 0.2 mm long. Capitulescences of tightly condensed clusters of capitula, 1.5-2.5 cm diam., with opposite, ovate leaves at base, blades 10.5 X 3.8 cm, branches to 10 cm long, densely pilose, hairs 1 mm long. Capitula radiate, subglobose, 6 mm high, 3-4 mm diam., sessile or shortly pedicellate; bracts narrowly ovate or linear, 10-35 mm long decreasing toward top; phyllaries 4, ovate, 6.5 X 3.5 mm, apices acute, abaxially strigose, hairs 1 mm long, margins ciliate on distal one-third, 4-5 veined. Pistillate fiorets 5, subtended by ovate paleae, 5.5-6 X 3.4-3.6 mm, 3-veined, margins with distal one-third ciliate; corollas 3.6 mm long, 1.6 mm diam., white, glabrous, 4-lobed, lobes deltoid, 1 mm long, margins shortly ciliate; styles 3 mm long, branches 1.6 mm long. Staminate fiorets 8, subtended by lanceolate paleae, 4.5 X 1.8-2.0 mm, 1-veined, apices obtuse, margins ciliate on distal one-third; corollas 5 mm long, white, 5-lobed, lobes 1.5 mm long, apices hirsute; ovaries pilose toward apex, hairs 1 mm long. Cypselae not seen. Chromosome num- ber unknown.

description: Biennial or short-lived perennial 4-10(2.5-12) dm tall, glabrous, or with minute tufts of hair in the axils of the leaves; stems arising singly or rarely 2 or more from an erect, short, fibrous-rooted caudex. Basal and lower cauline leaves spatulate to narrowly obovate in outline but deeply pinnate-lyrate; terminal lobe ovate to subcordate, contracted to a weakly winged or unwinged midrib; lateral lobes in 2-6(12) pairs; margins of lobes irregularly crenate-dentate or dentate to lacerate; overall leaf dimensions (2)3-5 cm wide and 10-25(8-35) cm long; petiole about half as long or equaling the blade. Upper cauline leaves similar to the basal ones but progressively smaller upwards, coarsely and irregularly incised to subpectinate, the uppermost reduced to sessile or clasping bracts. Inflorescence an open or sometimes congested corymbose cyme of 15-30(4-70) heads; principal involucral bracts about 13(21), (6)7-10 mm long; calyculate bracts few and inconspicuous, ray florets about 8(13), the ligule 10-15(20) mm long. Achenes glabrous, 4-5 mm long. n = 23 (Ornduff et al., 1963).

description: Stout perennial herb with deeply buried, horizontal underground stems giving rise to short, adscandent, above-ground leafy stems to 12 cm tall, densely clad in long, adpressed, sericeous pubescence. Leaves closely imbricate, rigid, spathulate to oblanceolate, obtuse-mucronate, 15-20 mm long, the elongate leaf-base 4-4.5 mm wide, gradually expanding into the blade 5-7.5 mm wide, above laxly clad in adpressed, sericeous hairs or glabrescent at the apex, beneath evenly and densely pubescent throughout; leaf-veins evident towards the base and distal part of the blade; blades 3-crenulate on both sides, margin of the crenulations continuous with the raised leaf veins, conspicuously thickened and slightly recurved, each crenulation terminating in an antrorse mucronate tooth. Capitula numerous, united in a dense terminal glomerule, the latter (8) 15-25 mm wide, (5) 12-15 mm long, hardly surpassing the surrounding leaves; involucre cylindrical; phyllaries 6-8, externally clad in weak, cobwebby pubescence, internally glabrous, the outermost linear, usually entire, 10.5-11 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, at apex acute and strongly mucronate, the innermost linear-lanceolate, 11-11.5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, 3-fid, the teeth strongly mucronate. Florets 3 per capitulum, white (?); corolla glabrous, bilabiate, 6.5-7.5 mm long, the tube 3-3.5 mm long, the internal lip 3/4 the length of the external one; anthers ca 2.5 mm long; style 4.5-5 mm long; stigma less than 1 mm long. Achenes cylindrical, 3.5-4 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, glabrous, pale brown; pappus a persistent, laciniate-dentate, lustrous, chaffy, white sheath, 2-2.5 mm high, transversally pleated at the base, incompletely surrounding summit of the achene.

description: Perennial emergent aquatic, erect, ca. 5-10 dm high; decumbent stems or rhizomes thick, hollow, with opposite scale leaves and rooting at the nodes; upright stems thick, hollow, striate, glabrate to sparsely pilose below, becoming densely pilose above; stem leaves opposite, sessile-clasping, inconspicuously dentate-serrate, lanceolate, with three principal parallel veins, up to 8.5 cm long and 1.7 cm wide, glabrate above, sparsely pilose below, especially on the veins; peduncles axillary, solitary, slender, pilose to densely pilose-strigose, ca. 7 cm long; heads campanulate, showy; phyllaries 15-22 in 1 or obscurely 2 series, ca. 6 mm high, linear-lanceolate, herbaceous, 3-4 nerved, the lower portion hirsute-pilose on and near the nerves, the upper portion glabrous except for a few appressed hairs on the margins, alae ca. 3-4 mm long, enveloping the ray achenes, margins erose; ray corollas white, ca. 12 mm long, 3 mm wide, the short tube ca. 0.2 mm long, apices minutely 2-lobed to entire; style branches of the ray short, lanceolate, flattened, glabrous, the apices obtuse; disk flowers numerous, the corollas yellow, ca. 3 mm long, basally constricted for ca. 0.8 mm, densely pilose on the constriction, glabrous above, style branches flattened, lanceolate, papillose-pubescent; achenes dark brown, minutely striate, shiny, oblanceolate, those of the ray mostly 3-angled, those of the disk 4-angled to terete; receptacle rounded-conical, ca. 4 mm long; paleae scarious, 3-nerved, broadly oblanceolate, glabrous, ca. 3.5 mm long, the upper portion lacerate-ciliate; 2n = 72.

description: Perennis, rhizomatifera; caule circa 1 m. alto, tereti, purpurascente, glabro ad inflorentiam, folioso; foliis lanceolatis vel inferioribus oblanceolatis, 5-10 cm. longis, serratis, acuminatis, superne glabratis, subtus adpresse brevi-pubeseentibus; marginibus hispido-ciliatis; inflorentia elongata, foliosa; ramis brevibus, patentibus, hispidulis; involuero circa 3 mm. alto; bracteis linearibus, acutis; ligulis circa 10; acheniis rariter hirsutis.

description: Plants perennial, 35-60 cm high, subdecumbent or erect, branching mostly from the base, hirsute; leaves 4-7.5 cm long, 2-9 mm wide, linear to linear-lanceolate, the margins entire, sessile to subpetiolate, hirsute on both surfaces; heads solitary on rather stout peduncles, campanulate, ca 1.5 cm in diameter; peduncles 6-15 cm long, bearing 1-3 minute, bract-like leaves, both puberulent and spreading hirsute, and with scattered glandular-capitate trichomes, especially near the heats; receptacle conical; chaff persistent, glabrous, 9-10 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, scarious, oblong, incised near the apex, with a purple-tipped, awn-like beak, ca 1/2 as long as the body, involucre 4-5-seriate; outer bracts linear-lanceolate, 3.5-6 mm long, 1.3-2 mm wide, obtuse, light green, purple toward the apex, margins ciliate, densely pubescent with short hairs and glandular trichomes; inner bracts progressively longer, the longest 8-9 mm long, 2.4-3 mm wide, light green, oblong, rounded to obtuse at the purplish apex, becoming membranous inward, densely pubescent except at the scarious, ciliate margins; ray flowers 6-8, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 6-6.5 mm, with conspicuous pinkish-lavender ligules, 7.5-12 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, oblong-obovate, obscurely three-lobed at the apex, the inner lobelets of the ray corolla vestigial; staminodia of ray florets composed of 2-5 linear appendages arising from the apex of the tube; ray pappus slightly shorter than that of the discs; disc corollas greenish-yellow, 7-7.5 mm long, the tube finely pubescent above, ca 2.5 mm long, throat tubular to narrowly funnelform, finely pubescent at the base, 3.8-4 mm long, lobes acute-obtuse, subinvolute at the apex, ca 1 mm long; style branches 2.8-3 mm long, recurved, dark brown, flattened, narrowly oblanceolate, with a subulate tip, densely and minutely pubescent; achenes black, narrowly turbinate, compressed, densely pilose with fine, light brown hairs (the hairs ca 0.6 mm long), 3-3.5 mm long; pappus or 20 subequal, light brownish, slender, plumose bristles, ca 3.5-4 mm long; anthers nigrescent, 3.8-4 mm long, sagittate at the base.

description: Frutices ramosi ca 3 m usque alti. Folia altema; petioli 4-15 mm longi; laminae ellipticae vel lanceolato-ellipticae (5) 8-1 2 (1 6.5) cm longae, (1. 5) 2-3 (6) cm latae, margine integrae. Capitulescentiae terminales et axillares corymboso-paniculatae. Capitula radiata, 8-10 mm alta, 6-8 mm lata; phyllaria 16-18, 2-seriata, extima 3-5 mm longa, ca 1 mm lata, intima 5-6 mm longa, ca 1.5 mm lata. Flores radiati 5; ligulae luteae, 7-15 mm longae, 3-5 mm latae. Flores disci 9-24; corollae tubulosae luteae, 4.5-5 mm longae. Achaenia 4-6 mm longa, sericea.

description: Shrubs to 3 m tall; trunks to 10 cm diam, bark peeling; branchlets striate, puberulent, resinous. Leaves alternate; petioles 4-15 mm long; blade elliptic to lance-elliptic, (5) 8-12 (16.5) cm long, (1.5) 2-3 (6) cm wide, penninerved, the lower surface finely prominulous-reticulate, glandular, resinous, the upper surface sparsely strigillose, glandular, resinous, basally broadly attenuate, apically acute to attenuate, the margins entire, strigillose. Capitulescences cymose-paniculate, 13-20-headed, the peduncles 1-3.5 cm long, bracteolate. Capitula radiate, 8-10 mm high, 6-8 mm wide (excluding ray florets); involucre campanulate; phyllaries 16-18, graduated, 2-seriate, puberulent, glandular with multicellular capitate trichomes, resinous, the outer linear-lanceolate, 3-5 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, acute, the inner lanceolate to lance-ovate, 5-6 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, acute to attenuate, striate, ciliolate; receptacle convex; paleae 6-8 mm long, apically rounded to cucullate, glandular, resinous; ray florets 5, the ligules oblong, 7-15 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, apically cleft, the tube 3-5 mm long, villous basally; disc florets 9-24, 4.5-5 mm long, cylindric-campanulate, 5-lobed, the tube 0.7-1.0 mm long, the lobes 0.6-0.8 mm long, the anthers ca 2.5 mm long, basally sagittate, the terminal appendage ovate, the style branches lanceolate, densely papillose. Achenes obconical, 4-6 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, densely villous; pappus of 2 awns, 2-3 mm long, readily disarticulating, squamellae absent. Chromosome number: n = 18.

description: Cormo 1-3 cm. crasso; caule 3-6 dm. alto, suleato plus minus hir- suto; foliis numerosis, plus minus hirsutis, vel glabreseentibus, 5-10 cm. longis, 3-6 mm. latis; spica laxa, 3-10 cm. longa; capitulis 3-10, subsessilibus, 1.5-2 cm. longis, 9-10 mm. latis; bracteis squarrosissimis vel etiam reflexis, valde hirsuto-ciliatis, exterioribus ovatis, breviter acuniinatis, interioribus ellipticis, obtusis vel inucronatis; corollis 1 cmii. longis, rubro-purpureis; acheniis 6 mm. longis, hirsutulis; pappo plunioso, cervino.

description: Plants annual, biennial or perennial; caespitose, subcaespitose, or with erect, leafy stems; basal leaves in a rosette, alternate, spatulate to oblanceolate, the margins entire to sinuate, dentate or dentately lobed; upper leaves much reduced, entire; indumentum consisting of glandular and nonglandular trichomes; inflorescence paniculate, racemose, cymose, or solitary; involucres hemispheric to cylindric, the involucral bracts arranged in several graduated, indistinct series, receptable flat, without conspicuous relief; ray flowers pistillate, fertile, 10-60, the ligule yellow, red-orange, or red; disk flowers perfect, fertile, the corolla yellow to red-orange; anther appendages deltoid; stigmatic branches short, obtuse, with papillose epidermal cells on the outer subapical surface; base chromosome number, x = 19

description: Herbae annuae, 10-30 cm altae. Caules ascendentes vel erecti, hirtelli, pilis 0.5 mm longis. Pedunculi 1.5-3.6 cm longi. Folia sessilia, linearia et integra vel profunde pinnatim divisa, 3-4.5 cm longa, 0.2-3.7 cm lata, apice acuta, basi attenuata vel obtusa, supra subtiliter strigosa, pilis 1 mm longis, subtus sericea, marginibus ir- regulariter ciliatis pilis 0.3 mm longis (basalibus longioribus). Capitula 5-6 mm alta, 8-11 mm diametro. Involucrum extimum cupulatum, 7-10 mm diametro; bracteae 5, obovato-rhombeae, basi leviter connatae, 4.5-5.5 mm longae, 3-3.5 mm latae, apice acuto-acuminatae, extus pilosae, pilis 1 mm longis, marginibus opacis, ciliatis, pilis 0.8 mm longis. Chrom- somatum numerus ignotus.

description: Perennial herb from a rhizome or short stout caudex; stem 0.5-7 din. high, glabrous to moderately villous below, usually rather densely villous under the heads (spreading-hirsute in var. hirsutus), amply leafy in larger forms, sub-scapose in smaller ones; basal and lowermost cauline leaves linear-oblanceolate to broadly oblanceolate or spatulate, tapering to the petiole, of various sizes and proportions up to 20 em. long and 4.5 cm. wide; middle and upper cauline leaves linear to broadly ovate, sometimes subelasping, ample, or greatly reduced, of various, dimensions up to 8 cm. long and 3 cm. wide; leaves glabrous, often long-ciliate on the margins, or sometimes sparsely villous on the main veins or even over the surfaces, or in one variety hirsute; heads mostly solitary, sometimes as  many as 8, the disk 10-25 mm. wide; involuere mostly 7.5-11 mm. high, sometimes  smaller in var. hirsututs and var. angustifolius; phyllaries linear, attenuate, loose,  mostly rather herbaceous and about equal, sometimes slightly imbricate, miostly  0.9-1.3 mm. wide (often narrower in var. angustifotius), glandular or more or  less villous with viscid-appearing hairs, sometimes ciliate on the margins and  merely glutinous on the back; ligules about 30-80, 8-25 mm. long and 2-4 mm.  wide, rose-purple or darker, sometimes very pale or even white; disk-corollas  about 4-6 mm. long, sometimes narrowed near the base, but with no well-marked  tube, the lobes about 0.7-1.0 mm. long; style-appendages deltoid or triangular-ovate, acute, 0.2-0.4 mm. long; pappus of about 20-30 bristles, sometimes with a  few outer setae up to 0.4 mm. long; akenes sparsel-y hairy, asymmetrically 4-7-nerved, most commonly 5-nerved, with one nerve on each of the two blunt angles,  one on one face, and two on the other.

description: Herba decumbens caespitosa, ramulis glabris superne cum vaginis foliorum tectis. Folia alterna in apice ramorum valde densis, 10-20 mm longa ciliato-spinulosa lamina digitato-trilobata cuneata in pseudopetiolum longum angustata, basi late vaginata amplectentia; lobis linearibus planis triangulari-acutis spinulosis exteriorbus bifidis, 3-5 mm longis 1-2 mm latis. Folia suprema 3-4 linearia indivisa spinuloso-ciliata, ad modum calyculi. Capitula discoidea heterogama. Involucrum 12-14 mm altum circiter 12 bracteis basi coalitis lineari-oblongis apice breviter ciliatis ceteris glabris. Flores-radii feminei corolla ad tubum brevem 2.5-3 mm longum laceratum reducta, stylo columnari erecto 8 mm longo apice in 2 ramos crassiusculos atratos apice truncatos papilloso-coronatos producto. Flores disci hermaphroditi corolla lutea 10 mm longa glabra tubulo 2.5 mm longo dentibus 1 mm longis; antheris 3.5 mm longis, ramis styli apice truncatis. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus setosus albus 8 mm longus.

description: Perennial herbs 0.6-1 m tall; stems terete, puberulent, purplish green. Leaves opposite, triplinerved; blades 2.5-7.5 cm long, 1.5-5 cm wide, smaller distally, ovate to deltate in outline, 2-3 X pinnatisect into broad to narrowly linear segments, primary segments 5-7, lowermost primary segments mostly 3X pinnatisect with blade of secondary segments narrowed into the rachis at insertion to main rachis, distalmost segments 2X pinnatisect, the segments ovate in outline, acute to acuminate, not conspicuously mucronate, often lobed, adaxial sur- face sparsely pubescent, the trichomes erect with broad multicellular bases, those along veins appressed, bright green, abaxial surface sparsely pubescent with trichomes slightly larger than those of adaxial surface otherwise similar in morphology and distribution, creamy green, margins rimmed with appressed trichomes; petioles 0.7-1.8 mm long. Capitulescence of 3-18 heads, dichasial, arranged in a paniculiform-cyme; peduncles 8-20 cm long, moderately puberulent, purplish green. Heads heterogamous, radiate, campanulate, 1.2-1.5 cm high, 1.5- 2 cm wide (excluding ligules). Phyllaries 15-21 in 2-3 dimorphic and slightly graduated series; phyllaries of first series 5-9 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, spreading, herbaceous, lanceolate, glabrous, green with blackish lines running lengthwise; phyllaries of second and third series 8-1 1 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, spreading, chartaceous, ovate to oval, glabrescent, central area dark purple to black, edges stramineous; the outermost phyllaries slightly larger and densely puberulent at tips, with sparsely distributed glandular trichomes, these more abundant on adaxial surface. Pales 8 mm long, 2 mm wide, similar in morphology and color to innermost phyllaries, lanceolate, with scattered glandular trichomes on adaxial surface, apices rimmed with multicellular non-glandular trichomes. Ray flowers 7-10, sterile, strongly reflexed, the corollas blackish purple or wine color, rarely magenta purple; ligule 1.2-1.6 cm long, 7-9 mm wide, oval to oblong, adaxial surface gla- brous, abaxial surface with multicellular trichomes along veins, scattered glandular trichomes between veins, apex trifid; tube 0.8-1 mm long, opening of tube into ligule reduced by a protuberance on adaxial surface of the ligule. Ray ovary 1.5 mm long, ovate to oval, flat to biconvex, glabrous, epappose. Disk flowers 18-32, perfect, protruding 3-4 mm beyond pales, the corollas tubular to narrowly campanulate, yellow to yellow-green; throat 6-7 mm long, 1-1.2 mm wide, slightly wider at top, essentially glabrous; tube 2 mm long, distal 2/3 of tube densely puberulent, greenish yellow; lobes 0.6-0.7 mm long, broadly deltate, glabrous; anthers 2-2.4 mm long, black, the appendages 0.5 mm long, ovate, yellow; styles 5 mm long, yellow basal 1/2 densely papillose; style branches 1.5 mm long, acute with appendage, yellow and basal 2/3 Of adaxial surface purple. Disk cypsela 1-1.3 cm long, 1- 2 mm wide; awns 2, retrorsely barbed, 3 mm long.

description: Herba annua, glabrata, erecta, tenuis, 3-5 dm alta; caule subsimplici erecte pauciramoso, caule ramisque costatis sulculatisque. Folia alternata, basalia elongate petiolata petiolo tenerrimo +1.5 dm longo, lamina irregulariter pinnatimque 2-5-foliolata, foliolis anguste linearibus vel (praecipue terminali) anguste oblanceolatis apice acuminato, integris, usque ad 6 cm longis et ad 6 mm latis; mediana superioraque similia vel interdum integra, petiolo saepius sub 4 cm longo. Capitula radiata pansa ad anthesin 2-3.5 cm lata, demum 7-10 mm alta. Involueri bracteae exteriores 5-7 (rarius 8), lanceolatae, 3-5 mm longae; interiores ovatae, duplo longiores. Flores ligulati 7 vel 8, aurei, ligula obovato-oblonga et plus minusve pedatim conspicueque lobulata, lobulo mediano latiore apice forsitan inciso 1.5-2 cm longo. Flores tubulosi flavo-straminei, stylorum ramis apice truncatis vel obtusissime brevi-conicis. Paleae anguste lineares, circa 5-6 mm longae. Achaenia corpore plana, subnitido-nigra, eirea 2.5-3 mm longa et 1.2-1.5 mm lata, anguste oblongo-obovata faciebus minutissime tuberculata aliter glabra, margine anguste hyalino-alata alis integris vel subintegris, sub 0.3 mm latis, apice exaristata vel plerumque minute denticulata.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1959. Notes on Coreopsidinae from Mexico and the United States. Brittonia. 11: 188-190.

description: Annual herb, glabrate, erect, slender, 3-5 dm tall; stem erectly few-branched, the branches like the stem ribbed and minutely grooved. Leaves alternate, the basal ones elongately petiolate with a very slender petiole (this +1.5 dm long), the blade irregularly and pinnately 2- to 5-foliolate (leaflets narrowly linear orespecially the terminal one-narrowly oblanceolate with an acuminate tip, entire, up to 6 cm long and 6 mm wide); median and upper ones similar but at times entire, the petiole more often under 4 cm long. Heads radiate, at anthesis 2-3.5 cm. wide including the rays, finally 7-10 mm tall. Outer phyllaries 5-7 (more rarely 8), lanceolate, 3-5 mm long; inner ones ovate, twice as long. Ligulate florets 7 or 8, golden-yellow, 1.5-2 cm long; ligule obovate-oblong and more or less pedately and conspicuously lobulate, the median lobe broader and perhaps apically incised. Tubular florets yellow-stramineous; style-branches apically truncate or very obtusely short-conic. Chaff-scales narrowly linear, about 5-6 mm long. Achenes with a flat body (this subglossy-black, about 2.5-3 mm long and 1.2-1.5 mm wide, narrowly oblong-obovate, on the faces very minutely tuberculate but otherwise glabrous), at the margins narrowly hyaline-winged (wings entire or subentire, under 0.3 mm wide), at apex awnless or commonly minutely denticulate.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1959. Notes on Coreopsidinae from Mexico and the United States. Brittonia. 11: 188-190.

description: Stem stout, simple to the infloreseence, 1-4 m high from fusiform, somewhat fleshy rhizomes, commonly scabrous, or with scattered hairs, dark red or purple; leaves characteristically lanceolate-ovate, mostly 8-20 cm long, 1.4-6 cm wide, variable, alternate, sessile or with short petioles 0.6-1.5 cm long; petioles with ciliate bases; upper surface of the blades with many short hairs, the hairs of the lower surfaces more abundant, occasionally longer, spreading; margins mostly serrate, but varying from subentire to coarsely toothed; phyllaries lanceolate, acumiinate, 1-2.2 cm long, with conspicuous long white cilia along the margins, the surfaces usually short-pubescent; heads 4-6 cm wide, in terminal racemose or paniculate infloreseences; peduncles variable in length, scabrous; disk florets 1-1.4 cm long, the corolla puberulent at base; ligules 12-20, mostly 1.5-3.6 cm long, pale yellow; chaff linear, acuminate, obscurely three-cuspidate, pubescent at tips.
bibliographicCitation: Long, Robert W. 1961. Biosystematics of two perennial species of Helianthus (Compositae), II. Natural populations and taxonomy. Brittonia. 13: 129-141.

description: Erect, slender annual herbs up to 4.1 dm tall; stems striate, strigose, yellow-brown to purplish; leaves narrowly lanceolate, up to 3.5 cm long and 6 mm wide, scabrous below, hispid-strigose above; peduncles 1 cm long or less, densely hispid above; heads hemispheric, ca 8 mm in diameter; phyllaries obovate, purplish-brown, essentially glabrous, the ininer ones squarrose and membranaceous at the apex, with a dark summit band; rays ea 9, orbicular, yellow, 2-5 mm lolng, the tube very short and lightly ciliate; ray achenes broadly obovate, prominently 3-angled, 3.1 mm long, serrate-crustose on all the angles, becoming tuberculate the pappus of 2 horns; disk corollas 2.9 mm long, yellow below, dark purple at the limb outside, purple inside the lobes with yellow marginal hairs; disk achenes obovate, black, smooth, 2.9 mm long, deeply emarginate, the margins crenate-crustose, the pappus none; chaff yellow below, becoming gradually dark purple, at the tips, ciliated along the keel and lightly glandular; the apices acute, often reflexed, entire; receptable conical.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1963. Taxonomy of Zinnia. Brittonia. 15: 1-25.

description: Herba, caudice ut videtur subterraneo; foliis coriaceis linearibus, 30-70 cm. longis, circiter 1.5 cm. latis, basin versus angustatis, apice obtusis, margine integris et leviter incrassatis, utrinque dense canes-cente- vel argenteo-tomentosis, costa crassa, nervis secundariis rectis patulis 20-30 per decimetrum saepe obscuratis; ramis florif eris crassis 8-12-capitulatis, e caudice erectis, folia aequantibus vel transcendenti-bus, ubique argenteo-tomentosis; capitulis maturitate circiter 2 cm. diametro racemosis, pedunculis gracilibus 4—9 cm. longis, bracteis linearibus 4r-7 cm. longis et 3—5 mm. latis subtentis; involucro circiter 3-seriato, phyllaribus circiter 60 oblongis vel oblongo-lanceolatis, ex-terioribus 10-11 mm. longis, circiter 4 mm. latis, apice acutis, extra dense tomentosis (pilis pallidis 2-3 mm. longis); floribus radii circiter 3-seriatis, lamina ad tubum brevem 2-2.5 mm. longum reducta, in-trorse aperta, margine crenulata, basi parce pilosa, stylo 3-3.5 mm. longo apicem versus bifido, achenio stramineo trigono circiter 1.5 mm. longo; floribus disci glabris vel apice hispidulis circiter 4.5 mm. longis, tubo quam limbo breviore, lobis deltoideo-ovatis circiter 0.5 mm. longis; staminibus maturitate exsertis, filamentis antheras subaequan-tibus; stylo exserto; paleis stramineis membranaceis oblongis vel oblongo-obovatis, circiter 5 mm. longis et 1.5 mm. latis, apice acutis, extra apicem versus hispidis, pilis pallidis circiter 1.5 mm. longis.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Koch, M. A. 1935. The genus Espeletia: a study in phylogenetic taxonomy. Brittonia. 1: 479-530. pl. 1, 2 + f. 1-5.

description: Unarmed shrubs 1-6 (-8) dm high; much branched. Stems pannose but for floccose to glabrescent streaks on the internodes subtending the primary leaves or older stems glabrescent and reddish brown. Primary leaves narrowly lanceolate, oblanceolate, or spatulate; mostly 1-3 (0.5-4.0) cm long, 2-4 (1-6) mm wide; sparsely tomentose to sericeous. Secondary leaves similar to the primaries but usually shorter and narrower. Capitula borne in compact or loose corymbose clusters of 3-6 (-8) at tips of branches. Peduncles 5-15 (-25) mm long; tomentose; ebracteate. Involucres turbinate to cylindric; 6-8 (-12) mm high. Phyllaries 4, subequal; oblong to ovate or lanceolate; acute to obtuse; often navicular; tomentose. Florets 4 per capitulum. Corollas bright yellow to cream; 9-11 (7-15) mm long; throat funnelform, short; lobes lance-linear, 2.5-5.0 mm long. Achenes 3-4 (2.5-5.0) mm long; glabrous or hirsute. Pappus of ca. 100-150 white to tawny bristles; 8-9 (6-11) mm long; often with some of the bristles penicillate; all free to the base or all united 0.5-1.0 mm from the base. Style branches 1.8-2.3 mm long; tips rounded, papillate. Anthers 3-6 mm long; deeply sagittate; apically lanceolate-acute. Pollen grains mostly 37-45 ,um in diameter. Figs. 2,A; 3,A.
bibliographicCitation: Strother, John L. 1974. Taxonomy of Tetradymia (Compositae: Senecioneae). Brittonia. 26: 177-202.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and stout much-branched caudex, the bark of the root light-colored, thin, and often peeling in layers; stem erect or nearly so, 5-35 cm. high, moderately grayish-strigose; leaves grayish-strigose, the basal ones tufted, linear or narrowly oblanceolate, up to about 7 cm. long and 5 mm. wide, usually smaller, the cauline ones reduced, linear, or the lower linear-oblanceolate, several or rather many; heads solitary, the disk 10-20 mm. broad; involuere about 6-9 mm. high, moderately hirsute-villous with crinkled somewhat flattened multicellular hairs, and obscurely viscid; phyllaries more or less strongly imbricate, somewhat yellowish-chartaceous at the base, the outer otherwise greenish, often with brown midrib, sometimes flanked by greenish strips, and straw-colored borders, all acuminate or acuminate-attenuate, the inner more strongly so; ligules about 25-60, pink, white, or sometimes violet-bluish, 8-15 mm. long, 2.0-3.7 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.0-5.7 mm. long, not especially narrow, the tube 0.7-1.4 mm. long, the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm. long, style-appendages 0.2-0.25 mm. long, a little narrower than deltoid, acute; pappus of about 30-50 rather coarse sordid bristles, sometimes with an outer series of relatively long bristles, or sometimes these latter appearing as part of the main series, though mostly less than half as long as the principal bristles; akenes densely pilose, 2-5-nerved (most commonly 4), often irregularly so.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Trees, 3-4 m. Leaves with petioles 6-13 cm long, densely tomentose; blade ovate or elliptic-ovate, 34 X 16-18 cm, coriaceous, base broadly rounded, oblique or cuneate, apex subacute, lower surface densely tomentose, upper surface glabrous, except for the tomentulose midrib, reticulate veined, 12-13 secondary veins on each side of the midrib, margins revolute, entire or rarely with minute callous teeth. Capitulescences subthyrsoid-paniculate. Capitula homogamous, discoid; involucre cylindrical, phyllaries 8, weakly biseriate, subcoriaceous, outer phyllaries oblong, 7.5 X 2.5 mm, densely woolly-tomentose, apex subacute, inner phyllaries elliptic, 7-7.3 X 3 mm, medially tomentose, margins scarious. Florets 10-11(-12), hermaphroditic, corolla 8.5-9 mm long, tube 3.5-4 mm long, limb 4,5-5 mm long, lobes linear, 3.5-4 mm long, fused ca. 1 mm at the base, apex subacute; anthers ca. 2.5 mm long, base sagittate, caudate, terminal appendage oblong, slightly obtuse; style branches with the apex sub-acute, dorsally papillose-pilose. Achenes oblong, 2.5-2.8 mm; pappus 7-8 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Correa, A. 2003. Revision of the genus Paragynoxys (Asteraceae, Senecioneae-Tussilagininae). Brittonia. 55: 157-168.

description: Trees, 6-12 m. Leaves with petioles ca. 20 cm long, slightly verruculose, densely tomentose; blade subovate-elliptic, 50-70 X 28-40 cm, base deeply cordate, apex attenuate, obtuse, lower surface densely woolly-tomentose, upper surface glabrate except for the densely woolly-tomentose midrib, reticulate veined, 14-15 secondary veins on each side of the midrib, the margins entire but slightly and irregularly undulate. Capitulescences thyrsoid-paniculate. Capitula homogamous, discoid; involucre cylindrical, phyllaries 5, weakly biseriate, papery, outer phyllaries oblong, 8.5 X ca. 2 mm, glabrous, apex subacute, ciliate, inner phyllaries elliptic, 8 X 3-3.5 mm, gla- brous, apex obtuse, margins scarious, erose-ciliate. Florets 5, hermaphroditic, corolla ca. 11 mm long, tube 5.5-6 mm long, limb ca. 5.5 mm long, lobes linear, ca. 5 mm long, apex acute; anthers ca. 3 mm long, base slightly sagittate, auriculate, terminal appendage lanceolate, acute; style branches with the apex acute, dorsally penicillate. Achenes subtriangular, ca. 3 mm long; pappus ca. 8 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Correa, A. 2003. Revision of the genus Paragynoxys (Asteraceae, Senecioneae-Tussilagininae). Brittonia. 55: 157-168.

description: Plants annual, procumbent, ca 1.2 dm tall, much branched from the base; stems brownish, hirsute; leaves entire, strigose, petioes up to 16 mm long, blades broadly lanceolate to broadly ovate, up to 5 cm long and 2.5 cm wide; peduncles 3 mm long or less, hirsute; heads hemispherical, up to 10 mm wide; phyllaries 20 or fewer, imbricate, graduated, coriaceous, often foliaceous, villous, ovate to obovate, apices rounded or mucronate; rays ca 12, up to 9 mm long, yellow to orange, glabrous, chartaceous, broadly elliptic to ovate, apices 2-3 lobed; ray style bifid, glabrous; ray achenes obtriangular, 3-angled, muricate, glabrous, ca 4 mm long with 3 divergent awns, awns ca 2 mm long, slender. mostly purple or purple tipped; disk corollas numerous, ca 3 mm long, yellow or purple on the limb, tube colorless, often with bright red-tipped trichomes at the base; sterile anther apices broadly lanceolate and conspicuously concave, filaments dilated above, style bifid, branches flattened inwardly, apices acute, base conspicuously dilated; peripheral disk achenes compressed to 4-angled, tuberculate, tubercles glabrous or ciliate, obtriangular, ca 3 mm long, winged or wingless with 1-2 very slender awns, central achenes smooth to sparsely tuberculate, 0-2 awned, margined to 1-2 winged, wings ciliate; paleae exceeding the disk flowers, cuspidate, yellow or purple, pubescenit along the keel; receptacle conical; n = 8.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1964. Revision of Sanvitalia (Compositae-Heliantheae). Brittonia. 16: 417-433.

description: Aromatic trees or shurbs to 12 m tall; leaves lanceolate to ovate, acuminate, glutinous, coriaceous, to 25 cm long and 11 cm wide, entire or denticulate, with a sessile leaf or winged petiole, the base of widest portion of blade attenuate, the leaf bases sometimes auriculate but not connate; margins, at least when dried, revolute; leaves densely tomentose below, shining glabrous above; peduncles and lower surface of phyllaries densely stipitate-glandular, the glands sometimes accompanied by hairs; phyllaries 4-5 in 1 series, ovate-lanceolate, ca 1 cm long and to 7 mm wide; ray flowers ca 12, the corollas yellow, to 9 mm long and 4 mm wide; disc flowers ca 4 mm long, the corollas yellow; ray paleae ovate, ca 5 mm long and 2 mm wide, minutely glandular below; disc paleae denticulate along upper margin the midvein prominent; achene obovoid, black, to 4 mm long and ca 2 mm broad.
bibliographicCitation: Wells, James R. 1965. A taxonomic study of Polymnia (Compositae). Brittonia. 17: 144-159.

description: Plants up to 1.6 dm high; stem greenish, slender, tomentose; leaves acerose to linear, 1-nerved, up to 2 cm long and 2 mm wide, strigose to essentially gla- brous; peduncles up to 2.5 cm long; heads narrowly campanulate, ea 6 mm high; phyllaries oblong, herbaceous, becoming scarious, their apices obtuse, ciliate, with a dark summit band or the summit only roughened and discolored; rays 4-6, white, oblong to suborbicular, 10 mm long or less, tubeless, green-nerved beneath; ray achenes oblanceolate, 3-angled, truncate at apex, 2.6-4 mm long, the awns striate, ciliate above, fused to and continuous with the main corolla nerves, or the 3 awns free, or a single free short awn on the inner angle; disk flowers 8-13, yellow (drying reddish), 6 mm long with lobes 1 mm long; disk achenes oblanceolate, compressed, 2.4-3.6 mm long, striate, strigose or only upwardly ciliate, the pappus usually of 2-3 unequal awns or these much reduced; chaff obtuse and erose at apex, uniformly yellow; receptacle convex.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Fragrant, erect, perennial herbs 2-5 (6) dm tall, generously provided with sessile glands, otherwise glabrous; stems many, with or without several strict branches, arising from an extensive woody branched caudex, often surmounting a taproot, remains of old stems present; leaves cauline, alternate, sometimes fascicled, the lower reduced, quickly withering or brown and scalelike, the upper bright green and bipinnatifid, 1.5-5 cm long, 1-2.5 cm wide, the 5-7 (9) primary segments 0.4-1.5 cm long, linear, widely spreading, narrowed at the base and joined along the rachis by decurrent leaf tissue, at least some of the secondary segments toothed, the apices acute and indurate, the margins slightly revolute, the petiole indistinct or lacking, the veins decurrent on the stem, the leaves in the inflorescence reduced, pinnatifid to entire; inflorescences narrowly paniculiform or occasionally racemiform, 5-20 cm long, 1.5-4 cm wide, the lower branches arising from the axils of the uppermost leaves; peduncles lacking or up to 1 mm long, subtended by a single linear-lanceolate bract 1-2 mm long; involucres cam- panulate to hemispherical, 2.5-3.5 mm long, 2-4.5 mm wide (pressed), subtended by 2-4 lanceolate bracts 1-1.5 mm long; receptacle flat to hemispherical, naked; phyllaries 9-11, broadly ovate, 1-3 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, obtuse to rounded, keeled, sometimes saccate, glandular at least at the base, the margins broadly scarious and erose; flowers (15) 20-35, perfect except for the 3-8 pistillate ones, all fertile or the central ones aborted, bright yellow, glandular externally, the tube 0.3-0.8 mm long, the limb 1-1.5 mm long; stamens 1.5 mm long, the filaments 0.5 mm long, the anthers 0.8-1 mm long, acute, bright yellow; style branches papillate and truncate in the perfect flowers, smooth and rounded in the pistillate flowers; achenes light brown, ellipsoid, ± arcuate, 1 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, epappose, the pericarp translucent, resinous, quickly swelling when moistened, with 4 prominent ribs at the base reduced to nerves near the minute crown.
bibliographicCitation: Grimes, James & Ertter, Barbara J. 1979. A new species of Artemisia [A. paclcardiae] (Asteraceae: Anthemidae) from southeastern Oregon. Brittonia. 31: 454-458.

description: Perennial reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes. Stems erect, 15 or fewer per plant, tomentose or canescent, simple to the inflorescence, 2-6 dm high. Leaves cauline, numerous and crowded, 4-8 cm long, 1-4 mm wide, narrowly linear, narrowed to a sessile base, essentially glabrous above but deeply pitted, with numerous bilobed and few "longhorn" glandular trichomes, tomentose below with dense bilobed, long- horn, and awl-shaped glandular trichomes, extremely revolute, the tips acute, the margins entire. Inflorescence compact with few to many heads. Heads 12-29- flowered. Involucre narrowly campanulate, 6-10 mm high, 5-8 mm wide; phyllaries appressed, densely tomentose, greenish with purple margins; inner phyllaries linear to oblong, 5-9 mm long, 1-1.7 mm wide, with mucronate to mucronulate tips; outer phyllaries ovate-lanceolate with acuminate tips. Achenes deeply ribbed, densely glandular, purple to tawny, ca. 4 mm long. Pappus purple or purple-based with tawny tips, the bristles ca. 7 mm long, the scales white, irregular, 0.5-1 mm long. Flowering from early June to August.
bibliographicCitation: King, Bruce L. & Jones, S. B. 1975. The Vernonia lindheimeri complex (Compositae). Brittonia. 27: 74-86.

description: Frutex scandens, partibus junioribus plus minusve breviter sordide brunneo-pubeseentibus, ramis teretibus, glabris, ramulis breviter dense pubeseentibus, eirciter 2 mm. diametro; foliis oblongo-ellipticis, integris, 5-7 cm. longis, 2-3 cm. latis, subcoriaceis vel firmiter chartaceis, basi rotundatis, apice brevissime late obtuseque acuminatis vel obtusis, utrinque, costa excepta, glabris, supra subolivaceis nitidis, minute puncticulato-glandulosis, subtus subeoncoloribus et distincte punctato-glandulosis, nervis primariis utrinque eirciter 8, subtus distinctis, elevatis, arcuato-anastomosantibus, reticulis sublaxis, gracilibus, elevatis, haud vermicularibus; petiolo breviter pubeseenti, 5-7 mm. longo; infloreseentiis terminalibus, paniculatis ad 15 cm. longis, foliaceis, ramis primariis paucis, subpatulis, inferioribus ad 8 cm. longis, superioribus brevioribus, capitulis subcorymbosis; capitulis eirciter 1 cm. longis, pedunculis bracteisque extus dense breviter brunneopubeseentibus, pedunculo 5-9 mm. longo, bracteis linearibus, pubeseentibus, eirciter 1 mm. longis; involueri bracteis inferioribus ovatis, acutis vel obtusis, 1.5 mm. longioribus, interioribus gradatim longioribus, internis oblongis vel oblongo-lanceolatis, eirciter 4 mm. longis et 1.8-2 mm. latis, omnibus extus pubeseentibus, intus glabris; floribus eirciter 10, corolla 9 mm. longa, tubo gracili, glabro, lobis lineari-oblongis vel lanceolatis, 2 mm. longis, glabris; acheniis subteretibus, obscurissime costatis, glabris, eirciter 2.5 mm. longis, setis numerosis, albidis, 8 mm. longis, exterioribus brevioribus.
bibliographicCitation: Merrill, Elmer D. 1941. Plants Collected on the Vernay-Cutting Expedition. Brittonia. 4 (1): 23-68.

description: Tall, slender tree-like shrubs ca 1.7-3 m tall; stems pachycladous, loosely branched, with golden-brown, densely tufted trichomes becoming dark with age. Leaves cauline and crowded, but deciduous from older stems; the sessile blades 5.2-9.5 (11) x 0.4-1.4 cm, oblanceolate, sometimes linear or lanceolate, widest above or sometimes below the middle, apically acute to obtuse or rounded, apic- ulate, basally truncate to rounded and encircled by villous pubescence, marginally entire and revolute, rugulose and often thinly pilose, especially on basal portion of midvein above, grey-felted below, except on prominent midvein which is en- larged basally. Inflorescences terminating lateral branches, composed of semi-spherical glomerules subtended by bracts. Heads 4-12-flowered. Phyllaries linear, straw-colored, glossy, 6-10 (18) x 1.5-2 mm, tips dark. description: The differences between the above taxa are so striking that it is tempting to treat them as species. The tall leafy-stemmed var. potentilloides with numerous heads could be treated as a species distinct from the var. nitrophila. Large specimens of var. nitrophila are readily separated from small var. potentilloides as the basal leaves of the former are nearly always merely pinnatifid instead of twice pinnatifid. The taxa are never sympatric so far as we know. Var. potentilloides is found from Lake County east to Harney County in Oregon, then south to Washoe County, Nevada and west to Plumas, Sierra, Lassen, and Mono counties in California; var. nitrophila occurs from Elmore County, Idaho south to Elko and Nye counties in Nevada. The two varieties are also ecologically distinct as the var. nitrophizla grows in strongly alkaline soils while var. potentilloides is found in meadow soils weakly alkaline at the most. In spite of these marked differences we are leaving the varieties without elevating them to specific rank, because they are so closely related.

description: Perennial herb with a short caudex and fibrous roots; stem generally curved or decumbent at the base, then erect, 3-35 cm. high, sparsely to densely spreading-villous with crinkled hairs; leaves loosely villous when young, the basal and sometimes also the cauline ones generally glabrate by flowering time; basal leaves oblanceolate or occasionally spatulate, up to about 9 cm. long and 8 mm. wide; cauline leaves generally several, reduced, lax, commoiily linear-lanceolate and acuminate or acuminate-attenuate, or rarely the stem subscapose;, heads solitary or rarely several, the disk 15-30 mm. wide; involuere 8-11 mm. high, more or less densely woolly-villous with long slender hairs, appearing somewhat tousled; crosswalls of the hairs clear, or sometimes tinted with bright reddish purple; phyllaries nearly always a rich reddish purple, about equal, lax, relatively broad, the outer 1 mm. w'ide or more, the tips generally loose and acuminate-attenuate; ligules about 100-200, deep pink or purplish to sometimes white, 3-6 mm. long, 0.3-0.55 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 3.8-5.0 mm. long, the tube 1.5-2.2 mm.; the lobes 0.5-0.6 mm.; style-appendages narrowly to broadly triangular, 0.1-0.15 mm. long; pappus of about 20-30 bristles, surpassing the disk-corollas, and with a few obscure outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, more or less hairy.

description: Viscid, erect, perennial herbs from a highly branched caudex atop a woody taproot; branching confined to lower 3/4 of plant. Stems white or purple, stout, usually 1.5-3 mm in diameter at midstem, 15-34 (54) cm long, densely glandular-hispid and occasionally sparsely pilose with longer, flattened hairs. Leaves sessile, spatulate, oblong, or obovate, rarely elliptic, 2.5-7 cm long, 0.5-2.4 cm wide, usually glandular with pilose margins, occasionally the entire blade both pilose and glandular or merely glandular; apex obtuse or acute, spinulose or mucronate; base attenuate; margins entire or spinulose-dentate, with 2-20 teeth per leaf. Heads solitary at the ends of the stems, hemispherical, (2) 2.8-4 (4.8) cm wide, pedunculate, the peduncles (3) 5-15 (18.5) cm long. Involucre loosely or tightly imbricated; phyllaries in 3-5 series, densely glandular-hispid, outermost phyllaries lanceolate, ovate, or obovate, usually herbaceous for their entire length, keeled basally or not, 1.2-1.8 cm long, 1.8-6 mm wide, with a thin hyaline, fimbriate-ciliate margin, the apex attenuate or acuminate; innermost phyllaries similar to outer phyllaries, longer or shorter than the preceding series, keeled basally or not. Ray flowers (18) 24-32 (34) per head; tube slender, 4.8-6.3 mm long; ligule light blue, rarely white, oblong to elliptic, 2-2.9 cm long, 5-6.1 mm wide, distinctly 3-toothed. Disc flowers 60-136 per head; corolla 7.5-10.5 mm long, gradually ampliate or narrowed below into a slender tube, 5-7 mm long, and expanded above into a narrowly funnelform throat; style branches linear, 1.6-2 mm long, 0.3 mm wide, the appendages acute to acuminate, 0.8-1 mm long, equal to or shorter than the stigmatic lines. Pappus of about 50-90 stout, unequal bristles, the largest up to 12 mm long. Achenes linear or clavate, 4-8 mm long, 1-2.5 mm wide, slightly compressed, velutinous with long, silky, subappressed hairs, and with striations that are obscured by the vestiture. Chromosome number n = 6.

description: Plantae annuae, glabrae. Caules usque ad 30 cm longi. Folia linearia, 2-6 cm longa, 1-2 mm lata. Pedunculi 1-3 cm longi, bracteolis 2-6. Capitula numerosa, 10-15 mm alta, 10-15 mm diametro. Phyllaria 8 (raro 7, 9, vel 10), 5-8 mm longa, 1-1.7 mm lata, anguste hyalino-marginata, glandibus 1-5 subterminalibus etiam 4-10 submarginalibus punctata. Flosculi radii 8 (raro 7, 9, vel 10); corollae 5-8 mm longae, glabrae vel parce glanduloso-puberulae. Flosculi disci 12-24 (-34); corollae 3-5 mm longae, glabrae vel glanduloso-puberulae. Achenia cylindrica, 3-5.5 mm longa. Pappus acheniorum radii coroniformis, ca. 0.2 mm longus, raro 1 vel pluribus angustis paleis aut setis usque ad 2 mm longis compositus. Pappus acheniorum disci setaceus vel raro coroniformis; setae 16-24, barbellatae, (2-)3-4 mm longae. Chromosomatum numerus: n = 12.

description: Stem solid, pithy, about 3.5 mm. thick, evenly but not densely hirtous with purplish-brown hairs 1 mm. long or less and not enlarged at base; upper internodes 11.5-15 cm. long; leaves opposite; petioles thick, unmargined, not appendaged at base, sparsely hairy like the stem or glabrate, 5-7 mm. long; blades of upper leaves (at base of inflorescence) 4-4.5 cm. long, 2 cm. wide, rather abruptly short-pointed (tip 3-5 mm. long), glabrous except for a few hairs on base of costa beneath and along margin and sometimes along veins beneath, densely but inconspicuously impressed-glandular and somewhat pustulose beneath, fuscous above, brownish beneath, narrowly marginate, feather-veined (only 3-4 pairs of ascending veins evident beneath, a few additional milnor primary veins showing above); panicle up to about 40 cm. long and 20 cm. wide, of about 7 pairs of compound racemes, the lower branches subtended by leaves 2.5-5 cm. long (including petiole), the upper leaves greatly reduced; bracts subtending the pedicels subulate, about 2 mm. long, equaling or usually much shorter than the pedicels; phyllaries 4, subequal, thickened at extreme base but not calearate, 1.2-1.5 mm. wide; corollas apparently whitish, sparsely sessile-glandular, otherwise glabrous, 4.3 mm. long (tube 2.2-2.6 mm., throat funnelform-campanula-te, 1.7-1.8 mm., teeth broadly ovate, 0.4-0.5 mm. long); achenes slender, 5-nerved, sparsely sessile-glandular, 4.2 mm. long; pappus whitish, 4.2 mm. long, of about 47 minutely hispidulous bristles, slightly thickened toward tip.

description: Plants 2.5-8.0 dm tall. Stems moderately winged, glabrous to sparsely pubescent. Peduncles 1.5-8.0 cm long, generally projecting the terminal heads well above the foliage. Leaves narrowly elliptic to narrowly oblong elliptic or occasionally irregularly laciniate, 3-10 times as long as wide, serrate to undulate-serrate or occasionally deeply toothed in the laciniate leaves; lower leaves essentially glabrous; upper leaves glabrous to moderately pubescent. Heads ca. 20-100 per plant, 8-12 mm high, 8-12 mm wide (excluding rays). Receptacle conical to ovoid, 3.0-6.0 mm high, 2.8-5.0 mm wide. Rays florets 9-13; ligules 2.7-9.1 mm long, 1.5-6.7 mm wide, yellow or yellow with a red base, sparsely to moderately pubescent on the under- surface. Disc corollas 5-lobed, 1.7-2.4 mm long, 0.7-1.1 mm wide. Achenes 1.0-1.4 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm wide. Pappus scales 0.4-0.7 mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm wide. Chromosome number, n = 13.
bibliographicCitation: Bierner, Mark W. 1972. Taxonomy of Helenium sect. Tetrodus and a conspectus of North American Helenium (Compositae). Brittonia. 24: 331-355.

description: Biennial or short-lived perennial (or annual?) 3-5 (6) dm tall, glabrous or sometimes with small lanate tufts in the axils of the leaves; stems single or occa- sionally 2 or 3, arising from a fibrous-rooted, weakly creeping caudex or horizontal rootstock. Basal and lower cauline leaves distinctly lyrate-pinnate, terminal lobe well defined, ovate to subcordate and about as long as wide; lateral lobes of (1)2-6 pairs or rarely absent; margins of lobes dentate or crenate-dentate; midrib un- winged; overall leaf dimensions 8-12(5-18) cm long and 2-6 cm wide; petiole 1-2 times as long as the blade. Middle and upper cauline leaves progressively reduced upwards, lyrate to sublyrate, terminal lobe less distinct, margins of lobes shallowly dentate, midrib winged; uppermost leaves reduced to bracts. Inflorescence a loose open cyme made up of one to several subumbellate cymules of 2-5 (6) heads each; principal involucral bracts about 13, green to yellowish tipped, 4-6 mm long; caly- culate bracts very small, few, and inconspicuous; ray florets about 8, the ligule yellow, 6-12 mm. Achenes 2-4 mm long, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, T. M. 1968. Taxonomy of Senecio multilobaius and its allies. Brittonia. 20: 267-284.

description: Viscid, erect, perennial herbs or subshrubs from a highly branched caudex atop a thick, woody taproot, plants occasionally with overwintering stems to 25 cm long; branching confined to the lower 1/2 of the seasons' growth. Stems (and branches) usually white (especially older growth), often tinged with purple; younger stems and branches (8) 17-36 (56) cm long, stout, 1.5-3 (6) mm in diameter, usually with two classes of pubescence, moderately to densely villous or tomentose with long, eglandular hairs and sparsely to densely glandular with stipitate-glandular or glandular- hispid trichomes, the lower portions of the stem less glandular, and sometimes the eglandular hairs confined to the foliate protions of the stem and/or to the phyllaries  Leaves lanceolate, linear, oblanceolate, or elliptic, 2.5-10 cm long, 0.4-3 cm wide, usually pilose to tomentose and glandular, less often merely glandular-hispid; apex acute to attenuate, spinose to spinulose; base truncate or subclasping; margins spinose dentate, 2-20 teeth per leaf. Heads solitary at the ends of the stems, hemispherical or broadly campanulate, (1.5) 1.6-2.6 (3) cm wide, pedunculate, the peduncles (3) 8-22 (24) cm long. Involucre loosely or tightly imbricated; phyllaries in 3-7 series; outermost phyllaries linear, lanceolate, or oblanceolate, usually herbaceous from 1/4 to 3/4 of their length, scarious below, often keeled basally, 0.5-2.5 cm long, 0.7-2.5 mm wide, usually pilose and glandular, entire or with a thin, hyaline, fimbriate-ciliate margin, the apex attenuate to acuminate; innermost phyllaries longer to shorter than the immediately preceding series, largely scarious, less pubescent, usually keeled basally, linear to lanceolate with acute to acuminate apices. Ray flowers (17) 25-60 (85) per head; tube slender, 2.5-5 mm long; ligule light blue, rarely white, oblong to linear-oblong, 1-3.3 cm long, 1.8-5.5 mm wide, distinctly 3-toothed. Disc flowers 72-112 per head; corolla 5.5-8.5 mm long, gradually ampliate or narrowed below into a slender tube, 2.5-4.5 mm long, and expanded above into a campanulate or broadly funnelform throat; style branches linear-subulate, 1.1-1.5 mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm wide, the appendages acute, 0.3-0.5 mm long, shorter than the stigmatic lines. Pappus of about 35-90 stout, unequal bristles, the largest up to 9 mm long. Achenes linear, clavate, or fusiform, 3-6 mm long, laterally compressed, velutinous with long, silky, subappressed hairs, and with several weak or prominent costae which are usually obscured by the vestiture. Chromosome numbers n = 6, 12.
bibliographicCitation: Watson, Thomas J., Jr. 1977. The taxonomy of Xylorhiza (Asteraceae-Astereae). Brittonia. 29: 199-216.
