description: Perennial herbs, 1-2.5 (3.2) dm tall, from a stout woody caudex; stems hirsute to hirsute-strigose or hirsute-villous, especially on upper portion, becoming glabrate below. Leaves on lower 2/3 of stem, the sessile blades (2) 3-5 (11) cm long, 0.1-1 cm wide, linear to linear-elliptic, widest at or below the middle, apically acuminate, basally cuneate, the margins revolute, hirsute to hirsute-villous, densely pubescent to glabrate above, hirsute to hirsute-villous or strigose, to almost glabrate beneath. Inflorescence of a single head terminating the stem. Heads (14) 23-38 (52)-flowered; peduncles ca 5-10 cm long, densely hirsute-villous to tomentose. Involucre broadly campanulate, 8-12 mm high, 8-12 (15) mm wide. Phyllaries imbricate in ca 2 indistinct series, hirsute-villous to strigose, sometimes ciliate, grayish-purple, the inner ones lanceolate (6.8) 8-9 (11) mm long, 1.2-2 (2.5) mm wide, acuminate, the outer ones lanceolate (3.8) 4-6 (9) mm long, (0.7) 1-2 (2.6) mm wide. Pappus brownish-straw-colored, the inner bristles (5.6) 7-10 (12) mm long, the outer ones, 1-2 mm long. Corollas (7.5) 9-11 (14) mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers 3-4 mm long. Achenes (1.5) 2-3.8 mm long, strigose. Flowering and fruiting from July to February.
bibliographicCitation: Henrickson, James. 1981. A new species of Satureja [S. maderensis] (Lamiaceae) from the Chihuahuan Desert region. Brittonia. 33: 211-213.

description: Small shrublets, 8 cm tall, much branched. Stems prostrate, subligneous, with adventitious roots, giving rise at their nodes to slender, herbaceous, ascending shoots with a terminal head. Leaves alternate, sessile and sheathed, entire, linear, mucronate at the apex, glaucous, 10-13 X 1-1.5 mm, margins with simple, short, pluricellular hairs and spherical multicellular glands on both surfaces. Heads with 12-18 ray flowers and 48-55 disk flowers, 20-25 mm diam. (including ray flowers). Involucre of ca. 50 bracts arranged in 6 series. External bracts 3 X 1 mm, with reflexed tips. Internal bracts 6 X 2 mm. Ray flower yellow, pistillate, fertile, with corolla of 9.5-11 mm long and limb 2 mm wide. Disk flowers yellow, perfect, with corolla 5 mm long. Pappus of disk and ray flowers caducous, of ca. 10 awns, remotely serrulate, 3.5-4 mm long. Achenes glabrous, quadrangular, ca. 3.5 mm long.

description: Erect, perennial herbs from a highly branched caudex atop a woody taproot; branching usually confined to the caudex, but occasionally with a few branches near the apex of the stem. Stems white (7) 9-33 (37) cm long, densely villous to glabrous, comparatively weak, usually 1-1.5 mm in diameter at midstem. Leaves linear or linear-lanceolate to oblanceolate, 1-7.5 cm long, 1-9 mm wide, glabrate to densely arachnoid- or canescent-villous with very long, fragile, transparent or white hairs; apex acute or obtuse, mucronate; base attenuate to truncate or rounded; margins entire or rarely with a few teeth. Heads solitary at the ends of the stems or branches, broadly campanulate or hemispherical, (1) 1.4-2.3 (2.5) cm wide, pedunculate, the peduncles (1.5) 2-5 (7.5) cm long. Involucre loosely or tightly imbricated; phyllaries in 2-3 series; outermost phyllaries linear or lanceolate to ovate, herbaceous for Y2 or more of their length, scarious below, usually keeled basally, glabrous to densely villous, 0.4-1.2 cm long, 0.9-3.5 mm wide, entire or with a thin, hyaline, fimbriate- ciliate margin; the apex acuminate to attenuate; innermost phyllaries similar to the outer phyllaries, but usually larger, more scarious, and less pubescent, always keeled basally. Ray flowers (10) 12-22 (29) per head; tube slender, 2-3.5 mm long; ligule whi,te or occasionally light blue, oblong to elliptic, 1.1-2 cm long, 2.4-4.5 mm wide, 3-toothed. Disc flowers 36-116 per head; corolla 4.5-6 mm long, gradually ampliate or narrowed below into a slender tube, 2.5-3 mm long, expanded above into a campanulate to broadly funnelform throat; style branches linear, 1.4-1.6 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, the appendages acute, 0.3-0.9 mm long, equal to or shorter than the stigmatic lines. Pappus of about 40-100 stout, unequal bristles, the largest up to 5 mm long. Achenes linear or clavate, 4-5.5 mm long, slightly compressed, veluti- nous with long, silky, subappressed hairs, often with numerous, weak striations which are obscured by the vestiture. Chromosome number n = 6.

description: Shrubs ca 2 m tall; stems gray-felted, thickened. Leaves cauline, crowded, the sessile blades 5-17 x 0.4-1.5 cm, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, apically acuminate, basally truncate, marginally strongly revolute, pubescence appearing waxy above, cinereous-felted below. Inflorescences terminal, of large, globose to conical or elongate glomerules. Heads 12-20-flowered. Involucre campanulate. Phyllaries arachnoid-villous dorsally, ca 14 x 1-1.5 mm, tips apiculate, glabrous and brownish. Pappus straw-colored; inner paleas 11-15 mm long, outer scales 1.5-2 mm long. Corollas 10-11 mm long, rosy-pink, lobes sometimes hirsute. Achenes ca 4 mm long, 10-ribbed, glabrous. Chromosome number: n = 17 Ils, Smith 998 (GA). Contrary to an earlier report in the literature, two types of achene are not present. Flowering and fruiting from February to March.

description: Shrubs or small trees; stems striate, villous. Leaves opposite, sessile, blade lanceolate to ovate or elliptic, 7-15 cm long, 2-5 cm wide, basally cuneate to auriculate, apically obtuse to rounded, lower surface tomentose and glandular, upper surface bullate and glabrate, margin irregularly crenate, slightly revolute. Capitulescences terminal and axillary, cymose-paniculate, peduncles 1-6 cm long, villous, bracteate, pedicels 3-6 mm long, villous, bracteolate. Capitula with 18-35 florets; involucre campanulate, 8-12 mm high, ca 5 mm wide; phyllaries 5-6-seriate, imbricate, graduate, the outer ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 1.5-3 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, arachnoid, ciliolate, the inner oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 8-10 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, sparsely arachnoid, ciliolate, all phyllaries apically obtuse to rounded, stramineous, coriaceous; receptacle convex; corolla white to violet, tube cylindric, 6-8 mm long, limb narrowly companulate, lobes 2-3 mm long, 0.5-0.6 mm wide, strongly reflexed, anthers ca 2.75 mm long, basally sagittate, auricles acute, terminal appendages obtuse, style branches filiform-subulate, ca 2.25 mm long, abaxial surface hispidulous. Achenes fusiform, (2) 2.5-2.8 mm long, 5-ribbed, sparsely glandular at base; pappus white, biseriate, filiform, outer bristles 0.5-1.75 mm long, inner bristles 5.5-6 mm long.

description: Perennial herbs from subsimple caudices with fibrous roots, each perennating crown producing 1-2 erect stems, usually with very short basal offsets produced from thin, herbaceous stolons with scale leaves. Stems 7-30 cm tall, simple, sometimes ascending at the base, greenish, longitudinally grooved, very sparsely pubescent with spreading, uniseriate trichomes, distally also sometimes slightly viscid with much smaller, appressed or spreading uniseriate trichomes. Leaves glabrous to very sparsely pubescent on the lamina, rarely sparsely pubescent on the midvein, margins entire, glabrous to sparsely or densely ciliate with spreading trichomes, particularly near the base of the blade, apex sometimes glandular; basal leaves 15-110 mm long, elliptic-obovate to elliptic or spatulate, 6-17 mm wide, sometimes conspicuously 3-veined, with entire margins and rounded to acute or obtuse apex, gradually or abruptly attenuate to petiole l/3-?/2 as long as the leaf; cauline leaves 6-11 in number, alternate, lanceolate to narrowly oblong- or linear-lanceolate, sessile, usually with clasping (lower) to subclasping (upper) bases, similar to the basal leaves in pubescence, mostly equal-sized or gradually reduced upward, 8-21 mm long, uppermost reduced to linear bracts. Heads sol- itary, terminal on a peduncle up to 10 cm long; involucres shallowly cupulate, 10-15 mm wide (pressed); phyllaries 2-3 (4) series of equal length, obovate to oblong-obovate with acuminate apex, 5-8 x 0.8-1.8 mm, thin-herbaceous, green with a thin golden midvein, outer sparsely spreading-pubescent, sometimes con- spicuously viscid with much smaller, appressed, uniseriate trichomes, margins sometimes with a very narrow, scarious rim, sometimes slightly lacerate-ciliate near the apex; receptacles low-conic, very shallowly alveolate. Ray flowers 20-55 in a single series, white, drying white or with a roseate or purple tinge, (7.5) 10-15. 1 mm long, the ligule 1. 1-2.5 mm wide, 4-5 (6) veined, sometimes curling at tip with maturity or drying, 2-3 denticulate at apex, tube conspicuously pu- bescent with long, biseriate and sometimes also with uniseriate trichomes, basal rim abruptly flaring; style branches 0.3-0.5 mm long. Disc flowers ca 70-1 10, narrowly funnelform, not inflated or indurated, 2-2.8 mm long, lower 1/5 sometimes slightly constricted, basal rim abruptly flaring, very sparsely pubescent with short, biseriate trichomes; style branches 0.5-0.8 mm long, including the lanceo- late to narrowly triangular collecting appendages 0.3-0.4 mm long. Achenes tardily released from flowers, obovate to widely obovate or oblong-lanceolate, plump, (1.4) 1.8-2.4 x 0.8-1.2 mm, stramineous to buffy-olive, surfaces shiny and gla- brous, those of the ray flowers 2-, 3-, or 4-nerved, those of the disc flowers 2- or 3-nerved, the outermost often thinly 3-nerved and subtriquetrous; carpopodium a minute, weakly differentiated cartilaginous ring 2-5 cells high; pappus of disc and ray achenes completely lacking or represented by a minute, cartilaginous rim.

description: Perennial herbs to subshrubs; stems generally blackish-canescent, or becoming somewhat glabrate. Leaves cauline; petioles 4-24 mm long, canescent; blades 8.5-14 cm long, 2-7.5 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, widest at or below the middle, apically acute to acuminate, basally cuneate to rounded or truncate, marginally revolute and remotely callous-toothed, glabrous, reticulate-veined, canescent on midveins or major lateral veins above, canescent beneath. Inflo- rescences small with relatively few large heads, cymose-paniculate. Heads 37-48- flowered; peduncles 1-5 cm long, canescent. Involucre broadly campanulate, 22-32 mm high, 12-20 mm wide; phyllaries loosely imbricate in ca 5-6 series, the inner ones linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 2.1-2.7 cm long, 1.6-3.5 mm wide, gla- brate to arachnoid, the outer ones ovate-lanceolate, 2.1-9 mm long, 1.1-2.6 mm wide, sometimes canescent. Pappus brownish, the inner bristles 10-11 lmm long and outer scales 2-3 mm long. Corollas 8-10.5 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous, generally exceeded by the inner phyllaries. Anthers 5-5.5 mm long. Achenes 3-4.5 mm long, pilose. Flowering and fruiting from June to October.

description: Plants annual, erect, up to 1.6 dm high, branched; stems strigose-hispid; leaves lanceolate to linear, hispid, subpetiolate or petioles up to 7 mm lone, blades ulp to 3.5 cmi long and 7 mm wvide; heads sessile, campanulate, ca 6 mm wide; phyllaries ca 14, imbricate, graduated, elliptic to obovate, sometimles foliaceous, lightly pubescent, apices often discolored; rays 7-12, yellow, triangular, persistent, ca 2 mm long, glabrous except for frequenlt apical hairs, apices acute, entire to 2-lobed, style filiform, bifid, apices acute; ray achenes ca 3 n m long, obtriangular, 3-angled with a thick cartilaginous ridge at each angle, smoothly to tuberculately crustose, the 3 divergent awns longer than the rays anld expanded basally; disk corollas nulmerous, ca 2 mm long, having a tube ansd limb, basally constricted, shorter than the achenes, lightly pubescent near the base with red-tipped hairs, otherwise glabrous, lobes very short, thickenedl marginally, filaments thickened near the anther, anther apices broadly lanceolate, concavre, style bifid, apices aculte, branches flattened inwardly, base dilated into a low, broad, striate cylinder; peripheral disk achenes compressed., obtriangular and cuneate, striate, tuberculate with a few hairs on the tubercles, broadly winged, apices notched; awnless or the single short rigid awn not persistenit; central ray achenes with 0-2 needle-shaped pubescent awns, 1-2 winged, margins cartilagenous; paleae purplish at the cuspidate apices, keel ciliate, not persistent, equalling the disk flowers; receptacle conical; n = 16.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1964. Revision of Sanvitalia (Compositae-Heliantheae). Brittonia. 16: 417-433.

description: Herba vel suffrutex ramosus ramis terminalibus viridibus leviter striatis glabris vel sparse puberulis. Folia alterna tenuiter herbacea sessilia, lamina laeteviridi glabra lineari- oblonga basi longe attenuata ad modum petioli, apice obtusa subite breviterque calloso-mucronulata margine integra laevi, 1.5-4.5 cm longa 0.2-0.45 cm lata, utrinque glabra laevi tantum nervo medio subtus prominulo venulis reticulatis valde delicatis paulo visibilibus. Inflorescentia corymboso-paniculata terminalis folia suprema excedens ramulis gracilibus subflexuosis sparse puberulis. Pedicelli teneres 5-20 mm longi 2-3 bracteolis anguste linearibus acutis circa 3-5 mm longis 0.5 mm latis praediti, extremo 4-5 bracteolis similibus ad modum calyculi dispositis. Capitula hete- rogama. Involucrum cylindricum 13 bracteis uniseriatis tenuiter herbaceis lineari- oblongis 7 mm longis 1-1.6 mm latis dorso viridibus glabris vel minute puberulis apice nigris acutis barbulatisque. Flores marginales feminei 8 ligulati, corolla lutea 10 mm longa tubulo capillare glabro 3.5 mm longo lamina oblongoa-elliptica 6 mm longa 2-2.3 mm lata 4-nervata 3-dentata, ramis styli paulo tubum excedenti- bus. Flores disci hermaphroditi circa 25 tubulosi, corolla lutea glabra tubulo 2 mm longo limbo tubuloso dentibus apicalibus brevibus 0.5 mm longis. Antherae 2 mm longae basi obtusae. Ovarium villosum. Achaenia sublaevia paulo compressa strigoso-villosa 2.5 mm longa. Pappus albis 6 mm altus setis capillaribus leviter repandeque strigillosis.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1956. Studies on Andean Compositae - III. Brittonia. 8 (3): 179-193.

description: Plants up to 9-10 dm tall; stems pilose-strigose, greenish, becoming yellowish to purplish, sometimes striate; leaves lanceolate, ovate or oblong, the- bases truncate, obtuse or subcordate, the apices acute; blades ea 8 cm long, 3.5 cm wide, or much smaller, sessile or subsessile, hirsute to strigose, glanduliferous with scabrous margins; peduncles up to 8.5 cm long, inflated or scarcely so, striate, sericeous, or densely strigose above; heads subhemispheric to hemispheric, up to 2.2 cm wide; phyllaries obovate, glabrous, their apices rounded, erose, squarrose, mostly with a dark summit band, or this only a discolored marginal zone; rays 8-20 (two or three times as many in cultivars), up to 2.2 cm long, spatulate to obovate, white, yellow, orange, pink, red, scarlet, lilac or purple, but usually red in nature, glandular beneath, often with scabrous margins, sericeous at the throat; ray style glabrous or lightly pubescent with spreading hairs; ray achene oblanceolate to cuneate, dorsally compressed with a promi- nent inner angle, sericeous, 6 mm long, searious-margined, awnless; disk flowers very numerous, 7 mm long, with lobes ea 1 mm long, inside yellow, velutinous, outside black, smooth, the tube yellow below; disk style ea 8 mm long with branches 1.5-2. mm long; disk achenes laterally compressed, often appearing wrinkled if from a crowded head, cuneate, sparsely pubescent or glabrous, becoming rugose, emarginate at apex, awnless, their margins finely ciliate; chaff exceeded by the disk flowers, outside sparsely ciliate mainly along the keel, the apices pink to red-purple (otherwise colored in cultivars), the lobes fimbriate; receptacle elongate-conical, up to 2.3 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1963. Taxonomy of Zinnia. Brittonia. 15: 1-25.

description: Herba crassa; foliis coriaceis oblongo-ovatis, 15-25 cm. longis, 2.5- 3.5 cm. latis, basin versus ad 8-9 mm. angustatis, ad vaginam coriaceam 2-3 cm. latam dilatatis, apice subacutis, margine integris, utrinque arete et dense ferrugineo-caneseente-tomentosis, nervis secundariis patulis eirciter 15 per decimetrum; ramis floriferis crassis e caudice erectis, 50-70 cm. longis, ubique flaccide caneseente-tomentosis; infloreseentia elongata eymosa thyrsiformi vel spiciformi, ramulis brevibus (4-10 cm. longis) alternatis- gracilibus, bracteis foliaceis (superioribus ad 3 cm. longis reductis) subtentis; capitulis 3-6 per ramulum lateralem, maturitate 12-15 mm. diametro breviter pedunculatis; involuero eirciter 3-seriato, phyllaribus eirciter 20 ovatis acutis, 6-8 mm. longis, eirciter 4 mm. latis, extra lana densa ferruginea indutis; floribus radii 80-120, 3- vel 4-seriatis, lamina ovato-oblonga, 2-2.5 mm. longa, eirciter 1.2 mm. lata, tubo hispidulo 1 mm. longo, introrse apice lobos 2 lineares 1 mm. longos gerente, stylo bifido 2 mm. longo, achenio trigono 1.5-2 mm. longo; floribus disci stramineis 3.5-4 mm. longis, tubo hispidulo quam limbo leviter breviore, lobis deltoideis 0.5 mm. longis; staminibus styloque maturitate exsertis; paleis obovatis, eirciter 4 mm. longis et 1.5 mm. latis, apice cuspidatis, apicem versus pilis 1.5 mm. longis hispidis.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Koch, M. A. 1935. The genus Espeletia: a study in phylogenetic taxonomy. Brittonia. 1: 479-530. pl. 1, 2 + f. 1-5.

description: Plants annual, 20-32 cm high, erect, hirsute; leaves 3-5.2 cm long, 1.5-2.2 cm wide, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, acute at the apex, cuneate at the base, serrate, evenly appressed-hirsute on both surfaces; petioles slender, 5-11 mm long; heads subcampanulate, rather elongated, 6-8 mm in diameter, solitary on slender peduncles which branch in subeymose fashion; peduncles 3-6.5 cm long, sparsely hirsute, the trichomes retrorsely appressed; receptacle elongate-conical, nearly cylindrical, ca 1 mm across, 5-6 mm high; chaff persistent, slightly ovate, ca 4 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, searious except near the greenish to purplish, rounded to obtuse apex; involucre 2-3-seriate, the outer bracts light green, obovate-elliptic, 2.5-3 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, acute and purple-tinged at the apex, the margins ciliate, these glabrate or sparsely pubescent with minute purple hairs; inner bracts light green, purple-tinged, becoming membranous, obovate, the longest 4-5 mm, ca 2 mm wide, acute to obtuse at the apex, the margins scarious and ciliate, pubescent with minute purple hairs, especially near the apex; ray flowers 6, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 2-2.5 mm, with conspicuous white, purple-tinged ligules, these 4-8 mm long, 4-6.5 mm wide, obovate, three-lobed at the apex, pubescent on the veins beneath and toward the base; pappus of the ray florets shorter than that of the disc, ca 1 mm long; disc corollas greenish-yellow, 3-3.5 mm long, the tube glabrous to sparsely pilose, 0.2-0.5 mm long, the throat tubular to narrowly funnelform, ca 1.8 mm long, glabrous to sparsely pilose at the base, the lobes acute, reflexed or erect, 0.5-1 mm long; style branches rather flattened, ca 1 mm long, brownish, revolute, finely pubescent, with a short subulate tip; achenes brownish-black, subturbinate, slightly diagonally compressed, obscurely 4-ridged, 2 mm long, densely pilose with the hairs arranged in vertical rows, alternately whitish to light brown or purple; pappus of 20 equal plumose bristles, ca 1.5 mm long, shorter than the achene, some of the bristles purple, at least at the base; anthers ca 1.5 mm long, sagittate at the base.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, William L. & Zamuco, Isidro T. 1965. Identify of 'Tinong' (Dipterocarpaceae). Brittonia. 17: 35-46.

description: Frutex ramis terminalibus copiose foliatis, striatis puberulo-glandulosis et parce lanuglnosis. Folia papyracea crassiuscula alterna. Petiolus circa 1 cm longus crassus dense tomentoso-lanuginosus. Lamina ovato-acuminata basi rotundata vel cordata, superne amplectens, apice acuta vel breviter cuspidata, margine serrato-denticu- lata bene revoluta dentibus acutis calloso-incrassatis; 11-13 cm longa 5.5-6.5 cm lata; supra asperula pilis crassis subtuberculatis copiose praedita, costa lata conspicua lanata nervis lateralibus notatis ceteris venulis reticulatis impressis superficie plus minusve rugulosa; subtus pilis crassis copiosis munita et albido- arachnoidea lanuginosa, costa crassa eminenti magis lanata, nervis secundariis 16-17 utroque latere prominentibus patulis ad marginem anastomosantibus re- liquis nervis reticulatis parum conspicuis. Inflorescentia corymboso-paniculata terminalis folia suprema paulo superans axi ramisque sparse glandulosis et lanuginosis bracteolis ovato-lanceolatis. Capitula radiata. Pedicelli 5-15 cm longi crassiusculi flexuosi tomentulosi. Calyculus 5-7 bracteolis angustissimis 5-7 mm longis parce puberulis. Involucrum campanulatum circa 7 mm altum 13 bracteis oblongo-lanceolatis 6 mm longis 1.5-2.5 mm latis apice acutis ciliolatisque basi plus minusve lanuginosis reliquo glabrato dorso incrassatis. Flores-radii feminei circa 14 ligulati; corolla lutea glabra 10 mm longa, tubulo 4 mm longo, lamina 1.5 mm lata apice tridentata. Flores disci hermaphroditi circa 30, corolla lutea glabra tubulosa 6.5-7 mm longa; antheris 2.5 mm longis; ramis styli apice obtusis. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus stramineus 6-6.5 mm longus.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1956. Studies on Andean Compositae - III. Brittonia. 8 (3): 179-193.

description: Frutex ad 2.5 met. altus ramuli flexuosi angulato-striati minute denseque griseo-tomentosi juveniles molliter ochraceo-tomentosi. Folia opposita petiolata coriacea. Petiolus crassiusculus 10-15 mm. longus adpresse tomentosus subtus carinatus supra sulcatus. Lamina elliptico-oblonga vel sublanceolata basi obtusa vel rotundata apicem versus paulo angustata apice acutiuscula minute mucronulata vel obtusiuscula, margine integra, 6-9 cm. longa, 1.8-3 cm. lata; supra siccitate pallide viridis costa angusta depressa nervulis minute reticulatis prominulis, glabra nitens; subtus dense ochraceo-tomentosa costa crassa elevata striolata, nervis secundariis 8-10 utroque latere conspicuis patulis furcatis nervulis in reticulo plus minusve prominulo. Inflorescentiae terminales cymoso-paniculatae basi foliosae folia subaequi- longae axi ramisque plus minusve flexuosis striatis dense tomentosis viridi- ochraceis, bracteis linearibus basi dilatatis 4-1.5 mm. longis tomentosis. Ca- pitula homogama cylindracea brevia glomerata breviter pedicellata pedicellis crassiusculis angulosis tomentosis praecipue 2 mm. longis vel interdum longiori- bus, numerosis bracteolis minutis ovato-linearibus acutis circa 1 mm. longis tomentellis ad apicem ad modum calyculi dispositis. Involucrum glabrum in sicco brunneo-stramineum 6-8 bracteis subcoriaceis oblongis apice subacutis 5 mm. longis, exterioribus 1.5-2 mm. latis, interioribus margine late scarioso, 2.5 mm. latis. Flores 7-9 omnes hermaphroditi tubulosi, corolla 4.8 mm. longa lutea glabra tubulo 2 mm. longo, dentibus oblongis acutiusculis 1.6 mm. longis apice papillosulis. Antherae 1.2 mm. longi basi sagittatae. Stigmata breviter conica apice piloso-apiculata. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus stramineus 5-6 mm. longus.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1954. New species of Compositae from Ecuador, collected by W. H. Camp. Brittonia. 8: 39-79.

description: Herba alnnua, gracillima, erecta, vix ramosa, ea 4-6 dm alta; caule tetragono, subglabro, tantum 1-1.5 mm crasso, internodiis elongatis 5-10 cm longris. Folia opposita, mlinima et graciliter bipinnata, petiolata petiolo filiformi et usque ad 1.5 cm longo, lamina saepius 1-2.5 cm longa et paulo angustiore, segmentis mem- branaceis linearibusque ea 1.5-2 mm latis, aegre setuloso-ciliatis et duabus facie- bus plus minusve hispidulis, apice mucronulatis. Capitula corymboso-disposita, pauca (2-10), pedunculos capilliformes sub 5 cm longos terminantia, erecta, radiata, pansa ad anthesin tantum ea 4-5 mm lata et alta. Involucri campanulati basi hispiduli bracteae exteriores ea 8, adpressae anguste lineares apice acres extus numme glabratae nune conspicue hispido-ciliatae sub 2 mm longae, quam interiores ovato-oblongae marginaliter diaphanae breviores. Flores ligulati ea 4 vel 5, patentes, albi (desiceati forsitan subrosei), ligula obovata sub 2 mm longa ea 4-6-atro-striata, apice aegre denticulata. Flores tubulosi pauci (sub 15), flavi. Paleae lineari-oblongae, apice abrupte angustatae et terminaliter pubeseentes. Achaenia pauca (tantuni 5-8) linearia, obcompressa, superne at- tenuata et patentia, faciebus glabra et nigra summam versus flavo-brunnea et sursum setulosa, marginibus involutis papillata et sursum setosa, apice exaristata sed erecte setosa, demum 10-12 nmm longa et ea 1 mm crassa.

description: Annnual herb, very delicate, erect, scarcely branched, about 4-6 dm tall; stem tetragonal, subglabrous, only 1-1.5 mm thick, the internodes elongate and 5-10 cm long. Leaves opposite, very small and delicately bipinnate, petiolate with a filiform petiole, this up to 1.5 cm long; blade more often 1-2.5 cm long and slightly niarrower, the segfments membranaceous and linear, ca 1.5-2 mm wide, weakly setulose-ciliate and on both faces more or less hispidulous, at apex mueronuilate. Heads corymbosely disposed, few (2-10), at ends of capilliform peduneles under 5 cm long, erect, radiate, expanded at flowering time only ca 4-5 mm wide and tall. Involuere campanulate, basally hispidulous; outer phyllaries about 8, appressed, narorwly linear, at tip sharp, outwardly now glabrate now conspicuously hispid-ciliate, under 2 mm long, shorter than the inner ovate-oblong marginally transparent ones. Ligulate florets ea 4 or 5, spreading, white (in dried material perhaps subrosaceous); ligule obovate, under 2 mm long, ea 4-6-dark-striate, at apex weakly denticulate. Flowers of the disk few (under 15), yellow. Chaff-scales linear-oblong, at apex abruptly narrowed and terminally pubescent. Achenes few (only 5-8), linear, obcompressed, near top yellowish- brown and upwardly setulose, attenuate and spreading apart above, on the faces glabrous and black near top yellow-brown and upwardly setulose, on the involute edges papillate and upwardly setose, at apex exaristate but erectly setose, finally 10-12 mm long and about 1 mm thick.

description: Low stout (branching?) shrub, the branchlets densely cinereous lanate; leaves densely aggregated and somewhat concealing the inflorescences, coriaceous, oblong, 25-30 cm. long, 8-9.5 cm. broad, narrowed towards the base to 8-10 mm., obtuse or subacute at apex, entire or minutely denticulate at the narrowly revolute margins, glabrous above (or lanate on costa), closely griseous tomentose beneath, the costa very prominent, the secondary nerves up to 90 per side, straight, spreading, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous beneath; inflorescences densely aggregated near ends of branchlets, broadly corymbose-paniculate, many-headed, the branches brownish lanate, subtended by bracts resembling small leaves, the ultimate bracts deltoid, 2-3 cm. long and 1 cm. broad, closely appressed to the heads; expanded heads about 25 mm. in diameter; involucre 2- or 3-seriate, the phyllaries 10-15, ovate, the outer ones about 13 mm. long and 6 mm. broad, acute, lanate without; ray florets about 25, 2-seriate, the corolla about 7 mm. long, the tube pilose, the lamina elliptic-oblong, 2.5-3 mm. broad, the achene about 3 mm. long; disk florets pilose on tube and lobes, about 6 mm. long, the limb equaling the tube, the lobes deltoid, the stamens about 3 mm. long; paleae oblong, 6-7 mm. long, densely pilose distally without.

description: Low stout (branching?) shrub, the branchlets densely einereous lanate; leaves densely aggregated and somewhat concealing the infloreseences, coriaceous, oblong, 25-30 cm. long, 8-9.5 cm. broad, narrowed towards the base to 8-10 mm., obtuse or subacute at apex, entire or minutely denticulate at the narrowly revolute margins, glabrous above (or lanate on costa), closely griseous tomentose beneath, the costa very prominent, the secondary nerves up to 90 per side, straight, spreading, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous beneath; inflorescences densely aggregated near ends of branchlets, broadly corymbose-paniculate, many-headed, the branches brownish lanate, subtended by bracts resembling small leaves, the ultimate bracts deltoid, 2-3 cm. long and 1 cm. broad, closely appressed to the heads; expanded heads about 25 mm. in diameter; involuere 2- or 3-seriate, the phyllaries 10-15, ovate, the outer ones about 13 mm. long and 6 mm. broad, acute, lanate without; ray florets about 25, 2-seriate, the corolla about 7 mm. long, the tube pilose, the lamina elliptic-oblong, 2.5-3 mm. broad, the achene about 3 mm. long; disk florets pilose on tube and lobes, about 6 mm. long, the limb equaling the tube, the lobes deltoid, the stamens about 3 mm. long; paleae oblong, 6-7 mm. long, densely pilose distally without.

description: Perennial from a stout short caudex; stem amply and equably leafy, 2-6 dm. high, usually noticeably purplish at the base, more or less spreading-hirsute, also glandular above; leaves entire, acute, villous-hirsute on both sides, the upper ones occasionally glandular and sometimes nearly glabrous except for the midribs and margins; leaves commonly becoming progressively wider (in proportion to their length) from base to top of stem, the middle cauline ones the largest; basal leaves relatively small, oblaneeolate or sometimes narrowly elliptic, the blade and petiole commonly well under 10 cm. long and 1 cm. wide, often deciduous by flowering time; middle cauline leaves mostly ovate or lance-ovate, 4-8 cm. long and 1-2.5 wide, sometimes larger, more or less clasping; upper leaves usually broadly ovate and strongly clasping, sharply acute or acuminate, or occasionally progressively narrower and smaller than the middle leaves, the heads then naked-pedunculate; heads usually solitary but occasionally 2 or 3, or even 6, usually without long naked peduncles; disk 13-20 mm. wide; involuere 7-12 mnm. high, equaling or surpassing the disk, moderately to very densely woolly or long-villous with long, flattened, shiny, multicellular hairs, some of which may have some of the crosswalls reddish purple; phyllaries about equal, slender and loose, the long-acuminate glandular often purple tips commonly reflexed; ligules about 75-150, pink or pink-purple, 12-20 mm. long, 0.8-1.6 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4-5.5 mm. long, the well-defined tube about 1.0-1.8 mm. long, the lobes about 0.5-0.8 mm.; style-appendages lanceolate to deltoid-ovate, acute or acuminate, about 0.2-0.25 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 15-20 bristles, the outer of conspicuous squamellate setae; akenes hairy, 2-nerved.

description: Plants annual, erect to ascending, ea 2 dm high, branched; stems strigosehispid; leaves lanceolate, strigose, petioles up to 1 cm long, blades up to 3 cm long and 1.5 cm wide; heads sessile, hemispheric, ea 8 mm wide; phyllaries ca 16, imbricate, graduated, sometimes foliaceous, sometimes mucronate, ovate, essentially glabrous except for the ciliate margins, often discolored near the apex; rays ea 13, white to pale yellow, angular ovate, ea 3 mm long, glabrous, persistent, margins involute on the basal half, apices generally 2-lobed and sometimes with 1-few hairs, style bifid, apices of style branches obtuse; ray achenes triangular, ca 4 mm long, striate, essentially glabrous the 3 divergent awns ca 3 mm long, yellow, the inner awn distinctly awl-shaped; disk corollas numerouLs, ca 2 mm long, green to pale yellow above, darker below, often dilated basally, the lobes with thickened margins, filaments not dilated above, anther apices concave (as seen from the outside) and lanceolate, style bifid, branch apices obtuse, branches flattened iniwardly; disk achenes ea 3.3 mm long, flattened to 3-4 angled with 2-4, rarely 5, slender, persistent, unequal awns, tuberculate with tufts of hairs along the margins and on the tubercles; paleae exceeding the disk flowers, not persistent, yellowish above, hyaline below, apices cuspidate, sparsely pubescent along the keel; receptacle low conical.

description:
A S. jorullense H.B.K. plantis subscapiformibus pagina inferiore foliorum (mini- mum infimorum) purpurata, capitulis congestis et a S. clinopodioide Greenm. foliis ovatis, plerumque planis, plantis elatioribus subscapiformibus differt.

Herba perennis rhizomatosa ad 0.5 m alta. Caules erecti vel primo decumbentes, plerumque solitarii, simplices e basi vel raro in speciminibus robustis vel veteribus sparsim ramulosi, purpurei et parce pilosi, superne puberuli. Folia opposita superiora sessilia inferiora petiolata, saepe conduplicata, elliptica vel ovata 2.5-4.5 cm longa 1-3 cm lata crenata (raro serrata), apice obtusa vel rotundata, basi acuta vel obtusa in petiolum decurrentia; superficies crispo-pilosa, puberula secus venas, non manifeste glanduloso-punctata; pagina inferior purpurea (minimum foliorum infimorum) pilulosa vel parce puberula parce glanduloso-punctata; venae coloratae, infra interdum parum elevatae; petioli 5-15 mm longi, folii laminam versus alati. Inflorescentia ad 2.5 cm lata e fasciculo parvo capitulorum sessilium constata; ramuli (si adsunt) plerumque elongati puberuli vel pilosi; bracteae majores foliaceae, bracteae minores squamiformes inconspicuae. Capitula 7-9 mm alta per anthesin, sessilia vel sub- sessilia in gregibus globosis vel hemisphaericis portata; involucra 5-6 mm longa purpurea anguste campanulata, phyllariis linearibus 5-6 mm longis 0.6-1.0 mm latis glabris subglabrisve, apice acutis vel acuminatis. Corollae 3.5-5.0 mm altae per anthesin, purpureae; lobi ca. 0.8 mm longi, puberuli; fauces cum tubo 3.0-4.5 mm longae glabrae vel sparsim puberulae. Achenia isomorpha exaristata 2.5-3.7 mm longa, sparsim hispida (fere glabra) fusca; pappus e corona squamellarum constans, squamellis integris vel serratis 0.2-0.4 mm altis.
bibliographicCitation: Grashoff, Jerold L. 1974. Novelties in Stevia (Compositae: Eupatorieae). Brittonia. 26: 347-384.

description: Annual branched herbs of moist areas with decumbent rooting lower nodes, ca. 1.5 to 3.0 dm high but capable of flowering when only 0.5 dm tall; stems dark reddish-brown, striate, hispid; leaves sessile, mostly ovate, up to 2 cm long, 1 cm wide, hirsute, apices acute, bases obtuse, margins essentially entire; peduncles hirsute, densely so near the slightly flared apex, very slender, ca. 1/3 the diameter of the subtending internode, up to 7 cm long; heads subglobose, ca 3 mm high, 3.5 mm wide in larger specimens; phyllaries 8-10, uniseriate, hirsute, linear, more or less flat dorsally, up to 2.5 mm long and somewhat discolored at the acute to obtuse apex; alae often rudimentary or wanting; rays when lacking replaced by tubular disk florets, but if present, bright yellow, ca 3 mm long, broadly ovate, mostly 2-lobed at apex, lobelets sometimes developing at the 0.3 mm tube; ray achenes 1 mm long, turbinate, obscurely striate; disk flowers numerous, the corolla ca. 1 mm long, yellow, the leaves 0.3 mm abruptly constricted and hirsute, disk achenes turbinate, terete to 4-5-angled, ca. 1 mm long; outermost paleae linear, hyaline, acuminate at apex, more or less flat or curved and incompletely enclosing the achenes, the inner more slender, all paleae black-tipped or not, more or less persistent; receptacle conical; 2n = 36.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1968. Revision of Jaegeria (Compositae--Heliantheae). Brittonia. 20: 52-73.

description: Trees, to 10 m. Leaves with petioles 10-20 cm long, densely tomentose; blade widely elliptic-ovate, obovate-oblong or ovate-oblong, 25-70 X 11-46 cm, papery, base deeply cordate, apex rounded or obtuse, abaxial surface tomentose, adaxial surface grabrous except for the tomentose midrib, reticulate veined with 7-8 secondary veins in each side of the midrib, margins almost entire with minute callous teeth. Capitules-cences thyrsoid-paniculate. Capitula homogamous, discoid, involucre cylindrical, phyllaries 5, uniseriate, subcoriaceous, oblong, 6-7 X 2.2-3.2 mm, glabrescent, apex obtuse or subacute, ciliate. Florets 5, hermaphroditic, corolla ca. 9 mm long, tube 3.5-4 mm long, limb ca. 5 mm long, lobes linear, ca. 4.5 mm long, apex acute; anthers ca. 3 mm long, base sagittate, caudate, terminal appendage lanceolate, acute; style branches with the apex acute, dorsally pilose. Achenes oblong, ca. 3 mm long; pappus, 8 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Correa, A. 2003. Revision of the genus Paragynoxys (Asteraceae, Senecioneae-Tussilagininae). Brittonia. 55: 157-168.

description:
Rami terminales teretes dense tomentosi. Folia alterna chartacea rigida magna petiolo 10-20 cm. longo flexuoso satis verrucoso dense tomentoso. Lamina late elliptico-ovata vel ovato-oblonga, basi profunde cordata, apice rotundata vel obtusissima, margine visu integra sed minutis remotisque dentibus subobsoletis munita, 50-70 cm. longa 32-46 cm. lata; in supremis foliis minor (25-30 cm. longa) basi rotundata brevior emarginata; supra glabra costa tomentosa excepta,nervis secundariis notatis reticulo venoso prominulo; subtus viridi-pallida dilute molliterque tomentella, costa crassa eminenti verruculosa densior tomentosa, nervis lateralibus 7-8 utroque latere valde prominentibus subascendentibusque furcatisque prope marginem reticulato-anastomosantibus, nerviis tertiis tenuibus laxe reticulatis.

Inflorescentia magna thyrsoideo-paniculata, ultra 40 cm. longa inferne foliata, axi robusto lanuginoso-tomentoso sparseque verruculoso, ramis ramulisque patulis flexuosis tomentosis bracteolis lineari-lanceolatis acutis 10-3 mmn. longis munitis. Pedicelli vulgo 2-3 mm. longi, teneres tomentelli 2-4 bracteolis anguste lanceolatis parce puberulis ad apicem 1-2 ad modum calyculi.

Capitula discoidea, involucro cylindraceo 6.5-7 mm. alto 5 bracteis sub-coriaceis violascentibus oblongis, apice obtusiusculis vel subacutis ciliatisque, dorso parcissime puberulis vel glabris, 6-7 mmr. longis 2.2-3.2 mm. latis. Flores 5 omnes hermaphroditi; corolla glabra tubulo 3.5-4 mm. longo, limbo laciniato lobis linearibus 4.5-5 mm. longo; antheris 3 mm. longis basi sagittatis. Rami styli longi contorti extus pubescentes ad apicem paulo dilatati acuti. Ovarium glabrum, leviter striatum. Pappus stramineus 8 mm. longus, setis rigidis stri- gosis biseriatis.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1955. Studies in Tropical American Leguminosae-II. Brittonia. 8 (2): 113.

description: Plants annual, 15-60 cm high; stems erect, the lower portion pubescent witb short appressed white hairs only, the upper portion and the inflorescence densely pubescent with both appressed and erect, gland-tipped hairs, the latter 0.25-0.4 mm long; lower leaves simple and opposite, the upper ones trifoliate and alternate (leaves rarely with 5 leaflets), all pubescent with scattered appressed white hairs; mid-stem leaves with petioles 1-3 cm long; leaflets broadly to narrowly ovate, 0.4-2 cm wide, 2-6 cm long, entire, (2-) 3-12 times as long as wide, broadly to narrowly acute at the apex; infloreseence a subcorymbose eyme with 5 to numerous heads; heads broadly turbinate, 4-7 mm across, 5-8 mm high, (10-) 15-25-flowered, on peduncles 5-25 mm long; principal involueral bracts 8-14, 4-7 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, with white membranous margins (very rarely somewhat reddish), broadly obtuse or rounded at the apex, pubescent with appressed hairs to nearly glabrous; florets white, distinctly zygomorphic; corolla 4-5 mm long, the tube glandular-pubescent, 1-1.5 mm long, the throat flaring, 2.5-3 mm long (including the lobes), the lobes of different lengths, 0.5-2 mm long; style branches flattened, 1.5-2 mm long, with well-defined stigmatic lines, abruptly terminated by a penicillate, cuspidate appendage, otherwise glabrous; achenes (3-) 4-5 (-6) mm long, obpyramidal, 4-sided, densely to sparsely pubescent with appressed hairs; pappus of 8-10 scales, 0.3-2 mm long, broadly rounded to truncate at the apex, without terminal awns or mucros; chromosome number, n = 10.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1963. Taxonomy of Forestina (Helenleae, Compositae). Brittonia. 15: 27-46.

description: Frutex glaber; ramulis acute pluriangularibus; laminis ovatis vel ellipticis, coriaceis lucidis, valde reticulato- venosis, subtus glanduloso-punctatis vel sparse glanduloso-strigulosis, margini- bus crenato-serratis; pedunculis monocephalis; capitulis radiatis, majusculis; involucris late companulatis vel hemisphaericis, bracteis involucri imbricatis, graduatis, interioribus oblongis, vittiatis, late scariosis, ciliatis; palliis lineari. bus vel lineari-oblanceolatis, induratis; ligulis luteis, striatis, glandulosis; tubis disci florum cylindricis; paliis pappi lineari-lanceolatis acutis, scariosis, laceratis.

description: Shrub to 1.5 m. high, essentially glabrous throughout; branches sharply multi-angled, internodes 0.5-4.0 cm. long, leaves opposite, sessile, subsessile, or with petioles as much as 3 mm. long; blades 2.5-6.0 cm. long, (1.5) 2.0-4.0 cm. broad, ovate to elliptic, obtuse, coriaceous, upper surface conspicuously lucidous, the lower surface glandular-punctate or very sparingly glandular-strigulose, margins crenate, serrate, the teeth terminating in blunt callouses, lateral veins conspicuous, decurrent along the midrib, freely anastomosing and reticulate; peduncle stout, monocephalous 1-2 cm. long, heads closely subtended by one or  two pairs of small leaf-like bracts; heads large, broadly campanulate, to hemi- spheric 1.0-1.5 cm. long, 1.5-1.75 cm. broad exclusive of the ligules, involucral bracts indurate, imbricate, graduated in about 5 series, the lowermost about 5 mm. long, cucullate, the innermost becoming 12-14 mm. long, oblong, conspicuously vittiate, broadly scarious, ciliate; palea at length indurate, somewhat infolded, 5-8 mm. long, linear to linear-oblanceolate, 2-3 toothed or lacerate at apex; ligules yellow 18-20 mm. long, 2-4 mm. broad, entire or 2-3 toothed, striate, sessile-glandular; disc flowers about 7 mm. long, the tube 2.0-2.5 mm. long, the limb 4-5 mm. long, cylindric, the teeth about 1 mm. long, erect, triangular; achenes 2.5-3.0 mm. long, sharply angled, the pappus palea 5-7, 1-3 mm. long, linear-lanceolate, sharply acute, scarious, somewhat lacerate.
bibliographicCitation: Lasser, Tobias & Maguire, Bassett. 1950. A report on the plant of the Phelps Cerro Yaví expedition of 1947. Brittonia. 7: 75-90.

description:
Ex affinitate S. elatioris H.B.K. et S. decumbentis (Robins. & Greenm.) Greene, sed foliis sessilibus subglabris caulibus brevibus erectis capitulis grandibus distincta.

Herba perennis rhizomatosa ad 0.5 m alta. Caules erecti solitarii vel pauci usque ad inflorescentiam simplices, minute stipitato-glandulosi et puberuli, rufi; internodia principalia laminis foliorum 1-2-plo longiora; internodia inferna breviora et mox defoliata, internodia superna elongata. Folia opposita sessilia ovata triplinervia 2.5- 3.7 cm longa 1.5-2.5 cm lata, crenata, apice obtusa, basi obtusa subconnata, axillis prolificantibus; superficies vivide viridis, glabra subglabrave sed minute stipitato- glandulosa prope marginem, glanduloso-punctata; pagina inferior pallidior sed saepe ex parte rufo suffusa, stipitato-glandulosa ad marginem et secus aliquot venas, cetero glabra subglabrave. Panicula laxa terminalis 8-15 cm lata altaque; ramuli dichotomi minute stipitato-glandulosi rufo-purpurei; bracteae foliaceae integrae vel subintegrae primariae ovatae et conspicuae, secundariae lineari-lanceolatae et minutae; pedunculi ad 16 mm longi stipitato-glandulosi. Capitula singulatim portata, 12-13 mm alta per anthesin; involucra cylindrica stipitato-glandulosa rufo-purpurea, phyllariis lanceolato-oblongis ca. 8.5 mm longis 1.5 mm latis, apice acutis vel breviter acumi- natis. Corollae aliquantum zygomorphae ca. 6 mm longae per anthesin; lobi 1.8-2.5 mm longi albi vel pallidissime lavanduli pubescentes; fauces 4 mm longae purpureae subglabrae et glandulosae; tubus 2 mm longus purpureus, basin versus viridulus, glandulosus. Achenia heteromorpha ca. 4.5 mm longa pappo excluso hispida nigra; pappus adelphocarpiorum triaristatus, aristis 7 mm longis, alatis ba,sin versus, purpureis juventute, bubalinis maturitate, et 3 squamellis 0.7 mm longis dentatis pellucidis alternantibus; pappus idiocarpii singularis e corona squamellarum constans, squamellis 0.7 mm altis conjunctis dentatis pellucidis.
bibliographicCitation: Grashoff, Jerold L. 1974. Novelties in Stevia (Compositae: Eupatorieae). Brittonia. 26: 347-384.

description: Annual or biennial, 1-4 dm. high, erect, or sometimes decumbent nlear the base, with an evident main axis; stem moderately short-hirsute, the hairs near the base spreading, those near the top appressed; leaves larger and broader than those of E. modestus, sparsely to moderately hirsute, the basal ones oblanceolate to suborbicular, the blades mostly 1-3 cm. long, 5-15 mm. wide, occasionally a little larger, entire or irregularly toothed to shallowly and irregularly lobed, tapering or abruptly contracted to petioles 1-3 cm. long, sometimes deciduous before flowering time, middle cauline leaves mostly narrowly oblong or a little broader, sessile, entire or somewhat toothed, mostly 1.5-4 cm. long anid 3-10 mm. wide, occasionally a little larger or smaller; heads 1-many in an open inflorescence, the disk 5-10 mm. wide; involucre about 2.5-4 mm. high, nearly. glabrous to moderately hirsute with curved hairs, and sometimes a little viscid or finely glandular; phyllaries subequal, or the outer a little narrower and shorter, the midrib and lower part brown or dark green, the tip searious; upper part of phyllaries commonly somewhat expanded and very thin, but not always so; ligules about 60-120, blue or white, 2.5-4.5 mm. long, 0.3-0.5 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 2.0-2.7 mm. long, the tube 0.4-0.5 mm. long, the lobes about 0.3 mm. long, style-appendages broadly triangular, obtuse, about 0.05 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about a dozen fragile bristles, the outer of short setae; akenes 2-nerved, or occasionally obscurely 4-nerved, sparsely pubescent.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herba crassa, caudice ad 2 m. alto; foliis et ramis floriferis summo dense arctatis, indumento arete tomentoso aureo vel aureo-canescente indutis; foliis oblongo-spathulatis, ad 30 cm. longis et 3.5 cm. latis, basin versus ad 10-15 mm. angustatis, ad vaginam dilatatis, apice obtusis, nervis omnino obscuratis et in foliis coriaceis immersis; ramis floriferis ad 70 cm. longis, inflorescentia 10-25-capitulata corymboso-paniculata ad 30 cm. longa, ramis inflorescentiae bracteis oblongis obtusis 4—7 cm. longis et 1-1.5 cm. latis subtentis; capitulis maturitate 20-25 mm. diametro, pedunculis ad 5 cm. longis; involucro ut videtur 2-seriato, phyllaribus 10-15 subaequalibus papyraceis deltoideo-ovatis, 11-13 mm. longis, 5-7 mm. latis, apice acutis vel subacuminatis, extra laxe aureo-tomentosis intus glabris; floribus radii circiter 70 circiter 3-seriatis, lamina oblonga, 12-14 mm. longa, 1.5 mm. lata, prope basin pilos stramineos adscendentes 1.5 mm. longos gerente, achenio obovato-trigono; floribus disci medio hispidis circiter 9 mm. longis, tubo quam limbo paullo breviore, lobis deltoideis subacutis circiter 1 mm. longis; staminibus circiter 6 mm. longis, filamentis quam antheris paullo longioribus; stylo leviter exserto; paleis stramineis subcoriaceis oblongo-lanceolatis, circiter 9 mm. longis et 2 mm. latis, apice obtusis, extra minute pulverulentis (apicem versus breviter hispidulis) intus glabris.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Koch, M. A. 1935. The genus Espeletia: a study in phylogenetic taxonomy. Brittonia. 1: 479-530. pl. 1, 2 + f. 1-5.

description: Perennial, 5-10 cm. high; stem and leaves conspicuously spreading-hirsute; basal leaves oblanceolate, acute or obtuse, tapering to short petioles or subsessile, the blade and petiole about 10-50 cm. long, 4 mm. wide or less; cauline leaves few, reduced, linear, about 1 mm. wide; peduncular hairs, and sometimes those farther down the stem, with black or purplish-black cross-walls near their bases; head solitary, the disk about 9-15 mm. wide; involuere about 5-8 mm. high, somewhat viscid or glandular, especially near the tip, and conspicuously villous or woolly with long hairs, some or all of which have black or purplish-black cross-walls at least near their bases, the hairs themselves generally appearing dirty white or grayish to the naked eye; phyllaries equal, slender, attenuate, loose, green to dark purplish black, some of the tips more or less recurved; ligules about 40-60, prominently 2-3-toothed at the apex, 9-12 mm. long, about 1.0-2.0 mm. wide, blue; disk-corollas about 3.7-5.0 mm. long, the lobes about 0.5-0.9 mm., the tube about 0.9-1.2 mm., the limb relatively broad; pappus double, the inner of 15-20 relatively firm bristles, the outer of a few inconspicuous setae; akenes villous-hirsute, 2-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Planta perennis 5-10 cm. alta caule et foliis patenti-hirsutis, foliis imis oblanceolatis 10-50 mm. longis usque ad 4 mm. latis, caulinis reductis linearibus, capitulis solitariis disco 9-12 mm. lato, involucro 5-8 mm. alto plus minusve viscidi-glandulosis (praesertim ad apicem) et perspicue villoso pilis longis parietibus transversis atropurpureis, bracteis tenebrosis laxis non imbricatis, ligulis ca. 40-60 caeruleis 9-12 mm. longis ca. 1.5 mm. latis, pappo duplici, corollis disci ca. 3.7-5.0 mm. longis, achaeniis villosis 2-nervis.

description: Rami volubiles paulo angulati striatique glabri. Folia alterna petiolata subcoriacea crassa. Petiolus 2-3 cm longus crassus basi magis incrassatus glaber. Lamina ovato-elliptica elongata vel oblongo. elliptica basi rotundata vel obutsa apice obtusa vel subite acutata margine plana integerrima, 13-17 cm longa 6.5-9.5 cm lata, costa supra paulo signata subtus crassa conspicua nervis lateralibus filiformibus immersis fere inconspicuis ceteris obsoletis. Inflorescentiae thyrsoideo-paniculatae axillares folia paulo excedentes axi robusto striato subrecto vel flexuoso tomentello sed basim versus glabrato, ramulis ascendentibus tomentellis, bracteis ovatis acutis vel ovato-lanceolatis basi late amplectentibus, 10-24 mm longis 5-12 mm latis puberulis margine lacerato-cilatis. Pedicelli 1-8 mm longi mediocriter puberulo-tomentelli sursum 4-6 bracteis lineari-lanceolatis tenuiter membranaceis 7-8 mm longis 1-1.5 mm latis levissime araneosis supeme ad modum calyculi involucrum subaequantibus dispositis. Capitula discoidea involucro campanulato 8-9 mm alto bracteis 12-13 herbaceis linearibus acutis 7-8 mm longis 1.5 mm latis margine scariosis dorso incrassatis, apice ciliatis ceteris subglabris tantum sparsis pilis araneosis ad basim magis congestis. Flores-radii 5-6 tubulosi feminei, corolla 5 mm longa, 5- dentata dentibus praecipue inaequalibus. Flores disci hermaphroditi circa 20, corolla lutea glabra 7 mm longa, tubulo 3 mm longo dentibus 1 mm, antheris 3 mm longis, ramnis stigmaticis truncatis papilloso-coronatis. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus 5 mm longus albus.

description: Frutex scandens usque ad 10 m altus. Folia 8-10 x 3.5-4.5 cm. Capitula 6-8-flora. Corollae albidae, 7-8 mm longae, glandulosae. Achaenia glandulosa, ca 5-6-nervia.
bibliographicCitation: Jones, Jr., Samuel B. & Stutts, John G. 1981. Three new species of Vernonia (Compositae: Vernonieae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 33: 544-546.

description: Scandent shrub; stems up to 10 m long, brown with prominent lenticels. Leaves cauline, spaced 2.5-3 cm apart; petioles 1.3-1.6 cm long, puberulent; blades 8-10 x 3.5-4.5 cm, elliptic, apically acuminate, basally cuneate, marginally strongly revolute with remote callous teeth, glabrate, with a few trichomes along major veins above, reticulate-veined, glandular-dotted and with a few dark trichomes below. Inflorescences paniculate-corymbose. Heads 6-8-flowered; peduncles 2-5 mm long, puberulent. Involucre campanulate, 7.5-8 x 3.5-4 mm. Phyllaries loosely appressed in ca 5 or 6 series, greenish tinged with purple along margins and with a dark green spot near apex; inner phyllaries soon deciduous, oblong, rounded to acute, 7.0-7.2 x 0.9-1.0 mm, the outer ones ovate, 1-2 x 0.7-0.9 mm. Pappus white, the inner bristles 4.5-5 mm, outer ones 1.2-2 mm long. Corollas 7-8 mm long, white, glandular. Anthers ca 4 mm long. Achenes 3-3.3 mm long, 5-6-ribbed, glandular, soon deciduous. Pollen type A. Flowering and fruiting from January to February.
bibliographicCitation: Jones, Jr., Samuel B. & Stutts, John G. 1981. Three new species of Vernonia (Compositae: Vernonieae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 33: 544-546.

description: Herba perennis erecta e radice tuberiformi fasciculataque orta, glabra, basi ramosa, 6-8 dm alta, caulibus gracilibus tantum ca 2-2.5 mm crassis, tetragonis, sulculatis, internodiis folia parce superantibus. Folia sessilia vel subsessilia, opposita, utroque jugo stellae simili, lamina supra viridi infra subbrunneo-purpurascenti, pinnata vel bipinnatisecta, 1.5-3 cm longa, pinnis usque ad 3 cm longis et 1-3.5 mm latis, subpedatifidis, segmentis ultimis supra obscure infra valde medianeque uninervatis, apice acerrimis induratisque, marginibus raro minutissime spinuloso-ciliatis. Inflorescentia exserta paniculato-corymbosa, ca 2- vel 3-capitulata; pedunculis gracillimis, rectis vel arcuatis, glabris, usque ad 1.4 dm longis et 0.2-0.6 mm crassis. Capitula radiata. pansa ad anthesin ca 3.7-4 cm lata et fere 1 cm alta. Involucri bracteae exteriores ca 10-12, anguste lineares, apice acutae, extus ca 5-7-purpureo-striatae, plus minusve patentibus, 5-7 mm longi, supra vix pulverulento-puberulae; interiores purpureo-striatae oblongae interdum paulo longiores. Flores ligulati atro-purpurascenti-rubri 7 vel 8, ligula obovata, 1.2-1.6 cm longa et 6-8 mm lata, longitudinaliter plurinervata nervis minute adpresseque albido-setulosis, apice orbiculato acerrime 3-denticulata. Paleae flavae anguste lineares superne attenuatae et flores tubulosos saepe superantes. Flores tubulosi flavi. Achaenia matura submaturaque non visa; ovariis minimis, ovalibus, biaristatis, aristis pauciter retrorso-barbellatis.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1964. Some new or otherwise noteworthy Coreopsidinae (Compositae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 18: 58-73.

description: Perennial herb, erect from a tuberiform and fascicled root, glabrous, basally branched, 6-8 dm tall; stems delicate, only ca 2-2.5 mm thick, quadrangulate, sulculate, the internodes scarcely surpassing the leaves. Leaves sessile or sub- sessile, opposite, each pair resembling a star; blade green above, brownish-purple beneath, pinnate or bipinnatiseet, 1.5-3 cm long; pinnae up to 3 cm long and 1-3.5 mm wide, subpedatifid, ultimate segments above obscurely beneath strongly and medianly 1-nerved, at apex very sharp and indurated, the margins rarely very minutely spinulose-ciliate. Inflorescence exserted, paniculate-corymbose, ca 2- or 3-capitulate; peduncles very delicate, straight or curved, glabrous, up to 1.4 dm long and 0.2-0.6 mm thick. Heads radiate, expanded at anthesis ca 3.7-4 cm wide and almost 1 cm tall. Outer phyllaries ca 10-12, narrowly linear, at apex acute, externally ca 5-7-purple-striate, more or less spreading, 5-7 mm lonig, toward apex scarcely pulverulent-puberulous; inner ones purple-striate and ob- long, at times a little longer. ILigulate florets dark-purple-red, 7 or 8; ligule obovate, 1.2-1.6 cm long and 6-8 mm wide, lengthwise several-nerved with inerves minutely and appressedly whitish-setulose, at apex orbiculate and very acultely 3-denticulate. Chaff-scales yellow, narrowly linear, attenuate above and often surpassing the disk-florets, these yellow. Neither mature nor suLbmature achenes seen; ovaries very minute, oval, biaristate, aristae scantily retrorse-barbellate.

description: Herba crassa, caudice ut videtur subterraneo; foliis papyraceis obovato-spathulatis, 25-40 cm. longis, 5-8 cm. latis, basin versus in petiolum 5-15 cm. longum anguste alatum dense albo-tomentosum attenuatis (vagina circiter 10 mm. lata), apice acutis, margine leviter crenulatis, supra fuscis, subtus arete canescente-strigosis, costa crassa supra plana subtus prominente, nervis secundariis numerosis rectis adscendentibus supra planis subtus elevatis, venulis copiose anasto-mosantibus; ramis floriferis crassissimis ad 100-capitulatis, e caudice erectis, ad 1 m. altis et 2 cm. diametro, parce albo-tomentosis, foliis caulis alternatis reductis; inflorescentia corymboso-paniculata, saepe 40 cm. longa et 30 cm. lata, ramulis bracteis oblongis acntis 3-8 cm. longis et 0.5-1.5 cm. latis subtentis, capitulis atropurpureis semiglo-bosis maturitate 1.5-2 cm. diametro; involucro 3-4-seriato, phyllaribns 80-100 lanceolato-oblongis, 8-12 mm. longis, 2-3 mm. latis, apice acntis, extra pilis 0.5-0.7 mm. longis dense strigosis; floribus radii   3-4-seriatis, corolla ad tubum minutum 1.5 mm. longum reducta, pilis rubidis circiter 0.5 mm. longis dense strigosa, stylo 3-3.5 mm. longo apicem versus bifido, achenio trigono 3-3.5 longo; floribus disci 6 mm. longis, apice dense atropurpureo-strigosis, tubo pallido-strigoso quam limbo breviore, lobis oblongo-deltoideis 1.5 mm. longis; staminibus exsertis, filamentis quam antheris longioribus; stylo exserto; paleis obovato-oblongis, circiter 6.5 mm. longis et 2 mm. latis, apice acutis, extra apicem versus atropurpureo-strigosis.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Koch, M. A. 1935. The genus Espeletia: a study in phylogenetic taxonomy. Brittonia. 1: 479-530. pl. 1, 2 + f. 1-5.

description:
Ab omnibus congeneribus gypsophila obligata diversa; a T. incana flosculorum radiatorum brevium (4- 7.5, nec 7-13 mm) pappo aut nullo aut coroniformi e squamellis minutis constanti, et a T. fendleri habitu caespitoso-pulvinato, flosculorum disci pappo corollae aequilongo, foliisque oblanceolatis succulentis dense strigoso-canescentibus absimilis.

Gynomonoecious, caespitose or pulvinate, taprooted perennial, 2-10 cm tall, forming a stout woody caudex in mature plants; stems intricately branched, the lower portion subterranean and covered by over lapping persistent leaf bases, the aerial portions densely canescent; leaves narrowly oblanceolate, 8-20 (25) mm long, 1-3 mm wide, acute and mucronate, strigose-canescent to canescent basally, moderately succulent, the margin entire, slightly to strongly involute, the leaf base persistent; heads terminal and solitary or occasionally paniculate; peduncles 3-8 mm long, densely canescent; involucre turbinate or campanulate, 4-6 mm long, 3-6 mm wide; receptacle setose; phyllaries in 3-4 series, 2-4 mm long, 1.0-1.5 mm wide, lanceolate, acute, broadly scarious margined, never reflexed even in fruit, the margin prominently ciliate, the midrib strigose becoming canescent, basally thickened, appearing keeled in mature heads; ray florets (4) 7-15 (16), uniseriate, the co- rollas white or tinged with pink adaxially, striped with pink abaxially, 4.0-7.5 (7.8) mm long, the tube 1-2 (2.3) mm long, the lamina 3.0-5.5 mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm wide; disk corollas tubular, yellow or tinged with pink, 2.3-3.2 mm long, the lobes 0.5 mm long, papillate apically; cypselas oblanceolate, 2.3-2.5 mm long, 0.7-1.0 mm wide, com- pressed, the margins nerved, the faces nerveless, densely pubescent with glochidiate hairs in ray cypselas, less so in disk cypselas; pappus heteromorphic, that of the ray floret absent or coroniform of minute squamellae less than 0.3 mm long, that of the disk floret white, of barbellate bristles 2.3-3.2 mm long, equalling the disk corollas.
bibliographicCitation: Lowrey, Timothy K. & Knight, P. J. 1994. Townsendia gypsophila (Compositae: Astereae): A new species from northern New Mexico. Brittonia. 46: 194-199.

description: Planta ad 3 m alta; caulibus dense lanatis, infra glabratis; foliis infra oppo- sitis, supra alternis vel suboppositis; petiolis 1 cm longis; laminis ovatis vel ovato-lanceolatis, 7.0 cm longis, 3.0 cm latis, acuminatis, basi rotundatis vel cuneatis, crenato-serratis, supra viridibus, appresse pilosis, infra dense albido- tomentosis vel lanatis; capitulis 1-3; pedunculis 3-8 cm longis, disco ca. 2 cm diam.; phyllariis oblongis vel oblongo-lanceolatis, 1.1 cm longis, 3 mm latis albido-tomentosis vel lanatis; radiis 16-20, 1.5 cm longis, 7 mm latis; corollis disci flaviis, 7-10 mm longis, prope glabris; columnis antheris nigris; receptaculi paleis acuminatis, dense villosis dorso, apice nigris; achaeniis ca. 5 mm longis; pappi aristis 2, lanceolatis vel subulatis, ca. 2.5-3.5 mm longis, inaequalibus, profunde 3-cuspidatis sine squamellis, vel integris cum squamellis; pappo radiorum nullo.
bibliographicCitation: Heiser, Charles B. 1957. A revision of the South American Species of Helianthus. Brittonia. 8: 283-285.

description: Shrubs or small trees to 8 m tall; stems puberulent or glabrous; leaves ovate to rhombic-ovate, long-acuminate, sessile or with a winged petiole, the base of the ex- panded portion oblique or attenuate, the margin crenate or sinuate to entire; leaves glabrous above, puberulent or glabrous below; peduncles puberulent; phyllaries ovate to round-ovate, puberulent or minutely glandular, to 7 mm long and 5 mm wide; ray flowers ca 10, their corollas yellow, 6 mm long, 2-3 mm wide; disc flowers ca 4 mm long, the corollas yellow; ray paleae broadly ovate, 2 mm wide and 3 mm long; disc paleae ca 2 mm long, the margin denticulate above, the midvein prominent; achene black, obovoid, ca 3 mm long and 2 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Wells, James R. 1965. A taxonomic study of Polymnia (Compositae). Brittonia. 17: 144-159.

description: Outer involucral bracts 3-4, 4-6 mm long, connate 2/3-3/4 of their length, the inner set cuneate and truncate to rounded or oblanceolate with a short mucro 0.1-0.2 mm long, 3-3.3 mm long, scarious margins at apex broad and often irregular, erose; ray florets 3-4, the ligule 3-5 mm long, the tube sometimes sparsely puberulent; disk florets 10-13, the corollas 2.5-3.5 mm long, sparsely to moderately puberulent; pappus absent or scales 2-4, the scales 1- 2 mm long; achene hairs sparse, flexuous, 1.5-2.1 mm long, opaque, tan to white.
bibliographicCitation: Wagner, Warren L., et al. 1999. Another look at Hymenoxys subgenus Plummera (Asteraceae: Heliantheae: Gallardiinae) from Arizona and New Mexico. Brittonia. 51: 79-86.

description: Plants annual, 15-40 cm high, erect, branching, hirsute; leaves ovate-lanceolate, margins serrate to subentire, 3.2-6.5 cm long, 1.5-3.5 cm wide, sometimes trilobate, the lobes sublanceolate, acute or obtuse at the apex, cuneate-attenuate or somewhat decurrent at the base, sparsely appressed-hirsute on both surfaces; petioles 3-10 mm long; heads suburceolate, solitary on rather long, slender peduncles; penducles 5-14 cm long, puberulent and spreading-hirsute; receptacle convex to nearly flat, 2-3.5 mm across, 0.5-1.5 mm high; chaff persistent, subobovate, scarious, glabrous, 7-8 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide, with laciniate margins, abruptly narrowing at the apex, forming an awn-like beak, ca 2 mm long; involucre 2-seriate, the outer bracts acute-attenuate and generally reflexed (subsquarrose), 6-8 mm long, (3.5-)4-5 mm wide, broadly ovate, with 2, usually spreading, linear-lanceolate bracts alternating with the broader ones, conspicuously hirsute or puberulent; inner bracts 8-10 mm long, broader than the outer, brownish-purple, sparsely pubescent; ray flowers ca 6, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 4-4.5 mm, with short yellow ligules, these 3.5-4 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, conspicuously 3-lobed at the, apex; ray corollas with 2 hyaline, linear, inner lobelets, these ca 1 mm long; pappus of the ray florets shorter than that of the disc, ca 2 mm long; disc corollas pale yellow, 5.5-6.5 mm long, the tube glabrous, 1.5-1.8 mm long, gradually passing into the throat, the throat tubular below, funnelform above, puberulent, 3.5-3.8 mm long, the lobes lanceolate, ca 1 mm long; style branches slender, rather flattened, ca 1.2 mm long, revolute, brownish, minutely pubescent beneath and near the subulate tip; achenes blackish-brown, subturbinate to narrowly obconical, 3-3.5 mm long, obscurely to rather distinctly ridged or sulcate, slightly flattened tangentially, densely short-pilose or tomentose; pappus of 20 subequal, slender, plumose bristles 2.5-3.5 mm long, brownish below, whitish above, the cilia short, silky; anthers 1.8-2 mm long, obscurely sagittate at the base.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, William L. & Zamuco, Isidro T. 1965. Identify of 'Tinong' (Dipterocarpaceae). Brittonia. 17: 35-46.

description: Herbae 1-5 dm altae. Folia cum 9-15 lobis pinnatifida, glandulis instructa. Capitula numerosa, 3-5-glomerata; pedunculi 1-2 cm longi. Involucra 10-12 mm alta. Phyllaria 5-6, ad apices versus purpurata, acuminata. Ligulae 5-6, inconspicuae, ca. 1.5 mm longae. Discorum corollae ca. 25, 4.5-5.0 mm longae. Pappus 5-6 mm longus, fulvus. Achaenia 5-6 mm longa, fusca.
bibliographicCitation: Strother, John L. 1968. Vilobia, a new genus (Compositae-Tageteae). Brittonia. 20: 343-345.

description: Glabrous annuals, 1.5-5.0 dm high, erect, diffusely branched from the base, the stems striate. Leaves at first opposite, becoming alternate, mostly 2-4 cm long, pinnately parted into 9-15 slender, sparsely toothed, opposite to subopposite lobes, the latter 8-15 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, bearing small, pellucid glands along the margins and especially at the base of each lobe. Heads, erect, pedunculate in loose clusters of 3-5 at the tips of branches; peduncles slender, striate, 1-2 cm long, naked or bearing a single foliaceous bract. Involucre open, campanulate-turbinate, 10-12 mm high, ca. 7 mm diam., the lower 2/3 greenish, indurate, the upper 1/3 purplish, moderately scarious. Phyllaries 5 (-6), connate ca. 4/5 their length, streaked with numerous linear glands ca. 1 mm long, 0.1 mm wide; apices of phyllaries tipped with a hispidulous, acuminate appendage. Receptacle convex, naked but for the shallow, laciniate margined sockets. Ray florets 5 (-6), pistillate, fertile; corollas pale yellow, inconspicuous; tube slender, ca. 5 mm long, sparsely pubescent on the upper half, the limb ovate-orbicular, ca. 1.5 mm long. Disc florets ca. 25, hermaphrodite, fertile; corollas pale yellow, 4.5-5.5 mm long, slender; tube and throat about equal, the latter sparsely hispidulose; lobes 5, equal, narrow-deltoid, scarcely 1 mm long, bordered by thick nerves originating below the sinuses. Anthers 5, ca. 0.8 mm long, the tips lanceolate, ca. 0.3 mm long. Style branches long, slender, bearing a short, papillate, conical appendage. Pappus of 10 + equal squamellae in 2 series, each squamella bearing a long central awn (slightly surpassing the disc corolla) flanked by 2-4 shorter ones, 1 or 2 additional, much reduced, 1-awned scales often present. Achenes 5-6 mm long, very slender, weakly 4-5-angled, finely striate, bearing short appressed hairs mostly along the angles.
bibliographicCitation: Strother, John L. 1968. Vilobia, a new genus (Compositae-Tageteae). Brittonia. 20: 343-345.

description: Stem stout, usually simlple to inflorescence, or with laterals beginning near the mid-stem, glabrous to hirtellous, 0.7-2 m high, generally light-green, yellow-green or light-red in color; leaves narrowly lanceolate to ovate, often opposite to mid-stem and becoming alternate near the top, stiffish, generally 10-20 cm long, 1.5-3 cm wide, variable, the upper surfaces with m-any short hairs, the lower with more abundant short hairs, the margins entire to distinctly serrate, variable, glossy green, pale green or gray-green in color, the lower surfaces somewhat lighter than upper, the petioles absent or obscure or distinct, 0.5-2 cm long; phyllaries 1-1.2 cm long, usually glabrous or with scattered hairs, the margins ciliate, often conspicuously so, rarely eciliate; heads in terminal racemes, usually spreading panicles, peduncles variable 1-5 cm long, scabrous towards top. Florets of disk 1-1.4 cm long, the corolla puberulous near base; chaff 3-cuspidate, often pubescent near the tips.
bibliographicCitation: Long, Robert W. 1966. Biosystematics of the Helianthus nuttallii complex (Compositae). Brittonia. 18: 64-79.

description: Perennial herb resembling E. ursinus in caudex and general habit; stem about 5-20 cm. high, sparsely or moderately strigose, the curved base purplish, but not always so strongly so as in E. ursinus; leaves sparsely or moderately hirsute- strigose, occasionally glabrate except for the ciliate margins, the basal ones oblanceolate or linear-oblanceolate, acute, up to about 6 cm. long aind 4 mm. wide; cauline leaves several, much reduced, mostly linear, acuminate; head soli- tary, the disk about 10-15 mm. wide; involucre 5-7.5 mm. high, strigose or strigose-hirsute with appressed or slightly loose hairs, only obscurely if at all viscid or glandular; phyllaries narrow, green or yellowish green, with an evident brown midvein, sometimes loose at the tips, usually not purplish, often somewhat imbricate; ligules about 40-100, mostly rather light blue, or pink-purple, about 7-14 mm. long and 0.8-1.3 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.1-5.6 mm. long, the tube about 1.0-1.4 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm., the limb narrow; style-appendages triangular-lanceolate, or a little narrower than deltoid, acute, 0.25-0.4 mm. long; pappus of about 14-21 slender but not excessively fragile bristles, commonly with a few slender and obscure outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, short-hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: V. salviniae simulans sed capitulis multo minoribus, phyllariis valde squarrosis apice cordatis glaucis utrinque pubescentibus.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1981. New species and combinations in Vernonia sections Leiboldia and Lepidonia (Asteraceae), with a revisional conspectus of the groups. Brittonia. 33: 401-412.

description: Shrubs 2-3 m tall, the foliage and young stems densely ferruginous-pubescent. Leaves narrowly elliptical, broadest at the middle, 4-7 (11) cm wide, 15-25 cm long; blades sparsely pubescent above, more densely so below, the margins re- motely denticulate to nearly entire; petioles densely pubescent, 3-5 cm long. Heads 3-8 in a terminal capitulescence. Involucre hemispheric, 10-12 mm high, 12-16 mm across; receptacle convex, glabrous, alveolate, florets ca 100; bracts graduated in 6-8 series, all of them squarrose or nearly so; the lower portion linear, cartilaginous, shiny and glabrous, the upper broadly ovate, acute, glaucous, pubescent both within and without with rather evenly spaced short, spreading hairs. Florets "light purple"; corolla atomiferous glandular, somewhat zygomorphic, 12-14 mm long, the lobes 2-3 mm long; tube gradually merging into an indistinct throat, 2-3 mm wide. Achenes 4-5-sided, ca 2 mm long, glabrous, the faces ribless or nearly so. Pappus tawny, of numerous, intergrading, delicate, caducous, flattened bristles 1-4 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1981. New species and combinations in Vernonia sections Leiboldia and Lepidonia (Asteraceae), with a revisional conspectus of the groups. Brittonia. 33: 401-412.

description: Plants perennial, 40-55 cm high, erect, sparsely hirsute and with glandular trichomes; leaves ovate to ovate-lanceolate or linear, 4.5-12 cm long, 1.5-3 cm wide, unevenly serrate to tri- to pinnately lobed or divided, attenuate at the apex, cuneate at the base, sparsely appressed hirsute on both surfaces; petioles 1-2 cm long, inflorescence weakly paniculate (the heads rarely single or few); heads campanulate, 8-13 mm in diameter; peducles 3-6(-12) cm long, sparsely hirsute and with glandular trichomes, especially near the heads; receptacle conical, 2-3 (-4) mm across, 1.5-3.0(-4) mm high; chaff persistent, subovate, scarious, glabrous, 7.5-10 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, tapering to a rounded apex, or attenuate, awn-like beak; involucre 4-5-seriate, the outer bracts oblong, striate, light green or tan, 2.5-4 mm long, 1-1.5(-2.5) mm wide, evenly puberulent and with short, glandular trichomes, these mostly near the rounded or obtuse apex, the margins ciliate; inner bracts progressively longer, the longest 7-9(-11) mm long, 2-3(-4) mm wide, oblong (rarely subobovate), partially purple or only so near the apex, the margins ciliate, short-pubescent and with glandular trichomes especially near the rounded (rarely obtuse) apex; ray flowers 6-8, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base for 4-5(-6) mm, with conspicuous white or roseate ligules, these 10-15 mm long, (4-)10-16 mm wide, broadly obovate to suborbicular, subtruncate to obscurely lobed at the apex; ray corollas with inner lobelets poorly developed or obsolete (rarely pronounced); disc corollas greenish-yellow, 5.5-6.5(-7) mm long, the tube almost as wide as the throat, 2.2-2.5 mm long, densely pilose, the throat tubular, 2-3 mm long, pilose at the base, the lobes lanceolate, ca 1.5 mm long, obtuse to acute, subinvolute; style branches rather broad and flattened, ca 1.5 mm long, recurved, blackish-brown, coarsely pubescent, especially at the subulate tip; achenes blackish to brownish, narrowly obconical to subturbinate, 3-3.5(-4) mm long, densely long pilose-hirsute; pappus of 11-20 unequal, linear-lanceolate fimbriate scales (rarely with minute plumose bristles), 1.5-3 mm long, the inner scales slightly broader and longer than the outer; anthers 3-3.8 mm long, sagittate at the base.

description: Perennial herbs from a horizontal caudex; stems canescent. Leaves cauline, sessile, (5.2) 6-7 (9.4) cm long, 2.2-4.5 cm wide, ovate or ovate-lanceolate to ovate-oblong, widest at or below the middle, apically acute, basally cordate to rounded, marginally revolute and remotely callous toothed, dark green and pilose-villous above, canescent to white-tomentose beneath. Inflorescences somewhat compact, bracteate and paniculate-cymose. Heads (7) 9-10 (11)-flowered, sessile. Involucre narrowly campanulate, 7-8 (9.5) mm high, 4-5.6 (6) mm wide; phyllaries loosely imbricated in ca 5 series, tomentose, the inner ones oblong-lanceo- late, acuminate, 6-7 (7.8) mm long, 1.1-1.5 (1.8) mm wide, the outer ones ovate-lanceolate, (1.4) 2.2-3 mm long, 0.8-1.4 mm wide. Pappus straw-colored, the inner bristles 5-6.5 mm long and outer bristles somewhat flattened 1.5-2.5 mm long. Corollas 6-8 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers 2.4-3 mm long. Achenes 1.5-2.2 mm long, pilose-strigose. Flowering and fruiting from March to July.

description: Frutex, ramulis densissime patenti-pilosis; folia ovata acunluinata basi cuneata serrata papyracea longe petiolata supra asperula subtus submolliter pubescentia; capitula minuscula approximata; phyllaria 3 late ovata acuta ciliolata sub apice sparse hirsutula 5-7-nervia; receptaculum intra flores fem. nudum; fl. fem. 3, hermaph. 4; achenia late ovalia basi rotundata apice hirsutula.
bibliographicCitation: Blake, Sidney F. 1937. New Asteraceae from Guatemala and Costa Rica Collected by A. F. Skutch. Brittonia. 2 (4): 329 -361.

description: "Brittle-stemmed shrub 4.5 m. (15 ft.) high"; branches brownish- gray, subterete, 3 mm. thick, densely short-spreading-pilose, glabrescent, their upper internodes 1-4 cm. long; branchlets of the year very densely short-griseous-pilose; leaves opposite; petioles similarly pubescent, slender, 2-4.5 cm. long; blades ovate, 9-16 cm. long, 3-6.5 cmn. wide, falcate-acuminate, acutely cuneate at base, acutely serrate or serrulate mainly above the subentire cuneate base (teeth about 13-19 pairs, acutely callous-pointed, 0.5-3 mm. high, 2-9 mm. apart), papery, above deep or grayish green, not shining, evenly but not densely rough- ish-hispidulous with mostly deciduous hairs with small persistent tuberculate bases, more densely so along the veins and there short- hispid, beneath griseous, densely and rather softly spreading-pilose along the costa and chief veins and more sparsely so on veinlets and surface, triplinerved 7-25 mm. above the base and loosely prominulous- reticulate beneath; panicles densely many-headed, pubescent like the stem, flattish or somewhat convex, 4-7 cm. wide, subtended by not at all reduced leaves, their bracts lanceolate, minute; heads in flower cylindric-oblong, 5 mm. high, 2 mm. thick, in youn g fruit obovoid, 4-4.5 mm. high, 2.5-3 mm. thick; phyllaries 3, broadly ovate to suborbicular-ovate, 3.3-4.5 mm. long, 2.5-3.8 mm. wide, acutely callous- pointed, ciliolate below the tip, sparsely hirsutulous on back above, with 5-7 chief nerves (the inner with about 4 additional weaker nerves); pales of pistillate flowers suborbicular-ovate, obtuse or obtusish, 3.5-4 mm. long, somewhat ciliolate, 3-5-nerved; pistillate corollas white, unequally 3-toothed, glabrous, 2.2 mm. long; hermaphrodite corollas white, densely hispidulous at apex, 3.3 mm. long; achenes broadly oval, lenticular, rounded at base, hirsutulous at apex, 2.2 mm. long, 1.8 mm. wide; ovaries of hermaphrodite flowers linear, deinsely pilose especially toward apex, 2.6 mm. long.

description: Plants annual (or biennial), 30-70 cm high; stems erect, striate, 1 or rarely 2 from a single tap root, glabrous; lower leaves pinnately twice or thrice dissected, the upper less so, the earliest ones forming a rosette, but subsequent ones conspicuously alternate; mid-stem leaves glabrous (rarely minutely puberulent), dissected, the ultimate divisions linear or spatulate-linear, 5-40 mm long, 1.5-4 mm wide; petioles 15-50 mm long; inflorescence a subcorymbose eyme of 20-numerous heads; heads turbinate, 3-4 mm wide, 6-8 mm long ineluding the projecting florets, 12- to 20-flowered, on glabrous peduncles 3-10 mm long; principal involucral bracts linear-lanceolate to ovate, 4-5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, glabrous with greenish-white, membranous margins, acute at the apex; disc florets "creamy white" or "lemon-yellow," indistinctly zygomorphic, corolla 5-5.5 mm long (ineluding the lobes); tube 2-2.5 mm long, the lobes of slightly different lengths, the throat tubular, 2.5-3 mm long, about twice as wide as the tube; ray flowers small, creamy white to yellowish, the ligules 4-5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide; style branches cylindric, 1 mm long, abruptly obtuse at the apex and terminated by a minutely pubescent small cone; achenes obpyramidal, 4- sided, 3.5-4 mm long, minutely puberulent to nearly glabrous; pappus of 14-18 linear-lanceolate paleaceous scales 3.5 mm long, the mid-nerve of each forming an awn 1-3 mm long at the apex; chromosome number, n=12 (Fig. 1).
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1962. Taxonomy of Hymenothriz (Helenicae, Compositae). Brittonia. 14: 101-120.
