description: Herba ut videtur perennis, glabra, 15-20 cm. alta, sursum leviter ramosa; foliis integris, radicalibus longe (2-4 cm.) graciliter petiolatis,, lanceolatis vel oblongo-lanceolatis, integris, lamina 2-3 cm. longa, 4-6 mm. lata, apiculato-acuminata, basi cuneata, submembranacea vel tenuiter chartacea, nervis primariis utrinque eirciter 3, distantibus, adscendentibus, gracilibus, subobscuris, arcuato-anastomosantibus, reticulis obsoletis; foliis caulinis paucis, radicalibus similimis sed minoribus, superioribus valde reductis, margine petioli deorsum dentes 5-7 linearis acuminatos ad 0.8 mm. longos adscendentes gerente, basi haud vel obscure amplexicaulibus; inflorescentiis laxe corymbosis, apertis, ramis primariis paucis, 5-8 cm. longis, paucifloris, capitulis gracilibus, 6-7 mm. longis, graciliter (1-1.5 mm.) pedunculatis, 5-floris; involueri bracteis paucis, exterioribus 3-4 ovatis vel oblongo-ovatis, 0.5-1 mm. longis, acutis vel acuminatis, interioribus 5 longioribus, linearibus, eirciter 5 mm. longis, 0.5 mm. latis, obtusis; floribus 5, flavidis, corolla 5.5-6 mm. longa, tubo gracili, 2.5 mm. longo, ligula oblonga, 3 mm. longa, 1 mm. lata, deorsum angustata, lobulis parvis, oblongis, 0.2 mm. longis; acheniis lanceolatis, 2.5-3 mm. longis, obscure eirciter 8-costatis, minutissime scaberulis vel subglabris, rostro 1.5 mm. longo, setis eirciter 20, albidis, 3 mm. longis.
bibliographicCitation: Merrill, Elmer D. 1941. Plants Collected on the Vernay-Cutting Expedition. Brittonia. 4 (1): 23-68.

description: Rhizomes conspicuously long, as much as 30 cm., 1.5-2.5 mm. thick, mostly unbranched, light yellow-brown, naked except for the reduced scales at the nodes; innovations occasionally produced at the rhizome tips; stems solitary, uibranched or occasionally branched below the middle, striate, coarse, 3.0(2.0)-5.0 mm. in diam., 2-9 dm. tall, variously pubescent or villous, becoming more or less densely glandular above; cauline leaves numerous 5 (4)-10 pairs, searcely reduced above, all sessile, or generally the lowermost petiolate, lanceolate to oblanceolate, the pubescence similar to but less conspicuous than that of the stems, the petioles connate by means of ocreae 1-5 cm. long; heads 5(3)-15, hemispheric-campanulate, 12-18 mm. high, the bracts biseriate, lanceolate, obtuse to acutish, conspicuously pilose at the tip; ligules usually pale, oblong, 15-18(20) mm. long, shallowly toothed; disc corollas tubular, occasionally broadly so, 7.5-11.2 mm. lonig, the tube 3.0-4.8 mm. long, the limb 4.5-6.4 mm. long, the collar usually inconspicuous; achenes (3.6)4-6 mm. long, slender, tapering toward the base, short hirsute and glandular to glabrate; annulus to tawny, -+ length of corolla, barbellate to subplumose, the setae 0.15-0.25 (0.30) mnm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Camp, Wendell H. & Gilly, Charles L. 1943. Part II: Systematic Treatment, [Arnica alpina-Arnica discoidea]. Brittonia. 4 (3): 405-457.

description: Frutices ramosi ca 3 m usque alti; caules velutini, spinosi; spinae axillares geminae, 3-5 mm longae. Folia alterna, brevissime petiolata; petioli 2-3 mm longi; laminae ellipticae, 3-4.5 cm longae, 1.5-2 cm latae, coriaceae, triplinerves, utrinque velutinae, margine integrae. Capitulescentiae axillares, ra- cemosae. Capitula ovoidea, sessilia, 7-9 mm alta, 5-6 mm lata; phyllaria ca 7-seriata, extima anguste ovata, 3-4 mm longa, 2-3 mm lata, coriacea, velutina, apice acuta vel obtusa, intima linearia, 7-8 mm longa, 1-1.5 mm lata, velutina. Flores 13-16, hermaphroditi; corollae tubulosae albidae, ca 5 mm longae; limbus quinquelobus; lobi ca 1.5 mm longi, velutini. Achaenia ca 2 mm longa, dense et longe fulvo-velutina; pappi setae plumosae, fulvae, ca 5.5 mm longi.
bibliographicCitation: Sagástegui Alva, Abundio & Dillon, Michael O. 1985. Four new species of Asteraceae from Peru. Brittonia. 37: 6-13.

description: Shrubs to 3 m tall, much-branched; stems terete, erect, velutinous, axillary spines paired, 3-5 mm long. Leaves alternate; petiole 2-3 mm long, velutinous; blade elliptic, 3-4.5 cm long, 1.5-2 cm wide, coriaceous, trinervate, both surfaces densely velutinous, basally acute, apically obtuse to rounded, mucronulate, the mucro 1-1.5 mm long, the margins entire. Capitulescences racemose on axillary branchlets, 3-8-headed, often glomerulate distally. Capitula discoid, sessile to subsessile, 5-7 mm high, 5-6 mm wide; involucre cylindrical to narrowly campanulate at maturity; phyllaries ca 7-seriate, the outer narrowly ovate, 3-4 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, coriaceous, velutinous, ciliolate, apically obtuse, spinulose, the inner linear to lanceolate, 7-8 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, coriaceous, velu- tinous, apically acute to obtuse, spinulose; receptacle planar, epaleate; florets 13-16, hermaphroditic, the corollas whitish, tubular, ca 5 mm long, the limb pilose, actinomorphic, the 5 lobes ca 1.5 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, apically velutinous, the anthers ca 1.7 mm long, basally sagittate, the terminal appendage bifid, the style briefly divided apically, papillose. Achenes cylindrical, ca 2 mm long, sericeous to velutinous; pappus of plumose bristles, ca 5.5 mm long, yellowish- brown.
bibliographicCitation: Sagástegui Alva, Abundio & Dillon, Michael O. 1985. Four new species of Asteraceae from Peru. Brittonia. 37: 6-13.

description: Herbae perennes, rhizomatibus brevibus gracilibus. Radices rhizomatum fibrosae, suberosae, nigrae, ca. 1-2 mm diam. Radices adventitiae ad bases caulium filiformes. Caules teretes, puberuli vel pubentes, superne stipitato-glandulosi. Folia ad bases caulium subterraneia triangularia, sessilia, 2-3 mm longa, 2.0-2.5 mm lata. Folia partium aeriarum caulium opposita, petiolata. Laminae ovatae, crenatae vel serratae, 2.5-6.0 cm longae, 1.5-4.0 cm latae, apicibus acutis vel obtusis, basibus cuneatis, paginis superis parce et breviter hirsutis, paginis inferis pallidioribus, pubescentibus secus venas. Petioli alati laminas versus, 0.5-2.5 cm longi. Venae majores 3, divergentes, vix in pagina inferiore elevatae, venae minores manifeste reticulatae. Inflorescentiae laxe paniculatae, trifurcatae (raro bifurcatae), primo terminales, postea inflorescentiis secundariis lateralibus concomitatae. Pedunculi necnon rami in- florescentiarum stipitato-glandulosi. Phyllaria 5-6, ovato-oblonga, acuta vel obtusa ad apicem, 4-5 mm longa, 1.5 mm lata, paginis exterioribus stipitato-glandulosis et interdum purpurascentibus. Flosculi 4-6 (plerumque 5). Corollae albae, aliquantum zygomorphae. Fauces una cum tubo 3 mm longae, extra glabrae vel hirsutae, intra ad bases loborum sinuumque hirsutae. Lobi 2.0-3.5 mm longi, hirsuti. Rami stylorum papillati, non expansi ad apices; nodi stylorum leves, non amplificati. Appendices apicales antherarum 0.5 mm longae, obovatae, omnino e cellulis elongatis rectangularibus compositae. Achenia 2.5 mm longa, hispidula ad apices costis pallidioribus atra.
bibliographicCitation: Grashoff, Jerold L. 1975. Metastevia (Compositae: Eupatorieae): a new genus from Mexico. Brittonia. 27: 69-73.

description: Perennial herb with a simple or moderately branched caudex and an evident usually relatively slender taproot; stem short-hirsute with spreading hairs, purplish and sometimes curved at the base, erect or nearly so, 10-50 cm. high; leaves short-hirsute like the stem, the marginal hairs, particularly on the basal leaves, often longer thain the others, the margin thus becoming irregularly more or less ciliate; basal leaves evidently triple-nerved, elongate, linear-oblanceolate, clearly acute at the apex, tapering gradually to the petiole, up to 15 cm. long and 14 mm. wide; cauline leaves several or rather many, slightly or conspicuously reduced, linear or linear-lanceolate, acute, mostly not over 10 cm. long, 1-5 mm. (rarely 8 mm.) wide, some of the lower ones triple-nerved; heads 1-10, or sometimes 16, the disk 7-13 mm. wide; involuere mostly 5-7 mm. high, equaling the disk, caneseently villous-hirsute with short subappressed hairs, and glutinous or obscurely glandular, the somewhat imbricate phyllaries only slightly or obscurely thickened on the back, green or tan, with darker midrib and purplish usually close tips; ligules about 35-65, deep blue, or occasionally pink, 7-13 mm. long, 1.2-2.0 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.0-5.3 mm. longy occasionally only long, the tube 0.7-1.0 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm.; style-appendages triangularlanceolate to deltoid, acute, mostly 0.2-0.25 mm. long, sometimes only 0.15 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of 20-30 firm bristles, the outer of evident setae or narrow squamellae; akenes 2-nerved, more or less hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: A congeneribus, cespitosis, capituliis solitaris radiatis, bracteis angustis mucronatis, et floribus ligulatis fertilibus, differt foliis longe petiolatis laminis elliptisis vel obovatis, pedunculis ac involucris lanuginosis.

description: Dwarf perennial herbs, caespitose, rhizomatous 5-8 cm tall. Stems short with radical leaves and solitary terminal heads. Leaves 1.5-4 X 0.8-1 cm, elliptic to obovate, spinulose margins, sparsely stipitate glands and simple pluricellular hairs on both surfaces; petiole narrow, nearly as long as the leaf blade. Peduncles 1-3.5 cm long, woolly, with stipitate glands and long simple pluricellular hairs, naked or with 1-2 bracts. Capitula radiate, 20 mm diam. (including ray florets). Involucre 10 mm high, phyllaries in 5-6 series. Phyllaries linearelliptic, < 1 mm, acuminate, mucronate, wooly, with stipitate glands and long simple pluricellular hairs. Ray florets yellow, pistillate, fertile, tube narrow, 4 X 0.3 mm, glabrous, limb 10 X 1.5 mm. Disk florets yellow, perfect, corolla 7 X 1 mm, glabrous. Cypselae fusiform, downy. Pappus of disk and ray florets persistent, with numerous bristles, 8-9 mm long, yellowish white.

description: Stem stout with rather abundant, short, white hairs, scabrous towards top; variable in color, green nmottled, light-red, light-brown, or yellow, often glaucous; leaves lanceolate, gradually acuminate to both apex and base, petioles short, 0.5-1.5 cm; margins shallowly serrate, sometimes irregularly or only obscurely toothed; lower surfaces with abundant, short white hairs; slightly conduplicate, light-green to gray-green in color; phyllaries variable usually with short, white marginal cilia and scattered pubescence over surface.

description: V. arctioidem simulans sed suffrutices ramosi debiles effusi, foliis petiolatis sparse pubescentibus vel glabratis, pedunculis multo longioribus, capitulis reflexis.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1981. New species and combinations in Vernonia sections Leiboldia and Lepidonia (Asteraceae), with a revisional conspectus of the groups. Brittonia. 33: 401-412.

description: Sprawling or open subshrub, 0.5-1.0 m tall, the foliage and young stems with a scurfy, sordid pubescence. Leaves narrowly elliptic, broadest at the middle, 3- 6 cm wide, 8-18 cm long; blades sparsely appressed-pubescent to glabrate, mi- nutely crenate-denticulate; petioles scurfy-pubescent, 1-2 cm long. Heads re- flexed at maturity, on peduncles 1-4 cm long, 3-8 in a terminal capitulescence. Involucre hemispheric, 1.4-1.8 cm high, 1.5-2.0 wide; receptable convex, alveo- late, glabrous, florets ca 100; bracts lanceolate, graduated in 6-10 series, all of them closely imbricate and ascending in the manner of V. arctioides, sparsely tomentose at first but soon glabrate. Florets "lavender" or "purple"; corolla atomiferous-glandular, ca 10 mm long, the lobes ca 2 mm long, the base of the tube gradually flaring upwards into an indistinct throat ca 2 mm wide, its base persisting as a corona on the achene (as in V. arctioides). Achenes 4-5-sided, ca 1.5 mm long, glabrous, the faces ribless or nearly so. Pappus tawny, seemingly in 2-3 series of numerous, delicate, deciduous, flattened bristles 1-2 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1981. New species and combinations in Vernonia sections Leiboldia and Lepidonia (Asteraceae), with a revisional conspectus of the groups. Brittonia. 33: 401-412.

description: Annuus; eaule 3-6 dim. alto, hispido et dense glandulari-pubescente, superne ramoso, foliosissimo; foliis oblanceolatis; inferioribus petiolatis, 3-10 dm. longis, argute serratis; dentibus lanceolatis; foliis floralibus lanceolati-subulatis, attenuatis; inflorentia corymbiformi, ramis dense glandulosis; involueris hemisphaericis, circa 1 cm. altis; bracteis anguste lanceolati-linearibus, 5-6-serialibus, albo-marginatis; ligulis 12-18, linearibus, 7-8 mm. longis; acheniis anguste conicis, strigosis, 2 mm. longis; pappo rubro-fusco, 2 mm. longo.
bibliographicCitation: Rydberg, Per A. 1934. Taxonomic notes on the flora of the prairies and plains of central North America. Brittonia. 1: 79-104.

description: Annuals (rarely), biennials (usually), or short-lived perennials (occasionally) with taproots; stem branched at or near the base, and freely branching upwards, 1-7 dm. high, pubescent with short spreading hairs; leaves all hirsute with spreading or sometimes appressed hairs; basal leaves broadly oblanceolate to spatulate, entire or sometimes coarsely toothed or even lobed, the petiole up to 5 cm. long, th blade up to about 2.5 cm. long and 1 cm. wide, rarely larger, usually deciduous before flowering time; cauline leaves linear or oblanceolate, numerous, the lower ones sometimes petiolate and resembling the basal ones, but narrower, the others mostly less than 4 cm. long and 5 mm. wide; heads several or usually numerous in a diffuse inflorescence; disk mostly 7-11 mm. wide; involuere 4-5 mm. high, finely glandular and moderately to densely hirsute with long spreading hairs; phyllaries with broad brown midvein, otherwise light yellow-greenish, acuminate, the inner ones broad, with thin often searious margins, the outer ones usually narrower and slightly shorter, without thin margins; ligules about 75-150, blue, pink, or white, mostly 5-10 mm. long and 0.5-1.2 mm. wide, occasionally much reduced and scarcely surpassing the disk; disk-corollas about 2-3 mm. long, with a well defined tube 0.3-0.6 mm. long that is surmounted by a characteristic white, nerveless, slightly indurated and slightly inflated nearly cylindrical portion of the limb 0.5-1.0 mm. long; corolla-lobes about 0.4-0.7 mm. long; style-appendages very short and broad, less than 0.1 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 5-12 very.fragile bristles, the outer of conspicuous setose squamellae; akenes sparsely hairy, 2-nerved or sometimes obscurely 4-nerved, the nerves usually colorless and inconspicuous.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Perennial herb with a relatively slender or moderately stout taproot and a simple or long and branched caudex; stem 10-25 cm. high, moderately hirsute with short spreading hairs, conspicuously decumbent at the somewhat purplish base, then aseending or suberect; leaves short-hirsute like the stem, but more densely so, green, the basal ones triple-nerved, occasionally with an extra pair of fainter submarginal nerves, tufted and erect, oblanceolate or spatulate to subelliptic, tapering to the petiole, rounded to obtuse or sometimes acutish at the apex, occasionally toothed above the middle, up to 12 cm. long and 15 mm. wide; cauline leaves several, fairly well developed, but conspicuously smaller than the basal ones, xnostly linear-oblong; heads 1-4, the disk 9-15 mm. wide; involuere 5-7 mm. high, finely glandular and sparsely to moderately spreading-hirsute; phyllaries slightly thickened on the back, more or less imbricate, usually green or greenish, often purplish and a little loose at the tips; ligules about 25-50, blue or white, 4-8 mm. long, 1.4-1.8 mm. wide; disk-corollas mostly 3.7-4.8 mm. long, the tube about 0.9-1.6 mm., the lobes about 0.6-0.7 mm.; style-appendages ovate, obtuse or rounded, 0.1-0.15 or 0.2 mm. long; pappus of about 15-20 fragile bristles, occasionally with a few inconspicuous, very slender or very short and subulate outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, somewhat hairy. Open places at moderate elevations; eastern Nevada and adjacent Utah.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Rosettes or sometimes ascending or spreading to 10 cm, with few to many pairs of leaves, moderately branched, with roots from lower nodes; internodes 0.3-1.3 cm long, sparsely pilosulous to glabrescent. Leaves usually sessile on basal sheath, less commonly tapered to a petioliform base, ca. 1 mm long; blades oblong to elliptical, 1- 1.5 cm long, 0.3-0.9 cm wide, margins remotely subdenticulate, apex rounded to obtuse, surfaces pilosulous to pilose. Peduncles elongating at or after anthesis, to 2.5 cm long, pilose, especially distally. Heads sessile until anthesis, 4-5 mm high, ca. 6 mm wide; involucral bracts 8 or 9, greenish, oblong, ca. 3.5 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, pilosulous outside; pales mostly restricted to periphery of receptacle, subulate, ca. 0.7 mm long. Ray florets ca. 12; corollas yel- lowish green, 1.5-2 mm long, hirtellous with spreading hairs mostly shorter than width of tube, trilobed limb 0.2-0.6 mm long, with 2 short resin ducts. Disk florets 10-22; corollas greenish to yellowish green, ca. 2 mm long, tube 0.7-0.8 mm long, hirtellous with spreading hairs mostly shorter than width of tube, throat moderately campanulate, 0.7-0.8 mm long, mostly glabrous and exposed, lobes 0.5-0.6 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm wide, with few or no hairs; anther thecae 0.4-0.5 mm long. Achenes 1.7-1.8 mm long.

description: Herba 3-5-pedalis superne racemoso-ramosa; caulis validus tenuiter arachnoideo-lanatus striatus cavus; folia infima ultra-pedalia lanceolata acuminata basi decrescentia alte pinnatisecta, segmentis saepius trifurcatis margine subnudis lobis spinis stramineis rigidis 5-8 mm. longis terminatis, rhachi inter lobos 5-7 mm. lata, supra arachnoideoeineraseentia denique viridia et tenuiter araneosa subtus albido-tomentosa; folia caulina similia lanceolato-oblonga sessilia non amplectentia vix decurrentia; capitula majuscula ca. 3.5-4.5 cm. alta 6-9 cm. diam. (sicca), in apicibvus ramorum paucifoliorum folia subaequantium solitaria v. terna sessilia v. subsessilia; involucri valde gradati ca. 7-9- seriati (phyllariis intimis 2-3-seriatis quam interioribus multo brevioribus et occultis exceptis) basi foliis paucis subaequilongis v. longioribus valde acuminatis suffulti phyllaria anguste lanceolata purpuraseentia erecta rigideque spinos,o-acuminata margine dense griseo-arachnoideociliata pilis recte patentibus; corollae "albae, stigmatibus purpureis," ca. 27 mm. longae, tubo quam limbo breviore, dentibus faucibus paene quadruplo longioribus.

description: E. piulvinatus Rydb. Fl. Rocky Mts. 911. 1917. Not Wedd. 1857. Pulvinate-cespitose perennial with a short much-branched caudex and a stout toproot; leaves all basal, finely strigose, linear, 4-20 mm. long, 0.6-1.1 mm. wide; scape 2-6 cm. high, finely strigose; head solitary, the disk 7-14 mm. wide; involucre 5-6 mm. high, finely strigose and obscurely glutinous; phyllaries slightly imbricate, yellowish straw-colored or light greenish, with brown midrib, the outer narrow and slightly thickened, the inner broader and thinner, sometimes purplish at the tips, all firm and acute; ligules about 15-30, white or pinkish,.6-9 mm. long, 1.7-2.2 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4.5-6.0 mm. long, the tube about 0.8-1.1 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm., the narrow limb somewhat constricted in the lower half, slightly flaring above the middle; style-appendages triangular-lanceolate, acute, 0.2-0.3 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of 30-40 slender firm slightly sordid bristles, the outer of long slender setae; akenes 2-nerved, conspicuously long-ciliate on the margins, otherwise glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: A low coarse plant ea 1.1 dm tall, often straggly; stems strigose; leaves linear, up to 3 en long, 4 mm wide, strigose, or essentially glabrous, the margins scabrous; peduncles less than 1.9 cm long, mostly strigose; heads broadly cylindric, 8-10 mm high; phyllaries oblong, green with a dark purplish-browni summit band or a discolored zone, the apices rounded, ciliate; rays wanting or when present 5-8, yellow (drying dull purple to reddish brown), reduced, up to 5.7 mm long but usually much smaller, scarcely tubed; ray style glabrous, its branches ea 1.9 mm long; ray achenes oblance-linear, 3-angled, 7-8 mm long, striate, sparsely strigose, the pappus none or of 1 or 2 very short awns; disk corollas ea 20, brick red, 5.5-6.2 mm long, the lobes 1 mm long, essentially gla- brous on the outer surface; disk achenes oblanceolate, 3.2-5.8 mm long, the pappus of 2 equal, 2 unequal or 3 unequal awns; chaff obtuse, erose, often red- or purplish-tipped; receptacle slightly concave to short conical.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Plant about 2-25 or 30 cm. high, often a little curved at the base; leaves relatively wider thars in var. asteroides; heads solitary or few, commonly borne on long arcuate-ascending peduncles; peduncles and involueres glandular, sometimes also sparsely or moderately hirsute; ligules generally pinkish, averaging broader and more conspicuous than in the other varieties, and more evidently exceeding the pappus.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Erect or procumbent annual herbs up to 5 dm tall; stems strigose to hispid, reddish brown; leaves variable, obovate to lanceolate, strigose to hispid, darker green on the upper surface, up to 5.5 cm long and 1.9 cm wide but usually smaller, sessile or with petioles up to 3.1 mm long; peduncles up to 7cm long, becoming upwardly tomentose; heads hemispheric, ca 9 mm wide; phyllaries obovate, dark yellow-brown to purple, rough-ciliate near the summit, or with a darker bald, the apices rounded, erose; rays 8-10, yellow, oblong to suborbicular, up to 1.2 cm long, smooth above, with two prominent veins below, finely strigose, the tube 1.2 mm long, laterally adnate to the awns; ray styles sometimes with a few spreading hairs; ray achenes narrowly elliptic, 3-angled, 3.2 mm long, smooth at first, becoming tuberculate, the stout awns fused to the corolla tube forming a reddish V; disk corollas 4 mm long, the lobes dark purplish below, the tube occasionally slightly dilated at the base; disk achenes cuneate, laterally compressed, 3 mm long, emarginate, the margins finely ciliated, becoming crustaceous, the faces becoming tuberculate; chaff yellow, the apices acute, entire, dark purple, exceeding the disk flowers, sparsely ciliated or glabrous; receptacle low-conical.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1963. Taxonomy of Zinnia. Brittonia. 15: 1-25.

description: Perennial herbs ca 3-7.4 dm tall; stems canescent, becoming glabrate. Leaves cauline, slightly reduced upwards; petioles 1-3 mm long; blades 6-11 cm long, 0.7-2.6 cm wide, elliptic to linear-elliptic, widest at the middle, apically acute, basally cuneate, marginally revolute, entire to remotely callous-toothed, dark green and glabrous or sometimes arachnoid-tomentose above, canescent to gray-felted beneath. Inflorescences cymose to paniculate. Heads 34-56-flowered; peduncles ca 1-3 cm long, canescent. Involucre broadly campanulate, 5-10 mm high, 8-12 mm wide; phyllaries imbricate in several series, arachnoid-tomentose dorsally, the inner ones oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, 5.1-8.5 mm long, 1.2-1.8 mm wide, the outer ones lanceolate, 2.9-4 mm long, 0.6-1.3 mm wide. Pappus straw-colored, the inner bristles 5.5-9.5 mm long and outer scale-like bristles 0.7-1.2 mm long. Corollas 8-13 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers 3.1-5 mm long. Achenes 3-4.4 mm long, 8-10 ribbed, strigose. Flowering and fruiting from October to March.
bibliographicCitation: Jones, Jr., Samuel B. 1982. A revision of Vernonia series Buddleiifoliae (Compositae: Vernonieae). Brittonia. 34: 102-117.

description: Emergent, aquatic annual herbs ca. 2 dm tall, rooting at the lower decumbent nodes, which may also have scale leaves; stems glabrous, purplish to brownish-yellow, finely striate, hollow, with conspicuous nodes; leaves glabrous, sessile, or with' petioles up to ca. 1.7 cm long, lance-linear if sessile to ovate if petiolate, up to 3.5 cm long and 0.6 cm wide; peduncles generally longer than the subtending internode and leaves, glabrous except for the minutely pubescent flaring apex; heads subglobose in bud, campanulate when open, ca. 9 mm wide exclusive of rays; phyllaries uniseriate, green, thin, mostly 11-15 but sometimes up to 18 or 20, flat, linear, mostly distinctly 3-veined, ca. 7 mm long, glabrous except at the margins which sometimes appear subscabrous due chiefly to the alar pubescence; alae thin, hyaline, marginally pubescent, slightly exceeding the achenes in length, laterally ca. 1/2 and medially ca. 1/3 the phyllary length, ray flowers 8-11 mm long; ray corollas spatulate to elongate ovate, 0-3-lobed at apex, essentially tubeless, more or less persistent on the achene, white to yellow to pink and purple, especially on young rays, thin and papery when dry; ray achene ca. 2.5 mm long, linear to turbinate; disk flowers numerous; corolla ca. 2 mm long, yellow, the basal constriction ca. 1/3-1/4 the length and lightly pubescent; disk achene ca. 2 mm long, linear, essentially terete; paleae not strongly keeled but more or less flat, thin, incompletely enclosing the disk achenes, semipersistent, shorter than the subtended disk floret, sometimes purple-tinged, spatulae to oblanceolate, apices acute to acuminate; receptacle conical; 2n = 18.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1968. Revision of Jaegeria (Compositae--Heliantheae). Brittonia. 20: 52-73.

description: Plants perennial subshrubs, branched, ca 2 dm high, spreading; stems slender, woody toward the base, lightly strigose; leaves subsessile, narrowly to broadly elliptic, lobed to entire, sericeous, ca 2.1 cm long, dark green; pedluncles up to 7 mm long, strigose; heads hemispherical, ca 6 mm wide; phyllaries ca 18, imbricate, graduated, sometimes foliaceous, broadly linear to obovate, margins ciliated, otherwise phyllaries glabrouis, apices acute to mucronate; rays 10-12, yellow, reflexed, persistent, obovate, 2-lobed, ca 7 mm long, apices acute, style glabrous with acute apices; ray aehene ca 2.5 mm long, obtriangular, 3-angled, obscurely striate, essentially glabrous, becoming tuberculate, the 3 or rarely 4 stout diverging awns ca 2.3 mm long; disk corollas numerous, of rather uniform width, ca 3 mm long, essentially glabrous, lobes ca 0.7 mm long, purplishbrown and with thickened margins, anthers with concave and lanceolate sterile apices, filaments dilated above, style bifid, branches flattened with obtuse apices, bases conspicuously dilated; peripheral disk achenes compressed to 3-angled broadly oblanceolate to cuneate, becoming tuberculate, margins minutely ciliate, 0-2 very short awns, central achenes with 2 unequal slender awns, compressed, broadly oblanceolate, smooth, lightly pubescent, margins inconspicuously winged, wings ciliate, achene apices notched; paleae acuminate, about equaling the disk flowers; receptacle conical.
bibliographicCitation: Torres, Andrew M. 1964. Revision of Sanvitalia (Compositae-Heliantheae). Brittonia. 16: 417-433.

description:
Perennial herbs. Stems erect, glabrous, simple to the inflorescence, 3-14 dm high. Leaves numerous, middle stem leaves 0.5-4.5 cm wide, 3.7-18.0 cm long, narrowly to broadly lanceolate, glabrous to minutely puberulent or somewhat scabrous above espe- cially along the margin, deeply pitted beneath, with glandular trichomes, apically acuminate or acute, narrowed to a sessile base, margin serrate to denticulate with ascending teeth. Inflorescence compact. Heads crowded, 10-26 flowered. Involucre campanulate to subcylindric, 4.1-8.9 mm high, 3.3-6.8 mm wide. Phyllaries imbricate and appressed, tips subacute to rounded, glabrous or thinly ciliate. Achenes glabrous to puberulent or resinous, 2.8-3.5 mm long. Pappus tawny to purple, inner bristles 5-6 mm long, outer scales 0.5-1.0 mm long.

Chromosome number: n = 17 (in ssp. fasciculata, Jones, 1970 and in ssp. corym- bosa, Anderson 3438 Kansas).

description: Perennial herb with numerous fibrous roots and a very short usually stout underground caudex, which gives rise to numerous slender stems; stems 5-35 cm. high, subglabrous or usually sparsely hirsute-strigose with appressed or ascending hairs, to sometimes rather densely spreading-villous; leaves thin, lax, subglabrous, with rather distantly ciliate margins, crowded, longer than the internodes, linear or linear-oblong to oblong-lanceolate, acute or obtuse and sometimes mucronulate at the apex, 1-5 mm. wide, up to 3 cm. long, often bearing short leafy shoots in the axils, these leaves somewhat reduced; heads solitary, rarely as many as 5, borne on conspicuous long naked or subnaked peduncles, to which the cauline leaves are very abruptly reduced; disk 6-12 mm. wide; involuere 4-6 mm. high, with a few slender and generally inconspicuous somewhat viscid hairs; phyllaries thin, lax, mostly tapering from near the base, acuminate or generally attenuate, often somewhat purplish near the tips, subequal, or slightly and irregularly imbricate; ligules 20-50, white, or sometimes pink or rose-purple, 4-8 mm. long, 0.8-1.4 mm. wide; disk-corollas 3.0-4.6 mm. long, the tube 0.8-1.4 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm., the limb rather broad; style-appendages varying from lanceolate and acute to ovate and obtuse, 0.1-0.25 mm. long; pappus of about 20-30 slender white or occasionally rusty bristles, with a few short inconspicuous outer setae; akenes 2-nerved, short-hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herbaceous perennial 3-5(2.5-6) dm tall, glabrous, or sometimes tomentulose when young, occasionally with small villous tufts in the axils of the lower leaves and rarely among the heads in the inflorescence; stems usually arising singly but sometimes several loosely clustered from an erect or trailing perennial or sometimes annual rootstock. Basal leaves narrowly lanceolate in outline but distinctly pinnatifid, 6-10(2-12) cm long and 1-2(0.5-3) cm wide, lobes toothed, cuneate to abruptly constricted at point of attachment to the midrib, the midrib only weakly winged; the lobes progressively smaller toward the apex with the terminal lobe normally distinctly smaller than the lateral lobes, six or more pairs of lateral lobes normally present. Cauline leaves pinnatifid to sublyrate, progressively reduced upwards, those of the lower third of the stem resembling the basal leaves in shape and size; uppermost reduced to mere bracts. Inflorescence a loose, subcorymbose cyme of 6-20 or occasionally more heads; principal involucral bracts (13) 21, 4-6 mm long, with green or yellowish but not black tips; ray florets (8) 13, the ligule (8) 10+ mm long. Achenes hirtellous on angles in all specimens studied.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, T. M. 1968. Taxonomy of Senecio multilobaius and its allies. Brittonia. 20: 267-284.

description: Perennial herbs (4) 5-6 (11) dm tall, from an enlarged woody caudex; stems tomentose, villous-tomentose, pilose-tomentose, or arachnoid-tomentose to almost glabrate. Leaves basal and greatly reduced upwards; the mid-stem blades (0.8) 2.5-3 (9) cm long, 0.3-1.5 (3.8) cm wide, the basal ones 7-15 (21) cm long, (2.2) 3-5 (7) cm wide, ovate, elliptic, elliptic-ovate, or obovate-elliptic, widest at or above the middle, apically acute to acuminate or rounded-acute, basally cu- neate, the margins revolute and usually remotely toothed, pilose, thinly pilose to glabrate, pilose-hispid or slightly scabrous above, pilose, thinly strigose, or glabrate beneath, the veins prominent and pilose beneath, anastomosing, long pilose where the sessile blades join the stem. Inflorescences cymose-paniculate, relatively small. Heads (15) 19-23 (26)-flowered, sessile to subsessile. Involucre broadly campanulate, (6) 7-9 (10.2) mm high, (6.5) 8-10 (11) mm wide. Phyllaries loosely imbricated in 3-4 series, arachnoid to arachnoid-lanate or strigose to basally pilose, the inner ones lanceolate, (5) 6-7 (8.5) mm long, 1-1.7 mm wide, long acuminate; the outer ones lanceolate (2) 2.5-3.5 (4) mm long, (0.5) 0.8-1 mm wide. Pappus whitish to straw-colored, the inner bristles 5.5-9 mm long, the outer scale-like ones (0.7) 1-1.2 (1.5) mm long. Corollas 6.5-9 (11) mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous or the tips of lobes sometimes glandular. Anthers (2.7) 3 (4) mm long. Achenes (1.3) 1.5-2 (2.7) mm long, thinly strigose, very rarely glandular at base. Flowering and fruiting from November to February.
bibliographicCitation: Jones, Jr., Samuel B. 1981. Revision of Vernonia series Flexuosae (Compositae: Vernonieae). Brittonia. 33: 214-224.

description: Arching or scandent shrubs, 3-6 m tall; stems 2-5 cm diam., running horizontal and rooting at the nodes, glabrate proximally to densely strigose distally, hairs 2 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades 7-15 X 3-9 cm, ovate to narrow-ovate, apices acuminate, bases cuneate, margins serrulate remotely denticulate more or less revolute; conspicuously 3-5-veined from near base, both faces glabrate to sparsely strigose, hairs up to 0.3 mm long; petioles <3 cm long, 1-1.5 mm diam., strigose, hairs 0.2 mm long. Capitulescences thyrsoid, flat-topped, 50-100 capitula, with clusters of 3-6 sessile capitula terminating all axes. Capitula radiate, 3-4 mm high, 3-4 mm diam.; involucres funnelform, 3-4 mm diam.; phyllaries 6, 4 X 2.5-3 mm, ovate, arranged in two series, abaxially strigose, hairs 0.3 mm long, the distal one-third of margin ciliate, apices acute, 7-12 veined. Pistillate florets 3-5, subtended by ovate paleae, 3 X 2.5 mm, 7- veined, apices acute, margins ciliate on distal-one-third; corollas white, 2 to 2.5 mm long, 1 mm diam., 4-lobed, lobes 0.5 mm long, deltoid, shortly ciliate at margin; styles 3 mm long, branches 1.5 mm long. Staminate florets 4-10, epaleaceous, corollas 3 mm long, 5-lobed, lobes deltoid, 0.4 mm long; anthers black, 2 mm long; styles 3 mm long; ovary 2 X 0.2 mm, villous toward apex, hairs 0.5 mm long. Cypselae 2 X 1.3 mm, glabrous. Chromosome number, n = 16 (Robinson et al., 1981).
bibliographicCitation: Arriagada, J. E. 2003. Revision of the genus Clibadium (Asteraceae, Heliantheae). Brittonia. 55: 245-301.

description: Annual 30-70 ern high; stems erect, greenish-striate, finely puberulous to nearly glabrous; leaves alternate, compound, the lowermost biternate or triter- nate, pubescent with long hairs, the middle and upper leaves becoming glabrous or nearly so; mid-stem leaves with petioles 2-4 cm long, the ultimate divisions linear to linear-oblanceolate, 1-3 cm long, 0.5-4 mm wide; infloreseence a subcorymbose eyme with several to many heads; heads turbinate, without rays, 5-7 mm wide, 8-10 mm high (including the projecting florets), 20- to 30-flowered, on glabrous (rarely viscid) peduncles 5-30 mm long; principal involueral bracts 8-12, linear-oblong, 4-7 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, broadly rounded or obtuse at the apex, with yellowish (rarely reddish) membranous margins; florets whitish (ochroleucous), distinetly zygomorphic; corolla 5-7 mm long, the tube cylindric, glandular- pubescent, 2-3 mm long, gradually flaring into a narrow funnelform throat 2-3 mm long; lobes unequal, 1-2 mm long; style branches flattened, stigmatic to the base, abruptly obtuse. and papillose at the apex; achenes narrowly cuneate, 3-5 mm long, 4-angled, the faces striate, evenly hirsute throughout; pappus of 13-16 linear-lanceolate, paleaceous scales 3-6 mm long, the mid-nerve of each scale extending into an awn 1-2 mm long; chromo- some number not determined.
bibliographicCitation: Turner, Billie L. 1962. Taxonomy of Hymenothriz (Helenicae, Compositae). Brittonia. 14: 101-120.

description: Much like E. pinnatisectus, but smaller and more compact, the leaf-lobes fewer and more crowded, the stems or peduncles rarely if ever more than 5 cm. high, the involucre 5-6.5 mm. high, the disk-corollas sometimes, but not always, a little shorter than in E. pinnatisectus; pappus apparently always conspicuously shorter than the disk-corollas; differing sharply from E. pinnatisectus in the complete absence of pistillate flowers.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Stems stout, rough, glandular-hispid, to 3 m tall; leaves sessile or with a winged petiole, scabrous above, densely puberulent below, broadly ovate, the lobes ca 5, serrate-dentate, the sinuses shallow, the base truncate to subsagittate; upper leaves not lobed, ovate-lanceolate; peduncles stout, densely hirsute to glandular-hispid; phyllaries ca 5, broadly ovate, obtuse, ca 12-14 mm long and 10-12 mm wide, dense- ly glandular or the glands among hairs; ray flowers to ca 20, the corollas yellow 8-9-nerved, pilose below, the tube densely pilose, ca 10 mmi long and 4 mm wide; disc flowers 5-8 mm long; ray paleae lanceolate, ca 7 mm long, disc paleae 5-7 mm long; achene black, obovate, 3 mm wide, 4.5-6 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Wells, James R. 1965. A taxonomic study of Polymnia (Compositae). Brittonia. 17: 144-159.

description: Perennial herb with a stout simple or subsimple caudex and stout thick root; stem 5-15 cm. long, decumbent or weakly ascending, glandular and viscid-villous with long spreading hairs; basal leaves conspicuous, rosulate-tufted, spatulate to obovate, short-petiolate or subsessile, somewhat glandular and mnore or less viscidvillous, coarsely toothed or incised, the earliest ones relatively short and broad, 2 cm. long or less, the later ones larger, sometimes as much as 9 cm. long and 2.5 mm. wide; cauline leaves well developed, broadly lanceolate to elliptic or ovate, entire, seldom 4 cm. long and 1 cm. wide, their vesture like that of the basal leaves; heads 1-several in a leafy infloreseence, the disk about 9-13 mm. wide; involuere 5-7 mm. high, equaling or surpassing the disk, somewhat glandular and more or less viscid-villous, the phyllaries about equal, thin, attenuate, with loose tips, the outer nearly wholly green or greenish, some of them occasionally a little broader than the others and quite foliaceous in texture; ligules pink or white, about 30-60, 5-8 mm. long, a little over 1 mm. wide; disk-corollas aboutt 3.4-4.7 mm. long, with a long prominent tube 1.0-2.0 mm. long and lobes about 0.4-0.8 mm. long, the limb commonly narrow in its lower part and flaring above; pappus simple, of about 15-20 slender bristles which are characteristically curled and twisted for at least the upper half or two thirds; akenes loosely hirsute, 2-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Basally woody perennial herbs or subshrubs (0.3) 0.5-0.7 (1.5) m tall, mostly cespitose, from a xylopodium. Leaves alternate throughout or sometimes proximally opposite; petioles up to 3 mm long; blades 2.7- 4.5 x 1-2 cm, subcoriaceous, elliptic or sometimes obovate, cunéate at the base, shortly acuminate and mucronulate at the apex, sparsely serrulate, both surfaces appearing subglabrate as the trichomes are so small, appressed, sparsely and minutely scabridulous. Outer phyllaries 9-12.5x2.5-4 mm, panduriform or elliptic beyond a short oblong base, proximally indurate; inner phyllaries 8-11x3-3.5 mm, panduriform to oblong to obovate. Paleae 7.5-9 x ca. 1 mm when folded, subulate. Ray florets fertile, tube 1.5-2 mm long, lamina 9-15x4-7 mm, ob- long, glabrous or with a few trichomes abaxially. Disc florets with corollas 4-6 mm long, lobes abaxially glabrous, conspicuously thickened at the tip. Cypselae 5- 6 x 2.5- 3 mm, the peripheral ones trigonous, winged, 3-awned, the inner lateral flattened, wings ca. 2 mm wide; pappus awns 3-5 mm long, very broad at the base, the longest the same or at least not less than 3A the length of the cypsela, crown 0.5-2 mm high, sturdy, usually partially fused to the body (less than 1/3) with erose, fìmbriolate.

description: Suffrutex erectus circiter 60 cm altus, caule tereti, striato, pilis longis et glandulosis vestito; foliis tenuibus, membranaceis, ovalibus oblongisve, utrinque pilis glandulosis sparsis, trisectis, segmentis dentatis vel lobatis, circiter 2 cm longis, 1.5 cm latis; petiolo circiter 1.5 cm longo; capitulis campanulatis, circiter 3.5 mm diametro et 5 mm altis (styli ramis computatis); bracteis involucralibus pubescentibus, 3-nervatis, oblongo-lanceolatis, apice acutis, marginibus fimbriatis et ciliatis; corollis infundibuli- formibus, roseis, circiter 3 mm longis (lobis inclusis), supra et infra lobis et corollae tubo pilis multicellularibus, uniseriatis dispositis; achaenia atro-brunnea, circiter I mm longa; pappi seta circiter 1.5 mm longa; polliniae granula sphaerica, tricolpata, dense spinosa, diametro circiter 20 /u; chromosomatum numero indeterminato.

description: Perennial herb with a simple or somewhat branched caudex and fibrous root system; stem 1-4 (rarely 5.5) dm. high, usually curved or decumbefit at the base, more or less glanrdular at least above, with or without eglandular hairs; hirsute, glanduilar, or glabrous below; basal and lowermost cauline leaves commonly glab- rate or with long scattered hairs, sometimes densely pubescent, oblanceolate or spatulate to oval, entire, commonly rounded or obtuse at the tip, sometimes acute, abruptly narrowed to a winged petiole or petioliform base, the blade and petiole if present mostly 2.5-15 cm. long and 4-15 mm. wide; middle stem leaves lanceo- late or oblong, sometimes ovate, commonly somewhat smaller than the lower ones, mostly 2-6 cm. long and 4-16 mm. wide, glabrous or somewhat hirsute, the mar- gins ciliate; upper stem leaves reduced, linear or lanceolate to ovate, the upper- most generally less than 15 mm. long, glandular or more or less hairy or both; heads 1-6, the disk 10-20 mm. broad; involuere 5-8 mm. high; phyllaries about equal, linear, the outer ones mostly 0.7-1.1 mm. wide, acuminate, glandular or viscid and often hirsute; ligules numerous, about 75-150, 8-15 mm. long and about 1 mm. wide, blue, rarely pink or white; disk-corollas 3.5-4.5 mm. long; style-appendages deltoid to triangular-lanceolate, acute, about 0.2 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of 15-25 bristles, the outer setulose and sometimes very scanty; akenes hairy, 2-nerved.

description: Plantae annuae, 30-45 cm altae, e basi ramosae, caules erecti, pars inferior tantummodo pilis candidis brevibus appressis aut paululum patentibus pubescens, pars superior atque inflorescentia pilis appressis aut ascendentibus, et/aut trichomatibus glandularibus brevissimis 0.1-0.2 mm longis sparsis intermixtis pubeseentes; folia simplicia ubique aut superiora trilobata a-Lt profunde tridivisa raro facta, pilis sparsis appressis pubescentia; folia medio in caule petiolos 0.6-1.4 mm longos habentia; laminae ovatae ad ovato-lanceolatas, 0.6-1.8 cm latae, 2-4 cm longae, 2-3-plo longiores quam latiores, ad apicem late aut anguste acutae; inflorescentia a panicula diffusa ad cymam subcorymbosam subcondensatam, capitulis 10 ad multis; capitula turbinata, 3-5 mm diametro, 6-8 mm alta, 12-18-flora, in pedunculis 5-30 mm longis portata; bracteae involucrales principales 89, 4-6 mm longae, 1.5-2.5 mm latae, marginibus membranaceis albis (raro aliquantulum subroseis) ad apicem rotundatis obtusisve, sparse pubescentibus ad fere glabros; flosculi albi perspicue zygomorphici; corolla 3-3.5 mm longa, tubo cylindrico, 0.75-1 mm longo, iugulo expandente, ca. 0.5 mm loiino, lobis imparibus, 1.5-1.7 mm longis; rami styli 1.2-1.5 mm longi, aliter velut illi generis descripti; achaenia 3-4 mm longa, obpyramidalia, quadrilateralia, pilis appressis aseendentibus aut ineurvatis sparse pubeseentia; pappus ex 8-10 squamis paleaceis 1.2-1.5 mm longis ad apicem late rotundatis ad fere truneatas, sine aristis auit mucronibus terminalibus constans; chromosomata: n = 10.

description: Frutex 1.0-2.5 m altus. Folia simplicia; laminae oblongae vel raro ovatae, 2-7 cm longae, 1.5-3.0 cm latae, subtus conspicue 3-nervatac, utrinque glanduloso-punctatae vel tantum viscidae (et ut videtur eglandulosae), remote serratae vel irregulariter dentatae vel fere integrae. Pedunculi ultimi bracteolati, 1-5 mm longi. Capitula 30-80. Flores 8-12 in capitulo; corollis 5-lobatis, ca. 2.5 mm longis, lobulis acutis externe glandularibus.

description: Shrub 1.0-2.5 m tall. Stems at first glandular-pubescent, light-brown, with age becoming grayish and glabrate. Leaves simple, avocado-green; petioles 5-20 mm long; blades oblong to rarely ovate, 2-7 cm long, 1.5-3.0 cm wide, prominently 3-nerved beneath, minutely glandular-punctate on both surfaces to merely viscid (appearing eglandular), remotely serrate or irregularly jagged to nearly entire. Inflorescence a terminal corymbose cyme, 3-8 cm across, composed of 30-80 heads. Heads "off- white," on ultimate bracteolate peduncles 1-5 mm long. Involucre turbinate, 2-3 seriate, 3-4 mm long, 2-3 mm wide. Florets 8-12; corolla 5-lobed, ca. 2.5 mm long, the lobes acute, glandular without. Achenes ca. 2.3 mm long, 5-angled, pubescent with scattered short ascending hairs; pappus of ca. 32 setose bristles 2-3 mm long.

description: Herbaceous perennial to 35 cm tall; stems erect or decumbent, very short, sparsely pubescent, unwinged. Leaves basal, alternate; blades oblanceolate to ob- ovate, to 15 cm long and 6 cm wide, margins laciniate, ciliate, apex broadly acute, blade narrowing to the sessile base, sparse pubescence above and below with appressed hairs, denser on the main veins. Capitulescences solitary (or 2) on slender pedicels 20-33 cm long. Capitula 0.5-0.9 cm wide. Involucre 2-seriate; outer bracts lanceolate, 2.8-3.4 mm long, 0.7-0.9 mm wide, densely pubescent, apex broadly acute, base not indurate; inner series longer, grading into the paleae. Paleae lanceolate to oblanceolate, 3.2-3.8 mm long, 0.7-0.9 mm wide, keeled, ciliate and pubescent along upper 1/3, apex acute, not distinctly herbaceous. Re- ceptacle short conical. Ray florets 1 1-13, ligules yellow to orange, pubescent on the dorsal surface, 4-4.3 mm long, 1.3-1.5 mm wide, apex rounded, tube sparsely pubescent, 0.4-0.6 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide. Disc florets ca 25, corolla yellow to orange, funnelform, 1.9-2.3 mm long, 0.9-1.3 mm wide, sparse pubescence on throat, tube glabrous, 0.8-1 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, anthers black, apical appendages acute, style branches acute. Ray and disc achenes similar, brown to black, 2.7-3.4 mm long, 0.9-1.7 mm wide, sparse pubescence over the entire surface, wings narrow, 0.2-0.4 mm wide, ciliate, pappus of 2 unequal awns, the shorter one to 2.3 mm long and the longer one to 3.9 mm long, both awns with a prominent recurved tip.
bibliographicCitation: Olsen, John S. 1986. Revision of Verbesina section Verbesina (Asteraceae: Heliantheae). Brittonia. 38: 362-368.

description: Frutex ramis ultimis plus minusve flexuo.sis, viridibus fuscescentibus striatis 1 anuginosoaraneosis glabratisque. Folia alterna petiolata coriacea. Petiolus circa 2 cm longus flexuosus sub-glaber, parce puberulus araneosusque. Lamina late ovato-lanceolata basi sub-rotundata vel obtusa et breviter decurrens apice angustata acutissima margine, integra parce revoluta, 5-9 cm longa 2-4.2 cm lata; supra laeteviridis glabra subnitida minute rugulosa epidermi papilloso-granulata, costa impressa ceteris nervis impresso-reticulatis; subtus dense sordido-ochracea adpresse lanata aspectu mucida costa eminenti nervis secundariis circa 8 utroque latere promi- nulis subarcuato-ascendentibus reliquis nervis obsoletis. Inflorescentiae axillares paniculatae ad terminationem ramulorum magnum thyrsum compositum formantes. Rami ramusculique brachiati vel subpatuli gra- ciles striati parce araneoso-arachnoidei minuteque puberuli; bracteis inferiori- bus foliis similibus sed angustioribus brevioribusque, superne anguste linearibus tenuibus flexuosis gradatim brevioribus. Pedicelli praecipue 5-15 mm longi teneres patuli recti vel flexuosi, araneosi et minute sparseque glandulosi, parcis bracteolis subulatis circa 2 mm longis muniti, interdum 2-3 ad basim involucri ad modum calyculi. Involucrum campanulatum 5.6 mm altum, 8 bracteis elliptico- oblongis 5-5.5 mm longis 1.5-2 mm latis apice subite acutis margine scariosis dorso parce lanuginoso-araneosis. Flores-radii feminei ligulati circiter 6, corolla lutea glabra 8-9 mm longa tubulo 2 mm longo lamina 1.5 mm lata 4-nervia, apice tridentata. Flores disci hermaphroditi circiter 12, corolla 7 mm longa lutea glabra tubulo 3 mm longo dentibus oblongis 1 mm, antheris 3 mm longis basi obtusis. Ovarium glabrum. Pappus albo-sericeus 5 mm longus.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1956. Studies on Andean Compositae - III. Brittonia. 8 (3): 179-193.

description: Plants perennial, suffrutescent; stems herbaceous, except at the base, hirtellous, simple below the inflorescence, loosely caespitose, from a stout taproot and branching, mostly underground, woody caudex; leaves arranged singly along the stems, evenly distributed or slightly clustered towards the base, erect or erect- ascending, linear, 0.5-4.5 cm long, 1-3 (4) mm wide, progressively reduced in size upward on the stem, glabrous or hirtellose, secondary fascicled leaves in axils of some lower leaves; inflorescence simple or sparingly branched with 1-15 heads per stem, the heads mostly solitary on bracteolate peduncles or some nearly sessile; involucre 5-9 mm high, 3-7 mm wide (up to 9 mm when pressed), campanulate, the bracts about 20, in 3 (4) overlapping series, mostly obtuse, the outer much smaller than the inner, glutinous, with translucent margins and greenish, thickened tip; ray flowers 4-10, 5-7 (10) mm long, 1-2 (4) mm wide when fresh; disk flowers 15-23, about 3 mm long; pappus scales about 10-12, unequal, 0.5-2 mm long, those of ray and disk flowers about equal; achenes pubescent, 3-4 mm long, slightly flattened, abortive in disk flowers.
bibliographicCitation: Welsh, Stanley L. 1981. New taxa of western plants--in tribute. Brittonia. 33: 294-303.

description: Rhizomes coarse, 4-6 mm. thick, extensive, producing long naked branches, these little rooting, but with conspicuous light brown, thin, connate, obtuse scales ca. 4 mm. long at the remote nodes; innovations unknown; stems solitary, coarse, 4-8 mm. thick, 3.0-8.0 dm. high, simple or branched above the middle, glabrous or becoming sparsely pubescent above; cauline leaves 12-20 pairs, sessile, connate sheathing, the ocreae 1-2 cm. long, the blades 1.3-4.0 cm. broad, 5-15 cm. long, narrowly to broadly lanceolate or oblanceolate, acute or acuminate, conspicuously and coarsely sharp-serrate, essentially glabrous, scabrous on the margins, only the floral leaves much reduced; peduncles 5-15 cm. long, becoming densely villous with moniliform hairs which are septate nearly to the tip; heads solitary or more frequently 5-15, broadly hemispheric-turbinate, 18-25 mm. high (and 20-35 mm. broad); perielinium short, similarly but less densely pubescent than the peduncle; involueral bracts in 2 series, 4-8 mm. broad, 14-20 mm. long, foliaceous, prominently nerved, broadly callus tipped, moderately to somewhat densely, coarse-pubescent, frequently glabrate toward the tips; ray flowers 10-16, the ligules 12-25 mm. long, 5-8 mm. broad, oblong-oblanceolate, the lobes blunt, 1-2 mm. long, the veins conspicuously branched; disc corollas numerous, dark yellow, 9-12 mm. long, broadly goblet-shaped, the tube 3.3(3)-4.5(4.8) mm. long, the base of the limb and the tube scantily or moderately appressed-villous with coarse septate hairs, the base of the tube obconic, the lobes 1.0-1.2 mm. long, acute, glabrate; anthers long exserted, purple; achenes cylindrical, little tapering, 6.5-9.0 mm. long, scantily strigose with septate single hairs, frequently glabrate toward the base; annulus short, ca. 0.15-0.20 mm. in length; pappus tawny, exceeding the corolla, barbellate, the setae divergent, ascending, ca. 0.12-0.22 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Camp, Wendell H. & Gilly, Charles L. 1943. Part II: Systematic Treatment, [Arnica alpina-Arnica discoidea]. Brittonia. 4 (3): 405-457.

description: Suffrutex 40 cm alta ramis tortuosis ramulis foliosis erectis dense albo-cinereo-lanatis. Folia alterna crassa sessilia oblonga apice obtusiuscula basi saepe dilatata amplectentiaque margine crasse revoluta, supra costa prominula subtus crassa sed tota folia cum lana alba deinde cinerea densa crassa obtecta, 1-2.5 cm longa, 0.3-1 cm lata. Capitula (1 cm diam.) homooama discoidea 2-3 in ramulis superioribus paniculam brevem subfoliosam terminalem ilnstructis; ramulis brevibus anlgulatis dense lanatis; pedicellis valde brevibus, 2-5 mm longis, lanatis, superne bracteolis subulatis 3-5 mm longis crasse lanatis. Involucrum campanulatum 13 bracteis herbaceis crassiusculis biseriatis oblongo-lanceolatis 7 mm longis 1-2-crassonervatis, exterioribus circa 1.5 mm latis interioribus circa 2.8 mm latis maroine searioso, omnibus apice ciliatis extus albo-lanatis. Calyculum 10-12 bracteolis subulatis acutis in lana tectis ad pedicellum deseendentibus. Receptacullum plano-convexum alveolatum, 3 mm diam. Flores omnes hermaphroditi circa 65 in capitulo, corolla lutea glabra 6.5-7 mm longa tuLbulo angusto 2.5 mm longo basi dilatato limbo tubuloso apice breviter dentatis dentibus deltoideis 0.5 mm longis. Antherae 2 mm longae base obtuse appendiculatae. Ralui styli crassiusculi contorti apice truneato penicillato-coronati. Pappus albo-serieeus circa 6 mm longus pilis 2-3 seriatis tenuibus minute strigosis. Ovarium villosum. Achaenia oblonga 3 mm longa angulata dense villosa pilis crassiusculis adpressis vestita.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1960. Studies on Andean Compositae--IV. Brittonia. 12: 182-195.

description: Perennial herbs 2.5-4.2 dm, from an enlarged caudex; stems leafy to inflorescence, hirsute-villous. Leaves cauline, gradually reduced upwards; leaf blades 4.5-9 cm long, 0.2-1.1 cm wide, linear to linear-lanceolate, generally widest at the middle, acuminate, basally cuneate, margins slightly revolute, very remotely callous-toothed, sparsely hirsute-villous beneath. Inflorescences small, panicu- late-corymbiform. Heads 30-44-flowered; peduncles 0.1-2.5 cm long, densely hirsute-villous. Involucre campanulate, 6.5-8.5 mm high, 6-9 mm wide. Phylla- ries loosely imbricate in 3 to 4 series, hirsute-villous on back, greenish-tan, the inner ones lanceolate, 5-6 mm long, 0.8-1.5 mm wide, long-acuminate, the outer ones lanceolate, 2.7-4.5 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide. Pappus whitish, the inner bristles 4.2-5.5 mm long, the outer scale-like ones 0.6-1.5 mm long. Corollas 5.5- 8 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous, tube 2.2-4 mm long. Anthers 2-3.5 mm long. Achenes 1.5-1.8 mm long, sparsely hirsute-villous. Flowering and fruiting from October to April.
bibliographicCitation: Jones, Jr., Samuel B. 1981. Revision of Vernonia series Flexuosae (Compositae: Vernonieae). Brittonia. 33: 214-224.

description: Woody vines; stems glabrous or young branchlets lanate. Leaves alternate; petiole 1-3 mm long or subsessile; blade narrowly lanceolate to linear, 5-11 cm long, 0.5-1 cm wide, membranous, base attenuate to acuminate, apex long-at- tenuate, lower surface sparsely villous, glabrescent, midrib prominent, reticulate- venation prominent, upper surface glabrous, the margins entire. Capitulescences corymbiform-paniculate, terminal and axillary; peduncles (3) 5-8 (10) mm long, densely lanate-tomentose. Capitula discoid, ca 10 mm high; involucre cylindrical, 7-8 mm long, 3-4 mm wide; phyllaries 12-13, 4-5-seriate, imbricate, the outer ovate, 3-5 mm long, ca 1.5 mm wide, villous, glabrescent, apex acute, ciliolate, the inner oblong-lanceolate, ca 7 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, apex acuminate, ciliolate; receptacle naked or with 1 palea, stramineous, membranous, apex at- tenuate; florets 4 (5), hermaphroditic, the corollas narrowly funnelform, 8-10 mm long, bright yellow-orange, the tube ca 4 mm long, the limb ca 2 mm long, 5-lobed, the lobes linear-lanceolate, 2-3 mm long, apex acute; anthers 3.5-3.75 mm long, the collars balusterform, 0.5-0.6 mm long, the terminal appendages lanceolate, attenuate, ca 0.75 mm long; style branches ca 2 mm long, terminal appendages lanceolate, acuminate, pilosulose. Achenes cylindrical, ca 4 mm long, costate, dark brown, glandular with multicellular, biseriate, capitate trichomes; pappus of sca- berulous bristles, ca 7 mm long, stramineous.
bibliographicCitation: Sagástegui Alva, Abundio & Dillon, Michael O. 1988. New species of Llerasia (Asteraceae: Astereae) from Peru. Brittonia. 40: 363-367.

description: Frutices ramosi ca 1.5 m alti. Folia alterna, brevissime petiolata; petioli 0.5-1 mm longi; laminae ovatae, 3.5-4 mm longae, 1.5-2 mm latae, coriaceae, basi truncatae vel cordatae, apice acutae, infeme dense albo-tomentosae, superne glabrae, nitidae, atrovirides, margine integrae vel remote denticulatae, fortiter revolutae. Capitulescentiae solitariae, terminales, subsessiles. Capitula heterogama radiata, ca 8 mm alta, 4-5 mm lata; bracteae calyculi 6-10 lineares, 2-4 mm longae, glabrae; phyllaria ca 13, subbiseriata, coriacea, extima lineari-lanceolata, ca 6 mm longa, ca 1 mm lata, glabra, intima lanceolata, ca 6 mm longa, 1-1.4 mm lata, glabra. Flores radiati pistillati ca 8; ligulae luteae, oblongae, 9-10 mm longae, 1.5-2 mm latae. Flores disci hermaphroditi 20-26; corollae tubulosae luteae, ca 6 mm longae; limbus quinquelobus, anguste infundibuliformis; lobi ca 1 mm longi, ca 0.3 mm lati. Achaenia 1.2- 1.5 mm longa glabra; pappi setae 5.5-6 mm longae, albae.

description: Shrubs to 1.5 m tall; stems much-branched, the branchlets leafy. Leaves alter- nate; petiole 0.5-1 mm long; blade ovate (or appearing narrowly triangular when margins strongly revolute), 3.5-4 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, coriaceous, discolor- ous, the base truncate to cordate, the apex acute, mucronate, the lower surface white-tomentose, the upper surface shiny, glabrous, glandular-punctate, dark green, drying dark brown, the margins entire or with 1 or 2 pairs of minute denticulations, usually strongly revolute. Capitulescences of solitary capitula, subsessile, terminal on branchlets. Capitula radiate, ca 8 mm high, 4-5 mm wide; involucre campanulate; calyculus of 6-10 linear bracts, 2-4 mm long, glabrous; phyllaries ca 13, weakly 2-seriate, coriaceous, the outer linear-lanceolate, ca 6 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, glabrous, the apex attenuate, glandular, puberulent, the inner lanceolate, ca 6 mm long, 1-1.4 mm wide, glabrous, the apex glandular, puberulent, the margins hyaline; ray florets ca 8, pistillate, the corollas yellow, the tube 3-4 mm long, glabrous, the ligule oblong, 9-10 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, the apex 3-toothed; disc florets 20-26, hermaphroditic, the corollas yellow, tubular, ca 6 mm long, the limb narrowly funnelform, ca 4 mm long, the apex 5-lobed, the lobes lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm wide, the apex thickened, the style branches ca 0.8 mm long, the apex obtuse to rounded, penicillate. Achenes cylindrical, 1.2- 1.5 mm long, costate, glabrous; pappus of 50-75, scaberulous bristles, 5.5-6 mm long, white.

description: Herbs or more commonly subshrubs, ca 0.4-1.5 m tall; stems erect, subterete, coarsely striate, puberulent to pubescent, often branched in the uppermost nodes, internodes ca 2-5 (9) cm long, about as long as or longer than the leaves. Leaves whorled with 3 (4) leaves per verticel, petiolate; blade subcoriaceous, ellipticovate, (1) 2-3.5 (4.5) cm long, (1.3) 1.7-2.5 (4) cm wide, basally cuneate to rounded, apically broadly acute or more commonly obtuse to rounded, coarsely serrate with ca 4-6 pairs of apically rounded teeth, venation trinervate, less commonly becoming pinnate, upper surface brownish-green, rugulose, glabrous to puberulent with uniseriate, multicellular, arcuate trichomes, lower surface rust- colored to pale green, reticulate, puberulent to pubescent with hairs as on upper surface and glandular pubescent with biseriate, multicellular, globular trichomes (glands). Capitulescence terminal, cymose, of ca 3-11 (32) capitula; peduncles 0. 5- 6 cm long, pubescent to densely so. Capitula radiate, ca 35-70-flowered; involucre hemispheric, 10-13.5 mm high, 8-11.5 mm broad, ca 3-5-seriate; phyllaries ca 17, imbricate, graduated, the ca 2-5 outer ones ovate, 3-6 mm long, 3.5-6.5 mm  wide, entirely herbaceous or at least apically so, with age commonly reddish or at least apically so, with ca 5 parallel nerves, abaxially puberulent and sometimes also lightly glandular, commonly obtuse apically, recurved, margins entire, the second series of phyllaries elliptic-ovate to elliptic, 6-8 mm long, 3.5-5.5 mm wide, scarious or slightly membranous apically, golden proximally, commonly becoming reddish apically, with ca 15-20 parallel reddish nerves, glabrous, apically obtuse to rounded, entire, innermost series of phyllaries elliptic, 9-12 mm long, (2.5) 4-5.5 mm wide, scarious, golden or yellow, with ca 15 parallel light red nerves, glabrous, apically obtuse, entire; receptacle dome-shaped, ca 2.5-3 mm tall and broad, paleaceous, the paleae elliptic-lanceolate, 7-9.5 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, conduplicate, entire. Rayflorets ca 8-10; corolla ca 15-18 mm long, yellow, the tube 2.7-3.5 mm long, glabrous, the ligule 5-nerved, ca 12-14.5 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide, apically 2- or 3-lobed, commonly abaxially glandular; style ca 7.5 mm long, branches recurved, ca 1 mm long. Disc florets ca 28-60; corolla cylindric, ca 5.5-6 mm long, glabrous or slightly glandular, yellow to golden- yellow, tube 1.5-1.9 mm long, limb only slightly wider than tube, throat 3-3.2 mm long, lobes 5, erect, triangular, 0.7-1.3 mm long; anthers partially exserted, yellow, ca 3 mm long, apical appendage deltoid, glandular abaxially; style to ca 6.5 mm long, branches recurved, ca 1 mm long. Achenes of ray and disc florets generally similar but differing in the length of the pappus, turbinate, strongly 4-angled, 2.5-3.2 mm long, black, puberulent on angles, faces glabrous; carpopodium tan, non-sculptured; pappus of ca 6-8 irregularly unequal ovate to elliptic scales, 1-3 of these often longer than the others, apically acute to rounded, marginally serrulate, stramineous, those of the rays ca 0.3-1 mm long or with 1 or 2 scales to 1.5 mm long, those of the disc florets ca 0.6-1.1 mm long but with 1-3 scales 1.5-2.5 (3.5) mm long and much longer than the rest. Pollen heliantheous, ca 25-35 Am diam. Chromosome number unknown.

description: Herbacea vel suffruticosa ca 0.4-1.5 m alta; caules puberuli vel pubescentes, striati, intemodiis ca 2-5 (9) cm longis; folia verticillata, plerumque tema, petiolata; lamina subcoriacea, elliptico-ovata, (1) 2-3.5 (4.5) cm longa, (1.3) 1.7-2.5 (4) cm lata, obtusa, serrata, subtriplinervis, rugulosa, glabra vel puberula, glandulosa; capitulescentia terminalis, cymosa, pedunculis 0.5-6 cm longis; capitula het- erogama, paleacea; involucrum hemisphaericum, 10-13.5 mm longum, 8-11.5 mm latum; phyllaria gradata, ca 3-5-seriata, praeter quatuor extema plerumque herbacea rubescentia, recurvata, pleraque scariosa; receptaculi paleae elliptico-lanceolatae, 7-9.5 mm longae, integrae; flosculi radiati ca 8-10, corolla ca 15-18 cm longa, luteola, tubo 2.7-3.5 mm longo, limbo 5-nervio, ca 12-14.5 mm longo, glandulifero; flosculi disci ca 28-60, corolla ca 5.5-6 mm longa, glabra vel glandulosa, luteola, lobis 0.7-1.3 mm longis; achaenia turbinata, 4-angulata, nigra, puberula, ca 2.5-3.2 mm longa; pappi squamae ca 6-8, ovatae vel ellipticae, inaequales, plerumque 0.3-1.1 mm, 1-3 autem 1.5-2.5 (3.5) mm usque longae.

description: Perennial, with a diffuse caudex divided into several or many rhizome-like branches; herbage densely glandular, very nearly or quite without long eglandular hairs; stem less than 1 dm. high; basal leaves petioled, about 1-4 cm. long, cuneate-flabelliform in outline, deeply 3-5-cleft into cuneate 3-lobed divisions, or simply 5-9-lobed at the apex; cauline leaves cuneate-obovate, smaller, subsessile, less divided, the uppermost entire; heads solitary at the ends of the several simple stems, the disk about 10-15 mm. wide; involuere about 7-8 mm. high, densely glandular; phyllaries purplish green, narrow, long-acuminate, with more or less spreading tips, subequal or some of the outer shorter; rays about 50-70, light pink or white, about 6-8 mm. long and 1.5-2 mm. wide; disk-corollas about 4 mm. long; pappus sinple, of about 20 bristles; akenes 2-nerved, short-hairy.

description: Twining to sprawling vine characterized by elliptical, spatulate, or rhomboidal leaves. The capitulescence is an open panicle with the heads remotely disposed in spikes or racemes 3-8 cm long.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and short branching caudex; stemn 2-30 cm. high, copiously spreading-hirsute; leaves spreading hirsute, the hairs on the surfaces commonly a little finer than those on the stem, the margins of the petioles often with some coarser stiffly spreading hairs; basal leaves linear-oblaneeolate to spatulate, up to 8 cm. long and 6 mm wide, long-petiolate, tufted and persistent, or in taller forms often deciduous; cauline leaves variously developed, sometimes oblanceolate and as large as the basal, except for being nearly sessile, sometimes linear and reduced, or absent; heads solitary, or several and borne on leafy branches; involuere 4-6 mm. high, coarsely spreading-hirsute and often also finely glandular; phyllaries subequal or slightly imbricate, slender, acuminate, green or greenish brown, thickened on the midrib; pistillate flowers present, tubular and eligulate, or sometimes bearing inconspicuous ligules shorter than the disk; disk-corollas about 2.8-4.9 mm. long, the tube 0.6-1.5 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.8 mm., the limb commonly firm and whitish below the middle, often also puberulent below the middle; style-appendages deltoid and acutish to very broadly triangular and obtuse, 0.1-0.25 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 7-20 bristles, the outer of evident, sometimes narrow, squamellae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely short-hairy. Southwestern Colorado, northern Arizona, Utah, Nevada, southwestern Idaho, southeastern Oregon, northern California, and southern California; reported from extreme northwestern New Mexico.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Shrubs, ca. 2.5 m tall; stems striate, strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate-lanceolate, 7-11 X 2.5-4 cm, apices acuminate, bases attenuate, margins serrate, 3-veined, both faces weakly strigose, hairs 0.5-1 mm long; petioles 1-2 cm long, 1 mm diam., strigose, hairs 0.5 mm long. Capitulescences thyrsoid, to 25 capitula; peduncle 1 mm long. Capitula 2-3 mm high, 3-4 mm diam.; involucres cupulate, 3.5 mm diam.; phyllaries 5-6, ovate, 3 X 2.5 mm, 5-7 veined, apices acute, strigose, hairs 0.1 mm long, distal one-third ciliate, bases fleshy at maturity. Pistillate florets 24-39, subtended by ovate paleae; paleae 3 X 2.5 mm, 5-veined, arranged in 5-6 series, bases fleshy at maturity; apices acute, strigillose toward apex, distal one-third of margin ciliate; corollas white, 1.5-1.2 X 1 mm, irregularly 4-lobed, lobes deltoid, margins short and scarcely ciliate. Staminate fiorets 6-10; corollas 1.5-1.2 mm long, 4-5 lobed, lobes, 0.4 mm long, margins scarcely ciliate; throats 1 mm long, 0.5 mm diam.; subtended by lanceolate to filiform paleae, 3- veined; apices ciliate; anthers black, 1-1.2 mm long; ovaries, 1.2 mm long, 0.3 mm diam., hirsute on distal one-third. Cypselae drupaceous, 2 X 1.5 mm, hirsute on distal one-third. Chromosome numbers unknown.

description: Submaritime often cespitose perennial from a stout thick rhizome or branching caudex; exceedingly variable in size and general development according to exposure; stem 5-50 cm. high, stout, usually sprawling at the base and curving upward, densely villous-hirsute with spreading hairs, especially upwards, to essentially glabrous or even glandular, the margins ciliate; basal leaves large and conspicuous, with obovate to broadly spatulate blades tapering to broad winged petioles, up to 15 cm. long and 5 cm. wide, usually rather distantly toothed above the middle, rounded or obtuse at the tips, rarely acute, the upper sometimes narrow and somewhat reduced; heads 1-15, on leafy often lonig branches which sometimes arise near the base of the main stem; disk 15-35 mm. wide and 7-13 mm. high; phyllaries numerous, equal, linear, acuminate or sometimes attenuate at the close or slightly loose tips, 0.7-1.5 mm. wide, scarcely herbaceous, often with dark or thickened midrib, from very densely long-villous with multicellular often viscid hairs to sparsely villous; ligules mostly about 100, 9-15 mm. long, 1-2 mm. wide, blue or white, sometimes turning yellow in herbarium specimens; diskcorollas mostly about 5 mm. long, narrow, with short lobes about 0.5 mm. long, constricted to a definite tube in the lower 1.5-2 mm.; style-appendages about 0.2 mm. long, broadly ovate, obtuse; pappus of about 20-30 dingy or reddish bristles, sometimes with a short setulose outer series; akenes from 2-nerved and obscurely 4-angled to commonly 4-nerved and 4-angled, or sometimes even 6-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Perennial herb with a generally stout taproot and rooterowrf; short stem-base often rhizomatous in appearance; stem 1-9 dm. high, erect or nearly so, generally spreading-hirsute at the base, soon becoming glabrous upward, or sometimes shortly appressed-hirsute to near the summit, or hairy below and becoming glandular upwards, or even glanduLlar throughout, but not, except near the base, approaching a spreading-villous condition; leaves numerous, longer than the internodes, only very gradually reduced upwards, without a basal tuft, firm, linear-filiform to narrowly oblong or sometimes oblong-oblanceolate, commonly with a short slightly cartilaginous area near the base, up to 5 cm. long and 6 mm. wide, those of the infloreseence often reduced and distant, glabrous or appressed hirtellous to sometimes loosely hirtellous or hispidulous, or rarely glandular (the uppermost more frequently so), but not at all villous, ciliate on the margins, sometimes very coarsely so; heads several or many, rarely solitary, the disk 8-17 mm. wide; involucre 3-9 mm. high, often much shorter than the disk, glabrous to densely glandular, rarely also slightly short-hairy; phyllaries strongly imbricate, narrow, sharply acute to long-acuminate, with brown midrib, otherwise greenish or more commonly yellow-greenish, often purplish above the middle; pistillate flowers absent, but rarely a few of the marginal hermaphrodite flowers with abortive stamens and short ligules; disk-corollas 4.2-8.0 mm. long, the tube 0.8-2.1 mm., the lobes 0.5-0.7 mm.; style-appendages broadly triangular, obtuse or acutish, 0.1-0.2 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 25-60 coarse brownish bristles, the outer of more or less evident setae; akenes 2-nerved, sparsely hairy. Dry, often rocky places at low or moderate elevations; from southeastern Washington, through eastern Oregon, to California, as far souith as Tulare County, and adjacent Nevada.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Perennial herbs, 2.2-3.7 dm tall; stems canescent, becoming dark and glabrate. Leaves cauline, crowded, only slightly reduced upwards, sessile, 3.3-6 cm long, 0.7-2.5 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, widest at or rarely below the mid- dle, apically acute to obtuse, basally cuneate to rounded, marginally revolute and remotely toothed, glabrous, sometimes arachnoid along midvein above, canescent beneath. Inflorescences of 1 or 2 (rarely more) heads on relatively long peduncles. Heads ca 69-103-flowered; peduncles 2-12 cm long, canescent. Involucre broadly campanulate, 12-30 mm high, 14-21 mm wide; phyllaries imbricate in several series, the outer series leaflike and usually exceeding the inner series, the inner ones oblong, acute, 8-15.5 mm long, 1.7-2.6 mm wide, the outer ones lanceolate, canescent dorsally, 14-20 mm long, 2-4.8 mm wide. Pappus straw-colored, the inner bristles 8-11 mm long and outer scale-like bristles 1.2-3 mm long. Corollas 9.2-16.5 mm long, reddish-purple, glabrous. Anthers 3.5-5 mm long. Achenes 34.7 mm long, 8-10 ribbed, strigose. Flowering and fruiting from December to April.

description: Herb 10-30 cm tall, branched from the base and above, rarely simple; glabrous except for sparse pubescence on peduncle and involucre; lower leaves 5-15 cm long, linear, entire, or with 1-3 linear lobes 1-3 cm long; upper leaves gradually reduced, entire, or 3-5 lobed; involuere 6-8 mm high, the 6-8 ovate phyllaries curved over the disk after flowering and slightly reflexed when achenes are ripe; ray florets 6-13, much exceeding the phyllaries, yellow (rarely white), with red stigmas; disk florets 30-70, 5-merous, yellow, their stigmas and pollen white; achenes 3-4 nmm long, strongly 4-6 alnoled; n = 9; self-in- compatible.

description: Plant annual or rarely biennial, mostly 3-.7 dm. high, finely strigose to moderately hirsute with long spreading hairs, sometimes almost glabrous; foliage appearing scanty; basal leaves mostly oblanceolate or elliptic, tapering to the petioles, entire or toothed, the blade and petiole up to 15 em. long and 25 mm. wide, usually smaller, often deciduous; cauline leaves linear to lanceolate; sometimes nearly as large as the basal ones, more commonly somewhat reduced, entire, or the lower and sometimes even the middle ones slightly toothed; heads several to very numerous in an open infloreseence; disk 5-12 mm. broad; involuere 2-5 mm. high; phyllaries subequal, or the outer slightly shorter, acute or acuminate, with brown midrib and light greenish or yellowish margins, finely and obscurely glandular and also more or less hairy; ligules about 50-100 (sometimes wanting), white, sometimes pink or bluish, 0.4-1.0 mm. wide, up to 6 mm. long; disk-corollas about 1.5-2.6 mm. long, the sharply marked tube about 0.2-0.5 mm. long, the lobes about 0.2-0.4 mm. long; style-appendages very short, broad, and obtuse, about 0.05 mm. long; akenes hairy, 2-nerved; pappus double, the outer setose-squamellate, the inner of about 10-15 very fragile bristles, these wanting from the pistillate flowers.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Perennial herb with a taproot and branched caudex; stem 3-30 cm. long, spreading or erect, hirsute with appressed or closely aseending hairs; leaves hirsute with appressed-ascending hairs; basal leaves linear-oblanceolate, up to 10 cm. long and 4 mm. wide, usually much smaller, the margins, especially liear the base, more or less ciliate with coarse spreading hairs unlike the other hairs of the leaves, often irregularly so; cauline leaves reduced, linear, sometimes well distributed along the stem, sometimes all near the base; heads solitary or few, the disk 7-18 mm. wide; involuere 4-8 mm. high, sparsely or moderately hirsute or hispid-hirsute with spreading hairs, and more or less glutinous or finely glandular; phyllaries subequal, narrow, green, usually with brown midrib and yellowish margins and tips; ligules about 35-100, white, sometimes pink or blue, 5-14 mm. long, 0.7-2.2 mm. wide; disk corollas about 2.7-4.2 mm. lolng, the tube 0.6-1.0 mm., the lobes 0.4-0.7 mm.; style-appendages deltoid and acutish to ovate and rounded-obtuse, about 0.15-0.2 mm. long; pappus double, the inner of about 12-20 slender and fragile white bristles, the outer of setae or narrow squamellae, sometimes obscure; akenes 2-nerved, finely hairy. Western Idaho and adjacent northeastern Oregon, to Wyoming, western Colorado, and southeastern Utah.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Plants annual, erect, slender, ea 2.6 dm high; stems strigose; leaves linear, sessile, entire, scabrous, up to 5 cm long and 4 mm wide; peduncles flaring at the apex, strigose, up to 3 em long; heads broadly campanulate, 4-5 mm high, phyllaries ea 9, linear, uniseriate, essentially glabrous, spreading at maturity, margins narrowly hyalinie; rays 5-9, glabrous, yellow, usually opposite a phyllary, ovate, weakly reflexed, ea 4 mm high, 8-10 green-nierved outside, nearly coriaceous, apex 2-lobed, basal margins adnate to the entire achene apex but corolla not tubed, style glabrous, branch apices truncate; ray achene ea 4 mm long, broadly obtriangular, 3-angled, cartilagenous, base and apex truncate, the 3 awns very short and very stout; disk corollas numerous, ea 2 mm high with distinct tube and limb, glabrous except for a few hairs, usually yellow, very small with thickened margins, anthers with concave, lanceolate apices, filaments thickened above, style branch apices obtuse, base of style conspicuously dilated; peripheral disk achenes ea 3.5 mm long, 3-4 angled, tuberculate, essentially glabrous, central achenes compressed, winged, all disk achenes apparently awnless; paleae not persistent, linear, glabrous, reddish-brown at apex, greenish below, apex acuminate; receptacle elongate conical; n = 11.
