description: Cespitose, matted, appressed pubescent perennial with numerous short leafy stems arising from a deep woody taproot, the stems covered by closely imbricate 2-ranked persistent stipules and petioles. Leaves numerous, the petioles as long as or several times as long as the always 3 leaflets, the frequently longitudinally folded leaflets linear, narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate or obovate, acute to rounded or with an apiculum 0.5-1 mm long, entire, sparsely to densely appressed pubescent abaxially, glabrous to sparsely hairy adaxially, the central leaflet 0.6-(1.7)-3.2 cm long, 0.15-(0.3)-0.6 cm wide, the lateral leaflets oblique. Stipules scarious, often purple and glabrous at the proximal end, pubescent at the distal end, entire, fused to the petioles by over half their length, the free tip linear and green. Inflorescence capitate, borne on scapiform peduneles 2-(5)-17 cm long, the heads of 6-(12)-16 flowers in alternate pairs or in 2-3 whorls of descending number, the flowers erect even in age, the pale, green-veined scarious bracts lanceolate or reduced to ir- regularly toothed to entire often whitish scales, 0.2-7 mm long, frequently fused at the base. Flowers with ochroleucous to pale or light violet standards and at least the tips of the keel and wings strong violet or the entire corolla strong violet to strong purplish-violet, rarely white, 1.2-(1.4)-1.6 cm long, the appressed pubescent pedicels straight, 0.5-1.5 mm long, the calyx tube 2.5-3.5 mm long, the central lobal veins prominent, those of the bifurcating sinal veins evident, the sinus rounded, the lobes linear-lanceolate, the laterals and abaxial longer than the adaxial, the longest lobe about 0.4-0.5 cm long. Standard elliptic-ovate, 0.6-0.8 cm wide, 1.2-1.5 cm long, apiculate with an apical fold, occasionally retuse; wings 1.3 cm long, the blade 0.6-0.8 cm long, 0.25 cm wide; keel slightly shorter than the wings, the blades 0.5-0.6 cm long, the claws free except below. Staminal sheath free, the anthers 0.6 mm long. Style 0.45-0.5 cm long, the ovary slender, appressed pube- scent. Legume 0.4-0.6 cm long, oblong, appressed pubescent, the 1-3 seeds dark brown. Fig. 1.

description: Glabrous, matted cespitose perennial with numerous short thickened leafy stems arising from a deep woody taproot up to 1 cm thick. Stems clothed in the closely imbricate persistent stipules and petioles. Leaves abundant and closely imbricate, the petioles up to several times longer than the leaflets; leaflets 3, oblanceolate to obovate, serrate to entire, acute to somewhat mucronate, 3-11 mm long, 1.5-5 mm wide, glabrous or with a few scattered hairs on the abaxial surface, the base at- tenuate. Stipules obliquely lanceolate, entire, the margins scarious, the margin fused to the petioles for one-third its length. Inflorescence nearly sessile or the peduncle up to 4 cm long, of usually 2, occasionally 1, rarely 3-4, strict flowers, the pale cupular floral bracts triangular, acute to attenuate, 0.5-1 mm long, fused below to form a reduced involucre. Flowers pale to light purplish violet changing to dark violet in dried specimens, occasionally white, becoming brown with age, 15-23 mm long, the often purple pedicels 1.5-2 mm long; calyx glabrous, whitened in age, 4-6 mm long, the tube 3.5-4 mm long, slightly gibbous adaxially, the lobal and sinal veins prominent, the lobes triangular, the usually shorter and closely paired adaxial ones to 1.5 mm long, the lateral 2 mm long, the abaxial 2.4 mm long. Standard broadly ovate, to 7 mm wide, the claw fused to the wings at the base; wings 14-15 mm long, the blade 8.5 mm long, appressed half the length to the slightly shorter keel blade, wings and keel fused to the staminal sheath for about half the length of their claws. Staminal filaments fused to about half the length of the keel blades, the anthers ca 0.8 mm long. Style 7-7.5 mm long, the ovary slender, glabrous. Legume glabrous, oblong, somewhat narrowed below, the walls reticulate, membranaceous, shattering easily, 1-4 seeded, the seeds smooth, 1-1.5 mm long. Fig. 3.

description: Perennial, forming patches from branched, slender rhizomes, older plants with a thick taproot bearing numerous leafy tipped stems frequently clothed with persistent stipules, the plants usually glabrous but often with scattered reddish-brown scale-like hairs or processes particularly on the upper part of the peduncle. Leaves numerous, the leaflets always 3, glabrous, elliptic to obovate, entire to serrate or dentate, acute to obtuse, rarely retuse, minutely apiculate, 1-(2.4)-4.1 cm long, 0.5-(1)-1.6 cm wide. Stipules membranaceous, obliquely ovate, scarious, lead- colored, occasionally purple, with prominent veins, the free margin entire or wavy toothed, the apex obtuse, acute or rarely somewhat attenuate, 1-2 cm long and to 1 cm broad. Inflorescence capituliform, of 15-20 flowers borne on a stout scapi- form peduncle extending above the leaves, the scarious oblong bracts frequently fused along the margin in pairs in the lower floral whorl, free in the upper whorls, the margin entire, the apex rounded, acute, bifid or irregular, the veins several, reticulate above. Flowers 1.2-2.2 cm long, the standard and wings pale purplish- violet, the keel strong purplish-violet turning strong violet in dried specimens; calyx glabrous, whitish, 6-9 mm long, the tube 3-4 mm long, very slightly gibbous, the lobes subulate to narrowly triangular, acute, with prominent green veins, the adaxial pair to 2 mm long, the lateral and abaxial to 3 mm long, the sinus smoothly curved, sinal veins frequently absent. Standard (when spread out) broadly ovate, to 9 mm wide, obtuse to acute; wings 14-15 mm long, the blade 8 mm long, ap- pressed in the lower part to the slightly shorter keel. Staminal filaments fused to the keel claws up to about the base of the blades, the anthers ca 0.5 mm long. Style ca 6 mm long, the ovary slender, oblong, glabrous or with a few scattered flattened scale-like processes, ovules 4. Legume to 6 mm long, oblong, the broad stipe to 1 mm long, the seeds 1-4, smooth, to 2 mm long. Fig. 2.

description: Liana or tree 6-40 m tall, 8-30 cm dbh. Leaves 23-34 cm long, stipules persistent, spinescent, 6-9 x 4-5 mm; rachis striate and glabrous; leaflets 7-11 (-13), obovate or elliptic, 4-20 x 2-8.5 cm, somewhat rough, glabrous above, brown-yellow puberulous below, the margin repand, the base rounded or obtuse, the apex cuspidate, sometimes emarginate; midvein prominent; secondary venation craspedodromus; tertiary venation parallel; petiolule 4 mm long. Inflorescence an axillary or terminal pseudopanicle, 15-34 cm long, composed of racemes 3-7 cm long; bracts spinescent, 2-10 x 2-3 mm; peduncle yellowish-brown puberulous to tomentose. Flowers greenish white, 9-10 mm long; sessile; bracteoles deltoid, 2 x 2 mm; calyx 3 mm, brown-tomentose, truncate; banner 10 x 4 mm, tomentose on the adaxial surface; keel petals 7 x 3.5 mm; wing petals 9 x 4 mm, with lamellate sculpturing; stamens monadelphous, 7-8 mm long, free part of filaments 1-1.2 mm long; style straight, 8 mm long, hirsute. Fruit a one-seeded samara, 5-8 x 1.3-2.5 cm, brown-puberulous when young, nearly glabrous at maturity; seed 1.5-2.3 cm.

description: Liana or scandent shrub, 3-15 m tall, 5-10 cm dbh. Stipules caducous, 2 x 2 mm; rachis brown-tomentose; leaflets glabrous above, yellowish-brown tomentose below, the margin swollen below, the base rounded or obtuse, the apex obtuse to acuminate, with a mucro 1 mm long or less; midvein prominent; secondary venation camptodromous; tertiary venation reticulate, obscure; petiolule 1.5-2 mm long. Inflorescence an axillary or terminal pseudopanicle, 8-24 cm, composed of racemose branches, these clustered into fascicles 2-3.5 cm long; peduncle brown-tomentose to-hirsute. Flowers purple, sessile; bracteoles ovate, 3 mm; calyx 3-4 mm long, pubescent, with five obtuse teeth; banner 8-10 x 6-9 mm, woolly on adaxial surface; keel petals 6-8 x 3-4 mm, sparsely hirsute above; wing petals 6-8 x 2.6-4 mm, hirsute above, with lamellate sculpturing; stamens diadelphous, 6-8 mm long, the free part of filaments 1-1.5 mm long; style curved.

description: Plants perennial, caespitose herbs, 2-2.5 dm tall; stems inconspicuous at anthesis, mostly hidden by the imbricated stipules in the lower portion, only one or two internodes below the peduncle visible, finely sericeous with closely ap- pressed hairs less than 1 mm long; stipules 1.5-2 cm long, the free tips lance- triangular, acuminate, 5-7 mm long, strigose dorsally; petioles finely and sparsely appressed puberulent, with some scattered hairs 1-2 mm long, the largest 15-20 cm long, somewhat fistulose; leaflets 9-11, elliptic-oblanceolate, glabrous above or occasionally sparsely strigose, finely sericeous to canescent below, tips acute-acuminate, the largest 5-6 cm long, 6-8 mm wide; peduncles 10-20 mm long, finely sericeous; racemes 8-10 cm long, rachis finely sericeous, flowers scattered to subverticillate; bracts 6-8 mm long, lance-acuminate, strigose dorsally; pedi- cels 2.5-3 mm long at anthesis, to 5 mm long in fruit, thinly hispidulose, the hairs ca 0.5 mm long; calyces strigose to spreading pilose outside, glabrous within except the tips of the lips, lower lip 5-7 mm long, triangular, base 2.5 mm wide, tip subentire to truncate-erose, upper lip 4.3-4.8 mm long, bifid, the notch 2.5- 3 mm deep, lobes 1.5 mm wide below, lips connate 1.4 mm, bracteoles linear to narrowly triangular, 1-1.5 mm long, attached 0.4 mm below the lips of the lateral sinuses; banner suborbicular, glabrous, 8.5-9 mm long, 6-9.5 mm wide appressed 4-4.5 mm, reflexed 3.2-4.5 mm, r/a ratio ca 1, the angle ca 135-140º; wings 8.5-10 mm long, 4.4-5.4 mm wide, the claw ca 2 mm long, lobe above the claw ca 1.5 mm wide, keel glabrous or with a few cilia above distally, 2-2.5 mm wide in the middle, the angle ca 95-105º; ovules 4-5; legumes 2 cm long, 6 mm wide, with abundant ascending curly hairs; seeds 3-4, tan with brown mottling, 3-3.6 mm long, 2.4 mm wide, funicular pit 0.4 mm in diam.

description: Tufted long-lived suffrutescent perennial herbs from woody taproot and repeatedly forking caudex beset with blanched wiry marcescent stem-bases and leafstalks of preceding seasons, the numerous slender, stiffly flexuous terete hornotinous stems erect and ascending (0.5) 1-1.5 dm, simple or once branched, the whole appearing glabrous but the stems, leaf-stalks, margin and dorsal face of leaflets, and axis of loosely few-flowered racemes remotely strigulose with straight appressed basifixed hairs 0.2-0.4 mm, the foliage pale green or subglaucescent concolorous. Stipules submembranous or the uppermost green-tipped, mostly erect, broadly triangular or deltate 0.8-2 mm, the lowest decurrent-amplexicaul around ±2/3 the stem, none connate. Leaves (3.5) 5-12 cm, with wiry tapering rachis shallowly sulcate ventrally and 4-6 (7) remote, distally decrescent pairs of shortly petiolulate, obovate, oblong-obovate or -elliptic obtuse or emarginate plane leaflets 2.5-7 mm, all carinate dorsally by the midrib but otherwise superficially veinless, the small terminal leaflet raised well above the distal pair. Racemes very loosely 2-5-flowered, the flowers widely ascending, the axis together with elongate peduncle becoming (3.5) 5-11 cm, as long or a little shorter than the subtending leaf; bracts membranous pallid triangular-lanceolate 1.1-2.2 mm; pedicels narrowly ascending straight or nearly so, in fruit becoming 2.4-6 (in an abnormal grallator form -18) mm, persistent with the fruit; bracteoles 0-2. Calyx 6.3-7.5 mm, sparsely white- or black-strigulose, the disc 1-1.3 mm deep, the campanulate tube 4-4.5 x 2.6-3 mm, the subequal lance-subulate erect teeth 1.8-3 mm, the whole marcescent unruptured around base of pod. Petals beyond pallid claws reddish-purple drying bluish; banner recurved through ±45º, rhombic-obovate-cuneate 12-14 x 8.5-10 mm; wings 11-12.5 mm, the claw 4-5 mm, the narrowly lance-oblong, gently incurved blade 8-9.5 x 2.8-3 mm, obtuse or obscurely emarginate at apex; keel 8.8-10.3 mm, the claws 4-5.3 mm, the triangular blade 5.5-6.5 x 3.3-3.5 mm, abruptly incurved through 90º to the triangular-deltate, scarcely porrect apex; anthers 0.5-0.6 mm; ovary strigulose. Pod stiffly widely ascending, stipitate, the stipe 1-1.5 mm, concealed by the marcescent calyx, the body lunately linear-oblanceolate in profile 15-21 x 2.8-3.8 mm, at base gradually tapering downward into the stipe, at apex abruptly contracted to the persistent recurved glabrous style, the body trigonously compressed, carinate ventrally by the gently concave suture, openly grooved dorsally, the lateral angles rounded, the lateral faces almost plane, the ripe valves stiffly papery stramineous, purple-suffused toward the sun, delicately transverse-venulose, inflexed below the short triangular 1-locular beak as an almost complete septum 1-1.3 mm wide; dehiscence apical, through the gaping beak, the valves finally coiling outward; ovules 16-19. Seeds (few seen) ±2.5 mm, the greenish, yellow-tinged testa irregularly pitted.

description: Dwarf perennial herbs from initial taproot with horizontally creeping subterranean stems up to 2 dm long, the emersed leafy axis only 1-2 cm, bearing usually 4-6 crowded leaves and only one subterminal raceme, the stems and foliage strigulose with straight appressed basifixed hairs up to 0.3-0.4 mm, the narrow, loosely folded leaflets cinereous dorsally, glabrous and pale green above, the inflorescence black-strigulose; stipules at buried nodes membranous ±1-1.5 mm, semiamplexicaul, those subtending developed leaves thinly herbaceous, broadly lanceolate or ovate-acuminulate 1.5-6 x 1-2 mm, variably decurrent on stem but free opposite the petiole; leaves 2.5-5 cm, the petiole 7-13 mm, the leaflets (7) 9-15 linear-oblanceolate or -elliptic, obtuse or subapiculate (3) 4-11 x 1.5-2 mm; peduncles incurved to vertical 1.5-2.5 cm; racemes shortly 7-10-flowered, the flowers early declined, the axis not or scarcely elongating, in fruit ± 1 cm; bracts membranous, narrowly ovate 1-1.5 mm; pedicels early recurved, in fruit ±41 mm, persistent; calyx 4.2-5.8 mm, the campanulate tube 2.6-3 x 2.2-2.4 mm, the subulate teeth 1.6-2.8 mm, the tube ruptured by the expanding ovary; petals lemon-yellow concolorous, the broadly obovate-cuneate banner ±8-8.5 x 6 mm, the wings 5.6-6.2 mm, the keel ±6 mm, its blades +3.5 x 2.3 mm, incurved through 100º to the obtusely deltate apex; anthers 0.55-0.7 mm; ovary glabrous; ovules 18; pod deflexed, sessile, tardily disjointing from the receptacle, obliquely ovoid or semi-ovoid 8-10.5 x 4-5.5 mm, subtruncate at base, abruptly and very shortly triangular-acuminulate at apex, obtusely trigonous, carinate ventrally by the slenderly 3-ribbed suture, rounded on lateral angles, openly sulcate dorsally, the valves at first carnosulous green purple-speckled becoming coriaceous stramineous, inflexed dorsally below the short 1-locular beak as a complete septum ±2 mm wide; dehiscence and seeds unknown.

description: Dwarf tufted, strictly acaulescent perennial herbs, the leaves and scapiform peduncles arising directly from the thickened crown of a vertical taproot, not developing an aerial caudex, except for the glabrous upper face of leaflets, the faces of stipules and the glabrous pistil, pilose throughout with fine weak spreading basifixed hairs up to 1.2-2 mm, the foliage notably bicolored, yellow-green above, blue-green beneath. Stipules imbricated on rootcrown, adnate through 2.5-6 mm to petiole, the lanceolate or lance-attenuate submembranous, early papery free blades (3) 4-8 mm. Leaves radially spreading, mostly humistrate 4-13 (15) cm, the petiole 1.5-4.5 (5) cm deciduous, the rachis 1.5-8.5 (10.5) cm; leaflets (5) 9-15 (17), of subequal length or a little descrescent distally, all broadly obovate emarginate or obcordate, the larger ones 8-16 mm. Peduncles stout 2-8.5 cm, early procumbent, prostrate in fruit; racemes shortly (4) 6-16-flowered, the flowers widely ascending, the axis not elongating, in fruit 0.4-3.5 cm; bracts lanceolate submembranous 4-8 mm; pedicels at anthesis 1-1.5 mm, in fruit ascending thickened 1.2-2 mm, persistent. Calyx thinly white-pilose 10.5-12.5 mm, the oblique disc ± 1.5 mm deep, the cylindric tube 2-bracteolate at base 8-9.4 x 3.7-4 mm. Petals (not seen fresh) bluish-purple when dry; banner recurved through ±30º, rhombic-oblanceolate 21.5-23.5 x 7-9.5 mm, emarginate at the narrowed apex; wings 17.5-19.5 mm, the claw 10.5-11 mm, the straight lanceolate blade 8.5-10 x 2.5 mm; keel 16.5-18 mm, the claws 10.5-11.5 mm, the lunately half-elliptic blades 7-7.5 x 2.5-3 mm, gently incurved through ±40º to the rounded apex; anthers 0.7-0.8 mm. Pod humistrate, when ripe readily disjointing from the receptacle, in profile shallowly lunate-elliptic (2.5) 3-5 (5.5) x 0.65-0.9 cm, abruptly obtuse at base, contracted distally into a triangular acuminulate 1-locular beak, trigonously compressed, carinate by the gently concave ventral suture, openly sulcate dorsally, the lateral angles obtuse, the smooth lustrous green or (toward the sun) purple-brown-tinged subcarnosulous valves becoming coriaceous stramineous, inflexed below the beak as a complete septum 3-4 mm wide; dehiscence both apical and basal, after falling, the valves gaping and recurved at both ends; ovules 30-34. Seeds mitten-shaped (3) 3.2-4 mm, the ochraceous or greenish-brown, purple-speckled testa sublustrous rugulose.

description: Species affinitatis paradoxae, pube dolabriformi et legumine emmenolobo pendulo turgido 1 -loculari cum A. ceramico Sheld. comparabilis, sed ab ea ut ab omnibus sect. Cusickianis adhuc relatis caulibus numerosis abbreviatis e radicis verticalis collo superficiali nascentibus, habitu ergo caespitoso (fere sect. piptolobam Desperatos revocanti) aliena, ulterius a var. ceramico (sympatrica sed quoad oecologiam vero distanti) foliolis omnibus petiolulatis, florum paullo minorum carina ±4-5 (nec 6.5-8) mm longa necnon legumine parvulo subsessili 8-14 (nec 15-30) mm longo diversa.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1983. Dragma Hippomanicum IX. A new Astragalus (Leguminosae: Astragalanae) from sandstone rimrock in New Mexico. Brittonia. 35: 109, 110.

description: Small tufted, shortly caulescent perennial herbs, gray-strigulose throughout with straight appressed or narrowly ascending dolabriform hairs up to 0.6-0.9 mm; stems numerous 1-5 (7) cm decumbent and incurved-ascending from superficial crown of taproot 1.5-3 mm diam, densely leafy, the early internodes not or little longer than stipules, some distal ones 5-12 mm but all much shorter than leaves. Stipules 2-5 mm, the small scarious lower ones amplexicaul and connate into a loose 2-dentate sheath, the upper ones ovate, thinly herbaceous, connate only at very base or free. Leaves (2) 2.5-8.5 cm, the relatively long wiry petioles sometimes persistent on caudex; leaflets 9-15, shortly petiolulate, elliptic or ovate-elliptic obtuse or subapiculate 2-8 X 0.8-2 mm, flat or loosely folded. Peduncles subfiliform 2-5.5 cm, ascending at anthesis, procumbent in fruit; racemes loosely or remotely 5-10 (14)-flowered, the ascending flowers declined in age, the axis becoming (1) 1.5-4 cm; bracts submembranous ovate 0.7-1.2 mm; pedicels very slender 1-1.6 mm, in fruit recurved or contorted, scarcely thickened, disjointing with the ripe fruit. Calyx 3.3-4 mm, the campanulate purplish white- or blackstrigulose ebracteolate tube 2.1-2.7 mm, the subulate teeth subequal 1-1.4 mm; petals whitish lilac-tinged distally, the keel purple-tipped; banner recurved through ±45º, amply rhombic-obovate emarginate 5.5-6 X 4.5-4.8 mm; wings almost as long, the claw 1.8-1.9 mm, the oblanceolate subincurved concave blade 3.7-4 X 1.8-2 mm; keel 4.1-4.8 mm, the claws 1.8-2.2 mm, the semi-obovate blades incurved through ±95º to obtuse apex; anthers 0.3-0.45 mm; ovary strigulose; ovules 12-14 (16). Pod pendulous (unless humistrate) crypto-stipitate, the stipe less than 1 mm concealed by marcescent calyx, the body narrowly obovoid-ellipsoid 8-14 X 4-6 mm, turgid or almost bladdery, gently obcompressed, cuneately attenuate at base, obliquely apiculate at apex, the thin red-mottled valves becoming papery-membranous but opaque, not inflexed; seeds (few seen) ±2 X 1.5 mm, the testa stramineous rugulose.

description: Slender, diffuse or prostrate perennial herbs, strigulose-pilosulous almost through out with straight, ascending or forwardly appressed basifixed hairs up to 0.5-0.7 mm, the foliage grayish-green, the lfts pubescent on both faces but sometimes medially glabrescent above; stems (1) 2-7 from crown of taproot or short caudex, subterra- nean through 1-9 cm, on emergence flexuously procumbent (1) 1.5-3.5 dm, simple or 1-2-branched below middle, thence floriferous from 2-5 distant nodes; stipules 1-5 mm, the lowest membranous pallid amplexicaul and connate into a cup or campanulate, shortly 2-dentate sheath, the rest herbaceous, deltate or triangular-lanceolate, almost or fully amplexicaul but connate only at extreme base or free; leaves 2.5-6 (6.5) cm, the petiole 5-18 mm; leaflets (9) 11-17 decrescent upward along rachis, in outline elliptic, oblong-elliptic or -obovate, emarginate or obtuse, 2-8.5 (10) mm, usually loosely folded, carinate dorsally by the midrib; peduncles incurved- ascending (3) 4.5-13 cm, longer than leaf; recemes loosely or remotely (2) 4.5-13- flowered, the flowers ascending, the axis becoming (0.5) 1.5-9 cm; bracts herba- ceous becoming dry but persistent, ovate or broadly lanceolate 1-2 mm; pedicels ascending straight or subarcuate, at anthesis 1.2-2 mm, in fruit scarcely thickened 1.5-2.6 mm, deciduous with calyx and pod; bracteoles 0; calyx 5.4-7.6 mm, strigulose with pale hairs, the symmetrically campanulate disc 0.7-0.9 mm deep, the campanu- late tube 3.4-4.6 X 2.4-2.8 mm, the subulate teeth subequal 1.9-1.3 mm, the whole becoming papery, marcescent unruptured; petals "pale yellow," ochroleucous when dry, immaculate, of subequal length, 9-9.8 mm; banner abruptly recurved through +/- 75º, the obovate-suborbicular blade 6-9 mm wide; claw of wings 4-5 mm, the oblanceolate, broadly obtuse, slightly incurved blade 5.2-6 X 2.2-2.7 mm; claws of keel 4-4.7 mm, the lunately semi-elliptic blades 5.2-5.6 X 2.2-2.7 mm, incurved through +/- 75º to the triangular, scarcely porrect, obtuse apex; anthers 0.5-0.8 mm; pod ascending, obscurely stipitate, the stipe 1-1.5 mm continuous with receptacle, the body lunately elliptic-oblanceolate in profile (13) 15-23 x 3.3-4 mm, ventrally carinate by the gently concave suture, below middle compressed-trigonous with obtuse lateral angles, openly sulcate, thence laterally compressed and contracted into a triangular-acuminate, finally dehiscent beak, the thin strigulose-pilosulous mottled valves inflexed below middle of pod as an incipient septum to 0.5 mm wide or this (in shorter pods) obsolete; ovules 10-12; seeds (few seen) 2.2-2.6 mm, the testa yellowish-tan, sublustrous, obscurely pitted.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1977. Dragma Hippomanicum III: Novitates Californicae. Brittonia. 29: 376-381.

description: Dwarf cryptophytic alpine herbs, the slender subterranean, sometimes adventitiously rooting caudex-branches charged with distant stipule-sheaths, the hornotinous emersed leafy stems only 1-2 cm long, these and the foliage pilosulous with ascending basifixed hairs up to 0.3-0.4 mm, the leaflets green, either pubescent on both faces or glabrescent above; stipules membranous pallid, fully amplexicaul and connate into a 2-dentate sheath 2-3 mm long; leaves (1.5) 2-7 (8) cm long, the lower ones longer- and the upper shorter-petiolate, the leaflets 9-15 (very rarely 17) subsessile, in outline lance- or ovate-elliptic, obtuse or acute 2-7 x (0.7) 1-2.5 (3) mm, plane or loosely conduplicate; peduncles at anthesis incurved-ascending, in fruit procumbent (0.5) 1-4 cm long; racemes (1) 2-(3)-flowered, the flowers ascending, the axis (0) 1-3 mm long; bracts membranous, lanceolate 1.5-2.5 mm; pedicels ascending 1-1.8 mm long; calyx ebracteolate, loosely black-strigulose (5) 5.7-6.7 mm long, the subsymmetrical hypanthium 1 mm deep, the campanulate tube (3) 3.4-4 x 2.1-2.4 mm, the slenderly subulate, erect teeth 1.8-3.3 mm long, the whole marcescent, either unruptured or split ventrally, about base of pod; petals whitish lavender-tinged, the banner striate, the keel purple-tipped; banner recurved through ±50º, oblong-obovate retuse 11-12 x 5.5-6 mm; wings ±10 mm, the claw 4.5 mm, the narrowly elliptic, gently incurved, obtuse blade 6.5 x 2 mm; keel 9-9.5 mm, the claws 4.5 mm, the lunately half-elliptic blades 5-5.7 x 2.1 mm, incurved through nearly 900 to the obtusely triangular apex; ovary sessile, strigulose or rarely glabrous; ovules 8-9; pod ascending (humistrate), sessile, not disjointing from the receptacle but falling with calyx and pedicel, in profile obliquely lance-ovate, acuminate, including the attenuate, incurved beak (but excluding the persistent style) 10-12 x 3-3.5 mm, the body bluntly trigonous, obtusely keeled ventrally by the suture, shallowly depressed dorsally, the lateral angles broadly rounded, the submembranous, when ripe thinly papery semitransparent, sometimes minutely purple-speckled valves either black-strigulose or glabrous, not inflexed; seeds mitten-shaped 2.5-2.7 x 1.8-2 mm, the smooth testa pale brown, unmottled.

description: Statura caespitosa, pube dolabriformi necnon legumine minuto 1-loculari cum sect. Humillimis Barneby congrua, sed ab ea floribus solitariis axillari-radicalibus arcte sessilibus, calycis tubo cylindrico, foliis eximie dimorphis synanthis brevissimis 3-5-foliolatis, hysteranthis elongatis 5-7-foliolatis basi stipulis breviter inter se contra petiolum connatis suffultis, necnon legumine subgloboso-pyriformi nullimodo compresso valde diversa, iisdem notis subsect. Nothorophacam Barneby, subsect. nov., constituens; a sect. Orophaca (A. Gray) Coult. & Nels. quoad habitum pubemque comparabili imprimis foliis pinnatis (nec palmatim 3-foliolatis), stipulis haud hyalinis, leguminisque forma remotior.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1979. Dragma Hippomanicum IV.New taxa of Astragalus sect. Humillimi. Brittonia. 31: 459-463.

description: Diminutive, densely cespitose perennial herbs with woody taproot and repeatedly forking caudex thatched with recurving marcescent petioles, forming depressed cushions of foliage up to 3 dm diam, in habit seasonally dimorphic, at vernal anthesis acaulescent, the short 3-5-foliolate leaves then not surpassing the solitary sessile radical flowers, the stems lengthening after anthesis and becoming 1.5-3 cm, composed of 3-5 developed internodes each bearing a much longer 5-7-foliolate leaf with filiform petiole, the foliage at all stages of growth silvery-strigulose with dolabriform hairs up to 0.5-0.7 mm, the pods remaining sessile at base of the mature stems. Stipules membranous pallid dimorphic, the vernal ones imbricated ovate-triangular ± 2 mm, almost fully amplexicaul but free, those subtending hysteranthous leaves lanceolate 3-5 mm, fully amplexicaul and shortly connate opposite the petiole. Leaves dimorphic: (a) synanthous radical ± 7-13 mm, the petiole not over 1 cm, the 3 palmate or 5 subpalmate leaflets oblanceolate obtuse 2-4 mm; and (b) hysteranthous cauline 2-6 cm, pinnately 5-7-foliolate, the erect petiole 2-4 cm, the rachis 3-16 mm, the leaflets linear-oblanceolate or -elliptic acute (5)6-12 mm. Peduncles obsolete 1-flowered, the erect flower itself sessile, subtended by an ovate submembranous bract ± 2.5 mm; bracteoles 0. Calyx 8-10 mm, the subsymmetric disc 0.7 mm deep, the cylindric tube 6-6.7 x 2-2.5 mm, the linear-subulate subequal teeth 2-3.3 mm, the whole marcescent but ruptured by the pod. Petals glabrous, purple beyond the pale claws and drying violet, the almost erect, broadly oblanceolate truncate-emarginate banner 14-16.5 x 6 mm; wings 14.5-17 mm, the claw 7.6-10.5 mm, the oblong- oblanceolate obtuse blade 7.2-7.5 x 1.8-2.1 mm; keel 11-13 mm, the claws 7-9 mm, the lunately half-elliptic blade ± 4.6 x 1.9 mm, incurved through ? 450 to the obtuse apex. Anthers 0.6-0.7 mm. Ovary strigulose. Pod strictly sessile, inversely plumply pyriform, the almost globose body 3 mm diam abruptly con- tracted into an erect subulate beak + 1.5 mm, the sutures equally convex, scarcely prominent, the firm green valves neither depressed nor sulcate, not inflexed; dehiscence not seen; ovules 7-8; seeds obliquely reniform ± 1.9 x 1.5 mm, the testa smooth lustrous brown purple-speckled.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1979. Dragma Hippomanicum IV.New taxa of Astragalus sect. Humillimi. Brittonia. 31: 459-463.

description: Quoad stipulas saltem imas breviter amplexicauli-connatas necnon floris parvi leguminisque triquetrim compressi structuram cum sect. Neonice perfecte congrua, sed satura nana caespitosa, petiolis mox induratis erinacea foliolisque minimis praestans, ab A. mulfordae M. E. Jones habitu toto necnon legumine minori, ab A. peckii Piper, petiolis rigescentibus comparabili, imprimis legumine stipitato subaequaliter 3-faciali (nec subsessili de latere compresso, facie dorsali angustiori sulcata) diversa.

description: Dwarf, densely tufted but shortly caulescent suffruticose herbs with multicipital taproot and closely branched caudex armed with stiff straight, weakly pungent annotinous and older leaf-stalks, the hornotinous stems 1-3 cm, their longer internodes 2-7 mm, the foliage of stiff tapering leaf-stalks and minute leaflets green but sparsely strigulose with subappressed basifixed hairs up to 0.25-0.4 mm, the filiform, remotely few-flowered racemes shorter than or barely equalling the leaves. Stipules membranous pallid + 1.2-2.2 mm, adnate to petiole through 1-1.5 mm, fully amplexicaul, at least the lowest shortly, sometimes obscurely connate opposite the petiole, the free blades deltate 0.6-1.7 mm. Leaves 2.5-4.5 cm; leaflets (7) 9-17 (19), opposite or scattered, decrescent distally, obovate, elliptic or linear-elliptic obtuse conduplicate, the lateral ones minutely petiolulate 0.7-3 mm, the terminal one 0.3-0.8 mm remote from the distal pair, either petiolulate or decurrent into the rachis. Racemes distantly 2-8-flowered, the peduncle 2-9 mm, often shorter than the distance between flowers; bracts membranous ovatetriangular 0.5-0.9 mm persistent; pedicels (1) 1.4-2.7 mm, early arcuate, disjointing with the ripe pod. Calyx 2.3-3 mm, strigulose with white or sometimes a few fuscous hairs, the symmetrical disc 0.5-0.6 mm deep, the campanulate tube 1.4-2,2 x 1.3-1.6 mm, the subulate or deltate teeth (0.3) 0.5-1.1 mm, the whole marcescent unruptured about the pod's stipe. Petals whitish, the banner faintly pink-striate internally; banner reflexed through ±50-85º, rhombic-elliptic emarginate 4.8-6.2 x 4-4.6 mm; wings nearly as long as banner, the claw 1.6-2.4 mm, the elliptic obtuse blade 4.1-4.5 x 1.4-2 mm; keel 3.8-4.4 mm, the claws 1.7-2 mm, the nearly semicircular blades 2.2-2.4 x 1.6-1.8 mm, incurved through ± 120º to the obtusely deltate apex; anthers 0.3-0.4 mm. Ovary strigulose; ovules 7-8. Pod naturally pendulous but often in fact confined among petioles and ascending, stipitate, the stipe 1.2-3 mm, the body in profile elliptic 4-7 x 2-2.8 mm, abruptly contracted at base into the stipe and at apex into a subulate stylebase, trigonously compressed, keeled ventrally by the gently convex suture, the equally wide faces all flat or slightly concave, the lateral angles narrow but obtuse, the pale green strigulose valves becoming papery stramineous, inflexed as a complete septum 1.1-1.8 mm wide; seeds 1.7-1.9 mm, the smooth testa ochraceous or pale greenish, not speckled.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1980. Dragma Hippomanicum VI: a new tragacanthoid Astragalus [A. yoderwilliamsii] from Nevada and Idaho. Brittonia. 32: 30-32.

description: Erect shrubs to 2.5 m with naked annotinous and densely leafy hornotinous branches, except for glabrescent upper face of the ample, strictly ascending 2- foliolate leaves, finely villosulous and setulose throughout, the setules arborescently villosulous, 0.3-0.6 mm, the foliage subconcolorous, the leaflets sublustrously olivaceous above, dull and slightly paler beneath, the inflorescence of few-flowered racemes axillary to distal leaves and not or little exserted. Stipules erect, narrowly subulate, ? 1.5 mm, deciduous. Leaves 3.5-6.5 cm, upwardly imbricate along stems, stoutly short-petioled, the petiole including scarcely swollen pulvinus 3-6 mm, at middle openly shallow-sulcate, + 1-1.5 mm diam, rounded dorsally; leaflets 1 pair, strictly ascending, turned half face to face on pulvinule 1.5-2.5 mm, in outline obovate obtuse, abruptly mucronate by excurrent midrib, 3.5-6 x 1.5-2.8 cm, at base subsymmetrically cuneate, the margin revolute, the straight centric midrib canaliculate ventrally, cariniform dorsally, the 7-10 pairs of camptodrome with fainter intercalary secondary veins subimmersed above, finely prominulous beneath, the faint irregular tertiary venulation prominulous only beneath. Peduncles scarcely longer than petiole; racemes shortly 2-5-flowered; bracts subulate, 4 mm, caducous; pedicels erect, 9-12 mm, bracteolate 3-4 mm below calyx; bracteoles subulate, 1.5 mm, caducous; flower-buds narrowly ovoid acuminate, villosulous and setulose; sepals yellow, the inner petaloid, all lanceolate acute, ± 1 cm; petals (of sect. Absus) yellow, glabrous, 4 narrowly obovate, 12 mm, the obliquely elliptic- oblanceolate fifth one ± as long; androecium 10-merous, the filaments 1.2-1.5 mm, the anthers 3-3.5 mm, the connective produced as a minute point ± 0.1 mm; ovary white-villosulous; ovules 5-6; style filiform, glabrous, ± 8 mm.

description: Inter Nigricantes juxta Ch. tephrosiifoliam (Bentham) Irwin & Barneby et Ch. philippi (Irwin & Barneby) Irwin & Barneby inserenda, ab utraque caulibus inflorescentiaeque axibus setis elongatis 1-2 mm longis pube minuta puberula immixtis armatis, foliolorum venatione simpliciter paucivenia, ulterius a Ch. philippi, quoad racemos laxos exsertos comparanda, pedicellis brevioribus foliolisque angustioribus diversa.

description: Slender erect, amply leafy arborescent shrubs at anthesis 1-4 m, the hornotinous stems, leaf-stalks and axes of inflorescence at once minutely incurved-puberulent and hispid with erect viscid setae up to 1-2 mm, the foliage bicolored, the leaflets aboVe dark green, viscidly lustrous and puberulent, beneath paler dull, on both faces charged with resinous dots but not setulose, the inflorescence of loosely (10) 15-50-flowered racemes terminal to branchlets exserted. Stipules spreading lanceolate or triangular-subulate, 0.8-3 mm, caducous. Leaves 4.5-12 cm; petioles including moderately dilated pulvinus 1-3 cm, at middle 0.4-0.9 mm diam, bluntly 3-ribbed dorso-laterally, narrowly sulcate ventrally; rachis ± 2-5 cm; pulvinules 0.7-1.2 mm; leaflets 5-7 (8) pairs, ascending from rachis face upward, accrescent distally, lanceolate- or the shorter proximal ones ovate-acuminate, the distal pair 12-30 x 3-7 (8) mm, at base shallowly cordate on proximal and cuneate on distal side, the margin revolute, the slender centric straight or slightly incurved midrib with ± 5-7 pairs of camptodrome secondary veins prominulous on dorsal face, scarcely so or immersed on ventral one, tertiary venulation almost 0. Raceme-axis including very short peduncle becoming 4-16 cm; bracts narrowly lanceolate ± 3-3.5 x 0.6 mm, caducous; pedicels 6-10 mm, bracteolate shortly below calyx; flower-buds lanceolate in outline, acute, finely viscid-puberulent; sepals subpetaloid, of almost equal length, in few flowers seen ± 10.5 mm, the outer elliptic-, the inner ovate-acuminate; petals (of sect. Absus) yellow, 4 ± 13 mm, 1 abaxial much smaller and narrower; androecium 10-merous, the glabrous filaments 0.6-1 mm, the oblong anthers up to 3 mm, the connective muticous; ovary viscid-puberulent; style filiform, gently incurved distally, ± 6.5 x 0.3 mm, glabrous. Pod ascending, obliquely oblong-elliptic in outline, ± 30 x 7-8 mm, the castaneous valves obscurely venulose, densely puberulent and glandular-verruculose (not setose); seeds (1 seen) obovoid-ellipsoid, 4.5 x 2.2 mm, the atrocastaneous testa sublustrous almost smooth, the serial pits differentiated faintly by color but scarcely depressed.

description: Slender erect shrubs with purplish-brown naked trunks to 2 m, distally forking and densely leafy, the hornotinous branchlets and foliage finely villosulous and viscid-setulose throughout, the shortly exserted racemes more coarsely yellowish-setose, the amply bifoliolate leaves olivaceous concolorous, dull or sublustrous. Stipules subulate 1-1.5 mm caducous. Leaves 7-9.5 cm; petiole including wrinkled but not much dilated pulvinus 2.5-3.5 cm, at middle 0.7-1 mm diam; leaflets 1 pair, widely ascending from apex of petiole, turned half face-to-face on reddish pulvinule ± 2 mm, in outline obliquely lance-ovate-acuminate (3.5) 4-6 x 1.1- 2.3 cm, at base rounded on proximal and cuneate on distal side, the margin plane, the excentric, forwardly curved midrib with 6-8 pairs of camptodrome (+ random intercalary) and connecting tertiary venules all subequally bluntly prominulous on both faces, the intervenium only faintly irregularly reticulate. Racemes ± 20-40-flowered, the expanded flowers raised to or beyond level of the nodding ovoid- apiculate buds, the axis including very short or obsolescent peduncle becoming 4-8 cm; bracts subulate ± 1.5 mm deciduous; pedicels 17-34 mm, bracteolate 1.5-2 mm below calyx; sepals submembranous petaloid ovate subacute 8.5-11.5 mm, thinly hispid dorsally with setae 1-1.5 mm; petals unknown; anthers ± 4 mm, the connective muticous; ovary densely setulose; style ± 12 mm pilosulous, distally incurved glabrate. Pod unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Irwin, Howard S. & Barneby, Rupert C. 1979. Two new Brazilian species of Chamaecrista Moench [C. onusta, C. hatschoacliii] (Leguminosae : Caesalpinioideae). Brittonia. 31: 464-468.

description: Chamaecristae bahiae (Irwin) Irwin & Barneby ut videtur proxime affinis, ab ea foliorum majorum foliolis maximis (2) 3 (nec exacte 2)-jugis rachi 5-11 (nec 2.5-5) cm longo insidentibus, glandulis petiolaribus maximis 2-5.5 (nec 1-2.5) mm diam, calycisque sepalis extus glabris 7-10 X 4-6 (nec 3-5 X 2-3 mm, dorso fere semper velutino-pilosulis) diversa.
bibliographicCitation: Irwin, Howard S. & Barneby, Rupert C. 1979. Two new Brazilian species of Chamaecrista Moench [C. onusta, C. hatschoacliii] (Leguminosae : Caesalpinioideae). Brittonia. 31: 464-468.

description: Amply leafy, prolifically cauliflorus shrubs ± 2.5 m, with obliquely ascending, densely lenticellate branches, glabrous except for the minutely ciliolate sepals, the dorsally puberulent petals and the pilosulous androecium and pistil, the coriaceous subconcolorous foliage lustrous olivaceous, the corymbiform racemes of large flowers solitary or commonly several together from a short common axis arising from axil of fallen leaves. Stipules not seen, probably minute caducous. Leaves 16-37 cm; petiole including wrinkled pulvinus 2.2-5 cm, at middle 1.5-3.5 mm diam, narrowly shallowly sulcate ventrally; rachis 5-11 cm; glands sessile between each pair of leaflets, shallowly cupular round or almost so, coarsely thick-margined, 2-5.5 mm diam, sometimes accompanied close below by a smaller glandule; pulvinules 3-9 (10, of major leaves mostly 5+) mm; leaflets (2) 3 pairs accrescent distally, the furthest pair broadly elliptic-obovate, obscurely or very shortly and bluntly acuminate 4-19.5 x 5-10.5 cm, 1.8-2.2 times as long as wide, at asymmetric base cuneately decurrent onto the pulvinule, the coarse straight or slightly incurved midrib subimmersed above, prominent beneath, giving rise to ± 7-8 pairs of camptodrome and many intercalary secondary veins, the secondary, tertiary and reticular venules all subequally prominulous on both faces. Racemes sessile 2-15-flowered, the axis (0.2) 0.5-2.5 (3) cm charged with sessile cupular glands 0.5-2 mm diam; bracts ovate 0.6-1.2 mm, early dry caducous; mature pedicels glabrous 3.5-4.3 cm, bracteolate 3.5-9 mm below calyx; flower-buds globose glabrous; sepals firm subpetaloid yellow obovate-elliptic obtuse, little graduated, the longer ones 7-10 x 4.5-6 mm; petals bright yellow, dorsally puberulent below middle, all but one abaxial one similar, oblong-obovate beyond the short claw, 18-26 x 8-15 mm, the vexillary one a trifle wider and the longer abaxial one a trifle narrower than its neighbors, the short abaxial petal broadly obovate-flabellate 12-16 x 10-15 mm; androecium (normally) 10-merous, the anthers subequal subsessile, broadly lance-oblong in outline 6-7 mm, densely pilosulous; ovary (sometimes abortive) pilosulous; style ± 7 mm. Pod unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Irwin, Howard S. & Barneby, Rupert C. 1979. Two new Brazilian species of Chamaecrista Moench [C. onusta, C. hatschoacliii] (Leguminosae : Caesalpinioideae). Brittonia. 31: 464-468.

description: Plant to 1.8 m tall. Leaves unfoliolate, elliptic, obovate or oblong, 4.1-10 x 1-4.5 cm, at apex rounded, mucronulate or acute, at base cuneate or rounded, sericeous above and beneath. Stipules absent. Inflorescences terminal, 7-33 cm long, bearing 5-15 flowers, bracts lanceolate, 9-17 mm long, usually persistent. Bracteoles on base of calyx. Flowers 12.5-25 mm long; calyx 12.5-25 mm long, sericeous. Banner yellow, 14-21 x 10-15 mm, bearing two lamelliform appendages at base. Wing petals oblong-obovate, 12-17 x 4.5-7 mm, claws 1.5-2 mm long. Carina 14-21 x 7-10 mm, beak twisted. Stamens dimorphic, elongate anthers 3.2-4 mm long, short ones 0.8-0.9 mm long. Ovary oblong, with a sharply geniculate style, measuring 11-15 mm from bend. Legume 3.1-4.5 cm long. Seeds ?33, to 3 mm long, brown.
bibliographicCitation: Windler, Donald R. & Skinner, S. G. 1982. The taxonomy and nomenclature of Crotalaria foliosa (Leguminosae) and related species. Brittonia. 34: 342-345.

description: Plantae 1.8 m usque altae. Folia plerumque elliptica 3.9-6.9 x 1.8-4.1 cm, apice mucronulata, rotundata vel late acuta, basi late cuneata vel rotundata, utrinque sericea. Racemi 3-7-flori, 1.8-7 (8) cm longi.

description: Plants to 1.8 m tall. Leaves unifoliolate, usually elliptic, 3.9-6.9 x 1.8-4.1 cm, at apex mucronulate, rounded or broadly acute, at base broadly cuneate or round- ed, sericeous above and beneath. Stipules absent. Inflorescences terminal, 1.8-7 (8) cm long, bearing 3-7 flowers, bracts lanceolate or narrowly lanceolate, 10-12 mm long, usually persistent. Bracteoles on base of calyx. Flowers 15-23 mm long; calyx 15-23 mm long, sericeous. Banner yellow, 10-13 x 9-10 mm, bearing two lamelliform appendages at base. Wing petals oblong-ovate, 12.5-13 x 5.5-6 mm, claws 2-2.5 mm long. Carina 13-14 x 7-8 mm, beak twisted. Stamens dimorphic, elongate anthers 2.9-3.1 mm long, short ones 0.8-1 mm long. Ovary oblong, with a sharply geniculate style, measuring 8.5-9.5 mm from bend. Legume 4.2-4.6 cm long. Seeds ±26, to 3 mm long, brown.

description: Foliolorum numero, ambitu glabritieque cum D. nemaphyllidia Barneby et calycis forma pubeque ex ipso basi sericeo-pilosa propius cum D. polystachya (S. & M.) Barneby comparabilis, ab ea foliolis inter se secus rachin distantibus tuboque calycino extus sericeo-villosulo, ab hac foliolis minus numerosis 6-13 (nec 12-20)-jugis angustissime oblanceolato-linearibus ±5-13 (nec oblongis 3-6) mm longis manifeste diversa.

description: Perennial herbs with few, sparsely leafy stems at anthesis ±1 m, virgately erect from a stout xylopodioid taproot, the fertile ones like the mature foliage glabrous up to the oblong-cylindric silky-pilosulous flower-spikes, only some basal inno- vations finely gray-villosulous; stipules subulate <1 mm, caducous; leaves 3.5-11 cm, the petiole 6-11 mm, scarcely longer than the interfoliolar segments of rachis; leaflets (4-) 6-13 pairs, linear or linear-oblanceolate obtuse ±5-13 x 0.8- 1.2 mm, the thick-textured blade on upper face smooth pallid concave, on lower face convex, sparsely livid-punctate, the terminal leaflet sessile between the distal pair; peduncles (few seen) opposed to distal leaves ±6 (-?) cm; spikes excluding petals and androecia ±2 x 1.1 cm, the silky-pilose calyces contiguous subsessile; bracts narrowly lance-attenuate, internally glabrous, caducous unless held fast between crowded calyces; calyx silky-pilosulous from base upward ±5 mm, the campanulate tube a trifle shorter than the linear-attenuate teeth, the ribs slender livid, the hyaline intercostal panels charged with yellowish glands, these 2-seriate or scattered only in the broader adaxial pair; petals heterochrome, the banner opening whitish, fading reddish-purple, the epistemonous ones blue, pallid when dried, perched 1.2-4 mm from base of staminal column; banner ±6 mm, its obtusely deltate blade 3 x 2 mm, charged at base with a small gland-crescent; wings including short claw ±4.5 mm, the elliptic blade 3 x 1.5 mm; keel 7 mm, its claws 3.3 mm, its blades 4.3 x 2.3 mm, not gland-tipped; androecium 10-merous, 7 mm, the longest filament free for ±2 mm; pod unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1980. Three new species of Dalea sect. Parosela (Leguminosae: Amorpheae) from western and southern Mexico. Brittonia. 32: 392-396.

description: Affinis D. lamprostachyae Barneby, quacum foliolorum numero margineque glandulis impressis denticulato-undulata, bracteis persistentibus necnon calyce longidentato bene quadrat, sed ab ea imprimis floribus subdimidio minoribus, calycis tubo 1.5 (nec ±3) mm longo, carinae laminis 4 x 3 (nec 7 x 4.5) mm, calycisque dentibus tubo 2.5-4 (nec minus quam 2)-plo longioribus, ulterius foliolis a rachidi pulvinulo recurvo deflexis eximie diversa.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1981. New species of Dalea section Parosela (Leguminosae: Amorpheae) from Peru [D. strobilacea] and Mexico [D. daucosma]. Brittonia. 33: 501-511.

description: Stiffly erect wandlike monopodial, distally branched shrubs up to 14 dm, flowering the first year as simple, distally few-branched herbs 6-10 dm tall, the old stems castaneous, the younger ones greenish-stramineous, the whole glabrous below the spikes or the stems distally charged with extremely fine straight divergent septate hairs up to 1-1.5 mm long, the foliage green, lustrous when fresh, the narrow deflexed leaflets elegantly gland-denticulate, the inflorescence a 3-4-spiked exserted panicle; stipules subulate 1.5-2 mm; primary cauline leaves 2- 3.5 cm, the slender leaf-stalk 13-26 mm, the 9-15 leaflets narrowly oblanceolate acute 7-12 x 1.5-2 mm, plane or shallowly boat-shaped, micropustular dorsally, the margin undulately denticulate by impression of a row of glands, the terminal leaflet sessile between the distal pair; peduncles 2.5-7 cm; spikes at first mod- erately dense, looser in age, the pilose axis becoming (1) 2-9 cm; bracts persistent through anthesis, lance-elliptic-acuminate 4.5-6 x 1-1.5 mm, glabrous, dorsally livid and densely gland-pustulate; pedicels subobsolete, not over 0.15 mm; calyx 5.5-7.7 mm, the shallowly campanulate tube ±1.5 mm deep, glabrous lustrous, prominently 10-ribbed, the intercostal panels either pallid or livid, charged with one row of small transparent glands, the lance-attenuate, lustrously long-ciliate gland-spurred teeth 4-6.2 mm, 2.5-4 times as long as tube; petals bicolored, the banner pale in bud, early lurid-purple, the epistemonous petals vivid violet-purple eglandular, perched ± 1 mm above hypanthium rim; banner ±5 mm, the deltate-cordate blade ±2.8 mm wide; wings 5.2 mm, the blade 4 x 2 mm; keel 5.5-6 mm, the broadly obovate blades ±4 x 3 mm; ovary glabrous, but the style-base remotely pilose; pod unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1981. New species of Dalea section Parosela (Leguminosae: Amorpheae) from Peru [D. strobilacea] and Mexico [D. daucosma]. Brittonia. 33: 501-511.

description: Bracteis floralibus dilatatis inter nervos 7 crassos hyalinis cymbiformibus D. insigni Hemsl. man- ifeste similis sed omnibus partibus villosa, bracteis ipsis minoribus absque cauda 4 x 2.5-3 (nec 6-8 x 3.5-5.5) mm utroque latere 3 (nec 4)-nerviis calycem sesquilongiorem haud omnino amplecten- tibus, dentibus calycinis subulatis 1-1.7 mm usque (nec deltatis 0.2-0.7 mm) longis, stipulisque obscure, nec valide palmatim nervosis diversa, pube calycisque forma ad D. obovatifoliam Ort. vergens sed ab hac bracteis absimillima.

description: Herbaceous but of unknown stature and duration, the upper stems and foliage softly densely villous throughout with fine erect and ascending straight hairs up to 1 mm, the broad flat leaflets subconcolorous, pubescent on both faces, finely punctate beneath; stipules obliquely lance-acuminate 5-8 mm, at base dilated on side further from petiole and cordately semiamplexicaul, the blade near base 2- 3 mm wide, faintly or obscurely nerved, not differentiated like the floral bracts into hyaline, gland-sprinkled intercostal panels; leaves (the possibly larger middle cauline ones unknown) 5-8 cm, the petiole 1.5-2.5 cm, the rachis 2.5-4.5 cm; leaflets 9-11, ovate- or obovate-acuminulate 7-15 x 4-8 mm, the submembra- nous blades plane, the terminal leaflet raised well above the distal pair; peduncles 2-5.5 cm; spikes densely many-flowered, oblong becoming cylindric, the pilo- sulous axis 2.5-9 cm; bracts persistent or the lowest tardily deciduous, dilated and navicular, nidulating the calyx but not fully concealing it, in profile semi-obovate 4 x 2.5-3 mm, the midrib produced into a subulate straight or gently recurved tail 2-2.5 mm, on each side of the cariniform midrib coarsely palmately 3-veined, the intercostal panels hyaline and gland-sprinkled; calyx subsessile 4- 5.3 mm, the tube (measured to an abaxial sinus) 2.9-3.7 mm, externally pilosu- Ious, the ribs stout livid, the intercostal panels hyaline and charged with many small scattered glands, the orifice oblique, the subulate teeth unequal, the dorsal one 1-1.7 mm, the rest slightly shorter; petals opening whitish except for lurid keel-tip, the banner rubescent in age, the soon purpurascent epistemonous petals inserted ±4 mm above hypanthium, a little above middle of staminal sheath; banner ±7 mm, the deltate blade 3.5 x 4 mm, open at junction with claw; wings 4 mm, the oblong blade 1.5 mm wide; keel ±6.7 mm, the claws 1.6 mm, the blade 6 x 4 mm; androecium 8.5 mm, the longer filaments free for 3 mm; pod of D. insignis, but finely pilosulous in distal half; seed pale brown, smooth and lustrous, ±2.5 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1980. Three new species of Dalea sect. Parosela (Leguminosae: Amorpheae) from western and southern Mexico. Brittonia. 32: 392-396.

description: Shrubs ±1.8 m, with purplish hornotinous and fuscous older branchlets, glabrous up to the thinly plumose flower-spikes, the ample paucifoliolate leaves olivaceous subconcolorous, the firm plane-margined leaflets glandular-punctate on both faces; stipules triangular or deltate 0.5-1 mm, persistent; primary cauline leaves 3-5 cm, the petiole 6-16 mm, the rachis 6-12 mm; leaflets 5, obovate, openly shallowly emarginate, the terminal one largest sessile, forming with the distal pair a palmate trefoil, these + 16-22 x 8-14 mm, in some spur-leaves slight- ly smaller and the proximal pair there sometimes lacking; peduncles (few seen) +1 cm; spikes loosely subracemosely + 10-15-flowered, the calyces of any one vertical rank separated by at least their own diam, the axis up to 2 cm; bracts thinly herbaceous lanceolate 4.5-5 mm, the lowest glabrous, the upper plumose-ciliate, all dorsally glabrous and coarsely gland-pustulate, persistent past anthesis; pedicels obscure but up to 0.2 mm; calyx 9-9.5 mm, silky-villous with fine, widely ascending, spirally twisted hairs up to ±1.2 mm, the tube ±3.2 mm long and diam, the linear-attenuate plumose teeth 5-6.5 mm, the dorsal one twice as long as tube, the intercostal panels of the tube charged with 1 (sometimes irregular) rank of yellow blister-glands; petals all violet-purple glabrous, the episte- monous ones perched ±1 mm above hypanthium; banner 6 mm, the obtusely deltate blade 4.2 x 3.4 mm, open at base; wings ±6 mm, the elliptic-oblong blade 4.6 x 1.6 mm; keel 7.5-8 mm, the claws 2.6 mm, the broadly elliptic blades 5- 5.5 x 2.7 mm, charged at apex with a linear-elliptic gland; androecium 6 mm, the filaments free for ±2 mm, the pale bluish anthers 0.65-0.8 mm; ovary pilo- sulous above middle and sparsely gland-sprinkled; pod not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1980. Three new species of Dalea sect. Parosela (Leguminosae: Amorpheae) from western and southern Mexico. Brittonia. 32: 392-396.

description: Stiffly erect xeromorphic microphyllous shrubs up to 4 (-?) dm tall, the leafless annotinous and older stems scaley and knobbed with persistent leaf-bases, the young stems charged with emergent prickle-shaped orange glands, the leaves crowded toward the end of branchlets, their narrow fleshy involute leaflets minutely silky-puberulent, densely gland-dotted externally, the conelike spikes of villosulous bracts terminal sessile; stipules subulate erect 1.5-2.5 mm; primary cauline leaves 12-25 mm, the leaf-stalk 10-22 mm; post-petiolular glands pricklelike recurved prominent; leaflets (7) 9-13, narrowly oblanceolate obtuse or emarginate, closely conduplicate and appearing subterete, 3-5.5 x 1 mm, charged at apex with a large orange prickle-gland; spikes squatly oblong in profile 1.5-2.5 cm long and without petals 1.3 cm diam; bracts contiguous firm, broadly obovate apiculate, each wrapped around and almost or fully concealing a calyx, in lateral view 4.5 x 2-2.5 mm, carinate dorsally, glabrous internally and sometimes also externally at base, otherwise densely gray-villosulous and inconspicuously glandpustulate; petals vivid blue except for white-tipped banner, this weakly pilosulous dorsally and like the keel tipped with a large orange gland; calyx ±6 mm, silky-villosulous from base upward or only distally, the shallowly pleated tube 5-5.5 x 3 mm, charged in each intercostal panel with a variably constricted linear glandbody, the orifice oblique, the dorsal tooth subulate 1-1.4 mm, the ventral pair shortest and broadest, deltate; banner 8.5-9.5 mm, the cordate blade 5-6 x 5 mm; epistemonous petals perched between 0.6 and 2.3 mm above hypanthium, the keel 10-12.5 mm, its elliptic blades 7-9 x 3-3.5 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1981. New species of Dalea section Parosela (Leguminosae: Amorpheae) from Peru [D. strobilacea] and Mexico [D. daucosma]. Brittonia. 33: 501-511.

description: Quoad phyllotaxin spiralem cum Ch. aspleniifolia (Irwin & Barneby) Irwin & Barneby, etiam Brasiliae orientali incola, sola comparabilis et ab ea glandula petiolari proximali exacte inter (nec infra) primum foliolorum par inserta, foliolis minus numerosis (8-12- nec 13-19- jugis) ex ipso racheos basi accrescentibus, foliolorum lamina utrinque lucida et reticulatim venulosa (nec obscure tantum dorso penninervia), racemique axi glandulis brevistipitatis obsito eximie diversa.

description: Cauliflorous shrubs -+ 4 m, the old branches brown lenticellate, the leaves spirally crowded around axis of brachyblasts beyond the flowers, the leaf-stalks and margin of leaflets pilosulous with ascending-incurved hairs 0.2-0.3 mm, the lustrous reticulate leaflets subconcolorous, the inflorescence of crowded sessile few-flowered racemes apart from distally glabrous petals densely silky-strigulose. Stipules triangular-subulate, -+ 0.5 mm, caducous. Leaves 6-11 cm; petiole including livid, little dilated pulvinus 4-8 mm, at middle 0.5-0.8 mm diam, deeply narrowly sulcate ventrally; rachis 4.5-8 cm; seta either subulate or dilated ovoid; glands between all pairs of leaflets, squatly trumpet-shaped, in profile 0.6-1 mm tall, the stipe puberulent, the concave head 0.5-0.7 mm diam; pulvinules (viewed dorsally) 0.3-0.4 mm, the leaflets (viewed ventrally) appearing sessile against rachis; leaflets 9-13 pairs, slightly accrescent upward, obliquely ovate obtuse, (5) 6-21 X (3) 4-9 mm, at base cordately rounded on proximal and broadly cuneate on distal side, the distal basal angle of blade angulately dilated, the margin revolute, the almost straight and centric midrib with +- 5-7 pairs of camptodrome (and few weak intercalary) secondary, connected by irregular tertiary venules all prominulous on both faces, a trifle more sharply so beneath. Racemes 2-8-flowered, the axis 3-15 mm, charged with glands resembling those of leaf-stalk; pedicels at anthesis 13-18 mm, in fruit 20-22 mm, minutely 2-bracteolate above middle; petals yellow, obovate, short-clawed, 3 ad- and 1 abaxial symmetrical and homomorphic, the fifth slightly longer and oblique, the longest 10-13 x 6-7.5 mm; filaments 0.8-1.2 mm; anthers in profile oblong, 2-3 mm; ovary densely strigulose; style -+ 4 mm, linear, -+ 0.6 mm diam just below the barbellate stigmatic cavity; ovules 9-10. Pod sessile, in outline narrowly oblanceolate, 10-12 x 1-1.2 cm, planocompressed, the stiffly chartaceous chocolate-brown lustrous valves coarsely venulose-reticulate, glabrate; seeds in outline broadly obovate-suborbicular, strongly compressed, -+ 7 x 6 mm, the castaneous lustrous testa minutely pitted overall.
bibliographicCitation: Breckon, Gary J. 1979. Studies in Cnidoscolus (Euphorbiaceae) I. Jatropha tubulosa, J. liebmannii and allied taxa from central Mexico. Brittonia. 31: 125-148.

description: Perennial from underground rootstock, villous throughout; stems 3-5 cm tall, erect to reclining, slender, angled but not winged; stipules broadly lanceolate with short basal lobe, 3-5 mm long; leaflets consistently 2 pairs, narrowly elliptic to narrowly oblanceolate, 5-10 (15) mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide; tendrils lacking, replaced by a short bristle; flowers consistently 2 in number, greenish-white with purple veins, 8-10 mm long; peduncles shorter than leaves; calyx lobes lanceolate, shorter than tube, all subequal, 1-1.5 mm long; fruit glabrous, 13-15 mm long, 2-3-seeded.

description: Caespitose perennial from branched woody caudex, the base clothed with old leaf-bases; stems erect, sericeous, 2.5-5 cm tall; leaves all basal, prostrate; petiole 4-12 (14) cm long; leaflets broadly oblanceolate-spathulate, obtuse, 11-20 (22) mm long, 5-11 mm wide, deeply boat-shaped, the lower surface densely graysericeous, the upper surface yellowish-green, pilose; raceme dense, 3-5 cm long, 2-3 cm wide, the flowers verticillate to subverticillate; bracts deciduous, linear, sericeous, 2.5-3 mm long; flowers 8-12 mm long; calyx bilabiate, the upper lip 4.9-5.1 mm long, the lower lip 4.9-5.2 mm long; banner glabrous, white aging pink, 8-10 mm long, slightly reflexed from keel; wings pink; keel pink, glabrous to sparsely ciliate, 8-12 mm long; legume tan, densely sericeous, 17-25 mm long, 5-8 mm wide; seeds 3-5, tan.

description: Trees to about 25 m tall, the trunk 1 m diam; young stems puberulent to glabrous; stipules not seen; leaves 5-foliolate, the rachis 5-8 cm long, glabrous; leaflets with petiolules about 5 mm long, the blades ovate to oblong, 4-8 cm long, 1.5-4 cm wide, breviacuminate, the base rounded to acute, the surfaces glabrous, nitid; inflorescences with axes brown-puberulent or subsericeous to tomentulose; bracts linear-deltoid, 1-2 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, sericeous; bracteoles deltoid, 1-2 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, sericeous; flower-buds rounded at apex and base; flowers about 7-7.5 mm long; calyx 4-5 mm long, 3 mm diam, fulvo-sericeous; petals "rosy" or "dull red"; ovary sessile, puberulent; fruit not seen but pre- sumably winged.

description: Tree to about 35 m tall, the trunk 50 cm diam; young stems glabrous with conspicuous vertical lenticels; stipules not seen; leaves 8-1 1-foliolate, the rachis glabrous, about 9-11 cm long; leaflets glabrous, the petiolules slender, 5-6 mm long, the blades elliptic-oblong to lanceolate-oblong, 4-9 cm long, (1.5) 2-3 cm wide, acute to acuminate, breviaristate at apex, acute to rounded at base; inflorescence axes brown-tomentulose; bracts deltoid to linear-deltoid, 4-5 mm long, (1) 2-5 mm wide, brown-velutinous, caducous; bracteoles linear-deltoid, 3 mm long, 1 mm wide, brown-velutinous, caducous; flowers 8-9 mm long; calyx brown-velutinous or tomentulose, 5-7 mm long, 4 mm diam; petals drying blackish (color not recorded by collector); fruit winged, 7-8 cm long, mostly 1-seeded, brown-velutinous when young, glabrescent with age, turning black on drying, the basal, seminiferous portion about 1.5-2 cm long, 1.5 cm wide, the terminal wing 5-6.5 cm long, 3 cm wide.

description: Tree 8-15 m high. Leaves up to 30 cm long, opposite or alternate. Petiole with a single gland on the upper side between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 6-10 pairs, opposite. Leaflets up to 21-31 pairs per pinna, opposite, oblong, up to 9-18 x 3-5 mm, at apex rounded or sometimes emarginate, at base weakly auriculate on proximal side; main nerve subcentral and straight at apex, secondary venation reticulate, prominent. Inflorescence axis ca 0.25 (1) m long, unbranched. Peduncles 3-9 per inflorescence, alternate, (0.5) 5-11 cm long. Capitula 4-4.5 cm long, biglobose with basal staminodial fringe ca 3-3.5 cm diameter and apical fertile part subspherical ca 2.5 cm diameter. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 5-6 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 0.5-1 mm) with lobes ca 1 mm long; corolla 6-7.5 mm long with lobes 1-1.5 mm long; filaments exserted 1-2.5 mm beyond calyx. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx 5-6 mm long. Staminodial flowers: calyx 5-6 mm long; corolla 7-8 mm long with lobes ca 4 mm long; filaments exserted up to 15 mm beyond calyx. Pods ca 15-26 cm long (including stipe of 4-6 cm) and 3-3.5 cm broad, strap-shaped, symmetrically attenuate into stipe, probably indehiscent, with sutures somewhat thickened and coriaceous valves shallowly corrugated. Seeds unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Hopkins, Helen C. F. 1982. Three new speices of Parkia (Leguminosae: Mimosoideae) from tropical South America. Brittonia. 34: 346-350.

description: Tree or shrub up to 5 m high. Leaves up to 20 cm long, alternate. Petiole with a single gland on the upper side between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 3-8 pairs, opposite. Leaflets up to 25-35 pairs per pinna, opposite, oblong, up to 13-26 x 3-6 mm, at apex obtuse, rounded or emarginate; main nerve central, sigmoid, curving towards distal margin at apex; secondary nerve at proximal margin prominent. Inflorescence axis up to 20 cm long, unbranched, more or less erect. Peduncles 1-6 per inflorescence, alternate, 1-7 (11) cm long, more or less erect. Capitula 5-6 x ca 4 cm, clavate with basal staminodial fringe poorly developed or absent, apical part spherical. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 7.5-9 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 0.5-1 mm) with lobes ca 1.5 mm long; corolla 9-11 mm long with lobes 2-3 mm long; filaments exserted ca 3-6 mm beyond calyx, free almost to base; anthers at least sometimes with small caducous gland. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx 6-8 mm long. Staminodial flowers few or some- times absent: calyx 4-6.5 mm long; corolla 6-9 mm long with lobes ca 1.5 mm long;filaments 9-13 per flower, exserted up to 17 mm beyond calyx mouth. Pods (4.5) 8-14 cm long (including stipe of 0.5-2 cm) and 2.5-5 cm broad, lingulate, somewhat coriaceous, velutinous, dehiscent along adaxial suture and sometimes tardily so along abaxial one. Seeds elliptical, 12-15 x 6.5-8.5 x 4-4.5 mm.

description: S. birostri var. hookeriana differt foliis 5-foliolorum; antheris fertilibus orificio apicali debile vel obsoletum diviso, petalo interno apice leviter acutato, staminodio 6-7 x 1.5 spathulato, inflorescentia 4-10-flora, ovario vel profuse pubescenti 20-29 ovulis; seminibus vel oblongis 9-24 in quoque fructu, superficiebus vas fructus obliquis; legumine subcylindrico, vel nigrescenti, corpore recto, 4-12 x 0.4-0.7 tiore densioreque, valvis coriaceis irregulariter tis, segmentis leviter rotatis.

description: Shrubs 0.5-1.5 m high, the branches branchlets subglabrous to pilosulous; 7 mm long, linear-lanceolate. Leaves pinnate, leaflets 5-10 pairs, glabrous, 32 x 4.5-9 mm, mucronulate, elliptic or lanceolate-oblong, petiole 10-15 mm long; rachis 5-11 cm with a stipitate gland, 3-5 mm long between the first and second pairs of leaflets. Racemes 4-10-flowered, peduncle 25-35 mm long, pedicels 10-20 mm long; bracts 30 mm long, linear-lanceolate. Sepals 5-10 mm long, lanceolate or obovate; petals 9-14 x 5-10 mm, yellowish, glabrous, the vexillary petal oblong; androecium with groups of stamens, the abaxial group curved main stamens with filaments 4-6 mm long and the anthers 4-5.5 mm long, the middle group of 4 straight stamens with filaments 2-3.5 mm long, anthers 4-6 mm long, the adaxial group of 3 staminodes 6-7 x 1.5 mm, spathulate; fertile anthers dehiscent by a terminal orifice divided by a weak, sometimes obsolete septum; gynoecium 10-15 mm long, ovary 8-13 mm long, oblong, margins profusely pilosulous, 20-29 ovules; style 1-2 mm long, curved; stigma concave, margin ciliate. Legume 4-12 x 0.4-0.7 cm, subclindric, with irregular constrictions, valves coriaceous, dark brown, straight; seeds 9-24, 3.9-5.3 x 2.2-2.8 mm, oblong, their flattened sides oblique to the valves.

description: Shrub 0.5-2 m high, subglabrous, occasionally branches and branchlets pilosulous; stipules 5 mm long, submembranous, linear-lanceolate, early caducous. Leaves paripinnate; leaflets 8-13 pairs, glabrous, 12-25 x 2.5-5 mm, oblong to elliptic; petiole 10-15 mm long; rachis 5-9 cm long, with a stipitate or claviform gland 3-5 mm long between the first and second pairs of leaflets. Racemes 8-15-flowered, peduncle 30-38 mm long, pedicels 18-26 mm long; bracts 20 mm long, linear-lanceolate. Sepals 4.5-10 mm long, lanceolate to obovate, glabrous, green; petals 10-14 x 5-12 mm, yellowish, glabrous, the vexillary petal orbicular, emarginate at apex; androecium with three groups of stamens, the abaxial group of 3 main incurved stamens with filaments 3-6 mm long, anthers 4-6 mm long, the middle group of 4 stamens straight with filaments 2.5-4 mm long, anthers 3.5- 4.5 mm long, the adaxial group of 3 staminodes 4.5-5 x 2-3 mm, rounded, apex slightly lobate; fertile anthers dehiscent by two apical slits; gynoecium 10-13 mm long, ovary 8-10 mm long, oblong, margins pilosulous; ovules 11-15; style 1-2 mm long, curved; stigma concave, margin ciliate. Legume 4-9.5 x 0.7-1 cm, compressed, locules evident, valves brownish, papery, slightly decurved, the seeds 3-10 seeds, 5.7-7 x 2.6-3.6 mm, oblong, their sides flattened parallel to the valves.

description: Arbor 15-metralis; foliolis 6-8-jugatis, laminis subcoriaceis anguste lanceolatis vel lineari-lanceolatis apice acutis mucronatisque basi suboblique rotundatis 2.5-6 cm longis 0.8-1.5 cm latis, foliolis terminalibus latioribus 1-1.8 cm latis, supra parce strigosis vel glabrescentibus subtus abundanter pallido- strigosis; inflorescentiis caulifloris fasciculatis racemosis 3-5-floris, ad 11 cm longis; petali lamina late suborbiculari-flabellato 2.7-3 cm longo 3.8-3.9 cm lato; staminibus maioribus ca 12, minoribus 150- 200, filamentis 10-20 mm longis glabris.

description: Tree 15 m tall, young branches fuscous. Leaves petiolate, petioles 1.5-2 cm long, densely brown-strigose; leaflets 6-8 pairs, narrowly lanceolate or linear- lanceolate, acute and mucronate at apex, rounded at the subunequal or suboblique base, 2.5-6 cm long, 0.8-1.5 cm wide or the terminal leaflet 1-1.8 cm wide, abundantly pale strigose beneath, sparsely strigose above or glabrescent, upper midrib densely strigose or with ascending to spreading hairs; rachis narrowly winged above, 1.5-3 mm wide, widest below base of leaflets, densely-brown strigose beneath, wing 0.3-1 mm wide, especially conspicuous in upper half of rachis, strigillose both sides. Inflorescence cauliflorous, simply racemose, in nu- merous fascicles, 3-5-flowered, up to 11 cm long; pedicels 1.3-2 cm long, thick- clavate, 2-3 mm wide at apex, densely dark brown-tomentose; bracts suborbic- ular-ovate, subacute, 3-4 mm long, 3-4 mm wide at base, dark brown-strigose without; bracteoles persistent, ovate, subacute, 3 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, densely dark brown-strigose without. Calyx segments 4 in full anthesis, persistent, thick- subcoriaceous, ovate- or oblong-lanceolate, subacute, 12-13 mm long, 6-9 mm wide in anthesis, 12 mm wide in bud, dark brown-tomentose without, glabrous within. Petal yellow, broadly suborbicular-flabellate, irregularly erose-denticulate, abruptly apiculate, broadly cordulate at base, abruptly stipitate, the stipitate portion 3 x 2 mm, the laminar portion 2.7-3 cm long, 3.8-3.9 cm wide, promi- nently 19-20-nerved, outer surface densely strigillose, especially around base and along nerves, inner surface glabrous, the midnerve minutely rugulose. Stamens numerous, the larger ca 12, with filaments ca 20 mm long, glabrous, the smaller 150-200, with filaments 10-15 mm long, glabrous; anthers broadly oblong, 1-2 mm long, 0.9 mm wide. Ovary curved, linear-subulate, in anthesis 25-30 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, in late maturity 30-35 mm long, 2 mm wide, 2-3 times longer than the style, laterally and ventrally densely pale-sericeous, dorsally glabrescent; gynophore sparsely strigillose; style terminal, 10-12 mm long, glabrous; stigma punctiform. Fruit not seen.

description: Leaflets commonly to 15 cm long, chartaceous, broadly ovate to lanceolate or elliptic, abruptly acuminate to a long, acute tip; pubescence long, tan, very dense on petiolule and lower surface of blade, moderately dense above. Bracteoles 2 mm long, obtuse. Pedicel 2 mm long. Calyx 25 mm long; pubescence long, tan, moderately to very dense; upper lip as long as tube, upper edge strongly concave behind apiculate tip; lowest tooth 4 mm long, subulate, slightly exceeding acute laterals. Standard 3 cm long. Pod commonly to 22 × 3.5 cm, compressed, tan, becoming blackish in age, tardily dehiscent or indehiseent; each valve with sutural ribs and an extra rib ea 1 mm from ventral rib. Seeds to 21 × 15 × 7 mm, oblong-elliptic, strongly compressed, light tan, some faintly marbled, becoming darker in age, not buoyant or impermeable; hilum ea 12 mm long.

description: Foliola late ovata, acuminata, utrimque parce pilosa. Bracteolae 2 mm longae. Legumen usque 18 cm longum, 3.5 cm latum, tarde dehiseens, sulco inter costas ea 8 mm lato. Semina brunnea, valde compressa, usque ad 24 mm longa, hilo 14 mm longo.

description: Leaflets commonly to 12 cm long, chartaceous, narrowly ovate-lanceolate, acuminate to a long, caudate, obtuse tip; pubescence long, tan, sparse on petiolule and lower surface of blade; upper surface glabrate. Bracteoles 2.5 mm long, obtuse. Pedicel 3 mm long. Calyx 23 mm long; pubescence long, tan, sparse; upper lip as long as tube, upper edge strongly concave behind apiculate tip; lowest tooth 4 mm long, subulate, slightly exceeding acute laterals. description: Stems erect, solitary, up to 0.8 m. in height, unbranched below inflorescence (or rarely branching as a result of injury to terminal growing portion), hairy with loose villous trichomes (glabrate in age). Stipules 0.5-1.5 cm. in length, 0.3-1 mm. wide, linear-filiform, ciliate, frequently early deciduous. Leaves borne in a close cluster 1-4 dm. above base of stem, or sometimes one or two blades somewhat separated from the remainder (above or below the main aggregation) or rarely all scattered. Petioles up to 1 dm. in length, horizontally extended, sparsely villous. Terminal leaflet larger than the lateral ones, 6-10 cm. in length, rounded, as broad as or broader than long, with a conspicuous acuminate tip. Lateral leaflets ovate, usually 1.2-1.5 times longer than broad, apically pointed but scarcely acuminate. Blades above or below main cluster frequently small in size or unifoliate. Leaflets slightly lighter below than above. Pubescence on lower surface of blades of loose villous hairs, the greatest concentration on the veins# Pubescence on upper surface of blades less abundant than below, of stiffer, somewhat strigose trichomes. Veins extending to margin or weakly curved away at the very edge of blade. Stipels apparently obsolete. Inflorescence rachis a continuation of leaf-bearing stem. Inflorescence much exceeding leaves, a simple raceme (on small plants) or more frequently much branched and compound, the branches divergent-ascending or somewhat apically incurved. Flowers 5-8 mm. long, on pedicels about 5 mm. in length. Calyx about 1.5 mm. high, similar to, but of slightly thicker texture than in D. nudiflorum, possessing fine, sub-appressed pubescence. Standard cuneate-tapering to the base. Wings rounded basally or with weak sagittate lobes. Keel petals broader than wings, slightly spurred. Loment stalk rather thick, 4-6 mm. in length. Pod 2-3 segmented, the joints 8-9 mm. long, 5-6 mm. high, widest 0.5-0.7 of the distance anteriorly. Posterior margin nearly straight, rather abruptly descending; ventral margin usually differentiated, short, evenly curved on both sides; anterior margin straight or concave, vertical.
bibliographicCitation: Isely, Duane. 1951. Desmodium: section Pododcarpium Benth. Brittonia. 7: 185-224.

description: Tree, aphyllous at anthesis; branchlets stout. aeuleate; petioles 3.4-16 cm. long, densely tomentose, often aculeate; petiolules 4-6 mm. long, 1.5-2.5 mm. in diam., pubeseent as petioles, occasionally atuleate; leaflet-blades subcoriaceous, sparsely tomentose above, densely tomen- tose beneath; terminal leaflet subrotund or broadly ovate or rhombic- ovate, 6.8-13.5 cm. long, 5.7-12 cm. broad, acute or obtuse at apex, subeordate or rounded at base; costa often aculeate above or beneath, the secondaries 6-8 per side; rachis 8.5-9.6 cm. long, densely tomentose; pedicels 1.6-2.7 cm. long, about 0.4 mm. in diam., glabrous; bracts and bracteoles not seen; ealyx chartaceouis, broadly campanulate, asymmetric, about 7 mm. long on the carinal side and 6 mm. long on the vexillar side, about 1.5 mm. broad at base, ampliate to about 12 mm. at apex, the calyx being stretched transversely just before anthesis, entire or nearly so at margin, callose and often calearate on the upper carinal side (spur up to 0.7 mm. long), thickened toward base, glabrous; standard scarlet (ex Steinbach), elliptic, 2.9-3.3 cm. long (including claw), 1.7-1.9 cm. broad, obtuse or rounded at apex and base, the claw up to 2 mm. long; wings oblong-ovate, often unguieulate at apex, about 7 mm. long and 3 mm. broad; keel-petals falcate, 24-27 mm. long, 4.5-5.5 mm. broad; stamens about 3.3 cm. long, separate for 0.5-1.1 cm.; pistil about 3.2 cm. long, the ovary densely tomentose (hairs fine and not spreading, often braiiehed), the gynophore sparsely so distally and glabrous proximally; fruit-pedicels 1.5-2.1 cm. long, about 1 mm. in diam.; pods chartaceous, about 11 cm. long and 1.4 cm. broad, not at all constrieted, with a very slender stipe about 1.3 cm. long, with a very stiff acumination about 0.5 cm. long, 1- or 2(?)-seeded; seeds blackish brown with indistinct tawny markings, about 12 mm. long and 6 mm. broad.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. 1939. The American species of Erythrina. Brittonia. 3: 205-337.

description: P. igneiflorae Ducke et P. discolori Spruce ex Benth. affinis sed a prima foliolis sigmoideis angustis (nec oblongis), costa ad apicem decurva (nec recta), pedunculis spiraliter (nec distiche) dispositis, et a secunda leguminibus longioribus badiis (nec primum rubris tunc nigrescentibus) aliquantum falcatis (nec oblongis rectis), valvulis vadose corrugatis (nec plano-convexis) diversa.

description: Tree up to 20 (35) m high. Leaves up to 30 cm long, alternate. Petiole with a single ovoid gland on the upper side between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 6-15 pairs, opposite or subopposite. Leaflets up to 28-41 pairs per pinna, opposite, up to 7-13 x 1.5-3 mm, sigmoidally curved, at apex acute or obtuse, at base strongly auriculate; main nerve sigmoid, at apex curving towards distal margin. Inflorescence axis up to 0.5-1 m long, more or less ascending to hori- zontal, unbranched. Peduncles up to ca 10 per inflorescence, alternate, pendent, 5-26 cm long. Capitula 4.5-7 cm long, biglobose with basal staminodial fringe 4-6 cm diameter and spherical to ellipsoid apical part 2.5-3.5 cm diameter. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 7-9 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 0.5-1.5 mm) with lobes up to ca 1 mm long; corolla 8-11 mm long with lobes 0.5-1 mm long; filaments exserted ca 2-3 mm beyond calyx, free almost to base. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx 6.5-9.5 mm long. Staminodial flowers: calyx up to 8-11 mm long; corolla 9-14 mm long with lobes 1-2 mm long; filaments exserted up to 32 mm beyond calyx, irregularly united to neck of corolla. Pods 8.5-35 cm long (including stipe of 0.5-7 cm) and 3.2-5.5 cm broad, the coriaceous valves shallowly corrugated, sometimes velutinous, indehiscent. Seeds 13-18.5 x 6-12 x 5-8.5 mm.

description: Suffrutex, brevipubens. Foliola subcoriacea, foliolis terminalibus oblanceolatis vel obovatis, glandula petiolari non nisi inter par infimum foliolorum. Antherae stramineae, minute rubro-punctatae. Legumen 4.5-8 cm longum, teres.
