description: Mostly spreading subshrub to 1 m tall; twigs sparsely to densely short-pubescent. Stipules caducous, subulate, 3-6 mm long, 0.4-0.7 mm broad, revolute along much of their length when dry, moderately short-pubescent on both faces; margin entire. Petiole 0.8-2.8 cm long, 0.7-1.4 mm thick; rachis 2.5-6 (8) cm long; leaf-axis with an abaxial groove, sparsely to densely short-pubescent, joined to the stem by a terete, wrinkled pulvinus 2-4 mm long which is similarly pubescent. Gland between the lowest pair of leaflets subsessile to stalked 0.5-1 mm, cylin- drical to fusiform, somewhat wrinkled, 0.8-1.4 mm long, 0.3-0.6 mm thick, usu- ally black when dry. Leaflets 5- to 7-paired, terminal pair the largest, lower pairs progressively smaller, each joined to the leaf-axis by a terete, pubescent pulvinule 1-2 mm long; terminal leaflets oblanceolate to obovate, rounded and retuse or obtuse and usually mucronulate (rarely somewhat acute), base oblique, cuneate on inner side, outer side rounded, glabrate above, moderately to densely pubes- cent below, subcoriaceous, 1.8-4.5 cm long, 0.7-1.8 cm broad, usually drab olive- green above, paler green below; margin entire, hyaline-bordered, tending toward revolute when dry. Inflorescence of axillary racemes, often terminally clustered; peduncle straight or slightly arching, 7-15 cm long, 1-2-times as long as the subtending leaf, sparsely to moderately short-pubescent, 12-20-flowered (but only 1-3 flowers open at any one time), 1-4-fruited. Bracts caducous, subulate, 3-4 mm long, 0.4-0.7 mm broad, somewhat involute when dry, glabrate on the abaxial surface, moderately pubescent on the adaxial face; margin entire, ciliate. Pedicel in flower 10-15 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm thick, sparsely to moderately pubescent; in fruit, 15-25 mm long, 0.7-0.9 mm thick, smooth to somewhat rough. Sepals olive-green to brownish with paler margins, narrowly to broadly ovate, unequal (outer ones in bud the shortest), 4-8 mm long, 2.5-5 mm broad, pubescent, especially at base. Petals yellow to orange-yellow, dark-veined with violet, nar- rowly to broadly obovate, clawed, slightly unequal, 8-12 mm long, 4-8 mm broad, glabrous. Stamens 10, free, with straw-colored to reddish-brown anthers, unequal (3 sterile at top [ca 2 mm long, on 1.5 mm filaments], 2 medium on each side [ca 3.5-4 mm long, on 1.5 mm filaments], 1 medium-long-exserted at the bottom [ca 5 mm long, on 2.5-3 mm filaments], and 1 long-exserted on each side of it [ca 5.5 mm long, on 4.5-5 mm filaments]), the longest anthers 0.8-1.2 mm thick, fertile anthers dehiscing by 2 pores, and with 1 longitudinal furrow on each side running their whole length. Ovary stipitate, dark brown, to 8 mm long at anthesis, ca 0.5 mm broad, moderately to densely medium-long-pubescent with yellowish-white hairs; ovules numerous; style terete, to 3 mm long, curving upward, glabrous; stigma subterminal, oblique on the upper side of the style. Pod pale brown to reddish-brown on the faces, sutures about the same color, the body oblong, terete to slightly compressed, 4.5-8 cm long, 0.6-0.8 cm thick, smooth to slightly rough, glabrous to sparsely short-pubescent, on a stipe to 0.5 cm long; style usually persistent on the pod as an apiculate point to 3 mm long. Seeds numerous, in 2 rows with the faces perpendicular to the long axis of the fruit, obliquely tear-shaped, olive-brown, slightly compressed, 3.8-4.5 mm long, 1.8-2.3 mm broad, smooth to slightly rough; hilum subterminal; pleurogram absent.

description: Tree to 9 m; branches glabrous. Leaf blades membranaceous to chartaceous, broadly ovate, 20-26 cm long, 17-20 cm wide, bilobed to ca 1/4 their length, lobes slightly divaricate, base cordate, apex of lobes attenuate, upper surface glabrous, lower surface tomentellous, at least on nerves, lighter in color than upper surface, 9-11-nerved; petioles 7-9 cm long, canaliculate, sparsely tomentellous to glabrate; stipules triangular-lanceolate, ca 2 mm long, caducous; adpetiolar intrastipular trichome enlarged, forming a laterally flattened, obtuse excrescence ca 1 mm long, others minute. Racemes cauliflorous, to 80 cm long, 20-40-flowered, the flowers paired; peduncle adnate to rachis, emerging just above next higher node; pedicel ca 1 cm long; bract and bracteoles triangular-ovate, ca 1 mm long, persistent; bud linear, ca 6 cm long, ecostate, the tip attenuate; hypanthium tubular, ca 1.5 cm long, obscurely 10-nerved; calyx irregularly splitting to hypanthium mouth into 2-5 lobes; petals 5, white, linear-lanceolate, ca 5 cm long, ca 6 mm wide, glabrous, the claw ca 5 mm long; fertile stamens 10, the filaments greenish-white, 3.5-4.0 cm long, irregularly connate at base for 1-5 mm into a sheath, this pilose- tomentose on inner surface, the anthers linear-oblong, 6-8 mm long, glabrous; pollen spheroid, polyporoidate, sexine reticulate with blunt infratectal spines; gynoecium ca 6 cm long, subequalling androecium, the ovary ca 12 mm long, tomentose, the gynophore 2.5-3.0 cm long, glabrous, the style ca 2 cm long, tomentellous near base, otherwise glabrate, the stigma obliquely capitate. Fruit (immature) linear-oblanceolate, apiculate with persistent style base, 20-22 cm long, 2.0-2.2 cm wide, brown, sparsely tomentellous to glabrate, the gynophore ca 3 cm long, glabrous; seeds not seen.

description: Small tree to 10 m; branches slender, glabrous. Leaf blades submembranaceous, suborbicular, 5-8 cm long, 6-10 cm wide, bilobed to about the middle, base deeply cordate, apex of lobes obtuse to rounded, upper surface glabrous, lower surface minutely strigose, lighter in color than upper surface, 9-(11)-nerved; petiole slender, 3-5 cm long, glabrous; stipules triangular-lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, caducous; intrastipular trichomes minute. Racemes terminal, or subterminal and axillary, minutely strigulose, the flowers paired; buds red, 5-6 cm long; pedicel 2-5 mm long; bract and bracteoles triangular-lanceolate, ca 1 mm long; hypan- thium tubular, 2.0-2.5 cm long, slightly arcuate; calyx spathaceous at anthesis; petals 5, red, subequal, glabrous, erect, oblanceolate, 4.5-5.0 cm long, 1.0-1.5 cm wide, tapering to claw 3-4 mm long; fertile stamens 10, red, 4.5-5.5 cm long, alternate slightly shorter, 9 united into a sheath for ca 3/5 their length, the 10th free for ca 0.5 cm further and slightly longer than others, the staminal sheath sparsely short-pilose on inner surface, the anthers ca 5 mm long, elliptic-oblong, glabrous; pollen spheroid, inaperturate, sexine reticulate with blunt, spinelike infratectal processes; gynoecium 6.5-8.5 cm long, subequalling or slightly ex- ceeding androecium, glabrous, the gynophore and style elongate, subequal, the stigma capitate. Fruit linear, apiculate with persistent style, light brown, glabrous, 16 cm long, 1.7 cm wide, the gynophore 4.5 cm long; seeds not seen.

description: Tree to 10 m; branches reddish-brown tomentellous when young, glabrate in age. Leaf blades chartaceous, oblong-suborbicular, 14-24 cm long, 13-21 cm wide, emarginate or bilobed to 1/4 their length, lobes slightly divaricate, base cordate, apex of lobes rounded, upper surface glabrous, lower surface shortly reddish-brown-tomentose or -tomentellous, at least on nerves, conspicuously reticulate-nerved, lighter in color than upper surface, 11-nerved; petiole 4-5 cm long, canaliculate, reddish-brown tomentellous; stipules lanceolate, ca 2 mm long, deciduous; intrastipular trichomes minute, adpetiolar one enlarged, forming a laterally flattened, obtuse excrescence up to 2 mm long. Inflorescence subterminal, axillary, geminate or short-racemose, shortly reddish-brown-tomentose, 2-4-flow- ered, the flowers paired, peduncle adnate to rachis (stem) and emerging just above next higher node; buds linear-fusiform, ca 5 cm long, the apex acute, obscurely 5-nerved; pedicels 2.0-2.5 cm long; bract and bracteoles triangular-ovate, 1.0- 1.5 mm long, persistent; hypanthium short-tubular, ca 1 cm long, 5- or obscurely 10-nerved; calyx irregularly splitting to hypanthium rim into 2-5 lobes; petals 5, white, subequal, linear, 4-5 cm long, 3-6 mm wide, the claw 1.0-1.5 cm long; fertile stamens 10, the filaments 3-4 cm long, alternate slightly shorter, irregularly connate at base for 1-2 mm into a sheath, glabrous, the anthers ca 1 cm long, glabrous; pollen subspheroid, polyporoidate, sexine reticulate with blunt infra- tectal spines; gynoecium ca 5 cm long, subequalling androecium, the ovary ca 1.5 cm long, tomentose, the gynophore ca 1.5 cm long, glabrate, the style ca 1 cm long, tomentellous, the stigma obliquely capitate. Fruits linear oblanceolate, apic- ulate with persistent style base, 20-25 cm long, 3.0-3.5 cm wide, light brown, glabrate, the gynophore ca 3 cm long, glabrate; seeds not seen.

description: Trees attaining 45 m with columnar trunk to 6.5 dm diam, the outer bark gray-brown, finely wrinkled, densely lenticellate, the inner bark orange, the branches, petioles and axes of inflorescence finely scurfy under magnification, the coriaceous lustrous leaflets bicolored, olivaceous above, brownish beneath, glabrous. Stipules unknown. Leaf-stalks ±8-17 cm, the petiole 2.3-7 cm long, enlarged but nonpulvinate at base; lentiform glands between pinnae 2-5 mm long, immersed in leaf-stalk, livid and wrinkled when dry; pinnae 1-3-jugate, their pulvinus livid but not wrinkled, their rachis 11-25.5 cm; leaflets 2-5-jugate, ovate, short-acuminate, entire 5.5-15.5 x 3.5-7.5 cm, the first pair arising 4-6 cm from pulvinus, the distal ones 3.5-8 cm apart, the last pair largest, the plane but undulate margin thickened, the reticulate venation evident but scarcely raised. Inflorescence openly paniculate, the primary axis 3-5 dm long, the secondary ones 1-2 dm, reddish-scurfy; flower-spikes solitary or 2-3 together, the peduncle 3-6 mm long, the flowering rachis 2-4.5 cm long, arising from a cupular bract, sometimes cleft on one side, visible between buds but concealed by open flowers, at once whitepuberulent and red-scurfy; floral bracts reduced to minute scales; calyx ±0.5 mm long, cupular with 5 minute deltate apiculate lobes, purplish and externally redpuberulent; corollas campanulate ±2 mm, the tube 1 mm long, the linear-oblanceolate lobes recurved, densely red-puberulent externally, lustrous-glabrous and 3-nerved within; filaments red-purple glabrous, united around an ovary-stipe of 0.5 mm, exerted 1 mm; ovary white-pilosulous; style glabrous ±2.3 mm long. Pod broadly linear ±10-11 x 1.5 x 0.5 cm, very slightly decurved, obtuse at both ends, compressed but plump, the stiffly papery valves becoming wrinkled, brown, minutely speckled, produced internally as incomplete septa ±1 mm tall; seeds transverse, in broad outline oblong 10.5 x 5.5 mm, seated on a shallowly sigmoid fleshy aril ± 1 x 4 mm, the soft green testa turning brown.

description: Perennial herb, leafy at anthesis; stems rather short and slender, usually aculeate; petioles 5-19 cm. long, puberulent, soon glabreseent, usually aculeate; petiolules 2.5-6 mm. long, 0.4-1.5 mm. in diam., puberuleInt, occasionally aculeate; leaflet-blades thin-chartaceous or ehartaceous, glabrous throughout (except veins beneath usually pu- beruleInt), usually aculeate on costa and veins beneath, rarely above; terminal leaflets ovate-deltoid or broadly ovate-deltoid or deltoid (or suborbicular), 3-8 (-11) cm. long, 2.2-6 (-8.5) cm. broad, obtuse or acute or rounded at apex, truncate or broadly cuneate (or subeordate) at base; secondaries 6-11 per side, the veinlets prominent on both surfaces; rachis 15-58 cm. long, puberulent, soon glabreseent or glabrous, often aculeate; pedicels 0.4-1.4 cm. long, about 0.4 mm. in diam., puberulent; larger bracts linear-lanceolate, up to 10 mm. long and 2 mm. broad, the smaller ones about 3.6 mm. long and 0.5 mm. broad; bracteoles linear, up to 9 mm. long and about 0.8 mm. broad; calyx thin-chartaceous, tubular-campanulate, 20-35 mm. long on the carinal side (excluding tooth), 14-25 mm. long on the vexillar side, 2-3 mm. broad at base, ampliate to 5-8 mm. toward apex, at margin entire or irregularly crenulate, occasionally lacerate at anthesis, provided with a tooth (up to 2 mm. long) on the upper carinal side, puberulent, at length glabreseent; standard pale orange, narrowly elliptic (occasion- ally broadest toward apex), (5.1-)6.5-8.5 cm. long, 1.1-1.5 cm. broad, acute or obtuse or rounded at apex, cuneate or cuneate-clawed at base; wings sublinear, 8-20 mm. long, 1-2 mm. broad; keel-petals usually obliquely narrowly elliptic, 24-37 mm. long, 2.5-5 mm. broad; stamens 4-6.6 cm. long, separate for 0.6-2 cm.; pistil 4-6.2 cm. long, the ovary and gynophore softly pubeseent; fruit-pedicels 1.2-1.7 cm. long and about 2.5 mm. in diam.; pods ligneous, 13-19 cm. long, 2-2.5 cm. broad, constricted between seeds, with a stipe 2.5-3.5 cm. long, with a very stiff acumination 2.5-3.5 cm. long, aculeate, 1-many-seeded; seeds black, about 19 mm. long and 14 mm. broad.

description: Diminutive prostrate herbs with many freely repeatedly branched, densely leafy stems radiating from the crown of a slender, apparently short-lived taproot and forming dense mats of pallid foliage 1-3.5 (4.5) dm diam, floriferous from base upward, gray-pilosulous throughout (except for medially glabrescent upper face of conduplicate leaflets) with fine, narrowly ascending, mixed straight and wavy basifixed hairs up to 0.4-0.6 mm; stipules submembranous, deltate or triangular, 1-2.5 mm, the lowest scarcely more than semiamplexicaul, none connate; leaves 8-26 mm, the slender petiole ± as long or longer than rachis; leaflets 7-9, petiolu- late, decrescent distally, in outline (opened up) obovate-cuneate-emarginate, 2-6 mm, commonly arched backward; peduncles mostly paired with a branchlet, 3- 7 mm; racemes loosely (3) 4-7 (8)-flowered, the flowers declined, the flexuous axis together with peduncle no longer than subtending leaf; bracts subulate 0.5-1.2 mm; pedicels 0.8-1.8 mm; calyx 3.6-4.2 mm, white-pilosulous, ebracteolate, the subsymmetric hypanthium 0.5 mm, the submembranous, obconic-campanulate tube 1.3-1.8 mm, the slenderly subulate or sublinear incurved green teeth 1.8-2.4 mm; petals whitish, the banner faintly lilac-tinged or -veined; banner recurved through ±90º, obovate-cuneate-emarginate, 4.8-5.3 x 4 mm; wings nearly as long, the claw 1.2-1.5 mm, the elliptic, obtuse, incurved blade 3.8-4 x 1.2-1.6 mm; keel 3.3-3.6 mm, the claws 1.3-1.5 mm, the semi-obovate blades 2.2-2.5 x 1.3-1.5 mm, incurved through ± 100º to obscurely porrect obtuse apex; anthers 0.3 mm; ovary pilosulous; ovules 3-4 (5); pod spreading-declined, sessile, 1-locular, when ripe deciduous from receptacle, in profile lunately elliptic-obovate, 4.5-5 x 2-2.5 mm, obtuse at base, abruptly apiculate at apex, laterally com- pressed but a trifle turgid, the prominulous ventral suture shallowly concave in profile, the dorsal one strongly convex and at mid-pod shallowly depressed, the thinly pilosulous valves subhyaline toward the ventral suture, a little firmer toward the dorsal one, the differentiated parts separated by a shallow longitudinal groove; dehiscence from base upward along both sutures, after falling; seeds usually 2 maturing, ellipsoid, deeply notched at hilum, 2.1-2.5 x 1.4-1.6 mm, the testa dull black.

description: Diminutive prostrate caulescent herb from loosely branched caudex, the simple or few-branched homotinous stems forming mats of greenish-cinereous foliage ±1-2 dm diam, the internodes 3-8 x 0.8-1 mm, the stems and leaf-stalks loosely strigulose with ascending straight white basifixed hairs 0.2-0.6 mm, the firm, green, conduplicate leaflets ciliolate and dorsally strigulose along midrib, otherwise glabrous, the flowers subcapitately racemose on short peduncles arising from distal leaf-axils; stipules membranous, pallid, 2-3 mm, amplexicaul and connate through more than half their length into a shortly bidentate sheath, externally white- or partly fuscous-strigulose; leaves including short petiole 1-3.5 cm; leaflets 19-31, decrescent distally, crowded when young but more distant in age, in outline oblong-elliptic, emarginate, the larger ones of fully developed leaves 2-4 x 0.8-1.6 mm, all essentially veinless externally; peduncles 2-15 mm, equalling or up to 5 times as long as associated stipules; racemes very shortly or subumbellately 3-6-flowered, the axis becoming 2-4 mm; bracts submembranous, pallid, broadly ovate, 1.5-2 mm; pedicels 0.3-0.5 mm; calyx 3.3-4.3 mm, partly or wholly fuscous-strigulose, the campanulate tube 2-2.5 mm, ultimately ruptured by the swollen pod, the subulate teeth subequilong 1.3-2 mm; petals purple, drying violet, the banner pale-eyed; banner recurved through ±40º, suborbicular-emarginate beyond short cuneate claw, 5-6.2 x 4.6-5.4 mm; wings 4.5-5.3 mm, the claws ±2 mm, the oblong, obtuse blade 3-3.4 x 1.3-1.5 mm; keel 4.2-4.5 mm, the claws 2 mm, the broadly ovate-elliptic, obtuse blades ±2.5 x 1.5 mm; ovary strigulose; style glabrous, the capitellate stigma 0.25 mm diam; ovules 2 collateral on dilated funicle; pod subsessile, the stipe concealed in the hypanthial cup, the body subglobose, 3-4 x 2.5-3.5 mm, rounded at base, bluntly carinate by the convexly arched ventral suture, abruptly cuspidulate by subulate style-base, 0.6- 0.9 mm, openly deeply sulcate dorsally at and below middle, the thin green strigulose valves becoming papery brownish, not inflexed; dehiscence inert tardy, annotinous pods sometimes coetaneous with new flowers; seeds 2, borne below middle of ventral suture, 2-2.5 x 1.7-2 mm, the smooth, brown testa purple-maculate.

description: Frutex ad 3 m altus, ramis erectis, rubrQ-ferrugineis demum glabratis. Folia pinnata, 7-9-juga, (15-) 20-25 cm longa; stipulae lineares vel anguste triangulares, 1 mm longae, 0.5 mm latae, rubro-ferrugineae; petioli 15-30 mm longi, glabri vel sparse pubescentes; foliola coriacea, nitida, siccata grisea, elliptica vel oblonga, integra, apice retusa, basi rotundata, 40-70 mm longa, (15-) 20-25 (-30) mm lata, supra glabra, costa valde impressa, subtus initio breviter rubro-pubescentia, fere scabra demum omnino glabra, costa valde elevata, nervis secundariis elevatis, valde reticu- latis; petioluli 2-4 mm longi, puberuli vel glabrati; stipellae nullae. Racemi in panicula terminali folia superante dispositi, 25-35 cm longi; bracteae anguste lineares, ferrugineae, caducae; pedicelli 15-20 mm longi, rubro-pubescentes; bracteolae caducae; calycis segmenta anguste ovata, acuta, 8-9 mm longa, extus rubro-ferruginea, intus praeter marginem revolutam glabra; petala 10-12 mm longa, unguiculata, lamina ovata, basi sagittata, intus glabra, extus secus axin glabra vel parce pilosa, ungue 5-6 mm longo, glabro; stamina (stamine magno petala aequante excepto) unguem aequantia; filamenta crassa, glabra; antherae subaequales, 1.5-1.9 mm longae, 1 mm latae, glabrae, staminis magni pilosissimae, staminum caeterorum glabrae; ovarium breviter stipitatum, 1.6-2 mm longum, dense rubro-pilosum, ovulis 5-6. Legumen oblongum, compressum, secus marginem late crenulatum, junius ferrugineum demum glabrum, immaturum 70-100 mm longum, 18-25 mm latum.

description: Arbuscula fruticosa usque ad 1.2 m alta, paene glabra; ramuli stricti, rigidi acuminatique, flavidi et juventute leviter glauci, aetate fusci; aculei solitarii, 0-8 mm sub nodis affixi, recurvati ad fere stricti vel absentes. Folia in fasciculis axillaribus densis, unipinnata, glauca; petioli phyllodinei, 5-16 mm longi, 1 mm lati, in pagina adaxiale manifeste trinervati; raches 1-5 mm longae, 0.5 mm latae; foliola 2 juga, raro 1-juga, crassa, 2-6 mm longa, 0.75-2 mm lata, oblongo-elliptica, integra, apice obtusa ad parum mucronulata, basi obliqua, abaxialiter manifeste nervosa. Flores circa 20 in capitulis globosis axillaribus tenuipedunculatis, in alabastro rosei. Fructus oblongi stipitati rostrati, valde compressi, 35-75 mm longi, 8-10 mm lati; margines undulati ad constricti, armati vel inermes; valvae leviter glaucae, in segmenta monosperma secedentes.
bibliographicCitation: Verhoek-Williams, Susan E. 1978. Two new species and a new combination in Manfreda (Agavaceae). Brittonia. 30: 165-171.

description: Shrubby tree to 1.2 m tall, essentially glabrous; branchlets straight, yellowish and lightly glaucous when young, becoming gray and thorn-like with age; bark of older branches shredding into fine fibers; nodes (short shoots) enlarged, protruding from branches; prickles solitary, 0-8 mm below node, recurved to nearly straight or absent, 2-5 mm long, enlarged at base. Leaves in dense axillary fascicles, once-pinnate, glaucous; stipules brown, subulate-lanceolate, tomentulose, 0.5-1 mm long; petioles phyllodal, 5-16 mm long, 1 mm wide, prominently 3-ribbed on the ventral surface; rachis 1-5 mm long, 0.5 mm wide; leaflets 4 in 2 pairs, rarely 2, thick, 2-6 mm long, 0.75-2 mm wide, oblong-elliptic, entire, obtuse to slightly mucronulate, oblique at base, veins prominent beneath. Flowers ca 20 in axillary, globose heads, pinkish in bud; peduncle slender, glaucous, (7) 12-20 mm long; calyx campanulate, ca 0.75 mm long, ca 1 mm wide; corolla cylindroidal, 1.5-2 mm long; corolla lobes ca 0.5-0.75 mm long, ca 0.5 mm wide; stamens 8, to 7 mm long. Fruits oblong, stipitate, beaked, strongly compressed, 35-75 mm long, 8-10 mm wide; margins undulate to constricted, armed or not; valves membranous, light brown, lightly glaucous, breaking into one-seeded segments. Seeds dark brown, nearly orbicular, 4 mm in diameter.

description: Tenuicaules prostrati et effusi. Foliola aut vel simul 1 cm longa et 2 mm lata, plerumque 4-6-plo longiora quam latiora. Racemi 3-7-flori. Corolla 7-9 mm longa. Legumina ca 1-1.5 cm longa. A varietate leptosepala foliis brevioribus angustioribusque, floribus brevioribus, et leguminibus brevibus 1-1.5 (nec 1.5-2.5) cm longis differt.

description: A proxime affini P. obliqua (Persoon) Macbride quoad inflorescentiam ac legumen vix diversa, sed arborea excelsa, petiolo communi abbreviata ± 1-3 (nec 2.5-5.5) cm longo, pinnis plerumque 1-, paucis 2-jugis (nec 2-3-jugis), foliolisque pinnarum longiorum 4-7(8)-nec 9-13-jugis duplo majoribus, iis ultimi paris 3-4.5 (nec 0.8-1.8) cm longis, omnibus simul penniveniis ac reticulatis (nec simpliciter penniveniis) abstans.

description: Trees attaining 31 m with cylindrical bole 4 dm diam, gray-brown fissured bark and pinkish-white wood, the annotinous branchlets brown, lenticellate, the hornotinous ones like all leaf-axes and at least the dorsal face of leaflets pilosulous with spreading gray or yellowish hairs ±0.2 mm, the leaves notably bicolored, lustrous dark green (when dry brunnescent) above, paler dull brown beneath, the amentiform flower-spikes solitary or 2 or 3 together in axils of contemporary leaves, immersed in foliage; axillary resting-buds ovoid, 1 mm, puberulent. Stip- ules deltate, thick-textured, livid, 1 mm, persistent. Leaf-stalks including hard, livid pulvinus 11-28 mm, the terminal appendage deltate, obtuse, glandular- thickened; a subglobose, obscurely porose nectary 0.8-1.3 mm diam between each pair of pinnae and smaller ones between 1 or 2 distal pairs of leaflets; pinnae 1, rarely 2 pairs, the axis of distal pinnae 3-9 cm, the interfoliolar segments 8-15 mm; leaflets (3) 4-7 (8) pairs, the first arising (3) 4-9 mm from pulvinus, the rest accrescent upward, all rhombic-ovate or elliptic from asymmetrically broad-cuneate base, subacuminate distally, minutely callous-tipped, the margin revolute, the blades of distal pair 3-4.5 x 1.3-1.8 cm, the forwardly arcuate midrib immersed above, prominulous beneath, the fine secondary pinnate and reticulate venulation delicately raised, more strongly so beneath. Peduncles 1.5-2 mm, the bracts united into a lobed deciduous cup; axis of spikes up to 9 cm; floral bracts 0.3-0.5 mm; flowers sessile, 5-merous, glabrous except for remotely puberulent calyx, this campanulate, 0.8-1 x 0.8-1 mm, the depressed-deltate teeth 0.2 mm; corollas white, ageing ochroleucous (brown when dry), ±2.5 mm, cleft half-way into strongly recurved lanceolate lobes 0.45-0.6 mm wide; 10 filaments united through 0.5 mm, of unequal lengths, ±3-4.5 mm; anthers 0.5-0.6 mm, the con- nective gland-tipped; ovary glabrous, elevated on a stipe 2-3.3 mm, the style 0.5-0.8 mm. Pods linear, straight or slightly arcuate, plano-compressed, 10-11 x 0.9 cm, contracted at base into a stipe ± 5 mm, the scarcely thickened sutures either shallowly undulate or deeply constricted between seeds, the stiffly papery valves becoming rich brown, furfuraceous dull, scarcely elevated over seeds, inertly dehiscent the length of both sutures; funicle sigmoid and thickened immediately below seed; seeds 10-12, basipetal, plumply discoid, ± 5.5 mm diam, the testa dirty white, smooth, the U-shaped pleurogram 2 mm tall; cotyledons enveloped in plates of albumen.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. & Grimes, James W. 1984. Two new mimosaeeous trees from the American tropics. Brittonia. 36: 236-240.

Coriaceis Benth. bene congruens, sed inter eas foliis parvis simpliciusculis, pinnis plerumque 2-jugis et pinnarum majorum foliolis 4-6-jugis, praeterea corolla parva 4.5-6 mm tantum longa praestans.

description: Trees (2) 5-15 m with trunk attaining 2 dm diam, the slender annotinous branches fissured gray, the reddish hornotinous ones with all leaf-axes and pe- duncles villosulous with mostly incurved yellowish hairs 0.2-0.5 mm, the foliage bicolored, the leaflets lustrous olivaceous and except for puberulent midrib gla- brous above, beneath paler dull and either glabrous or pilosulous, the margin ciliolate, the subglobose capitula axillary, solitary, immersed in foliage; an ovoid resting-bud of striate perules in most leaf-axils. Stipules dimorphic, one of each pair lance-ovate, ±4-8 x 1.5-2 mm, papery, castaneous, striate, the other much narrower, all ciliolate distally, caducous. Leaf-stalks including livid pulvinus 12- 20 mm, the petiole 3-8 mm, the 1 (2) interpinnal segments 7-12 mm; cupuliform nectaries between or immediately below each pair of pinnae 0.5-1.2 mm diam, 0.2-0.4 mm tall; pinnae (1) 2 (3)-jugate, accrescent upward, the rachis of distal pair 3-4.5 cm; leaflets upwardly accrescent, of proximal pair of pinnae regularly 2-4-jugate, of distal pair 5-6-jugate but the inner leaflet of first pair suppressed, the blades all asymmetrically trapezoid, semicordate at base, obtuse mucronulate at apex, those of distal pair 16-38 x 5-15 mm, the straight oblique midrib giving rise on each side to several widely ascending secondary venules and a reticulum prominulous on both faces of young leaflets but later immersed. Peduncles (1.5) 2-3 cm; flowers 30-40 per capitulum, sessile on conic receptacle ±1.5 mm, all homomorphic, 5-merous; bracts linear-filiform, 2-5 mm; calyx cylindro-campanulate, 2-2.8 mm, a little dilated in upper third, sordid-puberulous, the tube 5-nerved, the depressed-deltate teeth ±0.2 mm; corolla 4.5-6 mm, the tube 2.5- 4 mm, glabrous, the campanulate limb ±2 mm, its ovate lobes ±0.5 mm, externally puberulous; androecium 20-25-merous, the greenish-white filaments united into a tube 7-8.5 mm, free through 6 (7) mm; anthers ?0.3 mm diam; ovary elliptic, substipitate, puberulent distally, the glabrous style 10-12.5 mm. Pod indehiscent while on the tree, in profile broad-linear, plano-compressed, 11-18 × 1.9-2.5 cm, rounded mucronulate at apex, tapering at base into a stipe 1-5 mm, (3) 7-8 (9)-seeded, the slightly raised sutural rim shallowly undulate and crispate, the stiffly papery, glabrous or toward base puberulent valves becoming brown and finely venulose, scarcely elevated over each seed; funicle filiform; seeds plano-compressed, in broad profile obovate, 9 x 7 mm, subacutely marginate, the brown testa minutely punctate overall, the pleurogram 0.

description: Species nova, flosculis spicatis diplostemoneis cum ser. Leptostachyvis Benth. omnino congrua, leguminisque replo dilatato valvulis subaequilato M. insigni (Hassl.) Barneby manifeste affinis, ab hac pinnis 18-31 (nec 3-10)-jugis magis confertis et brevioribus (3.5-4.5, nec 6-9 cm usque longis), spicularum interpinnalium defectu, foliolis subdimidio minoribus 2.5-4 (nec 6-10) mm usque longis tenuissime (nec prominule) 3-nerviis, corollis filamentisque roseis (nec albidis), leguminisque (structura simillimi) articulis brevioribus 6-9 (nec 9.5-12) mm longis diversa.

description: Unarmed microphyllidious arborescent shrubs and treelets 1-3 m, the livid annotinous branchlets and all leaf-axes densely minutely puberulent with erect hairs not over 0.1 mm, the plane thin-textured concolorous olivaceous leaflets facially glabrous, ciliolate, the terminal, leafless or proximally leafy-bracteate pseudoraceme of narrow amentiform flower-spikes puberulent throughout and mi- nutely rufous-lepidote, eglandular. Stipules (caducous, few seen) linear-setiform 2-3 mm. Leaf stalks 10-15 cm, the petiole including obese pulvinus (5) 7-10 mm, at middle 1.2-1.7 mm diam, the interpinnal segments 4-6.5 mm, the ventral groove constricted at insertion of pinnae but spicules 0; pinnae 18-31 paired, a little decrescent near each end of leaf-stalk, the rachis of longer ones 3.5-4.5 cm, the interfoliolar segments 0.3-0.6 mm, their ventral ridge shallowly indented between each pair of leaflets but not widened distally; leaflets of longer pinnae 42-64-paired, subequilong except at each end of rachis, the small first pair arising 0.2-0.5 mm distant from minute paraphyllidia, the blades linear-elliptic from postically acutangulate base, obtuse or subacute, those near mid-rachis 2.5-4 x 0.7-0.9 mm, 3.6-5 times as long as wide, all veinless above, beneath finely 3-nerved from pulvinule, the costa centric, the lateral nerves narrowly intramarginal, pro- duced nearly to blade's apex. Primary axis of inflorescence ? 1-2 dm, the flower- spikes mostly 2-3 per node, their axis including short peduncle 6-11 cm; bracts lance-ovate, 0.4-0.8 mm, caducous; flowers 4-merous 8-androus, all or almost all bisexual, externally thinly puberulent overall and minutely rufous-lepidote (scales ±0.01 mm); calyx shallowly campanulate or subrotate ±0.5 x 1 mm, cleft half-way into low-deltate lobes; corollas pink, turbinate-campanulate 2.1-2.3 mm, the membranous ovate acute 1-nerved lobes ± 1 mm; filaments free almost to base, pink, exserted 5-5.5 mm; ovary villosulous; style ± as long as filaments. Pods linear, submoniliform, a trifle laterally compressed, attenuate at both ends, 45-80 x 3 mm, the continuous, shallowly undulate-constricted replum ± 1.5 mm wide, the firm subcoriaceous tuberculate glabrate valves tardily breaking up into 8-10 narrowly ellipsoid articles, 6-9 mm long, these rather reluctantly disengaged from the broad persistent replum; seeds vertically basipetal, plumply oblong-ellipsoid, 4.5-5 x 2 mm, the smooth testa dull brown.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1984. A new Bolivian Mimosa of section Habbasia series Leptostachyae (Leguminosae: Mimosoideae), close kin of the fictitious genus Schranckiastrum. Brittonia. 36: 248-251.

Glanduliferis (grege macrothermicae praesertim amazonicae et centrali-americanae) pertinens, ab affinibus quoad foliolorum numerum vel formam comparandis trichomatum furfuraceorum ruforum defectu necnon foliolis margine planis remota, patria et oecologia ab omnibus seriei speciebus distans.

description: Macrophyllidious shrubs with smooth arching red-brown stems up to 3-4 m, either unarmed or charged on leaf-stalks or on midrib of some leaflets with few random recurved aculei less than 1 mm, either glabrous except for minutely puberulent stipules and pulvini up to the partly axillary but later well-exserted pyramidal panicle of small white capitula or villous throughout except for ventral face of leaflets, the broad plane-margined leaflets dull brown-olivaceous above, paler beneath. Stipules erect subulate, linear-attenuate or subsetiform, 2-6 (7) x 0.4-0.6 mm, tardily deciduous. Leaf-stalks 2.5-8.5 cm, the petiole including livid pulvinus 0.5-3 cm, near middle ±1.5-2 mm diam and charged with an elliptic or subcircular urceolate nectary 2-3 mm in long diam, the 1 or 2 interpinnal segments 1.5-3.5 cm, the ventral groove bridged between pinnae and the bridge often surmounted by a small circular substipitate nectary; pinnae 2- or 3-jugate, the distal or penultimate pair longer, their axis 4-8 cm, the longer interfoliolar segments 1-2.3 cm; leaflets of proximal pinnae 2- or 3-, of distal ones 3-5-jugate, proximally decrescent, in outline broadly obliquely obovate or elliptic-obovate from inequilaterally cordate base, mucronate at obtuse or broadly deltate apex, the larger blades 2.5-5 x 2-3.4 cm, 3-5 (6)-nerved from pulvinule, the straight or subincurved costa giving rise on each side to 2 or 3 secondary venules bro- chidodrome well within the margin, these and fine 2- or 4-nary reticular venules prominulous on both faces of leaflet. Peduncles 2-5-nate, 3-10 mm, each fascicle subtended by a vestigial leaf-stalk bearing a scutellate nectary; capitula globose, without filaments 4-5 mm diam; bracts cuneate-spatulate, ±0.7 mm, early dry brown; flowers 5-merous, 10-androus, glabrous, many [male]; calyx campanulate, brownish, 0.9-1.2 mm, the deltate lobes 0.15-0.3 mm; corollas whitish, 1.6-1.8 mm, the erect, narrowly ovate, weakly 1-nerved lobes 0.5-0.6 mm; filaments whitish yellowing in age, shortly monadelphous under the ovary, exserted 1-2.5 mm; anthers ovate, 0.35-0.4 mm, apiculate by connective; ovary subsessile, densely pilosulous and sometimes minutely granular, after fertilization velutinous but the pod glabrate. Pod sessile, oblong, abruptly contracted at both ends, plano-compressed, crescentically decurved, 5-6 x 1.4-1.6 cm, the undulately constricted replum ±0.8 mm wide, smooth or remotely incipiently aculeolate, the papery venulose valves low-colliculate over each seed, breaking up when ripe into 6-8 broad panel-like articles ± 1 cm long; ripe seeds unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1984. The genus Mimosa (Mimosaceae) in Bahia, Brazil: new taxa and nomenclatural adjustments. Brittonia. 37: 125-153.

description: Unarmed shrubs or subshrubs of unknown stature, resembling M. gemmulata Barneby but notably different in indumentum, the young stems and leaf-stalks densely clad in erect, arborescently villosulous setulae up to 0.35 mm mixed with shorter gray puberulence, the narrow thick-textured leaflets densely tomentulose above, beneath both puberulent and charged with crowded sessile, brilliantly topaz-colored glands ±0.1 mm diam, submarginally ciliolate with substellately branched setulae, the long amentiform flower-spikes axillary to coevally expanding leaves. Stipules lance-subulate recurved, 1.5-2 x 0.4-0.6 mm, puberulent on both faces, persistent. Leaf-stalks of major leaves 4-9 cm, the petiole ±6-7 mm; a spicule between each pair of pinnae; pinnae 7-12-jugate, the rachis of longer distal ones 2-4.5 cm; leaflets up to 17-22-jugate, the blades linear obtuse, up to 6-7.5 x 1.5 mm, nerveless. Spikes including very short peduncle 5-7 cm, without filaments 3.5-4.5 mm diam; bracts less than 1 mm, caducous; flowers 4-merous, 8-androus, mostly bisexual; calyx campanulate, ±1 mm, thinly puberulent externally, the deltate teeth nearly as long as tube; corollas broadly turbinate-campanulate, 2.5- 2.7 mm, the ovate 1-nerved lobes ±1.5 x 1 mm, densely golden-glandular externally; filaments of unknown color but probably pink, free to base, exserted ±5 mm; ovary gray-pilosulous; pod unknown.

description: Hucusque fere ab omnibus cum M. pteridifolia Benth. commutata, ab ea stipulis parvis 0.5-2 (nec 1.5-7) mm longis, inflorescentia ad anthesin plerumque foliata, foliorum petiolo communi spiculis interpinnalibus instructo, foliolisque minoribus margine planis (maximis aut minus quam 3 mm longis aut minus quam 1 mm latis, nec 3.5-5 x 1-2 mm usque) diversa.

description: Slender shrubs 1-2.5 m or (var. adamantina) potentially arborescent and attaining 4 m with trunk up to 6 cm diam, the older defoliate branches often striped lengthwise, the hornotinous ones densely leafy, ±1-4 dm, these with axes of leaves and inflorescence pilosulous with erect, straight, or merely puberulent with shorter, incurved hairs up to 0.1-0.3 (0.4) mm intermixed in variable proportions with sessile spherical glands ±0.1 mm diam, the small crowded, plane-margined leaflets brownish glabrous and sublustrous above, beneath paler gland-sprinkled, minutely ciliolate, the flower-spikes arising mostly from axils of already expanded leaves, forming a contracted or rarely extended panicle. Stipules triangular or triangular-subulate, 0.4-1 (2) mm, deciduous. Leaf-stalks of major leaves 3-10.5 cm, the petiole including hard pulvinus 2-16 mm, the longer interpinnal segments 2.5-7 mm, the ventral groove charged between all or at least between some distal pairs of pinnae with a spicule 0.2-0.6 mm; pinnae of longer leaves 10-38-, com- monly less than 20-jugate, decrescent proximally, the rachis of longer ones 12- 55 mm, the longer interfoliolar segments 0.5-1.2 mm; leaflets of longer pinnae 18-55-jugate, subequilong except at ends of rachis, the blades oblong, oblong-elliptic, or rarely ovate, obtuse, at base inequilaterally rounded or obliquely sub- truncate, the longest 1.4-5 x 0.45-1.5 mm, ? 1.5-5 times as long as wide. Axis of flower-spikes including short peduncle (4) 5-12 cm; bracts minute, deciduous; flowers 4-merous, 8-androus, some functionally 8, the buds globose or plumply obovoid, thinly pilosulous and gland-sprinkled; calyx crateriform or shallowly campanulate, (0.3) 0.4-0.8 mm, either pilosulous or glabrate externally, the teeth 0.1-0.3 mm, separated by wide sinuses; corollas pink or creamy-pink, broadly turbinate, (1.5) 1.7-2.4 mm, the ovate subacute, 1-nerved lobes 1-1.3 mm; fil- aments pink or at times (? when fading) whitish, the longer ones exserted 4-8 mm. Pods ascending, sessile or shortly stipitate, the body narrowly oblong, when well fertilized 15-50 x (3) 3.5-5.5 (6) mm, the replum 0.4-0.8 mm wide, shallowly constricted between fertile articles or deeply so at aborted ones, the papery valves separating entire from replum and tardily breaking up into 3-9 articles 4-7 (8) mm long; seeds ±3-3.5 x 2.5 mm, the smooth but scarcely lustrous testa brown or mottled.

description: Shrubs attaining 1.5 m, with livid branches and small sensitive, dark green leaves, armed at most nodes with one infrapetiolar and two infrastipular aculei, and on internodes with random erect ones 0. 5-3 mm, the young growth puberulent and livid-granular, the leaflets smooth glabrous above, gland-dotted beneath, the loose flower-spikes racemose-paniculate. Stipules erect, linear-attenuate, + 3-4 x 0.5 mm, deciduous. Leaf-stalks 3-4 cm, unarmed or randomly aculeolate dorsally, the petiole 4-12 mm, the interpinnal segments (3) 4-7 mm, the sulcus interrupted between each pair of pinnae by a spicule; pinnae 4-7-jugate, the rachis of longer ones 12-25 mm; leaflets of longer pinnae 14-17-jugate, narrowly oblong obtuse, the larger ones 3.2-4.5 x 0.7-1.3 mm, all veinless except for weak centric midrib discolored dorsally. Axis of flower-spikes including peduncle 6-7 cm; bracts minute, deciduous; flower-buds plumply obovoid, not angulate; flowers 4-merous, 8-androus; calyx ±0.8 mm, puberulent externally, the rim obscurely undulate; corollas turbinate, ±2.4 mm, the ovate 1-nerved, nearly plane, pale pink lobes ±1 mm; filaments pale pink, free to base, the 4 longer ones exserted ±6 mm; many flowers functionally 8, the ovary of few bisexual ones glandular-papillate; pod unknown.

description: Arborescent shrubs 2-5 m, armed on infrastipular ribs of most intemnodes and on dorsal rib of some pinna-rachises with broad-based aculei 1-4 (6) mm, the cauline ones straight erect, the foliar ones recurved, the homnotinous branches, leaf-stalks, and axes of inflorescence minutely puberulent and granular, the firmly chartaceous, facially glabrous leaflets subconcolorous, the inflorescence an efoliate pseudoraceme of relatively short flower-spikes. Stipules lanceolate 4-7 x 0.6-1.4 mm, obscurely 1-nerved, persistent. Leaf-stalks 3-16 mm, the petiole 3-7 mm, the one interpinnal segment (when present) as long or a little longer; a spicule between each pair of pinnae; pinnae 1- or 2-jugate, the distal pair a little longer, the rachises 2-3.5 cm; leaflets 5-7-jugate, a little shorter near each end of rachis and commonly broader distally, the blades oblong or obovate-elliptic obtuse, the longer ones 15-24 x 5-13 mm, 4-7-nerved from pulvinule. Flower-spikes 1-4 per node, the axis including peduncle 2.5-7 cm; bracts minute, caducous; flowerbuds obovoid, glabrous beyond puberulous calyx; flowers 4-merous, 8-androus, all bisexual; calyx campanulate, 0.8-1 mm, the low-deltate teeth 0.1-0.2 mm; corollas white, pinkish in age, short-funnelform, 2.6-3 mm, the ovate acute lobes 1.2-1.8 mm; filaments white, exserted 3.2-4.5 mm; ovary glabrous. Pod sessile, broad-linear, plano-compressed, when well fertilized 5-7 x 0.8-1 cm, the smooth or remotely aculeolate replum ±0.6 mm diam, the glossy red-purple (when dry brunnescent) valves delicately venulose and minutely glandular, when ripe separating into 8-10 free-falling articles 6-9 mm long.

description: Drought-deciduous shrubs and bushy treelets 2-4 m, resembling M. bimucronata but more prickly and the epidermis of annotinous stems whitish, the young flowering branchlets either adversely or reversely aculeate, the paniculate inflorescence either efoliate or in part hysteranthously leafy, the young growth puberulent and livid-granular, the leaflets facially glabrous, ciliolate. Stipules (1) 1.5-6 x 0.5-1 mm, tardily deciduous. Leaf-stalks (1.5) 2-6 (7) cm, the petiole 8-22 mm, the interpinnal segments up to 5-10 mm; a spicule 0.4-0.9 mm between each pair of pinnae; pinnae (2) 3-7-jugate, the rachis of longer distal ones 2.5-4.5 mm, the interfoliolar segments up to 0.9-2.3 mm; leaflets of longer pinnae (17) 20-30-jugate, linear-oblong from obtusangulate base, abruptly apiculate, the larger ones 5-9 (11) x 0.8-2.1 (2.5) mm, 2 (3)-nerved from pulvinule, the displaced midrib dividing the blade 1:2-3.5, either simple or faintly penniveined above middle, the posterior vein produced almost to blade's apex. Peduncles 2- 5 per node, 5-14 mm; capitula globose, without filaments 4-5 mm diam; flower- buds obovoid, usually hispidulous near apex, sometimes subglabrous; bracts 0.7- 1 x 0.2-0.3 mm; flowers 3-merous, 6-androus, in some capitula partly or all functionally 6, in some all bisexual; calyx campanulate, 0.65-0.8 mm, the unequal triangular teeth up to 0.2-0.3 mm; corolla white, narrowly vase-shaped, ±2.2 mm, the ovate, 1-nerved lobes 0.7-1 mm; filaments white, exserted 3-5 mm; ovary glabrous. Pod either stipitate or subsessile, the stout stipe 0.7-5 mm, the broadly linear, straight or gently decurved, plano-compressed body 60-75 x 8- 10 mm, the shallowly undulate replum 0.6-0.8 mm wide, the stiffly papery valves becoming brown, sublustrous, venulose, scarcely elevated over seeds and there 0.1-0.15 mm thick in section, at the septa up to 0.2-0.3 mm thick but not suberose, when ripe separating from replum and breaking up into (6) 7-9 free-falling articles 6-8 mm long; seeds discoid, ±5.5 x 4.5 mm, the testa fuscous, dull.

description: Stout or spindling, potentially arborescent shrubs (1) 1.5-5 m, the lenticellate branches and at times some leaf-stalks erratically armed with straight or recurved, glabrous or gland-sprinkled aculei to 2-8 mm, the cauline aculei either infrastipular, or infranodal, or both, the young stems, leaf-stalks, and usually the inflores- cence in addition both puberulent and thinly to densely charged with gland-tipped setulae up to 0.1-0.5 mm (less often to 0.5-3 mm), the leaflets either glabrous, ciliolate, or glandular-ciliolate, the inflorescence an efoliate or proximally leafy-bracteate pseudoraceme exserted 1-2 dm from foliage. Stipules ovate-acuminate to narrowly lanceolate, 2.5-5 x 0.6-1.6 mm, 1-5-nerved, persistent. Leaf-stalks of primary leaves 4-13 cm (of smaller upper leaves, no further described, shorter), the petiole 8-19 mm, the longer interpinnal segments 6-12 mm; between each pair of pinnae a spicule 0.7-2 mm; pinnae 6-14 (16)-jugate, the rachis of longer ones 3.5-5 cm, its interfoliolar segments 0.6-1 (1.4) mm; leaflets of longer pinnae (27) 30-48-jugate, linear-oblong, obtuse or subapiculate, the larger ones 4.5-6.5 x 0.8-1.4 mm, the blades veinless above, subcentrically costate beneath, other venulation scarcely perceptible. Peduncles solitary and 2- or 3-nate, (1.5) 2-5 (5.5) cm; capitula subhemispherical, the lower flowers spreading-ascending, the whole without filaments 9-12 mm diam; bracts up to 1.5 mm or sometimes obsolete; flowers 4- or randomly 5-merous, diplostemonous, all bisexual; calyx campanu- late, 1.3-3.4 mm, its broadly ovate or obtusely deltate lobes separated by unequal sinuses (0.1) 0.3-0.9 mm deep; corollas greenish-white, 4.5-5.5 mm, the ovate, apically thickened, faintly 3-nerved lobes 1.4-2 mm; filaments whitish, nearly 0.3 mm diam, exserted 3-4 mm; anthers (0.55) 0.6-0.8 mm. Pods mostly 1-3 per capitulum, commonly subsessile, broadly linear, 9-13 x 0.7-0.9 cm, often lunately curved, at base cuneately contracted or tapering into a stipe up to 3 mm, at apex triangular-acuminate, the valves plano-compressed but colliculate over seeds, either glabrous or minutely puberulent and glandular-setulose overall, the shallowly undulate replum 0.6-1 mm wide, the glossy green, red-tinged, or mahogany-brown valves breaking up when ripe into 9-14 (15) free-falling, indehiscent articles 6-12 mm long; seeds ±5.5-6 x 4-4.5 mm, the testa brown or atro- castaneous, smooth.

description: Prickly sarmentose shrubs attaining 5 (-?) m, in habit, armature, scant pubes- cence, shape of leaflets and structure of pod not different from M. ceratonia var. pseudo-obovata, but in leaf-formula approaching M. carvalhoi, and the inflores- cence apparently much simplified. Peduncles (known in fruit only) arising from ±2-4 leaf-axils near end of branches, not arranged in ample leafless panicles as in related species. Pod of M. ceratonia, 6-8-seeded.

description: Subarborescent shrubs ±2.5 m with smooth, lustrous, reddish young branchlets, glabrous except for microscopic granules on new stems and axes of pyramidally branched, exserted inflorescence, armed only along back of leaf-stalks with reversed aculei ±1-1.5 mm, the few large, plane leaflets olivaceous above, paler beneath, palmately venose. Stipules triangular-subulate, 1-2.5 x 0.5-0.7 mm, 1-nerved, subpersistent. Leaf-stalks 3-9 cm, the petiole (1) 1.5-4 cm, the inter-pinnal segments 10-24 mm, the ventral groove bridged between pinnae but spicules 0; pinnae (1) 2- or 3-, in most leaves 3-jugate, subequilong or the distal pair longer, the first (or only) pair of leaflets arising (5) 8-15 mm distant from pulvinus, the interfoliolar segment, when present, ±10 mm; leaflets of almost all pinnae 1-, of rare distal pinnae 2-jugate, the blades obliquely broad-elliptic, very obtuse or subemarginate, 11-22 x 12-22 mm, as wide as or a trifle wider than long, reddish around plane margin, 5-7-nerved from pulvinule, prominulously so beneath. Peduncles 2-6 per node, 5-10 mm; capitula without filaments 4.5-5 mm diam; bracts ±1 x 0.4 mm; flowers 3-merous, 6-androus (rare random ones 4-merous, 8-androus); calyx campanulate, 0.7 mm, the rim shallowly undulate; corollas ochroleucous pink-tipped, vase-shaped, 2-2.3 mm, the ovate, 1-nerved, almost plane lobes ±1.4 x 1 mm; filaments ochroleucous, exserted 4-4.5 mm; ovary glabrous. description: Prostrate subshrubs with few-branched, reddish stems adventitiously rooting at some lower nodes and with back of leaf-stalks and peduncles densely hispid with fine, straight, erect, pliant, rufous setae ? 2-3 mm, the leaf-stalks in addition armed laterally with few horizontal aculei 3-5 mm and between all or most pairs of pinnae with a straight, stiffly ascending spicule 2.5-9 (11) mm, the leaflets glabrous and purplish-green above, beneath olivaceous, minutely puberulent and striately parallel-venulose, weakly setose-ciliate, the long-pedunculate flower-spikes axillary to coeval leaves. description: Slender, functionally subherbaceous subshrubs with remotely antrorse-aculeate, distantly leafy, simple stems ±1 m passing upward into an efoliate pseudoraceme ±1.5-2 dm of subglobose capitula, glabrous except for ciliolate stipules, floral bracts, and minutely ciliolate leaflets, the latter thick-textured, pale olivaceous and veinless above, beneath subglaucous and coarsely pallid-venulose. Stipules erect, ovate, 1.5-2.5 x 1-1.3 mm, 5-7-nerved dorsally, persistent. description: Sparsely leafy, in fruit ephedroid, erect-ascending suffrutescent herbs from carrot-shaped woody root, at anthesis (1) 2.5-7 dm, commonly glabrous throughout, but the stipules, distal branchlets, young leaves, and flowers at times thinly villosulous with fine erect hairs to 0.25-0.6 (0.7) mm and the branchlets and leaf- stalks microscopically granular, the stiff, ribbed stems repeatedly branched up- ward, the stiff leaf-stalks early leafless, the capitula shortly pedunculate in distal leaf-axils, not pseudoracemose. Stipules firm, ovate or lanceolate, 1.5-2.5 (3) mm, 1-nerved, persistent. Leaves strictly ascending, (3.5) 5-11 cm, the petiole (2.5) 4-9 cm, at middle (0.4) 0.5-1.1 mm diam, the rachis 4-25 mm, the longer (or only) interpinnal segment 4-16 mm; pinnae (1) 2- or 3-, of most leaves exactly 2-jugate, their rachis 2-12 mm, the first pair of leaflets arising 1-3 (4) mm distant from minute paraphyllidia, the longest interfoliolar segment 0.6-2.6 mm; leaflets 2-4 (5)-jugate, accrescent distally, in outline obliquely obovate or oblong-oblanceolate, obtuse or deltate-apiculate, the largest, commonly the penultimate pair, 2.5-6.5 x 1.2-3.5 mm, the thick-textured blades faintly 2-nerved from pulvinule, the midrib subcentric. Peduncles solitary or 2 (3) together, 1-2.5 cm; bracts ±1 mm; flowers 4-merous, 8-androus, the lower ones [male]; calyx membranous, obscurely denticulate, 0.3-0.4 mm; corollas turbinate-campanulate, 2.1-2.4 mm, the ovate, 1-nerved lobes 0.9-1.3 mm; filaments pink, exserted 3-4 mm. Pod subsessile, linear, acuminate at both ends, 30-57 x 3-4.5 mm, the smooth, undulate replum ±0.5 mm diam, the firm, brown, lustrous valves low-colliculate over each seed, either venulose or not, tardily breaking up into 5-8 (9) free-falling, oblong-elliptic articles ±4-5 mm long.

description: Unarmed, functionally herbaceous subshrubs with simple, pliantly humifuse stems radiating from knotty rootstock, viscid-villosulous throughout with erect, gland-tipped setae ±0.5-1.5 mm commonly mixed with fine puberulence, the plane, firm, olivaceous leaflets resinously sublustrous, the globose capitula solitary in distal leaf-axils on peduncle ± as long as the subtending leaf. Stipules mostly reflexed, broadly triangular-ovate-acuminate, 2-5 x 1.5-2.5 mm, 3-5-nerved, the midrib excurrent as a stiff yellowish mucro. Leaf-stalks 3.5-5 cm, the petiole 12-23 mm, 2.5-5 times as long as the interpinnal segments, these 3-5 mm; pinnae 6-9-jugate, the rachis of longer ones 10-17 mm; interpinnal spicules 0; leaflets of longer pinnae (13) 15-18 (19)-jugate, the blades narrowly oblong obtuse from shallowly semicordate base, those near mid-rachis 3.5-4 x 1-1.2 mm, all veinless above, beneath 2- or 3-nerved from pulvinule, the subcentric costa weakly but perceptibly pinnately branched. Peduncles 3-4.5 cm; capitula without filaments 6-6.5 mm diam; bracts linear-lanceolate, 0.9-1.3 x 0.2 mm, gland-fimbriolate; flowers 3-merous, 6-androus, some lower ones 6; calyx membranous, campanulate, 0.2 mm, the glabrous tube truncate, the rim charged with 2 or 3 minute gland-tipped setulae; corolla narrowly turbinate, nearly 3 mm, the ovate, 1-nerved lobes 1.4 x 1 mm, thinly gland-setulose dorsally; filaments pinkish-lavender, exserted 4 mm; ovary glandular-setulose. Pod narrowly oblong in profile, ±20 x 4.5 mm, 2- or 3-seeded, cuneately contracted at base into a stipe 1 mm, acuminate at apex, the shallowly undulate replum ±0.5 mm wide, the papery, stramineous valves elevated over each seed, the replum and valves alike glandular-setulose overall, the free-falling articles 4-5 mm long.

description: Slender, diffuse or ascending, functionally herbaceous subshrubs attaining ±1 m, the simple or remotely few-branched, sparsely leafy stems armed with recurved, stramineous brown-tipped, internodal aculei up to 0.6-2 mm and pilosulous with fine, white, erect hairs up to ?0.5-0.7 mm, the firm, plane leaflets glabrous, the small capitula all or mostly axillary and not or scarcely equaling the associated leaf. Stipules linear-lance-attenuate, (2.5) 3-7 x 0.45-1 mm, strongly 1-nerved, remotely ciliolate proximally, tardily deciduous. Leaf-stalks filiform, subterete, (2) 2.5-4 cm, bearing at apex a recurved appendage, one pair of pinnae, and between these an ascending spicule 1.5-2 mm, either unarmed or charged on dorsal rib with 1 or 2 small aculeoli; rachis of pinnae 8-12 mm, the longer interfoliolar segments 3-5 mm; leaflets 3- or 4-jugate, accrescent distally, the first pair arising 1.5-2 mm distant from lance-subulate paraphyllidia 0.7-1.3 mm, all obliquely obovate or broadly oblong-elliptic obtuse, semicordate at base, the distal pair 7.5-12 x 4-6 mm, all dorsally 2-nerved from pulvinule, the weak, moderately displaced midrib simple, the posterior nerve expiring beyond mid-blade. Peduncles mostly fasciculate by 2-4 (some early ones solitary), subfiliform, 18-37 mm; capitula without filaments 5-6 mm diam, the plumply ovoid flower-buds glabrous but lustrously papillate above middle; bracts 0.3-0.8 mm, 1-denticulate on each side, glabrous; flowers 3-merous, 6-androus, the lower ones mostly 6; calyx membranous, 0.3-0.4 mm, the minute teeth sometimes gland-tipped; corollas turbinate, 2.3-2.7 mm, the ovate lobes 1.2-1.4 mm, at apex purplish and a little thickened; filaments bright pink, exserted 3.5-4 mm; ovary glabrous; pod unknown.

description: Unarmed perennial herbs from weakly sufFrutescent base, the slender but stiff, erect or decumbent, simple or distally few-branched, obtusely ribbed stems (2) 3-5 dm, densely clad in strictly ascending, paucifoliolate leaves, glabrous except for a few fine cilia near base of stipules and paraphyllidia, the firm, green or subglaucescent leaflets essentially veinless externally, the small globose capitula elevated above the subtending leaf on a relatively long, slender, widely divaricate peduncle in distal leaf-axils. Stipules stiffly erect, narrowly linear-attenuate or subsetiform, 3-9 x 0.3-0.6 mm, 1-nerved, persistent. Leaf-stalks at and below mid-stem (5) 6-40 mm (a few lower ones, deciduous and not further described, up to 40-70 mm), dorsiventrally compressed, 3-ribbed, at middle 0.3-0.6 mm wide, at apex charged with a short appendage and a spicule between the one pair of pinnae; rachis of pinnae 4-9 mm, the longer interfoliolar segments 1-2 mm; leaflets 4-7-jugate, the first pair arising 0.7-2 mm distant from subulate, reddish paraphyllidia ±0.5 mm, in outline oblong-elliptic-oblanceolate, obtuse, accrescent distally, the last pair 3-5.5 x 1.5-2 mm, the immersed midrib scarcely displaced from center. Peduncles (13) 15-35 mm, compressed like leaf-stalks; capitula withoutfilaments 4-6.5 mm diam, the subglobose, reddish-purple flower-buds glabrous but resinously papillate; bracts less than 1 mm, persistent; flowers 3-merous, 6-androus, glabrous, some lower ones 6; calyx membranous, campanulate, 0.4-0.5 mm, the 3 deltate lobes sometimes minutely gland-tipped; corollas turbinate, 2-2.2 mm, the ovate, 1-nerved lobes 1.1-1.2 mm, a little thickened at reddish tip; filaments free to base, exserted up to 2.3-3 mm; ovary glabrous. Pods solitary or geminate, in profile linear, ±25-35 x 5 mm, 6-8-seeded, abruptly contracted at base into a stipe 1-2 mm and at apex into an erect cusp 1-2.5 mm, the smooth, glabrous, shallowly undulate replum 0.3-0.5 mm wide, the glabrous or microscopically puberulent valves low-colliculate over each seed, the free-falling articles ±2.5-3 mm long.

description: Haec species adspectu, oecologia necnon florum leguminisque structura arcte cum S. australi (Vell.) Irwin & Barneby congruit, sed ab ea foliolorum venis secundariis ultra mediam costam ortis ipsum in laminae marginem productis (nec intra marginem camptodromis) et in glandulam lividam excurrentibus, lamina ideo ultra mediam angulato-dentata (nec integerrima) primo intuitu distinguitur, ulterius petioli communis appendiculo terminali in nectarium phalloideum dorso nectario altero minori obsitum mutato abstat.

description: Lanky macrophyllidious shrubs and treelets 2-6 m, rufous-pilosulous especially on dorsal face of leaflets, these glabrous lustrous above, pallid beneath, the inflorescence composed of simple racemes axillary to distal leaves and shortly exserted from foliage. Stipules foliaceous, falcately semicordate and abruptly caudate-acuminate, the flabellately nerved blade up to 3-5 mm wide, the tail 2-4 mm long. Leaf-stalks 3-7 cm, produced beyond distal pair of leaflets as a phalloid glandtipped appendage bearing a smaller nectary on its back; petiole and interpinnal intervals ±10-23 mm; a subsessile nectary between each pair of pulvinules; leaflets 3 pairs, greatly accrescent distally, the blades obovate, shortly depressed-acuminate, the distal pair ±4-7 x 2.5-5 cm; costa of each leaflet pinnately branched, the proximal pairs of secondary nerves camptodrome within the margin but 2-3 distal pairs produced to margin and excurrent from it in the form of a livid gland, the tightly inrolled margin consequently angulately denticulate distally, the costa, secondary veins, and weak subscalariform tertiary venules all shallowly depressed on upper face, sharply raised and pallid beneath. Raceme-axis and peduncle together ±1-2 dm; bracts lanceolate ±3 mm caducous; pedicels 3-4 cm, subtended on one side by a phalloid nectary characteristic of ser. Laxiflorae; short outer sepals rufous-pilosulous, the inner ones glabrous, up to 12 mm; corolla of S. australis or S. velutina (Vogel) Irwin & Bameby but slightly smaller, the long abaxial petals scarcely 2.5 cm. Pod substipitate linear compressed-tetragonal ±12 x 0.45 cm, the prominent cordlike sutures shallowly undulate-constricted between seeds, the accessory valvular rib subcentric.

description: Cum sympatrica Ch. duartei (Irwin) Irwin & Bameby ob racemos e foliorum homotinorum axillis orientes comparanda, ab ea imprimis foliis abbreviatis, petiolo communi 3.5-7 (nec 7-16) cm longo, foliolis minoribus 6-12 (nec 11-18) cm longis, obtusis (nec acuminatis), coriaceis (nec papyraceis reticulatis), necnon florum subdimidio majorum sepalis 8-10 (nec 5-6) mm, petalis adaxialibus 20-22 (nec 10-13) mm antherisque 7 (nec 4-4.5) mm longis diversa. description: Arborescent shrubs attaining 3-10 m at anthesis, with trunk up to 1 dm diam, the bark of trunk and defoliate annotinous branches alike whitish-gray or pale orange-brown lenticellate, below the inflorescence glabrous throughout, the coriaceous leaves dark green above, paler (when dry brownish-olivaceous) beneath, the inflorescence of corymbiform racemes arising from axils of coetaneous leaves crowded toward tip of new branchlets. Stipules not seen, either early caducous or perhaps obsolete. Leaf-stalks 3.5-7 cm, shallowly openly grooved ventrally, the petiole 1.5-2.5 cm, at middle 1.5-2.3 mm diam, the one interpinnal segment 2-4.5 cm; a sessile shallowly saucer-shaped thick-margined nectary 2.5-3.5 mm diam immediately below each pair of pulvinules, these livid wrinkled 2-6 mm; leaflets exactly 2-jugate, the distal pair only a trifle larger, the blades elliptic or elliptic-obovate from cuneate base, broadly obtuse subemarginate or obtusely deltate at apex, the proximal pair 4-9 x 2-5 cm, the distal pair 6-12 x 2.5-6 cm; midrib of all leaflets immersed above, cariniform beneath, pinnately manybranched, the secondary nerves brochidodrome well within the revolute margin, the weak open reticulum faintly raised above, a little more pronounced beneath. Racemes simple or weakly branched from base, the primary axis 1.5-4 cm, charged with shallowly saucer-shaped nectaries 0.7-2 mm diam, the pedicels 1.2-4.5 cm, bibracteolate near or above middle, either glabrous or puberulent, the several simultaneously expanded flowers elevated above the subglobose flower-buds; sepals oblong-obovate obtuse 8-10 x 4-6 mm, fuscous-yellow, glabrous facially but minutely ciliolate; petals yellow, puberulent near short cuneate claw, all obovate or oblong-obovate obtuse but of different lengths, 3 contiguous adaxial subequilong 20-22 x 10-11.5 mm, 2 abaxial smaller and unequal, ±15-17 x 7-10 mm; filaments 10 stout 1.5 mm, densely silky-pubescent; anthers equilong, narrowly lanceolate obtuse 7 x 1.5 mm, pilosulous overall with short incurved hairs, more densely so along the sutures, each theca dehiscent by an oblique terminal slit, the connective muticous; gynoecium densely silky-strigulose, divaricate from flower's vertical axis. Pod (of sect. Apoucouita) in profile oblanceolate, a trifle incurved distally, when fully fertile ±15 x 2 cm, the rich-brown lignescent valves glabrous lustrous venulose; ripe seeds not seen.

description: Shrub 1-1.5 m tall, the trunk 2-8 cm in diameter, the branchlets glabrous; leaves estipulate glabrous, with terete petiole 15-30 mm long, the rachis 4-8 cm long; leaflets 2-3-jugate with petiolules 3-6 mm long, the blades coriaceous, ovate to elliptic-ovate, rounded and more or less cordate at the base, acute to subacuminate apically, 6-11 cm long, 3.5-5 cm wide, finely reticulate, the costa impressed on the upper surface, salient beneath; inflorescences terminal, corymbose, 6.5-12 cm long with peduncles 10-15 mm long, the axis minutely strigulose, the bracts caducous (not seen), the pedicels 18-20 mm long, minutely strigulose, the bracteoles thick-coriaceous, navicular, oblong, 18-22 mm long, 10 mm wide, the apex umbonate and with an immersed gland, externally minutely strigulose, glabrous on the inner surface, adherent with the hypanthium to the middle; hypanthium cylindric, 15 mm long, minutely strigulose; sepals subulate-lanceolate, 7.5-10.5 mm long, 1-1.8 mm wide, acuminate, glabrous except slightly strigulose minutely on the base externally; petalodia (petals none) subulate-triangular, 1-2 mm long, 0.4 mm wide, ciliolate apically; stamens 10, glabrous, the filaments 25-30 mm long, acicular, the anthers 4-5 mm long, 1.2-1.5 mm wide, oblong; stigma peltate-capitate, the style ca 20 mm long, strigulose basally, the ovary ca 5 mm long and 2 mm wide, densely strigulose, oblong, the free part of the gynophore ca 5 mm long, strigulose; fruits not seen.

description: Small glabrous tree; stipules deciduous, arcuate-linear, 3-3.5 mm long, 0.8 mm wide; petioles 5-6 mm long, slightly canaliculate on the upper surface, the rachis 10-16 mm long, canaliculate, marginate; leaflets 2-jugate, sessile, the blades more or less obovate, glabrous, discolorous, darker and shining above, paler and punctulate beneath, almost evenose but the costa salient, the blades apically obtuse, attenuate at the base, the basal pair smaller, 3-3.7 cm long, 1.5-2 cm wide, the upper pair 5.5-6 cm long, 2.5-3.3 cm wide; inflorescences axillary, racemose, 5.5- 7.5 cm long, glabrous, the bracts deciduous, thin, 3.5-4 mm long, 1.5-1.8 mm wide, oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, the pedicels 5-5.5 mm long, the bracteoles oblong-obovate, obtuse and apiculate apically, 5.5 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, thin; hypanthium glabrous with a stipe 0.3 mm long, strongly zygomorphic, cupular, 1.5 mm long; sepals 5, narrowly lanceolate, acuminate, glabrous except at apex sparsely villosulous, the 2 dorsal ones connate, 3.5 mm long, the other ones 5-5.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide; petal long-stipitate, the claw 4-5 mm long, basally auriculate, the auricles villous, the blade oblate, 3-4.5 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, glabrous; filaments slightly villous basally, 12-19 mm long, the anthers glabrous, oblong, ca 1 mm long and 0.8 mm wide; gynoecium glabrous, the stigma capitellate, the style ca 18 mm long, the ovary inequilaterally oblanceolate, 2-2.5 mm long, 1 mm wide, the gynophore 2.5-3 mm long; fruit not seen.

description: Herba prostrata, caulibus decumbentibus; stipulis amplexicaulibus, bidentatis, pubescentibus. Fo- liola (5) 7-8-juga cum impari (2.5) 3-4 x 1 mm, linearia vel elliptica, supra glabra, subtus strigoso- pubescentia. Pedunculi quam folia majores; racemis laxis 3-5-floris. Flores 6-6.5 mm longi; vexillo orbiculare 5.5 x 4 mm, reflexo. Legumen 1.5-2 x 0.25-0.3 cm, erectum, lineare, subfalcatum, fusi- forme, papyraceum strigosum vel glabrescens, subbiloculare; cum margine dorsale inflexo ? 1.2 mm lato et cum margine membranaceo inconspicuo contiguo in legumine aperto tantum viso. description: Prostrate caulescent herb from loosely branched caudex; stems 3-7 cm x 0.5 mm, the internodes 3-17 and leaf-stalks loosely strigulose; stipules membranous, 2 mm, amplexicaul and connate through more than half their length into a shortly bidentate sheath, externally white-strigulose; leaves including short petiole 3.3- 3.5 cm; leaflets (11) 15-17, opposite, decrescent distally, crowded when young but more distant in age, in outline linear-elliptic obtuse emarginate, sometimes minutely mucronate, all essentially veinless externally; peduncles 3.5-5 cm, longer than leaves; racemes loosely 3-5-flowered; bracts subulate, 0.5 mm; pedicels 1.5 mm; bracteoles 0; calyx 2.5-3.5 mm, white-strigulose, the campanulate tube 1.5- 2 mm, the subulate teeth subequilong, 1-1.5 mm; petals purple, drying violet, the banner pink to white-eyed; banner recurved through ?140?, suborbicular- emarginate, 5.5-4 mm; wings 5.5 mm, the claws 1.5 mm, the elliptic, obtuse blades 4 x 1.7 mm; keel 4 mm, the claws 1.5 mm, the semi-obovate blades 2.5 mm, abruptly incurved through 90? to the bluntly deltate apex; ovary strigulose; style glabrous, the stigma capitellate; ovules 14; pod erect, when ripe disjointing from the receptacle, in profile shallowly lunate-elliptic, 1.5-2 x 0.25-0.3 cm, ventrally carinate by the gently concave suture, below middle compressed-tri- gonous with obtuse lateral angles and openly sulcate, thence laterally compressed and contracted into a triangular-acuminate beak, the papery strigulose valves delicately transverse-venulose, narrowly inflexed below middle of pod, with an incipient septum to 0.2 mm wide, this obsolete in the beak; dehiscence unknown; seeds 13 or 14, reniform, 2.5 x 2 mm, the smooth testa pale brown, unmottled.

description: Shrub or tree 2-35 m, branches tomentose. Leaves imparipinnately (5-)9-15-foliolate; stipules subulate, 2.9-9.6 X 0.7-1.8 mm, tomentose; petiole 1.6-3.2 cm, terete, tomentose; rachis 10.5-22.5 cm, stipellate to alate, tomentose; stipels 2 X 0.5 mm, strigose to tomentose; wing 3.3 mm wide; petiolule 1.4-2.7 mm, puberulous to tomentose; terminal leaflets elliptic, 4.5-10.5 X 2.2-5.5 cm, the laterals ovate to oblong-elliptic, base rounded to cordate, apex acute to retuse-mucronate, all tomentose beneath, venation sulcate to plane above and prominent beneath. Inflorescence arising from leafless branches, racemose or paniculate, 4.6-23.8 cm, the axis tomentose; bracts attached to the pedicel base, ovate, 3-6.8 X 2.1-3.3 mm, tomentose; bracteoles attached to the pedicel apex, lanceolate, 2.2-4.7 X 1.3-1.5 mm, tomentose; pedicels 4.8-6.6 mm, tomentose. Buds globose, 6.9-10.3 X 6.6-9.3 mm, puberulous to tomentose. Calyx 3-5-lobed, the lobes heteromorphic, glabrous internally. Petal white, claw 3.1- 4.1 X 1.7-2.8 mm, the blade oblate, 9-10.7 x 14-18 mm, the base cordate, villous-sericeous externally. Stamens dimorphic, larger ones 4, the filaments 9-10 mm, white, villous, the anthers 2-2.5 X 1.2-1.5 mm, yellow, glabrous, the smaller stamens many, the filaments ±6.5 mm, white, gla- brous, the anthers 0.8 X 1 mm, glabrous, yellow. Gynoecium green-ferruginous, sericeous, gynophore 4.5-6.5 mm, ovary 6.5- 8.5 X 2.5-3.5 mm, style 1-1.9 mm, lateral, glabrous, stigma punctiform, glabrous. Legume 3-4 X 2-2.7 cm, brown, puberulous to tomentose, seed pale brown, aril yellow.

Gray et A. micromerium Bamneby referenda, a prioris var. crispulo, habitu florumque magnitudine simillimo, pilis omnibus basifixis (nec dolabriformibus), a secunda, quoad pubem simili, habitu robustiori, foliis longioribus, floribus magis numerosis, leguminibus admodum majoribus, ovulisque saepissime 6 (nec 4) diversa.

description: Humifuse matted perennial herb with many freely branching, densely leafy stems to 3.5 (4) dm, radiating from the scarcely indurated multicipital crown of a taproot, originating at soil surface but commonly buried for more than half the length by sand moving downslope, densely softly pilosulous throughout with fine, spreading-ascending, mixed sinuous and straighter basifixed hairs to ± 1 mm, the foliage silvery-gray. Stipules 2-5.5 mm, the small lowest ones early scarious, the upper herbaceous, all connate-amplexicaul, the lowest into cuplike sheath, the upper with deltate-acuminate, often squarrose blades, internally glabrous or thinly pubescent near the tip. Leaves arcuately spreading, (1) 1.5-4 cm long, the petiole ±0.5-1.3 cm, the rachis (0.5) 1-2.5 cm. Leaflets (7) 9-15, subsessile, decrescent upward along rachis, obovate- or oblong-elliptic, abruptly acuminulate, convex ventrally, (1.5) 2.5-9 x (0.7) 1-3 (4) mm. Peduncles subfiliform, 1.5-2.5 cm long, at anthesis incurved-ascending, humistrate in fruit. Racemes shortly but loosely 4-10-flowered, the flowers ascending-spreading, the axis scarcely elongating, in fruit 3-12 mm long; bracts narrowly lanceolate, 2-3.5 mm long; pedicels ascending, in fruit persistent but scarcely thickened, 0.9-1.5 mm long; bracteoles 0. Calyx ?5.5 mm long, pilosulous like the foliage with white and sometimes a few, commonly shorter, fuscous hairs, the oblique disc 0.6 mm wide, the campanulate tube 2.8-3 x 2.2 mm, ruptured by the pod, the narrowly subulate teeth 2.4-2.6 mm long. Petals whitish, fading or drying pale ochroleucous, the banner then faintly lilac-veined and often faintly blushed with lilac, the keel maculate with dull, dark purple; banner recurved through 40º, narrowly obovate or subrhombic- obovate, deeply notched, 7.6-8.2 x 4 mm; wings slightly shorter, ±6.8-7.1 mm, the claw 2.7 mm, the narrowly lance-elliptic, slightly incurved blade 4.6 x 1.3-1.8 mm; keel ±5.2 mm long, the claws 2.7 mm, the blades semiobovate, 2.8 x 1.7 mm, incurved through ±110º to the broadly deltate, slightly porrect apex; anthers 0.3 mm; ovary pilosulous; pod humistrately ascending, sessile, tardily disjointing from the receptacle, obliquely semi-ovoid, ±6 x 3 mm excluding the persistent style base, broadly rounded at the base, in the lower 2/3 triquetrously compressed, carinate by the concavely arcuate ventral suture, openly and shallowly sulcate dorsally, in the distal 1/3 laterally compressed and abruptly deltoid-beaked, the pale green, finally brownish chartaceous valves pilosulous with short ± straight and contorted hairs, sometimes faintly purple-speckled, not inflexed; dehiscence apical, through the gaping beak; ovules (4) 6; seeds brown, purple-dotted, smooth, dull, 1.9-2.5 mm long. Chromosomes, 2n = 24.

description: Mimosae adenocarpae Benth. certe, M. inamoenae Benth. distantius affinis, cum ambabus habitu, foliorum formula, petiolis spiculiferis, capitulisque parvis globosis congrua, sed ab ambabus caulibus inermibus, petiolo vero subnullo (pinnarum par primum juxta folii pulvinum oritur), petiolo communi breviori 1-3 (nec 3.5-11) cm longo, pinnisque 2-4 (nec 5-10)-jugis, ulterius a M. inamoena foliis viscido-villosulis (nec glabris) diversa.

description: Unarmed microphyllidious shrubs ±2 m with terete branches repeatedly forking distally, viscid-villosulous nearly throughout with erect or incurved plain hairs and gland-tipped setulae up to 0.2-0.25 mm, the many small subsessile leaves concolorous, the leaflets thinly puberulent beneath, glabrous above, glandular-ciliolate, the small globose capitula arising mostly from the axil of coevally expanding leaves, some at tip of secondary branchlets shortly pseudoracemose in praefloration. Stipules ascending, thinly herbacous lance-elliptic 1-2 mm, 1-nerved dorsally, glandular-puberulent, persistent. Leaf stalks 1-3 cm, the true petiole reduced or almost so to slender livid pulvinus, at most 1 mm longer than it, the longest of the slender interpinnal segments 6-14 mm, the narrow ventral groove bridged between each pinna-pair and there charged with an ascending stramineous spicule 0.4-0.9 mm; pinnae 2-4-jugate, accrescent distally, the rachis of longer ones 12-20 mm, the longer interfoliolar segments 0.8-1.2 mm; leaflets of distal pinnae 9-18-jugate, a little decrescent at each end of rachis, the first pair arising 0.7-1.3 mm distant from subulate paraphyllidia 0.2-0.6 mm, the blades linear- oblong from auriculate base, obtuse at apex, those near mid-rachis 2.3-4.2 x 0.6-1 mm, all nerveless above, beneath weakly 2 (3)-nerved from pulvinule, the straight simple midrib only a trifle displaced from center, the posterior nerve(s) weak, short or almost imperceptible. Peduncles solitary and paired 6-14 mm; capitula without filaments 4 mm diam, prior to anthesis moriform, the plumply obovoid flower-buds thinly viscid-villosulous; bracts spatulate-oblanceolate 0.5- 0.6 mm, minutely glandular-ciliolate; flowers 4-merous 8-androus, all but a few at base of capitulum bisexual; calyx membranous, shallowly campanulate 0.3 mm, glabrous or glabrescent, the minutely denticulate rim charged with a few gland-tipped setulae; corolla 1.9-3 mm, the turbinate tube glabrous, the ovate membranous 1-nerved, shallowly convex lobes ±1 x 0.7 mm, thinly glandular- puberulent dorsally; filaments lilac-pink, free to base, the longer set exserted ±3 mm. Pods numerous in loose heads, in profile undulate-linear, gradually contracted into a basipetally tapering stipe 3-5 mm and at apex into an erect cusp 3-7 mm, the seminiferous body 15-23 x 4 mm, 3-5-seeded, the replum ±0.4 mm diam, the papery valves bullately elevated over each seed, the replum and valves alike thinly pilosulous and viscid-setulose overall, the ripe valves breaking up into free-falling, individually dehiscent articles articles 2.5-4 (4.5) mm long; seeds unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. & Fortunato, Renée H. 1987. Four new diplostemonous species of Mimosa (Mimosaceae) from Paraguay and eastern Bolivia. Brittonia. 39: 165-174.

description: Omnibus fere notulis cum M. farinosa Griseb. congrua, sed foliorum pinnis 2-3-, nec exacte 1-jugis diversa; a M. dentinenti Bentham, cujus pinnae interdum inter 1-jugas nonnullae 2-jugae evadunt, aculeis ad nodos subrectis (nec recurvis), calycis dimidio brevioris dentibus erectis (nec apice incurvis), necnon legumine angustiori 7-9.5 (nec 12-16) mm lato glanduloso-puberulo (nec glabro) distantior.

description: Stiffly branched xeromorphic microphyllidious drought-deciduous shrubs 1.2-3 m, with stout purplish-castaneous, sparsely pallid-lenticellate branchlets armed at or close below random nodes with infrastipular, straight or subrecurved aculei 1.5-5 mm and viscidulous throughout with scattered minute capitellate setulae ±0.1 mm tall, the delicate leaves and solitary peduncles arising from brachyblasts thatched with imbricated stipules, the olivaceous concolorous thin-textured leaf- lets either glabrous or puberulent facially, minutely ciliolate or gland-fimbriolate, the marginal glands becoming impressed in mature leaflets. Stipules erect firm, accrescent upward along brachyblasts, varying from deltate to lanceolate 0.7-3 x 0.4-0.8 mm, the larger ones 3-nerved dorsally, all persistent. Leaf-stalks 4-10 mm, the petiole 1.5-4 x 0.2 mm, the longer interpinnal segments 1-3 mm, the ventral groove subobsolete, spicules 0; pinnae 2-3-jugate, the rachis 2.5-5 mm, the interfoliolar segments 0.2-0.5 mm; leaflets of distal pinnae 6-9-jugate, the first pair arising 0.3-0.5 mm distant from reflexed subulate paraphyllidia 0.2-0.4 mm, the blades elliptic or obovate-elliptic from auriculate base, obtuse at apex, the longer ones 1.2-3.5 x 0.4-1.5 mm, +2.5-3 times as long as wide, all faintly 2 (3)-nerved from pulvinule, the inner posterior nerve produced beyond mid- blade. Peduncles 5-13 mm; capitula globose, without filaments 6-6.5 mm diam, prior to anthesis moriform, the obtuse flower-buds puberulent at apex; bracts lance-elliptic 1-1.3 x 0.3-0.4 mm, brown-tipped, puberulent dorsally, glandular-ciliolate, deciduous; flowers 4-merous 8-androus, all bisexual; calyx campanulate 0.3-0.6 mm, externally puberulent, the unequal teeth 0.1-0.2 mm; corolla trumpet-shaped 2-2.8 mm, obtusely 4-angulate, the broadly ovate acute, almost plane, faintly 1-nerved lobes 0.6-0.9 mm; filaments either white or pink, shortly coherent around base of ovarian stipe, exserted 3-5 mm; style longer than stamens. Pod (not seen fully ripe), stipitate, the oblong body ±25-32 x 7-9.5 mm, abruptly apiculate at apex and abruptly contracted at base into a stipe ±7 mm, 4-seeded, the replum 0.2-0.3 mm diam, the papery purplish-brown valves puberulent and minutely sparsely glandular overall, the articles 5-10 mm long, presumably free-falling from replum.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. & Fortunato, Renée H. 1987. Four new diplostemonous species of Mimosa (Mimosaceae) from Paraguay and eastern Bolivia. Brittonia. 39: 165-174.

description: Hinc M. rojasii Hassler, illinc M. neptunioidi Harms, ambabus quoad stipulas bracteolasque florales striato-nervosas similibus, affinis, a prima pube nullibi glandulosa, pinnis abbreviatis 1.5-2 (nec 3.5-5) cm longis, foliolis 9-14 (nec 15-30)-jugis dorso dense puberulis, pedunculis elongatis 5-9 cm longis folio suffuilcranti subaequilongis, a secunda inter alia stipulis 9-11 (nec 30-50)-nerviis, pinnis 7-9 (nec 2-4)-jugis, necnon leguminibus 4-6 (nec 3-3.5) mm latis, ab utraque flosculis in spicam julaceam (1.5) 3-7 cm longam dispositis (nec capitulatis) eximie diversa.
