description: Unarmed, amply microphyllidious, functionally herbaceous subshrub with erratically few-branched terete humifuse stems 6 dm long or longer, finely villosulous and weakly hispid with short erect pallid hairs up to ±0.2 mm and weak subhorizontal tapering setae 0.5-2 mm, the brown-olivaceous concolorous leaflets glabrate ventrally, villosulous beneath, distantly setose-ciliate, immarginate, the dense oblong-cylindric flower-spikes solitary on a long peduncle in upper leaf-axils, humistrate in fruit. Stipules spreading and in age deflexed, broadly ovate-triangular obtuse 1.5-3.5 x 1.2-3 mm, the papery castaneous blades striately 9-11-nerved, dorsally puberulent, persistent. Leaf-stalks laterally compressed 5-8 cm, the petiole including livid pulvinus 6-11 mm, at middle 0.6-1 mm diam, the longer interpinnal segments 6-10 mm, the narrow ventral sulcus bridged between pinnae but spicules 0; pinnae 7-9-jugate, subequilong, the rachis 1.5-2 cm; leaflets 9-14-jugate, the first pair arising 1-2 mm distant from elliptic paraphyllidia 0.4-0.7 mm, the blades narrowly oblong obtuse from shallowly semi- cordate base, the larger ones 3-6 x 1-1.7 mm, 3.3-4.5 times as long as wide, all 3-4-nerved from pulvinule, the subcentric midrib 1-2 (3)-branched on each side near and above mid-blade, the anterior nerve and the inner posterior one narrowly intramarginal, produced to blade's apex, the outer posterior one very short, the venulation almost imperceptible on upper face, obtusely prominulous beneath. Peduncles stout ascending 5-9 cm, ± as long as subtending leaf-stalk; spikes densely many-flowered, without filaments ±4.5 mm diam, the axis becoming (1.5) 3-7 cm; bracts resembling stipules in shape, texture and striate venulation, 1-2 mm, puberulent dorsally, caducous; flowers 4-merous 8-androus, the proximal ones apparently all infertile; calyx papery-membranous, shallowly campanulate 0.2-0.5 mm, glabrous externally, the obscurely denticulate rim ciliolate with setulae 0.2-0.5 mm; corolla turbinate-campanulate 2.2-3 mm, the 4-ribbed tube glabrous, the triangular-ovate, shallowly cucullate, scarcely thickened lobes ±0.9 x 0.8 mm, thinly hirsutulous dorsally; filaments pale pink, united below ovary through ±0.2 mm, exserted 5.5-6.5 mm; ovary hirsutulous. Pods ±4-10 per spike, ascending from upper half of floral axis, in profile undulately linear 20-42 x 4-6 mm, 4-7-seeded, the shallowly constricted replum 0.5-0.7 mm diam, the papery brown valves colliculate over each seed, when ripe breaking up into free-falling, individually dehiscent articles 5-8 mm long, the replum and valves alike villosulous overall and hispid with slender erect setae up to ±1.5 mm; seeds compressed-obovoid ±3.5-4 x 2.5-3 mm, the atrocastaneous testa smooth lustrous.

description: Habitu toto M. uliginosae Hassler accedens, tam ab ea quam a M. paraguariae Micheli (iisdem locis obvia) foliorum petiolo communi spiculis conspicuis interpinnalibus praedito paraphylidiisque subulatis (nec dilatatis foliolaceis) diversa, iisdem notulis M. orthocarpam (remote allopatricam) revocans, ab hac setis caulinis glanduloso-capitatis inter se aequilongis (nec longioribus brevioribusque 0.2-1.4 mm longis commixtis) necnon foliolis 3-nerviis, nervo anteriori ultra mediam laminam brochidodromo abstans.

description: Erect, densely leafy microphyllidious shrubs perhaps 1 m or more, except for glabrous faces of leaflets viscid-hispidulous throughout with crowded erect gland-tipped setulae 0.2-0.3 mm and randomly armed with few straight erect stramineous internodal aculei up to 0.5-4 mm, the thin-textured leaflets olivaceous con- colorous, the ellipsoid capitula shortly pseudoracemose in praefloration, early equalled or surpassed by leaves, the fruits immersed in foliage. Stipules submembranous lanceolate 1.5-3 x 0.4-0.8 mm, 1-nerved dorsally, persistent, the plane margin glandular-fimbriolate. Leaf-stalks 4-8 cm, the petiole 6-12 x 0.5-1 mm, the longer interpinnal segments 5-9 (10) mm, the ventral groove bridged between pinna-pairs and there charged with a proximally puberulent spicule 1-2 mm; pinnae (5) 6-9-jugate, conspicuously accrescent upward, the rachis of distal pair (12) 15-30 mm, the longer interfoliolar segments 0.6-1.3 mm; leaflets of distal pinnae (15) 18-25-jugate, subequilong except at very ends of rachis, the first pair arising 0.6-1.8 mm distant from subulate paraphyllidia 0.2-0.5 mm, the blades linear-oblong from obtusangulate base, obtuse at apex, those near mid-rachis 2- 5.3 x 0.7-1.5 mm, +4-4.5 times as long as wide, all veinless above, beneath finely 3-nerved from pulvinule, the midrib subcentric, simple or weakly 1-branched on each side near apex, one anterior primary nerve and one posterior one brochid-odrome far beyond mid-blade, the plane margin glandular-fimbriolate. Peduncles solitary or geminate 1.5-3.5 cm; capitula ellipsoid, without filaments 8-10 x 4.5 mm, prior to anthesis moriform, the obtuse flower-buds thinly stipitate-glandular at tip; bracts membranous linear-spatulate 0.6-1 x 0.2-0.3 mm, glandular-fimbriolate; flowers 4-merous 8-androus, all but a few lowermost ones bisexual; calyx membranous campanulate 0.45-0.75 mm, the shortly denticulate rim glandular-fimbriolate; corolla turbinate 2.3-3 mm, the ovate, shallowly concave 1-nerved lobes 1-1.3 x 0.8-1 mm, thinly glandular distally; filaments pink, united at very base into a stemonozone 0.2-0.3 mm, exserted ±4.5 mm. Pods (not seen fully ripe) 5-12 per capitulum, ascending in dense clusters, in profile undulately linear from attenuate substipitate base, up to 40 x 4 mm, 8-12-seeded, the shallowly constricted replum ±0.4 mm diam, the papery valves bullately elevated over each seed, the replum and valves alike densely viscid-hispidulous overall with crowded erect gland-tipped setae, those of replum short, those of valves attaining 0.8-1.4 mm, the presumably free-falling articles 3.5-4 mm long; seeds unknown.

description: Leaves (18-) 21-30 (-4) cm long, typically both the glands and pubescence sparse to almost glabrous. Characterized especially by the 5 (-7) rather large, ovate to ovate-elliptic leaflets which are about half as wide as long, the blades of the terminal leaflet (9-) 12-15 (-19) cm long, (5-) 6-8 (-10) cm wide, all with long petiolules of (7-) 9-10 (-12) mm, and a non-papillate lower epidermis; axillary buds mostly golden-brown puberulent, markedly pointed, being long acuminate or narrow coneshaped (Fig. 3).

description: Shrubs 1-2 m; leaf-stalks of major leaves 3-8 cm, the petiole 2-4 (5) mm, the interpinnal segments 2.5-5 mm; pinnae 10-19 (29)-jugate; leaflets of longer pinnae 18-30-jugate; pod when well fertilized 3-5-seeded; otherwise as in key.

description: Hucusque cum M. zygophylla Benth. commutata sed ab ea petiolis ventre 2-nec 1-sulcatis, foliolis cujusque pinnae 2-3-nec exacte 2-jugis, leguminisque valvulis maturis articulatis (nec indivisis) manifeste diversa; leguminis forma M. boreali A. Gray et M. unipinnatae propius affinis videtur, a priori corollae lobulis ultra medium in tubum concretis (nec fere a basi inter se liberis) foliolisque minus numerosis, a secunda foliis bipinnatis (nec paripinnatis) flosculisque 5- nec 4-meris abstat.

description: Stiffly branched microphyllidious desert shrubs attaining 2 m, with divaricate long-shoots clad in pallid epidermis early shredded and exposing brownish wood, these armed at or well below most nodes with straight or recurved, early blanched aculei 1.5-5 mm, glabrous except for minutely filamentous-tomentellous stipules and (rarely) microscopically puberulent leaf-stalks; primary leaves of long-shoots solitary, soon deciduous, most leaves and all peduncles fasciculate on densely scaly hemispherical brachyblasts along annotinous branches, the thick-textured pale green or subglaucescent leaflets glabrous concolorous. Stipules of primary leaves subulate-setiform, 0.5-2 mm, those imbricated on brachyblasts triangular- subulate, less than 1 mm, persistent. Leaf-stalks (1.5) 2-14 (18) mm, dorsiventrally compressed and a little dilated distally, above middle 0.4-0.9 (1) mm wide, narrowly 2-grooved on each face; pinnae of most leaves 1-jugate, of rare primary leaves 2 (3)-jugate, the rachis then 1.5-4 (7) mm; paraphyllidia suppressed, or rudimentary and only on outer side of pulvinus; leaflets of almost all pinnae exactly 2-, in random primary leaves 2- or 3-jugate, the blades varying from obliquely ovate or lance-elliptic to oblanceolate or obovate, either obtuse or acute, the distal pair 1.5-4 x 0.6-2 mm, 1.5-4 times as long as wide, all veinless above, beneath faintly bluntly 1-3-nerved from pulvinule, the subcentric midrib simple or 1- or 2-branched on each side. Peduncles 1 or 2 per brachyblast, (4) 5-16 (20) mm; capitula without filaments (5) 6-8 mm diam; bracts minute caducous; ped- icels 0.4-1.5 mm; flowers 5-merous, 10-androus, mostly bisexual; calyx mem- branous, turbinate or campanulate, 0.45-0.9 mm, the subtruncate orifice glabrous or minutely ciliolate; corolla turbinate-campanulate 2-2.8 mm, glabrous exter- nally, the ovate, often unequal, weakly 1-nerved lobes 0.5-1.1 x 0.5-0.8 (0.9) mm, microscopically fimbriolate at margin; filaments pink, monadelphous through 0.2-0.5 mm around stipe of ovary, exserted 3-4.3 mm. Pods 1-2 per capitulum, subsessile but attenuate or abruptly contracted below first seed into a stipelike neck ?2-4 mm, the body in profile undulately linear, arched downward or variably twisted, (15) 25-60 x 5-8 mm, (2) 3-8 (9)-seeded, the constricted replum 0.4-0.7 mm wide, either unarmed or armed on dorsal rib of seminiferous suture with random erect aculei ±1-2.5 mm, the papery green, later stramineous or brownish valves bullately elevated over each seed, when ripe breaking up into free-falling, individually dehiscent articles 6-9 mm long; seeds plumpy ovoid, ±4 x 3.5 x 3 mm, the testa castaneous lustrous.

description: Caulibus herbaceis et floribus minusculis D. exili DC. proxima, sed habitu fortiori, caulibus 9 (nec 1.5-6) dm usque longis sicut folia pube e pills erectis tenuibus spiraliter tortis 0.5-1.2 mm longis constanti villosis, pedunculoque axin caulinum primarium terminanti valido 9-21 (nec 1-7) cm longo, ulterius a D. exilis formis in ditione Cajamarca vicinisque obviis florum majorum carinae petalis 4- 5 (nec 2.5-3) mm longis diversa.

description: Herbaceous from woody root +/- 5 mm diam, villous almost throughout with erect, fine spiral hairs of different lengths (+/-0.5-1.2 mm), the diffusely ascending, remotely glandular-punctate stems up to 9 dm long, randomly branched from near middle upward, the leaves pallid-green or subglaucous, the dense cylindric flower-spikes terminal to the main stem and lateral branches. Stipules linear- attenuate or softly setiform with flexuous tip, including leaf-spur 3-5 mm long, persistent. Leaf-stalks slender 8-21 mm, the interfoliolar intervals 1-3 mm; leaflets 1 1-15, subequilong, the 3 terminal ones palmate, the blades elliptic-oblanceolate or narrowly obovate 2.5-5.5 x 1.2-2.2 mm, obtuse but gland-mucronate, loosely conduplicate, smooth glandless above, beneath speckled with livid-brown glands 0.05-0.15 mm diam. Peduncles terminating each primary stem 9-21 cm, those of lateral branches shorter; flower-spikes 2-5 cm long, including bracts but without the petals +/- 1 cm diam; bracts cymbiform, the body (spread out) oblong-obovate ?4 x 3 mm, abruptly contracted into a subulate tail +/- 1 mm, in texture mem- branous, whitish except for a lurid, glandular-verruculose patch at tip. Calyx 4.5- 5 mm, densely finely villous with ascending hairs, the tube +/- 3 mm, the dorsal tooth 1.3-1.9 mm, the lateral ones a trifle shorter; petals bicolored, the banner ochroleucous but early rubescent, the wings and keel vivid blue-violet, all glandless or the base of banner-blade bearing an obscure gland-crescent and the keel an obscure subapical gland; banner 6-7 mm, the blade 3.5 x 4-4.5 mm; episte monous petals perched 2.5-3 mm above hypanthium, the detached keel 5.3-6.5 mm, its blades 4-5 x 3-3.6 mm; androecium 8 mm long. Pod in profile triangular +/-2.5 x 2.5 mm, the submembranous valves pilosulous above middle, almost eglandular.

description: Omnibus ab affinibus andinis foliis minimis palmatim 3-foliolatis diversissima. Fruticulus diffusus gracilis hinc inde radicans, praeter caulem canescentem parce puberulus, foliis plerisque secus brachy- blastos laterales confertis; inflorescentia spicata pauciflora subterminalis, floribus iis D. weberbaueri simillimis; calyx sericeus +/- 5 mm longus brevidentatus; petala bicoloria, vexillo juniore albido cito sordescenti, glandulis sparso, caeteris vivide purpureis, carinae laminis +/- 5 x 4 mm, glandula unica subapicali provisis.

description: Slender, procumbent, adventitously rooting shrublets with randomly branched stem 1-4 (-?) dm long bearing at short intervals densely foliate brachyblasts less than 1.5 cm long, puberulent with loosely ascending subflexuous pallid hairs up to 0.2-0.3 mm long, the primary stems subcanescently so, the very small trifoliolate leaves thinly so, green and grossly gland-punctate, the few, shortly, loosely flowered spikes leaf-opposed near end of homotinous long-shoots. Stipules lan- ceolate 1-1.5 mm long, when young reddish, in age dry, fuscous, deciduous. Leaf- stalks 0.7-1.4 mm long; leaflets 3, palmate, linear-oblanceolate 4-6.5 x ?0.5 mm, gland-mucronate, tightly involute, convex dorsally, narrowly sulcate ven- trally, charged dorsally on each side of the immersed midrib with one row of impressed glands 0.1-0.25 mm diam and toward margin with few scattered smaller ones. Peduncles 1-2.5 cm long; spikes loosely 7-12-flowered, the axis becoming 6-16 mm long; bracts ovate 3-4.5 mm, abruptly short-acuminate, in profile +/- 1.3 mm wide, becoming dry but persistent through anthesis. Calyx +/- 5 mm long, silky-villosulous, the 10-ribbed tube +/- 3.3 x 2.5 mm, the intercostal membranes charged with 2 or 3 small pallid glands, the dorsal tooth +/- 1.7 mm long, the rest scarcely shorter; vexillum +/- 7 mm long, the blade 5 x 6 mm, opening whitish but soon sordescent, gland-sprinkled; epistemonous petals perched 1.5-2 mm distant from hypanthium, the blades vivid purple, those of wings +/- 5 x 2.5 mm,  those of keel 5 x 4 mm, charged with one subapical gland; ovary pilosulous above middle; pod not seen.

description: Small suffruticose perennial to 25(-40) cm tall, with (1)2-3 main stems which bear short annually produced branches commonly <15 cm long, older branches beige and commonly with a thin layer of whitish cork; branches; the branches and foliage commonly glabrous or sparsely pilose with whitish hairs to 0.8 mm long, the plant otherwise glabrous. Stipules 0.4-1.5(-1.6) X 0.2-0.8(-1.6) cm, persistent, obliquely lanceolate or obliquely ovate, commonly falcate, the lower lobe forming an angle of (10-)20-45(-80)º with the longitudinal axis of the stipule, the upper lobe absent thus the edge adjacent to the petiole incurvate, or present and forming a - 135º to -180º angle with the longitudinal axis of the stipule, venation commonly inconspicuous in both surfaces especially in younger stipules, consistency rather thin, base lobate or rarely acute, apex acute, without a conspicuous mucro, sometimes the stipules of the same leaf from the upper portion of the leafless flowering branches united forming a 3-lobed structure. Leaves 5.6-10(-14) cm long; petiole (0.5-)0.7-1.5 cm long; rachis (1.1-)1.5-5.5(-7) cm long, with (5-)7-19 (-21) leaflets, stipels 0.4-1.2(-1.8) mm long, 0.1 mm wide at the base, often absent, linear triangular, yellowish green; petiolule 1-2 mm long, leaflets 0.7-2.7(-3.8) X 0.2-1(-1.4) cm, the lamina narrow elliptic to wide elliptic or lanceolate and folding in drying, consistency rather thin, the base acute, obtuse or rounded, the apex acute or rarely rounded, mucro 1-1.5 mm long. Flowers ascendant, borne solitary, in groups of 2(3), or on leafless branches and appearing racemose; peduncles 0.5-1 cm long; bracteoles (0.1-)0.3-0.6 X 0.08-0.1 mm, narrowly triangular to linear, normally persistent, opposite or rarely alternate; calyx 0.6-1.2 X 0.3-0.4 cm, campanulate; 2 vexillar lobes (3.8-)4-5(-7) mm long, (2-) 3(-4) mm wide (both lobes), free 1/4-1/3(-1/2) of their length; lateral lobes 3.8-5.5 X 1.5- 2 mm; carinal lobe (3-)4.3-7(-8) X (0.7-) 1.5-2.3 mm; standard (1-)1.5-1.9 X (1-) 1.9 cm, red, reflexed 80-1350, widely obovate and becoming narrowed at the base, auriculate, the apex deeply cleft to 2.8 mm long, claw 1.5-2.8 X 0.7-1 mm; wing petals 1.3-1.4 X 0.5-0.6 cm, obliquely oblanceolate, red, claw 2 X 0.3-0.4 mm; keel petals 1.2-1.4 X 0.47-0.6 cm, pinkish, lunate, the ventral face straight, claw 2 mm long, auricula of the keel forming a 1350 angle with claw; androecium 1.2-1.4 cm long; ovary 1.7 cm long, stamens diadelphous (monadelphous in one flower), with a brownish, infrastaminal disk 0.5 mm long at the base of the ovary, with 4-5 ovules, style 7 mm long, slightly exserted from the keel. Fruits and seeds unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Dorado, Óscar. 1999. Brongniartia riesebergii (Fabaceae: Faboideae): A new species from the state of Durango, Mexico. Brittonia. 51: 398-402.

description: Habitu inflorescentiam usque necnon foliolorum numero et ambitu Ch. adenophyllae (Taubert) Irwin & Barneby proxima, sed ab omnibus seriei suae speciebus floribus solitariis e folii evoluti axillo ortis (nec in racemo terminali brevibracteato dispositis), ulterius ab ipsa Ch. adenophylla pube viscidosetosa longiori, stipulis 3-4 (nec ±1) mm longis, necnon sepalis aureo-setosis diversa. Flores axillares et foliola 3-4-juga Ch. catharticam var. paucijugam Irwin & Barneby revocant, sed haecce a nostra foliolis majoribus margine revolutis corollaeque cucullo quam petala caetera breviori (nec longiori) distat.

description: Round-headed shrubs attaining ±2 m, with slender erect fuscous, repeatedly forking efoliate trunks and short, densely leafy hornotinous branchlets, the pale green or subglaucescent foliage villosulous throughout with fine plain hairs and (except for upper face of leaflets) viscid-pilosulous with erect bulbous-based yellowish excretory setulae up to ±1 mm, the flowers solitary in distal leaf-axils, immersed in foliage. Stipules erect, softly setiform 3-4 x 0.3 mm, green turning brown, deciduous. Leaf-stalks slender 2-3 cm, the petiole ±10-13 x 0.5 mm, the intervals between pinna-pairs 4-7 mm; leaflets 3-4 pairs, subaccrescent distally, the blades narrowly lance-oblong acute from moderately oblique base, the distal pair 10-15 x 2-3.5 mm, the margin of all slightly elevated on blade's ventral face, the centric midvein prominulous beneath only, indistinctly 3-5-branched on either side. Pedicels 7-12 mm, charged well above middle with 2 linear deciduous bracteoles ±2.5 mm; sepals where not covered in praefloration both villosulous and hispid with spreading golden setae up to 1.5-2 mm, the broad outer ones ovate, abruptly acuminate 8-10 mm; petals of series Adenophyllae, the cucullus (measured along line of curvature) 12-13 mm, longer than the 4 other obovate-cuneate petals; anthers up to 4 x 1.2 mm, the connective muticous. Pod ±20 x 5.5 mm, the papery purplish, finally castaneous valves villosulous, neither setose nor glandular-setulose.

description: Foliolorum numero cum Ch. stillifera Irwin & Bameby et Ch. catiarae Irwin & Bameby congrua, foliolorum ambitu priori propior; a Ch. stillifera foliorum breviorum petiolo communi 3-5 (nec 5-15) cm et petiolo proprio 1-1.5 (nec 3-7.5) cm longis, foliolorum petiolulo 1.5-2 (nec 2.5-3.5) mm longo, foliolis ultimi paris apice acuminatis (sed haud caudatis) 2-3.5 (nec 3.5-5.5) cm longis, necnon inflorescentia pauciflora simplici brevissime pseudocorymbosa (nec racemoso-paniculata) diversa; Ch. catiarae foliolis subduplo latioribus basi valde obliquis semicordatis, inflorescentia laxe racemosa necnon petalis sepala longe superantibus a nostra primo intuitu distinguitur.

description: Slender erect shrub with fuscous defoliate branches, thinly leafy distally, resinously verruculose throughout, the excretory trichomes reduced or almost so to their swollen base and even this immersed on each face of the plane, pale green concolorous leaflets, the inflorescence a few-flowered pseudocorymbose raceme less than 2 cm long scarcely exserted from foliage. Stipules subulate-setiform ±2 mm long, deciduous. Leaf-stalks 3-5 cm, the true petiole and the interfoliolar segments of rachis subequilong (±1-1.5 cm); leaflets 3-4 pairs, accrescent upward and tilted forward, turned half face to face on petiolule 1.5-2 mm, the blades in outline lance- or narrowly ovate-acuminate (but not caudate) from slightly or scarcely inequilateral base, the margin erose, the terminal pair 20-35 x 6-10 mm, the straight centric midrib weakly prominulous dorsally and faintly 4-6-branched on each side. Pedicels 10-12 mm; bracts and bracteoles linear-elliptic 2-3 mm, caducous; flower-buds ovoid-acuminate, resinously verruculose (rare verrucae bearing a rudimentary shaft to 0.5 mm); flowers of series Glutinosae, the lanceolate acute sepals and longer petals subequilong 15-16 mm. Pod unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Irwin, Howard S. & Barneby, Rupert C. 1987. Novelties in Chamaecrista section Absus (Caesalpiniaceae). Brittonia. 39: 7-10.

description: Species haec ab A. tequilana S. Wats. stipulis apice glandulosis, pinnis 1-3-jugis et pinnarum rachide stipellis prope basin instructa differt. Frutex 1-1.5 m alta; glabra. Stipulae 5 mm longae 1.5 mm latae, apice glandulosae, glabrescentes, caducae; folia bipinnata, 9-18 cm longa, decidua; petioli 3.8-5.5 cm longi; rachides 2.8-3.4 cm longae; pinnae 1-3-jugae 5-12 cm longae, stipellis prope basem instructae; foliola 1-3-juga, (1.2) 2-3.2 (3.5) cm lata, bene lato-obovata, base asymmetrico-obliqua, apicem versus rotundata, venatione reticulata utrinsecus bene distincta praedita, glabra. Racemi axillares vel verticillato-paniculati; pedunculi 1.5- 2.5 cm longi, glabri; pedicelli 1.5-2 mm longi, glabri; flores albi, in statu sicco flavi, sub anthesi 6 mm longi; calyx usque 1 mm longus, 5-lobulatus usque minus quam 1/2 suae longitudinis; corolla calyce duplo longior, profunde 5-lobulata usque plusquam mediam suae longitudinis; ovarium brevi- stipitatum, stipite usque minus quam 1/2 longitudinis ovarii, glabrum. Legumen 4.5-5.2 cm longum, 1.8-2 cm latum, planum, rectum, secus suturas ambas dehiscens; valvae chartaceae venatione reticulata bene distincta instructae, glabrae, base rotundatae stipite usque 2 cm longo instructae, apice acutae brevi-apiculataeque; rostrum usque 4 mm longum. Pollen 8-loculatum.
bibliographicCitation: Rico-Arce, María de L. 1987. Acacia sousae (Leguminosae: Mimosoideae), a new species from Mexico. Brittonia. 39: 130-132.

description: Shrub to 1.5 m tall, glabrous. Stipules lanceolate, 5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, apex glandular, caducous; leaves bipinnate, 9-18 cm long, deciduous; petiole 3.8- 5.5 cm long, terete; rachis 2.8-3.4 cm long, with 1-3 pairs of pinna; pinnae 5-12 cm long, their stipels linear, 1.5 mm long; leaflets 1-3 pairs per pinna, (2) 3-4.5 cm long, (1.2) 2-3.2 (3.5) cm wide, broadly obovate-oblique at base, rounded at apex, conspicuously pinnate-reticulate-veined on both surfaces, glabrous. Racemes axillary, simple or verticillate-paniculate, rachis 23 cm long; peduncles 1.5- 2.5 cm long, glabrous; floral bract clavate, 0.75 mm long, glabrous, early caducous; pedicels 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous; flowers white, yellow when dry, 6 mm long at anthesis; calyx ca 1 mm long, 5-lobed, the lobes less than 1/4 the length of the calyx; corolla 2.4 mm long, 5-lobed to more than halfway; stamens more than 300, free at base; ovary short-stipitate, the stipe shorter than the ovary, glabrous. Legume 4.5-5.2 cm long, 1.8-2 cm wide, flat, straight, dehiscent along both sutures; valves chartaceous, conspicuously reticulate, glabrous, rounded at the base; stipe to 2 cm long, acute and shortly apiculate at the apex; beak up to 4 mm long. Seeds 4-7 per fruit. Pollen grains in polyads of 8.
bibliographicCitation: Rico-Arce, María de L. 1987. Acacia sousae (Leguminosae: Mimosoideae), a new species from Mexico. Brittonia. 39: 130-132.

description: C. polystachyae Benth. forsan proxime affinis sed ab ea ramulis hornotinis pilosulis, foliis sub- sessilibus, foliolis 5-6 (nec 2-4)-jugis infra medium valde obliquis, antherisque totis (nec tantum secus suturas parce) puberulis optime diversa, a C. aiarana Irwin, sola sectionis Apoucouitae quoad folia subsessilia comparabili, foliorum numero, ambitu ac magnitudine, pulvinulisque abbreviatis multo distantius abstans.
bibliographicCitation: Irwin, Howard S. & Barneby, Rupert C. 1977. Monographic studies in Cassia (Leguminosae: Caesalpinioideae). IV. Supplementary notes on section Apoucouita Bentham. Brittonia. 29: 277-290.

description: Trees to 10 m, the trunk up to 2 dm diam, the young branchlets, leaf-stalks and axes of inflorescence pilosulous with loosely incurved or spreading sordid hairs to 0.2 (few to 0.4) mm, the foliage bicolored, the stiffly chartaceous leaflets lustrously brownish-olivaceous above, paler dull beneath, toward base minutely ciliolate but otherwise glabrous. Stipules not seen, either truly obsolete or early caducous. Leaves subsessile, the petiole proper only as long as the petiolar gland; pulvinus slightly swollen 4-6 mm, shallowly wrinkled; gland interposed between pulvinus and first pair of leaflets scutellate or shallowly dish-shaped, sessile in the petiolar groove, oblong-elliptic +/- 2-2.5 mm diam, sometimes a smaller gland at distal pair of leaflets; leaf-rachis 6-10.5 cm, openly grooved ventrally, the herbaceous margins of each seg- ment slightly dilated upward; leaflets 5-6 pairs, ascending from rachis face upward on discolored puberulent pulvinule +/- 2 mm, slightly accrescent distally, in outline obliquely oblong-elliptic or the smaller proximal ones obliquely ovate, all obtuse- subemarginate, (2.7) 3-7 X (1.5) 2-3 cm, at base on narrower proximal side of mid- rib cordately contracted into pulvinule, on broader distal side cuneate, the abaxial margin ? abruptly angulate below middle of blade, the slightly arcuate midrib pro- minulous dorsally, subimmersed ventrally, the 10-14 pairs of slender major second- ary venules and subsequent reticulation prominulous on both faces, a trifle more sharply so above. Racemes 1 or 2 from shortly above scars of leaves lately fallen, the axis 1-1.5 cm, charged with sessile scutellate glands + 0.6-1 mm diam; pedicels +/- 13-17 mm, bracteolate near middle; sepals oblong-obovate, the longer ones +/- 6- 6.5 X 4 mm, densely ciliolate; petals yellow glabrous, 4 obovate to broadly oblance- olate beyond the narrow claw, 15-19 X 8-9 mm, the cucullus about as long but obliquely reniform; anthers subsessile in outline lance-truncate, 4-angular, 4-4.5 mm, pilosulous all over; ovary and style thinly pilosulous. Pod and seed unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Irwin, Howard S. & Barneby, Rupert C. 1977. Monographic studies in Cassia (Leguminosae: Caesalpinioideae). IV. Supplementary notes on section Apoucouita Bentham. Brittonia. 29: 277-290.

description:
Inter affines sect. Apoucouitae statura fruticosa humili, stipulis evolutis setiformibus (1.5-8 mm), glandulis petiolaribus elevatim stipitatis, foliolis subsessilibus, pedicellisque fructiferis valde elongatis (4.5-5.5 cm) praestans; a C. ensiformi formis fruticosis stipitato-glandulosis praesertim stipulis, pulvinulis abbreviatis, sepalis magnis (5.5-8.5 mm), pedicellisque elongatis certe divers

Erect shrubs 2-3 m with slender brown, longitudinally ridged, densely lenticellate trunks, the hornotinous leafy branchlets and axes of inflorescence minutely pilosu- lous with fine erect hairs ? 0.1-0.3 mm, the olivaceous sublustrous foliage glabrous except for sparse puberulence along midrib and sometimes minutely ciliolate margin of leaflets, the short racemes cauliflorous from annotinous branches. Stipules erect firm subulate-setiform 1.5-6 (-8) mm, the blades involute, dorsally puberulent, in age pallescent, tardily deciduous. Leaves 8-17 cm, petioled; pulvinus ovoid 2-3 mm, wrinkled when dry; petiole 1.3-3 cm, at middle 0.7-1 mm diam, like the rachis openly shallowly canaliculate ventrally, the wings of each segment scarcely dilated upward; glands between each pair of leaflets, shallowly urceolate 0.6-1 mm diam stipitate, in profile truncate-claviform or slenderly trumpet-shaped, 1-2.5 mm long; leaflets 3-5, commonly 4 pairs, widely ascending from rachis, face upward, on wrinkled pulvinule 0.4-1 mm, accrescent distally, subsymmetrically ovate or ovate- elliptic, obscurely acuminate but at very apex obtuse, 1.5-6.5 X 0.8-2.8 cm, at slightly oblique base shallowly cordate on both sides, the rounded basal angles embracing the pulvinus and produced backward to the rachis, the margins subrevolute, the slender centric midrib immersed above, prominulous beneath, giving rise to 6-10 pairs of major incurved-ascending secondary venules, these and the subsequent reticulate venulation prominulous on both faces, more sharply so beneath. Racemes 1-3 together, sessile or pedunculate, 4 5-10-flowered, the axis 4 5-20 mm charged with drum-shaped nectarial glands; bracts ovate 1-1.5 mm, persistent; fertile pedicels at anthesis (1.5) 2-5.5 cm, in fruit thickened and mostly 4.5-5.5 cm, bracteolate 7-24 mm below calyx; sepals oblong or triangular-oblong obtuse 5.5-8.5 x 3-3.3 mm; petals yellow, externally puberulent on claws and veins of blade, the 3 adaxial broadly obovate-cuneate of nearly equal size, 15-19 X 10.5-13.5 mm, the 2 abaxial somewhat dissimilar, 1 resembling the adaxial but a trifle longer, 16-20 X 12-13, the cucullus suborbicular-cuneate and shorter, 15-19.5 X 13-16 mm; anthers subsessile subhomomorphic, densely pilosulous 5-5.5 mm; ovary pilosulous; style +/- 7 mm, thinly pilosulous to the stigma; ovules +/- 10. Pod narrowly oblanceolate 13-16 X 1.5-17 cm, the lustrously castaneous subligneous venulose valves persistently pilosu- lous along sutures, elsewhere glabrescent; seeds (few seen) +/- 6.5 X 5 mm, the lustrous castaneous testa obscurely minutely punctulate.

description: Foliolis subsessilibus basi utrinque cordatis C. scleroxylon simulans sed petiolo subtereti, pedi- cellis elongatis (1-2 nec 0.5-1 cm), necnon floribus majusculis (petalis majoribus 16-21 nec < 10 mm) cum ovario pilosulo (nec glaberrimo) certe diversa, a C. ensiformi praecipue foliolis basi cordatis distinguenda. Typus sub var. eitenorum indicatur.

description: Shrubs and small trees 3-7 m, the trunk (of var. eitenorum) up to 54 cm circumference, except for the yellowish-pilosulous leafbuds and inflorescence glabrous or the young branchlets minutely puberulent, the old wood brown or gray, lenticellate, the hornotinous branchlets purplish-brown lustrous, the ample thin-textured reticulate foliage either subconcolorous or brighter green beneath than above, sublustrous  when dry, the inflorescence borne on leafless branchlets of second or third year. Stipules not seen, either obsolete or caducous. Leaves 8-22 cm, slender-petioled; pulvinus ovoid livid 2-5 mm, wrinkled when dry; petiole (1.4) 1.7-4 mm, at middle 0.7-1.4 mm diam, terete or almost so but the segments (not dilated upward) shallowly canaliculate; gland between first or each pair of leaflets, variable as to var., de- scribed below; rachis (0) 1.5-8 cm; leaflets (1) 2-4 pairs, widely spreading-ascending, face upward from leaf-stalk, on wrinkled pulvinule 1-3.5 mm, appearing sessile or subsessile, the distal somewhat larger, in outline ovate, ovate-elliptic, or obovate, obtuse or obscurely short-acuminate but always rounded at very apex, (3) 4-9.5 x (1.5) 2-5 cm, at base subsymmetrically cordate on both sides, the descending obtuse angles produced backward around pulvinule nearly or quite to level of leaf-rachis, the plane margins obscurely undulate, the straight centric midrib immersed above, sharply elevated beneath, giving rise to +/- 7-11 pairs of major secondary veins, these and the subsequent reticulate venulation finely prominulous on both faces, the ulti- mate areoles mostly + or slightly less than 1 mm diam. Racemes 1-3, serially supra- axillary from old wood, sessile, +/- 5-20-flowered, the axis up to +/- 1-2 cm, charged with urceolate subsessile or drum-shaped glands 0.4-0.9 mm diam; bracts triangular- subulate 0.5-1.2 mm; pedicels at anthesis up to 1-2 cm, the fertile ones later thick- ened and up to 3 cm, bracteolate near or below middle, the bracteoles resembling bracts, slightly smaller; petals yellow, obovate beyond claw, 3 adaxial subhomo- morphic 15-20 x 8-14 mm, the 2 abaxial heteromorphic, one longest, symmetrically or falcately oblanceolate +/- 20-21 x 9-10 mm, the other broadly obovate-suborbicu- lar +/- 15-17 x 10-13 mm; anthers (3) 4-4.5 x + (1) 1.4 mm, thinly woolly-puberu- lent; ovary and style densely gray-strigulose; ovules +/- 10. Pod and seed unknown.

description: Cassia scleroxylon is readily separated from other Amazonian apoucouitas with pubescent androecium by the syndrome of fluted trunk, openly sulcate leafstalk, shortly stipitate glands, subsessile leaflets of thin texture brunnescent when dried, and small, short-pedicelled flowers; but from the preceding only by the pedicels, flower-size, and pubescent anthers. The pod of the one collection (Silva & Souza 2557, NY) received since 1967 is 10-13 X 1.1-1.3 cm, thus scarcely narrower, as supposed by Ducke, than that of C. apoucouita. Found on terra firme along the middle and lower Tapajos and Xingu' rivers in west-central Para, where readily dis- tinguished from the sympatric C. xinguensis by the fewer (mostly 4, not 6-10) pairs of leaflets and the intra (not infra)-foliolar position of the petiolar gland.

description:
Amply leafy shrubs of rounded outline 1-2.5 m, with blackish trunks, smooth atropurpureous hornotinous branchlets clothed in stiffly chartaceous foliage, except for the strigulose ovary glabrous, or the young leaves minutely fugaciously puberulent, the penniveined leaflets bicolored, lustrous above, paler and dull beneath.

Stipules erect linear-subulate 2.5-4.5 mm, fugacious, lacking from mature leaves. Leaves ascending 5-13 cm; petiole with pulvinus 5-14 mm, the latter 2-5.5 mm slightly inflated, wrinkled when dry, the petiole proper, like each segment of the leaf-stalk, openly sulcate ventrally, the sulcus gradually dilated upward; glands -between or immediately contiguous to each pair of pulvinules sessile or subsessile, round or broadly elliptic in outline (1.3) 1.6-3 mm diam, disci- or shallowly patelli- form, coarsely blunt-margined; leaflets (1) 2-3 pairs ascending from rachis face upward on dilated, when dry wrinkled, sulcate pulvinules 2-4.5 mm, accrescent distally, in outline subsymmetrically obovate to broadly oblanceolate obtuse, minutely or widely emarginate (1.5) 2.5-8 X (1-) 1.2-3 (3.8) cm, at base subequally rounded to broadly cuneate, the margin revolute, the straight midrib from base finely penniveined, with (5) 6-9 (10) pairs of widely ascending camptodromous secondary veins prominulous on both faces but more sharply so beneath, a fainter tertiary reticulation raised beneath.

Racemes short-pedunculate from upper leaf-axils, loosely 3-9-flowered, the peduncle and axis together 3-8 cm; bracts minute caducous, accompanied on one or other side (alternately) by a small deciduous claviform-stipitate gland; pedicels widely ascending 2.5-3.5 cm; sepals subpetaloid membranous-margined, all obovate obtuse but very unequal in size, 1 dorsal and 1 ventral exterior 3.5-5 mm, 3 inner larger up to 11-14 mm; petals yellow glabrous, all obovate obtuse or emarginate, narrowed at base into a slender claw + 3-5 mm, the vexillary and lateral ones plane, the 2 abaxial concave, all coarsely 3-veined from claw, the central vein arborescently branched upward; androecium 10-merous, of 3 staminodes ? 5 mm, 4 fertile stamens with short filament and thecae + 6-6.5 mm, and 3 abaxial fertile with filament + 5 mm and thecae 9-15 mm, the fertile thecae all contracted at apex into a biporose beak 0.7-1.2 mm; ovary strigulose; style + 1 cm, incurved and slightly dilated at tip; ovules 18-25.

Pod linear straight, strongly compressed, including short stipe and setiform beak 7.5-11.5 x 0.9-1.1 cm, the ripe valves nigrescent papery, tardily and inertly dehiscent along ventral suture; seeds oblong compressed 4.8-5.3 mm, the testa dull castaneous bearing on either face a paler, slightly depressed, oblong pleurogram + 2.5 x 0.5-0.6 mm.

description:
C. adiantifoliae Benth. foliolis numerosis parvulis basi angulatim expansis soli comparandae af- finis, sed phyllotaxi spirali (nec disticha), foliis manifeste petiolatis (petiolo cum pulvino 9-13 nec 3-6 mm longo), glandula petiolari stipitata, foliolis minus numerosis (15-19 nec 20-35-jugis) inter se secus rhachin distantius (5-7 nec 3-5 mm) separatis, patriaque procul aliena diversa.

Trees up to 8 m, with trunks 12 cm diam, the pliant purplish-brown, densely len- ticellate young branchlets, the ventral edge of leaf-stalks and the lower face of leaf- lets all minutely, sometimes very sparsely puberulous with incumbent or appressed hairs, the short cauliflorous inflorescence minutely but rather densely pilosulous, the thin-textured leaflets faintly discolorous, drying brown both sides but slightly paler beneath. Stipules vestigial or obsolete, not over 0.2 mm, when present caducous. Leaves 8-12.5 cm, the expanded blade oblong-elliptic in outline; pulvinus ovoid, 2- 2.5 mm, wrinkled when dry; petiole with pulvinus 7-13 mm, at middle 0.5-0.6 mm diam, narrowly wing-margined, the ventral face either openly canaliculate or nar- rowly sulcate; gland 1 near middle of petiole proper (2-5 mm below proximal pair of leaflets), shallowly urceolate and coarsely short-stipitate, 0.7-1.5 mm diam, in profile turbinate or obconic and 0.6-1.1 mm tall, usually a trifle shorter than diam of head, similar smaller and sometimes more slenderly stipitate glands between the second and some distal pairs; leaflets (10) 13-19 pairs, ascending from rachis at points +/- 5-7 mm apart, the lower- and uppermost smallest, in outline obliquely ob- long, obtuse or openly emarginate, (9) 11-18 x 4-6 mm, at oblique base cordate proximally, cuneate distally, immediately above base on distal side of oblique costa angulately dilated, the entire margins plane, the slender midrib immersed above, prominulous beneath, giving rise to 5-8 pairs of fine immersed secondary veinlets. Racemes solitary sessile on leafless annotinous branchlets, densely 5-15-fld, the eglandular axis 3-10 mm; bracts minute caducous; pedicels 13-15 mm, bracteolate near middle, the minute bracteoles persistent; sepals ovate 2-2.5 x 1.2-1.7 mm, pilosulous externally, the whole calyx when expanded +/- 7 mm diam; petals yellow, little known, but the longest apparently only +/- 10 mm, all puberulent dorsally on claw and middle of blade; anthers subsessile 3.5-4 mm pilosulous; ovary strigulose; ovules 13-16. Pod exactly linear or slightly widened distally, the stiffly coriaceous, sublustrously atrocastaneous valves obscurely venulose-rugulose, puberulent (especially along sutures) or glabrate; funicles broader than long; seeds (not seen fully ripe) +/- 5.5 mm, plumply compressed-ovoid, nearly smooth

description: Suffrutex, 30-40 cm altus; ramulis sparse puberulis vel glabrescentibus, raro tomentosis. Folia composita, petiolata; petiolo (2.5-)4-8 cm longo, tomentoso, ad vel supra medium ((1.5-)2-4 cm supra basim) cum glandula minima (diametro 0.05-0.1 cm) instructo; rachi (5-)10-15 cm longa, infra 1-3 paribus distalibus pinnarum glandulis instructa; pinnis (4-) 5-9-jugatis, alternis vel suboppositis, (3-)5-9 cm longis; foliolis 7-15-jugatis (in pinnis proximalibus tantum 4-jugatis), alternis, breviter petiolulatis, (0.3-)0.7-1.2 cm longis, (0.2-)0.4-0.6 cm latis, oblongis vel ovato-oblongis, utrinque glabris supra fuscis infra pallidis, basi truncatis leviter inaequalibus, apice obtusis vel rarissime leviter emarginatis, margine leviter revolutis, basi costae haud barbatis; rachilla sparse tomentosa, infra 1 vel 3 paribus distalibus foliolorum glandulis munitis. Inflorescentia racemosa, 1 (-2) in quoque axilla; pedunculo tomentoso, 2-4.5 cm longo; rachi ad 14 cm longa, dense tomentosa. Flores vinoso-purpurei. Calyx 0.05-0.1 cm longus. Corolla glabra, 0.2-0.3 cm longa, lobis 0.1-0.15 cm longis margine ciliolatis. Stamina 0.5-0.6 cm longa. Ovarium stipitatum, glabrum. Stylus glaber. Fructus immaturus sessilis, erectus vel leviter curvatus, 8.5 cm longus, subviridis, inter semine atro-ferrugineo- pubescens, super solo plano-insidens.

description: Large spreading short-boled tree, armed with spines, leafy at anthesis; branehlets rather stout, often aculeate; petioles (3.7-)8-19(-27) cm. longto, densely pubescent with stellate hairs, at length glabrescent; petiolules 3-7 mm. long, 1-2.5 mm. in diam., pubescent as petioles; leaflet-blades chartaceous, densely pubescent with stellate hairs, soon glabreseent especially on the upper surface; terminal leaflets subdeltoid or broadly ovate-rhomboid (or subrotund), 4.5-16 cm. long, 5.5-19 cm. broad, usually emarginate or retuse (or rounded or obtuse) at apex, truncate to subcordate or occasionally obtuse at base; secondaries 5-8 per side; rachis (4-) 7-23 cm. long, densely pubescent with stellate hairs, soon glabrescent proxinmally; pedicels 0.8-1.2(-2) cm. long, 0.5-1.5 mm. in diam., pubescent as rachis; bracts ovate, usually 2.3-2.9 mmn-. long and 1.5-1.8 mm. broad; bracteoles linear-lanceolate, usually 0.7-1.2 mm. long and about 0.4 mm. broad; calyx membranaceous, spathaceous, opening laterally on one side almiost to base, the part opposite the cleft broad, conspicuously veined, wrinkled transversely, truncate, with five blunt nearly equal small spur-like teeth, the calyx usually 20-30 mm. longv and 13-20 mm. broad when stretched, pubescent as pedicels; standard orange-red, obovate or ovate or elliptic, usually strongly reflexed and inequilateral, 3-5.5 cm. long (including claw), 1.4-3 cm. broad, emarginate or retuse or rounded at apex, broadly cuneate toward base, the claw up to 6 mm. long; wings usually obliquely obovate or obliquely elliptic, often curved, involute on the vexillar side, cun ate-clawed at base, 11-17(-29) mm. long, 5-9(-11) mm. broad, longer than keel-petals; keel-petals broadly obovate or obliquely so, often involute on the vexillar side or at apex, usually shortly clawed at base, 11-17 (-20) mm. long, 6-14 mm. broad; stamens 3.8-7.1 cm. long, separate for 1.3-2.6 cm.; pistil 4.1-7.3 cm. long, the ovary and gynophore densely pubeseent with stellate hairs; fruit-pedicels 1-2.5 cm. long, 1-1.5 mm. in diam.; pods ligneous, 7.5-14 cm. long, 1.2-1.7 cm. broad, irregularly and deeply constricted between seeds, with a stipe 1.5-2 cm. long, with a stiff acumination usually 0.5-1.3 cm. long, usually 1-4-seeded; seeds red with a broad black line extending from the hilum for approximately 3 mm. toward the chalazal end, (11-)14-17 mm. long, (6-)8-11 mm. broad.

description: Medium-sized tree, occasionally aculeate, leafy at alnthesis; braneh- lets rather slender, occasionally aculeate; petioles (5.5-) 11-36 (-55) em. long, puberulent, at length glabrescent or glabrous, occasionally acule- ate; petiolules 3-11 (-17) nim. long, 1.5-3.5 (-4) mmi. in diamn., puberu- lent, at length glabreseent or glabrous, occasionally aculeate; leaflet- blades chartaceous or subcoriaceous, occasionally aculeate on principal veins above, glabrous throughout (except prinicipal veins below often minutely puberulent), not ceriferous ben-eath; terminal leaflets usually ovate to broadly ovate (or elliptic or broadly elliptic or subrotund), 8-21 (-39) cm. long, (3-) 5.5-16.5 (-38) cm. broad, usually acute to acuminate at apex, rounded to truncate or obtuse to cuneate at base; secondaries 7-12 per side; rachis 8.5-50 cm. long, densely puberulent, soonl glabreseent; pedicels 0.3-0.8 cm. long, about 0.4 mm. in diam., densely puberulent, at length glabreseent; larger bracts usually laneeo- late, up to 5.2 mm. long and 1.5 mml. broad, the smaller ones ovate or lanceolate, about 0.9 mm. long and 0.4 mm. broad; bracteoles similar to the smaller bracts, somewhat smaller; calyx thin-chartaceous, broadly campanulate, 8-11 mm. long on the carinal side, 7-10 mm. on the vexillar side, 1.5-2 mm. broad at base, ampliate to 8-10 mm. at apex, irregularly lobed at margin (2 sinuses often much deeper than others), often cal- carate on the upper carinal side, pubescent as rachis; description: Tree, 5-25 m tall, 6-15 cm dbh. Leaves 13-28 cm long; stipules persistent, leaf-like, 5 x 3 mm; rachis with dark-brown hirsute indumentum; leaflets 13-17, oblong, 1.8-7 x 1-3 cm, subcoriaceous, glabrous and lustrous above, sparsely yellow-hirsute below, the margin swollen below, the base rounded, the apex emarginate, with a mucro less than 1 mm long; midvein prominent; secondary venation craspedodromus, nearly linear and parallel; tertiary venation reticulate; petiolule 2 mm long. Inflorescence an axillary or terminal panicle, 12-35 cm long; bracts deltoid, 3-4 mm; peduncle yellowish-brown hirsute. Flowers violet, 13 mm long; pedicel 2-3 mm long; bracteoles ovate, 2 x 2 mm; calyx 5 mm, velutinous, with five obtuse teeth; banner 9 x 8 mm, velutinous to woolly on adaxial surface, and with visible nervation on the abaxial surface; keel petals 6-7 x 5-5.4 mm, sparsely velutinous above; wing petals 7-8 x 5-5.5 mm, glabrous or nearly so, with visible nervation; stamens monadelphous, 8 mm, the free part of filaments 3 mm long; style curved, 7 mm long, woolly. Fruit a one-seeded samara, 5-6 x 1.5 cm, brown-yellowish velutinous; seed acuminate, 1 cm long.

description: Very large tree, 30-40 (-50) m tall with a trunk diameter of 6-15 dm above short buttresses of about 1-3 m high; bark about 10 mm thick, reddish-brown, the outer portion separating into rather small papery scales, a cut into the living bark produces a gelatinous secretion (Bena 1960). Leaves (14-) 17-32 (-15) cm long; stipules large, reniform, about 1.0 cm long, 1.5 cm wide, caducous; leaflets (5-) 7 (-9), long-ovate or elliptic but mostly oblong with acute bases and apices, the terminal blade (6-) 8-12 (-20) cm long, (3-) 4-7 (-9) cm wide, finely puberulent above becoming essentially glabrous with age; puberulent below with golden-brown hairs, the glands dark red-brown, thinly scattered and inconspicuous, the lower epidermis finely papillate. Inflorescence (12-) 19-34 cm long, 10-27 cm wide; flower buds 8-10 mm long, 5-7 mm wide. Sepals covered externally with golden-brown pubescence. Petals white with a darker 3-4 mm long claw, the blades 10-13 mm long, 10-12 mm wide. Filament of the longer (usually upper) stamen 5-7 mm long, its anther 6-8 thecate at the midpoint, filament of the shorter (usually lower) stamen 2-3 mm long, its anther 8-10 thecate at the midpoint. Pistil containing 4-6 ovules. Fruit (5-) 6-8 cm long depending upon the number of seeds, 3-4 cm wide, the dorsal sutural wing 4-7 mm wide; seeds 15-20 mm long, 12-17 mm wide, 2-4 mm thick (Fig. 6).

description: A medium to very large tree, reported up to 37 m tall (Krukoff 8635), crown often spreading, the bark thick and rather rough. Leaves 18-40 cm long; stipules not seen; leaflets 5-13, the terminal blade (4-) 7-12 (-19) cm long, (2-) 4-6 (-10) cm wide, essentially glabrous to minutely puberulous above, puberulous to quite pubescent below, the hairs golden to chocolate-brown, the lower epidermis may or may not be very finely papillate depending upon the variety. Inflorescence (9-) 18-31 (-35) cm long, (7-) 12-25 cm wide; flower buds 7-11 mm long, 5-7 mm wide, sepals covered externally with golden, chocolate-brown, or whitish pubescence; petals white or rosy white with a (2-) 3-5 mm claw, the blades 7-13 mm long, 5--10 mm wide; filament of the longer (usually upper) stamen 6-10 mm long, its anther 4 thecate, filament of the shorter (lower) stamen 2-4 mm long, its anther (6-) 8 thecate at the mid-point; pistil containing 3-4 ovules. Fruit 4-7 cm long depending upon the number of seeds, 3.0-3.5 cm wide, the dorsal wing 4-6 mm wide.

description: Shrub or scandent liana 3-10 m tall, 5-30 cm dbh. Leaves 15-35 cm long; stipules persistent, rigid and spinescent, 7-15 x 2-7 mm; rachis sparsely silvery-pilose; leaflets 19-70, narrowly oblanceolate, 10-35 × 5-10 mm, strigose above, sparsely strigose to sericeous below, the margin repand, the base rounded or nearly oblique, the apex emarginate; mid-vein prominent; secondary venation reticulate; tertiary venation lacking; petiolule 1-1.5 mm long. Inflorescence an axillary or terminal panicle, 14-37 cm long, composed of racemose branches, these clustered into fascicles, 3-5 cm long, subtended by reflexed bracts, 7-10 mm long; peduncle silvery or yellowish-brown hirsute or strigose. Flowers violet or light blue, 10-12 mm long; pedicel 3 mm long; bracteoles suborbicular, 2 x 2 mm; calyx 5-5.5 mm, glabrous or sparsely sericeous, with five obtuse teeth; banner 8 x 7 mm, velutinous on adaxial surface; keel petals 9 x 5 mm; wing petals 11 x 6-7 mm, glabrous, not lamellate; stamens diadelphous, 8 mm long, the free part of filament 3-4 mm long; style curved, 8 mm long, hirsute. Fruit a one-seeded samara, 5-7 x 1-1.7 cm, glabrous; seed 1.5-2 cm long.

description: Trees up to 25 m. high; twigs smooth, drying dull gray-black, the bark tight, the lenticels evanescent, the leaves 5-11 cm. long; leaflets 8-10 pairs, scarcely inequilateral, drying a chocolate-brown above, impunctate, glabrous and often glaucous above, minutely pubescent beneath, narrow-oblong to ovate-oblong, 1.8-3.5 cm. long, 1.1-1.9 cm. wide, obtuse and minutely retuse at apex, obtuse to subcordate at base, the costa plane or immersed above, prominent beneath, gla- brous above, pubescent beneath, the secondary veins 8+, crassate, immersed or plane, insculptate above, prominulous beneath (often obscured by pubescence), ascending from costa at an angle of 650-700, the reticulate areas insculptate, plane or immersed above, distinctly prominulous (or obscurely so because of pubescence) beneath, the margins glabrous or minutely pubescent, plane or curl- ing on drying; inflorescence paniculate, axillary, the panicles usually exceeding the leaves in length, apparently divergent, ovate-oblong in outline, the rachises woolly and golden-pubescent or subvillose, rather slender, irregular-marcescent- striate, up to 12 cm. long, the basal lateral branches up to 4 cm. long, the branches well-spaced, densely flowered, gradually becoming shorter toward apex of rachis; sepals red-brown when dry, unequal in size and length, glabrous on outside, hirsute-hairy within, oblong, 3.5-3.8 mm. long, 1.5-2.2 mm. wide, obtuse at apex, obtuse at base, the veins not visible; stamens 10, the anthers oblong, 1-1.3 mm. long, about 0.75 mm. wide, apiculate at apex, cordate at base; ovaries smooth, light-golden-brown, the valves marginally hirsute, irregular-oblong-rotund, about 1.3 mm. long, about 1 mm. wide, the style about 2 mm. long; fruit drying red or deep red-brown, the stipe 3.5? description: Leaflets commonly to 14 cm long, chartaceous, broadly ovate, usually obtuse in general outline, with a short, acute tip but varying even on one plant from completely obtuse to somewhat acuminate; pubescence medium long, white or tan, moderately to very dense on petiolule and lower surface of blade, sparse to moderately dense above. Bracteoles 1.5 mm long, obtuse. Pedicel 2 mm long. Calyx 12 mm long; pubescence short to medium long, white or tan, sparse to moderately dense; upper lip at least as long as tube, upper edge constricted behind apieclate tip; lowest tooth 2.5 mm long, subulate, exceeding the more or less acute laterals. Standard 2.25 cm long. Pod commonly to 20 × 2.5 cm, occasionally to 25 × 3 cm, slightly compressed, spirally dehiseent, dark brown to tan; each valve with sutural ribs and an extra rib ea 6 mm from ventral rib (rare variants occur with strongly curved pods and with 2 extra ribs instead of 1, described respectively as C. campylocarpa and C. anomala by Piper). Seeds to 18 × 12 × 9 mm, oblong, moderately compressed, olive, brown, or reddish brown, sometimes with dark marbling, varying in color with age, not buoyant or impermeable; hilum usually ca 8 mm but varying from 6-11 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sauer, Jonathan D. 1964. Revision of Casaratia. Brittonia. 16: 106-181.

description: Leaflets commonly to 15 cm long, chartaceous, broadly ovate, acuminate to a short, blunt tip; pubescence medium long, white or tan, dense on petiolule, sparse to dense on lower surface of blade, sparse above. Bracteoles 1.25 mm long, obtuse. Pedicel 2 mm long. Calyx 12 mm long; pubescence medium long, tan or white, sparse to moderately dense; upper lip shorter than tube, upper edge constricted behind non-apiculate tip; lowest tooth 2 mm long, acute, equalling obtuse laterals. Standard 3 cm long. Pod commonly to 17 × 3 cm, compressed, spirally dehiscent, pale brown; each valve with sutural ribs and an extra rib ca 4 mm from ventral rib. Seeds to 20 × 12 × 10 mm, oblong-elliptic, moderately compressed, brown or reddish brown, with black marbling, sometimes buoyant but not impermeable to water; hilum ca 11 mm long.

description: Shrub armed with spines, leafy at anthesis; branchlets rather slender, aculeate; petioles 8-27 cm. long, pubescent, at length glabres- cent, aculeate; petiolules 4-13 mm. long, 0.7-2.5 mm. in diam., pubes- cent as petioles; leaflet-blades chartaceous, pubescent with long villous hairs beneath, puberulent on costa and secondaries above, at length glabreseent (hairs on costa and secondaries often persisting and form- ing a ridge); bracteoles linear, 1.5-1.7 mm. long and about 0.3 mm. broad; calyx thin-chartaceous, broadly campanulate, 9-12 (-15) mm. long on the carinal side (including spur), 8-11.5 (-13) mm. long on the vexillar side, 2-3 mm. broad at base, ampliate to 9-11.5 (-15) mm. at apex, at margin bilobed, slightly calearate on the upper carinal side (spur up to 1.5 mm. long), shortly pubeseent, soon glabreseent; standard red (ex Russel & Souviron), broadly obovate or broadly elliptic or obovate or suborbicular, 2-4.4 cm. long, 1.4-2.5 cm. broad, rounded or retuse at apex, cuneate or broadly cuneate at base; wings variously shaped, 5-11 mm. long, 2-3.5 mm. broad; description: Arbor parva ramosissima ad 4 m alta, ramis junioribus puberulis demum glabratis. Folia imparipinnata, 7-9 cm longa, (21-) 27-29 (-31) -foliolata; stipulae nullae; petioli 15-20 mm longi; rhachides puberuli vel breviter tomentosi; foliola opposita vel subopposita, oblonga vel elliptica, apice obtusa vel apiculata, basi rotundata vel cuneata, minute asymmetrica, (5-) 12-15 (-20) mm longa, (2.5-) 4-5 (-7) mm lata, subcoriacea vel membranacea, utrinque strigosa demum glabra, pinnatinervia, costa et nervis primariis subtus manifestis; petioluli ad 1 mm longi, strigosi. Racemi axillares folia aequantes; pedunculi 8-15 mm longi, puberuli, sparse glandulosi, minute striati; bracteae anguste triangulares, 0.25 mm longae, ad 0.25 mm latae, strigosae demum caducae; pedicelli 1.5-2 mm longi, similiter ac pedunculi puberuli, sparse glandulosi; bracteolae nullae; calyx 3-3.5 mm longus, extus strigosus, glandulo- sus, intus pilosus vel strigosus, eglandulosus, tubo 1.9-2.1 mm longo, dentibus 1.1-1.2 mm longis; petala obovata vel oblonga, unguiculata, 3 mm longa, 1-1.2 mm lata, ungue 1-1.5 mm longo, extus secus axin glanduloso-pilosa, intus glabra; stamina 5-6 mm longa, valde exserta; antherae 0.75 mm longae, 0.5 mm latae, glabrae; ovarium 3 mm longum, stigma versus sericeum demum glabrum. description: Loosely tufted caulescent herbs from stout vertical taproot, the simple stems 5-15 cm, arising from shallowly buried root-crown, glabrous and leafless at base, each bearing ±5-10 leaves and usually 2 peduncles beyond middle, distally like leaf-stalks, dorsal face of leaflets, and peduncles thinly strigose with fine straight basifixed hairs less than 1 mm, the short racemes thinly villosulous. Stipules heteromorphic, those at lowest, leafless nodes connate into a membranous amplexicaul sheath up to 5 mm long, the distal ones almost fully amplexicaul but free opposite the petiole, the erect, lance- or ovate-acuminate blades 5-11 x 1.5- 5 mm, thinly herbaceous but membranous-margined, finely green-veined. Leaves 5-10 cm, the petiole ±2 cm; leaflets 19-27, elliptic or elliptic-obovate, shallowly emarginate, 7-16 x 2-4.5 mm, glabrous ventrally. Peduncles 4.5-7.5 cm, incurved-ascending at anthesis, humistrate in fruit; racemes shortly loosely 10-16- flowered, the axis becoming 1-2 cm; bracts lanceolate obtuse 6-10 x 1-2 mm, in texture resembling stipules, persistent; pedicels 2-2.5 mm; calyx 9-10.5 mm, the short-cylindric, membranous tube 7-8.5 x 3-3.5 mm, purplish on adaxial side, thinly pilosulous, in fruit circumscissile deciduous, the subulate subequal teeth separated by obtuse sinuses, the dorsal tooth +2 mm; petals purple with pale claw, the elliptic emarginate banner ?17-18 mm, near middle recurved through ±40º; wings scarcely shorter, the claw ±7-7.5 mm, the erect, narrowly oblanceolate, shallowly emarginate blade 10 x 3.5 mm; keel 13-14 mm, the claws ±8 mm, the half-elliptic blades incurved through nearly 90º to rounded apex; ovary glabrous; ovules 26-28. Pod sessile, firmly attached to receptacle, the inflated body varying from globose to broadly plumply oblong-ellipsoid 14-26 x 12-16 mm, a little obcompressed, at broadly rounded apex apiculate by an erect conic beak 1-1.5 mm, the sutures either shallowly depressed or bluntly prominulous, the valves differentiated into a double envelope separated by an airspace 1.5-2 mm wide, externally pale green but reddish on side exposed to sun, the exocarp of fully formed but unripe pod 0.4-1 mm thick, and the endocarp not over 0.35 mm thick, both becoming when dry stiffly chartaceous, the endocarp inflexed as a complete septum; cavity of the pod empty except for seeds, lacking pulpy filaments; seed-funicles adnate through ±1 mm to wall of septum; seeds (2.4) 2.6-3.5 mm diam, the testa dull black.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. & Bridges, Edwin L. 1987. A new species of Astragalus (Fabaceae) from Tennessee's Central Basin. Brittonia. 39: 358-363.

description: Leaflets commonly to 16 cm long, chartaceous, ovate, acuminate to a medium long, acute tip; pubescence medium long, white, sparse on petiolule and lower surface of blade; upper surface glabrate. Bracteoles 2 mm long, obtuse. Pedicel 2 mm long. Calyx 20 mm long; pubescence long, white, moderately dense; upper lip equalling or longer than tube, upper edge smoothly concave, not apiculate; lower teeth borne on a conmmon jaw-like base 1 mm long; lowest tooth 3 mm long, acute, exceeding acute laterals. Standard 2.5 cm long. Pod commonly to 28 × 4 cm, compressed, spirally dehiseent, dark brown; each valve with a rib along both sutures, the vental rib flattened and up to 10 mm wide. Seeds to 28 × 19 × 6 mm, convex along hilum, flattened below, strongly compressed, dark brown, not buoyant or impermeable; hilum about 30 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sauer, Jonathan D. 1964. Revision of Casaratia. Brittonia. 16: 106-181.

description: Arbor parva vel frutex 2-5 m alta, ramis armatis et tomentosis; pinnae (6) 8-11 (14)-jugae; foliola (10) 15-20 (23)-juga, prominule pinnato-venulosa. Flores pentameri diplostemonei, tomentulosi, in spicis (2.5) 4-6 (7) cm longis dispositi. Leguminis valvulae exarticulatae, tomentulosae et resinosopunctulatae, replo aculeato. Affinis ut videtur M. aculeaticarpae Ortega, sed floribus spicatis ab omnibus speciebus a Britton & Rose generi Mimosospidi relatis diversa.
bibliographicCitation: Grether, Rosaura & Barneby, Rupert C. 1987. Mimosa nanchititlana, a new species from the state of México, Mexico (Mimosaceae). Brittonia. 39: 345-347.

description: Small tree or shrub 2-5 m, the young branches ribbed, densely tomentose, when older striate and tomentose, armed with pairs of straight infrastipular aculei 6-10 mm and with scattered recurved intemodal ones. Stipules linear to subulate, ovate, or spatulate (3) 4-7 (10) mm, tomentose mainly at base and margins. Petioles ribbed, tomentose, unarmed 5-10 (13) cm, and primary leaf-rachis either sparsely aculeate or unarmed, (4) 5-9 (13) cm; pinnae (6) 8-11 (14) pairs, the rachis (1.5) 2-5 (6) cm; leaflets (10) 15-20 (23) pairs, obliquely linear-oblong to lanceolate and subfalcate, acute or mucronate, (3) 4-7.5 (9) x (0.5) 1-1.5 (2) mm, glabrous on both faces, strongly ciliate, the midrib moderately displaced, pinnately branched. Flowers spicate, the spikes axillary, solitary or 2-3 per node, the peduncle (1) 2-3 (3.5) cm, the floral axis (2.5) 4-6 (7) cm; bracts linear-lanceolate or spatulate-oblanceolate 0.5-1 mm, equaling or shorter than the calyx, 1/4-1/3 as long as corolla; calyx campanulate, short-toothed 0.7-1.3 mm, 1/3-1/2 as long as corolla, tomentulose overall and often resinous-punctate marginally; corolla 5-lobed, 2-2.6 mm, the lobes 1/4-1/2 as long as whole, pink, tomentulose at least beyond middle; stamens 10, free to base, 5.5-6 mm; pistil 6.5-7.5 mm, the stipitate ovary 0.5 mm, pubescent, the style 6-7 mm, the stigma poriform. Pod sessile, in profile narrowly oblong 20-40 x 5-7 mm, straight or slightly curved, 3-7-seeded, not constricted between seeds, the valves tomentose and resinous-punctate, nonarticulate, the replum either armed with recurved aculei or unarmed. Seeds ovoid or obliquely rhomboid, 4-4.5 x 3 x 1.4-1.6 mm, the pleurogram ±1/4 as long as seed.
bibliographicCitation: Grether, Rosaura & Barneby, Rupert C. 1987. Mimosa nanchititlana, a new species from the state of México, Mexico (Mimosaceae). Brittonia. 39: 345-347.

description: A P. peruviana (J. F. Macbr.) Barneby, quoad habitum scandentem aculeatum, foliola tenui-pa- pyracea majuscula necnon flosculorum petala erecta extus sericeo-strigulosa comparabili, foliolis simulduplo magis numerosis (15-17-, nec 4-7 (9)-jugis usque) ac dimidio minoribus, iis mediam rachin versus sitis oblique oblongis 1 1-24 x 4-14 mm (nec ovato-oblongis 30-60 x 15-28 mm usque) primo intuitu diversa.

description: Pinnarum et foliolorum numero et amplitudine necnon petalis erectis et filamentis brevissime monadelphis cum P. killipii J. F. Macbr. et P. cuzcoënsi Bameby (ambabus peruvianis andinis) comparanda, ab iis foliolis intricatim reticulato-nervulosis (nec 1-costatis) diversissima.

description: Either scandent and prickly or arborescent and (distally) unarmed shrubs and treelets attaining 8 m, pilosulous throughout with cream-colored hairs up to 0.2 mm, the young stems, leaf-axes and inflorescence densely so but sometimes gla- brate at maturity, the stems and leaf-stalks either smooth or armed with scattered broad-based brown-tipped, straight or recurved aculei 1-2.5 mm, the plane, pale green leaflets a trifle paler beneath, the inflorescence an axillary or terminal efoliate pseudoraceme of flexuously amentiform spikes exserted 1 dm or more from fo- liage. Stipules erect linear-subulate 2-4.5 x 0.3-0.5 mm, becoming dry fragile. Leaf-stalks 10-15 cm, the petiole including pulvinus 20-25 x 1 mm, the inter- pinnal segments 11-19 mm; an elliptic depressed crumpled nectary 1.7-3.5 mm in long diam near middle of grooved petiole, sometimes a smaller one on first interpinnal segment of rachis, and nearly always yet smaller ones on each pinna at or immediately below 2-4 distal leaflet-pairs; pinnae (5) 7-9-jugate, accrescent distally, the rachis of longer ones 5-7.5 cm, the interfoliolar intervals 3.5-5 mm, sulcate lengthwise on each side of a ventral ridge; leaflets of longer pinnae 14- 17-jugate, a little decrescent proximally, the inner member of first pair commonly reduced to a minute deciduous paraphyllidium, the blade of the rest oblong or narrowly ovate-oblong from asymmetrically rounded base, shallowly emarginate at broadly rounded apex and mucronulate by excurrent midrib, those at and beyond mid-rachis 8.5-12 x 3-5 mm, 2.4-2.8 times as long as wide, all delicately venulose on both faces, the subcentric midrib giving rise on each side to 3-6 major secondary venules camptodrome well within the blade's margin, a tertiary reticulum subequally prominulous on both faces. Axis of flower-spikes including short peduncle 4-7 cm; peduncular bracts caducous non-cupuliform; floral bracts linear-oblanceolate 0.6-1 mm, caducous; flowers 5-merous 10-androus; calyx campanulate 1-1.4 x 0.8-1.2 mm, thinly puberulent externally, the depressed- deltate teeth 0.1-0.2 mm; petals erect oblanceolate 2.5-2.8 x 0.5 mm, at early anthesis united nearly to middle, the greenish blades thinly finely strigulose ex- ternally; filaments monadelphous through ±0.4 mm, exserted 2-2.6 mm; stipe of ovary 0.8-1.2 mm, the body thinly pilosulous beyond middle, the glabrous style 1.6-2.5 mm. Pod (of Beck 8600, not fully ripe) pendulous, broad-linear plano-compressed ±15-20 x 1.5-1.7 cm, cuneately contracted at base into a puberulent stipe 10-15 mm, obtuse at apex, the almost straight sutures 0.7-0.9 mm wide, the plane, stiffly papery, early glabrate valves brown or purplish-brown, becoming openly reticulate-venulose, the dehiscence and seeds not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1986. A contribution to the taxonomy of Piptadenia (Mimosaceae) in South America. Brittonia. 38: 222-229.

description: Ut videtur P. killipii arcte affinis, sed pube minuta e villis subappressis 0.1-0.2 mm (nec patula e villis laxis 0.4-0.5 mm) longis constanti, flosculis brevioribus ±1.7 (nec 2.3-3) mm longis griseopuberulis (nec praeter calycis orem glaberrimis), necnon filamentis brevissime (per 0.2-0.3 mm, nec in vaginam camosulam 0.7-0.9 mm altam) monadelphis certe diversa.

description: Scandent shrubs attaining 6 (-?) m, densely armed on blunt angles of stem and along both dorsal and lateral ribs of leaf-stalks with stout broad-based brown- tipped recurved aculei 1-2.5 mm, and finely pilosulous almost throughout with sordid spreading-ascending hairs up to 0.1-0.2 mm, the bicolored foliage only thinly pubescent, the leaflets dark-olivaceous above, paler beneath, the narrow interrupted flower-spikes collected into axillary few-branched efoliate panicles up to 1 dm. Stipules caducous from short spur, not seen. Leaf-stalks 13-16 cm, the petiole ±30 x 1.2 mm, the interpinnal segments 8-15 mm; no petiolar nectary seen, but small doliiform ones ±0.5 mm diam between several pinna-pairs and yet smaller tub-shaped ones between 1-3 distal pairs of leaflets; pinnae 10-11 - jugate, the usually unarmed, rarely remotely aculeolate axis of longer distal ones 5-6.5 cm, the interfoliolar segments 2-2.5 mm; leaflets of longer pinnae 20-24- jugate, subdecrescent at each end of rachis, the first pair arising less than 1 mm distant from slender discolored pulvinus, the blades oblong from obliquely ob- tusangulate base, toward apex a little curved forward and at very apex acutely triangular and apiculate, those at mid-rachis 7.5-9 x 2-2.3 mm, 3.8-4 times as long as wide, the slightly displaced midrib immersed above, prominulous beneath, other venulation imperceptible. Flower-spikes fasciculate by 2-5, the flexuous axis including short peduncle 4.5-7.5 cm; peduncular bracts alternate, caducous; floral bracts 0.3-0.5 mm, deciduous; flowers 5-merous 10-androus; calyx campanulate 0.9 x 0.9 mm, externally densely appressed-puberulent, the low-deltate teeth 0.2 mm; petals permanently erect, oblanceolate 1.7 x 0.5 mm, apparently greenish- white or yellowish, early free to base, beyond calyx-tube densely gray-puberulent dorsally; filaments monadelphous through 0.2-0.3 mm, exserted 1 mm; anthers 0.3 x 0.15 mm, the caducous gland nearly 0.1 mm diam; ovary densely pilosulous, elevated on a glabrous stipe nearly 1 mm, the glabrous style ± 1 mm. Pod unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1986. A contribution to the taxonomy of Piptadenia (Mimosaceae) in South America. Brittonia. 38: 222-229.

description: P. floribundae Kleinhoonte notulis plurimis congruae certe affinis, sed his absimilis: foliorum nectaria obtuse conica (nec claviformia); pinnae foliorum fere omnium 4 (nec exacte 2)-jugae; foliola obovata emarginata 20-33 x 9-22 (nec obovato-acuminata 50-60 x 25-38) mm usque, dorso pube aurea (nec pallida) conspersa.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1986. A contribution to the taxonomy of Piptadenia (Mimosaceae) in South America. Brittonia. 38: 222-229.

description: Stout liana attaining 30 m, armed on obtusely ribbed, dark brown stems and on leaf-stalks with broad-based, recurved aculei 2-3.5 mm, the young growth densely pilosulous with fine tawny-golden hairs 0.1-0.3 mm, the foliage notably bicolored, the stiffly chartaceous leaflets smooth leaden-gray and only sparsely puberulent above, beneath prominently venose and tawny-pilosulous, the inflo- rescence a small, terminal or subterminal, efoliate panicle of narrow amentiform spikes. Stipules subulate 2-2.5 mm, very early caducous from an elevated scar ±0.2-0.4 mm diam. Leaf-stalks 8-12.5 cm, the petiole 30-50 x 1.5-2 mm, the interpinnal segments ±1-3 cm; below mid-petiole 1, or often 2-3 contiguous, even confluent, mounded or bottle-shaped, small-pored, bony nectaries up to 2- 3 mm diam at base and 1- 1.5 mm tall, and similar but smaller ones both on leaf- stalk below each pinna-pair and on pinna-rachises immediately below each pair of leaflets; pinnae 3 (4)-jugate, the rachis often recurved, that of longer distal pinnae 3-4 cm, the longer interfoliolar segments 8-13 mm; leaflets of distal pinnae 4-5-jugate, a little decrescent proximally, the blades obovate or oblong-obovate from rounded or broadly cuneate, subequilateral base, shallowly emarginate api- cally and bluntly apiculate by the excurrent midrib, the longest 20-33 x 9-22 mm, the straight centric midrib pinnately 6-9-branched on each side, the as- cending secondary nerves camptodrome just within the blade's revolute margin and giving rise to an open tertiary reticulum of finer veinlets. Flower-spikes in- cluding short peduncle 3-5 cm, without filaments 4 mm diam, the thick rachis, calyces, and petals all densely tawny-tomentellous overall; an enlarged bract (but no involucre) at base of first flower, the interfloral bracts 0.5-0.9 mm; flowers sessile, 5-merous 10-androus, all bisexual; calyx shallowly campanulate 0.6-0.7 × 1 mm, the depressed-deltate teeth 0.2 mm; petals free at full anthesis, narrowly lanceolate 1.7-1.9 x 0.5 mm, greenish-brown; filaments pallid, united below base of sessile pilosulous ovary into an obconical stemonozone ±0.6 mm, scarcely longer than corolla; anthers yellowish, ±0.3 mm long, the apical gland scarcely 0.1 mm diam. Pod not seen ripe, when first formed broad-linear plano-compressed, up to 12 x 2 cm, the straight sutures ±0.5 mm wide, densely tomentellous, the papery, rich-brown valves less densely tomentellous with suberect yellowish hairs mixed with sessile yellowish or reddish glands ±0.15 mm diam; dehiscence of pod unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1986. A contribution to the taxonomy of Piptadenia (Mimosaceae) in South America. Brittonia. 38: 222-229.

description: Leaflets commonly to 12 cm long, slightly coriaceous, ovate-elliptic, obtuse in general outline but with a short, subacute tip; pubescence long, white, moderately dense on petiolule, sparse on both surfaces of blade. Bracteoles 1 mm long, acute. Pedicel 2 mm long. Calyx 12 mm long; pubescence short, white, sparse; upper lip much shorter than tube, upper edge abruptly constricted behind apiculate tip; lowest tooth 2 mm long, subulate, exceeding acute laterals. Standard 2.5 cm long. Pod commonly to 14 × 4 cm, inflated, indehiseent or tardily dehiseent, tan; each valve with sutural ribs and an extra rib ea 3 mm from ventral rib. Seeds to 20 × 14 × 10 mm, oblong, dark reddish brown, buoyant but quickly permeable to water; hilum ca 13 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sauer, Jonathan D. 1964. Revision of Casaratia. Brittonia. 16: 106-181.

description: Meristems auxotelic, RGUs monomorphic; inflorescences metameric, the axis persistent; leaves developmentally sup- pressed, especially on axillary shoots, but never totally suppressed, every partial inflorescence at one time or another subtended by a leaf; axillary branch-buds proleptic.
bibliographicCitation: Grimes, J. 1992. Metamerism, heterochrony, and inflorescence morphology of the Pithecellobium-complex (Leguminosae: Mimosoideae: Ingeae). Brittonia. 44: 140-159.

description: Stem up to 1.5 m., much branched or nearly simple, glabrouls (uncommonly sparsely villous). Stipules narrowly lanceolate, mostly soon deciduous. Leaves numerous, scattered over entire length of stem and into the lower portion of inflorescence. Terminal leaflet ovate-lanceolate to nearly rhomboid, usually broadest below the middle, 2-2.5 times as long as broad, rarely somewhat wider, acute or somewhat acuminate at apex, basally cuneate or rounded. Lateral leaflets smaller than terminal one, commonly oblique. Blades most commonly thick and somewhat coriaceous, occasionally thin (mainly on plants bearing large, broad leaves-shade forms?), much lighter below than above, glabrous below or with a few scattered villous hairs along nerves, glabrous above except for a line of hooked hairs along mid-nerve and occasional trichomes over entire surface. Inflorescence usually much branched and compound, commonly basally leafy; rachis pubescent with fine uncinate hairs. Calyx glabrous or sparsely puberulent. Corolla and androecium as in Desmodium podocarpum; petals ca. 3 mm., subequal (wings slightly the longest); standard concave-cuneate towards claw; wings and keel not spurred. 3 mm. or rarely more), barely exceeding stamen column. Loments 2-3 jointed; isthmuses short. Segments 5-6 mm. long, 3-4 mm. wide, similar in shape to those of Desmodium podocarpum, except that the ventral margin is frequently more strongly developed.
bibliographicCitation: Isely, Duane. 1951. Desmodium: section Pododcarpium Benth. Brittonia. 7: 185-224.

description: Large tree armed with spines, aphyllous or with young leaves at anthesis; branchlets rather stout, aculeate; petioles 6.7-33 cm. long, tomentose, soon glabreseent, spineless or aculeate; petiolules 5-14 mm. long, 1-3 mm. in diam., pubeseent as petioles; leaflet-blades chartaceous, sparsely tomentose, soon glabreseent, the hairs on costa and secondaries often persisting and forming a ridge; terminal leaflet subrotund (often broader than lonig) or rhombic-ovate or broadly ovate, 7-24 cm. long, 6.5-25 cm. broad, acute to rounded at apex, truneate or rounded or subcordate at base; costa occasionally aculeate, the secondaries 6-10 per side; rachis 6-38 cm. long, pubescent with spreading rufous deciduous hairs; pedicels 1.5-4 cm. long, 0.4-1.5 mm. in diam., pubescent as rachis, soon glabreseent; bracts ovate, up to 1.4 mm. long and 0.7 mm. broad; bracteoles not seen; calyx chartaceous, broadly campanulate, asym- metric, 6-10 mm. long on the carinal side, 6-10 mm. long on the vexillar side, about 1 mm. broad at base, ampliate to 8-14 mm. at apex, the calyx being greatly stretched transversely just before anthesis, entire or nearly so at margin, callose arid often calearate on the upper carinal side (spur up to 0.7 mm. long), thickened toward base, pubescent as rachis, soon glabreseent; standard red (ex Ducke and Glaziou), broadly elliptic, 3.1-4.7 cm. long (ineluding claw), 2.2-2.9 cm. broad, obtuse or rounded at apex and at base, the claw up to 3 mm. long; wings oblong or oblong-ovate, 6-14 mm. long, 3.1-6 mm. broad; keel-petals broadly falcate, 30-42 mm. long, 7-11 mm. broad; stamens 3.7-4.9 cm. long, separate for 0.8-1.3 cm.; pistil 3.2-5.1 cm. long, the ovary densely pubescent with rather stiff spreading hairs, the gynophore sparsely so distally and glabrous proximally; fruits and seeds not seen, presumably resembling those of E. flammea.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. 1939. The American species of Erythrina. Brittonia. 3: 205-337.

description: Foliola ovata, acuminata, supra parce subtus densius pilosa. Bracteolae 1 mm longae. Calyx 12 mm longus, labio superiori apiculato, quam tubus multo breviori margine superiori leviter coneavo, dente infimo 1.5 mm longo, acuto, dentibus lateralibus obtusis, paulo brevioribus quam dens infimus. Legumen usque 15 cm longum, 1.5 cm latum, dehiseens, sulco inter costas ea 5 mm lato. Semina fusea, elliptica, compressa, usque ad 9 mm longa, hilo 7 mm longo.
bibliographicCitation: Sauer, Jonathan D. 1964. Revision of Casaratia. Brittonia. 16: 106-181.

description: Leaflets commonly to 11 cm long, chartaceous to slightly coriaceous, ovate, acuminate to a medium long, obtuse tip; pubescence medium long, white to tan, moderately to very dense on petiolule, sparse to dense on lower surface of blade, sparse above. Bracteoles 1 mm long, obtuse. Pedicel 1 mm long. Calyx 12 mm long; pubescence short, white, sparse; upper lip much shorter than tube, upper edge slightly concave behind apiculate tip; lowest tooth 1.5 mm long, acute, exceeding obtuse laterals. Standard 3.25 cm long. Pod commonly to 15 × 1.5 cm, compressed, spirally dehiscent, brown, with sparse to dense white pubescence; each valve with sutural ribs and an extra rib ca 5 mm from ventral rib. Seeds to 9 × 7 × 4 mm, elliptic, strongly compressed, brown, speckled with black, not buoyant or impermeable; hilum ea 7 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sauer, Jonathan D. 1964. Revision of Casaratia. Brittonia. 16: 106-181.
