description: Shrub or small tree, armed with spines, aphyllous or with young leaves at anthesis; branchlets rather stout, aculeate; petioles 5-15 (-26) cm. long, densely pubescent with long villous hairs, at length glabres- cent or glabrous, usually aculeate; petiolules 2-7 mm. long, 0.4- 1.5 (-2.5) mm. in diam., pubescent as petioles; leaflet-blades chartace- ous, pubescent when young, soon glabrous above, sparsely pubescent or glabreseent beneath, usually spineless, not ceriferous beneath; terminal leaflets deltoid or semiorbicular-deltoid, usually broader than lonig, 2.7-8.5 (-11.5) cm. long, 3.1-9 (-13) cnm. broad, obtuse to acute (rarely rounded) at apex, truneate or nearly so at base; secondaries 5-8 per side; rachis 6-23 cm. long, densely pubeseent with long villous rufous hairs, at length glabreseent proximally; pedicels 0.3-0.5 cm. long, about 0.7 mm. in diam., pubescent as rachis; larger bracts up to 5.2 mm. long and 1.6 mm. broad, the smaller ones usually ovate, about 1.3 mm. long and 0.6 mm. broad; bracteoles similar to the smaller bracts, somewhat smaller; calyx chartaceous, campanulate, 8.5-16 mm. long on the carinal side, 8-15 mm. long on the vexillar side, 1.5-2.5 im. broad at base, ampliate to 4.5-7 mm. at apex, at margin regularly 5-denticulate (tooth on the upper carinal side larger than others), pubescent as rachis; standard red, sparsely pubescent without, narrowly elliptic, 3.2-6.8 cm. long, 0.7-1.3 cm. broad, acute to rounded at apex, cuneate or cuneate-clawed at base; wings usually subcucullate at apex, usually sagittate or hastate on one side and toothed on the oppo- site side, clawed at base, longer or shorter than keel-petals, 7-12.5 mm. long, 3-4 mm. broad; keel-petals shortly apiculate or acuminate dor- sally at apex, sagittate or hastate, clawed at base, 6.5-11.5 mm. long, 3.5-5 mm. broad; stamens 2.8-5.8 cm. long, separate for 0.9-1.9 cm.; pistil 3.1-6 cm. long, the ovary and gynophore densely pubescent with brownish or rufous rather spreading hairs; fruit-pedicels 0.5-0.8 cm. long, 2-3 mm. in diam.; pods ligneous, 12-24 cm. long, 1.4-2 cm. broad, constricted between seeds (not moniliform), with a stipe 2-7 cm. long, with an acumination 2.5-6.5 cm. long, 1-many-seeded; description: Trailing or occasionally twining plants with elongated, robust stems, more or less densely hirsute or appressed-sericeous, the vesture white or tawny. Leaves pinnately trifoliolate, the hirsute or strigose petioles 2-11 cm long and rachis 2-12 mm long. Leaflets stipellate, broadly elliptic to rhombic, ovate or obovate, the terminal one 26-58 mm long, 17-33 mm wide, acute or obtuse and mucronate, obtuse or truncate at the base, more or less densely appressed-sericeous beneath and strigose or hirsute above. Leaflet venation prominently pinnate. Stipules lanceolate, 2-5.5 mm long. Racemes slender, 5-23 cm long, loosely 4-18-flow- ered. Pedicels 0.5-3 mm long. Bracts subulate-acicular, 1.5-5 mm long, exceed- ing the pedicels. Bractlets acicular, 1-3.5 mm long. Calyx 4-7 mm long, hirsute or silky-strigose, the vesture white or white and tawny, the calyx teeth lanceolate, setaceous, narrowly attenuate at the apex, the lower ones 2-4 mm long, equal to or more usually longer than the calyx tube, the upper pair united for about 2/3 total calyx length. Corolla pale to mid lavender or purple, the standard 7-10 mm long, wings 7-9 mm long, these exceeding the keel which is 5-7 mm long. Pod stout, linear, 10-29 mm long, 3-5.5 mm wide, 2.5-5 mm broad across suture, 2- 6-seeded, densely villous, hirsute, or occasionally strigose, the vesture white or tawny. Seeds 2.5-3.8 x 2-3 mm, rounded, oblong to ovoid, dark brown to black, muricate, the seed perisperm alveolate and tuberculate.

description: This quaint little astragalus, type and only species of Astragalus sect. Koelziana Sirj., is figured from the isotype, collected in the Bakhtiari country in west-central Iran (TYPE: Koelz 15115, now US!, not BPI as stated in the protologue). Its principal peculiarity is the reduction of the leaves to an amply dilated terminal blade. This is, however, sometimes accompanied by a pair of rudimentary, or at least very much smaller, lateral leaflets forming with it a sort of trefoil. Astragalus sect. Koelziana was acknowledged to have the flower of sect. Stereothrix Bunge, but was thought to differ not only in the modified foliage but in free stipules and small, thin- textured, subunilocular pods. We now have these last two features together in A. ledinghamii, with normally pinnate foliage, a combination that seriously weakens the claim of sect. Koelziana, at least as originally formulated, to its assigned rank. Astragalus sect. Stereothrix, together with the allied sect. Bornmuelleriana of southern Iran, is related to sect. Malacothrix Bunge and forms the climax of a series of in- creasingly xerophytic modifications traceable back to a primitive, mesophytic or cryophytic astragalus of a type resembling A. danicus Retz (of A. subgen. Hypglottis Bunge). In this series A. ledinghamii and A. koelzii clearly occupy terminal positions, highly specialized in their conelike inflorescences of tiny (probably autogamous) flowers, simplified foliage, and few-seeded pods dispersed on the plumose, pappus-like parachute of the disjointing calyx. The whole inflorescence and the dispersal of the propagule are curiously similar to those of some Mexican species of Dalea L. in- habiting an interior desert plateau at similar latitudes. The simplified leaf of A. koelzii has, of course, many well-known parallels, not only in distantly interrelated groups of Astragalus (e.g. A. bucharicus Regel, A. candolleanus Boiss., A. asclepi- adoides M. E. Jones, A. calycosus var. monophyllidius (Rydb.) Barneby), but in other genera and tribes of faboid and mimosoid legumes. Vassil'cenko, in his essay on neoteny (1965, cf. especially Figs. 12, 15, 16, 18), quotes many examples and attributes the phenomenon to selection by adverse environment.

description: Plants biennial or short-lived perennials, branching primarily from the base, 12-18 cm tall. description: Stems simple or somewhat branched, 0.4-0.8 m. high, sparsely pubescent with short spreading hairs and longer appressed trichomes. description: Plants to 1 m. in height (?). Stem sparingly hairy with upwardly appressed trichomes about 1 mm. in length and minute, incurved hairs. Stipules lanceolate-deltoid, strongly striate, up to 7 mm. in length and 3 mm. in breadth at base. Leaves subclustered, much exceeded by the inflorescence. Leaflets with incurved lateral nerves, subcoriaceous, only slightly lighter below than above, sparingly hairy or glabrate. Terminal leaflet usually considerably exceeding lateral blades, lanceolate, commonly 7-10 cm. long, apically acute, tapering to base. Lateral leaflets one-half to nearly as long as terminal one, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, markedly oblique at base. Blade pubescence mainly limited to a line of fine, incurved hairs on midrib, sometimes including also minute trichomes scattered over upper surface. Inflorescence simple or slightly branched, apparently usually terminal. Rachis sparingly pubescent with fine incurved hairs, appearing nearly glabrous. Calyx ca. 1.5 mm. in length. Petals about 4.5 mm. long, subequal. Standard broadly obtuse at base; wings and keel closely associated; wings oblong, spurred; keel narrowly obovate, not spurred. Fruiting pedicels ca. 6 mm. long, slender. Stalk approximating or slightly ex- ceeding stamen tube, 2-4 mm. in length. Loment 2-3 jointed, the segments about 4 mm. wide and 6-7 mm. long, commonly with a conspicuous ventral-anterior hook.

description:
Stem apparently nearly simple below inflorescence, up to 1.4 m. in height, sparsely hooked-hairy below, becoming closely pubescent above. Stipules lanceolate, to 8 mm. in length and 1.5 mm. in width at base, striate, pubescent with villous hairs. Leaves scattered, pinnately 7-foliolate, 15-30 cm. long including petiole. Petiole frequently exceeding 10 cm. in length, pubescent with fine hooked hairs and scattered longer villous ones; rachis likewise hairy. Leaflets up to (or sometimes exceeding) 15 cm. in length and 6 cm. in width, narrowly rhomboid-elliptic to ovate-lanceolate, subequal in size or the terminal one and uppermost laterals somewhat the largest; terminal leaflet longer stalked than lateral ones. Leaflet surface somewhat lustrous above, slightly lighter beneath, frequently appearing nearly glabrous, but with very small hairs over entire surface, sometimes with larger hooked hairs above (particularly along nerves), and long, stiff, appressed trichomes below, occasionally possessing villous pubescence along midvein.

Inflorescence simple or branched, terminal, or terminal and axillary from upper- most blades. Rachis densely hooked-hairy. Calyx ca. 3 mm. in length; terminal lobes distinci and dorsal teeth less com- pletely fused than in other species. Petals 7-9 mm. long. Standard obovate, cuneate-narrowed to base without a distinct claw. Wings oblong, truncate or with a slight hastate lobe at base, hyaline-bordered along ventral margin, apparently not hooked about keel as in other species. Keel petals elliptic, hyaline-bordered ventrally towards the tip. Fruiting pedicels 9-12 mm., stalk 10-15 mm., stamen tube ca. 5 mm. in length. Loment mostly 2-segmented, possessing a conspicuous stylar beak (about 5 mm. in length) on terminal joint. Segments 10-14 mm. in length, 5-7 mm. wide, straight or convex along posterior margin, concave anterior-ventrally.

description:
Stems 0.5 to 1.2 m., simple or branched above, closely hairy with villous pubescence and minute hooked hairs. Stipules narrowly lanceolate, 1-2 mm. in length, mostly soon deciduous. Leaves scattered over entire length of stem, or somewhat aggregated, all long petioled, or uppermost reduced, short petioled and continuing into inflorescence. Terminal leaflet obovate to broadly rhomboid or ovate, averaging 1.1-1.2 times longer than wide, broadest at or slightly above middle, obtusely-acuminate or sometimes rounded-truncate or emarginate at apex, cuneate at base. Lateral leaflets similar, somewhat smaller and narrower, usually unequal at base. Primary lateral veins of blades continuing to margin. Leaflet sur- face slightly lighter below than above, strongly reticulate, hairy on both surfaces. Pubescence predominately strigose above and spreading below, mostly lost in age. Pubescence on petioles similar to that on stem.

Inflorescence simple or iruch branched, less leafy than that of D. oxyphyllum. Calyx 1.5-2 mnm. in length, sparsely villous. Petals 3-3.5 mm. long. Standard cuneate-tapering to the basal claw. Wing and keel petals not spurred, the former oblong, slightly longer than the standard, the latter ovate, slightly shorter. Fruiting pedicel 3.4 mm., stalk 2.5-4 mm. (rarely longer), and stamen column 1-1.5 mm. long. Loment 2-3 segmented; isthmuses short. Joints ca. 5 mm. in length and 3.5-4 mm. high, greatest width 1/2-2/3 distance towards anterior end; posterior and anterior margins curving into one another more or less evenly, a ventral portion scarcely differentiated.

description: Plants to 1 m. or more (?). Stem simple or apically branched, usually pubescent, with lax, villous hairs. Stipules filiform-lanceolate, up to 10 mm. in length and 1 mm. in basal width, hairy, commonly quickly deciduous. Leaves mostly closely clustered, or approximate near base of stem, usually with 2-several smaller blades scattered above, less commonly scattered over entire length of stem; even wlhen leaves are scattered an aggregation of nodes on the basal portion of stem is usually to be found. Leaflets ovate to ovate-lanceolate, broadest below middle, usually pubescent on both surfaces but considerably lighter below than above; lateral nerves terminating in margin. Terminal leaflet subequal to, or considerably exceeding lateral ones, acuminate-tipped, cuneate-tapered at base. Lateral blades acuminate to acute, cuneate or rounded at base, usually somewhat oblique. Pubescence on upper leaflet surface of stiff appressed trichomes ca. 0.6 mm. in length, these hairs rather closely covering entire surface on young blades; lower blade surface finely velvety with minute, spreading trichomes. Inflorescence terminal, simple or branched, usually much exceeding leaves. Rachis glutinous-pubescent with hooked hairs. Flowers essentially similar to those in D. podocarpum, perhaps averaging slightly larger. Loment slender-pediceled and stalked; pedicel 5-6 mm., stalk 4.5-6.5 mm. and stamen column 1.5-2 mm. in length. Loment generally 2-segmented, isthmus somewhat drawn-out; joints 6-8 mm. in length and 4 mm. wide, concave on anterior margin, slightly concave on posterior, anterior-ventral angle evenly rounded or anteriorly drawn out into a hook.
bibliographicCitation: Isely, Duane. 1951. Desmodium: section Pododcarpium Benth. Brittonia. 7: 185-224.

description:
Stems 0.5-0.7 m. high, commonly basally branched, frequently somewhat dif- ferentiated into leaf-bearing and flowering shoots, the latter laterally placed and nearly naked. Pubescence of fine glutinous hairs. Stipules deltoid-lanceolate, to 10 mm. in length and 4 mm. wide. Leaves mostly approximate, considerably ex- ceeded by inflorescence. Petioles 3-9 cm. long, sparsely hairy with pubescence similar to that on stems. Leaflets mostly 1.7-2 times as long as wide, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, basally rounded and apically acuminate. Lateral blades oblique and from one-half to nearly as long as terminal ones. Principal secondary nerves not extending to margin; secondary reticulum well developed. Blades almost equally green on both surfaces; pubescence below of fine, appressed or spreading hairs following vein-reticulum or scattered over interspaces as well; indument on upper surface of mature leaves consisting primarily of short recurved hairs along the midnerve and principal laterals, on young blades consisting also of a sparse covering of long (1 mm. or more) stiff, appressed trichomes which are soon deciduous.

Inflorescence terminal on leafy stem or axillary- from basal shoots, usually considerably exceeding leaves, simple or branched, glutinous-hairy.

Calyx ca. 2 mm. high. Petals 5-6 mm. long. Standard abruptly narrowed to stalk. Keel and wing petals basally spurred, closely associated, the wings longitudinally hooked over opposing margins of the keel.

Fruiting pedicels 13-20 mm. long, capillary; stalk 10-18 mm. in length, stamen tube reaching 4-6 mm. Loment 2-4 jointed, the segments about 9 mm. in length and 4 mm. high, joined by a very narrow, rather extended isthemis; ventral and proxi- mal margins more or less continuous with one another, concave; ventral-anterior angle commonly drawn out into a prominent hook, the anterior margin thus con- cave and backwardly directed.
bibliographicCitation: Isely, Duane. 1951. Desmodium: section Pododcarpium Benth. Brittonia. 7: 185-224.

description: Folia unifoliolata, petiolata; foliolum cordiforme, apice rotundum et abrupte breviacumi- natum, mucronae ad 1-2 mm, apiculatum, basi late cordatum, margine subrevolutum; petiolo 4.5-6 cm; petiolulus 4-6 mm; inflorescentiae contractae, uni- seu biflores, flores albi, ca 3.5 cm; bracteolae 4-8 mm; calycis tubus 9-10 mm longus lobis tubo subaequilongis.
bibliographicCitation: Fantz, Paul R. 1979. A new section of Clitoria subgenus Neurocarpum (Leguminosae) and a new species endemic to Thailand. Brittonia. 31: 115-118.

description: Suffrutescent herb, scandent. Stems terete, angular, longitudinally striate, 1-2 mm diam, hollow, pubescence on juvenile portions uncinate and strigose, be- coming sparse; internodes 2-5 cm. Leaves 1-foliolate, thick-membraneous, long- petiolate; leaflet broadly ovate to nearly orbicular, cordiform, 7.5-10 cm long, 7-10 cm wide, apex rotund and abruptly short-acuminate, mucronate, acumen 1-2 mm, base broad, cordate, margin weakly revolute, midrib impressed above, primary nerves 10-12 pairs, upper surface of lamina green, glabrous, lower surface pale green, pubescence sparse, densest along nerves, macrotrichomes appressed (observe 1OX) overlying uncinate-microtrichomes (observe 30X). Petioles weakly quadrangular, longitudinally striate and canaliculate, 4.5-6 cm, sparsely pubescent; petiolules subquadrate, rugose, 4-6 mm, conspicuously pubescent. Stipules per- sistent, oblong-lanceolate, acute, striate on both surfaces, 5-8 (10) mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, sparsely pubescent; stipels similar, linear, 6.5-8 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm wide. Inflorescences axillary, racemose, contracted, conspicuously shorter than the petiole, 0.4-0.6 cm long, (1) 2-flowered; pedicels 4-5 mm. Bracts arranged in four series, sparsely pubescent, lanceolate, acute to broadly acuminate, 3.5-4.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide. Flowers all chasmogamous, white, ca 3.5 cm long. Bracteoles persistent, oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, 7-8 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, inserted to 0.5 mm below calyx, pubescence pilose toward apex with uncinate- microtrichomes scattered over the entire surface. Calyx pubescence dense, con- spicuous (10-20x), trichomes uncinate beneath appressed macrotrichomes, the tube 10-nerved, a nerve extending to each sinus which forks with two branch veins into each adjacent lobe and a nerve extending from the base into each lobe medially to apex; tube 9-10 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide at the base expanding to 4.5-5.5 mm wide at the throat, lobes broadly lanceolate, long-acuminate, 9-10 mm long, subequalling the tube, ca 2.5 mm wide near the base. Vexillum pubescence of uncinate-microtrichomes beneath scattered, appressed macrotrichomes, blade ca 2 cm wide. Alae extended beyond carina by 6 mm, blade oblong-spatulate, broad- ening beyond the carina, 14 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, claw 10 mm long. Carina falcate, blade 10 mm long, 3.5 mm wide, claw 12 mm long. Staminal tube 17 mm, incurved near apex, free filaments 1.5-3 mm long; anthers 1 mm long, 0.8 mm wide. Gynophore 2.5 mm, pubescence dense, trichomes uncinate; style 12 mm long, geniculate 4 mm below apex, pubescence hispid-bearded with inconspicuous uncinate-microtrichomes; stigma dilated, compressed, ca 1 mm diam, basally pubescent. Legume unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Fantz, Paul R. 1979. A new section of Clitoria subgenus Neurocarpum (Leguminosae) and a new species endemic to Thailand. Brittonia. 31: 115-118.

description: Folia trifoliolata, brevipetiolata, subtus secus nervos trichomatibus subappressis elongatis (1.5-2.5 mm longis) pubescentia. Stipulae magnae, conspicuae, reflexae. Inflorescentia subsessilis, floribus ad apicem aggregatis. Bracteolae et bracteae magnae, elongatae. Calyx pubescens trichomatibus albis elongatis (2-3 mm longis) hirtus; lobi 10-15 mm longi, conspicue reticulato-venosi in siccitate. Flores albi. Legumen brevistipitatum, costatum, uncinato-pubescens.
bibliographicCitation: Fantz, Paul R. 1980. A new species of Clitoria subgenus Neurocarpum section Neurocarpum [C. irwinii] (Leguminosae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 32: 376-379.

description: Subshrub 25-75 cm tall. Stems erect, unbranched or occasionally bearing a few branches from near the base, lignose, 4-7 mm thick, compressed-quadrangular becoming terete with longitudinal striations; juvenile stems pubescent with conspicuous, dense, white, shaggy trichomes 1-2.5 mm long which are subappressed, becoming spreading to reflexed, then dropping to expose a layer of dense, uncinate trichomes (vidi 30x), these, in turn, deciduous such that older stems are glabrous. Xylopodia subterranean, lignose, 3-5 cm long, 6-12 mm thick, knobby at the apex from which arise 1-2 aerial stems. Leaves 3-foliolate; leaflets thick-membranaceous to subcoriaceous, subsessile, oblong to elliptic-oblong to ovate-oblong, 5.5-11 cm long, 2.5-5 (-6) cm wide, apex obtuse sometimes retuse, mucronate, base rotund to weakly cordate, midrib on upper surface weakly raised, primary nerves 8-11 pairs, upper surface dark green, dull, glabrous, lower surface green with a pubescence of scattered, subappressed to spreading, 1.5-2.5 mm long trichomes located primarily along the nerves. Petioles nearly quadrangular, 0.5-1.3 cm long, pubescent with uncinate trichomes (30x) beneath and scattered, spreading to reflexed, shaggy trichomes; rachis 0.6-1.6 cm; peti- olules quadrangular, 2-4 mm. Stipules large, conspicuous, 20-30-nerved, oblong to ovate-oblong, 10-15 mm long, 4-7 mm wide, acute, ascending becoming soon reflexed; stipels linear, acute, 1-5-nerved, sparsely pubescent, the lateral ones 8- 12 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, the terminal 4-8 mm long, 0.2-0.8 mm wide. Inflo- rescence axillary, solitary, subsessile, the 4-8 flowers crowded at the apex of peduncle; axes pubescent, more or less purplish; peduncle 2-5 mm long, bearing chasmogamous or cleistogamous flowers; pedicels 4-6 mm. Chasmogamous flowers showy, resupinate, 5-6 cm long, white with purplish veins. Bracts crowded, lanceolate, acute, 9-12 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, pubescent with long shaggy trichomes. Bracteoles elongate, oblong, tapering rapidly near apex to acute tip, base broadly cuneate to rotund, 19-21 mm long, 4-6 (-7) mm wide, inserted ca 1 mm below the calyx, pubescent with long shaggy trichomes. Calyx pubescent with long (2-3 mm), white, shaggy trichomes; tube 10-nerved, 17-18 mm long, 5-6 mm wide at the base expanding to 8-10 mm wide at the throat; lobes ovate- oblong, 10-15 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, acuminate with acumen of 4-5 mm, basically 3-nerved with reticulate veins highly conspicuous and prominent in the dried state. Vexillum glabrate or sparsely uncinate-pubescent on the outer sur- face, blade 3.5-4 cm wide, claw ca 9 mm long with decurrent blade. Alae longer than carina by 8-11 mm, blade falcate, 21-24 mm long, 6-8 mm wide, claw 17- 20 mm. Carina falcate, acute, 11-15 mm long, 5 mm wide, claw 25-26 mm. Staminal tube 33-35 mm long, vexillary stamen coherent near base, free filaments 3-6 mm; anthers lanceolate, 1.5 mm long, 0.5 mm wide. Gynophore 4-5 mm, densely uncinate-pubescent; ovary costate, 9 mm long, 1 mm wide, densely uncinate-pubescent; style 29-30 mm, bearded, geniculate 9 mm; stigma capitate, ca. 0.5 mm diam. Cleistogamousflowers minute, inconspicuous, crowded in axils. Bracts 3-5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide. Bracteoles lanceolate, acute, 4-7 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide. Calyx short-pilose; tube 4-7 mm long, 2-3 mm wide at the throat; lobes lanceolate, acute, 3-4 mm long, 1.5 mm wide. Petals absent. Staminal tube ca. 0.5 mm long, free filaments 2-3 mm; anthers elliptic, 0.6 mm long, 0.4 mm wide. Gynoecium not observed (all developed into fruits). Legume short- stipitate, the stipe 5-6 mm, the valves green becoming brown, costate, turgid, 2.5-4 cm long, 7-9 mm wide, uncinate-pubescent, valves with slightly thickened sutures; costa imperfectly formed, raised ca 0.5 mm above the surface of the valve, extending from the distal end to one-half to three-fourths the length of the valve, becoming impressed into the surface toward the base; dehiscence causing the valves to twist from one-quarter to one-half of a turn. Seeds not observed, ca 1-4 per pod.
bibliographicCitation: Fantz, Paul R. 1980. A new species of Clitoria subgenus Neurocarpum section Neurocarpum [C. irwinii] (Leguminosae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 32: 376-379.

description: Leaflets to 9 cm long; pubescence long, tan, sparse on petiolule and lower surface of blade; upper surface glabrate. Bracteoles and pedicels not seen. Calyx 11 mm long; pubescence short, white, sparse; upper lip nearly as long as tube, upper edge constricted behind non-apiculate tip; lowest tooth 1.5 mm long, obtuse, equalling obtuse laterals. Standard 3 cm long. Pod to 6 × 3.5 cm, compressed, spirally dehiseent, dark brown; each valve with sutural ribs and an extra rib ea 6 mm from ventral rib. The single seed (pods rarely 2-seeded, according to Moore) to 24 × 17 × 7 mm, oblong-elliptic, strongly compressed, reddish brown, not buoyant; hilum ca 20 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sauer, Jonathan D. 1964. Revision of Casaratia. Brittonia. 16: 106-181.

description: Sectionis Dalbergiae, D. glaucescenti (Mart. ex Benth.) Benth. affinis, sed ab ea floribus luteis parvis, calycibus glabratis vel pilis paucis dispersis instructis, staminibus 9 subaeque diadelphis 6 et 4, rarius monadelphis, ovario glabro margine ciliato differt. Arbor excelsa. Stipulae cuneatae, caducae. Foliola 11 ad 13, rarius 15, oblonga vel oblongo- elliptica, basi obtusa, apice obtusa vel rotundata, saepe emarginata. Inflorescentia axillaris, paniculata. Bracteae parvae, late ovatae, villosae, caducae. Bracteolae bracteis similes, persistentes. Flores parvi, ca. 5 mm longi. Stamina 9, subaeque diadelpha 6 et 4, rarius monadelpha. Ovarium longe stipitatum, praeter marginem glabrum, margine ciliato, ovula 3(-4) includens. Legumen 4.7-7.8 cm longum, 1.4- 1.7 cm latum, oblongum vel oblongo-ellipticum, in medio stipitatum, glabrum, mono-vel dispermum.
bibliographicCitation: Carvalho, A. M. de. 1997. A synopsis of the genus Dalbergia (Fabaceae: Dalbergieae) in Brazil. Brittonia. 49: 87-109.

description: Tree up to 20 m; trunk straight, the bark peeling in flakes; young stems grayish brown, striate with lenticels; young stems, petioles, and leaf-rachises densely pilose; rachis of inflorescence villose with rust-colored hairs. Stipules ca. 2-2.5 mm long, broadly cuneate, densely pilose, early caducous. Leaves 8.5-13.5 cm long (including a petiole of 0.6-1.1 cm), 11-15-foliol- ate; leaflets 1-4.2 X 0.6-1.5 cm, oblong to oblong-elliptical, rarely oblong-ovate (the terminal leaflet usually obovate), with rounded to obtuse base and an obtuse, rounded or shallowly emarginate apex, the upper surface pilose on young leaves, becoming sparsely so at maturity, the lower surface densely pilose becoming pilose with small, appressed golden-yellow hairs. Inflorescence 3-7 cm long, paniculate, axillary, usually the small flowers congested; peduncle 0.2-0.6 cm; bracts ca. 0.5 mm, broadly ovate, villose, caducous; bracteoles almost as long as bracts, sparsely villose, sometimes with a few long hairs, persistent at the base of the calyx. Calyx 2-2.5 mm long, with a few scattered hairs; upper 2 teeth deltate, broader than the others and fused for 1/3 of their length; the 3 lower teeth cuneate, the lower middle one slightly longer, ca. 0.7 mm. Corolla pale yellow, fragrant; standard ca. 4.8 mm long (including a claw of 1.6 mm), the blade orbicular with an at- tenuate base and emarginate apex; wings ca. 4.4 mm, their blades oblong-obovate, with a slightly auriculate base; keel petals almost as long as wings, its blades oblong, the two petals fused for ca. 1 mm at apex. Stamens 9, diadelphous (5 + 4), sometimes monadelphous, the vexillary stamen usually almost free; ovary long-stipitate, glabrous except for a few long hairs on the margins and the stipe; ovules 3-4. Fruit 4.7-7.8 X 1.4-1.7 cm, oblong to oblong-elliptical, obtuse short-mucronate at apex, attenuate at base, medially stipitate; stipe ca. 4-5 mm long, membranaceous, glabrous except for a few scattered hairs; the reticulate venation slightly more prominent over the seed cavity; seeds 1-2.
bibliographicCitation: Carvalho, A. M. de. 1997. A synopsis of the genus Dalbergia (Fabaceae: Dalbergieae) in Brazil. Brittonia. 49: 87-109.

description: Sectionis Ecastaphylli, speciebus D. riedelii (Benth.) Sandwith, D. negrensi Radlk., et D. guttembergii A. M. de Carvalho affinis, sed ab omnibus stipulis magnis ca. 1.5 cm longis, apice acuminatis, bracteis bracteolisque item magnis differt. Frutex scandens. Ramuli novelli sinuati, tomentosi, nigrescentes. Stipulae ovatae, ca. 1.5 cm longae, caducae, apice acuminatae. Foliola 5 ad 7, ovata vel elliptica, basi obtusa, apice apiculata, breviter mucronata. Inflorescentiae ax- illares, racemosae vel paniculatae, fasciculatae. Flores parvi, ca. 6 mm longi. Petala albida. Ovarium longe stipitatum, glabrum, ovulum solitarium includens. Legumen non visum.

description: Scandent shrub or vine with twining branches; bark smooth, dark brown; young stems, petioles, and rachises of leaves villose with rusty hairs, becoming sparsely pilose; mature stems glabrous; rachis of inflorescence tomentose with rust-colored hairs. Stipules 15 mm long, ovate, acuminate, pilose, more densely so at the base. Leaves 7.5-10 cm (including a petiole of 0.5-1 cm), 5-7-foliolate; leaflets 3.9-6.3 X 1.8-3.2 cm, ovate to elliptical with obtuse base and slightly apiculate, shortly mucronate apex, the upper surface pilose, becoming glabrous, the lower surface pilose, more densely so on young leaves, with short, soft, yellowish hairs. Inflorescence up to 3 cm, paniculate or racemose, fasciculate, axillary; peduncle ca. 2 mm, tomentose; bracts 3 mm, oblong-lanceolate, pilose, caducous; bracteoles 1.8 mm, oblong, pilose, persistent at base of the calyx. Calyx 3 mm, pilose; upper 2 teeth cuneate, broader than the others and fused for 1/3 of their length; lower 3 teeth narrowly cuneate, the middle one longest, 1 mm. Corolla whitish; standard 6 mm (including a claw of 1.6 mm), the blade broadly elliptical with an attenu- ate base and shallowly emarginate apex; wings 5.5 mm long, their blades oblong with an auriculate base, above the claw; keel 5 mm, the 2 petals obovate, fused for ca. 1 mm at apex. Stamens 10, diadelphous in two groups of 5 or triadelphous (4 + 1 + 5) with the vexillary stamen free; ovary long-stipitate, glabrous; stigma inconspicuous; ovule 1. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Carvalho, A. M. de. 1997. A synopsis of the genus Dalbergia (Fabaceae: Dalbergieae) in Brazil. Brittonia. 49: 87-109.

description: Multiple-stemmed shrub to small tree with scandent branches, becoming vine-like in some instances; young stems, petiole, and rachis of the leaves and inflorescence tomentose with rusty hairs, becoming sparsely hairy at maturity. Stipules 5 mm, lanceolate, tomentose with rust-colored hairs, becoming glabrous, caducous or rarely persistent. Leaves 2.8-9.7 cm (including a petiole of 0.4-0.8 cm), 5-7-foliolate; leaflets 1.2-6.5 X 0.5-3.8 cm, ovate to elliptical with rounded to cordate base and obtuse to acute apex, the margins slightly revolute; the upper surface pubescent, becoming glabrous at maturity but sometimes hairy along the midrib and secondary veins, the lower surface pilose, more densely so on young leaves. Inflorescence ca. 2 cm, racemose or paniculate, fasciculate, usually tightly clustered in the leaf axils; peduncle ca. 2 mm long, tomentose; bracts ca. 1.5 mm, cuneate, tomentose, caducous; bracteoles 1.5 mm, cuneate, pilose, persistent at base of the calyx. Calyx 3 mm, pilose; the 5 cuneate teeth ca. 1 mm, the 2 upper ones broader than the others. Corolla whitish; standard 6.5 mm (including a claw of 2.5 mm), the blade orbicular, attenuate at base and shallowly emarginate at apex; wings al- most as long as standard, the blades obo- vate, auriculate at base above the claw; keel 5 mm, the blades obovate, fused for 2 mm at apex. Stamens 9 or 10, triadelphous (4 + 1 + 5) or (4 + 1 + 4), or diadelphous (5 + 4); ovary long-stipitate, glabrous; stigma inconspicuous; ovules 1. Fruit 1.8-3.2 X 1.4-2.1 cm, orbiculate to oblong-orbiculate, with a rounded, shortly mucronate apex, the base rounded, shortly stipitate, the stipe ca. 3 mm, the valves thick and coriaceous at maturity, glabrous, with rugulate venation; seed 1.

description: Meristems anauxotelic, RGUs monomorphic, though with dimorphic subunits; these subunits strictly reproductive (lacking leaves), arising from sylleptic buds, the axis ephemeral; the RGUs also floriferous, the axis +/- persistent; vegetative branching from proleptic buds.

description: A Bauhinia angulosa Vogel sensu lato foliis brevioribus cordate-acuminatis glaberrimis differt. Inflorescentia floribus B. angulosae var. bahianae similis, sed floribus longioribus et calycis tubo longioris conspicue 1 5-nervio lobisque lanceolatis abstans.

description: Liana or scandent shrub. Branchlets sub cylindric, glabrescent. Stipules minute falcate, obtuse, caducous, 2 x 2 mm. Petioles glabrous or sparsely pubescent 1-1.5 cm; leaf-blades entire, 5-7-nerved, subcoriaceous, cordate-acuminate, 3.5-6.5 x 3-4 cm, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescence a panicle on short lateral branchlets, the rachis glabrescent, the partial racemes sparsely flowered; pedicels 10-13 mm long, to- mentose to pubescent; bracts and bracteoles spathulate or lanceolate, 3-5 mm long, the bracteoles similar but slightly narrower; flower buds not seen. Flower up to 25 mm long at anthesis, the calyx-tube conspicuously 1 5-ribbed, externally sparsely pubescent, 10-1 1 x 10-1 1 mm, truncate, with 5 expanded lanceolate lobes ca. 1.5-3 mm long; corolla cream colored, the 4 lower petals 18-20 x 8-10 mm, asymmetrically obovate, cuneately contracted into a biauriculate tomentose claw, the upper one shorter, conduplicate, not auriculate, all externally ferruginous-tomentose; androecium 1 0-merous, the stamens shortly exserted from the calyx-tube, the filaments unequal up to 8 mm, the anthers ovate, 1.5 mm; gynoecium to 9 mm, the ovary sessile, densely ferruginous-tomentose, 5-ovulate, 4 mm long, the style glabrous. Fruit not seen.

description: Leaflets commonly to 14 cm long, chartaceous, broadly ovate, acuminate to a long, acute tip; pubescence medium long, white or tan, sparse to dense on petiolule, sparse to very sparse on both surfaces of blade. description: Stem 1-1.5 m., nearly simple below, much branched above, sparsely pubescent with upwardly appressed villous hairs. Stipules filiform-lanceolate, striate, de- ciduous or persistent. Leaves very numerous, distributed over entire stem and lower portion of inflorescence. Leaflets nearly equal, or the lateral slightly the smallest, linear-lanceolate, 4-6 times longer than wide, broadest at or slightly above middle, tapering gradually to both ends, sometimes somewhat acuminate at apex; primary lateral veins terminating in blade margin. Leaflets rather thick, reticulate, slightly lighter in color beneath than above, glabrous to sparsely hairy. Pubescence primarily localized along midvein with lax, villous hairs beneath and smaller, stiff, appressed or uncinate ones above; petiole pubescence similar to that on stem. Inflorescence usually diffuse, with numerous axillary, leafy branches. Rachis with stiff, hooked, or spreading hairs, as well as minute uncinate ones. Flowers similar to those of D. oxyphyllum and podocarpum but slightly larger. Calyx 1.5-2 mm. high. Petals ca. 4 mm., standard slightly the shortest. Fruiting pedicels 4-6 mm. long, stalks 2-3 mm. in length, slightly exceeding stamen column. Loment nmostly 2-jointed, the segments strongly margined, ca. 6 mm. long and 4-5 mm. wide; dorsal margin markedly convex, posterior edge oblique to nearly vertical; ventral portion usually distinct, convex; anterior margin nearly straight, vertical.

description: Shrub or small tree 1-4 m tall. Stems brittle, mostly 4-6 mm diam, with welldeveloped pith. Leaflets ovate to somewhat elliptic-oval, densely gray to tawny-tomentose with prominent veins, especially beneath; stipules 8-15 mm long; middle leaflet similar to but somewhat larger than the laterals, 2-12 cm long, 1-5 cm wide. Inflorescence an axillary or terminal raceme 5-15 cm long. Flowers reportedly "lemon-yellow," usually arising 3 at a node from the base of 3, relatively conspicuous, broadly ovate bracts; pedicels as long as or somewhat longer than the subtending bracts. Calyx 12-15 mm long, densely pubescent, the lobes acute, 2-5 mm long, upper two somewhat longer and fused so as to appear cleft. Banner broadly cordate, ca 25 mm long, 20 mm wide, notched at the apex, the claw ca 5 mm long. Wings very similar to the keel and about as long, blade 14-16 mm long, the claw ca 7 mm long. Stamens 10, 16-20 mm long. Ovary densely tawny-tomentose. Fruit a flattened, 2-7-seeded, puberulent, stipitate pod, 3-7 cm long, 0.8-1.2 cm wide; seeds ca 4.5 mm long, 4 mm wide.

description: Ut videtur arbor, perspicue breviter brunneo-pubescens, vel pilis olivaceo-brunneis vestitia, ramulis ultimis eirciter 5 mm. diametro; foliis bipinnatis, 27-32 cm. longis, pinnis utrinque eirciter 13, 6-9 cm. longis, 1.2-1.5 cm. latis, suboppositis, foliolis oppositis, utrinque 22-26, sessilibus, anguste subrhomboideo-oblongis, basi truneatis, marginibus parallelis, sursum abrupte excentrice curvatis, obscurissime apiculatis, eirciter 8 mm. longis et 3 mm. latis, supra in sieco olivaceis, glabris vel subglabris, subtus pallidis, praesertim ad costam excentricam breviter pubeseentibus, pinnis 1-1.5 cm. distantibus; petiolo dense brunneo-pubeseentibus, basi inerassato, 3-4 cm. longo, 1.5 cm. supra basin glandulis ellipticis perspicuis coneavis circiter 3 mm. longis instructo, rhachibus dense pubeseentibus, 15-18 cm. longis, infra pinnis ultimis et penultimis glandulis perspicuis instructis; infloreseentiis terminalibus, haud paniculatis, pedunculis dense brunneo-pubescentibus, 3-4-fasciculatis, sub anthesin 5-8 cm. longis, capitulis sub anthesin 5-7 cm. diametro; floribus numerosis, pallide flaveseentibus vel substramineis, breviter crasseque pedicellatis, pedicellis dense pubeseentibus, 1-2 mm. longis; calycibus subeylindraceis vel sursum leviter ampliatis, extus pubeseentibus, eirciter 5 mm. longis et 2 mm. diametro, lobis pubeseentibus, oblongo-ovatis, acutis vel obtusis, eirciter 1 mm. longis; corolla eirciter 11 mm. longa, pubeseens, lobis oblongis, eirciter 3 mm. longis; staminibus eirciter 30, glabris, 3 cm. longis, deorsum (6-7 mm.) connatis; ovario breviter stipitato, oblanceolato, deorsum glabro, sursum parce adpresse hirsuto.

description: Shrub or small tree, aphyllous at anthesis; branchlets rather slender, often aculeate; petioles 4.4-19.3 cm. long, pubescent, soon glabrescent or glabrous, often aculeate; petiolules 3.5-11 mm. long, 0.5-2 nim. in diam., pubescent as petioles; leaflet-blades thin-chartaceous, usually paler beneath than above, pubescent when young, soon glabrous above, sparsely pubescent beneath, spineless; terminal leaflets deltoid-rhombic or broadly deltoid or rhombic, often broader than long, 3.6-17 cm. long, 3.7-13 cm. broad, acuminate to acute at apex, truncate or broadly cuneate at base; secondaries 5-7 per side; rachis 9.5-37 cm. long, densely pubescent with cinereous hairs, soon glabreseent at least proximally; pedicels 0.2-0.5 cm. long, 0.8 mm. or less in diam., pubeseent as rachis; bracts usually ovate, 1.6-2.3 mm. long, about 0.8 mm. broad; bracteoles variously shaped, usually 0.6-0.8 mm. long and 0.2-0.5 mm. broad; calyx thin-chartaceous, campanulate, 7-14 mm. long on the carinal side (in- eluding spur), 6-13 mm. long on the vexillar side, 2-3 min. broad at base, ampliate to 5-7 mm. at apex, entire or denticulate at margin, slightly calearate on the upper carinal side, densely pubescent with pale einereous at length deciduous hairs; standard pink, narrowly elliptic, (3.2-)4.5-6(-7.3) cm. long, 0.8-1 cm. broad, retuse or rounded at apex, cuneate at base, densely pubescent without with pale cinereous strigillose hairs in bud, sparsely so at anthesis; wings conspicuously sagittate on one side, often provided with a tooth on the opposite side, clawed at base, smaller than keel-petals, 5-9 mm. long, 2-3.5 mm. broad; keel-petals acute at apex, conspicuously sagittate on onle side, clawed at base (claw 1.5-2 mm. lonig), 6-12.5 mm. long, 2.5-4 mm. broad; stamnens 4-6.4 cm. long, separate for 0.8-2.1 cm.; pistil 3.6-6.2 cm. long, the ovary and gynophore densely pubeseent; fruit-pedicels 0.4-0.7 cm. long, 2-3.5 mm. ill diam.; pods lignieous, 14-31 cm. long, usually 1.5 cm. or some- what less broad, constricted between seeds, with a stipe 2.5-7 ecm. lonlg, with a stiff acumination 1.3-3.5 cm. long, usually many-seeded (occasionially 2- or 3-seeded) ; seeds scarlet with a broad black line extending from the hilum for approximately 3 mm. toward the chalazal end, usually 11-13 mm. long and 5-7 mm. broad.

description: Macrophyllidious trees attaining 10 m, with crooked terete glabrescent branchlets, the new stems, leaves, peduncles and flowers pilosulous with soft, horizontal or forwardly inclined, pallid or pallidly rufescent hairs to +/- 0.5-0.7 mm, the subglobose capitula of greenish-ochroleucous flowers arising singly from contemporary leaf-axils on subfiliform, pliant peduncles; phyllotaxy subdistichous. Stipules lanceolate 1.5-4.5 mm, becoming firm and pallid, externally evenulose, mostly persistent. Leafstalks (0.8)1-4.7 cm, devoid of interfoliolar nectaries, the almost closed ventral groove continuous between pairs of pulvinules, the interfoliolar segments of rachis not winged; leaflets 1-3 pairs, when 2-3 pairs strongly accrescent distally; leaflet-pulvinules +/- 1.5- 3 mm long, not wrinkled; leaflet-blades elliptic from subequilaterally cuneate base, short-acuminate and mucronate, the distal (or only) pair 4-8 x 1.6-3 cm, 2.3-3.2 times as long as wide; venation pinnate, the mid- rib subcentric straight, the slender, widely spreading-incurved secondary nerves immersed or almost so on upper face, weakly rominulous beneath. Peduncles 4.5-10.5 cm long, 0.4-0.5 cm diam., ebracteate; capitula incipiently umbelliform, 18-30-flowered, the claviform receptacle +/-1.5-2.5 mm long; bracts linear, induplicate, distally incurved, 4-7 x 0.3-0.5 mm, persistent after fall of flowers; flowers homomorphic; pedicels 0.8-1.4 x 0.4 mm; perianth 5-merous, submembranous, the calyx green, bluntly angulate, the corolla and androecium ochroleucous; calyx narrowly campanulate-urceolate, 4.5 x 2 mm, the broad-lanceolate teeth erect, 1.3-1.4 mm long; corolla 6-6.4 mm long, slightly distended toward orifice, the erect ovate lobes +/- 1.1 mm; androecium 18.5-21 mm long, 22-30-merous, the tube 9.5-10.5 mm long, at middle 0.6 mm diam.; anthers 0.2-0.35 mm long; polyads (+/- 15 seen) 24-27-celled, the distal face of both the peripheral and central grains uniformly rugulose; ovary subsessile, slenderly ellipsoid, glabrous at anthesis; stigma truncate, 0.15 mm diam. Fruit seen only in fallen fragments, of unknown length, 13-14 mm wide, biconvex and bullately distended over the obliquely descending seeds, depressed between them, the sutures 0.6-0.9 mm wide, indehiscent but under pressure breaking between seeds, the valves stiffly papery, pilosulous, weakly venulose, dark brown when ripe, then +/- 0.1 mm thick in section; seeds plumply ellipsoid 8-11 x 6-7 x 4 mm, the testa papery fragile, dull brown, lacking pleurogram.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. & Grimes, James. 1994. A New Species of Inga (Fabaceae, Mimosoideae, Ingeae) from Atlantic Forest in Bahia, Brazil. Brittonia. 46 (1): 66-68.

description: Herbaceous perennial to 25 cm tall, with a thick woody tap root and woody crown; stems often numerous, slender, wiry, glabrous, diffusely branched from upper nodes, the internodes longer than leaves, the nodes often tinged black. Stipules scarious, whitish, deltoid, acuminate or truncate, to 1 mm long and 1 mm Wide. Basal leaves somewhat clustered, sessile, linear, at once shorter, slightly wider, and thicker than cauline ones, glabrous, to 7 mm long, to 1 mm wide; cauline leaves sessile, stiffly erect, filiform or linear, acuminate at apex, to ca 20 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm wide, rather rigid, glabrous or scaberulous, the midrib thick, the margin revolute. Flowers heterostylous, in small, few-flowered cymes, the pedicels filiform, to ca 1 cm long, the inflorescence very diffuse. Calyx glabrous, the lobes with thick midribs, linear-lanceolate, sharply acute or acuminate, stiffly erect, 0.8-3.0 mm long, ca 1/2-%A as long as corolla tube. Corolla funnelform, white with several dark nerves, glabrous externally, 2.3-4.7 mm long; corolla tube gradually widened distally, densely puberulent within, 1.3-3.0 mm long; corolla lobes ovate- lanceolate, puberulent within, 1.0-1.7 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm wide; pin flower with stigma branches 0.3-0.5 mm long, exserted 0.5-1.5 mm beyond corolla throat, anthers 0.8-1.0 mm long, included, attached near midpoint or 34-point of corolla tube; thrum flower with anthers whitish, ca 1 mm long, subsessile at sinuses of corolla lobes, and stigmas included in tube. Mature capsule 1/2-%A inferior, de- hiscing loculicidally, globose or subglobose, glabrous, 1.5-2 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, much exceeded by erect calyx lobes. Seeds ca 10-26 per capsule, elliptic, oblong or oval in outline, slightly or somewhat compressed, 0.4-0.7 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm wide, black or brown, finely reticulate, the hilum punctate, lacking a hilar ridge.

description: Herbaceous perennial to 4.4 dm tall, with a thick, woody root; stems erect, somewhat woody toward base, subterete, rather thick, glabrous, brown, sparsely branched. Stipules broadly rounded, to 1 or 2 mm long, their central lobe crowned with recurved glandular trichomes. Leaves short-petiolate, 1-nerved, lanceolate-ovate or lanceolate, somewhat acuminate, glabrous, slightly paler beneath, to 7 cm long to 2 cm wide. Flowers in terminal, few-flowered cymes, kind of styly not known, pedicels very slender, to ca 13 mm long, inflorescence widely branching, to ca 7 cm long ca 10 cm wide. Calyx glabrous, the lobes linear or linear-lanceolate, acute, to 4.7 mm long, 0.8 mm wide, 1/2-3/4 as long as corolla tube. Corolla broadly funnelform, white, glabrous externally, 7-10.5 mm long, the tube widened distally to ca 4 mm wide at throat, glabrous or puberulent within, 3-5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide at base, the lobes ovate, glabrous or puberulent within, 2.5-5.0 x 1.5-2.5 mm, shorter than to slightly longer than the tube; anthers narrow-oblong, 1.5-2.0 mm long, subsessile, attached at corolla sinuses; stigma and style included in corolla tube. Mature capsule (only previous year's dehisced capsules seen) 3/4-/8 inferior, subglobose, thin-walled, ca 3.0-3.5 mm long and wide. Seeds somewhat compressed, obtusely 5-7 sided or suborbicular or oval in outline, 0.6-1.1 x 0.5-0.9 mm, brown mottled with black, finely reticulate, dorsal and ventral faces convex or obtusely ridged, hilum punctiform in center of ventral face.

description: Herbaceous perennial to ca 3 dm high; stems suffruticose, long-trailing, prostrate or with ascending or erect branches, rooting at some nodes, wiry, tetrangular, reddish, nodes pubescent, internodes glabrous or puberulent, upper ones usually 4-20 mm long. Stipules ovate or deltoid, acuminate or somewhat cuspidate, to 1.5 mm long, densely pubescent, often with reddish glandular trichomes along margin. Leaves sessile or subsessile, thick, revolute, paler beneath, 1-nerved with conspicuous midrib, sometimes somewhat decurrent, ovate or oval, rounded to cuneate at base, acutish or obtuse at apex, (5) 6-10 (16) x (2.5) 3-5 (8) mm, glabrous above or puberulent only on midrib, glabrous beneath, margins glabrous or scabrous. Inflorescence terminal, of several-flowered cymes, flowers heterostylous, the pedicels slender, to ca 4 mm long. Calyx glabrous, lobes lan- ceolate-oblong, lanceolate, or lanceolate-ovate, obtuse, 1.1-2.6 x 0.5-0.9 mm, somewhat surpassing capsule. Corolla funnelform, white, glabrous externally, densely glandular-pubescent within, 4.2-6.6 mm long; the tube 2.0-3.4 mm long, 1.3-2.1 mm wide at throat; the lobes ovate or oblong, 1.9-3.6 x 1.2-1.8 mm; pin flowers with stigmas linear-oblong, ca 0.6-1.0 mm long, exserted to 3 mm beyond corolla throat; thrum flowers with anthers 0.8-1.2 mm long, blue, narrow-oblong, curved, exserted on filaments 1.0-1.5 mm long. Mature capsule 3/4-7/8 inferior, dehiscing loculicidally and then widely septicidally, subglobose, 1.5-3 x 2.0-3.5 mm, medium thick-walled, placenta attached at base of septum. Seeds slightly or somewhat compressed, suborbicular or oval in outline, sometimes appearing 3-angled, 0.6-0.8 x 0.45-0.75 mm, black, rather shiny, finely reticulate, dorsal face flat or slightly convex, ventral face rounded with conspicuous hilar ridge.

description: Low shrub ca 3 dm tall; stems woody, to 3 cm thick, the internodes short and partially obscured by overlapping leaves, the branches ascending, glabrous, angulate, densely leafy, tan or dark, becoming gray or tan with age and exfoliating. Stipules scarious, whitish, sheathing, truncate or deltoid, with 0-few minute teeth or glands. Leaves sessile, opposite, terete or subterete, somewhat fleshy, somewhat falcate, glabrous, 4-19 mm long, 0.8-1.3 mm wide, more or less cuspidate with whitish, rigid point. Flowers apparently (?) homostylous, in terminal, few-flowered, crowded cymes, the pedicels stout, 2-6 mm long. Calyx glabrous, the lobes spreading or erect, deltoid, lanceolate or ovate, acuminate or acute, 0.8-1.7 mm long, 0.7-1.0 mm wide at bases. Corolla short-funnelform, white, glabrous, 3-5 mm long, persisting through fruiting stage, the tube 0.7-1.1 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, scarcely wider distally, the lobes ovate-lanceolate or ovate, spreading or recurved, 1.5-2.3 mm long, 1.0-1.2 mm wide, 2-3 times longer than tube; anthers oblong, whitish or yellowish, 0.6-0.8 mm long, ca 0.2 mm wide, on filaments 0.5-1.5 mm long; stigma branches diverging, subglobose, 0.1-0.2 mm long, the styles ca 1.8-2.3 mm long; ovaries and developing capsules rose or pink. Mature capsule ca 1/2 inferior, thick-walled, dehiscing loculicidally, subglobose, 2-3 mm in all 3 dimensions, surrounded by dried persistent corolla, the apex obtuse or obtusely knobbed. Seeds ca 6-10 per capsule, black, shiny, finely reticulate, somewhat compressed, 0.5-0.8 mm diam., roundish-angular to elliptic or oblong in outline, shallowly concavo-convex (acetabuliform), the concave side with conspicuous acentric hilar ridge 12-7/s as long as seed and extending only one margin of the seed where higher, the seed sometimes with rudimentary wing-like margins.

description: Fruit long-ovoid, 20 mm diam., 40 mm long, with pericarp 2.5 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical. The species is distinctive within the subtribe in the dense mantle of brachysclereids separated from the epider- mis by a band of parenchyma with scattered raphide-bearing cells; vascular bundles with thick fibrous sheaths intermixed with fi- brous bundles and embedded within the mantle of brachysclereids; vascular bundles with thinner fibrous sheaths scattered throughout the middle and inner pericarp, along with scattered tanniniferous cells; distinctive also within the subtribe in the very thick palisade-like locular epidermis.

description: Herba perennis odorata 60-100 cm alta superne sat ramosa, ramis capitato-glandulosis et pilis extensis longioribus plus minusve conspersis; foliorum laminis ovatis 3-5 cm longis, acutis vel obtusis, in basi rotundatis vel sub-cordatis, irregulariter serrulatis, paginis ambabus glabratis vel sparse hirtellis, petiolis ca. 1 cm longis; floribus in paniculis plus minusve foliolosis, in cymulis dichotomis axillaribus paucifloris pedunculis 1-2 cm longis elatis; calycum florentium tubo 2.5-3 mm longo, maturis paulo aucto, extus hirtello-glanduloso, intus ad dentes annulato; dentibus deltoideo-lanceolatis acutis ca. 2 mm longis, inferioribus duobus paulo longioribus; corollarum rosearum tubo 5-6 mm longo; nuculis brunneis 5 mm longis, hilis pro rata majoribus.

description: Suffrutex parvus ut videtur altitudine ad 40 cm caulibus superne dense piloso-hispidis, internodiis superioribus 1-2 cm longis; foliorum laminis cori- aceis 1.5-2 cm longis ovalibus etiam obovatis, confertis, subsessilibus, irregulariter crenato-serratis, pagina superiore sparse pilosis, inferiore reticulato-venulosa ad venas densiore pilosa; capitulis ca. 1 cm diametro, pedunculis 2-3 mm longis, pluribus in capitulis maioribus subglobosis 2-3 cm diametro dense albolanatis colligatis unoquoque pedunculo crasso, 1-2.5 cm longo dense piloso terminaliter elatis; calycibus florentibus 5 mm longis extus lanatis dentibus tubo subaequilongis lanceolatis; corollarum tubo 5 mm longol intus retrorse piloso; nec calycibus maturis nec nuculis visis.

description: Fruit 7 mm diam., with pericarp 0.9 mm thick, stigmatic remains basal-distinctive for the thick subepidermal layer of tanniniferous cells, the raphide-bearing cells scattered in the middle pericarp, and the vascular bundles with very thick fibrous sheaths aggregated in the inner pericarp. description: Small epiphytic herbs up to 15 cm tall; stems elongate, fusiform, 3-5 cm long and 0.3-0.4 cm in diameter, bearing 3-5 leaves along the stem; leaves linear-lanceolate, acute, submembranaceous, 6-8 en long and 0.6-0.8 cm broad, the lowest often much smaller; leaf-sheath surrounding the stems, the lowermost somewhat inflated and somewhat pergamentaceous; infloreseence terminal, few-flowered, racemose, 5-9 cm long; bracts subtending the flowers ovate or ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, 2-3 mm long; flowers light rose; lip about 15 mm long and 10-12 mm broad, unguiculate, 3-lobed with the mid-lobe deeply divided, the lateral lobes oblong-ovate, rounded at the apex, about 6 mm long and 3.5 mm broad opposite the sinus, the mid-lobe bilobed and the lobes divaricate, oblong, about 5 mm long and 3 mm broad, the apices rounded; dorsal sepal elliptic-oblong, somewhat acute, 3-nerved, about 5.5 mm long and 2 mm broad; lateral sepals oblong-ovate, aeute, slightly falcate, 3-nerved, about 5.5 mm long and 2.5 mm broad; petals linear-oblong, truncate, about 5.5 mm long and 0.8 mm broad; column about 1.5 mm long, the claw of the lip solidly joined to it and somewhat unguiculate.

description: Shrub or small tree to 18 m tall, 20 cm diam, the branchlets quadrangular to subrotund, covered with brownish strigulose tomentum. Leaves with blades mem- branaceous, obovate to elliptic, 12-25 (45) x (6) 9-13 (17) cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp 1.5-2.5 cm long, obtuse to acuminate at base, glabrous above, floccose beneath; midrib strigulose and planar above, strigulose to short floccose and prominulous distally to prominent proximally beneath; primary veins 15-24 pairs, planar and sparingly strigose above, prominulous and mostly floccose beneath; petiole 25-40 (50) x 2-3 mm, vestiture strigulose; stipules 4, interpetiolar, cymbiform and narrowly triangular, 5-15 (25) mm long, strigulose with ciliate margins. Inflorescence broadly ovoid to spherical 8-13 (20) x 5-11 cm, with secondary rachises of a simple 3-flowered dichasium or a compound 7-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 2 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, strigose, 15-42 x 1.5-2 mm, subtended by ovate to lanceolate cymbiform bracteoles, these strigulose and ciliate, 5-7 (25) mm long, apex long-caudate especially beneath more proximal branches. Flowers: calyx red, cup-shaped, 6-7 x 5-6 mm, glabrescent inside, tomentose or strigose outside, 4-lobed, occasionally with one or several lobes elongated to 1.5 cm; corolla reddish-orange proximally, grading to yellow distally or rarely entirely white, the tube 50-70 mm long, densely tomentose outside, with copious yellow-villous pubescence inside restricted to around mouth, the lobes (5) 6, lanceolate, 6-8 mm long, cucullate at apices; stamens (4) 5 or 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, 8-10 mm long, the filaments ca as long as anthers; ovary (4) 5- or 6-celled; style 60-6 5 mm long, the stigma (4) 5- or 6-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, ca 2 mm long. Fruit a pyrene, broadly ovoid, ca 10 mm diam, scabridulous, pubescent; seeds 0.9-1 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to 20 m tall, the branchlets quadrangular to subrotund, covered with grayish-brown strigose tomentum. Leaves with blades chartaceous, ovate, elliptic or obovate, 29-64 x 10-30 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp 1.5-2 cm long, acuminate to attenuate or decurrent at base, glabrous above, sparingly setose beneath; midrib glabrous and planar to prominulous above, strigulose and prominent beneath; primary veins 16-23 pairs, glabrous and planar above, strigulose and prominulous beneath; petiole 5-50 x 2.5-5 (7) mm, vestiture strigulose; stipules 4, interpetiolar, lanceolate and somewhat falcate, 8-45 mm long, strigulose with ciliolate margins. Inflorescence shallowly deltoid to ovoid, 10-21 x 9-17 cm, with secondary rachises of a simple 8-18-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 4-9 flowers, the secondary rachises reddish- orange, spreading at 45-60 degree angles from primary rachis, strigose, 14-32 (45) x 1.5-2.5 (3) mm, subtended by triangular cymbiform bracteoles, these stri- gose and ciliate, 3-11 mm long. Flowers: calyx reddish-orange, cup-shaped, 2.5- 3 x 3 mm, glabrous inside, strigulose outside, indistinctly 4-lobed; corolla bright yellow, turning brilliant orange or reddish, the tube 24-28 mm long, strigulose to hispid outside, glabrous inside, the lobes 6, lanceolate, 8-9 mm long, with dense yellow-villous pubescence inside, usually with a tubercule protruding ca 1 mm on the outer surface; stamens 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, 4-6 mm long, the filaments ca as long as anthers; ovary (5) 6 (7)-celled; style glabrous, 20-28 mm long, the stigma (5) 6-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, 3.5-5 mm long. Fruit a pyrene, 6-8 mm diam, smooth, strigulose; seeds 0.6-0.9 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to 15 m tall, 35 cm diam, the branchlets subrotund to quadrangular, glabrescent or pulverulent. Leaves with blades membranaceous, elliptic to obovate, 18-65 x 9-18 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp 0.5-1.5 cm long, acute at base, glabrous above, white-canescent beneath; midrib glabrous and prominulous above, glabrescent or puberulent and prominent beneath especially proximally; primary veins 16-28 pairs, planar and glabrous above, prominulous and puberulent beneath; petiole 35-75 x 2.5-3 mm, glabrescent; stipules 4, interpetiolar, narrowly triangular, ca 9 mm long. Inflorescence ovoid to broadly ovoid, 8-22 x 6-18 cm, with secondary rachises of a simple 7-flowered dicha- sium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 3 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, glabrescent to strigulose especially in axes, 25-35 x 2.5-3 mm, subtended by widely ovate cym- biform bracteoles, these strigulose with ciliolate margin, 3-4 mm long. Flowers: calyx pinkish-green, cup-shaped, 4-6 x 5 mm, glabrous inside but with small patches of red squamose cells near mouth, glabrescent and scabridulous outside, indistinctly 4- or 5-lobed; corolla reddish-orange, the tube 43-65 mm long, pu- berulent outside, with copious yellow-villous pubescence inside restricted to around mouth, the lobes 6 or 7, spathulate, 8-10 (13) mm long with tubercules protruding externally 0.5-1 mm at junction of lobes and tube; stamens 6 or 7, the anthers narrowly oblong, 7-10 mm long, the filaments laminar, ca 2 mm long; ovary 5- or 6-celled; style glabrous, 41-53 mm long, the stigma 5- or 6-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, ca 2 mm long. Fruit a pyrene, very broadly ovoid, ca 10 mm diam, smooth or scabridulous, occasionally puberulent; seeds 0.8-1.1 mm long.

description: Shrub 5 m tall, the branchlets quadrangular, glabrous. Leaves with blades coriaceous, oblanceolate, 28-33 x 7-10 cm, acute or acuminate at apex, acute to attenuate at base, glabrous above with white tomentum beneath confined to the bottom of the areoles; midrib glabrous above and beneath; primary veins ca 25 pairs, impressed and glabrous above, prominulous and ciliolate beneath; petiole 25-40 x 2-4 mm, glabrous; stipules 4, interpetiolar, deeply bifid, ca 1 cm long with obtuse apices, glabrous. Inflorescence ellipsoidal, ca 22 x 7 cm, with secondary rachises of a compound 7-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having a simple dichasium of 3 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, glabrous, ca 30 x 3 mm, subtended by triangular cymbiform bracteoles, glabrous, 2-3 mm long. Flowers: calyx ca 7 x 5 mm, glabrous outside with conspicuous patches of red squamose cells inside, with acute lobes ca 2 mm long; corolla "brownish red with yellow border" (Weberbauer 7066), the tube ca 35 mm long, glabrous outside with villous pubescence inside around mouth and on inside of lobes, the lobes 5, ca 10 mm long, with obtuse apices; stamens 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, ca 8 mm long, the filaments ca 3 mm long; ovary 2-celled; style ca 35 mm long, the stigma 2-lobed, the lobes clavate, ca 6 mm long. Fruit unknown.

description: Shrub or small tree to 12 m tall, the branchlets quadrangular, strigulose. Leaves with blades membranaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic, 29-43 (68) x 14-20 (36) cm, acute to cuspidate at apex, the cusp 1-2 cm long, acute to rounded at base, glabrous above, white canescent beneath; midrib glabrescent or ciliolate and prominulous above, strigulose and prominent beneath; primary veins 19-25 pairs, planar and glabrescent to ciliolate above, prominulous and strigulose to canescent beneath; petiole (20) 40-120 x 2-5 mm, strigulose; stipules 4, interpetiolar, triangular, 5-13 (45) mm long, sometimes foliaceous. Inflorescence ovoid to ellip- soid, 16-34 x 7-9 cm, with secondary rachises of a simple 5-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 2 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, strigulose to tomentose especially in axes, 25-45 x 2-4 mm, subtended by widely ovate cymbiform bracteoles, these strigulose with ciliolate margin, ca 4 mm long. Flowers: calyx cup-shaped, 5-6 x 3-4 mm, glabrous or ciliolate inside, strigulose and scabri- dulous outside, indistinctly 5- or 6-lobed; corolla white, the tube 32-53 (60) mm long, with copious villous pubescence inside restricted to around the mouth, puberulent outside, the lobes S or 6, cucullate at apex, 10-14 mm long; stamens 6 or 7, the anthers narrowly oblong, 7-9 mm long, the filaments laminar, ca 3 mm long; ovary 2- or 3-celled; style ciliolate, 32-47 (57) mm long, the stigma 2-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, 3-5 mm long. description: Shrub or small tree to 12 m tall, 15 cm diam, the branchlets quadrangular, glabrous. Leaves with blades subcoriaceous, oblanceolate, 17-45 x 7-16 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp 0. 5-3.5 cm long, acuminate to attenuate at base, glabrous on both surfaces; midrib glabrous, prominulous above, prominent beneath, especially proximally; primary veins 15-20 pairs, prominulous above and beneath, generally glabrous but occasionally sparingly setose to short tomentose in small patches at juncture of midrib and primary veins beneath; petiole 35-70 x 2-4 mm, glabrescent; stipules 2, intrapetiolar, ca 5 mm long, widely ovate or triangular, glabrous with ciliolate margins. Inflorescence slightly pyramidal or more commonly cylindrical, 5-16 (25) x 3-5 (7) cm, with secondary rachises of a compound 7-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having a simple dichasium of 3 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 90 degree angles from primary rachis, glabrous or with small patches of tomentum, 10-1 5 x 1-2 mm, subtended by very widely ovate, cymbiform, ciliate bracteoles ca 1 mm long. Flowers: calyx red, shallow cup-shaped, 3-5 x 4-5 mm, glabrous inside but with small patches of red squamose cells near mouth, glabrescent outside, indistinctly 4- or 5-lobed with short, scattered cilia on margin; corolla tube pink, 9-13 mm long, glabrous outside, with copious yellow-villous pubescence down to within 1-2 mm from base within, the lobes 5 or 6, white, lanceolate to ovate, cucullate at apices; stamens 5 or 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, 4.5-6.5 mm long, acuminate at apex, the filaments ca as long as anthers; ovary (5) 6 (7)-celled; style 7-8 mm long, the stigma 6-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, 2-2.5 mm long. Fruit a pyrene, spheroid to broadly ellipsoid, ca 7 mm diam, glabrous; seeds 1-1.2 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to 12 m tall, 10 cm diam, the branchlets quadrangular to subrotund, strigulose to glabrescent. Leaves with blades coriaceous, ovate, 13- 39 x 6-17 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp 1-2 cm long, cordate to obtuse or rounded at base, glabrous above, sparsely to densely pubescent beneath; midrib glabrous to sparingly strigulose and prominulous above, strigulose and proximally prominent beneath; primary veins 16-21 pairs, planar and glabrous above, prominulous and strigulose beneath; petiole 20-25 x 2-3 mm, strigulose; stipules 4, interpetiolar, lanceolate, 15-25 mm long, margin entire. Inflorescence very broadly ovoid, 9-12 x 8-13 cm, with secondary rachises of a compound 3 1-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 3 or 4 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45-60 degree angles from primary rachis, sparsely to densely strigulose, 25-30 x 1-2 mm, subtended by widely ovate cymbiform bracteoles, these pubescent, 4-5 mm long. Flowers: calyx pink, cup-shaped, ca 4 x 3 mm, glabrous inside, sparingly to densely pubescent outside, 4-6-lobed; corolla tube pink, 5-13 mm long, with copious villous pubescence inside around mouth, glabrous outside, the lobes 6, oblong, white with purple markings at base within, 4-7 mm long, acute and cucullate at apices; stamens 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, 4-5.5 mm long, the filaments 3 mm long; ovary 4-6-celled; style 9-14 mm long, minutely tuberculate, the stigma 4-6-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, 1-1.5 mm long. Fruit a pyrene, broadly ovoid, ca 5 mm diam, strigulose, rugulose; seeds ca 1 mm long.

description: Shrub or large tree to 25 m tall, the branchlets quadrangular, viscid-strigulose to tomentose. Leaves with blades membranaceous, obovate to elliptic, 29-45 x 8-25 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp ca 2 cm long, acute, acuminate or rounded at base, glabrous above, glabrescent to tomentose beneath; midrib ciliolate and prominulous above, puberulent to tomentose and prominent beneath; primary veins, prominulous above and beneath; petiole 50-100 x 2-4 mm, puberulent to tomentose; stipules 4, interpetiolar, lanceolate, 15-30 mm long, the margins ciliolate. Inflorescence ellipsoid to broadly ellipsoid, 10-30 x 10-15 cm, with secondary rachises of a simple 5-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 2 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, strigulose to tomentose, 20-50 x 2-5 mm, subtended by lanceolate cymbiform bracteoles, these ciliolate, 10-20 mm long. Flowers: calyx 6-7 x 4-5 mm, glabrous inside but with scattered patches of red squamose cells, glabrescent and smooth outside, indistinctly 5- or 6-lobed; corolla white, the tube 60-75 mm long, with copious villous pubescence inside around mouth, pubescent outside grading to glabrous and rugulose distally, the lobes 6, oblong, 11-20 mm long, acute and cucullate at apices; stamens 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, ca 12 mm long, the filaments laminar, ca 3 mm long; ovary 2-celled; style 50-70 cm long, ciliolate, the stigma 2-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, 5-7 mm long. Fruit a berry, ellipsoid, ca 10 mm diam, smooth, glabrous; seeds 1-1.2 mm long.

description: Inter congeneras ovario 6-loculari et stigmatibus 6 instructas foliis subglabris et corolla circ. 5 cm longa, ante anthesin ad basin loborum alata noscenda. Arbor ca. 5 m alta. Rami novelli vix notabile papillosi, circ. 4.5 mm diam. Folia opposita petiolo glabro 1.5-4 cm longo instructa; lamina oblongo-obovata, 13-24 cm longa et 5-10 cm lata, caudato-acuminata, basi acuta vel subobtusa, sicc. supra brunnea et subtus viridi-brunnea, supra glabra, subtus costa nervisque vix notabile puberula, inter nervos glabra, costa supra colore coccineo conspicua, subtus prominente, nervis utroque latere costae 15-17 supra immersis, subtus prominulis, venulis transversis supra immersis, subtus colore saturatiore distinguendis. Stipulae lobis lateralibus orbicularibus circ. 5 mm longis instructae et inter lobos laterales cicatricem lobi centralis mox decidui exhibentes. Inflorescentia paniculiformis pedunculo ca. 5 cm longo, vix notabile puberulo elata, e rachide pedunculo subaequilonga et ramulis lateralibus in cymas plerumque 3-floras exeuntibus composita. Bracteae infimae subulatae, superiores deltoideae, longitudine sensim usque ad 1.5 mm decrescentes. Cymae flos centralis sessilis, flores laterales stipite 4-7 mm longo, apice bracteolis ovato-orbicularibus instructo elati. Ovarium 6-loculare. Calyx 4-merus glaber. Corolla 6-mera tubo rubro-lutea, limbo lutea, extus vix notabile papillosa, ca. 5 cm longa, ante anthesin ad basin loborum conspicue alata, tubo 4 cm longo, fauce barbato, lobis 10 mm longis, intus fere totis barbatis. Antherae 6.5 mm longae. Stigmata 6, 4.5 mm longa. Drupa nondum visa.

description: Shrub or small tree to 8 m tall, 13 cm diam, the branchlets quadrangular to subrotund, strigose to tomentose. Leaves with blades coriaceous, obovate to elliptic 22-42 x 8-15 cm, slightly cuspidate at apex, the cusp 0.5-1 cm long, acute to acuminate at base, glabrescent above, tomentose and prominent beneath; mid-rib strigulose and impressed above, tomentose and prominent beneath; primary veins 20-30 pairs, impressed and sparingly strigulose above, prominent and to- mentose beneath; petiole (15) 25-45 x 2-6 mm, strigose to tomentose; stipules 4, interpetiolar, triangular, 8-15 (20) mm long, strigulose with ciliolate margins. Inflorescence narrowly ellipsoid to ellipsoid, 10-34 x 7-12 cm, with secondary rachises of a simple 8- or 9-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 3 or 4 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, strigose, 15-35 x 1.5-3 mm, subtended by ovate to lanceolate cymbiform bracteoles, these strigulose and ciliate, 3-10 mm long, apex acuminate. Flowers: calyx cup-shaped, 7-8 x 4-5 mm, flaring at apex, sparingly strigose inside, more so outside, irregularly 4-lobed, the lobes broadly rounded, ciliate, ca 2 mm long; corolla yellow or orange, the tube 35-40 mm long, tomentose outside with copious golden-villous pubescence inside restricted to around mouth, the lobes 5 or 6, ovate, 4-7 mm long, acute at apices; stamens 6-8, the anthers narrowly oblong, 8-9 mm long, the filaments ca 3 mm long; ovary (2) 3-4-celled; style 38-40 mm long, the stigma 3- or 4-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, ca 3.5 mm long. Fruit a berry, broadly ellipsoid, 6-8 mm diam, scabridulous, strigose; seeds 0.9-1 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to 13 m tall, 20 cm diam, the branchlets subrotund, gla- brescent or pulverulent. Leaves with blades membranaceous, oblanceolate to ob- ovate, 19-48 x 6-17 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp 1.5-2 cm long, acute to acuminate or attenuate at base, glabrous above, glabrous beneath or rarely short ciliate and proximally prominent beneath; primary veins 12-19 pairs, prominu- lous above and beneath, glabrous or rarely ciliolate beneath; petiole 15-35 (50) x 1.5-2 mm, glabrescent; stipules 2, intrapetiolar, widely depressed ovate, ca 3 mm long, margin with several low teeth. Inflorescence ellipsoid to ovate, 8-14 x 7- 8 cm, with secondary rachises of a compound 1 1-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 2 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, glabrescent to ciliolate, 15-20 x 1.5- 2.5 mm, subtended by widely ovate, cymbiform bracteoles, these glabrescent to puberulent with aciliolate margin, ca 1.5 mm long. Flowers: calyx red, cup-shaped, ca 3.5 x 3.5 mm, mostly glabrous but with small patches of red squamose cells inside near mouth, glabrescent and smooth or slightly rugose outside, indistinctly 4-lobed; corolla reddish-violet proximally, grading to pink distally, the tube 35-50 mm long, with copious pinkish-purple- or yellow-villous pubescence inside restricted to around mouth, mostly glabrous but rarely puberulent outside, the lobes pink, 5 or 6, oblong, 6-8 mm long, acute and cucullate at apices; stamens 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, 5.5-6 mm long, the filaments laminar, ca as long as anthers; ovary (5) 6-celled; style 29-42 mm long, the stigma 4-6-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, 2-3 mm long. Fruit a pyrene, spheroidal, ca 8.5 mm diam, smooth, glabrous; seeds 1.2-1.3 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to 10 m tall, the branchlets quadrangular, covered with grayish-brown strigose tomentum. Leaves with blades membranaceous, elliptic to obovate, 22-44 x 13-27 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp 1.5-2 cm long, acuminate to attenuate at base, glabrous above, sparingly setose beneath; midrib strigulose above and beneath, planar to prominulous above, prominent beneath; primary veins 18-24 pairs, glabrous and planar above, strigulose and prominulous beneath; petiole 50-55 x 2.5-4 mm, vestiture strigulose; stipules 4, interpetiolar, narrowly triangular and somewhat falcate, 10-12 mm long, strigulose with ciliate margins. Inflorescence shallowly deltoid to ovoid, 20-25 x 10-15 cm, with sec- ondary rachises of a simple 9-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 4 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at 45-60 degree angles from primary rachis, strigose, 25-40 x 2-3 mm, subtended by triangular cymbiform bracteoles, these strigulose and ciliate, 4-18 mm long, sometimes aristate. Flowers: calyx green cup-shaped, ca 4 x 3 mm, essentially glabrous inside with occasional small patches of squamose cells near mouth, strigulose to gla- brescent outside, indistinctly 4-6-lobed; corolla first white or yellow, turning pink (or red?) with purple throat, the tube 3 5-40 mm long, strigulose and rugose outside, glabrous inside, the lobes 6, somewhat spathulate apically, ca 13-14 mm long, with dense (whitish?) villous pubescence inside; stamens 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, 6-6.5 mm long, the filaments ca 3 mm long; ovary (2) 3 (4)-celled; style ciliolate, ca 35 mm long, the stigma (2) 3 (4)-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, ca 3 mm long. Fruit a berry, broadly ellipsoid to spheroid, 5-6 mm diam, rugulose and sparingly strigose to glabrescent; seeds 0.9-1.1 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to 10 m tall, the branchlets subrotund or quadrangular, strigose to glabrescent. Leaves with blades membranaceous to subcoriaceous, obovate to ovate, 14-37 (47) x 5-22 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp 2-5 cm long, acute to rotund or decurrent at base, glabrous or scabrous above, glabrescent beneath; midrib strigose to glabrescent and prominulous above, strigulose to to- mentose and prominent beneath; primary veins 19-21 pairs, planar and strigulose to glabrous above, prominulous and hispid to strigulose beneath; petiole 10-50 x 1-3 mm, glabrous to tomentose; stipules 2, intrapetiolar, triangular, 8-9 mm long, margin ciliolate. Inflorescence narrowly ellipsoid, 5-19 x 5-11 cm, with secondary rachises of a single flower, or of a simple 3-flowered dichasium, or of a simple 5-flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 2 flowers, the secondary rachises lax and spreading at various angles from primary rachis, strigulose to tomentose, 3-25 x 1-2 mm, subtended by ovate to triangular cymbiform bracteoles, these glabrescent to puberulent with ciliolate margin, 2-3 mm long. Flowers: calyx red, cup-shaped, ca 3 x 3 mm, glabrous inside but with patches of red squamose cells near mouth, strigulose and somewhat rugulose outside, 4-lobed, the lobes 1 mm long, acute with ciliolate margins; corolla tube orange-red, 32-45 mm long, strigulose outside, glabrous inside but with copious yellow pubescence near mouth, the lobes 6, yellow, oblong, 3-6 mm long, villous pubescent inside, acute and cucullate at apices; stamens 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, ca 5 mm long, the filaments 3-4 mm long; ovary 5- or 6-celled; style glabrous, 35-40 mm long, the stigma 5- or 6-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, 2-3 mm long. Fruit a pyrene, obloid, 4-6 mm diam, smooth and strigulose or glabrescent; seeds 1-1.3 mm long.

description: Small tree to 16 m tall, 40 cm diam, the branchlets quadrangular, glabrescent to minutely strigulose. Leaves with blades coriaceous, obovate, 26-40 (80) x 12- 20 (35) cm, acute to cuspidate at apex, the cusp 0.5-1 cm long, acute to acuminate at base, glabrous above, silvery white canescent beneath; midrib glabrous and prominulous above, glabrescent to sparingly strigulose and prominent beneath; primary veins 19-24 pairs, planar and glabrous above, prominulous and puber- ulent beneath; petiole 30-65 (90) x 3-4 mm, glabrescent; stipules 4, interpetiolar, lanceolate, 15-35 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescence narrowly ellipsoidal, 10-24 x 4-11 cm, with secondary rachises of a single flower or a simple 3-flowered di- chasium or 2-flowered scorpioid cymes, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, glabrescent to puberulent, 20-30 x 2-3 mm, subtended by triangular bracteoles ca 2 mm long, margins ciliolate, apex acute. Flowers: calyx pale green to salmon-red, shallow cup-shaped, 5-6 x 4-8 mm, glabrous but with patches of red squamose cells inside, glabrescent outside, indistinctly 5- or 6-lobed, the lobes broadly rounded, ciliolate, ca 1 mm long; corolla tube red proximally grading to yellow distally, 40-55 mm long, white- or yellow-villous pubescent inside around mouth, glabrous outside with prominent tubercules distally, the lobes 6, with dense villous pubescence inside, glabrous outside, cucullate, 9-14 mm long, acute at apices; stamens 6, the anthers narrowly oblong, 8-9 mm long; ovary 2-celled; style 51-60 mm long, the stigma 2-lobed, the lobes narrowly oblong, 2-3 mm long. Fruit a berry, ellipsoidal, slightly asymmetrical, ca 9 mm diam, glabrous and smooth outside; seeds ca 1.5 mm long.

description: Small tree to 10 m tall, the branchlets subrotund or quadrangular, hirtellous to glabrescent. Leaves with blades rugose, subcoriaceous, elliptic to ovate, 24- 47 x 12-21 cm, cuspidate at apex, the cusp to 5 cm long, rounded or acute at base, glabrous above, hirtellous beneath; midrib strigulose and prominulous above, hirtellous and prominent beneath; primary veins 12-22 pairs, impressed and strigulose above, prominulous and hirtellous beneath; petiole 20-55 x 2-3 mm, tomentose; stipules 4, interpetiolar, lanceolate, ca 20 mm long, ciliolate. Inflorescence ovoid, 6-15 x 4-6 cm, with secondary rachises of a compound 11- flowered dichasium, the ultimate branches having scorpioid cymes of 2 flowers, the secondary rachises spreading at ca 45 degree angles from primary rachis, subtended by lanceolate cymbiform bracteoles, these strigulose with ciliolate mar- gins. Flowers: calyx cup-shaped, 4-6 x 4-5 mm, glabrous inside but with patches of red squamose cells near mouth, strigulose outside, indistinctly 4-lobed, the lobes with apices truncate or subtruncate; corolla tube ca 27 mm long (immature), glabrescent outside, villous inside around mouth, red, orange, or yellow, the lobes ovate to subovate, 3 x 1 mm; stamens unknown; ovary 5-celled; style unknown. Fruit a pyrene, subglobose, 5-5.5 mm diam, smooth and glabrous; seeds ca 1.1 mm long.
