description: Arbor ad 20 m. alta, trunco ad 20 cm. diametro; ramulis subtere-tibus cinereis glabris lenticellatis; petiolis rugosis canaliculatis 15-25 mm. longis; laminis glabris coriaceis elliptico-oblongis, 14-25 cm. longis, 5-9 cm. latis, basi acutis vel subattenuatis, apice obtuse breviter acuminatis, margine integris, costa subtus prominente, nervis secundariis utroque 15-22 prope margines adscendentibus supra prominulis subtus elevatis, venulis reticulatis planis vel leviter prominulis; floribus axil-laribus sessilibus in glomerulis 8-20-floris aggregatis; calyce sepalis 7-9 imbricatis constato, sepalis oblongo-orbicularibus utrinque breviter sericeis, margine membranaceis et fimbriatis, interioribus maximis, 3 mm. longis, 2.5 mm. latis; corolla glabra breviter campanulata 4 mm. longa, lobis 5 oblongo-rotundatis, 1.3 mm. longis, 1.6 mm. latis; stami-nodiis ovatis acutis 1 mm. longis; staminibus sub fauce insertis, fila-mentis 0.3 mm. longis, antheris deltoideo-ovatis basifixis 0.8 mm. longis; ovario globoso sub anthesi 1.5 mm. diametro dense hispido, loculis 5; stylo carnoso ovarium aequante, stigmate minute 5-lobato.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description: Arbor ad 40 m. alta, trunco ad 1 m. diametro; ramulis subteretibus glabris; petiolis gracilibus canaliculatis 8-15 mm. longis; laminis sub-coriaceis elliptico-oblongis, 9-14 cm. longis, 3-4.5 cm. latis, basi acutis vel subattenuatis, apice caudato-acuminatis (acumine 1 cm. longo ob-tuso), margine integris et leviter revolutis, costa utrinque subpromi-nente, nervis secundariis utroque 14-17 arcuato-adscendentibus utrinque elevatis, venulis reticulatis leviter prominulis; inflorescentiis axillaribus 3-7-floris, floribus fasciculatis; pedicellis 2-3 mm. longis (basi minute bracteatis) cum bracteis calyceque minute ferrugineo-sericeis; sepalis 5 vel 6 imbricatis ovato-orbicularibus, 2-3 mm. longis et latis, intus minute argenteo-sericeis; corolla glabra alba carnosa campanulata 3-4 mm. longa, lobis 5 oblongis obtusis 1.5 mm. longis et latis; staminodiis oblongis 0.5 mm. longis, apice truncatis; antheris subses-silibus deltoideo-ovatis circiter 0.8 mm. longis; ovario dense hispido globoso sub anthesi 1 mm. diametro, loculis 5, stylo carnoso quam ovario 1-2-plo longiore, stigmate obscure 5-lobato.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description: Arbor ad 20 m. alta, trunco 15 cm. diametro; ramulis subteretibus cinereis rugosis glabris; petiolis nigrescentibus rugosis 10-15 mm. longis; laminis chartaceis glabris oblongis, 14-20 cm. longis, 3-5.5 cm. latis, basi cuneatis vel subattenuatis, apice breviter acuminatis, margine integris, costa utrinque prominente, nervis secundariis utroque 12-16 arcuato-adscendentibus utrinque elevatis, venulis reticulatis utrinque prominulis; inflorescentiis 2-6-floris, floribus fasciculatis; pedicellis 1.5-2 mm. longis dense ferrugineo-pilosis; sepalis 5 (vel 6) oblongo-orbicularibus utrinque arete sericeis, interioribus ad 5 mm. longis et 4 mm. latis; corolla glabra campanulata circiter 6 mm. longa, lobis 5 oblongo-rotundatis circiter 2 mm. longis et latis; staminodiis anguste oblongis quam lobis paullo brevioribus, 0.8 mm. latis; staminibus apice tubi adnatis, filamentis 1 mm. longis, antheris deltoideo-ovatis 1 mm. longis mox deciduis; ovario globoso sub anthesi 1.5 mm. diametro dense pilis ad 1.5 mm. longis hispido, loculis 5, stylo carnoso filiformi 6 mm. longo, stigmate minute 5-lobato.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description: Caespitose terrestrials 40-60 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid to ovoid-oblong, com- pressed, sulcate, obtusely angled, scabrous, 9-12 x 4.5 cm. Leaves elliptic-lanceolate, acute or acuminate, 32-45 x 12-13 cm, the petiole short, channeled. Inflorescences short erect basal scapes, 2-6 per pseudobulb, from mature growths, just exceeding the pseu- dobulb, the peduncle to 17 cm long, 0.6 cm in diam., with several large infundibuliform bracts, the floral bract exceeds the ovary. Sepals and petals clear green, white at base, the labellum yellow, mid-lobe with or without reddish brown short streaks, base of lateral lobes white, the column and anther white. Dorsal sepal oblanceolate to oblong- oblanceolate, acute, 6.5-7.0 x 2.4-2.5 cm. Lateral sepals obliquely elliptic-ovate, fal- cate, blunt, 6.0 x 2.3-3.0 cm. Petals oblanceolate, lightly oblique, acute, 5.4-5.6 x 1.6- 1.8 cm. Labellum strongly 3-lobed, 5.6-6.0 x 2.5 cm, the lateral lobes obliquely ovate, acute, erect, involute, the mid-lobe oblong, the emarginate apex strongly deflexed, the mid-lobe margin shallowly lacerate diminishing towards the apex, the claw long with three conspicuous ribs continuing to callus apex, near the middle of disc two marginal ribs arise each soon dividing into a distinct separate pair which are abruptly divergent to the lateral margins well below the apex of the central ribs, the callus border distinctly obtuse-angled near the truncate to shallowly retuse apex. Column arcuate, 5.0 x 0.9 cm, a thick keel below, the lateral margins cord-like thickened from base to just below the anther, basal half and foot with fine, sparse pubescence, the anther bell shaped, 5.8 x 2.2 mm, the pollinarium 4.5 x 4.5 mm, the pollinia 4 in two unequal pairs, subrhombic-obovate, compressed, convex-concave, the larger 2.8 x 1.8 mm, the smaller 1.8 x 1.3 mm, the stipe 4.25 mm long, 1 mm broad across the union with pollinia, attenuate below, the viscidium widely transverse, saggitate, 0.18 mm long, 2.5 mm broad.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, D. & Christenson, E. A. 1994. New species of Peruvian Orchidaceae II. Brittonia. 46: 228-259.

description: Large, robust, caespitose terrestrials with scape subequalling the leaves. Pseudobulbs ovoid-oblong, sulcate, 7-10 cm long. Leaves lanceolate, acute, 80-95 x 18-21 cm, subcoriaceous, the petioles channeled. Inflo- rescences elongate erect scapes, the peduncle terete, 75-90 cm long, with 5-6 distant, lanceolate, acuminate bracts 9-1 1 cm long, the floral bract very large, far exceeding the dorsal sepal, ovate-triangular to lanceolate, acuminate, to 13.5 cm long, the margin sparsely, evenly denticulate. Flowers very fleshy, apices of sepals and petals conduplicate with thick, carinate tips, color not recorded by collectors. Dorsal sepal lanceo- late, 7.5 x 1.85 cm, the apex curved upwards slightly. Lateral sepals obliquely lanceolate, 9 x 2.1 cm, basally adnate to and forming a short mentum with the column foot. Petals obliquely elliptic-lanceolate, 6.6 x 1.9 cm. Labellum 3-lobed, 4.9-5.0 cm long when expanded, 2.25 cm across the lateral lobes, the lateral lobes obliquely el- liptic-ovate, erect, entire, the mid-lobe ovate, recurved near the middle, apex deeply emarginate, margins completely serrate dentate, the callus oblong-pandurate in outline, constricted above the middle with laterally compressed sides, apex retuse with upturned, concave margins, the mid-rib extends to the apex with 2 lateral ribs nearly as long, the claw with 7 nerves thickening into 7 ribs or keels above, 2 of which diminish leaving 5 near the middle including the compressed sides. Column convex, arcuate dorsally, with a low ventral keel extending nearly to the dilated base and foot, pubescent on the basal third to half and on the foot.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, D. & Christenson, E. A. 1994. New species of Peruvian Orchidaceae II. Brittonia. 46: 228-259.

description: Robust caespitose terrestrials 50-60 cm tall. Pseudobulbs narrowly ovoid-oblong, tapered, sulcate, trifoliate, 10-13 cm long. Leaves 3, lanceolate, acuminate, 40-45 x 5.5-6.5 cm, with 5 pale green ribs (inner 3 thicker), narrowed below to a short, channeled petiole. Inflorescence 1-2 erect, basal scapes, the peduncle 25-36 cm tall, terete, with 5-6 distant, tubular, loose bracts, the floral bract ovate-triangular, far exceeding the ovary, to 5.5 cm long. Sepals and petals green, the labellum yellowish green, the column pale green. Dorsal sepal narrowly elliptic-oblong, shortly acuminate, concave, arcuate, 5-veined, 4.8 x 1.8 cm. Lateral sepals elliptic, acute, falcate, recurved, con- cave, 7-veined, 4.8 x 1.8 when expanded, connate bases adnate to the column foot forming a complanate mentum. Petals obliquely elliptic-oblanceolate, subacute, lightly recurved, 7-veined, 5.5 x 2.1 cm. Labellum sharply 3-lobed, cuneate, arcuate, 6.3 x 2.0 cm, the lateral lobes obliquely elliptic-ovate, erect, incurved, the mid-lobe ovate, abruptly acute, 17-19 veined, the margins densely covered with a tangled mat of long, branched, flexuous trichomes, the callus fleshy, 4-lobulate, rhombic, at the junction of the mid-lobe with the lateral lobes, with the disc 7-ribbed at the base becoming 3-ribbed by the merging of two outer pairs and the elimination of the ribs directly to either side of the mid-rib, the mid-rib continuing to the apex of the callus, the base of the labellum adnate to the column foot forming a compressed sac. Col- umn arcuate, 4.6 cm long, 1.0 cm across the base, sparsely pubescent on the middle abaxial surface of the column and foot, the anther 2.6 x 3.3 mm, shaped like a widely flared bell, the pollinia 4 in two unequal, obovate, compressed pairs, each 3 mm long, the stipe lanceolate, 3 mm long, the viscidium saggitate, 2 mm broad.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, D. & Christenson, E. A. 1994. New species of Peruvian Orchidaceae II. Brittonia. 46: 228-259.

description: Miniature epiphytes to 1 cm tall. Pseudobulbs absent or when present obscure, subtended by 4-6 equitant, imbricate, oblique, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, acute, ancipitous, fleshy foliaceous bracts. Leaf 1, similar to and grading with bracts, 0.4-0.8 x 0.07-0.22 cm, reddish to green, with chartaceous margins. Inflorescences racemose, successively 2-flowered, filiform, axillary, erect, with 4-6 ovate-triangular, acuminate, carinate, distant bracts. Flowers campanulate, pale purple, petals paler and with 3 small purple spots, the labellum pale rose-purple, the column rose-pink, the anther white and basally dark red-purple, stipe white, pollinia yellow, viscidium light brown. Sepals subsimilar, oblong-lanceolate, acute, concave, 0.3 x 0.1 cm, the lat- eral sepals oblanceolate, oblique, acuminate. Petals oblanceolate, acuminate, shorter than the sepals. Labellum clawed, lamina ovate, attenuate, acute to obtuse, margin undulate. Column stipitate, clavate, straight, typical for the genus. Pollinarium long triangular; pollinia 2, obovate, compressed, attached to the stipe by slender caudicles, 0.08 x 0.03 cm.

description: Small, psygmoid, twig epiphytes to 6 tall and broad. Leaves sigmoid, conduplicate basally, bilaterally compressed apically, distichous, imbricate, glabrous, 2.5 x 0.6 cm. Inflorescences sequential from leaf axils, 6- 7-flowered subumbels subsequently followed by lateral branches arising just below the primary rachis, the peduncles filiform with 2-4 subremote lanceolate bracts. Flowers with sepals dull white tinted purple apically, the petals basally white with 3-4 broad, rose-purple transverse bands, dark purple above, the labellum claw white, rose-purple above, the column base yellowish, above pale yellowish lavender, the anther white and pale lavender, the pollinia cream-yellow on a white stipe. Sepals similar, lanceolate, long acuminate, 15-16 x 1.8 mm, the lateral sepals fused shortly at base. Petals obliquely lanceolate, curved and recurved above the middle, 12 x 1 mm. Labellum 3-lobed, the claw dilated, stout, with a thick clavate callus, the basal lobes auric- ulate, retrorse, separated from the mid-lobe by a conspicuous claw with evenly incurved, slightly revolute margins, the midlobe elliptic, long acuminate, basal margins serrulate, 10 x 2.5 mm. Column short, api- cally dilated in 3 fleshy lobes, the anther bed raised along the middle with a subcrenulate ridge, 5.5 mm long, 1.4 mm broad across the apex; stigma elongate, narrowly lanceolate in outline; anther apex scrotiform, base slipper-shaped, 2.7 x 1 mm; pollinarium 2.8 x 0.4 mm, the stipe margins lightly revolute, strongly tapered below to the cordiform viscidium, the pollinia 2, equal, turbinate, complanate.

description: Plants terrestrial, small, 8.5-9 cm tall, cormous, 1-leaved; the old corm obovoid, drying pale green, enveloped by the papery white remnants of old leaf sheaths and bases. Sheath 1, finely-veined, 1.5-2 cm long, tubular, glabrous, drying papery thin, whitish gray, the margin entire. Leaf 1, long- petiolate; petioles 3.5-5.5 cm long, tubular, narrowly compressed around scape, slen- der; blades ascending at 45-60, ovate to subcordate, 2.4-2.8 cm long, 1.7-1.9 cm broad, drying medium green, the margin entire. Scape from the old corm, encircled by the petiole, the emergent portion 3-4 cm long, erect or slightly curved apically. Inflorescence subumbellate, 5-9-flowered. Floral bracts lanceolate, 2-3 mm long, acute, conduplicate, chartaceous, persistent. Ovary filiform 5-6 mm long, slightly swollen at the apex; pedicels straight, apparently not twisted. Flowers small, 5-6 mm long, non- resupinate, yellowish-green with some dark markings at the base of the lip. Sepals free, elliptic, ca. 2.5 mm long, ca. 1 mm broad, acute at apex, reflexed, coiled, yellowish- green. Petals linear, ca. 2 mm long, 1-nerved, coiled. Lip sagittate, 6-7 mm long, the apex long-acuminate, deflexed, the base with 2 concavities separated by a dark raised keel, with two ear-like flaps on either side of the concavities, the basal lobes retrorse, prolonged 1.5-2 mm long, narrowly triangular with narrow filiform, often twisted, apices. Column short, stout, ca. 1 mm long, about as wide as long, subquadrate, thick, fleshy, dark green. Clinandrium simple, unwinged and untoothed. Anther short, with 2, closely adjacent thecae. Pollinaria 2, each formed by two unequal fused pollinia. Stigma transversely broadly elliptic, the surface flat to slightly concave. Capsule not seen.

description: Terrestrial herb, 15 cm tall including the inflorescence. Roots numerous, simple, slender, long pilose, produced from the base of the pseudobulb, to 2 cm long, ca. 0.5 mm diam. Pseudobulb apparently epigeous, subglobose, ca. 1 cm diam., when young concealed by a tubular, whitish, rounded sheath 2 cm long, ca. 4.5 mm diam., the sheath disintegrating into fibers with age. Leaves 2, short-petiolate; petioles tubular, 2.5 cm long, 3-4 mm diam.; blades opposite, spreading, broadly ovate-cordiform, acute to broadly obtuse, very thin and translucent (in dried condition), 4 X 3-4 cm. Inflorescence long-pedunculate, ca. 14.5 cm long including the short, subumbellate raceme, the latter ca. 13 mm long, 18 mm diam., producing up to ca. 40 flowers in succession, ca. 10 flowers open at a time; peduncle several-angled, 1.2 mm diam. Floral bracts spreading, green, trian- gular, slightly concave, 1-veined, 1.5-2 X 1- 1.3 mm. Flowers small for the genus (open perianth ca. 5 mm maximum length), green, not resupinate, with sparse raphide containing idioblasts on the floral segments and the column. Ovary straight, spreading, twisted near the base, 6-angled, 6-7 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm diam. Dorsal sepal widely spreading, appressed against the ovary, convex, elliptic ovate, rounded, 3-veined, with recurved margins, 2.6 X 1 mm. Lateral sepals widely spreading, convex, short-connate ca. 0.2 mm at the base, obliquely elliptic-ovate, rounded, 3-veined, with recurved margins, 2.5 X 1.3 mm. Petals strongly recurved, convex, linear, slightly falcate, acute, 1-veined, with recurved margins, 1.8 X 0.2 mm. Lip 3-lobed, deeply concave, ca. 1.5 X 1.5 mm excluding the basal lobes; cavity limited by a fleshy, raised ridge and ± divided into 2 portions by a slightly thickened longitudinal median ridge, covered toward the base by a translucent, transversely oblong membrane originally hidden under the column; basal lobes retrorse, in natural position erect, embracing the column, their apices convergent, when flattened divergent, narrowly triangular, attenu- ate, distally uncinate, ca. 1.5 mm X long ca. 0.5 mm wide at the base; apical lobe entire, triangular, rounded, slightly recurved, ca. 0.6 mm long. Column very short, wider than long, obtrapezoid, truncate, dorsiventrally compressed, ca. 0.5 X 0.8 mm, provided at each side with an antrorse, triangular, acute auricle. Anther dorsal, erect, 2-celled, yellow, wider than long. Pollinia 2, yellow, translucent, obliquely ovate-oblong, dorsiventrally compressed, each with an inconspicuous apical viscidium. Stigma subapical, transversely elliptic, disposed in an oblique plane with respect to the longitudinal axis of the column. Capsule unknown.

Leaf blades 5-18.5 X 2.4-10.5 cm, narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, membranaceous; upper surface very sparsely to glabrate, glandular at the base of the midrib; lower surface densely tomentose to tomentulose, rarely glabrate; apex acuminate; base obtuse to obscurely cordate; petioles 2-5 mm. Inflorescences usually shorter than the subtending leaves, glabrous, 5-11-flowered; peduncles 1-3.8(-12) cm; pedicels 0.6-1.4 cm; bracts 3-5 mm long, linear, scarious. Sepals 6-11 mm, narrowly ovate, acute to obtuse, foliaceous. Corollas salverform, yellowish, glabrous without; tube 1.3-1.9 cm x ca. 3 mm, straight; lobes 4.5-10 X 5-6.5 mm, obovate, spreading to somewhat reflexed. Stamens inserted near the orifice of the tube; anthers ca. 5 mm. Ovary ca. 1 mm long, glabrous; style 5-8 mm long; disk glands 1 mm long, distinct. Follicles 20.5-25.5 X 0.3-0.5 cm, glabrous, lenticellate. Seeds 9-10 mm.

description: Lianas; stems terete to subterete, sparsely puberulent to glabrate. Leaf blades 2.6-12(-13.8) X 1-5.2(-7.1) cm, elliptic, to narrowly elliptic, rarely obovate, membranaceous; upper surface sparsely puberulent to glabrate, glandular at the base of the midrib; lower surface densely tomentose to sparsely puberulent, rarely glabrate; apex acuminate to long-acuminate; base obscurely cordate; petioles 2-11 mm. Inflorescences shorter or longer than the subtending leaves, glabrous, 8-55-flowered, congested; peduncles 0.4-4.7 cm; pedicels 0.3-1 cm; bracts 3-4 mm long, scarious. Corollas salverform, greenish yellow, glabrous without; tube 0.5-0.8 cm X 2.5-4 mm, straight; lobes 3-5 x 2-2.5 mm, obovate, erect and inconspicuous. Stamens inserted near the orifice of the tube; anthers ca. 4 mm. Ovary ca. 2 mm long, glabrous; style 1-2 mm long; disk glands 2-2.5 mm long, distinct. Follicles 13.8 X 24.1 X 0.35-0.45 cm, falcate. Seeds 7-8 mm.

description: Lianas; stems terete, glabrous to glabrate, rarely sparsely puberulent. Leaf blades 2.1-6.4 x 0.5-2.6 cm, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, membranaceous, usually glabrous, rarely puberulent on the lower surface; apex acute, acuminate to mucronate; base obtuse to obscurely cordate, upper surface inconspicuously glandular at the base of the midrib, sometimes eglandular; petioles 1-7 mm. Inflorescences about as long as the subtending leaves, glabrous, 2-1 1-flowered; peduncles 0.2-0.6 cm; pedicels 0.2- 0.9 cm; bracts 2-4 mm long, scarious. description: Lianas; stems terete to subterete, densely puberulent to glabrate. Leaf blades 2-11 X 0.7-4.5(-6.5) cm, elliptic, very narrowly elliptic, ovate to narrowly ovate, membranaceous; upper surface very sparsely puberulent to glabrate, glandular at the base of the midrib; lower surface densely tomentose or tomentulose, rarely glabrate on both surfaces; apex acuminate to long-acuminate; base cordate, rarely obtuse; petioles 4-27 mm. description: Lianas; stems terete, sparsely puberulent when young, turning glabrate. Leaf blades 6.5-12.8 X (1.8-)3-6(-7.5) cm, elliptic, narrowly ovate to ovate, membranaceous; upper surface glabrate, glandular at the base of the midrib; lower surface sparsely puberulent along the midrib to glabrate; apex long-acuminate; base broadly cordate; petioles 13-30(-41) mm. Inflorescences usually longer than the subtending leaves, glabrous, 1-7(-10)-flowered; peduncles (0.5-) 1.5-3.3 cm; pedicels 0.7-3 cm; bracts 1-2.5 mm long, scarious. Sepals 4-6 mm, ovate, acute. Corollas infundibuliform, purple to lilac, rarely yellow, the throat yellowish within, glabrous without; lower part of tube 1.9-3.1 X ca. 1.5 cm, straight; upper part 1-1.2 cm long, 7-11 mm diam. at the orifice, conic; lobes 2.3-3.1 X 1.6-2 cm, obovate, spreading. Stamens inserted near the orifice of the tube; anthers 5.5-7 mm. Ovary 2.5-3 mm long, glabrous; style 19-24 mm long; disk glands 1.5-2 mm long, distinct. description: Lianas; stems terete, sparsely pilose to glabrate. Leaf blades (2.2-)4-7.5 x 2-4 cm, elliptic, narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, membranaceous; upper surface sparsely puberulent to glabrate, glandular along the midrib; lower surface pilose, rarely glabrate; apex acute to acuminate; base obtuse, obscurely cordate to auriculate; petioles 6-12 mm. Inflorescences about as long as the subtending leaves, glabrous, 7-16-flowered; peduncles 0.8-2 cm; pedicels 0.2-0.4 cm; bracts 12-29(-35) mm long, foliaceous. Stamens inserted near the orifice of the tube; anthers 3-4 mm. Ovary 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous; style 18-21 mm long; disk glands ca. 1 mm, distinct to somewhat connate at the base. description: Herba erecta omnino glaberrima usque 1-metralis, caulibus virgatis simplicibus vel superne ramosis acutate quadrangularibus; foliis linearibus acutis vel acuminatis 1-2 cm longis 1.5-2.5 mm latis; inflorescentia terminali cymoso-paniculata laxiflora 7-16 cm longa 4-8 cm lata; hypanthio breviter cylindrico 3.5 mm longo 2 mm lato; calyce 2.5-3.5 mm longo, ad basim 4-lobato, lobis lanceolatis subacutis 2.5-3.5 mm longis 1-1.5 mm latis; corolla scarlatina cylindrica 16 mm longa.

description: Erect herb, up to 1 meter tall, completely glabrous; stem virgate, acutely quadrangular, internodes elongated, 12-25 cm long; leaf pairs few, much reduced, linear, acute to acuminate, 1-2 cm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, 1-nerved, midnerve elevated below; inflorescence terminal, erect, loosely flowered, cymose-paniculate, 7-16 cm long, 4-8 cm broad; flowers pedicellate, pedicels erect-ascending, 5-15 mm long; calyx and hypanthium 6-7 mm long, glabrous; hypanthium shortly cylindric, 3.5 mm long, 2 mm wide; calyx 2.5-3.5 mm long, 4-lobed to the base; lobes lanceolate, subacute, 2.5-3.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, a setiform appendage with glandular processes present within at the base of the sinuses between the lobes; corolla scarlet, cylindric, 16 mm long, tube 14 mm long, 2 mm wide at base, 5.2 mm wide at orifice, tube glabrous without, 2 mm above the base with a pilose portion 1.5 mm long, elsewhere glabrous, lobes broadly ovate, subacute or obtusish, 4 mm long, 3 mm wide; anthers oblong, 3 mm long; filaments 1 mm long, inserted 7 mm above base of corolla-tube; style 14 mm long; immature capsule oblong-turbinate, 8-10 mm long, 4-5 mm wide; seeds membranous, reticulate.

description: Arbor glabra 6 m alta, 6 cm diametro, ramis longis debiliter porrectis; folia fere ad basin 5-lobata, angustissime peltata (etiam foliis maximis vix 1 mm); laminae 8-16 cm longae, 8-22 (-27) cm latae, lobis centralibus 3 integris sinuatis ellipticis, oblongis obovatisve, 2-5.5 cm latis, 5-14 cm longis, basi 8-20 mm latis sinibus angustis, apice anguste acuminatis, in setam 1-2 mm longam desinentibus; lobae infimae plusminusve reflexae, 2-8 cm longae, saepe falcatae inaequalesque, lobis centralibus duplo breviores; petioli ad 17 cm longi, saepe laminis longiores; stipulae ad 2.5 mm longae, lobulis angustis adscendentibus; racemus (4-) 6-16 cm longus, prope basin floribus ! 1-3 (tempore anthesis non vidi), pedicellis 3-6 (-10) mm longis; flores [male] ad 40, flavi ["clear pale yellow"], campanulati, 17-18 mm longi, calycis lobis patentibus late cordatis, late obtuseque acutatis breviacuminatisque, 7-8 mm longis, 7-10 mm latis, loborum vicinorum marginibus basilaribus paulum coalitis et ad calycis medium auriculas eminentes efficientibus; alabastra valde longitudinaliter 5-jugata et lateribus auriculatis; filamenta majora calycis lobis opposita, 13 mm longa; filamenta filiformia 8-9 mm longa; antherae 3-3.5 mm longae; glandula annularis, 10-dentata, 3-3.5 mm lata; fructus et semina ignoti.

description:
Arbor tenuis 5 m alta, inflorescentia ramulisque arachnoideo-tomentosis, dealbatis vel fulvescentibus; folia 5-lobata vel parviora 3-lobata, anguste peltata (foliis majoribus 3-4 mm), glabra vel praecipue juvenilia arachnoideovillosa, subtus glauca; laminae 7-9 (-12.5) cm longae, 9-12 (-19) cm latae, lobis oblongis ellipticis obovatisve, integris, rotundatis vel late acutis, plerumque mucronatis vel breviacuminatis, se ad folii basin distantiae dodrans extendentibus; lobus centralis 2.5-5 cm latus, 4-10 cm longus, basi 8-16 mm latus, sinibus angustis; lobi infimi patentes vel paulum reflexi; petioli 6-17 cm longi, superne arachnoideo-villosi, laminis saepe satis longiores; stipulae triangulares, 4 mm longae, basi 1.5 mm latae, chartaceae, mox deciduae; panicula angusta 10-12 cm longa, saepe ramo axillari superata et primo aspectu ut videtur supra-axillaris, ramis praecipuis 2-5 cm longis, paucifloris, bracteis parvis scariosis instructis; flores S campanulati, extus sparse puberulentes, flavi, 8-9 mm longi, lobis rotundato-deltoideis 4-5 mm longis, pedicellis 2-4 mm longis; calyx intus utroque latere loborum costae lacuna concava instructus; filamenta majora calycis lobis opposita, 8 mm longa; filamenta filiformia 5 mm longa, antherae 2 mm longae; glandula flava, disciformis, 3.5-4 mm diametro, lobulis 5 praecipuis ad medium bipartitis, cum calycis lobis alternantibus; flores 9, fructus et semina ignoti.

description: Inter congeneras stipulis obtusis parvis, margine eciliatis instructas foliis obovatis vel oblanceolatis, apice abrupte acuminatis noscenda. Frutex glaber, 1.75 m altus. Rami novelli 2.5 mm diam., mox cortice primum brunneo, lenticellis conspicue albo-punctato, deinde griseo vestiti, internodiis 1.5-7 cm longis. Folia sensim in petiolum 1-2 cm longum contracta; lamina obovata vel oblanceolata, 6.5-16 cm longa et 3-7 cm lata, apice abrupte acuminata, basi sensim contracta, utrimque opaca, sicc. grisea, costa nervisque supra prominulis, subtus prominentibus, venulis paucis et vix conspicuis, acarodomatiis nullis, nervis utroque latere costae 6 vel 7. Stipulae ovato-orbiculares, obtusae, margine eciliatae, 3 mm longae. Inflorescentia pedunculo 2-4.5 cm longo elata, corymbiformis, 4-7.5 cm diam. et 2-3.5 cm alta; ramuli infimi quaterni. Bracteae minutae et mox deciduae. Flores centrales dichasiorum sessiles, laterales pedicellis usque ad 2 mm longis elati. Calyx cupularis 1.2 mm altus, margine truncatus vel vix notabile 5-denticulatus. Corolla alba, tubo 4 mm alto, intus glabro, lobis 3 mm longis. Filamenta floris brachystyli 2.5 mm longa; antherae 1.5 mm longae, apice basique obtusae. Granula pollinis 3-porata 50 / diam. (aliquae 4-porata). Stylus floris brachystyli 2 mm longus; stigmata 1.5 mm longa. Drupa nondum visa.

description: Frutex bimetralis, foliis pendulis, valde revolutis, subtus viridi-griseis velutinis, supra glabratis vix punctatis fere eveniis; laminae anguste elliptico-lineares, utrinque anguste acutae, 4-7 cm longae, 6- 10 mm latae; petioli 4-5 mm longi velutini; paniculae perbreves griseae, 1-1.5 cm longae vel breviores, 1-4-florae, floribus racemosis oppositis sessilibus, bracteis 1 mm longis suffultis; alabastra ut videtur 3 mm longa, hypanthio breve campanulato 2 mm longo, dense cano-piloso; calyx pilosus non calyp- triformis, lobis 3-4 valde irregularibus inaequalibusque subcarnosis sub anthesi incurvis; petala 4-5 subaequalia, extus pilosa, suborbicularia vel rhomboidalia, 2.5 mm longa, apice ciliata, conspicue glandulosa; stamina ca 75, tubo hypanthii conico crebre insidentia; stylus 3 mm longus crassus, stigmate punctiforme; ovarium 2- vel imperfecte 3-loculare, loculis 2-ovulatis, vel loculo uno 3-ovu- lato, vel loculo tertio 1-ovulato; fructus seminaque desunt.

description: Shrub 2 m tall with slender gray branches; leaves subcoriaceous, drooping, strongly revolute, narrowly elliptic-linear, acute at both ends, 4-7 cm long, 6-10 mm wide, glabrate above, dull gray green above, gray-velutinous below, scarcely punctate; petioles 4-5 mm long; inflorescence drooping, grayish, very short, 1-4-flowered, 1-1.5 cm long; flowers racemose, opposite, sessile; rachis densely canescent; bracts 1 mm long; hypanthium shortly campanulate, densely gray- pilose, 2 mm long; calyx not calyptriform, pilose, lobes 3-4, subcarnose, manifestly irregular and unequal, incurved toward anthesis; petals subequal, 4-5, sub- orbicular or rhomboidal, 2.5 mm long, ciliate at apex, conspicuously glandular, pilose without; stamens ca 75, closely situated on the conical tube of the hypan- thium; style fleshy, 3 mm long; stigma punctiform; ovary 2- or imperfectly 3-celled, locules 2-ovulate, or one locule 3-ovulate, or a third locule 1-ovulate; fruit and seeds lacking.

description: Caespitose epiphytes to 25 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid-pyriform, complanate, 3 x 1 cm, unifoliate or rarely bifoliate, sub- tended by a series of imbricate, distichous, scarious bracts. Leaves 1-2, oblong-lanceo- late, acute, stiff, dark green, 10-20 x 1-1.5 cm, conduplicate at the petiolate base. Inflorescences erect basal scapes, 11-12 cm long, 0.2 cm in diam., subtended by 3 tu- bular, acuminate bracts, the floral bract subsimilar, subequal to the ovary. Flowers cam- panulate, the sepals and petals pale yellow, the labellum pale yellow with the apex carrot-orange with purple veins, the callus pale yellow with a carrot-orange apex, the column white and pale green with short, purple streaks ventrally, the anther bronze-green with crystalline papillae, the pollinia golden yellow, the viscidium tan. Sepals narrowly lanceolate, acute, carinate, 28 x 6 mm, the lateral sepals oblique and briefly connate at base. Petals linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 25 x 4 mm. Labellum 3-lobed, 15 x 4 mm when expanded, the lateral lobes obliquely ovate, obtuse, erect, the midlobe oblong, obtuse, dorsoventrally thickened, the dorsal thickening tomentose, the callus a raised longitudinal ridge half the length of the labellum, dilated at the apex, the margins hirsute. Column stout, nearly straight, clavate, 12 x 2.8 mm in profile, the clinandrium evenly and deeply fringed. Anther ornate  with a prominent central and two lateral papillate ridges, 3 x 2.5 mm, the pollinar- ium 2 x 1 mm, the pollinia 4, compressed, in two unequal pairs, the larger pair 1.5 x 0.5 mm, the viscidium semilunate.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, David E. & Christenson, Eric A. 1995. New species of Peruvian Orchidaceae III. Brittonia. 47: 182-209.

description:
Caespitose terrestrials 20-23 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ellipsoid-ovoid, strongly compressed, unifoliate, to 4.2 x 1.2 cm, subtended by imbricate, distichous bracts, the 2 uppermost bracts foliaceous with lamina to 9 x 1 cm. Leaf 1, linear-oblong, gradually tapered, sharply petiolate at the conduplicate base, obliquely bilobed, coriaceous, 11- 13 x 1.3 cm, dark green, the petiole offset on the pseudobulb. Inflorescences basal scapes to 8.0 cm long, concealed by imbri- cating, tubular, acute bracts, the floral bract similar, subinflated, subequal to the ovary. Flowers not resupinate, campanulate to par- tially closed, sepals and petals pale salmon with darker veins, the labellum lateral lobes salmon, the midlobe darker tannish salmon, the surface marked with irregular elongate markings, the column white tinged with red on the dorsal surface, the anther white. Sepals subsimilar, oblong, subacute, fleshy, 2.8-3 x 1 cm, the lateral sepals oblique.

Petals lanceolate, oblique, acute, 2.5 x 0.68 cm. Labellum 3-lobed, 1.6 x 0.9 cm when expanded, the lateral lobes erect with involute margins, obliquely subquadrate, the midlobe triangular, acute, with the apex slightly deflexed, the callus basal, elliptic, obtuse, to half the length of the labellum, with a hemispheric, darker crater at base of midlobe. Column lightly arcuate at apex, semiterete, 1.54 cm long with foot, the clinandrium unadorned. Anther 2.6 x 2.8 mm, with a median unadorned crest, the pollinarium 2 x 1.4 mm, the pollinia 4 in two unequal pairs, sessile on a small semilunate viscidium.

description: Caespitose epiphytes 60-70 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid-pyriform, sulcate in age, 4 x 2 cm, subtended by a series of distichous, imbricating, scarious, lanceolate bracts, the uppermost about twice the length of the pseudobulb. Leaves linear-lanceolate, attenuate to the conduplicate, briefly petiolate base, obliquely bilobed, 43-60 X 2.5-4 cm. Inflorescences basal scapes to 13 cm long, 2 mm diam., with several large, inflated, tubular, ovate, obtuse bracts, the floral bract subsimilar, slightly shorter than the ovary, 2.6 X 0.6 cm. Flowers campanulate, the sepals tannish yellow, exterior surface with maroon lines on the basal half, petals with distal half white, below heavily striped maroon-purple, labellum with lateral lobes whitish tinted purple with 3-4 maroon stripes on the exterior not reaching to the apical margin, the interior with 6 broad stripes for the entire length of each lobe, the midlobe nearly entirely dark yellow, the narrow exterior glabrous margin purple, the callus dull cream-yellow, the column intense purple with some white on the distal margin, the foot intense purple in the center with white outer margins, the anther offwhite, the viscidium white in the middle with purple lobes, the pollinia golden-yellow, the scape and ovary intense maroonpurple, the bracts and floral bract applegreen with maroon-purple spots. Sepals elliptic, abruptly acute, rounded, basally concave, apices briefly recurved, 2.2 X 1.4-1.5 cm, the lateral sepals divergent. Petals obliquely ovate, cuneate, subacuminate, the lower margins irregular, concave, apices briefly recurved, held parallel to the column, 2.1 X 1 cm. Labellum 3-lobed, 1.8 X 1.2 cm when expanded, the lateral lobes erect, involute, obliquely elliptic-obovate, obtuse, the midlobe oblong, rounded, retuse, sparsely hyaline pubescent, the apex deflexed, the apical margins inflexed, the callus an oblanceolate tomentose rounded ridge to below the middle. Column arcuate, stout, 15 X 3 mm, the foot 7 mm long. Anther helmet-shaped with a high dorsal keel, 4 X 4 mm, the basal margin ciliate, the pollinarium 4 X 3.5 mm, the viscidium semilunate, 3 X 3.5 mm, the pollinia 4 in 2 unequal compressed pairs, the larger pair 2.5 X 1.2 mm. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, David E. 1998. New species of Peruvian Orchidaceae IV. Brittonia. 50: 186-191.

description: Epiphytic herbs, cespitose, 25-30 cm tall. Rhizome abbreviated, clothed by scarious sheaths; pseudobulbs clustered, 2.5-4 cm tall, 1-1.5 cm wide and thick, ovoid or ovoid-ellipsoid, section circular, hence pseudobulbs subconical; 1-leaved apically, surface shiny, longitudinally many-ridged, then transversally closely and shallowly ridged, suggesting a network pattern, dull dark green but tinged with dull dark maroon basally in older pseudobulbs; sheaths enveloping the pseudobulb bladeless. Leaves 24-27 X 2-3 cm, erect on the pseudobulb, coriaceous, elliptic or rarely ovateelliptic, acute, pseudopetiolate; pseudopetiole 20-35 X 4-6 mm, deeply channeled on the ventral face, in transverse section elliptic. Inflorescences erect, shorter than pseudobulb; peduncle 8-12 mm long, terete. Floral bract 17-21 X 11-1.5 mm, broadly obovate or broadly obovate-elliptic, obtuse, apex mucronate, the mucro 1 mm long, basally loosely tubular, open at the apical half and inflated; ovary with pedicel 14-19 mm long, terete, shallowly ridged. Flowers deep dull red-maroon, the petals paler with a yellowish cast, lip dark redmaroon, apex dull deep yellow, column dull pale cream-yellow; resupinate, lasting 4-6 days. Sepals with 2-3 thick nerves at each side of midnerve, and 2-3 faint others, subfleshy; dorsal sepal 15-16 X 6.5-7 mm, oblong-elliptic, apex obtuse-rounded, in natural position slightly concave and subparallel to the column, margins obscurely revolute; lateral sepals 15-17 X 5-6 mm, oblong, slightly oblique, apex obtuse or obtuse- rounded, margins revolute, widely spreading in natural position; petals 14-15 X 4.5-5 mm, narrowly obovate or narrowly obovate-oblong, apex rounded or obtuserounded, 5-7-nerved, margins somewhat revolute; subparallel to column in natural position. Lip 14-16 mm long, 7.5-8.5 mm wide between the forcefully expanded apices of the lateral lobes, mid-lobe 7.5-9 mm long, 4.5-5.5 mm wide at apex, subquadrate-oblong or subquadrate-pandurate, somewhat expanded apically, apex subtruncate, shallowly emarginate; lateral lobes 1-1.5 mm long, ca. 1 mm wide at base, falcateuncinate, acute, emerging just below the middle portion of the lip; basal margins of the lip diverging at an 35-45º angle from the longitudinal axis of the lip; disk bearing a farinose yellow callus reaching midlength of midlobe, thicker at base and at the insertion of the lateral lobes. Column 8-10 mm long, 4-5 mm wide near the apex where broadly winged, hemiterete or somewhat dorsiventrally compressed in cross section at mid-length, arcuate; column-foot 4-5 mm long. Anther 2.5-3 X 1.5 mm, surface smooth; pollinarium typical of the M. rufescens group.

description: Epiphytes to 41 cm tall. Pseudobulbs oblong, complanate, ancipitous, 2.8 x 1.1 cm, with the apex oblique, subtended by a series of imbricating distichous bracts, the uppermost foliaceous, the lamina soon deciduous. Leaf 1, linear, acute, 35-38 x 0.4-0.5 cm. Inflorescences subsessile lateral scapes, the peduncle to 2.5 cm long. Flowers cam- panulate, cream-white, the labellum very pale yellow, the anther pale brown. Sepals subsimilar, elliptic-lanceolate, acute, rigid 1.44-1.5 x 0.5-0.55 cm, the dorsal sepal concave, parallel to the column. Petals subsimilar to the sepals, 1.2 x 0.4 cm, parallel to the column. Labellum obscurely 3-lobulate, densely granulate, 1 x 0.4 cm, the lateral lobules oblong, erect, forming a chamber with the petals, the central lobule triangular with a thick, fleshy apex, the cal- lus sulcate with 5 raised nerves, 5.5 x 1 mm. Column arcuate, 9 x 3 mm, the ven- tral surface finely granulate, the clinandri- um edge subpapillose, the base extended in a foot 5 mm long at right angles to the col- umn and labellum. Anther granulate along the central crest and along margins, 2 x 1.8 mm, the pollinarium 3 mm long, the pol- linia 4 in 2 unequal pairs, the larger pair 0.6 x 0.9 mm.

description: Epiphytic herbs, cespitose, often forming large clumps, 20-30 cm tall. Rhizome short, with scarious sheaths; pseudobulbs clustered to shortly creeping, 2.5-4.5 cm tall, 1.5-2.5 cm wide and thick, ovoid or ovoidconic; 1-leaved, surface rugulose to shiny when plump, dull or bright clear green; sheaths enveloping the pseudobulb bladeless. Leaves 20-36 X 2-3.5 cm, erect on the pseudobulb, thinly coriaceous, narrowly elliptic, acute, conspicuously pseudopetiolate; pseudopetiole 25-50(-65) X 4-8 mm, deeply channeled on the ventral face, in transverse section elliptic. Inflorescences erect or more often horizontally patent, 3-5 cm long, shorter to slightly longer than pseudobulb; ovary with pedicel 19-22 mm long, terete, shallowly ridged, longer than the floral bract. Flowers white to cream or pale yellow sometimes turning greenish with age, lip bright yellow-orange to orange, column dull pale cream-yellow or white, resupinate, lasting 4-6 days. Sepals with 2-3 thick nerves at each side of midnerve, and 2-3 faint others, thinly subfleshy; dorsal sepal 17-19 X 7-9 mm, broadly elliptic to broadly oblong-elliptic, apex obtuse-rounded, in natural position slightly concave; lateral sepals 17-20 X 7-9.5 mm, elliptic, slightly oblique, apex obtuse or obtuse-rounded, margins revolute, widely spreading in natural position; petals 15-17 X 6-7 mm, elliptic, apex rounded or obtuse-rounded, 5-7-nerved, subparallel to the column and covering it as a hood. Lip 8-13 mm long, 7-8.5 mm wide between the forcefully expanded apices of the lateral lobes, sigmoid (strongly incurved) in natural position 3-lobed at about the middle, midlobe very fleshy, lanceolate to triangular- lanceolate with a truncate or retuse apex, lateral lobes 1.2-1.5 mm long, erect, relatively long as compared to other members of the complex, falcate-uncinate to porrect, acute; disk bearing a farinose, spathulate yellow callus reaching mid-length of the midlobe, thicker at base and at the insertion of the lateral lobes. Column 8-9 mm long, arcuate, basally clavate, provided with a short foot, basally hemiterete or somewhat dorsiventrally compressed in cross section, winged on the ventral side of the upper half. Capsule ellipsoid, to 2 cm long. Pollinarium typical of the M. rufescens group.

description: Caespitose epiphytes to 35 cm tall. Pseudobulbs oblong-ovoid, complanate, rugose, 5.5 x 2 cm broad, 0.6 cm thick, subtended by imbricating bracts, the upper pair foliaceous with lamina 15 x 1.4 cm. Leaf 1  linear-lanceolate, acute, to 30 x 3 cm, the petiolate base conduplicate. Inflorescences short scapes from the axils of foliaceous bracts, to 8 cm long, 0.15 cm in diam., the bracts tubular, acuminate, lightly inflated, 2.2 cm long, the floral bract subsimilar, exceeding the ovary. Flowers campanulate, the sepals and petals cadmium yellow, the labellum cadmium yellow with the apex and margins rose-purple, the callus pale yellow with a few red-purple spots toward the base, the column white with a few red-purple markings, the anther white. Dorsal sepal broadly lanceolate, acute, concave, 2.5 x 0.8 cm. Lateral sepals oblique, broadly lanceolate, acute, 2.7 x 0.8 cm. Petals lanceo- late-elliptic, acuminate, 2.2 x 0.5 cm. Labellum 3-lobed, densely hirsute, 1.4 x 0.8 cm when expanded, the lateral lobes obliquely obovate, erect, the midlobe oblong, obtuse, convex, apex recurved, the callus a longitudinal elliptic ridge. Column arcuate, 1.2 x 0.3 cm from the side, with a denticulate clinandrial hood, extended in a foot. Anther 3 x 2.5 mm, the pollinia 4 in 2 unequal pairs, the viscidium semilunate.

description: Epiphytic herbs, cespitose or shortly creeping, 8-15 cm tall. Rhizome abbreviated, clothed by scarious sheaths; pseudobulbs clustered, 1-leaved apically, 2-4 cm tall, 0.6-1.5 cm wide and thick but always wider than thick, ellipsoid or oblongoid in outline, section rhombic, surface smooth or shallowly ridged-reticulate, pale yellow-green, sheaths enveloping the pseudobulb bladeless. Leaves 6.5-16 cm X 13-17 mm, erect on the pseudobulb, coriaceous, quite without petiole; blade elliptic or lanceolateelliptic, acute. Inflorescences erect or horizontally patent, shorter than pseudobulb; peduncle 8-12 mm long, terete. Floral bract 11-12 X 6-7 mm, obovate-elliptic, acuminate; ovary with pedicel 16-17 mm long, terete, shallowly ridged. Flowers dull yellow-green; lip yellow with orange-maroon speckles and callus, column pale green, resupinate, lasting 4-6 days. Sepals with 3 nerves at each side of the midnerve and a few cross-veins, subfleshy; dorsal sepal 12.5-13.5 X 6-7 mm, ovate-elliptic, acute, concave in natural position; lateral sepals 12.5-13.5 mm long, ovate, acute, apically mucronulate, spreading in natural position; petals 12.5-13.5 X 3.8-4.2 mm, lanceolate, acute, apically mucronulate, 5-nerved with a few cross-veins, somewhat convex, subparallel to column in natural position. Lip 10.5-11 mm long in natural position, reaching 12 mm when flattened, ca. 7 mm wide between the forcefully expand-ed apices of the lateral lobes; mid-lobe 5.8- 6.2 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide at apex, ovate-oblong-subquadrate, evenly tapering from base to apex, slightly expanded apically where it is folded-convex, apex subtruncate-rounded; lateral lobes 1.2-1.5 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide at base, triangular-ovate, obtuse, erect-uncinate in natural position, emerging from the lower 1/3 of the lip; basal margins of lip smoothly curved downward; disk bearing a narrowly triangular farinose callus that tapers toward midlip where it thickens again. Column 7.5-8 X 3-4 mm, near the apex where it is broadly winged, semiterete or somewhat dorsiventrally compressed in cross-section at mid-length, arcuate; column-foot 2-2.5 mm long. Anther 2.3-2.5 X 2.1 mm, surface smooth; pollinarium typical of the M. rufescens group.

description: Epiphyte; stems elongate, terete, pendulous, with narrowly elliptic, ancipitous, rugulose, monophyllous pseudobulbs, 3.4-4.2 cm long, 1-1.5 cm wide, the upper internodes of the stem shorter than the pseudobulbs, stem and pseudobulbs often covered with the persistent, dried bases of cataphylls and leaves. Leaves subco- riaceous, narrowly obovate to narrowly elliptic, 17-20 cm long, 3-4 cm wide, articulated 4 cm above the base, the apex unequally retuse to emarginate. Inflo- rescences short, 1-flowered scapes borne in the axils of cataphylls on flushes of new growth, the cataphylls conduplicate, 3-4 cm long, 2 cm wide, articulate 2.5- 3 cm above the base, the apex emarginate, recurved, the scapes 4-6 cm long, covered by 4-5 scarious, lanceolate, acute bracts. Flower large, fragrant; sepals white, obovate, 4-4.5 cm long, 2-2.3 cm wide, membranous, the base narrowed, the apex obtuse; petals white, obovate, 3.7-4 cm long, 1.7-2 cm wide, membra- nous, the base narrowed, the apex obtuse, slightly acuminate; lip clear yellow, 3-lobed, 2-2.5 cm long, to 1.3 cm wide when spread, contracted at the base and articulated with the column foot, the disk with a convex, liguliform, efimbriate callus, the lateral lobes erect, round, 4 mm long, the midlobe pendent, lanceolate to ovate, 6 mm long, 5-6 mm wide at the base, acute, serrulate, densely pubescent, slightly caniculate, slightly thick; column 1 cm long, slightly curved, semiterete, slightly winged toward the apex.

description: Caespitose terrestrial to 25 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid, complanate, ancipitous, sulcate, rugose, 6 x 2.5 cm, subtended by several imbricating sheaths, the uppermost fo- liaceous and quickly deciduous. Leaf 1, narrowly oblong, minutely bilobed, 20 x 2.6 cm, offset to one side of pseudobulb apex, with a conduplicate petiole. Inflorescences basal scapes subequalling the leaf, emerging with the new pseudobulb, the peduncle terete, convered by 6-8 close, tubular, acuminate, slightly inflated bracts, the floral bract subequalling the ovary. Flowers campanulate, the sepals and petals yellow, the exterior yellow mottled carmine-red, the interior immaculate, the labellum basally pale yellow, apically reddish brown, the callus dark yellow, the column yellow. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acuminate, apiculate, 3.5 x 0.8 cm, with revolute margins. Lateral sepals obliquely oblong-lanceolate, apiculate, basally connate in a short mentum, 3.6 x 0.8 cm. Petals obliquely lanceolate, falcate,long-acuminate, 3.5 x 0.7 cm. Labellum 3- lobed with the lobes subequal at the apex of the labellum, arcuate, 1.2 x 0.8 cm, the lateral lobes erect, incurved, the callus a longitudinal raised ridge, oblong, dilated at apex, obtuse. Column arcuate, 1.4 cm long, extended into a column foot, with a low clinandrial hood. Anther 3 x 2.8 mm, with a high central keel, the pollinarium 2 x 2 mm, the pollinia 4, subequal, the viscidium semilunate.

description:
Ascending epiphytes 12-20 cm tall. Rhizome pronounced, concealed by 3-4 pairs of distichous, imbricating sheathing bracts, the upper ones foliaceous, the lower ones scarious. Pseudobulbs ovate, compressed, 2 x 0.7 cm, separated by 3-4 cm on rhizome. Leaves 2, lorate, conduplicate basally, obliquely bilobed, 4.5 x 0.6 cm. Inflores- cences short axillary scapes, apparently solitary per axil, the peduncle concealed by 3- 5 imbricating bracts, the floral bract concealing the ovary and base of dorsal sepal.

Flowers campanulate, the sepals white, the lateral sepals with purple spots on basal 1/3, the petals white, the labellum maroon, the callus and center of the midlobe intense yellow, the labellum underside white with a broad maroon border, the column green with a broad purplish streak near the base, the anther bright yellow, the pollinia intense yellow, the stipe white, the viscidium tawny brown. Sepals ovate, acute, subsimilar, carinate, 1.1-1.3 x 5 mm, the dorsal sepal concave, parallel to the column and petals, the lateral sepals concave at base, spreading. Petals obliquely lanceolate, 10 x 3 mm, with a long attenuate claw, narrowed above the middle, the apex oblong, acute. Label- lum very obscurely 3-lobulate, ovate, ob- tuse, concave, thick, clawed, articulate to long column foot, 4.5 x 1.8 mm, the lateral edges erect, the callus comprising a cordi- form thickened plate with a raised central ridge, obtusely rounded in front, an erose margin delineates a shallow, broad, pouch extending from above the middle to near the labellum apex, with the basal margins tuberculate, with the callus and anterior margins of labellum verruculose. Column arcuate, 18 x 6 mm from the side, extended into a prominent foot. Anther 1.2 x 1.2 mm, with a low, granulate central ridge, the pollinarium 1.2 x 1.2 mm, the pollinia 4, in two unequal pairs, the stipe oblong, the viscidium transversely elliptic.

description: Multi-stemmed shrubs, 1-3 m tall, with leaves clustered at the ends of the terminal branchlets; bark smooth, light gray; wood white; young leafy branchlets 1-2 mm thick, terete. Stipules sheathing at base, del- toid at interpetiolar portion, connected to petioles, glabrous to puberulent to pilose outside, densely pilose inside, the free portion 0.5-1 mm long, long-persistent with two petiole scars on the sides, remaining on stem as a tight series of cup-shaped units; colleters absent. Blades 9-28 X 3-7 mm, length:width ratio 3:1 to 4:1, narrowly oblong to narrowly obovate, decurrent at base, rounded at apex, dark green above, pale green below, leathery; margins revolute; drying grayish brown (to olive green-grayish) above; glabrous above, glabrous to puberulent to sparsely pilose below; primary and secondary veins glabrous to puberulent below, visible above, the primary vein prominent below; secondary and tertiary veins sparsely reticulate; petioles 1-4 mm long, 0.4-0.8 mm thick, subterete. Inflorescences axillary, 2 per node, 0.5-2 mm long, 1 (-2)-flowered [commonly solitary flow- ers]; rachis glabrous to sparsely short-pu- bescent; bracteoles subtending the flowers narrowly lanceolate, 2-4 mm long. Flowers short-pedicellate; pedicels 1-2 mm long, thickening in mature capsules. Calyx mem- branaceous, 4-lobed, usually two opposite lobes larger than the other two, the two larger lobes obovate, 1.5-4 mm long, the smaller lobes rounded, 0.5-1 mm long, rarely rotate and faintly lobed, 2.5-6.5 mm long, glabrous to sparsely minute-puberu- lent. Corolla shortly funnelform, deeply lobed, 4.5-6 mm long, white, glabrous throughout; tube narrowly tubular, 2.5-3.5 X 0.6-0.8 mm, with annular thickening at orifice; lobes 4-5, imbricate in bud, rounded, 2.5-3 X 2.5-3 mm, thick (not membranous). Stamens 4-5, mostly included (only tips exserted), of equal length, subsessile, attached to the tube near the mouth; filaments 0.3-0.5 mm long; anthers narrowly oblong, 2.1-2.7 X 0.3-0.4 mm, dorsifixed near the base. Style exserted, 4.5-5.5 mm long, microscopically costate, glabrous; style branches broadly ovate, 0.2-0.3 mm long. Capsules narrowly oblong-obconical and multi-costate, decurrent at base, 6-8 X 1.5-2 mm, dark brown, sparsely minutely puberulent, bilocular, with 2-7 seeds per locule; persistent calyx usually breaking off at capsule maturity. Seeds peltate, vertical, linear-lanceolate, 2.5-3.5 X 0.3-0.5 mm, tricostate, with central hilum, with central narrowly ellipsoid endosperm, bipolar-winged.

description: Multi-stemmed shrubs, 1-3 m tall, with leaves clustered at the ends of the terminal branchlets; bark smooth, light gray; wood white; young leafy branchlets 1-2 mm thick, terete. Stipules sheathing at base, deltoid at interpetiolar portion, connected to petioles, glabrous outside, basally pilose inside, the free portion 1-2 mm long, long-persistent with two petiole scars on the sides, remaining on stem as a tight series of cup-shaped units; with or without 1-2 thick colleters inside. Blades (25-)30-65 x 13- 32 mm, length:width ratio 1.5:1 to 2:1, oblanceolate to ovate to broadly obovate, decurrent at base, rounded at apex; margins flat (not revolute); dark green above, pale green below, chartaceous to thickly foliaceous, drying reddish brown; glabrous above and below; primary and secondary veins glabrous, visible above and prominent below; secondary veins 3-6 each side, ter- tiary veins sparse and reticulate; petioles 3- 5 mm long, 0.3-0.6 mm thick, winged. In- florescences axillary, 2 per node, cymose, 12-35-flowered, 8-35 mm long; rachis and branches glabrous to sparsely short-pubes- cent; flowers in 2-3-florous cymules; distal bracts narrowly lanceolate, 0.3-1.5 mm long; bracteoles subtending the flowers mi- nutely lanceolate. Flowers short-pedicel- late; pedicels 0.5-2 mm long, thickening in mature capsules. Calyx rotate and membra- naceous, entire or with 3-4 round lobes, 0.6-1.2 mm long, glabrous throughout. Co- rolla shortly funnelform and deeply lobed, 3-4 mm long, white; tube cyathiform, 0.3- 0.6 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm wide at base, ca. 1 mm wide at orifice (without annular thickening), glabrous throughout; lobes 4(-5), imbricate in bud, rounded, ca. 2 X 2 mm, glabrous throughout, membranous. Stamens 4(-5), half-exserted, of equal length, subsessile, attached on the tube near the mouth; filaments 0.2-0.3 mm long; anthers broadly elliptic, ca. 0.5 X 0.4 mm, dorsifixed near the base. Style exserted, ca. 1.5 mm long, microscopically costate-winged, glabrous; style branches broadly ovate, 0.3-0.4 mm long. Capsules narrowly obconical and multi-costate, decurrent at base, 6-18 X 3-5 mm, dark brown, glabrous (or very sparsely puberulent), bilocular, with (1-)2 seeds per locule; persistent calyx usually breaking off at capsule maturity. Seeds peltate, vertical, linear-lanceolate, 5-8 X 0.5-0.7 mm, tricostate, with central hilum, with central ellipsoid endo- sperm, bipolar-winged.

description: Dioecious shrubs 1.5-5 m tall; bark thin, reddish brown. Young terminal branches slender, 2-3 mm thick, brittle, short-puberulent or glabrous. Stipules sheathing at base, splitting on one side, oblong, narrowly triangular at apex, membranous, 5-18 X 2-3 mm, acuminate at apex, membranaceous, sparsely pubescent outside, glabrous inside, deciduous, often subtended by a pair of smaller stipules; subtending stipules (when present) connected at base, deltoid to narrowly triangular, subcoriaceous, 4-6 X 2-3 mm, acuminate at apex, sparsely pubescent outside, glabrous inside, persistent; both sheathing and subtending stipules without colleters. Leaves opposite, petio- late; blades elliptic, lanceolate to oblanceo- late, (4.5-)6-13(-18) X (1.5-)2-5 cm, length:width ratio 1.6:1 to 2.3:1, acute and usually decurrent at base, acute and usually acuminate at apex, dark reddish brown and olive-green below when dry, glabrous above, glabrous to pubescent below; pri- mary, secondary, and tertiary veins gla- brous to sparsely adpressed-pubescent to densely pubescent to hirsute below, visible above and prominent below; secondary veins 7-12 each side; tertiary veins reticulate; petioles 3-10 mm long, ca. 1 mm thick, adaxially concave. Inflorescences terminal and solitary; staminate inflorescences corymbose, many-flowered, short-pedunculate, peduncles 0.7-1.8 cm long, sparsely short-pubescent; pistillate inflorescences single-flowered. Staminate flowers pedicellate, pedicels 2-5 mm long, with functional stamens and fully developed style that is exserted just above the stamens and functions for stylar pollen presentation (Fig. 4A, B); calyx cup-shaped, 5-6(-7)- lobed; tube cup-shaped, 0.5-1 X 2.5-3 mm, sparsely to densely pubescent outside; lobes narrowly triangular, acute at apex, 1-2 X 0.3-0.5 mm, sparsely to densely puberulent outside, contorted, persistent; corolla short-campanulate, 5-6(-7)-lobed, 5-8 X 3-4.5 mm, cream-white; tube campanulate, 3.5-4.5 mm long, 2.5-3 mm wide at base and 3.5- 4.5 mm wide at mouth in anthesis, minutely puberulent outside, densely pubescent at mouth (glabrous below) inside; lobes ovate, acute at apex, 2.2-3.5 X 1.6-2.4 mm, minutely puberulent outside, minutely puberulent to short-pubescent inside, contorted; stamens functional, as many as the corolla lobes and alternate with them, included just below the mouth, subsessile; anthers narrowly oblong, pointed at apex, rounded at base, 2.5-3.2 X 0.6-0.7 mm, dorsifixed near the middle, opening by longitudinal slits; pollen released in monads, tricolporate, exine surface reticulate; style with only tips exserted, 6-9 mm long, glabrous at base, pushing through the included anthers and functioning as a means for secondary pollen presentation (pollen is presented on the outer surface of the style, among the extrorse hairs); style branches 2-3(-4), 3.5- 4 X 0.2-0.3 mm, very narrowly ovate, with acuminate, glabrous extensions at apex, densely extrorse-pubescent, remaining ad- pressed to each other; ovary non-functional, broadly obconical, not ribbed, glabrous or sparsely puberulent to sparsely short-pubescent. Pistillate flowers with pedicels ca. 1 mm long, with non-functional stamens, and with fertile style and ovary (Fig. 4C, D); calyx cup-shaped, membranaceous, (5-)6-7-lobed, with minute lobes alternate to the main lobes; tube short, broadly tubular, 2.2- 2.5 X 4.5-5 mm, sparsely pubescent outside; lobes narrowly triangular, acuminate at apex, 1.5-2 X 2-4 mm, sparsely pubescent outside, persistent; corolla short-campanulate, (5-)6-7-lobed, 6-8 mm long, 4- 6.5 mm wide at mouth, cream-white; tube campanulate, 4-6 mm long, 2.5-4 mm wide at base and 4-6.5 mm wide at mouth in anthesis, minutely puberulent to short-pubescent outside, sparsely short-pubescent at mouth (glabrous below) inside; lobes ovate, acute at apex, 2.5-3.5 X 2.5-3 mm, minutely puberulent to short-pubescent outside, puberulent to short-pubescent inside, contorted; stamens non-functional, as many as the corolla lobes and alternate with them, included just below the mouth, subsessile; anthers narrowly oblong, pointed at apex, rounded at base, 2.5 X 0.5 mm, dorsifixed near the middle; style included (only tips of branches exserted), 4-6 mm long (approximately as long as corolla tube), sparsely short-pubescent just below the style branches, glabrous throughout, with receptive stigmatic surface; style branches (4-)5-6, broadly ovate, blunt at apex, otherwise glabrous, opening at later stage of anthesis; ovary 10-13-ribbed, 4-5-celled, ovoid-globose, 8-9 x 8-9 mm, ribs ca. 2 mm high, with sparse pubescence interspersed with minute puberulence. Fruits globose, 4-5- locular (locules difficult to detect in mature fruits), 9-10 X 8-9 cm, with many seeds per locule, interspersed within a fleshy pulp; exocarp papery, 10-13- ribbed, glabrate, black. Seeds ovoid, slightly laterally flattened, 6-6.5 x 4 mm, with fibrous exotesta.

description: Shrubs to about 3-4 m tall. Branchlets fractiflex, minutely and obscurely sericeous, soon becoming glabrous; leaves ovate-lanceolate to broadly elliptic, shortly acuminate, lateral veins numerous, ca 1 mm apart, or less, the blade 3-6 mm long and 1.5-3 cm broad, glabrous above, densely short sericeous pubescent below, the petioles 7-10 mm long, caniculate above, sericeous becoming glabrous; inflorescences axillary, apparently 1-flowered; flowers unknown but fruiting calyx 5-lobed, the lobes suborbicular, ca 1 mm long; fruit narrowly obovoid to nearly ellipsoidal, ca 20 mm long, the fleshy exocarp thin, the style located slightly to one side of the apex of the fruit and about 1 mm long; seed 15-17 mm long and 6-7 mm in diameter, slightly compressed laterally, attached toward the base ventrally, the ventral scar as broad as the seed and extending to below the middle of the seed.

description: Herba caespitosa 1.5-3 cm alta, caulibus dense foliatis setoso-hispidis pilis patentitus instructis; foliis depse coarctatis sessilibus lanceolatis aristatis 5-7 mm longis 0.7-2 mm latis ubique cinereohispidis; inflorescentiis capitatis densifloris terminalibus subglobosis 5-8 mm latis 5-6 mm altis, a bracteis foliaceis involucralibus subtentis; hypanthio cupulato-campanulato 1 mm longo 1 mm lato breviter pilosulo; calycis lobis 4 inaequalibus, 2 longioribus lineari-lanceolatis aristatis in dimidio inferiore ciliato-hispidis, 2 brevioribus triangulari-lanceolatis aristatis basi hispidulo-ciliolatis.

description: Caespitose herb 1.5-3 cm tall, stems spreading-ascending, densely foliaceous, setosehispid; stipule bristles 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous, 4 on each side; leaves spreading, densely crowded, sessile, lanceolate, aristate, 5-7 mm long, 0.7-2 mm wide, cinereous-hispid both sides; inflorescence capitate, densely flowered, terminal, subglobose, 5-8 mm broad, 5-6 mm high, subtended by foliaceous, spreading, involucral bracts; bracteoles numerous, filiform, 1.5 mm long; kypanthium cupular-campanulate, 1 mm long, 1 mm wide, shortly pilosulous; calyx lobes 4, unequal, the 2 longer linearlanceolate, aristate, 2.8 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm wide, ciliate-hispid on the lower half of the margins, the 2 shorter triangular-lanceolate, aristate, 1-1.2 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm wide, hispidulous-ciliolate at base; corolla white, 4.5 mm long, exceeding the calyx, tube subhypocrateriform, 3.2 mm long, 0.5 mm wide at base, sparsely puberulous without in upper half, otherwise glabrous, lobes broadly ovate, subacute, 1.2 mm long, 0.8-0.9 mm wide, puberulous without, glabrous within; stamens slightly exserted; anthers narrowly linear-oblong, 0.8 mm long; filaments 0.3 mm long, inserted in the throat; style 2.8 mm long, glabrous; stigmas linear, 0.8 mm long; seeds brown, orbicular, somewhat compressed, 0.3-0.4 mm diam.

description: Fruit 10-11 mm diam., pericarp 1.75 mm thick, stigmatic remains lateral-similar to the preceding two genera, but distinctive for its papillate epidermis, the thicker mantle of brachysclereids, and for the larger tanniniferous cells; some of the vascular bundles have very thick fibrous sheaths, and the locular epidermis is extremely thick (to 0.45 mm).

description: Shrub or small tree up to ca 7 m high, appearing to be glabrous but the young growth actually densely covered with minute whitish hairs, later glabrescent; hairs symmetrically dibrachiate, appressed, up to ca 0.1 mm long, whitish; twigs grey to yellowish tan, minutely puberulent at first, soon glabrescent; leaves obscurely appressed puberulent when young, glabrescent with age, elliptic to oblanceolate, 4.5-7 cm long, 1.5-3.3 cm wide, 2.6-3.7 times as long as wide; apex acute to acuminate; base acute, cuneate, or acuminate; petiole channeled, 3-6 mm long, 1-1.5 mm thick; midvein impressed above, prominent below; lateral veins ca 12- 14 pairs, faintly visible; marginal veins equalling the laterals in prominence; blades drying dark or light grey-green above, much lighter, sometimes silvery below, subcoriaceous; peduncles solitary or superimposed in pairs, 12-28 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, broadening to ca 1.5 mm wide near apex, densely covered with minute appressed hairs at first, later glabrescent; bracteoles suborbicular, ca 3-4 mm long, ca 4 mm wide, loosely clasping the hypanthium, essentially glabrous within and without; calyx a calyptra, moderately to sparsely covered with minute hairs without, glabrous within, the basal portion hemispheric, ca 3-4 mm long, the apex an apiculum 2.5-3 mm long; hypanthium obconic, ca 3 mm long, densely covered with minute hairs, these embedded in a waxy substance; disk ca 6-7 mm across, minutely puberulent at first, soon glabrescent; style ca 7 mm long, glabrous; stamens ca 350, 5-10 mm long; anthers ca 0.6 mm long; petals 4, glabrous, suborbicular, ca 6 mm long, sometimes remaining attached to the calyptra; ovary 4-locular; ovules 8-1 1 per locule; fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Landrum, Leslie R. 1984. Taxonomic implications of the discovery of calyptrate species of Myrceugenia (Myrtaceae). Brittonia. 36: 161-166.

description: Shrub or small tree up to ca 6 m high, the young growth densely covered with appressed hairs, these in turn embedded in filmy, waxy substance so the surfaces often appear smooth; hairs symmetrically dibrachiate, closely appressed, reddish-brown; young twigs densely covered with hairs at first, soon becoming glabrescent, straw colored or light reddish-brown, later sometimes dark grey; leaves densely covered with hairs beneath when young, glabrescent or nearly so with age, elliptic to suborbicular or occasionally obcordate, 3.5-8.5 cm long, 1.8-6.5 cm wide, 1.2-2.5 times as long as wide; apex bluntly acute or acuminate, broadly rounded, or cordate; base acute to acuminate; petiole channeled, 7-9 mm long, 1.5-2 mm thick, densely covered with hairs at first, soon glabrescent; midvein impressed slightly above, prominent below; lateral veins indistinct or ca 8 pairs scarcely visible; marginal veins equalling the laterals in prominence; blades drying olive-green, grey-green, or light reddish-brown above, light yellowish-green to reddish- tan below, thickly and stiffly coriaceous; peduncles solitary or superimposed in pairs, 10-18 mm long, ca 1-2 mm wide; bracteoles ovate to lanceolate, ca 4-6 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, ca 2 times as long as wide, moderately strigose without, glabrous to sparsely puberulent, or with a basal tuft of hairs within; calyx a calyptra, moderately strigillose or puberulent within, densely strigose without, falling as a single unit; hypanthium obconic, 2-4 mm long, densely strigose without; disk 4-6 mm across, moderately puberulent to glabrescent; style 6-10 mm long, glabrous; stamens 180-400, 5-12 mm long; anthers 0.4-0.7 mm long; petals 4, suborbicular, moderately to sparsely puberulent without, ca 5-7 mm long, sometimes remaining attached to the calyptra; ovary 4-locular; ovules 11-16 (20) per locule; fruit subglobose, ca 12 mm in diam; seeds 5 in one fruit seen, ca 6 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Landrum, Leslie R. 1984. Taxonomic implications of the discovery of calyptrate species of Myrceugenia (Myrtaceae). Brittonia. 36: 161-166.

description: Frutex 1-3-metralis; pili rufo-brunnei vel testacei, simplices et dibrachiati; ramuli juventute dense pubescentes, pilis effusis, persistentibus; ramuli vetustiores saepe laeves, aurantiaci; folia glabra vel pilis dispersis obsita, anguste oblanceolata vel anguste elliptica vel linearia, 8-25 mm longa, 2-4 mm lata, 3-7-plo longiora quam latiora; apex obtusus vel subacutus; basis cuneata; petioli 1-1.5 mm longi, circa 0.5 mm crassi, sparse vel dense pubescentes, adaxiale leviter canaliculati; laminae subcoriaceae, supra griseo-virides vel brunneo-virides, subtus pallide flavo-brunneae vel pallide griseo-virides, paginis hebetibus; pedunculi uniflori, leviter compressi, solitarii, 1.5-4 mm longi, 0.2-0.4 mm lati, dense pubescentes; bracteolae lanceolatae, 0.9-1.5 mm longae, 0.4-0.6 mm latae, 2.2-2.5-plo longiores quam latiores, submembranaceae, extus sparse pubescentes, intus glabrae, hypanthium amplectentes; calycis lobi ovati, 0.9-1.5 mm longi, 0.9-1.2 mm lati, 0.7-1.4-plo longiores quam latiores, submembranacei, concavi, extus sparse pubescentes, intus glabri; petala suborbicularia, circa 2 mm longa, glabra; hypanthium obconicum, circa 1 mm longum, dense pubescens; discus circa 1 mm latus, sparse pubescens; stamina circa 60, 2-5 mm longa, antheris in sicco 0.2-0.3 mm longis; stylus 4-5 mm longus, glaber; ovarium 2-3-loculare, loculis 3-8-ovulatis.

description: Small tree, 2-5 m tall, young branchlets pubescent. Leaf blades elliptic or narrowly elliptic, 11-17 x 4-7 cm, coriaceous, punctate with small glandular dots, glabrous above, sparingly pubescent below; apex abruptly acuminate; base obtuse to acute; midvein sulcate above, convex below; lateral veins 14-20 pairs, sulcate above, convex below; inframarginal veins 2, the innermost at 3-5 mm from the margin, the tertiary veins forming a fine reticulum; pet- iole 6-10 mm long, flaky. Inflorescences borne at leafless nodes on young branches, spike-like with occasional short branches, 2-6 cm long, with ca. 20 flowers or less, the axes pubescent with reddish brown hairs; buds pyriform, closed and apiculate, 2-3 mm long, glabrescent; calyx rupturing lon- gitudinally and irregularly into 5 calyx lobes, these pubescent within; hypanthium glabrous within, prolonged ca. 1-2 mm beyond the apex of the ovary; petals absent; style ca. 4 mm long, glabrous; filaments ca. 4 mm long, the anthers 0.5-1 mm long; ovary 2-locular, 2 ovules per locule. Fruits glo- bose, ca. 1 cm diam., glabrous, red to purple; seed 1, the testa chartaceous; embryo with the cotyledons thick, fleshy, partially separated to completely fused, radicle 1/2 the length of the embryo and densely coppery- sericeous.
bibliographicCitation: Kawasaaki, M. L. & Holst, Bruce K. 1994. New species and a new combination in Myrtaceae from northeastern South America. Brittonia. 46: 137-143.

description: Low dense, rounded shrub usually ca 1.5 m high, strongly glandular, glabrous or sometimes densely pubescent on young growth; hairs simple, straight or curved, grayish, mainly antrorse, to ca 0.3 mm long; twigs glabrous or sparsely to densely pubescent at first, losing any hairs with age, the young bark dark to light reddish brown, smooth, with age becoming gray and slightly rough; leaves elliptic, ovate, obovate, or suborbicular, 1-3.4 cm long, 0.6-3 cm wide, 0.9-1.6 times as long as wide, glabrous to densely covered with hairs when young, usually becoming glabrous with age; apex acute, rounded, or emarginate; base acute, rounded, or subtruncate; petiole 1-4 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, densely pubescent to glabrous; midvein flat or nearly so above, moderately prominent below; lateral veins indistinct or up to ca 6 pairs faintly visible, these nearly perpendicular to the midvein; marginal veins indistinct; blades stiffly and thickly coriaceous, usually somewhat revolute, drying gray-green to light reddish-brown, somewhat lighter below, some times lustrous above, sometimes blue-green above (due perhaps to an epiphytic alga or lichen); peduncles solitary, uniflorous or triflorous, 0.5-3 cm long, ca 1 mm wide near middle, up to ca 2 mm wide at apex, densely pubescent to glabrous; bracteoles linear, 1-2 mm long, ca 0.2 mm wide, persisting until about anthesis; calyx-lobes 5, unequal, subtriangular to hemiorbicular, usually two 1-1.5 mm long and three 2-2.5 mm long; petals 5, oblong to suborbicular, ca 5-6 mm long, glabrous except for a ciliate margin; hypanthium obconic to campanulate, 3-4 mm long, glabrous to densely pubescent, strongly glandular; disk 3-5 mm across, glabrous or pubescent; style 7-10 mm long, glabrous; stamens ca 140-150, 6-10 mm long; anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long; ovary 2-locular; ovules 5-11 per locule, radiating from a shortly stalked subpeltate placenta attached near the center of the septum; fruit subglobose, 1-2 cm in diam; seed usually 1, ca 1-1.5 cm thick.

description: Shrub, the younger parts densely canescent-pubescent throughout, the stems soon becoming glabrous. Leaves crowded, alternate, the petioles stout, 2 mm. long, the blades coriaceous, oblong, 2--3 cm. long, 8-12 mm. wide, acute at both ends, slightly revolute, 1-nerved, soon glabreseent and shining above. Flowers solitary in the upper axils, the peduncles about 5 mm. long; bracteoles linear, 4-5 mm. long, cafleseent. Hypanthiuin broadly canmpanulate, 3.5 mm. long, canescent. Sepals narrowly triangular, curved-divergent, 2.8 mm. long, canescent. Petals orbicular, 3.3 mm. long, finely ciliate, glandularpunctate. Stamens about 35, the anthers basifixed. Ovary 3-celled, with several ovules in each locule. Style 2.5 mim. long.

description: Acalypha villosa is the species of widest distribution in the subgenus, ranging from southern Mexico to southwestern Brazil, Paraguay, and northern Argentina. In Colombia, it has been collected mainly along the Atlantic coast but also on the Pacific coast and in valleys of the Cauca and Magdalena rivers, from sea level to 1300 (1800) m. Generally it is associated with secondary forest and scrub, mainly on sandy, humid soils. It is a variable species, especially in the indumentum and in shape and size of leaves. Many varieties of this species have been described (Miiller-Argoviensis, 1865, 1866, 1874; Pax & Hoffmann, 1924). Webster and Burch (1968) found these varieties irrelevant to Panamanian populations, and I see no reason to recognize them among the Colombian collections.

description: This species was described from the Cerro de La Pedrera, also known as Cupati or Yupati, where it was first collected in 1820. Only two further collections seem to have been made, both at the same locality (Balick, 1986). The new collections from the area of La Pedrera, as well as observations ofthe large populations, allow for a better understanding of this species and some new data can be added to Balick's (1986) description. Oenocarpus circumtextus is a solitary palm, 3-6 m tall, with the trunk completely covered by a dense net of interwoven fibers from the leaf sheath. The crown has 7 or 8 leaves with a petiole 72-75 cm long; the rachis is 175-180 cm long, and has 16-19 pinnae on each side. Inflorescences are interfoliar and erect, except for the pendulous rachillae. Fruiting rachillae are reddish. Eophylls are cuneate, bifid at apex for slightly more than 1/5 their length.
bibliographicCitation: Bernal, R. C., et al. 1991. Notes on Oenocarpus (Palmae) in the Colombian Amazon. Brittonia. 43: 154-164.

description: Stem solitary, 5-8 m tall, 7-8 cm diam, grayish, longitudinally fissured. Leaves 12; sheath 65-68 cm long, purplish, coarsely fibrous; petiole 15-25 cm long, covered with a gray, scaly indumentum, the latter more or less persistent adaxially, more or less deciduous abaxially; rachis 2.43 m long, with scaly indumentum like that of the petiole; pinnae 65 on each side, regularly arranged and in 1 plane, linear-lanceolate, acuminate, strongly plicate along secondary veins, concolorous, glabrous adaxially, covered abaxially with a thin, loose, wool-like, waxy indu- mentum, and sparsely beset with minute, white trichomes; basal pinnae 46.5- 50.4 x 0.8-1.5 cm; middle pinnae 73-75.5 x 5-5.3 cm; apical pinnae 29 x 1 cm. Inflorescence interfoliar; prophyll not seen; peduncular bract inserted 2.5-3 cm above prophyll, covered (at least in young bud) with purplish scales; peduncle 6.2-7.5 cm long, the distance between scars of prophyll and peduncular bract 2.8- 3 cm, the axis 9.5-16 cm long from the scar of peduncular bract (i.e., distal part of peduncle +/- rachis), circular in transverse section; rachillae 107-125, the longest ones 56-60 cm; flowers seen only in early bud; staminate flowers with sepals connate at base, the lobes triangular, carinate; petals free; stamens 6; pistillate flowers not seen; fruits ovoid, with apical stigmatic residue, 2.2-2.6 x 1.4-1.7 cm, the epicarp smooth, purplish-black at maturity, the fibers ca 0.2 mm wide; seed slightly ovoid to almost ellipsoid, 1.8-1.9 x 1.4-1.5 cm; endosperm white, with abundant brown ruminations; embryo well-developed, to ca 1.4 cm long; eophyll with 4 narrow pinnae palmately radiating from a very short rachis.
bibliographicCitation: Bernal, R. C., et al. 1991. Notes on Oenocarpus (Palmae) in the Colombian Amazon. Brittonia. 43: 154-164.

description: Stems cespitose, 3-4 m tall, 1.5-1.8 cm diam, with 2 or 3 main stems and several basal shoots, smooth, brown, conspicuously ringed, the internodes 1.5-3 cm long. Leaves 5-8, reddish when young, erect; sheath 41-45 cm long, purplish to green, fibrous on the margins, with purplish scales; petiole 24-28 cm long, 5 mm diam, subterete, with deciduous scales like those of the leaf sheath; rachis 63-67 cm long; blade entire, narrowly cuneate, apically bifid for ca 1/5 its length, 76-91 cm long, 14-18.6 cm at the widest point slightly below the bifurcation, the lobes ovate, cucullate, 15.5-16.5 cm long, including a narrow acumen, 3-4 cm long; primary veins 8-11 on each side, forming an angle of 6-8? with the rachis, abaxial surface whitish, waxy, with scattered, very short, white trichomes. Inflorescence interfoliar, erect at anthesis, pendulous in fruit, spicate or bifid, up to 73 cm long; prophyll bicarinate, acute at apex, chartaceous, 15-20 cm long, ca 1 cm wide, with scattered, purplish scales; peduncular bract cylindrical in the bud, expanded and flat at anthesis, 48-66 cm long, including a 3-4 cm long umbo, 1.8 cm wide, subcoriaceous, striate, with purplish scales; peduncle 16-37 cm long, 2-3 mm thick, with ferrugineous scales, occasionally bifid at apex for 10-19 cm, and then the inflorescence with 2 pedunculate rachillae; rachilla 21-25 cm long, 3-5 mm in diam, with deep pits, yellowish at anthesis, reddish in fruit, with ferrugineous scales; staminate flowers ovate-lanceolate, 3-4.5 x 1.5 mm; sepals connate at base, sometimes connate into a flattened, triangular calyx with concave sides, or into a strongly 3-carinate calyx, the lobes triangular, 0.8 x 0.5 mm; petals ovate-lanceolate, thick, 3 x 1.2-1.5 mm; stamens 6, the filaments undulate, inflexed at the apex, 1-1.5 mm long, anthers 1-1.5 mm long, bifid and inequilateral at base, the connective projected into a short point; pistillode 0.5 mm long; pistillate flowers ovoid when immature, ca 2.5 x 2 mm; sepals broadly imbricate, suborbicular, 2.5 mm high; petals broadly imbncate, suborbicular, cucullate, 1.5 mm high; gynoecium 1 mm long; fruit oblong-ellipsoid, 2.2-2.7 x 1.3-1.4 cm, with a prominent, cylindrical, slightly eccentric stigmatic residue, the epicarp purplish-black at maturity, with a thin layer of wax, the mesocarp with flat fibers; seed ovoid, 1.5 x 0.9 cm, the raphe branches loosely reticulate; endosperm homogeneous; eophyll in outline cuneate to obovate, bifid for 1/4 its length, the lobes long-acuminate and sometimes cucullate, whitish abaxially.
bibliographicCitation: Bernal, R. C., et al. 1991. Notes on Oenocarpus (Palmae) in the Colombian Amazon. Brittonia. 43: 154-164.

description: Caespitose terrestrial 35-40 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid, 5 x 3 cm, becoming wrinkled with age, with 2-3 subtending foliaceous bracts subsimilar to the leaves. Leaves 2-3, linear-lanceolate, acute, to 33 x 2.3 cm. Inflorescences erect, long-pedunculate panicles, 60-75 cm long, the branches clustered near the apex, with distant inconspic- uous bracts. Flowers spreading, dorsal sepal bright yellow with brown markings, the lateral sepals greenish yellow with brown markings, the petals bright yellow with brown markings, the labellum bright yellow with brown markings on the base of the lateral lobes, midlobe and callus, the column and anther yellow. Dorsal sepal ovate, acute to minutely apiculate, clawed, lightly concave, 7.5 x 5.2 mm. Lateral sepals lanceolate, cuneate, acute, reflexed, free, 10 x 3 mm. Petals ovate, shortly apiculate, clawed, arcuate through twisting at the base, 8 x 5 mm. Labellum 3-lobed, 19 x 20 mm, the lateral lobes narrowly elliptic, retrorse, the midlobe transverse-reniform, emargin ate, the callus basal, with 3 proximal irregular ridges becoming a series of blunt teeth distally. Column stout, with falcate, sub- dentate wings, 4 mm long, infrastigmatica simple. Anther 1.6 x 1.2 mm, the pollinia 2, cleft, the stipe linear-oblanceolate, the viscidium minute, orbicular.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, David E. & Christenson, Eric A. 1995. New species of Peruvian Orchidaceae III. Brittonia. 47: 182-209.
