description: Solitary, erect, pleonanthic, monoecious palm; stem 2.5-7.5 m high, 20-32 cm in diam, with leaf sheaths persistent on upper third and pronounced, closely spaced internodes on lower two-thirds of stem. Leaves 15-30, fewer in younger or senescent plants, spirally arranged in a broad, arching crown; sheath 40-130 x 20-22 cm, partially clasping, split opposite the petiole, thick, coriaceous, adaxial surface smooth and greenish, abaxial surface weakly gray-lepidote; petiole 10-20 x 5-10 cm, adaxial surface channelled and smooth, abaxial surface convex and weakly gray-lepidote; rachis 4.13-6.57 m long, base trough-shaped in cross- section, center more or less 4-sided, becoming triangular toward apex, abaxial surface weakly gray-lepidote; pinnae 132-191 per side, in groups of 2-6 on basal meter of rachis, otherwise regularly spaced and in a single plane, rigid to pliant, linear-lanceolate at center of rachis, plicate, acute, basally reflexed at attachment, 1-ribbed with prominent intermediate veins, adaxially green and smooth, abaxially dull-glaucous; basal pinnae 95-145 x 1-2.5 cm; middle pinnae 93-114 x 3.5-4 cm; apical pinnae 27-40 x 0.8-1 cm. Inflorescences interfoliar, yellowish at anthesis, bearing a prophyll; peduncular bract 75-160 x 11-30 cm, woody, longitudinally ribbed, brown, swollen in middle, persistent, with acumen 13-33 cm long, interior surface yellow at anthesis; peduncle 41-130 cm long; rachis 30-103 cm long; rachillae of staminate inflorescence simple, 150-448 in number, 5-18 cm long, linear to slightly undulate, slender, attenuate, arranged spirally around the rachis and subtended by a membranous bract 2.5-4 mm long, bearing sta- minate flowers arranged in longitudinal rows on abaxial side only; rachillae of androgynous inflorescence simple, ca 230 in number, 5-15 cm long, arranged spirally around the rachis, each rachilla subtended by a bract 9-13 mm long and generally bearing 1 pistillate flower at middle (ca 5 cm above insertion on rachis) and 2 rows of ca 20 staminate flowers on abaxial side extending to apex, or rachilla at base of rachis commonly bearing staminate flowers only. Flowers unisexual; staminate flowers yellowish, slightly fragrant, subtended by 1 or 2 bracteoles 0.5-1.5 mm long; sepals 3, free or basally connate, triangular to deltate, ca 2 x 1.2 mm, membranous; petals 3, free, straight to curved, 1-1.8 x 4-5 mm, lanceolate, acute at apex, coriaceous, with smooth to slightly crenulate margins; stamens free, 11-12; filaments straight, linear; thecae united and longitudinally dehiscent; pistillode reduced. Pistillate flowers not seen. Fruits obovate, 7.8-9.4 x 4.9-5.3 cm, 76-96 g each (dry weight), brown-lepidote throughout, frequently channelled or grooved on sides, with a weakly defined ring left by staminodial cupule; stigmatic residue persistent, often slightly eccentric; fruiting perianth indurate, consisting of 3 sepals 2.5-4 cm long, 3 petals 4-5 cm long, and a staminodial ring; epicarp 2-3 mm thick, fibrous; mesocarp 2-3 mm thick, oily, bright orange at maturity; endocarp 3.7-4.1 cm in diam, woody and very hard; seeds generally 3-4, ellipsoid, ca 3-4 cm long; endosperm white, oily, homogeneous; embryo basal.

description: Stem solitary, erect, columnar or slightly swollen at base or middle, to 20 m tall, to 35 cm diam, gray, smooth, with obscure nodes. Leaves 15-19, stiff and adscending, neatly abscising and leaving a clean stem; sheath open, not distin- guishable from the petiole; sheath and petiole 1.30-1.35 m long, flat adaxially, rounded abaxially, sparsely fibrous on the margins; rachis 3.2-4 m long, anvil shaped in cross-section; pinnae 127-165 per side, regularly spaced, stiffly spreading in one plane, opposite to subopposite, linear, bifid apically to 15 cm, glabrous; proximal pinnae 60-65 x 1-1.5 cm, middle pinnae 65-90 x 4 cm, apical pinnae 40-45 x 1.5 cm. Inflorescences (and infructescences) interfoliar, either predominantly staminate or staminate and pistillate, both types occurring on the same tree; peduncle short, to 20 cm long, to 6 cm diam, dorsiventrally flattened; prophyll to 40 cm long, to 20 cm diam, becoming very fibrous at apex; peduncular bract persistent, to 120 cm long, sheathing peduncle for ca 10 cm and then open except for a 20 cm pointed apex, woody, to 1.5 cm thick, deeply lirate abaxially; numerous smaller bracts to 15 cm long present on the peduncle; rachis to 40 cm long; rachillae to several hundred, to 15 cm long, closely bunched, sparsely covered with whitish scales, with 0-8 pistillate flowers proximally and paired or solitary staminate flowers distally; staminate flowers densely crowded onto the rachillae, each sub- tended by a small bract, arranged on 3 sides of the rachillae only, creamy white; sepals 3, spreading but briefly imbricate basally, triangular, gibbous, 2 mm long; petals 3, free, straight and incurved, lanceolate, to 7 mm long, to 1.5 mm diam; stamens 8 or 9, at anthesis exserted laterally from petals; filaments 1.5-2 mm long; anthers curled but not twisted (and straight in bud), medifixed, to 4 mm long; pistillode very small, 4 or 5-fid; pollen circular, monosulcate, with tectate, perforate exine with clavate projections; pistillate flowers sessile, with vestigial lateral staminate flowers present; sepals 3, imbricate, deltate, 11-20 mm long; petals 3, imbricate, deltate, 16-20 mm long; staminodial ring to 1.5 mm high with to 6 short projections; ovary glabrous, to 10 mm high; stigmas 3, well exserted from petals and recurved at anthesis; ovule basal; fruit widely ovoid with prominent apical stigmatic residue; epicarp reddish at maturity; mesocarp ca 5 mm thick, very fibrous; endocarp to 3 mm thick, with 3 basal pores and 3 small apical ridges; seeds irregularly ellipsoid, to 2 cm long and 1 cm diam; endosperm homogeneous with hollow central cavity; germination remote ligular; eophyll entire.

description: Tree, 7 m tall. Stipules 4 mm long. Leaves with petioles 5-11 cm long; blades narrowly ovate to narrowly elliptic, 15-22 x 6-7 cm, apex acuminate, base obtuse, abaxially with 1-2 glands on each side of midrib ca. 0.75 mm diam., with few hairs, most near primary vein, adaxially glabrous, secondary veins in 9-12 pairs excluding the apex. Thyrses orange-colored, at least twice branched; bracts of side branches ca. 1 mm long, a little wider than long; each branch with staminate part to 30 X 2-3 mm. Bracts of staminate cymules 1.25 mm long, evidently eglandular. Staminate flowers with pedicels to 0.5 mm long; sepals ca. 0.4 mm long, stamens 2 per flower (but only few flowers studied), the anthers ca. 0.35 mm long. Pistillate flowers 0-1 per branch of thyrse; pedicel hirsute-sericeous; sepals ca. 2 X 2 mm, glandular, glabrous; ovary densely hirsute, stylar column 2 mm long, glabrous, stigmas <1 mm long. Fruits in- tensely rose-purple, apically green, nearly circular in outline, 7-9 mm long, hirsute, slowly glabrescent; persistent central colu- mella ca. 4 mm long; mericarps regularly rounded, pericarp 0.6-0.7 mm thick. Seeds 6.5 X 6.5 X 6.5 mm, surface partly with larger, brown, colliculate cells, partly with smaller, paler, smooth cells.

description: Tree 15(-20) m tall, stem diameter to 15 cm. Wood quite hard, cream to yellowish. Living bark beige to brown, 1 mm thick, later on with lenticels ca. 1 mm diam. Younger branches densely hirsute-sericeous, glabrescent. Leaves with petioles 3-17(-22) cm long, sericeous to glabrous; blades narrowly elliptic, 18-33 X 5-8 cm, apex caudate to acuminate, base acute to obtuse, abaxially with 2-6 glands on each side of midrib 0.5-0.9 mm diam., sericeous on primary vein and, more rarely, on blade near base, glabrescent, adaxially nearly glabrous, secondary veins in (12-)15-19 pairs excluding the apex. Thyrses scarlet to purple except for the greenish pistillate flowers, 2-4(-5)-times branched, the whole thyrse to 25 X 15 cm; bracts of side branches 2-3 X 1 mm; each branch with staminate part 20-40 X 2-3 mm. Bracts of staminate cymules 1.2-2 X 1-1.5 mm, with minute glands; bracteoles small. Staminate flowers with pedicel 1-2 mm long, articulate near base; sepals ca. 0.7 mm long; stamens 4-6 in central flower, 1-2 in lateral ones, the anthers ca. 0.4 mm, the filaments ca. 0.2 mm long. Dry pollen grains prolate spheroidal, polar axis ca. 26 Km long, equatorial axis ca. 30 Km long. Pistillate flowers 0-1 per branch of thyrse; pedicel glabrous; sepals 1.5-2 X 1.5-2 mm, often glandular; ovary glabrous, stylar column ca. 1 mm long, stigmas 0.5-1 mm long. Fruiting pedicel to 5 mm long; fruits green to red, circular to transversely elliptic in outline, deeply sulcate, 13-18 X 16-25 mm, often with 1 vestigial and 2 well-developed mericarps, glabrous; persistent central columella 9-10 mm long; mericarps regularly rounded or slightly broadened at base, pericarp ca. 1.3 mm thick. Seeds 10-11 x 10- 11 mm, 9-10.5 mm deep, surface partly reticulate-foveolate with larger, medium brown cells, partly smooth with smaller, paler cells.

description: Fruit 8 mm diam., with pericarp 0.5 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-a very thin pericarp showing little specialization, resembling Iguanura, but linked with Actinorhytis and Dictyosperna on morphological grounds (Pintaud, in press); distinctive for the thicker band of fibrous vascular bundles, the apparent total lack of tanniniferous and raphide-bearing cells, the conspicuous but discontinuous band of brachysclereids in the outer pericarp, the papillate epidermis, and the compressed and sclerified parenchyma between the bundles and the locular epidermis. The latter feature has otherwise been found only in Neoveitchia in this alliance, and is reminiscent of the Ptychospermatinae.

description: Fruit ovoid, 9 mm diam., 13 mm long, with pericarp 0.8-1.1 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-remarkable for the continuous system of fibrous vascular bundles and longitudinal fibrous bundles, the two types of bundles intermixed and moderately flattened in the inner pericarp, becoming totally fibrous and nearly terete in the outer pericarp; further characterized by raphide-bearing cells scattered throughout the outer 2/3 of the pericarp, the lack of any brachysclereids or tanniniferous cells in the pericarp, and a very thin locular epidermis.

description: Perennials with stems much branched from a thick rootstock, the stems ascending to spreading, 1-1.5 dm long, glabrous except for a few hairs below the leaves to frequently pilose; internodes usually longer than the leaves. Leaves linear to ovate, 5-16 mm long, 1-8 mm wide, sessile, muricate, pilose on upper and lower surfaces occasionally glabrous: stipular sheath obscure, the setae few to numerous, up to 5 mm long, pilose. Capitula 10-20-flowered; involucral leaves 4, narrowly elliptic to broadly ovate. Calyx 4-6-lobed, to 1 mm long, sparingly to densely pilose; corolla white to rarely yellowish (Skafer 10634), funnelform, 3-4 (-5) mm long, the lobes 1-1.5 mm long; ovary 2 (-3)-carpellate, the stigmas linear to clavate, 2-lobed. Mericarps 2 (-3), 1.5-2.5 mm long, glabrous or infrequently with very short hairs apically, obovate, having rust-colored bands or speckles, dividing into halves or rarely into half and 2 quarters giving 3 mericarps, the adaxial face smooth, broad, and flat. Flowering year-round.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Walter H. & Oliver, Royce L. 1974. Revision of Richardia (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 26: 271-301.

description:
Perennis, radice palari longa, caulibus prostratis pulvinos implicitos 1.5 dm diam. facientibus, glabris vel scabris, internodiis longis. Folia subsessilia, anguste vel late ovata, 5-9 mm lata et 10-25 mm longa, glabra vel glabrata vel scabra, apicibus acutis, basibus anguste cuneatis; stipularum vaginae albidae papyraceae, 1.5 mm latae, setis pluribus brevibus imparibus praeditae. Capitula multiflora, floribus circa 25; folia involucrorum late ovata. Calyx 2.5-3 mm longus, glaber vel puberulus, lobis 4 lanceo- latis circa 1 mm longis, subaequalibus vel 2 multum deminutis; corolla alba tubiformis vel infundibuliformis, 5-6 mm longa, glabra, lobis brevibus circa 1 mm longis ovatis; ovarium 2-carpellatum stylo partim et stigmate 2-lobatis. Fructus ignotus.

Richardia boliviensis is related to R. cruciata, from which it differs in its glabrescent to scabrous stems and leaves, its multiflowered capitula, its glabrous calyx and corolla, the corolla 5-6 mm long with lobes 1/5 the length of the tube, and its 2- carpellate ovary. R. cruciata has densely pilose calyces and corollas 6-8 mm long with hairs on the outer face of the lobes and with the lobes 1/2 - 1-3 the length of the tube; the ovary is 4-carpellate.

description: Annuals often becoming perennial; stems commonly prostrate, occasionally ascend- ing, to 4 dm long, hirsute, rarely rooting from the lower nodes. Leaves elliptic to ovate, the apex acute to obtuse, the base attenuate with the petiole almost absent to ca. 1 cm long, the blade 1.5-4 (-7) cm long, 0.8-2 cm wide, scabrous on both sides; stipular sheath ca. 2 mm wide, the setae 1.5-5 mm long. Capitula many- flowered (usually 20 or more); involucral leaves 1-2-paired, usually broadly ovate, often estipulate, the second pair smaller. Calyx typically 6-lobed, the lobes 1.5-3.5 mm long, ca. 2.5 times as long as the tube, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, ciliate-margined, glabrous to scabrous; corolla white to less commonly rose, funnelform, (4-) 6-lobed the tube 3-8 mm long, the lobes 1-3 mm long, glabrous except for hair tufts on the lobes (sterile axillary flowers very rarely present, these with corollas 1.5 mm long, the tube essentially lacking, densely pilose without); stamens (4-) 6, the filaments usually very short and not exserted although sometimes strongly exserted on longer filaments; ovary 3-carpellate, the stigma capitate, 3-lobed. Mericarps 3 (rarely 2 by abortion), 2.5-3 (-4) mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, broadly obovate, abaxial face papillose and strigose (Fig. 11), adaxial face broad having a prominent median keel, concave, glabrous (Fig. 9), the base retuse. Flowering year-round in warmer climates, spring and summer in temperate zones.

description: Perennials with prostrate stems 4 dm or more in length, the stems rooting at the nodes and partially buried in the sand, densely pilose with whitish hairs on the newer growth. Leaves sessile, 1.5-3 cm long, 0.7-1.4 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-ovate to obovate, acute at the apex, cuneate at the base, the margins conspicuously and densely ciliate with the whitish hairs perpendicular to the margin, the upper surface glabrous, the lower surface white-pilose; stipular sheath ca. 1 mm wide, pilose, the setae 3-4 mm long. Capitula 10-15-flowered; involucral leaves 4, broadly ovate. Calyx margin white-ciliate, the hairs ca. 2 mm long; corolla white, 6.5 mm long, the 4 lobes ca. as long as the tube with ciliate upper margins; ovary 2-carpellate, the style glabrous, the stigma 2-lobed. Mericarps 2, 2.5-3 mm long, with an apical tuft of hairs on abaxial face, otherwise smooth. Flowering November. The floral descrip- tion is taken largely from Urban (Symb. Antill. 9: 540. 1928).
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Walter H. & Oliver, Royce L. 1974. Revision of Richardia (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 26: 271-301.

description: Perennials from a long slender taproot, with decumbent stems branching diffusely at the base, forming a matted cushion to 3 dm across; stems pilose, commonly 0.5 dm long; leaves linear to lanceolate, sessile, typically 1-3 mm wide, 5-10 mm long, glabrous to pilose, the margins revolute; stipular sheath 1 mm wide, the few setae ca. 2 mm long. Capitula 15-flowered or more; involucral leaves 4, linear. Calyx 1.5-2 mm long, sparingly ciliate, the 4 lobes lanceolate; corolla white (brown, Eyerdam 24778) with the lobes rose-purple, rotate, 1.5-2 mm long, the tube only ca. 0.5 mm long; flowers occasionally cleistogamous; ovary typically 4-carpellate, hispid, the stigma capitate, 4-lobed. Mericarps 4 (-5), ca. 1.5 mm long, sparsely scabrous towards the apex on the abaxial face, the adaxial face smooth and broad. Flowering October to May.

description: Perennials from a long, somewhat branching taproot, with stems diffusely branched at the base, the stems spreading, prostrate or nearly so, 2-4 (-6) cm long, strongly hirsute. Leaves ovate to occasionally broadly lanceolate, 2-5 mm wide, 5-10 mm long, subsessile, hirsute above and below; stipular sheath ca. 1 mm wide, the setae to 3 mm long, much obscured by the stem hairs. Capitula 2-8-flowered; involucral leaves 4, ovate to broadly ovate, otherwise similar to cauline leaves. Calyx 3 mm long, hirsute, the 4-6 lobes often unequal; corolla white, funnelform to salverform, 6-8 mm long, the lobes 2.5 mm long with a few hairs apically; ovary 4-carpellate, the stigma capitate, 4-lobed. Mericarps 4, 2 mm long, glabrous or minutely lepidote. Flowering August (one collection).

description: Annuals, perhaps becoming perennial from a slender or moderately thick rootstock, adventitious roots forming principally at the nodes; stems to 7 dm long, procumbent and sprawling, densely hirsute, the hairs commonly 2 mm long. Leaves linear- lanceolate and sessile, typically 1.5-4.5 cm long, 2-8 mm wide, infrequently nar- rowly elliptic and petiolate (northern range), hirsute to commonly strigose on both surfaces; stipular sheath 2-3 mm wide, papery, the several setae 2.5-8 mm long. Capitula many-flowered with long calyx lobes prevailing; involucral leaves 4, ovate, the apex acuminate, hirsute, the second pair smaller. Calyx 5-8 (-10) mm long, hirsute to scabrous, the 6 lobes linear-lanceolate, ca. 4-7 (-9) mm long, ciliate- margined; corolla typically pink, lavender, or lilac, occasionally white with lilac lobes, rarely pinkish orange (Irwin et al. 13395), funnelform to salverform, (8-) 12-20 (-25) mm long, the 6 lobes 2.5-5 mm long, often with apical hair tufts; stigma clavate, 3-lobed; ovary 3-carpellate. Mericarps 3, ca. 3 mm long, papillose and with blunt, rounded excrescences (Fig. 15), the adaxial face closed to a narrow groove (Fig. 14). Flowering September to April.

description: Perennials from a long, somewhat branching taproot, with stems diffusely branched at the base, forming prostrate mats to 1.5 dm across, the stems hispid, often rooting at the nodes, the internodes to 2 cm long. Leaves sessile to subpetiolate (1-2 mm long), elliptic-ovate, hispid and whitish in some, the largest leaves to 15 mm long and 10 mm wide; stipular sheath 1 mm wide or less, typically with 3-6 setae ca. 3 mm long. Capitula commonly to 15-flowered; involucral leaves 4, wider than cauline leaves, typically ovate to broadly ovate. Calyx 1.5-2 mm long, almost equal in length to the corolla, hirsute, the 4 lobes ciliate-margined; corolla white, funnelform or rotate, 1.7-2 mm long, the lobes ca. 1 mm long; ovary 4-carpellate, glabrous, the stigma capitate, 4-lobed. Mericarps 4, 2 mm long, glabrous, the adaxial face broad, smooth, and flat (Figs. 34-35). Flowering October to March (South America).

description: Annuals from a branched long slender taproot, with several stems from the base; stems to 7 cm long, hirsute, spreading, with internodes to 3 cm long. Leaves narrowly elliptic to broadly lanceolate, attenuate to subsessile, apically obtuse, 3-10 mm wide, 1.5-2.5 cm long, hirsute with whitish hairs; stipular sheath 1 mm wide, hirsute, the setae ca. 2 mm long. Capitula 5-10-flowered; involucral leaves usually paired and similar to cauline leaves. Calyx 2.5-3.5 mm long, hirsute, the 6 lobes lanceolate; corolla white, ca. 4 mm long, the lobes ca. 1.5 mm long; ovary 3-carpellate, the capitate stigma 3-lobed. Mericarps 3, 4-5 mm long or perhaps longer, obovate, the apex slightly emarginate, the base incised, the abaxial face papillose and strigose (Fig. 12), the adaxial face broad, glabrous, and with an obscure median keel (Fig. 13). Flowering October to November.

description: Perennials with prostrate creeping stems much branched from a longroot stock; stems white-pilose with internodes shorter than the leaves. Leaves linear to narrowly ovate, sessile, 3-15 mm long, 1-8 mm wide, sparsely to densely pilose, paired leaves equal or unequal; stipular sheath to 1.5 mm wide, the setae ca. 5, to 3 mm long, often obscured by indumentum. Capitula few- to many-flowered; involucral leaves 4, broadly ovate. Calyx 4-6-lobed, 2 mm long; corolla white, salverform, 6-7 mm long, the lobes 1.5-2 mm long; ovary 2-3-carpellate, the stigma (2-) 3-lobed, flattened. Mericarps 2-3, 1.5-2 mm long, the abaxial face with apical tufts of hairs, the adaxial face flat and smooth. Flowering August to December and perhaps for a longer period.

description: Perennials from a long slender taproot, often extensively branched; stems erect to 8 cm long, with few branches from the base, densely hirsute, the internodes long. Leaves linear to linear-lanceolate, sessile, ca. 0.5 mm wide, to 2.7 cm long, glabrous or with scattered hairs above, hirsute especially along veins below; stipular sheath 1.5 mm wide, the setae 3-4 mm long. Capitula up to 12-flowered; involucral leaves 4, typically linear-lanceolate, (15-) 20 (-25) mm long. Calyx to 2 mm long, hirsute chiefly along midveins, the lobes lanceolate; corolla white, more or less salverform, 5-9 mm long, the lobes 1-2 mm long, the tube narrow and elongate, (3-) 4-6 (-7) mm long; ovary 4-carpellate, somewhat hirsute, the stigma capitate with 3-4 obscure lobes. Mericarps 4 (or 3 by abortion), ca. 1.5 mm long, sparsely scabrous toward the apex of the abaxial face, the adaxial face smooth and broad. Flowering July to December.

description: Annuals erect to decumbent, the often sprawling stems to 8 dm long, loosely branching, hirsute, not usually rooting at the nodes. Leaves ovate to elliptic-lanceolate, rarely linear-lanceolate, 1-6.5 cm long, 3-13 mm wide, scabrous above and below, prominently so on principal veins, the apex obtuse to acute, basally attenuate, often petiolate up to 5 mm long or long-attenuate; stipular sheath ca. 2 mm wide, the setae 2-5 mm long. Capitula many-flowered (usually 20 or more); involucral leaves 1-2-paired, usually broadly ovate and estipulate, the second pair smaller. Calyx ca. 2.5-3.5 mm long, the lobes lanceolate, ca. twice the length of the tube, glabrous with the margins ciliate; corolla white, funnelform to salverform, the tube 2-8 mm long, the lobes ca. 0.5-2.5 mm long, occasionally tinged pink-lavender; stamens 6, exserted or not; ovary typically 3-carpellate, the stigma capitate, 3-lobed. Mericarps 3 (-6), 2-3.5 mm long, ca. 1.5-2 mm wide, more or less oblong to obovate, the abaxial face densely papillose and typically strigillose (Fig. 10), the adaxial face closed to a narrow groove (Fig. 8), the base somewhat retuse. Flowering year-round in warmer climates, spring and summer in temperate zones.

description: Richardia schumnannii is related to R. stellaris, from which it differs in its compact habit with short stems (to 4 cm) and internodes, its shorter involucral leaves to 7 (-10) mm long, its few-flowered (1-4) capitula, and its calyx only 1/4 the length of the corolla. R. stellaris is a spreading herb with long stems (to 1.5 dm) and internodes, long involucral leaves (10-20 mm), inflorescences with more flowers (maximum 7-15 per capitulum), and with a calyx about half the length of the corolla. R. stellaris is widely distributed (southern Brazil, Uruguay, northern Argentina, Paraguay, and Bolivia) whereas R. schumannii is endemic to the grasslands of southeastern Brazil (Figs. 3, 38).

description: Perennials from a long taproot, with many basal branches, the stems spreading to somewhat erect, up to 1.5 dm long, glabrous to more commonly hirsute. Leaves linear to commonly lanceolate or broadly lanceolate, sessile, 1-2.5 cm long, 2-4 (-7) mm wide, hirsute above and below to almost glabrous, the margins revolute; stipular sheaths 1 mm wide with long white setae usually 5-7 mm long. Capitula of few to many flowers (mostly 7-15); involucral leaves 4, commonly lanceolate (basally 2 mm wide or more), occasionally linear, 10-15 (-18) mm long. Flowers frequently cleistogamous, remaining in bud on developing mericarps; calyx acuminate, fimbriate, sparingly hirsute, the 4 unequal lobes ca. 1.5 mm long; corolla white, the chasmogamous corolla funnelform, (2.5-) 3-4 mm long, about twice as, long as the calyx, the lobes ca. 1.2 mm long (ca. 1/2 the length of the tube), the cleistogamous floral buds 1-1.5 mm long; ovary (3-) 4-carpellate, the stigma irregularly capitate. Mericarps (3-) 4 (when 3, either by abortion or from a 3-carpellate ovary), 1.7-2 mm long, glabrous to sparingly scabrous. Flowering September to April, rarely later.

description: Perennials from a long, sparingly branched taproot, with stems diffusely branched at the base; branches spreading or prostrate, forming mats up to 4 dm across. Leaves sessile, coriaceous, linear to linear-lanceolate, 4-25 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, the apex acute to acuminate, sparingly hispid to subglabrous, the margins revolute in dried specimens; stipular sheath 1-2.5 mm long with few whitish setae to 6 mm long. Capitula few- to infrequently many-flowered (3-10), very rarely subterminal, some- times appearing axillary by development of lateral branches; involucral leaves 4, linear to lanceolate. Calyx 2.5-3 mm long, puberulent to hirsute, the lobes (3-) 4 (-6), equal or subequal, lanceolate; corolla white, (3-) 4-6 mm long, funnelform, the lobes 3-4, 1-2 mm long; ovary (2-) 3-4-carpellate, the stigmas obscurely 2-4- lobed. Mericarps (2-) 3-4, 2 (-3) mm long, ca. 1 mm wide, often flushed reddish purple apically (Figs. 32-33).

description: Plants with glabrous or hirsute mericarps may be found in distinct populations; occasionally both forms are found in a single collection (e.g., Shinners 14495 and Trelease 55). Nevertheless, the predominance of hispid mericarps, three per fruit, and the typically 3-merous floral parts in addition to a distinct distribution all clearly serve to distinguish this subspecies.

description: Dioecious trees to 15 m tall, bole of the trunk to 8 m long, to 76 cm dbh; bark reddish brown when young, turning grayish brown; wood cream-white, hard. Yottng terminal branches 1.2-1.5 cm thick, brittle, covered by the persistent membranous stipules, densely long-pubescent. Stipules free at base, not connected to petioles, broadly ovate, acute at apex, 3.5-4.5 X 2-2.5 cm, membranous, long-sericeous outside, gla- brous inside, with many subparallel veins departing from the base, without colleters. Leaves short-petiolate; blades obovate to broadly obovate (rarely broadly elliptic), (18-)23-34 X (9-)12-18 cm, length:width 1.6:1 to 2.3:1, decurrent at base, acute to rounded and acuminate at apex, dark olive-green above, light whitish-green below, thickly chartaceous; sparsely pubescent above, densely pubescent below; primary, secondary, and tertiary veins densely pubescent above and below, prominent below; secondary veins 9-12 each side; tertiary veins sparse, subparallel-reticulate; petioles 0.5-1 cm long, 2-4 mm thick, winged. Pistillate inflorescences single-flowered, short- pedunculate; staminate inflorescences cymose, 5-9-flowered, long-pedunculate. Pistillate flowers short-pedicellate, non-functional stamens present or obsolete; staminate flowers long-pedicellate. Calyx membranous, 6-8-lobed; tube cup-shaped, 1.3-2 X 1.2-1.5 cm, densely pubescent outside and inside; lobes ovate, rounded at base, acute at apex, 2.3-2.8 x 0.9-1.2 cm, sparsely puberulent to pubescent outside and inside, contorted, persistent. Corolla 12-15-lobed, 5-7 cm long and 4.5-5.5 cm wide at anthesis, greenish yellow; tube obconical, 3.5-4.5 cm long, 1-1.3 cm wide at base and 2.5-3.5 cm wide at mouth, antrorse-pubescent outside and inside, densely pubescent at 4-5 mm from the base inside (glabrous below); lobes ovate, rounded at base, acute at apex, (2-)3-3.8 X 1-1.4 cm, minutely puberulent outside and inside, contorted. Stamens as many as the corolla lobes, included just below the mouth; filaments 1-2 mm long; anthers narrowly oblong, 12-14 X ca. 1 mm. Style included (only tips of branches exserted), approximately as long as corolla tube, terete, sparsely short-pubescent distally; style branches broadly clavate, minutely many-ribbed, 13-15 X 3-3.5 mm, microscopically (40X) foveolate. Young fruits oblong-ovoid, bilocular, with 13-18 seeds per locule, pubescent, crowned by the persistent calyx. Mature seeds unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Delprete, Piero G. 1999. Riodocea (Rubiaceae, Gardenieae), a new genus from the Brazilian Atlantic forest. Brittonia. 51: 15-23.

description: Caespitose epiphytes to 13 cm tall. Pseudobulbs small, complanate, 2 x 0.8 cm, sub-tended by 1-2 foliaceous bracts subequal and subsimilar to the leaf. Leaf 1, linear- lanceolate, acute, conduplicate, subcoria- ceous, 10-16 x 0.6 cm. Inflorescences short axillary racemes, to 6 cm long. Flowers 10, tubular, white with carmine spots. Dorsal sepal elliptic, cuneate, subacute, concave, 17 x 8 mm. Lateral sepals fused into a synsepal, oblong, concave-saccate, with apices free, 17 x 6 mm in natural position. Petals obliquely oblanceolate-elliptic, obtuse-rounded, 16 x 6 mm, held parallel to the column. Labellum obscurely 3-lobed, obovate, cuneate, emarginate, minutely apiculate, 24 x 11.5 mm when expanded, the lateral lobules erect, sublateral to the column wings, the callus a pair of longitudinal ridges from the base to the middle of the labellum with a smaller pair to the exterior. Column straight, 13 mm long, 7 mm broad across the triangular-falcate column wings. Anther rhomboid, 4 x 3 mm, the pollinarium 4.5 x 3 mm, the pollinia 2, cleft, the stipe oblanceolate, the viscidium minute, orbicular.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, David E. & Christenson, Eric A. 1995. New species of Peruvian Orchidaceae III. Brittonia. 47: 182-209.

description: Caespitose epiphytes to 15 cm tall. Pseudobulbs elliptic, complanate, ancipitous, 1.4 x 1.0 cm, 0.4 cm thick, enveloped at the base by 3-4 pairs of distichous, imbricating bracts, the upper pairs foliaceous and subequal to the leaf. Leaf 1, oblong, attenuate to shortly conduplicate base, otherwise flat, obliquely bilobed, obtuse, stiffly coriaceous, 7-14 x 2.4-3.0 cm, the margins uneven and lightly undulate. Inflorescences several, successively 5-7 densely flowered, fractiflex racemes from upper foliaceous bracts, shorter than the leaves. Flowers greenish-white becoming pure white after 2-3 days, the callus very pale yellow, with microscopic intercellular crystals. Dorsal sepal elliptic, blunt- ly obtuse, concave, 1.25 x 0.6 cm when expanded. Lateral sepals connate for their length in a cochleate, bidentate, conduplicate, basally saccate and scrotiform spur. Petals obovate, shallowly emarginate, con- cave, 1.3 x 0.65 cm. Labellum narrowly flabellate, emarginate, margins lightly undulate, deeply involute with the basal margins erect and partially enveloping the col umn, 1.4 x 0.6 cm; callus oblong, lightly concave, terminating in two low ribs diminishing and converging distally, the base thickened in a dorso-ventrally compressed, obtuse, hispidulous tip, shortly joined to the ventral column surface. Column clavate, semiterete below, ventral surface flat, 0.8 cm long, 0.15 (base)-0.3 (apex) cm across, excavated longitudinally below stigma for 0.2 cm, densely appressed hispid on basal third, with two minute flat triangular auricles appressed horizontally to ventral surface below anther bed. Stipe convex, obsaggitate, 0.16 x 0.875 cm. Pollinia 2.

description: Shrubs to subshrubs 10-200 cm tall, multistemmed, bark papery and whitish, or thin-coriaceous and light brown to blackish, exfoliating in small pieces; branches terete. Young branches glabrous to puberulent, dark green, terete; older branches rugose, terete. Stipules triangular, long-acuminate, glabrous outside, pubescent and with basal colleters inside, 4.5-6 mm long, 3-4 mm wide at base, persistent up to the third or fourth nodes, dark green; the older stipules sometimes dividing into two halves. Leaves 1.5-17 X 0.6-4.1 cm; narrowly elliptic, lanceolate to oblanceolate, acute at base and at apex (rarely short-acuminate); dark green above and pale green below, thinly foliaceous to coriaceous, drying olive-green; glabrous above and below (rarely puberulent below). Primary and secondary veins glabrous, slightly depressed above and prominent below, secondary veins 4-14 on each side; petioles 1-5 mm long, adaxially flattened; domatia absent. Inflorescences reduced-corymbose, (single-) few  to many flowered; 1-11 cm long, lateral branches 1- 2 pairs (rarely absent); rachis decussately compressed, rachis and branches glabrous to puberulent; terminal cymules with one to many flowers. Distal bracts linear, up to 9 mm long; bracteoles subtending the flowers narrowly triangular to linear, to 4 mm long. Flowers pedicellate, pedicels 2-15 mm long, glabrous to puberulent; hypanthium narrowly obconical, 3-5 X 2-3 mm, glabrous to puberulent. Calyx tube extremely reduced; calyx lobes linear, 3-12 x 1-3 mm; persistent. Corolla tubular and shortly lobed, 3.5-7.5 cm long, bright red, thinly fleshy when fresh; tube narrowly Funnel shaped basally constricted, curved or rectilinear, 2.1-6.3 cm long, 2-6 mm wide at base and 6-19 mm wide at the orifice, gla- brous outside and puberulent inside (with- out ring of hairs); corolla lobes 5, 5-14 X 3-7 mm, ovate, reflexed at anthesis, glabrous outside and inside. Stamens subsessile, filaments inserted at the sinuses of the corolla lobes; anthers narrowly elliptic, acute at both ends, 5-7 X 1-3 mm, dorsi-fixed near the center. Style exserted just above the corolla orifice, 3.7-7.8 cm long, medially to apically glabrous, basally puberulent, terminally broadened and with short reflexed stigmas, commonly unequal, 1.3-2 X ca. 0.9 mm, stigmatic surface smooth. Capsules obconical, turbinate to oblong, acute to rounded at base, truncate to rounded at apex, 12-26 X 6-9 mm, dark brown to black at maturity, capsule and disk glabrous; dehiscing explosively by contortion of the mesocarp (turning from fleshy to dry-woody); old capsules persisting on the stem. Seeds tetrahedral, truncate to uncinate at apex, 0.7-1.2 x 0.4-0.6 mm.

description: Fruit globose, 6 mm diam., with pericarp 0.8 mm thick, stigmatic remains subbasal-similar to Verschaffeltia, but the pericarp much thinner and with the mantle of brachysclereids thinner and less continuous; further characterized by tanniniferous cells that are sparse in the outer pericarp, but forming a massive mantle in the inner pericarp, with the vascular bundles flattened against that mantle, and by a very thick locular epidermis.

description: Much-branched shrubs 1-4 m tall. Stipules 0.2-0.3 cm long. Leaves subsessile or petiolate; petioles to 0.3 cm long; leaf blade elliptic, 1-5.5(-7) X 0.7-2.5(-3) cm, ob- tuse or acute at apex, attenuate to shortly attenuate at base, veins level adaxially, mid-rib and several of the secondary veins prominulous abaxially, tertiary veins and veinlets level on both sides, blade adaxially lightly sericeous when young, glabrescent, abaxially lightly sericeous when young, later mostly sericeous only on midrib and secondary veins. Flowers solitary and terminal. Calyx tube 0.2-0.4 cm, inside at base sericeous from a dense ring of hairs and colleters, lobes 0.3-0.6 cm long. Corolla tube 3-5(-6.5) cm long, outside ± antrorsely sericeous; lobes 1.2-3 X 0.4-1.3 cm. Anthers 0.6-0.8 cm long. Style 3-6.5 cm long, stigma lobes 0.3-0.5 cm long. Fruits spherical to ellipsoid, 1.5-3 cm long, 1-2 cm diam.; seeds 0.5-0.8 X 0.3-0.6 cm.

description: Shrubs or small trees to 4 m tall. Stipules ca. 0.3 cm long. Leaves subsessile or petiolate; petioles to 0.5 cm long on the long- shoots; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to obovate, 3.5-9 X 2-4 cm, acute to acuminate at apex, attenuate to shortly attenuate at base, all veins level adaxially or midrib and secondary veins immersed, abaxial side with midrib and several of the secondary veins prominulous, tertiary veins and veinlets level, leaf adaxially lightly sericeous when young, glabrescent, abaxially lightly sericeous when young, later mostly sericeous only on midrib and secondary veins. Flowers solitary and terminal. Calyx tube 0.4-0.6 cm long, hairs and colleters in a dense ring inside at base, lobes 0.4-0.9(-1.1) cm long. Corolla tube 6-10(-12) cm long, outside densely antrorsely sericeous, lobes 2.5-4.5 X 0.7-1.5 cm. Anthers 0.5-1 cm long. Style 6-12 cm long, stigma lobes 0.5- 0.8 cm long. Fruits subspherical to ellip- soidal, young fruits ± sericeous, to 4.5 cm long, to 2.5 cm diam.; seeds 0.5-0.8 X 0.3- 0.6 cm.

description: Shrubs or small trees 1-7 m tall. Stipules 0.3-0.6 cm long. Leaves subsessile or petiolate; petioles to 1 cm long on long-shoots; leaf blade elliptic to obovate, 4-12(-21) X 2-5(-7) cm, acute to acuminate at apex, at- tenuate to shortly attenuate at base, all veins level or midrib and secondary veins slightly immersed adaxially, midrib and several of the secondary veins prominulous abaxially, tertiary veins and veinlets level on both sides, blade adaxially lightly sericeous when young, glabrescent, abaxially lightly sericeous when young, later mostly sericeous only on midrib and secondary veins or glabrous. Flowers solitary and terminal. Calyx tube 0.5-1(-1.3) cm long, inside at base mostly with a dense ring of hairs and colleters or almost glabrous; lobes 0.6-1.7(-2.2) cm long. description: Inter congeneras stipulis pectinatis instructas maxime ut R. fissistipula Muell.-Arg. sed foliis subtus costa nervisque densius et inter nervos sparse pubescentibus, calyce extus glabro, corolla paulo breviore ab ea recedens. Arbor 3 m alta. Rami novelli 3.5-5.0 mm diam., puberuli, internodiis 3.0-4.5 cm longis, subcomplanatis; rami veteriores cortice griseo opaco vestiti. Folia petiolo puberulo-pubescente 1.0-1.5 cm longo instructa; lamina oblongo-elliptica, 16.5-19.0 cm longa et 6.7-8.4 cm lata, apice acuminata, basi paulum contracta, supra glabra et nitidula, sicc. olivacea, subtus costa nervisque densius, inter nervos sparse puberulo-pubescens, sicc. luteo-viridis, costa nervisque supra impressis, subtus prominentibus, venulis supra ubi e nervis oriuntur sicc. noduliforme prominulis, nervis utroque latere costae 8-10, reticulatione,laxa subtus prominula. Stipulae ovatae, margine pectinatae, ca. 13 mm longae, extus puberulae. Inflorescentia pedunculo 3.0-4.5 cm longo, dense puberulo-pubescente elata, e capitulis 3-5 composita; capitula lateralia ramulis 1-5 mm longis, capitulum terminale stipite usque ad 12 mm longo elatum; capitula e floribus 15-30 composita. Flores 5-meri, homostyli. Ovarium dense ferrugineo-pubescens. Calyx fere usque ad basim partitus, lobis anguste deltoideis, paulum inaequalibus, 3-4 mm longis, margine praesertim apicem versus ciliatis, ceterum glabris, sicc. nigrescentibus. Corolla alba, sicc. nigrescens, extus apicibus loborum sparse, ceterum densius puberulo-pubescens, tubo 4-5 cm longo et 1.8 mm diam., intus dimidio inferiore glabro, dimidio superiore piloso et ad orem subbarbato, lobis 7-9 mm longis et 1.5 mm latis, intus glabris, ad basim tamen barbatis, apicibus iam ante anthesim liberis. Stamina filamentis glabris ad incisuras corollae inserta; filamenta antheris dimidio breviora; antherae dorsifixae 2 mm longae, apice obtusae, thecis basi obtusis. Granula pollinis globosa, 48-50 It diam. Stylus glaber; stigmata 2 filiformia 1-2 mm longa, breviter exserta. Drupa nondum visa.

description: Arbor 5-metralis, ramulis glabris juvenilibus subquadrangularibus; stipulis late ovatis 16-20 mm longis in medio 10-13 mm latis extus minute puberulis irregulariter erosis laciniatisque ca 10 apicalibus longioribus 3-7 mm longis; foliis petiolatis petiolis 10-12 mm longis supra canaliculatis glabris; laminis subcoriaceis oblongo-ellipticis apice acute acuminatis basi acutis decurrentibusque 19-25 x 7.5-10.5 cm supra glabris subtus costa media nervisque minute sparsimque adpresso-puberulis; nervis later- alibus in quoque latere 9-10 adscendentibus supra sulcatis subtus elevatis ante marginem 10-12 mm conjunctis; inflorescentia conferta subcapitata sessili 11-18 mm longa 11-15 mm lata a stipula involventi partim occulta; calyce cum hypanthio 4.5 mm longo, hypanthio turbinato-campanulato 2 x 1.5- 1.8 mm glabro; calycis lobis quinque triangulari-lanceolatis subacutis 2.5 x 1-1.2 mm extus glabris marginibus valde ciliatis, basi inter lobos uniglanduliferis; disco cupulato umbonato 0.8 x 0.8 mm; corolla alba hypocrateriformi-subinfundibuliformi 2.7-3 cm longa, tubo angustato 20-23 mm longo 1- 1.5 mm lato in partem supremam usque 3 mm latam dilatato extus dense papillato-puberulo intus parte basilari 9 mm glabro fauce deorsum 12 mm pubescenti, lobis quinque lanceolato-oblongis obtusis 2.5 x 1.5 mm infra apicem appendiculo incurvato-cucullato angustato dorsum comiculatis, corniculo elongato 2-2.5 x 0.7 mm; antheris 1.5 x 0.7 mm paullo exsertis, filamentis ca 1 mm longis infra basin loborum corollae 2 mm insertis; stigmatibus linearibus 2.5 mm longis, stylo 22 mm longo glabro.

description: Arbor 5-metralis, ramulis glabris; stipulis obovato-flabelliformibus 1.5 x 0.8-0.9 cm profunde irregulariterque laciniatis glabris, lamina 7-10 x 8-9 mm; foliis petiolatis, petiolis 1.5-2.5 cm longis glabris; laminis oblongo-ellipticis apice abrupte acuminatis acumine 0.5-1.5 cm longo, basi cuneatim acutis 26-30 x 7-9 cm ubique glabris; nervis lateralibus utroque latere ca 4 supra obscuris subtus elevatis adscendentibus ante marginem 8-15 mm conjunctis; inflorescentia pedunculata terminali densi- et multiflora cymoso-capitata 2 x 2 cm, axibus lateralibus brevissimis, pedunculo 20 x 2 mm minute puberulo; floribus sessilibus; calyce cum hypanthio 2.2 mm longo extus dense puberulo, hypanthio cupulato 1.2 mm longo 2 mm lato; calycis lobis quinque late ovatis acutis 1 x 0.8 mm ciliolatis; disco prominenti 1 mm longo 1.2-1.5 mm lato lobos calycis aequanti vel superanti; corolla subhypocrateriformi 9 cm longa, tubo 8.2 cm longo plerumque 1.5-2 mm lato praeter partem supremam 13-15 mm ubi 2-2.5 mm lato extus sparsim papillato-puberulo intus glabro vel fere, lobis ligulatis 10.5 x 1.5 mm apice rotundato-obtusis paullo inflexo-cucullatis dorso paullo appendiculatis extus sparsim papillato-puberulis intus papillatis; antheris exsertis linearibus 4-4.5 x 0.8 mm, filamentis 4- 5 mm longis glabris in fauce insertis; stylo glabro tubo corollae aequilongo.

description: Shrub 3-5 m tall, much branched and with slender branches, outer branches often scandent; young branches glabrous and dark green, terete; older branches terete, pale brown to grayish and with sparse punctiform to linear lenticels. Stipules present only in bud, narrowly triangular, glabrous outside, glabrous and with few colleters inside, 30-40 mm long, 5-6 mm wide at base, dark green, leaving a linear whitish scar ca. 0.5 mm wide. Leaves petiolate, petioles 2-7.5 cm long, 2.5-4.5 mm thick, subterete, glabrous to hirsutulous; basally thickened but not pulvinated; blades 28-40 (53) cm long, 8.5-12 cm wide, length:width 3-3.5:1; narrowly lanceolate, oblanceolate to narrowly elliptic, acute at base, acute at apex, sometimes tapering to an acumen 2- 3 cm long, dark green above and pale green below, subcoriaceous; drying brown, stiff chartaceous; glabrous above, glabrous thirsutulous below, pellucid punctate. Pri- mary and secondary veins glabrous to hirsutulous and prominent below, secondary veins 15-25 each side; tertiary veins starting subparallel and openly reticulate in the center, evident below. Domatia absent. Inflorescences racemoid secundiflorous panicles to thyrsoid-secundiflorous with opposite or subopposite decussate branches, sometimes without lateral branches, 25-60 cm long, up to 17 cm wide, basal branches up to 20 cm long, lateral branches usually ascending 0-4 pairs, basal portion of axis not branched 2-15 cm long. Rachis terete, rachis and branches glabrous (rarely hirsutulous); flowers alternate on distal branches or rarely in cymules (the pedicels opposite or alternate and twisted downward and secund). Distal bracts 1-3 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, deltoid; bracteoles subtending the flowers 0.5-0.8 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, deltoid, glabrous. Flowers pedicellate, pedicel 4-25 mm long, glabrous to hirtellous; hypanthium narrowly obconical, 4-6 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, glabrous to hirtellous. Calyx reduced to a wavy margin with barely distinguishable lobes, ca. 1 mm long and persistent. Corolla tubular with lobes barely opening (not spreading), 2.5-4 cm long, flower bud cylindrical, greenish yellow (rarely pinkish yellow), semi-fleshy when fresh; tube subcylindrical and faintly striate, 1.5-2.5 cm long, 2.5-4 mm wide at base and 3.5-5 mm wide at the orifice, gla- brous outside; introrse-strigose at base inside, without a ring of hairs, the remaining medial and superior zone glabrous; corolla lobes 5, 9-13 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide at base, triangular to ovate, glabrous outside, glabrous and with minute conicalbullate hairs (hairs 0.1-0.3 mm long) throughout inside. Corolla lobes 1/4  to 1/3 of corolla length. Stamens 5, included (only the very tip exserted), subequal, filaments attached 4.5-5.5 mm from the base of the tube, anthers cylindrical and rectilinear (never convex), 9-12 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, dorsifixed near the base, base elliptic, smooth throughout; filaments 6-7 mm long, wide and flattened at base, microscopically (40X) papillose throughout and minutely barbate at base with white puberulent hairs. Style exserted, 30-40 mm long, glabrous and microscopically (40X) papillose, style branches ovate, 1-1.5 mm long, stigmatic surface smooth. Immature fruits reddish green, carnose. Capsules obovoid to oblong, shallowly hemispherical, (1)1.5-2 mm long, 7-9 mm wide, black and without lenticels, capsule and disk dark brown and glabrous, disk obviously exceeding the calyx; dehiscing loculicidally, disk-septicidal dehiscence absent even in old capsules.

description: Plants similar to S. palmetto but acaulescent, with 3-6 yellow-green leaves, petiole 40-60 cm long, 1-2 cm wide; hastula narrowly triangular, 1.5-5 cm long; segments 35-65, bifid, filiferous, 50-76 cm long, 1.5-3.5 cm wide. Inflorescence paniculate, horizontal-arcuate, loosely branched with 3 orders of branching. Flowers subsessile, perfect, white; calyx cup-shaped, 1-1.4 mm long, 3-lobed; petals 3, 3.3-3.7 mm long, ovate; stamens 6, as long as petals; connate at the base and basally adnate to the petals; gynoecium composed of 3 fused carpels, 2.5-3.5 mm long; ovary superior; stigma papillose. Fruit a 1-seeded berry developing from one carpel, globose, shiny, black, 15-19 mm in diam with a thick fleshy pericarp; seed oblate, concave on the funicular end, 10-11 mm in diam, brown; embryo sublateral; endosperm homogeneous, bony.

description: Planta scandens, caulibus indumento dimorpho vestitis, dense villosis pilis longioribus patentibus 1.5-2 mm longis cum pilis brevissimis crispatis adpressis commixtis; stipulis reflexis suborbiculariovatis cuspidatis 8-14 x 9 mm extus strigosis pilis 1.5 mm longis intus glabris, marginibus pilis 1.5 mm longis ciliatis; foliis petiolatis, petiolis 1-2.5 cm longis dense villosis, pilis divaricatis; laminis membranaceis ovatis vel oblongo-ovatis apice acuminatis basi rotundatis vel raro acutis 10-12 x 5.5-7 cm supra molliter dense villosis pilis 1-1.5 mm longis subtus molliter dense villosis costa media nervis lateralibus pilis 1.5-2 mm vestitis; nervis lateralibus in quoque latere 13-20 divaricate adscendentibus secus margines curvatis; inflorescentiis umbellatim densifloris 2.5-3 cm diam brevipedunculatis, pedunculo 5 mm longo dense villosulo; floribus numerosis fasciculate vel umbellatim aggregatis pedicellatis ad apicem ramulorum primariorum breviorum dispositis, ramulis 2-3 mm longis glabris, pedicellis 1.5-7 mm longis sparsim hirsutis; calyce cum hypanthio 7.5-9 mm longo villoso, hypanthio cupulato-campanulato 1.5 mm longo 1.5-1.8 mm lato hirsutulo demum glabrescenti; calycis tubo 1.5 mm alto 2 mm lato extus hirsutulo demum glabrescenti, lobis quinque oblongo-lanceolatis vel oblanceolatis acutis 5-6 x 2.5 mm (in sicco brevioribus) extus moderatim hirsutis pilis divaricatis 0.8-1 mm longis intus sparsim hirsutulis, marginibus ciliatis, in sinubus inter lobos 1-2-glanduliferis; corollis subinfundibuliformibus, tubo 8-9 x 2 mm, extus hirsutulo pilis adscendentibus praedito intus faucem dense villosulo parte suprema 2.5 mm puberula ceterum glabro, lobis quinque oblongo-lanceolatis acutis 3 x 1.7 mm extus hirsutulis intus praeter basin hirsutulam papillatis; antheris linearibus 3 mm subsessilibus, filamentis 0.5 mm longis superne infra basin loborum corollae insertis.

description: Pubescent shrub to ca. 1 m tall, the non- glandular trichomes to ca. 1 mm long. Twigs 3-5 mm diam., densely white- to yellowish-tomentose; internodes 4-16 mm long. Leaf blade 2-5 X 1-2.7 cm, ovate to elliptic, acute to acuminate at apex, acute and decurrent at base, coriaceous; margin serrulate to crenulate in the ca. upper 2/3 of blade; adaxial surface densely appressed silvery-sericeous, veins impressed; abaxial surface white- to yellowish-tomentose, with 3-5 orders of raised veins apparent through the indument. Petiole 2-6 mm long, whit- ish- to yellowish-tomentose. Principal inflorescence axis 4.5-7 cm long, densely white- to yellowish-tomentose; verticillasters densely clustered along the axis; internodes 4-9 mm long; cymes usually with 2-5 flowers; pedicels 2-5 mm long, densely white- to yellowish-tomentose; bracts 13- 21 X 6-11 mm, ovate to elliptic, apically cuspidate, entire-margined, caducous, whitish-tomentose on the abaxial surface. Calyx 11-14 mm long, 3-4 mm wide just below throat, densely white- to dull yellowish-to- mentose; upper lobe 2.5-4 mm long, acute to acuminate; lower lobes 1.5-3 mm long, acute. Corolla 21-28 mm long, 3-4 mm wide just below throat, pink to lavender; moderately to densely whitish-pubescent on all portions exceeding the calyx except the central lobe of the lower lip; upper lip 5-7 mm long; lower lip 3-5 mm long. Stamen filaments 4-5 mm long, usually with a short apical extension (0.3-0.7 mm long); connectives 22-27 mm long, the portion anterior to the filaments 9-12 mm long; pollen sacs 1.7-2 mm long. Style 28-37 mm long. Ovary 1.8-2.1 X 1.3-1.7 mm. Nutlets 2.1- 2.5 X 1.1-1.2 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Torke, Benjamin M. 2000. A revision of Salvia sect. Ekmania (Lamiaceae). Brittonia. 52: 265-302.

description: Pubescent shrub to ca. 4.5 m tall, the non-glandular trichomes often twisting, to ca. 0.6 mm long. Twigs 2-6 mm diam., densely cream- to yellowish-tomentose; internodes 5-50 mm long. Leaf blade 4-18 X 2.3-4.8 cm, elliptic-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, acute to acuminate at apex, rounded to acute at base, coriaceous; margin serrate to serrulate in the upper ca. 3/5 of blade; adaxial surface lustrous, dark- green when fresh, finely pubescent, veins impressed; abaxial surface light green, cream- to yellowish-tomentose, with 4-5 orders of conspicuously raised veins. Petiole 5-30 mm long, cream- to yellowish-to- mentose. Principal inflorescence axis 7-25 cm long, densely cream-colored to dull-yellowish tomentose; verticillasters moderately spaced along the axes; internodes 9-26 mm long; cymes usually with 2-5 flowers; ped- icels 2-5 mm long, densely cream- to yellowish-tomentose; bracts 11-18 X 4-8 mm, light-gray, ovate to elliptic, apically cuspidate, entire-margined, caducous, cream- to yellowish-tomentose on the abaxial surface. Calyx 8-12 mm long, 2.8-3.5 mm wide just below throat, densely cream- to yellowish-tomentose; upper lobe 1.5-3.2 mm long, acute; lower lobes 1.2-3 mm long, acute. Corolla 19-26 mm long, 3.2-4.2 mm wide just below throat, yellow to red, moderately to densely whitish-pubescent on all portions exceeding the calyx except the central lobe of the lower lip; upper lip 3-5 mm long; lower lip 2-3 mm long. Stamen filaments 3-5 mm long, with a short apical extension (0.3-0.7 mm long); connectives 19-29 mm long, the portion anterior to the filaments 8.5-13 mm long; pollen sacs 1.8-2.1 mm long. Style 27-36 mm long. Ovary 2-2.6 X 1.5-1.9 mm. Nutlets 2.1-2.8 X 1.1-1.4 mm.

description: Arbuscula caulibus supremis gracilibus ad flores pilis ramosis albidis inferne glabratis; foliis ovatis supremis 5-6 cm longis breviter acuminatis in basi ad petiolos 1 cm longos extenuatis crenato-serratis, pagina superiore sparse hirsuta, inferiore venulosa pilis ramosis sat flocculosa; floribus in spicis sat densioribus confertis, pedicellis 5-6 mm longis elatis, verticillis bracteis deciduis subtentis; calycum florentium 8 mm longorum labia superiore subrotundata 7-9 venis, quam inferior paulo longiore, utrimque pilis ramosis albofloccosis; corollarum vio-lacearum tubo eirciter 11 mm longo intus nudo, recto, labiis subaequilongis; staminibus ad fauces positis, gubernaculo subintegro vel obscure assurgenti- dentato, in labia superiore incluso; stylo utrimque hirsuto, ramo postico longiore; nuculis 2 mm longis ovatis.

description: Pubescent shrub to ca. 4 m tall, the nonglandular trichomes appressed, often twisting, to ca. 0.5 mm long. Twigs 2-6 mm diam., whitish- to yellowish-pubescent; internodes 5-35 mm long. Leaf blade 3-15 X 1.2-4 cm, elliptic-lanceolate to oblanceo- late, acute to acuminate at apex, acute and often decurrent at base, coriaceous; margin serrate to serrulate in the upper ca. 3/5 of blade; adaxial surface lustrous or not, dark- green when fresh, usually somewhat bullate, finely pubescent, veins impressed; abaxial surface, dull-green when fresh, areolate, grayish-pubescent, with 4-5 orders of raised venation. Petiole 4-20(-34) mm long, whitish- to yellowish-pubescent. Principal inflorescence axis 5-20 cm long, whitish- to yellowish-pubescent; verticillasters moderately spaced along the axes; internodes 5-25 mm long; cymes usually with 2-5 flowers; pedicels 1-4 mm long, whit- ish- to yellowish-pubescent; bracts 10-30 X 3-14 mm, obovate to elliptic, apically cuspidate, entire-margined, membranaceous, caducous, lavender or green (and then usually lavender-tinged), sparsely pu- bescent on the abaxial surface. Calyx 8-12 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide just below throat, whitish- to yellowish-pubescent with appressed trichomes; upper lobe 2.2-3.8 mm long, acute; lower lobes 1.5-3.5 mm long, acute. Corolla 18-28 mm long, 3.1-4.3 mm wide just below throat, yellow, moderately whitish pubescent on all portions exceeding the calyx except the central lobe of the lower lip; upper lip 4-6 mm long; lower lip 3- 5 mm long. Stamen filaments 3.5-5 mm long, with a short (0.4-0.8 mm) apical extension; connectives 20-28 mm long, the portion anterior to the filaments 9-13 mm long; pollen sacs 1.7-2.2 mm long. Style 26-38 mm long. Ovary 1.9-3 X 1.4-1.8 mm. Nutlets 2.1-3.2 X 1-1.6 mm.

description: Pubescent shrub to ca. 2 m tall, the non-glandular trichomes often twisting, to ca. 1 mm long. Twigs 2.5-6(-10) mm diam., moderately snow-white pubescent to tomentose; internodes 5-30 mm long. Leaf blade 4-15 X 2.2-6.5 cm, elliptic to obovate, acute at apex, acute to rounded at base, coriaceous; margin serrate to crenate in the upper ca. 2/3 of blade; adaxial surface dull to lustrous, dark green when fresh, white-pubescent, smooth between second- ary veins, with the midvein raised; abaxial surface minutely white-tomentose, with 5 orders of raised venation. Petiole 5-40 mm long, moderately to densely white-tomentose. Principal inflorescence axis 5-20 cm long, densely white-tomentose; verticillasters moderately spaced along the axes; internodes 5-20 mm long; cymes usually with 2-6 flowers; pedicels 1-4 mm long, densely white-tomentose; bracts 11-17 X 4.5-6 mm, obovate to elliptic, apically cuspidate, entire-margined, caducous, green or gray, white-tomentose on the abaxial surface. Calyx 8-11 mm long, 2.8-4 mm wide just below throat, densely white-appressed pubescent to tomentose; upper lobe 3-4.5 mm long, acute to acuminate; lower lobes 2.7-3.8 mm long, acute to acuminate. Style 25- 36 mm long. Ovary 1.8-2.3 X 1.3-1.8 mm. Nutlets 2.1-2.6 X 1.1-1.3 mm.

description: Much branched spreading shrubs 2-8 dm tall, 3-12 dm wide, typically broader than high; leaves opposite with axillary fascicles, cinereous, canescent with numerous scattered resin droplets on both surfaces, the blade obovate to spatulate, (16) 20-40 (50) mm long, (5) 8-22 (30) mm wide, the widest point (7) 10-26 (30) mm from the base, gradually narrowed to the petiole-base, the margin entire, seldom crenulate, apically acute or more often rounded, rarely truncate or emar- ginate, the petiole (6) 7-15 (20) mm long; inflorescences verticillate, conspicu- ously bracteate, the mature glomerules 10-20 (30) mm long, 20-45 (50) mm wide, 7-27 (30) mm apart, (1) 2-5 (6) on mostly terminal branchlets; bracts scarious, purple to rose, often greenish near the base, seldom entirely greenish-yellow, roughened, scurfy to scabrellous or occasionally scabrous with scattered resin droplets on the abaxial surface, the hairs septate with mostly 1 septum, the adaxial surface scabrellous to scabrous, the margin short to moderately ciliate with sep- tate hairs, the outer bracts ovate to elliptic or less often orbicular, (9) 12-20 (27) mm long, (4) 5-13 (20) mm wide, the apex rounded, truncate or cuspidate and often weakly spinescent, rarely emarginate, the inner bracts elliptic to spatulate, up to 13 (17) mm long and 6 (11) mm wide, with rounded or acute and weakly spinescent apices; calyx purple to rose, generally greenish basally, seldom en- tirely greenish-yellow, 7-12 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, more or less cylindrical, scurfy, scabrous or scabrellous with scattered resin droplets on the abaxial sur- face, the adaxial surface scabrous, the margins ciliate, the 2 lower lobes rounded or cuneate, often weakly spinescent apically, 1-3 mm long, the upper 2 usually united into 1; corolla blue to rose, (12) 17-23 (28) mm long with a white to cream tube (7) 13-18 (23) mm long, with a ring of villous hairs below the middle within, the upper lip ovate, bilobed or infrequently united, the 2 lateral lobes of the lower lip entire or erose, the middle lobe broadly obovate, erose or more often emar- ginate, always exserted beyond the lateral 2; style (14) 20-30 (35) mm long; sta- mens exserted 5-8 (10) mm beyond the corolla lobes (including a 1.5-2 mm long anther) and inserted on the throat (7) 14-16 (21) mm from the base of the tube, the filaments (4) 6-7 (8) mm long, the connectives 3-6 mm long, obliquely joined to the filament, the upper pair of stamens poorly developed, 1-7 mm long or lacking; description: Erect shrub to ca 3 m tall. Twigs gray-brown, quadrangular, 2-4 mm in diam, nodose, sulcate, each face with a longitudinal groove, 0.4-0.6 mm across, with internodes 1-3.7 cm long, appressed-pubescent with a dense covering of silvery, unbranched, multicellular hairs, to ca 0.5 mm long. Leaves opposite, clustered toward tips of twigs; blade 3.2-11.5 cm long, 1.6-4.5 cm wide, obovate, rarely elliptic, coriaceous, the petiole 0.7-2.3 cm long, just below the inflorescences smaller, the blade 1.9-2.7 x 0.7-1 cm, sessile or with petioles to ca 1.5 mm long, the apex short-acuminate or acute, the base cuneate or slightly decurrent, the margin conspicuously serrate in distal ca 3/4 of blade, plane; venation eucamptodromous, with 4-7 pairs of secondary veins, the midvein and secondary veins impressed adaxially, all venation prominently raised abaxially; adaxial surface green, shiny when fresh, glabrous except for a few scattered hairs similar to those on stem concentrated in impressions of veins; abaxial surface light gray, densely appressed-pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem, glandular-punctate. In- florescences racemose, terminal and axillary, composed of pseudoverticillate re- duced cymes borne along an unbranched or less commonly 1-branched indeter- minate axis, 4.5-8.7 cm long, 2.9-5.1 cm wide, forming a congested paniculate cluster distally on shoot, the internodes separating whorls of flowers 0.4-1.5 cm long; axes appressed-pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem; bracts caducous, green and moderately to heavily red-tinged when fresh, ovate, 18-24 mm long, 6-11 mm wide, the adaxial surface essentially glabrous, the abaxial surface appressed-pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem, the margin entire, pubescent, the apex acuminate, rarely acute; pedicels 2.7-6.5 mm long. Flowers zygomorphic. Calyx 9-costate, usually 3-lobed, with 3 veins entering upper lobe, 1 1-15 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, green and heavily red-tinged when fresh, drying gray-brown, densely appressed-pubescent externally with hairs similar to those on stem, glandular-punctate, the tube glabrous internally, the upper and 2 lateral lobes ovate, ca 5 mm long, pubescent internally, with acuminate, falcate apices. Corolla bilabiate, uniformly pale yellow to very lightly tinged with orange-red on margins of lips with age, 26-28 mm long, pubescent on portion exceeding calyx with hairs similar to those on stem, glandular-punctate, the tube ca 21 x 5 mm, epapillate; upper lip ca 7 x 3.5 mm, emarginate, margin slightly erose; lower lip 3-lobed, ca 6 x 7 mm, the center lobe ca 4.5 mm across, emarginate, margin entire, the lateral lobes smaller, rounded, margins slightly erose. Stamens 2, epipetalous, exserted; filaments ca 3.8 mm long, sparsely pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem; connectives 24-30 mm long, sparsely pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem, portions anterior to filament ca 12 mm long, +/- cylindrical, portions posterior to filament (rudders) becoming flattened, almost gla- brous, free at ends, otherwise coherent to connate; anther sacs 4-4.3 mm long, appearing versatile, becoming strongly curved after dehiscence. Style ca 35 mm long, +/- cylindrical, adpressed to upper lip by androecium, very sparsely pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem, appearing unbranched, but branching ca 1.4 mm below the apex, with a vestigial branch, ca 0.4 mm long, borne in a slight depression (Fig. 1G). Ovary superior, 1.4-1.8 mm long, 1.2-1.6 mm wide, glabrous, the apical ca 1 x 1 mm deeply 4-lobed, the basal disc prolonged into an adjacent, abaxial, irregularly-lobed nectar gland (gynobase horn) to ca 2.3 mm long (Fig. 1H, 11). Nutlets 4, or fewer by abortion, ca 2 x 1.2 mm, chestnut- brown, smooth, glabrous. Flowering December-February, fruiting March-June.

description: Pubescent shrub to ca. 5 m tall, the non-glandular trichomes fairly straight, silvery, to ca. 0.4 mm long. Twigs 2-6 mm diam., appressed-pubescent; internodes 8-60 mm long. Leaf blade 4.5-20 X 2.9-6.3 cm, obovate to elliptic or oblanceolate, acute to acuminate at apex, acute and often decurrent at base, coriaceous; margin serrate in the upper ca. 3/4 of blade; adaxial surface lustrous, green when fresh, nearly glabrous, with impressed veins; abaxial surface light-gray, minutely appressed-pubescent, with 5 orders of raised venation. Stamen filaments 3.3-4.2 mm long, with a short (0.3-0.5 mm) apical extension; connectives 24-32 mm long, the portion anterior to the filaments 11-14 mm long; pollen sacs 2.5-3 mm long. Style 33- 39 mm long. Ovary 1.8-2.5 X 1.3-1.8 mm. Nutlets 2-2.5 X 1.1-1.3 mm.

description: Herbae perennes 2-3 m altae. Caulis pilis appressis albis recurvatis multicellularibus pubescens. Foliorum laminae 6-14 x 2-6.3 cm, ovatae usque ovato-lanceolatae, apice acuminatae, basi cordatae. Racemi 0.3-1.5 m longi, cujusque verticillastri floribus 6-25. Calyx 6-7 mm longus, ca 3 mm latus, extus albolanatus. Corolla 3.2-3.4 cm longa, splendide rubra, siccate purpurascens; tubo prope basem constricta, intus prope basem in parem papillarum invaginato. Stamina corollam partim excedentia. Stylus corollae staminibus longior. Semina atro-fusca.

description: Perennial erect herbs 2-3 m tall; stem 4-angled, deeply sulcate on all sides, appressed-pubescent with white recurved multicellular hairs. Petioles 0.3-3.6 cm long, the indumentum as in stem; leaf-blades ovate to ovate-lanceolate, acuminate at tip, cordate at base, 6-14 x 2-6.3 cm, crenate-serrate, with 10-12 pairs of nerves, strigose above, pilose beneath, especially along nerves, this surface glanddotted. Inflorescence of terminal interrupted unbranched racemes (0.3-1.5 m long) of verticillasters, 6-25 or more flowers standing 0.5-6 cm apart; the axis appressed pubescent with white recurved hairs. Bracts ca 6 x 2 mm, ovate, acuminate, white pilose on back, erect, later spreading, early deciduous. Calyx 6-7 x ca 3 mm, white-woolly on the outside, glabrous within, 2-lipped, upper lip (3-nerved), 1- and lower one 2-lobed, the lobes caudate-acuminate, the acumens elongating (by 1 mm) in fruiting calyces. Corolla 3.2-3.4 cm long (tube ca 1.9 cm long, 0.45 cm wide), bright red when fresh, drying purple, pilose with multicellular hairs on the outside except towards the base and lower lip, the tube constricted near base on the lower side, invaginated into a pair of ca 1.5 mm long papillae; upper lip ca 1.5 cm long, greatly exceeding the lower, emarginate, galeate, lower lip ca 9 x 8 mm, reflexed, 3-lobed, the lateral lobes shorter, the middle one larger, all rounded. Stamens 2, exceeding the corolla by 1-1.5 mm, connective produced, 1.2-1.4 cm long, articulated on a ca 5 mm long filament, bearing ca 3 mm long anthers at end of upper arm, the lower reduced, stamen rudder ca 6 mm long, bearing a downward pointed minute tooth near intersection with filament. Style 3.7-3.9 cm long, exceeding corolla and stamens, divided into 2 unequal arms (upper longer), bearded. Gynobase horn ca 1 mm high; nutlets ca 1.5 x 1 mm, dark brown, shiny. Flowering August-September.

description: Herba perennis fragrans ut videtur alta ramis supremis pilis crassioribus intricate villosis; foliis superioribus ovatis vel ovato-lanceolatis in basi angustatis rarioribus rotundatis (? inferioribus fortasse truneatis etiam cordatis), pagina superiore villosa, inferiore ad venas villosa et valde punctulata, petiolis 5-6 cm longis (? et ultra) elatis; floribus in spicis densis in foliorum supremorum axillis dispositis, bracteis ovato-aduminatis sat firmis subintegris 1-2 cm longis longe perstatis subtentis demum deciduis, ad margines inferiores pilosis; calycibus florentibus eirciter 9 mm longis, labia superiore quam inferior duplo longiore attenuata, ambabus hirtellis et pilis sparsis ornatis, petiolis subnullis; corollarunm caerulearum tubo eirciter 6 mm longo intus nudo leniter ventricoso, labiis sub-aequilongis, extus et tubo glandulis sessilibus aureis dense conspersis; staminibus in labia superiore ut videtur inclusis vel parce exsertis, gubernaculo dente sat magno assurgente ornato; stylo glabro, ramo superiore triplove longiore.

description: Arbuscula parva multiramosa ut videtur reptans et ad humus extensa, ramulis inferne ad sulcis minute puberulis sed autem superne pilis longioribus glandulosis sparse pilosis; foliis crebris parvissimis 5-6 mm longis linearibus utrimque minute hirtellis etiam valde et dense punctulatis; floribus paucis in racemis 5-6 cm longis dispositis, oppositis, bracteis perstantibus foliolosis tamen latioribus ovatis 3-4 mm longis subtentis, petiolis gracilibus 3-5 mm longis elatis; calycibus florentibus eirciter 6 mm longis, labia superiore 5-venis, extus pilis longioribus glandulosis eis ramulorum similibus, in maturitate 8 mm longis sat amplis; corollarum albarum tubo eirciter 9 mm longo, cylindrato, intus papillis duobus parvis ornato; staminibus ad fauces positis in labia superiore inclusis, gubernaculo dente retrorso ornato; stylo utrimque hirtello, ramo postico longiore; nuculis glabris 2 mm longis.

description: Suffrutex vel herba ut videtur erecta et ramis lateralibus elongatis gracilibus extensis, ramulis et foliis utrinque pilis ramosis cinereo-puberulis; foliis maiori- bus 8-10 cm longis, ovatis, acuminatis, ad petiolos obscuros cuneato-angustatis, marginibus obscure crenatis, pagina inferiore pallida; foliis ramulorum deminutorum similibus remotis; floribus in spicas laxas ad apices ramorum lateralium gracilium 7.5-18 cm longorum positis, verticillastris plurifloris; calycibus ramoso-hirtellis 8 mm longis, labiis subaequalibus, superioribus integris vel obscure trimucronatis; corollarum atrocyanearum tubo 13-14 mm longo, intus nudo, labio inferiore 9 mm longo, superiore 6 mm longo, stylo hirsuto; nuculis non visis.

description: Pubescent shrub to ca. 3 m tall, the non-glandular trichomes coarse, erect, conspicuously thickened at the base, silvery, to ca. 0.7 long. Twigs 2-6 mm diam., scabrous- pubescent; internodes 8-60 mm long. Leaf blade 3.5-11 X 1.7-5.5 cm, elliptic to ovate, acute to rounded at apex, acute and often decurrent at base, coriaceous; margin serrate in the upper ca. 3/5 of blade; adaxial surface lustrous, dark-green when fresh, scabrous-pubescent (sometimes only on the veins), with the midvein and lateral veins often somewhat raised; abaxial surface dull-green when fresh, scabrous-pubescent, with 4-5 orders of raised venation. Petiole 5-32 mm long, scabrous pubescent. Principal inflorescence axis 8-25 cm long, scabrous- pubescent; verticillasters widely spaced to densely clustered; internodes 5-38 mm long, cymes usually with 2-8 flowers; pedicels 2-5 mm long, pubescent; bracts 17- 41 X 6-27 mm, broadly ovate (the lower- most often somewhat petiolate), apically cuspidate, serrate-margined or subentire (with at least a few teeth along the margin), with 5-9 more or less parallel veins arising from near the base, usually persisting throughout flowering and then falling, red to orange or green and red-tinged; the abaxial surface minutely pubescent. Calyx 11-15 mm long, 3-4 mm wide just below throat, pubescent; upper lobe 3.3-6 mm long, acuminate; lower lobes 3-4 mm long, acuminate. Corolla 28-33 mm long, 5.5- 6.2 mm wide just below throat, orange to red, sparsely to moderately whitish-pubescent on all portions exceeding the calyx except the central lobe of the lower lip; upper lip 5.8-6.2 mm long; lower lip 5.5-6 mm long. Stamen filaments 3-4 mm long; connectives 31-35 mm long, the portion anterior to the filaments 11-14 mm long; pollen sacs 2.9-3.3 mm long. Style 36-44 mm long. Ovary 1.8-2.2 X 1.3-1.7 mm. Nutlets 2-2.4 x 1-1.2 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Torke, Benjamin M. 2000. A revision of Salvia sect. Ekmania (Lamiaceae). Brittonia. 52: 265-302.

description: Pubescent shrub to ca. 2.5 m tall, the non-glandular trichomes erect and arching to appressed, to ca. 0.4 mm long. Twigs 2-6 mm diam., whitish pubescent; internodes 8-53 mm long. Leaf blade 3.5-14 X 1.3- 4.6 cm, ovate-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate (rarely broadly ovate to elliptic), acute to acuminate at apex, acute to rounded at base, coriaceous; margins serrate to crenate in the upper ca. 3/5 of blade; adaxial surface lustrous, dark-green when fresh, nearly glabrous except for a few trichomes on the veins, with the midvein slightly raised above, abaxial surface light-green when fresh, areolate, minutely whitish-pubescent, with 5 orders of raised venation. Petiole 8- 31 mm long, moderately pubescent. Principal inflorescence axis 4-13 cm long, moderately to densely whitish-pubescent; verticillasters moderately spaced; inter- nodes 5-31 mm long; cymes usually with 2-9 flowers; pedicels 2-9 mm long, mod- erately to densely whitish-pubescent; bracts 15-30 X 8-13 mm, ovate to broadly obovate, apically cuspidate, entire-margined or with several teeth (rarely serrate), sparsely pubescent to nearly glabrous on the abaxial surface, usually persisting throughout flowering and then falling, red or green and red-tinged. Calyx 12-17 mm long, 3.5-6 mm wide just below throat, red or green and red-tinged, sparsely to densely whitish-pubescent; upper lobe 3.2-8 mm long, acuminate; lower lobes 3-7 mm long, acuminate. Corolla 27-34 mm long, 5-6 mm wide just below throat, red to orange, finely whitish-pubescent on all portions exceeding the calyx except the central lobe of the lower lip; upper lip 5-7 mm long; lower lip 3- 5.5 mm long. Stamen filaments 2.7-3.3 mm long; connectives 29-36 mm long, the por- tion anterior to the filaments 13-15 mm long; pollen sacs 3-4 mm long. Style 37-44 mm long. Ovary 2.6-3.1 X 1.9-2.3 mm. Nutlets 3-3.5 X 1.5-1.8 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Torke, Benjamin M. 2000. A revision of Salvia sect. Ekmania (Lamiaceae). Brittonia. 52: 265-302.

description: Pubescent shrub to ca. 2 m tall, the non-glandular trichomes erect, thickened at the base, fairly straight, to ca. 1 mm long. Twigs 2-6 mm diam., densely golden-yellow pubescent; internodes 13-90 mm long. Leaf blade 4-15 X 1-3.6 cm, lanceolate to ovate, acute to acuminate at apex, acute and often decurrent at base, coriaceous; margins serrate to crenate in the upper ca. 3/5 of blade; adaxial surface lustrous, green when fresh, pubescent, with impressed veins; abaxial surface densely yellow-pubescent, with 4-5 orders of raised veins. Petiole 3- 30 mm long, densely golden-yellow pubescent. Principal inflorescence axis 8-24 cm, densely golden-yellow pubescent; verticillasters moderately clustered; internodes 5-28 mm long; cymes usually with 2-9 flowers; pedicels 2-10 mm long, densely golden-yellow pubescent; bracts 10-37 X 7-22 mm, ovate to elliptic, apically cuspidate, caducous, green, often red-tinged when fresh; the abaxial surface moderately to densely pubescent. Calyx 11-15 mm long, 3.5-4.5 mm wide just below throat, densely golden-yellow pubescent (turning reddish with age); upper lobe 2.8-5.5 mm long, acute to acuminate; lower lobes 2.1-4.5 mm long, acute to acuminate. Corolla 20-29 mm long, 3.5-4.5 mm wide just below throat, yellow (and often red-tinged) to red, densely pubescent on all portions exceeding the calyx except the central lobe of the lower lip; upper lip 4-5.5 mm long; lower lip 3-4.5 mm long. Stamen filaments 2.5-3.8 mm long, usually with a short (0.3-0.6 mm) apical projection; connectives 20-30 mm long, the portion anterior to the filaments 9-14 mm long; pollen sacs 1.8-2.5 mm long. Style 28-35 mm long. Ovary 2-2.7 X 1.5-1.9 mm. Nutlets 2.2-2.9 X 1.1-1.5 mm.

description: Fruit 7-7.3 mm diam., pericarp 1.5 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-similar to Dictyosperma and Clinostigma, but with a distinctive series of large vascular bundles with very thick fibrous sheaths in mid-pericarp, a papillate epidermis, many large brachysclereids loosely distributed in the outer third of the pericarp, raphide-bearing cells frequent in the outer pericarp, and tanniniferous cells confined to the inner pericarp and rather few in number.

description: Sufrútice densamnente foliado de hasta 1,5 m, ramitas vilosas o lanosas; hojas variables 4-18 mm de long., algunas veces semi-redondas otras elipticas, obtusas o redondeadas en el apice, estrechandose en la base hacia el peciolo 1-2 mm de long., m.rargenes enteras, haz glabra, enves densamente pubescente y levemernte viloso en las venas; flores fasciculadas o solitarias en las axilas de las hojas superiores; tubo del cáliz 2-2.5 mm de long., viloso, particularmente hacia la base, labio superior igual en longitud al tubo, dientes superiores 0.8-1.2 mm de long., deltoides aoudo-lancedados, iguales en longitud al tubo; tubo de la corola 11-20 mm de long., labio superior 2.5-3 mm de long.
bibliographicCitation: Epling, Carl C. & Játiva, Carlos D. 1964. Revisión del género Satureja on América del Sur. Brittonia. 16: 393-416.
