description: Perennis, 6-10 dm. alta; angulis caulis hispidis, setis brevis, validis, basi pustulata; lateribus scabro-hispidulis; foliis brevi-petio- latis vel superioribus subsessilibus; laminis foliorum 5-12 cm. longis, 2-4 cm. latis, serratis, dentibus multis, utraque pagina brevi-hispidula, venis paginae inferioris hispidis, basibus setarum pustulatis; bracteis lanceolatis, inferioribus quam floribus longioribus atque patentibus; superioribus brevioribus et reflexis; calyce hispida vel hispidula, tubo 3 mm. longo, dentibus lanceolato-subulatis, attenuatis, 3 mm. longis; corolla purpurea, 10-12 mm. longa; labro superiori externe puberulento.

description: Planta parva, epiphytica, usque ad 7 cm alta; folia lineari-oblanceolata, acuta, infloreseentia 2-4-flora; sepalum dorsale late ovatum, acutum, cochleatum, sepala lateralia late ovata, acuta, uninervia; petala elliptico-oblonga, obtusa, uninervia; labellum trulliformi-sagittatum, carnosum, aetutum, ciliolatum.

description: Small solitary epiphytic plants to about 7 cm tall; stem slender, bialate, the wings decreasing in width downward; leaves linear-oblanceolate, acute, soon deciduous, those at the base of the stem 15-22 mm long, and 2-4 mm broad, those of the stem (usually only one) very much reduced and bract-like; inflorescence 2- to 4-flowered, simple, the rhachis distinctly bialate, each wing to 1 mm broad; flowers nearly sessile, flowering in succession upward, subtended by an obtuse bract decurrent into the wings of the rhachis, dark reddish brown, the perianth parts all with a few oblong ocellate crystaline inclusions; dorsal sepals broadly ovate, acute, strongly cochleate and appearing suborbicular in natural position, 1-nerved, 2 mm long and as broad; lateral sepals broadly ovate, acute, 1-nerved, about 2 mm long and 1.7 mm broad; petals elliptic-oblong, obtuse, 1-nerved, the margins antrorsely ciliolate, the inner surface near the base obscurely pulvinate, about 2.5 mm long and 1.25 mm broad; lip trulliform-sagittate, acute, nerveless, the basal lobes short, subtriangular, fleshy, the base of the lip in front of the column with a sparse fringe of hirsute hairs, the margin retrorsely ciliolate, about 2.7 mm long and 2.5 mm broad; column fleshy, the lateral lobes rounded, each with a conspicuous coma of thick hairs, each hair branched toward the apex, the hairs 0.7 mm long or less, the dorsal lobe obseurely muricate above; pollinia 4, 2 large and 2 small, in unequal pairs, on a Y-shaped caudiele.

description: Caespitose acaulous epiphytes with fanshaped growths. Leaves 5-7, spatulate-oblanceolate, attenuate, acute, midvein carinate, stiff to subcoriaceous, progressively larger from the base, to 14.5 X 3.7 cm, dark green. Inflorescences ascending axillary scapes, the solitary floral bract tubular to 0.6 cm long. Flowers campanulate with overlapping segments, the sepals, petals and column pale clear green, the labellum pale yellowish green with scattered pale brownish spots on the exterior of the lateral lobes, interior markings pale reddish brown, the anther pale cream. Sepals very broadly elliptic, obtuse, apiculate, concave, 1.7-1.9 X 1.4 cm, the lateral sepals longer. Petals suborbicular, apiculate, concave, 1.6 X 1.5 cm. Labellum 3-lobed, saccate, 7.5 mm long, attached to the foot by an elongate, oblong basal papillose claw sharply recurved-conduplicate in the middle and held in close proximity or touching the rear surface of the callus, the lateral lobes erect, obliquely semiovate with an acute fold near the center of the labellum, the leading margin with a pronounced semielliptic undulation, the midlobe broadly triangular, conduplicate, the callus biseriate, the posterior callus erect, high, 3-tiered, papillose, extended along the midvein as a low thick rib, the anterior callus a transverse, repand, ribbonlike lamella, inner surface colliculate. Column fleshy, stout, arcuate, obscurely winged, 12.5 X 6.7 mm, with scattered short trichomes over the surface, forming an acute angle with the 8 mm long column foot, the anther transverse, broadly cordate, 4-celled, 2.5 X 2.7 mm, the pollinarium 3.6 mm long, the pollinia in 2 unequal pairs, obliquely obovate, convex-concave, 1.2-1.6 X 0.8-0.9 mm, the stipe rhombic with denticulate margins, the viscidium elliptic. Ovary 6-sulcate. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, David E. 1998. New species of Peruvian Orchidaceae IV. Brittonia. 50: 186-191.

description: Caespitose, acaulous epiphytes with fanshaped growths. Leaves 2-3, oblanceolate, acuminate, apiculate, midvein carinate, thin, bright greenish-yellow, 6.5-17.5 x 3.2-4.3 cm, conduplicate at the base and articulated to shortly imbricating, conduplicate sheathing leaf bases. Inflorescences laxly pendent basal scapes. Flowers semitranslucent pale greenish yellow, with the labellum cream yellow externally and internally with reddish-brown spots, the column pale green with a red-brown spotted foot. Dorsal sepal elliptic, apiculate, concave, 2.5 x 1.3 cm. Lateral sepals ovate-elliptic, apiculate, oblique, concave at the base, 3. 1 x 1.5 cm. Petals ovate, acute, oblique, 2.4 x 1.35 cm. Labellum 3-lobulate, saccate, extremely fleshy, clawed, 2.2 cm long, approximately 2.2 cm in circumference, lateral lobes semi- ovate and pinched together, the midlobe narrowly triangular, acute, the callus an irregularly margined transverse ridge with 2 longer unequal teeth, divided by a high, rounded keel shorter than the callus. Column strongly arcuate, fleshy, with large, truncate basal wings, the foot elongate with papillose base. Pollinarium 8.4 mm long, pollinia 4 in 2 very unequal pairs, the stipe with a small, pectinate-appendaged apex.

description: Caespitose acaulous epiphytes with fan- shaped growths. Leaves obovate-flabellate, attenuate at the base, acute, dark gray-green, to 9 x 3 cm. Inflorescences pendent scapes, the peduncles slender, the solitary basal bract tubular, the floral bracts 2, subopposite. Flowers spreading, greenish-cream, the lateral labellum lobes yellowish-green with pale purple spots, the column with pale reddish purple markings of the concave base and foot. Sepals subsimilar, subequal, elliptic, obtuse, concave, 2.2-2.3 x 1.25-1.3 cm. Petals obliquely obovate-elliptic, apiculate, 2.0 x 1.3 cm. Labellum indistinctly 3-lobed, saccate, broadly ovate, apex triangular, 9 mm long, the column foot sharply curved forward, joined to the claw forming a 900 angle, the basal callus ridge semielliptic, semiterete at the edges, basally tuberculate, the central callus long, transverse, multi- dentate. Column lightly arcuate, concave ventrally, basally tuberculate, with a nearly straight foot. Pollinarium to 4 mm long, the pollinia 4 in 2 unequal, tear-shaped, complanate pairs, the stipe very small, retrorsely pectinate, the viscidium oblanceolate.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, David E. & Christenson, Eric A. 1994. New Species and New Combinations in Peruvian Orchidaceae. Brittonia. 46 (1): 24-53.

description: Caespitose, acaulous epiphytes with fanshaped growths. Leaves obovate, rounded, carinate, conduplicate, petiolate, 6.5-8.3 x 2.3-2.9 cm, articulated to conduplicate, imbricating sheaths. Inflorescences pendent, axillary scapes, the peduncle with a solitary, basal, lanceolate, close bract. Flowers campanulate, pale semitranslucent green, the labellum white, tinged green towards the base with dark purple spots on the concave center. Sepals subsimilar, subequal, broadly elliptic, concave, apiculate, 1.5 x 1.0 cm. Pet- als oblique, very broadly obovate-elliptic, shortly acute, 1.5 x 1.2 cm. Labellum small, 0.5 x 0.57 cm when expanded, 3-lobed, cuneate, the column foot and claw folded into a high arch with a distinctive pointed tip, the lateral lobes erect, semiorbicular, broadly rounded, the midlobe much smaller, transverse, subtruncate, acute, the basal callus vertical, complanate, the transverse calli carinate, terminating in a prominent free tooth toward the middle, continuous with a central, low transverse ridge across the middle. Column thick, lightly arcuate, elliptic when seen from below, concave, basally papillose, the foot thick, recurved. An- ther 21 x 19 mm, the pollinia 4 in 2 unequal, claviform, complanate, arcuate pairs, 0.9-1.2 x 0.5-0.6 mm, the stipe shortly cleft, the viscidium lanceolate.

description: Shrub, somewhat woody, coarse, loosely long-climbing, glabrous to glabrate. Stems subquadrangular, main internodes about 10-30 cm. long, secondary internodes about 2-4 cm. long; usually with 2 adventitious root primordia on ground side of branches but seldom actually rooting. Petiole thickish, 1-2 cm. long. Leaves dark green, especially above, glossy on both sides, subcoriaceous, lanceolate; blades 7-12 cm. long, 2-3.5 cm. wide, rounded to somewhat acute at base, acute to slightly acuminate at apex, shallowly serrate to rarely subentire; the median vein above sometimes narrowly sulcate and then often setose in the groove (as is often true in S. kaalae Wawra). Flowers typically in whorls of 6; peduncles 5 mm. long or less and occasionally almost wanting, somewhat tawny-puberulent; pedicels slender, 4-5 mm. long, tawny-puberulent, each bearing 3 filiform bractlets, the central and lowest bractlet almost as long as pedicel, the lateral ones up to half as long. Calyx green to purplish, glabrous; tube narrow, angular, 7 mm. long, 4 mm. wide at end; lobes linear-lanceolate, sharply acute, 5 mm. long. Corolla dark purplish red, about 20 mm. long, glabrate under calyx, antrorsely pubescent elsewhere.

description: Plant slender, erect. Stem terete, slightly thickened, 4-16 cm long, bearing 4 or 5 leaves. Leaves alternate, lanceolate, acuminate to acute, 1.5-10 cm long, 7-201 mm broad, reddish underneath with a reddish margin above. Inflorescence terminal, from 4-27 cm tall, 2- to 10-flowered. Flowers 2.5-3.5 cm across, pale lilac and white. Pedicels 1.5-2.5 cm long. Sepals slightly longer than petals, not reflexed, clawed, lanceolate to oblanceolate, acute, 1.5-3 cm long, 3-9 mm wide. Petals ovate to oblanceolate, acute, 1.5-2.5 cm long, 5-9 mm wide. Lip adnate to the column for about 3 mm, pandurate, apex mucronate to rounded, 2-3.5 cm long, ca. 5 mm wide near the base, callus absent except for two slightly incurved lines near the base. Column with membranaceous wings, 1-1.4 cm long, 4-7 mm wide at the broadest part, white-yellow with numerous purple spots on the back. Ovary some- times with a sac-like nectary on the lower side.
bibliographicCitation: Thien, L. B. & Dressler, Robert L. 1970. Taxonomy of Barkeria (Orchidaceae). Brittonia. 22: 289-302.

description: Plant erect. Stem fusiform, 1.5-11 cm long, bearing 2-7 leaves, usually leafless when in flower. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 3-9 cm long, 5-15 mm broad. Inflorescence terminal, from 2.5-35 cm tall, 2- to 20-flowered. Flowers approximately 1-2 cm across, cream to pinkish. Pedicels 1-2 cm long. Sepals linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 7-15 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, petals greatly resembling sepals, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, acuminate, 7-15 mm long, 2-4 mm wide. Lip sometimes adnate to column for about 0.5 mm, deltoid-ovate, apex mucronate, 1-1.5 cm long, 5-12 mm wide, callus consisting of three verrucose keels running nearly to apex of lip, the lateral veins of the lip also verrucose. Column with membranaceous wings, 2-4 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, anther cap sometimes bright red. The clinandrium smooth or variously lobed (sometimes with dentate margins). Ovary occasionally with an externally visible sac-like nectary.
bibliographicCitation: Thien, L. B. & Dressler, Robert L. 1970. Taxonomy of Barkeria (Orchidaceae). Brittonia. 22: 289-302.

description: Plant slender, erect. Stem terete, thickened, 4-15 cm long. Inflorescence 6-45 cm tall, 3- to 12-flowered. Sepals and petals reddish, lip creamy gray with reddish veins. Pedicels 1-2.3 cm long. Flowers 2.5-3.5 cm across. Sepals and petals similar. Sepals lanceolate, acuminate, 1.3-2 cm long, 3-6 mm wide. Petals lanceolate, acuminate, 1.3-2 cm long, 3-6 mm wide. Lip sometimes slightly adnate to column; lip deltoid to ovate in shape, 1.3-1.9 cm long, 9-12 mm wide (at broadest part), apex somewhat rounded to sharply acute-acuminate; keel consisting of three verrucose lines running almost to apex of lip, the lateral veins with verrucose thickenings. Column 3-4 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, with widely spreading membranaceous wings. Ovary with a swollen conspicuous goiter-like nectary near summit, 2 mm long, 1 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Thien, L. B. & Dressler, Robert L. 1970. Taxonomy of Barkeria (Orchidaceae). Brittonia. 22: 289-302.

description: Plant slender, erect. Stem fusiform, 2-15 cm long, bearing 2-4 leaves. Leaves al- ternate, linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 3-8 cm long, 7-13 mm wide. Inflorescence ter- minal, 7-30 cm long, sometimes branched, bearing 2-30 flowers densely packed upon the inflorescence. Flowers 2-2.5 cm across, pale lilac with a tinge of yellow in the center of the lip. Pedicels 1.3-2 cm long. Sepals and petals resembling each other, swept forward; sepals linear to linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 1-1.7 cm long, 2-4 mm wide. Petals lanceolate, acute, 1-1.6 cm long, 3-4 mm wide. Lip sometimes adnate to column for ca. 0.5 mm, lip obovate, apex rounded, often with a mucro, 1-1.5 cm long, and ca. 1 cm wide at the broadest part, margin of lip denticulate to various degrees; callus consisting of three verrucose keels extending almost to the apex of lip, the lateral veins of the lip also with verrucose thickenings. Column 2.5-4 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide at the broadest part with widely spreading membranaceous wings. Ovary slightly curved and with an externally visible sac-like nectary 3-4 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Thien, L. B. & Dressler, Robert L. 1970. Taxonomy of Barkeria (Orchidaceae). Brittonia. 22: 289-302.

description: Plants slender, erect, caespitose. Stems terete, slightly thickened, 4-16 cm long, bearing 2-6 leaves (sometimes leafless when in flower). Leaves thin, alternate, linear to lanceolate, acuminate to acute, 3-12 cm long, 6-20 mm wide. Inflorescence a terminal raceme from 5-26 cm long, 1- to 4-flowered. Flowers 4-6 cm across. Pedicels 2.5-3 cm long. Sepals and petals mallow-pink. Sepals sometimes clawed, elliptic- lanceolate, acute, 2.5-4 cm long, 8-12 mm wide. Petals obovate to elliptic-ovate acute to obtuse, 2.5-3.5 cm long, 1-1.5 cm wide at the broadest part. Lip white with a large purple blotch on apex, adnate to column for 3-4 mm, appressed against lip, pandurate to obovate in shape, apex emarginate to apiculate, 2-3 cm long, 1.5-2.5 cm wide, callus consisting of three to five thin keels. Column with widely spreading membranaceous wings, 1.5-2 cm long, 8-13 mm wide at the broadest part.
bibliographicCitation: Thien, L. B. & Dressler, Robert L. 1970. Taxonomy of Barkeria (Orchidaceae). Brittonia. 22: 289-302.

description: Plant slender, erect. Stem terete, slightly thickened, 12-24 cm long, bearing 3-5 leaves. Leaves alternate, slightly thickened, lanceolate-elliptic, acute, 8-15 cm long, 2-3.2 cm broad, keeled below. Inflorescence terminal to 50 cm tall, 10- to 15-flowered. Flowers as much as 5 cm across, dark lilac and white. Pedicels 3-3.5 cm long. Sepals lanceolate, acute about 2.5 cm long, 8-10 mm wide. Petals ovate, sharply acute, 2.6-3 cm long, 1.3-1.5 cm wide. Lip oval to elliptic to oblong in shape. Lip base slightly enfolding the base of the column. Margin of the lip undulate, lip dark or pale lilac with a white to yellow spot in the center and with the apex (upper third of lip) a very dark lilac. Callus consisting of three thickened keels running almost to the apex of the lip, white to yellow with several small purple dots. Lip 2.4-3.3 cm long, 1.7-2 cm wide, apex of lip sharply apiculate to acute. Column 1.2-1.4 cm long, about 5 mm wide, with slightly fleshy wings, back of the column pale lilac with the wings white, yellow, and green with numerous small dark purple dots.
bibliographicCitation: Thien, L. B. & Dressler, Robert L. 1970. Taxonomy of Barkeria (Orchidaceae). Brittonia. 22: 289-302.

description: Plant slender, erect. Stem terete, slightly thickened, 8-15 cm long, bearing 3-6 leaves. Leaves alternate, ovate-elliptic, acute to acuminate, 5-10 cm long, 1.5-3.5 cm broad. Roots massive, 5 mm in diameter. Inflorescence terminal from 10-35 cm tall, 3- to 9-flowered. Flowers 3-4.5 cm across, deep magenta-red. Pedicels 2-3 cm long. Sepals lanceolate, acuminate, sometimes slightly clawed, 1.5-2 cm long, 4-6 mm wide. Petals ovate to elliptic, acute 1.7-2.4 cm long, 6-10 mm wide. Lip adnate to column for 2-3 mm, lip obovate, apex rounded with a small mucro, 1.5-2 cm long, 1.2-1.5 cm wide, callus consisting of three slightly thickened keels running almost to the apex of the lip. Column with widely spreading membranaceous wings, 1-1.2 cm long, 4-6 mm wide at the broadest part, with numerous dark purple dots on back of the column.

description: Plant slender, erect. Stem terete, slightly thickened, 6-15 cm long, bearing 3-7 leaves. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to broadly ovate or elliptic, acuminate to acute, 3-11 cm long, 1.5-4.5 cm broad. Roots massive 0.5 cm in diameter. Inflorescence terminal from 15-60 cm tall, 3- to 15-flowered. Flowers 3-4.5 cm across, pale lilac and white. Sepals lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 2-2.5 cm long, 9-14 mm wide. Lip adnate to column for 2-3 mm, lip slightly pandurate to obovate or sub-rectangular, apex rounded to square with a slight mucro, 1.7-2.3 cm long, 1-1.7 cm wide, callus consisting of three keels running almost to apex of lip (middle keel running beyond the other two). Column with widely spreading membranaceous wings, 1-1.4 cm long, 4-6 mm wide at the broadest part.

description: Plant slender, erect. Stem terete, thickened, to 17 cm long, bearing 2-5 leaves. Leaves alternate, elliptic to lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 4-12 cm long, 1-2.4 cm broad. Inflorescence a terminal raceme to 8 cm tall, from 4- to many-flowered (18-20). Flowers 2-3 cm across, rose-lilac. Pedicels to 2.5 cm long. Sepals and petals reflexed. Sepals lanceolate-elliptic, acute to acuminate, 12-15 mm long, 4-8 mm wide. Lip free or slightly adnate to column at base, not appressed, lip heart- shaped to more or less suborbicular, apex rounded to emarginate with a slight mucro, the margins undulate, the base more or less cordate, 10-16 mm long, 8-13 mm wide, with three keels running almost to apex of lip, the anterior portion usually slightly higher than the rest of the keel and with a few dark purple dots and streaks (white incurved teeth near base). Column 7-10 mm long, green and purple, 6-8 mm wide, the wings of column usually fleshy.

description: Plant slender, erect or ascending, loosely caespitose. Stem slightly thickened, fusiform, bearing 3 or 4 leaves, (sometimes leafless when in flower). Leaves alternate, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, acuminate to acute, 3-18 cm long, 1-2.8 cm broad. Inflorescence terminal, raceme rarely compound, from 9-45 cm long, 4- to many- flowered. Flowers 1.5-2.5 cm across, rose-purple or red-magenta. Pedicels 2-4 cm long. Sepals elliptic to lanceolate, acute-acuminate, 1.5-2.5 cm long, 4-5 mm wide. Petals elliptic to ovate, acute to sharply acuminate, 1.5-2.4 cm long, 7-12 mm wide. Lip adnate (along margins) to column for about one-half the length of the column, lip ovate in shape often resembling the petals in size, apex acute to sharply acuminate, 1.5-2 cm long, 7-13 mm wide, callus consisting of three yellow, thickened keels running to the apex of the lip. Column club-shaped with more or less fleshy wings, 6-7 mm long. Ovary sometimes with an externally visible nectary on the lower side.

description: Folia basilaria margine ciliata supra glabra subtus verrucata 2.4-3.0 cm longa. description: Leaves basal, with large water-filled cells, ciliate outer margin, upper surface glabrous, undersurface warty, 2.4-3.0 cm long. Scape with septate trichomes, greenish-white, to 11 cm long. Inflorescence pendent. Flowers several, narrow, tubular, upper 1/2 white, lower 1/2 green. Calyx with scattered trichomes on outer surface; lateral sepals connate at base, slightly falcate, lanceolate, obtuse, ca 5.4 mm long; dorsal sepal free of lateral petals, lanceolate, obtuse, ca 5.0 mm long. Corolla white, glabrous; lateral petals slightly falcate, oblong, obtuse, 4.6 mm long; labellum succulent at apex, oblong-lanceolate, clawed, nectar glands knob-like, 6.5 mm long. Ovary green, 3-ribbed. Column as described for genus.

description: Trees, rarely shrubs; bole irregular, with or without buttresses; buttresses sometimes very large, especially in the Amazonian species; bark fissured, light brown to grayish; wood yellow to reddish and very hard. Stipules interpetiolar, free or connate at base, persistent or caducous. Blades elliptic to ovate to obovate, usually acuminate at apex; domatia absent, or tuft of hairs. Inflorescences terminal and solitary, corymbose and with opposite to subopposite lateral branches terminating in cymules. Flowers protandrous, sessile to pedicellate, fragrant; hypanthium obconical to turbinate. Calyx truncate or with barely distinguishable lobes, persistent; calyx lobes 4 or 5; one lobe expanded into a cream to yellowish white calycophyll in a few species, in some of the flowers. Corolla funnelform to subrotate, white, greenish white, or cream white; corolla tube funnelform to ciatiform; with a ring of pubescent hairs inside on the tube or on the base of the lobes; corolla lobes 4 or 5, rounded; aestivation imbricate. Stamens central to the adjacent petals or alternate to the petals, exserted; anthers elliptic, dorsifixed, dehiscing by lateral slits; fil- aments attached on the upper part of the tube, slender and basally flattened, with a tuft of pilose to villous hairs at base. Style exserted; style branches opening after complete maturity of the anthers, long, narrowly oblong, reflexed at maturity. Ovary 2- celled, seeds horizontally attached on the septum (not peltate), obconical to oblong, with many ovules in each locule. Capsules globose, oblong or obovoid, dehiscing sep- ticidally; disk-loculicidal dehiscence pres- ent in old capsules of some species. Seeds with lateral hilum, uncinulate, flattened at polar ends, rarely with small wing. Pollen tricolporate, exine densely reticulate.

description: Shrubs to slender trees up to 15 m tall and up to 20 cm (or more) diam., without buttresses; bark smooth, pale brown; wood pale yellow. Young leafy branchlets 3-5 mm thick, terete to subterete, puberulent to pilose to densely hirsute. Stipules free at base and valvate in bud, not connected to petioles, narrowly triangular, appressed pubescent to densely pilose outside, glabrous inside, 2.5-3.1 mm long, 5-6 mm wide at base, readily caducous, leaving a scar encircling the stem just above the petioles; with two dense tufts of colleters at base between the stipules. Blades (12-)21-35 X (4-)8-1 8 cm, length:width 2-2.5:1, elliptic to narrowly obovate, acute at base and at apex, often with a short acumen, dark green above and pale green below, chartaceous; drying reddish brown above, and pale olive green to pale brown below; glabrous to sparsely hirsute above, puberulent to pilose to densely hirsute below; primary and secondary veins pubescent to hirsute and prominent below, the secondary veins 16- 36 each side, the tertiary veins subparallel throughout. Petioles 5-25 mm long, 4-8 mm thick, adaxially narrowly concave. Inflorescences terminal and solitary, corymbose and densely branched distally, with opposite to subopposite decussate branches terminating in small compacted cymules, 16-30 cm long; lateral branches 2-3 (-4) pairs, 5-15 cm long; rachis basally subter- ete and distally decussately compressed, the rachis and branches minute-puberulent to hirsute; distal bracts narrowly triangular, to 1 cm long and to 4 mm wide, sometimes expanded into leaf-like bracts to 3 cm long and 2 cm wide; bracteoles subtending the flowers deltoid and 1-2 mm long. Flowers fragrant, short-pedicellate; pedicels 1-5 mm long, puberulent to pubescent; hypanthium obovoid, 2-3 X 2-3 mm, puberulent to pubescent. Calyx long-cupular and lobed, 2- 4 X 3-5 mm, puberulent to pubescent, pale green; calyx lobes deltoid, 1-3 mm long, in some flowers one lobe of the calyx expanded into a calycophyll Calycophylls ovate to elliptic; petaloid blades 3-9 X 1.5-5.5 cm, with subpalmate venation, white to cream white to greenish white; stipes 1.5-3.5 cm long. Corolla short-tubular (narrowly in- fundibuliform) and shallowly lobed, 9-13 mm long, white to cream-white; tube subcylindrical, 7-9 mm long, 2-3 mm wide at base and 3-4 mm wide at orifice, glabrous outside and with a medial area of sericeous hairs inside; corolla lobes 5, imbricate in bud, reflexed at anthesis, 2.5-3.5 mm long, 2.5-3 mm wide at base, ovate with rounded apex, glabrous outside and inside. Stamens 5, obviously exserted, of equal length; filaments attached 5-6 mm from the base of the tube; anthers narrowly elliptic, 2.5-4 x 0.5-0.7 mm, dorsifixed near the base, the base rounded, the apex narrowly rounded; filaments 4.5-6 mm long, filiform, basally flattened and adnate to throat, sparsely sericeous-pilose at base. Style exserted, 8-10 mm long, terete, densely pilose, adpressed retrorse; style branches narrowly oblong, 2- 3 mm long, the stigmatic surface microscopically (40X) papillose. Capsules obovoid-globose, acute at base, rounded at apex, 3.5-5 X 3-4 mm, dark-brown, sparsely pubescent, without lenticels, with septicidal dehiscence; disk black when dry, glabrous, not exceeding the calyx; persis- tent calyx short-tubular, and sometimes splitting into 3-4 parts in old capsules. Seeds with lateral hilum, horizontally inserted, flattened to uncinulate at distal end, 0.07-0.1 mm long, with a minute perimetrical wing.

description: Tree to 25 m tall, 50-7 5 cm diam., usually unbranched until 10-15 m; buttresses small, from less than 1 m to 1.5 m high; trunk fairly smooth, light brown, with coarse warty lenticels, the rings from the petiole scars visible throughout; slash tan, slightly aromatic, without exudate, the inner bark gran- ular. Leaves spiral; blade ovate-elliptic, 12- 29 cm long, 7.5-12 cm wide, often with some leaves as small as 9 cm long, 4 cm wide, entire, subcoriaceous, pinnately veined, with ca. 12 lateral veins per side, the tertiary venation finely reticulate above, less prominent below, glabrous except villous on sides of the midrib abaxially when young, the hairs white, 1.5-2.5 mm long, usually glabrescent; twigs 4-8 mm diam., the leaf scars 2-4 mm apart; petiole 2-3.5 cm long, with complete scar, the adaxial surface convex, the marginal rim cartilaginous, transversely cracked, sparsely villous when young abaxially near tip, usually glabrescent; terminal bud protected by the stipular cap, ca. 2.2 cm long, 7 mm diam., the stipule 3.5 cm long at maturity, caducous, glabrous except white-villous abaxially in two lines to tip, where more generally villous, the first 1.5 cm attached to the petiole, the terminal 2 cm free. Flowers single, terminal, on a gradually expanded twig, the torus 1.5 cm diam.; flower buds green; sepals 3, broadly oval, 6 cm long, 4.5 cm wide, obtuse, thick-chartaceous, with ca. 15 obscure parallel nerves on adaxial surface, apparently deciduous by anthesis; petals 3 + 3, white, thick, cymbiform, obovate, the tip obtuse, but folded inward and appearing acute, the 3 outer petals the same size as the sepals, the 3 inner a few mm shorter and narrower; stamens ca. 130 and 163 (both counted from Vargas et al. 1224, the second a complete count from an unopened but nearly mature bud), yellow, 10-1 5 mm long, 2 mm wide, the sterile tip triangular, 2-2.5 mm long, slightly wider at the base than the blade of the anther, leaving shallow stamen scars in a ring 4 mm wide; inner stamens grooved abaxially from contact with adjacent anthers, the outer ones smooth; thecae 4, on the adaxial surface, linear, extending nearly to the base; carpels ca. 115 (Vargas et al. 1224), connate, in a spindle-shaped cone 2.5 cm long, 2.2 cm wide in anthesis, the lower carpels 1.5-1.8 cm long, 2 mm wide, the outer ones acutely 3-ribbed abax- ially on the fused part, the free tip (style) 5 mm long, free but tightly appressed, caducous. Fruit tan, heavy, ovoid, woody, 11- 14 cm long, 10-13 cm wide, not yet observed dehiscing on trees, but almost completely ripe fruit opening during drying, beginning in the upper part the outer half of the carpelar mass splitting irregularly along the carpellary divisions, into several woody parts 2.5 cm thick, the individual carpels not dehiscent abaxially, all pieces eventu- ally falling free; carpel boundaries obscure on outside, with a slightly raised scar where the style dehisced; carpels with 1 or 2 seeds, the chamber smooth and regular on inside; seeds dangling on the white, very fine and strong funicular threads, angular-obovoid, 10 mm long, 8 mm wide; testa bright red or red-orange, thinly fleshy, the inner cone of ovoid locular cavities 10.5-11 cm long, 4.5 cm wide, the lower 1.5 cm for attachment of the outer carpellary mass, the locules of basal carpels elongate, the others usually rhombic, 10 mm long, 7 mm wide, or irregular and to 15 mm long if with two seeds.

description: Arbor 25 m usque alta. Lamina foliorum elliptica, 12-29 cm longa, 7.5-12 cm lata, subcoriacea; petiolo 2-3.5 cm longo utraque margine cicatrice stipulari percurso; gemmae 2.2 cm longae, 7 mm diametro. Fructus ovoideus, carpellis obscure delimitatis, parte extema lignosa, 2.5 cm crassa, irregulariter fissa; semina per carpellum 1-2, 10 mm longa, 8 mm lata, sanguinea vel aurantiaca.

description: Arbor mediocris ramis terminalibus viridi-ochraceis glabratis, juvenilibus tomentosis pilis acutis basi tuberculosis patulis dense obtectis. Folia alterna simplicia. Petiolus 1.4-2 cm longus crassiusculus minute tomentosus pilis acutis basi conicis, supra sulcatus, infra apicem 2 glandulis cylindricis ca. 1.2 mm longis praeditus. Lamina firmula coriacea subobovata basi attenuata acute cuneata apice subite angustata breviter obtusiuscule acuminata, margine integra remotis glandulis annularibus minutis munita, 11-15.5 cm longa 5.5-7.6 cm lata, supra pallido-viridis (in sicco) pilis minutis patulis basi tuberculatis (bulbosis) ad costam copiosis in cetera sparsis vel raris praedita, costa nervis secundariis paulo notatis nervulis laxe reticulatis leviter prominulis; subtus pallidior costa elevata vulgo 4 nervis secundariis ascendentibus arcuatis nlervulis prominulis laxe reticulatis, pilis minutis acutis patulis sparsis vel sparssissimis sed ad costam nervosque secundarios copiosis. Inflorescentiae femineae (in statu fructifero tantuli visae) ca. 4 cm longae, axi minute tomeitoso pilis acutis patulis basi tuberculatis. Pedicelli teneres 8-10 mm longi. Sepala 3 brevia pubescentia. Discus hypogynus cupularis glaber basi fructus remanens 1.5 mm altus. Fructus sulcatus extus puberulus, seminibus rubris ovatis acutis compressis alveolatis ca. 5 mm longis 6 mm latis.

description:
Arbor mediocris, ramulis terminalibus viridibus adpresse pubeseentibus pilis malpighiaceis tectis. Folia alterna simplicia. Petiolus 5-12 mm longis adpresse pubescens semiteres supra suleatus subapicem 2 glandulis tubulosis patulis 1 mm longis instructus. Lamina chartacea viridis subobovato-oblonga basim versus paulo attenuata basi obtusa, apice subite attenuata obtuseque cuspidata, margine integra sed raris glandulis minutis praedita, 4-11 cm longa, 1.5-4.2 cm lata acumine 2-10 mm longo, 3 mm lato; supra puberula pilis minutis adpressis vel subadpressis sparsis mlunita, costa angusta impressa vel plana nervis secundariis paulo impressis filiformibus, venulis in reticulo prominulo notato; subtus puberulis, costa elevata magis adpresse pilosa, nervis secundariis 4-5 utroque latere prominentibus valde ascendentibus prope marginem arcuatis amastomosatis, venulis reticulum prominulum plus minusve conspicuum formantibus.

Inflorescentiae rnasculae in panieulis angustis raceinosis 2-4 cm longis, axi ramulisque teneribus adpresse pubeseentibus. Flores masculi solitarii breviter pedicellati basi bracteola glandulata breviter cupulari vel subdisciformi, pedicellis 0.5-2 mm longis. Flos masculus sepalis 3 ovatis acutis pubeseentibus 1.2 mm longis, 1 mm latis. Stamina 3 filamentis brevissimis antheris circa 1 mm amplis 4-lobulatis. Inflorescentiae femineae 2-6 mm longae, ramulis praecipue unifloris; pseudopedicellis 3-7 mm teneribus puberulis articulatis. Flos femineus sepalis 3 ovatis acutiusculis adpresse pubeseentibus 1.2 mm longis, 1 mm latis. Discus hypogynus glaber urceolato-cupularis calycis altitudinem attingens margine obsolete crenatus. Ovarim glabrumn ovoideum, stigmata crasso-subquadrato sessile.

description: Liana. Stems glabrous; leaves opposite, petiolate, narrowly elliptic, apex acuminate, base obtuse, glabrous, nonglandular, without colleters; petioles 6-18 mm long; leaf blade 4-9.2 cm long, 0.5-2.2 cm wide. In- florescence a pedunculate trichotomous subumbellate cyme; peduncle 1.3-4.7 cm long, glabrous; bracts very narrowly elliptic, 1-2 mm long; pedicels 4-7 mm long, puberulent-papillate to glabrate. Calyx lobes triangular to very narrowly elliptic, 1-2 mm long, puberulent to glabrate; colleters opposite the sepal, solitary, dentiform, ca. 1 mm long. Corolla rotate, petals of bud over lapping to the right, 4-5 mm long, glabrous, tube 1-2 mm, lobes ovate, 2-3 mm long; filaments pubescent, 0.8-1.2 mm long; an- thers 5, 2.5-3 mm long, adnate to pistil head, exserted 1-2 mm, base sagittate with blunt lobes; pistil 3-4 mm long; ovary ovoid, ca. 0.8 mm long; pistil head fusiform, ca. 2 mm long; stigma at base of pistil head; nectaries 5, essentially free, as long as to slightly shorter than the ovary. Follicles 2, constricted between the seeds, moniliform, united, 14-18 cm long, dark green, glabrous, dehiscent; seeds 6-9 per follicle, 0.8-1.3 cm long; coma white, 1-1.3 cm long, directed toward the apex of the follicle.

description: Fruit 11 mm diam., with the pericarp 2-2.5 mm thick, stigmatic remains basal, seed and locular epidermis grooved-showing no clear affinity with other genera; distinctive for the apparent total lack of tanniniferous or raphide-bearing cells, the concentration of brachysclereids just below the epidermis, and the occurrence of much larger sclereids scattered into the middle pericarp. Some of the larger vascular bundles have thick fibrous sheaths, but most have little or no fibers around them, resembling Brongniartikentia in this respect.

description: Plant epiphytic, rhizomatous, to 3.9 dm long. Roots numerous, slender, canescent. Rhizome stoloniferous, repent, decumbent, wiry, remotely several sheathed, sheaths scarious, triangular to lanceolate, acute, to 7 mm long and 4 mm wide. Stem modified into remotely produced pseudobulbs, to 4 cm apart, to 6 mm long and 3 mm wide, basally flattened, completely enclosed by 5-10 distichous leaves. Leaves produced at intervals along base of pseudobulb, yellow green with minute, reddish-purple spots, conduplicate, linear-falcate, to 8 cm long and 3 mm wide, acute, margin cartilaginous, crenate. Inflorescence lateral, to 3.7 dm long, peduncle slender, semi-erect, distantly several-sheathed, racemose, to 12-flowered. Floral bracts lanceolate, to 4 mm long and 2 mm wide, acute. Ovary pedicellate, slender, to 1.5 cm long. Dorsal sepal white, tinged with green, basal 2/3 brown, subspatulate, to 5 mm long and 2 mm wide, concave, emarginate, basally clawed. Lateral sepals oblanceolate, to 4 mm long and 1 mm wide, concave, acute, connate nearly to apex, basally clawed. Petals white, tinged with green, basal 1/3 with reddish-brown spots, spatulate, to 7 mm long and 4 mm wide, acute to emarginate, basally clawed, margin undulate. Labellum 3-lobed, white, to 1 cm long and 1.2 cm wide; lateral lobes basal, elliptic, obtuse to subacute, midlobe separated from lateral lobes by a short isthmus, isthmus with yellowish-brown blotches, margin fringed, midlobe broadly flabellate, emarginate with an apicule in the sinus, callosity on isthmus yellow with minute reddish-brown spots, usually with 2 anterior and 2 posterior tubercles connected by a central ridge. Column short, erect, white, to 3 mm long and 1 mm wide, with expanded lateral wings projecting from apex; lateral wings white, lanceolate, bilobed, base obtuse, apex acute, to 3 mm long and 1 mm wide. Anther cap pale purple. Capsule not observed.

description: Arbor 5 m alta, 7.5 cm diametiens, stellato-pubescens vel -tomentosa; folia utraque pagina viridia, supra non solum pilis minutis stellatis sed etiam pilis plurimis rigidiusculis simplicibus ca. 1 mm longis obsita; lamina ovata, late elliptica vel obovata, 2-4.5 cm lata, 3-7 cm longa, apice obtusa, acuta vel breviacuminata, basi rotundata, cordato-auriculata, ambitu conspicue serrata (dentibus quoque cm 3-8, distinctis, quadratis rotundatisve, ca. 1 mm altis vel denticulis immixtis); glandulae crateriformes prope basin marginaliter insertae, tum praeterea superficie inferiore duae aliae plerumque collocatae; petioli 0.6-1.5 cm longi; stipulae lanceolatae, seariosae, induratae, deciduae, 2-3 mm longae; folii nervi pinnatim dispositi, utroque latere ca. 5, subtus reticula scalariformia efficientes, partibus terminalibus anastomosantibus; planta e ignota; spicae 9 terminales, 3-6 cm longae, floribus 2-4 sessilibus; bracteae 9 cordato-ovatae, acuminatae, mox reflexae, 4 mm longae, bracteolae 2, bracteis similes sed minores; sepala 4, inaequales, usque ad 2.5-4 mm lata, 4.5-5.5 mm longa; discus subinteger, angustus; styli flabelliformes, basi crassi, compressi, ca. 1 mm lati longique, laciniis ca. 12, 3-4 mm longis, capsulae velutinae, valde 3-lobatae, 9-12 mm latae, 7-9 mm longae; semina (vix matura) 6.5 mm longa, cordiformes, apice carinata, basi truneata vel concava.

description: Branchlets, petioles and infloreseences thinly pubescent or tomentose, the hairs mostly appressed but some of them longer, fascicled, erect or nearly so; leaves slightly harsh to the touch; lower surface copiously stellate-pubescent with a few simple hairs (up to 1.3 mm long) intermixed; axils of the basal veins copiously tufted with long hairs that are paler (white) and more slender than those of the leaf-surfaces; glands prominent on the basal margins, the pair on the lower surface beside the base of the lowest large vein.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Volubilis, ad 2.5 m longa, basi lignescens, caulibus puberulenltibus hispidisque, pilis urentibus; inflorescentiae rami ovariumque valde stipitato-glandulosi; folia ovata vel triangulari-ovata 2-4.5 (-8) cm lata, 4-8 (-13) cm longa, saepe duplo (1.75-3-plo) longiora quam latiora, apice acuta, plerumque acurninata, basi cordata sinu lato lobisque latis suborbicularibus instructa, ambitu crasse acuteque sed breve serrata, dentibus utroque latere 15-25; lamina 3-nervia, nervis lateralibus omnibus adscendentibus curvatis, anastomosantibus, in dentes marginales directe non exeuntibus; petioli 1.5-4 (-7) cm longi; stipulae foliaceae, triangulares, ad 1 mm latae, 3 mm longae; racemi subfiliformes 3-7 cm longi, flore [female] supra basin 2-2.5 cm, deinde floribus [male] 15-50; sepala [female] lineari-lanceolata, anthesi 1.5-2.5 mm longa (fructus maturitate ad 3 mm); pedicelli fructuis 3-3.5 mm longi, ad medium vel infra articulati; styli e calyce florendi exserti, in colulnrnam 1.5 mm longam coaliti, ramis vix papillosis 1 mm longis recurvatis; ovarium dense glandulis stipitatis obsitum flores [male] pedicellis 1.5-2 mm longis, medio articulatis instructi; stamina 3; capsula valde 3-lobata lobis suborbicularibus, 7-8 mm lata, superficie aculeis herbaceis subulatis vel cristatis ad 2 mm longis apicibus glandulosis obsita; columella 2 mm longa, ramis triradiatis 1.5 mm longis; semina globosa, 2.75 mm diametientia, brunneo-lutea, fusco-marmorata.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Arbor vel frutex arborescens 5-6 m altus, inflorescentia ramulis petiolisque pubescentibus vel sparsim tomentosis, pilis stellatis fasciculatisve; folia utraque pagina viridia (subtus pallidiora), rare minuteque stellata, glabrescentia, scabridula; lamina ovata vel ovato-lanceolata, 2-6 cm lata, 4-10 cm longa, a medio vel ultra ad apicem obtusum cuspidatum angustata, basi rotundata vel obtusa, plerumque abrupte in petiolum 0.5-1.5 cm longum angustata, ambitu crasse sinuatim dentata, vel foliorum juniorum crenato-serrata (dentibus quoque cm 3-4); folii nervi pinnatim dispositi, utroque latere 5-6, infimi majores, valde ascendentes, omnes prope costam crassi, sed ad apices valde diminuentes anastomosantesque; planta [male] ignota; glandulae crateriformes prope basin marginaliter insertae; stipulae subulato-lanceolatae, scariosae, duriusculae, ante foliorum maturitatem deciduae, 1.5-2.5 mm longae; spica [female] terminalis, 1 cm longa vel minus, floribus solitariis bracteatis 1-3, bracteis deltoideo-cordatis, 2.5 mm latis, 3 mm longis, mox reflexis, bracteolis sepalis similibus 2 mm longis; sepala (3-) 4-6, inaequales, ovata, acuminata, 1 (-2) mm lata, 2 (-2.5) mm longa; discus nullus; carpella plerumque 2; styli divergentes et ad ovarium appressi, basi hirsuti, crassi, 2 mm longi et fere 2 mm lati, laciniis multi-partitis, flabellatis, 2-2.5 mm longis; fructus globosus vel nonnunquam paulum 2-4-lobatus, velutinus, spongiosus, 2 cm diametiens, ut Videtur indehiscens; semina fere hemisphaerica, 10-11 mm longa, 9-10 mm lata, 7 mm crassa, laevia, apice vix acutata, superficie ventrali plana, rapha 6-6.5 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Arbor 5-metralis, cortice grisea, ligno duro; foliorum superficies inferiores, inflorescentia, ramuli petiolique dense pilis stellatis grandibus confertis dealbatis (folii superficies inferioris pilorum rami 0.5-0.8 mm longi); folia asperula, supra obscura et rare stellato-pubescentia; lamina late ovata vel obovata, (2-) 3.5-7 cm lata, 4-8.5 cm longa, plerumque 1.25-1.5-plo longiora quam latiora, apice obtusa vel breviacuminata, basi rotundata, cordato-auriculata, ambitucrasse crenato-serrata vel subintegro-undulata (foliorum juniorum marginis dentes quoque cm 3-4); petioli 6-12 mm longi; stipulae lanceolatae, seariosae, duriusculae, mox deciduae, 2.5-3.2 mm longae; glandulae crateriformes subtus prominentes, earum par majus prope venarum lateralium infimarum basin usque ad 0.8 mm diametro; folium basi 3-nervatum, nervis lateralibus utroque latere 5-6, pinnatim dispositis, omnibus ad apices diminuentibus, sed in dentes majores marginales excurrentibus; planta [male] ignota; spica [female] terminalis, usque ad 6 cm longa, floribus sessilibus 2-4, bracteis cordato-ovatis acuminatis mox reflexis 3 mm longis; bracteolis sepalis similibus sed minoribus, ca. 2 mm latis, 2.5 mmn longis; sepala 4, inaequalia, usque ad 2 mm lata, 4 mm longa; discus angustus, pilosus, continluus, inlteger; styli ca. 3 mm longi, ad ovarium appressi, flabelli- formes, multi-laciniati; carpella 3; capsula plusminusve 3-lobata, 1 cm alta, 1.5 cm lata, velutino-tomelntosa dense pilis pallidis rigidis 1 mm longis vel ultra obtectis; columella ca. 5 mm longa; semina 7-8 mm longa, cordiformia, cicatrix fere centralis; apex carinatus; superficies ventralis plana convexa dua angulum obtusum efficientia, etiam in lobulas basilares prolongata.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Axils of the basal veins of the lower leaf-surface copiously tufted with paler (white) and more slender hairs than those of the leaf-surface in general; glands on the basal margins, and surface glands in addition to the large ones near the basal veins, usually present; spikes markedly zigzag.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: A suffruteseent perennial, woody at the base, with numerous straight, ereet, herbaceous branches 20-60 cm. long, these hirtellous with short, downwardly curled hairs, particularly on the faces directly above the leaves, occasioulally irregularly interspersed with sessile glands; leaves oblong to ovate, 1-3 em. long, 5-15 mm. broad, frequently with numerous smaller leaves on dwarf branches in the axils, acute to obtuse at the apex, acute or somewhat rounded at the base, sessile or with indefinite petioles as much as 5 mum. long, the margins entire, sometimes irregularly crenate, both surfaces sparsely hirtellous with short hairs curled toward the apex, often with numerous sessile glands; eymes as much as 4 cm. long, 1-7-flowered, borne in graceful narrow panicles; flowering calyces hirtellous with short, rather stout, upwardly curled hairs, or these nearly lacking, usually with many sessile or rarely capitate glands, 2.5-4 mm. long, increasing to 3.5-6.5 mm. in fruit, the teeth subequal, lanceolate to nearly deltoid, about the length of the tube; corolla-tubes not exserted from the calyx, straight, 2-4 mmn. long, the lower lip 5-10 mm. long; stamens strongly arched, 1-2.5 cm. long; nutlets 2-3 mm. long, 1.2-1.9 mm. broad, irregularly alveolate, the ridges not prominent, glabrous, sometimes minutely hirtellous at the apex.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.

description: A weedy annual herb as much as 40 cm. tall; stems freely branched, or unbranched in depauperate plants, hirtellous below the infloreseence with short, spreading or downwardly curled but seldom appressed hairs, often pilose with longer straight hairs about 1 mm. long, and occasionally and irregularly sprinkled with capitate glands; leaves elliptical, rarely nearly linear, 2-5 cm. long, 4-16 mm. broad, both surfaces hirtellous with short hairs curled toward the apex, usually sprinkled with capitate glands, acute at the apex, narrowed at the base to indefinite petioles as much as 1 cm. long, usually three-nerved, the two prominent lateral veins arising near the base of the blade, the margins entire, or sometimes irregularly serrate; eymes axillary, predominantly 1-flowered, often 2-3-flowered, the peduncles seldom exceeding 2 cm., clothed like the stemiis but usually more glandular, the bracts small, seldom exceeding 3 mm.; flowering calyces actinomorphic, the teeth 1.5-3.7 mm. long, iniereasing to 2.5-4.9 nlIn. in fruit, the tube shorter, 1.1-1.7 mm. long, becoming 1.5-2.8 mm. long at maturity; corolla-tube straight, flaring somewhat at the throat, not exserted from the calyx, 1.6-3.5 mm. lonff, the lower lip 1.3-2.1 mm. long, usually somewhat longer than the 4 upper lobes; stamens straight or but slightly arched, 2.3-4.2 mm. long, not greatly exserted from the corolla; nutlets 1.9-2.9 mm. long, 1.2-1.8 mm. broad, hirtellous at least at the ape:x with short, usually curled hairs anid irregularly sprinkled with capitate glands, alveolate, the ridoges prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.

description: A weedy aninual herb, as much as 1 m. tall; stems usually branched, hirtellous below the infloreseence with short, downwardly curled or straight spreading hairs, usually pilose with longer straight hairs, and occasionally sprinkled with capitate glands, rarely only pilose; leaves oblong to ovate, 15-60 mm. long, 5-25 mm. broad, both surfaces hirtellous with short hairs curled toward the apex, the apex acute to obtuse, the base narrowed to petioles 2-15 mm. long, the margins entire; cymes axillary, 3-7-flowered, the peduncles as much as 5 cm. long, the pedicels about 5 mm. long, both glandular with stalked capitate glands, usually hirtellous with short spreading hairs and having longer coarse hairs 2-3 times the length of the glandular hairs, or these absent, the bracts often leaflike; calyces strongly zygomorphic, the lower two teeth about one-third the length of the upper three which are fused one-half to two-thirds their length, the flowering calyces 2.7-6.0 mm. long, becoming inverted at maturity so that the three long teeth are lowermost, increasing to 4.6-8.9 mm. long; corolla-tube not extending beyond the longer calyx-teeth, 1.5-4.0 mm. long, the lower lip 1.5-7 mm. long; stamens exserted, arched, 6-16 mm. lonig; nutlets 1.5-2.9 mm. long, 1.1-1.9 mm. broad, glabrous, alveolate, the ridges prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: A rounded shrub, 5-15 dm. tall, freely branched, the branches erect, hirtellous below the infloreseence with short, downwardly appressed hairs; leaves normally linear, 3.5-7.5 cm. long, 1-5 mm. broad, rarely 7 mm., usually longer than the internodes, normally provided with a fascicle of smaller leaves in the axil, acute at the apex, sessile or narrowed at the base to short indefinite petioles at most 3 mm. long, their margins entire, strongly revolute, the upper surfaces green and glabrous, the lower densely gray,pubescent; eymes dense, nearly sessile, borne in the axils of the upper reduced leaves, forming an interrupted spike 10-40 cm. long, the glomerules approximate or as much as 4 cm. distant, the entire inflorescence woolly and floccose with fine blue, pink, or white hairs 2-3 mm. long whichconceal the short pedicels even in fruit; flowering calyces 5-8 mm. long, somewhat longer in fruit, the teeth subequal, ovate, acuminate or acute, equal to or longer than the tubes; corollas floccose on the outside, glabrous within, their tubes straight, much exceeding the calyx, 9-14 mm. long, the lower lip 7-12 mm. long; stamens arched, 2.5-4 cm. long; nutlets 2-4 mm. long, 1.2-2.2 mm. broad, irregularly reticulate, hirtellous with short spreading hairs at least at the apex.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: An erect annual herb 10-100 cm. tall, branched from near the base, the branches arcuate and ascending, relatively strict, or unbranched in depauperate plants; stems and branches viscid with spreading capitate glands, or these almost wanting, usually pubeseeilt as well with short, downwardly curled or appressed hairs, and pilose with longer, soft, but relatively stout spreading hairs; leaves lanceolate to lanceolate-ovate, 2-5 cm. long, 4-14 mm. broad, as much as 7 cm. long and 2 cm. broad in occasional robust forms, acute or acuminate at the apex, often pungent, acute or somewhat rounded at the base, sessile, or at most with indefinite petioles 3-4 mm. long, pinnately veined but the conspicuous lateral veins arising near the base of the blade and appearing parallel, margins entire, rarely with a few prominent lateral teeth on the lower leaves in robust plants, green or ashy, pubescent on both surfaces with usually spreading hairs of varied length, these interspersed with capitate glands; flowers in axillary racemes, forming a more or less secund inflorescence, these racemes as much as 4 cm. long, on peduncles as long as 5 mm., 1-many-flowered; flowering calyces 2.5-4 mm. long, increasing to 3.5-8 mm. in fruit, clothed like the stems, the teeth deltoid to lanceolate, the uppermost often narrower, acute or lightly acuminate, equal to, or as much as 3 times the length of the tube; corolla-tubes exserted from the calyx, 5-10 mm. long, acutely bent beyond the calyx, the lower lip 4.2-8.0 mm. long, strongly deflexed; stamens highly arched, 13-20 mm. long; nutlets alveolate, normally with several peg-like projections, hirtellous with short spreading hairs, particularly on the ridges, 1.6-3.1 mm. long, 1.2-2.3 mm. broad.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.

description: An erect annual herb 10-50 cm. tall, branching from near the base, or simple in depauperate or crowded plants; stems and branches often reddish, hirtellous with short, downwardly curled, appressed hairs, and viscid-glandular with spreading capitate glands as much as 1 mm. long, usually pilose in addition with longer, soft, spreading hairs; leaves lanceolate, sometimes lanceolate-ovate, 3-7 cm. long, 5-15 mm. broad, acute or lightly acuminate at the apex, tapering at the base into petioles 5-15 mm. long, the lateral veins evident, the margins entire, both surfaces pubescent like the stems, sometimes nearly glabrous on the upper surface; cymes axillary, many-flowered, the peduncles 5-10 mm. long, the lower eymes seldom few-flowered even in depauperate plants; flowerin(g calyces 2.5-4 mm. long, clothed like the stems, the teeth deltoid, longer than broad, 1.7-3.1 mm. long in fruit, acute, about equal to the length of the tubes, ofteni tinged with red at maturity, the uppermost narrower, often lanceolate; corolla-tubes exserted from the calyx, 4-8 mm. long, curved abruptly upward near the throat, the lower lip 4-7 mm. long; stamens strongly arched, 7-16 mm. long; nutlets irregularly alveolate, hirtellous with short spreading hairs, occasionallv subglabrous, 1.4-2.2 mm. long, 0.8-1.2 mm. broad.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: An erect annual herb, as much as 30 cm. tall, but depauperate individuals as short as 3-4 cm.; stems branched below the middle, hirtellous with short, downwardly curled, appressed hairs, interspersed with occasional short capitate glands, sometimes with a few longer spreading hairs near the tips of the branches; leaves narrowly elliptical, 2-4.5 cm. long, 2-6 mm. wide, sometimes less in depauperate plants or very young seedlings, acute at the apex, gradually tapering at the base into short indefinite petioles as much as 5 mm. long, equally covered on both surfaces with short appressed hairs, the lateral veins inconspicuous, the margins entire, eymes axillary, the lowermost 1-3-flowered, those in the axils of the median leaves scarcely more than 1 cm. long, about 10-flowered; flowering calyces 1.5-2.5 mm. long, the teeth lanceolate or somewhat deltoid, acute or lightly acuminate, 1.3-2.3 mm. long at maturity, longer than the tubes which are 0.9-1.5 mm. long; corolla-tubes shorter than the calyces, curved, 0.9-1.8 mm. long, the lower lip 1.3-2.1 mm. long; stamens somewhat arched, often quite straight, 2-3 mm. long, barely exserted from the lobes of the corolla; nutlets 1.2-1.7 mm. long, 0.8-1.2 mm. broad, reticulate, the ridges sharp, hirtellous on the ridges with short spreading hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: An erect annual herb as much as 50 cm. tall, the smaller depauperate specimens usually unbranched, the more vigorous ones well branched in the lower part, the branches sinuous, notably more slender than the main stem; stems and branches hirtellous with fine, downwardly appressed or spreading hairs and pilose with slender spreading hairs 1-2 mm. long, sometimes irregularly sprinkled with short capitate glands; leaf-blades varied in size and shape, prevailingly oval, 2-3.5 cm. long, 1-1.5 cm. broad, usually elliptical in depauperate forms and as narrow as 2-3 mm., as much as 2 cm. broad and 4 cm. long in robust forms, generally obtuse at the apex, narrowed below the middle and tapering to indefinite petioles as much as 5 mm. long, entire, the lateral veins conspicuous, both surfaces hirsute with slender hairs of varied length which resemble the elongate hairs of the stem, and sparingly sprinkled with capitate glands; eymes axillary, 3-5-flowered in depauperate individuals, or the flowers even solitary, more numerous and crowded in robust specimens, the eymes horizontal and spreading, scarcely longer than 2 cm. at most, borne on peduncles 1-5 mm. long; flowering calyces clothed like the leaves, the teeth lanceolate and lightly acuminate, normally broadest above the base, 1.5-3 mm. long, increasing in fruit to 3-5.6 mm. long, the tubes seldom exceeding 1 mm. in length, increasing slightly in fruit, as much as 1.5 mm. long, rarely more, notably shorter than the mature nutlets; corolla-tubes 2-3.5 mm. long, upwardly curved, usually not exceeding the calyx-teeth, the lower lip 2-3.5 mm. long; stamens arched, 2.7-5.3 mm. long, rarely as mnuch as 6 mm. long; nutlets 1.1-2.3 mm. long, 0.7-1.5 mm. broad, reticulate, hirtellous with minute, spreading hairs, and sprinkled with sessile glands, the ridges sharp.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.

description: An erect annual herb, 15-80 cm. tall, branched near the base, even in depauperate plants, the branches arcuate and aseendent, relatively stout; 'stems and branches lanate with fine, soft, tangled, upwardly curled or sometimes spreading hairs, sometimes irregularly sprinkled with capitate glands; leaves ovate to roundovate, 1.2-2.2 cm. long, 7-14 mm. broad, crowded on the stem, usually longer than the internodes, abruptly acuminate, usually pungent at the apex, normally rounded at the base or even cordate, but sometimes abruptly narrowed, sessile or nearly so, the margins entire, both surf aces caneseent and woolly or softly hirsute or pilose with fine hairs as much as 2 mm. long, occasionally sprinkled with a few capitate glands, pinnately veined, the prominent lateral veins arising near the base but not appearing parallel; eymes axillary, more or less hidden in the leaves, scarcely 1 cm. long, borne on peduncles as much as 3 mm. long, 1-8-flowered, usually forming a secund infloreseence; flowering calyces 2.5-3.5 mm. long, increasing to 3.2-4.8 mm. at maturity, clothed like the stems, the teeth ovate-lanceolate, 2-3.5 times as long as broad, lightly acuminate, twice, often three times, the length of the tube; corolla-tubes exserted from the calyx, 2.6-5.4 mm. long, curved abruptly upward at the tip of the calyx, the lower lip 3.5-5 mm; long, deflexed; stamens arched, 11-16 mm. long; nutlets 1.5-2.1 mm. long, 1.2-1.5 mm. broad, irregularly alveolate with prominent peg-like projections, hirtellous or pubescent with spreading hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: A suffruteseent perennial, woody at the base, 4-5 dm. tall; branches erect, hirtellous with short spreading hairs; leaves rhomboid-ovate, 2-3 cm. long, 1-1.5 cm. broad, acute or lightly acuminate at the apex, acute or somewhat rounded at the base, glabrate above, hirtellous beneath with short spreading hairs, sparingly glandular, entire; petioles short, scarcely 2 mm. long; eymes 1-5-flowered, aseendent, open, borne in the axils of the upper somewhat diminished leaves on peduncles 1-2 cm. long, the pedicels 5-8 mm. long; flowering calyces clothed like the stems, 4-5 mm. long, as much as 8 mm. long at maturity, cup-shaped, the teeth ovate or deltoid, acute or lightly acuminate, as long as or longer than the tubes; corolla scarlet (?), hirtellous with short hairs of varying length on the outside, glabrate within, 9-10 mm. long, the lobes oblong, the lower-lip deflexed, 5-8 mm. long; stamens nearly straight, 2-2.5 cm. long; immature nutlets hirtellous at the apex, essentially glabrous at maturity, lightly and irregularly venose-reticulate, 3.5 mm. long, 1.8 mm. broad.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: An erect annual herb as much as 50 cm. tall, branched near the base, the branches sinuous, or unbranched in depauperate specimens; stems and branches often reddish, glandular-pubeseent with short capitate glands, and pilose with longer straight spreading hairs about 2 mm. long, often hirtellous in addition with short, downwardly curled hairs; leaves lanceolate or lanceolate-ovate, 2-5 cm. long, clearly tapering above the middle, even acuminate, broadest below the middle, 7-12 mm. broad, somewhat smaller in depauperate specimens, narrowed into indefinite petioles as much as 5 mm. long, the lateral veins evident, the margins entire, both surfaces pilose and sparingly capitate-glandular; eymes axillary, the lower-most frequently 1-3-flowered, the upper ones as much as 2 cm. long, on peduncles 2-6 mm. long and having numerous flowers; flowering calyces clothed like the leaves, the teeth narrowly deltoid, unequal in breadth, the uppermost narrower, acute, 1.3-1.8 mmu. long, not more than twice the length of the tube, increasing in fruit to 2-3 mm. long, often tinged with red, the mature tubes 1.8-2.5 mm. long, longer than the mature nutlets; corolla-tubes exceeding the calyx-teeth, 3.5-4.5 mm. long, upwardly curved beyond the tip of the calyx, the lower lip 2.5-3 mm. long; stamens arched, 4-6 mm. long; nutlets 1.4 mm. long, 0.8 mm. broad, irregularly reticulate, the ridges sharp, hirtellous with short spreading hairs and having a few sessile glands.

description: A weedy annual herb, 10-50 cm. tall; stems usually branched, hirtellous below the infloreseence with short, downwardly curled hairs, rarely nearly glabrous; leaves linear to narrowly lanceolate, 2-5 cm. long, 1-5 mm., rarely as much as 7 mm. broad, both surfaces hirtellous with short hairs curled toward the apex, the apex acute, the base narrowed to an indefinite petiole as much as 5 mm. long, the margins entire; eymes axillary, 3-7-flowered, the peduncles as much as 5 cm. long, the pedicels about 5 mm. long, both clothed with short, stout, spreading hairs and glandular with stalked capitate glands, the bracts often leaflike, calyces strongly zygomorphic, the lower two teeth about one-third the length of the upper three which are fused one-half to two-thirds their length, flowering calyces 3.5-5.5 mm. long, becoming inverted at maturity so that the three long teeth are lowermost, increasing to 4.5-7.4 mm. long; corolla-tube not extending beyond the longer calyx-teeth, 2.3-3.8 mm. long, the lower lip 2.-8-6 mm. long; stamens exserted, arched, 8-20 mm. long; nutlets 1.5-2.1 mm. long, 1.1-1.6 mm. broad, glabrous, alveolate, the ridges prominent.

description: An erect annual herb, 1-4 dm. tall, usually branching near the base, save in depauperate specimens; stems and branches normally reddish, hirtellous with short, downwardly curled, appressed hairs, and viscid with conspicuous spreading capitate g]ands of varied length, but as much as 1 mm. long; leaf blades lanceolate to lanceolate-ovate, 2-5 cm. long, 5-15 mm. broad, acute or lightly acuminate at the apex, narrowed at the base to distinct petioles 7-15 mm. long, the lateral veins evident, the upper surfaces hirtellous with short appressed hairs, or somewhat viscid with capitate glands, often nearly glabrous, the lower viscid with capitate glands and bearing short spreading or appressed hairs at least on the veins, their margins entire; eyines axillary, many-flowered and as much as 4 cm. long, often 1-3-flowered in depauperate speqimens, borne on peduncles 5-15 mm. long; flowering calyces clothed like the stems, the teeth deltoid, 1.2-2.3 mmn. long, increasing in fruit to 1.8-3.5 mm., about the length of the tube; corolla-tubes not exserted from the calyces, 1.8-2.8 mm. long, the lower lip 1.9-2.9 mm. long; stamens somewhat arched, but not strongly so, 2.5-4.7 mm. long; nutlets 1.8-2.6 mm. long, 0.9-1.5 mim. broad, deeply and irregularly alveolate, hirtellous with short spreading hairs.

description: An erect annual or short lived perennial, 2-4 dm. tall, usually freely branched, the branches herbaceous, hirtellous below the infioreseence with short, downwardly (or rarely upwardly) curled or spreading hairs; leaves oblong to oval, 9-19 mm. long, 4-12 mm. broad, both surfaces hirtellous with short hairs curled toward the apex, the apex obtuse, even emarginate, acute at the base, the petioles as much as 4 mm. long; flowers in axillary eymes, 3-7-flowered, the peduncles as much as 4 cm. long, the pedicels about 5 mm. long, both viscid with capitate glands and more or less hirtellous with short, spreading, straight or upwardly curled hairs; calyces strongly zygomorphic, the lower two teeth about one-third the length of the upper three which are fused one-half to two-thirds their length; flowering calyces 2.8-4.6 mm. long, becoming inverted at maturity, increasing to 4.6-7.1 mm. long; corolla-tube not extending beyond the longer calyx-teeth, 2.6-3.4 mm. long, the lower lip 3.5-5.2 mm. long; stamens exserted, arched, 11-18 mm. long; nutlets 1.5-2.0 mm. long, 1.2-1.5 mm. broad, glabrous, alveolate.

description: Compact epiphytes to 25 cm tall. Rhizome terete, stout, variable to 3 cm long between pseudobulbs. Pseudobulbs complanate, sulcate-ridged, 7.5 x 2.5 cm, with a short, leaf-bearing apical internode. Leaves 3-4, oblong-obovate, subacute, 10-14 x 3.5-4.0 cm. Inflorescences several, erect scapes to 17 cm long, 3 mm diam., enclosed by a series of tubular, subinflated bracts to 2.5 cm long, the floral bract subsimilar to 3 cm long, subequal to the ovary. Flowers campanulate, the sepals pale greenish yellow outside, inner surface with the distal 2/3 purplish brownish with rose-red veins, the midvein olive green, the proximal 1/3 very pale green with more apparent venation, the petals greenish white with pale rose-purple spotting along the veins of the same color, the labellum lateral lobes and callus off-white with dark rose-purple and dark purple spots, the midlobe very pale brown basally becoming off-yellow apically, the column pale greenish white, the anther dark yellow, the pollinia brownish dark yellow, the stipe and viscidium pale tan. Dorsal sepal broadly oblanceolate, acuminate, 5 cm long, 1.8 cm wide across apex, 0.7 cm across the clawed base, 5-veined, apex recurved. Lateral sepals obliquely obovate, acuminate, 5 cm long, 2.2 cm wide across the apex, 0.7 cm wide across the clawed base, 7-veined, api- ces recurved. Petals oblanceolate, acuminate-apiculate, 5-7 veined, 2.8 cm long, 1.2 cm wide across the apex, 0.2 cm wide across the clawed base. Labellum 3-lobed, 1.4 x 0.7 cm in natural position, the lateral lobes erect, falcate, acute, the midlobe suborbicular when flattened, serrulate with the apex recurved, under surface verrucose in the middle. Column slightly arcuate, 1.2 cm long, 5 mm broad near the anther seen from the side. Anther ovate, with a central ridge of finger-like projections, 3.5 x 2 mm, the pollinarium 3 x 1 mm, the pollinia 4 in 2 unequal pairs, the viscidium stalked with a semilunate base.

description: Compact caespitose epiphytes suffused with dull, pale brick red (probably a response to high solar illumination). Pseudobulbs ovoid, rugose, sulcate, somewhat compressed, to 2.3 x 1.8 cm. Leaves 2, elliptic, obtuse, stiffly coriaceous, 4-7 x 1.4- 1.65 cm. Inflorescence an erect scape, 9-10 cm long, with lanceolate, acute bracts, the floral bract oblanceolate, acute, slightly longer than the ovary. Flowers campanulate, the dorsal sepal clear yellowish brown with red-purple veins, paler basally, the lateral sepals similar but tinted reddish across the middle, the petals pale brownish yellow, the labellum similar to the petals but the callus and central region shiny, dark brownish red, the lateral lobes pale yellow, the column pale green, the anther yellow. Dorsal sepal oblanceolate, acute, concave at base, re- curved-convex at apex, 5 x 1.6 cm. Lateral sepals obliquely obovate, acute-acuminate, concave at base, reflexed at apex, 6.4 x 2 cm. Petals obovate, acuminate, apiculate, 2.8 x 1.2, with a raised central pad. Labellum 3-lobed, 3.8-4 x 1.37 cm, articulated to a short column foot, the lateral lobes erect, obliquely obovate, abruptly acute, ciliate along the leading edge, the midlobe suborbicular, plicate, the callus 3-seriate. Column very slightly arcuate, 3 cm long. Anther bilaterally compressed with a longitudinal crest of finger-like projections, the pollinia 4, sessile on a semilunate viscidium.

description: Caespitose epiphytes with fan-shaped, pendent growths to 15 cm tall. Leaves oblanceolate, acute, dorsally carinate, 10-15 x 2-4.5 cm, the lower leaves proportionately wider. Inflorescences pendent scapes, the peduncles to 4 cm long, with 1-2 distant bracts, the floral bract ovate, obtuse, tubular. Flowers shallowly campanulate, cream-yellow with greenish yellow tips, the labellum base yellow with reddish brown markings, the apex pale yellow, the column cream-yellow extended into a golden yellow to yellow-orange foot with reddish purple markings, the anther cream with brown markings. Dorsal sepal ovate, acute, concave, 15 x 8.5 mm. Lateral sepals obliquely and broadly ovate, concave-subsaccate at base, 18 x 13 mm, adnate to the column foot. Petals obliquely oblong, apiculate, 15 x 10 mm, with a central ridge along the midvein. Labellum saccate, obscurely 3-lobed, articulated to the prominent column foot, 12.5 x 7.5 mm, the lateral lobes obliquely obovate, erect, partially enclosing the base of the column, the midlobe a recurved apicular tooth, with a small falcate tooth laterally to each side, the callus a fleshy, transverse ridge below the midlobe. Column straight, slightly dilated below the apex lateral to the stigmatic cavity, 9.3 x 3.9 mm, the foot 12 mm long. Anther 3.3 x 2.1 mm, the pollinarium 3.9 mm long, the vis- cidium ovate, acute, 1.4 x 1.2 mm, the pollinia 4, sessile on the viscidium, the larger pair 2.3 x 0.9 mm.

description: Herba terrestris tenera plus minusve 6 cm alta. Tuber carnosum, ovoideum, plus minusve 1.5 cm longum. Caulis erectus, glaber, purpurascens, e bi- ad trifoliatum. Folia purpurea rica inferne, 9-10 mm longa, 10-11 mm lata, late ovata, obtusata vel subacuta, membranacea, margine minute undulato, glabra, sessilia, amplexicaulia, patentia. Flores in apice scapi solitarii vel duo ad tres, alterni, pedicellati, nutantes, pallide rosei. Bracteae inflorescentiae foliaceae, plus minusve 4 mm longae, ovatae, subacutae. Ovarium lineari-fusiforme. Sepala et petala 6 mm longa, trans medium 2 mm lata, obovata, acuta vel subacuta, carinata, subpatentia. Labellum trilobatum, 5.5 mm longum, trans medium 4 mm latum, cuneatum, basi in unguem angustatum, leviter concavum, album con macula roseo-purpurea; lobi laterales 1 mm lati, subacuti; lobius medius vix 2 mm longus, 2.5 mm latus, cuneatus, truncatus, margine dentato; discus tricarinatus e basi usque ad medium, carinis parallelis. Columna 5 mm longa. Anthera rigida, erecta, apiculata. Massae polliniae ut in T. trianthophora.

description: Plants epiphytic, climbing. Roots aerial, few, slender, velamentous, produced at nodes. Stems terete, jointed, succulent, to 20 m long, 1.5 cm thick, dark green to yellowish green, internodes smooth, to 16 cm. Leaves alternate, one at each node, fleshy, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, acute to acuminate, to 9 cm long, 3 cm wide, conduplicate and recurved, their bases lacking abscission layer. In- forescence axillary from a node, to 21 cm long, racemose, fleshy, flowers to 8, ephemeral. Floral bracts fleshy, ovate, acute, conduplicate, recurved, to 2 cm long, 6 mm wide. Ovary slender, to 5.5 cm long. Sepals green; dorsal sepal oblanceolate, subacu terto acute, to 5.5 cm long, 1.3 cm wide; lateral sepals obliquely oblong-oblanceolate, subacute to acute, to 5.5 cm long, 1.3 cm wide. Petals green, obliquely oblanceolate, subacute, keeled on back, to 5.4 cm long, 1.2 cm wide. Labellum adnate to basal 21 of column, 3-lobed, white with a purple margin, cuneate or fabellate, tubular in natural position; midlobe recurved, to 6 cm long, 5.5 cm wide; lateral lobes orbicular, obtuse; middle of disc with retrorse tuft of white hairs and up to 8 lines of fimbriate lamellae extending from the tuft to the apex of midlobe. Column white, arcuate, to 3 cm long, 0.8 cm wide; anther white. Pod pendent, to 19 cm long, 1.3 cm thick, indehiscent.

description: Fruit 15 mm diam., pericarp 2.5 mm thick, stigmatic remains subapical, with seed and locular epidermis irregularly sculptured-similar to to Campecarpus and Cyphophoenix, but with the fibrous bundles shorter, more oblique and confined to the subepidermal region. Also distinctive is the papillate epidermis, the thick subepidermal zone of tanniniferous/pigment tissue, the dense mantle of brachysclereids around the fibrous bundles, the larger brachysclereids scattered toward the middle pericarp, a ring of small vascular bundles without sheaths just above mid-pericarp, large tanniniferous cells in the inner half of the fruit, lack of raphide-bearing cells, and the unevenly thickened locular epidermis (in other irregularly sculptured endocarps the locular epidermis is still evenly thickened).

description: Fruit globose, 2.5 cm diam., with pericarp 3 mm thick, stigmatic remains basal, seed and endocarp sculpted distinctive within the group for its large size, and for a thick zone of tanniniferous cells below the epidermis, followed by a dense zone of brachysclereids; further characterized by a broad zone of parenchyma with occasional tanniniferous cells, raphide cells and large, nearly terete vascular bundles with little or no fibrous sheaths, and by a very thick locular epidermis.

description: Shrub ca 1-3 m high, rather freely branching; twigs and foliage sparsely to rather copiously hirsutulous with whitish multiseriate hairs (0.1-0.5 mm long), glabrescent, or glabrous from the start. Twigs reddish-or purplish-brown, obscurely to distinctly angled, ca 2-4 mm thick. Cataphylls more or less scarious, stramineous, subpersistent; blade lanceolate, acuminate, 1.3-2.2 mm long; stipules triangular-ovate, acuminate, 1.4-1.8 mm long, 0.7-1.1 mm broad, becoming reflexed and eventually deciduous. Deciduous branchlets simple (pinnatiform) on the lower parts of branches, distally bipinnatiform, ca 5-25 cm long, with 9-22 nodes, the proximal 1-3 nodes with lateral (iterative) axes which are ca 5-12 cm long, with 7-15 nodes; axes of branchlets slender (ca 0.5-1 mm thick), distinctly angled and channelled, greenish to almost silvery. Leaves on both main and lateral axes of branchlet similar (none reduced to scales); blades chartaceous, reddish when young, elliptic to ovate, obtuse or rounded to slightly emarginate and sometimes minutely apiculate at the tip, rounded to barely subcordate at the base, mostly 1.5 -2.5 cm long and 1-2 cm broad (up to 4 cm long by 3 cm broad on sprout-shoots), sometimes sparsely hirsutulous above (but never scabrous), beneath glabrous to rather densely hirsutulous, midrib prominently raised, major lateral veins (ca 5-9 on a side) slightly raised, reticulum of veinlets prominent; margins plane or slightly revolute; petioles subterete, mostly 1.5-2.5 mm long; stipules lanceolate, acuminate, becoming scarious and more or less reflexed, 0.9-1.9 mm long, 0.5-1.1 mm broad. Monoecious; flowers in axillary clusters at most nodes of simple branchlets, and at all except the proximal nodes (those bearing iterative axes) on bipinnatiform branchlets. Cymules typically bisexual, conspicuously bracteolate, more or less stalked (peduncle becoming 0.5-1.0 mm long), with one central [female] and ca 7-15 lateral [male] flowers. Male flowers: pedicel glabrous, slender, 1.5-4.0 mm long. Calyx-lobes 6, biseriate, erect, obtuse to subacute at the tips, 1-nerved, with greenish midrib and whitish margins; outer lobes more or less oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 0.8-1.7 mm long, 0.6-1.0 mm broad; inner lobes elliptic to broadly ovate, 1.0-1.9 mm long, 0.9-1.7 mm broad. Disk-segments 3, massive, bilobed, deeply pitted, 0.4-0.7 mm in diameter. Stamens 3; filaments completely connate into a rather slender distally enlarged column 0.4-0.6 mm high; anthers sessile atop the column (the coinectives completely fused into a 3-angled somewhat umbonate platform), triangular or ovate, acute or subacute at the tip, strongly flattened, ca 0.3-0.4 mm long and broad, dehiscing horizontally; pollen grains spheroidal, 3-colporate, not syncolpate, the colpi distinctly marginate and di-orate, the exine with a complex LO pattern of verrucoid exerescences (not reticulate), ca 32-36 µ in diameter. Female flower: pedicel glabrous or hirsutulous, terete below, dilated and slightly to distinctly angled distally, sometimes reddish (especially toward the base), 3.5-10 mm long, becoming 5-10 mm long in fruit. Calyx-lobes 6, distinctly biseriate as in the male but more herbaceous and often reddish-tinged; outer lobes oblonglanceolate, (1.3-) 1.6-2.2 mm long, 0.6-1.0 mm broad; inner lobes more or less ovate, 1.7-2.2 mm long, 1.4-1.7 mm broad. Disk cupuliform, enclosing 1/2 to 3/4 the ovary, massive, deeply pitted, more or less 6-lobed, 0.6-0.8 mm high and 1.3-1.8 mm in diameter. Ovary smooth and glabrous; styles divergent-spreading (at a ca 45º angle), 0.6-0.7 mm long, deeply bifid beyond the middle into slender capitate branches. Capsule oblate, greenish, reticulate-veined, ca 5 mm in diameter; seeds plumply trigonous (somewhat plano-convex), reddish-brown to nearly blackish, finely and evenly verruculose-dotted, 2.3-2.5 mm long, 1.8-2 mm broad.
