description: Shrubs, treelets or trees to 6(-8) m tall, sparsely branched, stem to 5 cm dbh. Young terminal branchlets 2-4 mm thick, glabrous, rarely strigose, bark on older branchlets peeling. Stipules elliptic to nearly oblong, (6-)9-22 X 3-7 mm, fused intrapetiolarly to 6 mm, acute at apex, thin and brittle when dry, reddish, with parallel venation, glabrous outside or with pubescence along the sometimes elevated midrib, in particular at base, glabrous inside. Leaves with petioles 8-36 mm long, glabrous or sparsely strigose below, semiterete, slightly sulcate above, blades elliptic, 9-16.5(-22) X 3.5-7(-8.5) cm, length/width ratio (2.1-)2.5:3.5(-5.5), papyraceous to slightly coriaceous when dry, cuneate to narrowly cuneate at base, apex acuminate, tips narrowly acute or rarely obtuse, (3-)7-25 mm long, drying light or dark brown usually having lighter veins, secondary veins (6-)7-11(-12) pairs; upper surface matte, glabrous, midrib and secondary veins plane, distinct, tertiary veins distinct or indistinct; lower surface matte, glabrous except for sparsely strigose on midrib and secondary veins, midrib prominent, secondary veins prominulous, tertiary veins slightly elevated or plane, distinct to indistinct. Male inflorescence 4-16-flowered, thyrse-like, peduncle 1-4 mm long, glabrous, pedicels to 13 mm long, glabrous, drying black, inflorescence subtended by stipule-like bracts; calyx 0.2-0.5 X 1.5-2 mm, glabrous outside and inside, lobes usually absent, rarely occasional linear lobes; corolla salverform, sharply fragrant, fleshy, 4-lobed, 29-32 mm long, yellow-green on tube and outside of lobes, lobes white inside, drying brownish black, tube narrowly cylindrical, 13-18 (19 mm in bud) long, 2-3 mm wide, glabrous inside, glabrous or occasionally sparsely pilose outside, lobes oblong, 11-13 X 7 mm, 2/5-?/2 of the corolla length, obtuse at apex, glabrous outside and inside; stamens 4(6) included or tips barely exsert- ed, anthers linear, 8-13 X 0.8-1 mm (unopened anthers 7.5-9 X 0.8 mm long in bud), sessile, inserted on the upper part of the tube, ca. 12 mm above base, dorsifixed, area of insertion 3.5-6 mm above base of anther, apical connective process tiny, base truncate; pollen 6-7-porate; style 17-19 mm long, glabrous, style branches 2-3, erect, 2 mm long. Female infiorescence solitary, peduncle 2.5-3 mm long, glabrous, drying black, bracts stipule-like; calyx 0.5 X 3.5 mm, glabrous outside and inside, lobes absent; corolla salverform, fleshy, (4-)5-6- lobed, 31-33 mm long, white, drying brownish black, tube cylindrical, ca. 20 mm long, ca. 3.5 mm wide at lower part of the tube, ca. 4.5 mm at top, glabrous inside and outside, lobes oblong, 13-14 X 6 mm, 2/5-4/9 of the corolla length, obtuse at apex, glabrous outside and inside; stamens (4-)5-6, anthers linear, 10 X 0.8 mm, sessile, inserted around the middle of the tube ca. 9 mm above base, dorsifixed, area of insertion ca. 4.5 mm above base of anther, apex small, base acute or slightly cleft; style ca. 20 mm long, glabrous, style branches 9-11 mm long; ovary globose, ca. 7 X 8 mm, glabrous; placenta V-shaped, 2 mm tall, with 10-12 ovules. Fruit ± globose, wavy following the contours of the seeds, to 4.3 X 4.5 cm, glabrous, glossy, dark purple to black, with 3-9 mm long peduncle, mesocarp 1-3 mm thick; seeds semi-oblong to obliquely pyramidal, ca. 10 X 10 X 7 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Persson, C. 2003. Agouticarpa, a new neotropical genus of Tribe Gardenieae (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 55: 176-201.

description: Frutex 1.5-4 m alta, vel arbuscula leviter ramosa vel arbor ad 10 m alta, ramis juvenibus leviter puberulentis, hirsutis vel strigosis, raro glabris. Stipulae ellipticae vel obovatae, ad 50(-80) X 30 mm. Petiolus 8-15(-20) mm longus, omnilateraliter sparse hirsutus ad dense strigosus vel interdum adaxiali pagina glaber. Lamina oblanceolata, obovata vel fere elliptica, 18- 26(-38) x 6.3-10(-12.5) cm, in sicco papyracea, ad basin anguste cuneata ad cuneata, ad apicem acuminata, abaxiali pagina sparse hirsuta vel hirsuta. Inflorescentia masculina 3-9-flora, pedunculo non visibili, pedicellis ad 8 mm longis. Corolla hypocrateriformis, 6-loba, tubo anguste obconico, 28-32 mm longo, ad basin ca. 4 mm lato, ad apicem ca. 6 mm lato. Lobi oblongi vel elliptici, 12-20 x 8-13 mm, longitudine 1/3-2/5 corollae. Stamina 6, antheris 14-17 X 1.5 mm, medio tubi corollae inserta. Pollinis grana 3-4-porata. Inflorescentia femina ignota. Fructus sphaericus 4.3-5 x 4.5-5.5 cm, glaber, pedunculo 4-5 mm longo.

description: Shrubs 1.5-4 m, sparsely branched tree- lets or trees to 6 m tall, stem to 7(-15) cm dbh. Young terminal branchlets 2-4 mm thick, sparsely puberulent, hirsute or strigose, rarely glabrous, bark on older branch- lets peeling. Stipules elliptic to obovate, to 50(-80) X 30 mm, free or fused intrapetiolarly, to 10(-30) mm, acute to obtuse at apex, light brown to brown, with parallel venation, sparsely pilose to hirsute-strigose outside, usually with denser pubescence along midrib, glabrous inside. Leaves with petioles 8-15(-20) mm long, sparsely hirsute to densely strigose or sometimes glabrous below, semiterete, slightly sulcate above; blades oblanceolate, obovate or nearly elliptic, 18-26(-38) X 6.3-10(-12.5) cm, length/width 2.33:3.17, papyraceous, narrowly cuneate to cuneate at base, acuminate at apex with tips to 15(-25) mm, drying greenish brown, chestnut to dark brown above, dark beige, greenish brown or brown below, secondary veins 8-11(12) pairs; upper surface matte or glossy, gla- brous or sparsely hirsute, the midrib and secondary veins occasionally hirsute to stri- gose, veins plane or proximal part of midrib either slightly elevated or sulcate; lower surface matte, midrib prominent, secondary veins prominulous, hirsute to densely hir- sute, 30 and 40 venation distinct to promi- nulous, forming, sometimes together with 1(-3) intersecondary veins, a + distinct re- ticulate meshwork, these veins and inter- vening areas sparsely hirsute. Male inflo- rescence 3-9-flowered, thyrse-like or a 3- flowered dichasium, inflorescence branches glabrous, peduncle not visible, pedicels to 8 mm long, glabrous, bracts and bracteoles absent; calyx with wavy margin, 0.5-1 X 3-4 mm, glabrous outside and inside, lobes absent; corolla salverform, with unknown fragrance, rather fleshy, 6-lobed, 40-50 mm long, white (light green in bud), drying dark brown, tube narrowly obconical, 28-32 mm long, ca. 4 mm wide at base, ca. 6 mm wide at top, glabrous inside and outside, lobes oblong or elliptic, 12-20 X 8-13 mm, 1/3-2/5 of the corolla length, rounded at apex, gla- brous outside and inside; stamens 6, includ- ed, inserted around the middle of the tube, 15-18 mm from base of corolla tube, sessile; anthers linear, 14-17 X 1.5 mm (open), subdorsifixed, sessile, inserted 5-7 mm from base of anther, apical connective process tiny, base rounded and slightly cleft; pollen 3-4-porate; style 30-35 mm long, glabrous, style branches 3-4, erect, 3- 6 mm long. Female inflorescence unknown; ovary (young fruit) ellipsoid, glabrous, with ca. 20 ovules per placenta. Fruits + globose, 4.3-5 X 4.5-5.5 cm, glabrous, green (immature?), with a 4-5 mm long peduncle, mesocarp ca. 5 mm thick; seeds depressed globose to oblong, ca. 10 X 8 X 5 mm.

description: Frutex arbuscula arborve, ad 10 m alta, ramis juvenibus dense hirsutis. Stipulae ellipticae vel obovatae, 17-45 x 7-24 mm. Petiolus 6-20 mm longus, dense hirsutus. Lamina obovata, 15-28 X 6.5-13 cm, in sicco papyracea, ad basin anguste cuneata, ad apicem acuminata, abaxiali pagina sparse hirsuta vel hirsuta. Inflorescentia masculina 6-10-flora, pedunculo 5-7 mm longo, hirsuto. Flores sessilis vel pedicellis ad 25 mm longis. Corolla infundibuliformis, 6(7)-loba, tubo 15-20 mm longo, ad basim ca. 4 mm lato, ad apicem ca. 10 mm lato, extus hirsuto vel strigoso, intus glabro. Lobi oblongi, 5-7 X 5-6 mm, longitudine 1/5-1/4 corollae. Stamina 6, antheris ca. 7 X 2 mm, supra medium tubi corollae inserta. Pollinis grana 3-4-porata ad 3-colpoidorata. Inflorescentia femina ignota. Fructus sphaericus, ad 3 X 3 cm, sparse hirsutus vel hirsutus, pedunculo 3-14 mm longo.

description: Shrub, treelet or tree to 10 m tall, stem to 15 cm dbh. Young terminal branchlets 3-4 mm thick, densely hirsute. Stipules elliptic or obovate, 17-45 X 7-24 mm, free at base, obtuse at apex, light brown, strigose or hirsute outside, often more densely so along midrib, glabrous inside. Leaves with petioles 6-20 mm long, densely hirsute, semiterete; blades obovate, 15-28 X 6.5-13 cm, length/width ratio 2.1:2.7, papyraceous, narrowly cuneate at base, acuminate at apex with acute tips to 11 mm long, drying light brown to brown above, light brown below, secondary veins 7-10 pairs; upper surface matte, midrib plane to prominulous, hirsute, remaining venation plane, this and intervenous area sparsely hirsute to sparsely strigose; lower surface matte, midrib prominent, hirsute, secondary veins prominulous, hirsute, 3º and 4º venation distinct, forming a ± distinct reticulate meshwork, these veins and intervening areas sparsely hirsute. Male inflorescences 6-10-flowered, thyrse-like, peduncle 5-7 mm long, hirsute; flowers sessile or with pedicels to 25 mm long, hirsute, subtended by narrowly triangular bracts with colleters inside; calyx with wavy margin, 0.5-1 X 3 mm, densely hirsute outside, glabrous inside, lobes absent; corolla funnel-form, with unknown fragrance, membranaceous, 6(7)-lobed, 20-27 mm long, whitish or yellowish green, drying goldish light yel- low outside, inside of lobes drying black, tube obconical, 15-20 mm long, ca. 4 mm wide at base, ca. 10 mm wide at top in an- thesis, hirsute to strigose outside, glabrous inside; lobes oblong, 5-7 X 5-6 mm, 1/5-1/4 of the corolla length, rounded to obtuse at apex, hirsutulous to shortly strigose outside, glabrous inside; stamens 6, anthers narrowly oblong, ca. 7 X 2 mm (open), sessile, inserted in the upper part of the tube ca. 16 mm from base of corolla tube, tips barely exserted; subdorsifixed, area of insertion ca. 2 mm from base of anther, apical connective process absent, base rounded; pollen 3- 4-porate or colpoidorate; style ca. 20 mm long, sparsely hirsute; style branches 2, oblong, connivent, rounded at apex, ca. 7 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, glabrous. Female in- florescence unknown. Fruits globose (pressed), to 3 X 3 cm, sparsely hirsute to hirsute, green (immature?), with a 3-14 mm long peduncle; seeds irregularly globose, ca. 5-7 X 4 X 4 mm.

description: Tree 10-16 m tall, stem to 12(-25) cm dbh. Young terminal branchlets 3-5(-8) mm thick, glabrous, bark on older branchlets peeling. Stipules elliptic, to 29 X 16 mm, mostly free intrapetiolarly, or fused to 9 mm, acute at apex, thin and brittle when dry, reddish brown, with parallel venation, glabrous outside and inside. Leaves with petioles (25-)45-75 mm long, glabrous, semiterete, sulcate above; blades elliptic, rarely ovate, (19-)22.5-32(-37) X 11-18.5(-21) cm, length/width ratio 1.6:2.05, subcoriaceous to coriaceous when dry, truncate, obtuse or narrowly cuneate at base, shortly acuminate at apex with tips 10-15 mm long, drying light to dark brown above, usually chestnut colored to olive-greenish brown below, with darker reddish brown veins, secondary veins 9-12 pairs; upper surface matte or glossy, glabrous, veins plane or midrib slightly sulcate proximally; lower surface matte, glabrous all over, mid- rib prominent, secondary veins prominulous, tertiary veins rather dense, weak to distinct. Male inflorescence 9-16-flowered, thyrse-like, peduncle to 8 mm long, glabrous, pedicels 5-18 mm long, glabrous, inflorescence subtended by small stipules, bracteoles absent or present as a small callus at base of the pedicels; calyx with wavy margin, sometimes with up to 6 triangular lobes, 0.2-0.5 X 2.5-3 mm (incl. lobes), glabrous outside and inside; corolla salverform, very fragrant, membranaceous, (4-) 5(-6)-lobed, (33-)40-58 mm long, white, drying yellowish brown to brown, tube cylindrical, slightly wider at top, to 15-28 mm long, ca. 5 mm wide in lower part, ca. 6 mm at top, glabrous inside and outside, lobes oblong to narrowly ovate, (18-)25-30(-35) X 5 mm, 1/2-5/8 of the corolla length, obtuse or triangular at apex, glabrous outside and inside; stamens (4-)5(-6), included, anthers linear, (11.5-)16-18 X 1 mm (open), filament <0.5 mm long, inserted in the upper part of the tube, 10-15 mm above base; dorsifixed, filament inserted 8-9 mm from base of anther, apical connective process absent; pollen (3-)4(-5)-porate or colpoidorate; style 20-26 mm long, glabrous, style branches 2-3, erect, 2-7 mm long. Female inflorescence unknown; ovary (young fruit) solitary, globose, ca. 9 mm wide, glabrous, with ca. 20 ovules. Fruits globose or vertically slightly depressed, to 10 X 10 cm, glabrous, green, coffee-colored at ma- turity, with peduncle to 8 mm long, mesocarp to 20 mm thick; seeds subglobose or suboblong, 10-13 X 8-10 X 9-10 mm; placental pulp yellow.

description: Arbuscula vel arbor ad 10 m alta, ramis juvenibus dense hirtellis, pilosis vel glabris. Stipulae ovatae vel ellipticae vel leviter obovatae, ad 37 x 12 mm. Petiolus (17-)25-40 mm longus, adaxiali pagina glabra vel hirtella, abaxiali pagina hirtella. Lamina elliptica ad leviter obovata vel interdum ovata, 18-32 x 8-16 cm, in sicco papyracea, ad basin anguste cuneata, ad apicem acuminata, abaxiali pagina velutina. Inflorescentia masculina ca. 13-flora, pedunculo ca. 2.5 mm longo, glabro, pedicellis 3-8 mm longis. Corolla hypocrateriformis, 5-loba, tubo in alabastro anguste obconico, ad 14 mm longo, ca. 1.5 mm lato, extus et intus glabro, lobis ca. 13 mm longis, fere tubum aequantes. Stamina 5. Antherae ca. 11 X 1 mm. Pollinis grana 4(-5)-porata. Inflorescentia femina ignota. Fructus sphaericus ad 5.5 x 5.5 cm, glaber, pedunculo ad 7 mm longo.

description: Treelets or trees to 10 m tall, stem to ca. 3 cm dbh. Young terminal branchlets 3(-6) mm thick, densely hirtellous, pilose or glabrous, terete, bark on older branchlets peeling. Stipules ovate, elliptic or slightly ob- ovate, to 37 X 12 mm, free intrapetiolarly or fused to 8 mm, acute at apex, thin and brittle when dry, with parallel venation, reddish light brown, pilose outside, and usually hirsute on lower part of midrib, gla- brous inside. Leaves with petioles (17-)25-40 mm long, glabrous to hirtellous above, hirtellous below, proximally usually terete, distally semiterete, slightly sulcate above; blades elliptic to slightly obovate or occasionally ovate, 18-32 X 8-16 cm, length/width ratio 1 .7:2.3(-2.55), papyraceous when dry, cuneate at base, acuminate at apex, tips acute, 11-27(-35) mm long, usu- ally drying dark brown above, light brown, brown to olive-brown below, secondary veins 9-13(-15); upper surface slightly glossy to glossy, glabrous, veins plane or proximal part of midrib slightly sulcate (due to drying?); lower surface matte, velutinous all over, midrib prominent, usually densely velutinous, secondary veins prom- inulous, tertiary veins rather dense and distinct, perpendicular to 20 veins, and somewhat anastomosing. Male inflorescence ca. 13-flowered, thyrse-like, peduncle ca. 2.5 mm long, glabrous, pedicels 3-8 mm long, glabrous, bracts and bracteoles absent; calyx with wavy or completely revolute margin, ca. 0.5 X 2 mm, glabrous outside and inside, lobes absent; corolla salverform, with unknown fragrance, rather fleshy, 5-lobed, 27 mm long in bud, white, drying matte black, tube narrowly cylindrical, to 14 mm long in bud, ca. 1.5 mm wide, glabrous inside and outside, lobes ca. 13 mm long in bud, ca. 1/2 of the corolla length, glabrous outside and inside; stamens 5, anthers linear, ca. 11 X 1 mm (unopened), sessile, inserted slightly above the middle, ca. 8 mm above base of corolla tube, dorsifixed, area of insertion 5.5 mm from base of anther, apical connective process narrowly triangular; pollen 4(-5)-porate; style at least 8 mm long (the only one available broken), glabrous, style branches 2, erect, ca. 3 mm long. Female inflorescence unknown; ovary (or young fruit) ellipsoid, ca. 2 X 1.5 cm, glabrous, ovules ca. 20 per placenta. Fruit globose, to 5.5 X 5.5 cm, sometimes subtended by persistent stipules, glabrous, green (immature?), peduncle to 7 mm long, mesocarp ca. 6 mm, partitioned by false septa; seeds subglobose, subreniform, or oblong, ca. 11 X 9 X 6 mm; placental pulp yellow.

description: Treelets or trees to 25 m tall (one an epiphytic shrub), stem to 25(-40) cm dbh. Young terminal branchlets 3-6(-9) mm thick, glabrous, rarely strigose, bark on older branchlets often peeling. Stipules elliptic to obovate, rarely oblong, 8-35(-50) X to 20(-30) mm, sometimes with a distinct midrib, free or fused intrapetiolarly to 17 mm, acute or obtuse at apex, thin and brittle when dry, reddish brown, or beige when pubescent, with ± parallel venation, gla- brous or sparsely puberulent outside, proximally sometimes densely so along midrib, rarely strigose all over, glabrous inside. Leaves with petioles (10-)20-57 mm long, glabrous, sparsely puberulent, or strigose below, semiterete; blades elliptic to obovate, 10-30(-35) X 4.5-15(-20) cm, length/width ratio 1.4:2(-3), papyraceous to coriaceous when dry, narrowly cuneate to cuneate, rarely obtuse or truncate, at base, apex obtuse or sometimes short acuminate, with obtuse or acute tips, to 12(-18) mm long, drying chestnut-colored or reddish brown above, rarely light brown, usually of lighter color below, often with blackish veins, secondary veins 6-12(-16) pairs; upper surface glossy or matte, glabrous, veins plane; lower surface glossy or matte, midrib prominent, secondary veins prominulous, these glabrous or finely puberulent to strigose, tertiary veins rather sparse, usually indistinct, tertiary veins and intervenous areas, glabrous, rarely sparsely puberulent or sparsely strigose. Male inflorescence 3- 6(-9)-flowered, thyrse-like or 3-flowered dichasia, peduncle to 8 mm long, glabrous, pedicels 4-19 mm long, glabrous, drying black, inflorescence subtended by stipule- like bracts, partial inflorescence rarely subtended by a rim, 0.2-0.5 mm; calyx with wavy margin 1-1.5 X 3-6 mm, glabrous outside and inside, lobes absent; corolla salverform, aromatic, sweet-smelling, fleshy, 6(-7)-lobed, 44-60(-75) mm long, tube cylindrical, slightly wider at top, to 22-40 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, glabrous inside and outside, greenish white or yellow, lobes broadly elliptic, oblong, or obovate, (15-)20-30 X 8-15 mm, 1/3-1/2 of the corolla length, obtuse at apex, glabrous outside and inside, white, lobes and tube drying brownish black; stamens 6-7, anthers linear, 11-26 X 1-2 mm, sessile, inserted around the middle to upper part of corolla tube, 13-30 mm above base; dorsifixed, area of insertion 5.5-12 mm above base of anther, apical connective process 1.5 mm long, triangular, base truncate; pollen 3-porate; non functional style 25-42 mm long, glabrous, style branches 3-4, erect, (1-)4- 5(-7) mm long, sometimes ridged outside. Female inflorescence 1-3-flowered, pedun- cle to 6 mm long, glabrous, pedicels 4-5 mm, glabrous, drying black, bracts stipule-like; calyx 1.5-2 X 8-9 mm, glabrous outside and inside, lobes absent; corolla salverform, fleshy, 6-7-lobed, ca. 46 mm long, white, light green in bud, drying brownish black, tube cylindrical, ca. 20 mm long, ca. 7 mm wide at base, ca. 10 mm at top, glabrous inside and outside, lobes oblong, ca. 26 X 13 mm, ca. 5/8 of the corolla length, obtuse at apex, glabrous outside and inside; stamens 6-7, included, anthers linear, ca. 14 X 1 mm, sessile, inserted around the middle of corolla tube, ca. 9 mm above base; subdorsifixed, area of insertion ca. 6 mm from base of anther, apex indistinct, base trun- cate; style ca. 19 mm long, glabrous, style branches 6-8 mm long, ridged on back; ovary ca. 14 X 10 mm, glabrous, ca. 10 ovules per placenta. Fruit ± globose, to 8 X 9 cm, glabrous, green, with a 10-23 mm long peduncle, mesocarp to 18 mm thick; seeds subglobose, oblong, or obtusely three-cornered, to ca. 14 X 10 X 5 mm; placental pulp greenish brown.

description: Short-lived herbs, erect, few- to several- branched, 5-50 cm tall; stems pubescent-puberulent to glabrate, pale green, often vinaceous at the internodes; internodes 4.2-11.2 cm long. Stipular sheath, 2.5-3 mm long, pubescent, with (6-)7-9 linear setae 2-4 mm long, sparsely pilose at base. Leaves elliptic, attenuate at base, acute and mucronate at apex, (0.8-)1.1-4.5 X (0.2-) 0.9-1.3 cm, pale green, slightly scabrous on both sides; secondary veins 3-4 on each side, impressed above, prominent below. Flowering branches with 1-2 (rarely 3-5) glomerules terminal and axillary, pubescent and puberulous; internodes (1.5-)4.5- 8.5(-11.5) cm long; glomerules (0.5-)1.3- 1.9 cm diam., the terminal ones subtended by 4 bracts (rarely 6, when formed by two nodes, with an extremely reduced internode), the axillary ones subtended by 2 bracts; bracts elliptic to ovate-elliptic, (0.7-)2.2-5 X (0.4-)0.7-1.6 cm, pale green, often purple at the base (forming a purple ring around the glomerules); bracteoles setose, ca. 3 mm long. Flowers subsessile, slightly fragrant. Calyx lobes linear- lanceolate, pilose, the longer two (2-)2.5-3 mm long, the shorter two 1-1.5 mm long, usually with purple margins; tube (0.8-)1- 1.5 mm long (frequently longer when fruits mature). Corolla 4-5 mm long, outside gla- brous or minutely pilose on the upper third of the tube; lobes ovate-triangular, 1-1.5 mm long, pilose externally. Stamens sessile; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm long, yellow. Style 4-5 mm long; stigmatic lobes 0.7 mm long. Capsules obovoid, 1.5-2 X 1 mm, glabrous or rarely sparsely pilose at apex. Seeds obovoid, 0.8-1 X 0.5 mm, brown, with an X-shaped depression on the ventral face, and semicircular depressions on the dorsal face (the dorsal depressions being a continuation of the ventral ones, Fig. 2A, B).

description: Pyramidal treelets (or rarely few-branched shrubs), to 2.5 m tall, erect or somewhat prostrate when growing on cliffs; bark lightly fissured, cream-colored to pale brown. Stipules free or shortly connate at base, narrowly triangular to deltoid (rarely broadly triangular), 3.5-4.5 mm long, acute or acuminate at apex. Leaves shortly petiolate; petioles 2-5 mm long; blades narrowly elliptic, elliptic, or ovate to obovate, 4.5-11 X 2-5.1 cm, acute to acuminate at apex, acute or decurrent at base, subcoriaceous, margin not revolute. Inflorescences reduced cymes, axillary in last nodes of the stems, 1-2-flowered. Flowers with pedicels 1-1.5 cm long. Calyx lobes narrowly elliptic to narrowly lanceolate (rarely linear), 9-15 X (1-)2-3 mm, chartaceous. Corolla gradually expanding from the base to one-third of the length, subparallel at the medio-distal portion, and slightly flaring at mouth, 2.5- 5.4 cm long (including lobes), dark pink, red to deep crimson, often with 5 white lines along angles inside; tube 2.5-3 mm wide at base, 9-20 mm wide at mouth; lobes 5, broadly ovate or broadly triangular, 3-5 X 6-9 mm, round at apex. Filaments 1.7-3.2 cm long, pubescent at base, free at base; anthers completely included, elongate, slightly twisting at anthesis, 11-13 X 0.3-0.5 mm, base and apex round. Style included, shorter than corolla tube, glabrous; with two stigmatic lines 5-8 mm long. Capsules subglobose to obovoid, smooth when young, becoming slightly 5-costate at maturity, 9-18 X 7-15 mm. Seeds concavo-convex, round to broadly obovoid, 1.6-2 x 1.5-1.9 mm.

description: Campomanesiae macrobracteolatae primo adspectu simillima, sed bracteolis minoribus, lanceolato-ellipticis, ca. 5 mm longis, hypanthio protuberationibus elongatis. Arbor usque 27-metralis; folia elliptica, suborbicularia, oblanceolata, vel obovata, 5-13.5 X 4.3-9 cm, 1.2-2.3-plo longiora quam latiora; apex acuminatus vel acutus; basis acuta, vel rotundata; pedunculus 1-3- floribus; bracteolae foliosae, lanceolato-ellipticae, ca. 5 mm longae; lobi calycis subaequales, 4-7 X 4-5 mm, venis ca. 3, subaequalibus; hypanthium infundibulare vel campanulatum, 6-7 mm longum, prolongatum ca. 2 mm ultra ovarium, protuberationibus elongatis; discus ca. 7 mm latus; antherae oblongae, ca. 1 mm longae; stylus ca. 10 mm longus; ovarium 6-loculare, loculis 6-8-ovulatis.

description: Tree 5-27 m tall, sparsely to densely pubescent on young growth, the young growth glandular; hairs whitish to light reddish brown, to 0.5(-1) mm long; young twigs sparsely to densely pubescent, drying gray-green, the first bark flaking off, revealing longitudinal fibers beneath, the older bark scaly, grayish to light reddish brown. Leaf blades elliptic, suborbicular, to obovate or oblanceolate, 5-13.5 X 4.3-9 cm, 1.2-2.3X as long as wide, sparsely covered with hairs above, more densely so below, especially along the veins, with tufts of hairs often present in the axils of the lateral veins below, these often surrounding small pits (domatia), subcoriaceous, drying gray-green to reddish brown, somewhat lighter below than above, sometimes slightly lustrous above, sometimes glandular below; apex acuminate to acute, sometimes with a mucronate tip; base acute to rounded; lateral veins impressed above, prominent below, usually 6-9 pairs, the venation brochidodromous, the secondary veins numerous, often impressed above and raised below, connecting the laterals and about perpedicular to them, the smaller reticulate veins visible between them; midvein impressed above, prominent below; petioles channeled, 3-12 mm long, 1 mm thick. Peduncles 1-3-florous, 1-30 X 1-1.5 mm, moderately to densely pubescent, borne in the axils of leaves, the lateral flowers sessil or the pedicels to 18 mm long; bracteoles leaf-like, lanceolate-elliptic, to ca. 5 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, caducous at about anthesis, moderately pubescent; calyx-lobes about equal, leafy, broadly elliptic to triangular, 4-7 X 4-5 mm, with ca. 3 subequal veins, densely to sparsely pubescent; hypanthium infundibular to campanulate, 6-7 mm long, prolonged ca. 2 mm beyond the summit of the ovary, grayish pubescent, with tentacle-like protrusions to 2.5 mm long; disk ca. 7 mm across, pubescent; stamens to ca. 8 mm long, ca. 250; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm long; style ca. 10 mm long, the peltate stigma ca. 1 mm across; ovary 6-locular; ovules 6-8 per locule. Fruit unknown.

description: Campomanesiae dichotomae primo adspectu simil- lima, sed bracteolis foliosis, 9-22 mm longis, lobis calycis 4-13 mm longis. description: Tree or shrub to 3 m tall, subglabrous to densely pubescent on young growth, the young growth glandular; hairs whitish to light reddish brown, to 0.5(-1) mm long; young twigs sparsely to densely pubescent, drying gray-green, the first bark flaking off, revealing longitudinal fibers beneath, the older bark scaly, yellowish gray to light reddish brown. Leaf blades suborbicular, elliptic to ovate or obovate, 5-14.2 X 4.3- 10.5 cm, 1.1-1.4 X as long as wide, subcoriaceous, drying reddish brown, slightly lighter below than above, sometimes slightly lustrous above, covered with numerous glands below, subglabrous to sparsely pubescent along veins above, subglabrous or with tufts of hairs in the axils of lateral veins below, these tufts often surrounding small pits (domatia); apex acuminate to acute; base subcordate, acute, rounded, to attenuate; midvein impressed above, prominent below; lateral veins about flat above, prominent below, usually 4-6 pairs, the venation brochidodromous, the secondary veins numerous, connecting the laterals and about perpendicular to them, about flat above and below, the smaller reticulate veins visible between them; petioles chan- neled, 6-12 mm long, 1.2-1.5 mm thick. Peduncles 1-3-florous (perhaps rarely with more flowers), 3-30 X 0.8-1 mm, moder- ately to densely pubescent, borne in the ax- ils of leaves, the lateral flowers on pedicels to ca. 17 mm long; bracteoles leaflike, el- liptic, 9-22 X 5-10 mm, persistent, sparse- ly to moderately pubescent, petiolate, the petiole 1-3 mm long; calyx-lobes leafy, broadly elliptic to triangular, 7-15 X 4-10 mm, with ca. 3 subequal veins, sparsely to moderately pubescent within and without; petals suborbicular to obovate, ca. 10 mm long, sparsely to moderately pubescent, densely glandular; hypanthium infundibular to campanulate, 6-7 mm long, prolonged ca. 2 mm beyond the summit of the ovary, proximally light reddish brown pubescent, distally grayish pubescent, with warty pro- trusions; disk 4-10 mm across, pubescent; stamens ca. 7 mm long, ca. 140; anthers oblong, ca. 1.3 mm long; style 7-8 mm long, the stigma ca. 0.5 mm across; ovary 6-8-locular; ovules 14-18 per locule. Fruit globose, 10-17 mm wide. Seeds 1-2 per fruit.

description: Trees, 2-12 m. tall. The hairs, when present, yellowish to white, simple. Young branchlets puberulous to glabrous, strongly flattened, bicarinate, second-year branches with peeling bark. Leaf blades ovate to obovate, commonly elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 9-20 X 3-7.5 cm, chartaceous, puberulous to glabrous, discolorous, drying olive-green to brownish green above, yellowish to olive-green below, glands indistinct or with small glandular dots below, occasionally minutely impressed-punctate above; apex acute to acuminate or rarely long-acuminate; base obtuse to cuneate; midvein sulcate above, convex below; lateral veins 14-23 pairs, indistinct above, scarcely salient below; marginal vein ca. 2-3 mm from blade margin; petiole 5-10 mm long, canaliculate, puberulous, drying blackish. Panicles subterminal or axillary, 2 per node, 2-10 cm long, the axes pubescent; bracts 1-2 mm long, broadly ovate, acute, spreading, caducous at anthesis; bracteoles ca. 1 mm long, ovate, acute, caducous at anthesis; buds 3-4 mm long, shortly 4-lobed at apex, pubescent to puberulous, tearing irregulary and longitudinally at anthesis; hypanthium prolonged ca. 1.5 mm above apex of ovary; calyx lobes ca. 1 mm long, irregulary shaped, puberulent within; petals ca. 1 mm diam., suborbicular, puberulous; disk 1-1.5 mm diam., glabrous; filaments 4-6 mm long, the anthers ca. 0.5 mm long; style 6-7 mm long; ovary 2-locular; ovules 2 per locule. Fruits red, globose, 1-1.3 cm diam., sulcate, without consistent number of ridges, crowned by remnants of calyx lobes, puberulous to glabrous; seeds 1 or 2, ca. 8 X 6 mm, the seed coat membranaceous; embryo eugenioid, the cotyledons plano-convex, separate.

description: Trees ca. 18 m tall, the hairs when pre- sent whitish, simple or dibrachiate; young branchlets puberulous to glabrous, slightly compressed. Leaf blades ovate, elliptic or narrowly elliptic, 3.8-6 X 0.8-1.5 cm, chartaceous, puberulous to glabrous, dis- colorous, drying olive-green above, yellow- ish green below, with small glandular dots below; apex long-acuminate, the acumen 1.5-2 cm long; base obtuse to cuneate; mid- vein sulcate above, convex below; lateral veins numerous, indistinct above, barely ev- ident and elevated below; marginal vein to 1 mm from blade margin; petiole 2-3 mm long, canaliculate, puberulous. Bracteate shoots 3-7-flowered, axillary, 1-1.5 cm long, the axes puberulous; bracts minute, ovate, persistent; peduncles 1-3 mm long; bracteoles 0.3-0.5 mm long, caducous past anthesis; buds 2-3 mm long, shortly 4- lobed at apex, pubescent, tearing irregulary and longitudinally at anthesis; hypanthium prolonged ca. 1 mm above apex of ovary; calyx lobes ca. 1 mm long, irregulary shaped, densely puberulent within; petals ca. 1 mm diam., suborbicular, puberulous; disk ca. 1 mm diam., glabrous; filaments ca. 4 mm long, the anthers ca. 0.5 mm long; style 4-5 mm long; ovary 2-locular; ovules 2 per locule. Fruits orange to red, globose, ca. 0.8 cm diam., smooth, crowned by rem- nants of calyx lobes, puberulous to gla- brous; seeds 1 or 2, ca. 6 X 4 mm, the seed coat membranaceous; embryo eugenioid, the cotyledons separate.

description: Shrubs, to 4 m tall; dioecious or monoecious; indumentum simple; latex absent. Branches smooth, glabrescent, unarmed; lenticels inconspicuous and rounded; bark bright brown to reddish brown. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, 3-6 mm long, entire, spreading to appressed, tomentose, deciduous; petioles 0.5-2 cm long, densely tomentose; blades ovate to broadly ovate, 2.8-8 cm X 1.7-5.7 cm, the apex acute to rarely obtuse, the base cordate, rounded, truncate or slightly oblique, the margin dentate to crenate, velvety to the touch, adaxial surface greenish, villous hairs ca. 0.6 mm long, abaxial surface cinereous, dense villous hairs 0.6-1 mm long. Staminate inflorescences axillary, racemose, pedunculate, 1-1.5 cm long at anthesis, ca. 6-20-flowered, mostly with staminate flowers but rarely terminated by a pistillate flower; bracts 3-5, elliptic to triangular, imbricate, subtending 2 or 3 staminate flowers, cucullate, ca. 1.5 X 1 mm, acute. Staminateflowers on pedicels 1-1.5 mm long, sepals valvate, 5, narrowly triangular to elliptic, ca. 2.5 X 1.5 mm, densely pilose abaxially; petals absent; disk extrastaminal, annular, glabrous, fleshy, red; stamens 10, connate at the base, in two whorls, red to blackish purple; filaments 1.4-2.3 mm long, filiform, those of the outer whorl free above the base, those of the inner whorl connate and forming a column for ca. 1/3 to 1/2 their length; anthers bilocular, versatile, subdorsifixed, globose to elliptic, 0.3-0.5 mm long; pistillode present. Pistillate flowers solitary or rarely in 2-4-flowered racemes, axillary, subtended by bracts as in the staminate flowers, on tomentose pedicels 8- 8.5 mm long in fruit; sepals 5-6, valvate, triangular to oblong or oblanceolate, subequal, ca. 3.5-6.5 X ca. 1.5 mm, acute to obtuse at apex, densely pilose; disc annular, fleshy, glabrous; ovary subglobose, shallowly 3-lobed, densely tomentose; styles 3, united ca. 2/3-4/5 their length, 3-4 mm long, 2-parted and laciniate at the apex. Fruit capsular, (2-)3(-4)-lobed, 1-1.5 cm diam., densely tomentose, rugose beneath the pubescence. Seeds subspherical to ovoid, rounded apex and base, 5.3-7 mm diam., ecarunculate, slightly carinate on the back, testa crustaceous, chestnut-colored to nearly black, smooth but microreticulate under high magnification.

description:
Much-branched annual to ca. 60 cm; roots thin, fibrous; shoots ascending to decumbent; leaves spirally arranged, the sheaths 0.3-1 cm long, pilose-puberulous, ciliate at the apex; lamina sessile to shortly petiolate, linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate-elliptic, 4-9 x 0.4-1.9 cm, the apex acuminate to acute, the base cuneate, the margins ciliate with uniseriate hairs intermixed with hook-hairs and prickle-hairs, both surfaces pilose-puberulous.

Inflorescences lax, ovoid thyrses, to 3.5 cm long and 4 cm wide, terminal on the main flowering shoots and on axillary, perforating and nonperforating shoots, consisting of 1-3(4) alternate, ascending cincinni; peduncles of terminal inflorescences 3.5-10 cm long, puberulous; inflorescence bract (leaf or bract just basal to the terminal inflorescence) supramedial, bract-like or foliaceous, when foliaceous, then smaller than the leaf below and similarly pubescent. In- florescence axis puberulous. Cincinni to 3.5 cm long and 10-flowered. Cincinnus bracts membranous, 1-3 mm long, eglandular, glabrous. Cincinnus peduncles 6-12 mm long, puberulous. Cincinnus axis puberulous. Bracteoles attached 1.5-5 mm apart, membranous, asymmetrically cup-shaped, perfoliate or occasionally split to the base, ovate, 0.9-1.25 mm long, usually distinctly glandular near the apex, sometimes with apparent, small, marginal glands toward the base, sparsely puberulous basally, occasionally with a single, long uniseriate hair at the base.

Flowers bisexual. Pedicels 4-8 mm long, ± uniformly recurved in fruit ca. 120-180?, persistent, puberulous at least distally. Sepals glandular near the apex with bilobed glands, puberulous, the outer sepal 2.3-3 mm long, paired sepals 2.4-3.2 mm long. Petals pale blue. Staminodes apparently 3, with bilobed, yellow antherodes. Lateral stamens with glabrous filaments and broadly elliptic (in bud) anthers. Medial stamen with a larger, saddle-shaped anther. Ovary trilocular, densely puberulous, locules 1-ovulate; style tapered from the base; stig- ma capitate.

Capsules stipitate, trilocular, bivalved, obovate to subquadrate, 4-4.5 X 3.4-4 mm, carinate middorsally, gray, often pep- pered with black and dark brown, lustrous, puberulous, apex emarginate, dorsal valve deciduous, dorsal locule very prominent, humpbacked apically, (0)1-seeded, ventral locules 1-seeded, the cells of the capsule wall transversely elongate. Dorsal locule seed hemispherical, humpbacked apically, transversely elliptic in outline, 2.7-2.75 mm long, 1.95-2.1 mm wide, 1.6-1.7 mm thick; hilum dark brown, not in a groove, shorter than the seed; testa orange-buff, smooth, with loose, matted brown and white material around the hilum. Ventral locule seeds transversely elliptic, 2.7-3.2 mm long, 2-2.05 mm wide, 1.25-1.5 mm thick, somewhat thicker at one end; hilum dark, not in a groove, much shorter than the seed; testa scrobiculate to transversely ribbed, the underlying color orange-tan or gray, the whole surface covered by a matted farinaceous layer that can be scraped off in a sheet, the material on the ventral surface mainly blackish brown, that on the dorsal surface whitish or tan with darker brown spots; embryotega elliptic, concolorous with the underlying tests.

description: Epiphytes or terrestrials to 40 cm tall. Pseudobulbs aggregate, conical, dark green to brownish, 5-8 X 2-2.5 cm. Leaves lanceolate to ovate, membranaceous to sub-coriaceous, 15-30 X 6.5-10 cm, pseudo-petiole 0.5-2 cm long. Inflorescence 3-6 flowered, erect, up to 10 cm long, concealed by scape bracts, scape and floral bracts 2-3 X 1-1.5 cm. Flowers with a sweet and strong fragance, dark red to purple on the exterior, greenish yellow on the interior, the labellum yellowish pink with red stripes, 3.5 cm long, 2.5 cm wide. Sepals ovate, truncate, dorsal sepal 2.5-3.3 X 1.8 cm, lateral sepals acuminate in the apex, parallel to each other, 2-3 X 1.5 cm, spur with sepal segments superposed, 0.5 cm long. Petals oblanceolate, truncate, oblique to column, 1.8-2.3 X 1-1.4 cm. Labellum 3-lobed, obovate, puberulous, 1.7-1.8 X 1.2-1.3 cm when expanded, lateral lobes erect, involute, obovate, 0.8-1 X 0.3 cm, the midlobe obtuse, rounded, emarginate, recurved, with undulate margins, the claw 0.4 cm long, the callus 1.2 cm long, puberulous, on the anterior region 2-lobed to 3-lobed, protuberant and glabrous. Column glabrous, 0.9-1 cm, the foot straight, puberulous, 1-1.3 cm long. Anther with a prominent apex, 0.3-0.4 X 0.2-0.4 cm, the pollinia rounded, the stipe forked, 0.1 cm long, the viscidium cuneate, 0.1 cm long. Ovary-pedicel 3.5-5 cm long.

description: Epiphytes, rarely rupicolous plants, 10-25 cm tall. Pseudobulbs aggregate, conical to dorsiventrally compressed, dark green to brownish, 2.5-5 X 0.8-3 cm. Petals lanceolate, acuminate, oblique to column, 1.3-2.4 X 0.3-0.5 cm. description: Plant epiphytic. Leaves few in a suberect rosette, to 1.25 m long, coriaceous. Scape 50-75 cm X 4-5 mm, erect at first then pendant, green, coarsely white-lepidote; scape bracts elliptic, acute, 12-18 X 2-6 cm, entire, thin, nerved, pale-lepidote, the lowest bracts appressed and greenish white, the uppermost bracts spreading and rose to red. Inflorescence pendulous, simple, 15-25 X 12-17 cm, polystichously 20-40-flowered, the axis densely white-lepidote; floral bracts ovate, acute, 2-5 mm long, thin, nerved, white-lepidote. Flowers sessile, spreading ca. 450 from axis at anthesis, opening during the day; sepals elliptic to subtriangular, acute, slightly unequal, 17-25 X 4-7 mm, thin, nerved, blue, white-lepidote; petals ligulate, acute, tightly coiling abaxially, 88-100 X 4-9 mm, lustrous, pale green to gold-tinged green, each with two basal appendages, these 2-3 mm long; filaments 80-85 mm long; anthers narrow, 15-18 mm long; stigma conduplicately spiraled, ca. 15 mm long; ovary ellipsoid, 5-9 X 4-6 mm, the epigynous tube 4-5 X 5-8 mm, both white-lepidote and sulcate.

description: Terrestrial, perennial herbs, erect, 10-100 cm tall; corms erect, globose, 1-2 cm wide covered by sheathing scarious bracts. Inflorescence lateral, racemose or paniculate, 13-102 cm long; floral bracts ovate-lanceolate, 1.9-8.2 mm long, acuminate. Flowers erect, perianth lilac with shades of white, 2.3-3 cm long including the pedicellate ovary. Dorsal sepal separated from lateral sepals, pale lilac, 10.9-16 X 3-4.6 mm, lanceolate, erect, the apex reflexed, the lateral sepals horizontal at the base of the flower, whitish at base, lilac at apex, 10.2-14.2 X 3.9-5 mm, falcate, spreading, apex revolute and curved down- ward. Lip trilobed, obovate, whitish at the base, rose-purple at apex, the lateral lobes strongly turned up and enclosing the column, 9.1- 11.7 X 6.2-9 mm, the lateral lobes 5.7-7.6 mm wide, sinuses narrow, the midlobe 3.2- 5 X 3.1-7.6 mm, with an isthmus, obdeltoid, the margin undulate, the apex emarginate, lip position at an angle <1000 to the ovary, callus of the lip with 3-5 parallel white crests from the base to the midpoint of the midlobe. Ovary pedicellate, 0.9-3.1 cm. Column arched, prolonged at the base, where is inserted on the pedicellate ovary, two wings near the base, whitish, 8-9.6 mm long. Pollinarium 1-3 mm long, pollinia soft, elliptic. Capsule thin, curved, 2-3.2 cm long. Flowering March-May.

description: Perigonial bristles (Fig. 2A) light brown, on the same achene ca. ½ length of to ca. same length as achene, achenes falling with bristles firmly attached. Achenes (Fig. 2A, C) in outline obovate to obpyriform with rounded summit and pronounced, tapered beak; nearly equilaterally strongly trigonous with sides convex above and concave to- ward base, ca. 3.8-5.5 x 2-2.9 mm; ratio of maximum width: basal width = ca. 4:1. Surface unevenly to evenly grayish brown; appearing smooth to faintly cellular at 20 x; exocarp cells at 600 x (Fig. 2B) ca. isodiametric to irregularly shortly oblong, walls (particularly the longitudinal) raised and central zone depressed; poorly light reflective, slightly polished to dull, often variable within an individual. On soaking in water, viewed at 40 x, within one minute an air bubble appeared under the outer periclinal wall of each exocarp cell on most of the surface. After ca. 24 hours of soaking, the outer periclinal walls of the exocarp with the attached anticlinal walls were easily peeled away as fragments or sheets. The achenes at first floated in the surface film, but because they were denser than water they sank to the bottom after being pushed down through the surface. In transverse section (Fig. 2C, D): exocarp cells ca. isodiametric. Exocarp thickness ca. 1/7 to 1/4 of mesocarp thickness.
bibliographicCitation: Browning, J., et al. 1995. Achene structure and taxonomy of North American Bolboschoenus (Cyperaceae). Brittonia. 47: 433-445.

description:
Perigonial bristles (Figs. 3A, 4A) ca. 1/2 achene length, achenes mostly falling with bristles attached. Achenes (Figs. 3A, C; 4A, C) in outline elliptic-obovate to obovate with sloping to rounded summit, or often nearly truncate in Smith and Taylor 3134, the beak usually poorly developed; faintly trigonous to plano or unequally biconvex with convex sides; 2.5-2.9 x 1.3-1.9 in Nobs and Smith 1883; 2.8-3.3 x 1.8-2.3 in Smith and Taylor 3134; ratio of maximum width: base width 5:1 to 6:1. Surface color golden to mostly dark brown; at 20 x non-cellular in Nobs and Smith 1883, but in Smith and Taylor 3134 variably faintly to prominently cellular in same achene; epidermal cells at 600 x (Figs. 3B, 4B) isodiametric to slightly elongated, walls faintly raised above central area of each cell, somewhat light reflective, producing a shine. On soaking in water, viewed at 40 x, no air bubbles appeared at exocarp cells. After ca. 24 hrs soaking, the outer periclinal walls were not detachable.

The achenes at first floated in the surface film but sank to the bottom after being pushed downward because they were denser than water. In transverse section: exocarp cells differed in achenes from the two California collections examined. In Nobs and Smith 1883 (Figs. 3C, D), cells isodiametric, the ratio of depth:width 1:1 to 1:1.3; in Smith and Taylor 3134 (Figs. 4C, D), cells radially elongate, the ratio of depth: width for an individual cell 2.3:1 to 3:1. Presence of silica bodies not determined with certainty. Mesocarp of approximately same thickness in all achenes examined but pro- portions differ between the two collections according to depth of exocarp cells; namely, if exocarp cells are isodiametric (in Nobs & Smith 1883), exocarp ca. 1/3 as thick as mesocarp; if exocarp cells are radially elongate (in Smith & Taylor 3134), exocarp ca. 2/3 as thick as mesocarp.
bibliographicCitation: Browning, J., et al. 1995. Achene structure and taxonomy of North American Bolboschoenus (Cyperaceae). Brittonia. 47: 433-445.

description: Perigonial bristles mostly caducous, slender, retrorsely barbed, ca. 1/2 achene length. Achenes (Fig. 1A, C) in outline obovate, summit rounded to nearly truncate with short, abrupt beak, base narrowly cuneate; plano to unequally biconvex or concave- sided, very rarely compressed obtusely trigonous; 2.3-4.1 x 1.9-2.8 mm; ratio of maximum width: basal width = 6.5:1 to 7.5: 1. Surface medium to dark brown; distinctly cellular at 20 x; exocarp cells at 600 x (Fig. 1B) ca. isodiametric, 5-, 6-, or 7-sided, walls not raised, central zone flat, not depressed; very glossy, covered with a waterproof wax- like material. On soaking in water, viewed at 40 x, no air bubbles appeared at exocarp cells. After 24 hrs soaking, the exocarp or any part of it was not detachable. The achenes were much less dense than water and remained floating at the water surface for the 24-hr trial period even after being pushed down through the surface film, with no indication that they were absorbing water. In transverse section (Fig. 1C, D): exocarp cells radially elongate (oblong), ratio of depth: width of individual cell ca. 3:1; anticlinal walls somewhat wavy (walls appear crumpled or folded as in a bellows); silica bodies not observed in exocarp; exocarp ca. 1.6 to 2.5 x thicker than mesocarp.
bibliographicCitation: Browning, J., et al. 1995. Achene structure and taxonomy of North American Bolboschoenus (Cyperaceae). Brittonia. 47: 433-445.

description: In the types of both names, the base of the scape is sub-bulbiform with a short rhizome; the single capitate inflorescence is 0.9-1.2 (-1.5) x 0.9-2.3 cm, hemispherical, dense, and subtended by 3 or 4 leaf-like involucral bracts with dilated bases, the lowest two longer than the inflorescence; the anthers are linear, each with a pointed, prolonged connective which becomes thin after dehiscence; the achene is trigonous, oblong-obovoid, 1-1.2 x 0.8 mm with a papillose surface; and the style base is umbonate in the middle.

description: Caespitose perennial, to 5 dm tall. Leaves cinnamon-colored, minutely red-speckled under magnification, from 1/4 to 1/2 the length of the mature culms; blades 0.75 (1.0) mm wide, flat to somewhat involute, the veins numerous and prominent on both surfaces, two of these comprising the cartilaginous thickened, antrorsely scabrid margin; sheaths glabrous, the margin scarious, with scabrous to dendritic fimbriae apically. Culms slender, subterete to somewhat flattened, about as wide as the leaves, conspicuously many-ribbed and channeled, smooth cinnamon-colored, minutely red-speckled under magnification. Inflorescence a narrow anthella, 5-10 cm high, umbellate; involucral bracts 3-5, leaflike, subtending erect, slender, prophyllate rays, the longest involucral bract much overtopped by the inflorescence, the central spikelet sessile, 7-15 mm long. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate, acute, somewhat flattened, often proliferous, 0.5- 1.5 cm long, ca. 2 mm wide, long-pedunculate (except for the central sessile spike- let). Fertile bracts cinnamon-colored, sparsely puberulent to glabrous, lance-ovate, boat-shaped, 3 mm long, 1-1.2 mm wide, rounded to an emarginate apex, the midrib slightly or not at all excurrent. Flowers with 3 stamens, filaments flat, the anthers ca. 1.1 mm long, ellipsoidal, basifixed, apiculate, bilocular, longitudinally dehiscent; style 3-branched, the branches with minute rounded protrusions. Achene when mature narrowly obovate, obscurely trigonous, 1- 1.2 mm long, 0.7-0.8 mm wide, dark brown to grayish-brown, the angles light brown, the surface pebbled with coarse shiny papillae, these distributed evenly, or in indis- tinct transversely rugulose lines, the tubercle persistent, sub-conic.
bibliographicCitation: Strong, Mark T. 1993. Two overlooked species of Bulbostylis (Cyperaceae) from South America. Brittonia. 45: 162-169.

description: Caespitose perennial (Fig. IA); rhizome short; roots fibrous, brown, sometimes short caudiciform at base. Culm 15-25 cm tall, 0.5-0.7 mm wide, trigonous, nerved on the angles, with a single nerve medially on each side, glabrous, smooth, green, dark mottled and black-dotted with age. Leaves up to 15 cm long; blades ca. as wide as culms, 0.3-0.7 mm wide, green, glabrous, smooth, dark mottled and black-dotted with age, flattened-subulate, 3-nerved on abaxial side, the apex acuminate, subulate-tipped; sheaths (Fig. IB) smooth on adaxial sur- face, the abaxial surface finely veined, antrorsely ciliate-scabrous along veins distally, purplish to brownish black, the ventral apex prolonged into 2, uneven auricles bearing copious, white multicellular trichomes, up to 20 mm long. Inflorescence a single spikelet at the summit of the culm; spikelets (Fig. IC) ovoid, with spirally ar- ranged scales, 4-6 mm long (excluding de-nuded lower portion of rachis after mature scales and achenes have shed), 3-4 mm wide, subtended by a single scale-like involucral bract at base, frequently persistent on denuded rachis after mature scales and achenes have shed, the rachis elongating to 10 mm; scales ovate to broadly ovate, 2- 2.5(2.8) X 1.5-2 mm, glabrous, shiny, with 3-nerved, green costa, the midnerve not prolonged beyond the apex, the sides from base to near apex dark reddish brown to brown-black, lustrous, finely transversely rugulose, brown near apex, the margins ciliate-lacerate. Flowers with 3 stamens; filaments flat, the anthers 1 mm long, basifixed, apiculate, the thecae parallel, longitudinally dehiscent; style flattened-clavate above base, glabrous, or sometimes short- fimbriate at apex, the stigmas 3, about as long as unbranched portion of style, mi- nutely scaly to short-fimbriate. Achene (Fig. ID) trigonous, obovate, 0.9-1 mm X 0.7-0.9 mm, abruptly rounded to a truncate apex, stramineous to dark grayish brown at maturity, with minutely papillate surface (each isodiametric cell containing a single nodule), the style base persistent as a small, disk-shaped cap.
bibliographicCitation: Strong, Mark T. 1996. A new unispiculate species of Bulbostylis (Cyperaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 48: 96-99.

description: Annual, stems tufted, 0.7-2.0 (2.5) dm tall, the roots fibrous. Leaves ferrugineous, 1/3 as long as to equaling or exceeding the mature culms; blades 0.3 (0.5) mm wide, linear-filiform, somewhat involute, primarily 3-veined, the two marginal veins and adaxial surface upwardly scabrous to sparsely scabrous, the abaxial surface glabrous, minutely papillate on veins; sheaths upwardly scabrous along the veins on abaxial side, the summit acute to somewhat truncate, abruptly narrowed into the blade, apical fimbriae absent. Culms capillary, ca. 0.3-0.5 mm wide, 6-8 ridged, shallowly grooved, glabrous. Inflorescence an open umbellate cyme bearing 2-7 spikelets borne on erect, slender rays up to 2.5 cm long (except for the sessile central spikelet); in- volucral bracts 2-3, leaflike, subtending prophyllate rays, shorter than to twice as long as the inflorescence, the central spikelet sessile, 3.5-4 mm long, its lower bracts also subtending primary rays. Spikelets ovoid, acute, 3-4(-5) mm long, 1.2-1.5 (2.0) mm wide. Fertile bracts reddish-brown, short- hispidulous, ovate, curvate-keeled, 1.5-1.6 (2.0) mm long, 1-1.2 (1.5) mm wide, apex acute, the midrib included to short-mucronate at apex. Flowers with 3 stamens, filaments flat, anthers 0.6-0.7 mm long, lance-acuminate, basifixed, cordate at base, apiculate, thecae parallel, longitudinally dehiscent. Style 3-branched. Achene trigon- ous, obovate, shallowly 3-lobed at apex, 1 mm long, 0.6-0.7 mm wide, light brown, with lighter angles, the surface relatively smooth (at later stages of maturity, the outer walls of the epidermal cells loosen, becom- ing translucent and shiny, with a dark gray- ish-brown, papillate surface); tubercle depressed-globose.
bibliographicCitation: Strong, Mark T. 1993. Two overlooked species of Bulbostylis (Cyperaceae) from South America. Brittonia. 45: 162-169.

description: Planta ad 1.4 m alta. Lamina foliorum ovata vel ovato-elliptica ad 41 x 27 cm, obtusa cum acumine, basi rotundata, supra atroviridis maculis geminatis pallidis subrectangularibus notata, glabra, subtus ut supra notata sed glaucescenti-viridis et purpureo-notata, minute tomentosa; petiolus tomentosus; vagina obscure rubra vel purpurea, villosa. Spica turbinata ad 8 cm longa; bracteae spiraliter dispositae, olivaceae vel rubro-suffusae, fertiles 18-30, inferiores transverse ovato-ellipticae, superiores suborbiculares, villosae, apice emarginatis, steriles 5-13, summae ovatae, villosae; bracteolae 0 vel raro membranaceae; corollae tubus ad 1.7 cm longus, eburneus, lobis ad 0.9 cm longis; staminodium exterius obovato-ellipticum ad 1.1 cm longum, purpureum; staminodium callosum ad 1.1 cm longum, bilobatum purpureum.

description: Rhizomatous, perennial herb, 0.6-1.4 m high, bearing 1-3 (4) basal leaves. Cataphylls herbaceous along the margin, narrowly ovate, 16-41 cm long, apex obtuse, apiculate, dark red-purple, appressed-villose. Leaf-blade herbaceous, ovate to ovate-elliptic, (22) 27-41 x (13.5) 16-27 cm, apex obtuse with acumen, base rounded; upper surface shiny dark green with whitish to yellowish green subrectangular markings between the raised major veins, a narrow scalloped band near the margin and occasionally also a pale yellowish-green feathered band along the midrib, glabrous, midrib olive-green, tomentose; lower surface patterned as above in dark red-purple and light gray-green, minutely tomentose (14 x), midrib light olive-green, apical half red-purple, minutely tomentose. Pulvinus subrotund in cross-section, articulate with petiole, 2.3-5.8 (7.4) cm long, light olive-green, sparsely appressed-tomentose, hairs brown. Petiole 29-72 cm in subtending leaf, 3.5-73 cm long in others, dark red-purple, appressed-tomentose. Leaf-sheath not auriculate, 10-33 cm long, dark red-purple, villose, basal 2-3 cm swollen, pinkish. Inflorescence terminal, 1 per shoot, turbinate with apical coma of sterile bracts, 5.6-8 cm total height, 3.5-7 cm total width, region of fertile bracts, 4-5.5 x 3-4 cm; peduncle 9-25 cm long, red-purple, sparsely villose. Bracts imbricate, spirally arranged; the fertile (flower-subtending) ones 18-30, lowermost transverse ovate-elliptic, subsequent and upper ones suborbicular, 1.8-2.3 x 2.4-3.1 cm, sterile ones 5-13, ovate, 3.1-3.7 x 1.6-1.9 cm (the lowermost sterile bracts suborbicular, similar to uppermost fertile bracts), apex acute to 900, blunted; abaxial surface of fertile bracts deep olive-green, tinged red-purple, villose, adaxially shiny, glabrous; adaxial surface of sterile bracts semi-shiny green centrally, lighter at the margins, villose, abaxially light green, villose. Bicarinate prophyll ovate, obtuse, 17-20 x 7-8 mm carina to carina, total width 11-12.5 mm, olive-green apically, white or tinged red below, villose on margins. Secondary bract broadly ovate, 15- 19 x (9.5) 11-12.5 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, translucent olive-green or tinged red, villose. Bracteoles absent (rarely present, membranaceous). Sepals membranaeous, narrowly elliptic, acute, 11-14 x 2.5-3 mm, white basally, upper half pale green, glabrous. Corolla tube 16-19.5 mm, cream-colored, glabrous; lobes ovate-elliptic, acute, 7-9 x 3.5-4 mm, pale yellow. Outer staminode obovate-elliptic, one side considerably narrower than the other, 9-1 1 x 5-7 mm, apex shallowly emarginate, purple. Callose staminode petaloid apically, 9-11 x 6.5-8 mm, bilobate, petaloid portion purple, callose portion white. Cucullate staminode 4.5-5.5 x 3-4 mm, white, apex purple. Anther ca 2 mm long. Style and stigma white. Ovary 2 mm high, smooth, glabrous, pink.

description:
Acaulescent herb, 0.3-1.1 m high, bearing 1-2(3) basal leaves. Roots bearing tuber like swellings terminally. Cataphylls narrowly ovate, innermost one 9-36 cm long, apex obtuse, apiculate, purple, puberulous. Leaf blade elliptic, occasionally obovate, unequal, (I14)21-42 x 6-17 cm, apex obtuse with acumen, occasionally acuminate, base cuneate to obtuse or rounded and shortly attenuate. Leaf blade adaxially dark green with feathered light green to yellowish green band along midrib, glabrous, occasionally sparsely puberulous at base, midrib puberulous; blade abaxially deep purple or green tinged purple, puberulous along veins, puberulous throughout, or glabrous except the very margin of the wider side and the apex puberulous, midrib densely puberulous. Pulvinus (0.5) 1-4 cm long, maroon or tinged with purple, strigulose along upper side, the rest glabrous, occasionally strigulose throughout. Petiole 0-35 cm long, purple or green tinged purple, rather densely sericeous along upper side, the rest very sparsely puberulous or glabrous. Leaf sheath not auriculate, 5.5-14.5 cm long, sericeous, hairs longer near margin and more dense toward the base.

Inflorescence terminal on leafy shoot or borne on a separate shoot, 1 per shoot, ellipsoid to cylindric, 3-5 x 1.5-3 cm. Pe- duncle 8-35 cm long, red-purple, or green tinged purple, rather densely puberulous occasionally sparsely puberulous apically. Bracts 9-21, spirally arranged, imbricate, depressed ovate to broadly elliptic or broadly transverse elliptic, 1-2 x 1.5-3 cm, apex obtuse with an acumen, occasionally acuminate in lower ones, upper margin and apex patent; each bract subtending 2-3 flower pairs, outer surface pink, green, or light green tinged purple, rather densely sericeous throughout or with the central and basal portion sparsely puberulous or glabrous, inner surface puberulous apically. Bicarinate prophyll membranaceous, obovate, 1-1. 5 x 1-1.5 cm, ca. 0.5 cm wide between carina margins, apex obtuse, pale greenish, puberulous apically on sides only or on sides and central portion between the carinae. Sec- ondary bract membranaceous, broadly elliptic, 1-1.5 x 0.5-1 cm, apex rounded or very shallowly retuse, subglabrous or sparsely puberulous at apex. Braceteoles absent. Sepals narrowly elliptic, 12-15.5 x 2- 3 mm, apex acute, light green, glabrous. Co- rolla tube 12-13 mm long, white, glabrous; corolla lobes subequal, elliptic, ca. 8 mm long, apex acute, white to pale pink, glabrous. Outer staminode unguiculate, obovate, ca. 9 x 4 mm, apex slightly retuse. Callose staminode obovate-spathulate, ca. 7 x 4 mm, white throughout or with pur- plish stripes (fide de Granville 6369). Cucullate staminode ca. 4 x 3 mm. Anther ca. 1 mm long. Style white or purple (fide de Granville 6369). Ovary ca. 2 x 1 mm, glabrous. Capsule obovoid, ca. 7 x 6 mm; crowned by a persistent calyx. Seeds 3 per capsule, ca. 6 x 4 mm, bearing a white aril.
bibliographicCitation: Kennedy, H. 1995. Calathea maasiorum (Marantaceae), a new species from French Guiana and Surinam. Brittonia. 47: 156-159.

description: Planta ad 1.1 m alta. Folia valde plicata anguste elliptica vel anguste ovato-elliptica usque ad 40 x 9 cm, acuminata, basi cuneata, supra viridia glabra, secus costa tomentosa, ad apicem villosa, subtus viridi-grisea glabra purpureo-tincta ad apicem tomentosa; pulvinus subrotundus usque ad 1.8 cm longus, supra villosus; petiolus 0-9.3 cm longus, viridis, tomentosus ad apicem subvillosus; vagina viridis ad marginem et basin rubro-tincta, tomentosa, ad basin sericea. Spica ellipsoidea 2.9-4.7 cm longa, pedunculo minute tomentoso ad 37 cm longo elevata; bracteae 7-14, spiraliter dispositae, imbricatae, subcoriaceae, longitrorsus minute sulcatae, transverse ellipticae, obtusae vel rotundatae, rubrae, glabrae; paria florum ad 11 usque, unoquoque pari bracteolis 3 suffulto, 2 membranacis, 1 indurata claviculata ad 1.3 cm longa; flores omnino flavi; ovarium glabrum; sepala subcoriacea obovata ad 10 mm longa, obtusa vel rotundata, glabra; tubus corollae ad 9.5 mm longus, lobis late ovatis ad 6 mm longis; staminodia exterius deficiens, callosum obovatum ad 5 mm longum, cucullatum ad 4 mm longum. Capsula ignota.

description: Rhizomatous, perennial herb, 0.7-1.1 m high, bearing 1-2 (3) basal leaves and one cauline leaf. Cataphylls herbaceous, narrowly ovate, innermost one 12-30 cm long, abaxially purple or green tinged purple, tomentose. Leaf blade strongly plicate, narrowly elliptic to narrowly ovate-elliptic, 23-40 x 5-9 cm, apex acuminate, base cuneate occasionally obtuse; leaf upper surface sparkling dark green, glabrous, midrib tomentose becoming villous apically; lower surface grey-green often tinged purple, tomentose along margin and at apex, the rest glabrous, midrib yellow-green. Pulvinus subrotund, 0.7-1.8 cm long, yellow-green to brownish-green, villose along upper side, sparsely villose basally and occasionally along lower surface, articulate with petiole. Petiole 0-9.3 cm long, usually absent in cauline leaves, green, occasionally bearing a groove, tomentose basally to subvillous distally. Leaf sheath of subtending leaves 10-14.5 cm long, of basal leaves 10-38 cm long, deep green, margins tinged red-purple, minutely tomentose, base tinged purple, sericeous. Stem internode below subtending leaf 26-40 cm long, green, velvety-tomentose. Inflorescences 1 (occasionally 2) per main or lateral shoot, ellipsoid, 2.9-4.7 cm high, 1.3-1.8 cm in diam; peduncle 15.5-37 cm long, green to yellow-green, minutely pilose, subglabrous towards apex. Bracts 7-14, spirally arranged, semi-coriaceous, transversely elliptic to reniform, 1.1-1.3 x 1.8-2.2 cm, apex obtuse to rounded, in upper bracts occasionally retuse. Outer bract surface finely furrowed, red to red-orange, at base yellow, glabrous, each bract subtending up to 11 flower pairs. Bicarinate prophyll membranaceous, broadly ovate, 9.5-12 x 4-5 mm carina to carina, total width 9-10.5 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, reddish, glabrous. Secondary bract membranaceous, roundish to broadly elliptic, 9-11 x 9-10 mm, apex rounded, tinged reddish, glabrous. Bracteoles 3 per flower pair: 2 lateral, membranaceous, channeled, 9-10 x 3-5 mm; 1 median, claviculate, 1.2-1.3 cm long, yellow. Flower parts yellow throughout. Sepals firm, somewhat stiffish, obovate, cupped apically, 9-10 x 3-5 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, glabrous. Corolla tube 8-9.5 mm long, nectar holding area ca 4 mm long, glabrous; lobes broadly ovate, 4-6 x 3-4 mm, glabrous. Outer staminode absent. Callose staminode obovate, 4-5 x ca 5 mm, apical margin petaloid, rounded, occasionally retuse. Cucullate staminode 3-4 mm long with vestigial subterminal appendage less than 0.5 mm long. Stamen with lateral petaloid appendage to 1 mm wide extending to basal 1/3 of anther; anther 1.5-2 mm long. Style and stigma yellow. Ovary smooth, round in crosssection, 2-2.3 mm high, glabrous. Capsule and seeds unknown.

description: Planta 0.8-1.3 m alta. Folia 2-6, basalia; lamina ovata vel elliptica 56 x 33 cm usque, acuminata vel obtusa cum acumine, supra viridis secus costa atroviridis, glabra, subtus griseo-viridis, glabra; pulvinus 7-10 cm longus, glaber; petiolus glaber; vagina 40 cm usque longa, viridis ad basin purpureo- tincta. Capsula trilobata atro-coccinea vel purpurea; semina indigotica.

description: Rosulate herb, 0.8-1.3 m high, bearing 2-6 basal leaves and I or 2 bladeless sheaths. Roots stiff, wirey. Cataphylls herbaceous, narrowly ovate, innermost one 20-30 cm long, apex apiculate, purple, or dark green tinged with purple, tomentose toward base. Leaf blade semi-coriaceous, ovate to elliptic, 50-56 x 29-33 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate to obtuse with acumen, veins 18-22 per 5 cm, cross veinlets 23-26 per 5 mm. Leaf blade above green, often with darker green along the midrib especially prominent in juvenile foliage, glabrous, midrib deep green, often tinged red-purple in basal 1/4, glabrous; leaf surface below semi-shiny gray-green, glabrous, midrib yellow-green, glabrous. Pulvinus elliptic in cross- section, 7-10 cm long, olive-green, glabrous. Petiole 30-70 cm long, green, gla- brous to subglabrous. Leaf sheath not auriculate, 30-40 cm long, green, tinged dark purple toward base, yellow-green along margins, tomentose, more densely so toward the base. Inflorescence terminal, 1 per shoot, borne below the leaves, imbricate initially becoming lax in fruit, ovoid to fusiform, 16-21 x 4-8 cm; peduncle elongated in age, 5-38 cm long, dark purple, tomentose. Bracts ca 45- 65, spirally arranged, herbaceous, dying back apically while still flowering, elliptic to obovate-elliptic in upper ones, 4-6 (7) x (1) 1.5-3.3 (3.7) cm, apex emarginate in lower bracts, shallowly retuse in upper ones, each subtending up to 4 flower pairs. Outer surface of bract dark purple or green (fide Andersson 1197), minutely appressed-tomentose throughout or only at margins; inner surface shiny, green, occasionally purple marginally, glabrous. Bicarinate prophyll thickened basally and along carina, ovate, ca 2.5-3 x 1-1.5 cm, 0.5-1 cm carina to carina, apex obtuse, translucent pale tan, tinged purple medially in age, minutely tomentose abaxially, hairs borne on papillae. Secondary bracts membranous, ovate, 2.3-2.8 x 1.2-1.4 cm, apex retuse to obtuse, translucent cream-white, occasionally with tinge of purple apically, glabrous. Bracteoles lacking. Common pedicel 0.9-1.2 cm long, those of the first flower pairs longest, cream-white, base glabrous, upper half tomentose; pedicels 0.2-0.4 cm, the upper portion dotted purple, tomentose. Sepals herbaceous, the base somewhat thickened, elliptic to ovate-elliptic, ca 23-25 x 6-9 mm, apex obtuse, white or faintly tinged pink, minutely tomentose. Corolla ca 48-55 mm long, tube white, glabrous, ca 22-28 mm long, ca 3.5 mm in diam, staminal tube ca 4 mm long; lobes subequal, elliptic, 21-28 x 7-11 mm, apex obtuse to rounded with minute acumen, light yellow, tinged purple apically and along margin, glabrous. Outer staminode present or absent, when present obovoid. Callose staminode with acuminate tip petaloid, ca 8-9 x 6 mm, apex unequal, bilobed, 1 short and rounded, the other acuminate-attenuate, pale yellow basally, apical 1/3 dark purple. Cucullate staminode ca 8-9 x 6 mm, white. Stamen with lateral white petaloid appendage to 2 mm wide, extending to lower 1/3 of anther; anther 3-4 mm long, cream. Style white below, tip tinged purple. Ovary 3-3.5 x 3-3.5 mm, purple, densely appressed-tomentose. Capsule fleshy, surface minutely irregular, 3-lobed, obovoid, ca 15 x 12 mm, apex truncate, dark red to red-purple, sparsely tomentose, borne on an elongated pedicel to 10 mm long; calyx dies and rots off. Seeds usually 3 per capsule, ovoid, ca 8 x 6.5 x 6 mm, deep blue with a basal white aril.

description: Phyllopodic, caespitose; leaves basal, stiff, erect, coarse, 2-5 mm wide, apices abruptly attenuate; culms stiff, erect, to 3 dm high, generally longer than the leaves at maturity, roughened above; spikes two to four, the terminal gynaecandrous, lateral carpellate, oblong, sessile to short pedunculate, erect, closely approximate, the lowermost spike sometimes separate, spikes subtended by a short sheathing, leaf-like bract, shorter than to as long as the inflorescence; perigynia orbicular, 3 mm long, reddish brown, abruptly beaked, beaks emarginate to shallowly bidentate, perigynia papillose; carpellate scales broadly lanceolate to, ovate, as wide and as long as the perigynia, margins usually hyaline, apices obtuse to acute, midribs inconspicuous to raised and ending in a short mucro.
bibliographicCitation: Ornduff, Robert. 1969. Limnanthes vinoulans, a new California endemic. Brittonia. 21: 11-14.

description: Terrestrial, perennial, erect herbs, 25-30 cm tall. Corms erect, produced horizontally, globose, 1.5-2 cm diam., 1-2 basal scarious sheathing bracts, covering the corms. Leaves (2)3-5, linear, present at anthesis, 40-60 cm long, 1-3 cm wide. Inflorescence scapose, 80-120 cm long, the base of the peduncle with purple spots; floral bracts ob- long, clasped, acuminate. Flowers semi- erect, the perianth purple, salmon-purple in anthesis; pedicellate ovary 2-2.5 cm long, purple; dorsal sepal 3-3.8 cm long, 5-10 mm wide, oblanceolate, straight, with the apex recurved, acuminate; lateral sepals shorter, 2.8-3.2 cm long, 8-10 mm wide, ovate-oblanceolate, spreading, curved downward; petals 2.8-3.3 cm long, 5-14 mm wide, obovate, the apex obtuse and rev- olute, forming a hood over column, curved downward, enclosing completely the col- umn and the lateral lobes of the lip; lip trilobed, obovate in outline, whitish in the base, rose-purple in the apex of the lobes, the lateral lobes semi-enclosing the column, 2-3 cm long, 1-1.5 cm wide, the lateral lobes strongly turned up, 1.5-1.9 cm long, with narrow sinuses, the midlobe 1-1.3 cm long, 9-14 mm wide, quadrangular, its margin erose or undulate, declined with the apex curved downward; callus of lip with 3-5 parallel white crests from the base to the midpoint of the midlobe. Column arched, with 2 small wings near the base, whitish, with rose-purple spots, 2-2.4 cm long. Capsule oblong, curved, greenish, with purple spots.

description: Phyllopodic, caespitose; leaves basal, erect, 2-5 mm wide, apices long attenuate; culms erect, 2-5 dm high, longer than the leaves, ro,ughened above; spikes three to six, the terminal gynaecandrous, lateral carpellate, oblong-cylindric, sessile to, short pedunculate, approximate, erect, the lowermost spike sometimes, separate, spikes subtended by a short sheathing, leaf-like bract, shorter to longer than the in- florescence; perigynia elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 3 mm long, pale green becoming golden brown at maturity, abruptly beaked, beaks entire to shallowly bidentate, perigynia papillose above; carpellate scales broadly lanceolate, as broad as the perigynia at the base, shorter than the perigynia, apices obtuse to acute, midribs usually inconspicuous.
bibliographicCitation: Ornduff, Robert. 1969. Limnanthes vinoulans, a new California endemic. Brittonia. 21: 11-14.

description: Plantac dense caespitosae; culmi 5-30 mm alti; vaginae basales brunneae. Folia 3-6; laminae 5-50 mm longae, 0.3-0.5 mm latae, infra involutae super planae, apice acutae, marginibus scabrellae; vaginae glabrae, zona interiori pallide brunnea vel hyalina; ligulae breves, longiores quam latiores. Spica unica terminalis androgyna, 3-5.5 mm alta; bractea unica usque ad 40 mm longo. Pars mascula inconspicua abscondita 2- or 3-flora. Pars femina 4-6-flora; squamae pistillatae ovatae vel lanceolatae, 2.2-3.4 longae (excipio aristam), 1.1-2.2 mm latae, cuspidatae vel aristatae. Perigynia 2.5-3.2 mm longa, 1-1.7 mm lata, obovoidea, glabra (excipio rostrum), in rostrum abrupte contracta, venis 12-16 percursa; rostra 0.4-0.6 mm longa, hispidula, apice bidentata, dentibus 0.1-0.3 mm longis. Achenia 1.7-2.2 mm longa, 0.8-1.5 mm lata, obovoidea. Rachilla 0.7-1.2 mm longa, subulata. Stigmata 3. Antherae 3, 1-1.3 mm longae.

description: Plants low-growing, densely cespitose, with short rhizomes; fertile culms 5-30 mm tall, erect or slightly curved, terete, smooth, with light brown to dark brown basal sheaths. Leaves 3-6, mostly much exceeding the culms; blades 5-50 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide, erect or slightly curved, green, involute proximally, becoming ±flattened distally, apex sharp-pointed, margins antrorsely scabrous (especially near the leaf-tips); leaf sheaths light brown to dark brown, with 5-8 veins prominent, lowest 3 or 4 sheaths aphyllous or with short, setaceous blades; inner band of sheaths pale brown or hyaline, glabrous; ligules very short, rounded, slightly longer than wide. Vegetative shoots 1.5-6 cm tall; leaves similar to those of fertile culms; pseudoculms 0.7-2.2 cm tall. Inflorescence a single, terminal, androgynous, capitate spike, 3-5.5 mm tall, 3.5-6 mm wide, subtended by a solitary sterile bract; bract setaceous, antrorsely scaberulent, up to 40 mm long, sheathless (or nearly so). Staminate part largely concealed, 2- or 3-flowered; scales 2.2-3.4 mm long, 1.3-1.7 mm wide, acute. Pistillate part 4-6-flowered; scales ovate to lanceolate, the body 2.2-3.4 mm long, 1.1-2.2 mm wide, glabrous, with broad hyaline margins proximally and greenish center, 3-veined, the 2 outermost fertile scales with antrorsely scaberulent awns 2-10 mm long, the inner scales cuspidate. Perigynia 2.5-3.2 mm long, 1-1.7 mm wide, obovoid, obscurely tri- gonous in cross section, greenish to stramineous, the body subglobose with broadly elliptical to suborbicular sides, 2 lateral veins prominent and additionally 6-8-veined dorsally and less conspicuously 4-6-veined ventrally, glabrous except for the lateral veins hispidulous distally, stipitate, tapering to a ±spongy base, abruptly contracted to a short beak; beaks 0.4-0.6 mm long, hispidulous, the apex bidentate, with teeth 0. 1-0.3 mm long. Achenes 1.7-2.2 mm long, 0.8-1.5 mm wide, obovoid, obscurely trigonous, pale brown to brown, short-stipitate. Rachilla (when present) 0.7-1.2 mm long, subulate, margins smooth or sparingly ciliate. Stigmas 3. Anthers 3, linear, 1-1.3 mm long.

description: Phyllopodic, caespitose; leaves basal, erect, 2-5 mm wide, apices attenuate; culms erect to drooping at maturity, 3.0-5.5 dm high, longer than the leaves, slightly roughened above; spikes three to four, all gynaecandrous, the terminal as much as three-quarters staminate, the lateral occasionally only carpellate, narrow, long cylindric, pedunculate, approximate to, separate, the lower one or two long pedunculate and pendent, peduncles slender, roughened, spikes subtended by a short sheathing, leaf-like bract, shorter to longer than the inflorescence; perigynia elliptic to obovate, 3 mm long, pale green to whitish, abruptly beaked, beaks shallowly to deeply bidentate; carpellate scales lanceolate, as broad as and shorter than to as long as the perigynia, often with narrow hyaline margins, apices acute, midribs conspicuous, sometimes raised near the tip and ending in a short mucro.

description: Corms oblong-subglobose, ca. 3 cm long, 1.5 cm in diam; shoot with 3-4 tubular sheathing bracts at base; leaves 1 or 2, 30-45 cm long, 7-12 mm wide; scape arising from young growth before corm is mature, 30-55 cm high, sometimes faintly verruculose above; bracts subulate, 6-12 mm long, 2-6 mm wide; ovary with pedicel 20-28 mm long, strongly verrucose; flowers 2-4, each with a pronounced mentum at base (ca. 2.5 mm long); lateral sepals arcuate, acute, ca. 33 mm long, 11 mm wide; dorsal sepal elliptic, acute, ca. 36 mm long, 10 mm wide; petals arcuate-oblong, broadly acute, ca. 38 mm long, 11 mm wide; lip ca. 35 mm long and 36 mm wide across lateral lobes, truncate at base, distinctly 3-lobed, but with obtuse sinuses, lateral lobes obtuse, ca. 27 mm long (from base), 13 mm wide, mid-lobe subquadrate, ca. 12 mm long, 18 mm wide, 12 mm wide at base, with a very small elongate callus on disk, column arcuate, ca. 22 mm long and 8 mm wide at the expanded apex.
bibliographicCitation: Dressler, Robert L. 1968. Notes on Bletia (Orchidaceae). Brittonia. 30: 182-190.

description: Terrestrial, perennial, erect herbs, 36-5 8 cm tall. Corms erect, small, subglobose, whitish, 1.5-3.5 cm long, 1-2.2 cm wide; sheathing bracts 3-5, close, usually straw colored, rarely purplish, the basal bracts 2- 3 cm long, the apical ones 5-6 cm long. Leaves 5-6, present at anthesis, narrow and linear, 29-40 cm long, 3-7 mm wide, the basal leaves narrower than the apical ones. Inflorescence racemose, with 2-4 flowers, 34-45 cm long; floral bracts clasping, 6-10 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, acuminate. Flowers ascending, the perianth purple or purplish-blue, 4-5 cm long including the pedicellate ovary; sepals purple with dark veins  dorsal sepal 2.2-2.5 cm long, 4-5 mm wide, the apex acuminate; lateral sepals slightly shorter than the dorsal sepal, 1.8-2 cm long, the apex acute; mentum 2-3 mm long; petals purplish, with dark veins, 2-2.2 cm long, 8-9 mm wide, the apex acuminate; lip purple or purplish-blue with the margin and callus of a lighter color, ovate, the base very narrow, 2-2.3 cm long, 1.5-1.7 cm wide when flattened; lateral lobes semi-circular, 1.5-1.9 cm long, forming short sinuses when flattened; midlobe 1/3 the total length of the lip, 2-3 mm long, 5 mm wide, emarginate at apex, almost divided into two lobes, the margin erose; callus of lip with 3-5 parallel crests. Column wingless, 1.3-1.5 cm long.

description: Caespitosa ex rhizomatibus ut videtur brevirepentibus; culmi usque ad 6 dm alti, cum phyllopodiis, folia valde excedentes obtuse triquetri, vaginis basalibus rubro- tinctis; folia caulina 2-3, cetera 2-5 basalia, laminis planis vel marginibus paulo recurvatis, 15-30 cm longis, 3-4 mm latis, linearibus attenuatis, valde coriaceis marginibus scabro-serrulatis, vaginis rubellis, glabris; spicae 5-7, androgynae, pe- dunculis cernuis longis filiformibus, inferiores remotae, superiores contiguae, lineari- cylindricae, 2.5-4.5 cm longae, 4-6 mm latae, superne densiflorae basi pauciflorae, perigyniis 20-50, adscendentibus; bractea infima frondosa, longivaginata, culmo brevior, ventraliter rubra; squamae elliptico-ovatae vel ovato-lanceolatae, adpressae, acuminatae, cuspidatae vel breviaristatae perigyniis latiores et eis pro maxima parte occultantes, plus minusve carinatae, membranaceae, rubrae costa straminea promi- nente; perigynia fusiformia, 3-4 mm longa, 1-1.5 mm lata, obtuse trigona, glabra, pallido-viridia vel vinosa praesertim versus basim, bicostata et valde quasi 10-nervata, in stipitem 0.5-0.75 mm longum abrupte contracta, superne in rostrum brevem crassum praemorsum contracta orificio minute serrulato; achaenia ovoidea, 2 mm longa, 1 mm lata, trigona, substipitata, medio haud constricta.

description: Phyllopodic, caespitose; leaves basal, erect, 2-5 mm wide, apices attenuate; culms erect to drooping at maturity, to 5 dm high, longer than the leaves, smooth; spikes three to five, the terminal gynaecandrous, lateral carpellate or rarely gynaecandrous, spikes oblong to oblong-ovoid, sessile to short pedunculate, the uppermost con- tiguous, the lowermost spike occasionally separate, spikes subtended by a short sheathing, scale-like bract, occasionally with a foliaceous bract arising 2-3 cm below the scale-like bract, foliaceous bract as long as the inflorescence; perigynia ovate, 4 mm long, purplish brown with green to pale yellow margins, abruptly beaked, beaks entire to shallowly bidentate, base of beaks and upper perigynium margins often papillose; carpellate scales lanceolate, narrower than and as long as to longer than the perigynia, copper to brownish black but often developing hyaline margins at maturity, apices acute to acuminate, midribs inconspicuous to slightly raised and conspicuous.
