description: Perennis; culmi 8-9 dm alti, phyllopodi acute triangulares foliis multo longiores; folia 11-14 ad basim culmi maxima ex parte distiche aggregata, vaginis brevibus, ligula latior quam longa, laminis planis, rigidis, 2-3.5 dm longis, 5-7.5 mm latis, supra scabriusculis; inflorescentia 15-20 cm longa spica una vel duabus valde disjunctis exceptis; spicae 7-9, androgynae, (apicis 1/8-1/2 parte staminali) linearicylindricae perigyniis 30-110, 5-8 cm longae, 4-7 mm latae, adscendentes vel pendentes, pedunculis capillaribus plerumque longis (0.5-7 cm) plus minusve scabridis; bracteae frondosae inflorescentiam subaequantes, lamina infima 25-30 cm longa, vaginis longis (usque ad 8 cm); squamae oblongo-lanceolatae apice obtusae (raro acuminatae) hyalinae, 3.5-6 mm longae perigyniis paulo breviores, puniceorubiginosae media porphyrea; perigynia fusiformia, triangularia, 4.5-6 mm longa, 1-1.25 mm lata, sensim in rostrum 1.25-2 mm longum apice hyalino leviter bidentulato contracta; achaenia tringularia anguste ellipitico-obovoidea, 2.75 mm longa, 1 mm lata, minute papillosa.

description: Perennial; culms 8-9 dm high, phyllopodic, acutely triangular, much exceeding the leaves; leaves 11-14 to a fertile culm, mostly distichously clustered at the base of the culms, the sheaths short, glabrous (1-3 cm long) and early ruptured, the ligule wider than long, the blades flat, stiff, dull green, 2-3.5 dm long, 5-7.5 mm wide, scabridulous on the upper surface; cauline leaves 2-3; inflorescence 15-20 cm long, except for one or two widely disjunct spikes in the lowermost bracts; spikes 7-9, androgynous (the apical 1/8 to 1/2 staminate), linear-cylindric, flexuous, ascending or drooping, 5-8 cm long, 4-7 mm wide, with 30-110 ascending-spreading perigynia, on unequal, long (0.5-7 cm), capillary, more or less scabrous peduncles; bracts leaf-like, about equaling the inflorescence (the lowermost with a blade 25-30 cm long), the sheaths prolonged (up to 8 cm); scales oblong-lanceolate, obtuse (rarely acuminate) at the hyaline apex, 3.5-6 mm long, little shorter than the perigynia, dull purplish red, the center reddish brown; perigynia fusiform, trigonous, rather sharp-edged, not inflated, 4.5-6 mm long, 1-1.25 mm wide, straight or slightly excurved, membranaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous, olive-green below shading to purplish red above, slenderly nerved, tapering at the base, gradually tapering into a smooth, hyaline-tipped, obliquely cut and weakly bidentulate beak, 1.25-2 mm long (one-half the length of the body or more); achenes trigonous, narrowly elliptic-obovoid, 2.75 mm long, 1 mm wide, pale brown, minutely papillose.

description: Corms subglobose; shoot with tubular, sheathing bracts at base; leaves 1 or 2, 24-35 cm long, 28-40 mm wide; scape 45-60 cm tall, with 10-18 flowers; bracts subulate, 6-10 mm long, 2-4 mm wide; ovary with pedicel ca. 23 mm long; sepals oblong-obovate, acute, ca. 15 mm long, 4.5-5 mm wide; petals cuneate-obovate, obtuse or broadly acute, ca. 16 mm long, 6 mm wide; lip deeply 3-lobed, ca. 14 mm long, 12 mm wide across lateral lobes, the base cuneate, lateral lobes oblong, obtuse, ca. 8 mm long, 4 mm wide, mid-lobe oblong, truncate, ca. 8 mm long, 4 mm wide, base ca. 3 mm wide, mid-lobe with 5 lamellae, 2 (outer) near base, and 3 extending to near apex; column slightly winged near base, arcuate above, ca. 10 mm long.

description: Rhizoma breve, crassum, lignosum; culmi 8-10 dm alti, cum phyllopodiis obtuse triquetri folia excedentes; folia 5-9 (2-4 caulina excepta) ad basim culmi aggregata, longe vaginantia, culmo breviora, coriacea, plana vel in sicco valde revoluta, 4-5.5 mm lata, apice longe attenuata scaberulaque, vaginis antice tenuiter membranaceis, ligula latiore quam longa; inflorescentia quasi paniculata, 5.5-10 cm longa, spica infima (saepe composita) valde disjuncta excepta; spicae 4-7, cylindricae, 0.6-5 cm longae, 6-8 mm latae, densiflorae, terminalis 8 (raro V ) laterales 9 (apice saepe 8 ), adscendentes, sessiles vel plus minusve pedunclatae; bracteae frondosae inflores- centiam longe excedentes, vaginis longis; squamae persistentes ovato-lanceolatae, acutae vel abrupte acuminatae, 3-3.5 mm longae, perigyniis paullo breviores, rubro- lineolatae, statu fructifero patentissimae, trinervia, nervo medio in aristam brevem ciliato-hispidulam excurrente; perigynia horizontaliter patentes, inaequaliter ovoidea, plano-convexa vel gibbosa, turgida, rubiginoso-brunnea vinoso-maculata, multinervia, 3.25-4 mm longa, 1.3-1.8 mm lata, in rostrum 1 mm longum bidentatum contracta; achaenia trigona, elliptico-obovoidea, 2-2.5 mm longa, 1.25-1.5 mm lata, punctata, badia.

description: Rhizomes cord-like, less than 2 mm in diameter, short and simple, vertical or, if forking, with ascending to horizontal branches; sterile shoots elongate, up- curved-ascending, their blades (2) 4-25 cm long; culms solitary (occasionally arising together with 1-3 sterile shoots), erect, 0.5-2 dm tall, relatively soft, obtusely angled and smooth, shorter than the leaves, phyllopodic, light brown at base, the dried leaves of the previous year persistent; leaves all crowded near the base or sometimes spread over the lower 5/6 of the culm, the blades light yellowish- to bluish-green (glaucous when fresh), firm but not thick or stiff, flat or canaliculate, 2-18 cm long, 1.3-2.7 (3.4 on sterile shoots) mm wide, the mid-vein prominent beneath, the sheaths whitish-hyaline and very thin ventrally, soon breaking but not becoming filamentose, the lower becoming tinged with light yellowish-brown marginally, concave at mouth, the ligule longer than wide; bracts leaf-like, somewhat exceeding the inflorescence, nonsheathing, only the uppermost much reduced and scale-like; staminate spikelet solitary, occasionally developing a few perigynia at apex and/or a minute staminate spikelet at base, short-peduncled, linear-oblong, 11-28 mm long, 2-3 mm thick, the scales ob- trullate, obtuse to rounded, dark brown to purplish-black with green midvein and hyaline subciliate apex; anthers 1.8-2.5 mm long; pistillate spikelets 3-6, the lower often compound, the upper sometimes androgynous, erect, narrowly ob- long to oblong-ellipsoid, 6-31 mm long, 3-4 mm thick, densely 45-120-flowered, all crowded or the lowest 1 or 2 somewhat distant and short-peduncled or rarely basal on a long capillary peduncle, the upper sessile or subsessile, tending to be progressively shorter and overlapping the base of the staminate spikelet; scales ovate-oblong, 1.8-2.5 mm long, 1-1.2 mm wide, obtuse to acute, narrower than and from somewhat shorter than to equalling the perigynia, brownish-purple with narrow (0.2-0.3 mm) green center not extending to apex and barely developed hyaline margins; perigynia generally broadly obovate-elliptic to broadly elliptic (but those toward apex or base of the spikelet varying from obovate-orbicular to obovate or elliptic), plano-convex, strongly compressed, slightly inflated at ma- turity, small, 2.1-2.9 mm long (including the 0.2 mm subentire beak), 1.2-2 mm wide, conspicuously stipitate (stipe 0.3-0.4 mm long), rounded-truncate at apex and very abruptly apiculate, lightly 4-6-nerved on both faces, the ventral nerves mostly shorter and fainter than the dorsal ones, straw-colored below, green above, membranaceous, puncticulate, the margins sparsely and remotely, if at all, serrulate-scabrous toward apex; achenes lenticular, 1.3-1.8 mm long, 1.1-1.5 mm wide, brown, broadly substipitate and abruptly short-apiculate, obscurely jointed with the slender, somewhat exserted style; stigmas 2, protruding 1.3-1.8 mm.

description: Valde stolonifera; culmis paucis in caespite, 6-8 dm. altis, laevis, aphyllopodis; foliis caulinis 2-3, septato-nodularibus, laminis 40-60 cm. longis, 4-5 mm. latis, ciilmo excedentibus; vaginis ad faciem ventralem membranaceis; ligulis incon- spicuis aut obsoletis; spicis masculinis plerumque 3, anguste cylindricis, 1.5-3 cm. longis; spicis femineis 2-5, remotis, sessilibus 6-15 mm. longis, ca. 5 mm. latis, oblongis vel subglobosis; bracteis infloreseentiam excedentibus, solum mas- culinis deminutis; squamis femineis minutis ovatis, acutis vel mucronulatis; perigyniis 3 mm. longis, 2 mm. latis, coneavo-convexis, bicostatis, enervatis; rostribus brevis; acheniis ca. 1.5 mm. longis, 1.3 mm. latis, lenticularibus.

description: Strongly stoloniferous, the rhizomes horizontally spreading, light brown, the scales thin, soon shredding, light gray-brown; culms few together, 6-8 dm. tall, smooth, exceeded by the upper leaves, aphyllopodic, leaves of previous season shredding, light gray-brown, mostly disintegrated; sterile shoots apparently aphyllopodic; 2-3 well developed leaves per fertile culm, septate-nodular, the blades flat, 40-60 cm. long, 4-5 mm. broad, scabrous on the margins toward the acuminate apex, the sheaths membranous ventrally soon rupturing, ligule incon- spicuous or obsolete; staminate spikes usually 3, the terminal the largest, nar- rowly cylindrical, 1.5-3 cm. long; pistillate spikes 2-5, remote, the upper usually staminate at apex, sessile, 6-15 mm. long, ca. 5 mm. thick, oblong to subglobose, densely flowered or somewhat narrowed at the base, perigynia spreading; lowest bract leaf-like, sheathless, glandular-auriculate at base, conspicuously exeeeding the infloreseence, the remaining bracts conspicuous, only the staminate reduced and inconspicuous; staminate scales oblong-oblanceolate, obtuse, brownish, with inconspicuous center, hyaline at the apex; pistillate scales minute, ovate, dark brown -with a broad green eenter, sharply aeute or mucronulate, usually Com- pletely concealed by the perigynia; perigynia coneavo-convex, broadly ovate to obovate, 3 mm. long, 2 mm. wide, not turgid, 2-ribbed, nerveless, membranous, pink-splotched, greenish on the margins and apex, rounded and substipitate at base, rounded and granular above, the beak very short, entire, narrowly brown- margined; achenes ca. 1.5 mm. long, 1.3 mm. broad, lenticular, orbicular-obovate, light brown, broadly short-stipitate, abruptly apiculate, jointed with the style; stigmas 2, long, light brown.

description: Plants low-growing, densely cespitose, with short rhizomes; roots filiform, rigid, blackish (at least when dry); fertile culms 1. 5-3 cm tall, erect or more often curved, terete, smooth, with light brown to dark brown basal sheaths. Leaves 3-6, mostly much exceeding the culms; blades (5) 10-50 mm long, 0.4-0.8 mm wide, often strongly curved, yellowish-green to green, striate, canaliculate proximally, soon cylindrical but becoming biconvex distally, margins ? scabrous proximally (especially near the sheath) and scaberulent or more often smooth distally, termi- nating in a biconvex, often yellowish-tinged, pungent tip; leaf sheaths light brown to dark brown, with 5-8 veins prominent, the lowest 3 or 4 sheaths aphyllous; inner band of sheaths hyaline, glabrous; ligules very short, slightly rounded or sometimes retuse, wider than long. Vegetative shoots 3-12 cm tall; leaves similar to those of fertile culms; pseudoculms 1.5-6 cm tall. Inflorescence a single, ter- minal, androgynous, capitate spike, 4-6 mm tall, 5-6 mm wide; sterile bracts absent. Staminate part largely concealed, 2- or 3-flowered; scales 2.5-4 mm long, 1.5-1.9 mm wide, cuspidate. Pistillate part (4) 5-7-flowered; outermost pistillate scale bract-like, body 2.5-4.4 mm long, 1.8-2.5 mm wide, lanceolate, glabrous, with broad hyaline margins proximally and greenish center, prominently 5-veined, the awn 3.8-18.5 mm long and 0.4-0.6 mm wide, with margins smooth or sca- berulent and terminating in a pungent tip, the inner scales 3.5-5.2 mm long, 1.6- 2.1 mm wide, glabrous, with hyaline margins proximally and greenish center, 3- 5-veined, broadly ovate, cuspidate. Perigynia 2.6-3.8 mm long, 1.4-1.9 mm wide, obscurely trigonous, greenish to stramineous, the body subglobose, distal 1/3 to 2/3 of body finely pubescent, 2 veins prominent and hispidulous, the other veins obscure except in the proximal 1/3 of body which is sometimes 4-7-veined dorsally, short-stipitate, abruptly contracted to a short beak; beaks less than 0.8 mm long, hispidulous, the apex bidentate, with teeth up to 0.2 mm long. Achenes 1.6-2.4 mm long, 1.3-1.7 mm wide, obovoid, obscurely trigonous, pale brown, short-stipitate. Rachilla 0.7-1.4 mm long, lanceolate-elliptical, margins sparingly ciliate. Stigmas 3. Anthers 3, linear, 1-1.2 mm long.

description: Loosely caespitose in small clumps; fer- tile culms (35)45-95(1 10) cm tall, erect, tri- gonous, their lower nodes sometimes ex- posed above leaf sheath, smooth except for occasional finely scabrous angles below in- florescence; bladeless basal sheaths pale brown. Inflores- cences 2.3-8.4 cm long, typically nodding or arched above the lowest spike, spikes ap- proximate or more often separated, the low- est spikes 2.3-16 mm apart, spikes single at nodes, sessile, lowermost bracts incon- spicuous, setaceous and shorter than or mostly about as long as spike, 0.6-3 cm long and up to ca. 1.9 mm wide, sheathless, the upper bracts much reduced; spikes (3)5-8(9), gynaecandrous, often strongly clavate at base, otherwise conic to globose, 8-19 mm long, pistillate portion 5.5-9.6 mm long, 4.2-8.2 mm wide, 18-45-flow- ered, staminate portion 2-11 mm long, 10- 32-flowered. Perigynia 3-4.7 mm long, 1.9-2.8 mm wide, 1.3-2X as long as wide, appressed, bicon- vex with obovate to broadly elliptic bodies 2.3-3.4 mm long, and 1.8-3 x as long as beak, widest 1.4-2.2 mm above base, broadly winged and serrulate-margined except near base, abruptly contracted into a narrowly triangular beak, wing and beak greenish, body pale yellow or golden brown, glabrous, sessile, adaxial side distinctly 4-6(7)-nerved over achene, abaxial side distinctly 4-6-nerved over achene; beaks 0.9-1.7 mm long, flattened and serrulate-margined to apex, the apex obscurely bidentate with teeth up to 0.3 mm long. description: Planta cespitosa, caulibus numerosis sterilibus, rhizomatibus longe repentibus rhizomis ad 6 cm; culmi ad 3.5 dm alti, 0.3-0.7 mm lati, minute alati et antrorse scabri in angulis, aphyllopodici; matura folia 4-7 per culmum, 2 supera semper inflorescentiam excedentia; folia ad 2.5 dm longa, ad 1.7 (-2.0) mm lata, marginibus glabris, plana basin versus, plicata ad apicem; vagina arcta alba, 7-9 viridibus nervis praedita; ligula vix convexa erosa; spicae 4-5 androgynae, superae 2 approximatae, tertia 3-5 mm infra secundum, quarta 10-13 mm infra tertiam, quinta 12-17 mm infra quartum, inflorescentia omnino ad 3.8 cm longa; bracteae setiformes, infima ad 5 cm longa, interdum inflorescentiam excedens, superae reductae; glumae acutae vel acuminatae hyalinae, nervis centralibus viridibus, 1.5-2.0 mm longae, 1.0- 1.5 mm latae; masculini flores pauci inconspicui; perigynia 4-9 per spicam, 3.6-4.0 mm longa, 0.7-0.8 mm lata, glumas excedentia, ascendentia vel leviter radiantia, planoconvexa, pallida viride, enervia, serrulata in dimidio superiore, basi spongiosa.

description: Plantae perparvae, caespitosae; culmi 0.5-2.5 cm alti; vaginae basales glabrae, brunneo-purpureae. Folia 3-5, leviter curvata, plerumque basalia; laminae 5-25 mm longae, 0.4-0.7 mm latae; vaginae glabrae, zona interiori pallide brunnea vel hyalina; ligulae breves, leviter latiores quam longiores. Spica unica terminalis androgyna, 2.5-5.5 mm longa. Pars mascula inconspicua abscondita 1-2-flora. Pars femina 3-5-flora; squamae pistillatae late ovatae vel lanceolatae, acuminatae. Perigynia 2.5-3 mm longa, 0.8-1.2 mm lata, lanceolata, glabra, venis 2 inconspicuis percursae; rostra 0.7-1.2 mm longa, laevia vel sparsissime scabrella. Achenia 1.3-1.7 mm longa, 0.7-1.1 mm lata. Stigmata 3. Antherae 3, 1.2-1.5 mm longae.

description: Plants very small, cespitose, with short rhizomes; fertile culms 0.5-2.5 cm tall, very slender, erect, mostly exceeded by the leaves, obscurely trigonous, smooth, with glabrous, reddish-brown basal sheaths. Leaves 3-5, erect or more often slightly curved, mostly basal; blades 5-25 mm long, 0.4-0.7 mm wide, involute proximally, ±flattened distally, apex obtuse, margins smooth (or nearly so) proxi- mally, scaberulent distally; leaf sheaths less than 10 mm long, glabrous, yellowish- brown to reddish-brown; inner band of sheaths pale brown or hyaline, glabrous, the apex concave; ligules short, rounded, slightly wider than long. Vegetative shoots 1-3.5 cm tall; leaves 4-7, similar to those of fertile culms; pseudoculms 0.5-1.5 cm tall. Inflorescence a single, terminal, androgynous spike, 2.5-5.5 mm long; sterile bracts absent. Staminate part 1-2-flowered, inconspicuous at maturity; scales 1.9-2.6 mm long, 0.7-1.6 mm wide, acute. Pistillate part 3-5-flowered; scales glabrous, reddish-brown, with stramineous center, 3-veined, the 2 outer- most ones bract-like, the body 2.4-3.6 mm long, 1-1.8 mm wide, broadly ovate to lanceolate, with a smooth awn 1.6-3.8 mm long and 0.2-0.5 mm wide, the inner ones 2.3-3.6 mm long, 0.8-1.6 mm wide, ovate, acuminate. Perigynia 2.5- 3 mm long, 0.8-1.2 mm wide, mostly ascending, obscurely trigonous, lanceolate, glabrous, 2 veins faint and the rest obscure, short-stipitate, yellowish-green when immature, pale brown to reddish-brown at maturity; perigynium beak 0.7-1.2 mm long, smooth or scaberulent, the apex obliquely cut dorsally. Achenes 1.3- 1.7 mm long, 0.7-1.1 mm wide, obscurely trigonous, oblong-elliptical to oval, sessile, pale brown when immature, dark brown at maturity. Rachilla seemingly absent. Stigmas 3. Anthers 3, linear, 1.2-1.5 mm long.

description: Plantae caespitosae; rhizomatibus brevibus; culmis erectis, 4-5 dmi. altis, glabris, gracilibus; foliis 5-7, laminis 10-20 cm. longis, 2-3 mnm. latis; vaginis ad superficiem ventralem hyalinis, truneatis; spicis numerosis, androgynis, capitatis dense, ovoideo-orbiculatis, ca. 1 mm. latis; squamis ovato-lanceolatis, obtusis vel acutis, anguste hyalino-marginatis, quam perigyniis brevioribus; perigyniis plano-convexis, lanceolatis, 4 mm. longis, 1.5 mm. latis, ad faciem dorsalem subtile nervatis, ad ventralem valde nervatis; acheniis 1.5 mm. longis, 0.8 mm. latis, oblongo-ovatis.

description: Loosely caespitose from rather coarse, short-creeping, dark, scaly rootstocks; the culms erect, 4-5 dm. tall, smooth, slender; basal sheaths brown; leaves 5-7, confined to the lower third of the fertile culm, the lower with reduced blades, the upper with blades 10-20 cm. long and 2-3 mm. wide, the sheaths tight, hyaline on the ventral side, truncate, hardly prolonged as a ligtule; sterile shoots few; spikes numerous, indistinguishable, androgynous, densely aggregated into an ovoid-orbicular head about 1 cm. thick; staminate flowers inconspicuous, the perigynia several, somewhat spreading; bracts absent; scales ovate-lanceolate, obtusish to acute, light brown with light inconspicuous center, narrowly hyalinemargined, shorter than the perigynia; perigynia plano-convex, lanceolate, 4 mm. long, 1.5 mm. broad, brown-tinged, green- or light-margined, hardly conistrieted into a beak, finely several-veined vent-rally, prominently nerved dorsally, not inflated, sharp-edged, inconspicuously and minutely serrulate upwards, stipitate, rounded at the base,, not contracted into a well defined beak, bidentate, the teeth coinnivent and sometimes twisted, the orifice slightly hyaline; achenes lenticular, oblong-ovate, 1.5 mm. long, 0.8 mm. wide; stigmas 2, slender, light reddish-brown.
bibliographicCitation: Maguire, Bassett. 1944. Great Basin plants--VIII. New Species in Carex and Erigeron. Brittonia. 5: 199-202.

description: Caespitosa sed rhizomatibus validis brevirepentibus praedita; culmi 12-70 cm alti, stricti, obtuse triquetri, basi 2-3.5 mm crassi, striati, folia excedentes, sine phyllo- podiis; folia caulina 3-6 culmi basim versus aggregata laminis planis 8-20 cm longis, 2-4 mm latis apicem acuminatum versus scabridis, vaginis arctis ventraliter albido- hyalinis ligula latiore quam longa; spicae 4-12 gynaecandrae oblongo-ovoideae 6-9 mm longae, 3-6 mm latae, sessiles, perigyniis appressis multis apicibus haud patentibus in capitulum terminalem 1-2 cm longum, 7-15 mm latum confertae; bracteae capitulo breviores; squamae ovato-lanceolatae breviacuminatae brunneae marginibus plus minusve hyalinis perigynia haud occultantes; perigynia tenui-plano-convexa anguste lanceolata 3-4.75 mm longa, 1.1-1.5 mm lata, chartacea, brunnea vel fuligineo- brunnea, utrinque 3-7-striata, peranguste alata, ad basim sessilem spongiosam con- tracta, in rostrum serrulatum angustum 1-1.5 mm longum apice fuscum teres atten- uata; achaenia lenticularia oblongo-ovoidea 1.5 mm longa, 1 mm lata, sessilia; antherae brevipersistentes, apiculatae, 1.3-1.75 mm longae.
bibliographicCitation: Hermann, Frederick J. 1971. New species of Carex from Mexico and Guatemala. Brittonia. 23: 144-148.

description: C. rigido affinis; folia pallide viridia, nee coriacea, matura utrinque sparse vel dense pubeseentia; pedunculi foliis aequales vel longiores, basi dense pilosi, superne glabrati; bractea inferior spiculis longior, 15- 20 mm. longa, infra nmedium dense albo-pilosa, ultra medium glabra, margine longe ciliata; achaenium 1.6-1.8 mm. longum, 1.3 mm. latum; stylus cum stigmatibus quam achaenium duplo longior, pallide brun- neus vel rubro-brunneus.

description: Perennis. Folia conferta in apice rhizomatis, atroviridia vel pur- purea, coriacea, linearia, acuta, rigida, bicarinata, 3.5-8 cm. longa, 1.5- 2.5 mm. lata, margine minute scabra, in ore vaginae pilosa, matura glabra. Pedunculi axillares 6-10 foliis breviores. Spiculae 2-10, sessiles vel breviter pedicellatae ad apicem pedunculi. Bractea inferior spiculani subaequans, foliis consimilis, glabra margine excepto breviter piloso. Squamae ehartaceae, nervo medio promiiente; squamae masculae brunneae, lanceolatae, 3-4 mm. latae, acutae vel mucronatae, margine subpilosae; squamae foemineae latiores, brunneae vel purpur- eae, prope apicem in aristam abrupte constrietae. Stamina 6. Achaenium teres obovatumn, 2 mm. longum, 1.5 mm. latum, pallide flavo- brunneum, lineis 3 atris longitudinalibus notatum, basi angustatum, apice depressum; styli basis persistens bulbosa teres clavata, cum apice achaenii sparse vel dense breviter pubeseens; styli et stigmata longi- tudine achaenium aequantia vel parce longiora, atrobrunnea. Squamel- lae hypogynae 3, ad basin in poculum connatae, n-argine albo-ciliatae, ciliis 0.5-0.7 mm. longis.

description: Shrub or subshrub, erect, 1-3 m tall; stems quadrangular, glabrous below, the upper portion minutely and densely hirtellous, the trichomes upwardly appressed; leaf blades ovate or oblong-ovate, 8.5-13 cm long and 3.5-5.5 cm wide, acute to acuminate or short-acuminate, narrowed at base, moderately firm, entire or undulate, the upper surface drying dark green, glabrous or minutely and inconspic- uously puberulous, the costa and lateral veins (9 or 10 pairs) prominent but less so than those of the lower surface, the cystoliths minute and obscure on both surfaces, the lower surface drying a lighter green, sparingly and finely pubescent especially along the venation, both surfaces more or less bullate; petioles short, 0.5-1 cm long, sparingly appressed-puberulous; flowers borne in terminal and subterminal paired spikes, 6-8 cm long and 1-1.5 cm broad; peduncles 1.5-2 cm long, these and the rachis subquadrangular, canaliculate, puberulous with ascending, white trichomes; bracts lanceolate, 15-17 mm long, 5-6 mm wide, acuminate, narrowed at base, rather thin and veiny (the costa prominent), more or less minutely glandular-papillose, rather sparingly ciliate; bracteoles linear-fili- form, about 7 mm long and 0.6 mm wide, rather sparingly glandular-puberulous with a few larger, eglandular trichomes intermixed with the smaller ones, the margins ciliate; calyx 7.5 mm long, the five segments subequal, narrowly lanceolate, 6.5 mm long, 0.8 mm wide, sparingly glandular-papillose and like the bracts and bracteoles intermixed with a few longer, eglandular trichomes, the margins ciliolate; corolla scarlet, 5-5.5 cm long, the tube rather gradually ampliate distally, the proximal portion (5 mm long) 3 mm in diam, thence expanding to 5 mm at throat, sparingly and finely pubescent, the upper lip erect, oblong-ovate, 28 mm long and 6.5 mm wide near base, gradually narrowed, arched and bilobed at apex, the lobes rounded, 0.5 mm long and wide, the lower lip spreading or recurved, 3-lobed, elliptic, 8 mm wide at base of lobes, these ovate, about 3 mm long and  2.5 mm wide, rounded; stamens barely reaching the tip of the upper corolla lip, the anther lobes superposed, vertically attached to the connective, 2 mm long and 0.75 mm broad, the filaments flattened, 0.7 mm wide; pollen grains 2-porate, bilateral, 60 x 35 µm, the pores circular, the membrane sparsely granular, trema area studded with finely patterned insulae (Fig. 2A); pistil slightly larger than the stamens, the stigma bilobed, minute and rounded; capsule 13-15 mm long, 3.5 mm wide and 2.5 mm thick, 4-seeded, minutely puberulous, the solid stipitate portion about 5 mm long and 2.5 mm broad; retinacula straight or slightly curved, about 2 mm long, acute; seeds suborbicular, dark-brown, 3 mm long and 2.5 mm broad, 1 mm thick, rounded at tip, smooth, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Wasshausen, Dieter C. 1989. New species of Justicia (Acanthaceae) from the Planalto of Brazil. Brittonia. 41 (4): 379-384.

description: Tree, reported to be 60-70 ft high in Puerto Rico and up to 150 ft high in Dominican Republic; twigs typically reddish glandular-pubescent finially glabrate; pith light brown; terminal buds elongate; leaves elongate, 30-55 cm long and 14-25 cm wide; leaf-rachis of some trees glabrous, of many trees appearing glabrous but densely and minutely glandular-puberulent, and of a few trees reddish glandular-pubescent to -villous; terminal leaflet absent; leaflets (12-) 16-20 (-22), opposite or alternate, thin, oblong-lanceolate or sometimes ovatelanceolate, 6.5-11 cm long and 2.5-4.5 cm wide (1.8-3.7 times as long as wide), sessile or short-stalked, rounded to subcordate at base at maturity (lower leaflets of the mature leaves), sometimes oblique, acuminate at apex, very finely serrate to prominently serrate with blunt forward-directed teeth, or sometimes distantly serrate and appearing almost entire, on the upper surface almost glabrous except for short glandular puberulence on midrib and some of the lateral veins, on the lower surface commonly glabrate except for short glandular pubescence (or rarely glandular villosity) on the midrib, with tufts of whitish hairs in the axils of the veins, minutely puberulent or even glabrous on the lateral veins and the surfaces between the veins, very rarely minutely fascicled-hairy on main veins; young leaflets appearing glabrous but with very minute glandular hairs or also with fascicled hairs, for a short time lepidote with numerous small scales; staminate catkins 10-13 cm long and 1.5-2 cm in diameter, the flowers large, distant or somewhat crowded, with pedicel 2-3.5 mm long, the bract small, slender or triangular, 1-1.5 mm long, near the apex of the pedicel or on the back of the flower; stamens 60-85, the crown or appendage of the connective puberulent, deltoid or narrowly deltoid, pointed (Cuba, Walsingham & Eames) or in Hispaniola (Jimenez 2275; Ekman 7878) weakly developed to horizontally oblong, rather truncate, sometimes coarsely toothed along upper margin; floral organs in addition to the bract and two bracteoles commonly 4-8; pistillate spike 6-11 cm long including the peduncle often 3.5 cm long, the flowers 5-8, scattered, with ovaries at first minutely fascicled-hairy, but not truly tomentose, soon becoming densely and minutely glandular-puberulent aild usually conspicuously lepidote with numerous pale scales; sepals elongate (3 mm long) curved outward, conspicuous; stigmas Iono (1 cm long), slender, erect or spreading; apex of involucre toothed or lobed; fruiting rachis 6-20 cm long; fruit dark brown, frequently somewhat verrucose, glabrate or very minutely glandularpuberulent, subglobose to short-ovoid, 3.5 cm long and 2.6-4 cm in diameter; nut reddish brown to rather blackish (the remains of husk influencing the color?), subglobose to oval to subconical and then tapering from below the middle to the apex. not or slightly apiculate to definitely pointed, usually not compressed or but slightly so, 1.9-3.5 cm long and 1.9-3.1 cm in diameter, strongly longitudinally ridged, the ridges broad and flat, to rather narrow and rounded, somewhat interrupted, the dorsal partition medium, wall lacunae well developed, those at the ends of the primary partition lacking.
bibliographicCitation: Manning, Wayne E. 1960. The genus Juglans in South America and the West Indies. Brittonia. 12: 1-26.

description: Arbor parva, foliorum rachibus dense glanduloso-pubescentibus villosisve; folioli 16-20, oblongo vel ovato-lanceolati, basi acuti, subtus rubido-glanduloso-pubescentes vel -hirsuti; spica mascula 6-9 cim longa, floribus magnis, dissitis; nux subglobosa, sub-acute costata, diametro 2.3 cm, longitudine 2.5 cm.
bibliographicCitation: Manning, Wayne E. 1960. The genus Juglans in South America and the West Indies. Brittonia. 12: 1-26.

description: Low tree with spreading crown or sometimes a large tree; young twigs densely glandular-pubescent, in the second year glabrate with scattered glandular pubescence; pith light brown; leaves 43 cm long and 20 enl broad; rachis densely and conspicuously reddish glandular-pubescent or -hirsute; leaflets mostly opposite, 16-20, not conspicuously thick or rugose, sessile or short-stalked (stalk 1-2 mm long), oblong-lanceolate or sometimes ovate-lanceolate, 9-11 cm long and 3.5-4 cm wide, tapering or sometimes slightly rounded at base, sometimes strongly oblique, acuminate at apex, rather finely serrate with bluntish incurved teeth, almost glabrous above with glandular pubescence on midrib and with scattered glandular hairs on the lateral veins, beneath reddish glandular-pubescent or -hirsute on the midrib and all veins, the hairs slhorter on the smaller veins; young leaflets reddish glandular-puberulent and lepidote beneath; staminate catkins 5-10 cm long, the flowers few and widely separated, strongly stalked, the floral bract small, 1-1.5 (-2?) mm long, near the apex of the pedicel; stamens 95-105, the appendage of the connective weakly developed, barely exceeding the loculi, essentially truncate; pistillate spike elongate, 6- to 7-flowered, the ovaries densely whitish tomentose; peduncle of immature fruiting spike 2 cm lolng, the rachis 9 cm long; the immature fruits scattered, densely tomentose; complete fruits unknown; nut small, subglobose, 2.5 cm long and 2.3 cm in diameter, longitudinally ridged with rather narrow somewhat sharp ridges.
bibliographicCitation: Manning, Wayne E. 1960. The genus Juglans in South America and the West Indies. Brittonia. 12: 1-26.

description: Tree, up to 30 m high; bark on smaller limbs smooth and gray, on trunk 'moderately thick, brown, somewhat fissured," or "gray with deep longitudinal furrows"; young twigs at first covered almost completely by fascicled hairs, soon becoming mostly reddish glandular-hairy; twigs in the second year brown or reddish brown, prominently lenticellate, mostly reddish glandular-pubescent or sometimes also with scattered faseieled hairs, finally yellowish or grayish brown and almost glabrous with only scattered reddish glandular hairs; pith light brown; terminal bud slender, pointed; leaves commonly 34 cm long and 18 cm wide, but becoming 60 cm long and 30 cm broad; rachis at the very first fascicled-hairy, but typically soon becoming reddish glandular-pubescent, with fascicled hairs in some areas, finally glabrate in some leaves; leaflets (12-) 15-19, opposite or subopposite, thick, usually rugose, ovate to ovate-oblong to ovate-lanceolate, commonly 11 cm long, 5 cm wide (10-16 cm long, 4-8 cm wide), sessile or nearly so, rounded to subcordate and sometimes oblique at the base, abruptly acuminate at the apex, rather coarsely serrate with broad teeth (commonly 5 per cm), on the upper surface reddish glandular-pubescent on midrib anld maini veins with scattered fascicled hairs, elsewhere with scattered glandular hairs, on the lower surface typically pilose-tomentose with conspicuous fascicled hairs over a glaucous background, the midrib densely reddish glandular-puberulent with scattered fascicled hairs, finally glabrate in some leaves, inconspicuously lepidote; young leaflets conspicuously whitish- or yellowish-tomentose beneath with fascieled hairs; staminate catkins 10-20 (-25) long, and up to 1.5 cm in diameter; staminate flowers rather large, distanit, stalked; floral bract elongate, linearlanceolate, conspicuously whitish-tomentose, 2-5 mm long, on the back of the flower, those toward the apex of the catkiin shorter; stamens 60-85; connective produced into a crown or appendage above the loculi, the appendage minutely pubescent, horizontally oblong, usually truncate, coarsely toothed along the upper edge, rarely quite small or somewhat pointed; pistillate spike 4-5 cm long (-10 cm according to Dode), the rachis reddish glandular-pubescent or fascicled-hairy, with 5-10 flowers, these rather scattered; ovaries densely tomnentose with fascicled hairs; involuere strongly lobed at apex; sepals very long; stigmas elongate, fairly slender; old flowers or immature fruits denisely whitish tomentose, with dark warts sometimes showing through the hairs, the peduncle of older spikes 3 cm long and the rachis 5 cm long; fruit subglobose or broadly oval, usually 3.5-4 cm long and 3.5-3.8 cm in diameter, but sometimes 6 cm long and thick, almost glabrous or somewhat reddish glandular-hairy, sometimes rather conspicuously verrucose; nut blackish, subglobose to slightly depressed-globose or broadly oval, not appreciably compressed, commonly 4.2 cm long (2.8-5 cm) and 4.2 cm in diameter (3-4.5 cm), barely apiculate, conspicuously and deeply longitudinally ridged, the ridges rather broad and flat-topped, mostly not interrupted, the edges rounded to rather sharp; some of the ridges narrow and rather sharp; shell thick, the wall lacunae large and conspicuous in cross-section, the lacunae at the ends of the primary wall typically lacking.
bibliographicCitation: Manning, Wayne E. 1960. The genus Juglans in South America and the West Indies. Brittonia. 12: 1-26.

description: Shrub or small tree to 5 m, occasionally higher; young shoots yellowish brown to grey, densely lepidote. Leaves alternate or sometimes vaguely pseudoverticillate; blade broadly to narrowly obovate, sometimes broadly elliptic, 1-4.5 x 0.5-2.5 cm, coriaceous and very tough, seemingly glabrous or puberulous towards base, the lamina often recurved from midrib, sometimes strongly so; base attenuate; apex retuse or rounded, without or sometimes with a dark- ened point to 0.2 mm long; margins revolute; midvein in level with leaf surface or vaguely prominent on both sides, lateral veins inconspicuous or invisible; both surfaces smooth or the upper surface sometimes vaguely striate; petiole 2-6 mm long, 0.4-1 mm thick, puberulous-lepidote. Racemes solitary with 4-30 flowers; rachis 0.8- 6.5 cm long, 0.8-1.5 mm thick, puberulous in the axils and at base; bracts 0.5-0.7 mm long, inserted at the nodes; pedicels 7-12 mm long. Calyx lobes suborbicular or very broadly ovate, 1.8-2.5 x 2-3.5 mm, the margins erose, shortly erose-ciliate, or rare- ly subentire, erect in fruit. Corolla white or yellowish white, tube 3-3.5(-4.5) mm long, lobes obovate or oblong, 3.5-4.5 x 2-3(-4) mm; staminodes oblong or broadly oblong, 2.2-3 x 1.8-2 mm, obtuse, rounded or truncate at apex. Filaments 1.5-1.8 mm long, glandular-punctate; anthers 1.5-2 mm long, obtuse at apex. Pistil 2.8-4 mm long, style sparsely glandular-punctate; ovules 80- 120 in 5 or 6 rows. Fruits yellow, subspherical, 5.5-10 mm diam, apiculate; pericarp 0.2-0.4 mm thick. Seeds 3-8, often +/- flat- tened, oblong to elliptic, 2.5-3 mm long, dark brown or brown.
bibliographicCitation: Ståhl, Bertil. 1992. On the identity of Jacquinia armillaris (Theophrastaceae) and related species. Brittonia. 44: 54-60.

description: Shrub or small tree to 5 m, rarely higher; young shoots greyish brown, densely lepidote. Leaves pseudoverticillate, sometimes indistinctly so; blade broadly obovate to ob- ovate, 3-8(-12) x 1.5-4(-5) cm, coriaceous and mostly very tough, seemingly glabrous, the sides occasionally somewhat recurved; base attenuate; apex rounded or retuse, sometimes obtuse, without or rarely with a rigid spine to 0.5 mm long; margins +/- revolute; midvein prominent beneath, somewhat impressed or in level with surface above, lateral veins rather inconspicuous; petiole 2.5-7 mm long, 0.6-1.5 mm thick, sparsely to densely lepidote, sometimes subglabrous. Racemes solitary with 7-25 (-40) flowers; rachis (1.5-)3-6(-12) cm long, 1-1.6 mm thick, lepidote in axils and at base; bracts 1-1.5 mm long, inserted at the nodes or fused to the pedicels for 1-2 mm; pedicels 7-13 mm long. Calyx lobes very broadly ovate or suborbicular, 2.2-3.2 x 2.5-3.2 mm, margins entire or very vaguely erose, erect in fruit. Corolla white or yellowish white, tube 4-5 mm long, lobes broadly oblong, 2.8-4 x 2.5-3.5 mm; stam- inodes very broadly oblong to ovate, 1.8-3 x 2-3 mm, rounded or retuse at apex. Filaments 1-1.8 mm long, glandular-punctate; anthers 1.7-2 mm long, obtuse at apex. Pistil 3.2-3.8 mm long, style glandular-punctate; ovules 70-100(-125) in 4-6 rows. Fruits orange red or red, subglobose, 7-11 mm diam, apiculate; pericarp 0.2-0.3 mm thick. Seeds 2-4(-6), often somewhat flattened, oblong to elliptic, 3-5 mm long, light brown or brown.
bibliographicCitation: Ståhl, Bertil. 1992. On the identity of Jacquinia armillaris (Theophrastaceae) and related species. Brittonia. 44: 54-60.

description: Shrub or small tree to 6 m, sometimes higher, richly branched; young shoots grey or brownish grey, densely lepidote. Leaves pseudoverticillate; blade obovate to oblanceolate, sometimes broadly obovate, 2-7 (-9) x 0.8-3(-4) cm, coriaceous and rather tough, seemingly glabrous (i.e., without protrusive hairs but with immersed glandular hairs), the sides sometimes somewhat recurved; base attenuate; apex obtuse or rounded, sometimes acute or retuse, often with a rigid spine to 0.5(-1) mm long; mar- gins +/- revolute; midvein prominent beneath, slightly sunken or in level with leaf surface above, lateral veins usually rather inconspicuous; lower surface striate, the upper vaguely striate or smooth; petiole 1-3 mm long, 0.6-1.3 mm thick, glabrous. Ra- cemes solitary with 3-10 flowers; rachis rather slender, 0.5-3(-4.5) cm long, 0.5-1 mm thick, glabrous or lepidote in axils and at base; bracts 0.5-1.2 mm long, inserted at the nodes or fused to the pedicels for 1-2 mm; pedicels 6-12(-15) mm long. Calyx lobes very broadly ovate or suborbicular, 1.8-2.5 x 2-3 mm, margins ciliate, re- curved in fruit. Corolla tube yellowish white, the limb white, tube (3.5-)4-5.5 mm long, lobes broadly oblong, (2-)2.8-3.5(-4) x 2- 3 mm; staminodes broadly ovate, 1-2 x 1.2-2.5 mm, rounded or retuse at apex. Filaments 1-2 mm long, glandular-punctate; anthers 1.2-2 mm long, obtuse at apex. Pistil 2.8-3.8 mm long; ovules (30-)50-90 in 3-5 rows. Fruits orange-red, subglobose, 6- 10(-13) mm diam, apiculate; pericarp 0.2- 0.4 mm thick. Seeds 1-3, subglobose or +/- flattened and then elliptic to orbicular, 3-5 mm long, brown.
bibliographicCitation: Ståhl, Bertil. 1992. On the identity of Jacquinia armillaris (Theophrastaceae) and related species. Brittonia. 44: 54-60.

description: Frutex 2 m altus, rami hornotini tetragoni, lateribus alteris dense patente pilosis, alteris glabris, cystolithis nullis; spinae axillares pungentes teretes usque 1 cm longae interdum bifurcatae, glabrae; folia subsessilia obovato-oblonga vel obovata, basi acuta, apice rotundata vel obtusa, 3-6 mm longa, 1.5-3 mm lata, nervo medio supra parum impresso subtus prominulo, nervis lateralibus obsoletis vel utroque latere 1 vel 2 subtus tantum manifestis, integra plana glabra vel subtus ad nervum medium parce pilosula, non cystolithigera, in sicco nigra, membranacea; flores in axillis foliorum solitarii, pedicellis 3-4 mm longis; bracteae subulatae ca. 1 mm longae; calyx 3.5 mm longus, ad basim 0.5 mm coalitus; lobi 5 lanceolato-lineares, subulato-acuminati; corolla purpurea 25 mm longa; tubus cylindraceus sub-rectus, inferne sensim attenuatus et minute parceque pilosulus, lobis 4-5 mm longis; stamina 2, 1.4 cm ab corollae apice affixa, non exserta; filamenta quoad libera ca. 1 cm longa, antherarum loculis ad basim et ad apicem apiculatis, pro 2/3 longitudine appositis; ovarium lanceolatum minute pilosum; stylus 2 cm longus, inferne pilosus, stigma globosum.
bibliographicCitation: Liogier, Alain H. 1968. Novitates Antillanae. III. Brittonia. 20: 148-161.

description: Plants subcaulescent, erect, essentially glabrous, simple or usually with a few weak lateral branches arising from the stout fibrous base, to 2.5 dm tall. Leaves narrowly oblong, 6-7.5 cm long, 1-1.5 cm broad, pinnatisect, the leaflets obovate in 3-5 opposite, remote, sessile pairs, dissected into linear-acuminate ultimate divisions 1-2 mm long, less than 0.5 mm broad; petiole slender, 1-1.5 cm long, broadly scarious-sheathing; cauline leaves (of lateral branches) paired, like the basal. Terminal peduncle stout, 1.5-2 dm tall, ribbed, hirsutulous at apex. Involucre of 5-8 pinnatisect bracts 1-3.5 cm long. Rays of terminal umbel 10-12, stout, ribbed, spreading-ascending, unequal, 2-7 cm long. Umbellets 8-12-flowered, the mature pedicels stout, angled, spreading-ascending, 2-5 mm long. Involucel of 8-10 linear to lanceolate, pinnatisect or a few entire bracteoles 5-10 mm long, Flowers not seen. Fruit broadly ovoid, 4-5 mm long, 2-3 mm broad, subterete, narrowed toward apex, rounded at base, the mericarps lightly compressed dorsally in transection, the ribs prominently corky-thickened, each with a small air-space, much broader than intervals. Vittae large, solitary in intervals, 3-5 on commissure. Endosperm grooved beneath intervals. Carpophore halves divergent to form a small "Y" or "O" near apex. October.
bibliographicCitation: Mukherjee, Prasanta K. & Constance, Lincoln. 1986. Two new genera of Indian Umbelliferae/Apiaceae. Brittonia. 38: 145-149.

description:
Annual with tufted, much-branched, ascending to prostrate, rarely decumbent shoots to 30(46) cm long, rooting only near the base; roots thin, fibrous; internodes to 8 cm long, glabrous or glabrescent. Leaves spiral or distichous; sheaths 0.5-1 cm long, surface glabrous or with a line of pubes- cence along the fused edge, ciliate at the apex; lamina sessile, linear to linear-lanceolate or elliptic, usually conduplicate, occa- sionally planar, sometimes strongly recurved, (0.5)1-5 X 0.4-0.6 cm, the apex acute to acuminate, the base ± cuneate, the surfaces glabrous or pubescent.

Peduncles of the spathes 0.4-1.4 cm long, ascending, then spreading up to right angles to the stem, glabrous or puberulous apically, often deciduous at the base (the spathe plus peduncle then serving as a dis- seminule); spathes solitary, semilunate, not or slightly falcate, 0.9-2 cm long, 0.45-1 cm high, the apex acute to rounded, the base deeply cordate to ± hastate, the surfaces puberulous to glabrous, the margins free, glabrous or ciliate; upper cincinnus present, 1-flowered or abortive, the peduncle included in spathe, rarely shortly exserted, lower cincinnus 1-3(4)-flowered.

Flowers bisexual and male, ca. 1 cm wide, open in the morning; sepals 3, hya- line, tinged green, the upper sepal ovate to ovate-elliptic, 2.7-3 X 1.5-2 mm, the paired sepals free, broadly elliptic to ovate orbicular, 2.5 X 2 mm; paired petals 5-5.5 X 5-6 mm, the limb broadly ovate-reni- form, 4-5 X 5-6 mm, pale buff, buff-orange or apricot-pink, the apex rounded, the base cordate, the margin crenulate, the claw ca. 2 mm long, pinkish buff; lower petal broadly cup-shaped, ovate, ca. 2.5 X 3 mm, concolorous with paired petal limb; staminodes 3, equal, filaments pinkish buff tipped with yellow, ca. 2.5 mm long; an- therodes cruciform with minute pollen sacs, yellow, ca. 0.5-0.9 mm long; lateral stamens with filaments parallel to slightly divergent, sigmoid, ca. 3.2 mm long, pinkish buff, the anthers ovate, ca. 1 mm long, en- tirely yellow or with blue-black sutures, the pollen yellow; medial stamen with filament ca. 3 mm long, pinkish buff, the anther sad- dle-shaped, yellow, ca. 1.4 mm long, the pollen concolorous with lateral stamens; ovary oblong-elliptic, ca. 1.5 X 1 mm, green; style pinkish buff, or reddish purple basally and yellow apically, sigmoid, ca. 3.5 mm long; stigma capitate.

Capsules 5.5-7 X 3-4 mm, apiculate, the dorsal locule indehiscent, 0-1-seeded, the ventral locules dehiscent, 1-2-seeded. Ventral locule seeds transversely elliptic or transversely oblong-elliptic to broadly ovate, dorsiventrally compressed, 2.7-4.2 X 1.5-2 mm, testa medium to dark brown, foveate to foveate-reticulate with transversely elongate and ± round pits, each pit filled and bordered with paler farinaceous material, this material often also forming a fine reticulum or partial reticulum on the ridges.
bibliographicCitation: Faden, Robert B. 1996. New Endemic Species of Aneilema and Commelina (Commelinaceae) from Somalia. Brittonia. 48 (4): 544-550.

description: Frutex vel arbor 6-8 m usque alta, ramis 3.5-5.5 cm diam, costis 5-6 compressis 3-6 mm latis, crenatis, spinis divergentibus utriusque areolae 8-25, 0.3-2.1 cm longis. Flores terminales 5.7-7.2 cm longi, receptaculum tubulosum circa 2 cm diam, fulvo-olivaceum, segmentis interioribus albis. Fructus ellipsoideo-globosus vel obovatus. Areolae fructus spinosae usque ad fructus maturitatem perdurantes.
bibliographicCitation: Areces-Mallea, Alberto E. 1992. Leptocereus santamarinae (Cactaceae), a new species from Cuba. Brittonia. 44: 45-49.

description: Ut videtur frutex parvus, statura igiiota, ramis annotinis igiiotis, horilotinis eavis, teretibus, glabris vel conspersissime hirsutis, 5 mm. diametro, ramulis junioribus gracilioribus, perspicue patule longe ciliato-hirsutis, pilis pallide ferrugineis, ad 2 mm. longis; foliis maturis firmiter chartaceis, ovatis vel oblongo-ovatis, breviter petiolatis, eirciter 25 cm. longis et 10 cm. latis, longe acuminatis, basi late rotundatis, supra subolivaceis, nitidis, glabris vel ad costam consperse ciliato-hirsutis, subtus pallidis, subglaucis, ad nervis reticulisque primariis breviter consperse ciliato-hirsutis, reticulis ultimis subgranulosis, omnibus distinctis; nervis primariis utrinque eirciter 8, subtus elevatis, curvatis vel curvato-adscendentibus, perspicue arcuato-anastomosantibus, margine ad basim et apicem integris, ceteroquin apiculato-dentatis vel apiculato-serratis, dentibus 5-15 mm. remotis, foliis junioribus submembranaceis, minoribus, eirciter 15 cm. longis et 5 cm. latis; petiolo hirsuto, eirciter 8 mm. longo; stipulis reniformibus, subeoriaceis, eirciter 3 cm. latis et 1.4 cm. longis, subtus subglaucis, perspicue reticulatis et breviter hirsutis, persistentibus; infloreseentiis eirciter 14 cm. longis (vel longioribus), pedunculo 4-5 cm. longo, perspicue ciliato-hirsuto, multifloris, verticillis 6-1 floris, deorsum subremotis, sursum (floribus immaturis) subeontiguis, perspicue ciliato-hirsutis, bracteis inferioribus lanceolatis vel oblongo-lanceolatis, perspicue acuminatis, reticulatis, plus minusve ciliato-hirsutis, 2-3 cm. longis, 8-10 mm. latis, superioribus brevioribus; floribus eirciter 22 mm. longis, sessilibus, receptaculo 6-7 mm. longo, dense ciliato-hirsuto, pilis rectis, patulis, pilis capitatis brevioribus commixtis, sepalis oblongo-lanceolatis vel lanceolatis, acuminatis, 3-nerviis, 6-8 mm. longis eirciter 3 mm. latis, ciliato-hirsutis; corolla eirciter 1.5 cm. longa, sursum ampliata, extus plus minusve ciliato-hirsuta atque capitato-pilosa; filamentis breviter ciliatis; antheris ellipsoideis, 3 mm. longis; stylis deorsum breviter ciliatus, sursum glabris; stigmate capitato, 2 mm. diametro.

description: Perennial with tufted, erect to ascending, or somewhat clambering, much-branched, wiry shoots to 1.2 m tall, appearing woody when dry, shoot bases swollen; roots cordlike, not tuberous; internodes to 7 cm long, glabrous. Leaves borne mostly distally, being shed from the lower nodes, the sheaths to 2.7 cm long, glabrous or with a few mi- nute hairs at the summit, the lamina sessile, linear-lanceolate, 3-8.5 X 0.2-1.1 cm, apex acuminate to acute, the base cuneate, the margins planar, slightly scabrous, the surfaces glabrous, or abaxial sparsely puberu- lous with hook-hairs along the midrib. Spathes clustered, sessile, semilunate, strongly falcate, (1.3)2-3 cm long, (0.7)1.3-2.5 cm high, glabrous, apple green, turning brown and papery, the apex acute to obtuse, the base ± sagittate, the margins longly or shortly fused basally, glabrous, the upper cincinnus lacking, the lower 1-2-flowered; bracteoles present. Flowers palest yellow; upper sepal ca. 3 mm long; paired sepals fused laterally, ca. 3.5 mm long; lower petal linear-lanceolate; staminodes 3; medial stamen anther saddle- shaped, larger than the lateral anthers. Capsules broadly elliptic, ca. 5 X 4.5 mm, apparently with 3 1-seeded locules, the dorsal locule indehiscent, ca. 3 mm long, striate or with bumps and pits, the ventral locules smooth, dehiscent. Ventral locule seeds hemispherical, elliptic in outline, ca. 3.5 X 2.5 mm, the testa irregularly and deeply pit- ted dorsally, brown, with pale tan material in and around the pits, not farinose.

description: Frutex nanus; ramulis teretibus juventute densissime foliatis parce pilosis, mox glabris, demum defoliatis eineraseentibus, internodiis maturitate 1.5-2.5 mm. longis; petiolis ad ramulos adpressis complanatis praeter inargines minute albido-pilosos glabris 0.7-1.3 mm. longis; foliorum laminis crassis imbricatis ovato-oblongis, 4-6 mm. longis, 1.5-2.5 mm. latis, basi et apice obtusis, margine copiose et conspicue setosis (setis utroque eirciter 14 albidis eglandulosis 0.6-0.8 mm. longis), utrinique nitidis et glabris, subtus profunde suleatis; floribus solitariis vel binis terminalibus; pedicellis gracilibus saepe durvatis 10-22 mm. longis, densissinme setosis (setis castaneis vel fuscopurpureis 1-1.5 mm. longis eglandulosis vel saepe glandulas minutas mox deciduas gerentibus), arete albido-tomentellis; sepalis 6 vel 7 oblongo-lanceolatis acutis, 5-6 mm. longis, eirciter 1.5 mm. latis, decidue albido-tomentellis, dorsaliter et niargine copiose eglandulososetosis (setis ad 2 mm. longis, dorsaliter 20-30); petalis 6 vel 7 membranaceis obovatis, 10-12 mm. longis, 7-9 mmn. latis, apice rotundatis, glabris; staminibus 12 vel 14 glabris eirciter 5 mm. longis; filamentis ligulatis eirciter 3 mm. longis apicem versus angustatis; antheris lineari-oblongis 3-3.5 mm. longis; stylo crasso sub anthesi eirciter 2.5 mm. longo, ap ice inerassato et inconspicue lobato; capsula ovoidea valde verrucosa eirciter 8 mm. longa 4- vel 5-valvata.

description: Plants acaulescent, 0.3-5 dm high, villous-tomentose to glabrate, from a long, slender to thickened taproot. Leaves broadly ovate or obovate to oblong in outline, the blades 1-19 cm long, pinnately decompound or ternate, then 3-4 pinnate, the ultimate divisions crowded, linear to obovate, 1-7 mm long, about 0.5-1 mm broad, mucronulate or apiculate; the petioles 1-15 cm long, shortly sheathing below to wholly sheathing, usually purplish. Peduncles exceeding the leaves, 0.3-5 dm long. Involucre usually wanting. Rays 1-30, 0.1-8 cm long, spreadingascending, usually unequal, the central umbellets often sterile and short-rayed or sessile. Involucel of linear to linear-lanceolate, acute to acuminate, subscarious to scarious-margined, entire or lobed bractlets, distinct or connate at base, sometimes connate to above the middle, rarely conspicuously nerved, shorter than or equaling the flowers. Pedicels 1-15 mm long, the umbellets many-flowered, the central flowers male or sterile, subsessile or pedicellate. Flowers purple, yellow, yellow with purplish tinge, or yellow and purple flowers combined in the same umbellet, petals obovate with a narrower inflexed apex, glabrous, or pubescent along margins; calyx-teeth small or obsolete; styles slender, stylopodium absent, disk present. Fruit ovate-oblong to orbicular, 4-12 mm long, 3-8 mm broad, the dorsal ribs filiform or obsolete, the lateral membraneous winged, the body pubescent to glabrate, the wings pubescent to sparingly villous or glabrate, the wings narrower than the body, usually equal to or less than half the width of the body; vittae 1-7 in the intervals, occasionally with smaller accessory vittae, 2-8 on the commissure, occasionally with smaller accessory vittae, sometimes one at the base of each wing.
bibliographicCitation: Theobald, William L. 1966. The Lomatium dasycarpum mohavense foeniculaceum complex (Umbelliferae). Brittonia. 18: 1-18.

description: Annual or more often perennial herb, glabrous or sparsely pilose at the nodes or sometimes with scattered hairs throughout, frequently decumbent at the base, 17-37 (10-65) cm tall; leaves whorled below, opposite or alternate above, ovate to obovate, obtuse to acute or apiculate, glabrous or sparsely villous below or on both surfaces, 10-14 (6-21) mm long, 4.1-7.3 (3.1-9.1) mm wide; stipular glands present at the bases of the floral bracts, as well as the leaves and at the bases of at least some of the sepals in about one-half of the plants examined; inflorescence  paniculate; fruit subsessile or on pedicels up to 6 mm long; pedicels villous, sometimes sparsely so; sepals lanceolate, sometimes narrowly so, acute to acuminate, lightly appressed hairy inside, but otherwise glabrous, with prominent midrib and inconspicuous lateral veins, glandular-toothed, 2.6-3.0 (2.3-3.8) mm long; petals lemon-yellow, oblanceolate or narrowly obcordate, 3-5 mm long, glabrous; stamens 2-4 mm long, filaments slender, sparsely villous below, with 1 or 2 low, deltoid staminodia between; anthers narrowly elliptic, 0.6-0.8 (0.5-0.9) mm long; styles separate, strongly divaricate (in fresh material) at the base, 1.7-2.9 mm long, contorted soon after anthesis; fruit broadly ovate, obtuse, usually pubescent above, 1.5-1.8 (1.3-2.2) mm high, 1.5-2.3 mm in diameter, easily crushed in pressing; false septa poorly developed; septa glabrous or true septa with a few marginal hairs; seeds ovate, reddish brown, shining, 0.8-1.2 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Plants 0.5-1 m tall; rhizome pinkish to red. Leaves 3-6, concentrated toward the top of the shoot, reddish green, membra- nous; sheaths reddish, membranous, 7-16 mm diam. at the base of the plant; ligule membranous, truncate, (2)5-9 mm long; sheaths and ligules densely to rather densely villose. Lamina obovate-elliptic (10)13- 29 cm long, (6)8-16 cm wide, base acute, apex shortly acuminate (acumen 0.5-1 cm long) to acute, upper and lower side densely to rather densely villose, tertiary veins parallel (0.4-0.6 mm apart). Petiole 4-18 mm long, hairy as the ligule. Inflorescence terminal, obtrulloid to cylindric, 6-8 cm long, 4-6 cm diam., elongating during fructification to 10 cm long, acute to rounded at the apex. Indument of bracts, bracteoles, calyx, outer side of corolla, ovary, and capsule densely to rather densely puberulous. Bracts red to orange-red, herbaceous to co- riaceous, ascending and more or less patent, obovate to broadly ovate, 2.3-4.5 cm long, 1.1-2.5 cm wide, callus inconspicuous; appendages more or less distinctly separated from the bract proper, red, triangular-ovate to very shallowly triangular-ovate, 0.8-4 cm long, 1.5-2 cm wide, acute (lower bracts sometimes subtending two flowers (Wood s.n., U). Bracteole reddish, placed opposite the bract, triangular-ovate to narrowly triangular-ovate, bicarinate by longitudinal ridges on the adaxial side, often one of the ridges provided with a subapical callus, 24-32 mm long. Calyx reddish to red- orange, tubular to tubular turbinate, 9-20 mm long, 5-7 mm wide, the lobes ovate to broadly ovate, 2-5 mm long, 2.5-6 mm wide. Corolla pink to red with dark red apex, 45-47 mm long, tube 15-20 mm long, lobes ovate to narrowly ovate, 30-32 mm long, dorsal one 15-18 mm wide, lateral ones 10-12 mm wide, apex cucullate. Labellum white at the base graduating to dark red in the upper half, limb obovate when spread out, 27-30 mm long, 18 mm wide, involute and forming a tube 5-10 mm diam. with a ring of 2 mm long trichomes at the base of the tube formed by labellum and stamen, 5-lobulate, each lobule 2-3 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, acute, middle lobule subulate, 1 mm long. Stamen white with dark red apex, narrowly elliptic, 28 mm long, 8 mm wide, acute, anther 8 mm long, 4 mm wide. Style 43 mm long, stigma bi- lamellate, ovary obovoid to broadly obovoid. Capsule obovoid, 13 X 9 mm, ca. 40-seeded, seeds 1-1.5 mm diam., arillate.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M. & Maas-van de Kamer, Hillegonda. 1997. Two new species of Costus (Costaceae) from Costa Rica. Brittonia. 49: 274-279.

description: Perennial herb, 23-39 (18-68) cm tall, branching at the base and in the in- florescence, glabrous except for occasional hairs near bases of leaves; lower leaves in whorls of 4, upper alternate, sometimes mostly whorled or (as in type of L. greggii) mostly alternate, sessile, entire, lanceolate to oblanceolate, the larger 10-18 (9-21) mm long, 2.6-4.9 (1.8-6.0) mm wide; leaves and lower floral bracts with stipular glands; inflorescence paniculate, the flowers and fruits on pedicels very rarely over 1 mm long; sepals lanceolate, acute, glandular-toothed, the inner with narrow scarious margins, 2.5-3.2 (2.1-3.5) mm long; petals lemon-yellow, oblanceolate to narrowly obcordate, 4-5 (3-6) mm long, sparsely pilose at the base; stamens 2-5 mm long; staminodia low, deltoid, usually two between each of the stamens, sometimes one or none; anthers 0.4-0.5 (0.3-0.7) mm long; styles separate, 1.8-2.6 (1.6-3.0) mm long; fruit glabrous, broadly ovate, sharp pointed, easily crushed, readily dehiscing into 10 parts, 1.7-2.2 (1.4-2.5) mm high, 2.1-2.4 (1.8-2.5) mm in diameter; false septa quite incomplete, the true septa usually bearing marginal cilia; seeds reddish brown, shining, ovate, 1.1-1.3 (0.9-1.5) mm long, 0.6-0.8 (-1.0) mm wide.

description: Coarse perennial herb, glabrous or occasionally with a few scattered hairs; stems several from the base, mostly simple to the inflorescence, purplish, 45-167 cm tall (with small plants having probably been collected); leaves opposite or sometimes whorled below, alternate above, the lower elliptic, the principal stem leaves linear- lanceolate, the larger 15-36 mm long, 3-8 mm wide, entire, acuminate, appressed, sessile or narrowed to a very short petiole, lateral nerves indistinct; inflorescence with rather stiffly ascending-spreading branches; sepals lanceolate-ovate to ovate, 2.3-4.2 mm long, acute, entire or with a few scattered marginal glands, the inner somewhat broader and shorter, erose; petals yellow, obovate, 4-7 mm long; stamens 3-5 mm long, the filaments broadened at the base; anthers 0.4-0.9 mm long; staminodia very slender, up to 1.3 mm long; styles 2.0-3.3 mm long, united at the base as much as 1 mm, fruit turbinate, acute to acuminate at the summit, 2.3-3.2 mm high, 2.3-2.6 mm in diameter, readily dehiscing into 10 sharp pointed segments; false septa partially developed; true septa ciliate; seeds ovate, 1.3-1.5 mm long, 0.7-1.0 mm wide, reddish brown.

description: Plants (0.5) 1.3-2 m tall. Leaf sheaths to 7-15 mm diam., densely minutely puberulous; ligule unequally and bluntly 2-lobed, 15-30 mm long, densely minutely puberulous, near the margins densely puberulous, sometimes decaying into fibers (to 15 mm long). Lamina shiny, upper side dark green, lower side green, narrowly obovate to narrowly elliptic, 24-44 cm long, 6-12 cm wide, base decurrent but finally rounded, apex long-acuminate (acumen (1)2.5-5.5 cm long), upper side rather densely strigose, primary and secondary veins and margin densely puberulous to almost glabrous, lower side densely sericeous to almost glabrous, primary vein densely puberulous, tertiary veins parallel (0.5 mm apart). Petiole 0-5 mm long, hairy as the ligule. Inflorescence terminal, globose to broadly ellipsoid, 4.5-5 cm long, 4-5 cm diam., expanding during fructification to 12 cm long and 6 cm diam., rounded at the apex. Indument of the bracts, bracteoles, calyx, outer side of corolla, ovary, and capsule densely puberulous. Bracts dark or carmine red, herbaceous, broadly elliptic, 1.4-2.5 cm long, 0.7-2.5 cm wide, callus yellow (or green), 2-4 mm long, situated at the top of the bract just below the appendage; appendages carmine red, reflexed, concave, shallowly to very shallowly ovate-triangu- lar, 0.7-1.5 cm long, 0.8-2.7 cm wide, acute. Bracteole red at the base, orange at the apex, placed opposite the bract, broadly triangular-ovate, bicarinate by longitudinal ridges at the adaxial side, often one of the ridges provided with a subapical callus, 12- 18 (26) mm long. Calyx red, tubular to turbinate, 10-12 mm long, 8-10 mm wide, lobes very shallowly triangular, 2-4 mm long, 5-8 mm wide. Corolla basally white, middle part red to orange, apex yellow, 40- 47 mm long, tube 8-13 mm long, lobes nar- rowly elliptic to elliptic, 32-35 mm long, dorsal one 16-20 mm wide, lateral ones 13-19 mm wide. Labellum orange to red, lobules of limb dark red, limb elliptic when spread out, 20-35 mm long, 15-20 mm wide, involute and forming a tube 7-10 mm diam. with a ring of 1.5 mm long trichomes at the base of the tube formed by labellum and stamen, 5-lobulate, each lobule 4-5.5 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, acute. Stamen orange with dark red apex, narrowly ellip- tic, 16-35 mm long, 7-10 mm wide, acute, anther white, 8 mm long, 5 mm wide. Style 30-32 mm long, stigma bilamellate; ovary white, ellipsoid to globose. Capsule ellipsoid, 9 X 6 mm, ca. 30-seeded, seeds 1 mm diam., arillate.

description: Florigera plus quam 5 dm alta. Folia multa, rosulata, plus quam 4 dm longa; vaginis subquadratis, quam laminis vix latioribus, albis, glabris; laminis lineari-lanceolatis, acuminatis, ad 35 mm latis, coriaceis, glabris, atro-viridibus, lucidis, basi laxe serrulatis. Laminarum anatomia: Fila vascularia adaxialiter chlorenchymate non obsita; chlorenchyma abaxiale uniforme; cellulae subepidermales sub nervis elongatis inter nervas breviores irregulares plerumque resiniferae in parietibus tenues; cellulae substomatales non distinctae; pori omnino aperti rotundati vel ovali. Scapus erectus, apice 7 mm diametro, glaber; scapi bracteis subfoliaceis sed integris, erectis, dense imbricatis. Inflorescentia e racemis ca 15, laxe pinnata, 36 cm longa, glabra; bracteis primariis anguste triangularibus quam ramorum basibus nudis brevioribus; ramis simplicibus, rectis, divergentibus, ad 12 cm longis, sub- dense multifloris, eorum basibus nudis ad 4 cm longis. Bracteae florigerae triangulares, ca 2 mm longae, basi incrassatae, apice membranaceae; pedicellis divergentibus, gracilibus, 8 mm longis; fto- ribus atro-roseis. Sepala elliptica, 5 mm longa, membranacea, paucinervata; petalis ellipticis, late rotundatis, 12 mm longis, stamina superantibus; stylo gracili; ovario ellipsoideo; ovulis caudatis.

description: A strikingly beautiful species because of the thick leaves, dark above and paler below, the dark branchlets with the sturdy short shoots bearing a large rich infloreseence with numerous long-peduncled umbels, from the centre of which at the tip of each brachypod occurs a long slender densely tawny sericeous bud. Each bract is linear-lanceolate, densely pubescent without, glabrous and dark brown within. The bracts subtending the umbels are four in number, ovate, pubescent without, and deciduous at anthesis.

description: At first glance, the [female] and [male] trees of this species seem to differ in leaf characters. Although number 26 was collected only two days before number 31, the former seems to be in an earlier stage of development. The lower surface of the leaf of number 31, viewed under the microscope, shows the glaucous character to be due to minute droplets, perhaps crystallized, exuded from the leaf surface and adhering so closely that they form a dense covering. In number 26, these droplets are flatter, less dense and not whitish in color, hence the lack of glaucousiiess on the lower leaf surface of this number. Both specimens are sparsely covered with pubescence along the nerves beneath.

description: Shrubs 1.5-2.0 m high. Stems terete, densely puberulent to glabrate. Leaves penninervate, mostly 3 at a node (rarely 2 or 4 to a node on the same plant); petioles 6-24 mm long; blades narrowly to broadly lanceolate, 7-12 cm long, 1.5-4.5 cm wide, acute to somewhat rounded at the base, the apices acuminate, moderately to densely puberulent beneath, the trichomes mostly 0.5-1.0 mm long. Stipules connate, forming a somewhat scarious tube 4-8 mm high, the rim with slender appendages 4-10 mm long. Inflorescence a terminal cyme with numerous flowers on slender puberulent pedicels 8-12 mm long. Calyx 4-6 mm long, the lobes narrowly lanceolate, free, puberulent. Corolla bright red, narrowly to broadly tubular, 15-22 mm long, 2.5-5.5 mm wide, glabrous without, densely puberulent within near the base, the lobes ca 3 mm long, erect or nearly so. Stamens inserted, the anthers 2-3 mm long. Style exserted for 1-3 mm. Capsule puberulent, ca 6 mm wide, 3-4 mm high. Seeds immature.

description: Frutex volubilis, caulibus, teretibus, dense adpresso-pubescentibus, pilis brunneis. description: Herbaceous vine; stem terete, densely pubescent with appressed golden-brown trichomes. Leaves petiolate, the petiole 1.3-1.6 cm long, subquadrangular, densely appressed-pilose with golden-brown trichomes, the blade elliptic to ovate, 6-7 cm long, 4.5-6 cm broad, subobtuse and mucronate, the mucro about 2 mm long, rounded at base, firm, entire, the upper surface sparingly puberulous, the trichomes 1.5 mm long, more or less curved, the lower surface yellowish and densely and softly tomentose, the trichomes to 0.75 mm long, the costa and lateral veins (4 or 5 pairs) very prominent, the veinlets of the lower surface reticulate, the venation of the upper surface inconspicuous. Flowers axillary, 1 to several in each axil; pedicels 2.5-3.5 cm long, 1 mm broad at base, gradually enlarged to 2 mm at tip, terete, densely tomentose with soft, fine, brownish trichomes to 2 mm long; bracts oblong-ovate, 2-2.4 cm long, 1.1-1.3 cm broad, rounded and mucronate, the mucro about 1 mm long but obscured by the dense tomentose pubescence covering the outer surface of the bracts, the trichomes soft, yellowish-brown, about 2 mm long, the costa obscure, the inner surface of the bracts glabrous; calyx yellowish- brown, annular, subhyaline, 1.5 mm high, equalling the disc; corolla bright red, glabrous, 2.8 cm long, 5 mm broad at base, narrowed to 2.5 mm at 7 mm above base, then enlarged to 5 mm at throat, the lobes erect, obovate, 3.5 mm long, 2.5-3 mm broad, rounded or shallowly emarginate; pollen grain brevissimicolpate, prolate spheroidal, 41 x 35 ,um, sexine punctitegillate (Fig. 2B). Drupe not seen.

description: Frutex volubilis, caulibus subquadrangularibus, obscure sulcatis, glabris vel ad nodos parce adpresso- pubescentibus. description: Vine; stems subquadrangular, obscurely sulcate, glabrous or sparingly pubescent at or near the nodes, the trichomes straight, closely appressed, 0.5 mm long. Leaves petiolate, the petiole 2-3.5 cm long, subquadrangular, glabrous or sparingly hirsute, the trichomes similar to those of the leaf blades, the blade oblong-ovate, widest near the middle, 10-12 cm long and 4.5-5.5 cm broad, the tip abruptly acuminate (the tip itself blunt and terminating in a mucro 2.5-3 mm long) rounded to obtuse at base, firm, entire or undulate, both surfaces glabrous except the costa and lateral veins (3 or 4 pairs), the costa minutely strigose, the veins sparingly so or with the trichomes sometimes spreading or ascending, all of the trichomes straight, rigid and to 0.25 mm long, the venation of both surfaces rather obscure, the upper surface of the blades bearing inconspicuous straight, angled or sometimes stellate cystoliths, the lower surface of the blades minutely and inconspic- uously rugose. Flowers axillary, solitary or in pairs; pedicels 2-2.5 cm long, slender, glabrous or sparingly strigose toward base, grooved; bracts ovate to oblong-ovate, 2.5-3.2 cm long and 1.5-1.8 cm broad, rounded or obtuse at apex and tipped by a mucro 1 mm long, rounded at the base, green, thick, minutely muricate both within and without, the costa faint, sparingly strigose, glandular within; calyx annular, subhyaline, 1.5 mm high, equalling the disc; corolla cream-white with purple streaks in throat, glabrous, 4.5 cm long, 5 mm broad at base, narrowed 15 mm above base to 3.5 mm, thence enlarged to 12 mm at throat, the limb oblique, the lobes rounded, about 7-8 mm long and broad; pollen grain brevis- simicolpate, prolate spheroidal, 57 x 49 Aim, sexine punctitegillate (Fig. 2A). Drupe not seen.

description: Vine; young stem subcylindrical, appressed-pubescent, the trichomes 1.5-2 mm long, the internodes soon mostly glabrate. Leaves with petiole 1-3 cm long, appressed-pubescent; blades ovate to ovate lanceolate, 8.5-13 cm long, 4-9 cm wide, apically abruptly acuminate, the tip terminating in a mucro 2-2.5 mm long, basally acute to obtuse, adaxial surface glabrescent, with ascending trichomes arising from stellate base, abaxial surface hirsute, with trichomes 1-2 mm long, the venation prominent beneath, secondary veins coarsely reticulate. Flowers axillary, 2 or 4 in each axil; pedicels 1-2 cm long, densely hirsute, with yellowish brown trichomes 3.5-5 mm long; bracteoles lanceolate, 2.5-3.5 cm long, 0.8-1.4 cm wide, short-mucronate at apex, ciliate, the outer surface hirsute, with trichomes similar in color and length to those of the pedicels, the inner surface glabrous; calyx cupular, subhyaline, 2.5 mm long; corolla white with purple stripes internally in throat, glabrous, 4.5-5 cm long, 1 cm broad at throat, the upper lip the lobes subequal, oblong, 6-7.5 mm long, 8 mm wide, shallowly emarginate at apex, the lower lip with rounded lobes, 10 mm long, 8 mm wide; ovary with glandular tri- chomes, ca. 3 mm long, 2.5 mm diam., the style to 3.7 cm long, the stigma unequally lobed. Drupe green (immature) subglobose, oblique at apex, ca. 1.7 cm long, glabrous.

description: Vine; young stem cylindrical, densely pubescent, the trichomes fine, soft, eglandular, 1.5-2.5 mm long, near the internodes sparsely pubescent to glabrate. Leaves with petioles 1-2.5 cm long; blades oblanceo- late, 6-9.5 cm long, 3-5.5 cm wide, api- cally acuminate, the apiculate tip ca. 2.5 mm long, basally acute, adaxial surface pubescent, with curved, appressed or ascending trichomes arising from a stellate base, abaxial surface especially the costa and lateral veins densely pubescent, the veinlets of the lower surface reticulate. Flowers 2-4 in each axil; pedicels 1-1.7 cm long, villous, the trichomes brown, straight, appressed, 2- 3 mm long; bracteoles linear-lanceolate, 2- 2.5 cm long, 0.5-0.8 cm wide, mucronate at apex, ciliate with antrorse-flexuose trichomes, just abutting at margins, the outer surface villous especially on the costa, the inner surface glabrous; calyx cupular, subhyaline, 2.5 mm long; corolla white, glabrous, 3-4 cm long, 5 mm broad at the throat, the lobes subcircular, 4-5 mm long and broad, rounded; ovary with glandular trichomes, 5 mm long, 3 mm diam., the style to 3.5 cm long, the stigma unequally lobed. Drupe green (immature), oblong, 1.5-1.7 cm long, glabrous.

description: Vine, the stems sparsely puberulent to glabrous, the older stems corky; leaves petiolate, the petiole 1.8-3.5 cm long, the blades subcoriaceous to firmly membranous, narrowly elliptic, 9-16 cm long, 2.5-7 cm wide, apex long acuminate, base acute to obtuse, rarely rounded, glabrous above, densely and shortly pilose to rarely glabrous below, with 2 glands at the base of the upper surface, the secondary nerves 7-11 eachside; inflorescence subaxillary, 1-4-flowered, the peduncle 2.5-8 cm long, sparsely puberulent; sepals narrowly ovate, lanceolate or oblong, obtuse, 7-11 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, inconspicuously appressed-pilose with a gland in each sinus; corolla rotate, 28-32 mm diam., the petals broadly obovate, rounded and emarginate at apex, 10-13 mm long, 7-11 mm wide, short puberulent without, glabrous within, conspicuously brown-venose; gynostegium 3.6-4.2 mm long; anthers subtriangular, 2 mm long, 1.7 mm wide at apex, dorsally concave; corona fleshy, annular, 5-lobed, the lobes opposite the anthers, 2 mm long, 2.5 mm wide; pollinia more or less pendulous, narrowly pyriform, 1.4-1.5 mm long; corpusculum sagittate, 0.4 mm long, 0.84 mm wide; fruit unknown.

description: Volubilis; rami hirsuti et pulverulenti, grisei; folia (petiolo 1.3-2.3 cm longo, densissime glandulari-piloso et pilis paucis patentibus hirsuto), hastata, 3-5.5 cm longa, basi 1.3-2.5 cm lata, basi profunde cordata, bilobata, lobis rotundatis, 2 cm supra basin contracta, deinde oblonga, 8-12 mm lata, apice mucronata, nervo medio utrinque prominulo, lateralibus utroque latere 3-4, vel obsoletis, utrinque pilosula, subtus pallida, membranacea, margine plana; flores axillares solitarii, pedicellis 3-10 mm longis, glanduloso-pilosulis et hirsutis; sepala lanceolata, 3-4 mm longa, acuminata, hirsuta; corolla subrotata, lobis lanceolatis, 10-12 mm longis, 4 mm latis, extus glanduloso-pilosis, longit dinaliter 10-nervis; corona annularis, 10-lobata, lobis subulatis, 2 mm longis glabris; gynostegium depressum, 3 mm diam., antheris incurvis; pollinia oblique obovata, compressa, 0.8 mm longa, translatoribus subnullis, retinaculo triangulari, nitido, brunneo, 0.4 mm longo; follicula oblongo-lanceolata, 5-6 mm longa, 1.5-2 cm lata, longe acuminata, tuberculis filiformibus 6-8 mm longis, 1.5-2 mm latis obtecta; semina obovata apice rotundata basi abrupte angustata, margine incrassata 5 mm longa, 2 mm lata, lana usque 2 cm longa.

description: Cauliflorous trees 20 m tall or taller with trunk 6 dm diam at 6 m from ground but divided proximally into as many as 25 stilts 1-3 dm diam, glabrous throughout, the foliage dull olivaceous concolorous, the lax racemes arising both from trunks and from defoliate annotinous and older branches. Stipules not seen. Leaf-stalks 4-4.5 cm, the one interfoliolar segment +/- 27 mm, the ventral groove open, slightly widened distally. Leaflets 2 pairs, the distal pair longer; pulvinules 2-2.5 mm; blades elliptic-acumi- nate from broadly cuneate, subequilateral base, the distal pair attaining +/- 11 x 3-4 cm, the straight, centric midrib and fine secondary venation almost immersed. Raceme-axis 5-15 cm; bracts caducous (none seen); pedicels +/- 9-11 mm; bracteoles broadly oblanceolate obtuse 9-11 x 5-6 mm, separating nearly to base on each side; hypanthium +/- 7.5 x 1.5 mm; petal oblong- elliptic exunguiculate +/- 38 x 19 mm, elaborately undulate marginally, thinly pilosulous near and below middle; filaments +/- 3 cm, pilosulous at base; gynoecium arising from rim of hypenthium, the gynophore 5-6.5 mm, a little longer than the glabrous ovary. Fruit unknown.

description: The plants of this species are usually semiterrestrial, growing in shallow water or on mud. They are delicate, up to about 25 cm tall, and have light green stems rising from a rhizomatous base (Fig. 1 C, F). The leaves are opposite or in whorls of three, 1-8 mm long, linear or lanceolate in outline, and entire or pinnate with 1-3 pairs of segments. The leaf segments, especially those of the upper leaves, are often reduced to small stubs with swollen red callosities at the tips. The lower submerged leaves on semiterrestrial plants, and most of the leaves on aquatic plants, are in whorls of three and are pinnate, broadly ovate in outline, and have 2-4 (7) alternate segments on each side. The tip of the leaf rachis in submerged leaves is often bent in the direction opposite to that of the last segment and the whole leaf seems to be evenly pinnate (Fig. 1J). Both stem and leaves have numerous multicellular "myriophyllin" glands. Myriophyllum ussuriense has filiform winter buds (Fig. 1D) that consist of small narrow bundles of leaves developed in the leaf axils.

description: Shrub; stems woody, erect, to 1 m tall, 5 mm in diameter 30 cm from apex, internodes brown to reddish, pilose-hirsute. Leaves nearly equal in a pair; blades lanceolate, ovate to obovate, oblique, 4.2-9.3 cm long, 1.8-3.9 cm wide, membranous, the apex acute to acuminate, the base acute to cuneate, the margins serrulate, above dark green, covered with more or less erect uniseriate trichomes of 2 lengths, below lighter green or reddish, strigose along the prominent veins; petioles densely pilose, 0.5-1.8 cm long. Inflorescences axillary, of single flowers; peduncles, when present, slender to 1.5 cm long; bracts often caducous, linear, to 1.8 cm long, reddish, pilose, rarely bearing an undeveloped flower in the axil; pedicels slender, 0.3-1.5 cm long, elongat- ing in fruit, reddish, pilose. Flowers with the floral tube conic or oblong, 3-5 mm long, 3 mm in diameter, the veins prominent, densely pilose; calyx 5-lobed, lobes connate for only 1-2 mm above the flora tube, each narrowly triangular, ca 1.8 cm long, 2-3 mm wide at the base, the apex acuminate, the lower lobes prominently toothed on the apical half, the lateral lobes toothed on only one side (lower) or on both, the upper lobe entire or rarely toothed, outside pilose, inside sparsely pilose; corolla deep red, tubular, slightly curved, 4 cm long, 5-7 mm wide at the base, ventricose at the middle, ca 1.4 cm wide, narrowing to ca 1 cm in diameter at the throat, outside densely pubescent, inside glandular, limb 5-lobed, spreading, each lobe suborbicular, ca 5 mm long and wide, the margins toothed; stamens 4, with a staminode 5 mm long, not exserted, the filaments adnate to base of corolla for 1 mm, free part ca 3.5 cm long, coiling after anthesis, the yellow base sericeous, glabrescent above, the anthers suborbicular, joined in two pairs by their sides, ca 2 mm long and wide; disc annular, ca 1 mm long; ovary apex broadly conic, densely pilose; style curved, ca 4 cm long, pilose, more sparse toward the apex, stigma stomatomorphic, ca 1 mm wide. Fruit a dry capsule, splitting into two valves, ellipsoid-oblong, 1.2-1.7 cm long, 6-10 mm wide, the veins prominent; seeds numerous, fusiform, ca 0.5 mm long, striate, twisted, dark reddish brown.
