description: Small creeping epiphytic plants, the rhizome slender, apparently unbranched, 10 cm long or perhaps longer, closely covered with scarious, infundibuliform, apiculate, sheathing bracts which persist for some time; stems lateral on the rhizomes, terete, unifoliate, covered with bracts like those of the rhizome, 4-5 mm long; leaves one from each stem, elliptic, bi- or triapiculate at the apex,15-20 mm long and 4- mm broad; inflorescence subterminal on the stem, solitary; peduncle filiform, terete, with a searious, infundibuliform, apiculate bract above the middle and another subtending the single flower, usually with a short ligule (3-4 mm long) from the base of the flower; flowers solitary, greenish yellow; perianth parts all obscurely serrulate and ocellate; dorsal sepal oval or obovate, short caudate-acuminate, obscurely 3-nerved, about 10 mm long and 4.5 mm broad; lateral sepals connate into one, oval or broadly ovate, short caudate-acuminate, 5-nerved, about 12 mm long and 6 mm broad; petals essentially oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, subauriculate near the base on the lower side and near the middle on the upper side; labellum very small, transversely subquadrate, trilobate with the mid-lobe retuse and the laterals somewhat falcate, with a small, transverse, furfuraceous callus plate near the base of the lamina, about 1.5 mm long and 2.5 mm broad when spread; ovary about 5 mm long in flower, in fruit about 10 mm long.

description: Unarmed, eglandular, amply foliate shrubs, thinly minutely puberulent throughout and the leaf-axes and inflorescence in addition charged with reddish granular trichomes, the dull olivaceous leaflets mem- branous, paler beneath, the inflorescence a terminal panicle of axillary spiciform racemes. Stipules caducous (few observed) oblanceolate +5-12 mm, 1-nerved. Leaf- formula v-vii/9-1 1; leafstalks 6-10 cm, the petiole 1-2 cm, the longer interpinnal segments nearly as long; a slender spicule (to 1 mm) between the proximal and often be- tween further pinnae; pinnae distally accrescent, the rachis of penultimate pair ±5- 7 cm, the longer interfoliolar segments ? 1- 6 mm; paraphyllidia minute, deciduous; pulvinules green, not wrinkled, 0.4-0.5 mm; leaflets a little distally accrescent, opposite, the blades elliptic to oblong-obovate from semicordate base, broadly obtuse, the larger ones 10-22 X 4.5-7.5 mm, +2-3 times as long as wide; venation faint, of 3 - 4 primary nerves from pulvinule, the mid- rib displaced to divide blade ?1:2. Peduncles solitary or 2-3 per node, the axis together with that of raceme 4-8 cm; bracts linear-oblanceolate, <1.5 mm, caducous; pedicels 0.3-0.5 mm; perianth 5-merous, silky-puberulent overall, the corolla lavender; calyx turbinate-campanulate 1.2 mm, the deltate teeth scarcely 0.4 mm; corolla vase-shaped 3.8 mm, the lobes 1.1 umm; androecium 10-merous, the free filaments ±8.5 mm; gynoecium shortly stipitate, the ovary velutinous, 4-6-ovulate, the style linear filiform. description: Plantae minores, foliis inflorescentiisque glabris. Ramuli omnino furfuracei, leviter quadrangulares, sympodialiter ramosi. description: Rather small plants with glabrous leaves and inflorescences, twigs entirely furfuraceous and slightly quadrangular, branching sympodial, lateral branches and inflorescences emerging from conspicuous axillary craters, branches apparently lacking epicortical roots. Phyllotaxy decussate. Leaves thin, elliptical, to 4 x 2 cm plus petiole of about 3 mm, leaf margin somewhat callosed, venation evident, palmate, apex rounded, base tapering into petiole. Inflorescence 1 per axil, 4-8- flowered, less than 1 cm long when in flower but elongating to 2 or 3 cm in fruit. Flowers bisexual, hexamerous, subtended by 1 bract and 2 bracteoles each, 3 mm long, calyculus smooth or nearly so, petals 2 mm long, dimorphic, anthers on very short filaments which extend downwards as a ridge, at 2 different heights, the upper ones pressed against petal tips above and against lower anthers below; all anthers with prominent, deltoid connective and four minute pollen sacs with very few pollen grains. Style less than 2 mm long, straight, stigma undifferentiated. Fruit ellipsoid, 10 x 5 mm, calyculus inconspicuous; embryo slender, 6 mm long, 4 mm of which consists of 2 narrow cotyledons; radicular pole with papillate protuberances.

description: Dioecious, glabrous shrub with rather straight and stout branches which are terete or very slightly angular, the surface becoming grey-brown with numerous small, round lenticels. Branching sympodial by apical abortion, each season's growth consisting of up to 10 internodes, all but the lowest node fertile. Phyllotaxy decussate; leaves up to 5 x 2.5 cm in the pistillate plants but somewhat wider and shorter in the staminate plants, broadly lanceolate to obovate; apex acute to obtuse, the base acute to cuneate; petiole 2-5 mm long; venation palmate to pinnate when seen from above, all but the midrib obscure when seen from below. Inflorescence an in- determinate spike, sessile or nearly so, always single in the leaf axil, with decussating pairs of scale leaves which are conspicuously hyaline-margined; staminate spike up to 3 cm long, with up to 30 pairs of fertile scales; pistillate spike up to 2 cm long with ca. 16 pairs of fertile scales; in both sexes even the lowest scales floriferous, and each flower subtended by two 1 x 1.5 mm, blunt-tipped, naviculate bracteoles with heavy keels. Staminate flower slightly more than 2 mm long, hexamerous, both petals and stamens strongly dimorphic; upper anthers above and the lower anthers below middle of petals, both with 4 pollen-sacs and dorsifixed filaments; connective forming a projecting triangle rimmed with white papillate hairs; filament buttress pronounced on long stamens only; style prominent, straight and angled, the stigma conical, finely papillate. Pollen smooth, triangular-rounded, lacking any evident surface features. Pistillate flower slightly less than 2 mm long, hexamerous, petals and staminodes dimorphic, with filaments and aborted pollen sacs distinct; style ca. 1 mm long, compressed-hexagonal, with a dark, papillate, 3-lobed stigma; nectary smooth. Calyculus minutely dentate. Fruit smooth, elliptical, 7 x 3 mm, endo- spermous, with a 6 mm long, green embryo, the 2 cotyledons nearly 5 mm long and 1 mm wide, the haustorial end only slightly swollen.

description: Cespitose perennial herb, 1-2.5 (3.2) dm tall, few to several flowering stems from a simple or branched caudex, arising from a thick woody taproot, the caudex thick and densely clothed in old leaf bases; herbage completely glabrous or often the basal leaves sparsely ciliate with a few minute, broad-based hairs; flowering stems erect, occasionally branched at about the midlength, but typically unbranched; leaves basal and cauline, the basal leaves erect, rigid, rosulate, petiolate, the petiole narrowly winged and broadening at the base, 2-6 cm long, 3-6.5 mm wide, oblanceolate, often narrowly so, gradually tapered into the petiole, entire, acute apically, pinnately veined, the lateral veins divaricately ascending, the cauline leaves few, smaller, narrowly lanceolate to linear, sessile, entire, acute, ascending, with nearly obscure par- allel lateral veins; raceme compact in flower, elongating in fruit, glabrous; sepals 1.7- 2.5 mm long, ovate, obtuse to rounded, scarious margined, not saccate at the base, glabrous, often purplish; petals white, 2.8- 4 mm long, spatulate to clawed with an ob- ovate blade, rounded apically; stamens, the lateral shorter with filiform filaments, the median with slightly dilated filaments abruptly tapered to a narrow apex, the anthers 0.4-0.6 mm long, oval; nectar glands confluent around the bases of all the stamens; fruiting pedicels, the lower 3-9 mm long, slender, slightly flattened with narrowly winged margins, more or less straight, ascending, sometimes appressed to the rachis; siliques ascending to erect, 7-20 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, linear to narrowly fusiform or lanceolate, tapering at both ends, terete or slightly flattened parallel to the septum, torulose, straight or barely curved, weakly 1-few nerved in the proximal 1/4-1/2, the septum complete, transpar- ent; mature style 0.1-0.4 mm long, the stigma small, slightly broader than the style, entire; seeds uniseriate, 1-3 in each locule, 2-2.8 mm long, narrowly oblong, brown, not mucilaginous when wet, the cotyledons incumbent, the radical exceeding the cotyledons at the funicular end; 2n = 14.

description: Cespitose perennial herb, the caudex simple or branched, thickly clothed in old leaf bases; herbage glabrous or the leaves often ciliate with minute, simple hairs; leaves rigid, basal and cauline, the basal rosulate, petiolate, the blades oblanceolate, entire, the cauline leaves few, sessile, linear, entire; inflorescence an ebracteate raceme; sepals 4, not saccate; petals 4, spatulate to clawed, white; stamens 6; fruiting pedicels ascending, sometimes appressed to the rachis; fruit a dehiscent, nonstipitate, linear or narrowly fusiform silique, subterete to slightly flattened parallel to the septum, the valves weakly nerved below; mature style short, the stigma capitate; seeds uniseriate, 2-6, not mucilaginous when wet, the cotyledons incumbent; 2n = 14.

description: Herba decumbens, in scopulo verticali crescens; folia pendentia, 4-12 plo longiora quam latiora, subsessilia, margine ciliata, in dimidio distali serrata; inflorescentia pendens; bracteae et bracteolae minutae; corolla candida; stamina 4, staminodium parvum, anthera sterili.
bibliographicCitation: Feuillet, Christian P. G. & Skog, Laurence E. 2002. Novae Gesneriaceae Neotropicarum XII. New species of Gesneriaceae from the Guianas. Brittonia. 54: 352-361.

description: Herbs saxicolous, decumbent. Stems 5- 25 cm long, semiwoody, pendent, terete, unbranched, light brown, glabrous or with a few scattered long hairs, the young parts usually hidden by the persistent bases of fallen leaves, anchored to vertical cliffs by a few strong adventitious roots. Leaves opposite, crowded in a rosette at stem apex, variable in size following a gradient from longer pendent to shorter erect laminae, subsessile, very brittle when fresh (Granville 6718); blade thin, linear to narrow-oblanceolate, 4-25 X 0.5-2.5 cm; margin ciliate, serrate to obscurely serrate in distal half, with tips of teeth hardened (glandular?); apex acute to acuminate; base linear, densely cobwebby at the very base; adaxial side green, with sparse long hairs; abaxial side pale green or purplish, with sparse short hairs mostly appressed; petiole very short or lacking. Inflorescences more or less perpendicular to rosette at their bases, then curving upward, pedunculate, cymose, 2-many-flowered; peduncles slender, 5-15 cm long, with scattered long hairs to glabrescent; bracts linear, 4 X 0.2 mm, with long dense hairs to glabrescent on same plant; secondary rachis 4-6 cm long, with scattered hairs to glabrescent; bracteoles similar to bracts, but about half the size; pedicels 1-3 cm, glabrescent. Calyx actinomorphic; lobes free nearly to base, lanceolate, 5-6 X 1 mm, entire, the apices acute, the tips hard- ened (glandular?), with short hairs present outside, glabrous inside, with a midrib and a network of veinules. Corolla erect, pre- sumably white; tube 4-5 mm long; lobes wide-lanceolate; margin entire; apex round (possibly slightly emarginate); stamens 4, attached to base of corolla; filaments short and stout, 0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers sagittate, 0.6 X 0.5 mm; staminode small, with sterile anther (L. C. Richard, 1781- 1785, in sched.); nectary lacking; ovary globose, 2 X 1.2 mm, glabrous; style 3-3.5 mm long, glabrous; stigma navicular, barely swollen if at all. Capsule pale brown, ovoid, apiculate, with persistent style, 2 X 1.2 mm, glabrous, dehiscing loculicidally and septicidally into 4 valves, leaving the 2 placentae at the ends of a horseshoe-shaped structure; seeds ellipsoid, 0.3-0.4 X 0.1-0.2 mm, dark brown.
bibliographicCitation: Feuillet, Christian P. G. & Skog, Laurence E. 2002. Novae Gesneriaceae Neotropicarum XII. New species of Gesneriaceae from the Guianas. Brittonia. 54: 352-361.

description: Leaves with blades 3-14 cm long, 2-13 cm wide, chartaceous, ovate to elliptic, green adaxially and often mottled with reddish brown or purple especially on young leaves, green to dull purple abaxially, with raised veins, the sinus mostly shorter than midrib, the lobes overlapping to divergent, with apices acute to rounded. Flowers 3- 7.5 cm diam.; sepals with lines of insertion on receptacle straight, forming prominent tetragon; petals 10-17, acute to rounded at apex; stamens 30-70, yellow-orange, the inner often suffused with purple abaxially, the filaments distinctly widest above the middle and abruptly narrowed to base; carpels 5-10, the appendages (2) 3-4 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, cymbiform, purple tipped abaxially, the stigmatic rays purple. Chromosome number 2n = 112.
bibliographicCitation: Wiersema, John H. 1996. Nymphaea tetragona and Nymphaea leibergii (Nymphaeaceae): Two species of diminutive water-lilies in North America. Brittonia. 48: 520-531.

description: Stems reddish in new growth, pale green to yellowish in mature growth, striate, conspicuously resinous and rough in new growth. Petiole sulcate, 7-10 mm long, 1.5-3 mm diam, green, muriculate; blade dark green above, pale green below, narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, 2-12 cm long, 0.5-3.3 cm wide, subcoriaceous, base cuneate, apex acute, attenuate, mucronate, margins subsinuate. Inflorescence racemose or spicate, bearing flowers on proximal nodes and vegetative short shoots on distal nodes; rachis to 16 cm long, 1.5-4 mm diam, angled, resinous, rough, internodes to 7 mm long; flowers initially subsessile, later pedicellate; pedicels erect, extending to 6 mm during maturation, 0.5-1 mm in diam, resinous and minutely crusty, subtended by linear, herbaceous bract to 3 mm long, 1 mm wide; tepals subequal, ovate or broadly elliptic, often concave, 3-7 mm long, 2- 4 mm wide, subcoriaceous, apices obtuse or acute, margins entire; stamens 7, in a single series, 1-2 mm long, glabrous, anthers yellow, ellipsoid, 0.5-1 mm long; gynophore about 0.5 mm long during aestivation, extending to 3 mm during anthesis, ca 0.5 mm diam, striate, minutely crusty; ovary green, fleshy, obpyri- form; carpels 9, ovules 1 per carpel, reniform; styles 9, erect, filiform, ca 1 mm long, terminal on each carpel, basally connate. Maturing fruit a 9-ribbed berry, green, obpyriform, to 7 mm long, 5 mm wide, smooth or minutely papillose along crests of ribs; seeds 9, narrowly ellipsoid, to 2 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Martínez, J. G. & McDonald, J. A. 1989. Nowickea (Phytolaccaceae), a new genus with two species from Mexico. Brittonia. 41 (4): 399-403.

description: Stems pale green, scarcely striate, smooth, glabrous. Petiole sulcate, 5-15 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, green, smooth or rough; blade green above, pale green below, narrowly elliptic, 2.5-7.5 cm long, 1-2 cm wide, chartaceous, base cuneate, apex acuminate or attenuate, mucronate, margins entire. Inflorescence racemose; rachis to 25 cm long, 1-3 mm diam, angled, smooth, glabrous, internodes to 5 mm long; pedicels ascending, 2-12 mm long, to 0.3 mm diam, pale green, smooth, glabrous, subtended by a single variable bract; bracts green, herbaceous, lanceolate, to 16 mm long during anthesis, 3 mm wide, apex acute, occasionally red pigmented, punctate, chartaceous, glabrous; tepals unequal, herbaceous, elliptic to narrowly spatulate, 5-12 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, subcoriaceous, punctate, apices obtuse or acute, often concave; stamens 12-16, subequal, in a single series, 2-4 mm long, hyaline, glabrous, anthers yellow, ellipsoid, 0.5-1 mm long; gynophore extending to 12 mm during anthesis, ca 0.5 mm diam, smooth, glabrous; ovary green, fleshy, obovate, to 3 mm long, 3 mm thick; carpels 7-9, ovules 1 per carpel, a single style terminating each carpel, erect, filiform, ca 0.5 mm long. Maturing fruit a 7- 9-lobed berry, obovate.
bibliographicCitation: Martínez, J. G. & McDonald, J. A. 1989. Nowickea (Phytolaccaceae), a new genus with two species from Mexico. Brittonia. 41 (4): 399-403.

description: Rhizoma erectum, tuberosum, tantum sub germinatione stolones producens. Folia late elliptico- ovata vel suborbicularia, apice truncato vel plerumque mucronulata obtusangulata, integerrima, glabra, supra viridia nitida, maculis purpureis ubique sparsa, in siccis speciminibus punctis elevatis densis et lineolis elevatis brevioribus non ramosis ex sclereidibus interioribus omata, venatione in centro folii radiata et manifesta; petioli glabri. Flores natantes v. emersi, noctumi, sepalis cum petalis et staminibus extemis in verticillis tetrameris; sepala viridia vel ex purpureo brunnea, maculis nullis; petala 16 v. 20, alba, sclereidibus acicularibus interioribus nullis, tria cycli extemi ceteris latiora, petalis extemorum cyclorum ovato-oblonga, in cyclo intimo lanceolata, gradatim in stamina transeuntia; stamina 53-132, ebumea, sclereidibus acicularibus interioribus nullis, extema apiculis brevibus 1 mm superantibus; carpella 15-32, processubus coccineis, cylindro-clavatis, 5-9 mm longis, 0.7-1.5 mm crassis.
bibliographicCitation: Wiersema, John H. 1984. Systematics of Nymphaea subgenus Hydrocallis (Nymphaeaceae). I. Four new species from the neotropics. Brittonia. 36: 213-222.

description: Rhizome erect, ovoid, tuberous, stolon-forming only when germinating. Leaf blades subcoriaceous to almost skinlike in texture, broadly elliptic-ovate to sub- orbicular, to 24 cm long, to 21 cm wide, 1.05-1.25 times as long as wide, entire, truncate or more frequently obtuse-mucronulate at apex, peltate 2 mm or less from base of sinus, the sinus 0.36-0.46 times length of blade, the lobes obtuse to rounded with slight protuberance; upper surface glossy green with numerous purple flecks evident on younger leaves, when dried usually with numerous tiny prominences and short elevated lines from underlying trichosclereids and acicular sclereids; undersurface brownish purple, with dark flecks especially evident on younger leaves, glabrous; venation radiate and manifest centrally, faintly reticulate toward margin, the principal veins 13-22. Petioles to 5 mm in diam, glabrous, with 2-4 major air canals and 6-8 minor ones. Peduncles to 7.5 mm in diam, glabrous, with 5, 6, 15, or 18 major air canals. Flowers floating or slightly emergent, opening nocturnally, with sepals, petals, and outermost stamens in distinct whorls of 4; sepals uniformly green or somewhat brownish purple, ovate, 3-6 cm long, 1.1-3.4 cm wide, acute to somewhat rounded at apex, impregnated with acicular sclereids, the nerves slightly evident basally; petals 16 or 20, white, lacking scler- eids, those of the 3 outer whorls broader than inner and oblong-ovate, the outermost shorter than sepals and acute, those of the inner whorls lanceolate, 2.5- 3.5 cm long, 0.7-1.4 cm wide, acuminate; transition to stamens gradual; stamens 53-132, cream-colored, lacking sclereids, the outermost to 3.2 cm long, with filaments to 12 mm wide and connectives prolonged ca 1 mm or more beyond anthers, the inner with filaments sometimes slightly purplish at base, to 1.1 mm wide, and with connectives prolonged to 0.7 mm beyond anthers, the inner anthers 0.6-0.9 times as long as stamen; carpels 15-32, the appendages deep crimson, cylindric-clavate, 5-9 mm long, 0.7-1.5 mm in diam, with apex slightly incurved and somewhat apiculate; stigmatic rays not impregnated with acicular sclereids, the papillae cells separating into powdery mass; axial process acute or blunt. Fruits normally present; seeds 0.80-1.00 mm long, 0.55-0.75 mm in diam, 1.3-1.6 times as long as broad, finely granulate, with longitudinal rows of hairs 20-90 µm long.
bibliographicCitation: Wiersema, John H. 1984. Systematics of Nymphaea subgenus Hydrocallis (Nymphaeaceae). I. Four new species from the neotropics. Brittonia. 36: 213-222.

description: Rhizoma erectum, tuberosum, tantum sub germinatione stolones producens. Folia elliptico-ovata vel suborbicularia, integerrima, glabra, supra viridia, in siccis speciminibus punctis elevatis densis- simus ex trichosclereidibus interioribus omata. Flores natantes, noctumi, sepalis cum petalis extemis in verticillis tetrameris; sepala viridia vel ex purpureo viridia, plerumque maculis brevibus linearibus nigris sparsa; petala 19-35, alba vel ebumea, extema sepalis aequilonga vel longiora, et subaequilata vel latiora; gradatim in stamina transeuntia; stamina 99-248, ebumea, intema ex purpureo vel indigotico ebumea; carpella 20-39, processubus purpureis vel indigoticis, clavatis, 6-15 mm longis, supeme 0.6-1.9 mm crassis. Fructus nunquam observati, propagatione asexuali per flores submersos abortivos tuberiferos.
bibliographicCitation: Wiersema, John H. 1984. Systematics of Nymphaea subgenus Hydrocallis (Nymphaeaceae). I. Four new species from the neotropics. Brittonia. 36: 213-222.

description: Rhizome erect, ovoid to cylindric, tuberous, stolon-forming only when ger- minating. Leaf blades elliptic-ovate to suborbicular, to 22 (30) cm long, to 21 (29) cm wide, 1.0-1.25 times as long as wide, entire, rounded to somewhat obtuse-angled at apex, peltate 1-10 mm from base of sinus, the sinus 0.34-0.45 times length of blade, the lobes slightly tapering to broadly rounded; upper surface green, often flecked with purple, when dried densely covered with tiny prominences from underlying trichosclereids, lacking acicular sclereids; undersurface green or purple- tinged with dark flecks, glabrous; venation radiate and slightly raised centrally, becoming reticulate toward margins, the principal veins 13-19. Petioles to 6 mm in diam, glabrous, with 8 major air canals and 12 minor ones. Peduncles to 7.5 mm in diam, glabrous, usually with 6 or 18 major air canals and 12 or 24 minor ones. Flowers floating, opening nocturnally, sepals and outer petals in distinct whorls of 4; sepals green, sometimes suffused with purple, usually with short black streaks, ovate, 2.5-7.5 cm long, 1.3-3.2 cm wide, rounded at apex, lacking acicular sclereids, the nerves only faintly evident; petals 19-35, creamy-white, lacking acicular sclereids, the outer mostly equalling or longer and somewhat narrower to broader than sepals, with apex rounded, the inner 2.8-5.8 cm long, 0.6-2.9 cm wide, acuminate to rounded; transition to stamens gradual; stamens 99-248, outer cream-colored becoming indigo- or purple-tinged within, sparsely impreg- nated with fine acicular sclereids, the outermost to 5.5 cm long, with filaments to 14 mm wide and connectives prolonged 0.5-2.0 mm or more beyond anthers, the inner with filaments to 1 mm wide and connectives prolonged to 0.6 mm beyond anthers, the inner anthers 0.6-0.85 times as long as stamen; carpels 20- 39, the appendages indigo or purple, 6-15 mm long, with clavate tips 1.5-4 mm long, 0.6-1.9 mm in diam; stigmatic rays not impregnated with acicular sclereids, the papillae cells separating into powdery mass; axial process ca 1 mm long, acute to obtuse. Fruits and seeds rarely if ever produced. Tuberiferous "flowers" usually present, submersed; outer sepaloid bracts (3) 4, greenish to reddish, usually with short black streaks, subcoriaceous, ovate-triangular with truncate base, 3-6 cm long, 1.8-2.3 cm wide; tuber globose, densely woolly, producing alternating whorls of tuberous "flowers" and leaves in (3's) 4's; peduncle to 7.5 mm in diam, glabrous, abcission layer forming near apex.
bibliographicCitation: Wiersema, John H. 1984. Systematics of Nymphaea subgenus Hydrocallis (Nymphaeaceae). I. Four new species from the neotropics. Brittonia. 36: 213-222.

description: Rhizoma erectum, tuberosum, tantum sub germinatione stolones producens. Folia tenella, ovata vel elliptica, utrimque viridia, glabra, venatione in centro folii vix v. manifesta anastomosanti, margine integerrimo. Flores natantes, noctumi, sepalis cum petalis in verticillis tetrameris; sepala viridia, enervia; petala plerumque 12, 16, vel 20, alba vel ebumea cum staminibus et processubus carpellorum; sclereidibus acicularibus interioribus densioribus in petalis ut in sepalis et staminibus; carpella 19- 30, processubus clavatis, 7-16 mm longis, radii stigmatum sclereidibus acicularibus protrudentes. Fructus plerumque praesentes; semina minima, lat.: long. = 1:1.2-1.4, superficie minute granulata, imperfectis meridianis pilorum 20-70 ,um longorum instructa.

description: Rhizome erect, ovoid, tuberous, to 4.5 cm long, to 3.5 cm in diam, producing stolons only during germination. Leaf blades delicate, ovate to broadly elliptic, to 18 cm long, to 14 cm wide, 1.05-1.50 times as long as wide, entire, rounded at apex, peltate 0.5-3.5 mm from base of sinus, the sinus 0.37-0.48 times length of blade, the lobes acute to rounded at apex with slight protuberance; upper surface green, when dried with numerous tiny prominences from underlying trichosclereids interspersed with short elevated lines often visible from underlying acicular sclereids; undersurface green, glabrous, when dried often marked with slender, branched rusty-brown lines; venation slightly to evidently weblike centrally, di- chotomous and faintly reticulate toward margin, the principal veins 9-15. Petioles to 4 mm in diam, glabrous, usually with four major air canals. Peduncles to 6.5 mm in diam, glabrous, with an inner ring of 6 major air canals surrounded by 12 minor ones. Flowers floating, opening nocturnally, with sepals and petals in distinct whorls of 4; sepals uniformly green, oblong-ovate, 3-6 (7.2) cm long, 1- 3 cm wide, acute or somewhat rounded at apex, often marked with slender rusty- brown lines when dry, impregnated with acicular sclereids, inconspicuously nerved; petals usually 12, 16, or 20, densely impregnated with acicular sclereids, the outer greenish abaxially, shorter than sepals, with apex acute to somewhat rounded, the inner creamy-white, 2.1-4.4 cm long, 0.6-2.0 cm wide, acute to acuminate; tran- sition to stamens gradual; stamens 24-80, creamy-white, impregnated with acicular sclereids, the outermost to 3.3 cm long, with filaments to 15 mm wide, the inner with filaments to 1.5 mm wide and connectives prolonged to 0.3 mm beyond anthers, the inner anthers 0.4-0.7 times as long as stamen; carpels 16-30, the appendages cream-colored, 7-16 mm long, with clavate tips to 1.2 (1.5) mm in diam which usually darken upon drying; stigmatic rays with projecting acicular sclereids, the papillae cells remaining attached; axial process 1-1.5 mm long and blunt. Maturing fruits usually present; seeds 0.65-0.90 mm long, 0.50-0.70 mm in diam, 1.2-1.4 times as long as broad, finely granulate, with longitudinal rows of short hairs 20-70 µm long.
bibliographicCitation: Wiersema, John H. 1984. Systematics of Nymphaea subgenus Hydrocallis (Nymphaeaceae). I. Four new species from the neotropics. Brittonia. 36: 213-222.

description: Herbae aquaticae perennes (interdum annuae?) rhizomatosae foijis natantibus; foliorum laminae late ovatae vel orbiculares, 4-10(-12) cm diametro, superne virides et infra aliquando fuscatae; petioli foliorum vegetativorum 10-75 cm longi vel plurorum, petiolus foiji inflorescentiae 0.5-2.5 cm longi ex apice caulis petioloidi; inflorescentia 5-20 floribus, fasciculo bracteato congesto; alabastra capsulaeque sub- mersae; flores pantameri ephemeri emersi pedicellis 2-5 (-7) cm longis; sepala 6-7 (-10) mm longa; petala oblonga lutea, 12-15 mm longa, pubescentia copiose, alis fimbriatis trichomatum connatorum marginalium; petala caespite stipitato trichomatum basi; stylus floris longistyli 4-5 mm longus stigmate 2-4-lobato carnoso apicali; stylus floris brevistyli brevior stigmate subsessili; stamina floris longistyli filamentis brevibus antherisque cremeis 1.4-1.7 mm longis; stamina floris brevistyli filamentis longioribus antherisque cremeis 1.9-2.5 mm longis; capsulae ovoidea- globosae 5-7 mm longae; 10-2 5 semina 2-2.5 mm diametro, tuberculata vel fere laevia, brunnea vel pallide brunnea, modice compressa; chromosomatum numerus n = 18; florentes in menses omnia.
bibliographicCitation: Ornduff, Robert. 1970. Neotropical Nymphoides (Menyanthaceae): meso-American and West Indian species. Brittonia. 21: 346-352.

description: Herba perennis glabra gracilis ramosa 3-8 dm alta; folia basalia viridia subrosulata ovata 8-10 cm longa, 5-7 cm lata, pinnato-decomposita divisionibus ultimis lineari-lanceolatis; petioli graciles 5-12 cm longi basi late vaginantes; folia caulina similia; infloreseentia terminalis et lateralis, pedunculis 2-10 cm longis; bracteae involuerales 3-7, 10-30 mm longae spatulatae vel obovatae profunde lobatae pinnatifidaeve quam radiis plerumque breviores, radii 3-7 divaricati vel patenti-adscendentes 5-40 mm longi inaequales; bracteolae involucellorum 2-5 bracteis similes 2-12 mm longae pedicellos superantes; pedicelli 3-6 patenti-adscendentes 3-8(-15) mm longis; petala lineari-lanceolata attenuata alba; stylopodium breviter conoideum, stylis patentibus 0.2-0.5 mm longis; fructus oblongus 3.5 mm longus 1.5-2 mm latus ad apieem versus attenuatus, costis prominentibus obtusis quam vittis angustioribus, vittis magnis; semine sub vittis canaliculato facie eims parum colncava.

description: Bushy to slender perennial herb, usually prolifically branched, the foliage bright green; basal leaves clustered, the ultimate divisions 1-3 mm long, up to 1 mm broad, mucronate; petioles slender, 5-12 cm long, dilated at the very base into an- oval sheath; cauline leaves prominent, like the basal but reduced upward, the uppermost petioles wholly sheathing with broadly oblong sheaths; inflorescence paniculate to corymbose, with 5-10 lateral peduncles arising in the axils of the cauline leaves; bractlets linear to spatulate, entire to lobed or pinnatifid, usually exceeding the pedicels; pedicels spreading or spreading-ascending, unequal; petals with a darker midvein; stylopodium low conic.

description: Leaves with blades 3-19 cm long, 2-15 cm wide, subcoriaceous, obovate to elliptic, green adaxially, mostly deep purple abaxially, with impressed veins, the sinus mostly longer than midrib, the lobes usually divergent, with apices usually acute. Flowers 3-7.5 cm diam.; sepals with lines of insertion on receptacle curved, not prominent; petals 8-15, acute or more often rounded at apex; stamens 20-40, yellow, the filaments only slightly widest above middle and gradually narrowed to base; carpels 5-12, the appendages 0.6- 1.5 mm long, 0.8-1.4 mm wide, tapered or slightly cymbiform, yellowish brown abaxially, the stigmatic rays yellowish brown. Chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Wiersema, John H. 1996. Nymphaea tetragona and Nymphaea leibergii (Nymphaeaceae): Two species of diminutive water-lilies in North America. Brittonia. 48: 520-531.

description: Tree 2-30 m tall. Leaves obovate, acutely or cuneately narrowed at base, (3) 4-11 (18) x (1.7) 2-6 (10.5) cm, obscurely to prominently 13-23-crenulate or -crenate on each margin, secondary nerves 7-11 on each side of midnerve, inconspicuous or not markedly elevated on upper surface, tertiary venation inconspicuous on upper surface, all venation more conspicuously elevated beneath; petiole 5-10 mm long. Inflorescence consisting of few- to many-branched panicles, 3-4 fasciculate in an axil, shorter or longer than the leaves, 1.5-7 cm long; pedicels 1-4 mm long. Sepals mainly equal, suborbicular to oval, 0.5-1.5 x 0.8- 1.1 mm, slightly undulate-margined to conspicuously glandular-crenulate thickened; petals 4-5 mm long, 1.8-3 mm wide, 3-8 times longer than the sepals; filaments 3-5 mm long; ovary 1-3 mm long; style 1.3-3.5 mm long, 1.3-2 (3.5) times longer than the ovary. Capsule 6-9 (11) mm long, 3-4 mm diam; seeds castaneous, the body 2.1-5 mm long, the wing 3.8-4 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. & Luteyn, James L. 1980. Revision of the genus Ochthocosmus (Linaceae). Brittonia. 32: 128-143.

description: Tree 8 m tall. Leaves obovate or broadly oblong-obovate, acute to subacute at base, 6.5-13 x 3.5-8 cm, the margins obscurely crenulate with 8-10 sinuses along each side, the secondary nerves 5-6 on each side of the midnerve, together with the tertiary venation more or less conspicuous beneath, above secondary nerves subelevated or impressed (slightly elevated in F isotype), tertiary venation above inconspicuous; petioles 5-8 mm long. Inflorescence consisting of much-branched panicles, 11-14 cm long, 12-14 cm wide; fruiting pedicels 1.5-2.5 mm long. Sepals (fruiting) oblong to oval-oblong, 1-2 x 0.7-1 mm; petals (fruiting) 4-4.5 x 1-1.5 mm, 2.5-4 times the length of the sepals; filaments and ovary not seen; style (fruiting) 1-2 mm long. Capsule 8-11 mm long.

description: Shrub or tree, 2-30 m tall. Leaves crowded, suborbicular or broadly oblong to obovate-oblong or obovate, broadly rounded and emarginate at apex, rounded or obtuse to acute or cuneate at base, 3-13 (18) x 2-8 (10.5) cm, on each side obscurely 8-23-crenulate to strongly 13-15-crenulate or -crenate; lateral nerves 5-11 on each side of midnerve, either markedly or not markedly elevated above, more or less prominent below; tertiary venation impressed to markedly elevated above or inconspicuous, more or less conspicuous below; petioles 1-10 mm long. Inflorescence consisting of few- to many-flowered racemes or panicles, solitary or several and fasciculate, shorter or longer than the leaves, 1.5-14 cm long; pedicels 1.1-4 mm long. Sepals mainly equal, or somewhat unequal in var. gran- difolius, suborbicular to oblong, rounded at apex, 0.5-2 x 0.8-1.6 mm, margins usually conspicuously glandular-crenulate thickened; petals broadly obovate or oblong-obovate, rounded at apex, 3.5-6 x 1-3 mm, 2-8 times longer than the sepals; anthers 1-1.3 mm long; filaments 2.5-5 mm long; ovary 1-3 mm long; style 1-3.5 mm long, 1.3-3 times longer than the ovary. Capsule 6-12 mm long; body of seeds 1-5 mm, the wing 3.8-4.5 mm long.

description: Small ligneous plant 0.2-0.5 m tall to shrubs or small trees 0.7-5 (8) m, branches slender, wiry, wandlike, sparsely leafy. Leaves coriaceous, elliptic-oblong, oblong-oblanceolate, linear, or linear-oblong, rounded and emarginate or non-emarginate at apex, narrowed to an acute, subacute, or subobtuse base, 1-9 x 0.2- 3.2 cm, 1.7-6 times longer than broad, mainly lacking visible nerves above and below, or the secondary and tertiary venation more or less inconspicuously evident on upper surface, the margins entire or rarely with 1 or 2 subobsolete sinuses; petioles usually 1-5 mm long. Inflorescence consisting of simple racemes or more frequently subpaniculate, solitary or fasciculate in the upper axils or subterminal, shorter or longer than the leaves, 1.7-8 cm long; pedicels 1-4 mm long in anthesis, up to 5 mm long in fruit. Sepals mainly subequal or somewhat unequal, broadly oblong to suborbicular, 1-3.5 x 0.6-1.5 mm, the margins usually conspicuously crenulate and glandular-thickened, rarely subentire; petals obovate-oblong, 2.5-5 x 1.5-2 mm, 1.4-4.5 times longer than the sepals; filaments 4-6.5 mm long; ovary 1-1.5 mm long; style 1.5-3.5 mm long, 1.5-3 times longer than the ovary. Capsule (immature) 7 to (mature) 12.5 mm long; mature seed not seen.

description: Stems woody, glabrous, the internodes 5-10 mm. long. Petioles very stout, 1-2 mm. long. Leaf-blades ascending, coriaceous, broadly obovate, 10-30 mm. long, 8-20 mm. wide, retuse, apparently entire, but bearing about 6 semi-ovoid, appressed, glandular teeth on each side, obtuse to subrotund at base, glabrous, the veins obsolete above, prominulous and reticulate beneath; panicles slender, 6-10 cm. long, from the axils of the upper leaves, forming a widely spreading inflorescence, the branches racemose; flowers crowded in abbreviated racemes of 3-6, the pedicels 2-4 mm. long; outer 3 sepals firm, broadly ovate or subrotund, the outermost 0.8-0.9 mm. lolng, the third 1.3 mm. long; inner 2 sepals membranous, obovate-oblong, 2.4-2.9 mm. long, broadly rounded at summit; petals obovate-elliptic, 3.8-4.1 mm. long, 2.4-2.6 mm. wide, rounded at summnit; staminal disk very narrow; filaments slenlder, 4.2 mm. long; ovary ovoid-conic, 1.1 mm. high, 5-celled, abruptly tapering into a straight style 2.6 mm. long.

description: Shrub or tree 2-15 m tall. Leaves suborbicular to broadly subovate, retuse at apex, obtuse to rounded or cuneate at base, smaller and medium-sized ones 1.7- 3.5 x 1.7-3.2 cm, larger ones up to 6.5 x 6 cm, subentire except for 4-6 subobsolete, shallow sinuses on each side bearing scarcely projecting, deciduous glands; secondary nerves mainly (4) 5-7 (8) on each side on the midnerve, in- conspicuous and scarcely immersed above, tertiary venation obsolete above, secondary nerves impressed or subelevated below, tertiary venation below more conspicuous and subelevated; petioles 1-3.5 mm long. Inflorescences consisting of many-flowered and much-branched panicles, with several fasciculate peduncles in the upper axils or subterminal usually exceeding the leaves, 6-10 cm long; pedicels 2-4 mm long in anthesis, up to 6 mm long in fruit. Sepals usually unequal, the outer ones ovate-suborbicular 0.8-1.3 x 0.8-1 mm, the inner ovate-oblong 1.8-2.9 x 1.2-1.6 mm, the margins entire, eglandular; petals obovate-oblong, rounded at apex, 3.8-4.5 x 1-2.6 mm, 2.2-4 times longer than the sepals; fila- ments 4-4.5 mm long; ovary 0.9-2.2 mm long; style 1.2-2.6 mm long, shorter than to 1.3 (2) times longer than the ovary. Capsule 7-10 mm long; body of seed 0.5 mm, the wing 0.7 mm long.

description: Frutex 2-metralis; foliis coriaceis erectis ellipticis apice subobtusis subretusis vel integerrimis vel rotundatis basi acutis vel subobtusis 3.5-7.5 x 1.3-3 cm, marginibus utroque latere obsolete remoteque 5-12-crenulatis, nervis secundariis utroque latere 8-9 supra subimpressis subtus paullo prom- inulis; venatio tertiaria supra obsolete subimpressa subtus subelevata et reticulata; inflorescentiis axillaribus pauciramosis 3.2-6 cm longis folio brevioribus; pedicellis 4-6 mm longis; sepalis saepissime inaequalibus vel subaequalibus oblongis vel ovato-oblongis apice rotundatis vel obtusis 0.7-1.2 x 0.5-0.7 mm valde atroglanduliferis; petalis obovato-oblongis apice rotundatis 4-4.2 x 1.2-2 mm, 3.5- 5.3-plo longioribus quam latioribus; filamentis 4-5 mm longis; ovario 1.5 mm longo; stylo 2-3 mm longo 1.5-2-plo longiore quam ovario; fructu non viso.

description:

description: Plants fruticose, to 2 m tall; stems subquadrangular, pilose; leaves elliptic, the blade 10-23 cm long, 6-8 cm wide, glabrous except for the pilose costa of the lower surface, cystoliths present on the upper surface, the margin obscurely crenate with a cuspidate apex and a narrow base, the petiole 10-30 mm long, with pilose hairs; inflorescence a terminal thyrse 22 cm long on a densely pilose rachis with the flowers in fascicles of at least 6, the pedicel 4-6 mm long, pilose, the bracts lanceolate, 2.5-4 mm long, 1 mm wide at the base, the bractlets subulate, 1.5 mm long; calyx segments narrowly triangular, 3.5-4 mm long, 0.5 mm wide at the base, pilose; corolla yellow, glabrous without, with a few glandular hairs within, tubular, 2-2.3 cm long, the tube 3 mm wide at the base, 4 mm wide at the throat, the upper lip with the elliptic-ovate lobes 3 mm long, 2 mm wide at the base, the lower lip with the elliptic-oblong lobes 5-6 mm long, 2 mm wide at the base, the margins ciliolate; stamens extended to the middle of the upper lip, the filament 10 mm long, glabrous, the anthers 2 mm long; staminodes 2.5 mm long, glabrous; pistil included, the stigma 2-lobed, glabrous, the style 10 mm long, with a few hairs basally; ovary glabrous; capsules clavate, 10-15 mm long, 2 mm wide, 4-5 mm thick, (3) 4-seeded.

description: Plants scandent; stems subquadrangular to terete, glabrous; leaves oblong, the blade 12-20 cm long, 4-6 cm wide, glabrous or with a few hairs along the margins, cystoliths present on both surfaces, the margin undulate with an acuminate apex and a round base, the petiole 3-5 mm long, with pilose hairs; inflorescence a narrow compact spikelike terminal raceme 5-8 cm long on a sparsely pubescent rachis, the pedicel 2-3 mm long, the lowermost bracts linear and sterile, 6 mm long, the uppermost bracts lanceolate and fertile, 6 mm long and 1 mm wide at the base, the bractlets much smaller, 3 mm long, all ciliolate; calyx segments triangular, 3 mm long, 1 mm wide at the base, glabrous or with a few hairs at the tip; corolla red, glabrous throughout, tubular, 2.5-2.8 cm long, the tube 2-3 mm wide at the base, 4-5 mm wide at the throat, the upper lip with the oblong lobes 4 mm long, 2 mm wide at the base, the lower lip with the ovate lobes 3 mm long, 3 mm wide at the base; stamens extended to the base of the corolla lobes, the filament 10 mm long, glabrous, the anthers 2.5 mm long; staminodes 0.8-1 mm long, glabrous; pistil included, the stigma 2-lobed, glabrous, the style 10 mm long, glabrous; ovary glabrous; capsules not seen.

description: Plants fruticose to 2 m tall; stems terete in older portions to subquadrangular in younger portions, glabrate; leaves elliptic-lanceolate, the blade 9.5-14 cm long, 3-3.5 cm wide, scabrous on both surfaces, cystoliths sparsely present on the upper surface, the margin obscurely crenate with a cuspidate apex and a narrow, cuneate base, the petiole 5 mm long, with appressed hairs; inflorescence a short terminal raceme to 2.5 cm long, the flowers crowded along the pilose rachis, the pedicel 4 mm long, glandular-puberulent, the bracts lanceolate, 1-1.5 mm long, the bractlets 0.8-1 mm long; calyx segments narrowly triangular, 5-7 mm long, 0.5 mm wide at the base, glandular-puberulent; corolla white, glandular-puberulent without, pilose within at the base, tubular, up to 3 cm long, the tube 1.5 mm wide at the base, 5 mm wide at the throat, the upper lip with the elliptic-ovate lobes 2.5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide at the base, the lower lip with the elliptic-oblong lobes 4 mm long, 2 mm wide at the base; stamens extended to the edge of the corolla lobes, the filament 15 mm long, pubescent basally, the anthers 2-3 mm long; staminodes 1.5-2 mm long, retrorsely pilose, apically capitate with a rudimentary anther; pistil included, the stigma 2-lobed, glabrous, the style 30 mm long, sparsely pilose; ovary glabrous; capsules clavate, 30 mm long, 5 mm thick, glandular-puberulent, 4-seeded.

description: Terrestrial herb. Roots many, whitish, glabrous. Pseudobulbs completely buried, ovoid, leafless from the second year on- wards, externally white, (3-)4-6(-7) X (1-)1.5-2.5 cm. Leaves at flowering 3-6, little developed, 7-15 cm long, when fully developed 5-8, spreading, coriaceous, lanceolate, the lowermost 1-2 leaves sheath-like, the uppermost 4-7 leaves 13-33 X 1- 2.6 cm, articulate 1-2 cm from the surface of the soil, the apex acuminate. Inflorescence lateral, erect, racemose, lax, 26-56 cm, brownish to dark brown; peduncle 11-26 cm, the 2 sheath-like bracts strongly adpressed, 1.7-3.5 cm long; rachis 12-26 cm long; floral bracts oblong-lanceolate, 1-3 X 0.5-0.9 cm, greenish brown, acute to acuminate, the margins undulate, incurved; ovary with pedicel 1.4-3.9 cm long, dark brown. Flowers 9-15(-20) per inflorescence, sweet-scented. Sepals oblong-lanceolate to slightly lanceolate-ovate, light to dark brownish or brownish green, lighter at the base, frequently with dark-brown spots, the apex apiculate, the margin undulate; dorsal sepal (8-)11-13(-15) X 4-5(-6) mm; lateral sepals slightly oblique, (8-)11-13(-15) X 4-6(-7) mm. Petals concave, broadly elliptic to somewhat broadly lanceolate, (8-)9-12(-13) X 6-8 mm, the lower half greenish to light-brownish, occasionally with few to many small brown dots, the upper half dark-brown, color transition usually sharply delimited, the apex obtuse to rounded, slightly apiculate, the margins slightly undulate. Lip 3-lobed, (7-)9-11(-12) mm long, 10-12(-14) mm wide between the apices of the side lobes when spread, the base shortly unguiculate, 1 mm long, yellowish; lateral lobes erect, parallel, oblong-falcate, (3-)4-5(-6) X 2- 3(-4) mm, reddish to reddish purple, the apex obtuse, the base unconstricted, the margins entire, smooth; callus verrucose, slightly sulcate, extending from the base of the central lobe to the column foot, white, occasionally reddish white; isthmus separating the lateral lobes from the central lobe usually prominent, sometimes elongated, 1-2(-3) mm long; central lobe variable, obcordate to obovate-oblong to somewhat reniform, 5-7 x (5-)6-8(-10) mm, yellow with red to reddish-purple margins, occasionally with a few red dots at the base, the yellow becoming fainter towards aging, the apex with a protruding fold, retuse when flattened, the margin smooth, occasionally slightly verrucose at the apex. Column erect, slightly arcuate, trigonous, 6-7(-8) mm long, yellow at the base, reddish white at the middle, and greenish purple towards the apex; column foot (2.5-)3-4 mm long, yellow at the base, white at the middle with small numerous red dots that merge towards the apex. Anther ca. 2-2.5 x 1.5 mm, yellowish, apex green; pollinia 2, waxy, sulcate, ca. 1 X 0.5-0.6 mm, yellow; stipe triangular, hyaline, ca. 1 X 1 mm at base. Fruit deflexed, green, oblong to elongate, sulcate, ca. 6-8.5 X 1-1.5 cm when young, including the pedicel.

description: Terrestrial herb. Roots many, whitish, glabrous. Pseudobulbs exposed or occasionally partially buried, ovoid, acuminate, leafless from the second year onwards, externally greenish, 5-11 X 1.4-2.4 cm. Leaves at flowering 7-8, incompletely developed but already apparent, 11-23 X 0.6-1.4 cm, when fully developed 9-10, erect, coriaceous, linear-lanceolate, the lowermost 1-2 leaves sheath-like, the uppermost 8-9 leaves 16-35 X 1-1.8 cm, articulate 4.8- 6.2 cm from the leaf base, the apex acuminate. Inflorescence lateral, erect, usually simple, occasionally with a lateral branch up to 13 cm long, lax, 19-35 cm, greenish to brownish green; peduncle 11-20 cm, the 1-2 sheath-like bracts loosely adpressed, 1.5-3 cm long, frequently also with 1-2 pair of opposite bracts with abortive flowers; rachis 9-18 cm long; floral bracts deflexed, parallel and partially covering the rachis, broad, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, occasionally opposite, 2-2.7 X 1.4-2 cm, brownish green, the apex acute, discreetly apiculate, the margins undulate; ovary with pedicel 1.9-4.7 cm long, brownish green. Flowers 10-15 per inflorescence, showy, discreetly sweet-scented. Sepals reflexed in fully opened flowers, broadly lanceolate to ovate or elliptical, 15-20 X 9-14 mm, dark brownish-purple, the apex discreetly apiculate, the margin slightly undulate; lateral sepals slightly oblique. Petals usually reflexed in fully opened flowers, slightly concave, broadly obovate-oblong, 14-16 X 11-14 mm, brownish purple, base lighter, the apex rounded, slightly apiculate, the base attenuate, the margins entire, smooth. Lip 3-lobed, 10-12 mm long, 13-16 mm wide between the apices of the side lobes when spread, the base unguiculate, ca. 2 mm long, yellow; lateral lobes erect, not parallel, turned ca. 45º forward, reniform, (4-)5.5 X 6-7(-8) mm, the base and center lilac, towards the borders pinkish, the base constricted, the margins usually entire to occasionally slightly serrate; callus prominent, formed by (4-)6(-8) parallel lamellae, longitudinally extending from the base of the central lobe to the unguicule, the central 2(-4) lamellae rounded, thicker, yellow with the margins entire or slightly dentate, the outermost 2(-4) larger, slender, slightly spread, discreetly to profusely irregularly dentate, dark lilac; isthmus separating the lateral lobes from the central lobe discreet, ca. 1 mm long; central lobe, reniform to lunate and then with the lateral edges auriculate, 4-5 X 9-11 mm, the base and central part dark lilac, apex slightly orange, lateral edges yellowish, the lilac becoming faint orange with aging, the apex rounded or very discreetly retuse when flattened, the margin reflexed, slightly verrucose to completely smooth. Column erect, slightly arcuate, trigonous, 9-10 mm long, base yellowish white, middle lilac, towards the apex purple greenish; column foot 2-3(-4) mm long, at the very end immediately before the unguicule with a conspicuous dark brown stripe. Anther 3 X 2.5 mm, yellowish, apex green; pollinia 2, waxy, sulcate, ca. 1.3-1.5 X 0.8-1 mm, yellow, attached to a triangular stipe. Fruit not known.

description: Perennis; erecta. Folia pallide viridia, numerosa, acuta, rigida, canalieulata, 7-10 cm. longa, 2 nunn. lata, parce minute pilosa, margine breviter ciliata, pilis adpressis. Culmi floriferi saepissime 2, erecti, rigidi, 8-12 cmi. alti, breviter pilosi. Bracteae majores 2, foliis con-similes, minute pilosae, minute ciliatae; inferiores 2.5-3.5 em. longae, superiores dimidio breviores. Bracteae ininores breviores, saepissime 2-4. Spiculae 10-25, 2-3-florae, 2.5-3.5 mm. longae, capitato-congestae. Squamae albae vel pallide stramineae, brunneo-striatae, oblongae, ovatae vel lanceolatae, integrae, mucronatae, saepissime glabrae, ad apicem minute et sparse pilosae. Achaenium 1 mm. longum, 0.7-0.9 mm. latum, brunneum, obovoideum, plano-convexum vel subteres, apice paulo depressum; styli basis persistens pyramidalis, 2.5-4 mm. longa.

description: Half-shrub to 0.5 m high, covered with glands, villous. Stems indistinctly quadrangular or terete. Leaf blades rhombic to lanceolate, the margin slightly crenate, leaves 30-51 X 12-22 mm, on both sides covered with multicellular short hairs and densely so with sessile glands; the petioles slightly winged and 3-6 mm long, connate, forming a ring around the stem. Inflorescence terminal, 4-8 cm long at maturity. Calyx pilose, with the posterior segments subulate to lanceolate, 6-8 mm long, the anterior segment leaflike, 7-12 X 5-6 mm. Corolla tube ca. 15-19 mm long, minutely pubescent and densely covered with sessile glands on the outside, hirsute on the inner side in the middle, the upper lip almost orbicular and 9-11 X 9-11 mm, the lower lip 11-12 X 11-12 mm, with the outside slightly minutely pubescent and covered with sessile glands. Fertile filaments 3-4 mm long. Style slightly pilose. Capsule 7- 8 mm long and minutely pubescent. Seeds turbinate to ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm long, longitudinally reticulate to minutely pitted.

description: Half-shrub 0.5-0.6 m high, with erect or decumbent branches, with sparse or dense indument, covered with sessile glands. Leaves 8-70 X 2-20 mm, the blade narrowly ovate to lanceolate, gradually attenuate to base, leaf tip either acute or obtuse, on both sides densely or moderately covered with long white multicellular hairs and minute sunken white glands, the margins entire to minutely crenate. Inflorescence 15-45 cm long at maturity, with bracts 9-11 X 3-6 mm, the flowers on pedicels to 2 mm long. Calyx with linear to subulate inferior segments 5-6 X 0.5-1 mm, the posterior segment 6-10 X 5-6 mm, bluntly oval. Corolla violet, the tube 10-18 mm long, on the outside moderately covered with long retrorse hairs, villous on the inner side at least on the upper half, the upper lip almost orbicular, 6-15 X 6-15 mm, the lower lip 6-13 x 6-14 mm, with a white spot at the base, shortly 3-lobed. Stamens 4, the two posterior sterile, the two anterior fertile; filaments in one plane, fertile an- thers cohering. Ovary covered with short hairs, ovoid, bilocular. Style 9-10 mm long, glabrous. Capsule 6-7 mm long, shortly pubescent. Seeds 0.6 X 0.4 mm, shortly obtuse to ellipsoid, minutely pitted.

description: Stems rigid and rather robust, almost gla- brous, erect at the base, but decumbent es- pecially when growing in shade. Leaves lanceolate, slightly narrowed at the base, with narrow auricles curved upward and adnate to the stem, 43-1 10 x 10-35 mm. Inflorescence 3-6 cm long. Calyx sparsely villous.

description: Herb with woody base, glandular and villous. Leaves covered with glands and multicellular hairs, ovate to lanceolate, the margins entire or crenate to serrate, somewhat to clearly auriculate at the base, the auricles connected or touching, the margins slightly serrate to crenate or entire. Calyx villous, with inferior segments 9 X 1.5 mm and superior segment 9-18 mm long. Corolla tube 23-35 mm long, with rather long hairs on the outside, the upper lip 10-15 X 11-16 mm, the lower lip 10-15 X 10-14 mm, both with short hairs on the outside. An- thers with ellipsoidal to oblong pollen. Style shorter than the stamens, filiform. Capsule 6 X 2.5 mm. Seeds 0.4-0.7 X 0.4 mm, shortly obtuse, minutely pitted.

description: Half-shrub to 1-2 m high, branched at the base. Stems and leaves sticky, covered only with glandular hairs. Stems terete, the present year's stems indistinctively and obtusely quadrangular, especially distally, sometimes reddish, pale brown when biennial. Leaves with broadly elliptic blade, somewhat triangular to acute apically, with winged petioles, to 120 X 44 mm, the margins slightly crenate to serrate, dark brown to black when dried, the petioles of oppo- site leaves connate or touching at the base. Inflorescence 6-17 cm long at maturity; pedicels to 2 mm long. Calyx glabrous but covered with minute glands except on the margins, the lower segments narrowly triangular to subulate, 15 X 1 mm, the upper segment broadly ovate, almost circular at the apex, 11-20 mm long and to 10 mm wide. Corolla violet-blue to sky blue with a white spot on the lower lip at the throat, the tube 25-40 mm long, nearly cylindrical, slightly curved downward at the apex, glabrous to 3/4 of the length, further up minutely villous, the upper lip reniform, 15- 20 X 16-25 mm, the lower lip slightly 3- lobed and somewhat smaller. Anthers with globose pollen. Style 30 mm, slightly shorter or longer than the stamens. Ovary conical, 3 X 2 mm, loosely pilose, bilocular. Capsule 8 X 4 mm, minutely pubescent, opening by 2 valves bent inward. Seeds almost ovoid, strongly angled by caruncles disposed in longitudinal lines, 0.6 X 0.4 mm, dark brown.

description: Half-shrub 0.3-0.5 m high, pilose and covered with glands. Stems quadrangular to terete at the base. Leaves opposite, elliptical to narrowly ovate, narrowed at the base, 9- 31 X 3-10 mm, densely covered with sunken glands and multicellular hairs on both sides, the margins slightly crenate to serrate, dark green on the upper side when dried. Inflorescence to 6 cm long, with densely arranged solitary flowers on short pedicels, in the axil of normal leaves forming decussate bracts 7 X 4 mm. Calyx villous, especially on the outside, the four inferior segments lanceolate, 4-5 mm long, the posterior segment large and leaflike, ovate, blunt, 6-7 X 3-4 mm. Corolla violet with a white spot at the base of the lower lip, the tube 11-13 mm long, on the outside covered with glands and minutely pubescent, hirsute on the inner side in the middle, the upper lip almost orbicular; 7 X 8-9 mm, the lower lip 8 X 8 mm, slightly tripartite. Ovary shortly pilose. Style nearly glabrous, 15 mm long. Capsule 4 mm long, minutely pubescent. Seeds truncate to nearly ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm long, lengthwise reticulate to minutely pitted.

description: Half-shrub, 0.15-0.5 m tall, shortly pubescent. Stems erect, young stems quadrangular, nearly black when dried, older stems pale brown and woody, subterete. Leaves sessile, obovate, glandular-pubescent (velutinous) on both sides, 8-41 X 5-16 mm, margin of the upper half distinctively crenate to serrate, entire at the base. Inflorescence to >30 cm long, with 1-3 cm between each pair of the subsessile flowers, with 2 rotund bracteoles 2-3 mm long. Calyx green, with 4 lanceolate inferior teeth 4-5 mm long, the upper tooth ovate, 5-8 x 4 mm. Corolla purple with dark stripes on the lip and with a white spot on the throat of the lower lip, the tube hairy, 9-13 mm long, the upper lip 5-9 mm longand 5-8 mm broad, the lower lip 6-8 X 7- 8 mm and somewhat trilobed. Stamens not projecting, inserted at two different heights in the corolla tube, the two posterior sterile, the two anterior fertile and longer, the fertile filaments flattened; fertile anthers cohering. Ovary ovoid, bilocular; style glabrous, 10 mm long and slightly widened at the top, with 2 lobes. Capsule ovoid, pointed at the apex, 4 mm long, septicidal with 2 valves. Seeds numerous, 0.5 X 0.3 mm.

description: Half-shrub 0.5-1.5 m high, erect, covered with glands. Stems indistinctly quadrangular or terete, woody at the base. Leaves narrowly elliptic, to 75 X 28 mm, covered by glands, with only a few other hairs on the nerves, the margins crenate to serrate, the lamina gradually narrowing at the base, with petioles to 14 mm long. Inflorescence loose, to 12 cm long at maturity; the flowers on very short pedicels to 1 mm long, with 2 linear to narrowly elliptic bracteoles to 2 mm long. Calyx covered with glands, with the lower segments linear, 4-6 mm long, the upper segment elliptic to rhomboidal, 7-9 X 4 mm. Corolla tube 14- 21 mm long, curved down at the broadened apex, minutely covered with short hairs, especially at the apex, violet on the upper side, except at the white base, and on the lower side, except for the distal 3 mm, which is green; both lips longer than wide, the upper lip 13-15 X 11-12 mm, the lower lip 13-18 X 12-15 mm, both lips dark violet to blue, the inner side more colored, with a white spot at the throat of the lower lip; sometimes both lips reflexed. Fertile filaments 2-3 mm long, the anthers coherent. Style with few nonglandular hairs, 14-19 mm long, the stigma somewhat lower than the fertile anthers. Capsule pointed, 5 X 2- 3 mm. Seeds 0.5 mm, black.

description: Planta dense foliosa, glabra; internodia teretia, usque ad 2 cm longa. Folia decussata, obovata, atromarginata, in apice rotundata vel emarginata. Spica nulla. Uniflora, flos sessilis, 2 mm longus; petala 6, dimorpha; stylus ad medium inflatus.

description: Small, glabrous, probably pendent plants, with epicortical roots at the base, sparsely branched, internodes to 2 cm long, more or less terete, furfuraceus and light chocolate brown when young, becoming smooth. Phyllotaxy decussate; leaves to 2 X 1.5 cm, fleshy, broadly obovate to nearly orbicular, apex rounded, often emarginate; base abruptly tapering to very short (1 mm) petiole, venation nearly obscure except for midrib, with 2-4 faint palmate lateral veins; margins and lower midrib furfuraceous when young, these becoming smooth and dark (when dry) when mature, lower midrib and margins joining at the apex. Infiores- cence 1-flowered, the flowers seemingly sessile in clusters of 3 or more in leaf axils, each subtended by a nearly smooth-margined to slightly fimbriate scale leaf 1.5 mm long, this with acute apex, and flanked by 2 black-tipped bracteoles. Flowers 2 mm, possibly unisexual, equally divided in length between petals and ovary, the latter with irregularly lacerate calyculus; petals 6, strongly dimorphic; anthers (staminodia?) extremely small (ca. 0.25 mm), bilocular, sessile, placed at two different heights on the petals; style 1 mm, the upper half swollen in fusiform fashion; stigma scarcely differentiated. Fruit 3 X 2 mm, barrel-shaped, with lacerate, brown calyculus, waxy white when dry.

description: Tree up to 40 m. high, the trunk 50 cm. or more in diameter; branchlets slender, often striate, when young minutely and densely puberulent (hairs dark reddish brown, somewhat lepidote, sessile-stellate, 4-6- branched, about 0.1 mm. in diameter), soon glabrous; petioles slender, rugose, puberulent as the branchlets, shallowly canaliculate, narrowly winged, 15-30 mm. long; leaf blades often shining above, dark green, oblong-obovate, 8-20 cm. long, 3-6.5 cm. broad, gradually attenuate at base, rounded at apex and often slightly emarginate, glabrous above, glabrous (when young densely puberulent as the branchlets), minutely punctate, and often ceriferous beneath, the costa conspicuously grooved above, the secondary nerves 6-12 per side, ascending, slightly impressed or plane above, raised beneath, the veinlets obscure or slightly impressed above, plane or obscure beneath; staminate inflorescences densely puberulent on all exterior surfaces as the branchlets (hairs 0.2-0.3 mm. in diameter), 1-6 cm. long, the peduncle up to 2.5 cm. long; flowers solitary or in irregular fascicles of 2-8, subtended by minute coriaceous semiorbicular soon deciduous bracts less than 1 mm. long, the pedicels up to 5 mm. long, each bearing at the summit a bracteole (bracteoles coriaceous, semiorbicular, about 2 mm. broad at base and 1 mm. long) perianth about 4 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes oblong, subacute or obtuse; androecium 2.5-3 mm. long, the filament column 1 mm. long or less, the anthers 1.5-2 mm. long, the connective mass often produced beyond the anthers, obtuse at apex; pistillate inflorescences resembling the staminate, the bracteole up to 2 mm. long, the ovary conical, carnose, densely and minutely lepidote-tomentellous, the stigma sessile, oblique; fruitiiig inflorescences slightly longer than the pistillate, glabrous throughout at maturity, the mature fruits few, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 5-10 mm. long), coriaceous, conspicuously rugose when dry, 17-25 mm. long (including stipe and apex), 20-25 mm. broad, con- spicuously carinate, long stipitate at base, apiculate at apex, the pericarp 0.5-1.5 mm. thick (much thicker at the sutures), the seed about half as long as broad. (Fig. 6.)

description: Twining herb, dioecious. Stems dextrorse, terete, smooth to slightly sulcate; petioles 9 cm, sulcate, thickened and curved at base. Leaves 21-23 X 18-22 cm, ovate to suborbicular, cordate at base, the basal lobes slightly overlapping, acute at apex, 13-15-nerved, abaxially glabrous, adaxially puberulent. Staminate inflorescences corymboid up to 15 cm; bracts 2.4-3 X 0.5 mm, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, pedicels 1-4 cm; flowers dark red or purple; tepals 4 X 2 mm, oblong-lanceolate, 3-5- nerved; stamens 6, ca. 4 mm long, in a fleshy column 1-1.5 mm high, extrorse, originating and surrounded by a recurved, laciniate and fleshy structure 3 mm; pistillode lacking. Pistillate inflorescences unknown.

description: Twining herb, monoecious. Stems dextrorse, terete, smooth to slightly sulcate; petioles up to 9 cm (4 cm in juvenile leaves), sulcate, thickened and curved at base. Leaves trifoliolate; central leaflet 14- 15 cm (4 cm in juvenile leaflets) X 7.5-8 cm (1.8 cm in juvenile leaflets), lanceolate, elliptic to oblanceolate, acute at base and apex, 3-5-nerved; lateral leaflets 14.5-15.5 X 8-8.5 cm, falcate, 3-4-nerved. Staminate infiorescences up to 17.5 cm, fractiflex; pedicels 6-8 mm, flowers translucent brownish maroon; tepals 4 X 2 mm wide, oblong-lanceolate, 3-5-nerved; stamens 3, ca. 2 mm long, originating in a fleshy column ca. 1 mm high, introrse; pistillode lacking. Pistillate infiorescences up to 9.5- 10 cm, peduncle 8-8.5 cm; flowers trans- lucent brownish maroon, grouped at the apex of the rachis; tepals 1-2 X 0.5 mm, lanceolate; styles separate, sessile. Capsules 1.8-2.3 X 0.9-1.3 cm, oblong to elliptic, base and apex rounded, brown-reddish; immature seeds 2 per locule, 3-4 X 3-4 mm, winged downward.

description: Plants stout, to 1 m high, resinous and scented, profusely branching above the base, the foliage glabrous, often the nodes and the inflorescence scaberulous or puberulent, from a taproot terminating in a tuberous base; basal leaves ovate to triangular-ovate, 6-14 cm long and broad, pinnately decompound, the divisions linear-filiform, rigid, 2-8 mm long, acute, mucronate, the petioles stout, 1-2 dm long, about the lower 1/4 dilated and sheathing, the sheaths narrowly scarious-margined, the cauline leaves numerous, gradually reduced upward, their scarious petiolar sheaths strongly dilated and conspicuous, cordate at summit, the reduced blade arising from the depression, somewhat scaberulous or puberulent, the uppermost petioles wholly sheathing; inflorescence densely branched, the peduncles terminal and lateral, 5-18 cm long, scaberulous or puberulent at apex; involucre of 5-8 spatulate to linear, pinnatifid (or rarely merely lobed or entire) bracts 0.8-2.5 cm long, a little connate at base; fertile rays 8-15, 2-4 cm long, spreading-ascending, unequal; involucel of 6-12 linear bractlets like the bracts, entire or trifid, 4-9 mm long, about equaling the pedicels; fertile pedicels 6-12, 3-8 mm long, unequal, spreading-ascending or ascending; flowers white; petals oblong or oblanceolate, 2-2.5 mm long, acute; stamens ca 2 mm long, the anthers oval, ca 0.7 mm long; stylopodium low conical, the styles short and stout, 0.2-0.5 mm long, spreading; fruit oblong-oval, rounded at apex, truncate at base, 5-7 mm long, 2-3.5 mm broad, the dorsal ribs prominent, acute, the lateral rather narrowly thin-winged; seed face slightly concave.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1967. Some Umbelliferae of the Andean Paramos of South America. Brittonia. 19: 212-226.

description: Tubers usually solitary, without distinct stalk, branched, or more often unbranched, more or less vertically penetrating, slender, up to 1.5 m long and 5 cm in diam, sparingly to abundantly covered with rootlets, the surface pale brown, the tissue off-white or very pale orange, somewhat gritty, edible with no distinct taste; long roots arising near the origin of tuber, up to 75 cm long. Stem terete, up to 10 m long and 5 mm in diam at base, glabrous, leafless for ca 4 m from base, prickly for ca 3 m from base; prickles yellowish, usually directed downward, 1-2 mm long. Bulbils not seen. Leaves alternate; blade lanceolate to ovate or elliptic, basally acute to obtuse or rounded, apically acuminate, 7-21 x 2.5-8.2 cm. glabrous, coriaceous, drying green to brownish above and green to glaucous beneath; primary veins 3, acrodromous, prominent, stout, ridged below, often with 1 (2 in broader leaves) additional submarginal pair becoming gently scalloped and obscure toward apex, the innermost pair of veins for the most part located closer to margin than to midrib, sometimes becoming submarginal, especially in smaller leaves; secondary veins straight or sometimes bent or branched, slightly distinct above, distinct from lesser order veins below; reticulation mostly obscure on both surfaces; margin ca 0.2 mm wide, very prominent, firm, slightly undulated and inrolled, yellowish; petiole 1/8-1/4 the length of blade, 1-3.5 cm long, stout, geniculate, deeply channelled above with two edges narrowly winged or thickened; stipules absent. Staminate spikes in fascicles of up to 10 or arranged on an up to 1-cm-long rachis, in leaf axils, the axis 2-14 cm long, ridged, glabrous, up to 50- flowered. Flowers laxly arranged, 1.2-1.5 x 1.2-1.5 mm, shortly pedicelled; pedicel 0.2-0.5 mm long, thick; bract and bracteole widly ovate, acute, membranous, blotched with red, the bract 0.6-0.8 x 0.6-0.8 mm, the bracteole 0.5-0.7 x 0.4- 0.5 mm; tepals similar in size, 1-1.2 x 0.6-1 mm, erect, leathery, blotched with red, the outer ones ovate to widely ovate, acute, the inner ones ovate, apically acute to obtuse; stamens free, the filaments columnar, nearly 3 times the length of anther, 0.5-0.6 mm long, often blotched with red, the anther ca 0.2 mm long, the connective narrow; pistillode 0.5-0.8 mm long, fleshy, conical, 3-lobed. Pis- tillate inflorescence axillary, solitary, spicate (rarely fascicled on a short rachis), the axis 4-20 cm long, erect, ridged, glabrous, up to 24-flowered. Flowers laxly arranged, nearly sessile at anthesis; bract and bracteole as in staminate flower, but larger and somewhat fleshy, the bract ca 1.4 x 1.3 mm, the bracteole 1-1.2 x 0.8-1 mm; tepals as staminate flower, but somewhat fleshy, 1.1-1.4 x 1-1.2 mm, the inner tepals slightly narrower than the outer ones; ovary 3.5-5 x 1.5 mm, glabrous, with a short neck; staminodes 0.2-0.3 mm long; styles connate, 0.8-1 mm long; stigmas free, each lobed into 3 short arms. Capsules up to 12 per spike, ascending, 3-3.2 x 4 4.4 cm; wing slightly rounded to straight on sides. Seed winged all around, ca 20 mm across (5-7 mm exclusive of wing); wing 7- 10 mm at broadest.

description: Plants 3-6 dm high; leaves pinnately deeompound, with few divisionls, usually 2 at a node on the rachis; petiole hyaline-bordered, short, to 1 em long; involucre conspicuous, usually entire; involueel ilconspicuous, entire; primary rays 15-25, 1-3.5 cm long; petals white; anthers purple; styles 0.5-1.0 mm long, strongly recurved on the mature fruit; fruit orbicular, the dorsal ribs broad and rounded, the lateral ribs inconspicuous; oil tubes brown or dull black; corky band very prominent, at times swollen. Pollen grains 22.8-27.2 µ long, 11.9-13.6 µ wide. Chromosome number: n = 7. Common in moist prairies, abandoned rice fields, and roadside ditches. Texas and Louisiana, northward to Kansas and Missouri. June to August.

description: Liana, or shrub with scandent branches, the branchlets slender, einereous, copiously lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles stout, rugose, 6-12 mm. long, the leaf-blades thin-coriaceous, brownish when dried, elliptic- or obovate-oblong, 10-20 cm. long, 3.5- 9.5 cm. broad, obtuse at base, obtusely short-cuspidate at apex, entire or obsoletely crenulate and slightly thickened at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 9-12 per side, spreading, conspicuously prominulous on both surfaces, the basal ones short, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces or obseure above; inflorescence 1-2.5 cm. long at anthesis, compactly dichotomously several times branched, the peduncle short (less than 5 mm. long), often stout and woody, the branchlets slender, straight, the bracts papyraceous, ovate, acute, about 1 mm. long; flowers usually paired or ternate, 1.7-2.2 mm. in diameter at anthesis, each subtended by 2 or 3 minute bracteoles, the pedicels slender, about 1 mm. long; sepals papyraceous, ovate-deltoid, 0.4-0.6 mm. long, slightly broader, obtuse or rounded at apex, erosulous to densely ciliolate at margins; petals papyraceous or thin-carnose, oblong, 1-1.3 mm. long, about 0.7 mm. broad, erosulous or minutely ciliolate at mnargins distally; disk thin-carnose or submembranous, about 0.2 mm. high and 0.8 mnm. in diameter, subentire at margin; filaments about 0.6 mm. long; anther-locules distinct, slightly divergent at base, about 0.2 mm. long, dehiscing by longitudinal oblique clefts, the connective deltoid, not produced beyond locules; ovary about 0.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style about 0.3 mm. long, the stigmas obscure or minutely capitate; ovules 2 per locule, collateral-superposed; fruiting inflorescence swollen, the peduncle up to 3 mm. in diameter or more, woody, lenticellate, the immature fruits apparently 1 per inflorescence, sub- cylindric-ellipsoid, sometimes falcate, up to 3 cm. long and 1 cm. in diameter (doubtless larger at maturity), the pericarp woody, at least 2 mm. thick, the seeds probably reduced to 1 or 2 and imbedded in pulp.

description: Liana or scandent shrub ( ?); branchlets slender, lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles slender, 6-8 mm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceous, brownish when dried, obovate-elliptie, 10-15 cm. long, 4-6.5 cm. broad, acute to subattenuate at base, obtusely short-cuspidate at apex, entire or obsoletely crenulate at margins, the costa raised above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 7-9 per side, the basal 1 or 2 pairs sharply ascending and subparallel to margins, the others arcuate-ascending, all conspicuously prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets conspicuously reticulate and prominulous on both surfaces; infloreseence 2-3 cm. long at anthesis, dichotomously or pseudodichotomously branched, the pedunele 10-13 mm. long, the branchlets slender, the bracts less than 1 mm. long; flowers loosely arranged, about 4 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels about 2 mm. long; sepals rounded, fimbriolate at margins; petals oblong, thin-carnose, fimbriolate at margins; disk thin-carnose, entire at margin; filaments slender; anthers small, distinctly bilobed; ovary depressed-trigonous, the ovules 1 per locule (ex Miers).

description: Liana, or shrub with scandent branches; branchlets often rugose, conspicuously lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles stout, rugose, 8-18 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, olivaceous or brownish and minutely rugulose when dried, sometimes black-pune- tate beneath, elliptic-oblong, 10-19 cm. long, 4.5-9.5 cm. broad, obtuse to rounded at base, subacute to obtusely short-acuminate at apex, en- tire or inconspicuously crenulate and slightly thickened at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 5-11 per side, spreading, essentially plane or slightly impressed above, elevated beneath, the veinlets immersed, sometimes faintly prominulous be- neath; infloreseence 2-8 cm. long at anthesis, divided to base or short- pedunculate, glabrous throughout, thyrsoid-paniculate, the branchlets slender, alternate (subopposite distally), each subtended by a papy- raceous ovate acute bract less than 1 mm. long; flowers loosely arranged, 2.5-4.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, each subtended by 2 or 3 minute inconspicuous bracteoles, the pedicels slender, 1-2 mm. long; sepals papyraceous, semiorbicular-ovate to deltoid, 0.7-1.3 mm. long, 1-1.5 mm. broad, often conspicuously unequal, obtuse or rounded at apex, seariose and subentire at margins; description: Liana, or shrub with scandent branehes; branchlets einereous, lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles stout, rugose, 4-12 mm. loig, the leaf-blades coriaceous, olivaceous to dark brown when dried, often paler above, elliptic or obovate-oblong, 6-12 cm. long, 2.5-5 cm. broad, obtuse or acute at base, rounded or faintly emarginate and sometimes minlutely callose-apiculate at apex, entire and slightly thickened at margins, the costa raised or nearly plane above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 9-13 per side, spread- ing, plane or slightly impressed above, elevated beneath, the veinlets immersed, often faintly prominulous beneath; infloreseenees often subfasciculate in clusters of 2 or 3, 2-4 cm. long at anthesis, with slender peduneles up to 7 mm. long, glabrous throughout, thyrsoid- panieulate, the branchlets slender, alternate or opposite, often di- or trichotomously arranged, the bracts subcoriaceous, ovate, subentire, less than 1 mm. long; flowers loosely arranged, each subtended by 2 or 3 minute iniconspicuous bracteoles, the pedicels slender, less than 1 mm. long; sepals deltoid-ovate, 0.7-1.2 mm. long and broad, rounded at apex, seariose and subentire or erosulous-eiliolate at margins; petals suberect, obovate-oblong, 1.8-2.6 mm. long, 1-1.3 mm. broad, narrowed toward base, seariose and conspicuously erose-fimbriolate at margins; disk membranous, 0.4-0.5 mm. high, 1.2-1.4 mm. in diam- eter, crenulate at margin; filaments 0.8-1 mm. long, broadest at base; anther-locules about 0.3 mm. long, dehiscing by vertical extrorse-lateral clefts, the conlnective subacute, conspicuously produced 0.15- 0.2 mm. beyond locules; ovary about 0.7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style about 0.3 mm. long; ovules 2 per locule, collateral.

description: Low shrub up to 2 m. in height, the branchlets alternate, elongate, slender, often lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite or alternate, the petioles rugose, stout, 4-10 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous or thiln-coriaceous, dark brown or olivaceous when dried, elliptic or obovate or lanceolate, usually narrowly so, 5-12 (-15) cm. long, (1.2-) 1.5- 4(-5) cm. broad, gradually long-attenuate at base and decurrent on the petiole, rounded or obtuse or obtusely cuspidate at apex, crenate- serrate at margins (serrations 2 or 3 per centimeter), the costa promi- nent on both surfaces or inconspicuously so above, the secondary nerves 5-8 per side, ascending, anastomosing toward margins, con- spicuously prominulous on both surfaces or essenltially plane above, the veinlets reticulate, often prominulous on both surfaces, sometimes obscure or immersed above; infloreseence 0.5-3 cm. long at anthesis, compactly thyrsoid-paniculate, divided to base or with a slender peduncle up to 5 mm. long, the branchlets slender, alternate or suboppo- site, each subtended by a small bract up to 1 mm. long (bracts papyraceous, ovate to oblong-lanceolate, acute, often minutely serrulate or ciliolate); flowers congested or loosely arranged, usually 3-4 mm. in diameter at anthesis, each subtended by 1-3 minute bracteoles, the pedicels slender, 0.5-2.5 mm. long; sepals submembranous to thill- coriaceous, ovate-deltoid to oblong, 0.8-1.7 mm. long and broad, sub- acute to rounded at apex, entire to erosulous at margins; petals mem- branous or submembranous, oblong-obovate, often narrowly so, 2-3 mm. long, 1.3-2 mm. broad, erosulous or failitly ciliolate at margins (rarely subelitire); disk membranous, 0.3-0.7 mm. high, 1-1.4 mm. in diameter, unldulate or crenulate at margin; filamelits slightly di- lated at base, 0.6-1.3 mm. long; anther-locules 0.4-0.6 mm. long, paral- lel or faintly divergent at base, dehiscing by vertical extrorse-lateral clefts, the connective obtuse or minutely apiculate at apex and not at all or slightly exceeding the locules; ovary 0.5-1 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style slender, 0.2-0.6 mm. long, truncate or with an in- conspicuous obscurely capitate stigmatic shield (stigmas, if apparent, minute and alternate with stamens); ovules 2 per locule, collateral or sometimes nearly superposed; fruiting infloreseence enlarged, the fruits usually 1 per infloreseence, obovoid or essentially subglobose, up to 2.5 cm. in diameter (perhaps larger at maturity), often con- spicuously stipitate (stipe occasionally to 1 cm. long, sometimes en- tirely lacking), the pericarp coriaceous, glaucous when young, the seeds 2-4 (occasionally 1), imbedded in mucilaginous pulp.
