description: Plant acaulescent, flowering 35-70 cm tall with the inflorescence extended, propagating by stolons 10-20 cm X 5 mm. Leaves rosulate, erect to laxly spreading, 0.5-1 m long, inconspicuously appressed- punctate lepidote throughout. Leaf sheaths elliptic, 3-4 X 2-3 cm, pale or slightly castaneous adaxially, dark castaneous and lustrous abaxially. Leaf blades linear, attenuate, 6-16 mm wide, conspicuously plicate, bright green. Scape erect to arching, 15-35 cm X 2-4 mm, glabrous, green. Scape bracts erect, densely imbricate, the lower foliaceous, green, the upper elliptic, acute to long-acuminate, green, tinged red, or purple. Inflorescence declinate to pendent, simple, 15-50 cm long, very laxly 6-20- flowered. Floral bracts like the upper scape bracts, 25-60 X 6-15 mm, thin-coriaceous, the lowest much exceeding the sepals, the upper much shorter than the sepals, tightly enfolding the flowers, red, greenish red, reddish purple, or magenta. Pedicels slender, 5-10 mm long, 10-37 mm apart, spreading at 30-90? from the axis at anthe- sis. Sepals 35-53 mm long, connate 30-41 mm, the free lobes erect, imbricate, oblong, obtuse, yellow. Corolla with spreading to recurving lobes. Petals narrowly oblanceolate, acute, 55-65 mm long, more than 3/4 conglutinated, yellow to yellow-green. Stig- ma of the convolute-blade type. Fruit a dry, slenderly cylindric capsule 22-28 mm long. Seed coma brown.

description: Caules approximati, elongati, tenues, teretes, superne leviter com- pressi, sectione transversa elliptici, rigidi, nitidi, 26-55 cm longi, 0.15-0.16 cm diam., 6-8 folii, internodiis inferioribus 1.3-1.4 cm longis, superioribus acereseentibus ad c. 6-7 cm longis. description: Erect, ascending, suffrutescent, rather twiggy perennials 1.5-3 dm high; stems narrowly 4-sulcate, strigulose-puberulent with fine descending hairs under 0.1 mm long. Flowers axillary, sessile, solitary in upper half of plant, sometimes on elongate, interrupted spikes to 10 cm long, flowers then subtended by bract-like leaves to 3 mm long; paired bracteoles subulate, to 1 mm long; calyx 4-5 mm long, sepals 4, linear- lanceolate to subulate, 3.5-4.5 mm long, to 0.6 mm wide at base, puberulent as leaves; corollas 13.5-16.5 mm long, puberulent outside, tube 8-9.5 mm long, 0.7-1.1 mm broad, lavender to white, upper erect lobe oblong-elliptical, 4-5 mm long, 1.8-2.2 mm wide, recurving at obtuse, unnotched tip, lower 3 lobes spreading nearly perpendicular, lateral 2 oblong, 5-6 mm long (from throat), 2.3-3 mm wide, rounded at tip, mid lobe oblong-ovate, 3.4-5 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide, rounded at tip, with a depressed medial groove extending down throat, bordered by a pair of oblong, raised ridges ca 2 mm long, 0.7 mm wide, 0.4 mm high, lobes lavender-pink inside, white marked with darker purple to maroonish spots, lines along raised ridges; stamens 2, anther sacs divergent by ca 45 degrees, distal lobes subtransverse, 0.8-1 mm long, lower lobe somewhat parallel to filament, 0.4-0.6 mm long, somewhat pointed at base, both extended from filament by broad lateral connective extension 0.1-0.2 mm broad; filaments 2.2-3 mm long; styles 9-12 mm long. description: Erect or weakly spreading, sparingly branched shrubs 4-8 dm high from rhizomatous rootstock; stem terete; distally light green, densely spiculate and mi- nutely pubescent with hairs to 0.1 mm long, brownish, woody, glabrate below. Leaf-blades elliptic-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, (8.5) 10-16 cm long, (3) 4-8.2 cm wide, acuminate at tip, cuneate, sometimes oblique at base, entire to repand, bright green above, paler and duller olive-green beneath, glabrous; veins densely spiculate above, slightly raised, light yellow beneath; petiole 3-7 cm long, canaliculate, with dense, curved hairs on adaxial side to 0.1 mm long. Inflorescences of terminal and axillary spikes 1-4.7 cm long and 1-2.7 cm wide; flowers sessile, opposite and densely disposed along rachis, with bracts, bracteoles and sepals of similar dimensions, giving a loosely spreading appearance to inflorescence; in- ternodes (3) 4.5-6 (7) mm long, with 10-20 flowers per spike. Bracts linear-lanceolate to linear-subulate, acuminate, 12-22 mm long, 0.9-1.0 mm wide, sparingly pubescent; bracteoles linear-lanceolate to subulate, acuminate, 11-23 mm long, 0.6-0.7 mm wide, sparingly hirsute; calyx deeply 5-parted, 10-21 mm long; sepals linear-lanceolate, setaceous, 9.0-20.0 mm long, to 0.5 mm wide, sparingly hirsute; bracts, bracteoles and sepals slightly accrescent; corolla pale yellow, zygomorphic, 2-lipped, 21-22 mm long; upper lip slightly emarginate, 6 mm long, 2 mm wide, lower lip 3-lobed, middle lobe 7 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, lateral lobes 6 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, tube 1.0 cm long, 2.5 mm wide at base, narrowed to 1.5 mm about 4 mm above the base, finely pubescent with hairs to 0.05 mm long; style filiform, glabrous, 19 mm long, included; stigma 2-lobed, lower lobe more prominent, 0.6 mm long, 0.3 mm wide; stamens 2, included; the anthers 2-celled, 2 mm long, the sacs muticous, parallel, slightly superposed, the upper 1.9 mm, the lower 1.7-1.8 mm long; filaments 4-6 mm long, glabrous, inserted near distal end of posterior portion of tube near origin of upper lip; fruit an explosively dehiscent capsule, dark brown, clavate, woody, 14.2-15.2 mm long, lower portion contracted into a solid stipe 7.5-8 mm long, fertile portion expanded above, 6.5- 7.5 mm long, 3-4.4 mm wide; retinacula falcate, acicular, slightly cymbiform, 2.0-2.2 mm long, 0.8-1.1 mm apart; seeds 1-4, ellipsoidal, flattened, brown, minutely papillose, 3.5-4 mm x 3.1-3.6 mm.

description: Acaulescens perennis usque ad 25 cm alta, rhizomatosus; folia 4-verticillata; laminae oblanceolatae vel oblongae, 75-110 mm longae, 18-38 mm latae, utrinque pubescentes fulvo-tomentosae; inflorescentia scapoidea usque ad 19 cm longa, pedunculis et rachidibus pubescentibus; bracteae subulatae, 5-6 mm longae, 1.5 mm latae, conspicue triplinerves, abaxialiter dense pilosulae; bracteolae lanceato- subulatae, 2 mm longae; calycis segmenta lanceolata, adaxialiter glanduloso-punctata, ciliata; corolla subrosea vel purpurea, glabra, labio inferiore 3-lobato, lobis subaequalibus, abaxiliter glabris.

description: Acaulescent perennial 25 cm tall from a woody rhizome, the rhizome bearing numerous, well-developed, fleshy roots 10-13 cm long. Leaves clustered and appearing whorled, 4 per node, short-petioled, the petioles 7-15 mm long, the blades oblanceolate to oblong, 75-100 mm long, 18-38 mm broad, gradually narrowed and attenuate at base, obtuse to acute at apex, the surfaces pubescent, fulvous-tomentose, the lower surface, especially the costa and the lateral veins, more densely so than the upper surface, the margins entire or crenulate, ciliate. Flowers borne laxly, subopposite, on long-pedunculate scapes 16-19 cm long, the peduncles 6-13 cm long, these and rachis pubescent with trichomes 0.25 mm long, occasionally interspersed with a pilose overstory; bracts subulate, 5-6 mm long, 1.5 mm broad, conspicuously 3-nerved, densely pilose on abaxial surface, sparsely pubescent on adaxial surface, the margins ciliate; bracteoles lance-subulate, 2 mm long, 0.75 mm broad, pilose on apex of abaxial surface, glabrous on adaxial surface, the margins ciliate; calyx 6 mm long, the lobes lanceolate, 5 mm long, sparingly pubescent on abaxial surface, glandular-punctate on adaxial surface, the margins ciliate; corolla pale pinkish-purple, 16-17 mm long, the tube 6-7 mm long, the upper lip 10-11 mm long with lobes 6-7 mm long, the lower lip 11-12 mm long with subequal lobes 10-11 mm long, glabrous on the abaxial surface; stamens 2 mm long; anthers 1 mm long; pollen grains tricolpate, prolate, 41 x 26 µm, the apertures distinct, the exine of intercolpal region rather smooth, the colpi verrucose to gemmate (Fig. 2C); style filiform, pubescent, flared at apex into an asymmetrically hypocrateriform stigma. Capsule ellipsoidal, 12-13 mm long, minutely pubescent; seeds 4, laterally flattened, suboval in outline, 3 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, pubescent with long, appressed, bristle-like trichomes bearing minute lateral barbs or branches.

description: Herba caulescens perennis usque ad 50 cm alta; caules teretes vel subquadrati, dense pubescentes; folia opposita, brevi-petiolata, subcoriacea, laminis lanceolatis vel oblongis, 30-40 mm longis, 9-14 mm latis, supra atro-viridibus et nitidis, parce puberulis, subtus pallide viridibus, pubescentibus, margine cartilagineis et revolutis; inflorescentia spicata, 2-2.5 cm longa, pedunculis et rachidibus purpureis, pubescentibus; bracteae lanceato-subulatae, 6 mm longae, 1.25 mm latae, utrinque pubes- centes; bracteolae subulatae; 2 mm longae; calycis segmenta lanceolata, adaxialiter parce pubescentia vel glabra; corolla purpurea, intus albido-notata, labio inferiore 3-lobato, lobis subaequalibus, abaxialiter parce pubescentibus.

description: Caulescent perennial herb or subshrub to 50 cm tall. Stems terete to subquad rate, densely pubescent with straight to antrorse trichomes 0.25-0.5 mm long. Leaves opposite, short-petiolate, subcoriaceous, the petioles 1-2 mm long, the blades lanceolate to oblong, 30-40 mm long, 9-14 mm broad, narrowed to rounded at base, sometimes obliquely so, gradually narrowed to acute at apex, the upper surface dark green and nitid, sparingly and inconspicuously puberulous, the lower surface paler green, pubescent, the trichomes antrorse, the margin cartilaginous and revolute, glabrous. Inflorescence of terminal and subterminal spikes 2-2.5 cm long, the spikes sessile or borne on peduncles 1.5-3 mm long, the peduncles and spike axes dark purplish-red, pubescent like stem, the trichomes shorter, 0.25 mm long, the flowers subopposite to alternate along the spike axis; bracts lance- subulate, 6 mm long, 1.25 mm broad, pubescent on both surfaces with a mixture of eglandular trichomes and inconspicuous stipate glands, the margins ciliate; bracteoles subulate, 2 mm long, 0.5 mm broad, pubescent like bracts; calyx deeply lobed, 9 mm long, the lobes lanceolate, sparsely pubescent to nearly glabrous on abaxial surface; corolla purplish-red, marked with white writhin, 12-14 mm long, the tube 6.5-7 mm long, the upper lip 5 mm long with lobes 1.75-2 mm long, the lower lip 6.5-7 mm long, the lobes subequal, 5 mm long, the lower-central lobe sparsely pubescent on the abaxial surface; stamens 1.5-2 mm long; anthers 1.3 mm long; pollen grains tricolpate, subprolate, 39 x 30 ,m, finely reticulate, apertures distinct (Fig. 2A, B); style terminal, filiform, flared at apex into an asymmetrical subclavate stigma. Capsule ellipsoid, 8.5-9 mm long, glabrous to sparsely puberulent; seeds laterally flattened, suboval in outline, 3 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, densely pubescent with long, appressed, bristle-like trichomes bearing minute lateral barbs or branches.

description: Acaulescent perennial 12 cm tall from a woody rhizome, the rhizome bearing numerous, well-developed fleshy roots 10-12 cm long. Leaves clustered and appearing whorled, subsessile to short-petiolate, the petioles 8-13 mm long, the blades oblanceolate, 25-35 mm long, 5-9 mm wide, obtuse to acute at apex, gradually narrowed and attenuate at base, the surfaces pubescent, the trichomes confined mainly to the costa and the lateral veins, the margins cartilaginous, ciliate. Inflorescence a pedunculate scape 10.5 cm long, the peduncles 4.5-6 mm long, pubescent with flexuous trichomes 0.6 mm long and a glandular-punctate under- story, the flowers clustered, subopposite; bracts lance-subulate, 11 mm long, 3.5 mm broad, pubescent on abaxial surface, the margins ciliate; bracteoles lanceolate, 4 mm long, 1 mm broad, glabrous to sparsely pubescent at tip, the margins ciliate; calyx 7 mm long, the lobes lance-subulate, 5 mm long, glabrous; corolla magenta, 20-25 mm long, the tube 10-11 mm long, the upper lip 11-12 mm long, 10-11 mm broad with lobes 7-8 mm long, the lower lip 1 1-13 mm long with subequal lobes 11-12 mm long, the lobes glabrous, the tube sparsely pubescent on the abaxial surface; stamens 3 mm long; anthers 1.2 mm long; pollen grains tricolpate, prolate, 37 x 26 ,um, the apertures distinct, the exine verrucose (Fig. 2D); style filiform, pubescent, barely exceeding the stamens, flared at apex into an asymmetrical hypocrateriform stigma. Capsule not seen.

description: Frutex 1-3 m. altus; ramulis glabris, primo flavis deinde flaviglaucis, frequeintibus, maximis, spineseentibus; foliis coriaceis, 15-43 mm. longis, 5-17 mm. latis, ovatis vel ovato-lanceolatis, acutis vel obtusis, ad marginem integris vel subserratis, ad basim cuneatis; infloreseentiae axi crasso, 8-10 mm. longo, glabro, floribus non multis; bracteis deltoideo-ovatis vel latissimne deltoideis, ad dorsum sparse pubeseentibus, margine pilis brevibus et sparse glandularibus clavatisque ciliato; pedicellis crassis, glabris vel sparsissime puberulentibus, saepe 7 mm. longis; lobis calyeis deltoideis, acutis vel acuminatis, ad dorsum glabratis, pilis longis ciliolatis; petalis lanceolato-ovatis, truneatis, circa 2.5 mm. longis; drupis circa 8 mm. diametro.

description: Shrubs to 3 meters; braniehes glabrous, yellowish-tan, becoming, yellowish-gray; branchlets rather abundant, very stout, spineseent; leaves coriaceous, 15-43 mm. long, 5-17 mm. broad, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, acute to obtuse at the apex, the margin entire or with a few serrations, the base cuneate; infloreseenee-axis coarse, 8-10 mm. long, glabrous, with few flowers; bracts deltoid-ovate to very broadly deltoid, obtuse, sparsely pubescent on the outer surface, ciliate with short simple hairs and a few clavate glandular hairs; pedicels coarse, glabrous or very sparsely puberulent, about 7 mm. long; sepals deltoid, acute or acuminate, glabrate on the outer surface, ciliate with long simple hairs; petals lance-ovate, truncate, about 2.5 mm. long; fruit about 8 mm. in diameter.

description: Shrub or small tree; branches glabrous or minutely puberulent, grayish-tan to brown becoming maroon-gray, from little branched to much branched, the branchlets very slender, spineseent; leaves thinnish, glabrous or less often minutely sparsely pilose, 15-35 mm. long, 3-7 mm. broad, mostly oblanceolate (less often obovate, oblong, or spatulate), acute to obtuse at the apex, the margin entire (rarely serrate or dentate), the base subeuneate to cuneate; petiole slender, 1-3 mm. long, sparsely short-pilose; infloreseence an expanded pseudoraceme about 2 cm. long, the axis sparsely pilose to glabrate; bracts deltoid-ovate, sparsely pilose to glabrate on the outer surface, ciliate on the margin; pedicels glabrous to densely pilose (usually pilose below the abscission disk and sparse-pilose or glabrous above); sepals deltoid-ovate, sparsely pilose on the dorsal surface, ciliate on the margin; petals broadly obovate, glabrous, sometimes ciliate on the margin; anthers oval.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, F. A. 1944. Schinus L. Brittonia. 5: 160-198. f. 1-22.

description: Shrub or tree to 7 in.; branches thickish, glabrate, moderately branched; leaves imparipinnately compound, at length thickly membranaeeous, 8-17 cm. long, glabrous, the leaflets 7-13, usually about 9, obovate, 20-60 mm. long, subacute or rarely obtuse, mucronate, mostly entire or rarely crenate-serrate or serrate, tending to be subrevolute, minutely puberulent on the veins, darker and often shining on the upper surface, duller and lighter' below, subsessile; rachis-segments 1-3 cm. long, narrowly winged, minutely puberulent; petiole not winged, minutely puberulent, 2-3 cm. long; infloreseence an axillary panicle, 2-11 cm. long (usually about 8 cm.); bracts deltoid-lanceolate, puberulent on the outer surface, ciliate on the margin with simple hairs; pedicels sparsely pilose below the abscission plate, very sparsely puberulent with simple and glandular hairs above, about 1 mm. long; sepals broadly ovate, glabrous or very sparsely puberulent, ciliate with simple hairs; petals ovate, obtuse, glabrous; anthers ovate; fruit red, about 5 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, F. A. 1944. Schinus L. Brittonia. 5: 160-198. f. 1-22.

description: Trees; branches many, slender, brownish, minutely and sparsely puberulent at first but appearing glabrate; leaves imparipinnately compound, at length thickly membranaceous, 10-30 cm. long, glabrous or very sparsely and minutely puberulent, leaflets opposite, subopposite, or alternate on the rachis, 19-41, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 8-60 mm. long, acuminate or rarely acute, the tip usually curved, entire, with a few serrations, or serrate, cuneate to obtuse at base, sessile, slightly darker above, the rachis segments 4-11 mni. long, subalate, glabrous; petiole 2-3 cm. long, not alate, very sparsely and minutely puberulent; inflorescences terminal thyrses and much branched panicles axillary to the uppermost leaves, each 8-15 em. long, minutely puberulent; bracts deltoid, very sparselv and minutely puberulent on the dorsal surface, sparsely ciliate on the margin with simple hairs, caducous; pedicels about 2 mm. long, slender, puberulent below the abscission plate, glabrous above; sepals half-orbicular, glabrous on the outer surface, sparsely ciliate with simple trichomes; petals narrowly ovate, truncate, glabrous, about 2 mm. long; anthers oblong; fruit lavender-pink, about 7 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, F. A. 1944. Schinus L. Brittonia. 5: 160-198. f. 1-22.

description: Shrub to 3 m. high; branches light, glabrous, not spineseent; leaves coriaceous, ovate to orbicular, obtuse at the apex, entire to obscurely crenate-serrate, the base obtuse to subcordate, glabrous; petioles coarse, glabrous, 2-10 mm. long; inflorescence a coarse pseudoraceme, about 15 mm. long, glabrous; bracts deltoid, glabrate, ciliate on the margin; pedicels about 3 mm, long, glabrous; sepals deltoidovate, subacute, glabrous except densely ciliate with simple hairs on the margin; petals narrowly ovate, truncate, glabrous; fruit about 6 mm. in diameter.

description: Planta florens 22-34 cm diam et 54-98 cm alta; folia numerosa fragilia 11.5-29 cm longa spinosa ubique lepidota. Inflorescentia terminalis 5-6.2 cm diam lepidota; rami laterales 0.8-6.1 cm longi. Bracteae florales lepidoto-tomentosae pedicellum saepe excedentes margine erosae. Florum Q sepala late ovata vel ovato-triangularia 2-2.8 x 1.3-1.6 mm; petala adscendentia ovato-elliptica vel oblongo- elliptica 2.6-3.5 x 1.5-2.2 mm. Capsulae ovoideae (5.5) 6.5-8 mm longae.

description: Plant in flower 22-34 cm diam and 54-98 cm high, forming clusters of several individuals. Leaves many, brittle, 11.5-29 cm long; sheaths reniform, 1.6-3 x 3.8-5.3 cm wide, marginally finely spinose, glabrous becoming lepidote distally; blades triangular, 2-3.3 cm wide, covered with appressed cinereous scales above and beneath, dark green often suffused with red, marginally armed with antrorse and retrorse stramineous to red-brown spines 6-13 mm apart and 1.3-4 mm long. Inflorescence terminal, subcylindric, laxly bipinnate, 5-6.2 cm diam, densely lepidote when immature but becoming less so with age; scape 22-42 cm x 4.5- 6 mm, internodes 1-4.3 cm long, lepidote; lower scape bracts exceeding the internodes, uppermost scape bracts shorter than the internodes, ovate with linear appressed blades, 1.4-7.9 cm long, marginally sheaths denticulate, lepidote throughout; rachis 32-57 cm long; primary bracts similar to upper scape bracts, ovate with very short linear blades, 0.8-2.4 cm long, generally shorter than the branches, lepidote throughout; lateral branches subspreading, fertile throughout, generally densely to subdensely few-flowered, 0.8-6.1 cm long, lepidote. Flowers [male]: floral bracts generally exceeding the pedicels, membranous, flat to weakly navicular, narrowly ovate-triangular, 2-3.1 x 0.7-1 mm, apically acuminate, occasionally apiculate, marginally finely erose, sparingly tomentose-lepidote; pedi- cels slender, 1.5-2.3 mm long, glabrous to very sparingly tomentose; sepals ovate to ovate-elliptic, 1.3-2.2 x 0.9-1.1 mm, apically acute to obtuse, distally erose, glabrous; petals when dry appearing broadly ovate to oblong-ovate or obovate, distally somewhat convex, 2.6-3.5 x 1.6-2.4 mm, white, glabrous; ovary rudimentary; stamens apparently included, filaments adnate to base of petals. Flowers Q: floral bracts usually borne at the base of the pedicel but occasionally some distance up the pedicel, membranous, flat to weakly navicular, generally exceeding the pedicels, narrowly ovate to ovate-triangular, 1.6-4.5 x 1-2 mm, apically acuminate, distally erose, sparingly tomentose to lepidote; pedicels stout, 1.5-2.5 mm long, tomentose-lepidote; sepals broadly ovate-triangular to triangular, 2-2.8 x 1.3-1.6 mm, green-white, apically acute to obtuse, marginally hyaline, dis- tally erose, glabrous to sparingly tomentose; petals ascending, ovate-elliptic to oblong-elliptic, distally weakly convex, 2.6-3.5 x 1.5-2.2 mm, white, apically rounded, glabrous; ovary superior; stamens rudimentary. Capsules with stout pedicels 1.5-3.5 mm long, triqueterous, loculicidally and septicidally dehiscent, ovoid, (5.5) 6.5-8 x 3.5-5 mm, glabrous, faintly nerved.

description: Herbae perennes caespitosae, caulibus ramosis e basi erectis vel patentibus (9-)15-30(-33) cm altis; foIiis coriaceis, lamina foliorum radicalium triangularis vel oblongo-ovata (1-)2-5(-7) X (1-)2-6(-8) cm, pinnatisecta, lobis partitis, divisionibus ultimis brevibus triangularibus inaequalibus, rhachidibus peranguste alatis; petiolo laminae longiori; umbellis globosis terminalibus, involucratis; floribus bisexualibus subsessilibus (1-)3-6(-7), masculis pedicellatis (3-)8-16(- 20); calycis dentibus lineari-lanceolatis vel ovatis; corolla aurea; stylis divergentibus sepalis duplo longioribus; fructibus 1-5 fuscis ovoideis (2-)3-4(-5) X (1.5-)2-3(-3.5) mm, mericarpiis subteretibus, ultra medium spinulis brevibus, infra medium spinulis reductis vestitis.

description: Cespitose perennial herbs, glabrous, with 1-6 erect or ascending stems (9-)15-30(- 33) cm high, usually branching from a base covered with dried, blackened leaf sheaths and arising from a long, robust, vertical tap-root up to 2 cm diam. Basal leaves numerous, coriaceous, petiolate, triangular to oblong-ovate, (1-)2-5(-7) X (1-)2-6(-8) cm, pinnatisect, the lobes temately or pinnately divided into short, triangular, unequal, mu- cronate divisions with a narrowly winged rachis, the petioles (2-)4-8(-12) cm long, longer than the blade, narrowly scarious- sheathing at base; cauline leaves few, abruptly reduced upward. Inflorescence of simple globose cymes or solitary; peduncles slender, (0.5-)1-3(-6) cm long; involucre of 4-9 scarious-marginate bracts 1-5 mm long, entire or 3-5-lobed, connate at base. Umbels of (1-)3-6(-7) subsessile bisexual flowers and (3-)8-16(-20) staminate flowers with pedicels 1-3 mm long; calyx-lobes linear-lanceolate to ovate, ca. 1 mm long, mucronate; corollas bright yellow; styles twice as long as sepals, divergent. Fruits 1-5, dark brown, ovoid, (2-)3-4(-5) X (1.5-)2-3(-3.5) mm, cuneate at base, the mericarps subterete, their upper half covered with short, uncinate, basally dilated prickles ca. 0.5 mm long, their lower half with rudimentary prickles. Seed faces plane or with a slight commissural ridge.

description: Planta florens 21.5-27 cm diam et 42-79 cm alta; folia pauca 10.5-19.8 cm longa spinosa; lamina ubique lepidota. Inflorescentia terminalis 2-12.7 cm diam glabra; rami laterales (0.5) 2.2-6.3 cm longi. Bracteae florales glabrae plerumque subnaviculares margine erosae. Florum 6 petala oblongo-ovata vel ovata 3-4 x 1.9-2.6 mm patentia. Florum Q petala triangularia 3-3.8 x 2-2.5 mm. Capsulae late ovoideae 5.5-7 mm longae.

description: Plant in flower 21.5-27 cm diam and 42-79 cm high, forming large clumps of several to many individuals. Leaves few, 10.5-19.8 cm long; sheaths reniform, 1.8-2.8 x 3.5-4.5 cm, marginally inconspicuously spinose, glabrous and lustrous becoming lepidote distally; blades triangular, 1.7-3 cm wide, covered with appressed cinereous scales above and beneath, often suffused with pink, marginally armed with antrorse and occasionally retrorse red-brown spines 0.6-1.1 cm apart and 2.5-4 mm long. Inflorescence terminal, similar in both staminate and pistillate individuals, subcylindric or rarely cylindric, laxly bipinnate, 2-12.7 cm diam, glabrous; scape 12-29 cm x 3-5.5 mm, internodes 0.5-3.2 cm long, glabrous; lower scape bracts exceeding the internodes, upper scape bracts longer than to shorter than the internodes, ovate with linear, erose, appressed, lepidote blades, 1.8-5.7 cm long; rachis 18-55 cm long; primary bracts similar to upper scape bracts, narrowly ovate-triangular with linear lepidote blades, 0.9-1.7 cm long, generally much shorter than the branches and shorter than to exceeding sterile bases of branches, proximally erose, conspicuously nerved; lateral branches spreading, laxly few-flowered, proximally flattened, (0.5) 2.2-6.3 cm long or oc- casionally reduced to 2 collateral flowers. Flowers d: floral bracts shorter than or equal to slightly exceeding the pedicels, weakly navicular, ovate, 0.8-2 x 0.7-1 mm, apically acuminate, occasionally apiculate, lacerate to erose; pedicels slender, 0.8-3 mm long; sepals 3 or occasionally 4, ovate to broadly ovate, 1.3-2.3 x 0.9- 1.8 mm, green-white but drying brown centrally, apically rounded to acute, mar- ginally hyaline, distally erose, glabrous; petals 3 or occasionally 4, spreading, ovate or oblong-ovate, but appearing subspathulate after drying, 3-4 x 1.9-2.6 mm, white; stamens 6 or occasionally 8, exserted; ovary rudimentary. Flowers Q: floral bracts shorter than pedicels in fruit, flat to weakly navicular, narrowly ovate to ovate-triangular, 1-2 x 0.7-0.8 mm, apically acuminate, marginally hyaline, erose; pedicels on pistillate material at anthesis not seen; sepals ovate, 1.3-1.7 x 1.3- 2.2 mm, apically acute, marginally hyaline, glabrous; petals triangular, 3-3.8 x 2-2.5 mm; stamens rudimentary; ovary superior. Capsules with slender pedicels 1.5-3.5 (5.5) mm long, triqueterous, loculicidally and septicidally dehiscent, broadly ovoid, 5.5-7 x 5-6 mm, glabrous, castaneous, smooth.

description: Slender tree (ex Peyritsch) or liana ( ?), the branchlets cinereous, sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite or alternate, the petioles slender, 2-4 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, brownish when dried, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 3.5-6 cm. long, 1.8-3 cm. broad, rounded or obtuse at base, rounded or faintly emarginate at apex, the costa sharply elevated toward base and plane distally on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-8 per side, spreading, plane or faintly impressed on both surfaces, the veinlets immersed; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, fasciculate, 2-5-flowered, the peduncle minute; flowers about 10 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, 3-4 mm. long; sepals papyraceous, glandular-lineolate, broadly deltoid, about 1 mm. long, 1-1.8 mm. broad, obtuse at apex, entire or erosulous at margins; petals membranous or thin-carnose, glandular-punctate or -lineolate, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 5.4-5.8 mm. long, 3.5-4 mm. broad, entire and narrowly reflexed at margins; disk 2.2-2.5 mm. in diameter, about 0.5 mm. high at inner margin, inconspicuously flattened at outer margin; stamens spreading, the filaments about 1 mm. long, the anthers obrhomboid, about 0.5 by 0.7 mm., dehiscing by extrorse-lateral oblique apically confluent clefts; ovary short-conical, the style about 1 mm. long; ovules 4 per locule, in superposed pairs.

description: Shrub or slender tree 8 m. high, the branchlets slender, cinereous or brownish, usually sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles. stout, 7-20 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, olivaceous or greenish when dried, often glaucous beneath, oblong or elliptic or obovate-oblong, 15-27 cm. long, 4.5-11 cm. broad, attenuate (rarely obtuse or rounded) at base and decurrent on the petiole, shortly and obtusely acuminate at apex, entire and often narrowly revolute at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 7-11 per side, aseending, often arcuate, obscurely anastomosing near margins, prominulous or faintly impressed above, conspicuously elevated or prominulous beneath, the veinlets obscurely reticulate, immersed or faintly impressed on both surfaces; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, fasciculate, the peduncle glomerulate, few-flowered; flowers 24-30 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, 12-16 mm. long, subtended by crowded inconspicuous bracts; sepals thin-coriaceous, broadly ovate, 3-4 mm. long and broad, rounded at apex, entire and narrowly scariose at margins; petals 5 (rarely 6), papyraceous or submembranous, yellow or greenish, obovate-oblong, 10-13 mm. long, 7-10 mm. broad, entire, faintly parallel-nerved; disk 6-8 mm. in diameter, elevated at inner margin, conspicuously flattened and membranaceous at outer margin, concealing the petal-bases; stamens spreading, the filaments 2.3-2.7 mm. long, the anthers transversely ellipsoid, about 0.6 by 0.9 mm., dehiscing by horizontal apical confluenit clefts; ovary about 2 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style about 0.4 mm. long; ovules apparently 6 per locule, 2-ranked; fruiting pedicels conspicuously swollen, up to 4 mm. in diameter and 22 mm. long, the fruit apparenitly solitary, subglobose, 3-4 cm. in diameter, the. pericarp coriaceous, conspicuously rugose and lenticellate.

leaves opposite, the petioles 4-10 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous or thin-coriaceous, brownish when dried, obovate or elliptic-oblong, (6-) 8-17 cm. long, (2.5-)4-9 cm. broad, obtuse or narrowly rounded at base, cuspidate or short-acuminate at apex (acumen 2-7 mm. long, obtuse), entire and slightly thickened at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 7-11 per side, erecto-patent, prominulous or conspicuously raised on both surfaces, the veinlets reticulate, faintly prominulous oln both surfaces or obscure above; in- florescence axillary or on defoliate branchlets, 1-4(-10) cm. long, panieulate, usually shortly so, the peduncle stout, usually 2-5 mm. long, sometimes lacking, the primary branches congested on pedunele (sometimes solitary), few-flowered, slender, subtended by coriaceous ovate obtuse bracts 1-1.5 mm. long, the branchlets opposite or alternate; description: Liana, the branches stout, terete, the branchlets opposite, slender, cinereous, copiously lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles stout, 4-8 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, olivaceous or brownish when dried, obovate, 5-9 cm. long, 2.5-4.5 cm. broad, attenuate at base, roulnded and mucronate at apex (mucro 1-2 mm. long, callose, termi- nating the costa), entire and narrowly revolute at margins, the costa sharply raised above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 7-9 per side, spreading, straight, anastomosing near margins, prominulous on both surfaces, conspicuously so beneath, the veinlets inconspicuously reticulate, faintly prominulous on both surfaces; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, 2.5-4 cm. lonig, short-peduneulate, 4-6-times dichotomously branched, the branchlets stout, einereous, the bracts papyraceous, ovate, acute, about 1 mm. long; flowers solitary at apices of ultimate branchlets, 3.5-5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels 0.5-1 mm. long (above articulation); sepals carnose or sub-coriaceous, broadly ovate, 0.7-0.9 mm. long, 1.5-1.8 mm. broad, rounded or minutely apiculate at apex, irregularly erosulous at margins; petals thin-carnose or submembranous, broadly elliptic-oblong, 2.3-2.7 mm. long, 1.6-2.3 mm. broad, entire, obscurely longitudinally nerved; disk 1.5-1.7 mm. in diameter, 0.5-0.7 mm. high, sharply contracted at middle, expanded at basal and apical margins, projected beyond petal-bases, flattened at summit and connate with ovary except for staminal pockets; stamens erect, the filaments 0.5-0.6 mm. long, the anthers obrhomboid, about 0.2 by 0.3 mm., dehiscing by horizonital apical confluent clefts; ovary completely immersed, the style about 0.2 mm. lonlg; ovules 4 per locule, collateral in superposed pairs.

ovules 2 per locule, collateral; fruiting infloreseeniees greatly thick- ened, the pedicels 9-12 mm. in diameter, the fruits few (probably only 1 per inflorescence), subglobose, 6-8 cm. in diameter, the pericarp cori- aceous, 3-6 mm. thick, uniformly rugulose, the seeds apparently 3 or 4, oblong, about 4 cm. long and 2.5 cm. broad.

description: Slender tree with scandent branches or liana, the branchlets slender, einereous, sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles 6-15 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, brownish or olivaceous when dried, oblong-elliptic or obovate-elliptic, (7-)10-21 cm. long, (2.5-)4-7 (-8) cm. broad, rounded or obtuse or acute at base, rounded or faintly emarginate or obtuse or obtusely cuspidate at apex, entire (rarely obscurely crenulate) and narrowly revolute at margins, the costa sharply elevated on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-11 per side, erecto-patent, straight, arcuate near margins, plane or faintly prominulous or faintly impressed on both surfaces, the veinlets immersed; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, fasciculate, 6-16-flowered, the peduncle gemmiform, the bracts papyraceous, crowded, deltoid, minute; flowers 4-9 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, (2-) 4-10 mm. long; sepals papyraceous or submembranous, broadly ovate or ovate-deltoid, 1-2.2 mm. long, 1.5-3 mm. broad, rounded at apex, seariose and often erosulous or fimbriolate at margins, sometimes minutely glandular-punetate; petals similar to sepals in texture, oblong-ovate or elliptic-oblong, 3-5.5 mm. long, nearly as broad, entire or erosulous and often narrowly revolute at margins; disk 2-3.5 mm. in diameter, 0.5-1 mm. high, rounded or inconspicuously narrowed at outer margin; stamens suberect or spreading, the filaments 0.7-1.3 mm. long, the anthers reniform or obrhomboid, 0.4-0.5 mm. long, 0.6-1 mm. broad, dehiscing by extrorse oblique apically confluent clefts; ovary depressed-conical, the style 0.5-1 mm. long; ovules 4 per locule, in superposed pairs; fruiting pedieels 3-4 mm. in diameter, the fruit probably solitary, subglobose or obovoid, 1.5-2.5 cm. in diameter (probably larger at maturity), the pericarp coriaceous, 1-2 mm. thick, rugulose, glaucous, the seeds several, ellipsoid, up to 7 mm. long.

description: Slender tree or shrub up to 9 m. high, the branchlets stout, sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles stout, 10-17 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, olivaceous when dried, oblong-elliptic, 25-43 cm. long, 10-15 cm. broad, rounded or obtuse at base and apex, entire anid narrowly revolute at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 10-13 per side, erecto-patent, ascending near margins, prominulous above, prominent beneath, the veinlets immersed, sometimes faintly impressed; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, fasciculate, few-flowered, the peduncle gemmiform, the bracts small, coriaceous, erose at margins; flowers 15-18 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, 3-3.5 mm. long; sepals semiorbicular, imbricate, strongly unequal, the 2 outer ones 1-2 mm., the 2 inner ones 2-5 mm. long and broad; petals suborbicular or obovate, 7-9 mm. long and broad; disk about 5 mm. in diameter, 1-1.5 mm. high at inner margin, flattened on outer margin; stamens reflexed, the filaments about 2 mm. long, the anthers subreniform, dehiscing by extrorse-lateral oblique apically coiifluent clefts; ovary about 2 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style minute; ovules 2 per locule, superposed or collateral; fruiting pedicels greatly swollen, 5-7 mm. in diameter, the fruit probably solitary, subglobose, 5-7 cm. in diameter, the pericarp coriaceous, rugulose, lenticellate.

description: Perennis; caulibus gracilibus, glabris, ad 25 cm longis, internodiis folia excedentibus; foliis anguste lanceolatis, 3-5 mm lonais, 1.0-1.5 mm latis, patentibus vel recurvis, glabris, basi angustata, subpetiolata, pauce pilosis, apice acuto, minute apiculato; stipulis (vaginis) pauce pilosis; pedicellis axillaribus, glabris, capillaribus, 1-2 cm longis; floribus 4-meris, nutantibus; sepalis late ellipticoovatis, ca. 2 mm longis, 1.75 mm latis, submembranaceis, 1-nerviis; petalis oblanceolatis, 4-5 mm longis, bifidis, lobis 1-2 mm longis; stylis 3; ovulis nonnullis; seminibus oblique subreniformi-orbicularibus, 0.8-1.0 mm latis, facie minute vermiformi, dorso manifeste conico-tubereulato.

description: Stem suffruticose at base, prostrate, glabrous, tetragonal, very much branched, branches rising to ? 4 dm. tall. Leaves (at least of the numerous branches observed) spatulate-linear, 1-nerved, apically obtuse and mucronate or emarginate, 3-4.5 cm. long and 3-6.5 mm. wide, gradually attenuate below into a scarcely petiolate but when young hispid-ciliate base, blade glabrate on both faces but marginally ciliate. Panicle delicate, open and loose, 1.5-2.5 dm. long, lowest internodes about 4-7 cm. long, lowest rays 5-15 cm. long. Bractlets subulate, ciliate, about 3-4 mm. long. Pedicels puberulous, up to about 1.3 cm. long. Sepals attenuate-lanceolate, nerveless, glabrate or slightly puberulous; marginally hyaline, about 4 mm. long, barely exceeding the 3-valved capsule. Staminodia lanceolate-linear, attenuate above, apically entire, nearly equalling the sepals. Stamens scarcely exserted. Seeds said to be few and rugulose.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Suffruteseent, the straggling stems + 2 m. long, purplish. Leaves distant, broadly ovate or ovate-oblong, thick-chartaceous, dark-green and dull, at apex somewhat obtuse and mucronate, at base widely cuneate to rounded; blade 5-12 cm. long and 3-6.5 cm. wide, glabrous above, essentially so beneath, divided medianly by the single lengthwise nerve, lateral nerves evanescent; petiole nar- iow, 0.8-2.5 cm. long. Panicle very large, occasionally reaching 1.5 meters lonc, "foliose along the main rhachis," with 6-10 nodes, clammy-puberulous through- out, the internodes 1.5-2 dm. long, the lowest rays 3-4.5 dm. long. Bracts linear-lanceolate, 2-3 mm. long. Sepals caudate-acuminate, purplish, puberulous, -4- 3 mm. long. Staminodia nearly as long, filiform, entire, from an orbicular or deltoid base. Styles 3 or 4, long-exserted, as are the stamens. Capsule as long as the sepals. Seeds transversely rugose.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Stems erect or perhaps merely aseending, 3-6 dm. tall, fruticose at base, subterete or subtetragonal, nodose, much branehed, the branches very leafy, gla- brous, the internodes mostly 1-2.5 cm. long. Leaves spreading, mostly with smaller ones fascieled in their axils and thus appearing much crowded, filiform, principal ones 3-5 cm. long but only 0.4-0.6 (or at times 1) mm. wide, 1-nerved, involute, or channeled above, mucronulate, glabrous, their bases connate by a narrow membrane. Infloreseence a narrow and crowded, interrupted thyrse, much like that of Schiedea ligustrina, composed of from 3 to 5 pairs of many- flowered eymules, the lower pairs mostly rather distant and sometimes prolonged, the upper ones approximate; bracts of the lower pairs like the cauline leaves, of the upper very short and ovate- or lance-subulate, sparsely to densely puberulous. Peduncles and pedicels minutely pubeseent, 2-5 mm. long. Calyx campanulate, 2 mm. or less in length, usually five-parted; the sepals ovate, obtuse or a few subacute, rather fleshy, nearly nerveless, narrowly hyaline at edges, very slightly pubescent externally near the base. Staminodia at first short, finally almost as long as the sepals, linear-subulate, thickened at the base, where they are concave and apparently nectariferous on the inner side, at apex sharply bifid. Stamens normally 10 (8 in tetramerous flowers); filaments capillary, elongated and ex- serted. Ovary ovoid, containing about 15 ovules. Styles 3. Capsule ovoid, 3- valved, slightly exceeding the calyx. Seeds several, minute, reniform, nearly smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Subherbaceous, perennial, glabrous; stem 0.7-1.5 dm. long, tortuous, woody below, leafy toward apex. Leaves crowded and almost rosulate, spatulate or nar- rowly obovate-oblong; blade 9-19 cm. long and 3-6.5 cm. wide, pallid or sub- glaucous, thick-chartaceous and somewhat fleshy, weakly feather-veined (the ulti- mate veinlets ending free in the meshes of an areolar network), gradually nar- rowed below into a margined petiole (this ? 6 cm. long, thickened and almost clasping at the purplish base), at apex more or less obtuse (or bluntly rounded) and shortly or abruptly acuminate to mucronate (with an indurated, reddish point). Panicle stramineous when dry, very loose and open, 2-6 dm. long, with only 3-5 principal nodes, lowest internode 1.5-2.5 dm. long, lowest rays 2.2-3 dm. long (not 9-12 lines as apparently misprinted in Hillebrand, l.e.), median pedicels ? 1.2 cm. long. Bracts subulate, ciliate below, about 4 mm. long. Sepals nar- rowly to broadly lanceolate, hyaline at margins, more or less spreading- or retrorse-ciliolate, --- 4 mm. long. Staminodia slightly shorter than sepals (or at anthesis longer), linear or filiform from a suborbicular base, shortly bifid or sub- entire. Stamens long-exserted. Styles 3 or 4. Capsule ineluded. Seeds com- pressed, reniform-orbicular, transversely rugose, dark grayish-brown, dull, about 1 mm. across.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Suffruteseent or even more or less fruticose, 0.5-1.9 m. tall, the t.erete or sub- tetragonal stem branched near the base; branches straggling, glabrous. Leaves loosely disposed, glabrous, chartaceons, pale, greatly varying in shape from ovate- (or obovate-) oblong to narrowly elliptic-oblong (the blade from 5 cm. long and 3.5 cm. wide up t.o 10 cm. long and down to + 1.5 cm. wide, or in lower leaves much larger and ? 13 cm. long by + 6 cm. wide), aeuminate or bluntish at both ends (apex at times obtuse and abruptly mucronate), distinctly 1-nerved but with obsolete lateral venation, minntely revolute at the margin; petiole 1-7 mm. long. Panicle ample, very much branched, 1.5-4 dm. long, glabrate or toward florets slightly hispidulous, the rachis usually with 4-6 nodes, the lowest inter- nodes 5-10 cm. long, the lowest rays often 1-2.5 dm. long, many branches- in turn branching at their very base (into a main, spreading or ascending and a small, deflexed branhilet) ; ultimate branchlets filiform. Pedicels capilliform or gradually dilating above, commonly under 1.5 cm. long; bractlets short, subulate, at times somewhat puberulous. Sepals narrowly lanceolate, acute, glabrous, green (or, when dried, darkish but scarcely purplish), narrowly scarious-margined, about 3 mm. long. Staminodia linear from an orbicular base, apically bifid, ? 2.5 mm. long. Stamens exserted, filaments very delicate. Styles normally 3, long- exserted. Capsule usually a little shorter than sepals. Seeds few, black, com- pressed, much curved, transversely muricate or rugose, about 1 mm. long and 0.8 mm. wide.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Suffruticose, stem and branches more or less angled, glabrous, principal inter- nodes mostly 2-3 cm. long. Leaves broadly linear-oblong, with a not or scarcely narrowed auriculate and clasping base, 1-nerved, obtuse, mucronate, glabrous or at base of auricles setulose-ciliolate, flat or at extreme margins most minutely revolute, mostly 4-5.3 cm. long and 1-1.3 cm. wide. Panicle open, diffusely spreading, up to ? 3 dm. long (the 3 axial internodes observed on the one avail- able specimen each measuring 5-6 cm. long), its younger portions subglandular- puberulous; bracts ovate, apically attenuate or acuminate, basally broad and rounded-clasping, puberulous, 3-5 mm. long. Pedicels capillary, 8-16 mm. or median one ? 23 mm. long, subglandular-puberulous. Sepals ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate-linear, at apex acuminate, dorsally glabrate and more or less ob- viously 3-5-nerved, at margins scarious, about 4 mm. long. Staminodia lanceo- late, the attenuated apex entire. Stamens not exserted. Capsule 3-valved, nearly equalling calyx in length, few-seeded. Seeds smooth, flat, reniform-eircular, sub- mature ones about 0.9 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Very glabrous throughout, shrubby below, herbaceous abo-ve, perhaps under 0.7 m. tall, stem more or less subtetragonal and up to ? 1 cm. thick at the numerous nodes, simple or branched; branches at first divaricate then arcuate- ascending. Leaves narrowly lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate or uppermost linear, attenuate below to a subsessile base or to a margined petiole, elongately attenuate above to a very sharp apex, comumonly 1-1.8 dm. long and only 1.5-2 cm. wide. Panicle ? 1.5 dm. long, the filiform or capilliform rays spreading in all direc- tions, bractlets now broadly lanceolate now subulate, pedicels (glabrous) espe- cially delicate, median ones ? 2 cm. long. Sepals ovate to lanceolate, glabrous, at anthesis spreading, 1-2 mm. long and exceeding the anthers, searious at mar- gins; finally more or less costate below, approximate, becoming usually ? 3 mm. long. Stamens finally long-exserted. Staminodia at first entirely obscured by the short, congested stamens, finally elongated, flat-filiform from a broadish base, irregularly bifid. Styles 3, long-exserted. Capsule ellipsoidal in outline, scarcely exceeding the fruiting calyx.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Low, herbaceous, pruinose-puberulous on upper parts of branches and on infloreseence, otherwise glabrous, the simple branches rising from the base, 1.5-4 dm. tall, bearing 4 or 5 pairs of leaves. The lower leaves obovate-lanceolate or oblanceolate from a narrowed sessile base, at apex acute to acuminate, subcarneous, 3-10 cm. long and 1-2.5 cm. wide, 3-5-nerved, the uppermost 1 or 2 pairs diminished into small, subulate, 3-nerved bracts ? 2 cm. long. Flowers in a terminal, compact, globose thyrse about 2.5 cm. in diameter (sometimes with 2 lateral thyrses at the next lower node), composed of numerous many-flowered, short cymules. Sepals ovate, obtuse, nerved below the middle, 3-4 mm. long, shorter than the 4-valved capsule. Staminodia linear-oblong, obtuse, entire, one third to nearly as long as the sepals. Seeds few, larger than in the other species, tuberculate.

description: Glabrous, about 6 dm. tall, shrubby; stems numerous, somewhat assurgent and loosely intertwined, slender, stramineous, brittle, woody, their internodes + 2 em. long, the nodes swollen; leafy twigs green, often shaded with purple, espe- cially at nodes. Leaves fleshy, pale, somewhat flaccid, mostly filiform-linear but a few filiform, 1-nerved, shiny, acute at apex, slightly clasping at sessile base, with midrib deeply suleate above and prominently wide and thick below, 4-8 em. long and 1-3 mm. wide, entire with thickened margin, somewhat mareeseent. Flowers numerous, on slender pedicels; these puberulous, -+- 4 mm. long, bi- bracteolate at base, grouped in erect panicles 3-5 cm. long and ? 2 cm. wide. Sepals ? 3 mm. long, green, ovate, somewhat obtuse, glabrate. Staminodia slightly shorter than sepals, whitish, linear, with obtuse apex, swollen and yel- lowish near base. Stamens about 4 mm. long, those alternating with sepals slightly shorter than the others; filaments slender, white; anthers pale-yellow. Ovary pale-green, glabrous, subspherical; styles 3. Capsule about 4 mm. long. Seeds compressed, orbicular, 07 mm. wide, dark grayish-brown, dull, intricately and deeply stellate-grooved.

description: Perhaps suffruteseenit and elongate; internodes of the delicate, subterete, pallid, glabrous stem -+ 2.5 mm. thick and up to -+ 1.5 dm. long. Leaves oppo- site, pallid just as if glaucous, petiolate, up to 1.4 dm. long including petiole; petioles slender, involute, pilose-ciliate, 1-1.8 cm. long; blade subnarrowly deltoid- ovate, lengthwise more or less conspicuously 3-nerved, at apex sharply mucronate, at base subtruncate or moderately cordate, up to about 6 cm. wide, glabrate on both faces but irregularly and very sparsely ciliate oni the whitish-subindurated margins. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal, lax, more or less puberulent with commonly spreading and glandular setulae, without doubt very large; a sing,le branch seen, this basal, horizontal, filiform, about 2.6 dm. long, subtended by a lanceolate leaf less than 4 cm. long, its nodes 4, its lowest branchlets a single pair; these divaricate or even subreflexed, their bractlets ovate-lanceolate, hispid, at apex acuminate, about 5-8 mm. long. Median pedicels commonly 1.5-2.5 cm. long, very delicate, very minutely appressed-puberulent. Sepals oblong or ovate-oblong, more or less puberulent and glandular, 1.5-2.5 mm. long, at apex now obtuse now attenuate, subhyaline at the margins. Stamens (observed for a sing;fle flower at anthesis) ? half as long as the sepals; staminodia nlot observed. Styles 3, long-exserted, -+ 4.5 mm. long. Capsule very glabrous, shining, its valves 3- 3.3 mm. long. Seeds (a single one studied) brownish-black, compressed, orbieu- late in outline, entirely areolate-rugulose, about 1 mm. wide.

description: Liana, glabrous throughout or with the youlng parts sparsely brown-furfuraceous, the bralnchlets slender, lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles stout, 5-10 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous or thin-coriaceous, brownish or olivaceous when dried, obovate-oblong, 6-10 cm. long, 3.5-6 cm. broad, obtuse at base, rounded and usually mucronate at apex, entire and slightly thickened at margins, sparsely black-pune- tate beneath, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-8 per side, erecto-patent, straight, anastomosing near mar- gins, prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets inconspicuously reticu- late, usually prominulous above and plane beneath; infloreseence axil- lary, 1.5-5 cm. long, paniculate, the peduncle 6-18 mm. long, the branchlets opposite, few-flowered, subtended by coriaceous ovate obtuse bracts about 1.5 mm. long; flowers loosely arranged, often solitary at apices of ultimate branchlets, 8-10 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels stout, 3.5-4.5 mm. long (above articulation); sepals papyra- ceous or thin-carnose, ovate-deltoid, 1.3-2 mm. long, 2-3 mm. broad, rounded or obtuse at apex, oftenl narrowly seariose and faintly erosu- lous at margins; petals thin-carnose, elliptic-oblong, 4.8-5.5 mm. long, 3-4 mm. broad, subentire; disk 3-3.5 mm. in diameter, about 1.7 mm. high, contracted at middle, slightly expanded at basal and apical mar- gins, flattened at summit and connate with ovary except for staminal pockets, projecting about 0.4 mm. beyond petal-bases; stamens slightly reflexed, the filaments 2-2.2 mm. long, the anthers obrhomboid, about 0.4 by 0.6 mm., dehiscing by extrorse oblique apically confluent clefts; ovary completely immersed, the style about 1 mm. long; ovules 4 per locule, collateral in superposed pairs; fruiting infloreseences greatly swollen, the pedicels up to 6 mm. in diameter, the fruits few, obovoid, 7-9 cm. long, 3-4 cm. broad, obtuse or subacute at base and apex, conspicuously longitudinally striate when dried, the pericarp woody, rugose.

description: Arbor mlinima; ramulis gracilibus sed non 1 multis; foliis imparipinnatis, glabris, 7-12 mm. longis, foliolis 9-19 (plerumque 13-17) lanceolatis, lunatis, acutis vel acuminatis, ad basim subeuneatis, integris vel sparse serratis, 12-30 mm. longis; rhachidis segmentis alatis, 3-12 mm. longis; petiolis 10-13 mm. longis, arete alatis; infloreseentia panicula laterali 2.5-6 cmh. longa; bracteis deltoideolanceolatis, acuminatis, glabris vel margine minime ciliolato; lobis calycis deltoideis, subacutis, glabris et non ciliolatis; petalis anguste ovatis, truneatis, glabris; antheris ovatis.

description: Small tree; branches slender, glabrous, little br-anched; leaves imparipinnately compound, glabrous, 7-12 cm. long, the 9-19 leaflets (mostly 13-17) lanceolate, asymmetrical, acute to acuminate at the apex, subeuneate at the base, entire or sparsely serrate, 12-30 m. long; rachis-segments alate, 3-12 mm. long; petiole 10-13 mm. long, narrowly alate; infloreseences lateral panicles, 2.5-6 cm. long; bracts deltoid-lanceolate, acuminate, glabrous or with very few cilia on the margins; pedicels glabrous, about 1 mm. long and bearing 1 or 2 very small bracts; sepals deltoid, subacute, glabrous and not ciliate; petals narrowly ovate, trunicate, glabrous; stamens ovate.

description: Arbor; rami cylindrici 40-45 cm longi, 6-11 cm diametro, apice graciliores, costis leviter tuberculatis, supra areolas interdum constrictione horizontali; spinae radiales inaequales, duabus superioribus quam ceteris brevioribus; spinae centrales 1-3, inferiori longiore ad 4.5 cm longa; flos 6.5-7 cm longus, 4-5 cm latus; fructus ovoideus vel globosus, 5-6 cm diametro, spinis setosis flavis; semina 2.6-3.1 mm longa, 1.9- 2.6 mm lata.

description: Tree with few branches, 4-5 m tall; trunk well defined, 40-45 cm high, 19-20 cm diam. Branches mainly of first order, erect, parallel to each other, 6-11 cm diam., pale green; young branches with a slightly purple tint, not pruinose; mucilage cavities not evident in transverse stem sections; ribs 7-8(-9), slightly tuberculated, rounded to obtuse in transverse section, asymmetric in longitudinal section, 1 cm high, with a constriction on upper sides of areoles and sometimes an additional horizontal constriction between areoles; areoles in apical parts of tubercles, obovate to circular, 6-7 x 5-6 mm, with white nonglandular trichomes, deciduous at maturity; radial spines 7-9, acicular, stout, rigid, yellowish when young, white at maturity, becoming grayish with age, unequal in length, the longer ones to 1.3 cm, the two apical ones 2- 5 mm long; central spines 1-3, subulate, enlarged at base, stout, rigid, the basal spine longer than the others, 4.5 cm long, white, becoming gray with age, the 2 apical spines shorter than the other, 0.3-1 cm long. Flowers produced only at apices of the branches, one per areole, nocturnal, infundibuliform, 6.5-7 X 4-5 cm at anthesis; pericarpel with small, spherical tubercles, nearly 4 mm in diameter, green; areoles with reduced apiculate leaves and a few white non-glandular trichomes, but lacking spines; receptacular tube ca. 3 X 2 cm, with oblong bracts on decurrent podaria, the spines, 1-2, soft, setaceous; outer perianth segments obovate, green with reddish hue in middle, the margin entire to ciliate on the spatulate apex; inner perianth segments whitish green, the margin ciliate; stamens numerous, included, the filaments white; anthers basifixed, yellowish white; style whitish yellow; stigmatic lobes 6-7, 6 mm long, whitish yellow; nectar chamber 1.3 X 0.8 cm, with grooved walls, semi-enclosed by bend of lower stamens; ovary 5-6 X 5 mm. Fruit ovoid to globular, 5-6 cm diam.; spines setaceous, yellowish, 1 cm long, deciduous at maturity; seeds 2.6-3.1 X 1.9-2.6 mm, lenticular or ovoid, black, dull; testa with isodiametric cells on surface, the periclinal walls concave.

description: Reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes. Stems 3-10.5 dm long, reclining, trailing, or decumbent, branching, rooting at the nodes. Petioles 0.5-3 cm long, pubescent only at the base. description: Reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes. Stems (1) 4-13 dm tall, erect, simple or branching. Petioles 0.5-5 cm long, densely pubescent from node to base of leaf blade. description: Tree 8-10 m. tall with scaly, gray bark and branches symmetrically spreading into an oval crown. description: Simple or usually openly branched annual, 1-10 or more dmn tall; well developed stems rather coarse (2-4 mm thick), angled, glabrous to spreading-hairy, and often glandular-pubescent especially upward, often more or less reddish; most leaves alternate, ovate, the blades 1-4 cm long, 5- to 6-veined on each side of the midrib, glabrous to strigulose or strigose especially along margins and veins, serrulate, acute, rounded or subeuneate at base; petioles mostly 0.5-1.5 cm long, subglabrous to pubescent; upper leaves reduceed gradually to subulate or lanceolate bracts 1-12 mm long; infloreseence all open panicle of peduncled racemes elongating in fruit, more or less strigulose to glandular-pubescent; pedicels filiform, mostly aseending and 8-15 mm long; sepals red, oblong, obtuse, glabrous to setulose, mostly 3.5-4.5 mm long; upper petals rose or pink, oblong, obtuse, slightly exceeding the sepals, unituberculate, setulose on the claws; lower petals slightly longer, rose to pink, long-clawed, the distal half broadly spatulate to rounded; sterile stamen about as long as the sepals, with obcordate expanded tip; fertile stamen 3-4 mm long, the filament dilated toward base; anther about 1-1.5 mm long; style glabrous; stigma capitate; capsule subglobose, 3.5-4.5 mm in diameter; seeds more or less obovoid, about 1 mim long, brownish, tubercled.

Culm 1 per plant, scapiform, erect, central, 29-48 cm X 1.8-2 mm, trigonous, scabrous on angles; bract subtending the synflorescence foliaceous, linear, 9.5-27 cm long, surpass ing the synflorescence. Synflorescence terminal, paniculiform, pyramidal, somewhat condensed; main axis 5-8 cm long, strongly branched, the nodes 6-8, the first internode 1.7-3.5 cm long, the second internode 0.8-1.9 cm long, paraclades 3, on the basal node, patent, the second-order ramification present and branched, the main epipodium 0.7-1 cm long, strongly scabrous; prophylls 2-keeled; spikes sessile, ellipsoid, 5-7 mm long; spicoid bracts 1.5-1.7 mm long, pale brown, the apex obtuse, the margins membranaceous; floral bracts 3, partly connate, 1.8-2 mm long, the apex acute, the keel wingless, densely scabridulous; staminate flowers 3 per spicoid, the anthers obclavate, 1 mm long, the filaments 3-4 mm long; stigma branches 2, the style 0.5-0.7 mm long. Fructification biconvex, spheroidal, 2-2.2 X 1.1-1.3 mm, yellow-greenish and reddish-dotted, wrinkled, contracted at the apex and base.

description: A Lasiadenia rupestri Benth. habitu erecto parum ramoso, foliis oblongo-ellipticis apice obtusis vel rotundatis, floribus subsessilibus brevioribus, calycis lobis rotundatis differt.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. & Nevling, Lorin I. 1986. A new species of Lasiadenia (Thymelaeaceae) from Venezuela. Brittonia. 38: 114-118.

description: Erect, nearly unbranched or sparsely branched subshrub to 80 cm tall. Stem erect, straight, tapered from ca 8 mm in diam near base to ca 1.5 mm in diam at apex; bark on stem dark brown, dotted with small, round, light tan lenticels. Branches few, usually 1-2, reduced, short, subapical, floriferous, rarely with a few short branches appearing along stem. Twigs sericeous, glabrescent. Leaves few, 2-3 on new twigs, deciduous; lamina oblong-ellipsoid, 30-57 mm long, 12-32 mm wide, obtuse, rounded or retuse at apex, mucronate, obtuse to rounded at base, firmly chartaceous, glaucous or dark green and glabrous on upper surface, silvery green and densely sericeous on lower surface, the adaxial midrib somewhat immersed, the primary lateral nerves 10-12, diverging 55-70º from midrib, at first straight, then arcuately anastomosing ca 1 mm from margin, the veinlets finely reticulate, prominulous on upper surface, obscured by the indument on lower surface; petiole 2.5-3 mm long, stout, densely sericeous. Inflorescence terminal or subterminal, capitate, 10-15-flowered, short-pedunculate, the peduncle 1-2 mm long, densely sericeous. Flowers bisexual, grayish or yellowish-green, subsessile, the pedicel stout, 0.5-0.7 mm long, densely sericeous. Calyx tube suburceolate, straight, ca 7 mm long, 2-2.5 mm in diam at the orifice, strongly 10-ribbed, subcoriaceous, densely strigillose without, glabrous within, the calyx lobes 5, unequal, strigillose on abaxial surface, short-villous on adaxial surface, the outer broadly ovate-elliptic, obtuse or rounded at apex, 3.3-3.6 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, the inner suborbicular, rounded at apex, 1.8-2.5 mm wide. Stamens diplostemonous, subsessile, the antisepalous stamens inserted at the orifice, subexserted, the alternisepalous stamens included, inserted 2 mm below orifice; filaments slender, very short, 0.1-0.3 mm long; anthers equal, oblong, ca 1.2 mm long, 0.5-0.6 mm wide. Disc minute, annular, ca 0.5 mm long, densely strigillose. Pistil sessile, nearly equaling the calyx tube, densely strigillose. Ovary oblong-ovoid, 5-6 mm long, densely strigillose. Style terminal, ca 0.5 mm long, glabrous; stigma capitate, subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam, included. Fruits unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. & Nevling, Lorin I. 1986. A new species of Lasiadenia (Thymelaeaceae) from Venezuela. Brittonia. 38: 114-118.

description: Arbor 2-4-metralis; foliis oppositis simplicibus, laminis elliptico-lanceolatis vel oblanceolatis apice obtuse acutis vel acuminatis basi cuneatim angustatis 8-16 x 2.5-5.5 cm plerumque glabris, nervis lateralibus patentibus principalibus utroque latere ±50; inflorescentia cauliflora racemosa, 1-5.2 cm longa 3-multiflora, rhachide supra medium parce strigillosa basin versus glabrescenti; pedicellis in aestivatione 1 mm longis fructiferis 3-6 mm longis strigillosis; sepalis 4 vel 5 liberis aliquantum inaequalibus imbricatis orbicularibus ovalibusque vel obovatis apice rotundatis 2-3.7 x 2-2.5 mm apicem versus ciliolatis; petalis imbricatis valde inaequalibus, uno abaxiali libero oblanceolato- vel ligulato-oblongo, ceteris 3-4 in tubum conjunctis; staminibus fertilibus 2 adaxialibus interne connatis basi appendiculatis; staminibus sterilibus 2-3 liberis basi tubi insertis; disco cupulari leviter undulato; carpellis 4-5, fructificantibus 1-2 capsularibus ad apicem dehiscentibus monospermis obovatis 8-10 mm longis glabris extils prominente sulcatis costatisque 6.5 mm longis.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1980. New species from the summit of Cerro Guaiquinima, Venezuela. Brittonia. 32: 17-23.

description: Tree 2-4 m tall with gray, glabrous branches. Leaves petiolate, petioles 8-15 mm long; leaf-blades subascending to suberect, subcoriaceous, strongly punctate, dark green above, below dull green, mainly glabrous except for microscopic ap- pressed hairs toward the base of the upper midrib; lateral nerves extending to margin. Sepals 4-5, free, imbricate, somewhat unequal. Petals imbricate, strong- ly unequal, 1 abaxial petal free, oblanceolate- or ligulate-oblong, cucullate at the rounded apex, 5-5.5 mm long (immature), 2-2.2 mm wide (immature); other 3- 4 petals united into a tube 2.5 mm long, the 3-4 lobes oblong or spathulate-oblong, rounded at apex, 3 mm long, 2 mm wide. 2 fertile adaxial stamens connate within, oblong, 4.5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, appendiculate at the base with subshield- shaped, flattened appendages 0.3-0.4 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, one side dorsally minutely glandular-papillate; 2-3 sterile stamens free, inserted at the base of the tube, asymmetric, subfusiform-elliptic, one side somewhat curved, strongly nar- rowed toward the apex, 3-4 mm long, 0.5 mm wide at the base, densely villous on both sides in the middle. Disk 0.5 mm high. Carpels in bud 4-5, ovary 0.5 mm long, glabrous; ovules 2 in each cell, axile, superposed, ascending; fruiting carpels 1 or 2, capsular, dehiscent at the apex, obovate, 8-10 mm long, 7-8 mm wide, glabrous, prominently 12-sulcate and costate without, the costae covered with punctate glands; endocarp white, separating at maturity from the bony peri- carp. Seeds dark brown, broadly oblong-barrel shaped, 6.5 mm long, 5 mm broad, glabrous; aril white, delicate, present on the hilar side.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1980. New species from the summit of Cerro Guaiquinima, Venezuela. Brittonia. 32: 17-23.

description: Arbor parva, ramulis teretibus, brevi-fulvo-villosis; foliis oppositis, laminibus ovatis vel ovato-ellipticis, basibus fere obtusis, apicibus fere acutis, nrarginibus subintegribus, minute, remote, et inconspicuissime denticulatis, nerviis paucis, primis valde sursum curvatis, supra sparse villosis, subtus villosioribus, venis villosissimis; racemis supra-axillaribus, solitariis, unifloribus; receptaculis intus dense setoso-villosis, pauci-carpellatis; drupis sparse pubescentibus.
bibliographicCitation: Lasser, Tobias & Maguire, Bassett. 1950. A report on the plant of the Phelps Cerro Yaví expedition of 1947. Brittonia. 7: 75-90.

description: Tree 10-12 m. tall; branches terete, tawny, short-villous; leaves opposite, leaf blades 11-15 cm. long, 5-7 cm. broad, ovate to ovate-elliptic, the base ob- tuse or acutish, the apex acute or obtusish, the margins subentire, remotely and most inconspicuously and minutely denticulate, the primary veins conspicuous, of 3-5 more or less opposite or disjunct pairs, strongly curved upwards, the secondary reticulate, the upper leaf surface thinly villous, the lower more strongly vilIous, especially along the midrib and veins, the juvenile leaves densely tawny-villous, petioles about 1.5 cm. long, racemes supra-axillary, solitary, apparently uniflorus, peduncles about 1 cmr. long; pedicels about 5 mm. long, villous-tomentose; the receptacle reflexed, orbicular, densely setose-villose within, few-carpelled, apparently 7 or less; drupes about 1.5 cm. long, asymmetrical, subsessile, scantily pubescent.
bibliographicCitation: Lasser, Tobias & Maguire, Bassett. 1950. A report on the plant of the Phelps Cerro Yaví expedition of 1947. Brittonia. 7: 75-90.

description: Arbor ad 20 m. alta, trunco profunde sulcato; ramulis teretibus cinereis, juventute cum pedicellis arctissime puberulis mox glabris; pedicellis 12-20 mm. longis supra tenuiter canaliculatis; laminis sub-coriaceis oblongis, 6-10 cm. longis, 2.5-5 cm. latis, basi rotundato-truncatis, apice breviter obtuse acuminatis, margine integris, utrinque praeter costam subtus brunneo-tomentellam glabris, subtus disperse brunneo-glandulosis, costa supra elevata subtus prominente, nervis secundariis utroque 6-11 rectis prope margines adscendentibus supra leviter impressis subtus prominentibus, venulis conspicue transverse reticulatis utrinque prominulis vel subplanis; inflorescentiis spicatis axillaribus ubique brunneo-tomentellis, juventute ad 7 mm. longis; floribus nt videtur circiter 5-fasciculatis, bractea obovato-oblonga obtusa circiter 2 mm. longa subtentis; alabastris intus nigro-glandulosis.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description:
This species, the well-known Amazonian "Aquariquara, " noted for its extremely durable wood, is represented in Krukoff’s collections by:5159 (basin of Rio Jurua, Amazonas), 5716 (basin of Rio Purus, Acre Territory), 1690 (Rio Machado region, Matto Grosso), and by Froes 1773 (Rio Maracassume region, Maranhao). It has been mentioned in literature many times, but only van Tieghem1 appears to have accurately discussed the flowers. A more complete description of the inflorescence, based on Krukoff 5159, is here given:

Arbor 15-30 m. alta; inflorescentiis spicatis axillaribus breviter pedunculatis ubique dense brunneo-tomentellis, sub anthesi 2-4 cm. longis; rhachide angulata; floribus sessilibus 2-5-fasciculatis, bractea minuta ovata caduca subtentis; calyce cupuliformi, 1 mm. alto, 1.5-2 mm. diametro, intus nigro-glanduloso, margine obscure 5-dentato; petalis 5 carnosis valvatis ovato-oblongis, sub anthesi circiter 1.5 mm. longis et 0.7 mm. latis, apice acutis leviter inflexis, intus glabris et nigro-glandulosis; staminibus 10 alternatim inaequalibus quam petalis paullo brevioribus, filamentis gracilibus glabris basi cum petalis cohaerentibus; antheris 4-locellatis subglobosis circiter 0.3 mm. diametro; ovario globoso minutissime luteo-pulverulento, sub anthesi 0.6-1 mm. diametro, loculis 5 (dissepimentis evanescentibus), ovulo in quo-que loculo 1, a placenta centrali pendulo.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description: Frutex ut videtur erectus ramulis junioribus inflorescentiisque puberulis vel breviter pubeseentibus exceptis glaber, ramis teretibus, brunneis, vetustioribus, glabris, ramulis ultimis gracillimis; foliis membranaceis vel submembranaceis, oblongo-ellipticis vel late oblongo-lanceolatis, 5-10 cm. longis, 2-4 cm. latis, in sieco olivaceis, nitidis, utrinque glabris vel junioribus ad costam minutissime obscureque puberulis, longe acuminatis, basi late acutis vel subrotundatis, margine deorsum integris, sursum irregulariter late dentatis vel dentato-serratis, dentibus apicibus subindurato-glandulosis, obtusis, nervis primariis utrinque 7-8, gracilibus, subtus elevatis, distinctis, plerumque fureatis, in dentibus exeuntibus, haud vel obscurissime anastomosantibus, reticulis obsoletis vel subobsoletis, lineis nervilliformibus obsoletis; petiolo minute puberulo, 577 mm. longo; inflorescentiis axillaribus, subdense multifloris, paniculatis, 3-5 cm. longis, quam foliis multo brevioribus, minute brunlleo-puberulis, ramis primariis paucis, inferioribus ad 2 cm. longis, superioribus gradatim brevioribus, floribus subconfertis, in ramulis racemose dispositis, albidis, eirciter 4 mm. diametro, prophyllis binis, parvis, pubeseentibus, oblongo-ovatis, acutis vel acuminatis, 0.6-0.8 mm. longis, pedicellis pubeseentibus, 1.2-1.5 mm. longis, bracteolis lineari-lanceolatis, acuminatis, pubeseentibus, eirciter 1 mm. longis; calyeibus extus breviter pubeseentibus, lobis late ovatis, acutis vel subobtusis, eirciter 1 mm. longis, vix vel obscurissime breviter 2-lineolatis, margine brevissime ciliatis; corollae tubo eirciter 1.2 mm. longo, lobis 5, late suborbiculari-ovatis, late rotundatis, tubo subaequantibus, margine minute erosodenticulatis, lineato-nervosis, nervis 3, distinctis; filamentis glabris, eirciter 1 mm. lonrgis; antheris ellipsoideis, 0.5 mm. longis; ovario glabro, eirciter 1 mm. diametro, pulviniformi; stylis brevissimis.
bibliographicCitation: Merrill, Elmer D. 1941. Plants Collected on the Vernay-Cutting Expedition. Brittonia. 4 (1): 23-68.

description: Liana lignosa. Lamina foliorum majorum 8.5-15.3 X 4-6.8 cm, lanceolata vel elliptica, supra sparsim velutina vel glabrata vel glabra, subtus velutina, pilis V-formibus; petiolus 0.9-1.4 cm longus. Inflorescentia ex pseudoracemo axillari solitario vel pseudoracemis in thyrsis terminalibus dispositis constans, floribus in quoque pseudoracemo 12-20; pedunculi (2-)3-7 mm longi, pedicelli (4-)5-9 mm longi. Bracteae 1.3-1.5 mm longae, eglandulosae; bracteolae 1.2-1.7 mm longae, oblongae, una bracteola cujusque paris uniglandulosa, altera bracteola eglandulosa. Petala lutea, glabra, limbo abaxialiter carinato. Samara ignota.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, C. 2001. Novelties in Mascagnia (Malpighiaceae). Brittonia. 53: 405-415.

description: Woody vine. Laminas of the larger leaves 8.5-15.3 X 4-6.8 cm, lanceolate to ellipti- cal, apex acuminate to briefly caudate, base cordate to rounded, adaxially sparsely velutinous but soon glabrate to glabrous except for hairs retained on the costa and major veins, abaxially velutinous, hairs V-shaped and sessile or subsessile, the arms 0.1-0.6 mm long, with 1-2(-3) impressed glands near the base and 0-2 additional glands distally, usually with (1-)2 glands on the sur- face ca. 1-2 cm below the apex and with 2 marginal glands just below the apex; petiole 0.9-1.4 cm long, tomentulose, eglandular; stipules 1-2 mm long, linear, interpetiolar. Inflorescence unit a pseudoraceme of 12-20 flowers, borne on an axis 1-3 cm long, either axillary and solitary, or several arranged in a terminal thyrse. Peduncles (2-)3-7 mm long, 0.4-0.9(-1.4) X as long as pedicels, to- mentulose; pedicels (4-)5-9 mm long, very sparsely tomentulose. Bracts 1.3-1.5 X 0.3- 0.5 mm, narrowly triangular, eglandular or sometimes with an inconspicuous callose region at the base. Bracteoles subequal, 1.2- 1.7 X 0.4-0.6 mm, oblong, one of each pair with a discoid gland 0.3-0.5 mm diam., the second bracteole eglandular or sometimes with an inconspicuous glandular region at the base; pair of bracteoles subopposite or sometimes to 1 mm apart, inserted at about the middle of the peduncle or sometimes in the distal 1/4. Calyx of 4 biglandular lateral sepals and 1 eglandular anterior sepal; lateral sepals exceeding the glands by ca. 1 mm, the glands ca. 2.5 mm long, decurrent. Petals 5, yellow, glabrous, the limb abaxially carinate, the margin erose, eglandular; lateral petals: claw 1.5-2 X 0.5 mm, limb 4-4.5 X 4-4.3 mm, suborbicular; posterior petal: claw 2 X 0.7 mm, limb ca. 5 X ca. 4.5 mm, broadly obovate to suborbicular. Androecium of 10 subequal stamens; filaments (1.5-)2-2.5 mm long, the anterior one the longest, the posterior one the shortest and ca. 1.5 X as wide as the rest, connate at base; anthers ca. 1.3 mm long, glabrous. Ovary tomentose-sericeous; styles erect or slightly divergent, subequal, 2.7-2.8 X 0.4 mm, the apex dorsally blunt or acute. Samara not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, C. 2001. Novelties in Mascagnia (Malpighiaceae). Brittonia. 53: 405-415.

description: Liana lignosa. Lamina foliorum majorum 6.5-9.6 X 3.5-5.4 cm, ovata vel late elliptica, utrinque velutina, pilis V-formibus; petiolus 0.6-1 cm longus. Inflorescentia ex pseudoracemo corymboso solitario constans, floribus in quoque pseudoracemo 8-10; pedunculi 4-7.5 mm longi, pedicelli 7.5-9.5 mm longi. Bracteae 1-1.5 mm longae, eglandulosae; bracteolae 0.8-1.2 X 0.4-0.5 mm, oblongae vel ovatae, una bracteola cujusque paris vel ambae uniglandulosae. Petala lutea, glabra, limbo abaxialiter carinato. Samara 1.8-2.2 cm diametro, ala laterali basi continua, crista dorsali 2-2.5 mm alta.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, C. 2001. Novelties in Mascagnia (Malpighiaceae). Brittonia. 53: 405-415.

description: Woody vine to 9 m; branches tomentu- lose when young, becoming glabrous in age; flowering shoots leafy. Lamina of the larger leaves 6.5-9.6 X 3.5-5.4 cm, ovate or broadly elliptical, apex acuminate or briefly so, base truncate to cordate, adaxially and abaxially velutinous, the hairs V-shaped and sessile, each arm (0.2-)0.4- 0.6(-0.7) mm long, with 1-2 impressed glands near the base and 1-2 impressed additional glands distally or eglandular, with 2 marginal glands just below the apex; petiole 0.6-1 cm long, densely reddish velutinous, eglandular; stipules 1.2-1.5 mm long, linear, interpetiolar. Inflorescence an axillary, solitary, congested corymbose pseudoraceme of 8-10 flowers, borne on an axis 0.6-1.3 cm long, the 2 lowest flowers not distinctly separated from the aggregate. Peduncles 4-7.5 mm long, 0.5-0.8 X as long as pedicels, densely velutinous; pedicels 7.5-9.5 mm long, densely velutinous. Bracts 1-1.5 X 0.6-0.7 mm, oblong to sometimes ovate, eglandular. Bracteoles subequal, 0.8-1.2 X 0.4-0.5 mm, oblong to ovate, one or both with a prominent gland to 0.2 mm diam.; pair of bracteoles subopposite or to 0.5 mm apart, inserted usually at or near the apex of the peduncle or sometimes to 3.5 mm below it. Calyx of 4 big-landular lateral sepals and 1 eglandular anterior sepal; lateral sepals exceeding the glands by ca. 1 mm, the glands ca. 1.5 mm long, decurrent. Petals 5, yellow, glabrous, the limb abaxially carinate, briefly hastate at base, the margin erose, eglandular; lateral petals: claw ca. 1.5 X ca. 0.4 mm, limb ca. 4.5 X ca. 4.5 mm, orbicular; posterior petal: claw ca. 2 X ca. 0.6 mm, limb ca. 4.3 X ca. 3 mm, oblong. Androecium of 10 sub-equal stamens; filaments 2-2.7 mm long, the anterior one the longest, the posterior one and those opposing the posterior-lateral petals the shortest; anthers 0.9-1 mm long, glabrous. Styles erect and slightly divergent, subequal, 2.3-2.5 X 0.3-0.4 mm, the anterior one slightly longer and stouter than the posterior two, the apex dorsally blunt. Samara 1.8-2.2 cm diam., suborbicular to orbicular, the lateral wing continuous at base and at apex except for a distal shallow notch ca. 2 mm deep, sericeous; central dor- sal winglet (4.5-)5.5-7 X 2-2.5 mm; nut 3-3.5 mm high; torus 2 mm high, surrounded by a wide, glabrous, 3-lobed, disciform outgrowth of the receptacle.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, C. 2001. Novelties in Mascagnia (Malpighiaceae). Brittonia. 53: 405-415.

description: Shrub, to 4 m high, branched, the branches 2-5 mm in diameter, hirsute, becoming glabrescent, striate; leaves lanceolate, 27-128 mm long, 8-42 mm wide, usually acute, sometimes more or less acuminate, rarely obtuse, glabrous above, slightly pubescent beneath, becoming glabrescent, entire, attenuate at base, the costa prominulous beneath, with 6 to 8 pairs of lateral veins; petioles 1.5-6 mm long, concave above, convex beneath, hirsute; racemes conical, acute, 8-10 mm wide, simple, terminal or axillary, pedunculate (the peduncle 5-14 mm long), the axis 3.5-10 cm long, hirsute, striate, bracteate, the bracts acute-triangular, 1.8-2.2 mm long, 1.2-1.6 mm wide, deciduous, ciliate, 1-nerved, slightly pubescent beneath; flower 4.2-5. mm long, the pedicels 1.2-1.5 mm long, finely pubescent; outer sepals free, triangular, acute, ciliate, glabreseent beneath, the two lower 2-2.5 mm long, 1.6-1.8 mm wide, 3-nerved, rarely 1-nerved, the upper sepal 2.4-2.8 mm long, 1.8-2 mm wide, 5-nerved, rarely 3-nerved; wings 5-5.2 mm long, 4-4.8 mm wide, obovate, more or less acute at base, 3-nerved, finely pubes- cent beneath; keel 5.2-5.8 mm long, 3-3.8 mm wide, orbicular, plicate, glabreseent within, obtuse at base, 3-nerved, 3-lobed, the middle lobe obtuse-subemarginate, sometimes slightly pubescent on a convex longitudinal line; upper petals elongate-spatulate, pubescent; stamens 8, the filaments 3-3.8 mm long, almost entirely united, the free part 0.6-1.2 mm long, glabrous; ovary ovoid, 1.5-2 mm long, 1-1.2 mm wide, pubescent; style 2.4-2.6 mm long, geniiculate above the base, glabrous, thicker toward the apex; stigma with 2 lobes, the lower acute, the upper 1-tubereled, the tuberele papillose; drupe ellipsoid, 5-7 mm long, 3.5-4 mm wide, pubescent, reticulate.
bibliographicCitation: Ferreyra, Ramon A. 1957. A Revision of the Venezuelan Species of Monnina. Brittonia. 9 (1): 9-18.
