description: Humillima, breviter caulescens. Folia multa, caudicis apice rosulata; vaginis omnino occultis; laminis patentibus, linearibus, 6 cm longis, 2.5 mm latis, subcoriaceis, minute serrulatis, basi pilis albis crispis parcissime vestitis alibi glabris, interioribus basi albis. Laminarum anatomia: Fila vascularia adaxialiter chlorenchymate non omnino obsita; chlorenchyma abaxiale uniforme; cellulae subepidermales oblongae in parietibus tenues; cellulae substomatales scleroideae oblongae plerumque triseriatae in parietibus minute multo porosae. Inflorescentia subsessilis, e rosulae centro emergens, simplex, pauciflora, dense ovoidea, 10 mm longa, laxissime albo-villosa. Bracteae florigerae ovatae, acuminatae, quam sepala breviores, convexae, integrae, tenues, valde nervatae, virides. Sepala lib- era, lineari-lanceolata, membranacea, 7 mm longa, posteriora conduplicata, cucullata; ovario supero, pluriovulato. Capsula subellipsoidea; seminibus reticulatis.

description: Caudex ignotus sed verisimiliter crassus. Folia multa, rosulata; vaginis omnino occultis; laminis linearibus, acutis, pungentibus, ad 15 cm longis, 8 mm latis, supra vivis triste viridibus, siccis atris lucidisque, subtus pallidioribus, utrinque dissite lepidotis sed supra basin mox glabris, ad basin versus squamis albis tenue stellatis persistentibus et minute antrorso-serrulatis. Laminarum anatomia: Fila vascularia adaxialiter chlorenchymate non obsita; chlorenchyma abaxialia uniformia; cellulae sub- epidermales quadratae vel oblongae sub nervis saepe resiniferae in parietibus distincte variabiliter incrassatae; cellulae substomatales binis in parietibus mediocriter incrassatae; pori substomatales fere occlusi. Inflorescentia subsessilis, e rosulae centro emergens, simplex, submultiflora, dense ovoidea, 20 mm longa, glabra. Bracteae florigerae suborbiculares, integrae, rigidae, quam sepala paulo breviores, apice incurvatae, obtusae. Ovarium superum. Capsula ellipsoidea, seminibus reticulatis, exappendiculatis.

description: Shrubs about 2 in. high; leaf-scars crowded, oval, about 2 mm. wide; leafblades subsessile, coriaceous, oblanceolate, 5-11 cm. log, 8-15 mm. wide, triangular-acute at the apex, tapering narrowly at the base into a thick marceseent articulation-joint termiuating a cup-like projection (about 2 mm. long) of the stem, the costa promineuit above, subplaue beueath, the secondary veius plane above, prominulous and evanescent below, 0.5-1 mm. apart, aseending at an angle of about 550, the tertiary veius ofteu irregular-parallel, somewhat evanescent, the margin thickened, the teeth minute, appressed, 2-4 mm. apart; stipules persistent, deltoid, 3-4 mm. long, acute, the shorter lateral cilia subfimbriate at basal angle; flowers 5-10, termiual and solitary inl the axils of the uppermost leaves, the pedicels slender, about 0.5 mm. wide, the articulation-joiut extending at least to the middle, the bracts triauigular-subulate, the cilia short, well-spaced, ofteu with bractlets up to 2 mm. long scattered along the pedicel, 5-15 mm. from the base; sepals 5, unequal, coriaceous, deciduous at anthesis, dorsally submarceseent or smooth, subrotund to oblong, the outermost the smallest, about 4 mm. long, 5 mm. wide (when not flattened), obtuse, often vaguely or distinctly retuse, the sinus minutely erose-glandular or bearing a minute glandular cilium at its base, roundobtuse or auriculate at base, the margin thin, subpellucid, entire, the veins wellspaced, immersed, parallel-ascending in middle, flabellate toward the margin; petals yellow, equal in length, subequal in width, obovate-oblong, about 18 mm. long, 10-12 mm. wide, round-obtuse at the apex, subelawed or tapering little toward the base, the veins parallel-ascending; stamens unequal, subsessile (the mass of fused filaments about 0.5 mm. long), the anthers 20-25, linear, subfaleate, 6-7 mm. long, about 0.8 mm. wide, the ventral cells longer than the dorsal cells and forming a cup (about 0.3 mm. long) over the former; pistil arcuate, smooth, the ovary 3-angled, ovate-triangular, about 7 mm. long, 1.4 mm. wide, the style rostrate and awl-shaped; capsule thin-coriaceous, marceseent-striate, subfaleate and fusiform, 1.5-2 cm. long, the seeds smooth, terete, oblong, about 1.5 mm. the wing 0.5-0.7 mm. long at each end.

description: Shrubs; leaf-sears conspicuous; leaf-blades sessile, crowded, coriaceous, linearlanceolate, straight or somewhat sickle-shaped, 15-25 cm. long, 17-26 mm. wide, acute at the apex, tapering narrowly toward the base, the margin revolute, serrate, the teeth minute, 0.5 mm. long, 3-7 mm. apart, the costa striate, bigrooved (on the under side of lamina), the secondary veins subplane above, prominulous beneath, crowded, about 1 mm. apart, ascending from the costa at an angle of 40-50?; stipules widely ovate, 2-3 mm. long, appressed; flowers not seen; infloreseence (in fruit) racemose, the rachis rough, angular, up to 8.5 cm. long, the pedicels slender, up to 2.7 cm. long, expanding somewhat at base, the articulation-joint 2-7 mm. from base, the bracts deciduous; capsule erect or somewhat pendent, thin-coriaceous, irregular-striate, 3-angled, fusiform-faleate, 20-25 mm. long, about 2 mm. wide in the middle, the margin subsearious, the persistent style short and uncinate, the seeds glandular, shiny, terete, irregularly verrucose, narrow-oblong, about 2 mm. long, the wing about 0.5 mm. long at each end.

description: Herba carnosa glabra; caule singulo carnoso; foliis alternis ellipticis, elliptico-subovatis, suborbiculatis vel subobovatis, apice rotundatis vel subacutis, saepe emarginulatis, basi rotundatis obtusis ad petiolum transverse cordulatis, palmatim 5-7-nerviis; spicis in panicula laxa dispositis; drupa globoso-obovoidea, apice subobliqua.

description: A glabrous, succulent, terrestrial or saxicoline herb; stem simple, stout, up to 1 cm. thick when dry, ascending to 5 or 8 cm. from the decumbent, rooting basal part, the internodes very short, the nodal leaf scars large and conspicuous; leaves rather thick and fleshy when growing, alternate, elliptic, elliptic-subovate, suborbicular, or subobovate, with rounded or slightly pointed, often emarginulate apex, slightly narrowing downward to the rounded, obtuse base, with the margins cordulate and meeting over the petiole, up to 9.5 cm. wide x 12 cm. long but mostly somewhat smaller, palmately 5-nerved or the innermost pair of nerves slightly coalescent with the midrib near the base, or the larger leaves 7-nerved with the outermost pair inconspicuous, the midrib and lateral nerves delicately branched upward as viewed by transmitted light, green above, paler beneath with the nerves red, drying coriaceous and subtranslucent, narrowly revolute; petiole red, up to 12 cm. (or more?) long; spikes 6-8 or sometimes up to 14 cm. long, in a red, terminal or axillary, paniculately 2-4 di- or trichotomously branched inflorescence, up to 10 to 20 cm. long from the base to the first branch, but commonly somewhat shorter, the branches up to 3-6 cm. long, subtended by narrow bracts 5-10 mm. long; peduncles of the individual spikes 5-10 mm. long; floral bracts somewhat irregularly rounded-peltate; fruit about 0.8 mm. long, globose-ovoid, glandular-verrucose, with slightly oblique, obtuse apex; stigma slightly subapical.

description: Herbaceous plant 6-10 cm tall. Stem suberect, non-cormous, 1-2 cm long, 2-2.5 mm diam, glabrous; internodes few and short, 0.3-0.5 mm long. Leaves alternate, 2 or 3 per plant, petiolate; petioles 2-3.4 cm long, sparsely and remotely pubescent to glabrate, equalling or shorter than the leaf blade; leaf blade membranous (in dried state), ovate, acuminate at apex, subcordate or barely subpeltate at base, 4-5.2 cm long, 2.5-3.7 cm wide, glabrous both sides or the upper surface provided with a few remote hairs, 5 (7) palmately nerved, prominently ciliolate most of length with hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, not evidently punctate. Spike solitary, terminal, 6.5 cm long; rachis (in dried state) verruculose-papillate longitudinally; bracts orbicular, 0.3-0.4 mm diam, verruculose-papillate. Fruit basally attached, orange-brown throughout, ellipsoid-oblong, 0.6-0.7 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm wide, minutely verruculose, ventrally concave; stigma terminal, capitate.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1986. A new species of Peperomia (Piperaceae) from Venezuela. Brittonia. 38: 220, 221.

description: Herba minima ad 1-2 cm alta, saxicola, acaulis e tubere rhizomatoso 0.2-0.3 cm diam orta. Folia in rosula dense conferta, alterna. Petiolus 0.8-1 (1.5) cm longus, 0.2 mm diam, dense pilosus. Foliorum lamina tenuis peltata, orbiculata vel late ovata, 0.7-1 x 0.5-0.9 cm, basi et apice obtusa, dense utrinque longe pilosa, supra rubrinervis, pinnatinervis. Inflorescentia solitaria, axillaris, alba. Pedunculus 2-4 cm longus, dense pilosus, ebracteatus. Bacca minuta, ellipsoidea, dense papillata, stigmate apicali.
bibliographicCitation: Callejas, R. 1990. Studies in neotropical Piperaceae. II. Four new species and a new combination from Colombia and Peru. Brittonia. 42: 70-82.

description: A small, delicate, saxicolous herb, 1-2 cm tall, acaulescent with a tuberous, heart-shaped to rounded, smooth, glabrous rhizome, 0.2-0.3 cm diam, roots arising from the base. Leaves alternate, in a densely crowded rosette, long-petiolate, the petiole 0.8-1 (1.5) cm long, 0.2 cm diam, densely long-pilose, covered by simple uniseriate 3- to 6-celled, flexuous, white, translucent trichomes. Lamina peltate, the petiole attached to the lamina 0.5 mm above the lower margin, broadly ovate to orbiculate, 0.7-1 x 0.5-0.9, apically round-obtuse to bluntly acute, basally rounded, thin-membranous, dark green above, light green below, glan- dular-dotted (the glands raised), papillate and densely long-pilose on both faces, pinnately veined, with 2-4 pairs of widely spaced secondary veins arising through- out the length of the midvein, these arcuately ascending, reddish above, becoming white when dry. Inflorescence solitary, axillary, erect, white in flower and fruit; peduncle filiform 2-4 cm long, 0.3 mm diam, densely long-pilose, ebracteate; rachis 2-2.5 cm long, 0.5-0.8 mm diam in fruit, not obscured by the flowers, glandular-dotted, glabrous. Floral bracts orbiculate, peltate, 0.1-0.2 mm diam, glabrous, papillate, thin-membranous. Flowers widely spaced; anthers 0.1-0.2 mm long, pistil with an apical stigma. Fruit exserted from the rachis on a short (0.02 mm long) pedicel, 0.2 mm diam, ellipsoid, smooth and glabrous, densely papillate.
bibliographicCitation: Callejas, R. 1990. Studies in neotropical Piperaceae. II. Four new species and a new combination from Colombia and Peru. Brittonia. 42: 70-82.

description: Herbaceous plant with suberect to ascending, branching stem 4-8 cm long, 1 mm diam, minutely hirtellous with spreading hairs 0.1 mm long. Upper and middle internodes 4-10 mm long. Uppermost leaves mainly opposite, the others alternate, petiolate; petioles 3-8 mm long, moderately hirtellous with spreading hairs. Leaf blades fleshy-membranous, oblately suborbicular, emarginulate with minute hairs in the notch at the broadly rounded-truncate apex, subtruncate at the base or barely subpeltate, 5-8 mm long, 6-10 mm wide, palmately 3-5-nerved, the upper surface glabrous, the lower surface hirtellous at the base, elsewhere glabrous. Spike terminal, opposite the uppermost leaves, simple, sparsely flowered, 6-23 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm diam, the rachis glabrous. Peduncle 10-20 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, densely hirtellous with spreading hairs. Stigma apical, mammiform. Floral bracts scattered on the rachis, suborbicular, umbonate, the margins pale, 0.3 mm diam. Fruit stipitate, pale brown, oblong-elliptic, smooth, 1-1.1 mm long, 0.5 mm wide at and above the middle, crowned by the persistent conic style and apical stigma.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1988. A new species oïPeperomia [delascioi Steyermark] (Piperaceae) from the Venezuelan Guayana highland. Brittonia. 40: 294-295.

description: Herba diminuta, caule suberecto vel adscendenti tenui pilis patentibus praedito; petiolis 3-8 mm longis minute hirtellis pilis patentibus praeditis; foliis supremis saepe oppositis ceteris alternis palmatim 3-5-nerviis suborbicularibus apice late rotundatis emarginatulis basi subtruncatis vel inconspicue subpeltatis 5-8 mm longis 6-10 mm latis subtus basiatque incisura apicali minute pubescentibus aliter glabris; spicis solitariis 6-23 mm longis 0.5-0.7 mm diam; stigmate apicali mammiformi; fructu stipitato oblongo-elliptico laevi 1-1. 1 mm longo 0.5 mm lato, stipite 0.5-0.8 mm longo.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1988. A new species oïPeperomia [delascioi Steyermark] (Piperaceae) from the Venezuelan Guayana highland. Brittonia. 40: 294-295.

description: Suffrutescens, subseandens (?), ubique glaberrima, ovario excepto; petioli breves, supra basin glandulosi; folia oblonga, oblongo-lanceolata, vel subobovata, obtuse acuminata vel rotundata, integerrima, penninervia, coriacea; pedunculi solitarii vel bini; calycis tubus Cylindricus, sepalis petalisque linearibus; corona 3-seriata, filamientis extimis subligulatis, apice verruLuloso, alteris filiformibus et capillaceis, multo brevioribus; operculum cylilndricum, exsertum, deriticulatum; ovarium truneatum.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.

description: Plant suffruteseent, glabrous throughout except the ovary, apparently subseandent, the tendrils few; branches slender, subterete, dark brown; stipules soon deciduous; petioles 8-10 mm. long, slendler, biglandular just below the middle, the glands sessile, saucershaped, about 0.8 mm. long; leaf-blades oblong, oblong-lanceolate, or slightly obovate, 6-9 cm. long, 3-4 cm. wide, obtusely short-acuminate or rounded at apex, rounded at base, entire, penninerved (lateral nerves about 7 to a side), coriaceous, lustrous, the reticulations prominent beneath; peduncles solitary or in pairs, 1-1.3 cm. long, slender, articulate about 2 mm. above base; bracts triangular, about 0.5 mm. long, acute, borne close to base of pedunele and closely appressed to it; calyx-tube narrowly cylindric, 8-9 mm. long, 2 mm. in diameter, enlarged to about 3 mm. at base; sepals linear, 2.5 em. ]ong, 2.5-3 mm. wide, obtuse, ecorniculate, greenish red (?) without, pale aind reddish streaked within; petals linear, 1.5 cm. lonig, 2 mm. wide, obtuse, white, reddish streaked; corona-filaments in 3 series, those of the outermost series subligulate, 1-1.2 cm. long, enlarged to a width of about 1 cm. toward apex, erect, then taperinig to a verruculose tip, those of the second series filiform, about 3 mm. long, the innermost filaments capillary, barely 1 mm. lonig; operculiim narrowly cylindric, about 1.1 cm. long, 1.5 mm. in diameter, exserted beyond the calyx tube, reddish, minutely denticulate; ovary ovoid, trigonLous, truncate, densely canotomentulous, the styles arising at tops of angles of ovary.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.

description: Herba volubilis glabra; stipulae cordatae 13-15 mm diam., glandulis usque 1/3 ciliatae; petioli 30-40 mm, dimidium usque glandulis binis stipitatis 1 mm instructi; laminae 3-lobatae, lobis duobus 1/3 divisis. Bracteae cordatae 11-15 X 11-14 mm, verticillatae; flores 45-50 mm diam.; filamentorum corona tristicha, filamentis filiformibus, serierum 2 exteriorum 5 mm, tertiae interioris 1-1.5 mm; operculum modice incurvum basi membranaceum, apice versus filamentosum.
bibliographicCitation: Cervi, Armando C. 2002. A new species of Passiflora (Passifloraceae) from Amazonian Brazil. Brittonia. 54: 54-56.

description: Herbaceous climber, glabrous throughout. Stem cylindrical, striate. Stipules 13-15 X 13-15 mm, foliaceous, membranous, cordate, with glands along the proximal 1/3 of the margins, apex acute. Leaves simple, 3-lobed, 5-nerved, subpeltate at 1 mm from the truncate base, the apex obtuse, 40-45 mm long, 55-60 mm wide between apices of the lateral lobes. Peduncles 25-35 mm long; bracts 3, verticillate, cordate, 11-15 X 11-14 mm, situated 4-5 mm below the floral base; petiole 30-40 mm long, bearing a pair of stipitate glands ca. 1 mm long, near or slightly below the middle of petiole. Flowers axillary, solitary, 45-50 mm diam., floral tube campanulate, 4 mm long; sepals lanceolate, 20 X 7 mm, membranous, obtuse apex, green; petals membranous, 23 X 6 mm, obtuse apex, white; corona filaments in 3 series, the two outer series filiform, 5 mm long, the inner series 1-1.5 mm long; operculum incurved, 3.5 mm, the lower 1/3 membranous and the upper 2/3 filamentous; limen adnate to androgynophore, 3 mm; androgynophore 5 mm long; ovary ovoid, glabrous. Fruit globose, 30-50 mm diam., green, immature. Mature seeds unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Cervi, Armando C. 2002. A new species of Passiflora (Passifloraceae) from Amazonian Brazil. Brittonia. 54: 54-56.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Planta scandens glabra. Petioli 4-5 cm longi, 3 vel 4 paribus glandularum stipitarum 1 mm longarum ornati. Bracteae verticilatae ovataeque 1.7-2 cm longae, 1-1.3 cm latae. Flores 4-4.5 cm diametro. Corona filamentis in 3 seriebus instructa. Operculum erectum, 0.3 mm altum, ad basin membranaceum, ad apicem filamentosum.
bibliographicCitation: Cervi, Armando C. 1994. Studies in Brazilian Passifloraceae III. A new species of Passiflora. Brittonia. 46: 144-146.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Plant scandent, glabrous throughout; stem terete, striate, slender. Stipules ovate lanceolate, 2.2-3 cm long, 1-1.5 cm wide, attached on one side above base, hence often appearing sub-reniform; petiole 4-5 cm long, bearing 2-3 pairs of stipitate glands about 1 mm long; leaves simple, 3-lobed to about 2/33/4 of the limb, 5-nerved, truncate to cor- date at base, obtuse at apex, 5-5.6 cm long, 2 cm wide at midvein and 9.5-10 cm wide between apices of lateral lobes; the lateral lobes ovate-lanceolate, glaucescent. Peduncles slender, 2.3-2.5 cm long; bracts verticillate, ovate, 1.7-2 cm long, 1-1.3 cm wide, situated 3 mm from the floral base. Flowers axillary, solitary, 4-4.5 cm in diam.; calyx tube campanulate, 3 mm long; sepals lan- ceolate, 1.5 cm long, 0.4 cm wide, membranous, with obtuse apex, green mottled with red, bearing an awn 0.5-0.6 cm long on abaxial surface near apex; petals white, 1.2 cm long, 0.4 cm wide, with obtuse apex, membranous; corona filaments in 3 series, the filaments of the outer series capillary, 0.8 cm long, those of the two inner series capillary, 0.2 cm long; operculum erect, 0.3 cm long, the lower third membranous, the upper 2/3 filamentous, the filaments capillary; limen cupuliform, about 2 mm high, the apex dentate; ovary ovoid, glaucescent; styles mottled red. Fruit about 4 cm long. Seeds ovate, 3 mm long, foveolate.
bibliographicCitation: Cervi, Armando C. 1994. Studies in Brazilian Passifloraceae III. A new species of Passiflora. Brittonia. 46: 144-146.

description: Herbaceous vines with tomentose stems. Stipules 7-11 (without arista) X 4-5 mm, semi-ovate, sparsely pilose, the margin denticulate and glandular, the arista 3-4 mm. Petioles 1-1.7 cm long, tomentose, bearing 2-3 pairs of stipitate nectaries 1-1.8 mm long. Leaf blades 6-12 X 3-5 cm, discolorous, ovate-lanceolate to narrow elliptic, the base rounded to acute, glandular, the apex acute, mucronulate; abaxial surface villous with vinaceous veins; adaxial surface sparsely pilose, the trichomes semi-appressed, the main veins densely pilose. Peduncles 2.5- 3.5 cm long, tomentose. Bracts 1.5-2.1 X 1-1.2 cm, verticillate, ovate-lanceolate, pilose, the margins laciniate-serrate, greenish white to pinkish. Flowers solitary, 4-5 cm diam.; floral tube 4 X 12 mm, short-cylindrical; sepals 2.4-2.7 X 0.8-1 cm, oblong- lanceolate, aristate, the abaxial surface pilose at midvein, the adaxial surface white; petals subequal to the sepals, white; filamentous corona in 2 series, the outer filaments 1.3-2 cm long, the inner filaments 3-4 mm long; perculum 3 mm, erect, filamentous at margin; limen ca. 1.5 mm, membranous; gynophore 8-9 mm long; ovary 4 mm long, ovoid, villous.
bibliographicCitation: Vitta, Fabio A. & Bernacci, Luís C. 2004. A new species of Passiflora in section Tetrastylis (Passifloraceae) and two overlooked species of Passiflora from Brazil. Brittonia. 56 (1): 89-95.

description: Liana reaching the canopy, glabrous. Young stems terete. Tendrils thick. Stipules not seen, soon deciduous. Leaves: petiole 6-9 cm long, with 2 adaxial glands at the edge of the blade; blade broadly ovate, 10- 20 X 12-18 cm, rounded to emarginate at the apex, broadly and shallowly cordate at the base, the margin entire, drying dark brown adaxially, glaucous abaxially, 6-8 main lateral veins on each side of the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform. Inflorescence to 60 cm long. Pedicels 12-20 mm long, jointed 5-7 mm from the base. Flow- ers red or bright pink; hypanthium cylindrical, ventricose at the base, 3-4.5 cm long; sepals triangular, 11-13 X 3-4 mm; petals somewhat smaller; corona in 2 rows, the outer row of filaments 3 mm long, the inner of tubercles; operculum borne near the base of the hypanthium, 9-10 mm long, 5-lobed, lobes fimbrillate at apex; androgynophore 4-5 cm long; stamens filaments 4-5 mm long, anthers dorsifixed, rectangular, 4-5 X 2 mm, apiculate; ovary 4-6 mm long, glabrous; styles 3-4 mm long; stigmas 2 mm wide. Fruit (when young) pyriform, 4 X 2 cm, red with many small green spots; seeds (when immature) similar in shape and ornamentation to P. balbis.
bibliographicCitation: Feuillet, Christian P. G. 2002. A new series and three new species of Passiflora subgenus Astrophea from the Guianas. Brittonia. 54: 18-29.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herba parva; caule perbrevi; foliis rosulatis anguste linearibus 1-2 cm. longis parce longeque pilosis vel glabreseentibus; pedunculis den- siuscule villosis vel glabreseentibus, 1.5-5 cm. longis.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.

description: Small herb; stems very short or to 1 cm. long; leaves rosulate, basal, spreading or recurved, stiff and firm, narrowly linear, 1-2 cm. long, 0.5-1.5 min. wide, blunt at apex, sparsely long-pilose above and espe- cially at base, glabreseent and shiny in age; peduncles basal, 2-10 per plant, 1.5-5 em. long, rather densely spreading-pilose or villous or becoming glabreseent in age, several-costate, not noticeably twisted; sheaths close, 12-20 mm. long, obliquely split at apex, sparsely puberulent-pilose or glabreseent except for the more densely white-pilose mouth; heads subglobose, dark gray, 4-6 mm. wide; involueral bractlets oblanceolate, 1.5-2 mm. long, blunt at apex. glabrate; florets short-pedicellate; pedicels about 0.5 mm. long, subtencded by a whorl of long-villous erect hairs; receptacular bractlets oblanceolate, about 1.7 mm. long and 0.8 mm. wide, blunt or subacute at apex, long-villous throughout o0n the back and often more densely so in a tuft at center of apex; staminate florets: sepals 3, free or slightly connate at very base, oblanceolate, brunneous, about 1.5 mim. long and 0.6 mm. wide, rounded or emarginate at apex, cuneate at base, conspicuously crested with a dense tuft of long erect hairs from celnter from just above middle to apex, otherwise glabrous; petal-tube mnembranous-subhvaline, stramineous; pistillate florets: sepals 3, free, hyaline, narrowlv oblanceolate, about 1.3 mm. long and 0.3 mm. wide, acute at apex and there bearing a small tuft of erect villous hairs on the back, otherwise glabrous; petals 3, free, hyaline, similar in all respects to the sepals but slightly smaller; ovary 3-celled, 3-ovulate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Arbor dioica, ca. 12 m alta; cortice dilute brunneo, aetate griseo, longitudinaliter rimoso; ramulis subverticillatim dispositis, 2-2.5 mm diametro; alabastris apicalibus sphaericis ovoideisve, solitariis ternatisve, parvis, squamis adpressis imbricatisque, tenuibus, carinatis, ovatis obtusisve; foliis maturis 7-11 cm longis, 10-14 mm latis, spiraliter dispositis, linearibus oblongisve, versus apicem obtusis, in petiolum breve abeuntibus, supra laete canescente viridibus, subtus pallidioribus; foliis in arboribus immaturis (aet. ca. 10 ann.) ad 17 cm longis saltem, 20 mm latis; foliis in arboribus novellis (aet. ca. 5 ann.) parvis, 5-6 cm longis, 7-8 mm latis, spatulatis; strobilis S immaturis ternatis, pedunculatis ca. 2 mm; strobilis 9 axillaribus, solitariis, pedunculo 12-17 mm longo, strobilo ipso e squamis 2 inaequalibus coaleseentibus receptaculum efformanti, 9-11 mm longo; semine elongato, ca. 15 mm longo, ca. 10 mm crasso, crista minuta. Differt a P. sylvestre, cortice non rubro, foliis et strobilis maioribus, foliis crassioribus pro longitudine, obtusioribus (immaturis insigniter obtusis), viridibus dilutioribus, strobilorum e et 9 pedunculo duplo longiore.
bibliographicCitation: Manning, Wayne E. 1960. The genus Juglans in South America and the West Indies. Brittonia. 12: 1-26.

description: Suffrutex ligno molli glaber; foliis oblongo-ellipticis vel elliptico-suboblanceolatis, apice abrupte acuminatis, basi rotundatis subaequilateraliter cordulatis a medio infero pinnatim venosis, nerviis ca. utrinque 5 sub margine laqueatis, petiolo ad laminam vaginato-alato; spicis apiculatis, pedunculo gracili, bracteis triangulari-subpeltatis fimbriatis; drupa ovoidea subacuminata, stigmatibus parvis sessilibus.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1957. New species and new records of plants in Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 231-245.

description: A soft-wooded, glabrous, herb-like, branching shrub 1 m tall, the upper internodes slender, 2-15 cm long. Leaves oblong-elliptic or elliptic-suboblanceolate, the apex abruptly acuminate, gradually narrowing to the rounded, subequilateral, strongly cordulate base, the lateral margins meeting over the petiole, 5-6 cm wide and 14-17 cm long, pinnately nerved to about the middle, the nerves about 5 on each side, with slender cross-connecting-anastomosing nervules, the uppermost pair of lateral nerves arising near the middle of the blade, connected with the stout midrib upward with numerous, slender, secondary nerves, the nerves submarginally loop-connected, drying membranous, pale glandular-dotted beneath, translucent, finely pellucid-dotted, the petiole up to about 1 cm long, vaginate and strongly winged to the blade. 'Spikes 5 mm thick and 4-5 cm long, apiculate, the beak 2-3 mm long, the peduncle slender, 2 cm long, slightly curved, the bracts triangular-subpeltate, marginally fringed, the drupes annularly and loosely arranged, ovoid, pointed but scarcely stylkse, the stigmas small.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1957. New species and new records of plants in Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 231-245.

description: Herba minuta 1-2 cm. alta; foliis rosulatis filiformibus 3-10 mm. longis glabratis; pedunculis filiformibus 5-15 mm. longis glabris; vaginis minutis vel obsoletis; capitulis subglobosis griseis.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.

description: Plants minute, 1-2 cm. tall; leaves basal, rosulate, erect, filiform, 3-10 mm. long, subulate-tipped, glabrous; peduncles all basal, filiform, 2-8 per plant, 5-15 mm. long, several-costate, slightly twisted, glabrous; sheaths very tiny or obsolete; heads subglobose, 1-2 mm. wide, gray, the involueral bractlets numerous, ovate-lanceolate or elliptic, stramineous at base, hyaline and subacute at apex, 1.2-1.5 mm. long, 0.5-0.7 mm. wide, glabrous; receptacular bractlets elliptic, 1.5-1.6 mm. long, hya- line, about 0.6 mm. wide, acute, glabrous; florets short-pedicellate; pedicels about 0.3 mm. long, subtended by a whorl of long erect villous hairs; staminate florets: sepals 2, free, hyaline, elliptic, about 1.1 mm. long and 0.5 mm. wide, subacute at apex, narrowed at base, condupli- cate, glabrous; petal-tube hyaline, glabrous, deeply bifid, the lobes obo- vate, rounded at apex; stamens 2; pistillate florets: sepals 2, free, hyaline, elliptic, about 1 mm. long, and 0.7 mm. wide, acute at apex, abruptly narrowed at base, conduplicate, glabrous; petals 2, free, hya- line, obovate-spatulate, about 0.8 mm. long and 0.3 mm. wide, rounded and minutely apiculate at apex, cuneately narrowed at base; ovary 2-celled, 2-ovulate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.

description: Frutex scandens ligno molli, caule villoso, pilis retrorsis; foliis lanceolatis, apice sensim acutis, basi rotundato-truncatis, ad medium pinnatim venosis, nerviis utrinque 4 vel 5 sub margine laqueatis, supra ad costam pubescentibus vel glabris, venis in laminae facie infera pubescentibus, petiolo fere ad medium vaginato; spicis adhuc immaturis.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1957. New species and new records of plants in Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 231-245.

description: A soft-wooded vine. Stem villous, the hairs reflexed, 0.5-1 mm long, the internodes 5-8 cm or more long. Leaves lanceolate, gradually narrowing to the acute apex, the base rounded-truncate, or shallowly cordate, somewhat inequilateral with one side about 1 mm longer at the petiole, 3-3.5 cm wide and 7.5-9.5 cm long, pinnately nerved to about the middle of the blade, the nerves 4 or 5 on each side, with cross-connecting-anastomosing nervules, the uppermost pair of lateral nerves cross-connected with the midrib upward, submarginally loop-connected, thinly hairy above along the midrib or glabrous, the nerves beneath pubescent, the hairs somewhat appressed upwardly, the apex and margin lacking ciliation, the petiole 10-12 mm long, vaginate to near the middle or above, scarcely winged, reflexed-pubescent. Spikes as yet young, 3 mm thick and 1-1.5 cm long, the peduncle stout, 5 mm long, crisp-pubescent, the bracts triangularsubpeltate, marginally fringed, the ovary ovoid, bristly-hairy at the apex, the stigmas ligulate.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1957. New species and new records of plants in Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 231-245.

description: Frutex parvus ad 0.8-1 m altus, pauciramosus. Ramuli gracillimi, dense longe pilosi glabrescentes. description: Small, twiggy shrub, 0.8-1 m tall, sparsely branched. Branchlets slender, in- ternodes 1.5-4 (5.5) cm long, 0.7-1.2 mm diam, striate, densely long-pilose, glabrescent, covered by simple, uniseriate 6- to 10-celled, soft, brownish opaque, flexible trichomes. Shoot apex emergent from within the prophyll and free from the leaf base at nodes subtending inflorescences. Leaves short-petiolate, the petiole 0.5-0.8 cm long, vaginate, sparsely to densely long-pilose. Lamina variable, at sterile nodes widely ovate, basally cordate and equilateral, at fertile nodes narrowly elliptic, basally cordiform and inequilateral, the longer lobe often overlapping the petiole, 5.5-7 x 1.5-4.5 cm, apically short-acute to acuminate, pinnately veined, the 2-4 pairs of secondary veins arising from the lower half of the midvein and arcuately ascending, sulcate above, raised beneath, the blade glabrous above, densely short-pilose beneath along the veins, thin-membranous and bullate, glossy, deep green above, light green beneath. Prophylls caducous, ovate, 0.6-0.7 cm long, apically short-acute to obtuse, abaxially often short-pilose along the midvein, thin-membranous, brownish when dry. Inflorescences erect to slightly curved, white in flower, greenish in fruit; peduncle filiform, 3-4.5 cm long, 0.1-0.4 mm diam, striate, sparsely short-pilose, glabrescent; rachis 1.5-2 cm long, 0.2-0.4 cm diam in fruit, not obscured by the flowers, ridged, glabrous. Floral bracts narrowly to widely cucullate as seen from above, short-pedicellate, 0.4 mm broad, glan- dular-dotted, glabrous, not forming bands around the spike. Flowers widely spaced, trimerous; anthers 0.2 x 0.1 mm, laterally dehiscent; pistil with a short, thick style. Fruit exserted, globose, becoming 4-angled when dry, 0.2 mm diam, apically short-styled, glandular-dotted.

description: Low herb; stems elongate, to 15 cm. long, unbranched, densely leafy throughout; leaves closely imbricate, ensiform, thick, widely spreading, shiny, 1.5-5 cm. long, to 1 cm. wide at the base, blunt at apex, very minutely and obseurely puberulent and sparselv strigillose on both surfaces or glabreseent; peduncles borne in a terminial umbel, 15-45 per plant, stramineous, 7-17 cm. long, several-costate, twisted, shiny, glabrous; sheaths 2-2.5 cm. long, close, obliquely split at apex, rather abundantly long-pilose or villous with whitish spreading hairs; heads subglobose, often flattened above, gray, 3-4 mm. wide; florets short-pedicellate; pedicels about 0.5 mm. long, glabrous; involueral and receptacular bractlets oblong or oblong-lanceolate, about 1 mm. long and 0.3 mm. wide, rounded or subapiculate at apex, mostly bearing long erect villous hairs on margins at apex, especially in a dense tuft at center; staminate florets: sepals 3, free, broadly obovate-spatulate, brunneous or black (except at base), about 1.2 mm. long and 0.8 mm. wide, truncate at apex, cuineate at base, rather sparsely lolng-villous with appressed aintrorse hairs (especially toward base) and with a distinct tuft of similar erect hairs at center of apex; petal-tube hyaline, gla- brous; pistillate florets: sepals 3, free, obovate-spatulate, brunneous or black (except at base), about 1.2 mm. long and 0.7 mm. wide, truncate at apex, cuneate at base, long-villous with appressed antrorse hairs (especially toward base) on both surfaces and along marginis (espe- cially toward base), bearing a distinct tuft of similar long erect villous hairs at center of apex; petals 3, hyaline, free, oblanceolate, about 1 mm. long and 0.3 mm. wide, rounded at apex, cuneate at base, sparsely long-villous like the sepals; ovary 3-celled, 3-ovulate.

description: Annual herbs. Stems 5-50 cm long, 4-angled, green to brownish, simple or branched from base, glabrous or scaberulous-papillose. description: Annual herbs. Stems 5-80 cm long, 4-angled, green, erect to ascendent, simple to freely branched from below the middle, glabrous with smooth faces, or angles with sparse papillae; papillae conical, 40-60 [pm long. Leaves: basal leaves usually caducous or persistent at flowering, upper leaves abruptly reduced to scale-like bracts; ocreae 6-12 mm, glabrous or sparsely scaberulous-papillose, with the free part hyaline, lacerate; leaf blades linear, narrow-oblong, oblanceolate to oblong, 15-55 x 2-8(-12) mm, margins smooth or denticulate-papillose; apex acute or mucronate. Papillae on ocreae and leaf margins are similar to those on the stems, or they may be conic-cylindrical, 60-85 ptm long. Inflorescences terminal, elongated and spike-like; cymes 2-4-flowered, regularly spaced along the stem and branches; bracts equaling or somewhat longer than the flowers. Flowers closed; pedicels reflexed, 2-6 mm: perianth 3-4.5 mm. the tube 20-28% of the perianth length, perianth lobes petaloid or sepaloid, cucullate, naviculate, overlapping, tannish to green, margins white or pink, midveins usually branched, rarely unbranched (Fig. 3A); perianth lobe cells rectangular 30-60 x 9-15 wm with anticlinal walls straight or weekly sinuate; epicuticular wax pattern belongs to type I and has transversally reticulate rodlets (Fig. 4B). Stamens 6-8; anthers pink to purple, 125-150 µm long. Pollen of subtype Al, 22-24 µm (Fig. 6A). Achenes elliptic, oblong to ovate, 3-4(-4.5) mm, enclosed in the perianth at maturity, smooth or tubercled. Greene (1885) described P. douglasii var. latifolium with "saw-toothed," oblong blades, and oblong achenes, as opposed to var. douglasii having linear-lanceolate to lanceolate or oblanceolate, glabrous leaves, and ovate achenes. This variety has been accepted by Hitchcock (1964), but the authors abandoned the leaf margin and achene shape characters. Indeed, we have encountered P. douglasii plants with narrow-lanceolate leaves having denticulate-papillose margins, as well as plants with glabrous oblong leaves. Achene shape also varies from elliptic to oblong or ovate, with no relation to the blade width. Although plants with wide leaves tend to occur more frequently at higher altitudes, leaf shape varies continuously, and the two varieties cannot be satisfactorily separated. Plants with broad leaves bring P. douglasii close to P. austiniae and to P. sawatchense subsp. oblivium. In fact, Hickman (in herb.) regarded such plants as intermediates between P. douglasii "subsp. johnstonii (P. sawatchense subsp. sawatchense) and subsp. douglasii." However, P. douglasii is readily distinguished from P. austiniae by its bigger flowers and achenes. From P. sawatchense subsp. oblivium it differs by the glabrous stems, reflexed achenes, and the pollen of subtype Al. From both taxa, it is distinguished by the epicuticular wax sculpture of perianth lobes with transversally reticulate rodlets.

description: Annual herbs. description: Lianas with young stems glabrous or sparsely puberulent. Stipules filiform, 0.7-1 mm long, deciduous. Petioles 6-14 mm long, glabrescent or sparsely puberulous, canaU tlate; nectaries paired (rarely one), elliptical, sessile, 1-1.3 mm long, at or more frequently below the midpoint. Leaf blades 6-11 X 2.5-5.4 cm, elliptic to oblong or obovate, glabrous, coriaceous, the margin cartilaginous, the apex acuminate, the base acute to rounded. Inflorescences racemiform, the main axis 7-12 cm long, sparsely to densely puberulent, bearing sol- itary or rarely paired and puberulent pedi- cels 1.2-2.7 cm long, articulated at the very base, subtended by a falciform bract 1.1- 1.7 mm long; pedicel below articulation point 1.3-2.5 mm long, with 2-3 scattered sessile triangular bracteoles, these 1.1-1.3 X 0.5-0.9 mm; pedicel above articulation 1.1-2.5 cm long. Flowers 5-6 cm diam. with retrorse sepals and petals; sepals 2.3- 3.1 X 0.7-0.8 cm, the apex rounded, not aristate, the abaxial surface minutely puberulent; petals 2.3-3 X 0.5-0.7 cm; floral tube 0.3 X 1-1.2 cm, discoid, the outer surface minutely puberulent; filamentous corona 3-ranked, the outer series of filaments 6.5-7.7 mm long, the 2 inner series 2.5-5 mm long; operculum 3 mm, horizontally spreading, closely plicate, the margin denticulate; limen 3-3.5 mm high, fleshy, cupuliform; gynophore 1.7-2.4 cm long, slightly recurved; filaments united beyond the gynophore and grouped on one side of the gynophore toward the center of the flower, the free part of filaments 0.8-1 cm; anthers 1-1.3 cm; styles 8-9 mm; ovary 4.5-6.7 mm, ellipsoid, entirely minutely puberulent or only so at the apex. description: Annual herbs. Stems 5-10(-20) cm, 4-angled, green to purplish, much branched from base, ascending to erect, scaberulous-papillose on the ribs; papillae white, conical 40-60 µm. description: Annual herbs. description: Habitu S. cedron simulans. Inter sectione Floribundas et Grandifloras ambigens, cum illis petaloruir longitudine cum his gynophoro gracili congruens. Arbuscula usque ad 9 m alta vel altior. description: Small tree to at least 9 m. Stems few-branched with leaves clustered near apex. Leaves evenly pinnately compound with 4-6 pairs of opposite leaflets, the petiole 15-20 cm long, the rachis (including the petiole) 60-75 cm long. Leaflet blades ovate to obovate, decreasing in size towards base of leaf, the largest ones 20-26 cm long, 8.5-10.5 cm wide, subcoriaceous, olive green above and yellowish-green beneath when dry; the apex usually attenuate with a small glandular tip; secondary leaflet veins brochidodromous and slightly raised abaxially. Petiolules winged or at least flattened and transversely wrinkled, 4-10 mm long. Inflorescence paniculate, the lateral racemes bearing flowers singly or in fascicles of up to 3; main axis and lateral branches longitudinally wrinkled, to at least 20 cm long with flowers in all stages of development; main axis shiny, glabrous to sparsely pubescent; lateral branches ferrugineous, finely pubescent; each flower or fascicle subtended by a pendulous ovoid or discoid gland. Pedicel 4-6 mm long, occasionally branching, covered with dense, fine, ferrugineous pubescence; calyx discoid, pentagonal, 3.8-4 mm in diameter, with very short pubescence; petals 5, slightly imbricate, narrowly obovate, 11.5-14 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, yellow, drying to a creamy light brown, thinner along margins, with scurfy short pubescence adaxially and abaxially; stamens 10; filaments 7.5-8 mm long; appendage adaxial, ligulate, ca 4 mm long, the lower half adnate to the filament, glabrous on the face, the margins long ciliate; anthers 1.5-1.7 mm long; gynophore cylindrical, 2 mm high, 1.3-1.4 mm wide, glabrous, lightly sulcate; gynoecium depressed-globose, ca 1.5 mm high, 2.3 mm broad, 5-lobed, densely and finely ferrugineous-tomentose; style ca 5 mm long, narrowly subulate, glabrous except for basal 1 mm; stigma indistinct. Fruit a lenticular drupe ca 6.5 cm long, 4.5 cm wide, 3 cm thick, green drying to dark brown, glabrate except near base where sparsely pubescent; epicarp thin, fleshy, becoming wrinkled when dry; mesocarp hard, ca 4-5 mm thick; endocarp adnate to mesocarp, ca 1 mm thick, coriaceous; seed lenticular, 2.5-3 cm long.

description: Climbing shrub. Stems 1.5-2 mm diam., faintly 6-ribbed to nearly terete and glabrous; cross section of stem with a central, obtusely triangular, large stele and three peripheral, smaller, subterete, equidistant steles. Stipules ovatedeltate, 0.5-0.75 mm long, with glandular hairs along the margins. Leaves trifoliolate; petioles glabrous, subterete, 2-7.2 cm long, obscurely furrowed adaxially; leaflets sessile, narrowly ovate, 4.2-10.5 X 2-5.5 cm, discolorous, chartaceous, with glandular hairs but glabrescent, the apex acuminate or obtuse, mucronate, the margin remotely glandular-serrate, the terminal leaflet with attenuate base, the base of lateral ones asymmetric, with narrower acroscopic side, truncate or rounded at base. Thyrses axillary, simple, glabrous, longer than subtending leaf; axis subterete, 7-13.5 cm long; rachis angular when young, becoming nearly terete with age, (2.2-)3.8-23 cm long, bracts and bracteoles deltate, ca. 1 mm long (bracteoles smaller), margin with glandular hairs; cincinni alternate, 8-22-flowered, 2.5-7.5 mm long; pedicels articulated close to base. Flowers: sepals glabrous, margin ciliate, the outer 2 sepals 2.25-2.5 X 1.75-2 mm, ovate to oblong, the inner sepals 3.5-4.5 X 2.75 mm, obovate, third and fifth sepals completely connate or nearly so; petals white, 4.5 mm long, spathulate, lacking papillae, the apex rounded; appendages of central petals hood-shaped, with fleshy, entire or bifid apex; disk with four glands, the central glands ovoid, with obtuse apex, the lateral glands with elliptic outline; torus enlarged, glabrous; filaments flattened, pilose, 2.5 mm long, the anthers oblong, 0.5 mm long, puberulous; pistillode 1.5 mm long, glabrous. Fruits 2.8-3.45 X 2.2-2.8 cm, glabrous, outline oblong, the base cordate, the apex retuse; seed locules flattened, chartaceous, with slightly prominent veins, with a dorsal crest 2-2.5 mm wide; outline of wing not constricted below locule; endocarp glabrous. Seeds nearly lenticular, ca. 7.5 X 6.5 mm; embryo with biplicate, smaller, adaxial cotyledon and curved, larger, abaxial cotyledon.

description: Woody vine. Branches terete or nearly so, slightly striate, hirsutulose when young, becoming glabrous and slightly lenticellate with age; cross section of stems with xylem radially divided into five subequal parts. Stipules puberulent, lanceolate or ovate, 5-8 x 2-2.3 mm, the margins ciliate, entire. Leaves pinnately 5-foliolate; petiole and rachis not winged, shorter or equaling the leaflets, striate and setulose on adaxial surface; leaflets chartaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous except for a few erect hairs on veins and margins, both surfaces sparsely covered with minute resinous dots, the apex abruptly acuminate, the margins remotely glandular-serrate, terminal leaflet oval to subrounded, 6-12 x 4.5-8 cm, attenuate at base, lateral leaflets oblong or ovate, 5.5-9 x 3.8-6 cm, sub-cordate and slightly unequal at base; petiolules ca 5 mm long. Inflorescences shorter than the sub- tending leaf, the axes puberulent and hirsutulose; bracts subulate, 4 mm long, tomentose; cincinni 3-5 mm long, 4-6-flowered; bracteoles subulate, 2.5 mm long. Flowers functionally male or female; pedicels 3-4 mm long, articulated at 1 mm from the base; sepals 5, oblong to ovate, tomentose and with glandular hairs, the external ones 2.8-3 mm long, the internal ones 3.5-5 mm long; petals white, ca 5 mm long, obovate, adaxially papillose, the scales ca 4 mm long, fleshy; torus glands 2, ovate, ca 2 mm long; filaments covered with inflexed, white hairs. Fruit not known.

description: Plants acaulescent to very shortly caulescent; leaves persistent, dimorphic, those of the sterile offshoots 3-8 cm long, dark brown or black, corneous, barbed-spiniform; leaves of mature rosettes linear-lanceolate, arching, attenuate, variously serrate, occasionally entire except toward the base and apex, glabrous adaxially except along the margins and apex, narrowest immediately above the sheath, where usually deeply channeled, but not actually petioled; scape ascending or erect, variously floccose-lepidote to glabrescent; scape-bracts foliaceous exceeding the internodes basally but often shorter above, entire, with scattered floccose scales on both surfaces; primary bracts like upper scape bracts; branches laxly flowered; floral bracts narrowly triangular, entire, both surfaces white-flocculose at first, the lower ones often equaling or exceeding the pedicels, the upper much shorter; pedicels spreading; sepals red, narrowly triangular, imbricate, acuminate or acute, ecarinate, glabrous except for occasional tufted hairs at the apices; petals red, salmon-pink, or scarlet, lorate, bearing a truncate scale inside near the base, the three petals assuming a superior position above the exposed anthers and stigma; stamens included; filaments often with scattered glandular hairs: anthers versatile; pollen yellow; ovary glab- rescent, half inferior; ovules bicaudate; flowering peak in late winter to early summer, occasionally otherwise.

description: Leaves 50-140 cm long, 9-30 (8-32) mm wide near the middle, evenly serrate towards the base with white or green teeth ca. 2 mm long (sparsely elsewhere), densely white-lepidote abaxially (scales rarely sparsely and unevenly distributed), with persistent, usually crowded, interlocking and coalesced symmetrical fimbriate often cupulate scales, appearing quite silvery or white in life, obscure when dry; cells of the scales ovoid to spherical, appearing collapsed when dry; inflorescence 0.4-1.4 m long; primary bracts 2-6 cm long; branches 2-4 dm long; floral bracts green basally becoming red toward the apex of the usually red rachis; pedicels 0.9-2.4 (0.7-2.5) cm long [one population near Ocho Rios exhibits pedicels 2.0-3.4 (1.9-3.6) cm long]; sepals (1.5-) 1.6-2.5 cm long; petals (3.7-) 3.8-5.2 cm long; stamens 3.7-4.8 cm long; fruiting pedicels spreading or only very slightly curved.

description: Plant terrestrial, 50-70 cm tall in flower. Leaves 5-8, erect to spreading, green, the outermost leaves appearing as bladeless sheaths. Leaf sheaths narrowly elliptic, 8- 12 X 2-4 cm, entire, nerved, thin-coriaceous, brown-lepidote. Leaf blades pseudopetiolate, the pseudopetiole channeled, 6-12 X 1 cm, entire, nerved, fugaceously brown-floccose especially abaxially; blade lanceolate in upper portion, acute to acuminate at both ends, entire, 3-5 cm wide, channeled, nerved, abaxially brown-floccose. Scape erect, 20-30 cm X 3-4 mm, fugaceously brown-floccose, yellow green; scape bracts narrowly elliptic, attenuate, thin, nerved, abaxially brown-floccose, much exceeding but not concealing internodes. Inflorescence simple, erect, polystichously 10-20-flowered; floral bracts elliptic, acute, very thin, fugaceous, green, the lowest bracts exceeding the pedicels, the uppermost bracts exceeded by the pedicels. Flowers: pedicel slender, 8-20 mm long, spreading ca. 450 from axis at anthesis, orange red; sepals narrowly triangular, acute, 28-32 mm long, thin, nerved; corolla slightly zygomorphic; petals narrowly oblanceolate to linear, obtuse, 6-7 cm long, unappendaged; ovary ca. 1/2 superior; ovules immature but apparently caudate.

description: Plant lithophytic, stemless, to 70 cm tall in flower. Leaves dimorphic: some reduced to nearly bladeless, acute to attenuate sheaths, and persistent; others linear, 40-85 cm long, entire above the persistent often serrate sheaths, deciduous, the remnant spirally incurved. Leaf sheaths broadly triangular to ovate, 10-18 X 25-30 mm, entire or retrorse serrate, nerved, castaneous especially abaxially, pale-lepidote. Leaf blades absent or very narrowly triangular to linear, nerved, entire, 1-5 mm wide, tightly involute when dried, acute to long attenu- ate, pale-lepidote especially abaxially. Scape erect, 30-45 cm X 3-4 mm, glabrous; scape bracts erect, very narrowly lanceolate, acute to attenuate, equaling to exceeding internodes but not concealing them. Inflorescence simple or depauperately bipinnate, 15-30 X 3-6 cm; primary bracts like the floral bracts in all respects, much shorter than the sterile, ebracteate peduncle; branches with a 3-4 cm long slender peduncle, 2-3-flowered; floral bracts ovate to narrowly elliptic, attenuate, 5-15 mm long, thin, nerved, glabrous, reddish, exceeding the pedicels. Flowers: pedicel 3-6 mm long, spreading ca. 30? from axis, becoming pendent secund at anthesis, bright orange yellow; sepals subtriangular, acute to attenuate, 24 mm long, thin, nerved, glabrous; corolla erect, slightly if at all zygomorphic; petals narrowly oblanceolate, acute, thin, nerved, 38-40 mm long, each with an irregular bidentate basal appendage.

description: Vines or lianas, monoecious or dioe- cious, plants with staminate flowers and plants with staminate and pistillate flowers in the same population; stems terete, 4-25 m long, woody basal stems to 6 cm diam., the herbaceous parts glabrous, striated with conspicuous scars left by the abscission layer between stem and leaf. Leaves alternate, mostly densely grouped at the tips of lateral short shoots or sometimes widely spaced along vigorous primary shoots produced at the beginning of the growing season; petioles 0.4-3.5 cm long; blade 2.8-9 X 1.3-7 cm, suborbicular to ovate, the base obtuse to attenuate, sometimes acute, the apex acute to acuminate, the margins entire, sometimes sinuate, membranaceous when fresh, papyraceous or chartaceous when dry. Flowers solitary, nodding, without any obvious difference in color or size among pistillate and staminate flowers; peduncles 1.2-2.7(-7 in pistillate flowers) cm long; sepals 6 in two series of three, the first series 1.5-3 X 2-2.3 mm, suborbicular, flat to concave, green-yellow, the second series 5.5-6 X 4-4.5 mm, suborbicular, concave, the margins sometimes ciliolate, creamy green; petals 5, 6.3-6.6 x ca. 3.5 mm, cherry-red, in staminate flowers the base of the petal with a creamy pink callosity normally hidden by the androecium structure; an- droecium ca. 4.5 mm diam., of 5 stamens, tetrasporangiate, the anthers basifixed, each with its two thecae separated by a laminar and thick connective, each theca opposite the theca of the adjacent stamen, the five stamens covering the basal torus and form- ing a star-shaped androecium which in combination with the petal callosities pro- duce a shield-like pentagonal structure; fil- aments ca. 2 X ca. 2 mm, the thecae ca. 0.6 mm long; gynoecium with 20-30 free car- pels 1.5-2.3 X 0.7-1 mm, arranged along a toral column that elongates as fruits ma- ture, each carpel normally with 2 ovules; stigmatic surface resembling a small crest as a protrusion of the apex of the ovary 0.3-1 X 0.1-0.3 mm, the ovules anatro- pous, bitegmic, crassinucellate. Infructes- cence of 7-18 carpels variously spaced along the enlarged torus, 2-3.5 cm long. Fruit a drupe with 1 or 2 reniform seeds, ca. 5.5 X 4-4.5 mm; testa rugulose; endo- sperm abundant and oily.

description: Epiphytic shrub; branches and branchlets slender, brownish and puberulous, soon becoming einereous and glabrous; petioles subrugose, usually glabrous, 1-3 mm. long; leaf-blades thin-coriaceous, ovate, 2- 5.5 (rarely to 7) cm. long, 1.2-3 cm. broad, rounded or subcordate at base, obtuse or subacute at apex, entire and slightly recurved at mar- gins, glabrous, 3- or 5-nerved from base, the costa and secondary nerves often impressed above, raised beneath, the veinlets usually obscure; pedicels glabrous or puberulous, 10-25 mm. long; calyx tube usually deciduously villose, obconical or subglobose, 1-1.5 mm. long and in diameter at anthesis, the limb erecto-patent, 1-1.6 mm. long including lobes, the lobes 4 or 5, deltoid, apiculate, often tufted-setose at apex; corolla 4.7-8 mm. long, 1.5-2 mm. in diameter, glabrous, sometimes puberulous when young, the lobes 4 or 5, deltoid, subacute; stamens 8 or 10 (occasionally 7, 6, or 5), slightly alternately unequal or subequal, slightly shorter than corolla; filaments slender, sparsely villose, 2-4.7 mm. long; anthers 2-3 mm. long, the tubules about twice as long as the locules; fruit subglobose, often glabrous at dehiseence, 4-7 mm. in diameter.

description:
Leaf blades entire, broad lanceolate to lanceolate and elliptical and sometimes ovate; bases acute to obtuse and rounded; apices acuminate to long-acuminate, sometimes shortly caudate and occasionally acute, rarely mucronate or mucronulate. Leaves 7.6-20.4 cm long (mean 11.8 cm), 2.2-6.7 cm wide (mean 4.1 cm); petioles 1.3-2.9 cm long (mean 1.9 cm); pairs of prominent lateral veins 8-15 (mean 10); upper surface of leaf blades glabrous; lower surface glabrous or glabrate with peltate-stellate trichomes on midrib and rarely on the lateral veins, extending proximally to petioles and branchlets in increasing density when young. Swellings ("domatia") sometimes present in axils of lateral veins. Stipules soon caducous, more or less prominently nerved, sometimes with 1-3 thickened central veins, usually strikingly falcate, basally constricted and apically attenuate and sharppointed or occasionally lanceolate and acute at the apex, 1.4-3.1 cm long (mean 2.3 cm), 0.3-0.6 cm wide (mean 0.4 cm); abaxial surfaces peltate-stellate; adaxial surfaces glabrous. Expanding buds generally falcate and closely invested with low peltate-stellate trichomes.

Fruits 5-winged, the bases of the wings, especially the 2 inner ones which are so oriented that the adaxial facets are connivent, completely covering the maturing ovary, mature fruiting ovary 23 covered by sheathing wing bases; 3 outer wings oblanceolate to almost parallel-sided with rounded apices, longer and broader than the 2 inner linear acute-tipped wings; outer wings 6.7-10.8 cm long (mean 8.4 cm), maximum width 0.8-1.7 cm (mean 1.3 cm), minimum width 0.4-0.7 cm (mean 0.5 cm), main longitudinal veins 11-15 or more; inner wings somewhat carinate at the clasping bases, 3-5.1 cm long (mean 4 cm), 0.3-0.6 cm wide (mean 0.4 cm), the main longitudinal veins many. Sparsely scattered stellate trichomes present on abaxial surfaces of free and clasping portions of wings, the adaxial surfaces with scattered stellate trichomes especially at the tips and clasping bases. Fruiting ovary globose, 1-1.6 cm long (mean 1.3 cm), 0.7-1.3 cm in diameter (mean 1.1 cm), covered with a very short felt which is especially prominent at the apex, sometimes surmounted by a low dome or stylopodium supporting a more or less persistent stylar remnant 0.1 cm or less long, the fruiting ovary often sharply eccentric in shape, the tip then not parallel with the pedicellar axis.

description: Arbores excelsae. Folia simplicia, alterna, integerrima, subcoriacea, plerumque late lanceolate, 5.4-14.2 cm longa et 1.8-5.6 cm lata, acuminata, basi otundata, nervis lateralibus (venis primariis) prominentibus utrobique 6-10, precipue glabra, petiolis 0.7-1.9 cm longis; stipulae lineares apicibus rotundatis paullum curvatis, 0.7-1.2 cm longae et 0.25-0.4 cm latae, obscure nervatae, caducae. Ovarium fructescens turbinatum, 1.3-1.4 cm longum, 0.9-1 cm diametro, apice acuminatum, basi paullum angulatum, tenuiter tomentosum.

description: Tall forest trees of large diameter (75 cm in Stern 2102), the bark of trunk peeling in thick flakes; branchlets brown to black in life; lenticels -+ numerous, rounded, dark brown and inconspicuous to whitish and conspicuous; youngest branchlets variably covered with peltate-stellate trichomes. Leaf blades entire, mostly broadly lanceolate, lanceolate and elliptical to ovate and cordate, the base various, from nearly cuneate to obtuse, rounded, truncate, or almost cordate, the apex acuminate-attenuate to broadly and shortly caudate. Leaves 5.4-14.2 cm long (mean 8.4 cm), 1.8-5.6 cm wide (mean 3.2 cm); petioles 0.7-1.9 cm long (mean 1.1 cm); pairs of prominent lateral veins (primary veins) 6-10 (mean 8); leaf blades subglabrous on both surfaces when mature, but scattered stellate trichomes sometimes present on underside near union of blade and petiole. Swellings ("domatia"31) sometimes present on the lower sides of leaves in axils of primary veins. Stipules caducous, glabrous, red in life and in recently dried material, faintly nerved, linear with slightly curved, rounded tips, 0.7-1.2 cm long (mnean 0.9 cm), 0.25-0.4 cm wide (mean 0.32 cm). Expanding buds straight, glabrous. Flowers unknown. Fruits 5-winged, red in life, red-brown when dried, all wings expanded at the base and tightly clasping lower V3 of fruiting ovary; 3 outer wings long-obovate to broad-spatulate with obtuse rounded apices, longer and broader than the 2 inner linear to linear-spatulate wings; outer wings 4.5-7.9 cm long (mean 6.1 cm), the maximum width 1.0-1.9 cm (mean 1.4 cm), minimum width 0.3-0.5 cm (mean 0.4 cm), the main longitudinal veins 6-10 (mean 8); inner wings 1.3-4.1 cm long (mean 2.4 cm), 0.2-0.6 cm wide (mean 0.3 cm), the main longitudinal veins 6-9 (mean 7). Wings glabrous except for scattered stellate trichomes especially on bases clasping fruiting ovary, on thickened margins, and near the apices on both surfaces. Fruiting ovary turbinate, 1.3-1.4 cm long, 0.9-1 cm in diameter, covered with a fine low felt, the tip sharp-pointed and elongated, the base somewhat angular.

description: Young branchlets closely invested with coppery stellate trichomes diminishing with age. Leaf blades entire, narrowly to broadly elliptical to ovate and oblong, rarely lanceolate or obovate; bases mostly rounded, occasionally acute, obtuse, and truncate; apices usually attenuate, sometimes attenuate-caudate or acute. Leaves 8.7-19.7 cm long (mean 13 cm), 2.1-7.5 cm wide (mean 5.8 cm); petioles 0.7-2.2 cm long (mean 1.6 cm); pairs of prominent lateral veins 6-14 (mean 10); upper surface of leaf blades with golden to pale -yellow stellate trichomes along main veins, especially toward proximal portions of the depressed midrib and becoming sparser with age; lower surface with -+ regularly placed conspicuous trichomes on secondary veins; smaller stellate trichomes scattered among vein interstices. Swellings ("domatia") sporadic on lower sides of leaves in axils of lateral veins. Stipules soon caducous or sometimes persisting at least until leaves are fully expanded, prominently nerved, often with a thickened mid-vein, linear to lanceolate or somewhat falcate with acute usually sharp-pointed apex, 1.2-3.0 cm long (mean 1.9 cm), 0.4-0.8 cm wide (mean 0.6 cm); abaxial surfaces densely covered with stellate trichomes; adaxial surfaces more sparsely invested with hairs, especially near base and apex and on veins. Expanding buds straight, densely covered with long stellate trichomes. Fruits 5-winged, all wings expanded at the base and tightly clasping lower 23 of fruiting ovary; 3 outer wings almost parallel-sided or expanded near rounded apices, longer and broader than the 2 inner linear to long-triangular acute-tipped wings; outer wings 4.7-6.7 cm long, the maximum width 1.2-1.5 cm, minimum width 0.7-1 cm, the main longitudinal veins 14-15 or more; inner wings slightly carinate at the clasping base, 2.3-2.9 cm long, 0.6-0.9 cm wide, the main longitudinal veins 8 or more. Free surfaces of wings covered with sparse layer of stellate trichomes, the adaxial surfaces ensheathing fruiting ovary and densely invested with stellate trichomes. Fruiting ovary turbinate, 1.9 cm long, 1.5-1.9 cm in diameter, covered with yellow sericeous hairs inclusive of the sharp-pointed and short tip.

description: Small tree 3-7 m tall; stems strigose, becoming glabrous, with a gray-brown, wrinkled bark. Leaves alternate; petioles 4-10 mm long, sericeous, flattened above; blade ovate to oblanceolate, 7-25 cm long, 4-10 cm wide, membranous to subcoriaceous, glabrous and shiny above, glabrous to sparsely pubescent below, the base cuneate, the apex obtuse, often short-acuminate, the venation pinnate, forming looped veins toward the margins. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, a pair of umbels; primary peduncles 2.5-4 cm long, strigose; rachis 2.5-4 mm long; secondary peduncles 1-2 mm long. Staminateflowers 10-20 per umbel, creamy yellow; pedicels 7-15 mm long; sepals spreading to recurved, ovate, 6-8 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, thick, the apex rounded; stamens 4, antisepalous, filiform, 4-6 mm long, glabrous, fused to the sepals for 1-3 mm at the base, the thecae 1 mm long; pistillode narrowly ovoid, 1 mm long. Pistillate flowers 10-12 per umbel, creamy yellow; pedicels 7-10 mm; sepals spreading to reflexed, ovate, 3-5 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, the apex rounded; staminodes absent; pistil ovoid, the ovary 1.5-2 mm long, 2 mm diameter, the style 1 mm long, the stigma capitate. Drupes not seen.

description: Shrub to 2 m tall; stems glabrous, with smooth brown bark. Leaves alternate; petioles 10-14 mm long, thick, dark green, flattened above; blade obovate to oblanceolate, 18-32 cm long, 8-12 cm wide, glabrous, subcoriaceous to firmly membranous, dark green above, dull green below, the base cuneate, the apex obtuse, often short-acuminate. Inflorescences terminal, umbellate, dichotomously branched, glabrous to slightly pubescent; primary peduncles 3-7 cm long, longest on the staminate inflorescences; secondary peduncles 2-3.5 cm long; rachis 2-3 mm long. Staminate flowers 10-15 per umbel, yellow to whitish, drying dark brown; pedicels 7-10 mm long, filiform, pubescent; sepals spreading to recurved, lanceolate, 7-8 mm long, 2 mm wide, glabrous, the apex rounded; stamens 4, antisepalous, filiform, 7 mm long, fused to the sepals for 2-3 mm at the base, the thecae 1 mm long; pistillode subglobose, 1-1.5 mm long. Pistillateflowers 7-12 per umbel; pedicel 6-10 mm long; sepals recurved, narrowly ligulate, 5-6 mm long, 1 mm wide, cellular-pilose on the inner surface, pubescent at the apex on the outer surface, the apex rounded; staminodes 4, antisepalous, filiform, fused to the sepals, 1-1.5 mm long; ovary 3 mm long, the style 1-1.5 mm long, the stigma capitate, slightly 2-lobed. Young drupes ellipsoid, 1.5-2.5 cm long, dark green, 1 cm diam, the style persistent.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 4 mm. long; blades elliptic to elliptic-lanceo- late, 6-10 cm. long, 4-5 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, acute or obtuse and mucronulate at apex, the old ones shining and dark olive-green above, rusty benieath, subeoriaceous, 3 (5)-plinerved with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 0-4 mm. from base, at maturity im- pressed above, the secondaries impressed above and prominent beneath, reticulation faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets densely fulvous- pubescent with short adpressed curved hairs; petioles pubescent as branch- lets, becoming less densely so and with hairs becoming greyish in age; blades beneath densely pubescent with rusty, curved, sometimes matted hairs per- sistent well into age, above when young with conspicuous tubereles that sometimes disappear in age and with conspicuous, rather short, adpressed, curved hairs which in age become scattered and longer and often suberect on elongated bases, the indumentum being most persistent on midrib. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, corymbose and loosely flowered, very densely fulvous-pubeseent with short, adpressed, mostly curved hairs, pedi- eels up to 5 mm. long; calyx-lobes ovate to lanceolate, about 3 imm. long, acute to short-acuminate at apex, densely fulvous-pubeseent without with adpressed, slightly curved or rather straight hairs; corolla-tube up to 1.5 cm. long, with a double indumentum without (fulvous-pubeseent with short ad- pressed hairs as on calyx and also hirsute with long, rusty, spreading or ascending, straight hairs), densely pilose within above middle until near throat which is glabrous (and also with a developed corona, the lobed rim of which extends beyond corolla-lobes and is wooly, giving a bearded ap- pearance to throat of corolla-tube), corolla-lobes with an indumentum with- out as that on corolla-tube, white short-lanate within, sparsely so at base; anthers on distinct filaments (filaments about as long as anthers), exserted above corona, less than 1 mm. long and about as broad; style glabrous and not papillose above or very obseurely so. Fruits (Holden 1) immature, about 6 cm. in diam., shell about 2 mm. thick, rather shining and tuberculate or blistered.

description: Macroscopic.: petioles 1-6 mm. long; blades elliptic to lanceolate, ovate or oblanceolate, 6-20 cm. long, 3-8 cm. broad, subcordate to obtuse or rarely somewhat acute at base, short- to very long-acuminate and finely pointed at apex, rather dull, especially beneath, membranaceous to chartaceous, usually 5-plinerved with the inner pair opposite to conspicuously alternate and diverging at 2-20 mm. from base, reticulation faint to prominiulous on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets hirsute with long rusty spreading-ascend- ing (or retrorse) straight hairs; petioles hirsute with long hairs and also with curved shorter hairs or the latter lacking; blades densely fulvous- hirsute on both sides when young (pubeseenee remaining well into age, especially on principal nerves), and in addition often with shorter curved hairs on midrib on the upper surface, beneath usually with very minute tubercles, above sometimes with larger but less uniform and sparser tuber- dles, leaf-margins conspicuously setulose-ciliate. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, corymbose and loosely flowered, densely hirsute with long, spreading, more or less straight, hollow, rusty hairs con- sisting of a few long cells (the main infloreseence-axis in its lower part in addition with much shorter, hooked or hoop-curved, somewhat adpressed hairs), bracts linear and hirsute, pedicels up to 5 mm. long; calyx-lobes linear-lanceolate (or subulate), up to 6 mm. long, acuminate at apex, hirsute without; corolla-tube up to 1.5 cm. long, papillose and hirsute with- out with long spreading hairs except near base, pilose within mnostly below middle, otherwise glabrous, corolla-lobes pilose without, densely bearded at base within with soft hairs consisting of many short cells, papillose through- out, the apices densely so and often with a few sparse hairs of the many- celled kind; anthers on distinct filaments (filaments slightly shorter than anthers), exserted, less than 1 mm. long and about as broad; style glabrous. Mature fruits (Hook. Ie. P1. 4: pl. 364. 1841) globose, about 7 cm. in diam., shell bluish green and smooth, seeds 10-15, obliquely reniform, about 23 mm. long. Fruits (Krukoff 5081) immature, globose, about 3.5 cm. in diam., shell about 2 mm. thick, shining, smooth and with minute facets.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 0-1 mm. long; blades ovate to rhombic ovate or lanceolate, 6-12 cm. long, 3-5.5 cm. broad, rounded to narrowed and obtuse at the subsessile base, tapering and acute at apex, somewhat shining above, drying greenish, strikingly glauceseent-pale beneath, chartaceous, 3-plinerved (the basal-marginal nerves sometimes prominent) with the inner pair subopposite and diverging at 1-5 mm. from base, reticulation prominulous on both surfaces. description: Vine to 8 m. Laminas 6.2-23 cm long, 4.5-24 cm wide, usually cordate to ovate, sometimes elliptical to suborbicular, or sometimes 3-5 lobed, apex mucronate, base cordate or sometimes truncate or briefly attenuate, glabrate to glabrous above, densely pubescent with T-shaped hairs to tomentose below (trabecula 0.6-1.3 mm long, wavy to crisped and curled, stalk 0.1-0.3 mm long), margin with irregularly spaced sessile glands and also with filiform glands up to 6 mm long; petioles 1.7-10 cm long, with a pair of prominent but sessile glands at the apex, each gland 1-2.8 mm in diam. Flowers 15-40 (50) per umbel, these borne in dichasia, compound dichasia, or thyrses (axes to the 6th order). Peduncles 3.5-9 mm long, 0.7-2.1 times as long as the pedicels; pedicels 4-11 mm long, terete; both densely sericeous (hairs subsessile). Bracts 0.5-1.3 mm long, 0.5-1 (1.2) mm wide, triangular, apex acute or acuminate; bracteoles 0.5-1.5 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, oblong to triangular, apex obtuse, eglandular or sometimes with one or two inconspicuous glands (each ca. 0.2 mm in diam.); bracts and bracteoles sericeous abaxially. Sepals 1.8-2.2 (2.5) mm long, (1.8) 2-2.3 mm wide, glands 1.7-2.2 mm long, 0.9-1.2 mm wide. Lateral petals with the limbs orbicular, glabrous, margin denticulate or denticulate-fimbriate, teeth/ fimbriae up to 0.3 (0.4) mm long; anterior- lateral petals: claw (1.5) 1.7-2.2 mm long, limb 8-8.6 mm long, 7.5-8 mm wide; posterior-lateral petals: claw 0.8-1 mm long  limb ca. 7.5 mm long, ca. 6.5-7 mm wide; posterior petal: claw 2.8-3.2 mm long, apex indented, limb of posterior petal 6-6.5 mm long, 4-4.5 mm wide, elliptical to oblong, glabrous, margin with fimbriae up to 0.5 mm long. Stamens unequal, those opposite the posterior-lateral petals the largest, anthers of those opposite the lateral sepals with the connective enlarged and the locules re- duced or sometimes with only one reduced locule; anthers all loculate, glabrous. Anterior style 2-2.7 mm long, shorter than the posterior two, terete, glabrous, erect; apex 1.2-1.5 mm long, each foliole 1.3-1.6 mm long, 1.4-2 mm wide, square to sometimes subrectangular. Posterior styles 2.7-3 mm long, terete, glabrous, lyrate; folioles 1.3- 1.6 mm long, 1.4-2 mm wide, square to sometimes subrectangular. Dorsal wing of samara 3.7-4.5 cm long, 1.2-1.5 cm wide, upper margin with an obtuse or subacute tooth; nut bearing a pair of irregularly rectangular lateral winglets, these 4.7-5.5 mm long, 0.5-1.5 mm wide, or bearing spurs and/or crests or with only one or two lateral ridges; nut 4.5-6 mm high, 3.8-4.5 mm in diam., areole 2.8-3.5 mm long, 2.2-3.3 mm wide, concave, carpophore up to 4.5 mm long. Embryo 6-7.5 mm long, ca. 3 times as long as wide, laterally flattened, outer cotyledon 5.7-6.4 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide, inner cotyledon 4.9-6.3 mm long, 2.7-3.3 mm wide, both straight.

description: A canopy climber, to 4 inches in diameter; leaves granular-punctate and gla- brous above, distinguished from those of S. erichsonii by the fact that the mar- gins and main nerves are pilosulous.
bibliographicCitation: Fanshawe, Dennis B. 1954. The genus Strychnos in British Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 65-69.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 4-7 mm. long; blades broadly elliptic-ovate to narrowly lanceolate, 4-15 cm. long, 2-6.5 cm. broad, usually obtuse at base and acuminate at apex, dull to shining on both surfaces, drying greyish green or brownish, chartaceous to coriaceous, 3(5) -plinerved- with the inner pair subopposite or alternate and diverging at 0-15 mm. from base, reticulation obscure or intricate and somewhat prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: petioles densely pubescent with minute rusty subsetulose hairs or sparsely puberulent, becoming glabreseent or glabrous in age; blades beneath with obscure atomic dots and fulvous-velutinous or sparsely pubeseent with erect or suberect hairs, becoming glabreseent in age, above often tuberculate and pubescent with short curved hairs persistent on midrib or becoming completely glabrous. Inflorescences in congested eymes (sometimes up to 1.5 cm. long), fulvous-subsetulose with ascending or spreading hairs, bracts ovate-lanceolate, acute at apex, deeply concave and usually crowded, subsetulose and densely papillose-puberulent without, ciliate, pedicels short or none, becoming thickened; calyx-lobes ovate to ovate-lanceolate, up to 2 mm. long, acute to short-acuminate at apex, erect, papillose and puberulent without, sometimes pubescent toward apex within, ciliate, becoming inerassate at base; corollas not seen; ovary glabrous (rounded at apex after anthesis), style well pilose at base. Fruits (Krukoff 8038) globose, about 1.8 cm. in diam., shell about 0.5 mm. thick, yellowish, shining, smooth, reticulate-marked, seeds 1 or 2, usually orbicular, about 11 mm. in diam. and 3 mm. thick, somewhat convex on both faces; fruit-pedicels about 2.5 mm. in diam.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 5 mm. long; blades usually elliptic-lanceolate, 6-13 cm. long, 2.5-5.5 cm. broad, obtuse to acute at base, subacute to acumi- nate at apex, usually shining on both surfaces, sometimes rather dull, sub- coriaceous when mature, 3-plinerved with the inner pair mostly alternate, often conspicuously so, and diverging at 1-15 mm. from base, reticulation on old leaves rather prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: petioles with double indumentum, well pubescent with straight, ascending or somewhat spreading hairs and also with curved adpressed shorter hairs, becoming glabreseent ill age; blades beneath strigose or hirtellous on principal nerves and sometimes near margins, the remaining surface pubeseent in varying densities and in addition usually tuberculate, above sometimes tuberculate, sparsely pubescent with fulvous curved hairs on midrib, leaf-margins ciliate with ascending hairs, becoming glabrous in age. Iifloreseences in terminal eymes, corymbose, subsetulose with more or less adpressed fulvous hairs, bracts lanceolate, peduncles 0.5-2.5 cm. long, pedicels up to 3.5 mm. long; calyx-lobes lanceolate, about 2 mm. long, acute at apex, pubescent with adpressed hairs without (sometimes very sparsely so) and ciliate; corolla-tube up to 1 cm. long, papillose and densely fulvous- strigose without, pilose for the greater part within but.glabrous at base and throat, corolla-lobes strigose without, papillose and glabrous within, not bearded at base; anthers sessiloid, attached to filaments near base, exserted for the greater part, oblong, over 1 mm. long and more than twice as long as broad; style glabrous. [Fruits, etc. Ruiz & Pav. l.e.]. Fruits globose and 1-celled, about 7.5 cm. in diam., shell corky and fragile, yellowish green, pulp yellow, seeds about 4, suborbicular, flattened, usually variously angu- late, glabrous, with an ashy fragile covering.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 0.5-4 mm. long; blades ovate to lanceolate or obovate, 1-8 cm. long, 0.5-3.5 cm. broad, cordate to long-tapering at base, rounded or abruptly acuminate to long-tapering and mucronulate or finely tipped at apex, dull on both surfaces, paler beneath, membranaceous to subcoriaceous, 3- or 5-plinerved with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 0-1 cm. from base, sometimes pinnately nerved with 4 or 5 pairs of nerves, reticulation obscure or faint on both surfaces. Miicroscopic: branchlets and petioles glabrous or densely subhirtellous or puberulent with short, grey, more or less erect hairs; blades beneath with variable indumentum (densely subhirtellous with rather soft, pale hairs throughout or only on principal nerves or often merely puberulent on principal nerves or completely glabrous) without either barbation or membranaceous pockets in axils of inner principal nerves, above glabrous or rarely obscurely puberulent with very short hairs. Infloreseences in paniculate eymes, corymbose to hemispheric and loosely flowered with few to many flowers, 2-25 mm. long, puberulent with short grey straight erect hairs (or densely soft-pubescent with somewhat brownish-grey hairs), sometimes glabreseent, bracts lanceolate and acute, ciliate, otherwise glabrous, peduncles variable in length and about 0.5 mm. wide, pedicels short but distinct, about equal to calyx; calyx-lobes broadly ovate, about 1 mm. long, usually more or less acute at apex (sometimes obtuse), well ciliate or fimbriate-ciliate, otherwise glabrous or glabreseent; corollalobes glabrous and obscurely papillose without, densely bearded with long wool near middle within along an upwardly convex are, otherwise glabrous (papillose above) ; anthers barbate at base, filaments usually pilose the whole length and also at the place of their insertion on corolla-tube; ovary and style glabrous. [Fruits, etc., Prog. (26, p. 282) and from specimens.] Mature fruits globose, about 2 cm. in diam., shell less than 0.5 mm. thick, orange or yellow, shining, smooth, with minute facets or merely blistered, seeds 1 (or 2), globose, about 9 mm. in diam., embryo large, central, erect, cotyledons ovate-ellipitic or orbicular, radiele thick; fruit-pedicels about 2 mm. in diam.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.
