description: Macroscopic: petioles 2-7 mm. long; blades ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate or oblanceolate, 2.5-14 cm. long, 1-4 cm. broad, rounded to acute at base, acuminate and finely pointed at apex, dull oni both surfaces, mnembranaceous to chartaceous, 3-plinerved with the inner pair subopposite or alternate and diverging at 1-13 mm. from base, reticulation faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles grey-puberulent with short erect or ascending hairs, becoming glabreseent or glabrous; blades beneath puberulent on principal nerves, when young, and sometimes pale-barbate in axils of the inner pair, otherwise glabrous, above sometimes sparsely puberulent oln midrib, otherwise glabrous. Infloreseences in paniculate eymes, usually hemispheric and many-flowered, glabrous or very sparsely puberulent with short erect hairs, bracts mostly laneeolate and long-acuminate, sparsely ciliate, otherwise glabrous, peduncles flattened, 0-10 mm. long and 0.5-1 mm. wide, pedicels as long as calyx or shorter; calyx-lobes usually ovate-lanceolate, often unequal in length, slightly over 1 mm. long, acute to long-acuminate at apex, spreading, glabrous and apparently not ciliate (or subeiliate); corolla-lobes obscurely papillose without, rather densely long-bearded near middle within along an upwardly convex are, above this line of barbation papillose and glabrous, below neither pilose nor papillose; anthers glabrous or pilose; ovary and style glabrous. Fruits (Lundell 6266 and Gentle 3181) not completely mature, globose, about 5 cm. in diam., shell about 6 mm. thick, shining, tuberculate, seeds many, with white woolly (finally easily removable) covering, irregular, generally in bluntly 3-sided oblique pyramids with two faces plane and the remaining face rounded as the base, up to about 17 mm. long, pale brown or brownish-orange and translucent, stony, hilum generally umbonulate within a depression.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 0-1 mm. long; blades usually rhombic-ovate or broadly elliptic, 6-13 cm. long, 3-8 cm. broad, narrowed and obtuse at the subsessile base, tapering and acute at apex, somewhat shining above and paler beneath, chartaceous, 3-plinerved with the inner pair subopposite or alternate and diverging at 2-7 mm. from base, reticulation prominulous especially above. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles densely fulvousvelutinous, becoming sparsely subhirtellous or glabrous in age; blades beneath fulvous-velutinous, becoming in age sparsely subhirtellous or glabrescent (indumentum most persistent along principal nerves and on margins near base) and tuberculate with the bases of fallen hairs, above sparsely pubescent on principal nerves to glabreseent or glabrous. Infloreseences in eymes, corymbose to short-thyrsoid, becoming elongated, densely fulvous-subsetulose with spreading straight (or slightly curved) hairs of various lengths, bracts lanceolate, acute, sometimes pubescent both without and within, peduncles about 1 mm. wide, pedicels densely subsetulose, about as long as calyx or shorter, singly disposed on the infloreseencerachis or grouped on lateral branches; calyx-lobes ovate-lanceolate, up to 1.5 mm. long, acute at apex, sparsely pubescent without or tuberculate with the bases of fallen hairs, well ciliate, glabrous within except near apex, and there sparsely pubescent; corollas and stamens not seen; ovary anid style glabrous. [Fruits, etc. Sprague & Sandw. l.e.] Fruits flattened, up to 2.3 cm. in diam., shell brunneus, smooth, seed 1, broadly elliptic, 15 mm. long, 12-13 mm. broad, 5 mm. thick.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 2-13 mm. long; blades variable in shape, elliptic, suborbicular to lanceolate or oblanceolate, 7-26 cm. long, 3.5-13.5 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, usually abruptly short-acuminate at apex, dull to shining and usually concolored, the old ones often drying an oliveocher yellow (the young a russet-brown), coriaceous, 3- or 5-plinerved with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 0-10 mm. from base, reticulation prominulous to somewhat prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets densely fulvous-puberulent with very short, adpressed hairs; petioles puberulent with very short hairs, becoming glabreseent in age; blades beneath with atomic dots, sometimes obscure, and universally puberulent with very short, adpressed hairs, sometimes obscure in old age, above usually tuberculate to blistered and puberulent on midrib when young, otherwise essentially glabrous. Infloreseences in axillary (and terminal) thyrses, up to 2.5 cm. long, fulvous-puberulent with very short, adpressed hairs, pedicels about equal to or shorter than calyx; calyx-lobes broadly deltoid, about 1 mm. long, subacute at apex, puberulent to glabrous without with pubescence extending well within, ciliate; corolla-tube up to 0.8 cm. long, papillose anid glabrous without, pilose within from about middle up to throat, corollalobes papillose and glabrous without, bearded at base within (the wool continuous with pubescence within corolla-tube), otherwise glabrous (a few scattered hairs sometimes present) ; anthers on distinct filaments (filaments about 4 as long as anthers), slightly exserted from beneath wool on corollalobes; style glabrous. Fruits (Froes 11817) not completely mature, irregularly spheroid (in early immaturity elongated-ellipsoid), about 3.5 cm. in diam., mucronate at apex, shell about 2 mm. thick (about 1 mm. thick in Krukoff 9110 which is very immature), dull or somewhat shining, smooth or minutely tuberculate, seeds many, with irregular outlines, oval or irregularly oblong or ovate, with faces flattened (or convex on one and concave on the other), up to 20 mm. long, 12 mm. broad, 6 mm. thick (seeds in Pinlkus 174 immature, only 2, oval, about 23 mm. long and 18 mm. broad, testa with adherent membranaceous squamae).
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: A canopy climber to 12 inches in diameter; bark dark reddish-brown, rough, slash pale crimson, hard, brittle and thin.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 3-10 mm. long; blades usually lanceolate to elliptic, 5-15 cm. long, 3-7 cm. broad, obtuse to aeute at base, usually aeute to shortaeuminate at apex, shining on both surfaces, often drying a dull olive-ocher yellow, coriaceous or subcoriaceous, usually 3-plinerved with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 2-10 mm. from base, reticulation intricate and prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles of young leaves pubeseent with either very short or somewvhat longer substrigose hairs, sparsely so in age; blades beneath with inconspicuous atomic dots and essentially glabrous (scattered, very short hairs sometimes present) but usually conspicuously fulvous hirtellous-barbate in axils of the inner pair of principal nerves, above inconspicuously tubereulate or smooth and glabrous. Infloreseences in axillary thyrses, up to 3 cm. long, densely fulvous-puberulent with adpressed or ascending hairs, pedicels short or none; calyxlobes ovate to ovate-lanceolate, up to 1.5 mm. long, aeute at apex, sparsely puberulent or glabrous without; corolla-tube about 0.5 em. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose the whole length within (sparsely so at base), corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous without, bearded at base within, otherwise glabrous and papillose; anthers sessiloid, ineluded except for their tips; style glabrous. [Fruits, etc. Prog. 26, p. 274).] Fruits subglobose, about size of cherry, seed one by abortion, suborbicular, flattened, testa fuscous, minutely rugulose.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 2-6 mm. long; blades elliptic, lanceolate, oblanceolate or ovate, 5-18 cm. long, 2.5-9.5 cm. broad, rounded (sometimes subcordate) to obtuse or acute at base, usually short-acuminate at apex, usually dull (paler beneath) or shining on both surfaces, often drying an olive-ocher yellow, subcoriaceous, 3(5)-plinerved with the inner pair subopposite or conspicuously alternate and diverging at 5-25 mm. from base, reticulation faint or rarely prominulous on both surfaces. Microscopic: petioles puberulent or miinutely subsetulose, becoming glabreseent in age; blades beneath with atomic dots, sometimes obscure, essentially glabrous (scattered short hairs often present) but usually conspicuously hirtellous-barbate in axils of the inner principal nerves and when young more or less puberulent or minutely substrigose on principal nerves, above usually tuberculate, puberulent on midrib when young, leaf-margins sometimes ciliate near base. Inflorescences in axillary short thyrses, densely fulvous-puberulent to subsetulose with adpressed or ascending hairs; pedicels about as long as calyx; calyx-lobes lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, about 1.5 mm. lonig, acuminate or subacuminate at apex, well subsetulose without with short rusty hairs and ciliate; corolla-tube papillose and glabrous without, pilose within, corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous without, bearded at base within, otherwise glabrous; anthers sessiloid; style glabrous. Fruits (Tonduz 7236) globose, about 4 cm. in diam., shell less than 1 mm. thick, yellowish, shining, smooth or somewhat tuberculate, seeds many, irregularly oblong, about 20 mm. long, 15 mm. broad, 4 mm. thick, flattened on both faces or convex on one and concave on the other; fruit-pedicels about 4 mm. in diam.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: bases of branchlets often with conspicuous cataphylls; petioles 2-7 mm. long; blades variable in shape, ovate or elliptic or obovate, 5-15 cm. long, 3-9 cm. broad, rounded to subeordate or obtuse at base, short- acuminate or acute to rounded and mucronulate at apex, usually shining above and dull beneath, sometimes drying an olive-ocher yellow, coriaceous in age, usually 5-plinerved with the inner pair opposite to alternate and diverging at 6-30 mm. from base, well impressed above, reticulation faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets densely brownish-rusty pubescent with more or less adpressed hairs, the indumentum persistent in age; petioles densely pubescent; blades when young densely brownish-ruLsty pubescent on both surfaces, beneath in age becoming merely universally puberulent with short curved hairs (sometimes papillose at base) usually with minute in- conspicuous (or conspicuous) atomic dots, above becoming glabreseent with the puberulence mnost persistent on midrib and near margins. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, short-thyrsoid or corymbose and densely flowered, very densely brownish-rusty subsetulose with short, adpressed, slightly curved or straight hairs, pedicels short or none; calyx-lobes ovate, about 2 mm. long, somewhat acute at apex, subsetulose without as inflores- cences; corolla-tube up to 0.8 cm. long, papillose without and also setulose with spreading or ascending rusty hairs, densely pilose throughout within except at base and throat, corolla-lobes with an indumentum without as that on corolla-tube, densely bearded at base within, otherwise papillose and glabrous; anthers sessiloid, included, over 1 mm. long and about twice as long as broad; style glabrous. Fruits not seen.

description: Macroscopic: bases of flowering branchlets with cataphylls; petioles 4-8 mm. long; blades ovate or -elliptic, 8-10 cm. long, 3.8-5 cm. broad, cuneate or rounded at base, short-acuminate at apex, hardly shining on either surface, thin-coriaceous, 3-plinerved (the additional pair of basal- marginal nerves prominulous) with the inner pair opposite or subopposite and diverging at 3-9 mm. fromn base, tertiary nerves inconspicuous but the reticulation finely raised, especially above. Microscopic: leaves glabrous; blades above roughened with crowded elevated tubercles. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, broadly corymbose and densely flowered with branches acutely angulate and pubescent, bracts 1-2.5 mm. long, ciliate, peduncles 1.5-2.5 cm. long, glabrous, pedicels very short; calyx-lobes ovate to ovate-lanceolate, about 0.75 mm. long, obtuse at apex, ciliate; corolla-tube about 0.85 cm. long, 0.5-0.75 mm. broad, glabrous both without and within, not papillose, corolla-lobes about 2.5 mili. long, glabrous without, einereous- papillose within, especially toward margins and apex; anthers on very short filaments, exserted, oblong-oblanceolate, about 1.75 mm. long, acuminate at base; style glabrous. Fruits not seen.

description: Macroscopic: petioles hardly over 2 mm. long; blades ovate-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic, 3.5-12.5 cm. long, up to 4.5 cm. broad, obtusely cuneate at base, acute at apex, dull or somewhat shining on both surfaces, subcoriaceous or coriaceous, 3-plinerved (midrib somewhat raised above) with the inner pair opposite or subopposite and diverging near base, reticulation prominulous on both surfaces. Microscopic: leaves glabrous with blades somewhat tuberculate on both surfaces. Infloreseences in few-flowered glomerate eymes, sparsely pubescent with short, rusty, curved (or straight), adpressed or ascending hairs, bracts lanceolate and bracteoles ovate, ciliate, otherwise glabrous, pedicels very short or none; calyx-lobes broadly deltoid, somewhat less than 1 mm. long, usually obtuse at apex (sometimes rather acute), well ciliate with spreading rusty hairs, otherwise glabrous; corolla-lobes apparently not papillose (or minutely so) and glabrous without, flat and well bearded near middle within along an upwardly convex are, otherwise glabrous; anthers barbate at base; ovary and style glabrous. [Fruits, etc. Prog. I.c. and from Gcaudichaud s.n.] Seeds 2, oval, about 20 mm. long, 17 mm. broad, 4 mm. thick, convex on one face and concave on the other, rugulose, cotyledons lanceolate and about 3 times as long as the swollen radiele.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 2-6 mm. long; blades very variable, ovate to lanceolate or obovate to oblanceolate, 3-9 cm. long, 1.5-4.5 cm. broad, subcordate to cuneate at base, rounded to acute or acuminate at apex, mucronulate, dull or shining on both surfaces, paler beneath, submembranaceous to chartaceous or subcoriaceous, 3(5)-plinerved with the inner pair usually alternate and diverging at 0-13 mm. from base, reticulation usually faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets densely pubescent with minute, pale-rusty, ascending or adpressed, subsetulose hairs; petioles more or less puberulent or pubescent with minute, ascending or adpressed, subsetulose hairs; blades beneath with inconspicuous atomic dots, sometimes apparently lacking, and with variable indumentum (universally puberulent with very short, adpressed, straight hairs or pubescent with much longer, erect, curved hairs or with any or several of the intermediate forms of indumentum), the pubescence more dense in axils of the inner principal nerves, thus occasionally giving a barbate appearance, above tuberculate or smooth and pubescent with subsetulose hairs (hairs sometimes very short), becoming glabrescent, the indumentum most persisteint on midrib, leaf-margins often subeiliate near base. Inflorescences in short-racemose eymes, loosely few-flowered (flowers mostly 5-7), more or less subsetulose with short, rusty, adpressed or ascending hairs, bracts ovate to lanceolate, subsetulose, pedicels up to 4 mm. long; calyx-lobes variable, broadly ovate to narrowly lanceolate, often of unequal width in the same flower and from less than 1 mm. to over 1.5 mm. long, somewhat acute to acuminate at apex, usually sparsely subsetulose without and becoming glabrous, ciliate to a varying degree; corolla-lobes lanate on the lower half within, the upper half well papillose but glabrous or sometimes with a few stray pili; ovary and style glabrous. Fruits subovate or oblong, about 1.3 cm. in diam., mucronate at apex, shell thin, yellow, usually shining, smooth, sometimes finely tuberculate, seeds 1-2, cotyledons lanceolate; fruit-pedicels about 1.5 mm. in diam.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 1-5 mm. long; blades ovate to elliptic or lanceolate, 4-13 cm. long, 1.5-6 cm. broad, rounded to subacute or subeordate at base, acute to acurlinate and finely pointed at apex, usually dull on both surfaces, membranaceous, becoming chartaceous or even subcoriaceous in age, 3(5) - plinerved with the innier pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 0-15 mm. from base, reticulation prominulous or sometimes prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: petioles with double indumentum, fulvous-pubeseent with straight, rather stiff hairs and also with curved, adpressed, much shorter hairs, becoming glabreseent in age; blades beneath often tubercu- late, pubescent with short curved hairs on principal nerves and in addition often with a few long straight hairs, otherwise essentially glabrous, above often with whitish tubercles mostly between veins, pubescent with long, somewhat curved, deciduous hairs and often also with shorter curved hairs on principal nerves, otherwise glabrous, leaf-margins sparsely ciliate to glabreseent or glabrous. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, corymbose, pubescent in streaks with long, rather stiff, adpressed or ascending hairs or glabreseent, bracts lanceo- late and ciliate, pedicels up to 3 mm. long; calyx-lobes lanceolate, about 3 mm. long, acuminate at apex, ciliate, otherwise glabrous; corolla-tube up to 1.5 (-2) cm. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose within but glabrous at base and throat (sometimes near throat with a corona that has a crenate- undulate hardly raised shallow rim), corolla-lobes linear-lanceolate, densely papillose especially within and glabrous; anthers on long filaments (fila- ments more than twice as long as anthers), greatly exserted; style glabrous. Mature fruits 4-8 cm. in diam., many-seeded. Immature fruits globose, about 2.5 cm. in diam., mucronate at apex, shell about 0.75 mm. thick, smooth and with minute facets or somewhat reticulate-marked; fruit-pedicels about 6 mm. in diam.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 0.5-1 mm. long; blades ovate to ovate-lanceolate, about 4.5 cm. long and 2 cm. broad, usually rounded at base, short-acuminate and blunt at apex, dull on both surfaces and paler beneath, membranaceous to chartaceous, 3(5)-plinerved with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 1-8 mm. from base, reticulation obscure or faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles puberulent with short grey erect (or ascending) hairs, becoming glabreseent or glabrous; blades beneath puberulent on principal nerves when young, sometimes pale-barbate in axils of the innner pair of principal nerves (also less markedly in axils of the adjacent pair) and often also with long membranaceous pockets, above sometimes sparsely puberulent on midrib, otherwise glabrous. Infloreseences in congested eymes, spherically clustered, less than 1 cm. long, sparsely puberulent with very short, grey, spreading, straight (or slightly hooked) hairs, bracts narrowly lanceolate and acute, peduncles about 20 mm. long and 0.5 mm. wide (much longer than flower-clusters), pedicels none or very short; calyx-lobes lanceolate, from less than 2 mm. up to 2.5 mm. long (often in the same flower), acute or acuminate and finally recurved at apex, very sparsely puberulent both without and within, sparsely ciliate (cilia consisting merely of marginal puberulence); corollalobes papillose and glabrous without, bearded near middle within along an upwardly convex are with hairs that stray down margins toward sinuses, otherwise glabrous (papillose above); anthers pilose at base; ovary puberulent at apex and style at base. [Fruits, etc., Prog. l.e.] Fruits orbicular and flattened on sides, about 0.6 cm. in diam., subcoriaceous, mucronate at apex, seed 1, suborbicular, greatly flattened, testa glabrous; fruit-pedicels hardly inerassate.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 10 mm. long; blades elliptic-oblong, 8-18 cm. long, 3.5-9 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, usually abruptly acuminate at apex, dull to shining above and markedly pale-glauceseent beneath with petioles drying blackish, coriaceous, 3-plinerved (the basal-marginal nerves sometimes prominent; principal nerves usually impressed above) with the inner pair usually subopposite and diverging at 3-10 mm. from base, reticulation mostly impressed in the wrinkled surface above and faint beneath with the ultimate veinlets not raised, but sometimes with the reticulation raised either above or beneath or on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles puberulent with very short adpressed hairs (juvenile plants often with the branchlets hirsute with long spreading hairs); blades beneath with atomic dots conspicuous or obscure, densely universally puberulent with very short, adpressed hairs, above very sparsely puberulent on midrib near base, otherwise glabrous. Infloreseences in axillary greatly elongated and paniculate thyrses, densely many-flowered, densely brownish-ferrugineous puberulent with adpressed hairs, pedicels very short or none; calyx-lobes ovate, about 0.5 mm. long, somewhat rounded at apex, erect, densely puberulent without and ciliate; corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous without, lanate on the whole face within; anthers barbate at base and also with tufts of pili at apex; ovary broader than long, glabrous, truncate at apex, style puberulent, stigma conical and sharply pointed, about the length of style or somewhat longer. Fruits (Krukoff 9115) immature, globose-ellipsoid, about 2.3 cm. long, 2.0 cm. broad, rounded at base and mucronate at apex, shell about 1 mm. thick (exocarp carnose and the mesocarp osseous), rather dull, wrinkled (smooth in Moore 574), warty, rather dull, glaucous; fruit-pedicels about 5 mm. in diam.

description: Macroscopic: branches often pitted with conspicuous orbicular lenticels; petioles 1-3 mm. long; blades ovate or elliptic-orbicular to ovate-lanceolate, 1.5-6 cm. long, 1.5-3 cm. broad, usually rounded or subcordate to obtuse at base, obtuse to acuminate and mucronulate at apex, usually shining on both surfaces, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, 3-plinerved (principal nerves not prominent beneath) with the inner pair usually subopposite and diverging at 0.4 mm. from base, reticulation prominent to faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: petioles densely subhirtellous, becoming sparsely so; blades beneath in age conspicuously verrucular (tubereles following nerves and veinlets), glabrous or subsetulose on midrib (wads of dense indumentum sometimes persistent), above verrucular as beneath and glabrous or with curved hairs along midrib, leaf-margins more or less ciliate to glabrous. Infloreseences in short corymbose thyrses, rather densely flowered, pubescent with subsetulose, pale, adpressed, ascending or sometimes spreading hairs (sometimes glabreseent), bracts mostly lanceolate and acuminate, ciliate, otherwise glabrous, peduncles usually about 5 mm. long and 0.5 mm. wide, pedicels shorter than calyx, puberulent with very short, erect, thick hairs which are often lost; calyx-lobes broadly deltoid-ovate, 1-1.5 mm. long, acute at apex, spreading at anthesis, puberulent or minutely tuberculate without with the bases of fallen hairs, conspicuously ciliate; corolla-lobes finally spreading, glabrous and usually densely papillose without, bearded near middle within along an upwardly convex are (beard shading down margins with hairs becoming sparser toward sinuses), glabrous above the line of barbation and usually well papillose, flat and thickened, glabrous or sparsely pilose below; anthers barbate at base, filaments often pilose along their lengths and sometimes also at the place of their insertion on corollatube; ovary and style glabrous. [Fruits, etc. Prog. L.c. and from specimens. Mature fruits globose, about 1.5 em. in diam., shell less than 0.5 mm. thick, shining, smooth, very faintly reticulate-marked, seeds 1-3, orbicular, flattened, about 15 mm. in diam. and 4 mm. thick, embryo minute, cotyledons linear-lanceolate and about as long as radiele; fruit-pedicels about 1 mm. in diam.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 5-18 mm. long; blades usually elliptic, elliptic- lanceolate or elliptic-oblanceolate, 7-35 cm. long, 3.5-17 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, usually rounded and abruptly short-acuminate (sometimes gradually tapering) at apex, usually dull on both surfaces, sometimes shin- ing above and pale or glauceseent beneath, sometimes drying in part an olive-ocher yellow, thickly coriaceous in age, 3(5)-plinerved with the iniier pair subopposite or alternate and diverging at 2-5 (-10) mm. from base, reticulation loose and prominulous or faint on both surfaces, with the ulti- mate veinlets hardly raised. Microscopic: branchlets puberulent with very short adpressed hairs; petioles rugose, densely puberulent when young with very short hairs that are more or less persistent even in old age; blades be- neath often with atomic dots and universally puberulent with very short adpressed hairs that are either closely spaced or scattered (in age often very few or apparently none), above sometimes with conspicuous tubereles or smooth, puberulent on midrib, especially when young, otherwise glabrous. Ilfloreseences in axillary elustered eymes, subglobose and densely flow- ered, densely fulvous-puberulent with adpressed to erect hairs; pedicels short, up to 2 mm. long; calyx-lobes broadly ovate-deltoid, about 1 mm. long, somewhat acute at apex, densely puberutent without and ciliate; corolla-tube up to 0.9 cm. long (usually much shorter), densely papillose without and pubescent with usually thick, short, erect hairs (hairs diminishing in length and finally grading into mere papillae at base), pilose within from below middle to throat, corolla-lobes long-papillose or pubescent without, lanate within (very densely so at base and more sparsely so above middle); anthers sessiloid, included except for their tips, up to 1.5 mm. long and about three times as long as broad; style glabrous. Fruits (not completely mature) globose, about 6 em. in diam., shell about 6 mm. thick, dull, reticulate-marked and smooth or warty, seeds many, elliptic-oblong, about 25 mm. long, 18 mm. broad, 6 mm. thick, straight or shallowly concave on one side and convex on the opposite side, rather flattened on both faces (or convex on one face and concave on the other), testa with adhering membranaceous squammae; fruit-pedicels up to 20 mm. in diam.

description: A canopy climber, to 8 inches in diameter; bark dimpled, blackish.

description: Essentially like S. brachistantha with the following differences: pubescence on branchlets gen-erally of longer, more curved, less ascending hairs, blades beneath with principal nerves more sparsely puberulent, inflorescences pale-rusty or grey puberulent with moderately long, usually ascending and slightly hooked hairs, calyx-lobes sparsely ciliate, and the line of barbation within corolla-lobes is somewhat lower toward base. Fruits immature, rounded, shell about 0.75 mm. thick, shining, smooth, sometimes lightly retieulate-ridged, endocarp developing a thick pale wool that is adherent to testa of seed; seed 1 (?), spheroid, about 9 mm. long, brownish and translucent when divested of its wool; fruit-pedicels about 2 mm. in diam.

description: Infloreseences in paniculate eymes, corymbose or hemispheric and loosely flowered, puberulent with short, grey, erect, straight or slightly hooked hairs, bracts narrowly lanceolate, acuminate and usually subulate at apex, sparsely ciliate, otherwise glabrous, peduncles up to 10 mm. long and about 0.5 mm. wide, pedicels shorter than calyx but usually distinct, minutely puberulent; calyx-lobes lanceolate (rarely deltoid-ovate), about 1.5 mm. long (rarely less than 1 mm., up to 2 mm. long), acute at apex, very sparsely puberulent without, sparsely ciliate (cilia consisting merely of marginal puberulence), glabrous within or sparsely puberulent near apex; corolla-lobes glabrous and slightly papillose without, bearded near middle within along an upwardly convex are, otherwise glabrous (papillose above) ; anthers pilose or glabrous at base; ovary puberulent at apex and style at base. Mature fruits globose, about 1.5 cm. in diam., shell less than 0.5 mm. thick, shining, smooth, sometimes with reticulate markings, endocarp developing into a thick wool or into membranaceous squamae easily removable from testa, seeds spheroid, sometimes much flattened, about 7 mm. long, brownish and translucent, hilum umbonulate within a depression; fruit-pedicels about 1 mm. in diam.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Like S. pananensis with the following differences in the collections ex- amined: petioles 1-3 mm. long, blades usually shining on both surfaces, 3 (5) - plinerved with the inner pair divergiiig at 0-8 mm. from base, above and beneath with tubercles less conspicuous than in S. panamnensis, beneath when young often puberulent throughout, tube and lobes of corolla without with spreading subsetulose hairs of varying lengths and densities (often totally lacking near base of corolla-tube). Fruits (Steyermark 39380) mature, shell up to about 3 mm. thick, rather shining and smooth, sometimes minutely tuberculate or lightly reticulate-wrinkled and with a membrana- ceous, often exfoliating skin; fruit-pedicels up to 10 mm. in diam. Seeds (Gentle 592) many, irregularly 3-sided, flat on one face and bluntly tri- angular-convex on the opposite face, up to about 15 mm. long and 7 mm. broad.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 5-10 mm. long, often glauceseent; blades sub- elliptic, usually broadest below middle, 7-16 cm. long, 4-9.5 cm. broad, rounded to acute at base, usually short-acuminate at apex, shining on both surfaces or more often paler to glauceseent beneath, especially near base of midrib, the old ones often drying an olive-ocher yellow (the young ones brownish above and pale beneath), coriaceous, 3- or 5-plinerved with the inner pair mostly alternate and diverging at 5-10 mm. from base, retieula- tion usually prominulous on both surfaces. Microscopic: petioles densely puberulent with rusty or greyish, adpressed hairs, becoming glabreseent in age; blades beneath usually unniversally puberulent with very short adpressed hairs, especially when young, becoming glabreseent in age (hairs most per- sistent on midrib), and also with minute crowded whitish atomic dots which sometimes are hardly discernible, above essentially glabrous and occasionally tuberculate. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, subhemispheric and densely flowered, very densely fulvous-puberulent with short, adpressed, somewhat curved hairs, peduncles 2-4.5 cm. long, pedicels up to 2 mm. long; calyx-lobes deltoid-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, up to 1.5 mm. long, somewhat acute at apex, sparsely puberulent or glabrous without and ciliate; corolla-tube about 0.8 cm. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose from near base up to throat within, corolla-lobes about 4 mm. long, papillose and glabrous without, lanate-bearded at base and well soft-pilose on the whole face within; anthers flexible on very short but distinct filaments, subincluded; style glabrous. Fruits (Kru7koff 9056) immature, elliptic-globose or pyriform, about 3 em. long and 2 cm. broad, shell up to 3 mm. thick, loosely reticulate-wrinkled and minutely but conspicuously tuberculate, often glaucous; fruit-pedicels up to 9 mm. in diam.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 0-3 mm. long; blades broadly elliptic to ovatelanceolate, 3-6 cm. long, 2-4 cm. broad, subcordate to obtuse at base, acute to rounded and mucronulate at apex, dull or somewhat shining above and usually rusty beneath, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, 3-plinerved with the inner pair usually alternate and diverging at 2-10 mm. from base, reticulation faint or somewhat prominulous. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles densely fulvous-velutinous, becoming sparsely subhirtellou's in age; blades beneath densely fulvous-velutinous, becoming sparsely subhirtellous (wads of dense indumentum sometimes persistent) and tuberculate with the bases of fallen hairs in age, above tuberculate or smooth, velutinous when young, becoming essentially glabrous except for the pubescence on principal nerves and the sparse cilia on margins. Infloreseences in eymes, corymbose to short-thyrsoid and rather densely many-flowered, densely fulvous-subsetulose with spreading straight (or slightly curved) hairs and also with short curved hairs, becoming more sparsely so in age, primary bracts often linear-lanceolate, acute and subsetulose, peduncles about 1 mm. wide, pedicels shorter than calyx or none; calyx-lobes deltoid-ovate to lanceolate, about 1 mm. long, acute at apex, sparsely subsetulose without and well ciliate; corolla-lobes minutely papillose without and with few or many short hairs, well bearded near middle within along an upwardly convex are, the pili straying down margins to sinuses, otherwise glabrous and with the upper half of lobes minutely papillose and thickened but flat; anthers sparsely barbate at base or glabrous, (often with several pili on corolla-tube at base of filaments) ; ovary and style glabrous. [Fruits, etc. Prog. (26, p. 278) and from H. J. B. R. 3372.] Mature fruits globose, with shell about 0.5 mm. thick, dull, smooth, millutely tuberculate, seeds 2, orbicular, about 12 mm. in diam., flattened on both faces, testa rugulose; fruit-pedicels about 2 mm. in diam.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 5 mm. long; blades usually ovate, about 9 cm. long and 4.5 cm. broad, rounded or obtuse at base, acuminate at apex, submembranaceous, 5-plinerved with the inner pair diverging at 0-10 mm. from base. Microscopic: branchlets pilose; petioles glabrous or strigose; blades subglabrous. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, corymbose, about 4 cm. broad, bracts lanceolate, peduncles about 1.5 cm. long, pedicels about 2 mm. long; calyx- lobes lanceolate, about 2 mm. long, obtuse or acute at apex, ciliate; corolla- tube about 1.5 cm. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose only near middle within, corolla-lobes glabrous both without and within, not bearded at base; anthers on long filaments and attached near middle, slightly ex- serted, ovate-oblong, about as long as filaments and only slightly longer than broad; style glabrous. Pruits globose, about 9 cm. in diam., shell corky, yellowish green, pulp whitish, seeds many, irregular in shape, discoid, about 20 mm. broad, the outer seed-coat carnose, the inner pergameneous and somewhat smooth, embryo at base of horny albumen, excentric, erect, cotyle- dons ovate, nervose, radiele terete anid peripheral.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 5-15 mm. long; blades variable, broadly or nar- rowly elliptic or oblong, broadest above or below middle, 9-27 cm. long, 4.5-15 cm. broad, obtuse to acute at base, obttuse or very short- to long- acuminate or caudate at apex, more or less shining Qr sometimes dull, paler either beneath or above, coriaceous in age, usually 3-plinerved (the basal- marginal nerves sometimes prominent) with the inner pair subopposite and diverging at or very near base, reticulation prominulous or prominent oln both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets glabrous; leaves essentially glabrous; blades beneath with conspicuous crowded whitish atomic dots (sometimes deep within the tissue thus obscure, sometimes forming the bases of very short hairs), above tuberculate or smooth. Infloreseenees in axillary eymes, short-thyrsoid or corymbose and densely flowered, sparsely fulvous-puberulent to glabreseent, pedicels shorter than calyx or none; calyx-lobes ovate, less than 1 mm. long and about as broad, usually obtuse to rounded at apex, ciliate, otherwise glabrous or nearly so; corolla-tube up to 1 cm. long, glabrous both without and within, not papillose, corolla-lobes glabrous without, sparsely pilose along edges near middle within, otherwise glabrous; anthers sessiloid, somewhat exserted, oblong-oblanceolate, about 1.75 mm. long, acuminate and beset with several pili at base; style pilose. Fruits (Krukoff 9063) immature, globose, about 5 cm. in diam., shell about 5 mm. thick, hard, dull, with minute facets, the exocarp often chipping off and leaving the granulated mesocarp exposed seeds many; fruit-pedicels up to 11 mm. in diam.

description: A canopy climber, to 5 inches in diameter; bark very rough, scaly, black-brown; slash off-white, soft, thicker than S. diaboli bark. Distinguished from S. pedunculata by the glabrous, leathery, not intricately reticulate leaves.

description:
Macroscopic: petioles 3-12 mm. long; blades usually broadly ovate to narrowly lanceolate, 4-22 cm. long, 3.5-10.5 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse and often deeurrent at base on petiole, somewhat narrowed to long-tapering at apex, shining on both surfaces, often drying an olive-ocher or vivid russetbrown whell old, coriaceous, 3- or 5-plinerved with the inner pair subopposite or alternate and diverging at 2-15 mm. from base, reticulation usually loose and prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets sparsely puberulent and with the stipule-lines sparsely puberulent-ciliate; petioles puberulent with very short hairs, becoming glabreseent or glabrous in age; blades beneath with inconspicuous (or conspicuous and crowded) atomic dots, universally puberulent with very short, adpressed hairs, often very sparse, often faintly barbate in axils of the inner principaL nerves, above sometimes sparsely puberulent on midrib near base, otherwise glabrous and smooth.

Infloreseences in axillary eymes, densely hemispheric to short-thyrsoid, glabrous to sparsely puberulent, bracts ovate to lanceolate and ciliate, pedicels short and sparsely puberulent with very short, rusty hairs; calyx-lobes usually ovate-lanceolate, about 1 mm. long, unequal in length, acute to somewhat rounded at apex, glabrous or sparsely puberulent without and ciliate; corolla-tube up to 0.8 cm. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose within from near base up to near throat but glabrous at throat itself, corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous without, papillose from apex for about 3 the way down, there bearded along an upwardly convex are and at the very base neither bearded not papillose; anthers sessiloid, partly exserted, less than 1 mm. long; style glabrous. Mature fruits globose, about 3.5 cm. in diam., mucronate at apex, shell about 1 mm. thick, dull, variously tuberculate or warty, sometimes in part loosely reticulate-marked, seeds many, oval to more or less oblong, about 20 mm. long, 12 mm. broad, up to 6 mm. thick (but often much thinner in the same fruit), flattened on both faces (or convex on one and concave on the other), parts of the membranaceous squamae often adherent or, when completely fallen, leaving a rugulose surface; fruit-pedicels up to 8 mm. in diam.

description: E specimine unico cognita, florifera 35 cm. alta, generis e minimis; rhizomate sub-bulboso; foliis dense rosulatis, vaginis suborbicularibus, 3 cm. latis, pallidis, fere omnino glabris, laminis recurvatis, anguste triangularibus, pungentibus, ad 13 cm. longis, basi 16 mm. latis, spinis atris sursum curvatis ad 3 mm. longis sublaxe armatis, supra glabrisviridibusque, subtus dense adpresseque cinereo-lepidotis; scapo erecto, gracili, cinereo- lepidoto; scapi vaginis subfoliaceis, curvato-divergentibus, quam internodiis bene longioribus sed scapum paulo obtegentibus; inflorescentia bipinnatim paniculata, basi extrema interrupta excepta densissime ellipsoidea, 9 cm. longa, 4 cm. diametro; bracteis primariis ellipticis, acutis, cinereo-lepidotis, ad 2 cm. longis, infimis ramos subabortivos aequantibus, alteris quam eis brevioribus; racemis stricte erectis, subdense paucifloris; bracteis florigeris ellipticis, pedicellos superantibus, cum) floribus secunde versis; floribus patentibus; pedicellis gracilibus, 3-4 mm. longis, oblongo-lanceolatis, late acutis, 11 mm. longis, glabris; petalis ca. 14 mm. longis, stamina superantibus.

description: Description: Staminate flowers: sepals 9, the outer minute, the in- nermost largest, elliptic, about 2.9 mm. long and 1.9 mm. wide, acute at both ends, densely strigose-pubeseent with long appressed hairs outside, glabrous within; petals 6, obovate-spatulate, about 1.3 mm. long and 0.7 m. wide, roulnded at apex, long-cuneate at base, marked on the back with a broad band of long subappressed villous hairs from about the middle down to about one-third its length from the base, otherwise glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 6, varying from more or less united at the base to completely separate, equal, about 1.9 mm. long.

description: Description: Staminate flowers: sepals 18, the outermost minute, the innermost largest, elliptic, keeled, about 1.9 mm. long and 1.2 mm. wide, acute at apex, densely appressed-puberulent outside with very short hairs, glabrous within; petals 6, elliptic, about 1.9 mm. long and 0.7 mm. wide, rounded at apex, not cuneate at base, densely appressed- puberulent throughout outside with very short hairs, glabrous within; stamens 6, of two sizes, separate, 3 about 1.4 mm. long and with slender filaments, the other 3 about 2 mm. long and with ampliate filaments.

description: Shrubs ca. 3 m tall, the stems densely pulverulent, the hairs stellate, ca. 0.3 mm long with more than 10 radii. Leaf blades mostly 5-16 cm long, 3-10 cm wide, ovate or weakly trilobulate, cordate, irregularly crenate-biserrate, acute to acuminate, palmately 5-9-nerved, markedly discolorous, the upper surface with scattered appressed simple, bifurcate, or stellate hairs (or the upper surface glabrate), densely stellate-pubescent on main veins, the lower surface stellate-tomentose (densely so when young); petioles 1/4-1/2 times length of blade, densely pulverulent. Inflorescences cymose, axil- lary, the peduncles densely pulverulent, shorter than or slightly surpassing the sub- tending petiole, shortly branched in cymes of 3-4 flowers; flowers sessile or subsessile, congested at the end of the branch or subtended by a floral bract, the bract ovate, 1.7- 2 mm long, 0.8 mm wide, early deciduous; calyx 7-9 mm long, open when fruiting, half or more divided, the lobes acute, costate, the apex massive, cuspidate, subcucullate when fruiting, the outer surface densely stellate-pubescent, the inner surface glabrous; corolla rotate, lavender to whitish, the petals ca. 1 cm long, with a barbate ring of simple hairs at the base of the staminal tube, the staminal column otherwise glabrous. Fruits oblate, umbonate, 4 mm long, enclosed in calyx, glabrous; mericarps ca. 12, 3 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, 1-1.5 mm thick, shortly apiculate, the dorsal wall apically concave; seeds solitary, ca. 2 mm long, glabrous.

description: Plant 1-3 m high, with slender branches; main cauline leaves 4-15 cm long, 2-6 cm wide, narrowed gradually to petioles up to about 1 cm long; racemes mostly 1-1.5 dm long; bracts of the inflorescence mostly 1-2 cm long, on petioles 1-3 mm long; pedicels 0.5-2 cm long; floral tube gradually ampliate above the narrow basal half, 1.5-2 cm long, 0.4-0.6 cm wide at summit in pressed speci- mens; sepals mostly 2.5-3 cm long, 1.5-2 mm wide at base; petals about 8-12 mm long, 1 mm wide; stamens and style 3-3.5 cm long; anthers about 4 mm long; capsule 5-7 min long; seeds about 1 mm long.

description: Stem woody, freely branched, 35 cm. high. Stipules subulate, brown, 4-6 mm. long, with 4-6 stiff cilia 1-3 mm. long on each side. Leaf-blades subcoriaceous, nearly or quite sessile, narrowly lanceolate, up to 25 mm. long and 3 mm. wide, sharply acute, long-cuneate at base, thickened at margin, remotely serrulate with low appressed teeth; veins numerous, crowded, aseending at an angle of about 20? from the midvein, giving the surface of the leaf a striate appearance. Racemes 2-3 cm. long, with mostly 3 or 4 1- or 2-flowered clusters from the axils of greatly reduced leaves; pedicels capillary, ascending, 2-6 mm. long. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, acute, 3.9-4.2 mm. long. Petals rhombicobovoid, 4.5 mm. long, 3.4 mm. wide, abruptly acute, freely veined. Exterior staminodes about 40, clavate-subulate, 1.3-1.7 mm. long, distinet to base. Interior staminodes oblong-spatulate, 3.2 mm. loing, 1.1 mm. wide, rounded and slightly retuse at apex. Ovary conic-ovoid, obscurely 3-lobed, 1.3 mm. high; style 2.4 mm. long; stigma punctiform.

description: Subshrub to 1 m tall. Branchlets (at 10 cm from apex) terete, 1-2 mm diam., glabrous. Leaves alternate; blades chartaceous, elliptic (8-)10.5-15(-20) X (3.5-)5-7.5 cm, apically acuminate, the acumen 6-16 mm long, basally acute, smooth and somewhat nitid above, prominently black punctate below, the midrib raised above and below, the secondary veins 15-22 pairs, the margin entire, flat; petioles deeply canaliculate, 6-10 mm long, glabrous. Staminate inflorescence lateral (axillary), corymbose, 8-10 mm long; peduncle obsolete to 2 mm long; inflorescence bract early caducous, coriaceous, oblate, 0.4-0.6 X 0.6-1 mm, apex broadly rounded, densely and prominently brown punctate and punctate-lineate, the margin entire, glandular-ciliolate; floral bracts membranaceous, linear-lanceolate, or linear, 1.2-1.4 X 0.3-0.4 mm, apically obtuse to rounded, often erose, densely and prominently brown punctate and punctate-lineate, the margins entire to erose, sparsely glandular-ciliolate; pedicels terete, 3-3.6 mm long, densely and conspicuously black punctate-lineate. Staminate flowers 4-mer- ous, membranaceous; calyx erect, 1.4-1.7 mm long, the tube ca. 0.2 mm long, the lobes ovate, 1.3-1.5 X 0.9-1.1 mm, api- cally obtuse to broadly rounded, medially thickened, densely and prominently red and brown punctate and punctate-lineate, the margin irregular, hyaline, somewhat erose apically, and extremely minute glandular- ciliolate apically; corolla campanulate, 2.6- 2.9 mm long, the tube 0.3-0.4 mm, the lobes elliptic to oblong, 2.3-2.6 X 0.9-1.1 mm, apically obtuse to rounded, asymmetric, prominently orange punctate-lineate abaxially, glabrous, the margin entire, glabrous; stamens 1.6-1.8 mm long, the filaments inserted basally on the corolla tube, 0.7-0.8 mm long, the anthers oblongoid to lanceoloid, 1-1.2 mm long, apex abruptly apiculate, basally cordate, subversatile (dorsifixed just below the middle), the connective conspicuously brown punctate along the edges; pistillode obnapiform, 0.5-0.7 mm long, the ovary 0.3-0.4 mm long, 0.3- 0.4 mm diam., hollow, the style 0.2-0.4 mm long, the stigma undeveloped. Bisexual inflorescence as in the staminate, but pistil 0.9-1.1 X 0.6-0.7 mm, the ovary 0.3-0.4 mm long, the style 0.3-0.4 mm long, the placenta subglobose, the ovules 2, apically exposed. Fruit globose, bright red when fresh, (3.5-)4-6(-8) mm diam. when dried, densely and prominently black punctate, longitudinally costate.

description: Plants low densely tufted herbaceous perennials, 0.3-2.5 x 0.5-4 dm, with a highly branched, woody caudex system arising from a deeply-seated taproot, each ultimate caudex branch typically terminated by a single flowering stem or a tuft of leaves. Leaves glabrous on adaxial surface, appressed pustulate-based bristles on abaxial surface; basal leaves tufted, narrowly oblanceolate to narrowly spatulate, 1-25(30) x 1.5-3 mm folded and V-shaped in cross section, persistent and drying brown with distinct, white-pustulate bases, tapering to a narrowly triangular petiole-base up to 0.5 cm long; cauline leaves scattered, oblanceolate to spatulate, 10-40 x 2-4(5) mm, slightly folded or flat- tened in cross section, epetiolate. Stems erect to suberect, up to 2.5 dm long, softly hairy, the longer, spreading hairs on elevated ridges of stem up to 2.5 mm long, the shorter, more or less appressed hairs in depressions between ridges of stem up to 1 mm long. Inflorescences subcapitate to a slightly elongated helicoid cyme at anthesis with lower flowers occasionally well below terminal cluster, not much more open in fruit, spreading-hairy throughout with bright, crystalline hairs; bracts conspicuous, flat, lanceolate to broadly lanceolate, up to 1 cm long and 4 mm wide, glabrous adaxially, with appressed, pustulate- based bristles abaxially, often obscuring calyx. Flowers heterostylous. Calyx turbinate; calyx-segments narrowly lanceolate, 4-6 mm long in anthesis, (4)6-9 mm long in fruit, sharply acute apically, rather bristly abaxially but without distinct pustulate-bases, glabrous adaxially. Corolla salverform, white with prominent, broad, more or less reniform (when observed from above), emarginate, yellow fornices, these about as high as thick and about twice as broad as high; corolla-tube light green to yellowish green, minutely rugose in long rows, 10-12 mm long, prominently exserted from the calyx, not crested at the base; corolla-limbs white, spreading, 8-12 x 8-12 mm, free portion reniform and thus broader than long, about a third of the fused portion nearest the fornices infused a light yellow at anthesis. Nutlets usually all 4 maturing, ovate, 2.2-2.6 x 1.5-1.9 mm, rugose-tuberculate on both surfaces except for a thin, smooth, rounded margin on outer edge of each nutlet; scar open with its somewhat elevated margins slightly constricted below middle; style surpassing the nutlet by 4-7 mm.

description: Stem arborescent, smooth, steel-greyish without any persistent armour of leaf bases, rarely branched, approximately 5 m tall, 19-61 cm diam. Leaves numerous, ascending or spreading, 1-2.5 m long with 100-120 pairs of pinnae. Petiole 50-90 cm long, spinous, the spines 0.9-3 mm long. Attachment of median pinnae at 50-55' to the rachis; pinnae linear-lanceolate, glabrous with prominent midrib on both surfaces, 26-35 x 0.8-1.2 cm, the margin entire, the cross section of pinnae at the extreme base showing 3 mucilage canals adjacent to the inner side of the bundle sheath on the abaxial surface, the number gradually reducing to two at the median level and to one near the tip region. New growth of foliage loosely tomentose. Microsporangiate cone sub-conical, yellowish orange, prior to dispersal of pollen grains 30-50 cm long, 15-21 cm in diameter; microsporophyll cuneiform with apex widely apiculate with prominent inflexed, upturned apical spine, 6.3-8.3 x 1.8-2.6 cm, the fertile zone length 2-3.2 cm, the sterile zone 3.8-4.7 cm long (including upturned apical spine). Megasporophylls 9-24.2 cm long, with ferruginous trichomes densely covering the megasporophylls when young and almost hiding the apical and lateral spines, mostly shedding before maturity of seeds, the sterile apex of megasporophylls triangular, apiculate, shield-like, 1.9-5.5 x 1.3-4.0 cm, with ca. 5-18 regular hard lateral spines on either side of the median spine, 0.05-0.8mm long, the apical spine distinct, 3-25 mm long. Ovules 2-10, glabrous; seeds globose, platyspermic, 3.8-4.9 x 3.5-4.3 cm. Sarcotesta green when young, becoming mango yellow at maturity, 3 mm thick; sclerotesta stony, the inner layer membranous, a fibrous layer absent; germination hypogeal and cryptocotylar.
bibliographicCitation: Singh, Rita & Radha, P. 2006. A New Species of Cycas from the Malabar Coast, Western Ghats, India. Brittonia. 58 (2): 119-123.

description: Herba volubilis pubescens, stipula 5-6 palmata aristata, 5-8 mm longa, membranacea asymmetrica. Petiolus 10-15 mm longus, trichomatibus hirsutis haud viscosis et 2 paribus glandularum stipitatarum. Folia integra simplicia. Bracteae verticillatae ellipticae laceratae 1.5-2 cm longae, trichomatibus instructae. Flores bini 4 cm diametro. Corona filamentis in seriebus duabus, in serie externa filamentis filiformibus, 13-15 mm longis, in serie interna 3 mm longis ad apicem clavatis. Operculum incurvatum 3 mm, ad partem tertiam inferiorem membranaceum atque ad partes duas tertias superiores filamentosum, filamentis ad apicem clavatis. Ovarium ellipticum glabrum.

description: Herbaceous and pubescent climber. Stem cylindrical. Stipules 5-6 palmate-aristate 5-8 mm long, membranous, asymmetric, glabrous. Petiole 10-15 mm long with simple trichomes, hirsute, not viscid and with 2 pairs of stipitate glands. Tendrils axillary, conspicuous. Leaves simple, entire, ovate, 4.7-10 x 2.5-3.5 cm, 3-nerved at the base, apex acute, mucronate; mucron ca. 4 mm long; trichomes simple, hirsute on both surfaces. Peduncles 10-15 mm long, pilose; trichomes simple, ca. 4 mm long, yellowish up to the insertion of the bracts, glabrous from the insertion of the bracts to the flower base; bracts 3, verticillate, 1.5-2 cm long, elliptic, lacerate, with trichomes, located ca. 5 mm from the floral base. Flowers in pairs, ca. 4 cm in diam., calyx tube short, campanulate, ca. 3 mm long, glabrous; sepals lanceolate 15 x 7-8 mm, membranous, with trichomes on the midvein; apex, obtuse; awn ca. 2 mm long pilose dorsally; petals the same size as the sepals, white, glabrous; corona filaments in 2 series; the outer filiform, white with lilac spots, 13-15 mm long; the inner ca. 3 mm long with a clavate apex; operculum curved, ca. 3 mm long, the lower 1/3 membranous and the upper 2/3 filamentous; apex of filaments clavate; limen 1.5-2 mm tall, weakly involving the androgynophore base; androg- ynophore 10-12 mm long, glabrous; ovary elliptic, glabrous. Fruit elliptic, ca. 2 x 1.7 cm, immature. Seeds not seen.

description: Folia in ambabus faciebus laete virentia, glabra, nitida, anguste elliptica vel elliptico-lanceolata, (3-)7-10(-15) cm longa, (1-)1.5-2(-3) cm lata, acuta, obtusa vel rotundata, ad basim cuneata, rotundata, raro obliqua, marginibus semper integris, venis secundariis inconspicuis, venulis obscuris, leniter evolutis. Fructus binatus, pedunculo 6-10 mm longo; cupula acetabuliformis, 4-7 mm longa, 10-20 mm diametro, marginibus tenuibus, squamis subtilibus, laevibus, arcte adpressis; nux late ovoidea oblonga, 17-22 mm longa, 10-15 mm lata, ad basim truncata.

description: Small evergreen tree, often 8-10(-15) m high, the trunk short, sometimes tortuous, 25-30 cm diam., the crown broad and spreading, the branchlets crooked; or shrubs, 2-3 m high in more exposed plac- es; bark light gray to brown and smooth when young, dark brown and longitudinally striate or grooved on old individuals. Branchlets 2-4(-5) mm diam., at first thinly stellate pubescent, soon glabrous, light brown to reddish brown and lustrous; lenticels many, tiny, pale; buds round-ovoid, small, 1-2 mm long, brown, the scales ciliate; stipules linear, membranous, scarious, 3-6(-6.5) mm long, the margin pilose, caducous; petioles 2-7 mm long, glabrous. Leaf blades subcoriaceous, flat, thin, light green, glossy, minutely papillose (40X) and glabrous on both surfaces, narrowly elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, rarely ± falcate, (3-)7-10(-15) X (1-)1.5-2(-3) cm; apex acute, less often obtuse or rounded, mucronate or sometimes with a short aristate tooth, the aristae 1-2 mm long; base cuneate, rounded, rarely oblique; margins always entire, slightly revolute and undulate; adaxial surface finely reticulate, the veinlets impressed; abaxial surface slightly paler, smooth, minutely papillose, the secondary veins and veinlets obscure, the midvein glabrous or with few acicular hairs; secondary veins numerous, about 10-20(- 25) on each side, weakly developed, generally widely divergent and straight. Staminate catkins 2.5-6 cm long, loosely flowered, the rachis scattery pubescent. Staminate flowers 20-30, sessile or pedi- cellate, the pedicel 2.3-3 mm long; perianth cup-shaped, 2 mm high, glabrous, the margin long-pilose; anthers 4, pale yellowish, 1.3-1.5 mm long, glabrous, the filaments 2 mm long. Pistillate-flowers 1- 3, on peduncles (1.5-)3-10 mm long, hairs present; hairs sparse, minute, pale, stellate. Fruits paired, short-stalked, the peduncle 6-10 mm long, 2-3 mm thick, with small and pale lenticels; cupule saucer-shaped or flat, 4-7 mm high, 10-20 mm wide, thin-margined, the triangular scales canescent, membranous, tightly adpressed and smooth, with obtuse tips and dense pilose margins; immature nut depressed-globose, 8-18 mm high, 12-17 mm thick; mature nut elongate-ovoid, 17-22 mm high, 10-15 mm thick, flattened at the base, light brown, thinly puberulent, with only the base included in the cupule. Distribution and ecology. Quercus cualensis occurs in the NW Sierra Madre del Sur, along the highest peaks of Sierra de Cuale, Mun. Talpa de Allende in western Jalisco at 1800-2300 m (Fig. 1). It occurs abundantly in the seasonally dry pine-oak forest throughout a large area approxi- mately 15 km along the gravel road be- tween the village of Cuale and the Minas Zimapain. The rather crooked, twisted trees grow mostly on steep rocky talus slopes, in acidic soils derived from the underlying granitic rocks. At lower elevations (1830 m), E of Cuale, Q. cualensis occurs in more protected sites in the pine-oak forest, where numerous seedlings are also found. More common and wide-spread species that grow with it include Pinus oocarpa Schiede, P. jaliscana Perez de la Rosa, Quercus elliptica Nee, Q. laeta Liebm., Q. scytophylla Liebm., Clethra rosei Britton, and Clethra vicentina Standl. At the highest elevation of its distribution, on the prominent peak El Caracol (2300 m), 1 km W of Minas Zimapan, Q. cualensis is associated with P. ayacahuite Ehrenberg ex Schlechtendal, P. douglasiana Martinez, P. lumholtzii B. L. Robinson & Fernald, Juniperus jaliscana Martinez, Quercus hypoleucoides A. Camus, Q. coccolobifolia Trel., Clethra rosei, Agarista villarrealana L. M. González, Arbutus xalapensis H.B.K., Befaria mexicana Benth., Comarostaphylis discolor (Hook.) Diggs subsp. discolor, Comarostaphylis glaucescens (H.B.K.) Zucc. ex Klotz., and Comarostaphylis lanata Small, Vaccinium confertum H.B.K., and Vaccinium stenophyllum Steud. In the vicinity of El Caracol, it occurs as shrubs or small trees, on hillsides and ridges, or in sunny open grasslands, where Muhlenbergia cualensis Herrera & P. Peterson and Dodonea viscosa Jacq. are common. This new species of oak might also occur on the many other high peaks in the same part of the Sierra, areas not yet explored botanically.

description: Frutex vel arbor, ramis junioribus pubescentibus quin glabrescentibus. Folia matura obovata vel elliptica, apice aristata, acuta vel apiculata interdum rotundata, basi cordata aliquando rotundata vel obliqua, margine sinuata dentibus aristatis versus dimidium dis- tale, interdum prope basim munita. Pagina adaxialis plerumque glabra vel parciter pubescens stellato-pilosa, pubescentia arachnoidea; pagina abaxialis parce pubescens vel floccosa. Fructus annuus, in extremitate pedunculi tenuis usque 25 mm longi portatus, cupula hemispherica interdum leviter turbinata, glande ovo- idea.

description: Shrubs 3-5 m or trees 4-15 m tall. First-season twigs 1.5-3.5 mm diam., pubescent, becoming glabrescent in the second season, with fasciculate trichomes, these sessile or shortly stipitate. Terminal buds 2-6 mm long, 1-2.5 mm diam., ovoid; bud scales ovate with ciliate margin. Stipules deciduous. Young leaves with the adaxial surface slightly reddish and with many stellate trichomes and scarce brownish uniseriate glandular trichomes; abaxial surface densely covered with nonglandular trichomes. Mature leaves subcoriaceous, obovate to elliptic, 2.8-12 X 1.6-7.2 cm; apex aristate, acute to apiculate, sometimes rounded; base cordate, occasionally rounded or oblique; margin wavy with 1-6(-10) aristate teeth located on the distal half of the leaf, sometimes near the base. Secondary veins 6-12, raised and conspicuous, straight or slightly curved, those of the distal half of the leaf terminating in an aristate tooth. Adaxial leaf surface mostly glabrous or sparingly pubescent with stellate nonglandular trichomes, the trichomes becoming denser along the midvein. Abaxial leaf surface sparingly pubescent to floccose, with glandular and non-glandular trichomes; nonglandular trichomes of fasciculate type with 8-12 spreading rays giving an arachnoid appearance; glandular trichomes uniseriate, red- dish, brown or amber, scarce; epidermis smooth, occasionally slightly bullate. Petiole 2.5-7(-10) x 1-2.5 mm, densely pubescent to glabrescent with sessile fasciculate nonglandular trichomes. Male catkins 2-8 cm long; rachis pubescent; male flowers with a cup-shaped perianth, sparingly pubescent, with 5 ciliate lobes; stamens 5- 7, 2.4-3.1 mm long, exserted; anthers 0.9-1.17 mm long, glabrous, with a short mucro at the apex. Female flowers with densely pubescent cup scales, solitary or in groups of 2-3; styles 1 mm long; stigma broadly spatulate. Fruit annual, at the end of a peduncle 4-25 mm long, 1-2 mm thick; fruits 1-3; cupule hemispheric, sometimes slightly turbinate, 7-12(-15) mm diam., 2.5-7(- 10) mm tall, the scales ovate and imbricate, sparingly pubescent or glabrescent with ciliate margin; acorn ovoid, 7-19 mm long, 3.4-13 mm diam. Cotyledons free with apical abortive ovules.

description: Folia lanceolata, anguste oblonga vel elliptica, 5- 15(-18) cm longa, 1-3(-4.5) cm lata, acuta vel acuminata saepe aristata, plerumque rotundata, ad basim abrupte rotundata vel subcordata interdum obliqua, marginibus integris, leviter revolutis et undulatis; pagina abaxialis pilis glandularibus, vermiformibus, sucineis, secus costam densioribus induta atque pilis fasciculatis pallidis, longe stipitatis, ex axillis venarum grandium ortis instructa, venis secundariis 15-20(-30), plerumque arcuatis, ascendentibus et prominentibus. Fructus singulus aut binatus, quasi sessilis. Cupula hemisphaerica vel subhemisphaerica, 6-12 mm alta, 12-16 mm diametro, squamis adpressis, umbonatis, nux ovoidea, juventute conica, 10-15 mm longa, 12- 20 mm lata.

description: Medium to large evergreen tree, 10-15(-25 or seldom more) m high; trunk 30-50 cm, rarely to 1 m diam.; bark at first grayish, thin and flaking, becoming dark and furrowed with age. Branchlets 2-4(-5) mm diam., when young minutely pale yellowish stellate-pubescent, finally glabrescent; lenticels inconspicuous; buds ovoid, 2-5 mm long, brown, the scales ciliate; stipules linear to linear-oblanceolate, membranaceous, scarious, 3-5(-9) mm long, the margin pilose, caducous; petioles (1-)4-8(-10) mm long, minutely stellate-pubescent, sometimes glabrescent, thick at base. Leaf blades subcoria- ceous, thin, firm, lanceolate, narrowly oblong or elliptic, 5-15(-18) X 1-3(-4.5) cm; apex acute to acuminate, the tip often aristate, the aristae 3-5 mm long, or apex sometimes mucronate, very rarely obtuse; base rounded to shallowly cordate, sometimes oblique; margins entire, slightly revolute and undulate; adaxial surface light green, lustrous, rarely pubescent, glabrous at maturity, the hairs minute, stellate, the midvein with a few acicular hairs, the secondary veins depressed, the veinlets forming a fine reticulum; abaxial surface slightly paler and yellower, sometimes reddish brown, with amber-colored vermiform glandular hairs denser along midvein and tufts of pale long-stipitate trichomes with tangled branches in the larger vein axils, the midvein prominent; secondary veins numerous, about 15-20(- 30) on each side, well-developed, generally arcuate-ascending or straight, prominent, usually branching before reaching the margins. Staminate catkins 4-6 cm long, loosely flowered, the rachis pubescent. Staminate flowers 30-35, sessile or pedicellate, the pedicel 0.5 mm long; perianth campanulate, 1.5-2 mm high, the margin long-pilose; anthers 4, rarely 5, sparingly pilose, 1-1.6 mm long, the filaments 2-2.5 mm long. Pistillate flowers 1-3, on peduncles 3-9 mm long, minutely stellate-pubescent, finally glabrous. Fruits paired or solitary, nearly sessile. the peduncle 2-3 mm long, 3 mm thick; cupule hemispheric or shallower. 6-12 mm high. 12-16 mm wide, the scales adpressed. yellowish-canescent, the tips narrowly triangular, umbonate-thickened at maturity, the margins ciliate; nut conic when young. ovoid at maturity, 12-20 mm high. 10-15 mm thick, rounded at the base, light brown, puberulent, with one-quarter to one-third included in the cup.

description: Folil cadlca, lucida, pallido-virldia. anguste vel late elilptica, lanceolata, oblanceolata, saepe rhombico-oblonga, raro obovata, spathulata vel ± falcata, (6-)8- 13(-15) cm longa, 2-4(-5.5) cm lalta, acuta, vulgo aristata. ad basim plerumque cuLneata, aliquantum rotundata, obliclua, saepe decurrentia, mnLrginibus integris et leviter revolutis; pagina abaxialis gflabra praeter pilorum stipitatorum caespites e pills stipitatis ramosis contortis imnplexis compositos ad axillas venarum positos, venis secundariis 7-12(-15) in quoque latere. Fructus parvi, bini vel fasciculati (2-4), pedunculo 5- 20 mm lonigo; cupula parva, tul-binata rostellata, 5-10 mm di.ametro, 5-8 mm long.a, squamisadpressis, canescentibus vel glabris, marginibus ciliatis; nux oblongo-ovoidea, 8-15 mm longa, 5-10 mm lata.

description: Small to moderate-sized deciduous tree, (3-)8-10(-15) m high; trunk 25-30(-60) cm diam., crooked on some small trees; bark roughly furrowed, hard, brown to dark brown. Branchlets 2-3 mm diam., flexible, fluted, glabrous, lustrous, light reddish brown; lenticels many, small, rather conspicuous, gray, 0.5 mm long, pruinose on aging; buds ovoid, acute, 2-7 mm long, reddish brown, the scales glabrous except for the ciliate margins; stipules oblanceolate or linear, membranous, scarious, 7-13 mm long, 1-2.8 mm wide, the margins densely tomentose especially at apex, the hairs whitish, to I mm long, caducous. Petiole flattened adaxially, grooved, (5-)10-15(- 20) mm long, often pruinose. Leaf blades subcoriaceous, shiny light green, narrowly to broadly elliptic, lanceolate, oblanceolate, often rhombic-oblong, rarely obovate or oblong or rather oblong-spathulate, or ± falcate, (6-)8-13(-15) X 2-4(-5.5) cm; apex acute, commonly tapering to the aristate tip (aristae 2-3 mm long); base cuneate often decurrent, rounded or oblique; margins entire and slightly revolute; adaxial surface glabrous, glossy, flat or slightly planoconvex, the secondary veins inconspicuous, the veinlets forming a fine network; abaxial surface glabrous except for tufts of stipitate trichomes with contorted and tangled branches in the larger vein axils, the mid-vein prominent, the veinlets fine and reticulate, sometimes the epidermis pruinose; secondary veins 7-12(-15) on each surface, irregularly forked and anastomosing, commonly straight and parallel or somewhat arcuate-ascending with few or no intermediate veins. Staminilate catkins (1.5-)6-10 cm long, loosely flowered, the rachis slender, glabrous or sparsely villous. Staminate flowers 34-45, sessile, the perianth cup-shaped, 1.8 mm high, glabrous, the margin with long silky hairs; anthers 5-6, rarely 9, 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous, filaments 1.5-2 mm long. Fruits commonly paired or in clusters of 2-4, on slender peduncles 5-20 mm long, 1.5-2 mm thick; cupule somewhat turbinate, 5-8 mm high, 5-10 mm wide, the scales adpressed, woody, umbo glabrous with age, shiny, reddish brown, with ciliate margins; nut elongate-ovoid, 8- 15 mm high, 5-10 mm thick, light brown, pubescent, with one-third of the nut includ- ed in the cupule.

description: Plants geophytic vines to 2 m, frequently shorter; tubers napiform to 10 cm in diam.; stems annual, glabrous; sterile tendrils simple, 4-10 cm; internodes 1-5 cm. Leaves membra- nous, not punctate, mottled red and green; petiole 3-4.5 cm; lamina broadly cordate in outline, base cordate, apex acute, occasionally mucronate, 4-12 x 4-16 cm, 5-plinerved from base, margin entire, slightly revolute, deeply 5-lobed, lobes with lobules, veins red, mostly indistinct to raised. Gland(s) at base of blade at junction with summit of petiole 1-2, on 2 separate, adaxially-upturned appendages, 0.5-2 x ca. 1 mm, or when solitary, from fusion of glands and appendages; laminar glands abaxial, 5-14, 0.4-1 mm diam., at nexus of lobes. Stipules persistent and soft, linear, ca. 0.25 x 0.6 mm. Inflorescences ten-drillate, 6-7cm long including a ca. 3 cm simple axial tendril at apex of inflorescence, 1-2 flowered; bracts and bracteoles narrowly triangular, bases rarely lobed, apices acuminate, dentate-incised near apices, 1-2.2 x ca. 0.3 mm. Male flowers white to cream with some green, urceolate, 1.3-3.0 x 1-2 cm; pedicel 4-7mm long; stipe (fused tissue above pedicel, below hypanthium) ca. 2.5 mm long; hypanthium saucer-shaped, 5-saccate, 2-3.5 mm high at petal insertion, 6-15mm diam.; calyx tube urceolate, 10-11.5 mm long, sepal lobes broadly subulate, apices asymmetric-truncate to acuminate, ca. 5.5 x 3.5 mm, lobe margins entire to fimbriate; petals subulate-lanceolate, apices 8.5-9.0 x 1.5-2.0 mm, 3-nerved from base, green, margin unevenly fimbriate; filaments 4.2-4.7 mm including ca. 1 mm connation at their bases, inserted near base of hypanthium up to 0.6mm from base; anthers oblong, apices acute to obtuse, bases cordate, 7-8.6 x 0.7-1.8mm; septa appearing from connation of staminal filaments, ca. 2.4mm long x 1 mm deep; corona consisting of ring of lanate, occasionally branching hairs, extending from top of septa to point of petal insertion, hairs 1-3 mm long; disk glands 5, ca. 1.4 x 1.2 mm, inserted ca. 2.5 mm from base of hypanthium, alternating with petals; vestigial ovary, including 0.3 mm gynophore, 1.2 x 0.5 mm. Female flowers (inferred from base of immature fruit [R. Gereau et al. 2717 (MO)]) white to cream with some green, urceolate to campanulate; pedicel 4.7 mm long; hypanthium saucer-shaped, ca. 2.6 mm high; calyx tube urceolate ca. 6.5 mm long, sepal lobes oblong, apices acute to acuminate, ca. 7.75 mm, margins entire; petals linear to narrowly lanceolate, apices acuminate, ca. 7.25 mm long, 1-veined from base, margins entire; staminodes ca. 3.6 x 0.75 mm, connate in ring ca. 0.2 mm high; septa absent or re- duced to ridges ca. 0.1 mm high extending from staminode tube; corona as in male flower; disk glands as in male flower, sometimes contiguous. Fruits 1-2 per inflorescence, ellipsoid, red at maturity, including 1-2.5 cm gynophore, 5-8 x 2-3.5 cm; pericarp smooth, ca. 1 mm thick, 35-65 seeds per fruit. Seeds cordate to reniform, 5-5.5 x 6-6.5 mm, 6-8 pits along length of seed; funicle of mature seed ca. 4 mm long.

description: Plants pachycauls, glabrous; tubers in juveniles slightly enlarged or fleshy roots, in adults, stem tapering into fleshy root stock; trunk thickened, slowly-tapering cone, up to 30 cm in diam. at base, up to 2 m tall; stems emerging from trunk thin, vining, annual; sterile tendrils simple, ca. 4 cm long; internodes 5-9 cm. Leaves highly variable, sub- succulent, shiny, mottled whitish-green when immature, uniformly green when mature, not punctate, glabrous; petiole 5-10 cm; lamina broadly cordate to orbicular in broad outline, base cordate, apex acute, 5-15 x4-8 cm, margin entire, revolute, reticulation fine, juvenile leaves deeply lobed, sometimes laciniate or unlobed to 2-5 lobed, mature leaves (2-) 3-5 lobed, with 2-4 paired lobules at base of central lobe, (3-) 5-plinerved from base. Glands at base of blade and summit of petiole 2, 2-3 mm in diam. on adaxially up-turned, knobby projections; laminar glands 0 (juvenile)-10, 0.2-2mm in diam., at nexus between lobes. Stipules persistent, blackening and hardening with age, narrowly triangular, occasionally lobed at base, 0.5-1.5 x ca. 0.2 mm. Female inflorescences on old wood, clustered on short shoots to 7 mm long, 2-3 flowered; male inflorescences unknown; bracts and bracteoles subulate, expanding slightly near midpoint, apices incised, 1-3 x ca. 0.5 mm. Male flowers not known. Female flowers dark green to cream, campanulate-infundibuliform, 8-13 x ca. 5 mm, flowers sessile to subsessile; stipe ca. 2 mm; hypanthium cup shaped, 1.75-2.5 mm; calyx tube campanulate, 0.25-0.95 mm, sepal lobes subulate, apices truncate to acute, margin entire, 4-6 mm; petals lanceolate, apices acuminate, upper third occasionally laciniate to undulate, 3-4 mm, 1 or 3-nerved from base; staminodes ca. 0.7 x 0.3-0.4 mm, fused at base to 0.25 mm; septa from fusion of staminodes 0.15 mm tall (occasionally absent); corona absent or sparse papillate projections 0.1 mm tall; disk glands 0 or 0.25 mm; ovary oblong to narrowly obovate, not ribbed or weakly 3-ribbed, including 1.4-2 mm gynophore, 4.5-7 mm; styles 3-partite; stigmas globular, sessile or on styles 0.3 mm long. Fruits solitary on inflorescence, ovoid-narrowly ellipsoid, including ca. 10mm gynophore, 4-6 x 1.2-2.5 cm; pericarp smooth, internally with ridges, 0.4-0.7 mm thick; 10 seeds or more per fruit based on placental scars.

description: Plants glabrous, juveniles geophytic for several years, adults thin-stemmed pachycauls; tuber smooth and occasionally fissured, subterranean (or partially exposed), napiform, to 30 cm in diam.; trunk cylindrical, up to 2 m tall, less than 5 cm in diam.; stems emerging from trunk annual, thin, climbing to 10m; sterile tendrils simple, 7-13 cm long; internodes 3-15 cm. Leaves membranous, mottled white and green as juveniles, uniformly green as adults, adaxial punctations, when present, small, black, and numerous; petiole 2-4 cm long; lamina of mature leaf cordate to deltoid, base cordate to truncate, apex acute, 4-12 x 3-8 cm, margin entire, recurved, unlobed or (2-) 3-lobed, 5-7 plinerved from base, reticulation fine, slightly raised on abaxial surface, juvenile leaves deeply 5-lobed with lobules laciniate. Glands at base of blade and summit of peti- ole 2, on adaxially-upturned warty projections in mature leaves, ca. 2 mm in diam.; laminar glands 0-12 or more in juvenile leaves, 0.3-0.8 mm, occasionally marginal, usually at nexus between lobes. Stipules persistent, blackening and hardening with age, triangular, ca. 0.25 x 0.5 mm. Inflorescences tendrillate, 5-25 mm, 1-3 flowered, inflores- cence tendrils simple, 1-3 cm long; bracts and bracteoles triangular, apices acuminate, occasionally incised, 0.4 x 1 mm. Male flowers unknown. Female flowers (inferred from base of immature fruit) infundibuliform, ca. 9 mm long; pedicel ca. 1.5 mm; stipe 1.5 mm; hypanthium cup-shaped, ca. 3.1 mm deep; calyx tube absent; sepals narrowly triangular, apices acute to acuminate, ca. 7.3 x 1.5 mm, margins entire; petals narrowly oblong to narrowly lanceolate, apices acute, ca. 4.3 × 0.6 mm at broadest, 1-nerved from base, margins entire; staminodes ca. 1.75 mm tall, connate at base ca. 0.6 mm, inserted at base of hypanthium; septa apparently lacking; corona consisting of ring at level of insertion of petals of occasionally branched triangular appendages, ca. 0.15 mm long; disk glands apparently absent. Fruits (described from slightly immature fruit) solitary, fusiform to elongate ellipsoid, including 5-8mm gynophore, ca. 8 x 2 cm; pericarp coriaceous, smooth to weakly reticulate, 0.5-1 mm thick; 20-30 seeds. Seeds ovate, 5-7 x 4-5.5 x 2.5-3.5 mm; testa verrucate with 40-70 raised verrucae, each ca. 0.5 mm tall; funicle of mature seed ca. 2.2 mm long.

description: Arbores 6-10 m altae, laminis foliorum ovatis obscure crenato-dentatis acutis vel obtusis usque 5 x 4.5 cm discoloribus, stipulis obscuris; flores in fasciculis axillaribus, pedicellis in quaque axilla 2-15 ferrugineotomentulosis, involucello nullo, calyce quum in alabastro 5-angulari 5-6 mm longo ad basem ferrugineo, petalis 6-8 mm longis flavidis, ungue biauriculato (auriculis obscure pubescentibus); fructus oblati 5-angulares ferrugineo-pubescentes; semina solitaria subglabra.

description: Trees 6-10 m tall, the young stems minutely stellate-pubescent, the hairs farinose, whitish to ferruginous, the older stems becoming more or less glabrescent. Leaf blades broadly ovate, cordate, 3-5 x 2.5-4.5 cm, the margins sometimes undulate (when dry), obscurely crenate dentate, the veins terminating at the margin with a minute protruberance, acute to obtuse at apex, discolorous (whitish and densely tomentulose beneath, greenish above), palmately 7-nerved; petioles 1-2 cm long, with pubescence like stem; stipules obscure (vestigial or early caducous?). Flowers in axillary fascicles in uppermost leaf axils, 2-15 flowers per fascicle; pedicels 2-2.5 cm long, densely tomentulose, whitish to ferruginous; involucel absent; calyx 5-6 mm long, half or more divided, the lobes 5, more or less 5-angled in bud, densely tomentulose, ferruginous basally; petals pale yellow (fading purplish?), drying brownish, 6-8 x 4 mm, with the margins of the claw stellate-pubescent, otherwise glabrous, the base of the claw biauriculate, the auriculae minute to obsolete, pubescent (best observed in an abscised corolla from the abaxial side); staminal column ca. 5 mm long, yellowish, stellate-pubescent, the stamens borne distally, the filaments 1-2 mm long, the anthers ca. 1 mm, bright yellow; styles 5, slender, glabrous, exceeding the androecium, the stigmas capitate, more or less dark-pigmented. Fruits ferruginous-pubescent, oblate to more or less pentangular, the stylar remnant forming a beak, the fruit body 5-6mm diam., 3-4mm long; mericarps 5, trigonal in cross- section, ferruginous-pubescent on both the lateral and dorsal walls, somewhat winged or ridged along the juncture of the dorsal and lateral walls, the dorsal wall rounded between the wings; seeds [immature] one per mericarp, 2-2.5 mm long, subglabrous, blackish.
