description: Small tree 5-10 m tall, young branches puberulent with appressed brownish hairs, later glabrescent. Leaves alternate, distichous, petioles 1.5-2.2 cm long, with hairs similar to the young twigs, canaliculate along the length of upper side; lamina oblong-elliptic, 15- 25 x7-9 cm, broadest in the middle, chartaceous, base obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, with scattered appressed hairs on both surfaces, 3-veined from the base, these primary veins impressed on the upper surface of the lamina and elevated on the lower surface, densely covered with appressed hairs, secondary veins external to the two lateral veins weakly elevated on the lower surface of the lamina, plane on the upper surface, secondary veins emerging from the central vein slightly elevated on both sides; groups of tufted hairs (acarodomatia) present at the junction of the secondary veins and the central vein on the lower surface and at the junction of the two lateral veins with the external secondary veins; junction of the lamina and petiole with two conspicuous, embedded lateral nectaries, each in the form of an elliptical swollen ring. Inflorescence mainly axillary, shortly pedunculate (to 1 cm long in flower, to 4 cm long in fruit), 3.7-10 x 3.2-8.5 cm, many-flowered cymes, these 1-4(-more) times dichotomous, axes densely covered with appressed brownish hairs similar to the leaves and young twigs; pedicels 2-3 mm long at anthesis, to 1.5 cm long in fruit. Flowers cream-colored to greenish-yellow; calyx tube shortly turbinate, 5-lobed; petals 5, inserted on the margin of the disk, cucullate at apex, unguiculate below, 2- 2.5 mm long; stamens 5, opposite the petals, filaments 1.5-2.5 mm long, anthers basifixed, 0.2-0.4 mm long; ovary semi-inferior, 3- carpellate, with a thick nectariferous annular disk on the upper surface, ovules one per locule; style squat, ca. 0.5 mm long and wide, with an apical trifid stigma. Fruit a distinctly trilobed capsule, 2.5-2.8 cm diam when mature, 1.8-2 cm long, nonstipitate above the torus base, the calyx lobes deciduous; exocarp dry and endocarp hard at maturity, explosively dehiscent when mature. Seeds one per locule.

description: Tree or shrub 2-5 m tall, bark yellowish grey, exfoliating, corky on some parts of the trunk and principal branches; young stems sericeous, glandular-setose. Leaves bipinnate (5.7-)10-22.5 cm long; stipules ovate, 3.2- 6 x 1.3-2.2 mm, apex acute, margin glandular-ciliate, sericeous, caducous, petiole (1.8-)3.4-9.8 cm, sericeous-pilose, glandular- setose; rachis 2.5-14 cm long; pinnae in (3-) 7-11(-13) opposite pairs, (1.5-)3.4(-6.5) cm long; leaflets in (3-)4-6 opposite pairs, 1-2(- 2.4) x 0.5-1(-1.2) cm, elliptic, pilose-sericeous; venation obscure, secondary veins brochidodromous, margin with punctate glands. Inflorescence an erect or ascending, terminal or axillarly raceme, sometimes with 1-2 secondary racemes near the base, 30- 47 cm long; bracts caducous, ovate, (2.4-) 4.5-5 x (1-)1.8-2.3 mm, red, apex acuminate, hispidulous, margin glandular-ciliate; pedicels slender (9-)10-17 mm long, diameter 0.5 mm or less, articulated just below the calyx tube, hispidulous, red stipitate-glandular; calyx pink-orange, adaxial lobes ovate, 7-9 x 3.5-4.5 mm, apex acute, lateral lobes 7-9.5 x 5.2-6.5 mm, apex acute; abaxial lobe ovate, 7.5-9 x 4.6-5.5 mm, apex acute, concave, all lobes stipitate-glandular. Corolla pale red (yellow on herbarium specimens); petals clawed, the upper (adaxial) petal (standard) and upper lateral petals strongly reflexed; adaxial petal ovate, 8- 8.7 x 4.4-5.3 mm, with a red blotch at the base, cordate, apex acute, margin entire, claw 1.5-2 mm long, pilose, glandular-ciliate, outer surface with a pair of fleshy pilose appendages on the articulation; upper lateral petals ovate, 6.5-8 x 5.2-6.5 mm, base rounded, margin entire, glandular-ciliate along the basal 1/3, apex obtuse, claw 1.2-1.5 mm long, pilose, outer surface stipitate-glandular; lower lateral petals ovate, 7.2- 8.5 x 4.3-5.5 mm, margin entire, glandular- ciliate at the base, apex obtuse, claw 1-2 mm long, pilose, glandular-ciliate, glandular-stipitate on the abaxial surface; stamen filaments curved, 8.5-11 mm long, villous on the basal half, glabrous with lemon-green colored stipitate glands along the upper half; anthers oblong-ovate, 1.6-2 x 1-1.3 mm, brown; pollen harmomegathic, wet; ovary sessile, 2.5-3 mm long, densely sericeous, with red cup-shaped stipitate glands intermixed with the indumentum, style curved, (5.5-)8-10 mm long, adpressed-pilose along the basal 1/4; stigma terminal, fringed, concave; ovules 2(-3). Fruit falcate, (3.7-)4.5-5.5 x 1.2-1.7 cm, valves chartaceous, wine-red to purple when young, later yellowish, pilose, with or without red cup-shaped stipitate glands intermixed, elastically dehiscent. Seeds widely obovate, laterally compressed, 9-11 mm long x 7-10 mm length x 1.7-2.5 mm wide, apex rounded, almost truncate, base acute, light brown, 1-2(-3) per fruit. Seedling germination phaneroepigeal, cotyledons foliaceous, base cordate, apex rounded, first and second eophyll with three pinnae, internodes short, epicotyl and leaves with black stipitate glands.

description: Shrub or small tree, to 4 m tall, 10 cm dbh. Leaves 3-9 x 2-8 cm, broadly cordate, dark green above, greenish white and densely stellate beneath. Flowers in short racemes, actinomorphic, lemon-yellow; stamens 6-8. Fruits ca. 1 cm in diameter, round, baccate-like, with 2-6 seeds within a white sarcotesta "package" surrounded by a thin, flexible fruit wall that at maturity often cleanly dehisces from the fleshy interior by first separating itself basally from the short gynophore and then splitting along the fibrous repla strands into usually 4, thin, apically-united valves that fall soon afterwards to the ground as star-like units connected by the stigma, leaving the seed package (the stuck-together, sarcotesta-covered seeds) attached to the gynophore.

description: Shrub or small tree, to 5 m, densely stellate. Leaves deltoid-orbicular, often wider than long, 2-5 x 2.5-7 (-9) cm. Flowers in short racemes, relatively large, orange-yellow, showy stamens (3-) 5-7 fertile and 1-5 staminodal. Fruits dehiscent, densely stellate yellow berries 1-3 cm in diam on pedicels and gynophores 2-3 cm long; seeds 3-8 (-12), cochleate reniform, 6-8 mm long with the coriaceous testa covered by a white to yellowish sarcotesta (pulp!) infiltrated by many slender, unicellular unbranched hairs from the testa (Fig. 1), at maturity more or less stuck together as a "seed package" that cleanly separates itself from the 2-4 flexible and leathery fruit coat segments and falls to the ground as a unit; embryo snow white.

description: A scandent or leaning shrub or liana clambering over thickets, its unique life form betrayed by the whip-like thin ends of its primary branches and by its many retrorse, grapple-hook-like, secondary spur branches, these short, stiff and sharply pointed, all adaptations for scrambling over and holding fast to vegetation (Fig. 2A); stems and leaves densely stellate-tomentose throughout, at least when young, though the ovate to subcordate, thickly coriaceous and evergreen leaves soon glabrous and bright green above and, on drying, becoming sharply rolled inward to fracture all too easily in herbarium material; young branches also soon becoming glabrous, smooth and bright green. Flowers apparently solitary in the axils of leaves, a conjecture based on a single quite immature and 2 mm-long flower bud, with four equal, apparently 1-seriate, linear-lanceolate sepals enclosing the corolla bud. Fruit baccate, ovoid, much larger (5-6 cm long) than that of its putative relatives, with about 20-25 cochleate-reniform seeds within a flexible, rather thick and indehiscent(?) fruit wall. Seeds covered with a hair-infiltrated, pulpderived sarcotesta.

description: Folia ovata. Flores vulgo singulares, (4-)5 meri. Bracteae 14-15. Caylx per bracteolas apicalis usque ad apicem (98-110%) velatus; aestivatio imbricata; lobi ovati; sinu ob margines loborum imbricatorim clauso. description: Terrestrial shrubs, scandent or erect, 0.5-1.5 m tall. Young branchlets reddish, relatively smooth, densely villous with hairs simple, eglandular and golden brown, the mature branches similar but glabrate. Leaves 2-3 per centimeter, spiral; petiole 2.8-4.0 mm long, villous with eglandular hairs; lamina coriaceous, ovate, 1.8-2.8x 1.1-1.8 cm, basally obtuse or cuneate, marginally entire, not revolute in dry specimens, ciliolate at apex with simple, eglandular hairs, apically acuminate, adaxially glabrate with simple, eglandular hairs, abaxially glabrate with multicellular, glandular hairs, venation 5- plinerved showing on both sides, impressed adaxially and raised abaxially. Flowers solitary or rarely in 2-flowered fascicles; bracts green, 14-15, persistent, chartaceous, ovate, elliptic, or suborbicular, 0.7-6.3 x 1.4-6 mm, marginally eciliate, apically obtuse and often splitting, abaxially and adaxially glabrous; pedicel 0.8-2.4 mm long, much reduced and obscured by overlapping bracts and bracteoles, glabrate with hairs simple and egland- ular, or multicellular and glandular, with a ring of hairs at its articulation with calyx; apical bracteoles green, 2, distinct, chartaceous, enveloping calyx up to the upper half of the calyx lobes or the entire calyx (covering 98-100% of calyx), suborbicular, transverse-elliptic, or reniform, 6.3-6.5 x 6.3- 7.4 mm, marginally eciliate, apically obtuse, surface smooth, abaxially and adaxially glabrous. Flowers 5-merous (rarely 4-merous). Calyx green, campanulate, 5.6-6.5 mm long, aestivation imbricate; tube terete, 2-2.5 mm long, glabrate with eglandular hairs; limb 4.0-4.7 mm long, abaxially glabrate with eglandular hairs; lobes ovate, 2.8-3.2 x 2- 3.1 mm, about or as long as broad, marginally entire and eciliate, apically acute, surface striate in dry; sinuses obscured by the over lapping bases of the imbricate lobes. Corolla aestivation valvate, actinomorphic, pink with darker lobes, thick-fleshy, urceolate (distally inflated), 7.1-8 mm long, 4.4 mm diam. (3.5 mm when dry), 3 mm wide at throat (2.2-3.2 mm when dry), abaxially and adaxially glabrate with simple, eglandular hairs; lobes triangular, 1.2 x 1.2-1.6 mm, marginally entire, apically acute. Stamens 10(-12), ad- herent to corolla, 5.9-6.3 mm long, more than 2/3 or about as long as corolla, included; filaments connate into a tube, straight, 3- 3.3 mm long, abaxially glabrate with few hairs, adaxially pubescent distally, all hairs simple and eglandular; anthers distinct; thecae 1.5-1.7 mm long, papillate, without basal appendage, with abaxial small and flat spurs (flap-like) attached to the connate filaments at their base and to the connective and thecae through their inner side; tubules 2, distinct, 2- 2.2 mm long, smooth, dehiscing by longitudinal slits, 0.8-1 mm long. Style included, ca. 6.7 mm long, smooth. Nectary glabrous. Ovary 5-locular. Berry color unknown, with the persis- tent calyx lobes converging into a obconic structure; seeds more or less triangular, 1 x 0.7- 0.8 mm, viviparous; embryo color not seen.

description: Terrestrial shrubs, scandent or erect, up to 1.3-1.5 m tall. Young branchlets relatively smooth, generally glabrous or glabrate with hairs inconspicuous, simple, eglandular, and white, the mature branches similar. Leaves 1- 2(-3) per centimeter, spiral but sometimes appearing secund; petiole 3-5 mm long, glabrous or glabrate with simple, eglandualar hairs; lamina coriaceous, obovate, or elliptic, (1.6-)2.2-4.5 x (0.9-)1.3-2.7 cm, basally at- tenuate, marginally entire, sometimes slightly revolute in dry specimens, ciliolate at apex with simple, eglandular hairs, apically obtuse and apiculate, adaxially and abaxially gla- brate with hairs simple and eglandular or multicellular and glandular, venation 3- or 5- plinerved on both sides, impressed adaxially and raised abaxially. Inflorescences in 2-11 flowered fascicles or flowers appearing solitary due to asynchrony of floral bud development; bracts green, 2-3, persistent, chartaceous, ovate, 0.5-1.7x0.5-2.5 mm, marginally eciliate, apically obtuse, abaxially and adaxially glabrous; pedicel 0.5-1.5 mm long, much reduced and obscured by the overlapping bracts and bracteoles, glabrous, without a ring of hairs at its articulation with calyx; apical bracteoles green, two, distinct, coriaceous, enveloping calyx up to the base or the entire calyx tube [covering 39-50(-85)% of calyx], suborbicular, transverse-elliptic, or reniform, 2.2-3.2 x 3.7-4 mm, sometimes marginally ciliolate with minute simple, eglandular hairs, apically obtuse, surface smooth, abaxially and adaxially glabrous. Flowers 5- merous (although some calyces are 4- or 6- lobed). Calyx green, cylindric, 3.3-4 mm long, aestivation valvate; tube terete, 2- 2.1 mm long, glabrous; limb 1.4-2.1 mm long, abaxially glabrous; lobes triangular, 0.3- 0.5 x 0.5-1 mm, broader than longer, margin- ally entire and eciliate, apically acute, surface smooth; sinuses rounded (U-shaped). Corolla aestivation valvate, actinomorphic, pale pink or white, very thick-fleshy, urceolate, 5.2- 6.4 mm long, 2.6-3.5 mm diam. (2-2.6 mm when dry), 1.8-2.2 mm wide at throat (1.5- 1.8 mm when dry), abaxially glabrate with hairs minute, multicellular, and glandular, adaxially puberulous even in the lobes, with simple, eglandular hairs; lobes triangular, 0.8- 1 x 0.7-1 mm, marginally entire, apically acute. Stamens ten, adherent to corolla, 4- 4.7 mm long, more than 2/3 or about as long as corolla, included; filaments distinct, straight, linear, 3.4-4 mm long, abaxially glabrous, adaxially pubescent distally with simple hairs; anthers distinct; thecae 1.5- 1.7 mm long, basally papillate, with basal appendages; tubules 2, distinct, 0.3-0.5 mm long, very reduced and hard to differentiate from thecae, smooth, dehiscing by a cleft that extends almost to base of thecae, 1.4-1.5 mm long. Style included, 4.5-5 mm long, micro- papillose. Nectary glabrous. Ovary 5-locular. Berry translucent white, the persistent calyx lobes erect or spreading, becoming succulent and the color of the mature berry; seeds elliptic, 1.4 x 0.6 mm, with a mucilaginous coat; embryo color not seen.

description: Terrestrial shrubs, scandent or erect, 0.5-1.5 m tall. Young branchlets with papilliform outgrowths, puberulous with hairs simple, eglandular, and brown, mature branches similar or sometimes glabrate. Leaves one to three per centimeter, spiral, rarely appearing distichous, diffuse; petiole 2.8-3.2 mm long, puberulous with simple, eglandular hairs; lamina coriaceous, ovate or elliptic, 1.6-5 x 0.9-2.8 cm, basally cuneate, marginally entire, sometimes slightly revolute in dry specimens, ciliolate at apex with simple, eglandular hairs, apically acuminate or cuspidate, somewhat glaucescent underneath when fresh, adaxially glabrate with simple, eglandular hairs, abaxially glabrate with minute, multicellular, glandular hairs, venation adaxially seven plinerved and impressed, abaxially only the midvein prominent. Inflorescences in two to four flowered fascicles or appearing solitary due to asynchrony of floral bud development; bracts brown (even in floral buds), 4-5, persistent, scarious, ovate, obovate or suborbicular (some asymmetrical), 1.5-5 x 1.5-4.6 mm, marginally ciliolate with simple, eglandular hairs, apically obtuse, abaxially glabrate with simple, eglandular hairs especially distally, adaxially glabrous; pedicel 0.5-1 mm long, much reduced and obscured by overlapping bracts and bracteoles, glabrous, without a ring of hairs at its articulation with calyx; apical bracteoles brown, 2, distinct, scarious, enveloping 100% of the calyx and extending 2.5-3.8 mm beyond it, elliptic or suborbicular (some asymmetrical), (4-)5-6.7 x (3-)4-6 mm, marginally ciliolate with eglandular hairs, apically obtuse and usually splitting surfae slightly pustulate, abaxially glabrate with simple, eglandular hairs, adaxially glabrate with minute simple, eglandular hairs distally. Flowers 5- merous. Calyx green, cylindric (rarel drying campulate), 2.2 -3 mm long, aestivation valvate; tube terete, (1.1-) 1.3 - 2mm long, glabrous; limb 0.9 -1.1 mm long, abaxially puberulous at apex of lobed with simple, eglandular hairs; lobes triangular, 0.3- 0.7x0.3-0.7 mm, about or as long as broad, marginally entire and eciliate, apically acute, surface smooth; sinuses rounded (U-shaped). Corolla aestivation valvate, actinomorphic or sometimes slightly zygomorphic with a couple of lobes larger than others, pale pink or white, thin-fleshy, tubular, 7.1-9.1 mm long, 2.4- 6.1 mm diam. (2-2.5 mm when dry), 2.3- 6.6 mm wide at throat (1.5-2 mm when dry), abaxially glabrate with simple, eglandular hairs, adaxially glabrous; lobes triangular, 1.2-1.8x0.8-1.9 mm, marginally entire, api- cally acute. Stamens 10, adherent to corolla, 5- 5.9 mm long, 2/3 to about as long as corolla, included; filaments distinct, straight, long-triangular, 3.8-4.2 mm long, abaxially glabrate, adaxially puberulous distally, all hairs simple and eglandular; anthers distinct; thecae 1.3- 1.7 mm long, papillate, without basal appendages; tubules 2, distinct, 1.1-1.5 mm long, smooth, dehiscing by longitudinal slits almost reaching the base of tubules, 0.8-1.1 mm long. Style included, ca. 6.8 mm long, smooth. Nectary glabrous. Ovary 5-locular. Berry translucent white, more or less spherical, 7 mm diam. (mature?), the persistent calyx lobes erect or spreading, becoming succulent and the color of the mature berry; seeds more or less triangular, 1-1.2 x 0.5-0.6 mm, with a mucilaginous coat; embryo white.

description: Tree 8-25(-35) m tall; branchlets with sparse, minute trichomes then pale gray to brown striate, with many pale, Leaves alternate to occasionally usually crowded at tips foliolate; petiole semiterete, cm long, expanded at base, conspicuous dark glands, trichomes near apex, mostly glabrescent; leaflets subsessile or petiolulate, the petiolule 5-10(-30) mm long, not sharply separated from base of blade; blade elliptic, widely elliptic, or sometimes obovate, (13-)14-20 (-28) × 8-12(-15) cm and symmetrical when terminal, 8-12(-15) × 3.5-5(-7) cm and asymmetrical when lateral, acute, attenuate, or obtuse at the base, short- to long-acuminate at the apex, with an obtuse acumen, 5-23 x 2-3 mm, flat to slightly revolute at margin, chartaceous, pellucid-punctate, the glands visible as dark dots on both surfaces, the adaxial surface light-green, lustrous, glabrous, the abaxial surface concolorous, dull, glabrous or with very sparse, minute trichomes near the base; venation eucamptodromous basally to brochidodromous distally, the midvein very prominent on both surfaces, the secondary veins 6-9 on each side of midvein, ascendent, arching, prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence terminal, erect, a narrow thyrsoid, shorter than surrounding leaves, 12-17 cm long including the peduncle, this 2-7cm long, glabrous, conspicuously gland-dotted, lenticellate; partial inflorescences 6-13, monochasial or more frequently dichasial (usually 3-flowered cymules); first-order branchlets alternate to subopposite, ascending, 5-10 (-25) mm long; bracts and bracteoles linear or lanceolate, 2-5 mm long, pubescent, eventually deciduous or sometimes present in the flowering state; pedicel ca. 2 mm long, pubescent. Flowers: calyx urceolate, actinomorphic, yellowish green, 3-6 mm long, not keeled, truncate except for 5 very small teeth, with several prominent glands, mostly hidden by an ochraceous, appressed indumentum without, glabrous within, abscising along a circumscissile line; corolla tubular, straight to slightly recurved, (sub)zygomorphic, acute to rounded at apex in bud, cream to white, 5-merous, with prominent glands, the tube 22-24 mm long, ca. 4 mm wide, densely woolly-pubescent without, densely tomentulose within, twice as long as the lobes, these 13-16 mm long, 3.3-4 mm wide, imbricate in bud, recurved at anthesis, oblong or elliptic, rounded or acute at apex, short appressed-pubescent on both surfaces; androecium of 2 fertile stamens flanking the innermost petal and 5 staminodes; filaments flattened, connate into a tube which is adnate to the corolla at the base and adherent to it at the throat by the intertwining of the pubescence on adjacent surfaces, densely covered with long, retrorse trichomes on the abaxial surface, free above, free part of the staminodes ca. 3 mm long, glabrous, gland-dotted, attenuate, curved; anthers ca. 3.8 mm long, glabrous, sparsely glandular punctate, each with a sterile portion above its attachment to the filament and below this a notched, gland-dotted appendage, ca. 0.8 mm long, free from each other; disc cupular, regularly and finely denticulate at margin, glabrous, ca. 1.2mm high, slightly taller than the ovary; gynoecium glabrous; ovary globose, ca. 0.8 mm long, surrounded by a disc; style 17 mm long at anthesis, becoming 22-23 mm long, glabrous, densely gland dotted; stigma capitate, slightly unilateral away from fertile stamens. Fruit a 5-lobed capsule (or a schizocarp in the instances when the carpels separate completely from each other), 22-25 x 25-30 mm, glabrous, rugulose, dehiscent septicidally along the dorsal commissures from the apex to 4-6 mm above the base or to the very base and loculicidally from the base along the ventral sutures, each carpel with an obtuse keel, the apex of which is enlarged forming a short apophysis on the abaxial surface, subtended or not by a persistent calyx; endocarp smooth, ochre-yellow, hard, elastically (or explosively) dehiscent; seed 1 per locule, subovoid, ca. 7 x 6 mm, the testa crustaceous, brownish, smooth to slightly striate, the micropyle conspicuous, the hilum subcircular; embryo subglobose, the cotyledons conduplicate, plicate, covering the short radicle.

description: Treelet or shrub 2-6 m tall; branchlets greenish with sparse, minute trichomes when young, then pale gray and glabrescent, striate, with many pale, prominent lenticels. Leaves alternate, crowded at the tips of branchlets, (2)3-foliolate; petiole semiterete, (3.5-)5-13 cm long, slightly expanded at the base, provided with several conspicuous dark glands, with sparse, minute trichomes when young, then completely glabrescent; leaflets with petiolule 2-7 mm long, not sharply separated from the base of the blade; blade narrowly elliptic or obovate, 16-24 x 6-9 cm and symmetrical when terminal, 10-19x3.5-8.2 cm and asymmetrical (sometimes strongly so) when lateral, acute, attenuate, or obtuse at the base, short- to long-acuminate at the apex, with an obtuse, retuse, or emarginate acumen, 5-13 x 1.5-4 mm, plane to slightly revolute at the margin, chartaceous, pellucidpunctate, the glands visible as dark dots on both surfaces, more numerous on the abaxial surface, the adaxial surface light-green, dull, glabrous, the abaxial surface concolorous, glabrous, or with very sparse, minute trichomes on the midvein near the base; venation eucamptodromous basally to brochidodromous distally, the midvein prominent on both surfaces, the secondary veins 5-8 on each side of midvein, ascending, arching, slightly prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence lateral, ascending, a narrow botryoid or a depauperate thyrsoid, borne below the leaves, usually on leafless branches; partial inflorescences if present monochasial (usually 3 or 4-flowered), 6-9 cm long including the peduncle, this 1-3.5cm long, sparsely and minutely puberulent, then glabrescent, conspicuously gland-dotted; first-order branchlets when present spreading, 20-30 mm long; bracts and bracteoles linear, 0.5-1 mm long, puberulent, early deciduous; pedicel 7-17 mm long, sparsely and minutely puberulent or glabrous. Flowers: calyx urceolate, actinomorphic, yellowish green, 3.5-4 mm long, not keeled, truncate or with 5 inconspicuous teeth, provided with several prominent glands, with sparse, minute trichomes without, glabrous within; corolla tubular, straight to slightly arcuate, zygomorphic, acute at the apex in bud, cream to white, 5-merous, with several prominent glands, the tube 22-24 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, woolly-pubescent without, twice as long as the lobes, these 9-15 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, imbricate in bud, recurved at anthesis, oblong to elliptic, rounded or acute at apex, with pubescence of short appressed trichomes on both surfaces; androecium of 2 fertile stamens flanking the innermost petal and 5 or 6 staminodes; filaments flattened, connate in a tube adnate only to the throat of the corolla, adherent by the indumentum to its base, densely covered with long, curled trichomes on both surfaces, free above, the free part of staminodes 3-5 mm long, glabrous, gland-dotted, attenuate ; anthers ca. 5 mm long, glabrous, sparsely glandular-punctate, rounded or occasionally apiculate at apex, each with a sterile portion above its attachment to the filament and below this with a notched appendage ca. 1.5 mm long, connate to each other by these appendages; disc cupular, surrounding the ovary, irregularly and slightly crenulate at the margin, glabrous, 0.8-1 mm high, equal to or slightly taller than the ovary; ovary densely yellow-sericeous, globose, ca. 0.8 mm long; style 19mm long at anthesis, glabrous, densely gland-dotted; stigma irregularly 5-lobed, unilateral away from the fertile stamens. Fruit a 5-lobed capsule (or sometimes a schizocarp), 11-16 x 12-17 mm, glabrous, rugulose, dehiscent septicidally along the dorsal commissures from the apex to ca. 2-5 mm above the base or to the very base and loculicidally from the base along the ventral sutures, with a slight obtuse keel and without an apophysis on the abaxial surface of each carpel, subtended by a persistent calyx; endocarp smooth, ochre-yellow, hard, elastically (or explosively) dehiscent; seed 1 per locule, reniform, ca. 8 x 6 mm, the testa crustaceous, brownish, smooth, the micropyle conspicuous, the hilum subcircular to elliptic; embryo subglobose, slightly compressed, the cotyledons conduplicate, plicate, covering the short radicle.

description: Deciduous shrubs or trees, 1.7-9 m tall; branches striate, lenticellate, glabrous; stipules 0.15 mm long, ovate, strigose, ciliolate, caducous. Leaves alternate, 5-foliolate (rarely 3-foliolate); pulvinus rugose, pubescent or glabrescent; petiole 2-5 cm long, pubescent or glabrous, the rachis 2.1-3.7 cm long, pilose, petiole and rachis both slender, terete or caniculate; petiolule 4-7 mm long, rugose. Leaflets opposite, subopposite, or rarely alternate, elliptic, oblong or obovate, acuminate (sometimes the acumen slightly retuse) at the apex, obtuse, rounded or cuneate at the base, the leaflets of the base 2.6-6.4 x 1.6-3.9 cm, the middle ones 3.5-8.9 x 2-4 cm, the terminal one 3.4-8.6 x 1.6-4.9 cm, the margin plane, membranous, not pellucid-punctate, silver sericeous on both faces when young, coriacous, bicolorous, sericeous or glabrous, the trichomes ferruginou and yellow; veins impressed on the upper face, prominent beneath when mature. Inflorescence a pseudoraceme with flowers geminate, axillary, the axis sericeous, pilose or glabrous; bracts and braceteoles 1 mm long, lanceolate, pubescent, caducous, the latter inserted about the middle of the pedicels. Calyx 4-7 mm long, campanulate, wine - colored (living plant), 5 -lobed, the lobes prominent, deltoid or triangular, sometimes  truncate at the base, sericeous or pubescent, the margin ciliote. Petals lilac purple; standard 6-12 mm long, orbicular, obovate or oblique - obovate, with yellow macula, externally pubescent, claw 2-6 mm long; wings 8-11 mm long, ellptic, elliptic -oblong or subfalcate, short auriculate (sometimes withouth auricula), the claw 2-6 mm long, sculptured, pubescent or glabrescent; keel petals 7-9 mm long, oblong, the claw 2-6 mm long, pubescent mainly at the apex, joined at the back. Stamens 10, pseudomonadephous (the vexillary stamen free at the base), the staminal tube enlarged at the basel filments alternatley long and short; anthers glabrous. Ovary 6-9 mm long, linear, stipitate, densely sericous, 6-ovulate; style curved or arcuate, glabrous; stigma inconspicuous. Legume 3.8- 12.3 x 1.5 - 1.8 cm, coriaceous, compressed, oblong - elliptic or lanceolate, stipitate, the apex acuminate, ferruginous, yellow or brown, sericeous or glabrescent, the trichomes ferruginous and yellow, the margin thickened, the stipe 0.3- 0.9 mm long, 1-4 seeded. Seeds 9-12 x 6-7mm, broadly reniform, flattened, brown, glabrous, the testa smooth; hilum cream colored.

description: Herbs. Leaf sheaths conduplicate, ca. 20 x 3 cm; petioles 8-10 cm long; blades membranous, ca. 50 x 10.5 cm, lanceolate with caudate apices and subcordate, oblique bases, the veins prominulous on both sides. Inflorescences cephaloid, compressed, ca. 4.5 cm wide, subtended by 2 bracts; bracts green, ca. II cm long, lanceolate, cordate at base, acuminate and aristate at apex, the aristae to 4 mm long. Fruits 1- or 2-seeded, loculicidal capsules, obconic, 5 x 4 mm; seeds oblong, longitudinally striate, brownish, 4 x 1.5 mm.

description: Understory to canopy trees, reproductive size (3-)7-22m tall, 12-30cm diam. Trunk with steep plank buttresses to 1 m high. Bark: outer bark light brownish-gray, with hoop marks, lenticellate; inner bark dark reddish-orange (Pacheco et al. 175). Resin milky. Trichomes on various organs of five types: fine erect bristles to 0.1 mm long, golden glandular hairs, thick appressed hairs to 0.1(-0.2) mm long, malpighiaceous hairs to 0.1 mm long, and golden ascending to erect trichomes 0.05-0.25 mm long. Leaves (20-) 24.2-53 cm long, (2-)4-7-jugate; petiole 6.3-27 cm long, 2.3-3.2(-4) mm diam; interjuga 1.7-6.3 cm long; petiole and rachis with dense to sparse (less often scattered) bristles, glandular hairs, and erect hairs; lateral peti- olules 0.3-2(-2.6) cm long, deeply canaliculate, pulvinuli not evident; terminal petiolule 2-5(-6.2) cm long, pulvinulus inconspicuous; basal leaflets (4.1-)6.2-13.8 x (1.9-) 2.4-7 cm, ovate to slightly obovate or slightly oblanceolate, rarely broadly elliptic; other lateral leaflets (6-)6.8-26.2 x (2.1-)2.4- 7.9 cm, oblong-elliptic to slightly oblanceolate or sometimes broadly elliptic; terminal leaflet (4.5-)8-18.6 x (2-)3-8.5 cm, (broadly) elliptic; leaflet apex abruptly and usually narrowly long-acuminate, the acumen 0.9-2cm long, often slightly dilated and slightly mucronate or retuse; leaflet base truncate to obtuse but usually slightly concave at insertion on petiolule, subsymmetric on lateral leaflets; margin often slightly revolute, especially toward the base; leaflets coriaceous, drying brown to dark brown; abaxial surface dull, all veins narrowly prominent, the midvein with dense to scattered erect hairs to 0.1 mm long, dense to scattered bristles, and sometimes scattered glandular hairs, the secondary veins and rest of surface with scattered appressed and/or malpighiaceous hairs, rest of surface also with regularly spaced, (half-)sunken glandular hairs; adaxial surface usually glossy, the midvein and secondary veins impressed to flat, rarely slightly prominulous but sunk in a groove, higher order veins prominulous, surface with a few scattered appressed hairs. Inflorescences 7.5-33cm long, 0.8-4.3 mm diam, reaching the petiole length of subtending leaves; secondary branches well-developed, to 14.5cm long, the axes with dense to sparse golden as cending hairs, sparse bristles, and dense to sparse glandular hairs; pedicel 0.7-1.5mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm diam (0.6-0.8 mm diam in pistillate flowers). Bracts subtending inflores- cences 1.2-3.2 mm long, subulate and acumi- nate; those on primary axes 1.1-2.4 mm long, subulate to ovate; bracteoles subtending cy- mules or flowers 0.3-0.5 mm long, subulate to ovate, all densely provided with golden ascending hairs. Staminate flowers 2-2.5mm long; calyx green, 0.4-1 x 1.9-2.1 mm, usually shorter than the disk, shallowly cupular, with dense appressed to ascending hairs, the lobes 0.2-0.4 mm long, rounded depressed-deltate with slightly acuminate apex; petals (greenish) yellow, cream, or pale green, 1.8- 2.25 x 0.8-1.15 mm, broadly lanceolate to ovate, with an inconspicuous inflexed apiculum 0.2-0.25 mm long, the abaxial surface with usually dense hairs as on the calyx, sometimes sparse to glabrescent near the base, the adaxial surface and margin glabrous and not papillate; stamens strongly dimorphic (anthers of the two series not overlapping in height), the antesepalous series 1.75- 2.25 mm long, the antepetalous series 1.25- 1.7mm long, the filaments slender and slightly strap-shaped, the anthers dorsifixed, 0.45-0.6mm long, the antesepalous ones often longer than antepetalous ones, the anthers in lateral view oblique-oblong, in dorsal view the antesepalous ones oblong-lanceolate to narrowly ovate, the antepetalous ones ovate; disk 0.25-0.5 mm high, 0.15-0.4mm thick, slightly taller or shorter than the pistil- lode, with dense erect hairs 0.05-0.1 mm long on the inside, top, and upper 1/3 of the outer surface; pistillode 0.25-0.6 x (0.15-) 0.25-0.35 mm, (depressed-) ovoid, the ovary usually provided with locules (cylindric and parenchymatous in Vieira 46), the surface with dense ascending to erect hairs 0.1-0.15 mm long, the stylar part 0.15-0.25 mm high, 5-fluted, the stigmas not developing. Pistillate flowers 2.5-3 mm long; calyx 1- 1.2 x 2.5-2.8 mm, shorter than the disk, the lobes 0.3-0.4mm long; petals 2-2.1 x 1- 1.25 mm, fleshier; staminodes strongly dimorphic (anthers of the two series not overlapping in height), the antesepalous series 1.75-2 mm long with anthers 0.45-0.5 mm long, taller than the pistil, the antepetalous series 1.3-1.35mm long with anthers 0.4- 0.45 mm long, in dorsal view the antesepalous anthers oblong-lanceolate, the antepetalous ones ovate; disk 0.4-0.55 mm tall, 0.2- 0.25 mm thick, with pubescence as in the staminate flowers; pistil 1.25-1.3 x 1-1.1 mm, the ovary sessile and depressed-ovoid, with dense ascending hairs 0.15-0.25 mm long, the style ca. 0.15-0.25 x 0.45 mm, shortly 5-branched, the stigmatic area 0.15-0.25 mm tall, lateral and drooping, compressed-turbinate, sparsely spiculate but not caudiculate. Fruits 1.8-2.5(-2.8) x 1.3-1.8cm (to 3.4cm wide when more than one pyrene develops), borne on a slightly clavate pedicel 1.8-3.5 long and 2.2-2.6 mm diam, maturing orange or rarely brown or reportedly red, obliquely ovoid, the apex rounded to slightly and broadly short-acuminate, the base sessile and truncate or less often obtuse; surface densely and acutely rugose-verrucose (more verrucose than rugose), with ridges to 0.6 mm high and with dense thick erect hairs to 0.2 mm long, the valves red within; pseudaril covering the pyrene white, sweet, pulpy; pyrene 1.5-1.9 x 1-1.1 cm, ca. 0.25 mm thick (Vdsquez et al. 19768), cartilaginous, in dorsiventral view narrowly lanceolate or less often elliptic or narrowly ovate, in lateral view the posterior side semi-ovate with acute apex and truncate base, the anterior side semi-ovate or semi-obovate with acuminate apex and obtuse to truncate base, cleft 10-20% the distance from the apex at the site of funicle, the funicular scar oblunate, covering ca. 10% of the anterior surface. Germination and seedlings not seen.

description: Understory to mid-canopy trees, reproductive size 10-20(-25) m tall, 12-20 cm diam. Trunk sometimes with simple plank buttresses to 25 cm high and with a spread of 55 cm. Bark: Outer bark gray-brown, smooth to rugose, with fine close vertical fissures, also thin scales; inner bark deep pink or orange-red outside, orange to yellow-beige inside (oxidizing red). Resin (off-)white, odorless or with an agreeable aromatic odor. Trichomes on various organs of five types: fine erect bristles to 0.05 mm long, golden flexuous or suberect hairs to 0.7 mm long (shorter on inflorescence and flowers), appressed hairs to 0.1(-0.2) mm (only on petals), ascending hairs to 0.1(-0.25) mm long, and snail-shaped glandular trichomes. Leaves 51-104 cm long, 5-7-jugate; petiole 14.5-27 cm long, 2.5-5 mm diam; interjuga 2.6-8 cm; petiole and rachis with dense flexuous hairs, sparse bristles, and scattered snail-shaped glands; lateral petiolules 0.3- 0.9 cm, stout and negligibly canaliculate, pulvinuli not evident; terminal petiolule 1.5- 3 cm, the distal pulvinulus inconspicuous; basal leaflets 8.5-17.5 x 3.7-7.6 cm, broadly elliptic; other lateral leaflets 13.5-30 x 4.5- 7.8 cm, oblong-elliptic to oblong-oblanceolate; terminal leaflet 10-19.5 x 3.6-8 cm, (oblong- )elliptic, sometimes broadly so; leaflet apex abruptly and narrowly long-acuminate, the acumen 1.2-2.7 cm long; leaflet base truncate to slightly cordate, subsymmetric on lateral leaflets; margin slightly revolute; leaflets coriaceous, tobacco-colored when dry, the surface rugulose; abaxial surface dull, all veins narrowly prominent, the midrib and second- ary veins with dense flexuous or suberect hairs (these more erect on secondary veins), also with scattered bristles and sparse to scattered snail-shaped glands, hairs on remaining veins similar but the flexuous hairs sparse; adaxial surface dull, the midrib narrowly prominulous but sunk in a groove, the secondary veins like the midrib or sometimes simply impressed, remaining veins prominulous, the midrib and secondary veins with scattered flexuous or suberect hairs and scattered snail-shaped glands, rest of surface with a few scattered snail-shaped glands. Inflorescences dimorphic: staminate inflorescences 21-40 cm long, 2.8-6 mm diam, longer than petiole of subtending leaves, the secondary axes to 18 cm long; pistillate inflorescences not seen, the infructescences to 22 cm long; inflorescence axes with pubescence as on the petiole but the flexuous hairs shorter and more erect distally; pedicel 1- 1.7 cm long, 0.2-0.3 mm diam. Bracts subtending inflorescences not seen; those on primary axes 1-3.5 mm long, ovate to subulate, the apex often acuminate; those subtending flowers to 0.3 mm long, (broadly) subulate to ovate, all with hairs as on inflorescence. Staminate flowers 1.7-2.1 mm long; calyx 0.45- 0.8 x 0.7-1 mm, slightly taller than the disk, with dense ascending hairs to 0.25 mm long, the lobes 0.25-0.35 mm, rounded (depressed-) ovate, slightly acuminate; petals green, 1.75- 2 x 0.55-1.1 mm, oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate, (sub)erect at anthesis, slightly carinate, with a strongly inflexed apiculum 0.2- 0.25 mm, the abaxial surface with dense appressed hairs to 0.15 mm, the adaxial surface glabrous and non-papillate, the margin long- papillate; stamens in two unequal series but their anthers overlapping in height, the antesepalous series 1.05-1.4mm long, the antepetalous series 0.95-1.15mm long, the filaments subterete and fleshy, the anthers basifixed, 0.2-0.25(-0.3) mm long, in dorsal view broadly oblong to broadly ovate with retuse apex, in lateral view broadly oblong, the anther sacs separated by the connective; disk 0.25-0.4mm high, 0.1-0.15 mm thick, usually taller than the pistillode, glabrous; pistillode 0.2-0.35 x 0.15 mm, depressed- globose, ovary provided with locules and rudimentary ovules, the surface with dense ascending hairs 0.1-0.15 mm long, the stylar part 0.1-0.15 mm high, 5-lobulate. Pistillate flowers known only from parts persisting on fruits; petals fleshier and larger, 2.3-2.4 x 1-1.05 mm; staminodes in two unequal series but their anthers overlapping in height, the antesepalous series 1-1.05 mm long with anthers 0.25-0.3 mm long, the antepetalous series 0.8-0.85 mm long with anthers 0.2- 0.3 mm long, the filaments fleshy and broadened at the base, in dorsal view the antesepalous anthers oblong-lanceolate and the antepetalous ones narrowly lanceolate, in lateral view both oblong-lanceolate; stigmas lateral, sigmoid-caudiculate and angled upward distally, bulbous at base, lateral length 0.35 mm. Fruits 2-2.3 x 1.4-1.6cm, borne on a terete pedicel 2-3.2 long and 1.7-2.5mm diam, maturing orange-red, oblique-ovoid, the apex rounded to broadly short-acuminate and sometimes slightly rostrate, the base obtuse and sessile to slightly substipitate; surface acutely rugose-verrucose, with ridges 0.7 mm high and with dense (sub)erect hairs to 0.7 mm long; pyrene 1.3-1.5 x 0.8-1 cm, 0.15-0.2mm thick, thinly cartilaginous, in dorsiventral view narrowly ovate, in lateral view the dorsal side semi-ovate with acute apex and truncate base, the ventral side semi-obovate with abruptly acuminate apex and truncate base, with a sub-apical cleft ca. 13% the distance from the apex at site of the funicle, the funicular scar oblunate, covering ca. 20% of the ventral side; seed ca. 1.38 x 0.9cm. Germination and seedlings not seen.

description: Species Securidacae uniflorae Oort proxima, sed diversa: ramis teretibus; foliis laminis ovatis vel late ovatis, 5-15 x 4-11 cm, subtus glabris, chartaceis, basi rotundatis vel leviter truncatis, margine non revolutis, petiolo 4-7 mm longo, venulis intense reticulato-anastomosatis, scrobiculatis; inflorescentia 3-6-flora, pedicellis basi glandula unica praeditis; floribus 10-15 mm longis, sepalis exterioribus ovatis, 3-6 mm longis, interioribus obovatis, ca. 15rmm longis; petalis carina cristatis; fructu 7-8 cm longo, 2-3 cm lato, lobo secundarius obtusoobovato, 6-7 mm lato.

description: Plants lianas; lateral branches occasionally forming sensitive hooks or looped tendrils. Branches and branchlets terete, glabrous, longitudinally striate, bark flaking off in small plates when mature; nodal glands present at the base of the petiole, sometimes inconspicuous. Petioles 4-7mm long, 1-2mm wide, canaliculate, sparsely pilose, glabrous and transversely rugose when mature. Leaf blades ovate to broadly-ovate, 5-15 x 4-11 cm, glabrous on both surfaces, coriaceous, the base rounded to slightly truncate, the apex acute to acuminate, the acumen 5-12mm long, the margin entire, the venation brochidodromous, the midvein canaliculate above, prominent beneath, the secondary veins 15-20, very prominent on both surfaces, the veinlets strongly reticulate forming a net nervation. Inflorescence a short axillary raceme, 2-2.5 cm long, 3-6-flowered, the main axis and pedicels sparsely appressed pilose, glabrous when mature; pedicels 5-11 mm long, with a gland at the base, bracteoles not seen. Flowers 10-15 mm long; sepals unequal, quincuncial, the outer sepals 3, ovate, 3-6mm long, reticulate-veined, glabrous on both surfaces, distal margins ciliate, the inner sepals 2, lateral, petal-like, obovate, 10-15 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, strongly reticulate-veined, with ca. 15 major veins. Corolla blue-lavender; keel petal ovate, ca. 10 x 4 mm, glabrous on both surfaces, claw ca. 8 mm, crest flabellate, ca. 2 mm long; adaxial petals ca. 10 x 4 mm, oblong-lanceolate, glabrous, reticulate-veined. Filament sheath 5-6 mm long, sparsely pilose at the base, free filaments 8, ca. 5 mm long, se of peripheral stamens shortly geniculate those of peripheral stamens shortly geniculate just below the anthers; anthers oblong, ca. 0.5 mm long, dehisced anthers with a large, pore-like slit from the apex to below the midpoint of the adaxial face; pollen pantocolporate, colpi 12. Ovary ca. 1 mm long, unilocular, glabrous; style ca. 10 mm long, distally arcuate, glabrous; stigma capitate; nectary inconspicuous. Samara 7-8 x 2-3 cm, tan, secondary lobe rhomboid, 6-7 mm wide, glabrous, more or less continuous with the primary wing, primary wing ca. 6cm long, entire or distally lobed.

description: Strangler epiphytes, which with the death of the host can result in trees to 50 m, or free-standing shrubs or small trees. Leaves (3-)5-7 foliolate (Fig. la), petioles 50-130 mm, leaflets 45-130 x 15-40 mm, oblanceolate-obovate, markedly acute at apex, decurrent-cuneate at base, glabrous on adaxial surface, glabrous or glabrate or with sparse hairs or glandular papillae on abaxial surface, subsessile on petiolules 2-5 mm long. Flowers borne singly near stout branch tips (Figs. 1 a, 2). Pedicels ca. 20 mm, robust. Calyx 15-20 mm long, usually cupuliform (Figs. Ic, 2), glabrous externally, villous within, apex truncate or with 3-5 irregular, shallow lobes. Petals 60-120 x 15-25 mm, oblong to slightly spathulate, externally and internally sparsely sericeous, curled back at anthesis (Fig. 2), initially greenish white, finally suffused reddish. Staminal tube articulate, lower staminal tube 10-30 mm, densely greysericeous, upper tube 2-20 mm, sparsely hairy to glabrous (Figs. Ic, id), with five filamentous apical lobes 15-25 mm long, somewhat flushed red; upper thecae 10-13 mm and lower thecae 14-23 mm. Ovary pyriform, densely pubescent, with style also pubescent as it emerges from the tube, reddish, equal to or longer than the staminal filaments, terminating in a lobed stigma (Fig. le). Fruit a capsule 10-15 cm long.

description: Frutex glaberrimus, dense ramosus, ramis erectis. Folia rigida, elliptica, late elliptica, oblanceolata vel lanceolata, plerumque sparsim serrulata, interdum integra, ad apicem uncato-retusa vel raro retusa, uncato-obtusa, obtusa; laminis 1-4 cm longis x 0.4-1.1cm latis. Inflorescentia 7-21 mm longa, 2-3-flora vel flore solitario, pedicellis 2-15 mm longis. Corolla lobis erectis, staminodiis florum pistillatorum 11-14, staminibus florum staminatorum 15-20(-30), pistillodio plerumque omnino evoluto. Fructus 5-8 x 2-3.5 mm, ellipsoideus vel interdum ovoideus, endocarpio 0.7-1.5 mm crasso.

description: Evergreen dioecious shrubs 0.3-1(-1.5) m tall, much-branched from base or from middle upward, with erect, vaguely striate branches; branchlets densely striate, glabrous; vegetative buds glabrous. Petioles 1-5 mm long, adaxially flattened to concave, abaxially ± rounded, glabrous. Leaf blades 1-4 x 0.4-1.1 cm, 1.4-5.4 times as long as wide, elliptic to broadly elliptic, oblanceolate or lanceolate, glabrous, thick-coriaceous, dark green adaxially, light green abaxially, occasionally yellowish in dried specimens, base attenuate, apex hooked-retuse, rarely retuse, hooked-obtuse or obtuse, apical gland caducous or less often persistent, margin serrulate with 1-4 teeth or occasionally entire, revolute, marginal glands early caducous, rarely persistent, venation ± brochidodromous, primary to tertiary veins visible, not branched near median vein or near margin, median vein impressed or somewhat elevated adaxially and abaxially. Inflorescences cymose or racemose, 7-21 mm long, axillary, glabrous, 1- to 3-flowered, peduncle 4-12 mm long, ter- minal flower subsessile or with pedicel to 2 mm long, lateral flowers subsessile or with pedicel to 4 mm long, peduncle 2-15 cm long (when 1-flowered); bracts (one per flower or inflorescence) early caducous (only scars seen), glabrous, bracteoles 1-3 (one per flower), 0.8-1.5 x 0.4-0.7 mm, elliptic or rarely broadly elliptic, glabrous, pale green (light brown in dried specimens), persistent or caducous, apex acute or rarely obtuse-rounded, ±keeled, margin sparsely ciliate or less often entire, apical gland caducous or rarely persistent. Flowers 3-7mm long, hypanthium glabrous; calyx lobes 5, 0.7-1.2 x 0.7-1.2 mm, pale green, subdeltoid to deltoid, erect, glabrous, margin ciliate; corolla lobes 5, 3.2-4.5 x 1.8-2.7 mm, oblong or nearly so, white, somewhat erect and concave, glabrous, margin sparsely ciliate or glabrous; stamens 2- to 4-seriate; filaments 0.9-5.3 mm long, white, erect, glabrous, the longer ones exceeding the style and stigma (when present); disc flat, glabrous, green or orange along margin, smooth, 5-lobed, pentagonal. Staminate flowers with hypanthium 0.6-1 mm long, pale green or black, often smooth, rarely ± rugose; stamens 15-20(-30); style to 2.5 mm long, rarely wanting, straight to incurved, rarely bifurcate, glabrous, pale green; stigma obsolete, light green; ovary aseptate or with 1-3-septa, septa (when present) incomplete; disc 0.5-0.7 mm in diameter. Pistillate flowers with hypanthium 0.8-1.2 mm long, green, rugose; staminodes 11-14; style 0.8-2.1 mm long, straight, glabrous; stigma capitate, 3-lobed, dark green; ovary 3-locular; disc 0.6-0.9 mm in diameter. Fruit 5-8 x 2-3.5 mm, ellipsoid or occasionally ovoid, 1-locular, glabrous; disc conical, calyx lobes erect; endocarp 0.7-1.5 mm thick. Seed one, 4-4.5 x 2.8-3.2 mm, ellipsoid.

description: Perennial herbs from scaly (as a result of the persistent stipules), creeping and infrequently branched caudex. Indumentum of sparse to moderate, multicellular, short to long-stalked, minutely glandular-headed hairs. Leaves±forming a basal rosette and extending alternately along 1 to few, scape-like erect stems (these to ca. 8 dm tall, occasionally vine-like), stipulate, petiolate, the blades ovate, usually distinctly longer than wide (when basal lobes considered part of total length), shallowly 5- to 9-lobed, and palmately veined, the apex acute (rarely obtuse), the base cordate, the margins strongly to obscurely, irregularly serrate to nearly dentate, with each tooth ending in a multicellular, minutely gland-headed hair; largest rosette leaves 2.3-13 x 2-11.5 cm, with longest petioles 3-25 cm long; cauline leaves 0.7-9.5 x 0.7-8.7 cm, with length/width quotient of 0.83-1.44 (average 1.04; as measured from base of midvein to apex and across the widest point of the lamina), the petioles 0.5-9 cm long; leaves becoming smaller distally on the erect stems. Stipules paired and adnate to base of petiole, ± ovate-triangular, 2.3-16 mm long, membranous, the apex acute to obtuse, the margins with irregular glandular-serrations. Adventitious buds usually produced at the apex of the petioles of the rosette and cauline leaves, and these occasionally forming plantlets, and vegetative shoots occasionally also arising from axillary buds of cauline leaves. Inflorescences terminal racemes, 2.5-34 cm long, bearing few to numerous flowers. Flowers perfect, basically 5-merous, zygomorphic, pedicellate, continuing to grow after anthesis; pedicels 1-6 mm long, with subtending bracts obovate to ovate, oblong, or ±linear, 1.4-2.5 mm long, scarious, with glandular-fimbriate margins, and with 2 minute, opposite, ± linear bracteoles at base or borne on proximal third of pedicel. Calyx of 5 unequal sepals, arising from cylindric-funnelform hypanthium, which deeply ventrally cleft, 9-veined, and slightly gibbous at base, the hypanthium 2.7-7 x 1.8-4 mm, the 3 dorsal sepals ovate- to elliptic-triangular, 2.3-4 x 1.3-2 mm, with obtuse to rounded-mucronate apex, the two ventral-lateral sepals narrowly ovate-triangular to oblong-triangular, 1.6-2.8 x 0.45-0.8mm, with acute to acuminate apex, the hypanthium and sepals green with variable development of red-purple stripes, with short-stalked glandheaded hairs, sometimes also with a few longer-stalked hairs distally on sepals persistent. Petals 4, ± filiform, recurved, greenish to brown-purple, 3.5-11 x 0.1-0.2 mm, persistent. Stamens 3, inserted at apex of hypanthium opposite the dorsal sepals, slightly exserted, the filaments 1.4-5.6mm long, the anthers basifixed, reniform, 0.5-1 mm long, opening by 2 dorso-lateral slits, thus becoming peltate at maturity. Gynoecium of 2 fused carpels, the ovary superior, oblong, attenuate at base, 2-cleft at apex and each portion tapering into the style, 2.7-8 mm long (including narrowed basal portion) with scattered very short-stalked, gland-headed hairs; placentation parietal, with 2 placentae, each with numerous ovules; styles 2, slender, 1.6-4.6 mm long (including the apical clefts of ovary); stigmas capitate. Capsule membranous, with 2 diverging equal beaks, ovoid and tapering at the base, 8-15mm long. Seeds subglobose, 0.4-0.7 mm long, brown to nearly black, with testa distinctly muricate, the longest projections to 0.04-0.085 mm.

description: Shrub, decumbent to prostrate, the stems 40-50(-160) cm long, with branchlets 1-1.5 mm diam., brown-grayish, covered with both abundant simple spreading trichomes 0.4-0.55 mm long and sparse short glandular trichomes; leaves subcoriaceous, bullate with obvious venation, mostly 18-25 X 9-16 mm, elliptic to ovate, upper surface hispidulous, lower surface hispid with simple trichomes to 0.6 mm, abundant at the midvein, with the rest of the surface hispidulous, apex obtuse to rounded, base rounded, margins crenulate, slightly thickened, the teeth conspicuous and glandular; petioles 3.2-5 mm long, covered with both simple unicellular and glandular trichomes; flowers usually 2 per inflorescence, in ax- illary cymes, pendulous, in the terminal portion of the stems; peduncles 1.2-2.8 mm long; involucel bracteoles linear, 1.5-3 mm long; calyx 5-lobed, the lobes linear-lanceolate, shortly fused at the base, 4.8-6.5 X 0.6-1.2 mm, yellowish green, with short glandular trichomes and simple trichomes at the margins; corolla salverform, pinkish purple, the tube gradually expanded, 20-28 mm long, the narrow portion 2/3 as long, the widest portion 10.2-11.6 mm wide, externally with both glandular and short-spreading non-glandular trichomes, internally with short curved trichomes in the lower portion, the lobes ovate, 4.4-5.8 mm long, with both glandular trichomes and simple trichomes abaxially, glabrous adaxially, the upper 2 lobes slightly shorter than the lower 3; stamens 4, slightly exserted, 8-10 mm long, inserted at the middle of the corolla tube, the free portion of the filaments shorter than the attached portion; style 2-3 cm long; stigma subcapitate; fruit a rostrate indehiscent capsule, hispid 3.8-4.4 mm long, the rostrum 1-1.8 mm long, the persistent calyx slightly accrescent, yellowish green, seed obovate 2-2.6 X 1-1.6 mm.

description: Erect shrub 60-150 cm high, with slender branched stems; branchlets grayish, hispid, with abundant spreading simple trichomes 0.4-0.6 mm long and glandular trichomes; leaves thin, planar and herbaceous, with venation obvious, mostly 18-23 X 8-13 mm, elliptic to rhombic, upper surface hispidulous, lower surface usually hispid with abundant simple trichomes to 0.8 mm long on the central and lateral veins with the rest of the surface hispidulous, apex acute to obtuse, base acute to cuneate, margins serrulate with 5-6 pairs of glandular teeth; petioles 2.2-3.4 mm long, hispid; flowers in axillary cymes in the terminal portion of the stems; peduncles short, 0.8- 2.2 mm long; involucel bracteoles linear, 0.8-2.4 mm long; calyx 5-lobed, the lobes linear-lanceolate, shortly fused at the base, 5-8 X 0.6-1.4 mm, yellowish green, with both kinds of trichomes as on the stems, apex acute; corolla salverform, the base of the tube white, the lobes pinkish purple, the tube gradually expanded, 22-30 mm long, the narrow portion 2/3 the length, 8-10 mm wide at the widest portion, externally with both glandular and short spreading non- glandular trichomes, and internally with short trichomes in its lower portion, a strap-shaped nectariferous gland at the base of the tube, lobes ovate, 4.6-6 mm long, ciliate, glabrous adaxially, the upper 2 lobes slightly shorter than the lower 3; stamens 4, exserted, inserted at the middle of the corolla tube, 12-14 mm long, the free por- tion of the filaments shorter than the attached portion; style 2-3 cm long; stigma subcapitate; fruit a rostrate indehiscent capsule, hispid, 3.8-4.6 mm long, the rostrum 0.8-1.8 mm long, the persistent calyx slightly accrescent, yellowish green; seed obovate 2-2.6 X 0.8-1.6 mm.

description: Shrubs 40-50(160) cm high, with branched stems, grayish, bark thin; branchlets reddish, covered with both curved antrorse and short glandular trichomes; leaves thin, 9-20 mm long, 2-8 mm wide, elliptic, glabrous or with scattered unicellular trichomes, usually restricted to the midvein and margins, apex obtuse, base cuneate, margins dentate, the teeth minute and restricted to the upper 1/2, rarely entire, slightly thickened; petioles ca. 1 mm long, covered with both simple unicellular and glan- dular trichomes; flowers usually 1, rarely 2 in axillary cymes; peduncles ca. 1 mm long; calyx with 5 lanceolate lobes, shortly fused at the base, 4-7 mm long, ca. 0.6 mm wide, also with both kinds of trichomes as the branchlets and the leaves; corolla fun- nel-shaped, pinkish purple, the tube 25-30 mm long, 10-12 mm wide at the widest portion, with both glandular and short, spreading, non-glandular trichomes externally, and with short curved trichomes in its lower portion internally, the lobes ovate, 6-8 mm long, ciliate, glabrous internally, the upper 2 lobes slightly shorter than the lower 3; stamens 4, inserted at the middle of the corolla tube; style exserted; fruit a rostrate pyriform achene with the persistent calyx, 5-7 mm long, on a rostrum 2-4 mm long.

description: Spreading, much branched perennial herb, procumbent to semierect; long taproot semiwoody to woody; stems to 9 dm, stout, very viscid, densely glandular-pubescent, often reddish at nodes; petioles 1-9 cm long, viscid, pubescent, often reddish at base; leaf blades succulent, broad ovate, elliptic, suborbicular to deltoid-ovate, 2-8 cm long, 2-6 cm wide, glandular-puberulent above, glandular-pubescent below, margin repand to sinuate, frequently undulate, base subcordate, truncate to obtuse, tip obtuse to rounded; peduncles viscid, densely glandular-pubescent, 2.5-13 cm long; bracts 5-7, glandular-pubescent with margins often somewhat villous, 5-16 mm long, 2-10 mm wide, oblong-ovate, obovate, elliptic to oval, apex rounded to acute; flowers 20-75 per inflorescence; perianth tube 12-25 mm long, magenta, viscid, villous basally to glandular-pubescent apically; perianth limbs 8-10 mm wide, bright magenta, glabrous, lobe tips shallowly emarginate, notch usually less than 1.4 mm deep; anthocarps narrowly turbinate, beaked, glabrous with apex often glandular-pubescent, 6-9 mm long, 3-4.5 mm wide, thin, somewhat coriaceous to scarious; wings 5, narrow, finely reticulate to inconspicuously rugose, tops rounded or truncate and often pinkish, cavity extends throughout entire wing; achenes narrowly obovate to oblong-obovate, 2.2-3 mm long, dark brown.

description: Prostrate, much branched annual herbs; taproot slender; stems moderately slender to stout, 2-4 dm long, viscid, densely glandular-pubescent, hairs short, internodes short; petioles 2-4.5 cm long, viscid, puberulent; leaf blades succulent, 1-2.5 cm long, 0.6-1.5 cm wide, elliptic-oblong, oval to rhombic-ovate, glandular-puberulent, margins entire to repand, base rounded to acute, usually very unequal, tip obtuse; peduncles 2.5-5 cm long, glandular-puberulent to glandular-pubescent; bracts lanceo- late, lance-ovate to elliptic, 3-5 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, acute, puberulent to glandular- pubescent; flowers 15-35 per inflorescence; perianth tube 7-12 mm long, greenish, viscid, puberulent; perianth limbs greenish white, 4-6 mm broad, glabrous; antho- carps tapering at both ends, 4-6 mm long, 2.5-4.5 mm wide, deeply 5-lobed, the lobes wing-like, viscid-puberulent; achenes ovoid, 2-5 mm long, brown.

description: Much branched, decumbent to ascending annual, rarely perennial herbs; taproot long, fleshy; stems slender to moderately stout, 1-7 dm long, viscid, glandular- pubescent to short villous, often reddish at base and at nodes; petioles 1-7 cm long, glandular-pubescent to somewhat villous; leaf blades 1-5.5 cm long, 0.7-3 cm wide, ovate-oblong, lance-ovate, lance-oblong, deltoid-ovate to elliptic, margins entire to sinuate, infrequently shallowly lobed, sparsely puberulent to densely glandular- pubescent, base subcordate to rounded to obtuse, apex obtuse, infrequently acute; peduncles 2-10 cm long, viscid, glandular-puberulent to villous; bracts 5-10 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, attenuate, glandular-pubescent outside, sometimes puberulent inside; flowers 10-30 per inflorescence; perianth tube 10-20 mm long, puberulent above to villous at base, viscid; perianth limbs 6-8 mm across, pale pink to bright magenta, lighter eyespot; anthocarps thin-walled, deeply lobed, 5-10 mm long, 4-7 mm wide, villous at top and on upper wing margins, wings 5, thin-walled with cavity extending throughout entire wing, wing cavity separated from body cavity by thin membrane, membrane puberulent inside, wing tops truncate, with conspicuous inflations; achenes elliptic-oblong, 1.5-3 mm long, dark brown.

description: Perennial, stems few to numerous from the woody taproot, ascending, less fre- quently procumbent, moderately slender, 1.5-5 dm tall, often whitish, viscid-puberulent to glandular-pubescent; petioles 1-4.5 cm, puberulent to glandular-pubescent; leaf blades 2.5-5 cm long, 0.5-3 cm wide, lanceolate, lance-ovate, narrow ovate-oblong to elliptic-oblong, margins entire to somewhat sinuate, base obtuse to cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, glabrous above, nearly glabrous to puberulent below; peduncles 2- 5.5 cm long, puberulent to glandular-pubescent, somewhat viscid; bracts 4-8 mm long, 2-5 mm wide, ovate, oval-ovate to elliptic-ovate, glandular-pubescent, sometimes villous basally, tip acute to attenuate; flowers 15-30 per inflorescence; perianth tube 8-16 mm long, greenish, glandular-pubescent, often somewhat villous basally; perianth limbs 5-7 mm broad, very pale pink to light magenta; anthocarps thin-walled, 4-7 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, villous at top; wings 5, cavity extending throughout entire wing, wing tops truncate, with conspicuous dilations; achenes elliptic-oblong, about 2 mm long, dark brownish black.

description: Perennial, viscid herbs from slender to thick woody taproots; stems few to numerous, decumbent to erect, 1-5 dm long, sparsely glandular-puberulent to glandular  pubescent to viscid-villous, sometimes glabrous basally, often reddish tinged; petioles 1-4 cm long, puberulent to short villous; leaf blades 1.5-6 cm long, 0.5-3.5 cm wide, somewhat fleshy, elliptic-oblong, ovate-oblong, oval to rhombic-ovate, glabrous to puberulent above, thinly puberulent to pubescent below, margins entire to sinuate, often undulate, base obtuse, oblique to truncate, apex rounded; peduncles 2-12 cm long, puberulent to short villous; bracts usually 5, ovate, ovate-oblong, elliptic- oblong to obovate, scarious, 5-20 mm long, 3-10 mm wide, rounded to acute, glandular-pubescent to villous, frequently reddish at base; flowers 25-75 per in florescence; perianth tube 10-22 mm long, rose to greenish, glandular-pubescent above to villous at base; perianth limbs white, 5-8 mm broad, glabrous; anthocarps thin- walled, 5-12 mm long, 4-8.5 mm wide, glandular-pubescent to short villous on top, becoming nearly glabrous at base, tapered to the base, beaked; anthocarp wings 5, not folded, or 2 wings folded together, cavity extending throughout wing; wing-tops, except folded ones, truncate to somewhat rounded, inflated, dilations appearing diamond-shaped and flat from above, folded type without dilated tops, capitulum consisting of one type anthocarp only or of folded anthocarps peripherally and winged anthocarps in the center; achenes elliptic-oblong, 2.5-3.5 mm long, tan to medium brown.

description: Perennial, decumbent to ascending, much branched from a woody taproot; stems stout, often reddish at nodes, 2-8 dm long, glabrous to sparsely glandular-puberulent to glandular-pubescent; petioles 1-6 cm long, frequently as long as or longer than blades, nearly glabrous to glandular-pubescent; leaf blades 1-6 cm long, 0.5-4 cm wide, ovate-oblong, oblong-oval, ovate, ovate-elliptic to lance-elliptic, entire to sinuate, sometimes undulate, base oblique, rounded to cuneate, tip obtuse, infrequently acute; peduncles 4-15 cm long, glabrous to short glandular-pubescent, frequently reddish at least at base; bracts 5-12 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, lanceolate, ovate, elliptic to obovate, apex acute, glabrate to glandular-pubescent; flowers 25-60 per inflorescence; perianth tube 15-25 mm long, very slender, glabrous to puberulent above, puberulent to glandu- lar-pubescent below, greenish above to pale rose at base, infrequently white; perianth limbs white, 7-12 mm broad, glabrous; anthocarps 6-10 mm long, 4-10 mm wide, occasionally wider than long at apex, beaked, puberulent to glandular-pubescent, coriaceous, body rarely indurate; wings 2, these folded together, or more often 5 not folded, occasionally wingless, wings thin, without cavity or cavity extending only into base of wing, wings broad, narrowed at base, truncate to rounded above, margins sometimes undulate; achenes elliptic-oblong, 2.5-4 mm long, medium to dark brown.

description: Description: A subscandent shrub; wood of a very characteristic yellow color; braniehlets slender, rather densely puberulent with short brownish hairs (or subvelutinous on the voungest parts) ; leaf scars large and prominelnt; petioles slender, 2-7 cm. long, ampliate at base, inerassate and usually curvate at apex, densely puberulent or substrigose; leaf blades firmly membranous or subeoriaceous, elliptic or subobovate, 11-23.5 cm. long, 4-10.6 cm. wide, acute or acuminate (rarely obtuse) at apex, entire, acute at base, bullate, rather obscurely puberulent or strigillose on the larger venation on both surfaces, becoming glabrate, 3- or 5-pli-nerved; pistillate infloreseence axillary or supra-axillary, racemiform, 2-3 cm. long and 1-1.5 cm. wide at anthesis, enlarged to 9-10 cm. long and wide in fruit; rachis slender at anthesis and densely velutinous, greatly inerassate in fruit and then only rather obscurely appressed-strigose; pedicels slender, 3-6 mm. long, and densely strigose-pubeseent or subveluti- nous at anthesis, greatly inerassate, about 1 cm. long, and rather obscurely appressed-strigose in fruit, each bearing 1, 2, or 3 fruits; description: Shrubs, the older branches with grayish bark and prominent lenticels. Stems sparsely to moderately hirsute with simple hairs 1-2 mm long and a few minute stellate hairs, the hairs denser at base of petioles. Leaf blade cordate, ovate, remotely and shallowly denticulate, acuminate, the upper surface with appressed simple hairs 0.5-2 mm long and a few minute stellate hairs, the lower surface more densely and evenly stellate-pubescent, somewhat discolorous, pedately 7-9-veined, up to 15 cm long, 14 cm wide. Petiole 6 cm long becoming progressively shorter upwards, the pubescence like that of stem but denser becoming very dense at juncture with lamina. Stipules foliar, sessile, falcate to auriculate-clasp- ing, apically toothed or laciniate, 8-20 mm long, (3) 5-10 mm broad, marginally ciliate (hairs ca 1 mm), becoming paired floral bracts in the inflorescence where usually persistent, deciduous below. Inflorescence an elongate, interrupted, es- sentially unbranched raceme, the flowers solitary in the axils of the upper leaves (which are progressively reduced upwards), the uppermost flowers surpassing the leaves, in bud enclosed in the paired stipular floral bracts. Pedicel 0.3-1.5 cm long (in flower) to 2 cm long (in fruit), with pubescence similar to that of petiole, the hairs denser and longer toward apex (minutely stellate-puberulent in Hinton 11010), articulate somewhat above the middle. Involucel absent. Calyx 9-13 mm long, deeply 5-lobed, minutely stellate-puberulent and prominently ciliate (hairs 1-2 mm) on margin and principal veins; lobes ovate, acute. Petals yellow-orange, slightly reflexed, 9-15 mm long, minutely and densely bearded on claw, otherwise glabrous. Staminal column 5-7 mm long, pallid, globose and stellate-pubescent at base becoming columnar and sometimes glabrous above, giving rise to numerous filaments, these often paired or more complexly associated; anthers ca 50, yellowish. Styles slender, glabrous, pale greenish, eventually exceeding an- droecium; stigmas capitate, purplish. Young fruit minutely and evenly stellate- pubescent; mericarps 10-11, apically rounded-acute, 8-9 mm tall.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1980. Malvaceous miscellany, including new species from Mexico and Brazil. Brittonia. 32: 262-268.

description: Herb or subshrub to 1 m tall, widely branching, the branches supported on other vegetation, the branch tips drooping. Stems terete, green, with both minute stellate hairs and long (1-2 mm) simple hairs interspersed. Leaf blade up to 13 cm long, 9 cm broad, gradually smaller towards apices of branches, ovate, cordate, crenate, acuminate, palmately 7-nerved, slightly discolorous, minutely and evenly stellate-pubescent above and beneath, the hairs ca 0.5 mm diameter, those above sparser and asymmetrical. Petioles 5-45 mm long, '/6 to '/2 the length of the blade, with pubescence like that of stem. Stipules 4-8 mm long, subulate, pubescent. Peduncles usually solitary in the axils or on axillary branches, 4-12 mm long, articulated 1-2 mm below the flower, evenly and minutely stellate-pubescent and with glandular hairs. Involucel absent. Calyx 4 mm long, cupuliform, shallowly 5-lobed, glandular- and stellate-pubescent, tightly enclosing the base of the fruit, the lobes acuminate, the sinuses broadly rounded. Corolla yellow, 5-7 mm long, rotate. Anthers numerous, yellow. Fruit pseudocapsular (sep- ticidal dehiscence suppressed), 5-6 mm long (almost twice the length of the calyx), minutely stellate- and glandular-pubescent with a crown of short (0.5 mm) divergent spines; mericarps 5, oblong, apically acute forming spines, the lateral wall slightly reticulate basally, completely divided internally into 2 cells by a broad double endoglossum, the lower cell indehiscent, 1-seeded, the upper cell loculicidally dehiscent, 2-seeded (the seeds superposed, not collateral). Seeds glabrous, blackish, angularly reniform, minutely papillate, ca 1.6 mm long.

description: Stems often purplish-pigmented, minutely stellate-puberulent (the hairs 0.1 mm long). Leaf blade ovate, to 16 cm long, 13 cm broad, deeply cordate, crenate, acute to acuminate, somewhat discolorous, pedately 9-1 1-nerved, the lower sur- face densely whitish stellate-puberulent when young, eventually becoming more coarsely and sparsely pubescent, the upper surface with sparser pubescence, the stellate hairs having fewer arms and tending to be preferentially oriented toward the margin. Petiole shorter than to equaling the lamina, with pubescence like that of stem. Flowers solitary in the axils or on axillary branches forming panicles. Peduncle 1-4 cm long, articulated 3-5 mm below the flower, minutely puberulent, glandular hairs often present. Involucel absent. Calyx densely puberulent, more or less glandular, 5-lobed nearly to the base, 6-8 mm long; lobes narrowly lanceolate, 1.5-2.5 mm wide at base, reflexed in fruit. Petals 7-13 mm long, yellow- ish, lacking spot at base. Staminal column ca 8 mm long, stellate-pubescent except toward apex, pallid, antheriferous at apex; filaments 1 mm long. Mericarps ca 8, 15-19 mm long, rounded at base and strongly keeled dorsally, acuminate apically, usually hirsute (hairs 1-1.5 mm) especially on keel, with glandular hairs on face of mericarp. Seeds 2 mm long, reniform, glabrous, blackish.

description: Plant erect, apparently unbranched, the stems minutely and densely stellate-puberulent, the hairs 0.1 mm long. Leaf blade broadly cordate, ovate, dentate, acute, palmately 9-nerved, discolorous, densely and minutely stellate-puberulent (but not obscuring the leaf surface), up to 5 cm long, about as wide as long. Petiole more or less equaling the blade, minutely stellate-puberulent like the stem. Stipules 1-4 mm long, subulate or few-laciniate, caducous. Inflorescences terminal, leafless panicles. Pedicel 4-10 mm long. Involucel absent. Flowers unknown. Calyx 4-7 mm long, half length of mature fruit or less, more or less enclosing lower part of fruit, minutely pubescent. Mericarps 9-10, 7-9 mm long, at maturity straw-colored, stellate-pubescent (the arms 0.4-0.8 mm long), apically acute to obtuse, apiculate (the apiculum ca 0.2 mm long), loculicidally dehiscent to the base, tardily and imperfectly septicidally dehiscent. Seeds minutely pubescent (?).

description: Arbores horizontaliter ramificantes, ramulis interdum spiniferis. Folia decidua, glabra, ovata, 6-9 x 3.5-5.2 cm. Inflorescentia spicata, fasciculis 3-floris. Tepala 5, stamina 5, epitepala, filamentis dorso pilosis, glandula nectarifera 5-lobata, lobis oblongis, inter stamina productis 1.5 x 0.7-0.8 mm. Fructus drupaceus, globoso-ovoideus, 6.4 x 5-5.5 cm, exocarpio lignoso, granuloso, mesocarpio pulposo, endocarpio lignoso. Semen 2-2.5 cm diam.

description: Tree to 24 m tall, 65 cm diam.; outer bark greyish, nearly smooth, shallowly vertically fissured; inner bark thick, with a green layer, then yellowish cream or reddish, granular, with a strong smell; stem cylindrical, with buttresses in the lower 30-100 cm; branches more or less in verticils, spreading horizontally; very young twigs and leaves densely strigulose with yellowish simple hairs 0.1-0.3 mm long, soon glabrescent except for small rounded axillary buds, these rarely (in the material available) with a spine to 4 mm long developed between the petiole base and axillary bud; twigs with a peculiar gravy-like odor when cut, drying light tan, flattened and sharply angled and finely striately wrinkled. Leaves deciduous in the dry season, the young ones shiny, light green, sparsely strigosulose with simple hairs 0.2-0.3 mm long, soon glabrate except along midrib below, the older ones drying light green, mat; blades ovate, 6-9 X 3.5- 5.2 cm, apiculate, acute and abruptly short-attenuate onto the petiole at the base, with 5-7 major lateral veins per side, the tertiary venation fine and obscure, the margin plane except at the tip where rolled upward, cartilaginous; petiole wrinkled abaxially, canaliculate adaxially, 1.4-2 cm long. Flowering with the emergence of the new leaves; inflorescences from leafless axils of previous years' growth and on lower axils of new shoots from which the first leaves have fallen, or rarely in axils of current leaves, of a single axillary spike, or of several spikes on short indeterminate axes, the spikes 2.5-5 cm long, the flowers somewhat irregularly arranged, apparently basically cymules of 3 flowers subtended by a single bract, but often only 2 or 1 flower produced, the bracts 0.7-1 mm long, pubescent with ferruginous hairs to 1.1 mm long contrasting with the finer pale hairs of the rachis and flower buds. Flowers yellowish green, cupulate-rotate, 7 mm diam., the tepal lobes 5, triangular, 2.5 X 1.7 mm, puberulent on the outside, glabrous within; stamens 5, born near the base of the tepal lobes, the filament 1 mm long, 0.6 mm wide at the base, pilose abaxially, apparently glued to the tepal lobe by the sticky hairs; anther 0.6 X 0.6 mm, introrse; nectary 2 mm wide, completely occupying the space between the filaments and the style, and with 5 petal-like oblong lobes between the stamens, 1.5 X 0.7-0.8 mm wide; style continuous with the nectary, 1.7 mm long, with expanded funnelform tip. Fruits drupaceous, greenish and tan or orangish, globose-ovoid, 6.4 X 5-5.5 cm, the exocarp woody, granular, yellowish to reddish brown, 5-7 mm thick, the outer surface finely cracked-granular, the tepalar scar at the tip 3 mm wide, depressed, with remains of lobes or these broken off; mesocarp pulpy, creamy, slightly fragrant, 5- 7 mm thick, the taste not pleasant but apparently innocuous; endocarp reddish tan, 1 mm thick, woody; seed 2-2.5 cm diam., white and homogeneous and odorless when cut.

description: Planta perenne, (40-)50-70 cm alta, caespitosa. Caulis pubescens, basi bulbosus. Folia 5-8, marginibus pubescentibus. Bracteae involucrales squamis similes 3-4. Capitula hemisphaericum. Spiculae 10-20, squamis androgynis villosis. Setae (4-)5, 2.5-3.5 longae. Achaenium 1.8-2.5 X 1.3-1.6 mm, obovatum, biconvexum, laeve; stylus basi 0.6 X 0.4 mm, pyramidalis.

description: Perennial, (40-)50-70 cm tall, rhizomatous. Culms 0.8-1.6 mm wide, cylindrical, pubescent, base thickened. Leaves 5-8; sheaths 5-8 cm long, becoming fibrous when old, glabrous; blades 20-35 cm X 1.6-2.5 mm, half the height of the culm, linear-lanceolate, conduplicate or less often flattened, the margins pilose. Inflorescences capitate, subtended by 3-4 involucral bracts; involucral bracts similar to the spikelet scales, broadly ovate at the base, becoming narrow apically, flat, brown, chartaceous, the margins villous; basal bract 5-6 X 5-6.5 mm, the apex mucronate 0.7-1.1 X 0.2-0.6 mm; second bract (3-)5-8 cm long. Capitula 9-12 X 8-15 mm, hemispheric. Spikelets 10-20, 6-8 X 1.7-2.7 mm, lanceolate, comprising 8-9 scales, the basal 3 scales empty, followed by a single scale subtending a perfect flower and 4-5 distal scales subtending staminate flowers; distal empty scale 3-4.5 X 1.8-3 mm, ovate-lanceolate, brown, coriaceous, villous, the apex acute; scale of the perfect flower 5-6 X 2.5-3.5 mm, rhombic, convolute, brown, coriaceous, the keel villous; scale of the basal staminate flower brown, coriaceous, the keel slightly villous, the other staminate scales membranous, glabrous. Perianth bristles (4-)5, 2.5-3.5 mm long, surpassing the achene, plumose to near the apex, antrorsely scabrous apically. Anthers 2.5-3 mm long. Achenes 1.8-2.5 X 1.3-1.6 mm, obovoid, biconvex, brown, the surface smooth and shiny, the margins prominent, straight and not cartilaginous, smooth; style base persistent, 0.6 X 0.4 mm, pyramidal, not confluent with achene, apex glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Araújo, Ana C., et al. 2003. New unicapitate species of Rhynchospora (Cyperaceae) from South America. Brittonia. 55: 30-36.

description: This new species, with its lanceolate spikelets loosely disposed in small corymbs and with its slenderly linear leaves and culms, superficially resembles R. po,dosperma C. Wright. The character of its small, elliptic achenes, which bear callose thickenings proximally, places it in the neighborhood of R. brevirostris, a species that, however, shows a completely different superficial appearance. Although the achenes in these two species are similar in their grayish bony surfaces with a broad blackish longitudinal belt, as well as in having a pair of callose globular thickenings at the base, the new species clearly differs from R. brevirostris in its open corymbs and its much longer lanceolate spikelets, which are 7-9 mm long in contrast to the elliptic spikelets of R. brevirostris that range from 4 to 6 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Koyama, Tetsuo M. 1972. Two new species and a new section of Cyperaceae from Brazil. Brittonia. 24: 279-282.

description: Planta caespitosa gracilis perennis; culmi 10-15 cm alti; folia caulina plicata; laminae principales 70-130 x 0.7-1.5 mm; spiculae lanceoloideae, 4.1-4.9 x 0.8- 1 mm, aureo-brunneae, plerumque pedicellatae; setae nullae; achaenium lenticulare obovatum, 1.2-1.3 x 0.7-0.8 mm, subtiliter rugulosum; styli basis subulata vel anguste triangularis, 0.6-1 x 0.3-0.4 mm, utrinque sulcata vel obscure sulcata, ab achaenii apice distincta.

description: Slender, arching, caespitose perennial; stems 10-15 cm long. Leaves cauline, +/- evenly distributed along stem, the distal ones equalling to surpassing the inflorescence; largest blades 70-130 mm x 0.7-1.5 mm, plicate. Inflorescence of 2-4 open cymes; cymes ca 1-2 x 0.5-1 cm, of 2-7 spikelets each. Spikelets 4.1-4.9 x 0.8-1 mm, lan- ceoloid, usually pedicellate, golden brown. Hypogynous bristles absent. Achene 1.2-1.3 x 0.7-0.8 mm, deeply lenticular, obovate, finely rugulose. Style base 0.6-1 x 0.3-0.4 mm, subulate to narrowly triangular, sulcate or at least obscurely so on both sides, +/- raised and discontinuous with summit of achene.
bibliographicCitation: Thomas, William W. 1992. A synopsis of Rhynchospora (Cyperaceae) in Mesoamerica. Brittonia. 44: 14-44.
