description: Caespitose perennial; rhizome short, the culms and numerous basal leaves forming dense clumps; roots medium to coarse, brown. Culms ascending, 10-60 cm X 0.4- 0.9 mm, obtusely trigonous to compressed- trigonous or subterete, soft, flexuous, finely ribbed, channeled along one side distally, pale green, glabrous. Leaves ascending, numerous, primarily basal, 1-3 cauline, 6-40 cm long; sheaths quite long, particularly cauline ones, closely clasping culm, essentially eligulate, sometimes a faint rim of tis- sue present at adaxial junction of sheath and blade, herbaceous, finely ribbed, pale brown to stramineous proximally, glabrous, the inner band membranous on basal sheaths, herbaceous on upper cauline sheaths except for membranous orifice, with truncate to slightly concave orifice; blades narrowly linear, 0.3-1.1 mm wide (unfolded), V-shaped to subfolded or sometimes involute, firm, herbaceous, finely veined abaxially, smooth, glossy and minutely cellular-reticulate adaxially, light green or pale brown abaxially, green adaxially, glabrous, margins smooth proximally, antrorsely scabrous distally, the apex long-acuminate, triquetrous near tip. Inflorescence 1-3(-4) corymbose partial panicles from the upper sheathing bracts, panicles somewhat strict, the terminal panicle 1-6 X 1-2 cm, with 10-50 spikelets; sheathing bracts leaf-like, shorter and a little narrower than leaf blades, to 20 cm long; branches very slender and filiform, obtusely trigon- ous, flattened-trigonous or subterete in cross section; spikelets ovoid-ellipsoid, 2.5-3.2 X 0.6-1 mm, narrowly acute to acuminate at apex, becoming falcate with age, the scales spreading with maturing achenes; scales dorsally obtuse to rounded, herbaceous, distal scales of spikelet thinly herbaceous to submembranous, minutely cellular-striate, semi-glossy, reddish brown with slightly darker brown lineations, glabrous, margins narrowly scarious, slightly crisped, midcosta very fine, indistinct except at apex, prolonged beyond the narrowly acute to acuminate apex as a short mucro, lateral nerves indistinct; fertile scales 3-4, ovate-elliptic or widely ovate-elliptic to ovate-lanceolate, 1.6-2.7 X 0.9-1.4 mm; sterile scales 2-3 at base of spikelet, ovate- elliptic, 0.7-1.5 x 0.3-1.2 mm. Flowers bisexual; stamens 3, the anthers 0.8-1.2 mm long, minutely lobed at base, apiculate-papillate at apex, basifixed, thecae parallel, longitudinally dehiscent; style 2-branched, the branches equaling to 2/3 length of unbranched portion, long exserted from sub-tending scale, one branch often shorter than the other. Bristles absent. Achene biconvex, broadly rounded-obovate to depressed-obovate, 0.7-0.9 X 0.8-1 mm, truncate at apex, slightly narrowed to truncate or sub-rounded at short stipitate base, transversely rugose with 3-4(-5) coarse rugae on each face, narrowly cellular-reticulate along margins and at base, shining, glossy, red to reddish brown or brown; style base emphatically depressed-trigonous, oval-shaped from top view, unlobed, to 0.1(-0.2) mm long, often 0.1 mm long or less, 0.5-0.7 mm wide, dark brown or blackish.
bibliographicCitation: Strong, Mark T. 2000. A new species of Rhynchospora section Tenues Kükenthal (Cyperaceae) from Puerto Rico. Brittonia. 52: 241-245.

description: Planta perennis, glabra, rhizomatosa, rhizomate gracili, elongato, ramoso. Culmi erecti vel ascendentes, 11-16 cm alti. Corymbi 3-4, compacti, 8-14 mm longi, e 3-10 spiculis constantes. Setae 0.5- 1 mm longae, antrorsus scabratae. Corpus achaenii 1.7-2 x 1.3-1.4 mm, stramineum, leviter com- pressum, leviter transverse rugulosum, circacircum leviter longitudine striatum, basin versus vadose alveolatum, apice truncatum, annulatum. Basis styli late conica, cineracea, 0.54.6 mm longa.

description: Plant perennial, glabrous, rhizomatous. Rhizomes slender, elongate, branching. Roots slender. Culms erect to ascending, 11-16 cm tall, leafy, trigonous, the angles scabrellous and sharp. Basal leaves short, strongly imbricate, fibrillose, scale-like; principal foliage leaves erect or ascending, 11-15 cm long, mostly overtopping the inflorescence, gradually passing into bracteal leaves; blades narrowly linear, 1-1.3 mm wide, 5-10 times as long as the sheaths, plicate or involute, pale green; sheaths truncate, ventrally scarious. Corymbs 3-4, compact, 8-14 mm long, of 3-10 spikelets, lowermost long-pedunculate, the upper ones increasingly short- pedunculate; peduncles trigonous or flattened, scabrid. Spikelets 1-fruited, ovoid to ellipsoid or narrowly so, 4-5 x 1.5-1.8 mm, acuminate, reddish-brown. Sterile scales 3 or 4, lanceolate to ovate, ca 1.5-3.3 mm long, the lowermost cuspidate; fertile scales ovate, ca 3-3.7 mm long, glabrous, apically carinate, mucronate, marginally scarious, entire. Perianth bristles 6, 0.5-1 mm long, antrorsely sca- brous, ciliate basally. Stamens 3, anthers linear, ca 1.5 mm long; filaments ca 4 mm long. Achene body lenticular, obovate in outline, 1.7-2 x 1.3-1.4 mm, stramineous, transversely rugulose, peripherally lightly longitudinally striate, basally shallowly alveolate, apically annulate, thickened and truncate. Style base broadly conic, grayish, 0.5-0.6 mm long, slightly sunken in summit of achene; deciduous portion of style split ca halfway to base.

description: Planta perennis, valde rhizomatosa, Rhynchosporam candidam simulans; culmi erecti vel ascen- dentes, 60-85 cm alti; folia principalia 20-45 cm longa, 2-4 mm lata; corymbi 1-2, folia excedentes, diffusi, elongato-pedunculati, paucispiculati; spiculae lanceolatae, 7.3-11 x 2-3 mm, anguste acutae, eburneae; spicularum squamae fertiles anguste ovatae, 5-6 mm longae, mucronatae, apicem versus carinatae; antherae tres, 3 mm longae; styli basis triangularis, 0.9-2 mm alta, 1.3-1.7 mm lata, lunate decurrens; achaenium suborbiculare vel obovoideum, 2-2.3 x 1.5-1.8 mm, ? planoconvexum vel biconvexum, irregulariter transverse undulato-rugulosum, brunneum, late stipitatum.

description: Perennial with strong, stout, scaly rhizomes and coarse roots, 60-85 cm tall; culms slender, erect to ascending, smooth, subterete or obtusely triangular; leaves erect to ascending, mostly crowded toward culm base, 20-45 cm long; sheaths dark brown basally and sometimes hirsute; blades narrowly linear, 2-4 mm wide, flattened, attenuate, adaxially finely striate and sulcate along midrib, abaxially the midrib raised and strongest, the margins hirsute-ciliate to scabro-ciliate or rarely entire; inflorescence corymbose, of ca 8-30 spikelets total; corymbs 1-3, exceeding the leaves, diffuse, elongate-peduncled, of ca 4-10 spikelets each, the axis glabrous to sparsely hirsute; primary inflorescence branches somewhat spreading, basal branch 6-18 cm long, subsequent branches progressively reduced; lowest bracts leaflike, the distal bractlets lance-subulate and exceeded by spikelets; spikelets lanceoloid, 7.3-11 x 2-3 mm, narrowly acute, ivory-white; basal spikelet scales sterile, much shorter than fertile ones, lanceolate, carinate, narrowly acute; fertile scales ovate, 5-6 mm long, broadly acute to short-acuminate, carinate apically, the back rounded, the midcosta evident and included to short-excurrent; flowers perfect; perianth bristles absent; anthers 3, 3 mm long; style 2-branched at or slightly above the middle; style base triangular to deltate, somewhat compressed and 2-edged, 0.9-2 mm high, 1.3-1.7 mm broad at base, lunately decurrent on summit of achene; achene 2-2.3 x 1. 5-1.8 mm, subcircular to obovate in outline, +/- plano-convex to slightly biconvex, broadly stiped, margined, shiny brown to brownish-stramineous, irregularly and sometimes faintly transversely undulate rugulose.

description: Stems 25-110 cm. Largest blades 150- 300 mm x 1-2.5(4) mm. Inflorescence of 1-2(4) dense, fasciculate clusters of spikelets; terminal cluster 0.8-2 x 1-2.5 cm, simply fasciculate or corymbosely compound. Spikelets 3.7-4.7 x 1.1-1.5 mm, ellipsoid to ovoid, castaneous, the scale tips attenuate to aristate. Hypogynous bristles usually 5, longest ones 1/2 as long as to rarely equalling achene. Achene 1.2-1.6 x 1.1-1.4 mm, smooth and lustrous to very faintly cancellate, deep castaneous with paler, gold- en brown to stramineous disc. Style base 0.4-0.7 x 0.6-1 mm, deltate to broadly so, gray with pale ridge along interface with achene summit.

description: [Descr. amplif.] Herba perennis, rhizomate breve. Culmi solitarii vel laxe caespitosi, erecti, rigidi, 20-50 cm alti, 0.8-1.5 mm crassi, triquetri, pilis albis antrorsis dense pubescentes vel glabrescentes. Folia 5-8, radicalia; laminae lineares, 6-30 cm longae, 1/4-1/2 culmum aequantes, 1.5-4 mm latae, conduplicato-planae, laete virides, rigidae, ad apicem acutum sensim attenu- antes, supra glabrae, subtus ad margines costamque pilis albis antrorsis basi tuberculatis dense ciliatae; vaginae 1-3 cm longae, stramineo-virentes, 2-4 basilares squamiformes, brunneae, interdum leviter fibroso-solutae. Inflorescentia capitata; caput globosum vel hemisphaericum, 12-17 mm in diametro, castaneo-brunneum; bractea involucrantes 2-4, breviusculae, costa subtus et marginibus dense albociliatae, basi dilatatae, inferiores caput superantes, ima 2-4 cm longa. Spiculae multae, dense aggregatae, lanceolatae, 5.5-6.5 mm longae, ca 2 mm latae, de latere compressae, acutae, castaneo-brunneae, biflorae; flos inferior foemineus, superior masculus; glumae 6 vel 7, distiche dispositae, carinatae, plicatae, ovatae vel ovato-lanceolatae, apice acutae, 1-nerviae, chartaceae, castaneae, nitidulae, margine angustissime scarioso- pallescentes, inferiores 3 minores vacuae, quarta 3.2-3.5 mm longa fructifera, superiores 5-6 mm longa tenuiores. Achaenia obovata vel late obovata, 2-2.5 mm longa, 1.5-1.75 mm lata, de latere compressa, biconvexa, fulvo-castanea, laevia vel sparse tuberculata, basi subito con- tracta, apice annulata; stylopodium conicum vel depresso-conicum, 0.5-0.7 mm longum, basi 1/3 achaenium aequans, fulvescens; stylus filiformis, 6-8 mm longus, apice breviter bilobus vel sub-indivisus. description: Erect, reclining or climbing, 3-25 dm long; tubers 1-8 cm long and up to 1.5 cm thick; inflorescence a terminal raceme or open panicle of lateral racemes with rachises and pedicels short and stout, or long slender and flexuous; leaves glabrous, reniform to ovate in outline, 3-lobed, the lobes broad and shallowly toothed with broad blunt teeth, the lateral lobes sometimes 2-lobed; lowest leaves 4-10 cm wide, the cauline leaves becoming smaller upward (Fig. 1, a-d); stem glabrous; pedicels, or usually only their distal ends, pilose with straight and spreading hairs (Figs. 3, b-c); flowers pale to deep blue; helmet usually higher than long, 16-25 mm high and 15-20 mm long, rounded-conic and nearly vertical above the horizontal beak, or occasionally rounded above the scarcely-beaked apex (Fig. 4, b; 4, d, top); carpels 3, glabrous, pubescent or glabrate.

description: Planta perenne, 30-36 cm alta, caespitosa. Culmi 0.4-0.6 mm lati, quadrangulares. Folia 8. Involucrum bracteae capitulum parvulus. Capitulum digitatum. Spiculae 4-8, squamae ochraceae, marginibus albidis. Setae (4-)5, 2.5 mm longae. Achaenium obovatum, biconvexum apice tuberculatum, stylus basi 0.4 X 0.7 mm, pyramidalis.

description: Perennial, 30-40 cm tall, caespitose. Culms 0.4-0.6 mm wide, quadrangular, glabrous, not bulbous at base. Leaves 8; sheaths 0.7-1.5 cm long, not becoming fibrous with age, glabrous; blades 11-17 cm X 0.3-1.4 mm, half the height of the culm, linear, flat or conduplicate, the margins scabrous. Inflorescences capitate, subtended by 2 involucral bracts; involucral bracts similar to the spikelet scales, linear, conduplicate, stramineous; basal bract 2 X 1.6 mm, margins glabrous, the apex mucronate, 1 mm long; second bract similar to the first. Capitula 7-8 X 14 mm, digitate. Spikelets 5-8, 7-8.5 X 1.4-2 mm, linear, the basal 4 scales empty, followed by a single scale subtending a perfect flower and 5 distal scales subtending staminate flowers; distal empty scale 1.8 X 2.6 mm, broadly ovate, brown, the margins white, coriaceous, glabrous, the apex rounded; scale of the perfect flower 4 X 2.4 mm, ovate-lanceolate, convolute, brown, the margins white, coriaceous, glabrous, the apex acute; scales subtending staminate flowers brown, the margins white, the basal scale coriaceous, the others membranous, glabrous. Perianth bristles (4-)5, 2.5 mm long, equaling or surpassing the achene, plumose to near the apex, antrorsely scabrous apically. Anthers 3 mm long. Achenes 1.6-2 X 1-1.8 mm, obovoid, biconvex, brown, the surface smooth, the apex tuberculate, the margins prominent, smooth, straight and not cartilaginous; style base persistent, 0.4 X 0.7 mm, pyramidal, not confluent with the achene, apex glabrous.

description: Rhynchospora longibracteata is included in the newly conceived section Rigidifoliae with trepidation. Kukenthal (1949) grouped it with Rhynchospora consanguinea (Kunth) Boeckeler and related species in a new subsection of sect. Pluriflorae Kuk., subsect. Longibracteatae, corresponding to Bentham's sect. Asteroschoenus. It differs from species of sect. Asteroschoenus in its smooth achenes lacking hypogynous bristles and in its fully green involucral bracts. While its congested, head-like inflorescences, white spikelets, lack of hypogynous bristles, smooth achenes with simple triangular style bases, and geographical distribution are characteristic of the species of sect. Rigidifoliae, it is unusual in having three stamens. Its compressed, 2-3-flowered spikelets are similar to those found in the other members of sect. Rigidifoliae and are discordant with other sections in which it might be placed, including sect. Dichromena.

description: Perennial, 80-120 cm tall, caespitose. Culms 1-1.5 mm wide, quadrangular, glabrous, the base not bulbous. Leaves 8-12; sheaths 4-6 cm long, entire or becoming fibrous with age, glabrous; blades 40-55 cm X 2-2.5 mm, half the height of the culm, linear-lanceolate, conduplicate, glabrous. Inflorescences capitate, subtended by 0-1 involucral bracts; involucral bracts 4 X 2 mm, similar to the spikelet scales, lanceolate, conduplicate, brown, ciliate, the apex acute. Capitula 12-16 X 10-14 mm, oblong. Spikelets 100-150, 4-4.5 X 2 mm, oval, the basal 3 scales empty, followed by a single scale subtending a perfect flower and 4-5 distal scales subtending staminate flowers; distal empty scale 2.5 X 2.5 mm, oval, brown, chaffy, the keel scabrous, the apex wrinkled; scale of the perfect flower 3.5 X 3 mm, broadly ovate, convolute, brown, coriaceous, glabrous, the apex wrinkled and mucronate; scales of staminate flowers brown, the basal one coriaceous, the others membranous, glabrous. Perianth bristles 5, 1-1.8 mm long, surpassing the achene, plumose from the base to near the apex, the apex summit antrorsely scabrous. Anthers 2 mm long. Achenes 1.5 X 1.2 mm, widely elliptical, biconvex, dark, the surface smooth and shiny, the margins not prominent, smooth, straight and not cartilaginous; style base persistent, 0.2 X 0.4 mm, conic, confluent with the achene, apex glabrous.

description:
Sporophore solitary to gregarious or concrescent. Pileus up to 10 cm broad, plane to depressed, tomentose soon collapsing and becoming matted, glabrous at disc in mature material, usually colliculose, often pitted or scrobiculate, pileoli rarely present, radially rugose, white (6A1) at margin from actively growing tomentum or entirely so in immature collections, orange (6A6) to deep orange (6A8) or tangerine (6B8), bruising black; context up to 7 mm thick, duplex, zonate, elastic when fresh, hard to woody when dry, concolorous; taste unpleasant; odor slightly disagreeable. Stipe up to 3 x 1.5 cm, central, terete or attenuate below with bulbous base, spongy tomentose, becoming matted, concolorous. Spines up to 4 mm long, decurrent to a line, crowded, white (5A1) at active growing areas, to cognac (6E7) towards disc. Chemical reactions: context tissue darkening to brown or black in KOH or NH4OH.

Pileus trama hyphae up to 4 µm diam, uninflated, interwoven in subsurface layer, parallel below, clamps not seen; gloeoplerous-like hyphae up to 7 µm diam. Stipe hyphae up to 6 µm, uninflated, interwoven in subsurface layer, parallel below, clamps not seen; gloeoplerous-like hyphae up to 7 µm diam. Spine trama hyphae up to 6 µm diam, uninflated, clamps not seen. Basidia 35-48 x 8-11 µm (x = 8.24 + 0.51 x 10.34 ± 0.82 µm), clavate, clamps not seen, 4-spored; sterigmata up to 6 µm long (x = 5.25 ± 0.43 µm). Basidiospores 5.5-8 (9.3) x 5.5-6.5 (7) µm (X = 8.24 ± 0.51 x 6.19 ± 0.42 µm), subglobose, brownish; ornamentation tuberculate (Fig. IA), prominent, flattened to exsculpate.
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert & Thomas, W. 1986. Two new species of Rhynchospora (Cyperaceae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 38: 210-215.

description: Rhizomatous perennial. Rhizomes descending, ca 4-5 mm in diameter. Culms ± erect, ca 60-100 cm tall, angled, puberulent. Leaves basal and cauline, plicate or doubly folded ("M" shaped in cross section), the midrib and ca 10-20 lateral veins evident; larger basal leaves ca 40-100 cm long, 2.6-3.1 cm wide; cauline leaves usually 4 (rarely 2), the lowest ones approaching size of basal leaves, upper ones gradually passing into bracteal leaves; leaf sheaths puberulent. Inflorescence a series of 2-4 separate (at least the lower ones) panicles with ca 25-150 spikelets each, the branches puberulent; terminal panicle largest, 3-6 cm long and wide. Mature spikelets ovoid, 2.5-3.7 x 1.4-2 mm, usually with 2 fruits; scales pale stramineous with very fine striations, often spread apart and partially revealing achenes; sterile scales usually 3, rudimentary at base, the inner ones approaching fertile scales in size; fertile scales decreasing in size upward, the larger ones ovate, cucullate, 2.8-3.5 x 1-1.3 mm. Stamens 3; filaments 2.5-3 mm long; anthers 1.4-1.8 mm long. Hypogynous bristles usually 6, falling easily, minutely antrorsely barbed, most reaching the apex of the style base in length. Achene lenticular, obovate in outline, 1.5-1.8 x 0.8-1.1 mm, stramineous to golden-brown, longitudinally papillose to punctate; style base triangular, 1-1.8 mm long, 0.3-0.8 mm wide at base.

description: Perennial, robust, cespitose plant; rhizome vertical, lignified; culms 1-1.5 m tall, 2.5-4 mm wide, erect, trigonous, canaliculate, slightly scabrous on the angles. Basal leaves numerous, the sheath stramineous to green, 2-12 cm long, the contraligule membranaceous; blade conduplicate, 90 X 1.5- 3 cm, spongy; mesophyll with air cavities well developed, mostly rectangular in outline, filled with stellate cells; cauline leaves 8-9, the blade coriaceous, scabrous on the midrib and margins. Inflorescence a narrow compound of dense hemispheric to globose heads 3-6 cm diam., the peduncles 1.5-9 cm long; rays of first and second order 6- 8, developed, 6-8 cm long, scabrous, greatly contracted, forming 8-20(-50) heads in spikelets or anthelate; secondary and tertiary rays with fascicles of 7-25 spikelets; bracts leaflike, hardly longer than terminal inflorescence; prophylls slightly scabrous. Spikelets lanceolate, 10-11 X 2-3 mm when fruit mature; fertile scale 5-7(-10) mm long, membranous; only one flower bisexual; stamens 3; style undivided; bristles 5 or 6, subequal, 7-8 mm long, the margins antrorse-scabrous, strongly dilated at base; distal flower of a spikelet staminate. Achene obovoid, complanate, 4.8-5.5 mm X 2.6- 3.6 mm, brown, with a central concavity on both faces, slightly granulated, the upper border shaped like an inverted "U," the apical margins and sides with spinulose projections, the base short stipitate; style persistent, sulcate, antrorsely scabrous, the base subulate, 9-11 mm long X 0.8-1.1 mm, undulated.

description: Slender, caespitose, glabrous perennial; stems 15-55 cm long. Leaves mostly basal or from near base, plicate; largest blades 7- 20 cm x 1.2-2.8 mm. Inflorescence a series of 2-4, +/- congested to open cymes with ascending branches, the branches terminat- ing in 1-several spikelets; terminal cyme ca 1.2-4 x 0.6-4 cm. Spikelets 3-4 x 1-1.5 mm, ellipsoid to ovoid, castaneous to fer- rugineous. Hypogynous bristles usually 6, 20-67% the length of the achene, antrorsely scabrous. Achenes 1.4-1.7 x 0.9-1.2 mm, lenticular, obovate, stramineous to pale stramineous, transversely rugulose. Style base 0.3-0.5 x 0.4-0.7 mm, deltate to broadly so, clearly distinct on summit of achene, not confluent.

description: Cespitose perennial with knotted rhizomes; culms erect, 10-35 cm tall, compressed terete with a shallow groove on one face. Leaves basal or cauline near base, half as long to rarely equalling culm in length, 1.3-1.8 mm wide. Inflorescence paniculate of 2-4 partial panicles, +/- congested with ascending spikelets, 1.5-4 x 0.7-1.5 cm, of ca 15-60 spikelets. Spikelets lanceoloid, 5- 5.5 x 0.7-1 mm, castaneous. Hypogynous bristles 3, antrorsely scabrous, equalling or slightly exceeding achene. Achene elliptic, lenticular, 1.2-1.5 x 0.7-0.9 mm, castaneous to stramineous, shiny, short-stipitate, the surface longitudinally cancellate. Style base triangular, 1.3-2 mm long, 0.5-0.6 mm  wide at base, the basal edge ridged and pronounced on slightly constricted summit of achene.

description: Frutex scandens, glaber, terrestris vel epiphyticus, ramis pendulis, teretibus, ultimis eirciter 1.5 mm. diametro, aliquando radicibus ferentibus, internodiis 2-7 cm. longis; foliis oppositis, vivo ut videtur plus minusve carnosis, sieco chartaceo-coriaceis, plerumque supra olivaceis, subtus brunneis, utrinque minutissime subverruculosis, integris, oppositis, oblongo-ellipticis, 5-10 cm. longis, 2-4.5 cm. latis, basi late acutis, apice graciliter acute subcaudato-acuminatis, acuminibus 1.5-2 cm. longis, nervis lateralibus obscurissimis, aliquando obsoletis vel subobsoletis; petiolo 5-10 mm. longo; infloreseentiis axillaribus terminalibusque, pedunculatis, 1-floris, pedunculo 0.5-2 cm. longo, apice bibracteatis, bracteis lanceolatis, longe acuminatis, ad 1.5 cm. longis, pedicellis 7-10 mm. longis; floribus rubris, extus glabris, eirciter 4 cm. longis, leviter curvatis; sepalis liberis vel subliberis, lineari-lanceolatis, 6-7 mm. longis, eirciter 1 mm. latis, obtusis, glabris; corollae tubo eirciter 4 cm. longo, extus glabro, cylindrico, leviter curvato, deorsum eirciter 2 mm. diametro, supra medio plus niinusve ampliato et ad 3.5 mm. diametro, limbo leviter bilabiato; labio superiori 2-lobato, inferiori 3-lobato, lobulis omnibus subellipticis, rotundatis, margine distanter brevissime capitato-ciliatis, binis superioribus eirciter 4.5 mm. longis, trinis inferioribus paullo latioribus (ad 4 mm.) et 5.5-6 mm. longis; filamentis glabris vel subglabris, exsertis, antheris ellipticis, 1.7 mm. longis; stylis exsertis, consperse brevissime (0.3 mm.) capitato-ciliatis; capsulis cylindraceis, 11-12 cm. longis, longe stipitatis, acuminatis, eirciter 2 mm. diametro; seminibus (cum pilis) 5 mm. longis.

description: Tree, or large wide-spreading shrub often forming denise thickets; height to 12 m and to 3 (rarely 15) dm in diameter. Bark light gray or nearly white, smooth. Twig pale reddish-brown when young, glabrous; buds acute, resinotis. Leaf with 5 (4-7) leaflets on a petiole 1-12 cm long. Leaflets 7-17 cm long anid 2-6 cm wide, ovate-lanceolate, elliptical-oblong, oblong-lanceolate; apex acuminate; base subcordate, rounded, truncate, acute to acuminate; margin sharply serrulate; lower surface glabrous, slightly glaucous, with short white hairs on the veins; upper surface glabrous and dark green; petiolule 0.5-3 cm long, with scattered white hairs. Infloreseence narrow-columnar, 8-20 cm long, tomentose. Flower on pubescent pedical 3-10 nun long. Calyx 5-8 mm long, campanulate-tubular, lavender-gray to pink or purpiish, villous; sepals 5, variously united into 1 or 2 lips. Corolla of 4 or 5 petals, nearly white to light pink; upper and lateral petals 12-18 mm long, subequal, slightly spreading; claws shorter than the calyx, villous; blades oblong-obovate, obtuse, the surface and margins villous and eglandular; fifth petal usually small when present. Stamenls 5-7, unequal, 18-30 mm long, exserted, loniger in the staminate flower; filaments arcuate, purplish to white, glabrous; anthers bright orange, glabrous, glandular at the apex and base of the locules. Fertile pistil with style longer than the stamens, villous. Fruit obovoid, 5-8 cm in diameter; pericarp thin, glabrate, tomentulose or canescent, pale brown; seeds usually 1, pale orange-brown, 4-5 cm in diameter.

description: Shrub or small tree to 6 m tall and 15 cm in diameter. Bark smooth or slightly scaly with thin plates, or with thin furrows and light gray. Twig light reddish-brown when young, becoming gray, puberulous, at first glaucous; buds ovate and acute. Leaf of 7-11 leaflets; petiole 5-14 cm long. Leaflets 5-16 cm long, 1-3 (rarely 5) cm wide, elliptic-lanceolate, lanceolate, or very rarely obovate-lanceolate; apex acute or long-acuminate; base acute, acuminate, or cuneate; margin sharply and unequally serrate, often doubly (and irregularly) serrate, entire at the base; upper surface yellow-green and glabrous; lower surfaee pale, puberulous to tomentose; petiolule slender, 0-10 mm long, glabrate or puberulous. Calyx with 5 sepal lobes acute, obtuse or rounded, subequal (the lateral sepals often acute) ; the other three obtuse or rounded). Corolla 9-17 mm long; upper petals with the villous claw equaling the spatulate blade in length; lateral petals slightly shorter and wider than the upper pair, spatulate, the claw less than half of the petal length. Stamens 13-21 mm long. Fruit echinate with more or less deciduous tuberculate spines (or occasionally lacking spines completely), light or dark brown.
bibliographicCitation: Hardin, James W. 1957. A revision of the Americana Hippocastanaceae--II. Brittonia. 9: 173-195.

description: Large tree 20-30 m tall and with a diameter up to 1.5 m. Bark brown-gray wvhen young, becoming gray, densely furrowed and broken into large scaly plates, the surface roughened with numerous small scales (large plates on trees with diameter greater than 3 dm). Twig orange-brown at first, becoming gray-brown, smooth or gray-tomentose; buds obtuse, with scales rounded on the back, minutely apiculate and ciliate on the margins; scars large with many bundle scars in a triangle. Leaf with 5-7 deciduous leaflets; petiole 8-19 cm long, glabrous to tomentose. Leaflets 10-21 cm long, 4-8 cm wide, obovate-oblong to elliptic-obovate; apex ac-uminate, sometimes abruptly so; base cuneate; margin more or less equally serrate; upper surface dark green, glabrous or glabrescent; lower surface dull, glabrous with a few hairs on the veins or densely tomelntose; petiolule 2-3(4) mm long, glabrous to tomentose. Infloreseence oblong, 10-15 cm long, pubescent. Flowers pale to deep yellow, the claws very deep rich yellow changing to red-brown at anthesis; pedicel 4-8 mm long, stipitate-glandular or glandular-villous, the glands to 2 mm long and often black. Calyx 7-10 mm long, campanulate or tubular-campanulate, glandular-pubescent on the surface and margin, the longer glands of the pedicel often on the lower third of the calyx; sepal-lobes 5, rounded or obtuse. Corolla of 4 unequal petals, the claws villous and involute at the top, the blades glandular-pubescent oln the surface, and villous on the margin; upper petals 20-30 mm long, the claw 16-25 mm long, the blade minute and spatulate; lateral petals 16-25 mm long, the claw 8-15 mm long (longer than the calyx), the blade obovate or nearly roulnd and subeordate at the base. Stamens 7 or 8, 15-20 mnm long, included; filaments straight or arcuate, subulate or filiform, the lower half villouis; anther glabrous, glandular at the apex and base of the locules. Fertile pistil equal to or longer than the lateral petals, villous except for the stigma. Fruit subglobose, 5-8 cm in diameter; pericarp thin or thick, smooth or slightly pitted, pale brown; seeds 1-3 (rarely 4-6), chestnut-brown with a large pale hilum.
bibliographicCitation: Hardin, James W. 1957. A revision of the Americana Hippocastanaceae--II. Brittonia. 9: 173-195.

description: Shrub or small tree, 1-6 m tall and to 2 dm in diameter. Bark gray to nearly white on old trunks, smooth. Twig light gray, glabrous to slightly pubescent; buds not resinous. Leaf with 5-7 leaflets (rarely 3, or 1 by reduction of the lateral leaflets) ; petiole 1-10 cm long. Leaflets subeoriaceous, 3-12 cm long, 2-4 cm wide, obovate, oblong-obovate or oblong-elliptic; apex obtuse, broadly acute or rounded; base obtuse; margins entire to slightly repand; lower surface light-brown-tomentulose to dense-tomentose or woolly; upper surface green and glabrous or with scattered hairs; petiolule 0-5 mm long. Inflorescence narrow-columnar, 5-20 cm long, glabrous or with short tomentum. Flower with pedicel 4-6 mm long and tomentulose. Calyx campanulate, 4-9 mm long, tomentosevillous with stipitate glands; sepals fused to only half of their length, the lobes obtuse and subequal. Corolla cream-white, with its base orange, changing to maroon at anthesis. Petals 4 or 5, glandular-villous on the surface and glandular on the margin; upper pair 9-18 mm long, the claw with laciniate appendages (or a crest) at the top and strongly reflexed at this point, the blade obovate, acute or obtuse; lateral pair 8-11 mm long, erect or slightly spreading, not reflexed; fifth petal abortive or of variable size when present. Stamens 6-8, 10-20 mm long, aseending, exserted; filaments white, glabrous; anthers bright orange, glabrous, glandular at the apex and base of the locules. Fertile pistil glandular-villous on the ovary and villous on the style, 10-23 mm long. Fruit obovate to spherical, 2-3 cm in diameter; pericarp thin, tomentose, somewhat tubereulate (not spiny), light brown; seeds 1-3, 1-1.5 cm in diameter, dark brown to nearly black, the hilum white or light buff, 3-4 mm across.

description: Spreading shrub or small tree to 5 m tall and 10 cm in diameter. Bark light gray, smooth. Twig light tan, turning gray, glabrous; buds light brown. Leaf of 5 or 7 leaflets on a glabrous petiole 5-18 cm long. Leaflets 8-27 cm long and 3-11 cm wide. elliptic to oblong-obovate; apex acaminate or prolonged-acuminate; base round, obluse, or aeute; margin crenate-serrulate or serrate; lower surface commonly gray-toinentose, or glabreseent; petiolule glabrous or puberulous, 0.5-3 cm long. Infloreseence 20-30 cm long, narrowly cloumnar, glabrous. Flowers white, on a glabrous pedicel 4-8 mm long. Calyx campanulate-tubular, 4-7 mm long; sepals 5, unequal, the surface and margin villous (with simple and branched hairs), eglandular, the lobes obtuse. Corolla of 4 or 5 petals, 10-19 mm long; petals nearly similar, erect, divergent, long-clawed, the blade ovate, obovate, oblong, or spatulate, and truncate-emarginate at the apex; surface and margins with few hairs mostly papillose; fifth petal small or similar to the lateral petals or absent. Stamens 6-7, 25-40 mm long, straight, erect; filaments gYlabrous, pinkish white; anthers orange-red or yellow-red, glabrous, with only a slight indication of a glandular apex or base of the locules. Fertile pistil 30-35 mm long, villous (or with reddish, short tomentum) except for the stigma. Fruit obovoid, subglobose, 2.5-4 cm long; pericarp smooth, pale brown; seeds chestnutbrown, 1 or 2 per capsule.

description: Shrub or small tree 1-4 (rarely to 12) mn tall and to 2(5) dmn in diameter. Bark brown-gray to light gray, smooth. Twig reddish-brown; buds obtuse, broad ovoid, 1 cm long, with scales round-apiculate. Leaf with 5 or 7 leaflets; petiole 3-17 cm long, glabrous or pubescent. Leaflets 6-17 cm long, 3-6 cm wide, oblong, obovate, narrowly elliptic, lanceolate, or oblanceolate, membranaceous to subcoriaceous with veins deeply impressed above; apex aeuminate to abruptly acuminate; base acuminate or acute; margin irregularly serrate or crenate-serrate, entire at the base; upper surface glabrous with a few scattered hairs on the mailn veilns; lower surfaee glabrous to densely toluentose, a dull or bright green oftenl with reddish midrib and secolndary veins; petiolule 1-19 mm long, glabrous or pubescent. Infloreseence oblong, 10-25 cm long. Flower typically red, often yellowish-red, or yellow in the westernimost populations of central Texas; petal-claws yellow, turning maroon at ailthesis; pedicel 5-12 mm lonlg, usually very slender, short-tomentose, eglandular. Calyx 8-18 mm long, tubular-campanulate or tubular with a gibbous base, villous with scattered stipitate glands; sepal-lobes 5, rounded, glandular-pubescent, irregular in size (the upper and two lateral lobes longest, or the upper aild two lower longest). Corolla glandular-pubeseent on the surface and glandular (with or without a few small hairs) on the margin; upper petals 25-40 mm long, the claw 19-23 mm long and villous, the blade minute, oblong-obovate to suborbicular; lateral petals 20-31 mm long, the claw 10-17 mm long (more or less the length of the calyx), villous, the blade oblong-obovate. Stamens 6-8, 23-36 mm long, often slightly exserted beyond the upper petals; filaments villous on the lower half; anthers smooth, with a few hairs at top and bottom, very slightly glandular at the apex and base of the locules. Fertile pistil villous except for the stigma, the style equial to the stamens in length or 2-4 mm beyond the upper petals. Fruit subglobose to obovoid, 3.5-6 em in diameter; pericarp smooth; slightly pitted, light brown; seeds 2-3 cm in diameter, 1-3 or rarely 4-6, dark chestnut-browin or pale yellowbrown with a pale hilum.

description: Small tree to 15 m tall and 5-25 cm in diameter, or usually a small shrub 1-3 m tall. Bark dark gray to light gray, the surface separating into small thin plates. Twig light reddish-brown, glabrous; buds ovate, aeute or obtuse, 7-8 mm long, light brown, the scales short apiculate. Leaf with 5 or 7 leaflets; petiole 8-18 cm long, glabrous or slightly pubeseent. Leaflets 8-20 cm long, 3-7 cm wide, oblong-obovate, lanceolate, oblanceolate, or elliptic; apex acuminate to prolonged-acuminate; base aeute to acuminate; margin singly or doubly serrate, or irregularly crenate-serrate; surface glabrous (with few hairs on the veins) to tomentose, yellow-green above and green below; petiolule 3-12 mm long, puberulous. Infloreseence narrow or broad, pyramidal, 10-15 cm long, pubescent. Flower typically yellow, but often reddish; pedicel 3-5 mm long, puberulous to tomentose. Calyx 7-15 mm long, campanulate or tubular-campanulate, tomentose, a few glands on the surface or eglandular, the margin puberulous and eglandular; sepal lobes 5, oblong-obovate, narrow and rounded or obtuse. Corolla with claws and blade-margins villous, the blade-surfaces densely glandular and with few hairs; upper petals 25-37 mm long, the claws 21-32 mm long and equaling the lateral petals or longer, the blade minute and obovate or spatulate; lateral petals 20-30 mm long, the claws 10-18 mm long (exceeding the calyx), the blade broad and obovate, nearly round, often subcordate at the base. Stamens 6 or 7, 18-30 (rarely 15) mm long, included; filaments villous on the lower half; anthers smooth, glandular at the apex and slightly glandular at the base of the locules. Fertile pistil equal to or slightly exceeding the stamens, villous except for the stigma. Fruit globose, 2.5-4 cm in diameter; periearp thin, slightly pitted, light brown; seeds globose, or irregular, 1-3, rarely 4-6, dark chestnut-brown.

description: Herb; stems erect, to 60 cm tall, terete to slightly 4-angled, simple or rarely branched from the base, glabrous. Leaves opposite, sessile; blade linear-lanceolate, 2-5 cm long, 2-4 mm wide, glabrous, subcoriaceous, violet tinged, the base slightly narrowed, the margin entire, the apex acute, the midvein prominent. Flowers in a terminal raceme; bracts linear, 5-12 mm long, 1 mm wide; pedicel 2-5 mm long, glabrous, ebracteolate; calyx campanulate, obscurely 5-veined, glabrous, the tube 3 mm long, the lobes broadly triangular, 2-3 cm long, the apex obtuse; corolla funnelform, light purple, 1.6-1.9 mm long, 3 mm wide at the base, 1.8-2.1 cm wide at the mouth, externally villous, the lobes subequal, ovate, ciliate, 5-7 mm long, 8-11 mm wide; stamens didynamous, the filaments 8-10 mm long and 13- 15 mm long, glabrous, the anthers 4-5 mm long, divaricate, mucronate, slightly villous; ovary ovoid, the style 1.3-1.6 mm long, glabrous. description: Suffruticose herb; stems to 40 cm tall, 4-angled, scabrous, brittle, glabrescent below. Leaves opposite, sessile to short petiolate, narrowly ovate to ovate, 2-3.5 cm long, 6-11 mm wide, scabrous, the base narrowed, the margin entire, slightly revolute, the apex obtuse to rounded. Flowers in short racemes; bracts foliose; pedicels 1.2-1.8 cm long, glabrous; calyx tubular-campanulate, 10-nerved, glabrous, the tube 8-10 mm long, 10-12 mm wide at the mouth, the lobes triangular, 5-7 mm long, 4 mm wide at the base, recurved; corolla pale pink with white at the base, spotted with pale brown and deeper pink inside, tubular-campanulate, 2-2.5 cm long, 6 mm wide at the base, 18 mm wide at the mouth, externally villous, the lobes glabrous, ciliate, the upper lobes rounded, 8 mm long, 12 mm wide, the lateral lobes broadly ovate, 6 mm long, 13 mm wide, the median lobe ovate to rounded, 10 mm long, 7-10 mm wide; stamens 4, didynamous, 1.7-2.3 cm long, included, glabrous; ovary glabrous, the style 2.5 cm long. description: Herb; rhizome thick, woody; stems clustered, to 50 cm long, terete to slightly 4-angled, sparsely puberulous, glabrescent. Flowers in terminal racemes; bracts foliose; pedicels solitary, 1.3-1.5 cm long, puberulous; calyx campanulate, 5-nerved, glabrous, the tube 5-7 mm long, the lobes triangular, 5-6 mm long, acuminate, internally pubescent at the base; corolla pink to rose-pink, with 2 yellow lines and dark spots within, campanulate-funnelform, 2.5-4 cm long, 4 mm wide at the base, 16 mm wide at the mouth, externally villous, the lobes ovate-oblong, glabrous to villous, ciliate, the upper lobes 10-12 mm long, 8 mm wide, the lateral lobes 9-10 mm long, 8-9 mm wide, the median lobe 8-9 mm long, 7-8 mm wide; stamens 4, didynamous, 1.8-2.4 mm long, glabrous to slightly pubescent below, the anthers awned, 5 mm long, glabrous; ovary glabrous, the style 2.5 cm long, the stigma unequally bifid. description: Perennial herb; stems erect, to 1 m tall, terete to slightly 4-angled, with many short lateral branches bearing short leaves, glabrous. Leaves opposite, sessile; blade linear, 9-15 mm long, 0.5-1.5 mm wide, sparsely strigose above, glabrous below, the base narrowed, the margin entire, often with silicifications, the apex acute, only the midvein visible. Capsule ovoid, 7-8 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, brown; seeds unknown.

description: Species A. pensili Airy Shaw affinis, differt nerviis primariis utrinque distinctis, subtus foliis consperse longe ciliato-villosis, floribus flavidis, corollae tubo intus omnino albido-villoso. description: Tree, to 12 m tall. Twigs somewhat angular, glabrous or with some minute appressed hairs when young. Terminal buds densely whitish pubescent. Leaves alternate, chartaceous, 12-18 x 6-9 cm, elliptic, apex acute or shortly acuminate, base acute, gla- brous and opaque on both surfaces, lateral veins 6-8, arching upwards and loop-connected, midrib impressed on upper surface, otherwise venation immersed and scarcely visible; midrib raised, lateral veins and ter- tiary venation slightly raised on lower leaf surface. Petioles canaliculate, 6-9 mm long. Inflorescences about as long as the leaves, on leafless short shoots, these ca. 0.6 cm long, glabrous or with few hairs toward the flowers. Flowers creamy. Tepals 6, equal, outside sparsely appressed pubescent, inside more densely pubescent, ca. 1.5 mm long. Stamens 9, all 2-celled, outer 6 introrse, inner 3 extrorse, ca. 1 mm long, the filament pubescent; filaments of inner 3 stamens with 2 large glands near the base; staminodia 3, ca. 0.7 mm long, the base densely pubescent. Pistil 1.5 mm long, glabrous, the ovary gradually narrowed into the style. Receptacle shallow, densely pubescent inside. Fruits unknown.

description: Small trees or shrubs, the stems with minute stellate hairs, these stipitate or subsessile. Leaf blades broadly ovate, to 16 cm long, 11 cm wide, basally obtuse, irregularly crenate, acute, palmately 5-nerved, discol- orous, the upper surface sparsely stellate pubescent, the lower surface velutinous, densely stellate-tomentose, the veins prominent; petioles to 9 cm long, with indument like that of stems; stipules filiform, ca. 5 mm long, caducous. Flowers grouped in axillary fascicles, subumbellate; pedicels 2-3.5 cm long, articulate in the upper third, stellate- tomentulose; calyx campanulate, ecostate, 4-5 mm long, the lobes deltate, 2-2.5 mm long, the outer surface stellate-tomentulose, the inner surface glabrous, with a basal nec- tariferous disk ca. 1 mm in diameter composed of 5 nectaries; petals asymmetrically emarginate, 8 mm long, 6 mm wide, biauriculate, the outer surface minutely stellate-tomentose, the inner surface glabrous, the auricles densely stellate-tomentose; staminal column ca. 3 mm long, densely stellate-tomentose at the base; styles 5, ca. 5 mnm long, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 4 mm long, 3 mm wide, muticous, apically dehiscent, trigonal in cross-section, the apex and dorsal wall densely stellate-tomentose; seeds solitary, reniform, with scattered simple hairs at the apex.

description: Plants 5-34 cm high; leaves oblong in general outline, the blades 2.8-10 cm lolng, 0.9-5 cm broad, 1-2 pinnate, the pinnae broadly oblong to ovate or orbieu- lar, distinct or confluent, pinnately lobed and usually spinulose-dentate, 0.4-1 cm longr, 0.5-1.5 cm broad, occasionally puberulent on the veins; petioles 3-13.2 cm long; peduncles 10-34 cm long, longer than the leaves, occasionally puberulent at the base of the umbel; bracts of involuere usually wanting; rays 6-17, 0.3-3.1 cm long, the longest rays 1-3.1 cm long, sometimes puberulent; bractlets of the involueel laneeolate to linear, 1.5-4 mm long, membranaeeous and sometimes ciliate, the apex acute or acuminate, usually connate at the base; pedicels 1-2 mm long; calyx-teeth 0.5-1 min long; fruits in each umbellet 8-17, oblong, 3-6 mm long, 0.9-2.8 mmn broad, the dorsal and lateral ribs corky-winged, the wings usually shilny-yellow; vittae 1 in the intervals, 2 on the commissure, an accessory vitta present in each of the ribs.

description: Plants 10-36 cm high; leaves narrowly oblong in general outline, the blades 3.5-14 cm long, 1-3.5 cm broad, bipinnate, the ultimate divisions rigid, acute, 1-6 mm long, 1-2.5 mm broad, mostly confluent, appearing as lobes of a sub-cuneate pinna; petioles 3-12 cm long; peduncles 9-25 cm long; bracts of in- voluere usually wantin-g; rays 6-16 ,ascending, conspicuously unequal, the longest rays 3.4-6 em lonlg; bractlets of inv-olueel dimidiate, linear-lanceolate, entire, 3-15 mm long, usually longer than the flowers; pedicels 9-18, unequal, the longest pedicels 3-10 nmm long; calyx-teeth very conspicuous, oblong-lanceolate, 1-3.5 mm long; fruit niarrowly oblong, 3-6 mm long, 2-3.5 mm broad, lateral ribs sometimes shortly winged, the dorsal shorter than the lateral or obsolete; vittae one in the intervals, very rarely 2 or 3 in one of the intervals, 2, very rarely 3, on the commissure, accessory vittae absent.

description: Plantae caespitosae acaules vel caulescentes scaberulae 1-4 dm altae; foliis ternato-pinnatisectis 3-12 cm longis, 3-15 cm latis, foliolis ovatis vel ovato-lanceolatis pinnatim lobatis vel pinnatifidis, 0.5-4 cm longis, 0.2-4 cm latis; pedunculis 6-15 cm longis, foliis longioribus; involucro 0; radiis 4- 7, 1.5-3 cm longis inaequalibus; involucelli bracteolis lineari-acuminatis; pedicellis 10-20, 3-5 mm longis; calycis dentibus evidentibus triangulari-ovatis; petalis viridi-albis; stylis tenuibus, ca 2 mm longis; fructibus in umbellula quoque 2-6, oblongis vel ovoideo-oblongis, 6 mm longis, 3 mm latis, costis prominentibus suberosisque exalatis; vittis tenuibus plerumque in intervallis 3, in commissuris 2 et in costis solitariis.

description: Plants apparently cespitose from a branching root crown bearing old leaf sheaths, acaulescent or with 1 or 2 stem leaves, 1-4 dm tall, slightly scaberulous on foliage and inflorescence, or glabrate; leaves petiolate, ovate to ovate-lanceo- late, the blades 3-12 cm long, 3-15 cm broad, ternate-pinnately compound, the leaflets ovate to lanceolate, 0.5-4 cm long, 0.2-4 cm broad, usually pinnately lobed to pinnatifid with oblong to lanceolate, mucronulate ultimate divisions, scaberulous on veins beneath; petioles 3-15 cm long, scarious-sheathing at base; peduncles 6-15 cm long, longer than leaves, scaberulous at base of umbel; in- volucre usually 0; rays 4-7, unequal, 1.5-3 cm long, spreading-ascending, sca- berulous; bractlets of involucel 2-8, linear-acuminate, scarious- and scaberulous- margined, free to slightly connate at base; pedicels 10-20, 3-5 mm long, unequal; calyx lobes evident, triangular-ovate; petals greenish-white, narrowly ovate with a narrower inflexed apex; styles very slender, ca 2 mm long, flexuous; stylopodium 0; carpophore parted to the base, divergent in upper 1/3; fruits in each umbellet 2-6, oblong to oblong-oval, 6 mm long, 3 mm broad, the ribs subequally prominent and corky, but unwinged; vittae rather small, mostly 3 in intervals, 2 on commissure, and 1 in apex of each rib; seed subterete in transection, the face plane.

description: Plants 2-10 cm high; leaves oblong in general outline, the blades 1.8-3.2 cm long, 1-2 cm broad, 1-2 pinnate, the pinnae obovate to ovate-oblong, acute, confluent in the bipinnate leaves, appearing as lobes of the pinnae, 1-2 lobed, 7-15 mm long, 0.5-6 cm broad; peduncles 0.8-4 cm long, shorter than the leaves, sometimes puberulent at the base of the umbel; bracts of involucre usually wanting; rays 3-5, spreading, equal or unequal, 2.3-3.3 cm long, mostly glabrous; bractlets of the involueel linear, 3.5-4 mm long, acute, free, sometimes ciliate; pedicels 5-7, 1-2 mm long; calyx-teeth linear, about 1 mm long; fruit oblong to ovoid-oblong, 2-4.5 mm long, 0.8-2 mm broad, the ribs obscure, the vittae one in the intervals, 2 on the commissure, accessory vittae absent.
bibliographicCitation: Theobald, William L., et al. 1964. A revision of Aletes and Neoparrya (Umbelliferae). Brittonia. 16: 296-315.

description: Plants 6-25 cm high; leaves oblong to ovate in general outline, the blades 2.5-6 cm long, 1.4-3.5 cm broad, 1-2 pinnate, the pinnae linear to ovate or obovate, elntire or the broader incised and toothed, distinct or somewhat con- fluent, 5-32 mm long, 1-10 mm broad; petioles 4.2-11 cm long; peduncles 10-18 cm long, longer than the leaves; bracts of involuere usually wanting; rays 4-8, spreading, equal or slightly unequal, 0.4-1.7 cm long; bractlets of involueel linear, 1.6-5.5 mm lono, acute, free or somewhat connate at base; pedicels 6-11, the longest 4 mm lonig; calyx-teeth linear to deltoid, 0.3-1 mm long; fruit oblong, 3-8 mm long, 1.7-3 mm broad, at least the lateral ribs corky-winged, the wings broadly linear, rounded or acute at the apex; vittae solitary in the intervals, rarely two in one of the four intervals, 2 on the commissure, accessory vittae absent.

description: Trees or treelets 3-15 m high, branching only near the top. Young branches thick, glabrescent. Leaves crowded at the end of the branchlets. Stipule to ca. 4 cm long, its apex deeply bifid; petioles 30-70 cm long, cylindrical, slightly striate, glabrous; leaflets 5-10, horizontal; blade conduplicate, strongly coriaceous and contrasting, the adaxial surface glabrous, the abaxial persistently golden-sericeous, except on the glabrescent primary and secondary veins; primary vein prominent on both surfaces though more so on the abaxial one, secondary veins 8-11 per side, salient on the abaxial surface and impressed to slightly salient on the adaxial one, intersecondary veins absent; median leaflets: petiolules 4.5-12 cm long, cylindrical and canaliculate; blades 21-42 X 14.5-20 cm, elliptic to wide-elliptic or narrow-obovate, symmetric to clearly asymmetric, apex obtuse to rounded, tip cuspidate, base obtuse to rounded, margin entire, revolute; basal leaflets similar to the median ones, petiolules 2.5-6 cm long and blades 18.5-30 X 11-13 cm. Inflorescence terminal, erect, sparsely sericeous, glabrescent; peduncle reduced or to 1.5 cm long, rachis to 8 cm long; primary branches 13-17, of which 4-5 are terminal, 7.5-20 cm long, bracts ca. 1.5 cm long; secondary branches 10-24, 1-5 cm long, bracts 0.5-1.5 cm long, tertiary branches up to 1 cm long. Partial inflorescences with 8-12 flowers, the peripheral ones male, the central hermaphrodite, floral bracts 1-1.5 mm long. Flowers subsessile, pedicel to 2 mm long; hypanthium greyish-sericeous; calyx denticulate, with lacinia evident; petals 3.9-4 X 1.8-2 mm, sericeous on abaxial surface, glabrous on the adaxial, filaments ca. 1 mm long, anthers ca. 2.3 X 1.3 mm, ovary elongated, ca. 3 mm long, styles 2, free, erect, ca. 1.5 mm long, reflexed in fruit. Mature drupes blackish purple, laterally compressed, 15-19 X 17.5-20 mm, pedicel 1-2 mm long; pyrenes 2, ca. 16 X 8-8.5 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Fiaschi, Pedro. 2004. Schefflera aurata, a new species of Araliaceae from southern Bahia, Brazil. Brittonia. 56 (4): 357-360.

description: Suffrutescent herbs, rarely epiphytic or climbing/scandent, the shoots 50-200 cm tall, rarely branched, glabrescent at the base to pilose or villous and yellow-brown toward the apex, the internodes 1-9 cm long, to 0.8 cm diam. at base. Leaves opposite, equal in pairs; blades lanceolate, 7-14 x 1.5-3.5 cm, the apex acuminate, the base acute-cuneate, the upper surface dark green, shiny, glabrous or sparsely pilose, the lower surface dark purple, sparsely puberulent and pilose to villous at veins, the secondary veins ca. 6 per side; petioles 1-2 cm long. Inflorescences sessile in leaf axils, of 1 or 2 flowers; pedicels 1.5-4 cm long, pilose; bracts 1 or 2, ovate-lanceolate to triangular, 0.5-1.0 cm long, the margin fimbriate. Flowers pendent; calyx green, glabrescent to pilose, the lobes subequal to unequal, ovate-lanceo- late, 2.5-3.5 x 0.3-1.2 cm, the margin with fimbrils to 1.0 cm long and ca. 0.3 mm wide, each with some trichomes, especially apically; corolla 4.2-5.4 cm long, a basal blunt spur on lower side 7-9 mm long, the tube 3.2-3.8 cm long, diam. 4-6 mm for the basal 2/3, then widening to 10-13 mm in the throat, light yellow to bright yellow, outside pilose to villous, inside glabrous, the limb lobes subequal, rotund to acute with obtuse apex, 2-3 x 3-5 mm, the upper lobe erect, the lateral and basal lobes reflexed, yellow and glandular-hairy inside; stamens 4, the filaments 3.0-3.5 cm long, glabrous, connate at base and adnate to corolla tube base for 6-8 mm, the anthers included, coherent by their apices, ca. 2.5 x 1.5 mm; nectary a lobed dorsal gland ca. 2 mm high; ovary sericeous, the style 2.5-3.0 cm long, gla- brous, the stigma crateriform-capitate. Capsule ca. 1.5 x 1 cm, probably dehiscing with 2 longitudinal slits; seeds numerous, ellipsoid, ca. 0.8 x 0.3 mm, yellow-brown, longitudinally striate.

description: Nine species. Erect or spreading subshrubs with soft or rough stellate pubescence, often with simple hairs, sometimes viscid. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate or more or less 3-lobed, cordate, dentate, acute or acuminate, lacking foliar nectaries; stip- ules filiform or subulate, caducous. Flowers usually in terminal panicles; involucel absent; calyx 10-nerved, the lobes lanceolate; petals yellow-orange or white (fading rose), the claws ciliate, otherwise glabrous; staminal column included, glabrous, filamen- tiferous at apex, pallid, the anthers numerous, frequently orange; styles 5, slender, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic (but often functionally capsular), pubescent, 5-lobed, the lobes opposite the lobes of the calyx; mericarps 5, rounded or apiculate apically, more or less constricted below (sometimes also with an endoglossum) making two cells, the lower 1-seeded, the upper 2-seeded; seeds reniform, glabrous. 2n = 16 (five species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Shrub or tree 2-15 m. high; leaflets about 20-50, elliptic-oblong, rounded or sometimes retuse at the apex, acute at the base, 1-3.5 cm. long, 4-12 mm. wide, dark green and hirtellous-strigose to essentially glabrous above, paler and finely strigose to densely and uniformly short-villous beneath; sepals of the pistillate flowers firm, light greenish, villous-puberulent, ovate or elliptic-ovate, about 1.5 mm. long or less; sepals of the staminate flowers about 1.5-2 mm. long, broadly ovate, villous-puberulent; petals linear-filiform, white, 2-2.5 mm. long; filaments about 3-5 mm. long, hairy below the middle; disk very deeply lobed, glabrous except for a few hairs near the middle; rachis of the fruiting infloreseence densely spreading-villosulous; fruit lanceolate or sometimes lance-ovate, densely spreading villous on the margins, short-hairy on the surfaces, 8-18 mm. long, the tips of the sterile carpels forming two distinct teeth at the apex, the stigma of the fertile carpel inserted below and between them; seed cavity of the fertile carpel extending scarcely beyond the middle of the fruit; walls of the carpels distinctly less firm than those of A. sukbovata, more firm than in some other species.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1944. Studies in the Simaroubaceae--IV. Resumé of the American genera. Brittonia. 5: 128-147.

description: Shrub or small tree 1-7 m. high; leaflets 8-20, acute or obtuse at the apex, cuneate at the base, elliptic, the sides not parallel, mostly 12435 mm. long, 7-15 mm. wide, the lowermost ones shorter and relatively broader; leaflets leathery, glabrous, the upper surface bright green and usually slightly wrinkled in herbarium specimens, the lower surface papillate-glaucous and deep reddish-brown; staminate flowers with the calyx 2 mm. long or a little less, villous-puberulent, the ovate acute teeth longer than the tube; filaments about 3-3.5 mm. long, villous below the middle; disk moderately lobed, short-villous; pistillate flowers unknown to me; fruit glabrous, red or reddish brown, narrowly oblong, 10-15 mm. long, 3-4.5 mm. wide; fertile carpel produced into a short narrow wing at the base only, its stigma lateral, inserted below those of the sterile carpels; fruiting rachis and pedicels puberulent, the pedicels very short, only about 1 mm. long.

description: Shrub about 2-3 m. high; leaflets about 20-40, elliptic-oblong, rounded or obtuse at both ends, mostly 1-2.5 cm. long, 5-12 mm. wide, the lowermost sometimes smaller and subrotund, leathery, the upper surface daik'green, glabrous, and, in herbarium specimens, finely wrinkled, the lower surface light yellow-green, papillate-glaucous, somewhat spreading-villous on the midrib and often also to a lesser extent on the whole lower surface; sepals of the pistillate flowers villous puberulent, elliptic-ovate, about 1 mm. long or a little more; calyx of the staminate flowers about 2 mm. long, the teeth triangular-ovate and about as long as the tube; petals absent; filaments about 3-6 mm. long, villous below the middle; disk relatively shallowly lobed, densely villous; rachis of the infloreseence densely spreading-puberulent; fruiting pedicels densely spreading-villous; fruit narrowly to broadly elliptic, 9-13 mm. long, 3-5 mm. wide, densely villous on the margins, sparsely short-hairy on the surfaces; tips of the sterile carpels usually more or less divergent, forming two well-marked teeth at the apex of the fruit; stigma of the fertile carpel inserted in the notch between the teeth of the sterile carpel, or slightly lower and lateral, often deciduous by fruiting time; seed cavity of the fertile carpel narrow, extending a little beyond the middle of the fruit.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1944. Studies in the Simaroubaceae--IV. Resumé of the American genera. Brittonia. 5: 128-147.

description: Shrub or small slender tree, 1-8 m. high; leaflets about 12-40, rounded or retuse at the apex, similarly shaped at the base, mostly oblong, with nearly parallel sides, 1-4 cm. long, 5-12 mm. wide, the lowermost ones shorter and relatively broader, often subrotund, the sides not parallel; leaflets glabrous, leathery, the upper surface dark green, finely wrinkled in herbarium specimens, the lower surface yellow-green or slightly brownish, papillate-glaucous; flowers unknown to me; fruiting rachis and pedicels puberulent; fruit glabrous, reported to be red, brown in herbarium specimens, rotund-ovate or suborbicular in outline, 8-14 mm. long, 7-12 mm. wide; fertile carpel like the sterile ones, with the walls cohering and produced into a wing; stigmas all nearly on the same level, or that of the fertile carpel slightly lower.

description: Shrub 4-6 m. high; leaflets about 20-25, elliptic-oblong, rounded or retuse at the apex, obtuse or acutish at the base, 1.5-4 cm. long, 6-15 mm. wide, averaging larger than those of A. amorphoides, dark green and essentially glabrous above, when mature, paler and finely and thinly strigose beneath; sepals of the pistillate flowers firm, white, villous-puberulent, elliptic-oblong to elliptic-obovate, some much broader than others in the same flower, about 2 mm. long; staminate flowers unknown; axis of the infloreseence finely puberulent to densely spreading-villosulous; fruit lance-ovate, broadly rounded at the base, acute at the apex, 10-17 mm. long, densely spreading-villous on the margins, appressed-puberulent to spreading villous on the surfaces; fertile carpel well developed, its seed cavity extending to near the tip of the fruit, its stigma inserted nearly at the same level as those of the sterile carpels; walls of the carpels firm.

description: Rhizoma breviter decumbens, 2-3 cm longum, ca 5 mm crassum, squamis nigro-brunneis mox. in fibras nigrescentes solutis dense vestitum. description: Omnis glabra; ramuli teretes, internodiis foliiferis 2.5-4 mm. crassis, 1.5-5 cm. longis, nodis paulum incrassatis; folia opposita; peti-olus 3-6 mm. longus, basi vix incrassatus, subtus rotundatus, supra laminam versus applanatus; lamina obovata, 4-7.5 cm. longa, 2-4 cm. lata, apice rotundata, basi cuneata vel in petiolum attenuata, crasse coriacea, utrinque opaca, costa facie superiore maxima parte, facie in-feriore prope basin visibili, nervis ceteris vix visibilibus; inflorescentiae singulae in axillis foliorum vestustiorum, umbellae pedunculatae 4-ra'di-atae triadum, floribus lateralibus pedicellatis, intermediis sessilibus; pedunculus teres, basi nonnihil clavatus, ceterum 0.5-0.75 mm. crassus; radii umbellae 4 teretes nonnihil clavati, 6-7 mm. longi, basi c. 0.75 mm., apice c. 1 mm. crassi; pedicelli florum lateralium teretes clavati, 4-6 mm. longi, basi c. 0.5 mm., apice c. 0.8 mm. crassi; bractea bracteo-laeque ovatae obtusae vel subor'biculares, vix 0.5 mm. longae, calyci appressae; calyx campanulato-subglobosus, 1.5-1.75 mm. longus, limbo brevissimo integerrimo; corolla statu alabastri adulti gracilis 20-22 mm. longa, a basi paulum dilatata usque ad clavam apicalem obovatam ad 1.25 mm. crassam subcylindracea vel apicem versus quadriangula c. 0.5 mm. crassa; postea omnino divisa in petala 4 tenuissima, parte apicali spathulata crassiuscula c. 4 mm. longa reflexa; filamenti pars libera c. 2 mm. longa, anthera c. 1.5 mm. longa obtusissima; stilus corollae subaequilongus, filiformis; stigma subglobosum, stilo duplo vel triplo crassius; fructus ignotus.

description: Tree, to 40 m x 100 cm, with cylindrical trunk, unbuttressed to slightly buttressed at base. Bark longitudinally fissured, the inner bark resinous; petioles slender, 6-24 mm long, sparsely puberulous. Leaf blades oblanceolate to obovate, 7.5-18.7 x 4-7 cm, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous, midrib convex and very prominent abaxially, flat adaxially, with 9-15 pairs of secondary veins, prominent abaxially, prominulous or impressed adaxially; domatia present in axils of secondary veins abaxi- ally, deep, pit-like, lined with numerous short trichomes; base cuneate, attenuate or obtuse; apex short to long acuminate, oc- casionally rounded. Inflorescences 5.8-6.5 cm long, puberulous; peduncle 1 cm long, the basal bracts foliose, obovate, sparsely puberulous or glabrous abaxially, the distal bracts sepal-like, caducous, the pedicels densely puberulous, 1.5-2 mm long. Bisexualflowers: corolla campanulate; sepals narrowly ovate, 1.0-2.2 x 0.7-1.5 mm, puberulous abaxially; petals narrowly oblong, 4.7-6.7 x 1.1-1.6 mm, inrolled, puberulous  abaxially, densely pubescent adaxially, white or yellowish-green at anthesis, turning red after fertilization; staminal tube 1 mm long, slightly unequal in length around circumference; stamens 8-9, with one much larger, the largest filament 6 mm long, the remain- ing filaments strongly unequal in length, 1.0- 3.0 mm long, with anther of normal form; ovary 1.5 x 1.7-2 mm, glabrous, the style slightly excentric, 5 mm long, the stigma punctiform. Staminate flowers: similar to bisexual flowers in size of sepals and petals; pistillode 0.3 mm long. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Mitchell, J. I. 1992. Additions to Anacardium (Anacardiaceae). Anacardium amapaense, a new species from French Guiana and eastern Amazonian Brazil. Brittonia. 44: 331-338.

description:
Ab A. parvifolio differt: domatia ad nervos secundarios abaxialiter sunt foveae angustae profundae intus trichomatibus brevibus provisae (nec haud profundae intus trichomatibus glandulosis provisae); costa abaxialiter manifeste prominens (nec prominula); folia apice plerunque acuminata (nec plerunque retusa vel emar- ginata); filamentum maximum 6 mm (nec 3.1-4 mm) longum; et staminum minorum filamenta valde inter se inaequalia, 1.0-3.0 mm (nec subaequalia, 0.8-1.0 mm) longa.

description: Tree 8-15 m tall, 12-15 cm dbh. Leaves alternate, 1-foliolate; petiole 1.3-6 cm; blade oblong or elliptic, acute at base, short-acuminate or acute at apex, entire, 13.2-25.5 X 4.7-9.7 cm, glabrous, chartaceous, pellucid-punctate, the glands visible on abaxial surface; midvein raised adaxially, a fimbrial vein absent. Inflorescence of several thyrses borne at apex of stem, some axillary to the uppermost leaves and others to bracts (only their scars seen), each thyrse 5.7-10.5 cm including the peduncle, this 0.7-3.7 cm, the axes glabrous, the partial inflorescences stalked, dichasial at first and second nodes, the secondary axis 4-11 mm; pedicels 5.5-7.5 mm in flower, 12-14 mm in fruit. Calyx cupular, subentire, ca. 2 mm, glabrous without and within, persistent. Corolla somewhat zygomorphic, bright yellow; petals 5, imbricate in bud, free, unequal, narrowed and sinuate-strigose on both surfaces only at base, flat, the inner-most petal flanked by the two fertile stamens, equilateral, ca. 19 x 9.5 mm, the two petals flanking this innermost one inequi- lateral, declinate, 18-19 X ca. 6.5 mm, the other two ca. 18 X 4.5 mm. Androecium of 2 fertile stamens and 5 staminodes; filaments of fertile stamens narrow-trullate, ca. 8 mm, densely tomentose on both surfaces at base, the staminodes globose and glandular at apex, two of them adnate to the petals at base, free for apical 5 mm, the other three densely tomentose on both surfaces in lower half, slightly adherent to the petals at base, ca. 14 mm; anthers narrow-oblong, ca. 6.5 mm (including appendages and apiculum) X 0.8 mm, glabrous, conspicuously glandular-punctate on connective, narrowly attached to the filament, the apiculum ca. 1 mm, the basal appendages bilobed, connate, 0.7-1 mm; pollen 3-colporate, spherical, gemmate (Fig. 2). Disc cupular, ca. 1 mm high, slightly shorter than the ovary, glabrous, entire. Ovary of 5 carpels free except in the style, umbilicate, glabrous, densely glandular-punctate; style ca. 5.8 mm (including the stigma), glabrous; stigma subcapitate. Fruit of 1 (2) free mericarps, each 20-25 X 18-21 mm, suborbiculate, glabrous, shallowly ridged, rounded apically, dehiscing along the ventral suture. Seed 1 per carpel, smooth, dull, glabrous, ca. 14 X 10 mm, the testa papery. Embryo curved, the radicle adaxial, apical, the cotyledons rounded, cordate at base, conduplicate, plicate, equal.

description: Roots spongy, cespitose or spreading from short stolons up to 5 mm. thick; culms up to 1 m. tall, single at a node, slender, ca. 2 mm. thick, erect, sharply trigonous, scabrous on the angles; leaves numerous, basal, equaling or exceeding the culm, up to 6 mm. broad, scabrous on the margins and midrib, the short sheaths soon split and drying brown or blackish; involueral bracts up to 2 dm. long, unequal, leaflike, the umbellate infloreseence terminal, the primary rays up to 1 dm. long, terete, or flattened, smooth, the spikelets congested in groups of 4-10 on shorter secondary rays; spikelets 6-15 flowered; scales ca. 3 mm. long, green, smooth, lanceolate, acute; style deeply 3-fid, reddish; achene at first white, but finally dark brown, plano-convex, oval, hardly apiculate.

description: Much-branched, often wispy shrubs 1-3 m tall with numerous, arcuate to as- cending slender branches. Young stems striate-fluted; internodes 17-48 mm long, green to bluish-green, glabrous or with scattered recurved puberulent hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long in two lines below nodes, these often not continuous down node but continuous along basal leaf margins where connate around stems; older stems whitish, bark gray, smooth. Leaves linear to subulate, (1) 2-5 (8.5) cm long, (0.3) 1-1.7 (3.1) mm wide, attenuate at tip, tapering to a nearly sessile base, entire, glabrous except sometimes at basal margins, yellow-green; midvein yellowish, raised beneath, impressed above. Flowers borne in unilateral, mostly 1 (2)-flow- ered axillary dichasia along distal 1-2 dm of slender upper branches forming slender, leafy-bracted spikes or spicate racemes with internodes (0.3) 1-3 cm long; bracts subulate, leaf-like, 2-5 (12) mm long, usually glabrous, caducous; bractlets similar, 2-3 mm long, glabrous, rarely hirtellous as calyx, or puberulent along basal margins, usually caducous; pedicels absent or mostly 1-1.7 (2.2) mm long; peduncles very rarely present; calyx (4) 4.5-7 mm long at anthesis, tube (1.2) 1.5-3.2 mm long, lobes oblong-lanceolate, 2.5-4.2 mm long, to 0.8-1.2 mm broad at base, 1.3-3 times longer than tube; calyx-pedicels closely hirtellous with erect trichomes 0.2-0.5 mm long, lobes often puberulent-ciliate with trichomes to 0.2 mm long, these often forming tufts at lobe tips; corollas red to orange-red, (30) 40-56 mm long, tube (15) 20-24 mm long, upper lobe 17-35 mm long, 2.8- 5.2 mm wide, lower 3 lobes 13-27 mm long, 2-4.5 mm wide, external pubescence 0.1-0.5 mm long; filaments 18-25 mm long, yellowish near base, reddish at tip, glabrous; anthers 2.8-3.5 mm long, reddish; styles 35-55 mm long, reddish. Mature fruits 16-22 mm long, glabrous, heads 8-10 mm long, apiculate, flattened stipe 7-11 mm long; seeds 2-4, glabrous, unequally tuberculate, 4.5-5.3 mm long, thickish, brownish-black.
bibliographicCitation: Daniel, Thomas F. & Henrickson, James. 1982. On the recognition of Anisacanthus junceus (Acanthaceae). Brittonia. 34: 177-180.

description: Similar to A. puberulus but plants more delicate, with slender, often arcuate, much- to strongly-branched stems; young stems nearly glabrous or with decurved trichomes 0.1-0.2 mm long in two lines below nodes; internodes (0.5) 2-4.5 cm long. Leaves with petioles 0-3 mm long; leaf-blades linear-lanceolate to linear, (1) 2-4 (5.5) mm long, 1-3 (7.5) mm wide, attenuate to rounded at tip, cuneate at base, at margins entire to somewhat unevenly undulate-sinuate, glabrous, sometimes with few trichomes along basal margins, rarely along midnerves or lower surface, midnerves raised, yellow beneath, impressed above. Flowers mostly produced in summer to fall when plant is in leaf, in terminal, rarely axillary leafy-based racemes 2-8 (10) cm long, with internodes 2-7 (20) mm long; bracts ovate to subulate, 1.5-4 mm long, sometimes leafy; paired bracteoles subulate, 1.5-3 mm long; pedicels 2.5-7.5 mm long; calyces (4.5) 5-7 (8.2) mm long, tubes 0.8-1.3 mm long, lobes narrowly oblong-lanceolate (3.2) 4-6 (8.2) mm long, 0.5- 0.8 mm wide, 3-7.6 times longer than tube; inflorescence axis, bracts, bracteoles, pedicels, outer calyx surfaces closely hirtellous and with stipitate glands 0.1-0.2 mm long, with heads ca 0.1 mm broad, these sometimes restricted to base of calyx or rather sparse (rarely absent), calyx glabrous to sparsely glandular inside lobe tips; corollas orange-red, red to yellowish (albinos), 43-52 mm long, tubes 21-27 mm long, ampliate upper lobes 18-30 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, lower three lobes 19-31 mm long, 2.5-4 mm wide, external pubescence 0.2-0.3 mm long; filaments 30-35 mm long; anthers (2.5) 3.5-4.5 mm long; styles 42-55 mm long. Capsules 19-22 mm long; stipes 9-11.5 mm long; heads 10 mm long, 6-7 mm wide; seeds 2-4, orbicular, 5-6 mm long, 5 mm wide, 0.6-0.8 mm thick.

description: Unkempt shrubs 1-2.5 (3) m high with mostly erect-ascending, branched main stems. Young stems with recurved puberulent hairs 0.1-0.3 (0.5) mm long in two lines below nodes, occasionally more strongly villous throughout; young bark exfoliating in papery vertical strips, old stems gray-brown, smooth; internodes 1.5-5 (10) cm long. Leaves opposite, mostly ascending; petioles (5) 12-20 (27) mm long, pubescent, hirtellous to villous; leaf blades lanceolate, lance-ovate, to narrowly lanceolate, (2.5) 5-9 (15) cm long, (0.5) 1.5-3 (5) cm wide, rather acuminately tapering to a narrow, often rounded tip, rounded at base, at margins entire to sinuate-undulate, lineolate when dry, moderately, rarely strongly, pubescent mostly along nerves on both sides with erect to curved trichomes 0.1-0.3 mm long to nearly glabrate above; young leaves with some longer hairs to 0.5 mm long on margins; midnerves raised beneath, impressed above. Flowers ver- nal, usually produced before leaves, clustered at nodes of previous season or borne in unilateral racemes 1-7 cm long with internodes 5-7 mm long; bracts lanceolate to ovate, 2-5 mm long, sometimes leafy, persistent; paired bracteoles lance-subulate, 3-4 mm long, 0.7-1 mm wide; pedicels (2) 5-8.5 mm long; calyces 6-8 (10) mm long, tubes 0.6-1 mm long, lobes 5, erect, linear-lanceolate to linear, 5.5-9 mm long, to 0.8-1 (1.2) mm broad at base, attenuate, 7-9 times longer than tube, equal to subequal; inflorescence axis, bracts, bracteoles, and outer sepal surfaces all closely hirtellous and with conspicuous tack-shaped, stipitate glands 0.1-0.3 (0.4) mm long with heads ca 0.1 mm wide; corollas rose- to salmon-pink to cream-white (albinos), 37-52 (57) mm long, tubes ampliate, 15-27 mm long, lobes strap-shaped, upper lobes 18-25 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, upcurved; lower three lobes 15-22 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, recurved, tube and lobes pubescent outside with scattered trichomes 0.2-0.7 mm long; stamens 2, filaments attached to mid-upper tube, 22-30 mm long, glabrous; anthers 3.5-4.5 mm long (dried), reddish, anther sacs united for ca 70 percent total length, one slightly longer at base; styles 30-55 mm long, glabrous, lobes 0.2-0.3 mm long. Capsules clavate, 20-22 mm long, glabrous, tan; stipes 10-12 mm long, flattened, head apiculate, 10 mm long, 5-6 mm wide; retinacula 3-3.5 mm long, erose at end; seeds 2-4, ovate to orbicular, obtuse to rounded at tip, obliquely notched at base, 5.5-6 mm long, 4.5-5 mm wide, 0.7 mm thick, glabrous, stramineous or darker, edges entire, rounded.

description: Rhizomata usque ad 12 cm longa. Culmi foliati, usque ad 1 m alti; vaginae 1-5.5 cm longae, ore hyalino, truncato ad convexo; laminae 3-8 mm latae,5.5-34 cm longae. Setae 6, usque ad 2.5 mm longae, dentibus retrorsis subdensis. Stamina plerumque 3; styli trifidi; fructus obovati, apiculati, trigoni, 0.9-1.3 mm longi.

description: Description: A woody vine; older branchlets slender, solid, prac- tically glabrate, densely lenticellate, the margins of the elongated len- ticels elevated and expanded; younger branchlets very slender, very densely appressed-puberulent with fulvous or brownish hairs, the puberulence wearing off on older branchlets; petioles stout, 8-16 mm. long, densely appressed-puberulent as the branchlets when young, less so in age; blades coriaceous, very nitid on both surfaces (as though varnished), less so in age above, elliptic, 4-10 cm. long, 2-5.7 cm. wide, acute or slightly short-acuminate at apex, often more or less condupli- cate and then eucullate-reflexed or obtuse at apex, acute or obtuse at base, practically glabrous on both surfaces (sometimes with a very few minute obscure widely scattered hairs) ; venation beautifully reticulate above; midrib flat above, prominent beneath; primary and secondary veins prominent beneath; very dense and fine veinlet reticulum beauti- fully and conspicuously prominent above, but indiscernible beneath; infloreseence fasciculate in the axils of the uppermost leaves or forming rather elongate leafy pseudo-racemes, the peduncle and rachis slender, densely appressed-puberulent as the branchlets; onlv staminate flowers seen; description: Monotypic. Shrubs 2-3 m tall, with stellate puberulence. Leaf blades pentagonal to shallowly lobed, about as wide as long, cordate, coarsely crenate-dentate; petioles almost as long as blades below to much shorter upward; stipules linear-lanceolate, deciduous. Inflorescence racemose; pedicels axillary; involucel basally gamophyllous, the bracts 10-12, linear-acuminate, about equaling the calyx in fruit; calyx half divided; petals cream-yellow with darker veins, erect, forming a tubular corolla; androecium greatly exserted (at anthesis 3-4 times length of corolla), pallid, apically 5-dentate; stamens few, in upper half of column, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles 10, diverging above the staminal column, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic (a fleshy berry), 1 cm diam., oblate, blue- black at maturity, the 5 carpels each 1-seeded. 2n = 56.

description: Large shrub, minutely stellate-puberulent; upper leaves ovate-cordate, lower (climax) leaves pentagonal to shallowly 5-lobed, cordate, palmately 7-nerved, acuminate, coarsely crenate-dentate, up to 13 cm long and about as broad; petioles often reduced to < 1 cm in the leafy inflorescence, but attaining a length of 10 cm in climax leaves; stipules linear-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm long, deciduous very early; inflorescence racemose or sometimes paniculate; pedicels axillary, up to 4 cm long; involucel basally gamophyllous, exceeding the calyx in bud, equaling it in fruit, 10-12 parted, the individual segments linear-acuminate; calyx ecostulate, 12 mm long, 5-lobed, the lobes triangular, 6 mm long; petals creamy-yellow with darker veins, 25 mm long, asymmetrically obovate, overlapping to form a fairly tightly closed tube as in Malvaviscus, but lacking any auriculate appendage on claw; staminal column long and slender (10 cm long, 1 mm diameter), greatly exserted from the corolla (twice its length in bud, to more than four times its length in flower), pallid, with short (ca. 0.1 mm) scattered, simple hairs throughout, surmounted by 5 short (0.5 mm) triangular teeth; the 20-40 stamens scattered along the upper half of the staminal column; filaments 1-2 mm long; anthers yellow; pollen spherical, echinate; styles 10, diverging above the staminal column and exceeding it by 6-7 mm, with hairs similar to those of the staminal column; stigmas capitate. Fruits (immature) light green when fresh, hemispheric, 1 1/2 cm diameter, apparently fleshy but not seen at maturity.

description: Liana, glabrous throughout, the branchlets terete, einereous or brownish; petioles 5-12 mm. long; leaf-blades chartaceous or papyraceous, olivaceous or greenish when dried, elliptic or ovate-elliptic, (4-) 6-11 cm. long, (1.5-) 2.5-5 cm. broad, obtuse or acute at base and decur- rent on the petiole, gradually acuminate at apex (acumen up to 1 cm. long, obtuse or subacute), crenulate or serrulate (serrations 2-5 per centimeter, sometimes minutely apiculate) and often slightly thickened at margins, the costa elevated or nearly plane above, prominent be- neath, the secondary nerves 7-9 per side, erecto-patent, arcuate and anastomosing near margins, strongly prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets copiously reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces; inflores- cence 1.5-5 cm. long, forming a many-flowered cluster up to 6 cm. in diameter, the peduncle slender, straight, 5-15 mm. long, the branch- lets slender, subterete or 4-angled, subtended at each node by a pair of bracts (bracts ovate-oblong, 1-2 mm. long, acute, conspicuously erose-ciliate) ; flowers 5-8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the bracteoles minute, ciliolate, the pedicels slender, 2-5 mm. long; sepals submem- branous or papyraceous, broadly ovate to semiorbicular, 0.6-1 mm. long, 1-1.3 mm. broad, rounded at apex, minutely erosulous or cilio- late at margins; petals submembranous or carnose, elliptic-oblong or ovate-lanceolate, 3-4 mm. long, 1.3-2 mm. broad, rounded at apex, conspicuously serrate at margins (teeth 7-11 per millimeter) ; disk 1.2- 1.8 mm. in diameter, 0.3-0.4 mm. high, subentire or undulate at mar- gin and shallowly grooved on the slightly broadened apex; filaments submembranous, 0.2-0.4 mm. long, slightly contracted at middle, broadest at base and apex, the anthers 0.4-0.5 mm. long, about 1 mm. broad; ovary about 1 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style 0.2-0.6 im. long; fruits up to 14 cm. in diameter, the capsules firmly connate at basal margins for 25-45 mm., deltoid or oblong-deltoid, 5-7 em. long and broad, rounded or faintly emarginate at apex, the pericarp 0.3-1 mm. thick distally and 0.8-1.5 mm. thick toward base; embryonif- erous portion of seed ellipsoid or ovoid, about 15 mm. long and 5 mm. thick, the wing obovate-elliptic, slightly falcate, at maturity 3-3.5 cm. long and 1.5-2 cm. broad, acute at point of basal attachment, minutely glandular-punctate.
