description: Epiphytic shrub; stem subterete, bluntly and broadly ribbed, glabrous; twigs subterete, complanate, bluntly angled, striate, gla- brous, with scattered ovate-lanceolate, long-acuminate bracts to 10 mm long along twig proximal to first leaves. Leaves coriaceous, subsessile, clasping or amplexicaul, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, (7) 9-12 X 3-4.5 cm, base rounded, cordate, auriculate, apex obtuse or bluntly acute, margin entire and flat, glabrous but densely and deciduously glandular-fimbriate on both surfaces; weakly 5(7)-plinerved or pinnately nerved with 2-3 lateral nerves per side, midrib impressed above and conspicuously raised be- neath, lateral nerves and reticulate veinlets slightly raised on both surfaces; petiole sub- terete, strongly flattened above, rugose, to 2 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescence axillary, solitary, racemose, 12-21-flowered; rachis subterete, angled, striate, bracteate, overall 4.5-11 cm long but the proximal 3.5 cm usually naked and lacking fertile nodes, glandular-fimbriate throughout; floral bract apparently persistent, narrowly ovate, long acuminate, 3-5 mm long, glabrous, the margin weakly glandular-fimbriate; pedicel subterete, angled, striate, 16-22 mm long (post-anthesis), glandular-fimbriate; bracte- oles located near the middle, shaped like the floral bract but 2.5-3 mm long. Flowers (all post-anthesis) with calyx continuous, obconical, ca. 7 mm long, glabrous, glandular-fimbriate; hypanthium strongly 5-winged, ca. 5 mm long; limb erect, ca. 2 mm long; lobes ovate, apiculate, ca. 1.5 mm long; sinuses acute; corolla, stamens, and berry not seen.

description: Herba flaccida, usque 55 cm alta, dense cespitosa, rhizomatibus brevibus incon- spicuis. Culmi 3-angulati, foliis prope basim. Laminae projecturae breves vel taeni- formes usque 30 cm longae. Chlorenchyma supra et infra cavitates aerias in laminis et bracteis involucralibus. Inflorescentia pseudo-lateralis, compacta, saepe prolifera. Spiculae 1-3, usque 9 mm longae et 3.5 mm latae. Squamae medianae spicularum 3.3-3.7 mm longae, apicibus mucronatis usque 0.5 mm longis; nervi laterales numerosi. Appendices antherarum parvulae, usque 0.15 mm latae. Styli bifidi. Achaenia 1.4-1.6 mm longa et 1-1.2 mm lata, obovata, rostris brevibus cylindricis, atro-brunnea, porcis vix elevatis; pagina adaxialis concava.

description: Planta robusta, caulibus teretibus vel leviter compressis, foliis alternantibus. Folia apicalia spicarum diametro ad 4 cm, spicaruni excrescentium. multo majora. F]ores feminei ca 1 mm longi; fructus baccatus, ovatus, monospermus, diametro 4 X 3 mm; semen diametro 3 X 2 mm, ellipticum, fasciculis simplicibus a basi ad apicem percurrentibus.

description: A large plant with strikingly large (up to 18 cm in diameter) orbicular foliage leaves with cordate base and very short, stout, flattened petiole giving rise to about 5 major veins in a palmate fashion; phyllotaxy alternate. Branches often terete, but spikes and vigorous branches compressed or even keeled, inter- nodes then about 5 cm long. Spikes with deciduous scales, the former axillary in groups of half a dozen or more. Axillary region of large foliage leaves a cushion of 30-40 buds representing spikes to be developed in successive generations; one or two vegetative shoots may take their origin from the center of such a cushion. Pistillate spikes expanding in fruit, when determinate to about 4 cm, when becoming percurrent bearing fruit only near the base, producing more spikes and other branches hiorher up. Pistillate spikes with up to a dozen fertile caducous bracts the axil of each of which bearing 3-5 flowers in a transverse row; central flower or fruit largest, the lateral ones successively smaller. The apex of a young spike bears 1-3 minute bract-like organs which expand into small (up to 4 cm in diameter) foliage leaves, of the same shape and venation as large ones, when the spike elongates. Pistillate flower about 1 mm long; style prominent even in fruit, stigma small, capitate. Fruit an ovate, one-seeded berry 4 X 3 mm; seed 3 X 2 mm, elliptical, with about 6 unbranched vascular bundles connecting both poles.

description: Herba gracilis, repens, ad nodos saepe radicans; caules parce ramosi, glabri, striati, 0.5-2 m longi, 1-2 mm crassi, internodiis 2.5-7 cm longis, nodis junioribus sparsim villosis; folia membranacea, ambitu suborbicularia, aliquantum latiora quam longiora, (2.3-) 3-4.5 (-7.5) cm lata, supra viridia et subtiliter scabridula, subtus pallidiora et glabra, ad basim (5-) 7-nervia, lobis 3 (-5), late triangularibus vel etiam obtuse obovatis, intermedio apice obtuso cum acumine, sinubus lateralibus leviter angularibus vel etiam profunde ovalibus, sinu basilari late triangulari vel rectangulari vel elliptico interdum valde angusto vel clauso; laminae nervi supra brevissime denseque villoso- hirsuti, subtus prominentes glabrique, supra subtusque pauca trichomata alba usque ad 2 mm longa ferentes; petioli graciles, striati, (2.5-) 3.5-5.5 (-14) cm longi, glabri, saepissime latitudinem foliorum consociatorum aequantes vel longiores, apice aliquantum villosi; cirrhi breves, subtiles, glabri, inaequaliter 3-partiti (interdum 2- vel 4-partiti), pedunculis 2-5 mm longis, 0.5 mm crassis; flores albi, stelluliformes, 3.5-4 (-4.5) mm diametro, intus minutissime papilloso-glandulares, extus glabri; flores pistillati solitarii; calyx et corolla staminatis similes; pedunculus 7-10 mm longus, 0.75 mm basi, 0.5 mm apice crassus, glaber; ovarium ovoideum, glabrum, 1 mm longum, laeve; stylus 0.5 mm longus vel brevior, glaber; description: Trees, or sometimes large shrubs, 2-6 (10 or 15) m tall. Bark light or more often dark gray, rough, appearing checkered as a result of iso-diametric, rectangular segments or plates, 1-2 cm long and 2/3 as wide, retained on the bole and limbs of approximately 6 years and older. Twigs of the previous seasons with outer bark shed in small, roughened flakes. Vestiture of the current season's growth (i.e., flowering and vegetative axes, petioles [where most apparent], and leaf surfaces) usually with hairs of 2 kinds: 1) the longer up to 4.7 (5.2) mm, averaging ca 2.5 mm, flexuous, often straight and disposed more or less at right angles, rusty-colored when newly emerged, becoming clear, with reddish or yellowish glandular tips, the glands short clavate, rarely spherical, readily infected by a fungal anamorph, Sirosporium antenniforme (Berk. & Curtis) Bubak & Serebrianikow, that renders the glands black giving the infected specimens a speckled or dotted appearance; 2) the shorter hairs glandless, curly, producing a thinly tomentose in- dument. Buds glossy red, 3-7 mm long, usually only the terminal well-developed; scales imbricate, accrescent, glabrous, margins finely but unevenly short ciliate. Leaves olive-green, ovate, sometimes elliptic; blade usually widest slightly below middle, (2) 4.5-6.5 (9) cm x (1.5) 2-3 (5.5) cm, the longer and wider blades on sterile shoots; apex acute, often with a small (1-2 mm) cusp or short-acuminate tip (rarely obtuse and lacking a cusp); base variably tapered, rounded, truncate, or slightly cordate; margins finely serrate, especially on sterile shoots (coarsely toothed on sprouts), sometimes minutely serrate or entire on fertile shoots; upper surface usually slightly glossy, especially when fresh, glabrous except along the midrib where the glandular hairs are shorter than on the young twigs, diminishing in size and density distally; lower surface sometimes markedly lighter green, fleetingly floccose on newly emerged leaves, tomentum sometimes persisting on blades of sterile shoots, then tan or brown; midvein prominent, expanded below, sometimes impressed above, lateral veins numerous, not prominent, running 1/2 the distance to the margin then arching toward apex; petioles 1.2-2.7 cm long, conspicuously glandular hairy. Inflorescence a terminal cluster of racemes, these sometimes densely congested, axes (including the pedicels) densely glandular hairy. Flowers borne obliquely erect on slender, glandular-hairy, accrescent pedicels up to 1.1 cm long at anthesis, subtended by a dark reddish bract, ca 2.8 mm long, enclosing two smaller bracteoles; calyx at first cupulate, becoming curved back on itself owing to the swelling of the corolla, lobes scarious-margined, obtuse or rounded at the apex; corolla creamy white or yellowish, drying to pale yellow or tan, 5.2-6.3 (7.2) mm long, urceolate, but developing a post-anthesis circumferential dimple at about midway its length; corolla lobes with overlapping auriculate margins, reflexed; stamens distinct, from beneath a nectariferous disc; filaments slender above, abruptly expanded below into a finely villous swollen base; anthers 1.3-1.5 mm long, appendaged with a pair of very finely tuberculate spurs 1/3-1/2 the length of the sacs; ovary hemispherical, carpels 5, locules 5, ovules 2-several in each locule, placentation axile, style terminal, stigma capitate, extended into the mouth of the corolla, sometimes exserted. Fruit a berry, fleshy, ripening from orange to red, up to 8.5 mm diam; surface tuberculate-roughened; seeds irregularly angled, but prevailingly 3-sided in cross-section, averaging 2.1 mm long, surface finely reticulate.

description: Shoots up to 25 cm long, greenish-yellow or dark brown to almost black. Pistillate plants usually erect, but the staminate plants often strongly divaricate; internodes 0.4-2.2 cm long, 2-8 mm wide; staminate flower ca 3.5 mm long, up to 3.5 mm in diameter, mostly 3-merous; perianth segments ca 1.5 mm long, ca 1.5 mm wide, the apex rounded-obtuse; pistillate flower ca 1.5 mm long, ca 1 mm in diameter. Fruit ca 4-6 mm long, 2-3 mm wide; proximal portion 2-3 mm long, elliptical-obovate, conspicuously whitish-blue glaucous on proximal portion. Anthesis from approximately mid-February through April and possibly May.

description: Arbor mediocris ramulis tortuosis griseis rugulosis terminationibus brunneis adpresse squamulosis. Folia alterna coriacea integerrima; petiolus 2-5 mm longus crassiusculus supra planus subtus semiteres dense squamulosus; lamina subelliptica vel ovato- elliptica raro subobovata basi acuta vel subobtusa apice subite angustata lateque acuminata margine integra leviter revoluta, 4-7.5 cm longa 2-3.6 cm lata, acumine 5-8 mm longo 3-4 mm lato; supra opaca in sicco brunnea vel brunneo-nigrescens sublaevis copiose depresso-punctata sparsis squamis adpressis praedita, tantum nervo medio notato reliquis obsoletis; subtus in sicco tabacina dense granuloso-punctata spisse adpresseque stellato-lepidota, costa prominenti nervis sucundariis 8-12 utroque latere tenuiter prominulis arcuatis anastomosantibus venulis obsoletis. Inflorescentiae ramulos breves terminantes paniculatae foliis breviores vel aequilongae pedunculo crassiusculo circa 5 mm longo plus minusve adpresse squamuloso, ramulis brevibus striatis divaricatis dense ferrugineo-lepidotis; pedicelli striolati rigidi ferrugineo-lepidoti 2-3.5 mm longi; bracteae ovatae ses- siles margine scariosae eroso-dentatae 1-1.5 mm longae 0.6-1 mm latae; calyx 5 sepalis chartaceis ovatis basi coalitis apice obtusis vel subobtusis margine scariosis eroso-denticulatis dorso nigro-punctato-granulatis et lepidoto-vestitis, circa 1.5 mm longis 1 mm latis; corolla 5-petala roseo-alba aestivatione contorta; petala crassa lineari-oblonga 4-4.5 mm longa 1.5-2 mm lata apice subacuta basi in tubum 1 mm longum coalita margine scariosa dorso modice nigro-punctato (in sicco) et lineato-glanduloso; filamenta staminalia robusta crassa glabra circa 0.8 mm longa ad basim corollam adnata; antherae glabrae crassae oblongo-ovatae 2.2-2.4 mm longae basi cordatae; ovarium ovoideum obtusiusculum gla- brum multiovulatum; stylus apicalis filiformis plus minusve flexuosus circa 3 mm longus; stigma punctiforme; bacca sphaeroidea in sieco 5 mm diametens brunnea minute granulosa sparse punctataque pericarpio coriaceo crasso.

description: Herba perennis caudice subligneo. Caules circa 3.5 dm alti, superne sparse ramosi, inermes. Folia crassa dum sicea coriacea, glauca, lobata, sinibus autem 1/2-2/3 spatii usque ad costam tendentibus; lobis in apicibus rotundatis dentatis, dentibus marginalibus parvis; laminis subtus subinermibus, aculeis 0-2 per cm venae, supra autem inermibus. Dum folia inferiora oblanceolata, folia superiora ovata et semiamplexicaulia. Alabastra haud visa. Flores circa 6.5 cm diametro, petalis albis, obeuneatis vel suborbicularibus. Stamina circa 100, pistillo multo breviora tempore anthesis. Capsulae 3-4-carpellatae, ovatae, 12-13 mm latae, stigmatis additis 35-45 mm longae, stilo circa 1 mm longo, capsulae superficiebus aut omnino inermibus aut in quoque carpelo 1-3 aculeis. Semina haud visa.

description: Annual with bright yellow latex; stems stout, 4-12 dm tall or more, branched, smooth or armed with prickles or small reflexed spines; leaves very glaucous, the middle and upper ones half-clasping, the blades lobed about one-half to three-fourths the distance to the midrib, the sinuses usually narrower than the lobes, the marginal teeth broadly acute, each tipped by a short prickle, the lower surfaces of the leaves smooth or prickly on the veins, the upper surfaces smooth or similarly prickly on the veins with diminutive prickles; buds oblong, the body 8-14 mm broad, 16-24 mm long, smooth or prickly, the sepal horns subterete, 3-5 (-7) mm long, smooth, prickle-tipped; flowers 8-12 cm in diameter, the pedicels at anthesis often 1-2 mm lona, sometimes longer; petals pure white, obcuneate to suborbicular; stamens about 75, the filaments yellow, clavate, the anthers dark yellow, nearly as long as the pistil at anthesis; stigma purple, 3-6 mm wide, 2-4 mm high at anthesis; capsules 3- to 6-carpellate, ovate to lanceolate, the width, exclusive of spines, 12-22 mm, the length, including the stigma, 30-60 mm, the style essentially absent or up to 1 mm long, the surface spinescent, the largest spines 2-6 mm long, the density of the spines variable; seeds 1.8-2.2 mm long.

description: Annual or more enduring; stems 4-15 dm tall, usually with 2-4 main branches above, sparingly prickly throughout, the perpendicular or reflexed prickles 0-6 per cm2; leaves glaucous, the upper cauline usually half-clasping, the blade lobed up to three-fourths the distance to the midrib, the margins toothed, the teeth acute to lanceolate, each tooth with a slender apical prickle up to 8 mm long; lower surfaces of the leaves with scattered prickles along the main veins (0-5 per cm of vein), the upper surfaces smooth or at most with a very few prickles on the main veins; buds subspherical to oblong, the body 16-22 mm broad, 18-28 mm long, each sepal with usually 15-50 slender prickles, the sepal horn-s 5-9 mm long, usually smooth, the terminal prickle weak; flowers 8-12 cm in diameter the pedicels 5-20 mm long or more; petals white, very broadly obeuneate to suborbicular; stamens numerous, often 100 or more, the filaments pale yellow, the anthers yellow, about two-thirds the length of the ovary at anthesis; stigma purple, 4-6 mm wide, 2-3 mm high at anthesis; capsules 3- to 5-carpellate, broadly ellipsoid to subfusiform at maturity, the width, exclusive of spines, 15-25 mm, the length, including the stigma, 40-60 mm, the style up to about 2 mm long; surface armed with rather numerous, erect or spreading spines of different sizes, these perhaps 50-150 or more per valve, the largest spines 6-12 mm long and enlarged at the bases, the capsular surface partially to entirely obscured by the armature; seeds about 2 mm long.

description: Annual or perhaps longer-lived; stems 4-10 dm tall or more, branched at the top, densely prickly and hispid throughout; leaves glaucous, the cauline ones up to 15 cm long, much reduced upward, oblanceolate, not clasping, pinnatifid, the sinLuses often broader than the lobes, the margins of the lobes closely and irregularly dentate, both surfaces of the leaves densely bispid; buds subspherical to oblong, the body 14-16 mm broad, up to about 20 mm long just prior to anthesis, the sepals densely hispid, the sepal horns 2-4 mm long, apically indurated below the short terminal spine, angular in cross-section, prickly; flowers 6-10 cm in diameter, falsely loiig-pedunculate because of the reduced upper stem leaves, the pedicels often 15 mm long; petals lavender (to white ?), obovate to suborbicular; stamens about 80; stigma purple, 2-3 mm wide, about 1.5 mm high at anthesis; capsules 3- to 5-carpellate, ellipsoid, their width, excluding the spines, 12-16 mm; length, including the stigma, 30-50 mm; surface finely and very densely spilneseent, obsetred, the largest spines about 5 mm long; style about 1 mm long; seeds about 2 mm long.

description:
Sepalorum aculeis infirmis, fructibus ellipsoideis et dispersione montana habitat A. platyceras Link & Otto aemulans, sed spinis caulinis retrorsis sepalorum comubus teretiusculis 4-6 mm longis et fructuum spinis recurvis 3-9 mm longis differt

Robust, erect, perennial herbs 3-10 dm tall. Stems branching distally, glaucous, substriate, scantily spinose throughout, the majority of the spines retrorse, 2.5- 5.0 mm long. Leaves sessile; lamina lobed and incised, armed, glaucous, glabrous, the lower narrowly elliptic, 15-20 cm long, 3-5 cm wide, lobes 15-17, grading into the upper leaves, broadly elliptic to obovate, 3-5 cm long, 2-3 cm wide, lobes 5-7, terminating in stout prickles, the lower surface moderately prickly or with conspicuous papillae on the primary and secondary veins, the upper surface scantily prickly along the primary vein. Flowers solitary, often clustered loosely in terminal branchlets in groups of 4; mature buds broadly ellipsoid and truncated at the apex, 1.7-2.0 cm long, 1.3-1.5 cm wide; sepals broadly elliptic, 1.7-2.0 cm long, 2-3 cm wide, glabrous and sparingly armed, the prickles weak, ca 2 mm long, patent, the sepal horn flattened, erect or recurved, 4-6 mm long, ca 1 mm wide at the base, glabrous, coriaceous, terminating at the tip in a small prickle 1- 2 mm long; corolla 8-9 cm across during anthesis, petals white, obcuneate, 5.0- 5.5 cm long, 4.5-7.5 cm wide; stamens ca 150; filaments 6-10 mm long, anthers 2-3 mm long; stigma 4-lobed, ovoid and undulate along margins, 3-4 mm wide; ovary ellipsoid, densely armed; capsules 4-carpellate, narrowly ellipsoid initially, broadly ellipsoid at maturity, 2.4-3.4 cm long, 1.2-1.5 cm wide, valves reflexing at apex, closely armed, spines varying in size, to 9 mm long, obscuring surface until capsules are thoroughly dry, recurved at maturity; seeds 2.5-3.0 in diam, black, reticulate, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: McDonald, A. R. 1991. Plantae alpinae novae mexicanae: Argemone subalpina (Papaveraceae). Brittonia. 43: 120-122.

description: Herba annua vel subperennis. Caules 4-10 dm alti, superne ramosi, exique aculeati saltem ad apicem, aculeis perpendicularibus vel reflexis (per quemque cm quadratum sunt 0-5 aculei). Folia glauca, superioribus semi-amplexicaulibus, lobata, sinibus aequantibus 1/2-3/4 spatii a loborum apice usque ad mediam costam, marginibus dentatis, dentibus acutis, apice aculeatis; laminis subtus in venis aculeatis, aeuleis autem 0-3 per venae cm, supra levissimis. Alabastra subspherica vel oblonga, 8-14 mm lata, 14-20 mm longa, 2-10 aculeis in quoque sepalo praedita. Sepalorum cornua teretia, 10-14 mm longa, inermia. Flores 6-9 cm diametro, pedicellis 2-15 mm longis, petalis luteolis cuneatis vel sub-orbiculatis, staminibus 25-50 quorum filamenta luteola antherae autem luteae. Stigmata purpurea, 2-3 mm lata, 1.5-2 mm lonoa tempore anthesis. Capsulae coriaceae, 3-4 (-5) carpellatae, subellipsoidales vel subfusiformes, 10-16 mm latae, stigmatis inclusis 30-55 mm longis, stilo 0.5-3 mm longo, superficiebus spinis patentibus subequalibus armatis, spinis 2-18 in quoque carpello, spinis autein maximis 5-15 mm. lonais. Semina 1.8-2.5 mm. longa.

description: Glabrous vine. Petiole to 2.3 cm long; blade narrowly ovate, 14-16 X 5-6.5 cm, chartaceous, base truncate to slightly cordate and then the sinus to 4 mm depth, slightly peltate, apex acute to acuminate, venation acrodromous, prominent to prom- inulous on both sides, basal primary veins 3. Flowers on short (<5 mm long) cauliflorous racemes. Peduncle plus ovary to 1.5 cm long. Perianth slightly curved between the utricle and the tube, glabrous outside; utricle widely obovate, 6-8 mm long, 3-6 mm diam.; syrinx absent; tube slightly enlarged distally, 1.5-2 cm long, 2-3 mm proximal diam., 4-5 mm distal diam., forming an angle of 100-120º with the utricle; limb oblong, 1.6-2 cm X 1.2-1.5 mm, forming an angle of ca. 1800 with the tube, apex obtuse and acuminate. Gynostemium stipitate, to 4 mm long; anthers to 1.5 mm long. Capsule and seeds unknown.

description: Herbaceous liana; stems thin, glabrous, terete to slightly canaliculate, sometimes rooting from the nodes. Pseudostipules lacking. Leaves with petioles 12-20 mm long, glabrous; blade narrowly lanceolate, 7-9.5 cm long. 1-1.8 cm wide near the base, the base deeply cordate, the sinus 6-8 mm deep, 0.5-1.2 mm wide, the basal lobes rounded, the apex long-acuminate, membranaceous, glabrous above, pilose below, often glabrescent. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicel 2.5-3.5 cm long, glabrous; ovary 1-1.5 cm long, glabrous, ridged, with an angled hypanthium; calyx geniculate, green marked with purple and brown, the utricle ovoid, 6-8 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, arachnid-pilose within, the tube geniculate, tubular, 4 mm long, strigose within, the limb unilabiate, 2.5 cm long, funnelform at the base, acute, tuberculate above, the tubercles purplish-brown; gynostemium coroniform, 6-lobed. Capsule ovoid, 3-3.5 cm long, with 6 larger and 6 smaller longitudinal ridges, the valves smooth, glabrous, the persistent hypanthium 8 mm long; seed cordate, 5 mm long, 4 mm wide, smooth, light brown.

description: Woody liana; older stems with winged, corky bark; younger stems glabrous. Pseudostipules absent. Leaves alternate, distichous; petioles 3.5-6 cm long; blade triangulate, 10-12 cm long, 8-10.5 cm wide, glabrous dark green above, very light green below, the base shallowly cordate, the apex acuminate, the venation palmate, with 5 major veins diverging from the base. Flowers in racemes from older branches; pedicel 1.5-2 cm long, glabrous; ovary 1 cm long; calyx glabrous on the outside, yellow, marked with reddish-purple, the utricle ovoid, 1.5-2 cm long, the tube forming an acute angle with the utricle, 1.5-2.5 cm long, the limb peltate, spreading, slightly bilobed at the base, 3.5-5 cm long, 3-4 cm wide, the apex acuminate, marked with purple between the veins, with a reddish-purple spot at the upper junction of the tube and the limb. Gynostemium 6-lobed, coroniform, stipitate, 4-5 mm tall, bearing 6 tetrathecate anthers. Young fruit glabrous, slightly apiculate. Seed unknown.

description: Glabrescent liana. Petiole 3-4 cm long, with a basal abscission zone; blade oblong to elliptic, to 16 X 8 cm, membranaceous, glabrous above, glabrescent below, base rounded, obtuse or cuneate, apex acuminate; venation acrodromous, basal, primary veins 3. Inflorescences consisting of axillary, elongated rhipidia to ca. 7 cm long, with internodes to 1 cm long and bracteoles 4-8 X 1-2 mm; peduncle plus ovary 3.5- 4.5 cm long. Perianth to 12 cm long, strongly curved between the utricle and the tube, greenish to maroon, the outside surface puberulous when young and glabrescent at anthesis; utricle obovoid, 3-4.4 cm long, 2.2-2.7 cm diam.; syrinx (an inner flange at the juncture of the utricle and the tube) present, aequilateral, 1-2 mm long; tube narrowly funnelform, slightly bent, 2.3-3 cm long, to 5 mm proximal diam. and 8 mm distal diam., forming an angle of ca. [less than or equal to]45º with the utricle; limb 1-lobed, narrowly ovate, 3.5-4.5 X 2-2.3 cm, forming an angle of ca. 1800 with the tube, apex acuminate, smooth inside, margins revolute at late anthesis. Gynostemium sessile, to 7 mm long; anthers 3-4 mm long. Capsule broadly oblong, to ca. 7 cm long and 5 cm diam., muticous.

description: Subshrub (?). Stems zig-zag, densely pubescent. Leaves shortly petiolate, petiole 4-7 mm long, pubescent; blade narrowly ovate, obtuse, 8-12 X 2.2-3.5 cm, pubescent on both surfaces, cordate at base, sinus 2-5 mm deep; venation palmate, prominent below, basal veins 3(-5), higher-order veins densely reticulate. Pseudostipules absent. Inflorescences in densely pubescent rhipidia developed from the young axils, to 3 cm long, with very short internodes, bracts 1-3 X 1-2 mm. Floral peduncle with ovary club-shaped, 5-8 mm, 1.5-2.5 mm diam., densely pubescent. Perianth nearly straight, to 3.5 cm, pubescent outside, especially along the main veins; utricle subglobose, 5- 8 X 2.5-3.5 mm, with a basal stipe 2-3 mm, syrinx absent; tube subinfundibular, 9-12 mm, annulus absent; limb widely elliptic, 12-15 X 9-12 mm, very slightly tri-lobed at apex, brown inside. Anthers widely oblong, ca. 1 mm, about 1/2 the length of the whole 6-lobed gynostemium. Capsule subglobose, 15-18 mm, pubescent. Seeds triangular, concave-convex, ca. 4 X 3.5 mm, brown on both sides, warty, warts more or less circular, funicle massive, narrower than the seed itself.

description: Liana; stems 2 mm diam, villous, the trichomes branched, the internodes 12-17 cm long. Pseudostipules rounded, 8 mm long, apiculate, villous, not clasping the stem. Leaves with petiole 2-3 cm long, villous; blade ovate-cordate, (7) 8-9.5 cm long, (4.7) 5.2-6.3 cm wide, the sinus broad, 5-7 mm deep, the basal lobes rounded, the apex acute, apiculate, pubescent on both surfaces, especially along the veins, pale blue-green below, green above, with 5 major veins diverging from the base. Flowers solitary or paired at nodes on young growth; pedicels 4.5-5.5 cm long, densely villous; ovary 1-1.5 cm long, densely villous; calyx geniculate, pale green, sparsely villous on outside, the utricle ovoid, 2.3 cm long, 1.2 cm wide, pendent, the syrinx 2-3 mm long, the tube straight, 1.5 cm long, 6 mm wide, the limb funnelform, unilabiate, 4-6 cm long, acute, the edge purple, the interior yellow, with trichomes 1 mm long; gynostemium coroniform, 4-5 mm long. Fruit and seed not seen.

description: Herbaceous vine, becoming semi-woody toward base with age, but never truly woody; peridermis not corky; stem and leaves aromatic. Stem twining, ribbed, 3-4 mm diam. when young, reaching 1.5 cm diam. at the base of the plant, glabrous; hypopodium and prophyll not atrophied in branches (pseudostipules absent). Leaves alternate, distichous, simple; petiole 2.5-10 cm long; blade triangular-cordate, 5-27 cm long (from tip of basal lobes to apex), 5- 21 cm wide, cordate basally with a wide-open sinus 2-6 cm deep, and then attenuated into petiole, entire along margin, acute to acuminate apically, glabrous adaxially, glabrous to hispidulous abaxially; venation palactinodromous with 3 main veins diverging from the base, the main lateral veins curving into the basal lobes, with 4- 5 main branches each; tertiary veins more or less perpendicular to the primaries and secondaries; veins impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially. Inflorescences axillary from young stems, single-flowered, pendent; peduncle 6-10 cm long, bracteolate, green; bracteole suborbicular, perfoliate, with an acute apex, to 2 cm wide, green. Pedicel plus ovary to 8 cm long, straight, ribbed, reddish. Flower with a strong putrid smell. Calyx complexly three-dimensional in structure; utricle pyriform, gibbous, 14-19 X 5.5-10 cm, with 6 prominent external ribs, cream-colored with purplish ribs and reticulated venation externally, white with cottony hairs and a some bare, purple spots near the base internally. Nectary oval, 3.2 X 1.4 cm, orange-brown with a purple band distally. Syrinx cylindrical, to 3.5 cm long, 1.4-1.7 cm diam. at the opening, directed obliquely into the utricle, cream with a purple rim. Tube sigmoid, divided into a "gullet" and a "vestibule," 12.5 cm long, same color as utricle externally. Gullet U-shaped, 7.5 cm long, 2.8 cm wide at the bottom; white internally. Bottleneck 2 mm wide (in longitudinal section) in one measured first-day flower. Vestibule a wide, gibbous, more or less transversely bilobed chamber, 5 cm long, 7.5 cm wide, 2.8 cm deep at the middle; internal wall cream-colored, heavily blotched with transverse dark maroon bands that become solid in the distal third, covered by downward-pointing cream hairs. Annulus thin, sharp-edged, to 1.5 cm high, dark orange-brown, opening (fauces) 6.4 cm high (longitudinally), facing obliquely downward. Limb abruptly expanding from the annulus, mas- sive, the distal half folding under the tube, thus presenting two faces, cordiform with two wide upper lobes, 25-31 cm long, 25-30 cm wide when held flat, marginally fringed, the fringes flattened, cirrhose, 3-10 mm long; apically obtuse with a terminal cauda (appendix) 5 cm long, 2 mm wide; cream suffused with purple externally, the internal surface cream with clear orange-brown blotches (almost solid in some flowers), darker brown around the opening, velvety in texture, the whole surface densely covered by small vermiform projections (tentacles), these cylindrical, minutely papillose, clear orange-brown with a dark brown apex, 5-20 mm long, 1-2 mm thick (0.5-1 mm thick and totally black when dry). Frontal limb face directed obliquely upward with reflexed sides, 15-22 cm long, 15-18 cm wide (when sides reflexed); lower limb face almost horizontal, with sides and apex reflexed, 24 cm long, 13 cm wide (when sides and apex reflexed); appendix directed upwards and variously twisted. Gynostemium coroniform, sessile, radially symmetrical, 13 mm high, 7 mm wide at the apex, cream-colored with purple at the base; anthers 6, yellow; stigmatic surface white. Fruit a 6-carpelate, many-seeded capsule, cylindric-hexagonal with a blunt apex, 6-7 cm long (excluding pedicel), 3.5 cm wide, septicidally dehiscent, the carpels separating completely at maturity; green with purplish longitudinal ribs when developing, dry at maturity. Seeds obovoid-deltoid, 13-18 mm long, 11-17 mm wide, 2- 2.5 mm thick, seed coat suberized, brown.

description: Prostrate herb; stems branching, pilose, glabrescent. Pseudostipules lacking. Leaves with petioles 1-2.5 cm long, pilose; blade sagittate-cordate, 3-9 cm long, 2-5 cm wide, the sinus 5-10 mm deep, the margin concave, the apex obtuse to rounded, membranaceous, pilose below, glabrous above. Flowers solitary, axillary, geniculate; pedicel 1.5-2.5 cm long, pilose; ovary 1 cm long, with a conspicuously beaked hypanthium, pilose; calyx light green to tan, the utricle ovoid, 1 cm long, 5 mm wide, the tube funnelform, 1.5 cm long, the limb plane, triangular, 3-3.5 cm long, 1.2-1.5 cm wide, usually maroon above, often tipped with yellow, fimbriate, ciliate, apiculate; gynostemium coroniform, 6-lobed, 3-4 mm tall. Capsule 6-valved, ovoid, turning brown, 2-2.5 cm long, 1.5 cm wide, pilose, glabrescent, beaked by the persistent hypanthium.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms about 1-2 m. tall, triangular, clothed with the overlapping sheaths; leaves 15-30 cm. long, 12-20 mm. wide, linear-lanceolate, long-acuminate-attenuate, obscurely plicate, about 3-nerved, the nerves and margins very scabrous, densely pilose; ligule short, depressed-triangular, densely pilose; panicles several, lateral and terminal, usually rather densely flowered, especially when young; bracteal leaf foliaceous; spikelets ovoid, 3 mm. long; bractlets linear-setaceous, ciliate, dilated towards the base, elongate; scales green or purple-variegated, ciliate on the margins, the staminate lanceolate, the pistillate ovate-lanceolate; hypogynium obscurely 3-parted, narrow, pale, dark-purple, shallowly dentate; achene 3-4 mm. long, shorter than the scales, globose, white, very rough, the tubercles hairy on the tips.

description: Rhizome fibrous; culms 20-50 cm. tall, slender; leaves 1-2 mm. wide, glabrous; sheaths glabrous, the lower ones purplish; ligule minute, sparsely pilose; inflorescence a single terminal fascicle or with an additional one on a long slender peduncle from the axil of the uppermost leaf; bractlets linear-lanceolate, longer than the spikelets; spikelets 6-8 mm. long, a few densely clustered in the fascicle; staminate scales broadly lanceolate, acuminate, dark-purple, midrib green; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, dark-purple, midrib green; hypogynium triangular, sordid-white, the margin light-purple, supporting 6 tubercles; achene 2 mm. long, oblong, pointed, longitudinally ribbed, transversely rugose, especially towards the apex, white, apiculate.

description: Perennial by rhizomes; culms 3-5 dm. tall, triquetrous, slender, flexuous, the angles scabrous; leaves remote, about 2 mm. wide, scabrous on the margins and on the midrib beneath; sheaths essentially glabrous, triquetrous, very narrowly winged; ligule short-ovate, rigid, brown, hairy; peduncles 1-3, terminal and remote in the axils of the leaves, ancipital, few-flowered, the lateral peduncles capillary, long-exserted; bracts foliaceous, overtopping the culm; bractlets linear-lanceolate, attenuate-acuminate, ciliate on the margins and on the midrib beneath; spikelets 3-5 mm. long; staminate scales lanceolate, red-brown, mucronate; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, mucro-nate, purplish-tinged; hypogynium white, tinged with purple, distinctly 3-lobed, the lobes ovate, acute, the margin undulate; aehene 2-3 mm. long, white, apiculate, ovoid, smooth.

description: Herbaceous liana; younger stems ribbed, densely pubescent with brown, multicellular trichomes over 1 mm long. Pseudostipules absent. Leaves alternate, distichous, borne on swollen nodes; petiole 3-4 cm long, densely pilose; blade ovate, 12-14 cm long, 8-10 cm wide, the apex acuminate, the base slightly cordate, finely pubescent above, densely pubescent below, the venation pinnate, with 3 major veins diverging from the base, the secondary veins subopposite the tertiary veins diverging at right angles from the midrib and secondaries. Flowers axillary, appearing solitary; pedicel 3.5 cm long, pubescent; bract at base of ovary 3 mm long; ovary ribbed, 3 cm long; calyx densely pilose on the outside, the utricle ovoid, 3 cm long, 1.5 cm diam, white-hairy within, the syrinx 3-4 mm long, the tube 1 cm long, 0.5 cm diam, the limb cucullate, 5 cm long, 2 cm deep, the upper portion papillate within. Gynostemium 6-lobed, coroniform, stipitate, 6 mm tall, bearing 6 tetrathecate anthers. Fruit and seed unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barringer, Kerry A. 1983. Notes on Central American Aristolochiaceae. Brittonia. 35: 171-174.

description: Rhizome hard, thick, nodose, covered with red-brown scales; culms 2 m. tall or less, strict, sharply triangular, angles scabrous; leaves 1225 mm. wide, acuminate-attenuate, scabrous on the margins, otherwise glabrous, rigid; sheaths broadly winged, the wing-margins scabrous; ligule rigid, ciliate, ovate-triangular; panicles several, terminal and lateral, ovate-pyramidal, much branched, the lower on very long erect peduncles; bracteal leaf foliaceous; bractlets very short, setaceous-acuminate, the base broadly suborbicular, ciliate; spikelets prevailingly staminate, these 3 mm. long, ovoid; pistillate spikelets few, subsolitary in the axils of the branches; staminate scales pale-ferruginous, ovate, acute or minutely mucronate; pistillate scales orbicular-ovate, ferruginous; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes pectinate-lacerate, the teeth subulate, narrow; achene 2-3 mm. long, equaling or exceeding the scales, globose-ovoid, mucronulate, cancellate-rugose, hairy, dark-purplish-brown or black.

description: Rhizome short, massive; culms sharply triangular, tufted, 0.4-2 m. tall, angles roughened, otherwise glabrous, robust; leaves about 4 in number, lanceolate, 40-50 cm. long, 2.5-5.3 cm. wide, glabrous, flat or more or less plicate, rather abruptly narrowed near the tip, scabrous on the margin; lower bract of the inflorescence 10-25 cm. long, 1-4.5 cm. wide, retrorsely scabrous on the margins; sheaths inflated, loose, broadly 3-winged, the wings scabrous, often purplish-tinged, glabrous or sparsely pilose; ligule 4-13 mm. long, triangular-ovate, obtuse, rigid, glabrous or somewhat pubescent; inflorescence paniculate, axillary and terminal, conic or pyramidal, much branched, 20 cm. high, pnrple; rachis scabrous; bractlets filiform, 1-3 mm. long; pistillate scales ovate, purplish, midrib green, excnrrent margin ciliolate; staminate spikelets lanceolate, 3 mm. long; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes fimbriate, the fimbriations 1 mm. long, rigid, pnrple; achene 2-3 mm. long, white, tinged with dark purple to black, smooth, shining, depressed-globose or sometimes trigonous towards the apex.

description: Small, somewhat sprawling tree to 6 m tall; stems glabrous. Pseudostipules absent. Leaves alternate; petiole 1-1.5 cm long; blade narrowly elliptic to oblong, 10-20 cm long, 4-8 cm wide, glabrous, the base rounded, the apex acuminate, green above, silvery-blue beneath, the venation pinnate. Flowers solitary in leaf axils; pedicel to 2 cm long; calyx glabrous on the outside, the utricle ellipsoid, 2- 2.5 cm long, the syrinx absent, the tube extended from the side of the utricle, 5 mm long, the annulus 3-4 mm long, the limb pendent, 3-lobed, 3-3.5 cm long, the median lobe lowest, crateriform, cuspidate, the lateral lobes triangulate, with a persistent rugose swelling near the annulus. Gynostemium 3-lobed, columnar, stipitate, 5 mm tall, with 3 anthers. Fruits capsular, slightly woody, 3-5 cm long, narrow, glabrous, the valves 5 mm wide and rough-textured, dehiscence basipetal, becoming recurved and spreading. Seeds unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barringer, Kerry A. 1983. Notes on Central American Aristolochiaceae. Brittonia. 35: 171-174.

description: Tall, finely soft-hairy, forest lianas. Stems to 1 cm diam. in known material, ridged with low, longitudinal ribs of cork. Leaves oblong-ovate with 3 principal veins at the base, the petioles twisted, to 2 cm long, the thick blades basally subsagittate with 7 mm deep sinus, 10 cm long, 5 cm wide overall. Green flowers borne on short, 3-5-bracteolate, axillary peduncles, the tube and limb borne sharply erect from the declinate utricle. Peduncle and ovary about 4 cm long. Calyx 14-15 cm long, the utricle obovoid, 4 cm long, the syrinx regular, symmetric, 2 mm long, the tube abruptly narrowed from the apex of the utricle, arcuate, cylindric, 2 cm long, thence gradually enlarging into the bullate-swollen, translucid part of the limb, this part 5.5 cm long. The limb apex abruptly thickened, opaque, triangulate, 3 cm long. Gynostemium short-stipitate, 6-lobed, coroniform, 5 mm tall, 4 mm diam., anthers 6, equidistant and sessile on the stigmatic lobe bases. Fruits and seeds unknown.

description: Rhizome elongate, scaly; culms 25-65 cm. tall, strict, slender, sharply 3-angled, striate; leaves 10-15 cm. long, about 2 mm. wide, distant, rigid, erect, glabrous, shorter than the culm; sheaths glabrous, minutely pilose, the lower bladeless; ligule small, membranaeeous-margined, deltoid-obtuse; inflorescence a solitary terminal fascicle, few-flowered; bracteal leaf erect, foliaceous, appearing as a continuation of the culm, 3-5 cm. long; bractlets linear-lanceolate, somewhat ciliate on the margins; spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 5-10 mm. long; scales dark-purple-margined, ovate, acute, acuminate or short-mucronate, the back and keel green; hypogynium bearing 6 sordid-white rugulose tubercles; achene 2-3 mm. long, shorter than the scales, ovoid, apieu-late, white, smooth, shining.

description: Perennial by fibrous rootstocks; culms 30-50 cm. high, erect, triangular, glabrous or somewhat scabrous above, slender; leaves 2-4, not overtopping the culm, 8-15 cm. long, 1-2 mm. wide, glabrous or sparingly hirsute beneath; lower bract of the inflorescence 2-5 cm. long, setaceous; sheaths hirsute, sometimes glabrous; ligule none; inflorescence paniculate, terminal, loose, 4-9 cm. long; branches few, erect, somewhat scabrous; spikelets 3-5 mm. long, oblong; staminate scales ovate-lanceolate, the pistillate dark-brown, ovate-lanceolate, the lower acuminate; hypogynium indistinct; achene globular, 1-2 mm. long, white or dark-colored, transversely undulate-tuberculate, apiculate, with 3 ridges running from the base nearly to the top.

description: Perennial by thick horizontal nodose rhizomes; culms 0.6-3 m. high, coarse, smooth, triangular, ascending, at length diffuse, sub-scandent, sprawling on bushes, very leafy; leaves 15-45 cm. long, 6-18 mm. wide, flat, 3-nerved, the margins serrulate-scabrous, rough on both surfaces, especially beneath, tapering gradually from the base into a caudate tip, short-pubescent on both sides; sheaths purplish, villous-hirsute; ligule about 4 mm. long, ovate, obtuse, rigid, hirsute; inflorescence paniculate, the peduncles lateral and terminal, the upper staminate, the lower pistillate (rarely with an occasional pistillate flower in the staminate portion), brown, the rachis scabrous-hirsute; bracts of the pistillate inflorescence conspicuous, 0.4-7 cm. long, very scabrous, linear to filiform; bracts of the staminate inflorescence shorter, linear, scabrous; staminate spikelets several-flowered; pistillate spikelets few-several-flowered; scales purple, acuminate, the staminate ovate-acute, the pistillate ovate-lanceolate, cuspidate, the keel ciliate; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes rotund, with a dark-purple margin, entire or sometimes dentate; achene discolored or usually white, 2-3 mm. long, subglobose, apiculate-verrucose or sub-tuberculate, pubescent, at least on the tubercles. description: Rhizome not seen; culms 6 dm. tall or taller, robust, sharply triangular, the angles scabrous; leaves 2-5 dm. long, 7-15 mm. wide, scabrous on the margins and midribs beneath; sheaths narrowly winged or some of them essentially wingless, the wing-margins scabrous; ligule ovate, obtuse, rigid, 5-10 mm. long, without appendages; inflorescence solitary, terminal, ovate-conic, dense, red-brown, 3-6 cm. long; bracts foliaceous, mostly 3, 4-8 cm. long, 5-10 mm. wide; bractlets filiform, minute; staminate spikelets long-pedicelled, linear, very numerous; pistillate spikelets subsessile, few; staminate scales narrow, purplish to straw-colored, the upper long-mucronate, the lower acute; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, glabrous, purplish or stramineous; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes narrow, appressed to the angles of the achene; achene 2-3 mm. long, shorter than the scales, transversely tuberculate-rugulose, subrotund-ovoid, obtusely triangular, white or sometimes discolored, the tubercles hairy or glabrous.

description: Rhizome thick, woody; culms robust, 1 m. tall or nearly so, sharply triangular, angles scabrous or sometimes nearly smooth; leaves 2-6 dm. long, 10-20 mm. wide, the margins retrorsely scabrous; sheaths broadly winged, the wing-margins scabrous; ligule terminated by a broad scarious appendage 12-25 mm. long; inflorescence terminal or sometimes a second panicle near the top, broadly conic, 5-12 cm. long, 4-12 cm. wide near the base; rachis purple, sparsely pilose; bracts foliaceous, elongate; bractlets setaceous, 1-4 mm. long; staminate spikelets numerous, nearly sessile; staminate scales lanceolate, purplish, acuminate; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, purplish; hypo-gynium 3-lobed, the lobes deeply dissected into 3 or 4 linear-lanceolate teeth; achene 2-3 mm. long, shorter than the scales, ovoid, obscurely trigonous, sparsely short-pilose, purplish or discolored (or sometimes white), minutely verrucose.

description: Annual, with fibrous roots; culms 2-4 dm. high, slender, smooth, triangular, densely tufted, usually somewhat reddened at the base; leaves 20 cm. long or less, 2 mm. wide, glabrous, linear, flat; lower sheaths somewhat hirsute, the upper glabrous; ligule minute or none, usually a tuft of hairs at the summit of the sheath; infloreseence terminal, interruptedly glomerate-spicate, of 5-10 sessile red-brown glomer- ules; spikelets 3-4 mm. long, few-flowered; bractlets red-brown, narrowly linear, sparsely fringed with long brown hairs equaling the spikelets; staminate scales lanceolate, glabrous, red-brown; pistillate scales lanceolate, cuspidate, red-brown, the keel pilose; hypogynium nQne; achene 1 mm. long, globose, very smooth, shining, apiculate, 9-12-porose just above the stipe-like trigonous base.

description: Perennial, with a slender hard rootstock; culms 3-3.5 dm. tall, tufted, glabrous, slender, erect; leaves 10-15 cm. long, 2 mm. wide, glabrous, attenuate-acuminate, the margins scabrous; uppermost blades about equaling the culm; lower bract of the infloreseence setaceous; sheaths glabrous; ligule none or a tuft of hairs; infloreseence 5-8 cm. high, interruptedly glomerate-spicate; glomerules 6-8, few-flowered; bractlets equaling the spikelets, bearing brown hairs; spikelets 3 mm. long; scales dark-brown, the staminate lanceolate, acuminate, the pistillate ovate-lanceolate, aristate, glabrous; hypogynium none; achene verrucose-tuberculate, white, obtusely trigonous, 1.5 mm. long, 12-porose just above the trigonous base, shorter than the scales, subglobose-obovoid.

description: Rhizome horizontal, thick, woody; culms coarse, 1-2 m. tall, triangular, erect, nearly smooth; leaves 30 cm. long or longer, 1-2.5 cm. wide, scabrous, especially on the veins and margins, coriaceous, rigid, flat or somewhat plicate; sheaths 3-winged, scabrous on the angles, otherwise glabrous; ligule slightly pubescent, lanceolate-triangular, rigid, 2.5 cm. long or less; inflorescence paniculate, narrow, about 3 dm. long, elongate; branches erect; panicles 4 or 5, terminal and in the upper axils, dense; bracts leaf-like; bractlets setaceous; pistillate scales suborbicular, concave, mucronate, ferruginous; pistillate spikelets sessile; hypogynium-margin densely brown-ferru-ginous-ciliate, cup-shaped, 3-lobed; achene 2.5-3 mm. long (with the high hyppgynium, 4 mm. long), white, globose or subglobose, shining, smooth, terminated by the conic, pale, more or less deciduous style-base.

description: Rhizome thick, nodose, the roots deep-purplish-brown; culms 6-12 cm. high, filiform-setaceous, triangular, pilose on the angles; leaves few, mostly towards the base of the culm, exceeding the stem, very narrow, pilose, 10-15 cm. long, 1 mm. wide; ligule none;sheaths, densely pilose; inflorescence a singl terminal few-flowered fascicle; bracteal leaves strongly unequal, the lower appearing as a continuation of the culm, ciliate on the margins and keel; bractlets ovate-lanceolate, hairy; spikelets usually 2, few-flowered; staminate scales lanceolate, ferruginous, acute; pistillate scales ovate, ferruginous, acute; hypo- gynium none; achene 1-2 mm. long, shorter than the scales, subglobose, obsoletely trigonous, short-mucronate, white, verrucose-reticulate.

description: Perennial; culms robust, triangular, 1 m. or more tall; leaves 15-30 cm. long, 5-10 mm. wide, very strongly retrorsely scabrous on the margins and midrib beneath, rigid; sheaths retrorsely scabrous on the angles, the faces woolly-pubescent, especially near the apex, purplish-tinged; ligule woolly, short, ovate, obtuse; inflorescence elongate, terminal and in the axils of 5 or more of the upper leaves, the rachis pubescent; bracts setaceous, hairy at base, scabrous, short; stami-nate spikelets 5 mm. long, more or less curved, solitary; staminate scales ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, purplish-brown; pistillate spikelets broadly ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, purplish-brown, more or less finely pubescent, especially on the midrib; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes broad, rounded; achene 2-3 mm. high, smooth, shining, elliptic-globose, obtuse, dark purple-tinged or nearly white, especially where shielded from light, sometimes pubescent at base, exceeding the scales.

description: Rhizome horizontal, 3-5 mm. thick, nodulose; culms 30-50 cm. tall, slender, wiry, triangular, glabrous; leaves 12-16 cm. long or longer, 1-2 mm. wide, few, glabrous, linear or filiform, resembling the stem, involute, shorter than the stem; sheaths glabrous, the lower ones bladeless; ligule lacking; inflorescence a single terminal fascicle of 2-5 spikelets; lower bract 1-8 cm. long, 1-2 mm. wide, appearing like a continuation of the culm; spikelets 5 mm. long; bractlets glabrous, lanceolate; scales red-brown, glabrous, the staminate lanceolate, acumi- nate, the pistillate ovate-lanceolate, acuminate; hypogynium none; achene 2 mm. long, white, smooth, usually longitudinally ridged, dull, 6-porose near the base, ovoid, shorter than the scales, the base triangular.

description: Large tree with copious latex; leaves broadly obovate or ovate to oblong or broadly elliptic in general outline, mostly about 20-50 cm long, half as wide, varying in size and shape even on the same tree, with 3-5 (rarely 6) large acuminate lobes on a side; sinuses extending about 4/5 the way to the midrib; apex acuminate; base cuneate to subeordate-rounded; petiole stout, 2-4 cm long; texture of blade subcoriaceous to coriaceous, stiff, the upper side dark green, glossy but often roughish to the touch, especially on the midrib, the underside dull, with elevated midrib and main veins, sometimes glabrous but more usually variously sparsely pale pubescent or puberulent especially on midrib and veins; stipules oblong-lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, two at a node, unequal, enclosing the terminal bud, up to about 15 cm long at maturity, eaducous with the unfolding of the leaves, leaving a sear encireling the twig; flowers monoecious, in separate infloreseences, these in the upper leaf axils, the staminate usually above the pistillate; staminate inflorescences clavate, pedunculate, with a thick axis of spongy tissue covered by minute flowers each consisting of a reduced tubular perianth divided over halfway into two concave imbricate lobes and a stamen with a 2-celled, suleate anther on a thick filament, these flowers crowded on the surface of the rachis, the whole up to 2-3 cm wide at the widest part, and 10-20 cm long, rarely longer; pistillate infloreseences globose to cylindric; flowers crowded together on a thickened rachis, the perianths thickened and fused exposing only a polygonal disk representing each flower, this disk ranging from almost flat to prominently umbonate, with a tiny erect crown-like limb from which protrude the 1-2 (or 3) strap-shaped stigmas; ovaries and styles free, sunken in closed flask-like chambers (one in each perianth); the whole synearp 5 cm or more in diameter at anthesis, enlarging to 10-25 cm in fruit; fruit soft and pulpy within when mature, with a yellowish green rind, usually stained with latex exudations at maturity, typically seedless, but some forms with many large seeds (actually thin walled achenes or nuts), these subglobose or obovoid, 1-2 cm thick, embedded in the pulp; abortive seeds often numerous in the sterile forms.

description: Rhizome stout, horizontal, nodose, 6 mm. or less thick; roots coarse, fibrous; culms 4-10 dm. high, triangular, slender, glabrous, scabrous above; leaves essentially glabrous, 15-30 cm. long, 1-2 mm. wide; sheath glabrous; ligule short, rotund-ovate, scarious; inflorescence a single small terminal cluster or with an additional one from the axil of the uppermost leaf; lower bract foliaceous; spikelets oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, 3-5 mm. long; pistillate scales purplish-tinged, 3 mm. long, acute or acuminate; hypogynium obscurely 3-lobed, covered with a rough white crust; achene 2 mm. long, globose-oblong, verrucose-reticu-late, somewhat ridged, white, shorter than the scales.

description: Rhizome horizontal, thick, hard, nodose, clothed with chestnut-brown scales; culms 10-15 cm. tall, capillary, strict, triangular, the angles pilose; leaves few, mostly near the base, very narrow, 1 mm. wide, longer than the culm, erect, rigid, pilose; sheaths densely pilose; ligule none or very short; inflorescence a single terminal few-flowered fascicle; bracts 2, unequal, the lower elongate, strict, erect, appearing as a continuation of the culm, pilose; bractlets lanceolate; pistillate scales ovate, membranaceous, acute; hypogynium ferruginous, thick, supporting three 2-lobed light-brown tubercles; achene shorter than the scales, mucronate, 1.5-2 mm. long, strongly undulate-verrucose, white or discolored, ovoid.

description: Similar to A. alttitis but the leaves generally smaller, 10-30 cm long, half as wide, broadly obovate to broadly elliptic in outline, acute to acuminate, entire to variously lobed in the upper part; cutting usually not more than half way to the midrib, mostly less, the lobing extremely variable on the same tree; base cuneate; petiole up to 4.5 cm long, usually 2-3 cm; upper surface subglossy, the midrib and veins conspicuously brown appressed-hirsute beneath; staminate infloreseence generally not much over 10 cm long; anthers curved, at least on drying; fruit more or less short cylindric; apical disks of perianth conical when immature, becoming low at maturity, seedy. Adequate material for a proper description of the flowers, especially the pistillate ones, is not available.

description: Perennial by an elongate aromatic horizontal rhizome; culms 15-65 Cm. high, erect, slender, glabrous or pubescent lxear the apex, acutely triangular; leaves 4-20 cm. long, 2-5 mm. wide, linear, flat, pubescent or rarely nearly glabrous; sheaths hirsute; ligule minute or none; in- florescence interruptedly glomerate-spicate, simple, terminal, 4-12 cm. long, of 3-9 sessile, often nodding, more or less remote glomerules; rachis pubescent; bractlets long-pilose; staminate scales obtuse, nar- row, brown, hirsute on the back; pistillate scales broader, cuspidate, brown; spikelets 4-5 mm. long, castaneous, ferruginous or dark-red- brown to almost black; hypogynium none; achene 1-2 mm. long, obovoid to subglobose, white, smooth, shining, mucronulate, obscurely trigonous, the base cuneate-attenuate, not porose, or lightly 9-12-excavated.

description: Annual, with fibrous roots; culms 15-50 cm. high, triangular, sparsely hirsute with long white hairs or rarely glabrate; leaves 5-20 cm. long, 1-2 mm. wide, pubescent, flat, linear; sheaths pubescent; ligule minute, with a tuft of hairs, or none; infloreseence glomerate- spicate, 5-10 cm. long; glomerules 5-13; rachis hirsute; spikelets 2-4 mm. long; bractlets linear, hirsute with long white (or sometimes dark- brown) hairs; staminate scales lanceolate; pistillate scales ovate, purplish-tinged, the keel ciliate, mucronate; hypogynium none; achene sparsely rugose-verrucose or tuberculate, 1-1.5 mm. long, mucronate, trigonous, 12-porose at the attenuate base.

description: Low, rhizomatous, aromatic herb, individual plants forming clumps less than 4 dm across; rhizomes 2-4 mm diam, deeply buried, pseudodichotomously branched, with numerous leaf and bract scars, growth between first leaves of successive years 3-35 mm; roots fleshy, typically in a tuft at the base of the rhizomes; leaves evergreen, 1 pair per shoot per year, alternate, the blade dark green with a broad, tapered, white to silver band along the midrib and narrower bands along lateral veins (rarely completely green or almost white), cordate to cordate-reniform, at apex acute to broadly acuminate (rarely obtuse), sometimes mucronulate, at base cordate, 3-12 cm wide at the widest point, 4-14 cm long from the base of the lobes, length/width ratio 1.1 (0.75-1.4), glabrous or with short hairs along veins above, sparsely pubescent beneath, the margin ciliate, marginal hairs spreading at right angle to margin, petiole 5-20 cm long with scattered long hairs, sometimes moderately villous; flowers solitary, terminal, erect or slightly inclined; sepals 3, free, the lower segments contiguous and forming a subglobose false calyx tube, 6-10 mm long, 7-13 mm wide, pink to beige to light green, spotted red without, dark lustrous red within, sparsely to moderately villous without, puberulent to pubescent within, with dark red hairs; calyx lobes pale green without, beige to olive (rarely maroon at base) within, 17-52 mm long (avg. = 35 mm), 7-10 mm wide at the base (avg. = 8 mm), spreading to frequently erect, the lower segment triangular, the upper one attenuate, marginally revolute, with sparse, long, white hairs dorsally and short dark red hairs ventrally; stamens 12 in 2 whorls, the inner longer, with 1-3 additional staminodes in some flowers, filaments red to dark pink, connective surpassing anther, subulate; inner stamens longer, 3.2-8.7 mm long (avg. = 6 mm), filaments 1.2-3 mm long, anthers 0.8- 2.4 mm long, connective 1.2-3.8 mm long, outer stamens 2.3-5.7 mm long (avg. = 4.2 mm), filaments 0.6-2.1 mm long, anthers 0.9-2 mm long, connective 0.6- 2.7 mm long; style 3-4.5 mm long, 1.8-2.9 mm thick, shallowly to deeply lobed at apex; stigmas 6, dark red to pink, linear to narrowly elliptic, lateral to extending over the style lobe, 0.6-1 mm long; ovary inferior, pink to beige to light green with small red spots, villous, at apex light green to beige with a red band at the periphery; locules 6, placentation axile; ovules 26-46; fruit a loculicidal capsule; seeds with a fleshy funiculus.
bibliographicCitation: Mesler, Michael R. & Lu, K. L. 1990. The status of Asarum marmoratum (Aristolochiaceae). Brittonia. 42: 33-37.

description: Boots fibrous; culms retrorsely scabrous, triquetrous, 3-8 dm. high, robust; leaves 45-60 cm. long, 1-6 mm. wide, retrorsely scabrous, obtuse; sheaths narrowly 3-winged, purplish, retrorsely strigose; ligule rotund, the margin membranaceous; inflorescence paniculate, the branches ascending, rigid, axillary or terminal; lower bract of the inflorescence 4 cm. long or less; bractlets antrorsely scabrous, setaceous-subulate; staminate scales broadly lanceolate, mucronate, purplish-tinged; pistillate scales broadly ovate, abruptly acuminate, ciliolate on the margin, red-brown; hypogynium depressed, 3,-lobed, pale, the margin narrow, purplish; achene 3 mm. long, ovoid, white, smooth, shining, equaling or exceeding the scales.

description: Low, rhizomatous, aromatic perennial herb; roots fleshy, slender, arising along the length of a rhizome ca 2.5-3.0 mm diam, growth between first leaves of succesive years 5-21 mm; bracts 3; leaves deciduous, 1 pair per shoot per year, alternate, pale green to darker yellow-green to blue-green, the blade broadly reniform to cordate-reniform, at apex usually obtuse (broadly acute to almost flat), at base cordate often with broad, open sinus, 4-11 cm wide at widest point, 3-8 cm long to insertion of petiole, length/width ratio 0.68 (0.50-0.95), glabrous or with scattered hairs along veins above, sparsely pubescent below, the margin ciliate, sometimes gently undulate, especially near apex; petiole 3-15 cm long with scattered long, white hairs; flowers solitary, terminal, with a faint foul odor, erect to slightly inclined; sepals 3, the lower segments contiguous proximally and forming a subglobose, rectangular-urceolate to urceolate calyx-tube, 6-11 mm long, 8-13 mm wide, light green without, white to light green within, each with a red-maroon band along the top and sides and occasionally a red-maroon stripe down the center, sparsely to moderately villous without, densely puberulent within with short, maroon-tipped hairs; calyx-lobes white to pale green without, typically yellow-green (green-maroon) and often with a maroon band at the base within, 8-20 mm long (ave. = 14.5 mm), 6-10 mm wide at the base (ave. = 7.7 mm), spreading, bent through ± 90º near middle, the lower segment triangular (deltate to narrowly triangular) sometimes flared at the base, the upper one linear-triangular, marginally revolute, sparsely villous to villous dorsally with scattered white hairs, densely covered ventrally with straight, white, maroon-tipped hairs; stamens 12 in two whorls, the inner longer, and 1-3 additional staminodes opposite stamens of the inner whorl in about half of the flowers examined, filaments redmaroon, anthers dehiscent extrorsely, connective surpassing anther, bluntly triangular; inner stamens 2.5-5.0 mm long (ave. = 4.1), filaments 1.25-2.5 mm long, anthers 1.0-2.0 mm long, connective 0.3-1.0 mm long, outer stamens 2.25-5.0 mm long (ave. = 3.3), filaments 1.0-2.0 mm long, anthers 1.0-1.5 mm long, connective 0.25-1.0 mm long; pollen spherical, 43-55 Am in diam; style white or light green with few to many red spots or entirely red-maroon, 2.0-4.0 mm long, 1.0-2.5 mm wide, subtruncate to deeply lobed between stigmas; stigmas 6, dark maroon, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, lateral or extending over the apex of the style lobe, 0.5-1.25 mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm wide; ovary usually more than half inferior (50-95%), light green-white, sparsely to densely villous, at apex maroon to base of stamens or style; locules 6, placentation axile; fruit a loculicidal capsule; ovules 11-36 (45); seeds dark brown, widely cuneate, 4.0-4.5 mm long, 2.0-3.0 mm wide; funiculus fleshy, forming a prominent aril almost as long as seed and slightly narrower.

description: Rhizome thick, hard, nodose; culms 30-70 cm. tall, triangular, glabrous, channeled, the angles scabrous; leaves 10-30 cm. long, 3-7 mm. wide, the margins and principal nerves very scabrous; sheaths finely pubescent; ligule short, ovate, dimidiate, obtuse, margin hairy; inflorescence terminal, branched, lax, also axillary and remote, on very long, slender peduncles, the fascicles few-flowered; bracts foliaceous; bractlets elongate, linear-lanceolate, attenuate; staminate spikelets linear-oblong, somewhat compressed; staminate scales lanceolate, acute; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, acute or mucronate, stramineo-ferruginous, sometimes purplish-tinged; hypogynium ring-like, 3-lobed, the lobes light-yellow, lanceolate, cuspidate or acute, appressed to the achene; achene 2-3 mm. long, ovoid, white, faintly reticulate, sparsely pubescent, shorter than the scales.

description: Rhizome thick; culms triquetrous, sparingly pilose, strict, 1 m. tall or taller; leaves 45-60 cm. long, 2-5 cm. wide, abruptly narrowed towards the apex, lanceolate, glabrous, margins and nerves scabrous; sheaths narrowly 3-winged, the wings scabrous, sparingly pilose, or broadly winged, the wings short, tapering downwards; ligule 5-8 mm. long, triangular-ovate, strongly nerved, rigid, pilose or glabrous, margin cartilaginous; inflorescence subpyramidal, terminal and axillary, dense, the branches rigid, the peduncles compressed, scabrous, pubescent; lower bract of the inflorescence foliaceous, 15 cm. long or longer, 1 cm. wide; bractlets setaceous-capillary; pistillate scales membranaceous, exceeding the achene, ovate, mucronate, brown, minutely pubescent, the midrib green; staminate spikelets 3-4 mm. long, lanceolate, short-pediceled; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes deeply and irregularly fimbriate, the fimbriations brown or purplish; achene depressed-globose, white or purplish, smooth, 3 mm. long.

description: Perennial; rhizome elongate, horizontal; culms filiform, 2-6 dm. high, tufted; leaves glabrous, rigid, 15-30 cm. long, 1 mm. wide; sheaths pilose; ligule none; infloreseence terminal, 5-15 cm. long, interruptedly glomerate-spicate, sparingly or not at all branched; branches when present on short, filiform peduncles, rachis ciliate on the angles; bractlets capillary-setaceous, dilated at the base; spikelets linear-oblong, obtuse; scales glabrous, membranaceous, oblong, fer- rugineo-sanguineous, acuminate, the pistillate much exceeding the achenes; hypogynium none; achene 1 mm. long, fragile, short-stipitate, elliptic-globose, umbonate, white, transversely rugose-undulate to es- sentially smooth.

description: Annual, with fibrous roots; culms 2-4 dm. long, trigonous, glabrous or sparsely pilose; leaves flat, pilose with long white hairs, 1-2 dm. long, 2-4 mm. wide; sheaths hairy, loose; ligule minute, with a tuft of hairs; infloreseence 6-10 cm. long, interruptedly glomerate-spicate, the glomerules 5-8, the rachis pilose; spikelets 2-4 mm. long; bractlets brown, long-attenuate, pilose with long white hairs; scales dark-brown, the staminate lanceolate, the pistillate ovate-lanceolate; hypogynium none; achene 1 mm. long, white, smooth, shining, mucronate, globose, shorter than the scales, bearing 4 pores on each side of the trigonous base.

description: Perennial by rather short, nodulose rhizomes; culms often clustered, filiform, triquetrous, glabrous, at least towards the summit, 3-6 dm. high; leaves several, often more or less aggregated toward the middle of the culm, 10-20 dm. long, 1-3 mm. wide, involute, glabrous, the margins and keel scabrous; sheaths finely pilose or nearly glabrous, purplish (especially the lower, nearly bladeless ones); ligule short, triangular, rigid, pilose; inflorescence axillary and terminal, simple or branched, of 1—4 distant interrupted spikes, few-flowered, the spikes stalked or the uppermost sessile; spikelets 3-4 mm. long, few-flowered; bracts filiform, glabrous; bractlets glabrous, dark-brown, exceeding the achenes; scales dark-brown, ovate-lanceolate; hypogynium none; achene 2-2.5 mm. long, white, smooth, shining, oblong or ovate-elliptic, subacuminate-umbonate, the attenuate trigonous base non-porose.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome coarse, nodulose; culms 1 m. tall and taller, coarse, channeled, triquetrous, sparsely pilose or glabrous; leaves shorter than the culm, flat, 30-50 cm. long, 8-20 mm. wide, glabrous or sometimes ciliate on the margins and principal nerves, slightly scabrous or often quite smooth; sheaths loose, often dark-purple, glabrate or pilose; ligule broadly ovate-obtuse, the margin cartilaginous or membranaceous; panicles narrow, branches few, erect, densely flowered, terminal and axillary in the upper sheaths, the terminal panicle 5-7 cm. long; peduncles ancipital; bracteal leaf foliaceous; bractlets elongate, 2-5 cm. long, long-pilose, scabrous; staminate spikelets densely clustered, linear-oblong, 1 cm. long; pistillate spikelets densely clustered, obovoid; staminate scales narrowly lanceolate, attenuate-acuminate, hispid; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, often dark-purplish on the margin, strongly keeled, the keel hispid-pilose, long-awned, stramineous; hypogynium scutellate, polished, conspicuous, obscurely 3-lobed or almost entire, dark-sanguineous or black; achene 4-6 mm. long, oblong-ovate, shorter than the scales, white or discolored, smooth, obscurely trigonous.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms triquetrous, slightly scabrous on the angles, the portion seen 45 cm. long; leaves 15-30 cm. long, 3-5 mm. wide, almost glabrous except near the base, attenuate-acuminate; sheaths scabrous on the angles, very finely pubescent, the basal portion purplish; ligule short, rotund, the margin hairy; panicles several, terminal and on long slender rigid erect peduncles in the axils of the leaves, few-flowered; the rachis scabrous on the angles; bractlets linear-lanceolate, or subulate-setaceous; staminate spikelets few; scales ovate, mucronate, glabrous, purplish, margins ciliate; hypogynium obpyra-midal, 3-lobed, thick-coriaceous, irregularly undulate, yellowish-red; achene conspicuously exserted, conic, 3 mm. long, minutely transversely white-pilose, deep-violet or the base often white.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms robust, sharply triangular, scabrous on the angles, 2 m. long, scrambling over bushes; leaves close together, 3-5 dm. long, 5-10 mm. wide, retrorsely scabrous on the margins and veins, very cutting; sheaths winged; ligule very large, 1 cm. broad, obtuse, membranaceous-appendaged, 1.5 cm. long; inflorescence terminal, conic, dense; rachis white-pilose; lower bract of the inflorescence folia-ceous, elongate; bractlets narrowly linear, pilose; staminate spikelets very numerous, long-pedicelled; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, light-straw-colored to castaneous, with purple blotches; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes at the angles of the achene, ovate and erect; achene 3 mm. long, white, shining, ovoid, trigonous, minutely white-pilose, the apex acutely pyramidal.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Perennial by stout rhizomes; culms coarse, smooth, or the angles sometimes scabrous, sharply triangular, 1-3 m. high; leaves linear-lanceolate, 5-7-nerved, rigid, attenuate-acuminate, 2-4 dm. long, 1-4.5 cm. wide, smooth or somewhat roughened on the margins and veins beneath; sheaths 3-winged, the wing-margins roughened; ligule short, ovate, obtuse, rigid; inflorescence paniculate, terminal and axillary; branches erect, the spikelets densely clustered; bracts foliaceous; bractlets linear-setaceous, pubescent, especially at the base, elongate; staminate spikelets 4 mm. long, ovate to ovate-oblong; staminate scales lanceolate, acuminate, minutely pubescent; pistillate scales broadly ovate-orbicular, ciliate on the margins, minutely pubescent; hypogynium large, undulately 3-lobed, the margin more or less ciliate;  achene subglobose-ellipsoid, white or discolored, smooth, shining, 3.5-6 mm. long, tipped with the somewhat persistent conic pale style-base.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms erect or ascending, 2-3 m. high, sharply triquetrous, serrate-scabrous on the angles, not pubescent; leaves about 25 cm. long, 1-3.2 cm. wide, distant, flat, 3-5-nerved, very scabrous on the margins, glabrous, the apex attenuate-acuminate; sheaths glabrous below, densely appressed-pilose near the top, very scabrous on the angles; ligule short, depressed-ovate, cartilaginous-margined, pubescent; panicles terminal and in the axils of the uppermost leaves, open, oblong, 10-20 cm. long, rachis scabrous; bracteal leaf foliaceous; bractlets conspicuous, setaceous, 10 cm. long or less, yery scabrous; staminate spikelets 3-4 mm. long, unisexual, subsolitary, ovate-lanceolate, somewhat compressed; pistillate scales keeled, red-brown, glabrous, broadly ovate, the midrib exeurrent, green; staminate scales ovate-lanceolate, brown; hypogynium obpyramidal, white, 3-lobed, the lobes very short, undulate, thick, reflexed, yellow-strawcolored, the margin glabrous, entire; achene 4-5 mm. long, white, shining, ovoid, apiculate, exceeding the scales.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Perennial by horizontal, elongate, rather stout rhizomes; culms sharply triangular, glabrous, 0.5-2 m. high, erect or at length nodding; leaves 20-40 cm. long, 7-11 mm. wide, glabrous or slightly scabrous on the margins; sheaths 3-winged, glabrous or nearly so; ligule 1 cm. or less long, lanceolate, glabrous, rigid; inflorescence paniculate, the panicles axillary and terminal, usually several, erect, very narrow, loosely flowered; lower bract of the inflorescence foliaceous; bractlets linear-subulate, minute; staminate spikelets oblong-ovate; staminate scales ovate, obtuse, stramineous; pistillate scales ovate-orbicular, stramineous; hypogynium-margin more or less densely white-ciliate or ciliolate; achene 1-2 mm. long, exceeding the scales, ellipsoid-ovoid, smooth, white, shining, tipped by the more or less persistent style-base.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Annual, with fibrous roots; culms filiform, 1-5 dm. high, glabrous or somewhat hairy, triquetrous; leaves 3-11 cm. long, 1-2 mm. wide, somewhat scabrous on the margins, glabrous or hairy, about equaling the culm, more or less involute in drying; sheaths loose, hairy especially towards the top; ligule minute, hairy; inflorescence 5-10 cm. long, virgately branched; glomerules interrupted; rachis pilose to glabrate; lower bract foliaceous; bractlets dark-brown; scales acuminate, dark-brown, often with paler midrib, the staminate lanceolate, the pistillate ovate-lanceolate; hypogynium none; achene 1 mm. long, fenestrate-verrucose, white, shining, apiculate, trigono-globose, shorter than the scales, the base trigonous, attenuate, 5-porose on each face.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms about 1-2 m. tall, robust, triquetrous, channeled; leaves very rigid, plicate-nerved, 20-40 cm. long, 15-20 mm. wide, exceeding the culm, densely short-pubescent; sheaths minutely short-pubescent, winged, the wing-margins scabrous; ligule rigid, ovate-lanceolate, densely white-pilose; panicle terminal, dense, oblong-lanceolate, 20 cm. high, much branched, the rachis essentially glabrous except for the ciliate angles; bracts foliaceous; bractlets very minute, margin ciliate, ovate; spikelets solitary, ovate-lanceolate, apex recurved; scales stramineous, ovate-lanceolate, margin ciliolate; hypogynium not seen; achene not seen; the deep-black ovary of the type is oblong-cylindric, 1 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome none; roots fibrous; culms 15-25 cm. tall, very slender, triquetrous, sparsely pilose or almost glabrous; leaves 10-15 cm. long, 1-2 mm. wide, sparsely pilose or glabrous; sheaths more or less pilose; ligule minute or none; inflorescence paniculate, very lax, branches capillary, 6 cm. or less long; rachis pilose with long white hairs, the fascicles very small, distant; bractlets lanceolate, minute, pilose; spikelets 1.5 mm. long, 2-4 in a fascicle; scales ovate-lanceolate, pilose on the keel; hypogynium none; achene 0.75-1 mm. long, minutely apiculate, globose, transversely muriculate-tuberculose, white.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Perennial herb; root system of vertical taproots and horizontal runners con- necting clusters of stems; stems 2.5-10 dm tall, erect or ascending, stout, simple, few to several in a cluster; leaves densely white-woolly pubescent at first, becoming glabrous especially beneath, opposite, coriaceous, the upper ones broadly elliptic or (ob)ovate, (6) 7-9 (15) cm long, (3) 3.5-6 (8) cm broad, rounded to truncate and mucronate apically, rounded to subcordate basally, with petioles 1-5 (10) mm long, the lower leaves smaller, ovate, their acuminate apex sharply acute, sessile and cordate-amplexicaul basally; inflorescence white-lanate, the few cymose umbels lateral at the upper nodes, compactly many-flowered and spherical, the flowers so crowded as to prevent the corolla lobes from becoming truly reflexed, the pedicels 8-13 (20) mm long, cottony-pubescent, the peduncles 2-4 (7) cm long; sepals reflexed at the base, curving up through the sinuses of the corolla lobes, linear, (5) 6-7.5 mm long, green above and lanate beneath; corolla (5) 6-7 (8) mm long, reflexed at the base and the lobes usually forced upward in the thick-packed umbel, ovate, cream with a rose-tinged middle, tomentulose beneath; column ca 0.5 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm thick, pale green; hood 2.5-3.2 mm long, broadly truncate and open above, cream; horn exserted from and attached at the middle of the hood, falcately curved over the stigma head; anther head 1.2-1.5 mm high, 1.5-3.4 mm diam., the anther sacs violet-tinged, the wings broadest near the middle, cream, the appendages ca 0.5-0.8 mm long; follicle spreading to pendulous on a spreading pedicel, broadly fusiform, 4-7 (7.5) mm long, lanate to glabrate, bearing soft, subulate processes; seeds ca 1.2 mm long, broadly oval.
bibliographicCitation: Gates, Bronwen. 1979. New names in Banisteriopsis and Diplopterys (Malpighiaceae) of the Guayana Highland. Brittonia. 31: 108, 109.

description: Perennial by thick woody rhizomes; culms growing in clumps, stout, smooth or slightly roughened on the angles, triquetrous, 1-3 m. tall, strict; leaves 60 cm. or less long, 1-2.8 cm. wide, flat or somewhat plicate, rigid, glabrous, scabrous on the nerves above and on the margins; sheaths 3-winged; ligule 3 em. long or -less, lanceolate, glabrous; panicles 3 or 4, narrow, loosely many-flowered, about 30 dm. long, elongate, the branches erect; lower bract of the inflorescence f oliaeeous; braetlets very short, setaceous; spikelets short, ovoid; pistillate scales ovate-orbieular, abruptly acuminate; hypogynium truncate, densely fringed with brown or red-brown hairs; aehenes ellipsoid, 2-3 mm. long, smooth, white, sometimes black or discolored, lustrous, tipped with the small eonie black persistent style-base.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome none, roots fibrous; culms slender, erect, villous, 2-3.5 dm. high; leaves 10-20 cm. long, 1-2 mm. wide, narrowly linear, vil- lous; sheaths densely villous; ligule minute, villous; infloreseence glom- erate-spicate, 7-8 cm. long, of 12-15 glomerules; rachis villous; bractlets long-ciliate, 3-4 mm. long; staminate scales lanceolate, brown, more or less pilose; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, mucronate, brown, pilose with long white hairs; hypogynium none; achene 1-1.5 mm. long, ovoid-globose, white, shining, faintly reticulate below, the base trigonous, 4-porose on each side.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: A var. longifolia differt ramulis novellis laxis, glabreseentibus; foliis angustis oblongo-linearibus vel oblongo-lanceolatis, elongatis cuneatis obtusis supra ab initio glabris subtus primo rufo-sericeis vel glabris mox omnino glabreseentibus, petalis exterioribus albis vel albo-viridibus interioribus albis vel purpuraseentibus.
