description: Intermedia A. speciosa et A. longifolia; frutex ad 2 m altus; ramulis novellis minute ferrugineo-tomentosis, mox glabrescentibus et castaneis; vestutioribus cortice einereis obtectis. Lamina coriacea, supra ab initio glabra vel minute ferrugineo-tomentosa, dein glabreseens subtus praesertim in nervis tomentosa, demum in nervis fere glabreseens, oblonga oblanceelatave vel angtiste obovata, basi breviter acutata vel rotundato-acuta, apice rotundata, (5-) 7-15 cm longa. Flores in ramulis anni praeteriti 1-2 in axillis foliorum delapsorum evoluti. Pedicelli rufo-tomentosi, 1.5-4 cm longi. Petala exteriora magna, dilute albo-punicea vel alba; interiora alba, albo-viridia, purpurea. Shrub with numerous primary shoots from a vertical, stout-linear taproot, the branches regularly and alternately rebranched from above the middle; bark of new shoots tan to reddish, copiously red- or tan-tomentulose toward the tips; bark of one year old shoots reddish-brown, glabrous to sparsely hairy toward the tips; that of older wood gray-brown with raised, paler lenticels; leaf-apex rounded to broadly acute; base rounded, acute, more or less abruptly contracted to the short petiole 2-5 mm long; margin conspicuously revolute; surface of young leayes moderately red-hairy on the veins and veinlets below and sparsely appressed-red-hairy above; surface of mature leaves glabrous and dark green above, paler beneath with scattered hairs along the midrib alld veinlets; flowers pleasantly fragrant, on stout, erect to slightly nodding, redor orange-hairy peduncles from the axils of leaf scars of the preceding vear or flowering from the leaf axils of new shoot growth of disturbed shrubs; sepals about 1 cm long, ovate-triangular, red-hairy along the veins outside, glabrous within; outer petals white to pale pink, 3-7 cm long (-10 on sprouts fromi disturbed shrubs), oblong to ovate; inner petals ?/2-1/4 the length of the outer, white to maroon, oblong to hastate-lanceolate, saccate-based with a deep purple eorrugated zone on the lower part of the inner face; androecium globular, about 1 cm broad, pale green to pale pink at anthesis; gynoecium of 4-15 narrowly fusiform, appressed-red-hairy carpels; fruit sparsely hairy when young, aging glabrous to minutely hairy, 6-9 cm long, smooth or rugose with a prominent ventral suture; seeds 1-2 cm long, castaneous.
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert. 1960. A Revision of Asimina and Deeringothamnus (Annonaceae). Brittonia. 12 (4): 233-278.

description: Shrub (occasionally a small tree) 2-3 (-4.5) m tall from a stout-linear or sometimes branched root; primary shoots one to few, sub-erect to arching from the subterranean crown and branching alternately and regularly in one plane; bark of third year and older twigs glabrous, gray; that of second year wood glabrous, reddish-brown or light brown, with raised, pale lenticels; that of young shoots densely short red-tomentose toward the tips, sparsely so toward the base; leaves coriaceous, obovate to oblong, oblanceolate or ovate, 4--10 (-12) cm long+; apex rounded, emarginate, or obtuse; base rounded to subacute, more or less abruptly narrowing to the short (3-5 mm) petiole; margin scarcely to prominently revolute; young surface sparsely appressed-reddish- hairy above, densely so on the veins beneath, becoming glabrous and lustrous above and sparsely reddish-hairy on the veins beneath; flowers white (some- times with pink inner petals), 6-10 (-15) cm broad, fragrant, subsessile on the tips of new shoot growth or on densely red-hairy terminal peduncles no longer than 5 mm; sepals 0.5-1.5 cm long, elliptic to ovate, rounded, red-hairy along the veins on the outer surface, glabrous within; outer petals white, 4-6 (-8) cm long, oval to obovate, spreading, sparsely appressed-hairy along the veins outside, glabrous and impressed-veiny within; inner petals 1/5-1/2 length of the outer, oblong-oval to oblong or occasionally lanceolate, white or occasionally rose, slightly revolute, slightly saccate-based and with the basal 1/3-1/2 of the inner surface covered with purple corrugations, glabrous; androecium globular, 0.5-1 cm broad, pale green to pinkish at anthesis; gynoecium of from 3-8 (-11) narrowly fusiform sparsely appressed-red-hairy, glabrate carpels; fruit 5-9 cm long, short-oblong, terete to irregularly bulging, sometimes rugose, yellow-green when ripe; seeds 1-2 cm long, brown to eastaneous, in two irregular rows.
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert. 1960. A Revision of Asimina and Deeringothamnus (Annonaceae). Brittonia. 12 (4): 233-278.

description: Tall shrub or low tree 1-6 m tall from a stout, vertical taproot; bark of old wood gray-brown, that of new wood reddish-brown and reddish-tomentose toward the summit; winter buds globose, reddish-hairy, about 2.5 mm in diameter; leaves membranaceous, oblong-obovate to oblanceolate, 6-15 (-20) cm long; apex acute to acuminate; base more or less gradually attenuate to the short (0.5-1 cm) petiole; margin scarcely revolute; surface glabrous and bright green above, densely reddish-tomentose beneath when young, aging to sparsely red-hairy on the veins beneath; flowers maroon, 7-15 mm broad, with a faintly fetid aroma, subsessile or slightly nodding on reddish-hairy peduncles 0.3-0.8 cm long which develop from the axils of the prominent leaf scars; calyx 4-7 mm long, of three triangular-deltoid sepals which are striate with brown hairs on the outside, glabrous within; outer petals 1-1.3 cm long, fleshy, oblong to osvate, acute, with recurved tips, moderately reddish-hairy on 'the outside, glabrous and impressed-veiny within; inner petals about half the length of the outer, fleshy, ovate with strongly recurved tips and saccate bases which are incised- veiny within; androecium globular 4-6 mm in diameter, pale green at anthesis; gynoecium of 5-7 erect, fusiform, appressed-red-hairy carpels which surmount the receptacle; fruit 3-6 (-7) cm long, glabrate, oblong-cylindric, pale green in youth, ripening to a greenish yellow; seeds castaneous, 1-1.5 (-2) cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert. 1960. A Revision of Asimina and Deeringothamnus (Annonaceae). Brittonia. 12 (4): 233-278.

description: Dwarf shrubs, 2-3 dm tall from a stout, fusiform taproot; shoots one to several, sparingly branch or unbranched, reddish- to reddish-brown-barked, with pale, raised lenticels, sparsely appressed-rusty-hairy toward the tips when young, glabrate; leaves coriaceous, ascending-secund, variously shaped, obovate to cuneate or oblanceolate (rarely linear-elliptic), 4-7 (-11) cm long; apex rounded to obtuse or emarginate (occasionally acute) ; base acute to cuneate, tapering more or less gradually to the short twisted petiole 3-10 mm long; margin revolute; young leaf surfaces sparsely stippled with small appressed reddish hairs, in age dark green and glabrous above, paler and prominently reticulate beneath; flowers maroon, with a fetid aroma, nodding-seeund on slender peduncles 1.5-3 (-4) cm long, these arising singly from the axils of new shoot leaves; outer petals 1.5-3 cm long, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, pink with maroon streaks, or maroon, fleshy, revolute, with reflexed tips; inner petals 1/3-2/3 the length of the outer, deep maroon, ovate-acute to lance-ovate, fleshy and with a saccate base which on the inside is densely corrugated, the margins revolute, the tips abruptly recurved; androecium globular, 4-7 mm broad, greenish-white to pink at anthesis; gynoecium of from 2-5 narrowly fusiform, glabrate carpels; fruit curved, oblong-cylindric, 3-4 (-5) cm long, yellowish green when ripe; seeds about 1 cm long, brown, shiny, in two irregular rows.

description: Copiously and stiffly branched shrub to 1.5 m tall, the one to many primary shoots from a deep, linear or narrowly fusiform taproot; bark of old wood gray; that of second year wood brown to gray-brown, gray or pale-tomentose distally; that of new shoots reddish-brown to tan, with a light to dense coat of reddish-tan hairs toward the tips, leaves coriaceous, oblong to elliptic or cuneate, 5-8 cm long; apex acute, obtuse, or rounded-emarginate; base cuineate or abruptly rounded to the short (2-6 mm) petiole; margin strongly to moder- ately revolute; surfaces sparsely appressed-orange-hairy above, and densely so beneath when young, aging to glabrous and pale green above, sparsely hairy along the veins beneath, so pale beneath as to appear glaucous; flowers one to three per node, fragrant, nodding oIn slender, moderately orange-hairy peduncles 2-3.5 cm long, these developingr from the axils of the prominent leaf scars; calyx 8-10 mm long, of three (or four) trianaular-deltoid sepals which are striate with reddish hairs on the outside, glabrous within; outer petals 3-7 cm lonig, oblongo to oval or obovate, wavy margined, white, tan- or orange hairy on the outer vein-surfaces, glabrous and impressed-veiny within; inner petals 1/3-1/2 the length of the outer, lanceolate-hastate, revolute, fleshy, saccatebased, with the lower third of the inner face largely.covered by deep purple corrugations; androecium globular, 0.5 cm in diameter, pale green or pinkish at anthesis; gynoecium of from 3-8 fusiform, appressed-orange-hairy carpels; fruit short-oblonlg, 4-7 cm long, terete to irregularly bulging, glabrate, yellow-green when ripe; seeds 1-2 cm long, dark to pale browrn, lustrous, in two irregular rows.

description: Copiously and stiffly branched shrub to 1.5 m tall, the one to numerous primary shoots from a deep, narrow taproot; bark of old wood gray to gray- brown, that of second year wood brown to gray-brown and gray- or pale-tomentose toward the summit, that of new shoots reddish brown or tan, with color subdued by a dense blonde or whitish tomentum; leaves coriaceous, obovate to ovoid or elliptical (occasionally cuneate), 5-8 cm long; apex obtuse or rounded-emarginate; base rounded or abruptly narrowing to the short (2-6 mm) petiole; margin weakly revolute; surface densely white- or blonde-tomentose above and beneath when young, at maturity sparsely tomentose above and moderately so on the veins beneath; flowers 1-4 per node, fragrant, nodding on slender, densely blonde-hairy peduncles 2-3.5 cm long, these developing from the axils of the prominent leaf scars; calyx 8-12 mm long, of three (or four) triangular-deltoid sepals which are striate with orange hairs on the outside, glabrous within; outer petals 3-7 cm long, oblong to obovate, wavy-margined, white or yellowish white, tan-hairy on the outer vein surfaces, glabrous and impressed-veiny within; inner petals 1/3-1/2 the length of the outer, lanceolate- hastate, revolute, fleshy, saccate-based, with the lower 1/3 of the inner face largely covered by yellow corrugations; androecium 0.5-1 cm in diameter, pale green to pinkish at anthesis; gynoecium of 3-5 (-11) narrowly fusiform, pale, appressed-hairy carpels; fruit shortboblong, up to 8 cm long, terete to irregularly bulging, glabrate, yellow-green when ripe; seeds pale to rich brown, dull, 1-2 cm long.

description: Shrub 1-3 m tall from a stout-linear or sometimes branched taproot; primary shoots one to few, sub-erect to arching from the subterranean crown and branching alternately and regularly in one plane; bark of third year and older twigs glabrous, gray; that of second year wood glabrous,, reddish-brown or light brown, with raised pale lenticels; that of young shoots sparsely red tomentulose toward tho tips; leaves coriaceous, oblanceolate to elliptic or elliptic-spatulate, 5-10 cm long on undisturbed shrubs (-15 or -18 cm. long on disturbed shrubs); apex rounded to obtuse; base acutely narrowing to the petiole 2-3 mm long; margin slightly revolute; surface glabrous and rich green above, glabrate and paler green below, the reticulation evident; flowers pale to deep maroon, 2.5-3 cm broad, fetid, nodding or sub-erect on glabrate peduncles 1-2 cm long, these arising from the leaf axils on new growth; sepals three or four, about 1 cm long, elliptic or ovate, sparsely rusty-hairy along the veins on the outer surface, glabrous within; outer petals flesh-pink toward the tips, shading to maroon or maroon-striped toward the bases, 2-2.5 cm long, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, slightly revolute and recurved, sparsely stippled with pale hairs without, glabrous within; inner petals about half the length of the outer, maroon, ovate-acute or acuminate, saccate-based, revolute, and sharply recurved; androecium globular, 0.8-1.1 cm broad, pale green to pinkish at anthesis; gynoecium of from 3-11 narrowly fusiform glabrate carpels; fruit 5-9 cm long, oblong-cylindric with a prominent ventral suture, smooth to rugose, yellow-green when ripe; seeds 1-2 cm long, castaneous, in two irregular rows.
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert. 1960. A Revision of Asimina and Deeringothamnus (Annonaceae). Brittonia. 12 (4): 233-278.

description: Shrub or small tree 1.5-11 (-14) m tall from a stout, sometimes braliched, taproot; bark of older trees gray-brown, shallowly furrowed; that of new shoots moderately to copiously dark brown-hairy toward the summit, aging smooth, gray-brown; winter buds globose, dark brown-hairy, 2.5-5 mm in diameter; leaves membranaceous, oblong-obovate to oblanceolate, 15-30 cm long0; apex acute to acuminate; base more or less gradually attenuate to the short (0.5-1 cm) petiole; margin flat or scarcely revolute; young surfaces sparsely appressed- reddish-pubeseent above; densely so beneath, becoming glabrous above and sparsely hairy on the veins beneath; flowers maroon, 2-3 (-4) cm broad with a faintly fetid aroma, on densely dark brown-hairy, nodding peduncles (1-) 1.5-2 (-2.5) cm long which develop from the axils of the prominent leaf sears; calyx 8-12 mm long, of three triangular-deltoid sepals which are striate with brown hairs on the outside, glabrous within; outer petals 1.5-2.5 cm long, oblong- elliptic, with aseending bases and slightly to conspicuously recurved tips, copiously appressed-hairy along the veins outside, glabrous and impressed-veiny within; inner petals 1/3-1/2 the length of the outer, elliptic, saccate-based, recurved-tipped, glabrate without, glabrous and impressed-veiny within; andro- ecium globular, 0.5-1 cm broad, pale green at anthesis; gynoecium of 3-7 (-10) fusiform appressed-red-hairy carpels; fruit oblong-cylindric, 5-15 cm long, yellow-green to brownish when ripe; seeds 1.5-2.5 cm long, brown to castaneous, shiny when mature, bean-shaped, somewhat laterally compressed.
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert. 1960. A Revision of Asimina and Deeringothamnus (Annonaceae). Brittonia. 12 (4): 233-278.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms triquetrous, somewhat scabrous on the angles; leaves 40 cm. long, 15-18 mm. wide, serrulate-scabrous on the margins, rigid; sheaths 3-winged, the margins serrulate-scabrous; ligule short, ovate, rigid, margin cartilaginous; panicles axillary and terminal, much branched, pyramidal, conspicuously purplish; lower bract of the inflorescence foliaceous; bractlets capillary-setaceous; staminate spikelets ovoid, purplish, numerous; pistillate spike-lets few; pistillate scales broadly ovate, dark-purplish; hypogynium 3-lobed, irregularly laciniate; achene 1-2 mm. long, dark-purple or violet, depressed-globose, reticulate-rugose, the reticulations hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms robust, short-pilose, scabrous on the angles, 1-2 m. high; leaves 2-4 dm. long, 12-22 mm. wide, attenuate-acuminate, short-pilose, scabrous on the margins; sheaths broadly winged; ligule short-rotund, margin cartilaginous, pilose; inflorescence paniculate, oblong-pyramidal, yellow-brown, 10—20 cm. high, the rachis and branches short-pilose; bracts foliaceous; bractlets rather short, setaceous; staminate spikelets 3 mm. long, stramineous; pistillate scales ovate, ferruginous, glabrous or nearly so; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes white, deeply and irregularly laciniate; achene 1 mm. long, globose, smooth, white, shining.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Rhizomate non viso; culmis triangularibus, scabris, 75 cm. et ultra altis; foliis 5-10 mm. latis, 15-20 cm. longis, scabris; vaginis alatis, margine scabris; ligula brevi, triangulari, margine eartilaginea; paniculis terminalibus et pedunculatis ex axilla folii supremi, angustis, ramis paucis, erectis; bracteis elongatis, setaceis; spiculis 2 mm. longis, ellipticis; squamis foemineis ovato-orbicilaribus, abrupte breviterque acuminatis, brunneis; hypogynio atropurpureo margine undulato, ciliato; achaenio 2-3 mm. longo, globoso-oblongo, laevi, nitido, albido, ad apicem obtusam angustato.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1934. Studies in the genus Scleria. Brittonia. 1: 239-243.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms triangular, slightly roughened, 75 cm. tall or taller; leaves 15-20 cm. long, 5-10' mm. wide, scabrous; sheaths winged, the wing-margins scabrous; ligule short, triangular, margin cartilaginous; inflorescence paniculate; panicles terminal or also on slender peduncles in the axils of the uppermost leaf, narrow; branches few, erect; bracteal leaf elongate, setaceous; spikelets short, elliptic, 2 mm. long; pistillate scales ovate-orbicular, abruptly short-acuminate, brown; hypogynium low, purplish-brown, the margin undulate, eiliate; achene globose-oblong, tapering to an obtuse apex, smooth, shining, white, 2-3 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome elongate, 5 mm. or less thick, nodulose; culms slender, erect, 30-60 cm. high, sharply triangular, glabrous or nearly so, often glaucous; leaves 12-25 cm. long, 2-6 mm. wide, often glaucous, scabrous on the nerves and margins, glabrous, linear, the lower short, the upper elongate, somewhat revolute in drying; sheaths narrowly winged, pubescent or glabrous, the lower ones purplish-tinged; ligule short, ovate, scarious-margined, pubescent; inflorescence of 2-5 dense clusters, terminal and axillary, the lateral on long filiform peduncles, few-flowered, the peduncles scabrous on the angles, dilated towards the apex; bracts foliaceous, about 5 cm. long, ciliate; bractlets ciliate, pubescent on the back, linear-lanceolate; scales lanceolate-ovate, purplish-tinged, mucronate; hypogynium a narrow obtusely triangular border supporting 8 or 9 small tubercles, which are hemispheric and white-pulverulent; aehene 3-4 mm. long, ovoid, white, shining, shorter than the scales, obtusely pointed.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome thick, nodose, hard; culms 4-5 dm. high, triquetrous, channeled, somewhat scabrous; leaves 15-20 cm. long, 4-5 cm. wide, scabrous, especially beneath, very short and wide, elongate-oblong, very abruptly narrowed near the tip, forming an obtuse lobe on each side of the acuminate apex, acute, serrate on the margin near the tip; sheaths loose, winged, glabrous, the lower aphyllous; ligule nearly 1 cm. long, rigid, lanceolate-triangular, woolly; inflorescence paniculate, panicles usually 2, terminal and in the axil of the uppermost leaf, conic, dense, 5-10 cm. high, the lateral short-peduncled, smaller; rachis minutely pubescent; bracts foliaceous; bractlets capillary-setaceous, puberulent, elongate; staminate spikelets 4 mm. long, oblong, short-peduncled; scales membranaceous, rigid, ovate, ferruginous, puberulent, acute or submucronate; hypogynium deeply 3-lobed, the lobes incised-dentate; achene much exceeding the scales, subglobose, umbonate, smooth, shining, white, 2-3 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome thick, horizontal, nodulose; culms sharply triangular, somewhat pilose, strict, angles retrorsely scabrous, 0.3-2 m. tall; leaves lanceolate, flat, somewhat pilose, margins and nerves beneath scabrous, about 30 cm. long, 2-5 cm. wide; sheaths broadly 3-winged, pubescent, wing-margins scabrous; ligule short, ovate, obtuse, rigid, pilose, margin cartilaginous; panicles terminal and axillary, purplish; rachis and branches often densely pilose; bracts foliaceous; bractlets conspicuous, setaceous-subulate; staminate spikelets ellipsoid-oblong, 4 mm. long; scales purplish, the pistillate ovate-orbicular, abruptly acuminate, pubescent; hypogynium 3-lobed, irregularly laciniate, dark-purplish-tinged; achene 4 mm. long, white subdepressed-globose, strongly rugose-tuberculate, tubercles hairy or sometimes glabrate.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms 1 m. or more tall; leaves 15-30 cm. long, 10-18 mm. wide, minutely pilose above, glabrous beneath, about the same width from base to near the apex (“marginibus conspicue parallelism), then abruptly narrowed and terminated by a caudate tip 4 mm. long; sheaths ample, minutely pilose upwards; ligule 7-10 mm. long, broadly ovate, obtuse, pilose, the margin scarious; panicles terminal and axillary, 4 cm. high, conic, 3-4 cm. broad, rather open, the lateral ones remote, on long slender peduncles; bracts f oliaceous; bract-lets numerous, conspicuous, linear-setaceous, up to 5 cm. long; spikelets 4 mm. long, ellipsoid-oblong, solitary, sparse; scales ovate-lanceolate, red-brown; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes short, ovate, truncate, spreading; aehen ovoid-triangular, white, minutely transversely verrucose, 2-3 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizomes 5 mm. or less thick, elongate, hard, nodulose, clustered; culms erect, simple, somewhat scabrous on the angles, triquetrous, 20-50 cm. high, glabrate or hairy (villous in some forms), stiff, usually tufted; leaves 15-20 cm. long, 2 mm. wide or less, rigid, few, glabrate or short-pubescent (villous in some forms), scabrous on the margins, somewhat channeled; sheaths short-pubescent or sometimes villous; ligule short, obtuse, rotund; inflorescence consisting of a few spikelets in a terminal cluster or sometimes 1 or 2 axillary clusters, the lateral remote, on long filiform peduncles; bracts overtopping the culm, erect, ciliate or glabrate (conspicuously fringed in some forms), bractlets ciliate or glabrate; spikelets few-flowered; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, purplish-tinged, midrib ciliate; hypogynium a narrow triangular border bearing 6 usually finely pulverulent globose tubercles disposed in pairs (in var. kansana each set of tubercles consists of 2 large and 1 small); achene 1-2 mm. long, apiculate, white, globose, transversely verrucose-papillate, the lower papillae pointed downwards, elongate. Consists of several races, varying mainly in pubescence and number of tubercles.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome creeping in mud, horizontal; culms densely tufted, sharply 3-angled, 60-90 cm. tall, scabrous on the angles; leaves 3-4 dm. long, 3-8 mm. wide, glabrous, scabrous on the nerves beneath; sheaths narrowly 3-winged, or nearly wingless; ligule lanceolate, rigid, obtuse; inflorescence narrow, few-flowered, terminal, 8-10 cm. high; bracts elongate, foliaceous; bractlets short, linear; spikelets oblong, stramineous; pistillate scales ovate-orbicular, abruptly acuminate, shorter than the achene; hypogynium-margin ciliolate, cup-shaped, truncate or obscurely 3-lobed, about 1 mm. high; achene 2-3 mm. long, ovoid-globose, white or discolored, smooth, shining.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Rhizome short, thick, branched; culms loosely pilose, slender, strict, erect, 3-4 dm. high; leaves 15-20 cm. long, 2-4 mm. wide, densely pilose, scabrous on the margin, channeled, the midrib prominent beneath and rough; sheaths densely pilose; ligule oblong, obtuse, densely pilose; inflorescence of 1 or 2 rather dense clusters, 2-4 cm. long, the lateral with a slender long peduncle which is loosely hirsute; bracts foliaceous, overtopping the culm, sparsely pilose; bractlets rigid, hirsute; staminate spikelets oblong-lanceolate, 5 cm. long; staminate scales lanceolate, acuminate, pubescent; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, acute; hypogynium with 3 rounded appressed lobes; achene 2-3 mm. long, pubescent, transversely verrucose, abruptly apiculate, subglobose, white or sordid.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Annual, with fibrous roots; culms slender, erect, 1.5-4 dm. high, villous or glabrous; leaves sparsely pubescent with spreading hairs, 1-2 mm. wide; sheaths villous; ligule short, triangular, pubescent, or none; infloreseence interruptedly glomerate, 2-8 cm. high, of 2-12 glomerules; bractlets narrow, ciliate with long hairs; scales lanceolate- acuminate, long-pilose; hypogynium none; achene 1-2 mm. long, white, reticulate, globular, the base short-attenuate, trigonous, with a row of pits on each side.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome thick, hard, nodose; culms 1-2 m. tall, coarse, strict, sharply triquetrous, channeled, angles scabrous, minutely pubescent; leaves 30 cm. long and longer, 8-20 cm. wide, very scabrous on the upper side all over and on the margins and veins beneath, minutely pubescent, attenuate-acuminate; sheaths winged, wings scabrous on the margins, minutely pubescent; ligule ovate, obtuse, densely white-pubescent; panicles 2-5, terminal and axillary, purplish, the terminal ones 5-15 cm. long, the rachis densely white-pubescent; bracteal leaf foliaceous; bractlets elongate, capillary-setaceous, to 4 cm. long, scabrous; spikelets oblong, 3 mm. long, staminate scales lanceolate-ovate, purple, mucronate, minutely white-pubescent; pistillate scales ovate-orbicular, abruptly acuminate, minutely white-pubescent; hypogy-nium low, pale, 3-lobed, the lobes deeply and conspicuously fimbriate; achene 3-4 mm. long, ovoid, shining, equaling or exceeding the scales, white, minutely and sparsely tuberculate, the tubercles each bearing a tuft of white hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome thick, nodose, elongate, usually purplish-brown; culms 0.5-3 m. high, rather slender, erect, glabrous, sharply triangular, slightly rough on the angles; leaves 14-45 cm. long, 5-15 mm. wide, obtuse, glabrous, margin scabrous; sheaths narrowly 3-winged; ligule 4-10 mm. long, ovate-triangular, margin cartilaginous, pilose; inflorescence green or yellow-brown, sometimes purplish-tinged, the panicles 3 or 4, axillary and terminal, the rachis minutely pubescent or glabrate, triquetrous; panicles pyramidal, 5-15 cm. high; bracteal leaf foliaceous, equaling the stem; bractlets filiform, setaceous-capillary; spikelets greenish-brown or purplish-tinged; staminate scales lanceolate, acuminate; pistillate scales ovate-orbicular, abruptly acuminate, the tip frequently recurved, usually straw-colored, sometimes purplish-tinged; hypogynium depressed, 3-lobed, the lobes broad, rounded, ciliate or glabrous; achene 1.5-2.5 mm. long, smooth, white or yellow-brown, depressed-globose or sometimes pointed, apex subumbonate.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Perennial by a slender, horizontal rhizome; culms very slender, 2-6 dm. tall, glabrous, triangular; leaves 15-25 cm. long, 1-2 mm. wide; glabrous, not overtopping the culm; sheaths glabrous; ligule minute or none; infloreseence lax; branches capillary, erect, 5-15 Cm. high; rachis pilose to glabrate; spikelets oblong, in sessile fascicles along the sides and at the tips of the branches; branchlets ovate, red-brown, glabrous, inconspicuous; scales dark-brown, glabrous, ovate, mucronate; hypogynium none; achene smooth, shining, depressed-globose, 1 mm. long, white, shorter than the scales.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Annual with fibrous roots; culms very slender, tufted, erect, 12-30 cm. high, glabrous; leaves slender, erect or flexuous, hardly exceeding 10 cm. long, 1 mm. wide or less, glabrous; sheaths glabrous; ligule minute or none; inflorescence terminal, loosely paniculate, few-headed, rachis filiform; branches few, short, distant, very slender; clusters few, small, subglobose, 2 mm. long; bracts minute, scarious; bractlets linear-lanceolate, glabrous; spikelets few, short; scales ovate, short, acute, membranaceous, the midrib green and conspicuous; hypogy-nium none; achene 0.75-1.0 mm. long, globose, shorter than the scales, white, densely echinate .

description: Rhizome not seen; culms 1 m. tall or taller, robust, glabrous, much branched, sharply triquetrous; leaves 2-3 dm. long, 7-14 mm. wide, very scabrous on the margins, glabrous, rigid; sheaths glabrous, somewhat winged, the wing-margins scabrous; ligule terminated by a large rotund scarious appendage 1.5 cm. long; panicles terminal on each branch, dense, rigid, 5—10 cm. high, 4—7 cm. wide; rachis minutely pubescent; bracts foliaceous, greatly exceeding the inflorescence; bractlets linear-setaceous, stramineous; staminate spikelets very numerous; pistillate spikelets few, usually solitary at the bases of the panicle-branches; scales ovate-lanceolate, stramineous, acute to slightly mucro-nate; hypogynium-margin horizontal, not lobed; achene 2-3 mm. long, trigonous, ovoid, smooth, minutely pubescent, discolored, shorter than the scales, apiculate.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome very short, roots fibrous, capillary; culms triangular or somewhat compressed, glabrous, 20-50 cm. tall, slender, erect, somewhat scabrous below on the angles; leaves few, 10-20 cm. long, 1-3 mm. wide, flat, thin, not overtopping the culm; sheaths narrowly 3-winged, the wings smooth or somewhat scabrous, the sheaths otherwise glabrous; ligule short-rotund; panicles terminal and axillary, the lateral remote, sessile or on short erect peduncles each 1-3 cm. high, few-flowered; bracteal leaf exceeding the culm; bracts linear-setaceous, glabrous, elongate; staminate spikelets lanceolate, stramineous; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, straw-colored; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes lanceolate, obtuse, appressed to the base of the achene; achene 1-2 mm. long, conspicuously reticulate, globose, dull-white, mucronulate.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Annual with fibrous roots; culms 30-40 cm. high, extremely slender towards the apex, triangular below, compressed above, usually purplish near the apex, the angles retrorsely scabrous; leaves 10-20 cm. long, 2 mm. wide, rigid, erect, long-attenuate, the margin scabrous; sheaths glabrous; ligule short, ovate, obtuse, hairy; inflorescence paniculate, lax, few-flowered, the rachis slender, purplish; bracts linear-setaceous, elongate, the base purplish; bractlets linear-setaceous, elongate, the base purplish; spikelets few, remote; scales lanceolate-ovate, aristate, pale, purplish-tinged; hypogynium dark-purple, obscurely lobed, the lobes broad, the margin pale, reflexed; aehene 3 mm. wide, white, shorter than the scales, ovoid, smooth, shining, obtuse at the apex.

description: Annual, with capillary fibrous roots fragrant in drying; culms simple, triquetrous, glabrous, 1-6 dm. high, slender or filiform, erect, sometimes minutely pubescent; leaves 0.5-3 dm. long, shorter than the stem, 0.5-2 mm. wide, glabrous, linear or filiform, flat; sheaths usually pilose; infloreseence interruptedly glomerate, simple, of 2-8 erect glomerules, 4-15 cm. long; spikelets 2-3 mm. long, castaneous, few- flowered, alternate, sometimes appearing as if verticillate, sessile; bracts glabrous, 6-7 mm. long, often caudate; bractlets glabrous; scales glabrous, oblong-lanceolate, red-brown, keeled; hypogynium none; achene 1 mm. long, reticulate or verrucose, trigono-globose, white, fragile, mucronate, about 5-porose just above the attenuate trigonous base.

description: Rhizome thick, hard, nodose, covered with red-brown scales; culms  2 m. tall or taller, coarse, shining, sharply trigonous, angles somewhat roughened or smooth; leaves rigid, to 60 cm. long, 1-2 cm. wide, margins and main veins very scabrous, glabrous; sheaths triangular, angles scabrous, the lower red-brown, wingless; ligule rotund-triangular, bearing a greatly elongated (1-2 cm.) scarious appendage; panicles terminal, single, or a smaller one in the upper axil, ovate to ovate-rotund, dense, much branched, 8 cm. long, 8 cm. broad; rachis hirsute; branches short, divergent; bracts about 3, foliaceous, exceeding the inflorescence; bractlets narrow, linear-setaceous, stramineous; staminate spikelets numerous, linear, 5-6 mm. long, on pedicels 5-10 mm. long; pistillate spikelets few, solitary at the base of the branches, 1-flowered; staminate scales linear-lanceolate, acute, purplish; pistillate scales ovate-lanceolate, long-acuminate, membranaceous, stramineous, purplish-tinged; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes short, lanceolate, acute, white, shining; achene 3-4 mm. long, pyramidal, the apex acute, white tinged with violet, short-hispid.

description: Probably perennial; culms about 1 m. tall, stout, triquetrous, glabrous; leaves subcoriaceous, 3-5 dm. long, 6-12 mm. wide, glabrous, equaling the culm, nerves and margins scabrous; sheaths glabrous, somewhat retrorsely scabrous on the angles; ligule short, rotund-triangular, hairy or glabrous; inflorescence virgate, terminal; branches elongate, triquetrous, scabrous, very remote, slender; spikelets solitary or few together, remote, the lower often sessile in the axils of branches, 3-4 mm. long; bracts short-lanceolate; pistillate scales ovate, short, acuminate, keeled; hypogynium none; achene fragile, sordid-white, tuberculate-rugose, trigonous, 2-3 mm. long, mucronate, the base short, triquetrous.

description: Rhizome horizontal, elongate, nodose, hard; culms 50-80 cm. tall, sharply triquetrous, somewhat channeled, scabrous on the angles; leaves linear, acuminate, 30-45 cm. long, 8-10 mm. wide, scabrous on the margins and nerves; sheaths not winged, many-nerved, glabrous, very scabrous on the angles, the lower without blades, purplish; ligule rigid, short, rotund-obtuse, glabrous, the margin cartilaginous; inflorescence paniculate, the panicles terminal and 1 ox 2 axillary, pyramidal, the terminal branched, the lateral nearly simple, branches several, upright, rachis triangular, scabrous on, the angles; bracteal leaf foliaceous; bractlets linear-setaceous, elongate; spikelets loose, 4-5 mm. long; staminate scales lanceolate; pistillate scales broadly ovate-lanceolate, the exterior abruptly long-acuminate, brown, the interior acute or obtuse, brown; hypogynium narrow, obscurely 3-lobed, the lobes rotund-obtuse; achene 3 mm. long, subglobose, white, shining, short-hairy, equalling the scales.

description: Rhizome not seen; culms triquetrous, sparsely pilose, the angles smooth, 1 m. high or taller; leaves 15-30 cm. long, 6 mm. wide, glabrous above, minutely pubescent beneath, scabrous on the margins, especially so near the tip; sheaths narrow, triangular, striate, minutely hirsute, angles smooth; ligule truncate, short, densely pubescent; inflorescence loose, terminal and in the axils of the uppermost leaves, the terminal 10-15 cm. long, the axillary shorter, branches few, divaricate, rachis minutely pubescent; bracts foliaceous, nearly as long as the panicle; bractlets linear-setaceous, elongate; spikelets solitary, compressed, the staminate on elongate (1-1.5 cm. long) peduncles, the pistillate on shorter peduncles; scales green, with the margins purple-blotched, the staminate apparently distichous, lanceolate-acuminate, the pistillate 4-6, distichous, ovate-acuminate; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes rotund-obtuse, margin involute; aehene shorter than the scales, globose-elliptic, 4 mm. long, white, minutely verrucose, sparsely pilose, the beak often curved.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Rhizome horizontal; culms slender, 0.5-2 m. tall, sharply triquetrous, glabrous; leaves 15-30 cm. long, 5 mm. wide, linear, 3-nerved, glabrous; sheaths glabrous, often purplish; ligule rotund-ovate, pilose, 3 mm. long; inflorescence paniculate, few-branched, terminal and 1 or 2 axillary, the terminal one 5-10 cm. high, the others smaller; bracts linear; bractlets setaceous-subulate; spikelets oblong; pistillate scales ovate-orbicular, short-mucronate, purplish; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes thick, wrinkled; achene 2 mm. long, elliptic-globose, white, shining, minutely apicnlate.

description: Herbaceous plant, seasonally dormant, flowering simultaneous with young leaf bud or with fully mature leaf. Underground stem in young plants a short, thick rhizome, later changing into a subglobose or globose tuber with somewhat excentric main stem, to ca. 10 cm diam., ca. 9 cm high, whitish to greenish, developing several isolated or grouped, globose or short fusiform propa- gules, these 0.7-1 cm long, ca. 0.7 cm diam. Leaf petioles 10-70 cm long, 0.7-2.5 cm diam., smooth, green or dark olive green to purplish; lamina broadly obcor- date, entire in young plants, pinnatifid in mature plants, 10-40 cm X 10-40 cm, slightly leathery; lobes narrowly acute or acuminate, to ca. 14 cm X ca. 4 cm, upper surface slightly glossy green. Inflorescences 1 or 2 per season; peduncle 25-45 cm long, 0.9-1.2 cm diam., smooth, glossy, green; spathe elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, cymbiform, slightly or more strongly nodding forward, open almost to the base, 6-8 X 3-4 cm, margins curving inward, apex acute, outside and inside semiglossy, green to blackish green; spadix entirely adnate to the spathe, slightly shorter than spathe or nearly as long, 5-7.5 cm long; male flowers arranged longitudinally along the midrib; female flowers in two longitudinal rows, one on each side of the male zone, reaching to 2/3 the length of the male zone or to the top of the male zone; male flowers synandriate; filaments fused to form a long column; connectives slightly produced, knob-like, ca. 0.5 mm long and broad, free or only slightly fused at the base, off-white; female flowers surrounded at the base by 5-7 rod-shaped staminodes; ovaries ovate, whitish, locules 5-7, uniovulate; style elongate, green; stigma star-shaped, 5-7-lobed, pale yellow. Infructescence with persistent spathe, to 14 cm long. Berries depressed- globose, ca. 1 cm diam., green with greenish pulp, 3-7 seeded. Seeds elliptic, laterally flattened, ca. 8 mm X 4 mm, outer seed coat pale brown, inner seed coat bright red.
bibliographicCitation: Hetterscheid, W. L. A., et al. 2003. Two new species of Araceae tribe Spathicarpeae from Bolivia. Brittonia. 55: 37-41.

description: Perennial herbs with a subterranean root crown; stems erect or ascending, 30-40 cm tall, densely hirtellous throughout with hairs 0.5-0.9 mm long giving a whitish appearance; stipules membranous, free, ovate-triangular to subulate, 3-6 x 2-5 mm, the lowermost auriculate, hirtellous; leaves 8- 10 cm, the petiole 1-2 cm; leaflets 15-19, subopposite, petiolulate, elliptic to ellipticovate, emarginate, 9-12 x 6-9 mm, with appressed hairs 1-2.5 mm, denser on the abaxial surface; peduncles axillary, erect, shorter than the leaves, 3-5 cm long, dense- ly hirtellous; racemes 2-5 cm long x 2-2.8 cm diam., densely 10-30-flowered; bracts subulate, 5-8 mm long, sparsely hirtellous on the adaxial surface, persistent; pedicels 1-2 mm, caducous; calyx urceolate-globose, 9-10 mm, densely hirtellous, lacking black hairs, the tube 4-5 x 3-5 mm, the teeth narrowly subulate, 4-5 mm long; petals blue, the banner elliptic, emarginate, 16 x 8 mm, the wings auriculate, 13 x 3 mm, with the claw 5 mm long and the lamina 5 mm long, the keel ? 11 x 3.2 mm, with the claw 5 mm long and the lamina 6 mm long; sta- mens 9 + 1 +11 mm long and the free portion 2 mm; ovary subsessile, hirtellous; ovules 2 pairs; pod shortly pedicelled, suboblong, inflated, 6-8 x 4-6 mm, a little compressed laterally, contracted at the apex, with persistent style remnants, strigose, covered by the calyx; seeds 4, the testa smooth.

description: Perennial herbs with a taproot and subterranean root-crown; stems erect or ascending, 30-50 cm tall, hirtellous through- out with hairs 0.5-0.8 mm long, the young stems and foliage densely white-villous; stipules membranous, free, ovate-triangular to lanceolate, 2-5 x 2-5 mm, the lowermost slightly auriculate, slightly hirtellous or glabrate; leaves 5-8 cm long, the petiole +/- 1 cm; leaflets 17(-23), subopposite, petiolu- late, elliptic-obovate, emarginate, 5-20 x 4-10 mm, with scattered appressed hairs on the adaxial surface, slightly denser on the abaxial surface; peduncles axillary, erect, longer than the leaves, 5-15 cm long, 0.5- 1.8 mm in diam., hirtellous; racemes 3-10  cm long, loosely 10-20-flowered; bracts subulate, 3-5 mm long, sparsely hirtellous on the adaxial surface, persistent; pedicels slightly recurved, +/- 2 mm long in fruit, falling with the ripe fruit; calyx suboblong-ur- ceolate, 8 mm, covered with black hairs and scattered long white hairs, the tube 4-5 x 3-5 mm, the teeth triangular-subulate, 3 mm long; petals blue-violet, whitish at the base, the banner oblanceolate, emarginate +/- 14 x 6 mm, the wings auriculate, +/- 12 x 2 mm, with the claw 4 mm long and the lamina 8 mm long, the keel +9 x 3.5 mm, with the claw 4 mm long and the lamina 5 mm long; stamens 9 + 1, +/- 9 mm long and the free portion 1.9 mm; ovary subsessile, hirtel lous; ovules 2 pairs; pod shortly pedicelled, suboblong, inflated, +/- 6 x 4 mm, a little compressed laterally, abruptly contracted at the apex, with persistent style remnants, strigose, covered by the calyx; seeds 4, mitten-shaped, +/- 2.3 x 2 mm, brownish-red, the testa smooth, shiny.

description: Shrub, 2-3 m tall. Young branchlets densely pubescent with mostly simple and bifurcate, but also stellate and minute glan- dular hairs; older stems glabrate. Leaves lanceolate, 2.5-7.5 cm long, 0.5-1 cm wide, apices long acuminate, apiculate, bases narrowly cuneate, margins serrate, blades scabrous throughout, with mostly stellate and less abundantly bifurcate and simple hairs (these largely confined to the midvein, secondary veins, veinlets, and margins), and minute glandular hairs throughout; midvein raised above and below, with an inconspicuous multi-aperturate nectary ca. 2 mm from the leaf base below, nectary elliptic, ca. 1-2 mm long; secondary and tertiary veins also visible below; petioles 2-5 mm long, densely pubescent; stipules acicular, 2-4 mm long, sparingly pubescent, persistent. Infiorescences axillary, 1-3(+?)- flowered; peduncles ca. 1-2 mm long, pubescent; pedicels to ca. 8 mm long, articulated ca. 3 mm below the calyx, pubescent, subtended by 3, acicular bracts, sparingly pubescent, persistent, ca. 1-2 mm long. Ca- lyx 5-lobed, the lobes broadly lanceolate, joined briefly at the base, ca. 3 mm long, reflexed at anthesis, sparsely pubescent with mixed simple, bifurcate, and stellate hairs abaxially, minutely glandular pubescent adaxially. Petals 5, unguiculate, the claw filiform, ca. 6 mm long, glabrous, the lamina ± trapezoidal, ca. 1-1.5 mm long, ca. 1 mm wide, the lower lamina margin divided into 2 rounded lobes, each lobe basally ciliate, the upper lamina margin retuse to emarginate, the adaxial surface with 2 fleshy teeth, the abaxial surface with a terete appendage, ca. 0.5-1 mm long, inserted in the middle of the petal lamina near the apex. Androgynophore to ca. 3 mm tall, glabrous; staminal column campanulate, ca. 0.5-1 mm tall; stamens 5, anthers 3-thecate, filaments ca. ½ the length of the staminal column; staminodia 5, lobes ± triangular, fleshy. Ovary globose, style simple, short. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Dorr, Laurence J. 1996. Ayenia saligna (Sterculiaceae), a new species from Colombia. Brittonia. 48: 213-216.

description: Herbacea; caules erecti, 50-60 cm alti, non ramosi, glabrescentes, teretes; folia (petiolo alato 7-10 mm longo basi auriculato) lanceolata, 3.5-6 cm longa, 8-17 mm lata, basi et apice acuminata, basi in petiolum protracta, apice acuminata, nervo medio supra applanato, anguste sulcato, subtus prominulo, nervis lateralibus 2 vel 3 ascendentibus, supra pilis brevibus rigidis incrassatis scabra, subtus ad nervos pilis brevibus antrorse adpressis obsita, utrinque glandulo-punctata, margine minute serrata, membranacea; pedunculi 1 vel 2 axillares, 7-8 mm longi, dense et breviter pilosi; bracteolae lineari-subulatae, ad apicem pedicelli 2-2.3 mm longae, pilosulae; calycis lobi exteriores ovati, 7-8 mm longi, posticus apice bifidus, 4-nervus, nervis extus antrorse pilosis, laterales acuminati, 1-nervi, ad nervum pilosi, omnes margine ciliati, interiores lineari-subulati, 6-7 mm longi, uninervi, nervo et margine ciliati; corolla rubra vel purpureo-rubra (ex Ekman), tubulosa 7 mm longa, intus pilosa, lobis rotundatis 0.5 mm longis; stamina 4, inclusa, filamentis glabris, staminum posticorum 1.5 mm longis, anticorum 2.5 mm longis, antheris ellipticis; ovarium ovoideum, glabrum, 2 mm longum; stylus complanatus glaber, 3-4 mm longus, stigmatis lobis incrassatis, subspathulatis, apice rotundatis; capsula oblonga, apice rotundata, 4 mm longa, glabra, laevis; semina obovoidea, brunnea, reticulata, 0.6-0.7 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: Liogier, Alain H. 1968. Novitates Antillanae. III. Brittonia. 20: 148-161.

description: Arbores parvae caulibus foliisque dense puberulis, folia aliquantum discoloria plus minusve ferruginea; flores solitarii, calyx dense pubescens valde costatus 1.5 cm longus; corolla flava sine centro vinoso, 3-3.5 cm; styli et stigmata ca. 16; fructus ignoti.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. & Guadarrama Olivera, M. A. 2001. New Mexican species of Byttneria (Sterculiaceae), Bakeridesia (Malvaceae), and Triumfetta (Tiliaceae). Brittonia. 53: 59-65.

description: Treelet 3-4(-9) m tall; trunk slender, smooth, gray. Leaves densely pubescent with white, short, curved trichomes, partially glabrescent but persistently pubescent on midribs and petiole; petiole 1.5-3(-4) cm long, semiterete, slightly canaliculate adaxially, usually more densely pubescent adaxially at distal end; leaflets sessile to short petiolulate, obovate to elliptic, conspicuously black-punctate on both surfaces, the adaxial surface densely short-pubescent but (sub-)glabrescent, abaxial surface persistently pubescent to glabrescent, domatia densely hairy, margin entire to irregularly and slightly crenulate, flat to slightly revolute, apex obtuse and often emarginate, seldom acute, base attenuate in the terminal leaflet, obtuse and strongly asymmetric in the lateral ones; terminal leaflet 3.5-5.5(-8) X 1.4-2.5 cm, lateral leaflets 2.5-4(-7) X 1.5-2.5 cm. Inflorescence densely and many-flowered, 5-10 cm long; peduncle 2- 5 mm long or absent; first-order branches (paraclades) ca. 12, opposite, 4-9 cm broad, densely short-villous with white, curved trichomes; bracts and prophylls linear-lanceolate, short-villous. Pedicel 1-2 mm long, glandular-punctate, pubescent. Sepals green, suborbiculate to broadly ovate, 0.5 mm long, pubescent to glabrous abaxially. Petals white to cream-colored, oblong, obtuse at apex, attenuate at base, ca. 2 X 1 mm, pellucid-punctate, entire to slightly erose. Stamens ca. 1 mm long, filaments white, anthers yellow, ovoid. Samara 1.8-2.4 cm diam., the wings 1-2.4 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Pirani, José R. 1998. A revision of Helietta and Balfourodendron (Rutaceae --- Pteleinae). Brittonia. 50: 348-380.

description: Tree (6-)9-25(-32) m; trunk erect, 25- 80(-100) cm diam. Bark pale gray, smooth. Leaves initially pubescent but soon (sub-) glabrous; petiole (2-)3-8 cm long, semiterete, articulated at apex; petiolules 2-13 mm long; leaflets obovate-oblong to narrowly elliptic, punctate only on the abaxial surface, both surfaces with trichomes persistent only on the main nerve, abaxial domatia densely hairy to subglabrous, margin entire and flat to slightly revolute, apex acuminate to acute, rarely obtuse, base attenuate to cuneate on the terminal leaflet, strongly attenuate-asymmetric on the lateral ones, terminal leaflet 7-13(-15) X 2-5 cm, lateral leaflets 5.5-11.5 X 1.6-5 cm. Inflo- rescence generally loose, many-branched, (7-)14-19 cm long; peduncle 1-2 cm long, densely appressed-pubescent with short, white, curved trichomes or glabrescent; first-order branches (paraclades) (3-)8-10, usually subopposite to sometimes opposite, patent, (5-)9-14 cm long; bracts and pro-phylls linear-lanceolate, short-pubescent, ca. 0.8 mm long. Pedicel 1.6-2.3 mm long, pubescent. Sepals green, suborbicular to broadly ovate, ca. 0.8 mm long, pubescent without. Petals white to cream, oblong, ob- tuse at apex, subunguiculate at base, ca. 2.5 X ca. 1.5 mm, pellucid-punctate, entire. Stamens ca. 1 mm long, filaments white, anthers yellow, ovoid. Samara (2.5-)4.5-6 cm diam., the wings (2.5-)3-5 cm long.

description: Liana; foliorum petiolus 6-10(20) mm longus, aureo-tomentoso-sericeus, apice supra 2 glandulis magnis protuberantibus instructus; lamina 6.0-12.8 cm longa, 2.9-6.5 cm lata, ovata vel elliptica, basi cordata, apice obtusa vel acuta, supra glabrata, subtus dense appresso-sericea. Inflorescentia axillaris, aureo-tomentoso-sericea; racemus umbellarum 4-florarum vel racemulorum congestorum 6-flororum; bracteae bracteolaeque 1.2-1.5 mm longae, triangularae, involucratae, sparsim sericeae vel glabratae; pedicelli sessiles vel subsessiles, 6-10 mm longi, 0.4-0.6 mm diametro, sericeii. Petala lutea, 4 lateralia limbo orbiculari, longe fimbriato vel lacerato, petalum posticum ungue crassiore apice constricto, limbo obovato, longe fimbriato fimbriis basalibus apice glanduliferis. Filamenta staminum 3 sepalis anticis et 2 petalis posticolateralibus oppositorum quam ceteris filamentis paene duplo longiora; filamenta 3 staminum posticorum gracilia et inter stylos posticos inflexa; connectiva staminum 3 sepalis anticis oppositorum quam ceteris connectivis multo majora, globosa tumidaque. Stylus anticus rectus et erectus, styli posteriores lyrati, quam antico longiores. Fructus ignotus.
bibliographicCitation: Gates, Bronwen. 1979. New names in Banisteriopsis and Diplopterys (Malpighiaceae) of the Guayana Highland. Brittonia. 31: 108, 109.

description: Liana; folia coriacea, petiolo 5-14 mm longo, lamina 4.5-12.2 cm longa, 2.3-10.0 cm lata, ovata vel orbiculari, basi cordata, apice obtusa vel apiculata, margine revoluta, subtus basi juxta costam 2 glandulis sessilibus et distaliter margine vel sub margine glandulis nonnullis minutis instructa, supra glabra, subtus sparsim appresso-sericea vel glabrata, venis nervos laterales conjungentibus prominulis et scalariformibus. Inflorescentia axillaris, appresso-aureo-sericea, cymosa, floribus (2-)3-7-jugis secus ramulos ultimos; bracteae bracteolaeque usque 1.0 mm longae, triangulares, sparsim sericeae, involucratae; pedicelli sessiles 8-12 mm longi, appressosericei. Petala lutea, longe fimbriata; petalum posticum ungue distaliter latiore et concavo, limbo fimbriis basalibus apice glanduliferis. Filamenta staminum 3 stylis oppositorum (i.e. sepalo antico et petalis postico-lateralibus oppositorum) quam ceteris 7 filamentis longiora; connectiva staminum 3 sepalis anticis oppositorum tumida globulosaque loculos superantia. Styli recti parallelique, 2 postici quam antico parum longiores et interdum divergentes. Samara pilis appressis, irritantibus conspersa, trabecula 1.0-1.5 mm longa; nux carpophoro filiformi instructa; ala e tertia parte superiori marginis distalis nucis enascens, basi angusta distaliter dilatata.

description: Liana; foliorum petiolus usque 20 mm longus, apice biglandulosus, lamina usque 20 cm longa, 9 cm lata, ovata vel lanceolata, apice acuminata, margine parum revoluta et glandulis minutis instructa, supra glabra, subtus sparsim appresso-sericea, reticulo utrinque prominenti. Inflores- centia ex paniculis axillaribus congestis constans; bracteae bracteolaeque 0.8-1.2 mm longae, late triangulares, involucratae, sericeae; pedicelli sessiles vel subsessiles, 6-12 mm longi, 0.4-0.6 mm diametro, fructiferi crassiores. Petala citrina, 4 lateralia ungue brevi limbo denticulato vel subintegro; petalum posticum ungue longiore et suberecto, limbo basi fimbriato. Filamenta staminum sepalis oppositorum quam filamentis petalis oppositis longiora, ea petalis postico- lateralibus et sepalis antico-lateralibus opposita inter se paene aequilonga et postice inclinata; connectiva staminum sepalis oppositorum longiora obovataque, illa staminum petalis opposi- torum anguste oblonga. Styli aequales, e basi divergentes, apice inflexi, stigmatibus terminalibus. Samarae nux pilis appressis brevibus et flexuosis conspersa, utrinque ala laterali usque 3 mm lata instructa; ala dorsalis 18-32 mm longa, 11-15 mm lata, sparsim appresso-sericea vel glabrata, basi marginis adaxialis appendice 1-2 mm alta instructa.

description: Trees 5-12 m tall or woody vines; vegetative stems initially sericeous, soon glabrate, eventually forming punctate or somewhat elongated lenticels. Lamina of the larger leaves (8) 11-25 cm long, (3) 4.5-10 cm wide, obovate to nearly elliptical, attenuate and somewhat decurrent at the base, flat or very slightly revolute at the margin, short-acuminate or acute or occasionally obtuse or rounded at the apex, plane, with the veins and reticulum prominent on both sides, probably initially sericeous, at least on the midrib below, but quite glabrate at maturity, bearing typically 2 glands near the base and 2 in the distal 1/3 between the midrib and margin but sometimes 0 or 4 in either area; petiole (7) 10-22 mm long, initially sericeous but soon nearly or quite glabrate. Inflorescence (including peduncles and pedicels) thinly sericeous to eventually glabrescent; bracts 2-4.5 mm long, triangular to subulate, eglandular, often deciduous in anthesis and usually deciduous before maturation of the fruit; primary peduncle (from inflorescence axis to first joint) (5) 10-27 mm long; bracteoles 1-2.5 mm long, ovate to triangular, eglandular or abaxially callose at the base, often deciduous before maturation of the fruit; pedicel 7-20 mm long. Calyx glands 3.5-6 mm long, with ca 3 mm on the calyx and 0.5-3 mm decurrent on the pedicel, glabrous; sepals beyond glands 1.5-2 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide. Petals glabrous or with a few hairs at base of claw; outermost petal (one of the antero-lateral pair) with the limb 6.2-7.5 mm long and wide, deeply concave, the margin mostly erose and membranous; other 3 lateral petals with the limb 4-5.5 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, obovate and somewhat concave to flat, the margin + bluntly dentate and eglan- dular or more often glandular-thickened; posterior petal with the claw thicker, the limb 4-5.5 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, obovate and flat, the margin dissected with the rounded segments glandular-thickened all around or at least in the proximal 1/2. Filaments 1.2-1.5 mm long; anthers 1.5-2.1 mm long opposite the sepals, 0.7-1.5 mm long opposite the petals, glabrous. Perigynous cup glabrous on the inner face opposite the ovary. Ovary 2-2.5 mm high, very tightly sericeous; styles 2.5-3 mm long, straight in bud, slightly spreading in anthesis, stout, narrowing abruptly at the apex, with the stigma distinctly internal. Samara (45) 52-65 mm long, thinly sericeous to glabrate; nut 16-25 mm long, 9-11 mm wide, the ventral areole 16-25 mm high, 7-10 mm wide, ovate; dorsal wing (27) 34-50 mm long, 17-23 mm wide, flabellate to elliptical to falcate. Torus 8-12 mm high.

description: Liana lignosa; lamina foliorum bullata, margine revoluta, apice plerumque obtusa vel rotundata, pilis plerumque persistentibus in costa abaxiali; petiolus 2-3 mm longus, pertinaciter sericeus vel demum glabrescens in dimidio distali; inflorescentia pilis laxis; 4 petala lateralia subaequalia; filamenta 2.5 mm longa; antherae 2-2.5 mm longae, laxe sericeae; styli 4 mm longi, distaliter inflexi in alabastro; ovarium laxe sericeum; samara 39-43 mm longa.

description: Woody vines to 8 m; vegetative stems densely sericeous to soon glabrate, punctate-lenticellate. Lamina of the larger leaves 7.5-10.5 cm long, 3.5-4.6 cm wide, obovate or elliptical, attenuate or cuneate at the base, revolute at the margin, rounded or obtuse at the apex or very abruptly slightly acuminate, bul- late, with the veins and reticulum white and prominent on both sides, thinly sericeous to glabrate on both sides with some hairs usually persistent on the abaxial midrib, bearing 2-4 small ill-defined glands proximally near the midrib and 2-4 distally between the midrib and margin; petiole 2-3 mm long, densely and + persistently sericeous or eventually glabrescent on the distal ?2. Inflores- cence tomentose or loosely sericeous and eventually glabrescent; bracts and brac- teoles 1-2.7 mm long, narrowly triangular or subulate, eglandular, caducous or soon deciduous, the bracteoles borne slightly to distinctly below the joint; primary peduncle (from inflorescence axis to first joint) 4-14 mm long, loosely sericeous; pedicel 20-25 mm long, thinly sericeous and glabrescent. Calyx glands 5-6 mm long, with ca 3.5-4 mm on the calyx and 1-2 mm decurrent on the pedicel, pilose on the margins; sepals beyond glands 2 mm long and wide. Petals glabrous or thinly sericeous abaxially on the claw; lateral petals with the limb 6.5-8.5 mm long, 6-8 mm wide, deeply concave (outermost) to moderately concave, erose or subentire with the margin mostly slightly glandular-thickened or the outermost with the margin membranous; posterior petal with the claw thicker, the limb 6 mm long, 4.5 mm wide, obovate and flat, the margin dissected with the rounded segments largest at the base and smaller distally, all distinctly glandular-thickened. Filaments 2.5 mm long; anthers 2.3-2.5 mm long opposite the sepals, 2.0 mm long opposite the petals, the locules loosely sericeous. Perigynous cup sericeous on the inner face opposite the ovary, the hairs medifixed. Ovary 3.5 mm high, loosely sericeous; styles 4 mm long, with the distal 0.5 mm bent inward in bud and partly straightened in anthesis, slender, tapering gradually distally, with the stigma nearly apical. Samara 39-43 mm long, puberulent on the nut, distally glabrous at maturity; nut 15 mm long, 9-10 mm wide, the ventral areole 14-15 mm high, 5-6 mm wide, narrowly ovate; dorsal wing 25-30 mm long, 15 mm wide, roughly elliptical, the adaxial margin recurved, the abaxial ± straight or curved upwards. Torus 6 mm high.

description: Eight species. Spreading shrubs or subshrubs 0.5-2.5 m tall, densely stellate-pubescent to glabrate, sometimes viscid, the stems sometimes with purplish nodes. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate, usually cordate, serrate or dentate to subentire, acute or acuminate, usually soft-pubescent, often discolorous. Flowers solitary (or clus- tered) in the leaf axils, commonly aggre- gated into racemes or panicles; involucel absent; calyx usually ribbed, usually pubes- cent, equal to and clasping the fruit; petals 0.5-1.5 cm long, white to pale lavender; staminal column greatly shortened (rudi- mentary), the filaments 3.5-9 mm long, slender, erect; styles 3-4, pallid, slender, the stigmas dark, capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, obovoid, pubescent; mericarps 3 or 4 (rarely 5), apically rounded, more or less divided into an upper and lower cell, the upper 2-seeded, the lower 1-seeded, the upper cell dehiscent; seeds somewhat pubescent, the seed of the lower cell more prominently so. 2n = 30 (five species).

description: Ten species. Trees or large shrubs, the (young) herbage stellate-pubescent, the hairs very small with many radii. Leaves petiolate, the blades narrowly to broadly ovate, usually unlobed, often discolorous, truncate to deeply cordate, entire or serrate, with palmate venation, acute or acuminate. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, the flowers glomerulate or paniculate, subses- sile or short-pedicellate; calyx basally rounded, ca. half-divided; petals yellow Fruits schizocarpic, stellate-pubescent, oblate; mericarps 5-16, apically muticous, acute, or spinose, sometimes obscurely den- tate dorsally; seeds solitary, pubescent or glabrous. 2n = 28 (one species).

description: Tree, to 20 m tall. Twigs more or less terete, rather densely, minutely puberulous when young, glabrescent with age. Terminal buds densely yellowish brown tomentel- lous. Leaves alternate, firmly chartaceous, 5.5-12 x 2.5-5 cm, elliptic, base and apex acute, glabrous on upper surface, minutely appressed pubescent on lower surface (es- pecially on young leaves), lateral veins 5-7 on each side, midrib and lateral veins immersed on upper surface, slightly raised on lower surface, tertiary venation finely areolate-reticulate, visible on both surfaces. Petioles 6-12 mm long, shallowly canaliculate. Inflorescences axillary, 5-10 cm long cymosely paniculate, sparsely puberulous. Flowers hermaphrodite, greenish yellow, sparsely pubescent, the hairs short, erect. Tepals 6, equal or nearly so, broadly triangular, ca. 1 mm long. Stamens 6, representing the outer 2 whorls, 2-celled, broadly triangular, the filament short and broad, in- serted at the base of the tepals, filaments pubescent; staminodia 6, those representing whorl III columnar, the lower half densely pubescent, with 2 large glands attached near the base, those representing whorl IV min- ute, with some hairs near the base. Ovary glabrous, gradually narrowed into the style; shallow receptacle densely pubescent inside. Tepals and stamens dehiscent in old flowers, leaving the ovary exposed on the ped- icel. Fruits unknown.

description: Shrub to 5 m tall. Mature stems and older branches slightly fissured, glabrous; bark gray to dark gray; twigs subterete, dark gray or dark brown, glandular-hispid. Leaves coriaceous, flat, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 4.2-7.6 x 1.3-3.1 cm, base cuneate, rarely obtuse, apex acuminate or cuspidate, margin glandular-ciliate to serrate, both surfaces glabrous or adaxial surface and midvein glandular-hispid; petiole subterete, flattened adaxially, 4-7 mm long, glandular-hispid. Inflorescence a terminal raceme, 9-12-flowered; rachis 2.2-9.2 cm long and 0.8-1.1 mm diam, dark gray or dark brown, glandular-hispid; bracts lanceolate, flat or sometimes involute, 3-5 x 0.6-0.9 mm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to acute, margin glandular-ciliate, both surfaces glabrous or the abaxial surface glandular-hispid; pedicels ascending, 21-35 mm long and 0.2-0.4 mm diam, glandular-hispid; bracteoles inserted along basal 1/2 of the pedicel, linear to lanceolate, involute, 2.4-3.8 x 0.3-0.4 mm, base truncate, apex acuminate, margin glandular-ciliate, both surfaces glabrous or glandular-hispid. Flowers 7-merous; calyx 4.1-4.2 mm long; tube 1.5-2.2 mm long and 2.9-4 mm diam, dark brown to brown, glandular- hispid; lobes widely ovate, apex acute, 2.2-3 x 1.7-3.3 mm, longest lobe 2.6-3 mm long, margin entire or ciliolate, abaxial surface glandular-hispid, tomentose or glabrous; corolla tubular, pink; petals imbricate, undulate, oblanceolate, 21.5- 31 x 4-6.5 mm, margin entire, lamina distally slightly tomentose; stamens exserted (less than 1.2 times the petal length) or subequal to corolla, 24.5-32.5 mm long; filaments tomentose; anthers 2.1-2.5 mm long and 0.6-1.3 mm wide, glabrous; ovary glabrous; style exserted, ca. 36.5 mm long; stigma capitate. Capsules not seen; seeds not seen.

description: Subshrub; stems erect, to 1 m tall, slender, ca 5 mm in diameter, probably broader near base, the internodes to 8 cm long, above reddish or green, strigose to hirsute, below brown to gray, glabrescent. Leaves opposite, subequal to unequal; blades elliptic to broadly elliptic or obovate, 4.5-10.0 cm long, 2.2-4.2 cm wide, membra- nous, the apex acuminate, the base cuneate, the margins entire, above dark green, strigose or hirsute, below lighter green, strigillose, especially along the prominent veins; petioles 0.6-2.2 cm long, strigose. Inflorescences in the upper leaf axils, one- flowered; peduncles lacking; pedicels slender, erect, 2.5-4.0 cm long, 1 mm thick, broader toward the apex, hirsute. Flowers showy; calyx lobes erect, lanceolate, 1.7- 2.4 cm long, to 4 mm wide, the apex attenuate, the midvein prominent and thick, the lateral veins parallel, the margins thin, translucent, entire, green, both sides strigil- lose; corolla orange, equalling or shorter than the calyx lobes, the tube slightly oblique in the calyx, funnel-form, ca 2.2 cm long, 5 mm in diameter at the base, 10 mm in diameter at the throat, sightly ventricose above the middle, outside pilose or strigose, inside pubescent, the lobes rotund, ca 7 mm across, the margins entire; sta- mens included, the filaments curved, adnate to the base of the corolla tube for ca 10 mm, the free part ca 5 mm long, the anthers broadly sagittate, 2 mm long, 3 mm wide; disc annular, surrounding the base of the ovary, irregularly lobed; ovary oblong, 5 mm long, 3 mm in diameter, hirsute above the middle, the style ca. 1.2 cm long, densely puberulent, the stigma stomatomorphic. Mature berry and seeds not seen; immature fruit surrounded by the persistent calyx lobes.

description: Suffrutex terrestris erectus 0.2-0.4 m altus, non ramosus, caulibus superne perspicue hirsutis, pilis patentibus eglandulosis elongatis 2-5 mm longis hyalinis multicellu- laribus albidis; foliis per paria subaequalibus, petiolis 1.8-3.5 cm longis dense hirsutis, laminis membranaceis elliptico-obovatis vel ovato-ellipticis vel inferioribus sub- oblanceolatis 5-14 cm longis 2.2-6 cm latis apice acutis vel subacuminatis basi cuneatis supra atroviridibus subtus pallidioribus, utrinque moderatim villosis etiam supra strumosis, pilis 2-3 mm longis hyalinis multiseptatis, marginibus crenato- serratis, dentibus 25-35 utroque latere apice glandulosis, nervis lateralibus 9-11-jugis supra sulcatis subtus leviter elevatis; floribus 1-3 in axillis supremis foliorum vel terminalibus epedunculatis, pedicellis 3-6 mm longis dense eglanduloso-hirsutis; calyce flavo-viridi 1.5-2.7 cm longo post anthesim amplectente, tubo 1.5-2 mm longo, lobis falcato-lanceolatis acuminatis vel breviter subcaudatis inaequalibus 1.2-2.5 cm longis infra medium 3-5 mm latis integris intus glabris dorso et in marginibus villosis, pilis 1-3 mm longis; corolla non calcarata flava 26 mm longa, tubo late cylindrico vix ventricoso in fauce non contracto 5-18 mm longo basi 6 mm lato fauce 5.5 mm lato utrinque glabro, lobis inaequalibus patentibus, majoribus tribus inferioribus sub- orbicularibus rotundatis integris vel leviter remote undulatis apice saepe emarginatis 5.5-7 mm longis 6-7 mm latis, minoribus duobus superioribus late obovato-oblongis 5 mm longis 3-4 mm latis subintegris vel emarginatis utrinque glabris; staminibus inclusis, filamentis basi ad corollam 6-7 mm adnatis basi ampliatis parce ciliolatis ceterum glabris, antheris cohaerentibus subquadratis vel subreniformibus 1 mm longis 1.5 mm latis glabris; ovario conico in stylum attenuato glabro; stylo superne glabro infra medium pilosulo; disco annulari subintegro.

description: Shrub; stems short, slender, ca 5 mm in diameter, the internodes to 8 cm long, strigose-sericeous near the apex, nearly glabrous below. Leaves opposite, nearly equal in a pair; blades lanceolate, 5-9 cm long, 1.5-3.2 cm wide, subcoriaceous, the apex acuminate, the base acute or cuneate, the margin entire, above dark green, at first glandular, soon becoming glabrous, below lighter green, sparsely strigillose, the veins darker and prominent; petioles 3-8 cm long, strigose. Inflorescences in the upper axils, of one or two nearly sessile flowers per axil, usually only one; peduncles lacking; pedicels very short, 1-3 mm long, strigose. Flowers with the calyx lobes erect, lanceolate, 1.5-1.8 cm long, 2-3 mm wide, outside strigose, inside nearly gla- brous except at the entire margins, the midvein subprominent, slightly keeled at the base; corolla orange, somewhat oblique in the calyx, tube ca 1.1 cm long, narrowly funnel-form, 2 mm in diameter at the base, slightly broader (to 4 mm wide) above, nearly glabrous at the base, strigillose toward the limb, inside glandular, the lobes semi-orbicular, ca 4 mm long, 5 mm wide, the margins subentire, ciliate; stamens included, the filaments curved, adnate at the base of the corolla tube for ca 3 mm, the free part 4-5 mm long, glabrous, the anthers broadly sagittate, 1.5 mm long, 2 mm wide, coherent in 2 pairs by their apices, the staminode 3 mm long, bearing a short infertile anther; disc semi-annular at the base of the ovary, with a gap on the lower side, irregularly lobed; ovary ovoid, ca 3 mm long, glabrous, the style 5 mm long, glabrous, the stigma stomatomorphic. Berry surrounded by the persistent calyx, ovoid to globose, ca 1 cm long, white, glabrous, the apex prominent; seeds ellipsoid, ca. 0.5 mm long, deeply striate, light brown.

description: Trees large with rounded crown, the leaves dense. Infloreseence to 30 cm long, diffuse, often leafy at the base, the first internodes of the lowest branches often very long producing a flat-topped or corymbiform panicle; peduncles and pedicels pubeseent with a short golden-brown tomentum,n. Calyx greenish-maroon or maroon; sepals nearly equal in size and shape or quite irregular; inner sepals membranaceous and yellow or pinkish, usually the longest and broadest, 5-12 mm long, usually short-clawed or slightly tapering to the base, oblong, ovate or nearly rounded with obtuse or rounded apex, the margins slightly villous and the exposed areas with short golden tomentum; outer sepals the smallest, thick, firm, concave, 3-7 mm long, oblong with broad base and obtuse or rounded apex, the outer surface covered with a short golden tomentum. Corolla of 4 petals (a fifth one infrequently present), white with yellow base, and often pinkish on the outside, or with the veins, claws and crests reddish) ; upper petals 8-20 mm long, the hairy claws 1/3-1/9 the total length, the blade oblong or rounded, membranaceous and glabrous; lateral petals 8-18 mm long, with short hairy claws not exceeding 1/3 the length of the petal, the blade oblong or rounded; membranaceous and glabrous; fifth petal, when present, resembling a diminutive form of the lateral petal or of equal size. Stamens 6-8, 20-30 mm long; filaments red or white, often of two different lengths within a flower, with the longer ones most common in a staminate flower. Fertile pistil large, dark rose-red or pink; ovary glabrous, the style pubescent.

description: Trees large with rounded crowns, the leaves fairly dense. Inflorescence to 25 cm long, a pyramidal or ovoid panicle; peduncles and pedicels glabrous or rarely pubescent with short golden-brown tomentum. Calyx deep red, irregular; inner sepals and ineluded margins membranaceous and light red, 5-12 mm long, with a very short claw or at least a narrow base, oblong or, obovate; outer sepals 3-10 mm long, concave, thick and firm, oblong to ovate, glabrous or with a short tomentum on the outer surfaces and slightly villous on the margins. Petals 4 (the fifth infrequent), purple or intensely red or rarely pink; upper petals 10-25 mm long, the slightly villous claw 1/3-3/4 the length of the petal, the blade oblong or rounded, glabrous and membranaceous; lateral petals 10-23 mm long, the slightly villous claw usually 1/4-1/2 the length of the petal, the blade oblong, membranaceous, glabrous or with a short tomentum; fifth petal, when present, minute or the same height as-the lateral petal but more narrow. Stamens 6-8, 25-30 mm long; filaments red, often of two lengths, the shorter stamen included in the perfect flowers, the longer ones exserted in the staminate flowers. Functional pistil dark red; ovary glabrous, the style slightly villous.

description: A B. mucronato foliolis tantum ciliatis, rhachidibus et pedunculis laete strigosis-sericeis glabres- centibus, bracteis 0.6-1 mm longis, et capsula ad apicem puberula differt.
bibliographicCitation: Rico-Arce, María de L. 1987. Acacia sousae (Leguminosae: Mimosoideae), a new species from Mexico. Brittonia. 39: 130-132.

description: Herb, erect, usually rhizomatous; stems usually several from a single root system, unbranched or sometimes with 2-several crowded short branches at tip, occasionally branched in lower portion, mostly 10-38 cm long, 2-4 (5) mm thick, retrorsely strigose-sericeous with hairs ca 0.3-0.6 mm long, also obscurely sparsely glandular-puberulent with minute hairs less than 0.05 mm long, soon glabrescent, the apical (leaf-bearing) part to 4 cm long, abundantly pilose among leaf-bases and base-scars with erect hairs ca 0.5-1 mm long, at base of apical portion with a dense retrorse skirt of stiff hairs 1-2 mm long, these sometimes lost on older stems. Leaves pseudo-verticellate at stem apex, to 25 per stem, impari-pinnate with terminal leaflet reduced to a bristle-like mucro, 11-26-jugate; petiole 0.6-2 cm long, thickened at base, sparsely strigose-sericeous and obscurely and minutely glandular-puberulent, glabrescent; blade linear, mostly 6-15 cm long, 1.6-3.4 cm wide, sometimes smaller; rachis pubescent like petiole; leaflets sensitive to touch, longest at middle of leaf, gradually reduced toward apex and especially base, the basal leaflets obliquely deltate-ovate, 3.5-11 mm long, 2.3-4.5 mm wide, the middle leaflets obliquely oblong-rectangular, broadest at base, 7-16 mm long, 2.6-5 mm wide, at 65-80º to rachis, the base truncate, the distal leaflets very obliquely elliptic, broadest at or above middle, 7-14 mm long, 2-5 mm wide, at 25-45º to rachis, the base truncate on proximal side, very gradually rounded on distal side, dark green above and whitish green beneath (fresh), the margin usually with scattered appressed cilia, obscurely serrulate to entire, otherwise glabrous, the apex rounded or obtuse to a mucro to 0.5 mm long, secondary veins numerous, faint (sometimes conspicuous beneath), subparallel, branching and often reticulate, extending to thickened marginal vein; petiolule off-center toward proximal side of leaflet, fleshy, extremely short, much broader than long; young leaves very pale green with red rachises; bracts thick, lanceolate, to 4 mm long, mixed in with petioles and peduncles. Inflorescences up to 9 per stem, long-pedunculate, the flowering axis globose to cylindrical, to 1.3 cm long, with 1 or 2 flowers open at one time; peduncles 5-24 cm long, 0.5-1.5 times as long as leaves, glabrous to lightly strigose-sericeous; bracts very crowded, ovate to subquadrate, squamate, 0.6-1 mm long, glabrous, keeled with much thickened midvein extending into a short blunt somewhat inward-turned tip; bracteoles 2, smaller than bracts; pedicels 6-13 mm long, mostly patent or slightly reflexed, glabrous. Sepals lanceolate to lance-elliptic, 4-6 mm long, 1-2.2 mm wide, minutely and sparsely puberulent with thick, glandular hairs less than 0.05 mm long, superficially appearing glabrous except in bud, 7-15-nerved, green, the tip narrowly acute to acute, persistent and slightly accrescent in fruit; corolla white or very pale pink, with yellow eye and pink veins, the lobes oval-elliptic, usually broadly so, 4-6 mm long, ca 3.5 mm wide, the tube 2-3 mm long, broadly campanulate; stamens 10, dimorphic, longer filaments 3-3.5 mm long, sparsely puberulent, shorter filaments 2.5-2.8 mm long, glabrous; anthers cream-colored, 0.6-0.8 mm long; pistil 5-carpellate, surpassing stamens in length, the ovary distally puberulent; styles 3.5-4.5 mm long, lightly connate 2/3 or less of their length, puberulent in basal part; stigmas minute, minutely bifid. Capsule oblong, with rather abruptly rounded apex, 4-4.5 mm long, strigillose near apex and in basal part of persistent styles, also sparsely minutely glandular-puberulent, generally shorter than persistent calyx lobes, each carpel 1-5-seeded, opening flat at dehiscence; seeds red-brown, ellipsoid-triquetrous, flattened and more or less 2-edged in cross-section, the edges rounded, 1.5-1.8 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, ca 0.6 mm thick, one margin strongly convex, the other slightly so, shiny, longitudinally obscurely tuberculate.

description: Herba perenne, caudice simplici vel raro ramoso, caulibus infernis pubescentibus supernis glabris 10-20 cm altis, foliis basalibus petiolatis oblanceolatis vel obovatis 4-10 mm longis 1-4 mm latis laxe pubescentibus, foliis caulinis sessilibus auriculatis lanceolatis 4-8 mm longis 0.5-2.3 mm latis, sepalis 1.5-2.5(-3) mm longis 0.6-1.2 mm latis pubescentibus, petalis 3-4.5(-5.5) mm longis 0.6-1.4 mm latis anguste oblanceolatis insuper lavandulaceis subter albis, pedicellis fructiferis late divaricatis 3-8 mm longis plerumque glabris, siliquis late divaricatis acutis glabris 2-3 cm longis nervo centrali nullo vel obscuro, seminibus uniseriatis anguste alatis.
bibliographicCitation: Dorn, Robert D. 2003. A new species of Boechera (Brassicaceae) from Utah and Colorado. Brittonia. 55: 1-3.

description: Perennial herb; caudex simple or rarely branched. Stems several from crown, erect to ascending, 10-20 cm high, with spreading simple or forked hairs toward base, becoming glabrous upward; basal leaves many, oblanceolate to obovate, 4-10 X 1-4 mm, narrowing to a short petiole, acute to obtuse, entire or few-toothed, loosely pubescent with spreading hairs which are mostly 2- or 3-branched; cauline leaves few toward base, mostly lanceolate, sessile, auriculate, 4-8 X 0.5-2.3 mm, bluntly acute, mostly few-toothed, occasionally entire, hairs like on basal leaves but becoming very sparse or none on uppermost leaves. Flowers: sepals 1.5-2.5(-3) X 0.6-1.2 mm, pubescent with spreading branched hairs at least toward tip; petals 3-4.5(-5.5) X 0.6-1.4 mm, narrowly oblanceolate, lavender at tip, white toward base; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long. Fruiting pedicels widely spreading, 3-8 mm long, glabrous or rarely with a few hairs. Siliques widely spreading, acute, glabrous, 2-3 cm long, the midnerve usually lacking or obscure; style 0.1-0.2 mm long; seeds uniseriate, oval to suborbicular, ca. 1 mm long, narrowly winged.

description: Planta prostrata, caulibus fistulosis, glabris vel puberulis; radice crassa dauciformi; cymulis paniculatis axillaribusque, pedunculis validis rigescentibus semel vel bis ramificantibus, floribus glomeratis, perianthio limbo 2-2.5 mm longo cylindro-campanulato, anthocarpio fusiformi vel clavato, porcis glabris, sulcis glandulosis.
bibliographicCitation: Fosberg. 1988. New and Noteworthy Plants from Great Barrier Reef Sand Cays, Australia. Brittonia. 40 (1): 52-65.
