description: Description: A woody vine; staminate flowers: pedicels short or obsolete; bractlets 2, tiny, elliptic, about 0.5 mm. long and 0.12 mm. wide, acute at apex, very densely long-pubescent on the outer surface with distinct subvillous, brown, and spreading hairs; sepals 6, the 3 outer ones ovate, 0.8-1 mm. long, 0.5-0.6 mm. wide, acute at apex, very densely long-pubescent on the outer surface with distinct subvillous, brown, and spreading hairs, the inner 3 broadly obovate, thin-textured, about 1.5 mm. long and 1.2 mm. wide, subacute at apex, subacute or broadly obtuse at base, not cuneate, densely short-pubescent on the outer surface with appressed strigose antrorse hairs; petals 6, broadly obovate, 3-lobed, about 0.75 mm. long and wide, the central lobe trian- gular, distinct, acute at apex, larger than the 2 lateral ones, glabrous throughout; stamens 6, separate to base, 0.5-0.75 mm. long, the fila- ments approximately equal in diameter throughout or slightly ampliate at the very apex, obscurely longitudinally ridged, glabrous throughout, the anthers not immersed in the connective, opening by longitudinal slits.

description: Low perennial subshrub with erect branches; stems glabrate, weakly angular; leaves 5-nerved, 15-20 mm long, 20-25 mm broad, rhomboid, simple to slightly 3- lobed, cuneate, undulate, coarsely serrate, glabrous above and below, with char- acteristic musky odor when handled; foliar nectaries single, medially positioned; petioles 5-15 mm, scabrous near juncture with laminas, sparingly so elsewhere; stipules 1 mm, subulate, glabrous, sessile, caducous; peduncles 5-20 mm, axillary, articulate near center with small bract at articulation, punctate, surmounted by three large involucral nectaries; involucels of nine bractlets in three groups; bractlets 2 mm, triangular, punctate; calyces 7-8 mm, shallowly 5-lobed, costulate (costae green; intercostal areas scarious), epunctate, calyx lobes ovate, 3-5 ribbed, becoming torn in flower to pseudo-bilabiate form; petals 2 cm, punctate, externally dark purple with green margins (where exposed in bud), internally with dark spots covering lower third; staminal columns punctate, dark-purple; anthers numerous, dark-purple; anther masses ellipsoid; pollen cream-colored; styles exceeding androecia, punctate, yellowish; stigmas clavate, dark-purple; fruits 1 cm, globose, rostrate, 3-4 loculed, weakly strigose, punctate; seeds 5-6 mm, turbinate, densely sericeous; seed hairs up to 5 mm, nearly straight, creamy-tan.

description: Perennial subshrub; stems minutely puberulent, becoming glabrate, weakly angular, punctate; stem hairs ca 0.1 mm, often simple; leaves 3-5 nerved, 8-25 mm long, somewhat broader than long, suborbicular or partially 3-lobed to deeply dissected, truncate to cuneate; leaf segments obovate to linear, dentate, minutely ciliate-margined, minutely puberulent to glabrate, punctate especially on margins, having characteristic odor when handled; foliar nectaries 1-3 (or rarely lacking), incon- spicuous, medially positioned; petioles about equaling lamina, minutely puberulent (esp. on adaxial surface and near juncture with laminas) to glabrate, triquetrous, punctate; stipules 2-6 mm long, 1 mm broad, triangular, puberulent to glabrate, caducous; peduncles axillary, 4-25 mm, articulate near base and hence often appear- ing non-articulate, with small bract at articulation, minutely puberulent to glabrate, punctate, surmounted by 3 large involucral nectaries; involucels of 9 unequal bractlets irregularly disposed in three groups; bractlets 2-5 mm, triangular, the central one of each group often the longest, punctate, puberulent to glabrate, sometimes irreg- ularly adnate to one another; calyces 8-10 mm, very shallowly 5-lobed, costulate, green along veins, white between veins, punctate, becoming torn in flower and fruit; calyx lobes rotund-apiculate (nearly reduced to short teeth), 3-ribbed (central vein extending beyond margin to form a curved, pubescent mucro), minutely puberulent to glabrate without, sparingly short-pubescent at apices within; petals 15-25 mm, prominently punctate, sulfur-yellow, with large maroon spots covering basal half of petals; staminal columns maroon; anther masses globose; styles slender, exserted, nearly equaling petals; stigmas clavate, maroon; fruits 15-25 mm long, 6-9 mm broad, 3-loculed, sparsely pilose, punctate; seeds 5-7 mm, copiously hairy; the hairs nearly straight, tan or brown, 6-8 mm.

description: Plants acaulescent, epiphytic. Leaves in a subspreading to subascending rosette, 33-44 (48) cm long; blades (18) 20-24 (36) cm long and 3.6-5 cm wide, green suffused with maroon to entirely maroon, ligulate to broadly triangular, apex acute to acuminate; sheaths (12) 15-17 (19.5) cm long and 6-8.4 cm wide, obovate, castaneous, usually with a coating of cinerous trichomes. Scape de- curved, (34) 38-44 cm long and about 0.4 cm in diam; bracts (13) 17-23 (33) cm long and 3-4.2 cm wide, the blade and sheath portions not well differentiated, ascending to erect, becoming divergent or spreading near apex, enfolding the scape in the sheath area, usually red-pink, at times suffused with green or rarely entirely green, ligulate to subligulate or broadly triangular, apex acute. Lateral branches spreading, (0.9) 1.2-1.7 cm long, collaterally 2-flowered, peduncles 0.9-1.4 cm long, rachis wanting to 1.3 cm long. description: Plants acaulescent, epiphytic. description: Liana; stems glabrous to villous or sparsely sericeous, with sparse circular lenticels, tuberculate, fleshy. Trichomes malpighiaceous. Tendrils bifurcate, glabrous to sparsely sericeous in the ramification, adhesive discs not seen; scales ± 0. 1 cm long, triangular, glabrous, ciliate. Stipules 0.2-0.3 cm long X 0.1-0.2 cm wide, elliptic, herbaceous, glabrous to sericeous, the base gibbous, ciliate. Petioles 1.3-12.3 cm long, canaliculate, sparsely sericeous to sericeous; leaves imparipinate, with proximal to medial leaflets decompound or not, sometimes absent or reduced on distal portion of reproductive shoots, 5.2-26.3 cm long X 5.4-37.4 cm wide, the rachis 3.1- 24.1 cm long, sparsely sericeous to sericeous, the pinnae 7-15 per leaf, 0.9-18 cm long X 0.6-14 cm wide, with rachilla 2.1- 13.1 cm long; leaflets 1-15 per pinna, 0.6- 7 cm long X 0.7-2.8 cm wide, the leaflets or segments of leaflets elliptic, oval to cir- cular, membranous, glabrous to subsericeous on adaxial side, variously sparsely sericeous to hirsute on abaxial side, the base rounded, reniform to oblique, the apex acute, obtuse, rounded to obcordate, the margin denticulate. description: An erect perennial herb 3-5 dm. high, simple, woody at the base above a tuberous root, rather succulent, without tendrils, non-twining; stem unbranched, flexuous, brown-pustulate, curly-tomentose; internodes 2-3 cm. long; leaves undivided, irregularly dentate, rectangular-oblong, bluntly acuminate, truncate at base, 6-9 cm. long, 4-7 cm. wide, palmately 5-7-nerved, the secondaries and terti- aries ending in marginal dentations, white-pubescent below especially along veins, sparsely so above, slightly scabrous; petioles 1-2 cm. long, pubescent; inflores- cence eymose, terminal, and opposite upper leaves, the peduncles strong, pubes- cent, 10-12 mm. long, bearing distally and at base of secondary peduncles, char- taceous, brown, ciliate, acuminate bracts 1 mm. long; petals 4, greenish, coriaceous, broadly lanceolate, 1.5 mm. long, connate into a eaducous cap, glabrous; stamens 4; ovary 1-celled, 1 ovule developing, 3 aborting.

description: Liana; stems puberulent, terete. Trichomes not branched and not secretory mixed with secretory trichomes. Tendrils not seen. description: Liana; trichomes long and unbranched, whitish in living plants, brownish in specimen preserved in alcohol; branches terete, striate. Tendrils unbranched, devoid of scales. Stipules 6-7 mm long, subfalcate, hirsute. Leaves simple, drying brownish in specimens preserved in alcohol; petioles 5-7 cm long, cylindrical, hirsute; blades 9.5-11.4 x 9.2-12.5 cm, cordiform, papery, the base sagittate, the apex acuminate and apiculate, the margin dentate. Inflorescences compound cymes, 1.3-3.1 x 0.6-1.9 cm, flat-topped, with secondary branches abbreviated or not; peduncle 0.7-2 cm long; bracts triangular, 0.4-1.7 mm long, hirsute; pedicels (0.5-)1-1.4 mm long. Flower buds botuliform, cream-colored; calyx 1 mm long, 1.6 mm in diam., fleshy, glabrous, the lobes deltate, the margins papillose; corolla in bud 1.6 mm long, 1.4 mm in diam., the petals coherent, caducous after anthesis, glabrous; stamens 4, 1.1 mm long, the filament 0.5 mm long, enlarged in the base, the connective triangular, prominent, granular, drying dark brown, the anther 0.6 X 0.3 mm, oblong, latrorsely dehiscent; disc 0.3 mm long, 1 mm in diam., ± plane at apex, covering the apex of ovary; style ca. 1 mm long after anthesis, terete; stigma punctate, obscurely papillose. Fruit and seeds unknown.

description: Planta parva; caules parce ramosi, teretes; folia altema, ovata vel orbicularia, apiculata; lamina usque 1.5 x 1.5 cm, petiolus 1-2 mm longus; venatio fere palmata. Dioica; inflorescentiae vulgo solitariae axillares, sessiles, usque 4 mm longae, determinatae, floribus 5-7, crebris, binis; flos quisque bracteolis binis (raro singula), brevibus, camosis; flores superiores ebracteolati. Flores (feminei solum visi) 2 mm longi; petala quattuor, antheris inconspicuis, sessilibus, abortivis. Stylus 1 mm longus, clavatus. Fructus ovoideus, 4 x 2.5 mm; calyculus inconspicuus.
bibliographicCitation: Kuijt, Job. 1987. Miscellaneous mistletoe notes, 10-19. Brittonia. 39: 447-459.

description: Small plant, sparsely branched, stems when young densely covered by irregular, light brown, furfuraceous surface scales, terete. Phyllotaxy alternate, internodes 5-15 mm long. Leaves ovate to orbicular, apiculate, the smooth, terminal tooth 0.5 mm long, leaf margin finely furfuraceous, blade to 1.5 x 1.5 cm, petiole 1-2 mm; venation nearly palmate, the midvein running into the apex. Dioecious. Inflorescence usually solitary in the leaf axils, sometimes with an additional, superimposed one, sessile and very short, to 4 mm long, determinate, bearing 5-7 crowded, paired flowers each with a pair (rarely 1) of short, fleshy bracteoles, upper flowers ebracteolate; rarely, a flower develops in the axil of a bracteole. Flower (only female seen) 2 mm long, petals and ovary of equal length, the petals slightly dimorphic, 4, with inconspicuous, sessile, aborted anthers. Style 1 mm long, clavate, with well-differentiated, papillate stigma. Fruit ovoid, 4 x 2.5 mm, with inconspicuous calyculus and finely tubercular surface.
bibliographicCitation: Kuijt, Job. 1987. Miscellaneous mistletoe notes, 10-19. Brittonia. 39: 447-459.

description: Innovationes sat robustae, eramosae, ut videtur terminaliter abortivae; ramificatio sympodialis; rami teretes, vel leviter angulares. Phyllotaxis irregularis, interdum ad oppositam vertens; folia coriacea, plana, usque 70 x 25 mm, oblanceolata, basi angusta, contracta, venis prominulis, divergentibus, petiolo nullo vel brevissimo. Inflorescentiae singulae vel plures pro axilla, umbellas simplices 2-4-radiatas vel racemos breves formantes; pedunculus 2-7 mm longus; pedicelli bractea minuta, caduca, ±1 mm sub fructo suffulti. Petala ut videtur quattuor, alba, isomorpha, 6 mm longa; antherae sessiles. Ovarium 2 x 1 mm, doliiforme; calyculus laevis; stylus 6 mm longus, rectus; stigma capitatum. Fructus ellipsoideus, 7 x 4 mm.

description: Innovations up to 3 dm long, rather stout, unbranched, apparently aborting terminally, resulting in a sympodial habit, twigs to 3 mm thick, terete to slightly angular; host attachment not showing any sign of epicortical roots. Phyllotaxy irregular, sometimes tending to opposite. Leaves coriaceous and flat, to 70 x 25 mm, oblanceolate with narrow, tapering base, with prominent, diverging veins, median vein running into apex, the numerous, transversely placed stomata prom- inent through the dark pigmentation of the guard cells; petiole absent or very short. Inflorescences 1 to several per axil, being simple, 2-4-rayed umbels or short racemes; peduncle 2-7 mm long; pedicels of the same length, expanded slightly at tip when bearing fruit, and with a minute, caducous bract 1 mm below the fruit or lower which leaves a small scar; inflorescence sometimes reduced to 2 single, pedicellate flowers, in prophyllar positions, the floral bracts also in those positions (Fig. 2c). Petals apparently 4, white, isomorphic, 6 mm long, the sessile anther attached slightly above the middle. Ovary 2 x 1 mm, barrel shaped, calyculus smooth; style 6 mm long, straight, stigma capitate. Fruit (probably immature) green, ellipsoid, 7 x 4 mm.

description: As much as 5 dm tall; stems branched with numerous lateral stems from the base; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate to lanceolate, denticulate to subentire, 2-5 cm long, 3-6 mm broad, narrowed into petioles as much as 7 mm long; rachis of the in- florescence recurved in bud, becoming erect as the flowers open; hypanthium 1.3-3.8 mm long, uncolored or lightly colored within, the ring of hairs within 0.5 mm of the hypanthium lip and extending above it; sepals remaining united and deflexed to one side at anthesis; petals fan-shaped, entire to erose, 1-3 cm long, scarcely clawed, pinkish lavender above, white to pinkish tinged in the middle, and with a solid colored base or red line the same color or redder than the outer pigmented area, the intermediate unpigmented area often flecked with distinct reddish purple flecks or sometimes tinged with red; stamens 8, the outer 9.5-16 mm long, characteristically with bluish pollen, the inner 7-14 mm long with yellowish or bluish gray pollen; anthers the same length or shorter than the filaments, the filaments of both the inner and outer rows 0.2-0.5 mm wide at the base; stigma white to yellowish, the lower surface tinged with pink or red, conspicuously 4-lobed; style 10-18 mm long, exceeding the stamens at maturity; ovary 1.5-6.4 cm long, rarely sessile but usually on a pedicel as much as 3 cm long; mature capsules nearly straight, quadrangular to subterete, 1.4-7 cm long, 2-2.5 mm broad, beak 0-3 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Davis, W. S. 1970. The systematics of Clarkia bottae, C. cylindrica, and a related new species, C. rostrata. Brittonia. 22: 270-184.

description: As much as 6 dm tall; stems simple or branched; leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate, entire to denticulate, 1-6 mm broad, 1-6 cm long, sessile or narrowed into petioles as much as 5 mm long; rachis of the inflorescence recurved in bud, becoming erect as the flowers open; hypanthium 2-7 mm long, 1.4-4.5 mm wide, generally colored within, the ring of hairs at least 0.5 mm below the hypanthium rim, and not projecting above the rim; petals fan-shaped to somewhat spoon-shaped, entire to erose, 1-3.5 cm long, outer portion purple to pinkish lavender, shading to white in the middle and usually with a purplish red base, often flecked with reddish purple, the flecks diffuse and mostly in the pigmented distal one-half of the petal; stamens 8, the outer 7.5-17 mm long with bluish pollen, the inner 5-13.5 mm long with yellowish or bluish gray pollen; anthers the same length or longer than the filaments; filaments of the outer row 0.4-1 mm wide and approximately twice the width of the filaments of the inner staminal row; stigma white to yellowish, the undersurface lemon-yellow, greenish yellow, or tinged with pink; style 9-17 mm long and exceeding the stamens at maturity; ovary 2-7 cm long, sessile or on a pedicel as much as 10 mm long; immature capsules cylindrical or somewhat swollen above, sometimes club-shaped; mature capsule four-sided or subterete, sometimes enlarged above, 2-5 cm long, 1-2 mm broad, usually attenuated into a beak as much as 1 cm long.

description: Herba tenuis, erecta, pauciflora, altitudilne ad 4 dm; caulibus ramosis; foliis paucis, angusto-lanceolatis, 1-3.5 cm longis, 2-4 mm latis, integris vel subintegris; petalis cuneatis, marginibus erosis, 5-13 mm longis, 4-11 mm latis, roseo-purpureis, in basi macula purpureo-rubra clarissime circuinseripta; hypanthio brevi, 1-3 mm longo; staminibus 8, roseo-purpureis, quam stylo paulo brevioribus; stigmate quadrifido; ovario 4-canaliculato; capsula 2-4 cm longa, plus minusve 2 mm lata; semilnibus caineseentibus, squamosis, crista ad 0.2 mm longa.

description: A slender erect herb up to 4 dm in height, branched at the base and above or unbranched in depauperate individuLals, puberulent above; leaves narrowly lanceolate, 1-3.5 cm long, 2-4 mm broad, enitire or essentially so, sparse, shortpetioled; inflorescence few-flowered, the rachis erect; buds erect; hypanthium short, inconspicuous, 1-3 mm in length, not conspicuously colored within, the ring of hairs near the middle; sepals lanceolate, 4-5 mm long, 1-2 mm broad, remaining united and deflexed to one side at anthesis, rarely completely reflexed; petals wedge-shaped, conspicuously erose, 5-13 mm long, 4-11 mm broad, scarcely clawed, lavender-pink streaked Avitlh white, white below, with a conspieuous, sharply defined, bright reddish-purple basal spot; stamens 8; filaments lavender-pink, reddish-purple at the base; anthers darker lavender below, yellow above, with a point of sterile tissue at the apex; pollen dull yellow; stigma 4-lobed, the lobes linear, nearly white; style pale lavender, slightly exceeding the stamens at maturity; ovary slenlder, 1-2 cm long, 4-grooved, densely puberulent with short upwardly curled trichomes, sessile or on a pedicel up to 2 cm long; mature capsule blunt or with a short beak, nearly terete, 2-4 cm lonlg, about 2 mm broad; seeds grey, scaly, 1.2-1.5 mm long, the crest less than 0.2 mm lolng.

description: Herba annua erecta altitudine ad 6 dm; caulibus saepe simplicibus superne ramosis; foliis lanceolatis, 1-6 cm longis, 2-8 mm latis, sessilibus vel in petiolis ad 10 mm longis attenuatis; inflorescente nutante; hypanthio 1.5-2.5 mm longo, 2-2.5 mm lato, annulo pilorum ad apicem posito; petalis 1-2.5 cm longis; filamentis 0.2-0.3 mm latis; capsula matura lineari, 4-gona, 2-4.7 cm longa, rostrata, apice attenuata ad 15 mm; pedicello 0-5 mm longo.

description: Stems 1-several, 6-15 cm tall, with a fleshy taproot 5-10 mm thick; basal leaves spatulate to obovate, 3-7 cm lonig, 1-1.5 cm wide, decurrent on the petiole, with a broad, hyaline sheath at the base; stem leaves 2, opposite, suborbicular to ovate, 1-2.5 cm long, sessile, rounded to acute at apex; inflorescenise racemose, 1-8 flowered, the pedicels 1-2 cm long; sepals sometimes unequal, 5-6 mm long, ovate to orbicu- lar; petals white, 10-12 mm long, obovate to obcordate; capsule globose, 4-5 mm long; seeds black, lenticular, about 2 mm long.

description: Perennial, rhizomatous, fleshy, 4-12 cm tall; rhizome leaves alternate, oblanceo- late to almost spatulate, or linear, up to 35 mm long and 3 mm broad, gradually narrowed to a long petiole; stem leaves few, sessile, linear to narrowly oblanceolate, 1-2 cm long and 1-2 mm broad; inflorescence racemose, lax, with 1-5 flowers; bracts 1-2, oval to lanceolate, up to 5 mm long; flowers pink or white with pink veins; calyx lobes broadly obovate, 4-6 mm long, fleshy, with hyaline margins; petals obovate, 1-1.5 cm long; capsules not seen.

description: Corms globose, 5-25 mm wide, giving rise to 1-8 weak stems, 5-30 cm long; basal leaves 0-3, 8-20 cm long, the blades 1.5-7 cm long, elliptic, lanceolate, spatulate, narrowly ovate, or oblong, acute at the tips; stem leaves 2, opposite, usually long- petioled, the blades 5-25 mm broad, similar to the basal leaves; raceme 5-10 cm long, 2-15-flowered, the pedicels 1.5-3 cm long, often recurved in age; bract below base of lowest pedicel ovate, 1-3 mm long, scarious, often 1 or more reduced ones above; sepals ovate, obtuse to acute, 4-7 mm long; petals pink to white, with pink veins, obovate, rounded at apex, 7-15 mm long; capsule 3-4 mm long, ovoid; seeds dark brown, orbicular, 2.5 mm long; 2n = 24.

description: Perennial, with creeping or floating stems, producing axillary, filiform, cormlet-bearing branches, the main stems slender, ascending, with erect tips or branches, 1-2 dm long; leaves opposite, in several pairs, oblong, spatulate, obovate to oblance-olate, 1.5-5 cm long, 5-18 mm wide, rounded or obtuse at apex and narrowed to a winged petiole at base; flowers in axillary or subterminal, 1-10-flowered, bractless racemes; pedicels slender, 1-2.5 cm long, recurved in fruit; sepals slightly unequal, orbicular to obovate, 2-3 mm long; petals white to pink, 5-8 mm long, entire, obovate; capsule obovoid, 1-1.5 mm long; seeds 1-3, black, orbicular, ca 1.5 mm long, muriculate.

description: Plants 5-15 cm tall, with 1-several stems arising from a fleshy taproot 1-2 (-3) cm thick; basal leaves several, linear to linear-oblanceolate, 1-10 (-25) mm broad and subequal with the stem in length, the basal portion scarious, expanded, and slightly clasping the stems and crown, the veins fairly prominent; stem leaves linear to linear-lanceolate, attenuate, 1-3 cm long, 1-5 mm wide, sometimes slightly scarious at the base and subamplexicaule; inflorescence racemose, 2-5-flowered, with a semi-scarious, lanceolate bract up to 1 cm long below the lowest pedicel, with 1 or more reduced ones at pedicels above; pedicels slender, 1-3 cm long; sepals 2, ovate, obtuse, 6-10 mm long; petals usually white, occasionally pinkish, 12-20 mm long, 7-11 mm wide, claws separate at base, round to truncate or occasionally sub-emarginate at apex; stamens 5 mm long, the filaments broadened toward the base and attached to the claws of the petals; capsule 5-6 mm long, ovoid; seeds lenticular, ovoid, brownish-black and shining, 2-2.3 mm long.

description: Corms mostly globose, sometimes slightly depressed, or with a short neck, rough- ened by old leaf bases, 0.3-2.5 cm broad; stems I-several from each corm, 5-25 cm tall; basal leaves none to few, up to 15 cm long, the petioles usually longer than the blades, the latter lanceolate, oblanceolate, ovate or oval, acute or obtuse, with two varieties having linear leaves; stem leaves usually 2 and opposite, sessile or nearly so, 3-6-ribbed; raceme usually peduncled, rarely branching, 3-10 cm long, 1-15-, flowered, often with a small ovate bract at base of lowest pedicel, and sometimes with 1-2 reduced ones above; pedicels slender, 1-3 cm long, recurved in fruit; sepals orbicular to ovate, 3-4.5 mm long, rounded or acute at apex; petals pink to white with pink veins, often blotched with yellow toward base, or in one variety completely golden-yellow, 5-10 mm long, obovate, rounded to emarginate at apex, clawed at base and united; filaments broadened below and attached on petal claws; capsule slightly 3-angled, orbicular to obovate, ca 4 mm long; seeds black, smooth and shining, ca 1.5 mm broad.

description: A striking golden-flowered plant; corms globose, 1-2 cm in diameter; basal leaves 0-4, up to 15 cm long, narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate, 5-15 mm wide, on long petioles; stems weak, mostly prostrate, 1-5 from each corm, 10-25 cm long; stem leaves 2, lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 2-7 cm long; racemes 5-10 cm long, 3-12- flowered, with an ovate bract 3-6 mm long at base of lowest pedicel, and sometimes with 1-2 reduced ones above; sepals ovate, rounded at apex, ca 4 mm wide and 5 mm long; petals golden-yellow, 7-12 mm long, clawed, obovate, round at apex, and only very slightly united at base, if at all; stamens about half as long as petals, the fila- ments broadened at base, and attached on the claw near its base; capstule globose, 3-4 mm long; seeds black, shining, lenticular, 2 mm long; 2n = 16.

description: Smaller than var. megarhiza. description: Tap root to 25 mm thick, occasionally dividing, cross-marked by old leaf bases, elongating over the years so that the crown is well above ground; basal leaves numerous, fleshy, up to 1 dm long and 16 mm broad, spatulate, with petioles only slightly winged, but broadened and scarious at base; cauline leaves linear to linear- oblanceolate, up to 12 mm long; stems equaling or slightly exceeding the leaves in length; inflorescence subsessile, 1-9-flowered, with an ovate, long-acuminate, pink bract, 1 cm long at base of lowest pedicel and 1-4 more reduced ones above; sepals ovate, acute, 5-8 mm long; petals deep rose, 8-12 mm long, obovate, united at base; 2n = 16.

description: Plants 3-10(-15) cm tall, growing in shallow water or wet soil, from a tangled mass of underground, light brown rhizomes, 2-3(-5) mm thick, and bearing numerous fine rootlets; basal leaves on long petioles, oval, ovate, or spatulate, 5-15(-25) mm broad, and about equaling the stems in length; stem leaves 2, opposite or nearly so, sessile, oval to obovate, up to 15 mm long and 10 mm wide; inflorescence sub- umbellate, 1-8-flowered; petals white to pale pink, with deep pink veins, 8-10(-12) mm long, broadly spatulate; sepals broadly ovate, acute, 5-7 mm long; capsule ovoid, 3-3.5 mm long; seeds black, smooth, ca 2 mm long.

description: Somewhat larger than var. parvijolia: stems to 4 dm long; basal leaves to 6 cm long; sepals to 4 mm long; petals to 15 mm long. Fine flagellate runners very well developed.

description: Plants with taproots and slender, creeping, bud-bearing stolons; stems slender, unbranched to the inflorescence, 5-25 cm tall; basal leaves 3-10 cm long, the petiole very slender, the blades oval and acute at both ends to obovate and obtuse, 5-20 mm long and 3-10 (-20) mm broad; cauline leaves 2, opposite or nearly so, amplexicaule, ovate, acute, 3-7 mm broad, 6-12 mm long; inflorescence racemose, usually bractless, 2-6-flowered, the petals bright pink with darker veins, or occasionally white, 10-13 mm long, obovate to almost orbicular, short-clawed, the claws suffused with yellow, the apex retuse to rounded, slightly united at base, sepals orbicular to oval, 2-3 mm long; stamens attached near base of the petals; ovary oval, slightly 3-angled; seeds lenticular, about 15 mm broad, punctate; 2n = 16, 24, 28, 32.

description: Stems slender, few to numerous, from a taproot with a branching crown, 5-28 cm tall; basal leaves linear to linear oblanceolate, 2-15 cm long and 2-5 mm wide, the petiole scarious and broadened on the basal third; stem leaves 2, opposite, amplexicaule, linear to lanceolate or oblanceolate, 6-24 mm long; flowers mostly one on a stem, but occasionally as many as 4 in a corymb, equaling or usually surpassing the leaves; sepals oval to orbicular, 5-6 mm long, rounded to slightly emarginate at the apex; petals oval to obovate, 10-15 mm long, 6-9 mm wide, emarginate to rounded at apex and clawed at base, rich purple, palmately dark-veined, slightly united at base; filaments broadened on lower part, attached to claw of petal; capsule 4-6 mm long, oval; seeds lenticular, ca 2.5 mm long; 2n = 16.

description: Succulent perennials from slender rootstocks, sometimes blooming the first year; stems several, 15-45 cm tall, the leaf-bases thickened on the crown and often functioning as bulblets; basal leaves several, rhombicovate, truncate or attenuate at base and obtuse or acture at apex, the blades 2-5 cm wide and 2-6 cm long, on petioles 5-15 cm long; stem leaves 2, opposite, mostly sessile, similar to blades of basal leaves; inflorescence racemose, up to 30 cm long, sometimes with 1-3 branches and a pair of small leaves at the base of each branch; flowers few to numerous, with or without a linear to obovate bract 4-10 mm long at the base of each pedicel; pedicels slender, 1-3.4 cm long, divergent in age; sepals ovate to orbicular, 3-6 mm long, often enlarging in age; petals white to rose, obcordate, 7-10 mm long; capsule oval, about equaling the calyx; seeds lenticular, 2-2.5 min long, dark, shining, finely granulate.

description: Leaves distichous, 2-3 dm. long, erect or nearly so; sheaths about a third as long as the whole leaf, conduplicate and 1 cm. wide at the chestnut-colored base, 4 mm. wide at the summit, glabrous; blades 5-6 mm. wide, aeute and falcate at the tip, tomentose-ciliate along the anterior margin throughout and on the posterior margin distally. Scape 4 dm. tall, somewhat twisted, very flat, 3-4 mm. wide, tomentose- ciliate on -both margins and in the basal portion pubeseent along a single line adjacent to one margin, the line evident distally as a low glabrous ridge. Spikes 2, subglobose with loosely spreading scales wheln dry, round-ovoid and roundlv longitudinally 5-lobed when fresh, 10-13 mm. long. Scales spirally imbricate in five rows, dark chestnut- brown, glabrous, often somewhat lacerate at the margin but never scarious, only the upper fertile, the outer triangular, acute, 2-3 mm. long, the inner broadly elliptic, very concave, broadly rounded at the summit, progressively longer to 7 mm. long and 6.3 mm. wide. Lateral sepals conduplicate, somewhat falcate, linear, 6.5 mm. long, obtuse, glabrous on the searious sides, densely villous-eiliate on the keel in the upper third.

description: Stems simple, 1-4, 5-25 cm tall, from a globose corm up to 25 mm thick; basal leaves 1-2, about 3/4 height of stems, the blades linear-oblanceolate to lanceolate, 2-4 cm long, with a strong midrib; stem leaves 2, amplexicaul, 2-7 cm long, nar- rowly lanceolate; inflorescence a 2-10-flowered raceme, the pedicels 1-3 cm long, often recurved in age, sometimes some of them opposite or even united part way; an ovate, semiscarious bract present below the lowest, 1-2 reduced ones at pedi- cels above; sepals 2, ovate to orbicular, 5-7 mm long slightly scarious-margined; petals white, suffused with yellow toward the base and occasionally pink showing in the veins, 11-15 mm long and 8-10 mm broad, obovate, rounded or retuse at apex, clawed at base and slightly united; filaments greatly broadened downward and attached near base of petals; capsule ovate, 3-4 mm long, slightly 3-angled; seeds black, shining, reticulate, lenticular, 2-2.5 mm in diameter.

description: Corm rounded at first, but elongating at the top, becoming distinctly elongate pear-shaped, and up to 7 cm long, with the upper part of the neck covered by the old leaf bases, and 1-4 coarse roots from the lower part; stems and petioles 1-6 each from the corm and vary from 5-30 cm in length.' description: Stems short and tufted, or elongating and scandent or trailing in var. columbiana. Leaves biternate or more finely dissected, the leaflets deeply serrate or lobed. Apices of leaflets and lobes obtuse to acuminate; bases of leaflets cuneate to, cordate, often oblique. Flowers campanulate, with moderately divergent, flaring, lance-ovate to ovate sepals. Peduncles and p,etioles arising directly from the bud scales, or frequently terminating short branches of the current season, especially in var. columbiana. Outer stamens usually oblanceolate, occasionally narrowly spatulate, almost always antheri- ferous. Achenes ca. 5 mm long, usually pilose. Anthesis usually May-June (-July in localities where snow persists); occasional flowers produced sporadically through August. Two intergrading varieties.

description: Aerial stems typically short and tufted, often less than 0.1 m long, occasionally elongating up to 1 m. Leaves more or less succulent, completely or imperfectly biternate, the primary divisions divided into narrow lobes or small leaflets, mostly 1.5-5 mm wide. Sepals violet-blue, 1.5-5 cm long, acute to acuminate. Stamens 30-45 (avg ca. 35). Carpels 20-80 (avg ca. 50). Achene bodies short-pilose to sericeous. Fruiting styles 2-4.5 cm long. Foothills of Montana and northern Wyo- ming; Killdeer Mountains, North Dakota; Black Hills, South Dakota; intergrading with var. columbiana in western Montana, northern Utah, and Colorado. 2n = 16 (Montana, Meagher Co., summit of King's Hill: hoc loc., Fig. 7b, voucher Pringle 1198, HAM).

description: Planta perennis, rhizomatoza; radices crassae; caules breves; folia rubro-punctata; spicae capituliformes ultra 10-florae, 1.5-2 cm longae, 1.5-2.5 cm latae; bracteae numerosae, atro-castaneae, rugulosae, acutae vel acuminatae, dissitae; bracteae basilares 2, medianas superantes ca 1.0 cm longae, 0.5-0.6 cm latae, castaneae, margine basique lutescentes, ad apicem carinatae; bracteae medianae 1.2- 2 cm longae, 0.5-0.6 cm latae; bracteae fertiles subaequilongae, 0.9-1.5 cm longae, 0.5-0.6 cm latae; sepala lateralia libera, inaequilateralia, carinata, carina ad apicem dilatata, serrulata; ovarium angustum, ellipticum; ovula numerosa; funiculi elongati.

description: Perennial, rhizomatous; roots thick; stem short; leaves distichous, flabelliform, ensiform, 15-32 cm long, exceeding the sheath of the scape, leaf blade flat or twisted, striate, red-punctate, 15-25 cm long, 0.7 cm wide, margins hispid, apex subacute, curved; sheath with mucilage, paleaceus, strongly carinate, keel hispidu- Ious, base abruptly expanded, dark brown, margin narrow membranous for more than half the total length of the leaf, 15-18 cm long; sheath of the scape 20-47 cm long; spike capituliform, many-flowered (more than 10), 1.5-2 cm long, 1.5- 2.5 cm wide; bracts numerous, dark brown, rugulose, acute to acuminate, margins lacerate, membranous, yellow, patent; sterile bracts many, departing from various levels, basal bracts 2, brown, margin and base yellow at the apex, carinate, smaller than median bracts, ca 1 cm long, 0.5-0.6 cm wide; median bracts 1.2-2 cm long, 0.5-0.6 cm wide; fertile bracts reaching approximately the same level, 0.9-1.5 cm long, 0.5-0.6 cm wide; lateral sepals free, delicate, inequilateral, carinate, keel expanded and serrulate at the apex, 0.9 cm long, 0.1 cm wide; petal elliptic, intensely yellow, margin lightly erose, ca 0.7 cm long, 0.25 cm wide; staminodes bifurcate, densely pilose, with moniliform hairs; anthers sagittate, ca 0.2 cm long; ovary narrowly elliptic, ca 0.3 cm long; placentation basal, ovules numerous, funiculus elongate, style tripartite, stigma slightly expanded; capsule obovate; seeds lightly striate.

description: Vines usually prolonged, scandent or trailing (often short or suppressed in var. dissecta). Leaves simply ternate. Leaflets with distinct petiolules, lance-ovate to deltoid or nearly orbicular, uncleft or up to 3-lobed (or further incised in var. dissecta), acuminate at the apex, rounded to cordate at the base, the margins entire to deeply crenate-serrate. All vegetative parts pilose when young, becoming glabrate. Sepals generally 4, lanceolate to ovate or oblong-elliptic, densely villous along the margins, sparsely pilose on the dorsal surface. Outer stamens usually oblanceolate to narrowly spatulate, rarely broader, usually fertile, occasionally replaced by sterile staminodia. Achenes ca. 5 mm long, pilose at least on the upper half, with fruiting styles 3-7 cm long. Anthesis generally in spring, usually May-early June, -July in alpine regions. Three varieties.

description: Stems short, often tufted, usually 0.1-0.5 m long, occasionally elongating to 1.5 m and trailing. Flower and upper pair of subtending leaves borne on a short stem of the current season, or arising directly from the bud scales. Leaves ternate to subbiternate, the leaflets 1.5-6.5 (-9) cm long, prominently crenate-serrate to deeply incised. Flowers campanulate. Sepals moderately divergent, flaring, commonly reddish-violet, occasionally violet-blue, 2.5-4.5 (-6) cm long, ovate, the apices acute to acuminate. Stamens 30-40 (avg ca. 35). Carpels 40-100 (avg ca. 75). Cascade Mountains of Washington, principally in the Wenatchee Range. Chromosome number unknown; epidermal cell size similar to that of var. grosseserrata.

description: Vines 0.25-2.5 m long, scandent or trailing. Peduncles and petioles of subtending leaves usually arising directly from the bud scales, or the flower and upper pair of leaves occasionally terminating a short branch of the current season. Flowers rarely produced at the ends of long, leafy branches of the current season. Leaflets 2-11 cm long, unlobed or occasionally lobed, the margins frequently entire or nearly so, occasionally conspicuously crenate-serrate. Flowers campanulate at least at first. Sepals moderately divergent, flaring (in some populations ultimately becoming strongly divergent), violet-blue (a form with white sepals reported by Kelso, 1933), 3-6 cm long, usually lance-ovate, the apices slightly to strongly acuminate or rarely attenuate (occasional flowers with 6-10 narrowly lanceolate to linear, long-attenuate sepals, some of them deeply cleft). Stamens 25-50 (avg ca. 35). Carpels 45-175 (avg. ca. 90). Mountains of Colorado north to southwestern Yukon Territory, east to the Cypress Hills, Saskatchewan, and the Edmonton and Spirit River areas, Alberta. 2n = 16 (Colorado, Boulder Co., Hessie: Love & Kapoor, 1967; Alberta, Jasper National Park, Miette Hot Springs: hoc loc., Fig. 2i, voucher Pringle 1193, HAM).

description: Perennial 5-20 cm tall, unbranched or usually sparsely branched from the base, minutely glandular-pilosulose, particularly on the stem and the leaf-margins; leaves rather dense, sessile, oblong-elliptic, less frequently narrowly oblanceolate or obovate-elliptic, acute or rounded and apiculate, mucronate, narrowly attenuate to the base, 15-40 mm long, 6-11 (-14) mm wide, entire, dull above, shiny beneath, the nerves prominent, particularly the midrib and the submarginal veins; flowers borne singly in the axils of well-developed leaves; pedicels 12-20 mm long; sepals oblanceolate, acute, 4-5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, pubescent; petals obovate, rounded or slightly emarginate at the apex, attenuated to the slender base, 9-10 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, entire, in dried material whitish or yellow; stamens 10, 4 of them exapophysate with filaments 6-7 mm long, 6 apophysate with filaments 5 mm long, the apophyses subglobose and somewhat sulcate; anthers 1.5-2 mm long; ovary ovate, drawn out into the filiform style, pubescent; mature siliques strongly compressed, elliptic to suborbicular, acute to subrotund at both ends, 12-17 mm long, 7-13 mm wide, 2-4 mm thick, the valves sparsely puberulent and dull without, shiny within; styles filiform and setulose, 5-6 mm long; pedicels 18-32 mm long; siliques sharply deflexed; seeds 4-6 in each silique; nearly mature seeds, including spines, 5-5.3 mm long, 4.8-5.2 mm wide, about 2.8 mm thick, minutely puberulent, pronouncedly spiny on the back, the spines 80-100, brown, shiny; cleft membrane sunken, pale yellow, the cleft 0.5-1 mm long, narrow.

description: Erect, very slender, glabrous annuals, (6-)8-35 cm tall, usually simple at the base, unbranched or with few to several branehes above the middle; leaves sessile, narrowly linear to filiform, mucronate, 8-35 mm long, 0.3-1 mm wide, minutely denticulate on the margin, minutely stipulate; inflorescence a terminal raceme 3-10 cm long, open, appearing ebracteate, the flowers (usually 2-6 open at a time) subtended by minute, setaceous, hyaline or green bracts 1-1.5 mm long; pedicels 3-7 mm long; sepals oblanceolate to broadly elliptic, acute to obtuse and mucronate at the apex, attenuate to the base, 2-3 mm long, 0.6-1.7 mm wide, ciliolate on the margin, papillose oni the back; petals broadly elliptic-spatulate, rounded at the apex and more or less erose, abruptly attenuate to the short claw, yellow, fading to light purple or cream, of two sizes, the abaxial (lower) 6-8 mm long, 4 mm wide, the adaxial 5-6 mm long, 3 mm wide, the latter with a deep golden to purplish band near the base of the blade; stamens 6, 2 of them exapophysate with filaments 5-6 mm long and fertile anthers 1.2-1.3 mm long; 4 apophysate with filaments 2.5-3.5 mm long and abortive anthers 0.5 mm long, the apophyses "each . . . of two gibbous collars more or less surrounding the bases of the anthers, each collar prolonged downward on one side into a blunt, swollen spur; ovary linear, about 3 mm long, the filiform style 3 mm long; mature siliques linear-cylindric, acute at both ends, 15-25 mm long, about 2 mm thick; style filiform, 3-5 mm long; pedicel 5-7 (-8) mm long, the siliques deflexed; seeds 3-12 in each silique, 1.6-1.9 mm. long, 1.6-1.8 mm wide, aoout 1 mm thick, reddish brown, glabrous, strongly cochleate-reniform with the radicular claw curved and overlapping the tip of the cotyledonar claw, strongly transverse-rugose and tubercled, the processes sharply pointed.

description: Erect, slender, glabrous annuals 1-5 dm tall, simple at the base, usually much branched above; leaves sessile, singly or frequently (falsely) bunched at a node, filiform to very narrowly linear, setose-mucronate at the apex, 4-40 mm long, 0.3-1.0 (-1.6) mm wide, minutely ciliate on the frequently revolute margin; flowers born singly in the axils of well-developed foliage leaves; pedicels 6-12 mm long; sepals lanceolate to ovate, acuminate, 1.5-3 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, minutely and sparsely glandular-ciliolate, sometimes with few teeth near apex; petals oblanceolate-elliptic, acute to rounded, attenuate to the base but essentially sessile, (3-) 4-5 (-7) mm long, 1-2 mm wide, erose-denticulate or serrulate in upper half, yellow; stamens 6-9, 3-4 of them fertile and exapophysate, with filaments 4-5 mm long and anthers 0.8 mm long, the other 3-5 sterile and apophysate, with filaments 3-3.5 mm long and minute and abortive anthers, the apophyses globose to obeonic, separated from the anther by a short stipe or immediately beneath it; ovary linear; style short; stigma capitate; mature siliques linear-cylindric to oblong-ellipsoid, terete to more or less compressed, acute at both ends, sessile or subsessile, (10-) 20 (-35) mm long, 2-3 mm thick; style slender, 1-3 mm long; pedicel 7-15 mm long; siliques more or less divergent to deflexed; seeds 9-19 per silique, 1.5-2 mm long, 1.3-1.6 mm wide, 0.8-1.1 mm thick, obovoid, strongly tuberculate to transverse-rugose, blackish-green with white markings on the protuberances, greenish when immature, the protuberances conic to lamellate, aeute to obtuse, 0.1-0.3 mm long, the cleft membrane brown; cleft narrow, oblong, the radicular claw straight, pointed.

description: Slender, decumbent or erect annuals (or perennials?) 5-15 cm tall, ulsually branched from the base, eglandular-strigillose on the stem, midrib and margins of leaves; leaves sessile or subsessile, linear or linear-elliptic, aeute to acuminate, mucronate, slenderly attenuate to the base, 7-40 mm long, 1-4 mm wide, serrulate strigillose with stiff, ascending hairs on the margin; stipules minlute, setaceous; inflorescences very open, the flowers born singly in the axils of the 1-foliolate leaves; pedicels 9-17 mm long; sepals narrowly to broadly lanceolate, acuminate, 3-4 mm long, 0.8-1.5 mm wide, ciliate on margin and midrib; petals oblanceolate elliptic, acute, long-attenuate to the slender base, (3-) 4-7 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, bright yellow (drying to lilac in some collections), sparsely ciliate; stamens 6-7; filaments 3-4 mm. long, 2-3 of them with obconic apophyses, the remainlder exapophysate or only slightly clavate at the apex; anthers broadly oblong, 0.5 mm long, 0.4 mm wide; ovary sessile, strongly flattened, triangular to orbicular, inclosed, with filiform style; mature silicules strongly flattened, orbicular, rhomboid, or deltoid, broadly attenuate to the filiform style, more or less truncate at the base, 4-7 mm long, 5-8 mm wide, 1-2 mm thick, the valves thin, glabrous, smooth or slightly wrinkled, sparsely reticulate-nerved; style setose, 2-4 mm long; gynophore minute, 0.5-1 mm long; pedicels 5-22 mm long; silieules usually deflexed over the pedicels; seeds 1-6 in each silique, 2.5-2.8 mm long, 2.2-2.7 mm wide, 1.4-1.8 mm thick, pale or greenish yellow to light gray-brown when mature, somewhat varnished, conspicuously to obscurely tubereled and transversely ruoulose on the back, the protuberances obtuse to acute, relatively few in number, 0.1-0.4 mm long, under very high magnification finely puberulenlt; claws connected by a deeply sunken, very filmy membrane, the cleft oblong in cross section, the radieular claw pointed and surpassing the cotyledonar claw.

description: Slender, erect, glabrous annuals 1-4 dm tall, unbranched, or sparsely branched, frequently from the base, the branches strongly ascending; leaves unifoliolate, petioled, narrowly oblono-lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, narrowly acuminate, mucronate, acute to obtuse at the base, 18-50 mm long, 2-5 mm wide; petioles 5-9 mm long with clearly defined "pulvinus" beneath blade; stipules minute, triangular-lanceolate; flowering portions of racemes 3-7 cm long, relatively dense with 1-7 flowers open at one time, the lower flowers subtended by small leaves, the upper by minute, caducous, setaceous bracts 2-4 mm long; mature flowers frequently deflexed or pendent; pedicels 5-6 mm long; sepals lanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic, acuminate to caudate-acuminate, 2.5-3.5 mm long, ciliolate; petals broadly rhombic to broadly obovate, rarely broadly oblanceolate, acute to obtuse, attenuate to the base, short-clawed or subsessile, (5-) 6-8 mm long, (2-) 3-5 mm wide, erose-denticulate or irregularly sinuate in the apical half, yellow, orange, fading to white or pale purple when dry; stamens 6; 4 of them (or all 6 in one subsp.) exapophysate, with filaments 4-6 mm long and anthers 1.0-1.5 mm long; 2 filaments apophysate (except subsp. paraguayensis), 3-4 mm long, with anthers 0.8 mm long; style (1.5-) 2-3 (-4) mm long; pedicels usually curved and more or less strongly deflexed from the peduncle, 4-10 mm long; siliques most frequently somewhat deflexed, less frequently aseending, rarely strongly so; seeds 10-17, 1.2-2.4 mm long, 1-2.1 mm wide, 0.7-1.3 mm thick, more or less transversely lamellate-rugose and tubereled, the protuberances sharp, conic or flattened, the testa black or dark reddish-brown; radicular claw more or less curved over the cotyledonar claw; cleft membrane deeply sunken.

description: Glabrous perennial with 2-20 or more weak, slender, decumbent or aseending stems 15-45 em long, simple or rarely branehed, the roostock wiToody; leaves few and distantly spaced, usually 5-20 mm apart, subsessile (petiole 1.5 mm long or less), linear to linear-elliptic, rarely linear-oblong, narrowly acute, mucronulate, narrowly cuneate at the base, frequently conduplicate, 4-18 mm long, 0.5-2 mm wide; petioles 1-1.5 mm long, without pulvinus; stipules microscopic; inflorescence few-flowered alnd open, with 1-2 open flowers on a bralnch, the flowers borne singly in the axils of leaves; pedicels (7-) 10-15 (-20) mm long; sepals narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, acuminate, 3-4 mm long; petals narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate-elliptic, acute to obtuse, cuneate and sessile at the base, 7-11 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, yellow or pinkish-white; stamelns 6, shorter than the petals; filaments 2-3 mm long; anth.ers 1-1.5 mm long, linear-oblongoid; ovary sessile, fusiform; mature silique oblonig to fusiform, -+ flattened to terete, acute at the apex, attenuate to obtuse at the base, (9-)12-17 mm long, 3-5 mm wide; style 1-2 mm long; gynophore 0-1 mm long; pedicel 10-20 (-30) mm lonig, the siliquLes ascending; seeds 3-13 in each silique, subspherical, 2.3-2.7 mm long and wide, 1.5-1.8 mm thick, rusty brown, with many small, short obtuse murications or short transverse ridges on the testa; claws equal, the cleft mliembrane deeply sunken.

description: Slender perennials with very many prostrate or decumbent stems 2-30 cm long from slender taproots or sometimes from short underground rhizomes, unbranched or branched near the base, glabrous, sometimes papillose on the stem ridges, petioles and leaf margins; leaves very many and very small, narrowly to broadly ovate, elliptic or oblong, aeute to rounded at apex and base, mucronulate, 2-6 (-9) mm long, 1-3 mm wide, entire; petioles 1-2 mm long, without pulvinus; stipules minute; inflorescence open, with only 1-2 flowers open at any one time at the tip of an axillary branch; pedicels 3-12 mm long; sepals lanieeolate, elliptic or oblong, acute to acuminate, 1.5-2.5 mm long; petals oblanceolate to rhombicelliptic, acute to obtuse, attenuate to the base, (2-)3-5(-8) mm long, 2-4 mm wide, bright yellow, fading to purplish-white or white when dry; stamens 6; filaments 1.5-5 mm long; anthers 0.5-1.2 mm long, subspherical to oblong; ovary sessile, subspherical; mature siliques very shortly stipitate, obcordate, suborbicular, obovoid, ellipsoid, or fusiform, acute to emarginate at the apex, cuneate to attenuate at the base, 3-9 mm long, 2-4 mm thick, terete to strongly compressed; style setulose, 0.5-1.5 mm long; pedicel 3-17 (-23) mm long; seeds (1-) 5-18 per silique, 1-1.5 mm long, reddish-brown to dark brown, somewhat vernicose, transverse-rugose or rarely tubereled, the rugae usually small, dense and elongate; radicular claw usually one-third longer than the cotyledonar claw, rarely subequal, the membrane deeply sunken and whitish.

description: Stems decumbent, rather robust, 10-30 cm long; leaves oblong to ovate or elliptic, 3-9 mm long; pedicels of flowers 7-12 mm long, of fruits (7-)11-17 (-23) mm long; petals 4-8 mm long; mature siliques fusiform, acute to obtuse at the apex, acute at the base, 4-8 mm long, about 2 mm wide; style 0.6-1 mm long; seeds 1.1-1.5 mm long, 6-15 in each silique.

description: Procumbent to aseendilng, glabrous annuals or perennials to 30 cm high, the stems often decumbent and 10-60 cm long, usually much branched from and above the somewhat woody base; leaves petiolate, narrowly oblong-elliptic to linear-lanceolate, acute to obtuse, mucronulate, cuneate to broadly obtuse at the base, 5-25 mm long, 2-5 mm broad, entire, minutely papillose on the petiole and margins; petiole (1-) 2-4 (-5) mm long; stipules minute, hyaline, eaducous; flowers borne in the axils of the upper leaves, the infloreseence open, with 1-3 open flowers at the tip of the branch; sepals oblong-lanceolate, acute to actminate, 2.5-3 mm long, minutely ciliolate; petals obovate, less often oblanceolate-elliptic, obtuse to rounded, attenuate with a very short claw or subsessile, 4.5-5.5 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, yellow, orange yellow, or white, fading to pale purple or white, sparsely and minutely ciliolate and sinulate on the margin; stamens 6; filaments 3.5-4.5 mm long, exapophysate; anthers 0.7-1 mm long; ovary sessile, linear-fusiform, about 5 mm long, the style 1.5-2 mm long; mature siliques linear-cylindric, acute at both ends, more or less torulose, terete, (8-) 15-20 (-26) mm long, 1.5-2 mm thick; style 2-3 mm long; gynophore 0-1 mm long; pedicels 5-10(-14) mm long, the siliques erect, aseending or divergent; seeds 4-27, obovoid, flattened, 1.5-1.7 mm long, 1.3-1.6 mm wide, 0.9-1 mm thick, reddish-brown to dark-brown, prominently and very densely transverse-rugose and tubereled, the protuberances lamellate or less often conic, the cleft membrane sunken and whitish, the radicular claw obtuse, straight.

description: Decumbent or ascending perennials 8-30 cm long, with wiry branches from the base and above, finely glandular and crisp-puberulent throughout; leaves close together, sessile or subsessile, broadly elliptic, ovate to elliptic-obovate or suborbicular, rather abruptly acuminate to rounded and apiculate, pronouncedly mucronate, rounded to more or less abruptly attenuate at the base, (6-) 10-25(-35) mm long, (3-) 6-14 (-18) mnm wide, minutely stipulate (?), dull on both sides, the midrib, but not the nerves, conspicuous;- infloreseelice rather densely flowered, the flowers born singly in the axils of leaves; pedicels 8-14 mm long; petals oblanceolate, aeute to rounded, attenuated into a slender claw, 7-9 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, yellow to whitish-yellow; stamens 7-8, 4-5 of them exapophysate with filaments 4-5 mm long, 3-4 apophysate with filaments 3-4 mm long, the apophyses narrowly conie to subsagittoid, about 0.7 mm long; anthers 0.5-1.7 mm long; ovary elliptic, pubescent, inclosed, the filiform style projecting to the length of the stamens; mature siliques strongly compressed, ovate to elliptic or oblong-elliptic, broadly acuminate to rounded at the apex, acute to rounded at the sessile base, 8-14 mm long, 6-9 mm wide, the valves dull-green and puberulent without, yellow- or green-vernicose and glabrous within; style filiform, 2-4 mm long; pedicel 10-20 mm long, the siliques sharply deflexed; seeds (2-) 5-11 in each silique, (including spines) 3-4 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, 1.6-1.9 mm thiek, spiny on the back with 20-30 stout, narrowly conic, hard, gray-white to ivory spines 0.5-0.8 mm long, the body reddish- to blackish-brown, the whole varnished, seemingly glabrous but minutely puberulent under high magnification; cleft narrow, the cotyledonar claw longer than the radicular claw and prolonged into a stout spine.

description: Erect to procumbent, lax, branching annuals 1-9 dm long, generally sparsely eglandular-pilose to subglabrous, unarmed; leaves 3-foliolate, from long-petioled on the lower part of the stem to nearlv sessile at the apex, the petioles up to 3.5 cm long; leaflets rhombie-elliptic to elliptic or oblanceolate, acute to acuminate, less often obtuse to rounded at the apex, broadly atteniuate to cuneate at the base, 1-3 cm long, 0.5-1.7 cm wide, ciliolate-serrulate, short-petiolulate; inflorescences few-flowered and very open, the flowers borne singly in the axils of slightly reduced leaves; pedicels 11-21 mm long, sepals free, narrowly lanceolate, subcaudate-acuminate, 2.5-4 mm long, ciliate on the margin, deciduous; petals white, pink or lilac, the two middle ones when fresh with a yellow, transverse band, narrowly oblanceolate-elliptic, acute to obtuse and apiculate at the apex, gradually attenuate into a slender claw, 6-8 (-11) mm long, about 2 mm wide, glabrous, entire; disk obsolete, the receptacle 1 mm long; staminal filaments 5-7 mm lolng; anthers 1.5-2 mm long; ovary linear-cylindric, 5-15 mm long, glabrous, short-stipitate; stigma sessile, slightly expanded; siliques linear-cylindric, attenuate at both ends, 3-7 cm long, 3-4 mm thick, prominently longitudinally nerved, glabrous, continuous or slightly torulose; stigma slightly capitate, short-stipitate; gynophore 4-12 mm long; pedicels 18-30 mm long, the siliques usually ascending; seeds suborbicular, 1.5-1.9 mm long, 1.-1.7 mm wide, 1-1.3 mm thick, brownish-black, dull except for a varnished, round, elevated spot surrounding the vertex of the cleft, strongly transverse-ridged, the ridges elongate, about 20-30 in number, densely and minutely papillose or pubescent (as seen under a magnification of 40×) at the crest, finely longitudinally striate between the transverse ridges; cleft narrow but open, the claws not connected by a membrane, covered with a protruding white or brownish aril of densely aggregated bulliforin cells attached to both sides of the radicular claw, the cells of the aril frequently collapsed in dry seeds.
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert. 1960. A Revision of Asimina and Deeringothamnus (Annonaceae). Brittonia. 12 (4): 233-278.

description: Erect, slender, glabrous annuals 10-50 cm tall, simple or with abundant strongly ascending, strict branches; leaves petiolate, very narrowly linear to linear-lanceolate, long-acuminate, mucronulate, attenuate at the base, 10-40 (-70) mm long, 1-3 (-5) mm wide, entire, flat or with revolute margins; petioles 2-9 mm long with well-defined "pulvinus"; stipules minute, eaducous; racemes open, the flowering portion 1 (-3) cm long, with only 1-2, rarely 3 flowers on the branch tip open at any one time; bracts minute, eaducous, 0.5-3 mm long; pedicels 2-3 (-4) mm long; sepals oblong- to lanceolate-elliptic, acuminate, 2-3 mm long; petals narrowly oblanceolate to oblanceolate-elliptic, sessile, obtuse to acute, narrowly euneate, 3.5-5.5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, entire or uneven and sparsely ciliolate, whitish yellow to bright yellow, fading to white or pale pink when dry; stamens 6; filaments 2-4.5 mm long, exapophysate; anthers 0.7-0.9 mm long; mature siliques linear-cylindric, terete to mnore or less compressed, acute at the apex, acute to obtuse and sessile at the base, (15-) 25-30 (-35) mm long, about 2 mm wide, striatulate; style 1.5-2.5 mm long; pedicels 2-6 mm long, straight and strongly ascending, the siliques erect or nearly so; seeds 10-35 (or as few as 3 in Dugand 4534), 1.2-1.8 (-2.3) mm long, 1.1-1.5(-2) mm wide, 0.9-1.2 mm thick, black, gray or blackish-brown when mature, promninently transverse rugose to tubereled; cleft very narrow, the claws subequal.
bibliographicCitation: Iltis, Hugh H. 1959. Studies in the Capparidaceae-VI. Cleome Sect. Physostemon: Taxonomy, Geography and Evolution. Brittonia. 11 (3): 123-162.

description: Erect, slender glabrous perennials 20-40 cm tall, branched from or near the base, the branches slender, erect, rather stiff; leaves few, sessile, filiform, 15-55 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide, mucronate, sparsely ciliolate on the margin; inflorescences open, the flowers borne singly in the axils of well developed leaves; pedicels 10-12 mm long; sepals oblong to narrowly lanceolate, aeute, 4-6 mm long, 1.2-2 mm wide; petals rhombic-spatulate to obovate, aeute to obtuse, attenuate to the base, 10-14 mm long,, 4-5 mm wide, whitish to pale pink in dried specimens; stamens 6, 2 of them exapophysate with filaments 6-9 mm long, 4 apophysate with filaments 5-7 mm long; apophyses obeonic to spherical, about 1 mm in diameter; anthers 2-2.3 mm long; ovary sessile, compressed, elliptic, drawn out into a long (5-8 mm) filiform style; mature siliques strongly compressed, elliptic, acuminate at the apex, broadly acute and sessile or subsessile at the base, (9-) 15-19 mm long, (6-) 8-11 mm wide, the valves thin, glabrous, dull without, varnished within; style filiform and setulose (7-) 8-11 mm long; pedicels (8-) 10-12 mm long, the siliques divergent; seeds 4-7 in each silique, echinate on the back with about 40-60 sharp, slender spines 0.8-1.3 mm long, the whole seed (including spines) 4.5-5 mm long, 4-4.9 mm wide, 1.9-2.1 mm thick, rufous to dark brown, minutely puberulent throughout, the cleft narrow (seed-data from Gardner 2036, the only collection with mature seeds).
bibliographicCitation: Iltis, Hugh H. 1959. Studies in the Capparidaceae-VI. Cleome Sect. Physostemon: Taxonomy, Geography and Evolution. Brittonia. 11 (3): 123-162.

description: Slender, unbranched or sympodially branched, erect annuals 1-4 dm tall, essentially glabrous or sparsely glandular-scaberulous on the stem and petioles; leaves 3- to 5-foliolate, essentially glabrous; stipules minute and hyaline, about 0.3 mm long; petioles 5-25 mm long; leaflets linear-lanceolate to oblanceolate, obtuse to acute, less often rounded at the apex, usually hyaline-mucronate, narrowly cuneate at the base, 6-30 mm long, 2-5 mm wide, of rather firm texture, short-petiolate, the margin minutely scaberulous, serrulate-denticulate and pronouncedly thickened; racemes open and few-flowered, 5-20 mm long, ebracteate; pedicels slender, 4-8 mm long, subtended by a pair of minute, hyaline stipules, the uppermost flowers subsessile, minute; sepals linear-elliptic to broadly lanceolate, acuminate and usually hyaline-mucronate, about 2-3 mm long, ciliate on the margin; petals narrowly or broadly oblanceolate to oblong-elliptic, obtuse.to rounded at the apex, gradually attenuated to the base, 3-5 mm long, 1.5-2.2 mm wide, ciliate on the margin of the distal half, the blades glabrous, yellow (white in herbarium material); staminal filaments 2-5 mm long, often somewhat thickened in the apical half; anthers 1 mm long; ovary linear-cylindric or ellipsoid, 2-5 mm long, glabrous, sessile; style slender, 1-2 mm long, mature siliques linear cylindric, less often oblong-fusiform, acuminate, acute at the base, 11-33 mm. long, 1.5-3 mm thick, pronouncedly striate, glabrous, slightly torulose, sessile; style slender, stiff, 2-6 mm long; stigma minute; pedicels 4-10 mm long; siliques usually strongly ascending, less often divergent or slightly deflexed; seeds suborbicular, 1.5-1.7 mm long, 1.4-1.6 mm wide, 0.9-1.2 mm thick, the cleft wedgeshaped, covered at the vertex, the narrow mouth open, without an internal cleft cavity; testa black to dark reddish-brown, finely striate, pronouncedly transverserugose.

description: Leaves 3-foliolate, the petioles 0.7-1.7 mm long; leaflets linear-lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, acute, rarely subobtuse; petals narrowly oblanceolate, about 5-5.5 mm long, 1.5 nu wide; mature fruiting style 2-4 mm long.

description: Unbranched or branched, erect annuals 3-16 dm tall, more or less densely glandular-pubescent throughout, unarmed; leaves 3- to 5-foliolate, estipulate; petioles 1-6 cm long; leaflets oblanceolate-elliptic, acute to obtuse or less frequently rounded at the apex, attenuate to cuneate to the base, the central leaflets (0.6-) 2-6 cm long, 0.5-3 cm wide, entire and glandular-ciliate; petiolules 2-3 mm long; flowers few, solitary in the axils of the upper leaves; pedicels 8-23 mm long; sepals free, narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate-elliptic, acuminate, 5-10 mm long, 1-4 mm wide, deciduous; petals obovate to spatulate, rounded at the apex, gradually attenuate to the base, 7-14 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, pale to bright yellow or orange yellow, radially disposed in the open flower; disk obsolete; stamens (10-) 16-26 (or more?), included; filaments 5-8 mm long, 4-10 of the adaxial ones shorter and slightly clavate (apophysate) beneath the anthers; anthers 2-3 mm long; ovary linear-cylindric, densely glandular, included, sessile; style about 1 mm long; stigma capitate; mature siliques linear-cylindric, attenuate to the apex, broadly sessile, 3-10 cm long, 2-4 mm thick, glandular-pubes,cent or scaberulous, continuous, the valves strongly longitudinally striate and dull without, smooth and vernicose within, apically dehiseent longitudinally for a short distance, persistent; style 2-6 mm long; pedicels 6-30 mm long; siliques strongly ascending or erect; seeds suborbicular or obovoid, 1.3-1.8 mm long, 1.2-1.7 mm wide, 0.7-1.1 mm thick, dark reddish-brown, pronouncedly transverse-rugose with 30 or more rugae, finely and obscurely longitudinally striate, the claws free (that is, the cleft open but so narrow that the claws seem fused).
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert. 1960. A Revision of Asimina and Deeringothamnus (Annonaceae). Brittonia. 12 (4): 233-278.

description: Slender perennials with several to very many decumbent to ascending wiry stems usually 10-15 (-30) cm long, from slender or stout tap roots, branehed usually near the base, glabrous, sometimes papillose on the stem ridges, petioles and leaf margins; leaves elliptic- to linear-oblong, acute to rounded at apex and base, mueronulate, usually 4-12 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, entire; petioles 1-2 (-3) mm long, without pulvinus; stipules minute; infloreseence open, with only 1-2 open flowers borne on branch tips in the axils of leaves; pedicels 5-10 mm long; sepals variable, lanceolate, elliptic or oblong, aeute to acuminate, 1.5-3 mm long; petals oblanceolate to obovate- or rhombie-elliptic, acute to obtuse, attenuate to the base, 4.5-5.5 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, bright yellow fading to purplish-white or white when-dried; stamens 6; filaments 1.5-4 mm long; anthers 0.5-1.2 mm long, subspherical to oblong; ovary sessile, fusiform; mature siliques very shortly stipitate, linear-cylindric to oblong-fusiform, acute at apex and base, 7-15 (-18) mm long, 2-3 mm thick, terete to slightly compressed; style setulose, 1-1.5 mm long; pedicel (5-)7-16 mm. long; seeds about 11-22 per silique, 1.2-1.4(-1.6) mm long, reddish-brown to dark brown, somewhat vernicose, conspicuously transverse-rugose, rarely tubereled, the ruagae usually small, dense and elongate; radicular claw usually one-third longer that the cotyledonar claw, the two rarely subequal, the membrane deeply sunken and whitish.

description: Planta perennis, caespitosa, rhizomatoza; radices filiformes; caules breves; laminae foliorum 1.5-2.5 cm longae, 0.25 cm latae; spicae pauciflorae, elliptico-obovatae, 0.7-11 cm longae, 0.4 cm latae; bracteae steriles atro-castaneae, opacae, margine laceratae, membranaceae, patentes; bracteae basilares 2, triangulares, acutae, carinatae, concolores, 0.5 cm longae, 0.4 cm latae; bracteae medianae ovatae, ca 0.5 cm longae, rugulosae, castaneae, margine laceratae, clarae, bracteae fertiles cochleatae ad apicem carinatae, acutae, membranaceae, ad basin lutescente; sepala castaneo-rubescentia; antherae profunde partitae.

description: Perennial, caespitose, rhizomatous; roots filiform; stem short; leaves distichous, flabelliform, ensiform, 3-6.5 cm long; leaf blade flat, 1.5-2.5 long, 0.25 cm wide, nerves prominent, marginal vein thick, apex asymmetric-acute; sheath paleaceus, carinate, pilose, base abruptly dilated and darker, margin delicate and distinct, ciliate; sheath of the scape 3.5-6.5 cm long, short-laminate, blade acuminate, ca 1.5 cm long; scape cylindrical, erect or slightly twisted, bicostate, glabrous, ca 6-27 cm long, 0.5 cm wide; spike with ca 6 flowers, elliptic-obovate, 0.7-11 cm long, 0.4 cm wide; sterile bracts dark brown, opaque, margins lacerate, membranous, patent; basal bracts 2, triangular, acute, carinate, concolorus, ca 0.5 cm long, 0.25 cm wide; median bracts ovate, rugulose, brown, margins lacerate and paler, ca 0.5 cm long, 0.4 cm wide; fertile bracts cochleate, carinate at the apex, acute, membranous, yellow basally; lateral sepals free, subequilateral, carinate, acute, patent, reddish-brown, ca 0.6 cm long; petals obovate, ca 0.5 cm long, 0.25 cm wide; staminodes bifurcate, 0.25 cm long, branches long-penicillate with moniliform hairs; anthers deeply bipartite; style tripartite; stigma slightly prolonged; placentation basal, ovules numerous; funiculus elongate; seeds elliptic, dark brown, apiculate, striate, ca 0.7 mm long.

description: Malodorous annual, 0.5-4 dm tall, usually unbranched or with 1 to few long branches mostly from below the middle; herbage glabrous; petioles relatively long, those of the lower leaves mostly 2-6(8) cm long in well developed plants; leaflets elliptic, ovate, or ovate-oblong, mostly 8-24 mm long and 4-14 mm wide, 1.5-2.5(3) times as long as wide, tipped by a hair; stipules inconspicuous, fimbriate into a few slender segments; flowers numerous, crowded, relatively showy, in elongating racemes terminating the stem and branches, subtended by conspicuous simple leafy bracts, these progressively reduced upwards in the raceme; pedicels rather widely ascending or divaricately spreading, (4.5)9-17 mm long in fruit; sepals 1-2 mm long; petals yellow, (3.5)4-8 mm long; stamens conspicuously longer than the petals; style (0.7)1-2 mm long in fruit; silicle obtrapezoid or transversely rhomboidal, the 2 valves often broadly horned distally, the shape often governed by the seeds, 3.5-6 mm long, 4-9.6 mm wide; stipes 3.5-15 mm long in fruit, often reddish-purple; seeds (1)2-6, straw-colored or blackish- brown, 2-2.7 mm long, smooth or often blistery-roughened; 2n = 34 (macbrideana; Mulligan 1967).

description: Frutex; ramulis subteretibus subsucculentis in sicco sulcatis; petiolis 12-16 mm. longis ca. 2.5 mm. crassis; laminis obovato-orbicularibus vel obovatis subcoriaceis 6.10 cm. longis 5-8 (8.5) cm. latis, apice obtuso vel rotundato, base obtusa vel subrotundata, costa prominenti in apicem non extendenti, nervis lateralibus primariis 16-20 jugis non in nervo marginali collectis, supra prominulis, subtus prominentibus; cymis terminalibus (3) 5-7 floribus ca. 4-6 cm. longis, bracteis ovatis acutis navicularibus, 4-5 mm. longis, bracteolis 2 jugis sepala superiora prope subtendentibus late suborbiculari-ovatis 3-4 mm. longis 4-5 mm. latis; sepalis 4 decussatis suborbicularibus concavis 8-10 mm. longis anguste scarioso-marginatis; petalis 5-6, late obovatis ca. 15 mmn. longis albidis; staminibus numerosis 3-seriatis, filamentis in annulo ca. 0.5 mm. alto connatis, filamentis 0.5-1.2 mm. longis subgracilibus teretibus, antheris introrsis oblongis 10-1.5 mm. longis, connectivo in cuspo 0.5-1.0 mm. longo producto, cum staminodeis nunerosis in corpore globoso conglutinoso; floribus femineis non visis.

description: Small tree 2-3 m. tall; branches coarse, sulcate when dry, internodes 1.5-3.0 cm. long; leaves 5-9 cm. long, 3-6 cm. broad, obovate, rounded at the apex, acutish at the base, coriaceous, subsessile, mid-rib prominent, weakly or not at all continued from a point some 1-2 cm. below the apex, strongly keeled on the lower surface, primary and secondary ve ns about 2 mm. apart, merely prominulous on both surfaces, making a 600 angle with the mid-rib; cymes terminal, 3-flowered, sessile, pedicels no more than 5 mm. long; sepals 4, decussate, 6-8 mm. long, broadly ovate, the outer pair strongly keeled; petals apparently 5,12-15 mm. long, 6-8 mm. wide, oblong-obovate, yellow; staminodia obsolete; ovary 5-celled, styles stout, horn-like, about 5 cm. long, stigmas sessile, broadly obovate, 2.5 mm. long, fruit urceolate, 2.5 cm. long, 1.5 cm. broad, staminate flowers not seen.

description: Shrub or small tree; branches stout, 5-10 mm. diam., obscurely 4-angled, strongly sulcate, internodes 8-14 mm. long; leaf blades 510 cm. long, thick, coriaceous 2.5-6.5 cm. broad, obovate to oblanceolate, the apex rounded, the base obtuse or acutish, the margins somewhat revolute, mid-rib prominent, broad and conspicuously keeled on the under surface, primary and secondary veins about 2 mm. apart, prominulous on both surfaces, making a 60? angle with the mid-rib, petioles 1.0-1.5 cm. long, 4-6 mm. wide, axillary pit lunate, conspicuous, about 2 mm. high; inflorescence a terminal 1-3 flowered cyme, peduncle 1.5-2.0 cm. long, thick, sulcate, bracts suborbicular, strongly keeled, excurrent on the peduncle, pedicels less than 5 mm. long or the flowers subsessile; sepals 5 pairs, decussate, or the uppermost imbricate, the lowermost strongly keeled, excurrent, 8-15 mm. long, considerably broader, reniform to suborbicular, the margins con- spicuously white-scarious; petals 8, thick, veinless, oblanceolate, 2.0-2.5 cm. long, 1.2-1.6 cm. wide; staminodia about 50, biseriate, 5-6 mm. long, extrorse, the filaments thick, free to the base, anthers 1.0-1.5 mm. long, margined, lateral, dehiscing lengthwise, apparently producing functional pollen; ovary 8-celled, stigmas extrorse, sessile, triangular, about 5 mm. long, 3 mm. wide, centrally depressed; fruit globose, 2.5 cm. long, perhaps at maturity not exceeding 3 cm.

description: Stems herbaceous, glabrous or occasionally with long scattered trichomes, especially at the nodes. Leaves green; rachis 25-53 mm long, glabrous; petiolules 3-6 mm long, glabrous; blades 37-85 mm long, 16- 49 mm wide, elliptic to obovate, base acuminate to cordate, ciliate on the lowest leaf- let pair, pubescent along the abaxial veins, apex acute to acuminate. Inflorescence a dichasial cyme of 1-5 flowers, subtended by a pair of fully expanded foliaceous bracts. Peduncles 6.7-11 cm long, glabrous. Pedi- cels 10.5-16 cm long, sometimes curved in fruit, pilose at the base and apex with trichomes up to 4 mm long, occasional trichomes along length. Calyx segments green, 18-23 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, lan- ceolate to slightly oblanceolate, acute to acuminate, ciliate with both long and short trichomes, sometimes tomentulose near apex adaxially, with a few long scattered trichomes abaxially. Corollas light yellow or white, membranous, funnelform to narrowly campanulate, glabrous externally near base, increasingly glandular-puberulent toward apex; tubes 30-40 mm long, 17-29 mm wide, widest at apex; lobes 11- 17 mm long, 10-15 mm wide, widely ovate, apex rounded, emarginate. Stamens included; filaments 23-34 mm long, neither coiling or becoming undulate after anther dehiscence, converging on the ventral side of the corolla; anthers 4-8.5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, narrowly lanceolate, twisted after dehiscence. Style 28-43 mm long; style branches 3.5-7 mm long, terete, with short papillae covering nearly the entire surface. Fruit 32-47 mm long. Seeds 9-15 per fruit, 9-13 mm long, 6-8 mm wide, lacking scales.
bibliographicCitation: Prather, L. A. 1996. Three new species of Cobaea (Polemoniaceae). Brittonia. 48: 111-119.

description: Stems woody, villous at the nodes. Leaves green suffused with purple; rachis 28-61 mm long, sparsely and minutely puberulent; petiolules 2-7 mm long, puberulent; blades 46-103 mm long, 23-44 mm wide, obovate to elliptic to broadly elliptic, sometimes slightly constricted in center, puberulent along the abaxial veins, base acuminate to truncate, glabrous on the lowest leaflet pair, apex acuminate. Inflorescence a solitary flower, subtended by a pair of poorly developed bracts. Peduncles 1-4 cm long, puberulent. Pedicels 7-14 cm long, neither undulate or coiled in fruit, puberulent at base and sometimes slightly so along the length and at the apex. Calyx segments green, 20-27 mm long, 14-16 mm wide, ovate to lanceolate, long-acuminate, with a broad zone of dense pubescence adaxially, sparsely puberulent abaxially. Corollas white, tinted with purple or purple throughout, chartaceous, campanulate, eglandular villous near base, increasingly glandular puberulent toward apex; tube 35-38 mm long, 33-36 mm wide, widest at apex; lobes 15-18 mm long, 23-25 mm wide, broadly ovate, apex rounded. Stamens included; fil- aments 45-55 mm long, becoming undulate after dehiscence, converging on the ventral side of the corolla; anthers 7-9 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, narrowly oblong, not twisted after dehiscence. Style 40-45 mm long; style branches 4-5 mm long, broad, flat, with long papillae on the inner surface only. Fruit 45-55 mm long. Seeds several per fruit, 10-15 mm long, 7-12 mm wide, furnished with scales.

description: Stems herbaceous, villous at the nodes. Leaves green; rachis 40-85 mm long, sparsely puberulent; petiolules 6-12 mm long, puberulent; blades 35-80 mm long, 15-33 mm wide, obovate to elliptic to ovate, base acute to slightly cordate, ciliate on the lowest leaflet pair, apex acute to acuminate. Inflorescence a dichasial cyme of 1-4 flowers, subtended by a pair of fully expanded foliaceous bracts. Peduncles 6.5- 12 cm long, puberulent at the base and along the length, villous at the apex. Pedicels 17-29 cm long, slightly undulate in fruit, villous at base with trichomes up to 4 mm long, nearly glabrous along length, puberulent at apex. Calyx segments green, suffused with brown or red in center, 24- 33 mm long, 8-12 mm wide, widely lanceolate, acute, ciliate with both long and short trichomes, essentially glabrous adaxially, pilose to villous or rarely glabrous abaxially. Corollas yellowish green or oc- casionally yellow, chartaceous, campanulate, externally eglandular villous at base (rarely glabrous) and throat, increasingly glandular-puberulent toward apex; tubes 21-28 (36) mm long, 22-30 mm wide, widest below the apex; lobes 10-13 (17) mm long, 11-17 mm wide, deltate, apex imbricate, acute. Stamens about equalling the corolla tube or slightly exceeding it; filaments 27-29 mm long, coiling after anther dehiscence, converging on the ventral side of the corolla; anthers 7.5-8 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, narrowly oblong, twisted after dehis-cence. Style 42-49 mm long; style branches 5-7 mm long, terete, with short papillae covering nearly the entire surface. Fruit 34- 39 mm long. Seeds 10-15 per fruit, 14-18 mm long, 8-10 mm wide, lacking scales.
bibliographicCitation: Prather, L. A. 1996. Three new species of Cobaea (Polemoniaceae). Brittonia. 48: 111-119.

description:
A scandent shrub 2 m tall; stem black, ferruginous hirsute, petioles 3-6 mm long, strigose, borne above the middle of the ocrae which are spathaceous and flaring, oblique above, 5-7 mm long; blades oblong-lanceolate, 4.0-4.5 x 2 cm, apex short acuminate, base cordate, turning dark brown or black on drying, but dull, strongly bullate between the depressed veins, crispose-hirsute below, strigose on depressed midrib and veins above, ultimate venation finely reticulate; inflorescences terminal, spicate, 5-6 cm long, ocreae 7 mm long, membranaceous, spathaceous, rachis puberulent, only sta- minate flowering buds known, these black, bracts ovate, to 1 mm.

A distinctive, small-leafed species with oblong-lanceolate leaves that are cordate at the base, very dark brown or black on drying, conspicuously bullate between the main veins, and crispose hirsute pubescent and with spathaceous ocreae.

description: Small tree, 3-5 (10) m tall, ocrae membranaceous, 3 or 4 mm long, dark brown; petioles 5 mm long, dark brown to almost black, blades obovate, 2.2-5.5 x 1.2-4.0 cm, concolorous and tan when dry, apex rounded, obtuse to bluntly short mucronate, base cuneate to the petiole or slightly obtuse at the junction, glabrous; veins 3 or 4 pairs, margins entire, subcartilaginous. description: Tree, the branches yellow-puberulous; petioles 1-1.5 cm. long; lamiina oblong  or elliptic, 12-20 cm. long, 5-7 cm. wide, coriaceous, glabrous, the apex acuminate, the base rounded, sometimes oblique, the veins 8-9-paired, arcuate, suleate above, prominent below; infloreseence 1-2 in axils of leaves, peduncles stout, 1-1.5 cm. long, the rhachis yellow-puberulent; calyx cupular, irregularly and minutely 5-toothed, tomentose externally; petals oblong-lanceolate; stamens as long as the petals; pistil of male flowers rudimentary, ovoid, with a fleshy disk at the base; pistil of female flowers narrowly ellipsoid, constricted near the apex, the stigma disciform; fruit compressed, ellipsoid, to 2.5 cm. long, glabrous.

description: Tree to 10-12 m. tall, the branches terete, yellow-puberulent becoming glabrate; petioles 1-2 cm. long, stout, deeply canaliculate above, yellow-puberulent; lamina oblong-elliptic, 15-28 cm. long, 5-9 cm. broad, thinly coriaceous, glabrous above, puberulent becoming glabrate below, the apex acuminate, the acumen to 2 cm. long, the base broadly cuneate or rounded, slightly decurrent on the petiole, the midrib suleate above, prominent below, sparsely pubescent, the veins 10-paired, arcuate; infloreseence axillary, pedunculate, 2-3-chotomized, the branches cymose, yellow-puberulent; calyx cupular, 1.5 mm. in diameter, 1.3 mm. high, the lobes minute, to 0.3 mm. high, short crispose-pubeseent or puberulent; petals oblong, 4.5-5.3 mm. long, 1-1.3 mm. wide, yellow-puberulent outside; stamens in the male flowers 7.4-8 mm. long after anthesis, the filaments filiform, glabrous, the anthers oblong, 0.8-1 mm. long, the pistillate rudiment 2 mm. long, ovate or cylindrical, the base gibbose; female flowers not seen; fruit drupaceous, oblong, 2-2.5 cm. long, 7-9 mm. wide, gray-green, prominently 3-5-ribbed on the convex surface, the seed solitary, the embryo 1 mm. long.
