description: Annual, 2-6 cm tall, branching when well developed, eglandular and puberulent throughout, densely so on the peduncles and calyx teeth, ciliate on petioles and along lower edges of leaf blades and bracts; leaves entire and few, the lower petiolate and spatulate to spatulate-oblanceolate, (0.8) 1.7-2.2 (2.5) cm long, (2) 4-5 mm wide, (3.4) 4-5 (6.7) times as long as wide; main stem and branches terminating in dense leafy-bracteate flower clusters; bracts subtending the flowers, linear, (1.3) 1.5-2.5 (3.3) cm long, (1) 2-3 mm wide, (6) 7-11 (13) times long as wide, tapering to a slender point; calyx teeth narrow, firm, aristate-attenuate, unequal, the longer ones 3-5 mm long in fruit; corolla funnelform, about 1 cm long, the rounded lobes 2-2.5 mm long, blue with white throat; filaments ca 0.5 mm long, somewhat unequally inserted a little below the sinuses; style 5-6 mm long, stigma about level with the stamens; fruit capsular, the 3 locules each producing a single seed; the seeds mucilaginous when wet.

description: Much branched shrubs with both short-shoots (marked by fascicles of leaves) and elongate leafy twigs; nodes a little swollen; herbage when young with a reddish pubescence, when mature usually nearly glabrous (some plants retain pubescence especially on lower surfaces of mature leaves); leaves deciduous, opposite or subopposite or alternate; blades elliptic to broadly ovate to suborbicular, 0.7-5 cm long, 0.6-4 cm broad, at base rounded and often shallowly cordate and often a little inequilateral, at tip rounded or very obtuse and very narrowly retuse, marginally entire, penninerved with 3-6 pairs of laterals (these and the finer nerve-reticulum  slightly prominent beneath); petioles 3-10 mm long, on the adaxial surface at apex near juncture of blade bearing 1-3 ovoid-fusiform blackish or reddish glands 1-1.5 mm long; stipules caducous from elongate branches, long-persistent on short-shoots, intrapetiolar, ca. 1.5 mm long, either almost separate or joined to form a nearly entire structure. Cymes fasciculiform, 1-3-flowered, sessile; cup reddish-pubescent externally, 6.5-7 mm across, only one-third as deep as broad or even shallower; sepals erect, deltoid, 3 mm long, 2 mm broad, internally carinate, externally pubescent; petals ca. 2 mm long, entire, clawed; disk glabrous, thick, flat at summit, completely covering the ovary except at the central perforation; style cylindric with three short, spreading lobes at apex; fruits spherical or slightly oblate, shallowly tricoccous, 5-7 mm thick, in the basal third suffused by the accrescent cup and disk; seeds broadly ovoid or nearly orbicular, 3.5-4 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Trees 9-12 m tall with slender, pendent branches and trunk 12-43 cm thick; branchlets arcuate distally, rusty-pubescent, apparently quickly glabrate. Leaves alternate; blades oblanceolate, 8.5-20.3 cm long, 22-52 mm broad, at apex apiculate, firm-membranous to subcoriaceous, dark green, lustrous, margins on each side with ca. 65 minute glandular serrulations, with two strong basal-lateral primary veins and with 2-5 pairs of secondaries distally (all camptodrome near the distal margin) and with strongly percurrent tertiaries, glabrous except chestnut-pubescent along the larger veins beneath; petioles 6-9 mm long; stipules subulate, 3-5 mm long, rusty-pubescent, caducous. Flowers "waxy light yellow" in dichotomous thyrses or congested dichasia; thyrses ca. 8-12 mm long, 10-30-flowered; peduncle 3-4 mm long, the branches chestnut-pubescent; pedicels very slender, 3-4 mm long, elongating in fruit to ca. 20 mm; cup ca. 1.5-2 mm broad; sepals and petals ca. 1 mm long; disk massive but not quite obscuring the pubescent apex of the ovary; style deeply 3-parted, the divisions tapering. Fruit nearly globular (?; mature fruit not seen, but only an immature one ca. 6 mm thick, the cup of which was only 1.5 mm long).
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Clambering or sprawling woody vines or scandent shrubs or less commonly trees  up to 10 m tall (Fiji, A. C. Smith 14); branchlets slender and often somewhat zig-zag, the internodes 5-50 mm long. Leaves remotely alternate; blades ovate, 3-10 cm long, 15-63 mm broad, at base broadly rounded to often shallowly cordate (slightly narrowed when young), at apex acuminate, marginally on each side with 15 to 34 rounded, subappressed teeth (the lowest ones below the lower corners of the leaf), with each tooth marked by a minute dark gland and a microscopic, deciduous, dark glandular mucro, very thin, glossy, green, above essentially glabrous, with two prominulent basal-lateral primary veins and on each side two remote secondaries diverging from the distal three-fifths of the midvein and 2 or 3 secondaries diverging marginal from the lateral primaries, all these camptodrome near the margin, the tertiaries percurrent or the marginal ones craspedodrome to the glands of the teeth; petioles 7-17 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm thick; stipules deltoid, ca. 1 mm long. Thyrses severalflowered, pseudodichotomous, ca. 5-10 mm long, the two cymes elongate, racemiform, the peduncles 2-4 mm long, pedicels slender, greatly varying in length, in flower ca. 1-2 mm long, in fruit elongated to 5-15 (-20) mm long; flowers protandrous, rarely more than two of each cyme producing fruit, the oldest, lowest ones usually fertilized and then the upper ones often abortive, or if the early ones do not set fruit the later ones do; sometimes the upper flowers appearing unisexual (staminate); cup when young with some silky hairs, quickly glabrate, ca. 2 mm broad; style deeply 3-parted, the divisions slightly dorsiventrally flattened, spreading, at apex truncate, with a slightly broadened flange. Fruit 7-8 mm long (the cup about one-fourth as long) and thick, essentially spherical promptly dehiscent, breaking first loculicidally at the apex, thin-walled, the radial walls of the carpels membranous and occasionally parts of them adherent to the receptacle after dehiscence as a ragged, membranously 3-winged columella; placental pedestals low, flat. Seeds 4.5-6 mm long, ca. 4.5 mm broad, ventrally dihedral, dorsally convex, light (capable of floating), with a dull, brown, thin, easily breached coat, and dark, oleaginous endosperm as thick as the cotyledons which are yellowish.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Tree with trunk up to 21 m tall exclusive of crown, bole to 46 cm thick, sometimes with weak stilt-roots, some branches as much as 11 m long, but usually smaller trees; bark reddish brown or dark brown outside, smooth or dimpled or dented, very brittle; inner bark reddish or orange; sapwood pale yellow, very hard; branchlets closely rusty-pubescent. Leaves alternate; blades lance-ovate to elliptic-ovate or obovateelliptic, 12-22 cm long, 40-85 mm broad, at base cuneate or shortly rounded, at apex cuspidate or apiculate to long denticulate, marginally slightly revolute, on each side with about 60 obvious or obscure serrulations (each minute tooth with a black, gland-like point), firm-membranous to subcoriaceous, glossy, drying olive-green (upper side darker), with two strong basal-lateral primary veins and with 2-4 pairs of secondaries distally and with strongly percurrent tertiaries; venation slightly impressed above and raised below, the primaries and secondaries camptodrome; petiole 6-15 mm long; stipules subulate, 3-4 mm long, caducous. Flowers in congested dichasia or dichotomous thyrses; peduncle only 1-2 mm long (up to 1 cm in No. Born For. Dept. 4874); pedicels 1-3 mm long (elongating to 1-2 cm in fruit); flowers at anthesis not seen. Fruit ca. 10-16 mm long (the cup only 1.5-2 mm long), ca. 10 mm thick, nearly spherical to prolate; pericarp thin (flaking and black when dry) and readily detached; mesocarp thin, woody or cartilaginous, probably explosively dehiscent; endocarp cartilaginous distally tol membranous basally; ovular pedestals not prominent. Seed ca. 9-10 mm long, 7-9 mm broad, oboivate, dorsally hump-backed and strongly convex, ventrally dihedral, with a thin, dark, tawny-brown outer coat (not an aril) which detaches easily; endosperm very thin; cotyledons yellowish, oleaginous, very thick, easily separating from the thin covering, plano-convex; hypocotyl and epicotyl exceedingly small.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs; branches slender, internodes 2-25 mm long. Leaves alternate; blades broadly lanceolate to narrowly lance-elliptic, 5-10 (-12) cm long, 20-30 (-44) mm broad, 2.5-3 times as long as broad, at base rounded, at apex long-tapered, pointed (angle ca. 90º) with the midvein ending in a mucro, marginally slightly revolute with numerous obsolescent serrulations each marked by a minute, dark, glandular, deciduous  mucro, firm, above with sparse to fairly dense, loose to subappressed pubescence or tomentum, especially along the veins, beneath with dense sericeous tomentum, with two basal primary veins not much more prominent than the 5-7 pairs of secondaries all of which appear craspedodrome but are actually camptodrome very near the margin, with some tertiaries craspedodrome to the marginal glands and the other tertiaries inconspicuous and percurrent; petioles 3-8 mm long, ca. 0.8-1 mm thick; stipules subulate, 2-4 mm long, deciduous. Thyrses 1-2 cm long at anthesis; peduncles 8-20 mm long elongating in fruit; pedicels 1-3 mm long at anthesis, elongating to 7-10 mm in fruit; cup ca. 3 mm broad; style 3-parted more than half its length, the divisions tapering. Fruit ca. 8 mm long, nearly spherical, shallowly tricoccous (the cup slightly more than one-third as long as the fruit). Seed ca. 5-5.5 mm long, 4 mm broad, oval, black, shining, ventrally dihedral.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs to 3 m tall with slender, straight, tapering, often somewhat thorn-tipped  branchlets covered when young with a close, canescent tomentum (glabrous at thorntips); internodes 1-10 mm long. Leaves alternate or many of them fascicled at axillary short-shoots; blades oblong to obovate or rarely ovate-oblong, 12-30 mm  long, 5-15 mm broad, at base rounded to broadly cuneate, at apex rounded to emarginate to rarely pointed (angle ca. 100?), marginally mostly entire or usually at least some leaves on each specimen (especially at fast-growing tips) with 2-6 obscure serrulations on each side of the distal half, beneath finely and densely white sericeous-strigose, above finely and sparsely sericeous-hispidulous, membranous or firmer, the venation faint and essentially pinnate (by suppression of basal primaries), with 3 or 4 secondaries on each side camptodrome near the distal margin; petioles 1-2 (-5) mm long; stipules deltoid-subulate, 1-2 mm long, brownish on the adaxial surface. Flowers appearing in spring or summer following rains; thyrses 3-12- flowered, ca. 5-10 mm long, very compact, the peduncles 1-2 (-3) mm long; pedicels 1-2 mm long, elongating in fruit to 2-4 mm; cup ca. 3 mm broad; style 3-parted about one-third its length, the divisions tapering, spreading. Fruit 8-9 mm long (cup ca. one-third as long), ca. 10 mm thick, shallowly tricoccous, thick-walled, persisting 3-6 months. Seed turgid-lenticular, ca. 6-7 mm long, 6 mm broad; endosperm slightly thicker than the cotyledons.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Spreading trees 6-15 m tall; branchlets slender, ferruginous, densely sericeous pubescent to glabrous; internodes 1-6 cm long. Leaves alternate; blades broadly to narrowly ovate to lance-ovate, 7-14 cm long, 3-8 cm broad, at base rounded or rarely shallowly cordate, at apex shortly acuminate, marginally on each side with 60-80 minute, appressed, glandular teeth (each tooth with a minute, easily broken, glandular mucro visible from beneath), beneath densely sericeous pubescent to glabrous, above perfectly glabrous and very dark green at least when dry, with a midvein and a pair of subordinate primaries and 2 or 3 secondaries on each side diverging from the midvein, all camptodrome, the tertiaries irregularly percurrent or the numerous marginal ones acrodrome to the glands of the teeth; petioles 7-15 mm long; stipules subulate, caducous. Flowers in axillary cymes or foreshortened thyrses, the densely sericeous to glabrous peduncles slightly exceeding the petioles, becoming thickened in fruit; pedicels 2-3 mm long, elongating to 4-5 mm in fruit; cup 2-3 mm across; sepals triangular, 2-2.5 mm long; petals 2-3 mm long, markedly clawed and cucullate; style columnar, trifid one-eighth to one-third its length, the divisions linear. Fruit ca. 10-13 mm long, the thick, dark exocarp at length crustaceous and breaking irregularly, the remains of the cup (less than one-fourth as long as the fruit) adhering basally; fruit slowly maturing, persisting as long as 12 months after setting; three placental buttresses remaining on the cicatrix after dehiscence, massive and woody. Seeds 5-7 mm long, plump, and roundly bilenticular, dark brown, shiny with sculptured lines (reflecting the divisions of the cotyledons, epicotyl, and hypocotyl); seed-coat -relatively thick but brittle; endosperm scanty.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs or small trees; branches slender, the internodes 3-18 mm long; leaves remotely alternate; blades ovate-oblong to obovate-oblong to elliptic-oblong to lanceoblong, 3-11.5 cm long, 11-55 mm broad, 1.5-3.3 times as long as broad, at base rounded to broadly cuneate, at apex shallowly emarginate to rounded to acute or even very shallowly acuminate, marginally revolute, sometimes obscurely serrulate or crenulate (each of the numerous, obsolescent, appressed teeth with a deciduous, glandular mucro), firm to subcoriaceous, densely appressed tawny-tomentose above, beneath loosely tawny-tomentose (thickest at the venation), with two basal-lateral primary veins not much more conspicuous than the 5-9 pairs of secondaries which appear craspedodrome but are sharply camptodrome very near the margin; petioles 6-15 mm long, 0.8-1.3 mm thick; stipules linear-subulate, 3-8 mm long, caducous. Thyrses often somewhat corymbiform, much-branched, with 20-50(-70) flowers, 1-5 cm long; peduncle (i.e., main axis below first cyme) slender, 5-16 mm long; apparently elongating in fruit to 8-20 mm long; pedicels ca. 1-3 mm long at anthesis, elongating to, 4-8 mm in fruit; cup 2.5-5 mm broad; disk slightly verrucose to smooth; styles 3-parted about one-third to more than half the length, the divisions tapering, smooth. Fruit 7-9 mm long (the cup ca. one-third as long), nearly spherical, shallowly tricoccous, all dark brown to black and persisting unopened for some months; placental pedestals very small. Seed 4-5.5 mm long, narrowly obovate, somewhat compressed, ventrally dihedral, rich reddish brown to black, shiny.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrub or tree up to 25 m tall and 8 dm thick with rhytidome, platanoid bark caducous by plaques; youngest parts of herbage at least slightly rusty-tomentose including the abaxial surfaces the youngest leaves. Leaves opposite or subopposite, deciduous, glabrous or nearly so at maturity; blades lanceolate to broadly ovate, 2.5-12 cm long, 1.6-6 cm broad, at base obtuse or usually rounded or even slightly cordate, in the upper half attenuate or subacuminate-obtuse, entire-margined, pellucidpunctate, triplinerved at base (the two lateral primary veins attaining the upper third or quarter of the blade, and the finer nerve-reticulum eventually visible slightly beneath but not above); petiole 8-20 mm long; stipules half-intrapetiolar, caducous, deltoid, acute, up to 5-6 mm long, on the adaxial surface medially carinate and with 7 or 8 gland-tipped emergences. Cymes arising at the axils of already fallen leaves, few-many-flowered, up to 15 mm thick; peduncles 2-5 mm long, branched, all the axes rusty-pubescent; bracts minute, deltoid, obtuse, caducous; pedicels 2.5-3.5 mm long at anthesis, up to 6 mm long in fruit; cup shallow, up to 5 mm across, rusty pubescent externally; sepals 5(-6), triangular, ca. 2 mm long and broad, spreading at anthesis, densely puberulent dorsally, glabrous ventrally, on both faces medially carinate, pellucid-punctate as seen with transmitted light; petals 5(-6), ca. 1.8 mm  long, cucullate but not clawed, merely narrowed at base; stamens about equalling petals or a little longer; disk flat, glabrous, ca. 3.5 mm across, completely covering the ovary and padded from it with a mucilage layer; style up to 1 mm long, hairy at base, with three short, obtuse lobes at tip; fruit spherical or very faintly tricoccous, subtended by the cup (up to 5-6 mm across), 8-10(-20) mm thick, the exocarp at length thick and fleshy, later drying and separating from the endocarpids at their very tardy dehiscence; seed ovoid, 5-6 mm long, 3-4 mm thick, blackish brown, shiny, ventrally obscurely dihedral; endosperm thin.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs to 3 m; branchlets slender, dark rusty-tomentose; internodes 1-10 mm long; leaves alternate or on the floriferous twigs approximate or subopposite; blades ovate to elliptic-ovate, 3-8 cm long, 16-40 mm broad, thus about twice as long as broad, at base rounded, at apex acute (60-800 angle) to rarely blunt or even some leaves acuminate, marginally with 5-8 rounded, appressed teeth on the distal two thirds of each side, each tooth apically with a prominent dark gland on the abaxial surface, beneath slightly rusty-tomentose, above with sparser pubescence of long, white, silky hairs, with two basal primaries on each side not much more prominent than the 2 or 3 secondaries on each side diverging from the distal three-fifths of the midnerve at low angles, and all camptodrome very near the distal margin; tertiaries very faint and percurrent, or some of the marginal ones craspedodrome to the glands of the teeth; petioles 4-15 mm long, 1.5-1.8 mm thick, rusty-tomentose; stipules subulate, 2-4 mm long, deciduous, rusty-tomentose. Thyrses 5-10-flowered, 5-10 mm long, the peduncle greatly reduced; pedicels 1-2 mm long at anthesis, elongating to 10-13 mm in fruit, tomentose, glabrate; cup 3-3.5 mm across, externally rustytomentose; style 3-parted one-fifth to one-third its length, the divisions truncate and very slightly expanded at apex. Fruit 6-7 mm long (the cup one-third to, one-half as long), essentially spherical, thin-walled and only persisting 2-3 months before dehiscence. Seeds oblong, 3.7 mm long, 2.3 mm broad, black, shining.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs or trees 2-6 m tall (or, according to Sargent, Sylva 2: 49. 1892, up to 60 ft tall and with a trunk 4 ft thick on Umbrella Key, Florida); branches slender, inter- nodes 3-60 mm long, the younger ones with a sparse to dense pubescence of antrorsely appressed, buffy, silky hairs; leaves remotely alternate; blades ovate-elliptic to less commonly ovate to rarely obovate or still more rarely almost lanceolate, 2.5-9 (-12) cm long, 15-43 (-53) mm broad, or up to 60 mm broad (Turner 2089, Michoacan), or up to 12.5 cm long and 70 mm broad (in Honduras populations), usually about twice as long as broad (in McVaugh & Koelz 1595 from Colima most of the blades about three times as long as broad), at base rounded or broadly cuneate, at apex acute to usually acuminate, rarely rounded, margin entire but on each side ca. 1-10 mm from the base with a marginal gland and often 5-15 mm farther from the base another gland, rarely (or in Venezuelan populations commonly) with still another gland at about the midpoint of the margin, membranous to firm-membranous, green, above essentially glabrous, beneath with a very fine, close pubescence of tawny to buffy, silky hairs (denser near the veins) or glabrate, with pinnate nervation of, on each side, 5-9 secondaries, these crowded basally, remote distally, all camptodrome; petioles 5-25 mm long, 0.5-1 mm thick; stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long. Thyrses 8-20-flowered, 10-15 mm long, pseudodichotomous; peduncles 1-7 mm long; pedicels 2-4 mm long, elongating in fruit to 8-15 mm long; cup 2-3 mm across; style 3-parted about half its length, the divisions slightly dorsiventrally compressed and terminally truncate with a minute expansion or flange. Fruit 6-7 mm long, the cup about one- fourth or one-third as long, nearly spherical or slightly oblate, slightly tricoccous, brownish or reddish brown, promptly dehiscent, the walls rather thin (the inner, radial walls membranous and occasionally persistent after dehiscence as a ragged, membranous, 3-winged columella). Seeds 4-5 mm long, 2.8-4 mm broad, obovate, notched at the lower end, compressed, convex and slightly hump-backed, brownish black, shiny; wall rather thin, cotyledons and endosperm about equally thin.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs or trees even up to 30 m tall with a straight, cylindrical trunk; branchlets sparsely to densely rusty-tomentose, occasionally slightly zig-zag, the ultimate ones about 1 mm thick; leaves subopposite to alternate; blades ovate or varying to less commonly ovate-lanceolate or obovate, 2.7-11 cm long, 1.7-7 cm broad, at base rounded and sometimes shallowly cordate, at tip obtuse and often very shortly attenuate or acuminate, marginally entire to sinuate, membranous, either nearly glabrous or rusty-tomentose (especially beneath), triplinerved and in the upper half with 2 or 3 pairs of secondary veins, these and the finer reticulum of nerves slightly prominent beneath and impressed above, submarginally (several mm from margin) on either side with a row of small, circular glands especially visible beneath; petioles 2-6 mm long, glabrous or tomentose; stipules very small, lance-deltoid, caducous, tomentose. Cymes axillary, on peduncles, 3-40-flowered; pedicels 2-8 mm long at anthesis, elongating to 8-20 mm in fruit; bracts deltoid, ca. O.5 mm long; cup shallow, 2.5-4 mm across, externally buffy-pubescent to nearly glabrous; sepals 5, deltoid, 1.2-1.5 mm long and broad; petals 1-1.3 mm long, obtuse or even emarginate and cupped near tip, clawed; disk flat, glabrous, completely covering the ovary and padded from it by mucilage, perforated only narrowly at summit around the style; style 1 mm long, very shortly 3-lobed at tip, at the very base with an annulus of hairs; fruit glabrous to pubescent, nearly spherical, 8-10 mm thick, at base suffused by the cup about 4-5 mm broad; exocarp thin, remaining adherent to the cocci after dehiscence. Seeds black, slightly dorsiventrally compressed; endosperm rather thick toward the base.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Synonymies and typifications are given under the varietal headings. Trees 3-20 (-40) m tall with trunk up to 5 dm thick; youngest branchlets with a close, loose tomentum of ferruginous, silky, mostly antrorse hairs; leaves subopposite, seasonally deciduous (fide I. M. Johnston, Sargentia 8: 190. 1949); blades elliptic to elliptic-ovate to lanceolate, 7-25.5 cm long, 20-115 mm broad, 1.9-4 times as long as broad, at base rounded to very shallowly cordate to cuneate, at apex acute and usually very shortly acuminate or rarely obtuse, marginally entire to undulate (the shallow sinuses fitting between the glands), somewhat revolute in some popu- lations, above usually entirely glabrous and often dark green and lustrous with the veins slightly impressed, beneath with dark, rusty tomentum like that of the branchlets  or very quickly glabrate between the veins and also with some roundish black glands, mostly in a submarginal row or with the one or two, pairs nearest the base much larger than the rest or the glands nearly suppressed in a few populations, texturally from membranous (Panamna) to firm-membranous (Peru) to subcoriaceous (parts of Brazil and West Indies), with a regular pinnate venation of 4-6(-7) secondaries on each side camptodrome near the margins (the lowest pair often diverging from the very base of the blade making the latter trinerviate but not much more prominent than the other secondaries), the tertiaries irregularly percurrent; stipules subulate, 3-10 mm long, caducous, pubescent like the branchlets; petioles 5-25 mm long, 1-2.5 mm thick, pubescent like the branchlets. Thyrses 5-30 mm long, 10-50-flowered, dichotomous (composed of two equal cymes); peduncle 1-7 mm long, pubescent like the branchlets; pedicels 1-3 mm long, elongating to 3-12 mm in fruit, pubescent like the peduncles; cup ca. 2.5-3 mm across, externally pubescent like the pedicel; style 3-parted about a fourth to, two-thirds its length, the divisions slightly dorsiventrally compressed, terminally truncate or very slightly flanged. Fruit 6-8 mm long (the cup about two-fifths to a third as long), fuscous or black, glabrous, nearly spherical or somewhat oblate, very shallowly tricoccous, fairly thick-walled, explosively dehiscent. Seed obovate (to nearly orbicular?), ca. 4-5 mm long, 3-4 mm broad, turgidly biconvex, thick-walled, black, shiny, notched basally, the lateral lenses of white endosperm thicker than the adjacent yellowish cotyledons.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: The leaves are 90-215 mm long and 35-63 mm broad.

description: The blades are 8-15 cm long and 2-6 cm broad. This taxon, upon re-examination, does not appear to me to be as distinct as it did in 1963. As compared to its close relative, var. antillana, var. nipensis has long, narrow blades with a reduced number of submarginal glands, and smaller, fewer-flowered inflorescences. I have seen, in addition to the four collections cited in 1963, Howard 6177 and Ekman 1782, 3124, 3744, 4719, 6748, 9043, 9074, and 9671, all from the Sierra de Nipe and vicinity.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs or trees 1.5-5 m tall; branchlets slender, often somewhat zig-zag, with a shaggy tomentum of buffy, sericeous hairs, to glabrate; internodes 3-60 mm long; leaves remotely alternate; blades ovate to lance-ovate, 25-230 mm long, 9-110 mm broad, 1.4-2.8 times as long as broad, at base truncate to shallowly cordate, at apex acute or acuminate, marginally glandular-serrate, with ca. 50-100 forward-pointing (porrect) teeth per side, above with a sparser, soft, appressed pubescence of buffy to tawny-sericeous hairs, beneath with a dense tomentum of long, appressed, tawny hairs, with two basal primaries slightly more prominent than the 4 or 5 secondaries diverging from each side of the distal two-thirds of the midvein, all camptodrome extremely near the margin; tertiaries, faint, percurrent or some marginal ones craspedodrome to the glandular teeth; petioles 4-20 mm long, 1-2 mm thick; stipules 3-5 mm long, subulate. Thyrses 15-40-flowered, 15-30 mm long; peduncles 5-20 mm long; pedicels 1-3 mm long, elongating to 5-10 mm in fruit; cup ca. 2.5 mm broad; style 3-parted about half its length, the divisions tapering. Fruit 8-10 mm long (the cup about one-third that long), shallowly tricoccous, nearly spherical, tardily (in 4-12 months) dehiscing, thick-walled. Seed oblong to obovate, compressed, 5-6 mm long, black, shining; endosperm relatively thick for the genus, as thick as the cotyledons.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs or trees 2-7 m tall; younger branches with some coarse pubescence of antrorse, shiny, stiff, ferruginous hairs, densest at the leaf-buttresses; axillary thorns usually present, 5-20 mm long, representing the elongate peduncle of the thyrse (some thyrses split, however, by unarmed branches), thus bearing on each side, near the base, half of the thyrse; leaves remotely alternate or rarely 2 or 3 in a fascicle at a short-shoot; blades obovate to rarely ovate, 2.5-8.5 cm long, 17-60 mm broad (mostly 1.5-2 times as long as broad, or in Mexico tending to be only 1.5-1.7 times or in Panama' mostly 1.7-2 times as long as broad), at base rounded to usually broadly cuneate, at apex acute (angle ca. 900) to rounded (mostly acute in Panama and mostly rounded in Mexico with many exceptions), most or only rarely and almost imperceptibly acuminate, margins entire, firm-membranous, essentially glabrous or with some pubescence along the venation, with a pinnate venation of, on each side, 5-8 secondary veins camptodrome well within the margin, the tertiaries very faint and very irregularly percurrent, with marginal glands 0.5-5 mm from the base on each side (0.5-2 mm from base in Costa Rica and Panama', mostly 2-4 mm from base in El Salvador, and 3-5 mm from base in Mexico); petioles 3-18 mm long, pubescent and sometimes verrucose; stipules ca. 3-4 mm long, lance-subulate, caducous, the midveins spine-like at tip. Thyrses essentially sessile, 15-40-flowered (counting the halves on both sides of the thorn), pedicels 1-3 mm long, elongating to 10-18 mm in fruit; cup ca. 2 mm across; style slender, 3-parted about one-fourth to one-third the length, the divisions slightly dorsiventrally flattened, spreading, truncate, flanged. Fruit 5-6 mm long (the cup about one-fifth to one-fourth as long), ca. 7 mm thick, shallowly tricoccous, thick-walled, promptly dehiscent leaving a columella with three membranous wings on the small receptacle, these wings representing the radial walls of the carpels; seed ca. 3.6-4.2 mm long, 2.7-3 mm broad, obovate, basally notched, somewhat compressed, dorsally turgid and hump-backed, ventrally rounded- dihedral, dark reddish black, dull; all seeds seen were empty.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Divaricately much-branched shrub, the ultimate branchlets attenuate into a subacute  point, rather thorn-like and bearing rounded protuberances, alternate, 5-15  mm distant, where short-shoots emerge covered by little scales and crowned by 2- or 3-leaved fascicles. Leaves alternate, often fascicled; blades usually obovate or oblanceolate, 3-8(-15) mm long, 2-4 mm broad, toward the base a little attenuate and very obtuse, at tip rounded or emarginate, coriaceous, green when dry, glabrous when mature, smooth, with very inconspicuous venation including 1 or 2 pairs of laterals (secondaries); petioles 0.5-2 mm long; stipules very small, deltoid, lateral. Flowers solitary, terminating the leaf-fascicles, on pedicels 7-8 mm long; cup broadly obconic, 2 mm long, 3 mm broad; sepals and petals readily deciduous; disk glabrous, thick, with five broad lobes; style shortly trifid at apex. Fruit spherical, 6-7 mm thick; exocarp remaining adherent to the cocci, covered at base by the rather flat cup (5 mm broad) which covers the lower fourth of the fruit. Seeds brown.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs 1-3 m tall; internodes 1-25 (-40) mm long; blades ovate to ovate-oblong, 2-9 cm long, 1-7 cm broad, 1.1-2 times as long as broad, at apex rounded to less commonly acute, at base rounded to truncate to very shallowly cordate, marginally finely to very minutely appressed glandular serrulate, at each tooth with a minute to microscopic, deciduous, glandular mucro, membranous to firm, above strigose, beneath tomentose at least near the nerves, with two basal-lateral primary veins scarcely more conspicuous than the 4 or 5 pairs of secondaries diverging from the distal moiety of the midnerve, all weakly camptodrome very near the margin; petioles 2-20 mm long, 1-2 mm thick; stipules 2-3 mm long, subulate, caduous. Thyrses 1-2 cm long, 10-50-flowered; peduncles about as long as or slightly exceeding the petioles; pedicels 1-3 mm long, elongating to 3-9 mm in fruit; cup 2.5-3 mm broad; style 3-parted about half or more than half the length, the divisions tapering. Fruit persisting for a year or more unopened, nearly spherical or obovoid or slightly prolate, 11-13 mm long (the cup only one-fourth to one-sixth as long), often pendulous at length, very shallowly tricoccous, tough, the exocarp black eventually and forming on the distal dorsum of each coccid a slight hump or irregular Ceanaothus-like proliferation; placental buttresses not pronounced; seed 7-8 mm long, turgidlenticular, somewhat enlarged distally, very tough, brownish, shining, with little endosperm; cotyledons quite flat, ivory-colored.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrubs 3-4 m tall or small trees (Proctor 21888), the branchlets straight, those of the year with a very fine antrorsely appressed aureo-castaneous pubescence and in the pressed condition somewhat sulcate-costate with internodes 3-38 mm long, the year old branchlets with a grayish striate bark. Leaves alternate; blades obovate to elliptic-obovate, 5.3-11 cm long, 30-60 mm broad, at apex acute (forming a straight-sided angle of 65-80?) and very shortly rounded at extreme tip, at base rounded or less commonly narrowed, marginally entire, subcoriaceous, with a regular pinnated nervation including on each side 5-8 complete secondaries diverging at angles of 70-80?, arcuate, camptodrome near the margin, and also between the com- plete secondaries and near the base with a few incomplete secondaries which often (especially those near the base) terminate in black glands (the black basal glands so close to the petiole in Proctor 22192 and in some blades of Proctor 21888 that the relationship to the vein is obscure), the nervation, as a whole, flush on the adaxial surface which is glabrous, olive-green and somewhat lustrous, and only very slightly if at all prominulous on the abaxial surface which is brownish olive, dull and on the nervation having a pubescence like that of the branchlets; petioles stout, dark gray- brown, 6-16 mm long, pubescent like the branchlets; stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long, pubescent like the branchlets, caducous. Inflorescence a sessile, 15-20-flowered double cyme or often a thyrse by virtue of 2 or 3 cymes borne on a reduced leafless branchlet in which case the peduncle is 2-5 mm long and pubescent as are the branchlets; pedicels at anthesis 2-4 mm long and pubescent as are the branchlets; cup ca. 3 mm across, externally pubescent; disk thick, spongy, filling the cup and almost completely hiding the ovary to which it is coherent, flat on top with five radiate sulci leading to petals and stamens; sepals thick, deltoid, 1.5-2 mm long, externally pubescent like the branchlets; petals cuneate, slightly emarginate, con- siderably shorter than the sepals; filaments just as long as the petals so the anthers are not covered by the latter; anthers latrorse; ovary almost entirely coherent to the spongy disk, free at the top where glabrous, completely 3-locular; style short and thick, 3-parted about half the length, the divisions very slightly tapered, scarcely divergent. Fruit (Proctor 24901) very dark, almost black, nearly spherical, ca. 5 mm long, ca. 6 mm thick, very slightly tricoccous distally, rather thin-walled, fragile, very promptly dehiscent. Seed obovate, 3.5-3.7 mm long, ca. 3 mm broad, dorsally convex and slightly hump-backed, ventrally slightly dihedral, dark brown, somewhat lustrous.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Trees 5-13 m tall, entirely glabrous with very hard red wood; leaves opposite, decussate; blades ovate to ovate-elliptic, 6-12 cm long (in seedling to 2 dm), 3-7 cm broad (in seedling to 8.5 cm), at base rounded and very shallowly cordate, at apex acute and slightly short-acuminate, membranous, above green, beneath olive-green to somewhat glaucous, with glands of two kinds (small, blackish glands on the sub- marginal portion of the blade, and a peculiar proliferation in the axil of each of the secondary veins), with a pinnate venation of 5-7 secondaries diverging from each side of the midnerve and camptodrome well within the margin; tertiaries percurrent; stipules of the opposing leaves united into a lanceolate structure 6-8 mm long, darkly pigmented, very quickly caducous, leaving a prominent whitish scar; petioles 14-30 mm long (to 45 mm in a seedling), 0.6-1 mm thick. Thyrses 10-15 mm long, umbelliform, 10-12-flowered; peduncles 3-8 mm long; pedicels ca. 2-3 mm long, elongating in fruit to 6-13 mm; cup ca. 2.5 mm broad; sepals deltoid, ca. 1.5-2 mm long; disk 3 mm in diam.; petals ca. 1.5 mm long; style short, 3-lobed. Fruit ca. 10 mm long (the cup ca. one-third as long), a little greater in diameter, thus oblate, brownish, promptly and explosively dehiscent leaving a very small deltoid receptacle with minute pedestals. Seed obovate-oblong, 6-8 mm long, 4-5 mm broad, somewhat compressed, ventrally dihedral, dorsally slightly convex and somewhat hump-backed, black, shiny, at base shallowly notched, the lateral lenses of endosperm not as thick as the adjacent cotyledons.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Small tree (Baker) or straggling tree (Ridley); branchlets scarcely zig-zag, the internodes 5-38 mm long, when young with dense antrorse subappressed goldenbrown hairs; leaves remotely alternate (apparently deciduous after fruiting season- Ridley, Bot. Christmas Island, Jour. Straits Branch, Roy. Asiat. Soc. 45: 156-271. 1906), the blades narrowly ovate, 3-7 cm long (or 8-10 cm fide Baker), 2-4 cm broad (4-5 cm fide Baker), broadest about one-third the length from the base, at base rounded to rarely very shallowly cordate, at apex acute or at the extreme tip apiculatedenticulate, margins on each side with 14-20 appressed teeth (the lowest ones about one-sixth the length from the base), each marked by a minute, dark gland and a microscopic, dark, glandular mucro, firm-membranous, dull, olive-green or brownish green, above glabrous, beneath on the nerves with closely appressed brownish hairs, with two basal-lateral primary veins on each side and 3-5 secondaries diverging from the distal two-thirds to three-fourths of the midvein and five secondaries diverging from the marginal side of the lateral primaries, all these camptodrome near the margin, the tertiaries percurrent or the marginal ones craspedodrorme to the glands of the teeth; petioles 5-10 mm long, ca. 1 mm thick, pubescent; stipules subulate, 2.5-3.5 mm long, caducous, medially pubescent. Thyrses very compact, probably a few mm long in flower and pubescent with pedicels ca. 2-4 mm long, but on long, pubescent peduncles (31-39 mm long, fide Baker); in fruit the pedicels 8-11 mm long and the peduncles 28-40 mm long (not elongating?); flowers not seen (Baker says cup pubescent, sepals keeled ventrally, petals shorter than the sepals, ca. 2 mm long, stamens about as long as petals). Fruit ca. 7 mm long (the cup ca. one-fourth as long) and thick, essentially spherical, promptly dehiscent, breaking first loculicidally at the apex, thin-walled, the radial walls of the carpels submembranous; placental pedestals low, flat. Seed 4.5 mm long, ca. 4 mm broad, ventrally dihedral, dorsally plumply convex, light, with a smooth, polished, tough, brown outer-coat ca. 0.25-0.3 mm thick (thicker than in C. asiatica) and a slightly thinner inner coat, and on each side of the embryo an oleaginous lens of endosperm slightly thinner than either of the ivory-colored cotyledons.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Shrubs or trees 2-9 m tall; thorns 2-28 mm long, emerging in axils as prolongations of thyrse-axes (thus modified stems; occasionally with lateral cymes on the thorns and subsidiary thorns as in Macbride 5368); young internodes with very close pubescence of short, antrorse, stiff, dark chestnut hairs; older internodes glabrate; leaves remotely alternate, subdistichous or rarely in fascicles of 2 or 3 at a short-shoot, obovate or elliptic-obovate to almost rotund or nearly elliptic, 3.8-8 (-11) cm long, 25-60 mm broad, mostly 1.2-1.6 (-2) times as long as broad, at base rounded to broadly cuneate, at apex emarginate to rounded to acute (with angle of about 100?) and very shortly acuminate, olive-green, firm, above very slightly glossy and essentially glabrous, beneath dull and nearly glabrous or glaucous, at the petiolar attachment on each side with a conspicuous patelliform gland, and with inconspicuous, non-prominent pinnate venation on each side of 6-8 secondaries which are camptodrome well within the entire margins; tertiaries very inconspicuous, irregularly percurrent; stipules lance-subulate, 3-7 mm long, with prominent spine-like midvein, caducous; petioles (3-) 6-20 mm long, some of them highly verrucose. Thyrse much reduced, 20-30- flowered, "bisected" by the base of the thorn, usually appearing as two hemiglomerules, one on each side of the base of the thorn, the hemi-glomerules sessile, their bases forming fungoid knots; pedicels 1-3 mm long, elongating in fruit to 6-9 mm; cup 2.5-3 mm across; style 3-parted about one-third to two-fifths the length, the divisions spreading, dorsiventrally compressed, truncate. Fruit ca. 5-6 mm long (the cup about one-fourth to one-fifth as long), ca. 7 mm thick, oblate-spheroid, shallowly tricoccous, dark brown, promptly dehiscent leaving a membranously 3- winged columella (the lower parts of the radial walls of the carpels) persistent on the small receptacle. Seed obovate, ca. 4-5 mm long, ca. 3.5-4 mm broad, dorsally convex and hump-backed, basally very shallowly notched, ventrally dihedral, thinwalled (easily crushed), dark brown or black, shiny.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1971. Revision of Colubrina (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 23: 2-53.

description: Shrub ca. 4 m tall; branchlets slender, arcuate, covered with dense, shaggy tomentum of tawny, sericeous, antrorse hairs; leaves alternate or the uppermost  subopposite; blades ovate, 8-13 cm long, 5-9 cm broad, at base rounded, at apex  acute (angle ca. 70-802) and very slightly acuminate, marginally minutely erose  (under strong lens showing obsolete, appressed glandular serrations, each marked by a deciduous, glandular mucro hidden by the tomentum), beneath with a dense, matted tomentum of tawny, sericeous hairs, above darker, with a, much sparser strigose pubescence of subappressed, whitish-silky hairs; two, ba.sal primaries not much more prominent than the 4-6 pairs of s.econdaries diverging from the midvein, all appearing craspedodrome but actually sharply camptodrome very near the margin; tertiarie-sobscure, percurrent, or some of the marginal ones craspedodrome tol the obsolete teeth; petioles 7-22 mm long, 2-2.2 mm thick; stipules subulate, quickly deciduous. Thyrses erect, 20-30-flowered, 3-4 cm long on tomentose peduncles 2 mm thick and up to 3 cm long; pedicels 2-6 mm long, elongating to 5-10 mm in fruit; cup, ca. 4 mm broad, shaggy with tawny, s.ericeous tomentum, later glabrate; fruit ca. 15 mm long (the cup, about a fourth to, a third a.s long), tough, nearly spherical, shallowly tricoccous, the cocci without dorsal proliferations; seed very turgid, ca. 9 mm long, 8 mm broad, tough, the endosperm essentially absent; cotyledons extremely thick and yellowish, quite oily.

description: For synonymy and typifications see the varietal designations. Shrub or tree 3-12 m tall with trunk up to 3 dm thick; internodes quite variable, the youngest ones with inconspicuous pubescence of antrorse, closely appressed, buffy, stiff hairs, densest on the leaf-buttresses; older internodes glabrate. Leaves remotely alternate (subdistichous, teste Donnell-Smith, Bot. Gaz. 23: 4. 1897); blades 2.2-2.6 times as long as broad, at base very broadly cuneate to rounded, at apex rounded but very abruptly and pronouncedly cuspidate-acuminate, membranous, dull green, essentially glabrous on both surfaces, beneath at the very base on each side of the midvein with a very distinct, dark, fungoid or cupuliform gland, and on each side with 8-10 not prominent secondary nerves which are camptodrome shortly within the entire margin, the extremely faint tertiaries irregularly percurrent; stipules lanceolate, with a very pronounced spine-like midvein, quickly caducous leaving a large white scar; petiole 10-18 mm long, 1-1.5 mm thick, pubescent like the young internodes. Thyrses 5-8 mm long, 10-40-flowered, umbelliform or glomeriform and thus the true form obliterated, the pedicels attached merely to a fungoid mound representing the reduced axis and cyme-branches; pedicels 2-3 mm long, elongating in fruit to 6-14 mm; cup ca. 1.5-2 mm across; sepals and petals ca. 1 mm long; style short, slightly tricoccous terminally; fruit ca. 7-8 mm long (cup ca. one-third as long), ca. 8-9 mm thick, nearly spherical, reddish brown, promptly dehiscent leaving attached to the small, flat, non-pedestalled receptacle a columella with three membranous wings which represent the remains of the basal parts of the radial walls of the carpels. Seed dorsally convex, somewhat hump-backed, ventrally flat or very slightly dihedral, very thin-walled, basally notched; endosperm very thin.

description: Shrubs (presumably); branches virgate, straight or only slightly zig-zag; internodes 7-30 mm long, the younger ones with dense, appressed pubescence of buffy, silky hairs. Leaves remotely alternate, the blades ovate, 3-6 cm long, 2-4 cm broad, ca. 1.1-1.5 times as long as broad, at apex round to acute (angle ca. 80º), marginally on each side with 40-60 minute teeth each marked by a minute, appressed, glandular mucro, above minutely strigose to glabrate, beneath with a fairly dense but short, loose pubescence of subappressed, buffy, silky hairs, membranous, the two lateral primary veins slightly more prominent than the 3 or 4 lateral secondaries which are all camptodrome very near the distal margin, the tertiaries percurrent or some of the marginal ones craspedodrome to the glands of the teeth; petioles 3-10, mm long; stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long. Flowers in 6-15-flowered thyrses 10-13 mm long; peduncles 2-8 mm long; pedicels ca. 2 mm long, elongating after anthesis to 5-6 mm; cup ca. 2.5 mm broad; style deeply 3-parted, the divisions slender, tapering. Fruit ca. 7-8 mm long (the cup about one-third that long), 8-9 mm broad, shallowly tricoccous, with a fairly thick wall, persisting or tardily dehiscing (after several months). Seed very turgidly biconvex, ca. 5.5 mm long, 4.5-5 mm broad, black, shining, the cotyledons and endosperm about the same thickness, the walls strong, tough.

description: Large shrub; young branchlets with a close, dense, golden tomentum. Leaves alternate (or toward the flowering region subopposite, fide Beddome); blades narrowly elliptic-obovate, 5.4-12 cm long, 22-55 mm broad, at apex cuspidate-acuminate, at base rounded or very slightly cordate, marginally on each side with ca. 50, small teeth (each with a minute, glandular, black tip; the distal teeth more conspicuous than the proximal ones), membranous, with two basal-lateral primary veins not much more prominent than the four pairs of secondaries (the primaries and secondaries camptodrome, the tertiaries irregularly percurrent), mostly glabrous except golden-pubescent on some of the nervature especially beneath; petioles ca. 7-8 mm long; stipules subulate, minute, caducous. Inflorescence an axillary pseudodichotomous thyrse or congested dichasium; peduncles ca. 1 mm long; pedicels 4-5 mm long, probably elongating in fruit; flowers very much as in C. asiatica but larger, the whole in Wight 488 ca. 6-7 mm broad; styles nearly entire, with three small, capitate stigmas. Fruit not seen.

description: Slender shrubs to small, high branching trees mostly 2-8 m tall (to 15 m in the southern part of the distribution from Guerrero to Guatemala); trunk usually slender but up to 4 dm thick, with rough, dark gray bark; branchlets slender, ridged, often slightly zig-zag, slightly strigose to densely pubescent with buffy-sericeous, appressed to subappressed hairs. Leaves remotely alternate; blades ovate to lance-ovate, 3-14 cm long, 10-65 mm broad, 2-3 times as long as broad, at base rounded, at apex strongly acuminate, marginally on each side (in the distal three-fourths to four-fifths the length) with 3-10 prominent, remote, appressed, rounded teeth, each marked by an apical, dark gland which is more conspicuous on the underside (the populations to the south have on the average more teeth than those in the northern part of the range), membranous, above sparingly strigose to glabrate, beneath sparsely to densely pubescent with loose, grayish, sericeous hairs; the two later primary nerves slightly more prominent than the 2 or 3 secondaries which diverge on each side from the distal three-fifths of the midnerves and are all camptodrome very near the margin, the very faint internal tertiaries subpercurrent or some of the marginal ones craspedodrom  to the glands of the teeth; petioles 8-40 mm long, 0.5-1 mm thick; stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long, deciduous. Thyrses ca. 1 cm long or shorter; peduncles almost completely suppressed, rarely 1 mm long; pedicels 1-4 mm long in flower, elongating to 6-12 mm in fruit; 2-2.5 mm across; style 3-parted less than half its length, the divisions truncate and minutely flanged at apex. Fruit 6-8 mm long (the cup about one-third as long), nearly spherical or very shallowly tricoccous, dark reddish when ripe, thin-walled, dehiscing 1-3 months from anthesis ("pops open," fide Mexia 1892 label). Seed 4-4.5 mm long, 3 mm broad, oblong, compressed, black, nitid, with thin endosperm and thin cotyledons only slightly thicker than the endosperm lenses.

description: Terrestrial or less commonly epiphytic herbs or subshrubs, to 3 m tall, the shoots horizontal, strongly dorsiventral, to 2 m long, the stems glabrescent at base to golden-brown villous toward the apex, diam. to 1 cm, the internodes 1-4 cm long. Leaves strongly anisomorphic, petiolate; blade of the larger leaf in each pair oblanceolate, 8- 22 x 2-6 cm, the base oblique, cuneate, the apex acuminate, the margin weakly serrulate, the upper surface dull green, hirsute, lower surface lighter green to yellow-green, with a contrasting red to purple area in the apical fifth, pilose to strigose and pilose to sericeous at veins, the secondary veins ca. 8 per side; petioles 2-7 mm long; blade of the smaller leaf in a pair conspicuously oblique and lanceolate-subulate, 1.2-2.5 x 0.5-1 cm. Inflorescences in axils of the larg- er leaf in each pair, of 1 (2 or 3) flowers; bracts 2-4, lanceolate, the largest bract to 15 mm long, the others to 5 mm long, the apex acuminate, entire, purplish, golden- brown villous; pedicels to 5 mm long. Calyx deep purple, golden-brown villous, the lobes subequal, lanceolate, oblong to ovate, 12- 16 mm long, 3-6 mm wide medially, the apex acute to acuminate, entire to weakly serrulate; corolla cylindric to subventricose, 3.5-4.5 cm long, basally dorsally gibbous and 5-8 mm wide, narrowed to 2-3 mm above, widened to 4-7 mm medially and in throat, orange-red or yellow-red and villous externally, puberulent especially basally, and sparsely glandular-puberulent apically internally, the limb subequal, yellow or yel- low-brown, the lobes rotund, 1-1.5 mm long and 1.5-2.5 mm wide at base, yellow, with 2 brown dots on the dorsal lobes extending into the throat, the apex rounded, entire; filaments 20-30 mm long, connate ca. 3 mm at base, glabrous, the anthers included, coherent, ca. 2.5 x 2 mm; nectary a 3-lobed dorsal gland, ca. 2 mm high, 3 mm wide at base; ovary pilose-sericeous, the style 25- 30 mm long, reddish, glandular-puberulent overall, the stigma stomatomorphic. Berries globose, ca. 7 x 6 mm; seeds narrowly ellipsoid, ca. 1.2 x 0.3 mm, smooth, striate.

description:
A Columnea sanguinea (Pers.) Hanst. foliis apice cuspidatis, bracteis ovatis purpureis viridibusque et corollae ca. 2 cm longae flavae limbo 7-9 mm lato rubro differt.

Epiphytic, rarely terrestrial herbs to subshrubs, the shoots mostly horizontal, strongly dorsiventral and frequently branched, to 2 m long, the stems glabrescent at base to villous toward the apex, diam. to 6 mm, the internodes 0.8-1.8 cm long. Leaves strongly anisomorphic, sessile; blade of the larger leaf in each pair oblique, oblanceolate, 10-15 (20) x 2.5-4 (5) cm, the base cuneate, the apex cuspidate, the margin weakly serrulate, the upper surface dull green, hirsute, the lower surface lighter green, with a contrasting red-purple area in apical third, pilose and villous along veins, the sec- ondary veins ca. 8 per side; blade of the smaller leaf in a pair oblique and lanceolate, 1.5-3 x 0.3-1.2 cm. Inflorescences in axils of the larger leaf in each pair, of 1 or 2 flowers; bracts 3-7, the largest ovate with an acuminate-cuspidate apex, 2-3 x 0.5-2 cm, green and contrasting purple along its primary vein and/or apically (and rarely entirely) purple, pilose to villous, dentate to entire, the others lanceolate, 0.5-1.5 cm long; pedicels 4-8 mm long. Calyx pale green to white, the lobes subequal, lanceolate to subulate, 10-22 mm long, 2-5 mm wide medially, apex acuminate, with 1 or 2 "teeth" each ca. 1 mm long on each side, outside pilose, inside glabrous; corolla cy- lindric, 1.8-2.5 cm long, basally dorsally gibbous and 4-5 mm wide, narrowed to 2- 3 mm above, widened to 5-7 mm medially and in throat, yellow and pilose externally, glandular-puberulent internally particularly in the throat, the limb subequal, red, the lobes ovate, 4-6 mm long and 2-4 mm wide at base, red, with yellow margin inside, glan- dular-puberulent, the apex acute-obtuse; fil- aments 12-15 mm long, connate ca. 3 mm at base, apically puberulent and glandular puberulent, the anthers included, coherent, ca. 1.5 x 1.5 mm; nectary a 2- to 4-lobed dorsal gland, 1-1.5 mm high, 1-2 mm wide at base; ovary pilose-sericeous, the style 15- 20 mm long, glandular-puberulent apically, the stigma stomatomorphic. Berries ovoid, 10-15 mm long, 5-10 mm in diam. at the widest part, white; seeds ovoid-ellipsoid, ca. 1 x 0.5 mm, longitudinally striate.

description: Epiphytic or terrestrial herbs, the shoots up to 1 m long, strongly dorsiventral, glabrescent at the base to villous toward the apex, the internodes 2-3 cm long, to 7 mm diam. Leaves strongly anisophyllous, the blade of the larger leaf in each pair oblanceolate, 12-27 x 3-6 cm, the apex acuminate, the base cuneate, the upper surface dull green, sparsely pilose, the lower surface light green with sericeous veins, usually with 1 conspicuous translucent red-purple spot ca. 3/4 of the distance from the base to the apex, rarely nearly entirely red-purple, but then still only the usual area translucent, the secondary veins ca. 7 per side; petioles 0.3- 1.5 cm long; the blade of the smaller leaf in a pair lanceolate to subulate, to 1.5 cm long. Inflorescences in axils of the larger leaf of each pair, of 1 or 2 sessile flowers; bracts 1 or 2, lanceolate, to 1.5 cm long, caducous. Calyx yellow-green, villous, the lobes subequal, 2-3 cm long, filiform and laciniate, villous; corolla tube subventricose, basally and dorsally gibbous, 2.2-3 cm long (apart from corolla lobes), 2-3 mm diam. at base, widened medially to 4-6 mm, 3-4 mm diam. in throat, outside yellow, villous, inside glabrous, the lower 1/3- 1/2 of corolla papillate, the limb subequal, the lobes 6-11 mm long, villous, with short and glabrous appendages at the base of the lobes on the inside as in C. ililoba; filaments 1.8-2.2 cm long, with sparse glandular hairs, connate for ca. 6 mm at base and adnate to corolla tube base for ca. 2 mm, the anthers included, coherent, ca. 2 x 1.5 mm; nectary a 2- or 3-lobed dorsal gland, 1.5-2 mm high; ovary villous, the style 1.5-2.0 cm long, glabrous, the stigma bilabiate. Berry and seeds not seen.

description:
Planta glabrata caule ligneo, internodiis sulcatis, ribus bracteis 2 magnis 2 parvis appressis subtentis corollae lobis ventralibus longitudinaliter carinatis dorsales excedentibus ab omnibus congeneribus diversa

Epiphytic subshrubs or shrubs to 1.5 m tall, the shoots mostly horizontal, strongly dorsiventral, the stems rather woody, gla- brous with an irregularly sculpted cortex, diam. to 1.2 cm; the internodes 1.5-3.5 cm long, each with a lateral furrow from just above the large leaf at the node below and ending between the two leaves at the next node above, the nodes considerably wider than the internodes, surrounded by a cir- cular, narrow fissure between the attachment of the opposite petioles. Leaves strongly anisomorphic, petiolate; blade of the larger leaf in each pair oblique, oblanceolate, 14-22 x 3-6 cm, the base cuneate, the apex acuminate, the margin entire, the upper surface often undulate (at least in dried material), dull green, glabrous, lower surface lighter green with one large or several smaller contrasting purple translucent blotches near the midvein ca. 3/4 of the distance from its base mostly between the 2 apical pairs of secondary veins, glabrous, the secondary veins ca. 6 per side, occasionally sparsely appressed pilose; petioles 1-2 cm long; blade of the smaller leaf in a pair subulate, 1-2 x 0.2-0.4 cm, caducous. Inflorescences in axils of the larger leaf in each pair, of 1 flower; bracts 4, obovate rotund, the two lowest 1-1.5 cm long and 1-1.5 cm wide medially, with obtuse apex, the other 2 ca. 0.5 cm long and 0.5 mm wide, green, glabrous, entire; pedicel 2-4 mm long. Calyx green, glabrous, the lobes unequal, the ventral lobes largest, lanceolate-ovate, 12-20 mm long and 6-12 mm wide, the dorsal lobe smallest, lanceolate, 6-10 mm long and 2-3 mm wide, acute, serrulate-entire; corolla tubular-subventricose (as dried) to ventricose (on rehydration), 2.8-3.2 cm long, basally dorsally gib- bous and white, diam. 4-7 mm medially narrowed above to 2-3 mm in the throat, red and hirsute externally, paler red and nearly glabrous internally but sparsely glandular-puberulent mainly basally, with 10 15 parallel, longitudinal veins, the limb unequal, red, glabrous, the two dorsal lobes connate for 1-2 mm and with free, ternate lobes ca. 1 mm long and ca. 1 mm wide at base, lateral and ventral lobes ternate-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm long and ca. 2 mm wide at base, keeled along central vein externally, extending approximately 0.5 mm beyond the acute apex of the lobes; stamens included, the filaments ca. 15 mm long, basally connate ca. 3 mm (and surrounding the ovary with the nectary located in the dorsal slit), glabrous, the anthers coherent, ca. 2 x 1.5 mm; nectary a bilobed dorsal gland, ca. 1.5 mm high and ca. 2 mm wide; ovary ca. 4 x ca. 1 mm, appressed pilose mainly at the shallow longitudinal ribs, the style ca. 20 mm long, glabrous, the stigma stomatomorphic. Fruits and seeds not seen.

description: Erect, multi-stemmed shrubs, to 2 m tall; bark exfoliating in irregular plates. Young twigs densely glandular-hirsute with multiseriate-stalked, swollen-headed glandular hairs interspersed with shorter, uniseriate, hyaline hairs; leaves congested at stem tips. Petioles short, 0.5-1.1 mm long, densely glandular-hirsute as with young stems. Leaf blades coriaceous, narrowly ovate, narrowly elliptic, elliptic, or narrowly obovate, 4.3-11.5 cm long, 1.4-4.2 cm wide, tapering to a cuneate or narrowly cuneate base; margins plane to slightly revolute, entire, often with a few scattered teeth near the apex; apex acute to obtuse, often mucronate; upper surface bright to dark green, sparingly pubescent with scattered uni- and biseriate hyaline hairs and uniseriate-stalked, swollen-headed, glandular hairs, the hairs persisting on older leaves, along midribs, margins, and towards the base of the leaf; lower surface pale white to gray, densely lanate with uniseriate hairs and scattered uni- and biseriate-stalked, swollen-headed, glandular hairs, the glands red. Inflorescences paniculate, loosely and much branched, 10-20 cm long, rachis, pedicels, bracts, bracteoles, and calyx densely glandular-hirsute with multiseriatestalked, swollen-headed, glandular hairs, the glands red, imparting a reddish color to the entire inflorescence. Floral bracts narrowly ovate, 8-23 mm long, 1.5-4 mm wide, ciliate. Pedicels 8-16 mm long. Bracteoles 4.5-8 mm long, ciliate. Calyx lobes triangular, 1.7-2.1 mm long, 1-2.2 mm wide, acuminate, ciliate. Corolla urceolate, 5.2-7.1 mm long, 3.5-6 mm in diameter, red, the outer surface sparingly pubescent with scattered, short, uniseriate, hyaline hairs, the inner surface more densely pubescent distally with similar hairs; corolla lobes reflexed, 0.7-1.6 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide. Stamens 2-4 mm long; filaments dilated at the base, 1.8-3.5 mm long, glabrous or nearly so; anthers 1-2.2 mm long, 0.5-1.1 mm wide; spurs 0.4-1 mm long. Style 3.5-4.1 mm long, glabrous. Ovary glabrous or pu- bescent with unicellular, hyaline hairs. Fruit (immature) 3.5-4.5 mm in diameter. Seeds not seen.

description: Trees to 30 cm DBH and 10 m tall. Bark unknown. Sap red from inner bark. Branches subterete, semicanaliculate, 0.3-0.6 cm diam., rigid, wrinkled or longitudinally striate, tan to light brown to brown when dry, ferrugineous-tomentellous to tomentellous when young, ferrugineous-tomentellous in leaf axils to glabrescent elsewhere with age; hairs short-stalked, 2-branched to irregularly and minutely stellate. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged on upper trunk, distichous on branches, simple; petioles stout, terete to subterete, slightly to strongly canaliculate, 0.8-2.0 X 0.15-0.3 cm, slightly rugose, light brown to brown when dry, minutely to densely ferrugineous-tomentellous when young, becoming glabrescent to glabrous with age; hairs short-stalked, irregularly stellate or minutely dentritic. Leaf blades elliptic or slightly obovate-elliptic, 14.8-33.1 cm long, 3.8-9.0 cm wide at 1/4 length, 5.2-10.8 cm wide at 1/2 length, 4.3-8.5 cm wide at 3/4 length, thin to chartaceous; ad- axial surface olive brown to dull grayish brown and glossy-shining when dry, minutely ferrugineous-tomentellous when young, becoming glabrous with age; abaxial surface olive brown to dull grayish brown and minutely resinous-puncticulate when dry, sparsely ferrugineous-tomentellous when young, becoming glabrescent with age; hairs minute, sessile or short- stalked, irregularly stellate to dendritic; base rounded; margins conspicuously revolute; apex caudate to strongly caudate, the acumen 0.6-1.7 cm long. Leaf venation: adaxial costa raised and glabrous to glabrescent; abaxial costa prominently keeled, glabrescent to slightly ferrugineous-tomentellous (especially toward base); adaxial secondary venation brochidodromous, the veins arcuate-ascending, anastomosing near margins, 10-16 per side, spaced 1.0-2.7 cm apart, shallowly impressed, same color as lamina, glabrous to glabrescent; abaxial secondary veins prominent, same color as lamina, glabrescent to ferrugineous-tomentellous; marginal vein undulating; tertiary veins conspicuous, semiparallel, and semi-perpendicular to costa and secondary veins. Staminate inflorescences axillary, paired, paniculate, 3.3-4.4 X 0.5-1.1 cm, densely to sparsely ferrugineous-tomentellous, the hairs 2-5-branched, irregularly stellate; rachis alternately branched, the branchlets 11-26, 0.1-0.2 cm long, with a minute bract at apex; flowers arranged in clusters of 6-9 per branchlet, arising unilaterally from branchlet-bract axil, the pedicels slender, 0.05-0.35 X 0.01-0.02 cm. Staminate flower buds subovoid to slightly obovate. Staminate flowers: perianth subglobose-cupuliform, 0.09-0.21 X 0.07-0.15 cm, oil cells present (visible under low magnification and conspicuous when viewed in longitudinal or cross section), thick-chartaceous to thin-coriaceous, orange yellow when fresh, brown when dry, glabrous adaxially, densely to minutely ferrugineous- tomentellous abaxially, the hairs 2-4- branched, irregularly stellate; tube 0.03-0.1 cm long, the lobes 3-4, ovate to ovate-deltoid, 0.05-0.14 X 0.07-0.13 cm; androecium 0.07-0.11 cm long, the filament column 0.04 cm long, 0.02 cm wide at base and apex, the anthers 5-7, free, spreading from base, erect to slightly incurved above, 0.03- 0.07 cm long, the bases rounded, the apices strongly acute, oil cells present in filament columns and anthers (visible under low magnification and conspicuous when viewed in longitudinal or cross section). Pistillate inflorescences (as observed from infructescence) axillary, solitary or paired, paniculate, densely ferrugineous-tomentellous, the hairs 2-5-branched. Pistillate flowers (known only from persistent perianth subtending fruit): perianth thin-coriaceous, brown when dry, glabrous adaxially, densely to thinly ferrugineous-tomentellous abaxially. description: Trees to 25 cm DBH and 40 m tall. Bark unknown. Sap red when exuded from inner bark. Leaf venation: adaxial costa raised and glabrescent to ferrugineous-tomentellous locally or throughout; abaxial costa prominently keeled, glabrescent to densely ferrugineous-tomentellous (especially toward base); adaxial secondary venation conspicuously brochidodromous, the veins arcuate-ascending, anastomosing near margins, 7-27 per side, spaced 0.3-3.8 cm apart, shallowly impressed, same color as lamina, glabrous to glabrescent; abaxial secondary veins prominent, same color as lamina, glabrescent to ferrugineous-tomentellous; marginal vein undulating; tertiary veins conspicuous, semiparallel, and semi-perpendicular to costa and secondary veins. Staminate inflorescences axillary, paired, paniculate, 3.0-3.3 X 0.7-0.8 cm, densely ferrugineous-tomentellous, the hairs 3-5-branched, irregularly stellate to minutely dendritic; rachis alternately branched, the branchlets 14-17, 0.1-0.3 cm long, with a minute bract at apex; flowers arranged in clusters of 8-10 per branchlet, arising unilaterally from branchlet-bract axil, the pedicels slender, 0.17-0.24 x 0.02-0.03 cm. Staminate flower buds subovoid to slightly obovate. Staminate flowers: perianth ovoid-cupuliform, 0.09-0.17 x 0.07-0.12 cm, oil cells present (visible under low magnification and conspicuous when viewed in longitudinal or cross section), chartaceous to thin-coriaceous, orange yellow when fresh, brown when dry, glabrous adaxially, densely ferrugineous-tomentellous abaxially, the hairs 3-5-branched to irregularly stellate; tube 0.03-0.05 cm long, the lobes 3-4, ovate to deltoid, 0.5-0.12 X 0.1 cm, spreading from base, the apices acute, slightly incurved; androecium 0.05-0.06 cm long, the filament column 0.01 x 0.01 cm long, the anthers 6, distinct, spreading from base, slightly incurved above, 0.04-0.05 cm long, the bases rounded, the apices strongly acute, oil cells present in filament columns and anthers (visible under low magnification and conspicuous when viewed in longitudinal and cross section). Pistillate inflorescences unknown. Pistillate flowers (known only from persistent perianth subtending fruit): perianth thin-coriaceous, brown when dry, glabrous adaxially, densely to thinly ferrugineous-tomentellous abaxially. Fruits 1-2 per infructescence, ovate to strongly rostrate, 3.9-7.2 X 2.9-4.5 cm; pericarp ligneous, carinate, 0.1-0.2 cm thick between costae, the costae 9-10, longitudinal, projecting 0.1-0.2 cm above surface; green brown to brown when fresh, brown when dry, densely ferrugineous-tomentellous, the hairs 3-5-branched, irregularly stellate to minutely dendritic; base rounded; apex rostrate, the rostrum strongly acute, 0.2-0.5 cm long; indehiscent or slightly unilaterally dehiscent from base. description: Tree up to 10 m. high; branchlets slender; petioles rugose, shallowly canaliculate, often narrowly winged distally, 1-2 (-3.5) mm. in diameter, 7-12 (-20) mm. long; leaf blades coriaceous, oblong-elliptic, 10-20 (-35) cm. long, 2.5-9 (-12) cm. broad, acute to attenuate at base, ob- tusely cuspidate or short acuminate at apex (acumen up to 15 mm. long), often shining above, the secondary nerves 5-12 per side, ascending, raised above, prominent beneath, the tertiary nerves faintly raised or plane on both surfaces, the veinlets usually obscure; staminate in- florescenees minutely strigose on all exterior surfaces including perianths (hairs usually 2-branched, 0.1-0.3 mm. in total length), at length glabrous, at anthesis 4-15 cm. long, narrowly paniculate, the rachis usually simple, rarely 2-3-branched near base, bearing alternate lateral branches 2-10 mm. long, the peduncle up to 1.5 mm. long; flowers aggregated in irregular fascicles of 5-25 at ends of lateral branches, the pedicels slender, up to 2 mm. long; perianth thin carnose, often glandular- pellucid-punctate, 1.8-3 mm. long, 3 (rarely 4 or 5) -lobed about one-half its total length or slightly more, the lobes deltoid-oblong, obtuse or subacute; androecium 1.3-2.3 mm. long, the filament column carnose, 0.5-1.2 mm. long, the filaments sometimes free distally, the anthers 4-7 (rarely 10), 0.6-1.5 mm. long (usually subequal to the column or slightly longer), free, recurved, usually obtuse; pistillate inflorescenees resembling the staminate or more compact, the flowers sometimes 2 or 3 in sessile fascicles, the perianth carnose, the ovary ellipsoid, minutely strigose (hairs 4-6-branched or often 2-branched), the stigma cleft; fruiting inflorescences not known.

description: Shrub or small tree; branchlets rugose, cinereous; petioles rugose, shallowly canaliculate, 1.5-3 mm. in diameter, 12-16 mm. long; leaf blades coriaceous, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 10-16 cm. long, 3.5-8 cm. broad, attenuate at base and narrowly decurrent on the petiole, rounded or obtuse at apex, the secondary nerves 6-9 per side, arcuate-ascending, raised on both surfaces, the veinlets conspicuously and irregularly anastomosing, prominulous on both surfaces; staminate inflorescences glabrous throughout, compact, less than 1.5 cm. long, the rachis sometimes woody, the branches few; flowers white, in compact fascicles of 5-20 at the ends of minute branchlets, the pedicels slender, up to 2.5 mm. long; perianth carnose, about 2 mm. long, 3-lobed about one-half its total length, the lobes deltoid-oblong, obtuse; androecium about 1 mm. long, the filament column carnose, very short, the anthers 4 or 5, free, 0.6-0.8 mm. long, obtuse at apex, slightly recurved; pistillate perianth thick carnose, pure white (ex Ducke), the ovary subglobose, glabrous, the stigma peltate, subsessile; fruiting infloreseences compact, the mature fruits 2-4 per infloreseence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 5-7 mm. long, swollen distally), 17-22 mm. long, 9-12 mm. broad, orange red at maturity (ex Ducke), minutely stipitate at base, obtuse at apex, the pericarp brittle, about 0.4 mm. thick, the aril thick, waxy, purplish (ex Ducke). description:
Ad sectionem Coniostele pertinens; a C. Trianae et C. Mutisii (subtus descriptis) inflorescentiis masculis longioribus, perianthio saepe 4-lobato, floribus in fasciculis paucifloris aggregatis vel solitariis, forma androecii facile distinguenda.

description: Tree to 20 m high, the trunk 30 cm in diam, the inner bark exuding profuse red sap; branchlets flattened, robust, when young densely brown-tomentellous (hairs usually minutely stellate, short-stalked), later glabrescent, longitudinally striate, cinerescent. Petioles stout, 4-5 mm in diam, 14-20 mm long, slightly canaliculate, somewhat wrinkled, densely and minutely ferruginous-tomentellous. Leaf blades rigidly coriaceous, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 20-31 cm long, 7-11.5 cm broad, attenuate towards base, acute or acuminate at apex, slightly revolute at margins; surface above shining, glabrous, beneath dull, glabrescent or sparsely and minutely puberulent (hairs minute, sessile, short-stalked, stellate 2-rayed, or irregularly stellate); costa raised above, glabrous, prominent, glabrescent or sparsely pilose beneath; secondary nerves 10 or 11 per side, arcuate-ascending, con- spicuously anastomosing near margins with the undulating marginal nerve shal- lowly impressed above and prominent beneath; tertiary nerves subparallel, unclear above, lightly prominent beneath. Flowering inflorescences not seen; fruiting in- florescences axillary, apparently solitary; peduncle 20-40 mm long, 4-6 mm in diam, terete, densely brown-tomentose. Mature fruits 1-4 per inflorescence, ped- icellate (pedicels stout, 5-17 mm long, 3-4 mm in diam), elliptic, 4.5-5.5 cm long, 3.2-3.7 cm broad, abruptly acuminate at apex (acumen 1-3 mm long, blunt at tip), rounded at base, carinate on one side and also with 9 or 10 subsidiary longitudinal costae, these irregularly ridged and projecting to 2 mm from the surface; pericarp minutely muricate and ferruginous-tomentellous, when dried coriaceous, about 1 mm thick, unilaterally dehiscent when mature. Seed with a thin aril irregularly laciniate more than 1/2 its total length, yellowish when dry; testa dark brown and net-veined; endosperm white.

description: Shrub or small tree to 10 m high, glabrous throughout; branchlets when young somewhat wrinkled, striate, straw-yellow, later grayish. Petioles canaliculate, 7- 20 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam with colors similar to those of the branchlets. Leaf blades papyraceous, translucent, glabrous, oblong or ovate-elliptic, 6-21.5 cm long, 3-8 cm broad, slightly revolute at the margins, attenuate or acute, at base decurrent on the petiole or obtuse, acuminate at apex (acumen 10-20 mm long), often shining above, opaque beneath; costa prominent on both surfaces, the sec- ondary nerves 4-12 per side, arcuate-ascending, raised on both surfaces, the ter- tiary nerves and veinlets prominulous on both surfaces. Staminate inflorescences glabrous throughout, 1.5-6 cm long, axillary, 1-3 fasciculate, the peduncle slender, up to 2 cm long; the rachis usually simple or 3-10, alternate-branched; branchlets up to 6 mm long, 6-12 white flowers crowded at the apex; flower bud subglobose  or obovoid, rounded or obtuse at apex; pedicels slender, 1-3 mm long; penianth carinose, 1.7-2.2 mm long, almost equal-sided, 3-lobed about ?/ its total length, the lobes deltoid-oblong, obtuse; androecium 1-1.3 mm long; filament column terete, 0.3-0.4 mm long, the anthers 4 or 5, dorsally connate up to the middle, 0.6-1 mm long, obtuse, slightly recurved distally; pistillate inflorescences resem- bling the staminate, fasciculate-racemose, 3-4 cm long; the peduncle and rachis slender; 2 or 3 fascicles each with 3-8 alternate, sessile or subsessile flowers subtended by thin carinose, ovate, deciduous bracts about 1 mm long; pedicels slender, 3-4 mm long, perianth thick carinose, glabrous within; ovary subglobose, glabrous; stigma sessile, cleft; fruiting inflorescences 4-9 cm long; peduncle slen- der, 1-2.4 cm long. Mature fruits 1-4 per inflorescence, ellipsoid, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 7-18 mm long, swollen distally), 16-24 mm long, 12 mm broad, orange (ex Schultes et al. 12771), obtuse and abruptly stipitate at base (stipe about 2 mm long), obtuse or rounded at apex, the pericarp brittle, about 0.4-0.5 mm thick, the aril thin, usually bright red (ex Zarucchi et Balick 1727), waxy, laciniate at apex. Seed elliptic, about 1.5 cm long, 0.8 cm broad, the testa conspicuously dispersedly splotched with dull-brown.

description: Shrub or small tree up to 13 m. high, the trunk up to 25 cm. in diameter, the inner bark (at least sometimes) exuding a thin red liquid; branchlets slender, striate; petioles rugose, shallowly canaliculate, narrowly winged distally, 0.5-3 mm. in diameter, 8-25 mm. long; leaf blades chartaceous or thin coriaceous, glabrous, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 9-25 (-32) cm. long, 3.5-10 (-15) cm. broad, acute to attenuate at base, obtusely cuspidate or acuminate at apex (acumen up to 20 mm. long), often shining above, the secondary nerves 4-9 (-12) per side, ascending, raised on both surfaces, the tertiary nerves conspicuous, with the reticulate veinlets prominulous on both surfaces; staminate inflorescences glabrous throughout, 2-8 cm. long, narrowly paniculate or fasciculate-racemose, the rachis bearing alternate or subopposite lateral branches, these sometimes suppressed, usually simple, up to 1 cm. long, rarely branched, the peduncle up to 2 cm. long, flowers aggregated in irregular fascicles of 3-15 at ends of lateral branches, the pedicels slender, up to 2 mm. long; perianth thin carnose, often minutely yellow- glandular, 1.5-3 mm. long, 3(rarely 4)-lobed about one-half its total length, the lobes deltoid, obtuse or subacute; androecium 1.4 - 1.8 mm long, the filament column carnose, usually less than 0.4 mm. long, the anthers 4-8, 1-1.5 mm. long, usually free but sometimes dorsally connate up to the middle, obtuse or slightly apiculate, sometimes recurved distally; pistillate flowers up to 8 per fascicle, the perianth thick carnose, the ovary subglobose, minutely glandular, the stigma deeply lobed; fruiting inflorescences glabrous throughout, 2-8 cm. long, the miature fruits 1-4 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels 2-4 mm. long), 20-37 mm. long, 13-21 mm. broad, conspicuously stipitate at base (stipe slender, 2-5 mm. long), obtuse or rounded at apex, the pericarp brittle, 0.3 mm. thick or less, the aril usually red, waxy.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Tree, glabrous throughout; branchlets slightly rugose; petioles rugose, shallowly canaliculate, 2-2.5 mm. in diameter, 17-22 mm. long; leaf blades thick coriaceous, opaque, elliptic, 17-20 cm. long, 7-8 cm. broad, acute to attenuate at base and narrowly decurrent on the petiole, obtusely cuspidate at apex (acumen less than 5 mm. long), conspicuonsly revolute at margins, the secondary nerves 7-9 per side, ascending, raised above, prominent beneath, the tertiary nerves and reticulate veinlets conspicuously prominulous on both surfaces; staminate inflorescences 3-4 cm. long, narrowly paniculate, the rachis slender, bearing several alternate lateral branches 1-3 mm. long, the pedincle very short; flowers 4-7 at the swollen apices of lateral branches, the pedicels slender, up to 2 mm. long; perianth carnose, probably about 2 mm. long at anthesis, 3-lobed; androecium 0.6-0.7 mm long, the filament column very short, swollen distally and leading into a carnose obconical con- nective mass 0.8 min. in diameter at apex, the summit nearly plane, marked with faint radiating lines, the anthers 8 or 9, about 0.4 mm. long, the anther cells divergenit distally and separately adnate to the connectives; pistillate and fruiting inflorescences not known.
