description: Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout; branchlets slender, striate; petioles rugose, shallowly canaliculate, narrowly winged distally, slender, less than 2 mm. in diameter, 7-15 mm. long; leaf blades chartaceous or papyraceous, oblong-elliptic or narrowly elliptic, 10-23 cm. long, 3-8 cm. broad, attenuate at base and narrowly decurrent on the petiole, obtusely cuspidate or short acuminate at apex (acumen up to 15 mm. long), often shining above, the secondary nerves 4-8 per side ascending, raised on both surfaces, the tertiary nerves and reticulate veinlets prominulous on both surfaces; staminate inflorescences 1.5-3.5 mm. long, simple (rarely once-branched) or arising from a small swollen common peduncle, racemose or fasciculate-racemose, the peduncles short; flowers solitary or paired, subtended by minute ovate coriaceous deciduous bracts, the pedicels slender, up to 5 mm. long; perianth thin carnose, faintly and minutely puberulent or papillose within, 2.5-3 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes deltoid-oblong, obtuse; androecium about 1 mm. long, densely glandular-pucletate (except anthers), the filamenit column stout, carnose, leading into a truncate obeonical connective mass about 1.5 mm. in diameter at apex, the summit deeply concave, the individual connectives firmly connate but marked by small sinuses, the anthers 6-9, 2-celled, 0.3-0.4 mm. long, the anther cells contiguous but separately adnate to the connectives; pistillate inflorescences resembling the staminate but with slightly larger and more carnose flowers, the ovary subglobose, glabrous, the stigma small, subpeltate; fruiting inflorescences less than 5 cm. long, the mature fruits usually 1 or 2 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels 4-7 mm. long, swollen distally), 16-22 mm. long, 9-13 mm. broad, minutely stipitate at base (stipe about 1 mm. long), obtuse or minutely apiculate at apex, the pericarp brittle, less than 0.2 mm. thick, the aril white (ex Ducke), waxy.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Shrubs 2-3 m tall; primaries stout, 15-30 cm long, somewhat flexuous, not thorn-tipped, bearing numerous thorn-tipped stout secondaries 3-7 cm long which in turn bear short-shoots and some thorn-tipped tertiaries ca. 1 cm long, and some slender floriferous twigs of the season; epidermis yellowish green or reddish green, essentially glabrous; bark thin, flaky, gray or eventually smoother and dark brownish gray; internodes 2-5 (-10) mm long. Leaves alternate or occasionally in fascicles of 2-4 at short shoots; blades entire, obovate, 12-20 mm long, 8-14 mm broad, broadest abouat a third the length from the apex, apically truncate to rounded or even slightly poilnted (minimum angle ca. 1100), when rounded or truncate often mucronate or even eniarginate, basally cuneate, marginally entire, very slightly revolute but not at all thickened, membranous, bright green, rather smooth, micro vesiculate and not at all lustrous, glabrous; midvein yellowish green and slightly prominent beneath basally; upper and lower surface with slightly prominent impressed inconspicuous pinnate venation, the several pairs of laterals diverging at angles of 45º-85º, arching near to and paralleling the margin; petioles ca. 1.5-2.5 mm long, mostly glabrous but very slightly hispidulous in lateral lines; stipules subulate, ca. 1 mm long, with a hispidulous firm brownish median nerve and hispidulous white searious margins. Flowers solitary or occasionally in fascicles of 2-3 in the axils of the season's twigs; pedicels ca. 1 mm long; cup ca. 2.5 mm across, greenish, glabrous; sepals deltoid, a little more than 1 mm long, greenish, glabrous; petals absent; stamens shorter than the sepals; anthers ca. 0.2-0.3 mm long; disk rather flat and not very fleshy; ovary, styles and stigmas not seen; fruit when dry prolate, 6-8 mm long, 4.5-5 mm thick (probably somewhat bigger and more nearly globose when fully mature and juicy), reddish black to black, with thin pulp and large stone; stone rather heavy-walled, apparently constantly and completely two-celled and 2-seeded, the endosperm very thin.

description: Shrubs or small trees up to 4 m tall; wood anatomy described by Molle, 1939; trunk to at least 20 cm thick; bark smooth, usually grayish, thin, flaking after a year or two; older bark unknown; primaries 10-20 (-50) cm long, slender, arcuate, often slightly flexuous; secondaries thorn-tipped, (1-) 3-7 cm long, bearing numerous short shoots and often also thorn-tipped tertiaries ea. 1 cm long; epidermis purplish or brownish, more or less densely hispidulous or glabrous; internodes 2-9 (-20) mm long. Leaves alternate or mostly in fascicles of 1-8 at the short shoots, appearing in the spring (October); blades elliptic-obovate or occasionally obovate or elliptic-obovate, (13-) 15-25 (-45) mm long, (5-) 7-12 (-22) mm broad, broadest near the middle, apically rounded, often emarginate, often mucronate, basally acuminate, marginally entire and not thickened, when mature and dry very slightly revolute and toward the base often hispidulous, firm, above usually olive-brown or dark brown, microvesiculate and glabrous, beneath usually dark olive-brown or even chestnut-brown, glabrous or often microhispidulous, with usually inconspicuous flush venation including the midvein and 4-7 pairs of laterals diverging at angles of 50º-80º and gently arching near to and parallel the margin, the more distal ones closing to the mucro; petioles 2-5 mm long, purplish olive or grayish green, slightly hispidulous especially at the confluence of blade-margins; stipules triangular, ea. 1 mm long, subulate, firm, purplish gray to brown, slightly strigose or hispidulous. Flowers vernal, appearing with or before the leaves- (October), in fascicles of 2-10 at the short shoots; pedicels (2-) 3-6 mm long, rather slender, olivaceous or olive green, often slightly arcuate, glabrous or nearly so; cup 1.5-2 mm across, purplish brown and nearly glabrous; sepals deltoid-elongate, (1.3-) (1.6-1.8 (-2) mm long, purplish or olivaceous, nearly glabrous; petals absent; sta- mens shorter than the sepals, strongly introrse even at anthesis; anthers ca. 0.3-0.5 mm long; ovary globose, brownish, glabrous, completely 2-loculed, strongly constricted basally, each locule with one ovule; style, ca. 0.6 mm long, rather stout, slightly 2-grooved and very slightly knobbed apically, fruit (known only from Venturi 976) prolate, ca. 6.5 mm long and 4 mm thick (would be thicker if pulp were moist), with a thick 2-celled, 1- to 2-seeded stone.

description: Frutices ramulis spisse hispidulosis crassis, supra aculeis munitis, internodis 1-7 mm longis; folia alterna aut fasciculata, elliptico-obovata, 7-11 (-21) mm longa, 4-6 (-10) mm lata, integra, basi cuneata, utrinque hispidulosa, dilute viridia, venatione infra inconspicua, vix elevata, minus quam decimam partem superficiei occupante; flores fasciculati ca. 4 mm diam., apetali; pedicellis 0.4-1 mm longis; ovarium basi constrictum; styli integri; fructus atri 8 mm crassi; nucla prolata, bilocularis membrana crassa praedita; semina plerumque dua.

description: Shrubs 1-3 m tall; primaries stout, 10-35 cm long, arcuate, occasionally thorn-tipped, bearing numerous stout thorn-tipped secondaries 1-6 cm long, these in turn bearing leafy short- shoots and after the first year slender leafy and floriferous twigs ca. 1-2 cm long; bark grayish brown to nearly black, rather smooth or flaking in narrow undulating fissures; epidermis pale yellowish green, rather densely canescent-hispidulous; internodes 1-5 (-7) mm long. Leaves alternate or occasionally in fascicles of 2-4 at the short shoots; blades elliptic-obovate, 7-11 (-21) mm long, 4-6 (-10) mm broad, broadest ca. two-fifths the length from the apex, apically rounded and emarginate or apiculate or acute (minimum angle 900), basally cuieate, marginally entire and hispidulous and very slightly thickened, firm to subcoriaceous, above pale flavescent or canescent green and micro vesiculate and sparsely hispidulous, beneath very slightly paler flaveseent or canescent green and densely hispidulous and microvesiculate with inconspicuous but very slightly prominent concolorous venation including the midvein and 4-5 (-7) pairs of laterals diverging at angles of 350-600 and arching to near the margins; petioles ca. 1 mm long, pubescent like the blade; stipules subulate, ca. 1 mm long, firm, pale purplish olive, densely antrorsely hispidulous. Flowers in fascicles of (1-) 2-4 at the axils of the season's twigs; pedicels 0.-1 mm long, pubescent like the leaves; cup ca. 2 mm across, purplish olive, minutely and more or less densely hispidulous outside; sepals deltoid, ca. 1 mm long, purplish green, firm, minutely hispidulous outside; petals absent; stamens shorter than the sepals, introrse; anthers 0.2-0.3 mm long; disk rather flat, fleshy; ovary globose-conic, purplish brown, glabrous, basally strongly constricted, two-celled, each cell with an ovule; style stout, 0.5-0.7 mm long, brownish purple, slightly capitate and indistinctly grooved terminally. Fruit when dry prolate, when fully mature and juicy globose, ca. 8 mm thick, black with prolate, thick-walled two-celled and usually 2-seeded stone 7 mm long.

description: Shrubs 0.3-1 (-1.3) m tall; primaries slightly arcuate or nearly straight, 5-18 cm lolng, thorn-tipped, bearing few to numerous thorn-tipped secondaries 2-7 cm long and these in turn bearing leafy and floriferous short shoots and occasionally also some "tertiary" thorns 2-6 mm long; epidermis brownish or purplish olive, essentially glabrous; bark dark grayish to nearly black, rather thin and smooth; internodes 1-2 (-4) mm long. Leaves alternate or most in fascicles of 2-9 at the short shoots, essentially sessile; blades linear, 2-13 mm long, ca. 1 mm broad, apically shortly acute, marginally entire, coriaceous, grayish with a waxy texture, above rounded or with a slight median sulcus, beneath with a flat median portion (midvein) occupying most of the width, along which are grooves as if the vestigial lateral portions of the blade were revolute, often with some minute hispidulous hairs attached in the grooves (leaves otherwise glabrous) ; no venation visible; stipules subulate, ca. 1.5 mm long, brownish, with minutely ciliate margins distally. Flowers axillary, mostly in fascicles of 2-6 at the short shoots; pedicels 1-2.5 mm long, glabrous, yellowish; floral cup 1.7-2.5 mm across, yellowish, glabrous; sepals deltoid, ca. 1.5 mm long, yellowish, glabrous; petals shorter than the sepals and alternate with them, spatulate, emarginate, yellowish, membranous, reflexed, eaducous; stamens opposite petals; anthers 0.4-0.5 mm long; disk rather thin and very flat; ovary globose-conic, purplish-black, glabrous, strongly constricted basally, completely two-celled at least at an early stage (septum thin) and each cell with one ovule, or one of these suppressed early in the ontogeny. Styles stout, purplish-black, 0.6-1 mm long, entire but distinctly grooved terminally, persistent and basally enlarging to become the apiculation on the stone; fruit pronouncedly prolate, 7-12 mm long, 1.5-2 times as long as thick, when unripe or abortive dry and yellowish-brown, when fully mature and juicy (rarely in herbarium specimens) reddish black or purplish black with a thin pulp and a very thick-walled, apiculate stone usually only one-celled and 1-seeded (less commonly two-celled and 2-seeded as in E. J. Palmer 12494, A).

description: Rounded shrubs 0.5-3 m tall; primaries only 5-15 cm long, all thorn-tipped; secondaries proliferous near the ends of the primaries, 2-5 cm long, bearing numerous short-shoots; bark minutely furrowed, fuscous-gray to nearly black; epidermis olive-green, densely hispidulous; internodes 0.5-1 mm long or less. Leaves alternate or usually in fascicles of 2-5 at the short shoots; blades spatulate to narrowly spatulate, (2-) 3-7 (-9) mm long, (0.5-) 1-2.1 mm broad, broadest about one-third the length from the apex, apically acute with a minimum angle of about 90º, basally acuminate, marginally entire and not thickened, firm and slightly thickened medially, both surfaces olive green and perfectly glabrous and microvesiculate, the undersurface wrinkled when dry with no discernible venation except occasionally the broad flat midvein; petioles glabrous, less than 1 mm long; stipules deltoid, ca. 0.6 mm long, purplish, mar- ginally minutely ciliate. Flowers solitary in the axils of the primary innovations which appear in the summer and early fall following the sporadic rains, or rarely in fascicles of 2-3 at the short shoots; pedicels 0.6-1 mm long, olive, glabrous; cup 1.3-1.6 mm across, purplish-olive, glabrous; sepals elongate-deltoid, 1.2-1.5 mm long, fla- veseent-olive, glabrous; petals absent; stamens shorter than the sepals, introrse; anthers ca. 0.25 mm long; disk narrow and fleshy; ovary globose-conic, dark purple, glabrous, strongly constricted basally, two-celled, each cell with one ovule; style stout, ca. 0.6 mm long, purpish, with an obscurely capitate stigma which is grooved terminally; fruit markedly prolate or when quite mature and juicy nearly globose, 5-6 mm thick, black, with a relatively thick pulp and a narrowly ellipsoid usually 1-seeded stone.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Large shrubs or small trees (0.5-) 2-3 (-6) m tall; primaries 15-35 on cm long, arcuate, usually not thorn-tipped; secondaries numerous, thorn-tipped, 3-13 cm long, bearing numerous short shoots (which become rather more prominent in this species than in Nos. 5, 7 and 8, in some specimens resembling small strobili) and rarely a few thorn-tipped "tertiaries" ca. 3-4 mm long; bark rather smooth and gray, thin; epidermis pale olive or purplish or reddish-olive, glabrous or hispidulous (see varieties); internodes 2-7 mm long. Leaves alternate or mostly in fascicles of 2-7 at the short shoots; blades entire, spatulate, 3-12 mm long, 1.6-5 mm broad, broadest about a third the length from the apex, apically truncate or rounded or acute (minimum angle 700), basally long-acuminate, marginally entire and slightly thickened, pale yellowish olive or less commonly with a purplish tinge like the primary branches,, membranous but firm, glabrous or hispidulous, above smooth or microvesiculate, beneath with the prominent flat or suleate paler pinnate ven- ation occupying most of the surface of the smaller leaves (proportionately less area in the promptly deciduous and somewhat larger primary leaves of the elongating primary branches), with 3-4 pairs of laterals diverging at angles of 25 040' and paralleling the margin, seemingly abruptly terminating at the distal margin, petioles 1-2 mm long, slender, pale olive-green, glabrous or hispidulous; stipules triangular, ca. 0.6-0.7 mm long, dark brown, sparingly and minutely villous especially near the margin. Flowers in fascicles of (1-) 2-8 at the short shoots, appearing in the fall among the secondary leaves. Pedicels 2.5-4 (-6.5) mm long, very slender, pale olive or purplish, glabrous or hispidulous, commonly distinctly arcuate; cup 1-1.5 mm across, deep olive or purplish, glabrous to hispidulous without; sepals elongate-deltoid, ca. 1 mm long, yellowish olive-green, glabrous, to hispidu- lous outside, glabrous inside; petals absent; stamens shorter than the sepals, anthers 0.25-0.35 mm long; disk rather small, fleshy; ovary globose-conic, purplish, glabrous, strongly constricted basally, completely two-celled, each cell with one ovule; style 0.5-0.7 mm long, rather stout, apically with a slight groove. Fruit (maturing the spring following the fall flowering) globose or often very slightly prolate (or even rarely oblate, especially at the time of maximum juciness of the pulp), 3.4-5.1 mm long, black, with a thin pulp and large stone; wall of stone thick but brittle and not very strong, stone completely two-celled, 1-seeded or less commonly 2-seeded.

description: Large shrubs or small trees 2-4 m tall; branches stout; primaries stout, ar- cuate, somewhat flexuous or straight, 10-30 cm long, usually not thorn-tipped, secondaries numerous, 2- cm long, thorn-tipped, the thorns brown, valid, gla- brous, shining; secondaries also bearing numerous axillary short shoots and also sometimes some short thorn-tipped tertiaries; bark thin, brownish, flaky; epidermis purplish-brown, densely hispidulous or short villous; internodes 2-4 mm long. Leaves alternate or usually in fascicles of 2-6 at the short shoots; blades obovate, 8-12 (-16) mm long, 6.5-11 mm broad, broadest about a third the length from the apex, apically rounded or truncate or emarginate and mucron- ulate, basally short-acuminate, marginally entire and toward the base hispidu- lous, firm or subcoriaceous, above brownish green or dark olive, glabrous, when dry with a minute honeycomb pattern of shiny-vesiculate ridges, beneath olive or olive green, glabrous, with inconspicuous flush venation including a midrib and ca. 4 pairs of laterals diverging at angles of 40?-70?, arching to near the margin and then to a close near the apex; petioles ca. 1 mm long, pale-purplish- stramineous like the midrib basally, laterally densely hispid or strigose; stipules subulate, ca. 1-1.5 mm long, firm, dorsally round-keeled, straminous, ap- pressed-strigose. Flowers appearing in March in fascicles of (1-) 2-3 at the short shoots; pedicels slender, ca. 1 mm long at anthesis, elongating to ca. 2 mm in fruit; cup ca. 2 mm across, dark purplish, nearly glabrous; sepals triangular, 1-1.3 mm long, firm, pale purplish olive, glabrous; petals absent; stamens shorter than or almost equalling the sepals, the filaments introrse; anthers ca. 0.3 mm long; disk thick and fleshy, dark purple; ovary globose, dark purple, glabrous, basally strongly constricted, completely two-celled, each cell with one ovule; style very stout, ca. 0.6 mm long, purplish, apparently articulated basally, vaguely knobby and 2-lobed terminally; fruit globose or slightly prolate, black, ca. 5-6 mm long, with a thick-walled, two-celled, 1- to 2-seeded stone, and thin pulp.

description: Shrubs or small trees (1-) 2-3 (-7) m tall; primaries 10-35 cm long, stout to slender, arcuate and slightly flexuous or nearly straight, not thorn-tipped, bearing few to numerous thorn-tipped secondaries 2-4 (-7) cm long and these in turn bearing short shoots and rarely a few tertiary thorns ca. 0.5-1 cm long and the slender floriferous twigs of the season; epidermis quite glabrous or densely hispidulous; internodes 2-5 (-11) mm long. Leaves alternate or less commonly in fascicles of 2-4 at short shoots; blades obovate, (10-) 15-20 (-31) mm long, (5-) 9-12 (-19) mm broad, broadest about a third the length from the apex, apically mucronate and usually rounded or sometimes truncate and emarginate or rarely slightly acute (minimum angle ca. 1000), basally acuminate, marginally unthickened, entire or with 2-4 inconspicuous small introrse teeth on the distal half, membranous, above rather smooth and flavescent buffy green or occasionally flaveseent brownish green and glabrous or occasionally hispidulous, beneath paler flaveseent olive green with inconspicuous flush venation including the midrib and 3-4 pairs of laterals diverging at angles of 35º-60º and arching well within the margin, the most distalpair appearing to close at the mucro; petioles 1-2 (-4) mm long, hispidulous in lateral lines at the junction of the blade or less commonly hispidulous all over; stipules deltoid-acuminate, ca. 1 mm long, pale brownish, thin, antrorsely strigose at least marginally. Flowers solitary or usually in axillary fascieles of 2-3 on the twigs of the season; pedicels at anthesis less than 1 mm long, in fruit 1-2 mm long, green; cup 1.5-2 mm across, green, glabrous, sepals deltoid, ca. 1 mm long, green, glabrous; petals absent; stamens shorter than the sepals, introrse; anthers ca. 0.25 mm long; disk flat and somewhat fleshy; ovary globose, purplish-black, strongly constricted basally, completely two-celled, each cell with one ovule; style slender, 0.5-0.7 mm long, purplish, terminally indistinctly grooved, not at all capitate; fruit when fully mature and juicy black and globose and 5-6 mm thick with a thick pulp and a rather small globose or slightly prolate two-celled and 1- to 2-seeded stone 4-5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: A free translation of the description by Castellanos is given here: Shrubs 1-1.5 m tall, with trunk up to 5 cm thick, intricately branched; branchlets thorn-tipped, the secondaries ca. 5 cm long, much shorter than the primaries, and on each primary the lower secondaries much shorter than the upper secondaries; older branches with fuscous bark, younger ones with gray bark; epidermis of twigs purple. Leaves in fascicles of 6-14 at short shoots, spatulate, ca. 5-6 mm long, 1 mm broad, dark green, glabrous, apically mucronulate, somewhat thickened and fleshy, with conspicuous central venation beneath. Flowers solitary or in fascicles of 2 at the short shoots, not seen; the pedicels in fruit up to 3 mm long, drupes solitary at the short shoots, prolate, ca. 13 mm long and 9 mm thick, green when immature, passing through shades of red to black at maturity, somewhat fleshy.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Shrubs 1-3 m tall; primaries 20-35 cm long, arcuate, not ordinarily thorn-tipped, bearing numerous thorn-tipped secondaries 1.5-10 cm long on which are borne the non-thorn-tipped short-shoots, floriferous (after the first year) twigs and leafy twigs 1-2 cm long; epidermis olive-green to purplish olive, densely caneseent-hispidulous; bark grayish-brown to nearly black; internodes 1-3 (-10) mm long. Leaves alternate or in fascicles of 2-5 at the short shoots; blades obovate, (4-) 7-10 (-15) m mlong, (1.5-) 2.7-4 (-6) mm broad, broadest about a third to two-fifths the length from the apex, apically often acute (minimum angle 800) or sometimes rounded and emarginate, somewhat mucronate, basally shortly cuneate, marginally entire and hispidulous, above dark brownish-olive to fus- cuous-green and microvesiculate and glabrate, beneath somewhat paler and less brown and hispidulous with little obvious venation (under a good lens 3-5 pairs of very faint laterals can be discerned in some leaves); petioles ca. 0.8-1.4 mm lonlg, olive, hispidulous; stipules subulate, ca. 1 mm long, purplish-olive, densely antrorsely hispidulous. Flowers solitary or in axillary fascicles of 2-3; pedicels (0.2-) 0.5-1 (-2) mmn long (on one specimen elongating to 2.8 mm in fruit, but usually shorter than 1 mm even in fruit), densely caneseent-hispidulous; cup cupped, 1.5-2 mm across, purplish-olive, sparingly villous; sepals deltoid, 1-1.5 mm long, purplish-brown to pale olive-green, villous outside; petals absent; stamens alternate with and shorter than the sepals, introrse, the anthers ca. 0.2 mm long; ovary globose-conic, strongly constricted basally, dark purplish, glabrous or sparingly strigose, completely two-celled, each cell with an ovule; style stout, 0.7-0.9 mm long, dark purplish, terminally very slightly enlarged and grooved. Fruit slightly prolate, when mature nad juicy black and ca. 7 mm long and 5 mm thick, when dry prolate, ca. 5-6 mm long, the stone completely two-celled and 1- to 2-seeded.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Shrubs 0.8-2 (-2.5) m tall; wood anatomy described by Molle, 1939; primaries arcuate and somewhat flexuous, 15-30 cm long, bearing nlumerous thorn-tipped secondaries 2-6 (-10) cm long and these in turn bearing numerous leafy and floriferous short shoots and also some leafless thorn-tipped tertiaries 5-12 mm long; epidermis brownish olive or purplish brown, micro- scopically hispidulous or viscid-strigulose or glabrate; bark thin, flaky, gray or brown; internodes 1-3 (-5) mm long. Leaves alternate or usually in fascicles of 2-5 (-7) at the short shoots; blades obovate to elliptic-obovate, (3-) 4-7 (-17) mm long, (1.5-) 2-4 (-7) mm broad, broadest 'about a third to two-fifths the length from the apex, apically rounded to retuse to pointed (minimum angle 750), basally cuneate, marginally entire and slightly or not thickened, subcoriaceous or coriaceous, sordid olive-green to grayish olive, microscopically hispidulous to viscid- strigulose to glabrate, microvesiculate, 30-70 percent of the lower surface taken up by the dark but slightly prominulent to prominent veins including the midvein and (3-) 4-5 (-7) pairs of laterals diverging at angles of 10º- 35º and proceeding nearly straight to the distal margin where they seem to terminate; petioles less than 1 mm long (Escalante, 1946, says leaves sessile), grayish purple to brownish purple, microscopically hispidulous or glabrate; stipules lance-sublate, (0.6-) 1.2-1.5 mm long, firm-subehartaceous, purplish brown, antrorsely strigulose or microvelutinous. Flowers vernal (September through December), in fascicles of (1-) 2-5 at the short shoots; pedicels nearly straight, (2.5-) 5-6 (-8) mm long, stout, yellowish olive, microscopically hispidulous to viscid strigose to glabrate; cup 2.3-2.8 mm across, purplish brown, microscopically hispidulous to viscid strigose to glabrate; sepals elongate-deltoid, (1.2-) 1.5-1.7 (-1.9) mm long, pale olive or yellow-green, outside microhispidulous to viscid strigose to glabrate, often reflexed at anthesis, deciduous; petals absent; stamens alternate with the sepals, strongly inflexed, 1-1.3 mm long; anthers 0.4-0.9 mm long; disk yellowish olive, thin or, opposite the sepals, thickened; ovary globose-conic, dark purple, basally strongly constricted, glabrous, completely 2-celled, each cell with 1 ovule; style stout, ca. 0.9-1.2 mm long, dark purple, vaguely grooved at the distal end; fruit distinctly prolate, 7-9 mm long, 4-5 (-6) mm thick, ripening through shades of red and purple to black, apiculate, with a very thin flesh and a very thick-walled stone which is completely 2-celled and 1-2-seeded; one of the ovules commonly aborts, and when this occurs early in the maturation the fruit appears single-celled on cursory examination.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Frutices aut arbores parvae ramulis tenuibus subtilissime hispidulosis (nonnullis supra aculeis praeditis), internodis 1.5-10 mm longis; folia alterna, elliptica aut obovato-elliptica, (10-) 15-25 (-40) mm longa, (7-) 10-15 (-19) mm lata, prope partem mediam latissima, ad basim cuneata, subcoriacea, coeruleoviridia admodum glabra, marginibus integris aut dentibus paucis introrsis parte in distali instructis; venatione laterali subtus complana, haud conspicua; flores apetali, in fasciculis parvis ca. 4 mm diametro, pedicellis 0.1-0.7 mm longis; ovarium basi constrictum, omnino biloculare; stylus integer; fructus globosi, atri, 4 mm crassi, nucula fere globosa, biloculare, semine plerumque uno.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Shrubs or small trees 2-7 m tall; primaries very slender, 15-50 cm long, slightly arcuate and slightly flexuous, not thorn-tipped, bearing a few very slender thorn-tipped secondaries 2-8 cm long and these in turn bearing short shoots and occasionally a few slender thorns less than 1 cm long and the new floriferous twigs of the season a few cm long; epidermis olive-green to green, very finely hispidulous; bark thin, rather smooth, grayish or brownish; internodes 1.5-4 (-10) mm long. Leaves alternate or in fascicles of 2-4 at the short shoots; blades elliptic, obovate-elliptic, or even commonly ovate-elliptic, (10-) 15-25 (-40) mm long, (7-) 10-15 (-19) mm broad, broadest near the middle, apically rounded or often emarginate (never acute), basally cuneate, marginally with a very narrow slightly pale green thickening and slightly revolute and entire or with a few (3-4) small introrse teeth on each side along the distal half, firm to subcoriaceous, above dull and microvesiculate and dark green to dark olive or brownish olive and glabrous, beneath slightly paler and microvesiculate and glabrous with a prominent usually yellowish green midrib and 4-5 pairs of inconspicuous flush laterals diverging at angles of 45º-65º and arching well within the margin, the most distal pair appearing to close at the mucro; petioles yellowish-green, (1-) 2-3 (-4) mm long, hispidulous laterally in two lines where the base of the blade grades into the petiole; stipules subulate, ca. 1 mm long, purplish brown, antrorsely strigose, at least basally. Flowers solitary or in fascicles of 2-3 at the axils of the season's twigs; pedieels 0.1-0.7 mm long, green or purplish green, essentially glabrous; cup 1.5-2 mm across, green or purplish green, essentially glabrous; sepals deltoid, ca. 1 mm long, green or purplish green, essentially glabrous; petals absent; stamens much shorter than the sepals; anthers 0.25-0.3 mm long; disk purplish or green, rather flat and fleshy; ovary globose, greenish purple, glabrous, strongly constricted basally, completely and equally two-celled, each cell with one ovule; style ca. 0.5 mm long, terminally slightly grooved but not all capitate; fruit when fully mature and juicy black and globose, ca. 4 mm thick, with a rather thick pulp and a small nearly globose or slightly prolate stone, two-celled and usually only 1-seeded.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: A free translation of the description by Castellanos is given here: Dense, much-branched small trees 3-5 m tall, with short trunks ca. 10 cm thick (rarely thicker, usually more slender); old bark rough, logitudinally and transversely irregularly striate, fuscous; younger bark grayish-white; wood whitish, or the heartwood red; secondaries thorn-tipped, 8-10 cm long, and at times bearing tertiary thorns; epidermis of leafy twigs purple. Leaves in fascicles of 3-5 at the short shoots; blades "oblong" (but Castellanos, Fig. 1, shows them spatulate or obovate-spatulate), ca. 17 mm long, ca. 6-7 mm broad or at times larger, when young mucronate, when mature apically obtuse, marginally entire and shiny, above dark green, paler below and with a prominent broad flat midvein and about 4 prominent, broad, flat lateral nerves, the internerves occupied by a very fine reticulum and punctiform cavities; petioles ca. 2 mm long; stipules searious, pilose. Flowers in fascicles of 4 at the short shoots; pedicels 4-5 mm long (to 6 mm long in fruit), yellowish, slightly hairy; sepals triangular, mucronulate, 3 mm long, 2 mm broad, with a midvein and on each side a submarginal lateral vein; stamens ea 2 mm long; ovary slightly conic, ea. 0.5 mm long, topped by a conic trifid [sic?] stigma; drupes solitary or paired at the short shoots, when imma- ture prolate and green, passing through reddish-black to black when mature, globose, ea. 8.5 mm long, with a thick purplish black pulp; stone prolate, up to 6 mm long and 4 mm thick.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Low roulnded shrubs 0.5-1 (-2) mn tall; primaries 10-40 cm long, distinctly arcuate, apparently usually not thorn-tipped; secondaries numerous, 2-7 cm long, all thorn-tipped, straight, bearing numerous short shoots and often some thorn-tipped "tertiaries" 0.3-1 cm long; bark grayish brown to almost black; epidermis grayish-purple, perfectly glabrous; internodes 1-3 (-5) mm long. Leaves alternate or mostly in fascicles of 2-7 at the short shoots; blades entire, spatulate, 4-12 (-14) mm long, 1.6-3 mm broad, broadest ca. a fourth to a third the length from the apex, apically mostly rounded or less commonly amargillate or acute (minimum angle 900), basally acuminate, marginally en- tire alid slightly thickened and often a little revolute when dry, perfectly glabrous, firm, above grayish olive to tawny or brownish grayish olive, perfectly glabrous and often wrinkled when dry, beneath slightly paler and perfectly glabrous and with slightly raised, broad, flattened dark veins which occupy more than 40 percent of the surface including the midvein and 2-4 pairs of laterals which diverge at angles of 15?-30? (-40') and proceed parallel and nearly straight to the distal margin when they appear to terminate; intervein surfaces with some transverse rounded wrinkles; whole undersurface appear- ing as if molded in wax; petioles ca. 1 (-2) mm long, glabrous; stipules subu- late, ca. 1 mm long, purplish-brown, firm, nearly glabrous except with a dense villous fringe marginally. Flowers solitary in the axils or in fascicles of 2-5 at the short shoots, appear- ing in late summer and fall following aequinoctial rains; pedicels slender, (1.5-) 2-3 mm long, elongating to 2-4.2 mm in fruit, purple, glabrous, nearly straight; cup 1-1.5 mm across, dark purple, glabrous; sepals elongate-deltoid, 1-1.5 mm long, purplish, quite glabrous; petals absent; stamens shorter than the sepals, introrse; anthers 0.25-0.35 mm long; disk dark purple, rather fleshy; ovary globose-conic, dark purple, strongly constricted basally, completely two-celled, each cell with one ovule; style stout, 0.5-0.7 mm long, olivaceous to dark purple, slightly capitate terminally; fruit slightly prolate when dry or immature, or nearly globose when mature, black, ca. 3.5-4 mm long, 2.9-3.5 mm thick (big- ger when moist), with a two-celled but usually only 1-seeded stone.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Shrubs, presumably; primaries 15-35 cm long or longer, arcuate, not thorn- tipped, bearing numerous floriferous buds and a few thorn-tipped secondaries 3-6 (-10) cm long which also bear floriferous short-shoots; epidermis pale olive- green, obscured by the close, dense tomentum of short, spreading pale-yellowish- canescent, hairs 0.05-0.2 mm long; bark when 2 years old smooth and grayish brown, glabrous; internodes 4-10 (-14) mm long, rather long for this subgenus. Leaves alternate or in fascicles of 2-4 at short shoots; blades obovate to broadly elliptic, 7-19 mm long, 5-10 mm broad, broadest a third to half the length from the apex, apically rounded or usually acute (minimum angle ca. 900), basally cuneate, marginally entire, firm, membraneous, above olive-brown to dark purplish olive, villous to glabrate, beneath olive-green or grayish olive, villous (densely so along the midvein) with slightly prominent pale midvein and ca. 4-5 pairs of inconspicuous flush laterals diverging at angles of 50?-80? and arching near the margins; petioles 1-2 mm long, densely pubescent as the stem epidermis; stipules deltoid-subulate, ca. 1.5-2 mm long, firm, brownish but obscured by the dense antrorse tomentum of caneseent hairs. Flowers in fascicles of 2-3 at the short shoots or floriferous buds; pedicels much less than 1 mm long, cup ca. 2 mm across, pale purplish olive brown but this obscured by the dense external antrorse tomentum of caneseent hairs; sepals elongate-deltoid, 1-1.2 mm long, also densely villous outside; petals spat- ulate, 0.5-0.8 mm long, thin, membranous, whitish (?), apically emarginate; stamens opposite and nearly as long as the petals, introrse; anthers minute; disk thin and flat, glabrous; ovary globose, densely antrorsely tomentose with caneseent hairs, strongly constricted basally, at a very early stage unequally two-celled, the larger cell with a single ovule, no ovule discernible in the smaller; style ca. 0.6-0.8 mm long, terminally slightly capitate an vaguely grooved at top. Fruit slightly prolate when young, probably when fully mature and juicy nearly globose and at least 10 mm long,, the stone very woody-walled, ca. 8 mm long, prolate, 1-seeded.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Shrubs 0.7-4 m tall; primaries 15-40 em long, arcuate or nearly straight, usually not thorn-tipped, bearing numerous thorn-tipped secondaries 1-7 cm long, these in turn bearing a few short-shoots; bark grayish, often rather distinctly and narrowly fissured; epidermis olive, minutely and sparsely hispidulous or glabrous; internodes 1-2 (-4) mm long. Leaves alternate or occasionally in a fascicle of 2-4 at a short shoot; blades obovate to elliptic-obovate, 5-8 (-18) mm long, 2.3-4 (-10) mm broad, broadest a third to two-fifths the length from the apex, apically rounded and apiculate or truncate and emarginate or usually acute (minimum angle ca. 85?), basally cuneate, marginally entire and very minutely hispidulous at least basally or glabrous, firm, above yellowish green or grayish green and microvesiculate and sparsely and very minutely hispidulous or glabrous, beneath usually slightly more flaveseent or even glaucous and vesicular and sparsely and very minutely hispidulous or glabrous and with inconspicuous concolorous flush or very slightly raised pinnate venation including the midvein and 3-4 pairs of laterals di- verging at angles of 35?-55? and arching rather strongly within the margin, the distal ones closing at the apicule; petioles ca. 1 mm long, purplish green, minutely and sparsely hispidulous or glabrous; stipules subulate, 1-1.3 mm long, brownish, minutely antrorsely pubescent. Flowers solitary or in fascicles of 2-3; pedicels 0.4-1.1 mm long, greenish purple, essentially glabrous; cup 1.5-2 mm across, purplish, glabrous or when young very minutely strigulose; sepals deltoid, ca. 1 mm long; yellowish green glabrous or when young very minutely strigulose outside; petals absent; stamens alternate with and shorter than the sepals, introrse; anthers ca. 0.25 mm long; disk purplish, flat, fleshy; ovary globose, purplish, strongly constricted basally, two-celled, each cell with one ovule; style ca. 0.5 mm long, purplish, indistinctly grooved terminally. Fruit when dry slightly prolate, when mature and juicy black and globose or eveln slightly oblate and 5-6 mm thick with a small prolate 1-(-2) seeded stone.

description: Frutices ramulis (1-) 2-3 mm crassis, breviter hispidulosis, supra aculeis munitis, internodis (0.5-) 1-2 (-3) mm longis; folia fasciculata, spatulata, 3-7 (-10) mm longa, (0.5-) 1-2.6 (-5) mm lata, integra, basi cuneata, ca. 2-3.5- plo longiora quam latiora, utrinque hispidulosa, venatione elevata plus quam 0.3 partem superficiei inferioris occupante; flores fasciculati, apetali, ca. 4 mm diam., pedicellis hispidulous 0.5-1.2 (-2) mm longis; ovarium basi constrictum; stylus integer; fructus prolati atri sucosi, ca. 4.5-5 mm crassi; nucula bilocu- lare, semine uno praedita.

description: Shrubs 0.5-3 m tall; primaries 5-20 (-30) cm long, arcuate, usually eventually thorn-tipped; secondaries 2-7 (-9) cm long, straighter, all thorn-tipped, bearing numerous leafy short-shoots and occasionally a few tertiary thorns ca. 0.5-1 cm long; bark brownish gray to nearly black, furrowed; epidermis purplish-brown, densely short villous or velutinous, internodes (0.5-) 1-2 (-3) mm long. Leaves alternate or usually in fascicles of 2-5 at the short shoots; blades spatulate, 3-7 (-10) mm long, (0.5-) 1-2.6 (-5) mm broad, broadest ca. a third the length from the apex, apically usually acute (minimum angle ca. 85?), basally acuminate, marginally entire and hispidulous, firm, above sordid yellowish or brownish olive or grayish green and hispidulous, beneath dark olive-green or sordid gray-green and hispidulous with somewhat paler raised venation including the midvein and 2-4 pairs of flat-topped or suleate laterals diverging at angles of 20Q-35? nearly parallel and slightly arching and appear- ing to terminate at the distal margins, the venation altogether occupying 30-70 percent of the surface; petioles ca. 0.5 mm long, olive-green, hispidulous; stipules subulate, ca. 1 mm long, dark purple-brown, firm, densely hispidulous espe- cially marginally. Flowers solitary or in fascicles of 2-3 (-6) at the short shoots, appearing in the summer following rain; pedicels 0.5-1.2 (-2) mm long, olive, densely his- pidulous, perhaps elongating a little more after anthesis; cup 1.5-2 mm across, purple, hispidulous outside; sepals deltoid, ca. 1-1.8 mm long, purplish olive, hispidulous; petals absent; stamens shorter than the sepals; anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long; disk-purplish, fleshy, rather thin; ovary globose-conic, purplish-black, glabrous, strongly constricted basally, completely two-celled, each cell with one ovule; style stout, purplish, ca. 0.5-0.7 mm long, capitate terminally. Fruit prolate when immature to nearly globose when mature, black to reddish black, co. 4-6 mm long, 3-4.5 mm thick when dry (bigger when moist), with moderate amount of pulp and a large two-celled and 1- to 2-seeded stone.
bibliographicCitation: Johnston, Marshall C. 1962. Revision of Condalia including Microrhamaus (Rhamnaceae). Brittonia. 14: 332-368.

description: Shrubs 0.5-2 (-3.5) m tall; branches numerous, divaricate; primaries 10- 40 cm long, usually not thorn-tipped, slender, somewhat arcuate; secondaries numerous, 1-7 cm long, slender, often thorn-tipped, bearing numerous short- shoots and sometimes also thorn-tipped "tertiaries" ca. 1 cm long or less; bark thin, grayish-brown; epidermis shortly sericeous-pilose or densely hispidulous; internodes 4-10 mm long. Leaves alternate or mostly in fascicles of 2-7 at the short shoots; blades obovate to elliptic-obovate, (7.5-) 10-25 (-30) mm long, (3.5-) 6-12 mm broad, broadest about a third to two-fifths the length from the apex, apically rounded or slightly acute (minimum angle ca. 900), basally acuminate, mar- ginally entire and hispidulous or silky-villous, firm, above pale olive-green to dark brown and microvesiculate and glabrous or sparsely appressed silky- villous, beneath paler yellowish olive-green to sordid greenish olive and his- pidulous to appressed silkly villous especially densely so near the veins which are darker brown and often slightly prominulent including the midvein and 4-7 pairs of laterals which diverge at angles of 35?-50? and arch to a close near the apex from very near the margin; petioles 1.5-3 (-4) mm long, densely to sparsely hispidulous; stipules subulate, 1-2 (-3) mm long, densely appressed- strigose or villous. Flowers in fascieles of (1-) 2-6 at the short shoots (appearing in March, judging from the Ferreyra collection or in November according to Perkins); pedicels 3-6 mm long, slender, commonly arcuate, olivaceous, hispidulous; cup ca. 1.5-2.5 mm across (in fruit flattened and broader), hispidulous outside, purplish; sepals elongate-deltoid, 1-1.5 mm long, purplish green, hispidulous outside, deciduous; petals absent; stamens about as long as to shorter than the sepals, introrse; anthers 0.5 mm long; disk rather flat; ovary globose-conic, dark purple, slightly hispidulous to glabrous, strongly constricted at the point of attachment, two-celled, each cell with an ovule; style 0.6-1.2 mm long, stout, vaguely 2-lobed at the slightly enlarged tip; fruit prolate, ellipsoid, ca. 7-9 mm long and ca. 5-6 mm thick (bigger when moist), blackish when mature (purplish, say MacBride and Featherstone), with a thin pulp and a thick- walled, two-celled and usually two-seeded stone.

description: Frutex circa 3 m altus ramulis griseis striolatis verrucoso-lenticellatis primum puberulis deinde glabris. Cortice foliaque secretum rubrum gerentes. Folia alterna trifoliolata petiolo 1.5-5 cm longo leviter striolato parce ad- presseque puberulo vel glabro basi subite pulvinato-inerassato; internodio 5-15 mm longo; petioluli crassi pulvinati 2.5-3.5 mm longi glabri. Foliola chartacea flexibilia viridia punctata elliptico-oblonga basi obtusa apice attenuata acumi- nataque margine integerrima albo-calloso-marginata, 4-8 cm longa 1.4-2.5 cm lata terminale quam lateralia major; supra glaberrima nitida nervis reticuloque tenuibus plus minusve conspicuis costa anguste impressa, subtus glabra vel spar- sis minutis pilis adpressis costa elevata, nervis secundariis 9-10 utroque latere tenuibus prominulis arcuato-anastomosatis venulis paulo conspicuis, glandulis copiosis granulato-punctatis. Infloreseentiae paniculatae axillares et terminales ramis elongatis pseudorace-miformibus erectis vel flexuosis, breviter denseque ferrugineo-villosis. Ramusculi patuli tenues ferrugineo-tomentulosi 1-5 mm longi 1-5 flores ferentes. Pedicelli 0.5-2 mm longi. Bracteae bracteolaeque ovato-lanceolatae 0.5-1 mm longae. Sepala 5 oblonga apice angustata obtusiuscula vel subacuta 3.5 mm longa 1-1.3 mm lata extus breviter villoso-tomentulosa margine seariosa. Petala 5 luteseentia crassiuscula obovato-oblonga apice subite attenuata 5.5-6 mm longa 2-2.5 mm lata glanduloso-punctata sparsissimis pilis setosis tenuissimis praedita. Stamina 10 filamentis crassiusculis complanatis glabris vel brevibus pilis papillosis, inaequilongis alteris sterilibus, 3-2.5 mm longis basi in tubum coalitis. Antherae ellipsoideae glabrae dorsifixae, 0.8 mm longae. Ovarium oblongum dense tomen- toso-hirsutum. Fructus ignotus.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1959. Studies in South American plants--V. Brittonia. 11: 163-172.

description: Arbor parva. Rami novelli dense ferrugineo-villosi. Folia 3-foliolata. Foliola glabra, venis secundari is 8-10-jugis juxta marginem anastomosantibus. Inflorescentiae paniculatae, densiflorae, axillares vel pseudoterminales, rhachibus usque 21 cm longis, dense ferrugineo-villosis, sessilifloris. Petala elon- gata anguste-oblonga, calyce duplo longiora, paucipunctata vel epunctata, glabra; filamentis glabris. Folliculus non visus.
bibliographicCitation: Forero, Enrique. 1980. New species and varieties of Connarus (Connaraceae) from Brazil, Venezuela, and adjacent countries. Brittonia. 32: 33-42.

description: Small tree. Branchlets densely villous, ferrugineous. Leaves imparipinnate, trifoliolate, pulvinus 4-7 mm long, petiole up to 10 cm long, glabrous, rachis up to 3 cm long, glabrous. Leaflets (6) 8.5-15 cm long, (2) 3-5 cm wide, narrowly elliptic, chartaceous, glabrous, rounded at the base, acuminate at the apex, entire; petiolule 3-5 mm long, slender; the midrib prominent below, plane or slightly impressed above, lateral veins 8-10 pairs, diverging from midrib at an angle of 600, anastomosing clearly near margin, venation prominulous below. Inflores- cence paniculate, congested, the rachilla slender, up to 21 cm long, densely vil- Ious, ferrugineous, bracts conspicuous; flowers sessile; sepals 3-3.5 mm long, 1.2 mm wide, ovate, conspicuously punctate, tomentose without, glabrous within, acuminate at the apex, barbate, margin ciliate; petals 6-7 mm long, 1.5-1.8 mm wide, narrowly oblong, with 1-4 dots towards the apex or completely epunctate, glabrous; stamens 10, five short 4 mm, five long 5 mm, glabrous, anthers globose, 0.4 mm in diam; ovary densely villous. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Forero, Enrique. 1980. New species and varieties of Connarus (Connaraceae) from Brazil, Venezuela, and adjacent countries. Brittonia. 32: 33-42.

description: Tufted tree 3 m tall. Fruits cauliflorous, green. Sap red.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1957. New species and new records of plants in Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 231-245.

description: Tree 3-5 m tall, unbranched, trunk 2-4 cm in diameter, glabrous but in younger parts lenticellate. Leaves glabrous, 47-92 cm long, the terete petioles 7.5-15.5 cm long, rachis 29-61 cm long, terete; leaflets 10-12-jugate, opposite, subopposite, or subalternate, the petiolules 3-6 mm long, the blades 5-17.5 cm long, 2-4.5 cm wide, lanceolate to oblong-elliptic; base inequilateral, the upper side obtuse, the lower acute; apex caudate-acuminate. Venation plane and prominulous above, conspicuous and salient beneath, about 7 pairs of primary veins. Inflorescences borne on the trunk below the leaves in fascicles of racemes 2-4 cm long, the axes, pedicels, bracts, and bracteoles brown-stellate-pubescent, the bracts and bracteoles minute. Pedicels jointed apically, about 1 mm long. Calyx 5-lobed, united about two-thirds of its length, about 4 mm long, stellate-pubescent outside, glabrous within. Petals five, narrowly elliptic, 5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, punctate, glabrous. Stamens about 3 mm long, glabrous; pistil densely stellate-pubescent, the stigma capitate. Fruit obovate, apiculate, sparingly pubescent, 18-24 mm long, 9-12 mm wide, finely venulose. Seed black with a white aril, about 15 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1957. New species and new records of plants in Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 231-245.

description: Arbor parva vel frutex interdum scandens. Rami glabri. Folia imparipinnata. 3-foliolata. foliolis anguste-ellipticis vel raro ellipticis (5) 7.5-12 ( 15) cm longis, (2) 2.5-4.4 (6) cm latis. glabris vel versus basim costa barbatis. venis secundariis 6-8-jugis. tenuibus. Inflorescentiae racemosae, axillares vel pseudoterminales, rhachibus gracilibus usque ad 10 cm longis dense brunneo-tomentosis. pedicellis gracillibus, 1 mm longis. Sepala 2 mm longa punctis nigris munita; petala calyce duplo vel triplo longiora anguste-oblonga, pauci-punctata. 1-4 punctis nigris apicem versus notata vel raro epunctata.
bibliographicCitation: Forero, Enrique. 1980. New species and varieties of Connarus (Connaraceae) from Brazil, Venezuela, and adjacent countries. Brittonia. 32: 33-42.

description: Shrub, scandent shrub or small tree. Branchlets glabrous, inconspicuously len- ticellate, lenticels small. Leaves imparipinnate, trifoliolate, pulvinus 5 mm long, petiole glabrous, 1.5-9 cm long, rachis 0.5-1.5 cm long, glabrous. Leaflets nar- rowly elliptic or rarely elliptic (5) 7.5-12 (15) cm long, (2) 2.5-4.4 (6) cm wide, chartaceous, glabrous above, glabrous or rarely pubescent at the base of the midrib below, rounded or slightly cordate at the base, acuminate at the apex, entire; petiolule slender, 5 mm long; the midrib prominent below, plane above, lateral veins 6-8 pairs, diverging from midrib at an angle of 700, prominulous below, plane above. Inflorescence racemose, the rachilla 3.5-10 cm long, slender, densely brown-tomentose, bracts conspicuous, small; pedicel 1 mm long. Sepals ovate, 2 mm long, 0.7 mm wide, conspicuously puctate, densely puberulous without, sparsely pubescent within; petals narrow-oblong, 5-5.5 mm long, 1 mm wide, with 1-4 conspicuous black dots near the apex in most petals, some epunctate, glabrous; stamens 10, five long 4.5 mm, five short 3.5 mm, glabrous, anthers globose, 0.4 mm diam; ovary villous. Follicle stipitate, stipe 3-5 mm long, the fruit 1.8 cm long, 1.4 cm wide, long-apiculate, puberulous and with black dots; seed 1 cm long, 0.7 cm wide, arilloid 5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Forero, Enrique. 1980. New species and varieties of Connarus (Connaraceae) from Brazil, Venezuela, and adjacent countries. Brittonia. 32: 33-42.

description: Frutex scandens. Rami cortice albido, verrucoso lenticellato obtecti. Folia 3-foliolata, foliolis oblongo-obovatis 7-20 cm longis 3.5-9 cm latis, rigide coriaceis, glabris, basi angustatis vel subrotundatis, apice breviter acuminatis (acumine 2-3 mm longo), margine revolutis, costa subtus bene prominente, venis secundariis 9-1 1-jugis prope marginem anastomosantibus. Inflorescentiae paniculatae ad 10 cm longae, puberulae; petala elliptica, conspicue punctata, glandulosa; filamenta connata, tubo 5-7 mm longo, proprie parte libera punctata apicem versus glandulosa. Folliculus 2.2 cm longus. 1.4 cm latus. pericarpio extus glabro intus puberulo.
bibliographicCitation: Forero, Enrique. 1980. New species and varieties of Connarus (Connaraceae) from Brazil, Venezuela, and adjacent countries. Brittonia. 32: 33-42.

description: Scandent shrub. Branchlets whitish, conspicuously lenticellate, lenticels large and verrucose. Leaves imparipinnate, trifoliolate, pulvinus thick. 5-8 mm longs petiole lenticellate, glabrous, 1.6-5 cm long, rachis lenticellate, glabrous, 0.4-1.8 cm long. Leaflets oblong-obovate 7-20 cm long, 3.5-9 cm wide, rigid-coriaceous, glabrous, attenuate or rounded at the base, short acuminate at the apex (acumen 2-3 mm long), margin revolute; petiolule thick, 6-8 mm long; the midrib plane or slightly prominulous above, very prominent below, lateral veins 9-11 pairs, prominulous below, plane or slightly prominulous above, diverging from midrib at an angle of 700, anastomosing clearly near margin. Inflorescence paniculate, the rachilla up to 10 cm long, puberulous; pedicels 3 mm long, puberulous. Sepals ovate, 3 mm long, 1.6 mm wide, inconspicuously punctate and puberulous without, conspicuously punctate and glabrous within, the apex obtuse, the margin ciliate; petals elliptic, 4.2 mm long, 1.6-1.7 mm wide, conspicuously punctate, glandulose without, eglandulose within, the margin glandulose; stamens 10, five short 2 mm, five long 2.5 mm, glandulose, anthers globose, 4 mm diam; ovary velutinous, style glandulose. Follicle stipitate, the stipe 2-3 mm long, the fruit 2.2 cm long, 1.4 cm wide, striate, glabrous outside, puberulous inside; seed 1.3 cm long, 0.4 cm wide, arilloid 4 mm long, the margin laciniate.
bibliographicCitation: Forero, Enrique. 1980. New species and varieties of Connarus (Connaraceae) from Brazil, Venezuela, and adjacent countries. Brittonia. 32: 33-42.

description: Leaves trifoliolate. Leaflets oblong, rarely elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, chartaceous, rounded at the base, lateral veins (8) 10-13 pairs, slender, parallel, anastomosing clearly near margin. Inflorescence tomentose, ferrugineous. Young fruit tomentose, ferrugineous, soon glabrate.

description: A subsp. moniliformnis articulis plantarum juvenilium aegre areolatoreticulatis, areolis usque ad 5-7 mm diam., plerumque 1.5-2.4 cm inter se distantibus, margine lateribusque valde spinosis, spinis ut maximum utriusque areolae 10, multo plus longioribus (saepe 1.5-9 cm longis), maturarum areolis vulgo transverse triangularibus vel triangularrotundatis aut minus fre- quenter subrotundatis, pericarpelo semper spinoso basi haud compresso, stigmate stamina longe superante, fructibus sapiuscule spinosis omnino differt.

description: Tall and stout tree-like plant (2.5)3- 4(5.5) m tall branching at the summit, with an umbrella-like top whose edges tend to hang. Trunk distinct, unjointed, arising from the indeterminate shoot of the seedling, cylindrical, sometimes tapering gradually upward in age, (11)14-20(28) cm diam., terete in cross section, the bark exfoliating, rusty-brown, densely armed with spiny areoles. Main branches from the top, elongated, generally spreading at right angles to the trunk, curving inward and drooping, then curving outward again near the apex, rounded or slightly compressed in cross section, brownish. Lateral and ultimate stem segments determinate, those on juvenile plants and sprouts very scantily areolate-reticulate, lusterless, faint green, fairly frequently oblong, (10)18-33(45) cm long, (5)7-10(13) cm wide, 7-12 mm thick, slightly inequilateral, rounded to emarginate at apex, very spiny, those on adult plants similar in size to the juvenile but distinctly areolate-reticulate, obliquely oblong or oblong-ovate, often broader below the middle and with fewer and shorter spines, or spineless, frequently exhibiting a remarkable proliferation of small, globular, long-spined joints that are readily detached and on falling to the ground take root and produce new plants. Areoles on the trunk separated by (1.5)2-3.5(5) cm, rounded to transversely elliptic, 0.8-1.5 cm diam., tuft- ed with yellowish wool, 0.3-1 cm long, the upper part bearing numerous yellow glochids 0.5-1.3 cm long, with (8)12-25(40) white spines verging on gray or blackish with age, these acicular though somewhat twisted and undulated, divergent, the 2-5 centralmost ones usually longest, up to 18- 22 cm long, about 2 mm diam.; areoles on segments of young plants and vigorous shoots (1)1.5-2.4(2.8) cm apart, elliptic to nearly rounded, 3-7 mm long, 2-5 mm wide, bearing (2)4-7(10) very unequal white spines (their bases bright pink while growing) 0.5-10 cm long and above the spines a ridge of prominent, yellow glochids 2-7 mm long; areoles on ultimate segments of adult plants often transversely triangular to triangular-rounded or subrounded, elevated, 2-4 mm diam., those near the edges of the segments commonly bearing 1-5 acicular spines 1-3 cm long and a central fascicle of yellow glochids 2- 6 mm long, those on the sides often spineless. Flowers changing from orange-yellow to reddish, (2)2.2-2.7(3) cm broad when expanded, rather numerous, often 2-3 grouped on adjacent areoles at the edges of the joints near the apex; pericarpel cylin dric, terete or nearly so in cross section, (3 .4)3.7-4.8(5.2) cm long, (1.5)1.7- 2.3(2.5) cm thick, distinctly tuberculated, the tubercules closely set, bearing small, subulate leaves 1-2 mm long and rhombic to subtriangular areoles about 2-3 mm diam. and (3)4-6(8) mm apart, these beset with creamy wool, fascicles of yellow glochids 1-2.5 mm long, and 0-2(4) whitish spines (1)3-9(12) mm long, at 15-45º angles pointing upward; perianth segments 19-25, recurved at tips, commonly arranged in 3 series, the 3 outermost subdeltoid, very fleshy, 4.5-6 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, 2-3 mm thick, distinctly acuminate at apex, the following outer segments reniform to broadly obovate, 5-11 mm long, 6-12 mm wide, abruptly mucronulate-acuminate, very thick at middle, the inner segments obovate, 11-15 mm long, 9-12 mm wide, acuminate and somewhat thinner upwards; stamens erect, 2-6 mm long, filaments capillary, abruptly attenuate at tip, pinkish, anthers linear, very small and slender, often <1 mm long, cream-colored; nectar chamber flattened, 1.5-2.5 mm long, 4-5 mm wide; style long-exserted, excluding the stigma 1.2-1.3 cm long, 1.5-2.5 mm thick, with an obconical swelling 3-4 mm diam. surrounding its base, pink above, including the stigma extended 5-7 mm beyond the anthers; stigma lobes 6, 3-3.5 mm long. Fruits greenish, obovoid or oblong-obovoid to subglobose, not compressed, commonly 5-6 cm long, most of their areoles bearing 1-5 whitish, spreading spines to 2.5 cm long and numerous yellow glochids 2-7 mm long, or sometimes spineless. Seeds flattened, with hairy sides.
bibliographicCitation: Areces-Mallea, Alberto E. 1996. New taxa of Consolea Lemaire (Cactaceae: Opuntioideae) from Cuba. Brittonia. 48: 224-236.

description: A subsp. nashii statura minore (caule rare plus guam 2 m altitudinis), articulis dilute viridibus, areolis 2-4 cm inter se distantibus, saepe 2-3 (1-4) spinis et glochidiis flavescentibus armatis, primariorum florum pericarpelo ad 6 cm long, haud tuberculato, areolis rotundatis non vel vix elevatis et minus sparse obductis, plerumque inermibus, interdum spina solitaria usque ad 1 cm longa tantum munitis, segmentis perianthii apice acutis vel mucronulatis aut breviter acuminatis, stigmate stamina vulgo superante differt.

description: Low to medium-sized erect shrub (0.6)1- 2(5) m tall with diffuse branching and rel- atively large, much-branched crown, often broader than high. Trunk distinct, unjointed, arising from the indeterminate shoot of the seedling, occasionally ramified near the base, (4)5-10(20) cm diam., elliptic to nearly terete in cross section, the bark smooth, grayish, loosely covered with spiny areoles. Main branches elongated, spreading horizontally from and near the top, frequently 1 or 2 arising halfway to the top or even below, then gradually arching upward, more or less flattened, 40-90 cm long or sometimes much longer, grayish. Lateral branches determinate, smooth, lusterless faint green, oblong to narrowly oblong (22)31-45(50) cm long, (7.3)8-10(11) cm wide and 0.9-1.4 cm thick, slightly inequilateral, with sinuate margins and fairly emarginate apex. Ultimate stem segments similar to the lateral branches but smaller, (13)17-32(40) cm long, (6.5)7-8.5(10) cm wide, 6-9 mm thick, often rounded at the tip, the younger ones faintly areolate toward the apex and provided with greenish to red- dish green, early deciduous, subulate leaves 1.5-2.5 mm long. Areoles on the trunk separated by (2)3-4.5(5.5) cm, often rounded, 0.5-1 cm diam., with a tawny to grayish, compact tomentum of minute trichomes about 1 mm long, the upper border bearing a crown of glochids 2-6 mm long, and (2)3-8(12) whitish-gray spines, these straight, slightly twisted and very unequal, the longer (subcentral) one to 9-12 cm long and 2 mm diam., the others usually 1-6 cm long, narrower, arising at wide angles from the areole; areoles on lateral and ultimate branches somewhat elevated, 2-4 cm apart, elliptic to tear-shaped, 2-3.5(4) mm long or rarely rounded, those near the edges of the joints commonly bearing (1)2-3(4) acicular white spines turning ashy-gray with age, bright deep pink at base while growing, (1)1.5-3.5(4.7) cm long, ca. 1 mm diam., those on the sides of the segments unarmed and tufted with a short, grayish tomentum and a compact, central fascicle of very small, yellowish glochids not or scarcely protruding. Flowers changing from yellow to red, (1)1.2-1.9(2.2) cm broad when ex- panded, commonly several on the edges of the ultimate stem segments, very proliferous, often forming clusters of 3-7 secondary flowers and/or small segments after an- thesis; pericarpel of primary flowers clavate to narrowly obovate, nontuberculate, more or less compressed, (3)3.5-5.1(6) cm long, (1.4)1.6-2.1(2.4) cm thick, frequently with small, subulate leaves 1-2 mm long, its not or slightly elevated areoles rounded, 1.5-3 mm diam., (3)5-10(14) mm apart, tufted with tawny tomentum and bearing a short fascicle of yellow glochids, but commonly no spines (occasionally the upper areoles with a single, whitish spine 0.2-1 cm long); perianth segments 16-28, arranged in 3-5 series, the outer ones fleshy, ovate to obovate, 2-10 mm long, 2-8 mm wide, acute or mucronulate at the apex, the inner ones thinner, obovate to narrowly obovate or oblanceolate, 9-12 mm long, 4-9 mm wide, mucronulate to shortly acuminate; stamens erect, 3-9 mm long, the filaments pink-colored, tapering upwards from a moderately thin base to a very fine tip, the anthers linear, cream-colored, about 1 mm long; nectar chamber 2-3 mm long and 3-5 mm wide; style excluding the stigma 1-1.3 cm long, 1-2.5 mm thick, with an obconical swelling 3-4.5 mm diam. surrounding its base; stigma lobes 6-9, 2-3 mm long, often wholly exposed beyond the anthers. Secondary flowers similar to the primary ones but smaller, the pericarpel (2)2.2-3.3(3.6) cm long and more spiny, the areoles bearing (1)2-4(5) acicular spines (2)3-9(12) mm long. Fruits greenish, obovoid, compressed, (4)4.5-6(7) cm long, (1.8)2-3(3.5) cm wide, spineless or bearing one spine at some of the distal areoles, the umbilicus deeply concave, often exhibiting a remarkable proliferation of small spiny segments or secondary flowers, while attached to the plant. Seeds light yellowish, suborbicular,flattened, 3.2-4.5 mm diam., with sharp, cristate edges and few hairs on sides.

description: Frutex; rami teretes obscure brunnei lenticellati; ramuli teretes glandulosi et pilis albidis hirsuti; folia petiolo 1 mm longo vel subnullo, anguste oblonga vel linearia, 1.2-2.8 cm longa, 3-8 mm lata, basi acuta, obtusa vel rotundata, apice rotundata, nervo, medio et nervis lateralibus supra impressis, subtus prominulis, non reticulatis, supra setulis brevissimis basi incrassatis scabrida obscure viridia opaca, subtus setulis brevibus et dense glandulis parvis obsita, margine plana brevissime crenata, chartacea; inflorescentiae glomeratae 4-6-florae, pedunculis 3-7 mm longis, glandulosis et hirsutis; calyx 1.7-2 mm longus hirsutus et glandulosus, tubo campanulato 1.5-1.7 mm longo, lobis triangularibus 1-1.3 mm longis, exappendiculatis,  acuminatis; corolla 5 mm longa, extus apice glandulosa, lobis rotundatis ca. 1 mm longis et latis; stamina 5 aequilonga, 3 mm supra basin corollae abeuntia; filamenta quoad libera 1 mm longa; antherae ellipticae 0.6 mm longae; stylus 2 mm longus 4-fidus; ovarium subglobosum; fructus ovoideus, 4 mm longus, 2 mm latus, laevis.
bibliographicCitation: Liogier, Alain H. 1968. Novitates Antillanae. III. Brittonia. 20: 148-161.

description: Fruit ovoid, 9 mm diam., 26 mm long, with pericarp 1.6 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-resembling Chambeyronia, except that the vascular bundles are nearly terete, with very slender strands of vascular tissue surrounded by very thick sheaths, and occupying the inner half of the pericarp, lacking the larger sclereids below the mantle and lacking the sclerified parenchyma in the inner pericarp; further characterized by rather large raphide-bearing cells and a thin series of tanniniferous cells between the vascular bundles and the moderately thick locular epidermis.
bibliographicCitation: Essig, Frederick B. & Hernandez, N. 2002. A systematic histological study of palm fruits. V. Subtribe Archontophoenicinae (Arecaceae). Brittonia. 54: 65-71.

description: Plants 1.5-6.5 dm high, branching at or above the base, the foliage scaberulous; basal leaves ovate-lanceolate, 2-7 cm long, 1-4 cm broad, the divisions 1-4 mm long, acuminate, the petioles slender, 3-10 cm long, the lower 1/5 to 1/3 dilated and sheathing, the sheaths scarious-margined, the cauline leaves few, gradually reduced upward; inflorescence few branched, the peduncles 2-20 cm long, densely scabrous at apex; involucre inconspicuous, of 1 or several scarious-sheathing bracts 0.2-1 cm long, or lacking; rays 5-30 cm long; involucel of 3-6 entire bractlets 2-6 mm long, about equaling the pedicels; pedicels 2-6 mm long; petals ca 1 mm long; stamens ca 1.2 mm long, the anthers oval, ca 0.3 mm long; styles 1-1.3 mm long; fruit rounded at apex and base, 4-5 mm long, 2-4 mm broad, all the ribs acutely winged.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1967. Some Umbelliferae of the Andean Paramos of South America. Brittonia. 19: 212-226.

description: Tall, hemi-epiphytic tree. Leafy twigs ca 10 mm thick, white-appressed-puberulous, partly also brownish-hirsute, lenticels conspicuous. Lamina coriaceous, oblong to subobovate, 18-26 x 9-15 cm, apex short-acuminate to obtuse, base obtuse, margin entire; upper surface glabrous, lower surface sparsely appressed- puberulous; lateral veins 6-9 pairs, basal pair unbranched (or very faintly branched) reaching the margin at or just below the middle of the lamina, usually the second and/or third lateral veins (from the base) with one or two strong branches, tertiary venation distinct, slightly prominent; petiole 5-10 cm long, appressed-puberulous; stipules 1.5-2 cm long, yellowish- to brown-(sub)hirsute. Pistillate inflorescences branched; heads 10-20, sometimes partly fused, (sub)globose, 3-5 cm in diam; common peduncle 3-6 cm long, ca 2 mm thick, appressed-puberulous and partly also brownish-hirtellous; perianth ca 2 mm high, glabrous, ? distinctly ribbed. Interfloral bracts subulate to narrowly spathulate, with a few hairs at the apex.
bibliographicCitation: Berg, Cornelius C. 1990. New species of Coussapoa and Pourouma (Cecropiaceae). Brittonia. 42: 59-65.

description: Tree 18 m tall. Leafy twigs 5-12 mm thick, yellowish- to whitish-hirtellous. Lamina coriaceous, ovate to elliptic, 10-21 x 8-16 cm, apex short-acuminate (to acute), base rounded to subcordate, margin coarsely crenate to subentire; upper surface with sparse hairs on the midrib, lower surface hirtellous on the veins, in the reticulum minutely puberulous; lateral veins (10-) 12-14 pairs, basal pair branched, reaching the margin below the middle of the lamina, tertiary and quar- ternary venation and reticulum prominent; petiole 4-6 cm long, 2-4 mm thick, hirtellous, hairs not distinctly different in length; stipules 4-12 cm long, densely yellowish-puberulous and partly also hirsute. Pistillate inflorescences branched  heads 4 or 5, globose (to subdiscoid), in fruit 0.7-1.3 (1.5) mm in diam.; common peduncle 2.5-3 cm long, ca 2-2.5 mm thick, hirtellous; perianth ca 1.5 mm high, at the apex puberulous, in fruit red. Interfloral bracts absent.

description: Tree, hemi-epiphytic. Leafy twigs 5-10 mm thick, brown-strigose, at least at the scars of the stipules, glabrescent. Lamina coriaceous, elliptic, 15-17 x 1 1-14 cm, apex rounded to short-acuminate, base rounded to subcordate, margin sub- entire, at the base revolute; upper surface glabrous, lower surface strigillose at the base of the midrib, on the midrib and lateral veins with a soon disappearing white- arachnoid indument; lateral veins 8-10 pairs, basal pair +/- branched, reaching the margin at or just below the middle of the lamina, tertiary venation almost plane; petiole 5-6.5 cm long, glabrous or brownish-strigose; stipules 2-3 cm long, rather densely whitish-appressed-puberulous to -strigillose, or also with white- arachnoid hairs. Pistillate inflorescences branched; heads 3-9, 3-4 (in fruit 7-9) mm in diam; common peduncle 2-4 cm long, densely minutely puberulous; perianth ca 1.5 mm high, minutely puberulous around the aperture. Interfloral bracts absent.

description: Saxicolous herbs, erect, hairy, with fibrous roots. Stem thin, erect, terete, ca. 15 cm long, reddish violet, with short erect soft hairs; nectaries present at nodes; unbranched except possibly from base; adventitious roots lacking. Leaves opposite, petiolate, equal to unequal in a pair; lamina ovate-elliptic, 5-11 X 2.5-5 cm; apex acute to obscurely acuminate; base round to cordate and often unequal; margin serrulate to biserrulate; main veins 6-9 pairs; foliar nectaries lacking; adaxial surface with scattered hairs and slightly raised veins; abaxial surface with denser scattered hairs on slightly raised, much paler veins; petiole 1.5-7 cm long, clasping at base, with short dense erect soft hairs. Inflorescences axillary, sometimes adnate to base of petiole, raceme-like cymes with few flowers; peduncle ca. 7 cm long, with small narrow-triangular bracts 2-3 mm long; pedicels 1-1.5 cm long, with ovate bracteoles up to 5 mm long. Sepals free to base, narrowly elliptic, 7-8 X 2-2.2 mm, with 3 parallel veins; pilose on distal half; apex glandular; dorsal sepal narrower and reflexed under corolla spur. Corolla pale purple, salverform, dorsally spurred, nearly transverse in calyx, pilose inside; spur curved toward pedicel, rounded, 5 X 3-3.5 mm, hairy inside; tube slightly "S"-shaped, 15-18 mm long, 2.5 mm wide above base, ca. 8.5 mm wide at throat; lobes subequal, suborbicular, ca. 7-8 mm long; staminal filaments inserted on lower third of corolla tube, the 2 ventral connate at base; anthers coherent in a tetrad, in a pair apically, between the pairs laterally, oblong, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; staminode dorsal, minute, lacking anther; nectary ring reduced to a dorsal gland 0.5-0.6 mm tall; ovary superior, conical and grooved when dry, 2-2.2 mm long, 1 mm wide at base, shortly pilose; style 4-4.3 mm long, curved at apex toward ventral lobe of corolla, glabrous; stigma capitate, 1 X 0.7-0.8 mm, tomentose. Capsule surrounded by sepals, the valves 5-6 X 2-2.5 mm; seeds brown, elliptic, 0.5 mm long, striate longitudinally, the funicle short and wide.

description: Herbs, either terrestrial, or epiphytic in the moss layer on tree trunks; stems some- what stoloniferous with upright branches, the upright branches to 20 cm tall, most usually less than 10 cm, slender, 1-2 mm in diameter, green, villous to sericeous. Leaves subequal in a pair; blades ovate or elliptic, 1.2-2.8 cm long, 0.6-1.4 cm wide, membranous, the apex acute, the base acute to cuneate, the margins serrate, above dark bluish-green with midveins rarely silvery, bullate, furrowed along the impressed veins, long-pilose between the veins, below lighter green, appressed-pilose along the prominent veins; petioles 2-9 mm long, pilose. Inflorescences from the upper axils but appearing terminal, exceeding the leaves, shortly cymose-racemose, of 4-7 flow- ers; peduncles slender, erect, 1.5-2.3 cm long, ca 1 mm in diameter, green, long-pilose; pedicels 1-4 mm long, green, densely pilose. Flowers small; calyx tube obconic to turbinate, ca 2 mm long and wide, green, pilose to sericeous, 10-costate, the lobes ovate-triangular, 1 mm long and wide, green outside, pilose, inside glabrous; corollas white with purple spots or pink in the throat on the lower side, the tube funnel-form, 0.7-1.2 cm long, ca 1.5 mm in diameter at the base, ampliate above, to ca 3 mm in diameter at the throat, outside pilose to villous, inside glandular-pubescent, the limb bilabiate, the lobes obovate, the upper lobes 3 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, the lateral and basal lobes 4 mm long, 2 mm wide, the margins crenulate; filaments adnate to the corolla tube for ca 8 mm above the base, curved, reddish, glabrous; anthers broader than long, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.75 mm wide, coherent; disc annular, 1 mm high, shallowly lobed, reddish; ovary ovoid, 2 mm long, glabrous; style 1 cm long, gla- brous, the stigma stomatomorphic. Mature fruit and seeds not seen.

description: Understory trees in lowland terra firme forest, reproductive height 8-24 m; branchlets robust, (5) 6-8 mm diam at 2 cm from apex, with dense erect hairs 0.5-1 mm long (hairs at apex suberect); leaves (30) 41-56 cm long; petiole (8) 10.5-19 cm x 2.6-3.6 mm, with dense suberect to erect hairs 0.5-1 mm; juga 3- 5 (6), interjuga 4-6 cm long; lateral leaflets subsessile (Fig. 1A), terminal petiolule (2.3) 4-5.2 cm long; mature leaflets coriaceous, slightly rugose above, somewhat scabrous, laterals subsessile, elliptic to broadly so, the basal pair sometimes ovate, terminal leaflet broadly elliptic to sometimes obovate, basal pair (6) 10-11.5 x (2.8) 4.3-6.8 cm, ultimate pair 11-22 x 5-8.2 cm, terminal 14-25 x 6.6-8.8 cm, leaflet bases subequal, truncate to shallowly cordate (Fig. 1 C), apices cuspidate to acuminate, acumen serrulate (Fig. 1 B), margins serrulate, the teeth acute to obtuse, ascending, 0.8-1.2 mm long, (3) 5-8 (10) mm apart, midvein and secondary veins on the abaxial leaf surface prominent, with dense erect hairs (0.2) 0.35-0.5 mm long, higher order veins prominulous, these and the blade with sparse hairs (0.25) 0.4-0.7 mm long (on immature leaflets the hairs often so dense as to obscure the leaflet surface), also provided with snail-shaped glands (dense on immature leaf- lets); adaxial surface with midvein obtusely prominent, higher order veins pro- minulous but depressed in a groove, hairs on midvein and secondary veins dense to somewhat sparse, erect or spreading, (0.2) 0.4-0.7 (0.8) mm long, blade with sparse erect hairs 0.2-0.5 (0.7) mm long, denser and longer on the higher order veins than elsewhere; inflorescence (Fig. 1D) (11) 21-32 cm long, axis of panicle (1.3) 1.6-2.2 mm diam at the base, axes terete, 0.9-1.1 times length of subtending leaves, racemes (0.4) 2-5.4 (9.3) cm long, these not strongly branched; inflores- cence axes densely pubescent with erect hairs (0.3) 0.5-1 mm long, also provided with sparse snail-shaped glands; bracts subtending the racemes lanceolate to ovate (rarely foliose or trifoliate), 1-5 mm long, involute, coriaceous to somewhat fleshy, apex acute to obtuse, fugaceous rarely persistent; bracts on racemes chartaceous, narrowly lanceolate to broadly ovate, involute, apex acute to pungent, persistent or fugaceous; bracts densely pubescent adaxially and on the margin, hairs (0.15) 0.2-0.5 (0.7) mm long; pedicels clavate, sulcate when dry, short, (0.1) 0.3-0.6 (0.8) x 0.35-0.4 mm, with dense hairs 0.3-1.0 mm long; flowers at anthesis 2.6- 3 mm long, calyx 1.25-1.5 x 1.1-1.3 mm diam, calyx tube 0.25-0.5 mm long, lobes 0.8-1.0 mm long, about 2-4 times length of tube, lobes triangular to de- pressed-deltate, acute, pubescence on the pedicel and calyx sparse to somewhat dense, hairs erect, (0.2) 0.3-0.5 (0.7) mm long; petals (Fig. 1F, H) green and fleshy, narrowly elliptic, slightly asymmetrical, involute, slightly carinate, at anthesis erect or slightly inflexed or reflexed only toward the acute to obtuse apex, apiculum strongly incrassate, base broadly cuneate, abaxially with sparse to scattered erect to ascending hairs 0.35-1.0 mm long, near the apex <0.2-0.4 mm long, sometimes occurring only along the keel; stamens 10, filaments fleshy and papillate, moderately to broadly compressed-obclavate; staminateflowers (Fig. 1F, G): stamens exceeding the pistillode, 1.15-1.3 mm and 0.95-1.15 mm long, filaments 0.75- 0.8 mm and 0.8-0.85 mm long, anthers 0.2-0.25 mm and 0.35-0.45 mm long, disk annular,0.2-0.35 mm high x 0.25-0.3 mm wide; pistillode 0.8-0.9 mm long overall, reduced, glabrous, weakly 5-lobed, surrounded by the annular disk, ovary ovoid, 5-locular with reduced ovules, gradually contracted into a short thick stylode 0.35-0.4 mm long, stigmas not differentiated, rather the apex narrowly vertically 5-canaliculate; pistillateflowers (Fig. 1H-J): antepetalous staminodes 0.85 mm long, only antesepalous staminodes reaching the style, 0.95-1 mm long, antepetalous filaments 0.25-0.35 mm long, antesepalous filaments 0.4-0.45 mm long; all anthers 0.5-0.6 mm long; disk shallow and narrow, 0.1-0.2 x 0.1- 0.15 mm, negligibly undulate; pistil 1.45-1.5 mm long overall, ovary narrowly ovoid, 5-locular, gradually contracted into a short thick style 0.5 5-0.65 mm long, stigmas lateral, fleshy and globose, 0.2 mm high, hairs on the ovary dense, ascending, 0.2-0.45 mm long, style and stigmas glabrous; fruit (Fig. 1K) when mature red, 17-21 x 9-13 mm when dry (18-26 mm wide if 2 locules develop), drying smooth, apex of fruit obtuse to acute, a suture opposite the venter evident on monopy- renous fruits, hairs on the fruit dense but not obscuring the surface, erect, (0.3) 0.4-1 mm long; pyrenes cartilaginous, 1.5-1.6 x 0.8-0.9 mm, dorsally compla- nate, in plan narrowly ovate with acute apex, in lateral view asymmetrically obtuse-oblong, 2 lateral depressions forming a ridge at apex; embryo J-shaped (subhippocrepiform; Fig. 1L), only the apex of the cotyledons transversely re- curved, the inner cotyledon replicate the distal 1/4-1/3 its length, the outer replicate the distal 1/6-1/4 its length, partially overlapping the inner.
