description: Low, herbaceous perennial 2-16 cm tall, acaulescent to short-caulescent, not markedly aromatic unless crushed, with a straight to curved primary root 10-20 cm long or more, 3-8 mm in diam at the summit, the crown simple or with a few branches arising 1-6 cm below ground, the crown and branches enveloped by persistent, papery or somewhat fibrous leaf sheaths which often double the apparent diam; leaves petiolate, herbaceous, (1.5) 3-15 cm long, 0.5-1.5 (2.5) cm broad, mostly pinnate-pinnatifid to bipinnate, somewhat glaucous, glabrous ex- cept margins often minutely granular-roughened; petiole flat to U-shaped in cross section, (0.5) 1-6 cm long, often with a scarious margin 0.1-0.2 mm wide, gradually expanded below into an often prominent sheath; blade lanceolate to oblong or oblanceolate in outline, (1) 2-5 (6) cm long; lobes linear-lanceolate to elliptic or sometimes ovate; leaflets in 1-3 (5), opposite or subopposite pairs, the terminal leaflet deeply pinnatifid, usually confluent with the upper pair or pairs, the lower distinct, remote, the apices apiculate. Inflorescence of subcompact, compound umbels 3-15 mm in diam; peduncle terminal or axillary, ascending to erect, (2) 4-12 (15) cm long, shorter than to much exceeding the leaves, glabrous; involucre none; rays (3) 6-8, 1-3 (5) mm long, subterete to flattened, erect to spreading, often scariously winged, glabrous; umbellets andromonoecious, of 1-8 staminate and 1-4 (sometimes more) perfect flowers on pedicels 1-2.3 and 0.1-1 mm long, respectively, or wholly staminate; involucels dimidiate, the bractlets 3-7, linear to lanceolate or sometimes ovate, with scaberulose margins in at least the upper half, 1-3.2 (4) mm long and about equalling the flowers, distinct or connate for up to % (2/3) of length, white-margined. Flowers yellow; sepals broadly rounded to triangular, 0.1-0.4 mm long or obsolete, not enlarging in fruit; petals 1.5-1.8 mm long, obovate to obcordate below with a triangular, inflexed, plicate apex less than half the length; anthers yellow, 0.4-0.5 mm long; filaments 1.5-2 (2.8) mm long; styles filiform, terete, 1.5-2.2 mm long, spreading to recurved, not elongating in fruit; stylopodium none; disc present; ovary minutely granular-roughened, somewhat compressed laterally; carpophore bipartite, persistent. Fruit subterete to somewhat flattened laterally, broadly elliptic to suborbicular, not constricted at commissure, 3.5-4.8 mm long, 2.2-3 mm broad, minutely granular-roughened, dull, reddish-brown with light brown to whitish wings, the dorsal and intermediate wings 0.3-0.8 mm broad, the lateral wings 0.5-1.1 mm broad; oil tubes narrow, flat, reddish-brown, 5-9 in the intervals, 8-10 on the flat to somewhat curved commissural face; seed face involute. Chromosome number unknown.

description: Plantae humiles perennes acaulescentes ramis paucis vel pluribus e caudice fibroso; folia petiolata subcoriacea oblonga glabra vel scaberula 1-2-pinnata, divisionibus lanceolatis; inflorescentia ex umbellis compositis subcompactis constans pedunculis quam foliis longioribus; involucrum deficiens; radii pauci complanati; umbellulae andromonoeciae ex floribus staminatis pedicellatis pluribus et floribus perfectis subsessilibus 1-paucis constantes; involucellum dimidiatum bracteolis lineari-lanceolatis vel obovatis basin versus connatis; flores flavi, sepalis prominentibus ovatis vel lanceolatis, petalis obovatis, stylis filiformibus; stylopodium nullum, disco praesenti; carpophorum bipartitum persistens; fructus subteres late ovoideus, costis prominentibus suberosis, eis dorsalibus intermediisque humilibus rotundatis, eis lateralibus anguste alatis; vittae parvae in intervallis 3-5 in commissura 6-10; semen dorsaliter leviter compressum superficie plana.

description: Low, tufted, herbaceous perennial 4-15 cm tall, acaulescent or essentially so, not markedly aromatic unless crushed, with a straight to curved primary root 6-20 cm long, 2-6 mm in diam at the summit, the crown mostly with few to several branches arising 1-3 cm below ground, the branches enveloped above by marcescent, papery leaf sheaths (occasionally a few petioles as well) which often double the apparent diam; leaves petiolate, subcoriaceous, oblong in outline, 2-5 cm long, 0.4-1.5 cm wide, once-pinnate with leaflets entire or few to many unequally bilobed to pinnately 3-5 (7) lobed, or twice-pinnate (especially below), green to grayish-green, glabrous or minutely scaberulous on margins; petiole subterete in cross section (when fresh), glabrous, 0.5-3 cm long, expanded at base into a relatively broad, scarious sheath; blade (0.8) 1.5-2 (4) cm long; lobes or leaflets narrowly to broadly elliptic or sometimes lanceolate; leaflets in 3-5 opposite, distinct pairs, not decurrent on the rachis or petiole, the apices mostly mucronulate. Inflorescence of subcompact, compound umbels 3-8 mm in diam; peduncle terminal, erect or nearly so, 4-13 cm long, exceeding the leaves, glabrous; involucre wanting; rays 3-6, 2-5 mm long, flattened, spreading, sometimes scariously winged; umbellets andromonoecious, of several pedicellate staminate and 1-5 (or more) subsessile perfect flowers; involucels dimidiate, the bractlets 5-12, linear-lanceolate to obovate, entire and acute or few-toothed apically, 1.5-3 mm long and about equalling the flowers, connate for up to 1/3 of their length, sometimes thinly white-margined; pedicels 0.5-1.5 mm long. Flowers yellow (fading to pale yellow or white); sepals ovate to lanceolate, 0.4-0.7 mm long, subequal, not enlarging in fruit; petals 1.6-2 mm long, obovate below with a narrow, inflexed, plicate apex of nearly equal length; anthers yellow, 0.5-0.6 mm long; filaments 0.9-1.1 mm long; styles filiform, terete, 1-1.5 mm long, spreading, not elongating in fruit; stylopodium none; disc present; ovary glabrous; carpophore present, bipartite, persistent. Fruit subterete, broadly ovoid, not constricted at commissure, 3-4 mm long, (1.7) 2-2.5 (3) mm broad, glabrous, dull to somewhat lustrous, light brown, the dorsal rib and pair of intermediate ribs low and rounded but prominent, corky, unwinged, the lateral pair narrowly winged, about as broad as the intervals; oil tubes small, flattened, reddish-brown, 3-5 in the intervals, 6-10 on the concave commissural face; seeds slightly compressed dorsally in cross section, the face plane. Chromosome number, n = 11 (Henderson et al., 1980, as Cymopterus nivalis S. Watson).

description: Plantae humiles perennes acaulescentes, caudicis ramis paucis vel multis petiolis obtectis; folia petiolata herbacea oblonga vel lanceolata hispidula vel scaberula pinnato-pinnatifida vel 2-pinnata vel infra medium 3-pinnata, divisionibus ellipticis vel oblanceolatis vel obovatis; inflorescentia ex umbellis compositis subcompactis constans pedunculis quam foliis brevioribus vel multo longioribus; involucrum deficiens; radii pauci subteretes vel complanati; umbellulae andromonoeciae e floribus staminatis 3-pluribus et floribus perfectis 2-pluribus constantes; involucellum dimidiatum, bracteolis lanceolatis vel ellipticis, basin versus connatis; flores albi vel cremei, sepalis triangularibus vel lanceolatis, petalis obovatis, antheris flavis vel purpureis, stylis filiformibus, ovario puberulo; stylopodium nullum, disco praesenti; carpophorum nullum; fructus subteres vel dorsaliter complanatus late ellipticus vel suborbiculatus muricatulus, costis crassis; vittae parvae, in intervallis 4-6 in commissura 6- 9; seminum superficies plana vel concava.

description: Low, tufted, herbaceous perennial 1-19 cm tall, acaulescent, strongly aromatic when crushed with an odor of orange peels, with a primary root 5-50 cm long or more, 0.3-1.5 cm in diameter at the summit, the crown with few to many branches arising 1-9 cm below ground, the branches enveloped throughout or nearly so by persistent leaf petioles or their frayed remnants that increase the true diameter 2-4 times; leaves petiolate, herbaceous, (1) 1.5-13 cm long, (0.2) 0.5-1.6 cm broad, pinnate-pinnatifid to bipinnate or in part bipinnate-pinnatifid to tripinnate below, light green to gray-green, moderately to densely covered throughout with perpendicular trichomes 0.02-0.1 mm long, these conical to clavate, possibly somewhat glandular, or scaberulous to rarely glabrous; petiole half-terete with narrowly winged to ribbed angles or deeply grooved adaxially, (0.5) 1.5-7 cm long, expanded at base into a scarious sheath; blade narrowly oblong to lanceolate in outline, (0.7) 1.5-6 cm long; primary leaf divisions in (4) 5-7 opposite pairs, the terminal one deeply pinnatifid, often confluent with the upper pair, the lower distinct, relatively equally spaced except the lowest usually remote, the lateral primary divisions asymmetrically pinnatifid, pinnate to bipinnate (below) into 3- 13 (17) narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate or obovate lobes or leaflets, the apices blunt to apiculate. Inflorescence a subcompact compound umbel 6-18 mm in diameter; peduncle terminal, ascending to erect, or arcuate-spreading in fruit, (1.5) 3-19 cm long, shorter than to much-exceeding the leaves, pubescent like the leaves or sometimes glabrous; involucre none; rays 3-8, 0.3-3.5 mm long, or to 15 mm long in fruit, terete to somewhat flattened, unequal, spreading; umbellets mostly andromonoecious, of 3-7 staminate and (2) 6-1 1 (or more) perfect flowers; involucels dimidiate, the bractlets 4-9, linear to lanceolate or elliptic, entire to erose, acute, 1.5-4.5 mm long and about equalling the flowers, connate for up to 1/3 of their length, distinctly white- or purple-margined, pubescent like the leaves or glabrous; pedicels 1-5 mm long, or to 8 mm long in fruit. Flowers white or cream; sepals narrowly triangular to lanceolate, 0.5-0.9 mm long, subequal, not enlarging in fruit, white- or purple-margined; petals 1.5-1.7 mm long, obovate in lower 24 with a narrow, inflexed, plicate apex; anthers greenish-yellow to yellow or purple, 0.4-0.6 mm long; filaments 1.7-2 mm long; styles filiform, terete, 1.4- 1.8 mm long, or to 2.5 mm long in fruit, arcuate-spreading; stylopodium none; disc present; ovary puberulent; carpophore none. Fruit terete to somewhat flat- tened dorsally, broadly elliptic to suborbicular, not constricted at commissure, (2) 3.5-5.2 (5.8) mm long, (1.8) 2.3-3.5 (4) mm broad, moderately to densely covered with irregular tubercles or crests, each with 1 to few conical to cylindrical processes, dull, reddish-brown to purplish with tan to whitish ribs; dorsal and intermediate ribs 0.2-0.5 mm broad, 0.2-0.5 mm thick, rounded, usually broadly so; lateral ribs or wings 0.5-0.8 mm broad, 0.4-0.6 mm thick, rounded; oil tubes flat, reddish-brown, (3) 4-5 (6) in the intervals, 6-9 on the flat to deeply concave (especially when only 1 mericarp matures) commissural face; seed face flat to concave. Chromosome number unknown.

description: Low, tufted, herbaceous perennial 5-15 cm tall, acaulescent, not markedly aromatic unless crushed, with a usually straight primary root 8-20 cm long, 3-8 mm in diam at the summit, the crown mostly with few to several branches arising 2-6 (8) cm below ground, the branches enveloped throughout by marcescent, mostly frayed leaf petioles which double the apparent diameter; leaves petiolate, subcoriaceous, ovate to lanceolate in outline, 1.5-9 (11) cm long, 0.4-1.8 cm broad, deeply pinnatifid to once-pinnate, bluish- or grayish-green, glabrous except for the scaberulous margins and sometimes veins, or occasionally scaberulous over the abaxial surface; petiole flat to planoconvex in cross section with a scarious wing ca 0.1 mm wide, 0.5-7.5 cm long, gradually expanded below into the narrow sheath; blade (1) 1.5-2.5 (3.5) cm long; lobes or leaflets linear-lanceolate to oblong; leaflets in 3 to 5 opposite or subopposite pairs, the upper pairs confluent, the lower distinct, remote, and decurrent on the rachis or petiole, the apices apiculate. Inflorescence of subcompact, compound umbels 3-10 mm in diam; peduncle terminal, erect or nearly so, (3) 5-10 (15) cm long, usually much exceeding the leaves, glabrous; involucre usually wanting, if present then of 1-3 linear to lan- ceolate bracts; rays 2-6, 1-5 mm long, subterete to flattened, spreading, sometimes scariously winged; umbellets andromonoecious, of several pedicellate staminate and 1-5 (or more) subsessile perfect flowers; involucels dimidiate, the bractlets 5-12, ovate to lanceolate, mostly entire, 0.5-5 mm long and about equalling the flowers, connate for 1/4-/4 Of their length, white-margined; pedicels 1-2 mm long. Flowers yellow; sepals ovate to lanceolate, 0.2-0.6 mm long, not enlarging in fruit; petals 1.6-2 mm long, oblong to ovate below with a narrow, inflexed, plicate apex of nearly equal length; anthers yellow, 0.4-0.6 mm long; filaments 1-1.5 mm long; styles filiform, terete, 1-1.5 mm long, ascending to divergent, not elongating in fruit; stylopodium none; disc present; ovary glabrous; carpophore none. Fruit subterete, broadly elliptic to oblong, not constricted at commissure, (2.6) 3-4.1 mm long, 1.6-2.2 mm broad, glabrous, lustrous, light brown, the dorsal rib and pair of intermediate ribs low and rounded but prominent, corky, unwinged, the lateral ribs sharp-edged to narrowly winged; oil tubes broad, flat, reddish-brown, solitary in the intervals, 2 on the concave commissural face; seeds slightly compressed dorsally in cross section, the face plane to sulcate. Chromo- some number, n = 11.

description: Vine, the young stems with unifarious pubescence, mature stems glabrous; leaves petiolate, the petiole 0.3-0.5 cm long, the blades membranous, lanceolate, acute or subacute at apex, acute at base, 3.5-5.5 cm long, 1-1.5 cm wide, glabrous except shortly pilose along the upper midnerve, the secondary nerves 4-5 each side; inflorescence subaxillary, umbelliform, 2-3-flowered, the peduncle absent or up to 0.8 mm long, pubescent, the pedicels 2-3 mm long, pilose; sepals narrowly ovate, 0.7-0.75 mm long, 0.35-0.4 mm wide, with a small gland in each sinus; corolla shortly campanulate, 6 mm diam., the petals oblong, obtuse, 2.7-2.8 mm long, 0.7-0.8 mm wide at the base, glabrous without, papillose within; gynostegium sessile, 0.8 mm long; anthers 0.5 mm long, 0.37-0.4 mm wide; corona segments 5, narrowly lanceolate, acuminate, 1.5 mm long, 0.3 mm wide at the base, longer than the gynostegium; pollinia narrowly pyriform, 0.12 mm long; corpusculum linear, 0.12 mm long; fruits unknown.

description: Lianas; young stems more or less terete, glabrous, oldest parts ridged or thickened and sulcate, nodes with 2 small lateral nectaries, leaf axils without nectaries. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.9-4.5 cm long, glabrous or nearly so; blades glabrous, narrowly elliptic to narrowly or broadly lanceolate, 4.8-24 X 1.9-7.8 cm, secondary veins 7-9 pairs, base cuneate with 2 adaxial nectaries, apex acuminate. Inflorescences racemes of cymes, or rarely pseudopanicles, lateral, subaxillary, (3- )7-30-flowered; peduncle 0.9-2.5 cm long, scarcely appressed-puberulent, rachis 0.7-4.5 cm long, appressed-puberulent, bracts narrowly ovate, 0.5-0.6 mm long, pedicels 4-6 mm long, minutely appressed-puberulent. Flowers small; calyx lobes narrowly ovate 1 X 0.5-0.6 mm, margins ciliate, base without adaxial glands; corolla yellow or cream, lobes reflexed, narrowly ovate, 1.5-1.6(-2) X 1- 1.1(-1.5) mm, puberulent-papillose adaxially, glabrous abaxially; gynostegium short-stipitate, 1 X 1.3-1.35 mm, stipe ca. 0.2 mm long, stigma head with a small central bifid projection; anther wings 0.45-0.55 mm long, membranes erect or somewhat inflexed, 0.4-0.7 mm long; pollinia pendulous, narrowly ellipsoid or narrowly ovoid, 0.2-0.24 X 0.11-0.14 mm, caudicles 0.085 mm long, corpusculum narrowly to broadly ovoid, 0.14-0.2 X 0.1-0.14 mm; corona cup-shaped, 10- lobed, 1.1-1.3(-2) mm long, diam. 1.5-1.7 mm just above the base, abaxial surface rugose-papillose, lobes incumbent on gynostegium. Fruits unknown.

description: Vine, the young stems with unifarious pubescence; leaves petiolate, the petiole 0.7-1.5 cm long, pilose along upper margins, the blades membranous, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 3-5.8 cm long, 1.5-3 cm wide, apex long acuminate, base rounded to acute, the upper surface minutely appressed-pilose, the lower surface sparsely appressed-pilose to glabrescent, the secondary nerves 4-6 each side; inflorescence subaxillary, umbelliform, 4-6-flowered, the peduncle 0.5-2 mm long, densely appressedpilose, the pedicels 2.5-3.5 mm long, pilose; sepals ovate to deltoid-ovate, obtuse, 0.45-0.6 mm long, 0.6 mm wide, appressed-pilose, ciliate, with a small gland in each sinus; corolla short-campanulate, ca 4 mm diam., the petals white, narrowly ovate, 1.5-1.6 mm long, 0.8 mm wide, glabrous; gynostegium stipitate, 1.35-1.4 mm long; anthers 0.25-0.3 mm long, 0.35 mm wide; corona segments 5, narrowly ovate, 0.65 mm long, 0.5 mm wide at base; pollinia oblong, 0.17 mm long; corpusculum narrowly ovoid, 0.12 mm long; fruit unknown.

A D. colombiana base folioli obliqua, nervis secundariis arcuatis prominulis, nervis tertiariis alternatim-percurrentibus et fortuito-reticulatis et fructo ovoideo differt.

description: Tree, reproductive size 28-35 m X 49-100 cm. Trunk sometimes fluted at base. Bark pale gray, shallowly scalloped, densely lenticellate, shed in large thin irregular plates; inner bark light tan, scant, somewhat milky, drying cream-colored globules, flammable. Tri- chomes of five types: flexuous golden hairs to 0.6 mm long; thick, appressed golden hairs to 0.1 mm; fine, erect white hairs to 0.05-0.15 mm ("bristles"); golden snail-shaped glands; and erect golden hairs to 0.25 mm. Leaves 4-6-jugate, 17.8-34.5 cm long; petiole 3.8-8 cm X 2.6-3.8 mm; interjuga 1.9-2.5 cm long, petiole and rachis with sparse to dense bristles, usually dense appressed hairs, sparse to scattered flexuous hairs, and sparse to dense glands; lateral petiolules robust and shallowly canaliculate, 0.3-0.8 cm long, swollen at base but distal pulvinulus not apparent; terminal petiolule 0.8-1.8 cm long and pulvinulate distally; leaflets coriaceous, drying tan to brown abaxially, glossy grayish-brown adaxially; basal leaflets 5.1-9.5 x 2.7-5.3 cm, ovate, other laterals 6.5-13.5 x 2.4- 7.2 cm, (broadly) oblong-elliptic, elliptic, slightly oblanceolate or slightly (ob)ovate, the terminal leaflet 6-8.9 x 3-4.8 cm, slightly obovate, slightly oblanceolate, or elliptic, apex abruptly to gradually short-acuminate, the acumen 0.6-1.3 cm long, base of laterals oblique, the basiscopic side obtuse to acute and slightly decurrent, the acroscopic side truncate and slightly decurrent; margin usually slightly revolute; leaflet abaxial surface with midvein and secondary veins acutely prominent, rest of veins prominulous, abaxially the midvein with sparse to dense bristles to 0.15 mm long, sparse to dense appressed hairs, and dense to scattered long hairs to 0.6 mm long, secondary veins with scattered to dense bristles and scattered glands, also sometimes with scattered to sparse erect, golden hairs, rest of blade with scattered to dense glands and sometimes scattered to sparse erect, golden hairs; adaxial surface with midvein narrowly prominulous but sunk in a groove, rest of veins prominulous, adaxially the midvein glabrous or provided near the base with sparse to dense bristles and sparse glands and sometimes with sparse flexuous hairs, rest of adaxial surface glabrous or with a few scattered glands; the margin usually with scattered bristles and glands. Inflorescences axillary but subterminal, rather robust, 3.5-10.3 cm X 2.5-4.8 mm, secondary axes 0.6-3.2 cm, with dense to scattered flexuous hairs, dense to sparse glands, usually sparse to scattered bristles, and sometimes sparse to dense appressed hairs; bracts on the primary axes to ca. 2.5 mm long, essentially subulate to ovate, fleshy, leaving a broad scar when shed but not semi-clasping; bracteoles to 1.0 mm long, (broadly) ovate; pedicel (2.2-) 3.6-5 x 0.9-1.1 mm, terete, the pubescence as on inflorescence but usually lacking flexuous hairs and sometimes (in fruit) provided only with appressed hairs. Flowers pale green, hermaphroditic, 4.6-4.9 mm long (fresh or rehydrated) at anthesis; calyx deeply cupular and slightly urceolate, 1.9- 2.2 x 2.8-3.2 mm, exceeding the disk, the lobes (0-) 0.2-0.4 mm long, broadly depressed-deltate or (if separated by a flat sinus) triangular, sparsely pubescent, densely so along the margin, the erect white hairs to 0.15 mm long; petals pale green, 3.7-4.3 X 2.3-3 mm, slightly spreading at anthesis, broadly (oblong-)ovate, fleshy (particularly near the obtusely apiculate apex), abaxially with sparse appressed hairs to 0.05 mm long, adaxially with sparse to dense erect white hairs to 0.05 mm long, the margin short-papillate (sometimes only distally); stamens inserted near or at the base of the disk, at anthesis level with the stigmas (but exceeded by the pistil soon after fertilization), the antesepalous stamens 1.55-1.7 mm long, the filaments strap-shaped and broadened at base, the anthers 0.95-1.15 mm long, broadly oblong, the antepetalous stamens 1.45-1.6 mm long, the filaments broadly strap-shaped, straight, and nearly continuous with the anthers, these 0.9-1 mm long, broadly oblong-elliptic to broadly ovate; annular disk high and fleshy, 0.6-0.7 mm high x 0.3 mm thick; pistil 1.8-2 x 1-1.1 mm overall at anthesis, ovary 2-locular, slightly obovoid, glabrous, the style short and thick, 0.4 x 0.55 mm, stigma cap- itate, 2-lobed. Fruiting pedicel 3-5.2 x 1.6- 3.4 mm, usually clavate;fruits 2.3-3 X 1.5- 2 cm, (broadly) ovoid, slightly oblique (very young fruits often subglobose), with rounded apex and usually truncate base, yellow when immature, glabrous; pyrene slightly oblique, with a simple articulated plate on compressed side (see Daly & Martínez-Habibe, 2003). Seedlings: germination hypogeal and cryptocotylar; first eophylls opposite, trifoliate, the leaflets narrowly lanceolate, the margin entire.

D. kukachkanae, D. trinitensis, et D. belemensis foliolis glabris pedicello breviore flore et petalis brevioris calyce vadosior differt.

description: Tree, reproductive size 12-25 m X 18-35 cm diam.; buttresses absent. Outer bark café au lait to medium greenish gray brown to (pale) brown, thin, rough, with longitudinal fissures 2-3 mm deep, shed as small rectangular scales; inner bark cream colored to midbrown to (reddish) dark brown; wood cream to straw or bone colored. Resin transparent, aromatic, scant. Trichomes of four types: appressed yellowish hairs to 0.1 mm, fine erect white hairs to 0.05 mm, erect brownish hairs to 0.2 mm, snail-shaped glands less than 0.1 mm. Branchlets slender, 2-4.5 mm diam. at 2 cm below apex, usually lenticellate, the lenticels raised, dark brown, rounded to elliptic, 0.4-2 mm long, usually concentrated on and around base of petiole. Leaves 2-4-jugate, 11-29.3 cm long; petiole 2.3-7.5 cm X 1.4-2.4 mm diam., (semi)terete, usually sparsely lenticellate on and near base, the lenticels dark brown, raised, oblong to elliptic or less often subcircular, 0.3-2 mm long, trichomes of scattered appressed hairs and scattered to sparse snail-shaped glands; rachis trichomes same as petiole; interjuga 1.8-5 cm long; petiolules slender, the laterals 3-8 mm long, the terminal one 1.3-4.3 cm long, the pulvinuli conspicuous. Leaflets usually chartaceous, drying dark (reddish)brown; lateral leaflets 3.7-16 X 3.1-5.9 cm, the basal pair ovate to ovate-elliptic, the other laterals (broadly) elliptic or less often elliptic-obovate or elliptic-lanceolate, the base cuneate to acute or more often asymmetric, the basiscopic side acute to cuneate and the acroscopic side acute to rounded; terminal leaflet 15.3-19.1 X 3-5.5 cm, elliptic-obovate to elliptic-lanceolate or less often elliptic-ovate or narrowly ovate, the base acute; leaflet apex usually gradually and broadly short-acuminate (sometimes long- acuminate on sterile specimens), the acumen 4-11 mm long; both surfaces glabrous; veins on abaxial side acutely prominent to prominulous, on adaxial side prominulous to prominent. Leaflet venation (Fig. IM) festooned brochidodromus, with perpendicular epimedial tertiaries and weak intertertiaries; tertiary venation alternate-percurrent; quaternary venation random-reticulate and dichomotizing, forming irregularly shaped areoles; quinary venation dichotomizing and dendritic, with 2+-branched freely ending veinlets; fimbrial vein present; marginal veins looped. Inflorescence bracts lanceolate to ovate with slightly acuminate (rarely acute) apex, densely pubescent, the bracts on primary axis 1-2 mm long; bracteoles subtending the flowers 0.5- 0.6 mm long. Infiorescences dimorphic but always exceeding the subtending petiole, the staminate ones laxly branched, 14-32 cm X 0.7-1.6 mm diam. with secondary axes to 15 cm long, the pistillate ones 5- 7.8 cm X 0.5-0.7 mm diam. with secondary axes to 3.9 cm long (to 7.5 cm long in Stergios & Velazco 13970); axes with sparse to dense appressed yellowish hairs and snail-shaped glands, sparse to scattered fine erect white hairs (or absent), and sometimes sparse to scattered brown erect hairs; pedicels terete, the staminate ones 2.5-10 X 0.1-0.3 mm, the pistillate ones 2.5-6.5 X 0.25-0.4 mm. Flowers unisexual, 1.8-3 mm long at anthesis. Staminate flowers (Fig. 1H-J): calyx cupular, 0.6-0.8 X 1.5- 1.8 mm overall, exceeded by disk, with small teeth (lobes) 0.05-0.15 mm long separated by a flat sinus, the hairs sparse, appressed; petals reddish(brown) to wine red, ovate, 1.8-2.3 X 1.5-2.1 mm, membranaceous, the apex apiculum inconspicuous, inflexed, slightly thickened, papillate, 0.1-0.2 mm long; stamens 0.8 mm (antesepalous) and 0.75 mm (antepetalous) long (both stamens 0.75-0.8 mm on some flowers of Prance et al. 16147); filaments broadly strap-shaped and continuous with anthers (Fig. IJ); anthers broadly elliptic to subrotund, 0.5-0.55 mm (antesepalous) and 0.5 mm (antepetalous) long, the apex rounded to retuse; ovariodisk (fused disk and pistillode) parenchymatous, glabrous, 0.65-1 X 0.7-1.1 mm overall, the basal portion discoid and 0.15-0.35 mm high, the distal portion conical and 0.45-0.5 mm high, the apex slightly articulated and minutely lobulate, 0.1 mm long (Fig. 11). Pistillate flowers (Fig. IC-E): calyx 1-1.2 X 2-2.2 mm overall, the lobes 0.2-0.25 mm long, rounded perdepressed-triangular and notched at the sinuses; petals narrowly ovate, 1.75-2.5 X (1-)1.4-1.8 mm; staminodes 0.9-1.15 mm (antesepalous) and 0.8-1.05 mm (antepetalous) long; filaments broadly strap-shaped and continuous with anthers (Fig. IE); anthers devoid of pollen, very broadly elliptic to broadly oblong to subrotund, 0.5- 0.65 mm (antesepalous) and 0.45-0.6 mm (antepetalous) long, the apex rounded to retuse; disk 0.2-0.5 high X 0.1-0.15 mm thick; pistil (Fig. ID) 1.5-1.7 X 0.5-1 mm overall; ovary 2-locular, (narrowly) ovoid, glabrous, the base sessile, the style 0.2-0.4 mm long, the stigmas 0.2-0.3 mm high, (depressed-)discoid. Fruiting pedicel 5-8.8 X 1.1 mm. Fruits at least 2.1-2.4 X 1.1-1.4 cm (mature fruits unknown), ovoid, slightly oblique, the base truncate, apex rounded to truncate, the surface drying rugose, glabrous; pyrene (Fig. IL) 2-2.2 X 1.2 cm, slightly oblique-ovoid, cartilaginous, the ventral surface with a raised plate (corresponding to aborted locule and rather easily peeled off in immature fruits), the plate elliptic or ovate with acuminate apex. Cotyledons and germination unknown.

description: Herba scandens gracilis, caulibus longitudinaliter suleatis, eirciter 1 mm. diametro, internodiis 4-8 cm. longis; foliis biternatis, petiolo 1-2.5 cm. longo, plerumque eirrhiferis; foliolis membranaceis, oblongo-ovatis vel ovato-ellipticis, plerumque 3-5 cm. longis, 1.5-3 cm. latis, aliquot minoribus, in sieco supra subolivaceis, subtus subglaucis, acutis vel obscure acuminatis, basi rotundatis, lateralibus plus minusve inaequilateralibus, plerumque 5-nerviis, nervis gracilibus, adscendentibus, petiolulis brevibus, interioribus quam lateralibus longioribus, eirrhis ramosis, saltem ad 6 cm. longis; infloreseentiis -paucifloris, longe (ad 5 cm.) pedunculatis, 5-7-floris, pedicellis 7-10 mm. longis, bracteis linearibus, integerrimis, pedunculo subaequantibus; floribus flavidis, 2 cm. longis, compressis, eirciter 6 mm. latis, basi cordatis; sepalis 2, lanceolatis, acuminatis, 3 mm. longis; petalis binis exterioribus basi saccatis ad apicem eucullatis, supra eucullos late apiculatis, binis interioribus longissime (12 mm.) filiformiter stipitatis, lamina eirciter 8 mm. longa, 3.5 mm. lata, in dimidia parte angustata, supra medio suborbicularibus, apice rostrato-acuminatis, intus longitudinaliter bialatis; filamentis 6, partibus liberis filiformibus 4 mm. longis; ovario lineari-lanceolato, cum stylo 16 mm. longo, glabro, stigmate inaequaliter 4-lobulato; capsulis non visis, rubris, (ex collectore) ut videtur angustis, elongatis.

description: Arbor circa 8 m alta ramulis terminalibus dense crasseque cinereo-tomentosis in sicco ochroleucis pilis crispis intricatis et aliquis patulis longioribusque instructis, ramis deinde plus minusve glabratis cortice rugoso brunneo vel griseo. Folia alterna coriacea luteolo-viridia, late elliptico-lanceolata vel subobovato- oblanceolata basi attenuata subcuneata vel subobtusa, apice angustata acuta margine integra nervoso-marginata, petiolo crasso crispo-tomentoso 4-8 mm longo; lamina 6-14 cm longa, 2-6 cm lata, supra juvenilis pubescens mox glabra vel subglabra nitidaque costa nervis secundariis reticuloque venorum prominenti valde conspicuis; subtus tomento cinereo pilis longis crispis intricatis et parcis pilis rectis intermixtis tecta, costa prominenti nervis secundariis 10-12 utroque latere arcuato-ascendentibus prominulis nervulis venulisque in reticulum prominulum satis notatum anastomosatis. Inflorescentiae femineae umbellatae simplices extraxillares pedunculo robusto ascendente crispo-hirsutulo-lanato 1-2 cm longo apice incrassato ebracteato 10-16 flores ferenti; pedicelli crassi tomentosi 0.5-5 mm longi; flores feminei calyce (fere fructifero) circa 5 mm longo 3 mm diamitenti urceolato extus dense longeque crispo-tomentoso, segmentis 1.5 mm longis ovatis obtusis minute papillosulis intus glabris vel apice pilosulis tubo 3.5 mm alto intus glabro ad faucem 8 squamulis minutis (0.1-0.2 mm) staminodialis (4 oppositisepalis, 4 alternisepalis) et 8 squamulis papillosis per pares alternisepalis; discus annularis margine undulato membranaceus basi adnatus 0.2 mm altus; ovarium (valde maturum) obpyriforme 3-3.5 mm longum glabrum stigmate sessile eapitato tomentoso-papilloso.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1962. Studies in South American plants VI. Brittonia. 14: 50-56.

description: Arbor 5-7 m alta ramis terminalibus tortuosis subteretibus griseis paulo rugulosis einereo-cereus lenticellatis, juvenilibus adpresse puberulis demum glabris. Folia alterna simplicia coriacea petiolata, oblongo-obovata apice subrotundata vel obtusa vel breviter in obtusum acumen angustata basi cuneato-attenuata in petiolum 10-15 mm longum producta, margine anguste revoluta integerrima; lamina 6-13 cm longa 2.5-5 cm lata, supra pallide griseo-viridis pellicula cerea minute granuloso-scrobiculata praedita, costa notata nervis lateralibus parum conspicuis; subtus einerea velamine granulato-cereo tectis pilis rigidulis ad- pressis munita, costa eminenti plus minusve strigulosa nervis secundariis 8-11 utroque latere valde tenuibus subpatulis marginem versus arcuato aseendentibus anastomosantibusque venulis graciliter reticulatis plus minusve velatis sed conspicuis. Infloreseentiae femineae pseudoterminales dichotomo-paniculatae foliis valde breviores (2-10 cm amplae), pedunculo 0.5-1 cm longo striato sparse strigoso, ramulis divaricatis subeinereis striatis strigosis et sparse squamoso-cereis; flores feminei 10-16 ad terminationem ramusculorum apice capitato hirsutoque umbellati; pedicelli crassi 2-3 mm longi strigosi; calyx 3-3.5 mm longus crassus pallide viridi-luteus extus adpresse pubeseens tubo suburceolato 2-2.3 mm longo intus glaber lobis suborbiculatis 1-1.2 mm latis longisque intus glabris et minute papillosis vel subapicem pubescentibus; fauce annulo tenui brevi membranaceo 4 squamis (staminodia) 0.4 mm longis oppositisepalis exsertis, 4 squamis (staminodia) paulo brevioribus alternisepalis inclusis et 8 squamulis (petala?) brevissimis papillosis per pares alternisepalis; discus annularis brevis (0.2 mm altus) dentatus adnatus. Pistillum oblongum circa 3 mm longum ovario glabro; ovulo unico pendulo stylo brevi crasso stigmate capitato dense hirto-papilloso; fructus inmaturus obpyriformis circa 1 cm longus.

description: A Davilla cearensi J. Huber foliis 14-26 X 6-8 cm, subcoriaceis, ellipticis vel elliptico-lanceolatis, basi obtuse cuneatis, margine revolutis, nervis lateralibus in quoque latere 17-21, petiolo haud canaliculato, sepalis externis 4-5 mm longis atque capsula biseminali differt.

description: Liana, branches and branchlets sparsely appressed pubescent, glabrescent when mature. Leaf blades subcoriaceous, elliptic, elliptic-lanceolate, 14-26 X 6-8 cm, apices acuminate, bases obtuse-cuneate, margins revolute, entire to discreetly subsinuatedentate (mostly in the upper half), smooth and glabrous, except along the midrib and secondary nerves on the lower surface, which are covered by sparsely appressed pubescence, lateral nerves 17-21, convergent and linking close to the margin, tertiary venation evident on both surfaces; petioles thick at the base (4-5 mm wide), 1.5-3.5 cm long, subalate, discretely caniculate, sparsely appressed pubescent. Infiorescences terminal, paniculate, 7-8 cm long, sparsely appressed pubescent, pedicels 6-8 mm long, pubescence as the inflorescence, with a basal triangular bractlet, 1-2 mm long, margins ciliate, densely appressed sericeous externally, sparsely appressed pubescent internally. Calyx with 5 sepals, orbicular, unequal in size, the 2 inner larger, 1-1.2 cm long, papyraceous, strongly compressed and ciliate at the margin, sparsely appressed pubescent on both sides, glabrescent when mature, the 3 external shorter, 4-5 mm long, sparsely appressed pubescent externally, laxe-pilose to grabrescent internally. Petals and stamens not seen. Ovary with two carpels. Fruit a capsule, globose, 7-8 mm long; seeds 2, 5-6 mm long, black, rugose, glabrous, covered completely by a white papyraceous aril.

description: Liana, branches and branchlets striate, glabrous. Leaf blades coriaceous, lanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic, 15-20 X 7-8 cm, apices acuminate, bases obtuse, margins revolute, entire to slightly subsinuate, mostly in the upper half, smooth and glabrous on the upper surface, glabrous on the lower surface, except along the midrib and secondary nerves, which are covered by sparsely appressed pubescence, lateral nerves 12-16, convergent and joining close to the margin, tertiary venation evident on both surfaces; petioles thick at the base (3-5 mm wide), 3-5 cm long, alate, sparsely appressed pubescent to glabrescent. Inforescences, paniculate, 12-14 cm long, peduncles 3-4 cm long, glabrescent, pedicels 2.5-3 cm long, glabrescent, articulate at the base. Calyx with S sepals, orbicular, unequal in size, the inner 2 larger, rigid-coriaceous, 2-2.5 cm long, strongly compressed at the margin, punctate and shortly-pilose externally, glabrous internally, the 3 external shorter, 0.5-1 cm long, glabrous on both sides. Petals not seen. Stamens 150-200, filaments 4-5 mm long, glabrous, anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm long, glabrescent. Ovary with 2 carpels, carpels lenticellate, sparsely appressed pubescent, style ca. 1 cm long, glabrous, stigma capitate. Fruit not seen.

description: Frutex 0.2-0.7 m altus, 0.5-2 m latus; caules foliosi, hirsutuli; folia alterna petiolata exstipulata, laminis ellipticis hirsutulis, 1-1.5 cm longis, (4-) 5-7 mm latis; inflorescentiae cymosae, 1-3 (-4) cm longae; pedunculi erecti; involucra nulla; flores lutescentes 1.8-3 mm longi, hispiduli; achaenia 2-2.5 mm longa.

description: Large, densely branched shrubs 0.2-0.7 m tall, 0.5-2 m across, with numerous, gray, woody branches arising from a stout, woody root, the woody branches spread- ing, covered with thin, grayish bark, the bark becoming thicker and slightly reticulate near the base of the larger and more woody individuals, a single stem up to 3 cm across at the base, the upper herbaceous growth annually produced from the axils of the uppermost leaves of the previous year's growth, these branches thin and, with age and time, often becoming rigid and somewhat spinose; leaves alternate, green to yellowish-green, hirsutulous, the leaf-blade elliptic, 1-1.5 cm long, (4-) 5-7 mm wide, thin pubescent on both surfaces, the hairs slightly more dense and longer on the margin, the margin entire and plane, the apex acute to narrowly obtuse, the base tapering gradually to the 2-5 mm long petiole, the petiole greenish to whitish- yellow or tannish depending upon age, with the pubescence more pronounced along the margin, the petiole-base tannish to whitish-yellow, elongate-triangular, 0.8-1 mm long and wide, pubescent on both surfaces; flowering branches annually produced, greenish, erect or nearly so, leafy, 2-7 (-10) cm long, hirsutulous throughout with short, spreading hairs, the stems often becoming tannish with age especially among the leaves; inflorescences cymose, 1-3 (-4) cm long, mostly trichotomously branched, divided 1 to 4 times, the green hirsutulous branches becoming reduced in length upwardly, with a single, short-pedicellate flower and a single peduncle at each node; bracts of the inflorescence foliaceous and similar to the leaves except reduced in size toward the apex, the 3-4 bracts of the lowermost node up to 1.2 cm long, the 2-3 bracts of the upper nodes much reduced and somewhat scale-like, always less than half the length of the lower ones; description: Ewan's description leaves no doubt of the well marked species he had in mind, but the name is based on a mixed collection (Ewan 10295). The sheet which was received at the University of California, Los Angeles, includes a plant which is probably a hybrid derivative with D. parryi. This is indicated by the pubes- cence of the petioles and the color and conformation of the sepals. Hybrids of these species occur in nature and this aberrant form has been readily matched by us among garden F2 progenies or backcrosses to D. gypsophilum. The type specimen, cited as being at the University of Colorado (p. 189), cannot be lo- cated. We have not, therefore, been able to determine whether the name actually applies to the species described or to a hybrid. Professor Ewan has kindly sent us the sheet of the type collection now at Tulane University and this plant is typical of D. gypsophilum as he described it and as we understand it. If the type specimen has actually been lost, this specimen at Tulane can be taken as the lectotype. We have not examined other distributed sheets of the type collection and it is possible that some of them also represent hybrids.

description: Ascending or lianoid shrub. Mature stems terete, glabrous; bark thin, cracking into a reticulum, light brown when dry; immature twigs subterete, bluntly flattened, smooth or weakly striate, glabrous, reddish-brown when dry. Petioles terete, stout, glabrous, 3 X 2.5 mm, dark reddish-brown. Leaves coriaceous, opposite, broadly ovate, (1.5) 2-6.5 X 1.5-4.5 cm, basally shallowly cordate, apically acute or obtuse, entire or obscurely crenate distally with glandular-tipped teeth, glabrous but sparsely reddishglandular fimbriate beneath; pinnatinerved with 2-3 pairs of arcuate lateral nerves which anastomose near the margin, midrib and lateral nerves impressed above and slightly raised beneath, deep wine-red in color beneath (fide label data), veinlets inconspicuous beneath; pseudostipules paired, ovate-aristate, 4-5 mm long. Inflorescence axillary, fasciculate, with 2-4 flowers per fascicle. Floral bracts ovate, acuminate, 3-4 X 2 mm, midrib drawn-out into an apiculum, margins glandular-fimbriate. Pedicels cylindric, striate, continuous with the calyx, glabrous, 30-34 x 1.5 mm, deep red to, reddish-purple (fide label data), with scattered glandular fimbriae. Bracteoles basal, similar to floral bracts. Calyx glabrous, 15-16 mm long; tube obconic, slightly rugose, 2.5-4 mm long and 5-6 mm broad at the top; limb spreading campanulate, 11-13 mm long including the lobes; lobes lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, striate, 10-12 X 4 mm, with few caducous marginal fimbriae; sinus acute. Corolla cylindric, constricted at the throat, glabrous, 42-49 X 13-16 mm, rosy-pink to red (fide label data); lobes ovate or oblong-ovate, obtuse or acute, 6-8 x 5-7 mm. Stamens 10, 40-43 mm long; filaments distinct, alternately 2.5 and 5 mm long, densely short-hirsute on both sides and glandular-fimbriate on the dorsal side (Fig. 15C); anthers 37-40 mm long including the tubules, incurved and blunt at the base; thecae 6-8 mm long, granular; dehiscence by elongate slits (3) 5-8 mm long. Style 50-53 mm long, deep pink to red, and the stigma purple (fide label data). Fruit unknown.

description: "Multiple-stemmed, stiff, ascending 4-10 ft shrub" or "epiphytic shrub festooning from trees" (fide label data). Mature stems terete, glabrous, with epidermis cracking into a reticulum exposing a dark, reddish-brown bark; immature stems subterete, bluntly angled, densely short-white-pilose, light brown. Petioles subterete, dorsally flattened, rugose, short-white-pilose, 2.5-5 x 1 mm. Leaves coriaceous, opposite, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 1.5-2.5 x 1-1.5 cm, basally broadly rounded, apically obtuse, entire, sparsely short-white-pilose on both surfaces especially along nerves and blackish- or reddish-glandular-fimbriate on both surfaces; pinnatinerved with 2 pairs of lateral nerves, all nerves impressed above and slightly raised beneath but only the midrib and inner pair of lateral nerves conspicuous beneath; pseudostipules obscure, ovate, acuminate, 1-2 mm long. Inflorescence axillary, solitary, racemose, 8-20-flowered; rachis subterete or bluntly 4-angled, densely short-whitepilose and sparsely glandular-fimbriate, 2-3 (5) cm long and to 1 mm in diam at base. Floral bracts and bracteoles caducous, ovate-lanceolate, 3-4 X 1 mm, short-whitepilose, bracteoles ciliate with glandular fimbriae. Pedicels continuous with calyx, terete, striate, densely short-white-pilose, 10 mm long at anthesis and elongating to 15-20 mm, ca 0.5 mm in diam, charged with scattered reddish-brown glandular fimbriae. Calyx densely short-white-pilose, 5-6 mm long; tube terete or slightly angled, sparsely glandular-fimbriate, 2.5-3 mm long and ca 2-2.2 mm in diam across the summit; limb spreading, somewhat striate, ca 4 mm long including the lobes; lobes ovate, acuminate, 3.5 mm long; sinus acute. Corolla cylindric, widening towards the apex, densely short-white-pilose, 19-22 mm long and ca 3-3.5 mm in diam, rustrose, deep wine- to maroon-red (fide label data); lobes ovate, obtuse, 2-3 mm long. Stamens 10, ca 18 mm long; filaments distinct, alternately ca 1 and 2 mm long, shortwhite-pilose on both surfaces, not glandular-fimbriate; anthers 16-17 mm long including tubules; thecae granular, 3 mm long; dehiscence by clefts ca 1-1.3 mm long. Style glabrous, 20-21 mm long. Fruit unknown.

description: "Trailing and festooning liana" (fide label data). Mature stems terete or subterete and bluntly angled, smooth, glabrous, light to dark brown when dry; bark cracking into long strips. Pedicels continuous with the calyx, striate, 40-45 (50) x 1 mm, densely pilose with short, white hairs. Bracteoles basal, ovate, acuminate, 5 x 1 mm, densely short-white-pilose. Calyx pinkish to deep reddish-purple (fide label data), 36-46 mm long, short-white-pilose; tube obconic, striate, somewhat 5-angled opposite the sinuses, 4-7 mm long and 7-9 mm across the summit; limb spreading, 26-30 (40) mm long including the lobes; lobes striate, lance-elliptic, acuminate, 24-28 (38) X 6 (12) mm, short-pilose within the lobes; sinus acute. Corolla cylindric, deep rosy-pink to reddish-purple (fide label data), short-white-pilose, 50-54 (60) X 10-15 mm including the lobes; lobes triangular, obtuse, slightly spreading, 14-16 X 4.5-5 mm. Style exserted, 46-51 (54) mm long, pale pink (fide label data). Fruit unknown.

description: Rather large (50-70 cm), but delicate and diffulsely branched plant, glabrous, stems terete; lateral branches and inflorescences without cataphylls; older internodes to 5.5 cm long. description: Shrub ca 2.5 m. Leaves opposite, simple; blade entire, narrow to wide-elliptic to narrow-obovate, rounded, obtuse, or acuminate at apex, usually acute at base, 6-14.9 (19.3) cm long, 3.5-7.1 cm wide, chartaceous, glabrous, with 5-10 secondary veins per side, the venation brochidodromous with midvein raised on both surfaces; pet- iole flattened or canaliculate adaxially, 0.4- 0.6 cm long, puberulent. Inflorescence terminal, subsessile, 1- or 2-flowered; bracts lanceolate, 2.8-4.2 mm long, densely appressed-puberulent; pedicels 0.8-1.2 cm long in flower, appressed-puberulent. Calyx of 5 valvate sepals connate for ca 1/2 their length, 5-lobed, 1.8-2 cm long, 0.6-0.9 cm wide at middle, appressed-puberulent, glabrous within. Corolla zygomorphic, ca 6 cm long, salmon-pink (Collenette in Riley 470); pet- als tightly adherent to filaments, the result- ing tube straight, 2.0-2.7 cm long, 0.3-0.5 cm wide at apex, appressed-puberulent ex- ternally on petal bases and curly-tomentulose on abaxial surfaces of filaments exposed between the petal bases, sparsely tomentulose and with a densely woolly ring ca 3 mm wide beginning ca 3 mm above the base within, the lobes narrow-obovate or oblanceolate, unguiculate, obtuse at apex, 2-4 cm long, 0.8-1.1 cm wide, glabrous ex- cept for abaxially appressed-pilose midrib. Androecium of 2 fertile stamens flanking in- nermost corolla lobe and 5 staminodes; filaments adnate to the corolla; fertile fila- ments with free, linear tip 15-17 mm long and puberulent, the anthers (in bud) 4.2 mm long, glabrous, the apiculum 0.3 mm long, the flattened bilobed basal appendage ap- parently an extension of the connective, to 0.7 mm long; 3 antesepalous staminodes with free tip ca 12 mm long, the 2 antepetalous ones further united to petals and with free tip ca 6 mm long, all curly-tomentulose at base, flattened, glabrous, glandular-punc- tate at apex. Fruit and seeds unknown.

description: Dioecious trees, the inner bark exuding a watery reddish liquid (at least in several species), the branchlets subterete, when young usually strigose (hairs attached at the middle, usually 2-branched, sometimes 3-5-branched, but only 1 or 2 branches conspicuous), soon glabrous; leaves alternate, petiolate (petioles winged), the blades chartaceous or thin coriaceous in texture, entire and often slightly thickened at margins, glabrous above (at least at maturity) and usually minutely strigose beneath with typical 2-branched hairs (usually glabreseeilt at maturity), the costa prominent beneath, the secondary nerves several to many, obscurely anastomosing near margins, the veinlets obseure; inflorescences usually 1 or 2 in leaf axils, simple or 2- or 3-branched, usuallv minutely strigose on all exterior surfaces, the rachis bearing alternate or opposite sessile fascicles (1 fascicle usually terminal, the pistillate flowers sometimes solitary); bracts subtending the fascicles small or none; bracteoles none (rarely rudimentary at summit of pistillate pedicels); flowers pedicellate; staminate perianth small, usually thin carnose, glabrous within, 3 (rarely 4)-lobed; filaments connate in convex, the anthers 5 or 6, 0.5-0.6mm. long; pistillate inflorescences resembling the staminate but with fewer flowers, the perianth slightly larger than the staminate, the ovary subglobose, glandular - punctate, the stigma peltate, subsessile; fruiting inflorescences not seen; fruit ovoid, about 1.7 cm long.

description: Tree; branchlets slender, striate, minutely strigose or glabrous; petioles canaliculate, narrowly winged, 3-5 mm. broad including wings 20-30 mm. long, minutely strigose; leaf blades minutely papillose on both surfaces, with 2 or 4 conspicuous curved longitudinal lines (marks of conduplicate vernation), elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 11-19 cm. long, 6-9 cm. broad, attenuate at base, rounded or obtusely cuspidate at apex, glabrous on both surfaces or minutely strigose with 2-branched hairs beneath, the costa plane or slightly raised above, the secondary nerves about 15 per side, spreading, ascending near margins, plane or slightly impressed above, prominulous beneath; staminate inflorescences 1 or 2 in leaf axils, simple (at least in our specimens), minutely strigose on all exterior surfaces, 4-5 cm. long at anthesis, the peduncle up to 2 cm. long; fascicles alternate, 3 or 4 per inflorescenee, the bracts inconspicuous or none; flowers 3-6 per fascicle, the pedicels up to 4 mm. long; perianth 4-4.5 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes oblong, obtuse; androecium nearly as long as the perianth, the filament column conspicuously swollen, about 2 mm. long, the filaments conspicuously divergent distally, the anthers oblong, about 1.5 mm. long, affixed dorsally at base, slightly recurved at apex; pistillate inflorescenees up to 4 cm. long at anthesis, minutely strigose as the staminate, the flowers in fascicles of 2-5, the pedicels stout, up to 4 mm. long, sometimes bearing at summit a scar indicating a rudimentary bracteole; perianth carnose, slightly larger than the staminate, 3-lobed nearly to base, the ovary short stipi- tate, ellipsoid, densely strigose with 2-branched hairs, the stigma inconspicuously cleft; fruits (only one seen) short pedicelate, faintly cariniate, about 23 mm. long and 14 mm. broad, conspicuously stipitate at base, apiculate at apex with the persistent minute style, the pericarp about 2 mm. thick, rugose, the aril laciniate, the seed globose or slightly ellipsoid.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Medium sized tree; branchlets stout, rugose, minutely strigose, at length glabrous; petioles stout, conspicuously winged, 6-12 mm. broad including wings, 15-40 mm. long, soon glabrous; leaf blades minutely rugose on both surfaces, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 20-30 cm. long, 7-13 cm. broad, attenuate at base, cuspidate or short acuminate at apex, glabrous on both surfaces or minutely strigose beneath, the costa stout, nearly plane above, the secondary nerves 20-25 per side, spreading, slightly impressed or plane above, nearly plane beneath; staminate inflorescences sometimes simple and paired, sometimes solitary and 3-branched near base, minutely and inconspicuously strigose on all exterior surfaces, 10-16 cm. long at anthesis, the peduncle short, the rachis slender, striate, conspicuously swollen at the fascicles; fascicles alternate or opposite, 5-7 per inflorescence (or if inflorescence is branched, 5-7 per branch), the bracts apparently none; flowers 10-40 per fascicle, the pedicels very slelnder, up to 10 mm. long; perianth about 3.5 mm. long, 3-lobed more than one-half its total length, the lobes oblong, obtuse; androecium 1.8-1.9 mm. long, the filaments free at apex, the anthers about 0.25 mm. long, free to base, obtuse, attached dorsally at base; pistillate and fruiting inflorescences not known.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Arbor, antheris prope ad apices connlatis, inflorescentiis masculis et foliis subtus densissimn e tomentellis distinguenda; petiolis conspicue alatis D. latialatae affinis, characteribus supra enumeratis et floribus majoribus valde differt.

description: Tree; branchlets stout, densely tomentellous (hairs usually 2-branched, the branches up to 0.8 mm. long); petioles conspicuously winged, 10-14 mm. broad including wings, 25-40 mm. long; leaf blades coriaceous, minutely papillose above, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 17-28 cm. long, 6.5-11 cm. broad, attenuate at base and decurrent on the petiole, obtusely cuspidate at apex, glabrous above (at least at maturity), persistently tomentellous beneath (hairs of 2 types: very dense small scale-like hairs 0.15-0.2 mm. in diameter, sessile, irregularly 6-8-branched, with a darker center; sparser dialy antheroid hairs, the largest branch about 0.5 mm. long, the other 1-3 branches nearly sup- pressed), the costa stout, slightly raised above, the secondary nerves 12-18 per side, spreading, minutely impressed above, prominulous beneath; staminate inflorescences 1 or 2 in leaf axils, simple (at least in our specimens), densely tomentellous on all exterior surfaces with hairs  similar to those of the leaves, 6-9 cm. long at anthesis, the peduncle up to 5 cm. long; fascicles alternate, about 3 per inflorescence, the bracts inconspicuous or none; the flowers 10-20 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 7 mm. long; perianth carnose, about 5 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes oblong, obtuse; androecium about 3.5 mm. long, the filament column conspicuously swollen near base, the filainents completely connate, the anthers 3, about 0.8 mm. long, dorsally connate nearly to apex; pistillate and fruiting inflorescences not known. (Fig. 3. g-i.)
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Tree up to 30 m. high, the trunk up to 45 cm. in diameter, with low buttresses; branchlets rugose, slender, minutely strigose, glabrescent and cinereous; petioles shallowly canaliculate, narrowly winged, 1-6 mm. broad including wings, 15-35 mm. long, soon glabrous; leaf blades often minutely papillose on both surf aces, elliptic or obovate-elliptie, 10- 28 cm. long, 4-10.5 cm. broad, attenuate at base, subacute or obtusely cuspidate or short acuminate at apex, when young minutely strigose beneath, glabrescent, the costa plane or slightly raised above, the secon- dary nerves 8-18 per side, ascending, minutely impressed or plane above, raised beneath; staminate inflorescences 1-3 in leaf axils, slender, simple or 3-branched from near base, minutely strigose on all exterior surfaces (hairs usually 2-branched, the branches 0.2-0.3 mm. long), 3-15 cm. long at anthesis, the peduncle up to 2.5 cm. long, the rachis often flexuose; fascicles alternate, 2-12 per inflorescenee, the bracts semiorbicular from a broad base, 3-4 mm. long, soon deciduous; flowers 8-15 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 6 mm. long; perianth about 4 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes oblong, obtuse; androecium 2.4-3 mm. long, the filament column swollen at base, 1.6-2.5 mm. long, the filaments connate to apex, the anthers 0.5-0.8 mm. long, free to base or dorsally connate in the proximal one-half; pistillate inflorescences up to 5 cm. long, minutely strigose as the staminate, the flowers arranged in fascicles of 2-5, the pedicels stout, up to 6 mm. long, sometimes bearing at the summit a minute rudimentary bracteole; perianth carnose, up to 5 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the ovary short stipitate, ellipsoid, apparently glabrous, the style curved at apex, the stigma inconspicuous; fruiting inflorescences up to 8 cm. long, essentially glabrous throughout, the mature fruits 2-4 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 8-15 mm. long, swollen distally) , smooth or fainitly carinate, 21-33 mm. long, 16-23 mm. broad, conspicuously stipitate at base, cuspidate at apex, the pericarp 2-4 mm. thick, often conspicuously lenticellate, the aril laciniate nearly to base, the seed subglobose or slightly ellipsoid, obtusely cuspidate at apex, 13-22 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Tree 5-15 m. high; branchlets subterete or angled, striate, slender, when young minutely strigose (hairs 0.2-0.4 mm. long, attached by the middle), soon glabrous; petioles shallowly canaliculate, narrowly winged, 1-4 mm. broad including wings, 10-30 mm. long, strigose as the branchlets, glabrescent; leaf blades often minutely papillose or rugose on both surfaces, elliptic, 8-20 cm. long, 3.5-8 cm. broad, attenuate at base, obtusely short acuminate or cuspidate at apex, often glaucous and sparsely strigose beneath, soon glabrous, the costa shallowly grooved or plane above, the secondary nerves 8-14 per side, ascending, impressed or plane above, raised beneath; staminate inflorescences straight, slender, simple, fasciculate-racemose, strigose on all exterior surfaces (hairs usually 2-branched, 0.2-0.4 mm. in total length), 4-16 cm. long at anthesis, the peduncle up to 1.5 cm. long; fascicles alternate, 12-29 per inflorescence, each subtended by a bract (bracts chartaceous, semiorbicular, broadest at base, 1-1.5 mm. long, conspicuous and crowded in short young inflorescences, at length deciduous); flowers 2-13 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, 2-4 mm. long; perianth infundibuliforin or cupuliform, 3-4 mm. long, 3-lobed more than one-half its total length, the lobes oblong, obtuse; androecium 16-23 mm. long, the filainent column conspicuously swollen at base, 1.1-1.6 mm. long, the filaments slightly divergent at apex, the anthers 0.5-0.7 mm. long, free, often slightly recurved at apex; pistillate inflorescences 2-4 cm. long, slender, minutely puberulent or glabrous, the flowers solitary or paired on the rachis, the pedicels slender, 2-3 mm. long; ovary subglobose, rounded at base, glabrous, the stigma slightly swollen; fruiting inflorescences up to 7 cm. long, glabrous throughout, the mature fruits 2 or 3 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels 5-12 mm. long), smooth or faintly carinate, 25-27 mm. long, 20-23 mm. broad, short stipitate at base, often cuspidate at apex, the pericarp 1-2 mm. thick, the seed 17-20 mm. long, 15-20 mim. broad, the testa brittle. (Fig. 3. a-c.)

description: Herba scandens, glabra, caulibus plerumque 1.5 mm diametro; folia triternata, duabus divisionibus primariis foliolas gerentibus, tertia in cirrhum tenuem apice ramosum mutata, petiolus teres, brevis, 4-5 mm longus; petioluli primarii 3-5 cm longi, secundarii 0.5-3 cm longi, tertiarii 0.3-1 cm longi; foliola ovata, integra, apice rotundata mucrone minuto, basi cuneata plerumque obliqua, (8-) 12-20 (-30) mm longa, (4-) 10-18 (-25) mm lata, membrancea, venis 8-15, tenuibus leviter curvatis, e basi ad apicem percurrentibus. Inflorescentia corymbosus, 4-6 flora, pedunculo ca 3-4 cm longo, pedicellis 2-3 cm longis, bracteis lineari-lanceolatis, integris, 3-4 mm longis, scariosis; flores in vivo lutei, (ex collector) e 2.5 cm longi, 1 cm lati, basi profunde cordati, sinu angusto, 4-6 mm longo. Sepala ovata vel triangularia, ca 2 mm longa, caduca; petala exteriora 17-19 (-23) mm longa, 4-6 mm lata, basi obtuse calcarata, calcaribus 5-6 mm longis, apice cucullata supra cucullos late apiculato, partibus terminalibus liberis patentibus ca 5 mm longis; petala interiora 20-22 mm longa, parte exserta quam petalis exterioribus 5 mm longiore, lamina 6 mm longa, 3-4 mm lata, ungue filiformi 10-11 mm longo, crista 1-2 mm diametro; stamina 6, in phalanges duas ordinata, filamentis e basi ad 2 mm infra antheras connatis ideo parte libera 2 mm longa; calcar nectariferum ca 5 mm longum, apice ad instar litterae T. factum; granula pollinis pantocolpata cum verrucae minutae. Stigma quadrangulare, apice incisum. Fructus et semina ignota.

description: Scapose perennial from a short rootstock bearinig small, yellow, pea-shaped bulblets; leaves glaucous beneath, broadly trianigular in outline, ternately decompound, (10-)14-24(-30) cm long, (4-)6-14(-18) cm broad; petioles (5-)8-16 (-22) cm long; ultimate leaf segments linear to linear-elliptic or linearobovate, usually minutely apiculate, (2-)5-15(-23) mm long, (0.4-)2-3(-4) mm broad; racemes usually exceeding the leaves, (10-)15-27(-33) cm long; bracts ovate, 2-5 mm long, 1-3 mmn broad; pedicels (2-)3-7(-14) mm long, bibracteolate; sepals deltoid-acuminate to ovate-acuminate, 2-4 mm long, 1-2 mm broad, the margin entire; flowers in each raceme (3-)5-8(-12), very fragranit, pendent; corolla white, cordate in outline; outer petals (10-)12-16(-20) mm long, 4-5 mm broad, the reflexed portion 3-5 mmn long, the spur (2-) 3-5 (-8) mm long; inner petals (10-)12-15(-18) mm long, the blade (2-)3-3.5(-4) mm broad, the claw linear to linear-elliptic, (5-) 6-8 (-9) mm long; crest prominent, ca. 2 mm in diameter, exceeding the innier petal apices by ca. 2 mm; filaments of each phalange distinct nearly to the base; nectariferous spur terete, short, 0.5-1 mm long, vertically oriented; pollen grains synaperturate to 12-rugate, the exine finely reticulate; stigma 4-horned; style 4-7 mm long; fruit ovoid, taperinlg at both ends, (5-) 9-13 (-17) mm long, 3-6 mmii broad; seeds subreniform, black, lustrous, the testa very obseurely reticulate, an elaiosome present.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, Kingsley R. 1961. Revision of Diccutra (Fumariaceae). Brittonia. 18: 1-57.

description: Rigidly erect glaucous perennial, arising from a stout taproot; stems 1 or more, usually 0.5-1.5 m tall, rarely taller, stout, 1-2.5 cm in diameter at the base, the pith hollow at maturity; leaves sparsely scattered along the stem, more numerous toward the base, usually bipinnately (rarely tripinnately) compound, (10-) 15-30 (-45) cm long, (3-) 5-9 (-16) cm broad; ultimate leaf segments pinnatifid (10-)20-30(-60) mm long, (5-)10-20(-25) mm broad, the lobes oblong-acute; panicle usually at least five times as long as broad; flowers several to ca. 75, erect, with a slightly pungent, somewhat unpleasant odor; bracts lanceolate to ovate, 3-5 mm long, 1-2 mm broad, the margin entire; pedicels rigid, ebracteolate or rarely bracteolate; sepals ovate to cordate or nearly orbicular, (3-) 4-6 (-7) mm long, 2-5 mm broad, the margin entire; corolla golden yellow, cordate-oblong in outline; outer petals (10-) 12-16 (-22) mm long, 2-4 mm broad, the reflexed portion 4-7 mm long, the spurs very shallow; inner petals (8-) 15-17 (-21) mm long, the blade often purple-tipped, 3-5 mm broad, the claw nearly as broad as the blade, confluent with the blade; crest crisped, variable in diameter and exteilt, usually 1-3 mm in diameter, scarcely exceeding the inner petal apices; filaments of each phalange united from the base to shortly below the anthers, occasionally distinct to near the base; nectariferous spur wanting, but a small amount of nectariferous tissue present externally toward the base of the median filament; pollen grains tricolpate or 6-rugate, the aperture membranes conspicuously verrucate, the exine obscurely sculptured to psilate; stigma ca. 3 times as broad as long, 2-horned at the apex; style (4-)5-7(-10) mm long; capsule ovoid, tapering at both ends or rounded at the base, (5-) 15-25 (-32) mm long, 5-8 mm broad; seeds subreniform, 1.5-2.2 mm in diameter, black, dull, the testa densely papillate, an elaiosome wanting.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, Kingsley R. 1961. Revision of Diccutra (Fumariaceae). Brittonia. 18: 1-57.

description: Seapose perennial from a short rootstock bearing small like bulbiets; leaves glaucous beneath, broadly triangular decompouad, (10-) 14-16)(-36) cm long, (4-)6-14(-18) cm broad; petioles (5-) 8-16 (-24) cm long; ultimate leaf segments linear to linear-elliptic or linear-obovate usually minutely apiculate (2-)5-15(-23) mm long, (0.4-) 2-3 (-4.2) mm broad; racemes of (3-) 5-9 (-14) pendent flowers, usually exceeding the leaves; bracts minute; pedicels (2-)4-7(-12) mm long, bibracteolate; sepals broadly ovate, (1.8-)2.2-3.8(-5) mm long, (1.3-)2.4-3.4(-4) mm broad, the margin entire; corolla white, frequently suffused with pink, the petal apices yellow to orange-yellow; outer petals (1-) 12-16 (-20) mm long, the reflexed portionas 2-5 mm long, the spurs (3-)6-10(-13) mm long, divergent, forming with each other an angle of (30-) 85-110 (-125) degrees, inner petals (7.5-)9-12(-14) mm long, the blade (1.8-)2.5-3.5(-4) mm broad, the claw linear, (4-) 5-7 (-8) mm long, less than 1 mm broadT; crest prominient, ca. 2 mm in diameter; filaments of each phalange fused from the base to shortly below the anthers; nectariferous spur terete, (1-) 2-3 (-4.5) mm long; pollen grains synaperturate, occasionally 12-rugate, the exine finely reticulate; stigma 2-horned with 2 lateral papillae; style 2-4 mm long; fruit ovate in outline, tapering at both ends, (7-) 9-13 (-16) mm long, 3-5 mm broad; seeds reniform, ca. 2 mm in diameter, black, lustrous, the testa very obscurely reticulate, an elaiosome present.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, Kingsley R. 1961. Revision of Diccutra (Fumariaceae). Brittonia. 18: 1-57.

description: Scapose perennial from a stout, scaly rhizome; leaves (1-) 3-5 (-10) in number, glaucous beneath, broadly triangular in outline, (10-)20-35(-55) cm long, (5-)10-15(-30) cm broad; petioles (5-)10-20(-40) cm long; ultimate leaf segments lanceolate to oblong or ovate, incised-pinnatifid, (2-)3-4(-5) cm long, (6-)10-20(-35) mm broad; scapes naked, or rarely with a reduced leaf, usually exceeding the leaves, (20-) 30-45 (-65) cm long; panicle of (5-)10-30 (-45) pendent flowers; bracts lanceolate-acuminate, (3-) 4-6 (-11) mm long, 1-2 mm broad, the margin entire; pedicels ebracteolate, rarely bracteolate; sepals cordate-acuminate, (2-)3-5(-8) mm long, (1.5-)2-3(-4) mm broad, the margin entire to obscurely denticulate; corolla rose-purple to pink, rarely white, cordate-ovate in outline; outer petals (15-)20-25(-30) mm long, (3-)4-7(-9) mm broad, the reflexed portion 4-8 mm long, the spur 2-3 mm long; inner petals (15-) 18-22 (-25) mm long, (2-) 3-4 (-5) mm broad, the claw linear-lanceolate, (5-) 7-10 (-14) mm long, 1-2.5 mm broad; crest prominent, 1-3' mm in diameter, exceeding the inner petal apices by 2-3 mm; filaments of each phalange free shortly above the base, united toward the top, the median filament bending to form a loop which lies within the outer petal spur; nectariferous spur wanting, but a small amount of nectariferous tissue present externally toward the base of the median filament; pollen grains tricolpate, the exine reticulate; stigma 2-horned at the apex; style (7-) 9-12 (-14) mm long; fruit oblong to ovate in outline, tapering at both ends, (15-) 18-22 (-27) mm long, ca. 4 mm broad; seeds subreniform, ca. 2 mm in diameter, blaek, lustrous, the testa very finely reticulate, an elaiosome present.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, Kingsley R. 1961. Revision of Diccutra (Fumariaceae). Brittonia. 18: 1-57.

description: Scapose perennial from a stout, horizointal rhizome; leaves glaucous beneath, rarely glaucous on both surfaces, broadly triangular in outline, ternately compound, (15-)25-40(-55) cm long, (8-)12-20(-35) cm broad; petioles (5-)15-30 (-40) cm long; ultimate leaf segments oblong, incised-pinnatifid, the distal segments usually with 3 coarse teeth or lobes at the apices, (1.5-)3-14(-8) cm long, (4-) 10-20 (-50) mm broad; scapes naked, rarely with a reduced leaf, usually exceeding the leaves, (20-) 30-45 (-60) cm long; panicle of (2-) 5-15 (-30) pendent flowers; bracts linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 4-7(-12) mm long, 1-2 mm broad, the margin entire; pedicels 1- to 2-bracteolate or ebracteolate; sepals lanceolate to ovate or suborbicular, (2-)5-6(-7) mm long, 2-3 mm broad, the margin entire to obscurely denticulate; corolla rose-purple to yellow, rarely white, cordate-ovate in outline; outer petals (12-)16-19(-24) mm long, (3-)4-5(-6) mm broad, the reflexed portion 2-4 mm long, the spur 2-3 mm long; inner petals (12-) 15-18 (-22) mm long, the blade 2-4 mm broad, the claw linear-elliptic to linear-lanceolate, (7-) 8-10 (-12) mm long, 1-2 mm broad; crest 1-2 mm in diameter, exceeding the inner petal apices by 1-2 mm; filaments of each phalange united from shortly below the anthers to the base except for 2-3 mm just above the bases where the median filaments are free; nectariferous spur wanting; but nectariferous tissue present throughout the basal free portions of the median filaments; pollen grains 6-rugate, the exine finely reticulate; stigma rhomboidal in outline, 2-horned, with two lateral papillae; style (3-)5-7(-9) mm long; capsule oblong in outline, (15-)20-25(-28) mm long, 4-5 mm broad, surrounded at the base by the persistent corolla; seeds reniform, ca. 2 mm in diameter, black, lustrous, the testa finely reticulate, an elaiosome present.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, Kingsley R. 1961. Revision of Diccutra (Fumariaceae). Brittonia. 18: 1-57.

description: Leaves distinctly glaucous on both surfaces, (15-)20-30(-35) cm long, (5-)10-15(-20) cm broad; petioles (4-)10-15(-25) cm long; ultimate leaf segments (1.5-)2-3(-4) cm long, (4-)10-15(-25) mm broad; scapes naked, (12-) 25-35 (-38) cm long; panicle 2- to 12-flowered; outer petals ochroleucous, rarely yellow, (12-) 14-18 (-21) mm long, (3-) 4-5 (-6) mm broad, the reflexed portion 2-4 mm long, the spur ca. 2 mm long; inner petals white, rose-tipped, (12-)14-18(-21) mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm broad; capsule (12-)15-20(-24) mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Stern, Kingsley R. 1961. Revision of Diccutra (Fumariaceae). Brittonia. 18: 1-57.
