description: Plantae annuae biennesve 4-4.5 dm altae e radice palari omnino glabrae; foliis triangulari-ovatis biternatis vel ternato-pinnatis 3-4 cm latis, divisionibus linearibus acuminatis integris 2-3 cm longis, 1-2 mm latis; petiolis 3-5 cm longis; pedunculis terminalibus 1.5-2.5 dm longis; involucro 0; radiis plerumque 6 (2-4 fertilibus), 1-4 cm longis, valde inaequalibus; involucello 0; pedicellis immaturis 2-10, usque 1 mm longis; calycis dentibus triangularibus persistentibus usque ad 0.3 mm longis; petalis luteolis; stylopodio depresso; stylis tenuibus patentibus usque ad 1 mm longis; carpophoro incognito; fructibus immaturis oblongo-ovalibus 1.25-1.5 mm longis, 0.8-1 mm latis apice truncatis, costis hu- milibus filiformibusque.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1981. Two new Umbelliferae of the Chihuahuan Desert [Aletes calcicola & Donnellsmithia coahuilensis]. Brittonia. 33: 342-346.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Plants annual or biennial, slender, 4-4.5 dm tall from a vertical tuberous tap-root, the stem alternately branched, sparsely leafy, glabrous throughout; leaves triangular-ovate, biternate or ternate-pinnate, 3-4 cm broad, the leaf divisions linear, 2-3 cm long, 1-2 mm broad, acuminate, entire; petioles 3-5 cm long, narrowly sheathing below; cauline leaves alternate, reduced upward; peduncles terminal, 1.5-2.5 dm long; involucre and involucel 0; rays usually 6 (2-4 fertile), very unequal, 1-4 cm long, slightly scarious-webbed at base; immature fertile pedicels 2-10, to 1 mm long; calyx teeth triangular, persistent, to 0.3 mm long; petals light yellow, oblanceolate, 1 mm long, shallowly bifid at apex; stylopodium depressed; styles slender, spreading, ca 1 mm long; carpophore unknown; im- mature fruit oblong-oval, 1.25-1.5 mm long, 0.8-1 mm broad, truncate at apex, rounded at base, the ribs low and filiform.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1981. Two new Umbelliferae of the Chihuahuan Desert [Aletes calcicola & Donnellsmithia coahuilensis]. Brittonia. 33: 342-346.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herba perennis caespitosa; folia succulenta imbricata rosulata, 7-11 mm, late 1-1.7 mm, pilis simplicibus vel ramosis albis obsita glabrescentia; inflorescentiae umbellatae, involucratae, 3-5-florae; bracteae 5-9, ovatae vel ovatolanceolatae; pedunculi 1-6 mm long; corolla rosea, lobis emarginatis vel retusis; chromosomatum numerus n = 18.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1981. New taxa from the Venezueland Guayana. Brittonia. 33: 28-36.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Perennial herbs, cushion- to more often mat-forming, loosely caespitose from a slender tap root; stems prostrate to ascending, minutely pubescent, terminating in rosettes of entire leaves; leaves succulent, oblong to oblanceolate, obtuse to acute, 7-11 mm long, 1-1.7 mm wide, puberulent, becoming glabrous and strongly reflexed in age; inflorescence umbellate, (2) 3-5- (7)-flowered, involucrate; bra cts 5-9, lanceolate to lance-ovate acute to acuminate, 2.5-3.7 (5) mm long, 0.7-1.5 mm wide, with scattered simple white hairs, the margins ciliate; peduncles 1-6 mm long with simple to forked hairs throughout; pedicels 3-7 (10) mm long at anthesis, the length variable within the inflorescence, densely covered with simple to branched white hairs; calyx 4-7 mm long, the lobes 1-2 mm wide, the margins ciliate, the apices acute, the tube 2.4-3 mm with short, simple white hairs at least proximally; corolla salverform, (5) 6-10 (11) mm long, glabrous, the lobes broadly flared, 5-6 mm long, 3-4 mm wide in fresh specimens, 3-5 mm long, 1.8-3 mm wide in pressed ones, the apex emarginate to retuse (entire), the limb pink to magenta, the throat yellow and with 5 fornices, the tube 3.5-6 mm long, exceeding the calyx, lighter in hue than the limb; stamens 5, included; anthers oblong, 0.8- 1.1 mm long, yellow; style 1-1.8 mm long, the stigma small, capitate; capsules ovate, 5-valved, 1.4-2.6 mm long; seeds 1-several per capsule, dark reddish- brown to nearly black, minutely pitted, 0.9-2.5 mm long; n = 18.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1981. New taxa from the Venezueland Guayana. Brittonia. 33: 28-36.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Plants annual, 2-25 cm tall, pubescent throughout with stalked stellate trichomes, rarely glabrous; leaves in a basal rosette or occasionally a few cauline, obovate to oblanceolate with cuneate bases, 0.7-3-(6) cm long, 0.4-1.5-(2) cm broad, usually with 2-5 teeth in the distal half; racemes 1-12, weak, subdecumbent to ascending; pedicels 1-4-(5) mm long, ascending; sepals 0.7-1.2-(1.4) mm long; petals narrowly to broadly spatulate, emarginate, 0.7-2.5 mm long; fruits narrowly to broadly elliptic, rarely oblong, 3-6-(8) mm long, 1.5-3 mm broad, usually distributed over the entire length of the often filiform axis; stigma 0.1-0.3-(0.4) mm long; seeds 12-30, brownish-orange, 0.6-0.7 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Hartman, Ronald L., et al. 1975. Biosystematics of Draba cuneifolia and D. platycarpa (Cruciferae) with emphasis on volatile and flavonoid constitutents. Brittonia. 27: 317-327.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Scapose, cespitose perennial, 5-12 cm tall, with few to many stems from a branched caudex; herbage pubescent throughout, with stalked, 2-4-rayed stellate hairs, the leaf margins not ciliate; scapes erect to ascending, unbranched, arising from the apices of short, leafy, somewhat thicker basal stems; leaves rosulate to merely clustered at the base of the stem, 4-12 mm long, 2-5 mm wide, oblanceolate, sometimes broadly so, the lowermost tapering to a petiolar base, obscurely dentate, the upper (when separated by short internodes) sessile and sometimes shortly auriculate, obtuse to rounded apically, entire; raceme 11-20(27)-flowered, becoming greatly elongated, pubescent throughout with simple and 2-4-rayed hairs; sepals 2-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, obtuse to rounded, scarious-margined, sometimes pubescent; petals 3.7-5.2 mm long, oblanceolate to ob- ovate, not clawed, yellow; fruiting pedicels, the lower 4-9 mm long, divaricately as- cending, more or less straight; fruits 6- 8.5(11) mm long, 2-4.2 mm wide, lanceo- late, not twisted, pubescent with simple, once-forked, and 3- or 4-rayed hairs; ma- ture style 0.4-1.1 mm long; seeds about 1.2-1.5 mm long, flattened; 2n = 26.
bibliographicCitation: Holmgren, Noel H. 2004. A new variety of Draba pedicellata and a lectotype for D. cusickii (Brassicaceae). Brittonia. 56 (2): 107-114.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herbaceous, scapose perennial, 2.5-10 (12) cm tall, from a multicipital caudex; stems glabrous; leaves basal, acute, (3.5) 4.5-10 (15) mm long, (1.5) 2-3.7 (5) mm wide, the trichomes simple and restricted to the margins of the leaves, 0.2-0.6 mm long, 20-32 (35) per leaf; pedicels divaricately ascending; sepals 2.4-3.6 mm long; petals white, (3.8) 4.1-5.9 mm long; stamens 3-4 (4.2) mm long; siliques erect, (4.6) 5.6-9.5 (10) mm long, (1.7) 1.9-3.1 (3.6) mm wide; style (0.7) 0.9-1.9 (2.5) mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Tiehm, Arnold & Holmgren, Patricia K. 1991. A New Variety of Draba oreibata (Brassicaceae) from Nevada, U.S.A. Brittonia. 43 (1): 20-23.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Scapose, cespitose perennial, 2.5-14(20) cm tall, with numerous stems arising from a much-branched caudex; herbage pubescent mostly with stalked, once-forked, and 3- or 4-rayed stellate hairs, the scapes glabrous to sparsely pubescent above; scapes ascending, decumbent, or spreading, un- branched, arising from the apex of the short, leafy, somewhat thicker basal stems; leaves not rosulate, clustered at the base, alternate or sometimes opposite or subopposite, the lowermost 4-15(20) mm long, 2-4(5.7) mm wide, oblong or oblanceolate, sometimes broadly so, obtuse to rounded apically, entire; raceme 3-14-flowered, glabrous or rarely sparsely pubescent with simple or stalked 2-4-rayed hairs; sepals 1.7-2.5(2.8) mm long, oblong to broadly ovate, scarious-margined, glabrous; petals (3)3.5-5.5 mm long, obovate or spatulate, not clawed, yellow; fruiting pedicels, the lower 4-10(15) mm long, divaricately ascending to widely spreading and sometimes slightly reflexed (in var. wheelerensis), straight to curved upward; fruits (4.2)5.3-8(9.5) mm long, 2.2-4.2 mm wide, ovate-elliptic to broadly (ob)lanceolate, not twisted, glabrous to sparsely pubescent with short, simple or branched hairs; mature style 0.4-1.5 mm long; seeds 2-4(6) per locule, 1.3-1.8 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Holmgren, Noel H. 2004. A new variety of Draba pedicellata and a lectotype for D. cusickii (Brassicaceae). Brittonia. 56 (2): 107-114.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Plants annual, 4-30-(37) cm tall, usually simple or occasionally branching from near the base, often with lateral branches from the axils of the abundant cauline leaves, the stems and subinfructescence internodes covered with long, simple and short, branched trichomes; leaves oblanceolate to spatulate, with cuneate bases, 1-4 cm long, 0.5-2.7 cm broad, usually with 2-8 teeth in the distal half, the pu- bescence of stalked, stellate trichomes; racemes 1-15, erect or ascending, often more than half the total plant height; pedicels (3 )-4-9-( 11) mm long, divergent to ascending; sepals 1.4-2.2 mm long; petals (1.7)-3-3.5-(4) mm long, oblanceolate to linear, shallowly to deeply emarginate, often much reduced or absent in flowers of lateral or senescent inflorescences; fruits obovate to elliptic, rounded at the apex, 5-8.5-(9.5) mm long, 2.5-3.7 mm wide, covered with simple trichomes, never glabrous, usually evenly spaced along the axis; styles nearly obsolete to 0.2 mm long; seeds 20-80, dark reddish-brown, 0.6-0.7 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Hartman, Ronald L., et al. 1975. Biosystematics of Draba cuneifolia and D. platycarpa (Cruciferae) with emphasis on volatile and flavonoid constitutents. Brittonia. 27: 317-327.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Scapose, cespitose perennial, 3-8 cm tall, with numerous stems arising from a diffusely branched, elongate, and tangled caudex; herbage pubescent mostly with stalked, once-forked, and 3- or 4-rayed stellate hairs mixed with some simple hairs on the leaf margins (cilia), the scapes glabrous to sparsely pubescent above; scapes decumbent to spreading, unbranched, arising from the apex of short, leafy, somewhat thicker basal stems; leaves not rosulate, more or less clustered at the base of the plant, the lowermost leaves 3-8 mm long, 1.4-3 mm wide, oblong or oblanceolate, obtuse to rounded apically, entire, sometimes upper-most leaves minutely auriculate; raceme 5-12(16)-flowered, glabrous or sparsely pubescent with simple or once-forked hairs; sepals 1.7-2.3 mm long, oblong to broadly ovate, scarious-margined, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; petals 2.7-4 mm long, obovate or spatulate, tapered to the base, not clawed, yellow; fruiting pedicels, the lower 3-8 mm long, divaricately ascending, straight to slightly upcurved; silicles 3.5-7 mm long, 1.5-3.2 mm wide, ovate-elliptic to broadly (ob)lanceolate, partially inflated, not twisted, glabrous to sparsely pubescent with forked or branched hairs; mature style 0.3-1 mm long; seeds 2-4(6) per locule, 1- 1.4 mm long; 2n = 20.
bibliographicCitation: Holmgren, Noel H. 2004. A new variety of Draba pedicellata and a lectotype for D. cusickii (Brassicaceae). Brittonia. 56 (2): 107-114.

description: Perennis, caulibus perennibus patentibus bases foliorum basalium persistentes saepe ferentibus; radix palaris in plantis veterioribus incrassata; folia basalia oblanceolata, integra, 5-30 mm longa, 1-5 mm lata, utrinque stellato-pubescentia; folia caulina (1) 2-3 (5), integra, deminuta, utrinque stellato- pubescentia; caules 1 ad ca 20, 1-10 cm longi, stellato-pubescentes, densissime in inflorescentia; pedicelli ascendentes, 2-8 mm longi, dense stellato-pubescentes; trichomata foliorum, caulium atque pedicellorum brevistipitata, 4 vel interdum 5 radiis aequalibus, saepe tortis, his interdum dichotome ramosis; sepala 2-3 mm longa, 1-2 mm lata, trichomatibus simplicibus, furcatis vel stellatis pubes- centia; petala flava, unguiculata, 3-5 mm longa, 1.5-3 mm lata; styli 0.5-1.2 mm longi; siliquae ellipticae vel ovatae, 3-10 mm longae, 2-4 mm latae, planae vel aliquantum contortae; valvae tri- chomatibus simplicibus vel furcatis pubescentes vel interdum glabrae; semina ca 1.4 (1.1-1.7) mm longa, ca 0.8 (0.6-0.9) mm lata.

description: Perennial, often with spreading perennial stems bearing persistent leaf-bases; taproot thickened with age; basal leaves oblanceolate, entire, 5-30 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, stellate-pubescent on both surfaces; cauline leaves (1) 2-3 (5), entire, reduced in size, stellate-pubescent on both surfaces; stems 1 to ca 20, 1-10 cm long, stellate-pubescent, most densely in the inflorescence; pedicels ascending, 2-8 mm long, densely stellate-pubescent; trichomes of leaves, stems and pedicels short-stalked, with 4 or sometimes 5 equal, often twisted, rays, these sometimes dichotomously branched; sepals 2-3 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, pubescent with simple, forked, or stellate trichomes; petals yellow, clawed, 3-5 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide; styles 0.5-1.2 mm long; siliques elliptic to ovate, plane or somewhat contorted, 3-10 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, with simple or forked trichomes on the valves, or sometimes glabrous; seeds averaging 1.4 (1.1-1.7) mm long by 0.8 (0.6- 0.9) mm wide.

description: Fruit 45 mm diam., pericarp 4-5 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-not clearly similar to any other genus of the Iguanurinae. description: Epiphytic and climbing, or less commonly a terrestrial subshrub to 4 m tall, the shoots mostly horizontal, strongly dorsiventral, the stems glabrescent at base to villous with wine-red trichomes toward the apex, diam. to 8 mm, the internodes 1.5-4 (8) cm long. Leaves strongly anisomorphic, petiolate; blade of the larger leaf in each pair oblanceolate, less commonly obovate or elliptic, 7-22 x 2-10 cm, the base usually oblique, cuneate-acute, the apex acute-acuminate, the margin entire, ciliate and often undulate (possibly only in dried material), the upper surface dull green, pilose-sericeous, the lower surface usually with a purple sheen but not deep purple (and often more purple basally than apically and in younger rather than in older leaves), appressed pilose and pilosevillous along veins; the secondary veins mostly 6 per side; petioles 1-2.5 cm long; blade of the smaller leaf in a pair sessile, ovate, 2-5 x 1.5-3 cm, apex acuminate. Inflorescences in axils of the larger leaf in each pair, of 1 or 2 (4) flowers; bracts 3- 10, lanceolate, 5-15 mm long, apex acute, subentire, purplish, pilose; pedicels to 3 mm long. Calyx purple, pilose to sericeous, the lobes unequal, lanceolate to ovate, the largest 1.5-2.5 x 1-2 cm, the smallest 1-2 X 0.5-1 cm, the apex acute, weakly serrulate to entire; corolla cylindric, 2.5-4.5 cm long, basally dorsally gibbous and 4-9 mm wide, narrowed to 3-5 mm above, widened to 5- 9 mm medially and in throat, red or orange - red, densely villous externally, glabrous in- ternally, the limb subequal, red, lobes rotund, 1.5-3 mm long and 2-4 mm wide at base; filaments 15-25 mm long, connate ca. 3 mm at base, glabrous, the anthers included, coherent, ca. 5 x 1 mm, apparently first dehiscing apically from pores and later splitting longitudinally to 1/2-2/3 of their length; nectary a bilobed gland, ca. 1 mm high; ovary sericeous, the style 12-18 mm long, puberulent particularly toward the apex, the stigma stomatomorphic. Capsule ca. 1.5 cm long, flattened, ca. 1.5 cm wide and ca. 0.5 cm thick, dehiscence not observed but probably with two valves-the seed-mass was seen to be attached to a conspicuous pla- centa similar to the placentas displayed by other species of Drymonia; seeds ellipsoid, ca. 1 x 0.3 mm, smooth, striate, each at- tached to a funiculus.

description: Epiphytic vine-like subshrub; stems woody, slender, 3-5 mm in diameter above, green and glabrous toward the apex, brown below, the internodes to 3 cm long, the nodes prominent. Leaves equal to unequal in a pair; blades ovate or elliptic, 2.3-8.5 cm long, 1.0-3.5 cm wide, membranous, the apex acute to acuminate, the base acute, the margins serrulate, above dark green, strigillose, below lighter green, glabrous; petioles 0.5-2.0 cm long, glabrous, or verrucose on drying. Inflorescences in the upper axils, one-flowered; peduncles lacking; bracts minute, linear, 1-2 mm long; pedicels slender at the base, ca 2 cm long, ca 1.5 mm in diameter, broader toward the apex to 4 or 5 mm wide, glabrous, but strigillose at the apex. Flowers showy; floral tube ca 1 cm in diameter; calyx somewhat oblique, lobes ovate or triangular, 0.8-1.1 cm long, 0.5-0.9 cm wide, erect, except the upper lobe pushed back by the corolla spur, the basal lobes connate for ca 8 mm, the upper and lateral lobes con- nate ca 3 mm, the apex acute, the margins serrate, outside strigose, green and lavender or reddish, inside strigillose; corolla white with a deep red spot in the throat, the tube oblique in the calyx, funnel-form to subcampanulate, 3.0-3.6 cm long, the spur bulbous and fleshy, ca 5 mm long, the tube 6 mm in diameter just above the spur, suddenly larger at the middle and ampliate to ca 1.5 cm in diameter at the throat, outside pilose at the base, becoming strigose above, inside glandular, densely so on upper side, the limb oblique, the lobes rotund, the upper lobes 8 mm long, the lower 1.0 cm long, 1.3 cm wide, the margins crenate to erose; stamens included, the fila- ments broad and fleshy at the base, filiform above, to 1.8 cm long, yellow, glabrous, coiling after pollen release, the anthers sagittate, 4 mm long, 2 mm wide; disc reduced to a single ovate posterior gland; ovary narrowly conic, puberulent, the style curved, ca 1.2 cm long, pilose below, the stigma capitate. Capsule elongate globose, 1.0-1.2 cm long, 0.7-0.9 cm wide, dehiscent by 2 fleshy recurving lavender valves; seeds narrowly filiform, 1 mm long, longitudinally striate, dark reddish brown.

description: Perennial herb from a woody rootstock; stems perennial, wiry, ascending, 10-25 cm long, terete, blackish green, crisped-white puberulent, cystoliths abundant. Leaves shortly petiolate, the petioles 0-2 mm long, shortly puberulent; the blade obovate or, less commonly, narrowly elliptic, obtuse at apex, cuneate at base and ± decurrent onto the petiole, the margin obscurely repand, 1.3-3.2 X 0.5-1.6 cm, shortly puberulent especially on the margins and veins beneath, eventually glabrescent, cystoliths ob- scure, dotlike. Infiorescence of solitary, subsessile flowers in the axils of the uppermost 1-4 leaf pairs, these somewhat distant from each other; pedicels ca. 1 mm long; bracteoles lanceolate, ciliolate, 4 mm long, 1 mm wide; calyx 1.0-1.1 cm long, dull bluish green, united in a tube for 4-5 mm, lobes narrowly triangular-lanceolate, finely acuminate, 5-6 mm long, crisped-pubescent with white multicellular hairs; corolla funnel-shaped, slightly curved, 5-lobed, weakly 2-lipped, 2-2.3 cm long, pubescent outside, the tube whitish brown, narrowly cylindrical from a slightly bulbous base for ca. 5 mm, then abruptly widened to 5-6 mm at mouth, the lobes 7 mm long, 4 mm wide, oblong-obovate, rounded, blue violet; stamens didymous, inserted ca. 10 mm above base of corolla, filaments 6-7 mm long, glabrous above but with a few long spreading hairs below, anthers included, shortly spurred at the base, glabrous, ca. 2 mm long; style 1.4-2 cm long, pubescent, persistent long after the corolla has fallen, ovary glabrous. Capsule oblong, brown, glabrous except for a few short hairs at apex, 10 mm long and 2.5 mm wide, 4- seeded; the seeds ca. 3 X 2.5 mm, lenticular, glabrous.

description: Perennial herb with numerous decumbent or weakly ascending stems arising from a woody rootstock; stems perennial and somewhat woody or, more commonly, plant grazed to the base and stems annual and herbaceous, 5-40(-70) cm long, weakly quadrangular, often somewhat geniculate, densely or sparsely (crisped-) pilose or pubescent, mostly unbranched except at the base. Leaves shortly petiolate, the petioles 1-6 mm long; the blade oblong-elliptic or, less commonly, obovate or oblong, acute at apex, tapering at base, the margin entire or obscurely repand, 1.3-5 X 0.8-2.5 cm, commonly folded especially when young, indumentum very variable with both sur- faces sparsely to densely crisped-pubescent, sometimes X glabrescent, or with spreading hairs on the veins, beneath gland-dotted and with obscure greenish cystoliths making a weblike pattern. Inflorescence of dense, many-flowered, subsessile, bracteate cymes in the axils of the uppermost 3-9(-12) leaf pairs, forming a leafy spike especially when old; bracts variable in size and shape and essentially reduced leaves becoming oblong or narrowly oblanceolate, as small as 6 X 2 mm; calyx 1.3-1.6 cm long, united in a tube for ca. 6 mm, green except for the darker veins that extend as lobes, lobes subulate to a long fine point, pubescent with short crisped hairs and ciliate with spreading white trichomes; corolla funnel-shaped, gradually widened from a slightly bulbous base, 5-lobed, weakly 2-lipped, 2-2.1 cm long, the tube whitish, subglabrous, the lobes 6-7 mm long, broadly oblong, slightly emarginate, pubescent on the exterior, glabrous within, violet; stamens didymous, inserted ca. 10 mm above base of corolla, filaments 2.5 mm long, glabrous, one filament ca. 1.5 mm longer than the other in each pair, anthers equalling corolla mouth or very shortly exserted, shortly spurred at the base, 1.5-2 mm long; style 1.5-1.6 cm long, pilose, persistent long after the corolla has fallen, ovary glabrous. Capsule oblong, brown, glabrous, 9-11 X 2 mm, 4-seeded; the seeds ca. 2.5 mm long, lenticular, compressed, covered in whitish mucilaginous hairs.

description: Perennial herb from a thickened woody base; stems to 90 cm long, possibly ascending in habit, terete, bifariously pubescent with short crisped hairs. Leaves petiolate, the petioles 5-15 mm long, with white multicellular hairs and some scattered stalked glands; the blade oblong-elliptic, acute at apex, tapering at base and attenuate onto the petiole, the margin repand, 2-8 X 1-2.8 cm, pubescent on the margins and veins of both adaxial and abaxial surfaces, eventually ± glabrescent, cystoliths abundant. Inflorescence of reduced cymose clusters of subsessile flowers in the uppermost 3-5 leaf pairs, the clusters very distant and mostly 4-7 cm apart; bracteoles lanceolate, pubes- cent, 2.5 X 1 mm; calyx ca. 1.2 cm long, united in a short tube for 3-4 mm, lobes narrowly lanceolate, finely acuminate, 5-6 mm long, pubescent and shortly ciliate, occasionally with a few longer hairs; corolla funnel-shaped, 5-lobed, weakly 2-lipped, 2.5-2.7 cm long, pubescent outside, the tube pale, narrowly cylindrical from a slightly bulbous base for ca. 8 mm, then abruptly widened to 8 mm at mouth, the lobes 5-6 mm long, 4 mm wide, narrowly obovate, emarginate, pale blue; stamens didymous, inserted ca. 10 mm above base of corolla, filaments 5 mm long, sparsely to densely pubescent, anthers included, shortly spurred at the base, pubescent to subglabrous, ca. 1.75 mm long; style ca. 1.5 cm long, pubescent, persistent long after the corolla has fallen, ovary glabrous. description: Grayish, decumbent herb; stems up to 40 cm. long or more, densely pilose, the hairs up to 1 mm. long, mostly spreading; leaf blades elliptic, up to 1.8 cm. long and 9 mm. wide, rounded or obtusish at apex, narrowed at base and decur- rent on the petiole, entire or subentire, both surfaces densely pilose, the hairs spreading, straight or curved, up to 0.75 mm. long, the costa and lateral veins (4 pairs) distinct but obscured by the heavy pubescence; petioles up to 3 mm. long, pilose; flowers usually solitary, sessile, axillary or terminating short axillary branches and subtended by foliaceous bracts similar to the leaf blades but smaller; calyx up to 14 mm. long, the lobes 7-8 mm. long, 1 mm. wide at base, subulate, carinate, the costa prominent, the margin and outer surface pilose, the hairs spreading, various in length, some as much as 1.5 mm. long, the inner surface minutely strigose; corolla (immature) purple, 15 mm. long, the narrow portion of the tube about 6 mm. long and slightly more than 1 mm. in diameter, glabrous, the expanded portion about 3 mm. broad at mouth (the ovate lobes about 4 mm. long and 3.5 mm. wide), glabrous within, minutely pilose without, the hairs straight, spreading, or the lowermost retrorse; filaments of the. longer pair of stamens 4 mm. long, those of the shorter pair 3.5 mm. long, all glabrous; lower anthers about 1 mm. long and 0.75 mm. wide, the upper ones slightly larger; capsule cylindric, glabrous, 1 cm. long; seed not seen.

description: Low gregarious herb with thickened perennial base with numerous short fibrous roots, ca. 5 cm in length and a few short horizontally spreading rhizomes; stems 10- 20(-30) cm long, prostrate or decumbent, sparsely crisped-puberulent, weakly quadrangular. Leaves subsessile with petioles up to 3 mm long, obovate, the blade obtuse or shortly apiculate at the apex, tapering at the base, margins entire or obscurely repand, 8-15 X 3-6 mm, glabrous or with a few crisped hairs, especially on the margins, gland dotted and with obscure cystoliths beneath. Inflorescence of usually solitary flowers borne in small axillary, subsessile, bracteate cymes in the uppermost 3-5 leaf pairs; bracts variable in size, re- sembling reduced leaves; calyx 10-1 1 mm long, united in a tube for ca. 5 mm, the lobes narrowly lanceolate, acuminate, glabrous or minutely crisped-puberulent, the margin commonly whitish; corolla funnel-shaped, gradually widened from a slightly bulbous base, 5-lobed, weakly 2-lipped, 9- 1 1 mm long, the tube whitish, subglabrous, the lobes ca. 3 mm long, obovate-elliptic, rounded, pale blue, pubescent outside, glabrous within; stamens didymous, inserted ca. 4 mm above base of corolla, one filament ca. 1 mm longer than the other in each pair, glabrous, anthers included and not visible at corolla mouth, shortly spurred at base, glabrous, ca. 1.25 mm long; style ca. 7 mm long, pilose, persistent long after the corolla has fallen, ovary glabrous. description: Perennial herbs 1-1.5 m tall. Stem branched, terete, covered with spreading hairs. Leaves sessile, lanceolate, 2.5-6 cm x 3-15 mm, acute to acuminate, cuneate at base, entire, with scattered hairs on both surfaces; veins 3-4 pairs. Flowers in dense axillary clusters; bracts 6-9 mm long, linear. Calyx 1.5-1.7 cm long, tube ca 8 mm long; lobes lance-attenuate, keeled, ciliate-margined. Corolla reddish-brown (rubiginose), occasionally orange, 3.3-3.4 cm long (the ampliate tube ca 2.1 cm long), upper lip 2- and lower 3-lobed. Stamens 4, in pairs, filaments ca 2.6 cm long, those of a pair united below the middle; anther cells ca 4 mm long, mucronate at base. Style ca 2.6 cm long, pubescent, posterior stigma lobe rudimentary, the anterior lobe oblique. Capsule sessile, oblong, ca 1 cm long, enclosed in the persistent calyx tube, separating with difficulty into 2 valves; seeds 4, ca 5 x 3 mm, suborbicular, hairy, mucilaginous when wetted.

description: Climbing vine. Stems more or less straight, the internodes terete, 5-15 cm long, 3-4 mm thick, smooth; flowering branches 10-60 cm long, not zigzag, the inter- nodes 2-10 cm long, 1.8-3 mm thick, terete, smooth. Leaf blades ovate-lanceolate to lance-elliptic, or ovate to ovate-oval, 4-15 cm long, 1-6 cm wide (stem leaves up to 20 cm long, 15 cm wide), rounded to shallowly emarginate, less often somewhat cuneate-contracted at base, gradually narrowed from 1/3-2/5 above the base to acute or subabruptly acuminate apex, herbaceous to chartaceous, sometimes becoming thinly coriaceous, dull or slightly shiny above; costas 7 or 9, the principal ones 3 or 5, besides which 1 or 2 pairs of very weak marginal nerves are seen, all divided to base, the 3 or 5 principal costas ridged on lower surface, distinct on upper surface, the secondary nervules very fine, irregularly curved upward and divided, the reticulations fine, polygonal, slightly obliquely elongated; petioles 1-3 (in stem leaves up to 4) cm long, 0.8-1.5 mm wide, weakly laterally flattened, channelled on adaxial side, sheathing to 3-7 mm from base with narrow membranous greenish wings 0.5-1 mm wide; tendrils 0 to 3 cm long on branch leaves, 10-30 cm long on stem leaves. Umbels of both sexes solitary at leaf axils of flowering branches, the staminate ones 15-45 mm across, 15-55 (80)-flowered, borne at basal 3 to almost all nodes of branches, the pistillate ones 10-17 mm across, 15-30-flowered, at 2 to 4 basal nodes, the lowest 1 to 3 leaves subtending umbels of 10 flowers reduced to an ovate brownish scale 3 to 5 mm long; peduncles 1-6 cm long, 0.5-1.2 mm wide, obcompressed, non-prophyllate at base; receptacles of both sexes depressed-globose, 3-4 mm across, bracteoles ovate, ca 1/2 mm long. Staminate perianth on filiform rays, 5-17 mm long, obovate-fusiform, white (ex Thavorn), 4.75-6 mm long, broadest above the middle, 2-2.25 mm wide, gradually attenuate to base, contracted at 3-toothed apex, the teeth deltoid, subobtuse, 0.3-0.6 mm long. Stamens 3, monadelphous, as long as the perianth; anthers ovate-elliptic, (1.4) 1.8-2 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, the brownish connective projecting into an appendage ca 0.2 mm long; filaments fused for the entire length forming a column 3-4 mm long by 0.3-0.5 mm. Pistillate perianth on 3-4 mm long slender rays, ovoid-ellipsoid to ellipsoid, 2.5 mm long, 1.8 mm wide, rounded at base, contracted to 3-toothed apex, the teeth deltoid-obtuse, 0.3-0.5 mm high; ovary ovoid, 2.5 mm long, 1.4 mm wide, gradually narrowed to 3 recurved stigmas ca 0.3 mm long; staminodes 3, needle-like, 0.6-0.9 mm long. Fruiting umbel rays 8-20 mm long; berries globose to depressed-globose, 7-10 mm across, 6-7 mm high dark green (ex Ramos & Endafio, and Mamit).

description: Woody climber. Stems to 1.5 m long, 2-4 mm thick, the stems and branches pubescent, eventually glabrescent, terete, unarmed or rarely bristly; flowering branches 10-30 cm long, not zigzag, the internodes 1-4 cm long, 0.8-1.5 mm thick, subterete or angular. Leaf blades glabrous, lance-oblong or lance-ovate, 3.5- 16 cm long, 1-6 cm wide, rounded or cuneate-contracted at base, gradually ta- pering from 1/3_2/5 from base to acute or acuminate apex, subcoriaceous, slightly shiny above, the nerved margins weakly undulate; costas 7, of which the 2 marginal pairs close together along margins, the 3 main costas convex on lower surfaces, pronounced on upper surface, the secondary nervules obliquely ascending, ? straight, distinct, the reticulations fine, dense, transversely elongated; petioles 5- 25 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, obtuse on back, ventrally canaliculate, puberulent toward base, sheathing for 2-5 mm from base with herbaceous, puberulent often brownish-tinged wings ca 0.5 mm wide; tendrils on stem leaves up to 20 cm long, those of branch leaves vestigial to 3 cm long. Umbels of both sexes solitary at basal 2-6 leaf axils of flowering branches, 15-25 mm across, 10-27-flowered, the lowest 1 or 2 of those subtending leaves frequently reduced to an ovate, mem- branous, brown scale 3-6 mm long; peduncles 0.5-3 cm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, obcompressed, puberulent, non-prophyllate at base; receptacles 2-3 mm across; bracteoles ovate-acute, ca 0.3 mm long. Staminate perianth oblong-ellipsoidal, 5-6 mm long, 1.5-1.8 mm wide, tapering to both ends, the apex 3-toothed, the teeth lanceolate, acute, 0.8-1 mm long. Stamens 3; filaments 2 mm long, fused to half way up; anthers 1 mm long, ovate. Pistillate perianth ovoidal, 3-3.8 mm long, 1.8-2 mm wide, membranous red-brown, rounded to base, narrowed to 3- lobed apex, the lobes lanceolate, acute, 1 mm long, patent; ovary ovoidal, 2.8- 3.5 mm long, exposing stigmas above the base of perianth lobes, 1.8-2 mm wide; stigmas of 3-lobed annular disc. Staminodes 3, needle-like, compressed, 1-1.2 mm long. Berries depressed-globose, 5-7 mm high, 7-10 mm across, 1- to 4- seeded, maturing dark green (ex Wang & Tang) or red (ex Tsang).

description: Climber. Stems apparently herbaceous, terete, glabrous, smooth, laxly branched above, the internodes 5-25 cm long, 2-4 mm thick. Leaf blades orbicular-cordate to ovate-orbicular, sometimes ovate or ovate-elliptic, 7-25 cm long, 3-20 cm wide, rounded or shallowly cordate at base, subabruptly contracted to acuminate at apex, thinly herbaceous to membranous; costas 5 or 7 including a slender marginal pair, separate from the base, prominent on upper surface, highly elevated with narrow wing-like edge on lower surface, lateral nervules slender, close to- gether, obliquely ascending, forming fine distinct and obliquely elongate reticu- lations; petioles 15-40 mm long, few-costate, laterally weakly compressed with acute abaxial angle, sheathing for 3-7 mm, the wings nearly wanting; tendrils to 25 cm long. Umbels borne at lower few nodes of branches, both sexes 20-30- flowered; peduncles strongly flattened, 0.5-4 cm long; receptacles 4-8 mm thick; rays 1-1.3 cm long. Staminate perianth clavate, 7-9 mm long, attenuate to base, abruptly contracted at mucronate and 3-toothed apex, the teeth deltoid-acute, ca 0.3 mm long. Stamens 3; filaments connate to 1/3 or 1/2 way; anthers ovate, 1 mm long. Pistillate flowers not known. Berries globose to depressed-globose, 7-1 1 mm across, black at maturity, 1- to 3-seeded.

description: Climbing vine. Stems terete, rigid, smooth, the internodes 5-15 (25) cm long, 2-4 (7) mm thick; branches slender, subterete or distally somewhat angular, often zigzag, the internodes 3-12 cm long, 2-4 mm thick. Leaf blades ovate to ovate- orbicular or ovate-cordate, 4-15 cm long, 3-13 cm wide, rounded to subcordate at base, contracted above to acute or suddenly cuspidate apex, herbaceous to chartaceous, occasionally eventually subcoriaceous, not glaucous beneath; costas 7 including 2 weak outer pairs, all divided to base, the 3 median costas sharply ridged on lower surface, distinct above, the secondary nervules obliquely curved- ascending, distinct, the reticulations dense and fine, obliquely elongated; petioles 1-4 cm long, laterally flattened with acute dorsal angle, ventrally deeply chan- nelled, sheathing for 3-7 mm from base, the wings membranous, ca 0.5 mm wide, often tinged with red-brown; tendrils 5-15 cm long. Umbels solitary at 2 to several leaf axils of branches and distal part of stem; peduncles obcompressed, 1-5 cm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, non-prophyllate at base. Staminate umbels densely 15-50- flowered, the receptacles 2-3 mm across, the rays capillary, often flexuous, 5-20 mm long. Pistillate umbels 5-25-flowered, the receptacles 2-5 mm across, rarely elongated and bearing several flowers in somewhat corymbose manner, the rays 1-2 cm long. Staminate perianth ovoid-ellipsoid to ellipsoid, 4-4.5 mm long, 2- 3 mm wide, contracted at base, subobtuse to subacute at 3-toothed apex, reddish- purple at anthesis, the teeth deltoid, 0.3 mm long. Stamens 3, monadelphous with filaments connate their whole length, forming a column 2.5-3 mm long; anthers ovate, subobtuse, 1 mm long, 0.7 mm wide. Pistillate perianth ovoid-ellipsoid, 3.75-4 mm long, 2.2-2.5 mm wide, rounded-truncate at base, tapering above to 3-toothed apex, the teeth deltoid, 0.3 mm long. Ovary ovoid, 3 mm long, attenuate above to 3-lobed stigma ca 0.3 mm long. Staminodes 5 or 6, needle-like 1.5-1.75 mm long. Berries globose, 8-10 mm across, purple-black, 1-4-seeded.

description: Climbing vine. Stems 2-7 m long, the internodes terete, glabrous smooth, 2-16 cm long, 2-7 mm thick; branches 10-50 cm long, mostly not zigzag, the internodes 2-8 cm long, 1.5-3 mm thick. Leaf blades very variable in shape and size, mostly ovate to broadly ovate or ovate-oval, rather frequently ovate-lanceolate, less frequently ovate-orbicular, (3) 5-17 (22) cm long, (0.7) 2-12 (16) cm wide, usually cordate to emarginate, less often rounded or rounded-truncate, rarely cuneate at base, gradually narrowed from ca 1/3 above the base to acute or acuminate apex, mostly chartaceous to herbaceous, frequently thinly coriaceous, rarely membranous or coriaceous; costas 5 or 7, besides these a pair of slender marginal veins stretching half way up, all divided to base, the main 3 or 5 costas elevated on lower surface, distinct on upper surface, the secondary nervules di- vergent, sometimes branched, the reticulations fine, dense, transversely elongated; petioles 1.5-4 cm long, 0.7-3 mm thick, subterete to laterally compressed, obtuse or acute on back, channelled ventrally, sheathing for 3-8 mm from base with herbaceous, often brownish-tinged wings 0.5-1.2 mm wide; tendrils vestigial to 7 cm long on branch leaves, up to 20 cm long on stem leaves. Umbels of both sexes solitary at 3-12 lower leaf axils of flowering branches, 10-30 (40)-flowered, 1.5-3.5 cm across at anthesis; peduncles 1-5 cm long, rarely subsessile, obcom- pressed, 1-2 mm wide, non-prophyllate at base; receptacles depressed-globular, 2.5-4 mm across; bracteoles ovate, 0.5 mm long; rays 8-1 5 mm long, the staminate filiform, somewhat flexuose, the pistillate slightly thicker, + straight. Staminate perianth obovoid or obovoid-ellipsoid, 4.5-6.5 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, attenuate to base, contracted at 3-toothed apex, the teeth deltoid, acutish, 0.4-0.9 mm long. Stamens 3, rarely 2 or 4; filaments 2.5-4 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, fused to 1/3-2/5 from base; anthers ovate-orbicular, 0.7-1 mm long, apiculate with brownish connective. Pistillate perianth globose or ovoid-globose, 2.5-3.5 mm long, 2.7-3.2 mm across, rounded at base, rounded-mucronate at apex with three deltoid-acutish teeth ca 1/3 mm long; ovary ovoid-globose, 2.2-2.5 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide; stigmas 3, minute, erect, 0.2 mm long. Staminodes 3 (rarely up to 6), needle-like, 1-2 mm long. Berries on 1.5-3 cm-long wiry pedicel, globose to depressed-globose, apiculate, 6-10 mm high, 6-15 mm in diameter, maturing purple-black, 1-6-seeded. Chromosomes 2n = 62 (Sato, 1942).

description: Conspicue recedit ab H. gaudichaudiana floribus masculis atque foemineis dimidio brevioribus, perianthio masculo ovato-oblongo apice haudo denticulato. Liana caule usque 2 m longo. Umbellae d et 9 6-15-florae 7-20 mm diametro pedunculo 8-35 mm longo, radiis 6-12 mm longis. Perianthia 6 ovato-oblonga circa 3 mm longa 1.5 mm lata apice obtusotruncata; stamina 3 monadelpha. Perianthia 9 ovoideo-globosa 2.2-2.5 mm longa circa 2 mm lata apice ore 3-denticulato acuminata.

description: Scandent climber. Stems up to 2 m long (ex Lau), the internodes terete, 5-11 cm long, 2-4 mm thick, smooth, glabrous; flowering branches 6-40 cm long, the internodes obtusely angular, smooth, 1-6 cm long, 0.5-1.5 mm thick, the leaves on the flowering branches reduced to scales or the distal few bearing a small ovate blade. Leaf blades ovate-lanceolate or ovate, rarely ovate-orbicular, (2) 4-15 cm long, (0.7) 1.5-10 (13) cm wide, acute or subabruptly acuminate at apex, rounded to emarginate-truncate rarely cuneate or cordate at base, herbaceous or chartaceous, sometimes eventually subcoriaceous; costas (5 or) 7, of which the 3 median sufficiently ridged on lower surfaces, the remaining slender and placed near the margins, secondary nervules very slender, curved-ascending, forming dense trans- versely elongated reticulations; petioles 1-4 cm long, 0.3-2 mm wide, slightly laterally flattened, adaxially canaliculate, the base forming a sheath of 2-5 mm in length with membranous and often brown-tinged wings 0.2-0.5 mm wide; tendrils 2-15 cm long. Umbels of both sexes arising from basal 3 to 12 nodes of flowering branches, single at nodes, each 6-15-flowered, 7-20 mm across; pe- duncles 8-35 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, obcompressed, non-prophyllate at base, subtended by a scale; receptacles hemispherical, 2-4 mm across; bracteoles ovate- acute, membranous, fuscous, 0.8 mm long; rays 6-12 mm long. Staminate peri- anths ovate-oblong, 3.2-3.5 mm long, 1.5-1.7 mm wide, orange-red (ex Lau), contracted at base, hardly narrowed at obtusely-truncate apex, the orifice scarcely toothed. Stamens 3, monadelphous; filaments connate forming a column 3 mm long by 0.3 mm wide; anthers ovate-orbicular, 0.5 mm long, obtuse at apex. Pistillate perianths ovoid-globose, 2.2-2.5 mm long, 2-2.2 mm wide, pale-green (ex Lau), rounded at base, apiculate at 3-toothed apex, the teeth deltoid-acute, 0.2-0.3 mm long. Ovary broadly ovoid, 2.2 mm long, 2 mm wide, rounded at base, contracted to apex; stigmas 3 erect, 0.3 mm long. Staminodes 6, setaceous, 0.7-1.2 mm long. Berries globose or depressed-globose, first dirty red (ex How) then turning blackish (ex How & Chun), 8-15 mm in diameter, 7-10 mm long; seeds 1-4.

description: Herbaceous vine. Stems slender but rigid, 2-4 m long, subdensely branched above, terete, glabrous, smooth, occasionally striate, the internodes (3) 5-10 cm long, 2-3 mm thick. Leaf blades variable, those of main stems ovate to broadly ovate, 10-20 cm long, 6-13 cm wide, rounded or cordate at base; those of flowering branches ovate to lance-ovate or lance-elliptic, 5-13 cm long, 1.5-8 cm wide, cuneate to rounded at base, gradually narrowed to acute or subacute and cuspidate apex, thinly coriaceous, often more or less shiny on both surfaces, sometimes more or less white-thickened on margins; costas 7 including 2 slender marginal pairs, all divided at base, the median 3 costas sharply ridged on lower surface, often becoming winglike toward the base, somewhat depressed on upper surface, lateral nervules slender but distinct, forming very fine reticulations; petioles 1.5- 3 (on stem leaves up to 7) cm long, laterally compressed with 3 or 5 sharp angles, those often with narrowly (0.5-0.7 m) winged edges, the sheath less than 5 mm long, the wings ca 1 mm wide with membranous margins, not auriculate at apex; tendrils 7-13 cm long. Flowering branches borne at leaf-axils of distal part of stem 15-30 cm long, bearing 4-7 umbels, the leaves on flowering branches perfect, with blades up to 10 cm by 3 cm or all or some reduced to ovate bracts 3-7 mm long; tendrils vestigial on flowering leaves. Umbels solitary at non-prophyllate nodes of flowering branches; peduncles of both sexes 2-4 cm long, flattened, 1.5- 2 mm wide; staminate umbels 2.5-3 cm across, densely 25-60-flowered, the receptacle 2-3 mm across, the rays filiform 1-1.5 cm long; pistillate umbels 18- 35-flowered, the receptacle 3-4 mm across, the rays 1-2 cm long. Staminate perianth ellipsoidal rather suddenly narrowed at base, rounded at apex, 2.5-3 mm long, 2 cm across, only obscurely 3-toothed at apex. Stamens 3; filaments 0.7-1 mm long, connate at base to half way up; anther ovate, 1.5 mm long, 1 mm wide, apiculate at apex. Pistillate flowers not known. Berries (immature) globose.

description: Herbaceous climber. Stems rather rigid, 3-5 m long, slender, smooth rather densely branching above, the internodes 3-10 cm long, 0.7-1.5 mm thick, terete; branches 10-30 cm long. Leaf-blades lance-elliptic to lanceolate, or lance-ovate, 5-13 cm long, 1.5-6 cm wide, shallowly cordate to rounded at base, gradually tapering above to acute apex, herbaceous, thin; costas 5 or 7 including a slender marginal pair, all separate from the base, sharply raised on lower surface, slender but conspicuous on upper surface, lateral nervules divergent ascending, very slen- der, forming fine and transversely elongated reticulations; petioles 8-25 mm long, slender, subterete to weakly laterally compressed, the sheath 2-5 mm long with wings 0.6 mm wide, herbaceous, not auriculate at apex; tendrils slender, 7-15 cm long. Umbels solitary at 1 or 2 basal nodes of branches, both sexes 10-22-flowered; peduncles 3-10 cm long, slender; receptacles 1.5-2 mm across; rays 5-10 mm long at anthesis. Staminate perianth ovoid to narrowly ovoid, 4.5-6 mm long, 2- 3 mm wide, contracted at base, gradually tapering from above the base to obtuse apex, open with small 6-toothed orifice, the teeth ovate-obtuse, the 3 larger ones ca 0.5 mm long, about twice as long as the 3 smaller ones. Stamens 9-12, monadelphous; column of filaments 0.8-1 mm long; anthers linear-oblong, 0.8-1 mm long. Pistillate perianth broadly ellipsoid, 2.8-3 mm long, 2-2.25 mm wide, obtuse at both ends, the apex open with 6-toothed orifice, the teeth depressed-triangular, the 3 larger teeth ca 0.3 mm long, slightly larger than the 3 smaller ones. Ovary ovoid-globose, 2.5 mm long, 2 mm wide; stigmas 3, 0.5 mm long, recurved. Staminodes 3 (or 4), 1 mm long, needle-like. Fruits not known.

description: Climbing herbaceous vine. Stems to 3 m long, subterete, 4-7 mm thick below, glabrous, smooth; branches 20-30 cm long, more or less straight, the internodes 2-6 cm long, 1-2 mm thick, angular. Leaf blades ovate to broadly ovate, 5-15 (25 ex Hayata) cm long, 3-8 (18 ex Hayata) cm wide, rounded-truncate to shallowly emarginate at base, acute at apex, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, dull on both sides; costas 7, 3 prominent, convex on lower surface, 2 marginal pairs much weaker and the marginal pair reaching ca 2/3 from base, the secondary nervules divergent, the reticulations fine, polygonal, not markedly elongated; petioles 1-2 (3) cm long, subterete, 1-channelled on adaxial side, sheathing at base for 3-5 (7) mm with very narrow membranous wings; tendrils 1-12 cm long. Staminate umbels solitary at the axil of all leaves of flowering branches and on the distal part of stem, 1-2 cm across, densely 17-55-flowered; peduncles 2-7 cm long, obcompressed, non-prophyllate at base; receptacles 1.5-2 mm wide; rays 5-8 mm long. Staminate perianth ellipsoidal, 2.5-3 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, terete, mi- nutely 3-toothed at obtuse apex, the teeth 1/4 mm long, deltoid-obtuse. Stamens 9; anthers free, lance-ovate, 0.8-1 mm long; filaments 2-2.5 mm long, united through half their length. Pistillate flowers and fruits thus far not known.

description: Scandent to climbing vine. Stem 2-5 m long, terete, smooth, not zigzag, the internodes 5-15 cm long, 3-6 mm thick; flowering branches 15-60 cm long, more or less straight to weakly zigzag, weakly angular, smooth, unarmed, the internodes 1 . 5-8 cm long, 1-4 mm thick. Leaf blades ovate to ovate-orbicular, rarely broadly elliptic, (3) 5-16 cm long in branch leaves, up to 20 cm long in stem leaves, 2-12 cm wide in branch leaves, up to 17 cm wide in stem leaves, rounded-truncate to shallowly emarginate or cordate at base, contracted or rounded at acuminate apex, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, pale-greenish but not glaucous beneath; costas 9 including 2 slender marginal pairs, all divided to base, the 5 median ones pronounced, ridged on lower surface, distinct on upper surface, the secondary nervules slender, divergent, the reticulations dense and fine, slightly transversely elongated; petioles 1-3 cm long on branch leaves, up to 8 cm on stem leaves, weakly angular, obtuse on back, ventrally channelled, sheathing for 3-5 mm (to 10 mm on stem leaves) from base, the wings 0.7-1.2 mm wide, herbaceous, often tinged with light brown; tendrils vestigial to 5 cm long on branch leaves, up to 15 cm on stem leaves. Umbels of both sexes solitary, borne at 4-7 lower leaf axils of flowering branches, 2-4 cm across, densely 20-70-flowered; peduncles 1-3 cm long, obcompressed, 1.5-2.2 mm wide, non-prophyllate at base; receptacles 3-5 mm across; rays 10-18 mm long. Staminate perianth ellipsoidal or narrowly so, terete, subacute at base, abruptly narrowed above to 3-toothed at apex, 5.7-7.2 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide, broadest in middle, the teeth deltoid or depressed- deltoid, 0.3-0.5 mm long. Stamens as a rule 9 (rarely 7 or 8, as many as 12 according to Wang & Tang, 1978); filaments 3-4.5 mm long, fused for 1.2 to 2.8 mm from base forming a synandrium, upper part free, or occasionally the filaments of 3 central stamens fused for the total length and bearing vestigial anthers; anthers oblong-ovate, 1-1.2 mm long, bearing brownish connective ending in a subulate appendage. Pistillate perianth ovoid-globose, 3.8-4 mm long, 2.6-3 mm wide, rounded at base, suddenly contracted at 3-toothed apex, the teeth deltoid, acutish, 0.5 mm long. Ovary ovoid-globose, 3.2-3.5 mm long, 1.9-3 mm wide, rounded at base, contracted at apex bearing 3 recurved stigmas 0.25 mm long. Staminodes 3-6, needle-like, ca 1/2 as long as ovary. Berries globose or depressed-globose, 6- 9 mm high, 7-13 mm in diameter, maturing purplish, 1-4-seeded.

description: Well-branched vine. Stems slender, the internodes weakly angular or terete, smooth, unarmed, 2-6 cm long, 1.5-2.5 mm thick; flowering branches 7-15 cm long, only weakly zigzag, the internodes 1-3 cm long, ca 1 mm thick. Leaf blades ovate to broadly ovate, 2.5-5.5 cm long, (1) 1.5-3.8 cm wide, rounded or shallowly cordate at base, acute at apex, herbaceous to chartaceous; costas 5 or 7 and in addition a weak marginal pair reaching half way along the margins, all divergent from very base, ridged on lower surface, slender but distinct on upper surface, the secondary nervules obliquely divergent, the reticulations fine and dense; pet- ioles 8-20 mm long, rounded on back, ventrally shallowly furrowed, sheathing for 3-6 mm from base with membranous, brownish wings 0.3-0.6 mm wide, jointed with the blade at very apex; tendrils filiform, 2-4 cm long. Staminate umbels 5-9-flowered, borne at two (rarely 3) basal leaf axils on flowering branches, the lowest leaf subtending the umbel reduced to a brownish, ovate bract; peduncles 5-10 mm long, weakly obcompressed, slender; receptacles 1-1.5 mm wide, the bracteoles depressed-deltoid, mucronulate, brownish; rays 2-8, 10-12 mm long, filiform. Staminate perianth narrowly ellipsoidal to narrowly obovoidal, (6) 6.5- 9 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm across, dark reddish-brownish in dried specimens, at- tenuate to base, contracted to apiculate and minutely 6-toothed apex, the teeth deltoid, ca 0.25 mm long. Staminal column fusiform-cylindrical, 5.5-6 mm long, 1.5-1.8 mm wide at dilated apex, gradually attenuate to base; anthers 6 (or 9, ex Gagnepain), sessile, ovate-deltoid, 1-1.5 mm long, cream-white. Pistillate flowers and fruits thus far not known.

description: Stems cylindroid, decumbent, forming clumps of 30-100, apical erect part of stem pale green, 19 (11-24) cm high, 5.5 (4.5-7) cm in diameter; ribs 8 (7-10) deeply tuberculate with large, flat, triangular tubercles; areoles 2.8 (1.8-4.2) cm apart on the rib on the peaks of the tubercles; spines 8 or 9 (6-11) in a cluster, the number varying even on the same stem, frequently curved or twisted; central spine rhomboidal to nearly triangular in cross section, often grooved along the length, frequently splitting down the groove when old, 3.4-7.8 cm long, 0.9-1.4 mm in diameter at the base, porrect or curved downward, slate-blue with red-brown tip when young, bleach- ing to bone-white with age, always opaque; radial spines, upper 2-0 more or less like the central in shape, size and color, often becoming subcentral; other radials more or less terete, 1.3-3.8 cm long, opaque, white, rarely translucent, with or without brown tips; clusters and individual spines tending to abscise from the lower parts of the stem; flowers blooming from May through June, 5-6.5 cm long; pericarpel cone- shaped with the narrow end at the base, 1.5-2.5 cm long at anthesis; bracts on the pericarpel 24-35, on the floral tube 10-15, becoming up to 1.5 cm long at the top of the tube; pericarpel spines 1 to 10 mm long, in tufts, very small or missing on the lower part, tube spines in fans or tufts, up to 2.2 cm long at the top of the tube; tepals 20-25 often irregular in arrangement, the first 2 series sepaloid, 1.5-3 cm long, the last 2 series (occasionally 3) petaloid, phlox- to mallow-purple, 2.5-3.5 cm long, 0.8-1.6 cm wide; compared with E. stramineus and E. enneacanthus the fewer petals give the flowers of E. dubius a sparse or underdeveloped appearance; stamens 800-1,500; filaments greenish, sometimes tinged with pink, style 2-2.6 cm long, stigma-lobes 8 (6-10), ovules 1,000-1,500; fruit oval to globose 2.5-3.8 cm long, greenish or pinkish, white-fleshed, sweet, insipid; seeds 1.2-1.4 mm long, tubercles more or less confluent.

description: Stems cylindroid, decumbent forming clumps of 30-200 (rarely more), the apical erect portion dull green 17.5 (9-25) cm high, 4 (3.5-5.5) cm wide, ribs 8 or 9 (7- 10), smooth or shallowly tuberculate, areoles 1.6 (0.9-2.4) cm apart on the rib; spines 8-14, straight, translucent, central spine porrect (rarely curved downward), 1.2-4.8 cm long, 0.5-1.4 mm in diameter at the base, radial spines 0.6-3.4 cm long, lateral radial spines 4, shorter than the others, in two opposite pairs, central and upper radial spines often brown, the other spines white, often tipped with tan or brown; flowers blooming from April to early June, usually 6 (5.4-7) cm long, pericarpel nearly orbicular, 1.4-2.2 cm long at anthesis, bracts on the pericarpel 30-35, on the floral tube 15, becoming up to 1.5 cm long at top of the tube, pericarpel spines 8-15 in circular clusters, 2-16 mm long, the 1 to 3 central spines sometimes tan to brown, tube spines 6-2, in tufts or fans, up to 2 cm long at the top of the tube; tepals 25-30, the first two series 1.5-3 cm long, sepaloid, the last 3 (occasionally 4) series petaloid, yellow tinged at the base, true- or phlox-purple above, 2.6-5.5 cm long, 1.2-1.8 cm wide, stamens 800 to 1,500, filaments daphne-pink appearing crimson collectively, style 1.8-2.4 cm long, stigma lobes 8 to 10, ovules 1,500-3,000; fruit nearly globular, 2-2.5 cm in diameter, dark red, pink-fleshed, strawberry-flavored; seeds 1-1.3 mm long, tubercles uneven, sometimes more or less confluent.

description: Stems only slightly decumbent, broadly cone-shaped, forming hemispheroid mounds of 20 to 200 (or more); the apical, erect part of the stem light green, 15.5 (12-22) cm high, 5.5 (4.5-6) cm in diameter; ribs 11-13, smooth or shallowly tuberculate; areoles 1.6 (1.1-1.8) cm apart on the rib; spines 9 or 10 (8-11) in a cluster, straight or only slightly curved, central spine 3.6-6 cm long, sometimes longer, terete, 0.6-0.9 mm in diameter at the base above the bulb, sometimes splitting down the center when old, translucent, straw-colored fading to whitish and having a horny appearance at maturity, radial spines, the upper 2, sometimes 3, usually more or less like the central in shape, size, and color, often becoming subcentral, but rarely central, other radial spines short, 1.5-2.5 cm long, translucent, white, terete, usually arranged as 4 laterals and 2 or 3 lower radials, one lower radial sometimes longer than the others, approaching the central in length but not in color or thickness; flowers blooming from MIay through June, 8.5 (7.5-10) cm long, pericarpel oval, 2.5-3.5 cm long at anthesis, bracts on the pericarpel 35-45, on the floral tube 15-20 becoming up to 2 cm long at the top of the tube, pericarpel spines 4-10 mm long, in semi-circular clusters, tube spines in fans, up to 2.5 cm long at the top of the tube, tepals 25-30, first 2 series sepaloid 2-3.5 cm long, the last 3 or 4 series petaloid, phlox-purple, 3-4.5 cm long, 1.5-2 cm wide, stamens 1,200-1,800, filaments yellow-white, rarely pinkish, style 2.5-3 cm, stigma-lobes 11-12, ovules 3,000-4,000; fruit oval, 3.5-5 cm long, dark red, pink- or red-fleshed and strawberry-flavored; seeds 1.2-1.4 mm long, prominently and evenly tuberculate.

description: Liana, the branchlets brownish, often rugose; petioles nigrescent, 4-7 mm. lonig, the leaf-blades chartaceous, brownish when dried, shining above, narrowly elliptic or slightly obovate, 6-9 cm. long, 1.7-3.5 cm. broad, acute or attenuate at base, obtusely short-acuminate at apex (acumen 4-7 mm. long), conspicuously sserrate especially distally at mlargins (serrations 3-5 per centimeter), the costa raised or subpromi- nent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 7-9 per side, erecto-patent, arcuate and obseurely anastomosing lnear margins, prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces or niearly plane above; inflorescence axillary, 1.5-4.5 cm. long, 4-6-times branched, the pedulncle 6-20 mm. long, the rachis inconspicuous, the branches copiously divided, the bracts oblong-ovate, acute, 1-2 mm. long; flowers 1.5-1.7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, 1-2 mm. long; sepals thin-carnose, serniorbicular-ovate, 0.5-0.7 mm. long and broad, subentire or erosulous at margins; petals elliptic- or orbicular-oblong, 0.6-1 mm. long alnd nearly as broad, entire; disk 0.5-0.7 mm. in diameter, 0.1-0.2 mm. high, entire alnd often thickened at margin; filaments 0.2-0.3 mm. long, the anthers about 0.2 by 0.3 1171m.; ovary depressed-trigonous, the style inconspicuous, the stigmas often obscure; ovules 4 (or 2 ?) per locule, 2-ranked; fruiting pedicels hardly exceeding 1 mm. in diameter, the fruits apparently 3-6 per infloreseence, the capsules broadly elliptic or obovate, 2.5-3 cm. long, 3-4 cm. broad, about 3 mm. thick, rounded or faintly emarginate at apex, the pericarp thin-coriaceous (about 0.4 mm. thick), conlspicu- ously flabellate-costate without (nerves prominulous), smooth within, the opposite surfaces often coherent distally; seeds 2-4, broadly imbricate, the embryoniferous portion obovate, 10-12 mm. long, 6-7 mm. broad, the basal winig thin-coriaceous or papyraceous, oblong, 3-4 mm. lonig, greatly expanded on the ininer edge of the embryoniiferous portion into a broad oblong membranous lateral flange (15-19 mm. long, 10-13 mm. broad, rounded, enerved).

description: Liana (or slender tree with scandent branches), the branchlets cinereous or purplish; petioles 3-9 mm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceous, brownish when dried, often shining above, elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 5-12 (occasionally 4-16) cm. long, 2-5(occasionally 1.5-8) cm. broad, acute to rounded at base, gradually short-acuminate or cuspi- date at apex (acumen 3-10 mm. long, obtuse or subacute), entire or crenate-undulate at margins (undulations about 1 per centimeter), the costa prominllent oln both surfaces, the secondary nerves 4-7 per side, spreading or ascending, arcuate and inconspicuously anastomos- ing near margins, faintly prominulous or plane above, promiinulous beneath, the veinlets copiously reticulate, nearly plane above, prominu- lous beneath; inflorescences solitary or aggregated in clusters of 2-4, 2-11 (-16) cm. long, 4-8-times bralnched, the peduncle up to 3 cm. long, continued into a straight rachis, the branches paired at 2-4 nodes along rachis, distally bearing 2-4 shorter sharply divaricate copiously divided branchlets, the bracts thin-coriaceous, ovate, less than 1 mm. long, subacute; flowers 2-2.7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, often minutely cinereous-puberulent oln all exterior surfaces, the bracteoles ovate, about 0.3 mm. long, the pedicels slender, 1-2 mm. long; sepals submembranous or papyraceous, deltoid to semiorbicular, 0.3-0.5 mm. long, 0.4-0.7 mm. broad, subentire or erosulous at margins; petals smooth, oblong to elliptic, 1-1.7 mm. long, 0.6-1 mm. broad, entire or distally erosulous at margins; disk 0.6-0.8 mm. in diameter, 0.12-0.2 mm. high, undulate and slightly thickened at margin; filaments 0.3-0.4 mm. long, slightly broadened at base and apex, the anthers about 0.2 by 0.4 mm.; ovary 0.4-0.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style 0.1-0.3 mm. long, the stigmas forming a minute capitate shield, obtuse or faintly emarginate, often obseure; ovules 2 per locule, collateral; fruits ofteni 5-10 per infloreseelnce (pedicels slightly swollen, up to 1.5 mm. in diameter), the capsules elliptic or slightly obovate, 3-4.5(-6) cm. long, 2-2.5 cm. broad, about 3 mm. thick, obtuse or rounded or faintly emarginate at apex, the pericarp thin-coriaceous, conspicuously flabellate-costate without (nerves strongly prominulous, copiously branching), smooth within, 0.2-0.4 ml. thick; seeds 2, the embryoniferous portion ellipsoid, 15-22 mm. long, 7-13 mm. broad, the wing oblong, 4-5 mm. long, 2-3 mm. broad distally, gradually narrowed toward base, extendilng distally into a narrow thickened flange along the inner margin of enibryoniferous portion.

description: Liana, the branchlets cinereous; petioles 3-9 mm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceous, usually greenish when dried, elliptic, 5-10 cm. long, 2-3.5 cm. broad, obtuse to attenuate at base, obtuse to gradually short- acuminate at apex, undulate-crelnate or serrulate at margins (crenations 1-3 per centimeter), the costa elevated or subprominent on both sur- faces, the secondary nerves 5-8 per side, erecto-patent, incolnspicuously anastomosinig near margins, prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets reticulate, nearly plane above, prominulous beneath; inflorescences axillary or aggregated in small clusters at apices of branchlets, 2-7 cm. long, 4-6-times branched, the peduncle up to 3 cm. long, the rachis inconspicuous, the branches copiously divided, the bracts oblong, acute, 1-1.5 mm. long; flowers 1.5-2 mm. in diameter at anthesis, sometimes obseurely and minutely puberulent on exterior surfaces, the pedicels slender, up to 2 mm. long; sepals submembranous, deltoid, 0.4-0.5 mm. long, slightly broader, erosulous; petals oblong or elliptic-oblong, 1-1.2 mm. long, about 0.6 mm. broad, enitire; disk 0.6-0.8 mm. in diameter, about 0.2 mm. high, entire and slightly thickened at margin; filaments about 0.4 mm. long, slightly broadened at base, the anthers about 0.2 mm. long and 0.3-0.4 mm. broad; ovary about 0.4 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style about 0.2 mm. long, obtuse or minutely capitate at apex, the stigmas often obscure; ovules 2 per locule, col- lateral; fruiting pedicels hardly exceedinig 1 mm. in diameter, the fruits apparently several per infloreseence, the capsules elliptic or slightly obovate, 4.5-6 cm. long, 2-3 cm. broad, obtuse or rounded at apex, the pericarp papyraceous, ilnconspic-uously flabellate-costate without, the nerves prominulous within; seeds 2, immature in our specimens, the basal wing apparently with a broad flange along its inner margin.

description: Frutex erectus, inermis, ramis teretibus, brunneis vel purpureo-brunneis, ramulis ultimis 1-1.5 mm. diametro, dense adpresse lepidotis, lepidibus pallide brunneis; foliis membranaceo-chartaceis, anguste oblongis vel late oblongo-lanceolatis vel oblongo-oblanceolatis, 4-6 cm. longis, 0.8-2 cm. latis, acutis vel breviter acuminatis, basi cuneatis, junioribus supra plus minusve consperse decidue argenteo-lepidotis cito glaberrimis, puncticulatis, in sieco viridibus, subnitidis, subtus dense argenteo-lepidotis, nitidis, lepidibus paucis pallide brunneis inspersis; nervis primariis utrinque 5-6, gracilibus, vix anastomosantibus, reticulis obsoletis; petiolo 4-5.5 mm. longo, dense lepi- doto; floribus axillaribus, solitariis binis vel trinis, pedicellis 1-3 mm. longis, dense lepidotis, 10-12 mm. longis, bracteis lineari-lanceolatis, lepidotis, de- ciduis; perianthio extus dense lepidoto, tubo intus glabro, partibus inferi- oribus angustis, eirciter 3 mm. longis, 1-1.2 mm. diametro, partibus superi- oribus abrupte inflatis, 4-4.2 mm. longis, eirciter 2.5 mm. diametro, cylindra- ceis, haud campanulatis, longitudinaliter subsuleatis et obscure rotundato- angulatis, dense lepidotis atque breviter stellato-pubeseentibus, infra lobis haud constrictis, lobis 4, ovatis, acutis, 3-3.5 mm. longis, 2-2.3 mm. latis, intus consperse stellato-pubeseentibus; disco obscuro; stylis glabris, 6 mm. longis; filamentis deorsum ampliatis, glabris, 1.2 mm. longis.

description: Description: A vine of large dimensions when mature, often reach- ing the tops of the highest trees; fruiting pedieels slender, 8-9 mm. long, glabrate; torus expanded, about 3 mm. wide, glabrate; fruit oblong-ellipsoid, asymmetric at base, about 2.5 cm. long, 1.3-1.5 cm. wide, the exocarp coriaceous, lucidous, glabrous, fuscous or nigrescent in drying, the mesocarp pulpy, the endocarp osseous, areolate-rugose, longitudinally suleate in a median circumferential line and each half thus produced again suleate with a channel of similar depth and more or less paralleling the median one, but 4-5 mm. removed from it at all points except the base, with a basal longitudinal condyle extending about two-thirds the length within; seeds about 1.8 cm. long and 7 mm. wide, black, rugose, longitudinally suleate like the endocarp, glabrous, obtusely rounded at both ends.

description: Arbor ad 13 m. alta et 20 cm. diametro, omnino glabra, ramulis primo rubro-fuscis sed mox cinereis; stipulae persistentes, 6-8 mm. longae, triangulares, ad marginem striatis, scariosis, nonnihil erosis, valde trinervatis, ad apicem trifidis; bracteis ad 8 mm. longis et 4 mm. latis, lanceolatis, striatis, arista robusta, subulata, ad 6 mm. longa, a parte superiore superficiei dorsualis oriente, ad marginem scariosis, bracteis secundariis minoribus, 3-4 mm. longis, exaristatis; bracteolis linearibus, 2.5-3 mm. longis, bracteis et bracteolis per floritionem persistentibus; pedicellis 2-3 mm. longis, gracilibus; sepala 5, colorata, oblonga, 3.5-4.5 mm. longa, 1.5-2.5 mm. lata, concava, ad apicem rotundata, ad basim angusta; description: Low, few-branched, terrestrial (?) shrub. Branches coarsely angled and ribbed, glabrous, glaucous, brown when dry. Petioles subterete, coarsely rugose, glabrous, 8-15 mm long and 2-4 mm diameter. Leaves lance-elliptic, (8.5-)11-17 x (3-)4.5-8 cm, basally cuneate or obtuse, apically acuminate, essentially glabrous but with marginal scattered capitate, glandular hairs to 1 mm, pinnatinerved with midrib impressed above and prominently raised beneath, lateral nerves and veinlets raised on both surfaces with veinlets obscure beneath. Inflorescence racemose, 13-23 flowered, flowers secund; rachis coarsely ribbed, glaucous, 11-26 cm, with scattered capitate, glandular hairs proximal one-fourth. Floral bracts ovate, acute to acuminate, 4-6 X 2 mm, basally slightly clasping, lowest ones with laminas densely glandular pilose. Pedicels coarsely angled and ribbed, glabrous, glaucous, (13-)15-20 mm long and 1.5-2 mm diameter. Bracteoles ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, keeled, 4-4.5 X 1.5-2 mm, glabrous, glaucous, basally glandular-fimbriate margined, located at or just above middle of pedicel. Calyx stipitate (stipe to 1 mm), glabrous, glaucous, 10-11 mm; tube cylindric, rugose, slightly apophysate, 4.5-5.5 mm; limb campanulate, 4.5-6 mm; lobes triangular, 2-3 mm; sinus acute or obtuse. Corolla cylindric, coriaceous, prominently nerved, glabrous, glaucous, 27-30 mm long and 5-6 mm diameter; lobes oblong, obtuse, reflexed at anthesis, 4 X 2 mm. Stamens unequal, 8-9 mm; filaments alternately either 3.5 or 4.5 mm, densely short hirsute with tan hairs; anthers including tubules 6 mm; thecae 5 mm, granular; tubules 1 mm, dehiscing by strictly terminal, slightly flaring pores. Style strongly exserted, 32-35 mm. Berry not seen.

description: Herbaceous perennial, forming colonies by extensive system of pseudorhizomes; stems erect, up to 3 m tall, simple to much branched above, glabrous to very pubescent with short upwardly curled trichomes, the lower parts with exfoliating epidermis; leaf blades linear to broadly elliptic or lanceolate, the abaxial midrib glabrous to very pubescent; inflorescence showy, with from several to ca 100 flowers; petals pink, 3-17 mm broad, 7-22 mm long; style usually hairy at base; stigma opening 2-3 days after anthesis. description: Outer basal leaves 8-15 cm long, 2.5-4 mm wide, margin tomentose, sheathing base whitish-green. Scape glabrous, 37-44 cm high, bearing 4-6 small bracts, 0-1 of these within 3 cm of the lowest flower. Pedicels of flowers 1-2 mm long, in fruit 2-4 mm long. Calycular bracts 1.8-2.3 mm across, 1.5-2 mm long, usually wider than long. Flowers whitish?, 11-14. Tepals 5.5-6.5 mm long, to 2 mm wide. Filaments 3.5-4 mm long, narrowly subulate, base about 2/5 the width of the tepal. Anthers 1-1.5 mm long, apiculate. Ovary 2.5 mm long. Style (including stigma) 0.9-1.1 mm long, tip oblique. Stigmas facing outward. Capsule 3-ribbed, 6-7 mm long. In flower in July.

description: Short-lived perennials that flower the first year; stems several from the caudices, plants 15-30 cm high; leaves basal, 1-2.5 cm long and wide, subcordate to orbicular, the apices rounded, the bases subcordate to cordate, densely white-tomentose below, less so above, prominently veined, the petioles 3-8 cm long, floccose-tomentose; stems erect, slender, 5-15 cm long, often minutely viscid at the bases, glabrous and pruinose throughout; bracts scale-like, 2-parted, 1-3 mm long, triangular, closely appressed to the branches, widening from acute apices to broad connate bases, glabrous or minutely viscid without, glabrous or arachnoid-pubescent within; branches divaricate, spreading outwardly to form diffuse or open, flat-topped to hemispheric crowns, di- or trichotomous above, the internodes of the upper branches short, 5-15 mm long; peduncles lacking to 4 mm long, slender and deflexed; involucres campanulate, 1.5-2.5 mm long, (1.5) 2-2.5 (3) mm wide, the 5 acute lobes dividing the tubes 1/4 to 1/3 of their length, with brownish margins particularly between the lobes, glabrous and pruinose without, villous at the top, becoming less so to glabrous within the tubes, the bractlets oblanceolate, 2-3 mm long, densely hirsutulous with long tapering marginal cells, the pedicels glabrous or rarely sparsely hirsutulous at the bases, 2-3 mm long, 15-20-flowered; perianth 2 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, yellow with brownish midribs, glabrous, calyx segments dissimilar, the outer whorls reniform-cordate, the apices obtuse, the bases reniform to cordate, the perianth tubes somewhat inflated, brownish, the inner whorls broadly oblanceolate, 1-1.5 mm long; stamens included, 1.5 mm long, the filaments densely pilose at the bases, the anthers 0.3-0.4 mm long, greenish, oblong, the pollen grains ellipsoidal, 28-30 µ long, 20-22 µ wide, granular with two shallow furrows, 28-40 pollen grains per anther sac; achenes bronze to brown, 2 mm long, the globose bases narrowing to 3-angled beaks. 2n = 40.

description: Annuals; scapes one to several from the caudices, plants 5-30 (40) cm high; leaves basal or sheathing up the stems 1.5 cm, the leaves 1-3 (4) cm long, (1.5) 2-4 (5) cm wide, orbicular to cordate, the apices rounded, the bases cordate to subcordate, densely white-tomentose below, less so to subglabrous and green above; stems stout, erect, 2-7 cm long, glandular; bracts scale-like, 2- or 3-parted, 1-2 mm long, triangular, widening from obtuse or acute apices to connate bases, glabrous within, glabrous or glandular without; branches horizontal in low, flat-topped crowns, or spreading and forming subglobose crowns, trichotomous at the first node, dichotomous above, the ultimate branches often with alternating secondary branches which too have alternating branches, and racemose toward the tips of the branches, glandular; peduncles up to 15 mm long, slender to stoutish, deflexed and glandular; involucres turbinate to campanulate, 1-2.5 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, the 5 acute to obtuse lobes dividing the tubes about 1/4 of their length, glandular without, sparsely pubescent or glabrous within, the bractlets linear-oblanceolate, 1.5-2 mm long, hirsutulous with minute marginal cells, the longer cells tapering to points, the shorter cells capitate, the pedicels glabrous, 1.5-3.5 mm long, up to 10-flowered; perianth 1-2 (2.5) mm long, white becoming reddish at maturity in some, the midribs greenish or brown, glabrous, calyx segments dissimilar, the outer whorls ovate to oblong, the apices rounded, the bases cordate to auriculate, the inner whorls narrower and shorter than the outer whorl; stamens included to slightly exserted, 1.5-2 (2.5) mm long, the filaments glabrous or pilose at the bases, the anthers 0.3-0.4 mm long, green or reddish, oblong, pollen grain elliptical-oblong, 30-40 µ long, 30-35 µ wide, with one or two shallow furrows, 40-60 pollen grains per anther sac; achenes 1.5-2 mm long, brown to nearly black, the subglobose bases narrowing to 3-angled beaks. 2n = 40.

description: Low, matted, cespitose perennial herbs with a highly branched woody caudex forming a mat (0.8) 1-2.5 dm across, this arising from a stout, woody taproot; leaves basal, persistent, the old leaf-blades and bases often covering the upper 1-4 cm of the caudex branch, the leaf-blade oblanceolate to narrowly elliptic, 5- 15 mm long, 1.5-4 (5) mm wide, densely white-tomentose on both surfaces, only slightly less densely so above in some, not glandular, the apex acute or nearly so, the base cuneate, the margin entire and plane but slightly thickened, the petiole 0.3-1 (1.2) cm long, tomentose, the petiole-base elongate-triangular, 2-2.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, tomentose without, sparsely tomentose to glabrous within; flowering stems scapose, weakly erect, (1.5) 3-5 (7) cm long, floccose; inflorescences capitate, the head 5-8 mm across; bracts mostly ternate, scale-like, linear to narrowly triangular, 1.5-2 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, sparsely floccose without, glabrous within, connate basally; peduncles lacking; involucres congested, 5-7 per head, campanulate, rigid, 2-3 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, floccose without, glabrous within, the 5 acute and triangular teeth 0.5-0.8 mm long, the bractlets linear, 2-3 mm long, minutely fringed with capitate, gland-tipped cells, the ped- icels 2-3.5 mm long, glabrous; flowers yellow, the tepals with greenish-yellow midribs and bases turning reddish with age, 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous within and without except for minute glands along the midribs within, all essentially similar, oblong to oblong-obovate, those of the outer whorl 1-1.2 mm wide with the apex rounded to retuse, those of the inner whorl 0.7-0.9 mm wide with the apex rounded, united about 1/4 the length of the flower; stamens slightly exserted, 1.5-2 mm long, the filaments sparsely pilose basally, the anthers yellow, oblong, 0.4- 0.5 mm long; achenes light brown, 2 mm long, glabrous, the subglobose base tapering to a long, 3-angled beak.

description: Annuals; scapes one or occasionally several from thin caudices, plants (0.5) 1-7 (10) dm high; leaves basal or sheathing up the stems 1 cm, the leaves 1-2.5 (4) cm long 2-4 (5) cm wide, cordate, reniform, to nearly orbicular, the apices rounded to obtuse, the bases cordate, subcordate, reniform, or round-reniform, densely whitetomentose below, less so to subglabrous and green above, obscurely to prominently veined; stems erect or nearly so, slender or occasionally stout, inflated in some, 3-30 cm long, glabrous and glaucous; bracts scale-like, ternate, 1-3 mm long, triangular and erect or spreading, widening from acute apices to connate bases, arachnoid-pubescent or glabrous within, the margins often hirsute, glabrous without; branches erect or spreading, open to diffuse, trichotomously branched at the first node, di- or trichotomous above, the branches varying in length, becoming shorter toward the tips, inflated in some, short and stout, occasionally long whip-like and slender in which the secondary branches are at right angles to the main branches, glabrous and glaucous; peduncles lacking to 15 mm long, slender or stout, deflexed, glabrous; involucres narrowly turbinate to turbinate, 1-2.5 (3) mm long, 1-2.5 mm wide, the 5 acute to obtuse lobes dividing the tubes 1/t to 1/3 of their length, glabrous and glaucous within and without, the bractlets few to many, linear-oblanceolate, 0.5-2.5 mm long, hirsutulous with few to many minute marginal cells tapering to acute points or capitate heads, the pedicels glabrous, 1-3 (4) mm long, 5-25-flowered; perianth 1-2.5 (3) mm long, white to pinkish, maturing to reddish-white or yellowish in some, with green, red, or brown midribs, glabrous, calyx segments dissimilar, the outer whorls ovate to ovate-elliptic, or oblong, the apices retuse, truncate, or somewhat obtuse, the bases cordate, the inner whorls narrowly ovate to lanceolate, shorter than the outer whorl; stamens included, 1-1.5 mm long, the filaments glabrous or sparsely pilose at the bases, the anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long, green or red, oblong, the pollen grains ellipsoidal to oblong, 30-35 µ long, 25-30 µ wide, with one or two shallow furrows, 12-48 pollen grains per anther sac; achenes reddish-brown, brown, or dark brown, (1.5) 2-3 mm long, the subglobose bases tapering to long narrow 3-angled beaks.

description: Annuals; scape one, rarely more, from the caudices, plants 1-6 dm high; leaves basal or sheathing up the stems 2 cm, leaves (1) 2-5 cm long, 2-6 cm wide, cordate to subreniform, the apices rounded, the bases cordate to subreniform, rarely truncate, the margins rolled upward on the edges, densely white felty-tomentose below, tomentose above; stems erect, slender to stout, glabrous and glaucous; bracts scalelike, ternate, 1-3 mm long, triangular and erect, widening from acute apices to connate bases, glabrous within and without; branches spreading, subglobose or forming flattopped crowns with the outer edge lower than the center so as to give an "umbrella" appearance in some, in others the numerous branches are crowded and diffusely branched, glabrous and glaucous; peduncles lacking; involucres deflexed, broadly campanulate or hemispheric, 1-2 mm long, 1.5-3 (3.5) mm wide, the 5 acute lobes dividing the tubes about 1/3 of their length, with thin hyaline margins particularly between the lobes, glabrous within and without except for a few marginal hairs on the inner surface of the lobes, the bractlets numerous, linear-spathulate, 1.5-2.5 mm long, hirsutulous with minute cells tapering to acute points or capitate heads, the pedicels glabrous, 2-2.5 mm long, 5-15-flowered; perianth 1.5-2 mm long, yellow becoming reddish-yellow at maturity, glabrous, calyx segments dissimilar, the outer whorls orbicular, the apices rounded to obtuse, the bases cordate or hastate, the inner whorls oblong-ovate and shorter than the outer whorl; stamens included, 1.5 mm long, the filaments glabrous, the anthers 0.3-0.6 mm long, green or reddish, oblong, the pollen grains ellipsoidal, 24-31 ,1 long, 20-27 ,1 wide, with a single furrow, 12-16 pollen grains per anther sac; perianth elongating and expanding in fruit, the outer whorl becoming nearly isodiametric, 2-2.5 mm long and wide; achenes light brown, 2-2.5 mm long, the globose bases tapering to 3-angled beaks. 2n = 40.
