description: Low rounded subshrubs 1-5 dm high, 3-8 dm across with spreading and weakly erect woody caudices arising from a stout, gnarled, woody taproot; leaves basal and sheathing up the lower stems 1-8 (-10) cm, the leaf-blades ovate to elliptic or rhombic, 1-4 cm long, (0.4-) 0.7-2 cm wide, crassulate and persistent, thinly and finely villous and bright green on both surfaces with a greater concentration of hairs on the margins and midveins, often glabrate at maturity, the margins entire and plane, the apices acute, the bases acute to cuneate and more or less tapering to the petiole, the petioles broad but not laminar, 0.8-2 cm long, sparsely villous with somewhat longer hairs than those of the blade, the petiole-bases elongate-triangular and sheathing, 2-5 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, villous without, glabrous within; flowering stems erect or more or less spreading, 3-10 cm long, sparsely villous and bright green; inflorescences open, 1.5-4 dm long, di- or trichotomous at the first node, dichotomous above, the branches sparsely villous and glandular throughout, bright green to yellowish-green; bracts foliaceous, 5-6 in 2 whorls at each node, the outer whorl true bracts, these lanceolate to elliptic, 3-12 mm long, 2-3.5 mm wide, sessile and connate at the base, the inner whorl true leaves, these elliptic to ovate, 3-10 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, on short petioles 0.5-1.5 mm long, both bracts and cauline leaves thinly villous, glandular and bright green on both surfaces; peduncles slender, erect to ascending, (0.8-)1-3 cm long, glandular and sparsely villous; involucres campanulate, 2-3.5 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, glandular and villous along the margin without, the 5 lobes broadly lanceolate, (1-)1.2-1.6 mm long, 1-1.3 mm wide, the bractlets lacking, the pedicels (2.7-)3-4 mm long, minutely and sparsely glandular; stamens included, the filaments 1.5-2.5 mm long, glabrous, the anthers red to purple, 0.3-0.4 mm long, oval; achenes light brown, 1.5-1.8 mm long, the globose base tapering to a 3-angled beak.

description: Plants low matted herbaceous perennials with a highly branched, woody caudex system forming a mat 1-3(-4.5) dm across, this arising from a stout, woody taproot. Leaves basal; leaf-blades narrowly spatulate, 4-8 X (1.5-)2-4 mm, densely grayish white tomentose on both surfaces; apex obtuse to rounded; base cuneate; margins entire, thickened in some; petiole short, 1-3 mm long, tomentose; petiole-base triangular, 0.5-1.5 mm long, tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Flowering stems lacking. Peduncles erect, capillary, (1.5-)3-5(- 7) cm long, thinly tomentose, arising directly from the caudices. Inflorescences capitate, 5-9 mm across. Bracts lacking. Involucres solitary, turbinate to turbinate-campanulate, rigid, 2-3 X 1.5-2(-2.5) mm, thinly tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially; teeth 5, rounded, 0.4-0.6 mm long, erect; bractlets linear, 2-3 mm long, minutely fringed with scattered, marginal gland-tipped cells; pedicels 2-3.5 mm long, glabrous. Flowers white, 2-3.5(-4) mm long, glabrous except for scattered glands along the midrib adaxially; midribs green in early anthesis, becoming reddish brown, keeled and distinctly papillose in fruit; perianth lobes slightly dimorphic, those of the outer whorl oblong, those of the inner whorl oblong-oblanceolate, united about 1/5 of their length. Stamens slightly exserted, 2-3 mm long; filaments pilose basally; anthers pale yellow, 0.4-0.6 mm long, oblong. Achenes light brown, 2.5-3.5 mm long; base subglobose; apex 3-angled, slightly papillose.

description: Annuals; scapes usually one from the caudices, (0.5) 1-4 dm high; leaves basal, (0.5) 1-2.5 cm long and wide, orbicular to subcordate, the apices rounded, the bases subcordate to reniform, densely white-tomentose below, less so to subglabrous and green above; stems slender, 4-8 cm long, glabrous and glaucous; bracts scale-like, ternate, 1-2 mm long, triangular and erect or spreading, widening from acute apices to connate bases, arachnoid-pubescent within, glabrous without; branches spreadings as to form subglobose crowns, open to diffuse, trichotomous at the first node, dichotomous or rarely trichotomous above, often with deflexed involucre-bearing peduncles in the forks of the branches, glabrous and glaucous; involucres narrowly turbinate, (1.5) 2-3 mm long, 0.5-1.5 mm wide, the 5 acute lobes dividing the tubes nearly 1/4 of their length, the teeth erect or slightly turned inward, glabrous within and without, the bractlets few, linear-oblanceolate, 1-1.5 mm long, hirsutulous with numerous marginal cells tapering to acute points, the pedicels glabrous, 2-2.5 (3) mm long, 2-5 (7)-flowered; perianth 2-2.5 mm long, white to pinkish with green or reddish midribs, glabrous, calyx segment dissimilar, the outer whorls oblong to obovate, the apices rounded, the bases truncate to obtuse, the inner whorls ovate and shorter than the outer whorl; stamens included, 1.5-2 mm long, the filaments glabrous, the anthers 0.3-0.4 mm long, green or reddish, round to oblong, the pollen grains oval, 31-35 µ long, 30-32 µ wide, with two shallow furrows, 28-60 pollen grains per anther sac; achenes brown, 1.5 mm long, the globose bases tapering to 3-angled beaks. 2n = 40.

description: Plantae altae, caulibus subscapiformibus; folia linearia, margine omnino densissime sub- tiliterque spinoso-serrato, venis parallelis, foliis caulinis paucis semiamplexicaulibus; inflores- centia trichotomo-paniculata; capitula viridi-alba puberula ovoidea vel ovoideo-globosa; bracteae involucrales ovato-lanceolatae, basi manifeste connatae, quam capitulae multo breviores; sepala ovalia obtusa; styli sepalis longiores; fructus cuneato-ovoideus, mericarpiis papillis vesiculosis obsitis, dorsi superficie praeter vesiculas parvas ad apicem versus nuda.
bibliographicCitation: Constance, Lincoln. 1979. Three new species of Eryngium (Umbelliferae) from tropical South America. Brittonia. 31: 365-372.

description: Plants perennial, 1-1.5+ m tall from an oblique rootstock bearing fascicled fibrous roots, the flowering stems slender, scapose, leafy only below, solitary (?); basal leaves subcoriaceous, rosulate, linear, 30-55 cm long, 1-2 cm broad, acumi- nate, obscurely cartilaginous-margined, densely and finely spinose-serrate from sheath to apex, the minute spines ascending, 1-3 mm long, solitary, 3 or 4 per centimeter, the venation parallel, the lamina gradually broadened into a naked sheath of slightly greater width; cauline leaves like the basal, ascending, overlapping only below, semi-clasping, strongly reduced upward; inflorescence trichotomously paniculate, terminating in an umbellate cluster of 3 or 4 1-2-furcate fertile branches, supplemented by similar ones in the upper leaf axils; heads greenish-white, ovoid to ovoid-globose, 8-12 mm long, 8-10 mm broad, rounded at apex and base, many-flowered, scaberulous; involucral bracts 6-8, ovate-lanceolate, acute, entire, 4-5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm broad, 1-veined, scaberulous, conspicuously connate, much shorter than the heads; bractlets like the bracts, 3-4 mm long, slightly exceeding the fruit; sepals oval, obtuse, 1.5 mm long; petals oblong-oval, 1-1.5 mm long, the inflexed apex 3/4 as long as the limb, subentire; styles 2-2.5 mm long, longer than the sepals; fruit cuneate-ovoid, 3-4 mm long (including sepals), 2-2.5 mm broad, the flattened whitish vesicles forming a prominent calycine row and 2 marginal wings of separate, lanceolate, acute scales, the upper part of the dorsal surface covered with much reduced scales or vesicles, the lower part naked.
bibliographicCitation: Constance, Lincoln. 1979. Three new species of Eryngium (Umbelliferae) from tropical South America. Brittonia. 31: 365-372.

description: Plants perennial, rather slender, erect, 1-2 m tall, from an oblique rootstock bearing fascicled fibrous roots, the flowering stem solitary, diffusely branched and subscapose above; basal leaves rosulate, spreading, linear-attenuate, 4.5-8 dm long, 2-3.5 cm broad (including lobes, 1-2 cm without), coarsely spinose- lobed, the stout linear lobes 5-25 mm long, spreading or spreading-ascending, the longer often a little exceeding blade-width, usually with smaller axillary spinules, the blade spinose-acuminate at apex, passing at base into a naked sheath of about equal breadth and 10-12 cm long, the venation parallel; cauline leaves like the basal, alternate below, ascending, subamplexicaul and conspicuously spinose-lobed at base; inflorescence diffusely cymose-paniculate, ending above in a whorl of 2-4 trifurcate fertile branches surrounding the terminal peduncle, and supple- mented by few to numerous similar branches from the upper axils, the bracts greatly reduced; heads greenish-white, ovoid-globose, 0.7-1.2 cm long, 0.5-1 cm broad, slender-pedunculate, truncate at base, glabrous, few-flowered; involucral bracts 6-8, lanceolate-acuminate, 6-8 mm long, 1.5-2 mm broad, entire, shorter than the heads; bractlets like the bracts, 3-5 mm long, much longer than the fruit; sepals ovate, obtuse, apiculate, ca 1 mm long; petals oval, ca 1.5 mm long, the narrower inflexed apex about equaling the limb, fimbriate distally; styles 3-4 mm long, longer than the sepals;fruit ovoid, 2.5-3 mm long (including sepals), 2 mm broad, compressed dorsally, provided with whitish ovate squamae forming a prominent calycine row, 2 marginal wings of several free scales, and sometimes a few scales on the upper angles, the dorsal surfaces naked; chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Mickel, John T. 1980. Relationships of the dissected elaphoglossoid ferns. Brittonia. 32: 109-117.

description: Plantae humiles, caulibus subscapiformibus; folia disticha lineari-oblonga falciformia, margine cartilagineo praesertim ad apicem minute serrulato basin versus interdum spinoso-ciliato, venis parallelis, foliis caulinis paucis; inflorescentia terminalis ramis floriferis reductis monocephalis; capitula alba globosa; bracteae involucrales lanceolatae acuminatae quam capitulae multo breviores; sepala ovata obtusa; styli sepalis longiores; fructus cuneato-oblongus, mericarpiis papillis vesiculosis obsitis, dorsi superficie dense squamata.

description: Plants perennial, 4.5-10 dm tall from a stout oblique rootstock, the flowering stems solitary, subscapose; basal leaves subcoriaceous, rosulate, ascending, disti- chous, linear-oblong, somewhat falciform, 10-20 cm long, 3-5 mm broad, obtuse, cartilaginous-margined, frequently minutely and remotely serrulate, especially toward apex, sometimes spinose-ciliate toward base, the venation parallel, the sheath short and broad; cauline leaves few and remote, similar but much reduced upward; inflorescence of a whorl of a terminal peduncle and 1-4 reduced flowering branches each bearing a single head, sometimes with an axillary peduncle below, the bracts greatly reduced; heads white, globose, 8-12 mm in diameter; involucral bracts 8-10, lanceolate, acuminate, entire, 4-6 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, spreading or ascending and much shorter than the heads; bractlets like the bracts, 4-6 mm long, longer than the fruit; sepals ovate, obtuse, mucronulate, 1-1.5 mm long; petals narrowly oblong, 1.5-1.8 mm long, the inflexed apex %/3 the length of the limb, bifid; styles 2-2.5 mm long, longer than the sepals; fruit cuneate-oblong, 4-5 mm long (including sepals), 2-2.5 mm broad, densely covered with very un- equal tawny-colored squamae, the marginal ovate-lanceolate, flattened, acute, free, forming conspicuous marginal wings, the calycine similar, the dorsal surface with much reduced squamae.
bibliographicCitation: Constance, Lincoln. 1979. Three new species of Eryngium (Umbelliferae) from tropical South America. Brittonia. 31: 365-372.

description: Plants perennial, rather stout, glaucous, 0.5-2+ m tall from a thick, nearly vertical rootstock bearing fascicled fleshy-fibrous roots, the flowering stem soli- tary, subscapose above; basal leaves rosulate ensiform, mostly distichous, spreading-ascending, linear-lanceolate to linear-attenuate, 2-8 dm long, 1.5-4.5 cm broad (including lobes, 0.7-2.5 cm without), spinose-lobed, the lobes linear- to lanceolate-subulate, 3-20 mm long, divaricate to ascending, usually with an auxiliary axillary spinule, the blades rigidly attenuate at apex, at base slightly expanded into a naked sheath equaling or broader than blade-width and 3-15 cm long, the venation parallel, the blades deeper green above with a lighter central stripe; cauline leaves few, like the basal, alternate below the inflorescence, ascending or the upper somewhat recurved, strongly amplexicaul; inflorescence cymose-paniculate, consisting of a cluster of 1-3 basically trichotomous fertile branches surrounding and usually exceeding the terminal peduncle, usually sup- plemented by similar branches from the upper axils, or some of these branches reduced to 1 head or lacking, the bracts reduced upward; heads greenish-white (or very pale bluish-white), ovoid to globose, 1-2 cm long, 1-1.5 cm broad, long- pedunculate, glabrous (or nearly so), many-flowered; involucral bracts 6-10, lin- ear- or lanceolate-subulate, 0.5-2.5 cm long, 2-5 mm broad, mostly entire, or with a few spinose teeth, spreading or reflexed, usually longer (but occasionally shorter) than the heads; bractlets lanceolate-subulate, 5-8 mm long, exceeding the flowers; sepals oval, obtuse, mucronate or apiculate, 1.5-2 mm long; petals oblong-oval, 2-2.5 mm long, the narrower inflexed apex subequal to the limb, fimbriate distally; styles 3-4 mm long, exceeding the sepals; fruit cuneate-ovoid, 4 mm long (including sepals), 2-3 mm broad, compressed dorsally, provided with a prominent calycine row of flattened ovate or lanceolate, acute, white or yel- lowish scales and 2 lateral wings of 3 or 4 free scales each, the dorsal surfaces naked; chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Mickel, John T. 1980. Relationships of the dissected elaphoglossoid ferns. Brittonia. 32: 109-117.

description: Plants perennial, 0.6-1+ m tall from a stout, nearly horizontal rootstock bearing fascicled fibrous roots, the flowering stems very leafy, solitary; basal leaves subcoriaceous, clustered, linear-lanceolate, 30-40 cm long, 1-2 cm broad, acuminate, inconspicuously cartilaginous-margined, the lamina very densely spinose- ciliate to spinose-dentate throughout, the spines solitary, up to 5 mm long, the venation essentially all parallel, the lamina expanded into a naked entire sheath 5-7 cm long; cauline leaves very numerous, strongly overlapping at least below, densely spinose-ciliate to the prominently clasping base, gradually reduced upward; inflorescence thyrsoid, with a terminal peduncle and several trifurcate branches plus a trifurcate branch in each of the upper leaf axils, the bracts prominent; heads whitish, hemispherical, 10-15 mm in diameter, puberulent; involucral bracts 8-10, lanceolate, acute, mucronate, entire or with 1-3 spinose lateral teeth, 6-8 mm long, 1.5-3 mm broad, prominently 3- or 5-veined, strongly connate at base, much shorter than the heads; bractlets like the bracts, 4-6 mm long, lanceolate to linear- lanceolate, evidently scaberulous on the margins, exceeding the fruit; sepals lanceolate-acuminate, mucronate, entire, puberulent, 2-3 mm long; petals oval, 1-1.5 mm long, the inflexed apex fimbriate; styles 1.5-3 mm long, shorter than to slightly exceeding the sepals; fruit cuneate-oblong or cuneate-ovoid, 4-6 mm long (including sepals), 2-3 mm broad, the flattened shining, acute, white scales forming a single calycine row and 2 prominent marginal wings, the dorsal surface naked.
bibliographicCitation: Constance, Lincoln. 1979. Three new species of Eryngium (Umbelliferae) from tropical South America. Brittonia. 31: 365-372.

description: Plants perennial, rather stout, ca 1 m tall, from a short oblique rootstock bearing fleshy-fibrous roots; basal leaves rosulate, spreading-ascending, ensiform, linear-lanceolate, 3-5 dm long, 1.5-4 cm broad (including lobes), spinose-lobed, the lobes linear-subulate, entire, 2-25 mm long, definitely ascending, sometimes with a much smaller auxiliary axillary spinule, the blade attenuate (but scarcely rigidly spinose), somewhat narrowed at base and then expanded into a naked sheath about as broad as the blade and 5-10 cm long, the blades with or without a poorly defined lighter stripe, the venation essentially parallel; cauline leaves similar to the basal, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, spinose-lobed, alternate except for the whorl subtending the terminal cymose cluster, strongly subamplexicaul, ascending to slightly recurved; inflorescence paniculately cymose, ending in a small terminal cluster of 3 or 4 trichotomous flowering branches surrounding the terminal peduncle, supplemented by several to many similar axillary branches, the cauline bracts prominent; heads globose, greenish to blue, 10-15 mm in diameter, pedunculate, glabrous, many-flowered; involucral bracts 6-9, linear-lanceolate, 10-25 mm long, 2-3 mm broad, pungent, entire, ultimately reflexed and exceeding the heads; bractlets lanceolate-subulate, 2-4 mm long, exceeding the fruit; sepals ovate, obtuse, apiculate, 1-1.5 mm long; petals oblong-oval, ca 1.5 mm long, the narrower inflexed apex subequal to the limb, fimbriate; styles 2.5-3 mm long, exceeding the sepals; fruit cuneate-ovoid, 4-5 mm long (including sepals), 3 mm broad, compressed dorsally (but not flattened), provided with a row of tawny ovate calycine scales and lateral wings of 3 or 4 free squamae, the dorsal surfaces with beaded rows of vesicles, or naked (?); chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Mickel, John T. 1980. Relationships of the dissected elaphoglossoid ferns. Brittonia. 32: 109-117.

description: Plants perennial, very slender, erect, 0.8-2 m tall, from an oblique rootstock bearing fleshy-fibrous roots, the flowering stem solitary, scapose above; basal leaves rosulate, ascending, linear to linear-lanceolate, 2-5.5 dm long, 1-3.5 cm broad (including lobes, 0.5-1.0 cm wide without), coarsely spinose-lobed, the lobes linear-subulate, pungent, entire, 0.5-2.5 cm long, spreading-ascending, usually broader than blade-width, frequently with a much smaller auxiliary axil- lary spinule, the blade rigid-attenuate at apex, little narrowed at base and then dilated into a naked sheath about equaling or a little broader than the blade and 2-5 cm long, the venation parallel except for the veins entering the lobes; cauline leaves few, like the basal, alternate, subamplexicaul, ascending or recurving; inflorescence paniculately cymose, of a terminal cluster of few to several 1-2-trichotomous flowering branches surrounding and surpassing the terminal pedun- cle, usually supplemented by 1 to many similar branches from the upper axils, the cauline bracts greatly reduced; heads cream-colored, hemispherical to globose or ovoid-globose, 7-10 mm in diameter, pedunculate, usually puberulent; invo- lucral bracts 6-8, linear-lanceolate, 3-15 mm long, 1-2 mm broad, entire or with an occasional spinose tooth, spreading-reflexed, longer or shorter than the heads; bractlets lanceolate, mucronate, cymbiform, 3-4 mm long, usually manifestly puberulent, longer than the fruit; sepals ovate, acute or obtuse, apiculate, 1-1.5 mm long; petals oblong-oval, ca 1.2 mm long, the inflexed apex subequal to the limb; styles ca 3 mm long, longer than the sepals; fruit cuneate-oblong to -ovoid, 3-5 mm long (including sepals), 2-3 mm broad, compressed dorsally, provided with 1 or more rows of flattened, yellowish, lanceolate scales below the calyx, these extending to the base of the dorsal surface as vertical beaded rows of diminishing vesicles, the marginal wings of 5-8 quite distinct ovate scales; chromosome number n = 32.
bibliographicCitation: Mickel, John T. 1980. Relationships of the dissected elaphoglossoid ferns. Brittonia. 32: 109-117.

description: Shrub or tree often unbranched, 0.5-12 m tall. Leaf blade (narrow-oblanceolate) oblanceolate to lanceolate, acuminate to acute (less often obtuse or rounded) at apex, long-cuneate to long-decurrent at base, 15- 93.6 cm long, 3.5-14.7 cm wide, with 15- 34 secondary veins per side; petiole canaliculate or flattened adaxially, 0.7-7.6 cm long. Inflorescence lateral but not obviously axillary, perennating, umbelliform initially, elongate and +/- racemiform with lateral  clusters or short-shoots of flowers and often branched and cauline with age, (6) 16.9- 94.8 cm long; peduncle and rachis 3-4-an- gled, glabrous, often conspicuously warty especially near apex; bracts from linear to narrow-elliptic and 15-102 mm long and 2-15 mm wide to acicular and 5-10 mm long; pedicels 0.7-2.2 cm long in flower, 1.0-2.6 cm long in fruit, sparsely appressed- puberulent to glabrous, with often conspicuously warty and ultimately exfoliating epi- dermis. Calyx in flower variously lobed, 1.5- 4.3 cm long, 0.6-1.4 cm wide at middle, glabrous without, glabrous to appressed-pubescent sometimes only at tips within, red to pink-red, irregularly splitting as fruit develops, ultimately deciduous from mature fruit. Corolla actinomorphic, 4.3-7.5 cm long, the tube straight, 2-4.2 cm long, 0.4- 1.1 cm wide at apex, glabrous or more often with a sparsely pilose ring 3-7.5 mm wide beginning 6.5-14 mm above base within, the lobes oblanceolate to wide-obovate, obtuse or rounded at apex, 1.5-4.1 cm long, 0.55-1.9 cm wide. Androecium of 5 fertile stamens (rarely some transformed into ster- ile filaments); filaments connate into a tube adnate to corolla tube, with glabrous free tip 3-8 mm long; anthers narrow-oblong to lorate, 3-7 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, gla- brous or sparsely appressed-puberulent, with minute basal appendages to 0.2 mm long. Disc slightly 5-undulate, 1.5-5.2 mm high. Carpels connate axially at base and at apex in style, 1-2.1 mm high, glabrous or infrequently +/- pubescent; style 33.5-42 mm long at anthesis, glabrous or in one collection with a few spreading hairs. Fruiting mericarps 1.1-1.7 cm high, 0.7-1.3 cm deep, glabrous or sparsely puberulent, red when fresh. Seeds 6-8 mm long, 3.5-5 mm wide, brown or tan.
bibliographicCitation: Kallunki, Jacquelyn A. 1992. A revision of Erythrochiton sensu lato (Cuspariinae, Rutaceae). Brittonia. 44: 107-139.

description: Shrub or tree, few-branched, 1.2-4.5 m tall. Leaf blade oblanceolate, short- to long-acuminate (sometimes acute, obtuse, or even rounded) at apex, decurrent at base, 6.3-43.1 (51.5) cm long, 1.8-8.3 cm wide, with 7-21 secondary veins per side; petiole flattened or canaliculate adaxially, 0.4-2.5 cm long. Inflorescence lateral but not obviously axillary, perennating, umbelliform initially, elongate and racemiform with lat- eral clusters or short-shoots of flowers and often branched or cauline with age, 5-42 cm long, older cauliflorous ones to 155.5 cm; peduncle and rachis angled, glabrous; bracts linear to oblanceolate and 16-70 mm long and 2-16 mm wide to acicular and 4- 8 mm long and 1 mm wide; pedicels 1.2- 1.5 cm in flower, 1.4-1.9 (2.6) cm in fruit, sparsely appressed-puberulent. Calyx in flower variously lobed often to base and in fruit of free sepals, these lanceolate, 2.1-4.6 cm long, 0.35-0.9 cm wide, in bud sparsely appressed-puberulent without and within, in flower glabrous without and sometimes sparsely appressed-puberulent within, red in flower, green in fruit, persistent in mature and even very old fruit. Corolla zygomorphic, 5-6 cm long, the tube almost straight, 2.4-4.4 cm long, 0.3-0.7 cm wide at apex, with a densely woolly ring of white pubescence 2-10 mm broad beginning 2.5-7 mm above the base within, the lobes narrow- oblong to lorate, rounded at apex, 2-3.5 cm long, 0. 5-0.6 cm wide, the innermost spreading in upper position, the 4 others spreading to recurved below. Androecium of 2 fertile stamens and 3 staminodes; fil- aments connate into a tube adnate to corolla tube for most of their length, white; fertile filaments with free tip 1.5-7 mm long, the anthers narrow-oblong to lorate, 5-9 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, sparsely appressed- puberulent or rarely glabrous, white, the ap- pendages 0.3-0.5 mm long (when rehydrat- ed); staminodes spreading-erect as 4 upper corolla lobes, 1.1-2.2 cm long, curly-to- mentulose especially near base, white. Disc slightly 5-undulate, rarely unequally slit in one or more sinuses, 2.5-4 mm high. Car- pels free except at apex in style, 1-1.5 mm high, glabrous; style 23-44 mm long and exserted 7-10.8 mm from throat at anthesis, spreading puberulent; stigma oblique. Fruiting mericarps 1.1-1.6 cm high, 0.9-1.1 cm deep, glabrous. Seeds 5.5-7 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, tan.

description: Shrub or small tree usually unbranched, 3.5-5 m tall and ca 8 cm dbh. Leaf blade oblanceolate, rounded to short-acuminate at apex, cuneate or acute at base, 74-108 cm long, 19.5-24.5 cm wide, with 19-35 secondary veins per side; petiole flat above and canaliculate at base adaxially, 12-21 cm long. Inflorescence perennating, with short- shoots of flowers, often branched, 34-58 cm long (to 100 cm on label); peduncle angled, glabrous; bracts lorate or narrow-oblanceo- late and 30-84 mm long and 3-12 mm wide to lanceolate and 7-12 mm long and 2-3 mm wide; pedicels 2.3-3 cm long in flower, 3-4.5 cm and warty in fruit, glabrous. Calyx in flower variously lobed, 2.2-3.6 cm long, 1.4-1.5 cm wide at middle, glabrous with- out, appressed-puberulent within, irregular- ly split and persistent in mature fruit. Corolla subzygomorphic, ca 7.9 cm long, glandular-punctate without, the tube almost straight, 3.7-4.1 cm long, 0.5-0.8 cm wide at apex, pubescent within, the lobes narrow- to wide-obovate, rounded at apex, 3.2-4.2 cm long, 1.8-2.4 cm wide. Androecium (ob- served in buds) of 2 fertile stamens and 3 or 4 staminodes; "filaments connate in a tube adnate to corolla" tube (Kaastra & Gentry, 1978); fertile filaments with free deltate tip 4-5 mm long and 3.5-4 mm wide, glabrous, the anthers narrow-oblong, 8.5- 10 mm long, 1.5-2.4 mm wide, glabrous, the appendages ca 0.6 mm long; staminodes linear. Disc laciniate, ca 5-8.8 mm high. Carpels free except at apex in style, 1.5-1.8 mm high, style to at least 45 mm after an- thesis, glabrous. Fruiting mericarps 1.6-1.9 cm high, 1-1.1 cm deep, connate only at base, glabrous. Seeds 8-8.5 mm long, 5 mm wide, brown.

description: Shrub or tree 1.5-6 m tall, 5-10 cm dbh. Leaf blade oblanceolate or sometimes narrow-obovate, 17.5-36.4 cm long, 4.6-11 cm wide, acuminate at apex often with a blunt tip, cuneate to long-decurrent at base, with 7-13 secondary veins per side; petiole flat- tened adaxially, 0.5-3 cm long. Inflorescence produced at base of new season's growth, above a series of bracts, lateral but not obviously axillary, perhaps truly terminal and surpassed during same growth flush by development of uppermost axillary bud; peduncle 19.7-34.5 cm long, glabrous, at apex bearing 3-9 pedicellate flowers in 2-3 proximate clusters; bracts deciduous before anthesis, linear, 2-6.2 mm long, 0.5- 1 mm wide; pedicels 2.4-4.7 cm long in flower, 2.4-6.2 cm in fruit, sparsely appressed-puberulent, glabrescent. Calyx in flower 5-lobed for 1/2 its length or more, 2.5- 3.5 cm long, with lanceolate lobes 0.6-1.1 cm wide at widest point, conspicuously glandular-tuberculate when dry and glabrous without, puberulent and with spherical hairs of which the contents turn dark in age within, pale green becoming white at anthesis, persistent in mature fruit, absent in old fruit. Corolla slightly zygomorphic in the lobes, funnelform, 4.5-6 cm long, the tube straight, 2.5-4 cm long, 0.7-0.9 cm wide at apex, glabrous within, the lobes wide-obovate, rounded at apex, 1.7-1.8 cm long, ca 1.5 cm wide, recurved, the innermost slightly wider than others and in an upper position. Androecium of 5 fertile stamens; filaments connate into a tube adnate to corolla tube, with free tip 3-5 mm long, glabrous, white; anthers oblong, 7.2-7.5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, glabrous, without basal appendages, white. Disc entire or slightly undulate, 2.3-2.5 mm high. Carpels free except at apex in style, ca 1.5 mm high, truncate and two-ridged at apex, glandular- tuberculate, glabrous; style to 44 mm long, glabrous, white. Fruiting mericarps 1.6-1.9 cm high, 1-1.1 cm deep, truncate at apex, glabrous, enclosed by persistent sepals. Seeds 6.7 mm long, 5 mm wide, rusty brown.

description: Unbranched treelet. Leaf blade oblanceolate, acuminate, acute, or rounded at apex, acute or cuneate at base, 42.8-69 cm long, 7.8-12 cm wide, with 20-21 ("15-25") secondary veins per side; petiole canaliculate adaxially, 3-4.5 cm long. Inflorescence a sessile cymose cluster of short-shoots to ca 1 cm long, arising from midrib on lower surface of leaf 1/2-9/10 of the way up  base, with pedicel scars very close together; bract at base of one cyme lanceolate, 11.4 cm long, 3.7 cm wide, sessile; pedicels ca 1 cm long, sparsely appressed-puberulent. Calyx in flower campanulate, 3-lobed for ca 1/3 its length, 2.5 cm long, 0.9 cm wide at middle, glabrous or with scattered appressed puberulence and inconspicuously glandular-punctate without, appressed-puberulent within, "green." Corolla +/- actinomorphic, minutely tomentulose at base of lobes within, "white, washed with pink," the tube straight, 1.6 cm long, 0.2 cm wide at apex, with a sparsely pilose ring 5 mm wide beginning 10 mm above the base within, the lobes wide to narrow-obovate, rounded at apex, 2.9-3.4 cm long, 1.5-1.7 cm wide. Androecium of 2 ("3") fertile stamens and (2) 3 unequal staminodes; filaments adnate to the corolla, minutely curly tomentulose at base abaxially; fertile filaments with free tip 2.5-3 mm long, 1.8 mm wide at base, the anthers lorate, 10.3-10.5 mm long, 1.5-1.6 mm wide, glabrous, the appendages 0.7 mm long; middle staminode 13 mm and 2 flanking ones 22-24 mm long. Disc "urceolate-tubular," "enclosing ovary." Carpels densely pubescent; stigma "capitate." Fruiting mericarps not known.
bibliographicCitation: Kallunki, Jacquelyn A. 1992. A revision of Erythrochiton sensu lato (Cuspariinae, Rutaceae). Brittonia. 44: 107-139.

description: Few-branched shrub or tree 1.5-6 m tall. Leaf blade oblanceolate to narrow-obovate, acuminate to obtuse at apex, cuneate to acute at base, 17.8-60.5 cm long, 7.5- 18.5 cm wide, with 14-23 veins per side; petiole canaliculate or flattened adaxially, 2.8-9.8 cm long. Inflorescence lateral but not obviously axillary, perennating, with short-shoots of flowers, to 68.5 cm long; peduncle angled, glabrous; bracts 2.3-9.5 mm long, 0.7-1.4 mm wide, oblong to oblanceolate; pedicels 1.8-2.6 cm long in flow- er, 1.9-3.5 cm in fruit, glabrous. Calyx in flower 5-lobed for about 1/2 its length, 2.3- 2.7 cm long, with lobes 0.5-0.7 cm wide at widest part, glabrous without, puberulent within, red, in fruit more deeply divided, to 1 cm wide, and persistent. Corolla +/- acti- nomorphic, 6.1-7.2 cm long, glabrous without, the tube straight, 3.6-4.3 cm long, 0.4- 0.7 cm wide at apex, puberulent within, the lobes wide to narrow obovate, rounded at apex, 2.5-3.2 cm long, 1.2-1.6 cm wide, spreading to recurved. Androecium of 2 fer- tile stamens and 5 (7) staminodes; filaments adnate to corolla tube for most of their length; fertile filaments with free ovate tip 5-8 mm long, glabrous, the anthers narrow oblong, 7-8.3 (1 1) mm long, 1.4-1.7 mm wide, glabrous, the appendages ca 0.5 mm long; staminodes connate into a glabrous, 5 (7)-toothed tongue 8-14 mm long and 4.3- 7 mm wide. Disc entire, 3-4.5 mm high. Carpels connate only at base, 1-1.5 cm high, glabrous; style 40-45 mm long, glabrous; stigma oblique. Fruiting mericarps 1.5-1.7 cm high, 0.9 cm deep, glabrous, dorsally keeled but not winged. Seeds 6-7 mm long, 3.2-4 mm wide, brown.

description: Treelet unbranched, 2-4 m tall. Leaf blade oblanceolate, obtusely short-acuminate at apex, cuneate at base, 47-79.5 cm long, 12.2-18.2 cm wide, with 20-33 secondary veins per side; petiole canaliculate adaxially, 6.5-7.3 cm long. Inflorescence axillary and arching upward (Foster & Baldeon 12848), perennating, with short-shoots, 26- 47 cm long; peduncle angled at least at base, glabrous; bract (one seen) oblanceolate, 20 cm long and 3.5 cm wide; pedicels 3.7-4.5 cm long in flower, 3.8-4.5 cm long in fruit, glabrous. Calyx in flower 5-lobed for 1/6 to 2/3 its length, 2-2.5 cm long, 1.6-1.8 cm wide at middle, glabrous without, densely short velutinous and with midvein of each sepal prominent within, greenish white (Foster & Baldeon 12848), persistent or not in fruit. Corolla 3.8-4.2 cm long, the tube straight, 1.7-2.1 cm long, 0.6-0.75 cm wide at apex, moderately pubescent with short straight hairs without, glabrous within, the lobes wide-obovate, rounded at apex, 1.6-2.1 cm long, 0.8-1.2 cm wide. Androecium of 4 fertile stamens and 1 sometimes once-cleft staminode ca 1.3 cm long; filaments connate into a tube adnate to corolla tube, with glabrous free tip 3-5 mm long; anthers narrow- oblong, ca 9.5 mm long, ca 2.8 mm wide, sparsely puberulent on connective abaxially, with minute basal appendages to 0.4 mm long. Disc 3-5 mm high. Carpels free except at apex in style, 1-2 mm high, densely pubescent; style ca 24 mm long at anthesis, glabrous. Fruiting mericarps 1.5-1.7 cm high, 0.7-1 cm deep, sparsely appressed- pubescent. Seeds unknown.

description: Arbor parva ramulis crassiusculis laete griseo-brunnescentibus. Cataphylla disticha, stipulis foli- aribus similia, nigrescentia. Stipulae foliares persistentes, transverse triangulares, subcoriaceae, striate nervosae, apice esetulosae vel raro breviter 2-setulosae. Folia petiolata decidua; laminae suborbiculares, apice retusae, basi rotundatae, firme chartaceae, ubique impolitae, petiolo dorsiventraliter valde complanato. Flores e brachyblastis annotinis in cataphyllorum axillis nati, longe pedicillati. Calyx ad medium divisus, lobulis membranaceis venosis interdum cohaerentibus. Petali lamina ampla late ovata vel obovata, ungue parvo obtriangulari et ligula bilobata munita. Urceolus stamineus calycem aequans vel calyce paulo brevior, margine integer. Styli liberi.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. 1986. Four new species of Erythroxylum (Erythroxylaceae) from northeastern Brazil. Brittonia. 38: 189-200.

description: Small tree. Bark on branchlets grayish-brown to light tan, longitudinally wrinkled, the lenticels elongate, light tan; bark on older twigs dark brown, dotted with pale tan lenticels, longitudinally fissured. Branchlets distichous, sparse, consisting of both long and short shoots, diverging 40-60º from axis, compressed slightly at apex, ca 2 mm in diam, straight or somewhat flexuous. Internodes 3-20 mm long on long shoots, 0.5-0.7 mm long on short shoots. Cataphylls (ramenta) distichous, produced at base of new shoots for 7-10 mm, scarcely overlapping, similar to foliar stipules, persistent, turning black with age, the spinule (leaf rudiment) short, 1-1.1 mm long, stout, black. Foliarstipules persistent, appressed to stem, diverging somewhat with age, transversely triangular, 2-2.5 mm long, subcoriaceous, with flaking waxy covering, striate-nerved with 3-5 parallel, often branching nerves per side, obtuse to rounded at apex, the setae lacking or rarely with two very short setae, the keels prominent, slightly alate, the margin minutely erose. Leaves deciduous, 1 or 2 produced at tips of short shoots or scattered on long shoots, petiolate, the lamina undulate, suborbicular, retuse at apex, rounded at base, 30-35 mm long, 28-38 mm wide, firmly chartaceous, adaxially drying dull brown, abaxially drying pale tan, dull on both surfaces, elineate with no distinct central panel, the midrib flat on adaxial surface, drying ferruginous on both surfaces, the major nerves 10-11 per side, diverging 45-60? from midrib, more or less straight or somewhat upcurving, more or less parallel, arcuately anastomosing 3-5 mm from margin, adaxially prominulous, adaxially distinct, dark reddish-brown, the veinlets very finely reticulate, distinct. Petiole flattened dorsiventrally, 6-7 mm long, ca 1.2 mm in diam, adaxially shallowly grooved, drying dark brown. Flowers fasciculate in axils of past season's cataphylls, 1 or 2 per node, large and con- spicuous. Bracteoles triangular-ovate, 0.7-0.8 mm long, long-acuminate at apex, the acumen (seta) 0.5-1 mm long. Pedicel slender, distinctly 5-ribbed, 8-10 mm long, 0.7-0.8 mm in diam, thickened slightly toward apex. Calyx 2.5-3 mm long, divided ca 1/2 its length, the lobes triangular-ovate, 1.3-1.5 mm long, acuminate, membranous, longitudinally veined, the lobes sometimes coherent such that the calyx is 3-lobed. Petal white, the lamina spreading, ample, more or less plane, slightly concave at middle, broadly ovate to elliptic, rounded at apex, 4-4.5 mm long, 2.8-3.2 mm wide, the claw obtriangular, 2-2.5 mm long, the ligule 1.5-2 mm long, bilobate with a short, erect posterior medial appendage and a short triangular, inflexed anterior medial flap, the lobes simple, ovate, markedly erose at margin, ca 1.5 mm long. Staminal cup slightly shorter than calyx lobes, 1.8-2 mm long, entire at margin. Brachystylousflowers: filaments ca 5 mm long, the anthers ovate in outline, ca 0.8 mm long; styles free, 2.5 mm long, the stigmas large, broadly depressed-capitate, 0.5-0.6 mm long. Dolichostylousflowers: not seen. Ovary narrowly ellipsoid, 1.5 times length of staminal cup, 3 mm long. Drupe unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. 1986. Four new species of Erythroxylum (Erythroxylaceae) from northeastern Brazil. Brittonia. 38: 189-200.

description: Frutex vel arbor parva, ramis adscendentibus, ramulis laevibus. Cataphylla pauca disticha stipulis foliaribus similia. Stipulae foliares triangulari-ovatae vel lanceolatae membranaceae laeves non striato nervosae, apice minute 2-setulosae. Folia decidua breviter petiolata laminis ellipticis vel oblongis raro obovatis, apice rotundatis vel retusis, basi obtusis vel rotundatis, chartaceis vel subcoriaceis, subtus elineatis plerumque areolatis pallidis, ubique manifeste reticulato-nervosis. Flores pauci e ramulis aphyllis annotinis ad nodos nati. Urceolus stamineus dimidio calyce brevior, margine integer vel crenulatus. Drupa (maturam non vidi) oblongoidea, endocarpio oblongoideo, apice acuto vel retuso, inaequaliter 4-sulcato, uniloculari.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. 1988. New taxa of Erythroxylum (Erythroxylaceae) from the Venezuelan Guayana. Brittonia. 40: 256-268.

description: Shrub or treelet to 5 m tall, arising from 1 or several trunks; trunk to 6 cm in diam near base, the bark tan to grayish, relatively smooth, with fine longitudinal fissures. Branches ascending, relatively short and straight. Branchlets diverging 50-70º from axis, often appearing "knobby" at nodes with remnants of bracteoles, compressed toward apex, becoming terete, 2-3 mm in diam, grayish to dark brown or nearly black, smooth, becoming longitudinally finely striate, without distinct lenticels. Internodes 3-25 mm long. Cataphylls (ramenta) few, appearing at base of shoots, similar to stipules, chartaceous, usually not evident after one season, the spinule (leaf rudiment) 0.7-1.5 mm long, somewhat flattened, reddish-brown. Foliar stipules lasting one season, distichous, erect and appressed to stem, tri- angular-ovate to lanceolate, 2-3 mm long, membranous, nonstriate, pale green turning light brown on drying, obtuse or truncate at apex, with or without 2 minute apical setae, if present the setae 0.2-0.3 mm long, the margin minutely fimbriate to entire. Leaves completely deciduous, distichous, short-petiolate, the lamina plane, elliptic to oblong, rarely obovate, rounded or retuse at apex, obtuse to rounded at base, 4-11.5 cm long, 2.5-6.5 cm wide, chartaceous to subcoriaceous when fully mature, yellowish-green on the upper surface, very pale green on lower surface, abaxially dull on both surfaces, the lower surface not lineate but often with a distinct, paler green central panel, the adaxial midrib flat or narrowly canaliculate with a very slender medial ridge, the lateral nerves 15-20 per side, more or less straight, diverging at 50-70º from midrib, anastomosing 5-7 mm  from margin, the lateral nerves at maturity and usually also the veinlets conspicuous on both surfaces. Petiole 1.5-4 mm long, ca 1 mm in diam, subterete, a little flattened adaxially. Flowers appearing in last season's leaf axils when plant is completely leafless, 1-6 per node, sometimes rather congested at adjacent nodes, creamy white. Bracteoles broadly ovate to orbicular, concave, 1-1.4 mm long, rounded and abruptly acuminate at apex, paleaceous, persisting 1 season and giving twigs a knobby appearance. Pedicel terete, at anthesis 2-5 mm long, 0.5 mm in diam, in fruit very slender, elongating up to 15 mm long. Calyx 1.5-2 mm long, divided 3/4-5/6 its length, the lobes ovate to lanceolate, 1.3-1.8 mm long, membranous, pale green with thinner, paler green margins, acuminate at apex, the lobes recurving conspicuously following fertilization. Petal lamina broadly ovate to suborbicular, concave, rounded and sometimes incurved at apex, 2.8-3 mm long, 2-2.7 mm wide, the claw short, 0.8 mm long, 1.6 mm wide, thickened at base, the ligule bilobed, 1.5-2 mm long, the posterior auricle ovate, 1.5-2 mm long, the anterior auricle short, cuff-like, 0.8-1 mm long. Staminal cup 1/2 as long as calyx, 0.6-1 mm long, the margin entire or crenulate. Brachystylous flowers: filaments 2.5-3 mm long, the anthers suborbicular, 0.5-0.6 mm long; styles free, 1.2 mm long, the stigmas depressed-capitate, 0.4 mm long. Dolichostylous flowers: antisepalous filaments ca 1 mm long, the anthers suborbicular, 0.7 mm long; antipetalous filaments ca 2.2 mm long, the anthers suborbicular, 0.6 mm long; styles free or rarely and variably coherent, ca 4 mm long, the stigma depressed- capitate, 0.5 mm long. Ovary ellipsoid, rounded at apex, 1.8 mm long, twice as long as staminal cup. Drupe (somewhat immature) oblongoid, 8-10 mm long, 4 mm in diam, red at maturity, the mesocarp ca 0.4 mm thick, the endocarp oblongoid, straight, acute or obtuse at apex, 7-9 mm long, to 4 mm in diam, unequally 4-sulcate, unilocular, with abundant endosperm. Embryo ca 6.8 mm long; cotyledons oblong-lanceolate, rounded at apex, 4.5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, 0.4 mm thick; radicle 2 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. 1988. New taxa of Erythroxylum (Erythroxylaceae) from the Venezuelan Guayana. Brittonia. 40: 256-268.

description: Arbor parva, ramulis rectis crassiusculis tegumento laeve suberoso pallide coriicolore obtectis. Cataphylla pauca disticha nigrescentia, stipulis foliaribus similia. Stipulae foliares triangulari-ovatae coriaceae estriatae, apice fortiter 3-setulosae demum deciduae. Folia petiolata persistentia, laminis ellipticis oblongis vel obovatis, apice rotundatis retusisque, basi obtusis vel late cuneatis, coriaceis. Flores pauci e ramulis homotinis maturis in axillis foliorum vel cataphyllorum nati. Urceolus stamineus calycem aequans margine integro. Drupa sicca oblongoideo-fusiformis, endocarpio oblong- oideo-fusiformi leviter compresso irregulariter 6-sulcato uniloculari, apice anguste acuto et parum excentrico, endospermio mediocri.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. 1988. New taxa of Erythroxylum (Erythroxylaceae) from the Venezuelan Guayana. Brittonia. 40: 256-268.

description: Tree to 6 m tall with dense crown. Branchlets distichous, only rarely differ- entiated into long and short shoots, diverging 40-60º from axis, rather stout, ca 2 mm in diam, coated with a very light tan, smooth, thin-suberous layer, without lenticels. Internodes on normal shoots 1-20 mm long, on the occasional short shoots, 0.5-2 mm. Cataphylls distichous, few, produced at base of new shoots for 3-8 mm along stem, often overlapping, similar to but slightly larger than foliar stipules, drying black, tardily fugacious, the spinule somewhat flattened dorsi- ventrally, 0.6-1.4 mm long, drying black. Foliar stipules persisting 1 season, appressed to stem, diverging in age, broadly triangular-ovate, 1.5-3.5 mm long, coriaceous, non-striate but sometimes minutely longitudinally wrinkled, covered with thin flakes of wax when new, drying black, obtuse at apex, 3-setulose, the setae appearing rather stiff or filamentous, the lateral setae 0.5-1.1 mm long, the medial seta ca 0.5 mm long, evanescent, the keels slender, the margin minutely erose or entire. Leaves persistent, scattered on twigs, appearing dense, distichous, petiolate, the lamina held more or less erect, elliptic, oblong, or obovate, rounded and retuse at apex, obtuse or broadly cuneate at base, 2.5-8 cm long, 1.8-4 cm wide, coriaceous, adaxially drying dark grayish-brown and more or less shiny,abaxially drying dark reddish-brown and dull, elineate with no distinct central panel, the adaxial midrib slender, narrowly acute in cross-section, the lateral nerves 8-12, diverging 50-65º from midrib, straight or somewhat sinuous, anastomosing 2-6 mm from margin, prominulous or obscure on either surface, the veinlets finely reticulate, prominulous to obscure. Petiole 2-5 mm long, ca 1 mm in diam, subterete in cross-section, very shallowly canaliculate, drying black. Flowers borne in axils of leaves or cataphylls near tips of mature twigs of current season, 1-3 flowers per node. Bracteoles triangular-ovate, concave, 0.7-1 mm long, scarious, acute or acuminate at apex, sometimes short-setulose, the keel slender, sub-alate. Pedicel slender, lightly 5-ribbed, 5-7 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm in diam. Calyx 1.2-1.5 mm long, divided ca 1/2 its length, the lobes broadly triangular, 0.6-0.8 mm long, abruptly short-acuminate at apex. Petals unknown. Staminal cup equaling the calyx, ca 1 mm long, 10-glandular at middle, the margin entire. Brachystylousflowers (remnant in fruit): filaments ca 2.5 mm long. Dolichostylous flowers unknown. Drupe when dried oblongoid-fusiform, acute and somewhat eccentric at apex, ca 9.5 mm long, 3-4 mm in diam, the mesocarp ca 0.3 mm thick, the endocarp oblongoid-fusiform, lightly compressed (ca 3.5 mm wide x 2.5 mm thick), irregularly 6-sulcate, acute or slightly acuminate at apex, unilocular, the endosperm occupying ca 1/3 of locule. Embryo ca 6.7 mm long; cotyledons oblong-ovate, 4.5-5.5 mm long, 1.7-2 mm wide, ca 0.5 mm thick, rounded at apex, subcordate at base; radicle slender, 1-1.4 mm long, ca 0.3 mm in diam.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. 1988. New taxa of Erythroxylum (Erythroxylaceae) from the Venezuelan Guayana. Brittonia. 40: 256-268.

description: Frutex. Ramuli recti vel nonnumquam flexuosi, brunnei vel nigrescentes, lenticellis conspicuis elongatis albidis provisi. Cataphylla disticha, stipulis foliaribus similia, siccitate badia. Stipulae foliares persistentes triangulari-ovatae vel oblongo-ovatae, striate nervosae, apice 3-setulosae. Folia breviter petiolata persistentia(?); laminae ellipticae vel obovatae, apice obtusae vel rotundatae, basi obtusae vel acutae, chartaceae. Flores e ramulis homotinis in cataphyllorum vel foliorum axillis nati. Petali lamina ovato-oblonga, ungue obtriangulari vel rectangulari et ligula bilobata provisa. Urceolus stami- neus calyce brevior, margine integer. Styli usque ad medium connati. Drupa anguste ovoidea, apice obtusa vel rotundata, endocarpio anguste ovoideo 6-sulcato uniloculari et endospermio parvo provisa.
bibliographicCitation: Plowman, Timothy C. 1986. Four new species of Erythroxylum (Erythroxylaceae) from northeastern Brazil. Brittonia. 38: 189-200.

description: Shrub. Bark on branchlets dark brown to blackish, longitudinally wrinkled, furnished with conspicuous, elongate, whitish lenticels; bark on older twigs light to dark brown, longitudinally striate. Branchlets weakly differentiated into long and short shoots, distichous, straight or somewhat flexuous, diverging 40-65º from axis, compressed toward apex, ca 1 mm in diam. Internodes 3-20 mm long on long shoots, ca 0.5 mm long on short shoots. Cataphylls (ramenta) distichous, 5-7 scattered along base of new twigs or congested at apex of short shoots, similar to foliar stipules, persisting, 2-3.2 mm long, drying dark reddish-brown, the spinule (leaf rudiment) slender, dorsiventrally flattened, black, 1.2-2.2 mm long, apically sharp-attenuate. Foliar stipules persistent, distichous, appressed to stem, diverging somewhat with age, triangular-ovate to oblong-ovate, 1.5-3 mm long, subcoriaceous, striate-nerved with 3-5 parallel, irregularly branched nerves per side, drying dark reddish-brown, truncate or rounded at apex, 3-setulose, the 2 lateral setae 0.3-1.5 mm long, the medial seta 0.2-0.4 mm long, the setae eva- nescent, the keels sub-alate, the margins entire, becoming revolute. Leaves per- sistent(?), scattered on new twigs or 1 or 2 at apex of short shoots, distichous, short-petiolate, the lamina plane, elliptic to obovate, at apex obtuse to rounded, rarely wide-acute or retuse, at base obtuse to acute, 20-58 mm long, 12-32 mm wide, chartaceous, drying dark brown adaxially, drying lighter brown or ferrugi- nous abaxially, dull on both surfaces, abaxially elineate with no distinct central panel, the adaxial midrib flat with a low, fine medial ridge or broadly acute in cross-section, drying dark brown adaxially, ferruginous abaxially, the lateral nerves 10-13, diverging 50-75º from midrib, straight or somewhat crooked, more or less parallel, arcuately anastomosing 1.5-3 mm from midrib, indistinct on both sur- faces, the veinlets obscure adaxially, finely reticulate abaxially. Petiole 2-3.5 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm in diam, subterete, adaxially broadly canaliculate, drying dark brown. Flowers fasciculate in axils of leaves or cataphylls on current season's twigs, 1-4 per node. Bracteoles triangular-ovate to lanceolate, 0.7-1.3 mm long, firmly membranous, narrowly acute to acuminate at apex, the keel sub-alate, the seta 0.2-0.7 mm long. Pedicel slender, 5-ribbed, 3-5.5 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm in diam. Calyx 1.5-2 mm long, divided 1/2-3/4 its length, the lobes narrowly ovate to lanceolate, 1.2-1.5 mm long, narrowly acute to acuminate at apex; calyx in bud 5-angled, apiculate. Petal creamy white, the lamina ovate-oblong in outline, concave at upper middle, rounded at apex, 1.5-2 mm long, 1-1.2 mm wide, the claw obtriangular or rectangular, subcordate at base, 1-1.2 mm long, the ligule ca 0.8 mm long, 2-lobed, each lobe consisting of two auricles, the smaller anterior auricles rounded, 0.5 mm long, the longer posterior auricles ovate, 0.7 mm long. Staminal cup 2/3-5/6 times length of calyx, 0.8-1 mm long, the margin entire. Brachystylous flowers: filaments ca 2 mm long, the anthers orbicular in outline, 0.3 mm in diam; styles 0.9-1 mm long, connate 0.2-0.5 mm at base, the stigmas depressed-capitate, 0.2-0.3 mm long. Dolichostylousflowers: antisepalous filaments 0.5-0.7 mm long, the anthers orbicular, ca 0.5 mm long; antipetalous filaments 0.9-1 mm long, the anthers orbicular, ca 0.45 mm long; styles 2.2-2.8 mm long, connate 1.1-1.5 mm at base, the stigmas depressed-capitate, 0.2-0.3 mm long. Ovary narrowly ellip- soid, slightly longer than staminal cup, 1-1.5 mm long. Drupe narrowly ovoid, obtuse or rounded at apex, ca 9 mm long, ca 4.5 mm in diam, red at maturity, the mesocarp ca 0.5 mm thick, the endocarp narrowly ovoid, 6-sulcate, 1 -locular; endosperm occupying ca 25% of locule. Embryo 6 mm long; cotyledons elliptic, cordate at base, 5 mm long, 3 mm wide, 1 mm thick; radicle 1.7 mm long, 0.5 mm in diam.

description: Frutex. Ramuli recti, lenticellis abundanter punctati. Cataphylla disticha stipulis foliorum similia sed paulo majora. Stipulae foliares persistentes, triangulari-ovatae vel ovatae, manifeste striate ner- vosae, apice 3-setulosae. Folia breviter petiolata, persistentia; laminae lanceolatae, nonnumquam oblongae vel anguste ellipticae, apice acutae vel breviter acuminatae, apice ipso obtusae retusae, chartaceae. Flores e ramulis hornotinis maturis in cataphyllorum vel foliorum axillis nati. Petali lamina ovata vel oblonga ungue lato et ligula bilobata munita. Urceolus stamineus calyce sesquilongior, margine integer. Styli liberi. Drupa oblongo-ovoidea apice obtusa, endocarpio oblongo-ovoideo tereti uniloculari et endospermio nullo provisa. Embryo cotyledonibus ovatis vel ellipticis crassis provisus.

description: Shrub 1.5-2.5 m tall. Bark on branchlets reddish- to grayish-brown, longitu- dinally wrinkled, amply dotted with punctate to elongate, cream-colored lenticels; bark on older twigs light to dark brown, longitudinally wrinkled and finely fissured, dotted with light tan, punctate lenticels. Branchlets consisting only of long shoots, distichous, slender, straight, diverging 45-75º from axis, compressed toward apex, 1.3-1.5 mm in diam. Internodes 1-25 mm long. Cataphylls (ramenta) 3-7 at base of shoots, covering stem for 2-6 mm, persistent, similar to but slightly larger than stipules, 2-3 (4) mm long, reddish-brown, the spinule (leaf rudiment) straight, dorsiventrally flattened, 0.9-1.2 mm long, black, tapered to a sharp point at apex, the tip recurving slightly. Foliar stipules persistent, appressed to stem, diverging with age, triangular-ovate to ovate, 1.3-2.5 mm long, firmly chartaceous, markedly striate-nerved with 5-6 (8) slender, parallel, closely spaced nerves per side, the apex obtuse or truncate, 3-setulose, the setae filiform, evanescent, the lateral setae 0.3-0.8 mm long, the medial seta 0.2-0.7 mm long, the keels slightly alate, the margins entire, thin. Leaves persistent, scattered on branchlets, distichous, short- petiolate, the lamina plane, lanceolate, sometimes oblong or narrowly elliptic, acute to short-acuminate at apex, the tip itself obtuse and shallowly retuse, broadly to narrowly acute at base, 25-67 mm long, 13-32 mm wide, chartaceous, adaxially drying dark grayish-green or grayish-brown, appearing metallic, abaxially drying ferruginous, rather shiny on both surfaces, elineate with no central panel, the midrib flat or slightly raised and broadly triangular in cross-section, with a slender low medial ridge, the lateral nerves 9-12, diverging 50-90? from midrib, straight or somewhat upcurved, arcuately anastomosing 2-5 mm from margin, adaxially faint, abaxially prominulous, distinct, the veinlets reticulate, adaxially obscure, abaxially distinct. Petiole 1.5-3.5 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm in diam, subterete in cross-section, adaxially broadly canaliculate, drying dark reddish-brown. Flowers fasciculate in axils of leaves or cataphylls on mature twigs of current season, 1- 5 per node. Bracteoles persistent, cymbiform, broadly ovate in outline, 0.7-1.2 mm long, paleaceous, strongly keeled and sparingly nerved with 1-3 faint lon- gitudinal nerves per side, obtuse to widely acute at apex, the seta 0.2-0.3 mm long. Pedicel slender, markedly 5-ribbed, 1.5-3 (7.5) mm long, 0.4-0.8 mm in diam at anthesis, elongating after anthesis to 3.5-4.5 mm. Calyx 1-1.5 mm long, divided ca 1/2 its length, coriaceous, the lobes broadly triangular, 0.4-0.7 mm long, acute to short-acuminate at apex. Petal white, the lamina more or less plane, ovate to oblong, obtuse to rounded at apex, 1.5-2.5 mm long, 1.2-1.5 mm wide, the claw ca 1 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, basally subcordate, the ligule 2-lobed, 0.8-1.2 mm long, each lobe with two auricles, the larger posterior auricles 0.8- 1.2 mm long, ovate, concave, rounded at apex, erose at margin, the shorter anterior auricles 0.4-0.5 mm long, subhemispheric, with a small appendage between and immediately behind the posterior lobes, the appendage short, thickened, irregularly and shallowed 1-3-lobed, recurving slightly at apex. Staminal cup 1.2-1.5 times length of calyx, 0.8-1 mm long, entire at margin. Brachystylous flowers: filaments ca 2 mm long, the anthers suborbicular in outline, 0.4-0.5 mm long; styles free, 0.7-0.8 mm long, the stigmas depressed-capitate, ca 0.2 mm long. Dolichostylous flowers: antisepalous filaments 0.5-0.6 mm long, the anthers sub-orbicular, 0.4-0.5 mm long; antipetalous filaments 0.8-1.2 mm long, the anthers suborbicular in outline, 0.4-0.5 mm long; styles free, 1.7-1.8 mm long, the stigmas depressed-capitate, 0.2-0.3 mm long. Ovary subglobose to obovoid, a little longer than the staminal cup, 0.8-1 mm long. Drupe oblong-ovoid, drying ampullaceous when immature, apically obtuse, ca 8-9 mm long, 4.5-6 mm in diam, red at maturity, the mesocarp 0.6 mm thick, the endocarp oblong-ovoid, terete, uni- locular, lacking endosperm. Embryo 5-7.5 mm long; cotyledons thick, ovate or elliptic, cordate at base, 3.5-5.5 mm long, 2.7-3.8 mm wide, 1-1.7 mm thick, the radicle 1.5 mm long, 0.6 mm in diam.

description: Frutex. Ramuli atro-brunnei vel rubro-brunnei. Stipulae persistentes, manifeste striatae, bisetulosae. Folia brevissime petiolata, decidua; laminae forma variabiles, anguste vel late ellipticae, obovatae vel lanceolatae, apice obtusae, rotundatae vel retusae, chartaceae. Flores in axillis ramentorum vel foliorum a brachyblastis hornotinis producti, brevissime pedunculati. Petali lamina cymbiformis, anguste ovata. Urceolus stamineus quam calyx paulo longior, ad marginem 1 0-denticulatus. Drupa ellipsoidea, parum subfalcata et lateraliter compressa, apice rotundata, umbonulata, endocarpio curvato-ellipsoideo, lateribus excavatis triquetro, triloculari, loculi vacuis duobus magnis, loculo fertili parvo. Ab Erythroxylo laetevirenti 0. E. Schulz stipulis, petiolis et bracteolis brevioribus, pedicellis et urceolis stamineis multo longioribus et drupis minoribus differt.

description: Shrub 2.5-5 m tall with up to 3 main trunks 3-5 cm in diam near base. Bark on trunk smooth, greyish brown, punctate with light green dots and longitudinally striate with fine, light tan streaks, about 1 mm thick, dark reddish brown within. Branches erect-spreading, somewhat storied, lying in one plane, greyish brown. Branchlets distichous, consisting mainly of short shoots, more or less straight, diverging 30º-60º from axis, apically somewhat laterally compressed and often scaly ramentaceous, 1-2 mm in diam, dark reddish to blackish brown, smooth, somewhat shiny, often furnished with light tan, attenuate lenticels. Internodes on long shoots 3-15 mm long, on short shoots 0.2-2 mm long. Ramenta produced at base of long shoots or along short shoots, usually covering stem, 4-10 mm long, 2.5-4 mm wide. Stipules persistent, gradually disintegrating and wearing away, appressed to stem or diverging somewhat from axis, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.8-3.0 mm long, chartaceous, distinctly striate with 1-3 nerves per side, pale green, soon turning light brown, apically obtuse to acute, 2-setulose, the setae 0.3-0.5 mm long, evanescent, the keels prominent, somewhat alate and fimbriate when new, the margin erose-fimbriate to entire. Leaves deciduous, 1-2 produced at apex of short shoots or scattered along long shoots, distichous, short-petiolate, the lamina plane, variable in shape, narrowly to broadly elliptic, obovate or lanceolate, apically blunt, rounded or retuse, sometimes with a very short mucron 0.1 mm long, basally cuneate to narrowed, rarely rounded, 25-70 mm long, 14-40 mm wide, membranaceous, light to dark green above, pale glaucous green to silvery green beneath, dull above, sometimes drying somewhat shiny, dull beneath, elineate, the adaxial midrib flat or slightly raised, the lateral nerves 10-15, straight, somewhat irregularly diverging 25º-60º from midrib, prominulous above when dried, less distinct beneath, the veinlets reticulate, irregular. Petiole short, 1-2 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm in diam, canaliculate. Flowers in axils of leaves or ramenta, primarily on short shoots of the current season's growth, 1-2 flowers per node, white or greenish white, individual flowers sometimes short-pedunculate, the peduncle articulating with the pedicel to 1 mm long, thickened at apex into a short, broad torus. Bracteoles 2 per flower, somewhat protruding, broadly ovate to triangular ovate, 1.0-1.2 mm long, obtuse to acute at apex, 1-setulose, the setae 0.3-0.5 mm long. Pedicel pentangular, sparingly 5-alate, 3.5-6 mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm in diam. Calyx 1.2-2.5 mm long, divided less than 1/2 the length, the lobes triangular-ovate, apically acute, 0.5-1.3 mm long. Petal limb spreading, cymbiform or ladle-like, coriaceous throughout, narrowly ovate in outline, apically acute, blunt or rounded, 1.5-2 mm long, 1.0-1.2 mm wide, the claw 1.0-1.8 mm long, minutely papillose, the ligule 0.6-1.4 mm long, bilobate with a short, truncate, anterior-medial flap between the lobes, 0.2 mm long, the auricles rounded with irregularly erose margins. Staminal cup 1.2-1.8 times length of calyx, 1.2-1.5 mm long, the margin 1 0-denticulate. Brachystylous-flowers: filaments 2.0-2.5 mm long, the anthers orbicular, 0.4-0.5 mm long; style 1.1-1.5 mm long; stigma depressed-capitate, 0.2-0.3 mm long. Dolichostylous flowers: antesepalous filaments 0.2-1.0 mm long, the anthers orbicular, 0.35-0.5 mm long; antepetalous filaments 0.4-1.7 mm long, the anthers orbicular, 0.3-0.5 mm long; styles 1.5-2.5 mm long; stigmas depressed-capitate, 0.2-0.3 mm long. Ovary narrowly ellipsoid, apically rounded or truncate, equaling the staminal cup in length, 1.2-1.5 mm long. Drupe ellipsoid, somewhat falcate and laterally compressed, apically rounded and usually wearing a small umbo to 0.2 mm long, 5.8-7.5 mm long, 3.3-3.5 mm in diam, red at maturity, the mesocarp 0.2-0.3 mm thick, the endocarp falcate-ellipsoid, prominently 3-ribbed, 3-celled with 1 small fertile cell and 2 large empty cells, the endosperm occupying 1/2 to 2/3 of fertile cell. Embryo 5-6 mm long; cotyledons oblong, flattened, apically rounded, 3.8-4.5 mm long, 1.2-1.4 mm wide; radicle 1.5 mm long, terete.

description: Frutex. Ramuli laeves badii vel nigrescentes lenticellis albidis punctati. Cataphylla disticha, stipulis folioribus similia vel parum majora. Stipulae foliares mox deciduae, transverse triangulares, obscure striate nervosae, apice truncatae, 2-setulosae. Folia breviter petiolata decidua; laminae ellipticae vel ovatae, apice et basi rotundatae vel parum retusae, firme chartaceae, ubique impolitae. Flores e basibus ramulorum homotinorum in cataphyllorum axillis nati, bracteolis linearibus apice fimbriatis muniti. Urceolus stamineus calyce dimidio brevior, margine integer. Styli liberi. Drupa endocarpio oblongo-ovoideo, manifeste 6-sulcato, uniloculari provisa.

description: Shrub. Bark on branchlets longitudinally wrinkled, dark reddish-brown to blackish, the lenticels elongate, drying reddish-brown, not breaking surface; bark on older twigs dark grayish-brown, longitudinally fissured, dotted with whitish, punctate lenticels. Branchlets distichous, leafy, without short shoots, diverging 45-70º from axis, compressed toward apex, 1-1.5 mm in diam. Internodes 1-20 mm long. Cataphylls (ramenta) few, scattered, distichous, similar to but sometimes larger than foliar stipules, 1-2 (4) mm long, coriaceous, reddish-brown, early deciduous, the spinule (leaf rudiment) not observed. Foliar stipules early deciduous, appressed to stem, transversely triangular, 1-1.5 mm long, coriaceous, smooth, drying reddish-brown, striate-nerved with ca 5 parallel nerves per side, the nerves immersed in tissue and not prominent on surface, the apex truncate, 2-setulose, the setae filiform, 0.2-0.5 (1) mm long, evanescent, the keels slender, sometimes flattened, the margin minutely erose-fimbriate, becoming entire. Leaves deciduous, scattered along shoots, short-petiolate, the lamina elliptic to ovate, plane, rounded and sometimes slightly retuse at apex and base, 30-5 5 mm long, 18-32 mm wide, firmly chartaceous, adaxially medium green drying brownish, abaxially pale green drying ochreous, dull on both surfaces, elineate with no central panel, the adaxial midrib flat with a slender medial ridge, drying tawny or fer- ruginous, the lateral nerves 9-12, diverging 45-70º from midrib, slender, straight or somewhat flexuous, anastomosing 2-3 mm from margin, distinct but not prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets abaxially distinct, very finely reticulate. Petiole 1.5-3 mm long, 0.8-1 mm in diam, a little flattened dorsiventrally, broadly canaliculate, drying black. Flowers fasciculate in axils of cataphylls at base of current season's twigs, 1-3 per node. Bracteoles linear, 2-2.5 mm long, ca 0.2 mm wide, membranous, the keel somewhat winged, blunt and fimbriate at apex. Pedicel slender, pentagonal, 5-ribbed, 7-8 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm wide, the ribs drying light tan and contrasting with the dark brown furrows. Calyx 2-2.5 mm long, divided 3/4 its length, the lobes narrowly ovate, 1.5-1.7 mm long, acuminate at apex, strongly recurving in fruit, the lobe margins drying light brown in contrast to the very dark brown middle part. Petal not seen. Staminal cup 1/2 as long as calyx, 0.7-1 mm long, entire at margin. Brachystylousflowers: (in fiuit) styles free. Drupe oblong-ovoid, rounded at apex, 8-10 mm long, 4.2-5.2 mm in diam, the endocarp oblong-ovoid, obtuse at apex, 6-ribbed, unilocular, the endosperm occupying ca 30% of locule. Embryo ca 7 mm long; cotyledons oblong-ovate, rounded at apex, subcordate at base, 5.2-5.8 mm long, 3.3-3.5 mm wide, 1 mm thick; radicle 1.5 mm long.

description: Frutex vel arbuscula diffuse ramosa. Ramuli flexuosi, brachyblastis ramentaceis. Stipulae persistentes, estriatae vel juniores substriatae, 3-setulosae. Folia ad apicem brachyblastorum producta vel interdum dispersa, subsessilia, decidua; laminae ellipticae vel oblongae, raro obovatae, apice obtusae vel rotundatae, raro retusae vel acutae, margine undulatae, subtus semper aliquantum nitidae. Flores fasciculati in axillis ramentorum vel foliorum a brachyblastis homotinis producti. Petali lamina late ovata. Urceolus stamineus quam calyx 3/4-plo longior vel calycem aequans, ad marginem 10-denticulatus. Drupa anguste ovoidea, apice obtusa, endocarpio subtereti, 6-sulculato, ad maturitatem uniloculari. Ab Erythroxylo schomburgkii Peyr. foliis obtusis vel rotundatis, chartaceis, pagina abaxiali nitidulis, marginibus undulatis, pedicellis longioribus et urceolis quam calycibus brevioribus differt.

description: Erect, densely branched shrub or small tree to 8 m tall, with 1-3 main trunks to 6 cm in diam. Bark on trunk greyish brown with fine longitudinal fissures, 1.0-1.5 mm thick, reddish brown within. Major branches erect, virgate, greyish brown. Branchlets distichous, consisting mainly of short shoots, flexuous, spreading or bending upwards, diverging 45º-90º from axis, flattened apically, 1.5-2 mm in diam, greyish brown or reddish brown, waxy when young, verruculose, the lenticels numerous, elongate, light grey to greyish brown. Internodes on long shoots 3-22 mm long, on short shoots 0.5-5 mm long. Ramenta periodic on both long and short shoots, appearing at the base of new twigs, 5-20 mm long, 3-5 mm wide. Stipules persistent, diverging slightly from axis, ovate to triangular, estriate or substriate when newly formed, 1-4 mm long, subcoriaceous, light green, turning black with age, the margin entire, recurving in age, apically blunt to truncate, 3-setulose, the setae evanescent, 0.5-1 mm long, the middle seta a little shorter, the keels somewhat alate. Leaves deciduous, 1-3 produced at tips of the short shoots, or somewhat scattered along long shoots, distichous, subsessile, the lamina plane or somewhat laterally ascending, elliptic to oblong, rarely obovate, apically obtuse to rounded, rarely retuse or acute, undulate at margin, basally obtuse to rounded, 20-55 mm long, 11-22 mm wide, firmly chartaceous, medium to dark green above, lighter yellowish green beneath, shiny to rather dull above, consistently but to varying degrees shiny beneath, elineate, adaxial midrib flat or slightly raised, yellowish, the lateral nerves 8-10, diverging 40º-60º from midrib, straight then arcuately anastomosing 1-2 mm within margin, prominulous above, more or less obscure beneath, the veinlets finely reticulate. Petiole very short, 0.5-1.0 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm in diam, subterete, drying brown. Flowers in axils of ramenta or leaves on current season's twigs, 1-3 flowers per node, often congested at branch tips and appearing to be subtended by the apical leaves, the petals creamy yellow with a white "corona." Bracteoles 2, narrowly ovate to subulate, 1-2 mm long, acuminate or acute, 1-setulose, membranaceous. Pedicel 2-3 mm long, pentagonal in cross-section. Calyx 2-2.5 mm long, light green, deeply divided, the lobes ovate, apically acute or acuminate, 1.5-1.6 mm long. Petal limb spreading, concave, broadly ovate, rounded or truncate at apex, 2.5-3 mm long, 1.8-2 mm wide, the claw 1.5 mm long, the ligule 1.2-1.5 mm long, bilobate with a short, acuminate, posterior-medial appendage between the auricles, the auricles ovate to orbicular, rounded apically, 0.8-1 mm long. Staminal cup 3/4 as long as or equaling calyx length, 1.5 mm long, 10-denticulate at margin. Brachystylous flowers not seen. Dolichostylous flowers: antesepalous filaments 1-1.2 mm long, the anthers ovoid, apically apiculate, 0.5-0.7 mm long; antepetalous filaments 2-2.2 mm long, the anthers ovoid, apically apiculate, slightly smaller, 0.5-0.6 mm long. Ovary ellipsoid to globose, equaling or a little longer than staminal cup, 1.2-1.5 mm long; style 3-3.5 mm long; stigma obliquely depressed-capitate, 0.5-0.6 mm long. Drupe narrowly ovoid, apically obtuse, 8 mm long, 3.5-4 mm in diam, the mesocarp 0.5 mm thick, the endocarp narrowly ovoid, sub-terete in crosssection, with 6 shallow furrows, unilocular at maturity, the endosperm occupying about 30% of locule. Embryo 1.5 mm long; cotyledons elliptical, flattened, apically rounded, 5.5 mm long, 3 mm wide; radicle terete, 1.5 mm long.

description: Frutex vel arbuscula ramosa. Ramuli recti vel interdum flexuosi, rigidi, saepe spiniformes. Stipulae parvae, persistentes, estriatae, minute bisetulosae. Folia ad apicem brachyblastorum producta, brevissime petiolata, decidua; laminae suborbiculares vel obtriangulares, apice rotundatae vel retusae. Flores fasciculati in axillis foliorum deciduorum vel ramentorum a brachyblastis annotinis producti. Petali lamina vadose cymbiformis, ovata. Urceolus stamineus 1/2-3/4 longitudinis calycis, margine integer. Drupa ovoidea vel ellipsoidea, apice rotundata, endocarpio subtereti, dorsaliter sulculato, ad maturitatem uniloculari. Rich. calycibus majoribus, pedicellis brevioribus et endocarpiis teretibus, ab E. brevipede DC. stipulis minoribus et pedicellis brevioribus, et ab E. undulato Plowman floribus a brachyblastis annotinis productis, stipulis minoribus, foliorum paginis planis, et endocarpiis teretibus differt.

description: Diffusely branched shrub or small tree to 6 m tall, with 1-5 main trunks, 10-15 cm in diam near base. Bark on trunk smooth, or somewhat longitudinally rugulose, whitish grey-brown, reddish brown within, 1-1.5 mm thick, exfoliating in large, thin flakes; wood light tan. Branches straight to somewhat flexuous, terete, light greyish brown. Branchiets distichous, divaricating at wide acute to right angles, straight to somewhat flexuous, rigid, often becoming spine-like, apically flattened, 1-2 mm in diam, dark reddish brown, punctate-lenticellate, the lenticels scattered, small, somewhat rounded to elongate, whitish. Internodes 3-10 mm long on long shoots, highly contracted on short shoots, obscure. Ramenta present mainly at apex of short shoots, congested, 3-5 mm long. Stipules small, persistent, appressed, triangular, 1-1.5 mm long, membranaceous, pale green, turning black with age, apically obtuse to rounded, minutely 2-setulose, the setae 0.1-0.2 mm long, very fragile and early disappearing, the keels prominent, slightly alate, the margin fimbriate to ciliolate, becoming entire with age. Leaves deciduous, 1-3 produced at apex of the short shoots, distichous, very short-petiolate, the lamina erect or spreading, plane or lightly undulate, obovate, suborbicular to obtriangular, apically rounded or retuse, cuneate to obtuse or rounded at base, (4) 8-23 mm long, 5-11 mm wide, firmly membranaceous to subcoriaceous, medium green adaxially, pale glaucous green or whitish green abaxially, somewhat shiny above, dull green beneath, elineate, the midrib flat to somewhat convex in cross-section, adaxially yellowish-green, abaxially darker green, the lateral nerves 8-10, straight to somewhat sinuous, diverging 50?-70? from midrib, prominulous adaxially, somewhat obscure abaxially, the veinlets finely reticulate, prominulous adaxially. Petiole 0.5-2 mm long, subterete, light green, drying dark reddish brown. Flowers in axillary fascicles on last season's short shoots, rarely on last season's long shoots, scattered or somewhat congested, with 1-4 flowers per node; flowers white. Bracteoles 2, short, subhemispheroidal, broadly acute or abruptly acuminate at apex with a very short acumen, 1.0-1.5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, membranaceous, soon disintegrating. Pedicel subterete, apically pentangular, 0.5-2.0 mm long, 0.5 mm in diam. Calyx 1.2-2.0 mm long, light green, the lobes ovate to triangular, 0.8-1.5 mm long, apically acute to acuminate, drying dark brown with wide, light brown margins. Petal limb spreading, shallowly cymbiform, broadly ovate in outline, 2-3 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, apically rounded or obtuse, the claw 0.5-1 mm long, the ligule 1.0-2.0 mm long, bilobate, the auricles somewhat concave, ovate, erose at margin. Staminal cup 1/2-/4 as long as calyx, 0.8-1.5 mm long, entire at margin; anthers broadly ovate to orbicular. Brachystylous flowers: filaments 3 mm long, the anthers 0.5-0.75 mm long; style 1 mm long; stigma 0.3 mm long, obliquely depressed-capitate. Dolichostylous flowers: antesepalous filaments 1 mm long, the anthers 0.5-0.6 mm long; antepetalous filaments 1.5-1.8 mm long, the anthers 0.5 mm long; styles 3.0-3.2 mm long; stigma 0.3 mm long, obliquely depressed-capitate. Ovary ovoid to ellipsoid, 0.8-1.2 mm long. Drupes clustered on short shoots or solitary, ovoid to ellipsoid, apically rounded, 6-8 mm long, 3.5-5.0 mm in diam, red at maturity, the mesocarp 0.2-0.5 mm thick, the endocarp ellipsoid, subterete, dorsally 3-sulculate, unilocular at maturity; endosperm abundant, filling the endocarp. Embryo 3.5-4.5 mm long; cotyledons oblong, plano-convex, 2-2.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, apically rounded; radicle 1.5-2 mm long.

description: Shrub to 1 m tall; stems subquadrate, glabrous or minutely papillose on the angles, appearing jointed due to the persistent leaf bases. description: Herb; stems terete, glabrous, the internodes 1-2.5 cm long, the branches spreading. description: Tree to 20 m tall. Leafy twigs 5-10 mm thick, densely brown hirtellous to strigose to subvillous; periderm persistent. Lamina subcoriaceous, oblong to subobovate to lanceolate, 15-30 X 5.5-13 cm, symmetric; apex acuminate; base obtuse; margin entire; upper surface glabrous; lower surface densely brown substrigose to subtomentose, on smaller veins to tomentose; lateral veins (10-)13-15 pairs, the basal pair hardly different from the other pairs, up to 1/10-1/8 length of lamina, unbranched; tertiary venation scalariform with 10-20 intercostal veins in middle of lamina, prominent; petiole 1-1.5 cm long, brown substrigose; stipules 2-4(-5) cm long, pale brown to yellowish (sub)sericeous, subpersistent. Figs axillary, solitary or in pairs, sessile; basal bracts 2, 2-3 mm long; receptacle subglobose, 0.7-1 cm diam (when dry), densely (dark) brown puberulous to subvelutinous, of unknown color at maturity; ostiole ca. 2.5 mm diam (when dry), surrounded by a 3-lobed rim. Staminate flowers: pedicel 0.2-0.4 mm long; tepals 3, 0.6-1 mm long; stamen 1; anther ca. 0.5 mm long, not apic ulate. description: Tree to 15 m tall, or shrub. Leafy twigs 2-4 mm thick, glabrous or minutely puberulous; periderm persistent or flaking off. (when dry), smooth or ± wrinkled when dry, glabrous or sparsely minutely puberulous, emaculate or maculate, greenish to yellowish or red- dish (?) at maturity; ostiole ca. 2-2.5 mm diam. description: Tree to 50 m tall, hemiepiphytic. Leafy twigs 3-5 mm thick, minutely puberulous, the periderm shed in flakes. description: Tree to 8 m tall. Leafy twigs 1.5-2.5 mm thick, glabrous; periderm persistent. Lamina coriaceous, elliptic, 3-6 X 2-4.5 cm, symmetric; apex (very) shortly and bluntly acuminate; base rounded to truncate; margin entire; both surfaces glabrous; lateral veins 4-6(-7) pairs, often furcate far from margin, the basal pair slightly different from other pairs, up to 1/3-1/2 length of lamina, indistinctly branched; tertiary venation (loosely) reticulate; petiole (1.2-)2- 3.5 cm long, ca. 1 mm thick, glabrous, the epidermis persistent; stipules 0.5-0.7 cm long, glabrous, caducous. Figs axillary or (also) just below leaves, in pairs or solitary; peduncle 2-3 cm long; basal bracts 2, ca. 1.5 mm long, usually fused; receptacle sub-globose, 0.5-0.6 cm diam. (when dry), sub-glabrous, maculate, of unknown color at maturity; ostiole ca. 1.5 mm diam. (when dry), (slightly) sunken. Staminate flowers: pedicel 0.2-0.3 mm long; tepals 3, ca. 0.8 mm long; stamen 1; anther ca. 0.8 mm long, not apiculate. Pistillate flowers: tepals 3, 0.8-1.2 mm long; stigma ca. 0.25 mm long; long-styled flowers sessile, the style 0.8-1.2 mm long; short-styled flowers with pedicel 0.3-1 mm long, the style 0.5-0.8 mm long. Interfloral bracts 1-1.5 mm long. Internal hairs minute, dark brown, appressed on inner surface of receptacle.

description: Free-standing tree up to 25 m. Leafy twigs up to 0.7 cm thick, glabrous, periderm flaking off. Lamina ovate to narrowly elliptic 15-21 X 7-10.5 cm, coriaceous; apex shortly acuminate to acute; base rounded to obtuse; margin entire, revolute; upper surface (sub)glabrous; lower surface (sub)scabrous, with minute, distinctly brown pluricellular hairs on veins; mid-vein reaching the apex; lateral veins 17-22 pairs, divaricating ca. 850 at middle of lamina, brochidodromous and forming an entire arched submarginal vein; intersecondary veins present, mostly not reaching the sub- marginal vein; tertiary venation reticulate. Petioles 1.7-3 cm long, 2.5-3 mm thick, sulcate above, sparsely minutely puberulous, epidermis flaking off. Stipules up to 3.7 (6) cm long, up to 4.5 mm wide near base, caducous, glabrous or minutely white puberulous near base. Syconia solitary in the leaf axils, pedunculate; peduncle up to 1.1 cm long, ca. 2 mm thick, subglabrous, basal bracts 3, up to 2.5 cm long, basally minutely white puberulous; receptacle glo- bose, 2-2.9 cm diam., distinctly stipitate, (sparsely) minutely stiffly puberulous (sca- brous), sometimes with subglabrous and darker spots (rudiments of lateral bracts); ostiole hidden below a cavity formed by the receptacle apex, this cavity up to 0.7 cm deep. Staminate flowers not seen, pistillate flower with 4 tepals, free, linear, (1.5)2(2.5) mm long, style lateral, ca. 1 mm long, stig- mas 2, separate or fused.

description: Tree to 25 m tall. Leafy twigs 2-3.5 mm thick, white puberulous to hirtellous, the hairs distinctly different in length; periderm flaking off. (when dry), densely white-puberulous to -subtomentose, of unknown color at maturity; ostiole ca. 2 mm diam. (when dry), prominent to plane. description: Tree to 12 m tall, deciduous. Leafy twigs 1.5-2.5 mm thick, minutely puberulous to glabrous; periderm persistent or flaking off.
