description: Liana, climbing to 3-7 m; basal stems 4.5-7.6 mm diam., cylindrical, smooth-sided, twisted, glabrate, developing small scat- tered lenticels. Leaves opposite; petiole (22-)32-48 mm long, glabrous, confluent across the node and forming a corky ridge, bearing a pair of prominent glands at base, each gland 0.8-2.5 mm diam.; stipules ca. 0.5 mm long, borne on the base of the petiole, caducous; lamina of larger leaves (7.9-)9.4-14.2 X 3.2-9.5 cm, membranous, oblong, ovate, cordate-oblong to el- liptic, the base cordate or shallowly cordate, rarely acute, the apex obtuse, rounded or slightly retuse, the margin entire; hairs long-stalked in young leaves, forming a tomentose indument on primary and secondary veins on both sides, soon completely deciduous; midrib, lateral veins, and reticulum deeply impressed above and prominent below, producing a bullate surface. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal or axillary, pendulous, densely brown-sericeous, (9.5-) 14.5-21 (-35) cm long; primary branches 12-20, 0.3-14.7 cm long; secondary branches 2-8, 0.2-2.6 cm long; tertiary branches 5-7, 0.2-0.5 cm long or absent; ultimate units 4-flowered umbels; inflorescence bracts ca. 1.1 X 0.9 mm, triangular, bright green, the margins entire, the base eglandular or biglandular, the glands 0.4- 0.7 mm diam.; peduncle absent; floral bracts 0.5-1 X 1.3-1.6 mm, ovate, eglan- dular, densely sericeous abaxially, glabrous adaxially; bracteoles like bracts but smaller, eglandular; pedicel 4.8-6.6 X 1.1-2.6 mm (6.2-8 X 1.3-2.8 mm in fruit), densely brown-sericeous, somewhat thicker distally, straight. Sepals 1.6-1.8 X 1.4-1.6 mm, brown, rounded or acute at apex, strongly appressed to filaments in anthesis, tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially, the anterior sepal eglandular, the lateral 4 biglandular, the glands 2.4-2.9 mm long. Petals exposed in the enlarging bud, vivid yellow, glabrous, smooth abaxially; lateral petals spreading, the margin entire, the claw ca. 2.2 mm long, the limb 3.4-3.8 X 2.7-3 mm; posterior petal erect, minutely glan- dular-thickened at margin, the claw ca. 3.7 mm long, the limb 2.5-3 X 2.7-2.9 mm. Stamens glabrous, unequal; filaments 2-2.8 X 0.3-0.9 mm, connate ca. 1/2 their length; anthers 1.4-1.6 mm long, all alike, gla- brous, erect to reflexed, the connective swollen and uniformly dark red. Ovary 1.2- 1.4 mm high, densely sericeous; styles 3- 3.2 mm long, slightly exceeding anthers, glabrous; anterior style erect and straight, occasionally inclined toward posterior pet- al, the apex slightly truncate or rounded; 2 posterior styles somewhat arcuate at base, the apex rounded; stigmas internal and facing center of flower or on oblique inner angle. Samara pale brown, 29-52 mm long, borne suberect, sparsely tomentose to glabrate; dorsal wing almost as long as samara, 21-44 X 13-19 mm; nut 5-8 mm diam., ovoid, with smooth surface, without lateral crests or winglets.

description: Liana, flexuosa, ramis tomentosis demum glabratis. Lamina foliorum majorum 1.7-10 cm longa, 0.6-3.5 cm lata, ovata-lanceolata, oblongo-lanceolata vel obovata, basi cordata vel fere rotundata, margine revoluta, abaxialiter dense ferrugineo-tomentosa. Panicula deflexa, 2 umbellis 4 floris; pedunculo florifero nullo. Petala patentia, flavo-virescentia, in alabastro exposita, dorsaliter incrassata, margine integra vel breviter erosa; styli arcuati, in apice dorsaliter rotundati vel stylo antico in apice dorsaliter truncato. Samarae 23-42 mm longae, 5-15 mm latae, nuce laevi.

description: Liana with slender twining stems, climbing to 0.5-3 m; basal stems ca. 5 mm diam., cylindrical, loosely tomentose, soon glabrate; lenticels not seen. Leaves opposite; petiole 5-10 mm long, densely tomentose, bearing a pair of impressed glands at base, each gland ca. 0.4 mm. diam and hidden by indument; stipules minute, ca. 0.2 mm long, borne near the base of the petiole; lamina of larger leaves (1.7-)3.5-7.7(-10) X 0.6- 2.8(-3.5) cm, membranous to chartaceous, ovate-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate or sometimes oblong to cordate-oblong, the base obtuse or rounded to slightly cordate, the apex acute or sometimes obtuse to apiculate, the margins entire, strongly revolute; hairs with a short stalk and a horizontal crosspiece, later deciduous or persistent on both sides, forming a densely ferrugineous indument, sparsely tomentose on the adaxial surface and densely tomentose abaxially; adaxial surface with impressed veins. Inflorescence a small panicle, terminal, pendulous, densely ferrugineous-tomentose, 3-9 cm long; primary branches 8-10, 0.5-2 cm long; secondary branches rarely present, then ca. 0.2 cm long; ultimate units 4-flow- ered umbels; inflorescence bracts ca. 1.9 X 1 mm, narrowly triangular, the margins en- tire and eglandular; peduncle absent; floral bracts ca. 0.5 X 0.5 mm, ovate, eglandular, tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially; bracteoles like bracts but smaller, eglandu- lar; pedicel 6-6.6 X 0.8-2.3 mm (7.8 X 1- 2.5 mm in fruit), densely tomentose, somewhat thicker distally, curved. Sepals 1.7- 2.2 X 1.5 mm, pale brown, acute or slightly rounded at apex, appressed in anthesis, densely tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially, eglandular. Petals exposed in the enlarging bud, pale green yellow, glabrous, the margin entire or slightly erose, the limb thickened in center; lateral petals spreading, the claw 1.5-3.3 mm long, the limb 2.8- 4.5 X 2.2-3 mm; posterior petal suberect, the claw ca. 2.3 mm long, the limb 3 X 2.2- 2.5 mm. Stamens glabrous, slightly unequal; filaments 2-2.5 X 0.3-1.4 mm, connate ca. 1/2 their length; anthers 1.7-2.1 mm long, all alike, glabrous, erect, the connective proximally 2/3-4/5 dark red, distally 1/3-1/5 white. Ovary 1.5-1.8 mm high, thinly tomentose; styles exceeding anthers, glabrous or slightly tomentose at very base; anterior style ca. 2.9 mm long, straight, the apex slightly truncate or rounded; 2 posterior styles 2.5-2.6 mm long, somewhat arcuate at base and bent toward posterior petal, the apex rounded dorsally; stigmas internal and facing center of flower or on oblique inner angle. Samara reddish pink at maturity, 23-35(-42) mm long, borne erect when single, suberect when double, sparsely tomentose; dorsal wing almost as long as samara, 20-34 X 5-15 mm; nut 5-12 mm diam., ovoid, with smooth surface, without lateral crests or winglets.

description: Liana basi ramis teretibus, sulcatis, aplanatis vel trilobis. Lamina foliorum majorum 5-20.5 cm longa, 4-13 cm lata, elliptica, ovata, obovata, orbiculata, ovato- lanceolata, obovato-oblonga, cuneato-oblonga vel late lanceolata, raro obcordata, utrinque glabrata; petiolus 5-21 mm longus, basi biglandulifer. Panicula patentia vel contracta, 15-35 cm longa, in ramis deflexis, umbellis 4-6-floris, pedunculo florifero nullo, pedicello 3.5-8.5 longo, 0.9-1.9 mm diametro, leviter incrassato versus apicem. Petala lutea, in alabastro exposita, patentia, dorsaliter carinata, limbo rectangulato vel basi truncato, plano vel concavo; filamenta heteromorpha; styli recti vel lyrati, apice dorsaliter apiculati vel truncati. Samarae 37-43 mm longae, nuce lateraliter laevi.

description: Liana climbing to 1.5-15 m or forming a small shrub when nothing is available to climb on; stems at base 1-2 cm diam., the cross-section cylindrical, irregularly sulcate, flattened, or occasionally divided into 3 or more lobes, twisted, glabrate, developing small scattered lenticels. Leaves mostly plane, eventually erect in inflorescence, opposite, spreading; petiole (5-) 11- 21 mm long, initially sericeous and soon glabrate, bearing a pair of glands at base, each gland 1.2-1.6 mm diam.; stipules 0.2-0.3 mm long, seldom evident, borne on the base of the petiole, generally absent from old leaves; lamina of larger leaves (5-) 6.1-15.8(-20.5) X (4-)5-9(-13) cm, membranous to subcoriaceous, elliptic, ovate, obovate, orbicular, ovate-lanceolate, obovate-oblong, cuneate-oblong or widely lanceolate, rarely obcordate, obtuse to rounded, rarely acute at base, acute, rounded, shortly caudate or cuspidate, rarely retuse at apex, the margins entire or rarely irregularly dentate, bearing many small bor- dered glands and short cilia, especially in young leaves, glabrous or initially sparsely sericeous (with short, appressed, medifixed hairs) and soon glabrescent or rarely with a persistent sericeous-indument abaxially, the lateral veins slightly prominent below, reticulum very fine and more visible below than above. Inflorescence paniculate, spreading or sometimes contracted, 15-35 cm long, terminal or axillary, erect or more frequently pendulous, densely and persis- tently brown-sericeous, with the flowers borne ultimately in 4-6-flowered umbels; inflorescence bracts like leaves and gradually or abruptly reduced to 1.8-5 X 0.6-1.6 mm, lanceolate or triangular, the margins entire, eglandular or biglandular at base, the glands 0.6-1.5 mm diam., bright green; peduncle absent; bracts 0.7-1 X 0.8-1.3 mm, ovate or rounded, eglandular or sometimes biglandular, each gland ca. 0.9 mm diam., abaxially sericeous, adaxially glabrous; bracteoles similar to bract but smaller; pedicel (3.5-)5.2-8.5 x 0.9-1.9 mm (ca. 10 x 1.2-2.7 mm in fruit), brown-sericeous, slightly thickened distally, straight or curved. Sepals 1.3-1.5 X 1.4-1.8 mm, brown, obtuse or rounded at apex, ap- pressed against filaments in anthesis (prin- cipally 2 posterior sepals), abaxially brown- sericeous, adaxially glabrous, eglandular or the anterior sepal eglandular and the lateral 4 biglandular, the glands 1.7-2.4 mm long, elliptic. Petals exposed in the enlarging bud, yellow lacking red, glabrous; lateral petals spreading, margins proximally erose to rarely slightly denticulate, sometimes revolute in anthesis, claw 2-2.8(-3) mm long, limb 3.5-4.2(-4.8) X 2.1-3.8(-4.5) mm, ovate, irregularly rectangular, some- times truncate at the base, flat to deeply concave, membranous, slightly thickened in center of limb, or sometimes strongly cari- nate; posterior petal sub-erect, glandular- thickened at margins, claw 3-3.7 mm long, limb 2.5-3(-4) X (2.4-)3.1-3.3 mm, ovate and often truncate at the base, narrowly flat, thickened in center of limb but not carinate. Stamens glabrous; filaments heteromorphic, 2-3.5 X 0.2-0.9 mm, connate l/3-?/2 their length, the 2 stamens opposite posterior-lat- eral petals, 2.9-3.5 mm long, the longest stamen opposite anterior sepal, 2.7-3(-3.4) mm long, the shortest stamen opposite pos- terior petal, 2-2.5 mm long, the other sta- mens 2.5-3 mm long; anthers 1-1.8(-2.3) mm long, all alike or slightly unequal, reflexed or erect in anthesis, connective with proximal 2/3-4/5 dark red, the distal 1/5-1/3 pale yellow. Ovary 1.3-1.7 mm high, sericeous; styles 2.9-3.3 mm long, exceeding the anthers, glabrous, all 3 with a slightly flattened-elliptic top, the stigma internal; anterior and posterior styles nearly straight or sometimes somewhat lyrate, dorsally apiculate or truncate at apex, with all 3 facing toward posterior petal. Samara pale brown at maturity, 37-43 mm long, borne erect when single, obliquely or eventually horizontally when 2 or 3 develop, thinly sericeous to glabrate; dorsal wing 32-38 X 14-18 mm (sometimes much flared distally to produce a flabellate shape), the abaxial edge straight proximally; nut 4-7 mm diam., subspheroidal, smooth-sided, without lateral crests or winglets.

description: Liana, climbing to 1.5-4(-10) m; stems at base 1-3 cm diam., the cross-section usually strongly flattened, triangular, or deeply divided into 3 or more lobes, twisted, glabrate, developing small scattered lenticels. Leaves mostly plane, opposite, spreading; petiole 16-39(-45) mm long, initially densely sericeous and soon glabrate, bearing a pair of glands at base, each gland 1.2-1.6 mm diam. or rarely eglandular; stipules present on petiole, above base, as minute protuberances ca. 0.3 mm long, seldom evident, apparently absent from old leaves; lamina of larger leaves (6.5-)9-19.5(-23) X (4.5-)6.2-12.5(-16.5) cm, membranous, rounded, subrotund, ovate, elliptic, ovate- lanceolate, or oblong-lanceolate, rounded, obtuse, cuneate or rarely cordate at base, rounded and often apiculate to retuse at apex, the margins bearing many glands and short cilia, especially in young leaves, glabrous or initially sparsely sericeous (with short, appressed, medifixed hairs) and soon glabrescent, the lateral veins slightly prominent below, reticulum very fine and more visible below than above. Inflorescence pa- niculate, spreading, 23-35.5(-47) cm long, primary branches 4-22, 0.8-13 cm long, secondary branches 2-10 or absent, 0.5-2.5 cm long, tertiary and accessory branches if present very reduced; terminal or axillary, pendulous, densely and persistently brown- sericeous, with the flowers borne ultimately in lax 4-6-flowered umbels; inflorescence bracts like leaves, gradually or abruptly re- duced to ca. 8 X 1.1-3 mm, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, margins entire, eglandular or biglandular at base, the glands 1.8-2.2 mm diam., bright green; peduncle absent; bracts 1-1.6 X 2-2.1 mm, narrowly trian- gular, eglandular, abaxially sericeous, adax- ially glabrous; bracteoles like bracts but smaller; pedicel 10.4-18 X 1.6-3.5 mm (ca. 11 X 2-4.5 mm in fruit), slightly curved upward in flower, densely brown- sericeous, gradually thickened distally. Se- pals 1.7-2 X 2.2-2.5 mm, brown, obtuse or rounded at apex, pressed against filaments in anthesis, abaxially densely sericeous, adaxially glabrous, the anterior sepal eglan- dular, the lateral 4 biglandular, the glands 2-2.7 mm long, elliptic or orbicular. Petals exposed in the enlarging bud, orange suf- fused with red, the pigmentation evident in bud, glabrous; lateral petals spreading, mar- gins entire or slightly erose and revolute in anthesis, claw 1.7-2.2 mm long, limb 3-3.2 X 3-3.2 mm, dorsally slightly carinate with the keel 0.3-0.6 mm wide, slightly decur- rent; posterior petal sub-erect, minutely glandular-thickened at margins, claw 2.5-3 mm long, limb ca. 3 X 2.7-3.1 mm, sub- orbicular, thickened in center but not cari- nate. Stamens glabrous; filaments unequal, 2.5-3.6 X 0.2-1 mm, connate ca. 1/3 their length, the 2 stamens opposite posterior-lat- eral petals much thicker than others, ca. 3.3 mm long, the longest stamen opposite an- terior sepal, ca. 3.6 mm long, not coherent with adjacent filaments, the shortest stamen opposite posterior petal, ca. 2.5 mm long, other stamens 2.8-3.2 mm long; anthers (1.5-)1.8-2.2 mm long, slightly unequal, erect to reflexed in anthesis, connective not widened and equalling the locules, the proximal 2/3-4/5 dark red, the distal 1/5-1/3 pale yellow or sometimes uniformly dark red. Ovary 1.5-2 mm high, densely sericeous; styles 3.3-3.6 mm long, equalling or slightly exceeding the anthers, glabrous, all 3 with a flattened elliptic top, with stigma internal; anterior style nearly straight, dorsally very briefly apiculate at apex; posterior styles somewhat lyrate, dorsally truncate at apex. Samara brown at maturity, (52-)67- 77 mm long, borne obliquely, thinly sericeous or tomentose to glabrate; dorsal wing 40-63 X 22-30 mm, the abaxial edge nearly straight; nut 9-14 mm diam., subspheroidal or ovoid, smooth-sided, without lateral crests or winglets.

description: Leaf petioles 2.0-9.5 (-13.0) cm long, densely glandular-pubescent with hairs up to about 1.5 mm long; blades 1.0-4.5 cm long, 0.7-4.2 cm wide, ovate to nearly orbicular, the base truncate to broadly cuneate or occasionally slightly cordate, and the principal leaves with 5 (-7) usually overlapping lobes which are crenate with rounded or slightly mucronate teeth; leaves gray-green, densely glandular pubescent with long and short hairs, viscid, and usually retaining soil particles or plant fragments. Scapes 10.0-40.0 (-50.0) cm high with 1-3 yellowish to greenish, sometimes leaflike, ciliate bracts, glandular-villous below grading above into densely viscid pubescent with short and long glandular hairs; panicle (2.0-) 3.0-7.0 (-8.5) cm long, 1.2-1.7 cm wide in flower, 1.5-2.2 cm wide in fruit, strongly condensed above, occasionally interrupted below; eymules 1-4-flowered; bracts 6.0-11.0 mm long, 2.5-5.0 mm wide excluding cilia, green and leaflike, fimbriate, often trifid, glandular-pubescent, and frequently projecting beyond the eymules. Receptacle and sepals glandular-pubescent with short and long hairs; receptacle brownish or greenish; sepal lobes cream to yellow, 3.0-3.5 mm long, 1.5-1.8 mm wide; petals apparently wanting, the stamens included (0.9-) 1.3-2.1 mm long, the filaments approximately the same length as the anthers; capsule about 6.0-8.0 mm long, included to slightly exserted.

description: Robust, few to many-branched perennial shrub, 1-4 m tall. Stems sparsely to moderately aculeate, lower and mid-stem with a longitudinal line of dense fine pubescence to 2 mm long, alternating position at each node (Fig. 1), also with sparse, mostly simple hairs, upper stem densely and uniformly pubescent. Leaves those on lower and midstem sections shallowly 3-lobed or ovate, 4-8.5 cm long, 3-6 cm wide, with fine stellate hairs and long (to 0.2 cm), sparse simple hairs on veins of ventral surface and stellate hairs plus dense simple hairs on dorsal surface; vegetative branchlets arising in leaf axils giving rise to as many as 7 leaves which are ovate or obovate to narrowly obovate, 0.9-4 cm long, 0.4-2.5 cm wide, and pubescent as the mainstem leaves; base truncate to cuneate, apex acute, margin coarsely serrate; newly opened leaves exhibit a gland-like, thickened structure at apex of each serration, which is not visible in older leaves; leaf nectary present on midrib at base of dorsal surface, or apparently sometimes absent; upper leaves subtending solitary, axillary flowers, obovate to narrowly obovate (rarely 3-lobed), at the base of the flowering branch 2-5 cm long, 1.5-3.5 cm wide, thence progressively reduced in size, becoming bract-like distally and 0.7-1.8 cm long, 0.3-0.5 cm wide, densely pubescent with stellate and long, straight hairs, more densely so on the dorsal than on the ventral surface, base cuneate (rarely truncate), apex acute, margin serrate. Petioles from 0.3 cm long on upper leaves to 3.5 cm on lower mainstem leaves; on upper leaves, flattened, villous; on lower leaves, rounded dorsally, sparsely beset with aculei and with a background of dense, very fine hairs, flattened ventrally, villous. Stipules when seen, linear, 0.2-0.4 cm long, inconspicuous, with very fine, minute pubescence but usually lacking (caducous?). Flowers axillary, solitary, erect, disposed in the upper 7-23 cm of the branch. Peduncles articulating at the base, accrescent, 0.1-0.5 cm long in bud, 0.5-0.8 cm in flower, 0.5-2 cm at fruiting, with a dense, fine background of pubescence plus dense, straight hairs to 0.2 cm long. Involucellar bracteoles flattened, obscurely several nerved, 6-7 in number, united near base, 0.9-1.3 cm long, 0.1-0.4 cm wide, not apically bifurcate, with long (0.2 cm), straight simple hairs on margins, body villous below, with fine, dense, minute pubescence above. Calyx five lobed, longer than bracteoles at anthesis, 1.4-2.2 cm long, gamosepalous through ±1/3 its length, each lobe slightly to markedly acuminate at apex, with a thickened midrib and two thickened marginal ribs, villous below, finely pubescent above, calyx nectary mostly absent but present on midrib in a few collections. Petals obovate to broadly obovate, 3.0-5.5 cm long 3.0-5.5 cm wide, densely, finely pubescent in bud, glabrous to sparsely stellate or simple-pubescent in flower, varying from white to deep purple, judging from collectors' notes; in many intermediate shades, as follows: white, creamy-white, ivory, pale yellow, yellow, claret, rose, old-rose, heliotrope, pink, red, wine-colored, mauve, violet, purple, deep purple. Staminal column 0.2-0.4 cm long. Capsule broadly ovoid, 1.3-1.7 cm long, 1.1-1.7 cm in diam, with long, dense, straw-colored appressed pubescence; beak absent or up to 0.1 cm long. Seeds 0.4 cm long, 0.3 cm wide, subreniform, angular, the dark brown background covered with small, waxy, concentric rings and short, white, many-branched hairs.

description: Shrub 1 m tall, the stems to at least 12 mm diameter, stellate-pubescent, the hairs yellowish, appressed, usually 8-armed (6-15-armed), 0.3-0.4 mm long; climax leaves suborbicular to ovate, angulate, or sublobulate, up to 26 cm long, as broad or broader, palmately 9-nerved, truncate or subcordate, irregularly serrate, rounded-acute, both surfaces sparsely and minutely stellate-pubescent, the nerves prominently raised beneath, with an elongated foliar nectary on lower surface at base of lamina or displaced onto petiole (at least for uppermost leaves); leaves reduced upward becoming smaller and narrower, the uppermost virtually bract-like, subtending the flowers; petioles 1-5.5 cm long, stout, with pubescence like stem; pedicels 6-14 mm long, stout, densely stellate-pubescent, the hairs yellowish and much denser and slightly longer than the stem hairs, the flowers usually solitary in the axils, tending to form a terminal racemiform inflorescence that exceeds the foliage; involucel of 10-11 bracteoles, each bracteole ca 9 (6-10) mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, simple or obscurely bifurcate, sparsely stellate-pubescent; calyx 20- 25 mm long at anthesis, ca 2/3-divided, densely yellowish-hispid, the hairs 1-2 mm long, stellate, intermingled with much smaller hairs; calyx lobes with prom- inent reddish marginal costae and similar midrib, the latter with a prominent nectary medially positioned; petals pink with a dark red base, 6-7 cm long, externally sparsely stellate-pubescent, internally glabrous; staminal column ca 45 mm long, glabrous, with anthers scattered along its length; filaments mostly 2 mm long; pollen purplish; styles connate to within 2-3 mm of apex, pallid, subglabrous; stigmas 5, capitate, purplish, 1.5-2 mm diameter, villous, the hairs up to 1 mm long; fruits unknown.

inflores- cence (1-) 3-12 (-15) cm. long, 2-6-times branehed, the peduncle (up to 5.5 cm. long) and branches slender, terete, densely and closely brown-tomentellous, glabreseent after anthesis, the bracts papyraceous, ovate, acute, 1-1.5 mm. long; flowers 4-8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, each subtended by a eaducous bracteole about 0.5 mm. long, the pedi- eels slender, densely tomentellous, 1-3 mm. long; sepals papyraceous, inconspicuously tomentellous, broadly ovate to deltoid, 0.5-1.2 mm. long, 0.6-1.4 mm. broad, rounded or obtuse or obscurely apiculate at apex, erose or irregularly ciliolate at miiargins; ovary about 1 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style 0.8-1.3 mm. long; fruiting pedicels 1-2.5 mm. in diameter, the capsules obovate-elliptic or narrowly oblong-elliptic, (3.5-) 4-8 cm. long, 1.5-4 (-5) cm. broad, 2-4 mm. thick before dehiseence, obtuse and slightly swollen at base, rounded or emarginate (sometimes conspicuously so) at apex, subacute and entire at margins, the pericarp usually densely and finely flabellate-costate without (nerves prominulous), smooth within, 0.1-0.2 mm. thick (rarely to 1 mm. thick proximally); description: Shrubs or trees to 5 m. description: Bulbous perennial herb, 36-3 7 cm tall. Bulb unknown. Single leaf known, linear, ca 30 cm long, 16-18 mm wide, folded along midrib (juvenile?), when unfolded margins revolute and midrib depressed. Inflorescence scapose, umbellate, 7-flow- ered; scape solid (compressed?); bracts 3, lanceolate, 28-30 mm long; bracteoles shorter, linear; pedicels ca 50-60 mm long. Perianth white; tube ca 18.8 mm long, cylindrical below and 2-3 mm wide, dilated in upper 1/3-1/4 to 10 mm at throat. Limb of 6 ovate segments in 2 series spreading to ca 40 mm wide; outer segments 26.5 mm long, 9-10 mm wide, apiculate at apex; inner segments ca 24.3 mm long, 12-13 mm wide, acute at apex. Stamens 6, connate into a campanulate staminal cup ca 12 mm long, 16 mm wide (striped green within?); each stamen consisting of two obtuse lobes 3 mm long, 5 mm wide at base, and a narrowly subulate, incurved, 3.5 mm long anther-bearing portion inserted at the rim of the cup between the lobes; anthers linear, sub-basifixed, versatile, 6-7 mm long. Style filiform, equal to or slightly exerted beyond the cup, ca 34 mm long; stigma capitate, 3-lobed, pubescent, 1.7-2.0 mm wide. Ovary ellipsoid, trilocular, 10.7 mm long, 4.0 mm wide; owules axile, 20 or more per locule, biseriate, oblong, flattened and obscurely winged at the margin.

description: Stems slender, creeping, glabrous; leaves orbicular-reniform, not peltate, 1-7.5 cm. in diameter, 9-11-nerved, glabrous or sparingly pubescent, truncate-crenate or very shallowly lobed with the lobes truncate, subentire, undulate or crenate, the middle crenation equalling or shorter than the lateral crenations, the petioles 1.5-20 cm. long, pilose especially toward the apex with reflexed or divaricate hairs; mature peduncles longer than the leaves, 5-10 cm. long, pilose especially toward the apex with somewhat crispate, reflexed hairs; umbels simple, 20-30- flowered, the pedicels 1-3 mm. long, spreading and reflexed, glabrous; fruit suborbicular, about 1 mm. long, 1-1.5 mm. broad, glabrous, the ribs filiform, acute, the stylopodium depressed.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. 1936. The genus Hydrocotyle in northern South America. Brittonia. 2: 201-237.

description: Stems slender, creeping to suberect, glabrous to hirsutulous; leaves orbicular-reniform, not peltate, 0.8-9 cm. in diameter, the mature leaves averaging about 3 cm. broad, sparingly to densely appressed strigose on the nerves and veins, 7-11-lobed, the lobes crenate, the apical lobule -somewhat elongate, the petioles slender, 1-23 cm. long, hirsute especeially above; peduncles slender, usually longer than the leaves, 0.5-26 cm. long, more or less hirsute; umbels simple, 20-70-flowered (South American specimens 20-40-flowered), globose, compact, the petals green, the pedicels 1-7 mm. long (South American specimens 2-3 mm. long), spreading and reflexed, glabrous; fruit suborbicular, 1-1.5 mm. long, about as broad, glabrous, the ribs distinct, acute, the stylopodium depressed.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. 1936. The genus Hydrocotyle in northern South America. Brittonia. 2: 201-237.

description: Stems slender, creeping, glabrous; leaves not peltate, 3-5 cm. in diameter, trifoliolate, appearing 5-foliolate because of the extreme lobation of the leaflets, the leaflets cuneate, incised, puberulent on the nerves and veins above and below, the lobules obtuse, the petioles slender, 2-10 cm. long, glabrous below, hirsutulous above; peduneles about equalling the leaves, 5-6 em. long, sparingly hirsutulous especially above; umbels simple, 15-20-flowered, the pedicels 2-4 mm. long, spreading and reflexed, glabrous; fruit orbicular, 1.5-2 mm. long and broad, the ribs slender, distinct, the stylopodium depressed.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. 1936. The genus Hydrocotyle in northern South America. Brittonia. 2: 201-237.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Stems filiform, creeping; leaves thin, orbicular-peltate, 3-20 mm. in diameter, glabrous to sparsely villous above, glabrous beneath, shal- lowly 5-8-lobed, the lobes crenate, the petioles slender, 5-35 mm. long, glabrous to densely retrorse-villous; peduncles about equalling the leaves, 5-15 mm. long, glabrous to retrorse-villous; umbels simple, 2-6- flowered, the flowers sessile to subsessile; fruit transversely elliptical, about 0.5 mm. long, 1 mm. broad, sparingly hirsute to glabrous, the ribs obsolete, the stylopodium depressed-conical.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. 1936. The genus Hydrocotyle in northern South America. Brittonia. 2: 201-237.

description: Stems stout, creeping, glabrous to sparingly hirsute; leaves peltate, orbicular-acuminate, 5-12 cm. in diameter, angulately 5-lobed (lobes triangular-acuminate, the apical lobe conspicuously elongate), serrate at margins, hirsutulous above especially on the nerves and veins, more densely hirsutulous below with divaricate hairs, the petioles slender, 5-15 cm. long, more or less retrorse-hirsute; peduncles longer than the leaves, 7-10 cm. long, subglabrate; umbels simple, 30-80-flowered, the pedicels 8-13 mm. long, glabrous; fruit transversely elliptical, about  2 mm. long, 2.5-3 mm. broad, glabrous, the ribs distinct, acute, the stylopodium depressed-conical.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. 1936. The genus Hydrocotyle in northern South America. Brittonia. 2: 201-237.

description: Plants glabrous; stems slender to somewhat fleshy, floating or creeping; leaves not peltate, suborbieular-reniform, 0.5-8 cm. in diameter, 5-6-lobed, the lobes crenate or lobulate, the petioles mlostly slender, 1-34.5 cm. long; peduncles shorter than the leaves, 0.4-6 cm. long; umbels simple, 5-10-flowered, the pedicels 1-3 mm. long, spreading and ascending; fruit suborbicular, 1-3 mm. long, 2-3 mm. broad, the ribs obscure, the stylopodium depressed.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. 1936. The genus Hydrocotyle in northern South America. Brittonia. 2: 201-237.

description: Plants glabrous; stems slender to somewhat fleshy, floating or creeping; leaves orbicular-peltate, 5-75 mm. in diameter, crenate or crenately lobed, the petioles mostly slender, 0.5-40 cm. long; peduncles usually longer than the leaves, 1.5-35 cm. long; umbels simple (rarely with a slight proliferation along the main axis), many-flowered, the pedicels 2-25 mm. long, spreading to reflexed; fruit suborbicular, 1-2 mm. long, 2-3 mm. broad, the ribs distinct, obtuse, the stylopodium depressed.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. 1936. The genus Hydrocotyle in northern South America. Brittonia. 2: 201-237.

description: Planta H. tambalomaensis Wolff simulans; caulibus gracilibus, sparse hirsutis; foliis palaceis, orbiculari-reniforrnibus, 2.5-5 cm. diametro, angulate 5-7-lobatis, lobis triangularibus, crenatis vel duplocrenatis, crenis terminalibus quam lateralibus longioribus, sparse hirsutis, petiolis subtus sparse hirsutis, supra dense retrorso-hirsutis; peduncLulis quam foliis longioribus, glabris; umbellis simplicibus, 20- 30-floris, pedicellis 3-4 mm. longis, glabris; fructibus glabris, costis distinctis, acutis. Stems slender, creeping, very sparingly hirsute; leaves orbicularreniform, not peltate, 2.5-5 cm. in diameter, sparingly hirsute above and below, 7-9-nerved, angulately 5-7-lobed one-third to one-half the distance to the sinus, the lobes triangular, crenate or doubly crenate, the apical crenation longer than the lateral, the petioles slender, 3-13 mm. long, sparingly hirsute below, densely retrorse-hirsute above; peduncles longer than the leaves, 3-9 cm. long, glabrous; umbels simple, 20-30-flowered, the pedicels slender, 3-4 mm. long, reflexed and spreading, glabrous; fruit transversely elliptical, about 1.5 mm. long, 2-3 mm. broad, glabrous, the ribs evident, acute, the stylopodium depressed.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. 1936. The genus Hydrocotyle in northern South America. Brittonia. 2: 201-237.

description: Shrub or small tree to 3 m; branches drooping, virgate, gray, glabrous to hispid.. Leaves coriaceous, oblong to ovate, 1-10.5 cm long, 0.4-6 cm broad, 2-3 times longer than broad, glabrate to hispid on midrib and veins beneath, pinnately veined, the primary veins inconspicuous, the ultimate venation finely reticulate; areoles less than 0.5 mm diam, pellucid; margin entire, usually conspicuously undulate; apex acute to acuminate, apiculate; base rounded to subcordate; petiole 0.2-1.5 cm long, glabrous to hispid. Male inflorescences axillary, usually solitary, rarely clustered, racemose, shorter than to longer than the leaf, much longer than the petiole, ascending to spreading-ascending, filiform to slender, densely villous; peduncles 0.1-0.4 mm long; rachis 7-21 mm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.3-0.8 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, densely villous; pedicels 0.3-2 mm long; bractlets 2-3, lanceolate, ca 0.8 mm long, ca 0.4 mm broad, glabrous to villous. Flowers pale green to pale yellow, glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate, ca 0.7 mm long and broad, the inner broadly ovate, ca 1.2 mm long and broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate, ca 0.8 mm long and broad; stamens 6; filaments ca 0.4 mm long. Female inflorescences racemose; peduncles hispidulous; pedicels 0-3 mm long. Fruit glaucous, blue or purplish to red, obovoid to globose, glabrous, 15-25 mm long, 12-21 mm broad, only slightly or not at all compressed, the apex broadly rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Trailing or climbing woody vine to 14 m, slender or from a trunk to 12.5 cm diam; branches gray, striate, somewhat puberulous. Leaves coriaceous, narrowly to broadly ovate, 4.5-20 cm long, 2.5-12 cm broad, less than twice as long as broad, glabrous or sparsely strigose on midrib and veins, especially beneath, papillose, pinnately veined with 4-7 pairs of upwardly arching alternating primary veins, the lowest pair arising near or at the apex of the petiole, the leaf thus appearing triplinerved, the ultimate venation finely and irregularly reticulate; ar- eoles less than 1 mm diam; margin entire, sometimes undulate; apex acute to acuminate, rarely obtuse; base subcuneate to cordate; petioles 1-6 cm long, gla- brous to pubescent. Male inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, distinctly paniculate, much longer than the petiole, ascending to spreading-ascending, fili- form, glabrous to sparsely or densely golden-villous; peduncles 1-3.5 cm long; rachis 4-20 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.5-1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, usually villous, sometimes glabrous; pedicels 0.5-4 mm long; bractlets 3, ovate-lanceo- late, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, glabrous to villous. Flowers white, green- ish-brown or greenish-yellow; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate, ca 0.6 mm long, ca 0.4 mm broad, glabrous to very sparsely villous, the inner broadly ovate, ca 0.8 mm long, ca 0.7 mm broad, glabrous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, broadly obovate to orbicular, ca 0.5 mm long and broad, glabrous; stamens usually 6; filaments ca 0.4 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, usually solitary, paniculate, sometimes racemose, much longer than the petiole, ascending to spread- ing-ascending, slender, glabrous to villous; peduncles 1-2.8 cm long; rachis 3-15 cm long; bracts lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, glabrous to villous; pedicels 1-15 mm long; bractlets 3, lanceolate, ca 0.6 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, glabrous to sparsely villous. Flowers greenish-yellow, glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate, ca 0.8 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, the inner broadly ovate, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 1 mm broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, broadly obovate, ca 0.6 mm long, ca 0.4 mm broad; carpels usually 3, oblong-ellipsoid, ca 0.8 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, glabrous. Fruit green to purple, narrowly to broadly obovoid, glabrous, 12-23 mm long, 9-12 mm broad, terete to slightly compressed, the apex rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Slender liana to 20 m; branches terete, pilosulous to glabrate. Leaves coriaceous, ovate to broadly ovate or obovate, 3-9.5 cm long, 1.5-6 cm broad, less than twice as long as broad, glabrate to sparsely tawny pubescent, especially on the nerves above, tawny to golden-villous beneath, with 3 or 4 pairs of alternate arching inconspicuous primary veins, the lowest pair arising near the base of the blade, the ultimate venation finely reticulate; areoles evident, ca 0.3 mm diam; margin entire, rarely undulate; apex rounded to retuse, apiculate; base rounded; petioles 0.5-2 cm long, usually densely tawny-villous. Male inflorescences axillary, solitary or clustered, paniculate, equal to or usually much longer than the petiole, ascending to spreading-ascending, filiform to slender, villous; peduncle 0.2-1 cm long; rachis 1.5-7.7 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.8-1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 1-2.5 mm long; bractlets ovate-lanceolate, ca 0.6 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous. Flowers yellowish-green; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer narrowly ovate-lanceolate, ca 1.3 mm long, ca 0.7 mm broad, moderately villous, the inner broadly ovate to elliptic, ca 2 mm long, ca 6 mm broad, sparsely villous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 0.7 mm broad, glabrous; stamens 6; filaments ca 1 mm long. Female inflores- cences axillary, solitary (?), racemose, longer than the petiole, ascending, slender, villous. Flowers not seen. Fruit obovoid, glabrous, 10-15 mm long, 7-8 mm broad, slightly compressed, the apex rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: High climbing liana; branches terete, grayish, striate, glabrous. Leaves coriaceous, ovate-lanceolate, 7-20 cm long, 3-7 cm broad, mostly more than 3 times longer than broad, glabrous, pinnately veined with 5-8 pairs of alternating primary veins, the ultimate venation irregularly reticulate; areoles ca 1 mm diam; margin entire, slightly undulate; apex acuminate; base narrowed and rounded; petiole 1-2 cm long, conspicuously pulvinate above with horizontal ridges, glabrous. Male inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, paniculate, much longer than the petiole, ascending to spreading-ascending, filiform, sparsely to moderately villous; peduncles 0.05-0.4 cm long; rachis 0.2-0.75 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.5-1.2 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 0.5-2 mm long; bractlets 2 or 3, obovate-oblong, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, sparsely villous. Flowers yellow- ish; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer narrowly obovate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.6 mm broad, glabrous to sparsely villous, the inner obovate, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 0.8 mm broad, glabrous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate, ca 0.9 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, glabrous; stamens 6; filaments ca 0.5 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, solitary, racemose, longer than the petiole, ascending, slender, villous; peduncle 2-3 cm long; rachis 1.5-2 cm long; pedicels 14-16 mm long. Flowers unknown. Fruit ovate, glabrous, 18-20 mm long, ca 15 mm broad, compressed, the apex rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Tree; branches terete, glabrate to tawny-crispate. Leaves coriaceous, lucid, oblong to narrowly ovate, 4-18 cm long, 0.7-5 cm broad, 3-6 times longer than broad, densely tawny-crispate on the midrib; veins and nerves to glabrate in age, pinnately veined with prominent midrib and relatively inconspicuous primary veins, the lowest pair often prominent and appearing triplinerved; ultimate venation conspicuously finely reticulate above and beneath; areoles 0.3-0.7 mm diam; margin entire; apex rounded to acute, apiculate; base rounded; petiole 0.5- 2.5 cm long, densely tawny-crispate to glabrate. Male inflorescences axillary, solitary or clustered, spicate, mostly longer than the petiole, ascending, slender, densely villous; peduncle 0.5-1.5 cm long; rachis 1-2 cm long; bracts lanceolate, ca 0.7 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, densely villous; pedicels 0-0.5 mm long; bractlets 3, lanceolate, ca 0.4 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, villous. Flower color unknown; sepals 6 in 2 series, villous, the outer obovate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.7 mm broad, the inner broadly ovate, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 1 mm broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, glabrous; stamens 6; filaments ca 0.4 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, usually solitary, spicate, much longer than the petiole, ascending, slender, villous; peduncles 0.4- 2.3 cm long; rachis 1-2.5 cm long; bracts lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 0-1 mm long. Flowers not seen. Fruit green, globose, glabrous, 10-17 mm long, 10-17 mm broad, slightly compressed, the apex broadly rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Shrub or small tree to 12 m, to 13 cm diam; branches terete, brownish or grayish, striate, glabrous or slightly hispidulous to tomentulose in the leaf axils. Leaves coriaceous, ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 7-20 cm long, 3-10 cm broad, 2-3 times longer than broad, glabrous above, glabrous to tomentulose beneath especially on the midrib, with 3-6 pairs of alternating upwardly arching primary veins, the lowest pair often arising near or at base of blade; ultimate venation inconspicuously and finely reticulate; areoles ca 0.25 mm diam, finely papillate; margin entire, somewhat undulate; apex acute to obtuse; base truncate to subcuneate; petiole 1-3 cm long, glabrous to hispidulous, with a conspicuously longitudinally ridged pulvinus. Male inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, racemose to paniculate, mostly longer than the petiole, ascending, filiform, sparsely to densely villous; peduncle 0.4-1.8 cm long; rachis 0.5-3.5 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.5-1 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, villous; pedicels 1-5 mm long; bractlets 2 or 3, oblong-lanceolate to oblong-obovate, 0.5-1.5 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm broad, sparsely villous to glabrous. Flowers glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate, 1-1.3 mm long, ca 1 mm broad, the inner broadly obovate to orbicular, ca 1.5 mm long, 1-1.2 mm broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate to rhombic, 0.7-0.9 mm long, 0.5-0.6 mm broad; stamens 6; filaments 0.4-0.5 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, usually solitary, spicate to racemose, shorter to longer than the petiole, ascending, slender becoming stout with age, sparsely to densely villous becoming glabrate; peduncles 0.5-2.3 cm long; rachis 1-3 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.5-1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 0-8 mm long; bractlets 3, oblong-lanceolate, ca 0.8 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer ovate, ca 1.4 mm long, ca 1 mm broad, glabrous to villous, the inner ovate-oblong, ca 1.8 mm long, ca 1 mm broad, glabrous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate-oblong, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.6 mm broad, glabrous; carpels 3, ovoid, ca 0.8 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, glabrous. Fruits yellowish-green to red, usually obovoid, sometimes globose, glabrous, 16- 28 mm long, 15-24 mm broad, slightly compressed, the apex broadly rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Vine; branches terete, glabrate to tawny-woolly above. Leaves membranous, oblong-ovate to ovate, rarely obovate, 3.5-13 cm long, 1.5-6.5 cm broad, mostly more than twice as long as broad, glabrous or occasionally with clustered hirsute pubescence on the midrib beneath, especially when young, with 4 or 5 pairs of arching, alternating, ascending primary veins, the lowest pair arising at base of the blade, the ultimate venation inconspicuously reticulate beneath; areoles ca 0.5 mm diam; margin entire, more or less undulate; apex usually acute to suba- cuminate, rarely retuse and apiculate; base cuneate to rounded; petiole 1-3 cm long, glabrate to tawny-woolly especially above. Male inflorescences axillary, solitary or clustered, spicate to racemose, shorter than the petiole, ascending, slender to stout, densely villous; peduncles very short, 1-3 mm long; rachis 5-12 mm long; bracts lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, densely villous; pedicels 0-0.5 mm long; bractlets 3, lanceolate, ca 0.4 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, densely villous. Flowers greenish-yellow; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 0.7 mm broad, villous, the inner obovate, ca 1.8 mm long, ca 1 mm broad, glabrous to sparsely villous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.6 mm broad, glabrous; stamens 6; filaments ca 0.8 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, usually solitary, spicate to racemose, shorter to longer than the petiole, ascending, slender to stout, sparsely to densely villous; peduncles 0.1-1.7 cm long; rachis 0.5-5 cm long; bracts lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, densely villous; pedicels 0-6 mm long; bractlets 3, oblong- lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.4 mm broad, villous. Flowers greenish-yellow; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer ovate to obovate-lanceolate, ca 1.4 mm long, ca 0.9 mm broad, villous, the inner broadly ovate to obovate, ca 1.7 mm long, ca 1.2 mm broad, glabrous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, ovate to obovate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.8 mm broad, glabrous; carpels 2-4, globose, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.7 mm broad, glabrous. Fruit green, obovoid, glabrous, 17-20 mm long, 10-13 mm broad, slightly compressed, the apex broadly rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Shrub or slender tree to 15 m, to 3.5 dm diam; branches grayish to brown, striate, glabrous to puberulous especially at the nodes. Leaves coriaceous, nar- rowly to broadly ovate, 3-11 cm long, 2-7.5 cm broad, mostly less than twice as long as broad, glabrous, palmately veined with 3-5 primary veins from the base or near the base, then pinnately veined, the ultimate venation regularly reticulate; areoles ca 0.5 mm diam, somewhat papillose beneath; margin entire, rarely some- what undulate; apex obtuse and occasionally retuse; base broadly rounded to subcordate; petioles 1.5-5.5 cm long, inconspicuously pulvinate above. Male inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, racemose to paniculate, longer than the petiole, ascending to spreading-ascending, filiform, sparsely to densely villous; peduncle 0.5-2.2 cm long; rachis 2.5-7 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.3-1 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, villous; pedicels 0-1 mm long; bractlets 2 or 3, lanceolate, ca 0.5 mm long, 0.2 mm broad, villous. Flowers yellowish-green, glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer oblong-lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, the inner broadly ovate to obovate, ca 1.5 mm long, ca 1.1 mm broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, broadly obovate to orbicular, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad; stamens 6; filaments ca 0.5 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, often densely clustered, racemose to paniculate, usually longer than to equaling the petiole, sometimes shorter, ascending to spreading-ascending, slender, becoming stout in age, villous, becoming glabrate in age; peduncle 0.5-2 cm long; rachis 1-4 cm long; bracts lanceolate, ca 0.7 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 2-5 mm long. Flowers not seen. Fruit green, globose, glabrous to very sparsely villous, 8-12 mm long and broad, scarcely compressed, the apex broadly rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Frutex vel arbor ad 5 m altus. Folia coriacea, ovata, 8.5-21 cm longa, 3.5-8 cm lata, glabra et lucentia, triplinervia, pari infimo venarum conspicuo, 1-2.5 cm supra basem folii exorienti, venulis conspicius et tenuibus reticulatis, areolis ca 1 mm diam, margine integris, apice acutis vel acuminatis, ad basem cuneatis, petiolus 1-3 cm longus. Inflorescentiae masculae et femineae ignotae. Fructus aurantiacus, subglobosus, 25 mm longus, 20 mm latus, glaber, ad apicem rotundatus.

description: Shrub or small tree to 5 m. Leaves coriaceous, ovate, 8.5-21 cm long, 3.5-8 cm broad, glabrous and lustrous, with lowermost pair of veins conspicuous, aris- ing 1-2.5 cm above the leaf base, the venation thus appearing triplinerved, the ultimate venation conspicuously and finely reticulate; areoles ca 1 mm in diam; margin entire; apex acute to acuminate; base cuneate; petioles 1-3 cm long. Male inflorescences unknown. Female inflorescences unknown. Mature fruit orange-yellow, subglobose, 25 mm long, 20 mm broad, glabrous, the apex rounded.

description: Large shrub or tree to 10 m with a dense crown, the trunk to 40 cm diam; branches terete, the older ones gray, glabrate, the younger lighter in color, sparsely tomentulose. Leaves coriaceous, ovate, 8.5-20 cm long, 5-10 cm broad, no more than twice as long as broad, the dried leaves yellow-green, glabrous to sparsely tomentulose on the midrib beneath, pinnately veined with 4-6 pairs of prominent alternating arching primary veins, the lowest pair arising near or at the base of the blade, the ultimate venation finely reticulate, less conspicuous on the lower surface; areoles ca 0.3 mm diam, papillose within; margin entire, slightly undulate; apex obtuse; base truncate to subcuneate; petiole 3.5-7.5 cm long, glabrate to tomentulose above. Male inflorescences unknown. Female inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, racemose, equal to or longer than the petiole, spreading-ascending, very stout at maturity, densely villous; fruiting peduncle 0.5-3.5 cm long; rachis 0.5-1.7 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.8-1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 0.6-2.7 mm long. Fruit pendent, yellow, obovoid-orbicular, glabrous, 28-42 mm long, 23-35 mm broad, slightly compressed, the apex broadly rounded.

description: Small tree; branches terete, striate, glabrous to rarely golden-hispid. Leaves coriaceous, lucid, oblong to narrowly ovate, 9-18 cm long, 4-6 cm broad, ca 3 times longer than broad, glabrous, pinnately veined with 8-10 ascending pairs of veins, the ultimate venation finely reticulate; areoles less than 0.5 mm diam, microscopically pellucid; margin entire, conspicuously undulate; apex rounded to acute; base rounded to shallowly cordate; petiole 2-5 cm long, glabrous to rarely hispid. Flowers and fruit not seen.

description: Erect slender tree to 6 m, the trunk to 10 cm diam; branches tan to grey, glabrous. Leaves coriaceous, lucid, ovate, 8-24 cm long, 5-10 cm broad, ca twice as long as broad, glabrous; veins relatively inconspicuous above; ultimate venation conspicuously reticulate; areoles 0.5-1 mm diam; margin entire, somewhat undulate; apex acute to rounded; base rounded to subcordate; petiole 1.5-6 cm long, glabrous. Male inflorescences axillary, densely clustered. Flowers not seen. Female inflorescences cauliflorous and densely clustered, sometimes axillary, racemose to paniculate, longer than the petiole, ascending, slender, becoming stout with age, strigillose; peduncles 1.0-3.6 cm long; rachis 1.5-8.6 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.7-1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, strigillose; pedicels 1-5 mm long; bractlets 3, obovate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.8 mm broad, glabrous. Flowers yellowish-green, glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer ovate, ca 1.5 mm long, ca 1.1 mm broad, the inner broadly ovate to orbicular, ca 2.2 mm long, ca 2 mm broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate-spatulate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.8 mm broad; carpels 3-5, obovoid, ca 1.4 mm long, ca 1 mm broad, glabrous. Fruit green, obovoid to globose, glabrous, 12-15 mm long and broad, slightly com- pressed, the apex broadly rounded.

description: Shrub or tree to 10 m or more, the trunk to 19 cm diam; branches terete, the older ones gray, glabrate, the younger hispidulous to glabrate; axillary buds densely hispid. Leaves coriaceous, oblanceolate to angulate-obovate, 3-13 cm long, 1.5-4 cm broad, mostly 2-4 times longer than broad, glabrous; midrib ev- ident, the primary and ultimate venation obscure, inconspicuously papillose be- neath; margin undulate; apex acute to abruptly attenuate; base cuneate; petiole 0.5-1 cm long, hispidulous to glabrate. Male inflorescences axillary, solitary or clustered, racemose, longer than the petiole, ascending, filiform, villous; pedun- cle 0.4-1.7 cm long; rachis 1-3.6 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.5-1 mm long, 0.2- 0.4 mm broad, villous; pedicels 1-3 mm long; bractlets 3, oblong-lanceolate, ca 0.8 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous. Flowers greenish-yellow (?); sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, sparsely villous to glabrous, the inner broadly obovate, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 1.2 mm broad, glabrous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, orbicular, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, glabrous; stamens 3-5 (6); filaments ca 0.5 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, usually solitary, racemose, longer than the petiole, ascending, stout, villous, becoming glabrate with age; peduncles 0.3-1.1 cm long; rachis 0.3-2.5 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.7-1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 1-3 mm long. Flowers not seen. Fruit globose to obovoid, glabrous to very sparsely villous, 15-24 mm long, 18-23 mm broad, slightly compressed, the apex broadly rounded.

description: Frutex parvus ramis ramulisque exfoliatus brunneis cicatricosis peridermato-exfoliantibus, ramusculis foliatis erectis vel suberectis foliis congestis subimbri- catis patulis dense obtectis. Folia coriacea crassiuscula opposita sessilia ovato-rotundata vel orbiculata, apice rotundata vel obtusissime angulata margine integra tantum nervo medio paulo apparenti superficie laevis sed leviter papillosula pellueide punctata 4-6 mm longa 3.5-5 mm lata. Flores solitarii sessiles ramusculos dense foliosos terminantes. Sepala 5 eras- siuscula ovata apice subacutata 5 mm longa 3.8 mm lata, laevia. Petala lutea obovato-oblonga 9 mm longa 4 mm lata limbo valde obliquo. Stamina creberrima filamentis tenuis circa 5 mm longis. Ovarium 2-5 mm longum; stylis tribus 4 mm longis.

description: Shrub or small tree to 4 m; young stems slightly 4-angled, the surface smooth with rectangular epidermal cells. Petiole slender, 1-1.5 mm in diameter, 7-13 mm long, essentially bullate due to bulging of individual cells; leaf blade thinly coriaceous, dull green to olivaceous abaxially and stramineous adaxially (when dried), elliptic to elliptic-obovate, 3.5-9.2 X 1.4-3.6 cm, the base acute, the apex acute to slightly acuminate, rarely slightly emarginate or obtuse; margin plane or sometimes slightly revolute when dry; midvein nearly plane above and prominent beneath with ± rectangular epidermal cells, the secondary veins 5-8 per side, sub-immersed on both surfaces, obscurely anastomosing, with spicy-sweet, but lacking a strong anise fragrance when crushed. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary; subtending bracts 2- 5, orbicular to ovate-deltoid, ca. 1 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, caducous. Pedicels slender, 0.4-1 mm wide, 3.5-10 mm long at anthesis, with 2-3 caducous bracteoles. Perianth segments (tepals) 16-20, yellowish, tinged basally with salmon, or yellowish with peach margins, thick-carnose to subcoriaceous, glandular punctate, orbicular to broadly deltoid, the outer ones the largest, to 7 mm long, ovate, the entire surface densely covered with papillae spreading to the ciliate margin, the inner ones up to 4 mm long, orbicular, non-papillose with entire margins, the innermost sometimes transitional to stamens. Stamens 6 (rarely 8), uniseriate, to 2.5 mm long, carnose, the filament laminar, shortened and thickened, narrowed or truncate at base, obtuse at apex, the thecae introrse, sub-immersed in the connective tissue, 0.5-1 mm long. Carpels 10-13, in a single whorl, up to 2.5 mm long, often minutely papillose on the surface, the ovaries flattened, ellipsoidal, the styles erect. Follicles in star-like cluster, 22-30 mm wide, with each ending in a short acumen, sometimes with papillae on the suture; fruiting pedicels up to 18 mm long, but mostly 12-15 mm long. Seeds brown to stramineous, 4.8-5.5 mm long, 3.5-4 mm wide, the testa smooth.

description: Tree to 20 m. tall, the branches terete, the youngest twigs glabrous, shining when dry, the bark light brown, longitudinally striate; petioles 1-1.5 cm. long, sparsely hirsute or glabrate, deeply canaliculate above; lamina oblong, 6-11 cm. long, 3-4 cm. wide, coriaceous, turning black on drying, glabrous, shining above, the margin entire, slightly revolute, the midrib sulcate above, prominent below, the veins 6-8 pairs, oblique, arcuate near the margin and anastomosing, inconspicuous above, slightly prominent below, the apex acuminate with ultimate apex obtuse, the base cuneate, frequently slightly decurrent on the petiole; inflorescence axillary, the peduncle to 1 cm. long, bracteate, the rhachis hirsute, the 2-3-chotomized branches eymose, the flowers slightly glomerate, unisexual; calyx cupular, 2-2.7 mm. in diameter, 1-1.2 mm. high, indistinctly 5-toothed, glabrous; petals oblong, 4-4.2 mm. long, 1.7-2 mm. wide, glabrous, the apex inflexed; fertile stamens 3.2-3.4 mm. long at anthesis, the filaments broadly oblong, 0.9-1 mm. wide, fleshy, flattened, densely white-pilose above, the anthers elliptic-oblong, 0.9-1 mm. long; sterile stamens slightly smaller; pistillate rudiment terete or conical, 1.2 mm. high, immersed in a fleshy disk 1.2 mm. in diameter and 1 mm. high, undifferentiated; fertile pistil asymmetric, with a lateral gibbosity 1.6 mm. high, the fertile carpel 3.5 mm. high, 1.7 mm. wide and 0.3 mm. thick, glabrous, curved, the locule with two pendent anatropous ovules, the style none, the stigma sunken; drupe elliptic or broadly elliptic-ovate, flattened, 3 cm. long, 2 cm. wide, 0.6 cm. thick, one surface plane or rarely slightly concave, strongly ridged, the other surface convex, the T-shaped median ridge surmounted by an oblong fleshy appendage, the sareocarp fleshy, shining when dry, the putamen woody, the locule one, the seed one, anatropous, 1.6 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Howard, Richard A. 1943. Studies of the Icacinaceae--VI. Irvingbaileya and Codiocarpus, two new genera of the Icacineae. Brittonia. 5: 47-57. f. 1-3.

description: Tree up to 20 m. or more in height, the trunk slender; branchlets stout, when young densely strigose, soon cinereous-puberulent, at length glabrous and rugose; petioles canaliculate, 1.5-2 mm. in diameter, 9-12 mm. long, at first densely ferruginous-strigose, soon glabrous, rugose, nigrescent; leaf blades coriaceous, minutely rugose or finely papillose and dull on both surfaces, glabrous, elliptic-oblong, 10-15 cm. long, 3.5-6 cm. broad, rounded or obtuse at base, obtusely short acuminate at apex, the costa raised above, the secondary nerves 10-13 per side, spreading, slightly impressed above, nearly plane beneath, often obscure on both surfaces, inconspicuously anastomosing near margins, the veinlets immersed; staminate inflorescences 5-11 cm. long, narrowly paniculate (lateral branches numerous, straight, less than 1 cm. long, suppressed toward apex of inflorescence), densely ferruginous-strigose with hairs resembling those of the young branchlets, the peduncle less than 1 cm. long, the rachis slender, often curved; flowers 5-15 per fascicle, often clustered at the swollen ends of lateral branches, the pedicels slender, up to 5 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole one-sided, oblonig, 0.5-0.8 mm. long, membranous); perianth thin carnose, cupuli- form, 1.8-2.2 mm. long, 3-lobed more than one-half its total length, the lobes ovate-deltoid, subacute, spreading at maturity; androecium 1-1.2 mm. long, the filament column slender, the anthers 0.2-0.25 mm. long, dorsally connate by means of carnose fused connectives; pistillate inflorescences not seen; fruiting inflorescences up to 7 cm. long, the mature fruits often 2 or 3 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 6-10 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid or nearly subglobose, distinctly carinate, 20-24 mm. long (excluding stipe), 21-26 mm. broad, obtuse at apex, the stipe stout, 1-3 mm. long, the pericarp rugose, 3-4 mm. thick or slightly more on the sutures.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Large tree; branchlets slender, subterete or obtusely angled; petioles rugose, shallowly canaliculate, 1-2.5 mm. in diameter, 3-12 mm. long, glabrous; leaf blades coriaceous or thin coriaceous, finely rugose or minutely papillose on both surfaces, often shining above, elliptic-oblong, 9-22 cm. long, 4-9 cm. broad, obtuse at base, obtusely cuspidate or short acuminate at apex, the costa raised above, the secondary nerves 13-18 per side, spreading, impressed above, prominent beneath, conspicuously anastomosing near margins, the veinlets obscure or slightly impressed above; staminate inflorescences 0.5-3 cm. long, fasciculate-racemose, the peduncle inconspicuous, the rachis comparatively stout, the fascicles alternate or subopposite, 3-10 per inflorescence; flowers 5-10 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 3 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole one-sided, oblong, sometimes 2- or 3-cleft, less than 1 mm. long); perianth carnose or thin carnose, often glabrescent, cupuliform or subrotate, 1.5-2 mm. long, 3-lobed more than one-half its total length, the lobes deltoid, obtuse, spreading at maturity; androecium 0.8-1.3 mm. long, the filament column carnose, the anthers 0.25-0.4 mm. long, dorsally connate, the connectives inconspicuous or slightly carnose and swollen; pistillate inflorescences usually axillary, less than 1.5 cm. long, the fascicles 2-4 per inflorescence, the flowers densely aggregated in clusters of 7-12, the pedicels up to 2 mm. long, the ovary cylindric- conical, glabrous, the stigma subsessile, 2-lobed; fruiting inflorescences compact, 2-3 mm. long, the mature fruits usually 2-5 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 3-5 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid, at maturity up to 12 mm. long and 19 mm. broad, conspicuously carinate apiculate at apex, short stipitate at base (stipe stout, 1-2 mm. long), the pericarp rugose, about 0.5 mm. thick, thicker on the sutures and at apex, the seed smooth, transversely ellipsoid.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Tree up to 20 m. in height, the trunk slender; branchlets slender; petioles rugose, canaliculate, narrowly winged distally, 1-2 mm. in diameter, 6-15 mm. long, glabrous; leaf blades chartaceous or thin coriaceous, finely rugose or minutely papillose and usually dull on both surfaces, elliptic-obovate or obovate-oblong, 10-20 cm. long, 3-7 cm. broad, acute to subattenuate at base, obtusely short acuminate at apex, the costa raised above, the secondary nerves 10-17 per side, spreading, slightly impressed or faintly raised above, raised beneath, inconspicuously anastomosing near margin, the veinlets immersed; staminate infloreseences 2-9 cm. long, fasciculate-racemose (fascicles sometimes borne on minute lateral branches about 1 mm. long), uniformly minutely strigose, the peduncle short, the rachis sleinder, the fascicles alternate, 5-18 per inflorescence; flowers 3-7 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 6 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole membranous, oblong, rounded at apex, one-sided, less than 1 mm. long); perianth earnose or thin earnose, often glabrescent, cupuliform, 2-3.5 mm. long (normal flowers sometimes associated with unusually large and often abnormal flowers up to 4 mm. long), 3 (rarely 4)-lobed more than one-half its total length, the lobes deltoid, subacute; androecium 0.8- 1.5 mm. long, the filament column carnose, conspicuously swollen at base, 0.6-1.1 mm. long, the anthers 0.3-0.5 mm. long, dorsally connate or divergent in the distal one-half, the connectives usually inconspicuous, sometimes slightly carnose and glandular; pistillate inflorescences aggregated on the old bark of trunk, branches, or defoliated branchlets, 4-9 cm. long, usually 3-6-branched from base, the branches spreading, stout, ferruginous-strigose, sometimes again branched; flowers densely aggregated in clusters of 15-40 at the swollen ends of branchlets or fasciculate in smaller clusters near the ends of branchlets, the pedicels up to 4 mm. long, the ovary subglobose or ellipsoid, the stigma subsessile; fruiting inflorescences slightly longer than the pistillate, the mature fruits usually 1-3 per branch of inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 5-7 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid or subglobose, 13- 20 mm. long, 15-24 mm. broad, inconspicuously carinate (sometimes slightly impressed at the sutures), smooth at apex, the lateral extremi- ties rounded, the base flattened or obtuse, essentially estipitate, the pericarp rugose, 1-2 mm. thick, the aril inconspicuously laciniate in the distal one-third with broad lobes, the seed transversely ellipsoid or subglobose. (Fig. 5. a-i.)

description: Arbor 30-35 m. alta, ramis ramulisque subteretibus rugosis brunneis juventute parce puberulis mox glabris; petiolis minute puberulis rugosis gracilibus profunde canaliculatis 15-18 mm. longis; laminis subcoriaceis pellucido-punctatis obovatis vel obovato-oblongis, 9-11 cm. longis, 3-1 cm. latis, basi attenuatis, apice obtusis vel rotundatis, mar-gine anguste revolutis, utrinque glabris, supra nitidis, subtus minute ceriferis, costa supra impressa subtus prominente, nervis secundariis utroque 8 vel 9 adscendentibus supra leviter impressis subtus elevatis, venulis paucis reticulatis; inflorescentiis  axillaribus sub anthesi ad 1 cm. longis, 2- vel 3-floris, ubique minute brunneo-tomentellis; pedi-cellis 1-2 mm. longis; perigonio cupulari 4 mm. longo et diametro, lobis 3 deltoideo-ovatis obtusis circiter 2.5 mm. longis et latis, intus glabris; ovario glabro complanato sub anthesi 2.5 mm. longo, stigmate sessili; fructibus 1-3 per inflorescentiam, ut videtur maturitate circiter 1.5 cm. altis et latis, compressis, acute circumcarinatis, basi contractis.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description: Tree up to 25 m. high, the trunk often 50 cm. in diameter; branch- lets slender, rugose, glabrous, often conspicuously lenticellate; petioles shallowly canaliculate, 1-2 mm. in diameter, often narrowly winged 7-15 mm. long, glabrous; leaf blades chartaceous or thin coriaceous, nearly smooth on both surfaces, usually shining above, oblong or elliptic-oblong or obovate-oblong, 8-17 cm. long, 3-7 cm. broad, obtuse to attenuate at base, obtuse or obtusely short acuminate at apex, the costa slightly raised above, the secondary nerves 8-14 per side, spreading, slightly impressed or plane above, usually plane beneath, often obscure on both surfaces, inconspicuously anastomosing near margins, the veinlets immersed; staminate inflorescences fasciculate-racemose or narrowly paniculate (lateral branches few, not exceeding 2 cm. in length), 4-10 cm. long, sparsely strigose on all exterior surfaces, soon glabrescent, the peduncle up to 2 cm. long, the rachis and lateral branches slender, striate, the fascicles numerous; flowers 2-9 per fascicle, often irregularly arranged near the ends of short lateral branches, the pedicels slender, up to 12 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole cupuliform or cleft to base, membranous, 0.5-1 mm. long); perianth thin carnose, campanulate, flaring distally, 3.5-4.5 mm. long, 3-lobed about one-third its total length, the lobes deltoid, subacute; androecium 1.6- 2.3 mm. long, the filament column stout, carnose, the anthers 3, 0.4-0.5 mm. long, dorsally connate by means of carnose fused connectives; pistillate inflorescences resembling the staminate, often arising from the same branchlets, the perianth similar to the staminate, the ovary ovoid- conical, the style short, the stigma obliquely cleft; fruiting inflorescences often branching from base, the mature fruits 5-10 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, rugose, 5-10 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid, distinctly carinate, at maturity 15-23 mm. long (excluding stipe), 18-30 mm. broad, the stipe stout, 2-4 mm. long, the apex apicu- late, the pericarp rugose, 2-5 mm. thick, the seed up to 15 by 24 mm.

description: Tree up to 20 m. high or more; branchlets stout, subterete or obtusely angled; petioles rugose, soon glabrous, canaliculate, narrowly winged distally, 2-4 mm. in diameter, 10-20 mm. long, often nigrescent; leaf blades coriaceous, conspicuously papillose on both surfaces, paler beneath, elliptic-oblong, 15-30 cm. long, 4-10 cm. broad, acute or obtuse at base, obtusely short acuminate at apex, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 13-20 per side, spreading, slightly impressed above, raised beneath, regularly anastomosing near margins, the veinlets usually obscure; staminate inflorescences 3-8 cm. long, fasciculate-racemnose or narrowly paniculate (lateral branches less than 3 mm. long), minutely strigose, the peduncle less than 2.5 cm. long, the rachis usually straight, the fascicles alternate or subopposite, 7-12 per inflorescence; flowers 4-10 per fascicle, often clustered at the ends of the short lateral branches, the pedicels slender, up to 5 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole membranous, one-sided, 0.5-1.5 mm. long); perianth thin carnose, cupuliform, 2-3 mm. long, 3-lobed about one-half its total length, the lobes deltoid, subacute or rounded; androe- cium 1-1.6 mm. long, the filament column carnose, swollen at base, the anthers 0.4-0.5 mm. long, dorsally connate by means of carnose fused connectives; pistillate inflorescences not known; fruiting inflorescences compact, on principal branches or defoliated branchlets, the mature fruits few, pedicellate (pedicels rugose, 5-8 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid, faintly carinate, 13-17 mm. long (excluding stipe), 20-25 mm. broad, apieulate at apex, the stipe 2-3 mm. long, the pericarp less than 1 mm. thick, the aril cleft in the distal one-third with a few broad lobes.

description: Tree up to 17 m. high; branchlets stout, glabrous; petioles canaliculate, rugose, narrowly winged distally, 2-5 mm. in diameter, 10-20 mm. long, glabrous; leaf blades thick coriaceous, finely rugose or uniformly minutely papillose on both surfaces, oblong or obovate-oblong, 17-35 cm. long, 5-12 cm. broad (occasionally up to 40 by 14 cm.), subcordate or rounded or obtuse at base, obtusely cuspidate or short acuminate at apex, the costa prominent above, very strong beneath, the secondary nerves 14-20 per side, straight, spreading, slightly raised or shallowly impressed above, prominant beneath, conspicuously and regularly anastomosing near margins, the veinlets immersed; staminate inflorescences fasciculate-racemose, 3-7 cm. long (rarely 2-11 cm11.), minutely and sparsely strigose on all exterior surfaces, the rachis stout, striate, conspicuously swollen at the fascicles; fascicles alternate or subopposite, 6-13 per inflorescence; flowers 4-12 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 5 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole cupuliform or cleft to base, 0.7-1.5 mm. long); perianth carnose, 2-3 mm. long, flaring distally, 3-lobed about one-third its total length, the lobes deltoid, obtuse, often thickened at apex; androecium nearly as long as the perianth, the filament column carnose, 1.5-2.2 mm. long, the anthers 3, about 0.5 mm. long, free to base, the connectives swollen, glandular; pistillate inflores- cences not seen; fruiting inflorescences compact, less than 5 em. long, the mature fruits usually 3 or 4 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 5-10 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid, carinate, at maturity 8-24 mm. long, 10-26 mm. broad, inconspicuously stipitate, bluntly apiculate at apex, the pericarp rugose, 1.5-6 mm. thick, the seed transversely elliptic, slightly broader than long, the aril laciniate about half its total length.

description: Medium sized tree; branchlets slender, rugose, glabrous, cinereous; petioles shallowly canaliculate, glabrous, nigrescent, about 1.5 mm. in diameter, 10-13 mm. long; leaf blades coriaceous, minutely rugose or finely papillose and dull on both surfaces, elliptic or obovate-elliptic 9-12 cm. long, 3.5-6 cm. broad, obtuse at base, rounded or obtuse at apex, slightly thickened at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 12-15 per side, spreading, minutely impressed above, plane beneath, often obscure on both surfaces, obscurely anastomosing near margins, the veinlets immersed; staminate inflorescences 3-7 cm. long, fasciculate-racemose or narrowly paniculate (lateral branches few, not exceeding 2 cm. in length), sparsely strigose, often glabrescent, the peduncle short, the rachis and lateral branches slender; flowers 2-5 per fascicle, the fascicles usually sessile, the pedicels slender, up to 10 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole one-sided, membranous, ovate, subacute, about 1 mm. long); perianth thin carnose, cupuliform, 2-3 mm. long, 3-lobed more than one-half its total length, the lobes ovate, obtuse or subacute; androecium 1-1.3 mm. long, the filament column carnose, swollen at base, the anthers about 0.4 mm. long, dorsally connate, the connectives inconspicuous; pistillate and fruiting inflorescences not known.

description: Small tree, the branchlets rugose, slender, glabrous; petioles shallowly canaliculate, rugose, glabrous, 2-3 mm. in diameter, 5 mm. long or more; leaf blades chartaceous or thin coriaceous, smooth above, densely and minutely glandular beneath, elliptic-oblong, 15-24 cm. long, 4-6 cm. broad, obtuse at base, obtusely short acuminate at apex, the costa shallowly grooved above, the prinicipal secondary nerves about 12 per side, paralleled by numerous tertiary nerves, prominulous on both surfaces, spreading, conspicuously anastomosing near margins, the veinilets copiously reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces; staminate inflorescences simple or 2-5-branched (branches spreading, nearly as long as the main rachis, minutely bracteate at base), 9-15 cm. long, minutely strigose on all exterior surfaces, the peduncle 2-3 cm. long, the rachis and secondary branches slender, the fascicles essentially sessile, alternate or opposite, 3-10 per inflorescence (or per branch), the bracts inconspicuous; flowers 5-10 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 10 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole ovate-oblong, about 0.5 mm. long); perianth thin carnose, soon glabrous, campanulate, 3-4 mm. long, slightly flaring distally, 3-lobed about one-third its total length, the lobes ovate-deltoid, subacute, often glandular-margined; androecium nearly as long as the perianth, the filamnent column carnose, about 3 mm. lonig, the anthers 3, about 0.5 mm. long, dorsally connate; pistillate and fruiting inflorescences not seen.

description: Tree up to 30 m. in height, the trunk slender; branchlets subterete or obtusely angled, slender; petioles canaliculate, rugose, narrowly winged distally, 1.5-2 mm. in diameter, 6-12 mm. long, essentially glabrous; leaf blades coriaceous or thin coriaceous, finely rugose or minutely papillose or nearly smooth on both surfaces, often shining above, oblong-elliptic, 15-30 cm. long, 4-10 cm. broad, obtuse to acute at base, obtusely cuspidate or acuminate at apex (acumen occasionally up to 20 mm. long), the costa raised above, the secondary nerves 12-20 per side, usually deeply impressed above and prominent beneath, conspicuously and regularly anastomosing near margin, the veinlets immersed or faintly impressed on both surfaces; staminate inflorescences 0.5-9 cm. long, fasciculate-racemose or narrowly paniculate (fascicles sometimes borne on lateral branches up to 5 mm. long), uniformly minutely ferruginous-puberulent on all exterior surfaces, the peduncle short, the rachis slender, slightly swollen at fascicles, the fascicles alternate or subopposite, 3-17 per inflorescence; flowers 5-10 per fasciele, the pedicels slender, up to 5 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole one-sided or subpeltate, 0.5-1 mm. long); perianth carnose or thin carnose, often glabrescent, cupuliform, 1.5-3 mm. long, 3-lobed about one- half its length or slightly more, the lobes deltoid, subacute, spreading at maturity; androecium 0.8-1.5 mm. long, the filament column carnose, the anthers 0.2-0.6 mm. long, dorsally connate or divergent at apex the connectives inconspicuous or slightly carnose; pistillate inflorescences often aggregated on the old bark of trunk or branches, some- times axillary and much contracted, up to 8 cm. long (if axillary frequently less than 1 cm. long), usually few-branched from base; flowers aggregated in clusters of 10-40, the pedicels up to 5 mm. long, the ovary cylindric-conical, glabrous, the stigma subsessile, shallowly cleft; fruiting inflorescences slightly longer than the pistillate, the mature fruits usually 1-3 per branch of inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 5-9 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid, 8-11 mm. long (excluding stipe), 13-18 mm. broad, conspicuously carinate, apiculate at apex, the lateral extremities subacute, the stipe stout, 2-3 mm. long, the pericarp rugose, 0.5-1.5 mm. thick or slightly more on the sutures, the seed much broader than long, smooth. (Fig. 5. j.)

description: Frutex squamatus ramosissimus, statu sicco olivaceus. Internodia usque ad 7 cm longa, valde alternatim complanata, circumscriptione oblonga vel subrhomboidea, ad 10 mm lata, latitudine maxima paulum sub nodo, minima paulum supra nodum. Squamae foliaceae magnitudine infra 1 mm, obtuse triangulares; phyllotaxis decussata. Ramuli laterales vel flores haud ultra 5 pro axilla. Flores hermaphroditi, maturitate 2 mm longi, infra 1 mm lati. Calyculus manifestus. Perianthii partes 4, late ovales, ca 1 mm longae, antheris singulis sessilibus obsitae. Antherae sacculis polliniferis binis, minutis, longitudinaliter dehiscentes. Pistillum obtuse conoideum, basi quad- rilobatum, stigmate capitato. Stylus persistens. Fructus bacciformis, ovoideus, maxi- mus metatus 3.5 X 2 mm. Grana pollinis quadricolpata, globosa. Affixiones haustoriales observatae simplices, sine radicibus epicorticalibus.

description: Woody twining vine 5-8 m long, producing abundant milky sap in all its parts. Stems cylindrical, glabrous, lenticellate, reaching ca. 3 cm diam. at base; bark light gray. Leaves opposite, ovate, 6-6.5 X 3.5- 4 cm, coriaceous, involute, the apex acute, obtuse, or shortly acuminate, the base rounded, with 2 acicular glands at the junction with the petiole, the margins entire, revolute, the adaxial surface glabrous, slightly shiny, with whitish midvein, the abaxial surface glabrous or minutely puberulent, lighter than the adaxial; petioles 1.5-2 cm long, glabrous, light green, adaxially canaliculate. Inflorescence an umbelliform cyme, with 5-20 flowers; peduncle ca. 1 cm long; pedicels 7-10 mm long. Calyx light green, the sepals 5, imbricate, ovate, puberulent, 3-3.5 mm long, with obtuse apex and ciliate margins; corolla of 5 distinct, ovate lobes, 5.5-7 mm long, glabrous, green in the middle portion, purplish pink toward the strongly revolute margins, the apex reflexed; coronal appendages adnate to the staminal column, fleshy, asymmetrically pyramidal, ca. 2.5 X 3 mm, with inflexed apex; stamens oblong, 3-3.5 mm long; corpusculum dark brown, the translator arms nearly horizontal, the pollinia erect, ca. 0.7 mm long; stigmatic head flat. Follicle lance-fusiform, slightly flattened, woody, 11-13 X 2-3 cm. Seeds numerous, membranous, ovate, ca. 1 cm long; coma beige.
