description: Tree, 25 x 1 m. Sapwood scanty; heartwood brown (label data). Leaf-bearing branchlets glabrous, grey, developing longitudinal and transverse cracks with age, without conspicuous lenticels. Stipular glands crateriform, round to oblong, 0.5-2.5 mm diam., the callose margin brown, the center dark brown to blackish, and usually a small wart-like accessory gland 1-3 mm below main one. Leaf blades elliptic to obovate, 5-9 x 2.5-6 cm, chartaceous, glabrous, at apex acute to slightly acuminate, at base obtuse, the margins entire, the venation brochidodromous, with 5-8 pairs of lateral veins; petioles 10-15 mm long, darker than the midrib, grooved above. Inflorescence terminal, to 15 x 6 cm, tapering slightly towards the apex; principal rachis glabrous or puberulous towards the apex, with pedunculate, 2-10-flowered cymes scattered 1-3 cm apart along its length, the peduncle 4-10 mm long, pubescent, the pedicels 6-10 mm long, pubescent. Flower buds 6-8 mm long. Calyx greenish, densely pubescent, 5-lobed, the 3 smaller outer lobes carnose, obovate, 5-6.5 x 4.5-5.5 mm, the inner non-spurred lobe obovate, 8 x 6.5 mm, its margins slightly enrolled, the inner spurred lobe ovate, 9 mm long, its margins strongly enrolled to form a tube, the spur densely pilose, clavate, 6 x 2.5 mm, its wall 1 mm thick. Petal obcordate, 20-24 x 22-26 mm, short-clawed, glabrous throughout, violaceous. Filament 9 mm long, slightly curved, the anther 2 mm long. Ovary spherical, 2.5 mm diam, densely covered with stiff, upright, shiny, stramineous hairs; style 8-9 mm long, curved, light brown; stigma about as wide as the style. Fruit ca 6 cm long, the valves oblong, 1.5-2 cm wide.

description: Arbor 6-25 m alta. Folia alterna; petioli 9-20 mm longi; laminae ellipticae vel late ellipticae vel subobovatae, parum asymmetricae, integrae, 11-25 cm longae, 5-13 cm latae. Pedicelli floriferi 3-bracteolati, 9-10 mm longi. Calyx anguste conicus, aurantiacus, 14-18 mm longus. Petala 5, alba, spathulata, circa 32 mm longa, 5 mm lata. Columna staminalis crassa, 22-23 mm longa, stylo paulo brevior. Thecae 50, ellipticae vel reniformes, geminae. Ovarium 2-loculare. Fructus drupaceus, ovoi- deus vel ellipsoideus, lepidotus, 25-35 mm longus, ca 25 mm diametro, 1- vel 2-seminalis. Pedicelli fructiferi 14-27 mm longi. Calyx fructifer cupulatus, rugosus, aurantiacus, 22-27 mm longus.

description: Tree 6-25 m tall; trunk monopodial and somewhat fluted; branches plagiotropic (sensu Halle et al., 1978), horizontal, verticillate, initially 4 or 5 per whorl but  only 1-3 per whorl usually persisting; young branches grayish-brown, densely lepidote with brown fimbriate-peltate trichomes, glabrate and rugose with age; outer bark exfoliating in small rounded pieces, soft, rufous-brown. Stipules tri- angular, 4-7 mm long, ca 1.5 mm broad at base, deciduous, densely lepidote; leaves alternate, entire, simple (unifoliolate?); petioles terete, 9-20 mm long (in- cluding the proximal and distal pulvini), green when fresh, dull brownish-green or brown when dried, densely lepidote, the proximal pulvini 1-3 mm and the distal 6-14 mm long; leaf blades elliptic to broadly elliptic or subobovate, slightly asymmetric, 11-25 cm long, 5-13 cm wide, at base often oblique, cuneate or rounded to truncate, at apex acute to slightly caudate, pliable but relatively thick, medium to dark green and sparsely lepidote above, medium green and sparsely to moderately lepidote below, not barbate (i.e., without domatia along midrib below), without spicy odor when fresh or dried; secondary veins prominent below, pinnate, 5-8 per side (not including 1-2 additional weak basal veins per side, the base thus inconspicuously 3- or 5-palmate), gently arched, eucamptodromous on proximal half, becoming brochidodromous distally, forming a raised reticulum with the tertiary veins. Flowers actinomorphic, their angle of presentation un- known; pedicels 9-10 mm long, creamy apricot-brown, densely lepidote, bearing 3 bracteoles more or less equidistant along length; bracteoles triangular to broadly triangular, 2-3 mm long, 2-3 mm broad at base, densely lepidote; calyx narrowly conical, 14-18 mm long, ca 10 mm diam and unevenly 4- or 5-lobed at summit, longitudinally rugose when dried, creamy orange to apricot-brown when fresh, dull medium brown when dried, densely lepidote without, densely sericeous with long, pale, ascending trichomes within, the apical lobes acute or blunt, 4-7 mm long, often unequal and strongly reflexed; petals 5, spathulate, ca 32 mm long, 5 mm wide when dried, at apex acute to acuminate, white when fresh, dull brown above and dark sepia-brown towards base when dried, densely tomentose with pale stellate trichomes on both sides except for the glabrous base; staminal column cylindrical, relatively stout, 22-23 mm long (including the apical lobes), 2-3 mm diam and bluntly pentangular in cross-section when dried, dilated from the base to the summit, white to cream when fresh, when dried with color and indument similar to the dried petals, bearing 50 thecae towards summit, the apical lobes 5, 2.5-3 mm long, rounded or truncate at apex; thecae elliptic to reniform, 1.2-1.5 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, distinctly paired, arrayed in 5 pairs per staminal lobe; ovary 2-locular; style filiform, 24-25 mm long, at apex angular and densely to- mentose; stigma bilobed, 1-2.5 mm diam. Fruits drupaceous, ovoid to ellipsoid, 25-35 mm long and 22-25 mm diam when dried, at apex rounded and apiculate with the persistent style base; exocarp leathery, ca 1 mm thick, pale apricot-brown when fresh, drying to a slightly lustrous medium brown, extremely densely lepidote with minute, pale brown fimbriate-peltate to stellate-peltate trichomes; mesocarp pulpy-fibrous; endocarp bony-fibrous; pedicels of fruit 14-27 mm long, greatly dilated from the base to the apex, bearing 2 or 3 persistent bracteoles equidistant along length; calyx of fruit deeply cup-shaped, 22-27 mm long, 20-25 mm diam, accrescent, covering ca /2 of fruit when ripe, conspicuously rugose longitudinally, pale creamy-orange ("beige-cream-orange," Schatz 1068) when fresh, dull creamy- brown when dried, on outer surface densely lepidote with lustrous, brown fim- briate-peltate trichomes of various sizes, sericeous within; seeds 1 or 2 in number, not examined. Seedlings unknown but probably hypogeal and cryptocotylar (sensu Ng, 1978).
bibliographicCitation: Alverson, Andrew H. 1989. Quararibea (Bombacaceae): five new species from moist and wet forests of Costa Rica and Panama. Brittonia. 41(1): 61-74.

Pedicelli floriferi 3-bracteolati, 6-11 mm longi. Calyx anguste conicus, viridis, 9-13 cm longus. Petala 5, alba, spathulata, 15-25 mm longa, 5-7 mm lata. Columna staminalis 18-24 mm longa, stylo paulo brevior. Thecae 30, ellipticae vel reniformes, geminae. Ova- rium 2- vel 3-loculare. Calyx fructifer urceolatus vel cupulatus, viridis vel viridi-brunneus, 15-25 mm longus.

description: Tree 8-20 m tall, 20-60 (120) cm dbh; trunk monopodial or forked, irregular and angular in cross-section, fluted to ca 1/3 of height, not buttressed; crown irregular in forest-grown trees, conical to broadly pyramidal in open-grown individuals; plagiotropic branches usually horizontal or drooping, sometimes slightly ascending, verticillate, 4 or 5 per whorl, only 1-3 persisting at most older whorls; orthotropic branches relatively uncommon, developing from plagiotropic branches high in the crown or from the trunk itself (Fig. 4A); young branches slender, gray or grayish-brown when fresh, characteristically drying to dark brown or dark rufous-brown, densely tomentulose with dark brown fasciculate trichomes, glabrate and rugose with age; outer bark finely textured, medium brown, exfoliating in small, rounded plates to give the trunk a characteristic mottled appearance, the plates 1-10 cm diam and 1-2 mm thick; inner bark cream to yellowish-green with an anastomosing network of pale tenacious fibers. Stipules triangular, often keeled at base, 4-9 mm long, 2-3 mm broad at base, deciduous, firm, densely tomentulose; stipule scars characteristically pale and very conspicuous on the dark branchlets; leaves alternate, entire, simple (unifoliolate?); petioles terete, 9-23 mm long (including the proximal and distal pulvini), appearing granuliferous because of indument of squat, rufous-brown, echinate or stellate-peltate trichomes, the proximal pulvini 1-3 mm and the distal 6-16 mm long; leaf blades elliptic to ovate, mildly but conspicuously asymmetric, 7-23 cm long, 3-14 cm wide, at base oblique with one side cuneate to rounded and the other rounded to truncate or nearly subcordate, at apex acute to short-caudate, pliable but relatively incras- sate, on upper surface dark green, lustrous and glabrous to moderately pubescent with scattered rufous-brown stellate or stellate-peltate trichomes, especially on the veins, on lower surface medium green, sublustrous and moderately to densely pubescent with similar trichomes, not barbate, without spicy odor when fresh, developing a mild spicy odor in some dried specimens; secondary veins very prominent below, pinnate, 6-9 per side (not including the 1 or 2 additional weak basal veins per side, the base thus inconspicuously 3- or 5-palmate), ascending at a relatively high angle, eucamptodromous towards base of blade, becoming brochidodromous near middle, usually conspicuously yellowish-green when fresh or dried. Flowers actinomorphic, usually solitary and opposite the leaves, borne on short lateral shoots arising from the plagiotropic branches (Fig. 4B, C); pedicels 6-11 mm long; the basal 1/4?1/3 bearing 3 bracteoles, densely lepidote; bracteoles unequal in size, triangular to broadly triangular, ascending, 1.5-3 mm long, 1-2 mm broad at base, usually persisting in fruit, lepidote; calyx narrowly conical, 9- 13 mm long, ca 8 mm diam and 3-5-lobed at summit, green when fresh, matte greenish-brown when dried, densely granuliferous-lepidote with tiny, brown, pel- tate trichomes without, densely sericeous with long, pale, ascending trichomes within, the apical lobes triangular or irregular, 1-3 mm long, often reflexed; petals spathulate, 15-25 mm long, 5-7 mm wide when dried, at apex acute or rounded, strongly reflexed at anthesis, white when fresh, drying to pale brown apically and medium to dark rufous-brown towards the base, densely tomentose with pale, lax, stellate trichomes on both sides except for the glabrous base; staminal column cylindrical, 18-24 mm long (including the 5 short lobes at summit), 1-2 mm diam when dried, dilated from the base to the apex, white to cream when fresh, when dried with color similar to the bases of the dried petals, glabrous at base, becoming moderately tomentose with pale stellate hairs towards apex, puberulent between the thecae, the apical lobes truncate and emarginate to bilobed, 0.5-2.5 mm long, with a glandular appearance, medium brown; thecae 30, elliptic to reniform, 1.5- 3 mm long, 0.8-1.3 mm wide, distinctly paired when dried, arrayed in three pairs per staminal lobe, nearly sessile; ovary broadly ovoid to subpyriform, 1-1.3 mm high, ca 1.5 mm diam, usually bilocular, occasionally trilocular, each locule con- taining 2 ovules, each ovule ca 0.4 mm diam; style filiform, 20-26 mm long, 1- 2 mm diam, at base terete and glabrous or tomentulose, dilating upwards to the angular, densely tomentose apex; stigma capitate to bilobed, 1.5-3 mm diam. Fruits ellipsoid to ovoid, 24-27 mm long, 15-19 mm diam, at apex blunt and briefly convex when fresh, sometimes becoming submammilate when dried, ul- timately apiculate with the persistent style base; exocarp leathery, sublustrous, finely longitudinally striate, the apical 1/4 medium green and the basal 3/4 pale green to greenish-yellow when ripe and fresh, drying to olive-green, glabrous except for the densely tomentose-lepidote apex; mesocarp indistinct, together with the exocarp ca 3 mm thick, moist and fibrous, without distinct taste; endocarp ca 1 mm thick, bony-fibrous, persistent around the seeds; pedicels 7-13 mm long, much thicker than when in flower, bearing 1-3 persistent bracteoles; calyx of fruit urceolate to elongate-cupulate, 15-25 mm long, ca 16 mm diam and irregularly toothed or erose at apex, accrescent, covering ca 1/2 of fruit when ripe, green or greenish-brown when fresh, brown when dried, with vestiture as in flowering condition; seeds 1-2, occasionally 3, usually planoconvex, ca 13 mm long, 4-7 mm wide, 3-4 mm thick, consisting mainly of pale tissue of the 2 cotyledons; testa thin, dark rufous-brown. Seedlings hypogeal, cryptocotylar, bearing 5-10 dormant, stipulate nodes below the first true leaves, these more tender and thinner than adult leaves but otherwise similar.
bibliographicCitation: Alverson, Andrew H. 1989. Quararibea (Bombacaceae): five new species from moist and wet forests of Costa Rica and Panama. Brittonia. 41(1): 61-74.

description: Tree 5-8 m tall, to 15 cm dbh, without buttresses; trunk orthotropic (sensu Halle et al., 1978) and usually monopodial, sometimes multiple; branches ver- ticillate, horizontal (plagiotropic) and drooping towards tips; youngest branches very densely tomentose with pale brown echinate-stellate trichomes, glabrate, medium brown to reddish brown, and rugulose with age; outer bark thin (0.5 mm or less), reddish-brown, minutely roughened, not peeling in large strips or plates; inner bark thicker (ca 3 mm), pale, fibrous; wood pale, relatively hard. Stipules narrowly triangular, 5-13 mm long, 1-2 mm broad at base, deciduous, densely tomentose with echinate-stellate trichomes; leaves alternate, entire, simple (uni- foliolate?); petioles terete, 6-11 (14) mm long, bipulvinate but the pulvini inconspicuous, densely hirsute with pale stellate trichomes; leaf blades quite variable in shape, narrowly to broadly elliptic or ovate, (7) 10-23 (29) cm long, 4-10 (13) cm wide, at base either nearly symmetric and cuneate or rounded, or conspicuously asymmetric with one side cuneate and the other subcordate or truncate, at apex acuminate to caudate, slightly stiff and somewhat bullate when fresh, lustrous medium-dark green and moderately to sparsely hirsute with stellate or simple trichomes above, dull green and hirsute with echinate-stellate trichomes below, conspicuously barbate (i.e., with domatia in the abaxial vein axils); veins protrude slightly but conspicuously below; secondary veins pinnate, 6-8 per side (not including the pair of obsolete basal veins on each side), ascending at an acute angle, arched, brochidodromous. Flowers usually produced opposite the leaves near the branch tips; pedicels 20-28 mm long at flowering, usually curved, bearing 2 or 3 narrowly triangular bracteoles towards base; bracteoles 7-11 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide at base, usually persistent in fruit, densely tomentose; calyx narrowly conical, 22-29 mm long, ca 8 mm diam and irregularly cleft at summit, green and densely tomentose without, densely sericeous with pale, ascending trichomes within; petals 5, ligulate, 35-45 mm long and 4-8 mm wide when fresh, reflexed (but not coiled as in Q. parvifolia), pale greenish-white, tomentose with pale simple hairs without,  glabrous within; staminal column straight or gently curved, 67-72 mm long (in- cluding the apical teeth), extending 35-40 mm beyond corolla, antheriferous in ultimate 10-11 mm, minutely puberulous on distal third and glabrous proximally, at apex pentafid, bearing shallowly deltoid teeth ca 1.2 mm long; thecae ca 30, 1.5-3 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, sessile or nearly so; pollen triporate, isopolar, spherical, 45-70 Am diam, with reticulate muri and angular or rounded lumina, of the "asterolepis-type" (sensu Nilsson & Robyns, 1974); style filiform, extending 3-4 mm beyond staminal tube, 1.5-2 mm diam, tomentose with appressed stellate trichomes near apex; stigma 2-4 mm diam, capitate, sometimes slightly lobed. Fruits drupaceous, ellipsoid, 30-40 mm long, ca 19 mm diam, usually 2-seeded, sometimes 1-seeded by abortion, enclosed for 1/3-l/2 of length by persistent and irregularly toothed or erose calyx, bluntly mammilate, at apex minutely but distinctly 5-lobed, sometimes retaining 1 mm of the style base; exocarp coriaceous, green; mesocarp very fibrous, watery, pale brown, without discernible taste or odor; endocarp thin, fibrous; pedicels of fruit 25-55 mm long, usually retaining 2 or 3 bracteoles; seeds ca 19 mm long, 8 mm diam, planoconvex, the bulk of the tissue composed of a pair of pale, fleshy cotyledons; testa thin, brown. Seedlings unknown but undoubtedly hypogeal and cryptocotylar (sensu Ng, 1978), as are all known seedlings of Quararibea s. str.

description: Arbor 10-20 m alta. Folia altema; petioli 7-23 mm longi; laminae ellipticae vel obovatae, integrae, 10-25 cm longae, 4-10 cm latae. Flores penduli; pedicelli gracillimi, 55-193 mm longi. Calyx conicus, 14-25 mm longus. Petala 5, alba, ligulata, unguiculata, in ore corollae transverse plicata, ultra patentia et reflexa, 35 mm longa, 6 mm lata. Columna staminalis 32-67 mm longa, stylo paulo brevior. Ovarium 2-loculare. Fructus drupaceus, viridis, 20-25 mm longus, 15 mm diametro, 1- vel 2-spermus.

description: Tree to 20 m tall and 25 cm dbh; trunk orthotropic, slightly fluted but without buttresses; branches verticillate, more or less horizontal (plagiotropic); youngest branches pale brown, sparsely to densely lepidote-tomentose with echinate and peltate-stellate trichomes, becoming glabrate, darker brown and rugulose with age; outer bark thin (0.1 mm), medium rufous-brown, fairly smooth, not exfoliating in plates or strips; inner bark ca 1 mm thick, fibrous, pale brown, with conspicuous phloem rays; wood pale brown, without taste but with faint odor like fresh squash. Stipules narrowly triangular, 5-10 mm long, ca 1.5 mm broad at base, deciduous, densely lepidote-tomentose with peltate-stellate trichomes; leaves alternate, entire, simple (unifoliolate?); petioles terete, 7-23 mm long, the distal half conspicuously pulvinate, densely tomentulose-peltate with stellate, peltate-stellate and/or echi- nate trichomes; leaf blades elliptic to obovate, often slightly asymmetric, 10-25 cm long, 4-10 cm wide, at base, if nearly symmetrical, cuneate and often slightly attenuate, if conspicuously asymmetric, then one side cuneate or rounded and the other caudate, rounded, or subcordate, at apex acuminate, thickened-papy- riferous and slightly rubbery in texture, lustrous dark green above and below, nearly glabrous, nonbarbate to slightly barbate below; veins of leaf only slightly prominent below; secondary veins pinnate, 6-8 per side (not including the 1 or 2 obsolete basal veins per side), ascending at an acute angle, arched, brochidod- romous. Flowers very long-pendulous, more or less actinomorphic (the staminal column sometimes curved), borne opposite the leaves near the branch tips or on young spur shoots from small branches; pedicels 55-193 mm long at flowering, very flexible, bearing 2 or 3 narrowly triangular bracteoles on proximal half; bracteoles 3-6 mm long, 1 mm wide at base and densely lepidote-tomentulose; calyx conical, 14-25 mm long, 8-20 mm diam at summit, with irregularly lobed or erose margin, medium green proximally, the distal 5 mm a conspicuously paler green or pale brown, the outer surface completely lepidote-tomentulose with pale brown peltate-stellate trichomes and more densely lepidote-tomentulose towards summit with smaller, whitish, peltate-stellate trichomes, the inner surface densely sericeous with pale, ascending trichomes; petals 5, ligulate, ca 35 mm long, 6 mm wide, clawed for ca 8 mm at base, transversely plicate in mouth of corolla, the distal portions spreading and reflexing, white, tomentose with long, transparent trichomes without, glabrous within; staminal column usually straight, sometimes curved, 32-67 mm long, exserted for 15-35 mm beyond mouth of corolla, an- theriferous in ultimate 10 mm, sparsely to densely tomentose with pale stellate trichomes, at apex pentafid, the deltoid teeth 0.8-1.1 mm long (including an occasional 0.2 mm mucro); thecae 30, in 2 whorls of 15, not paired, 2 mm long, 1 mm wide, sessile or subsessile; ovary turbinate, 2-locular, 3.5 mm long, 2 mm diam, tomentose with stellate trichomes; style extending 2-3 mm beyond staminal tube, puberulous or glabrous and ca 0.3 mm diam near base, tomentose and ca 1 mm diam near apex; stigma capitate, 2-3 mm diam. Fruits ovoid to ellipsoid, 20-25 mm long, ca 15 mm diam, 1- or 2-seeded, at apex usually bluntly mammilate, enclosed for 1/2-2/3 of length by the persistent calyx; exocarp medium to dark green; mesocarp fibrous, without discernible taste or odor; endocarp densely fibrous; pedicels and calyx of fruit with same size and characteristics as when in flowering condition, the apex of calyx becoming pale brown or dull yellow; seeds ca 15 mm long, 6-10 mm diam, planoconvex (if paired in fruit) or biconvex (If solitary) the bulk of the seed composed of the pale, fleshy cotyledons; testa thin, brown. Seedlings hypogeal, cryptocotylar, producing 5 or 6 leafless, stipulate nodes below the first true leaves.

description: Frutex palmoideus, monopodialis haud vel sparsim ramosus usque ad 5 m, cauliflorus; foliis anguste oblanceolatis vel obovatis, acuminatis, ad basim auriculatis, 29-42 cm longis, 11-18 cm latis, gla- briusculis, rigidulo-chartaceis; petiolis brevibus, 5-7 mm longis. Flores pedunculis 2-3 mm longis gesti; calycibus 10-12 mm longis, 6 mm diam; petalis albis, obovatis vel spathulatis, 18-22 mm longis, 4-6 mm latis, contortis, reflexis; columna staminali 15-19 mm longa; stylo ca 2 mm ultra columnam exserto; ovario plerumque biloculari, utroque loculo biovulato. Fructus elliptici vel pyri- formes, 22-27 mm longi, 10-13 mm diam.
bibliographicCitation: Alverson, William S. 1984. Quararibea pumila (Bombacaceae) a new endemic from Costa Rica. Brittonia. 36: 252-256.

description: Erect, monoaxial or sparsely-branched monopodial, cauliflorous shrub with large leaves clustered at shoot tips in palmoid fashion, the axial buds sometimes developing into strongly ascending branches equal in size to main axis, but plant with a tendency towards a monopodial growth form dominated by the orthotropic main axis. Stems 2-5 m long, 5-10 cm diam at base, with age becoming reddish brown, sublustrous, rugose and peeling, longitudinally furrowed, with small (0.5 mm), pale, raised lenticels; lateral branches to 3 m long, 2-5 cm diam; wood pale cream and slightly brittle, without conspicuous flavor but with a faint, sweet odor; young branches pale green or pale brown with tan, sessile, stellate trichomes. Stipules soon caducous, linear acuminate, 9-15 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide at base, bright green when young, duller with age, with an irregular indumentum of tan, sessile, stellate trichomes, grooved at base on upper surface and leaving a crescent- shaped scar. Leaf scars blunt-cordate or obovate, 5-6 mm diam, the vascular traces recessed with numerous free central traces and a broadly U-shaped lower trace. Leaves alternate, short-petiolate. Leaf blades oblanceolate to obovate, (23) 29-42 (51) cm long, (8) 11-18 (19) cm wide, the base auriculate with lobes 6-8 mm wide, the apex broadly acuminate to slightly obtuse, sometimes apiculate, the leaf margins entire but sinuate with the basal 1/3 of blade forming a broad V-shaped trough, the distal 2/3 convex with arching, descending sides; firm-char- taceous, lustrous and dark green above, nearly glabrous but with pale, scattered, sessile, stellate trichomes on the veins; undersides pale green, sublustrous, glabrous except for an indumentum of pale tan stellate trichomes on veins; veins recessed from upper surface of blade, the blade raised and subbullate between veins, usually with 8-10 arching-ascending major secondary veins per side, plus 3-5 obsolete secondaries per side at base, smaller secondaries branch off from midvein at right angles between major secondary veins, as do tertiaries off the major secondary veins, the venation pinnate, the major secondary veins eucamptodromous proximally, becoming brochidodromous in the distal half of the blade, the midrib, when fresh, protruding ca 3 mm near base on abaxial side, secondary veins protruding ca 1 mm, tertiary and quaternary veins conspicuously protruding as well, forming a dense reticulum. Petioles green, 5-7 mm long, thick (ca 6 mm diam when fresh), with a few simple white hairs and a dense indumentum of brown stellate trichomes. Axial buds on the upper parts of stem developing, after leaf drops, into very compressed short shoots 1-10 mm long, from which numerous flower buds are produced. Flowers actinomorphic, produced singly or few at a time from these short shoots, the 2-3 mm long peduncles confluent with the calyx; bracteoles 3-4 on the calyx and peduncle, these subulate, 3 mm long, 1 mm at base. Calyx ovoid to ellipsoid, 10-12 mm long, 5-6 mm diam, with 3-5 broadly triangular teeth or with an erose summit, pale green and with dense, brown, tufted, stellate hairs outside and pale, ascending, sericeous hairs inside. Petals white, contorted, the lobes strongly reflexed at anthesis, oblanceolate to spatulate, slightly to moderately clawed at base, 18-20 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, abaxially with pale, stellate hairs, adaxially with very finely furrowed texture (when dried), but otherwise glabrous. Stamens monadelphous, the androecial column 15-19 mm long from its base to its antheriferous summit, ca 2 mm diam below, expanding to 4-5 mm diam above, sparsely covered with fine, pale, stellate trichomes; anthers sessile, the 15 pairs of thecae arrayed along margins of the 5- lobed summit of the androecium, extrorse by longitudinal slits. Pollen triporate, isopolar, spherical, 60-80 µm diam, with relatively smooth, reticulate muri and circular or rounded lumina, 2.5-7.5 µm diam; pori slightly elliptic, averaging 32 x 22 µm. Style exceeding androecium by 1-2 mm, extending straight beyond or curved sidewards or downwards, densely pubescent with simple and tufted white hairs; stigma capitate, 1 mm diam, sometimes slightly bilobed, minutely roughened. Ovary bilocular, sometimes trilocular, with 2 ovules per locule, the placentation axile with interlocular lacunae. Fruits drupaceous, with 1 or 2 seeds, enclosed for about 1/3 of length by the persistent, thick, accrescent calyx; pericarp fleshy but firm with an inner layer of tough fibers, pale green or pale lemon-green, with no conspicuous odor or flavor; fruits elliptic to pyriform, sometimes mammilate for 3-4 mm, or apiculate with the persistent style base, sometimes asymmetric, 22-27 mm long, 10-13 mm diam; fruiting peduncle 2-4 mm long. Seeds ellipsoid or ovoid to slightly reniform, 16-23 mm long, 8-10 mm diam, with thin brown testa. Embryo straight or slightly curved, with the cotyledons composing the bulk of the seed; cotyledonal tissue riddled with canals carrying clear mucilage. Seedlings cryptocotylar, hypogeal (sensu Ng, 1978); the germinating shoot with ca 6 nodes with paired stipules and dormant leaf buds below the first nodes with true leaves, the latter similar to adult leaves in shape, but proportionately wider.
bibliographicCitation: Alverson, William S. 1984. Quararibea pumila (Bombacaceae) a new endemic from Costa Rica. Brittonia. 36: 252-256.

description: Tree, 12 m tall, 15 cm dbh; trunk orthotropic, monopodial, smooth and without buttresses; branches 4-5-verticillate, horizontal (plagiotropic), drooping slightly at tips; young branches extremely densely tomentose with brown echinate-stellate trichomes, glabrate, medium brown and rugulose with age; outer bark thin, not exfoliating in plates or strips, matte brown, finely textured; inner bark at least 2 mm thick, pale and fibrous; wood cream. Stipules narrowly triangular, 3-4 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide at base, deciduous, densely tomentulose with flattened echinate trichomes; leaves alternate, entire, simple (unifoliolate?.); petioles terete, only 4-7 mm long, tomentose; pulvini inconspicuous; leaf blades usually elliptic, occasionally obovate, 6-14 cm long, 3-6 cm wide, at base rounded or truncate and often slightly asymmetric, minutely subcordate at the point of attachment to the petiole, at apex acute to acuminate, at very tip broadly rounded and usually minutely mucronate, slightly rigid and coriaceous, lustrous and very dark green above, sublustrous and medium green below, nearly glabrous but with widely scattered and conspicuous (when fresh), brown, stellate trichomes above, subto- mentose with scattered stellate trichomes and barbate in the axils of the secondary veins below; veins distinctly protruding below; secondary veins pinnate, 5-7 per side (not including the pair of small, obsolete basal veins), widely acute at point of divergence from midrib, arched, entirely and distinctly brochidodromous. Flowers actinomorphic, produced opposite young leaves near the branch tips and held on the horizontal plane formed by the foliage; pedicels 12-14 mm long at flowering, bearing 2 or 3 triangular bracteoles, these 1-1.5 mm long and ca 0.5 mm wide at base, both bracteoles and pedicel very densely tomentulose with many flattened, pale yellow, echinate trichomes and few pale, stellate trichomes; calyx funnel-shaped, 7 mm long, 6 mm diam and irregularly cleft at summit, rugulose when fresh, conspicuously rugose when dried, green, densely tomentulose with echinate and stellate trichomes without, densely sericeous with pale, as- cending trichomes within; petals 5, spathulate, 15-16 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, spreading or reflexed, white, tomentose with soft, colorless, simple and stellate trichomes without, tomentulose with a longitudinal median strip of such trichomes within; staminal column gently curved, 15 mm long, exserted beyond the petals for half of its length, longitudinally striate when dried, at least the distal half tomentose; thecae ca 25 in number, 1 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, sessile, borne on distal 3 mm of staminal column; pollen triporate, isopolar, spherical, 45-5 5 gm diam, of the "asterolepis-type" (sensu Nilsson & Robyns, 1974); style and stigma not available for examination. Fruits broadly ellipsoid, 10 mm long and 12 mm diam when immature, 1- or 2-seeded, slightly apiculate with the persistent style base; exocarp green, densely covered with pale echinate hairs that impart a frosty appearance; pedicel of fruit 12-14 mm long, sometimes bearing persistent bracteoles; calyx of fruit ca 10 mm long, irregularly cleft at apex, rugose, green, less densely pubescent than when in flowering condition; mature seeds and seedlings unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Alverson, Andrew H. 1989. Quararibea (Bombacaceae): five new species from moist and wet forests of Costa Rica and Panama. Brittonia. 41(1): 61-74.

description: Leaflets elliptical to obovate, usually tapering gradually to the base and abruptly acuminate at the apex, mostly 6-17 cm. long and 2-6 cm. wide, glabrous; wing of rachis segmented at the points of attachment of the leaflets, each segment gradually widening upwards and abruptly contracted at the top; sepals about 2 mm. long, triangular-ovate, rounded at the summit, glabrous except for the sometimes finely ciliolate margins; petals red or pink, mostly 3-5 cm. long; filaments evidently longer or a little shorter than the petals; fruit 1-1.5 cm. long, ovoid or ellipsoid, often with a peculiar constriction near the base.

description: Arbor 8 m altus, 5 cm diametro, ramulis novellis brunneo-strigulosis, glabrescentibus, internodiis compressis. Stipulae deciduae, subulatae, 4 mm longae, brunneo-strigulosae. Folia opposita, in sicco viridia infra, supra subplumbea; petiolus 9-12 mm longus, minute puberulus; lamina 13-28 cm longa, 4-9 cm lata, elliptica, ad basim decurrens, ad apicem acuminata, ad marginem undulata, tenuicoriacea, supra glabris puberulis costis exceptis, infra sparsissime puberulis; costa venisque infra et supra salientibus, venis 19-27-jugatis. Inflorescentiae axillares, congestae, fasciculatae, 1-1.5 cm longae, axe minute puberulo, 7-10 mm longo. Flores masculini solum visi, pedicellis 2.5-3 mm longis, glabris; 5 sepala ca. 1 mm longa, oblongo-ovalia, ciliolata, petalis glabris, 5, ca. 1.5 mm longis, ovalis, concavis. Stamina ca. 25, filamenta 0.6 mm longa, glabra, antheris ovalis.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1957. New species and new records of plants in Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 231-245.

description: Stem hypogeous, branching dichotomously with age, 15-27 cm long, 8-13 cm in diam. Cataphylls coriaceous, persistent, base triangular, apex aristate, 4.5x3.4 cm at base, brown tomentose. Ptyxis inflexed. Leaves 2- 3, ascending to descending 41-95x29-36 cm wide, brownish when emerging; petiole 10.2- 32 cm long, green in young leaves, subterete, armed with prickles up to 4 mm long; rachis subterete, up to 56 cm long, with few prickles along the proximal third. Leaflets 5-28 pairs sessile, coriaceous, lanceolate, opposite to subopposite, apex acute, base attenuate, mar- gins serrulate to slightly dentate along distal third, subrevolute; articulations brownish in young leaflets, 0.4-0.6 cm wide; the median leaflets 14-19x2.3-3.4 cm. Pollen strobili usually 1-2, erect, cylindrical, 6.3-11 cm long, 2.1-2.6 cm in diam, light brown tomentulose, apex acute; peduncle light- brown tomentose, 6.3 cm long, 1.2 cm in diam; pollen sporangiophores cuneiform, dis- tal face hexagonal-truncate, 0.3 cm long, fertile abaxial surface with 6-8 bisporangiate synangia per lobe. Ovulate strobili usually solitary, erect, ellipsoid to cylindrical, 8.1 cm long, 5.2 cm in diam, brown-yellowish, tomentulose, apex apiculate; peduncle densely brown tomentose, 3.9 cm long, 1.3 cm in diam; megasporangiophores peltate, distal face hexagonal - truncate, 0.6 - 0.8 cm high, 1.1 -1.5 cm wide. Seeds ovoid, sarcotesta pink when immature, orange at maturity, 2 - 2.8 cm long, 1.5- 1.7 cm in diam, sclerotesta smooth. Chromosome number. - 2n=23, 34, 25, 26, 27, 28 (Moretti & Sabato, 1984).

description: Macroscopic: petioles 3-8 mm. long; blades lanceolate to elliptic, 4-10 cm. long, 2-5 cm. broad, subacute to tapering at base, acute to acuminate and finely pointed at apex, shining on both surfaces, sometimes rather dull, chartaceous to subeoriaceous, 3-plinerved with the inner pair mostly subop- posite or opposite and diverging at 0-6 mm. from base, reticulation faint to rather prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets strigose with fulvous hairs of different lengths; petioles densely pubescent with ratber stiff, fulvous or grey hairs of different lengths adpressed or somewhat spread- ing, becoming subglabrous in age; blades beneath tuberculate when young, becoming smooth in age, densely fulvous-hirtellous with more or less curved hairs throughout to sparsely strigose on principal nerves, the pubescence generally more dense in axils of the inner principal nerves, thus occasionally giving a barbate appearance, above tuberculate as beneath but more mark- edly so, at maturity strigose or with erect hairs on midrib and sparsely hairy near margins or glabrous, leaf-margins subeiliate near base. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, corymbose anld rather densely flowered, densely fulvous-strigose, pedicels up to 2.5 mm. long; calyx-lobes linear- lanceolate, up to 3 mm. long, acuminate at apex, densely fulvous-strigose without; corolla-tube up to 1.5 cm. long, papillose and pubescent without with ascending or spreading, rusty, subsetulose hairs, pilose only near mid- dle within, corolla-lobes pubescent without as corolla-tube, bearded with soft pili near base within, otherwise glabrous (tufts of elongated papillae present at apex) ; anthers on short but distinct filaments, somewhat exserted; style glabrous. [Fruits, etc. Prog. (26, p. 272) ] Fruits globose, about 4 cm. in diam., seeds many orbicular, flattened. According to Ducke (Arch. Jard. Bot. Rio 6: 81. 1933) fruits resemble those of S. Erichsonii.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Perennis, rhizomate horizontali. Folia emersa, sagittata; laminae late ovato- triangulares, 21-25 cm longae (ab apice petioli ad apicem), 23-30 cm latae, lobis + triangularibus, ad basim ca. 15 cm longis X 10 cm latis, petiolo + 60-75 cm longo. Scapi ad nodos insigniter constricti, 30-85 cm longi, simplices vel ad verticillum imum breviter ramosi, cum 7-9 verticillis muniti. Bracteae versus basim connatae, mem- branaceae, ad 1 cm longae. Flores feminei in verticillis inferioribus positi, pedicellis brevibus, incrassatis, 2-3 cm longis, sepalis 6-12 mm longis, 0.7-1.2 cm latis, appressis, receptaculum immaturum obtegentibus; petalis oblongis, albis. Flores masculini in verticillis superioribus positi, quam flores feminei breviores, pedicellis ad 2 mm longis, staminibus 9-12, filamentis glabris, + 1 mm longis linearibus, antheris ovatis, 1.5 mm longis. Achaenia haud visa.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1971. New species of phanerogams from Amazonia. Brittonia. 23: 438-445.

description: S. graminea Michx. affinis sed rhizomatibus longioribus, usque 1 dm longis, foliis rhizomatum secundis, falcatis, verticillis (1) 2-4 (5), infimis 1-2 [female], staminibus 9-12, filamentis tumide conicis, 1.0-1.3 mm longis, albotomentulosis, acheniis ca 2 mm longis, asymmetrice obovato triangulatis, de latere compressis, margine ventrali recta, dorsali anguste rotundata, 3-cristata, cristis irregulariter undulatis v. dentatis, spongiosis sed tenuibus, pericarpio interdum tuberculis obsito et secus marginem ventralem ala humili aut serie tuberculorum limbato; rostro laterali, calcariformi, incurvato erecto, ca 0.3 mm longo, canalibus resiniferis numerosis 1-2 inter alas dorsales et per facies conspersis.

description: Submersed aquatic perennial with fibrous roots. Rhizome rigid, often elongated, ca 4-5 mm thick, often to 1 dm long, especially in sterile examples or in swift shallows. Phyllodia of two types, those of swift shallows secund along the rhizome, with blades linear, erect to ascending, falciform, (2) 5-8 (10) cm long, 2-5 mm wide, deep green, the apices acute but at the extreme tip narrowly truncate, with a concave callused area; the ventral margin joined in the blade, thus thickest; phyllodia in quiet or less rapid waters linear-subulate, erect to widely ascending (5) 10-30 cm long, medially terete, distally triangular or angulate or lingulate, apically as in all the other specimens; sheaths broad, pale, variously imbricated. Scapes erect, 1-4 (5) dm tall, terete but multicostate, flowering only toward the apex. Verticels (1) 2-4 (5), the lower 1-2 female. Bracts 3, basally connate, ca 4 mm long, the lobes ca 3 mm long, triangular, acuminate, smooth, indistinctly nerved. Pedicels 3 per node, slender but rigid, widely ascending, accrescent, (1.0) 1.5-2.5 (3.0) cm long. Sepals scarious, smooth, triangular-ovate, apically narrowly obtuse, 4-5 mm long, after anthesis reflexed or spreading, finely multinerved, yellowish-green. Petals reduced or none in the female flowers; petals of male flowers 3, white, 1.0-1.5 cm long. Stamens 9-12, filaments tumidly conic, 1.0-1.3 mm long, basally green, white-tomentulose, apically short-subulate; anthers oblong, yellowish, about equal to filaments. Fruiting pedicels erect or spreading. Akenes ca 2 mm long, asymmetrically obovate-triangular, laterally compressed, the ventral edge straight, the dorsal edge narrowly rounded, curvate, triple-crested with the crests irregularly undulate or coarsely toothed, spongy but thin; faces of fruit shallowly convex, the pericarp sometimes drawn up into flattened tubercles, and ventrally bordered by another, lower wing or line of flattened or domeshaped processes; beak lateral, spurlike, incurved-erect, ca 0.3 mm long; resin canals numerous, evident, one or two between the dorsal wings and also over the lateral faces.
bibliographicCitation: Churchill, Steven & Buck, William R. 1982. A taxonomic investigation of Leptotheca (Rhizogoniaceae). Brittonia. 34: 1-11.

description: Peduncles, pedicels (these more often 3-5 mm. long), and their subtending bracts all glabrous. Sepals from narrowly oblong or lanceolate to ovate, at apex mostly acute, externally glabrous or nearly so, under 2.5 mm. long.

description: Principal leaves larger, 5-10 cm. long and commonly 1-2 mm. wide, more or less flat (except for the extreme margins) or irregularly conduplicate. Inflores- cence larger, more decompound; peduncles, pedicels, and bracts glabrous. Sepals ovate or lanceolate or at times oblong, apically more or less acute, glabrous or on outer surface and edges very minutely puberulous, finally about 3 mm. long.

description: Woody vine, usually armed. Branches terete. Petiole 2-3 cm long, terete, the sheath 1-3 cm long, the wings ca. 1.5 mm wide; leaf blade coriaceous, narrowly to broadly ovate, 14-22 x 5.2-1 1 cm; apex acute or acuminate; base rounded or obtuse; principle veins 3-5, usually impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially, the tertiary and higher-order venation admedially ramified, prominulous ad  and abaxially. Inflorescence an axillary umbel, the peduncles 4-8 cm long, the pedicels 10-11 mm long. Staminate flowers: tepals narrowly elliptic, 5.2 x 1.2 mm; stamens 6, the filaments thick, 3 mm long, the anthers 1.4 mm long; pis- tillode lacking. Pistillate flowers not seen. Berries globose, 1-1.4 cm diam., orange when ripe.

description: A tall pandanloid tree 6-9 m high, branching above; wood dull white, the bark yellowish, smooth but for a few blunt protuberances; branches obscurely ringed with leaf-scars; leaves 150-250 cm long, 6-8 cm wide, glabrous, coriaceous, the margins antrorsely toothed (but the basomarginal teeth becoming crowded, learly perpendicular, triangular), midrib below antrorsely toothed; infloreseence a terminal compound panicle, recurved and pendent; peduncle 60-90 cm lolig, 2.5-5 cm in diameter; panicle 90-160 (or more?) cm long, 30 cm wide, the secondary branches 15-30 cm long, descending, copiously re- branched, all the stalks yellowish green and densely stellate-pubescent; branch- lets of the inflorescence bracteate, the bracts slender, acuminate, often forked, chartaceous, apparently searious; female flowers globose, 3 mm in diameter, subtended by a sparsely fimbriate cupule; male flowers of 12-20 stamens, subtended by a cupule, below this a minute searious bract; filaments clavate, 3.5 mm long; anther 1.3-1.9 mm long; fruit a polypyrenoid drupe, ripening to candy red, the cupule remaining green; drupes 6-8 mm broad, 5 mm long, subtriangular in profile, colisisting of 12-20 pyrenles; stigmas small, sessile, in two parallel rows along the median portion of the fruit; pryenes 3 mm long; 2 mm wide, thin and broadly ovate-reniform, rounded at both ends.
bibliographicCitation: Stone, Benjamin C. M. 1961. The genus Sararanga (Pandanaceae). Brittonia. 13: 212-224.

description: A tree, branching finally and becoming 20 m high; leaves up to 4.5 m long and 11-12 cm wide, broadly encircling the trunk at the base, gradually and evenly tapered to a long narrow tip, thick-coriaceous and rigid, indurate near the base, armed with strong teeth on the margins and the lower dorsal part of the midrib, often the middle portion unarmed; leaves of young plants (other conditions being equal) longer than those of older plants, and the degree of leaf-arming variable; infloreseence a terminal pendent panicle, the main pedicels flat- tened at the insertion on the central peduncle, subopposite, successive pairs 1800 apart, the last pair somewhat shorter than the termination of the infloreseence, which rebranches into smaller panicles; tertiary branches subopposite or irregularly spaced, bearing 3-16 (or more) flowers; fruits (at submaturity) orange, turning from greenish-white; pyrenes 30-80 per fruit; drupes when mature or nearly so usually 13-18 mm in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Stone, Benjamin C. M. 1961. The genus Sararanga (Pandanaceae). Brittonia. 13: 212-224.

description: Liana gracilis 0.6-3 m longa. Caulis gracilis, rigidus, pallide viridis, supra medium sparse ramosus, internodiis (1.5-) 4-15 cm longis 1-2 mm crassis. Folia remotiuscule alternata; laminae lanceolatae vel ovato-lanceolatae, interdum subdeltoideo-lanceo- latae, 3-15 cm longae, 1-5 cm latae, herbaceae aliquando tenuiter coriaceae, supra laete virides, subtus pallide virides sed non glaucae, basi rotundo-contractae vel sub- cordatae, ad apicem acutum sensim attenuantes; costae 7 cum duabus marginalibus crassiusculis, omnes e basi laminae divergentes, eminentes, elevatae, nervulis lateralibus oblique divergentibus, reticulum densum haud elongatum formantibus; petioli 10-25 mm longi, apice articulati, trigoni, basi alis perangustis (0.3-0.6 mm latis) margine vix membranaceis breviter (3-5 mm) vaginantes. Umbellae solitariae, ex axillis duabus basilaribus ramorum enatae; pedunculi basi sine prophyllo, 2-5 cm longi, graciles, vix compressi; receptaculi 1-1.5 mm crassi, bracteis lanceolatis vix 1 mm longis; umbellae masculae 8-22-florae, eae foemineae 6-18-florae; radii 8-15 mm longi, filiformes. Flores masculi olivaceo-virides (ex Forrest) vel pallide rubentes (ex Kingdon-Ward); tepala divergentia, externa oblanceolata, 2.8-3 mm longa, 1-1.2 mm lata, ad apicem breviter acuminatum subito contracta, interiora externis similia sed paullo angustiora tantum 0.8 mm lata; stamina 6, filamentis 0.6-0.7 mm longis, antheris globosis albis 0.5 mm longis. Flores foeminei pallide purpurei (ex Yu); tepala divergentia, ovato-oblonga, apice subacuta, externa 2.5 mm longa et 1 mm lata, interiora 2 mm longa et 0.8 mm lata; ovarium globosum, 1.25 mm longum ac latum, stigmatibus 3, leviter recurvis ca. 0.8 mm longis; staminodia 0-3, linearia, 0.4-0.6 mm longa. Baccae 5-7 mm in diametro, maturitate purpureo-rubentes; semina 1 vel 2, obovato-orbicularia.
bibliographicCitation: Koyama, Tetsuo M. 1974. Four new species of Smilax (Smilacaceae) from southeastern Asia. Brittonia. 26: 133-138.

description: Rhizoma repens, ad nodos crassiusculos radices fibrosas emittens. Caules humiles, simplices, e basi decumbente erecti vel oblique ascendentes, 10-22 cm alti, deorsum subteretes, sursum subtrigoni, laevissimi, internodiis 1-4 cm longis et 1-2 mm crassis. Folia ad apicem caulis aggregata; laminae ellipticae vel interdum ovato-ellipticae, 4-7 cm longae, 2.5-3.5 cm latae, basi subito contractae subacutae, versus apicem breviter caudatum subsensim attenuantes, tenuiter coriaceae, opacae, subtus palli- diores; costae 5 cum duabus marginalibus gracillimis, omnes ad basin separatae, 3 centrales eminentes, subtus ad modum elevatae, nervulis lateralibus gracilibus diver- gentibus reticulum sublaxum non elongatum nec eminens formantibus; petioli breves, patentes, 4-6 mm longi, trigoni, dorso subobtusi, antice canaliculati, basi vix vaginantes; cirrhi desunt. Inflorescentiae foemineae 1-umbellatae, ex axilla folii prophyllata ortae; axis tantum 5 mm longus, apice bibracteatus, bracteis lanceolatis 1-1.5 mm longis, inferiore vacua; prophyllum late ovatum, ca. 2 mm longum, mem- branaceum; pedunculus filiformis, 7-10 mm longus. Umbella foeminea 3-5-flora, receptaculo 0.5 mm crasso; radii 2-4 mm longi, basi bracteolis 0.2 mm longis del- toideis ornati. Perianthia foeminea sub anthesi patentia; tepala externa ovata vel ovato-elliptica, 1.25 mm longa, 0.5-0.7 mm lata, apice acuta, interiora lanceolata, 0.8 mm longa, 0.25 mm lata; ovarium globosum, vix 1 mm longum ac latum, stigmatibus 3, 0.5 mm longis, recurvis; staminodia 2 vel 3, 0.5 mm longa, filiformia. Flores masculi fructusque adhuc non visi.

description: Liana 3 m alta; caules teretes inermes ca. 5 mm diam., inconspicue striatuli, minute puberuli, pilis patentibus vix 0.25 mm longis, internodiis elongatis ca. 15 mm longis; petioli elongati 4-5 cm longi, eirros elongatos puberulos ca. 1 cm supra basim gerentes, parte libera supra medium articulata; lamilna foliorum late cordato-ovata, 17-18 X 13.5-14.5 cm, apice abrupte apiculata, basi late subeordata, sinu aperto, non lobata, chartacea, inermis, supra maturitate glabrata, subtus persistenter tenuiter pilosula, 1-nervia, nervis exterioribus submarginalibus, venulis albidis perspicue reticulatis subtus prominulis; inflorescentiae masculae in axillis ternae, pedunculis 2.5-3.5 cm longis, ca. 0.7 mm diam., subeomplanatis, dense puberulis, receptaculo globoso ca. 5 mm diam., bracteolis minutis dense pilosulis; pedicelli 10-12 mm longi gracillimi ca. 0.2 mm diam. ubique pilosuli; flores numerosi 40 vel plures, alabastris clavatis ca. 5 mm longis apice minute pilosulis; petala recurvata glabra apice excepta oblanceolata ca. 6 mm longa, 1-1.2 mm lata, exteriora et interiora aequalia; filamenta ca. 4 mm lonoia, gracilia, ca. 0.4 mm diam.; antherae oblongae filamentis multo breviores ca. 1.5 mm longae et 0.6 mm latae; flores foeminei et baccae ignotae.
bibliographicCitation: Morton, Conrad V. 1962. A reexamination of Mexico Smilax (Smilacaceae). Brittonia. 14: 299-309.

description: Liana robusta, caule usque ad 8 m longo et 10 mm crasso; rami 0.2-0.6 m longi, internodiis 3-10 cm longis, 2-4 mm crassis, teretibus, sparse aculeolatis, virentibus. Folia remotiuscule alternata; laminae ellipticae vel anguste ellipticae, raro ovato- ellipticae, 6-20 cm longae, 3-12 cm latae, subcoriaceae, basi subito contractae rotundaeve, apice rotundae vel leviter emarginatae et plerumque mucronatae, supra dilute virides, subtus pallidae; costae 5 cum duabus marginalibus valde gracilibus, 3 centrales basi breviter (5-10 mm) connatae, crassae, supra leviter impressae, subtus valde convexae, nervulis lateralibus oblique ascendentibus, reticulum sublaxum vix elongatum conspicuum formantibus; petioli 15-30 mm longi, trigoni, dorsaliter subacuti, interdum medio rufo-brunneo-tincti, parte inferiore 7-25 mm vaginantes, alis late ovatis, 5-12 mm latis, herbaceis mox marcidis brunnescentibus vel rufo- brunneis non vel haud amplexicaulibus; cirrhi 7-20 cm longi. Inflorescentiae 7-25- umbellatae; axis ex axillis prophyllatis ramorum atque apicis caulis enatus, 8-20 cm longus, 3-5-nodosus, internodiis 1-5 cm longis; prophyllum late ovatum, 5-7 mm longum, apice acutum. Umbellae 2-5-natae, 15-30 mm in diametro, 18-40-florae; receptacula 2-3 mm crassa; pedunculi 1-4 cm longi, divergentes. Perianthium masculum 4-5 mm longum; tepala flava vel flavo-viridia, valde recurva, externa oblonga 1-1.3 mm lata, apice obtusa, interiora linearia, 0.3-0.5 mm lata; stamina 6, antheris oblongis, 1.5 mm longis, albidis, filamentis 4-4.5 mm longis. Perianthium foemineum 3-4 mm longum; tepala recurva, lanceolato-oblonga, apice subacuta, externa 0.8-1.2 mm lata, interiora 0.5 mm lata; ovarium subglobosum, 1 mm longum ac latum, stigmatibus elongatis 0.8-1 mm longis; staminodia 3, setiformia, tantum 0.5 mm longa. Baccae usque adhuc non visae.

description: Liana usque ad 4 m longa. Caules graciles, subteretes, 2-4 mm crassi, laeves vel sparse aculeolati, sursum laxe ramosi; rami conspicue angulati, striati, valde flexuosi, internodiis 3-9 cm longis 1-2 mm latis, crassi, laevibus vel sparse aculeolatis. Folia remotiuscule alternata, semper valde deflexa; laminae lanceolatae vel oblongo-lanceo- latae, 9-16 cm longae, 3-4.5 cm latae, basi rotundo-contractae, ad apicem subacutum mucronatumque sensim attenuates, herbaceae, supra opacae, subtus pallidae; costae 5 cum jugo marginali, omnes e basi laminae divergentes, 3 centrales eminentes, subtus convexae, nervulis lateralibus oblique ascendentibus reticulum sublaxum inconspicuum formantibus; petioli 15-20 mm longi, dorso obtusi, e basi ad dimidium alis 0.5 mm latis membranaceis vaginantes; cirrhi graciles, 8-13 cm longi, vel in foliis floriferis saepe non evoluti. Inflorescentiae plerumque biumbellatae; axis ex axillis prophyl- latis ramorum enatus, divergens vel deflexus, 10-30 mm longus; prophyllum ovato- lanceolatum, 7-9 mm longum, apice sensim acuminatum, mox marcidum; pedunculi  10-20 mm longi. Umbellae masculae 18-25 mm in diametro, 18-30-florae; eae foemineae 13-25-florae, receptaculo 3 mm crasso; radii 5-8 mm longi. Perianthium masculum 5 mm longum; tepala externa oblonga, recurva, 1 mm lata, apice obtusa, interiora lineari-oblonga, 0.5 mm lata; antherae 0.7-1 mm longae, filamentis 5 mm longis. Flores foeminei a me non visi. Baccae (parum immaturae) ovoideae, 7-9 mm longae.

description: Planta inter S. herbaceam L. et S. pseudo-china L. quasi intermedia; differt a S. herbacea pedunculis brevioribus, floribus masculis et foemineis multo minoribus (tepalis 1.5-2.5 mm vs 3.5-4.5 mm longis), antheris filamentisque longitudine aequalibus, et foliis hastatis; a S. pseudo-china pedicellis longioribus, foliis neque valde hastatis neque coriaceis et habitu dissimilis.

description: Perennial herbaceous vine; rhizome brown or black, zig-zag (due to alternate origins of aerial stems), with many stout fibrous roots at the nodes; stems up to 3 m tall, with numerous secondary branches, smooth and shiny, with no prickles, containing a central pith; leaves dark green above, glaucous beneath, with short papillae produced by the epidermal cells, the blade of lower main stem leaves triangular with cuspidate apicies, concave lateral margins and truncate to slightly cordate or hastate (with rounded lobes) bases, (4) 5-6.5 (8) cm long, (2.5) 3-5 (5.5) cm broad, the blade of upper main stem leaves and those on the branches ovate, occasionally cordate (on some plants, all leaves broadly cordate, those of main stem 5.5-7.5 cm long, 6.5-8.5 cm broad), the lowermost 3-5 leaves reduced to bracts, loosely sheathing the stem or their axillary branches; petioles shorter than blade, producing tendrils at or slightly above base; peduncles axillary to foliage leaves, the male approximating the subtending leaf in length and withering after flowers fall, the female long (up to 13.5 cm) and stout in fruit; male umbels with up to 20 flowers; male tepals elliptic to oblong, 2.5 mm long, 1.5 mm broad, often 3-veined, spreading or reflexed from base; anthers slightly shorter or equal to the filaments, 0.7-1.0 mm long; female umbels few- to many-flowered (up to 40), hemispheric or spherical; female tepals as in male; staminodes filiform, 1.5 mm long; ovary globose, 1.5 mm diam., 3-locular; stigmas 3, ligulate, spreading, 0.5-0.7 mm long; ovules pendulous orthotropous, 2 per locule; berry probably blue (drying dull maroon-brown), 6-8 mm diam., on pedicels up to 1.8 cm long, with 2-6 (?) seeds.
bibliographicCitation: Steere, William C. & Buck, William R. 1979. Macromitrium crumianum (Musci: Orthotrichaceae), a new species from Guatemala. Brittonia. 31: 395-398.

description: Ramuli inermes elongati ca. 3 mm diam. perspicue hirsuti, pilis 1.5 mm longis vel plus, internodiis elongatis, 11-13 cm longis; petioli 2.5-3 cm longi, supra medium articulati, valde hirsuti, eirros hirsutos crassos ca. 1 mm diam. 7-8 mm supra basim gerentes; folia late ovata 12 X 8 usque ad 14.5 X 11 cm, apice abrupte cuspidata, basi cordata, sinu subangusto sed non clauso, non lobata, chartacea, utrinque hirsuta, pilis 1.5-1.8 mm longis, 7-nervia, nervis lateralibus submarginalibus, venulis supra inconspicuis subtus prominulis reticulatisque; flores foeminei ignoti; pedunculi infloreseentiae masculae solitarii axillares nutantes 3.5-4.5 cm longi, graciles, ca. 1 mm diam., hirsuti; bracteolae hirsutae; petala ca. 6 mm longa, 1.8 mm lata, apice obtusa, pilos paucos gerentia; filamenta ca. 2.5 mm longa, crassa, ca. 1.6 mm lata, antheris latiora; antherae ca. 1.5 mm longae et 0.5 mm latae.
bibliographicCitation: Morton, Conrad V. 1962. A reexamination of Mexico Smilax (Smilacaceae). Brittonia. 14: 299-309.

description: Multi-stemmed shrubs, 1-3 m tall, to rarely small trees, 5-6 m tall, with leaves present on the last 5-7 nodes on terminal branchlets (not clustered on terminal branches); bark smooth, light brown; wood white; young leafy branchlets 2-3 mm thick, terete to subterete. Stipules free at base, deltoid and acuminate at apex, connected to petioles, sparsely puberulent outside and inside, basally pilose inside, the free portion 1-2 mm long, caducous; with 2-3 rows of many colleters inside. Blades (3-)5-8.5 X (2-)3.5-5.5 cm, length:width ratio 1.5:1 to 2:1, elliptic to ovate to broadly ovate (rarely obovate), acute to rounded at base, acute at apex; margins flat (not revolute); dark green above, pale green below, thickly foliaceous, drying reddish brown; glabrous above and glabrous to sparsely puberulent below; primary and secondary veins glabrous above, glabrous to puberulent below, prominent below; secondary veins (4-)5-9 each side, tertiary veins sparse and reticulate; petioles (0.5-)1-1.8 cm long, 1-1.5 mm thick, adaxially canaliculate. Inflorescences terminal, solitary, cymose, (7-)15-35-flowered, 1.5-5.5 cm long; rachis and branches glabrous to sparsely short-pubescent; flowers in 3-5-florous cymules; distal bracts narrowly lanceolate, 3-4 mm long; bracteoles subtending the flowers minutely lanceolate, to 1 mm long. Flowers sessile to short-pedicellate, fragrant; pedicels to 4 mm long, thick- ening in mature capsules. Calyx 4-5-lobed, the tube extremely reduced, 0.3-0.4 mm long, the lobes rounded to oblong, 2.5-4 X 1.5-2.5 mm, sparsely puberulent. Corolla hypocrateriform (with spreading lobes), 28-35 mm long, white; tube long-tubular, grad- ually expanded toward the orifice, 22-28 mm long, ca. 1 mm wide at base and ca. 3 mm wide at orifice (without annular thickening), short puberulent outside, pilose toward the orifice inside; lobes 4-5, imbricate in bud, rounded, ca. 3.5-4 X 3.5-4 mm, glabrous throughout. Stamens 4-5, the tips exserted (most of the length included), of equal length, subsessile, attached on the tube near the mouth; filaments 0.5-0.7 mm long; anthers narrowly oblong, 4.5-5 x 0.5-0.7 mm, dorsifixed near the base. Style exserted, 3-3.5 mm long, smooth, glabrous; style branches narrowly oblong, ca. 4 X 0.4 mm. Capsules narrowly-obconical, multicostate, often slightly curved, decurrent at base, 13-23 mm long, 4-6 mm wide at apex, dark brown, glabrous (or very sparse- ly puberulent), bilocular, with (10-)15-30 seeds per locule; calyx persistent; disk exceeding the calyx in mature capsules. Seeds peltate, vertical, fusiform, (2-)4.5-7 X (0.4-)0.8-1.2 mm, flattened, with central hilum, with central ellipsoid endosperm, bipolar-winged, with irregularly fringed margin.
bibliographicCitation: Delprete, Piero G. 1999. The Cuban endemic genera Ariadne, Mazaea, Acunaeanthus, Phyllomelia (Rondeletieae), and Eosanthe (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 51: 217-230.

description: Plants entirely herbaceous, apparently short-lived perennials. Stems very slender; underground caudices unexpanded, prostrate, minutely nodulate, highly rhizomatous, and bearing numerous, very thin, fibrous, descending rootlets emanating from the minute nodes; above ground portions gla- brous, ascending-erect, solitary but occa- sionally accompanied by 1-2 depauperate, sterile side branches from near ground level, unbranched above, 15-21 cm tall, proximal portions sometimes weakly persistent. Leaves 5-30 mm long, linear-filiform, mostly sessile and not at all clasping, glabrate to very sparsely villosulous, relatively few, mostly alternate, ascending, entire to pin- nately divided below, usually pinnately divided above into 3-7 relatively short, linear-filiform, divaricate segments, 1- 10 mm in length. Inflorescences solitary, showy, but bearing 1-2(-4) flowers in a short, secund raceme, usually with a small  open cluster of sterile apical bracts. Flowers on pedicels 3-13 mm long. Bracts very similar to leaves in most characters but sometimes proximally lanceolate and usually gradually reduced in size distally, "bright red" at least distally. Calyx 30-40 mm long, tubular, "greenish-yellow", glabrate to very sparsely villosulous, divided about 3/4 in front and 1/8-1/6 in back, lobes lanceolate, entire, and acute or less often emarginate, with two short, triangular segments about 1 mm long but often slightly unequal in length. Corolla 45-50 mm long, "greenish- yellow"; corolla beak 30-32 mm long, clearly exceeding the tube in length and well-exserted beyond the calyx, mostly glabrous, becoming villosulous on the dorsal surface; lower corolla lip ca. 1-2 mm long, barely exserted from the calyx and strongly reduced to three incurved, dark greenish, lanceolate, acute-tipped teeth. Stigma exserted 1-5 mm beyond corolla, dark green, unlobed, and only slightly capitate-expanded. Stamens about equaling the corolla in length, with anthers 2-3 mm long. Pollen grains ovate. Capsules ovoid, 12-13 mm long, 6-7 mm wide, with a strongly apicu- late tip, 1-2 mm long. Seeds ovate to truncate-ovate, 1-2 mm long; seed coat tight fitting, very shallowly reticulate, reticulation cells narrowly oblong, radial walls of reticulations smooth, inner tangential walls smooth, glassy, and unruptured at maturity.
bibliographicCitation: Egger, M. 2009. A new species of Castilleja (Orobanchaceae) from Trujillo, Venezuela. Brittonia. 61 (1): 41-45.

description: Dalea tomentosae (Cay.) Willd. var. mota similis sed differt foliis punctatis in superficiebus ambabus, summis unifoliolatis bracteiformibus tis, inflorescencia corymboidi-paniculata spicis minimum 15-26, bracteis persitentibus glabris, calyce 3.3-3.8 mm longo non recesso vexilum (non obliquo), costis calycis non manifestis glandibus olei, dentibus dorsalibus calycis triangularibus spinulosis in amplitudine corollis albis vel albidis.

description: Suffruticose herbs. Stems erect, 33-50 cm tall, 2-2.6 mm diam., corymbosely branching distally, densely silky-pilose to satiny-pilose throughout with fine, straight, ascending hairs, 0.5-1.3 mm long, densely leafy, the branches and stems sparsely and minutely glandular. Stipules linear-lanceolate to triangular lanceolate, 2.9-4.2 mm long, persistent, pilose, brown to dark brown. Leaves pinnate e (1-)2-3.7 cm long, petiolate, the uppermost bracteiform or unifoliolate; petioles 4-9 mm long; leaflets (1-)2-3 pairs, elliptic, elliptic-obovate to obovate, 5-16 x 3-7.5 mm, flat, veinless, both surfaces densely pilose, both surfaces sparsely glandular-punctate (more densly so abaxially), the terminal leaflet sessile, the rachis canaliculate; intrapetiolular gland 1, linear-lanceolate, 0.3-0.5 mm long, brown to reddish brown; post-petiolular glands 2, linear-lanceolate, 0.2-0.3 mm, brown to reddish brown. description: Liana, with the branches and branchlets densely sericeous, striate when mature, brown. description: Plants epiphytic, pseudobulbs lacking or extremely small and completely hidden by the sheathing leaves and not terminated by a leaf; leaves ovate-elliptic to linear- lanceolate, 15-40 cm long, 2-6 cm wide. description:
Drvmariae axillari Brandegee similis sed differt petalis breviunguiculatis, doubus in 4 lobos bifurcatis, trunco (pars laminaris petalina sub supraque unguem) ad basim leviter, stipulis carentibus, et seminibus lacriformibus tuberculatis.

description: Suffrutescent herb to 50 cm tall, with simple or few-branched stems from a woody base; rhizomes short with extended roots, divergent and fusiform; stems ascending to suberect, terete, ± angular at the apex, 1-2.5 mm diam., tomentose to sericeous, pubescent on old branches, the hairs spreading yellowish to ivory; description: Tree ca. 6 m tall. description: Tree 3-10 m tall, stem erect with bark grey and thin with shallow transverse fissures; young branches cylindrical or angulate, glabrous, lenticellate. Tree 3-10 m tall, stem erect with bark grey and thin with shallow transverse fissures; young branches cylindrical or angulate, glabrous, lenti cellate. Pseudoracemes 5-5.5 cm long, axillary, congested and shorter leaves; peduncle 2-3 mm long, rachis 1.8-3.8 cm long, both angulate and shortly ferruginous-sericeous, flowers geminate; primary bract (at base of inflorescence) caducous; secondary bracts (that enclose the bract at the base of pedicel) 0.9-1 mm long, broadly ovate, ferruginous-sericeous externally; tertiary bracts (at base of each pedicel) ca. 1 mm long, narrowly ovate, ferruginous-sericeous externally; pedicels 45 mm long, cylindrical, shortly ferruginous-sericeous; bracteoles (situated on upper part 2-3 mm long, rachis 1.8-3.8 cm long, both angulate and shortly ferruginous-sericeous, flowers geminate; primary bract (at base of inflorescence) caducous; secondary bracts (that enclose the bract at the base of pedicel) 0.9-1 mm long, broadly ovate, ferruginous-sericeous externally; tertiary bracts (at base of each pedicel) ca. 1 mm long, narrowly ovate, ferruginous-sericeous externally; pedicels 45 mm long, cylindrical, shortly ferruginous-sericeous; bracteoles (situated on upper part of pedicel) 1-1.1 mm long, narrowly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, apex acute, densely sericeous externally, subopposite and punctate. Flowers purple; pedicels 2-3 mm long, cylindrical, ferruginous-sericeous; calyx 4.8-5 x3.8-4 mm, campanulate, gibbous on the vexillary surface and with prominent punctations, especially at the base, densely ferruginous-sericeous externally, glabrous internally, margin ciliate, base rounded, vexillary lobe retuse, carenal lobes 3, broadly triangulate, acute at the apex; standard reflexed, with a white blotch at the base, blade 9-9.5x10-11 mm, ovate, apex emarginate, base subtrucate without callosities or auricles, glabrous internally and shortly sericeous on the central-apical region of the dorsal face, sparsely punctate, the claw 4.9-5x2.9-3 mm; wings 10—11 x 4 mm, oblong, punctate, apex rounded, base truncate on the vexillary margin, sericeous on the central-apical region of the lower surface, with lunate sculpturing above the claw, claws 5-5.1 mm long; keel petals 7.8-8x3-3.1 mm, elliptic-falcate, punctate, umbonate, apex obtuse, base attenuate on the vexillary margin, lower surface shortly sericeous on the dorsi-ventral region, including at the apex, tri-chomes more concentrated at the apex, claw 5-5.1 mm long; staminal tube ca. 5 mm long, fleshy, glabrous, slightly bicallose basally, the free portion of the filaments ca. 7 mm long, anthers ca. 0.7 mm long, ovoid, apiculate; ovary 6.9-7 x 0.7-0.8 mm long, lanceolate, curved, shortly and densely sericeous along its whole length, style ca. 5 mm long, curved, sparsely sericeous, stigma punctate; stipe ca. 1.2 mm long; ovules 6, suborbicular; hypan-thium ca. 0.5 mm long, asymmetrical. Fruit 4.6-9.5 x 1.7-2.3 cm, 2-seeded, indehiscent, elliptic or oblong-elliptic with or without constrictions between the seeds, base attenuate, apex acuminate, vexillary margin nerviform, coriaceous, with shallow transverse fissures at maturity, shortly ferruginous-sericeous, stipe 6-11 mm long; seeds 1.4-1.5 x 11.1 cm, thickened, reniform, castaneous, smooth.

description: Small tree 4-5 m tall. Trunk erect with grey bark. Branches cylindrical to angulate, lenticellate, with shallow transverse fissures, erruginous-tomentose on the young branches, petioles, and rachises. Leaves 7(-5)-foliolate, pulvinus 2.5-2.8 mm long, pubescent, 1.1-1.2mm long; petiole 1.5^1.9 cm long, rachis 3-5.7 cm long, both canaliculate dorsally; petiolule 2-2.3 mm long, angulate, slightly rugose. Leaflets 3.4-8x2-3 cm, opposite, the basal ones ovate-elliptic with an oblique base, the median ones elliptic and the terminal ones elliptic to elliptic-obovate, both with the base cuneate, thin-chartaceous, apex acute and retuse, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface shortly and sparsely ferruginous-sericeous, margins slightly revolute, discolorous; venation brochidodromous, midvein and secondary veins impressed on upper surface and prominent on lower surface, secondaries forming an angle of 35-45° with the midvein. Pseudoracemes 4-7 cm long, axillary, multiflorous, congested and shorter than leaves, rachis ferruginous-sericeous, flowers geminate; primary bract (at base of inflorescence) caducous; secondary bracts (bract at the base of pedicel) 0.9-1 mm long, broadly ovate, rigid, ferruginous-sericeous externally, persistent, without punctations; tertiary bracts (at base of each pedicel) 1.2-1.3 mm long, linear-spatulate, ferruginous-sericeous externally, without punctations, caducous; pedicel 4-4.5 mm long, cylindrical, shortly ferruginous-sericeous; bracteoles (situated at apex of the pedicel) 1.4-1.6 mm long, linear, opposite to subopposite, apex acute, densely sericeous externally, opposite to subopposite. Flowers pink to purple; calyx 2-2.2 x 2.8-3.2 mm, campanulate, shortly ferruginous-sericeous externally, glabrous internally, without punctations, margin ciliate, base rounded, vexillary lobe truncate; the 3 carenal lobes, rounded at the apex; standard reflexed, with a whitish blotch at the base, blade 4.9-5 x 6.9-7 mm, ovate, apex emarginate, base subtruncate, without callose appendages or auricles, glabrous internally and shortly sericeous on the central-apical region of the dorsal face, claw 44.5 mm long; wings 4.9-5 x 2.5-3 mm, obovate, apex rounded, base sagittate on the vexillary margin, sericeous on the central-apical region of the dorsal face, claw 4-4.2 mm long; keel petals 4.9-5 x3-3.2 mm, subrhombic, umbonate, apex acute, base subtruncate to obtuse on the vexillary margin, dorsal surface shortly sericeous on the dorsientral region, including the apex, trichomes denser at the apex, claw 3.5-4 mm; staminal tubes 4.9-5.1 mm long, narrow, glabrous, pigmented, membranaceous, without callosities, free portion of the filaments 2-3 mm long, anthers ca. 0.4 mm long, ovoid; ovary 4.9-5 x 0.7 mm, linear, curved, shortly and densely sericeous along its whole length, style strongly curved, sericeous, stigmas punctiform; stipe 1.4-1.6 mm long; ovules 5, reniform; hypanthium ca. 0.5 mm long, asymmetrical. Fruits 5-6.7x0.8-0.9 cm, lanceolate, 1-2-seeded, indehiscent, base oblique, apex obtuse and mucro-nulate, vexillary margin nerviform, chartaceous, shortly ferruginous-tomentose; seeds 5-6 x 2.62.7 mm, subreniform.

description: Small tree 4-5 m tall, 20-25 cm in diameter, branchlets dark brown with a waxy cuticle, glabrous. Stipule intrapetiolar, membranous, connate basally for at least 3 mm, distal portion of stipule linear 1.1-1.4 cm long, 0.4-0.6 cm wide, caducous (Fig. 1D). Leaves simple, alternate, entire, coriaceous, dark green in life, elliptic oblong 18.5-32 cm long, 7-11.5 cm wide, petiole terete, 0.5- 0.7 cm long, base of leaf acute-cuneate, enrolling and tapering down the pulvinus; pair of crater like glands at either side of the midvein at base of lamina (Fig. 1C), apex acuminate 1.2-2 cm long, mucronate; venation brochidodromous, prominent especially on the underside (abaxial surface; Fig. IB). Inflorescence an axillary or terminal, compact  raceme 0.5-1.5 cm long; bracts that subtend the inflorescence persistent, 5-6 mm long, 4- 5 mm wide, green, triangular, acute, strigu- lose abaxially and the margins ciliolate; floral bract 11 mm long, 10 mm wide, free, ciliolate on margins but otherwise glabrous; bracteoles united almost to apex, enclosing bud except at apex, 7-9 mm long, 6-8 mm wide, green, quadrangular, margins hyaline, membranous, glabrous; pedicel 4 mm long, 2 mm wide, quadrangular, ca. 9 mm from insertion of bracteoles to base of hypanthium; hypanthium cupular, 8 mm long, 6 mm wide, glabrous. Sepals 4, 15-17 mm long, 6- 10 mm wide except adaxial sepal 12 mm wide, green externally with red margins, red internally. Petals 5, lateral petals 16-17 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, in life red with white streaks, adaxial petal 18-19 mm long, 7 mm wide, clawed, light red, glabrous except for a ciliate apex, edges crisped. Stamens 9, all fertile, 40-60 mm long, bright red, filaments pilose from base to apex, all united to form a tube approximately 1 mm long, anthers 7- 8 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, red, versatile, densely pilose along outer edge, elliptic, pollen exine verrucate; gynoecium glabrous, 9 mm long, 2 mm wide at anthesis, stipe 2 mm long, glabrous, style 2.8-4 cm long, stigma capitate, minutely papillose. Mature fruit not seen.

description: Haec species ad subgenus Hebecladam sepalis ante- rioribus extemis fere omnino connatis et carina non cristata pertinens. Herba. Caulis erectus. Radix lignosa. description: Herbs erect, 15-60 (72) cm tall; root lignose; stems several, slender, distally few-branched, subaphyllous, pubescent, the trichomes patent, straight or slightly curved, forming two groups of different lengths, short ones ca. 0.1 mm long, and long ones ca. 0.3 mm long, with few of intermediate length. Leaves with a linear or scale-like blade, alternate, chartaceous times caducous, 2-15(-20)x 1-2 mm, the petiole 0.6-1.5 mm. Inflorescence terminal, axillary or extra-axillary racemes, (1.5-)2- 7.4 x 1-1.5 cm in flower, increasing to 11.5 cm long after the fruits have abscised. Peduncles 0.2-1.3 cm long; bracts 0.7-1.2 x 0.4-0.9 mm, pentagonal, persistent after fruits fall, 2.7-5 times longer than the bracteole, ciliate at margin with non-glandular trichomes; bracteoles ca. 0.2 mm, glabrous or ciliate with non-glandular trichomes; pedicels 2-3.3 mm, 2/5-7/10 of flower length, glabrous, curved or less often straight in fruit. Flowers 1 or 2 open at the same time, pendulous or more rarely sub-patent, 4.7- 5.4 mm long; outer sepals ovate, concave, green, subfleshy, apex acute, glabrous or ciliate along the margin, glandular and non-glandular trichomes often mixed, the abaxial sepals 1.4-2 x 1.3-1.6 mm, connate almost the length of the margin; inner sepals (wings) 4.1-4.8 x 3- 3.9 mm, the adaxial sepal 1.6-2.1 x0.8-1 mm, pale lilac, the width 66-85% of the length, elliptic to obovate, glabrous or ciliate along the proximal half of the margin; keel pale lilac, not cristate, almost trilobate, glabrous on the outer surface, inner surface puberulous, apex yellow; base ciliate; 4.6-5 mm long, the unguiculus 1.4-1.8 mm, the cuculus 2.6-2.9 mm wide; lateral petals 4.2-5.1 mm long, the apex 1.5- 1.9 mm wide, broadly deltate, the base auriculate; androecium basally adnate to lateral petals, free portion of filaments 1.9-2.3 mm long; ovary with basal disc; style bent ca. 900, the base 2.5-3.4 mm long, the apex 2.1-2.2 mm long. Capsules 4-4.3 x 2.5-2.8 mm, oblong elliptic, glabrous; seeds 2.6-3.1x 1.2- 1.4 mm; indument sericeous, trichomes white, caruncle 0.8-1 x 1-1.3 mm, with two lateral appendices; trichomes 0.5-0.9 mm.

description: Shrub up to 2 m high, erect, stems leafless below, glabrous, terete, well- branched to the apex, sometimes sprouting from lateral buds at the base after burning, branches straight and slightly rugose, with conspicuous stipular tissue. description: Trepadoras lenosas, con zarcillos cauli-nares, monoicas (flores funcionalmente uni-sexuales), glabriusculas; pelos dispersos, breves, adpresos, amarillentos o blanquecinos en ramas muy jovenes y pedunculo de la inflorescencia parcial. Ramas floriferas de 25 mm de diam., finamente estriadas, con lenticelas pequenas, puntiformes, amarillentas, con cambium unico. Ramas viejas de 11 mm de diam., con 5 costillas redondeadas, notables, correspondientes a los 5 cambiumes perifericos, con abundantes lenticelas horizon-tales sobre las costillas y puntiformes en las depresiones. Hojas 3-folioladas; estipulas triangulares, ca. 0.5 mm de largo, puberulas; peciolo 1.5-4 cm de largo, canaliculado ventralmente, glabro o raramente puberulo; peciolulo 2-5 mm de largo, siempre de mayor longitud en el foliolo terminal; foliolos carta-ceos, levemente discoloros, oblongos, rara vez ancho-oblongos, los foliolos laterales con la semilamina externa poco mas ancha que la interna, 4.8-7.8><2.2-3.9 cm, la base decurren-te, rara vez obtusa en los foliolos laterales; apice obtuso, rara vez emarginado o redon-deado, mucronulado, el margen entero, algo ondulado, con linea cartilaginea castano-oscura; epifilo verde oscuro, glabro, con vena media algo sobresaliente y a veces abundantes puntos translucidos castanos; hipofilo verde mas palido, glabro, la venacion marcada; venacion camptodroma-broquidodroma, con 8-10 pares de venas secundarias curvadas abruptamente. Tirsos umbeliformes, simples o dobles axilares, ecirrosos, el pedunculo de la inflorescencia 0.8-2.8 cm de largo, el pedunculo del cincino 2-8 mm de largo, los cincinos plurifloros; pedicelo floral 1.5^1 mm de largo, glabro, en el fmto 3-4 mm de largo, articulado en la base o en un tercio basal; bracteas y bracteolas triangulares, 0.5 mm de largo, ciliadas. Flores blanquecinas, de 3-5 mm de largo; caliz ca. 1.3 mm de largo, los lobulos ovados, obtusos, ca. 0.5 mm de largo, glabros, rara vez glabriusculos, ciliados; petalos espa-tulados, unguiculados, erosos, 2 mm de largo, glandulosos, con pelos pluricelulares lineares dispersos, con dos apendices lineares, diver-gentes, vellosos naciendo de la una del petalo; disco nectarifero anular, glabro. Flores esta-minadas con 8 estambres, ca. 4.8 mm de largo; filamentos vellosos en 1/2 basal; anteras glabras; pistilodio ca. 0.3 mm de largo. Granos de polen isopolares, tricolporados, medianos, subesferoidales-suboblatos a prolato-esferoidales, el eje polar (23.75-)33.5(-40) pm, diam. ecuatorial (27.5-)36.75(-42.5) qm; sexina tectada, estriada-microperforada, el colpo con membrana apertural verrucosa. Flores pistiladas con 8 estambres, ca. 2 mm de largo; filamentos vellosos en 1/2 basal; anteras indehiscentes; gineceo brevemente estipitado, ca. 3 mm de largo; ovario trigono-ovoideo, con pelos adpresos en las costillas dorsales, el resto con pelos glandulares ferru-gineos; estilo puberulo, de igual longitud que las ramas del estigma. Frutos cartaceos, 3.6-4.2(-5.4) x 2.6-3 cm, incluido el estipite 3-6 mm de largo; porcion seminlfera del mericarpo ventricosa, obovoide-truncada, castano-oscura, 7-8(-9.5) x 5-6.8 mm, con una leve constriction sobre el loculo; epicarpo glabro; endocarpo con pelos aracnoideos, no glandulares, pluricelulares, biseriados en parte, simples o ramificados, blanquecinos o ferrugineos. Semillas obovoideas, 6.8 x 5.6 mm, insertas en la base de los loculos; embrion con el cotiledon extemo curvo y el intemo biplicado. Distribution, ecologlay fenologia.Thinouia restingae esta retringida a los estados de Rio de Janeiro, Espirito Santo y Bahia, en los dos primeros estados es una especie de la restinga arborea, mientras que en Bahia esta documentada para el bosque mesofilo a unos 50 km de la costa. Florece desde octubre hasta diciembre y presenta frutos maduros en agosto.

description: Subshrub ca. 0.8-1.0 m tall; stems erect, glabrous, punctate, striate. Leaves with four leaflets; sessile to subsessile, punctate. Leaflets 0.8-35(-50)x 1.5-5 mm, sessile, punctate, glabrous to pubescent, filiform to linear, apex acuminate, base cuneate, margin revo- lute. Stipules 3.2-7x 1.6-2.5 mm, lanceolate, peltate, punctate, glabrous, margin ciliate. Inflorescence spiciform, terminal or axillary, 4.2-17 cm long, villous. Bracteoles to 9x 3 mm, elliptic, villous, punctate, 4-5-nerved; auricle minute (to 0.5 mm long), punctate. Calyx campanulate, 5-lobed, glabrous to pubescent, margin ciliate, 7-13-nerved, punctate; tube 3 mm long, vexilar lobes 2, carinal lobes 3, one of them bigger than the others. Corolla yellow and purple striate. Standard 8-10 x 10-11 mm, orbicular, apex retuse, base auriculate, upper surface glabrous to pilose, margine ciliate; claw 2.5 -3 mm long. Wing petals 8-12 x 3-4 mm, ovate apex rounded, glabrous. Keel petals 8.5-12 x 3.5-5 mm, as long as the wing petals, ovate-falcate, apex acute, glabrous. Stamens monadelphous, dimorphic. Ovary 8-10 mm long, pilose; style curved, stigma minute. Loment with 2-4 articles; articles 4-5 x 2-3 mm, punctate, reticulate, pubescent, bristly, bristles to 3.5 mm long. Seeds 3x2 mm, oblong, flattened, dark brown, smooth.
