description: Pseudobulbs elliptic-pyriform, smooth, dark green. Leaves linear-lanceolate, 10-36 cm long, 1.0-2.5 cm wide, acuminate, dark green, sheathing bracts leaf bearing. In- florescence about the length of the leaves or slightly shorter. Flowers clustered on the peduncle. Floral bracts large, 0.6-2.5 cm long, 0.5-1.0 cm wide, navicular, papery, as long as the often short pedicel, pedicel 0.6-1.5 cm long. Flowers red-orange, not open- ing completely, the sepals and petals forming a tube. Sepals all alike, linear-lanceolate, 2.0-3.8 cm long, 0.3-0.8 cm wide. Petals similar to the sepals, linear-lanceolate, rarely slightly falcate, acuminate, 1.5-2.5 cm long, 0.3-0.7 cm wide. Lip linear-lanceolate, 1.0-1.6 cm long, 0.2-0.6 cm wide, more or less parallel to the column. Callus of two membranous lamellae terminated by two erect, recurved tooth-like masses, neither the lamellae nor the terminal masses so well developed as in the other species of the genus, the lamellae at times continuing beyond the too,th-like masses. Column short, stout, 0.4-0.5 cm high. Viscidium ovate, stipe obdeltoid, apical margin of stipe entire or slightly emarginate, often apiculate. Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador (?).

description: Stems slender, 0.5-2 dm tall, arising from a stout underground rhizome 0.6- 0.8 cm in diameter; leaves elliptic, sessile, (2.2) 2.5-4.5 (4.8) cm long, 1.5-2.5 (2.8) cm wide, dark green above and below with a purplish tinge below, rarely so above, acute to subobtuse apically, acute basally; pedicels lacking; sepals erect, exceeding the petals in length, narrowly ovate, (1.3) 1.5-2 (2.4) cm long, 0.6-1.2 (1.4) cm wide, dark green with a thin, hyaline often wavy margin, the apex distinctly cymbiform; petals spreading, white to pink especially after anthe- sis, 1.5-2 cm long, 0.5-1 cm wide, narrowly ovate, the margin undulate with an emarginate apex; stamens 0.8-1 cm long, about half the length of the petals, the filaments broadened at the base, about the length of the linear anther, the connective purple; style straight, 0.2-0.3 mm long, green, with each of the recurved 0.6-0.8 mm long whitish stigmas bearing a slightly wavy margin (Fig. 1).

description: Ex affinitate Trillui erecti, T. flexipedis, T. similis et T. vaseyi, a quibus pedicellis longis, floribus ringentibus et minoribus, sepalis et petalis apicem versus sulcatis differt. Folia subsessilia, late elliptica vel obovata, apice acuminata, basi gradatim descrescentia, cuneata. Pedicelli longi, stricti, erecti vel fere horizontales sed supra folia. Flores parvuli, ringentes, deorsum aspicientes. Sepala elliptica, ple- rumque purpureotincta vel non nisi margine purpurea, sulcata et interdum apicem versus introflexa, peranguste acuta vel acuminata, persistentia. Petala ovata, apice acuta, profunde vinacea vel purpurea, interdum alba vel luteola, plerumque non nihil longiora quam sepala et similiter apicem versus saltem in senectute sulcata aut partim recurva. Capsula succulenta, globosa, opace rubra, basi irregulatim dehiscens, apice stigmatibus recurvis, atropurpureis, marcescentibus aucta. Flores leniter suaveolentes, odorem fungi vivi accendentem, non foetidum emittentes.

description: Perennial, glabrous herbs. Stems erect, (22) 30-40 (53) cm tall. Leaves (8) 10-15 (19) cm long, (7) 9-14 (20) cm wide, subsessile, broadly elliptic to obovate, the apex acuminate, the base gradually narrowing, cuneate. Pedicels (3) 5-9 (12) cm long, straight, erect to almost horizontal but above the leaves. Flowers relatively small, ringent, turned downward. Sepals elliptic, (16) 20-3 5 (42) mm long, (7) 8-15 (16) mm wide, green and generally purple-tinged or purple only at the margin, sulcate and sometimes bent inward apically, narrowly acute to acuminate. Petals ovate, (17) 22-38 (54) mm long, (9) 12-24 (29) mm wide, deeply wine-colored to purple, sometimes white to light yellow, generally not much longer than the sepals and similarly sulcate apically, at least during senescence, or partly recurved. Stamens erect; filaments (2.5) 3-5 (6) mm long, purple to white; anthers (5) 5.5-10.5 (12) mm long, purple to yellowish, somewhat overtopping the ovary. Ovary dark purple to white, globose to flask-shaped, strongly hexagonal in transverse section, unilocular. Capsule fleshy, globose, dull red, irregularly dehiscent, the sulcate, purple-tinged sepals persistent at the base, the recurved, deep purple stigmas withering at the apex. Flowers mildly fragrant, the odor resembling a fresh fungus, not fetid. Somatic chromosome number, 2n = 10.

description: Hierbas terrestres, rara vez rastrera, epifitas o sobre troncos caidos, pocas veces ramificadas, 0.45-1.0 (-1.62) m de alto, pilosas a velutino-sas, con tricomas multicelulares, uniseriados, constituidos de 5 celulas a manera de artejos, hialinos o de color amarillento, con las divi-siones generalmente purpura-rojizas; raices poco profundas; llegando ha ser muy ramificadas; tallos erguidos, con la base algunas veces postrada, huecos, fragiles, de maximo 1 cm de diametro, purpura cuando jovenes y amarillento a gris cuando maduros, pilosos a densamente pilosos hacia el apice de la planta. Hojas opuesto-decusadas, dispuestas hacia el apice de la planta, anisofilas, elipticas, lamina grande de 13.4-27.5x6-13.5 cm, base ligeramente oblicua a aguda, apice acuminado a agudo, margen irregularmente aserrado a crenado-truncado, ciliado, 52-86 dientes, venas secun-darias con patron semicraspedodromo, venas superiores ligeramente mas agudas, 9-11 pares de venas secundarias; lamina pequena de 8- 14x4.4-8.1 cm, 39-68 dientes; 7-8 venas secundarias; haz generalmente mgosa, escabro-sa por levantamientos conicos sobre los que se asientan los tricomas, amarillentos con las divisiones purpura-rojizas, superficie verde oscuro, vena media generalmente purpura y a los lados de color blanquecino; enves con hundimientos distribuidos de manera regular, los cuales corresponden a los levantamientos del haz; piloso, con tricomas como el haz, superficie de color purpura-rojizo, vena media de color purpura, venas secundarias y terciarias amarillentas, ambas velutinas, estomas amarillentos evidentes al microscopio de luz, distribuidos en toda la superficie, y en particular en los hundimientos, arreglados dando la aparien-cia de remolinos. Peciolos de la laminas grandes de 2.2-6 cm de largo, de la laminas pequenas de 1.6-3.3 cm de largo, de color purpura, velutinos, tricomas como la hoja; camosidades a los lados de la base del peciolo evidentes, rojizas. Inflorescencias axilares en las ultimas hojas del tallo, cimoso-umbelada, de 8-15 flores, pocas veces menos. Botones florales velutinos, amarillos dentro del caliz rojo. Pedunculo reducido. Pedicelos de 2.2-2.8 cm de largo, purpura-rojizos, pilosos a densamente pilosos. Bracteas lanceoladas de 1.5-3 x 0.3-0.6 cm, pilosas a densamente pilosas, ciliadas,verde- rojizas. Caliz rojo, mas o menos camoso en fresco, con los lobulos ampliamente ovados a ovados, ligeramente concavos y reflejos, acuminados, cortamente aserrados hacia el apice, casi entero el dorsal y ligeramente mas pequeno, ciliados, 1.2-1.3 x 0.6-1.2 cm, densamente piloso, principalmente en la base, tricomas con divisiones amarillentas. Corola tubular-urceolada, 2.5 cm de largo, base sacciforme de 5-6 mm de ancho, tubo ventricoso de 9-11 mm de ancho en su parte mas ancha, garganta constrenida de 78 mm de ancho, tubo amarillo-blanquecino, por fiiera densamente viloso, con tricomas como el caliz, por dentro pequenos tricomas glandulosos de pie ancho y glandula grande,; lobulos cortos, casi iguales, 1-2. mm de alto, 2-3 mm de ancho, los dorsales casi fusionados, los laterales expandidos y el ventral dirigido ligeramente hacia el frente, de color amarillo a rojizo. Estambres epipetalos solo en la base, 11.2 cm de largo (parte libre), unidos en la base 4-5 mm., dispuestos lateralmente en pares. Nectario con una glandula blanquecina, 3 mm de alto, 2.7 mm ancho, mas o menos camosa, ovado-aguda, con un ligero hundimiento longitudinal medio, glabra. Ovario supero, bianco, vilosulo; estilo corto, bianco, pilosulo con tricomas glandulares pequenos y muy delgados; estigma estomatomorfo, bianco o rojizo. Fruto una baya (inmadura), esferica, con parte del estilo persistenete. translucida, vilosula, con semillas negras.

description: Trees, 18 m tall; branches pubescent; stipules caducous, not seen. Leaves 17- 2 1 -foliolate, alternate, imparipinnate or par- ipinnate; petiole 1.7-2.2 cm long; rachis 15.5-19 cm long, petiole and rachis both pubescent and slightly canaliculate along upper side; stipels 0.7-1 mm long, linear- lanceolate, caducous; petiolule 2.5-3.5 mm long, glabrescent. Leaflets 4.5-7x2.5-3.5 cm, alternate or opposite, oblong to oblong-elliptic, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent, slight- ly discolorous, dull mid-green adaxially, paler abaxially, obtuse or obliquely cunéate at the base, retuse or emarginate at the apex, venation brochidodromous, secondary veins 8-12 pairs, forming angles of 65-70° with the leaflet costa. Inflorescence a compound raceme, usually terminal; primary axis 1 8-24 cm long, pubes- cent; secondary axes 10-20 cm long, pubes- cent, usually branched. Bracts 0.8-1.2 mm long, linear-lanceolate, pubescent, caducous, inserted at pedicel base; bracteoles similar to bracts, 0.5-0.7 mm long, opposite, paired, inserted near middle of pedicel. Pedicels 1 .2- 2.1 mm long, with a ring of red-brown glands clustered at the points of insertion of the bracts and bracteoles. Floral buds 1.8-2 mm long, obovoid. Flowers 6-8 mm long; hypanthium 0.7-1 mm long. Calyx turbinate-campanulate, pubescent, 5-lobed, tube 1-1.2 mm long, lobes 1.5-1.8 mm long, triangular, the two adaxial lobes broader. Petals 5, white, clawed, gla- brous; adaxial petal slightly differentiated in shape and size, widely obovate, apically slightly emarginate, 3.7-5x2.5-3 mm; lateral and abaxial petals subequal, obovate, apically obtuse or praemorse, 4.5-5.2 x 2-2.2 mm. Stamens 10, free, filaments 4-6 mm long; anthers 0.5-0.6 mm long, widely elliptic. Ovary 2.5-2.7x0.9-1 mm, ellipsoid, pubes- cent, covered with white trichomes, 3-ovulate; stipe 1.5 mm long, glabrous; style 1.7-3 mm  long, glabrous; stigma punctiform. Fruits and seeds not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Rodrigues, R. S. & Tozzi, A. M. G. A. 2010. Two new species of Leptolobium (Leguminosae, Papilionoideae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 62 (1): 20-25.

description: Trees, 5-6 m tall; branches pubescent; stipules caducous, not seen. Leaves 9-13- foliolate, alternate, imparipinnate; petiole 1.3-2 cm long; rachis 4.2-8 cm long, petiole and rachis both pubescent and adaxially canaliculate; stipels 0.7-1 mm long, linear- lanceolate, caducous. Leaflets alternate or opposite, petiolules 2.5-3.5 mm long, pubes- cent or glabrescent, leaflet blades 3-5.5 * 1.5- 2.5 cm, elliptic, glabrous on both faces, discolorous, dull dark green adaxially, greyish green abaxially, obtuse or obliquely cunéate at base, acuminate or acute at apex, venation brochidodromous, secondary veins 6-9 pairs, forming angles of 45-55° with leaflet costa. Inflorescence a compound raceme, usually terminal; primary axis 15-18 cm long, pubes- cent; secondary axes 8-14 cm long, pubescent, usually not branched. Bracts 1.6-2.1 mm long, linear-lanceolate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially glabrous, caducous, inserted at pedi- cel base; bracteoles similar to bracts, 0.8- 1.1 mm long, opposite, paired, inserted near middle of pedicel. Pedicels 1.5-2 mm long, with a ring of red-brown glands clustered at the points of insertion of the bracts and bracteoles. Floral buds 2.7-3 mm long, obovoid. Flowers 9-11 mm long; hypanthium 1-1.2 mm long. Calyx turbinate-campanulate, abaxially pubes- cent, 5-lobed, tube 1-1.5 mm long, lobes 2-2.5 mm long, triangular, the two adaxial lobes broader than the others. Petals 5, white, clawed, glabrous; adaxial petal slightly differ- entiated in shape and size, widely obovate, apically emarginate, 5.5-6.5 x 4-5 mm; lateral and abaxial petals subequal, obovate, apically emarginate or praemorse, 6.5-7.5x3-3.5 mm. Stamens 10, free, filaments 7.5-8.5 mm long; anthers 0.6-0.8 mm long, widely elliptic. Ovary 2.8-3.2 x 0.9-1 mm, ellipsoid, covered with white trichomes, 3 - 4 ovulate; stipe 1.5- 2 mm long, glabrous; style 3.8-5 mm long, sparsely pubescent; stigma punctiform. Fruits 4-6 x 1.8-2 cm, 1-2 seeded, indéhiscent, flattened, elliptic or oblong, coriaceous, reticulate, brown, glabrous; stipe 3-5 mm long. Seeds 7-7.2 x 5.5-6 mm, 3-3.2 mm thick, oblong, compressed, rusty; hilum 1-1.2 x 0.9- 1 mm, suborbicular, subterminal; rim-aril white; embryo with a bulbose and straight radicle; endosperm present.

description: Epiphytic, thin, delicate subshrubs. Twigs subterete to angled, often sharply complantate, puberulous, the hairs simple and of two types, unicellular and eglandualr, or multicellular and glandular; mature stems subterete to angled, the bark fissured, grayish, glabrate, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; prophylls 2, opposite, valvate, ovate, inconspicuous, 0.6 mm long, the apex acute. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged; petioles subterete, flattened above, ca. 1mm long, puberulous, the hairs simple, unicellular, and elgandular; blades subcoriaceous, ovate to ellipticovate, 8-12 x 5-6mm, the base rounded, the margine entire, eciliate, the apex bluntly acute, glabrous above, glaberscent beneath with scattered, simple, multicellular, reddish-brown, glandular hairs; venation 3 - plinerved, conspicuous only on the youngest leaves, otherwise only the midrib inconspicuoulsty raised on both surfaces. Axillary solitary flowers; bracts and floral undifferentiated, 4-5, narrowly triangular, 1-1.2 mm long, the margin ciliolate with simple, unicellular, eglandular hairs, the apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; pedicels continuous with calyx, subterete, angles, ca. 1-1.6 cm long, glaberscent with few simple multicellular, glandular hairs; bracteoles 2, dinstinct, persistent, inserted towards base of pedicel, subopposite or opposite, triangular 1.0 -1.6 x 0.7 -0.8 mm, the margin ciliolate towards apex, the hairs simple, unicellular and elglandular, the apex acute. flowers 4- merous, diplostemonous. Caylx campanulate overall, strongly winged, 5.2 -6.5 mm long, glabrate, the hairs inconspicuous, scattered, simple and of two types, multicellular and glandular, or inicellular and elgandular, the aestivation valvate; tube obconic, 3.5 -4 mm long; limb 2-3 mm long; lobes deltate, 1.5 - 2x 2-2.5 mm, the margin eciliate, the apex acute; sinuses acute (V-shaped). Corolla bistratose, fleshy, red, urceolate, broadest below middle, 7.3 - 9(-10) mm long and 3.5 - 5 mm diam., glabrous within and without, the aestivation apparently valvate; lobes deltate, 0.5 -1.2 x 1-1.2 mm long, the apex acute. Stamens 8, equal, included, 6.3-6.5 mm long; filaments equal, distinct, linear, stright, 3 -3.5 mm long, densely puberulous in distal half on both surfaces, the hairs simple, unicellular and elgandular; anthers equal, 3.6 - 3.8 mm long; thecae 2-2.2mm long, minutely papillate, cells with polygonal shape; tubules 1.5 -1.8 mm long, smooth, dehiscing by interorse slits, ca. 1-1.4 mm long. Ovary 4-locular, placentation axile; style included, 8 mm long. Berry Unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Pedraza-Peñalosa, Paola & Luteyn, James L. 2010. New species of Ericaceae (Vaccinieae) from the Andes of Bolivia and Peru. Brittonia. 62 (1): 39-56.

description: Epiphytic shrubs. Twigs terete to subterete, often bluntly angles, puberulous, the hairs simple, some unicellular and eglandualr, or multicellular, glandular and deciduous; mature stems terete, the bark fissured, brown, glabrescent, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; prophylls 2, opposite, ovate, obscure, < 0.5 mm long, the apex obstuse. Leaves alterante, spirally arranged; petioles terete, 0.8-1.5 mm long, glaberscent with simple deciduous hairs, both glandular and muticellular long, and, eglandular and unicellular; blades subcoriaceous, elliptic to ovate- elliptic, 1.2 - 2.5 x (0.6-) 0.7 -1.1 cm, the base cuneate to obtuse, to bluntly acute, glabrescent above with simple hairs, some glandular and mutlicellular, others eglandular and unicellular, glabrescent beneath with scattered simple, multicellular and glandular hairs; venation obscurely 3-plinerved, the midrib conspicuous and slightly impressed above, raised beneath, the secondary and tertiary nerves obscure above, slightly raised beneath. Axillary solitary flowers; bracts and floral bract 3-5, undifferen- tiated, ovate to reniform, 0.4-0.5 mm long, the margin eciliate, the apex obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces; pedicels inconspicuously articu- late with calyx, 1.3-2.5 mm long, glabrescent with scattered simple, multicellular and glan- dular hairs; bracteoles 2, distinct, persistent, inserted towards base of pedicel, subopposite, transversely elliptic, 0.6-1x1.2-1.8 mm, the margin eciliate, the apex truncate, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers 4-merous, diplostemonous. Calyx campanulate overall, conspicuously winged, 3.2-3.7 mm long, glabrescent over the lobes with hairs simple, multicellular and glandular, and also simple, unicellular and eglandular, the aestivation unknown; tube obconic, 2-2.2 mm long; limb 1.2-1.6 mm long; lobes deltate, 0.6-0.8x1.2 mm, the margin eciliate, the apex acute; sinuses broadly acute. Corolla apparently bistratose, pale pink, cylindric, 8 mm long, 3 mm diam., glabrous without but puberulous within, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, the aestivation apparently valvate; lobes deltate, 1-1.2 x 1.8 - 2mm, the apex acute. Stamens 8, equal, included, 6.8-7 mm long; filaments equal, distince, long triangular and straight, 3.2 - 3.5 mm long, glabrescent in distal half on both surfaces but more abundantly adaxially, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; anthers equal, distinct, 3.8 -4 mm long; thecae 1.3 -1.5 mm long with basal appendage, smooth, cells with polygonal shape; tubules 2, distinct, 2.7 mm long, minutely papillate especially at base, dehiscing by introrse slits, ca. 1.2 mm long. Ovary 4-locular, placentation axile; style included, 7-8 mm long, Berry unknown.

description: Epiphytic shrubs. Twigs subterete, flattened, almost glabrous, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; mature branches terete, the bark fissured, turning whitish, glabrous; prophylls 2, opposite, valvate, ovate, 0.8-1.5 mm long, the apex acute. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged; petioles subterete, 1.6-2.4 mm long, glabrous; blades coriaceous and fleshy, ovate or elliptic, 1.3-2.2x0.6-1.2 cm, the base cunéate, the margin entire, cilio late towards apex of young leaves, the hairs simple, unicellular and egland- ular, the apex bluntly acute, glabrous above, or sometimes inconspicuously glabrescent along midrib with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, glabrous beneath; venation pinnate, raised on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 2-4 per side, anastomosing, the tertiary nerves branching freely. Inflorescences axillary, fas- ciculate, 2-flowered, or sometimes flowers solitary; bracts and floral bract undifferentiated, 5-7, persistent, cuculiate, ovate, 0.6-1.6 mm long, the margin sometimes ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, the apex obtuse or acute, glabrous on both surfaces pedicles articulat with calyx, reduced and hidden by bracts, 0.4 -0.7 (-1.5) mm long, glabrous except for a ring of simple hairs ate articulation, the hairs of two kinds, unicellular adn elgandular, or multicellular and glandular; bracteoles 2, distinct or rarely fused (in latter case the "single" bracteole 2- costate), persistent, inserted at base of the short pedicel, ovate 0.9 - 1.1 x 1- 1.3 mm, the margin apically ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular and elgandular, the apex obtuse or obcordate (only when a "single" bracteole present), glabrous on both surfaces. flowers 4- merous, diplostemonous. Calyx cylindirc overall, apparently slightly angualte, probably fleshy when fresh (when dried very thick and irregularly wrinkled), 5-7.2 mm long, puberulous with hairs simple, unicellular, eglandualr and slightly wavy, the aestivation valvate; tube cylindric, 2-3 mm long; limb 2.8 - 4.2 mm long; lobes triangular 1.8 -3 x 2-2.2 mm, the margin ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular and elgandular, the apex acute; sinuses acute (V shaped). corolla bistratose, fleshy, pink, urceolate, 6-7 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, the aestivation valvate; lobes triangular, 2x 1.7 -1.8 mm, the apex acute. Stamens 8, equal, included, 6- 6.3 mm long; filaments equal, distinct, more or less linear and straight, 2.9 -3.2 mm long, puberulous on both surfaces with hairs simple, unicellular and elgandualr; anthers equal, 3.6 - 4.0 mm long; thecae 1.5 -1.6 mm, papillate basal appendix with simple, unicellular hairs, cells with polygonal shape; tubules 2, distinct 2.1 - 2.5 mm long, smooth, dehiscing by introrse slits, 0.6 - 0.7 mm long. Ovary 4- locular, placentation axile; style exserted, 5.8 -6.2 mm long. Fruit unknown.

description: Large, leggy, scandent plants, glabrous, internodes 5-10 cm long, terete, with occasional epicortical roots. Leaves to 10.5x5 cm, thin, obovate to broadly lanceolate, apex truncate to obtuse rounded, with conspicuous, acute apiculus to 5 mm long, leaf base tapering to slender petiole 5-25 mm long, venation pinnate, evident, the prominent midvein running into the apiculus. Dioecious. Inflorescences indeterminate, simple or compound, to >15 cm long, with several to 12 pairs of triads per simple inflorescence or per lateral branch of compound inflorescences; flowers yellow to whitish, sessile, triads essentially so, calyculus smooth; bracts and bracteoles caducous. Female flowers not seen. Male flower buds 6 mm long, yellow; anthers 1.5 mm long, at least some with small connectival horn. Fruits 8 x 5 mm, ellipsoid, purple, all fruits on pedicels 2-3 mm long but fruiting triads essentially sessile on the axis.

description: Inconspicuous plants, percurrent ? (possibly sympodial), glabrous; internodes mostly 2-3 cm long, terete. Leaves paired, to 7x 3 cm, thin, obovate-elliptical with rounded or very obtuse apex, base cuneately tapering into indistinct, slender petiole to 1 cm long; venation pinnate but obscure. Inflorescence solitary in leaf axils, without basal crater, very short, with apparently a single pair of triads; inflorescence peduncle 4-5 mm long, stout, with conspicuous, pustule-like lenticels, and terminating in a small spur; triad peduncle 3 mm long, bracts and bracteoles 2 mm wide, nearly acute. Fruit 1.5 x  1.25 cm, ellipsoidal, salmon - red, calyculus fairy prominent; embryo dicotylous, cotyledons large and flat, blunt tipped; endosperm present.

description: Slender, glabrous plants, apparently lacking basal epicortical roots, with whip like, very slender, much elongated stems on which internodes may be as long as 10 cm where bearing minute, awl- shaped leaves 1-1.5 mm long which eventually subtend inflorescences, these internodes occasionally forming epicortical roots; lateral branches subtended by a pair of small, acute prophylls. Leaves to 5x 1.5(- 3) cm, thin, narrowly obovate to lanceolate, base acute, grading into slender petiole ca. 3 mm long, apex rounded to obtuse, often with minute terminal tooth, venation pinnate, midvein nearly reaching apex. Inflorescences sessile, one or more per axil, each with 2(-4) triads, the lowest ones emerging more or less directly from the leaf axil; triad peduncle 2 mm, bracts and bracteoles obtuse, persistent; male buds 2.5-3 mm long, obovoid, ovary ca. 0.5 mm, calyculus more or less smooth, filament 1 mm long; female flowers the same, but much more slender. Fruits not seen.

description: Suffrutescent perennial herbs with multiple, erect stems arising from subterranean branches after first year; branches curved outward from shoot, becoming erect distally, epidermis white, pubescent, shedding with age. Leaves green, 0.9-9.5x0.5-3.2 cm; lower leaves generally petiolate with spatulate to elliptic lamina, upper leaves short petiolate or sessile with elliptic to obovate lamina, generally with a nonclasping, tapering base; mar- gins slightly lobed to toothed (rarely entire) with 2-8 (-12) lobes up to 2.3 mm. Bracts entire, subtending capsule, 2-6.5 x 0.4-2 mm.  Androecium cream - white; stamens numberous, those of inner whorls shorter than outer, filaments glabrous, anther epidermis papillate; five outermost stamens in median antesepalous positions staminodial and petaloid 9-18 x 1-1.3 mm; stamens flanking median antesepalous staminodes staminodial, linear to narrowly spatulate, apices acute; filaments of outermost fertile stamen linear and dorsiventrally flattened, filaments of inner stamens terete. Ovary inferior; style 5.8 -7.4 mm, stigmas 3. Fruit capsule, cup-shaped, 5.5-10 x 5-9 mm, rounded basally, opening apically by 3 valves. Seeds pale gray with a whitish wing, leticular- ovoid, 2.4 -2.7 x 2-2.1 wide; testa reticulate, seed coat aniticlinal cell walls straight to slightly arced, central papillae 8-14 per cell.

description: Arbor usque ad 6 m alta. Folia decidua; lamina oblanceolata vel elliptica-oblongata, 2-7 cm longa, l- 2.5 cm lata, apice obtusa vel rotunda, saepe reticulata, basi decurrente; petiolo 2-4(-6) cm longo. Inflorescencia terminalis, cymosa, densiflora. Flos calyce campanulata, 3 mm longo; corolla alba, campanulata, 15-17 mm longa, 5-lobata, lobulis 4 mm longis; staminibus 5, filamentos dense hirsuta. Fructus drupaceus, 4-6 mm latus, maturitate intra calyceum accrescentem, 5 mm longum omnino inclusus.

description: Leggy, glabrous plants, internodes 7-10 cm long, straight and erect, each innovation of one internode terminating in a whorl of three leaves, between which the apex aborts. Leaves to 13x6 cm, thin, lanceolate, apex rounded-obtuse, base acutely tapering into 5 mm long, indistinct petiole; venation  pinnate, the midrib nearly running into the apex. Inflorescence on older, swollen nodes, from all around the node, which becomes corky; inflorescence dyadic, its peduncle, dyad peduncles, and floral pedicels 6-8 mm long, bracts and cupules ca. 4 mm wide, the latter fimbriate margined. Bud to 9 cm long, more or less straight, including the cylindri- cal, 3.5x2.5 mm ovary with somewhat fimbriate calyculus; bud apex acute. Petals 8.5 cm long, isomorphic, lacking basal ligule. Stamens nearly isomorphic; anthers acicular, 15-16 mm long, upper and lower anther lobes 2 mm apart at the base, apex needle  like; filament 20 mm, confluent with, and of the same thickness as, the anther, finely tuberculate at the base, as on the adjacent petals for some distance downward. Stigma poorly differentiated, nearly smooth. Fruit not known.

description: Shrub or tree 3-8 loosely spiral, sometimes petiole 5.5-11.0 cm thin longitudinal ribs petiolule 4-7 mm elliptic-lanceolate, olive-abaxially, glabrous mature 21-32x7.5-13.2 cm (L/W=2.0-2.5), the base widely cunéate, the apex acuminate, the margin more or less entire, the lateral nerves 27-33, prominent beneath, brochidodromous, the submarginal nerve 3-7 mm from the margin. Inflorescence pseudoracemose, axillary to leaves near apex of branch or sometimes also extra-axillary and encircling nodes (as in type), to 8 mm long, glabrous, the main axis 3-4 mm long with persistent bracts ±ovate to lanceolate and 0.5-1.5 mm long, the seconary axes 0.5 -0.8 mm long, crowded by 2 opposite lanceolate floral bracts 0.5 -0.7 mm long. Pedicels 1 mm long. Flower with calyx of 4 sepals, these connate in lower half, 0.6 -0.9 x 0.8-1.0 mm, brown - puncate and papillose (when fresh) abaxially, glabrous, the lobes ovate to usually deltoid; petals 4, oblong, ca 3.0 x 1.7 mm, rounded at apex, subhyaline at margin, cream and erect at anthesis, pinnatinerved adaxially, the distal 2/3 brown puncate abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 6, the filaments free, ca. 2mm long, inserted at base of ovary, complanate, granulose, glabrous, the anthers ca. 0.8 x 0.5 mm, elliptic, papillose (when fresh) positioned just above stigma;  ovary somwhat ovoid, ca. 0.8 x 0.6 mm, verruculose, glabrous, on a short and stout gynophore ca. 0.6 x 0.5 mm; stigma conical, fleshy - papillose (when fresh). Drupes unknown.

description: Large canopy tree to 35 m tall, cm diam., glabrous. Bole cylindrical, ing high up to 20 m, base swollen, often straight, robust and rounded buttresses 0.5 m high. Bark greyish and smooth young individuals, flaking in rectangular irregular patches in adult trees, reddish slash, exudating a whitish-translucent branches spreading into a dense crown. Leaves paripinnate, crowded at the end of branches, yellowish when young, (40- )60- 115 cm long; petiole 12-28 cm long, base swollen, generally with 2 nectaries; rachis (30-)43-90 cm long, glabrous; leaflets opposite, 6-13 pairs, petiolules 1-2 cm long, lamina of basal pairs of leaflets 9-20 x 5- 10 cm, apical pairs up to 16-56 x 4.5-13 cm, oblong, discolorous, apex rounded to broadly acute, mucronate, the muero flattened laterally, thick and spatulate, glandular, base cunéate to rounded, slightly asymmetrical, midrib prominent beneath, with 8-20 secondary veins on each side, tertiary venation loose and flat. Inflorescences pendulous thyrses, in groups of 6-10 at the end of branches, in axils of undeveloped leaves up to 3 cm long, (35)60-100(120) cm long, very much ramified, lower branches up to 15 cm long, transversely scurfy; peduncle 8-14 cm long. Flowers 1-3, born in axil of a 1 mm long, scaly bract; (4)5-merous, pedicel (1.5- )2 - 3.5 mm long, often angular in section and transversely scurfy; calyx green, lobes nar- rowly triangular to broadly ovate, 1-1.5 mm long, margins ciliolate; petals whitish to yellow-green, free to the base, oblong or obovate, 4- 6 x 2-3.5 mm; staminal tube white, urceolate, 3.5-5 mm long, ca. 4 mm diam., with 10 truncate or more or less emarginate lobes; anthers or antherodes 10, oblong, sessile, alternating with lobes, included with- in the tube, ca. 0.7 x 0.4 mm in carpellate flowers, 0.7-0.9x0.4-0.6 mm in staminate flowers; nectary cushion-shaped, white, 0.7- 1.3x2-3 mm; ovary 5-locular, ovoid to globose in carpellate flowers, 1-1.7 x 1.5- 1.8 mm, conical in staminate flowers, 0.6 - 1.5 x 0.5-1.3 mm; ovules 4 per loculus; style less than 0.7 mm long in carpellate flowers, 1-1.5 mm long in staminate flowers; stigma discoid, yellow, 1.4 - 2mm diameter. Fruit a capsule, green when immature, becoming brown at maturity, globose to ovoid 7-11 x 6-17 cm, apex often conspicuously acuminate; valves with more or less developped warty excrescences and numberous extrafloral nectaries, seeds 2.5 - 4.8 x 3 - 5.5 cm, up to 4 per valve; hilum oval, 4.5 -12 x 1.5 - 6mm; testa brown and smooth. seedlings; epicotyl 30-50 cm tall, the first leaves simple, blades discolorous, the adaxial surface pale greyish green, bright.

description: Small-leaved plants, internodes mostly 1.5-2.5 cm long (the lowest ones on innovations to 4 cm), angular when young, becoming terete, finely brown-furfuraceous when young. Phyllotaxy irregularly paired to alternate; leaves to 3*1.5 cm, obovate, apex deeply notched, with strongly developed, acute tooth projecting in abaxial direction; venation more or less palmate, with several strong, low, lateral veins, the midvein running into the tooth. Dioecious. Inflorescence to 3 mm long, peduncle 1 mm, (perhaps always) determinate, solitary in leaf axils, made up of a nearly capitate cluster of 5-7 flowers crowded below a very short terminal internode with 1 flower; each lateral flower subtended by 1 short, acute bract and 2 small bracteoles fused with the bract, this fused structure later forming a united, shallowly toothed cupule investing the base of the fruit. Female flower 2 mm long, equally divided between the cylindrical ovary and the 4 isomorphic petals, which lack vestigial anthers but bear an almost indiscernible slight thickening on the upper petal; style somewhat shorter than the petals, stigma distinct, capitate. Fruit 4x2 mm, narrowly ovoid, embryo 2 mm long, made up mostly of 2 flat cotyledons. Male plants unknown. Known only from type.

description: Robust, golden yellow or yellowish-green plants, glabrous or nearly so, dichotomous with innovation of 1 main internode each, internodes to 11 cm long, stout, terete. Basal cataphylls 1 pair, 4-8 mm above the base, tubular, shallowly bifid. Leaves to 8 x 5 cm somewhat leathery, blade broadly elliptical, apex very broadly rounded, base truncate to nearly acute, petiole 1 cm, distinct; venation more or less pinnate but nearly obscure. Dioecious. Male inflorescence apparently only terminal, to nearly 11 cm long, peduncle simple, 1-2 cm long, followed by 3-6 fertile internodes, the lowest one to 3.5 cm long and bearing to 60 flowers per fertile bract, regularly triseriate. Females plants unknown.

description: Medium-sized, glabrous, pendent plants, internodes to 10 cm long, flattening to 7 mm just below the nodes. Basal cataphylls 1-3 pair, the lowest (or single) pair to 4 mm above the base, the upper sterile internode to 12 mm long. Leaves to 12.5(-15) x3 cm, very thin, ovate or lanceolate to somewhat falcate, apex tapering but ultimately more or less rounded, base acutely long-tapering to indis- tinct, slender petiole 8-10 mm long; venation pinnate, with 2 conspicuous low lateral veins. Dioecious, sterile internode 1, 4-5 mm long flowers triseriate. Male inflorescence to 4cm long, very slender, fertile internodes 4(-5), flowers minute, to 25 per fertile internode, < 1 mm in diameter. Female inflorescence to 3.5 cm long, fertile internodes 3-7, flowers 4- 18 per fertile bract. Fruit 2mm diam, globose, petals closed.

description: Profusely branched plants, somewhat succulent. Internodes 1-3 cm long, terete, densely covered with broad - based, tapered trichomes. Basal cataphylls absent but prophylls prominent, acute, bearing short unicellular hairs; basal foliar organs median in position; Leaves to 1 x 1 cm, orbicular to slightly elliptical, petiole 1 mm, stout; venation obscure, margin smooth, leathery. Monoecious. Inflorescence to 2.5 cm long, peduncle 6-8 mm long, simple, followed by 1 or 2 fertile internodes; flowers to 14 per fertile bract, uniseriate, deeply recessed. Fruits ca. 2x 1.5 mm, ellipsoid, white, petals erect.

description: Rather small, densely leafy plants, glabrous except for sparse, minute epidermal papillae on the stem; internodes 2-4 cm long, terets; basal cataphylls absent, prophylls very inconspicuous. Leaves to 4 x 1.5 cm, lanceolate, apex more of less acute, vase acute, petiole 2-3 mm long, fairly distinct; venation obscure except for a median vein, which is apparently flanked by 2 lateral, basal veins. Dioescious. Female Inflorescence ca. 7 mm long at anthesis, doubling in fruiting; peduncle  3-8 mm long, simple, slender; fertile internodes 2. Flowers mostly 1, sometimes 2 per fertile bract, uniseriate. Fruit 4.5x3.5 mm, ovoid, petals closed and surface verrucose when dry. Male plants unknown.

description: Shrubs 1.5-2.5 m tall. Branchlets with continuous growth, young branchlets brown, sparsely to densely tomentose, rhytidome absent, old branchlets gray to brown, glabrous to glabrescent. Leaves evenly distributed along the branchlets; petioles 1-6 x 0.8- 1 mm; lamina (l.l-)2-5.2 x (0.6-)l-2.3 cm, chartaceous, plane, elliptic to narrowly ellip- tic, base acute to attenuate, apex slightly caudate or rounded, adaxial surface glabrous to glabrescent, venation raised to flat, brochi- dodromous, secondary veins 5-8 pairs, diverging from the primary vein 30-60°, aréoles 0.1-0.3 mm diam., abaxial surface glabrous, glabrescent, to sparsely pubescent at the base, venation raised, rarely flat, with domatia irregularly circular to elliptic, totally open, densely pubescent, rarely absent. Cataphylls absent. Inflorescences 2.1-6 cm long, botryoid, in the axils of the leaves, rarely extra-axillary, stems sparsely tomentose. Flowers bisexual, 4-8 mm long; pedicels 1- 4 mm long; receptacle 0.7-2 x 1.3-2.2 mm, outer surface sparsely pubescent, inner surface densely pubescent; tepals 6, 1.3-2.5 x (0.8-) 1-1.6 mm, elliptic, obovate, ovate, to oblong, adaxial side sparsely pilose-papillose, abaxial side glabrous, glabrescent, to sparselt pubescent at the base; stamens 9; whorls I and II 1-1.6 mm long, filaments 0.3-0.6 mm long, sparsely pubescent, anthers 0.6-0.9 x 0.5-0.7 mm, elliptic, apex 0.05-0.1 mm long, acute to obtuse, sparsely papillose, upper and lower pollen sacs introrse, whorl III 1-1 .6 mm long, filaments 0.5-0.9 mm long, sparsely pubescent, anthers 0.5-0.7 x 0.5-0.7 mm, oblong to trapeziform, apex emarginate to truncate, glabrous to sparsely papillose, upper pollen sacs latrorse, lower pollen sacs extrorse to latero-extrorse, glands paired at the base of whorl III stamens, staminodia 3 (whorl IV), 0.6-1 mm long, sparsely to densely pubescent, davate to fusiform; ovary 1-1.3 mm long, ellipsoid, style (0.1-)0.3-0.7 mm long. Only immature fruits and cupules seen. Cupules hemispheric, margin single, tepals deciduous. Fruits ellipsoid.

description: Sparsely branched plant, young stems more or less terete, densely covered in furfuraceous material produced in irregular, cone - like protuberances. Internodes to 2 cm long. Leaves to 4.5 x 2.5 cm, ovate to elliptical, lower midrib and margins prominently brown - furfuraceous, apex rounded, petiole 3 mm long; venation obscure, probably pinnate. Inflorescence essentially sessile, to 1 cm long, producing to 6 pairs of lowers or fruits. flowers hexamerous, dark red. Bracteoles flat, shiny, dark, scarcely reaching the margin of the  floral depression. Petals dimorphic; anthers with 2 pollen sacs, lower anthers with prominent connectival horn, upper ones blunt. Style 0.5 mm long, bright red, stigma clavate. Fruit 2.5 x 2mm, globose, very slightly tuberculate, apex truncate.

description: Caules plus minusve teretes, novelli maniifeste furfuracei; internodia usque ad 2 cm. Folia ca. 4.5 x 2.5 cm, lamina ovata vel elliptica, petiole 3 mm longo. Inflorescentia axillaris, isquie ad 1 cm, floribus vulgo 6-8. Stamina dimorpha, thecis 2. Fructus ca. 2.5 x 2 mm, globosus.

description: Shrub ca. 1 m tall. Branchlets with rhyth- mic growth, young branchlets brown, sparse to densely sericeous, rhytidome absent, old branchlets brown, glabrous. Leaves clustered on the tips of branchlets; petiole 2-4 x 2- 3.2 mm or absent, lamina (3-)5-9.2 x (1.3-) 2-3.5 cm, coriaceous, plane, narrowly ellip- tic, obovate, rarely ovate, base acute, apex acute to obtuse, rarely slightly caudate or rounded, adaxial surface glabrous, venation raised, flat, or sunken, brochidodromous, abaxial surface glabrous, venation raised, secondary veins 6-10 pairs, diverging from the primary vein 30-60°, aréoles 0.1-0.5 mm diam., without domatia. Cataphylls 1-6 x 1- 3 mm, abaxial side densely sericeous. Inflor- escences 3.3-9.3 cm long, botryoid to thyr- soid, in the axils of cataphylls or leaves, to extra-axillary, stems sparsely pubescent. Flowers bisexual, 4-7 mm long; pedicel 2- 4 mm long; receptacle 0.8-1 x 1.2-2 mm, outer surface sparse to densely pubescent, inner surface densely pubescent; tepals 1.5 - 2.5 x 1-1.5(-2) mm elliptic, ovate to obovate, adaxial side glabrous, glabrescent to sparsely papillose at the apex, abaxial side sparsely to densely pubescent to sericeous; stamens 9: whorls I and II 1.2-1.5(-1.8) mm long, filaments 0.5-0.7 mm long, sparsely pubescent, anthers 0.5-0.8(-l) x 0.4- 0.7 mm, elliptic, glabrous to sparsely papil- lose, apex 0.1-0.2 mm long, rounded to obtuse, upper pollen sacs introrse, lower pollen sacs introrse to latero-introrse, whorl III 1.4- 1.5(- 1.7) mm long, filaments 0.7- 0.8 mm long, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, anthers 0.7-0.8 x 0.4-0.5 mm, oblong to elliptic, glabrous, rarely sparsely papillose, apex truncate, emarginate to rounded, upper pollen sacs latrorse, lower pollen sacs latero- extrorse, paired glands at the base of whorl III stamens, staminodia 3 (whorl IV), 0.7-0.9 mm long, filiform to slightly davate, sparse to densely pubescent; ovary 0.8- 1.2(- 1.5) mm long, ellipsoid, style (0.4-)0.6-l mm long. Cupules and fruits not seen.

description: Plantae percurrentes, paribus basalibus cataphyllorum ad 6, paribus intercalaribus cataphyllorum 4, intemodiis teretibus. Folia ca. 13x5 cm, ovato-elliptica, palmatinervia. Infructescentiae usque ad 8 cm longae, intemodiis fertilibus 5-7, quaque bractea fertili ad 13 flores subtendente, floribus triseriatis. Fructus 4 x 3 mm, ovoidus, petalis clausis.

description: Large, percurrent plants, branches 1 m or more long. Internodes to 5 cm long, terete. Intercalary cataphylls 1-4 pairs between successive leaf pairs, basal cataphylls ca. 6 pairs; all scale leaves, including those of the inflorescences, large, yellowish, conspicuously bifid, and somewhat tubular. Highest cataphylls at, or well above, the middle of the interfoliar portion. Leaves to 13 cm x 5 cm, ovate to elliptical, apex obtuse, base nearly acute, petiole rather stout and distinct, ca. 4 mm long; venation more or less palmate, with at least 5 conspicuous veins, the median one reaching the apex. Dioecious; Female inflorescence ca. 4.5 cm long at anthesis, reaching to 8 cm in fruit; peduncle 8-12 mm long, with 3-5 sterile internodes; fertile internodes 5-7, flowers 10-13 per fertile bract, triseriate, immersed in the inflorescence axis. Fruit 4x3 mm, ovoid, pale yellow, petals closed. Male plant unknown.

description: Large, glabrous, percurrent plants, internodes to 10 cm long, terete below and somewhat compressed above. Basal cataphylls 2-4 pairs, the lowest pair 1-2 mm long, the uppermost pair ca. 2.5 cm above the base. Leaves to 17x6 cm, lanceolate to narrowly ovate, apex long-tapering, base acute, tapering into flat, indistinct petiole ca. 1.5 cm long; venation palmate, usually with 5 major veins. Probably  monoecious. Inflorescence to 5cm long, peduncle 3-4 mm long, simple; fertile internodes 6 or 7, flowers to 18 per fertile bract, triseriate or partly so, the distal fertile bracts with 4 flowers. Fruit 7 x 5mm, ellipsoid, petals closed. Known only from the type.

description: Plants epiphytic. Pseudobulbs elliptic, unifoliate, with numerous sheathing leaves. Leaves lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 8-30 cm long, 1.4-3.5 cm wide, short acumi- nate. Inflorescence almost as long as the leaves, 3-10 flowered. Floral bracts 1.0-2.0 cm long, 0.5 cm wide when spread, papery, usually not quite the length of the pedicel. Pedicel 0.9-1.1 cm long. Flowers open, floral parts spreading or reflexed. Sepals all alike, 1.3-2.0 cm long, 0.2-0.3 cm wide, lanceolate, acuminate, slightly reflexed. Petals similar to the sepals, 0.9-1.5 cm long, 0.15-0.30 cm wide, slightly reflexed, lanceolate, acuminate. Lip elliptic-lanceolate, 0.8-1.1 cm long, 0.3-0.45 cm wide, usually reflexed at the middle, the base enclosed by the base of the column which also hides the base of the callus. Callus of two fleshy curving lamellae which converge at their apices to form a cup, terminated by two tooth-like masses. Column short, stout, quite enlarged basally, 0.4-0.5 cm high. Viscidium ovate, stipe obdeltoid, apical mar- gin of stipe entire or apiculate, pollinia reniform-obovate, surface rugose, ventral groove present. Panama, Costa Rica, Nicaragua (?), at elevations of 1000-2000 meters.

description: Pseudobulbs long elliptic. Leaves numerous, long lanceolate-linear, 8-40 cm long, 0.5-1.6 cm wide. Inflorescence length variable, longer or shorter than the leaves. Floral bracts broadly lanceolate, 0.8-1.2 cm long, 0.2-0.5 cm wide, usually slightly longer than the pedicel, the pedicel 0.6-1.4 cm long. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, 0.8-1.3 cm long, 0.2-0.3 cm wide, lateral sepals 1.3-1.6 cm long, 0.15-0.25 cm wide, linear- lanceolate, slightly channelled along the inner surfaces. Petals broadly lanceolate, rarely slightly falcate, 0.7-1.1 cm long, 0.15-0.25 cm wide. Lip elliptic-lanceolate, 0.5-1.0 cm long, 0.4-0.5 cm wide, usually reflexed at or slightly beyond the middle. Callus of two converging lamellae, terminated by two tooth-like apical masses. Column enlarged at the base, 0.4-0.5 cm high. Viscidium ovate, stipe obdeltoid, the apex divided, pollinia flattened reniform. Colombia, Ecuador, Peru.

description: Shrub or treelet to 5 m. Branchlets erect patent, gray to dark brown or blackish, the lenticels circular. Cataphylls persistent, black, similar to stipules. Stipules triangular, not striated, 0.9-1.5 mm long, subcoriaceous, the apex obtuse, 1-3 terminal setae ca. 0.2 mm long, usually persistent in mature stipules, the margin entire. Leaves often grouped at apex of shoots. Petiole 2.8-7.4 mm long, 0.75 mm in diameter, strongly canaliculate at the base. Lamina elliptic, ovate or obovate, 4.5-8.6 x 2.3-4.5 cm, firmly membranaceous, the apex obtuse or rounded, the base acute to obtuse, the margin plane or slightly revolute, drying adaxially dark brown or green, drying abaxially pale brown to pale green, without vernation lines; midrib adaxially slightly impressed at the base, abaxially prominent, pale green to reddish; secondary veins 8-11, prominent on both faces; reticulations prominulous on both faces. Flowers in axils of previous  season's cataphylls, 1-4 at each node. Bracteoles triangular, keeled, 0.6-1.2 mm long, membranaceous, the apex acute, the margin entire. Pedicel pentagonal in cross section, 4.5-6.5 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm in diameter at medial zone, at anthesis slightly thickened at the apex. Calyx 1.5-1.75 mm long, divided ca. 1/2 its length; lobes triangular, the apex acute or acuminate, the inner surface papillate, the margin entire. Petals lamina ovate, cuculate, acute to obtuse at apex, 1.9-2.2x1.1-1.3 mm, the claw ca. 0.3x1.2 mm, the ligule bilobed, ca. 1 mm long, each lobe consisting of a short anterior auricle and a large posterior auricle, the posterior two auricules ca. 0.7 mm long, triangular, acute at apex, entire or erose at margin, the anterior two auricules ca. 0.4 mm long, triangular, the apex obtuse, the margin entire. Staminal cup slightly longer than the calyx, margin crenate or entire, with a small appendage between the posterior lobes. Longistylous flowers: antisepalous filaments 1.7-2.1 mm long; antipetalous filaments 1-1.2 mm long; anthers oblong, ca. 0.6x0.5 mm; styles free, ca. 3.5 mm long; stigmas depressed- capitate. Brevistylous flowers unknown. Drupe ellipsoid to ovoid, 6-7 mm long, 3- 4 mm in diameter; endocarp terete, 1-locular.

description: Shrubs ca. 1.5 m tall; branchlets terete, smooth, glabrous. Leaves alternate; blades elliptic, 13-14.2x5-5.5 cm, chartaceous, the base cuneate, the margins slightly undulate, the apex acute to slightly acuminate, the adaxial and abaxial leaf surfaces glabrous; secondary veins conspicuous; petioles slightly canaliculate, 10- 16 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences ramiflorous and axillary, fasciculate, 1-1.5 cm long, glabrous; pedicels terete, 3.5-4 mm long, glabrous. Staminate flowers 4- merous, 3-3.5 mm long; caylx erect 1.5- 1.7 mm, the sepals chartaceous, ovate, 0.8 - 1 x 0.5 - 0.6 mm, margins erose, apex rounded; corolla campanulate, 2.8- 3.3 mm long, the tube ca. 0.5mm long with papillae on the inner surface; corolla lobes membranous, elliptic, 2-2.2 x 1.2 -1.4 mm, symmetric, apically obtuse, glabrous, apparently non punctate, margins entire; stamens 2.1 - 2.4 mm long, the filaments inserted basally on the corolla tube, 0.9 - 1.1 mm long, the anthers oblong, 1.2 -1.6 x 0.6-0.9 mm, basally cordate, apically obtuse and apiculate, dehiscent by short longitudinal slits with dilated apical pores; pistilode absent. Bizexual flowers and fruits not observed.

description: Treelet 3-4 m tall, branched. Branches cylindrical, brown to grayish, with longitudinal grooves, glabrous. Leaves alternate, 1-foliolate, forming congested groups at the apex of the branches; petioles 0.6-7.0 cm long, cylindrical, thickened at base and apex, glabrous; blades elliptic, narrowly elliptic, lanceolate or oblan- ceolate, the base abruptly and veiy narrowly attenuate to the swelling, the apex acute, rounded or acuminate, 10-21x2.7-7.5 cm, chartaceous to slightly coriaceous, glabrous, with sparse pellucid dots (volatile oil glands) visible when against a light; venation brochidodromous, midvein plane to slightly sunken adaxially, prominent abaxially, secondary veins 9-18, alternate to subopposite. Inflorescence an erect, terminal thyrse, 8-19 cm long; peduncle cylindrical or complanate, puberulent; secondary axes up to 9 cm long, usually branched, puberulent; primary and secondary bracts triangular, 1-2 mm long, puberulent abaxially; pedicels 0.5 - 3mm long in flower, 3-5 mm long in fruit. Bus oblong at anthesis. Caylx creamy white, shortly campanulate, 1-2 mm long, puberulent mainly at margin, deciduous, the lobes 5 ovate-triangular, ca. 1.5x1.5 mm, each with a globose nectary at the apex. Corolla white with a subtle lilac spot at the tip of the abaxial surface of the petals (only seen in living buds and flowers), the petals 5, free, imbricate, 1.3-1.7x0.2-0.3 cm, spatulate, abaxially swol- len, tomentose-villous at both surfaces, the base adaxially glabrous, with many glands abaxially. Androecium of 3 fertile stamens and 2 stamin- odes; filaments free from each other and free from the corolla, 8-10 x 1-2 mm, abaxially swollen, tomentose-villous at both surfaces, adaxially with a tuft of trichomes on the median region and glabrous on below half, the stamin- odes 11-14x0.5-1 mm, tomentose-villous, the median region with a tuft of trichomes adax- ially, the apex glandular; anthers linear-oblong, ca. 2.5 X 1 mm, abaxially villous; disc cupular, ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous. Pollen in monads, isopolar, of medium size (44.27-52.39 'xm , mean 47.70 µm ±2.22 µm), with radial symmetiy, amb circular, pantocolporate; ectoaperture colpate, endoaperture circular, exine homobrochate, microreticulate (muri and lumina smaller than 1 цт, Fig. 2B). Carpels 5, free; ovary ca. 1 mm long, sericeous, apically tapered into the style; style single, 6-11 mm long, pubescent, glabrous at base; stigma 5-lobed. Fruit a schizocarp of 1-2, rarely 3-5 free mericarps, these subglobose, 0.8-1.2 x 0.7-1 cm, brown, rugose, sparsely puberulent to glabrescent, with dehiscence along ventral suture; endocarp woody, yellowish, splitting into two valves when mature. Seed 1 per carpel, reniform, ca. 8x 6 mm, brown to nigrescent, smooth, glabrous, the testa leathery, hilum oblate. Mature embryo not seen.

description: Evergreen shrubs to ca. 7 m tall, taprooted, at least when young, the roots with methyl salicylate (wintergreen odor), with one or a few trunks at ground level, sometimes reaching a diameter of ca. 1 dm although usually much less, proximally branched and usually also much-branched above, with several main stems at breast height, dbh to 3(-5) cm (usually much less), the main stems erect with arching, spreading branchlets; wood very hard; bark pale brown to gray, fairly smooth except for numerous small fissures and lenticels; stems ca. 0.7 mm wide near second node from base on young lateral branches, 1-1.2 mm wide below the uppermost expanded inflorescence on the main stem, 1.7-2.3 mm wide near midpoint of main branch; internodes 3.7-9.2 mm long; young stems compressed, irregularly angled, terete with age; densely pubescent, the hairs concolorous with the brownish stem, to white or yellow; older stems glabrate. Hairs simple, unicellular, dense to sparse on nearly all parts, at least when young, generally in patches or zones on floral parts, mostly less than 0.1 mm long, antrorsely appressed to slightly spreading, tapering in the upper fourth to an acute apex, the surface with minute irregular bumps and small ridges (verrucae), infrequently 0.2-0.3 mm long, e.g., on the upper filament sheath, and then also slightly kinked or twisted. Leaves alternate, mostly distichous, exstipulate, simple, entire, coriaceous, isomorphic or sometimes dimorphic in shape and size on the same branch, nyctinastic, folding downward in the evening and, sometimes, on overcast days so that the abaxial surfaces on opposite sides of the stem touch; petiole 1.4-3 X 0.8 mm, often with very slight decurrent ridges from blade base, densely to moderately pubescent (to glabrate, in part); blade elliptic to ± oblong, slightly obovate, slightly ovate, often rhomboidal and somewhat asymmetric with a slightly different distance to the widest part on each side, 11- 24 x 10-15 mm, 7-10 mm from apex to widest point, usually flat to slightly abaxially cupped, shiny, wrinkled (on drying), coriaceous, the apex acute, sometimes abruptly apiculate (with apiculus 1-1.5 mm long), the base acute (margin forming an angle of ca. 40° with midvein at junction with petiole); margin slightly revolute, inrolled portion 0.2-0.3 mm wide basally and medially, to ca. 0.1 mm or plane apically, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, with 2-3 (-4) hairs per linear mm of blade tissue, hairs sometimes blackish on abaxial surface of lamina and appearing as dark punctations to the naked eye, although the punctations primarily result from a dark, shallow pit at the base of each hair; venation pinnate, brochidodromous, the midvein visible to apex (at least abaxially), with sparse appressed to slightly spreading hairs, usually with a prominent lateral secondary vein from the base on each side of the midvein (i.e., triplinerved) and 1-3 additional secondary veins per side that are generally relatively obvious when fresh, very slightly sunken above and raised below, not visible adaxially when dried, inconspicuous abaxially on most leaves, alternate near base of leaf to often opposite apically, when visible slightly raised to flush with the blade, darker than the blade, poorly branched and the loops not obvious on most leaves, the secondary-to-midvein angles 40-50°, the basal ones sometimes as shallow as 30°, the first non-basal secondary vein 3.4-5.5 mm from the base, 15-16.5 mm long. Inflorescences axillary racemes, although often reduced and fasciculate, at several consecutive nodes, usually subapical, sometimes with tiny buds in many or all of the upper nodes, and on many or all of the upper nodes of lateral branches, with 1 to ca. 12 flowers per inflorescence, but usually only 1 or 2 open at any one time, 5-9 x 6-9 mm; peduncles (0.3-)1.1-1.6(-2.8) mm long, densely hairy; with 2 small bracteoles (prophylls) subtending the peduncle, these persistent from bud, densely hairy, narrowly triangular, acute apically, 0.7-1.2 x 0.3 - 0.4 mm, shriveling and curling adaxially with age; a bract and 2 adjacent bracteoles at base of each pedicel, these triangular, blunt to acute apically, 0.4-0.6 x 0.4-0.5 mm, with hairs dense (sometimes sparse with age). Flowers complete, structurally perfect (but some flowers appear to be functionally imperfect with misshapen anthers and non- viable pollen; if there are flowers that are functionally staminate, the carpellode is not obviously different from a functional carpel), strongly zygomorphic, 3-4.5 mm long (excluding pedicels); pedicels 1.5-2.2 mm long, densely to moderately pubescent. Sepals 5, free, herbaceous, tardily deciduous (falling in young fruit, after the corolla, although the upper sepal is rarely persistent), ovate, green (when fresh), usually widest just above the rounded, slightly narrowed base, rounded to bluntly acute apically; the outer sepals (1 upper and 2 lower) subequal, 1-1.8 x 0.8-1.1 mm, sparsely pubescent on both sides, densest near the midvein, especially near the apex, marginally ciliolate to ciliate; the 2 inner, lateral sepals (wings) ca. 1/3 longer than the outer sepals and much smaller than the petals, 1.4-2.4 x 1.1-1.5 mm, the margin ciliate hairs sometimes longer than on the outer sepals, 4 often denser on the lower edge. Petals 3, herbaceous, the 2 upper petals and the lower keel petal free from each other but basally fused to the filament sheath, so the corolla falling as a unit with the androecium shortly after fertilization; upper petals lingulate to narrowly ovate or oblong-elliptic, slightly shorter than or nearly equaling the keel, 2.1-3.8 x 0.6-1.3 mm, usually with the width nearly constant over most of the petal's length, although often not appearing so due to the tapered apex and apparent constriction near the middle, i.e., the narrowing in the middle of the upper petals usually results from the cupped, inrolled margins, and the petal being incurved in this region, but sometimes the middle portion actually 0.1-0.2 mm narrower than the parts above and below, the bases curved around the gynoecium, filament sheath, and keel base, fused to the lateral base of the filament tube, with the fused portion varying in depth (very shallow near the base of the upper corner, angling diagonally to ca. 1/3 the total length along the lower edge), the bases of the upper petals effectively capping the basal portion of the upper edge of the filament sheath, the apical portion of the upper petals often cupped and marginally inrolled, at anthesis curving out (toward the base of the flower), tapering fairly abruptly to a bluntly acute apex, the margins inrolled, subentire to minutely erose, ciliate, the upper petals basally green, apically white to yellow or yellowish green, densely pubescent adaxially, nearly glabrous at the apex, abaxially sparsely pubescent; keel petal conduplicate, with the halves folded upward around the androecium and gynoecium, bluntly wedge-shaped, widest near the blunt apex, without a beak or crest, 2.6-4.2 x 1 .2-2 mm, and up to 1 mm across, especially at full anthesis when the lateral pouches flare out, green basally, white or yellowish-green along the upper margins, at least with age; the keel with three non-discrete zones, the laterally compressed apex, often white or yellowish- green, the medial region with poorly developed lateral "pouches" or folds, i.e., apically undulate, expanded projections, and the reduced, narrow, semi-tubular basal region; the pubescence varies from dense lateral patches of appressed hairs to fairly sparse or even glabrous on portions of the surface abaxially with spreading hairs near the base and also adaxially in the upper apical fold; the basal portion of the keel fused to the lower filament sheath for 0.4- 0.7 mm, sometimes with the zone of adnation fairly loose in parts, the upper margin subentire to minutely erase near the apex, undulate, the basal margin ciliate. Stamens 8, 2.2-3.9 mm long; filaments fused into an adaxially-split, strongly laterally compressed sheath around the gynoecium, the sheath 1.5-3.2 mm long, 0.6- 1.3 mm tall near the base (flaring at the very base to ca. 1.8 mm), 0.4-0.6 mm tall near the apex, the free apical portion of each filament 0.2-0.8 x 0.05-0.15 mm, the outermost, i.e., lowest, earliest diverging, filaments tend to be longer and wider, the adaxial upper filament sheath and free filaments densely covered in long (0.2-0.3 mm) spreading, ± wrinkled, mostly strongly compressed to subterete hairs (sterile anthers sometimes with only a few scattered short hairs), adaxially glabrous near the base, abaxially hairy in patches near the base and along the margins to ± glabrous elsewhere; the anthers bisporangiate, apparently unithecal from developmental suppression of the ventral sporangia, 0.35-0.9 x 0.1-0.3 mm, each anther opening by an apical pore, the open pore up to ca. 0.3 mm across; rarely with 2 adjacent anthers semi-fused, i.e., sharing a common filament and appearing as a 2-lobed anther. Pollen polycolporate, with 8(9) apertures. Gynoecium 2-2.5 mm long in flower; stipe 0.15-0.3 x 0.1 mm; nectar disk small, at base of stipe; ovary bicarpellate and bilocular, laterally compressed, flattened-ellipsoid, ca. 0.6-0.9 x 0.5-0.6 mm (width perpendicular to central axis), pubescent along margins with appressed to ascending hairs less than 0.1 mm long (sometimes nearly glabrous), these largely deciduous in fruit; placentation axile, with a single ovule per carpel, attached apically along the central axis by a relatively stout funiculus; style 1, apically curved, 1.2-1.5 x 0.15-0.3 mm, ca. 0.7-0.9 mm from apex of the ovary to where upward curvature begins, the style curvature to ca. 0.65-1 mm deep, and style positioned well below the anthers at anthesis to slightly surpassing them (especially in flowers with apparently non-functional stamens), elongating so that the stigmas are eventually held subequal to slightly surpassing the anthers, to 2-3 times as long as the ovary, deciduous in fruit; stigmas 2, depressed capitate, the abaxial one (associated with the lower carpel) apical (as a result of style curvature), the adaxial one subapical and slightly smaller, the stigmatic regions very closely spaced, ca. 0.1 mm high. Infructescences with only 1-2 fruits each; prophylls, bracts, bracteoles, and pubescence of peduncle and pedicels persistent in fruit, the upper sepal rarely also persistent; fruiting peduncles 0.3 - 1.4mm long, most infructescences nearly sessile. Fruits laterally flattened capsules, obcordate, obdeltoid, to quadrate, somewhat coriaceous, the valves dehiscing toward the central axis, often with one locule aborted, i.e., underdeveloped and with no seed, and then with a lopsided oblong shape, 13-16 mm long (including stipe), with an apical sinus between the carpels, the sinus depth 0.2-0.3 mm, but many fruits with a blunt triangular projection at the mid-apex so that the sinus is elevated up to ca. 1 mm above tops of the lobes, the base with a triangular flange of tissue up to ca. 1 mm long, the fruit margin not conspicuously winged, but once fruit splits, a winged flange, 0.5-0.9 mm wide, is evident outside the suture zone, the epidermis nearly glabrous, sometimes with a few scattered minute appressed hairs, especially on the stipe or along fruit margin, the hairs most common and obvious along the open suture; stipe 1.6-2.7 x 0.5-0.6 mm (width at midpoint); capsule body 7.5-11 x 8.5-12 mm, taller than wide when one-seeded, mostly wider than tall when two-seeded (although sometimes nearly isodiametric), the long axis of the ovary lobes mostly angled outward, up to about 1 mm longer than the capsule length; fruiting pedicel 2.5-3 x O.6-0.7 mm, the floral receptacle persisting as a swollen, knobby area, paler than pedicel and stipe, 0.5-0.8 mm long. Seeds typically oblong-ellipsoid (rarely, and presumably aberrantly, bluntly triangular), laterally compressed, bluish-black at maturity, glabrous, 6—6.5 x 4-4.6 mm, 1-1.5 mm thick, bluntly rounded at the chalazal end, acute at the funicular end and covered by a fleshy orange aril; aril glabrous with 2 main lobes, one on each side of the seed, each lobe with smaller, irregular lobes, 2.5-3 mm tall near funiculus to 1.5 mm tall distally, 4.2-5 mm wide (narrower apically above the funiculus), the lower margin with 2-3 shallow lobes (fitting into grooves of the indented scar at apex of seed), the exposed funiculus 0.5 mm long, the seed persistent in fruit (presumably bird dispersed); germination from a very thin walled section at the funicular end; seed coat relatively thin, embryo straight, endosperm lacking at maturity, hypocotyl and radicle poorly differentiated, cotyledons ovate, fleshy (apparently for storage), nearly flat with the margins cupped, overlapping, and tightly adherent around the embryonic first leaves.

description: Perennial, hemicryptophytic, rosulate herbs about 4 cm tall and 10 cm in diam., stem not or barely branched. Leaves alternate, spatulate, 1-5 cm long, partially fleshy, round at apex, attenuate at base into a petiole; the upper ones villous at the margin and particularly at the petiole base; petiole 0.5-3x0.1-0.5 cm, furrowed; blade ovate, 0.5-1.5x0.5-2 cm, surface aciculate with margin entire, sinuate. Peduncles shorter than the leaves, terete, furrowed, bearing only one terminal head each; usually with 1 or 2 central, thicker peduncles (1.5x 0.5 cm) bearing a larger inflorescence, and some lateral slender peduncles (2.5x0.15 cm), with medium size or small inflorescences. Involucre with 5 or 6 broad triangular lobules 0.3-0.7 cm long, villous maiginally. Receptacle convex, 0.53 cm in diam., accrescent, hemispherical during fruit maturation. Paleas linear to linear-spatulate, partially fleshy, scarcely villous at apex, persistent, 0.3-0.5 cm long in receptacles with flowers, to 1 cm long in receptacles with fruits. Flowers white, 30-300 per inflorescence. Calyx pentamerous, sepals with imbricate aestivation, foliose, obovate, uneven, maigin sinuate, 0.85x0.6 mm. Corolla infundibuliform with tube 1.75-1.96 x 0.6-0.8 mm, limb campanulate, 2.2-2.35 x 1.6-1.7 mm, with a slight constriction at the base; lobules valvate, triangular, uncinate, 1.2 x 0.8 mm. Staminal tube 2.3 mm long, inserted midlength on the corolla tube, nectary glands reduced, of median position; apical free filaments of 0.5 mm long. Anthers connate, 1 mm long. Style exserted, 4-5 mm (staminate phase) to 5.7-5.8 mm long (pistillate phase). Ovary terete, 1.3x0.5 mm. Achenes terete 5^1.5 mm, with 5 longitudinal, obtuse keels, and transverse wrinkles, terminating in a conical, conspicuous apiculum, 1.2-1.8 mm long, and crowned by the foliose, accrescent (4x2.5-3.3 mm), truncate, orbicular sepals. Seed 3.5 x 1 mm.

description: Perennial, hemicryptophytic, rosulate herbs about 4 cm tall and 1 1 in cm diam., stem not or barely branched. Leaves alternate, spatolate, 2-5.5 cm long, thick, glabrous; petiole 1-2.5x0.5 cm; limb 1.2-3x1-2 cm, margin crenate-mucronate, base cuneate-attenuate, apex obtuse; blade adaxial surface slightly aciculate, and nervation strongly marked on the abaxial surface. Peduncles shorter than the leaves, 1-2 cm long, terete, furrowed, bearing only one terminal head each; usually with only one central peduncle surrounded by 1-5 lateral ones, or the central inflorescence sessile. Involucre with 5-6 wide triangular lobules, 0.3-0.7x0.25-0.85 cm; lobes with apex obtuse to rounded, mucronate. Receptacle convex, 1-4 cm diam., accrescent, hemispherical during fruit ripening. Paleas few, very dispersed, linear-spatulate, mucronate, fleshy, glabrous, persistent, 0.3 cm long in receptacles with flowers, to 0.5 cm long in receptacles with fruits. Flowers 100-150 per inflorescence. Calyx pentamerous; lobules with imbricate aestivation, foliose, uneven, margin undulate, 1—2 x 1—1.15 mm. Corolla infundibuliform, 4-4.5 mm long; tube 1.852.2 x 0.7-1.2 mm; limb 2-2.5x1.2-2.35 mm, deeply cleft; lobules triangular, uncinate-cucullate, 1.6-2 x 0.8 mm, with a globose expansion at apex and valvate aestivation. Staminal tube 3 mm long, inserted at midlength on the corolla tube, with 5 oblong glands in the central portion, 1x0.25 mm, and distally ending in 5 minute free filaments. Anthers connate, 1.5 mm long. Style exserted, 2 mm long (staminate phase) to 5.5 mm long (pistillate phase). Ovary terete, 2-2.5x1-14 mm. Achenes prismatic, 4.5 x 2.5 mm, glabrous, smooth, or eventually developing some wrinkles; apiculum 0.4-0.6 mm long, with 5 longitudinal wings of rhomboid transverse section and acute margin, crowned by the accrescent sepals that are 1.5-2.6 x 1.11.25 mm, navicular, obtuse-mucronate, corky, with undulate margin. Seed 3x1 mm.

description: Terrestrial or epiphytic herb; stems dorsiventral, rarely to frequently branched, 20 - 40 cm tall, herbaceous, terete, glabrescent below, pilose above. Leaves membranaceous, opposite, distichous, unequal in a pair; larger leaf with petioles terete, 3-8 mm long, usually oblong, occasionally obovate, (6-) 10-15 x(2-)3-5 cm, base acute and asym- metrical, apex obtuse to rounded, margin crenate to serrate, adaxially pale green, uniformly pilose to densely pilose on veins and leaf margins, abaxially dark green, uniformly pilose; smaller leaf usually sessile or rarely petiolate, petiole terete, 1-3 (-5) mm long, blade ovate to orbicular, 5-13x2-5 mm, vestiture and coloration same as larger leaf. Inflorescences in upper leaf axils, usually sessile or rarely pedunculate, flowers terminally clustered (pseudoumbellate), 1-2 mature flowers/inflorescence, when present peduncle 2-4 mm long, often with remnant pedicel scars appearing gland-like; bracts absent; flowers sessile to pedicellate, when present pedicels 1-2 mm long; calyx lobes 5, fused for 2/3 of their length, equal, lobes erect during anthesis, persistent and spreading in fruit to form a splash cup to 5 mm wide in fruit, apex acute, uniformly green, outside pilose, inside glabrous; corolla to 5 mm long, tubular, base to mid-region 1 mm in diameter, becoming apically ventricose on lower side to 2 mm in wide at apex, throat appearing laterally compressed, inside mostly glabrous with gland-tipped trichomes near apex of throat, uniformly white or white suffused with red on upper region of throat, outside mostly glabrous at base to pilose near apex, uniformly white, limb bilaterally symmetri- cal, lobes reflexed and unequal, lower three lobes rotund, ca. 1x2 mm, upper two lobes rotund, 0.5x1 mm, margins serrulate; stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments adnate to base of corolla for 2 mm and free for 1-1.5 mm, glabrous; anthers broader than long, ca. 0.25 x 0.5 mm; style and stigma glabrous, ca. 1 x 0.25 mm, style and stigma glabrous. Fruit a dry 4 - valved capsule; seeds numerous, narrowly elliptic, ca. 0.3 x 0.2 mm, light brown, irregularly striate.

description: Arbores usque ad 30 m altae. Carapae guianensi valde affinis, sed ramis in inflorescentiae costis foliolorum, pedicellisque florum indumento dense farinoso praeditis, apicibus foliolorum rotundatis vel obtusis pedicellis 2-4 mm longis, loculis ovarii 6-ovulatis et seminibus minoribus hilis reductis ca 3 mm longis differt.  Tree to 30 m tall, 25(-53) cm dbh. Bole straight, cylindrical, up to 15 m long, but- tresses lacking; bark soft, smooth, becoming flaky on older trees, slash pink; branches spreading, arching upwards. Leaves 45- 95 cm long; petiole 10-28 cmx 0.5-0.8 cm, base swollen, generally with one nectary on each side of the abaxial surface; rachis 30- 70 cm long, glabrous; leaflets 6-10 pairs, the petiolules 0.5-2 cm long, densely farinose; basal leaflet 10-20x6-10 cm; ultimate pairs 19-36x6-10 cm, coriaceous, glabrous beneath, oblong to elliptic-oblong, the apex rounded to obtuse, mucronate, the base rounded, midrib prominent beneath, densely farinose; secondary veins 8-17 on each side, tertiary veins dense and ± raised beneath. Inflorescence in the axils of fully developed or reduced scale - like leaves, (20-) 40-60 cm long, erect to spreading, densely farinose; peduncle 11-24 cm long, lowermost branches up to 25 cm long. Flowers 4(5)-merous, pedicel 2-4 mm long, densely rusty farinose; sepals green, glabrous, lobes ca. 1 mm long; petals 4-6x2-5 mm, cream- white, glabrous to sparsely and finely farinose, with 1(2) nectaries towards the apex; staminal tube urceolate, 4-5.5 mm long, the lobes 0.8- 1.4 mm long, reflexed; anthers 0.7-0.9x0.5- 0.7 mm; antherodes ca. 0.5x0.4 mm; disk ca. 1 mm high, 2-3.5 mm diam, white; ovary 1.5-1.8x1.4-1.7 mm in carpellate flowers, 0.8-1.5x0.8-1.3 mm in staminate flowers; locules 6-ovulate, glandular; style ca. 1 mm long in carpellate flowers, 1-2 mm long in staminate flowers; stigma 1-1.5 mm in diam. Fruit 6-7x6-6.5 cm, globose, brown, 4- valved, each valve with a median rib, surface with numerous black nectaries. Seeds angu- lar, 2-3x2-3 cm wide, up to 6 per valve; hilum 3-7x2-3.5 mm; testa dark brown, smooth on the sides, edges rugose and wooly on the angles, often with numerous black glands.

description: Perennial herb, 8-17(-20) cm tall, caespitose or sometimes forming loose mats from a much-branched caudex, sometimes short rhizomes present, from a soft, woody taproot; herbage green, the stems often glandular puberulent above, the leaves glabrous or often finely scabrid-ciliolate below, rarely glabrous or glandular-puberulent throughout; sterile stems short, spreading to ascending, terminating in tight clusters of leaves; flowering stems erect, ascending, or decumbent, sparsely leafy; leaves best developed on the short shoots, these flexuous, herbaceous, and relatively long, (2.5-)2.8-5 cm long, 0.4- 0.6 mm wide, filiform, the apex acute, often soft-spinose, the leaves of the flowering stems in (1-)4 or more widely separated pairs, becoming reduced in length upwards; inflorescences usually terminal 3 -flowered cymes, sometimes compound cymes with 4 or more, rarely up to 15 flowers in exceptionally robust plants, the peduncles and pedicels sparsely to densely glandular-puber- ulent; bracts paired, much smaller than the subtending leaves, lanceolate to ovate, acute, mostly scarious; pedicels 2-22 mm long, straight; sepals glabrous or rarely sparsely glandular-puberulent on the herbaceous part, 1 -veined, sometimes 3 -veined, the lateral pair of veins and sometimes the midvein obscure, (4-)4.5-6.5 mm long, expanding to 7 mm in fruit, broadly lanceolate to ovate, the scarious margins broad, the apex obtuse to acute, sometimes spinose-tipped; petals white, 6-7.5(-8.5) mm long, about 1.2-1.3 times as long as the sepals, oblong to spatulate, the apex entire; stamens 10, the filaments 4.5-6.5 mm long, the anthers 0.6-0.7 mm long; styles 3, more or less erect, 3-4.6 mm long; nectaries small, fleshy, horizontally elongate, cup-shaped lobes at the outside base of the antisepalous filaments; capsules 4-7(-7.5) mm long, ovoid to elongate-ovoid, glabrous, opening by 6 recurved teeth, containing only a few seeds; seeds 1.9-2.4 mm long, obovoid, oblong, or comma-shaped, tuberculate on the rim and the sides with low, elongate tubercles, black to dark brown.

description: Small tree 3 m tall. Branchlets diverging 20-50° from axis, blackish, often lichenized, with trans versei and longitudinal striations. Cataphylls persistent along short shoots, similar to stipules. Stipules persistent, oblong triangular, 1.75-2.50 mm long, not striated, chartaceous, the apex acute, sometimes obtuse, with two caducous setae, these short and flattened, projecting from the keel, the margin entire. Leaves generally grouped at the apex of the shoot. Petioles canaliculate, the margin involute, 5-7 mm long. Lamina broadly obovate, 2.1-2.6x1.2-1.5 mm, thinly chartaceous, the apex rounded to emarginate, mucronate, the base cuneate, the margin flat or softly revolute, when dry adaxially dark brown, abaxially brown, without vernation lines; midrib greatly impressed adaxially, prominent and reddish abaxially; secondary veins and reticulations prominent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, generally in the leaf axils. Bracteoles 1-2 per flower, triangular, thinly coriaceous, 1 .2-2 mm long, dark brown, the apex obtuse, apiculate, the apicule persistent ca. 0.25 mm long, the keel patent, the margin membranaceous, sometimes fimbriate. Pedicel pentagonal, 1 .2-3 mm long, thickened at apex. Calyx 1.5-1.75 mm long, divided ca. 1/2 its length; lobes triangular, thickened, longitudinally striated, the apex acute with a pale projection on the inner surface (Fig. ID). Petal lamina more or less plane, ovate, the apex obtuse, ca. 2.5x1.5 mm, the claw obovate to oblong, ca. 2 X 1 .5 mm, the ligule ca. 1 mm long, bilobed, each lobe consisting of two auricles, these entire to crenate at margin, ca. 0.5 mm long; a short and swollen appendage between the auricles. Staminal cup slightly longer than the calyx, 1-1.25 mm long. Longistylous flowers: antisepalous filaments ca. 0.6 mm long, the antipetalous filaments ca. 1 mm long, both ca. 0.25 m wide at base; styles connate ca. 1/2 their length; stigma depressed capitate. Brevistylous flowers unknown. Drupes unknown.

description: Planta herbácea perenne, glabra, acaule o con tallo corto de 1.5 cm de largo y 1 cm de diámetro; raíces fibrosas a algo carnosas. Hojas dispuestas en rosetas laxas de 7- 25 cm de diámetro, con 17-36 hojas, láminas obovadas, espatuladas a obovado-espatuladas en contorno, con el ápice agudo cuando jóvenes y obtuso a redondeado en la madurez, con un mucrón de 1 mm de largo, margen ondulado-lacerado cuando jóvenes y entero cuando viejas, 2.7-13.5 x 2-5.8 cm, 3 mm de grosor, la cara superior aplanada, ligeramente acanalada en el centro, la cara inferior convexa a aplanada, ligeramente aquillada, verde claro, verde olivo, verde grisáceo o púrpura, marcadamente pruinosas, bordes hialinos, blanquecino con tonalidades amarillentas o rojizas. Inflorescencia en forma de panícula, 1-3 por roseta, lateral, de 15- 43 cm de alto, con (2)3(4) cincinos, éstos con (3-)5-9 flores cada uno, total de flores 7-28, pedúnculo de (13- )18- 32.5 cm de largo hasta la primera ramificación, diámetro de la base 5.5-8 mm, color verde claro a rojizo. Hojas del pedúnculo de (4-)7-13(-20), alternas, ascendentes, oblanceoladas a oblongas, caedizas en la fructificación, con la cara superior aplanada a cóncava y la inferior convexa, 2.9-4.6*0.9-2.9 cm, de 3-5 mm de grosor, verde amarillento a púrpura, pruinosas, ápice agudo a obtuso, mucronado. Bracteolas oblongas a oblongo-oblanceoladas, espolonadas en la base, adpresas, ápice agudo, mucronado, de 7-20 mm de largo y 1.2- 6 mm de ancho, verde pálido, verde azuloso (grisáceo) a crema, pruinosas; pedicelo de (5-)5.5-14 mm de largo, de i .4-2 A mm de diámetro, verde claro a rojizas. Cáliz de 5 sépalos unidos en la base, lanceolados, ápice agudo, desiguales, extendidos a erectos, con- vexos en la cara inferior y convexos a aplanados en la superior, los mayores de 6.6-15 mm de largo, 5 mm de ancho y ca. 2.5 mm de grueso, y los menores de 3.3 de largo, 1.6 mm de ancho y ca. 1.5 mm de grueso, verde grisáceo, pruinosos. Corola conoide, ligeramente urceolada, de (9-) 10- 12(- 13) mm de largo y 5.3-10 mm de diámetro en la base, ligeramente gibosa, pentagonal, naranja-rosado a rosa, pruinosa; pétalos 5, laceolados a oblongo-lanceolados, unidos en la base formando un tubo de 1.5- 2.2 mm de largo, aquillados en su cara externa, de 11-13 mm de largo y 4-6 mm de ancho, ápice agudo, la parte exterior naranja-rosado a rosa, pruinosos y la interior amarillento y ápice rojizo; estambres 10, 5 epipétalos de 7.5-8 mm de largo, 5 antesépalos 9.2-9.6 mm de largo, amarillo pálido a blanquecinos, anteras oblongo elípticas, con la base oblicua, de ca. 1.4-1.5 mm de largo, amarillo; nectarios reniformes a oblongos, truncos, de 1.9- 2.6 mm de ancho amarillo pálido. Ovario supero de 5 carpelos libres, 6 mm de largo y 2.5 - 2.8 mm de ancho amarillo pálido, estilo de 3-3.7 mm de longitud, rojizo obscuro; estigmas verde a blanquecinos; folículos maduros ascendentes café rojizo. Semillas numerosas de color café rojizo de ca. 0.6 mm de longitud.
