description: Scapes erect, usually pilose near top (rarely glabrous), (16-) 20-35 (-39) cm long, (2.5-) 3-4 (-5.5) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, lanceolate to broadly ovate or elliptic, (5-) 6-10 (-12) cm long, obscurely mottled, often pilose on veins beneath, the bases rounded, obtuse, or cuneate, the apices acute to slightly acuminate. Sepals lanceolate to ovate or narrowly oblong-elliptic, (15-) 20-35 (-40) mm long, widely spreading to horizontal, often with dark purple margins and purple-tinged at base, the bases rounded, the apices usually acuminate-blunt or acute (buds normally apiculate). Petals narrowly elliptic to lanceolate or linear, (16-) 20-36 (-42) mm long, widely spreading to horizontal, usually twisted, dark purple or yellow, the apices sharply acute to rounded. Stamens erect or slightly incurved, (11-) 15-22 (-26) mm long, about %/3 length of petals; filaments short, (1-) 2-3 (-4.5) mm long, slightly dilated at base; anther sacs extrorse on thick or flattened connectives (pollen brownish or olive-orange); connectives little prolonged, if at all, the projection 0-0.5 (-1) mm long. Carpel height usually less than 1/2 stamen length; ovary ovoid, (3.5-) 4.5-6.5 (-9) mm long, distinctly 6-ridged or -winged below stigma bases; stigmas linear, (3-) 5-9 (-11) mm long, widely spreading from narrowed apex of the ovary, with tips recurved or recoiled, often extending between stamens. Flowers with strong carrion odor, extremely fetid. Berry ovoid to ellipsoid, usually sharply 6-angled or sometimes distinctly winged.

description: Scapes erect, usually scabrous, (18-) 30-46 (-59) cm long, (1.7-) 3.0-3.6 (-4.6) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, elliptic-ovate to broadly ovate or elliptic, (8-) 9-13 (-15) cm long, very obscurely mottled or not mottled, usually without upper epidermal stomata or with few only at tips, the apices usually acuminate (rarely acute). Sepals lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, (35-) 38-54 (-63) mm long, widely divergent or spreading, usually purplish basally, the apices acute or acutish. Petals linear-spatulate to narrowly spatulate, (43-) 48-75 (-85) mm long, erect, greenish or yellowish green above the distinct purple claw, sometimes purple or yellow-green throughout, the apices acute-rounded or rounded. Stamens erect, connivent, or overlapping-entangled, (14-) 18-27 (-31) mm long, standing (1.5-) 2 (-3.8) times the height of carpels; filaments (2-) 2.5-4.5 (-6) mm long, slightly dilated basally; anther sacs lateral on linear connectives (pollen usually yellow); connectives slightly prolonged 0.5 mm (range 0-1 mm) beyond anther sacs. Carpels often less than '/2 as tall as stamens; ovary ovoid, (5-) 6-9 (-12) mm long, 6-angled or -winged, inequilaterally hexagonal in cross-section; stigmas nearly linear, (5-) 6-10 (-12) mm long, often slightly longer than ovary, widely spreading, the tips recurved or recoiled, often extending between stamens. Flowers with inoffensive musty-spicy odor. Berry ovoid, usually 6-ridged below the stigma bases (rarely winged); stigmas more or less erect, dried and brittle, persisting.

description: Scapes erect, glabrous, (6.5-) 10-21 (-26) cm long, (1-) 1.5 (-2.5) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, (5-) 7-13 (-15.5) cm long, typically lanceolate, rounded basally and with sides nearly straight from broadest width to the sharply acute apex (rarely almost ovate with slightly acuminate apex), usually conspicuously mottled with 3-5 or more shades of green on either side of a paler green strip along midvein. Sepals lanceolate to ovate, (23-) 30-55 (-65) mm long, usually ca. 3.5-4 times as long as wide, divergent to spreading with tips straight or recurved, the apices acute to rounded. Petals narrowly oblanceolate to narrowly elliptic, (25-) 35-85 (-110) mm long, mostly 3.5-5 times as long as wide, purple or brownish purple varying to greenish yellow, the apices acute to rounded. Stamens (7.5-) 10-17 (-22) mm long, erect or slightly incurved; filaments very short, (1-) 1.5-2.5 (-3) mm long, usually 1/6 to 14 length of anthers; anther sacs lateral on flattened linear connectives (pollen yellow); connectives prolonged (0.5-) 1-1.5 (-3.5) mm beyond anther sacs into acute projection often about as long as the filaments. Carpel height about 2/3. the length of stamens; ovary ovoid to ellipsoid, (5-) 6-10 (-13) mm long, 6- angled or -winged, with deep narrow groove below each stigma causing a transverse section to appear as a triangle with a concavity at each angle; stigmas linear, very short, (1.5-) 2.5-5 (-7) mm long, abruptly recurved or recoiled upon the ovary. Flowers often with fetid, carrion-like odor. Berry ellipsoid to ovoid or obovoid, sharply 6-ridged or -winged, the two dorsal ridges on each carpel closely parallel.

description: Roots 0.4-2.2 mm wide. Stems 4-11 x 2.8 - 12.5 mm. Leaves 5-10 times dichotomously or subdichotomously divided, 6-30.7 mm long, petiole 1.5-5.7 x 1.4-4.7 mm wide, (0)1-10 veined (at base), ultimate divisions 0.1-1.6 x 0.1-0.2 mm. Spathella 3-6.2 x 1.3-1.9 mm, rupturing into 3-8 segments. Flower pedicel 2-16 mm long during anthesis. Tepals 2-5, 1.5- 3.5x0.1-0.3 mm. Stamens 1-4, filaments 1.1- 5 x 0.1-0.8 mm during anthesis, anthers 1.1-3 x 0.4-0.8 mm. Ovary in post-anthesal flowers 1.6- 3.7 x 0.9-1 .5 mm. Stigmas 0.3-1.4 x 0.5- 1.9 mm during anthesis. Capsules 2-4.2 x 1.1-2.8 mm. Seeds 150-380 per capsule, 0.17-0.18 x 0.08 - 0.12 mm.

description: Vegetative parts lacking from the only specimen. Floral bracts thin triangular, 1.4-2.3 cm long, 0.2-0.35 cm wide. Pedicel 1.4-1.7 cm long. Sepals linear-lanceolate, 1.1-1.3 cm long, about 0.15 cm wide. Petals broadly lanceolate, short acuminate, about 1.3 cm long, 0.3 cm wide. Lip pandurate with an emarginate apex, 1.0 cm long, 0.8 cm wide. Callus of two parallel basal lamellae terminated by two tooth-like masses. Col- umn 0.3 cm high, not noticeably enlarged basally. Stipe more or less rectangular, pollinia long ovoid, with a long ventral groove.

description: Geoxylic suffrutex forming mats up to 1.5 m in diam.; aerial shoots to 80 cm high, erect, glabrous, terete, usually unbranched. Stipules 8-12 mm long, appressed to stem, persistent, covering entirely the leafless portion of die stem, ferruginous, the stipular blade linear-lanceolate, the margins and apex fimbriate, the basal cilia branched, the terminal ones more erect and elongate. Leaves densely clustered distally, ascending, becoming appressed in dried material, strongly imbricate, glabrous, sessile; lamina 0.8-2 x 0.5-1.2 cm, chartaceous to coriaceous, elliptic to broadly ovate, rarely obovate, the base and apex obtuse to rounded, the margin sharply serrulate, the tip of each serration bearing a minute, sharply apiculate, and dark reddish gland, midrib and secondary veins impressed on both sides, the secondaiy veins in 6-11 pairs, ascending from the midrib at 20-40° to connect to the clearly defined marginal vein, the tertiary veins inconspicuous. Inflorescences umbellate, 2-4 cm long, arising from a distinct peduncle attached to the leaf axil at the branch apex, slightly horizontal to erect, many-flowered, with 2-5 flowers at anthesis simultaneously; peduncle 1.2-3.5 cm long, terete or occasionally compressed; bracts 4-7x1-2.5 mm, sepaloid, green-vinaceous, glossy, glabrous, elliptic, the upper margin ciliate-glandular, sometimes fimbriate on the lower maigin or subtended by a pair of fimbriate, stipular structures; pedicel 10-15 mm long, green-vinaceous, slender; flower buds 4-8 mm long, conical. Flowers 8-12x10-13 mm, nodding, appearing slightly tubular-campanulate due to the ascending, imbricate petals, pentamerous; sepals 4.5-6x1-2.2 mm, dark reddish to vinaceous, glossy, glabrous, unequal in width, ovate to elliptic, the apex apiculate, the margin conspicuously ciliate-glandular, the glands concave, the cilia 0.1-0.2 mm long; petals 7-10x4-6 mm, contorted in aestivation, light to dark pinkish, glabrous, easily deciduous, broadly elliptic, oval or obovate, the apex obtuse to rounded, the venation parallel; outer staminodial whorl absent, the inner whorl ca. 5 mm long, deep pink, with a white tip, fused into a narrowly conical tube enclosing the stamens and ovary, 5-lobed, splitting readily along segmental lines during the expansion of the fruit; stamens 5, free; anthers 2-2.5 x 0.8-1 mm, borne on a very short, ca. 0.1 mm long, thick filament, oblong, bi-apiculate, tetrasporangiate, dithecal, dehiscing longitudinally; gynoecium 3.5- 6 mm long; ovary ca. 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous, ovoid, 3-lobed, 3-carpelled, uni- locular, the placentation parietal, many ovulate; style 2.5-4 mm long, subulate, protruding up to 1 mm beyond staminodial tube; stigma simple. Capsules 5-7 mm long, glabrous, ovoid-apiculate, septicidal, dehiscing halfway from apex to base, 3- valved, the valves subcoriaceous, with persistent sepals, staminodes, and stamens. Seeds 0.8-1x0.3-0.8 mm, brown, ellipsoid to ovoid, foveolate.

description: Typifications and synonymies are presented under the varietal headings that follow the description. Scapes erect, (25-) 30-60 (-67) cm long, (2.3-) 3.0-3.3 (-4.5) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile (rarely subsessile), ovate to very broadly ovate, (7.5-) 10-18 (-21) cm long, usually more or less mottled with small brownish splotches, sometimes unmottled, the apices rounded, blunt, or obtuse. Sepals lanceolate, (32-) 38-63 (-70) mm long, divergent or divergent-spreading, the apices acute to obtuse or blunt-rounded. Petals oblanceolate, varying from linear-oblanceolate to obovate, (50-) 65-90 (-110) mm long, erect, pale greenish yellow, greenish bronze, and purplish green to dark purple, sometimes pale yellow only at the base in var. chloropetalum and ranging from white to garnet- or red-purple in var. giganteum, basally cuneate, the apices obtuse, rounded, acute, or blunt. Stamens erect, (15-) 18-30 (-35) mm long; filaments relatively thick, (3-) 3.5-5 (-6) mm long, purple; anther sacs introrse on purple flattened connectives (pollen yellow to brownish); connectives prolonged (0.5-) 1.0-1.5 mm into rounded-acute or obtuse projections. Carpels usually ca. '/2 as tall as stamens; ovary ovoid, (5-) 6-9 (-13) mm long, purple, more or less 6-angled; stigmas oblong-subulate, (3-) 4-7 (-10) mm long, divergent-erect, purple, straight, usually truncate. Flowers with pleasant rose-like (or sometimes more spicy) odor. Berry broadly ovoid, obscurely 6-angled above middle.

description: Scapi erecti, (20-) 30-55 (-66) cm longi, bracteis (1.7-) 3.0- vel 3.5 (-4.8)-plo longiores. Bracteae sessiles, ovatae vel late ovatae, (7-) 10-18 (-20) cm longae, maculatis parvis atroviridibus obscure maculatae vel immaculatae, apicibus obtusis vel rotundatis. Sepala lanceolata, (27-) 35-60 (-80) mm longa, divergentia, apicibus acutis, obtusis, vel rotundatis. Petala oblanceolata vel obovata, (40-) 50-85 (-110) mm longa, erecta, albida vel raro subrosea, interdum rosea vel purpurea versus basem, basaliter cuneata, apicibus rotundatis, obtusis, vel acutis. Stamina erecta, (14-) 18-27 (-31) mm longa; filamenta tenuia, (2-) 3-4 (-5.5) mm longa, albido-viridia vel raro purpurea; antherarum thecae laterales, (12-) 15-23 (-25.5) mm longae, in connectivis linearibus viridulis; connectiva plerumque ultra thecas ca. 1 mm (raro 2 mm) prolongata in prominentias rotundatas; pollen luteum. Carpella altitudine plerumque ca. l/2 longitudinis staminum aequantia; ovarium ovoideum, (3-) 6-10 (-14) mm altum, viridulum vel raro purpureum, in sectione transversali rotundato-hexagonum; stigmata subulata, (2-) 3-7 (-9) mm longa, divergentia vel erectiuscula, viridula vel interdum purpurea, apicibus interdum recurvatis. Flores suaveolentes, odorem rosaceum exhalentes. Bacca late ovoidea vel subglobosa, vix porcata praeter versus apicem modo infra stigmata persistentia et succulenta vel marcescentia.

description: Epiphytic shrubs, the branches long-pendent, to 0.5-1.2 m long. Twigs subterete, densely pubescent, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, the mature stems subterete or some angulate, pubescent to glabrate, the bark exfoliating in long, thin strips; buds supra-axillary, prophylls 2, opposite, valvate, ovate, inconspicuous, 0.5-0.8 mm long, apically acute, pubescent and marginally ciliolate, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular. Leaves alternate, imbricate, adpressed, subsessile; petioles twisted ca. 180°, subterete, 1-2 mm long, pubescent with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; blades coriaceous, succulent, drying wrinkled, elliptic to lanceolate, 3.24.8 x 0.8-1.5 cm, basally attenuate, marginally entire, eciliate, not revolute when fresh, but sometimes slightly revolute at base when dry, apically acuminate or sometimes short-acuminate, densely pubescent on both sides (especially in young leaves), but hairs caducous adaxially, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; venation mostly obscure although suggested in dry specimens (especially in younger leaves), the midrib and two pairs of basal lateral nerves slightly elevated above (5-plinerved). Inflorescences axillary, 2-4-flow-ered fascicles or flowers solitary, flowers subsessile, obscured by leaves; all bracts undifferentiated, chartaceous, ovate, gradually varying in size, 0.4-0.75 x 0.2-0.5 mm, marginally ciliate or ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically subacute, glabrous; pedicels subterete, 0.5-0.8(-l) mm long, articulate with calyx, glabrescent; brac-teoles 2, persistent, opposite, inserted near middle of pedicel, lanceolate, carinate, ca. 0.75 x 0.5 mm, marginally ciliate with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically acute, glabrous. Flowers 4-merous, diplostem-onous. Calyx aestivation valvate, obconic overall, 2.8-4 mm long, densely pubescent with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; tube obconic, terete, the base rounded, 1.5-2 mm long; limb erect, 0.5 mm long; lobes deflate, 0.8-1 x 1.3-1.5 mm, marginally ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically acute; sinuses acute to subacute. Corolla aestivation valvate, white to greenish-white, campanulate, 1.5-2 mm long, ca. 2 mm diam., glabrous within and without; lobes ovate, deep, 1-1.5 x 2 mm, apically subacute, slightly reflexed. Stamens 8, equal, included, 1.62 mm long; filaments equal, distinct, long-ligulate, slightly incurved, 0.9-1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers equal, distinct, 0.9-1.25 mm long; thecae 0.5-0.75 mm long, slightly papillose near base; tubules 2, distinct to base, 0.40.5 mm long, dehiscing by oblique pores, 0.20.3 mm long. Ovary 4-locular, placentation axile; nectariferous disc pulvinate, glabrous; style filiform, terete, 1.5 mm long, glabrous; stigma simple. Berry apparently immature, blue-black, spherical, to 4 mm diam., puberulous; seeds immature, apparently one per locule.

description: Epiphytic shrubs, the branches pendent. Twigs subterete, hirsutulous, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, the mature stems more or less terete, the bark dark brown, fissured, glabrescent; buds axillary, prophylls 2, opposite, valvate, linear, conspicuous, 1.53.2 mm long, apically acute, pubescent and marginally ciliolate, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular. Leaves alternate, imbricate, adpressed, subsessile; petioles twisted ca. 180°, subterete, 1.4-2 mm long, hirsutulous and glabrescent with age, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; blades coriaceous, lanceolate, 1.6-2.4 x 0.4-0.5 cm, basally attenuate, marginally entire, eciliate, strongly revolute especially distally where opposing margins touch, apically acuminate, glabrescent above and puberulous beneath, the hairs simple and of two types: unicellular and eglandular, and multicellular and glandular; venation mostly obscured in dry, occasionally the midrib and two basal secondaries raised above. Inflorescences axillary, flowers solitary and subsessile; all bracts undifferentiated, chartaceous, ovate, the prophylls surpassing them, 0.4-1.2*0.4-0.8 mm, apically obtuse or acute, marginally ciliate with hairs all simple, some unicellular and eglandular, others multicellular and glandular (these caducous), glabrous; pedicels terete, 0.51 mm long, articulate with calyx, glabrescent with a ring of simple, multicellular, glandular hairs at articulation, otherwise the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; bracteoles persistent, 2, opposite, inserted toward base of pedicel, ovate, 0.5-0.9><0.5-0.7 mm, apically obtuse, marginally ciliate with hairs all simple, some unicellular and eglandular, others multicellular and glandular, sometimes adjacent glandular hairs fused and forming prominent glandular fimbriae. Flowers 5-merous, presumably diplostemonous (the nectariferous disk has 10 lobes, but the material has incomplete stamens). Calyx aestivation unknown, campanulate overall, 3.8-5 mm long; tube obconic, terete, 1.32.3 mm long, hirsutulous with hairs simple, unicellular, eglandular and dense enough to obscure surface; limb erect or slightly spreading, 2.5-2.7 mm long, glabrate with hairs similar to those of tube; lobes lanceolate, 2-2.3 x 0.6-0.7 mm, marginally cilio-late with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically acuminate; sinuses narrowly rounded. Corolla aestivation unknown, red-orange, apparently cylindrical, at least 7 mm long, glabrous within and without; lobes unknown (incomplete corolla). Stamens presumably 10 (the nectariferous disk with 10 lobes); filaments not seen; anthers 5 mm long; thecae 1.5 mm long, smooth, with basal appendage; tubules 2, distinct to base, 3.5 mm long, dehiscing by introrse longitudinal slits, 1 mm long. Ovary 5-locular, placentation axile; nectariferous disc pulvinate, glabrous; style not seen. Berry not seen.

description: Species nova foliis marginibus planis atque integris, in apice acuminatis vel acutis, floribus in fascículos vel solitariis, pedicellis conspicuis 4-10 mm longis, calyce pedicello continuo, corolla rubra, urceolata, 7-8.5 longa distincta; a Vaccinio continuo perulis axillaribus, brevibus, inconspicuis (non supra-axillaribus, longis, conspicuis), foliis in pagina inferiore pilis fasciculatis atque dendroideis carentibus (non pilis fasciculatis atque dendroideis), bracteolis 1 (non 2) differt. Epiphytic shrubs, the branches long-pendent. Twigs subterete, sparsely pilosulose, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, the mature stems terete, the bark dark brown, fissured, glabrescent; buds axillary, prophylls 2, opposite, valvate, ovate, inconspicuous, ca. 1 mm long, marginally eciliate, glabrescent, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically acute. Leaves alternate, imbricate, adpressed to ascendent, subsessile; petioles twisted ca. 180°, subterete, 1.5-2 mm long, pilosulose, the hairs simple, unicellular, and eglandular; blades coriaceous, succulent, drying wrinkled, ovate to lanceolate, (2-)2.3- 3 x 0.8-1 cm, basally rounded, marginally entire, ciliolate especially distally in young leaves with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, basally revolute when dry, apically acuminate or sometimes acute, glabrescent on both sides with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, beneath also with few, inconspicuous, simple, multicellular and glandular hairs; venation obscure when dry, but apparently pinnate, sometimes with the midrib raised beneath. Inflorescences axillary, 2-flowered fascicles or flowers solitary, flowers pedicellate; all bracts undifferentiated, chartaceous, ovate, ca. 0.5x0.5 mm, marginally eciliate, apically obtuse, glabrous; pedicels terete, slightly widening distally, 0.4-1 cm long, continuous with calyx, glabrescent with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, also with few, simple, multicellular and glandular hairs distally; bracteoles 1, persistent, inserted at base of pedicel, transverse-elliptic, 1-1.2 x 1.6-1.8 mm, marginally ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically obtuse and obcordate, glabrous. Flowers 4- merous, diplostemonous. Calyx aestivation valvate, campanulate overall, 3.7-4.5 mm long, puberulous, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; tube obconic, terete, 1.5- 1.7 mm long; limb spreading, 2.2-2.3 mm long; lobes deltate, 1.6-2x0.8-1.2 mm, marginally eciliate, apically acute; sinuses acute. Corolla aestivation valvate, red, urceolate, 7- 8.5 mm long, ca. 4.5 mm diam., 2.5 mm wide at throat, glabrescent without with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, glabrous within; lobes ovate, ca. lxl mm, apically acute. Stamens 8, equal, basally adherent to corolla, included, 6.5-7 mm long; filaments equal, distinct, long-triangular, straight, 3- 3.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers equal, 4- 4.5 mm long; thecae 1.8-2 mm long, minutely papillose; tubules 2, distinct to base, 2.2-2.4 mm long, dehiscing by introrse longitudinal slits, 1.2 - 1.6 mm long. Ovary 4- locular, placentation axile; nectariferous disc pulvinate, glabrose; style included, filiform, terete, 8 mm long, glabrous; stigma simple. Berry not seen.

description: Vaccinio sphyrospermoidi marginibus folii crenatis, pilis fasciculatis, corollis rotatis, viridibus similis, sed floribus subsessilifloris 5-7-meris (non pedicellatis, [4-] 5-meris), calycibus glabris (non confertim hirsutis) differt. Terrestrial shrubs , to 2 m tall. Twigs ridged, pilosulose, the hairs simple, unicellu- lar, and eglandular, the mature stems more or less terete, the bark light brown, fissured, glabrescent; buds axillary, prophylls 2, opposite, valvate, ovate, inconspicuous, 1-1.2 mm long, apically acute, marginally ciliolate at apex, the hairs simple, unicellular, and eglandular, glabrous. Leaves alternate, ascendent; petioles not twisted, subterete,  1.1 -2.7 (-3.4) mm long, inconspicuously glabrescent, the hairs simple, unicellular and elgnadular; blades corieacous, ovate or elliptic, 1-2.5 x 0.4 - 1 cm, basally rounded or cuneate, marginally thickened and cren- ulate, the teeth terminated in a caducous seta, with the tendency to be slightly revolute basally when dry (but flat in fresh material), apically ciliolate in young leaves with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandu- lar, apically obtuse or acute, mucronate, the muero fragile, short, 0.4-0.8 mm long, glabrescent above (especially over midrib) with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandu- lar, almost glabrous beneath with few clustered unicellular/eglandular hairs radiat- ing around a single multicellular/glandular hair; venation obscure when dry with only the midrib impressed adaxially. Inflorescen- ces axillary, 2 -flowered fascicles or some- times flowers apparently solitary, flowers subsessile; all bracts undifferentiated, char- taceous, ovate or elliptic, gradually varying in size, 0.8-1.5 x 0.6-1.3 mm, apically obtuse, marginally eciliate, glabrous; ped- icels subterete, 1-1.5 mm long, articulate with calyx, glabrous except for simple, multicellular and glandular hairs at articu- lation; bracteoles 2, persistent, opposite or subopposte, inserted at base of pedicel, similar to bracts, ovate, 1.4x0.6-0.8 mm, marginally ciliolate with hairs simple, uni- cellular and eglandular, apically acute, glabrous. Flowers 5-7-merous, haplostemo- nous. Calyx aestivation valvate, campanu- late overall, 3.8^.3 mm long, glabrous; tube obconic, terete, 2.0-2.8 mm long; limb spreading, 1.5-1.9 mm long; lobes deltate, 1 .3-1 .5x1 .3-1 .5 mm, marginally eciliate, apically acute; sinuses acute. Corolla aesti- vation valvate, light green, rotate, 2.7- 3.2 mm long, 2.7-3 mm diam., glabrous within and without; lobes ovate, deep, 1.7- 2.1x1.8-2.7 mm, apically acute, strongly reflexed. Stamens 5-7, equal, basally adher- ent to corolla, exposed, 1.5-1.6 mm long; filaments equal, distinct, long-triangular, incurved, 1-1.1 mm long, glabrous; anthers equal, distinct, 0.8-1 mm long; thecae 0.7- 0.8 mm long, inconspicuously papillose; tubules 2, distinct to base, inconspicuous, very reduced, 0.1-0.15 mm long, dehiscing by terminal pores, 0.2 mm diam. Ovary 4 - locular, locules sometimes of variable size, placentation axile; nectariferous disc pulvinate, glabrous; style exposed, filiform, terete, 1.5 - 1.9 mm long, glabrous, stigma simple. Berry spherical, 5.5 - 7.5 mm diam., dark purple; seeds many per locule, but apparently few fully developed, ellipsoid, 1.6 x 0.9 mm, with mucilaginous coat, embyro white.

description: Vaccinio aristato affinis, sed foliis ellipticis vel obovatis apice rotondato atque valde et persistenter mucronato, mucrone vel apiculo 1-2.5 mm longo, lamina folii marginibus interdum obscure crenatis (non integris), in pagina inferiore pilis dendroideis (non pilis dendroideis nullis), calyce breviore 3-3.5 (non 4-4.7) mm longo, corolla cylindrica vel urceolata (non cylindrica vel infundibulari) Terrestrial shrubs to 1 m tall. Twigs angled, glabrescent with minute, simple hairs, some unicellular and eglandular, others multicellular and glandular, the mature stems subterete, the bark fissured, light brown to grayish, glabrous; buds axillary, prophylls 2, opposite, valvate, ovate, inconspicuous, 1-1.5 mm long, marginally eciliate, apically obtuse, glabrous. Leaves alternate, diffuse; petioles not twisted, subterete, 2-3.5 mm long, glabrous to glabrate with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; blades coriaceous, succulent, mostly elliptic and sometimes slightly obovate, 1.8-2.3x1-1.2 cm, basally rounded or less often cuneate, marginally entire or with very inconspicuous crenulations, ciliolate in young leaves with simple hairs both uni- cellular-eglandular and multicellular-glandular, the margin itself thicker than lamina in  dry specimens (also different in color when dry), apically rounded and distinctly and persistently broadly apiculate or mucronate, the extended point 1-2.5 mm long, glabrescent above with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, puberulous beneath with minute hairs of two types: simple hairs multicellular and glandular, and compound dendritic hairs with unicellular branches arising from either a glandular hair or from a thick and finger like projection (some are ca. 0.5mm long and are more evident on young leaves); venation apparently pinnate, but only the midrib evident in dry specimens, impressed above and raised beneath. Inflorescences axillary, 3-4-flowered fascicles, flowers pedicellate; all bracts undifferentiated, chartaceous, ovate, gradually diminishing in size, 1.5-2.4x 1-2 mm, marginally ciliate with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically obtuse, glabrous; pedicels subterete, 5-10 mm long, articulate with calyx (more evident at bud stage or in young flowers), puberulous to glabrescent with simple hairs unicellular/eglandular and multicellular/glandular; bracteoles 2, early caducous, opposite, inserted toward base of pedicel, lanceolate or oblong, 1.4-2x0.5-0.7 mm, marginally ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular, eglandular and whitish, apically subacute, glabrous. Flow- ers 4(-5)-merous, diplostemonous. Calyx aestivation valvate, campanulate overall, 3- 3.5 mm long, glabrescent with short hairs both straight multicellular/glandular and wavy unicellular/eglandular; tube conical, slightly angulate when dried, 1.1-1.9 mm long; limb campanulate, 2-2.4 mm long; lobes triangular, 1- 1.3 x 1.5 mm long, marginally ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically acute; sinuses broadly rounded. Corolla aestivation valvate, white, cylindrical to slightly urceolate, (6-)7-7.5 mm long, 3 mm diam., 1.6- 2.2 mm wide at throat, glabrous within and without; lobes deltate, obtuse, 1.5 x 2 mm, spreading. Stamens 8 or 10, equal, included, 5-6 mm long; filaments equal, distinct, long-ligulate, straight, 2.5-3.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers equal, 3.5- 4 mm long, with basal appendage alternately more or less prominent; thecae 1.5-1.6 mm long, minutely papillose and with some simple and unicellular hairs basally; tubules 2, distinct to base, 1.8-2 mm long, dehiscing by short, introrse, longitudinal slits, 1 mm long. Ovary 4-locular, placentation axile; nectariferous disc pulvinate, glabrous; style included, filiform, terete, 5.5-6, glabrous. Berry not seen.

description: Epiphytic shrubs , branches pendent, long. Twigs angulate, pubescent, simple, unicellular and eglandular, clustering, the mature stems subterete, ridged, the bark light brown glabrescent; buds supra-axillary, opposite, valvate, ovate, conspicuous, 3 mm long, apically acute, glabrescent the hairs simple, unicellular and Leaves alternate, imbricate, adpressed, sile; petioles twisted ca. 180°, subterete, 2 mm long, puberulous, the hairs unicellular and eglandular; blades lanceolate, 3-4 x 0.9-1.2 cm, basally the base revolute in dry material, entire, eciliate, apically acuminate, above with hairs few, scattered, cellular and eglandular, puberulous with simple, unicellular, eglandular scattered or clustered around a multicellular/ glandular hair, compound dendritic hairs also present and consisting of a main multicellular/ glandular hair with unicellular/eglandular branches; venation mostly obscure but apparently pinnate when dry, the midrib impressed adaxially and raised abaxially, sometimes 2 basal secondary veins suggested. Inflorescences axillary, 2-flowered fascicles or flowers solitary, flowers pedicellate; all bracts undifferentiated, chartaceous, ovate, inconspicuous, gradually varying in size, 2-2.4 x 0.8- 1.6 mm, marginally ciliolate hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, apically obtuse, glabrous; pedicels terete, 1-1.3 cm long, continuous with calyx, puberulous, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular; bracteoles 2, persistent, opposite, inserted in basal half of pedicle, lanceolate, 1-1.4 x 0.3-0.4 mm, marginally ciliolate with hairs simple, unicellular and elglandular, apically obtuse, glabrous Flowers 4 - merous, presumably diplostemonous(nectariferous disk with 8 lobes). Caylx aestivation unknown, cream colored, infundibuliform overall, 9-10 mm long, puberulous, the hairs simple, unicellular and elglandular; tube obconic, terete, 6.2 - 7 mm long; limb more or less erect, 2.8 - 3mm long; lobes deltate, 1.6 - 1.7 x 3- 3.2 mm, marginally eciliate, apically acute; sinuses rounded. Corolla aestivation and color unknown, presumably campanulate and dorsally carinate along petals, ca. 7 mm long, glabrescent without with hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, glabrous within; lobes ovate, ca. 1 x 1 mm, apically acute. Stamens presumably 8 (nectariferous disk with 8 lobes; filaments distinct, geniculate, long-ligulate, ca. 2mm long, glabrous; anthers distinct, 1.3 mm long; thecae ca. 0.9 mm long, inconspicuously papillose; tubules 2, distinct to base, 0.4 mm long, dehiscing by terminal pores, 0.4 mm diam. Ovary 4- locular, placentation axile; nectariferous disc pulvinate, glabrous; style filiform, terete, ca. 4.5 mm long, glabrous; stigma simple. Berry not seen.

description: Vine from stout, twining stems, 8 mm thick, climbing up to 7 m long, glaucous, glabrous or thinly pubescent, hairs minute; stipules triangular-subulate, 2-3 mm long, slightly ciliate; stipels deltoid to lanceolate, 2-3 mm long; striate, glabrous to slightly pubescent, caducous. Leaves pinnate-trifoliolate, 12-28 cm long; petiole 5-12 cm long; rachis 2.5-4 cm long; leaflets widely ovate to rhombic, 6-12 x 6-10 cm with conspicuous venation, glabrous to slightly strigillose in both sides, lateral leaflet bases regularly asymmetric. Inflorescences pseudoracemes, axillary, 25- 40 cm long; peduncle 15-30 cm long, rachis with ca. 20 conspicuous floral nodes, 3.5-5 mm diam, with 7-12 flowers, lax and spirally arranged; bracts lanceolate to subulate, 1.5 x 0.5 mm, caducous, bracteoles subpeltate, ca. 1 mm long, caducous; pedicels 3-4 mm long. Flowers 1.2 mm long; calyx campanulate, reddish-purple, 5-6 mm long, 2-lipped, upper lip widely oblong to obliquely oblong, 3-4 mm long, the margin often ciliate, reflexed in live material; corolla deep purple to violet, the standard widely ovate, 7.5-9.2 mm long, slightly wider than longer, bent backwards and reflexed at anthesis with a basal yellow maculae, the base auriculate, short-clawed, the apex emarginate; wings adnate to keel walls, obliquely-oblong to slightly obovate, clawed and auriculate, 7.5-9 mm long, lamellate outer surface; keel incurved, 5.5-6.5 mm long, beak slightly twisted at apex shortly retuse, clawed stamens 10, diadelphous, staminal tube wider at base, vexillary stamen with a prominent basal appendage; pollen tricolporate, brevicolpate, oblate-spheroidal, exine reticulated, heterobrocate; ovary linear-oblong, 4 mm long, appressed-pubescent on the ventral side, densely pubescent on the upper suture, the ovules 5-7, the style filiform on the lower half, upper portion slightly thickened, 3-5.5 mm long, the pollen brush below stigma, introrse and distally by rotation of style extrorsely placed, the stigma ca. 0.5 mm long, ciliate, introrse-lateral by an apical twist. Legume cylindrical, 8-11 cm x 10-13 mm, valves subcoriaceous, glabrous, slightly compressed between the seeds, the beak 4-6 mm long, glabrous, elastically dehiscent along both mar- gins. Seeds 5-6, aligned longitudinal to the fruit, oblong-reniform, 8.5-12 x 6.3-8.0 mm, 5.9-8.1 mm thick, testa dark brown, hilum linear- oblong, covered by white epihilum, ca. 54 percent of the seed length, 4.3-6.3 mm, lens discernible and divided. Seedlings hypogeal germination, the stipules deeply divided in 4, petioles with basal and apical pulvini, eophylls ovate.

description: Suffruticose perennial herbs. Stems terete, paniculately branched, branches slender, up to 1.4 mm diameter, glabrate, not densely leafy, the internodes longer than leaves. Intrapetiolular glands 0 or minute, conic or subspheric; post-petiolular glands 2, prom- inent, hemispheric, one below each leaflet, brown or brown-orange. Stipules subulate, 0.5-1.1 mm long, caducous. Leaves odd- pinnate, up to 1.8 cm long, petiolate; petioles 0.3-2.4 mm long, the rachis 2.5-15 mm long; leaflets (5- )9- 1 1(- 13) per leaf, petiolulate, narrowly obovate to narrowly oblanceolate, loosely conduplicate, 1.8-5.5x0.6-1.2 mm, glabrate, smooth and green above, thick- textured, glandular-punctate beneath, the glands small, spherical, brown. Inflorescences terminal, compact spikes (3- )5- 7 flowered, the peduncle (9-) 13-47 mm long, the axis 1- 2 mm long, the flowers papilionaceous, subsessile; bracts minute, caducous. Calyx campanulate, 4-4.5x2.5-3.1 mm, faintly 10- nerved but not pleated, glabrous externally, the tube 3.1-3.3x2.5-3 mm, the teeth (0.7-) 0.9-1.5 mm long, broadly triangular to triangular-ovate, abruptly acute, green, the orifice silky-ciliolate with exserted hairs; corolla greenish (stated on the label), drying pale greenish-yellow, glabrous, the banner and inner petals faintly gland-tipped, the epistemo- nous petals inserted 2.0 (wings) - 2.7 (keel) mm above base of filament-sheath; banner 5- 5.3 mm long, the claw 2.8-2.9 (-3.2) mm long, the blade wide-rhombic, wider than long, 2- 2.1x3-3.8 mm; wings 4.4-4.6x1.8-2.0 mm, obliquely oblong-obovate, auriculate basally; keel 6.4-6.5 mm long, the claw 1.8-1.9 mm long, the blade 4.5-4.6 x 1.8-1.9 mm, elliptic- obovate; stamens 10, 7-7.6 mm long, the filament free for 2-2.4 mm, the anthers 0.7- 0.9x0.5 mm, light-brown; ovary at anthesis 1.8-2x1 mm, membranous at base, thinly villosulous beyond middle, ovules nor seen, the style 4.8 - 5mm long, stigma linear. Fruit unknown.

description: Scapes erect, (19-) 25-48 (-67) cm long, (1.6-) 2.4-2.6 (-4.6) times as long as bracts. Bracts subsessile, ovate to broadly ovate, (9-) 10-20 (-24.5) cm long, basally divergent, the blades spreading, sparingly mottled with small brownish or dark green spots or unmottled, sometimes glossy beneath, the bases abruptly contracted into short thick petiole 10-25 mm long, the apices obtuse, rounded, or blunt. Sepals narrowly oblong-lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, (30-) 35-55 (-65) mm long, basally divergent, outcurved and spreading near middle, the apices acute or rounded-acute. Petals linear, (50-) 60-95 (-110) mm long, (6.2-) 8.0-9.8 (-11.0) times as long as wide, erect, dark purple, the apices acute, rounded-acute, obtuse, or blunt. Stamens erect, (11-) 14-20 (-23) mm long; filaments short, (2-) 3-4 (-5) mm long, slightly dilated basally, purple; anther sacs introrse, (9-) 12-17 (-18) mm long, on linear purple connectives (pollen yellow); connectives slightly prolonged about 1 mm (range 0-1.5 mm) into rounded projections. Carpels 4/a as tall to equaling stamens; ovary ellipsoid-ovoid, (5-) 8-13 (-14) mm long, dark purple, usually sharply 6-angled near apex, sometimes with distinct wings; stigmas thickly subulate, (2-) 4-5 (-7) mm long, erect, dark purple. Flowers with spicy-musty odor. Berry ellipsoid to subglobose, with sharp angles or wings extending and converging from sides to the persistent, fleshy stigmas.

description: Pseudobulbs elliptic-pyriform, smooth. Leaves lanceolate, 7-50 cm long, 2.1-3.6 cm wide. Inflorescence as long as or longer than the leaves. Floral bracts large, papery, 2.5-3.5 cm long, 0.7-0.9 cm wide. Sepals linear-lanceolate, acuminate, the lateral sepals slightly falcate, 2.0-2.5 cm long, 0.3-0.4 cm wide. Petals shorter than the sepals, lanceolate, falcate, 1.0-1.8 cm long, 0.25-0.35 cm wide. Lip ovate, acuminate, re- flexed near the apex, 1.0-1.9 cm long, 0.4-0.7 cm wide. Callus of two parallel lamellae with a small tooth-like area at or beyond the middle of each lamella. Column 0.4-0.5 cm high. All pollinaria examined in poor condition.

description: In America-Boreali occidentali indigenum, T. albidum Freeman simulans. Scapi erecti (15) 18-24 (33) cm longi, bracteis (1.5) 2.0-2.5 (3.5)-plo longiores. Bracteae subsessiles, ovatae vel late ovatae (6) 8.5-11.5 (14) cm longae, guttis parvis atroviridibus obscure maculatae vel immaculatae, apice obtusae vel rotundatae. Sepala lanceolata, (15) 18-22 (31) mm longa, divergentia, apice acuta, obtusa, vel rotundata. Petala lineari lanceolata (20) 28-40 (50) mm longa, erecta, albida, interdum versus basem purpurea, basaliter cuneata, apice obtusa vel rotundata. Stamina erecta (9.0) 10.5-14.0 (16.5) mm longa; filamenta tenuia (1.0) 1.5-2.5 (3.5) mm longa, albido-viridia vel raro purpurea; antherarum thecae laterales, (8.0) 9.0-11.5 (13.0) mm longae, connectivis linearibus viridulis connexae; connectivae plerumque ultra thecas ca. 0.4 mm (raro 1.0 mm) in apiculum rotundatum prolongata; pollen luteum. Carpella quam stamina pleurumque ± duplo breviora; ovarium ovoideum, (3.0) 5.0-7.5 (9.0) mm altum, viridulum, basaliter purpureum, in sectione transversali rotundato hexagonum; stigmata subulata (2.0) 3.0-4.5 (6.0) mm longa divertigentia vel erectiuscula, intus viridula et extus purpurea, apicibus interdum recurvatis. Flores suaveolentes, odorem fere caryophylli vel Epigaeae repentis simile exhalentes. Bacca late ovoidea vel subglobosa, atrorubiginosa.
bibliographicCitation: Soukup, Victor G. 1980. A new Trillium [T. parviflorum] (Liliaceae) from the northwestern United States. Brittonia. 32: 330-333.

description: Trillium parviflorum is an erect scapose herb usually less than 30 cm tall; the scape averages 2.0-2.5 times as long as the bracts. The bracts are subsessile, ovate or broadly ovate, averaging about 10 cm long, with a petiole 0.3-1.0 mm long, slightly and obscurely mottled with darker green or unmottled, apex rounded or obtuse. Sepals are lanceolate, averaging 20 mm long, divergent, green with acute, obtuse or rounded apex. Petals are linear-lanceolate, usually about 30-40 mm long, erect, white sometimes tinged with purple at the base, cuneate, with rounded or obtuse apex. Stamens are erect, averaging about 12 mm long; the short filaments are slender, whitish-green or rarely purple, with lateral anther cases on linear greenish connectives which are prolonged about 0.4 (rarely 1.0) mm into rounded projections. The carpel is about 1/2 the height of the stamens; ovary ovoid, about 7 mm tall, greenish, tinged purple basally, rounded-hexagonal in cross-section; stigmas subulate about 4 mm long, divergent or erect, greenish with exterior surfaces purple, apices often recurved. The flowers have a pleasant clove-like fragrance suggestive of that of trailing arbutus (Epigaea repens). The fruit is broadly ovoid or subglobose with a somewhat glossy surface and is dark- maroon in color.

description: Scapes erect, glabrous, very short, (4.5-) 5.5-16.5 (-18.5) cm long, reaching only to or just above soil surface. Bracts long-petioled, (9-) 12.5-20 (-22.5) cm long; petioles /4 to '/2 the length of bracts; blades elliptic to transversely elliptic or ovate, (5.5-) 7-11 (-14.5) cm long, not mottled, the apices rounded or obtuse. Sepals narrowly elliptic-oblanceolate to oblong-elliptic, (21-) 28-42 (-53) mm long, divergent, reflexed in gentle curve near middle, the apices acute. Petals lanceolate to linear, (28-) 33-47 (-58) mm long, basally erect, becoming incurved near apices (forming pyriform outline) or erect, purple, greenish purple, or greenish, the apices acute. Stamens erect, (13-) 17-24 (-30) mm long, about 1/2 as long as petals; filaments (4-) 4.5-6.5 (-7) mm long; anther sacs lateral on linear connectives (pollen yellow to olive or orange); connectives little if at all prolonged, to rarely 0.5 mm. Carpels usually 3/5 to 4/5 as tall as stamens; ovary ovoid, (3-) 4-8 (-9) mm long, sharply wing-angled below stigmas; stigmas linear-subulate, (5.5-) 9-18 (-22) mm long, slightly divergent, often with upper portions recurved and extending between stamens. Berry broadly ovoid, sharply winged.

description: Scapes erect, glabrous, (16-) 18-41 (-47.5) cm long, (1.7-) 2.7-3.0 (-4.1) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, ovate-elliptic to very broadly ovate or elliptic (rarely subcordate), (5.5-) 8.5-13.5 (-16) cm long, more or less obscurely mottled, the apices usually acuminate, sometimes long-acute-acuminate in narrower shapes or abruptly short-acuminate in broader shapes. Sepals lanceolate, varying toward narrowly oblong-elliptic, (25-) 30-55 (-67) mm long, widely divergent, the apices rounded-acute, obtuse, or blunt. Petals elliptic-obovate or elliptic-ovate, varying to oblanceolate, elliptic-rhombic, obovate, or very narrowly elliptic, (30-) 40-70 (-90) mm long, bright lemon-yellow or greenish yellow, the bases usually cuneate, the apices acute or rounded-acute. Stamens erect, (8-) 11-21 (-26) mm long, about 1/4 to 1/3 as long as petals; filaments (1.5-) 2-3.5 (-4.5) mm long, dilated basally; anther sacs introrse or lateral on broadly flattened or linear connectives (pollen yellow); connectives pale green, very little prolonged, extending 0-0.5 (-1) mm beyond anther sacs. Carpels about 2/3 to 4/5 as long as stamens; ovary ovoid, (4-) 5-10 (-13) mm long, pale green, hexagonal or 6-ridged, usually tapering slightly to bases of stigmas; stigmas linear to thickly subulate, 3-7 (-10) mm long, erect to divergent with tips recurved. Flowers with strong, penetrating lemon-oil fragrance. Berry ovoid to broadly ovoid, sometimes sharply angled but not winged, pale greenish yellow outside, becoming purplish on inner walls of locules.

description: Scapes erect, glabrous, (8-) 16-25 (-35) cm long, (2-) 3 (-5) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, elliptic to broadly elliptic or ovate, (3.5-) 5-9 (-11) cm long, often not mottled or sparingly mottled with small dark spots of green or brown, the apices rounded, slightly acuminate or acute. Sepals lanceolate to ovate, (13-) 17-33 (-40) mm long, divergent to spreading, sometimes with purple margins or purple at the base, the apices usually rounded-acute. Petals narrowly elliptic to elliptic or lanceolate, (17-) 21-40 (-47) mm long, sometimes with a very short claw, dark purple to greenish yellow, the apices acute to rounded-acute. Stamens (9-) 12-20 (-24) mm long, straight, erect; filaments (2-) 3-4 (-5) mm long, slightly dilated basally, less than ?/2 length of anthers; anther sacs introrse on flattened connectives (pollen yellow); connectives prominently prolonged (1-) 2-3.5 (-5) mm beyond anther sacs into acute or rounded-acute projections, usually approximating filament length. Carpel height approaching tops of anther sacs or bases of connective prolongations; ovary broadly ovoid to subglobose, (3-) 4-7 (-9) mm long, sharply 6-angled or -winged, narrowed at the apex below the stigmas; stigmas very narrowly to narrowly subulate, erect, usually 1.5-2 times as long as ovary. Flowers with spicy, slightly pungent odor. Berry very broadly ovoid or subglobose, prominently 6-angled or -winged.

description: Scapes erect, glabrous, (10-) 15-28 (-37) cm long, (1.9-) 2.4-2.8 (-3.8) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, lanceolate to broadly ovate, (5-) 6-11 (-14.5) cm long, usually distinctly mottled, the apices rounded or rounded-acute. Sepals lanceolate, (21-) 25-40 (-51) mm long, widely spreading, sometimes with tips reflexed, the apices acute or acute-rounded. Petals linear-oblanceolate, (26-) 35-55 (-67) mm long, divergent-erect, usually greenish above the narrow purple claw-like bases or purple throughout, the apices acute or rounded. Stamens erect, (9.5-) 12-17 (-20) mm long; filaments (2-) 2.5-3 (-3.5) mm long, dilated basally; anther sacs lateral on linear connectives (pollen olive to orange); connectives slightly prolonged up to 0.5 mm (range 0-1 mm) into rounded projections. Carpels about 3/4 to 5/6 as tall as stamens; ovary triangular-ovoid, (4-) 5.5-8 (-10) mm long, often sharply 6- angled; stigmas subulate, (3.5-) 4.5-10 (-11.5) mm long, continuous in outline with the ovary, basally divergent-erect, apically spreading with tips recurved or recoiled, usually grooved on outer face or sharply angled basally. Flowers with musty carrion odor. Berry ovoid, more or less 6-angled, usually with prominent grooves extending from the ovary sides onto the persisting stigma bases.

description: Scapi decumbentes vel quasi decumbentes, glabri, (5.5-) 7.5-17 (-24.5) cm longi, bracteis (1-) 1.6- vel 1.9 (-2.75)-plo longiores, e basi versus apicem aequicrassi vel infra bracteas leviter angustati et 6-angulati. Bracteae sessiles, ellipticae vel late ovatae, (5-) 6.5-10 (-13) cm longae, a latitudine maxima ad apicem acutum vel obtusum conveximarginatae, maculatis parvis atroviridibus vel atropurpureis con- spicue maculatae praecipue inter nervos laterales et vittam pallide viridem costam secutam. Sepala lanceolata, (18-) 25-38 (-52) mm longa, divergentia et planiuscula vel patentissima apicibus recurvatis, plerumque superficie purpurascentia vel basaliter purpurea, apicibus acutis vel rotundatis. Petala anguste (raro late) elliptica vel anguste (raro late) oblanceolata, (22-) 30-50 (-60) mm longa, erecta, atropurpurea, viridi-purpurea, vel flava, leviter tortilia, apicibus acutis. Stamina basaliter erecta, versus apicem incurvata et conniventia vel superposita, (11-) 14-22 (-29) mm longa, ca. 0.4-0.5 longitudinis petalorum aequantia; filamenta brevia, (1-) 1.5-2.5 (-4) mm longa; antherarum thecae introrsae in connectivis linearibus; connectiva ultra thecas (1-) 1.5-2.5 (-3.5) mm manifeste prolongata in prominentias acutas filamenta longitudine plerumque aequantes; pollen luteum. Carpella altitudine plerumque minus quam 1/2 longitudinis staminum aequantia; ovarium ovoideum, (4-) 5-9 (-11) mm altum, manifeste 6-alatoangulatum; stigmata linearia, brevia, (1.5-) 2-3.5 (-4.5) mm longa, divergentia, apicibus recurvatis. Flores foetidi, odore ei carnis putridae simili. Bacca ovoidea, versus apicem acute alato-angulata.

description: Rhizomes slender, elongated, 6-12 cm long, 4-12 mm diam. Scapes erect, glabrous, (15-) 20-40 (-50) cm long, 3-8 mm diam. Bracts petiolate, (5-) 7-11 (-18) cm long; petioles equaling (0.05-) 0.1-0.2 (-0.3) the total bract length; blades lanceolate to broadly ovate or elliptic, obscurely mottled with darker green, the apices acute to slightly acuminate. Sepals lanceolate to ovate, (15-) 20-30 (-40) mm long, abruptly recurved basally, the apices acute. Petals lanceolate to ovate or angular- obovate, (18-) 25-40 (-50) mm long, erect, dark purple to pure yellow, the bases attenuate to clawed, the apices acute to obtuse. Stamens (8-) 10-15 (-20) mm in height; filaments straight, erect, 1/3 to 1/2 the stamen length; anther sacs introrse on broad, strongly incurved connectives that often overlap; connectives prolonged beyond anther sacs (0.5-) 1.5 (-2) mm into a rounded projection. Carpel height usually slightly exceeding filament length; ovary transversely rhombic to angular- ovate in outline, (3-) 4-6 (-8) mm long, with 6 prominent wings extending be- tween the filaments; stigmas nearly linear, widely divergent, about as long as ovary, the tips recurved. Berry transversely angular-ovoid to rhomboid, prominently winged.

description: Rhizomes short, very compact, with closely spaced nodes (indicated by cataphyll scars), the internodes usually 1-2 mm long. Scapes erect, glabrous or occasionally with a few scattered short trichomes near the top, (9-) 16-28 (-32.5) cm long, (1.5-) 2-2.5 (-3.25) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, (4.5-) 7-12 (-14) cm long, elliptic to subcircular, varying to ovate or obovate, usually distinctly mottled with small dark green splotches on a more obscurely mottled background (especially evident before anthesis), the apices abruptly acuminate in broader examples, sharply acute in narrower examples. Sepals lanceolate to ovate, (16-) 20-30 (-38) mm long, divergent, the apices acute (appearing acuminate because margins near apex inturned in apiculate buds). Petals spatulate to narrowly spatulate, (25-) 33-48 (-54) mm long, twisted slightly and tapering below into broad cuneate claws, pale sulfur yellow with the claw greenish or rarely purplish, the apices abruptly blunt- mucronate, apiculate, or acuminate. Stamens (8-) 10-15 (-19) mm long, erect or incurved; filaments very short, (1-) 1.5-2 (-2.5) mm long; anther sacs introrse at stigma level but often basally lateral on the connective (pollen yellow to orange); con- nectives prolonged (0.5-) 1-1.5 (-2) mm beyond anther sacs into a distinct rounded- acute beak. Carpel height usually reaching about to middle of anthers; ovary ovoid, (2.5-) 3-6 (-8) mm long, each carpel with 2 prominent dorsal ridges continuing onto or tapering to bases of stigmatic branches; stigmas short, subulate, (1.5-) 2-4 (-6) mm long, divergent to nearly erect, straight or with tips slightly spreading. Flowers pleasantly spicy-fragrant. Berry broadly ovoid to subglobose with evidence of the angled condition of the ovary persisting just below the stigmas in the form of 6 sharp angles or wings.

description: Scapi erecti, versus basem papillosi, (7-) 9-27 (-33.5) cm longi, bracteis (1-) 2 (-3.5)-plo longiores. Bracteae sessiles, ellipticae vel ovatae, (5-) 7-12 (-15) cm longae, plerumque manifeste maculatae, apicibus acutis vel obtusis. Sepala lanceolata, (15-) 20-35 (-46) mm longa, horizontaliter extensis, apicibus acutis. Petala anguste elliptica vel lineari-lanceolata, (19-) 25-50 (-63) mm longa, atropurpurea vel lutea erecta, plerumque leviter torta et versus apicem incurvata, apicibus acutis. Stamina erecta, (7-) 11-20 (-26) mm longa, tria exteriora tribus interioribus leviter longiora et haec includentia, plerumque ca. 0.3-0.5 longitudinis petalorum aequantia; filamenta (2.5-) 3-5 (-6.5) mm longa, versus basem leviter dilatata; antherarum thecae introrsae in connectivis late complanatis; connectiva ultra thecas (0.5-) 1-1.5 (-2) mm prolongata in prominentias rotundatas complanatas quam latitudinem connectivi paulo breviores; pollen luteum. Carpella infra bases stigmatum angustata, gynoecium leviter obpanduriforme formantia, plerumque ca. 4/5 longitudinis staminum aequantia vel eam raro superantia; ovarium ovoideum, (4-) 6-10 (-13) mm altum, carpellorum planitiebus dorsalibus angustioribus quam planitiebus in locis conjunctionis carpellorum, ovarium in sectione transversali itaque inaequilatere hexagonum; stigmata erecta, ovarii altitudinem subaequantia, crasse subulata, ad planum apicis ovarii crassissima et basaliter ad latera ovarii gradatim decrescentia. Flores foetidi, stercorei vel odore carni putridae similes. Bacca ovoidea, leviter 6-angulata versus apicem.

description: Scape decumbent, densely puberulent, (4.5-) 6-16 (-20) cm long, (0.5-) 1-1.5 (-2.5) times as long as bracts and usually increasing in diam. toward bract bases. Bracts sessile, ovate to very broadly ovate or subcircular, (5.5-) 7-10 (-13.5) cm long, usually with mottling of silvery lighter green in the shape of a broad irregular "V" on a darker green background, the apices acute to rounded. Sepals lanceolate to ovate, (20-) 25-40 (-50) mm long, divergent, sometimes tinged with purple at the base. Petals oblanceolate to lanceolate, usually narrowly elliptic-oblanceolate (35-) 50-70 (-85) mm long, erect, twisted, dark purple, sometimes fading in upper portions to greenish yellow during flowering season, the bases rounded-sessile, the apices acute. Stamens (9.5-) 11-21 (-26) mm long, straight, erect; filaments 2.0- 3.5 (-5) mm long, about 1/3 or less length of anthers; anther sacs extrorse on broad, flattened connectives (pollen yellow); connectives prominently prolonged (1-) 2-4 (-5) mm beyond anther sacs into rounded to acute projections about equal to or longer than the filaments, the prolongation slightly dilated just above anthers. Carpel height reaching about ?/2 to 3/4 length of stamens; ovary ovoid, (3-) 4.5-7.5 (-11) mm long, deeply grooved below stigmas, with 6 sharp angles or wings; stigmas subulate, (3-) 4.5-6 (-10) mm long, divergent or spreading, with recurved tips. Berry broadly ovoid to subglobose, prominently and sharply 6-ridged, borne on naked scapes at maturity.

description: Scapi erecti, glabri, (16.5-) 23-39 (-46.5) cm longi, bracteis (2-) 2.5- vel 3 (-3.5)-plo longiores. Bracteae sessiles, typice lanceolatae, (7.5-) 10-16 (-18.5) cm longae, basaliter rotundatae, a latitudine maxima ad apicem acutum rectimarginatae, obscure vel conspicue maculatis atroviridibus maculatae praeter vittam pallide viridem secus costam currentem. Sepala lanceolata vel ovata, (35-) 40-65 (-75) mm longa (plerumque 3.0-3.5-plo longiora quam latiora), divergentia, acuta. Petala obovata vel oblanceolata, (40-) 50-80 (-100) mm longa (plerumque 2-3-plo longiora quam latiora), plerumque flavida vel viridulo-purpurea vel etiam fusco-purpurea, apicibus acutis, obtusis, vel rotundatis. Stamina (11-) 14-20 (-25) mm longa, erecta, recta vel super gynoecium arcuata; filamenta (1-) 2-3 (-4) mm longa, antheris ca. 5-7-plo breviora; antherarum thecae in connectivis linearibus complanatis laterales; connectiva ultra thecas (0.5-) 1-2 (-2.5) mm prolongata in prominentias acutas vel rotundatas quam filamenta plerumque breviores; pollen luteum. Carpella altitudine ca. 2/3 longitudinis staminum aequantia; ovarium ellipsoideum, (6-) 8-12 (-15) mm altum, per sulcos angustos in carpellis infra stigmata acute 6-porcatum; stigmata linearia, (3-) 4-9 (-12) mm longa, basaliter erecta sed supra basem late expansa, apicibus super ovarium recurvatis vel tortis. Bacca typice ellipsoidea, carpellorum sulcis dorsalibus quam planitiebus conjunctione carpellorum formatis profundioribus et angustioribus.

description: Scapes erect, glabrous or scabrous near top, (10.5-) 17.5-40 (-51.5) cm long, (1.4-) 2.2-3.7 (-4.8) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, broadly ovate-elliptic (oval), varying to very broadly elliptic or ovate, (5.5-) 7.5-13.5 (-16) cm long, mottled with two shades of green, sometimes scabrous on lower veins, the bases usually rounded, overlapping, the apices acuminate, obtuse, or acute. Sepals lanceolate (variable towards oblong or elliptic), (23-) 30-55 (-75) mm long, widely divergent usually green, sometimes purple, purple-tinged basally, or purple-margined on upper surface, the apices acute-rounded. Petals oblanceolate to elliptic-obovate, (32-) 40- 70 (-90) mm long, erect to divergent-erect, sometimes twisted, brownish purple, purple, greenish purple, or yellow, the bases usually cuneate (sometimes narrowed toward spatulate but not clawed), the apices acute-rounded, acutish, or blunt. Stamens nearly straight, erect, (10-) 13-22 (-28) mm long, usually more than 1/4 and less than 1/3 as long as petals; filaments (1.5-) 2-3.5 (-5) mm long, dilated basally; anther sacs usually lateral (pollen yellow or olive) on linear connectives (sometimes introrse on broadened connectives); connectives slightly prolonged up to 0.5 mm (range 0-1 mm) into rounded projections. Carpels usually about 4/5 as tall as stamens; ovary ovoid, (4-) 6-10 (-15) mm long, usually 6-ridged (rarely winged), nearly hexagonal in cross-section; stigmas linear-subulate to thickly subulate, (2.5-) 4-11 (-15) mm long, usually divergent and slightly outcurved, varying to erect or spreading. Flowers with musky (sometimes fetid) or spicy odor, usually resembling that of Asimina or Calycanthus. Berry ovoid, 6-angled or smooth (angles evident only at apex), the stigmas usually withering.

description: Scapi erecti, (25-) 28-44 (-54) cm longi, bracteis (2.0-) 2.3-2.5 (-2.9)-plo longiores. Bracteae sessiles, ovatae vel latissime ovatae, (6.5-) 11-18 (-20) cm longae, atrovirides, obscure vel conspicue maculatis perviridioribus et pallidius viridibus maculatae, infra hebetatae, basibus leviter rotundatis vel obtusis, apicibus plerumque leviter acuminatis vel raro obtusis vel rotundatis. Sepala lanceolata, (32-) 42-70 (-90) mm longa, divergentia, viridula vel basaliter purpurea, apicibus acutis vel rotundato-acutis. Petala oblanceolata, (40-) 65-105 (-140) mm longa, (2.7-) 3.3-4.6 (-6.0)-plo longiora quam latiora, erecta, lurido-purpurea, plerumque infra magis atrantia quam extra, basaliter cuneata, apicibus acutis vel leviter rotundatis. Stamina erecta, (14-) 16-25 (-30) mm longa; filamenta brevia, (2-) 3-4 (-5) mm longa, versus basem dilatata, atropurpurea; antherarum thecae introrsae, (12-) 14-21 (-24) mm longae, in connectivis linearibus complanatis; connectiva usque ad 0.5 mm prolongata; pollen luteum. Carpella altitudine ca. 4/5 longitudinis staminum aequantia; ovarium ovoideum, (7-) 9-13 (-15) mm altum, atropurpureum, in sectione transversali rotundato-hexagonum; stigmata crasse subulata, (5-) 6-8 (-10) mm longa, erecta, atropurpurea. Flores odorem sub anthesi mucidum, interdum versus finem anthesis foetidum exhalentes. Bacca ovoidea vel ellipsoidea, obscure angulata modo infra stigmata succulenta persistentiaque.

description: Scapes erect, glabrous, (16-) 20-32.5 (-36) cm long, (2.4-) 3.2-3.5 (-4.3) times as long as bracts. Bracts sessile, elliptic or elliptic-ovate to obovate, narrowly or broadly so, (6-) 6.5-9.5 (-13) cm long, dark green, usually distinctly mottled with small darker spots, the apices rounded, obtuse, or acute. Sepals narrowly lance-oblong, relatively short, (15-) 18-26 (-34) mm long, basally at right angles to scape axis, widely spreading in open curve and finally reflexed at the tips, usually dark purple on upper surface, the apices slightly acuminate-blunt or obtuse (buds often slightly apiculate). Petals linear-elliptic or linear oblanceolate, usually relatively short, (17-) 21-35 (-46) mm long, (1.5-) 2.0-2.3 (-3.0) times as long as stamens, erect, usually dark purple or yellow, the apices acute or rounded. Stamens erect, (8.5-) 11-17 (-19) mm long; filaments (1.5-) 2-3 (-3.5) mm long, nearly straight; anther sacs introrse on linear connectives (pollen creamy-yellow); connectives usually slightly prolonged (0-) 0.5 (-1.0) mm into short beak. Carpel height usually reaching only slightly more than ?/2 length of stamens; ovary ovoid, (3.5-) 4-7 (-11) mm long, 3-angled in cross-section; stigmas subulate, usually short, (1.5-) 2.0-4.5 (-6.5) mm long, basally divergent with tips recurved, extending sides of ovary to lyre-shaped outline. Flowers with odor like morel fungus (Morchella). Berry ovoid, smooth; stigmas usually withering-persistent.

description: Pseudobulbs fairly large, pyriform, sheathing leaves numerous. Leaves linear- lanceolate, 18-60 cm long, 2-4 cm wide. Floral bracts papery, broadly lanceolate, 1.7-3.5 cm long, 0.7-1.0 cm wide. Pedicel 2.0-3.5 cm long. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, 4-6 cm long, 0.3-0.7 cm wide, lateral sepals falcate-lanceolate, acuminate, 3.5-8.0 cm long, 0.2-0.6 cm wide. Petals shorter than the sepals, falcate, acuminate, 2.2-5.5 cm long, 0.3-0.7 cm wide. Lip ovate-oblong, long-acuminate, usually not reflexed, 1.6-3.3 cm long, 0.7-1.5 cm wide. Callus of two arching basal lamellae with two much smaller terminal tooth-like recurved masses. Column 0.4-0.6 cm high. Stipe broadly obdeltoid. Venezuela, Colombia.
bibliographicCitation: Williams, Norris H. 1972. A reconsideration of Ada and the glumaceous Brassias (Orchidaceae). Brittonia. 24: 93-110.

description: Pseudobulbs elliptic-oblong. Leaves linear-lanceolate to elliptic-ovate, 7-45 cm long, 1.0-4.5 cm wide, numerous sheathing leaves. Floral bracts as long as the pedicel, 2.0-4.5 cm long, 0.6-1.2 cm wide, papery, slightly appressed to the pedicel or to one side of the pedicel, the pedicel 1.4-2.7 cm long. Sepals all alike, linear, acuminate, 1.5-4.5 cm long, 0.3-0.5 cm wide. Petals shorter than the sepals, 1.5-2.2 cm long, 0.3-0.4 cm wide, linear-lanceolate, often somewhat falcate. Sepals and petals usually spotted with maroon or brown spots, the spots rarely lacking and the sepals and petals then brown with light yellow tips. Lip lanceolate, 0.9-1.1 cm long, 0.5-0.7 cm wide, often reflexed at the middle, apiculate to caudate. Callus of two fleshy lamellae termi- nated by two small rounded or pointed tooth-like masses. Column long, stout, 0.5-0.6 cm high at the back. Viscidium ovate, stipe obdeltoid with an entire apical margin, the apical margin rarely slightly emarginate, never deeply lobed. Colombia, Ecuador, Peru.

description: Caulescent, mostly unbranched woody perennials, 2-3.5 m tall, 30-50 cm dbh, forming isolated colonies of 3-15 ramets or "individuals" from rhizomes and fallen, aged trees. Rosette radially symmetrical, with a somewhat flattened top. Leaves grayish green to glaucous (new growth), numerous, linear, twisting slightly outward distally, persistent with age, reflexing and completely covering the trunk, turning gray when dead with a mustard yellow band at the reflexed base, 34-38 cm long, 4-5 mm wide at middle with the upper half 1 mm wider than the middle and the lower half 1 mm narrower than the middle, convex on both surfaces on lower half, flattened to concave on inner surface above middle; margin thin, comeous, pale yellow and minutely dentic- ulate; base 2.4-3 cm wide; spine dark reddish brown to black, 0.3-0.8 cm long, pungent. Panicle 60-80 cm long, moderately branched, erect, basally enclosed within the rosette on a short, somewhat succulent scape. Longest branches (base of inflorescence) 1 1- 13 cm long, glabrous, with 4-6 flowers per branch. Flowers creamy white, campanulate, pendant; tepals free, glabrous, outer whorl elliptical in shape, 3-3.3 cm long, 1.5 cm wide, those of inner whorl obovate in shape, 3 cm long, 2 cm wide. Stamens 1.6 - 1.7 cm long; filaments reflexed for distal 1/4  of the length, basally flattened, gradually widening toward apex, with echinate papil- lae, attached to ventral side of anthers at the base; anthers 1-2 mm long, with elon- gate, rounded, basal lobes. Pistil 2.3-2.7 cm long; ovary oblong-cylindric, 0.9-1 cm wide, with deep carpellary sutures at the base and surmounted by long-tapering shoulders to- ward style; styles 3, 6-7 mm long, with each lobe retuse, erect to spreading and the style branches papillose for 3 mm from the apex. Fruit fleshy, indehiscent, pendant, asymmetrical, 5-7 cm long, 2.3-2.5 cm wide, narrowly ovoid with apex constricted and forming an angle of about 150 with the axis; base bears persistent swollen recurved stamen bases. Seeds polymorphic, black, dull; those from middle of fruit D-shaped to cuneate, 5-7 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, thinner near placental edge (2.5 mm) thicker toward outside (4 mm); those from base and apex smaller, spherical to flattened, conforming to shape of fruit; endosperm copious, ruminate.

description: Caules inermes graciles subeomplanati vix striati non angulati minutissime puberuli demum glabrati; ramuli teretes vix striatuli evidenter pilosuli; folia distantia, internodiis 4-5 cm longis, petiolis ca. 11 mm longis crassis ca. 1.3 mm diam., eirros duos elongatos ca. 0.5 mm diam. ca. 4 mm supra basim ferentibus, dense brunneo-tomentosis, lamina inermi oblongo-lanceolata, 6.5 X 3.5 cm usque ad 12 X 4.5 cm, apice acriter acuminata, basi cordata, sinu angusto, non lobata, papyracea, 7-nervia (nervis duobus submarginalibus inclusis), supra reticulatovenosa in nervis et venulis pilosula demum glabreseente, subtus dense et persistenter pilosula, pilis albis patentibus acutis curvatis; pedunculi in axillis solitarii 16-18 mm longi recti dense pilosi; receptaculum globosum, ca. 5 mm diam.; bracteolae nigreseentes, pilosae; flores multi, 50 vel plures; pedicelli 3-6 mm longi, parce pilosuli; alabastra clavata, ca. 3.5 mm longa et 1.5 mm lata apice pilos 1-paucos gerentia; petala exteriora et interiora aequalia, ca. 4 mm longa et 1.3 mm lata, apice ineurvata et subeucullata saepe pilum singulum gerentia, integra, costa obvia; filamenta ca. 2 mm longa, crassa, ca. 0.4 mm lata; antherae ca. 1.5 mm longae; flores foeminei ignoti.
bibliographicCitation: Morton, Conrad V. 1962. A reexamination of Mexico Smilax (Smilacaceae). Brittonia. 14: 299-309.

description: Ramuli folia et inflorescentias ca. 9 ferentes, internodiis 2-2.5 cm longis, dense luteo-hirsuti pilis crassis acutis patentibus ca. 1.5 mm longis; petioli crassi, 10-13 mm longi, ca. 1.6 mm diam., densissime luteo-villosi, cirros graciles luteovillosos ca. 4 mm supra basim ferentes; lamina foliorum oblongo-lanceolata, 9 X 3 cm usque ad 19 X 7 cm, apice acuminata, basi cordata, sinu angusto, non lobata, 9-nervia (nervis exterioribus submarginalibus inclusis), chartacea, supra evidenter et persistenter villosa, pilis patentibus elongatis 1-2 mm longis, subtus in venis venulisque valde villosa; pedunculi 10-12 mm longi, dense luteovillosi; receptacula globosa, ca. 4.5 mm lata, bracteolis villosis; flores numerosi; alabastra valde immatura atra, pilos paucos elongatos ferentia; baccae in pedunculo ca. 6, globosae, 8-10 mm latae, lucentes.

description: Planta acaulis monocarpica; foliis 25-30 rosulatis ovato-lanceolatis carnosocoriaceis persistenter glaucis, crassis 35-50 cm longis, 15-25 em latis, spina terminali aculeato-pungenti 1-3 cm lonlga; spinis nmarginalibus inaequalibus, 1-2-euspidatis, obtusis, brunneis, 1-4 mm longis, 2-9 mm latis; scapo infloreseentia inclusa 2-4 m alto, gracili; bracteolis seariosis, subulato-lanceolatis, 1-2 em longis; pedunculis 1-2-fureatis, 8-25 mm longis; ovario cylindrico viridi, 15 mm longo apice constrieto; tubo nullo; segmentis aequalibus, 17-18 mm longis exterioribus 5 mm latis, interioribus 4 mm latis, pallidi-luteis, adscendentibus; filamentis 30-35 mm longis ad basin segmentorum insertis; antheris luteis 13 mm longis. Acauleseent, mostly single, few-leaved, light gray or white-glaucous; open rosettes with ca. 30 leaves at maturity; leaves ovate to ovate-lanceolate, shortacuminate, openly ascending, nearly plane above but briefly and narrowly channeled apically, the margins variously serrate with flattened, blunt, 1- to 2-cuspidate, dark brown, fine or coarse teeth; epidermis finely and densely papillate; spine acicular, dark brown, rounded above and below, not decurrent or decurrent for about its own length in a corneous margin; infloreseence spicate, the stalk flowering from near the base, erect; upper bracts and bracteoles similar, 1-2 cm long, 3 mm wide at the deltoid base, searious, recurved, long attenuate, with a dark midvein; flowers inconspicuous, 33-35 mm long (from base of ovary to apex of tepals) at anthesis; tepals pale yellow or yellowish white, elliptic, openly ascending, straight; anthers yellow, excentrically attached, versatile; capsules (immature) 22-24 mm long, oblong, thin-walled.-Type, in U.S. National Herbarium (US), Gentry 16436, 25-27 km NW of Tehuantepec, Oaxaca, Mexico, 22 Mar 1957, on Guiengola limestone at 125 m altitude. From the same locality, Gentry 12241, 30 Sep 1952, leaves and young plants only.
bibliographicCitation: Manning, Wayne E. 1960. The genus Juglans in South America and the West Indies. Brittonia. 12: 1-26.

description: Large, monocarpic, rosette-forming succulent herbs sometimes producing basal suckers. Leaves ca. 100-220(-244) x (8-) 12-30(-40) cm, straight or curved outward, occasionally slightly twisted, green with light glaucescence, the marginal teeth (0.1-) 0.5-3(-5) mm long, highly variable, antrorse to retrorse, deltoid to acicular, usually more or less lens-based, usually dark-colored (or reddish when fresh), the terminal spine to (5-)10-30(-45) mm long, 5-10 mm diam., comprised of hardened inrolled leaf margins, stout and sharp, recurved, or straight, or incurved, long-tapered to short and stubby, blackish. Inflorescence and stalk 3-8(-10) m tall, 8-16(-20) cm dbh, with up to 4(-5) orders of branching (excluding pedicels), the pedicels 7-25 mm long. Bulbils borne along the lower portion of the scape [Barbados, Dominica] and/or (more commonly) among the flowers. Flowers 5.5-10.5 cm long (when fully open and with filaments extended), often aborting before anthesis or shortly after opening, protandrous with the style elongating well after anther dehiscence, golden-yellow, the tepals (14-)20-25(-37) X 3-8(-12) mm, ligulate, united at the base into a broad-conical tube ca. (2-)4-12(-15) mm long; filaments (2-)2.5-6(-6.5) cm long, inserted at or very near the top of the floral tube; anthers 10-25 mm long, attached at or near the center; ovary (18-)20-42(-48) mm long, fusiform and constricted apically beneath the floral tube, containing anatropous ovules [Barbados]; style (2.4-)3.8-6.5 cm long, elongating late in anthesis (though sometimes protruding from bud prior to stamen elongation); stigma 3-lobed, with the lobes separating and becoming moist after style elongation [Barbados]. Loculicidal capsules 3-6(-6.2) cm long, ca. 2 cm diam. when closed, often failing to form, opening loculicidally to near the base, the valves usually elliptic or oblong, often beaked, divergent, the basal stipe 2-10 mm long, comprised of an unthickened portion of the ovary between the pedicel and the expanded portion of the capsule. Seeds 6.5-9 mm in the greatest dimension, D-shaped or irregularly polygonal, black (or white when infertile), wafer-thin.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, G. K. 2000. A taxonimic revision of the genus Agave (Agavaceae) in the Lesser Antilles, with an ethnobotanical hypothesis. Brittonia. 52: 218-233.

description: Planta perennis, caespitosa, rosula densa; folia viridi-glauca, lineari-triangularis vel falcata, recta vel arcuata, acuminata, striata, marginibus hyalinis subtiliter denticulatis, (1-)20-35(-50) cm longis, (0.7)0.8-1.2(1.4) cm latis, spina terminali rigida (8-)10-19(-23) mm longa; inflorescentia (42-)70-170 cm longa (pedunculo incluso), in spicam densa; flores geminatio, infundibuliformes, (20-)22-23(-24) mm longo, ovario viridi, cylindrico, 7-9 mm longo, 3-3.5(-4) mm lato, tubo 7-7.5(-10) mm longo, perianthii segmentis 4-6(-8) mm longis, 2-4(-6) mm latis, ovato-ellipticis, incurvatis; filamenta (22-)28-38(-45) mm longa; capsulae subsphaericae, 7-13 mm longae, 6-9 mm latae.
bibliographicCitation: Carrillo-Reyes, Pablo, et al. 2003. Agave rzedowskiana, a new species in subgenus Littaea (Agavaceae) from western Mexico. Brittonia. 55: 240-244.

description: Plant perennial, cespitose. Stem repent to 50 cm long. Rosette hemispheric, compact, 25-45(-65) cm diam., 20-40 cm tall, grayish green. Leaves 100-260 in each rosette, linear-triangular, straight or falcate, rigid, acuminate, striate on both surfaces, glaucous or green, (11-)20-35(-50) X (0.7-)0.8- 1.2(-1.4) cm (width in the middle; leaf widest at base, to 2.1 cm); margins hyaline, minutely serrulate with 17-30 teeth per cm; spines (8-)10-19(-23) mm long, rigid, reddish brown. Inflorescence including the peduncle, (42-)70-170 cm long, inclined to decumbent, occasionally sinuous; fertile portion to 10-32(-53) cm long, densely spicate, located in the upper 1/8-1/3 portion of the scape; bracts of the peduncle 2.5-9 X 0.5-0.7 cm, widest near the base, narrowed upward, acicular, pale yellow, base pale pink or pale purple, terminal spine reddish brown; floral bracts triangular, 4.2-0.7 cm long, the upper ones shorter, apex caudate, 1.9-3.5 X 0.6-0.7 cm, pale yellow, base purple, persistent, longer than the flowers. Flowers 50-200 pairs per spike, funnelform, greenish purple, (20-)22-23(-24) mm long; pedicels less than 1 mm long at anthesis, to 2 mm in fruit. Ovary 7-9 X 3- 3.5(-4) mm, cylindric to fusiform, glabrous, slightly protruding from the perianth tube; perianth tube 7-7.5(-10) X 9-10 mm. Tepals incurved, the inner tepals slightly narrower than the outer ones, ovate-elliptic, 4-6(-8) X 2-4(-6) mm, with a tuft of microscopic hairs at apex. Anther filaments (22-)28-38(-45) mm long, inserted at the middle of the tube; anthers centric, arched, oblong, rounded at both extremes, 8-10(-12.5) mm long, yellow or brownish. Style filiform, sinuate when young, straight at anthesis 40-48(-51) mm. Capsules erect or appressed, nearly deltoid in cross section, subspheric, 7-13 X 6-9 mm, smooth or verrucose, dehiscence apical; the perianth occasionally persistent. Seeds 2.4-3.1 X 1.2-2.1 mm, hemispheric, triangular in cross section, black.

description: Bulbi ovoidei, tunicis exterioribus fibroso-reticulatis; folia cujusque scapi 3-5.5 (-6.5) mm lata, 11-18 (-20) cm longa, scapo (11-) 12-21 cm longo aequilonga vel parum breviora; bracteae 2-4, partim indivisae, plerumque 1-nerviae, 8-14 mm longae; perianthii urceolato-campanulati roselli tepala (6-) 7-8.5 (-10) mm longa, exteriora lanceolato-ovata vel lanceolata acuminata, basi gibbo alte carinata, interiora anguste lanceolata acuminata; ovarium processibus 6 parvis tuberculiformibus circa styli basin nidulantibus cristatum; capsula obovoidea (3.2-) 3.5-4.5 mm longa; semina atra nitida irregulatim alveolata ac minute pustulosa.

description: Bulb more or less ovoid, usually one of a cluster with long slender rhizomes from the base, inner coats whitish, outer coats grayish or brownish, membranaceous with or without obscure cellular markings; leaves 3-5, channeled, concave-convex in cross section, 1-2 mm broad, shorter than or equal to scape in length, green at anthesis; scape 1-3 dm tall, terete or somewhat ridged; spathe membranaceous, acuminate, breaking before anthesis into two separate or partially united, lanceolate, acuminate, 3-5-nerved, ultimately reflexed bracts; umbels with few flowers, the pedicels being replaced (all or in part) by ovoid bulbils, some of which may in turn bear secondary umbels; pedicels (when present) two to several times the length of the perianth; perianth broadly campanulate, the spreading segments 3-6 mm long, lanceolate, acute to acuminate, entire, white with deep red midribs which are scarcely thickened at base; stamens shorter than perianth, filaments broadly dilated below and united into a cup, anthers oblong and obtuse; ovary crestless, style linear, shorter than perianth, stigma capitate; seeds not observed.

bibliographicCitation: Meerow, Alan W., et al. 1999. Two new species of Alstroemeria L. (Alstroemeriaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 51: 439-444.

description: Herb, 4.5-6.5 dm tall; roots not tuberous at apex; rhizomes thickened to 5 mm diam.; vegetative stems arching to decumbent, wiry, very slender, the pseudo-internodes abruptly zig-zag, 20-35 cm long, ca. 1.5 mm diam., the leaves arranged alternately throughout the length of the stem; flowering stems appearing after the vegetative, suberect to arching, 4.5-6.5 dm X 3-4 mm; vegetative leaves 8-10, nonaggregated, nonresupinate, narrowly lanceolate, 4-8.5 x 0.8-0.9 cm, leathery, glaucous on both sides, the margins cartilaginous, apically acute, sessile; leaves of the flowering stem 8-10, narrowly lanceolate, nonresupinate, erect, 7-11 cm X 3.7-8 mm, sessile, the uppermost scarious and bract-like. Inflores- cence of 3-5 cymes (rays), each 2-flowered, subtended by 2 linear-lanceolate bracts 9- 10 X ca. 1.5 mm, pedicels slender, 8-2.2 cm long, subtended by a small scarious bracteole, 2-8 mm long. Flowers 6-10, 3.2-3.7 cm long; perianth slightly zygo- morphic, funnelform-campanulate, 3-3.5 mm wide at base, spreading to 2 cm wide distally; tepals of outer whorl 2.8-3.3 cm long, ca. 1.2 cm wide at middle, obtrullate, acute to minutely apiculate at apex, atten- uate-unguiculate at base, 3-nerved, the mar- gins slightly undulate above the middle, abaxial surface reddish orange, adaxial surface yellow; inner tepals 3-3.5 cm long, ca. 1 cm wide at middle, narrowly obtrullate, acute at apex, attenuate-unguiculate at base, the margins coarsely crenate in upper half, abaxial surface orange, adaxial surface yellow, suffused with orange at margins, sparsely spotted purple-brown; stamens not exceeding perianth; filaments 27.5-30 mm long; anthers 3-3.4 X 2.2-2.4 mm, greenish purple, latrorse; pollen yellow; style filiform, ca. 3 cm long; stigma 3.2-3.5 mm wide; ovary obconic, 4.5-5 mm long and wide, prominently 6-ribbed. Fruit and seed unknown. 2n = 16.
bibliographicCitation: Meerow, Alan W., et al. 1999. Two new species of Alstroemeria L. (Alstroemeriaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 51: 439-444.

description: Caulibus valde dimorphis, caulibus vegetativibus hysteranthis, et floribus fere albis a congeneribus brasiliensibus differt.
bibliographicCitation: Meerow, Alan W., et al. 1999. Two new species of Alstroemeria L. (Alstroemeriaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 51: 439-444.
