description: Trees to 20 m tall and 30 cm dbh.; bark distinctive, split at intervals leaving flat-topped ridges, these light gray, the splits darker; twigs strongly stellate-pubescent when young, partially glabrate. Wood of the "lapacho group," hard, heavy, the heartwood dark olive-brown, distinctly demarcated from the lighter sapwood. Leaves palmately compound, opposite (rarely alternate), 5-foliolate; petioles terete to semi- terete, stellate-pubescent, 6-14 cm long, pulvinate, the petiolules stellate-pubescent, articulated to the leaflets, the terminal 0.8-3.8 cm, the intermediate 0.7-3 cm, the laterals 0.2-1 cm long; leaflets oblong-obovate, abruptly acuminate to apiculate, obtuse to truncate, the terminal 5-13 cm long, 1.8-7.5 cm wide, the intermediates 4.2-11.3 cm long, 1.4-7.4 cm wide, the laterals 2.8-9.3 cm long, 1.6-5.3 cm wide, entire, membranous, somewhat glandular-lepidote above and below, stellate-pubescent, glabrescently so above, very densely so below, the many-branched multicellular hairs completely covering the undersurface of the leaf. Inflorescence terminal, very con- gested; flowers many, not opening synchronously, borne with or without leaves; peduncle and pedicels compacted, stellate-pubescent. Calyx campanulate, more or less 5-lobed, 8-15 mm long, 5-10 mm wide, woolly-pubescent with shorter stellate tomentum and thick covering of long (to 7 mm), simple hairs (a few intermediate long short-barbate hairs rarely present), the indumentum usually appearing golden yellow. Corolla yellow with reddish lines in throat, the veins in dried specimens be- coming obscure in the lobes, dried tube and corolla lobes distinctly different in color, the tube usually brownish, the lobes yellowish; infundibuliform; 4.5-8 cm long; very slightly bilabiate, the five lobes 10-24 mm long; glabrous without, villous on anterior surface within, the pubescence converging from lower four sinuses to level of stamen insertion, a few scattered hairs also on upper side of tube, the hairs relatively short, flat, uni- to multicellular, simple or once branched. Stamens didynamous, the longer filaments 15-20 mm long, the shorter 9-15 mm long; staminode 2-11 mm long; anthers 2-5 mm long. Pistil 20-27 mm long; ovary linear 4-5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, terete, lepidote to somewhat pubescent, the hairs both simple and stellate; disk patelliform, 1 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide. Fruit elongate-cylindrical, attenuate, 18-30 cm long, 1-1.4 cm wide, abundantly golden woolly-pubescent with both a short stellate tomentum and a longer indumentum of simple hairs; calyx deciduous; seeds biseriate, bialate, membranous-winged, 0.4-0.8 cm long, 1.8-2.9 cm wide.

description: Arbores ca 3.5 m usque altae. Folia opposita; petioli 5-10 mm longi, dense ferrugineo-tomentosi; laminae late ovatae vel ovales, 1.2-2.4 cm longae, 1-2 cm latae, coriaceae, basi cordatae, apice obtusae vel rotundatae, infeme dense ferrugineo-tomentosae, superne atrovirides, nitidae, margine integrae. Capitulescentiae terminales cymosae. Capitula heterogama radiata, 6-7 mm alta, 4-5 mm lata; bracteae calyculi 3-5 lineares, ca 3 mm longae, dense ferrugineo-tomentosae; phyllaria ca 8, subbiseriata, extima lanceolata, ca 5 mm longa, ca 1.5 mm lata. Flores radiati pistillati ca 5; ligulae luteae, 5-6 mm longae, 1.5-2 mm latae. Flores disci hermaphroditi 8-10; corollae tubulosae luteae, ea 6 mm longae; limbus 2-2.5 mm longus, campanulatus quinquelobus; lobi ca 1 mm longi, ca 0.5 mm lati. Achaenia (immatura) ca 1 mm longa, glabra, costata; pappi setae 4-5 mm longae.

description: Small to large trees, to 30 m tall and 50 cm dbh., smaller farther north; trunk usually unbranched for some distance, the crown rounded and spreading; bark pale to dark gray, when older somewhat split and scaly; twigs variously stellate-pubescent, becoming glabrate. Wood of the "lapacho group," hard, heavy, the heartwoo,d dark olive-brown, distinct from lighter colored sapwood. Leaves palmately compound, opposite (rarely alternate), 5-foliolate; petioles somewhat tetragonal, stellatepubescent to glabrate, 5-16 cm long, pulvinate, the petiolules stellate-pubescent to lepidote, articulated to the leaflet, the terminal 1.2-7.5 cm long, the intermediates 0.7-5.5 cm long, the laterals 0.3-1.5 cm long; leaflets broadly elliptic to obovate (rarely almost lanceolate), abruptly acuminate, obtuse to truncate or asymmetrically subcordate, the terminal 6-18 cm long, 4-11 cm wide, the intermediates 5-17 cm long, 3.4-10 cm wide, the laterals 2.5-13 cm long, 1.4-8 cm wide, entire to dentate, generally membranous, somewhat glandular-lepidote above and below, stellate- pubescent sometimes above, always to some extent below, the much-branched multicellular hairs on the main nerves and scattered on leaf undersurface. Inflorescence terminal, sometimes appearing axillary, somewhat congested, the compacted peduncle and pedicels stellately pubescent, flowers few to many, not opening synchronously, borne with or without leaves. Calyx campanulate, 5-lobed, 8-11 (5-12) mm long, 3-10 mm wide, stellately pubescent, the stellate hairs usually intergrading with abundant short-barbate hairs, the indumentum usually reddish brown. Corolla yellow with reddish lines in throat, the veins in dried specimens distinctly inter- connected and readily apparent to the margins of lobes, the dried tube and lobes indistinguishable in color; infundibuliform; 3-8 cm long; slightly bilabiate, the lobes 9-26 mm long; glabrous without, within with four lines of simple or usually once- branched 2- or 3-celled hairs from four lower sinuses to level of stamen insertion, the lines converging, usually near level of stigma. Pistil 18-31 mm long; ovary linear, 3.5-5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, terete, glabrous to lepidote or very sparsely stellate-pubescent, appearing rather rugose when dry; disk patelliform, 0.5-1 mm long, 2-3 mm wide. Fruit elongate-cylindrical, attenuate and usually recurved at the ends, the length variable, 11-50 cm long, 0.6-2.0 cm wide, very sparingly short-stellate pubescent; calyx deciduous; seeds biseriate, bialate, membranous-winged, 0.4-0.9 cm long, 1.4-3.3 cm wide.

description: Trees 10-27 m tall, to 1 m dbh.; trunk usually straight and cylindrical, sometimes twisted or fluted, the branches opposite, ascending; crown usually spreading; buttresses if present 3 or 4 and narrow, to 2.5 m tall; bark moderately rough, finely ridged, dark gray to brown, ca. 1 cm thick, the inner bark white; twigs glandular- lepidote. Wood of medium density, light grayish brown, with distinct pattern, the heartwood brownish, not well differentiated from the white sapwood; odor when fresh suggesting watermelon. Leaves palmately compound, opposite, often anisophyl- Ious, 5-foliolate; petioles semiterete, lepidote, 5-30 cm long, pulvinate, the petiolules lepidote, articulated to the leaflet bases, the terminal 2-10 cm long, the intermediates 1.5-9.5 cm long, the laterals 0.2-2.4 cm long; leaflets elliptic-oblong to elliptic-ovate, acute to acuminate (very rarely retuse), rounded to cuneate, the terminal largest, 8-33 cm long, 3-18 cm wide, intermediates 6-30 cm long, 3-16 cm wide, laterals 3.5-23 cm long, 1.4-12 cm wide, entire, subcoriaceous (membranous in seedlings), glandular-lepidote, otherwise glabrous. Inflorescence terminal, open, dichotomously branched; many-flowered; flowers usually in twos, borne with or without leaves; peduncle and pedicel densely lepidote. Calyx campanulate, bilabiate, 15-19 (11-21) mm long, 6-12 mm wide, densely glandular-lepidote. Corolla white to pink or lavender, throat opens yellow turning white; infundibuliform; 5-10 cm long; slightly bilabiate; glabrous without, sparsely pubescent within, the lobe margins ciliate, two lines of small mostly unicellular hairs from two lower sinuses to just above level of stamen insertion. Stamens didynamous, the longer filaments 14-19 mm long, the shorter filaments 10-14 mm long; staminode 2-6 mm long; anthers 5-7 mm long. Pistil 19-32 mm long; ovary linear, 5-8 mm long, 1 mm wide, terete in cross-section, densely glandular-lepidote; disk cupuliform, 2 mm long, 2 mm wide. Fruit elongate- cylindrical, attenuate at both ends, to 38 cm long, 1.5 cm wide, glandular-lepidote; calyx usually persistent; seeds biseriate, bialate, membranous-winged, 0.7-1.0 cm long, 2.8-4.4 cm wide.

description: Trees 5-14 m tall, to 60 cm dbh., usually slender with spreading branches; o-ld bark gray, relatively smoolth; twigs terete, glabrate, the tips of the young shoot mealy-pubescent. Wood dark greenish brown, very dense, the vessels containing lapachol. Leaves ptalmately compound, opposite, often anisopnhyllous, 5-foliolate; petioles nearly terete, lepido-te and puberulous, 4-13 c.m long, pulvinate, the petiolules lepidote and slightly pubescent, articulated to the leaflet blades, the terminal 1-4 cm, the intermediates 0.9-4 cm, the laterals 0.2-2 cm long; leaflets ovate to ellip-tic, acuminate, cuneate to rounded, rarely subcordate, the terminal largest, 5-18 cm long, 1.5-8 cm wide, the intermediates 4-14 cm long, 2.8-9 cm wide, the basals smallest, 2.2-11 cm long, 1.5-8.3 cm wide, entire, rarely serrulate when young, membranous, somewhat glandular-lepidote above and below, pilose below at least inC axils of lateral veins, often slightly so a.bove on midrib, the hairs multicellular, simple., or sometimes forked. Inflorescence terminal, usually congested; flowers in threes, not opening synchronously, seldom borne while leaves are otn tree; peduncle and pedicel distinctively whitish to tannish mealy-pubescent. Calyx cupuliform to campanulate, truncatea or sometimes obscurely 5-lobed 4-6 (p3-9 ) mm long, 3-6 mm wide, prominently mealy-pubescent with small, thick-stellate hairs. Corolla pink to purple, the yellow throat turning to purple in older flowers; elongate-campanulate; 4-7.5 cm long; very slightly bilabiate; puberulous without, a few scattered simple hairs within. Stamens didynamous, the longer filaments 16-23 mm long, the shorter 10-16 mm; staminode 3-7 mm long; anthers 5-7 mm long. Pistil 27-34 mm long; ovary linear, 3-4 mm long, 1 mm wide, tetragonal in cross-section, glabrous to slightly lepidote; disk cupuliform, slightly lobate, 1-1.5 mm long, 2 mm wide. Fruit elongate-cylindrical, attenuate at both ends, 12-56 cm long, 1.3-2.5 cm wide, glabrous; calyx deciduous; seeds appearing uniseriate, large and thick, bialate, membranous-winged, 1-1.6 cm long, 3-4.8 cm wide.

description: Erect shrubs or small trees 1-4 m tall, sometimes with twisted trunks, the branches slender and sprawling, thickened at each dichotomy; bark light gray, smooth, very thin. Wood whitish, of light to medium density. Leaves 1- to 3-foliolate, opposite; petioles semiterete to terete, lepidote, 2.3-10 cm long, somewhat pulvinate, the petiolules lepidote, merging into the leaflet base and sometimes not differentiated, conspicuously articulated to the petiole, the terminal 1-3.5 cm long, laterals when present 2-15 cm long; leaflets narrowly oblong, acute, attenuate (laterals often subsessile), the terminal largest, 10-19 cm long, 2.1-5.6 cm wide, the laterals when present 5-16 cm long, 1.1-3.6 cm wide, entire, subcoriaceous, heavily glandular- lepidote below, less so above. Inflorescences terminal on reduced branches subtended by two larger lateral branches; cyme 2- to 5-flowered; peduncle and pedicel lepidote. Calyx 2- or 3-labiate, 10-20 mm long, 4-10 mm wide, glandular-lepidote. Corolla white with two yellow lines in throat; infundibuliform; 5-6.8 cm long; slightly bilabiate; glabrous without, with two lines of thick hairs in throat within which converge from two lower sinuses to meet at the level of stamen insertion, a few scattered hairs on lobes and in sinuses. Stamens didynamous, the longer filaments 18-23 mm long, the shorter 14-16 mm long, staminode 5-7 mm long; anthers 5-6 mm long. Pistil 25-30 mm long; ovary linear, 5 mm long, 1 mm wide, very densely glandular-lepidote, the scales extending up base of style; disk thick, pulvinate. Fruit oblong, attenuate at both ends, 8-9 cm long, 1.6-2.6 cm wide.

description: Trees up to 20 m tall and 22 cm dbh; bark smooth, reddish, peeling off in vertical stripes; wood extremely hard, yellowish white. Stipules connate at base (rarely free) and often connected to petioles, deltoid and not acuminate, glabrous outside, readily caducous, reddish green, leaving a scar encircling the stem and connected to the petiole scar, 1-2 mm wide. Blades 14-20 cm long, 6-11 cm wide, length: width 1.5-1.7: 1, obovate, acute at base, obtuse at apex; dark green above and pale green below, semi coriaceous; drying reddish brown, semi leathery; glabrous above and below. Primary, secondary, and tertiary veins glabrous and prominent below, secondary veins 7-10 each side; tertiary veins parallel throughout. Petioles 25-35 mm long, 3-4 mm thick, terete to adaxially flattened or narrowly concave, glabrous. Domatia absent. Inflorescences terminal and solitary, corymbose and densely branched distally, with opposite branches terminating into cymules, (7)14-20 cm long; lateral branches 6-18 cm long with terminal cymules 4.5-6 cm wide. Rachis basally subterete and distally decussately compressed, rachis and branches white or golden minute-puberulent; flowers on distal branches in condensed cymules. Distal bracts absent to fo- liose, deltoid to obovate (when foliose); bracteoles subtending the flowers absent or reduced to microscopic scales. Flowers fragrant, sessile to short-pedicellate, pedicel 0-1.5 mm long, puberulent; hypanthium narrowly obconical, 1-1.5 mm long, ca. 1 mm wide, puberulent. Calyx truncate to short-lobed, 0.3-0.6 mm long, 1-1.7 mm wide, golden puberulent, pale green; calyx lobes barely distinguishable, 0-0.5 mm long, in some flowers one lobe of the calyx expanded into a calycophyll. Calycophylls obovate, blades 3.5-5 cm long and 1.4-3 cm wide, with peltate venation, white to cream white; petioles 1-2 cm long. Corolla funnelform and deeply lobed, 3.5-4.5 mm long, white to greenish white; tube short cylindrical, 1.5-2.5 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm wide, pubescent outside and glabrous in- side; corolla lobes 5, rounded and with a fringed margin, 0.6-0.7 mm wide, sparsely puberulent outside, glabrous inside. Sta- mens 5, obviously exserted, equal length; filaments attached 1.5-2 mm from the base of the tube; anthers elliptic, 5 mm long and 3 mm wide; dorsifixed, base rounded, apex acute to short mucronate; filaments terete, basally flattened and connate to throat, sparsely white pilose at base (sometimes glabrous throughout). Style exserted, ca. 4 mm long, terete, glabrous; style branches opening after complete release of pollen, ca. 1 mm long, stigmatic surface microscopically (40X) papillose. Capsules narrowly obovoid, acute at base, narrowly rounded at apex, 8-15 mm long, 3.5-5 mm wide, capsule black, sparsely minute-puberulent, without lenticels; disk black and glabrous, not exceeding the calyx; disk-loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules. Seeds strongly bipolar, with acute apices, 8-13 mm long and 0.9-2 mm wide including wing.

description: Shrub, epiphytic, 1-2 m tall; young branches angled, 1-2 mm diam., glabrous to sparsely pilose; older stems with a light gray bark. Leaves opposite, subequal; peti- oles 8-12 mm long, glabrous, unwinged, slightly channeled above; blade elliptic to lanceolate, 4-9 X 1.7-2.5 cm, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous, shiny and dark green above, dull and pale green below, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, the secondary veins 3 or 4 per side, the venation slightly impressed above, prominent below, domatia present though often poorly developed, glandular pits few, scattered. Flowers solitary or paired, sometimes appearing axillary; pedicel 1-2 cm long, glabrous, thicker above; calyx campanulate, magenta to pink, the tube 3-5 mm long, the enations linear, 3-5 mm long, broadly winged, the wings 3-5 mm wide, glabrous to sparsely ciliate near the tip, the tip incurved, the fruiting calyx accrescent, the tube to 6 mm long, the lobes 4-5 mm long, the wings 7-10 mm wide; corolla tubular, the tube white to pale violet, 2-2.7 cm X 3-4 mm, membranaceous, the lobes violet, ligulate to rounded, 3 X 2-3 mm, ciliolate; stamens attached 3-4 mm above the base of the corolla tube, the filaments 1.8-2.3 cm long, glabrous; staminode 8 mm long, filiform; pistil glabrous, the ovary globose, 2-3 mm long, the style slender, 1.8-2.3 cm long, the stigma slightly capitate. Immature berry white to pink.

description: Shrub or small tree, epiphytic or terrestrial, 1-4 m tall; young branches strongly angled, light brown, 3-6 mm diam., glabrous; older branches with a light gray bark. Leaves opposite, equal; petioles 4-10 mm long, slightly winged to unwinged, glabrous or rarely sparsely pubescent, terete to slightly channeled; blade elliptic, 3-8 X 2- 3 cm, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous, base broadly cuneate, margin slightly revolute when dry, apex acute, the secondary veins 1-3 per side, impressed above, usually prominent below, with prominent domatia in the axils of veins below, glandular pits few, near the base of the leaf. Flowers in condensed panicles, few-flowered; primary peduncle 0.5-1.3(-1.8) cm long, secondary peduncles to 1 mm long; bracts narrowly triangular, 3-8 mm long, glabrous to inconspicuously lepidote, sparsely ciliate; pedicel 1-1.7 cm long in flower, 2-3 cm long in fruit, glabrous to sparsely lepidote; calyx campanulate, pink to mauve, the tube 3-4 mm long, slightly 5-ridged, glabrous to sparsely lepidote, the lobes linear, 4-6 mm long; corolla tubular, magenta, 1.5-2 cm X 2-3 mm, the lobes rounded, 1.5-2 mm long, sparsely ciliate; stamens inserted 4-5 mm above the base of the corolla tube, with a ring of trichomes at their base, the filaments 1.3-1.5 cm long; staminode 2-3 mm long; pistil glabrous, the ovary globose to oblate, 1-1.5 X 1-1.5 mm, the style 1.5 cm long. Berry globose, white, 5-8 mm diam.; seeds many.

description: Shrub, epiphytic, to 2.5 m tall; young branches terete to slightly angled, pubescent or glabrous; older branches with a gray-brown bark. Leaves opposite, equal to subequal; petiole 0.5-1.5 cm long, slightly winged, glabrous; blade elliptic, ovate or obovate, 4-12 x 2-6.5 cm, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous, shiny above, base cuneate, margin often ciliate, apex obtuse to acuminate, the veins often impressed above, prominent below with 4 or 5 secondary veins per side, without or with very few glandular pits below, pocket domatia in the vein axils below. Flowers in panicles, sometimes few per panicle, the primary peduncle 0.5-1 cm long, pilose, the bracteoles narrowly triangular, 1-2 mm long, pilose; pedicels 1-2.5 cm long, thick above, glabrous; calyx campanulate, green, 2-4 mm long, glabrous, the lobes narrowly triangular, 1-5 mm long; corolla red to purple, tubular, 2-3.5 cm X 3-5 mm, the lobes subequal, rounded, 2-4 mm long, often ciliate; stamens inserted 4-5 mm above the base of the corolla tube, the filaments filiform, 2-2.5 cm long, with a ring of trichomes at their base; staminode 0.4-1 cm long, filiform; pistil glabrous, the ovary globose to oblate, 1.5-2 mm wide, the style 2.5 cm long, the stigma slightly capitate. Berry globose to oblate, 5-10 mm diam., the seeds 10-12, reticulate.

description: Shrub, epiphytic, to 1.5 m tall; young branches 2-4 mm diam., terete to slightly angular below the raised leaf bases, pubescent with stiff, straight, glabrous or with multicellular trichomes, glabrescent; older branches with a light gray-brown bark. Leaves opposite to subopposite, anisophyllous; larger leaves with petioles 4-13 mm long, 0.8-1.7 mm thick, glabrous to slightly puberulous when young; blade elliptic, 5- 7.5 X 2.5-4 cm, membranaceous to subcoriaceous, shiny above, sparsely pubescent below, base cuneate, apex rounded to acute, the midvein impressed above, prominent below, the secondary veins impressed above and below, 2-3 secondary veins per side, glandular pits sparse on the leaf underside, pocket domatia sometimes present in the vein axils below; smaller leaves similar but the lamina 2-4 X 1.5-3 cm. Flowers in short, axillary panicles, sometimes condensed and appearing fasciculate; primary peduncle to 8 mm long; bracts narrowly triangular, 2-4 mm long, glabrous or sparsely villous; pedicels 1-2.5 cm long, glabrous or very sparsely villous; calyx narrowly campanulate, slightly pubescent on the angles, the tube 3-5 mm long, the teeth narrowly triangular, slightly winged, 5-8 mm long; corolla tubular, reddish violet to pink, 1.5-2.5 cm X 3-5 mm, glabrous, the lobes rounded, 1-2.5 X 1-2 mm; stamens attached 3-4 mm from the base of the co- rolla tube, with a ring of trichomes where attached; filaments 1.8-2 cm long, glabrous above the base; staminode 4-6 mm long, filiform; pistil glabrous, the ovary ovoid, 1-1.5 mm wide, the style 1.6-2.2 cm long, the stigma slightly capitate. Berry globose to subglobose, green turning white, to 1 cm diam.

description: Shrub, epiphytic, to 3 m tall; bark gray-brown; stems angled to winged, glabrous, to 5 mm diam., with raised leaf bases at the nodes. Leaves opposite, subequal to equal across the node; petioles 5-14 mm long, glabrous or sparsely pilose, unwinged, channeled above; blade ovate to obovate or lanceolate, 6.5-14.5 X 3-6.2 cm, coriaceous, glabrous, shiny above, base cuneate, apex acuminate, the secondary veins 3 or 4 per side, impressed above, prominent below, glandular pits in fields between the veins below, pocket domatia occasionally present in the axils of the midvein and secondary veins toward the base of the blade. Flowers in congested, axillary panicles; primary peduncle to 1.5 cm long; bracts narrowly triangular, 3-5 mm long, pubescent; the secondary peduncles to 7 mm long; bracteoles to 3 mm long, ovate, acuminate; pedicels 2.5-3.5 cm long, thicker above; calyx funnelform, the tube 5-9 mm long, red to purple, the lobes narrowly triangular, unequal, 7-13 mm long, long-acuminate, glabrous to minutely ciliate; corolla cylindric, slightly ampliate above, 3.5-4 cm long, 6-7 mm diam., reddish pink to red, fleshy, the upper lobes rounded, 3-4 X 3- 4 mm, the lateral lobes rounded to ligulate, 4-5 x 4 mm, the median lobe ligulate, 4- 6 X 3-4 mm; stamens attached 6-9 mm from the base of the corolla tube, filaments 20-26 mm long, glabrous; staminode 10- 20 mm long, filiform, the apex clavate; pistil glabrous, the ovary globose to oblate, 2- 3 mm diam., the style 30 mm long, the stigma slightly bilobed. Berry globose, 8-10 mm diam., pale green to white.
bibliographicCitation: Barringer, Kerry A. 2004. A revision of Gibsoniothamnus L. O. Williams (Schlegeliaceae). Brittonia. 56 (3): 213-237.

description: Tree or shrub, terrestrial or epiphytic, 1.5-5 m tall; bark light brown; young branches strongly angled, 6-7 mm diam., glabrous to sparsely pubescent, with raised leaf bases at the nodes. Leaves opposite, equal to subequal; petioles 5-15 mm long, glabrous to sparsely strigose, glabrescent, unwinged, channeled above; blade elliptic, 4-13 X 2-8.5 cm, coriaceous, glabrous or with a few trichomes on the major veins below, gland-dotted, base cuneate, apex acute, the veins impressed above, prominent below, the secondary veins 2 or 3 per side, glandular pits sometimes found on the leaf undersides toward the base of the lam- ina. Flowers in congested, terminal panicles; peduncles to 5 mm long; bracts subulate, 1-2 mm long, sparsely strigose; pedicels 2-3 cm long, glabrous, thicker above; calyx funnelform, purple to purplish pink, rarely white, glabrous or sparsely strigose, the tube 8-12 mm long, subcoriaceous, the lobes triangular, subequal, 2-6 mm long, acute; corolla tubular, not ampliate, 2.5-3 cm long, 5 mm diam., reddish purple to purple, rarely white, waxy, not fleshy, the lobes rounded, 2 X 1-2 mm; stamens inserted 6-7 mm from the base of the corolla tube, the filaments 1.8-2 cm long; staminode 4-5 mm long, filiform; pistil glabrous, the ovary globose 1.5-2 mm wide, the style 2.2-2.5 cm long, the stigma subcapitate. Berry globose, pale green to white, 5-10 mm diam., the seeds 20-35, angular.

description: Shrub or tree, epiphytic, to 3 m tall; young branches subangular, villose; older branches with a light brown bark, with per- sistent raised leaf bases at the nodes. Leaves opposite, equal to subequal; petioles 5-12 mm long, densely villose, unwinged, slight- ly channeled above; blade obovate-elliptic, 3-12.5 X 1.5-6 cm, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, pilose, base cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, the venation inconspicuous above, prominent below, the secondary veins 2-4 per side, glandular pits few and scattered on the leaf underside, pocket domatia present. Flowers solitary or in congested axillary panicles; pedicel 0.7-1 cm long, densely pilose; calyx campanulate, pink to magenta, villose, the tube 5-7 mm long, ridged, the lobes linear, 2-2.5 cm long; corolla tubular, red to magenta, 3.5-4.3 X 0.5-0.6 cm, glabrous, the lobes rounded, 3 X 2-3 mm, ciliate; stamens attached 5 mm from the base of the corolla tube, the filaments to 3 cm long; staminode 5 mm long, filiform; pistil glabrous; ovary obovoid, 2 mm wide, slightly 2-lobed, the style 3 cm long, the stigma slightly 2-lobed. Berry globose, white, 10-14 mm diam.
bibliographicCitation: Barringer, Kerry A. 2004. A revision of Gibsoniothamnus L. O. Williams (Schlegeliaceae). Brittonia. 56 (3): 213-237.

description: Shrub or small tree, epiphytic, to 4 m tall; young branches glabrous to sparsely pubescent, terete to slightly angled, 1-1.5 mm diam.; older stems with light gray bark and persistent raised petiole bases. Leaves opposite, anisophyllous; larger leaves with petioles 5-7 mm long, glabrous to slightly pubescent with gland-tipped trichomes, unwinged, channeled above, the lamina narrowly lanceolate to lanceolate, 3-5.5 X 1-1.8 cm, coriaceous, glabrous to sparsely ciliate with glandular trichomes, gland-dotted, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate to long-acuminate, the veins immersed above, prominent and often reddish below, 2 or 3 secondary veins per side, the upper surface dark green, shiny, the lower surface light green, dull, domatia present in the axils of the secondary veins; smaller leaves with petioles 2-5 mm long, glabrous to slightly pubescent with gland-tipped trichomes, unwinged, channeled above, the lamina ovate-lanceolate, 1.6-2.2 cm X 0.6-1.4 mm, coriaceous, glabrous, gland-dotted, base rounded, apex rounded to obtuse, rarely acuminate, the veins impressed above, prominent below, 1 or 2 secondary veins per side. Flowers solitary or in pairs, axillary; pedicels 1.5-2 cm long, glabrous to sparsely pubescent with glandular trichomes, slightly thickened above, bracteolate at base, the bracteoles linear, to 1 mm long; calyx campanulate, red to purple, the tube 3-4 mm long, the lobes 8-9 X 1 mm, narrowly triangular, slightly winged, glabrous to glandular-pubescent, spreading to porrect; corolla cylindric, purple to reddish violet, 1.5-2 cm long, 3 mm diam., the upper lobes broadly ovate, 1.5-2 X 2-2.5 mm, the lateral lobes ovate, 1.5-2 X 1.5-2 mm, the median lobe ovate, 1.5 X 2-2.5 mm, the lobes generally more darkly colored than the tube; stamens 4, attached ca. 5 mm above the base of the corolla tube, with a ring of trichomes at the level of attachment, the filaments 12-16 mm long, filiform, curved above, slightly thickened at the base; staminode 1.7-5 mm long; pistil glabrous; ovary globose, 1 mm tall, glandular at the base, the style elongate, 15-18 mm long, the stigma clavate to capitate. Berry globose, to 1 cm diam., white, with 10-20 seeds.

description: Shrub, epiphytic, to 1.5 m tall; bark pale gray-brown; stems angled, glabrous, the leafy portions 1-3 mm diam., the older portions with light brown bark. Leaves opposite, unequal to subequal; petioles 4-12 mm long, glabrous, unwinged; lamina ovate- lanceolate, the larger leaves 15-25 x 9-16 mm, the smaller leaves 5-15 X 4-10 mm, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous, gland-dotted, base cuneate, apex acuminate, the midvein impressed above, prominent below, the secondary veins impressed above, prominent below, 2 or 3 per side, domatia occasionally found on the underside of the lamina near the base, larger leaves 15-25 X 9-16 mm, the smaller leaves 5-12 x 4-8 mm. Flowers borne near the tips of the branches, solitary, axillary; pedicels 1-2 cm long, thick above, bracte-olate at base, glabrous; calyx campanulate, purple to red, the tube 6-8 mm long, the lobes 8-9 mm long, triangular, the wings broad, rounded, 3-4 mm wide; corolla tubular, white, 2-2.5 cm long, 4-5 mm diam., the upper and lateral lobes rounded to ligulate, 3-4 X 3-4 mm, the margin ciliate, the median lobe ligulate 3 X 1.5-2 mm; stamens attached 5 mm above the base of the corolla tube, with a ring of trichomes at the point of insertion, the filaments 17-18 mm long; staminode 5-6 mm long; pistil glabrous, the ovary globose, 1.5 mm diam., the style 14 mm long, the stigma capitate. Immature berries globose, 5 mm diam.
bibliographicCitation: Barringer, Kerry A. 2004. A revision of Gibsoniothamnus L. O. Williams (Schlegeliaceae). Brittonia. 56 (3): 213-237.

description: Shrub, epiphytic, 1-2 m tall; young branches 4-winged, glabrous; the older branches with a light brown bark. Leaves opposite, equal; petioles 0.8-2 cm long, glabrous, unwinged, channeled above; blade elliptic, 3.5-10 X 1.4-4 cm, coriaceous, glabrous, base cuneate, apex acute, the veins 1-3 per side, impressed above, prominent below, glandular pits in the vein axils below, pocket domatia in the vein axils. Flowers in congested, terminal panicles; bracts triangular, 2 mm long, usually glabrous; peduncles 1-6 mm long; pedicels 1.5-2 cm long, glabrous; calyx pink to magenta, turning purple, campanulate, the tube 5-6 X 5-6 mm, truncate, minutely lepidote, with 5 minute submarginal enations; corolla tubular, pink to magenta or white, 2-2.5 cm X 3-4 mm, the lobes rounded, 2-3 mm long, ciliate; stamens inserted ca. 5 mm above the base of the corolla tube, with a ring of trichomes at the point of insertion, the filaments 1.3-1.6 cm long, the anthers divergent, 1 mm long; staminode 3 mm long; pistil glabrous, the ovary globose, ca. 2 mm diam., the style 14-15 mm long, the stigma capitate. Immature berry globose.
bibliographicCitation: Barringer, Kerry A. 2004. A revision of Gibsoniothamnus L. O. Williams (Schlegeliaceae). Brittonia. 56 (3): 213-237.

description: Shrub or climber, epiphytic; bark gray-brown; stems angled, glabrous to sparsely pilose, with raised leaf bases at the nodes. Leaves opposite, equal to subequal; petioles 5-12 mm long, pilose, unwinged, chan- neled above; blade narrowly elliptic, 4-11 X 1.7-4 cm, subcoriaceous, dull olive-gray above, tannish below, sparsely pilose above, with scattered trichomes along the midvein below, strongly lepidote-glandular below, apex acute to acuminate, base cuneate, pocket domatia absent, glandular pits in the vein axils below. Flowers in terminal panicles; pedicel 2-3 cm long, sparsely pi- lose, slightly thickened above; calyx cam- panulate, pink to mauve, the tube 3-5 mm long, the lobes nearly linear, 7-12(-15 in fruit) mm long, porrect, then reflexed after anthesis; corolla tubular, white or reddish violet, 2 cm long, 4 mm wide at the base, 3 mm wide near the apex, the lobes ovate to round, 1.5-3 mm long; stamens inserted 4-5 mm from the base of the corolla tube, with a ring of trichomes at their base, the filaments 1 cm long; staminode 5 mm long, filiform; pistil glabrous, the ovary depressed-globose, 2 mm long, the style 15 mm long, the stigma subcapitate. Immature berry green, subglobose, 6 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Barringer, Kerry A. 2004. A revision of Gibsoniothamnus L. O. Williams (Schlegeliaceae). Brittonia. 56 (3): 213-237.

description: Shrub or small tree, 2-7 m tall, the hairs where present brown; young branchlets tomentose. Leaf blades elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 12-20 x 3.5-8 cm, coriaceous, discolorous, the upper surface smooth, gland- dotted, glabrous, and drying olive-green, the lower surface pubescent, glabrescent, and drying ochre or light-brown; apex acute to acuminate; base acute to obtuse; midvein sulcate above, convex below; lateral veins ca. 20 pairs or more, convex on both surfaces, joining in a straight inframarginal vein at 1-2 mm from the margin; petiole 5-10 mm long, canaliculate, puberulous. Inflorescences paired reduced panicles with ca. 5 flowers per panicle, 1.5-3 cm long, the axes tomentose; bracts persistent, ovate, 10- 15 x 5-10 mm, pubescent; pedicels 0-3 mm long; bracteoles not seen; flower buds obovoid, ca. 5 mm long, pubescent; hypanthium prolonged above the ovary, pubes- cent inside, splitting longitudinally and irregularly after anthesis; style ca. 5 mm long; filaments 4-5 mm long, the anthers 0.5-1 mm long; petals absent; calyx calyptrate, de- ciduous; ovary 2-locular, 2 ovules per locule. Fruits globose, ca. 1.3 cm diam., tomentose, glabrescent; seeds 1 or 2; embryo myrcioid.

description:
Plants robust, 12-40 cm high. Bulbs large, 2-3 cm in diameter. Basal leaves about 3, pleated, linear to ensiform, usually exceeding the inflorescence. Stem erect, usually- bearing one or more branches at each node. Cauline leaves usually well developed 4-11 mm wide, resembling the basal leaves. Inflorescence several-flowered, spathes 2-5 cm long, herbaceous, membranous at the apex, the outer spathe somewhat shorter. Flowers blue, white at the center, opening in the morning; tepals subequal, 2.5-3 cm long, ovate-lanceolate, spreading. Filaments free or connate at the base only; anthers exceeding 1 cm (1.1-1.5 cm). Stigma short, dividing below the anthers, stigma branches deeply divided, 5-6 mm long. Capsules ovoid, truncate, to 2 cm long. Chro- mosome number not known.

Flowering time: Spring; April and May; flowers open midmorning and fading before sundown.
bibliographicCitation: Goldblatt, Peter. 1976. Revision of the bulbous Iridaceae of North America. Brittonia. 27: 373-385.

description: Plantae robustae usque ad 40 cm altae; flores 2 vel 3, flavi; bulbus latis-ovoideus vel subglobosus, 2.5-4.0 cm longus, 6-10 cm subterraneus, tunicis atropurpureobrunneis, extensus sursum in collo brevi caulem et folia cingens; folia basalia 1 vel 2, folium primum 34-48 cm longum, 0.7-1.9 cm latum, glabrum, plicatum, linearilanceolatum, folium secundum, si praesens, folium primum aequans vel brevius angusti-lineare; folium caulinum unicum, 27-40 cm longum, 6-11 cm latum, interdum cum ramo in axilla; folia basalia et caulina inflorescentiam superantia, caulis teres, 15-29 cm altum, in spatha terminans; spathae bracteae subaequales, 5.0-8.0 cm longae, interdum duae, plerumque tres, duae exteriores interior includens, unaquaque florem subtendens, exteriores herbaceae, interior cum margine membranaceo; pedicelli filiformes, in fructu dilatati; ovarium angusti-turbinatum vel clavatum, 7.5-10 mm longum; tepala dimorpha, flava, exteriora oblanceolata, acutata, 36-43 mm longa, 10-13 mm lata, interiora lanceolata, acutata, 13-17 mm longa, 3.5-5.0 mm lata; filamenta connata, 5-7 mm longa; antherae luteae, 23-27 mm longae; stylus et fila in longitudine aequalia; styli rami purpurascentes vel lavenduli ad basim, apices albi, 4-5 mm longi; capsula elliptica-clavata, 18-27 mm longa; semina ovoidea angulata, castenea, 2-3 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: Molseed, Elwood W. & Cruden, Robert W. 1968. A new species of Nomartylis (N. movanghii) (Iridaceae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 20: 235-237.

description:
Plants slender, tall, to 120 cm. Bulbs about 1.5 cm in diameter, brown, ovate. Basal leaves 2 or 3, linear, up to 1 cm wide, plicate. Stem slender, several- to many- branched. Cauline leaves leaflike below, bractlike toward the apex. Inflorescence usually 2-flowered, spathes herbaceous with dry apices; the inner spathe 2.5-3 cm long, the outer one about half that length. Flowers dark blue, opening in the late afternoon; tepals ovate-lanceolate, spreading, about 2 cm long. Filaments joined in a tube about 2 mm long; anthers less than 1 cm long. Style branching at the apex of the filament tube; branches about 5 mm long, divided to base. Capsule about 1 cm long, ovoid, truncate. Chromosome number: 2 n = 56

Flowering time: Late summer and autumn; from August to early October; flowers open about 4 p.m., lasting about two hours (Small, 1931b).

description:
Plants small, slender, to 30 cm high. Bulb dark brown, ca. 1.5 cm in diameter. Basal leaves 1-4, short at flowering time, later extending to the height of the inflores- cence, plicate, narrow to linear. Scape erect, bearing 1 or 2 reduced leaves. Inflores- cence 1- or 2-flowered, spathes often dry and brown above, 2-4.5 cm long, the inner ones exceeding the outer ones. Flowers blue, tepals to 2.5 cm long, ovate, subequal. Stamens erect, symmetrically disposed; filaments free. Style declinate, ca. 1 cm long, expanded upwards and dividing into 3 short, flat lobes. Capsule ellipsoid, to 2 cm long, truncate; seeds angular. Chromosome number not known.

Flowering time: April and May.
bibliographicCitation: Goldblatt, Peter. 1976. Revision of the bulbous Iridaceae of North America. Brittonia. 27: 373-385.

description: Caespitose perennial herb, glaucous green; roots numerous, spreading, light to dark brown; leaves slender, erect or ascending, generally shorter and narrower than the stem, 0.8-1.9 mm wide, gradually tapering to a very sharp apex, the margins entire; stems simple, 2-winged, 0.8-2 mm wide, up to 3 dm tall, the margins entire; spathe terminal on the stem, the bracts very unequal in length; inner bract (13-) 15-24 (-27) mm long, the inner margins broadly hyaline below, tapering abruptly to a thin line below the tip, the outer margin entire, convex, the slender tip curving to meet the outer bract; outer bract 20-55 (-70) mm long, tapering to a slender acute tip, the outer margin entire, the inner margins narrow-hyaline, connate at the base for 1.5-2 (-3.5) mm; flowers 2-5 on slender, spreading, glabrous pedicels generally shorter than the inner bract; perianth blue-violet to white, with a yellow eye, the segments narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate, apiculate to aristulate but not emarginate, (7-) 9-12 mm long; outer tepals with a length/width ratio of 3-3.5; filament column (2-) 3-4 mm long, yellow-glandular proximally 0.5-1 mm; anthers yellow, 1.5-2.2 mm long; ovary at anthesis 1.4-2 mm long, moderately glandular- stipitate, often with tangled hairs; capsules obovoid to spherical, 3.5-5 mm long; seeds 0.5-1.2 mm in diam., black, angled, finely pitted, 12-30 per capsule; n = 16.

description: Caespitose perennial herb, often less than 3 dm tall, light green; roots numerous, fibrous, spreading; leaves to 2/3 the height of the stem, ascending, 1-2.3 mm wide, the margins generally entire; stems simple, 1-1.9 mm wide, the margins entire to often denticulate distally; inflorescence terminal; spathe bracts often denticulate or serrulate on dorsal keel or base of margins, acute to more often acuminate, the outer 24-55 (62) mm long, tapering evenly to the apex, 1.8-2.4 times the length of the inner, (0.7) 1-1.6 mm wide above the apex of the inner, tapering gradually to its own apex, the outer connate basally 1.2-2.8 (4) mm, the inner (12) 15-23 mm long, the margins narrowly hyaline to the recurved tip, not gibbous based; flowers 1-5 on slender, usually glabrous, erect pedicels subequal to the inner bract, the tepals blue-violet and yellow basally, the outer 9-12 mm long, the length-to-width ratio 2.5-3.5, elliptic with the apices long-aristulate and generally rounded or occasionally slightly emarginate, the filament column 2-4.3 mm long, yellow to dark violet or occasionally bicolored, the anthers 1-1.6 mm long, the ovary at anthesis 1.4-2 mm long, ovoid, moderately glandular-pubescent; capsule 2.7-5 mm long, brown; seeds 0.8-1.1 (averaging 1.0) mm long, black, testa reticulate, occasionally reticulate-granular, 15-35 per capsule; n = 16.

description: Caespitose perennial herb, medium green to glaucous green; roots numerous, slender, dark brown; leaves lax to ascending or erect, shorter or occasionally longer than the stems, 1.5-3.5 mm wide, tapering to an acute, often recurved apex, the margins smooth or sometimes with a few widely spaced fine teeth; stems erect to ascending, simple or occasionally branched, 2-winged, (1.2-) 1.7-2.8 (-3.1) mm wide, up to 3 dm tall, the margins entire or occasionally with widely spaced fine teeth; spathe generally terminal on the stem, the bracts unequal in length; inner bract 20-30 mm long, the outer margin entire, the inner margins broadly hyaline, the hyaline portion narrowing only slightly toward the tip; outer bract 27-48 mm long, tapering abruptly to an acute apex, the outer margin entire, the inner margins nar- rowly hyaline, extending nearly to the apex, connate at the base 3-5 mm; flowers 2-7 on erect or spreading, slender, glabrous pedicels that are about the same length as the inner bract; perianth light blue with a yellow eye, the segments oblanceolate, rounded, apiculate to aristulate but never emarginate, 11-14 mm long; outer tepals with a length/width ratio of 2.6-3; filament column 4.5-5.5 mm long, yellow-glan- dular proximally for 1.5 mm; anthers yellow, 1.2-1.8 mm long; ovary at anthesis (1.2-) 1.9-2 (-2.5) mm long, with short, stipitate-glandular hairs of moderate density; capsules (3-) 4-5 (-6) mm long, subglobose to globose; seeds 1-1.5 mm in diam., dark brown, angled, coarsely reticulate, 18-37 per capsule; n = 48.

description: Slightly caespitose perennial herb, light green to only slightly glaucous green, darkening somewhat upon drying; roots few, slender, spreading, tan to dark brown; leaves lax to ascending, rarely strict, mostly shorter than the stems, 2-5.5 mm wide, the margins entire to finely denticulate; stems 1 or 2, erect to ascending, simple or often branched with a leaf-like bract subtending two or three pedunculate spathes, conspicuously 2-winged, (1.7-) 2.2-3.5 mm wide, up to 4.2 dm tall, the margins entire or more often finely denticulate; spathe terminal on the stem or pedunculate, the bracts very unequal in length when simple-stemmed or sub-equal if pedunculate; inner bract 21-36 mm long, the outer margin entire or with widely spaced minute teeth, the inner margins narrowly hyaline nearly to the tip; outer bract (25-) 36-58 (-75) mm long, often 2-3.5 mm wide well above the apex of the inner bract and tapering abruptly to an acute apex, the outer margin entire or with widely spaced, minute teeth, the inner margins narrowly hyaline 1/2-34 the length of the bract, connate at the base (3-) 4.5-7 mm; flowers (1-) 2-4 (-5) on slender, glabrous, erect to slightly spreading pedicels equaling or slightly exceeding the inner bract; perianth light blue or more often deep blue-violet, with a yellow eye, the segments narrowly elliptic to narrowly oblanceolate, rounded to slightly truncate, aristulate, rarely emarginate, 11-16 mm long; outer tepals with a length/width ratio of ca. 3; filament column (4-) 4.5-5.5 mm long, glandular proximally for ca. 1.5 mm; anthers pale yellow, 1.2-1.7 mm long; ovary at anthesis 2.4-3 mm long, sparsely stipitate- glandular, obovoid; capsules (5-) 6.2-8.1 (-9) mm long, globose to obovoid; seeds 1.2-1.5 (-1.7) mm in diam., dark brown to black, spherical to angled, coarsely reticulate, 15-33 per capsule; n = 48.

description:
Plants 8-20 cm high. Bulbs 1.5-2 cm diameter. Basal leaves 3-6, equal or exceed- ing inflorescence, seldom more than 6 mm wide. Stem erect, occasionally branching. Cauline leaves, if present, reduced to bractlike structures. Inflorescence several-flow- ered, the spathes up to 5 cm long, herbaceous, brown-tipped. Flowers blue-purple; the outer tepals to 2.5 cm long, lanceolate, flaccid and spreading; the inner tepals about 8 mm long, lanceolate, dark-colored. Filaments united in a tube about 5 mm long; anthers 7-10 mm, spreading. Style branches about 5 mm long, slender, depressed, with winglike membranous margins; bifurcate at apex for 2 mm. Capsule ovoid, truncate, to 2.5 cm long. Chromosome number not known.

Flowering time: Mid-March to early May.

description: Perennial herbs seldom exceeding 25 cm in height. Rootstock a bulb. Basal leaves plicate, linear. Stem simple, occasionally branching, bearing reduced bractlike leaves. Inflorescence few-flowered; spathes herbaceous with dry, brown, acute apices, the inner spathe exceeding the outer. Flowers usually blue to purple; the outer tepals large, spreading, much exceeding the inner ones. Stamens erect with united filaments; the anthers spreading, appressed to the style branches but exceeding these. Style erect, branching near the apex of the filaments, the branches spread, the apices shortly divided. Basic chromosome number: x = 7.

description:
Plants small, to 30 cm. Bulb ovoid, to 1.5 cm in diameter. Basal leaves 2 or 3, linear, to 25 cm long. Stem usually simple. Cauline leaves usually solitary, leaflike. Inflorescence 1- or 2-flowered; spathes herbaceous to membranous; the outer one to 2.5 cm, the inner one about 4 cm. Flower pale blue; tepals subequal, 2-3 cm long, ovate-lanceolate. Filaments 2.5-3.5 mm long, joined in a column for about two- thirds of their length; anthers about 8 mm long. Style branching below base of anthers; the branches about 3.5 mm long. Capsule oblong, to 2.5 cm long. Chromo- some number not known. A chromosome count of 2 n = 14 for "N. tenuis" from Mexico has been reported by Molseed (1970).

Flowering time: Summer; June, July, and August.

description: Perennial herbs of medium size. Rootstock a bulb. Basal leaves plicate, ensiform. Stem, usually laxly branched, rarely simple, bearing several leaves. Inflorescence few-flowered; spathes herbaceous, acute, the inner spathe exceeding outer one. Flow- ers purple and yellow; tepals unequal, the outer tepals somewhat larger, ovate, plane, the inner with a band of hairs across the center and with lateral margins folded con- volutely over this area. Stamens erect, free or with filaments united partly or entirely; anthers distinctive with pollen sacs at the margins of a broad pandurate connective. Style slender below, funnellike above, dividing into 3 branches each in turn divided for more than half their length, the branches filiform, ascending and curving out- wards, above the anthers. Capsule ovoid truncate. Basic chromosome number: x = 7 (based on the cytology of one species only).
bibliographicCitation: Goldblatt, Peter. 1976. Revision of the bulbous Iridaceae of North America. Brittonia. 27: 373-385.

description:
Plants 15-45 cm high. Bulbs dark brown, ovate (0.5)-1-1.5 cm in diameter. Basal leaves 2 or 3, linear-ensiform, to 1.5 cm wide and 30 cm long. Stems simple or usually laxly branched, terete or grooved. Cauline leaves leaflike below, becoming bractlike above. Inflorescence few-flowered, the inner spathe 3-4 cm long, the outer one more than half length of the inner. Flowers purple, speckled with brown near the center, the inner tepals marked with yellow; the outer tepals ovate, 2-2.5 cm long, the inner ones about 1.5 cm long, the margins tightly inrolled over a band of hairs. Filaments broad at base, free or connate; anthers 6-8 mm long. Style dividing at the apex of the filaments, the branches exceeding the anthers. Capsule 1.5-3 cm long. Chromosome number: 2 n = 28 (Lewis & Oliver, 1961; Molseed, 1970).

Flowering time: Early summer; from late May until July.

description: Fruit ovoid, 28 mm diam., 55 mm long, with pericarp 5 mm thick, stigmatic residue apical. description:
Plants small, slender, 18-35 cm high. Bulb about 1 cm in diameter. Basal leaves 1 or 2 or lacking, linear, about as long as the inflorescence. Stem erect, simple or rarely 1-branched. The lowermost cauline leaves linear plicate, reaching the inflorescence, the others reduced and bractlike. Inflorescence 1- or 2-flowered; spathes herbaceous with a brown apex; inner spathe to 3 cm long, the outer one about 2 cm long. Flower pale blue, tepals subequal, about 2 cm long, ovate. Filaments joined in a tube 1-2 mm long; anthers about 4 mm long. Style branching well above the apex of the fila- ment tube, branches divided to the base, about 2 cm long. Capsule clavate, 1.5 cm long. Chromosome number not known.

Flowering time: Summer; late May, June, and July; flowers open late afternoon (5-7 p.m.; Steyermark, 1963) and last only a few hours.

description: Epiphytic. Roots terete, arising from nodes of the rhizome, not or rarely branched. Rhizome creeping, with membranous scales. Pseudobulbs erect, short ovoid, 1-4 cm apart, 5 mm long, 3 mm in diam. Leaf 1, oblong, 1.5-3 x 0.8-1 cm, retuse. Inflorescences erect, arising from the rhizome or the base of the pseudobulb, 3.5-4 cm long, 0.5 mm in diam., slightly higher than the leaves, 1-3-flowered. Bracts 3-5, lanceolate, 2 mm long. Flower white, not fully opening. Ovary with pedicel 1-1.5 cm long. Sepals similar; dorsal sepal slightly shorter than lateral sepals, 6 x 3 mm, acuminate; the lateral sepals lanceolate, 3 veined, 7 X 3 mm, acuminate, free. Petals ovate, 4 X 1.5 mm, rounded. Lip ligulate and sigmoid, fleshy, 4 X 1.5 mm, channeled at the base, with two ridges at each side. Column 1-1.5 mm long, without stelids. Column foot 1.5-2 mm long. Pollinia 2.

description: Fruit 14-14.5 mm diam., pericarp 2-2.5 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-similar to Cyphophoenix and Burretiokentia, but also to Heterospathe, especially H. woodfordiana, with numerous, terete bundles of rather thin-walled fibers occupying the outer half of the pericarp. Distinctive for the large and abundant tanniniferous cells occupying the inner half of the pericarp, vascular bundles with scant fibrous sheaths, a thick (0.25 mm) locular epidermis, rather few brachysclereids, no raphide-bearing cells, and a very thick layer of tannin/pigment below the epidermis.

description: Tree up to ca 22 m high and diameter at breast height of 34 cm, appearing glabrous, sparsely to densely covered with minute hairs on young growth; hairs whitish or reddish-brown, most less than 0.1 mm long; young twigs light or dark reddish-brown to yellowish-brown, moderately glandular, the older twigs with somewhat flaky to stringy bark; leaves probably persisting over a year, mature at anthesis, lanceolate or less often elliptic, 2-7 cm long, 0.8-2.6 cm wide, 2.5-3.2 times as long as wide, usually inconspicuously puberulent on the petiole and base; apex acuminate to caudate; base cuneate to acuminate; petiole channeled, 3-5 mm long, 0.5-1 mm thick; midvein impressed for most of length above, prominent below; lateral veins weak, ca 8-10 pairs faintly visible, each leaving the midvein at an angle of ca 45 degrees, broadly arching near the margin to connect with the next, the arches not forming a well defined lateral vein; blades subcoriaceous, drying reddish-brown to gray-green, somewhat lustrous above, covered with numerous small amber-colored glands below, crescent-shaped, pouchlike folds of epidermis ca 1-2 mm long often present below, these near, but not touching the midvein, the leaf margin entire to slightly undulate; peduncles solitary, uniflorous, appearing glabrous, sparsely puberulent, glandular, 8-18 mm long, ca 0.6-1 mm wide, arising from the axils of mature leaves; calyx closed in the bud, tearing irregularly as the bud opens, persisting until the fruit matures, covered with many small glands without, moderately to densely covered with small reddish-brown hairs within; petals 4 in flowers seen, obovate, ca 10 mm long, ca 7 mm wide, glandular; hypanthium campanulate, ca 3 mm long, densely papillose with glands; style ca 6-7 mm long, glabrous; stamens ca 140-150, 6-8 mm long; anthers ca 0.6 mm long; ovary 6-8-locular; ovules 10-15 per locule; fruit ca 1.3-1.8 cm in diam, subglobose; seeds probably 1 or 2 per fruit, ca 6 mm long including the locular wall.
bibliographicCitation: Landrum, Leslie R. 1987. A new species of Campomanesia (Myrtaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 39: 245-247.

description: Shrubs or treelets 2.5-6 m high. Young branches 3.5-4.5 mm diam., striate longitudinally. Stipule ca. 2 mm long, entire.  Leaves spirally alternate, sometimes subopposite, crowded on the terminal portion of the branches or separated by internodes to ca. 3 cm long; petiole 0.5-6.5 cm long, slightly compressed laterally, adaxially plane or slightly canaliculate, thickness uniform or thicker at apex and/or base; blade horizontal, plane, papery, discolorous, 3.7-14.7 cm long, 1.4-6.4 cm wide, elliptic to slightly obovate, symmetric or slightly asymmetric, the apex obtuse to rounded, sometimes mucronate, the base cuneate to attenuate, the margin entire, plane or slightly revolute; venation acrodromous suprabasal, imperfect, brochidodromous, the main vein prominent on both surfaces, more so on abaxial one, the secondary veins in 6-8 pairs, slightly prominent on abaxial surface; the basal pair diverging from midvein at ca. 1.5 cm from blade base, distinct, the angle of divergence 25º-50º, other pairs with angle of divergence 50º-60º, the intersecondary veins clearly thinner than secondary ones, the tertiary veins and reticulation hardly to easily visible and prominent on abaxial surface. Inflorescence terminal, erect, the main axis up to ca. 1.5 mm long; the primary branches 6-8, 4.5-11 cm long, umbellately or sub-racemosely arranged, erect to sub-horizontal, with whorled bracts 1.5-4.5 cm from the base, the apex thickened. Terminal inflorescence units with 25-30 flowers grouped in umbels. Flowers greenish, the pedicel 0.7-1.8 cm long; hypanthium 2-3 mm long, longer than corolla; calyx lobes evident; petals 5, triangular, 2.1-2.4 mm long, 1.1-1.7 mm wide, the apex cucullate; stamens 5, white, the filaments 1.8-2.2 mm long, the anthers versatile, ca. 1.2 mm long, ca. 1.2 mm wide, dorsally glandular at the apex; styles 0.5-0.7 mm long. Fruits unknown.

description: Trees or hemi-epiphytes to ca. 10 m high. Young branches 2-3 (-5) mm diam., striate longitudinally. Stipule reduced, to ca. 1.5 mm long, entire. Leaves spirally alternate, sometimes sub-opposite, crowded on the terminal portion of the branches or separated by internodes to ca. 2 cm long; petiole 0.5-2.5(-5) cm long, laterally compressed, usually thicker at the base; blade horizontal, plane, papery, slightly discolorous, 3.9-14 cm long, 2.2-6.5 cm wide, elliptic to slightly ovate or obovate, symmetric to slightly asymmetric, the apex acute to acuminate, mucronate, the base obtuse, rarely cuneate or rounded, the margin entire, slightly revolute, sometimes with as many as two pairs of small teeth (each less than 1 mm long) in the distal third; venation acrodromous suprabasal, imperfect, brochidodromous, the main vein prominent on both surfaces, more so on abaxial one, the secondary veins 6-9 pairs, prominent only on the abaxial surface, the basal pair diverging from midvein at ca. 0.5 cm from blade base, sometimes indistinct, the angle of divergence 40º-50º, other pairs with angle of divergence 60º-70º, the inter-secondary veins similar to secondary ones, the tertiary veins and reticulation evident on the abaxial surface. Inflorescence terminal, or pseudo-lateral due to the subsequent growth of a new vegetative branch, the main axis 0.5-1 cm long; the primary branch 1, geniculate or rarely sub-erect, 4.2-8 cm long, purplish to blackish when mature, lacking whorled bracts. Terminal inflorescence units with 25-30 flowers grouped in umbels. Flowers not seen. Fruits obloid, 5-6-lobed when dry, ca. 6.5 mm long, 8.5 mm wide, the stylar column 1-1.2 mm long; pyrenes 5(6), 4.5-5.5 mm long, ca. 3 mm wide.

description: Perennial herb, 10-70 cm long, erect or prostrate, sometimes rooting at the basal node, the indument variable, pubescent to hirsute. Leaves 1-3 x 0.5-1 cm, sessile, lanceolate to ovate, subglabrous to scabrous, the midvein prominent on the abaxial surface; stipular sheath more or less pilose, the setae 7-9, glabrous, 1-3 mm long. Flower: 1 or few in each leaf axil, tetramerous; hypanthium more or less hirsute; calyx lobes usually uequal, 1-2.5 mm long, the margins scabrid; corolla white to lilac, infundibuliform, 5-14(-16) mm long, outside pubescent, inside glabrous with only a ring of hairs near the base; stamens subsessile, anthers 0.7-1.7 mm long; style filiform, 6-8 (-12) mm, stigma capitate, bilobed. Fruit a schizocarp, hirsute to subglabrous, 2.5-4 mm long, the mericarps with 3-5 carinate ridges on dorsal side. Seed 1.5-2 mm long, the apex incurved.

description: Suffruticose herb, the stems tetragonal, pilose or only pilose at the angles. Leaves 2-3 (-5) X 0.7-1.5 (-2) cm, sessile, ovalelliptic, apex acuminate, base obtuse, subauriculate; secondary veins 4-6 pairs, impressed above and prominent below; stipular sheath 2-3 mm long, pilose, with 10-12 linear-subulate setae, each 3-5 mm long, pubescent. Heads (inflorescences) axillary, 3-10 flowered. Flower: calyx tetramerous, the lobes triangular, slightly dimorphic, in general two larger, 2-2.5 mm long, the margins pilose with a glabrous dorsal surface; corolla white, infundibuliform, 4-lobed, 8-10 mm long, glabrous, slightly pilose on the dorsal surface of the lobes, with a ring of hairs internally near the base; stamens 4, exerted, anthers ca. 1.8 mm long, filaments ca. 1.2 mm long; style exerted, to 12 mm long, filiform, scarcely widened toward the apex, stigma capitate, slightly bilobed; disk divided in two parts. Fruit obovoid, 3-4 X 3-4 mm, puberulous, the mericarps with bony endocarp. Seeds 2-2.2 mm long, obovoid, the adaxial face with two deep furrows, the apex recurved inward and with a dorsiventral furrow.

description: Tree 6-7 m tall, hairs where present ferrugineous to ochraceous, to 1 mm long; young branchlets tomentose, bark somewhat flaky on older branchlets. Leaf blades elliptic to narrowly elliptic or ovate, 4-9.5 X 2-5 cm, 2-3 times as long as wide, drying olive-green, slightly discolorous, chartaceous, conspicuously rugose or bullate; adaxial surface sparsely pubescent; abaxial surface tomentose, hairs especially along the veins, with numerous, small glands; apex acute to acuminate, apiculate; base cuneate, obtuse, or subcordate; petiole slightly canaliculate, 2-4 X 1 mm, tomentose; midvein impressed above, prominent below; lateral veins 8-12 pairs, at an angle of ca. 450 with the midvein, strongly impressed above, prominent below, venation eucamptodromous to reticulodromous. Flowers solitary in the axils of leaves, subsessile; peduncles tomentose, 1-3 X 1 mm; bracteoles lanceolate, 2-3 mm long, tomentose, deciduous before anthesis; buds 7-8 mm long, tomentose; calyx open in bud, the lobes triangular, 3-4 X 3-4 mm, tomentose on both surfaces; petals 5, obovate, ca. 7 x 5 mm, pubescent without, glabrous within; hypanthium campanulate, ca. 4 mm long, tomentose; disk 3-5 mm diam., pubescent; stamens ca. 200-300, 3-6 mm long; anthers ca. 0.8 mm long, with one terminal gland; style 4-6 mm long, glabrous; ovary ca. 11-locular; ovules ca. 10 per locule. Fruit green-yellowish, subglobose, 1-1.5 cm diam., pubescent; seeds to 3 in fruits, 4-5 mm long including locular wall, the wall chartaceous, orangish, densely glandular; embryo myrtoid, spiral with a swollen hypocotyl and small leafy cotyledons.

description: Tree up to ca. 25 m tall; up to ca. 45 cm DBH. Branches lenticellate. Terminal buds 5-9 mm long, minutely hirsute, similar in male and female plants, and with two distinct basal knobs. Leaves with petiole 4-6 mm long (up to 1 cm long on female plants), canaliculate on adaxial surface; lamina leathery, symmetric to clearly asymmetric, 7-16.5 cm long, 3.5-9 cm wide, elliptic to ovate, apex acute to attenuate, sometimes acuminate, base cuneate or obtuse to rounded, rarely truncate or subcordate, margin entire; venation brochidodromous, main vein prominent only on abaxial surface, secondaries 7-9 pairs, impressed on both surfaces or slightly prominent on abaxial surface, intersecondary veins present. Male inflorescences many-flowered. Staminate flowers greenish yellow, sessile, with 4 imbricate (decussate) bracts ca. 1.5 mm long, 1 mm wide. Sepals (4) 5, the outer 1-2 a little shorter, ca. 2 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, the inner ones ca. 2.5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, glabrous. Petals 5, up to ca. 2.5 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, ciliate; extra-staminal disk lobed; stamens 5, filaments united ca. 1 mm at the base; pistillodes 2. Female inflorescences with 1-3(-5) flowers. Pistillate flowers brownish green, pedicels 8-10 mm long, hirsute. Sepals and petals as many as in male flowers. Sepals pubescent on abaxial surface, the outer ca. 3 mm long, 2 mm wide, the inner ones ca. 3 mm long, 1.5 mm wide. Petals pubescent on abaxial surface, 2.5-3 mm long, 0.5 mm wide; styles united in a column 2.5-3 mm long, hirsute; stigma lobed and reflexed; ovary surface smooth, densely hirsute-pubescent. Fruits unknown.

description: Subshrub, 20-30 cm tall; stem decumbent, subquadrangular, narrowly winged, glabrous. description: Subshrub, ca. 1 m tall, erect; stem branched, subquadrangular, the cortex dark brown to black, glabrous, the internodes 2- 4.5 mm long. Leaves 20-48 X 4-12 mm, elliptic-lanceolate, apex acute or acuminate, base acute, subchartaceous, glabrous, the secondary veins in 2-3 pairs, basally adherent at mid-vein from which they gradually separate towards the apex; stipular sheath 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous or puberulous, the setae 3-5, glabrous, 5-12 mm long. Inflorescences terminal, thyrsoid. Flower: hypanthium 1.5-2.5 mm long, obconic, glabrous or puberulous; calyx 4-merous, the lobes 1.5-2.8 mm long, triangular- subulate, glabrous, toothed between the lobes; corolla funnelform, white, the lobes longer than the tube, minutely papillose externally, the hairs moniliform, thinner and shorter above the middle of the tube, and thicker and longer on the lobes, internally; disk entire, papillose. description: Subshrub, 30-50 cm tall, erect; branched, the cortex reddish, glabrescent to puberulous, the internodes 1.5-4 (-6) cm long. Leaves 18-45 x 3-4.5 mm, linear-lanceolate, apex acute or attenuate, base acute or decurrent, puberulous to pubescent, the secondary veins in 3 pairs, impressed above and prominent below; stipular sheath (1.5-) 2-2.5 mm long, pubescent, with setae 5-9 (-10) glabrous, reddish, 5-9 mm long. Inflorescences lateral and terminal, condensed, thyrsoid. Flower: hypanthium 1-1.5 mm long, obconic, puberulous; calyx 4-merous, lobes 1-1.5 mm long, triangular-subulate, glabrescent to puberulous, teeth between the lobes; corolla funnelform, white, the lobes shorter than the tube, minutely papillose externally; disk entire, pilose. Thrum flower: corolla 4-4.5 mm long, the moniliform hairs thinner and shorter on the tube, internally; anthers 0.7-1 mm long; filament 0.8-1 mm long; style 2-2.5 mm long, stigma bifid. Pin flower: corolla 3.5-4 mm long, the hairs moniliform, thinner and shorter above the middle of the tube, and thicker and longer internally on the lobes; anthers ca. 1 mm long; filament ca. 0.5 mm; style ca. 4 mm, stigmatic lobes linear. Fruit 2-2.5 mm long, puberulous to pubescent. Seeds 1.5-2.5 mm long, with narrow wings at apex, strophiole deciduous.

description: Herb, 8-22 cm high. Bulb subglobose, 15-20 mm wide, covered by dark-brown, membranous coats, prolonged upwards into a neck. Leaves 1-3, plicate, linear, at anthesis green, erect, 4-5 cm X 1-2 mm. Inflorescence a 1- or 2-flowered rhipidium; spathes green, the lower one 2-2.3 cm long, the upper 2.5-3 cm long. Flower pale lilac, radially symmetrical, 2.5-2.9 cm wide. Outer tepals obovate, 1.7-2.1 X 1-1.3 cm, with a yellow linear stripe at the base; inner tepals oblanceolate, 3-4 X 2-3 mm, pale lilac with a 2 mm long yellow medial stripe. Filaments united in a column, 3-4 mm long, pale lilac with red, adpressed hairs along the column, free apically for 1 mm; anthers linear, curved at dehiscence, 4-5 mm long. Ovary 4.5-5 X 2.5 mm. Pollen yellow. Style arms channeled, pale lilac, 4 mm long, bifid for 2.5 mm, the divisions divaricate, recurved, apically stigmatose. Capsule oblong, 9 X 5 mm. Seeds obovate, slightly angled, pale brown, 1.5 X 1 mm.

description: Small tree, sparsely branched; branchlets stout, grayish, acutely tetragonal, very pronouncedly decussate-ampliate and flattened toward the apex, roughened-puberulent; internodes 1-2.5 cm. long; leaf-sears elevated, vertically eloingate, narrow, about 3 mm. long and 2 mm. wide, the edges not at all sharp or prominent; leaves large, decussate, bunched at the ends of the branchlets; petioles stout, 1-2 cm. long, canaliculate above, puberulent; blades coriaceous, dark and nitid above, paler beneath, laneeolate or obovate, 7-24 cm. long, 6-7 cm. wide, obtusely acuminate at apex, entire or slightly revolute at the margins, very long-cuneiform at the base and attenuate into the petiole, minutely puberulent on both surfaces, probably becoming glabrate; midrib stout and very prominent beneath, prominulent above, rapidly diminishing in size and prominence toward the apex; secondaries 12-16 pairs, arcuate-aseending, obscure above, rather prominent and quite densely puberulent beneath, plainly anastomos- ing along the margin beneath; veinlets very few, inconspicuous; in- florescence axillary; eymes solitary, opposite, to 3 cm. long, brachiate, few-flowered, lax; flowers very odorous; peduncles about 5 mm. long, stout, puberulent, verrucose; pedicels slender, about 5 mm. long, ineanous-pubeseent, becoming thickened and verrucose in fruit; bract- lets and prophylla minute, subulate, pubescent; calyx rather narrowly campanulate, 10-11 mm. long, about 6 mm. wide, pubescent, its rim 3-5-parted, its lobes irregular, about 3 mm. long, slightly emarginate; corolla rotate or hypocrateriform, rather small and included by the calyx, white, its tube subconic, 4.5-7 mm. long, its lobes 5, broadly ovate-lingulate, 6-6.5 mm. long, about 3.7 mm. wide, obtuse at apex; stamens 5, equal, inserted about 2.5 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, scarcely exserted (in Y ); filaments slender, about 1.6 mm. long (in 9 ), finely pubescent; anthers elliptic-oblong, about 4.3 mm. long and 1.2 mm. wide, forming a loose tube about the style, yellow, dorsifixed just above the base; pistil exserted (in 9 ); style slender, about 5 mm. long, glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches fili- form, about 3.7 mm. long, woolly; ovary spherical, dark, about 0.6 mm. long and wide, glabrous, 4-celled; fruiting-calyx greatly enlarged and indurated, rather verrucose and heavy, gray, obvolute and eucul- late with a somewhat irregularly lobed or split rim, about 15 mm. long and 12 mm. wide, glabrate, completely including the fruit; fruit hard, light in color, oblong, about 9 mm. long and 8 mm. wide, con- spicuously flattened and umbilicate at apex, glabrous, 4-seeded; seeds large, nut-like, furrowed.

description: Branchlets terete, tetragonal-compressed at the nodes, glabrous, but roughened by elevated tubercles; leaf-blades coriaceous, obovate oblong, abruptly short-acuminate at apex, entire, glabrous on both surfaces; inflorescence terminal, paniculate, almost equaling the leaves; calyx-rim toothed, its teeth cuspidate from a subquadrangular base; corolla softly pubescent, 5 or 6 times as long as the calyx.

description: Shrub; branchlets obtusely tetragonal or subterete, glabrate or minutely puberulent; internodes 1-2.5 cm. long; leaves decussate; petioles 3-5 mm. long, weak, glabrate; blades muembranous, lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, varying to obovate, 7-9.5 cm. long, 1-3.5 cm. wide, acuminate at apex, more or less acuminate at base, glabrate or somewhat roughened-pulverulent on both surfaces, the larger leaves with 1-3 broad and distant teeth on each margin, the smaller leaves often only sinuate or almost plane; midrib slender; secondaries 4-6 pairs, slender, arcuate-ascending, irregularly auastomosing near the margins, with usually only a small veinlet extending into the teeth; infloreseence axillary and terminal; peduncles slender, about 2 cm. long, puberulent; axillary eymes few or none; terminal panicle about 6 cm. long and wide, its sympodia slender and abbreviated; bractlets linear, about 4 mm. long; calyx eyathiform, abouLt 2 mm. long and 3.1 mm. wide above, contracted from the base to about the middle, greatly ampliate above, glabrate, its rim subtrLneate; corolla infundibular, its tube narrow-cylindric, to 3.1 mm. long, its lobes 4, oblong-lingulate about 3.9 mm. long and 2.3 mm. wide; stamens 4, inserted at the mouth of the corolla-tube; filaments filiform, about 1.5 mm. long, glabrous; anthers oblong, about 1.5 mm. long and 0.7 mm. wide; style capillary, 2 mm. or more in length, glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches about 1 mm. long; ovary subglobose, minute, glabrous, 4-celled; fruiting- calyx and fruit not seen.

description: Shrub or low tree; branches stout, angular, cano-tomentose; branch- lets rather stout, obtusely or aeutely tetragonal, somewhat flattened and ampliate at the nodes, very densely cano-tomentose with the pubes- cence becoming ochraceous toward the apex of the branchlets, occa- sionally becoming glabrate in age; internodes 8-20 mm. long; leaf- scars elevated, often rather quadrangular, prominent; leaves decussate; petioles semi-terete, flattened and canaliculate above, 1.5-4.5 cm. long, densely cano-tomentose or ochraceous; blades subcoriaceous, dark green above, lighter beneath, elliptic-oblong, 6-19 cm. long, 3-9 cm. wide, acute at apex, entire or somewhat repand along the margins, acuminate at base and decurrent into the petiole, ochraceous-tomentose above when immature, becoming glabrous in age, ineanous or ochra- ceous-tomentose beneath, often somewhat scabrous on both surfaces; midrib prominent on both surfaces, especially stout and prominent beneath; secondaries 6-10 pairs, short, ascending and somewhat arcuate, impressed above, prominulent beneath, conspicuously anas- tomosing some distance from the margins; veinlets delicate, impressed above; infloreseence axillary; eymes corymbose, to 9 cm. long and 8 cm. wide, usually few-flowered, often long-pedunculate, subequaling the petiole or greatly exceeding it, very pronouncedly brachiate and lax when in fruit, often somewhat smaller and less spreading in anthesis; peduncles very short in bud, rapidly elongating to 5.5 cm. in anthesis and fruit and then very stout, straight, woody, and cano- or ochraceous-tomentose; pedicels 2-15 mm. long, densely ochraceous or cano-tomentose; bractlets and prophylla linear-subulate or setaceous, scattered or occasionally numerous at the base of the pedicels; calyx turbinate-campanulate or broadly obconic, angulate, 6-15 mm. long, 5-7 mm. wide, densely ochraceous-tomentose, very lax around the corolla-tube, its rim truncate and subentire or minutely 4-apiculate; corolla infundibular or hypocrateriform, yellowish, glabrous, its tube cylindric, about 15 mm. long and 3.6 mm. wide, ampliate above, its lobes 4 or 5, equal, oblong or oblong-ovate, about 9 mm. long and 5 mm. wide, spreading, acute or obtuse at apex; stamens 5, inserted just below the mouth of the corolla-tube, included or a trifle exserted; fila- ments filiform, about 1 mm. long, glabrous; anthers oblong, about 3.1 mm. long and 1.3 mm. wide, bright yellow, conspicuously bilobed at the base, dorsifixed about 1 mm. above the base; pistil included; style stout-capillary, about 5.7 mm. long, glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches about 3.4 mm. long; ovary small, subglobose, 4-celled [sometimes im- perfectly so or apparently 2-celled], 4-ovuled; fruiting-calyx enlarged and greatly indurated, cupuliform, 10-18 mm. long, 7-16 mm. wide, verrucose, tomentose or subglabrate, its rim varying from subentire to deeply lobed or irregularly split; fruit oblong, about 10 mm. long and 7 mm. wide or larger, umbonate at apex, glabrate, 4-seeded.

description: Shrub, 1-2 m. tall or taller; branches very stout, acutely tetragonal with somewhat sulcate sides, brownish, very medullose, densely puberulent, sometimes asymmetrical or even genuiflexuous at the nodes; branchlets similar, becoming very much flattened toward the apex; internodes 2.5-10 cm. long; leaf-scars not conspicuous; leaves decussate-opposite or subopposite or ternate; petioles very stout, 1-3 cm. long, densely puberulent or incanous; blades membranous, dark green above, paler beneath, oblong or obovate, 13-27 cm. long, 3.5-9 cm. wide, acute or shortly acuminate at apex; acuminate at base and long-attenuate into the petiole, with numerous small apiculations or subcrenations along almost the whole margin, densely puberulent on both surfaces; midrib very stout and prominent beneath, rapidly diminishing toward the apex, densely puberulent; secondaries 10-13 pairs, conspicuously arcuate, often issuing at almost right angles to the midrib, slightly prominent beneath, rather inconspicuously anastomosing near the margins; veinlets obscure; inflorescence axillary and terminal; cymes solitary, opposite, frequently small and subsessile, sometimes larger and pedunculate, 1-6 cm. long, 1-4.5 cm. wide, dense and congested, many-flowered, very abundantly and conspicuously bracteolate; panicle terminal, 7-20 cm. long, 2.5-4 cm. wide, narrow and dense, subsessile or pedunculate, composed of 3-7 small cymes which are very conspicuously bracteolate, its sympodia short and abbreviated, flattened, several-sulcate, shortly incanous-pubescent; peduncles rather slender, axillary ones 2-30 mm. long, terminal ones 2-7 cm. long, usually flattened and deeply sulcate, densely incanous-puberulent; pedicels slender, 1-4 mm. long, densely incanous-pubes-cent or velntinous; bractlets very numerous and conspicuous, especially so on somewhat immature cymes, very narrow-elongate or linear, to 2 cm. long, contorted, incanous-pubescent or velutinous, greatly exceeding and sometimes completely hiding the flower-buds, sometimes subequaling the mature flowers; calyx large, long-turbinate or obconic-campanulate, 7-9 mm. long, 3-4.8 mm. wide, constricted for some distance above the ovary, densely incanous or velutinous-pubescent, very lax around the corolla-tube, its rim distinctly 4-toothed or deeply 4-lobed, its lobes oyate, about 2.4 mm. long, rounded at the apex into an acute or acuminate point; corolla infundibular or hypocrateriform, its tube extremely narrow-cylindric, 2.4 - 12 mm. long, very abruptly ampliate above, its lobes 4, ovate-lingulate or oblong-ovate, 3.7-4.3 mm. long, 1.6-2 mm. wide, obtuse at apex; stamens 4, inserted 1-3 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, long-exserted (in male)or included (in female) filaments filiform, 0.5-10 mm. long, glabrate; anthers oblong or somewhat obovoid, 1.5-1.6 mm. long, 0.7-1 mm. wide; pistil subincluded (in male) or long-exserted (in female) style capillary, 1.5-8 mm. long, glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches about 5.5 mm. long; ovary globose or obpyriform, 0.5-1 mm. long and wide, flattened and 4-lobed at apex, glabrate, 4-celled; fruiting-calyx and fruit not seen.

description: Shrub; branches rather stout, obtusely tetragonal, gray, ridged and roughened; branchlets slender, tetragonal, densely pubescent; internodes 1-2 cm. long [or less]; leaves opposite or approximate, apparently crowded on the young shoots; petioles slender, 4-9 mm. long, densely pubescent; blades chartaceous, lanceolate, 6.5-12.5 cm. long, 2-3 cm. wide, acute or acuminate at apex, entire, long-acuminate at base, densely pubescent on both surfaces, especially along the midrib; midrib rather prominent beneath; secondaries 8-10 pairs, arcuateascending; veinlets obscure; infloreseence axillary; eymes numerous, opposite, solitary, very few-flowered; peduncles slender, about 1 cm. long, densely pubescent; flowers not seen; fruiting pedicels 3-10 mm. long, pubescent; fruiting-calyx broadly campanulate, inerassate, about 5 mm. long and 9 mm. wide, pubescent, its rim subtruneate, with 4 apiculations which are each about 1 mm. in length; fruit oblong, about 9 mm. long and 7 mm. wide, smooth, 4-celled, 4-seeded.

description: Subscandent shrub; blanchlets slender, obtusely tetragonal, densely appressed-pubescent or strigose with short antrorsely-curved yellowish-brown hairs; internodes 5.5-7.5 cm. long; leaves decussate; petioles slender, erect, 6-8 mm. long, densely short-pubescent; blades membranous, rather dark green above, lighter beneath, oblong, 6.5-10 cm. long, 3.5-4.5 cm. wide, short-acuminate at apex, entire, not ciliate, rounded at base, very sparsely short-pubescent above with widely scattered and very short hairs, rather more densely so on the midrib, more densely short-pubescent beneath, especially on the midrib and larger veins, the hairs yellowish-brown or ferruginous, very short, apparently eventually deciduous, leaving the surface of the lamina densely marked with minute punctae, without any or with only a very few scattered glands beneath; midrib slender, prominent on both surfaces, especially so beneath, often conspicuously yellow-pubescent with short antrorse hairs on immature leaves; secondaries slender, 8-11 pairs, arcuate-ascending, beautifully and conspicuously anastomosing near the margins beneath; inflorescence apparently terminal only; panicle narrow and elongate, 12.5-22 cm. long, 3-5 cm. wide, composed of 3 or 4 or more pairs of cymes, densely appressed-pubescent with short yellowish-brown antrorse hairs, bracteate, very conspicuously bracteolate, its cymes very short-stipitate, many-flowered, dense and congested, very greatly furcate, its sympodia similar to the branchlets in all respects; peduncles slender, about 5 cm. long, appressed-pubescent like the branchlets and sympodia; pedicels very short or obsolete in bud, eventually 1-3 mm. long, densely appressed-pubescent; bracts few, variable, oblong and foliaceous or broadly linear, 1.5-3.5 cm. long, 2-10 mm. wide; bractlets and prophylla very numerous throughout the inflorescence, linear, pubescent, 2-13 mm. long, greatly exceeding the buds on immature specimens, becoming less conspicuous in flowering cymes; buds small, very densely hirsute-pubescent; calyx campanulate, about 2.5 mm. long and 2 mm. wide, densely pubescent with antrorsely-appressed hairs, its rim 4-toothed with broadly triangular teeth about 0.4 mm. long; corolla infundibular, its tube cylindric, about 4.8 mm. long, glabrous, its lobes 4, ovate-lingulate, about 2.6 mm. long and 1.8 mm. wide, acute at apex; stamens 4, inserted about 0.8 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, exserted (in male); filaments filiform, about 4.5 mm. long; anthers oblong, about 1.3 mm. long and 0.5 mm. wide; pistil included or subincluded (in male); style capillary, about 3.5 mm. long, glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches about 1.6 mm. long; ovary subrotund, about 1 mm. long and wide, 4-celled, glabrous; fruiting-calyx and fruit not seen.
