description: Woody perennial 3-6 dm tall; stems terete or subquadrangulate, densely puberulent, pubescent, or scaberulous, epidermis exfoliating with age, internodes usually 10-25 mm long; stipules scarious, to 3 mm long and 3 mm wide, with several trichome-like teeth to 4 mm long from margins; leaves opposite or in whorls of 3, fasciculate at some nodes, 1-nerved, sessile or tapering to a short petiole, 15-45 mm long, (1) 2.5-10.5 (13) mm wide, glabrous or scabrous, linear- lanceolate, narrowly oblanceolate, narrowly elliptic, or ovate-lanceolate, sharply acute or mucronulate at apex, revolute; flowers in terminal, several-flowered cymes, fragrant, remaining open at night, heterostylous, subsessile or on short pedicels, peduncles and pedicels subtended by conspicuous stipular teeth to ca 4 mm long; calyx glabrous or scabrous, the lobes lanceolate or oblanceolate, acute or mu- cronate, 3-10 mm long, 0.8-1.6 mm wide, sinuses between lobes bearing 1-few trichome-like, whitish teeth or colleters; corolla 4- or occasionally 5-lobed, sal- verform, white or "fading to pale rose," sometimes tinged with rose or purple on midveins and apices of lobes, 30-50 mm long with lobes extended, glabrous externally, corolla tube 25-41 mm long, 1-2 mm wide at base, gradually widening to 1.5-3 mm wide at throat, corolla lobes ovate to elliptic, oblong, or obovate, obtuse, glabrous within or puberulent near base, 4.5-10 mm long, 2-6 mm wide; anthers subversatile, linear, yellowish or black, ca 1.8-3 mm long; styles often white, stigma-branches green or yellow, linear, 1-5 mm long; thrum flowers with anthers exserted beyond corolla throat on filaments 1-2.5 mm long, the filaments attached just below corolla mouth, the style and stigma included, stigma located ca 1-4 mm below corolla mouth (stigma sometimes aborted); pin flowers with style and stigma-branches exserted 2-5 mm beyond throat (or sometimes stigmas exserted from apices of buds to ca 7 mm beyond bud apices), the anthers included, sessile, inserted 1-4 mm below corolla throat; capsules 3/4 to fully inferior, rather thin-walled, dehiscing loculicidally and sometimes later septicidally, subglobose, glabrous, when mature 3-6 mm long, 3-6 mm wide, placenta attached to septum ca 1/3 of distance from base to top of septum; seeds dark brown or black, 0.45-1.0 mm long, 0.3-0.65 mm wide, moderately to strongly laterally compressed, irregularly and sharply angulate, the hilum punctiform at apex of a narrow hilar ridge, the testa polygonal-reticulate. Chromosome number n = 13, 2n = 26.

description: Scandent shrub; branchlets slender, obtusely tetragonal or subterete? pronouncedly hirsute with brown and often reflexed hairs; internodes 5-6 cm. long; leaves decussate; petioles very weak, about 5 mm. long, densely hirsute; blades membranous or chartaceous, rather dark green above, somewhat lighter beneath, very nitid, oblong or oblong-ovate, 6.5-13.5 cm. long, 2.5-5 cm. wide, long-acuminate or caudate at apex, entire and ciliate along the margins, rounded or slightly subcordate at base, hirtous on both surfaces with long brown spreading hairs, rather sparsely above, more densely so beneath, with the hairs about twice as numerous on the secondaries and 4 times as numerous on the midrib; midrib slender, prominent on both surfaces, especially beneath; secondaries slender, 8-11 pairs, irregularly disposed, prominulent beneath, arcuate-ascending, beautifully and conspicuously anastomosing near the margins beneath; inflorescence apparently terminal only; panicle about 11.5 cm. long and 4 cm. wide, composed of 4 or more pairs of small, dense, and very congested cymes, bracteate, its sympodia similar to the branchlets in all respects; peduncles slender, about 4 cm. long, brown-hirsute like the branchlets; pedicels slender, about 1.5 mm. long, densely hirsute; bracts linear-lanceolate, to 2.5 cm. long, stipitate, densely hirsute beneath, less so above; bractlets linear-elongate, very numerous, densely hirsute; pro-phylla numerous, setaceous; flower-buds densely hirsute with brown multicellular hairs which are to 1.5 mm. long and stand out more or less at right angles; calyx broadly campanulate, about 2.1 mm. long and 4.2 mm. wide, spreading-pubescent or hirsute, its rim shallowly 4-lobed; corolla infundibular, its tube cylindric, about 11.4 mm. long, ampliate above, its lobes 4, oblong-obovate, about 4.2 mm. long and 2.9 mm. wide, acute at apex; stamens 4, inserted about 4.2 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, exserted (in male); filaments filiform, about 10.4 mm. long (in male), pilose below; anthers oblong or rotund, about 1.5 mm. long and 1 mm. wide; pistil included (in male); style capillary, about 2.9 mm. long (in male), glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches about 3.4 mm. long; ovary oblong, about 1 mm. long and 0.8 mm. wide, 4-celled; fruiting-calyx and fruit not seen.

description: Small solitary palm; trunk grey, slender, 2-8 m tall and 2.5-3.9(-4.5) cm dbh, vertically cracked in the lower 1-2 m, the nodal scars barely noticeable, irregularly shaped, the internodes at breast height variable and irregular, of about 0.5-1.5 cm. Root cone at the base of the stem often present, up to 40 cm in both height and basal diameter. Leaves 9-20 in crown, 68-98 cm long (from sheath base to leaf tip). Skirt of dry leaves often covering the upper 0.5-3 m of the stem. Leaf sheath 20-30 cm long, pale brown, flexible, unarmed, covered in a whitish deciduous tomentum that rapidly disappears from exposed parts; sheath fibres 0.5-3.5 mm thick, straw-colored, confluent, initially joined at their tips, forming an acuminate free flap of 6-13 cm, then split as new leaves are produced; free strands 3-7 cm wide. Petiole biconvex, 20-26(-31) cm long (sheath excluded), 5-9 mm wide close to the base of the blade; blade semiorbicular (to 3/4 orbicular); segments 16-19, the central ones 24-30(-42) cm long, reaching maximum width of 2-2.5 cm at shoulder at 3/5 of their length; palman irregular, oval-shaped, 13-mm wide, with thick bright yellow ribs the adaxial surface, ending in a thicker reinforced sinus between segments, with a bright brown scar; central two segments often more deeply divided than the others; adaxial face of the leaf green, glaucous, unevenly coated with a shiny wax that is absent from youngest and oldest leaves; abaxial surface green, with silvery deciduous indumentum; adaxial hastula small, rigid, triangular-ovate, 5-10 mm long, yellow and shiny; abaxial hastula triangular, acute, not often prominent. Inflorescences 90-109 cm long (from base to tip), curved at tip, longer than leaves, emerging above crown, 2-3 fresh ones borne at a time together with older dead ones; partial inflorescences 3-4; rachillae 4-12 in each partial inflorescence, ca. 1 mm thick close to the base, (1.9-)5-7.5 cm long, white during anthesis, turning yellow-green as fruits develop; bracts membranous, with deciduous brown tomentum persisting at the tips, green then green-white at anthesis and afterwards brown; bracts of partial inflorescences thinner and after anthesis becoming papyraceous and semitransparent; rachilla bracts lanceolate, 1-1.7 mm long. Flowers sessile, creamy white, mildly and sweetly scented (reminiscent of Nerium oleander); perianth lobes 6, 1.3-1.6 mm long, shortly joined at the base; anthers sagittate, 1.6-2 mm long, white; ovary globose, green; style 1.5 mm long, apex obtuse. Unripe fruits 2-4 mm, light green, smooth, densely packed together on the rachilla, stigmatic scar prominent; ripe fruits globose, creamy white, 4.8- 6.3 mm in diam.; overripe fruits browning and cracking, with endocarps partially exposed as the result of sunburn. Seed 3.4-4.5 mm in diam., slightly compressed, with 3-4 grooves, weighing 51.6 mg on average; cotyledonary petiole 10-14 mm long; basal ligule 7-8 mm long; eophyll rigid, flat, 1.2- 1.4 mm x 80-90 mm, with 3 veins; eophyll petiole exposed, elongate.

description: Plant a pendent, epseudobulbous, psygmoid epiphyte, to 8 cm tall. Roots flexuous, glabrous, ca. 1 mm in diameter. Leaves distichous, laterally flattened (equitant), narrowly elliptic-subfalcate, acuminate, grayish green, 5-6.5 x 0.5-0.8 cm, articulate at the base with rectangular-obtrapezoidal sheaths provided with hyaline margins, to 1.3 x 1.1 cm. Inflorescence racemose, many-flowered, to 9 per inflorescence, to 10 cm long, produced from the axils of the upper leaves, pendent and upcurving, becoming apically erect at maturity; peduncle and rachis terete, glabrous, the peduncle to 3 cm long, concealed at the base by a short triangular bract up to 2.5 mm long. Floral bracts ovate, acute, spreading, subhyaline, becoming papyraceous with age, to 2 x 2 mm. Ovary pedicellate, terete-subclavate, glabrous, 5 mm long including the pedicel. Flowers non-resupinate, segments spreading, translucent white, the callus of the lip adorned with three emerald-green spots. Dorsal sepal subrectangular-oblong, erect, widely obtuse to subtruncate, erose, concave toward the apex, ca. 3 x 1.5 mm, abaxially aristate, the arista (awn) to 1.2 mm long. Lateral sepals oblong to narrowly obovate, obtuse to rounded, minutely erose, strongly reflexed, concave toward the apex, ca. 3 x 1.4 mm, abaxially aristate, the awn flexuous-falcate, ca. 1.2 mm long. Petals spathulate, rounded, erose, abaxially carinate, the keel erose, ca. 3.2 x 2.3 mm, porrect and with the lateral margins revolute in natural position. Lip 3-lobed, narrowly hastate, ca. 5.2 x 2.5 mm across the lateral lobes, the lateral lobes triangular-ovate, erose-denticulate, to 1 mm long; midlobe linear, acute, conduplicate and subreflexed at apex, ca. 4 x 1.2 mm; disc provided with a massive, obreniform, 2-lobed, thick callus 1.2 x 1.6 mm, the lobes rounded, suberect, concave, the median groove with a conical tuft of stiff glandular hairs. Column erect, terete, ampullaceous at the base, long-acuminate to caudate at apex, ca. 4.3 x 0.8 mm at the base; stigma rounded; clinandrium concave, subquadrate; rostellum acicular, abruptly curved at the middle. Anther cap narrowly triangular-acuminate, basally rounded, 2-celled. Pollinia 4, spherical, in two pairs, on a hyaline, filiform, apically dilated stipe; viscidium narrowly elliptic, brown.

description: Shrubs and small trees flowering at 3 m tall, to 15 m tall; stems quadrangular, glabrous. description: Shrub (?); branchlets very slender, obtusely tetragonal, often somewhat sulcate, appressed-puberulent with very minute yellowish hairs; internodes 2.5-4.5 cm. long; leaf-scars enlarged and prominent; pistil long-exserted (in female); style capillary, 17-21 mm. long (in female), glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches about 9.3 mm. long; ovary obovate, dark, about 1.5 mm. long and 1.3 mm. wide, 4-lobed at apex, glabrous, 4-celled; description: Shrub or tree, 3-9 m. tall; wood thin; pith very ample; branches and branchlets acutely tetragonal, deeply canaliculate along the sides, decussately flattened and ampliate at the nodes, very medullose, rather densely ineanous-pubeseent or sericeous; internodes 5-7 cm. long; leaves decussate-opposite or very rarely approximate; petioles 4-13 mm. long, canaliculate above, ineanous-pubeseent; blades membranous or chartaceous, rather shiny-green above, paler beneath, varying from oblong to obovate or elliptic, 7.5-35 cm. long, 3.5-15 cm. wide, acuminate at apex, entire or denticulate, long-attenuate at base and decur- rent into the petiole, appressed-hirtous or ineanous-tomentose above, becoming glabrate but remaining slightly roughened in age, appressed- sericeous-puberulent or delicately ineanous-tomentose beneath, espe- cially along the midrib and larger veins, dotted with cutaneous glands beneath, slightly aromatic; midrib stout, prominent beneath, densely ineano-sericeous; secondaries slender, 10-15 pairs, usually prominent beneath, arcuate-aseending, more or less anastomosing near the mar- gins, densely ineano-sericeous; veinlets very slender and delicate; in florescence axi[lary; eymes solitary, opposite, half as long as the sub- tending leaves or less, dichotomous or trifid, conglobate or capitately corynibose, dense, many-flowered, or sometimes somewhat lax-flowered, bracteolate; flowers copious, pronouncedly dielinous; peduncles slen- der, 2-5 cm. long, shorter in 9 than in &, often flattened and dis- tinctly canaliculate, densely strigose-sericeous or ineanous; pedicels filiform, up to 5 mm. long in &, very short or obsolete in 9, ineanous- pubescent; bractlets and prophylla usually absent, or, when present, few, linear, subulate, firm, very short, ineanous; calyx clavate-infun- dibular or subturbinate-tubular (or turbinate-campanulate in 9 ), subangular, rather firmly membranous or subherbaceous, 5-8 mm. long, about 3 mm. wide, densely ineano-sericeous outside, softly sericeous within, lax around the corolla-tube, its rim acutely 4-dentate, 4-lobed, or 4-split, its lobes ovate, acute at apex, often patulous; corolla infundibular, white or yellowish, its tube cylindric, slender, 4-12 mm. long, puberulent toward the apex, its lobes 4, ovate- or lanceolate- lingulate, 2-4 mm. long, about 2 mm. wide, spreading, often reflexed, acute at apex; stamens 4, inserted about 1 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, exserted (in d ) or equaling the corolla-tube (in 9 ); filaments filiform, 0.2-7 mm. long, glabrous; anthers oblong, erect, about 1 mm. long and 0.5 mm. wide, subsessile and tabeseent in 9; pistil included (in d ) or exserted (in 9 ); style capillary, 3.7-7 mm. long, glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches 2.4-3.4 mm. long [or longer in 9 ], papillose; ovary subglobose, about 1 mm. long and wide, flat at both ends, glabrous, 4-lobed at apex, 4-celled; fruiting-calyx greatly enlarged and indurated, cupuliform, rather shallowly and irregularly lobed, enclosing the base of the fruit; fruit subglobose or obovate, about 8 mm. long and 7 mm. wide, depressed at apex, smooth and shiny, green or yellow at base, becoming orange, 2-4-seeded, its base invested by the mature calyx; description: Small or arborescent shrub, 2-4 m. tall; branches acutely tetrag- onal or becoming subterete, decussately flattened and somewhat ampli- ate at the nodes, very brachiate, spreading, with light gray bark, appressed-incanous or sericeous, becoming glabrate in age; description: This variety differs from the typical form of the species in its more ovate, ovate-elliptic, or elliptic blades, which are rather obtusely acuminate at apex and rounded at base, only 4.5-8 cm. long and 2.5-4 cm. wide, and have only 4-6 pairs of secondaries, in its usually more twiggy habit, with each twig terminated by an abbreviated panicle, in its usually much more abbreviated and loosely flowered panicles, in its filaments to 11 mm. long, and in its corolla-tube to 9.6 mm. long. The type of this variety was collected by William Harris (No. 8166) on Plowden Hill, Jamaica, at an altitude of 270 m., November 22, 1901, and is deposited in the Krug & Urban Herbarium at Berlin. It has been given specific rank by Urban. However distinct the type collection may appear on account of its many short axillary twigs, each surmounted by an abbreviated panicle, and because of its large flow- ers [which characters would seem to relate it to the Trifidae group mostly endemic to Jamaica], it greatly resembles such specimens as Lloyd 606 from Dominica, Smith & Smith 336a from St. Vincent, and others, which, in turLLn, are very obviously only a form of A. mar- tinicensis. 18.

description: Frutex scandens, ramulis subangulatis glabris; folia opposita, simplicia, membranacea, glabra, oblongo-ovata, 8-13 cm. longa et 3-5 cm. lata, basi subcordata vel truneata, apice acurginata, supra viridia, subtus paullo pallidiora, eximie quinquenervia, nervorum jugo interno laminae longitudinem totam aequante, externo dimidiam, trabeculis inter nervos scalariformibus, petiolis glabris 1.0-1.5 cm. longis non-articulatis; infloreseentiae laxe eymosae, axillares terminalesque, bracteis minutis instructae; calyx glaber, pedicello 1.0-1.5 cm. longo, tubo 2 mm. longo, lobis 5, 1 mm. longis deltoideis subearinatis abrupte apiculatis; corolla nivea, tubo 1 cm. longo, lobis 5 plus minusve reflexis subrotundatis apiculatis 0.5 cm. longis; stamina 2, tubae medio adnata, antheris subapiculatis, magnis, basifixis 4-5 mm. longis et 1-2 mm. latis; ovarium bilobum, stylo simplice, 1 cm. longo, apice inerassato stigmatibus 2 corniculatis, corollae faucem longitudinem aemulantibuls; fructus ignotus.

description: Tall shrub or tree, 3-10 m. tall, or subscandent; branches tetrag- onal and flattened or subterete, lax, rufescent tomentose-villose or subhirsute; bark cinereous; branchlets acutely tetragonal or decus- sately flattened, ampliate at the nodes, densely rufescent tomentose- villose or subhirsute, very twiggy with very short twigs toward the apex, ending rather abruptly; internodes 1-4 cm. long; leaves decus- sate-opposite or subalternate, usually only approximate; petioles slender, 7-12 mm. long, densely tomentose-villose; blades chartaceous, deep green above, paler beneath, oblong-lanceolate or oblanceolate, 10-20 cm. long, 2.5-7 cm. wide, acute or slightly acuminate at apex, entire, acute or often oblique at base, sometimes attenuate into the petiole, strigose or subvillose and viscid above, subvillose or pilose beneath; midrib slender, prominent and densely pilose beneath; sec- ondaries very slender, 10 or 11 pairs, arcuate-ascending, slightly prominulent and densely pilose beneath; veinlets delicate, inconspicu- ous; inflorescence axillary, often densely congested on many short axillary twigs near the apex of the branchlets; cymes corymbose, solitary, opposite, very lax, bracteolate, loosely many-flowered; pedun- cles very slender, 9-15 mm. long, densely rufescent-villose, lax and flaccid, often subnutant; pedicels slender and filiform, about 6 mm. long, densely villose; bractlets slender, subulate, 7-9 mm. long, densely villose; prophylla linear, 1-2 mm. long, villose; calyx obconic, 6-7.5 mm. long, about 3.3 mm. wide, subappressedly villose, its rim 4-toothed, its teeth distinct, about 2 mm. long, often long-cuspidate or setaceous at apex from a short and triangular base, sometimes irregu- lar with wide sinuses; corolla infundibular, greenish-white or yellowish, glabrous, its tube slender, cylindric, about 7.549 mm. Ping, its lobes 4, oblong-lingulate, about 7 mm. long and 2 mm. wide, obtuse at apex; stamens 4, inserted about 3 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, long-exserted (in d ); filaments capillary, to 15 mm. long (in d ), glabrous; anthers oblong, about 2 mm. long and 1 mm. wide; pistil included (in d ); style capillary, about 6.5 mm. long (in d ), glabrate; stigmiia bifid, its branches about 4.2 mm. long, puberulent; ovary subrotund, flattened above, 4-lobed at apex, glabrous, 4-celled; fruiting-calyx enlarged and indurated, cupuliform, light, about 7 mm. long and 9 mm. wide, very densely pilose with yellowish hairs, loosely investing the lower half of the fruit, its rim subtruncate, with 4 regular apiculations about 1 mm. long; fruit oblong, about 11 mm. long and 6 mm. wide, orange, glabrous, 4-seeded, very wrinkled in drying; seeds extremely oily.

description: Shrub; branches medium-slender or stout, light gray when young, becoming chestnut-brown in age; branchlets slender, light gray, very medullose, very lightly puberulent or glabrate, often with elevated lenticels, twiggy; internodes 1.5-6 cm. long; leaf-scars prominent; leaves decussate-opposite or subopposite; petioles very slender, 8-13 mm. long, canaliculate above, slightly winged, very minutely puberu- lent; blades extremely thin-chartaceous, very dark above, paler be- neath, oblanceolate or obovate, 6.5-9.5 cm. long, 2-3.8 cm. wide, abruptly narrowed to an acute or acuminate point at apex, entire, cuneate at base and long-attenuate into the petiole, very sparsely strigillose above, more densely puberulent beneath; midrib very slender, prominent beneath; secondaries about 6 pairs, very slender, very slightly prominent beneath, arcuate-ascending, rather incon- spicuously anastomosing near the margins; inflorescence axillary, glomerate, sessile; glomerules small, solitary, opposite, 1-3-flowered; flowers not seen; peduncles obsolete; fruiting pedicels stout, 1-3 mm. long, puberulent or very shortly appressed-strigose; fruiting-calyx indurated, cupuliform, to 8 mm. long and 15 mm. wide, densely puberulent or very shortly and minutely appressed-strigose, its rim 4-lobed, its lobes broadly triangular-ovate; fruit subrotund, about 8 mm. long and wide, 4-celled, included by the calyx when immature.

description: Shrub; branchlets elongate, quite slender, obsoletely tetragonal or subterete, brownish, short-pubescent or pilose, especially toward the apex; internodes 4.5-8 cm. long; leaves decussate; petioles slender and weak, 5-10 mm. long, puberulent or shortly pilose-pubeseent; blades thin-chartaceous, dark green on both surfaces, blackening and becom- ing more or less undate in drying, rather nitid, oblong or oblong- lanceolate, 14-23 cm. long, 4-6.5 cm. wide, acuminate at apex, entire, acute or acuminate at base, sometimes very shortly decurrent into the petiole, glabrate above except for a slight puberulence on the midrib and larger veins, rather more densely puberulent or short-pubescent and densely impressed-puLnetate beneath; midrib very slender, promi- nent on both surfaces, usually pronouncedly undate or tortuous in drying; secondaries very slender, 6-10 pairs, irregularly disposed, often with short and very irregularly branched ones intervening be- tween the normal larger ones, rather prominent on both surfaces, usually undate, arcuate-aseending, anastomosing near the margins; veinlets very slender and delicate, usually pronouLncedly undate in drying and thus conspicuous; infloreseence terminal; panicle pyra- midal, to 16 cm. long and 6 cm. wide, many-flowered, brachiate, bracteate, its branches numerous, short, the lower ones often de- flexed, its sympodia many, short, slender, tetragonal, suleate, short- pubescent or brownish-pilose; peduncles slender, 2.5-4 cm. long, densely short-pubescent; pedicels filiform, 4-5 mm. long, puberulent; bracts apparently few, small, subfoliaceous, ovate or acumiliate-spatu- late, eaducouis; bractlets linear, to 5 mm. long; prophylla setaceous, 1-2 mm. long; calyx campanulate or eyathiform, 2.3-3.3 mm. long, about 3.1 mm. wide, pulverulent-puberulent, its rim truncate, entire or 4- apiculate; corolla infundibular, yellowish, its tube narrow-cylindric, 4.1-4.3 mmin. long, glabrate, its lobes 4, oblong-lingulate, about 4.6 mm. long and 1.8 mm. wide, acute or obtuse at apex; stamens 4, inserted about 0.5 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, long-exserted (in male); filaments filiform, to 7.8 mm. long (in male), glabrous; anthers oval or oblong, about 1.3 lum. long and 1 nmm. wide; pistil included (in male) style capillary, about 3.6 mm. long (in male), glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches about 2 mm. long; ovary obovate, about 1 mm. long and 0.9 mm. wide, glabrate, 4-celled; fruiting-calyx greatly enlarged and in- durated, heavy, cupuliform, 3-4 mm. long, 8-10 mm. wide, glabrate, its rim truncate and elntire, perfectly eireular; fruit oblong, glabrous, 4-seeded.

description: Habit exactly that of L. laciniata, but the leaves fewer (up to about 10), and quite entire except for the callose tip which is transversely elongate; roots up to 2 mm in diameter and 10 cm long; flowers usually 1 only; cylindric basal portion of the corolla-tube about 2 mm long and the filaments adnate to this part only; hypanthium at maturity subglobose, about 2.5 mm in diameter, more than twice as thick as the stout pedicel; ovary nearly wholly inferior, the free part convex, included in the hypanthium-rim which is 0.6-O.8 mm high and topped by the short triangular calyx-lobes which are widely separated by rounded sinuses; ovules probably 20 or fewer; placentation and division of ovary not ascertained; calyxlobes little enlarged in fruit, 0.2-0.8 mm long and about as wide, entire, widely separated and appearing as small lobes of the hypanthium-rim; seeds fusiform, lustrous, with fine longitudinal cellular lines, about 1.3 mm long.

description: A cushion-forming perennial from a stout tap-root, the plants up to 5 cm across and 3 cm high; root-crown enlarged and fleshy (or woody?), up to about 1.5 cm long and thick, bearing toward the end the very numerous (200-300) spirally arranged leaves and, toward the center of the tuft, the 50 or more flowers; leaves thin, linear, about 1 mm wide, 18-20 mm long, with blunt, callose tips; margins entire (or occasionally with a small callose tooth), but usually ciliate except sometimes at the tip; surfaces of the blade sometimes sparingly hispid with pale hairs (like the marginal cilia) up to 0.2 mm long; leaves somewhat narrowed below, often not more than 0.3 mm wide just above the base, and widened to 1 mm at the insertion on the stem; flowers 7-9 mm long, the erectblackanthers standing conspicuously above the rest of the plant; pedicel 6 mm long or less; corolla white, about 6 mm long, the tube broadly cylindric, 3-3.5 mm long (2-2.5 mm long to the dorsal sinus), the limb not strongly bilabiate; all the lobes elongate, somewhat recurved, narrowly pointed, the dorsal about 0.9 mm wide, 2.7-3 mm long, the 3 ventral ones somewhat united, 0.7 mm wide, 2.5 mm long; filamenttube 5-6 mm long, exserted nearly half its length, adnate to the base of the corolla about 1 mm; anther-tube black (Stork & Porton), 1.6-2 mm long, not incurved (i.e. erect and exactly in line with the filaments), narrowed to both ends (the long anthers neither much enlarged nor incurved at the tips, the orifice of the tube thus subterminal and the processes (0.3-0.6 mm long) at the ends of the short anthers erect, and much exceeding the tips of the long anthers, until pushed down by the elongating style); mature bypanthium about 2-2.5 mm thick, 3-4 mm long, obliquely obconic; calyx glabrous or sparingly ciliate, the lobes entire, ovate-oblong, blunt-pointed, unequal, the dorsal 3 mm long, the lateral pair 2 mm, the ventral pair 1.5 mm; sinuses narrow, each bearing in the deepest part an erect, slender tooth up to 0.3 mm long; ovary unilocular; ovules about 20 or fewer, attached to the ventral wall; seeds oblong, brown, nearly smrrooth, about 1 mm long, with a longitudinal cellular pattern.

description: Perennial, with latex, glabrous, the 50-80 leaves stiff, in dense rosettes at the tips of stout, woody, branched caudices; leaves (1.3-) 2.5-3.5 cm long, thick, opaque, lustrous, the surface glassy, the tips with prominent, thick, erose, glassy margins and points; leaf as a whole linear-oblanceolate, the blade proper 2-4 mm wide and entire near the abruptly and very sharply pointed tip, thence tapering gradually to near the margined, scarious base, where enlarged and up to 5 mm wide; leaves usually toothed below the middle, the teeth slender, terete, blunt, antrorsely appressed, increasing in length to the base of the leaf, where up to 1.5 mm long; flower and pedicel together less than 2 cm long, the whole immersed in and concealed by the rosette-leaves; corolla pure white (Camp), 6-7 mmi long, the broad tube 3.5 mm long (1.5 mm to the dorsal sinus), oblong-campanulate; limb scarcely bilabiate, the dorsal lobes longest, lanceolate, 1-1.2 mm wide, 3-3.5 mm long, recurved, the ventral lobes relatively broader, 1-1.5 mm wide, somewhat united but individually recurved (not deflexed as a lip), the free parts 2.2-2.8 mm long; stamens wholly included, the filamenttube 1.8-2 mm long, adnate to the base of the corolla about half its length; anthers 1.5 mm long, purplish (Camp) or ultramarine-blue (Espinosa), the short anthers naked at the tips; hypanthium at anthesis hardly differentiated from the pedicel, in fruit campanulate, 2.5 mm thick and 2.5-4 mm long, angled, tapering to the flattened pedicel which is 1-1.2 mm thick at the summit; calyx-lobes 4-5.5 mm long, about equal, narrowly triangular, sharp-pointed and glassy-margined like the leaves, appressed and mostly inclosing the corolla, usually with one slender, appressed tooth on each side below the middle; ovary imperfectly bilocular, the ovules about 50, attached to both sides of the placenta, the distal part of the ovary unilocular; operculum shallowly conic, 2 mm in diameter; seeds light brown, 0.8 mm long, ovoid-ellipsoid, srmooth

description: Stems 3-10 cm long; leaves 10-16 rrmm long, 0.3-0.7 mm wide, sparingly callose-denticulate, the blunt tip with a prominent glandular callosity; flowers white (Espinosa), the pedicels up to 4 mm long; hypanthium at anthesis hardly differentiated from the pedicel, in fruit narrowly ellipsoid, terete, 1.3-1.5 mm thick, 3-4 mm long, distally unilocular, the placenta in the proximal third with the ovules borne at its summit, and the membranes below this dividing the ovary into two chambers; calyx-lobes like the leaves but entire and narrower, 3.7-4 mm long, appressed to the corolla, unequal, the dorsal one longest; seeds broadly ovoid or subglobose, about 10 (ovules probably about 20), 0.7-1 mm long, brown, the surface shallowly or deeply honeycombed.

description: Plants rosette-form, the leaves up to 40 in number, arising nearly at one level (the bases much overlapping) from a corm-like stem up to 1 cm in diameter, from which arise also up to 25 clustered, fleshy, fusiform roots 1-4 mm in diameter and 2-10 cm long; leaves usually elongate, large for the plant, 3-8 cm long, linear to oblanceolate to obovate, usually with a division into blade and petiole, the blade elliptic to linear, about half as long as the whole leaf (or the basal petiolar portion much elongated when the plants grow immersed in moss or mud), bluntly pointed, usually attenuate at the base, the leaf as a whole thus narrowest in the middle and gradually widened toward the elongate base which is glabrous, flattened and membranous, lacking chlorophyll, scarious and veiny when dry, up to 4-6 mm wide at its junction with the stem; margins obscurely or conspicuously callose-denticulate, sometimes apparently entire, or varying to sinuate-dentate or with prominent, widely spaced teeth, or pinnatifid; flowers erect, short-pedicellate, axillary, immersed in the rosette at anthesis or the corolla (only) exceeding the leaves; pedicels usually somewhat flattened tangentially, in fruit 1-1.5 (-2.5) mm wide, 1-4 cm long; flowers the largest in the genus, 1.5-5 cm long, the corolla white, usually with yellow tube and the ventral side of the throat yellow with red or purple markings; corolla-tube straight, with a narrowly cylindric proximal portion (often about 0.5 mm in diameter near the base, and about 1 mm thick for most of its length) several times as long as the broadly cylindric or narrowly campanulate throat which may be 2-3 mm in diameter at the orifice (i.e. distally) and 3-6 mm long; tube as a whole very variable in length, but chiefly in the narrow proximal portion rather than in the throat; dorsal sinus slightly deeper than the lateral ones; limb strongly bilabiate, the dorsal lobes lanceolate, acute, erect or somewhat recurved, 1-2 mm wide, 4-6 mm long, the ventral lobes somewhat united and forming a slightly reflexed lip, the divisions ovate-lanceolate, acute, 1.5-3 mm wide, 2.5-5 mm long; all the lobes and the throat roughened within with very short papillose hairs, or the hairs longer and slender; filament-tube varying in length in the different subspecific taxa, usually about 1 mm longer than the corolla-tube, the filaments free from the corolla in the throat only; anther-tube blue-gray to black, somewhat incurved, oblong, (1.5-) 1.8-2.3 (-2.6) mm long, its variation in length not correlated with those of the corolla-tube and filaments; ventral anthers about 0.5 mm shorter, each tipped with several short, white, blunt bristles and also cornute, the hyaline appendage (often flattened in drying) up to 0.5-0.8 mm long; hypanthium in fruit ellipsoid, often broadly so and somewhat flattened tangentially, the ovary usually more than half inferior, the free beak conic and attenuate into the style-base; ovules probably usually 50 or fewer (fewer developing), borne on the two sides of the flattened placenta which is attached near the base of the ventral side of the ovary; placenta nearly as wide as the hypanthium and flattened parallel with it, attached to the edges by fragile membranes and making the hypanthium in effect bilocular, but not extending into the unilocular beak which forms the operculum; calyx-lobes little-enlarged i n fruit, triangular-subulate to linear or broadly triangular, variously toothed and ciliate or entire and glabrous, the sinuses between them broad and rounded (at least in fruit) and their bases connected and forming an evident ring 0.5-1 mm high above the summit of the hypanthium; lobes often partially undeveloped at anthesis and lacking chlorophyll; seeds oblong-ellipsoid or fusiform, lustrous, without prominent surface features but with fine longitudinal cellular reticulation.

description: Apparently a short-lived perennial, hirtellous, sparingly branched, erect, 4-8 cm high, from a thickened and apparently somewhat fleshy base, the leaves entire, lanceolate, 1-1.7 mm wide above the decurrent base, 4-6 mm long, somewhat keeled near the tip and near the base on the dorsal (outer) surface; hairs pale, up to 0.3 mm long, slender and straight, erect, tapering to a sharp point, abundant and uniformly distributed along the leaf-margins and on the dorsal surface, sparse or wanting on the ventral surface except near the tip; corolla. tube narrowly funnelform, 3-3.7 mm long (1 mm at the dorsal sinus); filamenttube 4-4.2 mm long, attached to the corolla at the base only; hypanthium in fruit about 1.5 mm thick, 2.5 mm long, apparently unilocular, few- (about 5- to 8-?) seeded; calyx-lobes entire, erect, triangular-lanceolate, sharper than the leaftips, the longest (dorsal) lobe (2-) 2.7 mm long, the lateral pair about 2.5 mm long, the ventral pair about 2 mm; dorsal surface of all lobes hirtellous like the leaves and the hypanthium; seeds brown, 0.5-0.7 mm long, broadly ovate or fusiform, longitudinally 6 to 8-angled, each angle with 12-15 transverse lines.

description: Hypanthium unilocular, flattened dorsally, in fruit about 1 mm thick with acute margins, in outline elliptic, about 1.8 mm wide and 3 mm long; ovules about 7, attached near the base of the ovary on the ventral surface; calyx-lobes entire, triangular-lanceolate, acute, about 0.5 mm wide, the dorsal one 1.7-2.2 mm long, the lateral and ventral pairs successively shorter, all fimbriate-ciliate except at the very tips; seeds at maturity in 1 layer in the capsule, brown, ovoid or subglobose, about 1 mm long, pebbled, when dry longitudinally 8- to 10-angled.

description: Individual plants erect, glabrous but ciliate, 1-3 cm high, thickly aggregated in mosslike mats; stems sparingly branched, 1-2 mm thick, the bases covered with persistent, rough leaf-bases; leaves very numerous, ascending, thickly imbricated along the stems, linear, sessile, boat-shaped, entire, the tips blunt and cucullate with one terminal glandular callosity; blades lustrous, strongly rounded on the backs (often so much so as to appear cylindric), the veins not apparent; cilia glassy in texture, somewhat thickened at the base, up to about 0.3 mm long; flowers few in the upper axils; corolla apparently always white (or purplish?); limb hardly bilabiate, the lobes ovate-triangular, acute, somewhat falcate, the dorsal pair slightly the longest; stamens included, or the anthers somewhat surpassing the recurved tips of the corolla; anthers slightly incurved, the short ones minutely appendiculate; ovary unilocular; calyx-lobes entire, ciliate and gland-tipped like the leaves but broader, ovate-triangular, unequal; ovules probably always about 10; seeds ellipsoid, about 0.6 mm long, dark brown, without prominent surface features but with minute cellular markings.

description: Perennial, glabrous, the 50 or more leaves stiff, in dense rosettes at the tips of the stout, woody, branched caudices; leaves 1.5-2 cm long, thick, opaque, lustrous, the surface and the tips somewhat glassy; blade proper concave above, lanceolate, 6-8 mnm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, abruptly pointed at the entire and minutely serrulate tip, bidentate at the base and there giving way abruptly to the slightly narrower, scarious, spinescent-ciliate petiolar base which is 1.2-1.5 mm wide at the base of the blade and slightly widened (to 2 mm) at the junction with the stem; flower and pedicel together less than 1.5 cm long (the pedicel 1-2 mm long), the whole no more than equaling the spreading rosette leaves; corolla white (Steyermark), about 9 mm long, the tube 5 mm long (4 mm to the dorsal sinus), cylindric, about 1.5 mm thick; limb bilabiate, the lobes apparently all recurved; dorsal lobes about 1 mnm wide, 4 mm long, the ventral broader, somewhat united, about 1.5 mm wide, apparently deflexed somewhat together as a lip, the free parts 3 mm long; stamens apparently well exserted beyond the recurved corolla-lobes, the filament-tube 5.5 mm long, adnate to the base of the corolla for nearly 1 mm; anthers 2 mm long, the short ones with apical bristles and each cornute with.a hyaline process 0.5 mm long; hypanthium at anthesis hardly differentiated from the pedicel, in fruit 2.5-2.7 mm in diameter and 3 mm long, angled, the nearly straight sides tapering to the very short, stout pedicel; calyx-lobes triangular-subulate, 3.5-4 mm long, all about equal, shorter than the corolla-tube, each with a tooth on each edge below the middle; sinuses very narrow, acute; ovary bilocular except at the summit, the ovules probably about 50, on both sides of the flattened placenta; operculum elongate-conic, about 1.5 mm across at base, 2.5 mm long; seeds light brown, 0.8 mm long, slenderly ovoid-ellipsoid, smooth, lustrous.

description: Perennial, glabrous, the [?30-401 leaves stiff, spreading, in a dense rosette at the tip of an apparently stout-herbaceous branch 3 mm in diameter; basal part of the stem, and the root-system, unknown; leaves 11-13 mm long, oblanceolate, thick, opaque, lustrous, the surface glassy; blades with a firm distal portion 1.5-2 mm wide, obtuse or rounded at the tip, with a terminal callosity and 1-4 additional marginal glandular-callose teeth on each side, the margin in outline entire or shallowly crenate; distal part of the blade ("blade" proper) about 7 mm long, narrowly elliptic and differentiated slightly from the linear and more delicate petiolar base which is 4-6 mm long; flower sessile, about 17 mm long, somewhat surpassing the subtending leaf; corolla elongate, apparently white, the tube subcylindric, 9 mm long to the lateral sinuses (7.5 mm to the dorsal sinus), sligbtly curved toward the ventral side, slightly enlarged from the base to near the summit where it is about 1.5 mm in diameter; lobes apparently nearly straight (position uncertain), narrowly triangular, the dorsal ones longest,, about 1 mm wide at the base and 4 mm long; stamens apparently somewhat exserted froni the dorsal sinus when fresh, the filament-tube 9 mm long [attachment to the corolla not ascertained, but probably at the base only], the anther-tube nearly black, 1.6 mm long, probably incurved; hypanthium [seen in flower only] oblong, probably tangentially flattened in the rosette, 3 mm long; calyx-lobes with the texture of the leaves, broadly linear, appressed, I mm wide or a little less, 4.5 mm long, equal, abruptly blunt-pointed and callose-tipped, entire or with one small tooth on each side.

description: Erect perennial herbs, subacaulescent or the mostly unbranched stems 2-9 cm high, the numerous (often up to 100) leaves mostly aggregated at the tip of the stem in a terminal rosette; leaves narrow, flat, glabrous or hirtellous, linear to oblanceolate, usually entire, the tip acute, with a terminal glandular callosity, the base attenuate, sessile, often dilated at the point of attachment to the stem; flowers numerous, up to 50 or more, in the upper axils, shorter than the principal rosette-leaves at anthesis but conspicuous among them (pedicels 2-5 mm long, but often much elongate and up to 20 mm long in fruit); corolla white to pale yellow, yellow tipped with red, reddish-brown, purplish-brown, or brown, 2.2-4.5 (usually 2.5-3.5) mm long, usually less than twice as long as the longest calyx-lobes; corolla-tube 1-2 mm long (0.5-1.5 mm long at the dorsal sinus), funnel- form; limb scarcely bilabiate, all the lobes falcate-triangular, curved to the ventral side, acute, the dorsal pair largest, 0.6-1 mm wide at the base, 1.2-2 (-2.5) mm long; lateral and ventral lobes similar, 1.1-1.5 mm long; stamens included; filament-tube 1-2 (-2.6) mm long, attached to the corolla at the base; anther-tube incurved, 1-1.5 mm long, the short anthers with appendages 0.2-0.3 mm long; ovary unilocular, campanulate, often hardly thicker than the pedicel at anthesis, at maturity often oblique, concave on the ventral side and gibbous on the dorsal, (1-) 1.5-2.5 mm in diameter, 1.5-4.5 mm long, attenuate at the base, membranous except for the 5 prominent angles formed by the vascular strands which are somewhat decurrent on the pedicels; calyx-lobes entire, broad, very unequal, the dorsal usually surpassing the dorsal sinus of the corolla, 1-3 (-5.5) mm long and 1-1.5 (-2.5) mm wide, oblong or narrowly triangular; lateral and ventral lobes successively shorter, the ventral rounded or deltoid, 0.4-1.5 (-2.5) mm long and about as wide; ovules 15-?30, attached to the ventral wall of the ovary in about two rows; seeds oblong-ellipsoid, brown, 0.6-1 mm long, with irregular longitudinal furrows and nearly smooth surface with very indistinct cross-lines.

description: Rosette shrub, apparently polycarpic; stems 0.2-0.5 m tall, 0.6-1.4 cm diam. at apex, ca. 3 cm diam. at base, forking near the middle into few or several major branches, yellowish green to brown, hollow, with numerous trapezoidal leaf-scars, gla- brous; latex milky. Leaves numerous, helically arranged, forming a dense globose or oblate rosette at the apex of the stem, gla- brous; lamina 7-1 1 cm long, 1.5-3 cm wide, oblanceolate, frequently revolute, coria- ceous; dorsal surface dark green, shining; ventral surface yellowish green, dull; margin callose-serrate with 15-24 straight or incurved teeth per side, the teeth 1-3 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide, 3-5.5 mm apart; apex cuspidate; base attenuate, narrowing imperceptibly into the winged petiole; petiole 0.8-1 cm long, shortly decurrent on the stem. Flowers 20-30 in an erect terminal raceme, but only 2-3 in full anthesis at any one time; peduncle 9-11 cm long, 0.5-0.6 cm diam., glabrous; rachis 13-50 cm long, glabrous toward the base, villous toward the apex; bracts 18-32 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, linear, subtending the pedicels and adnate to them basally, villous, the margin entire, the apex acuminate; pedicels 20-40 mm long, 0.8-1.6 mm diam., ascending, curved slightly just below the apex during anthesis making the flower nearly parallel to the rachis, afterward more strongly curved so that the spent flower is perpendicular to the rachis, bibracteolate at the curve, vil- lous; bracteoles 3-9 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm wide, linear or linear triangular, subopposite, villous, the apex acuminate. Hypanthium 7-8 mm long, 8-10.5 mm diam., very widely obovoid or widely depressed obovoid, villous. Calyx lobes 3-6 mm long, 3-4.5 mm wide, triangular, widely deltate or deltate, erect, villous, the margin entire, the apex acuminate. Corolla 20 mm long, pale green or yellowish, unilabiate, villous externally; tube 4-5 mm long, 5-5.5 mm diam. at base; dorsal lobes 15-16 mm long, 1.3-1.7 mm wide, linear, downcurved, the apex acute; ventral lobes connate into a shortly trifid downcurved lip 10-12 mm long and 4.5 mm wide at apex. Staminal column exserted, erect, positioned between the dor- sal corolla lobes; filament tube 14 mm long, 1-1.2 mm diam., glabrous; anther tube 6- 6.5 mm long, 2.2-2.8 mm diam., very slightly downcurved, all five anthers densely white bearded at apex, otherwise glabrous. Mature fruit and seeds not seen.

description: Perennial soboliferous herbs 15-25 cm tall. Stems decumbent, usually simple, pilose, green. Leaves cauline; petiole 10-12 mm long on lower leaves, much reduced distally, green, hispid; blade suborbicular, more ovate to cordate above, 15-40 mm long, 18-30 mm wide, cordate at base, acute at tip, the margins appearing entire to minutely dentate on lowest leaves becoming dentate above, green and pilose throughout. Inflorescence of secund (?) racemes, the peduncle 3.5-6 cm long; bracts subulate, entire, 3.5-4 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, glabrate; pedicels 3-4.5 cm long with the lowest pedicels much elongated presenting flowers at the same level as terminal flowers (?), glabrous; bracteoles absent. Flowers ca 1 cm long (measured from base of spur to tip of anthers); hypanthium asymmetrical, upper side 3-3.5 mm long, lower side extending with corolla tissue into spur; spur conical-cylindrical, ca 8 mm long (measured from the base of the upper calyx lobes), extending 5.5-7 mm below ovary; calyx lobes subulate, 4-4.5 mm long, green, often purple-tipped (?), the 2 lower ones slightly shorter, positioned ca 1 mm above base of spur; corolla pink to pinkish-purple (?), the tube 5-5.5 mm long, slit dorsally to base, the upper lobes subulate, 5-6 mm long, 1.8-2 mm wide, reflexed, the lower lobes obovate, 4-5 mm long, 3.5-4 mm wide, apiculate, with 2 small green circular spots opposed to lobe sinuses at throat (?); stamens 6.5-7 mm long, the filaments white, connate in the distal half, the anthers 1.5-2 mm long, blue, pilose in lines on sutures, the 2 shorter anthers with subulate trichomes at tip. Fruit and seeds unknown.

description: Perennial, glabrous, the leaves 20-60 in stiff rosettes from a short, branched, woody caudex covered by persistent, imbricated leaf-bases; leaves thick, lustrous, opaque, 15-20 mm long, the blade proper narrowly elliptic, 2-3 mm wide and about 1 cm long, blunt-pointed, narrowed gradually to the base and then slightly widened again to the flat, margined attachment of the leaf; margins with 1-5 rounded glands on each edge near the tip of the blade, the glands with a depressed center when dry; lower surface of the blade sharply keeled and with prominent stomatal openings, the upper surface with a deep central longitudinal furrow bordered on each side by a pale rounded ridge parallel to it (furrow and ridges together occupying about one-third the width of the entire blade); flowers slightly exceeding the leaves, white, about 2 cm long; pedicel less than 1 cm long; corolla-.tube 11-12 mm long (10 mm at the dorsal sinus), straight, the basal portion cylindric, very slender (about 0.5 mm in diameter), 7-8 mm long, rather abruptly expanded at the summit into a narrowly campanulate throat 4-4.5 mm long and 2.5 mm thick; limb bilabiate, the dorsal lobes lanceolate, recurved, 1.5 mm wide, 5-6 mm long, the ventral lobes lance-ovate, 2.3-2.5 mm wide, 4.5 mm long, somewhat united and forming a distinct deflexed lip; filament-tube somewhat exserted (from the dorsal sinus), 12 mm long, free from the corollain the throat only; anther-tube apparently black, somewhat incurved, 2 mm long, each of the short anthers tipped by a few bristles and by a sharply pointed, narrowly triangular, hyaline process 0.8 mm long; hypanthium at anthesis hardly thicker than the pedicel, angled when dry, about 3 mm long, not seen in fruit; ovary imperfectly bilocular, the ovules about 100, attached on both sides of the flattened placenta which is connected to both sides of the base of the ovary by delicate membranes; calyx-lobes entire, linear-lanceolate, about 0.9 mm wide, bluntly pointed and gland-tipped, appressed in flower, slightly unequal (the dorsal 5 mm long, the lateral pair 4.5 mm, the ventral pair 4.1 mm).

description: Flowers white (Espinosa), not surpassing the leaves, on pedicels 2-2.5 mm long, these connate more than half their length with the ventral surface of the subtending leaf; corolla-tube broad and straight, 1.2 mm long (0.5 mm long at the dorsal sinus); hypanthium at maturity campanulate, about 1.3 mm thick and 2.5 mm long, unilocular, the ovules about 10?, attached along the linear placenta which extends nearly the length of the ventral side of the ovary; seeds ellipsoid ovoid, 0.8-1 mm long, brown, cellular-reticulate longitudinally and sometimes cross-striate.

description: Small upright, glabrous plants 1-4 cm high, with numerous thickly imbricated, appressed small leaves, the whole compared by Goebel to Lycopodium selago; plants probably perennial, somewhat fleshy, from a short, upright, fleshy crown, the base of the stem marked with old leaf-scars and bearing numerous slender roots below this; leaves very numerous, entire, appressed, triangular-lanceolate, sessile, rounded on the backs, 1-1.5 mm wide, 3-4.5 mm long, tapering to a blunt or rounded tip which bears a single glandular callosity; branches, with the leaves, 7-10 mm thick; leaf-surfaces hard and glossy, the veins not apparent; flowers in the up per axils, whitish (Goebel), or yellow (Hanbury.Tracy), inconspicuous, sessiile, the tips of the corolla lobes and the tips of the fruiting calyx-lobes barely surpassing the leaves; corolla glabrous, 2-2.5 mm long, the tube straight and broad, about 1.2 mm long to the lateral sinuses and 0.6-0.8 mm to the dorsal; lobes shorter than the tube, acute, apparently all somewhat decurved and the tips cucullate, the dorsal pair longest, up to 0.6 mm wide and 0.8 mm long; filaments about 0.8 mm long, attached to the corolla at the very base; anther-tube somewhat incurved, about 0.8 mm long, appendaged; hypanthium unilocular, flattened dorsally, in fruit about 1 mm thick, 2 mm wide, 2.5-3 mm long, elliptic in outline; ovules about 20, attached above the middle of the ovary on the ventral side; calyx-lobes large for the flower, entire, broadly ovate, acute (evidently broader than, and the distal half more nearly deltoid than, the corresponding parts of the surrounding leaves), up to 1.2 mm wide at the base, the dorsal one largest, 1.441.6 mm long, the lateral pair 1.1-1.4 mm long, the ventral pair 1-1.1 mm; seeds ovoid-ellipsoid, 0.7-0.8 mm long, brown, the surface essentially smooth and without angles but with minute cellular markings.

description: Small creeping glabrous plants, from short branched woody rootstocks 1-2 mm in diameter, up to 5 cm long, the lower parts covered with persistent scattered leaf-bases; leaves in clusters of 10-20 near the tips of the branches, long petiolate, the elliptic blades blunt-pointed or rounded, with a callose tip, the upper surface sometimes with a few bristles near the tip; base of the blade attenuate to the margined petiole which is slightly dilated at the attachment to the stem; flowers few, sessile, large for the plant; corolla white or marked with violet dots; limb bilabiate, the dorsal lobes longest, upright or the tips recurved, the ventral lobes somewhat recurved and united; lobes all acute; anther-tube black, incurved, the short anthers bristly and also cornute at the tips; hypanthium unilocular, much enlarging in fruit, becoming oblate, hard and strongly ribbed, about 2.5 mm in diameter and 2 mm high, with a shallowly convex operculum about 1.5 mm in diameter; calyx-lobes unequal.

description: A densely tufted, completely glabrous perennial from short, branched root. stocks 2-2.5 mm in diameter, up to 5 cm long and covered by persistent leafbases; leaves in somewhat one-sided tufts especially near the tips of the branches, linear, 0.7-1 mm wide, 6-10 mm long, with blunt, callose tips and the margins entire or obscurely sinuate, with 1-5 glandular callosities on each edge; flowers 1-3 in each terminal tuft of leaves, erect on ascending pedicels about 4 mm long; corolla white with elongate, deep purple dots in the throat (Camp), 7-8 mm long, the tube broadly cylindric, enlarged a little toward the apex, 3-3.5 mm long (2 mm to the dorsal sinus); limb strongly bilabiate, the dorsal lobes about 1.2 mm wide, 4 mm long, lanceolate, the tips recurved; ventral lobes united into a lip, lance-ovate, 1.3 mm wide and the lip divided 3.5 mm; filament-tube 5 mm long, adnate to the very base of the corolla only; anther-tube purple-nigrescent (Camp), incurved, about 2 mm long, the short anthers cornute and also bristly at the apex; hypanthium not seen in fruit; calyx-lobes 0.6-0.8 mm wide at the base, nearly linear but narrowed slightly to a blunt tip, entire or with one tooth near the middle, slightly unequal (the dorsal 2.5-2.7 mm long, the lateral and ventral 2.3-2.5 mm long); sinuses very narrow, acute, with a small ellipsoid swelling below each one; ovary unilocular, the ovules about 50; seeds not seen.

description: Perennial soboliferous herbs 15-20 cm tall. Stems decumbent, usually simple, velutinous. Leaves cauline; petiole 3-8 mm long on lower leaves, much reduced distally, green, hispid; blade narrowly ovate, more lanceolate above, 15-30 mm long, 18-25 mm wide, cordate at base, acute at tip, the margins deeply dentate usually with 3 teeth, green and pilose throughout. Inflorescence of secund racemes, the peduncle 5-7 cm long; bracts somewhat foliaceous and lanceolate proximally becoming subulate distally, sharply dentate, 5.5-8.5 mm long, ca 3 mm wide, ciliate; pedicels 4-4.5 cm long, glabrous; bracteoles absent. Flowers 1-1.2 cm long (measured from base of spur to tip of anthers); hypanthium asymmetrical, upper side 2.5-3 mm long, lower side extending with corolla tissue into spur; spur conical-cylindrical, 8.5-10 mm long (measured from the base of the upper calyx lobes), extending 5.5-7 mm below ovary; calyx lobes subulate, 4.2-4.8 mm long, green, often purple-tipped, the 2 lower ones slightly shorter, positioned 0.3-0.5 mm above base of spur; corolla pink to pinkish-purple, the tube 5-5.5 mm long, slit dorsally to base, the upper lobes broadly spatulate, 8.5-9 mm long, 4-4.5 mm wide, erect and spreading, the lower lobes obovate, 11-12 mm long, 6-7 mm wide, apiculate, with 2 small green circular spots opposed to lobe sinuses at throat; stamens 5-5.5 mm long, the filaments white, connate in the distal half, the anthers 1. 5-2 mm long, blue, pilose in lines on sutures, the 2 shorter anthers with subulate trichomes at tip. Fruit and seeds unknown.

description: Herbaceous perennial herbs (1) 4-6 cm tall. Stems procumbent, rooting at nodes, green suffused with purple, puberulent. Leaves cauline; petiole 1-4 mm long, green, pilose; blade orbiculate to widely ovate, 3-6 (8) mm long, 3-6 mm wide, cordate at base, rounded or obtuse at tip, the margins entire to shallowly dentate, pilose with slender white trichomes throughout, green above, purple beneath and along margins. Inflorescence of solitary flowers borne on ascending, purple, glabrous, rarely pilose pedicels (1) 3-6 cm long, these produced terminal to axillary branch- lets or in the axils of primary stem leaves; bracteoles absent. Flowers ca 1 cm long (including hypanthium); hypanthium asymmetrical, upper side 3-4.5 mm long, the lower side extending with corolla tissue into spur; spur conic, 5-7 (8) mm long (measured from base of the upper calyx lobes), extending 2-3 (4) mm below ovary; calyx lobes subulate, 2.5-2.8 mm long, the 2 lower ones slightly shorter, spreading, positioned 0.2-0.3 mm above base of spur; corolla pink to pinkish- purple, the tube white, 5-6 mm long, slit dorsally to base, the upper lobes spatulate, 2.5-3.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, strongly reflexed from tube, the lower lobes obovate, narrowly divergent, 4.5-6 mm long, 2.8-3.5 mm wide, apiculate, with 2 small circular green spots opposed to sinuses at throat; stamens 6-7 mm long, the filaments white, connate in the distal half, the anthers ca 1.5 mm long, blue, pubescent in lines on sutures, the 2 shorter anthers with subulate trichomes at tip. Fruit 5-6 mm long, 2.5-3 mm wide. Seeds ellipsoid, dark brown, ca 0.5 mm long, testa sculpturing sulcate, appearing faintly lined to the naked eye.

description: Perennial soboliferous herbs 3-8 (12) cm tall. Stems decumbent, usually simple aboveground, pilose below, glabrate above, purple. Leaves cauline; petiole 5-15 mm long, much reduced above, purple, pilose; blade ovate to broadly lanceolate, 15-20 mm long, 10-15 mm wide, truncate to cordate at base, acute or rounded at tip, the margins appearing entire in lowest leaves, but becoming shallowly to deeply dentate in the upper ones, often ciliate, pilose on both surfaces, trichomes white, appressed, mainly associated with veins on abaxial surface, green above, purple beneath or purple throughout. Inflorescence of bracteate racemes; bracts foliaceous, lanceolate, 6-9 (15) mm long, 2-6 mm wide, sharply dentate; pedicels 2-3 (4.5) cm long, the lowest much elongated, elevating their flowers to the level of terminal ones, glabrous; bracteoles absent. Flowers 0.7-1 cm long (including hypanthium); hypanthium asymmetrical, upper side 3-4 mm long, lower side extending with corolla tissue into spur; spur conical-cylindrical, 3-4 mm long (measured from the base of the upper calyx lobes); calyx lobes subulate, 3-4 (5) mm long, green, often purple-tipped the two lower ones slightly shorter, positioned at base of spur, which is even with base of ovary; corolla pink to pinkish-purple, veins more deeply pigmented, the tube 5-5.5 (6.5) mm long, slit dorsally to base, the upper lobes spatulate, 5-7 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, erect, slightly spreading, the lower lobes broadly obovate, 5-7 (9) mm long, 3-3.5 (6) mm wide, apiculate at tip, with 2 broad green triangular patches opposed to sinuses at throat; stamens 6-7 mm long, the filaments pink above, white below, connate in the distal half, the anthers ca 2 mm long, blue, pubescent in lines on sutures, the 2 shorter anthers with subulate trichomes at tip. Fruit 4-6 mm long, 3 mm wide. Seeds ellipsoid, dark brown, ca 0.5 mm long, testa sculpturing sulcate, appearing faintly lined to the naked eye.

description: Prostrate, glabrous perennial with long, procumbent, much-branched stem, rooting freely at nodes. Leaves dense, erect, secund, subsessile, narrowly elliptic, 4-10 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, apex acute, gland- tipped, margins thin, appearing entire or denticulate with 3-7 pairs of linear, red glands on adaxial surface appressed to margin or curved toward midvein, the blade narrowing slightly to base. Flowers pseudo- resupinate; pedicel 6-16 mm long; hypanthium narrowly obconic; calyx lobes broadly triangular, imbricate, ca. 3 mm long, apex apiculate, margins dentate with 2-3 pairs of glands crowded near base; corolla pink purple with purple-blue elongate spots at throat, tube funnelform, 5-6 mm long to lateral sinus, limb bilabiate, the lips presented vertically facing the stem apex, the upper (dorsal) lobes lanceolate, ca. 6 mm long, reflexed at tips, ciliate, the lower (ventral) lobes lanceovate, 6-7 mm long, deflexed, glabrous; filament tube equal to or slightly longer than corolla tube, anther tube blue-black, ca. 2 mm long, slightly exserted from corolla, the 2 shorter anthers with a few short linear trichomes and 1 triangular trichome ca. 0.5 mm long at apex; ovary turbinate, unilocular, placentation parietal, ovules crowded onto an intruded placenta on the ventral surface. Fruit turbinate, ca. 3 mm long and wide. Seeds ovoid, light brown, narrowing slightly to the prominent circular hilum. Chromosome number unknown. Endemic.

description:
Procumbent or decumbent, glabrous perennial with thin, branching rhizomes that form dense cushions; stems thin, dichotomously branched, with elongate internodes and minute, persistent leaf bases. Leaves in dense rosettes at the ends of the branches, with a distal elliptical lamina, 5-6 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, slightly keeled, apex acute, gland-tipped, margins thickened, glassy, minutely crenate with 2-3 pairs of spherical glands on margin at crenations, the blade attenuate into a petiole shorter than the blade, base not broadened and sheath-like. Flowers pseudo-resupinate; pedicel ca. '-1 mm long or less; hypanthi- um (and ovary) short-cylindrical, 2.5-3 mm long, minutely winged at ribs when dry; calyx lobes narrowly triangular, equal, ca. 2.5 mm long, apex acute, margins entire with a single gland at the apex; corolla white with purple-blue elongate spots at throat, tube 11-12 mm long to the lateral sinus, the basal portion cylindrical, ca. 7 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, abruptly expanded at the summit into a narrowly campanulate throat, ca. 4 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, limb bilabiate, the lips presented vertically facing the stem apex, the upper (dorsal) lobes lanceolate, ca. 4 mm long, reflexed at tips, the lower (ventral) lobes lance ovate, 4-5 mm long, deflexed; filament tube equal to corolla tube, anther tube blue-black, ca. 1.2 mm long, slightly exserted from corolla, the 2 shorter anthers with a few short linear trichomes and 1 triangular trichome ca. 0.5 mm long at apex; ovary short-cylindrical, unilocular, placentation parietal, ovules attached in 2 rows on the ventral surface. Fruit short cylindrical, ribbed when dry, 3-4 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide. Seeds ovoid, light brown, narrowing slightly to the prominent circular hilum. Chromosome number unknown. Endemic.

Lysipomia caespitosa is known only from the type collection in wet paramo at 3000-3400 m. The epithet refers the growth habit, and although that term has been used to describe the genus generally (McVaugh, 1955; Wimmer, 1953), this species is the only one known to date that forms dense cushions (Ayers, unpubl.). It resembles L. laricina E. Wimm. in its long corolla tube that is cylindrical at the base, but L. caespitosa can be easily distinguished from that species by its elliptic leaves (vs. linear in L. laricina), similar in shape to the leaves of L. bilineata McVaugh and L. cylindrocarpa. The habit of L. caespitosa differs markedly from all other species in southern Ecuador in its lack of fleshy rhizomes or above-ground stems that are covered with persistent imbricate leaf bases.

description: Erect, glabrous perennial with a thickened, dichotomously branched, woody stem covered by persistent, imbricated leaf bases. Leaves in dense rosettes at the ends of the branches, with a distal elliptical lamina, 10-20 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, keeled at visible midvein below, apex acute, sparsely ciliate and gland-tipped, margins thickened, glassy, minutely crenate with 3-5 pairs of spherical glands on adaxial surface at crenations, the blade attenuate into a petiole about as long as the blade, the base broadened and sheath-like, long persistent with a portion of the petiole up to 5 mm long. Flowers pseudo-resupinate; pedicel 2-4 mm long; hypanthium (and ovary) cylindrical, pedicel-like; calyx lobes narrowly triangular, subequal, decreasing in length from dorsal to ventrals, 3-4.5 mm long, apex acute, margins entire with a single gland at the adaxial apex and an elongate gland just below lobe sinuses; corolla white with purple-blue elongate spots at throat, tube funnelform, 4-7 mm long to lateral si- nus, limb bilabiate, the lips presented horizontally or vertically facing the stem apex, the upper (dorsal) lobes lanceolate, ca. 6 mm long, reflexed at tips, lower (ventral) lobes lance-ovate, 6-7 mm long, deflexed; filament tube equal to corolla tube, anther tube blue-black, ca. 2 mm long, slightly exserted from corolla, the 2 shorter anthers with a few short linear trichomes and 1 triangular trichome ca. 0.5 mm long at apex; ovary obscure, appearing as a pedicel, uni- locular, placentation parietal, ovules attached in 2 rows on the ventral surface. Fruit cylindrical, ribbed when dry, 15-40 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, long-persistent, especially the veins. Seeds ovoid, light brown, narrowing slightly to the prominent circular hilum. Chromosome number unknown. Endemic.

description: Frutex 3 m alta, ramulis juvenilibus sparse puberulis mox glabrescentibus. Folia alterna, petiolata; petiolo 1-3 mm longo, circa 1.5 mm lato, lanato-glabrescenti, rugoso; laminae ellipticae vel oblongo-ellipticae, coriaceae, 3-6 cm longae, 1.4-3 cm latae, apice rotundatae vel acutae, sed emarginatae, basi subcuneatae, utrinque glabrae; nervis secundariis 5-7-jugis, utrinque prominulis. Stipulae lanceolatae, 1-2 mm longae, glabrescentes, caducae. Flores in paniculis cymularu 3-4 mm longis dispositi; rachi ramisque sparse puberulis. Bracteae bracteolaeque ovatae, 1-1.5 mm longae, persistentes, chartaceae, utrinque puberulae. Recep- taculum campanulatum, leviter asymmetricum, extus griseo-tomentellum, intus tomentosum; pedicelli circa 1 mm longi. Calycis lobi 5, acuti, extus tomentelli, intus puberuli. Petala 5, extus puberula. Stamina 7, in orbem completum inserta; filamenta calycis lobis breviora. Ovarium ad basim receptaculi insertum, lanato-pilosum, uniloculare. Stylus e basi ovarii ortus, praeter basim glaber. Drupa (immatura) ellipsoidea; exocarpio laevi, glabro; mesocarpio tenue, carnoso; endocarpio tenue, duro, osseo, intus tomentoso, longitudinaliter aperienti.

description: Arbor ad 25 m alta, ramulis juvenilibus sparse tomentellis mox glabris lenticellatus. Stipulae caducae (non visae). Flores 4-5 mm longi, in paniculis racemosis terminalibus subterminalibusque 8-12 cm longis dispositi, rachi ramisque ferrugineo-tomentosis. Bracteae bracteolaeque membranaceae, caducae, extus tomentosae intus sparse pubescentes. Re- ceptaculum globosum, sessile, extus ferrugineo-tomentosum, intus tomentosum, prope faucem pilis longis deflexis ornatum. Calycis lobi 5, acuti, triangulares, extus ferrugineo-tomentosi intus brunneo-tomentelli. Petala 5, extus tomentella, intus versus apicem tomentella versus basim glabra, marginibus ciliatis. Stamina 30-35, in orbem completum disposita; filamentis exsertis ad basim liberis. Ovarium ad basim receptaculi insertum, lanatum. Stylus e basi ovarii ortus, lanato-pilosus, filamenta aequans. Fructus ignotus.

description: Tree to 12 m tall, the young branches sparsely-puberulous soon becoming glabrous and conspicuously lenticellate. Leaves with laminas oblong-elliptic, subcoriaceous, 5-8.5 cm long, 2.8-3.8 cm broad, acuminate at apex, the acumen 5-6 mm long, subcuneate at base, glabrous; midrib prominulous above, prominent beneath; primary veins 8-11 pairs, prominulous above, prominent beneath; petioles 9-14 mm long, glabrous, terete, eglandular, with very distinct articulation at junction with branch. Stipules caducous (not seen). Inflorescences (not fully developed in specimen examined) of terminal and axillary panicles, the rachis and branches yellow-brown tomentellous. Bracts and bracteoles triangular, caducous, puberulous on exterior. Receptacle broadly campanulate, tomentellous on exterior, hirsute within; pedicels ca. 0.5 mm long. Calyx lobes 5, acute, tomentellous on exterior, puberulous within. Petals 5, glabrous with ciliate margin. Stamens 13-15, inserted around a complete circle; filaments slightly exserted, free to base. Ovary inserted at base of receptacle, glabrous or with only a few hispid hairs. Style sparsely hirsute. Fruit not seen.

description: Shrub, 3-7 m. tall, very robust; "stems jointed like bamboo"; wood soft, white, brittle; branches exceedingly stout and robust, terete, to 1.5 cm. in diameter, hollow in the center, light gray, gla- brous; branchlets obtusely tetragonal, deeply canaliculate toward the apex, grayish-brown, glabrous or minutely puberulent, somewhat ampliate at the nodes, stout; buds minute; internodes very variable, 2-7.5 cm. long; leaves decussate; petioles slender or stoutish, 3-10 cm. long, glabrous; blades chartaceous, rather dark green and nitid on both surfaces, oblong to elliptic, often extremely large, 16-35 cm. long, 9-23 cm. wide, slightly acuminate at apex, entire, broadly acute or slightly acuminate at base, very minutely puberulent on both surfaces, becoming glabrous; midrib stout, prominent beneath; secondaries about 10 pairs, ascending, very prominent beneath; veinlets rather few, slender; inflorescence axillary, sessile; cymes numerous at the nodes of the branches of 1 or 2 years back, dense, glomerate or fascicu- late, many-flowered; flowers very odorous; pedicels slender, 1-2 mm. long, puberulent; bractlets small, linear, puberulent, inconspicuous; calyx campanulate, herbaceous, about 3.5 mm. long and wide, glabrate or minutely pubescent, lax around the corolla-tube, its rim mem- branous, subtruncate or shallowly repand, scarious; corolla infundibu- lar, white, its tube slender, cylindric, about 10.5 mm. long, somewhat ampliate above, glabrous or minutely puberulent, its lobes 4, broadly ovate-lingulate, about 3.7 mm. long and 3.8 mm. wide at base, abruptly rounded at apex; stamens 4, inserted about 3.7 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, somewhat exserted (in 9 ) or long-exserted (in & ); filaments filiform, 5-11 mm. long, glabrous; anthers ovate, about 1.3 mm. long and 0.8 mm. wide; pistil included (in & ) or long- exserted (in 9 ); style capillary, 5-15 mm. long, glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches slender, 3.7-6 mm. long, papillose; ovary dark, subglobose, flattened and umbilicate at apex, about 0.8 mm. long and wide, glabrous, 4-celled; fruiting-calyx cupuliform, greatly enlarged and indurated, verrucose; fruit subglobose or oblong, 6-7 mm. long and wide, green, flattened and umbilicate at both ends, glabrous, up to semi-included by the mature calyx.

description: Tree; branches and branchlets slender, obtusely tetragonal or subterete, densely fulvous-pubeseent; internodes 3.5-8 cm. long; leaves decussate; petioles slender, weak, about 7 mm. long, densely fulvouspubescent; blades chartaceous, deep green on both surfaces, oblong, 9-12 cm. long, 4-4.5 cm. wide, acumninate at apex, entire, acute at base, fulvous-pubeseent and roughened above, very densely fulvous-pubescent beneath; midrib rather slender, prominent at base beneath; secondaries 6-8 pairs, very slender and delicate; veinlets inconspicuous or hidden; inflorescence axillary and apparently terminal; eyines solitary, opposite, apparently 2-6-flowered, very loose and lax, brachiate, bracteolate; terminal panicle precisely like an axillary eyme in size and shape, standing at the termination of the branchlet, about 5 Cm. long and wide, very loosely few-flowered; peduncles [in fruit] slender, very weak and tortuous, 1-3 cm. long, densely fulvous-pubescent; pedicels [in fruit] thick, about 1 cm. long, weak, densely fulvouspubescent; bractlets and prophylla few, subulate, about 2 mm. long; flowers not seen; fruiting-calyx cupuliform, indurated, about 10 mm. long and 15 mm. wide, veiny, dark toward the rim, lighter at base, densely fulvous-pubeseent, its rim subtruneate, entire or somewhat repand; fruit oblong, about 13 mm. long and 10 mm. wide, flattened and umbilicate at apex, "yellow," glabrous, 3- or 4-seeded.

description: Arbor mediocris ramis tenninalibus puberulis vel parce araneosis demum glabris brunnescens vel griseis. Folia simplicia alterna tenuiter coriacea. Petiolus 3-4 mm longus crassus subteres pubescens. Lamina elliptico-acuminata vel lanceolato-elliptica basi obtusa vel subrotundata vel obtuse cuneata apice attenuata acuta vel breviter cuspidata, margine integerrima 3.5-8 cm longa 1.4-3 cm lata; supra in sicco brunneo-pallida glabra nitida costa prominula reliquis nervis subimmersis paulo conspicuis; subtus subochraceo-cinerea minutissime lanuginoso-tomentella indumento valde adpresso costa eminenti nervis secundariis tenuibus prominenti- bus 9-10 utroque latere subpatulis prope marginem arcuato-ascendentibus anasto- mosantibus, venulis minoribus prominulis reticulatis. Stipulae anguste subulatae 5-6 mm longae deciduae. Inflorescentiae subterminales thyrsoideo-paniculatae ad 8 cm longae et latae axi ramisque robustiusculis tomentello-pubescentibus, bracteolis ovato-acuminatis 141.5 mm longis acutissimis extus pubescentibus. Flores sessiles 3-7 in extremo ramusculorum 2-5 mm longorum glomerati. Hypanthium campanulatum 1.8 altum extus tomentosum intus longe alboque hirsuto-sericeum. Sepala triangularia acuta 1.2 mm longa tomentella. Petala nulla. Stamina 8 filamento rubro glabro 3 mm longo, anthera rotundata 0.6 mm ampla. Ovarium globosum subnitidum rubellum basi setosum ceterum sparsis setis munitum. Stylus basilaris 4 mm longus ruber dimidia parte inferiori longe setosa.

description: Arbor mediocris; ramulis tenuibus teretis glabris conspicue lenticellatis; foliis parvis, petiolis 812 mm. longis, dense brevivillosis, demum subglabres- centibus transverse rimosis, eglandularibus vel inconspicue biglandularibus, infra glandibus pilisque obscuris; laminis orbicularibus vel oblongis (4) 5-6 cm. longis 3.0-5.5 cm. latis apiculatis, supra glabris costa nervisque lateralibus impressis, subtus pallido-brunneis tomentosis costa et 6-8 jugis nervis lateralibus rufo-brunneis prominentibus; inflorescentia paniculata terminalis vel axillaris 8-16 cm. longa pallido-fulvo-brevipilosa, ramis patentibus maximis 6 cm. longis; floribus numerosis in cymis subsessilibus vel pedunculatis 1-2 mm. longis; bracteis late lanceolatis caducis, bracteolis anguste lanceolatis acuminatis 2-4 mm. longis; hypanthiis campanulatis sessilibus 5-6 mm. longis, lobis 2.0- 2.5 mm. longis, triangulari-lanceolatis acutis, extus viridi-sericeis, intus dense deflexo-longivillosis; petalis 5 cuneato-oblanceolatis 2-3 mm. longis marginibus sparse lanato-puberulentibus; staminibus ca. 30, filamentis 10-2.5 mm. longis, in coronis membraneis 1 mm. altis dispositis indistincte in phalangibus dispositis; ovario uniloculari biovulato ad medium tubum affixo; ovulis glabris compressis; stylis 4-5 mm. longis basi dense longi-pilosa; fructibus non visis.

description: Tree 14 m tall (fide Cabrera), the young branches glabrescent. Leaves oblong- lanceolate to oblong-elliptic, coriaceous, 12-18 cm long, 3-6 cm broad shortly and abruptly acuminate at apex, the acumen 2-10 mm long, rounded at base with a closely appressed waxy pubescence beneath, glabrous above, the lower surface with conspicuous and frequent palisade glands; midrib prominent on both surfaces, glabrous above, sparsely appressed pubescent beneath; primary veins 12-16 pairs plane to prominulous above, prominent beneath; petioles 4-8 mm long, glabrous, scaly, terete, eglandular. Stipules not seen. Inflorescences of terminal and axillary racemose panicles, the rachis and branches ferrugineous-arachnoid pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles 0.5-1.5 mm long, linear, membraneous, tomentellous on exterior, glabrous within. Flowers 2-3 mm long borne sessile on primary and secondary inflorescence branches. Receptacle globose, sessile, ferrugineous tomentose on exterior, tomentose within, with a ring of pilose deflexed hairs around mouth below stamens. Calyx lobes 5, arachnoid pubescent on exterior, almost glabrous within, acute. Stamens ca. 32, inserted in a complete circle, the filaments slightly exserted beyond calyx lobes, free almost to base, glabrous. Ovary inserted on base of receptacle, lanate-pilose. Style equalling filaments, lanate-pilose throughout. Fruit unknown.

description: Tree with young stems moderately pilose; leaves petiolate, petioles 1-1.5 cm long, moderately pilose, the blades elliptic-oblong, acute or obtuse at apex, subacute or obtuse at base, 6.5-12 cm long, 2.5-5 cm wide, upper surface sparsely pubescent, pilose on the midnerve, more densely and laxly pubescent beneath along midrib and base of the secondary nerves, these divaricate-ascending, 11-15 each side; inflorescence axillary, trichotomously cymose, pedunculate, the floriferous portion 3-4 cm long, 3-3.5 cm wide, the ultimate branches 3-flowered, densely pilose, the peduncle 1.5-4 cm long and densely pilosulous in anthesis, 4-6 cm long and glabrescent in fruit, the pedicels clavate, 1-2 mm long, pilosulous, the bracts lanceolate or spathulate, subacute or rounded at apex, 2 mm long, 1 mm wide, pilosulous; calyx lobes slightly unequal, ovate, acute, 1 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, densely pilosulous; petals slightly connate at base, linear-subulate, acute, 9-11 mm long, 0.6-0.7 mm wide, glabrous, margins subinvolute; stamens: the anthers ovate-oblong, rounded at apex, obtuse at base, 1.5 mm long, 0.8 mm wide, the filaments 0.4 mm long, 0.4 mm wide; pistil 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous; drupe ovoid-oblong, subacute or obtusely acute at apex, obtusely narrowed at base, 1.9-2.1 cm long, 1.1-1.2 cm broad.

description: Tall shrub or tree, to 7 m. tall; stems erect, medullose, branching, subeinereous; wood very durable; branches stout, tetragonal, com- pressed and ampliate at the nodes, rather sparsely and unevenly short- hirsute, becoming merely granulose-tomentose at the nodes; branchlets stoutish, subterete, softly purplish-tomentose or hirsute, becoming merely granulose-tomentose; internodes 5-30 mm. long, extremely abbreviated on some short lateral twigs; leaf-scars, even on the smaller twigs, large and elevated, with a much-thickened margin; leaves decus- sate; petioles very slender, 5-12 mm. long, purple, granulose-tomentose when young, becoming merely strigillose or glabrate; blades char- taceous, dark green above, much lighter beneath, ovate-lanceolate or ovate to oblong-ovate, 6.2-11 cmn. long, 3-5.8 cm. wide, abruptly acute or rounded at apex, entire, cuneate at base and attenuate into the petiole, glabrate above, sublanate-villose or lanuginous-pubescent be- neath, especially on the midrib, secondaries, and veinlet reticulation; midrib slender, slightly prominent beneath; secondaries about 6 pairs, slender, prominent beneath, arcuate-ascending, not conspicuously anastomosing; veinlets slender, prominent beneath; inflorescence axil- lary; cymes in the axils of the leaves or at the nodes of the preceding year, solitary, opposite, densely many-flowered, often congested and compact, sometimes 2-3-fid; peduncles obsolete or to 3 mm. long and granulose-tomentose; pedicels obsolete or 1-3 mm. long and canescent- tomentose; bractlets minute; calyx campanulate or turbinate, 3.6-6.2 mm. long, 4-6 mm. wide, very densely purple-pubescent or tomentose, becoming rather lax around the corolla-tube, its rim 4-toothed, its teeth short and very broad at base; corolla infundibular or hypocra- teriform, red-purple, its tube cylindric, about 13 mm. long, very ampliate above, pulverulent outside, glabrous within, its lobes 4, ovate-lingulate, erect or reflexed, about 5.2 mm. long and 3.6 mm. wide, obtuse at apex, pulverulent outside; stamens 4, inserted about 2 mm. below the mouth of the corolla-tube, included (in 9 ); fila- ments filiform, about 0.5 mm. long (in 9 ), glabrate; anthers oblong, about 1 mm. long and 0.5 mm. wide; pistil exserted (in 9 ); style capillary, about 15 mm. long (in 9 ), glabrous; stigma bifid, its branches about 3.1 mm. long; ovary subglabrous, dark, about 1 mm. long and wide, glabrous, 4-celled; fruiting-calyx enlarged and in- durated, shallowly patelliform, about 8 mm. wide, somewhat verrucu- lose, pubescent; fruit subrotund, tetragonal, dark purple, depressed at both ends,  4-seeded; seeds obovate or triangular, osseous, convex outside, striate.
