description: Stems clustered, 2-3 m tall, 0.9 cm diam., light brown, the internodes 0.4 cm at apex of stem. Leaves simple; sheaths 8.5 cm long; petioles 6-10.5 cm long; rachis 24.4 - 26.7 cm long, 2.9 - 3.4 mm wide at the base; veins diverging at an angle of 26-30 º from the rachis; apical divisions 14.5 17.5 cm long, the veins diverging at an angle of 22-26º from the rachis. Inflorescences anthesis, branched 9.9-10 cm long, brown nally furrowed, splitting peduncular bract not from prophyll; peduncles 9.5 cm long, 2.6 mm wide at the first branch; rachilla 34, 8.2 cm long at base of inflorescence, 1.3 mm wide, sparsely covered with white, wooly, branched indument; flower pits spirally arranged, tricussately at apices of rachillae; upper lips hooded, without a central split, not ciliate, lower lips scarcely developed; staminate flowers 1.8 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 1.8 mm long, ciliate; petals connate for ca. half their length, valvate above, 1.7 mm long; stamens 3; filaments united below for 1 mm, free above; thecae free, inflexed, borne on a short, bifid connective; pistillodes inconspicuous; pistillate flowers 1 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 1 mm long; petals connate for ca. half their length, valvate above, 1 mm long; staminodial tube blunt at the apex; fruits not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Henderson, Andrew A., et al. 2008. New species of Geonoma (Palmae) from Ecuador. Brittonia. 60 (2): 190-201.

description: Herba perennis. Inflorescentia racemosa laxa pauciflora; bractea floralis ovarii dimidium aequans. Flores parvi; sepala petalaque ex rubello viridi-luteola; labelli pagina adaxialis rubella, pagina abaxialis albida. Sepalum dorsale ellipticum usque oblanceolatum obtusum; sepala lateralia subelliptica subfalcata. Petala elliptica subfalcata. Labellum ovato-ellipticum, base cordatum, apice rotundatum, margine integrum.

description: Plants perennial terrestrial, deciduous, 30-35 cm high. Corms subglobose. Sheathing bracts 3-4, originating from the basal nodes of the corm, tubular, successively larger upwards, apex obtuse, margin entire. Leaves 2, petiolate, articulate, blades ascending-arcuate, plicate, elliptic to obovate, up to 26 cm long, ca. 8 cm wide, margin entire to obscurely undulate, apex sharply acuminate. Inflorescence 30-35 cm long including the stalk, originating from an upper internode of the corm, erect, with a solitary, narrow, tubular, scarious-membranous bract ca. 1 cm long, racemose, with about 8-13 flowers, the portion of the inflorescence bearing flowers approximately 10 cm from middle to apex; floral bract sessile, about half as long as the ovary triangular in outline, apex acute, 1.2-1.4 cm long, ca. 3 mm wide, margin entire, greenish and membranous when fresh, when dried scarious-membranous, brown. Flowers ascending, 1.5-2 cm high, showy, sepals and petals green-yellowish, dorsal sepal and petals in both surfaces with shades of red, the lateral sepals tinged with reddish in the adaxial surface, the adaxial surface of lip reddish, the abaxial face whitish, lacking marginal apical spots. Pedicellate ovary ascending, straight to slightly arcuate, 1-1.5 cm long, ca. 1 mm diameter. Dorsal sepal in an angle of 70º to pedicellate ovary axis, smoothly arcuate, forming a hood with the petals, slightly concave in the apical half, flat in the basal half, elliptic to oblanceolate when flattened, apex obtuse, mucronate, 11-14 mm long, 3-4 mm wide near the apex, margin entire, 5-veined. Lateral sepals arising from the lower margin of the column foot, spreading from the column axis, overlapping at the base, the apices close together, sometimes overlapping, when flattened subelliptical, smoothly falcate, apex acute, 8-10 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, margin entire, 5-veined. Petals arising from the lateral margins of the column foot, arcuate under the dorsal sepal forming a loose hood over the column, adjacent margins overlapping from the base to above the middle, elliptic when flattened, slightly falcate, apex acute, 9-11 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, margin entire, 7-veined. Lip forming a short, flexible claw at the base of the column foot, the apical half abruptly decurved, widely concave transversely nearly to the apex, broadly ovate-elliptic when flattened, the base cordate, apex rounded, 5-6 mm long, 4 mm wide, margin entire. Column ascending, in an angle of 45º to the pedicellate ovary axis, then arcuate, ventral side deeply rounded, canaliculated in its entire length, the lateral margins above the middle forming a pair of vertical, widely rounded wings, about half as long as the column, column 6 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide across the wings, whitish, with a few reddish, irregular lines or dots abaxially near the column foot, column foot deeply canaliculate, the thick walls of the channel continuous with the sharp sides of the column which above become the wings, 2-3 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide. Anther prominent, subconical, unilocular, 0.7 x 0.9 mm, with a short truncate beak at the apex, 149 µm long. Pollinia 4, in two pairs, in each pair the pollinia unequal, subellipsoidal, somewhat dorsiventrally compressed, 354 x 248 µm, sculpture lacunose.
bibliographicCitation: Gibbs, P. E. & Alverson, William S. 2006. How many species of Spirotheca (Malvaceae s.l., Bombacoideae)?. Brittonia. 58 (3): 245-258.

description: Stem branching pattern and height unknown 3.5 cm diam., plants 2-4 m tall. Leaves 12-21, simple or with one division; sheaths 23 cm long; petioles 26 cm long; rachis 81-111 cm long, 5.2-7.1 mm wide at the base; pinnae 1 or 2, drying dark brown, the veins raised adaxially; veins diverging at an angle of 24-36º from the rachis; apical divisions 21.7-39.5 cm long, diverging at an angle of 23-300 from the rachis. Inflorescences interfoliar at anthesis, branched; prophylls and peduncular bracts not seen, the peduncular bracts inserted 2.2 cm above the prophyll; peduncles 55 cm long, 4.3-7.2 mm wide at the apex; rachillae 2-4, 16.5-20.5 cm long, 5.8-6.7 mm wide, covered with wooly, brown indument; flower pits spirally arranged; lower lips well-developed, with a central split, briefly overlapping the upper lip; upper lips well-developed; staminate flowers 4 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 3.5-4 mm long; petals connate for ca. one third their length, valvate above, 3.6-4 mm long; stamens 6; filaments briefly united below, free above; thecae inflexed on a short connective; pistillodes obscure or absent; pistillate flowers 3 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 3 mm long; petals connate for ca. one third their length, valvate above, 3 mm long; staminodial tube digitately lobed at the apex; fruits globose, 17.4-24.9 mm long, 15.4-17.8 mm diam., black, with a rough surface, splitting when mature.

description: Stems solitary, 0.1 m tall, 2.5 cm diam., light brown, the intemrnodes not seen. Leaves irregularly pinnate with multi-veined pinnae; sheaths and petioles not seen; rachis 13- 27 cm long, 1.5-2.4 mm wide at the base; pinnae 3-5 on each side of rachis; basal pinna 1-9 cm wide at the base, 11.5-17 cm long, diverging at an angle of 40-53º from the rachis; apical pinna 3-7.4 cm wide at the base, 9.2-13 cm long, diverging at an angle of 35-45º from the rachis. Inflorescences interfoliar at anthesis, unbranched; prophylls 12.3 cm long, splitting apically, persistent; peduncular bracts 18.4 cm long, inserted 0.8 cm above the prophyll; peduncles 60 cm long, 1.4-1.8 mm wide at the apex; rachilla 1, 5-9.2 cm long, 3.8-4.6 mm wide, sparsely covered with whitish-brown, wooly indument, becoming orange in fruit, with an apical, sterile section; flower pits spirally and closely arranged; lower lips with a central split, not or scarcely ciliate; upper lips low; staminate flowers 3 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 2.8 mm long, ciliate; petals connate for ca. half their length, valvate above, 2.8 mm long, ciliate; stamens 6; filaments united below for 1 mm, free above; thecae free, inflexed, the connective scarcely developed; pistillodes inconspicuous; pistillate flowers 2.5 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 2.4 mm long, ciliate; petals free, valvate, 2 mm long, ciliate; staminodial tube digitately lobed; mature fruits not seen.

description: Stems solitary or clustered, 0.5-2 m tall, 0.5-0.9 cm diam., light brown, the intemrnodes 0.7-3.1 cm at apex of stem. Leaves 7-11, simple; sheaths 4-12.1 cm long; petioles 11- 27.5 cm long; rachis 10.7-18.7 cm long, 1.2- 2.5 mm wide at the base; veins diverging at an angle of 33-46º from the rachis at the base, 36-43x at apex, blade split at apex for 10.2-17 cm. Inflorescences interfoliar at anthesis, branched to one order; prophylls 9.6-10.5 cm long, splitting apically, persistent and tattering; peduncular bracts 7.8 cm long, inserted 1-6.9 cm above the prophyll; peduncles 4.4-15 cm long, 1.2-2.4 mm wide at the first branch; rachillae 2-5, 6-15.5 cm long at base of inflorescence, 1-2.4 mm wide, angular, densely covered with whitish-brown, wooly indument; flower pits spirally arranged; upper and lower lips continuous, forming a slightly raised cupule with irregular splits; staminate flowers 3 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 3 mm long; petals connate for ca. half their length, valvate above, 2.4 mm long; stamens 6; filaments united below for 1 mm, free above; thecae free, inflexed, the connective scarcely developed; pistillodes inconspicuous; pistillate flowers 3.2 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 3.2 mm long; petals connate for ca. half their length, valvate above, 3 mm long; staminodial tube blunt at the apex; fruits globose, 7-9.5 mm long, 5.4-6.8 mm diam., apiculate, black.

description: Stems solitary, 1.2-4.2 m tall, 1-1.3 cm diam., light brown, the intemrnodes 2.3-5.7 cm at apex of stem. Leaves 5-9, irregularly pinnate with multi-veined pinnae; sheaths 19-30 cm long, fibrous; petioles 33.5- 98.5 cm long, densely, felty brown tomentose initially; rachis 17-74 cm long, 2.3-5.1 mm wide at the base, tomentose as the petiole; pinnae 3-16 per side of rachis; basal pinna 0.6-2 cm wide at the base, 24-35.5 cm long, diverging at an angle of 61-90o from the rachis; apical pinna 2.7-11.3 cm wide at the base, 12.5-22 cm long, diverging at an angle of 21-33O from the rachis. Inflorescences infrafoliar at anthesis, branched to three orders; prophylls 9.5-21 cm long, brown tomentose, longitudinally furrowed, splitting laterally and early deciduous; peduncular bracts 7-14 cm long, inserted 2.6-5.5 cm above the prophyll; peduncles 13-31 cm long, 2-8.5 mm wide at the first branch; rachilla 18-39, 7.5-18.3 cm long at base of inflorescence, 0.8-2.2 mm wide, glabrous or sparsely to densely covered with reddish brown, branched indument; flower pits spirally and distantly arranged; upper and lower lips continuous, forming a raised cupule, not ciliate on the margins; staminate flowers 2.2 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 2.2 mm long; petals connate for ca. half their length, valvate above, 2.2 mm long; stamens 6; filaments united below, free above; thecae free, inflexed, the connective scarcely devel- oped; pistillodes inconspicuous; pistillate flowers 3.8 mm long; sepals free, imbricate, keeled, 3.8 mm long; petals connate for ca. half their length, valvate above, 2.6 mm long; staminodial tube blunt at the apex; fruits globose, 6.4-7.2 mm long, 5.5-6.8 mm diam., purple-black.

description: Tree or shrub, (0.5-)2-4(-8) m tall (label of Proctor 36833: 15 m tall, see note below); twigs ± pubescent when young, glabrescent, sometimes some internodes pilose and others glabrous. Stipules deltoid, acute, 2-3(-4) x 1- 2.5 mm, usually pubescent abaxially when young, glabrescent. Petiole 2-5(-8) x ca. 1 mm, glabrous, rarely with scattered hairs. Leaf blade obovate or elliptic, sometimes oblong, rarely orbicular to transverse elliptic, apically acute, obtuse, rounded, truncate or retuse, sometimes apiculate or short-acuminate, sometimes with a terminal or subapical glandular dark mucro ca. 0.1 mm long, basally acute, obtuse or rounded, rarely narrowly cuneate, (1-)2-4.5(-8)x (0.7-)1.2-2.5(-4.5) cm, not to hardly revolute, glabrous, rarely with scattered hairs abaxially, coriaceous to thinly chartaceous, discolorous or concolorous, yellowish green to olive-green adaxially, usually shiny, often lighter and duller abaxially, midvein moderately prominent to flat adaxially, strongly prominent abaxially, higher venation prominent on both surfaces or only abaxially. Sepals 5, ovate or oblong, obtuse to rounded, 1.5-2 x 1-2 mm, pilose to pubescent abaxially, sometimes fimbriate. Petals 5, spathulate to obdeltoid, erose to lacerate, usually emarginate, 1-1.5 x 1-1.5 mm, shorter than the sepals. Disc ± distinctly crenate or lobed, the lobes altemipetalous, to 1 mm long. Stamens 5; 2-4 mm long; filaments free or basally fused for ca. 0.5 mm, 1.5-3 mm long; anthers ovoid to ellipsoid, 0.7-1.2 mm long. Pistillode 1-2 x ca. 0.5 mm, as long as or (if filaments are fused) slightly longer than the sepals, sparsely pilose to pubescent. Pistillate Jflowers solitary, 3-4x3-4 mm; bracts as in staminate flowers; buds subsessile or short- pedicellate, globose to ellipsoid. Pedicel 1-4 x 0.7-1.5 mm, glabrous to pubescent. Sepals 5, ± orbicular, ovate or deltoid, obtuse to rounded, 1-2 x 1-2 mm, pubescent abaxially, sometimes fimbriate. Leaf blades obovate, more rarely oblong to nearly elliptic, apically obtuse, rounded, turncate or retuse, more rarely very short- acuminate, basally acute or narrowly cuneate, rarely obtuse, (1.2-)2-9(-11.5) x (0.8 -) 1.5 -4(-5.5)cm, not to strongly revolute at the margin, glabrous, rarely with a few hairs abaxially, coriaceous, ± concolorous, olive -green or reddish brown, midvein much less prominent adaxially than abaxially, higher venation on both surfaces or only abaxially prominent. Sepals 5, ovate, oblong, deltoid, more rarely obovate, acute to rounded, 1.5 - 2.5 x 1 -1.5 mm, sometimes fimbriate, pilose to pubescent abaxially. description: Terrestrial plant 30-40 cm tall. Stem erect, base with 2-3 sheaths. Leaves two, opposite, attached one third the distance from the base of the stem, 1.5-4 x 1.2-3 cm, broadly ovate to ovate, apex acute. Inflorescence laxly many-flowered; peduncle puberulent, ca. 5 cm long; rachis puberulent, 15-20 cm long. Floral bracts ovate to elliptic, 4-6 mm long. Pedicel with ovary 1 cm long, pedicel puberulent. Flowers uniformly green. Dorsal sepal elliptic, ca. 4 x 2.5 mm, acuminate. Lateral sepals narrowly elliptic, ca. 4 x 1.5 mm, reflexed along the ovary. Petals linear, 3 x 0.5 mm. Lip 8-9 x 7 mm, base cuneate, margin toothed, claw with two auricles, apex bilobed; disc with a thickened mid-line extending into a small tooth between two lobules; auricles triangular, 1.5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide at base; lobules oblique, diverging at 300, ca. 5 x 3 mm. Column curved, 2-3 mm long.

description: Terrestrial herb ca. 35 cm tall including the inflorescence. Roots whitish, lanate, 0.5-1 mm in diam. Pseudobulbs epigeal, clustered, narrowly ovoid, up to 3.5 × 1.5 cm, covered by cataphylls 3-6.5 cm long, these initially green but becoming scarious as the pseudobulb matures. Leaves 2, two-edged, 10-11 × 0.2-0.6 cm; blades spreading oppositely atop the petioles, olive green, somewhat translucent (in dried condition), ovate to ovateelliptic, base rounded, apex acuminate, 14-17 20-21 cm long from the point where it emerges from within the leaf petioles; peduncle with several longitudinal, low keels, to 2 mm wide; raceme umbellate, with ca. 60 flowers open at a time (but there are flower buds above and developed capsules below), ca. 3-4 cm long and wide. Flowal bracts spreading at anthesis, erect and appressed to the rachis after the rachis after the fall of the flower, trianglar, long-acuminate, green, with a dorsal keel decurrent on the rachis, 1.5-3 mm long. Flowers pale green, ascendent upon anthesis but becoming horizontal and resupinate afterwards; floral segments bearing spare, large, raphide-containing idioblasts, these more dense in the labellum and column. Sepals spreading, convex-tubular as a result of their strongly revolute margins; lateral sepals erect, obliquely elliptic-ovate, obtuse-rounded, somewhat thickened externally near apex, 3-veined, 4 x 1.8 mm; dorsal sepal strongly reflexed, appressed to the ovary, ovate, subacute, 3-veined, 3.6 x 1.6 mm. Petals strongly recurved, convex, linear, 2.6 x ca. 0.1 mm, slightly broadened near the base, unveined. Labellum entire, fleshy, elliptic, 3.7 x 2.6 mm, provided below the middle with a deep excavation, which is divided longitudinally into two oval cavities by a fleshy, blunt ridge; each of the two cavities of the labellum has a rounded, marginal process at base; above the middle the labellum is slightly concave as a result of the incurved distal margin. Column dorsiventrally compressed, subquadrate, clawed, truncate, ending in a narrow pointed lobule at each side of apex, ca. 1 mm long and wide. Anther dorsal, erect, two-celled. Stigma ventral, lunate. Pollinaria 2, oblongfalciform, divergent, each resulting from the fusion of two pollinia and bearing an apical viscid droplet. Rostellum obscure, merely a membranaceous margin at the apex of the column. Ovary slightly arching, twisted near the base, 6-angled, 14-17 mm long, ca. 0.8 mm in diam. near the middle but slightly thickened towards both the base and apex. Capsule narrowly ellipsoid to obovoid, 9-11 x 3-4 mm, plus a slender pedicel 14-15 mm long (mature capsules not seen).

description: Glabrous throughout. Stems stout, sharply 4-angled or narrowly 4-winged, at least when dried, the internodes mostly 1.5-3 cm. long. Stipules connate, terminated by an erect, appressed, coriaceous acumen 2-4 mm. long. Petioles stout, about 3 mm. long. Leaf-blades fleshy, narrowly obovate-oblonog, 25-40 mm. long, 12-20 mm. wide, roulinded or barely apiculate at summit, entire, cuneate to base, 1-nerved. Flowers solitary in the upper axils, on stout pedulincles 3-5 mm. long. Bracts 2, elliptic, sessile, 10-13 mm. long. Pedicel none. Calyx-lobes erect or somnewhat spreading, niarrowly elliptic, 17 mm. long, acute, persistent in fruit. Corolla-tube slender, 8 cm. long; corolla-lobes widely spreading, oblong, about 25 mm. lonig, broadly acute.

description: Shrubs 0.5-3(-4) m tall, monoecious; branches generally smooth, glabrous in age, bark grayish brown. Leaves alternate; stipules rudimentary; petioles 0.6-2(-3.5) cm long, tomentose; blades 4-8.7(-13) x 1.5-5(-8.5) cm, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, base acute to obtuse, occasionally subcordate, apex generally acuminate, mucronulate, margin entire to slightly repand, venation actinodromus with 3 basal nerves, glabrescent on the upper surfaces, tomentose on the lower surface with whitish hairs, lacking glands. Inflorescences terminal bisexual thyrses 4.8-5.5(-8.5) cm long, with pistillate flowers at the base and staminate flowers towards the apex, without bisexual cymules; staminate bracts 0.8-1.2 x 0.3-0.4 mm, lanceolate, pubescent, apex acute, margin entire, subtending a single flower, pistillate bracts 1-1.2 mm x 0.3-0.4 mm, similar to those of the staminate flowers. Staminate flowers actinomorphic; pedicel 2.8-5.7(-11) mm long, glabrous or with scattered stellate hairs; sepals 5, ovate, 1.4-2 x 0.5-1.2 mm, equal, united at the base, pubescent on the outer surface, apex obtuse, margin entire; petals 5, spathulate, 2.4 x 0.8 mm, equal, free, glabrous on both surfaces, white, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin ciliate with unbranched hairs; stamens 15, filiform, 1.6-2.2 mm long, villous towards the base; anthers oblong, 0.5-0.6 mm long. Pistillate flowers actinomorphic; pedicel stout, 0.5-1.1 mm long, stellate pubescent; sepals 5 or occasionally 6, 1-1.2 x 0.5-0.7 mm, lanceolate, equal, free, pubescent in both surfaces, apex subacute, margen entire, withering in fruit; petals absent; ovary subglobose, tomentose when young, echinate with stellate hairs at the end of an elongate protuberance 0.1-1.1mm long; styles 3, 2-2.5 mm long, bifurcate one time. Capsules subglobose, 6-8 x 6.5-7.6 mm, echinate, stellate-pubescent, septicidally and loculicidally explosively dehiscent into three 2-valved cocci; columella 4.2-5.1 mm long. Seeds elliptic, 3.6-5.3 x 3-4.7 mm, brown-gray, dorsiventrally compressed, smooth, with a yellowish caruncle 0.3-0.7 x 1.1-2.4 mm.

description: Plants saxicolous, short caulescent, ing 0.8-1.4 m high, propagating shoots; leaves ca. 15 in number, suberect, densely arranged in a funnelform rosette; sheaths broadly ovate, 12-17 x 9-10.5 cm, pale brown becoming soft green toward apex abaxially, whitish becoming greenish adaxially, densely brown lepidote on both sides; blades sublinear, apex cuspidate, 24-42 x 4.5-6 cm, lustrous, green on both surfaces, with a narrow (i.e., ca. 0.8 mm wide) dark wine-colored line along the margins, glabrous, involute, suberect with recurved apices, coriaceous, distinctly nerved, weakly plicate in cross section; scape 60-75 cm long, exceeding the rosette, with 4.5-7 cm long internodes, 1.3-1.7 cm diam., pale green underneath the bracts but dark wine-colored at exposed portions, glabrescent, distinctly nerved, slightly curved; scape bracts: the proximal ones subfoliaceous, the distal ones ovate, apex long-attenuate and slightly recurved, 8-14 x 3-3.6 cm, densely white lepidote and totally green becoming purple toward apex adaxially, sparsely lepidote and deep purple becoming greenish with purplish-red dots toward apex abaxially, margins with a very narrow purple line all along, involute, suberect, densely imbricate, the basal ? firmly conceal- ing the scape, distinctly nerved with some prominent veins, weakly plicate in cross sec- tion; inflorescence once branched, elliptic in outline, 46-54 x 23-26cm, main axis with 3- 4 cm long internodes; flowering branches laxly to subdensely arranged, 4-12 in number, 6-14- flowered, pendulous to arcuate, some of them distinctly tortuous or somewhat twisted; rachis geniculate, almost quadrangular in cross sec- tion, 8-20cm long, 4mm diam., green, glabrous, with 2.7 (proximal) to 1.2 cm (distal) long internodes separating the flowers; primary bracts broadly ovate, 5-6 x 3.2-3.6 cm, apicu- late, slightly inflated, dark wine-colored at the insertion line, along the margins and toward the apex, and greenish in the central portion, distinctly nerved, lepidote; peduncles flattened, elliptic in cross section, 4-9 cm long, 7 mm diam. at the base, green, glabrous, bearing 1-2 sterile bracts; sterile bracts broadly ovate, shortly attenuate, 3-4.2 x 2.5-3.5 cm, purplish green, glabrous or nearly so, symmetric, carinate; floral bracts broadly ovate, apex obtuse, 2.8-3.6 x 2.5-2.8 cm, glabrous or nearly so, green with few purple spots along the margins, symmetric, membranaceous, carinate toward the apex; pedicels obconic, 4-6mm long, 4-5 mm diam., green; flowers odorless, not secund; sepals elliptic, apex acute, 3.5- 3.8 x 1.2-1.8 cm, equaling the floral bracts to exceeding them for ca. 2 mm, free, symmetric, glabrescent, green, ecarinate; petals long-linear with an acute apex, golden-yellow, inconspicuously whitish at the base, recoiling and spiraling, 5.7-6 x 0.6-0.7cm, free, symmetric, glabrous; petal appendages 2, ligulate, 14- 20 x 1-2mm, longitudinally adnate to the petals for 1.1-1.6 cm; stamens free; filaments terete, slightly flattened, 5.2-5.5cm long, ca. 1 mm thick, white; anthers sagittate, 1.2-1.5 cm long, ca. 1 mm thick, dorsifixed near the base, rimose; style terete, white, 7.5-7.7 cm long, ca. 1 mm diam.; stigma lobes white, ca. 3 x 1 mm, erect; ovary ca. 11 x 3-4 mm, ovate, hypanthium ca. 5 mm in length; ovules numerous, ca. 1.4 mm long, with an elliptic apical appendage, restricted to the upper 1/2-portion of the ovary; fruits and seeds unknown.

description: Plants saxicolous, short caulescent, flowering up to 2.5 m high; rosette (0.7-)1.3-1.7 m diam., crateriform; leaves numerous, spreading, arcuate; sheaths broadly ovate 19-27 x 8-19 cm, pale brown adaxially, dark brown becoming pale brown with dark wine- red color inclined lines at the top abaxially, densely brown lepidote on both surfaces; blades linear, long-attenuate, 61-75 x 7.5-11 cm, green, lustrous, inconspicuously dark wine-red along the margins, wine-colored spotted on both sides or only abaxially, lepidote on both sides but glabrescent toward the apex adaxially, coriaceous, distinctly nerved with some prominent longitudinal veins; blade apex acute to cuspidate, totally green or dark wine-red colored, recurved, apiculus twisted; scape erect, stout, 2-4 cm diam., 0.8-1.2 m long, with internodes of 3.5- 6.5 cm long, green underneath the bracts, wine-colored maculate on sun exposed portions, glabrous or nearly so; scape bracts: the proximal ones subfoliaceous and suberect, the distal ones spreading, recurved toward apex, broadly lanceolate, with an ovate base and a caudate and a dark wine-colored mucronate apex, completely green maculate with red or totally red at the base and green maculate with wine-red toward apex, brown lepidote, involute, distinctly nerved; inflores- cence once branched, pyramidal to elliptic in outline, 0.6-1.3 x 0.7-1 m, main axis with 4-9 cm long internodes; flowering branches subdensely arranged, 14-32 in number, (3-) 10-18-flowered, peduncle arcuate, the mid portion patent, and the terminal portion slightly erect or the entire branch weakly arcuate; rachis geniculate, 18-27 cm long, 4 mm diam., olive-green toward apex, glabrous, with 3.5 (proximal) to 1 cm (distal) long internodes separating the flowers; primary bracts broadly ovate, 6-9 x 6 cm at the base, with a 2-6 x 0.6 cm narrowly triangular and caudate apex, apex with a prominent vein and a recurved and rigid apiculus, shorter than the peduncles, green at the central portion and wine-colored along the margins and at the top or totally wine-colored, brown lepidote, involute, spreading, coriaceous, distinctly nerved; peduncles cylindrical to slightly flattened, 9-22 cm long, 6-7 mm diam. at the base, glabrescent, bearing 1-3 sterile bracts; sterile bracts suborbicular, apex obtuse, discretely mucronate, 3- 3.7 x 3-3.2 cm, glabrous abaxially, brown lepidote adaxially, involute, erect, symmetric or nearly so, coriaceous, distinctly nerved, carinate toward apex; floral bracts convex, suborbicular, apex obtuse, discretely mucronate, 3.4-3.7 x 3.6-4(-4.4) cm, glabrous and lustrous abaxially, brown lepidote adaxially, green at the central portion and wine-colored along the margins, membranaceous and pale yellow along the margins and coriaceous at the central portion on the dried material, distinctly rugose-nervate, carinate, inflated and densely imbricate at the branches apical portions; pedicels obconic, 8-11 mm long, ca. 4 mm diam.; flowers odorless, not secund; sepals obovate, apex acute and minutely apiculate, 3.6-4(-4.4) x 1.4-1.8 cm, exceeding the floral bracts for ca. 1 cm, free, sparsely brown lepidote adaxially, green with membranaceous hyaline margins, ecarinate; petals long-linear with an acute apex, yellow in flower buds and immediately after the anthesis, fading quickly to creamy white, spreading, weakly twisted, 9.3-11 x 1-1.2 cm, free, glabrous, inconspicuously white spotted, margins entire with the distal 1/2-portion slightly undulate; petal appendages 2, ligulate, 3.4-3.7 x ca. 0.3 cm, longitudinally adnate to the petal for 2.9-3.1 cm, the apex free, apices overlapping and completely hiding the ovary from a top view; stamens free; filaments terete, 9-10cm long, ca. 2mm thick, white; anthers sagittate, 1.2-1.6cm long, ca. 1 mm thick, dorsifixed near the base, rimose; style terete, white, 9.3-10cm long ca. 2 mm diam.; stigma lobes white, ca. 4 x 1 mm, spreading; ovary ca. 22 x 6 mm, narrowly ovate, hypanthium ca. 8 mm in length; ovules numerous, ca. 1.6 mm long, with an elliptic apical appendage, restricted to the upper 1/2-portion of the ovary; fruit an ellipsoid, rugose, dark castaneous, 5.3- 6.2cm long capsule; seeds narrowly elliptic, brown, ca. 6 x 1 mm; seed appendages: fimbriate, the apical ones pale brown, ca. 15 mm long, the basal ones whitish, ca. 7 mm long.

description: Palma caespitosa. Caudex gracilis 2-5 m altus, 1-1.5 cm crassus; internodia spinarum annulis munita. Folia 7-12, circa metralia; lamina simplex, bifurcata, obovata. Inflorescentiae pedunculus 8-13 cm; pedunculi spatha 18-26 cm, extus pallide fusco-tomentosa; spadix patens, ramulis 3-6 gracilibus, 7-10cm longis, rhachi 1-2cm. Fructus globosi vel late obovoidei, 1.5-2.5 cm diam., atropurpurei.

description: Cespitose understory palm; stems 5-15 (or more), 2-5 m tall, 1-1.5 cm in diam.; internodes 2-8 cm long, usually armed under each leaf scar with rings of 1-2.5 cm long black, flattened spines. Leaves 7-12, 0.8-1.1 m long; sheath pale brownish green, lepidote, 13-20 cm long, sheath and petiole armed with brown to black, slightly flattened spines, 0.5-5 cm long; petiole cylindrical, canaliculate adaxially, light green, whitish floccose (including the spines) when young, basally erect, arching, 7-35 cm long, 4-5 mm in diam.; blade horizontally spreading, entire, obovoid, deeply bifid at apex, cuneate, sometimes slightly asymmetric at base, green, membranous, bullate; the apical lobes 20-30 cm long, acute; rachis 35-50 cm long, with a few pale brown spines adaxially; 17-19 pairs of primary lateral veins, these prominent abaxially. Inflorescences 1-3 per stem, infrafoliar, erect and arching at anthesis, pendulous when fruiting; prophyll membranous, glabrous, light brown, 7-10 cm long, 10-14 mm in width; peduncular bract 18-26 cm, with a fusiform part light brown, arachnoid-tomentose, densely covered with brown, erect hairs 1-5 mm long; peduncle 8-13 cm long, slightly curved apically, laterally flattened, brown velvety to hairy on upper half; rachis green, 1-2 cm long, bearing 3-6 green, glabrous, slender, rachillae, 7-10cm long, with pistillate flowers scattered among male flowers, the distal part with staminate flowers only; staminate flowers 2-3 mm long; sepals whitish, glabrous, acute triangular, united at base, 0.2 x 0.8 mm; petals cream, glabrous, fleshy, obovate, valvate, united at base, 1-1.5 x 2-3 mm; stamens 6, the filaments ca. 2 mm long, inflexed at apex, the anthers dorsifixed, 0.8-1 mm long; pistillate flowers pale green at anthesis, 4 mm long; calyx cupular, glabrous, 3-denticulate, ca. 2 mm long, 1.2 mm in diam.; corolla as long as calyx, conspicuously puberulous; ovary green, cylindrical, exceeding calyx, 4 mm long. Fruit globose to widely obovoid, glabrous, smooth, shiny, slightly apiculate at apex, green becoming red wine to dark purple at maturity, 1.3-2.5 cm in diam.; mesocarp flashy, white, 2-2.5 mm thick; fruiting perianth with corolla green, puberulous, irregularly split at margin, 8-10 mm in diam., without a staminodial ring, and calyx pale yellowish green, glabrous, 5-6 mm in diam.; endocarp turbinate, 0.3 mm thick, 8-10 mm long and 12-15 mm wide, brownish black; endocarp fibers numerous, terete, black, with attached juice sacs; endocarp poses displaced; endosperm white, solid, homogeneous.

description: Croton hibiscifolio Kunth affinis sed inflorescentiis pendentibus, stigmatibus quadrifidis, floribus foemineis breviter pedicellatis, staminibus ca. 24, stipulis ovatolaciniatis differt.
bibliographicCitation: Riina, Ricarda, et al. 2007. A new species of "sangre de drago" (Croton section Cyclostigma, Euphorbiaceae) from coastal Ecuador. Brittonia. 59 (1): 97-101.

description: Tree 3-8 m high, ca. 20 cm DBH; young branches covered with dense whitish to golden yellow indumentum of stellate-porrect trichomes with central porrect rays 1.5-2 mm long; upper surface of foliage dark green, lower surface pale green; latex from the stem and young branches dark red. Stipules ovate-lanceolate, 3-6 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, persistent on young branches, margins conspicuously laciniate, with 12-16 nonglandular laciniae. Leaves alternate, membranaceous to papery (when dry), with a pleasant smell when fresh leaves are rubbed; leaf blade unlobed or with 2 or 3 acute to acuminate lobes in the upper third of the blade, 5-15(-20) x 3-14(-16) cm; apex sharply-acute to caudateacuminate; base usually cordate or less commonly truncate; margin minutely denticulate with numerous ovoid glands; venation actinodromous, palminerved with 3-5 veins from base and 5-8 lateral veins per side of midrib further up the lamina, tertiary veins scalariform, weakly sinuous, the primary and secondary veins raised on the abaxial surface; foliar glands 2, acropetiolar, attached to the petiole on the abaxial surface, discoid, elliptic, 0.7-1 mm in diam., glandular surface lustrous and yellow in life, sessile to shortly stipitate; petioles 1.5-10cm long, with dense indumentum of stellate-porrect trichomes, rays 0.08-0.10mm long, central porrect ray 1-1.5mm long; adaxial leaf indumentum sparse, trichomes stellate-porrect, denser along the veins; abaxial leaf surface with denser indumentum of stellate-porrect trichomes, those along the veins with longer porrect central rays. Inflorescences terminal, arching-pendent, 5.5-30 cm long; upper cymules with 3-5 flowers, rachis angular, golden brown with dense covering of stellate-porrect trichomes, lower cymules bisexual with 3-8 staminate flowers and 1 or 2 pistillate flowers; pistillate bracts widely triangular, ca. 2 x 1 mm; staminate bracts linear, 1-1.2 x 0.2-0.4mm. Staminate flowers distributed along the inflorescence from base to top; pedicels 4-6mm long; sepals 5, valvate, ovate, acute, 2-3 x 1.5-2.5 mm, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface with a dense indumentum of rosulate and/or multiradiate porrect trichomes; petals 5, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, creamcolored, 2-3 x 1-1.2 mm, the adaxial surface glabrous except for a cluster of long hairs at the base, abaxial surface sparsely pilose, edges lanate; receptacle densely pilose; stamens ca. 24; filaments 2-3 mm long, glabrous, inflexed in bud; anthers 0.8 x 0.3-0.4 mm. Pistillate flowers subsessile or short-pedicellate, pedicels 0.5-1.5 mm long; sepals 5, valvate, broadly lanceolate to oblong, somewhat unequal, 2.4-3 x 1-1.5 mm, apex acute, adaxial surface densely pilose toward the edges, abaxial surface densely covered with multiradiate, tall stellate-porrect trichomes; malformed petals generally present, more rarely a stalked or sessile gland present in the same position; ovary 3 x 2.5 mm, covered with golden-yellow multiradiate and tall stellate-porrect trichomes; styles quadrifid, with 12 (-14) stigmas, the nonreceptive surfaces covered with sparse stellate trichomes. Mature fruits and seeds unknown.

description: Trees or shrubs, 1-8 m tall. brownish, flattened, densely becoming glabrous bark falls, the older twigs becoming brownish-gray and smooth or the bark peeling in small scales or strips. Trichomes simple, whitish to tan, less than 0.3 mm long. Leaves elliptic, 2-5.8 x 1-3.2 cm, the margin often with ciliate appressed-antrorse white trichomes, revolute when dry especially at the base; apex acute to acuminate; base cuneate to attenuate; blades thin, submembranous to slightly chartaceous, slightly discolorous, somewhat shiny and dark green above, duller and dark olive green beneath, densely glandular; venation brochidodromous; midvein glabrous or sparsely pubescent with appressed trichomes, flush to slightly raised above, prominent and raised below; secondary veins 6-9 pairs, distinct, raised on both surfaces, the marginal vein 1-1.8 mm from the margin at the midpoint of the leaf; tertiary veins indistinct; petiole channeled, 2-4mm long, ca. 0.8 mm thick, densely to sparsely puberulent. Flower bud pyriform, (3-)4-5 mm long, the globe of the bud ca. 2.5 mm in diameter; peduncles 3-13 x 0.5 mm, flattened, axillary, solitary or often in pairs on short, bracteate shoots, these shoots to 2(-5) cm long, sometimes terminating in a dichasium; bracteoles early caducous or present until fruit matures, ovate-lanceolate, 0.5-1x0.2-0.3mm; calyx open, the lobes 4, ovate to suborbicular, 1.5-2 x 1.5-2 mm, pubescent adaxially and with a densely ciliate margin, glandular, glabrous on the abaxial surface; petals 4, obovate to suborbicular, 3-3.5 mm long, the base at the point of attachment ca. 0.8 mm wide, white, glandular on the adaxial surface, sometimes with a ciliate margin. Hypanthium campanulate, 4-angled and slightly winged in cross section, 1.5-2 mm long, not tearing between the calyx lobes; hypanthium tube ca. 1 mm long; disk 1.5-2 mm wide, the staminal ring brownish, ca. 0.5 mm wide, glabrous. Stamens 70-95; filaments 2-4mm long; anthers narrowly elliptic, 0.6-1 x 0.2 mm, with 1 raised, terminal gland, the gland shortcylindric, yellowish brown, to 0.1 mm long. Style 4-5.5 mm long, ca. 0.1 mm thick, glandular. Stigma slightly peltate. Ovary 2-locular; placentation axile, the ovules 12-20, radiating from the central, slightly protruding placenta. Fruits, 4-angled, slightly winged, oblanceolate to oblong, green turning black at maturity, somewhat fleshy, 12-19 x 5 mm, densely glandular. Seeds 4-7 per fruit, cochleate with a soft center, flattened, 2-4 mm long, 0.5 mm thick, the seed coat coriaceous, wavy-papillose, the central portion smooth and dark brown with isodiametric cells, somewhat lustrous, brownish, 1(-3) cells thick, the cells of the rim elongate with the long axis radiating outwards from the center of the seed, the micropylar operculum present at the hypocotyl end of the embryo. Embryo C-shaped, the cotyledons not reflexed, ca. 1/6 the length of the hypocotyl. Distribution and Ecology (Fig. 3). This species grows only in the Planalto of the states of Parani and Santa Catarina, in southern Brazil, from 750-950 m. Landrum has seen it as a small tree of the understory in the forests dominated by Araucaria angustifolia (Bertol.) Kuntze and other Myrtaceae common near Curitiba. Legrand and Klein (1969) describe it as being heliophytic and xerophytic, occurring in the campos and small forests. Silva and Casteleti (2003) have proposed provisional biogeographic subregions of the Atlantic Forest based on the distribution of endemic species of well known groups of animals as either areas of endemism or areas of transition. Using this classification, Curitiba occurs in the Brazilian Pine (Araucaria) Forests subregion in the Plantalto Meridional. They consider this region to be a "broad transition area between the Atlantic Forest and the temperate biome of South America" and note that it does not contain any endemic birds, mammals or butterflies.

description: Caulis dextrorsum volubilis. Foliorum lamina (3.5-)6-15(-27)x (2.7-)4.5-10(-20) cm, fere usque ad basim triloba, basi subtruncato-cordata, utrinque glabra infra adpresso-pilosa, 5-9-nervata, petiolo (1.3-)2.3(-7) cm. Racemi [male] in panicula axillari basi ramosa 3.5-20 longi, laxiflori, floribus singulatim pedicellatis; staminibus 3, antheris introrsis, rudimento stylino nullo. Racemi [female] 9 paribus axillaribus vel alter forum ad florem pedicellatam singular reductus, pedunculati; perianthio [female] floribus masculinis simili, stylis distinctis, subulatis. Capsula vel 11 mm, 4-6 mm, anguste oblonga vel elliptica, membranacea. Semina 4-6 x 2-3 mm lata, oblonga vel triangularia, deorsum alata.

description:
Long-trailing or climbing annual vine arising from a shallow rhizomes 5-15 cm, hypogeous, conic, the base lobate-undulate or palmatiform, occasionally L-shaped, bark light brown, inner tissue white. Stems dextrorsely twining, purple to green, lineate to sulcate, essentially glabrous to minutely puberulent; petioles (1.3-)2.3(-7) cm, glabrous to minutely puberulent, purplish or green, lineate, stout. Leaves trilobate (or the lower ones almost trifoliolate), occasionally the lobes slightly overlapping.

Leaves (3.5-)6-15(-27) x (2.7-)4.5-20 cm, alternate; central lobe oval to oblong, abruptly acuminate, 3-nerved; lateral lobe semiovate, acute, 2- to 3-nerved, glabrous on both surfaces or sparsely appressed-pilose on the lower one, base retuse triangular to cor- date. Staminate inflorescences axillary, compound, racemose, branched near the base; individual racemes 4-20 cm long, loosely flowered; pedicels 3-3.5 mm long, their subtending bracts ca. 1 mm long, ovate-acute; perianth segments 1-1.5 mm long, 1-nerved, oblong, obtuse, reflexed at maturity; stamens 3, 0.3-0.5 mm long, about 1/3 the length of the segments, arising from a disc at the base of the perianth, filaments with fleshy base; anthers introrse; stylar rudiment lacking. Pistillate inflorescences racemes in pairs 5-15 cm long (or with the second one reduced to a single pedicellate capsule), pedunculate with a peduncle 3-4 cm long; perianth with segments reflexed, staminodia lacking; stylar column lacking, styles 3, single, free from base, terete, thin, stigmas simple. Capsules 8-11 x 4-6 mm, narrowly oblong to elliptic, membranous, light brown to reddish at maturity, base rounded to oblique, apex obtuse; seeds 4-6 x 2-3 mm, oblong to triangular, 2 per locule, winged basally, brown-reddish, smooth.

description: Plant perennial; roots coarse, fibrous, mostly drab-brown; rhizomes elongated, to 3.5 mm thick, the scales to 8.6 mm (few seen). Culms triquetrous, (56-) 67-83 cm x (4.2-)4.4-5.6(-5.8) mm, soft, internally spongy, with incomplete transverse septa, smooth to finely longitudinally striate, grayish green when dry. Leaves 2(-3), reduced to sheaths, apically oblique, membranous, loose, friable, proximally dark maroon, becoming chestnut to tawny distally, the apex acute. Spikelets cylindric, acute, (3.7-)4-5.1(-5.3) cm x (5-)5.1-6 mm, at least the proximal 2 to 3 scales empty, the first amplexicaulous and appearing as a continuation of culm; floral scales conspicuously spirally arranged, somewhat appressed to loose at maturity, ovate to widely ovate, 5.1-5.7(-6) x (3-) 3.2-4(-4.3) mm, cartilaginous, stramineous, adaxially red-maculate, the distal 0.2-0.3 mm translucent and hyaline-erose, the central area nearly flat, the apex obtuse to rounded (the cartilaginous region appearing acute), abaxially coarsely many-veined, the veins raised and visible at 20x, only the mid-vein distinguishable in adaxial view. Flowers with 6-7 perianth bristles, these unequal (some greatly reduced), stiff, short, 0.4-0.7(-0.9) times achene length, irregularly spinulose, the spinules mostly spreading (a few retrorse or antrorse), stramineous or sometimes colorless, usually a conspicuously forked bristle present adaxially; stamens 3; anthers (1.5-)1.9-2.6 mm long, reddish brown; style trifid. Achenes biconvex, broadly ovoid to obovoid, 1.8-2.1 (-2.2) x 1.4-1.6(-1.7) mm, with (17-)18-22 longitudinal rows of concave transversely oblong polygonal cells visible through transparent periclinal layer on each achene face, dull, light brown splotched with amber maturing to cinnamon brown, the apex constricted to a distinct neck about 0.5-0.6 times the width of achene. Tubercle lamelliform, deltate, 0.7-0.9 x 0.8-0.9(-1) mm, dark brown.

description: Perennial herb 1.1-1.4 m tall; stems cylindrical, 0.4-0.8 mm diam., glabrous. Leaves of the vegetative stem 12-16(-18) x 2.5-4.6(-6) cm, resupinate, membranaceous to chartaceous, distributed along the upper half of the stem, elliptic, apex acute or acuminate, base attenuate, both surfaces glabrous, veins promiment; leaves of the floral stem 3.5-7 x 0.3-0.7 cm, resupinate, membranaceous, sparsely distributed along the stem, linear, apex acuminate or cuspidate, base cuneate, both surfaces glabrous. Inflorescence a congested umbel-like simple cyme with 5-10 flowers; pedicels glabrous, 2.5-7 cm long; bracts leaf-like, membranaceous, 2-7.5 x 0.2-0.4 cm, linear. Flower patent, campanulate, red to orange, 3-4 cm long. Tepals 6 in two whorls; outer tepals ruby-maculated, all three very similar, elliptic, apically acuminate, basally attenuate; distal margin entire; upper tepal ca. 2.5 x 1 cm; lower two ca. 2.2 x 0.7 cm; inner tepals ruby-maculated and striped, all three very similar, spatulate, apically cuspidate, basally attenuate, distal margin entire to slightly crenulated; upper two tepals ca. 3.2 x 0.6 cm; lower tepal ca. 2.2 x 0.5 cm. Stamens 6, included, filaments glabrous, ca. 2.2 cm long; stigma included, style glabrous, ca. 2.5 cm long. Capsule not seen.

description: Solitaria vel caespitosa. Caudex erectus, 2-3.5 m altus, 2-3 cm diam. Rachis foliorum 42-50 cm longus; lamina ambitu obovata, pinnata; pinnae 2-4 in utroque latere rachidis, apicales magnae, racheos parum plus quam dimidium amplectentes, nervis primariis 10-11 percursae; reliquae uninerviae, lanceolatae, sigmoideae. Spadix simpliciter ramosus; pedunculus ut rachillae valde longus; rachis brevis. Flores masculi regulariter dispositi. Fructus subglobosus vel oblongus, 12 mm longus, 9-10 mm diam, niger.

description: Solitary or caespitose. Stem erect, 2-3.5 m high, 2-3 cm diam, green. Leaves 7-10, scattered along the upper portion of the stem; sheath 16 cm long, tubular, green, striate; petiole 5-6 cm long; rachis 42-50 cm long; blade obovate in outline, with 2-4 pinnae on each side, the apical ones very large, 10-11 nerved, occupying a little more than half of the rachis, elliptic, slightly toothed toward the apex, ca 50 cm long, 18-20 cm wide, the remaining pinnae lanceolate, sigmoid, acuminate, 25-32 cm long, 5-7 cm wide, 4-5 cm apart, uninerved with a yellow primary vein and several secondary and tertiary veins; primary veins in total 13 on each side. Inflorescence once branched; staminate inflorescence with a prophyll and 5 tubular, membranous to papyraceous, slightly striate peduncular bracts, the upper one ca 20 cm long, 1 cm wide; peduncle 72 cm long, 3 mm wide; rachis 7-8 cm long; rachillae 14, very long and slender, to 30 cm long, 1 mm diam, pendulous and rigid; staminate flowers regularly arranged on a rather lax spiral, dark when dried, ovate to oblong, 3-3.5 mm long; calyx 1.5 mm high, trilobate, lobes broadly rounded, 1.5 mm wide; petals valvate, coherent at apex, lanceolate, thick, 3 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide; filaments 1 mm long; anthers straight, oblong, ca 2 mm long, white when fresh; pistillode columnar, subcapitate at apex, as long as the stamens. Pistillate inflorescence green at anthesis, red when mature and fresh; prophyll and 5 peduncular bracts similar in shape and size to those of the staminate inflorescence; peduncle 60-70 cm long, ca 4 mm wide; rachis 6-13 cm long; rachillae 11-14, rigid, 16-20 cm long, 1.5 mm diam; pistillate flowers superficially and laxly disposed, ovoid, 1.8-2.5 mm long, dark when dried; calyx cupulate, 1.3 mm long, trilobate, lobes broadly rounded; petals imbricate, broadly ovate, thick and acute at apex, ca 2.5 mm long; gynoecium ellipsoid, 2.2 mm long, briefly trilobate at apex. Fruits subglobose to oblong, 12 mm long, 9-10 mm diam, black when mature; stigmatic residue basal; seed oblong, brown, 10 mm long, 8 mm diam.

description: Leaf-blades 2-4 mm wide, 3-6 mm long, on petioles 10-13 mm long, prominently crenate with usually 2 recessed callose-glandular teeth on each side; upper (adaxial) surface very slightly roughened (as seen under a rragnification of 20 times), the lower surface smooth; flower about 10 mm long; corolla white [according to Wimmer the upper lobes white, the lower white with two violet dots, the throat yellow with violet dots], 9 mm long, the tube 5.5-6 mm long or slightly shorter at the dorsal sinus, narrowly funnelform, about 1 mm wide at the base and 2 mm wide at the summit; dorial lobes about 1.5 mm wide, 3.5 mm long; filament-tube 6.5-7 mm long, free from the corolla except at the base (or apparently adnate along the dorsal side in the proximal half); anther-tube 1.7-2 mm long; calyx-lobes erect, broadly linear, entire, or with 1 or 2 teeth on each side, blunt-tipped, the tips spreading; dorsal lobe about 1 mm wide, 2.5-3 mm long; seeds not seen.

description: Tiny plants 1 cm high, in mats among moss; leaf-blades up to 1 mm wide, 1.5-2.5 mm long, on petioles 2-4 mm long, entire or with 1 or sometimes 2 scarcely recessed callose teeth on each side; upper surface mrarkedly papillose-roughened, the lower surface smooth; flowers about 8 mm long, the corolla white (Pennell), 7 mm long; tube 5 mm long with narrowly cylindric base, and this abruptly expanded into a funnelform throat 1.5 mm long; dorsal lobes 1 mm wide, 1.8 mm long; filament-tube about 5 mm long, adnate to the corolla-tube except in the expanded throat; anther-tube 0.8 mm long; calyx-lobes erect, triangular-linear, callose-tipped, entire or with one tooth on each side near the base, the dorsal 0.8 mm long in flower, 1.3 mm long in fruit; seeds 0.8 mm long, ellipsoid with blunt ends, the surface with pale cellular network.

description: Leaves in outline oblanceolate to obovate, sinuately toothed to bipinnatifid, usually with evident distinction between the elliptic blade and the elongate, dilated base; leaf as a whole 3-10 mm wide at the widest point, (10-) 25-60 (-80) mm long, (2-) 4-8 (-12) times as long as wide, the blade often about half the length of the entire leaf, blunt or rounded at the tip, attenuate at the base; leaf-margins in most plants tending to be pinnatifid, the teeth callose-tipped and some of them usually standing well out beyond the edge of the blade, even in nearly entire leaves; corolla 1.5-2.5 cm long, the tube 10-16 mm long; corollalobes usually with some long slender hairs on the inner surface and at the summit of the throat; filament-tube 11-18 mm long; capsule a little more than half-inferior, the lower part 2-3 mm in diameter, 2.5-3 mm long, somewhat compressed tangentially, on a stout somewhat compressed pedicel 1-1.5 mm wide, 1040 mm long; calyx-lobes 1.2-2 (-3) mm long, entire or toothed; seed fusiform, 1.3-1.6 mm long, with minute longitudinal cellular markings.

description: Leaves about 0.7 mm wide, 2.7-3.2 mm long, bearing 10-15 cilia along each margin, and a cluster of similar cilia at the tip; cilia stiff and erect, evenly distributed along the margins, clustered at the tip and on the dorsal surface near the tip, diminishing in frequency to the middle of the leaf, and mostly wanting below this except along the margins; flowers subsessile or (usually) the pedicels 2-4 mm long at least in fruit; corolla 1.6-2 mm long, the lobes sparingly ciliate at the tips; tube narrowly funnelform, 1.1-1.3 mm long (0.4-0.6 mm long to the dorsal sinus); dorsal lobes 0.4-0.6 mm long; filaments 1 mm long or less, adnate to the corolla at the base; anthers 0.6-0.8 mm long; hypanthium in fruit obconic, 1-1.5 mm wide and long, attenuate into the slender pedicel; calyx-lobes about 0.7 mm wide at the base, the dorsal one 1.2-1.5 mm long in fruit; seeds not angled.

description: Aerial stems 1-7 per rootstock, apparently annual, slender, erect, sparsely branched, (7)15-25(30) cm long, 0.7-2 mm diam. at base, sparsely to densely hirsute-velutinous; stem trichomes uniseriate, multicellular, white, occasionally with yellowish deposits at crosswalls, 1.3-2.3 mm long. Cyathia on distal and sometimes basal to middle portions of stems; solitary, in dichasial or pseudomonopodial positions; peduncles 2-5(13) mm long; involucre campanulate or sometimes hemispherical, externally short hirsute velutinous, 1.3-1.6(2.1) X 1.6- 2(2.6) mm at mouth; primary lobes 5, keeled, entire, white ciliate; glands 4, transversely ob- long, drying light to dark brown to green, densely white ciliate on inner side; gland bas- es short hirsute-velutinous; appendages obovate-rounded, unequal (to somewhat larger), 1-2.5 mm long, planar, perpendicular to rim of cyathium, glabrous, repand to erose, white (sometimes pink). Staminate flowers ca. 30. Pistillate flower with gynophore 2.3 mm long at maturity, short hirsute-velutinous; ovary pubescence short, uniseriate, multicellular white hirsute-velutinous; styles 1 mm long, glabrous to sparsely short hirsute-velutinous, connate basally, lower portion erect, bifid for 1/3 of length, tips recurved; stigmas clavate. Capsule hirsute-velutinous, 2.7-3.3 mm X 3- 3.3 mm wide; trichomes short, uniseriate, multicellular, white. Seed subovoid, ± tetragonal, 1.8 X 1.1 mm, rugose-punctate, brown; base truncate.

description: Fruit ovoid, 30 mm diam., 55 mm long, with pericarp 2.4 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-as in the following genera, fibrous bundles are short, oblique, embed- ded in a mass of brachysclereids, and located just below the outer epidermis; further characterized by the presence of additional, larger brachysclereids scattered just below the outer mantle, scattered clusters of tanniniferous cells in the inner pericarp, by a thick zone of sclerified parenchyma surrounding the inner vascular bundles, which are moderately flattened and have thick fibrous sheaths, and by a moderately thick locular epidermis.

description: Trees up to 15-25(30) m tall, with small butresses; bark deeply fissured, fibrous; wood yellow and extremely hard. Young leafy branchlets 4-8 mm thick, semi-succulent, terete to subterete, glabrous; older branches smooth, grayish pale brown. No lenticels seen. Stipules connate at base and not contorted in bud, often connected to petioles, deltoid and not acuminate, glabrous outside, microscopically (40X) ciliolate, glabrous with a basal triangular area of colleters inside, 8.5-9 mm long, 6.5-10 mm wide at base, subcaducous, reddish green, leaving a scar encircling the stem and connected to the petiole scar, 1-2 mm wide. Blades (7)12-23 cm long, (4)8-13 cm wide, length: width 1.5-1.7:1, pandurate, obtuse to rounded at base, concave at basal area, obtuse at apex, acumen absent; dark green above and pale green below, semi coriaceous; drying reddish brown, semi leathery to leathery; glabrous above and below. Primary and secondary veins glabrous and prominent below, secondary veins 7- 10 each side; tertiary veins subparallel throughout. Petioles 6-12 mm long, 2-3 mm thick, terete to adaxially flattened or narrowly concave, glabrous. Domatia absent. Inflorescences 2 per node, corymbose and densely branched distally, with opposite to subopposite decussate branches terminating into cymules, forming a continu- ous flowering plane; 9.5-15 cm long, 7.5- 11 cm wide, lateral branches 1-2 pairs, basal portion of axis not branched, 4.5-7.5 cm long. Rachis basally subterete and distally decussately compressed, rachis and branch- es white or golden minute-puberulent; flowers on distal branches in condensed cymules. Distal bracts absent or extremely reduced, deltoid to linear, up to 4 mm long and up to 1 mm wide; bracteoles subtending the flowers absent or reduced to microscopic scales. Flowers very fragrant, sessile to short-pedicellate, pedicel 0-1.5 mm long, puberulent; hypanthium narrowly obconi- cal, 1-1.5 mm long, ca. 1 mm wide, pu- berulent. Calyx truncate to short-lobed, 0.4- 0.8 mm long, 1.3-2 mm wide, golden puberulent, pale green; calyx lobes barely distinguishable, 0-0.5 mm long, in some flowers one lobe of the calyx expanded into a calycophyll. Calycophylls ovate to elliptic; blades 3.2-5 cm long and 1.6-3 cm wide, with peltate venation, pale green to white; petioles 1.5-2 cm long. Corolla funnelform and deeply lobed, 3.5-4.5 mm long, white to greenish white; tube short cy- lindrical, 1.5-2.5 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm wide, glabrous outside and inside; corolla lobes 5, reflexed at anthesis, 2-2.5 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm wide at base, narrowly oblong with acute apex, glabrous outside, with a basal area white-pilose and with distal zone glabrous inside. Stamens 5, obviously exserted, equal length; filaments attached 1-2 mm from the base of the tube; anthers elliptic, 0.6-0.7 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide, dorsifixed at medial zone, base rounded, apex acute to short mucronate; filaments 3.5-5 mm long, terete, basally flat- tened and connate to throat, sparsely white pilose at base. Style exserted, 5-6 mm long, terete, densely strigose, adpressed-retrorse; style branches extruding as two lips above corolla before anthesis, oblate, 0.3-0.6 mm long, stigmatic surface microscopically (40X) papillose. Capsules narrowly obconical to turbinate, acute at base, rounded at apex, 3.5-4.5 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, capsule rust-brown, densely golden puber- ulent, without lenticels; disk white-pubescent, not exceeding the calyx; disk-loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules. Seeds with central hilum, with fringed concentric wing, 8-12 wide including wing.

description: Arbor ad 6 m. alta et 5 cm. diametro, glabra inflorescentiis exceptis, ramulis subteretibus, nitidis, rubro-fuscis, stipulis depresso-rotundatis, mucrone 0.8-1.2 mm. longo terminatis; petioli 1 mm. longi, foliorum laminae 4.5-8 cm. longae, 3-5.5 cm. latae, rigido-coriaceae, ovatae, ad basim cordatae, ad apicem gradatim vel subabrupte acutae, extremitate obtusa, margine revolutissimo et integro, ad faciem su- periorem costa et venis primariis fortissime impressis, infra fortissime salientibus, supra nervis caeteris impressis, subsalientibus infra, venis primariis in paribus 6-7 spatio ab margine ca. 5 mm. anastomosantibus; inflorescentiae paniculatae, 6.5-8.5 cm. longae, axillares, ramis pedicellisque pilis rfiinutis rectis vestitis, pedunculis 2.5-5 mm. longis, pedicellis 1.5-2.5 mm. longis; calyx carnosus, 4(-5)-lobatus, lobis ovatis, 1-1.5 mm. longis, 1 mm. latis, ad apicem acutis, corolla quadri- vel quinquelobata, dilute flava, 7 mm. longa, ad fauces 4.5 mm. lata, infundibularis, lobis rotundatis, in alabastro clavato leviter imbricatis, 1.5 mm. longis, 1.8 mm. latis; stamina 4 (vel 5), inclusa, ad basim corollae in- serta, antheris linearibus, 3-3.3 mm. longis, filamentis filiformibus, ad basim in tubo connatis 0.6 mm. longis, villosis basi apiceque exceptis; stigma simplex, obtusum, nonnihil angulare, papillosum, stylus 5.5-6 mm. longus, 0.3 mm. diametro, teres, discus depressus, annularis, 0.7 mm. diametro, ovarium 1.5 mm. altum, ca. 1 mm. diametro, cellis duobus, utroque unum ovulum pendulum gignenti; fructus immaturus purpureus, fructus maturus drupaceus, ovalis, lateraliter depressus, 6 mm. longus, 5 mm. latus, externe carnosus, endocarpio crustoso-cartilagineo; semen unum, 5 mm. longum, 3 mm. latum, planum, oblongo-ovale, diluto-fuscum, reticulatum, ad marginem crassius; germen rectum, 2 mm. longum, cotyledonibus orbicularibus, radice 1.5 mm. longo.

description: Gramen perenne, caespites 20-50 cm altos formans. Folia per complementum 5-9; laminae ovato- lanceolatae, acuminatae, 5.5-7 cm longae, 2.1-2.6 cm latae, ad basin asymmetricae; vaginae margi- nibus ciliatae; pseudopetiolus 1.5-2.0 mm longus, pilis densis adpressis pubescens. Spiculae femineae lanceolatae, 13.1-14.4 mm longae, 3 mm latae; inter glumas anthoeciumque internodium nullum; gluma infera 9-nervia, supera 7-9 nervia; lemma 7.3-8.1 mm longum, dorsaliter papillosum, ventraliter marginibus pubescens. Spiculae masculae 4-4.5 mm longae.

description: Perennial in cespitose clumps with 4 or 5 culms in a fascicle. Culms unbranched, erect to geniculate-ascending, 2-5 dm tall, cylindrical, glabrous to sparsely pubescent just below the nodes, the nodes thickened, dark, glabrous or pubescent along a line; internodes hollow. Leaves 5-9 per complement, drooping, rarely ascending in the upper part; blade ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, 5.5-7 cm long, 2.1-2.6 cm wide, asymmetric at the base, greenish, glabrous with an inconspicuous median nerve and scabrous margins; pseudopetiole 1.5-2 mm long, densely pilose with thick appressed hairs; sheath with ciliate margins, otherwise glabrous; ligule an inconspicuous, membranous-ciliate rim, 0.3-0.5 mm long, brown. Inflorescences numerous from the upper nodes with several produced at each, the prophylla conspicuous, villous. Panicles 1.4-2.5 cm long with ca 8-10 male spikelets below the single terminal female spikelet or the panicle with male spikelets only; axis angular, hispid, the male spikelets in pairs or in 3's on hispid club-shaped pedicels, the female on thick, hispid pedicels flattened on one side. Female spikelets fusiform, subulate, 13.1-14.4 mm long, 3 mm wide, glabrous, whitish, internode absent between the glumes and anthecium; glumes subequal, strongly nerved and longer than the anthecium; lower glume subulate, 9-nerved with transverse veinlets, scabrous toward the summit of both surfaces, otherwise glabrous; upper glume acute to acuminate, 12-13 mm long, 7-9-nerved with transverse veinlets, scabrous toward the tip on both surfaces, otherwise glabrous; anthecium ellipsoid, 7.3-8.1 mm long, 2.5-2.9 mm wide, stramineous to brown, densely pubescent at the base of the ventral surface, lemma pubescent along the borders of the ventral surface and with sparse hairs at the tip on the back; palea smooth or with sparse papillae toward the apex; lodicules 3, 0.4 mm long; ovary glabrous with a single long flattened and glabrous style terminating in 2 plumose stigmas. Male spikelets long-ellipsoid, 4-4.5 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, whitish, scabrous; glumes lacking; lemma acute, 3-nerved, with transverse veinlets toward the apex, scabrous; palea 4-4.5 mm long, 2-nerved, glabrous; anthers 3, 2 mm long. Fruit a brown caryopsis with a linear hilum extending its length.

description: Perennial grass in cespitose clumps with usually 12-14 culms in a fascicle, found on shaded, rocky ledges of humid forests above mountain stream. Culms un- branched, erect or spreading, thin, 22-27 cm tall, internodes solid, the lowest short (ca 1 cm long), followed by two elongate ones (5-11 cm long), and a series of short ones with imbricate sheaths (the leaf complement), the internodes slightly sulcate-ridged, glabrous and shiny throughout except for a round spot of different texture just below the succeeding node, glabrous; exposed nodes 3, prominent. Leaves below the leaf complement consisting of a sheath only or sheath with a rudimentary blade, much shorter than the internode, the strong nerves stramineous, internerves green-mottled, glabrous or sparingly papillose-pilose toward the summit. Leaves 10-22 per complement: blades linear-lanceolate with an acute tip and symmetric base, 4-5 x 0.5-0.8 cm, glabrous on the upper surface, pilose on the lower, the margins serrate; midrib prominent on the upper surface, thickened at the base and terminating nerves 2 or 3 on each side of the midrib, manifest only on the lower surface, not connected by manifest transverse veinlets. Sheaths strongly ribbed, green-mottled, pilose on the upper half or third. Petiole ca 1 mm long, sparsely pilose below, densely so above. Ligule ca 0.4 mm long, a thin, truncate membrane with a ciliolate margin. Inflorescences borne at the lowermost and uppermost nodes of the leaf complement with as many as 7 or 8 panicles issuing from the mouth of the sheath accompanied by prophylla that extend just a little beyond the sheath, these glabrous except for a few appressed hairs toward the apex. Panicle erect, narrow, ca 5 cm long, the peduncle up to 4 cm long, mostly enclosed within the subtending sheath, the panicle consisting of a single large terminal 9 spikelet and pedicelled 9 spikelets below, these usually 8-10 in number and mostly in pairs, one long-pedicellate, the other short-pedicellate, or with the [female] spikelet lacking and only [male] spikelets present. Spikelets unisexual, dimorphous, and 1-flowered, the axis greatly thickened below the [female] spikelet, the glabrous pedicels only slightly thickened below the [female] spikelets. Male spikelets caducous, the [female] glumes falling at the same time or after the anthecium matures. [female] spikelet obovate-lanceolate, 9.6-11 mm long, whitish; glumes subequal, exceeding the anthecium by about half its length, obovate- lanceolate, long-attenuate, the upper margins folding inward to form a more or less apiculate tip, membranous, glabrous; lower glume 10-nerved, with a few transverse veinlets; upper glume a little shorter than the lower, 8-nerved, with a few transverse veinlets. Lemma 6.5-6.8 mm long, ovate, apiculate, 5-nerved, at first fleshy, becoming hard and whitish and shiny at maturity, with pale brown mottling, densely pilose on the lower half of the back and front and along the margins and apex, the hairs white. Palea 6.1 mm long, of the same texture as the lemma, lanceolate, 4-nerved, not keeled, at first fleshy and becoming indurate and whitish and shiny at maturity, partially enclosed in the overlapping margins of the lemma, glabrous except for a few long hairs between the central pair of nerves above. Lodicules 3, ca 0.68 mm long, one median and posterior, the other two lateral and anterior, more or less truncate, moderately thick and fleshy throughout, vascularized. Gynoecium: ovary glabrous; style 1, long, flat and ribbonlike; stigmas 2, plumose. Caryopsis more or less ovoid-spherical, with a linear hilum extending its whole length, ca 4 mm long. o spikelet linear-lanceolate, 3.4-4.3 mm long. Glumes lacking. Lemma and palea membranous, acute, about equal in length, glabrous. Lemma 3-nerved. Palea 2-nerved. Lodicules all about the same size, shape, and texture, resembling those of the [male] spikelet, ca 0.4 mm long. Androecium: stamens 3, anthers yellow, 1.5 mm long, the filaments attached about 1/4 from the base.

description: Gramen cespitosum culmis 30-35 cm altis. Folia ascendentia laminae glabrae, 8-14 X 1.5-3 cm, lanceolatae, basi asymmetricae, apice acutae; vaginae secus marginem lateralem ciliatae secus marginem superum sericeae; petiolus 1-2 mm longus utrinque sericeus. Spicula [female] ovato-lanceolata, 1.3-2.2 cm longa, viridula vel albida; glumae subaequilongae quam anthoecium multo longiores, infernae 9-1 1-nervatae, superiores 8- vel 9-nervatae; lemma 8.5-10.3 mm longum, 5-nervatum, indurescens, albidum, ex parte pilosum aliter glabrum nitidumque; palea ca 8 mm longa, multinervata, indurescens; lodiculae 1.1-1.2 mm longae. Spicula [male] 3.2-6.4 mm longa; lodiculae 0.3-0.4 mm longae; antherae 1.9-2 mm longae.

description: Perennial grass in cespitose clumps with usually 6-12 culms in a fascicle' found in shaded, sloping sites of protected places at the base of trees. Culms unbranched, erect or geniculate-ascending, 30-35 cm tall; internodes solid, slightly sulcate- ridged, glabrous and shiny throughout except for an oval or elliptical spot of different texture toward the summit just below the succeeding node, this frequently (at least when young) covered by short dense appressed hairs; exposed nodes 3-6, prominent, the lower part of the node a thickened ridge. Leaves of the basal 2 or 3 nodes consisting of a sheath only or with a rudimentary blade; midculm and lower-culm sheaths shorter than the internode, glabrous except for the densely ciliate overlapping margin and the sericeous upper margin. Sheaths of the leaf complement imbricate, longer than the internodes, similar to those below or with some additional sparse hairs toward the summit. Ligule ca 0.8 mm long, somewhat thick, ciliate. Petiole ca 1-2 mm long, sericeous on both surfaces. Blade ascending, 8-14 cm long, 1.5-3 cm wide, lanceolate, strongly asymmetric at the base and evenly narrowed to an acute apex, glabrous on both surfaces, the margins serrulate becoming ciliate with brown hairs at the tip; midrib on both surfaces thickened at the base and terminating abruptly in a knoblike process above the petiole; primary nerves 4 on each side of the midrib, secondary nerves 4-8 between each of these; nerves not connected by manifest transverse veinlets. Inflorescences borne at any of the nodes except the lowest, with as many as 8 panicles issuing from the mouth of the sheath, accompanied by prophylla that extend a little beyond the sheath, these villous with rufous hairs. Panicle erect, narrow, 4-8 cm long, the lower half (peduncle) enclosed in the subtending sheath, consisting of a single large terminal [female] spikelet and pedicelled [male] spikelets below, usually in pairs, sometimes the [female] spikelet lacking and up to 20 or more [male] spikelets present in a narrow panicle. Spikelets unisexual, dimorphous, and 1-flowered, the axis greatly thickened below the [female] spikelet, the antrorsely scaberulous pedicels only slightly thickened below the [male] spikelets. [male] spikelets caducous, the [female] glumes falling at the same time or after mature anthecium shed. [female] spikelet 1.3-2.2 cm long, pale green or almost whitish; glumes subequal, exceeding the anthecium by about half its length, ovate- lanceolate, long-attenuate, membranous, glabrous; lower glume 9- to 11-nerved, with a few transverse veinlets, the tip antrorsely scaberulous; upper glume about equal in size and shape to the lower, 8- or 9-nerved, with a few transverse veinlets. Lemma 8.5-10.3 mm long, ovate-lanceolate, apiculate, 5-nerved, at first fleshy, becoming hard, pale green and mottled at maturity, with patches of appressed brownish-white silky hairs between the nerves on the back at the base and upper part and along the margins that overlap the palea and on the tip, otherwise glabrous and shining. Palea ca 8 mm long, of the same texture as the lemma, linear- lanceolate, faintly 9- or 10-nerved, at first fleshy, becoming hard and white at maturity, appressed pubescent on the upper third of the dorsal side, otherwise glabrous and shining. Lodicules 3, 1.1-1.2 mm long, one median and posterior, the other two lateral and anterior, obliquely truncate, moderately thick throughout. Gynoecium: ovary glabrous; style single, long, flat and ribbonlike; stigmas 2, plumose. Caryopsis with a linear hilum extending its whole length. [male] spikelet linear-lanceolate, 3.2-6.4 mm long. Glumes not developed. Lemma and palea membranous, awn-tipped, about equal in length, glabrous or antrorsely scaberulous. Lemma 3-nerved. Palea 2-nerved. Lodicules 3, in one verticil, similar to those of the [female] spikelet except slightly smaller, 0.3-0.4 mm long. Androecium: stamens 3, anthers yellow, 1.9-2 mm long, the filaments attached about 1/4-1/3 from the base.

description: Perennial grass in small cespitose clumps, with 5-10 culms in a fascicle, found in shaded gallery forests. Culms unbranched, lax or geniculate-erect, to 27 cm tall, internodes solid, the lowest short (1-2 cm long) internode followed by 2 longer ones (2-6 cm long), with a sheath only or rudimentary or reduced blade, and the following internodes with fully developed leaves, the culm ridged and furrowed, glabrous, stramineous; exposed nodes 3 or 4. Leaves below the leaf complement consisting of a sheath only or sheath with a rudimentary blade, much shorter than the internode, strongly nerved, stramineous, glabrous. Leaves 5-8 per complement with several of the lower sheaths shorter than the internode: blades narrowly obovate-lanceolate gradually narrowed to an acute tip and asymmetric at the base, 4-5 cm x 0.8-1 cm, glabrous on both surfaces, the margins antrorsely ciliolate; midrib prominent on both surfaces, the upper one thickened at the base and terminating abruptly in a knoblike process above the petiole, primary nerves 2 or 3 on each side of the midrib, clearer on the lower surface, not connected by manifest transverse veinlets. Sheaths strongly ribbed, stramineous. Petiole ca 1 mm long or less, dark brown on both surfaces, glabrous below and with a few erect hairs above. Ligule 0.6 mm long or less, a thin + truncate membrane with a ciliolate margin. Inflorescences borne from the middle nodes with usually 3 or 4 panicles issuing from the mouth of the sheath accompanied by glabrous prophylla that extend just shortly beyond the sheath. Panicles erect, narrow, 4-5 cm long, the long peduncle exserted from the subtending sheath, spreading outward, panicle consisting of a single large terminal 9 spikelet and below this 1 or 2 single and 2 or 3 pairs of 9 spikelets, one short-pedicellate, the other long-pedicellate. Spikelets unisexual, dimorphous and 1-flowered, the axis greatly thickened below the [female] spikelets, the glabrous pedicels only slightly thickened below the [male] spikelets. [male] spikelets caducous, the [female] glumes falling at the same time or after the anthecium matures. [female] spikelet obovate-lanceolate, ca 8.5 mm long, whitish; glumes unequal, the lower longer than the upper and both exceeding the anthecium by a little; lower glume obovate-lanceolate gradually narrowing to an attenuate-curving tip, 5- or 6-nerved, with a few transverse veinlets; upper glume shorter than the lower, 5- or 6-nerved, with a few transverse veinlets. Lemma ca 5 mm long, ovate- elliptic with a cucullate tip, 5-nerved, the nerves connected by transverse veinlets, the lemma at first fleshy, becoming hard and whitish and shiny at maturity, mostly glabrous on the back except for a few hairs toward the summit, densely pilose at the base toward the front and all along the margins that face the palea, glabrous at the very tip. Palea 4.5 mm long, of the same texture as the lemma, obovate- lanceolate, with 2 major nerves, the palea at first fleshy and becoming indurate and whitish and shiny at maturity, partially enclosed in the overlapping margins of the lemma, pilose at the apex, otherwise glabrous. Lodicules 3, ca 0.5 mm long, one median and posterior, the other two lateral and anterior, more or less truncate, moderately thick and fleshy throughout, vascularized. Gynoecium: ovary glabrous; style 1, long, flat and ribbonlike; stigmas 2, very plumose. Caryopsis not seen. [male] spikelet linear-lanceolate, 3.7-4 mm long. Glumes lacking. Lemma and palea membranous, acute, about equal in length, glabrous. Lemma obovate-lanceolate, broadly acute, with 3 strong nerves and an additional pair connected by transverse veinlets. Palea linear-lanceolate, 2-nerved. Lodicules all about the same size, shape and texture, resembling those of the [female] spikelet except thinner, ca 0.5 mm long. Androecium: stamens 3, anthers yellow, 1.8-2 mm long, the filaments attached about 1/4 to 1/5 from the base.

description: Gramen perenne, caespites 30-40 cm altos formans. description: Perennial in cespitose clumps with usually 10-12 culms in a fascicle. Culms unbranched, erect or geniculate-ascending, 3-4 dm tall; internodes hollow, com- pressed, shiny, with a line of pubescence along one side and a spot of different texture toward the summit just below the node; exposed nodes 3 or 4, dark brown, short-pilose on one side, formed of the thickened basal rim of the sheath above and the thickened upper rim of the internode below. Leaves of the basal nodes consisting of a sheath only or sheath with rudimentary blade, the sheaths shorter than the internodes. Foliage leaves 4-8 per complement; blade linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 10-14.5 cm long, 0.8-1.3 cm wide, ascending, pale green and short-pilose on both surfaces, the hairs appressed, the midrib thickened toward the base on the adaxial surface, scabrous along the margins; pseudopetiole 2 mm long, brown, densely pilose, with long and thick golden hairs on both surfaces; sheath short-pubescent along the margins, more densely so toward the summit, longer than the internodes; ligule a thin membrane with a ciliolate margin, 0.5-0.7 mm long. Inflorescences borne at the lower and upper nodes of the culm with up to 4 from each node. Panicles erect, narrow, 1.5-2 cm long, with a single large terminal female spikelet and ca 8 male spikelets in pairs below, one short-pedi- cellate, the other long-pedicellate or with the female spikelet lacking and only male spikelets present; axis angular, short-pilose; pedicels of the female spikelets thickened, short-pilose, those of the male spikelets slightly thickened, short-pilose. Female spikelets lanceolate, long-attenuate, 18-20 mm long, 2.1-2.9 mm wide, glabrous, whitish; glumes subequal, membranous, exceeding the anthecium in length; lower glume 9-nerved, with transverse veinlets, scabrous toward the tip; upper glume 16-18 mm long, 9- or 10-nerved, with transverse veinlets, glabrous; anthecium lanceolate, acuminate, 10.8-12.6 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, whitish, with a prominent internode below; lemma 7-nerved, at first fleshy, becoming indurate, smooth, shiny, covered with appressed, white, silky, flat hairs at the base and borders on the ventral side, more sparsely so on the dorsal view; palea of the same texture as the lemma, faintly 8- or 9-nerved, densely pilose with flat hairs at the middle, otherwise glabrous, smooth; lodicules 3, ca 1 mm long, obliquely truncate; ovary glabrous with a single long style; stigmas 2, plumose. Male spikelets lanceolate, acuminate, 5-6.7 mm long, 0.7 mm wide, whitish, scabrous, membranous; lemma 5-nerved, scabrous, more so toward the apex; palea 5-6 mm long, acute, 2-nerved; anthers 3, 1.7 mm long, attached toward the base. Fruit not known.

description: Plants perennial, tufted; culms erect, 40- 70 cm tall, sometimes branching above the base when growing up through shrubbery; internodes terete, glabrous to minutely puberulent. Leaves basal to usually cauline. Sheaths longer than the internodes, gla- brous or scaberulous except for the summit, rounded on the back; collars with a conspicuous tuft of cobwebby hairs at the corners, the hairs often reflexed; throat glabrous or minutely puberulent. Ligules a minute fringe of hairs. Blades usually tightly rolled or occasionally loosely folded when fresh, to 18 cm long, 0.5-0.7 mm wide (rolled), glabrous abaxially, minutely scaberulous adaxially. Panicles narrow and contracted to open and diffuse, 9-19 cm long, the nodes glabrous; primary branches appressed to spreading from the main axis, 2-6 cm long; pulvini absent to present. Spikelets and pedicels appressed to widely spreading from the branchlets, the spikelets generally rather widely spaced and overlapping 1/2 or less their lengths at mid-panicle. Glumes brown or tan when mature, subequal or the first slightly shorter, 1-nerved, first glume 4-11 mm long, second glume 5-13.5 mm long. Lemmas glabrous to scaberulous upward, often mottled, 8-13 mm long; beak somewhat narrowed and often twisted, usually extending past the glumes, 2-4 mm long; awns essentially single; central awn well-developed, 5-12 mm long, often horizontal when mature; lateral awns highly reduced, 0-3 mm long, erect; callus 0.5-1 mm long with stiff hairs to 1 mm long. Paleas completely enclosed by the lemmas, 2-nerved, hyaline, rounded, much shorter than lemmas and slightly shorter than the lodicules. Stamens 3, anthers 1.4- 2 mm long. Lodicules 2, flabellate. Cary- opses fusiform, brownish, 5-9 mm long.

description: Plants perennial, usually densely tufted; culms erect, 15-60(75) cm tall, only rarely branching above the base; internodes terete, glabrous to minutely puberulent. description: Erect, caespitose perennial 50-80 cm tall. Culms simple, glabrous, with glabrous nodes. Leaf sheaths striate, glabrous or sparsely pilose, margins sparsely pilose.
