description: Culms (0.2)0.4-2.5 cm diam., (0.6)2- 4(5) m tall, erect at the base and arching or scrambling above. Internodes 4-14 cm long, deeply sulcate above the bud/branch complement, becoming more shallowly sulcate to flattened above for the full length, glabrous or hirsute for 0.5-2 cm below the nodal line or hirsute for nearly the full length. Culm leaves (12)13.5-33 cm long, extending past the next node, often extending for two internode lengths, loosely wrapped around the culm, usually deciduous, brittle, the juncture of the sheath and blade abaxially obscure; sheaths 11-24.5 cm long, 3-10(22) times longer than the blade, abaxially retrorsely scabrous but glabrous toward the summit and densely hirsute toward the base, sometimes scabrous only on the lower 1/3 and hirsute only at the base or scabrid and hirsute only at the base, no median nerve visible, the margins slight- ly scarious, glabrous, not fused at the base; blades 0.7-5.7 cm long, triangular, erect, persistent, abaxially pubescent, adaxially densely pubescent, sometimes only on the apical half, the apex subulate, the margins slightly scarious, glabrous; girdle ca. 1.5 mm wide, hirsute; inner ligule 0.5-2 mm long, chartaceous, marginally ciliate. Nodes at mid-culm with one triangular central bud subtended by 18-32 smaller subsidiary buds in usually 3 constellate rows; nodal line nearly horizontal, dipping only slightly below the bud/branch complement; supranodal ridge swollen, prominent. Branching extravaginal; central branch often developing but only after the subsidiaries; leafy subsidiary branches 80-150 per node, 5-11 cm long, ca. 1 mm diam., straight, spreading, rebranching from the very base but not above. Foliage leaves 3-4 per complement; sheaths striate, pubescent between the nerves, the summit prolonged on each side for 1-4(7) mm, usually to 1 mm on one side and 3-4(7) mm on the other, adnate to the inner ligule and apically ciliate, the margins usually glabrous, rarely sparsely ciliate; blades (7.5)8.5-16(19) cm long, (0.15)0.2-0.3 cm wide, L:W = 43-82(104), linear, stiff, adaxially glabrous or a few nerves (including the midrib) with prominent prickles along their length, not tessel- late, abaxially glabrous but the nerves with fine prickles along their full length, not tessellate or weakly so, usually somewhat glaucous, the nerves projecting on both surfaces, with the midrib somewhat more prominent than the rest, the apex tapering, subulate, the base attenuate, the margins usually sparsely and irregularly denticulate; pseudopetiole region 1-2 mm long but indistinct; outer ligule 0.1-0.2 mm long, glabrous; inner ligule 1-3 mm long, asymmetrical. Inflorescence 6-10.5 cm long, paniculate, narrow, the base retained within the subtending leaf sheath, without spathes; rachis angular, glabrous; branches angular, glabrous, generally ebracteate but the basalmost branch subtended (and the rachis encircled) by a glabrous papery bract 1.5-3 mm long, the basal branches 1.5-3 cm long; pedicels 1-4 mm long, angular, glabrous. Spikelets 5-6.5(7) mm long, more or less laterally compressed; glumes I and II to 0.2 mm long, forming a minute cupule at the spikelet base, sometimes appearing absent; glumes III and IV 1/2-2/3 the spikelet length, subulate, slightly navicular, abaxially gla- brous, 3- or 5-nerved, the midnerve prominent; glume III 2.4-4.2 mm long, the tip 0.3-1 mm long; glume IV 2.7-4.1 mm long, the tip 0.4-0.6(1) mm long; lemma 4.5-5.7(6.2) mm long, shortly subulate or mucronate, navicular, abaxially pubescent between the nerves toward the apex, 7- nerved, the nerves equal, becoming more prominent toward the apex; palea (4)4.4- 5.7 mm long,  bimucronulate, sometimes slightly blunted, abaxially scabrid, 4- nerved, the central 2 nerves more prominent, forming a sulcus on the upper 1/3-½, the sulcus scabrous or scabrous-pubescent. Lodicules 3, the anterior pair ca. 1 mm long, the posterior one ca. 0.6 mm long, all  apically ciliate. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5-3 mm long. Mature fruit unknown.

description: Culmi 3-5 mm diam., 1-1.5 m longi, valde arcuati. Folia culmorum 4.5-7.3 cm longa, nodum proximum non superantia, decidua; vaginae 4.3-7 cm longae, 12- 22(35)-plo longiores quam laminam, abaxialiter gla- brae; laminae 0.2-0.5 cm longae, apice mucronatae; cingulum ca. 1 mm latum, pubescens. Ramificatio extravaginalis; rami subsidiarii cujusquisque nodi 20-45, 5-9 cm longi, ca. 1 mm diam., rectivel curvati. Folia cujusquisque complementi 4-5; vaginae glabrae, apice non prolongatae; laminae 2.4-4.5 cm longae, 0.25- 0.35 cm latae, long./lat. = 10-15, glabrae, basi attenuatae. Inflorescentia 4.5-6.5 cm longa, paniculata, angusta, curvata. Spiculae 4.8-5.5 mm longae; gluma I 0.5-0.7 mm longa, 1/1o-plo longior quam spiculam, acuta; gluma II 0.8-1.3 mm longa, V5-plo longior quam spiculam, rotundata vel asymmetrica; gluma III 2.6- 3.1 mm longa, (?/2)2/3-plo longior quam spiculam, mucronata; gluma IV 2.8-3.3 mm longa, ca. 3/4-plo longior quam spiculam, mucronata; lemma 3.6-4.8 mm longum, mucronatum; palea 3.3-4.8 mm longa, sulco sca brido.

description: Culms 0.3-0.5 cm in diam., 0.5-1 m tall, erect. Internodes with the basal ones 4.5- 13.5 cm long, the distal ones 1.5-7 cm long, terete, pubescent just below the nodes, oth- erwise glabrous, more or less waxy. Culm leaves 5.5-11 cm long, persistent, abaxially glabrous, juncture of sheath and blade abaxially an obscure, inverted "V"; sheaths 3.4- 9.4 cm long, 1.6-6.2 times as long as the blade, fused for ca. 1 cm at the base, the margins glabrous; blades 0.9-2.5 cm long, triangular, erect, persistent, apex mucronate to subulate; girdle ca. 1 mm wide, glabrous; inner ligule 0.5 mm long. Nodes slightly swollen, the one triangular central bud flanked by one robust subsidiary bud on each side, these subtended by 5 or 6 tiers of smaller subsidiary buds totalling 30-60 buds; sheath scar dipping below the branch complement; supranodal ridge obscure; root primordia absent. Branching extravaginal; central bud does not develop; leafy subsidiary branches 30-60 per node, 1.5-5 cm long, horizontal to curving upwards, not rebranching. Foliage leaves 4-7 (12-15) per complement; sheaths persistent, pubescent between the nerves, glabrescent; blades 0.8 5-2 cm long, 0.1-0.2 (0.3) cm wide, L:W = 5-12, stiff, glabrous, not tessellate, apex subulate, base rounded-cuneate; pseudo- petiole 0.2-0.5 mm long; outer ligule ca. 0.1 mm long, ciliolate; inner ligule 0.2-0.5 mm long, truncate or slightly rounded. Panicles 1-1.5 cm long, narrow, the base retained within the subtending sheath; rachis angular, pubescent; branches and pedicels an- gular, pubescent, appressed, the pedicels 1- 3 mm long. Spikelets 4.7-5.5 mm long, slightly farinose when young, the anthecium 1.2-1.5 mm wide, more or less terete to slightly dorsally compressed. Glumes 2, scalelike, obtuse, abaxially scabrid-pubescent, nerves absent; glume I 0.4-0.8 mm long, less than 1/10 the spikelet length; glume 11 0.6-1.2 mm long, ca. 1/8 the spikelet length. Sterile lemmas 2, 2.9-4 mm long, subulate, abaxially scabrid-pubescent on the upper one-half, 1-, 3-, or 5-nerved; sterile lemma I 1/2-2/3 the spikelet length; sterile lemma II 3/4-4/5 the spikelet length. Fertile lemma 4.5- 5.5 mm long, mucronate, abaxially scabrid pubescent toward the apex, 5- or 7-nerved. Palea 4.5-5.3 mm long, subequal to the fertile lemma, sulcate toward the apex, bimucronulate, 4-nerved. Stamens 3, the anthers 2.5-2.7 mm long. Lodicules unknown. Fruit unknown.

description: Culms 0.7-2.5 (3) cm in diam., 1.5-4 (5) m tall, erect to somewhat arching at the apices. Internodes 9-26 cm long, more or less terete to slightly flattened above the branch complement, glabrous, waxy. Culm leaves 12.6-29 cm long, caducous, juncture of sheath and blade abaxially a more or less horizontal line or a shallow, inverted "V," obscure or distinct; sheaths 6.9-27.3 cm long, 1.2-27.5 (50) times as long as the blade, abaxially glabrous or retrorsely scabrous toward the apex or in one population densely tomentose with appressed hairs along one shoulder near the apex, the margins usually glabrous, sometimes ciliate toward the apex, often somewhat scarious; blades 0.3-5.7 (9.2) cm long, triangular, erect, persistent, rarely deciduous, abaxially and adaxially glabrous or retrorsely scabrid or abaxially glabrous and adaxially scabrid, the apex subulate; girdle (0.5) 1-2 mm wide, glabrous; inner ligule 0.5-6 mm long, irregular, ciliolate, sometimes absent. Nodes slightly swollen, the one triangular central bud sub- tended and partially encircled by 1 or 2 rows of smaller subsidiary buds in a constellate array, with usually two of the subsidiaries robust and much larger than the others; sheath scar dipping slightly below the bud complement; supranodal ridge prominent; root primordia absent. Branching modified extravaginal, the culm leaves often split at the base but falling as the branches develop; central branch 50-75 cm long, divergent, rebranching; smaller leafy subsidiary branches 15-80 per node, 6-20 cm long, divergent to ascending, occasionally rebranching, the robust subsidiary branches 2 or 3 per node, 26-100 cm long, divergent, rebranching. Foliage leaves 5-9 per com- plement; sheaths deciduous, usually uniform in color, rarely maculate with light green spots, glabrous, the margins glabrous or ciliate, scarious; blades 3.4-11.4 cm long, (0.2) 0.5-0.9 (1.2) cm wide, L:W = (4) 7.5- 24, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glabrous or less commonly pilose, not tessellate, apex subulate, base attenuate to rounded-attenuate; pseudopetiole 1-2 (3) mm long; outer ligule 0.1-0.5 (1) mm long, glabrous or ciliolate; inner ligule 0. 5-4 mm long, rounded, glabrous or abaxially pubescent at the base. Panicles 1.5-5 cm long, the mature panicle narrow or the basal branches divergent or all branches and pedicels divergent to recurved and the panicle open, the base usually retained within the subtending sheath, sometimes fully exserted; rachis angular, usually scabrous-pubescent at base, only the edges scabrous toward the apex, or less commonly completely scabrous-pubescent or completely glabrous; branches angular, usually glabrous with only the edges scabrid, sometimes completely glabrous to completely pubescent, the lower ones to 1 cm, these appressed or reflexed; pedicels 1.5 mm long, angular, glabrous, the edges scabrid, or completely pubescent, appressed or re- flexed, often slightly sinuous. Spikelets 4.3- 7.5 mm long, glabrous, sometimes slightly falcate, the anthecium 0.9-1.6 mm wide, more or less dorsally compressed. Glumes 2, 0.1-0.4 mm long, less than 1/20 the spikelet length, scalelike, nerves absent. Sterile lemmas 2, 1.8-3.8 mm long, ca. 1/2 the spikelet length, mucronate or subulate, 1- or 3-nerved. Fertile lemma 4.2-6.4 mm long, mucronate, 7-nerved. Palea 4-6.6 mm long, palea and fertile lemma subequal or the palea overtopping the fertile lemma, sulcate toward the apex, bimucronulate, 4-nerved. Stamens 3, the anthers 3-3.7 mm long. Lodicules 3, the anterior pair ca. 0.7 mm long, the posterior one ca. 0.5 mm long, all ciliate. Fruit unknown.

description: Culmi 1-1.2 cm diam., 2-4 m alti, erecti vel inclinati. Folia culmorum 7.5-14 cm longa, decidua; vaginae 7.2-10.2 cm longae, 2-3.3 (6.5)-plo longiores quam laminam, glabrae; laminae 1-4.6 cm longae, loratae, erectae reflexescentes, deciduae. Ramificatio extravaginalis mutata; ramus centralis 0.5-1 m longus, divergens; rami subsidiarii tenues cujusquisque nodi 4-10, 16-23 cm longi, adscendentes, duo robustiores, 20-50 cm longi, adscendentes. Folia cujusquisque complementi 7-8; vaginae deciduae, glabrae; laminae 7-16 cm longae, 0.4-1.1 cm latae, ratio long./lat. = 11-19, glabrae, non tessellatae, basi attenuatae vel rotundato attenuatae. Panicula 3-3.5 cm longa. Spiculae 8.3-9.1 mm longae, glabrae. Glumae 2, squamiformes. Lemmata sterilia 2, subulata, 2/5 spiculam attingentia. Lemma fertile 7.9-8.3 mm longum, subulatum. Palea 7.6- 7.9 mm longa.

description: Culms 1-1.2 cm in diam., 2-4 m tall, erect to leaning. Internodes 16-22 cm long, terete, glabrous, glaucous when young. Culm leaves 7.5-14 cm long, deciduous as the branches develop, the base often splitting, juncture of sheath and blade a more or less horizontal line; sheaths 7.2-10.2 cm long, 2-3.3 (6.5) times as long as the blade, abaxially glabrous, the margins ciliate; blades 1- 4.6 cm long, straplike, articulated with the sheath, erect becoming reflexed, deciduous, abaxially glabrous, adaxially pubescent at the base, the apex mucronate, the margins serrulate; girdle 0.5 mm wide, glabrous; inner ligule 0.4 mm long, ciliolate. Nodes with the nearly circular central bud subtended by 1 row of smaller subsidiary buds in a con- stellate array, two of the subsidiaries robust and larger than the others; sheath scar dipping slightly below the bud complement; supranodal ridge prominent; root primor- dia absent. Branching modified extravaginal, the culm leaves often split at the base but falling as the branches develop; central branch 0.5-1 m long, divergent, rebranch- ing; smaller leafy subsidiary branches 4-10 per node, 16-23 cm long, more or less ascending, occasionally rebranching, the robust subsidiary branches usually 2 per node, 20-50 cm long, ascending, rebranching. Foliage leaves 7 or 8 per complement; sheaths deciduous, uniform in color, glabrous, the margins sparsely ciliate; blades 7-16 cm long, 0.4-1.1 cm wide, L:W = 1 1-19, abaxially and adaxially glabrous, not tessellate, the apex short setose, the base attenuate to rounded-attenuate; pseudopetiole 1.5-3 mm long; outer ligule 0.5-2 mm long, glabrous; inner ligule 1-3 mm long, rounded, abaxially pubescent. Panicles 3-3.5 cm long, narrow, the base retained within the subtending sheath; rachis angular, glabrous, the edges scabrous; branches angular, glabrous, the edges scabrous, the lower ones 0.5-0.8 cm long, appressed; pedicels 1-3 mm long, angular, glabrous, the edges scabrid, appressed. Spikelets 8.3-9.1 mm long, glabrous, sometimes slightly falcate, the anthecium 1.3-1.5 mm wide, dorsally compressed. Glumes 2, 0.1-0.2 mm long, less than 1/30 the spikelet length, scalelike, nerves absent. Sterile lemmas 2, 3.5-4.5 mm long, ca. 2/5 the spikelet length, subulate, 1- or 3-nerved. Fertile lemma 7.9-8.3 mm long, subulate, 7- or 9-nerved. Palea 7.6-7.9 mm long, subequal to the fertile lemma, sulcate toward the apex, the sulcus scabrid, bimucronulate, 4-nerved. Stamens unknown. Lodicules unknown. Caryopsis 4.1 mm long, reddish-brown.

description: Culmi 1-1.5 cm diam., (1-2) 4-5 (6) m alti, erecti ad basim, interdum leviter arcuati ad apicem. Folia culmorum 6.6-17 cm longa, decidua, plerumque fissa ad basim, vagina et lamina plerumque confluentes, margines connati ad basim per 0.3-1.5 cm; vaginae si manifestae 5.6-12.6 cm longae, 3-6.5 (10)-plo longiores quam laminam; laminae si manifestae 0.8-2.3 cm longae, triangulares. description: Culms 1-1.5 cm in diam., (1-2) 4-5 (6) m tall, erect at base, sometimes slightly arching at the apex. Internodes 7.7-14 cm long, slightly flattened above the branch complement, glabrous, waxy. Culm leaves 6.6-17 cm long, deciduous as the branches develop, the base usually splitting, usually no clear distinction between the sheath and blade present, abaxially retrorsely scabrous on the upper half, glabrous below, the apex subulate, the margins fused at the base for 0.3-1.5 cm; sheaths when manifest 5.6-12.6 cm long, 3-6.5 (10) times as long as the blade; blade when manifest 0.8-2.3 cm long, triangular, erect, persistent, adaxially retrorsely scabrous-pubescent; girdle 0.5 mm wide, glabrous; inner ligule usually absent, when present ca. 0.5 mm long, ciliolate. Nodes with the central bud flanked by 2-5 subsidiary buds on each side; sheath scar more or less horizontal; supranodal ridge obscure; root primorida absent. Branching intravaginal; central branch 32.5-100 cm long, nodding, rebranching; leafy subsidiary branches 5-10 per node, (8) 18.5-65 cm long, nodding, rebranching. Foliage leaves 4-8 (14) per complement; sheaths persis- tent, usually pubescent between the nerves, less commonly glabrous; blades 2-5.3 cm long, 0.06-0.15 cm wide, L:W = (25) 33- 60, adaxially scabrid, abaxially glabrous, not tessellate, apex subulate, base attenuate; pseudopetiole 0.5 mm long; outer ligule a minute, glabrous or ciliolate rim 0.1 mm long; inner ligule 0.2-0.5 mm long, truncate. Inflorescence a panicle or raceme, 0.5-1 cm long, spikelike, the base retained within the subtending sheath; rachis angular, scabrous-pubescent; branches and pedicels an- gular, scabrous-pubescent, the pedicels 2.5-4 mm long. Spikelets 5.6-6.6 mm long, pu- bescent, the anthecium 1-1.2 mm wide, more or less terete. Glumes 2, 0.6-0.8 mm long, ca. 1/2 the spikelet length, scalelike, acute to obtuse, nerves absent. Sterile lemmas 2, 2.8-3.2 mm long, ca. 1/2 the spikelet length, subulate; sterile lemma I 1-nerved; sterile lemma II 3-nerved. Fertile lemma 5.2-5.9 mm long, subulate, 7-nerved. Palea 4.7-5.6 mm long, slightly shorter than the fertile lemma, sulcate only toward the apex, acute, 2-nerved. Stamens 3; anthers 2.6-2.8 mm long. Fruit a caryopsis.

description: Culms 0.5 -1 cm in diam., (0.5) 2-3 m tall, erect. Internodes 3-11 cm long, terete, sometimes pubescent below the nodes when young, otherwise glabrous, waxy. Culm leaves 5.3-14.2 cm long, persistent, abaxially glabrous or retrorsely scabrid, juncture of sheath and blade a more or less horizontal, indistinct line; sheaths 3.2-11.7 cm long, 1.4-4 (6) times as long as the blade, triangular; blades 1.3-5 cm long, triangular, persistent, adaxially retrorsely scabrid, apex subulate; girdle 0.5-1 mm wide, pubescent; inner ligule 0.2-1 mm long, ciliolate. Nodes with the central bud more or less linearly subtended by 5-20 subsidiary buds; sheath scar more or less horizontal; supranodal ridge obscure; root primordia absent. Branching intravaginal; central branch 10- 65 cm long, erect, rebranching; leafy subsidiary branches 5-20 (30) per node, (4) 8- 21 cm long, fine, erect, often rebranching from basal and upper nodes. Foliage leaves 10-12 (16) per complement; sheaths per- sistent, finely pubescent between the nerves; blades 1.5-4.7 (6.6) cm long, 0.07-0.25 (0.4) cm wide, L:W = (8.6) 17-31, stiff, glabrous and not tessellate, apex navicular-subulate to setose, base attenuate; pseudopetiole 0.2- 1 mm long, not very distinct; outer ligule a minute rim, virtually absent; inner ligule 0.3-0.5 mm long, truncate. Panicles 1-2 (4) cm long, narrow spikelike, the base retained with the subtending sheath; rachis angular, scaberulous to pubescent; branches less than 1 cm long, appressed, angular, scabrid to pubescent; pedicels 1-3.5 mm long, angular, scabrid to pubescent. Spikelets 5-7.1 (8.1)  mm long, finely pubescent on the upper half of each bract, the anthecium (1. 1) 1.2-1.7 mm wide, more or less terete. Glumes 2, nerves absent; glume I 0.3-0.9 mm long, less than 1/10 the spikelet length, scalelike; glume II 0.4-1.3 mm long, ca. 1/10 the spikelet length, scalelike to oblong. Sterile lemmas 2, 2.9-4.3 mm long, 1/2-2/3 the spikelet length, mucronate, 1-, 3-, or 5-nerved. Fertile lemma 4.7-7.5 mm long, mucronate to subulate, 5-, 7-, or 9-nerved. Palea 4.3-7 mm long, subequal to the fertile lemma, sulcate only toward the apex, bimucronulate, 4-nerved. Stamens 3; anthers 2.8-3.5 mm long. Fruit unknown.

description: Culms ca. 1 (1.5) cm in diam., 1-1.5 m tall, erect. Internodes 5-8 cm long, slightly flattened above the branch complement, glabrous, waxy. Culm leaves 6.6-11.4 cm long, persistent, abaxially retrorsely scabrid, juncture of sheath and blade abaxially a more or less horizontal line; sheaths 3.6-8 cm long, 1.2-3.6 times as long as the blade, more or less triangular, the shoulders slightly rounded, the margins glabrous, ciliate at apex; blades 2-4 cm long, triangular, erect, persistent, adaxially glabrous, the apex subulate; girdle 0.5-1 mm wide, pubescent; inner ligule 0.5 mm long, ciliolate. Nodes not swollen, with one triangular central bud flanked by 2 or 3 smaller subsidiary buds on each side; sheath scar horizontal; supranodal ridge present; root primorida absent. Branching intravaginal; the central branch 24-52 cm long, erect at base, ascending but gently curving away from the main culm, rebranching; leafy subsidiary branches 4-6 per node, 10-13 cm long, erect, not rebranching. Foliage leaves 8-10 (13) per complement; sheaths persistent, pubescent between the nerves; blades 3.5-4.7 cm long, 0.3-0.4 cm wide, L:W = 10-13, glabrous, not tessellate, the apex subulate, the base rounded; pseudopetiole ca. 0.5 long; outer ligule 0.1-0.2 mm long, ciliolate; in- ner ligule 0.3 mm long, truncate. Inflorescence unknown.

description: Culmi erecti usque ad 10 m alti, internodio 2 cm diametro. Culmorum folia straminea, persistentia: vagina crustacea, glabra; lamina recta, glabra, dimidiam longitudinem vaginae attingens. Ramificatio extravaginalis. Folia 2 vel 3 in complemento: laminae lineari-lanceolatae apice acuminatae, 10-17 cm longae, 1-1.5 cm latae. Inflorescentia paniculata usque ad 25 cm longa, ramis appressis usque ad 8 cm longis. Spiculae pallide virentes, lanceolatae, 8-9.4 mm longae, glumis 4. Gluma I, triangularis, 1.8-2.3 mm longa, uninervis; II, triangularis, 2.6-3.6 mm longa, trinervis; III, obovato-triangularis, 4.5-5 mm longa, 7-nervis; IV, lanceolata, 7.1-9.8 mm longa, 7-nervis. Lemma lanceolatum, 9.4-10.6 mm longum, 7-nerve. Palea membranacea, 8.2 mm longa, bicarinata, 2 nervis lateralibus.

description: Clump-forming bamboo with pachymorph rhizomes and erect solid culms up to 10 m tall and 2 cm thick at the base, arching above; internodes solid, green, scabrous in the larger specimens. Culm leaves persistent, stramineous: sheath crustaceous, glabrous; blade erect, ca half as long as the sheath, continuing almost imperceptibly from it and becoming acute at the apex, disintegrating with age, chartaceous, gla- brous on the outer surface, scabrous on the inner; inner ligule a short, membranous ciliolate rim. Nodes at mid-culm with a dominant central bud and numerous sub- sidiary ones. Branching: extra-vaginal, the principal bud developing into a primary branch, the subsidiary buds developing into normal leafy branches and (in our specimens, due to fungal infection) modified fibrillose branches, the two kinds inter- mixed. Foliage leaves 2 or 3 per complement: blades linear-lanceolate with an acuminate tip, 10-17 cm long, 1-1.5 cm wide, the upper surface glabrous, not tessel- late, the lower surface sparingly pilose, slightly tessellate with a thickened glabrous midvein and 4 or 5 well-defined primary nerves on either side, and with scaberulous cartilaginous margins, with a glabrous petiole ca 2 mm long; sheaths prominently ribbed, rounded and stramineous below, carinate and maroon toward the summit, densely ciliate along the entire outer margin and on the summit of the inner margin that extends above the juncture of sheath and petiole; outer ligule a thick prominent ridge 0.7-0.8 mm long with a premorse ciliolate margin; inner ligule a thin glabrous membrane ca 1 mm long. Inflorescence a contracted panicle terminating leafy branches, up to 25 cm long with appressed branches up to 8 cm long disposed along one side of a flattened green, glabrous rachis 0.8 mm wide. Spikelets pale green, terete, lanceolate, 8-10.3 mm long, held erect on antrorsely scaberulous pedicels 2 mm long. Transitional glumes 4. I-III coriaceous, stramineous, with a thickened midvein and thick lateral veins; I triangular, 1.8-2.3 mm long, the single midvein terminating as a mucro; II triangular, 2.6-3.6 mm long, 3-nerved, with the midvein terminating in a mucro; III obovate-triangular, 4.5-5 mm long, 7-nerved, with the midvein terminating in a mucro. Transitional glume IV and lemma membranous, lanceolate, scaberulous, pale green, 7-nerved, the nerves all similar, the midnerve extending into a mucro; transitional glume IV, 7.1-9.8 mm long; lemma 9.4-10.6 mm long. Palea membranous, 8.2 mm long, 2-keeled and deeply furrowed between the keels, with 2 lateral nerves, puberulent between the keels, otherwise glabrous. Lodicules 3, broad below with an obtuse apex, the 2 anterior 2-2.6 mm long, thick- ened on the lower half, especially toward the inner margins, membranous on the upper half, multinerved, ciliate on the upper margins, the posterior lodicule 1.7 mm long, thinner and narrower than the anterior, few-nerved; stamens 3, the anthers yellow, 4.7-4.9, mm long, the filaments attached at the lower fifth. Ovary with 2 styles bearing plumose stigmas, rarely a third rudimentary stigma present. Fruit unknown.

description: Culms ca. 0.4 cm in diam. Internodes 3- 3.5 cm long, slightly flattened above the branch complement, glabrous, waxy. Culm leaves persistent, disintegrating, no complete examples available. Nodes not swol- len; sheath scar horizontal; supranodal ridge obscure; root primordia absent. Branching intravaginal; one or three subequal branches per node, erect, 21-28 cm long, not rebranching. Foliage leaves 6 or 7 per com- plement; sheaths persistent, pubescent between the 2 or 3 marginal nerves, otherwise glabrous; blades 7.3-10.8 cm long, 0.8-1.1 cm wide, L:W = 9-10, glabrous, not tessellate, the apex subulate to short setose, the base rounded; pseudopetiole ca. 1 mm long, distinct; outer ligule ca. 0.3 mm long, ciliolate; inner ligule 1 mm long, truncate, pubescent. Panicles 3-4 cm long, narrow, the base retained within the subtending sheath; rachis, branches, and pedicels angular, scabrous, the pedicels 2-3 mm long. Spikelets 5.2-5.8 mm long, glabrous, the anthecium 1.2-1.3 mm wide, laterally compressed. Glumes 2, scalelike; glume I 1/10-1/15 the spikelet length; glume II ca. /8 the spikelet length. Sterile lemmas 2, mucronate; sterile lemma I 1/2-2/3 the spikelet length; sterile lemma II ca. 2/3 the spikelet length. Fertile lemma mucronate. Palea subequal to the fertile lemma or slightly shorter. Flowers and fruits unknown.

description: Culms to ca. 1 cm in diam., ca. 1 m tall, erect. Internodes 6-8 cm long, shallowly sulcate above the branch complement, glabrous, waxy. Culm leaves 10.6-13 cm long, persistent until the subsidiary branches re- branch, then deciduous, juncture of the sheath and blade abaxially a more or less horizontal, indistinct line; sheaths 6.4-9.2 cm long, 1.5-2.8 times as long as the blade, more or less triangular, abaxially scabrid for the upper 2/3, margins glabrous to sparsely apically ciliate on the overlapping margin; blades 3.2-4.2 cm long, triangular, erect, persistent, abaxially glabrous, adaxially retrorsely scabrid, the apex subulate; girdle 1- 2 mm wide, glabrous; inner ligule 1-2 mm long, slightly irregular, ciliolate. Nodes slightly swollen; the one triangular central bud flanked by 2-4 smaller subsidiary buds on each side; sheath scar more or less horizontal; supranodal ridge prominent; root primordia sometimes replacing the supranodal ridge at the more basal nodes. Branching intravaginal; central branch 15- 30 cm long, usually curving horizontally away from the main culm, then curving upwards, rebranching; leafy subsidiary branches 4-8 per node, 7-15 (21) cm long, more or less erect, sometimes curving, often one subsidiary branch on each side of the central branch more robust, up to twice the diameter of the other subsidiaries. Foliage leaves 4-8 per complement; sheaths persis- tent, glabrous to pubescent between the nerves; blades 3.6-5.9 cm long, (0.5) 0.8-1 cm wide, L:W = 5.5-8.6, glabrous, not tessellate, the apex subulate, base rounded to rounded-attenuate; pseudopetiole 0.5 (1) mm long, distinct, often conspicuously pul- vinate; outer ligule 0.1-0.3 mm long, glabrous, somewhat irregular; inner ligule 1. 5- 2 mm long, rounded, glabrous. Panicles 1.5- 2 cm long, narrow, the base retained within the subtending sheath; rachis, branches, and pedicels angular, pubescent-scabrous, the edges scabrous; branches to 1 cm long, appressed; pedicels 2-3.5 mm long. Spikelets 4.3-4.9 mm long, glabrous, the anthecium 1.1-1.2 mm wide, more or less terete. Glumes 2, scalelike, less than 1/20 the spikelet length. Sterile lemmas 2, 2.8-3.2 mm long, 2/3 the spikelet length, mucronate, 3-nerved. Fertile lemma 4.3-4.8 mm long, shortly mucronate, 7-nerved. Palea 4.1-4.7 mm long, subequal to the fertile lemma, sulcate only toward the apex, bimucronulate, 4-nerved, the sulcus scabrous-pubescent. Lodicules unknown. Stamens unknown. Fruit unknown.

description: Ab omnibus ceteris speciebus generis culmis floriferis decumbentibus differt. Gramen perenne, culmis vegetativis (raro floriferis) usque ad 20 cm adscendentibus, culmis floriferis decumbentibus geniculatisque laminis deminutis munitis. Folia per complementum 12; laminae oblongo-lanceolatae, 1.8-2.1 cm longae, 6-7 mm latae, ad basin apicemque asymmetricae; vaginae carinatae; pseudopetiolus utrinque dense pubescens; ligula inconspicua, 0.9-1.5 mm longa. Inflorescentia racemiformis, spicula terminali feminea, spiculis basalibus binatis, feminea breviter mascula longe pedicellata. Spiculae femineae 7.6-8.5 mm longae; gluma infera 5-nervia, supera 5-7-nervia. Spiculae masculae 3 mm longae; antherae 3. Fructus caryopsis fusiformis.
bibliographicCitation: Soderstrom, Thomas R. & Zuloaga, Fernando O. 1985. New species of grasses in Arberella, Cryptochloa, and Raddia (Poaceae: Bambusoideae: Olyreae). Brittonia. 37: 22-35.

description: Perennial?, culms 15-30 or more in a fascicle, these decumbent, geniculate, densely branched and rooting at the lower nodes with many branches produced at each node, then ascending and reaching approximately 2 dm in height, keeled, sparsely pubescent to glabrous; internodes hollow, the lower ones bearing a sheath only or a sheath with rudimentary blade; nodes compressed, sparsely pubescent. Leaves 12-15 per complement, ascending; blade oblong-lanceolate, apiculate, 1.8- 2.1 cm long, 6-7 mm wide, the base and apex asymmetric, scabrous, greenish on the upper surface, purplish on the lower, the midnerve not prominent, short- pubescent to glabrescent on both surfaces, the hairs sparse, scattered; pseudopetiole inconspicuous, ca 1 mm long, brown to greenish, densely pubescent on both surfaces; sheath keeled, sparsely pubescent toward the margins with short retrorse hairs; auricles inconspicuous, membranous; ligule membranous, short-ciliate on the upper part, 0.9-1.5 mm long, pubescent on the inner surface. Inflorescences mostly on lower culm, racemiform, with several at each node and small in size, consisting of a pair of basal spikelets and a long-pedicellate terminal female spikelet, the pedicel thickened, scabrous, with the basal pair consisting of a short- pedicellate female spikelet and a male spikelet on a long thin scabrous pedicel; axis short, scabrous; prophylla glabrous. Female spikelets fusiform, 7.6-8.5 mm long, 1.8-2 mm wide, greenish to purplish, glabrous; glumes subequal, longer than the anthecium; lower glume acuminate, 5-nerved, the midnerve manifest, the lateral ones inconspicuous, with transverse veinlets toward the apex, scabrous toward the apex of the outer surface, otherwise glabrous; upper glume acuminate, 7.4-8.2 mm long, 5-7-nerved, the nerves tessellate, scabrous toward the apex of the outer surface, otherwise glabrous, shining on the inner surface; anthecium fusiform, 6-6.2 mm long, 1.6-1.9 mm wide, glabrous, shining, finely papillose on the lemma and palea, the papillae rounded, small, unevenly distributed; lemma 5-nerved; palea concave at the apex; lodicules 3, 1.3 mm long. Male spikelets oblong, obtuse to subacute, 3 mm long, 0.7 mm wide, scaberulous; lemma obtuse to subacute, 3-nerved, scaberulous; palea 2.8 mm long, 2-nerved, scaberulous; anthers 3, 1.1 mm long. Caryopsis fusiform, 4.2-4.4 mm long, 1.7 mm wide, brown; hilum linear, as long as the caryopsis; embryo 1/5 or less the length of the caryopsis. Fruit not known.

description: Plants perennial, short-rhizomatous forming fascicles of 7 or 8 culms, 30-50 cm tall, the roots fibrous, with thin but firm culms bearing 2 or 3 exposed nodes below the leaf complement, the culms purple, smooth, ridged, the exposed nodes bearing reduced blades, these fully developed only in the leaf complement. Foliage leaves 4-6 per complement, ascending-spreading: blades linear-lanceolate with symmetric base and acuminate tip, to 10 x 1-1.5 cm, pale green above, dark purple below, the upper and lower surfaces glabrous, with a midrib prominent on both surfaces and a short glabrous petiole; sheath glabrous, strongly ribbed, the internerves papillose; oral setae lacking; outer ligule lacking; inner ligule prominent, thin, brown or purplish-brown, exceeding the petiole, 4.4-5.2 mm long, rounded at the ciliolate apex, glabrous. Inflorescences paniculiform, 3 or 4 at each of the upper nodes of the leaf complement, hardly exserted and more or less concealed by the ascending blades, with one terminal female spikelet and 1 or 2 short-pedicellate lateral spikelets and 1 branch of 5-8 male spikelets only, borne at the lower node of the flowering axis or, in the final inflorescences of the series, the inflorescence consisting of male spikelets only on the main axis and branches from it. Female spikelets narrowly oblong, 9.4-11.1 mm long, disarticulating above the glumes. Glumes purplish-green, thin, firm, glabrous, with 3 strong nerves and 2 weak ones near the margins, the lower glume 10.8 mm long, acuminate, the upper 9.2 mm long, acute. Lemma 6.8 mm long, narrowly ovate with an acute apex, glabrous, fleshy-firm at first, at maturity hard, white and shiny, 5-nerved with some transverse veinlets, separated from the upper glume by an internode ca 1.7 mm long. Palea narrowly ovate with an acute apex, 2-nerved, at first fleshy, becoming hard and white at maturity, the margins folding toward the center and almost meeting. Lodicules 3, fleshy, cuneiform, glabrous. Ovary slender, with a single style and 2 plumose stigmas, exserted from just below the summit of the lemma and palea. Male spikelets deciduous after anthesis, 2.7-3 mm long, purplish. Glumes lacking. Lemma elliptic and acute at the slightly curved apex, glabrous, thin, 3-nerved. Palea narrowly elliptic, 2-nerved, glabrous. Lodicules 3, fleshy, glabrous, cuneiform, truncate, ca 0.4 mm long. Stamens 2, the anthers orange, basifixed, 1.3 mm long. Fruit a caryopsis, orange, ellipsoid, slightly flattened on the embryo side, the hilum narrow, extending the length of the fruit, the embryo ca 1/5 the length of the fruit.

description: A congeneribus omnibus androecio 2 (nec 3)-mero, inflorescentiis tantum e nodis summis ortis, foliisque 4-5 lineari-lanceolatis ad apicem caulis strictissimi confertis inferne saturate purpureis diversa. Culmi 30-50 cm alti. Folia 4-6 in quoque complemento: laminae lineari-lanceolatae, usque ad 10 x 1-1.5 cm, supra virides infra purpureae; petiolus brevis glaber; ligula prominens, 4.4-5.2 mm longa. Inflorescentiae 3 vel 4 e nodo supero productae, paniculiformes: axis primarius cum 2 vel 3 spiculis femineis; axis lateralis cum 5-8 spiculis masculis. Spiculae femineae 9.4-11.1 mm longae. Spiculae masculae 2.7-3 mm longae. Antherae 2. Fructus: caryopsis ellipsoideus.

description: A congeneribus omnibus inflorescentia spiculam femineam singularem ferenti et anthoecio femineo omnino vel ex parte pubescenti differt. Gramen cespitosum culmis erectis usque ad 0.5 m altis. Folia 4-6 in quoque complemento; laminae anguste-oblongatae apice asymmetrico, 8-12 x 1.5-2 cm, utraque superficie pallide virides et glabrae; petiolus utraque superficie incanus; vaginae subtiliter puberulae inter nervos; ligula interna membranacea, brevis, ca 0.5 mm longa. Inflorescentia racemiformis, ex 1 spicula feminea terminali et 2 spiculis masculis infernis constans, racemis 3-5 e quoque nodo superno productis. Spiculae femineae fusiformes, 17-20 mm longae. Spiculae masculae 4.3-4.6 mm longae.

description: Plants perennial, short-rhizomatous forming fascicles of 5-10 firm erect culms up to 0.5 m tall, with a node toward the base bearing a culm leaf with very reduced blade, a long internode with a node bearing a heart-shaped culm leaf blade, and a long internode preceding the leaf complement, the culm smooth and shiny with light ribs alternating with darker bands. Foliage leaves with 4-6 leaves per complement, ascending; blades narrowly oblong narrowing abruptly to an asymmetric tip, 8-12 cm long and 1.5-2 cm wide, pale green and glabrous on both surfaces, the midrib prominent only on the lower surface, the short petiole densely short-pubescent on both surfaces; sheath finely appressed-puberulent on the bands between the nerves; oral setae lacking; outer ligule lacking; inner ligule not manifest or extending just beyond the sheath as a short truncate rim less than 0.5 mm long. Inflorescences racemiform, 3-5 borne from the uppermost nodes and hardly exserted, concealed by the ascending foliage, with 1 terminal female spikelet and just below this a pair of male spikelets, one subsessile, the other short-pedicellate, or the ultimate inflorescence consisting of male spikelets only, the axis long and narrow, with the sheath gradually thickened upward to the exposed spikelet-bearing portion. Female spikelets fusiform, ca 17-20 mm long, disarticulating above the glumes. Glumes dull green except for the narrow white margins, thin, firm, glabrous but with a beady surface, not shiny, with 3 strong nerves and 2 weaker ones near the margins, and some transverse veinlets, the lower and upper about the same length, 17-20 mm long, linear-lanceolate. Female anthecium white, shiny, 14 mm long, separated from the glumes by a white internode 3-4 mm long, hard at maturity, glabrous and shiny except at the narrowed pubescent tip. Lemma glabrous and shiny except at the pubescent apex, hard, white and shiny at maturity. Palea a little shorter than the lemma, hard, shiny, and glabrous except at the pubescent tip. Lodicules 3. Ovary with a single long style and 2 stigmas. Male spikelets pale green, deciduous after anthesis, slightly falcate, 4.3-4.6 mm long, glabrous becoming puberulent toward the apex. Lemma narrowly elliptic, hyaline, 3-nerved. Palea a little shorter than the lemma, very thin, narrowly elliptic, faintly 2-nerved. Lodicules 3. Stamens 3, the anthers orange, mucronate, basifixed, ca 2 mm long, the filaments not elongated. Fruit unknown.

description: Viekery comparanda sed ab ea foliorutm laminis filiformibus, antheris minoribus certe distineta. Grameen perenne, caespitosum; cullmi pergraciles, glabri levesque, usque 40 cm alti, striati, nodis glabris; foliorum lamninae usque 25 cm longiae, filiformes, complicatae marginibus involutis, rigidae, supra pilis minutissimis obtectae, explanatae profunde suleatae, infra glabrae levesque, marginibus nervis medianisqne crassis; vaginae culmos arete complectentes, glabrae levesque vel minutissimie scaberulae, marginibus hyalinis; ligulae membranaceae, acutae, 3 mm longae; inflorescentia racemosa, usque 5 cm longa, 4 mm lata; spiculae uniflorae, virides vel albeseentes, hiantes; glumae aequilongae, 5 mm longae, 1-nerviae, carinis scaberulae; anthoecium [male/female], ut videtur cleistooamum; lemma 4 mm longum, callo barbato, dorso apicem versus scabrum, supra basin aristatum; palea lemmati aequilonga, 2-nervia; rhachilla producta, brevissime pilosa, anthoecio vestigiliale coronata; staminia 3; antherae 0.5 mm longae, inclusae; hilum punctiforme; embryo parva; caryopsis suleata; arista perfecta, 5 mm longa; columma aurea, torta, 2.5 mm longa.

description: Gramen perenne, caespites 40-50 cm altos formans, culmis altis (plerumque vegetativis) et culmis brevibus (florentibus). Culmi alti: folia per complementum 4-6; laminae ovato-lanceolatae, 10-16 cm longae, 1-4 cm latae, ad basin symmetricae, ad apicem acutae; vaginae glabrae; pseudopetiolus utrinque pilosus. Culmi breves: folia per complementum 1; lamina ovato-lanceolata, 5-7 cm longa, 1-2 cm lata, inflorescentiam tegens. Inflorescentiae spiciformes, usque ad 8 paria spicularum (1 masculina, 1 feminea) continentes. Spiculae femineae ovoideae, 6.1-6.2 mm longae, 2-2.3 mm latae, integrae cadentes; gluma infera 9-nervis, supera 7-9-nervis; lemma 5-nerve, glabrum; lodiculae connatae; ovarium stylo singulari et 2 stigmatibus plumosis. Spiculae masculae fusiformes; glumae minutae; lemma 3-nerve, glabrum; lodiculae 3, acutae, ciliatae; stamina 2; pistillodium 1 stigmatibus 3. Fructus caryopsis, hilo lineari caryopside paulo breviore.
bibliographicCitation: Soderstrom, Thomas R. & Zuloaga, Fernando O. 1985. Diandrolyra tatianae (Poaceae: Olyreae), a new herbaceous bamboo from Brazil. Brittonia. 37: 1-5.

description: Plants perennial, short-rhizomatous and forming fascicles of 15-20 culms, these erect or occasionally geniculate at some of the lower nodes, in 2 classes, short and tall: short culms ca 2 dm tall, bearing a single leaf with the blade overtopping an inflorescence; tall culms 4-5 dm tall with leaf complements of 4-6 leaves, usually sterile but occasionally bearing a terminal inflorescence; nodes dark, short-pubescent, the whitish hairs retrorse; internodes hollow, strongly ridged, glabrous, shining. Foliage leaves: blades ovate-lanceolate, more or less symmetrical at the base with an acute apex, glabrous on both surfaces, these green or the adaxial sometimes purplish, the margins smooth, with the median nerve manifest on both surfaces, the blades of the tall culms 10-16 cm long, 1-4 cm wide, those of the short culms 5-7 cm long, 1-2 cm wide; sheaths pale green to stramineous, strongly ridged, glabrous; ligule a short brown membrane, glabrous; pseudopetiole ca 2 mm long, brownish, thick and densely pubescent on both surfaces. Inflorescences spiciform, with 6-8 pairs of spikelets, these borne on one side of the axis, the other side, lying against the overtopping blade, flat; peduncle hispid; axis glabrous, with a solitary female spikelet borne at the base, followed by 5 or 6 pairs of spikelets, the lower male and more or less sessile, the upper female and shortly- pedicellate, the pedicels strongly angled, glabrous, the terminal pair with the male spikelet on a long pedicel and bearing glumes as long as the anthecium. Female spikelets ovoid, acute, with the bases of the glumes fused and forming a thickened pilose process, the spikelets falling entire, 6.1-6.2 mm long, 2-2.3 mm wide. Lower glume acute, 5.4 mm long, 9-nerved, the nerves anastomosing, sparsely pilose on the nerves. Upper glume acute, 5.2 mm long, 7-9-nerved, the nerves anastomosing, sparingly pilose on the nerves. Anthecium ovoid, ca 5 mm long, 2 mm wide; lemma 5-nerved, its borders flat, not inrolled over the palea, sca- berulous at the acute apex, otherwise glabrous; palea 2-nerved, glabrous. Lodicules 3 (?), fused into a single fleshy structure. Ovary with a single long style and 2 plumose stigmas. Male spikelets fusiform, bearing 2 glumes on the terminal spikelet with 5 nerves each (the glumes abbreviated on the lateral spikelets), in addition to the lemma and palea, the spikelets falling entire. Anthecium fusiform, 4.9 mm long, 0.8 mm wide, the lemma 3-nerved with a few transverse veinlets, lanceolate, scaberulous at the acute apex, otherwise glabrous, the palea 2-nerved, 3.8-4.7 mm long, scaberulous at the apex, otherwise glabrous. Andrecium consisting of 2 stamens and a pistillodium composed of a long style and 3 short stigmas, the filament attached toward the base of the anther. Lodicules 3, ca 1 mm long, fleshy below with the upper margin thin, acute, ciliate. Fruit a caryopsis flattened on one side with a linear hilum reaching ca 3/4 its length.
bibliographicCitation: Soderstrom, Thomas R. & Zuloaga, Fernando O. 1985. Diandrolyra tatianae (Poaceae: Olyreae), a new herbaceous bamboo from Brazil. Brittonia. 37: 1-5.

description: Tufted perennial. Culms usually stiffly erect, 15-50 cm tall, freely branching in age, with glabrous or puberulent internodes and glabrous or slightly hairy nodes. Lower sheaths usually pubescent, pilose or hispid, the upper ones often glabrous. Ligule a fringe of hairs 1 mm or less long. Blades of midculm leaves stiff, narrow, linear or linear-lanceolate, gradually tapering to the tip, in Mexican plants glabrous and mostly 5-10 cm long and 2-5 mm broad. Panicles small, open, few-flowered, the primary panicles mostly 5-8 cm long, the panicles de- veloped on the erect or stiffly-spreading branches usually less than 3 cm long and with a dozen or less spikelets, the panicle axis glabrous or scabrous. Spikelets 2.3-2.5 mm long (in plants of the United States the spikelets to 2.9 mm long), broadly elliptic or obovate, usually puberulent. First glume 1/4-1/3 the spikelet length, rounded or abruptly pointed at apex.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Plants usually developing basal rosette of short broad blades before elongation of culms. Culms mostly 15-50 cm tall, in large or small clumps from a firm base, in age freely branched and rebranched to produce fascicles of reduced branches, leaves and inflorescence. Herbage variously hairy to nearly glabrous. Ligule a ring of silvery hairs 2-5 mm long, the hairs all about the same length. Blades relatively broad and thin in most plant forms, usually 5-10 cm long and 5-10 (12) mm broad. Panicles open or somewhat contracted, mostly 4-8 cm long. Main panicle axis pilose or glabrous. Spikelets ovate, elliptic or slightly obovate, pu- berulent, 1.6-2.4 mm long. First glume broad, rounded or abruptly pointed, 1/5-1/3 as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Sheaths, at least the lower ones, papillose-pilose. Ligules 1-5 mm long. Blades firm, strigose or puberulent to nearly glabrous, often with a few long hairs inter- spersed with short ones, mostly 2-6 cm long and 2-5 mm broad. Spikelets puberulent. First glume broad, about 1/4 as long as spikelet.

description: Sheaths glabrous on back, pilose or ciliate on margins. Ligule a ring of hairs 2-5 mm long. Blades bright green, glabrous or slightly pilose. Panicles 3-8 cm long. Spikelets 1.6-2 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Coarse perennial, mostly 60-110 cm tall from a hard, knotty base, sparingly branched at upper nodes in age and often developing slender secondary shoots at base late in growing season, typically with 5-10 or more nodes elevated above base, glandular-blotched just below internodes, the lower internodes and sheaths hispid or pilose but in age sometimes nearly glabrous, the upper sheaths usually shaggy-pilose on margins and glabrous on back, the culms and leaves occasionally hispid or pilose throughout. Sheaths purple-tinged, often blotched with white. Ligule a minute fringed membrane or absent. Blades flat, broad, cordate-clasping at base, the culm blades typically 10-20 cm long and 10-20 mm broad but much shorter and narrower on some plants; blades usually glabrous or sparsely hispid on the surfaces but occasionally densely hispid or pilose on one or both surfaces. Panicles open, 10-18 cm long, the spikelets loosely and widely spaced on short or long pedicels, the axis and main branches glabrous. Spikelets 2.6-3.2 mm long, narrowly elliptic, usually slightly puberulent. First glume 1-1.5 mm long, rounded or broadly acute at apex. Second glume weakly 7-nerved. Lemma of lowerfloret weakly 5-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Plants moderately branched from a firm, often somewhat knotty base. Culms slender, often wiry, to 70 cm tall, simple or sparingly branched in age, never developing fascicles of reduced leafy branches, glabrous or slightly pubescent. Sheaths commonly glabrous or sparsely hairy on back, hispid or villous on mar- gins and often across collar. Ligule a minute fringe or absent. Blades lanceolate, glabrous, strigose, or thinly short-pilose on the surfaces, often ciliate on margins, the larger blades commonly cordate at base, 6-9 (12) cm long and 7-10 (15) mm broad. Occasional shoots with all blades broad at base but not cordate. Panicles open, longer than broad, relatively few-flowered, the main axis glabrous, 5-10 cm long. Spikelets on short (lateral) or long (terminal) pedicels, elliptic or nar- rowly elliptic, 2.1-3.2 mm long, glabrous or pubescent. First glume usually about 1/3 or slightly more as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Plants tufted, sometimes rosette-forming, with stout culms 15-40 cm tall, covered by closely imbricate, somewhat distichous leaves with thick, flat, broad, short blades. Sheaths puberulent to glabrous on back, usually hairy on margins at least above. Ligule mostly 0.3-0.5 mm long. Blades 2-5 cm long and 4-8 mm broad, glabrous except those immediately below inflorescences ciliate on margins near base with a few papilla-based hairs. Panicle 3-5 cm long, the main axis and appressed branches glabrous or sparsely pilose or hispid. Spikelets 2-2.7 mm long. First glume 1- or 3-nerved, slightly more to slightly less than half the spikelet length.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1978. New Taxa from the Avila and Naiguata Mountains, Venezuela. Brittonia. 30 (1): 39-49.

description: Plants low, much-branched, in tufts or dense tussocks to 60 cm in diameter, the erect, floriferous culms mostly 8-20 cm tall. Ligule less than 1 mm long. Blades flat, lanceolate, 1.5-3.5 cm long, 1-3 mm broad, densely puberulent on adaxial surface to nearly glabrous, the margins not ciliate, with 3 strong nerves separating four groups of 3, occasionally 4 or 5, smaller nerves. Panicles mostly 1.5-3 cm long, the main axis and branches usually pilose. Pedicels variable, from 1/3-2 or 3 times as long as spikelets. Spikelets 2.5-3.1 mm long. First glume 1/2-2/3 as long as spikelet, usually 3-nerved.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1978. New Taxa from the Avila and Naiguata Mountains, Venezuela. Brittonia. 30 (1): 39-49.

description: Plants with a firm, somewhat knotty base, developing a basal rosette of short, broad blades before the culms elongate. Culms 15-80 cm tall, with glabrous (rarely puberulent) internodes and glabrous or long-bearded nodes, becoming much-branched in age, often with fascicles of reduced branches, leaves, and panicles. Sheaths glabrous on back, ciliate or pubescent with soft hairs on mar- gins. Ligules absent or a ring of hairs not over 0.5 mm long. Blades lanceolate, 2-10 mm broad, usually glabrous but occasionally pilose. Panicles mostly 2-8 cm long; late-formed lateral panicles much-reduced and few-flowered, the axis and branches usually glabrous, occasionally pilose. Spikelets oblong or slightly obovate, puberulent or glabrous, 1.1-2.4 mm long, those terminating branchlets long-pediceled, the lateral ones usually also with well-developed pedicels.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Culms typically delicate, 15-45 cm tall. Blades ascending or spreading, 2-5 cm long, 2-4.5 (6) cm broad, with thickened, whitish borders.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Culms in clumps or tufts, the flowering culms mostly 10-35 cm tall. Sheaths variously hispid or pilose to nearly glabrous, usually ciliate-pubescent on upper margins. Ligule usually not over 0.5 mm long. Blades firm, narrowly lanceolate, mostly 2-5 cm long and 1-3 mm broad, tapering from below middle to tip, usually involute and more or less terete at tip, mostly glabrous or scabrous but blade on leaf immediately below panicle often strigose-pubescent on adaxial surface. Panicles mostly 2-10 cm long, with short, erect-spreading branches, the main axis and branches usually densely hispid. Spikelets 2-2.5 mm long. First glume commonly 14 but occasionally to 1/3 as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1978. New Taxa from the Avila and Naiguata Mountains, Venezuela. Brittonia. 30 (1): 39-49.

description: Low, tussock-forming plants with short, densely leafy, repeatedly branched culms, the tussocks often 20-30 cm in diameter, the tightly-packed erect culm branches mostly 3-15 cm long. Leaves many-nerved, closely imbricated. Sheaths densely hispid or hirsute to glabrous. Ligule 0.5-1.5 mm long. Blades flat, lanceolate, often twisted or spoon-shaped, mostly 0.8-6.5 cm long and 3-10 mm broad, coarsely ciliate on margins with long, stiff, papilla-based hairs, the surfaces glabrous. Panicles few-flowered, 1-2 cm long, not or only slightly exserted above the leaves; the main axis, branches, and pedicels glabrous. Spikelets 1.8-2 mm long. Lower glume about 1/3 as long as spikelet, 1- to faintly 3-nerved. Palea of lower floret about 2/3 as long as lemma of lower floret.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1978. New Taxa from the Avila and Naiguata Mountains, Venezuela. Brittonia. 30 (1): 39-49.

description: Low, tussock- or mat-forming plants with numerous, tightly packed, densely leafy branches 5-15 cm tall. Leaves short, narrow, strongly-veined, closely imbricated. Ligule minute, usually not over 0.2 mm long. Blades mostly 0.7-1.8 cm long and 1-1.8 mm broad, glabrous or scaberulous, tapering to a narrow, involute tip. Inflorescence a contracted panicle or more commonly a raceme of 2-3 (occasionally to 6) spikelets. Axis of inflorescence glabrous. Spikelets 2-3 mm long. First glume mostly 1/2-2/3 as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. 1978. New Taxa from the Avila and Naiguata Mountains, Venezuela. Brittonia. 30 (1): 39-49.

description: Plants densely tufted, often somewhat mat-forming. Culms slender, erect culms 8-35 (45) cm tall, usually unbranched above base, the internodes (below panicle) glabrous, the nodes retrorsely bearded with soft hairs. Sheaths typically pilose with spreading or reflexed hairs mostly 1.5-3 mm long, the hairs of basal sheaths sometimes remaining erect due to compression and crowding. Ligule a fringe of hairs 0.2-1.5 mm long. Blades flat, hispid or pilose, usually ciliate on margins, yellowish-green, highly variable in development but blades of basal leaves and those of culm leaves typically all of about the same size, mostly 3-6 cm long, 3- 5 mm broad in the smaller clumps and 6-12 cm long, 6-8 (10) mm broad on larger plants. Panicles open, mostly 3.5-6 cm long and about 2/3 as broad, well-exserted above basal tuft of leaves or remaining partially hidden in them, the axis and branches usually sparsely hirsute with long, soft hairs. Spikelets narrowly elliptic, puberulent, 1.8-2.1 mm long. First glume 1/3-1/4 as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Plants tufted, usually forming low, dense mats or pads. Culms commonly unelongated and unbranched below inflorescence but inflorescences usually on slender peduncles 5-10 cm or more long, the internodes glabrous, the nodes glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Sheaths commonly glabrous on back and pilose on margins. Blades typically short and broad, mostly 3-6 cm long and 3-8 mm broad, mostly coarsely ciliate on margins to or near apex, glabrous on surfaces or with a few long, strigose hairs on adaxial surface. Panicles open, few-flowered, mostly 3-4 cm long, partially hidden in basal tuft of leaves or elevated on slender pe- duncles, the main axis and primary branches often pilose. Spikelets glabrous, elliptic or slightly obovate, mostly 1.3-1.6 mm long. First glume 1/3-1/2 as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Strong perennial. Culms 50-80 cm or more tall from a firm, knotty base, purplish, not blotched with white, with 4-6 leafy nodes, rather uniformly short-hispid from base to the inflorescence, the main inflorescence axis and branches also hispid or pilose. Sheaths short-hispid. Ligule a minute, fringed membrane. Blades lanceolate, mostly 7-15 cm long and 10-15 mm broad, cordate-clasping at base, hispid to scabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescence open, relatively few-flowered, to 13-18 cm long, with spikelets short-pediceled and closely appressed in clusters of 3-4 on terminal branchlets, the inflorescence axis and main branches hispid or pilose. Spikelets narrowly elliptic or slightly obovate, minutely puberulent, 3.8- 4.2 mm long. First glume (1.5) 2-3 mm long, most commonly tapering to a nar- rowly acute apex.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Culms tufted, firm, 20-50 cm tall, curving-erect from a sub-rhizomatous base, the nodes glabrous to minutely pubescent, the lower internodes papillose-hispidto densely short-pubescent. Sheaths, at least the lower ones, puberulent or short-pilose on back, often with longer hairs on margins. Ligule a dense ring of hairs commonly 0.3-0.6 mm long. Blades firm, lanceolate, relatively broad and short, rather abruptly acute at apex, not cordate at base, mostly 3-7 (9) cm long and 4-7 (9) mm broad, usually minutely puberulent on both surfaces, often papillose- hispid on margins. Panicles few-flowered, mostly 5-10 cm long, with spikelets more or less appressed along the spreading primary branches, the lower internodes of the axis puberulent. Spikelets narrowly obovate or obpyriform, 3.7-4.1 mm long, puberulent. First glume 1/3 (1/2) length of spikelet, appearing distant from second glume due to constriction at base of the latter.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Culms loosely or densely clumped, firm at base, mostly 15-70 cm tall, with glabrous, scabrous, appressed-hispid or pilose internodes and glabrous or slightly bearded nodes. Sheaths usually sparsely hispid or pilose with papilla-based hairs. Ligule a fringe of hairs 0.2-1 (2) mm long. Blades firm, flat, glabrous for the most part but occasionally scabrous or sparsely hispid, 4-10 (12) cm long and 4-11 mm broad, broad at base but not cordate. Panicles open or loosely contracted, few- flowered mostly 6-9 cm long, the spikelets on pedicels 3-15 mm or more long. Spikelets broadly elliptic or slightly obovate, 3-4 mm long, rounded or obtuse at apex, sparsely pubescent, the hairs often minutely papilla-based. First glume usually 1/4-1/3 the length of spikelet, typically broadly pointed at apex.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Culms 20-50 (70) cm tall from a knotty, tufted base, the internodes mostly bearded, the lower internodes strigose, hispid or pubescent, rarely glabrous, the upper internodes often glabrous. Sheaths pubescent or hispid to nearly glabrous. Ligule a ring of hairs 0.2-0.8 mm long. Blades firm, flat, usually acuminate, typically 6-15 cm long and 3-8 (13) mm broad, usually narrowing slightly at base but occasionally slightly cordate, sparsely hispid or pilose on surfaces, often ciliate on margins below middle with widely-spaced, papilla-based hairs. Panicles usually narrow, few-flowered, mostly 3-5 (8) cm long, with erect or erect-spreading branches and appressed branchlets and pedicels. Spikelets narrowly obovate, 3.4-4.1 mm long, sparsely pubescent or glabrous. First glume well-developed, 3-nerved, often 1/2-2/3 as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Tufted perennial with culms erect or decumbent at base, often much-branched in age. Culm nodes more or less bearded, usually several, often closely spaced at base of plant, the internodes at least the lower ones, puberulent to short pubescent. Sheaths pilose to nearly glabrous, usually ciliate on margins. Ligule a ring of minute hairs, mostly 0.2-0.5 mm long. Blades relatively thin, lanceolate, glabrous or pubescent, never with long hairs except for marginal cilia which often are present on lower half of blade, not cordate at base. Panicle open, few-flowered, 3-9 cm long, the spikelets terminating branchlets on long pedicels, those not terminating branchlets on short, often appressed pedicels, the main axis scabrous or pubescent. Spikelets broadly elliptic to slightly obovate, mostly 2.9-3.5 mm long, usually more or less pubescent. First glume 1/4-1/3 length of spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Tufted perennial developing a conspicuous winter rosette of short, broad blades early in the growing season. Culms erect or decumbent at base, mostly 20-45 (60) cm tall, typically glabrous but occasionally sparsely hairy on lower internodes, not or sparingly branched in age, not developing fascicles of reduced branches, leaves and inflorescences. Sheaths glabrous on back, fringed on margins with soft hairs, mostly as long as or longer than culm internodes. Ligule absent or a fringe of hairs to 1 mm long. Blades of basal and midculm leaves lanceolate, thick and broad, usually cordate at base, glabrous on surfaces and ciliate on margins at and near base, highly variable in size but mostly 5-9 cm long and 7-14 mm broad. Panicles open, well-exserted, 5-10 cm long, the main axis and branches glabrous. Pedicels mostly longer than spikelets. Spikelets broadly elliptic or subspherical, glabrous or puberulent, 1.5-2 mm long. First glume usually a broadly rounded scale about 1/4 as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Coarse perennial. Culms mostly 50-100 cm long, ascending from a decumbent, often widely spreading base, freely branching at the middle nodes in age, typically with many nodes and short internodes, the lower portions of the culms and the associated sheaths typically villous or hispid but frequently glabrate. Sheaths shorter than internodes. Ligular hairs 1.5-4 mm long, occasionally with a ring of short hairs in front of the long ones. Blades lanceolate, rather thick, usually (5) 6-11 cm long and 1-2.5 mm broad, cordate at base, short pilose to villous on surfaces but occasionally nearly glabrous, often slightly ciliate on lower margins. Panicles open, usually many-flowered and with many spikelets clustered about the main axis, (4) 6-10 cm long, usually elevated on peduncles 12-35 cm long, the upper portion of peduncles and lower portion of inflorescence axis usually pilose. Spikelets elliptic, slightly pointed at apex, 1.8-2.1 mm long, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. First glume acute at tip, variable in shape, usually about 1/3 as long as spikelet. Lemma of upper floret slightly umbonate.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Small epiphytes to 15 cm tall. Pseudo- bulbs approximate, elliptic-oblong, complanate, rugose, 45 x 9 mm, subtended at the base by 2 pairs of distichous, imbricating bracts, the upper pair foliaceous. Leaf solitary, linear-lanceolate, acute, to 14 x 1.3 cm. Inflorescences short, axillary, loosely 2- 3 flowered racemes. Sepals and petals pale green, the labellum white, the column white tinted pale rose below, the anther red-brown, the stipe hyaline, the pollinia bright yellow. Sepals and petals subsimilar, subequal, lanceolate, acute-carinate, 1.6-1.7 x 0.4-0.5 mm. Labellum transversely broadly ovate, concave, very shortly clawed, with lateral margins revolute, 1.35 x 1.68 cm, the disc with a low oblong thickening near the base. Column elongate, somewhat dorsoventrally complanate, 9 x 3 mm, the hooded clinandrium continuous with lateral column wings, the stigma bilobed, sparsely hispid laterally. Anther operculum globose, sparsely tuberculate-spiculate, narrowly cuneate below, 2.5 x 1.5 mm, pollinarium 3.5 mm long, pollinia 2, the stipe triangular-spatulate, the viscidium minute.
bibliographicCitation: Bennett, David E. & Christenson, Eric A. 1994. New Species and New Combinations in Peruvian Orchidaceae. Brittonia. 46 (1): 24-53.

description: Gramen perenne, usque ad 70 cm altum, glabrum. Spiculae cleistogamae in vaginis culmi crescentes. Laminae 4-8 cm x 1-2.5 mm, firmae, glabrae, attenuatae. Inflorescentia 7-11 cm longa, ovata; ramis divergentibus. Spiculae 5.5-14 x 1.5-2.5 mm, 7-17-florae, lineari-oblongae; glumis inequalibus, lanceolato-subulatis, 1-nerviis; lemmatibus 2.2-3 x 0.4-0.6 mm, (1) 3-nerviis. Stamina duo, antheris 0.2-0.35 mm longis. Caryopsis ellipsoidea, 0.7-0.8 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: Judziewicz, Emmet J. & Peterson, P. M. 1990. A new cleistogamous South American species of Eragrostis (Poaceae: Chloridoideae). Brittonia. 42: 47-49.

description: Tufted perennials; culms 30-70 cm long, glabrous, unbranched above the base, often whiplike and partially decumbent; lower and middle leaves often bearing solitary or few cleistogamous spikelets hidden within their sheaths, the leaves borne all along the culm, the uppermost ones progressively reduced; leaves gla- brous, rather coriaceous; ligules 0.2-0.3 mm long, erect, densely white-ciliolate; blades 4-8 cm x 1-2.5 mm, inrolled to flat, attenuate, somewhat pungent, divergent from the culm, often tardily deciduous from the summit of the sheath, glabrous or with a few delicate hairs in back of the ligule on the adaxial surface. Peduncle included within the uppermost leaf sheath or exserted up to 2 cm, glabrous. Inflorescence 7-1 1 x 3-6 cm, ovate, few-flowered, of 3-5 slender, straight branches up to 3.5 cm long, diverging from the rachis at an angle of ca 450; primary branches with their axils glabrous, scaberulous, sparingly rebranched. Spikelets 5.5-14 x 1.5-2.5 mm, strongly laterally compressed, linear-oblong, 7-17-flowered, hyaline, glabrous, greenish-stramineous, the florets rather loosely overlapping, disarticulation various, the florets falling with their attached rachilla inter- nodes in a basipetal direction, the glumes persistent or not, or the lemmas and caryopses falling from the persistent rachilla and paleas; glumes lanceolate-subulate, 1 -nerved, the lower (0.3) 0.5-1.5 mm long, the upper 1.8-2.5 mm long;florets with rachilla internodes glabrous, concealed or exposed; lemmas 2.2-3 x 0.4-0.6 mm, folded at the midrib, slenderly lanceolate, acute to slightly acuminate, most tapering evenly to their apex, (1) 3-nerved, the lateral nerves absent or up to 2/5 as long as the lemmas; paleas 1.8-2 mm long, elliptical, strongly keeled, the keels bowed-out, scabrid, bearing wings 0.1-0.15 mm wide; stamens 2, the anthers 0.2- 0.35 mm long, purple. Fruit a caryopsis 0.7-0.8 mm long, narrowly ellipsoidal, reddish-brown, translucent, produced in both axillary and terminal inflorescences. Chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Judziewicz, Emmet J. & Peterson, P. M. 1990. A new cleistogamous South American species of Eragrostis (Poaceae: Chloridoideae). Brittonia. 42: 47-49.

description: Perennial bunchgrass. Culms 30-70 cm tall, stiffly erect or slightly geniculate at the lower nodes, much exceeding the basal tuft of sterile leafy shoots. Sheaths shorter than their internodes, glabrous, or rarely somewhat pilose toward the apex, with a tuft of hairs at either side of the base of the blade. Ligule a dense row of hairs less than 0.2 mm long. Blades pilose on the adaxial surfaces, usually glabrous beneath; the lower blades spreading, 6-12 cm long; the upper slightly shorter, erect and partially enclos- ing the culm. Panicles terminal and axillary; the terminal exserted, 6-19 cm long, 4-16 cm wide, with stiff, spreading to ascending primary and secondary branches with glabrous axils and appressed pedicels; axillary panicles smaller, enclosed within their sheaths or partially protruding, with few spikelets. Spikelets strongly laterally compressed, longer than their pedicels, plumbeous to stramineous, the larger 9-17 mm long, with 18-36 florets, at maturity the glumes and lemmas falling away leaving the persistent paleas and rachillas. Glumes acuminate, 1-nerved, the first from 2/3 as long to equal to the lower lemmas, the second glume slightly longer, usually as long as the lowest lemma. Lemmas acute, the larger 1.9-2.3 mm long, with conspicuous lateral nerves. Palea white, keel minutely scabrous, 34 as long as the lemma. Stamens 2, anthers 0.20-0.48(-0.84) mm long. Caryopses smooth and shining, ellipsoid to ovoid, 0.49-0.65 mm long, endosperm translucent, yellow-brown; embryo dark brown, opaque, its long axis oriented at 45-90º to the axis between the style and attachment scars. Pollen diameter, xx = 28.5 µm, sx = 2.7 µm. 2n = 40 (n=20)
bibliographicCitation: Koch, Stephen D. 1975. Eragrostis scaligera (Gramineae, Eragrostoideae), an overlooked species. Brittonia. 27: 123-126.

description: Perennis, rhizomatibus brevibus; culmi erecti glabri 30-40 cm. alti; vaginae glabrae; ligula 1-2 mm. longa; laminae glabrae erectae planae vel +/- involutae, 1-4 mm. latae, marginibus scaberulis; panicula an-gusta compacta 6-7 cm. longa; glumae glabrae acutae circiter 5-6 mm. longae; flores masculae pubescentes 5 mm. longae; lemma primum breviter aristata; lemma secundum arista 3 mm. longa exserta dona-tum; flos f ertilis 2 mm. longus.
bibliographicCitation: Hitchcock, Albert S. 1936. Papuan grasses collected by L. J. Brass. Brittonia. 2: 107-130.

description: Perennial, with short rhizomes; culms erect, loosely cespitose, glabrous, slightly scaberulous below the panicle, 30-40 cm. tall, with 1 or 2 nodes near the base; sheaths glabrous, longer than the internodes; ligule rounded, 1-2 mm. long; blades firm, erect, flat or, especially on the innovations, more or less involute, glabrous, scaberulous on the margins, less than half the height of the culm, 1-4 mm. wide, the uppermost below the middle of the culm, 1.5-3.5 cm. long; panicle narrow, almost spikelike, somewhat lobed, brown-purple, 6-7 cm. long, the axis sparsely hirsutulous, the branches appressed, as much as 2 cm. long, the pedicels appressed-hirsute especially just below the spikelet; glumes acute, glabrous, the first about 5 mm. long, the second broader and about 1 mm. longer; staminate florets subequal, brown, obtusish, pubescent, about 5 mm. long, the first with a short straight awn, the second with a slightly bent awn exserted about 3 mm., fertile floret glabrous, about 2 mm. long.

description: Tufted, stoloniferous, with slender glabrous stems, internodes of stolon-like branches to 15 cm long, upper ones much shorter except fertile culms that may be up to 15 or more cm; small tufts of leafy stems from primary root-crown and from rooting nodes of branches or stolons, sheaths strongly overlapping, lowest ones may be bladeless, conspicuously 2-ranked and basal parts appearing com- pressed but scarcely carinate, sheaths and blades minutely scabrous, especially on margins, blades at a narrow to wide angle with sheath, scabrous on both surfaces and strongly on margins, involute and quill-like when dry, up to 13 or more cm long, mostly shorter, narrow, apex long-subulate, ligule narrow, truncate with stiffly short-ciliate margin; fertile culms leafy in lower half, glabrous; inflorescence and spikelets hispidulous; rachis jointed, about 1.3-1.5 mm thick, lowest 1-3 joints with single spikelets, upward in pairs, with articulation becoming transverse (right angle to axis) rather than oblique, uppermost several joints again with 1 spikelet or only the terminal one a single spikelet, this one with 2 subulate or shortly awned glumes; joints of rachis 5-7 (8) mm long, disarticulating when mature, spikelets sunken in grooves in rachis with rounded prominences at bases, lower glume apparently lacking except in terminal spikelet, upper indurate, striate- ribbed, oblong-ovate, somewhat acuminate to notably subulate even on same spike; 2 florets in a spikelet, the lemma of the lower membranous cymbiform, elliptic-ovate, with 3 ribs, lateral very weak, edges involute, enfolding the palea which is subequal with it but with 2 faint ribs or none, second floret similar with but 1 faint midrib in the lemma, probably only staminate or sterile, this one smaller on a very short rachilla, and from its inner base a very slender prolongation of the rachilla, terminating in a tiny vestige of the base of a floret.

description: Gramen perenne 15-17 cm altum rhizomatibus brevibus, culmis tenuibus, internodis fistulosis, teretibus, glabris. Folia 2-4 in quoque complemento: laminae lineari-lanceolatae basi valde asym- metricae, usque ad 6 cm longae et 8 mm latae, utrinque hirtellae; petioli breves supra hirsuti infra pilosi; vagina glabra; ligula membranacea, glabra, truncata, 0.18 longa. Inflorescentiae 2-morphae: (1) alia spiculam femineam singularem continens ad nodos inferiores producta, (2) alia 2-6 spiculas masculas continens, ad nodos superiores producta, ex folio supremo exserta. Inflorescentiaefeminea: spicula triangularis, gibbosa, 7.3-7.7 longa, supra glumas disarticulata. Glumae membranaceae, gla- brae, stramineae, anthoecio longiores, inferior 7-9-nervata, superior 5-7-nervata. Lemma gibbosum, 3-3.5 mm longum, album, glabrum, durum, a gluma superiore internodio distincto 1 mm longo se- paratum. Palea 2-nervata, oblonga, lemmate brevior, marginibus lemmatis inclusa, glabra, alba, dura. Lodiculae 3. Styli singularis stigmata 2 plumosa. Inflorescentiae mascula glaberrimae usque ad 4 terminales exsertae, supra folium subtendentem extensae: inflorescentia singula e spicularum paribus 1 vel 2 infra medio rachi (cujusque paris alia brevipedunculata) insertis spiculisque una superiori et una terminali composita. Spicula mascula lineari-lanceolata, ca 6 mm longa. Glumae 0. Lemma aristatum, membranaceum, fere translucidum, 3-nervatum, glabrum. Palea lineari-lanceolata, mem- branaceo-translucida, 5-7 mm longa, 2-nervata, glabra. Lodiculae 3, 1 postica plus minusve rectan- gularis, truncata, 0.3 mm longa, carnosa; 2 anticae majores, basi angustatae, 0.33-0.36 mm longae. Stamina 3, antheris flavis, 4.2-4.7 mm longis, plus minusve basifixis, filamento ad connectivum in ima decima antherae parte affixo; dehiscentia longitudinalis, extrorsa. Fructus: caryopsis brunnea, gibbosa, hilo angusto caryopsidi fere aequilongo.

description: Short-rhizomatous perennial grass, appearing cespitose, with delicate culms of 5 or 6 nodes, 15-27 cm tall, the glabrous nodal region marked by 2 prominent ridges, the lower from the thickened summit of the preceding internode and the upper from the thickened base of the succeeding sheath, the internodes hollow, terete, ridged, glabrous. Foliage leaves with 2-4 leaves per complement: blades linear-lanceolate with a very asymmetric base, to 6 cm long and 8 mm wide, thin, the upper and lower surfaces hirtellous with a prominent white midvein thickened at the base on both surfaces, with a short petiole, hirsute on the upper surface, sparsely pilose on the lower surface; sheath glabrous, strongly ribbed above; oral setae lacking; outer ligule lacking; inner ligule a membranous, glabrous, truncate ridge 0.18 mm long. Inflorescences of 2 types, one bearing a single female spike- let, borne at the lower nodes, and exserted from the lower half of its subtending sheath; the other bearing 2-6 male spikelets, borne at the uppermost node and exserted beyond the uppermost leaf. Female inflorescence: rachis ca 8-10 mm long, emerging midway from the sheath of its subtending leaf, glabrous, contain- ing a single terminal female spikelet and below this a thin rudimentary flap of tissue. Female spikelet triangular in lateral view, gibbous, 7.3-7.7 mm long, dis- articulating above the glumes. Glumes thin, glabrous, stramineous, extending beyond the anthoecium, the lower 7-9-nerved, the upper 5-7-nerved. Lemma gibbous, 3-3.5 mm long, white, glabrous, hard, the nerves not visible at maturity, separated from the upper glume by a distinct internode 1 mm long. Palea 2-nerved (the nerves not visible at maturity), somewhat oblong, shorter than the lemma and enclosed by it along the margins, more or less flat with inrolled mar- gins, at maturity white, glabrous, hard. Lodicules 3. Ovary with a single style and 2 plumose stigmas exserted from between the lemma and palea. Male inflo- rescence: up to 4 inflorescences exserted terminally, extending ca 2 cm beyond the subtending leaf, each inflorescence consisting of a single rachis with 1 or 2 pairs of spikelets on the lower part (one spikelet short-pedicellate, one long- pedicellate), an upper short-pedicellate spikelet, and terminal spikelet, all parts glabrous. Male spikelet linear-lanceolate, ca 6 mm long. Glumes lacking. Lemma awn-tipped, membranous, almost translucent, 3-nerved, glabrous. Palea linear- lanceolate, membranous-translucent, 5.7 mm long, 2-nerved, glabrous. Lodicules 3, the posterior small, more or less rectangular, truncate, 0.3 mm long, fleshy throughout, the anterior 2 larger, with a narrow base and broad above, 0.33-0.36 mm long. Stamens 3, the anthers yellow, 4.2-4.7 mm long, more or less basifixed with the filament attached to the connective at the lower 1/10 th of the anther; dehiscence longitudinal, extrorse. Fruit a brown caryopsis, gibbous, the hilum a narrow band extending almost the full length of the caryopsis.

description: Perenne; culmi erecti, 40-75 cm. alti, glabri, nodis pubeseentibus; vaginae glabrae vel ad verticein pilosae, marginibus ciliatis; ligula ciliata, 0.1 mm. longa; laminae 5-10 cm. longae, 3-5 mm. latae, superiores reductae, utrinque pubescentes, marginibus crassis scabris; racemus 5-11 cm. longus; spiculae 5-6 mm. longae; gluma prima 5.2 mm. longa, 3-nervia, pubeseens vel scabra, carina in parte inferiore ciliata; gluma secunda 4.5 mm. longa, 3-nervia, carina et marginibus ad apicem sparse hispidis; lemma sterile 4.6 mm. longum, 5-nervium, reticulatum, ad verticem hispidum ad basim pubeseens; lemma fertile acuminatum, 4.5 mm. longum, minute striatum, apice compressum.

description: Perennial; culms solitary or in small tufts, erect, 40-75 cm. tall, glabrous, the nodes appressed-pubescent; leaves mostly basal; sheaths glabrous below, appressed-pilose toward the summit, the margins ciliate, the lower ones overlapping, the upper ones shorter than the internodes; ligule ciliate, 0.1 mm. long; blades firm, stiff, erect or ascending, 5-10 cm. long, 3-5 mm. wide, the upper ones much reduced, pubescent on both surfaces, the thick usually white margins very scabrous; raceme erect, 5-11 cm. long; spikelets 5-6 mm. long; first glume 5.2 mm. long, 0.9 mm. wide from keel to margin, 3-nerved, more or less pubescent on the back, the keel long-ciliate on the lower third, scabrous above, the summit minutely notched; second glume 4.5 mm. long, 3-nerved, the keel and margins sparsely hispid toward the summit, otherwise gla- brous; sterile lemma 4.6 mm. long, 5-nerved, the lateral nerves very faint, reticulate-veined near the summit, hispid on the upper third of the keel and on the upper two-thirds of the lateral internerves, sparsely pubescent on the back toward the base; fruit acuminate, 4.5 mm. long, minutely striate, the tip eompressed in a short beak about 1 mm. long.
