description: Annual; culms 20-65 cm tall, branching at most nodes, glabrous, the internodes hollow, the nodes, especially the upper, brownish black. Sheaths rounded on the back, slightly inflated, glabrous, strongly nerved, the margins membranous, extending into small auricles 0.5-1.5 mm long on the larger leaves; ligule 0.5-1.1 mm long, membranous, ciliolate; blades loosely involute in herbarium specimens, 1-4 mm wide when unrolled, mostly 5-30 cm long, the lower surface glabrous except for the scabrous midrib at the leaf apex, the upper surface densely scaberulous throughout. Racemes solitary per branch, mostly 3-8 cm long, 0.8-1.3 mm in diam, cylindrical, usually exserted at maturity on most branches, the peduncle glabrous; rachis readily deciduous, the internode segments 2.7-4.9 mm long, the callus peglike, 0.3-0.5 mm long, completely inserted in the rachis segment, swollen and oily at caryopsis maturity. Sessile spikelets 3.0-4.9 mm long, narrowly oblong-lanceolate; lower glume coarsely corrugate along the margins with 6-11 corrugations, slightly longitudinally striate on the back but usually not corrugate in the middle on the back, rarely corrugate completely across the back, 4-7-nerved, the midnerve often suppressed, the tip usually bifid, the teeth sometimes awn-tipped to 1.9 mm long; upper glume slightly shorter than the lower, hyaline except for the 3Ygreen nerves, awned, the awn 5-16 mm long; lower floret sterile, usually with a minute rudimentary flower, the lemma 2.3-3.1 mm long, the palea 1.2-2.1 mm long, both hyaline; upper floret bisexual, the lemma 1.8- 3.1 mm long, the palea 0.9-1.6 mm long, both hyaline; anthers 3, 0.6-1.2 mm long; styles 2, separate, the stigmas plumose; caryopsis 2.0-2.3 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm wide, oblong-lanceolate in side view, circular in cross-section, the hilum punctate, the embryo ca half the length of the caryopsis. Pedicellate spikelets reduced to flattened pedicels 2.8-5.2 mm long, awnless.

description: Annual, (18-)39(-75) cm tall. Blades (15-) 31(-50) x (1-)3(-5) mm, base rounded, apex obtuse or abruptly acute. Inflorescence composed of terminal and axillary spiciform racemes, peduncle of the inflorescence 5- 32 mm long, spatheole 11-22 mm long, racemes 10-22 mm long, of 3-8 pairs of spikelets, usually partially enclosed by the spatheole. Rachis internodes 2-3 mm long, usually glabrous or scabrous. Callus (spikelet- rachis joint) short, 0.1-0.5 mm long, usually pilose, with hyaline hairs 0.5-1.2 mm long, seldom glabrous. Sessile spikelet 2-4 mm long, including the callus; lower glume dorsally convex or flat-concave, papyraceous, 2 to 4- nerved; upper glume 2.2-3.8 mm long; sterile lemma 2.2-2.7 mm long; fertile lemma 2.5 mm long, awned between 2 lobes, the awn 6-12 mm long. Palea lacking. Caryopsis 2 mm long. Pedicellate spikelet neuter, upper glume 0.5-1.2 mm long, apex usually aristate, the awn 2-6 mm long, pedicel 1.75-2.9 mm long, usually glabrous.

description: Perennial, (30-)57(-100) cm tall. Culms slender, delicate, branched, glabrous, straight or decumbent at the base, lower nodes rooting. Nodes glabrous. Sheaths keeled, glabrous, smooth, hyaline margins; blades (15-)52(-95) × (1.8-)2.5(-3.25) mm, conduplicate or flat, slightly narrowed at the base and at mid-nerve adaxially, margins scabrous, apex acute or subobtuse. Inflorescence 15-45 cm long, lax, elongated, panicle with spatheate spiciform racemes; peduncle of the inflorescence filiform, 19-45 mm long, minutely scabrous and broader at the apex; spatheole. Rachis internodes thin, 2-3.25 mm long, articulate, with slender hairs, scabrous on one margin or both, apex of internode concave and hollow, shortly denticulate, apical border minutely scabrous. Callus short, 0.2-0.5 mm long, glabrous, rarely pilose, with hyaline hairs 0.15-0.5 mm long. Sessile spikelet 2-3.75 mm long (including the callus); lower glume as long as spikelet, coriaceous, dorsally roughly tuberculate, green with mid-furrow reddish or purple, margins narrowed, inflexed, apex bidentate, minutely scabrous. Upper glume 2.2-4.65 mm long, chartaceous, 1-nerved, keeled, scabrous on the black and keels, apex boat-shaped, margins ciliolate and inflexed. Sterile lemma hyaline, 2.7-3 mm long, apex subacute, margins ciliate. Fertile lemma 2.5-2.8 mm long, membranous, hyline, apex bilobed, awned between lobes, the lobed 2 mm long, margins ciliate, the awn 5.5-11 mm long, lower segment 3.5-5 mm long, twisted, reddish, upper segment 2-6 mm long, scabrous . Palea lacking. Lodicules 2, 0.3 mm long, truncate. Stamens 3, anthers reddish, 0.8-1 mm long, style branches 2, stigmas plumose. Caryopsis 1-2 mm long, subcylindroid, purplish brown, embryo 1/3 of its length. Pendicellate spikelet sterile, upper glume 0.5-1.5 mm long, apex short, with scabrous awn, 2 mm long, and mucronate, scabrous, 0.5 mm long, pedicel 1-3 mm long, distal portion minutely scabrous, with stiff hairs on the margins.

description: Drought-deciduous shrubs, 1.5-2.5 m tall, the bole well-developed or multi- stemmed from the base; crown strict or spreading; basal stem(s) 5-10 cm in diam., the bark light grey, semi-lustrous, smooth except for the persistent spine pedicels; latex white. Branches monomorphic, twigs 5-10 mm in diam., terete, green, glabrous or sparsely hirtellous at the petiole bases, new bark pale to dark vinaceous; stinging hairs scattered to abundant, 7.5-14 mm long, yellow at first, becoming reddish, pedicellate when mature, persisting for 2-3 seasons, the mature pedicels hemispherical to hemiovoid, persisting for 4-5 seasons or more; pith well-developed, lamellate. Stipules thin, fugacious, 1.5-5.5 mm long, 1-2.5 mm wide, deltoid, the apex filiform, the margins and basal portions of adaxial surface papillate-glandular. Petiole terete, equalling the lamina, slender, glabrous proximally, hirtellous to sub- tomentose distally; stinging hairs abundant. Acropetiolar gland often absent, small, low-mammiform, solitary, terminal on an erect, peg-like pedicel, ca 1 mm high arising from the petiole apex (not or only poorly reviving in pressed material). Lamina chartaceous, (8) 10-13.5 (17.5) cm long, (9) 11-13 (18.5) cm wide, ovate, W/L = (0.75) 0.85-1.25 (1.35), deeply palmately 5-lobed, the primary veins 5; lobe apices acuminate to long-acuminate, aristate; base open cordate; apical lobe extending for (0.55) 0.6-0.75 (0.8) of the lamina length, the basal width (1) 1.5-2 (2) cm, maximum width (3.5) 5-6.5 (8.5) cm, elliptic-ovate to ovate, maximum W/L = (0.6) 0.75-0.8 (1.0), dentate to dentate-lobate, the lobes median in position, typically one per side; distal lateral lobes obovate to ovate, the proximal lobes trailing, oblong; margins strongly vertically undulating (folded and overlapped when pressed), dentate to dentate-lobate, the teeth deltoid, aristulate to aristate or capitate by a sessile pelviform gland; lamina edge plane, stimulose- ciliated by appressed stinging hairs; adaxial surface glossy green, glabrous, sparsely stimulose near the base, the stomates absent; abaxial surface duller and paler, hirtellous to subtomentose proximally on the primary veins, sparsely stimulose. Dichasium 5-13 cm long, the peduncle 4-11 cm long, 1-3 mm in diam., the primary branches 2 or 4, opposite or whorled, dichotomized 3-4 times, spreading, moderately floriferous; pubescent to tomentose, stimulose; pistillate flower pedicels 1-6 mm long, terete, the staminate flower pedicels obscure, peg-like; bracts 2-3 mm long, deltoid, the margins entire to weakly lacerate; bracteoles 0.5-1 mm long, deltoid. Staminate flowers salverform, white, (10) 15-17 mm long; perianth segments connate for ca 0.5 of their length, the tube conic, glabrous, not stimulose; bud broadly and evenly clavate; stamens 10, monadelphous in two whorls of unequal length, the anthers dorsifixed, the upper whorl exserted, its filaments 7.5-11 mm long, connate for 0.5-0.7 of their length; anthers of lower whorl filling throat, the filaments 3.5-5.5 mm long; pubescent zone 1.5-2.5 mm long, open tomentose to villous, not extending to the glabrous, discoid gland; sterile processes 2-3, 1-4 mm long, filiform. Pistillate flowers salverform, white, 9-12.5 mm long; perianth segments glabrous, + sparsely stimulose, 8-11 mm long, connate for 0.3-0.5 of their length, the tube subcylindric, tapering slightly upward, not expanding and obcampanulate in age; receptacle green, pubescent to subtomentose, the rim low, entire; ovary 2-4.5 mm long, 2-3.5 mm wide, ovoid with an acute apex, densely strigillose by upward appressed hairs, not stimulose, styles 4-5 mm long, basally connate for 0.2-0.3 of their length, dichotomized 2-3 times, exserted; disc 1.5-2 mm in diam., flat, shallowly lobed, glabrous, obscured by the receptacle rim; staminodia obscure, narrow-deltoid. Capsules 10-15 mm long, oblong-elliptic, the apex obtuse with a small, pallid beak formed by the indurate style bases; surface pusticulate, green and glabrous or greyish-pubescent, the stinging hairs scattered; outer pericarp separating from the inner, 0.3-0.4 mm thick, brittle; inner pericarp bony, 0.5-0.7 mm thick; columella 9-14 mm long. Seeds elliptic in outline, (7.5) 8-9.5 (9.5) mm long, (4.5) 4.5-5.5 (6) mm wide, W/L = (0.5) 0.55-0.65 (0.7), dorsally convex, (3) 3-4 (4.5) mm high, W/L = (0.35) 0.4-0.45 (0.45), the apex acute with an abrupt, sharp apiculus; base truncate, shallowly cordate; surface light brown with raised dark brown to black mottling, often mottling quite extensive and then nearly concolorous; caruncle fleshy, yellowish, 1-1.5 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, depressed-ovate to depressed-deltoid, the apex obtuse to rounded, exceeding the testa, the base truncate cordate, the sinus deep, the lobes free and exceeding the micropyle.

description: Drought-deciduous shrubs, 0.5-3.5 m tall, typically multi-stemmed from the base, varying from open, low and spreading to densely branched and strict, the basal stems to 3-4 cm in diam., the bark silver-grey, semi-lustrous, smooth or with persistent spine pedicels; latex white. Branches mostly monomorphic, the tubercle- like short-shoots very rarely present; twigs 4.5-10 mm in diam., terete, pale yellow- green to green, glabrous, the new bark tan to orange-brown, vinaceous in the second season; stinging hairs abundant in scattered patches, (5) 8.5-14 (16.5) mm long, yellowish, pedicellate when mature, persisting for ca 2-3 seasons, mature pedicels subconic to turbinate, persisting for 4-6 years; pith well-developed, lamellate. Stipules thin, fugacious, 1.25-3 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, deltoid, the apex filiform, the margins and adaxial surface glandular-papillate. Petiole terete, costate when dried, + equalling the lamina, slender, glabrous, sparsely stimulose. Acropetiolar gland mostly present, sessile or low-mounted, solitary, depressed- ellipsoid to obovate, cordate, low-mammiform. Lamina chartaceous, (5) 6.5-12 (15) cm long, (5.5) 7-12 (15) cm wide, ovate to suborbicular, rarely obovate, W/L = (0.9) 0.95-1.15 (1.4), palmately 3- (5)-lobed, the lobing shallow to median, at times obscure, the primary veins 5 or 7; lobe apices short, abruptly acuminate, aristulate to aristate; basal sinus narrow to closed by overlapping lobes; apical lobe extending for (0) 0.2-0.4 (0.55) of the lamina length, the basal width (2) 2.5-5.5 (6.5) cm, maximum width (2.5) 3-5.5 (6.5) cm, hemiovate to oblong, rarely obovate, maximum W/L = (0.8) 0.9-1.9 (2.75), remotely dentate distally; lateral lobes + ovate; margins plane, subentire to dentate or dentate-lobate, the teeth deltoid, aristulate; lamina edge plane, stimulose-ciliated, the hyaline stinging hairs often lost and only the flat, reddish pedicels persistent; lamina surfaces glabrous, scattered-stimulose, green to dark green, paler below, the stomates absent to very rare above. Dichasium 4-12 cm long, the peduncle 3-9.5 cm long, 1.25-3 mm in diam., the primary branches 2 to 4, opposite or whorled, dichotomized (1) 3-4 times, sparsely to moderately floriferous, glabrous, strongly stimulose; pistillate flower pedicels 2-4.5 mm long, stout, terete; staminate flower pedicels obscure, peg-like; bracts 0.5-1.25 mm long, deltoid above the clasping base; bracteoles small, oblong to deltoid. Staminate flowers salverform, white, 13-18 mm long; perianth segments connate for 0.35-0.5 of their length, the tube conic and slightly swollen in the region of the disc, glabrous, stimulose or not; bud broadly and evenly clavate; stamens 10, monadelphous in 2 whorls of unequal length; anthers dorsifixed, the upper whorl exserted, its filaments 8.5-10.5 mm long, connate for 0.75-0.8 of their length; anthers of lower whorl partially exserted to exserted, the filaments 4-7 mm long, connate for 0.7-0.8 mm of their length; pubescent zone ca 1.5 mm long, puberulent to villous, not extending to the glabrous, discoid gland; sterile processes 3, 1.5-3 mm long, filiform. Pistillate flowers salverform, white, 13-19 mm long; perianth segments glabrous, + sparsely stimulose, 10-17 mm long, connate for 0.35-0.65 of their length, the tube subcylindric, tapering slightly upward, not expanding and obcampanulate in age; receptacle green, glabrous, the rim low, entire; ovary 3-4 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, cylindric to oblong-ellipsoid, typically with a cylindric rostrum at the apex, sericeous with upward-appressed hairs, the indumentum often limited to the rostrum, not stimulose; styles 3-5.5 mm long, basally connate for 0.25-0.45 of their length, dichotomized 2-3 times, exserted; gland 1.5-2.2 mm in diam., flat, shallowly lobed; staminodia obscure, deltoid, fleshy. Capsules 9-12 mm long, ellipsoid to slightly ovoid, the apex with a sharp, yellowish beak formed by the indurate style bases; surface irregularly rugulose-pusticulate, pale yellow-green, glabrous overall or hirtellous at the apex, the stinging hairs sparse to abundant; outer pericarp separating from the inner, 0.3-0.6 mm thick, brittle; inner pericarp bony, (0.5) 0.6-0.7 (0.8) mm thick, the columella 9-10 mm long. Seeds elliptic in outline, 8.5-11.5 mm long, 4.5-6 mm wide, W/L = 0.55-0.7, convex dorsally, 3.5-4 mm high, H/L = 0.35-0.5; apex acuminate-apiculate, the apiculus sharp; base truncate to broadly obtuse, shallowly cordate, the surface reddish-brown with abundant darker mottling, appearing black to the naked eye; caruncle fleshy, yellow-brown, depressed-ovate, the apex rounded and exceeding the testa by ca 1 mm, the base cordate around and exceeding the micropyle.

description: Plants, perennial, rhizomatous; rhizomes scaly, stout and short. Culms 0.9-1.6 m tall, 2-3.5 mm diam., erect, terete, hollow, glabrous. Internodes terete, smooth, and glabrous. Nodes densely pubescent, yellowish to brown. Leaves: sheaths 14-23 cm X 6- 7 mm, glabrous; ligules 2.4-3.5 X ca. 2.5 mm, membranous; auricles 3-4.6 mm long, membranous; blades 16-30 cm X (3.8-)5- 7 mm, linear, flat, acute, the margins smooth or somewhat scabrous and glabrous. Peduncles 34-40 cm long. Inflorescences a panicle, 16-20 cm long, pyramidal, contracted, brownish; basal branches 3.3-5.9 cm long; main axis of the inflorescence 14.5-16.3 cm X 0.7-0.9 mm. Spikelets 5.9-6.5 X 1-1.2 mm, dorsally compressed, light brown to stramineous, disarticulating below the glumes; callus obtuse, villous. Glumes coriaceous; first glume 5-5.8 X 1.2-1.8 mm, apex slightly truncate, lanceolate, 9-nerved, abaxially pilose; second glume 5.4-6 X 1.3-1.4 mm, lanceolate, acute, 5-nerved, abaxially keeled. Sterile lemma 3.2-4.6 X 0.7-1 mm, hyaline, ciliate, 2-nerved. Fertile lemma 2.4-4.4 X 1-1.3 mm, bifid, hyaline, 2-nerved, awned. Awn 2.5-3 cm long, geniculate, tightly twisted below the bend. Anthers 3, 2.2-2.5 mm long, dorsifixed, yellow. Caryopses not seen. Sterile pedicel 3-4.5 mm long, vilIous.

description: Small annual; culms and leaf sheaths compressed; blades plicate when young, linear, usually 2-6 cm long, 2-3 mm wide, tapering to acute tip. Inflorescence ter- minal; club-shaped floriferous head usually 0.5-.75 cm long, 2-2.5 mm wide; main axis cylindrical with 2 rows of racemes, each reduced to a single spikelet, embedded in opposite sides; racemes usually numbering 3--5, borne at nodes about 0.25 cm apart. Lower and upper glumes reduced to truncate scales, less than 0.5 mm long, nerveless. Sterile lemma 2-2.5 mm long, 3 nerved, outer face convex; fertile lemma similar; paleas obtuse, the sterile one 2-carinate on back. Caryopsis ovate, about 2 X 1 X 0.75 mm.

description: Robust perennial; culms and leaf-sheaths compressed; blades plicate when young, oblong-linear, usually 5-20 cm long, 5-12 mm wide, obtuse. Inflorescences terminal; floriferous portion usually 6-12 cm long, 3-5 mm wide; main axis flattened, mem- branaceous, with margins toothed at least above, and with a narrow, sinuate midrib between pockets bearing the racemes; racemes usually numbering 10-15, borne at nodes 1-3.5 cm apart below and less than 1 cm apart in middle of inflorescence; each raceme bearing 3-8 spikelets on an angulate rachis. Lower glume obtuse, 1-1.5 mm long, nerveless, commonly erose or ciliate; upper glume acute or acuminate, 4-5 mm long, 7-9 nerved. Sterile lemma 4-5 mm long, 5-7 nerved, outer face flat or convex; fertile lemma similar, 5 nerved; paleas acuminate. Caryopsis oblong, about 1.75 X 1 X 0.5 mm.

description: Robust perennial; culms and leaf-sheaths compressed; blades plicate when young, oblong-lanceolate, usually 10-20 cm long, 7-10 mm wide, abruptly acute. Inflores- cences mostly terminal; floriferous portion usually 10-15 cm long, 3-6 mm wide; main axis strongly flattened, membranaceous, with sinuate margins and narrow, sinuate midrib between pockets bearing the racemes; racemes usually numbering 8-10, borne at nodes 2-3 cm apart below and about 1 cm apart in middle of in- florescence; each raceme bearing 4-8 spikelets on a membranaceous rachis. Lower glume ovate, 2-3 mm long, obtuse or acute, 5-7 nerved; upper glume similar but about 4 mm long. Sterile lemma 4-4.5 mm long, 5-7 nerved, outer face concave; fertile lemma slightly shorter, 3-5 nerved; paleas acuminate. Caryopsis ovate, about 2.5 X 1.75 X 1 mm.

description: Slender annual; culms and leaf sheaths terete; blades flat, lanceolate, usually 3-12 cm long, 4-15 mm wide, gradually tapering to acute tip. Inflorescences mostly ter- minal, floriferous portion usually 5-20 cm long, 1-2 mm wide; main axis cylindrical with 2 rows of racemes embedded on opposite sides; racemes usually numbering at least 20, borne at nodes more than 1 cm apart below and less than 1 cm apart in middle of inflorescence; lower racemes each bearing 3-6 spikelets on an angulate rachis, upper racemes commonly with a single spikelet. Lower glume obtuse or erose, 0.5-1 mm long, nerveless; upper glume obtuse or acute, 1-1.5 mm long, nerveless. Sterile lemma 2.5-3.5 mm long, 3-5 nerved, outer face flat; fertile lemma similar, 3- nerved; sterile palea none; fertile palea acute. Caryopsis oblong-lanceolate, about 1.75 x 0.75 x 0.5 mm.

description: Low-growing perennial; culms and leaf sheaths compressed; blade plicate when young, oblong-linear, usually 2-8 cm long, 3-8 mm wide, obtuse. Inflorescence terminal; club-shaped floriferous head usually 0.5-1.5 cm long, 3-4 mm wide; main axis cylindrical with 2 rows of racemes, each reduced to a single spikelet, embedded on opposite sides; racemes usually numbering 4-6, borne at nodes about 0.25 cm apart. Lower and upper glumes reduced to obtuse scales, about 0.5 mm long, nerveless. Sterile lemma 2-2.5 mm long, 3-5 nerved, outer face convex; fertile lemma similar; paleas obtuse. Caryopsis not seen.

description: Slender perennial; culms and leaf-sheaths compressed; blades plicate when young, oblong-linear, usually 5-12 cm long, 3-6 mm wide, obtuse. Inflorescences terminal; floriferous portion usually 15-25 cm long, 1-3 mm wide; main axis flattened, mem- branaceous, with entire margins and narrow, sinuate midrib between pockets bearing the racemes; racemes usually numbering 12-16, borne at nodes 2-3.5 cm apart below and less than 1 cm apart in middle of inflorescence; each raceme bearing 2-4 spikelets on an angulate rachis. Lower glume emarginate or bilobed, about 0.5 mm long, nerve- less, subtended by a tuft of hairs; upper glume acuminate, about 5 mm long, 7-9 nerved. Sterile lemma about 5 mm long, 5-9 nerved, outer face concave; fertile lemma slightly shorter, 5 nerved; paleas acuminate. Caryopsis not seen.

description: Epiphytes to 20 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid-pyriform, compressed, 2.5-8.0 x 1.2- 4.0 cm, subtended by several distichous, imbricating foliaceous sheaths. Leaves 2, oval to elliptic-oblong, shortly acute to re- tuse, 4.0-14.5 x 4 cm, dark green. Inflorescences few-flowered basal racemes; peduncle 15-25 cm, terete, with 7-10 distant bracts. Flowers dark rose-purple, the labellum white with lilac blotches on callus teeth, mid-lobe tinted lilac, the column white with lilac markings basally tinted pale lilac. Dorsal sepal oblong-obovate, apex conduplicate, apiculate, 1.1 x 0.4 cm. Lateral sepals obliquely elliptic, apex keeled, apiculate, 1.2 x 0.4 cm. Petals obliquely elliptic-oblanceolate, acuminate, 1.0 x 0.4 cm. Labellum trullate, cuneate, lateral lobes spreading, midlobe reflexed, 1. 1 x 0.8 cm, with sparsely hispid 4-ridged callus. Column 0.6 x 0.3 cm, with prominent apical oblong-triangular acuminate auricles and separated, obovate, stigmatic cavities; rostellum shortly bifid extending downward between thick- ened, protruding stigmatic lobes. Pollinarium of 2 obovoid, slightly cleft pollinia, the stipe oblong with involute wings, the vis- cidium elliptic.

description: Perennial, ca l3 m tall, the culms borne close together from the proximate nodes of the rhizome and forming a fascicle held at or above soil level by thick prop roots; culms strongly ribbed, smooth, with 2 visible nodes, the first 3-5 cm from the base, separated from the next by a long internode; nodes brown to black, the lower glabrous, the upper short-pilose in a line on one side, the lowermost nodes (not manifest) bearing expanded, brown, papyraceous sheaths, these glabrous, shiny, narrowed to an acute apex, the lower manifest node bearing a sheath without blade, becoming somewhat expanded with age, at first purplish becoming stramineous, maculate with numerous small round spots, the upper-most manifest node marking the commencement of the arching, graceful leaf complement of 4-8 leaves; leaf sheaths strongly ribbed, the internerves papillate, short-pilose on the overlapping margin and over more of the surface on the upper sheaths, pale green, maculate with dark green; blade 6-7 cm long, 2-2.5 cm wide, ovate-triangular with a slightly asymmetric base, glabrous on both surfaces, with a prominent midrib, + antrorsely scaberulous on both surfaces, pilosulous on the lower nerves at times, the lower surface clearly showing the midvein and 3 or 4 prominent secondary veins on each side, tessellate venation manifest only on the lower surface, the margins of the blade smooth below, increasingly scaberulous upward; petiole 1.2-1.3 mm long, short-pilose on the upper surface, glabrous on the thick midrib of the lower; ligule a tiny short-ciliate membrane ca 0.2 mm long, barely manifest from the outside. Inflorescences borne on a separate culm with leaves consisting of an elongated sheath and rudimentary blade ca 1 cm long, paniculiform, pyramidal, ca 15 cm long, 5 cm wide, the branches whorled, flattened on one side, the lowermost 7-8 cm long, these and the axis densely covered with short white hairs, the branches bearing numerous male spikelets usually in pairs (one long-pedicellate, one short-pedicellate) in alternate fashion along one side of the branch, the branch terminating in 1 or 2 female spikelets. Female spikelets: ca 1 cm long, ovate, borne on a thickened pedicel; lower glume embracing the upper only at the base, ovate with broad flaring margins at base and an acuminate awn-tip, strongly 5-nerved and with transverse veinlets, finely short-pubescent, the margins cartilaginous, the whole glume twisting at maturity of the anthecium; upper glume similar to the lower but with the margins more strongly bowed out below, the apex narrowed but not awn-tipped, strongly 3-nerved and with transverse veinlets, finely short-pubescent, twisting at maturity; lemma ca 7 mm long, narrowly ovate, completely embracing the palea, white, coriaceous when young, glabrous, the surface pitted, 5-nerved and with transverse veinlets; palea slightly shorter than the lemma, of the same tex- ture and surface, with 2 strong nerves and some transverse veinlets; lodicules 3, strongly vascularized, the 2 anterior broad, fleshy, cuneiform, ca 1.2 mm long, the posterior shorter and narrower; staminodes not seen; ovary narrowed into a long flat style parting into 2 plumose stigmas; fruit not seen. Male spikelets without glumes, 7-10 mm long, linear; lemma acuminate at summit and prolonged into an awn, 3- or 4-nerved, membranous, glabrous, diaphanous; palea a little shorter than the lemma, 2-nerved, glabrous, diaphanous; lodicules 3, scarcely vascularized, the anterior pair a little less than 1 mm long, narrow at base and somewhat rounded or truncate at apex, fleshy, the posterior about half as long, fleshy, cuneiform at apex; stamens 3 (4-6), the larger anthers ca 4-5 mm long, orange, basifixed, with attachment of filament to connective on their lower fifth.
bibliographicCitation: Soderstrom, Thomas R. 1981. Sucrea (Poaceae: Bambusoideae), a new genus from Brazil. Brittonia. 33: 198-210.

description: Perennial, 0.5-1 m tall, the culms borne close together from the approximate nodes of the rhizome and forming a fascicle held at or above soil level by thick prop roots; culms strongly ribbed, smooth, with a few nodes, the lowest visible one ca 1/3 from the base, separated from the next by a very long internode; nodes black, glabrous, all except the uppermost bearing an expanded and flattened brown papyraceous sheath narrowed to an acute apex, the surface covered with appressed spicules, the sheaths forming a dense covering to the culms at their base, the terminal node with a short unexpanded sheath merging into the short petiole of the blade, the sheath-petiole to 6 cm long and bearing a large, broad, obovate blade up to 38 cm long and 10 cm wide, ovoid at base and acute at apex, glabrous on both surfaces, with a broad flat glabrous midvein on both surfaces and with 6-8 prominent secondary veins on each side of the midrib, these and the tessellate venation manifest on the lower bluish-green surface, the margins of the blade smooth below, increasingly scaberulous upward; ligule not manifest in the sheath-petiole. Inflorescences on long, pilose peduncles produced in succession (up to 4 in number) at the apex of the culm, subtended by the reduced blade or sheath of the uppermost node, the inflorescences paniculiform, pyra- midal, up to 17 cm long, 8-10 cm wide, the lowermost 6 or 7 branches whorled, up to 10 cm long, these and the axis covered by short white antrorse hairs, the lower branches bearing male spikelets only or male at the base of the branch and female at the summit, as in the upper branches. Female spikelets: 6.5-8.5 mm long, ovate, green with purplish veins, borne on a thickened pedicel; lower glume embracing the upper only at base, ovate with broad margins at base and an acute tip, with the cartilaginous margins fused and producing a tiny awn, strongly 5-nerved with some transverse veinlets, finely short-pubescent, the whole glume twisting at maturity of the anthecium; upper glume similar to the lower but not awn-tipped, strongly 3-nerved with 2 faint lateral nerves at the base and transverse veinlets, finely short-pubescent, twisting at maturity; lemma ca 5.7 mm long, fusiform, embracing the palea almost completely when young, white, at first coriaceous becoming indurate, glabrous, the surface pitted, 5- nerved with transverse veinlets; palea slightly shorter than the lemma, of the same texture and surface, with 2 strong nerves and transverse veinlets; lodicules 3, the 2 anterior broad, fleshy, cuneiform, strongly vascularized, ca 1 mm long, the posterior shorter and much narrower; 3 staminodes present; ovary narrowed into a long flat style parting into 2 plumose stigmas; fruit a caryopsis, with a linear hilum extending its whole length and a small basal embryo. Male spikelets without glumes, 5-7 mm long, linear, maroon; lemma acuminate at summit and prolonged into an awn, 3-nerved, membranous, glabrous except for a few hairs on the awn and nerves, diaphanous; palea a little shorter than the lemma, acute with a slightly bifid apex, 2-nerved, membranous, glabrous, diaphanous; lodicules 3, fleshy, cuneiform, with 1 or 2 vascular traces, the anterior pair ca 0.5 mm long, the posterior narrower and a little shorter; stamens 3, the anthers ca 4 mm long, yellow, ba- sifixed, the filament attached to connective on the lower sixth of the anther.

description: Culmi erecti usque ad 1 m alti, internodio 2-5 mm diametro. Culmorum folia persistentia, nigrescentia: vagina ex parte laxa pilosa; lamina recta, adpressa, anguste triangularis basi subconstricta, 3/5 longitudinem vaginae attingens. Ramificatio intravaginalis. Folia 10-13 in complemento: laminae lineari-lanceolatae apice acuminatae, 6-8 cm longae, 2-5 mm latae, revolutae. Inflorescentia paniculata, spiciformis, 4-10 cm longa, 5-13 mm lata. Spiculae stramineae vel violaceo-stramineae, 3.5-7.5 mm longae, glumis 4. Gluma I, squamiformis, 0.6-1.7 mm longa, uninervis; II, triangularis, apiculata, 2-2.5 mm longa, 3-nervis; III, obovata vel obovato-lanceolata, apiculata, 3.2-5 mm longa, 5-nervis; IV, lineari-lanceolata, apiculata, 5.5-6.6 mm longa, 5-nervis. Lemma oblongo- vel lineari-lanceolatum, apiculatum, 6-7 mm longum, 7-nerve. Palea lemma aequans, bicarinata.
bibliographicCitation: Soderstrom, Thomas R. & Calderón, Cleofe E. 1978. Chusquea and Swallenochloa (Poaceae: Bambusoideae) : generic relationships and new species. Brittonia. 30: 297-312.

description: Dense clump-forming bamboo with pachymorph rhizomes and erect culms 0.3-1 m tall, 2-5 mm in diam; internodes cylindrical, solid (with thick walls and pith) at least below, in some fistulose higher on the culm, stramineous to dark brown, glabrous. Culm leaves persistent, becoming black with age and disintegrating in place, ca 5 cm long, the blade ca 3/5 as long as the sheath: sheath in part weakly pilose; blade erect, appressed, narrowly triangular, slightly constricted at the base, with an acuminate apex, sparingly pubescent on the outer surface, sparingly pilose on the inner; inner ligule apically convex, membranous, a little less than 1 mm long. Nodes at mid-culm with a central appressed branch and 1-3 collateral branches on each side. Branching intravaginal. Foliage leaves 10-13 per complement: blades linear- lanceolate, 6-8 cm long, 2-5 mm wide, revolute, narrowing abruptly at the summit and tipped by a slender rough to smooth awnlike apex 6-8 mm long and rounded at the base into a very short (1 mm to sub-obsolete) glabrous petiole, hispid through- out on both surfaces, the hairs longer on the lower surface, the margins cartilaginous and revolute, secondary veins usually 2 on each side, tertiary 3-6 (more commonly 4 or 5) in each space, the transverse veinlets not manifest; sheath pilose; outer ligule lacking; inner ligule a little less than 1 mm long, rounded, with a ciliolate margin. Inflorescence a narrow, secund panicle 4-10 cm long, 5-13 mm wide, terminal to branches with reduced leaf-blades; peduncle a little shorter than the sheath that embraces it, the uppermost blade embracing or sometimes overtopping the panicle; rachis strigose-hispid, the branches and pedicels sub-lanate, short, appressed, the pedicels 1-4 mm long. Spikelets stramineous to stramineous-violet, slightly com- pressed laterally, obovate-lanceolate, 3.5-7.5 mm long, held erect on antrorsely sca- berulous pedicels 1 mm or less long. Transitional glumes 4 (rarely 5): I, scalelike and rounded apically, 0.6-1.7 mm long, stramineous-violet, 1-nerved, appressed- puberulent; II, scalelike and rounded apically or triangular-apiculate, ca 2-4 times as long as the first glume, 2-2.5 mm long, stramineous-violet, 3-nerved, appressed- puberulent; III, obovate or obovate-lanceolate, apiculate, 3.2-5 mm long, stramin- eous-violet, 5-nerved, on the outside appressed-puberulent, on the inside glabrous below, appressed-puberulent above; IV, linear-lanceolate, apiculate, 5.5-6.6 mm long, stramineous-violet, 5-nerved, on the outside appressed-puberulent, on the inside glabrous below, appressed-puberulent above. Lemma oblong- to linear-lanceolate, apiculate, 6-7 mm long, pale green, 7-nerved, glabrous below, puberulent toward the summit. Palea equal to or a little shorter than the lemma, 2-keeled (each keel a nerve), flat below and glabrous with a puberulent sulcus above between the keels. Lodicules 3, the 2 anterior 1.4 mm long, spathulate, strongly vascularized with the upper margins ciliate, the posterior ca 0.8 mm long, spathulate, weakly vascularized with the upper margins ciliate. Stamens 3, the anthers yellow, ca 2.7 mm long. Ovary with 2 styles, each terminating in a plumose stigma.

description: Culmi erecti vel subscandentes usque ad 10 m alti, internodio 2-3 cm diametro. Culmorum folia persistentia: vagina firma, infra glabra, superne papillosa; lamina recta, 1/4 longitudinem vaginae attingens, anguste triangularis apiculata, glabra. Ramificatio intravaginalis. Folia 5-8 in comple- mento: laminae ascendentes, lanceolatae, 34 cm longae, 2 cm latae, utrinque glabrae; vaginae com- pressae-carinatae, glabrae. Inflorescentia paniculata, ca 50 cm longa ramis infernis usque ad 10 cm longis; rhachis ? triquetra, ca 2.2 mm lata. Spiculae violaceo-stramineae, teretes, obtriangulares, 5.5-7.5 mm longae, oblique dispositae, glumis 4. Gluma I, ca 0.9 mm longa, glabra; II, spathulata, 1.3-1.8 mm longa, glabra, 1-nervis; III, triangularis, apiculata, 3.5 mm longa, 2- vel 3-nervis, glabra; IV, triangularis, apiculata, parce tessellata, 5.4 mm longa, 3-7-nervis. Lemma obovato- triangulare, apiculatum, 7.5 mm longum, indistincte 9-nervatum. Palea 6.2 mm longa, 4-6-nervata.

description: Bamboo with 30-50 erect or subscandent culms to 10 m tall and 2-3 cm in diam, the tallest arching and drooping; internodes with the pith breaking down upon desiccation, stramineous, glabrous. Culm leaves persistent, rotting away as the branches grow, strongly fibrous: sheath firm, 18 cm long, the outer surface glabrous on the lower half, papillose on the upper half, the inner surface smooth, shiny; blade erect, continuous with the sheath, ca one-fourth as long as the sheath (in the single exam- ple available), narrowly triangular, apiculate, smooth on the abaxial surface, strongly nerved and antrorsely hirtellous on the adaxial surface; inner ligule membranous, truncate, ca 2 mm long, ciliolate on the margin, pilose on the abaxial surface. Nodes at mid-culm containing a central branch, flanked by 1-5 smaller collateral branches. Branching intravaginal: lateral branches sometimes rebranching, all branches appressed to the culm and each terminating (in our specimen) in a spikelike inflores- cence. Foliage leaves 5-8 in a compressed-keeled leaf complement: blades ascending, lanceolate, firm, 34 cm long, ca 2 cm wide, with a strong midvein prominent on the abaxial surface, depressed on the adaxial surface, glabrous on both surfaces, abscissile leaving a broad more or less flat cupule, with a glabrous petiole 3-4 mm long; sheaths compressed-keeled with a thick midrib, light purplish-green becoming stramineous, glabrous; outer ligule a minute glabrous rim; inner ligule long-attenuate, charta- ceous, up to 7 cm long, strongly nerved, sparingly tessellate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescence a compressed panicle terminating leafy branches, ca 50 cm long, the lower branches to 10 cm long, secund, with the opposite side of the rachis flat; rachis more or less triquetrous, with the broadest flat side ca 2.2 mm wide, pubescent. Spikelets stramineous with a violet blush, terete, obtriangular, 5.5-7.5 mm long, held obliquely on sparsely pubescent pedicels 2-3.5 mm long. Transitional glumes 4: I, scalelike, ca 0.9 mm long, glabrous; II, scalelike, spathulate, 1.3-1.8 mm long, 1-nerved, glabrous; III, triangular, apiculate, 3.5 mm long, 2- or 3-nerved, glabrous; IV, triangular, apiculate, 5.4 mm long, 3-7-nerved, sparingly tessellate. Lemma papyraceous, obovate-triangular, glabrous and shining, stramineous with a violet blush, apiculate, 7.5 mm long, indistinctly 9-nerved. Palea papyraceous, 6.2 mm long, flat on the back with the 2 central nerves thickened above and sulcate between them, 4-6-nerved. Lodicules 3, the 2 anterior 1.2 mm long, thickened on the lower half toward the inner margins, spathulate, the upper margins ciliolate, the posterior lodicule thin throughout, narrow-spathulate, the upper margins ciliolate. Stamens 3, the anthers yellow, linear, 2.8-4.4 mm long, the filaments attached to the connective at the lower quarter. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, with 2 styles each bearing a plumose stigma. Fruit unknown.

description: Culmi arcuati usque ad 10 m alti, internodio 3 cm diametro. Culmorum folia triangularia tarde decidua: vagina 14 cm longa, lamina 5-7-plo longior, utrinque glabra; lamina recta, dehiscens, 3 cm longa, intus puberula, extus glabra. Ramificatio intravaginalis. Folia 5-8 in complemento: laminae lineari-lanceolatae, attenuatae apice filiformi, usque ad 20 cm longae, forte tessellatae et utrinque glabrae, marginibus albis cartilagineis; vaginae parce compressae-carinatae folio 2-plo brevior, glabrae; inflorescentia paniculata usque ad 30 cm longa, ramis appressis usque ad 9 cm longis. Spiculae pedicello usque ad 7 cm longo, erectae, lineari-obovatae, 8-9 mm longae, glumis 4. Gluma I, rotundata, 1.3 mm longa, enervis; II, rotundata, 1.9 mm longa, scaberula, enervis; III, oblongo-lanceolata, scaberula, 6.2 mm longa, 5-nervis; IV, oblongo-lanceolata, scaberula, 7.2 mm longa, 5-nervis. Lemma obovatum, 3.8 mm longum, 9-nerve. Palea tessellata, apicem versus pubes- cens caeterum glabra, 5-7-nervis.

description: Dense clump-forming bamboo with pachymorph rhizomes and erect culms up to 10 m tall, 3 cm in diam, arching above; internodes solid, stramineous, glabrous. Culm leaves tardily shed, triangular, the sheath 5-7 times as long as the blade with which it is contiguous and from which it is hardly distinguishable: sheath 14 cm long, finely ridged, glabrous on both surfaces; blade erect, dehiscent, 3 cm long, puberulent on the inner surface, glabrous on the outer surface; inner ligule a hard smooth membrane ca 0.6 mm long, with a ciliolate margin. Nodes at mid-culm delimited by 2 well-defined ridges, and with a central larger branch and usually 2-5 collateral branches on each side. Branching intravaginal. Foliage leaves 5-8 per complement: blades linear-lanceolate, long-attenuate above with a threadlike tip, up to 20 cm long, strongly tessellate and glabrous on both surfaces, with a firm midvein on both surfaces and white cartilaginous margins, scabrous along the edges, with a petiole 1.3 mm long; sheaths green-stramineous, slightly compressed and keeled above, ca 1/2 as long as the blade, strongly ribbed, glabrous, extending along one margin into an auricle ca 2 mm long, pilose on the upper margin; outer ligule an inconspicuous glabrous rim ca 0.2-0.3 mm long; inner ligule a glabrous membrane with an irregular broadly dentate margin. Inflorescence a narrow panicle up to 30 cm long, with appressed branches up to 9 cm long; peduncle terete, slightly to long-exserted, villous; rachis strongly angled, villous, flat along one side where branches not produced. Spikelets dark violet, somewhat compressed laterally, linear- obovate, 8-9 mm long, held erect on antrorsely scabrous pedicels up to 7 cm long. Transitional glumes 4, scaberulous: I, a rounded, nerveless scale 1.3 mm long; II, a rounded, nerveless scale 1.9 mm long, with a tuft of hairs on the upper margin; III, oblong-lanceolate, 6.2 mm long, 5-nerved, ciliolate on the upper margins; IV, oblong-lanceolate, 7.2 mm long, ciliolate on the upper margins, 5-nerved. Lemma obovate, 3.8 mm long, purplish-stramineous, 9-nerved. Palea membranous, papyra- ceous, a little shorter than the lemma, 5-7-nerved with cross veins, 2 nerves forming keels above with an included sulcus apically, glabrous over most of the surface except at the summit where pubescent on and between the keels. Lodicules 3, the 2 anterior ca 1.4 mm long, thickened below, membranous above with ciliate upper margins, several-nerved, spathulate, the posterior lodicule ovoid, slightly thickened below, membranous above, glabrous with a ciliate upper margin. Stamens 3, the anthers yellow, ca 4 mm long, the filament attached to the connective 1/4 of the length from the base, dehiscence by an apical pore from each theca. Ovary glabrous, with 2 styles, each bearing a plumose stigma. Fruit unknown.

description: Gramen perenne; culmi caespitosi, erecti, graciles, ramosi, glabri vel sparsim non nisi sub inflo- rescentia papilloso-pilosi, 35-40 cm longi; vaginae compressae, carinatae saltem sub fauce, minimum superne dense hirtae, marginibus ciliatae; ligula anguste deltata, membranacea, 1.5-2 mm longa; laminae plicatae, angustissime lineares, attenuatae, utrinque puberulae villosaeque, 6-20 cm longae, ca 1 mm latae, marginibus ciliatae; racemi terminales, solitarii, arcuati, 1-4 cm longi; rhachis alata, 3-4 mm lata, dorsaliter et ad margines dense pilis fortibus aureisque instructa; spiculae ellipticae, ca 2 mm longae, 0.6 mm latae; gluma prima carens; gluma secunda elliptica, acuta vel parum erosa, tenuis autem firma, anthoecio paulo brevior, glabra vel ad apicem sparsim pilosa, 3-nervia; lemma sterile elliptico-oblongum, subinduratum, sub apicem cristatum, ceterius glabrum; anthoecium regu- lariter papilloso-striatum, 1.7 mm longum; lemma fertile ad apicem pilosum.

description: Perennial; culms densely tufted, erect, slender, branching freely, glabrous or sparsely papillose-pilose below inflorescence only, 35-40 cm long; nodes retrorse- ly bearded; leaf sheaths longer or shorter than internodes, compressed-keeled at least upwards, densely shaggy with long tubercle-based hairs at least towards throat, the margins ciliate; ligule narrowly deltoid, membranous, 1.5-2 mm; leaf blades folded, very narrowly linear, attenuate, puberulent and shaggily pilose on both surfaces, 6-20 cm long, ca 1 mm broad, the margins ciliate with tubercle- based spreading hairs, these reaching 7 mm in length; racemes terminal, solitary, long-exserted, distinctly arcuate, 1-4 cm long; rachis winged, 3-4 mm broad overall, practically concealing the spikelets, the dorsal surface and margins dense- ly covered with stout golden hairs arising from large tubercles; spikelets elliptical, ca 2 mm long by 0.6 mm broad; first glume minute or lacking; second glume elliptical, acute or slightly erose, thin but fairly firm, a little shorter than the anthoecium, glabrous or with a very few apical hairs, 3-nerved, the midnerve usually suppressed and the lateral pair becoming rather prominent towards the base; sterile lemma elliptical-oblong, subindurate, sulcate and early-splitting, gla- brous except for a weak crest near summit of each half; sterile palea well de- veloped, slightly shorter than lemma, hyaline at center, the margins firm; an- thoecium pale, regularly striate, 1.7 mm long, the lemma bearing a strong apical tuft of white hairs, the palea rather delicate, glabrous.

description: Perennial; culms tufted, erect, moderately robust, simple, glabrous, 50-70 cm long; nodes densely retrorsely bearded; leaf sheaths longer or shorter than in- ternodes, compressed-keeled, rather lax, exposing culms, densely pilose with tubercle-based hairs, the margins ciliate; ligule erose, membranous, ca 1.5 mm; leaf blades flat, narrowly lanceolate, acuminate, both surfaces pubescent and also pilose with long tubercle-based hairs, the margins ciliate, 8-15 cm long, 1.5- 4 mm broad, the uppermost reduced; racemes terminal, solitary, short- to long- exserted, arcuate, tapering to a point, 8-13 cm long; rachis winged, 3-4 mm broad overall, almost concealing the spikelets, the dorsal surface sparsely pilose with weak white hairs, the margins bearing soft, white, tubercle-based cilia; spike- lets narrowly elliptical, pale to purplish, ca 3.1 mm long (excluding callus), 0.7 mm broad, the callus rather large; first glume lacking; second glume narrowly elliptical, entire, acute, more or less the length of the anthoecium, 3-nerved, the midnerve often reduced or suppressed, glabrous or sparsely and softly pilose near apex, hyaline at center, the margins firm and ciliate with soft white hairs; sterile lemma elliptical, subindurate, sulcate and early-splitting right to the base, glabrous except for subapical crest on each half and occasional pubescence on keels; sterile palea well developed, slightly shorter than lemma, hyaline at center, the margins firm; anthoecium pale or purple, minutely and regularly papillose-striate, ca 2.5 mm long, the lemma glabrous except for a strong apical tuft of white hairs, the palea subacute, glabrous.

description: Gramen perenne; culmi usque ad 60 cm longi, erecti vel ascendentes, ramosi, pubescentes; vaginae internodiis breviores, compressae, carinatae, glabrae vel sparsim pilosae, marginibus ciliatae; ligula brevis, truncata; laminae planae, lineares, acuminatae, utrinque puberulae, 3.5-10 cm longae, 4 mm latae; racemi terminales et axillares, 1-4, 5-7 cm longi; rhachis 1 mm lata, intra pubescens, marginibus minute scabra, pilis paucis longis instructa; spiculae 2.4-2.6 mm longae, glabrae; gluma prima bre- vissima, membranacea; gluma secunda fructu paulo brevior, conspicue 7-nervis, obtusa; lemma sterile fructum paulo excedens, minute papillosum; fructus 2.1 mm longus, ellipticus, acutus, papillosus, pallens.

description: Perennial; culms tufted, erect or ascending, moderately slender, compressed, mostly branching, glabrous or pubescent, up to 60 cm long; sheaths shorter than internodes, compressed-keeled, glabrous or with short isolated tubercle-based hairs, the margins ciliate; ligule short, truncate, membranaceous with a row of white hairs behind; blades flat, linear, acuminate, puberulent on both surfaces, 3.5-10 cm long, 4 mm wide; inflorescences terminal or axillary, of 1-4 arcuate racemes, 5-7 cm long; rhachis narrowly winged, ca 1 mm wide, pubescent on inner surface, margins minutely scabrous with scattered straggly tubercle-based hairs up to 3.5 mm long; spikelets elliptical-oblong, glabrous, 2.4-2.6 mm long, the pedicels pubescent; first glume very short, obtuse, membranaceous, nerveless; second glume ca 4/5 the length of the fertile floret, obtuse, conspicuously 7-nerved, the nerves often anastomosing at the summit; sterile lemma slightly longer than the fertile floret, firm, minutely papillose, splitting late or not at all; sterile palea well-developed, slightly shorter than the lemma, hyaline; fruit 2.1 mm long, elliptical, acute, pale, papillose.

description: Perennial; culms tufted, erect, moderately robust, branching below, glabrous or sparsely pilose near nodes and below inflorescence, up to 12 dm long; nodes retrorsely bearded; leaf sheaths usually shorter than internodes, occasionally longer and overlapping below, compressed-keeled towards throat, glabrous to papillose-pilose, the margins ciliate; ligule truncate, membranous, ca 2 mm, with numerous white hairs behind, these up to 5 mm; leaf blades flat, linear, acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, 6-30 cm long, up to 9 mm broad, the margins sparsely tubercular-ciliate; racemes terminal, solitary or frequently 2-3 on a short common axis, long-exserted, slightly to strongly arcuate, 9-16 cm long; rachis narrowly winged, ca 2 mm broad overall, the dorsal surface glabrous or puber- ulent near base, the margins strongly papillose, densely ciliate, the hairs white, weak, disorderly, up to 10 mm long; spikelets elliptical, ca 4 mm long, 1.4 mm broad;first glume 1.2 mm long, broadly deltoid, membranous, nerveless, glabrous or occasionally bearing a few sparse hairs near apex; second glume elliptical, subacute, firm, a little shorter than the anthoecium, glabrous or weakly pubes- cent at margins, (5) 7-nerved, the nerves reticulate and often excurrent at apex; sterile lemma elliptical-oblong, subindurate, sulcate and late-splitting, glabrous or occasionally weakly pilose near apex, nerves reticulate above; sterile palea well developed, as long as lemma, hyaline at center, the margins firm; anthoecium pale to purplish, regularly striate, 3.5 mm long, the lemma slightly tufted at the apex, otherwise glabrous, the palea firm, glabrous.

description: Probably perennial; culms tufted, erect, slender, simple, glabrous, up to 55 cm long; sheaths shorter than internodes, compressed-keeled, glabrous or puberulent with isolated long tubercle-based hairs, especially near throat; ligule membra- naceous, subacute or erose, ca 2 mm long; blades flat, linear, acuminate, densely puberulent on both surfaces, 2.5-12 cm long, up to 2.5 mm wide; racemes ter- minal, solitary, arcuate, 2.0-4.5 cm long, short- to long-exserted on very slender pedicels; rhachis winged, ca 2 mm wide, embracing the base of the spikelets, glabrous, the margins minutely scabrous; spikelets 1.4-1.6 mm long, 0.7 mm wide, elliptical, subacute, the pedicels densely pubescent; first glume 0.3 mm long, obtuse, membranaceous, nerveless, scale-like; second glume as first, 0.4 mm long; sterile lemma length of fertile floret, sulcate, very thinly membrana- ceous, 3-nerved but the mid-nerve usually suppressed, glabrous or with isolated hairs; sterile palea lacking; fertile floret subacute, stramineous; fertile lemma strongly convex, indurate, glabrous, regularly and conspicuously papillose, al- most enclosing fertile palea; fertile palea elliptical, depressed and papillose between nerves, the margins hyaline.

description: Gramen perenne; culmi robusti; erecti, ramosi, pubescentes; vaginae laxae, inferiores pubescentes, ad summum villosae, suprema glabra; ligula acuta, 5-6 mm longa; laminae lineares, supra minute denseque pubescentes, subtus glabrae, 12-30 cm longae; racemi 1-3, terminales et axillares, arcuati, 14-30 cm longi; rhachis alata, ca 2 mm lata, secus marginem longe ciliata; spiculae 3.5-4.0 mm longae, ellipticae; gluma prima brevissima, gluma secunda parum brevior vel fructum aequans, ad basin et secus marginem pilosum, ad apicem glabra, 5-nervis; lemma sterile fructum superans, acutum, carinis minute pubescens, apice barbatum; palea sterilis lemma aequans; fructus induratus, ellipticus; lemma fertile minute papiloso-striatum, secus marginem et ad apicem pilosum; palea fertilis ad apicem minute barbata, marginibus hyalina.

description: Perennial; culms robust, erect or ascending, branching at lower nodes, terete, pubescent, villous below and at nodes; sheaths lax, compressed-keeled, the lower pubescent below, becoming densely villous above and at throat, with two tufts of hairs at collar, the uppermost glabrous, elongate; ligule acute or irregular, thinly membranaceous, 5-6 mm; blades linear, acuminate, adaxial surface mi- nutely and densely pubescent, abaxial surface glabrous, 12-30 cm long, 4-7 mm wide, the uppermost much reduced; inflorescences terminal and axillary; racemes 1-3, arcuate, short- to long-exserted, 14-30 cm long; rhachis winged, ca 2 mm wide, margins untidily long-ciliate, white hairs up to 4 mm long; pedicels short, densely pilose; spikelets 3.5-4.0 mm long, 0.8 mm wide, elliptical; first glume usually minute, rarely as much as 1/6 length of spikelet, membranaceous; second glume equal to or slightly shorter than fertile floret, pilose at base and along margin, glabrous or with isolated hairs above, 5-nerved; sterile lemma longer than fertile floret, acute, indurate, sulcate, splitting, each half with a tuft of white hairs at base, hispid-ciliate at apex, and a line of minute pubescence along keel, oth- erwise glabrous; sterile palea well-developed, length of lemma; fertile floret in- durate, elliptical; fertile lemma regularly and minutely papillose-striate, the upper margins and summit pilose; fertile palea bearing a minute tuft of hairs at summit, the margins hyaline.

description: Culmi brevissimi foliis confertis. Foliorum laminae breves et latae vel lineares. Ligula membranacea, glabra. Paniculae compactissima vel capitiformis. Glumae 2, 1-nerves, apiculatae, glabrae. Flos 1, rhachilla non producta. Lemma pubescens, abrupte apiculatum vel apiculo in aristam brevissimum paulo prolongato, 1-5-nerve. Palea 1-nervis apice acumine vel 2-nervis apice 2-dentatum. Hilum punctiforme.

description: Very small annual alpine grass, 0.4-1 cm tall and up to 2 cm across from leaf tip to leaf tip, plants sometimes bearing basal innovations that give rise to smaller secondary tufts. Culm very condensed and completely concealed by the several closely packed leaves; nodal pulvini absent. Leaves short and very broad, often without external indication of the ligule position, or the lower leaves with broad sheath and linear blade, 1 or 2 hyaline scales (reduced leaves) occasionally present between the uppermost fully-formed leaf and the inflorescence. Sheaths green or hyaline with broad membranous, free margins. Ligule ca 0.3 mm long, an entire membranous flap arching across the leaf, everywhere the same length or slightly longer at the middle, glabrous. Auricles absent. Leaf blade flat or folded, soft, glabrous and smooth, apex cucullate. Inflorescence terminal, closely surrounded by the leaves and usually shorter than them. Panicle capitate or very compact; main axis stout, condensed, with primary branches (up to 16) issuing from about its apex. Primary branches giving rise to 2-10 secondary branches each bearing a spikelet (small plants with only 1 to few spikelets, larger plants with up to 30 spikelets). Spikelets hermaphrodite, laterally compressed, disarticulating above the glumes, 3-3.5 mm long (including mucro). Glumes 2, equal, each slightly shorter to slightly longer than the lemma, glabrous, 1-veined, apiculate (the sometimes recurved), membranous except for narrow green strips beside the vein; the vein thickening and hardening with age, forming a keel in the lower half. Floret 1, rachilla not prolonged. Lemma 3-3.5 mm long, membranous but slightly firmer than the glumes, slightly keeled and uniformly pubescent on the back, apiculate, with wide, gradual or abrupt shoulders below the point; apiculum some- times extending into a short (less than 1 mm), straight, smooth or scabrid awnlet; lemma veins 1-5, the midvein strong and reaching the apex, lateral veins when present short and faint; callus obscure, glabrous. Palea subequal to or slightly 2-veined with 2 apical points (not awns) and rounded on the back or 1-veined with 1 point and somewhat keeled on the back (the keel not scabrid) and resem- bling the lemma. Lodicules 2, free, glabrous, veinless, slightly fleshy at base and membranous distally, unequally 2-lobed, the lobes pointed. Stamen number un- certain, 2 or 3; anthers ca 0.4-0.6 mm long, yellow or white, exserted from the tip of the floret at anthesis. Ovary glabrous, oblong; styles 2, free, terminal, style and stigma together ca 1 mm long; the stigma branching very near the base, white, plumose, protruding from the tip of the floret at anthesis. Caryopsis pale brown, 1.3-1.7 mm long, broadest above the middle, laterally compressed, ungrooved, pericarp not free. Embryo 2/% as long as the caryopsis, protruding prominently at the base; endosperm hard, staining intensely with lipid stains, starch grains compound. Hilum reddish, punctate, 1/8-1/7 as long as the caryopsis.
bibliographicCitation: Macfarlane, Terry D. & But, Paul P. 1982. Tovarochloa (Poaceae: Pooideae), a new genus from the high Andes of Peru. Brittonia. 34: 478-481.

description: Plants usually glabrous throughout except for the upper surface of the blades along the midrib near the base. Sometimes a considerable portion of the upper surface of the blade may be sparsely pilose, especially on specimens from Florida and along the Gulf Coast; occasionally, the pubescence may extend to the young sheaths of the branches. The more pubescent forms connect the typical subspecies with ssp. hispidum, which occurs in Mexico. The terminal inflorescences are usually in digitate clusters of two or three spikes, while the axillary spikes may be single. Sometimes, especially in Texas, the terminal spikes are also single.

description: Leaves mostly 1-2 cm broad, often hispidulous on the upper surface; sheaths, especially the lower, sometimes hispid; terminal racemes usually 3-5; staminate spikelets 7-9 mm long, spindle-shaped, often rather abruptly narrowed above the middle, one of the pair distinctly pediceled (Hitchcock, 1906; 1951, p. 792). The type is considered to be Hartweg 252 from "Aguas Calientes" (Hitchcock, 1906; Cutler & Anderson, 1941), which I have not seen.

description: Culm robust, 1 cm in diameter, glabrous; sheaths glabrous or pubescent above; auricle more densely pilose; ligule very short, scarcely 3 mm long, fimbriate; blade 4.5-6.5 cm wide, sulcate, upper surface pilose, lower surface minutely tuberculate scabrous or glabrescent; spikes of terminal inflorescence 5-8, compressed, drooping, more slender than those of T. dactyloides; staminate spikelets sessile or nearly so, 3-4 mm long; outer glumes oblong, rounded at apex, scabrous-ciliate on marginal keels, rather minutely striate with about 10 nerves.

description: Stems 3-4.5 m tall, glabrous; leaf sheaths glabrous; blades up to 8 dm long and 9 cm wide, glabrous, long acuminate; branches of terminal inflorescences usually 5 to 8, sometimes fewer as on lateral branches, flexuous, up to 2 dm long; pistillate spikelets ca. 5 mm long, the outer scale ovate; staminate spikelets 8-9 mm long, outer glume elliptical acuminate or oblanceolate with obtuse tip, one sessile or rarely with a short pedicel, the other on a slender pedicel 3-4 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Randolph, Lowell F. 1970. Variation among Tripsacum populations of Mexico and Guatemala. Brittonia. 22: 305-337.

description: Robust perennial up to 4.5 m tall, densely caespitose; culm thick, erect, cylindrical at base, up to 4 cm in diam., completely glabrous, extensively branched at maturity with primary and secondary branches; blade glabrous, margins serrulate; basal leaves oblanceolate, 1.5-2 m long, 7-10 cm wide, narrow at the base; blades of the middle and the topmost leaves lanceolate; auricles wide and well defined; sheaths at base densely hirsute throughout, not compressed, those of the middle section densely hirsute along two-thirds of its lower portion, or totally hirsute; sheaths of upper leaves glabrous (scabrous or rugose), or totally hirsute; terminal inflorescence of 18-50 branches, central rachis thickened with primary, secondary, and tertiary branching; spikes slender, flexuous, and drooping, up to 25 cm long, pistillate portion from 0-3 cm long, often absent in upper portion of inflorescence; pistillate segment of the lateral spikes much longer than of the terminal; staminate spikelets in pairs, one sessile, the other with a very slender pedicel 4-6 mm long; glumes slender lanceolate, acute, soft, 6-8 mm long; internodes of rachis unequal; pistillate spikelets flattened, 4 mm long, glumes cuneate. Chromosome number 2n = 36
bibliographicCitation: Randolph, Lowell F. 1970. Variation among Tripsacum populations of Mexico and Guatemala. Brittonia. 22: 305-337.

description: Gramen perenne, leniter rhizomatosum; culmi erecti, 6-15 dm alti, interdum ramificantes supra; laminae planae, 9-15 cm x 1.5-8.5 mm, ad apicem acuminatum angustatae; inflorescentia paniculata 1 1-29 x 2-15 cm, ramis omnibus juventute ascendentibus, ramis infemis demum laxioribus; spiculae 2 (interdum 3)-florae, 3-5.2 mm longae; glumae primae 1-nervatae, in carina atque marginibus scabrellae, lanceolatae 1.8-2.5 mm longae, apice acutae, glumae alterae naviculares, anguste ellipticae 2.8-3.8 mm longae, apice acuminatae, 3-nervatae, costa nonnum quam scabrellae; lemmata lanceolata, dorsaliter rotundata, obscure 5-nervata, glabra, infima 2.7-4.3 mm, altera 2.7-3.5 mm longa, dentibus apicalibus 0.1-0.2 mm longis; paleae lemmate 1/2-4/5-plo longiores, nervis 2 prominentibus percursae; rachillae rectae vel sigmoideae, prope apicem pilis 1-1.8 mm longis instructae; aristae 0.6-1.2 mm infra apicem lemmatis ortae, graciles atque flexibiles, saepe tortae, 3.6-5.7 mm longae; stamina 0.5- 0.9 mm longa; lodiculae oblongae truncatae 0.2-0.3 mm longae; caryopsides complanatae pallide fuscae translucentes 1.7-2.2 x 0.4-0.6 mm; endospermium molle, non liquescens; embryo caryopside 1/5-plo brevior.
bibliographicCitation: Morden, Clifford W. & Valdés-Reyna, Jesús. 1983. Trisetum curvisetum (Poaceae: Aveneae), a new species from Mexico. Brittonia. 35: 374-378.

description: Perennial grass, weakly rhizomatous, rhizome internodes 1-4 cm long glabrous, scale leaves 1.7 mm long acute; culms erect 6-15 dm tall, 0.7-1.7 mm thick, occasionally branching above; prophyll 1.5-2.0 cm long membranous 3-lobed, with the 2 nerves running to cleft between lobes. Leaf sheath shorter than culm internodes, glabrous to hirtellous with hairs 0.5-1 mm long; ligule truncate, entire or erose, 1.1-2.3 mm long; blade flat (5) 9-15 (19) cm x 1.5-8.5 mm, tapering to an acuminate apex, hirtellous on adaxial surface primarily on leaf veins, with hairs 0.5-1 mm long, abaxial surface glabrous. Inflorescence a panicle 11-29 x 2-15 cm, all branches ascending when young, the lower ones becoming lax with maturity; lower inflorescence nodes with 3-5 branches per node, the branches unequal, the shortest 1-4 cm, the longest 5-14 cm long, all floriferous from the base or not, the lower nodes 2-10 cm apart, becoming crowded near the apex with branches 1-3 cm long. Spikelets 2 (3)-flowered, 3.0-5.2 mm long. First glume 1-nerved, minutely scabrous on keel and margins, lanceolate acuminate 1.8-2.5 mm long, 1/2-2/3 as long as second glume. Second glume navicular, narrowly elliptic acuminate 2.8-3.8 mm long, 3-nerved, the lateral nerves extending 2/3 the length of the glume, the midnerve minutely scabrous or not. Florets proportionally similar, the second 1/2-2/3 the length of the lowermost, the third when present about 2/3 the length of the second. Lemmas lanceolate, rounded on back, obscurely 5-nerved, glabrous, the lowermost 2.7-4.3 mm, the second 2.7-3.5 mm, the third about 2.5 mm long, the apical teeth 0.1-0.2 mm long. Paleas 1/2_4/5 as long as lemma, prominently 2-nerved, the lowermost 2.3-3.1 mm, the second 2.0-2.5 mm long. Rachilla straight or sigmoid, puberulent on abaxial surface, shortly villous near apex, 1.0-1.8 mm long. Awns arising 0.6-1.2 mm below apex of lemma, thin and flexuous, often twisting, (1.5) 3.6-5.7 mm long. Stamens 3, 0.5- 0.9 mm long (0.3 mm in third floret). Ovary broadly ellipsoid, 0.4-0.8 mm long, style branches 2, 0.4-1.0 mm long. Lodicules oblong truncate, 0.2-0.3 mm long, nerveless. Caryopsis flattened, light brown, translucent, 1.7-2.2 x 0.4-0.6 mm; endosperm soft, not milky; embryo 1/5 the length of the caryopsis.
bibliographicCitation: Morden, Clifford W. & Valdés-Reyna, Jesús. 1983. Trisetum curvisetum (Poaceae: Aveneae), a new species from Mexico. Brittonia. 35: 374-378.

description: Herba epiphytica, silvicola. Rhizoma et radices non visa. Pseudo bulbus (imperfectus) apice bifoliatus. Folia elliptico-oblanceolata, acutis- sima, inferne in petiolum angustata, chartacea. Pedunculus nudus, vagin- aruin dense imbricatarum fasiculo infra racemum ornatus. Flores pro genere parvi. Sepala similia, oblongo-ovata, acuta vel acuminata, lateralia basi valde coneava. Petala lanceolato-linearia. Labellum ecarinatum, super medium trilobatum, parte basali in positu naturali columnam eircumdans, lobo medio ovato recurvato. Columna crassa, supra leviter dilatata.
bibliographicCitation: Merrill, Elmer D. 1941. Plants Collected on the Vernay-Cutting Expedition. Brittonia. 4 (1): 23-68.

description: Plant epiphytic, sonmetimes exceeding 3.7 dm. high. Rhizome, roots and complete pseudobulb absent in our specimen. Pseudobulb apparenltly com- planate-eylindric (only the apical portion present), bifoliate at the apex, greenish yellow and dull in the dried specimen. Leaves elliptic-oblanceolate, sharply acute, gradually narrowed below into a short suleate petiole, up to 18.5 em. long and 3.5 em. wide, chartaceous, with about 7 more prominient nerves beneath. Infloreseence terminal, up to 3.5 dm. long, glabrous, naked below. Just below the raceme and sometimes interrupting the raceme there is a cluster of densely imbricating distichous bracts which is 2.7-4.5 cm. long. Rachis lightly fractiflex. Floral bracts deciduous. Flowers rather numerous and dense, mostly simultaneous but the lower ones (where sepa- rated by a cluster of imbricated bracts) deciduous, "rich mahogany red with black tip, " small for the genus. Dorsal sepal oblong-ovate, acute, about 11 mm. long and 6 mm. wide, 5-nerved. Lateral sepals similar, about 12 mm. long and 5.5-5.9 mm. wide, acuminate, apiculate, lightly eymbiform, concave at base. Petals linear or lanceolate-linear, about 11-11.3 mm. long, acute, 1-nerved. Lip 3-lobed above the middle, with the basal part erect, tubular-concave and embracing the column and with the terminal lobe recurved in natural position; lamina when expanded broadly ovate in out- line, rather fleshy, ecarinate, concave-saccate at base, slightly shorter than the lateral sepals and about 8.6-9 mm. wide; free part of lateral lobes very short, porrect, obliquely semiorbicular; mid-lobe elliptic-ovate, about 5 mm. long and 3.8-4 mmi. wide, subacute, minutely papillose and ciliolate. Col- umn stout, about 6.7 mm. long, slightly dilated and arcuate above; clinan- drium lightly 3-lobulate, with the lobules irregularly denticulate. Anther obliquely semiglobose, 2-celled. Pollinia 4, obliquely complanate-ovoid.
bibliographicCitation: Merrill, Elmer D. 1941. Plants Collected on the Vernay-Cutting Expedition. Brittonia. 4 (1): 23-68.

description: Culmi 1-2 m alti, 2-3 mm diametro, erecti vel scandentes. Vaginae foliorum papilloso-pilosae, auriculatum; auriculae 2, 3-4.5 mm longae; fimbriae 22-34, 8-17(- 30) mm longae, lanceolatae; laminae foliorum 7-14 cm longae, 1.3-2.2(-3) cm latae, reflexae, glabrae. Inflorescentia paniculata, 16-24 cm longa. Spiculae 20-37 mm longae, puberulentes, (4-)5-7(-8) flosculos continentes; glumae 2, acutae, gluma I 2.5-3 mm longa, gluma II (3-)3.8-4.5 mm longa; lemma 6.5-8.5 mm longa, acuta. Stamina 3; antherae 3-4 mm longae.
bibliographicCitation: Judziewicz, Emmet J. & Tyrrell, Christopher D. 2007. Aulonemia yanachagensis (Poaceae: Bambusoideae: Bambuseae): A new species from central Peru. Brittonia. 59 (1): 83-87.

description: Erect to scandent, shrublike woody bamboo. Culms 1-2 m long, 2-3 mm in diameter, glabrous or very sparsely papillose-pilose, freely branching with one branch per node and a promontory absent. Culm leaves not seen, perhaps not differentiated from foliage leaves. Foliage leaves 3 or 4 per complement; sheaths glabrous below, papillose-pilose above; sheath auricles present, paired with one on each side of the sheath summit, 3-4.5mm long, 1 mm wide, crescent-shaped (falcate), dark brown, deciduous, with numerous papillose-based fimbriae; fimbriae 22-34 per leaf sheath summit, each 8-17(-30) mm long, radially spreading, sinuous, with hispidulous margins; outer ligules 0.2-0.3 mm long, indurate, pale, ciliolate; inner ligules absent or confluent with the sheath auricles; pseudopetioles 1-2mm long, dark, thickened; blades 7-14 x 1.3-2.2 (-3) cm, lanceolate, glabrous, reflexed, deciduous, rounded at the base, acuminate at the apex, glabrous, scabrous on margins near the apex. Inflorescences 16-24 cm long, 6-25 cm wide, paniculate, ovoid, with glabrous capillary branches. Spikelets 20-37mm long, 1- 2mm wide, (4-)5-7(-8)-flowered, stramineous, puberulent throughout; rachilla internodes 4.5-5.8mm long; lower glume 2.5-3.0 mm long, ovate-lanceolate, acute, 7-nerved; upper glume (3-)3.8-4.5 mm long, lanceolate, acute, 7-nerved; lemma 6.5-8.5 mm long, lanceolate, (7-)9-nerved, acute; palea 6.5- 8.5 mm long, slightly longer than and protruding from the lemma, bicarinate, bifid, the keels ciliolate, the sulcus 0.8-1.0mm wide; uppermost floret often sterile, only ca. 5 mm long. Stamens 3, the anthers 3-4 mm long, 1 mm wide. Ovary ca. 2.5 mm long, pubescent. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Judziewicz, Emmet J. & Tyrrell, Christopher D. 2007. Aulonemia yanachagensis (Poaceae: Bambusoideae: Bambuseae): A new species from central Peru. Brittonia. 59 (1): 83-87.

description: Tree ca. 3.5 m high, essentially glabrous except for strigose-puberulent inner surface of calyx-lobes and young fruits (probably petals as well); hairs asymmetrically dibrachiate, whitish, yellowish, or reddish brown, up to ca. 0.2 mm long; young twigs glabrous, subterete, gray, the bark remaining more or less smooth, gray on older twigs. Leaves elliptic, oblong-elliptic, ovate, lanceolate, 4.2-6.5 x 1.7-2.3 cm, 2.2-3 times as long as wide, the margin revolute; apex strongly acuminate; base cuneate to attenuate; petiole 3-5 mm long, ca. I mm thick, channeled; midvein impressed above, prominent below; lateral veins ca. 20-30 pairs faintly visible, straight, raised slightly above, leaving at an angle of greater than 45 degrees, near the margin joining a faint lateral vein that parallels the margin, the smaller veins between laterals indistinct to scarcely visible, dendritic; blades coriaceous, drying reddish brown, somewhat darker above than below, somewhat lustrous above. Flower buds unknown but perhaps similar to C. moritzianus; peduncles solitary in the axils of leaves or bracts, to ca. 1 cm long, ca. 1 mm wide, terete, sparsely strigose; bracteoles suborbicular, 2- 3 mm long, persisting until fruit develops; calyx probably nearly closed but with a terminal pore in bud, tearing into 4-5 truncate lobes, these ca. 5-8 mm wide at base, ca. 5 mm long, densely strigose within, apparently without an appendage; petals 5 (known through scars only), perhaps similar to those of C. moritzianus; disk 6-8 mm across, the staminal ring pubescent; stamens ca. 200 (known through scars only); ovary 5-locular, the locular wall with scattered glands; ovules probably about 8-25 per locule, the placenta capitate, central; fruit subglobose to ca. 22 mm in diameter, red and yellowish (ex Anderson 10981); seeds 20-40, ca. 5 mm long, the outer rim hard, light brown, ca 4 cells thick, the central portion soft, darker.
bibliographicCitation: Landrum, Leslie R. 2008. Two new species of Calycolpus (Myrtaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 60 (3): 252-256.

description: Shrub ca. 60 cm high, sparsely to densely tomentulose on young twigs, some floral surfaces, and young leaves; hairs yellowish gray to silvery gray, some curled and appressed, others nearly straight and erect, up to ca. 1 mm long; young twigs densely tomentulose at first, losing the longer hairs first, shorter hairs later, the first bark smooth, yellowish white, cracking and flaking off, the older bark gray to brownish, the leaf and fruit scars prominent; leaves subsessile, ovate to lanceolate, 1.7- 4.5x1.1-3.3 cm, 1-2.5 times as long as wide, puberulent basally above, densely tomentulose below at first, most hairs falling with age, the margin recolute; apex acute to acuminate or obtuse, the very tip often blunt; base truncate to cordate; petiole less than 0.5 mm long, ca. 2mm wide, tomentulose; midvein prominent below, flat above; lateral veins up to ca. 12 pairs, straight, leaving the midvein at an angle of ca. 45º or more, uniting with a marginal vein that closely parallels the margin, up to ca. 2mm from margin; blades thickly coriaceous, somewhat lustrous above, dull below, impressed glandular above. Flower buds campanulate-pyriform, ca. 8 mm long, sessile or subsessile, bomrne at leafless nodes or axils of leaves near the tips of twigs; peduncles essentially none as flowers are sessile; bracteoles ovate to line- arlanceolate, involute clasping, 3-5 mm long, glabrous within, tomentulose without, cadu- cous at about anthesis; calyx open, the truncate appressed bases ca. 1.5 x 3 mm, connate as a tube before anthesis and tearing between the lobes to the staminal ring at anthesis, subglabrous proximally within, otherwise pubescent within, the apical appendage scarcely distinguishable, broadly triangular, ca. 2 x 3 mm, puberulent within, the outer calyx surface tomentulose; petals glabrous, glandular, ca. 8 mm long; hypanthium tomentulose, the hairs persisting in fruit; disk in fruit 4-5 mm across, the staminal ring puberulent, the center recessed; stamens prob- ably ca. 200 (known through scars only); anthers unknown; style unknown; ovary 3- locular; ovules 9-12 per locule, uniseriate along the edge of a peltate placenta; fruit globose, up to ca. 12 mm in diam.; seeds ca. 8, ca. 5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Landrum, Leslie R. 2008. Two new species of Calycolpus (Myrtaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 60 (3): 252-256.

description: Terrestrial herbs, 45-65 cm tall including the inflorescences, drying pale yellowish-tan, glabrous, apparently procumbent with an erect, apical, leaf-bearing portion. Roots pubescent, white, 1-3 mm thick. Stems terete, 3-5 mm thick, 8-10 cm long, the erect leafy section 5- 7 cm long, laxly enveloped by the leaf-sheaths. Leaves distichous, the sheaths 1-2 cm long, tubular and clasping the stem, the blades 13- 21 x 1.5-2.4 cm, oblong-lanceolate, with 5-7- primary veins and conspicuous reticulate secondary venation, the apex acuminate, the margins undulate or sinuate, the base gradually attenuated above the sheath into a pseudope tiole 1-3 cm long. Inflorescence 62 cm long, erect, bearing up arranged flowers opening + simultaneously, peduncle 10-12 cm long, the rachis long, winged; floral bracts larger base of the rachis, 9-16x 1-3 lanceolate, sharply acuminate, margins undulate, shorter than ovary and pedicel. Flowers resupinate perianth segments spreading widely, (fide collector), to 2 cm long and the spread apices of the petals; 10 mm long, winged; ovary ca. sepals similar but the lateral somewhat 10.5-11.5 x 1.8-2.2 mm, narrowly long acuminate, 1-nerved, the margins lose; petals 9.5-10.5x0.9-1.1 mm, linear- lanceolate, the distal portion linear, attenuate, acute, apparently incurved in natural position, the margins smooth, glabrous; labellum 10- 12 x 4-5 mm, convex in natural position, narrowly ovate, the apex long acuminate and variously curved, 5-nerved, the margins con- spicuously and irregularly papilloseciliate, basally subcordate with two short retrorse, coarsely ciliate, thickened auricles that clasp the column, the base above column with two min, suborbicular calli at each side of midnerve, each with an elongated, linear, falcate projection; column short, thick, 1.5 mm long; pollinia 2; fruit obconic, 8 mm long, 4 mm thick, 5-costate.
bibliographicCitation: Noguera-Savelli, E., et al. 2008. Description of a new species and notes on Crossoglossa (Orchidaceae: Epidendroideae: Malaxideae) from eastern Andes in Colombia and Venezuela. Brittonia. 60 (3): 240-244.

description: Crotoni hemiaryreo Mill. Arg. affinis sed indumento rufo-argenteo, foliis ad margines integeris, stipulis caducis, bracteis ovato-lanceolatis, staminibus circa 25, floribus femineis majoribus, stylis inclusis differt.
bibliographicCitation: Caruzo, Maria B. R., et al. 2008. Croton campanulatus (Euphorbiaceae s.s.), a new species from the Brazilian Atlantic rain forest. Brittonia. 60 (3): 261-264.

description: Tree 4-5 m tall, monoecious, indument rufous-silvery, lepidote trichomes without a central ray, those pale, reddish or sometimes with a reddish center and a pale margin, 0.3- 0.5 mm; branchlets cylindric, strongly striate, rufous-silvery, covered by reddish and scattered pale trichomes. Leaves alternate; lamina 3.5-17.5x 1.5-9.5 cm, ovate, discolorous, upper surface green with scattered pale trichomes and lower surface silvery with scattered reddish trichomes or trichomes with a reddish center and a pale margin, apex acuminate, base rounded to truncate, margin entire, upper surface lepidote, lower surface densely lepidote, venation pinnate, brochi- dodromous, secondary veins 4-6, abruptly upturned towards the next ones, tertiary veins percurrent; petiole 1.5-9 cm long, with a pair of stalked acropetiolar glands; stipules deciduous. Inflorescence 4-12 cm long, terminal, without interruption between the pistillate and staminate cymules; inflorescence axis appressed, striate, lepidote; promximal cymules bisexual, with 1 pistillate flower and 2 staminate flowers, distal cymules with 3 staminate flowers; bracts 4-9 mm long, ovate - lancolate, prophylls 1-2 mm long, lanceolate. Staminate flowers 8-10 mm long, campanulate, pedicels 2-3 mm long; calyx 3-4 mm long, lepidote externally, rufous-silvery, covered by reddish and scattered pale trichomes, glabrate internal; calyx lobes united half of their length, 1.5- 2 mm long, entire, equal, valvate, ovate, apex acute; petals 5 mm long, spathulate, apex obtuse to rounded, lepidote externally; disk 5-segmented; stamens ca. 25, filaments subulate; receptacle villous with simple trichomes. Pistillate flowers 8-10 mm long, campanulate, not fleshy, sessile to short pedicellate; calyx 7-9 mm long, lepidote externally, rufous-silvery, covered by reddish and scattered pale trichomes, glabrate internally; sepals 5, 7-9 mm long, equal, quincuncial, broadly ovate, not fleshy; petals reduced to glands; disk entire, deeply 5-lobed; ovary globose, lepidote; styles 3, tetrafid, slightly joined at the base, inserted. Capsules 10- 15 mm long, globose, lepidote, calyx strongly accrescent and inflated, covering the young fruit, pedicel slightly accrescent; seeds 6-8 mm long, globose-elliptic, smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Caruzo, Maria B. R., et al. 2008. Croton campanulatus (Euphorbiaceae s.s.), a new species from the Brazilian Atlantic rain forest. Brittonia. 60 (3): 261-264.
