description:
Slender trees to 15 m tall and to 20 cm diam., without buttresses; bark smooth, pale brown; wood reddish. Young leafy branchlets 1-3 mm thick, terete. Stipules free at base, not connected to petioles, deltoid, glabrous outside and inside, ciliolate at margins, 2.5-3 mm long, 2-3 mm wide at base, caducous, leaving a thin scar encircling the stem at petiole attachments, with sparse col- leters at base inside. Blades 5-15 X 3-7 cm, length: width ca. 2:1, elliptic to narrowly ovate, decurrent at base, acute and acuminate at apex, dark green above and pale green below, chartaceous, drying reddish-vinaceous, glabrous throughout. Primary and secondary veins glabrous and prominent below; secondary veins 5-8 each side; tertiary veins subparallel-reticulate.

Petioles 1.5-3 mm long, 0.5-1.5 mm thick, terete. Inflorescences terminal and frondose, corymbose, with opposite to subopposite decussate branches terminating in cymules, 5-15 cm long; lateral branches 2-3 pairs, 4-9 cm long. Rachis decussately compressed, the rachis and branches gla- brous and lenticellate; flowers on distal branches in cymules. Distal bracts reduced to deltoid scales or absent, up to 2-3 mm long; bracteoles subtending the flowers microscopic deltoid scales. Flowers long-pedicellate; pedicels thin and delicate, 2-5 mm long, puberulent; hypanthium obconical, 0.5-1 mm long, puberulent. Calyx cupular and 4-lobed, 1-2 X ca. 1.5 mm, puberulent; calyx lobes deltoid, one lobe 1-3 mm long, the other three 0.5-0.7 mm long before an- thesis, the larger lobe expanding into a pterophyll in mature capsules. Corolla funnel- form and deeply lobed, 6-7 mm long, yellow; tube 2-2.5 mm long, 0.6 mm wide at base and 2 mm wide at orifice, glabrous outside and inside; corolla lobes 4, right-contorted in bud, ovate with acute apex, ca. 4 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide at base, glabrous outside and inside. Stamens 4, half-exserted, of equal length; filaments attached 1.5- 2 mm from the base of the corolla tube; anthers narrowly elliptic, ca. 3 x 0.5 mm, dorsifixed near the base, rounded at apex and long-tailed at base; filaments 0.5 mm long, filiform, basally flattened and adnate to corolla throat, glabrous throughout. Style exserted, 7-8 mm long, terete, glabrous; style branches ovate, 0.3-0.4 mm long. Fruits narrowly cylindrical and multicostate, decurrent at base, 6-7 X 1.1-1.6 mm, reddish-brown, sparsely puberulent, without lenticels, bilocular and with solitary seeds, indehiscent; disk black, glabrous, not exceeding the calyx; persistent calyx cupular and with 1 pterophyll. Pterophylls narrowly ovate; blades 2-2.5 X 1-1.5 cm, with pal- mate (acrodromous) venation, reddish; petioles 3-5 mm long. Seeds vertically inserted, clavate, fleshy, smooth, 4-6 mm long, 0.5-0.6 mm diam., with basal hilum.

description: Single-stemmed shrubs 1-2 m tall to trees to 10 m tall, and 10 cm (or more) diam.; wood pale yellow; bark dark green to blackish, smooth; leafy branchlets terete, glabrous. Stipules free at base, triangular and short-acuminate, glabrous outside, with a row of sparse colleters intermixed with sericeous hairs at base inside, 2-3 mm long, 2-3 mm wide at base. Blades 8-17 X 3-7.5 cm, narrowly elliptic to elliptic to narrowly obovate, acute at base, acute and acuminate at apex, acumen 1-2 cm long, dark green above and below, drying black, papiraceous, glabrous throughout; primary and secondary veins prominent below, of the same color as the blades; secondary veins 5-8 each side; tertiary veins reticulate; petioles 3-10 mm long, adaxially flattened to concave, glabrous; domatia usually with minute crypt domatia at the basal axils of the secondary veins, or rarely absent. Inflorescences terminal, short-pedunculate, compact, reduced cymes of (3-)5-7 sessile flowers, peduncles 1-3 mm long. Open flowers not seen, only flower buds observed, protandrous. Calyces short-cupular, 4-lobed, to 1 mm long, glabrous, persistent; lobes minute, triangular, 0.2-0.5 mm long, glabrous. Corollas (in flower buds), short-tubular, 4-angular, to 14 mm long, greenish white, glabrous outside and inside; lobes 4, valvate in bud, ca. 8/10 of corolla length. Stamens 4, equal in length; filaments attached near the base of the corolla tube, terete, glabrous; anthers (in flower buds) narrowly oblong, ca. 3.5 X 0.5 mm, dorsifixed at medial zone, acute and apiculate at apex, rounded at base. Style observed only at early stage, glabrous. Drupes ellipsoid, sessile, 14-20 X 12-14 mm, mesocarp thick and coriaceous (ca. 2-3 mm thick when dry), green, 2-locular, with one pirene per fruit by abortion of one locule. Pyrenes solitary, basally inserted, erect, ellipsoid and flattened on one side, 8-9 X 7-8 mm, pale orange when dry.

description: Monoecious shrub to 3 m, 4 cm diam at base, the bark dark reddish-brown, fissured, slightly peeling, the branches dark brown to gray, glabrate, slightly roughened by raised scars of deciduous scales (stellate hairs with the bases of the rays fused), the young stems scaly, densely covered with whitish overlapping appressed scales (the rays fused for ca 1/2 their length) 0.4-0.6 mm diam. Leaves petiolate, the lamina 2.5-7 cm long, (0.8) 1-3 cm wide, mostly (2) 3-4 times longer than wide, lanceolate to elliptic, the base cuneate to acute, the apex acute to apiculate, the margin entire to remotely serrulate, the teeth sometimes terminating in a minute gland, penninerved, the secondary veins 4-6 pairs, the basal pair usually most prominent, the young leaves densely pubescent above with whitish, 7-10-rayed stellate hairs up to 0.25 mm diam, densely scaly below with overlapping white deeply divided scales (with mostly 14-26 long rays) 0.5 mm diam, punctate, at maturity bright green and moderately to sparsely pubescent above, paler below, the pubescence thinly persistent, especially along the midveins; petiole (2) 4-10 mm long, the pubescence white, the scales 24-30-rayed, the glands 2-4, paired at or just below the base of the lamina, conspicuous, sessile to (usually) stalked, yellowish, cupshaped glands to 1 mm long at or just below the leaf base, occasionally absent; stipules 3-6 mm long, linear-subulate, each with a tuft of setae 0.5-1 mm long at the tip, pubescent, deciduous. Inflorescence terminal and in uppermost 1 or 2 leaf axils, solitary or in groups of 2 or 3, a densely white-scaly (the scales somewhat divided) raceme 1-7 cm long, the peduncle 1-3 cm long and usually bearing a pair of leaf-like, lanceolate bracts 1-2.5 cm long. Staminate flowers crowded distally on the inflorescence, 8-14, sometimes fewer or not developing, each subtended by a bracteole similar to the stipules, ca 2 mm long; pedicels 2-3 mm long, ca 0.3 mm wide; sepals 5, valvate, ovate, ca 1.5 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, densely stellate-pubescent without, glabrous within; petals white, oblanceolate, ca 2 mm long, densely white-villous below; stamens 1 1, the filaments glabrous, 2-3 mm long, the anthers 0.5-0.6 mm long. Pistillateflowers proximal, 1-15, erect, each subtended by a linear stipule-like bracteole (similar to the stipules and the bracteoles of the staminate flowers) ca 3 mm long; pedicels 1-1.5 mm long, ca 0.8 mm wide; sepals 5, linear-lanceolate, stellate-scaly (scales deeply divided, 20-36-rayed), unequal, the outer 4 (2) 3-4 mm long, ca 0.5 mm wide, the inner 1 ca 1.5 mm long; petals lacking; ovary oblong, 1-1.5 mm long, densely stellate-scaly with whitish scales ca 0.5 mm diam; styles 3, once-divided nearly to the base, filiform, 2 mm long, stellate-pubescent. Capsule 3.5-5 mm tall, oblong, green to orangish, moderately pubescent with persistent appressed scales, the columella 3-4 mm long. Seeds 3, grayish-brown, finely striate longitudinally, shiny, oblong, 2-4 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, the caruncle 0.7-1.5 mm wide, entire.

description: The [female] calyx often develops 1 or more extra lobes, smaller than the rest, often on the abaxial side of the flower. Plants of this species suggest super- ficially a sparsely pubescent, long-petioled shade-form of Croton repens Schlecht. or a dentate-leaved form of C. soliman Schlecht. & Cham. From C. repens it seems that C. cupulifera differs in the acutely pointed leaves with longer petioles, the small ventral rather than large lateral or essentially dorsal petiolar glands, and the filiform rather than linear or triangular stipules. From C. repens the new species differs also in the repeatedly dichotomous or trichotomous branching and the tendency for all or nearly all the upper leaves to be opposite. From C. soliman it differs in the perennial habit, in the coarsely toothed leaves and in the stipules and calyx-lobes, which in C. soliman are more or less beset with very slenderly stalked stipitate glands. The [female] flowers of C. soliman are long pedicelled, not subsessile as in C. cupulifera.

description: Shrubs or trees, to 6 m high. Year-old branchlets reddish brown, not pruinose, sparsely pubescent to glabrous; new branchlets green becoming reddish brown, moderately to densely pubescent. Expanded leaf blades lanceolate to elliptic-oblanceolate, 5-9 X 1-2 cm, entire to serrate, glabrous adaxially except for midrib, sparsely to densely pubescent and glaucous abaxially; petioles 2-7 mm long; stipules 3-7 mm long and deciduous. Aments in axils of mature leaves. Staminate aments 1-2 cm long, sessile or on leafy branchlets to 0.7 cm long; anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long. Pistillate aments 1.5-2 cm long, sessile or nearly so. Capsules 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous; styles 0.5-0.8 mm long; stipes 0.5-1 mm long. Floral bracts oblong to obovate, 1.2-2 mm long, brown or blackish brown, with dense to moderate hairs toward base, hairs sparse or none at tip.

description: Shrubs, rarely tree-like, to 10 m high. Year-old branchlets reddish brown to greenish yellow (ashy white), glabrous to densely pubescent; branchlets of year green at  first soon becoming reddish brown (rarely yellow-green), glabrous to densely pubescent. Leaf blades narrowly elliptic or lanceolate to lance-ovate, rarely ovate, oblanceolate, or elliptic-obovate, the larger expanded blades (2)4-12(17) cm long, (0.8)1-4(6) cm wide, tip acute to attenuate (obtuse), base cordate, rounded, or cuneate, margin serrate to entire, glabrous to pubescent when young, generally glabrous or glabrate when expanded except sometimes the midrib and lower blade, glaucous or not beneath, petiole 3-20(25) mm long, stipules 1-17 mm long, rarely lacking entirely, often persistent. Staminate aments precocious to coetaneous, 1-5 cm long, floriferous branchlets lacking or to 6(8) mm long, anthers 0.3-0.7 mm long. Pistillate aments precocious to coetaneous, 1-6(9) cm long, floriferous branchlets lacking or to 15(30) mm long. Capsule glabrous (rarely pubescent, in hybrids), 3-6(7) mm long, style 0.1-0.7(1) mm long, stipe 0.5-5 mm long. Floral bract lan- ceolate to oblanceolate or oblong, rarely obovate or suborbicular, tawny or light brown to dark brown or rarely black, 0.8-2(2.5) mm long, glabrous to densely woolly-pubescent. 2n 38. Flowering April through June. S Yukon to Newfoundland S to Cal- ifornia and Florida (not seen from Okla- homa, Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Carolinas). Stream banks, shores, swamps, and other moderately wet areas from sea level to 3050 m elevation.

description: Trees or shrubs to 17 m high. Year-old branchlets brownish or reddish brown, or sometimes grayish before exfoliation, rarely yellowish or purplish, glabrous or sometimes pubescent; branchlets of year green at first, becoming brown or reddish brown (yellowish, purplish), pubescent or sometimes glabrous. Expanded leaf blades mostly linear to elliptic, (3-)4-17 X (0.2-)0.3-1.3(-2.3) cm, entire or serrulate (denticulate) with the teeth mostly widely spaced, not glaucous (glaucescent), pubescent or glabrous; petioles 0-6(-10) mm long; stipules lacking or to 4 mm long and soon deciduous. Staminate aments (0.5-)1.5-6 cm long, on leafy branchlets 0.5-18 cm long; anthers 0.3-1.1 mm long. Pistillate aments (1-)1.5-10 cm long, on leafy branchlets 0.5-18 cm long. Capsules 3-8(-10) mm long, glabrous or pubescent; styles 0-0.5 (-1) mm long; stigmas 0.2-1.2 mm long; stipes 0-1.5(-2) mm long. Floral bracts lanceolate to ovate (rhombic, oblanceolate, obovate), usually pointed at tip, 1-5 mm long, pubescent at least toward base.

description: Shrubs or trees, to 12 m high. Year-old branchlets yellow, green, or reddish brown, usually not pruinose, pubescent to glabrate (glabrous); new branchlets green and usually becoming brown or reddish brown, moderately to densely pubescent, rarely glabrate. Expanded leaf blades narrowly elliptic, oblong, or oblanceolate to obovate, (2.5-)3.5-12.5(-22) X 0.6-3.2(-4.5) cm, entire to irregularly serrate or crenate, densely pubescent to glabrate on both sides or becoming glabrous adaxially (and rarely abaxially), glaucous abaxially; petioles 2- 16(-20) mm long; stipules 2-9(-20) mm long and usually deciduous. Aments precocious or subprecocious, sometimes in axils of mature leaves to the south. Staminate aments 1.5-7 cm long, sessile or on leafy branchlets to 0.7 cm long; anthers 0.4-0.7 mm long. Pistillate aments 1.5-7(-9) cm long, sessile or on leafy branchlets to 0.7 (-1) cm long. Capsules 2.5-5.5 mm long, glabrous; styles 0.2-0.8(-1) mm long; stipes 0.5-1.8(-2.2) mm long. Floral bracts oblanceolate or obovate to oval, 1-2.5 mm long, brown, with dense, untangled hairs generally exceeding the bract by less than the bract length. 2n = 76 (Raven et al., 1965).

description: Shrubs or trees, to 14 m high. Year-old branchlets reddish brown, not pruinose, densely pubescent to glabrate; new branchlets green becoming brown or reddish brown, densely pubescent to glabrate. Ex- panded leaf blades elliptic or oval to obovate, 3.6-7(-17) X 1.7-6.3(-10) cm, irregularly crenate or serrate to entire, densely pubescent to glabrous on both sides, usually less densely pubescent adaxially, glaucous abaxially; petioles 4-20(-30) mm long; stipules 4-15(-25) mm long, sometimes deciduous. description: Shrubs, to 7 m high. Expanded leaf blades narrowly elliptic, oblong, or oblanceolate, 4.7-12 X (0.5-)0.8-2.2 cm, entire to serrate or crenate, glabrous or rarely sparsely pubescent, glaucous abaxially; petioles 3-15 mm long; stipules lacking or to 2(-7) mm long and soon deciduous. description: Shrubs to 3 m high. Year-old branchlets reddish brown, densely pubescent or pubescence patchy, especially behind buds; branchlets of year green at first, soon becoming brown, densely pubescent. Leaf blades elliptic, lanceolate, or ovate, the larger expanded blades (3)4-7.5(12) cm long, (1.5)2-4.5(6.5) cm wide, tip acute to cuspidate, base cordate to rounded, margin sharply serrate, often to the point of being minutely incised, densely pubescent when unfolding, sometimes becoming glabrate but hairs usually more or less persistent and rel- atively long, not glaucous, petiole 1-13(18) mm long, stipules 2-17 mm long, usually persistent. Staminate aments coetaneous, 1.5-4 cm long, floriferous branchlets 2-13 mm long, anthers 0.4-1 mm long. Pistillate aments coetaneous, 2-6(7) cm long, floriferous branchlets (5)10-30 mm long. Cap- sule glabrous, 4-9 mm long, style 0.3-1.8(2) mm long, stipe 0.3-1.3 mm long. Floral bract lanceolate or ovate to oblanceolate or obovate, light brown, 1-2 mm long, somewhat densely long hairy. 2n = 38. Flowering May through July. W Ontario to Labrador S to Wisconsin, Indiana, and New York. Sand dunes on shores of Great Lakes to stream banks, flood plains, and fens in north from sea level to 185 m elevation (Fig. 3A).

description: Shrubs, to 4 m high. Year-old branchlets yellowish brown or reddish brown, pubescent to glabrate; new branchlets green or brown becoming yellowish brown or reddish brown, pubescent. Expanded leaf blades elliptic to obovate, (3-)4-10.5(-13) X 1.5-5(-6) cm, entire (serrulate), moderately to sparsely pubescent adaxially, moderately to densely pubescent and glaucous abaxially, rarely glabrate, veins prominently raised abaxially; petioles (3-)4-1 1(-13) mm long; stipules 0-5(-8) mm long, deciduous. Aments precocious or subprecocious. Staminate aments (1-)1.5-3 cm long, sessile or on leafy branchlets to 1 cm long; stamens 2; anthers 0.3-0.8 mm long. description: Trees or tall shrubs, 2-(6)-16 m tall. Stems erect, forming colonies by root shoots. Juvenile leaves yellowish green or obscured by moderately to very densely sericeous, white indumentum. Largest mature leaf blades linear, narrowly elliptic, or very narrowly obovate, 13-42 mm long, 1.1-4.4 mm wide, length-width ratio 5.8-24.6, apex acute (apiculate), base acute, margin entire, sometimes with distant glands or teeth, 0-6 per cm, blades amphistomatous, abaxial surface glaucous or non-glaucous, densely to sparsely sericeous, villous with appressed, straight, white hairs, or glabrescent, adaxial surface shiny or dull, moderately densely to sparsely sericeous or sericate with white hairs, or glabrescent, sec- ondary veins, when evident, pinnate and curved; petioles 0.2-1.5 mm long, sericeous or sericate. Stipules absent or minute rudiments. Flowering coetaneous (on short, flowering branchlets), or serotinous (on long, flowering branchlets). Floral bracts tawny, 1.3-2.8 mm long, abaxial surface moderately to sparsely hairy, apex acute or obtuse, apex margin glandular dotted, toothed, or entire, pistillate floral bracts deciduous after flowering. Staminate aments 7-20 mm long on flowering branchlets 1.5-290 mm long, aments densely flowered; stamens two, an- thers 0.4-0.7 mm long, filaments free, hairy on lower half (or more), staminate abaxial floral nectaries one, adaxial nectaries one, rod-like or square, 0.5-0.8 mm long. description: Shrubs to 4 m high. South side of Lake Athabasca, Saskatchewan on sand dunes, ca. 215 m elevation (Fig. 1).

description: Trees or shrubs to 10 m high. Year-old branchlets mostly reddish brown, pubescent or glabrous; branchlets of year green to reddish brown or purplish, densely pubescent to glabrate. description: Rounded shrubs 5-10 (-20) dm tall; leafy flowering branchlets usually 5-20 cm long, with a dense stellate tomentum, the trichomes with central processes longer than the radii; blades usually obovate (varying to ovate especially late in the season toward the ends of the branchlets), 20-30 (15-60) mm long, 12-20 (8-37) mm broad, usually broadest near or slightly above the middle, basally rounded, essentially entire, apically variable, often very shortly acuminate, the angle formed by the terminal 3 mm being 40 to 90 degrees, less commonly the apex rounded (as in the first leaves of the elongating twig), the upper surface yellowish green with nearly sessile stellate trichomes spaced 0.2-0.3 mm from center to center, each with an antrorsely inclined central process 0.1-0.6 mm long and 4 to 8 antrorsely inclined radii 0.1-0.4 mm long, the lower surface grayish yellow-green with a dense, interlocking tomentum of nearly sessile or short stalked stellate trichomes 0.1-0.3 mm from center to center, each with an erect or nearly erect central process 0.1-0.5 mm long and 7 to 20 spreading to somewhat raised radii 0.4-1 mm long; leaf nervation pinnate with 3 to 5 pairs of obscure, camptodrome secondaries; petioles 1-3 mm long with pubescence like that of the twigs, the stellate trichomes spaced 0.1-0.2 mm from center to center, each with an erect or nearly erect central process 0.1-1 mm long and about 10 spreading or raised radii 0.2-0.5 (-1) mm long; stipules subulate, 0.5 mm long, nearly glabrous on the adaxial side, caducous; flowers monoecious; inflorescences terminating the twigs, raceme-like, 2-6 cm long, 6-10 mm thick, with 2-6 (-10) pistillate flowers near the base and numerous staminate flowers above (fewer in depauperate, drought-struck plants). Staminate flowers often in glomerules, individual pedicels ca. 1 mm long; calyx densely stellate-tomentose externally, divided nearly to the base into 5 oblong, blunt lobes each about 1 mm long; petals 5, about equalling the sepals, whitish, oblong-elliptic, spreading; stamens 13-15. Pistillate flowers nearly sessile; calyx with a flat central portion ca. 0.5-0.7 mm across and 5 somewhat spreading, narrowly deltoid lobes 0.8-1 mm long, densely stellate-tomentose externally, dark and glabrous internally; petals absent; disk essentially absent; ovary densely stellate-tomentose, nearly round, each of the 3 style-branches bifurcate near the base, 1 mm long, blackish, usually spreading or appressed to the ovary, nearly glabrous, long tapered, accrescent after anthesis up to 3 mm long and filiform; capsule 6-7 mm long, ca. 6 mm thick, shallowly tricoccous; seed grayish, ca. 4.8-5.5 mm long, 3.2-3.4 mm broad (tangentially), 2.3-2.5 mm thick (radially), nearly oblong in ventral view, dorsally hemicylindrical, the caruncle slightly convex, only a little protruding from the very broad micropyle.

description: Arbor parva 5-7 m alta, cortice albo, ramulis inflorescentiaque dense lepidotis; folii pagina inferiori, capsula, ovario, et nonnumquam petiolis ramulisque stellato-pubescentibus vel tomentosis; folia ovata, 2.5-5 cm lata, 4-9 cm longa, basi 5-7-nervata, rotundata vel emarginata, apice acuminata vel apiculata, ambitu sinuata; lamina supra viridis glabraque, subtus pubescens vel subtomentosa, squamis paucis et pilis multis multiradiatis hyalinis tenuibus obsita; petioli 1-2 cm longi, glandulis minimis; stipulae subulatae, duriusculae, 2-3 mm longae; inflorescentiae axillares terminalesque, 2 cm longae vel minus, basi floribus [female] paucis, pedicellis 1-2 mm longis, sepalis anguste deltoideis 1.7-2.3 mm longis, petalis laciniatis 1 mm latis, 2.3-3 mm longis; flores & ca. 20, pedicellis 1 mm longis, staminibus ca. 16; ovarium tomentosum pilis multiradiatis opertum (pilorum radiis basi vix conjunetis); styli 3 mm longi, saepius bifureati; capsula 7-8 mm longa, crassistellata, pilorum ramis suberectis; columella 5 mm longa; semina ignota.

description: The young branchlets and leaves, and the inflorescence in this species are densely lepidote, without any trace of the long-rayed hairs that are abundant on the ovary and the older foliage. The 5 prominent veins at the base of the leaf are distinctive in a group of species in which the principal basal veins are usually 3 in number. Additiolnal collections with flowers and fruit are much to be desired; the flowering season is probably in Winter and early Spring.

description: Solitary or clustered, stemless or with up to 5 trunks to 2 m high, 2-3 cm diam, green or grayish-brown, with acicular spines to 3 cm long, the internodes 5-7 cm long, often with adventitious roots and suckers high on the trunk. Leaves 5-7; sheath 7-13 cm long, fibrous, with sparse, appressed, flattened, dark brown spines to 6 mm long; petiole 14-36 cm long, with brown membranaceous scales, the adaxial surface with sparse dark brown spines to 1 cm long; rachis 36-71 cm long, unarmed, adaxially acute, glabrous, abaxially with deciduous brown scales; blade simple or with 3-4 pinnae on each side (even on the same plant), the apical pinnae much larger than the remaining, ca 20 times as wide as those along the rachis; pinnae membranaceous, glabrous, the lower ones 1-nerved, narrowly to widely cuneate, to 18 cm long and 8 cm wide, obliquely truncate at the apex, the distal margin projected into a tail 2-4 cm long, the apical pair of pinnae (or the whole blade in simple leaves) forming an elliptic lamina 46-82 cm long, 25-37 cm wide, with sinuate-denticulate-praemorse margin, bifid at the apex in 10-19 cm, and forming an angle of 300, with 13-19 primary nerves, the latter 1-3.5 cm apart at base, very prominent and acute on both sides, adaxially with scattered, soft, brown bristles to 1.5 cm long, abaxially with scattered, flat, brown spines to 1 cm long, more abundant toward base; secondary and tertiary veins numerous, connected by transverse ribs, the latter more conspicuous on the adaxial surface. Inflorescence spicate, 52-144 cm long; prophyll 11-21 cm long, tubular, bicarinate, fibrous, glabrous, unarmed or the abaxial surface with a few dark, short spines and bristles; peduncular bract 38-81 cm long, inserted 2.5-3 cm above the insertion of the prophyll, fibrous, acuminate, with scattered brown scales, otherwise glabrous, unarmed or with some dark spines to 8 mm long; peduncle 34-120 cm long, 3-5 mm diam, with brown scales, provided with a few flattened spines to 1 cm long and with dark bristles to 3 mm long; spike 18-28 cm long, 4 mm diam, its axis with many dark bristles; flower groups sunken, the lower ones with 1 pistillate flower below and 2 staminate above, the upper with 1 pistillate below and 1 staminate above. Staminate flowers ovoid, acute at the apex; sepals 1.5-3 mm long, connate for 1-1.5 mm, the lobes 1 mm wide, triangular, acute, striate-nerved, yellowish; petals 6-6.5 mm long, connate into a tube 1-1.5 mm long, the lobes 2-2.8 mm wide, elliptic, obtuse, orange when fresh; filament 1 mm long, wider at base; anthers ovate, 0.3-0.5 mm long, slightly asymmetrical; pistillode minute, inconspicuously 3-gibbous. Pistillate flowers smaller than the staminate; sepals 2.7-3 mm long, 2 mm wide, ovate-triangular, acute; petals 3.5-4.5 mm long, 1.8-2.2 mm wide, connate for 0.4-0.5 mm, the lobes ovate-triangular, acute, striatenerved, dark; staminodial cupule 1-1.5 mm long, inconspicuously toothed; gynoecium 2.1 mm long, 0.6 mm diam, ellipsoid-subcylindrical, unarmed. Fruit ellipsoid, rostrate, 10 mm long, 7 mm diam, red or orange when ripe; endocarp ellipsoid, thin, the pores slightly over the equator; seed smooth, shaped like the endocarp, with a central cavity.

description: Clustered, with 2-20 stems to 5 m high, 2.5-4.5 cm diam, brown to grayish, with internodes 4-8 cm long, usually armed with dark, flattened spines to 20 cm long, occasionally completely unarmed, sometimes supported by stilt roots very densely arranged in a cone to 50 cm high. Leaves 2-8; sheath 20-40 cm long, brown, more or less densely armed with flattened, black spines to 7 cm long; petiole 9-21 cm long, unarmed to densely covered with short brown bristles, or with flattened brown spines to 7 cm long, their margins white-tomentose, the petiole covered initially with a dense tomentum of whitish hairs, the surface finally appearing glabrous or shortly hirsute; rachis 66-135 cm long, densely covered with short, yellow to ferruginous, sometimes caducous bristles 1-1.4 mm long, the abaxial surface armed also with scattered, flattened, tomentose-margined, purplish-brown spines 1-6 cm long, rarely the rachis completely unarmed; pinnae 9-22 on each side, in remote (to 21 cm apart) groups of (1) 2-5, multifarious, broadly cuneate, 1-nerved, with many secondary veins, the apex sinuate-dentatepraemorse, the upper margin usually with a tail-like projection 2-7 cm long, the midvein usually longer than the lower margin and often almost as long as the upper margin (without the projection), the apical pinnae very broadly cuneate, 5-7 nerved, extending up to 17.5 cm along the rachis, their apex obliquely truncate, all pinnae sparsely to densely hirsute adaxially with long, yellowish, sometimes caducous hairs, densely hirsute abaxially with persistent hairs like those of the adaxial surface, occasionally with 1-2 flattened, purplish-brown spines to 5 cm long on the proximal half of the midvein; basal pinnae 12.5-20 cm long, 2.4-8 cm wide at the apex, middle pinnae 21.5-45 cm long, 5-13 cm wide, apical pinnae 23.5-34 cm long along the upper margin, 15-40 cm wide at the apex. Inflorescence to 1.7 m long; prophyll 38-49 cm long, 1-2 cm wide, bicarinate, with a purplish brown scaly indumentum, abaxially unarmed or with short, scattered spines; peduncular bract 111-163 cm long, ca 1.6 cm wide, rigid, minutely striate, unarmed, with an indumentum of brown scales, occasionally densely hirsute with bristly, brown hairs; peduncle 52-120 cm long, 0.4-1 cm diam, with a brown scaly indumentum, or else densely hirsute, sometimes with slender spines to 2.5 cm long; rachis up to 46 cm long, hirsute, the hairs short, bristly, yellowish to purplish, with a whitish base; rachillae 15-28, purplish, with an indumentum like that of the rachis, the lowermost ones up to 40 cm long, 2-5 mm diam at base, with triads of 1 pistillate and 2 staminate flowers for half their length, and staminate distally, the upper rachillae 13-21 cm long, 1-2 mm diam, staminate. Staminate flowers 1.5-2.3 mm long, 1.8-2.5 mm wide; sepals ca 1.3 mm long, shortly connate, membranaceous, ovate, cucullate at base, carinate-winged at the apex; petals ca 2 mm long, elliptic to broadly ovate, inequilateral, acute, thick; filament short; anthers slightly wider than high, almost rectangular in shape, 0.6-0.7 x 0.4-0.5 mm; pistillode small, ovoid, trilobed. Pistillate flowers 4.5-6 mm long; sepals ca 3 mm long, transversely elliptic, glabrous; petals 4-4.3 mm long, connate at base, the lobes ovate, acute, the abaxial surface with scattered, short, yellowish hairs; staminodial cupule with remote, triangular teeth; gynoecium with a few short, flattened, yellowish trichomes scattered below. Fruits globose, shortly rostrate, 10-11 mm diam, red when ripe; exocarp minutely verruculose, glabrous, or more often provided, especially near the apex, with scattered, short, purplish trichomes; mesocarp orange when fresh, mealy, with many soft fibers; endocarp globose, 8.5-9.5 mm diam, 0.5-1 mm thick, with many pits; pores with many radiating fibers; seed irregular, with homogeneous endosperm.

description: Caudex solitarius, procumbens vel erectus, ad 4.5 m altus, armatus vel inermis. description: Stem solitary, frequently procumbent, to 4.5 m tall, 2.5-6 cm diam; base sometimes with a cone of adventitious roots, to 15 cm high, individual roots red or brown, ca 2 cm diam, with white, prickly lenticels; internodes 2-8 cm long, unarmed or with black, applanate spines to 5 cm long, in bands below the nodes. Leaves 8-10, erect and arching; sheath, petiole, and rachis with a brown, caducous, scaly indument; sheath 23-37 cm long, green, open almost to base, with yellow to brown, applanate spines to 5 cm long; petiole 8-18 cm long, with spines similar to those on sheath, to 6 cm long, rarely almost unarmed; rachis 74-120 cm long, hirsute, otherwise unarmed or abaxially with spines similar to those on the sheath; pinnae 11-14 per side, inserted in groups of 2 or rarely 3, in different plants, groups separated by 10-20 cm, the proximal pinna of each group shorter and relatively wider than the distal, more erect than this, apical pinna 1-3-ribbed, the remainder 1 -ribbed, thin, cuneate to broadly cuneate, 1-3 times as long as wide, the margins forming an angle of (25) 35-70, apex strongly tricuspidate, erose, distal margin caudate, cauda to 9 cm long, adaxial side smooth or rough, midrib prominent, abaxial side noticeably paler than the adaxial, hirsute or rarely smooth, midrib yellow, with 0-5 yellow to black spines to 5 cm long, basal pinnae 6-18 x 1-13 cm, middle pinnae 11-23 x 12-20 cm (proximal of a group), 18-29 x 8-18 cm (distal of a group), apical pinnae 8-23 x 6-30 cm. Inflorescence interfoliar, erect or somewhat curving; prophyll ancipitous, 20-56 cm long, 1-3.5 cm wide, cream at base, green above, brown and fibrous apically, unarmed or with scarce yellow spines to 1 cm long; peduncular bract 100-170 x 2-2.5 cm, with a brown, caducous indument, unarmed or with some yellow spines to 1 cm long; peduncle 67-148 cm long, 0.5-1 cm diam, with a brown, caducous indument, and many yellow spines to 1 cm long; rachis 15-55 cm long, unarmed or basally armed as the peduncle; rachillae 12-52, unbranched or occasionally bifurcate, hirsute, each subtended by a small, ca 5 mm long bract, basal rachillae 28-50 cm long, sometimes pedunculate for up to 6 cm, 2 mm diam at base, with linear triads of 1 pistillate and 2 staminate flowers for ca half of their length, distally with dyads of staminate flowers, apical rachillae 4-8 cm long, staminate; flower groups deeply sunken into the rachillae, each triad subtended by a bract that covers the pistillate and the lower staminate flower before anthesis, each dyad subtended by a similar, but smaller bract, covering the lower flower. Staminate flowers violet, the proximal of each triad distinctly pedicellate, the remainder more or less sessile; sepals free, imbricate, carinate, membranous, shorter than the petals, 1-1.5 mm long; petals free, valvate, ovate-acute, fleshy, 1.5-2.5 mm long; filaments basally connate in a narrow ring, free part variable in length, even in the same flower, 0.2-1.5 mm long; anthers nearly square or rectangular, 0.5- 0.8 mm long, ca 0.5 mm wide; pistillode minute, three-lobed. Sepals of pistillate flowers free, imbricate, arched, carinate, somewhat fleshy, 2.5-3 mm long; petals connate for ca half their length, valvate above, ovate-acute, fleshy, 2-4 mm long; staminodial cup ca 1 mm high, adnate to the corolla tube; pistil conical, 1-2 mm high, glabrous. Developing fruits dark brown, with a green ring near apex, rostrate; mature fruits not seen.

description:
Arbor parva ad 7 m alta, 10 cm diametiens, ramulis infloreseentiaque dense lepidotis; folia late rotundato-ovata (vel ramulorum lateralium brevium angustiora), 4-11 cm lata, 6-13 cm longa, base 3-5-nervata, rotundata vel truneata vel late obtusa (vel in petiolum cuneatim angustata); apice obtuse breviacuminata, ambitu sinuata; lamina supra rare lepidota sed viridis, subtus semper argenteo-viridis, superficie squamis imbricatis tecta; petioli 2.5-4 (-7) cm longi, glandulis nullis vel convexis, inconspicuis; stipulae subulatae, nigres- centes et ut videtur induratae, 2.5-3.5 mm longae; racemi terminales, usque ad 22 cm longi, cernui, basi floribus [female] 1-2, pedicellis 1.5 mm crassis, 6-12 mm longis (fructeseentibus vix inerassatis), sepalis deltoideo-ovatis, permaneseenti- bus sed vix acereseentibus, cum petalis ca. aequilongis, 3.5 mm latis, 4.5 mm longis; flores [male] 50-60, distantes, racemi pars [male] ante fructus maturitatem plerumque marceseens; pedicelli ad 6 mm longi; stamina ca. 16, antheris 1.2 mm longis, connectivo dense glandulis maculato; capsulae ovariique squamae pallidae, telnues, irregulariter laciniatae, plus quam 1 mm latae, pars centralis quam apicibus liberis filiformibus angustior; styli 5-6 mm longi, rotati, basi compressi et ibidem ca. 1 mm lati, tota fere longitudilne partiti, ramis quibusque fere ad basin bipartitis, deinde quater bifureatis; capsula longior quam latior, 1.3-1.5 cm longa, tuberculis multis earnosis conicis 2 mm longis obsita; semina (vix matura) 11 mm longa.

description: Climbing vine; flowering stems 1.5-2 mm thick, terete, copiously hirtellous. Leaves: stipules reflexed, deciduous, drying brownish, broadly lanceolate, obtuse or acute, densely appressed-hirsute, 9-12 x 4-5 mm; petiole terete, hirtellous with some stimulose hairs, 4-17 cm long; stipels at base of blade lanceolate, 3- 3.5 x 0.8-1 mm; lamina chartaceous, sparsely pubescent above with some stim- ulose hairs, paler and densely hirtellous beneath, trilobed, mostly 7-22 cm long and broad; middle lobe oblong, short-cuspidate, 4-10 x 2.5-9 cm; base of blade cordate, sinus relatively narrow, ca 1.5-2.5 x 0.5-1 cm; major veins usually 5 from the base, lateral veins sharply arcuate-ascending, veins and veinlet reticulum prominulous beneath; margins subentire (obscurely and minutely glandular-den- ticulate). Inflorescences terminal on axillary short shoots 0.5-1 cm long, with a highly reduced (often bladeless) leaf at the single node, often with one or more  supernumerary inflorescences on lateral shoots at the same axil; peduncle 1-2 cm long; involucral bracts pale greenish-white or green, ovate, 1.2-1.5 x 1.3-1.7 cm, obscurely tricuspidate at tip (middle tooth 1-2 mm long), obtuse or rounded at base, 7-ribbed (with 2 additional weaker marginal veins), hirtellous on both faces, margins entire; bracteal stipules subequal, lanceolate, the lower ones 3.5-4 x 0.7- 1 mm, upper 2.5-3 x 0.5-0.8 mm. Pistillate cymule: outer bract and inner bract- lets reniform, entire, minutely but copiously hispidulous, 2-2.5 x 3.5-5 mm. Pistillate flowers subsessile at anthesis; sepals 9-12, 1.5-2 mm long, conspicuously capitate-glandular on margins, with 5-8 lobes per side; ovary hirsute; stylar col- umn cylindrical, slightly clavate, slightly hispidulous below, 4.5-5 x 0.7-0.8 mm proximally, 1-1.2 mm distally; stigmatic apex 3-angled, symmetrical, terminally excavated, 1.8-2.5 mm across. Staminate cymule subsessile (peduncle usually ill- defined and not over 1 mm long); involucel 2-lipped, 2.5-3 x 6.5-7 mm; lips of involucel entire, faces minutely hispidulous; staminate flowers 12-16; resiniferous bractlets laminate, entire or obscurely crenulate at apex; resinous secretion pale, whitish. Staminate flower: pedicel ca 3 mm long, articulated about 1 mm below the top; mature buds hispidulous; sepals 4, 1.5-2 mm long; staminal column slender, glabrous or sparsely hispidulous distally, 2-2.2 x 0.3-0.4 mm; stamens 9-11, the filaments ca 0.2 mm long, anthers ca 0.4-0.5 mm long. Central fruiting pedicel ca 8-12 mm long, laterals 4-5 mm long; fruiting sepals 9-12 mm long, rachis ca 0.5 mm broad, much narrower than the subulate gland-tipped lobes (these 5-8 per side, 0.5-1.5 mm long), with sparse stiff simple hairs 1-2 mm long and much shorter stimulose hairs. Capsule: cocci reticulate-veiny, ca 7 mm long, wall 0.7-0.8 mm thick, stiffly and sparsely hirsute; columella distally expanded, ca 4 mm high; seeds subglobose, smooth (undulate), grayish-mottled, 3.7-4 mm long.

description: Clambering vine; stems twining, terete, 0.5-1.2 mm thick at growing tips, strig- ulose with persistent whitish incurved hairs ca 0.1 mm long. Leaves alternate, simple; stipules spreading-reflexed, commonly deciduous, lanceolate-falcate (ovate on fertile short-shoots), 3-8 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, sparsely strigulose, striate- veined; petioles terete, 1-4.5 cm long, strigulose as stem; stipels at base of blade 2, lanceolate, 1-2 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm wide, the point of attachment surrounded by cluster of ca 12 glands; blades chartaceous, ovate, unlobed, 3-10 cm long, 2- 7 cm wide, sparsely strigulose above and densely strigulose below with minute whitish hairs 0.05-0.1 mm long; base shallowly cordate, the sinus 5-10 mm deep, 3-5 mm wide at petiole, 10-25 mm wide at outer margin of blade; apex cuspidate; margins plane, entire to sinuate, with glandular processes 0.1-0.2 mm long; prin- cipal veins 5 (7) from base, the secondaries ascending, the tertiaries scalariform, sparsely strigulose with whitish incurved hairs ca 0.1 mm long. Pseudanthial inflorescences solitary on reduced axillary short-shoots 2.5-8 cm long at anthesis, pubescent as stem, with 1 or 2 nodes each with reduced stipules, the leaf usually deciduous; or pseudanthial inflorescences borne on determinate shoots, 10-20 cm long with 2 or 3 nodes, each with a persistent or deciduous leaf, 1 pseudanthial inflorescence terminal, with additional pseudanthial inflorescences on axillary short-shoots produced from nodes; distance between ultimate node and proximal involucral bract 12-40 mm at anthesis in both arrangements. Involucral bracts green at anthesis, unlobed, lanceolate, sparsely strigulose with small incurving hairs, the base cuneate, the apex acuminate; proximal bract (subtending pistillate involucel) 4-10 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, the margin plane, glandular-dentate, the prominent veins 5 from base; distal bract (subtending staminate involucel) 3-6 mm long, 0.5-2 mm broad, the margin plane, entire, the prominent veins 3 from base; stipules of proximal bract lanceolate-falcate, 2-3 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide strigulose, the apex acute, striate with 5 or 6 parallel veins, with several glands at point of attachment, those of distal bract similar except 2.8-3.5 mm long. Staminate cymule with densely puberulent peduncle 3.5-7.5 mm long, 1.2-1.5 mm thick at anthesis; involucel of 2 pairs of more or less decussate, free bracts, these broadly ovate, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, puberulent at base, indistinctly striate- veined, the apex more or less acute, the margins entire, ciliate; staminate flowers 10 (1 1), arranged in a 4-branched pleiochasium with 1 terminal flower, 3 branches with usually 3 flowers each, and a fourth (= dorsal, opposed pistillate cymule) arm usually sterile (rarely 1-flowered), each arm subtended by 2-5 lanceolate or ob- lanceolate bractlets, the tip blunt to acute, sometimes broader than limb, often deeply toothed and glandular-laciniate, elsewhere margins entire to laciniate. Sta- minate flowers on sparsely strigose pedicels 3-5 mm long, ca 0.7 mm thick, articulate near top; calyx sparsely strigulose, splitting into 3 or 4 obovate, acute, spreading segments, ca 2 mm long, ca 1 mm wide; staminal column glabrescent, 2-2.5 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm thick; stamens 8-10 (11), the filaments hirsute with spreading hairs on outer surface, ca 0.2 mm long, the anther sacs ca 0.4 mm long. Pistillate cymules sessile; involucel of 1 abaxial bract and 2 adaxial bractlets, these puberulent near base, glabrescent elsewhere, the margins entire, ciliate, striate- veined; abaxial (proximal) bract simple, triangular, 3-4 mm long, 2-3 mm wide; adaxial (lateral, distal) bractlets simple, lanceolate, 1.5-2.3 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide. Pistillateflowers 3, on pedicels 2.2-3.7 mm long, ca 1 mm thick at anthesis, strigulose-puberulent; sepals 6, narrowly lanceolate, 2.4-4 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm wide, sparsely strigulose, the margins entire, ciliate; ovaries 1.1-1.5 mm high, 1.5-2 mm in diam, tomentose; stylar column more or less straight, subcylindrical, 7-9 mm long, 1.5-2.6 mm thick, thickest at ca 1/3 of length, gradually tapering to a blunt point distally, the tip with pit below center, the base of style puberulous, the stigmatic surface glabrous, covering distal 2/3 of stylar column. Pedicels in fruit 12-23 mm long; pistillate sepals persistent, similar to at anthesis. Capsules 7-8 mm in diam, strigulose; seeds subspherical, slightly flattened, ca 4 mm in diam, 3 mm thick, the surface slightly and irregularly pusticulate, mottled white and dark brown, the hilum round, ca 0.2 mm in diam.

description: Twining vine; flowering stem 1.5-2 mm thick, retrorse-hirtellous. Leaves: stipules reflexed, deciduous, linear-lanceolate, acuminate, entire, 3.5-7 x 0.7-1 mm; petiole densely hirtellous, ca 1-3.5 cm long, 0.5-1 mm thick; stipels at base of blade mostly 2, 0.8-1 mm long, with smaller clustered glands; lamina chartaceous, glabrescent above (at first minutely hispidulous), beneath copiously hirtellous along veins with mostly non-stimulose hairs, 3-lobed, ca 5-8.5 x 6.5-10 cm; middle lobe oblong, minutely apiculate, 4-6.5 x 1.2-2.2 cm; lateral lobes spread- ing (nearly perpendicular), ovate-oblong, 3-6 x 1-2.5 cm; base deeply and narrowly cordate, the sinus ca 0.5-1 cm long and broad; major veins usually 5 from base, the lower 2 pairs diverging at low angles, the larger veinlets prominulous beneath; margins plane, subentire. Inflorescences solitary on axillary short-shoots 3-4.5 cm long; short shoot usually with 2 nodes bearing reduced leaves 2-5 cm long; peduncle 2-3.5 cm long at anthesis. Involucral bracts creamy white at anthesis, 1.5-2 cm long and broad, 3-lobed, 5-ribbed with 2 weaker laterals, velutinous on both faces; middle lobe oblong, acute, 6-9 x 4.5-5.5 mm; margins denticulate (teeth obscured by indument); bracteal stipules subequal, narrowly lanceolate, acuminate, entire, strigose, 2.2-2.7 x 0.3-0.6 mm. Pistillate cymule sessile; inner bractlets 2, entire or irregularly lobed, 3-5 x 4-5 mm; outer bract entire, eglandular, ovate, 4.5-6 x 7.5-8 mm. Pistillate flower: pedicel ca 1.5-2 mm long at anthesis, densely hispidulous; sepals 10-12, 1.5-2 mm long at anthesis  laciniate-toothed with eglandular lobes, hirsute; ovary trigonous, stiffly and dense- ly hirsute; stylar column cylindrical, not markedly clavate, hispidulous below, 3.2-3.5 x 0.7-0.8 mm; stigmatic disk peltate, symmetrically foveolate, 3.2-4 mm across. Staminate cymule subsessile or peduncle up to 1.5 mm long and about as thick; involucel 2-lipped, of 4 nearly discrete, entire, eglandular bracts; middle adaxial bract obdeltoid, 3.5 x 2-3 mm; lateral adaxial bracts 3.5-4 x 4.5-5 mm; abaxial bract 1.5-2 x 7 mm; staminate flowers 9-12; resiniferous bractlets lam- inate, ca 1.5-2 mm high, divided 1/3 to 1/2 their lengths into slender teeth. Staminate flower: pedicel 3.5-5 x 0.5-0.6 mm, hispidulous, articulated at about the middle; sepals 4 (5), obovate, mucronate, reflexed-recurved, 2.5-3.2 x 0.7 mm; stamens 18-22; filaments ca 0.5 mm long, hispidulous; anthers 0.5-0.7 mm long. Central fruiting pedicel 12-13 mm long, laterals 6-7 mm; fruiting sepals linear-lanceolate, 8.5-9.5 x 1.7-2 mm; lateral teeth 10-14 per side, 0.5-1 mm long, not glandular. Capsule ca 11 mm broad, hispid and minutely hispidulous; cocci ca 8.5-9 mm long, wall 0.9-1.3 mm thick. Columella 4.8-5 mm high. Seeds subglobose, smooth, mottled, ca 4.2 mm long.

description: Clambering vine; stems twining, striate-channelled, ca 2-4 mm thick, at growing tips hirsute with ± deciduous whitish hairs ca 2 mm long and puberulent with persistent incurved hairs 0.2-0.5 mm long. Leaves: stipules greenish, becoming ± spreading or reflexed, persistent, ovate, narrowed to an acutely or obtusely pointed tip, entire and nonglandular, indistinctly longitudinally striate-veined (with ca 12-15 veins), copiously strigose on both sides, 12-23 mm long, 7-13 mm broad; petiole pubescent as the stem, 5.5-10.5 cm long; stipels at base of blade oblong to lanceolate, gland-tipped, usually 2 larger lateral ones accompanied by 1 or 2 smaller central ones with basal glands, larger stipels 2.5-4.5 mm long, 0.8-1.5 mm broad; leaf blades chartaceous, glabrescent above, persistently puberulent beneath, monomorphic (always trilobed), 10-20 cm long, 8-20 cm broad, the middle lobe obovate, abruptly short-acuminate, 7-10 cm long, 4-7 cm broad, base of blade deeply cordate, sinus ca 2-4 cm long, narrow or sometimes occluded by overlapping basal lobes; venation palmate, major veins usually 7 from the base, secondaries ascending, tertiaries scalariform, veinlet reticulum pale and prominulous beneath; margins subentire or inconspicuously crenulate, glandular when young. Inflorescences usually solitary on axillary short shoots 0.7-3 cm long; short shoot usually with single bladeless leaf (represented only by the stipules); peduncles mostly 1.5-4 cm long at anthesis, becoming up to 5 cm long in fruit; involucral bracts subequal, green at anthesis, conchoidal (distinctly convex in the middle with upturned margins), broadly ovate, 4-6 cm long at anthesis, becoming 6-7.5 cm long in fruit, (2.5) 3.5-6 cm broad, acutely 3-toothed at tip (middle tooth 6-11 mm long, laterals 3-7 mm long), cordate and 9-veined at base (2 basal veins not prominent), copiously puberulent on both sides, margins minutely glandular- denticulate; stipules 11-15 (19) mm long, dimorphic, the outer pair (belonging to lower bract) elliptic and broader (5-8 mm across), the inner pair falcate, oblong, and narrower (3.5-5 mm across), entire, strigose-puberulent. Pistillate cymule with involucel of distinct bractlets; adaxial bractlet auriculate- reniform, bilobed or bipartite, ca 2-3 mm high and 3-5 mm broad (rarely with additional bractlets ca 2 mm across); abaxial bractlet 2.5-3.5 mm high, 6.5-8.5 mm broad; bractlets with conspicuously glandular-dentate margins (capitate glands distinctly stalked), inner and outer faces copiously strigose. Staminate cymule with stout hirsutulous peduncle 2.5-5 mm long; involucel (of connate bractlets) 2-lipped, adaxial lip (subtending staminate flowers) horizontal, ca 2.5-4 mm long and 10-11 mm broad, abaxial (subtending ceriferous bractlets) upright, 2-3 mm high, 8.3-10.2 mm broad; lips of involucel with conspicuously glandular- dentate margins, minutely scabridulous on both faces; staminate flowers (8) 10; glandular complex with ceriferous bractlets laminate, entire, each 2.5-5 mm broad and 0.2-0.3 mm thick, in two rows; secretion resinous and sticky, yellow or orange. Staminate flowers with stout pedicels 3-5 mm long, articulate near the top; mature buds 3.5-3.7 mm long, 2.8-3.2 mm broad, densely hispidulous; calyx splitting into 4-6 segments, 4-4.7 mm long, 1.7-2.5 mm broad, with mostly 6 or 7 inconspicuous straightish veins; staminal column distinctly hispidulous, at anthesis becoming 3.5-4 mm long and 0.7-0.9 mm broad; anthers 15-24, on slender sparsely hispidulous filaments 0.4-0.6 mm long; anther-sacs asymmetric, 1-1.2 mm long. Pistillate flowers with short pedicels, the central ca 4 mm long at anthesis, the laterals 1.7-2.2 mm long; sepals 10-12, ca 2-3 mm long at anthesis, deeply laciniate with ca 7-10 gland-tipped hispidulous subulate lobes on each side; ovary ca 2 mm high and 3 mm across, hispidulous, carpels 3; stylar column cylindrical, 9-11.5 mm long, 0.9-1 mm broad, minutely hispidulous below, smooth above; stigma disciform, peltate-concave, entire, smooth and glabrous, 2.8-3 mm across. Central fruiting pedicel ca 12-15 mm long, laterals ca 4-5 mm long; fruiting sepals mostly 7-10 mm long, with width of midstrip about equalling length of gland-tipped lobes (ca 1.5-2.5 mm), hispidulous with short stinging hairs (less than 0.5 mm long). Capsule 13 mm in diameter, sparsely hispidulous; cocci 8-8.5 mm long; columella distally expanded, ca 4.5 mm high; seeds globose, smooth, grey with white stripes and dark brown mottling, ca 4.9-5.4 mm long; hilum narrowly elliptic, 0.6-0.8 mm long.

description: Clambering vine; stems twining, terete, 1-1.5 mm thick at growing tips, the young shoots densely strigose-tomentose with persistent, slightly curved, whitish hairs 0.1-0.4 mm long. Leaves alternate, simple; stipules spreading-reflexed, com- monly deciduous, lanceolate to ovate, 2.5-5 mm long, 1.2-1.5 (1.7) mm wide, striate-veined, the margins entire, ciliate, the abaxial surface sericeous, the adaxial sparsely strigose; petioles terete, (1.5) 3.5-10 cm long, 1-2.5 mm thick, pubescent as stem; stipels at base of blade 2-4, minute, ca 0.2 mm long, glandular; blades chartaceous, unlobed, ovate, (4) 7-27 cm long, 3-20 cm wide, the abaxial surface strigose with whitish hairs ca 0.3 mm long and tomentose with shorter brown hairs, the adaxial surface glabrous; base of leaf truncate to deeply cordate; apex acuminate; margins plane, sinuate with glandular processes ca 0.1 mm long; major veins 5 from base, strigose with whitish hairs, the secondaries ascending, the tertiaries scalariform. Pseudanthial inflorescences 1 to several on reduced axillary short-shoots, these at anthesis 1-3 cm long, pubescent as stem, with 1 or 2 nodes, each with leaf and axillary bud, often producing second pseudanthial inflorescence, or commonly leaf deciduous and only stipules and axillary bud persistent; distance between ultimate node and proximal involucral bract 5-10 mm at anthesis; su- pernumerary buds in leaf axils of long-shoot commonly developing into 1 or 2 additional inflorescence-bearing short-shoots, these smaller than first. Involucral bracts pale green at anthesis, subequal, unlobed, lanceolate or oblanceolate, 10- 15 (20) mm long, 4-6 mm wide, sparsely strigose below, glabrescent above, the base attenuate, the margins revolute, glandular-undulate, ciliate, the prominent veins 1 or 3 from base; stipules of proximal bract reflexed, ovate-falcate, 3-5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, the abaxial face sparsely strigose, the adaxial face glabrescent, the apex subacute, the margin plane, entire, ciliate; stipules of distal bract similar but up to 2.5 mm wide. Staminate cymule with stout, densely strigose peduncle, 2-4.2 mm long, 1-1.8 mm thick; involucel of 2 pairs of more or less decussate, free bracts; bracts depressed-obovate, cupped adaxially, 2.6-3.2 mm long, 4.5- 5.5 mm wide, striate-veined, the margins weakly erose, minutely ciliate; staminate flowers 7-9, arranged in branched pleiochasium with 1 terminal flower and 3 arms, each arm 2- or 3-flowered, subtended by 2-4 strap-shaped or square, blunt bractlets, these 2-2.5 mm long, 0.1-2.5 mm wide, the apical margins laciniate, the laciniae 0.5-1 mm long, 0.1 mm thick, resiniferous, secreting a greenish-blue resin; bractlets of fourth (sterile) pleiochasial-arm 2 or 3, similar but up to 3.5 mm wide and rolled together. Staminate flowers on stout pedicels 1-4 mm long, ca 1 mm thick, articulate near top, sparsely puberulent; calyx sparsely hispidulous, splitting into 4-6 lanceolate-ovate, acute, spreading segments 1-2 mm long, 0.8- 0.9 mm wide; staminal column with only a few hairs near top, 1.5-2.1 mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm thick; stamens 8-22, the filaments hirsute with spreading hairs on outer surface, ca 0.1 mm long, the anther sacs 0.2-0.3 mm long. Pistillate cymules sessile; involucel of 1 abaxial bract and 2 adaxial bractlets, these sparsely puber- ulent, the margins erose, ciliate, striate-veined; abaxial (proximal) bract simple, depressed obovate, 1-2 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide; adaxial (distal) bractlets simple, squarish, 1-2 mm long, 1-2 mm wide. Pistillateflowers 3, on short pedicels 0.3- 1 mm long at anthesis; sepals 6, puberulent, ovate, 1-1.5 mm long, 0.4-1.0 mm  wide, the margins entire, ciliate; ovaries hirtellous, 0.7-1.1 mm high, 0.7-1.3 mm in diam; stylar column straight, cylindrical, of nearly equal diam throughout length, 4-6 mm long, 0.8-1 mm thick, hirtellous only at extreme base, the glabrous stigmatic surface covering nearly entire length, the tip blunt, undilated, foveolate. Pistillate pedicels in fruit 9-13 mm long; pistillate sepals triangular, 2-3 mm long, 1.6-1.8 mm wide, sparsely pubescent, ciliate. Capsules 35-40 mm in diam, with massive woody walls 3-6 mm thick, sparsely strigose; seeds flattened-oval, 9-11 mm in diam, 8-8.5 mm thick, the surface smooth, with sparse small hairs, dark brown with gray mottling, the hilum round, ca 2 mm in diam.

description: Clambering vine; stems twining, terete, ca 1 mm thick at growing tips, strigose with persistent, yellowish to whitish, incurved hairs 0.1-0.5 mm long. Leaves alternate, palmately trifoliolate (rarely 4- or 5-foliolate), with 5 major veins from base (1 in central leaflet, 2 each in lateral leaflets), these sparsely strigose as stem abaxially, densely tomentose-strigose with yellow hairs adaxially, the secondary veins ascending, the tertiaries scalariform; stipules spreading reflexed, persistent or deciduous, lanceolate, 3-7 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, the abaxial surface sparsely strigose, the adaxial surface finely and sparsely puberulent, striate-veined, with several glands at attachment of stipule to stem; petioles terete, 2-10 cm long, 0.9- 2.3 mm thick, strigose as stem, except near attachment of leaflets where tomentose on adaxial surface; petiolules terete, 2.5-6.5 mm long, 0.8-2.1 mm thick, strigose as stem abaxially, densely tomentose with yellow hairs adaxially; stipels at base of petiolules 2, lance-linear, 2-3 mm long, ca 0.3 mm wide, with a few glands at point of attachment to petiolule; blade of central leaflet chartaceous, oblanceolate to obovate, 4-15 cm long, 2-7 cm wide, glabrescent on both surfaces, the base cuneate, the apex acuminate, the margins sinuate to shallowly serrate, ciliate, with glandular processes ca 0.1 mm long; lateral leaflets similar but lanceolate to ovate, the base asymmetric. Pseudanthial inflorescences solitary on reduced axillary short- shoots 2-3 cm long at anthesis, these puberulent to strigose, with 1 or 2 nodes, each represented by a pair of stipules; distance between ultimate node and proximal involucral bract 15-20 mm at anthesis. Involucral bracts green at anthesis, subequal, slightly concave adaxially, unlobed, spathulate with distinct limb and claw, 5-8 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, the limb 3-4 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, cuneate at base, the claw 2-4 mm long, 1-2 mm wide; surface of involucral bracts puberlant:  margins of claw plane, ciliate, the margin of limb plane, with glandtipped laciniae along basal half, erose along distal half; bracts more or less striateveined with 1-3 indistinct main veins from base; stipules of proximal (pistillate) involucral bract triangular-falcate, 1.5-2.8 (3.6) mm long, 1-2 (2.4) mm wide with both faces obscurely puberulent, the margins entire, sparsely ciliate, the apex subacute, striate-veined; stipules of distal (staminate) involucral bracts similar to those of proximal but larger, 2-3 (3.8) mm long, 1.5-2.2 mm wide, and tip rounded. Staminate cymule with short, stout, puberulent peduncle 0.6-2.0 (2.8) mm long, ca 2 mm thick; involucel of 2 pairs of more or less decussate, free bracts, these depressed obovate, 3.2-5.4 mm long, 4.9-8.0 mm wide, puberulent, striate-veined, the margins erose, sparsely ciliate; staminate flowers 10, arranged in branched pleiochasium with 1 terminal flower and 3 arms, the fourth arm sterile; each fertile arm 3-flowered, subtended by 3-6 strap-shaped, rectangular to obtriangular bractlets, 3-5 mm long, 0.5-3.5 mm wide, the margins at tip with terete, glandular, resiniferous laciniae 1-2 mm long, 0.1-0.2 mm thick; bractlets of sterile (dorsal) pleiochasial arm similar, but 4-6 arranged concentrically, the largest wrapping from adaxial side, the smallest to the center on the abaxial side. Staminate flowers on short stout pedicels 1-3 mm long, 1-1.5 mm thick, these articulate near top, puberulent; calyx triangular, subacute, the spreading segments 1.6-2.8 mm long, 0.5-3.5 mm wide; staminal column short and stout, 0.5-1 mm long, 1-2.5 mm thick, glabrous; stamens (60) 70-80 (95), the filaments ca 0.5 mm long, with a few short hairs, the anther sacs 0.2-0.35 mm long. Pistillate cymules sessile; involucel of 1 bract, this depressed obovate, 2-4 mm long, 3.5-4.5 mm wide, puberulent, striate-veined, the margin erose to dentate, sparsely ciliate. Pistillate flowers 3, on pedicels 0-0.6 mm long at anthesis; sepals 6 (5-7), 2-4 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, deeply divided longitudinally into 2-4 lobes, or rarely unlobed, the margins entire, sparsely ciliate; ovaries 1-1.5 mm high, 1-2 mm in diam, finely strigulose; stylar column puberulent, more or less straight, cylindrical with distinct capitate tip, 2.7-3.3 mm long, 0.5-1 mm thick, the tip ca 2 mm in diam, shaped like a swollen annulus, with deep central pit on ventral side of end, the stigmatic surface densely papillate, confined to swollen tip of style. Pistillate pedicels in fruit 2-12 mm long; pistillate sepals usually 2-4-lobed, 3-4 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, hispidulous. Capsules 8-9 mm in diam, puberulent, trigonous, each lobe projecting up 2-3 mm beyond-the attachment of the style; seeds sphe- roidal, 3-4 mm in diam, the surface slightly roughened, with 3 or 4 faint ridges on the side opposite the hilum, brown with white mottling, the hilum triangular, 0.8-1 mm long.

description: Fruit narrowly ovoid, 4 mm diam., 12 mm long, with pericarp 0.5 mm thick and stigmatic remains basal distinctive within the subtribe for the single series of small, widely spaced fibrous bundles with occa- sional brachysclereids just below the epidermis, and for the single series of heavily sheathed, nearly terete vascular bundles in mid-pericarp; further characterized by a thick pigmented zone below the epidermis, by the tanniniferous cells packed densely throughout the pericarp, and by the moderately thick locular epidermis.

description: Pseudobulbi approximati, angusti, versus apicem attenuati, c. 3-5 cm longi, 1-folii, vaginis punctatis 3.5-5 cm longis initio ad basin. Folium breviter petiolatum, lanceolatum, apicemn versus angustatum, basi acutum, nervis inajoribus c. 9 dorso prominentibus praesertim costa media, papyraceo-coriaceum, c. 13-15 cm longum, 1.5-2.65 cm latum; petiolus distinctus, canaliculatus, 1.2-2.4 em longus. Inflores- centiae e pseudobulbis fere maturis, foliis multo longiores, laxe mul- tiflorae, pedunculo filiformi, 9-10 cm longo, rachide arcuata, quad- rangula, 12.5-24 cm longa, internodiis 0.5-0.55 cm longis. Bracteae persistentes, parvae, patentissimae, marginibus involutis, expansae oblongae, apice rotundatae, multinerviae, c. 0.37 cm longae, 0.2 cm latae. Flores majusculi. Sepalum dorsale anguste lanceolatum, apicem versus angustatum, acutum, 3-nervium, c. 0.875 cm longum, 0.2 cm latum. description: Stem to 2 m long, acaulescent or subterranean, solitary or clustered. Leaves (2)4-8; sheath and petiole densely tomentose; pet- iole 10-20 cm long, ca. 5 mm diam., densely covered with beige woolly tomentum; rachis 40-70 cm long, triangular in cross-section at apex, densely woolly-waxy; pinnae 25-40 per side, shortly lanceolate, with lobed tips, irregularly inserted in obscure groups of 1-4, 2-3 cm apart, opened to rachis, plicate at base and densely covered with wool- ly hairs and ramenta, at obtuse apex asymmetrically split for 0.5-4 cm, with evident midrib on both surfaces, with transverse veinlets not evident, green and lustrous adaxially, glaucous abaxially; basal pinnae 15-25 x 0.4-1.8 cm; middle pinnae 10-22 x 0.7-2 cm; apical pinnae 4-9 x 0.2-0.9 cm. Inflorescences 35-90 cm long; peduncle 45-80 cm long, 0.4-0.6 cm diam., slender, muricate, scarcely to densely covered with floccose hairs and brownish scales; rachis 10- 15 cm long, bearing whitish woolly hairs; prophyll 25-30 cm, tubular, scarious; peduncular bract 50-90 cm long, 1.7-4 cm diam., apiculate, inflated above, woody, sulcate, beige-waxy at apex externally, gla- brous and brownish-violet internally; peduncular bracts 1 or 2, brown, scarious, dentate, at 2.5 cm from apex of peduncle. Staminate flowers 3-4.5 cm long, shortly pedicellate (to 1 mm), inserted parallel to perpendicular, in diads distally; sepals connate to middle, glabrous, membranous, two ca. 2.5 x 1.5 mm, onelargerca. 3.5 x 1.5 mm, much smaller than the petals; petals valvate, connate to middle, glabrous, membranous, ca. 6 x 2 mm; stamens 15, ca. 6 mm long, the filaments not columnar, ca. 1.5 mm long, the anthers ca. 4 mm long, sagittate at both ends; pistillode trifid. Pis- tillateflowers inserted on proximal 5-12 cm of rachis, fibrous; sepals free, triangular, 3- 5 x 3 mm, contorted to left, glabrous, irregular to dentate on margin; petals free, triangular, 3-5 x 3 mm, imbricate to right, glabrous; staminodial ring adnate to petals; pistil conical, 3-5 mm tall; stigma capitate, shorter than 1 mm, with three short branches, wrinkled, glabrous. Fruit ovate to turbinate, 1.5-2 cm long, ca. 1.3 cm diam., the stigmatic remains truncate with stigmas sessile and minute, the persistent perianth shorter than half of fruit; endosperm ho- mogeneous; seed 1.

description: Fruit 10-11 mm diam., with pericarp 0.9 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-resembling Iguanura and Rhopaloblaste in the numerous vascular bundles with thick fibrous sheaths that form a mantle in the inner pericarp, but differing in possessing a loose mantle of large fibrous bundles in the outer pericarp. This is one of the few genera (along with Neoveitchia and Alsmithia) in the Iguanurinae that form such a dual system of protective fibers. It also resembles Clinostigma, but the fibrous bundles are more oblique in the latter and the fibrous vascular bundle sheaths not as well developed. Also distinctive are the extremely large and numerous raphide-bearing cells, the thin, intermittent layer of brachysclereids just below the epidermis, and the confinement of tanniniferous cells to the innermost pericarp.

description: Caespitose epiphytes. Roots thick, fleshy, white, fragrant. Pseudobulbs fusiform, to 12 x 3 cm. description: Caespitose epiphyte to 35 cm tall. Roots thick, fleshy, white, fragrant. Leaves elliptic-lanceolate to oblanceolate, acute, the uppermost with a large, close, sheathing base soon tapering to a channeled petiole-like leaf base. Inflorescence an arching, stout, lateral, basal raceme. Flowers 5-10, nonresupinate, strongly fragrant, the sepals and petals pale greenish yellow, the labellum exterior pale buffyellow, the saccate interior greenish yellow, the column base greenish yellow becoming more yellow toward the apex, the anther white, the pollinia dark yellow, the stipe pale yellow with prominent hyaline basal auricles, the viscidium pale brownish lavender. Sepals subsimilar, elliptic-oblong, blunt, the dorsal sepal 3.1 x 0.75 cm, the lateral sepals 2.2 x 0.8 cm, with carinate, apiculate apices. Petals ovate, acute, 2.3 x 1.4 cm. Labellum ovate, obtuse, rigidly fleshy, 2.3 x 1.7 cm when expanded, base concave-saccate, with prominent triangular calli to each side of the labellum opening. Column extremely short and stout, 1.1 x 0.7 cm. Anther 4.2 x 3.2 mm. Pollinarium 4.2 x 2.7 mm, the stipe base divided at rear in two obovate, hyaline, concave, auricles spreading outward over the suborbicular viscidium.

description: Epiphyte; stems erect, branching from the base, caespitose, to 50 cm tall, terete, leafy above. description: Epiphyte; stems erect or rhizomatous, the erect stems 5-7 cm long, terete, caespitose, leafy above the base, the rhizomes to 20 cm long, rooting and sprouting branches at the nodes. description: Epiphyte; roots fibrous, glabrous; stems caespitose, branching at the base, to 1 5 cm long. description: Small equitant monopodial epiphytes to 6 cm tall. Roots pubescent. description: Plants predominantly epilithic, rarely epiphytic, rhizomatous, to 145 cm tall. Roots many, slender to thick, velamentous or canescent. Inflorescence terminal, to 133 cm tall, peduncles slender, erect, distantly several-sheathed, paniculate above, lateral branches semi-erect, flowers to 60. Petals yellowish-orange with reddish-brown striping to- wards apex, oblanceolate to spatulate, acute to obtuse, to 1.9 cm long, 6 mm wide. description: Plant epiphytic or lithophytic, rhizomatous, to 8.5 dm long. Roots numerous, slender to thick, velamentous or canescent. description: Plant epiphytic, rhizomatous to 6.5 dm long. Roots many, slender, velamentous. Rhizome short, stout, creeping, enclosed by imbricating scarious sheaths. description: Plant epiphytic, rhizomatous, to 6 dm long. Roots numerous, slender, velamentous. Rhizome short, stout, creeping, enclosed by imbricating scarious sheaths. description: Plants epiphytic and epilithic, rhizomatous, to 1.5 m tall. Roots many, slender, velamentous becoming canescent when epilithic. Rhizome short, stout, creeping, enclosed by imbricated scarious sheaths. Stem modified into pseudobulbs, erect, clustered, elongate, narrowly ovoid, attenuate, to 9.6 cm long, 2.8 cm thick, enclosed by scarious sheaths, to 3 leaves at apex. Leaves coriaceous, ligulate, acute, to 37 cm long, 1.8 cm wide, leaf bases lacking abscission layer. Inflorescence terminal, to 1.4 m tall, peduncle slender, erect, distantly several-sheathed, panicu- late above, to 28 flowers. Floral bracts broadly ovate-triangular, acute, to 0.4 cm long, 0.4 cm wide. Ovary pedicellate, slender, to 2.8 cm long. Sepals and petals green to greenish-yellow with reddish-brown striping or suffusion near the apex. Sepals oblanceolate, acute, to 2.1 cm long, 0.5 cm wide. Petals spatulate to oblanceolate, acute, to 2.0 cm long, 0.4 cm wide. Labellum free, deeply 3-lobed, to 2.5 cm long, 2.0 cm wide, white with radiating purple lines on lobes, the lateral lobes apically yellow to greenish-yellow, margin of disc yellow to greenish-yellow; lateral lobes oblong, obtuse, erect, embracing column; midlobe round to obovate, apex emarginate; callosity under column is 2 lateral erect keels joining at junction of lobes and extending into disc. Column purple, streaked with reddish-purple, to 0.9 cm long, 0.4 cm wide, with membranous incurved rounded auricles at apex. Anther terminal, yellow, incumbent, operculate; pollinia 4, waxy, with a caudicle. Capsule ellipsoid, to 3.2 cm long, 1.4 cm thick.

description: Multi-stemmed shrubs, 3-6 m tall, with leaves present on the last 7-10 nodes of the terminal branchlets (not apically clustered); bark smooth, dark brown; wood white; young leafy branchlets 3-6 mm thick, densely minutely puberulent, decussately subtetragonal, copiously resinous, the resin exuding from young stems and stipular colleters. Stipules a sheathing truncate ring 3-4 mm tall, connected to the petioles, minutely puberulent outside, densely covered with minute colleters throughout the whole surface inside; long-persistent with two petiole scars on the sides, remaining on stem as a tight series of ring-shaped units. Blades (2.5-)4.5-8 x 1-2.5 cm, length: width ratio 3.2:1 to 4.5:1, subsessile, elliptic to broadly obovate, rounded at base and at apex, dark olive-green and shiny above and pale green below, coriaceous, drying greenish brown above and olive-green below; glabrous above and below; primary and secondary veins glabrous; primary veins prominent below, secondary veins 8-12 each side faintly visible above, tertiary not visible (submersed within the mesophyll); petioles to 3 mm long, 2-3 mm thick, subterete. Flowers axillary and solitary, 2 per node, without bracteoles subtending the flowers; pedicels stout, 4-5 mm long, ca. 1 mm thick. Calyx glabrous throughout, deep orange, with 4 membranaceous, foliose lobes; tube extremely reduced, ca. 0.3 mm tall; lobes ovate, 12-17 X 5-6 mm, with sub-parallel venation veins 5-7. Corolla tubular, short-lobed, ca. 2 cm long, yellow; lobes 4, imbricate in bud, glabrous throughout. Stamens 4, half-exserted, of equal length, subsessile; filaments attached on the tube near the mouth; anthers narrowly oblong, dorsifixed near the base. Style exserted, terete, glabrous, with style branches. Capsules turbinate, decurrent at base, ca. 3.5 mm long, glabrous, bilocular, with solitary seeds, indehiscent; disk glabrous; persistent calyx functioning as a pterophyll on mature fruits. Seeds basally inserted, obovoid, fleshy, smooth, with basal hilum.

description: Caespitose epiphytes with stems 10-12 cm long. Leaves 3-5, graduating in size towards the apex, ligulate, emarginate, coriaceous, to 6.5 x 1.6 cm. Inflorescence subsessile, terminal, few-flowered umbel. Flowers yellow-green, fragrant; dorsal sepal elliptic, obtuse, recurved, 16.5 x 4 mm, the lateral sepals obliquely elliptic, obtuse, recurved, 14 x 3.7 mm; petals linear-oblanceolate, obtuse, 1-veined, 13 x 1.8 mm; labellum transversely reniform-bilobulate, strongly convex (the halves strongly deflexed along the midvein), 8 x 16 mm, with paired 1 mm globose calli at base; column slightly arcuate, 1.1 cm long, with hooded, fringed clinandrium; ovary 2.8 cm long; pollinia 4.

description: Trailing epiphytes to 8 cm tall. Rhizome terete, segments to 2.5 cm long, covered with persistent, scarious, imbricating, +/- distichous bracts. Stems 2.5 x 0.8 cm, green with dark greenish black spots and markings over the surface under the chartaceous bracts. Leaves 2, linear, semiterete, acute, thickly coriaceous, to 6 x 0.4 cm. Inflores- cences erect, apical, few-branched panicles to 24 cm long, the peduncle to 0.1 cm in diam., with sparse bracts to 0.4 cm, dark red densely covered with hyaline trichomes, the branches few flowered. Flowers flat, spreading, with a faint delicate fragrance, semitranslucent greenish yellow, the column green with purple streaking and an ivory-white apex, the anther rose and yellow, the pollinia bright golden yellow, the caudicles dull yellow. Dorsal sepal linear-lanceolate, acute, 4 x 1 mm. Lateral sepals obliquely broadly elliptic-lanceolate, acute, carinate-apiculate, 4 x 1.8 mm. Petals lin- ear, acute, 3.7 x 0.8 mm. Labellum ovate, acuminate, concave, 3.5 x 2 mm, more or less free from column, with 3 parallel callus ridges at base. Column lightly arcuate, subcylindric, 3 x 1.1 mm. Anther transverse, 0.9 mm wide, the pollinia 4 in 2 pairs on linear-filiform caudicles.

description: Fruit 25 mm diam., pericarp 5.5 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical-distinctive for the seed angled in cross section, the complex inner mantle made up of cable-like fascicles of vascular bundles with massive fibrous sheaths, a separate system of terete fibrous bundles in the outer pericarp, vascular bundles with scant fibrous sheaths scattered throughout the middle pericarp, numerous small tanniniferous cells embedded within the peripheral regions of the fibrous bundles and sheaths, larger tanniniferous cells abundant in the region between the two fibrous zones, brachysclereids lacking, raphide-bearing cells scarce, and the locular epidermis unusually narrow. This is a unique, highly specialized pericarp, with some similarity to Heterospathe and Neoveitchia in the possession of an expanded series of nonvascular fibrous bundles, and to Carpoxylon in the tendency to form large compound vascular bundles with heavy sheaths.

description: Tree or shrub. Branches thin, with a sparse pubescence of straight or curved hairs, glabrescent. Stipules 8-10 mm long, linear-lanceolate to subulate, persistent, glabrate, with some marginal hairs. Petiole 3-4 mm long, densely pubescent, with curved hairs. Stipels absent. Leaf blade 11.5-16.7 cm long, 3.2-5 cm wide, elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, membranous, the base cordate, strongly asymmetrical, the apex acuminate, ca. 1.5 mm long, mucronate; margin irregularly serrate or crenate-serrate, the tooth apex slightly callous; upper surface with minute pustules, glabrous except on the midrib, which bears two types of hairs, one short and curved, the other long and straight; lower surface with irregular minute foveas near the margin, glabrous except the nerves, which have appressed hairs and others similar to those found on the upper surface; venation pinnate, the secondary veins 12- 23 per side. Female inflorescence 8-12 cm long, with flowers in slender axillary racemes; rachis filiform, pubescent with curved hairs; bracts ca. 0.5 mm long, with 3-4 irregular ciliate-pubescent teeth. Male inflorescence not seen. Female flowers in groups of 2-3 per bract, the pedicel 1-2(2.5) mm long at anthesis, pubescent; sepals 4- 5, ca. 5 mm long, triangular-lanceolate, with ciliate margin; ovary densely papillose, hispidulous; styles 2.5-3 mm long, basally papillose, glabrous, laciniate into ca. 18 narrow segments. Capsule (immature) ca. 1.3 mm wide, papillose, glabrate. Seed (immature) ca. 1 mm long, minutely foveolate, the caruncle obsolete.

description: Suffrutex altitudine ad 1 m, ramulis pilis curvis puberulis internodiis 1-2 cm longis; foliorum laminis sat magnis 4-5 cm longis (? et ultra) ovatis vel ovalibus, obtusis, in basi rotundatis, marginibus crenato-serrulatis, pagina superiore hirtella, inferiore subtomentosa, petiolis 1-2 cm longis elatis; paniculis sat amplis pilis glandulosis brevibus extensis hirtellis; calycum florentium tubo 1.5 mm longo, extus hirtello, in maturitate campanulato 3.5-4 mm longo, dentibus posteriore excepto brevibus obscuris, pedicellis 3 mm longis elatis; corollarum tubo 5-6 mm longo, campanulato; nuculis atris.

description: Shrub, 1.5-2.5 m tall, young branchlets sericeous. Leaf blades elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 11-18.8 X 4.1-7 cm, chartaceous to coriaceous, with glandular dots indistinct on both surfaces, the upper surface glabrous, the lower surface densely and permanently silvery-sericeous; apex acuminate; base cuneate; midvein convex above; lateral veins 10-12 pairs, convex on both surfaces, joining in a looped marginal vein at 3-6 mm from the margin, a less conspicuous outer marginal vein present at ca. 1 mm from the margin; petiole 3-5 mm long, rimulose. Inflorescences reduced bracteate shoots, appearing fasciculate with 1-3 decussate pairs of flowers, often at leafless nodes; pedicels 3-8 mm long, sericeous; bracteoles persistent, ovate, ca. 1 mm long; buds 4-5 mm long; hypanthium shortly prolonged above apex of ovary, sericeous; calyx lobes suborbicular, obtuse, 2-3 X 2-3 mm, sericeous; petals broadly elliptic, 6-7.5 X 4.5-5 mm, white with evident reddish glands; style ca. 4 mm long; ovary 2-locular, ca. 11 ovules per locule; filaments 3-5 mm long, the anthers ca. 1 mm long. Fruits not seen.

description: Small tree or shrub, 2.5-9 m tall, young branchlets glabrous. Leaf blades elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 8-13 x 4-7 cm, chartaceous to coriaceous, glabrous, drying olive- green, the upper surface lustrous, smooth, glandular dots indistinct, the lower surface paler and punctate with translucent glands; apex acute to acuminate; base obtuse to cu- neate; midvein convex or biconvex above; lateral veins 7-9 pairs, convex on both surfaces, but not strongly apparent, joining in a strongly looped inframarginal vein at 5- 10 mm from the margin, a less conspicuous outer inframarginal vein present at 1-2 mm from the margin; petiole 5-10 mm long, canaliculate, glabrous. Inflorescences re- duced racemes, appearing fasciculate with ca. 2 decussate pairs of flowers; pedicels 6- 20 mm long, glabrous; bracteoles persistent, ovate, ca. 1 mm long, ciliolate; buds ca. 6 mm long; hypanthium slightly prolonged above apex of ovary; calyx lobes ovate, ob- tuse, 3-4 x 2-3 mm, ciliolate; petals suborbicular, ca. 7 mm diam., white; style ca. 8 mm long, glabrous; ovary 2-locular, many ovules per locule; filaments ca. 6 mm long, the anthers ca. 1 mm long. Fruits globose to depressed-globose, turbinate, ca. 2.5 cm diam., yellow to orange when mature; seed 1; embryo eugenioid, undivided.

description: Arbor parva, 6-13 m; ramuli glabri; folia elliptica, 5-9 cm longa, 1.5-4 cm lata, apice acuminata, margine planis; ramuli inflorescentiarum sinuosi, glabri, 3-6 cm longi, ca 1.5 mm diam; fibres ignotifructus laevis, 12-13 mm longus; pericarpium tenue, ca 0.5 mm crassum, in 6 cocca dehiscens, endocarpio a mesocarpio secedens; mesocarpii nervi 2-3 mm ultra dehiscentium coccorum marginem lateralem projecti; semina subcylindrica, 9-11 mm longa, ca 7 mm lata; testa laevigata, castanea, chartacea, ca 0.1 mm crassa.

description: Small trees, 6-13 m tall; twigs glabrous. Leaves elliptic, 5-9 cm long, 1.5-4 cm wide, the apex acuminate, the base acute, the margins flat; petioles 5-8 mm long, blackened, canaliculate on the upper surface; stipules distinct to connate, ca 2 mm long, 1-2 mm wide. Inflorescence axis sinuous, 3-6 cm long, ca 1.5 mm thick; flower clusters 3 or 4 per cm at middle of axis. Flowers unknown. Fruits smooth, 12-13 mm long, borne on pedicels 5-6 mm long; pericarp thin, ca 0.5 mm thick, dehiscent into 6 mericarps (cocci), the endocarp separating from mesocarp, the inner surface of mesocarp bearing raised veins that project 2-3 mm beyond lateral margin of dehisced valves. Seeds subcylindric, somewhat flattened ventrally, with 2 small basal lobes and a low dorsal ridge, 9-11 mm long, ca 7 mm wide; hilum elliptic ca 2 mm wide and 3 mm long; testa glossy, dark chestnut- brown, chartaceous, ca 0.1 mm thick.
