description: Arbor ramis terminalibus crassis subteretibus glabris, stipulis brevibus obtusis intraxillaribus haud coalitis. Folia simplicia rigide coriacea glabra. Petiolus robustus 10-12 mm longus. Lamina elliptica vel subobovato-elliptica utrinque rotundata vel interdum obtusissima apice subite breviterque aeuminata vel mutica, margine integro revoluto; 6.5-14 cm longa 3-7.5 cm lata; supra in sieco pallide roseo-glauceseens costa fili- formi et impressa nervis secundariis reticulaque prominulis; subtus in sieco pallide carnea costa crassa elevataque nervis secundariis patulis prominentibus vel proominulis 8-10 utroque latere ad marginem curvatis evanescenti-anastomos-antibus venulis reticulo laxo paulo conspicuo vel obsoleto. Inflorescentiae terminales panieula pauciramea brevi folia non superanti, ramis crassis robustis glabris, floribus sessilibus glomerulos formantibus. Bractea infloreseentiae late ovatae amplexicaules 3-4 mm altae. Bracteae floriferae ovatae acutissimae dorso angulato-carinatae 3-3.5 mm longae. Sepala ovato-triangularia acuta 2-2.5 mm longa. Discus in floribus masculis crassus circa 1 mm diamitens. Capsula crassissima subglobosa 3 cm diamitens in 3 valvas bifidas dehiseens. Valvae ovatae apice acutae cirea 3 X 2 cm monospermae epicarpio crasso (3 mm crasso) granuloso, endocarpio durissimo. Columella centralis crassa triquetra glabra apice subtrialata, circa 1.7 cm longa. Semina ecarunculata laevia oblongo- ellipsoidea circa 1.8 cm longa.

description: Monoecious trees, 4-20 m tall; twigs brown, glabrous, with abundant lenticels. Leaves elliptic, 5-13.5 cm long, 1.5-6 cm wide, coriaceous, the apex acuminate, the base acute to obtuse; petioles 4-10 mm long, corky, canaliculate on the upper surface; stipules distinct, 2 mm long, 1 mm wide. Inflorescence axis slightly sinuous or straight, with prominent lenticels and/or transverse corky ridges, gla- brous; floral bracts with a median row of short trichomes abaxially; flowers green- ish-white to cream or yellow. Staminate flowers sessile, about 5 mm in diam; sepals 2-3 mm long, imbricate, oblong, with rounded apex; petals scale-like, 1 mm long, clawed, the limb peltate-concave; disk annular, lobed, ca 0.5 mm tall, ca 2.5 mm in diam; filaments ca 1.5 mm long, inserted above the disk; anthers ca 1 mm long; pollen reticulate; pistillode cylindric, ca 1 mm tall, 0.3 mm diam. Pistillate flowers 5-6 mm wide, on glabrous pedicels 1-3 mm long; sepals 2-3 mm long, ovate, with acute apex; petals 1 mm long, 1 mm wide, clawed, the limb planar-reniform or peltate-concave; disk 0.5 mm tall; ovary 2-3 mm tall. Fruits minutely warty, green, 12-18 mm long, borne on pedicels 3-4 mm long; pericarp ca 1 mm thick, dehiscing into 6 mericarps (cocci), the endocarp separating from mesocarp, the mericarp margins smooth. Seeds subglobose to hemispheric, more or less flattened ventrally, with a longitudinal dorsal ridge, 10-12 mm long, 8-9 mm wide; hilum round to elliptic, up to 2 mm wide and 4 mm long; testa tan to brown, 0.5-1 mm thick, the inner sclereid layer well developed; embryo ca 8 mm long.

description: Trees; young twigs densely rufous-hirtellous. Inflorescence axes densely rufous hirtellous, ca 2 mm thick, somewhat sinuous. Flowers and fruits unknown.

description: Arbor vel frutex, usque ad 8 m altus; ramulis rubiginoso-castaneis, juvenilibus strigillosis vetustioribus glabris; foliis brevipetiolatis, petiolis 3-5 mm longis dense breviter pubescentibus; laminis elliptico-lanceolatis vel lanceolatis apice obtuse acutis vel acutis basi obtusis vel subacutis 4.5-10.5 x 1.5-3.5 cm, supra per costam mediam modice puberulis alibi pilis dispersis instructis, subtus costa media manifeste strigosis alibi moderate adpresso pubescentibus; nervis lateralibus utroque latere 12- 17; venulis tertiariis ubique conspicue minuteque reticulatis; inflorescentia axillari vel terminali, floribus praecipue solitariis vel binis; pedunculo filiformi elongato 1.5-4.5 cm longo laxe piloso; calycis lobis 4 reflexis suborbiculari-oblongis apice rotundatis 2.3-2.4 mm longis supra medium 2 mm latis extus dense sericeis intus glabris; petalis 4 reflexis elliptico-oblongis apice rotundatis 6-7 x 3-4 mm ubique praeter margines ciliatos glabris; staminibus 50-60, filamentis 2-4.5 mm longis glabris; receptaculo plano 2.5 mm praeter marginem minute puberulam glabro; ovario 2-loculari; stylo 4-4.2 mm longo glabro; ovulis 6, in quoque loculo 3; fructu nutanti subgloboso 2 cm longo 2.5-3.5 (5) cm lato; exocarpio 2 mm crasso; semine uno, subgloboso 1.4-2.5 cm longo 1.6-2.6 cm lato.

description: Tree or shrub up to 8 m tall, the trunk up to 15 cm diam; old bark rough, longitudinally furrowed; branches mahogany-colored, youngest strigillose, older ones glabrous; buds and bud scales densely gray-white strigillose, opposite to subopposite; leaves short-petiolate, petioles mahogany-colored, 3-5 mm long, densely pubescent with ascending hairs; leaf-blades firmly membranous, deep green both sides, not noticeably fragrant, elliptic-lanceolate to lanceolate, obtusely acute to acute at apex, obtuse to subacute at base, 4.5-10.5 x 1.5-3.5 cm, shortly puberulous above with scattered hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, but more moderately pubescent along the depressed midrib, below more moderately appressed-pubescent on surface and abundantly strigose on the elevated midrib with rufous hairs up to 0.3 mm long; lateral nerves faint, 12-17 each side, impressed above, faintly elevated below, widely ascending at a 250 angle, anastomosing 2-5 mm from margin; tertiary venation prominently and minutely reticulate on both sur- faces; inflorescence axillary or terminal, mostly with solitary, sometimes 2 flow- ers at an axil; peduncle spreading to declinate, in anthesis 1.5-4 cm long, in fructification 3.5-4.5 cm long, filiform, 0.4-0.5 mm diam, laxly pilose with pale ascending-spreading hairs 0.6-0.7 mm long; calyx lobes 4, reflexed, gland-dotted, suborbicular-oblong, rounded at apex, united 1 mm at the base, subcucullate, densely pale sericeous without, hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, glabrous within; hypanthium little or not at all prolonged beyond the summit of the ovary; petals 4, reflexed, elliptic-oblong, rounded at apex, 6-7 x 3-4 mm, moderately ciliate on margins with hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, elsewhere glabrous on both surfaces, gland- dotted; stamens 50-60; filaments unequal, 2-4.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers suborbicular-reniform, 0.7-0.8 x 0.7-0.8 mm, glabrous; receptacle flat, quadrangular, alveolate, 2.5 mm diam, glabrous except for the minutely puberulous outer border; style 4-4.2 mm long, glabrous, punctiform; stigma discoid, minute; ovary 2-celled, ovules 3 in each cell; fruit pendent, dull yellow, depressed-subglobose, 2 cm long, 2.5-3.5 (5) cm diam, 1-seeded; exocarp fleshy, 2 mm thick; seed depressed-subglobose, 1.4-2.5 cm long, 1.6-2.6 cm broad.

description: Tree, 4-7 m tall, hairs where present red- dish brown. Leaf blades mostly narrowly obovate or oblong, 9-15 X 3-5 cm, chartaceous to coriaceous, glabrous; glandular dots inconspicuous on both surfaces; apex abruptly acuminate, reflexed; base acute to cuneate; midvein narrowly sulcate on upper surface, lateral veins flat or scarcely raised on lower surface; marginal vein 1, 2-3 mm from the margin, barely visible; petiole 6-12 mm long, canaliculate. Inflorescences reduced bracteate shoots, appeanng glomerate, with 2 or 3 pairs of flowers, often several together at the same node and on leafless nodes; bracteoles ovate, ca. 2 mm long, tomentulose, persistent; flowers known only as buds, these 2-3 mm long; hypanthium not prolonged above apex of ovary, tomentulose; calyx lobes ovate, obtuse, 2 X 3 mm, tomentulose; petals suborbicular, ca. 1.5 mm diam.; ovary 2-locular; ovules many per locule. Fruits globose, 3-4 cm diam., dark-purple, glabrous; seeds 1 (2?); testa membranaceous; embryo eugenioid.

description: Arbuscula 3 m alta. Ramuli subteretes, laeves. Folia opposita, coriacea, glabra, oblongo,-elliptica 11-18 cm longa, 4.5-9 cm lata, basi subcordato-rotundata, apice breviter acuminata, supra nitida, subtus opaca et velutina, nervis lateralibus principali- bus utrinque 15-18, inter se 8 mm distantibus, sed totidem interstitialibus acutis, in facie superiore perspicuis sicut rete tertiario, subtus tantum lateralibus principalibus perspicuis, interstitialibus minus distinctis. Petiolus 3-5 mm longus. Inflorescentiae terminales, paracladiis ex axillis supremis auctae. Pedunculus 5-10 mm longus; pedicelli 3-5 mm longi. Lobi calycis suborbiculares, glabri, 2.5 mm longi, 3 mm lati, intus pauciglandulosi. Corollae albae tubo 10 mm longo, 3 mm lato, in media parte paulo ampliato, extus glabro, intus supra stamina pilis rudis dense obtecto; lobi patuli, obtusi, 15 mm longi, 4 mm lati, obliqui, in alabastro dextrorsum torti. Fila- menta brevissima medio tubo inserta; antherae subsagittatae, 5 mm longae, 1 mm latae, apice acutissimae, thecis basi obtusis, subincurvis, pollinibus usque ad basin repletis. Ovarium glabrum, conicum, 3.5 mm longum, 1 mm latum. Stylus 2 mm longus. Caput stigmatis supra basin patelliforme cylindricum, apice 5-auriculatum et breviter apiculatum.

description: Habitu perenni, stipulis minutis glanduliformibus, foliis alternis linearibus integerrimis, cyathiis 5-partitis glandulis petaloideo-appendiculatis provisis, necnon seminibus haud profunde foveolatis sectioni Tithymalopsidi (Klotzsch & Garcke) Boiss. subgeneris Agalomatis (Raf.) House pertinens, E. wrightii Torrey & Gray affinis sed ab ea foliis reflexis brevipetiolatis et caulibus ubique alternatim ramosis diversa.

description: Plants suffrutescent with densely clustered, erect, wiry stems, including many dead ones persisting from past seasons, 2.5-4.5 (6) dm tall and about as wide, arising from a woody caudex surmounting a thick taproot; herbage ascending- pilose-pubescent, becoming sparsely strigose to glabrous with age; stems apparently annual (new growth originating at the caudex), green, longitudinally striate, erect, monopodially branched at vegetative (lower) nodes, the internodes exceed- ing the leaves, the floral (upper) nodes sympodially branched with the main axis terminating in a cyathium and a lateral branch becoming the leader; leaves al- ternate, the stipules minute glands 0.1-0.25 mm long or occasionally obsolete, the petiole short, 0.2-2.2 mm long, soon becoming reflexed, usually a pale green or yellowish-green, the blade entire, symmetrical at the base, 1-3.2 cm long, quite variable in shape, but the lower ones usually broader and shorter, ovate to lan- ceolate, 2-6.5 mm wide, obtuse, those of the branches and upper stems lanceolate, linear, or filiform, 0.5-3 mm wide, acute, the midvein prominulous beneath, impressed above; inflorescence of solitary cyathia at upper leaf nodes and terminating the branches, the peduncles 0.5-2.5 (10) mm long; cyathium 5-lobed, hemispheric to campanulate, 2.2-3.7 mm high (measurement including the appendages), 1.5-2.5 mm wide from just below the often slightly flaring appendages, moderately strigose, green, often with a brownish tinge, the free lobes of the rim that alternate with the glands within the cup, rounded to obtuse, lacerate-fimbriate, slightly exceeding the glands, whitish-green or sometimes with a reddish tinge, the glands 5, reniform, depressed in the center, ca 0.8-1.2 mm wide (measured parallel to the rim), erect, dark green, the appendages erect or slightly flaring, subequal or slightly unequal, flabellate, glabrous, veiny, white to pink, 0.5-1.5 mm long, 0.8-2.2 mm wide, the apices rounded, truncate, bifid, or dentate, the bracteoles between the male flowers plumose; staminateflowers 20-25, on glabrous pedicels ca 2 mm long, the anther sacs 2, separated by the broad connective, subspherical, 0.2-0.3 mm wide; pistillateflower solitary, on an elongating gyno- phore, the ovary 3-carpellate, strigose, each carpel 1-ovulate, the styles 3, ca 1- 1.3 mm long, connate at the base, forked near apex, the stigmas capitate; gynophore at maturity erect, 3.5-5 mm long, glabrous; capsule depressed-globose and roundly 3-lobed when all 3 ovules matured, septicidal, sparingly strigose, 2-3 mm long and up to 4 mm wide, the walls hard; seed globose-ovoid, 1.8-2.2 mm long, 1.2- 1.6 mm wide, with a few shallow rounded pits in about 10 longitudinal rows (Fig. 2), without a caruncle, the apex subacute to rounded, ashy green or ashy brown, the pits sometimes a darker color.
bibliographicCitation: Pruski, John F. & Urbatsch, Lowell E. 1988. Five new species of Calea (Compositae: Heliantheae) from planaltine Brazil. Brittonia. 40: 341-356.

description: Annua, ramosa, adscendens vel erecta, ad 30 cm alta, caulibus ramisque exigue pilosis, ramulis florentibus glabris vel subglabris; folia opposita, oblonga ovata subrotundave, ve] summa lanceolata, omnia apice obtusa vel rotundata, basi inaequilateralia, cordata vel rotundata, utroque latere fere usque ad basin serrata; caulum folia 1.1-1.8 cm. longa, 6-8 mm lata, ramulorum 7-10 mm longa, 3-6 lmm lata; petioli 0.5-1.5 mm longi; stipulae plerumque coalitae, scariosae, anguste triangulares, ciliato-laciniatae et saepe anguste lobatae; cymae ad ramulorum furcatorum apicem corymbulosae, cyathiis brevipedunculatis paucis (usque ad 15) bracteatis; involucra 1 mm longa, lobis angustis triangularibus, glandulas rotundas stipitatas superantibus; appendicibus albis vel rubellis, lunatis vel late flabellatis, speciosis, quam glandulis 3-4-plo latioribus; flores S ca. 10; capsula glabra, 3-lobata, late ovoidea, infra medium latior, 1.7 mm longa; styli 0.7-0.9 mm longi, basi paulum coaliti, ad medium bipartiti; semina ovoideo-tetragona, 1.1-1.3 mm longa, obtuse angulata, rubella, pallida, ad facies lacunis concavis brevibus et jugis humilibus latis obsita.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Annua nana ramosa 3-5 (-10) cm alta, leviter strigosa, foliis ramulisque juvenilibus et involueris sparse pilis pallidis articulatis obsitis; folia ad nodos infimos 2 et nodos approximatos 1-3, ramulos fiorescentes terminantes, opposita; altera alterna; rami divaricati, saepe ad nodum secundum oppositi longi (2-5 cm); foliorum laminae suborbiculatae, 4-9 mm longae lataeque, nune apiculatae nunc emarginatae, integrae; petioli 3-6 mm longi; stipulae minutae glandiformes; cymulae pauciflorae terminales binis foliis mediocribus oppositis subtentae, utraque deinde circa 2-bifureata, foliis oppositis redactis subbractiformibus; involuera campanulata 0.8 mm longa, 1 mm lata, e pedunculo breviusculo 0.6 mm crasso oriunda; lobis hyalinis, quadrato-oblongis, glandulas superantibus, apice dentibus 5-7 brevibus digitiformibus instructis; glandulae 5 apice coneavae, transversaliter elongatae 0.3 mm longae, appendiculatae, appendicibus ut videtur e glandulae basi oriundis, patentibus vel adscendentibus, in lobulas 2-3 digitiformes 0.2 mm longas partitis; gynophorium 1.5-2.5 mm longum plerumque recurvatum; capsula exserta glabrata subrotunda trisulcata, infra medium latior, 1.7-1.9 mm longa lataque; columella 1.3-1.5 mm longa; styli 0.3 mm longi subcapitati bipartiti; semina biconvexa ovoidea, ecarunculata, laevia, 1.2-1.4 mm longa, 1-1.2 mm lata, 0.7-0.8 min crassa, pallida, caesia vel adusta, marmorata.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Annua, ad 40 cm alta, caulibus ramisque lineatim multifarie plerumque pubescentibus; folia opposita, oblonga oblongo-ovata oblongo-lanceolatave, 8-15 mm longa, glabra vel rarissime longipilosa, apice obtusa subacutave, basi cordata vel inaequilateralia (latere superiori rotundato, inferiori prolongato et auriculato), ambitu prope apicem latere superiori (brevi) serrulata, inferiori fere ad basin; petioli 0.5-1.5 mm longi; stipulae triangulares, coalitae, 1 mm longae (superiores nonnunquam distinctae); cyathia plerumque in dichotomiis superioribus solitaria; glandulae minutae, stipitatae, quam appendicibus 0.2 mm latis duplo angustiores; capsula sparse aequabiliterque pilis debilibus erectis hyalinis 0.5 mm longis obsita, 3-lobata, 1.5-1.7 mm longa lataque; styli 0.6-0.8 mm lonlgi, ad medium vel ultra bifidi; semina prope nigra, oblongo-tetragona angulis acutis, 1.2 mm longa, ad facies irregulariter obscureque transverse rugulosa.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Verisimiliter perennis sed anno primo saepe florens, caulibus tenuibus subglabris ascendentibus 20-50 cm altis, paucis vel multis e radice lignescenti; folia caulinia alterna (infloreseentiae basi dua opposita; bracteae nonnunquam foliaceae oppositaeque; basi plantae ramuli foliaque suboppositi); folia inferiora latiora, elliptica vel raro suborbicularia; mediana superioraque plerumque elongata, oblonga vel linearia, apice obtusa vel ad apicem basinque attenuata, 2-5 mm lata, (2.5-) 4-10 cm longa; petioli 4-8 mm longi; stipulae glanduliformes, subulatae vel latiores, 0.1-0.3 mm longi; infloreseentiae rami tenuissimi, subnudi, in modum eymae semel- vel bifureati, foliorum caulinium pari summa subtentes; eymarum bracteae valde reductae, vix foliaceae, plerumque petaloideae, earum ultimae albae vel dilute rubeseentes, oblanceolatae, ca. 1 mm latae, 4-5 mm longae, eyathia conferta pauca, folia superantia, 1.2-1.5 mm longa; pedunculis 1-3 mm langis; -lobis- laciniatis, latis, albis, cum appendicibus 0.5-1 mm longis subaequilongis; glandulis 4, ut videtur in basibus coneavis appendicum albarum vel dilute rubeseentium, ovatarum curvato-patentium depressis; styli 0.7-1 mm longi, bipartiti; capsula 3-lobata, 2 mm alta, 3 mm lata; columella 1.5-1.7 mm longa; gynophorium 1.5-4 mm longum recurvatum; semina ovoidea, nigreseentia, basi rotundata, apice pyramidata, superficie foveolata nonnumquam tuberculataque, foveolis grandis, concavis.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Most of the collections appear to be anlnuals or delicate perennials with small roots and solitary or few stems. In Mexia 1667 there are 20 or more stems arising from a woody root about 2 cm thick; the bases of old stems may be persistent; the very youngest growth may be pubescent, and the leaves scabrous on the involute margins and strigose beneath; the seeds are of a common type, with about 10 longitudinal rows of pits, 3-4 pits in each row, the surface smooth or obscurely tuberculate.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Perennis, glabra, "procumbens" [ex Hinton], caulibus pluribus ad 20 cm longis, e radice erecta lignosa oriundis; folia ovata, integra, 8-13 mm longa, 4-9 mm lata, acuta vel ilnferiora obtusa, omnia basi inaequaliter cordata (uno latere rotundato tantum, breviore), marginiibus involutis; petioli 1-1.5 mm longi; stipulae scariosae, coalitae vel distinctae, triangulares vel apice obtusae, laciniatae, ad 1.5 mm longae lataeque; cyathia terminalia solitaria, pedunculis 2-7 mm longis; involucrum 2 mm longum, intus ad marginem pilosum, lobis deltoideis, 0.5-0.6 mm longis, eorum margines scariosae laciniatae, et costa viridis; glandulae transverse ellipticae obovataeve, 0.5-0.7 mm latae, appendicibus linguiformibus, infra glandulam angustatis, 0.6-1 mm latis, (0.8-) 1.8-2 mm longis; flores [male] ca. 50, fasciculis distinctis coaliti; apices bracteolarum pilosi, inl partes filiformes divisi; capsula 3 mm longa, acute 3-lobata, latior quam lolngior, parte latiore infra medium; styli 0.8-1 mm longi, ad medium bipartiti; semina 2 mm longa, laevia, cineracea, trigona (facie ventrali plana), basi truncata, 1.2 mm lata, lateribus ad apicem pyramidalem angustatis.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Herba perennis ad 50 cm alta, erecta, ramosa, e radice tuberosa subglobosa ad 2 cm crassa oriunda, pilis albis obtusis vel attenuatis 0.5-0.8 mm longis obsita; rami adscendentes, medianis verticillatis, superioribus (foliisque) oppositis, inferioribus nonnunquam alternis; caules saltem infra glabri, minute scabriduli; folia mediana superioraque 3-5-verticillata, lanceolata vel elliptica, 2.5-9 mm lata, 1.5-6 cm longa, (3-) 4-10-plo longiora quam latiora, obtusa vel apiculata, basi attenuata vix petiolata, vel petiolo ad 5 mm longo instructa; stipulae glanduloso-seariosae vel rubidae, laciniatae, ad 1 mm longae, saepe nullae; inflorescentiae rami 2-4-fureati; eymae ultimae cyathiis 1-3 pilosis, late campanlulatis, basi saepe rotundatis, 1.5-2 mm longis (appendicibiis inclusis) instructae; glandulae 5, ellipticae; appendices reniformes rotundataeve, virides vel purpurascentes, crassistipitatae, integrae vel lobulato-crenatae, corpore 1.2-1.3 mm,lato, 0.8 mm longo, in margind angusto ultra glandulam producto; ovarium pilis albis hirsutum; styli 1.5-1.7 mm longi, basi breve connati, fere ad mediumn bipartiti; capsula pilosa, 3-lobata, 4 mm longa, 5-5.5 mm lata; gynophorium 5 mm longum, valde recurvatum; semina rotundato ovoidea, laevia, obscura, nigrescentia, 2.5 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Herba perennis 50-70 cm alta rhizomata, caulibus erectis tenuibus multoties ramosis vel dichotomis inferne glabris, supernie sparse pilosis, pilis appressis vel adscendentibus, acutis, subflavis, usque ad 0.6 mm longis; folia opposita, valde asymmetrica, integra vel sinuosa vel vix denticulata, oblongolanieeolata vel -elliptica, (10-) 15-32 mm longa, 5-12 mm lata, apice obtusa vel rotundata, basi unilateraliter rotundata, margine altero latere fere recto; petiolis 1-2 mm longis; stipulis distinctis subulatis, juventute fimbriato-ciliatis, 1-1.5 mm longis; eymulae 2 subcapitatae terminales brevipedunculatae, peduiculis 1-10 (-40) mm longis parvibracteatis, eyathiis numerosis congestis; ilnvoluera anguste infundibuliformia, base attenuata vel paululum in pedicellum contracta, 1-1.5 mm longa, 0.6-0.9 mm lata, glandulis stipitatis (3-) 4 instructa; glandulae transverse ellipticae, apice coneavae, ut videtur infra medium appendicum albarum lateraliter insertae; appendices albae spatulatae subpatentes, basi angustatae, cum stipite 1-1.2 mm longae, lamina 0.3-0.5 mm lata; involueri lobi oblongi, fimbriati, glandulas plus minusve aequantes; flores [male] 7-10; gynophorium glabrum, breviexsertum, recurvatum; capsula 3-lobata, 1.5-1.8 mu longa, 2-2.2 mm lata, ilnfra medium latior, sulcis exceptis pilosa. pilis flaccidis subflavis; styli 0.5-0.7 mm longi subcapitati bifidi; semina ovoideo-quadrangulata, 1.1-1.3 mm longa, fusco vel rufo-livida, ventraliter obtuse angulata, dorsaliter carinata, faciebus dorsalibus convexis, rugulis anastomiosantibus obscure reticulatis.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Flowering stems few or several from the sparingly branched slender black rhizomes 1-2 mm thick, 20-30 cm long; leafy stems up to 1-1.5 mm thick, with few nodes and very long (5-10 cm) internodes; inflorescence moderately pilose; leaves glaucous and sparingly pilose beneath, glabrous above, almost all on each plant with a few small teeth at east lnear the tip; inflorescence usually sessile or nearly so at the terminal niode, sometimes on a leafy peduncle, rarely at the penultimate node also.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Frutex invalidus ad 1-2 mm longus, caulibus diametro ad 1 cm; caules aequabiliter crispo-pubeseentes; folia aequabiliter sed saepe sparse strigosa, glabrata; laminae oblongae, ellipticae, ovatae obovataeve, 1.5-2.5 cm longae, 8-13 mm latae, ramulorum juvenilium saepe minores, aut angustiores aut breviores et subrotundae; folia apice acuta vel rotundata, basi rotundata vel semicordata (inaequilateralia), ambitu utroque latere fere ad basin serrulata, dentibus lateris longioris (cordati) manifestioribus; petioli 1-2 mm longi; stipulae (plerumque) distinetae, nonnunquam coalitae, pallide brunneae, anguste triangulares, 0.5-0.8 mm longae, basi saepe induratae et multilobatae; cyathia solitaria vel in cymis parvis bracteatis; involucrum 1.5 mm longum, urceolatum, basi rotundatum, extus ad marginem pilosum, pedunculo 2-3 mm longo instructum; bracteolis tenuilobatis apice piloso-cristatis; lobis late deltoideis, cum glandulis ellipticis sessilibus viridibus ca. aequilongis, appendicibus integris, albis vel dilute rubidis (puniceis), ad 0.4 lum latis, quam glandulis duplo vel ultra latioribus; floribus 8 ca. 20; capsula glabra, 1.5 mm longa, ca. 2 mm lata, valde 3-lobata lobis acutis, infra mnedium latior; styli 0.7-1.2 mm longi, basi vix coaliti, ultra medium bipartiti; semina 0.8-1 mm longa, ovoideote tragona, basi truncata, puniceo-albida vel rubella, obscure scrobiculata vel valde transverse jugata.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description:
Perennis vel fortasse annua 40 cm alta, caulibus tenuibus erectis basi lignescentibus, iiiferne et ad angulos glabris, superne sparse pubescentibus; folia (eis inflorescentiae ramos subtendentibus exceptis) alterna, ovata vel oblongo-elliptica, 1-1.4 cm lata, 2.5-3.2 cm longa, rare pilosa, apice obtusa vel subacuta, basi rotundata vel obtusa, marginibus revolutis integris, basilaribus supra petiolum continuis, folia itaque subpeltata; petioli 7-12 mm longi; stipulae glandiformes; cymae 10 cm longrae, 3-5-dichotomae, cyathiis fere solitariis brevipeduiiculatis; involucrum turbinatum appendicibus inclusis 1-2 mm longum, cum pedunculum pilis appressis flaccidis obtusis 0.3 mm longis obsitum, lobis brevibus rotundatis ciliatis, quam glandularum stipitibus brevioribus; glandulae 5 stipitatae, ellipticae vel reniformes, 0.5-0.7 mm longae, appendicibus plerumque 3-lobatis, lobis (nonnumquam 2 vel 4) viridibus ovatis, subulato- vel caudato-acuminatis, basi ad 0.4 mm latis, 0.6-1 mm longis; flores [male] ca. 12 stipitati; bracteae lineares plumosae; styli 0.6-0.8 mm longi, tota longitudine bipartiti, subcapitati; capsula valde 3-lobata, laevis, 3.5 mm lata, 2.7-3 mm longa; gynophorium 2.5 mm longum, glabrum, vix recurvatum; semina ovoidea, adusta, 2 mm longa vel paulum longiora, punctato-favosa et tuberculata.

Species comite adjutoreque Joseph Sooby juniore (1924- ), qui mecum anno 1952 per terram mexicanum lustravit, nominavi.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1961. Euphorbiaceae novae-galicianae. Brittonia. 13: 145-205.

description: Stems cespitose but generally only one developed with suckers at base, erect, 5-11 m tall, 5-7 cm diam at base, 3 cm diam at apex, grayish, slightly fissured longitudinally. Leaves 9-12, spreading, arching; sheaths closed and forming a crownshaft, 48-65 cm long, green, distally with moderate covering of woolly, reddish-brown trichomes; petiole 20-35 cm long, concave adaxially, rounded abaxially, green (reddish, as the rachis, in young plants), densely covered on both surfaces with woolly, reddish-brown trichomes; rachis 112-145 cm long, ridged adaxially, slightly rounded abaxially, densely covered on both surfaces with woolly, reddish-brown trichomes; pinnae 48-69 per side, subopposite, regularly spaced, linear-lanceolate, inserted in one plane, almost pendulous (form- ing a roof shape), with mid-vein prominent adaxially and abaxially and with 2 submarginal lateral veins, pinnae margins and veins adaxially and abaxially with scattered brown scales; proximal pinna 20-25 cm long, 1-2 mm wide; middle pinna 35-41 cm long, 6-10 mm wide; apical pinna 14-15 cm long, 5 mm wide. Inflorescence infrafoliar at anthesis; peduncle 4-5 cm long, 1 cm diam at peduncular bract scar; prophyll 32 cm long; peduncular bract 32 cm long, 2 or 3 smaller peduncular bracts present to 4 cm long; rachillae ca 30, to 30 cm long, 2 mm diam, slightly swollen at base, each subtended by a small bract, with a dense covering of short, reddish-brown trichomes, these straight or slightly undulate, fasciculate, less than 0.5 mm long; triads not sunken into rachillae, surrounded by a prominent, apiculate bract to 1 mm long; flowers in triads proximally, paired or solitary staminate distally, or occasionally inflorescence almost all staminate; staminate flowers (immature) to 4 mm long, glabrous; sepals briefy imbricate and free distally, connate proximally, gibbous, deltate, apiculate, 2.5 mm long; petals valvate, lancolate, to 3 mm long; stamens 6; anthers basifixed, shortly sagittate, 1 mm long; filaments 0.3-0.6 mm long; pistillode much longer than stamens, 3 mm long; pistillate flowers (immature) surrounded by 2 low bracts; sepals free, imbricate, deltate, 1.5 mm long; petals similar to sepals; staminodes absent; fruit ellipsoid, 1 x 2 cm, with prominent subapical stigmatic residue ca 2.5 mm long, and with an expanded perianth to 7 mm long; epicarp black; mesocarp to 0.5 mm thick, prominently 2-layered, with parallel fibers; endocarp thin, adherent to seed; seed ellipsoid; raphe branches few, anastomosing; hilum basal, elongate; endosperm homogeneous, with central air space; embryo basal; eophyll pinnate.

description: Inflorescentia sessili e triadibus piuribus composita a congeneribus omnibus distincta. Arbor ca. 10 m alta, trunco 10 cm diam. Rami novelli 3 mm diam., complanati, lateribus angustioribus sulcatis, internodiis 7-10 cm longis. Inflorescentia sessilis, e triadibus 15-20 umbellatim dispositis composita; triades stipite 1.3-2.0 cm longo instructae; pedicelli 7-10 mm longi. Bracteae minimae et filiformes, mox deciduae. description: Large forest trees up to 30 m tall and 2 m DBH; bark light brown, rough, consisting of scales 0.5-2 cm in diam; sapwood reddish-brown; heartwood black; lenticels abundant, whitish, elliptic, oriented parallel with the axis, furrowed in the center, expanding laterally with age and becoming square to oblong; shoots glabrous. Leaves simple, alternate; blades thin, chartaceous, green above, glaucous below, but occasionally with reddish veins on both surfaces, ovate to elliptic, 4-14 cm long, 2-9 cm wide, frequently larger on stump shoots, pinnately veined, glabrous, apex acute, margins entire, bases truncate to rounded or oblique; petioles 0.5-2 cm long, glabrous; stipules deltate, 2-3 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, margins laciniate-ciliate. Flowers unisexual, in minutely bracted axillary clusters of 2-6; plants dioecious. Staminate flowers ? actinomorphic; pedicels 3-4 mm; sepals 5, green with brownish tips, free, unequal, 1.5-2 mm long, subspatulate, with ragged margins; petals absent; stamens (3) 5, inserted alternately with the somewhat irregular lobes of the floral disk, opposite the sepals; filaments short, 1-2 mm long; anthers 4-sporangiate, 2-loculed, extrorse, basifixed, 1-1.5 mm long; pistillode conic, projecting ca 0.3 mm above the disk. Pistillate flowers ± actinomorphic; pedicels 7-14 mm, dilated slightly apically; sepals 5, glabrous, 1-2.5 mm long, unequal, ranging from deltate and ascending with acute apices to spatulate and spreading with rounded upturned laciniate apices; petals absent; disk hypogynous, 0.3 mm high, projecting scarcely beyond perimeter of ovary; staminodes absent; ovary superior, unlobed, globose, 2.5-3 mm long, consisting of 3 (4) fused carpels, with 3 (4) locules, and axile, nearly apical placentas; stigmas 3 (4), sessile, bilobed; ovules 2 per locule, hemitropous, with an obturator covering the micropyle. Fruits baccate, reddish-brown to black, juicy, globose, 3-6 mm in diam, subtended by persistent sepals, pedicels 0.5-2 cm; pericarp ca 1 mm thick. Seeds slightly curved, 2-4 mm long, 1 mm wide, + triangular in cross section, with flat radial faces and convex outer tangential face; micropyle apical; raphe ventral, extending to middle of seed; testa 2-layered, the outer layer consisting of large thin-walled cells forming a minutely reticulate surface, the inner layer consisting of palisade-like macrosclereids and enclosing a pit-like depression ca 0.5 mm deep located on the ventral surface below the hilum; embryo embedded in peripheral endosperm, with radical superior and cotyledons slightly bent.

description: Plants tiny, epiphytic, leafless when flowering. Roots very few, fasciculated, thick, tuberous, 2-4 cm long. Leaves not seen, absent at flowering. Stems 1 1-13 cm tall, erect, glabrous, stiff; bracts 1-2 cm long, clasping the stem, tubular, long acuminate to long- apiculate, several clustered at base, drying chartaceous. Inflorescences 4-5 cm long with 5-6 flowers, lax, the axis glabrous, the flowers opening in succession from below. Floral bracts clasping the ovary, 4-9 mm long, shorter towards apex of inflorescence, long acuminate, thin, glabrous, the margin smooth and entire. Flowers green, very small, resupinate, sessile, the perianth segments much shorter than the ovary. Dorsal sepal 2.5-3 mm long, 1-1.3 mm broad at base, oblong, acuminate at apex, glabrous, 3-nerved, forming a hood with the petals, the distal one-third ascending at ca. 450, the margins entire. Lateral sepals ca. 3 mm long, ca. 1 mm broad at base, lanceolate-triangular, falcate, acuminate at apex, 1 -nerved, glabrous, the margins entire. Petals 2.5-3 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm broad, lanceolate, acute, adherent to the dorsal sepal, asym- metrical, 1-nerved, glabrous, the margins entire. Lip clawed (claw 0.3-0.5 mm long), 3-lobed, ca. 3 mm long, ca. 1.5 mm broad across the widest portion of the lateral lobes, distinctly geniculate one-fourth way from base, gently arcuate from there to apex; central part of lip with a thickened, bright red callus with 3 prominent veins starting at base, the lateral two stopping just below apical lobe, the center vein continuing to the tip of the lip; the lateral lobes rounded and upturned, with small auricles at base, with a pronounced network of 1-3 veins, the distal margin of lateral lobes minutely erose; the apical lobe ca. 0.8 mm long, triangular, acute, the margin slightly undulate and erose. Column ca. 2 mm long, slender, erect, somewhat tetragonal, minutely puberulent on inner surface. Anther ca. 1 mm long, ovate; rostellum remnant notched. Ovary 4- 7 mm long, cylindrical, slightly twisted, ascending, glabrous. Capsule not seen.

description: Plants lax and flexible, mostly 12-28 cm tall, the leaves, flowers, and fruits relatively large and few; herbage very finely scabrous or pubescent, the hairs minute and widely scattered, or herbage sometimes essentially glabrous; longest internodes 2.2-2.8-3.7 cm, 1.2-1.9-3 times as long as leaves; leaves generally thin, consistently plane, narrowly to broadly elliptical or ovate, the apices gradual or sometimes rather abrupt, obtuse or usually acute, not pungent; longest leaves 9-16-25 mm, length/breadth inidex 1.2-2.6-5; inflorescences with few miioderately long ascending branchlets, the branchlets few-flowered; pedicels of pistillate plants usually somewhat arcuate and downwardly flexed; corollas rather large, rotate, usually glabrous, or sometimes minutely pubescent, often expanded at the sinuses; corolla base + lobe 1.6-2.8 mmni, the lobes 5-6 tinmes as long as the united portion; fruits large, 6-8 mm across, the hairs very fine, yellowish or brown, usually long alnd abundant; epidermal cells not embossed to miuch embossed.

description: Planta perennis polygama erecta 15-35 cm alta, nodis basalibus lignosis; caules foliaque velutini; folia uninervia, anguste vel late elliptica vel ovata, apicibus acutis sensim angustatis; folia inferiora conferta 2.5-5 mm longa, internodia aequantia, superiora remota ad 11 mm longa, quam internodia 2-4-plo breviora; stomata de- pressa, in pagina superiore deficientia; cellulae glandulosae subapicales vel saepe deficientes; inflorescentia tantummodo bracteata, plerumque angusta, ramis brevibus sed interdum patentioribus longioribusque; corollae rotatae glabrae plerumque rubrae sed interdum viridi-flavae, apicibus prolongatis; fructus sicci, pilis rectis hispidi; chromosomatum numerus, 2n = 22.

description: Frutex ad arbor glaber, aliquando epiphyticus, inermis, ramulis 4-5 min. diametro, in sieco rugosis; foliis longe (7-18 cm.) petiolatis, petiolis gracilibus, omnibus 3-f oliolatis, foliolis longe petiolulatis, ovatis vel elliptico-ovatis, chartaceis, graciliter acute acuminatis, basi rotundatis, 8-15 cm. longis, 3.5-8 cm. latis, in sieco olivaceis vel brunneis, margine argute serratis, denti- bus, 2-4 mm. distantibus, lanceolatis, acuminatis, nervis primariis utrinque 7-9, curvatis, arcuato-anastomosantibus, subtus elevatis, perspicuis, reticulis sublaxis, elevatis, distinctis; petiolulis valde inaequalibus, lateralibus 1.5- 5 cm., medianis 3.5-8 cm. longis; paniculis terminalibus, amplis, apertis, 15- 20 cm. longis, 25-30 cm. latis, rhachibus 2-3 cm. longis, ramis primariis eirciter 10, subverticillatis, eirciter 15 cm. longis, umbellis 15-30-floris, in ramis primariis racemose dispositis, inferioribus oppositis vel alternis, termi- nalibus verticillatis, pedunculis 3-5 cm. longis, bracteis lineari-lanceolatis, longe acuminatis eirciter 6 mm. longis, eaducis, bracteolis brevissimis, eirciter 1 mm. longis, anguste lanceolatis, eaducis; pedicellis gracilibus, 1.5-2 em. longis sub calycem articulatis; floribus viridibus, 5-meris, calycis tubo circiter 3 mm. longo, subellipsoideo, dentibus 5, triangularibus, acutis, 0.5 mm. longis; petalis oblongo-ovatis vel late oblongis, 2-2.2 mm. longis, 1 mm. latis, obtusis, intus longitudinaliter carinatis; staminibus 5, filamentis sursum angustatis, 2 mm. longis; antheris ellipsoideis, 1.2 mm. longis; ovario 5-loculari; stylis cylindraceis, truneatis, 1.8-2 mm. longis, stigmatibus 5, minutis.

description: Tree 5 m. tall; branches brown to gray, smooth; leafy branchlets 1-2.5 mm. in diameter, subquadrangular, brown, puberulous but the hairs more or less concealed by a viscid or resinous coating; leaf scars transversely oval, 1-1.5 mm. high; internodes 3-30 mm. long; buds rounded but changing shape as the oppo- site, inflexed leaves pull out from the solid coating of resin; sheathing stipules forming a prominent collar 2.5-4 mm. high, puberulous but resin-coated, the petioles fused to the stipular ring, and attached to it about half way from the base; leaves sparse, in 2-3 pairs at the tips of the branchlets; petioles 1-7 mm. long, stout, compressed, puberulous and at first heavily resinous; blades 2-10 cm. long, 15-55 mm. wide, oval or nearly ovate, obtuse or subacute, firm-chartaceous, above shiny with resin at least at first, below dull, pale gre.en, above glabrous ex- cept for the puberulous midrib near the union with the petiole, below glabrous except for the hirsute domatia in the primary vein axils, the 6-11 prominent lateral veins on each side ascending, almost straight, then arching forward within the margin; flowers single, terminal, but later surpassed by two opposite axillary branchlets; pedicel 3-5 mm. long, subappressed-puberulous, resinous; bud, flower, and fruit terminal; ovary 5-8 mm. long, 2-3 mm. in diameter at base, 4-5 mm. in diameter at base of calyx lobes, green or dark green, narrowly obconic, 4-5-an- gled towards the tip, the surface appressed-puberulous and resinous; hypanthiun rim narrowly funnelform, 5-8 mm. high; calyx lobes 5 or occasionally 4 in num- ber, in anthesis 7-16 mm. long, 1.4-2.5 mm., wide, linear or obliquely spatulate- linear, obtuse or subacute, green, foliaceous but coriaceous, their blades lying each in a plane radial to and including the axis of the flower, in flower diverging at from 150 to 250 and in full-sized fruit diverging up to 400, and attaining a length of 22 mm., gradually narrowed to the base, longitudinal veins 2-3, anas- tomosing; bud not seen; flowers fragrant; corolla glabrous, white, thick and firm, but shrinking about 20 per cent on drying, the tube when dry 15-20 mm. long, the lower half tubular, 1.8-2 mm. in diameter, the upper half slender-funnelform; corolla lobes 6 or rarely 7 in number, when dried 7-17 mm. long, 5-12 mm. wide, oval, spreading and becoming recurved, eireinate-overlapping at base; stamens alternate, as many as the corolla lobes, attached by the middle to the tube, the filaments almost wholly adnate; stamens projecting into the throat; anthers when dried 5-5.5 mm. long, 0.4-0.5 mm. wide, linear, the sacs each dehiscing by a longi- tudinal slit; style 1 cm. long, stout-filiform, glabrous; stigmas 5-, unequal, eirei- nate into a fusiform body nearly filling the throat; fruit body 2-5 cm. long, usually globose, less commonly ellipsoid, up to 3.5 cm. in diameter, the surface smooth or with a distinct line (but not a salient ridge) descending from each calyx lobe, the funnelform hypanthium rim 4-10 mm. long, present on the ripening fruit, but on maturity deciduous with the calyx lobes, leaving the mature fruit as a globose or ellipsoid beakless structure; ripe fruit hard, the color not recorded; endocarp 0.2-0.3 mm. thick, bony, stramineous; the cavity filled with apparently yellowish pulp in which are imbedded the numerous seeds; seeds 4-5 mm. long, 3-4 mm. wide, 1-1.5 mm. thick, stramineous, finely pitted.
bibliographicCitation: St. John, Harold & Kuykendall, J. R. 1949. Revision of the native Hawaiian species of Gardenia (Rubiaceae). Hawaiian Plant Studies 15. Brittonia. 6: 431-449. f. 1-8.

description: Tree 3-13 m. tall, and to 3 dm. or more in diameter; branches glabrate, pale to dark brown, roughened and ringed; leaf scars 4-5 mm. wide, broadly oval, gray, then brown; leafy branchlets 2-6 mm. in diameter, somewhat quadrangular, puberulent, but the hairs more or less obscured by a coating of greenish resin; buds completely covered with a thick coating of hard, dry, greenish, semi-transparent resin, the buds change in form from subglobose to angular, then horned, as the opposite leaves unfold and gradually pull away in arcs from the center, still thickly covered by and rigid from the hard resin which if heated as on a plant drier liquefies and glues the specimen to the sheets; foliage ample, crowded on the young branches, conspicuously pale green as seen among other forest trees; leaves decussate; blades 5-22 cm. long, 4.5-10 cm. wide, oblance-ellip- tie, the apex subacuminate to abruptly acuminate, the base varying from sub- cordate to rounded to abruptly cuneate, texture firm-chartaceous, above gla- brous, the midrib and primary laterals impressed between the convex intervals, the margins entire, revolute, below the midrib and primary laterals raised, pale and viscid-puberulous, the vein axils. pilosulous-tufted and the midrib mostly pilosulous-bordered, the intervals remotely puberulous to glabrate, the color of the lamina on the upper side parrot-green (Ridgway, R. Color standiards ar'4d color nomrenclature, pl. 6. 1912), and on the lower side oil-green (Ridgway, pl. 5); youngest blades shiny from the thin coat of resin but this vanishing before maturity; petioles 3-8 mm. long, stout, 2-3.5 mm. in diameter, subterete, the fine puberulous indument more or less obscured by solid resin; stipules forming an intrapetiolar ocrea or sheath 6-10 mm. in diameter, 4-8 mm. high, fleshy, green, with a thick resinous coating obscuring the appressed puberulence; flowers with a strong, spicy "Gardenia" scent, single, axillary from one of the upper nodes, short-lived, withering and turning brown apparently one day after anthesis; pedi- cel 3-13 mm. long, 3 mm. in diameter, angled, usually lengthening towards ma- turity, turning abruptly and.bearing the flower at right angles to the stem, finely viscid-puberulous but the hairs pretty well covered by resin; hypanthium 15-18 mm. long, 8-11 mm. in diameter at base of calyx lobes, green, obconic, sharply 4-6-angled, the sides flattened, resinous and puberulent throughout; calyx lobes 4-6 in number, 24-38 mm. long, 8-19 mm. wide, green, coriaceous, radial, as cending at from 400 to 650, averaging 50O divergence from the axis of the co- rolla tube and ovary, the lobes asymmetrically obovate, the inner margin straight or but gently curved, the outer strongly curved, the apex broadly obtuse, per- sisting and foliaceous on the fruit; bud clavate with closely eireinate lobes; co- rolla 3-4.5 cm. long, thick, firm, and almost subcoriaceous, the tube 20-23 mm. long, 6 mm. in diameter at base, 9-10 mm. at the throat, the outer surface and the outer edge of each corolla lobe exposed in the bud, pale yellow-green (Ridg- way, pl. 5) and viscid-puberulous, within glabrous; corolla lobes 6-7 in number, 16-18 mm. long, 10-14 mm. wide, broadly oval, broadly obtuse, white, thick and firm, the lobes at full anthesis speading or the tips somewhat recurving; stamens alternate, as many as the corolla lobes, attached on the corolla tube one-third of the distance from the throat; filament with the free portion a mere bridge-like connection; anthers 13-15 mm. long, linear, the sacs dehiscing longitudinally; style 1 cm. long, cylindric, stout; stigmatic tip 1.4 cm. long, clavate, acute, striped with brown, eireinate lines, the apex almost filling the throat of the co- rolla; rim of the hypanthium 4-5 mm. deep, brown-hirsutulous and heavily resinous; fruit a berry or better a pepo because of the hard, cartilaginous, pale endocarp, the body of the fruit 2-3 cm. long, 18-25 mm. in diameter, oval-sub-globose, with 4-6 sharp longitudinal ridges, one running down from the base of each calyx lobe, at maturity the surface orange; fruit crowned by a cupulate calyx tube 5-7 mm. high, the inner suf ace of the endocarp with raised, sharp, dark, longitudinal ridges equal in number and more or less alternating with the calyx lobes, cavity filled with a fruit-like pulp,- apparently yellow but on slow drying becoming black; seeds very numerous, crowded in the pulp and without any obvious attachment, 1.8-2 mm. long, 1.3-1.4 mm. wide, 0.8-0.9 mm. thick, irregularly obovate, the surface cells elongate-elliptic-oblong, their walls making a prominent reticulate network on the surface, the surface color black probably owing to the discoloration of the pulp in which they are imbedded.

description: Arbor alta ubique glabra; ramulis crassis teretibus rugosis; foliis simplicibus, petiolis striatis leviter canaliculatis, 1.5-6 cm. longis, laminis coriaceis, oblongis vel anguste obovatis, 9-15 cm. longis, 3-6 cm. latis, basi acutis vel obtusis, apice acutis vel breviter acuminatis, margine integris vel remote calloso-denticulatis, pinnatinerviis, costa prominente, nervis secunidariis utroque eirciter 7 curvatis, cum venulis reticulatis prominulis vel planis; umbellis probabiliter 3-5 per infloreseentiam, in racemos breves axillares dispositis, rhachide brevis- sima, pedunculis crassis, eirciter 2 cm. longis, conspicue bracteatis, articulatis, et saepe geniculatis 5-7 mm. supra basin (bracteis coriaceis 1-2 mm. longis connatis); floribus 8-15 per umbellam, receptaculo eir- citer 6 mm. lato, pedicellis crassis 3-7 mm. longis; floribus 7-9-meris, calyce carnoso cupuliformo, 3-4 mm. longo et diametro, limbo brevi denticulato, deintibus deltoideis brevibus; petalis carnosis oblongo-del- toideis, 2.5-3 mm. longis, 1-2 mim. latis, apice subacutis; filamenitis brevibus ligulatis distaliter angustatis, antheris globoso-oblongis eirciter 1 mm. longis; stylis connatis conum carnosum rotundatum formantibus; ovario carnoso, loculis ovulisque 7-9.

description: Tree to 10 m tall, 30 cm diam, the branchlets quadrangular, ribbed, covered with sparse, mostly appressed, tan-colored setae ca 1 mm long; dark red, resinous exudate from stem. Stipular lobes 4 per node, inserted with one edge above a petiole and the other interpetiolar, 13-28 x 8-14 mm, ovate to elliptical with mucronate apex, united basally for 8-17 mm, glabrous except for a patch of pannose, tan-colored hairs around the apex adaxially and scattered setae around the entire margin, provided adaxially at the base with colleters. Leaves 15-22.5 x 9-13.5 cm; lamina coriaceous, elliptic to obovate, apex mucronulate, obcordate, retuse, or rounded, base acuminate, somewhat oblique, usually with revolute margins, with 9-11 pairs of lateral nerves, adaxially glabrous, the costae sunken, abaxially glabrous except for major veins, these prominent and bearing densely hispid hairs ca 1 mm long, tertiary and higher order veins prominulous; petiole 12-25 mm long, sparsely setose. Inflorescence 10-22 x 13-22 cm, branched at base or with peduncle to one half the length of inflorescence; secondary axes alternate or opposite; all axes and pedicels densely hirsute, the hairs spreading, 1.5-2 mm long, tan-colored. Flowers: hypanthium obconic, densely hirsute; calyx lobes 5, pinkish-white, oblanceolate, 52-75 x 9-17 mm, adaxially glabrescent, abaxially appressed-strigulose along mid-vein, margin ciliate with hairs to 3 mm long; corolla pink, the tube ca 20 mm long, glabrous inside, setose outside, the lobes 5, ca 15 mm long, cucullate at apex, setose inside and outside; stamens 5, the anthers fusiform, 6-7 mm long, the filaments ca 4 mm long, inserted at top of tube; ovary 2-celled; style ciliolate, ca 21 mm long, terete, the stigma 2-lobed, the lobes decurrent, 8-9 mm long. Fruit unknown.

description: Plant typical for the genus, to 50 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid, to 10 cm x 5 cm, 7-9- ribbed, bifoliate, covered at the base by 3- 4 chartaceous, nonfoliaceous sheathing bracts to 8 cm long. Leaves to 26 x 8 cm, acuminate, light green, thin-textured, with 3 prominent abaxial veins, the petiole indistinct, to 8 cm long. Inflorescence a pendent raceme from the base of the pseudobulb, to 60 cm long, many-flowered, the rachis angular, winged, to 4 mm wide, the floral bracts 3 x 2 mm. Flowers small to average size for the genus, color variable ranging from white heavily spotted with dull red-brown to solid brownish-purple. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acute, concave, 24 x 6 mm long, adnate to column for proximal 8 mm, strongly revolute. Lateral sepals ovate-triangular, oblique, acute, reflexed, 23 x 9 mm. Petals sigmoid, aristate, adnate to column for most of length, free portion 6 x 1 mm. Column arcuate, clavate, 15 mm long, 3 mm wide at apex, the foot 4 mm long, claw lacking. Labellum to 19 mm long, conspicuously divided into hypochile and epichile; the hypochile slender, 4 mm at widest, tapering proximally, with the hypochilar horns relatively long, hook-shaped, slender, round in cross-section, 2.5-3.0 x 0.5 mm, curved adaxially, the abaxial surface of hypochile concave, the distal end bearing a pair of adaxially pointing seta to 9 mm long; the epichile 10 mm long, conduplicate, saccate, tapering distally, the basal folds of epichile enclosing an erect callus 3 mm tall, 2 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, barely projecting beyond folds of epichile. Pollinia 2, hard, waxy, clavate, 2 x 0.4 mm, the stipe and viscidium 1.0 x 0.3 mm. Ovary and pedicel terete, 36 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, dull red- brown. Fruit not seen.

description: Caespitose epiphytes, plant typical for the genus, to 50 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid, approximate, 7-9-ribbed, to 10 X 6 cm, subtended by 3-4 chartaceous, nonfoliaceous sheathing bracts to 8 cm long. Leaves oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, light green, thin-textured, to 26 X 8 cm, with 3 prominent veins beneath, with an indistinct petiole to 8 cm long. Inflorescence a basal, stiffly erect, 10-15-flowered raceme to 30 cm long, the rachis angular, winged, to 4 mm wide at the base, the floral bracts 4 X 2 mm. Flowers average size for the genus, solid dark blackish purple, the labellum shiny, the ovary and pedicel dull purpleblack. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acute, strongly revolute, 17 X 7 mm, adnate to column for proximal 5 mm. Lateral sepals ovate-triangular, oblique, acute, 23 X 9 mm. Petals sigmoid, aristate adnate to column for most of their length, the free portion 6 X 1 mm. Labellum 17 mm long, claw absent, conspicuously divided into hypochile and epichile, the hypochile broad, 11 mm at widest (including basal horns), tapering distally, abaxial surface concave, the hypochilar horns relatively broad, flattened, triangular, winglike, curved adaxially, the distal end of the hypochile bearing a pair of adaxially pointing seta 9 mm long, the epichile 7 mm long, conduplicate, saccate, tapering distally, with basal folds enclosing an erect callus 3 mm tall, 2 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, the callus barely projecting beyond folds of epichile. Column 15 mm long, 3 mm wide at apex, the column foot 4 mm long. Pollinia 2, hard, waxy, yellow, clavate, 2 X 0.4 mm, the stipe and viscidium 1 X 0.3 mm. Ovary and pedicel terete, 30 mm long, 1.5 mm diam. Fruit not seen.

description: Scandent shrub without raphid crystals, generally strigose with stiff, appressed, stramineous, septate hairs; branchlets slender, 0.5-0.8 mm in diameter toward apex, terete, the internodes 8-13 cm long, dark red-brown, eventually glabrous except for a persistent ring of strigose hairs above stipule scars; stipules inter- petiolar, membranaceous, broadly subulate to long-deltoid, 1.5-3.5 x 0.6-1 mm, long-tapering toward apex, entire, strigillose externally with a few scattered hairs, glabrous internally; petioles slender, subterete, to 2 cm long, about 0.5 mm broad, densely strigose; leaf blades membranaceous, conspicuously rugulose-striate above and beneath, oblong-ovate to elliptic to obovate, 4-8 x 1.5-3 cm, sharply acuminate at apex, acute at base, entire at margin, strigose above and beneath with stiff, appressed hairs to 0.7 mm long, these often more numerous on costa and nerves, the costa prominulous to plane above, raised and rounded beneath, the secondary nerves 4-6 per side, arching gradually outward toward margin, plane above, prominulous beneath, the veinlets consisting of conspicuous tra- cheary elements which form a raised reticulum; flowers solitary, terminal, sub- sessile; calyx membranaceous, laciniate, the lobes 4, subequal, broadly subulate, to 2 cm long, free or united through 1-3 mm at base, acute to acuminate at apex, densely strigose without, glabrous within and charged at the base with ?8 clavate, reddish glands about 0.2 mm long; corolla salverform, membranaceous, the tube slender, to 4.5 x 1.5-2 mm, densely strigose without with stramineous hairs to 1 mm long, glabrous within but very finely papillose to scurfy at throat and on upper surface of lobes, the lobes 4, imbricate in bud, broadly ovate to orbicular, (5-) 12-15 x (5-) 7-12 mm, rounded at apex, entire to erosulous at margin; sta- mens 4, attached about 10 mm below corolla throat, included, the anthers sub-sessile, dorsifixed, attached about 2 mm from base, long-oblong, about 6 x 0.5 mm; ovary obovoid to ellipsoid, about 2.5-3.5 x 1.5 mm, densely strigose with hairs to 1.5 mm long, bilocular, each placenta laminar, rounded at apex and base, about 2.3 mm long, projecting about 0.6 mm from dissepiment, attached over most of length; description: Plant epiphytic, leafless. Stem reduced. Roots aerial, chlorophyllous, to 38 cm long. Inflorescence a simple raceme, occasionally paniculate, to 10 cm long, to 5-flowered. description: Stout perennials 28-40 cm tall. Shoots few, pubescent with tightly retrorsely curling hairs above, puberulent below, branching mostly confined to the lower regions of the stem with the secondary branches long and ascending at close angles. Leaves spreading, narrowly elliptical or linear, at least three times as long as wide, 9-13 mm long, 1.5-4 mm wide, the margins denticulate with the teeth confined to the distal regions of the blade, the base tapered and subsessile, the apex sharply acute, the surfaces glabrous or glabrate above, glabrate below, nerves elevated, the secondariesconsisting of 2 or 3 subopposite, straight, unbranched pairs which depart from themidrib at acute angles. Juvenile foliage distinct from the adult, narrowly ellipticalto ovate, entire, and evenly glabrate. Cymules 5-10-flowered, dense and congested  well spaced or crowded along the upper two-thirds of the shoots; primary peduncles inconspicuous; primary pedicels, 4-5 mm long, puberulent; bracteoles lanceolate. Calyx 5.2-5.8 mm long; the tube 3.7-4.2 mm long, gibbous below for ca. one-half of the tube's length, the distended region 1-1.2 mm wide dorsiventrally, the tube hirtellous with short, stiff, spreading hairs, the upper calyx teeth only slightly united to, form an upper lip 0.9-1 mm long, the lobes narrowly triangular, subulate, 0.1-0.2 mm wide at the base, 0.8-0.9 mm long, laterally spreading and reflexed, hirtellous-ciliate, the lower teeth subulate, recurved, ca. 0.3 mm wide at the base, 1.2-1.7 mm long, hirsute-ciliate; annulus dense, ca. 0.5 mm wide and seated approxi- mately at the juncture of the upper and lower teeth. Corolla 8.9-9 mm long, lavender, annulate with short hairs; the tube 6.8-7.8 mm long, slightly dilated upward, the upper lip ligulate, emarginate, ca. 1 mm wide, 1.2 mm long, conspicuously shorter than the lower lip, reflexed away from the axis, the lower lip spreading, ca. 3 mm wide, ca. 3 mm long.

description: A small perennial caespitose herb ca. 4 cm high, probably forming mats. Leaves coriaceous and sharply ascending, appressed to the stems, ovate, entire, sessile, tapered to a narrowly obtuse or acutish apex, 5 mm long, 2.5-3 mm wide, margins pilose-ciliate, the upper and lower surface glabrous, with 1 olr 2 slightly raised subopposite secondary veins diverging from the midrib at acute angles, straight and craspedrome. Calyx 7.5 mm long, somewhat coriaceous, the tube tubular- funnelform, not at all gibbous below, dilated upwardly, ca. 5 mm long, pilose, the hairs long and spreading, the upper teeth connate for ca. one-half o,f their length, forming a broad upper lip, ca. 2.5 mm long, the lobes triangular, ca. 1.2 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm wide at the base, slightly laterally spreading and reflexed, pilose-ciliate, the lower teeth narrowly triangular-lanceolate, ascending, ca. 2.5 mm long, pilose- ciliate; annulus dense, included, ca. 1.1 mm wide, seated deep within the tube ca. 2 mm below the juncture of the upper and lower lips. description: A small, perennial, caespitose herb forming mats. Stems numerous, unbranched, 3-5 cm tall, arising from a slender woody caudex or trailing rootstock, canescent with short retrorse hairs. Leaf pairs crowded with the internodes shorter than 1.8 mm. Leaf blades entire, ovate, sessile, coriaceous, and somewhat folded, ca 4 mm long, ca 2 mm broad; secondary nerves of 4-5 prominent pairs, forming regularly spaced costae on the underside and diverging from the midrib at angles of ca 550, nearly straight and craspedodrome; dark, regularly spaced, glandular dots occur between the costae; not costate above; margins finely ciliate, both surfaces evenly puberulent with short appressed hairs. Flowers solitary in the upper leaf axils, borne on short canescent pedicels 1-2 mm long. Calyx tubular, slightly distended at the base, 4.5-5.3 mm long; nerves prominent, (12-) 13 (-15), puberulent with hairs upwardly curling; calyx-teeth weakly disposed into the bilabiate condition and strongly pubescent on the inner faces; lower calyx-teeth lanceolate, ascending, ca 1 mm long, the upper calyx-teeth deltoid, ca 0.7 mm long, slightly spreading, with the central tooth commonly reduced to ca '/2 the width and height of the 2 adjacent teeth; tube with a densely hirsute annulus seated ca 0.5 mm below the bases of the teeth and closing the throat. Corolla tubular but slightly dilated above, distinctly bilabiate, 10-11 mm long, lavender; upwardly covered by an appressed pubescence, pubescent within on the palate and basal portions of the tube; upper lip erect and slightly notched at the apex, ca 1.5 mm long; lower lip subequally 3-lobed and spreading ca 2 mm long. Lower stamen pair ascending under th'e upper lip and included by it; upper stamen pair reduced to short staminodia bearing abortive anthers; fertile anther sacs divaricate, separated by a well developed connective. Style glabrous and unforked. Nutlets ovoid, 1-1.1 mm long, dark brown at maturity; surface minutely roughened and becoming mucilaginous when moistened.

description: Tree 3.5 m tall, branches lanulose; stipules interpetiolar, simple, triangular, aristate, 2-3 mm long, persistent, lanulose without; leaves petiolate, petioles 4-5 mm long, lanulose; leaf-blades subcoriaceous, lanceolate-elliptic or elliptic, obtusely acute at apex, cuneately narrowed at base, 2-3.6 cm long, 0.8-1.5 cm wide, white-lanulose below, above sparsely lanulose along midrib, elsewhere mainly glabrescent, margins revolute; lateral nerves 6-8 each side, prominent, sulcate above, elevated below, ascending; inflorescence terminal, many-flowered, densely corymbosely-cymose, trichotomous, epedunculate, subtended by 2 bracts, axes densely lanulose; bracts triangular, acute at apex, glanduliferous, 0.5-0.8 mm long, densely white-lanulose without, margins denticulate, glanduliferous; flowers sessile, subtended by a bract; calyx and hypanthium shortly cylindric, 2 mm long, white-tomentose; calyx 1 mm long, teeth 5, broadly deltoid-triangular, acute and thickened at apex; corolla lavender-purple, hypocrateriform, 9-9.5 mm long, tube 6 mm long, 1.5 mm wide at base, 2 mm wide at orifice, tube densely sericeous without, glabrous within at base, puberulous at orifice and near stamens, lobes 5, valvate, lanceolate, subacute, 2.5 mm long, 1 mm wide; stamens heterostylous, 5; anthers linear, included or exserted, 1.5 mm long; filaments 0.6 mm long, inserted 4 mm above the base of the corolla tube; style 6.5 mm long, puberulous; stigma lanceolate-linear, subacute, pubescent; disk fleshy, umbonate, entire; ovary 2-locular, ovules 6-8 in each cell, vertically disposed, peltately attached; capsule crustaceous or subosseous, 4-5.5 mm long, at first septicidally dehiscent, finally splitting partly downward into bifid valves; seeds rufous-brown, ovate, exalate, margins entire, one end rounded, the other end narrowed, 1.8 mm long, 1 mm broad, flattened, membranous, shallowly reticulate.

description: A tall shrub 2-3 m. high; branchlets thick, densely short-villous; bark of branches fissured, scaly; leaves 1.5-4 cm. long by 1-3 cm. wide, broadly ovate or elliptic, coriaceous, glabrate above, densely white-villous-tomentose below, broadly and irregularly dentate with short teeth; lateral veins 5-8, impressed above, prominent beneath; petiole 2-4 mm. long, villous; stipules ovate, decidu- ous, 1-2 mm. long; flowers in fascicles of 2-3, clustered; floral tube in flower 5-6 mm. long, white-villous, sessile or very short pedicellate; calyx limb 4-5 mm. wide; stamens 20-30, the anthers sparsely hairy; floral tube in fruit 6-9 mm. long, sessile or very short pedicellate (1 mm. or less); style in fruit 3-4.5 cm. long, filiform, sparsely covered with very fine hairs.

description: Tree 3-8 m. high; young twigs red, densely short-villous; leaves 3-7 cm. long and 2-4.6 cm. wide, somewhat coriaceous, obovate to oval, light green and glossy above, densely tomentose beneath with white or tawny tomentum, lateral veins 7-10, margins crenate, sometimes broadly serrate with apiculate-tipped teeth, to nearly entire with somewhat revolute margins; petiole 5-10 mm. long, tomentose; stipules woolly, deciduous, 4-5 mm. long; flowers in fascicles of 3-5, the fasci- cles in axillary groups, or in subcapitate groups at the ends of very short spur branchlets; floral tube in flower 4-6 mm. long, sessile, spreading-villous to woolly; limb 3-5 mm. wide; stamens 20-30, the anthers sparsely hairy; floral tube in fruit 7-10 mm. long, spreading-villous, sessile or very short-pedicellate; style in fruit 4-8.5 cm. long, filiform, covered with very fine, rather sparse spreading hair.

description: Shrub or small tree 2-5 m. high; branches terete, smooth, glabrous; branchlets and young branches somewhat angled, reddish, sericeous; leaves alternate, petio- late, subelliptic, 2-3.5 cm. long, 1.2-1.7 cm. wide, coriaceous, the distal half serrate with broad short apiculate-tipped teeth, dark green and glabrate above, light green and tomentulose beneath, the lateral veins 4-8, depressed above, prominent beneath; petiole 1-3 mm. long, appressed-silky-strigose, the stipules scarious, 2-3 mm. long, acute or acuminate, deciduous; flowers sessile or very short-pedicellate, in fascicles of 2 or 3, the fascicles sometimes crowded on the short spur branchlets into groups of 5-15 flowers; floral tube in flower 5-7 mm. long, appressed-silky; calyx-limb 3-5 mm. wide; stamens 20-30, anthers hairy, exserted; floral tube in fruit 7-9 mm. long, strigose or glabrate, pedicel 4-5 mm. long; style in fruit 3-5 cm. long, filiform, covered with spreading, fine, rather sparse hair.

description: Frutex 5-15 dm. alta; ramis patulis, fere atris; petiolis ellipticis, 2-3.5 cm. longis, crenatis, valde rugosi-reticulatis; basi aeuta, apice acuta vel obtusa, utraque pagina delicate villosa; pedicellis fere 1 cm. longis; fructu ellipsoideo, plene, 1.5 cm. longo, circa 1 cm. lato, luteo, cute tenui.

description: Arbor usque ad 8 m. Folia ovata vel oblongo-ovata, acuminata, integra, ad basem subtruncata, glabra; inflorescentia axillaris, spicatoracemosa, compacta; flores sessiles; calyx deciduus, prope basem circumscissile; petala suborbiculares; stamina plusminusve 25; stigma truncata.

description: Trees about 8 m tall, the branchlets rather heavy and thick with abundant oval lenticels. Leaves ovate or oblong-ovate, acuminate, subtruncate at the base, entire, subcoriaceous becoming coriaceous, glabrous, with about 12 pairs of lateral veins, the blade 13-16 cm long and 6-7.5 cm broad, the petiole thick and fleshy, canaliculate, 1-1.5 cm long; inflorescences axillary, compact, densely-flowered spicate racemes shorter than the leaves, ca 1.5 cm in diameter; flowers sessile or nearly so on the somewhat fleshy rachis, small; calyx deciduous, circumscissile near the base, narrowly campanulate, ca 3 mm long, the lobes short, narrowly triangular; petals inserted on the throat of the hypanthium, white, suborbicular, 2-2.5 mm long and as broad, soon deciduous; stamens ca 25, attached on the throat of the hypanthium, the filaments free, ca 3-3.5 mm long; ovary glabrous, the style ca 2 mm long, terminal, soon deciduous, the stigma truncate; fruit unknown.

description: Glabrous, some individuals lacking even the characteristic tufts along the midribs; many individuals have the tufts but are otherwise glabrous. Foliage leaves mostly 2.5-4 cm. wide, 8-12 cm. long, 2.5-3.5(-4.3) times as long as wide; petioles 1-2(-2.5)cm. long; blades with 5-11 (usually 5-7) teeth per cm. of margin. Second floral leaf mostly about 2.2 cm. wide (1-3.6 cm.) and 6 cm. long (2.5-9.5 cm.), the l/w ratio usually about 2.8 (1.7-4.6 in individual plants). Petioles usually about 1.2 cm. long (0.5-2 cm.), blades with about 7 teeth per cm. of margin (5-11). Flowering branches averaging about 15 cm. long; flowers usually about 35; pedicels about 4 mm. long in flower, 6 mm. in fruit (the range, 2.5-9 mm.); calyxlobes 1.5-2.5 mm. long (usually about 1.7 mm.); petals mostly about 3.5 mm. long and wide; longer filaments up to 5 mm. long; anthers averaging about 0.8 mm. long; style averaging about 1.7 mm. long; fruit up to about 2.5 cm. across.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1951. A revision of the North American black cherries (Prunus scrotina Ehrb., and relatives). Brittonia. 7: 279-315.

description: Arbor glaberrima, 6-8 m. alta, ramis teretibus, laevibus, consperse lenti- cellatis, atropurpureis vel purpureo-brunneis, ultimis eirciter 2 mm. diametro; foliis plerumque 10-20 cm. longis, rhachibus supra canaliculatis vel angustissime alatis, in axillis petiolulorum plus minusve glandulosis; foliolis 11-13, oppositis vel suboppositis, brevissime petiolulatis, sessilibus vel subsessilibus, papyraceis vel submembranaceis, oblongis vel oblongo- ellipticis, rotundatis vel subacutis, basi inaequilateralibus, plerumque plus minusve oblique truneatis vel subrotundato-truneatis, margine argute acumi- nato-serratis (basi integris), 2.4 cm. longis, 0.8-1.5 cm. latis, nervis primariis utrinque 8-10, subtus distinctis; infloreseentiis 8-10 cm. longis, paucifloris, pedunculatis, ramis paucis, pedicellis 1-2 cm. longis; floribus pro genere magnis, eirciter 11 mm. longis et 15 mm. diametro, roseis; calycibus eirciter 8 mm. diametro, tubo 4 mm. longo, lobis late triangularibus, eirciter 2 mm. longis, basi 3 mm. latis, acutis, margine sursum leviter glanduloso-serratis; petalis late ovatis, rotundatis, eirciter 6 mm. longis et 5 mm. latis; staminibus eirciter 20, filamentis 3-4 mm. longis, sursum angustatis; antheris ellipsoideis, 1 mm. longis; stylis 5, liberis, 5 mm. longis; fructibus ovoideis vel anguste ovoideis, eirciter 1 cm. longis.

description: Low mat-forming herbaceous perennial from a branched woody caudex, the base clothed with old leaf-bases; stems ascending to erect, 4-9 cm long; leaves essentially basal, greenish, 1.5-4.5 cm long, the leaflets 5-15 pairs, tightly imbricated, canescent, divided to base into 3-5 oblanceolate-obovate segments, 0.5-1.5 mm long; inflorescence a paniculate-cyme, 2-6 cm long; bracts leafy, often appearing near the middle of the stem; hypanthium shallowly cupulate, 1-2 mm wide, yellow within; receptacle densely covered with long silky villous hairs; bractlets triangular, about 2/3 the length and 1/2 the width of the sepals; sepals yellowish, triangular, 1.0-1.5 mm long, 0.7-1.0 mm wide; petals yellow, linear, 0.25-0.75 mm long, 0.1-0.15 mm wide; stamens 5, inserted at the margin of receptacle; filaments yellow, glabrous and dilated at the base, 0.25-1.0 mm long; anthers ovate, yellow except for purple marginal sutures, 0.25-0.5 mm long; pistils glabrous, 2-3 in number; styles yellow, glabrous, 0.75-1.0 mm long; achenes brown, smooth, 0.75-1.0 mm long, 1, occasionally 2 in number. Flowering mid-June to mid-July.

description: Perennial herb from a branched caudex surmounting a long taproot; herbage non-glandular, ascending-strigose, the undersides of the leaves with the addition of a fine, dense, whitish tomentum; flowering stems spreading to prostrate with upcurved tips at anthesis, 0.4-1.1 dm long, surpassing the leaves in length; leaves mostly basal, 2.5-4 (5) cm long, these pinnately 5-foliolate with a short rachis, the petiole 1-2.5 (4.2) cm long, the leaflets 7-15 mm long, the terminal one usually the largest and the proximal pair the smallest, oblanceolate to obovate, cuneate, the apex of the terminal leaflet (2) 3 (5)-lobed, the lateral ones 1-3-lobed, or some of them entire, especially when small, the midvein impressed above and pro- minulus beneath, the cauline leaves few or none, usually 3-foliolate, the stipules lanceolate, acute; cyme 1- or 2-flowered or sometimes openly 3-flowered, non- glandular, strigose-sericeous, the pedicels 1-3 cm long; hypanthium shallowly cupulate; bractlets 2-4 mm long, elliptic, rounded or obtuse, usually darker than the sepals with a brownish tinge; sepals 3-5 (6) mm long, deltoid-lanceolate or -ovate, acute; petals 4-6.5 mm long, ovate to suborbicular, rounded, truncate, or usually retuse, yellow; stamens 20, the anthers 0.7-0.8 mm long; pistils ca 25, the styles 1.8-2.4 mm long, filiform, subterminally attached; achenes ca 1.7 mm long (not fully developed).

description: Glaucous, nearly glabrous perennial from a stout taproot; crown simple or with few short stout branches, clothed with the dark reddish-brown remnants of the previous years' leaf-bases; stems several, prostrate to decumbent (to ascending in dense vegetation), up to 5 dm long, glabrous, becoming purplish with age; basal leaves numerous, prostrate, rosette-forming, 6-12 (18) cm long, pinnate, the sheathing base flattened, 12-18 mm long, 5-10 mm wide, becoming reddish-brown, the broad membranous margins extended into triangular apiculate stipules with herbaceous midribs 4-5 mm long, minutely ciliate, the rachis of the lowermost leaves diverging at nearly right angles above the stipules, bearing (5) 10-15 (20) pairs of subopposite leaflets occupying essentially the entire rachis, the uppermost pairs ±confluent to form a lobed terminal leaflet, the leaflets narrowly to broadly elliptic, 4-10 (20) mm long, 2-5 (10) mm wide, acute to obtuse, glaucous, sparsely ciliate apically (especially when young), otherwise glabrous, simple and entire to (especially middle leaflets) divided into 2 or 3 lobes, plane of the leaflets nearly perpendicular to the rachis in living material, the primary lobes diverging at ca 800 from the vertical, the secondary lobes diverging at ca 400, forming four ranks that are particularly distinct in developing leaves; stem leaves similar to basal leaves but smaller, with fewer pairs of leaflets, these simple or divided, almost sheathless, the stipules wholly herbaceous, distinctly veined, ciliate; inflorescence cymose, sometimes appearing racemose due to suppressed development of one branch; pedicels diverging at 35-45?, in fruit 1-4 cm long, becoming somewhat flexuose, glabrous or with scattered appressed hairs, especially distally; flowers 5-merous, occasionally 4-merous with one bractlet bifid and broader than the other 3; hypanthium bowl-shaped, 2-2.8 mm across in flower, enlarging in fruit, sparsely hairy and faintly 1 0-nerved externally, internally beset with stiff white hairs arising from the base, the inside rim ringed with an annular thickening that bears the anthers; bractlets lanceolate to ovate, 1.8-2.1 mm long, 0.6-1 mm wide, about half as long as the sepals, sparsely hairy apically, purple-tipped becoming purple overall in fruit; sepals lanceolate to narrowly ovate, 3.1-4.2 mm long in flower, elongating to 5.5 mm in fruit, 1.4-2.2 mm wide, green with purple tips abaxially, yellowish adaxially, sparsely hairy on both sides, the proximal margins hyaline; petals bright yellow, obovate, shallowly notched at the tip, 4.8-6.3 mm long, 2.6-3.8 mm wide, not persistent; stamens 15-20 in 3 or 4 cycles of 5, the antisepalous ones longest with filaments 2.5-3 mm long, arising from the underside of the hypanthium ring, oriented inwardly toward the styles at anthesis, the antipetalous ones shortest with filaments 1.5-2 mm long, some or all often absent, arising and oriented as above, the parapetalous ones of intermediate length with filaments 2-2.5 mm long, arising from the top of the hypan- thium ring, oriented outwardly at anthesis; anthers yellow, ovoid-ellipsoid, ca 1 mm long; ovules 3-10; styles filiform, 1.9-2.6 mm long, tipped with a small capitate stigma; achenes 2-10, pale brown and lightly rugose at maturity, obliquely ovoid in lateral view, 1.8-2.1 mm long, 1.2-1.6 mm wide, attached below the middle, the style scar subterminal, 0.2-0.3 mm below the apex.

description: Low, perennial, mat-forming herb from a well developed, much-branched cau- dex clothed in old dark brown petiole bases and stipules; vestiture villous to glabrescent with non-glandular hairs and finely puberulent with sessile or short- stalked glandular hairs; flowering stems few to several, decumbent in flower, spreading to often prostrate in fruit, 0.5-1.3 (1.7) dm long; leaves mostly basal, ternate, the petiole 1.4-5.5 (7) cm long, the leaflets (3) 5-12 mm long, obovate, rhomboid, or flabellate, cuneate at base, pinnately veined and lobed, the lobes ovate, acute, (3) 5-7 (9) teeth on the terminal leaflet and 3-5 on the smaller, oblique lateral pair, the midvein somewhat prominent beneath and impressed above, the cauline leaves 1 or 2, reduced, the stipules ovate, acute or obtuse; inflorescence 1- or 2-flowered or on robust plants loosely 3- or 4-flowered, the pedicels ascending, 7-23 mm long, the flowers 5 (4)-merous; hypanthium shallowly cupulate; bractlets 1.3-1.9 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, rounded or obtuse, entire or bifid, sometimes deeply cleft or paired; sepals 2.4-3.2 mm long, ovate or deltoid-lanceolate, acute, spreading at anthesis; petals (2) 3-4 mm long, obovate, rounded, truncate, or retuse apically, yellow fading whitish; stamens 15, yellow, the anthers 0.3-0.4 mm long, often wider than long; pistils few on a club- or dome-shaped receptacle, the style 0.9-1.2 mm long, glandular-thickened at the base, subterminally attached; achenes 1. 1-1.3 mm long, smooth.

description: Grayish hairy perennial herb from a few- branched caudex sheathed with old leaf bases, surmounting a thick taproot. Stems +/-  prostrate-decumbent, ca. 4-17 cm long, ca. 2-3 times leaf length, with abundant short crisped hairs. Leaves primarily basal, +/- pinnately compound with 2-4 +/- overlapping pairs of lateral leaflets, ca. 2-6 cm long; sheathing bases dark brown, generally glabrous; stipules +/-  triangular, brown, papery, sparsely hairy at tip; petiole ca. 1/4_1/3 of leaf length, 0.5-2.5 cm long; terminal leaflet largest, 5-25 mm long, +/ - oblanceolate, pinnately toothed ca. 1/4 to base with 3 or 4 pairs of teeth; lateral leaflets often cleft to base into 2 segments, these varying from simple to pinnately toothed; leaflet vestiture bicolored, upper side green with appressed, stiff, often +/- yellowish hairs, lower side densely white-tomentose, strigose along veins. Inflorescence cymose, not leafy; pedicels slender, 0.2-0.5 mm thick, generally 1-2.5(3) cm long, becoming +/- recurved, with short crisped hairs. Flowers up to ca. 15 per stem; hypanthium bowl-shaped, 2.5  5 mm wide (pressed); bractlets +/- ovate, 1.8- 3 mm long; sepals +/-iangular, ca. 3-5 mm long, with short crisped hairs, often becoming reddish tinged; petals bright yellow with orangish spot at base, broadly obovate with shallow notch at apex, 4-6 mm long; stamens 20; filaments 1-2 mm long; anthers 0.5-1 mm long; styles ca. 15-20, +/-  1.5-2 mm long. Achenes 1.6-1.8 mm long, pale brown with slight ridges.

description: Shrub or tree 1-8 m., rarely up to 12 m. high; bark red-brown, the younger often covered with a thin white epidermis, the older deeply furrowed and rough with persistent scales; branches thick and tortuous; the young branchlets reddish and pubescent, later becoming white and glabrous, rough with leaf scars;. leaves 0.5-3.0 cm. long, lanceolate, narrowly lanceolate, or linear, coriaceous and often resinous, the young often tomentose, later usually becoming glabrous and shining above, tomentulose to pale- or rusty-tomentose beneath, midrib prominent, lateral veins obscure, margin entire, revolute; petiole 0-5 mm. long, often narrowly winged, villous or glabrate; stipules brown, acute, scarious, deciduous, less than 2 mm. long; flowers solitary or geminate, axillary; floral tube in flower 3-6 mm. long, white-woolly, sessile; calyx-limb 2-6 mm. wide, turbinate, woolly without, the sepals triangular, woolly; stamens 10-25, the anthers glabrous, exserted; floral tube in fruit 3-10 mm. long, brown, with short white wool, sessile; tail of achene stout, 1-7 cm. long, silky-plumose, twisted and curved; flowering time April to June.
