description: Erect evergreen shrubs and small trees, 2-8 m tall, with stiff, sharp branches, the elongating, young branches reddish, finely villous or tomentose with crinkly white hairs, the older branches ashy-gray; leaves 1-3 (4) cm long, 1.5-8 (10) mm wide, lance-elliptic, narrowly (ob)lanceolate, or linear, cuneate basally, acute apically and often apiculate, entire and revolute-margined, coriaceous, dark resinous green and sparsely lanate on young leaves above and moderately to densely white-pubescent beneath, the midrib prominent, the petiole 1-6 mm long, the stipules brown, with a thick midvein and membranous margins, longest on the nonfas- cicled leaves of elongating branches where 3-7.5 mm; flowers subsessile; hypanthium tube persistent, 2.5-13 mm long, densely lanate with curly hairs, the deciduous, expanded rim (hypanthium cup) 1.5-3 mm high, broadly campanulate, reddish; sepals (0.9) 1.2-2.4 mm long, broadly triangular, rounded, recurved, woolly-pubescent, especially at the apex; stamens 15-25, the anthers 0.6-1.3 mm long, glabrous; achene 7-9 mm long, the mature style 4-10 cm long, bent or spirally coiled, plumose; 2n = 16.

description: Branchlets usually glabrous except at extreme base where about one plant in ten is minutely puberulent (in the southeastern United States occasional plants are uniformly hirsutulous on the young growth); petioles and leaves usually gla- brous except for the tufts or fringes along the midrib on the lower surface. Foliage leaves mostly about 4 cm. wide and 9 cm. long, 2-2.5 times as long as wide; individual leaves much smaller, or up to about 7 cm. wide and 15 cm. long; l/w ratio varying from 1.7 to 2.4 or from 2.5 to 3.5 (rarely 2.3 to 4.0) on the same plant, the variation in the population as a whole thus appearing to be on the order of twice that in most individuals; petioles mostly 0.8-2 cm. long, averaging 1.5 cm.; blades with 3-10 (usually 5-7) teeth per cm. of margin, the variation in any individual usually not more than 1-2 teeth per cm., this caused by the occasional occurrence of small intermediate teeth. Second floral leaf mostly about 2 cm. wide and 4 cm. long, and l/w ratio about 2.1, but varying in individual plants from 1.6 to 3; petioles averaging 1.1 cm. long (0.4-1.7 cm.); blades with 4-20 (usually 7-9) teeth per cm. of margin; teeth of floral leaves often 1-2 more per cm. (occasionally 5-6 more) than in the foliage leaves of the same plant, especially before maturity of the foliage. Flowering branch averaging about 12 cm. long (6-21 cm. in specimens noted, the length rarely exceeding 15 cm.); flowers usually about 35 (greatest number observed, 93); pedicels about 4.5 mm. long in flower, 6 mm. long in fruit (4-10 mm. in individual plants); calyx-lobes 1-1.5 mm. long (usually about 1.3 mm.); petals mostly 2.5-3.5 mm. long and wide; longer filaments up to-4 mm. long; anthers averaging about 0.6 mm. long; style averaging about 1.6 mm. long (1.2-2.2 mm.); fruit about 1 cm. across. Woodlands, thickets, roadsides and fence-rows, from sea-level to mountain- summits at elevations of 1800-2000 m., a common tree in the Deciduous Forest region of eastern North America, from Nova Scotia and New Brunswick to Florida (about to the latitude of Tampa Bay), and west to the north shore of Lake Su- perior, Minnesota, South Dakota [North Dakota, according to Fernald in Gray's Man. Bot. ed. 8 (1950), but this report not verified by me], eastern Nebraska, eastern Kansas, eastern Oklahoma and eastern Texas. A constituent of the original forest, but now often a weed-tree in second-growth areas and a characteristic plant of road-sides.

description: Branchlets uniformly hirsutulous, the rufous hairs extending in densely pubescent plants to the inflorescence axis, the pedicels and the hypanthia; petioles usually hirsutulous on all sides, the hairs extending sparsely up the sunken midvein on the upper surface of the blade; lower surface of the blade rather generally pubescent with similar hairs, even in otherwise glabrous plants, the hairs mostly confined to the veinlets and the larger veins; midvein pubescent uniformly on all sides near base, lacking the conspicuous tufts or fringes found in the other subspecies of P. serotina. Foliage leaves strongly whitened beneath, little or not at all drooping, prevailingly obovate, or elliptic-obovate, often blunt-tipped, without acumen except on shoot-leaves, averaging about 4.5 cm. wide and 8.5 cm. long (in the approximately 35 collections studied), mostly less than twice as long as wide (l/w ratio varying from about 1.5 to 2.75, the latter in shoot-leaves); petioles mostly 0.7-1 cm. long, (0.5-1.6 cm., but those longer than 1 cm. rare even on shoots); blades with 4-11 (usually 6) teeth per cm. of margin. Second floral leaf averaging about 2.7 cm. wide and 4.8 cm. long, the I/w ratio about 1.6-1.7 (varying from 1.3 to 2.5 but rarely exceeding 2); petioles averaging about 0.75 cm. long (0.4-1.3 cm.); blades with 5-9 (usually about 7) teeth per cm. of margin. Flowering branch averaging about 15-16 cm. long (9-23 cm. as noted); flowers averaging about 45 in number (30-70); pedicels 2.5-5(-7) mm. long in flower, 4.5-7(-10) mm. long in fruit; calyx lobes 1-1.5 mm. long; petals 3-3.5 mm. long (data from 4 specimens); longer filaments 2.5-3 mm. long (data from 8 specimens); anthers 0.6-0.7 mm. long (data from 6 specimens); style 1.4-1.8 mm. long (data from 4 specimens); fruit about 1 cm. across, said to be red.

description: Frutex 1-4 m altus; folia geminata laminis ovatis vel ovato- ellipticis, margine sinuatis vel 1-2-lobatis. Inflorescentiae brevipedunculatae, 10-16-florae; pedicellus et calyx extus pilis glandularibus minutis; calyx cupuliformis deis; corolla pentamera, lobis tubum aequantibus, extra intraque puberulis, margine involuto, apice cucullato. menta staminalia in tertio basali tubi corollini inserta, partibus liberis et faucis pariete tomentosis; antherae apiculatae. Ovarium late ovatum, stylo clavato, stamina non superanti. Semina ad maturitatem alata.

description: Shrubs 1-4 m tall; stems 4-angled, branches geniculate; foliage and inflorescences covered with uniseriate multicelular-trichomes 0.42- 0.75 mm long. Leaves geminate, membranaceous, ovate to ovate-elliptic, the base rounded, slightly asymmetric, the apex acute to acuminate, the margins sinuate or with 1-2 deltoid lobes on each side; large leaves with petioles 2.5-7 cm, lamina 9-23 x 5.5-11 cm, the small leaves with petioles 1.3-3.5 cm, lamina 5-12x3.5-8 cm. Inflorescences 10-16 flowered; rachis 3-8 mm; pedicels 15-28 mm; calyx tube 2.2-3.8 mm long, 3.7-4.5 mm wide, 5-lobed, lobes deltoid, 0.5-2.2 mm long, 0.8-2.3 mm wide, pedicel and calyces with tiny trichomes of three uniseriate cells; corollas 5-lobate, tubular-urceolate, whitish-cream, greenish-purple towards base, the tube 7-8.5 mm long, 3.5-4.2 mm wide, the lobes oblong, 4.5-6.5 mm long, 2.5-3 mm wide, with involute margins and cucullate apex, abaxial and adaxial surfaces puberulent with uniseriate multicelular-trichomes 0.12-0.2 mm long, the adaxial surfaces of lobes with purple stains at their bases; filaments basally adnate to the corolla tube, the free portion of filaments 1.8- 2.1 mm long, tomentose, with uniseriate multi- celular-trichomes 0.48-0.73 mm long; anthers oblong, 2.7-3 x 1-1.3 mm, surpassing of the tube by less than a third of their length, apiculate, the apiculum 0.4-0.7 mm long; ovary ovoid, 1.1- 1.4 x 1.3-1.6 mm; style clavate, 5-5.8 mm long, not surpassing the stamens. Fruits spherical, 5- 8.5 mm diameter, glabrous; calyx accrescent 3.5-4.5 x 5.8-7.8 mm, covering 35-45% of the fruit; seeds ca. 80, idioblasts 6-10 per fruit. Seeds lenticular, 1.3-1.6 mm diameter, 0.5-0.7 mm thick, surfaces reticulate, edge winged.

description: Herba vel frutex, 1-7 m altus. Inflorescentia axillaris, 1-2-flora, pedicellis per anthesin 20-25 mm longis, fructiferis 24-45 mm longis; calyx cupulatus, 2.5 mm longus, appendicibus 5, per anthesin 0.8-1.8 mm longis, plerumque 5 appendicibus interpositis brevioribus; corolla angusti-campanulata, 10.5-13 x 4-6 mm, lobis 3 x 2 mm, flava; filamenta 4.5 mm longa; antherae 2-2.1 mm longae. Fructus globosus, 9-11 mm diam., vivide ruber, sapore pungenti; semina 5-17, reniformia, 3.8-4.2 x 3.2 mm.

description: Herb, shrub or treelet, 1-7 m tall; stems glabrous or sparsely pubescent with simple hairs. Sympodial units difoliate and geminate. Leaves 2-13 x 0.8-4.2 cm, more or less uniform in size and shape, lanceolate, glabrous adaxially and abaxially or sparsely pubescent abaxially along the midrib with simple hairs 0.3 mm long; base acute to attenuate and somewhat oblique; margin slightly revolute; apex attenuate; petioles 2-8 mm. Inflorescences axillary, 1-2-flowered; pedicels 20-25 mm in flower, 24-45 mm in fruit, terete, pendulous, slender, 0.6 mm wide at base, 1.4-1.8 mm wide distally, glabrous. Calyx cupulate, 2.5 mm long, the margin truncate, with 5 appendages 0.8-1.8 mm long in flower and with 5 intermediate, slightly shorter ones alternating with these, the appendages (1-) 3-5 mm long in fruit, sparsely pubescent with simple hairs; corolla 4-6 mm in diameter, 10.5-13 mm long, narrowly campanulate, lemon yellow, shallowly 5-lobed, the tube 3-6 mm, the lobes ca. 3 x 2 mm, narrowly triangular, acute at apices, glabrous abaxially, papillose at tips of lobes; stamens included; filaments 4.5 mm, attached ca. 1 mm above base of corolla tube, broadened at base, but without two flaps of tissue on corolla tube above site of insertion; anthers 2-2.1 x 0.8-0.9 mm, oblong, yellow, longitudinally dehiscent; ovary glabrous; style ca. 6 x 0.25 mm, cylindrical to clavate, glabrous; stigma truncate to capitate. Fruit a globose berry, 9-11 mm in diameter, pendent, glabrous, bright red, pungent (or apparently sometimes not); seeds 5-17, 3.8-4.2 x 3.2 mm, reniform, flattened, pale yellow, the surface loosely foveolate.

description: Frutex ad 1.5 m altus. Folia geminata, 5.5-22.5 x 2-6.5 cm, fere glabra. Fructus baccatus, coccineus, 1 cm diametro.

description: Shrub 1.5 m. tall; young stems minutely puberulent with antrorsely curved simple hairs, older stems nearly glabrous. Sympodial units difoliate and geminate. Leaves 2-22.5 x 0.6-6.5 cm, dimorphic, the minor leaves similar to the majors but about 1/3 the size, elliptic to oblanceolate, nearly glabrous adaxially and abaxially, with minute appressed hairs 0.2-0.3 mm long, mostly along the margin; base attenuate and often oblique; margin slightly revolute; apex long-attenuate; petioles to 3 cm on the largest leaves, mostly less than 8 mm in the flowering portion. Inflorescences axillary to the major leaf, evidently 6-9-flowered from the prominent corky pedicel scars, only 1-4 fruits forming per node; pedicels ca. 9 mm in flower, 19-23 mm in fruit, conspicuously ribbed and winged, erect, 1 mm in diameter at base, gradually ampliate distally to 2.2 mm in diameter, minutely puberulent. Calyx cyathiform, 5-5.5 mm long, the margin truncate to undulate, with 5 incurved appendages 2-2.5 mm long in flower and fruit, these somewhat flattened laterally, glabrous; corolla ca. 0.5 cm in diameter, ca. 6 mm long, broadly campanulate to subrotate, yellow with darker green spots within, deeply 5-lobed, the tube ca. 3 mm, the lobes 3.5 x 1.5 mm, deltate, acute at apices, glabrous except for the papillose infolded margin; stamens included; filaments ca. 1 mm, inserted low within the calyx tube and apparently without two flaps of tissue on corolla tube above site of insertion; anthers ca. 1.8 x 1.5 mm, ovate, the color unknown, longitudinally dehiscent; gynoecium structure not known with certainty. Fruit a globose berry, ca. 1 cm in diameter, erect, glabrous, bright red, juicy; seeds unknown.

description: Frutex erectus 1.5 m altus; caulibus sparse villosis, deorsum glabratis; petiolis ad 3.5 cm longis; laminis ovato-lanceolatis vel ovatis, attenuatis, ad 8.0 cm longis, 6.3 cm latis, sparse ad dense villosis vel tomentosis; pedunculis erectis geminatis vel ternatis, 1.2 cm longis; calyce ca. 1.5 mm alto, dentibus 5 linearilanceolatis, 1 mm longis praedito; corolla rotata, 1.2-1.5 cm lata, lobis violaceis vel violaceo-marginatis, maculis flavescentibus; filamentis tenuibus 2 mm longis, albis; antheris flavis. 1.5 mm longis; baccis rubris, subovoideis, 1 cm longis, 7 mm latis; seminibus pallidis flavescentibus.

description: Plantae usque ad 1 m altae, perennes, suffrutescentes. Caules diffusi vel scandentes, sympodialiter ramosi. Folia decidua, alterna, ovato-lanceolata (juniora trullata), 3.5-8.2 X 1.5-3.8 cm, venatione pinnata (brochidodroma), lamina supra glabra vel sparsim pubescente infra sparsim pubescente etsi villosa in venarum axillis, apice acuminata vel attenuata, margine integra trichomatibus strigillosis uniseriatis instructa, basi attenuata, petiolo parum canaliculato 1-3 cm longo. Inflorescentia axillaris e dichasiis compositis constata. Flores de facto uni- vel bisexuales, actinomorphi; calycis tubus calathiiformis, 1.3-1.9 X 1.8-2.6 mm, membranaceus inter lobis, dentibus 5 variabilibus 0-1.3 mm longis glabris vel puberulis; corolla purpurea cremeaque vel cremea, punctis viridibus duo basi cujusque lobi maculata, campanulata, 4.4-8.5 mm lata, lobis cum vel sine unguibus apicalibus, marginibus loborum varie papillatis; stamina 5 epipetala, lobis corollae altema, antherarum sacculis (thecis) parallelis extrorsis dorsifixis; ovarium bicarpellatum, 0.9-2.6 X 0.9-1.5 mm; stylus apicalis, hetero- morphus, 1.5-7.6 mm; stigma clavatum bilobum vel quadrilobum; ovula 4-8 in quoque ovario, anatropa. Fructus bacca gustu pungens rubra globosa 4.4-7.6 X 4.2-7.3 mm, pedicello 1-2 cm longo. Semina 3.5-4.5 mm longa, cremea, striata vel reticulata, minute tuberculata, auriformia. (n = 12). Florescentiae mense Maio.

description: Plants to 1 m tall, perennial. Suffrutescent, stems diffuse or clambering, sym- podially branched. Leaves deciduous, alternate, ovate-lanceolate (trullate when young), 3.5-8.2 X 1.5-3.8 cm, venation pinnate (brochidodromous), blade gla- brous to sparsely pubescent above, sparsely pubescent below, villous in axils of veins beneath, apex acuminate to attenuate, margins entire, with uniseriate strig- illose trichomes, base attenuate; petiole slightly channeled, 1-3 cm long. Inflo- rescence composed of axillary compound dichasia. Flowers functionally unisexual or bisexual, actinomorphic; calyx tube cup-like, 1.3-1.9 X 1.8-2.6 mm, mem- branous between lobes, teeth 5, variable, 0-1.3 mm long, glabrous to puberulent; corolla purple and cream or cream, marked with 2 green spots at base of each lobe, campanulate, 4.4-8.5 mm broad, lobes with or without an apical claw, margins of lobes variously papillate. Stamens 5, epipetalous, alternating with the corolla lobes, anther sacs (thecae) parallel, extrorse, dorsifixed; ovary bicarpellate, 0.9-2.6 X 0.9-1.5 mm; style apical, heteromorphic, 1.5-7.6 mm long, stigma clavate or 2-4 lobed; ovules 4-8 per ovary, anatropous. Fruit a pungent red globose berry, 4.4-7.6 X 4.2-7.3 mm, pedicel 1-2 cm long. Seeds 3.5-4.5 mm long, cream colored, striate to reticulate, minutely tuberculate, auriform. (n = 12). Flowering in May.

description: Cestro mizicrocalyci Francey similis sed his notulis diversa: ramorum foliorum pubes dendritica; folia bullata, venis supra impressis, subtus elevatis; corolla longior; filamenta per 4-5 mm libera, basi geniculatotumida; calyx fructusque majores.
bibliographicCitation: Benítez de Rojas, Carmen E. & Sawyer, N. W. 1999. A new species of Cestrum (Solanaceae) from the Cordillera de Mérida, Venezuela. Brittonia. 51: 163-165.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 6-8 m tall, branched, the branches slender and lax, somewhat angular when young, terete when mature, pubescent with dark, dendritic trichomes; petioles 1.2-2 cm long, covered with dendritic trichomes; leaves firmly chartaceous, undulate, 9-15 X 2.5-4.5 cm, narrowly elliptic, glabrous except for dendritic trichomes 0.7-1.5 mm across with branches 0.3-0.9 mm long on the veins and the surface beneath, the secondary veins 6-9 on each side, extending to the margin, there looping and uniting, appressed above, elevated beneath, the apex abruptly acuminate, the base cuneate; minor leaves lacking. Inflorescence a lax, axillary, pedunculate panicle, 5-10 cm; peduncle 1.5-3.5 cm; bracts 1.5 mm, linear. Flowers sessile; calyx drying dark brown, tubular, 3.5-4.5 X ca. 3.5 mm, externally glabrous, apical half pubescent within, lobes 5, 1 X 1 mm; corolla green, purplish toward the apex, 14.5-17 mm long; tube 12-14.5 mm, gradually expanded apically, the throat 2-4 mm diam.; lobes 5, 2.5-3 mm long, ovate, the apex acute, the margin short pilose; stamens ca. 13 mm; filaments adnate for 8-9 mm, the adnate portion pubescent, the free portion immediately above the point of insertion distended and geniculate; anthers ovate, 1-1.5 mm diam.; ovary 1 mm diam., glabrous; ovules 6-8; style ca. 15 mm long, stigma bilobed. Fruit a subglobose, dark purple berry 6-6.5 X 6-7 mm, the pericarp thin, seeds 2-3, 5-6 mm long, light brown.

description: Deprea bitterianae affinis, a qua calyce fructifero fructui adpresso et lobis longis subulatis differt. Specierum Depreae calycibus fructiferis includentibus baccam arcte, Deprea nubicolas a qua longitude pedicelli, colore floris, et lobis longs subulatis differt.

description: Shrubs to 2 m. Stems flexuose, distal on the branches, pubescent, soon glabrescent. Leaves never geminate, pubescent, soon glabrescent, the young leaves pubescent with multicellular simple, non-glandular and glandular hairs 0.4-0.6 mm long, the blades somewhat fleshy, elliptic, 2.8-6 x 1-1.8 cm, the base oblique, cuneate, the apex acute-attenuate, glabrescent along margins and veins above and below; petioles 0.3-1 cm long. Inflorescence with a free, puberulent peduncle on puberulent pedicels 12-20 mm long. Calyx in anthesis green, puberulent, 2-4 mm long, ca. 3 mm in diameter, the lobes triangular, somewhat subulate, 0.3-1.1 mm long. Corolla purple above the calyx, infundibular, membranous, 13-25 mm long, puberulent externally and with sessile glands, puberulent internally with 0-2 non-glandular hairs per mm2, the tube 10-20mm long, the lobes of the limb triangular, slightly flared in anthesis, 1.8-2.5 mm wide at the base, 3-5 mm long. Filaments 15-20 mm long, glabrous, adnate to the basal third of the corolla tube for ca. 3 mm, broadening gradually in width basipetally where adnate to the corolla below; anthers included to slightly exserted, purplish, ovate-elliptic, minutely apiculate, the bases of thecae connivent, 1.7-2 x ca. 1.5 mm; pollen sacs lacking calcium oxalate crystals. Ovary conical, ca. 1 x 1.2mm; style reddish purple, 14-18 mm long, elongating in anthesis to bring the stigma level with the anthers; stigma sub-bilobate. Fruiting pedicels 2-2.5 cm long, pu-berulent. Fruiting calyx green, urceolate, 7-8 x 5-7 mm, tightly investing the fruit, glabres- cent externally, with sessile glands internally; lobes strongly subulate, of unequal lengths, 0.8-1.7 mm long. Berry color unknown, globose, 4.8-7.2 mm in diameter, containing seeds 3.2-3.6 mm in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Sawyer, Neil W. 2007. Deprea nubicola (Solanaceae), a new species from northern Colombia. Brittonia. 59 (1): 54-56.

description: Suffrutescent to small shrub, to 1.2 m. Young branches, leaves and the abaxial face of the corolla and calyx covered with multicellular, erect finger hairs (sometimes gland-tipped, uniseriate but sometimes branched on calyx). Leaves single or paired, lanceolate with the apex acuminate, to ovate with the apex obtuse, entire to sinuate-cre- nate, to 9.5 cm long by 5.5 cm wide but usually somewhat smaller. Inflorescence 4- 7(-10) flowered, rarely branched. Corolla with a short tube (5 mm, evident only on some herbarium specimens) and reflexed limb (Fig. 1D) 2 cm diam., center dark violet to blue, paler peripherally. Filaments densely villous proximally with uniseriate finger hairs, glabrous distally (Fig. 1 D). An- thers 1.3-2 mm long, dark. Style twice as long as stamens. Description based on the herbarium specimens cited below. See Bit- ter (1921) and Macbride (1962) for other descriptions, in Latin and English, respectively.
bibliographicCitation: Mione, T., et al. 1993. Jaltomata I: Circumscription, description, and new combinations for five South American species (Solaneae, Solanaceae). Brittonia. 45: 138-145.

description: Shrub to 1 m. Axes and abaxial face of calyx bearing both gland-tipped finger hairs and shorter, non-glandular dendritic hairs interspersed among each other. Leaf blades typically entire, ovate, the apex acute, less than 11 cm long and 8 cm wide. Inflorescence 4-9 flowered. Peduncle 4.5-11 mm long. Pedicel 6-9 mm long, with dense glandtipped finger hairs. Lobes of calyx and corolla triangular to narrowly triangular. Flowering clayx 8-9 mm diam., lobe radius 4-5 mm long, sinus radius 2 mm long. Corolla tubular with a broad limb. Corolla tube 6.5-8 mm long, partially to nearly com- pletely filled with red nectar on living material. Corolla limb rotate to campanulate, cream or pale-green, 14-23 mm diam., re- maining open at night. Stamens (including expanded base) 9.2-10.9 mm long, exserted from corolla up to 7 mm. Filaments, slender part with a few to several finger trichomes to 0.5 mm long on basal 1/4_1/3 of the length. Anthers undehisced 1.9-2.1 mm long x 1.4- 1.5 mm wide, dehisced 1.2-1.3 mm long. Style 8-13.3 mm long. Stigma exserted beyond anthers up to 8 mm but sometimes not exserted, overhead dimensions 0.46- 0.56 mm by 0.4-0.46 mm, often protruding through the otherwise closed corolla prior to anthesis. Ovules 70-78 per ovary. Fruiting calyx-lobe radius 6-8 mm. Mature berry orange in greenhouse. Seed (field collected) 1.36-1.48 mm long. Chromosome number 2n = 24 (Diers, 1961), n = 12 (this study, meiosis of anthers from plants from seeds of Chavez s. n.). Description based on living plants of Chavez s. n., provided by R. Cha- vez and T. Davis IV. See Bitter (1924) and Macbride (1962) for other descriptions, in Latin and English, respectively.
bibliographicCitation: Mione, T., et al. 1993. Jaltomata I: Circumscription, description, and new combinations for five South American species (Solaneae, Solanaceae). Brittonia. 45: 138-145.

description: Erect shrub to 1 m high, glabrate. Leaves ovate, acute, blade to 6.5 cm long by 4.5 cm wide, entire or less commonly sinuate- dentate or toothed with no more than 3 teeth per margin, the upper surface bright green. Inflorescence usually 1-2(-4) flowered (sometimes branched on cultivated plants from seed of Leiva 138 but not mentioned in the original publication nor shown in the lectotype). Peduncle 4-9 mm long, green, terete. Pedicel 7-16 mm long, always longer than peduncle to which it is attached, green terete. Flowers nodding from 450 below horizontal to pendent. Flower buds triangular when viewed perpendicular to bud's length. Flowering calyx shiny green abaxially, 18- 22 mm diam., lobe radius 9.5-10 mm, sinus radius 3-5 mm. Corolla, tube urceolate, limb completely and outwardly retrorse and 10- lobed, 8-10 mm long, 12-14.5 mm diam., whitish to pale yellow, remaining open at night. Base of the flower filling with orange red nectar that is visible through the corolla. Stamens (not including expanded base) 14- 15 mm long, exserted beyond corolla 7-9 mm. Filaments, slender part pubescent on basal half, the hairs purple, branched with up to 4 termini, the hairs to 0.7 mm long. Anthers, undehisced 2.6-3.0 mm long x 2.0- 2.2 mm wide, dehisced 2-2.3 mm long. Style 13.8-15.7 mm long. Stigma exserted beyond anthers to 5 mm. Ovules 118-181 (n = 3 ovaries) per ovary. Mature berries red according to collector, orange in green house. Description based on living plants of Leiva 138 (provided by S. Leiva, A. Sa- gastegui A. and M. 0. Dillon). Chromosome number n = 12 (this study, meiosis of anthers from plants from seeds of Leiva 138). See Macbride (1962) and Baker (l.c.) for other English descriptions.
bibliographicCitation: Mione, T., et al. 1993. Jaltomata I: Circumscription, description, and new combinations for five South American species (Solaneae, Solanaceae). Brittonia. 45: 138-145.

description: Herb to shrub, to 2 m high, sometimes scandent. Leaves and young axes velutinous to less commonly puberulent with multicellular, uniseriate, unbranched finger hairs, sometimes to mostly gland-tipped. Leaves entire to toothed, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, the apex acuminate. Inflorescence (1-)2(-4) flowered. Corolla tubular, the tube (1-)2 cm long, pale green, less commonly white or pale yellow, the five larger lobes alternate with five smaller lobules, all flaring. Anthers 1.7-2.2 mm long. Stigma and anthers some- times differing in height by up to 5 mm, either may be exserted. Mature berries or- ange ("reddish" on Fosberg 20426), broader than high (oblate spheroid) and transversely oblate, 13-19 mm diam., 10-12 mm high (Mione 458-460). Chromosome number n = 12 (Heiser, 1963). Description based on numerous herbarium and field-collected specimens from throughout the range of the species.
bibliographicCitation: Mione, T., et al. 1993. Jaltomata I: Circumscription, description, and new combinations for five South American species (Solaneae, Solanaceae). Brittonia. 45: 138-145.

description: Herbae perennes vel suffrutices; folia ovata vel obovata trichomatibus simplicibus uniseriatis glanduliferis dense pubescentia; inflorescentiae axillares triflorae dense pubescentes; calycis lobi trichomatibus simplicibus uniseriatis glanduliferis pubescentes; corolla caerulea, lobis ad marginem trichomatibus minute dendriticis pubescentibus; filamenta prope basin pubescentia; bacca aurantiaca 5-8 mm diametro.
bibliographicCitation: Knapp, Sandra, et al. 1991. A New Species of Jaltomata (Solanaceae) from Northwestern Peru. Brittonia. 43 (3): 181-184.

description: Plants herbaceous to suffruticose. Stems terete, hollow, densely velutinous, the trichomes of 2 types, the majority 0.25-0.4 mm long, 2-3-celled, gland- tipped, these forming a dense uniform covering, scattered and evenly distributed among these shorter trichomes are 2-3 mm long, gland-tipped trichomes. Sympodia difoliate, geminate on reproductive nodes. Leaves ovate to obovate, 3.5-6.5 cm long, 2.5-4 cm wide, with 3 or 4 pairs of primary veins, the lamina adaxially and abaxially pubescent with erect, uniseriate, gland-tipped usually 3- celled trichomes 0.25-0.75 mm long, these denser along the veins, the margins of young leaves erose-sinuate, of older leaves erose-dentate, bearing uniseriate, multicellular trichomes 0.4-0.6 mm long, the apex acute to acuminate, the base truncate, somewhat winged onto the petiole; petiole 1.2-2.3 cm long, minutely and assymetrically winged. Inflorescence axillary, (I)-3-flowered, peduncle 3-6 mm long, pedicels 5-8 mm long, the entire inflorescence densely pubescent with simple, uniseriate, gland-tipped trichomes like those of the stems. Flowers with the calyx pentamerous, 1-1.4 cm in diam at anthesis, enlarging in fruit, the abaxial surface pubescent with simple, uniseriate, gland-tipped trichomes 0.5- 1 mm long, denser along the veins, the calyx lobe margins with some longer trichomes to 2 mm long; corolla blue, rotate-campanulate, glabrous adaxially, sparsely papillate abaxially, the papillae denser along the veins, the margins of the lobes with multicellular, dendritic, non-glandular trichomes 0.1-0.3 mm long: stamens 5, anthers 1.4-1.5 mm long, dehiscing by longitudinal slits, the filaments ca 1 mm long in the pistillate phase, 9-9.5 mm long in the hermaphroditic phase, pubescent with simple, uniseriate, multicellular trichomes 0.5- 1.5 mm long in the distal 1/3, inserted on the ventral face of the anther; ovary glabrous, bicarpellate with numerous ovules, with a nectariferous disk; style ca 1 cm long, glabrous, the stigma capitate, bilobed, exserted beyond the anthers. Fruit a globose, many-seeded, orange berry, 5-8 mm in diam; fruiting calyx accrescent, 1.6-2.4 cm in diam, not completely enclosing the berry. Seeds ca 1 mm in diam, the surfaces minutely verrucose.
bibliographicCitation: Knapp, Sandra, et al. 1991. A New Species of Jaltomata (Solanaceae) from Northwestern Peru. Brittonia. 43 (3): 181-184.

description: Frutex epiphyticus ramulis crassis terminationibus floriferis ferrugineotomentellis demum glabratis. Folia alterna integra coriacea. Petiolus crassus 1-2 cm longus dense crasseque ferrugineo-tomentosus, pilis grandis patulis brachiato-ramosis. Lamina oblonga sublanceolato-elliptica apice acutiuscula basim versus attenuata obtuse cuneata margine integra leviter revoluta, 13-18 cm longa 5-7.5 cm lata; supra luteoloviridis statu juvenili leviter tomentella deinde glabrata tantum sparsissimis pilis brachiatis praedita, costa impressa nervis lateralibus laxum reticulum valde impressum formantibus superficie inter nervos subbullata; subtus costa crassa eminenti tomentoso-ferruginea reliqua lamina dilute ferrugineo-tomentella, nervis secundariis circa 10 utroque latere prominentibus aseendentibus marginem versus arcuatis anastomosatis nervis tertiis laxo reticulo prominenti, venulis minoribus inconspicuis. Infloreseentiae breves corymbosi subterminales in ramulis ultimis aphyllis fertilibus tomentellis cicatricosis saepe valde inerassatis instructae. Pedicelli 1-1.5 cm longi sursum sine sensu inerassati dense ferrugineo-tomentosi. Calyx cupulato-cuneatus carnoso-coriaceus usque ad medium vel denique usque ad basim 5-partitus, 1.6-2 cm longus; intus tomentellus pilis simplicibus vel fureatis, extus brunneus dense tomentosus pilis brachiato-ramosis; laciniis ovato-oblongis vel oblongis acutis 5-8 mm latis. Corolla carnosa eburnea tubulosa extus tomentosa intus ad insertionem staminorum pilosa reliqua glabra superne leviter ampliata 5-lobata, circa 2.6 cm longa 7 mm crassa, lobis reflexis ovato-oblongis 7-8 mm longis circa 5 mm latis. Stamina 5 filamentis 5 mm longis glabris complanatis ad dimidiam corollae insertis, antheris elliptic-o-oblongis (4 mm longis) birimosis glabris corollae tubum excedentibus. Discus perigynus crassus 1 mm altus sinuatus. Ovarium glabrum. Stylus tenuis glaber circa 18 mm longus apice bilobato-lamellatus. Fructus baccatus ovatus circa 1.2 cm diamitens. Semina reniforma compressa minute alveolata circa 4 mm longa 1.8 mm lata, embryone recto brevi.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1958. The Colombian species of Juanulloa. Brittonia. 40: 146-150.

description: Arbuscula ramulis pendulis minute pulverulenti-pubescentibus deinde glabratis. Folia chartacea alterna integerrima. Petiolus 5-14 mm longus breviter parceque pulverulens vel glaber. Lamina glabra ovato-oblonga vel oblongo-sublanceolata basi rotundata vel obtusa vel cuneata ad apicem attenuata acute acuminata, margine integra, 8-20 cm longa 4-7 cm lata; supra viridis sublaevis costa nervis secundariis paulo conspicuis reliquis obsoletis; subtus costa prominenti, nervis secundariis prominulis circa 6 utroque latere curvato-aseendentibus marginem versus anastomosatis ceteris nervulis fere inconspicuis. Inflorescentiae axillares brevissimae 3-4-floris corymbosis subumbellatis, axe crassiusculo 0.5-1.5 cm longo pulverulenti, bracteolis ovatis subacutis amplectentibus pulverulentibus 1.5-2 mm longis. Pedicelli 5-15 mm longi crassiusculi apicem versus magis inerassatis minute pulverulenti-tomentosi. Calyx crasse membranaceus badius vel ruber intus sparse minuteque puberulus extus minute tomentello-pulverulens usque ad basim 5-partitus laciniis oblongo-lanceolatis acutissimis 15-22 mm longis basi 2-5 mm latis. Corolla crassiuscula luteoochracea tubulosa circa 3.5 cm longa tubulo circa 8 mm longo 5 mm crasso limbo ampliato circa 8 mm diamitenti apice paulo constricto lobis ovalibus obtusis circa 2 mm longis reflexis; extus sparse puberula, intus ad insertionem staminoruLim barbata reliqua glabra. Stamina 0.7-1 cm supra basim in tubo corollae inserta filamentis crassiusculis 12-15 mm longis glabris, antheris basifixis circa 8 mm longis oblongo-lanceolatis basi subcordatis apice acutis, birimosis usque fere ad basim dehiseentibus. Discus epigynus crassus undulatus circa 1 mm altius. Ovarium glabrum. Stylus tener glaber apice bilobato-ampliatus. Bacca ovoidea circa 1.2 mm lata.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1958. The Colombian species of Juanulloa. Brittonia. 40: 146-150.

description: Ramusculi laminae foliorum petioli pedunculique glabri. Calyx corollaque glabri. Lamina foliorum magis oblonga basim versus angustata cuneata vel obtusa, nervis secundariis aseendentibus.

description: Erect to scandent shrub, to 2 m tall. Indument of grey, simple, one-to several-celled, glandular trichomes. Stems pale greenish brown and herbaceous when young, the older growth brown and distinctly woody; first branching point dichasial, the subsequent branching points uni- or dichasial; longest sympodia after first branching point (2.5-)4- 8(-10)cm long, 2-3.5(-4)mm in diam., pubescent to pilose with spreading trichomes (0.25-)0.5-1.5(-2.5) mm long, often glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, the upper and lower sides similar in color and texture, puberulent to pubescent with erect trichomes (0.1-)0.25-1(-2.5) mm long, the lamina widely ovate, elliptic, to obovate, the leaf venation brochidodromous, the tip acute to acuminate, the margin entire, the base truncate to abruptly attenuate, sometimes oblique, the petiole narrowly winged, the largest leaves with lamina (6-)8-14(-18.5) x 3-8.7 cm, the petiole (0.4-)1-4(- 5) cm long, the smaller geminate leaves with lamina 3-10 x 1.9-5.6cm, the petiole 0.2- 3 cm long. Inflorescence with (1-)2(-3) flowers; pedicels mostly erect, (0.5-)2-3.5(- 4.5) cm long, pubescent to pilose with spreading trichomes (0.1-)0.25-2(-2.5) mm long, the pedicel scars simple and not distinctive; calyx widely urceolate to crateriform, 3-7.5mm long, (3-)4-7.5(-11)mm in diam., glabrous except for the puberulent to pilose base with hairs as on the pedicel, the calyx rim undulate, the teeth subtending the rim reduced to (5-)9-10 oval protuberances 0.25-1 mm in diam.; corolla rotate to slightly campanulate, 1.4-2.5 cm in diam., pale lilac to blue purple with darker purple on adaxial side of lobes, the lobes (0.5-)0.8-1.25(-2) mm long, glabrous, open in very early morning, closing by mid-morning; androecium with glabrous, straight filaments, these unequal with four short and one long, the short 1-4 mm long, the long 3-7 mm long; anthers elliptic, 3-3.5 mm long, the base cordate, the pores apical, ovate; gynoecium with ovary globose, glabrous, 2-2.7 mm long, the style erect with slight curve near apex, 6-10 mm long, the stigma round, slightly bilobed. Fruit ovoid, 0.7-2 cm long, 0.5-1.2 cm in diam., green when immature, red when mature, glabrous, the seeds 90-200 per fruit, flattened, depressed-obovate to reniform, 0.8-1.7 x 0.6-1.5 mm, tannish orange to darker reddish brown in color, the surface uniformly pitted and ridged.

description: Frutex 2 m. altus. description: Shrub 2 m. tall with slender, flexuous branches, irregularly dentate leaves, and 3-4-fowered infloreseences. description: Perennial herb, plants the most robust in the genus, 20-40 cm tall, to 1 m wide. Stem thick, almost straight, to 5 mm diam.; main stem erect to ascending; lateral stems developing from the base of the main stem, ascending; each stem almost always divided into 2 branches at the node bearing the first flower, densely glandular-pilose; hairs contorted, ca. 1 mm long, white; internodes 20-45(-75) mm long. Leaves attenuate to cuneate at base, acute to obtuse at apex; lower leaves oblong to elliptic, rarely lanceolate-oblong to ovate, (30-)40-65(-75) X (11-)14-28(-33) mm; upper leaves linear-oblong, smaller; surface sparsely to densely glandular-pilose, often ciliate, the midrib densely glandular-pilose. Peduncles (7-)11-21(-26) mm long at anthesis, densely glandular-pilose. Calyx large, divided into 5 segments 2-3 mm above the base, the segments linear, (8-)10-15(-19) X 1-2(-3.2) mm, rotundate at apex, both sides densely glandular-pilose, elongate and deflexed in fruit. Corolla large, (33-)35-48 mm long overall; tube 20-28 mm long, fun- nel-shaped, lower side remarkably intruding toward the mouth, reniform in plan (Fig. 2A, C) and urceolate in lateral view (Fig. 2B); tube within pale purple with deep pur- ple stripes and reticulation on the upper side (Fig. 2D), glabrous; tube without reddish purple, glandular-pilose; corolla divided into 5 light reddish purple lobes, each lobe orbicular to triangular, acute to mucronate, occasionally rotundate at apex (Fig. 2A). Stamens 5 (2 long, 2 medium, 1 short); filaments glabrous, affixed to the base of the corolla tube, filament of the long stamens 15-19(-21) mm long, slightly incurved in the upper portion; anthers of the long stamens 1-3 mm apart, lobes of the dehisced anthers flat to weakly deflexed, positioned with pollen grain side facing each other (Fig. 2C). Pistil 13-17 mm long; ovary ovoid; style glabrous, curved upward in the upper part; stigma weakly bilabiate, located between anthers of long and medium stamens (Fig. 2D). Pedicel strongly deflexed in fruit, (11-)13-33(-43) mm long. Capsule ovoid to globose, mucronate at apex, 5-7(-9) mm long, 1/3-1/2 of the calyx length. Seeds minute, globose, 0.5-0.7 mm diam. Chromosome number 2n = 14.

description: Perennial herb, 20-40 cm tall. Stem branched, especially at the base and in the upper half; main stem erect; lateral stems developing from the base of the main stem ascendant to prostrate; each stem often branched into 3 branches around the node bearing the first flower (Fig. 1), densely glandular-pilose; hairs contorted, 0.5 mm long, white; internodes 8-35(70) mm long. Leaves oblong to broadly linear, occasionally elliptical, (24)30-43(52) mm long, (6)10-19(32) mm wide, attenuate to cuneate at base, acute, rarely obtuse to rotundate at apex, subglabrous to sparsely pilose except on the margin and ribs, ciliate, the nerves pilose. Peduncles short, 5-13(21) mm long at anthesis, densely glandular-pilose. Calyx cleft into 5 segments above the 1.5-2.2 mm base, the segment linear to nar- row lanceolate, short, 3-6(7) mm long, 0.9-1.1 mm broad, rotundate at apex, both sides densely glandular-pilose. Corolla small, (18)20-25(28) mm long including the lobes; tube funnel-shaped (Fig. 2B), 12- 17 mm long, the inner surface glabrous, pale purple with deep purple stripes and reticulation on the upper side (Fig. 2D), the outer surface glandular-pilose; lobes reddish purple, shallowly divided into 5 segments, each segment transverse-elliptical to transverse-oblong, occasionally truncate, mucronate or cuspidate at apex (Fig. 2A). Stamens 5 (2 long, 2 medium, 1 short); filaments glabrous, 13-15 mm long, incurved in the upper portion, affixed to the base of the corolla tube (Fig. 2D); anthers of the long stamens making contact with each other in front of the stigma (Fig. 2C), the lobes of dehisced anthers oblong to elliptical (Fig. 2F), evidently channeled (Fig. 2C, E, F).  Pistil 11-13 mm long; ovary ovoid; style glabrous, curved in the upper part; stigma obconical to truncate, located between anthers of long and medium stamens (Fig. 2D-F). Pedicel strongly or weakly deflexed, 8-20(37) mm long in the fruiting state (Fig. 1). Capsule ovoid, mucronate at apex, (3)5- 6(7) mm long, longer than 1/2 of the calyx length. Seeds minute, globose to subreni form, 0.5-0.7 mm long. Chromosome number 2n = 14.

description: Perennial herb, 0.5-2 (4) m tall, recumbent upon adjacent plants. Stems branched especially at the base and in the upper half, ascendant, subglabrous or glandular-pilose; hairs contorted, 0.5 mm long, brown; internodes 1-5 (9) cm long. Leaves lanceolate- oblong to oblong, occasionally ovate to el- liptical, 25-45 (60) mm long, 6-18 (25) mm wide, evidently petiolate at base, acute at apex, glandular-pilose, rarely subglabrous except on the margin and ribs, ciliate, the nerves pilose, the hairs contorted, prostrate, the petioles 6-10 (12) mm long, pilose. Peduncles 13-30 (35) mm long at anthesis, glandular-pilose. Calyx deeply cleft into 5 segments above the 2-3 mm base, the segments linear to narrow lanceolate, 8-12 mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm broad, obtuse to rounded at apex, basal part of the whole calyx tubular (Fig. 2B, C), glabrous or subglabrous externally except on margin and midrib, pilose internally on lobes. Corolla 35-40 (43) mm long including the lobes, the tube narrow, 25-34 mm long (Fig. 2B, C), the inner surface of the tube glabrous, pale greenish-yellow with dense, deep purple stripes and reticulation (Fig. 2C, D), the outer surface of the tube pilose, pale greenish-yellow with obscure purple stripes and reticulation, the lobes reddish purple, deeply divided into 5 segments, each segment slightly deflexed, occasionally patent (Fig. 2B), orbicular, mucronate at apex (Fig. 2A). Stamens 5 (2 long, 2 medium, and 1 short), the long ones extending to the throat of the corolla tube (Fig. 2C); filaments (22) 25-32 mm long, glabrous, almost straight, affixed to the base of the corolla tube, the affixed portion of fil- ament twice as long as the ovary (Fig. 2C); anthers of the long stamens clearly separated from each other (Fig. 2D). Ovary ovoid; style (22) 25-33 mm long, slender; stigma exserted above the anthers of the long stamens (Fig. 2C), strongly vertically bilobed, 1.2-1.5 mm long, 0.6-0.9 mm broad (Fig. 2D). Pedicel weakly or strongly deflexed, 22-40 (50) mm long in the fruiting state. Capsule 6-9 mm long, globose, mucronate at apex. Seeds minute, subreniform, 0.7-0.9 mm long. Chromosome number 2n = 14

description: Perennial herb, 10-20 cm tall, to 50 cm wide. Stem thin, 1.3-2.4(-3) mm diam., prostrate, usually elongated in zigzags; each stem divided into 2 branches at the node bearing the first flower, densely glandular-pilose; hairs contorted, ca. 1 mm long, white; internodes 7-40(-63) mm long. Leaves attenuate to cuneate at base, acute to rounded at apex, erect in full sun; lower leaves linear-oblong to elliptic, rarely obovate, (15-)20-45(-60) X 8-20(-32) mm; upper leaves linear to oblong, smaller; surface densely glandular-pilose. Peduncles 10-25(-32) mm long at anthesis, densely glandular-pilose. Calyx divided into 5 seg- ments 2-3 mm above the base, the seg- ments linear, rarely narrowly oblanceolate, 7-13(-18) mm long, 0.8-2 mm broad, rounded at apex, both sides densely glan- dular-pilose, deflexed in fruit. Corolla large (Fig. 4A, right), (32-)35-55 mm long, overall reddish purple, solid color including the tube and lobes; tube narrowly funnel- shaped (Fig. 4B, top), 21-30 mm long, the basal part cylindrical (Fig. 4C), with 5 grooves (Fig. 4D); the outer surface glan- dular-pilose; the inner surface glabrous, rarely obscure stripes or reticulation on the upper side; corolla shallowly divided into 5 lobes, each lobe depressed-orbicular, acute to mucronate at apex (Fig. 4A, right). Sta- mens 5 (2 long, 2 medium, 1 short), inserted in the corolla tube (Fig. 4C); filaments glabrous, curved upward in the upper part, the basal half or more affixed to the base of the corolla tube, the affixed portion of the filament three times as long as the ovary (Fig. 4C), filaments of the long stamens 16-21(-24) mm long; anthers of the long stamens connivent in front of the stigma. Pistil (11-)13-19 mm long; ovary ovoid; style glabrous, curved upward in the upper part; stigma obconical to truncate, located between anthers of long and medium stamens (Fig. 4C). Pedicel strongly deflexed in fruit, (7-)12-28(-36) mm long. Capsule ovoid to globose, mucronate at apex, 5-8(-9) mm long, usually more than 1/2 the length of the calyx. Seeds minute, globose, 0.6-0.8 mm diam. Chromosome number 2n = 14.

description: Arbor parva; caules virides glabri valde alati, cortice griseo; folia geminata elliptica apice acuta, basi acuminata, parallelinervia utrinque glabra subtus pallide viridia, petiolo alato; inflorescentiae foliis oppositae vel intemodales simplices vel furcatae, cicatricibus pedicellorum arcte confertis; pedicelli sub anthesi deflexi camosi; gemmae ovoideae clausae; calycis lobi irregulariter deltati; corolla alba camosa, lobis planis fere ad basin divisis; bacca globosa viridis 4 cm diametro dense cameo-griseo-papillosa, pedicello fructifero lignoso deflexo; semina fusca ovoidea reniformia, testa foveolata.

description: Shrub or small tree, 2-6 m tall; young stems and leaves densely red-papillose, appearing grayish and matte on live plants; stems fleshy and green, strongly winged, the wings 2-5 mm broad; bark of older stems soon glabrate, grayish. Leaves geminate, elliptic, widest at the middle, glabrous and shiny above, paler below, occasionally minutely red-papillose on the veins below; major leaves 20- 50 cm long, 10-20 cm wide, the apex acute, the base acuminate, decurrent on the petiole and from there onto the stem, with 15-17 pairs of secondary veins; petiole strongly winged from the bases of the decurrent leaves, 4-7 cm long; minor leaves differing from the major ones only in size, 15-19 cm long, 9-11 cm wide; petiole 1.5-2 cm long. Inflorescences opposite the leaves or sometimes intemodal, simple or very occasionally furcate, 0.5-1 cm long, 3-5-flowered, minutely red-papillose like the young stems and leaves; pedicel scars closely spaced and overlapping; pedicels at anthesis white and fleshy, 1.5-2 cm long, abruptly narrowing below the calyx tube, then tapering to 0.5-1 mm in diam (dry specimens, thicker in live plants); buds ovoid, the calyx completely closed until just before anthesis, when the corolla emerges and tears the lobes; calyx tube campanulate, 3-3.5 mm long, occasionally minutely red-papillose, the lobes very irregular in shape, 3-5 mm long, the margins thick and white in dry specimens; corolla white, rather fleshy, 2-3 cm in diam, planar at anthesis, lobed nearly to the base, the corolla tube only 1 mm long, the lobes wider at the middle than at the base, the tips and margins of the lobes minutely papillose; anthers 4-6 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, poricidal at the tips, the pores becoming slit-like upon drying, the anthers tightly connate at anthesis; free portion of the filaments ca 1 mm long, the filament tube ca 0.5 mm long; ovary densely pinkish-gray-papillose, the papillae minute in flower, growing with the fruit; style straight, ca 1.3 cm long; stigma 2-lobed, the surface minutely papillose. Berries globose, green with creamy white flesh, ca 4 cm in diam (in live plants, the fruits shrink when dried); mature fruit glabrate, the young fruit covered with minute pinkish-gray papillae, these making the fruit look grayish in live plants, pinkish in dry specimens; fruiting pedicels very woody, deflexed, 2-2.5 cm long, 3-3.5 mm in diam at the base; seeds pale tan, ovoid-reniform, ca 5 mm long, 4 mm wide, the surfaces minutely pitted. Chromosome number: n = 12 (voucher Knapp & Mallet 6180).

description: Shrubs, 0.5-1.5 m tall; young stems and leaves minutely and densely redpapillose, this soon deciduous; older stems glabrate; bark grayish, faintly longitudinally striate. Sympodial units plurifoliate. Leaves occasionally geminate, narrowly elliptic to linear, widest at the middle or just above, 11-20 cm long, 1-4 cm wide, with 6-10 pairs of secondary veins, these impressed above, yellowish beneath in dry specimens, glabrous above, minutely golden-puberulent along the veins beneath, the trichomes unicellular and barely visible, the apex long-acuminate, the base attenuate; petiole winged from the decurrent leaf bases, 1.5-2 cm long. Inflorescences opposite the leaves or sometimes intemodal, 1-4 cm long, occasionally branched once, bearing 3-5 open flowers at a time, but with many scars, glabrous or minutely red-papillose at the tip; pedicel scars closely spaced but not overlapping, beginning at the base of the inflorescence; pedicels at anthesis deflexed, 0.8-1 cm long, tapering from the base of the calyx tube to a slender base ca 0.4 mm in diam; buds elliptic even when very young, the corolla not early exserted from the tube; calyx tube broadly cup-shaped, 1-1.5 mm long, the lobes deltoid, 1-2.5 mm long, the margins white and thickened in dry material, minutely puberulent along the margins and tips of the lobes; corolla white, 0.8-1 cm in diam, lobed nearly to the base, the lobes planar or slightly reflexed at anthesis, the tips and margins of the lobes minutely papillose; free portion of the filaments ca 0.5 mm long, the filament tube ca 0.25 mm long; anthers 2-2.5 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, poricidal at the tips, the pores becoming slit-like upon drying; ovary glabrous; style straight, 5-6 mm long; stigma capitate, 2-lobed, minutely papillose. Berries globose, green, 1-1.2 cm in diam; fruiting pedicels erect and woody, 1.5-1.7 cm long, ca 1 mm in diam at the base; calyx lobes slightly woody and accrescent in fruit, 3-5 mm long; seeds pale brownish-green, ovoid-reniform, 2-3 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, the surfaces minutely pitted. Chromosome number not known.

description: Shrubs or small trees 1-6 m high; trunks to 5 cm in diam., bark pale to dark brown. Young branches terete, rough granular, pubescence ferrugineous, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate. Leaves somewhat coriaceous, lanceolate, oblanceolate or narrowly elliptic, the apices long attenuate, the bases long attenuate, decurrent along entire length of petiole or nearly so, mostly 10-17 cm long, 2-3 cm wide; scabrous to nearly smooth above, the hairs sessile, porrect-stellate, sparse to nearly touching; ferrugineous-pubescent below, the hairs thick-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate; petioles scabrous, the hairs mostly porrect-stellate; axillary leaves absent. Inflorescences 7-15 cm long; peduncles unbranched for 4-13 cm, 1.1-2.9 mm thick, rough granular tomentose, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate; pedicels 2-6 mm long, pubescent, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate. Flower buds obovoid to ellipsoid, 4-5 mm long at anthesis, pubescent, the hairs sessile and shortstalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate; calyx lobe sutures conspicuous as lines of minute whitish hairs. Calyx lobed 1/2 way, the lobes semi-ovate to acute, 1.5-2.8 mm long by 1.5-2.2 mm wide in flower, 2.3-4.2 mm by 1.7-2.9 mm in fruit, glabrous or with stellate hairs within. Corolla weakly exserted from calyx at anthesis, white, 9-12 mm across, the lobes glabrous or with few simple hairs within. Anthers 2.0-2.8 mm long, inserted on corolla tube 1.0-1.2 mm above base, the filaments 0.6-1.5 mm long. Ovary and lower 1/2 of style tomentose. Fruits 8-10 mm in diam., pubescence persistent. Seeds 1.4-2.0 mm long, 1.1-1.7 mm wide.

description: Shrubs or small trees 1-10 m high, trunks to 13 cm in diam., bark pale gray-brown. Young, branches terete, granular whitish to grayish tomentose, the hairs dendriticechinoid and echinoid. Leaves rather thin, ovate to obovate, the apices acute or attenuate, the bases long attenuate along nearly entire length of petiole, usually 8-29 cm long, 3-11 cm wide; finely scabridulous to velutinous above, the hairs sparse, sessile or short-stalked, mostly simple and few-rayed stellate, sometimes vestigial, multangulate; whitish tomentose below, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrectstellate, multangulate, and echinoid; petioles scabridulous, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrect stellate and multangulate; axillary leaves present on recent growth of young plants, often lacking on branches of mature plants. Inflorescences 8-15 cm long; peduncles unbranched for 4-9 cm, 2.0-3.8 mm thick, granular tomentose, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, mostly multangulate, some dendritic-echinoid; pedicels 2-7 mm long, pubescent, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, multangulate and echinoid. Flower buds nearly globose to ellipsoid, 4-5 mm long, pubescent, the hairs multangulate and echinoid, partly minute; calyx lobe sutures evident as lines of minute whitish-brown hairs. Calyx lobed ?-3/4 way, the lobes semi-ovate, often uneven in size, 1.7-4.9 mm long by 1.0-3.7 mm wide in flower, 2.4-5.1 mm by 1.8-5.0 mm in fruit, usually thin, somewhat translucent, pubescent on upper 1, within, the hairs minute, stellate or multangulate. Corolla included in calyx nearly until anthesis, very pale to rich violet, 10-17 mm across, the lobes with scattered simple and stellate hairs on upper 1/2 within. Anthers 2.6-3.7 mm long, inserted on corolla tube 0.8-1.2 mm above base, the filaments 0.7-1.0 mm long. Ovary tomentose. Style tomentose 1/3 way from base. Fruits 9-12 mm in diam., pubescence persistent. Seeds 1.8-2.6 mm long, 1.3-2.1 mm wide. Chromosome number: 2n = 24 (voucher: Roe, Roe & Mori 773).

description: Shrubs or small trees 1-5 m high, open branched, trunks to 9 cm in diam., bark pale brown. Young branches terete, granular greenish-yellow tomentose, the hairs dendritic-echinoid and echinoid. Leaves rather thin, obovate, ovate or broadly elliptic, the apices obtuse, acute or short acuminate, the bases long attenuate along nearly entire length of petiole, usually 14-30 cm long, 4-1.2 cm wide; scabridulous above, the hairs sessile or short-stalked, sparse, simple and porrect-stellate; pubescent below, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate; petioles scabridulous, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate; axillary leaves nearly always developed on young branches. Inflorescences 7-14 cm long; peduncles unbranched for 3-8 cm, sometimes with a pair of small leaves at the first dichotomy, 2-4 mm thick, granular tomentose, the hairs sessile and shortstalked, porrect-stellate, multangulate, echinoid and dendritic-echinoid; pedicels 3-7 mm long, pubescent, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate. Flower buds obovoid-oblong, 5-7 mm long at anthesis, tomentose, the hairs often appressed, mostly porrect-stellate and multangulate, the tomentum usually so dense as to obscure the calyx lobe sutures. Calyx lobed 1/2-2/3 way, the lobes acute, obtuse or semi-ovate, often uneven in size, 3-5 mm long by 1.9-3.7 mm wide in flower, 3.9-6.5 mm by 1.8-4.5 mm in fruit, usually thin, somewhat translucent, simple and stellate pubescent within. Corolla included in calyx until anthesis, white, 15-21 mm across, the lobes with minute stellate hairs on upper 1/2 within. Anthers 2.9-4.4 mm long, inserted on corolla tube 1.3-1.7 mm above base, the filaments 1.1-1.5 mm long. Ovary tomentose. Style tomentose about 3/4 way from base. Fruits 11-14 mm in diam., yellow when ripe, pubescence persistent. Seeds 2.0-2.8 mm long, 1.5-2.1 mm wide. Chromosome number: 2n = 24 (voucher: Roe & Roe 1937).

description: Delicate shrub or small slender treelet, 1-3 m tall; young stems glabrous, shiny and green; bark of the older stems gray. Sympodial units unifoliate. Leaves not geminate, elliptic to lanceolate, widest at the middle, 8-16 cm long, 2-5 cm wide, glabrous on both surfaces, the undersurface pale in both dry and live plants, with 7-9 pairs of secondary veins, these raised above, in dry specimens somewhat prominent below, darkish, the tertiary venation obscure, the apex acute, the base acute, decurrent on the petiole; petiole 0.8-2 cm long, longer on older leaves. Inflorescences opposite the leaves, simple, 3-5 mm long, 3-6-flowered, glabrous; pedicel scars closely spaced, but not overlapping; pedicels at anthesis slender, 6- 8 mm long, deflexed, ca 0.3 mm in diam at the base; buds globose, when very young minutely hirsute with uniseriate trichomes ca 0.1 mm long or less, the corolla soon exserted from the calyx; calyx tube not much differentiated from the pedicel, ca 0.25 mm long, the lobes broadly deltoid, minutely apiculate, ca 0.25 mm long, glabrous except for the tips of the lobes; corolla white, minute, 4-5 mm in diam, lobed ca 2/3 Of the way to the base, the lobes reflexed at anthesis, the tips of the lobes minutely papillose; free portion of the filaments ca 0.25 mm long, the filament tube ca 0.25 mm long; anthers 1-1.5 mm long, ca 0.75 mm wide, poricidal at the tips, the pores becoming slit-like upon drying; ovary glabrous; style straight, ca 3 mm long in long-styled flowers, ca 1 mm long in short-styled flowers; stigma a papillose area on the tip of the style. Berries globose, green, ca 1 cm in diam (immature); fruiting pedicels erect, woody, 2-2.2 cm long, ca 0.75 mm in diam at the base; seeds not mature in fruits examined. Chromosome number not known.

description: Robust shrubs or small trees 2-12 m high, open branched, trunks to 31 cm in diam., bark pale greenish-brown. Young branches terete or longitudinally angled and grooved, whitish granular tomentose at tips, the hairs multangulate and echinoid, some long-stalked; soon glabrescent. Leaves rather thin, ovate or broadly ovate, the apices short acuminate, the bases long attenuate, usually 24-40 cm long, 10-26 cm wide; scabrous above, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, spaced to touching, simple, correct-stellate, multangulate and echinoid, tomentose below or sparsely pubescent only along veins, the hairs sessile and stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate; petioles granular tomentose, the hairs echinoid; axillary leaves usually present. Inflorescences 8-17 cm long; peduncles unbranched for 5-13 cm, 3-8 mm thick, granular, the hairs sessile and long-stalked, multangulate and echinoid; pedicels very short, 1 mm long or less in flower, 1-5 mm long in fruit, pubescent, the hairs echinoid, some long-stalked. Flower buds globose when immature, becoming elongated, 5-8 mm long at anthesis, tomentose, the hairs echinoid; calyx lobe sutures sometimes evident as lines of minute whitish hairs. Calyx lobed 1/4-1/2 way, the lobes acute to slightly ovate, small, 1.2-2.5 mm long by 1.4-2.4 mm wide in flower, 3.6-5.0 mm by 3.5-4.7 mm in fruit, pubescent within, especially upper 1/2, the hairs porrectstellate and multangulate. Corolla strongly exserted from calyx at anthesis, lined and longitudinally ridged before opening, white or rich violet, 14-20 mm across, the lobes with occasional porrect-stellate hairs along midvein within. Anthers 3.2-4.5 mm long, inserted on corolla tube 1.9-2.6 mm above base, the filaments 1.8-2.1 mm long. Ovary tomentose. Style tomentose more than 1/2 way from base or nearly to stigma. Fruit 11 mm in diam., pubescence persistent. Seeds 2.1-2.6 mm long, 1.6-2.3 mm wide. Chromosome number: 2n = 24 (voucher: Roe, Roe & Mori 741).
bibliographicCitation: Roe, Keith E. 1967. A revision of Solanum sect. Brevantherum (Solanaceae) in North and Central America. Brittonia. 19: 353-373.

description: Shrubs or small trees to 4 m high; bark pale brown. Young branches strongly sulcate, grayish to reddish, softly tomentose, the indument persistent, becoming matted, the hairs short- to rather long-stalked, porrect-stellate, multangulate, den- dritic-multangulate, and dendritic-echinoid, nearly furfuraceous. Leaves thick, coriaceous, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 14-32 cm long, 6-12 cm wide, above dark green, velutinous to glabrate, the hairs touching or lacking, short-stalked, porrect-stellate, beneath whitish tomentose, the hairs stalked, porrect-stellate; apices acute or attenuate, bases acute, obtuse, or cuneate; petioles 1-5 cm long, tomentose, the hairs mixed sessile and stalked, porrect-stellate, multangulate, and dendritic-mult- angulate, nearly furfuraceous. Axillary leaves lacking. Inflorescences 7-16 cm long; peduncles unbranched for 3-7.5 cm, 2-5 mm thick, sulcate, softly tomentose, the hairs mixed sessile and stalked, porrect-stellate, multangulate, and dendritic- multangulate; pedicels 2-3 mm long (to 5 mm in fruit), tomentose, the hairs mixed sessile and stalked, porrect-stellate, and multangulate. Flower buds oblong, 6-8 mm long at anthesis; corolla tomentose, the hairs mixed sessile and short-stalked, porrect-stellate, thin-walled, transparent; calyx lobe sutures obscured by tomentum. Calyx thin, somewhat translucent, accrescent, lobed 1/2-2/3 way to base, the lobes often splitting unevenly, acute, obtuse or semi-ovate, 2-4 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide in flower, 2.9-6 mm by 5-6 mm in fruit, a few minute simple and porrect- stellate hairs within on upper fourth of lobes, tomentose without, the hairs sessile and short-stalked, porrect-stellate, and multangulate. Corolla soon exserted, nearly the length of calyx or its lobes by anthesis, white, 16-22 mm across, the lobes 6-8 mm long, with few simple and porrect-stellate hairs on upper fourth within. Anthers 3.7-4.4 mm long; filaments 0.9-2.0 mm long. Ovary tomentose, the hairs porrect- stellate and multangulate. Style exserted from stamens, pubescent on lower 2/3_3/4, the hairs porrect-stellate and multangulate. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., sparsely pubescent. Seeds 3.4-3.8 mm long, 2.6-3.0 mm wide.

description: Shrubs or small trees 2-6 m tall; young stems densely white pubescent with simple, uniseriate trichomes ca. 1 mm long composed of 2-5 cells; older stems remaining densely white pubescent, occasionally glabrate, unarmed. Sympodial units unifoliate or difoliate and geminate. Leaves 1.5-17 x 1-6 cm, simple, dimorphic, the major leaves 9-17 x 3-6 cm, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, the minor leaves 1.5-3 x 1-2 cm, differing from major leaves only in size, but occasionally somewhat rounder in outline, thin-textured, drying pale green, evenly pubescent adaxially with simple uniseriate trichomes ca. 1 mm long, densely pubescent abaxially with white uniseriate trichomes 1-1.5 mm long, the trichomes denser on the veins; base acute; margin entire; apex acute, rounded at the very tip; petioles 0.3-0.7 cm in major leaves, ca. 0.5 cm in minor leaves, densely pubescent. Inflorescences 1.5-5 cm, opposite the leaves or occasionally somewhat internodal, unbranched, with 10-20 flowers, all flowers apparently perfect, the axes densely white-pubescent with simple uniseri- ate trichomes 0.5-1.5 mm; peduncle 1-3 cm; rachis 1-4.5 cm; pedicels 10-12 mm in flower, tapering from the abrupt base of the calyx tube to a slender base 0.5-0.8 mm in diameter, deflexed, 15-22 mm in fruit, 0.5-1 mm in diameter at the base, pendent, woody, closely packed, often overlapping, articulated at the base. Buds when very young appearing globose, the corolla soon exerted from the calyx lobes, the buds later becoming obovoid just before anthesis. Calyx 2-2.5 mm long, the tube 1-1.5 mm, the lobes ca. 1 × 1 mm, deltate to broadly triangular, abruptly constricted too an elongate tip ca. 0.5 mm long, densely pubescent with simple, uniseriate trichormes like those of the rest of the inflorescence; fruiting calyx not accrescent, the lobes ca. 1 x 1 mm, brittle and somewhat patent; corolla 1.5-2 cm in diameter, ca. 10 mm long, stellate, white or tinged purplish in some plants, the tube ca. 1 mm, the lobes ca. 1 x 0.5 mm at base, ovate-lanceolate, reflexed at anthesis, acute at apices, densely and evenly pubescent abaxially with simple uniseriate trichomes ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous adaxially except for the densely papillose margins, the tips of the lobes densely papillose and somewhat cucullate; filaments glabrous, the free portion 0.8-1 mm, the filament tube 1-2 mm, with small teeth arising from the filament tube between the anthers; anthers 4-5 x 1-1.5 mm, oblong, slightly sagittate at base, connivent, yellow, the pores tear-drop shaped, opening into longitudinal slits with age; ovary glabrous; style 6-7 x ca. 0.05 mm, cylindrical, straight, glabrous; stigma capitate. Fruit a globose berry, 1-1.2 cm in diameter, green, glabrous. Seeds numerous (more than 15) per fruit, 3-3.5 x 2- 2.5 mm, flattened-reniform, pale yellow in dry material, the surfaces minutely pitted, the margin incrassate and darker yellow.

description: Shrubs or small trees 1-4 m high, forming flat-topped spreading crowns; trunks to 8 cm in diam., bark greenish or yellowish brown. Young branches terete or longitudinally angled and grooved, whitish to yellowish granular-tomentose, the hairs sessile and stalked, multangulate and echinoid. Leaves rather thin, ovate, lanceovate or broadly elliptic, the apices acute, attenuate or acuminate, the bases short attenuate, sometimes abruptly so, usually 13-33 cm long, 5-15 cm wide, scabridulous to velutinous above, the hairs spaced to overlapping, sessile and short, stout-stalked, simple, porrect-stellate and multangulate; tomentose below, the hairs sessile and stalked, porrect-stellate, multangulate and echinoid; axillary leaves usually lacking or rare on mature plants. Inflorescences 8-14 cm long; peduncles unbranched for 4-10 cm, 2.5-4.5 mm thick, granular-tomentose, the hairs sessile and stalked, multangulate and echinoid; pedicels 2-6 mm long, pubescent, the hairs sessile and shortstalked, multangulate and echinoid. Flower buds subglobose to oblong at anthesis, tomentose, the hairs multangulate and echinoid, often appressed; calyx lobe sutures evident as lines of minute white hairs. Calyx lobed 2 way, the lobes acute to semiovate, often of unequal size, i.e. the calyx not split along all sutures, 1.4-4.3 mm long by 1.4-2.6 mm wide in flower, 2.0-5.6 mm by 2.6-4.4 mm in fruit, glabrous or with occasional simple or stellate hairs within. Corolla only weakly exserted from calyx at anthesis, white or violet, 12-17 mm across, the lobes with few simple or stellate hairs within. Anthers 3.1-4.7 mm long, inserted on corolla tube 1.7-1.9 mm above base, the filaments 1.4-1.6 mm long. Ovary sparingly to moderately pubescent. Style glabrous or with occasional stellate hairs on lower 1/2. Fruit 12-14 mm in diam., yellow when ripe, glabrescent. Seeds 1.7-2.4 mm long, 1.4-1.9 mm wide. Chromosome number: 2n = 24 (voucher: Roe, Roe & Mori 986).

description: Low shrub with spreading branches, with a yellowish cast from the dense tomentum, strongly armed with straight, spreading, acicular, yellow spines of various sizes, up to 1.2 cm long. Stem terete, densely yellowish-tomentose with sessile to short-stalked, multangulate stellate hairs, the stalk up to 0.5 mm long, the longest stalks often with a few scattered rays beneath the main group, the rays of the main whorl 8-15, 0.2-0.5 mm long, the midpoint longer, up to 1.0 (1.5) mm long, many (all?) gland-tipped; cauline spines straight, spreading, slender, up to 7 mm long, shorter than those of leaves, glandular, especially in the lower half, with minute, simple, gland-tipped hairs ca 0.1 mm long and often with a few small stellate hairs at the very base. Leaves single, 5-10 cm long, 4-7 cm wide, ovate, irregularly and shallowly lobed with 3-5 pairs of obtuse lobes reaching less than halfway to midrib, the lobes with small, crenate, obtuse teeth; blades unequal at base, obtuse at tip; petiole 2-5 cm long, with pubescence like that of stem, with 5-15 spines like those of stem but mostly longer, up to 1.5 cm long; blade above moderately tomentose with short, simple, gland-tipped hairs to 0.2 mm long mixed with 4-10-rayed, sessile stellate hairs (ca 0.5-0.8 mm wide) and with longer midpoint 0.8-1.3 mm long; blade below similarly but more densely tomentose, the stellae on larger veins often with short stalks up to 0.4 mm long. Inflorescence extra-axillary, simple, up to 6 cm long, the common peduncle 1-2 cm long, ca 8-flowered, the rachis densely glandular-tomentose like the stem, with short spines, the rachis more slender above the first flower and often deciduous after flowering, only the lowest flower fertile; pedicels 0.5-1 cm long in anthesis, the fertile one 1-2 cm long in fruit, 2-3 mm in diameter (nearly the same diameter as the peduncle), with spines and pubescence similar to those of peduncle and rachis. Calyx densely glandular-tomentose, only that of the fertile flower armed with acicular spines, 6-8 mm long in anthesis, lobed halfway to base, the lobes tri- angular, enlarging only slightly in fruit, to ca 1 cm long, 4-5 cm wide at base. Corolla white, ca 1 cm long at anthesis, deeply lobed but with some interpetalar tissue, tomentose externally on midrib with sessile, 8-15-rayed stellate hairs, the midpoint to 0.8 mm long. Anthers equal, 5.5-6.5 mm long; filaments ca 1 mm long. Style rudimentary in male flowers, ca 1 mm long, in fertile flowers ca 1 cm long and exceeding anthers by ca 3 mm. Fruit globose, glabrous, light green-dark green striped when young, yellow at maturity, ca 4 cm in diameter. Seeds numerous, pale tan, 2.8-3.2 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, very finely and obscurely pitted, nearly smooth.

description: Slender shrub 1-2.5 m tall; stems glabrous to densely pubescent with unbranched hairs, some with broad multiseriate bases giving the young stems a corky or roughened appearance, unarmed. Sympodial units difoliate, geminate. Leaves 3-12 x 0.5-3 cm, simple, dimorphic, the major leaves 5-12 x 1-3 cm, narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, the minor leaves 3-4 x 0.5-1 cm, differing from the major ones only in size, usually subcoriaceous, glabrous adaxially, glabrous to moderately pubescent abaxially with unbranched hairs; base cuneate to long-tapered; margin entire, glabrous to ciliate; apex acute to acuminate; petioles 0.5-2 cm, 1-2 cm in major leaves, ca. 0.5 cm in minor leaves, glabrous to moderately pubescent in adaxial channel. Inflorescence 0.5-2 cm, opposite the leaves, unbranched or rarely forked, with 1-6 flowers, all flowers perfect, the axes glabrous to sparsely pubescent; peduncle 0.2-2 cm; rachis very short, 1-4 mm; pedicels 10-20 mm in flower, 15-35 mm and slender and curved in fruit, congested and spaced up to 3 mm apart, articulated at the base. Calyx 2-3 mm long, the tube ca. 1 mm, the lobes 1-2 x 1.5-2 mm, broadly deltate, almost truncate with a small acumen at tip, glabrous at base, tomentose at tips; fruiting calyx not accrescent, the lobes 1-2 x 1.5-2 mm; corolla 1- 1.5 cm in diameter, 4-7 mm long, stellate, white, the tube 1-2 mm, the lobes 3-5 x 2- 2.5 mm at base, narrowly triangular to ovate, acute at apices, glabrous abaxially at base, tomentose at tips of lobes, glabrous adaxially; filaments glabrous, the free portion 0.5- 1 mm, the filament tube absent to 0.5 mm; anthers 3-4 x 1.5-2 mm, oblong, connivent, yellow, the pores broad, directed distally and adaxially, often opening into longitudinal slits with age; ovary glabrous; style 4-5 x ca. 0.5 mm, cylindrical, straight; glabrous; stigma truncate. Fruit a globose berry, 1-1.5 cm in diameter, orange when ripe, glabrous. Seeds fewer than 15 per fruit, ca. 4 x 3 mm, somewhat flattened, yellow-brown, the surfaces rugulose.

description: Frutex 1.5-3 m altus; rami juniores aculeis rectis vel parum recurvatis ad 8 mm longis armati, vetustiores saepe inermes; caules dense stellato-tomentosi; folia ramorum floriferorum plerumque inermia, ovata, 7-20 x 3-10 cm, ambitu variabilia, integra, repanda vel lobulata. Inflorescentiae 2-4-ramosae; calyx tubo 2 mm longo, lobis lanceolatis ad fere linearibus; corolla rotato-quinquangula, 2-2.5 cm lata; antherae 4.5-5 mm longae, fere lineares; ovarium dense stellato- tomentosum. Baccae dense stellato-tomentosae, 1.9 cm diametro; semina complanata, reniformia, 3.6 x 2.9 mm.

description: Shrubs 1.5-3 m tall; stems densely stellate-tomentose, ferruginous when young, paler when mature, with 6-9-rayed stellae ca. 0.6 mm broad, the midpoints ca. 0.2 mm long, young plants and sprouts normally armed with broad-based prickles to 8 mm long, these mostly straight, some slightly reflexed or recurved, the base usually densely tomentose, older stems mostly unarmed. Sympodial units difoliate, not geminate. Leaves 7-20 x 3-10 cm, simple, more or less uniform in size and shape on flowering branches, but those of young plants or sprouts much larger (to 35 x 23 cm), ovate, thin-textured, pubescent adaxially with stipi- tate stellae 0.3-0.6 mm broad, the rays 6-8, the midpoints ca. 1 mm long, the stipes variable in length, up to 0.2 mm long, more densely stellate-tomentose abaxially and with the stellae lighter in color, unarmed ex- cept rarely with a few stout prickles on major veins on undersides of sprout leaves; base truncate to rounded, oblique; margin highly variable in outline, with leaves of flowering stems often entire or irregularly repand or lobed near the base, the juvenile leaves with three lobes per side, the sinuses to reaching within 2 cm of the midrib and the lobes again pinnately lobed, the lobes rounded to rarely acute; apex attenuate to sometimes rounded; petioles to 5 cm, densely stellate-tomentose, unarmed except on sprouts, then with prickles 1.5-2.5 (-4) cm long like those of the stem. Inflorescences 4-8 cm, extra- axillary, 2-4 branched, with few to 26 flow- ers, all flowers evidently perfect, the axes densely stellate-tomentose with hairs like those of the stem, unarmed; peduncle 1-2 cm; rachis 2-6 cm; pedicels ca. 10 mm in flower, 17-19 mm in fruit, sulcate and slightly clavate, spaced 2-4 mm apart, articu- lated at the base; calyx 3-7 mm long, the tube ca. 2 mm, the lobes 4.5-8 x ca. 1.5 mm, lanceolate to nearly linear, densely stellate- tomentose abaxially; fruiting calyx not ac- crescent, the lobes 4.5-8 x ca. 1.5 mm; corolla 2-2.5 cm in diameter, 8-11(-16) mm long, rotate-pentagonal, white, the tube 1 mm, the lobes 7.5-11(-15) x 2.5-5 mm, deltate, with ample interpetalar tissue, densely stellate-tomentose abaxially on the midribs with slightly smaller and finer stellae than on the stems, glabrous adaxially; fila- ments glabrous, the free part ca. 1.5 mm, the filament tube absent; anthers 4.5-5 x 1-1.3 mm, nearly linear, connivent, yellow, the pores minute and directed distally, not opening into lognitudinal slits with age; ovary densely stellate-tomentose; style ca. 7 x 0.4- 0.5 mm, cylindrical, straight or slightly curved, with a few stellae in the basal third; stigma capitate. Fruit a globose berry, to 1.9 cm in diameter, shiny, green when immature, the color when mature not known, densely stellate-tomentose with sessile stellae, tardily glabrescent. Seeds ca. 25 per berry, ca. 3.6 x 2.9 mm, flattened, reniform, yellowish tan, the surfaces minutely foveolate.

description: Herbae scandentes, fruticantes, radiculis adventitiis; rami floriferi herbacei, pubescentes, veteres ad 4 mm diametro, sulcati. Folia plerumque imparipinnata, 1-4- juga, raro simplicia; foliola elliptica vel ovata, lateralia 1.8-3.5 x 0.8-1.6 cm, terminalia ovalia, 2.8-4.1 x 1-2.5 cm; pedicelli 1-4 in apice ramulorum floriferorum; calyx dentibus 5, 2.5 x 0.8 mm; corolla stellata, lobis 4.5 x 1.5 mm; stamina 5; filamenta 0.3 mm longa, pubescentia; antherae oblongae, 1.7 x 0.8 mm; stylus 4.5 mm longus, ad basin pubescens. Bacca globosa, ca. 1 cm diametro; semina compressa, integumento pilifero.

description: Herbaceous vines to several meters; lower stems soft-woody, to at least 4 mm in diameter and sulcate, mostly tightly appressed to tree trunks by clusters of short, fasciculate adventitious roots at the nodes, pubescent when young with weak, simple 3-4-celled hairs 0.4-0.9 mm long, glabrescent when older, unarmed. Sympodial units 3-4- to plurifoliate, not geminate. Leaves 4-12 x 1.5-5 cm, mostly imparipinnate, more or less uniform in size and shape, generally with (3-) 7 (-9) leaflets or rarely simple grading into 3-foliolate leaves on some branches, the leaflets opposite to subopposite, membranous to slightly fleshy, sparsely pilose adaxially with 2-4-celled simple hairs ca. 0.8 mm long, the basal cell much the largest, pubescent abaxially with hairs like those of the stem; lateral leaflets 1.8-3.5 x 0.8-1.6 cm, narrowly elliptic to ovate, the bases unequal and obtuse to truncate, the margins revolute, the apices obtuse to acute, the petiolules 1- 2.5 mm long; terminal leaflet 2.8-4.1 x 1- 2.5 cm, always larger than the laterals and usually more broadly ovate, the base acute, the margin revolute, the apex obtuse to acute, the petiolule 9 mm long; petioles 1-4 cm, sparsely pubescent; pseudostipules 3.5-8 mm, foliaceous, cordate. Inflorescence (0-) 0.5-2 cm, borne on small axillary somewhat leafy short-shoots with bract-like leaves 1-2 mm long along the axis, unbranched, with 1- 4 flowers, all flowers perfect, the axes pubes- cent to nearly glabrous; peduncle 0.4-2 cm; rachis 0-0.2 cm; pedicels 13-18 mm in flower, to 19 mm in fruit, spaced 0-3 mm apart, articulated at the base. Calyx ca. 3.5 mm long, the tube 1 mm long, the lobes 2.5 x 0.8 mm, lanceolate, acute at apices, pilose; fruiting calyx not accrescent, the lobes 2.5 x 0.8 mm; corolla ca. 1 cm in diameter, 5-7 mm long, stellate, white or white with blue, the tube 1-2 mm, the lobes 4.5 x 1.5 mm, lanceolate, acute at apices, glabrous abaxially at base, minutely puberulent at tips, glabrous adaxially; filaments pubescent, the free portion ca. 0.3 mm, the filament tube absent; anthers 1.7 x 0.8 mm, oblong, connivent, yellow, the pores broad, directed introrsely, often opening into longitudinal slits with age; ovary glabrous; style ca. 4.5 x 0.2- 0.4 mm, cylindrical, straight, pubescent in the lower half; stigma clavate. Fruit a globose berry, ca. 1 cm in diameter, orange or red, glabrous. Seeds ca. 15 per fruit, ca. 2.5 x 2 mm, flattened, light brown, the entire surface covered by hairlike extensions of the epidermal walls.

description: Shrubs or trees 1-5 m high. Young branches terete, whitish to yellowish granular tomentose, slowly glabrescent, the hairs mostly short, thick-stalked, porrectstellate and multangulate. Leaves relatively thick, oblanceolate to broadly elliptic, 10-24 cm long, 3.5-8 cm wide, dark green, scabrous above, the hairs spaced to touching, short, thick-stalked on groups of prominent epidermal cells, simple, porrectstellate and few-rayed multangulate, often vestigial-rayed, pale whitish green pubescent beneath, the hairs mixed sessile and thick-stalked, porrect-stellate; apices acute or short-attenuate, bases cuneate or attenuate, the blades often decurrent along  nearly the entire length of petioles, these unwinged for 0-1 cm, scabrous, the hairs short-stalked, porrect-stellate. Axillary leaves lacking. Inflorescences 8-24 cm long; peduncles unbranched for 5-13 cm, 2-5 mm thick, tomentose, the hairs shortto long-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate; pedicels 2-5 mm long (to 7 mm in fruit), pubescent, the hairs short to long, thin-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate. Flower buds orbicular or obovate, 5-7 mm long at anthesis; corollas  tomentose, the yellowish hairs short- to rather long-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate; calyx lobe sutures obscured by tomentum. Calyx relatively thick, lobed '/2-2/3 way to base, the lobes acute to obtuse, 1.7-3.9 mm long, 1.8-2.5 mm wide in flower, 3.5-4.6 mm by 2.4-3.1 mm in fruit, glabrous within, tomentose without, the hairs partly to mostly long, thin-stalked, porrect-stellate and multangulate. Corolla exserted relatively early, moderately so at anthesis, white to violet, 12-15 mm across, the lobes 5-6 mm long, glabrous within or with few simple hairs at tip. Anthers 2.9-3.4 mm long, filaments 1.3-1.5 mm long. Ovary pubescent to tomentose, the hairs multangulate. Style glabrous or pubescent 2/3 way from base, exserted from stamens. Fruits glabrescent. Mature seeds not seen.
