description: Trees 20-2 5 m with rough gray bark, smooth terete fuscous branchlets, ample bifoliolate leaves, and terminal exserted panicles of small white-silky-velutinous flowers crowded into short dense spikes, except for the spike-axis and the perianth with androecium glabrous throughout, the coriaceous, reticulate, sparsely punctate leaflets lustrous dark green above, paler dull beneath. Stipules not seen, either lacking or very early caducous. Petioles including pulvinus 10-17 mm, at middle 0.9-1.2 mm diam.; leaflet-pulvinules (4) 6-8 mm, cari- nate ventrally, slightly twisted outward; blade of leaflets inequilaterally broad-ellip tic, +/- 5-9 x 3-5.2 cm, 1.7-2 times as long as wide, at base abruptly decurrent into pul- vinule, broadly rounded and emarginate at apex; midrib forwardly displaced to divide blade +/- 1:1.5, gently incurved, plane ven- trally, prominulously carinate dorsally, the stronger secondary nerves +/-10-14 on each side, incurved-ascending from midrib at +/-  40º, the coarse reticular venules forming areoles 0.5 mm diam. or less. Efoliate branches of panicle +/- 1-2 dm, the ultimate floriferous branchlets sessile, 10-23 mm, 7- 24-flowered; bracts suborbicular, +/- 2 mm, dorsally subglabrous verruculose, caducous from narrow ledge long before anthesis, shortly densely pubescent dorsally at mid- dle but glabrous around margin; flower-buds subspherical-pyriform; hypanthium less than 1 mm tall, solid; sepals 4, suborbicular 5 mm diam., the adaxial and abaxial pair exterior in vemation, all densely white-velutinous on both faces except for a narrow glabrous border internally; petals 5, mem- branous, whitish, minutely punctate, oblanceolate, +/- 4-5 x 1.5 mm, erose, glabrous, caducous; stamens 10, the filaments ? 6 mm, the elliptic dorsifixed anthers 1.5-1.6 x 0.9-1 mm, yellow; ovary sessile, inserted centrally at level of androecium, in profile 2.5 x 2 mm, densely white-velutinous overall, faintly 2-3-ridged vertically on each face, the glabrous style 2.1-2.4 mm, the capitate stigma 0.6 mm diam. Fruit samaroid, plano-compressed, in profile obliquely elliptic orbicular +/- 2.6-3 x 2.3-2.5 cm, the narrowly winged ventral suture 1.7-2.2 cm long, low-convex and describing a little less than 1/3 periphery of the fruit, its wing dilated upward and +/- 1.5-2 mm wide at base of style, the dorsal suture narrowly ribbed but not winged, the dull brown, stiffly coriaceous valves glabrescent, intricately low venulose, thinly resin dotted; seed 1, plumply discoid, +/- 15 mm diam., the hard testa smooth, tan, the shallowly lobed aril +/- 4 mm diam.

description: Subshrub; stems erect, to 1 m tall, ca 5 mm in diameter at 15 cm below the apex, reddish, densely white-sericeous near the apex, brownish-gray and glabrescent below, the internodes 1-2 cm long. Leaves nearly equal in a pair; blades elliptic to obovate, subfalcate, 8-15 cm long, 3-6 cm wide, membranous, the apex acute to acuminate, the base acute or cuneate, oblique, above dark gray-green, strigose, below lighter green, pilose to hirsute; petioles 2-5 cm long, 2 mm thick, dark green or reddish, villous. Inflorescences congested in the upper axils, cymose; peduncles very short or lacking; bracts lanceolate, ca 1.5 cm long, 2 mm wide, serrulate, pinkish, sericeous; pedicels to 7 mm long, pink, sericeous. Flowers with the calyx lobes equal, erect, free to the base, lanceolate, 1.0-1.2 cm long, 2-3 mm wide at the base, pink, seri- ceous except for glabrous base inside; corolla white, nearly erect in the calyx, the tube subarcuate, 1.9 cm long, slightly gibbous at the base, ca 4 mm in diameter, subventricose above the middle, ca 7 mm in diameter, slightly constricted at the throat, outside sericeous, inside glandular especially at the throat, the limb spreading, the lobes suborbicular, the lateral and basal lobes 4 mm long and wide, the upper lobes 2-3 mm long, the margins suberose; stamens included, the filaments 1 cm long, adnate to the base of the corolla tube for ca 4 mm, flattened, ca 1 mm wide, pilose at the base, above free, terete, glabrous, coiling after anthesis, the anthers broader than long, 1 mm long, 2 mm wide; disc reduced to a single deeply bilobed posterior gland; ovary ovoid, strigillose, the style 1.3 cm long, red, glabrous, the stigma scoop-shaped, erose. Fruits and seeds not seen.

description: Herb or subshrub; stems erect to decumbent, the upright part ca 20 cm tall, becoming woody below and rooting at the nodes, slender, ca 3 mm in diameter above, to 5 mm below, reddish, sparsely villous. Leaves nearly equal in a pair; blades lanceolate, narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate, 7-17 cm long, 1.2-3.5 cm wide, membranous, the apex acute to acuminate, the base cuneate, somewhat oblique, the margins sharply serrate to double-serrate, above green, sparsely villous, below lighter green, sparsely villous, the hairs more dense along the midvein; petioles slender, elongated, 1.5-5.0 cm long, reddish brown, sparsely hirsute. Inflorescences axillary, cymose, 4-6-flowered; peduncles ca 5 mm long, reddish, glandular; bracts linear, ca 1-5 cm long, serrulate, ciliate; pedicels slender, ca 6 mm long, green or reddish, glandular. Flowers showy; calyx lobes distinct to the base, subulate or lanceolate, ca 2 cm long, ca 1 mm wide at base, the margins remotely serrulate, reddish, ciliate; corolla white with a purplish area ("eye") and with purplish veins, the tube oblique in the calyx, ca 3 cm long, with a 3 mm long spur at the base, infundibuliform, 2-3 mm in diameter at the base, ampliate above, ca 1 cm wide, outside sparsely villous, inside glabrous; stamens included, the filaments adnate to base of the corolla for ca 5 mm, the free part ca 2.5 cm long, yellow and sparsely pubescent below, reddish above, glabrous, the anthers ca 1 mm long, coherent in 2 pairs by their apices, the locules divergent, the connective reddish; disc reduced to a single posterior gland; ovary villous apically, the style reddish, pilose, the stigma bilobed. description: Epiphytic herbs; stems very short, 2-5 cm long, 1 cm thick, appearing rhizomatous but fibrous rooted, rugose, purplish or brown, strigillose toward the apex, glabrous below. Leaves very unequal in a pair; larger blade of a pair elongate-elliptic, 19-27 cm long, 7-11 cm wide, very thin, the apex acuminate, the base decurrent into the petiole, the margins dentate, above green, sparsely appressed-pilose, below green to brownish pink, appressed-pilose or strigillose along the veins; petioles 2-6 cm long, pilose; smaller leaf of a pair reduced to a linear bract, 1-2 cm long. Inflorescences in the axils of the uppermost leaves, the flowers several in a dense cyme atop the pedun- cle; peduncles erect, elongate, 10-14 cm long, 1-2 mm in diameter, reddish, nearly glabrous; bracts linear-lanceolate, 1.0-1.7 cm long, reddish or green, sparsely pilose; pedicels short, 0.3-1.0 cm long, sparsely pilose. Flowers with the calyx lobes erect, shortly connate at the base, lanceolate, 7-9 mm long, 2 mm wide at the middle, green, glabrous except pilose on the margins, the apex acuminate, remotely serrate; corolla white, cream to rose, or reddish, usually darker at the limb, and reddish lines in the throat, the tube narrowly funnel-form, to 2.5 cm long, the base slightly gibbous, 4 mm in diameter at the base, from a point 7 mm above abruptly broader to 9 mm in diameter, outside long-pilose, inside glandular, the lobes spreading, semiorbicular, each ca 4 mm long and 6 mm wide, entire; stamens included, the filaments adnate to the base of the corolla tube for 7 mm, the free part ca 7 mm long, contorted, yellow, glabrous, the anthers coherent, broadly and shortly sagittate, ca 1 mm long and wide, darker on back, not bearded; disc reduced to a single posterior gland; ovary narrowly ovoid, 2-3 mm long, appressed-pilose, the style ca 1.4 cm long, sparsely pilose, the stigma narrowly stomatomorphic. Capsule ovoid, 5 mm long; seeds fusiform, ca 0.5 mm long, longitudinally striate, dark reddish brown, attached to a white funicle.

description: Frutex scandens, partibus junioribus plus minusve pubeseentibus (floribus ignotis), ramis teretibus, glabris, in sieco longitudinaliter striatis, purpureo-brunneis; foliis 3-foliolatis, petiolo eirciter 7 cm. longo, glabro, linea pubeseente supra excepta; foliolis firmiter chartaceis vel subcoriaceis, integris, ovatis vel elliptico-ovatis, lateralibus leviter inaequilateralibus, supra, costa breviter pubeseens excepta, glabris, in sieco olivaceis, subnitidis, subtus pallidioribus (pallide brunineis vel aliquantum subglaucis), glabris, breviter acuminatis, basi late rotundatis vel lateralibus leviter obscure cordatis, 7-9 cm. longis. 4-5.5 cm. latis, nervis primariis utrinque 4-5, adscendentibus, subtus cum reticulis laxis elevatis perspicuis arcuato-anastomosantibus, petiolulis 9-12 mm. longis, leviter pubeseentibus; infloreseentiis axillaribus, solitariis, sub fructu 4-8 cm. longis, pedunculatis (pedunculo 1-4 cm. longo), breviter pubeseentibus, ramis primariis paucis, ad 1 cm. longis; fruetibus bialatis bicarinatisque, eirciter 2.5 cm. longis cum alis 5.5 em. latis, glabris vel junioribus breviter pubeseentibus, alis chartaceo-coriaceis, sursum vix vel leviter angustatis, latissime rotundatis, brunneis, nitidis, striatis, eirciter 2.5 cm. longis latisque, carinis acutis, haud productis.

description: Trees or shrubs, 10-30 m tall, and to 4 (rarely 8) dm in diameter. Bark light or dark gray-brown when young, becoming smooth ashy-gray or nearly white, or often light or dark gray-brown and divided by shallow fissures and separated on the surface into small thin plates. Twig reddish-brown, becoming light gray, glabrate, sometimes with slight fetid odor when bruised; buds conic and acute-acuminate; outer bud scales keeled, minutely apiculate, with margins ciliate. Leaf of 5-7 leaflets; petiole 5-15 cm long. Leaflets 6-16 cm long, 2-6 cm wide, oblong-obovate or elliptic-obovate; apex acute, acuminate, or prolonged acuminate; base acute or acuminate; miargin unequally serrate, crenate-serrate or serrulate, often entire near the base; lower surface glabrous (with scattered hairs on the veins) to tomentose or woolly, dark green, pale or glauceseent; petiolule 0-11 mm long. Inflorescence 10-15 cm long, glabrous or densely pubescent. Flower pale yellow or greenish-yellow; pedicel 2-5 mm long. Calyx campanulate, 3-8 mm long, villous, the 5 lobes rounded, obtuse and subequal. Corolla of 4 nearly equal petals, 10-19 mm long; upper petals with a villous claw half the blade length and equaling the calyx, the blade oblong-spatulate and narrower than the blade of the lateral petal, villous, eglandular; lateral petals with a short villous claw, the blade broad, ovate or oblong. Stamens 7, exserted, 15-23 mm long, longest in the staminate flower; filaments arcuate, villous on the proximal half; anthers orange, slightly pubescent at top and bottom, minutely glandular at the apex and base of the locules. Fertile pistil glandular-villous on the ovary, the style villous. Fruit ovoid or obovoid, 2-5 cm in diameter; pericarp tuberculate-spiny, the spines often deciduous or rarely lacking, pale brown; seeds 1-3 (rarely 4-6), 2-4 cm in diameter, dark chestnutbrown with a small pale hilum.

description: Liana, glabrous throughout, the branchlets subterete or faintly quadrangular, cinereous or brownish; petioles 5-8 mm. long; leaf- blades papyraceous, brownish or greenish when dried, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 8-11 cm. long, 3-5.5 cm. broad, obtuse at base, obtuse or obtusely short-cuspidate at apex, undulate or crenulate (crenations 2 or 3 per centimeter, blunt) at margins, the costa elevated or nearly plane above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 7-9 per side, arcuate-aseending, conspicuously prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets copiously reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces; inflorescence 2.5-5 cm. long, forming a eluster up to 7 cm. in diameter, the peduncle slender, often obscurely quadrangular, 5-20 mm. long, the branchlets resembling the peduncle, subtended at each node by a pair of bracts (bracts ovate-oblong, 1-2 mm. long, conspicuously erose); flowers 10-11 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the bracteoles ovate, erosulous, the pedicels slender, 3-6 mm. long; sepals papyraceous, semiorbicular, 1.3-1.5 mm. long, 2-2.2 mm. broad, rounded at apex, erosul- ous at margins; petals carnose, elliptic-oblong or ovate-lanceolate, 5-5.5 mm. long, 2.5-3 mm. broad, rounded at apex, conspicuously serrate at margins (teeth 4-7 per millimeter, often irregularly paired); disk 1.7-2 mm. in diameter, about 0.5 mm. high, entire at margin and flattened or rounided (not grooved) on apex; filaments thin-earnose, 0.8-1 mm. long, slightly broadened toward base, the anthers about 0.6 mm. long and 1-1.2 mm. broad; ovary about 1 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style about 0.5 mm. long; fruits up to 15 cm. in diameter, the capsules connate at basal margins for 45-50 mm., oblong-deltoid, 7-8 cm. long and broad, often conspicuously emarginate at apex (sinus 5-8 mm. deep), the pericarp about 0.2 mm. thick distally and 0.5 mm. thick toward base; seeds immature but apparently 10-14 per capsule.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Liana, the branchlets elongate, cinereous, lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles stout, rugose, 8-12 mm. long, the leaf- blades coriaceous, brownish when dried and finely rugulose beneath, elliptic-oblong, 9-17 cm. long, 4-8 cm. broad, rounded or obtuse at base, obtusely short-cuspidate at apex, inconspicuously undulate- crenlliate at margins (crenulations about 1 per centimeter), the costa conspicuous on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 7 or 8 per side, erecto-patent, essentially plane (or faintly prominulous or impressed) above, conspicuously prominulous beneath, the veinlets immersed, obseure; infloreseence 1.2-3 cm. lonlg after anthesis, apparently compactly thyrsoid-paniculate and divided to base; flowers (detached in our specimens) 2-2.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, less than 1 mm. long; sepals papyraceous, deltoid, 0.4-0.6 mm. long and broad, obtuse, minutely erosulous; petals erecto-patent, submembranous or papyraceous, obovate-oblong, 1.6-1.8 mm. long, 0.8-1 mm. broad, subentire or minutely erosulous at margins; disk thin-carnose, about 0.2 mm. high and 1 mm. in diameter; filaments 0.7-0.8 mm. long; anther-locules divergent at base, about 0.2 mm. long, dehiscing by longitudinal oblique clefts, the connective not produced beyond locules; ovary depressed-subglobose, the style minute, the stigmas obseure; immature fruits usually 1 per infloreseence, ellipsoid, up to 17 mm. long and 10 mm. broad, the pericarp coriaceous, smooth, less than 0.5 mm. thick, the seeds apparently several, imbedded in pulp.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Slender tree with scandent branches, the branchlets slender, cinereous or greenish; leaves opposite, the petioles slender, 7-10 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, greenish or brown when dried, lanceolate-oblong or narrowly elliptic, 4-10 cm. long, 1.3-3.3 cm. broad, acute or attenuate at base and decurrent on the petiole, acute or bluntly cuspidate at apex, entire and slightly thickened at margins, the costa sharply elevated on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-9 per side, ascending, immersed or faintly impressed on both surfaces, the veinlets immersed; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, fasciculate, 2-6-flowered, the peduncle gemmiform, the bracts crowded, minute; flowers 6-8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, 2-4 mm. long; sepals submembranous, often conspicuously glandular-punctate or -reticulate, broadly deltoid-ovate, 1-2.4 mm. long, 1.5-2.7 mm. broad, rounded at apex, entire or minutely ciliolate at margins; petals similar to sepals in texture, oblong or elliptic-oblonig, 2.6-5 mm. long, 1.7-4 mm. broad, entire and often narrowly revolute at margins; disk 2.2-2.4 mm. in diameter, 0.4-0.7 mm. high, rounded or inconspicuously narrowed at outer margin-; stamens suberect, the filaments 0.5-1.3 mm. long, the anthers transversely ellipsoid, 0.4-0.6 mm. long, 0.5-0.9 mm. broad, dehiscing by horizontal apical confluent clefts; ovary conical, the style 0.5-0.8 mm. long; ovules 2 per locule, superposed.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Shrub or small tree, the branchlets opposite or alternate or dichotomously arranged, cinereous, often lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles slender, 4-9 mm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceous, brownish or olivaceous when dried, elliptic or slightly ovate- or obovate-elliptic, (4.5-)6-12 cm. long, (2-)3-6 cm. broad, acute or subattenuate at base, obtuse or acute at apex, conspicuously crenate-serrate at margins (serrations 2-4 per centimeter, often mueronulate or spinulose), the costa slightly raised above, prominent benleath, the secondary nerves 6-9 per side, erecto-patent, essentially plane or faintly prominulous above, strongly prominulous beneath, the veinlets conspicuously reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces or immersed above; inflorescence compact, axillary, not exceeding 1.5 cm. in length (including flowers), short-peduneulate (peduncle slender, 2-5 nim. long), simple or once dichotomously branched, the bracts paired, papyraceous, ovate, subacute, 1-1.5 mm. long; flowers paired, 2 or 4 per infloreseence, 10-15 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, 3-5 mm. long, often subtended by 2 small bracteoles; sepals papyraceous, glandular-reticulate within, ovate or broadly ovate, 1.3-2 mm. long, 2-3 mm. broad, rounded at apex, entire and often slightly inflexed at margins; petals submembrancous or thin-papyraceous, densely and often conspicuously glandular-lineolate, broadly obovate, 5.5-7 mm. long, 5-6.5 mm. broad, minutely erosulous at margins; disk 2-2.3 mm. in diameter, conispicuously elevated and about 0.6 mm. high at inner margin, flattened at outer margin (outer margin entire or slightly undulate, plane or somewhat upcurved, less than 0.5 mm. broad); stamens sharply reflexed, the filaments often glandular-lineolate, 0.7-1 mm. long, the anthers transversely ellipsoid, about 0.2 mm. long and 0.7 mm. broad, dehiscing by horizontal extrorse-apical confluent clefts; ovary produced into a short conical truneate style, the stigmas obseure or connate into a minute deltoid shield and alternate with stamens; ovules 6-8 per locule, in 2 collateral ranks; fruits (ex Miers) large, ovate, at length yellowish, up to 9 cm. long and 6 cm. in diameter (ex Vellozo), the pericarp very thick (about 6 mm.), smooth or verruculose, the seeds 10-12, ovate, up to 15 mm. lonig and 10 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Liana, the branchlets cinereous or brownish, densely lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles slender, 13-20 mm. long, the leaf-blades thin-coriaceous, brownish when dried, elliptic-oblong, 8-14 cm. long, 4-5.5 cm. broad, rounded or obtuse at base, obtusely short-acuminate at apex, slightly undulate or obscurely crenate and thickened at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 10-13 per side, spreading, anastomosing near margins, conspicuously prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces; inflorescence axillary or arising from old branchlets, fascieulate, 2-8-flowered, the peduncle gemmiform, the bracts numerous, coriaceous, deltoid, minute; flowers 6-7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels (4-8 mm. long) and calyx densely farinose-ceriferous; sepals papyraceous or thin-coriaceous, broadly reniform-ovate, 1.3-1.5 mm. long, 3-3.5 mm. broad, rounded, entire, faintly nerved; petals thin-carnose, obovate- or oblong-spatulate, 3-3.5 mm. long and broad, entire and seariose at margins; disk 2.5-3 mm. in diameter, about 1 mm. high, ineurved toward apex, thinner than high, adnate to ovary by interstaminal septae; stamens reflexed, the filaments 0.8-1 mm. long, the anthers transversely oblong, about 0.2 by 0.5 mm., dehiscing by horizontal subapical confluent clefts; ovary immersed, the style carnose, 0.4-0.5 mm. long; ovules 8 per locule, 2-ranked.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Shrub or slender tree, the branches probably subscandent, the branchlets cinereous or brownish, sparsely lenticellate; leaves alternate, the petioles 4-10 (-16) mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, brownish or olivaceous when dried, elliptic-oblong, 6-17 cm. long, 1.8-8(-10) cm. broad, rounded or obtuse at base, rounded or emarginate at apex, slightly thickened and undulate at margins, the costa sharply elevated on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-9 per side, ascending or arcuate-aseendin-g, plalne or failntly impressed oni both surfaces, the veinlets obscure, usually immersed; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, fasciculate, the peduncle gemmiform, the bracts minute; flowers 3-4.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, usually 4-8 per infloreseence, sometimes crowded and up to 20, subsessile, the pedicels 1.5-2 mm. long; sepals papyraceous, broadly ovate or deltoid, 1-1.3 mm. lolng, 1.3-2.2 mm. broad, rounded or obtuse at apex, seariose and usually conspicuously fimbriolate at margins (cilia up to 0.7 mm. long); petals submembranous or thin-carniose, oblong-elliptic or suborbicular, 1.8-2.6 mm. long, 1.5-2.6 mm. broad, subentire and usually narrowly revolute at margins, often obscurely glandular-reticulate; disk carnose or thin-carnose, cupuliform or short-tubular, 1.2-1.6 mm. in diameter, 0.25-0.4 mm. high (thinner than high), entire or crenulate at apical margin; stamens erecto-patent, the filaments 0.5-1.1 mm. long, the anthers deltoid or ovate-oblong, 0.2-0.5 mm. long. 0.4-0.6 mm. broad, dehiscing by oblique extrorse-lateral apically confluent clefts; ovary 0.5-1 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style 0.3-0.5 mm. long; ovules 2 or 4 per locule, superposed or 2-ranked; fruiting pedicels very short, swollen (about 4 mm. in diameter), the fruits 1 or 2 per inflorescence, ellipsoid or obovoid, up to 2 cm. long and 1.5 cm. broad, obtuse at base and apex, the pericarp coriaceous, rugose.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Liana, the branchlets brownish, often densely lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles 6-14 mm. long, the leaf-blades thin-coriaceous, brownish when dried, oblonig- or obovate-elliptic, 11-18 cm. long, 4.5-8 cm. broad, obtuse to acute at base, short-acuminate or cuspidate at apex (acumen 4-10 mm. long, obtuse, often callose-thickened), entire and slightly revolute at margins, black-punctate beneath, the costa elevated above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 8-11 per side, straight, erecto-patent, prominulous above, strongly elevated beneath, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous or obscure on both surfaces; infloreseence axillary, paniculate, 3-4 cm. long at anthesis, the peduncle short, often subtended by numerous closely imbricate coriaceous bracts, the branchlets straight, usually opposite, subtended by bracts about 1.5 mm. long; flowers numerous, 3-4 mm. in diameter at anthesis, solitary at apices of ultimate branchlets; pedicels slender, 1-2 mm. long (above articulation with ultimate branchlets); sepals thin-coriaceous, deltoid-ovate, about 1 mm. long and 1.3 mm. broad, sub-acute or obtuse at apex, entire or erosulous at margins; petals thin-carnose, oblong, 1.8-2 mm. long, 1.2-1.5 mm. broad, erosulous or fimbriolate at margins; disk about 1.8 mm. in diameter, conspicuously elevated and about 0.4 mm. high at inner margin, flattened at outer margin; stamens sharply recurved, the filaments 0.7-0.9 mm. long, the anthers transversely ellipsoid, about 0.2 by 0.3 mm., dehiscing by horizontal apical confluent clefts; ovary about 0.8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style about 0.6 mm. long; ovules 2 per locule, collateral- superposed.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Slender tree with scandent branches (or liana ?), the branchlets slender, lenticellate; leaves alternate, the petioles 5-10 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, brownish or olivaceous when dried, niarrowly elliptic-oblong, 8-15 em. long, 1.5-5 em. broad, obtuse or acute at base, gradually narrowed to an acute or obtuse apex, conispieuously thickened and often obsoletely callose-serrulate at margins, the costa prominient on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 8-12 per side, ascending, arcuate and inconspieuously anastomosing near margins, plane or fainitly impressed on both surfaces, the veinlets immersed; inflorescence axillary, fascieulate, the peduncle gemmiform, the bracts minute; flowers 4-5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, crowded, up to 20 per inflorescence, subsessile (pedicels up to 2 mm. long, sometimes glaucous); sepals papyraceous or thin-coriaceous, broadly ovate, 1-1.7 mm. long, 1.7-2.6 mm. broad, rounded at apex, seariose and conspicuously fimbriolate at margins (cilia up to 0.4 mm. long, sometimes lacking on inner sepals) ; petals submembranous or thin-carnose, oblong-elliptic or suborbicular, 2.2-3.5 mm. long, 2-2.7 mm. broad, subentire and often narrowly reflexed at margins; disk annnlar-pulvinate or cupuliform, 1.4-2 mm. in diameter, 0.4-0.5 mm. high (thinner than high), entire at apical margin; stamens suberect, the filaments 1-1.3 mm. long, the anthers broadly deltoid-ovate, 0.5-0.6 mm. long, 0.6-0.8 mm. broad, dehiscing by oblique extrorse-lateral apically confluent clefts; ovary subconical, the style 0.4-0.8 mm. long; ovules 2 per locule, superposed.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Liana (?), the bralnchlets einereous, slender, lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles slender, 4-8 mm. long, the leaf- blades coriaceous, brownish when dried, paler belneath, oblong-elliptic, 6-8.5 cm. long, 2-4 cm. broad, acute or subatteniuate at base, obtusely short-cuspidate at apex, enitire anid slightly revolute at margins; the costa strongly raised on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-8 per side, spreading, iniconspicuously anastomosinig, prominulous onl botb surfaces or nearly plane above, the veinlets obscurely reticulate, immersed or faintly prominulous; inflorescence axillary, 2-4 cm. long at anithesis, 3- or 4-times dichotomously branched, the peduncle up to 1 cm. long, the branchlets slender, the bracts papyraceous, ovate, acute, about 0.7 mm. long; flowers in ultimate dichotomies or paired at ends of ultimate branchlets, 3-4.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the bracteoles minute, the pedicels slender, 1-3 mm. long; sepals carnose or subcoriaceous, deltoid-ovate, 0.4-0.6 mm. long, 0.8-1 mm. broad, obtuse or rounded at apex, entire and sometimes narrowly seariose at margins; petals thin-carnose, elliptic-oblong, 1.5-1.7 mm. long, 1-1.3 mm. broad, entire and often narrowly reflexed at margins; disk 1.2-1.6 mm. in diameter, elevated and about 0.4 mm. high at inner margin, conspicuously flattened and projecting beyond petal-bases at outer margin; stamens sharply recurved, the filaments membranous, 0.5-0.7 mm. long, the anthers transversely ellipsoid, about 0.2 by 0.3 mm., dehiscinlg by extrorse oblique apically confluelnt clefts; ovary about 0.8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style inconspicuous, less than 0.2 mm. long; ovules 2 per locule, collateral-suspended; fruits subglobose, faintly trigonous, up to 5 cm. in diameter, the pericarp coriaceous, faintly rugulose, the seeds several.

description: Liana, the branehlets slender, sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles stout, 3-5 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, greenish, glaucous beneath when dried, linear-oblong, 5-18 cm. long, 1-4 cm. broad, rounded or cordate at base, obtusely apiculate or rounded at apex, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 9-14 per side, spreading, usually prominulous on both surfaces, occasionally subimmersed; infloreseence and flowers essentially similar to those of S. Wrightii; fruits probably solitary, borne on swollen pedicels to 3 mm. in diameter, narrowly ellipsoid, up to 4 cm. long and 1.5 cm. broad, narrowed toward base, obtuse at apex, the pericarp coriaceous, strongly rugose.

description: Shrub or slender tree up to 7 m. high, the branclhlets elongate, slender, sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles stout, 13-20 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, smooth and shining above, olivaceous when dried, narrowly oblong, 20-27 cm. long, 5-8 cm. broad, rounded or obtuse at base, obtusely short-acuminate at apex, entire and slightly revolute at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 8-12 per side. arcuate-ascending, usually prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets immersed or faintly impressed beneath; infloreseence arising from defoliate branchlets, fasciculate, the peduncle gemmiform, the bracts crowded, minute; flowers 5-8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, 5-7 mm. long; sepals thin-carnose, oblong or ovate-deltoid, 1-1.3 mm. long, about 1 mm. broad, rounded, entire; petals rotate or reflexed at anthesis, thin-carnose, ovate-oblong, 2.2-2.6 mm. long, 2-2.3 mm. broad, entire; disk about 2 mm. in diameter and 0.5 mm. high, rounded or inconspicuously narrowed at outer margin; stamens suberect, the filaments 0.8-1 mm. long, the anthers transversely ellipsoid, about 0.15 by 0.25 mm., dehiscing by horizontal apical confluent clefts; ovary conical, the style about 0.4 mm. long; ovules 4 per locule, in superposed pairs.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Tree to 8 m. high, the branehlets stout, greenish brown, copiously lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles stout (4-5 mm. in diameter), stronigly rugose, flattened above, 25-32 mm. lonig, the leaf-blades chartaceous, olivaceous when dried, elliptic-oblong, 25-37 cm. long, 10-14 cm. broad, obtuse or acute at base, probably acute at apex (good speci- menis not seen), entire and narrowly revolute at margins, the costa strongly raised above, prominenit beneath, the secondary nerves 11-13 per side, ascending, straight, inconspicuously anastomosing near margins, prominulous above, sharply elevated beneath, the veinlets horizontally reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces or nearly plane above; infloreseeniee arising from defoliate branchlets, 1.5-2.5 cm. long, compactly paniculate, the peduncle short, the primary rachis stout, the branchlets alterlnate and distally pseudo-dichotomously several times branched, the bracts and bracteoles papyraceous, ovate, about 0.5 mm. long; flowers arranged in small clusters at apices of ultimate branchlets, 3-3.5 mm. in diameter at alnthesis, the pedicels slender, about 1 mm. long; sepals membranous, ovate-deltoid, 1-1.2 mm. lon-g, 1-1.5 mm. broad, cuspidate or subacute at apex, subentire or erosulous at margins; petals thin-carnose, pink, orange-tinged, elliptic-oblong, 1.5- 1.8 mm. long, 1.3-1.5 mm. broad, subacute or obtuse at apex and re- flexed in the apical 0.5 mm., irregularly transversely tubereulate within toward apex, seariose and subentire or minutely erosulous at margins, profusely but inconspicuously glandular-punctate or -lineolate; disk conical-pulviniate, 1-1.2 mm. in diameter at base, niarrowed to 0.3 mm. in diameter at apex, 0.5-0.6 mm. high, submembranous dis- tally and produced into 3 subacute deltoid teeth about 0.1 mm. long alternate with stamens, completely elnveloping ovary, faintly pentago- nous at base; stamens sharply reflexed, the filaments membranous, filiform-ligulate, about 1 mm. long, the anthers oblong, about 0.1 mm. lonig and broad, dehiscing by horizontal apical confluent clefts; ovary immersed in disk anid connate to it, about 0.6 mm. in diameter at alithesis, the style filiform-subulate, 0.8-1 mm. long, truneate or minutely capitate at apex; ovules 2 per locule, collateral.

description: Liana (?) ; branchlets slender, terete; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles slender, 4-6 cm. long, the leaf-blades papyraceous or chartaceous, dark green when dried, oblong or obovate-oblong, 7-11 cm. long, 2.5-4 cm. broad, obtuse at base, abruptly short-acuminate at apex (acumen broad, 5-13 mm. long, obtuse), entire at margins, the costa prominent oni both surfaces, the secondary nerves 7-10 per side, spreading or slightly arcuate, anastomosing toward margins, faintly prominulous above, conspicuously so beneath, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces; infloreseence 1.5-3 cm. long at anthesis, divided essentially to base, dichotomously 2-4-times branched, the branehlets very slender, stramineous, the bracts ovate, acute, about 0.5 mm. long; flowers loosely arranged in elusters of 2-4 near apices of ultimate branchlets, 2.2-2.7 mm. in diameter, the pedicels slender, 1.5-2 mm. long at anthesis; sepals membranous, oblong-deltoid, 0.6-0.9 mm. long and broad, rounded or obtuse, subeiitire and narrowly reflexed at margins; petals miembranous, yellow, oblong, 1-1.2 mm. long, 0.6-0.7 mm. broad, rounded at apex, entire and often narrowly reflexed at margins; disk thin-earnose, erect or slightly spreading, about 0.2 mm. high, 0.8-1 mm. in diameter, entire at margin, thicker at apex than at base; stamens suberect or spreading, the filaments submembranous, 0.3-0.4 mm. long, the anthers about 0.1 by 0.3 mm., dehiscing by confluent horizontal apical clefts; ovary conical, about 0.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style about 0.3 mm. long, truncate; ovules 2 per locule, superposed.

description: Liana ( ?) ; branchlets elongate, slender, terete; leaves opposite (rarely subopposite) ; petioles rugose, stout, 7-10 mm. long; leaf-blades thin-coriaceous or chartaceous, brownish or dark green when dried, lanceolate-oblong, 9-15 cm. long, 2-4.7 cm. broad, attenuate at base and decurrent on the petiole, gradually narrowed to an obtuse or sub- acute or short-cuspidate apex, crenate-serrate and minutely revolute at margins (serrations 1 or 2 per centimeter), the costa sharply raised above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 7-10 per side, sharply aseending, prominulous on both surfaces or essentially plane above, the veinlets usually prominulous-reticulate, sometimes essentially plane above; infloreseence 1.5-3 cm. long, thyrsoid-paniculate (branchlets alteriiate or subopposite, the main rachis not distinguishable), several times branched, the peduncle stout, less than 3 mm. long, the bracts aild bracteoles oblong, acute, less than 1 mm. long; flowers sessile, each sub- tended by a cupule of 3 minute bracteoles; sepals semiorbicular-ovate, about 1 mm. long and broad, rounded, subentire or obseurely glandular- serrulate at margins; petals oblolig-obovate, about 0.8 mm. long, 1.3-1.6 mm. broad, rounded, entire; disk submembranous, erect, about 0.2 mm. high and 1.2 mm. in diameter, entire; stamens suberect, the filaments about 0.8 mm. long, the anthers about 0.2 by 0.4 mm.; ovary subtrigo- nous-globose, about 0.6 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style often faintly suleate, abouit 0.3 mm. long, the stigmas entire, deltoid, obtuse, about 0.3 mm. long, alternate with stamens; ovules 4 per locule, in collateral superposed pairs.

description: Liana, the bralnches terete, stout, conspicuously anid copiously lenticellate, the branchlets subterete; leaves opposite, the petioles rugose, stout, 11-13 mm. long, the leaf-blades coriaceous, olivaceous above when dried, brownish beneath, obovate or obovate-elliptic, 8-14 cm. long, 4.5-7.5 cm. broad, cuneate at base, rounded or bluntly short cuspidate at apex, entire and narrowly revolute at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, terminating in apex, the secondary nerves 8-11 per side, spreading, ascending and anastomosing near margins, conspicuously prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets obscurely reticulate, often faintly prominulous; flowers subsessile, congested, about 3.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis; sepals papyraceous, ovate-deltoid, 0.6- 0.9 mm. long, about 1 mm. broad, rounded, narrowlly seariose, erosulous or irregularly fimbriolate at margins; petals submembranous, obovateoblong, 2-2.2 mm. long, 1-1.5 mm. broad, rounded at apex, minutely erosulous at margins, sometimes obscurely puberulent distally without; disk thin-carnose, erecto-patent, 0.2-0.4 mm. high, subentire or undulate at margin; description: Liana, the branchlets cinereous or brownish, often- conspicuously pale-lenticellate; petioles 4-9 mm. long, the leaf-blades papyraceous or chartaceous, elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 6-11 (occasionally 4-13) cm. long, 2-6 em. broad, acute or obtuse at base, acute or gradually acumi- nate at apex (acumen 3-10 mm. long, obtuse or minutely apiculate), subentire or obscurely crenate at margins (crenations about 2 per cen- timeter), the costa elevated above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 6-9 (-12) per side, erecto-patent, arcuate and anastomosing near nmargins, conspicuously prominulous on both surfaces; inflorescence 1.5-4 cm. long, dichotomously branched, 3-5(-7)-times branched, the peduncle slender, subterete or faintly quadrangular, 5-12 m-m. long, the branches divaricate, the bracts opposite, ovate-oblong, 1-1.5 mm. long, subacute; flowers 2-4 nin-i. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels less than 1 mm. long; sepals niembranous, deltoid to broadly ovate, 0.5-0.8 mm. long, slightly broader, minutely erosulous or faintly glandular-ciliolate at margins; petals erecto-patent, thin-carnose or subniembranous, elliptic or oblong, 1.5-2.6 mm. long, 0.8-1.4 mm. broad, entire; disk 0.8-1.2 mm. in diameter, about 0.1 mm. thick; stamens suberect or spreading, the filaments 0.3-0.6 mm. long, gradually broadened toward base, the anthers about 0.2 by 0.3-0.4 mm.; ovary 0.5-0.7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style 0.2-0.4 mm. ]ong; ovules 2-6 per locule; fruiting pedicels about 1 mm. in diam'neter, the fruits 1-3 per infloreseence, the capsules elliptic, 3.5-5 cm. long, 1.5-2 cm. broad, about 2 mm. thick before dehiseence, subacute or obtuse at apex, the pericarp papyraceous, about 0.2 mm. thick, inconspicuously flabellate-costate without, smooth within; seeds usually 4 (probably sometimes 2-6), the embryoniferous portion flattened, obliquely ellip- soid, up to 15 mm. long and 6 mm. broad, the wing elliptic, up to 30 mm. long and 15 mm. broad.

description: Liana, the branchlets elongate, slender, einereous or brownish, lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles rugose, flattened above, 3-6 mm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceous or thin-coriaceous, conspicuously bullate, dark brown when dried, narrowly elliptic-oblong, 7-14 cm. long, 1.7-3.7 cm. broad, acute or attenluate at base, eaudate-acuminate at apex (acumen very slender, 1-2 mm. broad, 10- 20 mm. long, obtuse), obscurely crenulate at margins (obsolete teeth 5-7 per centimeter), the costa sharply prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 10-15 per side, spreading, conspicuously anas- tomosing near margins, conspicuously prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets obscurely reticulate, essentially plane or faintly prominulous; infloreseence 1.3-2 cm. long at anthesis, dichotomously or pseu- dodichotomously several times branched, divided to base or with a short slender pedunele, the branchlets slender, the bracts ovate, sub- acute, about 0.7 mm. long; flowers apparently solitary at apices of ultimate branchlets, 1.7-2 mm. in diameter at anthesis, each subtended by 2 minute bracteoles, the pedicels slender, 1-1.5 mm. long; sepals papyraceous, ovate-deltoid, 0.6-0.9 mm. long and broad, subacute at apex, narrowly seariose and erose-fimbriolate at margins; petals thin- carnose, oblong, about 1 mm. long and 0.5 mm. broad, obscurely erosulous distally at margins, sometimes minutely farinose-puberulent distally within; disk thin-carnose, 0.2-0.3 mm. long, about 0.6 mm. in diam- eter, undulate-crenulate at margin; filaments thin-carnose, 0.6-0.8 mm. long, gradually broadened toward base; anther-locules about 0.2 mm. long, dehiscing by slightly oblique extrorse-lateral clefts, the connective deltoid, obtuse, not produced beyond locules; ovary about 0.4 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style 0.2-0.3 mm. long, truncate or with an inconspicuous obscurely capitate stigmatic shield; ovules 2 per locule, collateral; fruiting infloreseence swollen, the pedicels greatly thickened, the fruits probably 1 per infloreseence, glaueous when young, obovoid-ellipsoid, the pericarp smooth.

description: Shrub or small tree; branchlets slender, elongate, at length einereous and usually conspicuously lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles slender, rugose, 5-12 mm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceous, brownish when dried, narrowly elliptic, 10-15 cm. long, 3.5-5 (rarely to 7) em. broad, attenuate to acute at base, acute to short-acuminate at apex (acumen gradually tapering to an obtuse or faintly emarginate or callose-apiculate apex), conspicuously crenate-serrate at margins (ser- rations about 2 per centimeter) and slightly thickened or faintly revo- lute, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 7-10 per side, arcuate-aseending, plane or faintly prominulous or slightly impressed above, conspicuously prominulous beneath, the veinlets usually immersed and obscure, occasionally prominulous beneath; in- florescence compact, 1-3 cm. long at anthesis, divided essentially to base or with a short peduncle, 3-6-times dichotomously branehed, the branchlets slender, usually closely hirsute with short stout ferruginous hairs, the internodes short, the bracts conspicuous, ovate, acute, usually fimbriolate, 1.5-2 mm. long, usually connate at base in pairs, rarely subopposite; flowers subsessile (pedicels less than 1 mm. long), con- gested in elusters of 3-5, each subtended by 1 or 2 inconspicuous brac- teoles; sepals papyraceous, semiorbicular to deltoid, 0.7-1 mm. long and broad, rounded at apex, narrowly seariose and subentire at mar- gins; petals submembranous, minutely but often conspicuously glandular-lineolate, obovate-ligulate, 2-2.8 mm. long, about 1 mm. broad, conspicuously narrowed distally, seariose and erosulous at margins; disk membranous, 0.4-0.5 mm. high, 1.2-1.4 mm. in diameter, crenulate at margin; filaments 0.7-1 mm. long; anther-locules about 0.3 mm. long, dehiseing by vertical clefts, the connective subacute, conspicu- ously produced, exceeding the anthers by 0.1-0.2 mm.; ovary less than 1 nmm. in diameter at anthesis, the style slender, 0.2-0.3 mm. long; ovrules 2 per locule, collaterally suspended; fruits depressed-globose, up to 4 cm. in diameter (ex Miers), the pericarp chartaceous, less than 1 mum. thick, the seeds 6, collaterally placed in a single series, probably imnbedded in sparse mucilaginous pulp, oval, aingular by mutual pres- sure, up to 1.3 cm. long and 1 cm. broad, the testa coriaceous.

description: Slender tree, the branches probably scandent, the branchlets slender, elongate, brownish, conspicuously tuberculate-scabrous; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles rugose, 4-12 mm. long, the leaf-blades papyraceous or thin-chartaceous, olivaceous or brownish and finely rugulose when dried, elliptic-oblong, 9-12 cm. long, 3.5-5 cm. broad, acute or subattenuate at base, obtusely short-acuminate at apex (acumen broad, 5-10 mm. long), crenate-serrate at margins (serrations conspicuous, 2 or 3 per centimeter), the costa often sharply elevated above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 5-7 per side, arcuate-ascending, obscurely anastomosing, essentially plane above, prominulous beneath, the veinlets obscurely reticulate, immersed or faintly prominulous; infloreseence 0.8-1.5 cm. long at anthesis, compactly thyrsoid-paniculate, the peduncle slender, often about 5 mm. long, with the few alternate branchlets minlutely tuberculate-scabrous, the bracts papyraceous, ovate, acute, about 1 mm. long; flowers few, loosely arranged, 2-2.7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, each subtended by 1-3 minute bracteoles, the pedicels slender, about 0.5 mm. long; sepals submembranous or papyraceous, ovate-deltoid, 0.6-1 mm. long and broad, obtuse at apex, narrowly seariose and entire at margins; petals suberect, thin-carnose, oblong, 1.3-1.6 mm. long, about 1 mm. broad, entire; disk submembranous, 0.3-0.5 mm. high, about 1.3 mm. in diameter, crenulate-undulate at margin; filaments 0.5 or more mm. long, gradually broadened toward base; anther-locules 0.5-0.6 mm. long, dehiscing by longitudinal extrorse clefts, the connective obtuse, not produeed beyond locules; ovary about 0.8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style about 0.4 mm. long; ovules 2 per locule, collateral.

description: Liana; branchlets cinereous, terete, striate; leaves opposite, the petioles nigreseent, rugose, 6-8 mm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceous, brownish when dried, elliptic- or ovate-oblong, 9-14 cm. long, 4-5.5 cm. broad, rounded or broadly obtuse at base, cuspidate at apex (acumen about 1 cm. long, obtuse, slightly callose), entire at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-8 per side, arcuate ascending, essentially plane above, prominulous beneath, the veinlets immersed, sometimes faintly discernible beneath; infloreseenee arising from defoliate branchlets, 6-8 cm. long at anthesis, thyrsoid-paniculate, often branehed to base, the branches and pedicels closely and minutely brown-tomentellous, the main branehes obvious, the branchlets alternate or subopposite, several times branched, the bracts and bracteoles oblong, less than 1 mm. long, soon deciduous; flowers 2-2.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, about 1 mm. long; sepals rotate, membranous, broadly ovate-deltoid, 0.3-0.4 mm. long, 0.7-0.9 mm. broad, rounded, entire and narrowly reflexed at margins; petals membranous, yellowish white, oblong-elliptic, 0.9-1.1 mm. long, about 0.8 mm. broad, rounded, entire and often narrowly reflexed at margins; disk thin-carnose, erect, 0.1-0.2 mm. high, 0.8-1 mm. in diameter, entire at iliargin, slightly thicker at apex than at base; stamens subspreading, the filaments membranous, 0.4-0.5 mm. long, the anthers about 0.1 by 0.2 mm., dehiscing by confluent horizontal apical clefts; ovary conical-trigonous, about 0.5 mm. in diameter at anthesis, gradually narrowed to a short carnose conical truncate style; ovules 2 per locule, superposed.

flowers 2.5-4 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, up to 1.5 mm. long; sepals submembranous, ovate-deltoid to semi- orbicular, 0.5-1 mm. long, 0.6-1.2 mm. broad, seariose and subentire or minutely erosulous at margins, sometimes glandular-punctate dis- tally within; description: Plantae annuae graciles erectae glanduloso-hispidulae 1-3.5 dm altae; foliis infimis oppositis eis ad apicem versus alternantibus lanceolatis vel ellipticis sub- integris petiolatis 1-5 cm longis 2-15 mm latis; floribus in cincinnis numerosis; sepalis subaequalibus lineari-oblanceolatis vix accrescentibus glanduloso-hispidulis 1.5-2 mm longis 0.3-0.5 mm latis; corolla dilute caerulea pelviformi tarde decidua, 4-5 mm longo calyce 1/2 longiore; marginibus liberis squamulorum jugorum vicinorum connatis; staminibus paulum exsertis glabris 5-7 mm longis; stylo paulum exserto basi glanduloso 4-5 mm longo, infra medium partito; capsula ovata valde complanata acuta 3-4 mm longa; semine solitario oblongo foveolato 1.5-2 mm longo  Annual, 1-3.5 dm tall from a slender taproot, bluish-green, sage-scented, glandular- hispidulous throughout; stems erect, branched from the base or above or simple. Lower leaves entire, opposite, the upper cauline leaves fairly numerous, alternate, lanceolate to elliptic, 1-5 cm long, 2-15 mm broad, entire or with 1-6 lateral teeth, tapering into a slender peiole. Flowers numerous in dense, often branched cymes, the cymes up to 1 dm long and erect in fruit; calyx lobes linear-oblanceolate, 1.5-2.5 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm broad, subequal, glandular-hispidulous, slightly enlarged (2.5- 3.5 mm long) in fruit; corolla very pale blue, pelviform, sparsely puberulent externally and internally, immediately above the scales, marcescent, 4-5 mm long, 3-3.5 mm broad, the lobes oval, ca. 2.5 mm long and 2 mm broad, the whole twice as long as the calyx; stamens exserted 2-3 mm, 6-7 mm long, the anthers oval, about 0.5 mm long, the filaments glabrous; scales lanceolate, the free edges connate; style a little exserted, 4-5 mm long, parted to below the middle and glandular at base, the tips lavender; capsule ovate, strongly flattened, 3-4 mm long, acute, hirsute; seed 1, oblong, 1.5-2 mm long, light brown, coarsely foveolate in definite rows; chromosome number 2n = 16.

description: Erect, virgate to variously branched annuals 1-6 dm tall; pubescence hirsute to hirtellous, with scattered uniseriate glandular hairs; leaves linear to elliptic, 1-7 cm long, the broader ones incised into 2-5 linear lobes; lower leaves tapering to a short petiole or sessile, the upper ones sessile; flowers borne in open eymes 2-15 cm long, the pedicels 2-5 mm long and ascending; calyx lobes lanceolate to oblanceolate, growing with and exceeding the capsule, reaching when mature a length of 8-15 mm; corolla 5-20 mm long, glabrous on both inner and outer surfaces, lavender to pale lavender, open-campanulate, cleft about 1/3 of its length into broad, rounded-truneate lobes; linear scales or flaps adnate to the lower half of the corolla tube, each scale or flap fused along one edge to a lateral vein, the free edge overlying the mid-vein, each pair overlying papillate, nectar-secreting epidermal cells; stamens slightly shorter than the corolla, the filaments with tapering non-glandular hairs along the distal third and with capitate, uniseriate glandular hairs along the proximal two-thirds; filament bases glabrous and free of the corolla scales; style equal to gtamens, cleft about 1/5 of its length, with glandular and non-glandular hairs on the undivided portion; capsule 6-10 mm long, acuminate, with dark brown to black reticulate-pitted seeds 1-1.5 mm long.

description: Annual, 2-30 cm in diameter from a slender taproot, bluish green, odorless, succulent, hispidulous and non-glandular throughout; stems prostrate, branching dichotomously near the base and becoming semi-dichotomous. Leaves mostly cauline, numerous, alternate, ovate-lanceolate to obliquely elliptic, the lamina 5-15 mm long, 3-8 mm broad, entire, tapering into a slender petiole as long as or longer than the blade. Flowers several in compact, leafy, axillary glomerules; calyx lobes linear, 1.5-2 mm long, ca. 0.3 mm broad, subequal, hispidulous, elongating slightly in fruit; corolla white with lavender midveins, tubular, deciduous, 1.5-2 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm broad, the upper tube and lobes pubescent on the back, the lobes oblong-oval, 0.3 mm long, 0.2 mm broad, the whole about 1/4 longer than the calyx; stamens included, somewhat unequal, 0.5-0.7 mm long, the anthers oval, ca. 0.2 mm long, the filaments glabrous; scales completely lacking; style included, 0.5 mm long, parted to the middle, glabrous; capsule ovoid, slightly flattened, 2-3 mm long, obtuse, hispidulous; seeds 4-7, oblong, angled, 1-1.5 mm long, dark brown, shallowly foveolate in indefinite rows; chromosome number 2n = 22.

description: Tree, 7-18 m tall; young twigs at first minutely fascicled-hairy, soon becoming mostly glandular-puberulent or pubescent; one year old twigs reddish brown, glandular-puberulent with dense but short hairs; older twigs grayish brown; pith light brown; terminal buds slender, whitish-tomentose; leaves mostly 30-37 cm long (up to 50 or even 64 cm), 18-27 cm broad; rachis at the very first tomentose, becoming almost at once glandular-pubescent or puberulent, and finally glabrate; leaflets mostly 14-16 (up to 18 or 20), ascending, opposite or alternate, sessile or nearly so, thin and not rugose, the larger ones ovate, ovate-lanceolate, or ovate-oblong, mostly about 11 cm long (8-16 cm) and 4.5 cm wide, (3-5 cm), rounded to subcordate at base, frequently oblique (apparently tapering at base in some leaflets, these probably young ones), abruptly acuminate at apex, finely serrate or denticulate, commonly 7 teeth per cm, mostly glabrate above, or glandular-puberulent along some of the main veins, beneath rather densely fascicled-hairy with short hairs or on some leaves with scattered fascicled hairs, in most cases becoming almost glabrous except for glandular puberulence on the midrib and main lateral veins, or with short solitary or paired pointed hairs, densely lepidote with minute yellow glandular scales; very young leaflets densely whitish-tomentose with some glandular puberulence; staminate catkins rather small and slender, 6-15 cm long, the floral bract about 1 mm long on the back of the flower; stamens 50-85 (21-25 according to Dode); loculi usually divergent on one side toward apex; appendage of the connective poorly developed, usually truncate, not or only slightly extending beyond the loculi, occasionally even retuse (appendage "lobed"); pistillate spike short, 1-3.5 cm long (rarely -4 cm long, with peduncle 1.8 cm, and rachis 2.2 cm), the rachis fascieled-hairy and also glandular-pubescent; flowers 3-5 (6), crowded or very rarely somewhat scattered; ovaries densely tomentose with fascicled hairs; involucre truncate at apex, not lobed; sepals rather short, broad, inconspicuous; stigmas short, broad, recurved at maturity; immature fruiting spike usually 3-3.5 cm long, the immature fruits densely and minutely puberulent (or with fascicled hairs?), often appearing glabrous; fruit subglobose to broadly oval, rather small, coinmonly 3-3.2 cm long and (2.5-) 2.7-3 (-3.5) cm in diameter, densely pubescent or glabrate, sometimes strongly verrucose; nut subglobose to broadly ovoid, 2.3-2.7 (-3?) cm long and 2.1-2.4 cm in diameter, essentially striate, that is with broad ridges and very shallow anastomosing furrows.
bibliographicCitation: Manning, Wayne E. 1960. The genus Juglans in South America and the West Indies. Brittonia. 12: 1-26.

description: Large tree, up to 35 m high; bark dark brown with flat scaly ridges and shallow furrows; youngest twigs densely but minutely fascicled-hairy, somnetimes ultimately or soon glabrate; twigs of the second year dark brown; older twigs (as cultivated in Costa Rica) sometimes ashy gray; pith light brown; terminal bud pointed; leaves up to 70 cm long and 30 cm broad; rachis appearing glabrous, but densely minutely glandular-puberulent (stipitate-glandular), with rather numerous to very few scattered minute fascicled hairs, not tomentose; leaflets 14-18 (-22 according to C. DeCandolle, -30 according to Dode), the terminal one usually absent, the lateral ones opposite or alternate, rather thin, not rugose, oblong-, oval- or ovate-lanceolate, 13-17 cm long and 5-6.5 cm wide, sessile or nearly so, tapering at base, gradually long-acuminate at apex, rather remotely serrate with fine, mostly outwardly projeetly teeth (in older leaves 4-5 teeth per cm) ; upper surface glabrate, the lower surface appearing glabrous but minutely puberulent on all nerves with stipitate glands, the midrib and the areas between the veins minutely lepidote; youngest leaflets (3 mm wide) densely but minutely fascicled-hairy but not tomentose, very soon becoming merely reddish-glandular (lepidote?), hence essentially glabrous; staminate catkins 10-16 cm long, slender, with small (youngo0?) scattered flowers, the floral bracts 1-1.5 mm long, very small and very narrow, glabrate or somewhat whitish puberulent, on the -back of the flower; perianth parts up to 7 or 8 in addition to two bracteoles; stamens 50-105; crown or appendage of the connective deltoid, pointed, hairy; pistillate spike short, 2-5 cm long ineluding the peduncle 0.5 cm long, 3-to 6-flowered; ovary usually glabrate, densely glandular but not really hairy, or very minutely fascicled-hairy but not tomentose; involucre truncate at apex, not definitely lobed; sepals of medium length (5 mm); stigmas short, rather erect, about 6 mm long; immature fruit unknown; size of mature fruit unknown, but the length probably 4-6.5 cm, and the diamneter 4-5.4 cm; nuts blackish, large, mostly broadly ovate or oval, or subglobose, usually somewhat drawn out at apex, not compressed, mostly about 5 cm long (3.5-5.5 cm) and 4 cm in diameter (3.5-4.5 ecm), conspicuously longitudinally ridged with rather broad, wavy-topped ridges frequently interrupted with strong, deep, and small shallow lines (veins) wall la-unnae mostly large, those at the end of the primary partition frequently present and well developed.

description: Plants short-caulescent, 1-5 dm high, villous-tomentose to glabrate, the stems 3-11, radiating from a long, slender or thickened, usually branched, taproot, the lower stem horizontal for 1.5-8.2 cm, then ascending, usually purplish, especially below, sometimes alternately few-branched. Leaves oblong to ovate or obovate in outline, the blades 3-16 cm long, pinnately decompound or ternate, then 3-4 pin- nate, the ultimate divisions crowded, linear to filiform, 0.5-3.2 mm long, 0.1-1.6 mm broad, acute, sometimes apiculate; the petioles 2-10.8 cm long, sheathing to near the middle. Peduncles terminal or sometimes axillary, exceeding the leaves. Involucre usually wanting, or of 1-2 inconspicuous linear bracts, 5-17 mm long, 0.5-1 mm broad. Rays 10-23, 0.7-9.3 cm long, spreading-ascending, usually unequal, the central umbellets often sterile and short-rayed. Involucel of linear-lanceolate, acute to acuminate bractlets, entire or rarely cleft above, distinct or connate at base, sometimes connate for more than one-half of length, equaling or exceeding the flowers. Pedicels 3-24 mm long, longer or shorter than the mature fruit, the umbellets many flowered. Flowers greenish to greenish-yellow, appearing white because of the pubescent petals, very rarely glabrous, rarely with purplish tinge, the central flowers of umbellet often sterile; calyx-teeth small; petals obovate with a narrower inflexed apex; styles slender, the stylopodium absent, the disk present. Carpophore 2-cleft to the base. Fruit orbicular to ovate-oblong, 7-21 mm long, 6-18 mm broad, the dorsal ribs filiform or obsolete, the lateral membraneous-winged, the body tomentose to glabrate, the wings tomentulose to glabrate, broader to narrower than the body; vittae 1-4 in the intervals, occasionally with smaller accessory vittae, 2-4 on the commissure, occasionally with smaller accessory vittae, sometimes one at the base of each wing. Gametic chromosome number, n = 11.

description: Plants 0.7-4 dm high, villous. Leaves broadly ovate to ovate-oblong in outline, the blades 2-15 cm long, the ultimate divisions linear to obovate, 1-6 mm long, 0.5-1 mm broad, apiculate; petioles 1-4.3 cm long, shorter than the blade, usually sheathing throughout, purplish. Peduncles 1-4 dm long. Rays 2-17, 0.5-6 cm long, spreading-ascending, usually unequal. Involucel of linear, acute to acuminate, usually distinct bractlets, shorter than or equaling the flowers. Flowers usually yellow, sometimes purple, or yellow with purplish tinge, or yellow and purple flowers combined in the same umbellet; petals glabrous. Fruit ovate-oblong to orbicular, 5-11 mm long, 4-8 mm broad, the body and wings pubescent, the wings narrower than the body; vittae 1-6 in the intervals, 3-8 on the commissure.

description: Stout acaulescent herbs with massive taproot and multicipital caudex impacted with clay and marcescent leaf-bases, glabrous throughout, the sparse rushlike foliage pale green or subglaucescent. Leaves 3-7 from each division of the caudex, mostly 1-3 dm long (the first often depauperate and only 2.5-10 cm), erect; petiole terete, striate, (1.5) 5-14 cm long, 0.8-1.6 mm diam., dilated at the base into a pallid, when old brunnescent, dorsally ridged sheath; blade narrowly elliptic or obovate-elliptic in outline, remotely 1-pinnate or 3-foliate, the 1-3 pairs of narrowly ascending lateral segments linear, acute, entire, resembling the petiole but obscurely sulcate ventrally, (1) 1.5-13.5 cm long, the terminal one similar, (2) 4-22 cm long. Scapes stout, ascending and erect, (0.8) 1-2.5 dm long, often purplish at the base; involucre absent (exceptionally 1 linear bract 1-2 cm long); umbels (6-) 8-12-rayed; rays all fertile or the 1 or 2 inner ones short and sterile, the fertile ones spreading-ascending, in fruit 1.5-4.5 cm long; involucels of several narrowly lance-acuminate or subulate bracts 1.5-3 mm long, often connate at the base; pedicels unequal, ca 1-1.5 mm in flower, in fruit becoming 4-11 mm, be- coming slightly swollen at the base; calyx lobes triangular or subulate, more or less 0.5 mm long; petals white, ca 1 mm long; filaments 2-3 mm long; anthers 0.6 mm long. Fruit broadly oblong-elliptic or -obovate in dorsoventral view, shallowly emarginate at both ends, (9) 10-14.5 mm long, (5.5) 6-8.5 mm wide, the finely (3-) 5-ribbed body of the mericarps 3-3.5 mm wide, their white or sometimes purplish, scarcely thickened wings more or less 2.5 mm wide; vittae (oil tubes) very slender, more or less 5 in the intervals, 3 on the commissure.

description: Plants 8-29 cm high; leaves oblong in general outline, somewhat rigid, the blades 4.5-11.5 cm long, 1.2-5.3 cm broad, pinnately divided, the pinnae distinct, linear, remote, 5-32 mm long, 1.5-4 mm broad; petioles 3.5-12.5 cm long; peduncles 8-26 cm long; bracts of involuere wanting; rays 5-10, subequal or unequal, 5-18 mm long, reflexed in flower and fruit; bractlets of involueel incon- spicuous, linear-lanceolate, sometimes minutely scaberulous on the margins; pedicels 6-10, 1-5 mm long, reflexed in fruit; styles 2-3 mm long; fruit oblong, 3.5-5 mm long, 1-2.5 mm broad, ribs deltoid in transection, not winged; vittae scattered throughout the pericarp in both immature and mature fruits.

description: Plants 6-15 dm high, robust; leaves pinnately decompound with many divisions, usually so crowded as to appear verticillate; hyaline border on the petiole inconspicuous, the petiole 1-3 cm long; involuere consicuous, usually entire; involucel inconsicuous, entire; primary rays 16-24, 1-4.5 cm long; petals white with narrowly inflexed apex; anthers rose-colored; styles long, 1-3 mm long, spreading; fruit suborbicular, the dorsal ribs rounded, the lateral ribs inconspicuous; oil tubes brown or dull black; corky band not prominent, usually flat. Pollen grains 27.2-33.5 µ long, 12.8-15.3 µ wide. Chromosome number: n = 16. Swamps, marshes, and poorly drained acid soil. Sporadic, has been found in eastern Texas, Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee, Illinois, and Missouri. June to October.

description: Plants glabrous; stems slender, creeping; leaves orbicular-peltate, 5-60 mm. in diameter, 8-14-nerved, shallowly 8-14-lobed, the petioles slender, 1.5-35 cm. long; infloreseence an axillary interrupted simple, rarely branched, spike, 8-22 cm. long, with few 4-15-flowered verticils, the interverticillar distance 4-40 mm., the pedicels 1-10 mm. long, spreading to ascending; fruit oblong-ovoid, 1-3 mm. long, 2-4 mm. broad, the ribs distinct, acute, the stylopodium depressed.

description: Shrub or small tree to 10 m tall, 50-60 cm thick at base. Stems terete, densely fine- puberulent, the hairs 0.1-0.13 mm long, gradually narrowed from base to tip, sometimes minutely enlarged at the apex. Leaves linear-subulate, caducous, 0.1-1.2 mm long, succulent, puberulent. Thorns straight to curved, terete, puberulent, 33-82 mm long and 1.2-2.0 mm thick at the base, gradually thinning to a brownish-black sharp tip. Inflorescence a 10-18-flowered slender raceme to umbelliform raceme, the axis 1-7 cm long, terete to irregularly angled, puberulent; pedicels terete, thin, puberulent, gradually shortening from base to apex, 2-10 mm long; bracts linear, succulent, puberulent, ca. 1.5 mm long, caducous, each accompanied by a pair of subulate to linear to ovate stipules, 0.3-0.7 mm long, puberulent. Sepals broadly ovate-deltate, ca. 1.3 x 1.3 mm, glabrate to puberulent, the margins subentire to irregularly serrate-dentate to suberose. Petals white to yellow, glabrous, 4-4.8 mm long, ovate-cymbiform, the margins entire, the apices rounded, the bases attenuate, nerves obscure. Stamens 8; filaments glabrous, thickest near the middle; anthers 0.8-1 mm long. Pistil 3.3-3.8 mm long; stipe 0.5-0.8 mm; ovary proper ca. 1.8- 2.0 mm in diameter, the surfaces glabrous, rugose in dried state; style 1-1.2 mm long, thinning from base to apex, straight or sometimes the apex bent or curved in dry condition into an uncinate or "s" shape, the surfaces striate; stigma entire to occasionally obscurely lobed. Berry black, globular, 4- 5 mm, glabrous. Seeds cochleate, ca. 3.3 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, and 1.3 mm thick; surfaces cancellate.

description: Planta suffructicosa procumbens; rami striati fuscorubri paucifoliati; folia carnosa lanceolata integra acuminata vel mucronata ad basin attenuata, breviter petiolata; flos roseus; sepala 4; petala 5, 3 anteriora libera lanceolata longe attenuata, 2 lateralia unguiculata, adaxialiter rugosa; nux globosa spinosa, spinis ad apicem echinatis.

description: Sprawling suffructescent, sparsely-branched shrubs to 60 cm tall, often partially buried in sand; branches to 1 m long, striate, glabrescent, often dark brown when dry. Leaves sparse, simple, lanceolate, acute to mucronate apically, petiolate, 15-26 mm long including the 1-2 mm long petiole, 3.5-4 mm wide; surfaces variably tomentose. Flowers zygomorphic, borne in terminal racemes; flowering stalks short, to 5 mm long, the peduncles and pedicels separated close to the rachis by a pair of small bractlets; peduncles and bractlets remaining on the branch if flowers abort; sepals 4, lanceolate in outline, entire, deep pink to violet, tomentose, especially on the portions exposed in the bud; lowermost sepals ca 9 mm long, 4 mm wide, slightly saccate; uppermost sepals 7-9 mm long, 4 mm wide; lateral sepals narrower than the upper or lowermost ones; glandular petals 2, appressed laterally to the ovary, cuneate, 2-3 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, deep purple-red, their external surfaces covered with irregularly shaped blisters; petaloid petals 3, inserted together above the ovary, (5) 7-8 mm long, clawed, the white claws connate basally for 1-2 mm, free above, the lanceolate, extremely acuminate, deep red-purple blades ca 5 mm long, 2 mm wide; stamens 4, subequilong, 5-6 mm long, inserted at the juncture of the petaloid petals and the ovary, free from the point of insertion; pollen globose, ca 30-32 µm in diam with 3 equatorially expanded (almost touching) pores 4 µm wide at the widest part; ovary ovoid, 2.5 mm long, densely pubescent and surmounted by a thick, recurved style 4 mm long; locule 1, bearing 2, anatropous, pyriform ovules attached to the adaxial side of the carpel. Fruits globose capsules, 4.5-5 mm in diam excluding spines, tomentose and bearing numerous yellow or reddish spines 3.3-4.5 mm long and 0.25-0.5 mm in basal diam; individual spines with many small subterminal retrorse barbs and a few scattered unicellular trichomes at the base; seeds 1 per fruit, globose, dull gray, glabrous; endosperm lacking; cotyledons large, orbiculate. Chromosome number unknown.

description: A rounded shrub 4-12 dm. tall, freely branched, the branches erect, hirtellous below the infloreseence with short, downwardly appressed hairs; leaves normally linear, 2-6 cm. long, 1-6 mm. broad, usually longer than the internodes, normally provided with a fascicle of smaller leaves in the axils, acute at the apex, occasionally obtuse, sessile or narrowed at the base to short indefinite petioles 5 mm. long at most, their margins entire, strongly revolute, the upper surfaces green, minutely rough-hispidulous or sometimes pubescent with longer hairs, particularly near the base of the blade, the lower densely gray-pubescent; eymes open, spreading, borne on peduncles 5-15 mm. long, the pedicels as much as 10 mm. long, borne in the axils of the upper reduced leaves, forming an open panicle 15-30 cm. long at maturity, the entire infloreseence woolly and floccose with fine blue, pink or white hairs which are 1-2 mm. long, sometimes less, or these nearly wanting and replaced by the short pubescence of the stems, but in no case obscuring the pedicels; flowering calyces 3-5 mm. long, somewhat longer in fruit, the teeth subequal, ovate to lanceolate, acute or lightly acuminate, equaling the tubes; corollas floccose or at least pubescent on the outside, glabrous within, the tubes straight, exceeding the calyces, 4-7 mm. long, the lower lip 5-9 mm. long; stamens arched, 15-25 iuml. long; nutlets 1.8-3.7 mm. long, 0.8-1.7 mm. broad, irregularnly reticulate, pubescent at least at the apex.
bibliographicCitation: Lewis, Harlan. 1945. A revision of the genus Trichostema. Brittonia. 5: 276-303. f. 1-5.

description: Spreading shrubs 1-5 dm tall, 1-12 dm wide; leaves ovate to obovate or spatulate, the blade 6-18 (20) mm long, (4) 6-10 (20) mm wide, the widest point (2) 5-11 (13) mm from the base, abruptly narrowed to the petiole-base, the petiole 3-8 (12) mm long; mature glomerules 8-15 mm long, 15-25 mm wide, 6-25 mm apart, 2-5 per branchlet; bracts roughened, scabrous to sparsely puberulent or glabrous abaxially, glabrous or sparsely puberulent adaxially, the margins short to moderately long ciliate, the outer bracts orbicular, ovate or obovate, (4) 6-10 (14) mm long, 4-8 (13) mm wide, rounded or cuspidate but seldom acute or emarginate apically, the inner bracts elliptic, spatulate or oblanceolate, up to 10 mm long and 6 mm wide, rounded or acute, often weakly spinescent apically; calyx 6-10 mm long, 3-4 (7) mm wide, scabrellous to scabrous or minutely pu- berulent abaxially, scabrellous or minutely puberulent adaxially, the lower lobes rounded or more often acute and weakly spinescent apically, 1-3 mm long, the upper lobes weakly distinct or less often united, occasionally erose apically; stamens exserted 1-5 mm beyond the corolla lobes and inserted on the throat 6- 8 mm from the base of the tube, the filaments 4-5 mm long, the connectives 2- 3 mm long, occasionally forked, the upper pair of stamens poorly developed, up to 2 mm long or lacking; 2n = 30 (Epling et al., 1962, as reported for subsp. gilmanii).
bibliographicCitation: Strachan, Jeffrey L. 1982. A revision of the Salvia dorrii complex (Lamiaceae). Brittonia. 34: 151-169.

description: Arbor, ad 20 m. alta et 5 dm. diam., truncis 2-numerosis, ramis cinereis, juventute brunneis, striatis subteretibus minute sed conspicue lenticellatis exfoliantibus glabris. Folia alternata, petiolis crassis glabris brunneis canaliculatis 5-12 mm. longis et ad 3 mm. latis, laminis utrinque glabris coriaceis supra atrovirentibus lucidis, subtus pallidioribus, ellipticis vel elliptico-ovatis vel ellipticoobovatis, 7-12 (-16) cm. longis et 3-5 (-7) cm. latis, ad basim plus minusve cuneatis vel acutis, ad apicem acutis vel breviter et obtuse acuminatis raro emarginatis, penninerviis, costa crassa supra ad apicem leviter elevata, ad petiolum plana latioraque, nervis 6-8 paribus flavovirentibus gracilibus supra elevatis, angulo 35-45? divergentibus, rete venularum utrinque conspicuo. Inflorescentia axillaris vel subterminalis, robusta, glabra, paniculata, ad 5 cm. longa, brevipedunculata. Flores ad 12 mm. longi, sessiles vel brevipedicellati, perianthio suburceolato virides centi carnoso glabro, lobis exterioribus ovato-orbicularibus apiculatis, extus glabris intus minute adpresseque pubescentibus, ad 3 mm. latis, interioribus suborbicularibus intus ad basim minute pubescentibus ad 1.5 mm. latis; tubo quam lobis longiore; staminodiis ser. I & II variabilibus, saepe subpetaloideis ad basim minute pubescentibus, 1.3 mm. longis, staminibus fertilibus ser. Ill inclusis in tubum connatis suborbicularibus, filamentis indistinctis biglandulosis, glandulis sessilibus; ser. IV O; gynaecio ad 2 mm. longo, ovario ovoideo glabro stylo gracili aequante vel breviore. Infructescentia leviter robusta, glabra, ad 5 cm. longa, brunnescentia. Fructus atrocaeruleus ad violascenticaeruleus vel niger, plus minusve oblongus, apice basique rotundatus, ad 15 mm. longus et 6-7 mm. latus, viscidus, cupula plus minusve cyathiformi ad 12 mm. longa et 8 mm. diam., margine duplici, exteriore leviter undulata, interiore exteriore 3 mm. longiore et leviter lobata, pedicello brevi crasso apice 4 mm. diam. striato.
bibliographicCitation: Allen, Caroline L. & Gregory, Luis E. 1951. A new Species of Licaria from Puerto Rico. Brittonia. 7: 267-269.

description: Arbor usque 20 m alta, ramulis foliiferis 1.5-4 mm crassis, glabrescentibus. Folia petiolis 4-10 mm longis, 1.2-2.3 mm latis; laminis 4-12.5 cm longis, 2-4 (5.5) cm latis, elliptico-obovatis vel elliptico- oblongis, in petiolum gradatim decrescentibus, apice plerumque breviter acuminatis, basi anguste cuneatis, subcoriaceis in sicco, supra glabris, subtus glabrescentibus, nervis secundariis 3-6-jugis, domatiis depressis in pagina inferna, minute pilosis. Inflorescentiae 9-13 cm longae, pedunculis ca 1.5 mm crassis, pedicellis ca 2 mm longis. Flores 2.5-3 mm longi, 2.5-3 mm lati, tepalis late obtusis, minute sericeis in pagina externa; staminibus 1.2-1.4 mm longis, puberulis, glandulis ca 0.6 mm altis et latis; gynoecio ca 2 mm. longo, ovario ellipsoideo, stylo ca 0.9 mm longo, angusto, stigmate simplici. Fructus globosus vel pyriformis, usque 8 cm longus; cupula 10-17 mm lata.
bibliographicCitation: Burger, William C. 1988. A new genus of Lauraceae [Povedadaphne quadriporata] from Costa Rica, with comments on problems of generic and specific delimitation within the family. Brittonia. 40: 275-282.

description: Trees 6-20 m tall, trunks to 45 cm thick, leafy branchlets glabrescent, dark grayish, shoot-apex covered with densely appressed lustrous sericeous hairs. Leaves alternate, petioles 4-10 mm long but poorly defined because of the decurrent lamina-base, 1.2-2.3 mm broad, usually glabrous, with thin lateral margins and sulcate near the base; laminae 4-12.5 cm long, 2-4 (5.5) cm broad, elliptic-obovate to elliptic-oblong, short acuminate at the apex or occasionally obtuse, gradually narrowed to the cuneate or attenuate base and decurrent on the petiole, drying subcoriaceous and often brown or olive green, glabrous above and with the major veins slightly elevated, glabrous or very sparsely puberulent beneath and becoming glabrescent, axils of larger secondary veins usually with conspicuous pit-domatia ca 1 mm broad and filled with minute whitish hairs beneath, with 3-6 major secondary veins on each side, central secondaries arising at angles of 30-45º. Inflorescences solitary and axillary to distal leaves or undeveloped distal leaves, 9-13 cm long, paniculate with short (3 cm) lateral branches, peduncles 4-7 cm long and 1.5 mm thick, minutely appressed-puberulent, flowers often in distal 3-flowered cymules, pedicels ca 2 mm long. Flowers 2.5-3 mm long and equally broad, apparently urceolate but becoming campanulate when pressed, minutely sericeous on the outside, tepals broadly obtuse; fertile stamens 9 and similar in form, 1.2-1.4 mm long, columnar and puberulent, glabrous at the top with the 4 minute valves dehiscing apically, ca 0.6 mm broad at the top, the 6 glands short- stipitate with broadly rounded sagittate apex ca 0.6 mm broad, free of the inner stamens and exterior to them, staminodes absent; gynoecium ca 2 mm long, ovary ellipsoid and 0.7 mm thick, style narrow and ca 0.9 mm long, stigma simple. Fruit (not present in the type) borne on a thickened (8 mm) pedicel with the receptacle becoming slightly expanded to (10-17 mm) broad and 1-3 mm deep; fruit to 8 cm long and 6 cm in diam, globose to pyriform, seed large (ca 4-5 cm in diam), reddish-purple in cross-section.

description: Annua-biennis. Rhizoma simplex breve radicibus adventitiis filiformibus numerosis. Folia 4-8 radicalia rosulata circuitu +/- late obovata 14.0-18.5 mm longa, 11.0-17.0 mm lata basin versus cuneatim angustata apice rotundata integerrima margine paulum involuta superne glanduloso-viscosa glandulis sessilibus dense et glandulis stipitatis modice dense vestita laete virentia. Hibernacula nulla. Pedicelli 1-5 luteo-virides erecti uniflori 13.4-39.5 mm alti filiformes glandulis stipitatis modice dense obsiti. Flores parvi 3.0-9.0 mm longi (calcari incluso). Calyx viridis bilabiatus extus glandulis stipitatis dense obsitus; labium superum usque ad basin fere trilobum lobis oblongis obtusis vel acutiusculis; labium inferum usque ad 1/3-1/2 longitudinis bilobum lobis oblongis acutiusculis. Corolla subisoloba lobis albidis fauce fulva extus glandulis stipitatis singularibus obtecta lobis rectangulo- oblongis apice leviter truncatis vel subrotundatis paulum longioribus quam latis 0.4-4.0 mm longis, 1.5-4.0 mm latis. Tubus subcylindricus 2.6-5.0 mm longus 2.5-4.0 mm latus luteus violaceo-striatus cum palato et cymatio palati basi albidus intus disperse pilosus in regione palati pilis longis clavate capitatis in regione cymatii palati pilis longis crassioribus retro conversis fulvis. Palatum fulvum hemisphaericum +/- 0.8-1.2 mm diametro pills tenuibus mediocribus dense obtectum. Calcar luteum breve ex basi lato cylindricum apice rotundatum vel acutiusculum cum tubo angulum obtusum subvalidum formans 0.5-2.6 mm longum quintam totius corollae longitudinis partem subaequans. Stamina 0.8-1.0 mm longa; antherae 0.4-0.6 mm longae; pollen 5-6 colporatum. Ovarium sub- globosum 0.3-0.6 mm diametro glandulis stipitatis modice dense obsitum. Stigma bilabiatum, labium inferum papillatum 0.2-1.0 mm longum. Capsula viridis subglobosa 1.9-3.8 mm diametro calycem non superans. Semina scobiformia numerosa. Chromosomata 2n = 16. Floret: (?-) II (-?).

description: Herba annua glabra; caules 5-30 cm alti, parce vel multum e basi ramosi, erecti vel ascendentes; prima folia plantulae integra; folia plantarum maturarum usque ad 10 cm longa, pinnata, longe petiolata, 1-2 paribus foliolis integris anguste obovatis obsita, 5-20 mm longis; flores pentameri, perfecti, campanulati vel rotati; sepala lanceolata, 6-7 mm longa; petala cuneata, 12-18 mm longa, emarginata, nivea, sed in sicco basibus flava; venae petalorum hyalinae, pilis sparsis crispis longis obsitae, pilis marginalibus unguum brevissimis; stamina 5-6 mm longa; antherae 1.5-2 mm longae; stylus 4.5-6.5 mm longus; nuculae obovoideae, 3-4 mm longae, brunneae vel fuligineae, tuberculis brevibus latisque confertim vestitae; chromosomatum numerus n = 5.
bibliographicCitation: Ornduff, Robert. 1969. Limnanthes vinoulans, a new California endemic. Brittonia. 21: 11-14.
