description: Glabrous annual; stems 5-30 cm tall, sparingly to much branched at the base, erect or ascending; first foliage leaves of seedling entire; leaves of mature plants long petiolate, to 10 cm long, pinnate, with 1-2 pairs of entire, narrowly obovate leaflets 5-20 mm long; flowers 5-merous, perfect, campanulate to rotate; sepals lanceolate, 6-7 mm long; petals cuneate, 12-18 mm long, emarginate, white, but drying with a yellow base, the veins hyaline with occasional crisped, long hairs, and with marginal hairs on the petal claw; stamens 5-6 mm long; anthers 1.5-2 mm long; style 4.5-6.5 mm long, nutlets obovoid, 3-4 mm long, dark brown, densely clothed with short, broad tubercles; n = 5.
bibliographicCitation: Ornduff, Robert. 1969. Limnanthes vinoulans, a new California endemic. Brittonia. 21: 11-14.

description: Glabrous annual herb, branched at the base and in the inflorescence, 18-33 (11-50) cm tall; leaves alternate or the lower opposite, more numerous on the lower part of the stem, linear, 9-14 (8-17) mm long, 0.7-0.9 (0.5-1.3) mm wide, entire; stipular glands present in about 75% of the individuals examined; inflores- cence open, floral bracts moderately glandular-toothed; longer pedicels 2-12 mm long, mostly about 5 mm long; sepals thin, lanceolate, sometimes narrowly so, 5.0-6.2 (3.7-7.8) mm long, the outer very sparsely toothed, the inner abundantly toothed, all 1-nerved, tending to persist; petals yellow-orange to salmon with maroon base, broadly obovate, 12-14 (10-17) mm long, pubescent at the base; stamens 6-7 (4-8) mm long; anthers narrowly elliptic, 1.1-1.5 (0.8-1.8) mm long; styles 5.9-7.6 (3.2-8.0) mm long, united nearly to the summit; stigmas dark; fruit ovate, easily crushed in pressing, 3.3-3.7 (3.0-4.1) mm high, 2.5-3.2 mm in diameter, the cartilaginous plates poorly developed; false septa incomplete, ending in a loose fringe; seeds reddish brown, 2.0-2.8 mm long, 0.9-1.3 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Coarse perennial herb, glabrous or nearly so, with a stout taproot, stems branched at the base and in the inflorescence, 72-93 (49-119) cm tall (with small plants certainly on occasion having been collected); leaves opposite or occasionally whorled near the base, alternate above or rarely opposite to the inflorescence, entire, linear- lanceolate to ovate, the largest near the center of the stem, 26-38 (21-44) mm long, 9-17 (5-20) mm wide, tapering to truncate or subcordate at the sessile or very short petiolate base, acute or rarely subacuminate at the apex, often ciliate-margined and occasionally with a tuft of small hairs at the apex, sometimes sparsely hairy on the lower side, pinnately veined, with two rather prominent lateral nerves from near the base; stipular glands present; inflorescence ample, of rather stiffly spread- ing-ascending branches; fruit short pedicellate; sepals lanceolate to ovate, the inner somewhat broader, 2.5-3.6 mm long, sometimes with glands at the base, the outer entire or very sparsely glandular-toothed, the inner conspicuously glandular- toothed or sometimes entire, all commonly appressed puberulent inside and often with a small tuft of hairs at the apex; petals yellow, obovate, 8-11 mm long, glabrous; stamens 5-8 mm long, the filaments conspicuously broadened at the base, alternating with eccentrically placed staminodia up to 1 mm long; anthers elliptic, 0.8-1.2 mm long; styles 4.5-5.3 (4-6.7) mm long, united one-half to three-fourths of their length; fruit ovate to triangular, 2.7-3.1 mm high and about as wide, the upper portion usually suffused with purple, dehiscing into 10 very sharp pointed segments; false septa partially developed, the septa strongly ciliate; seeds reddish brown, elliptic, 1.5-1.7 mm long, 1.0-1.1 mm wide.

description: Annual or weak perennial herb, often decumbent at the base, villous throughout, 8-48 cm tall, but mostly under 30 cm; lower leaves in whorls of four, alternate above or commonly alternate nearly to the base, the lower obovate or elliptic, the upper lance-ovate, gradually reduced into the inflorescence, the larger 5-13 mm long, 1.6-4.6 mm wide, sessile, obtuse to acute, the upper and the floral bracts with numerous glandular teeth; stipular glands present at the bases of leaves and lower floral bracts; inflorescence few branched, sometimes subsimple; fruit subsessile or on pedicels up to 6 mm long; sepals ovate, 1.9-2.9 mm long, prominently and closely glandular-toothed, hairy at least on the veins, appressed hairy inside; petals yellow, obovate, 3-4 mm long; stamens 2-3 mm long, filaments sparsely villous below; staminodia low, deltoid, 1 or 2 or sometimes absent; styles separate, 1.7-2.5 mm long; fruit ovoid, hirsutulous near the summit, often purplish above, easily crushed, 1.5-1.8 mm high, ca. 1.7 mm in diameter; false septa only partially de- veloped; septa without marginal cilia; seeds ovate, 1.0-1.1 mm long, 0.6-0.7 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Annual or rarely a short-lived perennial, 15-29 (10-37) cm tall, scabrous or puberulent at the base, otherwise glabrous, branched at the base, the branches spreading to suberect, terete below, sharply striate above; leaves opposite near the base or alternate throughout, linear to narrowly linear-lanceolate, up to 15-25 (11-30) mm long, 1.2-2.1 (0.9-3.0) mm wide, largest just below the inflorescence; stipular glands present; floral bracts with irregular scarious margins; pedicels thick; sepals strongly 1-nerved, the outer broadly lanceolate to ovate or obovate, 6.2-7.4 (5.3-8.7) mm long, conspicuously aristate and with wide undulate or crenate scarious margins, a sessile gland near the summit of each crenation, the inner sepals somewhat shorter, regularly and delicately glandular-toothed; petals obovate, yellow, grading to reddish near the base, 12-14 (9-18) mm long, pubescent near the base; stamens 5-8 mm long, with or without diminutive intervening staminodia; anthers 1.2-1.6 (0.8-2.0) mm long; styles 6.7-8.3 (5.0-9.8) mm long, united nearly to the summit; stigmas pale; fruit ovate, 4.0-4.5 (3.3-4.7) mm high, 3.2-3.7 (3.0-3.8) mm in diameter, the walls opaque, the basal cartilaginous plates 5-sided and united more than halfway to the summit; cartilaginous portion constituting more than one-half of the false septum; seeds ovate, 2.3-2.8 mm long, 1.0-1.3 mm wide.

description: Annual glabrous herb, with a stout taproot, 20-40 (8-47) cm tall, typically much branched throughout, broomlike, the branches slender, stiffly spreading-ascending; leaves alternate or the lowermost opposite, linear, entire, 7-13 (6-20) mm long, 0.4-0.8 (0.3-1.1) mm wide, more or less concealed by the branches; stipular glands present in about 90% of the plants examined; inflorescence a diffuse panicle, flowers scattered; pedicels slender; outer sepals linear-lanceolate, attenuate, 6.5-7.9 (5.3-9.0) mm long, the inner somewhat broader, shorter, with scarious margins, all with many glandular teeth; petals obovate, yellow to yellow-orange throughout, 8-12 mm long, pubescent at the base; stamens 5-6 (-7) mm long; staminodia none; anthers elliptic, 0.8-1.0 (0.7-1.1) mm long; styles 4.8-5.7 (4.3-7.2) mm long, united nearly to the summit; stigmas pale; fruit elliptic, clearly longer than broad, pale, thin walled, 3.7-3.9 (3.3-4.2) mm long, 2.5-2.8 (2.4-3.0) mm in diameter; cartilaginous portion constituting less than one-half of the false septum; seeds lanceolate, 2.6-3.0 (2.4-3.1) mm long, (0.8-) 0.9-1.0 mm wide.

description: Annual herb, puberulent near the base, otherwise glabrous 13-32 (10-53) cm tall; leaves alternate, linear, entire, the longer 7-17 mm long, 0.5-1.4 mm wide; stipular glands prominent at the base of leaves, floral bracts, and at the bases of sepals in about 50% of the plants examined; sepals mostly 1-nerved, thin textured, lanceolate, 4.0-6.2 mm long, scarious margined, glandular-toothed, slender-pointed; petals yellow to yellow-orange throughout, 8-10 mm long; stamens 5-7 mm long, without staminodia; anthers 0.6-1.0 mm long; styles 3.6-5.7 mm long, united nearly to the summit; fruit ovoid, with wall thickened as in var. australe, 3.2-3.5 mm high, 2.7-3.0 mm in diameter; seeds 2.0-2.7 mm long, 0.8-1.2 mm wide.

description: Annual herb, with a slender taproot, closely resembling L. imbricatum in habit, 11-23 (5-30) cm tall; stems hirsutulous on the angles above, otherwise glabrous, branching from the base, the branches ascending to erect, nearly terete below, striate above; leaves narrow, opposite near the base, alternate above, the larger 6-9 (5-10) mm long, 0.7-0.9 (0.5-1.1) mm wide, imbricated throughout, the lower spreading to ascending, the cauline closely appressed, the lower sharp pointed, the upper with a short, slender terminal awn, all entire, the uppermost with a narrow scarious margin; stipular glands none; inflorescence few flowered, the lower, longer fruiting pedicels 8-13 (3-15) mm long, all usually conspicuously exserted beyond the subtending leaves; sepals persistent, the outer lanceolate to ovate, 5.5-6.2 (4.5-7.2) mm long, with a very broad scarious entire or sparsely delicately toothed or, in age, somewhat lacerate margin, the slender herbaceous median portion extending into a conspicuous awn, the inner sepals similar, but more prominently toothed; petals obovate, yellow, with or without a dark red base, 8-12 mm long, pubescent at the base; stamens ca. 5 mm long; staminodia none; anthers elliptic, 1.0-1.6 mm long; styles 2.7-6.3 mm long, united nearly to the summit; fruit pale, broadly ovate, 2.7-3.5 mm long, 2.8-3.6 mm in diameter; false septa tomentose near the summit, entirely hyaline, or with a uniformly very narrow outer cartilaginous portion; seeds ovate, 2.0-2.7 mm long, 1.0-1.2 mm wide, wedge-shaped in cross section, reddish brown.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Low annual herb, 11-20 (6-27) cm tall, from slender taproot, branched at the base, sometimes divaricately, in plants from along the Gulf shore; stems spreading to ascending or erect, terete or nearly so below, strongly striate above, glabrous below, conspicuously short hirsute with stout-based hairs above; leaves narrow, opposite near the base, alternate above, the larger 6-8 (5-9) mm long, 0.7-0.9 (0.5-1.2) mm wide, strongly imbricate, the lower spreading-ascending, the cauline rather strongly appressed with cartilaginous-based midribs, short awned, the upper ciliate-margined; stipular glands none; inflorescence few flowered, the lower, longer pedicels 4-6 (2-11) mm long, the upper mostly hidden by the subtending leaves; sepals persistent, usually with a few stiff hairs along the midrib, ovate, 4.6-5.5(4.2-6.1) mm long, with broad, commonly purplish, scarious margins, prominently toothed above the middle, the median herbaceous portion extended into an awn; petals yellow, with or without a dark red base, obovate, 6.5-8.0 mm long, pubescent at the base; stamens ca. 5 mm long; staminodia none; anthers elliptic, 0.6-1.2 mm long; fruit pale, broadly ovate, 2.6-3.0 mm high, 2.9-3.3 mm in diameter; false septa appressed pilose along the inner margin, otherwise essentially glabrous, mostly hyaline, but with a cartilaginous portion along the ovary wall, this cartilaginous strip conspicuously broader toward the base of the carpel; styles 2.0-4.3 mm long, united nearly to the summit; seeds flattened, ovate, 2.0-2.6 mm long, 1.1-1.5 mm wide.

description: Glabrous perennial herb, branched at the base, the branches ascending to erect from decumbent base, 10-24 (6-30) cm tall; leaves opposite near the base or alternate throughout, 1-nerved, very crowded, especially near the base, basal leaves thick, narrowly lanceolate, rounded to subacute at the apex, the cauline leaves similar or on taller plants intergrading to much larger, linear-lanceolate, acute to acuminate leaves, the larger leaves 7-16 (4-26) mm long, 1.6-2.5 (1.1-3.3) mm wide; stipular glands none; inflorescence paniculate or thyrsoid; fruits subsessile or on pedicels up to 5 mm long; sepals lanceolate to ovate, the outer entire or sparsely glandular-toothed near the summit, 3.0-3.6 (2.4-4.5) mm long, the inner about as long, glandular-toothed; petals yellow, oblanceolate to obovate, 6-10 (5-12) mm long, glabrous; stamens 5-7 (3-8) mm long, filaments con- spicuously broader near the base; staminodia none; anthers narrowly elliptic, 1.8-2.3 (1.4-2.7) mm long; styles separate, 5.2-6.3 (4.1-6.8) mm long; fruit ovate- pyriform, tapering to a point at the summit, 2.3-4.0 mm high, 2.8-3.6 mm in diameter, commonly suffused with purple in the upper portion, easily crushed, freely dehiscing into 10 segments; false septa partially developed, septa ciliate; seeds elliptic to narrowly ovate, 2.0-2.7 mm long, 1.0-1.4 mm wide, reddish brown.

description: Glabrous, sometimes glaucous annual herb, 21-43 (12-61) cm tall, branched from near the base, the branches erect or at length shortly decumbent at the base; leaves entire, 1-nerved, opposite near the base, sometimes to the middle of the stem, otherwise alternate, the lower narrowly to broadly elliptic-oblanceolate, subacute, the middle cauline leaves larger, linear-lanceolate, acute to acuminate, the larger 10-15 (8-17) mm long, 1.6-2.2 (1.3-2.6) mm wide; stipular glands none; inflorescence very slender, thyrsoid; sepals linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, acute to acuminate, the outer entire or very sparsely glandular-toothed, 3.1-4.0 (3.0-5.3) mm long, the inner nearly as long, conspicuously glandular-toothed; petals yellow, oblanceolate, 4-7 mm long, glabrous; staminodia none; filaments broadened at the base, 3-5 mm long; anthers narrowly elliptic, 1.2-1.5 (0.8-1.7) mm long; styles separate, 1.8-2.3 (1.5-3.0) mm long; fruit triangular-ovoid to broadly ovate, the upper portion suffused with purple, 2.9-3.2 (2.5-3.4) mm high, 2.7-3.5 mm in diameter, somewhat tardily dehiscing into 10 segments; false septa partially developed; septa with ciliate margins; seeds pale reddish brown, elliptic-ovate, 2.0-2.5 mm long, 1.1-1.3 mm wide.

description: Annual herb, 13-21 (4-26) cm tall, sometimes branched at the base, densely gray-puberulent throughout; leaves all alternate or the basal occasionally opposite, 1-nerved, linear, 10-13 (7-20) mm long, 0.8-1.2 (0.6-1.5) mm wide, entire or the upper as well as the floral bracts with a few glandular teeth; stipular glands conspicuous, frequently at the bases of the sepals as well as bracts and leaves; inflorescence open, paniculate; sepals lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 5.8-6.7 (4.5-7.4) mm long, puberulent at least on the midrib, outer sepals 3-nerved, the inner with scarious margins, all glandular-toothed; petals obcordate or broadly obovate, yellowish orange to salmon, with maroon or reddish base, 9-12 (7-14) mm long, pilose at the base; stamens 5-6 (4-7) mm long; anthers 0.7-1.1 (0.6-1.4) mm long; styles 3.5-5.7 (2.8-7.0) mm long; united nearly to the summit; stigmas dark; fruit ovate, pale, 3.5-4.0 (3.3-4.1) mm high, 2.8-3.0 (2.5-3.2) mm in diameter; seeds ovate, 2.5-2.8 (2.3-3.0) mm long, 0.9-1.3 mm wide, reddish brown.

description: Annual herb, 12-24 (5-40) cm tall, hirsutulous near the base, occasionally so on the angles above, otherwise glabrous, branched near the base and in the in- florescence, sometimes throughout, the branches spreading-ascending, striate; leaves opposite near the base or alternate throughout, linear to linear-lanceolate, the largest near or above the middle of the stem, the larger 16-22 (13-29) mm long, 1.6-2.6 (1.3-4.1) mm wide, entire or the upper leaves and floral bracts with a few diminutive teeth, mostly 3-nerved; stipular glands present in about 80% of the plants examined; inflorescence mostly rather dense, tending to be flat topped; pedicels short; sepals lanceolate, attenuate, 7.2-8.7 (6.0-12.5) mm long, predominantly 3-nerved, con- spicuously glandular-toothed, the inner somewhat broader with scarious margins and more densely and delicately toothed; petals yellow to orange, reddish below the middle, broady obovate, 13-16 (11-19) mm long, pubescent at the base; stamens 6-7 (4-9) mm long; anthers narrowly elliptic, 1.3-1.8 (0.8-2.2) mm long; styles 7.0-8.5 (6.0-9.1) mm long, united nearly to the summit; stigmas pale; fruit triangular-ovoid, 3.9-4.3 (3.6-4.6) mm high, 3.3-3.9 (2.9-4.3) mm in diameter, thick walled, with cartilaginous portion constituting more than one-half of the false septum; seeds narrowly ovate, 2.9-3.2 (2.6-3.3) mm long, 1.1-1.4 (1.0-1.6) mm wide, reddish brown.

description: Perennial herb, glabrous or rarely with lower part of stem sparsely hairy, 28-42 (24-73) cm tall, branched at the base and in the inflorescence; leaves opposite near the base or alternate throughout, linear to linear-lanceolate, 1-nerved, acute, 10-16 (8-19) mm long, 0.8-1.1 (0.6-2.1) mm wide; stipular glands present; inflorescence paniculate with ascending to spreading branches; fruit short pedicelled; sepals lanceolate to ovate, sharp pointed or acuminate, 2.9-4.3 (2.5-5.0) mm long, conspicuously glandular-toothed, the inner with a narrow scarious margin; petals lemon-yellow, oblanceolate or narrowly obcordate, 7-10 (6-11) mm long, pilose near the base; stamens 3-5 (2-8) mm long with diminutive slender triangular staminodia usually present; anthers elliptic, 0.6-0.8 (0.5-1.0) mm long; styles separate, 3.3-5.5 (2.8-6.5) mm long; fruit glabrous, ovate, sharp pointed, 2.3-2.8 (2.0-3.2) mm high, 2.3-2.5 (2.1-2.6) mm in diameter; false septa partially developed, both septa with marginal hairs; seeds reddish brown, ovate, 1.4-1.6 (1.2-1.9) mm long, 0.8-1.0 (0.7-1.1) mm wide.

description: Annual or frequently short-lived perennial herb, glabrous and glaucous, 26-38 (15-50) cm tall, branched usually at the base and above the middle, the branches rather stiffly spreading-ascending; leaves alternate, or the lowermost opposite, crowded at the base, entire, thick, oblanceolate to lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, the larger 8-17 mm long, 1.2-2.3 mm wide; stipular glands none; inflorescence ample, open, paniculate, the lower fruiting pedicels 5-46, commonly 20-30 mm long; sepals thin, lanceolate, 5.0-6.2 (4.4-7.0) mm long, the outer very sparsely glandular-toothed, the inner conspicuously toothed; petals lemon-yellow, 9-15 mm long, obovate, pubescent at the base; stamens 5-7 mm long; anthers 1.0-2.1 mm long; styles 5.7-8.9 mm long, separate 0.8-2.8 mm at the summit; stigmas pale; fruit ovate, distinctly longer than broad, sharp pointed and very easily crushed, 3.7-4.6 mm long, 2.5-3.1 mm in diameter, cartilaginous plates poorly developed; false septa not fully developed, but with loosely woven fringed margin; seeds reddish brown, 2.5-3.0 mm long, 0.9-1.2 mm wide.

description: Erect annual, glabrous throughout or puberulent near the base of the stem, 22-38 (15-52) cm tall, with few spreading-ascending branches; leaves alternate, linear 18-24 (11-30) mm long, 0.9-1.3 (0.7-1.6) mm wide, entire or the upper sparsely toothed; stipular glands none except in one northern plains population; inflorescence open, paniculate; sepals lanceolate, sometimes broadly so, sharply acute to acuminate, 1-nerved or faintly 3-nerved, conspicuously glandular-toothed, 5.9-8.0 (5.2-9.6) mm long, the inner with conspicuous scarious margins; petals yellow, obovate, 12-14 (9-18) mm long, pubescent near the base; stamens 6-8 mm long; anthers narrowly elliptic, yellow, 1.3-1.6 (1.0-1.8) mm long; styles 6.0-8.8 (4.7-11.0) mm long (or in one northern plains form as short as 3.0 mm); fruit elliptic, 4.0-4.3 (3.5-4.7) mm high, 2.9-3.0 (2.6-3.4) mm in diameter, pale, the dark seeds showing through the ovary wall; seeds brownish, narrowly ovate, 3.0-3.3 (2.6-3.6) mm long, 0.9-1.2 mm wide.

description: Annual herb, puberulent near the base, otherwise glabrous, striate, especially above, sparsely to rather profusely branched, the branches stiffly ascending-spreading, few flowered near the summit, 22-33 (11-57) cm tall; leaves alternate, linear, entire, the longer 10-17 (9-20) mm long, 0.8-1.3 (0.7-1.9) mm wide; stipular glands present near the base, or nearly throughout in a northern population; sepals mostly 1-nerved, thin textured, lanceolate to narrowly ovate, 5.0-5.6 (4.1-6.5) mm long, scarious margined, all delicately glandular-toothed, slender pointed; petals yellow to yellow-orange, without reddish base, oblanceolate to narrowly obovate, 6-8 (5-9) mm long; stamens (3-) 4-5 mm long, without staminodia; anthers 0.5-0.7 (0.4-0.8) mm long; styles 2.7-3.3 (2.0-4.0) mm long, united nearly to the summit, the stigmas pale; fruit ovoid, 3.4-3.7 (3.2-4.2) mm high, 2.8-3.1 (2.5-3.4) mm in diameter, relatively thick walled and with characteristic thickened areas at the summit in the region of the true septa; cartilaginous portion occupying somewhat less than one-half total of false septum; seeds lanceolate or narrowly ovate, 2.5-2.8 (2.1-3.0) mm long, 1.0-1.2 (0.8-1.3) mm wide.

description: Shrub to small tree 0.3-4 m tall. Leaves elliptic-oblong to oblong-oblanceolate, 3.6-8 x (1.5) 2-3 cm; secondary nerves usually absent below, faint above, 6-7 on each side of midnerve; tertiary venation none on the lower side, slightly im- pressed on upper side; petioles 2-5 mm long. Inflorescence 1.7-6 cm long. Sepals usually subequal, 1.1 x 0.9-1 mm; petals 3-4.5 x 1.8-1.9 mm, 4 times longer than wide; filaments 4-5 mm long; ovary 1-1.5 mm long; style 1.5-3.5 mm long, 1.5-2.7 (3) times longer than the ovary. Capsule 7-12.5 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree 2-5 m tall. Leaves coriaceous, suborbicular, obovate-oblong, or broadly oblong, 3-10 x 2-6 cm, obtuse to rounded at base, upper surface shining with prominently elevated 5-9 secondary nerves on each side of the midnerve and prominently elevated tertiary venation, lower surface with more or less prominent secondary and tertiary venation, the margins broadly and shallowly crenulate with 9-14 obscure sinuses on each side; petioles 1-3 mm long. Inflorescence consisting of many-flowered panicles, solitary or fasciculately clustered in the upper axils or subterminal. Sepals mainly equal, 1.2-2 x 1-1.5 mm; petals 4.1-6 x 2.1-2.5 mm, 2-3 times the length of the sepals; filaments 2.5-5 mm long; ovary 1.2-1.5 mm long; style 2-2.2 mm long, 1.4-1.8 times the length of the ovary. Capsule and seed not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. & Luteyn, James L. 1980. Revision of the genus Ochthocosmus (Linaceae). Brittonia. 32: 128-143.

description: Planta annua erecta, gracilis, simplex, 4-8 din. alta; caulibus obscure stramineis, teretibus striatis pubeseentibus et barbatibus; foliis alternis, aseendentibus, scabris, plerumque 5-7 cm. longis, 5-10 mm. latis, angusto-lanceolatis, ad basim lobis variabilibus deltoideis obtusis praeditis, marginibus varie serratis; inflores- centia corymbosa, 1-3 dichotoma; sepalis distinctis, anguste lanceolatis, longe acuminatis, 6 mm. longis; petalis luteis, ovatis, ad basim angustatis, 8 mm. longis; staminibus 10-15, omnibus ut videtur fertilibus, simplicibus.

description: An erect slender simple annual 4-8 dm. tall with ascending narrow leaves, branched only in the infloreseence. Stems dull straw-colored, terete, striate, pubescent and sparsely hispid with barbate hairs; leaves alternate, ascending, scabrous, mostly 5-7 cm. long, 5-10 mm. wide, linear-lanceolate with two variable deltoid, obtuse lobes at base, margins variably serrate, dark green and strigose above, light green, finely pubescent, and strigose below, venation pinnate, the midvein strong; infloreseence dichotomously branched 1-3 times, the later ones subtended by leaves or leaf-like bracts, pubescent and hispid; sepals distinct, narrowly lanceolate, long-acuminate, 6 mm. long, with a minute callous at apex; petals yellow, ovate, narrowed at base, 8' mm. long, nearly glabrous at apex; stamens 10-15, apparently all fertile, filaments simple, 4-5 mm. long; capsule sessile, linear, strongly barbate-hispid, 17-23 mm. long; seeds irregularly ribbed, striate, tuber- culate.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 5 mm. long; blades lanceolate, (3)5-6(7) cm. long, 1-2 cm. broad, obtuse at base, narrowed and acute at apex, dull, greyglauceseent above and fulvous beneath, chartaceous or subeoriaceous, 3-plinerved (principal nerves not prominent beneath), with the inner pair subopposite and diverging at 0-5 mm. from base, reticulation obscure on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets, petioles and blades beneath very densely fulvous-subhirtellous or velutinous, above minutely subsetulose with ascending or erect hairs forming a conspicuous fulvous line on midrib. Infloreseences in short-racemose eymes, loosely few-flowered (flowers mostly 5-7), fulvous-subhirtellous with spreading and ascending hairs, bracts lanceolate, subhirtellous, pedicels up to 3 mm. long, subhirtellous or glabrous; calyx-lobes deltoid-oblong, about 1 mm. long or somewhat longer, acute at apex, glabrous and very minutely papillose without, sparsely ciliate; corolla-lobes lanate on the lower half within, the upper half glabrous and papillose; ovary and style glabrous. Fruits not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description:
Macroscopic: petioles 3-4 mm. long; blades elliptic-obovate to lanceolate, 5-17.5 cm. long, 2.5-5 cm. broad, attenluate or subacute at base, usually short- to long-acuminate at apex, shining on both surfaces, drying greyish green with darkened petioles, coriaceous or subeoriaceous, 3-plinerved with the inner pair opposite and diverging at 1-12 mm. from base, reticulation mostly prominent or prominulous on both surfaces. Microscopic: leaves glabrous; blades beneath with whitish atomic dots within the tissue, above smooth to unevenly tuberculate.

Infloreseences in terminal eymes, broadly corymbose and rather loosely flowered, sparsely puberulent with short, greyish, erect or ascending hairs, bracts ovate or ovate-lanceolate, ciliate, peduncles none, pedicels up to 4 mm. long; calyx-lobes broadly ovate, about 1 mm. long, usually somewhat rounded or obtuse at apex, ciliate, otherwise glabrous; corolla-tube about 1.5 cm. long, glabrous both without and within, not papillose, corolla-lobes about 4 mm. long, glabrous without, papillose and glabrous within except for sparse long hairs near sinuses; anthers sessiloid, slightly exserted, oblong- oblanceolate, up to 2.75 mm. long, acuminiate and glabrous at base; style pilose. Fruits not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 5 mm. long; blades lanceolate or elliptic, about 7 cm. long and 2.5 cm. broad, obtuse to acute at base, acuminate and mostly pointed at apex, rather shining on both surfaces but paler beneath, chartaceous or subcoriaceous, 3-plinerved with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 1-6 mm. from base, reticulation rather faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets glabreseent and with the stipule- lines sparsely ciliate; petioles minutely and sparsely puberulent, sparsely ciliate near base; blades essentially glabrous on both surfaces, beneath with minute whitish atomic dots when mature. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, corymbose, glabrous, bracts ovate to ovate-lanceolate and ciliate, otherwise glabrous, pedicels up to 2.5 mm. long; calyx-lobes broadly ovate, about 1 mm. long, acute at apex, ciliate, otherwise glabrous; corolla-tube up to 1.3 (-1.5) cm. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose within from about middle upward and glabrous at throat (sometimes with a corona as in S. panamensis), corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous both without and within, not bearded at base; anthers and style essentially as in S. panamensis. Fruits not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 3-12 mm. long; blades ovate to lanceolate, 4-13 cm. long, 3-6.5 cm. broad, subeordate to obtuse or subacute at base, rounded to acuminate at apex, often mucronulate, mostly shining on both surfaces and metallic in appearance,, sometimes paler beneath, chartaceous to coriaceous, 5-plinerved (the basal-marginal nerves sometimes prominent) with the inner pair usually alternate and diverging at 8-30 mm. from base, the principal nerves often manifestly pinnate along midrib, reticulation usually prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: essentially like S. guianensis except that there is a marked trend towards extreme glabrescence. Inflorescences essentially as in S. guianensis, usually more glabreseent; flowers as in S. guianensis. Fruits globose, about 2 cm. diam., yellow, seeds thick, reniform.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 5 mm. long; blades elliptic to lanceolate, (6-)10-15(-17) cm. long, 3.5-7 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, acuminate and finally pointed at apex, dull on both surfaces, greyish green on drving, chartaceous, 3-plinerved (principal nerves impressed above) with the inner pair subopposite and diverging at or near base, reticulation finely intricate and faint or prominulous on both surfaces. Microscopic: branches and petioles hirsute with long (up to about 1.5 mm.) rusty straight hairs and also with shorter curved inconspicuous hairs; blades beneath hirsute with long rusty hairs on principal nerves and sometimes sparsely so on lesser veins, above tuberculate, hirsute on midrib and less densely so on the inner pair of principal nerves, leaf-margins subeiliate with long hairs. Infloreseences in congested eymes (about 0.8 cm. long), densely fulvoushirsute, bracts lanceolate and long-acuminate, hirsute without and glabrous within, pedicels very short or none; calyx-lobes narrowly lanceolate, 2-3 mm. long, acute to subulate at apex, hirsute without, ciliate, not papillose or inerassate; corollas not seen; ovary glabrous or with several pili at apex, style pilose at base. Fruits (Krukoff 6060) ellipsoid ( ?), 2.5 cm. long, 2 cm. broad, mucronate at apex, shell about 0.5 mm. thick, carnose and not osseous, wrinkled, shining, seeds 1 (or 2), about 20 mm. long, 14 mm. broad, 3 mm. thick, testa rugulose on with brownish membranaceous squamae still adherent; fruit-pedicels about 1 mm. in diam.

description: Macroscopic: branchlets slender; petioles 1-2 mm. long; blades lanceolate from an ovate base, 3-7 cm. long, 1.5-2 cm. broad, rounded or truncate or obscurely subcordate at base, long-acuminate and finely poilited at apex, rather dull on both surfaces, brighter green beneath, membranaceous, be- coming chartaceous in age, 3-plinerved (principal nerves not prominent above) with the inner pair opposite and diverging at or very near base, reticulation loose and faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets pubescent with short curved hairs; petioles rather densely pubescent with short curved hairs and also with longer straight hairs; blades beneath pubescent with short, mostly curved hairs on principal nerves, especially on midrib, and with inconspicuous minute whitish atomic dots which sometimes form the bases of very short hairs, above puberulent on principal nerves or often sparsely hairy throughout, especially near margins, leaf-margins sparsely ciliate, especially near base. Infloreseences in terminal (and axillary) eymes, corymbose and rather loosely few-flowered, puberulent to subsetulose with short, ascending, rusty, somewhat curved hairs, pedicels up to 4 mm. long; calyx-lobes linear-lanceo- late, up to 3 mm. long, acute at apex, well pubeseent without, especiallv near the ciliate margins, sparsely pubescent within, especially near apex; corolla- tube up to 1.3 cm. long, papillose and glabrous without (papillae above sometimes elongated, giving the appearance of pubescence), pilose from below middle upward to throat within, corolla-lobes glabrous without, pilose within mostly on the lower half with an indumentum continuous and similar to that within corolla-tube; anthers sessiloid, ilieluded except for their tips; style glabrous. Shells of mature fruits (H.J.B.R. 22350) less than 0.5 mm. thick, shinino and smooth, lightly reticulate-wrinkled with ridges hardly raised, seeds 2, generally oval, with opposite sides and faces somewhat convex on one and lightly concave on the other, up to 13 mm. long and 10 mm. broad. Embryo (Progel, l.e.) in middle of seed, cotyledons subcordate-ovate and somewhat longer than the arcuate radiele.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 4-11 mm. long; blades usually elliptic to lanceolate, 8-20 cm. long, 3-10 cm. broad, obtuse to acute at base, gradually narrowed to subacuminate at apex, dull or somewhat shining on both surfaces, sometimes glaueeseent beneath, drying greyish green with blackened petioles, chartaceous or subcoriaceous, 3(5)-plinerved with the inner pair usually alternate and diverging at 0-11 mm. from base, reticulation on both surfaces prominent to rather faint with the ultimate veinlets hardly raised. Microscopic: branchlets essentially glabrous and with the stipule-lines faintly puberulent-ciliate, becoming glabrous; leaves essentially glabrous, the blades beneath with inconspicuous atomic dots within the tissue (sometimes scattered, very short hairs present), above essentially smooth. Infloreseences in congested eymes (up to 1.5 cm. long), densely puberulent or subhirtellous with short pale hairs, becoming glabreseent, bracts usually broadly ovate, rounded or obtuse at apex, concave and usually crowded (bracteoles often imbricate under calyx), subhirtellous without but glabrous near the ciliate margins, pedicels very short or none, becoming thickened; calyx-lobes broadly ovate, about 1 mm. long, rounded to obtuse or subacute at apex, puberulent or subsetulose with short, greyish, adpressed or ascending hairs without but glabrous near the ciliate margins, glabrous or with sparse hairs within, becoming inerassate at base; corolla-lobes densely lanate on the whole face within; ovary pilose on the upper half  (usually tapering at apex after anthesis), style pilose at base. Fruits (Smith 2904) immature, ellipsoid, about 3 cm. long and 2 cm. broad, short-stalked at base and mucronate at apex, shell about 0.75 mm. thick, exocarp carnose and mesocarp somewhat osseous, shining, wrinkled in drying, seeds 2, oval, about 16 mm. long, 12 mm. broad, 4 mm. thick, flattened or somewhat convex on both faces, testa rugulose; fruit-pedicels about 2 mm. in diam.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: branches einereous; bases of branchlets with many per- sistent keeled acute cataphylls; petioles about 8 mm. long; blades elliptic- obovate to elliptic-oblanceolate, 10-15 cm. long, 5-7 cm. broad, obtuse or subacute at base, usually abruptly short-acuminate at apex, shining on both surfaces, drying greyish green with darkened petioles, coriaceous or sub- coriaceous, 3-plinerved (the additional pair of basal-marginal nerves prominulous) with the inner pair opposite and diverging at 0-4 mm. from base, reticulation prominent or prominulous on both surfaces. Microscopic: leaves glabrous; blades beneath with whitish atomic dots within the tissue, smooth on both surfaces. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, broadly corymbose and somewhat densely flowered, glabrous, bracts ovate to ovate-lanceolate, ciliate, peduilcles 0-2 cm. long, pedicels short or none; calyx-lobes broadly ovate, about 1 mm. long, usually somewhat rounded at apex, ciliate, otherwise glabrous; corolla- tube up to 2 cm. or more long, glabrous both without and within, not papillose, corolla-lobes about 4 mm. long, glabrous without, papillose and glabrous within except for sparse long hairs along edges near sinuses; anthers sessiloid, slightly exserted, oblong-oblanceolate, up to 2.5 mm. long, acuminate and beset with several short pili at base; style glabrous. Fruits not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 1 mm. long; blades ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.5-4.5 cm. long, 1.5-2.5 cm. broad, conspicuously cordate to rounded at base, gradually narrowed or rounded and mucronulate at apex, dull or somewhat shining on both surfaces, paler beneath, memnbranaceous to chartaceous or subcoriaceous, 3(5)-plinerved (principal nerves not prominent beneath) with the inner pair opposite or subopposite and diverging at 0-3 mm. from base, reticulation faint or obscure on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles densely pubescent with minute, pale-rusty, ascending (or spreading), subsetulose hairs; blades beneath pubescent with minute, rusty, erect or ascending, straight or curved, subsetulose hairs, the indumentum more dense in axils of the inner principal nerves, thus occasionally giving a barbate appearance, above pubescent with minute subsetulose deciduous hairs, most persistent on midrib. Infloreseences and flowers essentially as in S. guianensis except that the infloreseences are subsetulose with hairs somewhat more spreading. Fruits (Krukoff 7804) immature, ellipsoid, about 2 cm. long and 1 cm. broad, shell less than 0.5 mm. thick, shining, smooth, regularly spotted with black dots, seed 1, somewhat elliptic, about 15 mm. long, 8 mm. broad, 4 mm. thick, straight or slightly concave on one side and convex on the opposite side, flattened or irregularly convex on both faces and umbonulate at about middle of one face, testa with adherent remains of brownish membranaceous squamae.

description: Macroscopic: petioles about 8 nim. long; blades usually elliptic to lanceo- late, 6-15 cm. long, 2.5-8.5 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse or acute at base, abruptly short-acuminate at apex, shining on both surfaces, oftell drying an ocher yellow with blackened petioles, coriaceous, usually 3-plinerved with the inner pair subopposite or conspicuously alternate and diverging at 4-15 mm. from base, reticulation usually intricate and prominent, especially be- neath. Mtcroscoptc: petioles very sparsely puberulent, becoming glabrous; blades essentially glabrous on both surfaces, beneath with conspicuous crowded whitish atomic dots (sometimes forming the bases of very short, adpressed hairs), above sometimes uiievenly tuberculate. Infloreseences in axillary clustered eymes, congested and many-flowered, sparsely puberulent with short adpressed rusty hairs, pedicels very short or none; calyx-lobes broadly ovate, less than 1 mm. long, usually rounded at apex, ciliate, otherwise glabrous or with a few hairs without; corolla-tube up to 0.8 cm. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose within, most densely so near throat but glabrous at throat itself, corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous without, densely bearded at base within (sometimes on a flap of raised tissue) ; anthers sessiloid, hidden beneath wool on corolla-lobes, less than 1 mm. long; style sparsely pilose. Fruits not seen.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 5-10 mm. long; blades variable in shape, elliptic, oblong or elliptic-ovate to lan?eolate, 6-13 cm. long, 3.5-6.5 cm. broad, rounded or obtuse to attenuate and acute at base, acuminate at apex, usually dull on both surfaces, drying aA olive-ocher yellow with brownish or black- ened petioles, coriaceous, 3- or 5-plinerved with the inner pair subopposite or alternate and diverging at 0-7 min. from base, reticulation faint and loose to somewhat prominulous on both surfaces, the ultimate veinlets hardly raised. Microscopic: branchlets glabrous or puberulent (densely or sparsely so) with very short, pale-rusty, more or less adpressed hairs; petioles glabreseent or well puberulent with very short, pale, adpressed or ascending hairs; blades beneath with inconspicuous atomic dots and inconspicuously or well universally puberulent with very short, adpressed hairs which are sometimes elongated in the axils of inner principal nerves, above smooth to tuberculate or blistered and glabrous or puberulent on midrib (and on the inner pair of principal nerves) near base. Infloreseences in terminal eymes, subhemispheric and many-flowered, about 4 cm. long and somewhat broader (the flowering branches about 6 cm. long exclusive of infloreseence-length, glabreseent, the leaves reduced to cataphylls), sparsely puberulent with scattered, adpressed, short hairs of unequal length, pedicels distinct, up to 2 mm. long, glabreseent or sparsely puberulent; calyx-lobes deltoid-ovate to deltoid-lanceolate, about .75 mm. long, acute at apex, ciliate, otherwise glabrous both without and within; corolla-tube about 7 mm. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose within for the greater part but glabrous at throat, corolla-lobes up to 3 mm. long, papillose and glabrous without, densely lanate-bearded at base within, other- wise glabrous and densely papillose; anthers sessiloid, generally hidden beneath wool on corolla-lobes, oblong, less than 1 mm. long; style glabrous. Fruits not seen.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 3-8 mm. long; blades broadly ovate or orbicular to elliptic-lanceolate, 15-30 cm. long, 7-21 cm. broad, rounded or subcordate at base, usually abruptly short-acuminate from a rounded or somewhat narrowed apex, dull on both surfaces and usually rusty beneath, coriaceous, usually 5-plinerved (principal nerves deeply impressed) with the inner pair alternate and diverging at 3-30 mm. from base, either approximate or far removed from the next adjacent pair of principal nerves, the reticulationl of secondaries and tertiaries deeply impressed above, giving a bullate appearance, conspicuously prominent beneath and very loose, the fine reticulation of veinlets faint or obscure. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles very densely fulvous-tomentose with somewhat matted, curved (or straight) hairs; blades beneath densely fulvous-subhirtellous or velutinous to more sparsely pubescent and tuberculate with the bases of fallen hairs, above fulvous-velutinous when young to very sparsely subhirtellous (indumentum most persistent in the channel of midrib) and tuberculate with the bases of fallen hairs or smooth. Infloreseences in very densely congested eymes, corymbose to shortthyrsoid and many-flowered, thickly and densely fulvous-tomentose, bracts terminating the naked peduncles lanceolate, spreading at right angles, tomentose without and less so within, the secondary and tertiary bracts progressively shorter, becoming ovate and glabreseent to glabrous within, bracteoles crowded closely under calyx, peduncles about 2.5 mm. wide, pedicels very short or none; calyx-lobes broadly ovate, about 1 mm. long, more or less acute at apex, erect, papillose without and pubescent from about center to base, ciliate; corolla-lobes erect, papillose without with papillae often elongate into short hairs, rather densely long-bearded (with upwardly oblique hairs) near middle within along an upwardly convex are, above which the lobes are not papillose but thick and keeled, and below which, on the lower half, they are obscurely papillose and often with a few stray pili along margins, otherwise glabrous; anthers barbate at base with conspicuous pili which are easily broken off, filaments often pilose near base and at the place of their insertion on corolla-tube; ovary and style glabrous. Fruits (Krukoff 7803) mature, globose, about 2 cm. in diam., shell about 0.75 mm. thick, dull, smooth, somewhat reticulate-marked or tuberculate, seeds usually 2, oval, about 16 mm. long, 11 mm. broad, 5 mm. thick, convex on both faces, testa rugulose; fruit-pedicels about 3 mm. in diam.

description: Ramuli hornotini dense ferrugineo-hirtelli; petiolus 4-7 mm. longus, ferrugineo-hirtellus; folia 13-19 cm. longa, 5-11.5 cm. lata, elliptico-lanceo- lata vel elliptico-orbicularia, breviter acuminata, ad basim ex rotunda ad obtusa, subeoriacea vel coriacea, opaca, 5- vel 7-nerva, subtus dense ferrugi- neo-tomentosa, supra plus minusve setulosa, nervi intimi principales ad basim laminae orientes 1-2 cm., supra depressi. Macroscopic: petioles 4-7 mm. long; blades mostly broadly elliptic to lanceolate, 13-19 cm. long, 5-11.5 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, rounded to short- or long-acuminate at apex, dull on both surfaces, the old ones sometimes drying in part an olive-ocher yellow, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, 5- or 7-plinerved with the inner pair usually alternate, diverging at 10-20 mm. from base and with the greatest distance from midrib usually above middle, deeply impressed above, the secondaries im-pressed above and prominent beneath, reticulation very loose and faint above, more prominent beneath. Microscopic: brainchlets hirtellous and dlensely pubescent with brownish-rusty adpressed hairs; petioles rugose, usually densely pubescent with mostly spreadinig, rather stiff hairs; blades beneath densely, becoming sparsely, brownish-rusty pubescent and tuberculate with the bases of fallen hairs, above densely to sparsely pubescent, especially in channels of principal nerves.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 0.5-3 mm. long; blades ovate to lanceolate, 2-8 cm. long, 1.5-4 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, acuminate and usually finely pointed (sometimes blunt) at apex, dull on both surfaces and paler beneath, membranaceous to chartaceous, 3(5) -plinerved with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 1-11 mm. from base, reticulation obscure or faint on both surfaces. Microscopic: essentially like S. Poeppigi'i. Inflorescences and flowers essentially as in S. Poeppigii except that the peduncles are lacking or shorter than flower-clusters and the calyx-lobes are linear-lanceolate, 2-4 mm. long, and blacken upon drying. Mature fruits globose, about 1.2 cm. in diam., shell less than 0.5 mm. thick, shining, smooth, seeds 1 (or 2 ?), spheroid, 7-10 mm. long, brownish and translucent, sometimes covered with adhering thick pale felt formed in endocarp; fruitpedicels about 1 mm. in diam.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 6-13 mm. long; blades elliptic, broadly ovate, lanceolate or oblanceolate, 7-16 cm. long, 3.5-10 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse or somewhat acute at base, abruptly short-acuminate at apex, usually shining on both surfaces but duller beneath, the old ones often drying an olive-ocher yellow (the young a bright russet-brown), coriaceous, 3- or 5-plinerved with the inner pair opposite or subopposite and diverging at 2-10 mm. from base, reticulation prominent or prominulous on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets densely pale-fulvous puberulent with short adpressed hairs; petioles puberulent with short adpressed hairs at first palefulvous, becoming greyish in age; blades beneath with inconspicuous atomic dots and an universal puberulence of short adpressed hairs, becoming sparser but still obvious in age, above sometimes sparsely puberulent near base of midrib, otherwise essentially glabrous and smooth. Infloreseences in axillary elongated thyrses, up to 4 cm. long, densely fulvous-puberulent with adpressed, usually straight hairs, pedicels short or none; calyx-lobes ovate-lanceolate, up to 2 mm. long, acute at apex, ciliate and puberulent without and more conspicuously so within; corolla-tube densely papillose and glabrous without, glabrous at base within, otherwise pilose, corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous without, pubescent throughout within and very densely bearded at base; anthers sessiloid, slightly exserted from beneath wool on corolla-lobes, less than 1 mm. long; style glabrous. Fruits not seen.

description: Ramuli hornotini dense puberulentes; petiolus circa 7 mm. longus, puberulens; folia 8-14 cmi. longa, 3.5-7.5 cm. lata, elliptico-oblanceolata vel laneeolata, acuminata, ad basim plerumque obtusa, coriacea vel subcoriacea, supra nitida, subtus paullo pallidiora, 5- vel 3-nerva, subtus puberulentia, axillis nervorum subtus plerumque barbata, nervi intimi principales supra conspicue depressi ad basim laminae orientes 2-20 mm. Macroscopic: petioles about 7 mm. long; blades more or less elliptic, 8- 14 cm. long, 3.5-7.5 cm. broad, usually obtuse at base, gradually acuminate or abruptly caudate and blunt at apex, shining above, dull and pale beneath, drying an olive-ocher with blackened petioles when old, 5(3) -plinerved with the inner pair subopposite or alternate and diverging at 2-20 mm. from base, principal nerves and secondaries deeply impressed above, reticulation faint or prominulous on both surfaces with the ultimate veinlets hardly raised. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles densely puberulent with short rusty hairs, becoming sparsely so or glabreseent in age; blades beneath with crowded whitish atomic dots and universally puberulent with short, mostly adpressed hairs, sometimes with short pockets in axils of principal nerves and often barbate with rusty subbirtellous hairs that continue for a short distance up midrib, above puberulent on midrib near base, otherwise glabrous.

description:
Macroscopic: petioles 7-15 mm. long; blades elliptic to ovate, 6-22 cm. long, 4-13 cm. broad, rounded to acutish at base, abruptly short blunt-acuminate at apex, shining on both surfaces, mature leaves drying brownish with blackened petioles, coriaceous, 3-plinerved with the inner pair subopposite and diverging at about 5 mm. from base, reticulation intricate and prominent on both surfaces.

Microscopic: branchlets sparsely puberulent with short rusty curved hairs; petioles sparsely puberulent, becoming almost glabrous; mature blades beneath with inconspicuous atomic dots and well puberulent with short curved hairs especially along the midrib, immature blades barbate in axils of the inner pair of principal nerves, above puberulent along the midrib, becoming glabreseent and with obscure atomic dots embedded in the tissue, smooth.

Infloreseences in terminal eymes, subhemispheric and somewhat congested, sparsely puberulent with short rusty curved hairs, peduncles about 3 cm. long, pedicels very short or none; calyx-lobes deltoid-ovate, 1-1.5 mm. long, blunt to subacute at apex, well pubeseent without and ciliate; corolla-tube 0.5-0.7 cm. long, densely papillose without and well pubescent with mostly spreading, rusty, soft hairs, pilose within for the greater part but glabrous at throat, corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous to well pubescent without, densely bearded at base within and more or less pubescent the entire face; anthers sessiloid, about 1 mm. long; style glabrous. Fruit not seen.

description:
Macroscopic: petioles 4-5 mm. long; blades ovate-elliptic, about 10 cm. long, 6 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, obtuse to acute at apex, somewhat shining on both surfaces, subcoriaceous or coriaceous, 3-plinerved with a fainter pair of nerves near margins, the inner pair opposite or subopposite anld diverging 5-10 mm. from base, midrib raised above, reticulation prominent on both surfaces, the ultimate areolae being usually almost microscopic. Microscopic: leaf-blades belneath hirtellous-barbate in axils of the illnier principal nerves (more faintly so in axils of outer pair), otherwise glabrous, sometimes tuberculate.

Inflorescences in short corymbose thyrses, rather densely many-flowered, densely grey-puberulent with short erect hairs intermnixed with scattered, longer, brown hairs, bracts lanceolate and bracteoles ovate, ciliate, grey-puberulent without, pedicels very short or none; calyx-lobes broadly ovate, somewhat more than 1 mm. long, obtuse or rather acute at apex, well ciliate with spreading pale hairs, grey-ptiberulent without; corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous without, strongly bearded within along an upwardly convex are, otherwise glabrous; anthers barbate at base; ovary and style glabrous.

description: Dioecious, glabrous shrub, the foliage becoming dark when dry, in appearance very similar to Oryctanthus spicatus (Jacq.) Eichler; stems compressed when very young, with furfuraceous lines (as shown in Fig. 10) not reaching adjacent nodes; older stems terete, with minute lenticels and fine longitudinal cracks. Branching percurrent? Phyllotaxy decussate; leaves elliptical to broadly lanceolate, up to 6 X 4 cm inclusive of 6-9 mm, slightly canaliculate petiole; apex and base obtuse, the margins of the blade and petiole callused; venation pinnate but obscure, the blade rather coriaceous. Inflorescence a slender, indeterminate spike, single in the leaf axil, up to 4 cm long of which at least 1 cm consists of a 1 mm thick peduncle, the peduncle compressed and the 2 edges furfuraceous nearly to the lowest bracts. Flowers (only pistillate seen) dull green, up to 50 per spike, in decussating pairs, subtended by dark-margined bracts; bracteoles 2 per flower, black-margined, some- what less than 1 mm long, closing in a beak-like fashion when no fruit develops. Petals 6, 1.5 mm long, dimorphic, the long stamens with aborted anthers above middle of petal, attached by a slender, 0.5 mm long filament in basifixed fashion, the filament continuing downwardly as a thick buttress, the aborted anther with 4 well developed, yellow pollen-sacs (but lacking pollen) and terminating in a massive, conical, dark connective, the short stamens similar but the aborted anther in the middle of the petal on a shorter filament which is dorsifixed. Style straight, 1.5 mm long, with a capitate, papillate stigma, and surrounded by a smooth nectary.

description: Liana ramis vegetativis sericeis vel demum glabrescentibus, pilis aureis demum decoloribus, sessilibus, rectis et valde adpressis, brevissimis (ca. 0.2 mm longis). Folia opposita, basi petioli stipulis minutis triangularibus 0.5 mm longis instructa; petiolo 1.1-1.7 cm longo, sericeo, eglanduloso; lamina 11.0-17.5 cm longa, 6.5-11.5 cm lata, elliptica vel ovata vel rotunda, basi obtusa vel rotundata, margine plana integraque, apice acuminata, utrinque sparsim sericea vel demum glabrata, (0) 2 (4) glandulas abaxiales planas immersas in dimidio proximali inter costam marginemque aequidistantes gerenti; nervis lateralibus principalibus utrinque 5-6 venis tertiariis parallelis connexis, utrinque praecipue subtus prominentibus. Folia in inflorescentia minora. Inflorescentia terminalis axillarisque, decomposita, thyrsiformis, ramulis usque ad 7 in quoque nodo, proximaliter sericea ramis vegetativis similis, distaliter brevi-tomentosa, nodis distalibus bracteas foliiformes sed abrupte redactas 6-17 mm longas, petiolatas, sericeas, prominente 2-4-glanduliferas gerens; floribus in umbellis 4-floris vel corymbis 6-floris; bracteis floriferis 2-4 (6) mm longis, 1-2 mm latis, ovatis vel ellipticis, planis vel navicularibus, utrinque praecipue subtus tomentellis, eglandulosis; pedunculo 1.0-3.5 mm longo, tomentello, apice vel sub apice 2 bracteolas gerenti, has bracteis similes sed breviores et planiores. Floris pedicellus 2-4 mm longus, tomentellus. Sepala 5, libera, 2.5-3.0 mm longa, 1.0-1.5 mm lata, anguste ovata, apice obtusa et revoluta, abaxialiter tomentella, adaxialiter glabra, anticum eglandulosum, 4 lateralia omnia 1 glandulam magnam 1.5 mm longam, 1.0-1.5 mm latam, ovatam, apice acutam revolutamque gerentia. Petala 5, viridi-flava, abaxialiter sericea versus marginem glabra, adaxialiter glabra. Petala 4 lateralia inter sepala patentia, ungue 1.5-2.5 mm longo, 0.3-0.5 mm diametro, gracili, limbo 3.0-4.5 mm longo, 2.5-4.0 mm lato, rotundo vel latissime obovato, concavo, basi rotundato vel parum hastato, margine eroso et eglanduloso vel juxta petalum posticum pauciglandulifero; 2 petala antica parum majora quam 2 postica. Petalum posticum erectum, ungue 2.0 mm longo, 0.5 mm diametro, limbo 2.5-2.8 mm longo, 1.5-2.5 mm lato, elliptico vel obovato, basi cuneato, plano, margine toto circuitu glanduloso. Staminum 10 filamenta glabra, basi connata (usque ad 1 mm), 1.8-2.5 mm longa, in eodem flore heterogenea, longissimo sepalo antico opposito, 3 crassissimis petalis postico-lateralibus posticoque oppositis. Antherae subaequales, 0.8-1.0 mm longae, glabrae, basi cordatae, connectivo nonnullarum glanduloso-tumido. Pollen sphaericum 6 poris instructum. Ovarium 1.5 mm altum, sphaeroideum, tomentellum, 3 carpellis omnino connatis omnibus longitudinaliter 3-cristatis, triloculare loculis omnibus uniovulatis. Styli 3, 2.0 mm longi, antheras aequantes vel parum superantes, subaequales, glabri vel piliferi, anticus versus petalum posticum inclinatus, 2 postici arcuato-ascendentes, apice interne stigmatiferi et dorsaliter truncati vel unco brevissimo rotundatoque instructi. Fructus sparsim sericeus ex 3 (vel abortu 2-1) samaris in toro pyramidali gracilique gestis constans. Samara elliptica, 5-8 cm longa, 2.5-3.5 cm lata, nuce 10-13 mm longa, 7-9 mm lata, loculum fertilem ca. 4.5 mm diametro et 2 cavernulas laterales 1.5 mm diametro continente, areola ventrali lineari 11 mm longa 1.5 mm lata basi in rostrum 1.5 mm longum producta; alis lateralibus basi confluentibus apice discretis utraque late ovata, 2.5-4.0 cm longa, 2.5-3.5 cm lata, integra vel repanda; ala dorsali centrali 2.0-2.7 cm lata, 1.0-1.3 cm alta, semicirculari, repanda, apice nucis inter alas laterales parum producta; alis dorsalibus intermediis nullis vel in quoque latere crista dissecta usque ad 3 mm alta. Semen pyriforme fere 1 cm longum; embryo directus, radicula 1 mm longa, cotyledonibus 8 mm longis, 4 mm latis, crassis, in sectione transversali semicircularibus, subaequalibus, minori omnino directa, majori apice parum inflexa.

description: Shrub 2.5-4 m tall, the branchlets loosely sericeous to glabrate. Lamina of the larger leaves 15-17 cm long, 5-7.2 cm wide, elliptical or obovate, cuneate at the base, abruptly acuminate at the apex with the acumen 1-2 cm long, glabrate adaxially or sparsely sericeous on the midrib, loosely sericeous or subtomentose abaxially on the midrib and lateral veins and thinly so between the veins, bearing variable numbers of small impressed glands abaxially near the midrib or distant from it; petiole 1 1-15 mm long, sericeous or eventually glabrescent, eglandular; stipules 3.5-4 (5) mm long, narrowly triangular, connate except for the distal 1-1.5 mm, abaxially sericeous, adaxially sericeous proximally, glabrous distally. Inflorescence terminal, (10) 15-36 cm long, pendent, loosely sericeous or tomen- tose, a thyrse composed of 60-130 horizontal or reflexed cincinni of 1-3 (4) flowers; bracts 1.2-2.4 mm long, triangular, abaxially sericeous, eglandular; pri- mary peduncle (from base to joint of first flower) 3-13 mm long, bearing slightly below its apex 2 triangular bracteoles like the bract but smaller, both eglandular or 1 terminating in a stalked peltate gland, the more distal bracteoles of the cincinnus glandular or eglandular (1-flowered cincinni produce a gland on 1 of the first 2 bracteoles, but larger cincinni usually defer production of glands to the third or later bracteoles). Pedicel (8) 10-12 mm long in anthesis, up to 15 mm long in fruit, loosely sericeous. Sepals extending 0.5-1.5 mm beyond the glands, ovate, rounded at the apex, revolute in anthesis, glabrous on both sides but occasionally bearing a few hairs on the margin, all biglandular, the glands white, 2-3 mm long, ellipsoidal, free from the sepal distally and slightly reflexed, not fused with adjacent glands. Petals pink, glabrous, nearly entire (minutely dentic- ulate), dorsally smooth or slightly carinate only on the claw, 5.3-6 mm long, with the claw 1.5-2 mm long, the limb 3.8-4 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide, somewhat sagittate at the base and often revolute at the margin in anthesis, the posterior petal hardly different from the lateral 4 but more erect and with a slightly longer claw. Filaments straight, glabrous, free or slightly connate only at the very base, 2.2-2.5 mm long opposite the sepals, 1.8-2 mm long opposite the petals; anthers 1.3-1.4 mm long, glabrous, the wing 0.2-0.4 mm wide, widest distally and some- times exceeding the locules; pollen 3 (4)-colporate, with the colpi bifurcate at both ends. Receptacle glabrous. Ovary 1.5 mm high, glabrous, with all 3 locules fertile; styles ca 3 mm long, slightly exceeding the stamens, straight or slightly inbent at the apex, borne at the apex of the ovary. Cocci separating from a pyramidal base ca 0.8 mm high, 5.7-6 mm long, 3-3.3 mm wide, 2.5-2.8 mm deep, glabrous, narrowly ovoidal, not or only obscurely carinate at the apex, the proximal 1/5-1/4 filled with tough fibrous aerenchyma, the distal 3/4- 4/5 filled with the seed. Embryo with the thick cotyledons equal, flat, folded upward near their middle.

description: Frutex scandens ramis volubilis terminalibus teretibus adpresse pubescenti-sericeis. Stipulae minutae basi petioli coalitae. Folia subeoriacea flexibilia opposita. Petiolus 6-8 mm longus robustus dense adpresse sericeus supra suleatus parte media duobus glandulis parvis munitus basi stipulis minutis vel obsoletis adnatis. Lamina obovato-lanceolata vel obovato- elliptica acuminataque vel obovata apiceque rotundata basi obtuse cuneata interdum subrotundata, margine integra leviter inerassata saepe sparsis vel sparsis- simis glandulis subeylindricis praedita, 6-15 cm longa 3-9 cm lata; supra viridis glabra vel juvenilis praecipue supra costam pilosa, costa tenui impressa nervis secundariis filiformibus venulis tenuibus prominulis reticulatis; subtus pallide ochracea dense adpresseque pubescenti-sericea, costa elevata nervis secundariis 6-8 utroque latere prominentibus subpatulis marginem versus curvatis tenuiori- bus evenescentibus nervulis minoribus paucis prominuli-conspicuis ceteris obsoletis, basi eglandulosa. Inflorescentiae terminales thyrsoideae basi foliosae folia excedentes vel breviores 8-16 cm longae. Flores circa 7 mm diamitentes 6-10 in ramulis pseudoracemosi instructi. Axis rami ramulique paniculae dense adpresseque pubescenltes ochraceo-cinerei, basi pari foliis sursum bracteis ellipticis et linearibus decres- centibus 1.5-0.3 cm longis. Bracteae fertiles ovato-lanceolatae 1-1.4 mm longae. extus pubescentes. Pedunculi brevissimi 0-0.5 mm longi apice 2 bracteolis ob- longis extus pubescentibus 0.6-1 mm longis. Pedicelli teneri flexuosi rubescentes albo-sericeo-puberuli. Sepala crassiuscula ovata subacuta circa 1.6 mm longa 1 mm lata extus pubescenti sericea. Glandulae calycinis 8 ellipsoideis circa 1 mm longae. Petala lutea glabra lamina elliptico-oblonga (subobovata) margine integra 2.5-2.8 mm longa 1.5 mm lato, ungue circa 1 mm longo. Stamina subaequalia filamentis basi ampliatis coalitis glabris circa 1 mm longis, antheris ellipticis 0.5-0.6 mm longis connectivo granulato. Styli crassiusculi erecti glabri 1 mm longi apice truncato leviter dilatato et compresso angulo dorsali obtuso vel recto. Ovarium dense sericeo-villosum. Samarae alis lateralibus membranaceis late flavellatis margine superiori leviter vel profunde irregulariterque dentatis parce setosis 10 mm longis 10-18 mm latis, ala dorsali cristiformi acute denticulata 3-4 mm alta nucula ovoidea puberula 3.5 mm longa areola ventrali suborbiculari 1 mm diamitenti.

description: Frutex scandens ramis terminalibus sarmentosis tenuibus valde volubilis pubeseentibus. Stipulae geminatae interpetiolares triangulari-subulatae circa 1 mm longae. Folia chartaceo-membranacea opposita. Petiolus 1-14 mm longus flexuosus patulo-pubeseens apice biglandulosus. Lamina ovata basi rotundata vel subcordata apice attenuata acuteque acuminata margine integra leviter revoluta, 4-8 cm longa 2-5 cm lata, pallide ochraceoviridis; supra glabra nervis principalibus tenuissimis ceteris obsoletis; subtus dense molliterque pubeseens, pilis longis tenuibus supra basim fureatis patulis, costa prominenti nervis secundariis circa 5 utroque latere ascendentibus curvatis ad marginem tenuioribus anastomosantibus nervulis tertiis transversis parcis ceteris obsoletis, basi interdum glandulosa. Inflorescentiae thyrsoideae terminales basi foliosae ad 10 cm longae, floribus circa 1 cm diam. usque ad 35 in ramulis elongatis pseudoracemose dispositis; axi ramulisque dense einereo- vel ochraceo-tomentosis; bracteis inferioribus ovatis pubescentibus 2-3 mm longis, ceteris subulatis circa 1.5 mm longis. Pedunculi 1-2 mm longi pubescentes persistentes rigidi apice bibracteolati, bracteolis 0.5-1 mm longis subulatis. Pedicelli tenues 2-6 mm longi pubescentes. Sepala ovata obtusa extus pubescentia circa 1.8 mm longa. Glandulae calycis 8 ellipsoideae 1.5-1.8 mm longae. Petala lutea glabra lamina subrotundata vel late elliptica basi subcordata margine minute erosa 3.5-4 mm longa 3-4 mm lata, ungue crasso 1-1.5 mm longo. Stamina alternatim aequilonga filamentis glabris tenuibus 2-2.5 mm longis, antheris ellipticis glabris 0.8-1 mm longis. Styli paulo curvati crassiusculi glabri circa 2 mm longi apice leviter inerassati angulo interno protruso dorsali sterile obtuso. Ovarium dense tomentosum dorso alis lateralibus incipi- entibus minutissimis jam conspicuis.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1959. Studies in South American plants--V. Brittonia. 11: 163-172.

description: Shrub 1-4 m tall (rarely small tree), in thickets along streams and on plains and in mixed hillside forests. Bark grayish. Meristems densely tan-puberulent, but stems (and most herbage) becoming quickly glabrate. Leaves moderately to deeply cordate, broadly ovate, sometimes weakly 3-lobed, acute to abruptly acuminate, discolorous, minutely punctate (esp. below on main veins), 7-9-nerved, minutely ciliate-margined, glabrate above and below (or sometimes sparsely puberulent below, on veins), 13-23 cm long, usually somewhat broader than long. Domatia present. Foliar nectaries 3-5, small (2 mm long) but prominent, the central one 1/4-4/3 distance from leaf base, the lateral ones sub-basal. Petioles approximately equaling lamina, punctate, glabrate (or slightly puberulent apically). Stipules caducous. Pedicels 1-2 cm long (in flower) to 1.5-3 cm long (in fruit), stout and woody (2-3 mm diam.), densely puberulent becoming glabrate, surmounted by 3 bordered involucral nectaries that are somewhat irregularly inserted. Involucral bractlets 3, linear, 5-7 mm long, puberulent, caducous in fruit leaving scars above nectaries. Calyx 7-12 mm long, truncate becoming torn, pentamerous venation often discernible, yellowish puberulent without, pubescent within, becoming flaring (to 1.5 cm diam.) and ligneous in fruit. Flowers 5 cm diam., perfect. Petals 3 cm long, yellowish puberulent without where exposed in bud, otherwise glabrous, punctate, reflexed. Staminal column extended (4-5 mm long); filaments 4-10 mm, punctate; anthers yellow. Capsules 3-loculed (rarely 4-loculed), stipitate, elongate (3.5-4.5 cm long, 1.5-2 cm diam.), yellow-green puberulent without, glabrous and punctate within, with sparse hairs along suture, ligneous. Seeds 8-12 per locule, to 8 mm long, shiny glabrous, arillate, angularly turbinate, brown-black.
bibliographicCitation: Wilbur, Robert L. 1970. A new Costa Rican species of Centrapogon [C. talamancensis] (Campanualaceae-Lubelioideae). Brittonia. 21: 353-358.

description: Shrub or small tree to 12 m height. Stems densely tan-puberulent, becoming somewhat glabrate in age, showing punctae where puberulence has worn off. Leaves with small auriculate appendages, truncate to somewhat cordate, entire, ovate, 7-9-nerved, obtuse to acuminate, discolorous, glabrous above, up to 22 cm long, almost as broad, densely matted below with minute, pallid puberulence. Foliar nectaries 5-7, often elongate (1-5 mm), the central one ca. 2/3 distance from base, the lateral ones progressively nearer base. Petioles minutely puberulent or glabrate, approximately equaling lamina or somewhat shorter. Pedicels 1-2 cm long (in flower) to 3 cm (in fruit), densely and coarsely yellowish puberulent. Involucral bractlets three, subulate, 1-2 mm long, puberulent, often caducous. Calyx 5-10 mm long, yellowish, densely granular-puberulent without, glabrous and punctate within, hemispheric in bud, truncate becoming torn in flower and fruit. Petals (of staminate flowers) prominently punctate, reflexed, ca. 2 cm long, white; flowers 2.5 cm diameter. Staminal column with a dense cushion of white hairs; filaments numerous, 5-8 mm long, punctate; gynoecium lacking. Pistillate flowers smaller (1.5 cm diam.); filaments 1-2 mm; anthers sterile; stigma decurrent, recurved. Capsules 3-celled, 2-2.5 cm long, 1-1.5 cm diameter, ovoid to obovoid, yellowish green, granular-puberulent without, glabrous within; carpel wall 1.3 mm thick with glands buried in it. Seeds 8 mm long, angularly turbinate, glabrous, dark brown, arillate.
bibliographicCitation: Wilbur, Robert L. 1970. A new Costa Rican species of Centrapogon [C. talamancensis] (Campanualaceae-Lubelioideae). Brittonia. 21: 353-358.

description: Large shrub or small tree commonly up to 7 m, rarely taller. Bark grayish. Stems usually densely brown-tomentose. Leaves truncate or weakly cordate (rarely cuneate); ovate, elliptic, or rotund; obtriangular, angularly obovate (obtrullate), or shallowly 3-lobed; acute to acuminate, 5-7-nerved, glabrate above (except puberulent on main veins), puberulent below, discolorous, minutely punctate, 8-17 cm long, 2%3 as wide to slightly wider than long. Foliar nectary single, basal or nearly so (rarely extending onto petiole), 2-5 mm long. Petioles tomentose, 1/4 length of lamina to nearly equaling lamina. Stipules inconspicuous (2 mm long), caducous. Pedicels usually densely tomentose, 1.5-4 cm long, slender (0.5 mm diam.). Involucral nectaries lacking. Involucral bractlets 3, linear, puberulent, 1-4 mm long, caducous before anthesis. Calyx hemispheric to ovoid in bud, densely tan-puberulent, 4-7 mm long, truncate (or rarely weakly 5-lobed), splitting in flower and reflexed in fruit, punctate. Flowers 1.5-2.5 cm diam. Petals white (sometimes pinkish in sicco), punctate, 1-1.5 cm long, yellowish lepidote without where exposed in bud, glabrous within, reflexed. Stamens (of staminate flowers) numerous, punctate, 3-5 mm long; gynoecium lacking. Stamens (of pistillate flowers) reduced, non-dehiscent; stigma decurrent, linear, pubescent, recurved, exceeding androecium by 4-5 mm. Capsules globose to ovoid (often trigonally so), 3-loculed, rostrate, densely grayish green- puberulent without, 1.5 cm long, nearly as wide, woody; carpel walls 1.5-3 mm thick, glabrous within except for sparse hairs along suture. Seeds 3 or 4 per cell, 4-5 mm long, turbinate, glabrous, brown-black (except for paler vasculature), arillate; aril nearly enclosing seeds.
bibliographicCitation: Wilbur, Robert L. 1970. A new Costa Rican species of Centrapogon [C. talamancensis] (Campanualaceae-Lubelioideae). Brittonia. 21: 353-358.

description: Shrub or small tree 2-7 m tall. Meristem brown-pubescent but herbage otherwise essentially glabrous. Stems glabrate, minutely but densely punctate. Leaves deeply cordate or sometimes truncate, sometimes weakly lobulate but usually cordate-acuminate, discolorous, 7-9-nerved, minutely punctate, glabrous above and below (or with scattered stellate hairs on main veins below), 7-16 cm long, as broad or slightly broader, without domatia. Foliar nectaries inconspicuous (1-2 mm), 3-5, the central one 1/2-/8 distance from leaf base, the lateral ones progressively nearer base. Petioles usually glabrous, punctate, 1/2 length of lamina to slightly exceeding lamina. Stipules linear, inconspicuous (2-3 mm long), pubescent, early caducous. Pedicels 1-1.5 cm long (in flower) to 1-3 cm long (in fruit), 1-1.5 mm diam., glabrous or somewhat lepidote, punctate. Involucral nectaries 3, raised and bordered, usually irregularly inserted (often on pedicel below calyx). Involucral bractlets minute, subulate, very early caducous. Calyx ovoid in bud, 6-9 mm long, weakly 5-nerved, often 5-toothed (with slight pubescence at apices), sparsely lepidote to glabrate, yellowish toward base, obscurely punctate, splitting in flower and somewhat reflexed in fruit. Petals white, 1.5-2 cm long, punctate, densely lepidote without where exposed in bud, glabrous within. Flowers 2.5 cm diam., perfect. Stamens yellow, numerous; filaments 3-6 mm long; stigma clavate, recurved, not exceeding androecium. Capsules 3-loculed (rarely 4-loculed), elongate (3-3.5 cm long, 1.5-2 cm diam.), stipitate, obtuse or sometimes retuse, densely yellow-puberulent without, glabrous and white within. Seeds black, arillate, ca. 6-8 per locule. Cotyledons symmetrical, foliose.
bibliographicCitation: Wilbur, Robert L. 1970. A new Costa Rican species of Centrapogon [C. talamancensis] (Campanualaceae-Lubelioideae). Brittonia. 21: 353-358.

description: Large tree of 10-30 m height. Bark grayish white; wood white, weak. Twigs terete, densely brown-puberulent, but worn smooth when woody. Leaves entire, truncate or slightly cuneate, ovate to elliptic, acute to acuminate, 5-nerved, up to 20 cm long (ca. 1 1/2 times as long as broad), discolorous, glabrate (or sparsely puberulent) above, densely and finely brown-puberulent below, with very small auriculate appendages at base. Foliar nectaries 3-5, small (1-3 mm) but often prominent, the central one ca. 1/2 distance from leaf base, the lateral ones progressively nearer base. Petioles 1/3-1/2 length of lamina (rarely shorter), puberulent. Pedicels 1.5-2 cm long (in flower), 2-3 cm long (in fruit), slender (1-2 mm diam.), densely brown-puberulent, sometimes surmounted by three prominent, bordered involucral nectaries. Involucral bractlets 3, triangular, minute (1 mm), puberulent. Calyx hemispheric in bud, truncate becoming torn in flower and fruit, 5-8 mm long, yellowish tan-puberulent. Petals densely yellowish puberulent without where exposed in bud, glabrous within, sparsely punctate, reflexed, 2 cm long or longer, white. Flowers 2.5 cm diameter. Filaments (of staminate flowers) white, sparingly punctate, 9-10 mm long with cushion of hairs at base of staminal tube (i.e., in throat of corolla). Pistillate flowers not seen. Fruits yellow-puberulent, obovoid, 2.5 cm long, 1.5 cm diameter.

description: Shrub 2-4 m tall. Meristem minutely red-brown-puberulent but foliage otherwise glabrescent. Stems glabrate, punctate. Leaves truncate or cuneate, elliptic or ovate, entire, acuminate, 3-5-nerved, glabrate, without basal appendages, copiously punctate, 20-25 cm long, 1/2-2/3 as wide as long. Foliar nectaries single, basal, 2-3 mm long. Domatia absent. Petioles 1/2-2/3 as long as lamina, glabrate, punctate. Stipules linear, 7-12 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, brownish puberulent, punctate, caducous. Flowers axillary, on branched peduncles rather than in fascicles; inflorescences short; peduncles 4-6 mm long, brown-puberulent; pedicels 6-7 mm long (in fruit), 1.5 mm diam., brown-puberulent. Involucral nectaries lacking. Involucral bracts 3, brown-puberulent, 1-3 mm long, linear. Calyces brown-puberulent, punctate, 3-4 mm long, minutely 5-denticulate on margin, not tearing in fruit. Petals white, punctate; anthers yellow. Capsules stipitate, globose, 1.5 cm long, 3-loculed, brown-puberulent without, glabrous within with no suture hairs. Seeds 7-8 mm long, shiny black, glabrous, arillate (aril small).

description: Small tree 4-7 m, often with multiple trunks. Young growth densely brown- puberulent; twigs angular. Leaves profoundly cordate, 7-9-nerved, 15-26 cm long, 18-31 cm broad, 3-5-lobed, lobes acute to obtuse, sparingly puberulent to glabrate above, moderately puberulent below. Foliar nectaries 5-9, narrowly elongate (2-8 mm long), all distally placed (1/2-7/8 distance from leaf base). Petioles densely and finely puberulent, almost equaling to slightly exceeding length of lamina. Stipules linear, 3-15 mm long, puberulent, caducous. Pedicels 0.5-2 cm long (in flower) to 2-3 cm long (in fruit), angular, densely yellowish puberulent, 2-3 mm diam. In- volucral nectaries 3, bordered. Involucral bracteoles 3, linear to triangular, 3-8 mm long, yellowish puberulent, exceeding calyx in young buds but shorter than calyx in flower, caducous in fruit. Calyx roughly oblate in bud, transversely rugose on lower half, upper half flat-topped, with 5 minute teeth on margin and corresponding pentamerous venation, expanding and tearing in flower and fruit, 8-10 mm long, yellow-puberulent. Flowers 3.5 cm diameter, perfect. Petals white, 1.5-2 cm long, yellow-lepidote without where exposed in bud, nearly glabrous (and somewhat shiny) within except along exposed margin where covered with simple ascending hairs (ca. 0.3 mm long), punctate. Stamens numerous; filaments punctate, up to 8 mm; anthers yellow, dehiscent. Pistil present, not exceeding stamens; stigma clavate with somewhat divergent lobes (?). Capsule 3-loculed, elongate (3-4.5 cm long, 1.5-2 cm diam.), chartreuse-puberulent without, glabrous and white within except along suture margin, which has dense white hairs (1-2 mm long) directed inwards. Seeds 8-10 per locule, 5-7 mm long, rounded, glabrous, brownish, arillate; arils small.
bibliographicCitation: Wilbur, Robert L. 1970. A new Costa Rican species of Centrapogon [C. talamancensis] (Campanualaceae-Lubelioideae). Brittonia. 21: 353-358.

description: Small tree to 12 m tall, in wet forest, usually growing directly on stream bank. Twigs glabrate (except for slight puberulence on meristem), minutely punctate. Leaves entire, truncate to slightly cuneate, ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, 5-7-nerved (sometimes with domatia), usually 12-23 cm long (1.5-2 times as long as broad), minutely punctate, discolorous, glabrous above and below without marginal cilia. Foliar nectaries 3-5, small (0.5-1 mm) and inconspicuous, round, the central one 1/2-3/4 distance from leaf base, the lateral ones progressively nearer base. Petioles 1/-2 to almost equaling the length of lamina (rarely shorter), minutely punctate, minutely brown-puberulent at distal end but otherwise glabrate. Stipules 2-10 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, linear, punctate, somewhat puberulent, caducous. Pedicels 1-2 cm long (in flower) to 2-3.5 cm (in fruit-rarely to 6 cm), slender (1-1.5 mm diam.), minutely brown-puberulent or glabrate. Involucral nectaries lacking. Involucral bractlets 3, linear, 1/2-3/4 mm wide, of variable length, sometimes 2-3 mm long, sometimes up to 10 mm long (and then often exceeding calyx), minutely punctate, minutely and sparsely brown-puberulent, usually inserted on calyx, often caducous, leaving scars. Calyx hemispheric in bud, truncate, densely and minutely brown-puberulent, 4-6 mm long, flaring in fruit, the margin becoming undulate rather than torn. Flowers 1.5-2 cm diam. Petals densely lepidote without where exposed in bud, glabrous within, punctate, reflexed, 1-1.5 cm long, yellowish white. Filaments (of staminate flowers) numerous, 3-5 mm; anthers bright yellow. Pistillate flowers not seen. Fruits 3- celled, densely and minutely brown-puberulent without (brownish green when fresh), spherical to slightly obovoid, obtuse (or with short apiculum), 1.5-2 cm long, densely rufous-hirsute within (hairs simple, 1 mm). Seeds 1 per locule (?), 9-10 mm long, shiny black, glabrous, arillate.

description: Subspecies sharpiana is distinguished by the glabrate petioles, fine crenate leaf margins, and smaller flowers which are 4-5.5 cm in diameter and with petals 2-3 cm long.
