description: Arbor parva dioecia, 7-10 m, sylvarum humilium deciduarum. Surculi densissime fulvi-puberuli. Folia truncata vel profunde cordata, ovata vel aliquantum 3-lobata, acuta vel acuminata, 5-7-nervia, 10-19 cm longa, 2/3 latiora quam longiora vel paulo latiora quam longiora, parce puberula supra (praecipue in venis; pili stellati saepe 2 brachia ascendentes diminutis sunt), dense mollis-puberula infra (pilis stellatis multi-brachiatis). Nectaria foliorum 1-5, parva, nectario centrali in centro laminae disposito (ca. 1/2-2/3 e basi semotus). Petioli quam laminae 1/3_2/3 longiori, dense puberuli. Stipulae filiformae, pubescentes, 3-8 mm longae, punctatae, caducae. Pedicelli 8-12 mm longi (in floris) vel 1.5-4 cm longi (in fructus), dense tomentosi et graciles (1-2 mm diam.) in floris, validescentes et lignosescentes (2-3 mm diam.) in fructus. Nectaria involucralium saepe prominentes, marginata. Bracteolae involucralium 3, lineares, calycem sub-aequans (4-8 mm longae, 0.5 mm latae), punctatae, tomentosae moderate. Calyces in alabastra ovoidei et praeclusi, truncati, lacerescentes in florem et reflexescentes in fructum, dense et minute puberuli, 5-12 mm longi. Petala 1.5 cm longa, punctata, lepidota extus, glabra intus, flavida, reflexa. Stamina florum pistillorum aggregata infra stigma in fila brevia; antherae non-dehiscentes; stigmata clavata, torta et recurvata, androecia 2-3 mm excedentes. Flores staminati ignotus. Capsulae 3-loculatae, ovoideae vel globosae, 2.5-3.5 cm longae, flavidae-puberulae extus, glabrae intus; parietes carpellorum lignei, 2 mm crassi. Semina 5-8 per loculum.
bibliographicCitation: Wilbur, Robert L. 1970. A new Costa Rican species of Centrapogon [C. talamancensis] (Campanualaceae-Lubelioideae). Brittonia. 21: 353-358.

description: Arbuscula vel frutex amplus, late ramosus, usque ad 10 m, dioecia, sylvarum pluvialum tropicalum, et terrarum turbatarum contiguarum. Cortex cinerascens; ramunculi virides, glabrati. Folia cordata vel interdum truncata, late ovata vel modice trilobata, acuta vel acuminata, palmatim 7-9-nervata, plerumque 15-20 cm longa, fere quam lata, obscure punctata, glabrata supra et infra (raro puberula minute et parce infra), domatiis nullis. Nectaria foliorum 5-7, parva (1 mm), nectario centrali distali disposito (ca. 2/3-/8 e basi semotus), nectariis lateralibus proximalio- ribus dispositis. Petioli longitudines laminarum aequantes (raro superantes) vel dimidio longiores, glabrati, minute punctati. Stipulae filiformes, 2-4 mm longae, glabratae, caducae maturae. Pedicelli 1-2.5 cm longi (in floris) vel 1.5-4 cm longi (in fructus), graciles (0.75-1.5 mm diam.), flavescentes-puberuli. Nectaria in- volucralium nulla. Bracteolae involucralium 3, subulatae, inconspicuae, 1-3 mm (raro 8 mm) longae, flavescentes-puberulae, saepe caducae, ad basim calycis insertae. Calyces hemisphaerici (in alabastra), truncati, flavescentes-puberuli, 4-8 mm longi (plerumque 5 mm), non (vel rarissimo) lacerescentes in florem et fructum. Flores 1.5-2 cm diam. Petala alba, 1-1.5 cm longa, parce punctata, flavi-lepidota extus ubi in alabastra exposita, glabra intus, reflexa in florem. Stamina florum staminorum numerosa, exserta; tubi staminum glabri, punctati, ubique antheriferi; filamenta pallida, epunctata, 5-9 mm longa; gynoecia nulla. Flores pistillati androeciis reductis: filamentis 1-2 mm longis; antheris non-dehiscentibus; cumulis antherarum 2-4 mm diam.; stigmatibus androecia excedentibus, clavatis, recurvis. Capsulae flavovirentes- puberulae, globosae, stipitatae, rostratae, 1.5-2 cm longae, patentissimae ubi maturae; parietes interior carpellorum albi, glabri praeter secus suturas cum pilis albis. Semina arillata, nigra, nitida-glabra, ca. 8 mm longa; arillus dimidia seminis includens, amylaceus, niveus ubi vivus. Plantulae cotyledonibus asymmetricis carnosis ex parte.
bibliographicCitation: Wilbur, Robert L. 1970. A new Costa Rican species of Centrapogon [C. talamancensis] (Campanualaceae-Lubelioideae). Brittonia. 21: 353-358.

description: Branches loosely spreading to ascending, sparsely to densely pubescent when young, soon glabrate. Leaves up to 20 cm long, mostly about as broad as long, generally deeply and angulately 3-, 5-, or 7-lobed, often to beyond the middle, with narrow-deltoid to deltoid or oblong-ovate lobes and sinus angles less than 900, rarely only 3-lobate or unlobed, the base mostly cordate, sometimes obtuse or trun- cate, ventral pubescence thin, often of simple or bifurcate hairs. Flowers mostly pendulous on elongate, slender pedicels in open, few-flowered, axillary cymes in turn forming large, often apically naked panicles. Involucral bracts free at the base, arising at the base of or up to 1 mm below the calyx, filiform or linear, 2-3.5 (-4.5) mm long, rarely exceeding the calyx tube. Calyx rather depressed-quadrate in outline with a flat, open tube and ascending lobe tips, 5-7 mm long at anthesis; lobes 3.5-5.5 mm long, 2.5-5 mm broad, deltoid- to cordate-ovate, short-acuminate. Corolla depressed-quadrate with the petals arising in a flat whorl from the base of the staminal column, then sharply ascending distally. Petals 4-7.5 mm long, 3-6.5 mm broad, broadly elliptic-obovate to suborbicular, narrowed abruptly at the base to a very short claw, glabrous. Staminal column composed of a depressed-ovate, apically hirsute, ovary-cup abruptly constricted at the apex to form a tube less than 1 mm long from which the filaments (1-2.5 mm long) radiate; anthers (13-) 15-23. Style branched nearly to the base, usually pubescent. Carpels 10-13. Gametic chromosome number, n = 16.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1967. Some Umbelliferae of the Andean Paramos of South America. Brittonia. 19: 212-226.

description: Small trees or shrubs to 5 m tall, the stems covered with minute stellate hairs. Leaf blades ovate to elliptic, to 11 cm long, 6 cm wide, basally subcordate, entire, acute or obtuse (sometimes retuse), palmately 7-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface with sparse, minute stellate hairs, the lower surface densely and minutely stellate-to- mentose, the veins prominent; petioles to 3 cm long, with indument like that of stem; stipules ca. 3 mm long, caducous. Flowers in terminal panicles; pedicels 10-20 mm long, articulated near middle or above, minutely stellate-tomentose; calyx campanulate, ecostate, ca. 4 mm long, 4-5-lobed, the lobes ca. 2 mm long, the outer surface stellate-tomentose, the inner surface glabrous with a ring-shaped basal nectary composed of long glandular hairs; corolla rotate, yellow; petals 5, ovate, 10 mm long, 7 mm wide, symmetric, with stellate hairs on margins of claw, otherwise glabrous; staminal column 2-3 mm long, glabrous, the anthers 20-30; styles 5, ca. 6 mm long, surpassing the stamens, with capitate stigmas. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 5, trigonal in cross section, apically dehiscent, densely stellate- tomentose; seeds solitary, reniform, brown, with arachnoid pubescence of stellate hairs.

description: Frutices 3 m alti ramis novellis dense pubescentibus; laminis foliorum late ovatis molliter tomentosis aliquantum discoloribus; floribus solitariis in foliorum axillis pedicellis floriferis brevibus, fructiferis elongatis; involucellorum bracteolis ca 8 lanceolatis vel spatulatis ad basem connatis, fructiferis accrescentibus 15 mm usque longis; calycibus 5-6 mm longis; petalis rubris corollam tubiformem efformantibus; androecio exserto purpurascenti, antheris secundis; stylis purpurascentibus; fructibus 11-12 mm diametro glabris; mericarpiis 7-9 mm longis ligneis; seminibus 5.5 mm longis.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. & Koch, Stephen D. 1991. Pavonia Ecostata (Malvaceae), a New Species from Jalisco, Mexico. Brittonia. 43 (1): 24-26.

description: Shrubs ca. 3 m tall, the stems densely yellowish puberulent, the hairs stellate, often stipitate, the stipe ca. 0.3 mm long, then tufted with ca. 10 radii or more. Leaf blades 8-18 cm long, ovate or weakly trilobulate, cordate, irregularly crenate-serrate, acute or acuminate, palmately 5-7-nerved, the upper surface with scattered appressed simple or bifurcate or stellate hairs (or glabrate), densely stellate on main veins, the lower surface stellate-pubescent (densely so when young), markedly discolorous; petioles 1/4- 1/2(-l) times length of blade, densely puber- ulent. Inflorescences racemose, axillary or terminal, often branched, the peduncles densely pulverulent, the flowers congested at the ends of the branches; calyx 7-9 mm long, ecostate, the outer surface densely stel- late-pubescent, the inner surface glabrous, half or more divided, the apices massive, subcucullate when fruiting, caudate; petals ca. 1 cm long, lavender or whitish, barbate at the claw; staminal column glabrous. Fruits oblate, 5-6 mm long, enclosed in calyx, glabrous; mericarps 10-12, 4 mm long, often shortly apiculate; seeds solitary, ca. 2 mm long, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. & Fuertes, J. 1992. A re-evaluation of the Abutilothamnus complex (Malvaceae) I. Two new species and two new genera, Sidasodes and Akrosida. Brittonia. 44: 436-447.

description: Frutices caulibus dense puberulis; laminis foliorum ovatis serrulatis molliter puberulis; inflorescentiis axillaribus inflorescentiam compositam supra folia facientibus; calycibus ecostatis; petalis flavidis; fructibus oblatis vel subglobosis pubescentibus, mericarpiis 9- 10 in 2 cellulis per endoglossum rigidum divisis; semi- nibus in cellula inferiore solitariis.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. & Fuertes, J. 1992. A re-evaluation of the Abutilothamnus complex (Malvaceae) I. Two new species and two new genera, Sidasodes and Akrosida. Brittonia. 44: 436-447.

description: Shrub 1-1.6 m tall, the stems densely puberulent, the hairs 0.1-0.3 mm long, stellate, yellowish. Leaf blades mostly 3-5 cm long, 2.5-4 cm wide, ovate, basally cordate, serrulate, acute or somewhat acuminate, palmately 7-9-nerved, more or less discol- orous, densely and softly puberulent above and beneath; petioles 0.5-2 cm long, with pubescence like stem; stipules 2-3 mm long, subulate, caducous. Inflorescences in the axils of the uppermost 3-5 leaves, long-pedunculate, racemosely or subcymosely branched, the aggregate (more or less paniculate) inflorescence overtopping the leaves; peduncles mostly 2-6 cm long, supporting 6-12 flowers each; pedicels 0.5-1.5 cm long, puberulent; calyx 4 mm long, ba- sally rounded, ecostate, puberulent, ca. half- divided, pentamerous, the lobes triangular; petals 5-6 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, yellow or orange-yellow, glabrous; staminal column ca. 2 mm long, stellate-pubescent, pallid, the filaments ca. 1 mm long; styles 9- 10, slender, slightly exceeding the androe cium, the stigmas truncate or subcapitate. Fruits oblate to subglobose, densely stellate pubescent, 5-6 mm in diameter; mericarps 9-10, divided into two cells by a stiff endoglossum inserted dorsally; seeds [immature] solitary in the lower cell, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. & Fuertes, J. 1992. A re-evaluation of the Abutilothamnus complex (Malvaceae) I. Two new species and two new genera, Sidasodes and Akrosida. Brittonia. 44: 436-447.

description: Frutex usque ad 40 cm altus fide collectoris; caules erecti, lignosi, viriduli, saltem 3 mm diametro minimum, dense vel demum moderate stellato-pubescentes; pili plerumque quadri-brachiati (2 brachiis ascendentibus ac 2 brachiis descendentibus). Folia lanceolata, acuta, usque ad 50 mm longa, 18 mm lata, nisi integra ad basem 9-12 dentibus grossis in quoque latere, sparse pubescentia supra (pilis plerumque simplicibus), moderate ita infra (pilis stellatis, 3-4-brachiatis), palmatim 5- nervata. Petioli 11-15 mm longi, stellato-pubescentes, pubescentia petiolorum pubescentiae caulium simili sed magis densis apicem versus. Stipulae 8-9 mm longae, minus quam 1 mm latae, lineares, sparse stellato-pubescentes, caducae. Pedicelli usque ad 2 cm longi, graciles, solitarii in axillis, stellato-pubescentes. Calyces profunde 5-lobati, 1.0-1.5 cm longi; lobi calycis plicati, late cordati (fere quam latiores quam longiores), margine ciliati, stellato-pubescentes extus (pilis 4-brachiatis), glabri intus, obtusi cum acuminibus, acumina 2 mm longa. Petala circa 1.5 cm longa, flavida(?) basibus purpurascentibus, glabra praeter minute ciliata in unguibus (pilis 0.1-0.2 mm longis) et sparse ciliata in marginibus distalibus (pilis circa 0.5 mm). Columnae staminales conicae, glabrae, antheriferae supra; partibus liberis filorum brevissimis (minus quam 1 mm); antherae itaque con- fertae, numerosae, pallidae; pollen flavum, sphaericum, spinosum. Styli verosimiliter 8, androe- cium 1-2 mm excedentes, glabri, albidi(?) stigmata capitata. Fructus ex 8 mericarpiis constans; mericarpia columellam congentes; columellae 3-4 mm longae; mericarpia ex columella et inter se secedentia, circa 3 mm alta, 5 mm longa, 1.5 mm crassa, nigra, in dimidio inferno et in pariete dorsi reticulata, in dimidio supero laevi, rostrum auctum et obtusum formanti. Semina solitaria, 3 mm longa, minute pubescentia.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1978. Neotropical segregates from Sida L. (Malvaceae). Brittonia. 30: 447-462.

description: Herba annua, glanduloso vel viscido-pubescens, procumbens, ramosissima, ad ca. 7 dm lata et 5 dm alta; folia opposita vel alterna, 5-10 palmatiloba vel pinnatiloba, basi cordata vel inaequilateralia, marginibus inaequaliter dentatis, petiolis 5-10 cm longis; racemi terminales, 5-15 flori, pedicellis per anthesin tenuissimis, ca. 1.75-3.75 cm longis, in maturitate crescentibus ad ca. 5 cm longis; calyx 1.3-1.8 cm longus, 5-lobatus, obliquus, ad basim ventraliter fissus, basi bracteolis duabus, lanceolatis vel ovatis praeditus; corolla obliqua infundibularis, 2.75-3.75 cm longa, limbo 5 lobato, 2.5-3.5 cm lato, luteo-violaceo; stamina fertilia 4, didynama, quinto rudimentario; stylus stamina superans; stigmata duo; fructus ovatus, 8-10 cm longus.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, Edward F. 1970. The biogeography, ecology and taxonomy of Lophophora. Brittonia. 21: 299-310.

description: Viscid to glandular pubescent annual herb arising from a well developed tap root with fibrous secondaries; stems 15-45 cm in height, the branches and leaves opposite or subopposite to alternate; petioles 5-10 cm long, glandular-pubescent on the nerves below; basal leaves 7-14 cm long and 7-12 cm wide, deltoid to ovate in general outline but deeply and irregularly palmately 5-10-lobed or pinnatifid; the lobes irregularly dentate-serrulate, sinuate or lobed; the central lobe acute to rounded, generally broader than the lateral lobes; inflorescence racemose, 5-15-flowered, 15-30 cm long; pedicels in anthesis erect to ascending 1.75-3.75 cm long, 1 mm thick but becoming reflexed, thicker (2 mm) and longer (up to 5 cm) in fruit; calyx thin, papery, 1.3-1.8 cm long and about 8 mm broad, 5-lobed, the terminal lobe extended, the lateral lobes about 3 mm broad, the basal lobes about 5 mm long, the intermediate lobes 9\-10 mm long, the sinuses ?/2-1/3 the length of the lobes; bracts 2, broadly ovate, lanceolate or linear-falcate, 4-6 mm long; corolla 2.75-3.75 cm long, ventricose, the tube about 2 cm long, yellowish purple within and without, a pronounced yellow band extending somewhat over the lower lobe, the limb 2.5-3.5 cm wide, violet, the upper lobes frequently with large, dark purple splotches, the lobes 1-1.5 cm long and 1 cm wide; stamens 4, didynamous; ovary 1-celled with two parietal placentae, style exceeding the stamens, stigmas two, obovate and sensitive; fruit an ovate ligneous drupe, 4-5 cm long with a prominent dorsal crest and horns 4-5 cm long; seeds numerous, 6-8 mm long, the testa black with corky tubercles.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, Edward F. 1970. The biogeography, ecology and taxonomy of Lophophora. Brittonia. 21: 299-310.

description: Frutex sempervirens 1.5-4 m alta foliis dense dispositis, lenticellis in ligno venusto ellipticis acris, laminis plerumque obovatis et 2 X longiore quam latiore, marginibus integris, apice variabilis base plerumque cuneatis punctatis punctis resinosis rubris, infloreseentiis masculinis plerumque axillariis fasciculatis in ligno hornotino ex gemmis omnino florigeris praeditis, interdum solitariis lateralibus, fasciculatis floris et pedicellatis et pedunculatis, in florescentiis femininiis et axillariis fasciculatis et axillariis solitariis in ligno hornotino ex gemmis omnino florigeris praeditis, vel lateralibus ex gemmis mixtis praeditis in baso ligno hornotino vel raro axillariis ex gemmis omnino florigeris in ligno venus to praeditis, floris 4-meris, anthers et fertilis et sterilis breviore quam filamentis; bacco drupis ignoti.
bibliographicCitation: Edwin, Gabriel. 1965. A new Peruvian Ilex [I. macbridiana]. Brittonia. 17: 284, 285.

description: Evergreen shrub 1.5-4 m tall, densely foliaceous; new wood drying black, glabrous to sparsely or subsensely puberlent with very short, white hairs, the older branchlets glabrous, drying dark grey-black to black and beset with elliptical lenticels that are pointed at base and apex; leaf-blades chartaceous to subcoria- ceous, glabrous or occasionally with a few short, white hairs on the midvein of the upper surface, mostly 2-3.5 cm long (a few a little longer or shorter) X 0.9-1.6 cm wide (a few a little narrower or wider), at least twice as long as broad, mostly obovate, sometimes elliptically obovate, the margins entire, a little thickened and revolute or less often plane, the apex variable, (in order of frequency) broadly acute, acute, emarginate, or obtuse and often with a very small, less than ca 0.3 mm long, spinose apiculum, the base usually cuneate, less often acute or suba- cuminate, narrowly decurrent over the petiole, drying dull, dark, olive-green or brown-green above, paler beneath, the midvein plane or insculpt above, little ele- vated beneath, the lateral veins obsolete or subobsolete above and beneath, occasionally epunctate, usually sparsely to densely punctate with refractory resin-like, red punctations beneath; petioles glabrous, thickened and blackening when dry, deeply grooved, 2-5 (-6) mm long; staminate inflorescences mostly axillary, fasciculate and compound on new wood from wholly floral buds, occa- sionally laterally solitary, when fasiculate the fascicles composed of pedicellate flowers and flowers borne on once branched peduncles that are 3-5-pedicellate (usually containing 2-5 basal flower stalks), when lateral composed of a 3-flowered peduncle, the pedicels and peduncles glabrous or sparsely puberulent, the ped- uncles and non-pedunculate pedicels 5-10 mm long, the pedunculate pedicels 1-3 mm long; pistillate inflorescences axillary and few-fasciculate or axillary and solitary from wholly floral buds, or solitarily axillary or lateral from mixed buds, developing at the base of current growth, occasionally axillary from floral buds borne on last year's wood, the peduncles not or only rarely evolved; pedicels 6-12 mm long, glabrous or sparsely puberulent; flowers 4-merous; staminate calyx ca 3 mm in diameter, glabrous, subcupuliform, the deltoid-acute, eciliate lobes longer than the tube; corolla ca 5.5-6.5 mm in diameter, glabrous, the petals ca 2.5 mm long X 2 mm broad, broadly elliptical to suborbicular, united ca 0.3 mm, obtusely rounded; stamens a little shorter than the petals, the elliptic to subovate-elliptic anthers shorter than the thickened, terete filaments; pistillodium ca 1 mm high and in diameter, pulvinate; pistillate flower ca 7-8 mm in diameter with lobes of the calyx longer than in the staminate flower and acuminate; petals narrower (1.5 mm) and a little longer (3 mm), elliptic to awl-shaped, otherwise the perianth as in the staminate; staminodes ca 1/2-2/3 the length of the petals, the sterile anthers ovate, small, ca 1/3-1/4 the length of the flattened filaments; ovary ovoid or cylindric-ovoid, 1.5 mm long X 1.5 mm broad at base; stigma coronate, ca .0.5 mm long X 1 mm broad; fruting material unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Edwin, Gabriel. 1965. A new Peruvian Ilex [I. macbridiana]. Brittonia. 17: 284, 285.

description: A shrub 1-3 meters high. Younger stems densely hirsute with yellowish, mostly flexuous, partly glandular hairs up to 3 mm. long, averaging about 1 mm. Petioles stout, 1-2 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Leaf-blades firm, ovate-lanceolate, oblong-ovate, or ovate, up to 18 cm. long by 9 cm. wide, acuminate, minutely toothed, ciliate, rounded at the base, 5-nerved, densely short-hirsute above and below, the hairs yellowish, mostly 1-1.5 mm. long. Infloreseences spiciform, somewhat flexuous, rarely with one or two lateral branches, slender, usually 10-15 em. long, the lateral elusters mostly 1-flowered or 2- flowered; internodes slender, 1-2 cm. long, conspicuously glandular with hairs 0.5-1 mm. long and sparsely hirsute with much longer simple hairs. Hypanthium broadly tubular, 3.5-4 mm. long, densely hirsute with upwardly curved hairs usually about 1 mm., occasionally up to 3 mm. long, also thinly stellate-pubescent; glandular hairs few or none. Calyx-tube prolonged about 0.7 mm.; sepals broadly quad- rate, 2 mm. long from the torus, ciliate; exterior teeth stoutly subu- late or conic, often ineurved, 2.5-3 mm. long from the torus, pubes- cent like the hypanthium. Petals obovate-oblong, 4-5 mm. long. Fila- ments 2.5-3 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, 2.5-3 mm. long, the thecae convolute, the pore ventro-terminal; connective simple, slightly gibbous near the base. Ovary two-thirds inferior, 5-celled, the free sum- mit truncate-conic, setose around the style; style 5-7 mm. long; stigma truneate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Coarse shrub, 1-3 meters high. Sterns delnsely hirsute with siluple brown hairs mostly 1-2 mm. long. Petioles stout, mostly 5-10 mm., rarely up to 20 mm. long, hirsute like the stem. Leaf-blades firm, usually brown-green when dried, oblong-lanceolate to oblong or elliptic, 10-20 cm. long by about one-third as wide, acuminate, entire or obscurely denticulate, obtuse to rounded and usually oblique at the base, 5-pli-nerved, the inner pair of primaries usually alternate at their bases, short-setose above (hairs rarely more than 1 mm. long), with a strip of longer more crowded hairs along the primaries, hirsute below, especially on the veins (hairs mostly 1-2 mm. long). Infloreseelice few-flowered, 1-3 cm. long, hirsute like the stem. Hypanthium cup- shaped, about 3 mm. long, very densely hirsute with spreading hairs up to 2 mm. long; toral scales triangular, fimibriate. Calyx-tube pro- longed about 1 mm., truncate, the sepals undifferentiated; exterior teeth subulate, spreading or ascending at anthesis, erect in fruit, 2-5 mm. longer than the calyx, hirsute like the hypanthium. Petals obo- vate, about 7 mm. long. Filaments strongly extrorsely curved, thick- ened distally; anthers stoutly subulate, nearly straight, 3-3.5 mm. long, the pore dorso-terminal; connective prolonged below the thecae about 0.3 mm. Ovary 5-celled, about two-thirds inferior, the glabrous trun- cate-conic summit ending in a terete crown; style 4-5 mm. lonlg; stigma capitellate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: A shrub about a meter high, freely branched above. Stems freely hirsute with straight, spreading, glandular hairs 1-2 mm. long, also minutely pubescent. Leaves often distinctly unequal in each pair. Petioles slender, 1-2 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Blades thin, blackening in drying, ovate-oblong to oblong, up to 12 cm. long and 5 cm. wide, acuminate, serrulate, broadly obtuse to rounded at the base, 5-pli-nerved, rather sparsely pilose on both sides (hairs 0.5-2 mm. long). Infloreseence apparently terminal, becoming lateral by pro-liferation, mostly 3-flowered, the peduncles 5-10 mm. long; bracts oblong, hirsute, 3-5 mm. long. Hypanthium campanulate-cylindric, about 4 mm. long, densely and softly villous, the hairs lengthening distally to 1 mm. Calyx-tube barely prolonged; sepals triangular- ovate, 2-2.5 mm. long from the torus, densely ciliate; exterior teeth stoutly subulate, densely long-villous, 3-3.5 mm. long. Petals nar- rowly obovate, 3.5-4 mm. long. Anthers subulate, 4.5-5 mm. long; connective not prolonged, slightly gibbous on the back at the base. Ovary half inferior, 3-celled, its summit truncate-conic, minutely glanidular-pubeseenit around the style; style 3.5-4 mm. long; stigma minutely capitellate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Secutnditolrae: Frutex 2-3 m. altus, eaulis parte superiore dense strigosa. Petioli validi 2-6 cm. longi dense strigosi. Laminae membranaceae ovatae, in quoque jugo fere aequales, 18-23 cm. longae, 10- 13 cm. latae, aeuminatae, minute serrulatae, eiliatae, basi leviter cordatae, late truneatae, vel rotundatae ad basin imam late cuneatam, 7- 9-nerviae vel fere pli-nerviae, supra pubeseentes, pilis dimorphis, majoribus subrigidis 1 mm. longis e basi papillosa, minoribus parvis flexuosis gracilibus, subtus ad paginam densius hirsutae, ad venas densissime substrigosae; venae primariae utrinque vix elevatae, secundariae supra obscurae subtus planae subrectae. Inflorescentia terminalis pyramidalis 10-20 cm. longa ramosa, axibus densissime strigosis. Flores secuindi sessiles conferti 5-meri. Hypanthium anguste campanulatum 3.2 mm. loingum, densissime strigosum atque parce glanduloso-pilosum. Sepala vera (ab exteriore non videnda) late semicircularia 0.5 mm. longa; dentibus exterioribus triangularibus fere 2 mm. longis erectis dense strigosis. Petala lanceolata acuta glabra 2.5 mm. longa. Stamina isomorpha. Filamenta gracillima 3.5 mm. longa. Antherae lineares 2 mm. longae, connectivo crasso basi tubereulis 2 minutissimis ornato. Ovarium inferum 5-loculare summo minute glanduloso-hirsutum. Stylus gracilis glaber 6.5 mm. longus, stigmate parvo capitellato.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: The typical variety has the stems, leaves, and hypanthia glandular-hirsute, often densely so, with long yellow-red hairs, broadened and flattened at the base and with red gland tips. The hairs on the stem and leaf surfaces are 1-3.7 mm long, on the leaf margin 0.8-2.2 mm long, and on the hypanthium 1-2.6 (-4.5) mm long. The hypanthium is yellow at first, becoming red before anthesis. The petals are white, with a red basal marking (perhaps unmarked in some).
bibliographicCitation: Whiffin, Trevor. 1971. Studies in the genus Maieta (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 23 (3): 325-329.

description: Shrub to tree or vine-like tree, 1.5-6 m high or sometimes to 15 m high and 40 cm in diameter at breast height; bark gray to brown to reddish, smooth or with many cracks, shreddy; young twigs narrowly 4-winged, glabrous or puberulent; petioles 0.3-3.0 mm long; blades rich green, shiny above when fresh, less so, below, ovate to ovate-triangular or elliptic-ovate or narrowly so, 15-90 mm long, 8-40 mm wide, entire, the base cordate with a small notch or rarely truncate, the apex acute or abruptly so to acuminate, the margin entire and sometimes crisped, the midrib grooved above, rounded to angled and glabrous o,r puberulent below; lateral nerves invisible or obscure; stomatal crypts none; flowers mostly axillary, less often at the nodes on leafless twigs to 2 mm thick, 1-3 pier axil, each flower single on a bracted stalk of 1-3 internodes, the stalk in all 0.7-4 (-6) mm long (excluding the true pedicel), or very rarely the flowers to 5 per peduncle; bracts 0.6-3.2 mm long, triangular to ovate, acute or acuminate; true pedicels 0.2-6.5 mm long; flowers sometimes reported to be fragrant; length of calyx plus ovary 3.5-6.5 mm; surfaces glabrous or bracts, axes, and pedicel more or less puberulent; free hypanthium 1.3-1.8 mm long; calyx green or greenish white to yellow, its lobes fused together 0.3-1.2 mm, the free ends triangular and acute to abruptly acuminate, 0.7-3.0 mm long, their edges minutely ciliate; total calyx length from stamen attachment 1.5-3.8 mm, the fused part splitting at anthesis; petals white to yellow or pink, triangular to lanceolate, sometimes acuminate, abruptly narrowed to a basal claw, 3.2-7.0 mm long, 1.6-4.5 mm wide; filaments white to yellow, the antesepalous ones 3.3-4.5 mm long, the antepetalous 4.5-7.0 mm long; anthers yellow, 1.5-2.7 mm long with sporangia 1.1-2.2 mm long and a gland 0.3-0.8 mm long; style white, 8-11 mm long; stigma salmon (one report); inferior ovary 1-locular, with 6-11 free-central ovules in a single whorl; calyx lobes tardily deciduous from the fruit, the ripe fruit roundish, 7-10 mm thick, red-orange, red, pink, or in Panama sometimes dark red, purple, or black, containing 1 or sometimes 2 roundish seeds 5-8.4 mm thick with a hard polished integument and a rough basal hilum ca. 1.9 mm in diameter. The cotyledons remain in the seed coat in the seedling (Duke, 1969, p. 158 and Fig. 69, p. 159).
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1971. Geographic Variation in a Widespread Neotropical Species, Mouriri Myrtilloides (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 23 (4): 413-424.

description: Erect, simple or sparingly branched, 15-40 cm. high; leaves broadly ovate or subrotund, sessile, cordate at base, 5-7 mm. long; pubescence of straight spreading hairs 0.5-1 mm. long; sepals 1 mm. long.

description: Delicate herb, freely branched above, sparsely glandular-villous, especially above; leaves nearly round, 4 mm. in diameter, on petioles 2-3 mm. long; peduncles 5-18 mm. long; heads 1-6-flowered; bracts obovate, spinulose-ciliate, thinly villous; hypanthium tubular, 3 mm. long in fruit; sepals triangular, acute, 1 mm. long; petals pale lilac.

description: Erects shrubs 0.3-3 m tall. Distal branches sparsely to moderately appressed-strigose, the hairs whitish to reddish, ca. 0.3- 0.8(-1.2) mm long; nodes setose with setae ca. 0.5-1 mm long, reddish; internodes ca. 3-9 cm long. Petioles 0.5-1.5 cm long, moderately strigose; leaf blades narrowly elliptic to elliptic, 2.5-8.8 X 0.7-3.5 cm, the apex acuminate, the base cuneate where the 3 primary nerves join the petiole, then rounded beyond, 3-nerved at the base with an obscure pair of veins close to the margin; the upper leaf surface strigose with hairs to 2 mm long, adnate to the surface 1/3-2/3 their length; the lower leaf surface sparsely strigose with appressed whitish hairs to 0.8 mm long, the hairs on the veins setose, appressed, to 1 mm long; the margin serrulate to crenulate with each tooth terminating in a seta ca. 1 mm long. Inflorescences lax compound dichasia, terminal on lateral branches, 3-12 cm long, with 26-90 flowers; peduncles ca. 2-7 cm long, densely strigose with whitish hairs to 1.5 mm long; bracts lanceolate to oblanceolate, 2-4 mm long, strigose abaxially, glabrous adaxially, caducous; pedicels 1.5-4 mm long. Hypanthia urceolate, 2.5-3(-4) mm long, 2-2.5 mm broad at the torus, sparsely strigose with hairs 0.5-1 mm long, these mostly eglandular but sometimes glandular (Fig. 5). Calyx lobes 5, lanceolate, shorter than the hypanthium, 2-3 mm long, triangular at base, sparsely strigose along margin and midvein with whitish or reddish appressed hairs to 0.6-1 mm long, otherwise glabrous. Petals 5, magenta, purple-pink, or lilac, broadly obovate, 0.5-1.2 X 0.4-1 cm, ciliate along margin, with or without a terminal seta. Stamens usually 10, rarely 8, slightly dimorphic in size, all yellow; larger stamens with filaments 1.5-2(-2.5) mm long, thecae 1.7-2(-2.5) mm long, often drying slightly rostrate, the connective very short, ca. 0.3 mm long, with 2 minute basal lobes or these completely absent; smaller stamens with filaments (1.5-)2-2.5 mm long, thecae 1.2-1.5 mm long, the connec- tive very short, ca. 0.2 mm long, with 2 minute basal lobes or these absent. Ovary ovoid, 2-3 mm long, sparsely setose in distal 1/4, lacking apical appendages; styles 4- 6 mm long. Capsules 3-3.5 mm long; seeds ca. 0.3 mm long.

description: Shrub. Younger sterns densely hirsute with stoutly stipitate stellate hairs 1.3-2.6 mm. long with a few very short delicate terminal branches, also thinly pubescent with sessile stellate hairs, becoming glabrate with age. Petioles slender, 2.5-4.5 cm. long, pubescent like the stern, the short stellate hairs more numerous. Leaf-blades thin, oblong-ovate, up to 15 cm. long by 8 cm. wide, short-acuminiate, minutely denticulate, rounded or very broadly cuneate at the base, 7-pli-nerved, above densely pubescent or alml-ost velutinous, the hairs simple, about 0.5 mm. long, beneath pubescent on the principal veins like the stern, on the surface softly tomentose with erect stellate hairs about 0.3 mm. lolng. Ilnflorescence few-branched, about 5 cm. long, pubescent like the stern; bracts minute or none. Flowers 5-merous, sessile. Hypanthium cup-shaped, 3.5 mm. long, delicately villous with sessile stellate hairs and densely hirsute with stoutly stipitate stellate hairs up to 0.7 mm. long. Calyx tube barely prolonged; sepals quadrate-ovate, about 1 mlml. long from the torus; exterior teeth stoutly subulate, 2.5-3 mm. long, setose at the tip, hirsute like the hypanthiumi, the hairs shorter. Petals round-obovate, 3 mm. long. Filaments 2.5-3 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, 3-3.5 mm. long, the pore terminal; connective simple, the filament dorsally attached. Ovary half inferior, its rounded summit glabrous; style stout, 7 mm. long; stigma punctiformn.

description: Shrub. Stems subterete, pubeseent when young with nmostly glandular hairs up to 0.5 mm. long, on the youngest parts subtomentose with erooked, strongly plumose hairs up to 0.4 mm. long, glabreseent with age. Petioles variable, 1.5-5 cm. long, pubeseent like the stem but with longer hairs and fewer plumose hairs. Leaf-blades thin, ovate, up to 15 cm. long by 8 cm. wide, abruptly and slenderly shortaeuminate, finely dentate and eiliate, rounded to obseurely eordate at the base, 5-7-nerved, short-hirsute on both sides. Inflorescenee triehotomous from near the base, 10 cm. long and wide, loosely branehed, pubeseent like the stem, the simple hairs beeoming mostly glandular distally; braets laneeolate-subulate, 0.5-1 mm. long; pedieels 3-4 mm. long. HypanthiuLim eup-shaped, 2 mm. long, densely short-hirsute with stout hairs 0.2-0.4 mm. long, a few of them glandular. Calyx-tube barely prolonged; sepals spreading, membranous, semieireular, 0.8 mm. long from the torus. Exterior teeth filiform, 3 mm. long, pubescent like the hypanthium. Petals narrowly obovate, 4-4.5 mm. long, not retuse, equilateral. Filaments stout and flat, 2 mm. long; anthers stoutly linear, 1.7 mm. long, the pore terminal; connective simple, but extending with the thecae into two short basal lobes. Ovary half inferior, 5-celled, the truneate-conic summit glabrous, obscurely ribbed; style 5 mm. long, tapering to the punetiformi stigma.

description:
Slender shrub 12 dm. tall. Young stems densely tomentose with yellow hairs up to 10 mm. long, permanently setose at the nodes, the elongate internodes soon glabeseent. Petioles slender, 2-4 cm. long, densely pubescent when young, glabrate with age. Leaf-blades thin, bright-green, ovate, up to 12 cm. long by 7.5 cm. wide, abruptly shortacuminate, minutely appressed-ciliate, shallowly cordate at the base, 7-nerved, glabrous above, very sparsely pubescent on the veins beneath, glabrous on the surface; lateral veins diverging at an angle of about 60º. Cymes several-flowered, 1-2 cm. long, sessile, trichotomous from the base, glabrous; bracts minute, subulate, aristate. Hypanthium obconic, 3 mm. long, pale, glabrous, obscurely 10-nerved. Calyx-tube about 0.6 mm. long, slightly flaring; sepals triangular-ovate, 1.3 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth 2-3 mm. long, triangular and adnate below, the free portion filiform. Petals oblong-obovate, 6 mm. long. Filaments broad and flat, 2.4 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, 2.3 mm. long, the pore dorso-terminal; connective simple. Ovary two-thirds inferior, 5-celled, the summit glabrous, truncate-conic; style

6-6.5 mm. long; stigma capitate, 0.7 mm. in diameter.

description: Shrub 1-2 meters high. Younger sterns densely stellate-tomentose with yellowish hairs, also hirsute with both simple and glandular hairs up to 3 mm. long. Petioles stout, 1-3 cm. long, pubescent like the stem, the hairs longer toward the summit. Leaf-blades firm, ovate-lanceolate to oblong, up to 15 cm. long by 8 cm. wide, acuminate, entire to denticulate, long-ciliate, broadly rounlded at the base, 5-nerved, sparsely bullate, setose, and often sparsely stellate-pubescent above, thinly to deinsely stellate-tomentose beneath and often also setose, especially on the veins. Inflorescences racemiform, 3-5 cm. long, densely stellate-tomentose and glandular-hirsute, the hairs mostly 1 mm. long or less. Hypanthium broadly tubular, 5.5 mm. long, stel- late-tomentose, glandular-hirsute, and setose especially toward the summit with simple hairs 2-3.5 mm. long. Calyx-tube prolonged 1 mm., pubescent like the hypanthium, the hairs often more or less reflexed, minutely stellate within; sepals 2.5-3 mm. long from the torus, oblong-ovate, glandular and stellate externally; exterior teeth stoutly subulate, exceeding the sepals by about 1 mm. Petals oblong- obovate, 6-7 mm. long. Filaments 3.5-4 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, 3.5-4 mm. long, the pore ventro-terminal, the thecae strongly convolute; connective not prolonged, slightly gibbous near the base. Ovary half-inferior, 5-celled, the truncate summit glandular-setose; style 7 mm. long; stigma truncate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Shrub, the slender stems usually with lolng internodes, densely stellate-tomenltose, the hairs long-stipitate, slightly surpassed by numer- ous spreading glandular hairs. Petioles 1.5-4 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Leaf-blades firm, velvety green above, ovate to ovate-oblong, 10-15 cm. long, 5-8 cm. wide, faleately acuminate, minutely denticulate, rounded at the base, 7-9-nerved, bullate-hirsute above and sparsely stellate-pubescent, especially on the veins, beneath foveolate, gray, densely stellate-tomentose. Inflorescence racemose, with a well defined central axis, up to 10 cm. long, pubescent like the stem; lateral branches mostly about 1 cm. long; bracts linear-subulate, 1 mm. long. Flowers sessile, 5-merous. Hypanthium tubular-campanulate, 4-4.5 mm. long to the torus, slightly constricted above the ovary, densely stellate-tomentose, abundantly glandular-hirsute, and with a few sim- ple bristles up to 1 mm. long. Calyx-tube about 0.5 mm. long; sepals very thin, broadly roulnd-ovate, 1.7-2 mm. lolng and about as wide, erose, pubescent on the back; exterior teeth triangular, adnate to the middle, barely surpassing the sepals, stellate on the back, with a few stout cilia on the free tip. Petals oblong-obovate, 4.5-5 mm. long by half as wide, slightly retuse. Stamens isomorphic; filaments slender, 3 mm. long; anthers narrowly subulate, 2.7-2.9 mm. long; connective thickened below and very briefly prolonged below the thecae. Ovary three-fourths inferior, 5-celled, the rounded summit villous and sparsely glandular-setose; style slender, 4-5 mm. long; stigma barely capitellate.

description: A shrub. Younger portions of the stem slender, thinly to densely hirsute with sinmple hairs rarely as much as 3 mm. long, glabrescent with age. Petioles slender, up to 6 cm. long, usually much shorter, pubescent like the stem. Leaf-blades thin, ovate or ovate-oblong, up to 15 cm. long by 8 cm. wide, finely but conspicuously and irregularly dentate, broadly acute to rounded at the base, 5-nerved, hirsute above, the slender hairs averaging 2 mm. long, more densely pubescent beneath with slightly shorter hairs. Infloreseence lax, trichotomous from near the base, 3-5 cm. long, hirsute, the hairs mostly 1-2 mm., rarely up to 3 mm. long, a few of them glandular. Hypanthiuin urn-shaped, 2.5-3 mm. long, densely hirsute with somewhat retrorse hairs up to 2 mm. long. Calyx-tube barely prolonged; sepals broadly quadrate, about 1 mm. long from the torus, ciliate and erose; exterior teeth filiform, 3-5 mm. long, hirsute. Petals oblong-ovate, 4-5 mm. long. Filaments 2-2.5 mm. long; anthers stoutly linear, 2-2.5 mm. long, the stout connective prolonged about 0.2 mm. below the thecae. Style straight, 5 mm. long, tapering gradually to the punctiform stigma.

description: Branches roundly 4-angled and conspicuously suleate, densely hir- sute with erect, stout, straight, dark purple, glandular hairs about 0.7 mm. long and 0.2-0.3 mm. apart; petioles stout, as much as 15 mm. long, dark purple, essentially glabrous; leaf-blades firm, elliptic- lanceolate, as much as 6 by 20 cm., sharply acuminate, entire, obtuse or broadly acute at base, 5-pli-nerved; upper surface sparsely and minutely white-stellate when young, becoming glabrous in age; lower surface minutely puberulent on the veins and veinlets; primaries and secondaries conspicuously impressed above, elevated beneath, the lat- ter not continuous between the primaries, about 4 mm. apart, aseend- ing at an angle of about 70?; tertiaries plane above, conspicuously reticulate beneath; panicle about 12 cm. long, rather densely branched, with a few glandular hairs on the lower internodes, other- wise glabrous; pedicels about 2 mm. long, jointed near the top; flowers 5-merous; hypanthium urceolate-hemispheric, 4.3 mm. long to the torus, glabrous, its walls very thick and fleshy; calyx-tube some- what flaring, prolonged 1 mm. to the acute sinuses; sepals triangular, 1.6 mm. long, rounded above, membranous; exterior teeth triangular, 1.7-1.8 mm. long, acute, free, thick and fleshy, closely appressed and somewhat ineurved; petals narrowly obovate or spatulate-obovate, 7 mm. long, 3.6 mm. wide, somewhat unguiculate at base, many-nerved, very obscurely and slightly inequilaterally retuse; stamens iso- morphic; filaments thick but flat, 3 mm. long, sparsely glandular- puberulent, especially distally and dorsally; anthers stoutly oblong, 4.3-4.5 mm. long, obtuse, 4-celled, opening by a minute terminal pore; connective slightly elevated toward the base, but neither prolonged nor appendaged; ovary two-fifths inferior, 5-celled, its conic free sum- mit 10-ribbed and minutely white-punetate; style stout, 8.5 mm. long, finely villous on the basal three-fourths; description: Stems conspiduoLisly but roundly 4-angled above, densely hirsute with slender hairs 1.5 mm. long, dark blue on the younger parts, be- coming brown on the older terete stems; petioles stout, 10-18 mm. long, hirsute like the stem with somewhat shorter hairs; blades thin, dull bluish green, ovate-lanceolate, as mnuch as 75 by 32 mm., acumi- nate, rounded at base, minutely serrulate, 5-nerved; primaries and the inconspicuous secondaries lightly depressed above and elevated be- neath, the latter about 2 mm. apart, ascending at an angle of about 700, tertiaries obscure above, plane to barely elevated beneath; upper surface hirtellous with slender hairs 0.6-0.8 mm. long; lower surface essentially glabrous, the veins and larger tertiaries freely pubescent with erect or spreading hairs about 1 mm. long and tending toward blue in color; infloreseence laxly paniculate, few-branched and few- flowered, 10 cm. long, hirsute like the stem, the hairs becoming glan- dular distally and decreasing in length; bracts setaceous, 2 mm. long, including the terminal gland-tipped seta; pedicels apparently 2.5 mm. long, actually, above the joint, only 1-1.5 mm.; flowers both 4- and 5-merous; hypanthium campanulate, 2.7 mm. long to the torus, densely hirtellous with stout glandular hairs 0.5 mm. long; connective prolonged 0.3 mm. at base dorsally into 1 (epipetalous) or 2 (episepalous) obtuse lobes; ovary 3-celled, the broadly conic summit tipped with a cluster of erect glandular hairs 0.2-0.8 mm. long; style slender, glabrous, 7 mm. long; stigma capitate.

description: Glabrous throughout, the branches acutely 4-angled and shallowly 4-suleate; petioles rather stout, as much as 1 cm. long but mnostly muLch shorter, sharply carinate on the back, the carina extending out the midvein; blades narrowly elliptic-lanceolate, as much as 4 by 15 cm., long-acuminate at both ends, gradually merging into the petiole below, entire, 5-pli-nerved; primaries lightly impressed above; secondaries aseendinlg at an angle of about 750, 1-2 mum. apart, plane on both sides; tertiaries obsolete above, plane and reticulate beneath; panicle small, loosely flowered, with few branches, its axes sharply 4-angled, the nodes subtended by deflexed setaceous bracts 1 mm. long; pedicels about 0.7 mm. long, very thick; flowers 5-merous; hypanthium nar- rowly campanulate or obconic, 4 mm. long to the torus, its walls very thick and fleshy; calyx-tube prolonged 0.4 mmn., erect; sepals 0.5 mm. long, 1.6 mm. wide, broadly truncate, separated by narrow but rounded sinluses, the distal half membranous and minutely ciliolate, the basal half thicker and bearing at the center a minute protuberance representing the external tooth; petals broadly obovate-oblong above a very broad base, 4 mm. long, 3 mm. wide, thick and fleshy, inequi- laterally retuse; stamens isomorphic; filaments broad and flat, 2.2 mm. long; anthers linear, 3 mm. long, straight, opening by a fairly wide terminal pore; connective flat, perfectly simple; ovary appar- ently wholly inferior; style very stout, almost fusiform, 4 mm. long; stigma capitellate, 0.8 mm. in diameter.

description: Stem densely hirsute with brown, suLbulate, almost contiguous hairs about 1.3 mm. long, from distinctly swollen or papillose bases; petioles stout, as much as 2 cm. long, more densely hirsute than the stem but with more slender hairs; blades firm, narrowly ovate-laneco- late, as much as 135 by 45 mm., long-acuminate, obtuse at base, weakly 5-pli-nerved, the laterals arising 2-4 mmn. above the base; secondaries 2-3 mm. apart, almost perpendicular to the primaries; upper surface densely papillose-hirsute, the hairs nearly contiguous at base, the swollen bases 0.6 mm. long, the stout ascending tip 0.7-1 mm. long; lower surface very densely pubescent with nearly straight and erect gray hairs 1-1.5 mm. long from slightly enlarged bases; flowers 5-merous, sessile in capitate elusters, subtended by broadly ovate bracts 2-3 mm. long and densely hirsute on the lower surface and margin; hypanthium broadly campanulate-hemispheric, 2.8 mm. long to the torus, densely strigose-hirsute with curved-ascending hairs 1 mm. long and slightly swollen at the base; calyx-tube prolonged 0.5 mm. to the rounded sinuses; sepals erect, oblong, 1.2 mm. long, obtuse, membranous, minutely hirtellous on back and margin; exterior teeth broadly triangular, acute, 0.6 mm. long; petals irregularly or- bicular, 2 mm. long, inequilaterally retuse; stamens isomorphic; fila- ments thick, 2.5 mm. long, hirtellous on the inner face, abruptly bent above; anthers very thick, ellipsoid, obtuse, 1.9 mm. long; connective neither appendaged nor prolonged; ovary almost wholly inferior, 5-celled, its broadly conic summit with a circle of about 10 simple erect hairs; styles stout, 3.6 mm. long, finely hirtellous with short crooked hairs; stigma capitate, barely expanded.

description: Glabra infloreseentia excepta; petiolis brevibus gracilibus; foliis elliptico-oblongis vel obovato-oblongis, breviter aeuminatis basi aeutis vel cuneatis suberenatis 3-pli-nerviis; panicula laxa pauciflora; floribus 5-meris longe pedicellatis; hypanthio urceolato carnoso; sepalis late triangularibus, dentibus exterioribus crassis toto adnatis; petalis rotundato-obovatis; staminibus isomorphis; filamentis crassis superne glanduloso-puberulentibus; antheris anguste obovoideis obtusis bi- porosis; ovario, fere toto infero 5-loculare, sulmmo coneavo; stylo crasso glabro; stigmate lato poculiforme.

description: Glabrous to the infloreseence; stem subterete, sparingly branched; petioles slender, up to 10 mm. long; blades firm, elliptic-oblong to obovate-oblong, as much as 32 by 75 mm., short-acuminate, acute or cuneate at base, obscurely and shallowly crenate, with a minute callous tooth in each sinus, 3-pli-nerved; primaries lightly impressed above, elevated beneath, the secondaries very obscure above, plane beneath, almost perpendicular to the midvein; infloreseence few-flowered, loosely paniculate, 5-8 cm. long, minutely and deciduously glandular- punctate; pedicels apparently 5-10 mm. long, the 5-merous flowers actually completely sessile; hypanthium broadly urceolate, 4.4 mm. long to the torus, its wall very thick and fleshy; calyx-tube 0.7 mm. wide, becoming thinner toward the membranous margin; sepals broadly depressed-triangular, 0.5 mm. long; exterior teeth thick pro- tuberances, almost totally adnate, barely surpassing the sepals; petals rotund-obovate, 5.5 mm. long, 4.5 mm. wide; stamens isomorphic; filaments stout and thick, 3.6 mm. long, sparsely glandular-puberulent in the distal half, especially on the ventral side; anthers narrowly obovoid or oblong-obovoid, 3-3.2 mm. long, opening by 2 small ap- proximate pores; connective neither prolonged nor appendaged; ovary almost wholly inferior, 5-celled, its top concave; style very stout, 7.5 mm. long; stigma 2 mm. in diameter, concave.

description: Caule subterete dense tomentoso pilis plumosis; petiolis gracilibus quam laminis 4-5-plo brevioribus dense tomentosis; laminis ellipticis obtusis remote spinuloso-ciliatis basi obtusis 3-nerviis supra juventute stellatis, pilis einereis sessilibus vel breviter stipitatis, mox glabreseen- tibus opacis, subtus stellato-pubeseentibus pilis stipitatis; panicula mediocre ramosa tomentosa eymulis 3-floris ramulos terminantibus, pedicellis elongatis ad medium articulatis; floribus 5-7- (praecipue 6-) meris; hypanthio anguste campanulato cinereo-stellato; sepalis reflexis anguste linearibus hypanthium subaequantibus; dentibus ex- terioribus obsoletis; petalis obovato-oblongis; staminibus subdimor- phis; filamentis glanduloso-hirtellis; antheris oblongis; connectivo basi producto in lobos 2 laterales vel lobos 2 laterales et 1 dorsalem; ovario infero 3-loculare superne truneato dense glanduloso-villoso; stylo elongato inferne glanduloso-tomentoso; stigmate capitato-hemi- sphaerico.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. Studies on the Flora of Northern South America.-XVI. Eleven Neglected Species of Miconia. Brittonia. 1 (3): 113-126.

description: Stem freely branched, subterete, densely gray-tomentose when young with strongly plumose hairs, glabreseent with age; petioles slen- der, as much as 10 mm. long, tomentose like the stem but more densely, the hairs increasing in length distally to nearly 1 mm.; blades firm, drying brown, narrowly elliptic, up to 19 by 45 mm., obtuse or barely apiculate at top, obtuse or subrotund at base, entire, but remotely cili- ate, with short, spinulose, ascending teeth, 3-nerved; primaries im- pressed above, lightly elevated beneath; secondaries obsolete above, they and the tertiaries plane, obscure, reticulate, and scarcely differ- entiated,beneath; upper surface freely stellate when young, very soon glabrous and opaque; lower surface persistently stellate with stipitate hairs; infloreseence paniculate, 6-8 cm. long, rather freely branched, tomentose like the stem, its branches ending in 3-flowered eymules, the pedicels 4-6 mm. long, jointed near the middle; flowers 5-7- (mostly 6-) merous; hypanthium narrowly campanulate, 5 mm. long to the torus, loosely gray-stellate with sessile or short-stipitate hairs; calyx- tube prolonged 0.6 mm., pubescent like the hypanthium; sepals sepa- rated by narrow but rounded sinuses, reflexed, narrowly linear above a triangular base, 4 mm. long, pubescent like the hypanthium on the outer side and the distal half of the inner side; exterior teeth none; petals narrowly obovate-oblong, 5.3 mm. long by half as wide, rounded above, somewhat inequilat,eral; stamens obscurely dimorphic; fila- ments 3 mm. (outer series) or 3.2 mm. (inner series) long, flattened, sparsely glandular-hirtellous mostly on their inner face; anthers scarcely broadened distally, oblong, 4.2 mm. long, opening by a large, obliquely ventral pore; connective prolonged 0.4 mm. below the pol- len-sacs into (outer series) a single, rounded and thickened, lateral lobe on each side, or (inner series) a small latero-ventral lobe on each side and a single dorsal lobe which is truncate or obscurely retuse at base; ovary wholly inferior, 3-celled with numerous ovules, its trun- cate summit densely glandular-villous and 5-foveolate around the style; style 8.5 mm. long, densely glandular-tomentose below, the hairs becoming sparser distally and absent from the upper third; stigma capitate-hemispheric, 1 mm. in diameter.

description: Praeter foliorum margines toto glabra; caulibus obtuse quad- rangulatis, ad nodos membrana crassa reflexa eircumdatis; petiolis gracilibus quam laminis 3-4-plo brevioribus; laminis membranaceis anguste obovatis acuminatis ad basin cuneatis spinuloso-ciliatis 3-nerviis; panicula laxa ramosa, pedicellis elongatis; hypanthio parvo campanulato-hemispherico; sepalis e sinubus latis triangularibus sub- acutis, dentibus exterioribus minutis toto adnatis; petalis obovatis; staminibus isomorphis; filamentis sub apicem angustatis et genticu- latis; antheris obovoideis poro lato dehiseentibus; connectivo dorso incrassato basi in lobum 1 dorsalem et lobos 2 latero-ventrales producto; ovario semi-infero 3-loculare; stigmate capitato.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. Studies on the Flora of Northern South America.-XVI. Eleven Neglected Species of Miconia. Brittonia. 1 (3): 113-126.

description: Glabrous throughout except the leaf-margin; stems conspicuously but roundly 4-angled when young, terete with age, the mature inter- nodes about 3 cm. long, the nodes surrounded by a stout reflexed membrane about 2 mm. wide; petioles slender, 1-2 cm. long; blades thin, bright green, narrowly obovate, as much as 95 by 37 mm., sharply acuminate, long-cuneate at base, spinulose-ciliate (about 15 teeth per centimeter of margin, ascending, 1 mm. long), 3-nerved; primaries lightly impressed above, elevated beneath; secondaries plane above, barely elevated beneath, about 3 mm. apart, ascending at ani angle of about 700; tertiaries obscure above, reticulate beneath; panicle freely branched, lax, 10-12 cm. long and wide, the pedicels apparently 2-4 mm. long, but jointed near the summit, the actual pedicels only 0.5 mm. long; hypanthium broadly campanulate-hemi- spheric, 1.3 mm. long to the torus; calyx-tube very narrow; sepals broadly triangular, 0.4 mm. long, subacute, from broadly rounded sinuses, each with a minute distal thickening representing the ex- terior tooth; petals obovate, 1.8 mm. long, slightly retuse; stamens isomorphic; filaments 2.4 mm. long, flattened below, narrowed and somewhat geniculate at three-fourths of their length; anthers obovoid, 1.3 mm. long, 2-celled, opening by a wide ventro-terminal pore; con- nective thickened basally into a narrow dorsal ridge, ending at base in an obtuse dorsal lobe and 2 minute latero-ventral lobes; ovary half- inferior, apparently 3-celled; style straight anid terete, 3 mm. long; stigma capitate, 0.5 mm. in diameter.

description: Caule tenuiter puberulente atque dense hirsuto pilis violaceis su- perne glandulosis; petiolis elongatis hirsutis; laminis opacis cordato- ovatis obtusis minute erosis 9-nerviis supra subbullatis scabris subtus ad venas hirtis; panicula laxa pauciflora ramis elongatis patulis glan- duloso-hirsutis; floribus 5-meris; hypanthio late campanulato glandu- loso-hirsuto; sepalis late triangularibus e sinubus rotundatis; dentibus exterioribus connatis parte adnata triangulari parte libera crasse sub- ulata sepala excedente; petalis rotundo-obovatis; staminibus isomor- phis; antheris crassis oblongis; connectivo dorso elevato, basi in lobum 1 dorsalem obtusum producto; ovario praecipue infero 5-loculare parte libera breviter conica glabra; stylo gracile; stigmate truneato.

description: Stem freely branched, thinly puberulent and also densely hirsute with erect, dark violet hairs 2-3 mm. long, these simple on the older stems but sparsely glandular distally; petioles slender, hirsute like the stem, the lower 6 cm. long, the upper gradually shortened to 1 cm. or even less; blades firm, dull green, broadly cordate-ovate, as much as 5 by 7 cm., obtuse or obscurely acuminate, minutely and irregularly erose, deeply cordate at base, typically 9-nerved, the outer primaries descending into the auricles; secondaries not well differentiated, with the larger tertiaries strongly elevated beneath, deeply impressed above, forming a bullate upper surface; lower surface freely pubescent on the veins, the hairs decreasing in length with the order of venation; upper surface scabrous with short hairs tending to be grouped in the center of each bullate elevation; upper leaves much smaller, ovate, obscurely cordate at base, more acute, with fewer nerves; infloreseence a loose, widely spreading, open panicle 8-12 cm. long, hirsute like the stem; pedicels 3-5 mm. long, puberulent and glandular; flowers 5-merous; hypanthium broadly round-campanu- late, 2 mm. long to the torus, glandular-hirsute, the hairs denser on the 10 obseure ribs; calyx-tube slightly flaring, prolonged 0.5 mm. to broadly rounded sinuses; sepals depressed-triangular, subacute, 0.8 mm. long; exterior teeth connate at base, the adnate portion of each broadly triangular, the free tip stoutly subulate, 0.8 mm. long, glandular-hirsute throughout; petals spreading, round-obovate, 4 mm. long, barely inequilateral, not retuse; stamens isomorphic; filaments glabrous, flat, 2.3 mm. long; anthers stout and thick, 2.2 mm. long, opening by a minute ventro-terminal pore; connective elevated on the back into a rounded ridge, prolonged 0.6 mm. at base into a bluntly rounded dorsal lobe; ovary two-thirds inferior, 5-celled, the free sum- mit depressed-conic, glabrous; style slender, 6 mm. long; stigma truncate.

description: Caule crasso folioso superne subtomentoso, pilis flexuosis paullum ramosis; petiolis brevibus; laminis coriaceis oblongis abrupte acumi- natis basi obtLsis vel late cuneatis revolutis ciliatis 3-nerviis supra glabris subtus ad venas primarias pubescentibus ceterum glabris; panicula dense ramosa confertiflora inter foliis superioribus sessile; floribus 5-meris brevissime pedicellatis; hypanthio late campanulato tenuissime puberulento; sepalis truneato-triangularibus vel late rotundatis membranaceis; dentibus exterioribus triangularibus ad- pressis sepala subaequantibus; petalis obovatis; staminibus dimorphis; in serie exteriore: antheris oblongis 4-locularibus poris 4 oblique velntro-terminalibus dehiscentibus; connectivo basi paullum elevato et dilatato lobis 2 terminato; in serie interiore: antheris obovatis 2-locularibus poris 2 dehiscentibus; connectivo ad basin insigniter incrassato lobo 1 rotundato terminato; ovario semi-infero 3 loculare glabro; stylo crasso; stigmate capitato.

description: Stem stout, sparsely branched, subterete, leafy (internodes mostly 15-20 mm. long), roughly subtomentose above with very irregular crooked, stout, sparsely branched hairs; petioles slender, 5-10 mm. long, pubescent like the stem but less densely; blades thick and cori- aceous, drying brown above and yellowish beneath, ovate-oblong to obovate-oblong, as much as 30 by 50 mm. (those of the flowering branches shorter and proportionately narrower), abruptly acuminate, obtuse or broadly cuneate at base, strongly revolute, ciliate with stoutly subulate, ineurved teeth, 3-nerved, glabrous above, pubescent on the primaries beneath; primaries strongly impressed above, the secondaries 1.5-2 mm. apart, ascending at an angle of about 700, the tertiaries obsolete; infloreseencee a short (3-5 cm.), freely branched, densely flowered panicle, sessile and surrounded by the upper leaves, pubescent like the stem, especially at the nodes, but with shorter hairs; pedicels merely puberulent, 0.6-0.8 mm. long; flowers 5-merous; hypanthium broadly campanulate, 2.2 mm. long to the torus, essentially glabrous, but actually obscurely puberulent with appressed reddish hairs only 0.03 mm. long; calyx-tube very slightly flaring, prolonged 0.5 mm. to the broadly rounded sinuses; sepals truneate- triangular or broadly rounded, membranous, 0.6 mm. long; exterior teeth acutely triangular, appressed, mostly free, about equaling the sepals; petals obovate, rounded above, 2.2 mm. long; stamens di- morphic; outer series: filaments flattened, 2.8 mm. long, somewhat ineurved at two-thirds of their length; anthers stoutly oblong, 1.4 mm. long, 4-celled, opening by 4 oblique, ventro-terminal pores; connective somewhat elevated and broadened basally, ending in 2 barely divergent, dorsal lobes; inner series: filaments as before, 2.6 mm. long; anthers flat, obovate, 1.2 mm. long, 2-celled and 2-pored; connective prominently thickened basally into a dorsal ridge ending in a rounded basal lobe; ovary half-inferior, 3-celled, the free summit truncate, glabrous; style stout, 3.6 mm. long; stigma capitate, 1 mm. in diameter.

description: Caule 4-angulato ad nodos dense ad internodos breves sparse setoso; petiolis brevissimis glabris; laminis parvis oblongo-ellipticis subacutis basi rotundatis subrevolutis spinuloso-ciliatis 3-nerviis supra glabris subtus ad venas verrueulosis; infloreseentia breve laxa, eymis trifloris ramulos terminantibus; pedicellis brevibus glabris; floribus 5-meris; hypanthio obconico glabro punctato; sepalis triangularibus e sinubus rotundatis; dentibus exterioribus crassis semi-adnatis tri- angularibus acutis; petalis obovatis; filamentis superne angustatis et geniculatis; antheris subdimorphis, obovatis, poro unico dehiseentibus; connectivo in serie exteriore basi subito elevato in carinam angustain lobo obscuro basale terminato, in serie interiore infra antheris in lobos 2 breves rotundatos producto; ovario semi-infero 3-loculare; stylo gracile; stigmate capitato.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. Studies on the Flora of Northern South America.-XVI. Eleven Neglected Species of Miconia. Brittonia. 1 (3): 113-126.

description: Stem strongly 4-angled, heavily setose at the nodes and sparsely so on the internodes with stout smooth hairs 1-2 mm. long, the inter- nodes about 1 em. long; petioles glabrous, 3-5 mm. long, reduced to 2 mm. distally; blades firm, oblong-elliptic, as much as 17 by 30 mm., subacute, rounded at base, sonmewhat revolute, sharply spinulose-ciliate with stout appressed teeth, 3-nerved, glabrous above, sparsely punctu- late and verruculose on the veins beneath; midvein lightly impressed above, elevated beneath; secondaries 1-2 mm. apart, arising at an angle of about 750, the smaller veins all obscure above, lightly ele- vated and reticulate beneath; infloreseence 3-7 cm. long, sparingly and loosely branched, the angular axes nearly glabrous, or setose on the lower nodes, the pedicels 1 mm. long, glabrous; flowers 5-merous, in 3-flowered eymules; hypanthium obconic, 4 mm. long to the torus, glabrous, remotely red-brown glandular-punctate; calyx-tube slightly flaring, 0.5 mm. wide; sepals membranous, triangular, 0.7 mm. long, obtuse or rounded, from broadly rounded sinuses; exterior teeth thick, fleshy, half-adnate, broadly triangular, acute, ineurved, equaling the sepals; petals broadly obovate, 2 mm. long; filaments 4 mm. long, ineurved and narrowed at two-thirds of their length; anthers flat, narrowly obovate-oblong, 2.2 or 2.7 mm. long, opening by a huge terminal pore; connective of the smaller anthers abruptly elevated basally into a narrow dorsal ridge terminating in an obscure basal lobe, that of the larger anthers flat below, continued below the pollen- sacs into 2 short, rounded, barely divergent lobes; ovary half-inferior, 3-celled, its free summit truncate-conic; style straight, slender, 6.5 mm. long; stigma capitate, 0.8 mm. in diameter.

description: Leaves ovate, 6-10 cm. long, acuminate, 5-nerved, cuneate at base; hypanthium 5 mm. long, in fruit elongating to 16 mm. Schomburgkc without number; also in the Amazon valley from Par'a to eastern Peru.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Small to medium tree, sometimes shrub-like; angles of young first-year twigs narrowly but prominently winged; petioles 0.5-2 (-3) mm long; blade ovate to narrowly or broadly elliptic or almost round to obovate, 1.0-3.4 (-3.7) cm long, 0.5-1.9 (-2.4) cm wide (the parenthetical measurements all refer to Ekman 115047); margin often somewhat revolute, the base narrowly to broadly acute, often cuneate, the apex narrowly to broadly acute (the acuteness sometimes accentuated by inrolled margins on both sides) to rounded to emarginate, often mucronulate; midrib rounded to flat below, rarely (Ekman H15047) somewhat rectangular in the middle, not winged; lateral veins not visible, or very indistinct, above and below; upper surfaces of dried leaves smooth to minutely rugulose or less often punctulate, the lower surfaces smoother; stomatal crypts when regularly present 30-85/mm2, their cavities averaging 40-60 µ, in diameter; central bodies of foliar ternminal selereids when elongate up to 3 times as long as wide, the arms usually prominent, their length up to twiee the body thickness, 5--40 per cent of the selereids having the body very short and with a stellate appearance; upper epidermis predominantly single, sometimes up to 6 per cent of the cells doubled, the inner walls of the epidermal cells not mucilage-thickened (a few doubtful instances seen in Abbott 2233). Racemes 1 per leaf axil, 5-12 mm high to the ovary base of the terminal flower; joints in the central axis 2, the flowers per raceme 1-3, the bracts at the joints ovate-trianoular, acute, 0.8-1.3 mm long, deciduous early or late, often presenlt when the fruit is imature; length of the true pedicel (ovary to first joint below) 1.5-3.5 mm. Inferior ovary ca. 1.6 mm high, turbinate, the sides only slightly convex, angle "o" (fig. 6) 1600-1640; length of the calyx (including ovary height) ca. 5.3 fmnr; ratio of length of calyx to width of calyx-lobe ca. 3.15; calyx-lobes ca. 1.0-1.7 mm high from the stamein attachment, ca. 1.6-2.1 mm wide, 0.5-1.0 times as high as wide, the free ends triangular or broadly so, acute (fig. 17), the margins minutely fringed with short hairs; fusion distance of adjacent lobes above the stameen attachmelent 0.4-0.7 mm, the lobes usually separating at anthesis; ratio of fusion distance to width of lobe 0.2-0.4; mature petals unknown, the immature ones ovate-triangular, acute, 4 mm long, 3 mm wide, the base truncate or with a claw ca. 0.3 mm long and 1.5 mm wide; anthers 2.25-2.45 mm long; ovary 2-locular, 7-9-ovuled; ripe fruits orange, 1-4-seeded, more or less globose when 1-seeded, their dry measurements then ca. 5-8 mm in diameter, 5-9 mm long, lobed according to the number of seeds, up to ca. 10 mm or more thick when more than 1-seeded.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1957. A Revision of Mouriri, Section Nesophytum. Brittonia. 9 (2): 109-131.

description: Strict plants, 3-10 dm tall; shoots arising from a conspicuously enlarged, whitish, spongy crown, the cylindrical tap root large (up to 3 dm long and 2 cm thick), whitish, spongy, non-tuberous and with poorly developed branch roots. Stems becoming woody or spongy below, nearly terete about the middle, sometimes compressed upward, with white and green speckled unequal faces with narrow, light green or yellowish vertical striae, the edges of the faces very slightly if at all winged, the nodes and internodes glabrous. Leaves 2-8 cm long, 4-15 mm wide, 3(-5)-nerved, the nerves usually yellowish, especially near the base, sessile, glabrous on both surfaces, the lower ones sometimes grayish, appearing glaucous; juvenile and basal leaves frequently subrotund, the middle and upper leaves lanceolate (-elliptic), with acute (-acuminate) apices, the margins entire or more often distantly serrate beyond the middle. Flowers few to many in open, much-branched cymes; bracts above the first flower conspicuously smaller than the leaves, early deciduous, somewhat clasping, densely glandularpubescent on the margins and the abaxial surfaces (occasionally glabrous), the upper surfaces glabrous. Hypanthium (fig. 5) at maturity varnished-appearing, densely glandular-hispid (occasionally glabrous), 8-12 mm long, the neck usually shorter than the body, not constricted at the base and gradually, if at all, ex- panded above; calyx-lobes small, ca. 1-2 mm long, deltoid to lanceolate, and usually spreading. Petals purple, spreading, usually with glandular hairs on the abaxial surfaces, relatively large (up to 2-2.5 cm long), of a broad obovate type. Anthers long, mostly 7-9 mm in length, declinate, strongly curved to sigmoid, appearing smooth under 10 x magnification, becoming more or less symmetrically oriented in such a way that they tend to be parallel and declined toward one side of the flower, dehiscing by a small pore ca. '/3 the diameter of the anther tip, the appendage wanting or present as a minute protuberance or spur. Capsule glabrous, or with a few purple, glandular hairs near the apex, broadly pyriform, ca. 5-7 mm long and 4-5 mm wide, the style deciduous slightly above the capsule, leaving a short tubercle at the apex. Seeds (fig. 21) oblong, ca. 1-1.5 mm long, appearing smooth under 10 x magnification, the micropylar end larger, tapering somewhat toward the chalazal end. Flowering from May through Aug.
bibliographicCitation: James, Charles W. 1956. A Revision of Rhexia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 8 (3): 201-230.

description: Plants frequently rigid, 3-7 dm tall; shoots arising from each of several tuberous roots formed the previous year. Stems usually much-branched above, becoming thickened, brown-spongy below, the faces essentially equal with thin, usually inconspicuous wings at their edges; internodes glabrous; nodes with dark brown, relatively conspicuous, divergent bristles ca. 1-3 mm long. Leaves linear- lanceolate to lanceolate, 2-3.5 cm long, 3-9 mm wide, 3-nerved, the nerves prom- inent below and yellowish, sessile, glabrous below, with few scattered hairs above, the tips obtuse (-acute), the margins serrulate (-serrate) especially be- yond the middle. Flowers usually numerous in much-branched cymes, the bracts similar to the leaves, persistent. Hypanthium (fig. 6) at maturity 7-11 mm long, glabrous or with few scattered hairs on the body and neck, and with yellowish bristles, some as long as the calyx-lobes, about the rim of the hypanthium, the neck usually shorter than the body, not constricted below, gradually and only slightly expanded above; calyx-lobes linear to lanceolate, 3-6 mm long, frequently l/- the length of the hypanthium, ascending, the tips conspicuously aristate. Petals dark rose to purple, spreading, with glandular hairs on the abaxial surfaces, 11-20 mm long, and of a broad obovate type. Anthers long (ca. 6-9 mm in length), declinate, curved, appearing smooth under 10 x magnification (minutely papillose basally under 20 x magnification), dehiscing by a small pore ca. l/3 the diameter of the anther tip, the appendage wanting or short, spur-like. Capsule glabrous, somewhat elongated, with a more or less conical apex, ca. 5-7 mm long, and 4-5 mm wide. Seeds (fig. 22) cochleate, ca. 0.5-0.7 mm long, with relatively thick, verrucose, compressed-appearing, longitudinal ridges. Flowering from June through September.
bibliographicCitation: James, Charles W. 1956. A Revision of Rhexia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 8 (3): 201-230.

description: Shoots (1-)2.-4(-5.5) dm tall, arising from the bases of previous shoots, from extensive, horizontal-spreading roots, or from specialized tuberous roots. Stems with well-developed, leafy, axillary branchlets, glandular-hirsute, one pair of opposing faces flat to concave, of a lighter, yellowish-green color, and much narrower than the other pair of rounded or convex faces, the edges of the faces inconspicuously winged, if at all. Leaves linear, obovate, (elliptic, (1.5-)2-3.5 (-5) cm long, 1-4(-6-8) mm wide, with obtuse (-acute) apices and acute or cuneate bases, the margins thin, serrulate to shallowly serrate, frequently ciliate, the cilia divergent, 1-nerved (lateral veins occasionally present, but inconspicuous), glabrous on both surfaces or glandular hirsute above and with few hairs on the veins below. Flowers few to numerous in much-branched cymes; upper bracts of the larger inflorescences gradually reduced in size, persistent. Hypanthium (fig. 7) at maturity glandular-hirsute, (9-)10-13(-15) mm long, the neck longer than the body, not constricted below, gradually expanded above; calyx-lobes deltoid to lanceolate, 2-4 mm long, divergent, the tips generally straight. Petals typically purple, occasionally dark rose, spreading, the margins of the abaxial surfaces commonly glandular-hispid, (1-)1.5-2(-2.5) cm long, of a broad obovate type. Anthers 7-11 mm in length, declinate, free from the connective basally, curved, the basal portion appearing papillose under 10 x magnification, dehiscing by a small pore ca. 1/3 the diameter of the anther tip; the appendage short spur- like or filamentous and up to ca. 0.5 mm in length. Capsule glabrous, globose, with an obtusely conical apex, 5-8 mm long, 4-6 mm wide. Seeds (fig. 23) coch- leate, ca. 0.55-0.75 mm long, with very conspicuous, compressed-appearing, nearly continuous ridges. Flowering from March through August. (Flowering period more irregular in southern Florida and the West Indies; flowering collections are known from these areas in December and February.)
bibliographicCitation: James, Charles W. 1956. A Revision of Rhexia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 8 (3): 201-230.

description: Shoots 1-5 dm tall, arising from a thickened crown with few to many cylindrical, fibrous, non-tuberous roots. Stems usually much-branched, becoming woody below, the faces flat to convex with thin inconspicuous wings at their edges; internodes glandular-hirsute, the nodes glabrous or with few, short, appressed hairs. Leaves 1.5-2.5 cm long, 2-8 mm wide, 3-nerved, sessile (-subpetiolate), abaxial surface minutely pustular with scattered hairs; lower leaves oblong to obovate with entire margins and obtuse apices, the middle and upper ones obovate, linear to elliptic with glandular-ciliate (-serrate) margins, acute or frequently cuneate bases, the apices apiculate or with a gland-tipped hair. Flowers usually numerous in 3-flowered cymes, the bracts persistent, essentially like the leaves. Hypanthium (fig. 3) at maturity glabrous or with few scattered glandular hairs, ca. 5-8 mm long, the neck shorter than the body, extending upward for ca. 0.5 mm, then abruptly expanded above to a diameter somewhat less than that of the body; calyx-lobes deltoid, ca. 1-3 mm long and nearly as wide at the base; the adaxial surface pustular, the abaxial surface and margins with glandular hairs. Petals yellow, divergent to somewhat ascending, glabrous, 7-13 mm long, and of an oblong type. Anthers short, 1.5-2 .5 mm long, erect, straight, adnate with the connective their entire length, appearing smooth under 10 x magnification (minutely pustular under higher magnification), dehiscing by a very large pore nearly the diameter of the anther tip. Capsule glabrous, subglobose, the apex long-attenuate, extending into the neck of the hypanthiuni. Seeds (fig. 19) cochleate, 0.5-0.7 mm long, with low, thin, continuous longitudinal ridges. Flowering from April through July.

description: Shoots 3-8(-10) dm tall, arising from the bases of previous shoots, from extensive, horizontal-spreading roots, or from tuberous roots. Stems with well- developed, leafy, axillary branchlets, (nearly glabrous) to hirsute, sometimes densely so with coarse, yellow or purple hairs; one pair of opposing faces flat to concave, lighter, yellowish-green in color, and much narrower than the other pair of rounded or convex faces, the faces with inconspicuous wings, if any. Leaves lanceolate to (elliptic), (3-)4-5(-7) cm long, (5-)7-12(-15) mm wide, with acute to acuminate tips and rounded to acute bases, the margins serrulate to serrate, usually ciliate, 3-nerved, commonly sessile (-petiolate), the quality and degree of pubescence like that of the stem. Flowers few to many in open cymes, the bracts persistent, the upper ones usually much reduced, with entire (-serrate) margins. Hypanthium (fig. 8) at maturity typically glabrous, occasionally with few scattered, glandular hairs, (9-)10-12(-14) mm long, the neck usually longer than the body, not constricted below and gradually if at all expanded above; calyx-lobes 1-3 mm long, deltoid to (lanceolate), divergent, the tips generally straight. Petals usually deep purple, occasionally dark rose, spreading, the margins of the abaxial surface commonly glandular-hispid, (1-)1.5-2.5(-3.5) cm long, of a broad, obovate type. Anthers 7-9(-11) mm long, declinate, curved, free from the connective basally, the lower part appearing papillose under 10 x magnification, dehiscing by a small pore ca. 1/3 the diameter of the anther tip, the appendage filamentous, up to 1.5 mm long. Capsule nearly pyriform, glabrous or occasionally with few gland-tipped hairs at the apex, ca. 5-7 mm long and 4-6 mm wide. Seeds (fig. 24) cochleate, ca. 0.5-0.7 mm long, with longitudinal rows of short papillae (usually longer and more conspicuous at the distal end). Flower- ing from March into October.
