description: Small, occasionally prostrate plants, 0.4-3.5 dm tall; shoots arising from the bases of previous shoots or from a woody crown; the roots non-tuberous. Stems commonly unbranched, becoming woody below, the faces flat to convex and essentially equal, with thin inconspicuous wings at their edges; internodes gla- brous, the nodes glabrous or with few short, appressed hairs. Leaves 4.12 mm long, 3-10 mm wide, 3-nerved, subpetiolate, glabrous on both surfaces, the lower surface frequently reddish; lower leaves rotund with entire margins and obtuse apices, the middle and upper ones rotund-ovate (-ovate-elliptic) with serrulate (sometimes distantly so) or glandular-ciliate margins. Cymes somewhat con- densed, few (-8)-flowered, the bracts persistent. Hypanthium (fig. 1) at maturity densely glandular-hispid, 5-8 mm long, the neck shorter than the body and conspicuously constricted below to 1/4 the diameter of the body or less, abruptly expanded above to a diameter nearly equaling that of the body; calyx-lobes 1-2 mm long, about as broad as long, rounded to deltoid, spreading, the margins entire. Petals rose to purple, ascending to divergent, with glandular hairs on the abaxial surface, 8-12 mm long, and of an oblong type. Anthers short, ca. 1-2 mm long, erect, straight, adnate with the connective their entire length, appearing smooth under 10 x magnification, and with a remnant of a partition sometimes present on the adaxial wall, dehiscing by an arc-shaped suture on the adaxial surface near the apex which breaks loose after anthesis leaving a very large pore nearly the diameter of the anther tip; appendage absent or occasionally present as a minute protuberance or spur. Capsule glabrous, subglobose, ca. 3-4 mm long and 4.S mm wide, the apex depressed, the style deciduous at the pit of the depression. Seeds (fig. 17) curved, nearly semicircular, ca. 0.6-0.7 mm long, with short, low, interrupted and irregularly spaced ridges, more or less oriented in a longitudinal plane. Flowering from May through September.

description: Small plants, 1-2 dm tall; shoots arising from the bases of previous shoots, from a slightly thickened crown, or along slender, horizontal-spreading, non- tuberous roots. Stems usually branched above the middle, hirsute, becoming woody below; the faces inconspicuously winged, nearly equal below the middle, but with the flat to concave pair of faces becoming narrower above and of a lighter, yellowish-green color. Leaves mostly 1.5-3.5 cm long, 4-8 mm wide, 3-nerved, with few scattered gland-tipped hairs on both surfaces, definitely petio- late, the petioles 2-4 mm long with few glandular hairs; the lower leaves obovate to rotund, the lower surface sometimes reddish; the middle cauline leaves usually elliptic to somewhat lanceolate with acute apices and acute or occasionally cuneate bases, the margins uniformly serrate, frequently ciliate; upper leaves smaller, with fewer hairs and less conspicuous serrations. Flowers small, borne in rather open, sparsely branched, few-flowered cymes; bracts similar to the upper leaves, persistent. Hypanthium (fig. 4) at maturity 4-6 mm long, glabrous or with few inconspicuous gland-tipped hairs mostly about the neck, the neck shorter than the body, neither constricted below nor expanded above; calyx-lobes deltoid to lanceolate, with entire margins, ca. 1.5-2 mm long, erect to spreading, and usually equaling or exceeding the length of the neck. Petals small, white, spreading, glabrous, ca. 6-9 mm long, and of a broad obovate type. Anthers short (ca. 2-3 mm long), erect, only slightly curved, the extreme basal portion free from the connective, the entire surface usually appearing minutely papillose under 10 x magnification, dehiscing by a small pore ca. 1/3 the diameter of the anther tip, the appendage present, short-spur-like or filamentous and up to 1 mm long. Capsule glabrous, subglobose, ca. 3-4 mm high and 4-5 mm wide, the style deciduous flush with the rounded apex. Seeds (fig. 20) cochleate, ca. 0.4-0.5 mm long, with low, compressed-appearing, longitudinal ridges, and usually papillose at the distal end. Flowering in June and July.

description: Frequently rigid plants, 2-7 dm tall; shoots arising from the bases of previous shoots or from a somewhat thickened, cylindrical crown, rarely from horizontal-spreading roots; roots non-tuberous. Stems strict, sometimes branched above, becoming woody below, the faces flat to convex with thin, inconspicuous wings at their edges; internodes glabrous, the nodes glabrous or with short, appressed hairs. Leaves 1-2.5 cm long, 4-14 mm wide, 3-nerved, subpetiolate to petiolate, the abaxial surface glabrous, the adaxial surface with long, frequently purple, usually non-glandular hairs; lower leaves rotund to ovate with obtuse apices and serrulate to serrate margins (sometimes distantly so, rarely entire), the upper leaves ovate to elliptic with acute apices and serrate to ciliate margins. Flowers several in few, relatively condensed cymes, the bracts leaf-like and appearing as a loose involucre about the inflorescence. Bypanthium (fig. 2) at maturity glabrous, 5.9 mm long, the neck conspicuously constricted below and abruptly expanded above; calyx-lobes conspicuous, 2.4 mm long, 2-3 mm wide at their bases, divergent, with serrate to ciliate margins. Petals rose to purple, ascending to divergent, glabrous, 0.9-2 cm. long, and of an oblong type. Anthers similar to those of R. nuttallii except that a protuberance or spur-like appendage is more often present. Capsule like that of R. nuttallii except usually slightly larger (ca. 4-5 mm long and 4-6 mm wide, and the seeds (fig. 18) also somewhat larger ca. 0.65-0.75 mm long). Flowering from June into October.

description: A shrub 1-3 meters high. Stems freely hirsute with spreading simple bristles usually 2-4 mm. long. Petioles stout, hirsute like the stern, mostly 8-15 mm., rarely up to 30 mm. long. Leaf-blades firm, usually ovate, varying to subrotund or oblong, abruptly acuminate, usually distinctly crenate and long-ciliate, at the base sometimes obtuse, usually broadly rounded or more or less cordate, 5-nerved, the smaller veins usually strongly elevated beneath, hirsute on both sides (hairs mostly 2-4 mm. long). Infloreseelnces 5-12-flowered, 2-3 cm. long, trichotomous from near the base, densely hirsute. Hypanthium broadlyi cylindric, 4-4.5 mm. long, densely hirsute, the hairs simple, spreading, 2-4 mm. long. Calyx-tube flaring, prolonged about 0.5 mm.; sepals obscure, depressed, 1 mm. long or less from the torus; exterior teeth subulate, about 4 mm. long, hirsute. Petals white, obovate-oblong, 8-11 mm. long. Anthers subulate, 4.5-5 mm. long; connective prolonged below the filament into a minute dorsal lobe. Ovary two-thirds superior, tipped with a terete glabrous neck; style about 8 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: A shrub 1-2 meters high. Branches stout, the younger densely tomentose with short-stipitate stellate hairs surmounted by numerous simple and glandular bristles. Petioles stout, 5-10 mm. long, tomentose like the stem. Leaf-blades thick, velvety-green, oblong-ovate or ovate-lanceolate, up to 15 cm. long by 7 cm. wide, acute to acumi- nate, minutely denticulate, barely cordate at the base, 7-nerved, above elosely bullate, each projection tipped with a short stout hair, be- neath foveolate, densely stellate-tomentose, also setose on the primary veins; veinlets finely reticulate. Infloreseences usually 2-4 cm. long, stout and compact, the lateral branches about 5 mm. long. Hy- panthium hemispheric, 3 mm. long, densely stellate-tomentose, densely hirsute with mostly glandular hairs about 2 mm. long. Calyx-tube barely developed; sepals oblong, 1.3 mm. long from the torus, rounded above, ciliate; exterior teeth subulate, 4 mm. long from the torus, pubescent like the hypalnthium. Petals narrowly obovate, 4-5 mm. long. Filaments 3-3.5 mm. lolng; anthers curved, slelnderly subulate, the thecae 2.5 mm. long; colnnective sleilder, prolonged 0.7 mm. below the thecae. Ovary half-inferior, 5-celled, glandular-setose at the sum- mit; style 3.5-4 mm. long; stigma capitellate.

description: A shrub 1-3 meters high. Younger stems densely hirsute with yellowish, mostly flexuous hairs up to 6 mm. long, overlying an indument of stellate hairs. Petioles stout, usually 5-15 mm. long, densely hirsute like the stem, the hairs nearly or quite as long. Leaf-blades firm, oblong-ovate to broadly ovate, up to 20 cm. long by 10 cm. wide, acute or more often acuminate, inconspicuously denticulate and long- ciliate, rounded or rarely subeordate at the base, 5-nerved, densely hirsute above, the hairs mostly 1-1.5 mm. long, densely pubescent beneath with crisped or flexuous hairs usually 1-1.5 mm. long, the stel- late hairs nearly concealed. Infloreseences crowded, spiciform, mostly 3-5 cm., rarely up to 10 em. long, the lower lateral clusters sometimes short-stalked; axis and branches densely hirsuite, the hairs up to 6 mm. long, also sparsely glandular with much shorter, almost concealed hairs, the internodes rarely more than 1 cm. long. Bracts, hypan- thium and calyx densely hirsute, the hairs up to 6 mm. long, and usually concealing the exterior teeth of the calyx; also stellate- tomentose. Hypanthium canipanulate, about 3 mm. long. Calyx-tube nearly 1 mm. long; sepals depressed-ovate, 1.6-2 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth 3-4 mm. long from the torus. Petals oblong-obo- vate, 6 mm. long. Anthers stoutly subulate, 2 mm. long, the thecae convolute; connective simp]e. Ovary 5-celled, half inferior, setose around the base of the style; style 5-7 mm. long; stigma truncate.

description: Resembling the preceding species in habit. Stems very minutely furfuraceous. Petioles of the larger leaves 4-10 cm. long, minutely furfuraceous. Blades thin, ovate or ovate-oblong, 12-20 cm. long, 8-13 cm. wide, sharply acuminate, conspicuously serrate, cordate at the base, 7-nerved, essentially glabrous on both sides. Smaller leaves lanceolate, short-petioled, 1-5 cm. long. Cymes branched only at the base, about 3-flowered, each branch about 3 mm. long, with a single terminal flower and a pair of minute bracts at the middle. Flowers 4-merous. Hypanthium urceolate, 2-2.3 mm. long, constricted above, hirsute with simple bristles up to 2 mm. long, minutely punctate beneath the bristles. Sepals triangular-ovate, about 1 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth foliaceous, oblong, up to 5 mm. long, more or less dentate, irregularly long-ciliate. Ovary 4-celled.

description: A shrub 1-4 meters high. Younger sterns slender, densely glandular- pubeseent, the straight hairs 1 mm. long or less, and thinly stellatepubeseent. Petioles slender, 1-4 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Leaf-blades thin, ovate-lanceolate to ovate-oblong, up to 18 cm. long by 9 cm. wide, usually much smaller and very irregular in size on each branch, acuminate, inconspicuously denticulate, rounded to broadly acute alnd usually inequilateral at the base, 5-pli-nerved, the lateral primaries often alternate, minutely pubescent on both sides, especially on the veins beneath. Infloreseence sparsely branched, lax, few-flowered, 3-8 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Hypanthiuni tubular, 2.5 mm. long, glandular-hirsute and densely furfuraceous. Calyx-tube 0.3 mim. long, the sepals scarcely differentiated; exterior teeth erect, subulate, 1 mm. long. Petals oblong, 2-2.5 mm. long, ierveless. Anthers stoutly subulate, 1.5-2 mm. long; connective simple.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Shrub, the stem furfuraceous-puberuleiit and hirsute with straight hairs 2-3 mm. long. Leaves thin, ovate or round-ovate, 10-20 cm. long, 5-17 cm. wide, sharply acuminate, conspicuously denticulate and ciliate, cordate-claspinig at the sessile base, 7-nerved, the outer pair more or less submarginal, setose above with hairs about 1.5 mm. long, 1-1.5 mm. apart, the primary veins (and to some extent the secondary ones) often outlined by a line of shorter, more crowded hairs, inereasing in density toward the base, beneath glabrous alnd finely reticulate on the actual surface, setose oln the veins and veinlets, the number of hairs inereasing on the larger veins; formicaria basal, about 5 mm. in diameter, didynious, pubescent like the stem. Inflorescence freely branched, up to 15 cm. long, pubescent like the stem; bracts subulate, 1 mm. long, with a subulate terminal seta 3-4 mm. long. Hypanthiumn narrowly campainulate, about 5 nim. long, very minutely puberulent and sparsely setose (hairs about 1 mm. long). Calyx-tube prolonged 0.5 mm.; sepals broadly triangular, 1 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth spreading, stoutly subulate, 1.7 mm. long. Petals obovate-oblong, 2.5 mm. long. Filamelnts clavate, 2.2 mm. long; alnthers stoutly linear, 2.8 mm. long, the pore terminal; colnnective simple. Ovary inferior, 4-celled; style tapering above, 7-8 mm. long; stigma capitellate.

description: Shrub up to 2 meters high, beginning to flower when herbaceous and 2-3 dm. high. Stems stout, very densely hirsute with spreading, matted, ascending, or subappressed, yellowish or brownish, simple hairs, the internodes usually only 2-3 cm. long. Petioles none, or stout, up to 3 cm. long, averaging about 5 mm., pubescent like the stem. Leaf-blades thick, dark-green above, varying from oblong-lanceolate to broadly elliptic, up to 12 cm. long by 6 cm. wide, acute or even aeuminate to broadly obtuse, minutely denticulate to entire, cunieate to broadly rounded at the base, 5-pli-nerved, above minutely bullate and densely hirsute, beneath foveolate and softly villous. Flowers few, sessile in the axils. Hypanthium cylindric, 3.5-4 mm. long, densely hirsute with aseending simple hairs. Calyx-tube very short; sepals triangular-ovate to semicircular, 1-1.3 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth triangular at the adnate base, above stoutly subulate, divergent, 1-1.5 mm. long from the torus, hirsute like the hypanthium. Petals obovate-oblong, 2-3 mm. long. Filaments slightly clavate, 2-3 mm. long; anthers straight, linear-subulate, 3-4 mm. long, the pore dorso-teriminal, the thecae convolute toward the base; connective minutely prolonged. Ovary two-thirds inferior, 4-celled, glabrous or glandular-setose at the summit; style 6-8 mm. long; stigma punctiform.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Shrub, the stems very minutely stellate-furfuraceous and delnsely hirsute, the hairs mostly 2-4 mm. long. Formicaria at the base of the petiole, up to 15 mm. in diameter, pubeseent like the stem. Petioles slender, 12-40 mm. long, pubescent like the stem (some hairs often glandular), one of each pair usually twice as long as the other. Leaf blades thin, broadly ovate, up to 18 cm. long by 13 cm. wide, sharply acuminate, broadly dentate, densely ciliate, subcordate at the base, 5-nerved or ocasionally 7-nerved, sparsely setose above (hairs usually 2.5 mm. long, 1.5-2 mm. apart), beneath setose on the primary and secondary veins (hairs decreasing in number and length on the secondaries), glabrous and resinous-dotted on the tertiaries and surface. Infloreseence very small and compact, the peduncle 1-3 mm. long; bracts subulate, 1-2 mm. long, short-setaceous at the tip. Hypanthium narrowly campanulate, 3-3.5 mm. long, minutely puberulent. Calyxtube erect, 0.6 mm. long; sepals triangular, obtuse, about 1 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth stoutly subulate, spreading or decurved, 0.7 mm. long, densely hirsute with hairs 2-3 mm. long. Petals obovateoblong, 2 mm. long. Filaments narrowly clavate, 3 mm. long; anthers linear, 3.5 mm. long; connective simple. Ovary inferior, 4-celled; style 7-8 mm. long; stigma truncate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Frutex epiphyticus ad 4 m altus, ramis, petiolis, laminis, pedunculis, et bracteis utrinque hirsutis, trichomatibus omnino ebarbellatis aliquando glandulosis. Folia dimorphica, chartacea, elliptica vel oblongo-elliptica, ad basim acuta vel rotundata, ad apicem caudata, subtus plerumque 3-nervata aliquando 5-nervata, nervorum pari interiore prominente, pari exteriore inconspicuo, petiolo (3-) 6-14 mm longo. Lamina major (6.8-) 8-14 (-16) cm longa et (3-) 4-6 cm lata. Lamina minor 1.5-5.5 (-7.5) cm longa et 1-3.5 cm lata. Pedunculi graciles, axillares, solitarii, 3.5-5.8 cm longi, bracteis sessilibus, trichomatibus 0.5-1 mm longis indutis, eis paris exterioris elliptico-lanceolatis, ad apicem acuminatis, (18-) 21-28 mm longis et 6-10 (-12) mm latis, eis paris interioris elliptico-lanceolatis, ad apicem acutis, (16-) 19-22 (-26) mm longis et (5-) 7-10 mm latis. Hypanthium (maturum) sub- globosum a medio ad apicem contractum, strigosum, trichomatibus ebarbellatis aliquando glandulosis. Calycis lobi filiformes, hirsuti, 15-22 mm longi et 0.5-1 mm lati. Petala alba vel subrosea, glabra, obovata, ad apicem emarginata, 14-18 mm longa et (10-) 12-15 mm lata. Stamina isomorphica, glabra, inter se non cohaerentia, filamentis (3-) 4-5 mm longis, thecis oblongis 4-5 X 1-2 mm, connectivo dorsaliter 1-1.5 mm supra basim calcari minuto elevato. Stylus glaber, 12-13 mm longus; stigma punctiforme; ovarii apex glaber. Semina 1-1.5 mm longa, brunneola, nitida, clavata, lunata vel anguste pyriformia.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, Jr., F. 1974. A New Epiphytic Blakea (Melastomataceae) from Panama. Brittonia. 26 (4): 393-397.

description: Stems slender with elongate internodes, densely arachnoid-tomentose with appressed or matted stellate hairs. Leaves unequal in each pair. Petioles 5-15 mm. long, slender, pubeseent like the stem. Leafblades thin, broadly ovate or subrotund, 9-16 cm. long, 6-14 cm. wide, rounded above to an abruptly acuminate tip, entire, broadly rounded at the base, 5-7-nerved, glabrous above, thinly arachnoid-stellate on all veins beneath, glabrous on the surface. Infloreseence freely branched, about 10 cm. long, pubeseent like the stem; peduncle 3-4 cm. long; bracts subulate, 1 mm. long; pedicels 0.4 mm. long. Hypanthium distinctly urceolate, 3.5 mm. long to the torus, strongly 8-costate, closely stellate-tomentose, the hairs about 0.3 mm. across. Calyx erect, its tube scarcely prolonged; sepals broadly triangular, 0.6-0.7 mm. long from the torus, the free margin none; base of the exterior teeth covering the whole sepal, the body conic, divergent or slightly ascending, 0.6 mm. long on the top, 1.2 mm. long from the torus, tipped with a short seta. Petals broadly oblong-obovate, 2.2 mm. long, slightly retuse, nearly equilateral, obseurely nerved. Filaments broad and flat, 1.7 mm. long; anthers straight, subulate, the thecae 2.5 mm. long, the pore dorso-terminal; connective prolonged 0.4 mm. below the filament into a broadly rotund, minutely glandular, dorsal appendage. Ovary inferior, 4-celled; style terete, 4.5-5 mm. long; stigma truneate.

description: Shrub 1-3 meters high. Younger branches slender, terete, hirsute with brownish, slender, simple, somewhat deflexed bristles about 2 mm. long. Petioles rather stout, 1-2 cm. long, hirsute like the stem. Leaf blades thin, ovate-lanceolate, 7-14 cm. long, 2-6 cm. wide, long-acuminate, obseurely crenate, conspicuously ciliate, obtuse to rounded at the base, 5-nerved, hirsuLte above with slender hairs 1.5-2 mm. long and 1-2 mm. apart, hirsute on the veins beneath with somewhat shorter hairs, glabrous on the suLrface; secondary veins spreading at an angle of about 80º. Panicle trichotomously branched from the very base, 2-3 cm. long, hirsute like the stem, the hairs shorter; apparent pedieels slender, about 6 mmn. long; aetual pedieels very short; braets subulate, about 1 mum. long. Flowers 5-merous. Hypanthium broadly tubular, 3.5-4 mmn. long, hirsute with spreading simple hairs up to 1.5 mm. long and (unless faded) distinetly reddish or purple in color. Calyx-tube prolonged about 0.5 mm.; sepals subsearious, ovate or triangular-ovate, 1.2 mm. long from the torus, setose at the tip; exterior teeth triangular and adnate below, the free portion spreading, subulate, 1.6 mm. long. Petals oblong-obovate, 4-4.5 mm. long. Filaments strongly flattened; anthers semiovoid, 1.4 mm. long; eonneetive thickened basally and very minutely prolonged below the theeae. Ovary wholly inferior, 5-celled; style 4-4.5 mm. long; stigma capitellate.

description: Slender shrub 3 m. high, the stems subterete, very minutely and closely brown-furfuraceous. Petioles about 1 cm. long. Blades thin, bright-green, elliptic, up to 15 cm. long and 6 cm. wide, acuminate, entire, cuneate at base, 5-pli-nerved, glabrous on both sides; secondary veins obscure above, spreading at nearly right angles. Peduncles axillary, very minutely fttrfuraceous, simple and 15-20 mm. long with a terminal glomerule, or forked and 1-10 mm. long, with one terminal and two lateral partial peduncles about 15 mm. long, each bearing a terminal glomerule, or proliferate with one terminal and two sessile lateral glomerules. Glomerules 2-6-flowered; outer bracts opposite, round-ovate, 3 mm. long, spreading; inner bracts broadly obovate, erect, 2.5 mm. long, becoming deeply bifid. Flowers 5-merous, sessile. Hypanthium campanulate, 2 mm. long, minutely furfuraceous. Calyx irregularly split at anthesis inlto 3-5 triangular acute lobes 0.8 mm. long; exterior teeth stoutly subulate, slightly spreading, 0.5 mm. long. Petals white, obovate-oblong, 4 mm. long. Filaments stout, 2 mm. long; anthers semi-ellipsoid, 1.5 mm. long, opening by a ventro-terminal pore; connective simple. Ovary inferior, 5-celled; style straight, stout, 5 mm. long; stigma truncate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Sect. Staphidinm: Frutex gracilis 3 m. altus. Rami superiores graciles subteretes aretissime einereo-stellato-furfuracei, internodiis 3- 5 cm. longis. Petioli 10-15 mm. longi, superne anguste alati. Laminae membranaceae oblongo-ellipticae, usque 15 cm. longae 5.5 cm. latae, abrupte acuminatae, basi breviter cuneatae, integrae, 5-pli- nerviae, subtus ad venas primarias tenuissime furfuraceae ceterum glabrae. Pedunculi axillares, aut simplices 10-20 mm. longi, aut 2-10 mm. ultra basin trifureati, ramis 10-15 mm. longis, aut proliferati capitula 2 opposita et ramum terminalem gerentes, ubique minutis- sime furfuracei. Capitula 1-3-flora, bracteis infimis basi connatis late ovatis coilcavis 3 mm. longis, bracteis superioribus erectis 2.5 mm. longis alte bifidis. Flores sessiles 5-meri. Hypanthium campanu- latum ad torum 2 mm. longum minutissime furfuraceum. Calyx 1.3 mm. longus ad anthesin in lobos 3-5 late triangulares irregulariter ruptus, dentibus exterioribus crasse subulatis patulis 0.5 mm. longis. Petala alba obovata 3.8 mm. longa, apice rotundata, paulo inaequilatera. Stamina 10 isomorpha. Filamenta curvata alba glabra 2 mm. longa. Antherae complanatae semi-ellipticae 2-loculares 1.5 mm. longae. Ovarium inferum 5-loculare. Stylus subrectus glaber 5 mm. longus, stigmate truncato.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: A shrub up to 1.5 meters high. Younger stems strongly flattened and 2-edged, nearly black beneath with furfuraceous dull-brown indu- ment, eventually glabrous. Larger leaves sessile, chartaceous, ovate- lanceolate, up to 19 cm. long and 7 cm. wide, acuminate, entire, rounded or broadly obtuse at the base, 3-nerved with an additional pair of marginal veins, glabrous and shining above, very finely pubescent with pale-brown hairs along the veins beneath; smaller leaves lanceolate, 1-3 cm. long, soon deciduous. Infloreseences long-peduncled, freely branched, many-flowered, up to 18 cm. long, the branches very slender, minutely pubescent. Flowers apparently long-pedicelled, actually sessile. Hypanthium campanulate, 3 mm. long, very minutely furfuraceous. Calyx-tube prolonged about 0.7 mm., the broadly rounded sepals scarcely differentiated; exterior teeth stoutly subulate, barely exceeding the sepals. Anthers linear, the connective prolonged 0.3 imm. below the filament into a thick, flat, subrotund, obscurely 3-lobed, dorsal appendage. Ovary 4-celled; style 4 mm. long; stigma punctiform.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Frutex radicibus scandens; caules juniores paleacei; petioli breves paleacei; laminae obovato-oblongae 3-nerviae supra glabrae, subtus in vena media paleaceae ceterum glabrae; flores 5-meri; hypanthium tubulosum fere glabrum; sepala brevia semicircularia, dentibus exterioribus brevibus subulatis; petala minima, connectivum infra filamenti apicem in lobum ovatum dorsalem productum.

description: A shrub climbing by numerous roots. Younger stems terete, evanes- cently paleaceous with straw-colored scales 1-2 mm. long, the internodes about 1 cm. long. Petioles stout, 4 mm. long, paleaceous like the stem. Leaf-blades thin, narrowly obovate-oblong, up to 18 cm. long by 7.5 cm. wide, one member of each pair about half as long as the other, short- acuminate, entire or barely undulate, narrowed below to a rounded base, 3-nerved with an additional pair of marginal veins, glabrous above, beneath densely paleaceous on the midvein, thinly so on the laterals, glabrous on the surface. Flowers verv few, 5-merous, the clusters 1-3 cm. long. Hypanthium tubular, 2.4 mm. long, sparsely puberulent with ineurved hairs 0.04 mm. long. Calyx-tube somewhat flaring; sepals depressed semicircular, 0.5 mm. long froin the torus; exterior teeth broadly triangular below, the free tip 0.4 mm. long. Filaments broad and flat, 1.1 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, 2 mm. long, the pore dorso-terminal; connective prolonged 0.4 mm. below the filament into an ovate dorsal lobe. Ovary wholly inferior, 4-celled; style 4.5 mm. long, somewhat thickened in the middle; stigma truncate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Stems slender, terete and essentially glabrous. Petioles 8-12 mm. long. Leaf-blades firm, shining, elliptic, 6-9 cm. long, 2.5-4 cm. wide, abruptly contracted into a linear tip 2-3 cm. long, entire, cuneate at the base, 3-pli-nerved, glabrous. Panicle sessile, trichotomous from the base, the branches divaricate, very slender, 3-5 cm. long, each bearing 3-5 4-merous flowers on pedicels 2-3 mm. long. Hypanthium (after anthesis) subglobose, 2.2 mm. long, very minutely lepidote (as also the pedicel and calyx). Sepals triangular, subacute, 0.9 mm. long; exterior teeth exactly similar, appressed, almost wholly adnate. Petals and stamens unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Frutex; caules hirsuti atque dense furfuraceo-tomentosi; folia petiolata, ovata, breviter acuminata, integra vel serrulata, basi obtusa vel rotundata, 5-nervia, supra purpureo-setosa, subtus pilosa et ad venas furfuracea; panicula subsessilis conferta furfuracea; hypan- thium subglobosum dense hirsutum, toro annulo pilorum ornato; sepala carnosa patula triangularia, dentes exteriores paulo excedentia; petala quadrata; antherae crasse subulatae, connectivo in calearem dorsalem brevem produeto; ovarium inferum; stylus longus inedio inerassatus, stigmate punctiformi.

description: Shrub about a meter high. Stems when young densely or sparsely hirsute with simple hairs 1-4 mm. long, overlying a dense furfur- aceous tomentum. Petioles stout, 1-3 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Leaf-blades thin, deep green, ovate, 8-17 cm. long, 4-9 cm. wide, short-acuminate, rounded or broadly obtuse at the base, 5-nerved, sparsely hirsute above with purple hairs, deusely pilose on the surface and also furfuraceous on the veins beneath. Panicles sessile, 1-2 cm. long, crowded or often with only 1-4 flowers; pedicels stellate-furfur- aceous, 2-5 mm. long. Flowers 5-merous. Hypanthium densely hirsute with simple purplish hairs 1-1.8 mm. long and nminutely stel- late-furfuraceous; torus densely pubescent with a ring of ascending hairs 0.4 mm. long. Calyx fleshy, spreading, the sepals depressed- triangular, about 0.5 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth slightly shorter, mostly adnate, pubescent like the hypanthium. Petals thick, obliquely quadrate, 1.4 mm. long and wide. Filaments very stout, flattened, 1.3 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, arcuate, the thecae 1.8 mm. long; connective prolonged straight back into an oblong dorsal spur 0.4 mm. long. Ovary wholly inferior, 5-celled. Style straight, 5.6 mm. long, conspicuously thickelled in the middle; stigma punctiform.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Shrub, the stem densely hirsute with retrorse setae 7-10 mm. long. Petioles stout, 2-5 cm. long, hirsute like the stem, the hairs somewhat spreading. Formicaria at the summit of the petiole, 15-20 mm. long, semi-ovoid, long-hirsute with spreading hairs. Leaf-blades ovate or ovate-oblong, up to 20 cm. long by 11 cm. wide, abruptly short-acuminate, entire, prominently ciliate, broadly rounded to subcordate at the base, 5-7-nerved, hirsute above with slender yellowish hairs up to 8 mm. long, beneath densely hirsute on the primary veins at their base, decreasingly so on the smaller veins or glabrous. Inflorescence trichotomous, 3-8 cm. long, of which half is peduncle, long-hirsute; bracts subulate, about 1 mm. long, short-setose at the apex. Hypanthium campanulate, 2-2.5 mm. long, nearly square in cross-section, very minutely puberulent (hairs 0.02-0.04 mm. long) and occasionally with a few long setae. Calyx sparsely hirsute with a few stiff setae, the tube 0.8 mm. long; sepals ovate-triangular, obtuse, 1.3 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth slenderly subulate, erect, inserted above the level of the sinlus, exceeding the sepals by 0.3 mm. Petals narrowly obovate-oblong, 5 mm. long. Filaments flat, 2.5 mm. long; anthers linear, truncate, 2.5 mm. long; connective simple. Ovary half inferior, 4-celled, the free summit conic, minutely pubescent; style 6 mm. long; stigma punctiform.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Arbor parva 3-4 m. Ramuli primum paulo compressi demum teretes sicut petioli foliorum subtus laminae inflorescentia hypanthiaque dense indumento stellulato-lepidoto appresso induti. Petioli 0.8-1.7 cm; lamina 7.5-12 X 2.4-4 cm chartacea elliptica vel elliptico-lanceolata apice acuminata basi acuta, 3-plinervata. Panicula 2-2.5 cm longa; flores 5-meri sessiles, bracteolis 3-4 X 0.5 mm linearioblongis valde caducis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 3 X 2.5-3 mm; calyx primum in cono apiculato clausus demum in lobos irregulares persistentes ruptus, dentibus exterioribus obscuris. Petala 4 X 2 mm glabra obovato-oblonga apice oblique truncata. Stamina isomorpha glabra; filamenta 2.5-3 mm longa; antherarum thecae 2 X 0.75-1 mm oblongae, connectivum nec prolongatum nec appendiculatum. Stylus 6-6.5 mm glaber; stigma punctiforme; semina 0.5 mm cuneata et calcarata.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, Frank. 1983. Three New Mesoamerican Species of Miconia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 35 (1): 42-48.

description: Tree 3-4 m tall. Distal branchlets flattened and 2-edged when young, becoming rounded with age. Young shoots, distal internodes, petioles, lower leaf surfaces, inflorescences, and hypanthia reddish-brown and densely stellulate-lepidote. Leaf blades chartaceous, entire or sometimes varying to bluntly denticulate, 7.5-12 cm long and 2.4-4 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, acuminate apically and acute basally, commonly stellate-lepidote above when young but glabrous at maturity, 3-plinerved with a prominulous network of secondaries and tertiaries, the innermost pair of primaries diverging from median nerve mostly 0.4-1 cm above the petiole-laminar junction; petioles 0.8-1.7 cm long and 1.5-2 mm broad. Inflorescence a panicle mostly 2-2.5 cm long, shorter than subtending leaves, the ultimate units commonly terminating in congested clusters of 3 sessile flowers; bracteoles sessile, apparently early deciduous and mostly absent at anthesis, linear-oblong to oblanceolate, 3-4 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, stellulate-lepidote throughout. Hypanthium (at anthesis) narrowly campanulate to suburceolate, 3 mm long to the torus and 2.5-3 mm broad. Calyx closed in bud and rupturing at anthesis into irregular ± persistent lobes mostly 2 mm long; calyx teeth obsolete or evident as blunt protuberances at or near the torus. Petals 5, glabrous, reportedly white but turning pink when dry, oblong-obovate, truncate to oblique apically, entire, 4 mm long, 2 mm wide distally. Stamens 10, isomorphic; filaments glabrous, ligulate, constricted distally, 2.5-3 mm long, ca 0.25 mm wide; anthers 2 mm long and 0.75-1 mm wide, yellow, linear-oblong, ± rounded distally and tipped with a ventrally inclined pore; connective simple, barely thickened dorsally but not dilated or prolonged below the thecae. Ovary totally inferior with a densely setose rim surrounding the crateriform cavity created by stylar abscission. Style straight, glabrous, 6-6.5 mm long; stigma punctiform. Berry globose, 3-4 mm long to the torus and 4 mm in diameter. Seeds 0.5 mm long, cuneate, angularly ridged with a conspicuous spur on the distal truncate surface.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, Frank. 1983. Three New Mesoamerican Species of Miconia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 35 (1): 42-48.

description: Sect. Eunticontia: Frutex 3 m. altus, ramis superioribus molliter tomentosis, pilis brunneis apice ramosis. Petioli validi, 2-3 cm. longi, stellato-tomentosi. Laminae elliptico-oblongae vel anguste ovatae, membranaceae, maximae 28 cm. longae 13 cm. latae, acuminatae, leviter serrulatae, majores basi rotundatae et leviter cordulatae, minores basi acutae, 5-nerviae, supra ad venas primarias stellato-hispidae, ad pa- ginam sparsissime et minute pilosae, subtus molliter stellato-tomentosae praecipue ad venas; venae secundariae et tertiariae supra obsoletae, subtus prominentes et reticulatae. Infloreseentia paniculata paucira- mosa 5-10 cm. longa, stellato-tomentosa. Flores 5-meri, sessiles, il glomerulos 3-floros aggregati. Hypanthiunm carnosum poculiforme 2 mm. longum, dense tomentosum, pilis albidis stellatis. Calycis tubus erectus, 0.5 nmm. longus; sepala ovata vel triangulari-ovata, 0.8 mm. longa, dentibus exterioribus adnatis tuberculiformibus. Petala alba obovato-oblonga 2.7 mm. longa, apice rotundata, fere aequilatera. Stamina isomorpha. Filamenta tenuia complanata 2 mm. longa. Antherae lineares 2-loculares, 1.7 mm. longae, connectivo basi in lobum dorsalem decurvum producto. Ovarium semi-inferum 5-loculare, summo glabrum. Stylus glaber 4 mm. longus, stigmate truneato.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: Arbor parva 3-5 m. Ramuli graciles primum rotundato-quadrangulati demum teretes sicut petioli laminae subtus inflorescentia hypanthiaque sparse stellato-puberuli. Petioli 0.6-1.5 X 0.5 mm; lamina 6-11.3 X 2.1-3.4 cm elliptica vel elliptico-lanceolata apice abrupte caudato-acuminata basi obtusa, 3-nervata vel 3-plinervata, chartacea et integra vel obscure crenulata. Panicula 3-5 cm longa; flores 5-meri sessiles vel subsessiles, bracteolis 0.5-1 mm longis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 1 mm altum; lobis interioribus late triangularibus in fructu persistentibus, dentibus exterioribus minutis paullulo (0.25 mm) eminentibus. Petala 1.5-2 X 1 mm obovato-oblonga. Stamina paulo dimorpha glabra; filamenta 1.5-2 mm longa; antherarum thecae 1.5 X 0.25 vel 1.25 X 0.25 mm angustae oblongae, poro paulo ventraliter inclinato (stamina maiora) vel dorsaliter inclinato (stamina minora); connectivum (stamina maiora) ad basim dorsaliter cauda 0.25 mm longa armatum, connectivum (stamina minora) ad basim dorsaliter ca 0.1 mm prolongatum. Stylus 3.5-5 mm glaber, stigma subcapitatum.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, Frank. 1983. Three New Mesoamerican Species of Miconia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 35 (1): 42-48.

description: Tree 3-5 m tall. Young internodes subquadrangular, becoming rounded with age. Distal branchlets, petioles, inflorescences, and hypanthia copiously stellate pubescent. Leaf blades chartaceous, typically entire but varying to bluntly crenulate, 6-11.3 cm long and 2.1-3.4 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, caudateacuminate apically and acute basally, sparsely stellate pubescent above when young but becoming glabrate at maturity, sparsely to moderately stellate below, 3-nerved or 3-plinerved with a faint network of secondaries and tertiaries below; petioles 0. 6-1.5 cm long and 0.5 mm broad. Inflorescence a laxly branched panicle 3-5 cm long, shorter than subtending leaves; bracteoles sessile, widely spreading, subulate, 0.5-1 mm long and mostly less than 0.25 mm wide, copiously stellate pubescent. Flowers sessile or subsessile, closely subtended by two bracteoles. Hypanthium (at anthesis) campanulate, 1 mm long to the torus and 1-1.5 mm broad. Calyx lobes (on fruiting hypanthium) erect, persistent, 0.25 mm long, depressed-triangular to bluntly acute; calyx teeth consisting of persistent, deltoid or subulate callosities largely concealing calyx lobes. Petals 5, glabrous, reportedly white but drying yellow, obovate-oblong, ± rounded apically, entire, 1.5-2 mm long, and mostly 1 mm wide. Stamens 10, anisomorphic; filaments alternately 1.5 mm and 2 mm long; anthers linear, alternately 1.25 mm and 1.5 mm long, the larger with a truncate somewhat ventrally inclined pore and a connective that is prolonged dorsally below the thecae into a blunt, caudiform, ventrally concave appendage, the smaller with a dorsally inclined pore and a small lobate distension of the connective below the thecae. Ovary ca 1/3 inferior, glabrous at the summit. Style straight, glabrous, 3.5-5 mm long; stigma subcapitate. Berry globose, costulate when dry, reportedly red but drying purple, 2-2.5 mm long to the torus and 2-2.5 mm in diameter. Seeds ovoid to ? pyriform, beige, smooth and vernicose, mostly 0.75-1 mm long.

description: Young twigs usually puberulent, rarely glabrous; under side of leaf midrib usually glabrous, rarely puberulent; petioles 0.2-1.0 (-1.5) mm long; blades (30-) 40-210 times as long as the petiole, 1.3-3.2 (-3.8) times as long as wide; true pedicels 0.2-2.0 (-3.0) mm long; free part of calyx lobes (0.8-) 1.0-3.0 mm long; calyx length from stamen attachment (1.2-) 1.5-3.8 mm; petals 3.8-5.8 mm long, 1.6-3.6 mm wide, 1.6-2.7 times as long as wide; anther sporangia 1.1-1.9 mm long.

description: Rami subsucculenti subquadrati juniores cum petiolis pedicellisque densiuseule puberuli glabrati. Petioli 1.5-4 cm longi graciles; lamina integra memrbranacea 6-12 X 4-8 cm late elliptica apice breviter (ad 5 mrm) subabrupteque acuminata basi late obtusa 5-nervia (nervulis marginalibus tenuibus neglectis) nervis secundariis supra et subtus tenuiter prominulis ca. 2 mm inter se distantibus, supra glabra et dense albo-punctulata, subtus in nervis primariis densiuscule furfuracea alioqui glabra. Flores 6-meri in axillis foliorum fasciculati in quaque axilla ca. 5; pedicelli graciles, ad anthesim 1.2-1.5 cm longi; bracteae liberae 4.5-5.5 mm longae suborbiculares apice rotundatae vel late obtusae, extus basim versus sparse furfuraceae. Hypanthium glabrum 5 mm longum (ad torum); calycis tubus 1.2-1.3 mm altus, lobis vix conspicuis ca. 0.8 X 3.1-3.5 mm. Petala 11.5 X 7.5-8.5 mm obovata apice rotundato-truneata inconspicue ciliolata (ciliis ca. 0.1 mm longis) apicali-centraliter modice punctata. Antherae inter se adhaerentes; filamenta 10.5 mm; thecae 9.8 mm longae lineares apice dorsaliter porosae, connectivo dorsaliter in calear hebes 1.1 X 0.6 mm prolongato. Stylus 13.6 X 0.5-0.6 mm; stigma truneatum; ovarium liberum glabrum 6-loculare apice truneatum et coneavum, fovea ca. 0.6 mm alta.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1957. Certamen Melastomataceis IV. Brittonia. 9: 101-109.

description: Epiphytic, epipetric, or terrestrial suffrutescent herbs 1-3(6) dm tall. Uppermost cauline nodes and internodes terete, moderately to copiously beset with a mixture of appressed or antrorsely spreading, partly glandular compressed hairs (0.25)0.5- 2(4) mm long and an inconspicuous ground layer of minute, glandular hairs but typically glabrous with age. Principal leaves strongly dimorphic in each pair, chartaceous and ciliate; above typically glabrous or sparingly beset with a few simple hairs mostly 0.5-1.5 mm long; below moderately strigose on the elevated primary and secondary veins, otherwise essentially glabrous. Larger leaf at each node 5.5-13.2 cm long and 1.8-5.5 cm wide, obovate-panduriform, abruptly long- acuminate at the apex, obliquely rounded to cordulate at the base, 5-plinerved, crenate to crenulate along the distal half of the blade varying to subentire; petiole 0.4-1.5 cm long. Smaller leaf at each node 3-9 mm long and 3-8 mm wide, ovate to suborbicular or subreniform, bluntly acute to obtuse at the apex, mostly sym- metrically cordate at the base, faintly 3-nerved, entire; petioles up to 0.5 mm long but commonly appearing subsessile. Inflorescence terminal, (2)5-13(18)-flowered, 2-10 cm long, beset with an indument like that of the uppermost cauline inter- nodes. Pedicels (in fruit) 1-2 mm long, with pubescence like that of the uppermost cauline internodes. Hypanthia (at anthesis) 1.5-2 mm long, beset with pubescence like that of the uppermost internodes but often becoming glabrate with age. Calyx lobes (flowering hypanthia) 0.5 mm long and 1 mm wide basally between sinuses, bluntly deltoid to broadly rounded, erose and glandular-ciliolate, otherwise es- sentially glabrous or sparingly beset with a few hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially; calyx teeth subulate or setiform, 0.5-1 mm long, inserted subapically on the abaxial surface of calyx lobes. Petals glabrous, typically white (rarely pink), obovate, entire, bluntly acute to rounded at the somewhat thickened apex, 3.5 mm long and 3 mm wide. Stamens dimorphic. Antesepalous stamens: filaments 2 mm long and 0.5 mm wide at the broadened base; anthers linear-oblong, 1 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, the apical pore ventrally inclined; connective prolonged ca. 0.25 mm below the thecae, the 2 ventral clavellate appendages mostly 1.75 mm long  Antepetalous stamens: filaments 1.5 mm long; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, the apical pore as in the antesepalous anthers; connective prolonged less than 0.25 mm below the thecae, modified dorsally into a minute, rounded knob and ventrally into an upturned, bifid appendage 0.5 mm long. Ovary gla- brous, inferior. Style 3.25 mm long; stigma subtruncate. Fruiting hypanthia 3-4 mm long and 6-9 mm wide on each of 3 sides. Seeds 0.5 mm long.

description: Epiphytic or climbing, rooting in mosses on trees, the slender stems sordid-tomentose. Larger leaves on pubescent petioles 5-10 cm. long; blades meinbranous, broadly round-ovate, up to 20 cm. long by 14 cm. wide, but usually proportionatelv broader, abruptly short-acuminate, irregularly erose-crenate, ciliate, broadly rounded or subtruneate at the base, 7-nerved, above hirtellous with hairs 1 mm. long or less and the same distance apart, similarly pubescent on the lower surface, more densely so on the primary and secondary veins. Smaller leaves ovate-lanceolate, short-petioled, 1-3 cm. long. Panicles divaricately branched, 1-2 cm. long, produced far below the leaves and scarcely protruding from among the roots and mosses, the slender branches thinly furfuraceous; bracts triangular-subulate, 1-1.5 mm. long; pedicels about 0.5 mm. long. Flowers 4-merous. Hypanthium urceolate, 2 mm. long, constricted above, hirsute with simple bristles up to 1 mm. long. Calyx tube not prolonged, bearing several erect setae up to 2.5 mm. long; sepals cartilagilnous, semicircular, 0.5-0.6 mm. high, almost wholly adnate; exterior teeth foliaceous, obovate or subrhombic, 2.5 mm. long, thick, with a few stout setae on the margin. Anthers oblong, 4-celled, the inner cells not extending to the apex. Ovary inferior, 4-celled.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Shrub about a meter high. Stems slender, apparently sparsely branched, thinly but closely stellate-tomentulose when young, glabrescent in age. Petioles slender, unequal in alternate pairs, 8-33 mm. long, stellate like the stem. Leaf-blades membranous, ovate, 5-12 cm. long, about half as wide, acuminate, entire, finely spinulose-ciliate, rounded or subcordate at the base, 5-nerved, glabrous above, very minutely stellate beneath on the primary and secondary veins only. Panicles few-flowered, branehed mostly from near the base only, the branches capillary, nearly or quite glabrous, up to 2 cm. long; bracts subulate, 1 mm. long or less; actual pedicels up to 1 mm. long, pubescent like the hypanthium. Hypanthium obeonic to subeylindric, 3 mm. long, ribless, sparsely covered with minute, short-stalked, brownish, stellate hairs about 0.1 mm. long. Calyx-tube prolonged about 0.5 mm., somewhat flaring; sepals broadly triangular, 1.5 mm. long from the torus, broadly acute, separated by sharp sinuses; exterior teeth conspicuously thickened on the back of the sepals, prolonged into a conic tip, about 2 mm. long from the torus. Petals cuneate or narrowly obovate, 8-9 mm. long, equilateral, barely retuse. Filaments very narrowly clavate, 3 mm. long; anthers stoutly linear, 2.7 mllm. long, the pore terminal; connective simple. Ovary two-thirds inferior, 4-celled, its glabrous summit truneate-conic; style very slelnder, 6 mm. lolng; stigma minute but capitate.

description: A freely branehed shrub. Younger stems sparsely hirsute witl dark-maroon hairs up to 4 mm. long, soon glabreseent; internodes up to 12 cm. long. Petioles slender, up to 5 cm. long, hirsute like the stem. Leaf-blades thin, ovate-oblong, up to 15 cm. long and 9 cm. wide, acuminate, remotely denticulate (teeth 0.4 mm. long, about 2 mm. apart), cordulate at the base, the sinus very narrow, 5-nerved, glabrous on both sides. Infloreseences up to 15 cm. long, when young hirsute like the stem, the internodes and primary branches up to 5 cm. long, the secondary branches much shorter, the flowers rather crowded and very short-pedicelled. Hypanthiuni 2 mn. long, glabrous, very minutely red-pinctate. Calyx-tube prolonged; sepals nearly semi-circular, 0.7 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth almost wholly adnate, equaling the sepals, triangular-acuminate, scarcely spreading. Petals obovate, 3 mm. long, "yellow." Anthers semi-ovoid, 1.5 mm. long; connective simple, slightly gibbous near the base. Ovary 5- celled, two-thirds inferior; style 4 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Stems densely hirsute with slender spreading simple hairs up to 6 mm. long, overlying a thin indument of very slender appressed hairs 1-2 mm. long. Petioles stout, 2-4 cm. long, pubescent like the stem, the smaller hairs more loosely appressed. Leaf-blades firm, ovate-oblong, up to 15 cm. long by 7 cm. wide, acuminate, minutely denticulate and ciliate, rounded at the base, 5-nerved, above sparsely hirsute with subulate hairs up to 1 mm. long and about the same distance apart, beneath densely villous, the slender hairs varying from 3 mm. long on the primary veins to 1 mm. long on the surface. Infloreseence fewflowered, divaricately branched, 2-3 cm. long. Hypanthium cupshaped or subcylindric, 2.7 mm. long to the torus, thin-walled, ribless, densely hirsute with ascending simple hairs reddish in color, up to 2.2 mm. long. Calyx-tube slightly flaring, prolonged 0.3 mm.; sepals trianlgular froim rounded sinuses, acute, 1.6 mmn. long from the torus; exterior teeth divergent shortly below the apex of the sepal, curvedascending, 3 mm. long from the torus, pubescent like the hypanthium, the hairs decreasing distally. Petals thick, oblong, 3.7 mm. long, 1.1 mm. wide, entire, equilateral. Filaments flat, slightly thick celled distally, 2 mm. long; anthers stoutly fusiform, 2.3 mm. long; connective simple. Ovary half inferior, 4-celled, its summit glabrous, 4-lobed; style very slender, 5.6 mm. long; stigma punctiform.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Frutex, ramis petiolisque dense fulvo-hirsutis, pilis usque 11 mm. longis simplicibus; laminae longe petiolatae, ovato-oblongae, acuminatae, crenatae, basi rotundatae, 3-nerviae, utrinque setosae; inflorescentia ramosa pluriflora, dense hirsuta, bracteis hirsutis lanceolatis magnis; hypanthium campanulatum, longe hirsutum atque minutissime glandulosum; sepala semicircularia, eroso-ciliata, minutissime glandulosa, dentibus exterioribus subulatis apice longe setosis; petala obovato-oblonga; antherae crasse lineares, connectivo basi brevissime producto; ovarium semi-inferum 5-loculare; stylus medio incrassatus, stigmate truneato.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Shrub. Younger branches 4-angled, dark maroon, freely hirsute with simple bristles up to 11 mm. long, the internodes much elongate. Petioles stout, up to 4 cm. long, hirsute like the stem. Leaf-blades rather firm, ovate-oblong, up to 15 cm. long and 7 cm. wide, crenate (teeth 2.5 mm. long, 1 mm. high) and ciliate (cilia mostly 2-3 mm. long), rounded or broadly obtuse at the base, 3-nerved, setose above with brown hairs 2-2.5 mm. long, setose beneath with straw-colored hairs as much as 5 mm. long on the primary veins, decreasing to 1 mm. long and mostly confined to the veins. Infloreseence freely branched, many-flowered, densely hirsute like the stem; bracts persistent, lanceolate, up to 10 mm. long, densely hirsute-ciliate; pedicels about 2 mm. long. Hypanthium tubular-campanulate, 3.5-4 mum. long, densely hirsute with slender hairs up to 3 mm. long, a few of them glandular, also closely red-punctate with glandular hairs 0.1 mm. long. Calyxtube prolonged nearly 1 mm.; sepals searious, erect, 1.6 mm. long from the torus, semicircular, erose-ciliate, glandular like the hypanthium; exterior teeth almost wholly free, triangular at the base, subulate above, about 5.5 mm. long, or nearly 10 mm. including the long terminal seta, long-setose throughout. Petals narrowly obovate-oblong, 8-8.5 mm. long. Filaments flat, 2.5-3 mm. long; anthers stoutly linear; connective prolonged about 0.6 mm. below the thecae. Ovary half inferior, 5-celled, the summit truncate-conic, 1.3 mm. high, glandular like the hypanthium; style 4-4.5 mm. long, slightly thickened about the middle, tapering above; stigma truncate.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Shrub. Stems densely tomentose with brownish stellate hairs, also glandular with stout spreading hairs up to 0.5 mm. long. Petioles stout, 15-35 mm. long, pubescent like the stem. Leaf-blades firm, ovate-oblong or ovate-lanceolate, iup to 22 cm. long and 12 cm. wide, subacuminate, obscurely ciliate-denticulate (cilia curved-ascending, 0.5 mm. long), rounded at the base, 5-nerved (an additional pair of submarginals may be conspicuous), densely pubescent above (hairs about 0.3 mm. apart, varying from stout, curved, nearly 1 mm. long, to slender, straight, 0.4 mm. long), densely tomentose beneath with short-stipitate stellate hairs. Infloreseence up to 10 cm. long, pubescent like the stem, the flowers closely aggregated at the ends of the branches; bracts subulate, up to 1 mm. long; pedicels 0.5-1 mm. long. Hypanthium tubular, 3.5 mm. long, thick-walled, thinly tomentose with subsessile stellate hairs, densely glandular-pubescent (hairs stout, 0.2 mm. apart, 0.5 mm. long). Calyx-tube erect, 0.7 mm. long, thinly stellate externally; sepals broadly ovate-triangular, 1.3 mm. long from the torus, stellate externally, internally closely glandular with incurved hairs 0.03 mm. long; exterior teeth arising near the end of the sepals, divergent at right angles, 0.3-0.4 mm. long from the sepals. Petals obovate, 3.5 mm. long, very inequilateral. Anthers linear-subulate, 3 mm. long, the pore terminal; connective simple. Ovary half inferior, 4-celled, the free summit truncate-conic, glabrous; style 5.5 mm. long, tapering to the punctiform stigma.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Low tree; younger stems and petioles densely strigose with simple hairs 1-1.5 mm. long. Petioles 2-3 cm. long. Leaf-blades firm, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 10-13 cm. long, 4.5-6 cm. wide, acuminate, finely and irregularly denticulate, ciliate, rounded at the base, 7-plilerved, the inner pair arising at a fifth to a fourth of the length of the blade, scabrously hirsute above, the hairs with broadly conic bases 0.5-1 mm. wide ending in a curved subulate bristle 0.8-1.5 mm. long, marked with narrow glabrous strips along the secondary veins, thinly strigose on the midvein (more or less so on the laterals), beneath foveolate, strigose on the primary veins, softly villous on the other veins (hairs about 0.3 mm. long), glabrous on the surface. Panicle trichotomous from the base, 10 cm. long and wide, its branches strigose like the stem; bracts narrowly subulate, 1.5-2 mm. long; pedicels 1-2 mm. 1ong. Flowers 5-merous. Hypanthiuini cup-shaped, 2.2 mm. long to the torus, densely substrigose with gray simple bristles 1.5-2 mm. long, 0.2 mm. apart. Calyx-tube prolonged about 0.3 mm.; sepals very thin, depressed-ovate, obtuse, glabrous, 1 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth triangular at the base, adnate for 0.5 mm., thence subulate, 4-4.5 mm. long, densely gray-substrigose. Petals and stamens immature. Ovary half inferior, 5-celled, minutely pubeseent on the rounded summit; style immature.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Sect. Euniconia: Frutex 2.5 m. altus, ramis superioribus gracillimis juventute minutissime pilosulis mox glabris, pilis simplicibus, internodiis usque 12 cm. longis. Petioli graciles, 1-3.5 cm. longi, minutissimne pilosuli. Laminae membranaceae, siceitate nigreseentes, anguste elliptico-oblongae, utrinque acuminatae, integrae, minute sparseque ciliolatae, usque 18 cm. longae 6 cm. latae, in jugis alternis paulo inaequales, 5-plinerviae, utrinque minutissimne pilosulae (pilis circa 0.05 mm. longis) mox glabreseentes, venis supra planis tertiariis obsoletis, subtus leviter prominentibus late reticulatis. Inflorescentia paniculata 5 cm. lata 4 cm. longa, ramosa, ramis gracilibus minutissime hirtellis. Flores 4-meri sessiles. Hypanthium subglobosum 1.6 mm. longum, minutissime pilosulum, obscure 8-costatum. Calyx tenuis membranaceus 0.8 mm. longus, ad anthesin irregulariter ruptus, dentibus ex- terioribus minutis tuberculiformibus acutis. Petala ovata 1.8 mm. longa 1 mm. lata, subacuta, 3-nervia. Stamina isomorpha. Filamenta leviter arcuata, 1.3 mm. longa, superne dilatata. Antherae crasse lineares, 2 mm. longae, poro minuto dorso-terminali dehiseentes, con- nectivo basi paulo dilatato in appendicem ovatam obtusam producto. Ovarium semi-inferum 2-loculare, summo rotundato glabro. Stylus rectus glaber, 3.3 mm. longus, stigmate truneato.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: Shoots 0.1-1.2 m tall, arising from tuberous roots, the roots cylindrical, thickened, fibrous, bearing I-several tuberous organs. Stems simple or branched, frequently becoming woody or thickened, brown-spongy below, the faces slightly convex, essentially equal and with well-developed wings (ca. 0.25-2 mm wide) at their edges; internodes with few, scattered, horizontal-spreading, glandular hairs, the nodes usually more or less tufted, with soft hairs. Leaves ovate or ovate-lanceolate to elliptic, with obtuse (-acute) bases and acute (-obtuse) apices, the margins serrate-ciliate, (1-)2-7(-10) cm long, (0.5-)1-2(-3.5) cm broad, 3-5(-7)-nerved, sessile to petiolate, the petioles up to 5 mm long; upper surface hirsute, scattered hairs below commonly restricted to the veins. Flowers few to numerous in much-branched cymes, the bracts serrate to glandular-ciliate, gradually decreasing in size upward (abruptly so in larger inflorescences). Hypanthium (fig. 11) at maturity sparsely glandular-hispid, 7-10 mm long, the neck shorter than the body, not constricted below, gradually if at all expanded above; calyx-lobes deltoid to lanceolate, 1-2.5 mm long, divergent to recurved (usually ascending and incurved in flowers terminating main stems). Petals dark rose to purple, spreading, 8-17 mm long, of a broad, obovate type, with few to many glandular hairs on the abaxial surface. Anthers 5-7 mm long, declinate, curved, free from the connective basally, appearing papillose near the base under 10 x magnification, dehiscing by a small pore ca. 1/3 the diameter of the anther tip, the appendage short, spur-like or filamentous and ca. 0.5-1 mm long. Capsule pyriform, glabrous or with a few gland-tipped hairs at the apex, ca. 5-7 mm long and 4-5(-6) mm wide. Seeds (fig. 27) cochleate, ca. 0.65-0.8 mm long, with relatively thick, conspicuous papillae, especially on the dorsal crest. Flowering from June into October.
bibliographicCitation: James, Charles W. 1956. A Revision of Rhexia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 8 (3): 201-230.

description: Shoots (2-)3-6(-8) dm tall, arising from the lower axillary buds of previous shoots or from various points along thin, extensive, horizontal-spreading, non- tuberous roots. Stems with well-developed, leafy, axillary branchlets, glandular- hirsute; one pair of opposing faces flat to concave, of a lighter, yellowish-green color, and much narrower than the other pair of rounded or convex faces, the edges of the faces with thin, inconspicuous wings, if any. Leaves elliptic, some- times narrowly so, occasionally lanceolate, with acute tips and bases, the mar- gins serrate, usually ciliate, (2-)3-6 cm long, (0.5-)0.8-1.5(-2) cm wide, 3-nerved, petiolate, the upper surface hirsute, the lower surface with few scattered hairs at least on the veins. Flowers few to many in open cymes; the bracts persistent, gradually reduced above, their margins entire to serrate or ciliate. Hypanthium (fig. 9) at maturity glandular-hirsute (rarely glabrous), (8-)9-11 mm long, the neck usually lohger than the body, not constricted below and gradually if at all ex- panded above; calyx-lobes 1-3 mm long, deltoid to lanceolate, the tips often recurved. Petals light lavender-white to rose (occasionally dark rose), spreading or even reflexed, glabrous, ca. 1-1.5(-2) cm long, of a broad obovate type. Anthers (4.5-)6-8(-9) mm long, declinate, curved, appearing papillose at least near the base under 10 x magnification, dehiscing by a small pore ca. 1/3 the diameter of the anther tip; appendage filamentous, 0.75-1.5 mm long. Capsule glabrous, glo- bose, with somewhat ittenuate apex, mostly 5-7 mm long, 4-6 mm wide. Seeds (fig. 25) cochleate, ca. 0.5-0.7 mm long, sparsely muricate to short papillose, the processes usually oriented in longitudinal rows. Flowering from June into October.
bibliographicCitation: James, Charles W. 1956. A Revision of Rhexia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 8 (3): 201-230.

description: Shoots simple or branched, 4-6 dm tall, arising from the bases of previous shoots or from short, cylindrical, non-tuberous roots. Stems glandular-hirsute, becoming woody below, occasionally brown-spongy, the faces flat to convex, essentially equal, with thin, inconspicuous wings at their edges. Leaves narrowly to broadly elliptic with acute bases and apices, the margins serrulate to serrate, ciliate (sometimes glandular), 2-6(-7) cm long, 10-25 mm broad, 3(-5)-nerved, sessile to short-petiolate, the bases sometimes red; upper leaf surfaces with scattered hairs, the lower surfaces usually with few hairs, mostly on the veins. Flowers few to many in much-branched open cymes, the bracts persistent, the upper ones much reduced in the larger inflorescences. Hypanthium (fig. 13) at maturity with scattered glandular hairs, 7-9(-10) mm long, the neck shorter than or nearly equaling the length of the body, not constricted below, gradually expanded above, calyx-lobes deltoid to lanceolate, 1.5-3 mm long, glabrous or with very few glandular hairs. Petals deep rose to purple, spreading or reflexed (?), with glandular hairs on the abaxial surfaces, 8-12 mm long, of a broad, obovate type. Anthers long (5-8 mm in length), declinate, curved to sigmoid, appearing papillose basally under 10 x magnification, dehiscing by a small pore ca. 1/3 the diameter of the anther tip, the appendage filamentous, ca. 1 mm long. Capsule glabrous, globose, with a slightly attenuate apex, ca. 4.5-6.5 mm long and 4-5 mm wide. Seeds (fig. 29) cochleate, ca. 0.5-0.7 (rarely up to 0.8) mm long, with low, rounded, inconspicuous, somewhat longitudinally oriented processes. Flowering from mid-June through early October.
bibliographicCitation: James, Charles W. 1956. A Revision of Rhexia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 8 (3): 201-230.

description: Shoots 2.5-8 dm tall, arising from the bases of previous shoots or from various points along sometimes extensive horizontal-spreading, non-tuberous roots. Stems simple or branched, glandular-hirsute, sometimes woody below, the faces flat to convex, essentially equal, with thin, inconspicuous wings at their edges. Leaves ovate-elliptic, broad- or narrow-elliptic to lanceolate, the margins serrulate to serrate, ciliate, 2-6 cm long, ca. 1-2 cm wide, 3-nerved, sessile (or petiolate), with scattered hairs on both surfaces (fewer below, mostly on the nerves). Flowers few to many in open, branched cymes, the bracts persistent, gradually becoming reduced in size above. Hypanthium (fig. 14) at maturity with scattered glandular hairs, (9-)10-12 mm long and ca. 5-7 mm wide at the base, the neck nearly equaling the length of the body, not constricted below, and gradually if at all expanded above; calyx-lobes deltoid to lanceolate, 2-3 mm long, divergent to spreading, sparsely glandular-hairy. Petals dark rose to purple, spreading, with glandular hairs on the abaxial surface, ca. 1-2 cm long, of a broad, obovate type. Anthers long (6-9 mm in length), declinate, curved to sigmoid, appearing minutely papillose near the base under 10 x magnification, dehiscing by a small pore ca. 1/3 the diameter of the tip of the anther, the appendage filamentous, ca. 0.5-2 mm long. Capsule glabrous, pyriform, (5-)6-8 mm long, 5.7 mm wide. Seeds (fig. 30) cochleate, ca. 0.5-0.7 (rarely up to 0.8) mm long, with longitudinal ridges of thin, conspicuous papillae. Flowering from June into September.
bibliographicCitation: James, Charles W. 1956. A Revision of Rhexia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 8 (3): 201-230.

description: Similar to var. virginica, but more often strict, with stems glabrous or nearly so. Leaves with a greater length-width ratio, typically lanceolate but also ovatelanceolate or ovate, (2-)3-6(-7.5) cm long, 0.5-2(-3) cm wide, the lower surface glabrous except occasionally along the veins. Upper bracts usually conspicuously smaller than the leaves, entire (-serrate), glabrous. Hypanthium (fig. 12) generally smaller (mostly 7-8 mm long), frequently glabrous; calyx-lobes lanceolate, 2-4 mm long, usually ascending, incurved. Abaxial surface of the petals glabrous or with few scattered, glandular hairs. Anthers appearing smooth or very minutely papillose near the base under 10 x magnification, the appendage merely a protuberance, or spur-like to filamentous and up to ca. 0.5 mm long. Capsule globose, somewhat smaller, with a more attenuate apex. Seeds (fig. 28) cochleate, smaller (ca. 0.5-0.7 mm long), verrucose-ridged to thin, short-papillose. Flowering from July through September.
bibliographicCitation: James, Charles W. 1956. A Revision of Rhexia (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 8 (3): 201-230.

description: Frutex epiphyticus ca 2-3 m altus. Lamina 10.5-21.5 x 6-15 cm, elliptica, elliptico-ovata vel elliptico-obovata, apice cuspidata basi acuta vel obtusa, ad maturitatem supra glabra, subtus modice pilis gracilibus ca 1-1.5 mm longis setosa. Flores in quoque nodo superiore 1-2 (3); bracteae liberae elliptico-ovatae vel elliptico-lanceolatae utrinque glabrae, exteriores 17-25 x 12-18 mm, interiores 12-19 x 10-16 mm. Hypanthium (usque ad torum) 8-10 mm longum glabrum; calycis tubus ca 1.5-2 mm longus, lobis late triangularibus vel ovatis. Petala viridia 15-20 x 12-17 mm obovata (apice rotundato). Filamenta 5-6.5 mm longa; thecae 5.5-6.5 x 1.5 mm, poris binis terminalibus; connectivum dorsaliter basi calcari 0.5 mm longo caudato armatum.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, F. 1981. Blakea penduliflora (Melastomataceae): a new green-flowered species from Costa Rica. Brittonia. 32: 508-511.

description: Coarse spreading epiphytic shrub 2-3 m tall. Older cauline internodes glabrate, ±terete to subquadrangular. Distal branchlets, vegetative buds, and juvenile leaves beset with an indument of dense brown subulate trichomes mostly 0.5-1.5 mm long. Mature leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, entire, but often revolute on drying, 10.5-21.5 x 6-15 cm, elliptic to elliptic-ovate or elliptic-obovate, cuspidate apically and acute to obtuse basally, 5-nerved, olive-green and glabrous above, pale brown and moderately covered with ±curved to uncinate, smooth and/or shaggy plumulose subulate trichomes below; petioles 23-50 (60) mm long and 3-4 mm diam. Flowers 6-merous, pendent, solitary, geminate or occasionally borne in clusters of three in the axils of distal branches; pedicels 2.8-5.6 cm long, essentially glabrous but conspicuously lenticellate. Floral bracts ±elliptic but varying to elliptic-ovate and elliptic-lanceolate, entire, green, glabrous, and obtuse to rounded apically; outer bracts connate basally for ±2-3 mm, 17-25 x 12-18 mm; inner bracts free, 12-19 x 10-16 mm. Hypanthia (at anthesis) campanulate, glabrous, 8-10 mm long to the torus and 7-8 mm broad. Calyx lobes persistent on mature hypanthia, broadly triangular to ±ovate, entire and completely glabrous, 4-6 mm long and 4-7 mm wide basally between sinuses. Petals somewhat fleshy, glabrous, imbricate when fully expanded, purplish basally within, otherwise green throughout, obovate and rounded apically, entire but occasionally fringed with a few glandular cilia distally, 15-20 x 12-17 mm. Stamens isomorphic, free; filaments glabrous, ligulate, 5-6.5 x 1.5 mm; anthers 5.5-6.5 mm long, glabrous, dark purple, laterally compressed, ±linear-oblong when viewed dorsally or ventrally but essentially obcalvate in profile view, tipped with 2 ± truncate of somewhat dorsally inclined circular pores; connective thickened dorsally near the point of filament insertion and dilated basally into a short deflexed caudiform appendage. Style straight, glabrous, conspicuously exserted, 17-18 mm long; stigma truncate. Berry 11-15 mm long to the torus and 13-18 mm diam. glabrous, subglobose, spongy and varying from white to pink or deep red at maturity. Seeds beige or brown, clavate to narrowly pyriform, smooth and nitid, mostly 1-1.5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, F. 1981. Blakea penduliflora (Melastomataceae): a new green-flowered species from Costa Rica. Brittonia. 32: 508-511.

description: Shrub 2 m, with smooth hairs; branchlets rotund-quadrangular, as the primary leaf veins beneath rather sparsely strigulose with slender hairs 1-1.5 mm long. Petiole ca 0.6-1 cm long; blade 4-7 (8.5) x 1.5-2.5 (3) cm, lanceate with narrowly acute apex and broadly acute to obtuse base, chartaceous and entire, above sparsely strigose with slender hairs mostly 1-2 mm long and ca 1/3 adnate, below along the secondary veins and venules sparsely strigulose with slender hairs 0.5-1 mm long but glabrous on the surface, 5-nerved with the lateral primaries coalesced 0.3- 0.5 cm at the base and the secondary nerves ca 2 mm apart. Panicle 3-8 cm long and submultiflorous; flowers 5-merous, the pedicels 1-3 mm long, the lanceate bracteoles 1.5-2.5 x 1-1.5 mm. Hypanthium to the torus 4-4.2 mm long, mod- erately lax-strigose with slender eglandular hairs 1-2 mm long; calyx tube 0.3- 0.4 mm long, the lanceate, acute lobes 3-3.6 x 0.8 mm, ciliolate and sporadically sparsely strigulose within apically. Petals white, 8-8.8 x 4-6 mm, obovate with rotund apex, apically eglandular-ciliolate but otherwise glabrous. Stamens glabrous, slightly dimorphic in size; anthers yellow, subulate, with a ventrally inclined pore 0.15 mm diam. Large stamens: filaments 4.1-4.3 mm long; thecae 4.2-4.5 x 0.5 x 0.4 mm, the connective prolonged 1-1. 1 mm, the blunt ventral lobes 0.3- 0.4 x 0.3 mm. Small stamens: filaments 3.5-3.7 mm long; thecae 3.3-3.6 x 0.5 x 0.4 mm, the connective prolonged 0.6-0.7 mm, the blunt ventral lobes 0.3 x 0.25 mm. Style 9 x 0.4 mm, glabrous; ovary hairs 0.3-0.8 mm long, eglandular.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1988. New Melastomataceae from Peru and Bolivia. Brittonia. 40 (1): 7-15.

description: Tree 8 m x 10 cm, not buttressed; young branchlets obtusely sulcate-quadrangular, becoming terete, as the petioles, primary leaf veins beneath, and inflorescences densely rufidulo-furfuraceous with dendritic hairs 0.1 (0.2) mm long; in- terpetiolar lines developed, elevated ca 0.2 mm. Petiole (2) 3-6 cm long; blade (12) 21-27 (33) x (4.5) 7-10 (12) cm, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, the apex gradually 1-2 cm acuminate, the base acute, chartaceous and entire or obscurely undulate- serrulate, above glabrous, below very densely subamorpho-stellulate-puberulous, 5-nerved (including the thin 3-5 mm-inframarginal pair) with the secondary veins 4-6 mm apart and the plane veinlets beneath with areoles 0.5-0.8 mm wide (but obscured by the pubescence). Panicle (22) 25-29 cm long and multiflorous, the pedicels mostly 2-3 mm long and articulate ca 0.5 mm below the hypanthium, the caducous bracteoles 1.5-2 x 0.2 mm; flowers 5-merous and very fragrant. Hypanthium to the torus 4 mm long, densely furfuraceous with stellulate hairs ca 0.05 mm diam; calyx ca 1.2 mm long and closed in bud, dehiscing at anthesis into ovate-oblong lobes ca 1.2 mm wide and with external teeth projecting 0.2- 0.3 mm, deciduous after anthesis; torus within very sparsely glandular-setulose. Petals yellow-green, 2.7-2.8 x 1.6-1.7 mm, obovate with emarginate apex, gla- brous. Stamens slightly dimorphic and glabrous, the subulate thecae with a pore 0.1 mm diam. Large stamens: filaments 3.5 mm long; thecae 4 x 0.6 x 0.6 mm with ventrally inclined pore, the connective at the base ca 0.9 mm thick. Small stamens: filaments 2.8-2.9 mm long; thecae 3.3 x 0.5 x 0.5 mm with dorsally inclined pore, the connective at the base ca 0.6 mm thick. Stigma expanded, 0.6 mm diam; style 7 x 0.4 mm and immersed in the ovary collar 0.2 mm, moderately glandular in the basal 2 mm; ovary 3-locular and ca 1/6 inferior, sparsely glandular apically.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1988. New Melastomataceae from Peru and Bolivia. Brittonia. 40 (1): 7-15.

description: Shrub 1-2 m; branchlets at first slightly quadrangular but later terete, as the petioles and primary leaf veins beneath towards the base densely setose with stipitate-stellate hairs (stalk mostly 2-4 mm long; radii few and 0.3-0.5 mm long). Petiole 0.5-1 (2) cm long; blade 16-30 x 7-11 cm, narrowly ovate to oblong elliptic, the apex gradually acuminate, the base somewhat (ca 0.5 cm) cordate, chartaceous and entire, moderately ciliate with smooth hairs 2-3 mm long, above glabrous, beneath on the secondary and tertiary veins sparsely setulose with stip- itate-stellate hairs 0.5-1 mm long and glabrous on the surface, 5-nerved with the secondary veins ca 5 (7) mm apart and the veinlets beneath slightly elevated- reticulate (areoles 0.2-0.3 mm wide). Panicle 10-11 cm long and submultiflorous, the branches and branchlets rather densely setose with stipitate-stellate hairs 1- 2 (3) mm long; flowers 4-merous, the pedicels 0.1 (0.7) mm long, the setuliform bracteoles 0.5-0.7 mm long and persistent. Hypanthium to the torus 1.5 mm long, glabrous; calyx hyaline and closed in bud, ca 0.5 mm long and 0.6 mm apiculate, dehiscing irregularly at anthesis, with setulose external teeth ca 0.6-0.7  mm long; torus within sparsely glanduliferous. Petals 2 x 1-1.1 mm, oblong- obovate with broadly acute apex, glabrous. Stamens slightly dimorphic in dimensions and glabrous, the filaments 1.4 mm or 1.2 mm long; thecae 1.3-1.4 x 0.3 mm or 1.1-1.2 x 0.3 mm, oblong-subulate and with a dorsally inclined pore 0.1 mm diam; connective obscurely (0.05-0.1 mm) prolonged, at the base ventrally exappendiculate and dorsally with a blunt descending tooth 0.2-0.25 mm long. Stigma not expanded, 0.1 mm diam; style 4.2 x 0.2 mm, glabrous, immersed 0.3 mm in the ovary collar; ovary 3-locular and 1/2 inferior, glabrous, with lobulate apex.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1988. New Melastomataceae from Peru and Bolivia. Brittonia. 40 (1): 7-15.

description: Shrub or small tree 0.5-3 m; branchlets at first slightly compressed but soon terete, as the petioles, primary leaf veins beneath, inflorescences, and hypanthia densely covered with sessile stellulate hairs 0.2-0.3 mm diam. Petiole 4-10 cm long; blade 18-31 x 10-15 cm, elliptic to ovate-elliptic, the apex gradually or through 1-1.5 cm subabruptly acuminate, the base narrowly obtuse to rotund- truncate, chartaceous to subcoriaceous and bluntly serrulate, densely stellulate- ciliolate, above at first moderately stellate-puberulous but soon glabrate, beneath on the secondary and tertiary veins sparsely to moderately stellulate-puberulous and on the surface sparsely and deciduously stellulate-puberulous, 5-nerved (including the 5-7 mm-inframarginal exterior pair) with the secondary veins 6-8 (10) mm apart and the plane venules beneath laxly reticulate (areoles ca 1 mm wide). Panicle 6-8 cm long and multiflorous; flowers 5-merous and sessile, sub- secund on the branchlets, the deciduous lanceate bracteoles 1.5-2 x 0.5 mm. Hypanthium to the torus 3 mm long; calyx tube 0.8 mm long, the oblate interior lobes ca 0.2 mm long and minutely ciliolate, the thick external teeth slightly inframarginal; torus within moderately glandular-ciliolate (0.1 mm). Petals white, 5.2-5.4 x 3.5-3.7 mm, oblong-obovate with the apex rotund or slightly emarginate, obscurely ciliolate, outside pruinose and centrally sparsely stellulate-puberulous. Stamens essentially isomorphic; filaments 4.5 mm long, sparsely to very  sparsely glandular-puberulous (0.05-0.1 mm); thecae 4.1-4.3 x 0.5 x 0.4 mm, subulate, the anther pore 0.15 mm and slightly inclined dorsally, the connective not prolonged but basally slightly elevated and sparsely glandular. Stigma not expanded; style 9.5 x 0.35-0.3 mm, at the base sparsely glandular and immersed in the ovary collar 0.4 mm; ovary 3-locular and ca l/3 inferior, sparsely glandular.

description: Caulis breviter hirsutus, pilis ipsis pubeseentibus; laminae ovatae, acuminatae, vix crenulatae, ciliatae, basi rotundatae vel subcordatae, 5-nlerviae, supra flavo-hirsutae, subtus hirsutae, pilis brevioribus flexuosis; inflorescentia pauciflora pauciramosa, dense hirsuta; flores 5-meri; hypanthium urceolatum, dense strigosuni, pilis asperatis reflexis; sepala subseariosa, ovata, vix erosa, ciliolata, dentibus exterioribus fere adnatis, apice libero sepala excedentibus; petala obovatooblonga; antherae subulatae, connectivo infra thecas brevissime producto; ovarium subsemi-inferum, 5-loculare, summo truneato-conico glabrum; stylus superne angustatus, stigmate capitellato.

description: Shrub. Younger branches slender, hirsute, the hairs slender, pubescent, 1-1.5 mm. long. Petioles stout, up to 3 cm. long, very densely hirsute, the hairs varying from slender, flexuous, 0.6 mm. long to stiff, straight, and 2.5 mm. long. Leaf-blades rather thin, ovate, up to 13 cm. long and 7 cm. wide, abruptly acuminate, obscurely crenulate and conspicuously ciliate, broadly rounded to subcordate at the base, 5-nerved, densely hirsute above with yellowish hairs 0.9-1.3 mm. long, beneath more densely hirsute with slightly shorter hairs. Inflorescence sparsely branched, few-flowered, densely hirsute; flowers 5-merous in clusters of 3, the pedicel less than 1 mm. long and covered by the hypanthial hairs. Hypanthium somewhat urceolate, 4.4 mm. long, densely reverse-strigose with stout, roughened, yellow hairs up to 1 mm. long. Calyx-tube prolonged 0.6 mm., sepals ovate, almost searious, 2.5 mm. long from the torus, slightly erose, inconspicuously ciliate; exterior teeth 4.6 mm. long, broadly triangular below, the free tip flat, linear. Petals narrowly obovate-oblong, 9-10 mm. long. Filaments flat, 4.5 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, 4.5 mm. long, the pore terminal; connective somewhat thickened toward the base and very slightly prolonged below the thecae. Ovary three-fifths inferior, 5-celled, the summit truncate-conic, glabrous; style 11-12 mm. long, gradually tapering; stigma capitellate, 0.8 mm. in diameter.

description: Ramuli primum paulo compressi demum teretes sicut folia inflorescentia hypanthiaque ubique glabri. Petioli 0.7-2.7 cm longi; lamina 8.9-16.5 x 2.4-6.3 cm elliptica vel elliptico-obovata apice obtusa vel rotundata vel acuta basi acuta vel cuneata, coriacea et integra, 3-nervata. Panicula 1 1-15 cm longa multiflora; flores 5-meri, pedicellis (ad anthesim) 2-4 mm longis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 2.5 mm longum; calyx 0.5 mm longus truncatus, dentibus exterioribus non evolutis. Petala 2.5-3 x 1-2 mm elliptico-oblonga. Stamina dimorpha glabra; antherae ad basim in staminibus maioribus distincte biappendiculatae in staminibus minoribus obscure appendiculatae. Ovarium 5-loculare glabrum. Fructus maturus ignotus.
