description:
In overall appearance T. cereifolius most closely resembles T. heterostemon to which it seems most closely allied. The two species share several features such as elliptic-oblong petals, prolonged connectives on the larger stamens, and elliptic to elliptic-obovate leaves. Although T. cereifolius shares several morphological characters with T. heterostemon and is probably derived from it, the latter differs in branchlet shape, petal details, and calyx morphology. The branchlets of T. heterostemon are distinctly quadrate whereas those of T. cereifolius are terete. The petals of T. heterostemon are 5-7 x 3.5 mm, white, and conspicuously papillose adaxially. In T. cereifolius the petals are 2-5 x 1-2 mm, pink, and glabrous or only sparingly papillose on the adaxial surface. Even in fruiting condition these two species can be distinguished by calyx differences. The calyx lobes of T. het- erostemon are broadly rounded to deltoid but often appear apiculate because of the short but conspicuous exterior calyx teeth. In T. cereifolius the calyx is truncate and lacks exterior teeth. In addition, the distal branchlets, lower leaf surfaces, and inflorescences of T. heterostemon are beset with lepidote hairs. In the new species all of these structures are glabrous. The mature leaves and fruiting hypanthia of T. heterostemon also appear to be modally larger than those of T. cereifolius but additional collections of both taxa are needed to confirm the diagnostic value of these latter differences.

Trees to 15 m tall. Older cauline internodes terete and glabrous; distal branchlets somewhat compressed and 2-edged, glabrous throughout. Leaves of a pair essen- tially equal or only slightly unequal in size; petiole 0.7-2.7 cm long; blade coriaceous, 8.9-16.5 cm long, 2.4-6.3 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-obovate, apex obtuse to rounded but varying to acute, base acute to cuneate and briefly decurrent on the petiole, margin entire, 3-nerved abaxially, the outer pair of primary nerves conspicuous and encircling the leaf blade, the transverse secondaries elevated like the other primaries and spaced 0.4-1.2 cm apart at the widest portion of the blade, glabrous above at maturity, inconspicuously punctate but glabrous below. Inflorescence a terminal multiflowered panicle 11-15 cm long; bracteoles paired, early deciduous, elliptic, 0.2 cm long, 0.1 cm wide, margin entire but irregularly fringed with minute deciduous glands, otherwise glabrous throughout. Pedicels 2-4 mm long, glabrous. Hypanthium (at anthesis) campanulate, 2.5 mm long to the torus, glabrous. Calyx tube 0.5 mm long (on young fruiting hypanthium), erect and truncate; calyx teeth obsolete. Petals 5, reportedly pink, 2.5-3 mm long, 1- 2 mm wide, elliptic-oblong, inconspicuously keeled apically and terminated by a small tooth mostly less than 0.25 mm long, glabrous abaxially, glabrous or sparingly and inconspicuously papillose adaxially, the margin minutely and finely ciliolate. Stamens 10, strongly dimorphic with larger stamens inserted on the torus opposite the calyx lobes and smaller ones inserted opposite the petals; filaments somewhat declinate, complanate, and glabrous; anthers yellow and 2-celled. Large stamens: filaments 5 mm long; anthers geniculate at the filament insertion, 3.5- 4 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, subulate, ventrally arcuate and channeled between the thecae, opening by 2 ventrally inclined confluent pores; connective prolonged 2-2.5 mm below the thecae and modified dorso-basally into a ventrally upturned deeply bifid appendage, with each irregularly angled and distally spurred lobe 1.5- 2 mm long and 0.5 mm wide. Small stamens: filaments 5 mm long; anthers 3.5 mm long and 0.5-0.75 mm wide basally, linear-oblong, erect to somewhat incurved with the two thecae of each anther diverging from one another for the distal 2/3 of their length, each theca opening by a dorsally inclined pore; connective thickened and prolonged ca 0.5 mm below the thecae and modified dorso-basally into a deflexed triangular tooth 0.25-0.5 mm long and dorso-ventrally into a sessile bilobulate appendage. Ovary (at anthesis) superior, 5-celled, ovoid and glabrous. Style 4.5 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, glabrous, declinate and slightly incurved distally; stigma subtruncate. Mature capsule and seeds not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, Frank. 1990. A Third Species of Tessmannianthus (Melastomataceae: Merianieae) from Panama. Brittonia. 42 (1): 7-11.

description: Shrub, 1-1.5 (2) m high. Branchlets angled, as the petioles, and inflorescences loosely strigose with smooth, glandular or eglandular hairs, the gland tips caducous. Leaves opposite, petiolate, estipulate, blades ovate, 4.5-6.5 (10) x 1.5- 4 cm, basally obtuse or rounded, apically acute, 5 (9)-nerved, the lateral pairs of primary nerves arising at the blade base, upper surface smooth, lower surface on the midrib and the lateral pairs of primary nerves substrigose with subulate glandular or eglandular hairs, the veinlets finely reticulate, sparsely hirsute with glan- dular or eglandular hairs or lacking hairs, the veinlets and areoles densely papillose; petioles 0.4-1 cm long. Inflorescence a many-flowered, terminal panicle to 18 cm long, flowers hermaphroditic, 4-merous, pedicels 1 mm long, hypanthium nar- rowly campanulate, 2.2 x 2 mm, calyx lobes triangular, 1.1-1.2 mm long. Petals thin, narrowly elliptic, apically acute, pale purple with darker blotches at the base, 3-4.5 x 1.2-2 mm. Stamens slightly dimorphic, filaments 3.4-3.8 or 3-3.6 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca 2 mm long, the connective prolonged below the pollen sacs 0.8-1.0 or 3-3.5 mm long and modified at the base into 2 blunt, ventral lobes. Ovary free from the hypanthium wall, globose, glabrous, 2-locular; style arising abruptly from the ovary apex, filiform, sigmoid; stigma punctiform. Fruit a loculicidal, many-seeded capsule, 2.2 x 2 mm. Seeds 0.8-0.9 mm long, co- chleate, testa shallowly tuberculate to slightly foveolate.

description: Frutex divaricatus ramosus 1 m. altus ubique glaber. Rami graciles einerei, internodiis 2-4 cm. longis. Folia subsessilia solemniter alterna, loco folii seecLndi cicatrice minima notato. Petioli 1-2 mm. longi. Laminae chartaceae oblongo-lanceolatae vel lanceolatae, 7-12 cm. longae, 2-3.5 cm. latae, in cuspidem linearem 10-15 mm. longam acuminatae, integrae, basi rotuLndatae et ad basin imam cordulatae, 5- nerviae; nerviis primariis supra leviter impressis subtus prominulis, secundariis sub angulo 70º divergentibus atque tertiariis supra planis obseuris subtus reticulatis. Infloreseentia cyrnosa ex axillis superior- ibus, ramis fere capillaribus. Flores 4-meri ut videtur longe pedicel- lati sed propter articulationem sub hypanthio vere sessiles. Calycis lobi minutissimi triangulares. Petala staminaque desiderantur. Fructus globosus 3 mm. diam. valde 8-costatus.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: Woody climber; branchlets terete, as the petioles, primary leaf veins beneath, inflorescences, and hypanthia, rather densely puberulous with dibrachiate some- what deciduous hairs. Petiole 0.3-0.5 cm long; blade (2.5) 3-4 x (1.5) 2-3 cm, elliptic to ovate-elliptic, the apex bluntly acute to obtuse, the base rotundate- cordulate, coriaceous and entire, densely appressed-ciliolate with dibrachiate hairs, above caducously puberulous with slender dibrachiate hairs, below along the secondary veins moderately and on the surface sparsely puberulous with rather deciduous dibrachiate hairs, 5-nerved (including the weak inframarginals) with the secondary nerves 2-3 mm apart and the venules obscure. Panicle ca 3-5 cm long and submultiflorous; flowers 5-merous, the pedicels 2-3 mm long, the linear caducous bracteoles 2-3 mm long. Hypanthium to the torus 4 mm long, 10- costulate; calyx tube 1 mm long, the oblate interior lobes ca 1.1 mm long and ciliolate, the setulose external teeth projecting ca 0.3 mm. Petals white, 12-13 x 8.7-9 mm, asymmetrically obovate with the apex rounded and slightly emarginate, glabrous. Stamens dimorphic, glabrous; filaments 7 mm or 7.4-7.5 mm long; anther thecae 7.5 mm or 4 mm long and subulate, the pore 0.1-0.2 mm diam and dorsally inclined, the basal tooth ca 0.4 mm long and obtuse or denticulate, the ascending appendage 2.3-2.5 x 0.3 x 0.3 mm with a blunt or barely emarginate apex. Stigma scarcely expanded; style 8 x 0.5 mm, glabrous; ovary 5-locular, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1987. Notes on Melastomataceae of the Guianas. Brittonia. 39 (2): 159-164.

description: Shrub to 7 dm; branchlets terete, as the petioles, formicaria, and primary leaf veins beneath moderately to rather densely setose with smooth and in small part gland-tipped hairs (1) 2-3 (4.5) mm long. Free petioles 1-1.5 cm long; formicaria 0.8-2 x 0.5-0.8 cm, oblong, about 1/2 immersed in the blade base; blades (6) 14- 20 x (3) 6-11 cm, elliptic, the apex subabruptly acuminate 1-1.5 cm, the base broadly acute to obtuse, chartaceous and slightly ciliate-crenulate, on both surfaces sparsely setose with smooth and in part gland-tipped hairs mostly 1. 5-2 mm long, shortly (ca 0.5 cm) 5 (7)-plinerved with the secondary nerves ca 5-7 mm apart and the venules beneath laxly reticulate (areoles ca 1-1.5 mm wide). Inflorescences solitary in upper leaf axils, ca 12-25-flowered and 1-2 cm long; flowers 5-merous and subsessile (the indistinct pedicels ca 0.5 mm long), the persistent lanceate bracteoles 3-4 x 1-1.5 mm. Hypanthium to the torus 3 mm long, very sparsely setose; calyx tube 0.5 mm long and externally sparsely setose, the rotundate-ovate interior lobes 0.6-0.7 mm long, the subulate and setulose external teeth projecting ca 0.6 mm; torus within moderately glandular-ciliolate (0.2 mm). Petals white, 7.2-7.3 x 3.7-3.8 mm, obovate-oblong and slightly emarginate at the apex, sometimes with a single gland-tipped setula but otherwise glabrous. Stamens essentially isomorphic, glabrous; filaments 2.8-3 mm long; anthers yellow, 2.7-2.8 x 0.7 mm, oblong-subulate and with a terminal or slightly dorsal pore, the connective dorso-basally with an emarginate tooth ca 0.1 mm long. Stigma capitate, 1.5-1.6 mm diam; style 6.4 x 0.5-0.8 mm, glabrous, immersed 0.7 mm in the ovary collar; ovary 3-celled and ca 2/3 inferior, the apex moderately glandular-setulose (0.2-0.25 mm).
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1987. Notes on Melastomataceae of the Guianas. Brittonia. 39 (2): 159-164.

description: Tree 3 m; branchlets terete, along with the primary leaf veins beneath moderately setulose with mostly gland-tipped hairs 0.5-1 mm long (a few hairs 1-2 mm long intermixed). Leaves in each pair dimorphic, the chartaceous blades ciliate with smooth in small part gland-tipped hairs 1.5-2 mm long. Large leaves: petiole 0.4-0.6 cm long; blade (5) 7-11 x 2-3.5 cm, oblong-elliptic with the apex 0.5-1.3 cm acuminate and the base asymmetrically rotundate-cordulate, denticulate with teeth 1-2 mm apart, above sparsely to very sparsely and deciduously setulose with in part gland-tipped hairs 0.3-0.5 mm long, below glabrous on the surface and sparsely setulose with mostly gland-tipped hairs 0.3-0.5 (1) mm long on the secondary and tertiary veins, 5-nerved (including the inframarginal external pair) with secondary veins 2-3 mm apart and the plane venules beneath with areoles 0.7-1 mm wide. Small leaves: petiole 0.05-0.1 cm long; blade 0.4-0.8 x 0.4-0.7 cm, broadly ovate to suborbicular with the apex subabruptly acuminate ca 1 mm and the base cordulate, on both sides very sparsely glandular-setulose, 3-nerved. Panicles few-flowered and solitary from upper leaf axils, 6-9 cm long, sparsely glandular-setulose with hairs 0.2-0.3 mm long; flowers 5-merous, the pedicels mostly 4-6 mm long and articulate 0.5-0.8 mm below the hypanthium, the subpersistent bracteoles 0.5-1 x 0.2-0.4 mm. Hypanthium to the torus ca 2.7 mm long, moderately setulose with gland-tipped hairs ca 0.2 mm long; calyx tube 0.4 mm long, the interior lobes 0.2-0.3 mm long, the narrow external teeth projecting 0.6-0.7 mm. Petals 2.2-2.5 x 1.3 mm, oblong and rotund-retuse at the apex, glabrous. Stamens isomorphic, glabrous; filaments ca 2 mm long; anthers ca 2 x 0.4 x 0.4 mm, oblong-subulate with a ventrally inclined pore 0.15 mm diam, the connective not prolonged but at the base ventrally obscurely bilobulate and dorsally not appendaged. Stigma ca 0.3 mm diam; style ca 5 x 0.25 mm, glabrous; ovary 3-locular (?) and ca 2/3 inferior, glabrous at the apex.

description: Shrub or small tree to ca 5 m tall with gray-brown, smooth to slightly furrowed bark, ultimate branches often arching-pendent. Twigs slightly to moderately quadrangular, usually red-purple, nodose, 1.5-3 mm in diam, smooth or slightly tuberculate, with a ridge encircling each node, and 2 longitudinal grooves, ca 0.4 mm wide, on opposite faces of internode positioned 90º from attachment of leaves of adjacent upper node, pubescent, with brown, unbranched to irregularly branched and matted multicellular hairs, to ca 1 mm long, concentrated in intemodal grooves and on nodal ridges of youngest twigs; internodes (0.6) 1-2.8 (7.2) cm long. Leaves opposite; petiole (2) 6-14 (19) mm long, red-purple, smooth or slightly tuberculate, canaliculate, with hairs similar to those on stem concentrated on edges of groove; blade coriaceous, ovate or elliptic, (1.6) 2.5-7.6 (10.4) cm long, (0.8) 1.5-3.2 (3.9) cm wide, very slightly curved abaxially; apex acuminate or, less commonly, acute, often curved downward; base cuneate or slightly decurrent, rarely acute or obtuse; margin often slightly revolute near base, serrate on distal ca 3/4, teeth with caducous acicular projections to ca 0.3 mm long; venation ac- rodromous, suprabasal, with 2 conspicuous secondary veins joining midvein 0.5- 5 (7) mm above lamina base, 2 less conspicuous intramarginal secondary veins, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins more or less perpendicular to the midvein; adaxial surface with midvein, 2 major secondary veins (very rarely 4 secondary veins), and tertiary veins slightly to strongly impressed, midvein often red-purple in basal portion, the surface glabrous except for minute, conical or cylindrical, unbranched, multicellular glandular hairs, 0.02-0.1 mm long, caducous or often persisting in impressions of midvein and 2 conspicuous secondary veins; abaxial surface with midvein and 2 secondary veins prominently raised, these veins often red-purple, 2 intramarginal secondary veins and tertiary veins less raised, qua- ternary and higher order veins reticulate, flat, the surface sparsely pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem concentrated on veins and in axillary tufts at junction of midvein and 2 major secondary veins, minute glandular hairs, similar to those persisting in vein impressions on adaxial surface, sparsely covering entire abaxial surface. Inflorescences axillary, paniculate cymes borne among leaves and on leafless nodes below them, usually borne singly, but occasionally with two inflo- rescences in the same leaf axil, each 2.2-4 cm long, 0.7-2 cm wide, 1-2 branched, the axes green to tinged heavily with red-purple, bracteate, with opposite, ca- ducous, narrowly triangular bracts to ca 1.6 mm long; peduncle 5-14 mm long. Flowers 4-merous, sessile, each subtended by 2 opposite, narrowly triangular bracteoles, ca 0.4 x 0.2 mm. Hypanthium green or tinged heavily with red-purple, slightly obconical or subglobose, ca 1.7 x 1.7 mm, smooth, sparsely to moderately pubescent with minute glandular hairs similar to those on leaves; portion free from ovary ca 0.6 mm long; proximal non-membranous portion of calyx (bearing external calyx lobes) ca 0.25 mm long. External calyx lobes reduced to 4 triangular teeth, ca 0.2 x 0.2 mm. Internal calyx lobes fused in a calyptra, ca 0.5 mm high, which is ruptured irregularly at anthesis, terminated by a caducous apiculum, ca 0.1 (0.4) mm long. Petals 4, white, obovate, 1.5-1.7 mm long, 1-1.2 mm wide, slightly cupped adaxially, spreading; apex rounded, emarginate, with an asymmetrically placed notch ca 0.5 mm across; margin entire, sometimes slightly involute. Stamens 8, white, inserted above an adaxial erose fringe ca 0.4 mm high, geniculate, folded adaxially in bud; proximal segment (filament) 1.8-2 mm long, flattened dorsally, narrowly ovate, ca 0.5 mm wide, strongly curved; distal segment (anther sacs and elongate connective) obovate, 1.5-1.8 mm long, ca 0.2 mm wide at base, ca 0.4 mm wide at apex, the anther sacs 0.6-0.8 mm long, dehiscing confluently by a single gaping apical pore formed from 2 lateral slits, the bifid outer face of pore shorter than the inner face. Ovary inferior, ca 1.1 x 1.4 mm, the apex prolonged into a collar-like, 8-ribbed appendage, ca 0.5 mm high, which encases the folded distal stamen segments in bud and encircles the style. Style white, cylindrical, ca 3 x 0.3 mm; stigma papillose, ca 0.4 mm across. Berries and seeds not known.

description: Arbor 4.5-10 m. Ramuli teretes, sicut petioli inflorescentiae hypanthiaque dense pilis stellatis induti demum glabrati. Petioli 1-2.1 cm; lamina 11-23 X 4-7.5 cm elliptica vel elliptico-lanceolata apice gradatim acuminata basi acuta vel obtusa, chartacea et integra, supra glabra, subtus densiuscule persistenterque stellato-puberula pilis ca 0.25 mm diam, 3-nervata (pari exteriore debili intramarginali neglecto). Panicula 3-5 cm longa, flores 6-meri, bracteolis 0.5-1.5 mm longis valde caducis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 2 mm altum; calyx in alabastris 0.5 mm altus clausus (apice dentibus exterioribus subuliformibus armato) demum ad torum dehiscens. Petala glabra 2-3 X 1 mm oblonga apice rotundata. Stamina paulo dimorpha glabra; filamenta 3-3.5 mm longa; antherarum thecae 2.5 vel 2 mm oblongo-subulatae, poro paulo ventraliter inclinato (stamina maiora) vel paulo dorsaliter inclinato (stamina minora); connectivum ad basim dorsaliter trilobulato-prolongatum. Stylus 4-5.5 mm basaliter sparse glanduloso-puberulus; stigma non expansum.

description: Tree 4.5-1 0 m tall. Distal branchlets terete, copiously stellate-furfuraceous when young, becoming glabrate with age. Leaf blades chartaceous, entire, 11-23 cm long and 4-7.5 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, acuminate apically and acute to obtuse basally, glabrous above, densely stellate-tomentose below, 3-nerved (excluding the inconspicuous submarginal pair) with an elevated network of secondaries and tertiaries; petioles 1-2.1 cm long and 1-2 mm broad. Inflorescence a multiflowered panicle 3-5 cm long with 1-4 primary branches per node; bracteoles sessile, early-deciduous, linear-lanceolate and ± navicular, 0.5-1.5 mm long and 0.25-0.5 mm wide, stellate-tomentose. Hypanthia (at anthesis) densely stellate furfuraceous, narrowly campanulate to subcylindric, 2 mm long and up to 2 mm broad. Calyx lobes 6, appearing fused or closely connivent in bud, the expanded lobes 0.5 mm long and 1 mm wide at the base between sinuses, acute, obtuse, or varying to broadly deltoid, collectively abscissing as a ring following anthesis; calyx teeth subulate to obconic, 0.5 mm long and widely spreading on flowering hypanthium. Petals 6, glabrous, white, oblong, adaxially concave and strongly deflexed, rounded to bluntly lacerate apically, 2-3 mm long and 1 mm wide. Stamens 12, inconspicuously anisomorphic; filaments alternately 3-3.5 mm and 3 mm long; anthers linear to linear-subulate, alternately 2.5 mm and 2 mm long, the larger with a ventrally inclined pore and connective thickened dorsally and prolonged below thecae into a trilobate or cordiform appendage, the smaller with a truncate to ± dorsally inclined pore and a minute dorsally trilobate connective prolongation. Ovary 1/2 inferior, the distended domelike summit minutely papillate. Style ñ straight to somewhat curved distally, sparsely glandular-puberulent basally, 4-5.5 mm long; stigma truncate. Berry globose, granular-furfuraceous and costulate when dry, reportedly red-brown but turning purple at maturity, 5.5-6 mm long to the torus and 4-5.5 mm in diameter. Seeds ovoid to pyriform, brown, minutely papillate on the convex side, 1.5-2 mm long.

description: Shrub. Stem slender, herbaceous, densely covered when young with slender, yellowish, spreading bristles as much as 15 mm. long. Petioles 1-2 cm. long, setose like the stem. Formicaria epiphyllous, densely setose, about 1 cm. long. Leaf-blades firmn, broadly elliptic, 12-20 cm. long, 7-17 cm. wide, abruptly short-acuminate, nearly entire, rounded at base, 7-pli-nerved, heavily bullate above, each conic projection tipped with a slender seta 3-10 mm. long, deeply foveolate beneath, villous-pubescent with short hairs on the tertiaries, setose oln the primaries and secondaries with hairs up to 8 min. long, underlaid by short villous hairs. Infloreseenee from the -upper axils, many-flowered, compact, the peduncle 3-5 cm. long, densely pubeseent or tomentose with slender hairs 2 mm. long and also densely long-setose; pedicels 2.5 mm. long. Flowers 5-merous. Hypanthium campanulate, 3 mm. long, densely villous with fine crooked hairs 0.4 mm. long. Calyx-tube prolonged 0.7 mm., somewhat flaring, pubescent like the hypanthium and also with 15-20 slelnder setae 8-9 mm. long; sepals ovate, obtuse,. 0.7 mm. long, finely glandular-ciliate; exterior teeth stoutly subulate, 2 mm. long, villous at base and with 3 or 4 long setae. Petals elliptic, 5-6 mm. long. Filaments flat, glabrous, 2 1m1. long; anithers stoutly oblong, 2 mm. long, laterally flattened, opening by a termin-al pore; conneetive simple but elevated into a low dorsal ridge near the base. Ovary wholly inferior, 5-celled, its summnit prolonged into a short glabrous beak; style slender, 6.5 mm. long; stigma capitate.

description: A shrub, the stems very minutely puberulent, densely hirsute when young with stiff, spreading or retrorse hairs up to 10 mm. long. Petioles 2-7 cm. long, pubescent like the stem, the hairs more spreading, up to 15 mm. long. Formicaria epiphyllous, semi-ovoid, 10-15 mm. long, conspicuously 2-lobed, glabrous or sparsely setose. Leaf-blades membranous, elliptic-oblong, often somewhat falcate, up to 20 cm. long by 10 cm. wide, abruptly short-acuminate, nearly entire, finely ciliate, rounded or subcordate at the base, 5-pli-nerved, apparently long-setose above when young, eventually glabrous or with a few persistent setae, finely pubeseent beneath on all the veins and veinlets, setose on the primaries near the base. Infloreseence small, few-flowered, on an elongate slender peduncle. Fruiting hypanthium glabrous, subglobose. Calyx-tube sparsely setose. Ovary 4-celled. Petals and stamens unknown.

description: An epiphytic shrub, the younger stems densely and minutely stellate-furfuraceous, soon glabreseent; internodes 8-10 cm. long. Petioles slender, 1-2 cm. long, furfuraceous like the stein. Leaf-blades thin, broadly ovate, up to 16 cm. long and 12 cm. wide, abruptly short- acuminate, entire, ciliate (cilia 1.5-2.5 mm. apart, 1.5 mm. long), abruptly cuneate at base, 5-inerved, glabrous above except on the base of the primary veins, minutely and sparsely stellate beneath on the veins and veinlets, glabrous on the surface; secondary veins 6-8 mm. apart, diverging nearly at right angles; all veins elevated and con- spicuously reticulate beneath. Infloreseences nearly sessile, trichotomous, 3 cm. long, furfuraceous like the stem; bracts oblong, aristate, about 1 mm. long. Flowers sessile, 5-merous. Hypanthium broadly tubular or slightly urceolate, 3.2 mm. long, obscurely 10-ribbed, stellate-furfuraceous; torus minutely glandular-pubeseent. Calyx-tube not developed; sepals triangular from acute sinuses, 0.7 mm. long, subacute; exterior teeth half adnate, triangular below, stoutly subulate above, equaling the sepals. Petals and stamens not seen. Ovary wholly inferior, 5-celled, its summit minutely pubescent; style 3 mm. long, somewhat thickened in the middle; stigma capitellate.

description: Arbor 8 m. alta, ramis patulis. Ramuli crassi, rotunde quadrangulares, tenuiter furfuracei mox glabreseentes. Petioli graciles, 30-55 mm. longi, tenuiter furfuracei. Laminae in quoque jugo aequales, tenues, late ovata, usque 19 cm. longae 15 cm. latae, abrupte breviterque acuminatae, sinuato-denticulatae, basi late rotundatae, 5- nerviae jugo marginali neglecto, subtus ad venas tenuissime furfura- ceae, ceterum utrinque glabrae nitentes; venae secundariae 3-6 mm. dissitae, sub angulo 70-90? divergentes. Flores 6-meri, in fasciculis circa 7-floris ad basin foliorum inferiorum vel ad nodos defoliatos superiores. Pedicelli crassi, 3-5 mm. longi, sparse furfuracei. Brac- teae 4 liberae, exteriores late ovatae, 12 mm. longae, 7 mm. latae, abrupte acuminatae, interiores late ellipticae, 8.5 mm. longae, 6.7 mm. latae, apice rotundatae. Hypanthium campanulatum carnosum, ad torum 5.5 mm. longum, sparse furfuraceum. Calycis tubus circa 3 mm. longus, lobi breviter triangulares, 1-1.3 mm. longi, dentibus ex- terioribus minutis apicalibus tuberculiformibus. Petala rosea oblonga, paulo inaequilatera, 15 mm. longa, 8 mm. lata. Stamina isomorpha. Filamenta complanata uninervia, 13 mm. longa. Antherae subulatae, 11 mm. longae, poro dorso-terminali dehiseentes, connectivo basin versus gradatim inerassato, in calear basalem crassum teretem obtusum 1.2 mm. longum producto. Ovarium liberum, summo corona dentata styli basin eingente ornatum. Stylus 13 mm. longus, stigmate capitato.

description: C. puberulae Cogn. et C. extinctoriae (Bonpl.) D. Don affinis, sed alabastris apice longe apiculatis. Rami obtusissime quadrangulati prirnul dense rufo-furfuracei (pilis stellatis) demum glabrati. Petioli 7-12 mm longi, cum laminae venis primariis subtus et alabastris densiuscule stellato-furfuracei; lamina 5-10.5 (acumine non incluso) X 2-4.5 cm elliptica apice longiuscule (ca. 1 cm) caudato-acuminata basi acuta, brevissime 5-plinervia (nervis interioribus 1-3 mm supra basim insertis) nervis primariis supra leviter insculptis subtus leviter elevatis secundariis supra glabra, subtus in venulis primum sparse stellato-furfuracea demumi reticulatis, ad marginem obscure remoteque denticulata (ut videtur integra), supra glabra, subtus in venulis primum sparse stellato-furfuracea demum glabrata. Panicula 4-6 cm alta cum pedunculo pedicellis bracteolisque dense stellato-furfuracea. Pedicelli 4-7 mm longi plerumque in medio uninodosi, bracteolis 3-5 mm longis linearibus mox eaducis; flores 6-meri. Alabastra matura longe (2.8 mm) apiculata ad torum bene constrieta supra (apiculo excluso) 6 mm longa diam. max. 5.2 mm; hypanthium (ad torum) 5.5 mm longum, diam. max. 4.7 mm, diam. ad torum 4.3 mm. Petala 8-9 X 6-7 mm obovata acuta apicem versus irregulariter denticulata. Stamina 20-21, isomorphica; filamenta 4.5 mm longa; theeae 3.5 mm longae, connectivo ad basim non protracto. Stylus 7.4 X 0.5-1 mm apicem versus expansus; stigma capitellatum 0.7 X 1.4 mm; ovarium glabrum 6-loculare, ad apicem in collum 0.7 mm altum circum stylum protractum.

description: Shrub or small tree to ca 5 m tall. Young twigs not ridged, +/- elliptic, 4-9.5 (1 1) mm wide, sulcate, becoming terete with age, the indumentum usually dense, +/- glabrescent; internodes 1-7.5 (9) cm long. Leaves with petiole 1-5 cm long, the indumentum dense; blade ovate to occasionally elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 8- 26 x 2.7-12 (14.7) cm, flat, coriaceous, the apex slightly to clearly acuminate, the base (acute) obtuse to slightly cordate, the margin usually clearly and irregularly serrate, the largest teeth (0.3) 0.4-3 mm long, becoming entire near base (ca 3- 33% of margin without teeth), plane; venation acrodromous, slightly suprabasal, with midvein and 4 or 6 secondary veins, with 2 conspicuous secondary veins placed ca 3-20 (27) mm in from margin and 4 or less commonly 2 inconspicuous secondary veins closer to margin, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented subperpendicular to midvein, the tertiary veins joined by percurrent-orthogonal quaternary veins; adaxial surface dark green, the indumentum dense when young, quickly glabrescent, the midvein and major secondary veins impressed, minor secondary, tertiary veins (and higher order veins) slightly impressed; abaxial surface ferrugineous, very light golden to dark reddish-brown, densely (moderately) covered with multicellular, stellate hairs to ca 0.8 mm across, the midvein and major secondary veins prominently raised, minor secondary, tertiary, and quaternary veins raised, the higher order veins slightly to not at all raised. Inflores- cences terminal, many-flowered, open, paniculate cymes of usually 3 to 5 major branch-pairs, ca 3.5-15 cm long, 3.5-12 cm across; lowermost inflorescence branches with basal segment 1-4.7 cm long, distal internodes increasingly shorter, all with dense pale to deeply ferrugineous indumentum; peduncle 3-10.5 cm long; the inflorescence branches associated with an early caducous, broadly elliptic to narrowly ovate, ca 6-15 mm long bract; flowers in dichasia, each flower associated with a pair of caducous, narrowly elliptic to ovate or linear bracteoles, ca 2-6 x 0.5-1 mm, the indumentum dense, the apices acute to obtuse. Flowers with pedicel 0.4-1.3 mm long. Hypanthium +/- cylindrical, free portion ca 1.7-2.2 mm long, the outer surface with moderate to dense ferrugineous indumentum, the inner surface glabrous and 1 0-ridged, the apices of the ridges forming minute projections ca 0.1 mm long. External calyx lobes 0.4-3 x 0.9-1.5 mm, broadly to narrowly triangular with acute to acuminate apex, dense ferrugineous indumentum; internal calyx lobes ca 1.2-3.3 x 2.3-3 mm, broadly ovate-triangular, the apex rounded (obtuse to acute), the margin minutely erose, with sparse to dense ferrugineous indumentum on both surfaces; calyx tube 0.3-0.8 mm long. Petals broadly ovate to elliptic or obovate, 3.8-6.3 x 2.8-4.8 mm, white. Stamens geniculate; proximal segment (filament) 1.3-2.9 mm long; distal segment (anther and connective) 2.6- 4.2 mm long, with minute dorsal projection, the anther ca 1.8-3.2 mm long, with fertile portion of anther sacs ca 1.6-2.8 mm long, the connective extending 1.6- 2.8 mm beyond the base of anther sacs. Ovary 5-loculate, ? half-inferior, short- ovoid, 2.2-3.4 x 2.9-4.5 mm, glabrous and 10-ridged, with minute apical pro- jections, to ca 0.4 mm long, encircling base of style; style 3.3-4.8 mm long; stigma truncate. Mature berries globose, ca 8-1 1 mm long and wide, blue (red when immature), moderately to sparsely covered with globular-stellate hairs. Seeds angular-obovoid, 0.5-0.8 mm long.

description: Frutex, caulibus superioribus 4-suleatis, cum petiolis et inflores- centia dense breviterqcue stellato-tomentosis et longius glanduloso- setosis; lamninae ovatae, acuminatae, denticulatae, basi cordulatae, 7-9- nerviae, supra glanduloso-setosae, utrinque tenuiter stellatae; panicula divaricata trichotoma; flores 7-meri subsessiles; hypanthium subglo- bosumi superne constrictum, stellatum et glanduloso-hirsutum; sepala obloinga fere 3 mm. longa, erosa, ciliata, dentibus exterioribus subulatis sepala aequantibus; petala anguste obovata-oblonga; antherae lineares, connectivo basi brevissime 4-lobato.

description: Shrub. Stems 4-suleate, roundly 4-angled, densely stellate-tomentose, glandular-hirsute, the hairs 0.5-3 mm. long. Petioles slender, 3-6 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Blades thin, ovate, 8-15 cm. long, 5-9 cm. wide, acuminate, conspicuously denticulate, subcordate at the base, 7-9-nerved, above finely stellate and (probably glandular-) setose, the hairs 0.6-1.3 mm. long, beneath finely stellate, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm. long. Infloreseence trichotomous, the divaricate branches about 8 cm. long, pubescent like the stem; bracts linear-subulate, 1 mm. long. Flowers 7-merous, subsessile. Hypanthiuln subglobose, constricted above, 4-4.5 mm. long, densely stellate-tomentose, densely glandular-hirsute with stout hairs up to 1.4 mm. long; toral scales none. Calyx-tube 0.6 mm. long, pubescent like the hypanthium; sepals oblong, 2.8 mm. long from the torus, rounded at the summit, finely ciliate and erose, the free tip 0.5 mm. long; exterior teeth forming a narrowly trialigular ridge below, the free tip subulate, scarcely divergent, glandular-setose, just equaling the sepal. Petals narrowly obovate-oblong, 8 mm. long. Filaments slender, 3.6 mm. long; anthers linear, 3.2 mm. long, the pore terminal; connective prolonged 0.4 mm. below the thecae into 2 lateral and 2 dorsal lobes. Ovary wholly inferior, its surface apparently glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Shrub 3 m; branchlets essentially terete, as the petioles, primary leaf veins beneath, inflorescences, and hypanthia moderately puberulous with stellulate dendritic hairs 0.05-0.1 mm diam. Petiole (1) 1.5-2 cm long; blade (8) 9-11.5 x (1.3) 2-3.5 cm, elliptic to lance-elliptic, the apex rather gradually caudate-acuminate 2-3 cm, the base acute, chartaceous and entire, eciliate, above glabrous, below on the veins and veinlets moderately resinous-granulose but glabrous on the surface, 3-nerved (excluding the weak inframarginals) with the secondary veins ca 3 mm apart and the plane veinlets beneath with areoles 0.5-0.7 mm wide. Panicle 3-5 cm long and few-flowered; flowers 6-merous, the pedicels 4-5 mm long and articulate ca 0.5 mm below the hypanthium, the caducous bracteoles not seen. Hypanthium to the torus 3.8 mm long, densely resinous-granulose; calyx 1.1-1.2 mm long, obscurely (0.05-0.1 mm) 6-undulate, within (except for a few glands) glabrous. Petals white, 9-9.7 x 2.6-2.8 mm, outside densely resinous- granulose, obovate-oblong with a rounded slightly emarginate apex. Stamens di- morphic, the filaments glabrous, the subulate yellow anthers in both whorls with a dorsally inclined pore 0.1 mm diam. Large stamens: filaments 7 mm long; thecae 6 x 0. 5 mm, the connective at the base ca 1 mm wide and the blunt ventral lobes each with 1 (2) glands 0.15 mm diam. Small stamens: filaments 5 mm long; thecae 4.5 x 0.5 mm, the connective at the base eglandular. Stigma not expanded; style 11 x 0.7-0.3 mm, glabrous, immersed ca 0.2 mm in the ovary collar; ovary (3) 4-locular and ca 1/4 inferior, the apex slightly granulose.

description: Sect. Chaenopleura. M. corymbhiformri Cogn. infloreseentiae forina similis, sed folia ramisque modice glanduloso-hispidis. Rami subteretes eum petiolis pedunculoque modice hispidi pilis patentibus gracilibus subflexuosis 1-4 mm longis pro parte glanduliferis, ad foliorum nodos cum linea stipulacea manicata armati. Petioli 3-5 cm; lamina tenuis 8-12 X 6-8.5 cm late elliptico-ovata apice breviter (5-10 mm) acuminata basi leviter (2-4 mm) cordata ad marginem leviter irregulariterque undulata 7- vel sub-9-nervia nervis secundariis tertiariisque leviter reticulatis, supra modice strigosis pilis laxis ca. 2-3/mm2 ca. 1 mm longis, subtus in nervis nervulisque modice setulosa pilis subappressis 1-2 mm longis superficie glabra. Panicula corymbiformis, pedunculo 6.5 cm longo, ramulis sparse glanduloso-setosis; pedicelli plerumque uninodosi sub articulo 5-9 mm, supra ca. 1 mm, glabri vel sparsissime glanduloso-setulosi; flores 5-meri ovarii apice excepto glabri. Hypanthium 4.7 (ad torum) X 4.2 mm hemisphaericum; calyeis tubus 0.3 mm altus, lobis vix perspicuis 0.5 X 3 mm late rotundatis extus inconspicue dentatis dente ca. 0.2 mm alto. Petala 5.3 X 5.3 mm suborbicularia anguste retusa. Stamina ut videtur isomorphica; filamenta 3.8 mm; thecae 1.7 mm longae ventraliter 1.3 mm rimosae dorsaliter 0.7 mm rimosae, connectivo sub thecis ventraliter 0.7 mm prolongato vix bilobulato dorsaliter subealearato. Stylus 5.5 X 0.5 mm; stioma truneatum; ovarium 5-loculare apice in collum 0.7 mm altum coronatum, collo apice sparse glanduloso-setuloso.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1957. Certamen Melastomataceis IV. Brittonia. 9: 101-109.

description: Shrub 3 meters high. Stems slender, 4-costate, apparently glabrous, actually minutely punetate-furfuraceous with hairs about 0.04 mm. long. Petioles slender, 1-3.5 cm. long, punctate like the stem. Leaf-blades thin, ovate-oblong to broadly elliptic, up to 15 cm. long and 10 cm. wide, acuminate, entire, minutely spinulose-ciliate with ineurved teeth, rounded or obseurely subcordate at the base, 5-nerved, minutely stellate-puberulent on both sides when young, soon glabrescent, except along the larger veins beneath. Inflorescences arising from leafless nodes, freely and divaricately trichotomous from near the base, 3-5 cm. wide and long, the very slender branches minutely furfuraceous; bracts subulate, 0.5 mm. long, setose-tipped; pedicels 0.3 mm. long. Hypanthium globose, 1.7 mm. long, microscopically furfuraceous. Calyx-tube about 0.3 mm. long, slightly spreading; sepals depressed-triangular, 0.6 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth thick, broadly triangular, divergent, about as long as the sepals. Petals oblong, 1.7 mm. long, broadest at the base, minutely ciliate at the apex. Filaments slender, 1.5 mm. long, geniculate near the summit; anthers obovoid, 1 mm. long; connective simple. Ovary inferior, its summit glabrous; style 4 mm. long; stigma punctiform.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Sect. Sagraea: Frutex 3 m. altus. Rami superiores brunnei leviter 4-angulati glabri, ad nodos paulo inerassati, internodiis 3-5 cm. longis. Petioli graciles glabri 1-3.5 cm. longi. Laminae membranaceae, ovato- oblongae, late ellipticae, vel obovato-oblongae, usque ad 15 cm. longae  abrupte acuininatae, integrae, basi rotundatae vel levissime cordulatae, 5-nerviae, supra glabrae, subtus juventute leviter furfuraceae mox glabrae. Cymae infra folia orientes, rarnosae, 3-5 cm. longae, multiflorae, ramis fere capillaribus, flores versus minutissime furfuraceis. Flores 4-meri sessiles, terminales pseudopedicellati. Hypanthium glo- bosum glabrum, 1.7 mm. longum. Calycis limbus leviter patulus, sepalis late triangularibus, 0.3 mm. longis, dentibus exterioribus crassis patulis triangularibus sepala fere aequantibus. Petala oblonga albida 1.7 mm. longa, apice rotundata parce ciliata. Stamina 8 isomorpha. Filamenta glabra graciles 1.5 mm. longa, prope apicem geniculata. Anitherae crassae oblongae 2-loculares obtusae, connectivo simplici. Ovarium inferum 2-loculare glabrum. Stylus teres 4 mm. longus, stignmate punctiformi.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: A low, freely branched shrub. Stems thinly but closely stellate-puberulent. Petioles stout, 2-8 mm. long, pubescent like the stem. Larger leaf-blades thin, oblong to obovate-oblong, up to 16 cm. long and 7 cm. wide, acute or subacuminate, entire, obtuse at the base, 3-plinerved with an additional pair of submarginal veins, very sparsely pubescent with stellate hairs or glabrous above, beneath thinly pubes- cent on the larger veins, glabrous oni the surface, the tertiary veins conspicuously and coarsely reticulate. Smaller leaf-blades broadly elliptic to subrotund, up to 2.5 cm. long by 2 cm. wide. Inflorescence racemiform, 6 cm. long, of which half is peduncle.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: Sect. Glaziophytutmi,: Frutex gracilis 1-2 m. altus. Rami superiores paulo complanati glabri, internodiis 2-3 cm. longis. Petioli crassi circa 1 cm. longi, dorso glabri supra dense brunneo-pilosi. Laminae membranaceae opacae anguste oblongo-ellipticae, usque 20 cm. longae 6.5 cm. latae, longe acuminatae, integrae, tenuissime ciliatae, basi acutae, utrinque glabrae, insigniter 5-pli-nerviae; venis supra planis subtus leviter prominentibus arete reticulatis. Paniculae axillares glabrae 2-3 cm. longae, ramis capillaribus, bracteolis 0.5-2 mm. longis subulatis. Flores 5-meri sessiles sed ut videtur pedicellati. Hypanthium tubulosum basi inerassatumn, 3-3.5 mm. longum sparse pilosum, pilis patulis glandulosis 1 min. longis. Calycis tubus erectus, lobi late rotundati 0.2 mm. longi, margine glandulis 2-3 stipitatis coronati. Petala erecta oblonga, 2.1 mm. longa 0.9 mm. lata, apice obtuso, dorso dente exteriore patulo subulato 1.6 mm. longo ornata. Stamina iso- morpha. Filamenta glabra 1.6 mm. longa. Antherae subulatae 2.4 nm. longae, thecis basi breviter productis, connectivo simplici. Ovarium inferum. Stylus glaber 5.5 mm. longus, stigmate truneato.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: Herba perennis scandens 3.5 m. alta (teste schedula). Rami jluni- ores obscure 4-angulati atque petioli pedunculi bracteae et calyces densissime glanduloso-pubeseentes, pilis circa 1 mm. longis; internodiis 2-3 cm. longis. Laminae firmulae late ellipticae, maxima qua adest 15 cm. longa 10.5 cm. lata, superne abrupte rotundatae in cuspidem triangularem 1 em. longam, levissime denticulatae et glandulosociliatae, basi rotundatae, 5-nerviae, jugo exteriore submarginali, supra sparse glanduloso-pubescentes, subtus densiore praesertim ad venas primarias; venae secondariae sub angulis fere rectis divergentibus. Pedunculi solitarii in axillis supremis, 3-4 cm. longi. Bracteae liberae, ser. ext. rotundae, 10 mm. longae 11 mm. latae 3-nerviae, apice abrupte ro- tundatae in cuspidem 3.5 mm. longam, ser. int. late ovatae, 11 mm. longae 9 mm. latae. Hypanthium hemisphaericum 5 mm. longum, in- ferne glabrum, ad torum sparse glanduloso-pubeseens. Calycis tubus 2 mm. longus, lobi subpatuli e sinubus rotundis, oblongi, 5 mm. longi obtusi. Petala obovata glabra 13 mm. longa 9 mm. lata. Filamenta gracilia glabra 4.5 mm. longa; antherae valde complanatae, ellipsoideae vel obovatae, 5 mm. longae, connectivo dorso inerassato basi truneato, calearem brevem triangularem simulante. Ovarium inferum, ad summum planum appendiculis carnosis subulatis erectis numerosis (ca. 30) ornatum. Stylus rectus glaber 13 mm. longus, stigmate punctiformi.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: Liana lignosa glabra. Rami superiores graciles cinerei subteretes, internodiis 10-15 cm. longis. Petioli graciles 1-2 cm. longi, basi lineatim connati. Laminae chartaceae ellipticae, usque ad 115 mm. longae 56 mm. latae, apice abrupte angustatae in cuspidem triangularem 1 cm. longam, margine cartilaginea levissime sinuatae, inferne rotundatae ad basin late acutam, 5-nerviae. Flores 6-meri in quaque axilla 3, pedi- cellis supremis 1 cm. longis, inferioribus gradatim brevioribus. Bracteae exteriores late ovatae, fere ad basin liberae, 3 mm. longae, minute cuspidatae, interiores paulo breviores latissime rotundae et fere truncatae. Hypanthium poculiforme 3.3 mm. longum. Calyx 2 mm. longus, lobis brevissimis triangularibus apice tubereulatis. Petala alba jam immatura. Antherae (an maturae?) subulatae 3 mm. longae, connectivo non appendiculato. Ovarium liberum summo rotundatum.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1937. Some New or Noteworthy Melastomes. Brittonia. 2 (4): 319-327.

description: Suffrutex diffusus ad 1.5 m altus; rami dense vel modice strigosi, 2-3 m longi, trichomatibus omnino ebarbellatis. Folii lamina strigosa, elliptica vel elliptico-ovata vel elliptico-lanceolata, basi late acuta vel rotundata, apice acuta, (9-)14-35(-41) mm longa et (4-)6-14(-17) mm lata, plerumque 3-plinervata, aliquando 5-nervata, pare interiore supra basin divergente, pare exteriore inconspicuo, petiolo (2.5-)4- 9(-12) mm longo. Inflorescentiae terminales et axillares, dichasiales, bracteis ovatis vel ellipticis, acutis, (2-)4-10(-15) mm longis et 2-6 mm latis, petiolis 1-2 mm longis praeditis. Hypanthium campanulatum vel obconicum, strigosum, trichomatibus ebarbellatis et eglandulosis. Calycis lobi lanceolati, 6-10 mm longi et 2-3 mm lati, persistentes. Petala alba vel subrosea, obovata, 15-19 mm longa et 13-15 mm lata. Stamina dimorphica, glabra, staminum maiorum filamentis 6-8 mm longis, thecis 6-8 mm longis et 0.7-1.0 mm latis, appendicibus dorsalibus 4-6 mm longis et 0.5- 1.0 mm latis, staminum minorum filamentis 9-11 mm longis, thecis 3.5-5 mm longis et 0.5-1.0 mm latis, appendicibus dorsalibus 3-4 mm longis et 0.2-0.8 mm latis. Stigma punctiforme; stylus glaber, (6.5-)7-8 mm longus; ovarium apice setosum. Capsula urceolata, 6-8 mm longa et 4-6 mm lata. Semina plerumque 0.5 mm longa, atrobrunnea, nitida, cochleata.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, Jr., F. 1974. Monochaetum Talamancense (Melastomataceae): A New Species Endemic to Costa Rica. Brittonia. 26 (1): 70-73.

description: A K. tetramera foliis distincte serratis plerumque latioribus floribus 5-meris paulo maioribus differt. Ramuli teretes primum sicut petioli foliorum venae primariae subtus inflorescentiaque modice appresso-setosi, pilis ca. 2-3(-4) mm longis laevibus gracilibus p.p. inconspicue caduceque glanduliferis. Petioli 0.7-1.4 cm longi; lamina (9-)10-17 X (5-)6-9 cm elliptica apice breviter gradatimque acuminato basi late acuta vel obtusa, membranacea et distincte ciliato-serrata (dentibus ca. 1 mm altis), supra primum sparse strigosa pilis gracilibus 1-3 mm longis tarde plusminusve glabrata, subtus sparse appresso-setosa pills gracilibus plerumque ca. 2 mm longis, breviter (0.5-1 cm)5(-7)- plinervata nervis secundariis ca. 5 mm inter se distantibus nervulis subtus planis areolis ca. 1 mm latis. Inflorescentia 1-2 cm longa (pedunculo 0.5-1 cm longo incluso) (1-)3-flora; flores 5-meri, pedicellis 7-10 mm longis circum medium bibracteolatis, bracteolis 5-6 X 1-2 mm subpersistentibus. Hypanthium (ad torum) 8 mm longum teres dense incurvo-setosum pilis gracilibus laevibus ca. 3-4 mm longis inconspicue caduceque glanduliferis; calycis tubus 2 mm altus, lobis interioribus ca. 3 mm longis apice per 1.5 mm paulo acuminato, dentibus exterioribus 5-7 mm eminentibus setulosis ca. 0.4 mm latis; torus intus glaber. Petala 7.6-8.3 X 6-7 mm et ca. 1-1.2 mm apiculata oblongo- ovata pilis extus secus costam 1.5-2 mm longis. Stamina maiora: filamenta 8.3 mm longa; anther- arum thecae 9 X 0.8 mm, poro 0.2-0.3 mm diam.; connectivi appendices ventrales 2.4-2.6 X 0.2-0.3 X 0.4-0.9 mm apice vix emarginato. Stamina minora: filamenta 6.2 mm longa; antherarum thecae 5 X 0.8 mm, poro 0.2 mm diam.; connectivi appendices ventrales 0.8-0.9 X 0.2 mm hebetes. Stigma 1.5 mm diam., 1 mm altum; stylus 8.5-9.5 X 0.8 mm; ovarium 5-loculare apice libero 2 mm alto pilis coroniferis 2.5 mm longis.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1976. Endemic Melastomataceae of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia. Brittonia. 28: 138-143.

description: Plants glabrous; petioles 0.3-1.3 mm long; blades (23-) 36-150 times as long as the petiole, (1.6-) 2-3.7 times as long as wide; true pedicels 0.7-2.0 mm long; free part of calyx lobes 0.7-1.3 mm long; calyx length from stamen attachment 1.5-2.1 mm; petals 3.2-5.9 mm long, 1.8-4.1 mm wide, 1.1-2.4 times as long as wide; anther sporangia 1.1-1.7 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1971. Geographic Variation in a Widespread Neotropical Species, Mouriri Myrtilloides (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 23 (4): 413-424.

description: Sect. Cremnanium. M. rudi Cogni. & Gleason ex Gleason affilnis, sed cum floribus minoribus, pubescentia venularum foliorum subtus minus distineta, folia proportionaliter angustioribus. Rami juveniles obscure quadralngulati fusei dense vel densiuscule brunneofurfuracei inflorescentiam versus et in petiolis glabriores. Petioli 2-5 mm; lamina tenuiter coriacea 1.5-4 X 1-2 cm (in ramis sterilibus ad 5 X 3 cm) elliptica vel obovato-elliptica apice acuta vel brevissime hebeti-acuminata basi aeuta, marginibus apicem versus serrulatis i.s. plerumque reeurvis, trinervia nervis primariis supra conspicue impressis secundariis tertiariisque reticulatis vix conspicuis, supra glabra, subtus in nervis sparse et persistenter furfuracea. Flores glabri 5-meri breviter (0.4-0.9 mi) pedicellati, bracteolis lillearibus ad 1 mm longis valde eaducis. Hypanthium 1.3-1.4 mm longum (ad torumm); calycis tubus 0.3 mm altus, lobis interioribus 0.4 mm altis rotundatis, dente exteriore acuto lobum interiorem aequante. Petala 1.3-1.5 X 1.3-1.4 mm late obovata apice retusa. Stamina vix dimorphica, antheris quadrilocularibus; filamenta 1.2-1.7 mm; thecae 0.6-0.9 mm late 4-porosae, connectivo sub thecis in dente hebeti dorsali et dentibus duobus ventralibus 0.2-0.3 mm prolongato. Stylus 2.3-2.8 X 0.25-0.35 mm; stigma paulo inerassatum 0.4-0.5 mm diam.; ovarium 3-loculare glabrum apice conicum cono 1 mm alto; fructus ca. 2.5 mm diam.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1957. Certamen Melastomataceis IV. Brittonia. 9: 101-109.

description: Herba erecta 0.5-2 m alta; ramuli sulcato-quadrangulati sicut pedicelli inflorescentiaque sparse pilis glanduliferis ca 1-2 mm longis demum glabrati. Petioli 1.3- 4 mm longi; laminae 4-9.3 x 2-4.8 cm ovatae vel ovato-lanceolatae apice acutae vel gradatim acuminatae basi rotundatae vel subcordatae, supra glabrae vel pilis glandulosis, sparse strigulosae, subtus glabrae vel sparse glanduloso-setulosae, 5-7-nervatae. Inflo- rescentia 10-22 cm longa multiflora; flores 4-meri. Hypanthium (ad torum) 4-5 mm longum; calycis lobi 1.5 x 1.5-2.5 mm. Petala 8-16 x 6-13 mm obovata. Sta- mina dimorpha glabra, thecis subulatis, poro ventral- iter inclinato. Stamina maiora: thecae 2.5-3 mm longae; connectivum 4-6 mm prolongatum, appendice ventrali 2-2.5 mm. Stamina minora: thecae 2-3 mm longae; connectivum non prolongatum vel 0.25 mm prolongatum, appendice ventrali 0.5-0.75 mm. Ovarium 4-loculare; semina 0.75 mm longa. Chromosomatum numerus: n = 15.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, Frank. 1994. Arthrostemma primaevum (Melastomataceae): A new species endemic to southeastern Mexico. Brittonia. 46 (1): 75-80.

description: Erect or somewhat arching perennial herb 0.5-2 m tall. Uppermost branchlets succulent, quadrangular, the angles conspicuous ly carinate to narrowly winged, glabrous or sparsely beset with spreading glandular trichomes 1-2 mm long, the nodes caducously setose and forming prominent interpetiolar ridges on older branches. Leaves of a pair somewhat unequal in size; petioles 1.3-4 mm long, glabrous or with a few spreading glandular trichomes at or near the laminar junction; blade chartaceous, ciliolate-ser- rulate, 4-9.3 cm long, 2-4.8 cm wide, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, apex acute to long-acuminate, base rounded to subcordate, 5-7- nerved, the adaxial surface essentially glabrous or sparsely covered with appressed or antrorsely spreading glandular trichomes, the abaxial surface glabrous or sparsely glandularsetose. Inflorescence a laxly branched compound cyme 10-22 cm long; bracts and bracteoles 1-4 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, sessile, tardily deciduous, nar- rowly triangular to linear-oblong, glabrous, entire, sparingly fringed with spreading glandular trichomes. Pedicels 2-3 mm long at anthesis, lengthening to as much as 6 mm on the infructescence. Hypanthium (at an- thesis) campanulate, 4-5 mm long to the torus, glabrous throughout. Calyx tube 0- 0.25 mm long upward from the torus, the adaxial toral rim discontinuously ringed with a minute glandular puberulence, calyx lobes (fruiting hypanthium) antrorsely spreading, broadly deltoid, entire, 1.5 mm long and 1.5-2.5 mm wide basally between sinuses, each lobe typically beset with an apical or subapical glandular trichome. Petals pink, glabrous, obovate, entire, obliquely apiculate, 8-16 mm long, 6-11(-13) mm wide. Stamens markedly dimorphic, differing in size and form, anther thecae glabrous, linear-oblong, the ventrally inclined pore bordered dorsally by a hoodlike distension of the connective especially evident in the smaller set of anthers. Larger (antesepalous) stamens: filaments glabrous, 3-5 mm long, thecae pink or lavender, 2.5-3 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, +/- erect to ascending; connective prolonged 4-6 mm below the thecae, modified ventrally at the filament insertion into a narrowly clavate, yellow appendage 2-2.5 mm long, either simple dorso-basally or prolonged into a deflexed toothlike appendage to 0.75 mm long. Smaller (antepetalous) stamens: filaments glabrous, 3.5-5 mm long, thecae yellow, 2-3 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, erect and incurved; connective not prolonged below the thecae or prolonged less than 0.25 mm, modified ventrally into a simple erect triangular or oblong com pressed spur 0.5-0.75 mm long and dorsobasally into an inconspicuous lobule or spur 0.25 mm long or less in length. Ovary (at anthesis) elliptic and glabrous. Style 5-6 mm long, erect but abruptly incurved apically below the punctiform stigma. Fruiting hypanthium urceolate, 8-10 mm long to the torus and 5-6 mm wide. Seeds cochleate with a series of smooth continuous semicircular ridges, 0.75 mm long.

description: Shrub 1-3 meters high, freely branched. Younger stems densely gray-stellate-tomentose, hirsute with both silmlple and glandular hairs 1-2 mm. long, glabreseent in age. Petioles slender, 1-2 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Blades velvety-green above, pale beneath, ovate-lanceolate, up to 17 cm. long and 8 cm. wide, long-acuminate, minutely denticulate, cordate at the base, 7-nerved, above bullate, each bulla tipped with a short stout bristle, at least when young, often also with a few stellate hairs, beneath foveolate, beautifully reticulate, densely gray-stellate-tomentose, sparsely glandular-setose on the primary veins. Infloreseences ample, freely branched, up to 10 cm. long, with lateral branches up to 3 cm. long, pubescent like the stem; pedicels about 1 mm. long. Flowers 7-merous. Hypanthium cup-shaped, 4 mm. long, densely tomentose with stellate hairs 0.4 mm. across, glandular-hirsute with spreading hairs about 1 mm. long. Calyx-tube about 0.4 mm. long; sepals suberect, oblong-ovate, 2 mm. long from the torus, stellate and glandular, the free tip almost obsolete; exterior teeth subulate, 3.5-4 mm. long, pubeseelit like the hypanthium, the hairs shorter. Petals oblong-obovate, 5-6 mm. long, barely retuse. Filamelnts slender, 4.5-5.5 mm. long; anthers slenderly subulate, 5.5 mm. long, the pore ventro-terminal; connective prolonged about 1 mm. below the thecae. Ovary half inferior, its roulided summit villous at the summnit; style about 5 mm. long; stigma truncate.

description: Description: A woody vine; staminate inflorescence (not previously described) axillary, paniculate, to 12 cm. long, the rather numerous branches short and few-flowered, the peduncles, rachis, and inflores- cence branches uniformly very slender and uniformly appressed- puberulent; pedicels about 1 mm. long, appressed-puberulent; stami- nate flowers: sepals 18, the outer closely imbricate, the outermost minute, gradually increasing in size to the 6 valvate inner ones, which are lanceolate, about 2.9 mm. long and 1 mm. wide, acute at apex, entire, acute or acuminate at base, all appressed-strigose on the out- side, glabrous within, the hairs often not noticeably overlapping the margins; petals 6, elliptic-cucul]ate, rather fleshy, about 1.9 mm. long and 0.7-0.9 mm. wide, obtuse or rounded at apex, the margins greatly inflexed, strigose on the outside, glabrous within; stamens 6, of 2 lengths, slightly connate at base, 3 about 1.4 mm. long and the other 3 about 1.9 mm. long; filaments glabrous, inerassate, ampliate above.

description: Description: A woody vine; branchlets slender, very minutely puberulent, glabreseent in age; petioles slender, 1.1-5 cm. long, rather sparsely strigillose when immature, glabrate when mature; blades membranous, nitid on both surfaces, ovate-elliptic, 4-20 cm. long, 2.4- 10.1 cm. wide, long-acuminate at apex, entire, varying from subtrun- cate to acute or very short-acuminate at base, glabrous on both surfaces, plainly 3-pli-nerved with another more tenuous and less conspicuous pair of veins serving as collective-veins along the margins; primary veins prominent on both surfaces, only the midrib extending through to the very apex, the lateral pair continuous for about two-thirds or three-fourths the length of the blade and then broken into numerous arches; secondaries numerous, slender, prominulent on both surfaces, issuing at right angles to the primaries and connecting them; veinlet reticulation abundant (on older leaves) or rather sparse, the larger portions prominulent on both surfaces, the ultimate portions often obscure on younger leaves, but prominulent on both surfaces on older ones; staminate infloreseence axillary, racemose, 2-5 cm. long, un- branched, 6-10-flowered; peduncles and rachis very slender or filiform, very sparsely scattered-pilose; pedicels very slender, 1-2 mm. long, densely appressed-puberulent with einereous hairs; staminate flowers: sepals 18, the outer 9 small, the inner 9 rather uniformly large, elliptic-ovate, about 1.9 mm. long and 0.9 mm. wide, concave when viewed from within, acute at both ends, densely appressed-puberulent with very short hairs which project over the margins, causing a densely ciliate appearance from within; petals 6, elliptic, about 1.2 mm. lolng and 0.5 mm. wide, rounded at apex, not cuneate at base, uniformly appressed-puberulent in a median band and on the margins from base to apex outside, glabrous within; stamens 6, equal, separate, about 1.2 mm. long, the filaments inerassate; fruit obovate, about 1.8 cm. long and 1 cm. wide at apex, the exocarp densely puberulent with albidous hairs.

description: Slender tree to 15 m; branches terete, grayish, striate, puberulous. Leaves coriaceous, oblong-lanceolate, 11-26 cm long, 3.5-7.5 cm broad, more than three times longer than broad, glabrous above, puberulous on midrib and veins beneath, pinnately veined with about 6 pairs of arching alternating inconspicuous primary veins; areoles subrectangular, ca 1 mm diam, more conspicuous beneath; margin entire; apex narrowed, obtuse; base rounded; petiole 1.5-2.5 cm long, puberulous. Male inflorescences axillary, solitary or clustered, spicate, shorter than the petiole, ascending, slender, densely villous; peduncles 0.2-0.4 cm long; rachis 0.7-1.7 cm long; bracts lanceolate, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, villous; pedicels 0-0.5 mm long; bractlets 1-3, oblong-lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous. Flowers greenish; sepals 6 in 2 series, glabrous, the outer narrowly obovate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.6 mm broad, the inner obovate, ca 1.5 mm long, ca 1 mm broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate-rhombic, ca 0.7 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, glabrous; stamens 6; filaments ca 1.2 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, solitary or clustered, shorter than the petiole, ascending, stout, densely villous; peduncles 0.2-0.5 cm long. Fruit globose, glabrous, 17-20 mm long, 14-16 mm broad, somewhat compressed, the apex broadly rounded. Distribution: Known only from the vicinity of the type locality at 1000 m.

description: Description: A woody vine; branchlets stout, minutely pulverulent; leaf scars very large and prominent; petioles slender, 7.5-15 cm. long, conspicuously ampliate at base, inerassate and often curvate at apex, very sparsely and minutely pilosulous or glabrate; leaf blades subcoriaceous, nitid, oblong-elliptic, 19.5-24.5 cm. long, 8.5-10.5 cm. wide, abruptly acute or short-acuminiate at apex, entire, very abruptly acute or short-acuminate at base, glabrous o01 both surfaces; midrib impressed above, very sharply prominent to the apex beneath; secondaries slender, 5-7 per side, irregularly disposed, impressed above, very prominent beneath, arcuate-aseending, not anastomosing; tertiaries slender, issuing at about right angles to the secondaries and connectiing them, impressed above, prominent be- neath; vein and vein]et reticulation mostly obscure or indiscernible above (or the larger portions discernible), the larger portioils prominulent beneath, the ultimate reticulum discernible only uander a hand-lens; staminate infloreseence axillary, racemiform or obscurely subpaniculate, 10-12 cm. long, 1-1.5 cm. wide in anthesis, many- flowered; rachis densely tomeentellous with brown hairs, its branehes minutely and very sparsely pilosulous, very slender; staminate flowers: sepals 6, the 3 outer ones elliptic, about 2.4 mm. long and 1.2 mm. wide, abruptly obtuse at apex, obtuse at base, somewhat con- vex, the 3 inner ones broadly elliptic or orbicular, about 2.4 mm. long and wide, rouncded at both ends; petals 6, obovate, about 1.4 mm. long and 1.2 mm. wide, conspicuously involute along the sides and at apex, rounded at apex, not cuneate at base; stamens 6, 0.49-0.73 mm. long, conspicuously widened (to 0.49 mm.) at apex; pistillate infloreseence and fruit not known.

description: Description: A vine of large dimensions when mature, often reach- ing the tops of the highest trees; branchlets slender, subterete, densely appressed-puberulent or pulverulent-puberulent, less noticeably so in age, the puberulence grayish; description: Descriptionr: A vine, often climbing trees up to 30 m. tall or taller; branchlets rather slender, subterete or slightly angled, very densely and uniformly appressed-puberulent with einereous hairs; description: Glabrous vine of unknown dimensions, the epidermis of trunk pale brown, exfoliating in papery tatters, the annotinous branchlets smooth, canaliculate. Petioles 4-6 cm x 0.6-0.9 mm; leaf blades submembranous, pale green, moderately lustrous, ovate from shallowly cordate base, abruptly short-acuminate 9-13.5 x 5.5-7 cm, the acumen ±5 mm obtuse, mucronulate; primary veins 5 from insertion of petiole, the outer pair short and weak, the inner pair incurved-ascending beyond middle of blade, the midrib giving rise beyond middle to 2 pairs of major secondary veins, these all raised on both faces but more prominent beneath, the intervenium sharply regularly reticulate-venulose, the larger ultimate areoles not over 0.5 mm diam. description: Shrub or tree to 10 m, sometimes diffuse to vine-like, the trunks to 1.5 dm diam; branches subterete, the older ones gray, glabrate, the younger grayish to tawny-tomentulose. Leaves stiff, coriaceous, narrowly to broadly ovate, 1.7-20 cm long, 1.2-16.5 cm broad, less than twice as long as broad, glabrous to pilo- sulose on the primary veins above, tawny-tomentulose beneath, pinnately veined with 4 or 5 pairs of prominent alternating arching primary veins, the ultimate venation finely reticulate on both surfaces but more conspicuous beneath; areoles ca 0.5 mm diam, minutely papillose within; margin entire to more or less repand- denticulate to pungent-spinose; apex rounded to spinose-acute; base cuneate to cordate; petiole 0.5-4 cm long, tomentulose to glabrate. Mate inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, ascending, short, stout, dense, spicate or sometimes elongate and racemose, shorter to slightly longer than the petiole, densely to- mentulose; peduncles 0-1 cm long; rachis 0.3-4.2 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.5-0.8 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, densely tomentulose; pedicels 0-1 mm long; bractlets 3, narrowly obovate-elliptic, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, glabrous to very sparsely pubescent. Flowers greenish-white to yellow, glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate-elliptic, ca 2 mm long, ca 0.8 mm broad, the inner broadly obovate, ca 2 mm long, ca 1.3 mm broad; petals absent, 3 or 6 in 1 or 2 similar series, obovate-oblong, ca 0.6 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad; stamens 6; filaments ca 1.2 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, spicate, shorter to slightly longer than the petiole, ascending, tomentulose; pedun- cles stout, 2-7 mm long; rachis 1-4.2 mm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.5-0.9 cm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, tomentulose; pedicels 0-1 mm long; bractlets 3, ovate-lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.6 mm broad, densely pubescent. Flowers greenish-white to yellow; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer oblong, ca 1.8 mm long, ca 0.9 mm broad, pubescent, the inner ovate-orbicular, ca 2.2 mm long, ca 1 mm broad, sparsely pubescent; petals 6 in 2 similar series, oblong, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, glabrous; carpels 3 or 4, ovoid, ca 1.6 mm long, ca 0.8 mm broad, glabrous. Fruits green to orange, obovoid-orbicular, glabrous, 16-20 mm long, 16-18 mm broad, slightly compressed, the apex broadly rounded.

description: Decumbent or climbing to 6 m or a small tree to 5 m, the trunk to 7.5 cm diam; branches terete, striate, usually glabrate but occasionally hispid. Leaves coriaceous, narrowly ovate to rarely obovate, 7-16 cm long, 2.5-6 cm broad, 2-3 times longer than broad, glabrous or rarely hispid on the midrib beneath, pinnately veined, the 3-6 pairs of primary veins relatively inconspicuous, the ultimate venation finely reticulate; areoles ca 0.5 mm diam; margin entire, more or less undulate,; apex usually acute to acuminate; base mostly rounded; petiole 1-4 cm long, mostly glabrous. Male inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, paniculate, variable in length but usually equal to or longer than the petiole, ascending, usually filiform, sparsely to moderately villous; peduncle 0.2-1 cm long; rachis 0.4-4 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.5-1 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, villous; ped- icels 0.5-1.5 mm long; bractlets 2 or 3, oblong-lanceolate, 0.5-1.2 mm long, 0.2 mm broad, villous. Flowers greenish-yellow, glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer narrowly obovate to obovate-oblong, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 0.7 mm broad, the inner broadly obovate to orbicular, ca 1.6 mm long, ca 1.2 mm broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate, ca 0.6 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad; stamens 6; filaments ca 0.5 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, usually clustered, ra- cemose, usually shorter than the petiole, ascending to spreading-ascending, filiform to slender, villous; peduncles 0.2-1 cm long; rachis 0.5-1.5 cm long; bracts lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 1-2.5 mm long; bractlets 3, lanceolate, ca 0.5 mm long, ca 0.2 mm broad, villous. Flowers greenish-yellow, glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer ovate-oblong, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 0.8 mm broad, the inner ovate, ca 1.5 mm long, ca 1 mm broad, glabrous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate, ca 0.7 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad; carpels 3, ovoid, ca 0.6 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, glabrous. Fruit globose, glabrous, 20-25 mm long, 20-23 mm broad, compressed, the apex broadly rounded.

description: Tree ca 25 m tall. Leafy twigs 1-2.5 cm thick, yellow-hirsute, pluricellular hairs absent. Lamina ca 25-40 x 25-40 cm, 5- or 7-fid to parted, coriaceous, apex acuminate, base deeply cordate with overlapping lobes; upper surface smooth to slightly scabrous, yellow-hirsute to -hirtellous on the whole surface or only on the main veins, lower surface hirsute to hirtellous on the veins, arachnoid hairs in the areoles and on the reticulum; lateral veins 16-25 pairs; petiole ca 25-40 cm long, yellow-hirsute; stipules 10-15 cm long, outside yellow-hirsute, inside gla- brous, caducous. Staminate inflorescences ca 12-22 cm long and ca 8-14 cm wide; peduncle 4-8 cm long, peduncle and branches yellow-hirtellous to-puberulous; flowers in globose heads, these up to 7-12 mm in diam; perianth tubular, 1-2 mm long, puberulous at the apex; stamens 3 or 4, filaments completely connate, 3-6 mm long. Pistillate inflorescences up to 10 cm long and up to 12 cm wide, branched; peduncle 3-5 cm long, peduncle and branches yellow-hirsute to -hir- tellous; flowers ca 40-70; pedicel ca 5 mm, in fruit up to 12 mm long; perianth ca 5 mm long, yellow-hirsute to -hirtellous, sparsely so in the uppermost part; stigma peltate.
bibliographicCitation: Berg, Cornelius C. 1990. New species of Coussapoa and Pourouma (Cecropiaceae). Brittonia. 42: 59-65.

description: Small or medium sized tree; branchlets slender, soon glabrous and cinereous; petioles rugose, canaliculate, slender, 1-1.5 mm. in diameter, 7-15 mm. long, glabrous; leaf blades chartaceous or thin coriaceous. finely rugose or nearly smooth on both surfaces, often shining above, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 9-18 cm. long, 3-8 cm. broad, acute to attenuate at base, obtusely cuspidate or short acuminate at apex, the costa raised above, the secondary nerves 8-12 per side, spreading, shallowly impressed or plane above, nearly plane beneath, often obscure ascending near margins and obscurely anastomosing, the veinlets immersed; staminate inflorescences 3-9 cm. long, fasciculate-racemose (fascicles sometimes borne on minute lateral branches up to 2 mm. long), the rachis slender, the fascicles alternate or subopposite, 7-20 per inflorescence; flowers 2-7 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 4 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole membranous, one-sided, obtuse, about 1 mm. long); perianth carnose or thin carnose, often glabrescent and sparsely glandular-punctate, cupuliform or rotate, 1.3-2 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly. to base, the lobes deltoid-ovate, subacute, conspicuously spreading at anthesis; androecium ellipsoid or obovoid, 0.4-0.6 mm. long and nearly as broad, the filament column contracted at base, the anthers 0.2-0.3 mm. long, dorsally adnate to carnose fused connectives; pistillate inflorescences borne on larger branchlets (or on trunk?), about 2 cm. long, few-branched from near base, ferruginous puberulent; fascicles few, the flowers 2-10 per fascicle, the pedicels up to 2 mm. long, the perianth thick carnose, the ovary cylindric, truncate at summit, the stigma sessile; fruiting inflorescences up to 6 cm. long, the mature fruits usually 2-4 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 3-5 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid, 17-20 mm. long (excluding stipe), 21-27 mm. broad, conspicuously carinate, apiculate at apex, the lateral extremities rounded, the stipe stout, 2-3 mm. long, the pericarp rugose, 2-4 mm. thick or more on the sutures, the aril red, obscurely laciniate distally, the seed conspicuoisly broader than long.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Shrub or low tree up to 6 m. high; branchlets rugose, slender; petioles shallowly canaliculate, 1-2 mm. in diameter, 6-10 mm. long, soon glabrous; leaf blades chartaceous or thin coriaceous, finely rugose or uniformly minutely papillose on both surfaces, elliptic-oblong, 10-22 cm. long, 3-6 cm. broad, acute to attenuate at base, obtusely acuminate at apex, the costa raised above, the secondary nerves 9-16 per side, ascending or arcuate-ascending, slightly impressed above, raised beneath, the veinlets immersed; staminate inflorescences fasciculate- racemose, 1-4 cm. long, slender, minutely strigose on all exterior surfaces; fascicles 3-5 per inflorescence, the flowers 2-5 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 5 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteoles cupuliform or cleft nearly to base, 0.3-1 mm. long); perianth thin carnose, campanulate, 2.5-3.5 mm. long, flaring at apex, 3-lobed about one-third its total length, the lobes deltoid-ovate, obtuse; androecium nearly as long as the perianth, the filament column carnose, 1.8-2.5 mm. long, the anthers 3 or 4, 0.3-0.6 mm. long, loosely connate to apex or free to base, the connectives inconspicuous; pistillate inflorescences shorter than the staminate (less than 1 cm. long), the flowers few, the ovary glabrous, leading imperceptibly into the short carnose style, the stigma inconspicuous; fruiting inflorescences compact, less than 4 cm. long, the mature fruits usually 2 or 3 per infloreseence, pedicellate (pedicels 3-6 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid, carinate, at maturity 9-14 mm. long (excluding stipes), 12-20 mm. broad, conspicuously stipitate (stipe 2-3 mm. long), conspicuously apiculate at apex, the pericarp 0.5-1.5 mm. thick, the seed conspicuously transversely ellip- soid, up to 9 mm. long and 16 mm. broad.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Slender tree up to 15 m. high, the branchlets elongate, subterete or slightly angled, densely and closely ferruginous-puberulent, soon glabrous and cincereous; petioles deeply canaliculate or subterete, 1.5-3 mm. in diameter, 7-17 mm. long, puberulent as the branchlets; leaf blades coriaceous, narrowly oblong or narrowly elliptic, 16-33 cm. long, 4.5-8 cm. broad, cordate to rounded or broadly obtuse at base, long acuminate at apex, uniformly and densely tomentellous beneath (hairs  sessile-stellate, several-branched, 0.1-0.2 mm. in diameter, sometimes with darker centers, sometimes interspersed with dark punctations), the costa prominent on both surfaces, strong beneath, the secondary nerves 12-20 per side, curved near margins, impressed or slightly raised above, prominent beneath, the veinlets obscure or faintly prominulous; staminate inflorescences feew-branched, comparatively few-flowered, 1-4 cm. long, the peduncle less than 1 cm. long, with the branchlets and flowers closely dark brown tomentellous (hairs sessile-stellate, 5-8- branched, about 0.1 mm. in diameter), ebracteate; flowers in ultimate clusters of 2-8, the pedicels slender, up to 1.5 mm. long; perianth carnose, infundibuliform, 1.7-2 mm. long, 3-cleft about one-third of the length, the lobes rounded or obtuse; androecium 1.2-1.4 mm. long, the filament column thick carnose, abruptly narrowed at apex, 0.7-0.8 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Tree up to 25 m. high, the trunk up to 1 m. in diameter; branchlets closely tomentose, the hairs irregularly branching, 0.5-1 mm. long, at length deciduous; petioles subterete, stout, 3-5 mm. in diameter, 9-15 mm. long, tomentose as the branchlets; leaf blades coriaceous, oblong, 18-45 cm. long, 6-15 cm. broad, deeply cordate to truncate at base, acuminate or cuspidate at apex, above glabrous or tomentellous on the costa, beneath uniformly densely tomentose with stalked irregularly branched hairs about 0.5 mm. long, the costa raised above, very prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 16-28 per side, ascending, arcuate near margins, slightly impressed or prominulous above, prominent beneath, those near the base often recurved, the veinlets prominulous or obsecire; staminate inflorescences broadly paniculate, freely branching, many-flowered, up to 25 cm. long and broad, the peduncle 5-8 cm. long, with the branchlets copiously tomentellous (hairs 0.2-0.5, rarely to 0.8, mm. long, irregularly branched, often with short lateral spurs); bracts inconspicuous, soon deciduous; flowers loosely arranged, ultimately in small clusters of 3-7, the pedicels slender, 1-2 mm. long, with the perianth densely tomentellous (hairs irregularly branched, 0.2-0.4 mm. long); perianth thin carnose, 2.3-3 mm. long, infundibuliform, puberulent within, 3- or 4-cleft about one-third its length, the lobes deltoid-oblong, obtuse; androecium 1.5-2 mm. long, the filament column carnose, swolleil at base, 0.4-0.5 mm. long, the anthers 3, 1.1-1.5 mm. long, divergent at apex and each terminated by a slender apiculum 0.1-0.15 mm. long; pistillate inflorescences 6-18 cm. long, tomentellous as the staminate inflorescences; flowers in ultimate clusters of 2-5, short pedicellate, the ovary subglobose, densely tomentose (hairs 1.5-2.5 mm. long, jointed, with numerous short lateral branches); fruiting inflorescences up to 9 cm. long or more, the fruits 4-8 per inflorescence, short pedicellate, subglobose, 15-30 mm. in diameter, densely and persistently tomentose (hairs as those of the ovary, 3-4.5 mm. long), the pericarp brittle, 0.3-0.7 mm. thick; aril laciniate nearly to base; seed subglobose or slightly ellipsoid, 10-12 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. & Wodehouse, R. P. 1938. The American species of Myristicaceae. Brittonia. 2: 393-527. f. 1-9.

description: Slender tree 5-12 m. high, the trunk up to 35 cm. in diameter: branchlets stout, persistently tomentose, the hairs ferruginous, 1-2 mm. long, multicellular, jointed, the lateral branches spur-like, obvious; petioles stout, terete, 3-8 mm. in diameter, 8-21 mm. long, tomentose as the branchlets; leaf blades thin coriaceous, oblong or obovate-oblong, 25-50 cm. long, 8-19 cm. broad, deeply cordate to rounded at base, long acuminate or abruptly acuminate at apex, above glabrous or deciduously tomentose on the costa, beneath densely brown tomentose, the hairs stalked, jointed, 1-1.5 mm. long, with numerous lateral branches, those of the principal nerves usually somewhat longer, the costa prominent on both surfaces, very conspicuous beneath, the secondary nerves 15-30 per side, nearly straight, slightly impressed or prominuous above, prominent beneath, those near the base often recurved, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous or obscure; staminate inflorescences broadly paniculate, freely branching, many-flowered, up to 25 cm. long and 18 cm. broad, the peduncle 3-8 cm. long, with the branchlets densely tomentose with hairs similar to those of the foliage branchlets; bracts ovate, about 6 mm. long, densely tomentellous, soon deciduous; flowers loosely arranged, ultimately single or in clusters of 2-5, the pedicel at length to 3 mm. long, tomentellous; perianth thin carnose, infundibuliform, about 2 mm. long, densely tomentellous without, 3-lobed about one-third the total length, the lobes obtuse; androecium about 1.4 mm. long, the filament column 0.4-0.5 mm. long, the anthers 3, connate to apex, about 1 mm. long, apiculate at apex, the apiculum about 0.1 mm. long, single or cleft; pistillate inflorescences not seen; fruiting inflorescences 4-5 cm. long, the fruits 5-10 per inflorescence, short pedicellate, subglobose, 11-14 mm. in diameter, densely and persistently tomentose (hairs 2-2.5 mm. long, the main branch flexuose, jointed, with numerous short lateral branches), the pericarp brittle, less than 0.5 mm. thick.
