description: Tree up to 17 m. high; branchlets stout, rugose, glabrous; petioles canaliculate, rugose, 13-22 mm. long, 3-5 mm. in diameter, glabrous; leaf blades thick coriaceous, finely rugose or uniformly minutely papillose on both surfaces, oblong or elliptic-obloug, 23-45 cm. long, 6-13 cm. broad, acute or cuneate at base, obtusely cuspidate or short acuminate at apex, entire and narrowly revolute at margius, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 17-20 per side, straight, spreading, slightly raised or shallowly impressed above, prominent beneath, conispicuously and regularly anastomosing near margins, the veinlets immersed; staminate inflorescences narrowly pauieulate, 15-23 cm. long, minutely strigose on all exterior surfaces, the rachis stout, striate, the secondary branches 14-23 per infloresceuce, alternate, stout, 2-5 mm. long (shorter or suppressed uiear apex); flowers 7-15 per fascicle, aggregated at the swollen ends of the lateral branches, associated with minute ovate deciduous bracts, the pedicels slender, up to 8 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteoles cleft to base, about 1.5 mm. long, membranous); perianth carnose, campanulate, flaring distally, about 4 mm. long, 3-lobed about one-third its length, the lobes ovate-deltoid, obtuse, thickened at apex; androecium 2.5-3 mm. long, the filament column 2- 2.5 mm. long, slender, the anthers 3, about 0.5 mm. long, free to base, the connectives swollen, sparsely glandular; pistillate inflorescenees not seen; fruiting inflorescences up to 10 cm. long, the fruits few, short- pedicellate, slightly transversely ellipsoid, inconspicuously carinate, up to 26 mm. long and 33 mm. broad, the pericarp woody, 3-7 mm. thick.

description: Arbor 30-35 m. alta; ramis rugosis cinereis glabris, ramulis juve-nilibus angulatis flexuosis dense et arete brunneo-pilosis; petiolis velut ramulis pilosis saepe complanatis 3-5 mm. longis; laminis papyraceis vel submembranaceis, juventute minutissime pellucido-punctatis, oblongis, 6-8 cm. longis, 2-3.5 cm. latis, basi cordatis, apice obtusis vel subacutis, margine integris, supra glabris, subtus dense minute stellato-pilosis (pilis 3-5-ramosis), costa supra impressa subtus prominente, nervis secundariis patulis rectis 6-9 per centimetrum subtus leviter elevatis; inflorescentiis axillaribus paniculatis ad 8 cm. longis ubique brunneo-pilosis; pedunculis complanatis 1 cm. longis; floribus dense aggregatis circiter 15 in fasciculis; pedicellis 1 mm. longis; perigonio infundibuliformi 2 mm. longo intus glabro, lobis 3 ovato-oblongis obtusis, 1.5 mm. longis, 1 mm. latis; antheris connatis acutis 1 mm. longis, quam columna glabra duplo longioribus.

description: Slender tree 4-10 m. high, the trunk about 7-12 cm. in diameter; branchlets densely and persistently tomentose, the hairs ferruginous, 1.5-4 mm. long, multicellular, jointed, the lateral branches numerous, spur-like or suppressed; petioles stout, terete, 2.5-6 mm. in diameter, 3-12 mm. long, tomentose as the branchlets; leaf blades thin coriaceous or papyraceous, oblong, oblong-elliptic, or narrowly obovate-oblong, 15-35 cm. long, 4-10 cm. broad, cordate or rounded at base, gradually attenuate to an acute or acuminate apex, above glabrous or sometimes tomentose on costa, beneath densely or sparsely tomentose with stalked irregularly branched hairs about 1 mm. long, the hairs of the nerves usually 2-3 mm. long, the costa nearly plane or somewhat prominent above, very prominent and strong beneath, the secondary nerves 15-26 per side, nearly straight, arcuate near margins, slightly impressed above, raised beneath, the veinlets copiously reticulate, prominulous on both surfaces or obscure; staminate infloreseences broadly paniculate, freely branching, many-flowered, up to 25 cm. long and 15 cm. broad, the peduncle 4-12 cm. long, slender, with the branchlets densely tomentose with hairs similar to those of the foliage branchlets; bracts linear- lanceolate, about 3 mm. long, densely ferruginous-tomentose, soon deciduous; flowers loosely arranged, ultimately single or in small clusters, the pedicels slender, 2-4 mm. long, loosely tomentellous; perianth submembranous, infundibuliform, 1.5-2.5 mm. long, tomentellous with- out (hairs about 0.1 mm. long, stellate), 3- or 4-lobed nearly one-half its length, the lobes deltoid, obtuse; androecium 1-1.4 mm. long, the filamnent column 0.4-0.6 mm. long, the anthers 3, connate to apex, 0.5- 0.8 mm. long, apiculate at apex, the apiculum single or cleft, about 0.1 mm. long; pistillate inflorescences comparatively slender, up to 15 cm. long, tomentose as the staminate inflorescences; flowers in ultimate clusters of 5-10, subsessile, the ovary globose, densely tomentose (hairs up to 1 mm. long), the stigma sessile; fruiting inflorescences up to 35 cm. long and 15 cm. broad, the fruits about 10-40 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels stout, 3-5 mm. long), subglobose, 13-22 mm. in diameter, densely and persistently tomentose (hairs 7-9 mm. long, copiously jointed, the lateral branches very short or suppressed), the pericarp brittle, usually less than 0.5 mm. thick. description: Tree up to 65 m. high, the trunk robust, about 25 m. to the first branch; branchlets slender, sparsely canescent-puberulent, glabrescent; petioles canaliculate, densely puberulent, 1-2 mm. in diameter, 5-10 imm. long; leaf blades thin coriaceous, narrowly oblong, usually with parallel margins, 9-16 cm. long, 2.3-4 cm. broad, attenuate or acute at base, cuspidate or short acuminate at apex, glabrous above, pale puberulent beneath (hairs sessile-stellate, 4-6-branched, about 0.1 mm. in diameter), the costa shallowly grooved above, prominlent beneath, the secondary nerves 25-30 per side, nearly straight, olbseurely anastomosing near margins, faintly impressed above, sharply raised beneath the veinlets sharply impressed or obseure; staminate inflorescences (immature in our specimen) paniculate, up to 4 cm. long, the branchlets and flowers densely brown tomentellous (hairs several-branched from base, about 0.1 mm. long); bracts ovate, puberulent, 3-5 mm. long, soon deciduous; flowers arranged in ultimate clusters of about 10 ( ?); perianth thin carnose, faintly pellucid-punetate, about 2 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes oblong, obtuse; androecium 1.7-2 mm.

description: Shrub up to 5 m. high; branchlets slender, when young sparsely strigose, soon glabrous and cinereous; petioles shallowly canaliculate, narrowly winged distally, about 1 mm. in diameter, 6-12 mm. long, soon glabrous; leaf blades chartaceous, finely rugose or uniformly minutely papillose on both surfaces, elliptic, 10-15 cm. long, 3.5-6.5 cm. broad, acute to attenuate at base, obtusely short acuminate at apex, the costa raised above, the secondary nerves 8-12 per side, spreading, slightly impressed or plane above, raised beneath, the veinlets immersed; staminate inflorescences fasciculate-racemose, up to 1 cm. long, slender, few-flowered, minutely strigose on all exterior surfaces, the peduncle very short, sometimes woody; fascicles 2-4 per inflorescence; flowers 2-4 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 3 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteoles cupuliform, submembranous, 0.5-0.8 mm. long); perianth thin carnose, campanulate, 2.5-3 mm. long, flaring at apex, 3-lobed about one-third its total length, the lobes deltoid, subacute, androecium nearly as long as the perianth, the filament column carnose, about 1.8 mm. long, the anthers 0.8-1 mm. long, free to base, the connectives broad, conspicuously carnose, flattened, glandular; pistillate inflorescences shorter than the staminate and with fewer flowers; fruiting inflorescences compact, less than 2 cm. long, the mature fruits 1-3 per inflorescence, pedicellate (pedicels 2-4 mm. long), transversely ellipsoid, nigrescent, faintly carinate, at maturity up to 10 mm. long and 15 mm. broad, conspicuously stipitate at base (stipe about 2 mm. long), apiculate at apex, the pericarp about 0.5 mm. thick. (Fig. 4, a-d.)

description: Medium sized tree; branchlets stout, glabrous, cinereous; petioles canaliculate, narrowly winged distally, 2-4 mm. in diameter, 12-17 mm. long, glabrous; leaf blades coriaceous, smooth and dull on both surfaces, oblong, 20-28 cm. long, 6-8.5 cm. broad, obtuse at base and narrowly decurrent on the petiole, obtusely short acuminate at apex, the costa raised above, the secondary nerves 28-32 per side, spreading, straight, impressed above, prominent beneath, conspicuously and regularly anastomosing near margins, the veinlets immersed or slightly impressed above; staminate inflorescences about 2 cm. long, compactly fasciculate-racemose, densely ferruginous-tomentellous on all exterior surfaces (hairs 2-4-branched, 0.2-0.4 mm. long), the peduncle very short, the rachis stout, straight, the fascicles several; flower- 8-12 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 3 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole membranous, one-sided, oblong, about 1 mm. long); perianth carnose, cupuliform or subrotate, about 1.8 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes ovate-deltoid, subacuto; androecium about 0.7 mm. long, the filament column carnose, cylindric, the anthers about 0.25 mm. long, dorsally connate, the connectives inconspicuous; pistillate and fruiting inflorescences not seen.

description: Small tree; branchlets subterete or obtusely angled, stout, glabrous; petioles canaliculate, narrowly winged distally, glabrous, 2-3 mm. in diameter, 10-14 mm. long; leaf blades thick coriaceous, finely rugose on both surfaces, oblong, 12-20 cm. long, 4.5-6.5 cm. broad, obtuse or rounded at base, obtusely short acuminate at apex, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 13-16 per side, spreading, conspicuously impressed above, nearly plane beneath, arcuate and anastomosing near margins, the veinlets reticulate, slightly impressed above, obscure beneath; staminate inflorescences 6-9 cm. long, fasciculateracemose, the rachis slender, usually straight, the fascicles alternate or subopposite, 15-25 per inflorescence, sessile or at the ends of minute lateral branches 1 mm. long or less; flowers 2-7 per fascicle, the pedicels slender, up to 4 mm. long, bracteolate at summit (bracteole cupuliform truncate, about 0.5 mm. long); perianth carnose, cupuliform or subrotate, 1.5-2.2 mm. long, 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes ovate-deltoid, subacute, spreading at anthesis; androecium ellipsoid or obovoid, 0.6-0.7 mm. long and nearly as broad, the filament column carnose, minutely glandular, the anthers about 0.25 mm. long, dorsally adnate to carnose fused connectives; pistillate and fruiting inflorescences not seen.

description: Annual, much branched, succulent herbs, procumbent to semierect; long taproot, fleshy; stems stout, 1-7 dm long, often reddish at least at nodes, viscid, sparsely glandular-pubescent to puberulent or with moderately dense short hairs; petioles 1-6 cm long, sparsely glandular to puberulent; leaf blades from oblong-lanceolate to ovate to rhombic to elliptic-oblong, entire, often undulate, often scabrous when young, margin often scabro-ciliate, base oblique, truncate, obtuse to cuneate, tip obtuse to acute; peduncles 1.2-11 cm long; bracts 5-8, lanceolate to ovate to elliptic, often attenuate, sparingly glandular to glandular-pubescent, margins often ciliate; receptacles with pedicel-like projections to 2 mm long; 10-25 flowers per inflorescence; perianth tube 12-30 mm long, white to pink to reddish purple; perianth limbs 10-15 mm wide, deeply emarginate, raphid bundles apparent, slender, directed toward throat; anthocarps usually 3-winged, sometimes 2- or 4-winged, 15-35 mm long, 10-25 mm wide, body indurate with from 1-3 prominent longitudinal ribs between the wings, sometimes ribs lacking, body glabrous, seldom sparsely pubescent; wings glabrous, margin scabro-ciliate, the hairs short conical, nearly as wide as long; achenes elliptic- oblong, length to 9 mm, tan to light brown.
bibliographicCitation: Galloway, Leo A. 1976. Systematics of the North American desert species of Abronia and Tripterocalyx (Nyctaginaceae). Brittonia. 27: 328-347.

description: Plants sometimes somewhat scabrous, hairs finer, to 1.5 mm long, and overall more dense in this variety; stems 1-6 dm long; petioles 0.5-6.5 cm long; leaf blades ovate, ovate-rhombic, oblong-ovate, deltoid-ovate to elliptic-oblong, 1.5-8 cm long, 0.6-5 cm wide, somewhat glaucous below when living, base truncate to cuneate, infrequently oblique, apex obtuse, rarely acute; peduncles 4.5-17 cm long; bracts linear-lanceolate, lance-ovate to ovate, somewhat attenuate, 5-14 mm long, 1.5-5 mm wide; perianth tube pink to pinkish red, often glaucous when fresh; perianth limbs 8-11 mm broad, interior white, exterior white to pale pink with darker pink to pinkish red ribs; antho- carps 13-27 mm long, 9.5-17.5 mm wide; achenes 6-7.5 mm long, tan.
bibliographicCitation: Galloway, Leo A. 1976. Systematics of the North American desert species of Abronia and Tripterocalyx (Nyctaginaceae). Brittonia. 27: 328-347.

description: Decumbent to nearly erect much branched annual herbs; long fleshy taproot; stems 1-3 dm long, viscid, lower stem glabrous to densely glandular-pubescent, upper stem sparsely glandular-pubescent to densely short villous; petioles 1-4.5 cm long, some- what viscid, glandular-pubescent; leaf blades ovate, oblong-ovate, elliptic-oblong to elliptic, 2.5-7 cm long, 1-3 cm wide, margins entire to sinuate, base obtuse to cuneate, apex obtuse or infrequently acute, blades somewhat viscid, short glandular- pubescent; peduncles 1-6 cm long; bracts ovate to lanceolate, somewhat attenuate, 3-12 mm long, 1.5-3.5 mm wide, viscid, sparsely to densely glandular-pubescent, margin ciliate, glabrous inside; receptacles flat to somewhat conical; pedicel-like projections to 1 mm long; flowers 10-30 per inflorescence; perianth tube 8-25 mm long, glandular-pubescent to short villous, base of tube pink, upper portion greenish to pink; perianth limbs 10-15 mm diameter, usually 4-lobed, bright magenta, glabrous, deeply emarginate, conspicuous raphid bundles near upper surface of limb giving the appearance of appressed hairs directed toward throat; anthocarps normally 2- winged, infrequently 3-winged, 7-13 mm long, 8-17 mm wide, body rugose to trans- versely ribbed, glandular-pubescent to short-villous, veins and margins of wings glandular-pubescent; achenes elliptic-oblong, 5-6 mm long, light brown.
bibliographicCitation: Galloway, Leo A. 1976. Systematics of the North American desert species of Abronia and Tripterocalyx (Nyctaginaceae). Brittonia. 27: 328-347.

description: Viscid, much branched, sometimes scabrous annual herbs, procumbent to nearly erect; long fleshy taproot; stems 1-6 dm long, somewhat viscid, lower stem glabrous to short glandular-pubescent, upper stem sparsely glandular-puberulent to glandular- pubescent; petioles 10-40 mm, glandular-pubescent; leaf blades lanceovate, oblongovate, ovate, oblong-elliptic to elliptic, entire to sinuate, often undulate, 10-60 mm long, 4-25 mm wide, base obtuse, tip obtuse, blades glabrous to short thin glandular- pubescent above, glandular-pubescent below, margin ciliate, the hairs short-conical; peduncles 2-45 mm long, sparsely to moderately glandular-pubescent; bracts lanceolate to ovate, somewhat attenuate, 3-9 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, glabrous to glandular pubescent, margins ciliate; receptacles flat with pedicel-like projections to 1.5 mm long; flowers 5-15 per inflorescence; perianth tube 6-18 mm long, greenish to pink, sparsely to moderately glandular-pubescent basally to puberulent above; perianth limbs 3-4 mm diameter, lobes 4-5, inconspicuous, lobe tips shallowly emarginate to nearly truncate, green to pink, glabrous; stamens 3-5; anthocarps usually 3-winged, infrequently 2- or 4-winged, 10-20 mm long, 10-18 mm wide, exterior of body often spongy, interior indurate, longitudinal ribs between wings lacking or 1-3, often inconspicuous, body puberulent to short glandular-pubescent, wings glabrous, wing margins usually ciliate with short conical hairs; achenes elliptic- oblong, 6-8 mm long, light brown to straw color.

description: Branches 1.2-7 dm long; petioles 0.5-4 cm long; leaf blades 1-4.5 cm long, 1-3.5 cm wide; peduncles 2-8.5 cm long; bracts 2.5-9 mm long, 1-2.5 mm wide; perianth tube 1-2 cm long, limbs seldom over 1.5 cm wide; anthocarps 5-8 mm long, 4-13 mm wide, body rugose, often appearing pitted; achenes 2.5-4 mm long, medium to dark brown.

description: Rhizoma erectum, tuberosum, per tempus vegetativum stolones producens. Folia subcoriacea, late ovata vel suborbicularia, integerrima, glabra, supra viridia, in speciminibus siccis punctis stellatis et ex trichosclereidibus interioribus elevatis omata; venatione in centro folii radiata et subtus subimpressa. Flores natantes, noctumi, perianthio intemo cum staminibus spiraliter disposito, praeter sepala et petala extema non distincte verticillato; sepala flavovirentia, coriacea, plerumque maculis paucis et parvis linearibus nigris sparsa; petala 8-14, alba vel ebumea, chartacea, abrupte in stamina transeuntia; stamina 80-130, ebumea, filamentis atropurpureis, extema apiculis brevibus 2 mm superantibus; carpella 20-28, processubus ebumeis basi in dorso purpureis, lingulatis, 5-14 mm longis.
bibliographicCitation: Wiersema, John H. 1984. Systematics of Nymphaea subgenus Hydrocallis (Nymphaeaceae). I. Four new species from the neotropics. Brittonia. 36: 213-222.

description: Rhizome erect, ovoid to subglobose, tuberous, sprouting freely, often stolon-forming throughout vegetative period. Leaf blades subcoriaceous, broadly ovate to suborbicular, to 25 cm long, to 21 cm wide, 1-1.3 times as long as wide, entire, rounded at apex, peltate 1-6 mm from base of sinus, the sinus 0.37-0.45 times length of blade, the lobes rounded or with small obtuse protuberance; upper surface green, when dried ornate with star-shaped expressions of underlying tricho-sclereids, also impregnated with acicular sclereids; undersurface red to reddish purple, glabrous; venation radiate but scarcely evident centrally, somewhat impressed, the principal veins 15-21. Petioles to 6 mm in diam, glabrous, with 2, 4, or 6 major air canals. Peduncles to 7 mm in diam, glabrous, with an inner ring of 5-6 major air canals surrounded by 10-12 minor ones. Flowers floating, opening nocturnally, the inner parts spirally arranged, except sepals and outer petals not in distinct whorls; sepals 4, yellowish green, sometimes flecked with black, subcoriaceous, ovate, 5-8 cm long, 1.5-3.1 cm wide, acute to rounded at apex, impregnated with acicular sclereids, inconspicuously nerved; petals 8-14, creamy-white, chartaceous, with lacework venation, acicular sclereids present but often inconspicuous, the outer petals shorter than sepals, with apex rounded or somewhat acute, the inner 4-7 cm long, 1.3-2.7 cm wide, acute to acuminate; transition to stamens abrupt; stamens 80-130, creamy-white with dark purple filaments, impregnated with acicular sclereids, the outermost to 5.6 cm long, with filaments to 9 mm wide and connectives prolonged 2 mm or more beyond anthers, the inner with filaments to 1.8 mm wide and connectives 0.5-1 mm or more beyond anthers, the inner anthers 0.7-0.8 times as long as stamen; carpels 20-28, the appendages creamy-white with purplish base abaxially, lingulate, 5-14 mm long, to 2 mm wide at base; stigmatic rays not impregnated with acicular sclereids, the papillae cells remaining attached; axial process ca 1 mm long and blunt. Fruits unknown except from type collection; seeds 1.05-1.20 mm long, 0.80-0.90 mm in diam, 1.3 times as long as broad, finely ruminate, with longitudinal rows of short hairs 30-70 µm long.

description: Arbor ripicola glabra usque ad 20 m. alta; ramulis subteretibus rugosis fuscis; foliis prope apicem ramulorum confertis, stipulis jam delapsis; petiolis rugulosis 5-8 mm. longis supra complanatis basi incrassatis; laminis coriaceis obovato-oblongis, 8-14 cm. longis, 4-6 cm. latis, apice profunde (ca. 5 mm.) emarginatis, margine integris paullo incrassatis callosis, basi cuneato-attenuatis, costa utrinque prominente, venulis lateralibus creberrime parallelis sub angulo 60-70° divergenti-bus utrinque levissime prominulis; pedunculis paucis ex axillis, 3-4 cm. longis, 2-4-floris; pedicellis prope apicem aggregatis 10-15 mm. longis, 1-3 mm. supra basin articulatis; sepalis 5 in fructu juvenili erectis coriaceis oblongis, 20-23 mm. longis, 5-6 mm. latis, acutis, basi paullo angustatis, integris, longitudinaliter striatis; petalis et stamini-bus desinentibus; fructu capsulari bivalvi ellipsoideo vel fere obovoideo, 40 mm. longo, 25 mm. diametro, apice rotundato et breviter apiculato, ruguloso, pericarpio lignoso 3 mm. crasso; seminibus numerosis parie-talibus brunneis oblongo-obovoideis rugosis in sicco 8 mm. longis.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description: Arbor glabra ad 20 m. alta, trunco ad 20 cm. diametro; ramulis teretibus rugosis, internodiis 1.5-3 cm. longis; petiolis rugosis sulcatis 5-8 mm. longis; laminis valde coriaceis oblongo-ovatis, 7-11 cm. longis, 2.5-4.5 cm. latis, basi acutis, apice obtuse acuminatis, margine integris et leviter revolutis, supra nitidis, costa subtus prominente, nervis lateralibus patulis cum venulis supra planis subtus prominulis; fructis valde numerosis; pedicellis fructiferis gracilibus 4-5 mm. longis; calyce fructifero erecto coriaceo plicato drupae longitudinem superante, 15-20 mm. radio, 5-lobato, lobis obtusis 5-7 mm. longis; drupa globoso-ellipsoidea, circiter 7x8 mm., longitudinaliter striata, apice acuta.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description: Frutex glaber 6 m. altus; ramulis gracilibus teretibus striatis; peti-olis gracilibus minute alatis 10-15 mm. longis; laminis papyraceis elliptico-oblongis, 13-22 cm. longis, 4-9 cm. latis basi attenuatis, apice breviter acuminatis, margine leviter revolutis; costa supra leviter ele-vata subtus prominente, nervis secundariis utroque 6-9 arcuato-ad-scendentibus utrinque cum venulis reticulatis prominulis; inflores-centiis axillaribus; floribus 2-6-fasciculatis, bracteolis minutis papyraceis subtentis; pedicellis 1-2 mm. longis; calyce erecto-patente 1 mm. longo, limbo minute 5- vel 6-dentato; petalis 5 vel 6 submembranaceis lanceolato-ovatis, 4-5 mm. longis, 1-1.5 mm. latis, basi connatis, apice acutis et leviter recurvatis, intus hispidulosis; staminibus 10 vel 12 alternatim inaequalibus; filamentis gracilibus glabris circiter 1 mm. longis; antheris subglobosis 0.4 mm. diametro; ovario globoso striato glabro sub anthesi 1 mm. diametro, loculis 3, 1-ovulatis; stylo carnoso quam ovario paullo breviore; pedicellis fructiferis ad 4 mm. longis; calyce fructifero coriaceo crasso parvo, circiter 2 mm. radio, margine subintegro; drupa ellipsoidea, ad 11 mm. longa et 7 mm. lata, apice mucronulata; pericarpio tenui.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.

description: Arbor parva, ramulis crassis glabris rugulosis; foliis magnis rigide coriaceis ubique glabris; petiolis crassis ca. 5 mm longis, 3 mm crassis rugulosis; laminis oblongis vel ovato-oblongis 10-13 cm longis, 5-6.5 cm latis, ad basin rotundatis vel obtusis, ad apicem rotundatis, plusminusve emarginatis usque ad paullo angustatis, supra lucidis, subtus pallidis; marginibus integris, revolutis; venis lateralibus utroque latere 6-10; inflorescentiis racemoso-paniculatis, ca. 2 cm longis glabris, floribus ca. 10; calyce cupuliforme glabro; corolla ca. 1 cm longa, extus glabra, intus versus basin dense longe-pilosa; antheris ca. 1.3 mm longis latisque; staminodiis ca. 4.3 mm longis bipartitis; pileo ovarii ca. 0.5 mm alto tomentuloso; stylo praeter basin glabro; stigma capitata 3-lobulata.
bibliographicCitation: Monachino, Joseph V. 1961. A new Liriosma [crassa] from Roraims. Brittonia. 13: 113-115.

description: Branchlets comparatively thick (3-4 mm), subterete, obtusely angled; tissue of the lower side of the blades with microscopic dots, the midrib raised on the upper side, rugulose, glabrous, the lateral nerves straight, spreading-ascending, connected by an arching submarginal nerve, the veinlets obscure; inflorescence axillary, the rachis slightly geniculate; pedicels 4-5 mm long; calyx merging into the pedicel at the base, truncate above, the free part a shallow margiln, 2-2.4 mm wide; corolla carnose; lobes 6, valvate, forming a tube in the lower one-third, easily separating into 3 segments, the upper two-thirds of the lobes eventually spreading, ligulate, 1.3 mm wide, glabrous, lightly concave within, the apex eucullate, short-beaked; stamens 3, inserted one-third the way up from the base of the corolla; filaments free for about 1 mm, pilose; anthers broadly oval, sparsely pilose on the back; staminodes 6, their filaments free for about 1 mm, pilose, the anther-homologue membranaceous, spatulate, 2.7 mm long, bipartite, slightly lobed at the base; ovary inferior, 3-locular; ovules solitary in each cell, pendulous from the apex, tapering-conic or carrot- shaped, about 1.3 mm long, the ovary-cap (free apex of ovary) convex, 0.5 mm high, puberulent-tomentulose; style 2.7 mm long, the stigma microscopically papillose.
bibliographicCitation: Monachino, Joseph V. 1961. A new Liriosma [crassa] from Roraims. Brittonia. 13: 113-115.

description: Annual, or especially in the southern part of its range, persistent and woody at the base, nmostly 2-12 dm high, openly branched, the stems glabrous but more uisually with some, or sometimes with many, spreading stiff hairs, occasionally coarse and angled; leaves opposite or alternate, ovate to lance-ovate, more or less acuminate, closely and finely serrulate, with about 7-11 main veins on each side of the midrib, glabrous to quite pubescent with rather coarse hairs, subsessile or the petioles up to 4 cm long, the blades mostly 1.5-5 (-10) cm long, only gradually reduced up the stem, the uppermost passing into leafy then subulate bracts; inflorescence rather short, simple, or more usually of several racem es in an open panicle, subglabrous or usually strigulose; pedicels filiform, mostly 1-2 cm long; sepals dark red, glabrous to setulose, lance-linear, 4-6 mm long; petals whitish to pinkish, the 2 upper linear- to oblong-spatulate, with a pair of short flaring lobes and 2 tubercles at the base of the blade, the claw glabrous; 2 lower petals 5-8 mm lono, long-clawed, with rounded to spatulate blades; sterile stamen purplish or reddish, shorter, more or less emarginate; fertile stamen about 4 mm long, with stout filament; capsule subglobose, 2-3 mm in diameter; seeds dark, tubereled, about 0.6-0.7 mm long.

description: Shrub 3-18 dm high, the branches slender, glabrous to hirsute-pubescent; leaves opposite or alterinate, lailce-ovate to ovate, subacuminate, scarcely serru- late, with about 6-7 veins on each side of the midrib, subglabrous to pubeseeiat especially on veins beneath, the blades mostly 1.5-4.5 cm lolng, 1-2.3 cm broad, on petioles 0.5-1 cm long; racemes short (the flowers crowded), mostly less than 1 dm long, in terminal panicles, subglabrous to strigulose to setulose; pedicels aseendinoi to spreadinig, 1-1.5 cm long; sepals reddish, lance-linear, 5-6 mm long; petals whitish to pink, the upper linear-spatulate, 4-5 mm lolig, bitubereulate below the 2-horned base of the blade, the claw glabrous; lower petals clawed about two-thirds their length, thefn suborbicular; sterile stamen white to pinkish, 4-5 mm long, the obovate blade about one-half the total length; fertile stamen with the filament broadenied toward the base; stigma coneavo-capitate; capsule subglobose, 2.5-3 mm in diameter; seeds brown, about 1 mm long, tubercled.

description: Shrubby, 1-2 m high, subglabrous to more or less pubeseent, from a tuberous root and with thickish rather fleshy branches; leaves mostly opposite, lance- ovate to elliptic-ovate, gradually narrowed at both ends, the blades 5-16 cm long, 2-6 cm broad, serrulate, subglabrous to more or less pnbeseenit, especially on the veins beneath, acuminate, with 15-25 main veilns oin each side of the midrib, somewhat paler beneath; petioles 0.5-3 cm long; stipules modified into red pyramidal glands; infloreseence corymbose-paniculate, sparsely strigfose, 1.5-3 cm long; bracts foliose, mostly 1-5 cm lonog; pedicels ascending, 1-4 cm long; flowers deep rose; floral tube scarcely developed; sepals 4, lanceolate, divergent, subglabrous, 15-20 mm long; petals 4, the 2 upper oblong-lanceolate, equaling the sepals, the blades asymmetrical at the base, clawed but inot glandular-tuberculate, the 2 lower oblong-ovate, erose somewhat shorter and narrowed to a clawlike base; fertile stamen about as long as the shorter petals, the filament fleshy and the anther bluish-purple; sterile stamen linear-oblong, petaloid, erisped at the margin; style about as long, hairy near base; stigma depressed-capitate; capsule subglobose, 6-9 mnm in diameter, 4-valved; seeds numerous, in 2 rows in each locule, muricate-rugulose, ovoid dark, scarcely 1 mm long.

description: Apparently fruticose, 1.5 m tall, the twigs slender, simple, densely strigose; leaves opposite, the upper sessile or short-petioled, densely strigose, ovate to broadly lanceolate, acute, serrulate, 1.5-3.5 cm long; inflorescence terminal, laxly racemose-paniculate, subglabrous; bracts 4-10 mm long, subulate to lance-linear; pedicels filiform, 1-2 cm long; floral tube scarcely evident; sepals about 8-10 mm lonu, linear-lanceolate, subglabrous, red; petals red, clawed, the upper spatulate, about 8-9 mm long, 3 mm wide, with 2 glandular disks above the claw; lower petals about 7 mm lonig, with suborbicular blade, suberenulate; sterile stamen narrowly lanceolate, 8 mm long; fertile stamen 6.5 mm long, the anther 2-4 mm long; style about 2 milm long; capsule globose, about 5 mm in diameter; seeds many, brownish when immature, about 1 mm long, densely short-papillose.

description: Erect annual, branched, the stems slender, somewhat angled, 1.5-5 dm tall, glabrous or with a few scattered long hairs; leaves well distributed, lance-ovate to ovate, subglabrous, the blades subentire, mostly 1-4.5 cm long, 0.4-2.4 cm broad, acute to acuminate, with 3-6 main veins on each side of the midrib; petioles 0.2-1 cm long; infloreseence of long mostly simple racemes with the foliage leaves at base gradually giving way to lanceolate leafy bracts and then to subulate bracts 4-5 mm long; pedicels spreading, filiform, 1-2.5 cm long; sepals deep red, linear-oblong, 3-5 mm long; upper petals oblong-linear, pinkish?, bituberculate above the glaberous claws; lower petals about 4-5 mm long, with orbicular limb and narrow claws; sterile stamen 3-5 mm long, the upper part obcordate, pale; fertile stamnen about 3 mm long, the filament somewhat dilated; capsule rounded-obovoid, with subeuneate base and 4 flaring horns at the summit between the valves, 3-5 mm in diameter (about 3 mm in Palmer 367, 4-5 mm in Pringle 10103); seeds brown, tubercled.
bibliographicCitation: Munz, Philip A. 1961. The Lopezieae (Onagraceae). Brittonia. 13 (1): 73-90.

description: Perennial, from a large woody-fleshy root; stems angled, glabrous, openly bralnched, 3-10 dm long; leaves ovate to round-ovate, alternate or the lowest opposite, shallowly serrulate, gradually narrowed apically and acute, rounded at base, glabrous or sometimes strigulose on the midrib, with about 4-5 veins on each side of the midrib; petioles slender, mostly 2-17 mm long, strigulose at base; leaves gradually reduced up the stem to subulate or lanceolate bracts 2-10 mm long; inflorescence racemose or more or less open-paniculate, more or less strigulose; pedicels ascending, 1-2 cm long; flowers pale purplish red, the petals with dark red bands and white tips; sepals oblong-linlear, 5-7 mm long, 1-2 mmn broad, glabrous to finiely puberulent; upper petals 4-7 mm long, clawed for about one-third their length, unituberculate, with long curly hairs on the linear part below the expanded white summit; lower petals linear, slightly shorter, with long slender hairs almost throughout; sterile stamen not hairy, 4-5 mm long, reddish throughout; fertile stamen not hairy, the anther almost 2 mm long; style with lonog slenlder hairs; capsule ovoid-globose, 4.5-6.5 mm in diameter, subglabrous to puberulent; seeds black, the body subovoid, papillose-tubercled, broadly winged, about 1 mm long.

description: Strigose annual 2-5 dm tall, freely branched; leaves ovate, sparsely strigulose, sessile or subsessile, cuneate at base or narrowed, then with subparallel sides near base, acute at apex, shallowly serrulate, 1-4 cm long, 0.7-2.4 cm broad, with about 6-12 veins oln each side of the midrib; ilnfloreseence a diffuse open paniele with slender branehes; bracts subulate to lanice-linear, mostly 1-10 mm long,; pedicels filiform, purplish, ascending, 10-15 mm long; flowers purplish red; sepals linear, about 4 long long; 2 upper petals linear-oblong, about 5 mm lono, each with a single glalnd at the base of the blade, this gland or tuberele surrounded by short clavate hairs; 2 lower petals spreading laterally, obovate, tapering into slender claws; sterile stamen 3-4 mm long, with a terminial triangular-obovate blade; fertile stamen about 3 mm long; stigma sub-capitate; capsule globose, 3-3.5 mm in diameter; seeds about 1 mm long.

description: Erect slender-stemmed annuals, usually with aseending branches through-out, rarely almost simple, 1-3.5 dm tall, quite glabrous throughout; leaves opposite or alternate, suberect, well distributed; petioles 1-8 mm long; blades lanceolate, entire, acute at base, almost obtuse at apex, 0.5-2.5 cm long, 0.1-0.5 cm broad, the uppermost reduced to narrow bracts; flowers rather numerous in terminal racemes 2-10 cm long; pedicels capillary, aseending to spreading, 8-15 mm long; sepals purplish, 2.5-3 mm long, laneeolate, reflexed separately in anthesis; petals white, the 2 lower 3-4 mm long, orbicular-obovate, narrowed into a slender claw, the 2 upper about as long, clawed, the blades lance-oblong, with a reddish transverse blotch and a green "eye" just below the bar; fertile stameni about 2 mm long; sterile stanmen somewhat longer, white, deeply ob- cordate; style slender, about as lono as the petals; stigma subglobose; capsule about 2 mm long, subglobose, 4-angled, tapering at base; seeds dark brown, narrowly obovoid, tuberculate-roughenled, about 1 mm long.

description: Apparently mostly perennial, becoming more or less suffrutescent at base, the basal branches decumbent and sometimes rooting, then erect, 1-6 dm long, slender, leafy, sparingly and rather coarsely strigose; leaves mostly alternate, sometimes with axillary fascicles, lanceolate, the blades gradually narrowed at both ends, acuminate, 1-5 cm long, 0.2-1.2 cm broad, remotely serrulate to sub-entire, sparingly strigose, on petioles 0.2-1.5 cm long; leaves gradually reduced up the stems; flowers white with red streaks, solitary in the upper axils, forming leafy racemes; pedicels ascending, slender, 1.5-3 cm long; sepals red, lanceolate, 5-7 mm long, the lower one quite free, the 3 upper more or less united to each other and to the 2 upper deeply laciniate striped whitish obovate petals; middle upper sepal with a large gland above the base within; 2 lower petals linear-oblong, entire, about 5 mm long, slightly emarginate; sterile stamhen straight, narrow, about 3 mm long and attached to the inner base of the lower sepal; fertile stamen slightly shorter, the anther roulnded, ca. 1 mm long; style 3-4 mm long, with capitate stigma; capsule roun-ded-obovate, 3-4 mm in diameter, 4-valvate; seeds compressed, black, tubereled, about 0.6 mm long.

description: Annual, erect, more or less diffusely branched throughout, 3-6 dm tall, from almost glabrous throughout to finely and inconspicuously glandular-puberulent and with scattering longer stiff hairs; leaves alternate or the lower opposite, mostly oni the lower half of the plant; petioles very slender, 5-20 mm long, more or less pilose; blades ovate, coarsely serrate, subglabrous to somewhat pilose, acute to acuminate, mostly rather thin, 2-5 cm long, 0.5-2.5 cm wide, the upper- most reluced to lance-linear bracts; racemes terminal, pedunculate, 5-30 cm long; pedicels filiform, ascending, commonly 1-2.5 cm long; sepals deep pink, about 5 mm long, lanceolate, the lower one free, the other 3 united one-third to one-half their length and with a yellowish gland on the basal part of the central one; petals pink, the 2 lower broadly obovate, about 5 mm long, tapering to a narrow base, the 2 upper borne in the 3 upper sepals, about 3 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, somewhat clawed at base but without glands at the summit of the claw; fertile stamen about 1.5 mm long; sterile stamen slightly longer, reddish, embracing the style which is about as long, with small terminal "cup-shaped" stigma; capsule cylindric-clavate, mostly 8-10 mm long, 1.5 mm thick, 4-valved at summit; seeds many, obovoid, ca. 0.5 mm long, brown, miniutely tubercled.

description: Epiphytes, 20-40 cm tall. Pseudobulbs aggregate, conic, dark green, 3.5-7 X 1.4-2.6 cm. Leaves lanceolate, membranaceous to subcoriaceous, 14.7-30 X 3-5 cm, pseudo-petiole 3-10.5 cm long. Inflorescence 3-5 flowered, erect, 12-38 cm long; scape bracts 1-1.5 X 0.5-0.6 cm, floral bracts 0.3-0.5 X 0.1-0.2 cm. Flowers with a subtle fragrance, white on the exterior, pink to white on the interior, labellum with pink to red stripes, 2.2-2.3 cm long, 1.2-1.5 cm wide. Sepals ovate, truncate, dorsal sepal 1.2-2 X 0.4-1 cm, lateral sepals parallel to each other, 1.1-1.7 X 0.5-0.9 cm, spur with sepal segments superposed, 0.4-0.6 cm long. Petals ovate, entire to 3-lobed, oblique to column, 1.2-1.7 X 0.5-1 cm. Labellum 3-lobed, obovate, puberulous, with irregularly crenate margins, 1.2-2 X 1-2.1 cm when expanded, lateral lobes oblong, involute, midlobe strongly emarginate, recurved, the claw 0.1-0.3 cm long, the callus 0.4-0.8 cm long, puberulous, on the anterior region 3-lobed, glabrous to puberulous. Column puberulous to pubescent, 0.5-0.7 cm, the foot straight, glabrous to puberulous, 0.4-1 cm long. Anther 0.15-0.2 X 0.15-0.2 cm, the pollinia rounded, the stipe forked, 0.1-0.15 cm long, the viscidium truncate, 0.05 X 0.1 cm long. Ovary-pedicel 1.5-2.8 cm long.

description: Malaxi tipuloides (Lindl.) Kuntze var. exigua Garay was recognized as a variety based on its flowers being much smaller than those of the type variety, as suggested by the varietal epithet (from the Latin exiguus, small, short, poor, scanty; Brown, 1953, p. 311). The plant and inflorescence of the type material of M. tipuloides var. exigua are of about the same dimensions as that of the type of Microstylis tipuloides Lindl. [Colombia. Popayin on Pacific slope, K. T Hartweg s.n., holotype K-Lindley, photo = Crossoglossa tipuloides (Lindl.) Dodson] and of other material referable to the species, but a close examination reveals important difference in the size of the flowers and shape of the leaves (summarized in Table II). Furthermore, C. tipuloides is a species form the western slope of the Andes ranging from Cosat rica southward to Ecuador while the var. exigua is an entity from the Eastern Cordillera of the Andes. Thus, we propose to treat the var. exigua as a distinct species.

description: Liana or shrubs with old stems suberous, young stems short-tomentose, the trichomes 0.3 mm long. Petioles 2-7.5 cm, tomentose, bearing in the lower half of the petiole a pair of sessile, discoid, black nectaries 0.8-1.1 mm diam. Stipules 3-3.9 mm long, linear, pilose, deciduous. Leaf blades (obscurely) 3-lobed or entire and elliptic (sometimes the two leaf types in the same individual); margin revolute; abaxial surface villous; adaxial surface lustrous, the nerves impressed, velutinous; entire leaf blades 3.5-5 X 2-3 cm, the apex emarginate to acute, mucronulate; lobed leaf blades 2.5-5.4 X 3-4.5 cm, lobed for 38-60% the distance to the base, the base subcordate to rounded, the angles between midvein of lateral lobes 60º-100º; central lobes 1.9-3 X 1.3-2 cm; lateral lobes 0.5-1.5 X 0.8-1 cm. Peduncle 1.1-3 cm long, articulate at 4-5 mm from flower base. Bracts 6-7 X 2-6 mm, narrow-elliptic to elliptic; margin lacerate; abaxial surface tomentose; adaxial surface glabrous. Flower solitary, 3.2-4 cm diam.; floral tube 1.4-1.8 X 0.5-0.6 cm, tubular, sometimes slightly dilated at base, glabrous, red; sepals 1.9-2.3 X 0.5-0.6 cm, glabrous, red, the awn pilose, 3 mm long; petals 1.8 X 0.4 cm, red; corona in 3 series, the 2 outer series of filaments 4.5-6 mm long, subfalcate, dull red, the in- ner series of filaments 3-3.4 mm long, linear, flat, sometimes connate, whitish; operculum 4.2-4.6 mm, inserted at base of floral tube, erect, membranous, the margin denticulate; limen ca. 3 mm; gynophore 2.8-3.2 cm long, green; filaments 7 mm long, red; anthers 5 mm long, red; ovary 4 mm long, ellipsoid, glabrous; styles 5-6 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Vitta, Fabio A. & Bernacci, Luís C. 2004. A new species of Passiflora in section Tetrastylis (Passifloraceae) and two overlooked species of Passiflora from Brazil. Brittonia. 56 (1): 89-95.

description: Calyx cup-shaped at the base, abruptly expanding above into an expansive flange (fig. 12), up to 2 cm wide, with spreading, obtuse lobes, ridged-reticulate inside the tube with small, regular, square to rectangular spaces between the ridges, the lobes reddish-brown inside, each with usually 5 colorless stripes lengthwise; peduncles relatively long, up to 4 cm. Leaf-blades triangular to broadly triangular, subhastate at the base. The only species having triangular leaves which is ridged-reticulate within the calyx-tube (fig. 12). Type locality: near Booth, Autauga Co., Alabama.

description: Folia cordata, 3.2-5.8 cm longa, 3-5.8 cm lata, apicibus obtusis, lobis sinuus basalaris non superpositis, non variegata. description: Low, evergreen, aromatic herb; rhizome short with scale leaves. Petioles ca 12 cm long, blades glabrous, cordate, 3.2-5.8 cm long, 3-5.8 cm wide, not variegated, the apex obtuse, the sinuses of the lobes not overlapping at the base of the leaf. Flowers solitary; pedicels 1.5-3 cm long; calyces rhombic-ovate to rhombic-urceolate, broadest at the middle, (14) 16-24 (27) mm long, 12-19 mm in diameter, dark purple to whitish on the outside above the base, dark purple to light purple at the middle, the lobes (3) 4-6 (7) mm long, dark purple to white on the outside, dark purple with white spots on the inside; corolla lobes absent. Stamens sessile, 3-4 mm long, with anther connectives extending slightly longer than the anthers. Ovary superior. Styles 3-4 mm long, exserted 2-3 mm beyond the stigma, and divided 1-1.5 mm at the apex. Stigmas round.

description: Leaf-blades generally of a triangular-sagittate to -subhastate type, less commonly ovate-sagittate, and rarely deltoid, subcordate or subrotund, 16-20 cm long by 5-15 cm broad in the widest part, the sides straight to convex with or without low shoulders, rarely concave, the basal lobes relatively broad and long, commonly one-third the length of the blade, rarely almost absent in deltoid forms, rounded at the apices, commonly variegated with light green areas between the principal veins. Calyces narrowly to broadly flask-shaped with prominent, more or less spreading lobes, or ovate with short, erect lobes, the tubes 1.2-2.8 cm long by 6-12 mm wide in the widest part before maturity of the ovary. Stamens sessile or with very short filaments, the anther-connective extending into a short (0.5 mm), blunt appendage. Style-extensions above the stigmas bifid to the stigmas, the lobes divergent at anthesis, the stigmas often extending inward between the lobes. Ovaries ca. one-third inferior.

description: Calyx cylindric to cylindro-campanulate, thin-walled, with a flare about the middle, greenish-grey on the outside with purplish specks and purplish stripes, the tube 1.5-1.8 (1.7) cm long, with numerous longitudinal ridges inside, the lobes rounded-deltoid, 10-17 mm long by 10-17 mm wide at the base, commonly strongly spreading but sometimes recurved or incurved at the tips, usually with wavy margins, dark purplish-red on the inside, marked with colorless spots, bearing relatively long, whitish hairs. Anthers essentially sessile, the connective pro- longed into a short, blunt appendage. Ovary wholly superior, about 14-20 mm high and about 10 mm in diameter at antheses. Styles about 4 mm long, the ex- tensions above the stigmas shallowly divided at the apex. Leaves scattered or 2-several grouped, the blades triangular-cordate, cordate, orbicular-cordate or retuse, the sinuses broad, the variegation extending to the anastomosing veins; petioles puberulent on the sides. Rhizomes of two kinds, some long and slender with long internodes, others short and flower-bearing (figs. 4, 15, 21, 28).

description: Calyx cylindric with a slight flare in the upper part of the tube, slightly contracted above this, thick-walled, dark brown, the tube 1-1.4 cm long by 1.2 cm wide, ridged-reticulate inside the lower part of the tube with a close, more or less irregular network of short, ca. 3.5 mm long Anthers essentially sessile connective not prolonged. Ovary ca. one-third inferior. Styles 3 mm long, the extensions above the stigmas notched at the apex. Leaf-blades cordate with mostly rounded apices to orbicular-cordate or retuse (figs. 5, 16, 22, 31, 34).

description: Calyx campanulate-urceolate, pale brown with brownish spots to dark reddish- brown, thin-walled, mostly relatively large, the tube 1.5-4 cm long and to 2 cm wide at the widest part, ridged-reticulate inside the lower part with vertical ridges which are joined by horizontal ridges from which shorter ridges of various lengths extend into the square to more or less rectangular spaces between; lobes large., spreading, up to 1 cm long by 2 cm wide at the base, reddish-brown to purplish inside with colorless spots. Anthers sessile, ca. 3 ca. 3 mm long, the connection prolonged into a very short, blunt appendage. Ovary wholly superior, slightly contracted below the stamens, and grooved between projected areas below the anthers. Styles relatively long, 3-4 mm, the extensions above the stigmas relatively long and slender, notched at the apex. Leaves very variable in size, the blades cordate, with acute to obtuse apices, to orbicular-cordate, the basal lobes sometimes overlapping over the petiole, often variegated. Rhizomes usually short and thick, but slender rhizomes sometimes present (figs. 2. 13, 19, 27, 36).

description: Calyx cylindraceous with a slight flare in the upper part of the tube, relatively thin-walled, 0.8-1.5 (1.15) cm long, ridged-reticulate inside the tube with widely spaced vertical ridges joined by a more or less irregular network of low, rounded ridges; the lobes relatively long, 0.7-1(0.87) cm long by 0.6-1(0.8) cm wide, spreading. Anthers 2.5-3 mm long, sessile or with very short filaments, the con- nective slightly prolonged. Ovary essentially superior. Styles 3-3.5 mm long, the apices acute to obtuse, to orbicular-cordate, rarely retuse, the surface mostly smooth, rarely rugose, not often variegated, the basal lobes often overlapping over the petiole (figs. 3, 14, 20, 29, 37).

description: Folia cordata vel orbiculari-cordata, ca. 4-5.75 cm longa 4-5.5 cm lata, apicibus obtusis, sinibus latis vel angustis, variegata. Calyces parvi, cylindrici, 1.2-1.3 cm longi per axim, 6-7 mm per diametrum, hepaticolores vel ad super hasim pallidi; lobi non maculati, 5.5 mm longi, 7 mm lati ad basim. Stamina sessilia, conjunctionibus antherarum in appendices non protractis, 1.61-1.84 mm longa. Ovarium ca. '2 inferius. Styli ca. 2.5 mm longi. super stigma ca. 0.75 mm exserti, et in apices 0.25 mm divisi.

description: Leaf-blades cordate to orbicular-cordate, 4-5.75 cm long by 4-5.5 cm wide, the apices obtuse, the sinuses broad to narrow, the lobes rarely overlapping, usually variegated along the principal veins. Petioles averaging 10.5 cm long. Rhizomes short and moderately branching. Calyces relatively small, brown, the tube cylindric, slightly narrowing upward, 7 mm long by 6.5 mm in diameter, sometimes pale brown above the base, the lobes relatively large, flaring at the base, 7 mm wide at the base by 5.5 mm long, moderately spreading, without colorless spots inside. Stamens essentially sessile, those opposite the styles conspicuously shorter than the alternating ones, 1.61-1.84 mm long, the anther-connective not prolonged into an appendage. Ovary ca. 1/2 inferior. Styles ca. 2.5 mm long, ex- tending 0.75 mm above the stigma, only notched at the apex. liature seeds not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Blomquist, Hugo L. 1957. A revision of Hexastylis of North America. Brittonia. 8: 255-281.

description: Folia lato- vel orbiculari-cordata, ca. 6.5 cin longa, 5.5 cm lata, apicibus obtusis (raro acutis) vel retusis, sinibus latis vel angustis, non variegata. Calyces anguste vel late ampulliformes, 1.5-2.75 cm longi per axim, 1.2-1.7 cm per diametrum, conspicue super basim coarctati; extrinsecus super basim pallidi et subflavi, media parte hepaticolores, et superiore parte flavi des maculis purpureis notati; tubulus calycis intrinsecus hepaticolor, et infra parce rugoso-reticulatus; lobi calycis intrinsecus subflavi, maculis vel areolis subalbidis notati. Stamina sessilia, conjunctionibus antherarum in brevis appendices obtusos, 0.5 mm longos protractis. Ovarium ca. 1/3 inferius. Styli ca. 3 mm longi, super stigma ca. 1 mm exserti, et in apice 0.5 mm divisi.

description: Leaf-blades broadly- to orbicular-cordate, averaging 6.5 cm long by 5.5 cm broad, the apices obtuse (rarely acute) to retuse, the sinuses broad to narrow with lobes sometimes overlapping over the petiole, scabridulous at the base on the gated. Petioles averaging 12 cm long, Rhizomes short and freely branching. Calyces broadly flask-shaped, 1.5-2.75 cm long by 1.2-1-7 cm wide, prominently contracted above the base, expanded above this, then gradually narrowing upward to the base of the slightly spreading, acute to obtuse lobes, colored on the outside pale yellow above the base, purplish about the middle, fading upward to pale yellow with purplish spots, on the inside the tube purplish-brown and sparingly ridged-reticulate below, the lobes yellowish inside with purplish spots or areas and short-pilose. Stamens essentially sessile, the anther-connective prolonged into a blunt appendage ca. 0.5 mm long. Ovary ca. one-third inferior. Styles ca. 3 mm long, extending 1 mm above the stigma, divided at the apex 0.5 mm. Seeds 2-5 per locule, 4 mm long.

description: A caulescent, succulent, shrub-like, terrestrial herb, profusely branched, 0.8- 1.2 m tall, the main stem 4-9 mm diam, woody in appearance when dry, blackish, leaf scars prominent, epidermis early-exfoliating. Branchlets 3-5 mm diam, internodes 2-6 mm long, densely hirsute, with simple, uniseriate, 8- to 16-celled, rigid trichomes, 0.7-1 mm long, each with an oversize basal cell, glossy yellow when dry. Leaves alternate, clustered apically, short-petiolate, the thick petiole  0.8-1.2 mm long, densely hirsute. Lamina widely to narrowly elliptic-lanceolate (2.5) 3-4 (4.5) x 5-6 cm, apically short-acute to acuminate, basally cuneate, pinnately veined, the 2 or 3 pairs of secondary veins arising from the lower 1/3 of the midvein, obscure and sulcate above, prominent and raised beneath, the blade densely hirsute on both sides, glandular-dotted, thick, chartaceous and brownish when dry. Inflorescences conjugate, erect, on a common primary peduncle 1.5- 1.8 cm long, densely hirsute, bibracteate, the small bracts 0.1-0.2 mm long, opposite, bract scars prominent; secondary peduncles 0.5-0.7 cm long, sparsely hirsute; rachis 1. 5-2.5 cm long, 0. 1-0. 2 cm diam in fruit, partially obscured by the flowers, glandular-dotted, glabrous. Floral bracts orbicular, peltate, 0.6-0.8 mm diam, thick-chartaceous, glandular-dotted, glabrous, dark orange when dry. Flowers widely spaced; anthers 0.2-0.3 mm long; pistil with a subapical stigma. Fruit globose-ovoid, 1-1.2 mm diam with a short, chartaceous, oblique beak, the stigma on the center of the beak, glandular-dotted.
bibliographicCitation: Callejas, R. 1990. Studies in neotropical Piperaceae. II. Four new species and a new combination from Colombia and Peru. Brittonia. 42: 70-82.

description: Herba terrestris, caulescens, succulenta, profuse ramosa, florifera usque ad 0.8-1.2 m alta. Ramuli densi, hirsuti nigrescentes. Folia altema, petiolo brevi crasso, 0.8-1.2 m longo, lamina lanceolata angusta ve dilatatim elliptica, apice acuta vel breviter acuminata; venae sulcatae subter prominentes pinnatae, dense hirsutae. Inflorescentiae conjugatae e foliorum summorum axillis ortae. Pedunculus primarius bibracteatus, 1.5-1.8 cm longus, bracteis oppositis. Pedunculi secundarii 0.5-0.7 cm longi.
bibliographicCitation: Callejas, R. 1990. Studies in neotropical Piperaceae. II. Four new species and a new combination from Colombia and Peru. Brittonia. 42: 70-82.

description: Herba sat parva succulenta suberecta simplex; foliis alternis aggregatis oblique subrliombeis vel dolabriformis, apice abrupte faleatim acutis, basi acutis; petiolo brevi; spicis solitariis terminalibus; bracteis ovatis acutis peltatis; ovario ovoideo apice obliquo, stigmate subapicali.

description: A rather small, glabrous, somewhat granuate-papillate, succulent herb; stem unbranched, alQout 5 mm thick and abruptly ascending from a short-decumbent base, the leafy lower part about 10 cm long with very short internodes, terminating in an elongated, distantly-bracteate, spike-bearing part up to 30 cm or more long; leaves alternate, congested, obliquely subrhomboidal or dolabriform, abruptly and falcately acute at apex, acute at base, the lower ones up to 1.5 cm wide and 2 cm long, the upper 1 cm wide and 2 cm long, becoming narrowly lanceolate bracts on the elongated upper part; blades obscurely palmately 3-nerved, drying thick and opaque; petiole about 2 mm long, flattened, broader near the base; spike solitary, terminal, moderately to densely flowered, 2 mm thick and up to 20 cm long, the peduncle about 1 cm long, the floral bracts ovate, acute, peltate, the anthers oblong, versatile, the ovary ovoid with an obtusely oblique apex, the stigma comparatively large, 2 or 3-parted, promiliently ciliate; matured fruit not seen.

description: Frutex; internodiis superis sat crassis glabris; foliis elipticis, apice acuminatis, basi subaequilateris acutis utrinque glabris, marginaliter submarginaliterve conferte ciliolatis, a medio infero pinnatim venosis, venis utrinque 5 simplicibus; petiolo canaliculato ad basem vaginato; spicis rectis; pedunculo robusto, brevibus; bracteis rotundato- vel triangulari-subpeltatis margine conferte brunneo-fimbriatis; drupa oblongo-obovoidea apice puberula; stylo crasso brevi, stigmatibus linearibus coronatos.

description: An essentially glabrous, nodose shrub 3.5 m high; upper internodes moderately stout, longitudinally striate when dry, 3-5 cm long; leaves elliptic, acuminate at apex, subequilaterally acutely short-decurrent at base, glabrous on both sides but marginally and submarginally finely puberulous-ciliate above, finely glandular-dotted, 7-9 cm wide and 15-19 cm long, pinnately nerved from the lower half, the nerves 5 on each side, unbranched, with slender cross-connecting anastomosing nervules; blades drying chartaceous, subtranslucent, finely pellucid-dotted; petiole about 1 cm long, caiialiculate and ridged by the decurrent blade margins, vaginate at the base; spikes straight, 5 mm thick and 8-10 cm long, the peduncle stout, about 5 mm long, the bracts round, or triangular-subpeltate, the margin and pedicel strongly brown-fringed; fruit oblong-obovoid, strongly brown-hairy about the top, tapering into a short, stout style, the stigmas 3, linear, recurved, about as long as the style.
bibliographicCitation: Yuncker, Truman G. 1961. New taxa of Peruvian Piperaceae. Brittonia. 13: 58-63.

description: Frutex; internodiis superis gracilis villosis, pilis erectis albidis 1-2 mm longis; foliis oblongo- vel lanceolato-ellipticis, utrinque modice villosis, apice acuminatis, basi inaequilateraliter cordato-auriculatis, sinu obliquo, margine ciliatis, ad medium laminam pinnatim venosis, venis utrinque 5-6; petiolo usque ad laminam vaginato; bracteis triangulari-concavis; ovario ovoideo, stigmatibus parvis stylum sat longum fultis.
bibliographicCitation: Yuncker, Truman G. 1961. New taxa of Peruvian Piperaceae. Brittonia. 13: 58-63.

description: A slender-branched shrub 1.8 m high, the axes ancd leaves conspicuously soft-white-villous, the hairs 1-2 mm long, the upper internodes mostly 5-8 cm long; leaves oblong- or lance-elliptic, the apex acuminate, the base inequilaterally cordate-auriculate with oblique sinus, one side 1-2 mm shorter at the petiole and rounded, the longer side auriculate and covering the petiole, moderately villous on both sides, the hairs along the nerves erect, the margin ciliate throughout with erect hairs averaging about 5 per mm; blades pale glandular-dotted, drying membranous, translucent, finely pellucid-dotted, 3.5-5 cm wide and 11-14 cm long, pinnately nerved to about the middle, the nerves slender, 5 or 6 on each side plus one or two short nerves descending in the larger lobe; petiole 5-15 mm long, vaginate-winged to the blade, dilated and clasping at the base; spikes 4 mm thick and 15-18 mm long, the peduncle scarcely 1 cm long, dark-glandular-dotted, the bracts broadly triangular-concave, pilose on the upper concave side, glandular-dotted, the anthers apiculate, glandular-dotted, the ovary ovoid, tapering into a rather long, subulate, strongly glandular-dotted style, the stigmas 3, small.
bibliographicCitation: Yuncker, Truman G. 1961. New taxa of Peruvian Piperaceae. Brittonia. 13: 58-63.

description: Frutex; internodiis superis gracilis glabris; foliis elliptico-subovatis, apice acuminatis, basi inequilateris subauriculato-cordatis, supra scabridis hispidulis subtus ad venas conferte adpresse-pubeseentibus, margine conferte ciliatis, ad medium laminam pinnatim venosis, venis utrinque 8-9; spicis gracilibus, bracteis rotundato- vel triangulari-subpeltatis breviter fimbriatis; drupa oblongoobovoidea glabra; stigatibus parvis sessilibus.

description: A shrub 3-4 m high; upper internodes rather slender, 9-13 cm long, glabrous, longitudinally striate when dry, leaves pale glandular-dotted, somewhat obliquely elliptic-subovate, 5.5-7.5 cm wide and 12-17 cm long, minutely hispidulous and scabrid above, acuminate at apex, inequilaterally cordate at base with one side about 2 mm shorter at the petiole, the longer lobe subauriculate and covering the petiole; nerves beneath densely appressed-white-hairy, the nervules more thinly so or hispidulous; margin strongly ciliate with white, appressed hairs; blades pinnately nerved to about the middle, the nerves 8 or 9 oIn each side, unbranche'd, with one or two additional short nerves descending in the lobes, with slender cross-connecting anastomosing nervules; dry blades chartaceous, translucent, pellucid-dotted; petiole scarcely 2-3 plus 2 mm long, vaginate and dilated-clasping at the base, hispidulous; spikes scarcely 2 mm thick and 5-7 cm long, the peduncle slender, 15 mm long, glabreseent, the bracts round- or triangular-subpeltate, short-fringed, the fruit oblong-obovoid, somewhat wedge-shaped, glabrous, the stigmas small, sessile.
bibliographicCitation: Yuncker, Truman G. 1961. New taxa of Peruvian Piperaceae. Brittonia. 13: 58-63.

description: An erect or suberect branching herb; stem glabrous, 5 mm thick toward the base and with prominent leaf scars when dry, ascending to 20 or 30 cm, with slender flowering branches above, the internodes very short (2-3 mm) below, up to 4 or 5 cm on the upper branches; leaves alternate, elliptic-suboblanceolate, very variable in size, reduced upward, those on the basal part 1.5-2.5 cm wide and 4-6 cm long, those on the flowering branches 1 cm wide arnd 2 cm long or less; margin smooth or verrucosely uneven when dry; blades dry thin and translucent, palmately 5-nerved, the midrib and innermost pair of lateral nerves rather prominent, the outermost pair slender and inconspicuous, the nerves and midrib unbranched upward; petiole up to 3 cm long on the lower leaves, reduced upward, those on the upper flowering branches commonly less than 5 mm long, canaliculate, clasping-decurrent, the margins aijd decurrent ridges smooth or papillate-roughened; spikes terminal or in the axils of reduced bract-like uppermost leaves, 1-1.5 mm thick anld 4-6 cm long, the peduncle about 1 cm long, smooth or lineately papilate, the bracts roundpeltate, the fruit globose-ovoid, with thickened apical mammiform crown and subapical stigma.
bibliographicCitation: Yuncker, Truman G. 1961. New taxa of Peruvian Piperaceae. Brittonia. 13: 58-63.

description: Subshrub, 0.8-1 m tall, sparingly branched. Internodes 4 4.7 cm long, 3.5-4.5 mm diam, densely long-villous, covered by simple, uniseriately 10-1 5-celled, soft, flexible, white trichomes. Leaves long-petiolate, the petiole 3-4 cm long, densely long-villous, with prominent, caducous stipular margins that extend the full length of the petiole. Lamina elliptic-ovate to wide-ovate, 20-22 x 12-14 cm, apically shortly acute, basally obtuse to cordiform, the basal lobes shorter than the petiole; venation pinnate, the 9 or 10 pairs of major secondary veins arising throughout the length of the midvein, impressed above, raised beneath; blade dotted throughout with raised glands, glabrous above, densely short-pilose beneath along the veins, covered by 6-10-celled, rigid, branched, 2-4-armed, often Y- or T-shaped trichomes, pilose along the margins (trichomes branched), chartaceous when dry, dark green on both faces. Shoot apex at first enclosed within the sheathing leaf base at all nodes. Prophyll not seen. Inflorescence axillary, emerging from within the prophyll and free from the leaf base, erect at all stages, white in flower, green in fruit. Peduncle 2-2.6 cm long, 1.5-2 mm diam, ebracteate, densely long-villous. Rachis 2.1-4.3 cm long, 2.1-7.6 mm diam, obscured by the flowers, rigid, short- pilose. Floral bracts wide-deltate as seen from above, 0.5-1 mm wide, marginally short-fimbriate, centrally glabrous, not forming bands around the spike. Flowers tightly congested, tetramerous; anthers 0.2-0.3 mm broad and 0.1 mm long, laterally dehiscent, the connective protruding above the anthers and glandular- dotted at the top; pistil with a long, terete style, 3-4 mm long, glabrous. Fruit ovoid to obovoid, 1-2.3 mm diam, apically long-styled, glabrous, eglandular.
bibliographicCitation: Callejas, R. 1989. Studies in Neotropical Piperaceae I. A new species of Piper from Ecuador. Brittonia. 41: 325-327.

description: Frutex parvus 0.8-1 m usque altus, pauciramosus. Ramuli dense longe villosi. Folia longe petiolata, petiolo 3-4 cm longo, dense longe villoso; lamina 20-22 cm longa, 12-14 cm lata, ovato-elliptica vel late ovata, basi obtusa vel cordiformis, plerumque punctata, supra glabra, infra ad nervos et margine dense pilosa, pilis ramosis. Inflorescentia axillariQ 2.1-4.3 cm longa. Pedunculus 2-2.6 cm longus, 1.5-2 mm diametro, ebracteatus, dense longe villosus. Androecium tetrandrum. Stylus 3-4
bibliographicCitation: Callejas, R. 1989. Studies in Neotropical Piperaceae I. A new species of Piper from Ecuador. Brittonia. 41: 325-327.

description: Calyx broadly flask-shaped, the tube 2-2.5 cm long by ca. 10 mm wide at the widest part before maturity of the ovary, more or less abruptly narrowed upward, then slightly expanding below the more or less spreading lobes, the lobes relatively large, 12-20 mm long by 8-15 mm wide at the base. Leaf-blades thin in texture, rarely showing much variegation, tending to be ovate-sagittate, less often triangular- sagittate, to -subhastate (figs. 17, 26,38).
bibliographicCitation: Blomquist, Hugo L. 1957. A revision of Hexastylis of North America. Brittonia. 8: 255-281.

description: Herbage variable as to indument, commonly villous with rather long, soft hairs, in some forms the hairs coarse and often minutely papillate, in other forms the plants approaching var. lindheimeri in having only sparsely hairy culms and leaves. Spikelets 1.6-2.1 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Rhizomatous perennial. Culms 50-135(-173) cm. tall, erect or spreading, tufted. Nodes (2) 3-5 (6), glabrous. Internodes glabrous, rarely pubescent just below the nodes. Leaves with sheaths glabrous, rarely pubescent to pilose, the blades 11-35(-42) cm. long and 5-15 mm. wide, glabrous on both surfaces, rarely pubescent to pilose. Auricles short, vestigial, or absent. Ligule 0.8-3 mm. long, erose, truncate. Panicle 10-20(-27) cm. long, erect, open, the axis glabrous, the branches (3-)4-5(-8) per node (not whorled), spreading or spreading.ascending. Spikelets (1.8-)2-3.3 cm. long with (5-)8-10 florets. Glumes glabrous, subulate, the first (4-)6-8(-9) mm. long, 1 or rarely 3-nerved, the second (5-)7-10 mm. long, 3-nerved. Lemmas 9-13 mm. long, glabrous or scabrous to sparsely puberulent on the margins, 7- (3- or 5-) nerved, awnless or bearing a short awn up to 3 mm. long below an entire apex. Palea shorter than the lemma, ciliate on the nerves, glabrous or puberulent between the nerves. Anthesis in June, July, and August. Ovarian appendage with posterior lobe slightly notched, truncate, or obtuse, with a median thickening. Anthers (3.5-)4-6 mm. long, exserted at anthesis. Caryopsis 6-10 mm. long, spathulate, oblanceolate, or ellipsoidal to linear, amber-colored, rarely purple-black, adhering to the palea and lemma. Modal length of guard cells (44-)46-60(-70) µ; modal diameter of pollen grains 42-45(-49) [t. Chromosome number 2n= 56.
bibliographicCitation: Wagnon, Harvey K. 1952. A revision of the genus Bromus, section Bromopsis, of North America. Brittonia. 7: 415-480.

description: Culms erect and stout to spreading and delicate, 26-60 cm tall. Blades usually cauline. Panicle elegant, usually nodding, purplish to greenish, the branches usu- ally capillary, drooping to flexuous. Glumes unequal, the first 4-9 mm long, the second 7-16 mm long. Lemma 6-12 mm long, 0.1-0.3 mm wide near the apex, glabrous, scaberulous, or tuberculate-scabrous, the tubercles in lines or somewhat scattered. Awns (1.5) 2-6 (6.5) cm long, 0.1-0.3 mm wide at the base.
bibliographicCitation: Allred, Kelly W. 1984. Morphologic variation and classification of the North American Aristida purpurea complex (Gramineae). Brittonia. 36: 382-395.

description: Culms mostly 25-70 cm tall, the nodes glabrous or bearded with long, soft, spreading hairs; culms in age becoming much-branched and often developing dense fascicles of reduced stems, blades, and inflorescences. Sheaths glabrous on back (rarely the lower ones pilose), glabrous or pilose on margins. Blades thin or rather firm, lanceolate, the primary culms mostly 4-12 cm long and 3-10 cm broad, usually glabrous on both surfaces, sometimes ciliate on margins near base. Panicles open, well-exserted, the lateral spikelets on short pedicels. Spikelets glabrous or occasionally puberulent, elliptic or obovate, 1.5-2.4 mm long. First glume 1/3-1/4 as long as spikelet.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1980. The Mexican species of Dichanthelium (Poaceae). Brittonia. 32: 353-364.

description: Verisimiliter perennis. Caulis gracilis, 25 cm. altus, a basi sparse ramosus, nodis 10 subremotis, foliis inferiora glabris, oppositis, superiora eglanduloso- pubeseentibus, alternis. Folia inconspidua, linearia vel anguste elliptica, breviter acuminata, calloso-cuspidata, 5-22 mm. longa, 1-3 mm. lata. Cymae 1- ad 3-florae, bracteis minoribus, pedicillis 3-11 mm. longis. Sepala 7-9 mm. longa, aequalia vel subaequalia, costa inconspidua, apice anguste deltoideo, calloso- cuspidato, 3/5 longitudine conjuncta, membrana intersepalina lata, plana vel corrugata. Corolla rosea, inter infundibuliformis et hypocrateriformis, tubo 12 mm. longo, ex 1.5 ad 3 mm. expanso, extus glabro, intus 1 mm. super basim pu- beseenti, lobis obovatis, ca. 4 mm. longis et 3 mm. latis, ad apicem obtusis, integris. Stamina inaequalia, inclusa. Styli 2.5 mm. longi, dimidio conjuncti.
bibliographicCitation: Wherry, Edgar T. 1943. Microsteris, Phlox, and an intermediate. Brittonia. 5: 60-63. f. 1.

description: The difficulty with the Steele collection is that there are two sheets at US, each with the same date, "3 & 21 Aug 1897." Each sheet clearly represents a single plant so that it is likely that one sheet was gathered on 3 Aug and the other on 21 Aug. We have designated the sheet that best fits the protologue as the lectotype and consider the second US sheet (no. 364023) a syntype. The NY sheet appears to be a duplicate of the lectotype. Greene also cited a N. L. Britton collection gathered at "Garretson" [now Garretson Street] on Staten Island in Richmond Co., New York, on 25 Aug 1889, considering it to be "nearly the same." This syntype is at NY and at US.
bibliographicCitation: Reveal, James L. & Atha, Daniel E. 2010. New combinations and typifications in Bistorta, Persicaria, Polygonum, and Rumex (Polygonaceae). Brittonia. 62 (3): 243-263.

description: Plants spreading to prostrate, 1-2.5 dm tall, (0.3) 1-3 (5) dm across, yellowish- green to reddish-brown throughout; leaves basal, the blades spatulate to oblan- ceolate, 1-6 (8) cm long, 0.3-1.2 (1.8) cm wide, strigose and glandular on both surfaces, plane, the apex retuse, the base tapering gradually to a broad petiole, the cauline leaves lacking or represented only by a few simple hairs; stems (1) 2-6 (12), 2-5 (5.5) cm long, densely glandular especially basally; inflorescence open or more commonly densely branched, usually with many supernumerary branches, often becoming spiciform distally, the glands scattered or somewhat basally concentrated on the internodes, each node bearing a single sessile or pedunculate involucre; bracts 3, with an awn less than 0.5 mm long, those of the first node spatulate to linear, 5-14 mm long, 0.5-2 mm wide, foliaceous, those of the remaining nodes ovate to triangular, 3-8 mm long, basally connate to half- united and placed opposite the peduncle, often strongly reflexed, sparsely glandular on both surfaces; peduncles usually erect, slender, up to 10 mm long, frequently reduced or lacking above, sparsely glandular near the base or glabrous and glaucous; involucres narrowly to broadly turbinate, the lobes 5 (6), 4-7 mm long (excluding the awn), 0.8-1.5 mm wide, oblanceolate, united 1/5 to 1/4 their length, usually outwardly geniculate, yellowish-green to reddish-purple, glaucous and sparsely glandular within and without, the awns 0.3-1 mm long; bractlets linear and hyaline, 0.2-0.8 mm long, often highly reduced or even lacking, ciliate and sparsely glandular; pedicels 0.5-1 mm long, sparsely glandular, not becoming recurved; flowers 2-3 per involucre, included; tepals 1-2 mm long, greenish or ochroleucous to reddish with a green or red midvein, essentially monomorphic, ovate-oblanceolate, hirsute basally on the outer surface and sparsely glandular, the upper 1/5 (less in immature) divided into 3 short simple lobes; stamens included, the filaments 0.8-1.2 mm long, glabrous except for a few short basal projections, the anthers 0.2-0.4 mm long, oval, red to light brown; achene golden to red-brown, 1.2-1.5 mm long, the body trigonous, the beak 1/3 of the total length; n = 20 (Reveal & Ertter 4572).
bibliographicCitation: Newell, C. L. & Hymowitz, T. 1980. A taxonomic revision in the genus Glycine subgenus Glycine (Leguminosae). Brittonia. 32: 63-69.

description: Plants erect to spreading, 0.4-4 dm tall, 0.3-4.5 dm across, green to reddish or purplish throughout; leaves basal or basal and cauline, the basal blades linear to linear-oblanceolate, 1-4.5 cm long, 0.1-0.7 cm wide, densely hirsute above, less so below except along the midvein, sparsely glandular on both surfaces, plane to revolute, the apex acute or rarely obtuse, unawned, the base tapering gradually to a narrow petiole, the cauline leaves rudimentary or absent, linear to oblanceolate, 0.5-4 (10) mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide; stems 1-6 (12), 1-6.5 cm long, sparsely to densely glandular throughout; inflorescence open to densely branched, rarely with supernumerary branches, often becoming spiciform or ra- cemiform distally, the glands scattered on the internodes, each node except some- times the first bearing a single pedunculate or sessile involucre, the lower nodes of robust plants often possessing one or more rudimentary cauline leaves as well; bracts 1-18 mm long and 0.5-4 mm wide with an awn less than 0.5 mm long or rarely lacking altogether, those of the first node (2) 3 (4), linear to triangular or ovate, sometimes foliaceous, hirsute and glandular, those of the remaining nodes 2-3, with the middle bract usually reduced or lacking, linear to subulate or triangular, sometimes foliaceous, free or basally connate and placed opposite the branches, hirsute and glandular below, becoming ciliate or glabrous and glaucous above; peduncles erect to deflexed, very slender, 0.5-15 mm long, 0.1-0.2 mm wide, well-developed throughout or reduced to lacking above, glabrous and glaucous; involucres narrowly turbinate, the lobes (3) 4, 1-2 mm long (excluding the awn), 0.3-1 mm wide, triangular, united 1/3 to 1/2 their length, sometimes outwardly geniculate, green or purplish, glabrous and glaucous or sparsely glandular marginally, the awns 0.5-3 mm long; bractlets linear and hyaline to linear-oblan- ceolate and greenish-brown, 0.5-2 mm long, ciliate and sparsely glandular, rarely with a small awn and then looking like a small involucral bract; pedicels 1-2 mm long, glabrous, often becoming recurved through the sinuses of the involucre; flowers 2-6 per involucre, exserted at anthesis; tepals 1-2 mm long, white to pink with a green or red midvein, distinctly dimorphic and unequally pubescent, the outer 3 elliptic to oval or ovate, glabrous to strigose externally with short, curved, pustulate hairs, often sparsely glandular as well, the apex entire, the inner 3 narrower, ovate to elliptic-oblong, glabrous or strigose only at the base of the midvein, the apex entire or sometimes retuse with the lobes rounded or acute; stamens included, 0.5-1.5 mm long, the filaments glabrous, the anthers 0.2-0.3 mm long, oval, cream to red; achene yellow-brown to deep maroon, 1- 2 mm long, the body globose-lenticular, the beak 1/4 to 1/2 the total length.

description: Plants delicate to robust, 0.5-4 dm tall, 0.3-4.5 dm across; leaves 1-4.5 cm long, 0.1-0.7 cm wide; bracts 1-18 mm long, 0.5-4 mm wide, the middle bract quickly reduced above; involucres sessile to subsessile above or long-pedunculate throughout; bractlets primarily linear and hyaline, 0.5-1 mm long, rarely if ever oblanceolate and opaque; flowers 2-6 per involucre; tepals 1-2 mm long, the outer densely strigose externally, the inner usually entire, rarely retuse, or if so then with the lobes rounded; achene 1.5-2 mm long, the beak 1/3 to 1/2 the total length; n = 20 (Reveal & Ertter 4574).

description: Plants erect to somewhat spreading, (0.5) 1-6 dm tall, 0.5-4 dm across, blue- green to reddish throughout; leaves basal and cauline, the basal blades broadly obovate or spatulate to oblong or oblanceolate, 1-7 cm long, 0.5-2 cm wide, ciliate-denticulate but otherwise glabrous or with a few simple hairs near the midvein, plane, the apex rounded or mucronate, the base tapering gradually to a broad petiole, the cauline leaves rudimentary, linear to lanceolate or oblanceolate, 0.5-5 (10) mm long; stems 1 (6), (1) 2-11 (15) cm long, glandular basally; inflorescence open and spreading, rarely with supernumerary branches, often becoming racemiform distally, the glands noticeably concentrated in a band on the lower half of the internode, each node except the first bearing a single pedunculate involucre, the lower nodes usually possessing 1 or more rudimentary cauline leaves as well; bracts (2) 3 (4), with an awn 0.2-1.5 mm long, those of the first node triangular to lanceolate, 2-4 (10) mm long, (0.5) 1-3 mm wide, sparsely glandular and ciliate, those of the remaining nodes triangular, with the middle bract sometimes reduced or lacking, 1-4 (8) mm long, 0.5-2 mm wide, basally connate to half united and placed opposite the peduncle, or, if reduced to 2, then placed opposite the branches, glabrous to sparsely glandular; peduncles erect to deflexed, long and slender, (0.3) 1-5 (7.5) cm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide, reduced above, glandular on the lower third, otherwise glabrous and glaucous; involucres turbinate, 1.5-2 mm long (excluding the awns), green, glandular near the top within, the lobes 4-30 (36), 1/2 to completely united, stiffly erect, the awns 2-5 mm long, occasionally with a few depauperate awns interspersed; bractlets linear and hyaline or oblanceolate and greenish-brown, 0.5-2.5 mm long, glan- dular and ciliate; pedicels 1.5-2.5 mm long, glabrous, sometimes becoming recurved through the sinuses of the involucre; flowers 3-12 (20) per involucre, exserted beyond the lobes but rarely beyond the awns; tepals 2-2.5 mm long, white with pink or red midveins, essentially monomorphic, elliptic to oval, hirsute to strigose mainly at the base externally, often sparsely glandular as well, the apex entire or rarely irregularly lobed; stamens included, the filaments 2-2.5 mm long, glabrous or with a few short stubby hairs at the base, the anthers 0.3-0.6 mm long, oval to oblong, bright red; achene dark brown to deep maroon, 1.7-2 mm long, the body globose-lenticular, the beak 1/5 to 1/4 the total length.
bibliographicCitation: Newell, C. L. & Hymowitz, T. 1980. A taxonomic revision in the genus Glycine subgenus Glycine (Leguminosae). Brittonia. 32: 63-69.
