description: Plants spreading, 0.6-2 dm tall, 0.5-4 dm across, reddish throughout; leaves basal and cauline, the basal blades spatulate to oblong or oblanceolate, 1-6 cm long, 0.3-1.5 cm wide, ciliate-denticulate but otherwise glabrous or with a few simple hairs near the margin or the midvein, occasionally sparsely glandular on both surfaces, plane, the apex obtuse, sometimes seemingly cuspidate by the aggregation of hairs near the tip, the base tapering gradually to a broad petiole, the cauline leaves rudimentary, spatulate to oblanceolate or obovate, 0.5-4 mm long; stems 1 (5), 0.5-4 cm long, glandular distally; inflorescence open to densely branched, supernumerary branches lacking, seldom if ever becoming spiciform distally, the glands noticeably concentrated on the lower half of the internode, each node except the first bearing a single sessile or subsessile involucre, the lower nodes usually possessing one or more rudimentary cauline leaves as well; bracts of the first node 4-5, triangular to lanceolate, 2-10 mm long, 0.5-4 (8) mm wide, sparsely glandular on both surfaces, the awn 0.5-1 mm long, the 3 bracts of the remaining nodes united into an orbicular to somewhat triangular, perfoliate disk 1-2.5 cm across, gradually becoming reduced in size upwardly, glabrous on both surfaces or sparsely glandular, the awns 1-3 mm long, the bracts of the terminal nodes often not distinctly perfoliate, acerose, 0.5-2 mm long, 0.1-0.4 mm wide, glabrous, the awn 0.5-2 mm long; peduncles erect or nearly so, short and thick, 0.3-0.8 mm long, reduced to lacking throughout, glabrous and glaucous; involucres narrowly turbinate, the lobes 4, 2-5 mm long (excluding the awn), 0.3-1 mm wide, triangular to acicular, united 1/4 to 1/2 their length, reddish, glabrous or sparsely glandular, the awns 2-3 mm long; bractlets linear and hyaline or oblanceolate and greenish, 0.3-2.5 mm long, glabrous to glandular and ciliate; pedicels 1-2.5 mm long, glabrous, usually becoming recurved through the sinuses of the involucre; flowers 5-10 per involucre, exserted at anthesis; tepals 1.5-2.5 mm long, white or greenish-yellow with a light green or pink midvein, essentially monomorphic, ovate to lanceolate, pubescent externally with short, minutely echinulate clavate hairs, often sparsely glandular as well, the apex entire; stamens included, the filaments 1-1.5 mm long, minutely papillate, the anthers 0.2-0.5 mm long, oval, pink to red; achene deep maroon to dark brown, 1.5-2 mm long, the body globose-lenticular, the beak 1/5 to 1/4 the total length; n = 20 (Reveal 4440).

description: Plants erect or more commonly spreading to prostrate, 0.7-5 dm tall, 0.7-6 (11) dm across, yellowish-green to reddish-brown throughout; leaves basal, the blades spatulate to oblanceolate or linear, 1-5 (9) cm long, 0.2-0.7 (2) cm wide, sparsely strigose and glandular on both surfaces, plane, the apex retuse or apiculate, often with an upturned awn 0.5-4 mm long, the base tapering gradually to a broad petiole, the cauline leaves usually lacking; stems 1 (5), 0.5-3 cm long, glabrous to densely glandular; inflorescence open, rarely with supernumerary branches, usually becoming racemiform distally. the glands scattered or somewhat basally concentrated on the internodes, each node bearing a single pedunculate involucre; bracts 3 (4) with an awn 0.8-1 mm long, those of the first nodes spatulate to triangular or broadly oval, 3-15 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, often subfoliaceous, those of the remaining nodes ovate to triangular, 2-8 mm long, basally connate to half-united and placed opposite the peduncle, sparsely glandular without, less so to glabrous within; peduncles erect or at right angles to the stem, long and slender, 0.5-1.5 cm long, well-developed throughout, sparsely glandular near the base, otherwise glabrous; involucres broadly turbinate, the lobes 5 (6), linear-oblanceolate to obovate, 3-8 mm long (not counting the awn), 0.8-1.8 mm wide, united 1/5 to 1/3 of their length, sometimes outwardly geniculate, yellowish-green to purplish-red, rarely with a slight white margin, sparsely glandular and glaucous within and without, the awns 0.3-2 mm long, rarely with the main awn flanked by two smaller awns up to 0.5 mm long; bractlets linear and hyaline, 0.5 mm long, ciliate and sparsely glandular, rarely lanceolate and green, 1-1.5 mm long; pedicels 0.5-1.2 mm long, glabrous, not becoming recurved; flowers 3-5 (10) per involucre, mostly included; tepals 2.5-4 mm long, white to pink with a green midvein, often whiter at the tips, essentially monomorphic, hirsute basally on the outer surface and sparsely glandular, oblong, the upper 1/3 to 1/2 divided into 3 overlapping lobes, the outer lobes broad-based and tapering to the tip, the central lobe attenuate-based with the central portion broader before tapering to the tip, all lobes irregularly margined or divided into linear segments; stamens mostly exserted, 1-4 mm long, the filaments glabrous, the anthers 0.5-0.7 mm long, elliptic to oval, red to maroon; achene golden-brown, 1.2-2 mm long, the body trigonous, the beak 1/4 to 1/3 of the total length; n = 20 (Reveal & Ertter4571).
bibliographicCitation: Newell, C. L. & Hymowitz, T. 1980. A taxonomic revision in the genus Glycine subgenus Glycine (Leguminosae). Brittonia. 32: 63-69.

description: Plants erect to spreading, 0.5-2.5 dm tall, 0.4-4 dm across, green to purplish- red throughout; leaves basal and cauline, the basal blades spatulate or obovate to oblanceolate, 0.7-4 cm long, (0.1) 0.5-1.2 cm wide, sparsely strigose above, less so or glabrous below except along the midvein, sparsely glandular on both surfaces, plane, the apex obtuse, unawned, the base tapering gradually to a nar- row petiole, the cauline leaves rudimentary, linear to oblanceolate, 0.5-4 mm long; stems 1 (3), 2.5-4.5 cm long, glandular throughout; inflorescence open to densely branched, often only dichotomous at the first node, rarely if ever with supernumerary branches, often becoming spiciform distally, the glands scattered on the internodes, each node except sometimes the first bearing a single sessile or subsessile involucre, the lower nodes usually possessing one or more rudimentary cauline leaves as well; bracts 1-5 mm long and 0.5-3 mm wide with an awn 1-3 mm long, those of the first node 3 (5), linear to ovate, ciliate and glandular, those of the remaining nodes 2-3 with the middle bract usually reduced or lacking, linear to triangular, sometimes strongly recurved, free or basally connate and placed opposite the branches, ciliate and glandular below, becoming glabrous and glaucous above; peduncles deflexed, short and thick, 0.5-2 mm long, reduced to lacking throughout, glabrous and glaucous; involucres narrowly turbinate, the lobes 4, 1.5-2 mm long (excluding the awns), 0.3-1 mm wide, triangular, united 1/3 to 1/2 their length, sometimes outwardly geniculate, green or purplish, sparsely glandular marginally and glaucous, the awns 2.5-3 mm long, reddish; bractlets linear and hyaline to spatulate and opaque, 0.5-1 mm long, glabrous to glandular and ciliate; pedicels 1-2 mm long, glabrous, usually becoming recurved through the sinuses of the involucre; flowers 2-4 (7) per involucre, exserted at anthesis; tepals 1-1.5 mm long, greenish-white to pink with a green or red midvein, dis- tinctly dimorphic and unequally pubescent, the outer 3 oval to ovate, strigose externally with short curved pustulate hairs, often sparsely glandular as well, the apex entire, rounded, the inner 3 narrower, ovate or oval to elliptic, glabrous or pubescent only at the base of the midvein, the apex entire, rounded to truncate; stamens included, 1-1.5 mm long, the filaments glabrous, the anthers 0.2 mm long, oval, pale brown to cream; achene dark brown to deep maroon, 1-1.5 mm long, the body globose-lenticular, the beak 1/3 of the total length; n = 20 (from seeds of Reveal 4827 grown in a greenhouse; voucher at MARY).

description: Flowers bisexual, protandrous; stigmas 3, stellate-fimbriate, with 3 deflexed styles; ovary 3-angled, becoming a trigonous achene; achene golden-brown, elliptic, 1-1.4 mm long, with sharp angles, enclosed by the perianth in fruit; stamens 6; filaments short; anther sacs yellowish, not exserted; valves golden to straw-colored at maturity, papery, reticulated, each valve with 4-6 spiny teeth which diverge 0.5-1.5 mm beyond the valve; all valves with tubercles, though they may vary in size; all three tubercles usually prominent, pale plump-ellipsoid; outer sepals linear-lanceolate, ca 1 mm in length, somewhat recurved; pedicels slender, articulated near the base and becoming deflexed; inflorescences of dense, globose clusters of fascicles, in the axils of leaves, appearing terminal in dwarf plants, leafy-bracteate; leaves lanceolate with acute to obtuse tips and obtuse to truncate bases; leaves may be papillate or crisped minutely at the margins; upper leaves lanceolate with short petioles, bract-like and linear in the upper inflorescence; petioles up to 4 cm long on lower leaves, reduced upward; stipules scarious, disintegrating; stem hollow, erect to sprawling, usually much branched; nodes scarcely swollen; plants 2-60 cm tall, from a fibrous, annual root- stock; 2n = 40.
bibliographicCitation: Mitchell, R. S. 1978. Rumex maritimus L. versus R. persicarioides L. (Polygonaceae) in the Western Hemisphere. Brittonia. 30: 293-296.

description: Plants commonly spreading to prostrate, 0.3-3 dm tall, 0.3-5 dm across, reddish or purplish green throughout; leaves basal, the leaf-blades spatulate to oblanceolate, 1.5-7.5 cm long, 0.4-1.5 cm wide, sparingly strigose and glandular on both surfaces, plane, the apex retuse and mucronate or merely retuse, the base tapering gradually to a broad petiole, cauline leaves lacking; stems 1 (3), (0.5) 2-10 cm long, glandular throughout; inflorescence open, rarely if ever with supernumerary branches or becoming racemiform distally, the glands scattered on the internodes, each node bearing a single pedunculate involucre; bracts 3 with an awn 1-2 mm long, those of the first node spatulate to triangular or broadly oval, (0.5) 1-1.5 cm long, often subfoliaceous, those of the remaining nodes ovate to triangular, 0.5-1 cm long, basally connate to half united and placed opposite the peduncle, often becoming recurved, sparsely glandular; peduncles erect, long and slender, 0.5-3 cm long, well-developed and glandular throughout; involucres broadly funnelform and laterally compressed, 4-8 mm long, 9-12 mm wide, the 5 papery lobes united 3/4 or more of their length into a concave disk, their free portions obtuse, the upper 0.5-1.2 mm of the sinuses scarious and white to light pink, the remainder reddish-purple, glandular within, glabrous and usually glaucous without, the awns 1-1.5 mm long; bractlets linear-oblanceolate and hyaline, 0.5-0.8 mm long, ciliate and sparsely glandular; pedicels 1-2 mm long, glandular; flowers 3-6 per involucre, only the apices exserted; tepals (2) 3-4.5 (5) mm long, white to light pink with a red midvein, often whiter at the tips, essentially monomorphic, narrowly oblong, hirsute to lanate basally on the outer surface andsparsely glandular, the upper 1/3 to 1/2 laciniate into 3-5 main lobes with these often subdivided into fine linear segments; stamens mostly exserted, the filaments 3-5 mm long, densely and minutely papillate throughout, the anthers 1-1.2 mm long, oval to oblong, bright red; achene golden-brown, 1.8-2 mm long, the body trigonous, the beak 1/3 of the total length.

description: Annual herbs. Stems 5-12(-15) cm long, 4-angled, green, wiry, zigzagged, angled, simple or branched from base, glabrous. Leaves: basal leaves persistent at flowering and gradually transformed into bracts; oc- reae 2-5 mm, glabrous, free part is lacerate; blades oblanceolate to obovate, 5-20 x 2- 5 mm; margins revolute, smooth, apex is rounded or mucronate. Inflorescences terminal, spiciform, bracteate, dense; cymes 3-5-flowered, congested at the tip of stems and branches; bracts numerous, much longer than the flowers. Flowers wide-open; pedicels erect to patent, 2-3 mm; perianth 2-2.5 mm, tube 12-25% of the perianth length, perianth lobes petaloid, oblong to oblong-obovate, cucullate, naviculate only in the upper 1/4, overlapping (Fig. 3H), pure-white, midveins pink or greenish, unbranched; perianth lobe cells irregularly branched, 20-35 x 18-26 µm, with anticlinal walls strongly sinuate; epicuticular wax pattern of type 1, with a dense pattern of intertwined, reticulate rodlets. Stamens 8; anthers purple, 325-350 µm. Pollen of type B, 27.3-29.1 µm. Achenes ovate to oblong-ovate, 1.8-2.1 mm, included or slightly exserted from the perianth at maturity, smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Costea, Mihai & Tardif, F. J. 2005. Taxonomy of the Polygonum douglasii (Polygonaceae) complex with a new species from Oregon. Brittonia. 57 (1): 1-27.

description: Annual herbs. Stems 15-60 cm long, 4-angled, green, erect, simply to freely branched, scaberulous-papillose on and between ribs; papillae white, patent or reflexed, dense, conical-elongate to cylindrical, 100-200 µm. Leaves: basal leaves often caducous at flowering, upper leaves abruptly reduced to scale-like bracts; ocreae 6-12 mm, scaberulous-papillose, free part lacerate or disintegrating into fibers; blades 15-70 × 2-8 mm; margins narrowly revolute, denticulate-papillose: apex acute or mucronate; papillae on the ocreae and leaf margins are similar to those on the stems. Inflorescences terminal, spike-like, open thyrses; cymes 2-5-flowered ± uniformly spaced on stems and branches; bracts equaling or somewhat longer than the flowers. Flowers wide-open or semiopen; pedicels patent in flower and reflexed in fruit, 0.5-1 mm; perianth (3.5-)4-5 mm; tube 9-17% of the perianth length, perianth  lobes petaloid, cucullate, naviculate only in the upper 1/4 part, overlapping, white or pink, borders white to pink; midveins green, unbranched or with short lateral branches; perianth lobe cells elongated, 45-60 × 6-9 µm, with anticlinal walls strongly sinuate; epicuticular wax pattern of type 2, with a dense intertwined pattern of reticulate rodlets at the top of cells (Fig. 4F). Stamens 8, anthers pink to purple, 400-500 µm. Pollen of type B, 31-33 µm (Fig. 6H). Achenes elliptic, 3.5-5 mm, enclosed in perianth at maturity, smooth or tubercled (Fig. 7E).

description: Annual herbs. Stems 2-30 cm long, 4-angled, reddish brown, wiry, prostrate to erect, often zigzagged, simple or branched from base, scaberulous-papillose on and between the ribs; papillae red, orange or sometimes white, patent, conical with a swollen base, 40-60 [pm (Fig. 1B). Leaves persistent at flowering, evenly distributed or crowded at branch tips, hardly reduced distally; ocreae funnelform, 1-4 mm, scaberulous-papillose, free part entire or dentate-lacerate; blades narrow-elliptic, elliptic, ovate, obovate, or subcircular, 6-27 X 3-8 mm; margins plane, irregularly thickened or denticulate-papillose (rarely glabrous), apex acute or mucronate. Papillae on the ocreae are often retrorse, similar to those on the stem; papillae on the leaf margins are white, conic-cylindrical, 100-180 r.m, Inflores- cences axillary; cymes 1-3-flowered starting from near stem and branch bases, sometimes also crowded at branch apices; bracts leaf-like, much longer than the flowers they subtend. Flowers semiopen or closed; pedicels erect to patent, 2-3 mm; perianth 1.8- 2.5 mm; tube 22-29% of the perianth length; perianth lobes almost sepaloid, cucullate, naviculate to obscurely so, overlapping, green with narrow white or pink margins, midveins thickened, unbranched: perianth lobe cells are irregularly shaped, 35-45 × 10-65  µm with the anticlinal walls moderately sinuate; epicuticular wax pattern of type 1, with a dense pattern of reticulate and intertwined rodlets (Fig. 5E). Stamens 8: anthers purple, 120-165 µm. Pollen of subtype A2, 26-28.2 µm (Fig. 6E). Achenes elliptic to ovate, 1.8-2.3 mm, enclosed in the perianth at maturity, or only with the tip exserted smooth.

description: Annual herbs. Stems (5-)10-35 cm long, 4-angled, purplish, wiry, sometimes zigzagged, simple or branched, spreading to erect, scaberulous-papillose on and between the ribs (Fig. IF); papillae red, orange or sometimes white, patent or retrorse, conical with a swollen base, 40-60 µm. Leaves: basal leaves persistent at flowering, evenly distributed or crowded at branch tips, gradually transformed into bracts; ocreae 3-4 mm long, funnelform, scaberulous-papillose, free part finally lacerate; blades linear to narrow-elliptic, 8-30 x 1-4(-7) mm, ± glaucous adaxially; margins revolute, smooth; apex acute or acuminate. Papillae on ocreae are often retrorse, similar to those on the stems (Fig. 1F). Inflorescences terminal, spiciform, dense and bracted; cymes with 2-3 flowers, aggregated at the apices of branches; bracts much longer than the flowers they subtend. Flowers semiopen or closed; pedicels erect or patent, 2-3 mm; perianth 1.8-2.4 mm; tube 25-33% of the perianth length, perianth lobes petaloid, cucullate, usually naviculate only in the upper 1/4, ± overlapping (Fig. 3C), pinkish green with pink borders, midvein greenish, un- branched; perianth lobe cells rectangular or irregularly shaped, 35-45 x 10-16 µm with anticlinal walls moderately sinuate; epicuticular wax pattern of type 1, with a dense pattern of reticulate and intertwined rodlets (Fig. 5F). Stamens 8; anthers purple, 250-325 µm. Pollen of type B, 27-29.2 µm (Fig. 6F). Achenes elliptic to ovate, 1.8-2.3 mm, enclosed in perianth at maturity, smooth.

description: Annual herbs. Stems 5-50 cm long, 4-angled, green, divaricately branched, scaberulous on and between ribs (Fig. 1C) (rarely almost glabrous); papillae white, patent, dense, conical-elongate to cylindrical, 100-200 µm. Leaves: basal leaves usually caducous at flowering, upper leaves abruptly reduced to scale-like bracts; ocreae 8-12 mm, scaberulous-papillose, free part disintegrating into a few persistent fibers; blades linear to lanceolate, 35-60 x 1-3 mm, sometimes with scarce papillae (Fig. 2E); margins plane or very narrowly revolute, denticulate-papillose; apex acute or mucronate. Papillae on the ocreae and the margins of leaves are similar to those on the stems (Fig. 1C); papillae from the leaf blade are conical, shorter, 40-60 µm, with a heavy cuticle (Fig. 2E). Inflorescences terminal, spiciform, dense; cymes 2-5-flowered, crowded and ± overlapping at branch tips; bracts equaling or somewhat longer than the flowers. Flowers open or semiopen; pedicel patent to erect, to 2 mm; perianth 3-5 mm, tube 9-17% of the perianth length, perianth lobes petaloid, cucullate, usually naviculate only in the upper 1/4 part, overlapping, pink or white, with broad pink borders; midveins green or brown, with short lateral branches; perianth lobe cells elongated, 50-65 x 6-9 µm with the anticlinal walls strongly sinuate; epicuticular wax pattern of type 2, with a narrow pattern of reticulate rodlets at the top of cells (Fig. 4E). Stamens 8, anthers pink to purple, 400-550 µm. Pollen of type B, 31-33 pm. Achenes narrow elliptic to elliptic lanceolate, 3-5 mm, enclosed in the perianth at maturity, smooth or tubercled (Fig. 7F).

description: Annual herbs. Stems 5-50 cm long, 4-angled, green or brownish, erect, simple or branched, with a few to many branches, upper edges glabrous, ± winged or denticulate-papillose; papillae on the edges (when present) conical, 80-120 µm, papillae on the stem faces spherical, 7-18 µm, located at the same level with the epidermis cells (Fig. 1A). Leaves: basal leaves caducous or persistent at flowering; upper leaves reduced to scale-like bracts upward; ocreae 6-15 mm, glabrous, free part soon disintegrating into a few brown fibers; blades narrowly lanceolate to linear, with 2 deep pleats parallel to the midvein, 25-40 x 1-8 mm, margins usually plane, denticulate- papillose, apex mucronate or cuspidate. Papillae on leaf margins conic-elongated or cylindrical, 110-200 [im. Inflorescences terminal, spike-like, slender and elongated; cymes 1 or 2(3)-flowered, widely spaced along stem and branches; bracts shorter to equaling the flowers they subtend. Flowers closed; pedicels erect, 1-1.5 mm; perianth 2.5-4.2 mm, the tube 15-22% of the peri- anth length, perianth lobes petaloid or se- paloid, cucullate, naviculate, overlapping, green (often brownish when dried), with pink or white borders; perianth lobe cells rectangular, 33-45 x 18-22 [tm, with the anticlinal walls straight; epicuticular wax pattern of type 1, with a transversal pattern of rodlets (Fig. 4A). Stamens 8, with pink or purple anthers, 125-150 [Lm long. Pollen of subtype Al, 21-24 µm (Fig. 6B). Achenes elliptic to oblong, 2.3-4 mm, included in the perianth or slightly exserted at maturity, smooth or minutely striate-tubercled near the edges and apex (Fig. 7C). 2n = 20 (Love & Love, 1956).

description: V ine, the stems often persistently pilose just below nodes with pale, several-celled, crispate hairs 0.3-0.7 mm long, otherwise glabrate; petioles 18-50 mm long, sparsely spreading-pilose like nodes, glabrate; leaf-blades drying dull green, broadly ovate, (4-) 5.5-13 cm long, (2.5-)3.5-8.5 cm broad, glabrous on both sides or spreading-pilose on nerves beneath, conspicuously cordate to subcordate at base and with a cluster of many glands on the upper surface at apex of petiole (these ovoid, 0.3-0.5 mm long), caudate- acuminate at apex (acumen usually slender, 10-15 mm long, callose-mucronulate), 5-nerved from base, the costa canaliculate to acutely elevated above, subprominent beneath, the secondary nerves 4-6 per side, spreading, anastomosing toward margin, prominulous on both surfaces or plane above; inflorescences rarely 2 per node, umbelli- form-cymbose, 4-8 cm long at anthesis, elongating in fruit, composed of (1-)2 or 3 congested-racemiform umbels borne laterally on a slender fractiflex axis, the peduncle slender, (1-)2.5-5.5 cm long, like the rachis and pedicels sparsely pilose with pale brown several-celled hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, glabrate; flowers 10-20 per umbel (lower ones caducous, leaving scars as the umbel elongates), subtended by membranaceous bracts, these ovate-oblong, 0.3-0.7 mm long and broad, obscurely ciliolate, the pedicels terete, slender, 6-23 mm long at anthesis, sparsely strigillose with pale brown hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, soon glabrate; corolla 4-10 mm in diameter at anthesis, the tube 0.5-1.5 mm long, the lobes sometimes inflexed in bud, ovate-oblong or deltoid, 2-3.5 mm long, 1.2-2.7 mm broad, obtuse or subacute at apex, obviously nerved, often slightly recurved at margin; gynostegium 1.5-2 mm long, the filament-tube 0.4-0.6 mm long, the anthers laterally connate or partially free, 0.5-1 mm long to fusion with stigma and conspicuously dorsally spurred, each spur antrorse, narrowly oblong or conical, often curved, sometimes laterally compressed, 0.2-0.7 mm long, the appendages oblong, 0.3-0.6 mm long and broad, the translators slender, 0.1-0.3 mm long, laterally or subbasally bearing caudicles 0.1-0.2 mm long, the pollinia ellipsoid or obovoid, about 0.2 mm long; ovaries subconical, slender, 1-1.3 mm long at anthesis, tapering into very short styles, the stigma 0.7-1 mm in diameter; follicles solitary, slenderly fusiform, to 250 mm long, 10-13 mm broad; seeds 11-14 mm long, about 4 mm broad.

description:
Plants perennial, twining; stems up to 4 m long and 4 min in diameter, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, the internodes to 12 em long; leaves ovate-triangular, 5-10 cm long, 4-6 cm broad, cordate at base, mucronate at apex, glabrous above and below except on the veins; petiole pubescent, 2-5 cm long; infloreseence extra-axillary, the peduncles appearing between the two petiole bases, many-flowered, racemose (the arrangement of the pedicels is varied, two often arisinig at the same level); peduncle pubescent, 3-4 cm long; calyx-teeth linear-lanceolate, 5-6 mm long, 1.5-2 mm broad, pubescent oni the outside, gla- brous within; corolla lavender to white, the tube campanulate, 2-3 mm long, the lobes linear-lanceolate, 7-8 mm long, 3 mm broad at the base, profusely lanose-bearded on the inner surface and glabrous without; gynostegiuni sessile, 2-5 mm high; anthers 1.5 mm long; stigmatic appendage 6-7 mm long, the apex short-bifurcate; retinaculum linear-oblong, 0.4-0.5 mm long, 0.1-0.2 mm wide; caudiculae horizontal, longer than broad, about 0.2 mm long; pollinia ovoid, 0.5 mm long, 0.3 mm wide; fruit tubereculate, ovoid-lanceolate, 4-7 cm long.

description: Plants erect, 15-20 cm high (shoots much longer in cultivation), roots fibrous. Shoots succulent, verrucose, prominently glaucous when old, glabrous, internodes 6- 10 mm diam. Leaf scales caducuous, petiole 1 mm long, blade 3-4 mm long, 1 mm wide, ovate, basally rounded, apically acute. Inflorescences sciadioidal, 2-6-flowered, all flowers open at the same time; peduncles 2-4 mm long, glabrous. Flowers sweetly scented, floral bracts 0.7-1 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm wide at the base, deltate, glandular over the whole surface; pedicels 2-4 mm long, glabrous, glaucous. Floral buds 7-8 mm long, 4-5 mm diam., subglobose to conical, with imbricate aestivation. Calyx fused basally, glabrous, lobes 2-2.5 mm long, 1.5-1.7 mm wide, ovate to ob- long, apically acute to acuminate. Corolla cyathiform, lobes fused basally, 7-10 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, abaxially bright grey green (occasionally with rose tinge), adaxially rose to brown with purplish veins, basally green, free lobes incurved, ovate to lanceolate, keeled, apically obtuse to emarginate, with revolute margins. Gynostegial corona white, 3.5-4 mm long, equalling the gynostegium in height, not vertically articulated. C(is) consisting of Cs and Ci fused for about ¾ of total corona height, abaxially papillose, Cs and Ci differentiated, Ci shorter and thinner than Cs, Ci dorsally connate to Cs. Cs indistinct, consisting of just a fringe supporting the massive adaxial appendage, appendage adnate to the back of the stamens, falsely suggesting a standard Cs, apically erect, solid, ovate, inflexed. Ci laminar, strongly keeled, resulting in a re- flexed spur with apically involute margins.

description: Shrub to 2 m high, with white latex, the branchlets terete, slender, strigose distally with pale hairs 0.2-0.4 mm long, at length glabrate, rugulose in drying; leaves opposite, the petioles slender, shallowly canaliculate, 1.5-4 mm long, strigose like branchlets, the blades subcoriaceous, narrowly lanceolate but appearing linear because of the strongly revolute margins, 3-10 cm long, 2-6 mm broad but sometimes tightly revolute and less than 1 mm broad, subacute or obtuse at base, subacute and callose-tipped at apex, glabrous above except with a few hairs mixed with minute glands in basal sulcus, strigose along costa beneath, the costa often sharply impressed above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves inconspicuous, 2-4 per centimeter, ascending, immersed or plane on both surfaces; inflorescences lateral to a leaf, 1 per node, umbelliform, 3-10 mm long at anthesis, composed of a congested-racemiform umbel borne at the apex of a peduncle, this 1-2.5 mm long, strigillose wvith several-celled hairs about 0.2 mm long, at length glabrate, the short rachis verruciform with scars left by caducous flowers; flowers 25-30 (lower ones soon caducous), each subtended by 2 or 3 bracts, these marginally imbricate, deltoid, 0.3-0.4 mm long and broad, subacute, minutely ciliolate, the pedicels terete, glabrous, 1.5-2.5 mm long at anthesis; calyx subrotate at anthesis and 2-3 mm in diameter, 5-lobed nearly to base, the lobes quincuncial in bud, ovate, 0.5-1.5(-2) mm long, 0.7-1 mm broad, minutely ciliolate, rounded at apex, obscurely nerved, the sinuses obscurely glandular within; corolla thin-carnose, campanulate-subrotate, 3.5-6 mm in apical diameter, the tube 0.5-1 mm long, the lobes 5, narrowly dextrorsely imbricate, oblong-deltoid, 1.8-2.2 mm long, 1.2-1.5 mm broad, villose within with pale hairs 0.2-0.5 mm long, obtuse at apex, copiously but inconspicuously reticulate-nerved; gynostegium obovoid, 1.3-1.7 mm long, the fila- ment-tube membranaceous, 0.3-0.5 mm long, adnate to corolla-tube, the anthers oblong, laterally coherent, narrowed proximally, 0.3-0.5 mm to fusion with stigma, the terminal appendages membranaceous, orbicular-oblong, imbricate, 0.6-0.8 X 0.4- 0.6 mm, copiously opaque-glandular, rounded or obtuse, carnose-thickened proximally within, the thickenings concave-margined, each sheltering a pollinium, the translators narrowly oblong, 0.2-0.3 mm long, the caudicles basal, curved, 0.2-0.3 mm long, the pollinia oblong, erect, 0.15-0.17 mm long; description: Vine, the young parts copiously strigillose with pale brown hairs 0.1-0.3 mm long, the stems soon glabrate; petioles (3-)8-13 mm long, subglabrate; leaf-blades drying greenish brown, slightly paler beneath, ovate-lanceolate, (3-)5-7.2 cm long, (1.5-)2- 3.2 cm broad, strigillose-puberulent on both sides when young, at length glabrate except sometimes on costa and nerves, broadly obtuse to subcordate at base, lacking basal glands above or these minute and obscure, obtuse or obtusely short-cuspidate at apex, entire or subundulate and narrowly recurved at margin, the costa subplane above, raised beneath, the secondary nerves 5-9 per side, spreading or curved-ascending, inconspicuously anastomosing toward margin, prominulous on both surfaces; inflores- cences umbelliform-cymose, 1-2 cm long at anthesis, composed of 1-3 congested- racemiform umbels borne at the apex of a peduncle, this 3-11 mm long, pilose like young parts but soon glabrate: flowers (8-)25-30 per umbel (including lower ones that are caducous, leaving conspicuous scars), subtended by minute bracts, these deltoid, 0.2-0.3 mm long, acute, dorsally strigillose, soon caducous, the pedicels terete, slender, 4-5 mm long at anthesis, soon glabrate: calyx 2-2.5 mm in diameter, the lobes ovate, 0.6-0.9 mm long and broad, obtuse or rounded at apex, inconspicuously ciliolate with glandular hairs less than 0.1 mm long, strigillose without with brown hairs about 0.1 mm long, glabrate, obscurely nerved, minutely glandular at sinuses; corolla 4-4.5 mm in diameter at anthesis, the lobes oblong, 1.8-2.2 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, obtuse at apex, inconspicuously nerved; gynostegium obovoid, 1.3-1.5 mm long, the filament-tube 0.4-0.5 mm long, the anthers laterally connate, dorsally thickened proximally, about 0.5 mm long to fusion with stigma, the appendages oblong, 0.5-0.7 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm broad, the translators slender, about 0.2 mm long, the caudicles basal, 0.2-0.3 mm long, the pollinia ellipsoid, about as long as the caudicles an(l basally attached: ovaries ovoid, with inconspicuous styles about 0.3 mm long, the stigma 0.6-0.7 mm in diameter.

description: Perennial, semi-fleshy herbs with short caudices, and spreading or decumbent slender stems, 1-4 dm long, often also with basal, fine stolons; basal leaves in a rosette, obovate to oblanceolate, 1-6 cm long, the petiole broadened and scarious near the base, the stem leaves reduced upward, becoming bract-like at the top, and sometimes bearing bulblets in the axils; flowers 1-8, racemose-cymose, at the end of the stems; pedicels filiform, 5-15 mm long; sepals 2-4 mm long, striate, usually slightly unequal, rounded-ovate; petals pink or white with pink veins, 7-15 mm long, oblanceolate, rounded or emarginate at apex; stamens two-thirds length of petals; capsule subequal with the calyx, ovoid; seeds black, minutely pitted, 1.5 mm long.

description: Planta perennis longaeva ex caudice incrassato interdum usque ad 10 cm elongato; radices primariae crassae, interdum unica, sed pro parte maxima tantum paucae; rosulae folia plura, plana, oblanceolata vel spathulata, plerumque obtusa, (2-) 4-7 (-10) mm longa, 10-15 (-20) mm lata, irregulariter grosseque serrata, in petiolos latos insuper planatos subtus triangulari-rotundatos contracta; caules 1 vel plures (usque ad 15), scapiformes, (5-) 10-20 (-25) cm alti, in sectione transversali infra ramos floriferos elliptici; folia caulina interdum 2, saepe opposita vel subopposita, usque ad 1 cm longa vel minus multum reducta, marginibus glandulis rubris dentata, bracteolae ramos floriferos vel flores suffulcientes etiam magis reductae; panicula bracteata ex ramis paucifloris vel plurifloris consistens; pedicelli graciles, 3-8 mm longi; sepala duo, ca. 2 mm longa, dentibus stipitato-glandulosis 12-18 ornata; petala 5, elliptica, acuta vel obtusa, ca. 6 mm longa, 2.5-3.0 mm lata, dilute rosea venulis perroseis plerumque 3 (usque ad 5) ornata; stamina 5, ca. 5 mm longa, antheris saturate roseis, 0.8-1.0 mm longis, filamentis ad basem versus aliquantulum expansis; ovarium ovoideum, 1.5-2.0 mm longum, stigma 3-lobatum; capsula petalis stamini- busque persistentibus involuta, attenuato-ovoidea vel ovoidea, ca. 3 mm longa, in ambitu irregularis semina maturantia accomodans, secus suturas tres plerumque apice vel interdum lateraliter vel basaliter dehiscens; semina in capsula quaque 1-3, anthracina, nitentia, 1.2-1.5 mm longa, ca. 1 mm lata.

description: Reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes. Stems 0.8-2 (3.5) dm tall, erect, primarily simple or occasionally branching. Petioles 1-4 mm long, pubescent from node to base of leaf blade. Cauline leaves 2.8-7.5 cm long, 1-2 (3) mm wide, linear, the base cuneate to tapering, pubescent, the apex acute. Basal leaves (when persistent) as a rosette, obovate, clavate, or spatulate, the petioles longer than the blade. Flowers solitary in apical leaf axils and inserted in leaf axils of flowering branches. Pedicels 0.5-1.5 cm long. Sepals 3-4.5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide. Petals 3.5-6 mm long, 3-4.5 mm wide, apiculate. Capsules 2-3 mm in diameter, containing 20-36 seeds; 2n = 34.

description: Reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes. Stems 2.5-8 (10) dm tall, erect, often ascending, simple or frequently branching. Petioles (0.2) 0.6-4 cm long, decreasing in length from basal to apical portion of the plant, pubescent along basal half, essentially glabrous near the blade. Cauline leaves 2-8 (10.5) cm long, 1-3 cm wide, ovate to lanceolate, the base rounded to cuneate, the apex acute. Basal leaves ovate to lanceolate, the petiole longer than the blade, seldom persistent as a rosette. Flowers solitary but clustered in apical leaf axils and inserted in leaf axils of flowering branches. Pedicels 1-4.2 cm long. Sepals 4-8 mm long, 0.5-4 mm wide, the venation conspicuous. Petals 5-10.5 mm long, 4-10 mm wide, apiculate. Capsules 4-6.5 mm diameter, containing 20-35 seeds; 2n = 34.

description: Reproducing vegetatively by rhizomes. Stems (1.2) 2-10 dm tall, erect, simple or branching. Petioles 1-5 (9) mm long, pubescent only at the base. Cauline leaves linear to narrowly lanceolate, 3.4-8 (9) cm long, (2) 3-5 mm wide, the base cuneate to tapering, the apex acute, the midrib prominent, the lateral veins not evident or obscure. description: New shoots initiated from crown of perennial root. Stems 3-7 dm tall, erect, simple or branching. Petioles 0.5-4.5 cm long, pubescent only at the base. description: Herbae perennes tenellae glabrae 1-5 (-10) cm altae; folia membranacea linearia vel anguste oblanceolata, adulta spatulata, (1-) 1.8-5 (-6.5) cm longa, (0.1-) 0.2-5 (-6.5) mm lata, in petiolum alatum sensim contracta, apice rotundata; scapus saepissime 1-, rarius 2-florus, (1.5-) 14-36 (-62) mm longus; bractea involucralis (0.6-) 1-3 (-5) mm longa membranacea ovata vel lanceolata obtusa vel rotundata; pedicellus 2.5-12 (-23) mm longus; calycis anguste campanulati (3.3-) 4-6.5 (-8) mm longi, dentes 1.2-2.4 (-3) mm longi, lanceolati obtusi vel acuti; corollae tubus luteus, (4.8-) 5.5-8 (-8.5) mm longus, fauces 0.5-1.2 (-1.8) mm longae, lobi violacei demum purpurascentes, emarginati vel obcordati, (1.2-) 2.4-4.2 (-5) mm longi, (1-) 1.6-3.8 (-4.7) mm lati.

description: Scapose perennials with fibrous roots; leaves 1-4 cm long, elliptic-oblanceolate and narrowed gradually to the winged petiole, efarinose or farinose on the abaxial surface when young, the blade margins crenulate or denticulate, sometimes entire; scape 6.5-24 cm long, medium green proximally and darkening distally; inflorescence an umbel, farinose; involucral bracts 4-7 mm long, lanceolate, sometimes slightly gibbous-based, the apex obtuse or acute; flowers 3-10 on nearly erect, farinose, purplish-green pedicels; calyx 4-6.5 mm long, puberulent and farinose, sometimes with purplish blotches, lobed about 1/3 to 1/2 of its length, apex of the lobes generally acute; corolla tube 4-7 mm long, lobes 3-5 mm long and deeply bifid, white with yellow fomnices; fruit a capsule; n = 9.

description: Plants covered with white farina in youth, usually becoming glabrous with age. Scapes 2-40 cm tall, frequently ascapose at first flowering with scape greatly elongating in age. Leaves variable, lanceolate to elliptical, 0.7-3 cm wide; margins entire to dentate or serrate; petioles winged or obsolete. Involucral bracts lanceolate, 0.2-1 cm long, acute or obtuse at the tip, of unequal width. Umbel (3) 5-20 flowered, blooming asynchronously; pedicels 0.3-3 cm long. Flowers homostylous. Calyx green or greenish-black, 0.5-0.7 cm long, divided nearly to the base with lanceolate teeth. Corolla rose-magenta, tube 1-1.5 cm long at anthesis, strongly exserted from the calyx; limb to 1.5 cm diam; lobes entire or slightly emarginate. Stigmas broadly capitate to bilobed, at anthesis located at or just below the annulus; anthers adjacent. Pollen ca 22 µm diam; exine reticulate, 3-syncolpate. Capsule cylindrical at maturity, to 3 times the length of the calyx. Seeds 1-2 mm long, medium brown, vesiculate. Chromosome number: 2n = 22 (Alaska. Cape Prince of Wales: Kelso 83-288. St. Matthew Island: Martin s.n. in 1985, both at ALA. Also reported in Johnson & Packer, 1968; Zhukova, 1966, 1969, 1982; Zhukova & Tikhonova, 1971, 1973; Zhukova et al., 1973).

description: Plants completely efarinose, glabrous. Scapes to 10 cm tall. Leaves to 4 cm long, less than 0.4 cm wide, linear-lanceolate, entire or remotely dentate at the apex; petioles obsolete. Involucral bracts lanceolate, to 1 cm long, acute or obtuse at tip, flat at the base. Umbel 1-3 flowered; pedicels 0.2-1 cm long. Flowers distylous. Calyx green or greenish-black, 0.5-0.7 cm long, deeply divided by narrow teeth. Corolla rose-magenta, the tube equal in length to the calyx; limb to 1.2 cm diam; lobes usually entire, sometimes cleft to the base. Stamens ca 1 mm long, anthers 0.3-0.5 cm below the throat of the corolla in pin plants. Stigma capitate, in pin plants located near throat of corolla tube, in thrum plants positions reciprocal. Pollen ca 17 µm diam in pin plants, ca 22 ,um diam in thrum plants; exine reticulate, 3-syncolpate. Capsule cylindrical at maturity, twice the length of the calyx. Seeds 1-2 mm long, medium brown, vesiculate. Chromosome number 2n = 22 (Kelso 83-103 at ALA; Zhukova, 1982).

description: Aquatic or semi-aquatic, mostly rooted plants with dimorphic fronds. Sterile fronds lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate to deltoid to cordate in shape, (2.0-) 6.5-59.0 (mean: 30.5) cm long, 1.3-20 (mean: 8.1) cm wide; stipes (0.2-) 2-31 (mean: 12.8) cm long, 0.7-8.0 (mean: 2.9) mm wide at their broadest point near the base; blades (1.8) 4.5-41 (mean: 18.7) cm long, pinnate to frequently bipinnate with deeply incised pinnules to tripinnate; pinnae lobed or incised, elliptic to lanceolate to ovate to deltoid in shape, 1.0-12.5 (mean: 5.5) cm long; lowermost pinnae inserted mostly alternately on the stipe; bud initials frequent in pinnule sinuses, mostly dormant on living fronds. description: Epiphytic to epipetric; rhizome horizontal, short-creeping, ca 1 mm diam; rhi- zome scales golden, narrowly deltate, entire, shining, ca 3 mm long; phyllopodia lacking; sterile fronds 3-16 cm long, 1-2 cm broad; stipe 3/8-5/8 of the frond length, stramineous; stipe scales abundant, occasionally sparse, spreading, stramineous, lanceolate, entire to denticulate, lustrous, 1-2.5 mm long; blade lanceolate to widely ovate in juvenile fronds, base inequilaterally to equilaterally cordate to truncate, apex generally notched with bud, sometimes poorly developed; veins rarely distinct, 1.5 mm apart, running at ca 50 degree angle to the midvein; hydathodes evident; blade scales sparse on both sides, spreading, lanceolate, dis- tantly serrate, stramineous, sometimes appearing iridescent, 0.5-1.5 mm long, sometimes more dense on midvein and margin; fertile frond the same length as the sterile, but the stipe is ca 3/4-4/5 of the frond length, blade elliptic to widely ovate, base truncate to cuneate, apex rounded; intersporangial scales abundant, golden, lustrous, lanceolate, denticulate, ca 2 mm long, somewhat more dense along midvein and margin; spores perforate with low, narrow crests (Fig. 15).

description: Aquatic, mostly floating but sometimes rooted. Sterile fronds deltoid to ovate to cordate in shape, 8-33 (mean: 16.6) cm long, 5-24 (mean: 10.9) cm wide; stipes 1-19 (mean: 6.3) cm long, 4-17 (mean: 10.4) mm wide at their broadest point; blades 5-19 (mean: 10.1) cm long, mostly simple and palmately 3-lobed or pinnately 5-lobed, sometimes pinnate near the base; lowermost pinnae or veins of lobes in- serted mostly opposite on the stipe; bud initials commonly developing into plantlets attached to living fronds. description: Aquatic and subaquatic, mostly rooted. Sterile fronds mostly deltoid to ovate to lanceolate in shape, 8-45 (mean: 29.1) cm long, 3-24 (mean: 13.3) cm wide; stipes 3-15 (mean: 11.5) cm long, 0.8-6.5 (-12) (mean: 4.2) mm wide at their broadest point; blades 5-31 (mean: 16.1) cm long, pinnate-pinnatifid to bipinnate with deeply incised pinnules; pinnae deltoid to ovate in shape, 1.6-14 (mean: 7.2) cm long; lowermost pinnae mostly inserted alternately on the stipe; bud initials mostly dormant on living fronds. Fertile fronds erect, deltoid to ovate to lanceolate in shape, longer than sterile fronds, 15-86 (mean: 45.4) cm long, 4.5-30 (mean: 15.1) cm wide; stipes 6-41 (mean: 20.3) cm long, 0.5-11.0 (mean: 3.8) mm wide at their broadest point; blades 8.5-51 (mean: 25.9) cm long, 4- to 5-pinnate below in larger fronds, bipinnate above, with narrowly deltoid to deltoid pinnae, the lowermost commonly inserted alternately on the stipe; terminal segments linear-acute to linear- attenuate to lanceolate in shape, 0.3-7 (mean: 2.9) cm long, 0.7-2 (mean: 1.3) mm wide, with margins inrolled to enclose 1-4 rows of mature sporangia; sporangia with 14-64 (mean: 39.9) indurated annulus cells; spores 16 per sporangium, 107- 150 (mean: 129) µm in distal diameter.

description: Rhizome creeping with upturned tip, often growing around a tree trunk so as to form a "shelf"; woody portion 4(-7) mm thick, completely enveloped and hidden by a dense mat of long scales, resulting in a composite diameter of 3-7 cm, thickest at rhizome tip. Scales light to dark brown, linear-lanceolate, 1.5-2 mm wide, 1.5-3 (-4.5) cm long, shiny and quite smooth (Fig. 27) to crinkled and twisted in upper portion (Fig. 28). Stipe glabrous, slender, 2-3 mm thick, 2-13(-26) cm long; phyllopodium more or less immersed in rhizome scales. Sterile lamina (11-)20-35(-40) cm long, (2-)3-4(-6.5) cm wide, oblanceolate to narrowly elliptic or even linear, with apex obtuse to acute and base cuneate or narrowly decurrent; both surfaces quite glabrous; veins prominent to obscure (depending on thickness of lamina), parallel and free (Fig. la). Fertile lamina narrowly elliptic to linear, with acute apex; stipe (6-)14-26 cm long, lamina 14-26(-30) cm long, 1.6-3 cm wide. Chromosome number: n = 41 (Wagner 65246). Fig. 33.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, William R. & Crosby, M. R. 1966. A revision of the Hawaiian species of Elaphoglossum. Brittonia. 18: 380-397.

description: Rhizome creeping, 4-10 mm thick, with scales varying in shape and size from tiny, triangular, 1-2 mm long and with an irregular cell-net to linear-lanceolate, 1-2 cm long and with regular tissue of rectangular cells, and varying in color from black to light brown and translucent; scale margins sparsely glandular-ciliate, especially in var. parvisquameum. Sterile frond narrowly elliptic to broadly oblanceolate or spatulate, apex acute to acuminate, lamina decurrent below forming wing along some or all of stipe; lower stipe bearing scales similar to rhizome scales but usually smaller. Lamina thin, veins distinct, parallel and free to margin, there arching and uniting to form a continuous intramarginal vein (Fig. 1c); surfaces often bearing minute squamules, especially abundant on abaxial surface and midrib. Sterile frond exceedingly variable in size: Unwinged stipe 1-7(-10) cm long; lamina, including winged portion of stipe, 15-55(-80) cm long, 3-8.5(-11) cm wide. Fertile frond with apex acute, lamina decurrent, forming a very narrow sterile wing to much of stipe; total frond length (18-)23-62 cm long; lamina 2-4 cm wide; sporangia not extending beyond intramarginal vein, leaving a sterile membranous stramineous border 1-2 mm wide.

description: Rhizome woody, 5-10 mm thick, densely clothed with closely imbricated scales; composite diameter (rhizome + stipe bases + scales) 1-2.5 cm. Scales lanceolate, 1-1.5(-2) cm long, 1.5-4 mm wide at base, light brown to reddish brown to black, with margin usually lighter than center; margin abundantly ciliate (Fig. 6-7). Stipes crowded at tip of rhizome. Stipe (2.5-)4-10(-27) cm long, rounded, often bearing scattered scales persistent on base and above. Sterile lamina (7.5-)16-25 (-50) cm long, (1.5-)3-5(-7.5) cm wide, broadly oblong-lanceolate, with blunt tip (acute in largest specimens). Lamina quite thick and brittle; veins indistinct in fresh material, bifurcating and anastomosing freely throughout to produce a conspicuous reticulum (Fig. lb); surfaces never scaly, but sometimes squamulose. Fertile frond with stipe (8-)15-32 cm long; lamina (1.5-)2-4(-4.5) cm wide and often same length as sterile lamina, (8-)16-30(-37) cm long. Cf. Fig. 36. Chromosome number: n = 41 (Wagner 65247). Fig. 31.

description: Epiphytic. Rhizome 5-8 mm wide, short-creeping, scaly, brown; scales 3-6 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, reddish brown, with a few distant cilia, the apex attenuate, flexuous. Sterile leaves 20-65 cm long, 1-2 mm apart; phyllopodia present, 0.5-1 cm long; petioles 1/3-1/2 the length of the sterile leaf, stramineous to tan or light brown; scales reduced to resinous dots or 0.8-2 mm long, lanceolate, light brown, sometimes also with substellate scales; laminae 15-45x1.5-3 cm, narrowly elliptic, chartaceous to coriaceous, the base gradually tapered, ending well above the phyllopodia, the apex attenuate to acuminate; veins conspicuous, 1 mm apart, at an angle of 75° with respect to the costa, the apices free; hydathodes absent; lamina scales on the abaxial surface of the laminae reduced to resinous dots, those on the adaxial surface and the margin less than 0.5 mm long, substellate, appressed or subappressed, thin, pale, with irregular teeth; marginal scales caducous (most easily seen on young leaves), 0.2-0.3 mm long, entire or subentire. Fertile leaves ca. equalling the sterile; petioles 2/3 the length of the fertile leaf, tan to brown; laminae 0.4-1 cm wide, linear, adaxially scaly, the base narrowly cuneate, the apex acuminate.

description: Epiphytic, rarely terrestrial; rhizome compact, horizontal to erect, ca 5 mm diam; rhizome scales linear-lanceolate, entire, castaneous, lustrous, 5-6 mm long; phyllopodia lacking; fronds clumped; sterile fronds 9-32 cm long, 1.4-5.8 cm broad; stipe 1/10-1/3 of the frond length, stramineous; stipe scales abundant, subulate, spreading, light brown, 2-3 mm long; blade narrowly lanceolate, base rounded to broadly truncate, apex generally notched with retuse bud, rarely acuminate and nonproliferous; veins distinct to indistinct, 1.5-2 mm apart, running at 70 degree angle to the midvein; hydathodes evident; blade scales sparse on both surfaces, subulate, spreading, 2-3 mm long, more dense along midvein and margin; fertile fronds slightly longer than the sterile, narrowly lanceolate, with stipe ca 3/4 of the frond length, 15-30 cm long, blade 0.9-2.5 cm broad, base cuneate, apex acuminate; intersporangial scales subulate, 2-3 mm long; spores perforate, verrucate (Figs. 7, 8).

description: Rhizome creeping, 2-6 mm thick, bearing few to many appressed scales but becoming naked with age. Scales membraifous, broadly lanceolate, 2-5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, centers black to light brown, margins brown to stramineous and bearing multicellular gland-tipped cilia. Great variation in size and shape of sterile fronds. Stipes 3-15 cm long, inserted 3-9 mm apart, stramineous except for phyllopodia, bearing scattered scales similar to rhizome scales but broader and less pigmented. Sterile lamina 1-2.2 cm wide, coriaceous, glabrous or bearing a few scattered scales, especially along abaxial midrib; one or both surfaces often bearing tiny squamules (probably scale bases persisting from the fiddlehead); veins obscure, parallel and free (Fig. la); margins (ca. 1 mm) yellowish or colorless, revolute. Laminae of smaller specimens 8-12 cm long, elliptic with obtuse to acute apices and only slightly decurrent bases; laminae of larger specimens 12-26 cm long, linear and narrowing gradually to acute apices and winged stipes. Fertile fronds with stipes 4-24 cm long and laminae 4-20 cm long, 1-2 cm wide; margin colorless, sterile, and often revolute upon outer sporangia. Chromosome number: n = 41 (Wagner 65317). Fig. 32.

description: Rhizome scales 5-8 mm long, brown to brownish orange, narrowly lanceolate, spreading. Leaves 25-80 cm long; petioles to 20 cm long, 1/3-3/4 the length of the laminae, non-alate to narrowly alate; laminae not or only slightly reduced basally, the apical pinna continuous with (i.e., not articulate to) the rachis; pinnae 5-9.5 X 1.2-1.6 cm, pairs 11-26, alternate, slightly ascending, oblong, the apices acute and entire or nearly so, the bases subequilateral (slightly reduced on the basiscopic side), cuneate, sessile or nearly so; ra- chises narrowly alate to strongly marginate throughout. Fertile pinnae 2-3 mm wide; paraphyses absent; annular cells ca. 20; spores minutely papillose.

description: Rhizome scales 2-5 mm long, pale brown, lanceolate, spreading. Leaves to 70 cm long; petioles to 17 cm long, 1/7-1/2 the length of the laminae; laminae strongly to slightly reduced at the base, with larger leaves tending to have less reduced bases, usually oblanceolate, with the apical pinna continuous with (not articulate to) the rachis; pinnae 4-11 X 1-1.5(-2) cm, pairs 10-23, alternate, patent, narrowly lanceolate, serrulate throughout (strongly and sharply dentate on small leaves), the base cuneate, equilateral, at least the proximal pairs stalked, the stalks 2-6 mm long, the apices gradually tapered; rachises marginate to narrowly winged. Fertile pinnae 4-8 mm wide; paraphyses absent; annular cells 14 or 15; spores smooth, very pale yellowish to hyaline.

description: Plants small, epiphytic; rhizomes with a heavily sclerenchymatous inner cortex; rhizome scales 2-3 mm long, linear-lanceolate, rounded, truncate, or subcordate basally, mostly acuminate-subulate at the apex, eglandular; cells of rhizome scales generally rectangular or quadrate, 1-3 times as long as broad; fronds 2-10 cm long, erect or arching; xylem of leaf trace in a single arc from origin; foliar trichomes generally absent or occasionally present as multicellular, glandular or eglandular hairs; stipes short or nearly absent, 0.2-0.3 mm in diameter, terete, but soon becoming alate and merging with the lamina; blades coriaceous, linear or sublinear, rounded to acute apically, with an entire, undulate, or slightly crenate margin; lateral veins simple or once-forked; sori 1-2 mm in diameter, usually developed on the upper 1/2-3/4 of the frond; paraphyses consisting of weak, uniseriate hairs lacking a terminal gland in most plants; sporangia with 10-12 thickened bow cells; spores 36-43 µm in diameter.

description: Filix comparate magna, epiphytica; rhizomate dorsiventrali, strato cellularum corticalium dense incrassatarum carenti; squamis rhizomatis 2-4 mm longis, lineari- lanceolatis, basi truncatis vel rotundatis, generatim cellulam glandulosam singularem ad apicem subulatum ferentibus; cellulis squamarum rhizomatis rectangularibus vel fusiformibus, plerumque 2-4plo longioribus quam latioribus; frondibus 10-40 cm longis, pendentibus; trichomatibus foliaribus frondis in omnibus partibus praesentibus, 3-8 cellularum longitudine, cellula terminali saepe eglandulosa; stipitibus vulgo minus quam 1 cm longis, 0.3-1 mm diametro, teretibus vel anguste alatis; laminis profunde pinnatifidis, membranaceis vel subcoriaceis, fere ad costam incisis, linearibus vel sublinearibus, ad utrasque extremitates angustatis, absque segmento terminali caudato; segmentis 5-15 mm longis, approximatis vel dissitis, oblongis vel anguste triangularibus, ad apicem acutis obtusis vel rotundatis, integris crenatis vel serrato- dentatis, margine trichomatibus patulis ciliatis, segmentorum axibus a costa plus minusve ad angulos rectos patentibus; venis in quoque segmento pinnatis; soris plerumque frondium fertilium in parte medio tantum effectis, 1-1.5 mm in diametro, saepe in quoque segmento in duabus seriebus dispositis; sporangiorum annulo 9-11 cellulas incrassatas includenti; sporis 37-42 µm in diametro.

description: Rhizome scales 2-10 mm long (2-5 mm long in Mesoamerica and South America on the western side of the Andes; 4.5-10 mm long elsewhere), dark brown to black, narrowly lanceolate to linear, entire to sparsely ciliate, somewhat spreading or (in Mesoamerica and western Andes) mostly apressed. Leaves to 105 cm long; petioles 8-30 cm long, 1/10-1/4 the length of the laminae; laminae reduced toward the base or (in the Guianas) only slightly so; pinnae 14-22 X 2.8-5 cm, pairs (6-)8-12(-16), alternate to subopposite, patent, lanceolate to oblong, entire, the base broadly rounded to cuneate, occasionally excavate basiscopically, sessile or short-stalked, the stalks (when present) to 3 mm long, the apices acuminate; rachises not alate. Fertile pinnae 1-2 cm wide; paraphyses usually present, when present consisting of branched hair-like scales; annular cells 12-15; spores smooth, very pale yellowish. n = 41 (Walker, 1985).

description: Rhizome scales 1-2.5 mm long, lustrous black with a narrow reddish margin (this often abraded and therefore absent), ovate to lanceolate, sparsely ciliate, appressed. Leaves to 100 cm long; petioles 10-30 cm long, 1/5-1/3 the length of the laminae; lamina not or only slightly reduced toward the base, with the apical pinna continuous with the rachis (i.e., not articulate); pinnae 13-21 X 3.2-5.5 cm, pairs 5-10, alternate, patent, elliptic to lanceolate, entire, the base cuneate, occasionally excavate basiscopically, at least the proximal pairs stalked, the stalks (2-)3-6 mm long, the apices acuminate to abruptly narrowed and subcaudate; rachises not alate. Fertile pinnae 0.7-1.6 cm wide; paraphyses absent; annular cells 13-15; spores pale yellowish spiny, the spines numerous, about 1/2 the length of the spore.

description: Trunks to 10(-15) m high and 12 cm diam., without persistent petiole bases, but with a thick, cobwebby cover of light brown to tan or gray scales (Fig. 2A) and many black, upward-curved squaminate spines to 2 cm long. Trunk apices surpassing the youngest fronds (i.e., frond buds elevated above the last array of developed fronds). Frond scars well spaced, round to oval, hardly visible between the scales (Fig. 2A). Adventitious buds may occur, growing out into new trunks, forming groups of moderate size. Petioles up to 110 cm long, blackish to dark brown, rarely orange-brown or partly yellowish, with black squaminate spines to 8 mm long. Petiole scales 1.5-15 X 0.3 mm, light brown with a darker central stripe, only one apical seta per scale (Fig. IF); setae to 1.5(-2) mm long, often shorter than 1 mm. Laminae to 270 X 90 cm, bipinnate-pinnatifid, apices abruptly reduced and mostly pinna-like. Rhachis brown to tan, with brown scurf and small black squaminate spines in the proximal half. Costae and costules with scattered ciliate squamules (Fig. 1G) abaxially, and some white lanceolate scales with one apical seta (Fig. IC, arrow), especially on the costules. Pinnae short-stalked (Fig. 1A), acuminate (Fig. 1E), distally green-alate, the wings at least slightly arcuate (Fig. 1E, arrow); pinnules short-stalked to sessile, acuminate (Fig. IB); fertile and sterile segments plane, their margins serrate at least at the tips (Fig. 1C); short trichomes on both surfaces near the margin, especially to- wards the sinuses, on and between the veins (Fig. 1C). Sterile veins simple, rarely forked; fertile veins forked or simple (Fig. 1C), some with short trichomes or minute squamules abaxially (Fig. 1G). Sori costal; indusia cyatheoid to urceolate [rarely subsphaeropteroid (Fig. 1H) or sphaeropteroid], with some septate trichomes (Fig. ID), visible in immature sori. Paraphyses as long as the sporangia, tufted; receptacle globose (Fig. ID). Spores trilete, perispore in ridges.

description: Rhizome moderately creeping, ca 2 mm diam; rhizome scales dense to sparse, ovate-lanceolate, tan with varying degrees of dark, shiny, sclerotic streaking, 2- 4 mm long (deeply cordate, appearing peltate), entire or with occasional small, irregular teeth; phyllopodia distinct; fronds spaced 2-10 mm apart, (4) 9-22 (41) cm long, 0.9-2.6 cm broad; stipe 1/6-1/3 of the frond length, with sparse, tan, ovate scales, at least at the base; blade narrowly elliptic, apex acuminate, base cuneate; coriaceous; veins obscure, free, simple or once-forked, ca 1 mm apart, running at 60-70º angle; hydathodes lacking; adaxial blade surface essentially glabrous, abaxial surface with very slender scales, linear with hastate or stellate base, to deeply stellate; fertile fronds similar to the sterile in blade size and shape but usually somewhat longer; scales lacking on abaxial surface; spores with low ridges.

description: Terrestrial or saxicolous. Rhizome 3-7 mm wide, erect or ascending, scaly, black; scales 13 mm long, lanceolate, black, rigid and flat, entire, the apex often piliform, tortuous. Sterile leaves (10-)17-34 cm long, 1-2 mm apart; phyllopodia present but often weakly defined and hidden by the scales; petioles 1/4-1/3 the length of the sterile leaf, tan to brown; scales present, 0.5-1.5 mm long, lanceolate, dark or light brown, usually spreading, the larger ones often becoming dark first at the apex; laminae (6-) 15-24x0.8-1.6 cm, linear, subcoriaceous, the base narrowly cuneate, ending well above the phyllopodia, the apex obtuse or broadly acute; veins inconspicuous, 1 mm apart, at an angle of 60-75° with respect to the costa, the apices free; hydathodes absent; lamina scales present on both surfaces (some of them reduced to resinous dots), those on the abaxial surface present mainly on the costa, 0.5-1 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, light brown to white, subentire; those on the adaxial surface, 0.30.8 mm long, round to ovate, appressed, thin, pale whitish, entire; marginal scales sparse, 0.5-1 mm long, lanceolate, subentire. Fertile leaves typically longer than the sterile; petioles ca. 2/3 the length of the fertile leaf, tan to brown; laminae (6-)8-11 cm wide, linear to narrowly elliptic, scaly, the base narrowly cuneate, the apex obtuse to broadly acute.

description: Rhizome scales 5-10 mm long, whitish, narrowly lanceolate to linear, spreading. Leaves 30-50(-60) cm long; petioles 3-20 cm long, 1/10-1/3 the length of the laminae; laminae widest basally (at least on large leaves); pinnae 6-12 x 1.2-2 cm, pairs (12-)20-30, alternate to subopposite, patent, oblong to lanceolate, entire or becoming serrate apically, equilateral or nearly so, truncate to broadly rounded (rarely in some specimens from the Chocó region narrowly rounded), sessile or nearly so, the apices acute to acuminate; rachises narrowly winged or marginate distally. description: Rhizome scales 7-15 mm long, whitish, stramineous, or pale orange, lanceolate to linear, ascending and slightly spreading. Leaves 30-80 cm long; petioles 10-25 cm, 1/3-1/2 as long as the lamina, not winged; laminae widest at the base or only slightly reduced, the apical pinna continuous with (i.e., not articulate to) the rachis; pinnae 8-20 X 1-2.7 cm, pairs 12-20, alternate, sessile or nearly so, lanceolate to oblong, usually widest near the middle, sometimes slightly falcate basally, the bases often slightly inequilateral, rounded to narrowly cuneate, the apices acuminate to attenuate, subentire to minutely crenulate to serrulate; rachises exalate or narrowly alate distally; paraphyses absent. Fertile pinnae 2-4 mm wide; annulus cells 14 or 15; spores irregularly crested.

description: Rhizome 1.5-2 cm diam., branching not seen. Frond with normal circinate vernation; basal petiole scales narrow to long-lanceolate, coriaceous, light orangish yellow to light yellowish brown, conform, the cilia short to minute, flaccid; distal petiole scales similar, but broader, chartaceous to papyraceous, light orangish yellow; small petiole scales ovate-caudate, broadly to narrowly lanceolate, orangish yellow. Lamina 15-30 cm long, 2-pinnate, attenuate, chartaceous, dull green adaxially when fresh; rachis without a proliferous bud, the rachis scales orangish yellow. Pinnae 2-8 X 1-2 cm, acute to acuminate, attached at right angles to rachis, the basal pinnae usually as long as or longer than rest; abaxial pinna- rachis scales mostly narrow-lanceolate, deep orangish yellow to orangish yellow, with cilia occasional. Pinnules crenate, often attached at oblique angles, acute to obtuse, flat, the basal acroscopic pinnules longer than next distal, the basal basiscopic pinnules near lamina base shorter than next distal pair; veins all free; short spinules usually developed on most vein tips. Sorus terminal on vein, the true indusium 0.6-1.7 mm diam., peltate, orangish yellow or light yellowish brown.

description: Rhizome slender, ca 1.5 mm diameter, short-creeping, sometimes branched, at least the apices ascending; rhizome scales linear-subulate, ca 2 mm long, bicolored with broad, opaque, sclerotic, dark brown median stripe and very narrow, translucent, hyaline, light brown, entire margins; scale apex slender, elongate, fragile, cells with rather conspicuous reddish crosswalls. Fronds (measurements are from well developed fertile fronds; smaller fronds are frequent) 9-22 cm long; paired, crowded along rhizome, bases arcuate-ascending. Stipe 0.4-0.6 as long as blade, shallowly sulcate or flattened on upper surface, dark castaneous, lustrous, densely covered (at least when young) with light brown, linear to filiform (hair-like) scales, some with irregular, narrow, dark median stripe, the smaller ones laxly curved, some scales with delicate tips bearing a terminal reddish "gland" (this perhaps composed of cell wall material). Vernation non-circinate (developing frond forms a hook, not a coil). Blade elliptic or lance-elliptic, somewhat narrowed at base, gradually tapered to apex, 8.5-16.0 cm long, 2.5-7.0 cm wide, thick-herbaceous, bipinnate to mostly bipinnate-pinnatifid to ca tripinnate; pinnae lanceolate, spreading or ascending, opposite or alternate, ca 9-15 pairs, lower 1 to 2 pairs somewhat reduced, median pinnae ca 2.5-4.0 cm long, 0.7-1.7 cm wide, with 5-8 pairs of pinnules, terminal "segment" elongate, acute to obtuse; pinnules ovate, oblong, or inequilaterally auriculate at distal base, subentire, auriculate, pinnatifid or pinnate, 5-10 mm long, 2-6 mm wide, mostly short petiolulate; upper surface of segments dark green, moderately (when young) to sparsely pubescent with simple (unbranched), filiform, hair-like, light brown, laxly curved scales; lower surface light green, densely (when young) to moderately pubescent with similar scales, the leaf tissue not obscured; crosswalls of the hairlike scales with "tongue-in-groove" arrangement, these conspicuous and reddish. Indusial margin of segments somewhat modified, whitened or translucent, becoming more so near edge, somewhat revolute but spreading at maturity, entire, continuous on segments or lobes. Spores 64 per sporangium, globose, trilete, with rugulose perispore, 33.0-39.0 ,tm in diameter with x = 35.5 ,tm (10 spores measured in lactic acid at 1000x; Mickel 4210).

description: Epiphytic or rarely terrestrial. Rhizome 13 mm wide, compact, glabrous, black, resinous. Sterile leaves 11-30 cm long, 1-2 mm apart; phyllopodia present, 0.6-1 cm long; petioles 1/30-1/5 the length of the sterile leaf, stramineous to tan or light brown; scales absent or reduced to resinous dots; laminae 10-30x 1.2-2 cm, narrowly elliptic or narrowly oblanceolate, papyraceous to chartaceous, the base decurrent all the way to the phyllopodia, the apex obtuse or broadly acute; veins conspicuous or inconspicuous, 1.5-2 mm apart, at an angle of 65° with respect to the costa, the apices free; hydathodes absent; lamina scales reduced to resinous dots, these often on both surfaces but more pronounced on the abaxial side; marginal scales sparse, 0.3-1 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, dissected. description: Epiphytic or rarely terrestrial. Rhizome 2.5-3 mm wide, short- to long-creeping, glabrescent, black, often resinous; scales sometimes present but minute, easily seen in older parts of the rhizome and not in the apex, scales 0.2-0.5 mm long, round, whitish to castaneous, subentire. Sterile leaves (18-)25- 53 cm long, 5-15 mm apart; phyllopodia present, 4-8 cm long; petioles 1 /3-2/5(-1/2) the length of the sterile leaf, stramineous to tan or light brown; scales absent or reduced to resinous dots; laminae 15-30x1.1-2.6 cm, narrowly elliptic, chartaceous, the base evenly or abruptly cuneate, ending well above the phyllopodia, the apex acute to acuminate; veins conspicuous, 1 mm apart, at an angle of 75° with respect to the costa, the apices free; hydathodes absent; lamina scales reduced to resinous dots, often on both surfaces but more pronounced on the abaxial side, sometimes with scattered scales in the abaxial costa, 0.51 mm long, lanceolate, tan, entire; marginal scales caducous (most easily seen on young leaves), 0.1-0.3 mm long, lanceolate, subentire or entire. description: Caudex apparently erect, 3-5 mm. in diameter, densely paleaceous, the scales castaneous at base, purplish above, piliform, 2-4 mm. long, conisisting of 10-20 cells; stipes probably 10 or more per plant, caespitose, subterete, to 50 cm. long, 2-4 mm. in diameter, usually straight, castaneous at base, paler distally, finely striate when dry, densely paleaceous near the base with scales simnilar to those of the caudex; fronds once-pinnate, lanceolate, 25-45 cm. long, 4-7 cm. broad at base, gradually tapering distally; rachis slender, faintly flexuose, with the upper part of the stipe paleaceous (scales piliform, 0.5-1 mm. long, of 2-6 cells); stipes of the pinnae slender, to 1 cm. long, subterete, shallowly canaliculate on each side; pinnae alternate (basal ones occasionally subopposite), 20-24 per side (on young fronds sometimes only about 7 per side), thick-coriaceous, pale green, glabrous above, beneath on veins sparsely and inconspicuously setose (hairs pale or castaneous, 0.2-0.5 mm. long, several-celled), orbicular-reniform, 15- 25 mm. long, 17-35 mm. broad (pinnae toward apex often much smaller), subcordate to obtuse at base, rounded at apex, entire or undulate and slightly recurved to conspicuously revolute at margins, flabellate-veinled, the veins spreading from base, several times forked, 50-100 at margin, elevated on both surfaces; sori linear, 1.5-4 mm. long, produced near apices of veins (usually extending to about 0.5 mm. from margin), often nearly contiguous and forming a conspicuous band, the receptacles slightly sunken in the frond tissue; sporangia oblong-ellipsoid, 0.4-0.6 mm. long, subsessile; cells of the anilulus with conspicuous castaneous walls; paraphyses abundant, castaneous, longer than the sporangia (0.5-0.8 mm. long), 5-8-celled.

description: Trunks to 4 m high and 10-15 (-20) cm diam., with persistent old petiole bases in small plants (-2 m high), but balding when older and larger (Fig. 3A). Trunk apices hidden in a fascicle of young petioles (Fig. 3A); new fronds expanding subsequently in small plants, simultaneously by 4-5 in large ones. Frond scars ovate-elliptic (Fig. 3A), often hardly visible between the trunk scales. Ad- ventitious buds absent. Petioles 25-60 cm long, brown to stramineous, rarely darker, aculeate to verrucate (Fig. 3B), with inconspicuous brown scurf of appressed lacerate squamules (Fig 3B, C), and sometimes with small appressed hairs. Petiole scales (1.6-)3-5(- 8.2) x (7-)20-26(-36) mm, concolorous brown or concordantly bicolorous with margins tan or rarely whitish (Fig. 3D), lustrous, lacking marginal setae or teeth. Laminae to 80-160 cm x 60-110 cm, opaque, light green, bipinnate-pinnatifid, apices gradually reduced. Rhachises brown to tan or stramineous, inermous or sparsely verrucate, with dense pubescence of pluricellular whitish to tan hairs to 1.2 mm long; adaxial hairs antrorse, rigid, persistent, abaxial hairs spreading, flaccid, some catenate, persistent to glabrescent, leaving smooth or scabrous surfaces. Pinnae sessile to short-stalked to 4 mm, acuminate (Fig. 3E), distally greenalate, the wings at least slightly arcuate. Costae and costules tan to stramineous, iner- mous, densely hairy like rhachis, but hairs shorter (0.6-0.8 mm). Pinnules 50-75(-90) x 10-15(-17) mm, sessile to subsessile with stalk to 1 mm, truncate to rounded basally, linear-oblong to linear-obovate, acuminate apically (Fig. 3F); segments plane, weakly falcate, the margins weakly or deeply crenate to serrate (Fig. 3G); white pluricellular hairs (0.4-0.6 mm) on and between the veins abax- ially and adaxially (Fig. 3G), abundant and equally distributed on both sides to nearly glabrous with more real hairs adaxially than abaxially (here substituted by short appressed trichomidia); few to many bullate squamules, 0.6-1.0 mm (Fig. 3H), shiny auburn to orange brown, rarely paler to whitish, on costules and larger veins abaxially. Sterile veins simple or forked; fertile veins forked, rarely simple (Fig. 3G). Sori costal, in vein forks; indusia sphaeropteroid (Fig. 3G), lustrous brown to auburn, firm, persisting as fragments, each with an apical umbo; paraphyses as long as the sporangia. Spores trilete, exospore smooth, porate near the laesura, perispore finely baculate (Fig. 2C).

description: Rhizome scales 7-10 mm long, whitish to dark reddish, lanceolate to linear, ascending- spreading. Leaves 30-100 cm long; petioles 8-25 cm, 1/3-1/2 as long as the lamina,  not winged; laminae not or only slightly reduced basally, the apical pinna continuous with (i.e., not articulate to) the rachis; pinnae 8-20 X 1-3 cm, pairs 12-20, alternate, stalked, the stalks to 5 mm, lanceolate to oblong, broadly rounded to narrowly cuneate basally, entire or nearly so but often serrulate apically, the apices acuminate to attenuate; rachises marginate or narrowly alate distally; paraphyses absent. Fertile pinnae 4-10 mm wide; annular cells 14 or 15; spores crested.

description: This species has dark brown to blackish large petiolar scales with well-defined dull whitish, erose to setose margins, whitish to orange, dentate, lanceolate small petiolar scales, and long, narrow, orange to brown, dentate rachis scales that often have a black basal spot. The leaves are up to 110 x 25 cm, with 25-30 pinnule-pairs per pinna, and pinnules to 10 X 6 mm. Some specimens bear buds on the bases of distal pinnae. Polystichum mexiae is known from the type and several other collections from Ecuador, and three Bolivian collections; it is to be expected in Peru and Colombia. It grows at 2100-3200 m in humid montane forests.

description: Shoots erect, indeterminate, 12-45 cm tall, becoming long-decumbent, evergreen with long-trailing senescent portion turning brown; juvenile and mature portions similar without strong annual constrictions. Stem (without leaves) 2-3 mm diam. Juvenile bud erect. Gemmiphores and gemmae produced mostly among the sporophylls (mostly in the terminal 1/3 of the fertile zone), less frequently in the 1-8 mm breaks between fer- tile regions. Gemmae 5-6 x 3-4 mm, lateral lobes broadly obtuse, 1.7 mm wide. Leaves spreading-reflexed, dark-green, lustrous, stomates on both abaxial and adaxial surfaces; leaves all more or less linear, 5-7 mm long, 1.3-1.6 mm wide with entire margin. Spores 31-42 µm diam. (ave. 37).

description: Plants 4-11 cm tall, with short slender erect rhizome bearing several long fleshy roots and usually one or two leaves during a single growing season. Vegetative reproduction common, by means of modified long slender roots 1.2-1.6 mm diam., buds from these giving rise to new plants. Common stalk 1-6 cm long. Blade thin in texture, lanceolate-ovate, or elliptical-ovate, acute to obtuse at apex, narrowly to broadly cuneate to rounded at base, cuneate into a short haft or sessile, 2.0-4.5 x 0.8-2.0 cm. Venation reticulate with included veins few, areoles mostly elongate. Fertile stalk 1.5-5 cm long, equalling or slightly longer than the sterile blade. Fertile spike 0.6-2.0 cm long.

description: Plants epipetric. Ventral leaves appressed, imbricate, buff to light brown or golden-brown, thin-charta- ceous, lanceolate, 2.5-3.5 x 0.5-0.9 mm (wider at middle); base rounded to subcordate, weakly decurrent, pubescent or some- times glabrescent; apex acuminate, short- aristate, arista hyaline, white-hyaline to yellowish, edges dentate, 0.13-0.35 mm; margins ciliate, cilia hyaline, spreading at proximal half, short-ciliate to serrate to- ward apex, cilia or teeth ascending, 0.06- 0.16 mm. description: Plants terrestrial or epipetric. Stems erect from a creeping or decumbent rhizomatous and stoloniferous base, to 45 cm tall, 1-2 mm diam. (on erect stems) or 0.2-0.85 mm diam. (on creeping stems), not articulate, light-green to straw-colored, 2-4-branched; stolons restricted to lowermost part of stem; apex of both stem and branches often fla- gelliform, flagelliform tips usually long-creeping, touching ground and sending up erect frond-like branches or sometimes found as creeping mature stems, which eventually send up erect, frond-like branches. description: Stems prostrate, creeping, 4-10 cm long, rooting from the top (dorsal) surface at branch divergences, ca 0.5 mm in diameter, subarticulate (see discussion), stramineous, monostelic; leaves fairly stiff, on main stems openly disposed, not overlapping, on branches the median leaves imbricate, the lateral ones not overlapping, the two surfaces ± concolorous, epidermal cells ± rectangular, ca 4-8: 1, with strongly wavy walls, the eligular surface with small, serially arranged papillae, in (1) 2 rows, over the cell lumina, the ligular surface smooth, bordered by 1-3 rows of pale, linear, thick-walled cells, the border papillose almost to base, shortly serrate above, the teeth becoming shorter and denser toward apex, the cells forming serrations without papillae; lateral leaves ovate to oblong-ovate, 1.3-1.9 mm long, attached basally, obtuse to acute or sometimes obtuse-mucronate, stomata on both surfaces restricted to vicinity of midrib, asymmetric, the marginal serrations usually extending further down basiscopic margin than acroscopic one, the midrib ending 0.08-0.15 mm from leaf apex; median leaves oblong-ovate, 1.2-1.7 mm long, peltately attached, the basiscopic portion with a single, broad, irregularly rounded "auricle," gradually acute to short-acuminate, the apex mostly obtuse, stomata on ligular surface extending to the margin, those on eligular surface restricted to vicinity of midrib, asymmetric, the outer (basiscopic) margin broader, the inner (acroscopic) margin with teeth extending further down, the "auricle" on the outer side of leaf; axillary leaves similar to lateral ones except with a single, small auricle; strobili 2-3 mm long, ca 1.5 mm wide, sporophylls only slightly dimorphic, erect to erect-spreading, ovate, keeled, 1.2-2.1 mm long, gradually tapered to an obtuse or rarely acute apex, finely serrate almost to base, the eligular surface with (1) 2 rows of serially arranged papillae over the cell lumina, without stomata, the ligular surface smooth, the stomata restricted to trench formed by the thickened keel, midrib ending ca 0.25 mm below apex, margins bordered by a single row of smooth cells, almost each protruding to form a tooth; megasporangium basal, single, megaspores bone-white, 430-575 µm in diameter, low-reticulate; most sporophylls above without sporangia, rarely with a single microsporangium near apex of strobilus, microspores dark-cream to light-tan in mass, 20-26 ,um in diameter, smooth to finely papillose.

description: Quantitative measurements (Fig. 2) also document the hybrid's intermediacy. Counts of the number of pinnate lateral pinnae on one side of the blade showed that Adiantum latifolium had 1-4 pinnate pinnae, A. petiolatum had none, and the hybrid had 1 or (more frequently) 2. Also intermediate was the number of pinnules on the acroscopic side of the basal pinnae: A. latifolium had 7-15 pinnules, A. petiolatum had none, and the hybrid had 1-4. The hybrid was also intermediate in lamina length, internode length, and length of the basal pinnae (Fig. 2). The spores of the hybrid were examined with a light microscope and appeared malformed. They were usually concave or dimpled on the distal face and often remained stuck together in tetrads. They never became shriveled and blackened like the spores of hybrids in many other fern genera.

description: Epiphytic or saxicolous. Rhizome 2-3 mm wide, short-creeping, glabrous, black, highly resinous. Sterile leaves 15-25 cm long, 14 mm apart; phyllopodia present, 0.2-0.9 cm long; petioles 1/4-1/2 the length of the sterile leaf, tan to brown; scales absent or reduced to resinous dots, rarely with a few minute (ca. 1 mm) dark scales toward the base; laminae 5-16(-20) x 0.6-1.5 cm, linear, papyraceous to chartaceous, the base narrowly cuneate, ending well above the phyllopodia, the apex gradually tapered and narrowly acute or rarely short-acuminate; veins inconspicuous, 1 mm apart, at an angle of 65° with respect to the costa, the apices free; hydathodes absent; lamina scales reduced to resinous dots, these often on both surfaces but more pronounced on the abaxial side. Fertile leaves usually longer than the sterile; petioles 1/3-1/2 the length of the fertile leaf, tan to brown; laminae 0.4-0.8 cm wide, linear, glabrous, the base cuneate, the apex acute.

description: Plants terrestrial.
