description: To Brause's incomplete description I can add: A mighty species of the section of G. glauca (Hicriopteris Presl), according to Brause 7-8 m. high; Mr. Brass says: "conspicuous, rambling amongst forest fringe bushes and small trees; fronds 4-5 m., with 6-8 or more pairs of large spreading pinnae.'" The horizontally creeping rhizome is 5-7 mm. thick with few wiry roots, terete, brown, densely clothed with castaneous, glossy, ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, finely ciliate, thick scales, which when f alling leave raised points, the rhizome therefore asperous as is the basal portion of the stipe; this is pure brown, terete with a shallow furrow above, 5 mm. thiek and several decimeters long; the termninal eireinate bud densely paleaceous with dark castaneous, glossy, lanceolate, ciliate-dentate scales and subtended by 1-2 small adventive pinnae. Pinnae opposite, about 1 m. long by 30 cm. wide, the rachises of 2-3-4 order stramineous, densely covered on both sides with a rieddish tomentumn consisting of smnall fringed often stellate scales, easily abraded; pinnules II. ord. horizontal, alternate, sessile, up to 15 cm. long, 3 cmn. wide, the ultimate pinnules horizontal, separated at base, linear, 2.5 mm. wide, roundish-obtuse, entire, the margins subrevolute; sporangia when young tomentum.

description: Rhizome dark brown, creeping, 1-2 mm thick, bearing many light to dark brown, stiff, linear-lanceolate scales, 0.25 mm wide and 2-3(-4) mm long (Fig. 8-9), or older portions of rhizome becoming naked. description: Thalictrum cooleyi is a very slender-stemmed, glabrous plant averaging 47 cm in height with an infloreseence averaging 7 cm in length. The very lax stems are usually supported by surrounding vegetation. The caudex is short with a fibrous root system. The 3-5 basal leaves are mostly 2-ternate, rarely 3- or 1-ternate. The three or four, rarely five, cauline leaves decrease rapidly upward both in size and in number of divisions, and are separated from one another by long internodes. The upper leaves, usually 1-ternate, are frequently sessile, occasionally subsessile or on short petioles up to 1 cm long. The leaflets, glaucous beneath, have revolute margins and are quite different from those of most other Thalictra in being very strikingly narrow and only occasionally lobed, particularly on the cauline leaves. The terminal leaflet of each division averages 15 mm in length and 7 mm in width on basal leaves, 20.5 mm in length and 4 mm in width on cauline leaves. Of the 58 terminal leaflets from which the above measurements were made, 15 were 3-lobed, 4 were 2-lobed and the remaining 39 were unlobed. The lateral leaflets of each division average 12 mm in length and 6 mm in width on basal leaves, and 16 mm in length and 4 mm in width on the cauline leaves. Of the 111 lateral leaflets measured, 10 were 3-lobed, 11 were 2-lobed and 90 were unlobed. The flowers are borne in an open panicle on pedicels up to 2 cm long. The sepals of staminate flowers, pale yellowish to white in color, are about 1.5 mm long and are very early deciduous. The filaments, slightly clavate, are pale lavender, 2-3 mm long. The lance-oblong anthers are obtuse, 1.5 mm long, and bright yellow. The pistillate flowers are greenish, with smaller sepals and pubescent stigmas, 1.5-2 mm long, as long as or longer than the glabrous ovary. The achenes are ellipsoid, sessile or subsessile, 4.5-6 mm long and 1.5-2.5 mm wide and glabrous with 8-10 prominent, sinuous ribs. The stigmas remain oni the fruit to maturity. Only a few (1-6) fruiting heads mature in each inflorescence. The fruiting pedicels are very variable, ranging from 2 to 48 mm in length.
bibliographicCitation: Ahles, Harry E. 1959. Thalictrum cooleyi sp. nov. Brittonia. 11: 68-70.

description: Aerial stems usually elongating 0.1-1.5 (-3.5) m, occasionally short and tufted. Leaves membranous, usually completely biternate, the divisions sessile or petiolulate. description: Stout herb, the caudex subterranean or short erect, probably not more than 10 cm. high and in diameter; leaves coriaceous, oblong-obovate, 20-40 cm. long, 3-5 cm. broad, long attenuate proximally to 6-15 mm., acute or subacute at apex, entire at margins, cinereous tomentose on both surfaces, less densely above, the costa stout, the secondary nerves 1 or 2 per centimeter, spreading, visible beneath, the veinlets immersed; flowering branches erect, up to 2 m. high, cinereous tomentose, at length glabrous, much-branched towards apex, corymbose-paniculate, the branches opposite, subtended by linear-oblong foliaceous bracts 2-7 cm. long and 4—8 mm. broad; heads crowded, at maturity 10-20 mm. in diameter; phyllaries about 25, 2- or 3-seriate, papyraceous, ovate-oblong, acute, the outer ones 5-7 mm. long, 3-4 mm. broad, tomentose without; ray florets numerous, 2- or 3-seriate, the corolla about 5 mm. long, the tube about 1.5 mm. long, frequently bearing 2 minute lobes introrsely distally, pilose, the lamina oblong, about 2 mm. broad, 3-lobed at apex, the style and stigmas 2.5-3 mm. long, the achene about 2 mm. long; disk florets sparsely strigose, about 6 mm. long, the tube slightly shorter than the limb, the lobes ovate-deltoid, the stamens about 4 mm. long; paleae membranous, stramineous, oblong-oblanceolate, about 6 mm. long and 2.5 mm. broad, rounded at apex, essentially glabrous.

description: Shrub or tree 1.5-12 m tall, to 33 cm dbh, the bark pale, the indument on petioles and peduncles frequently visible to the naked eye, composed usually of at least some erect or ascending, ± straight trichomes (the longest 0.3-1 mm) and often also of shorter, ± curled trichomes, rarely only of the latter and then indument not visible to the naked eye. Leaflet-blade acuminate at apex, usually pubescent on margin and midrib, sometimes also with scattered trichomes on secondary and lower order veins on abaxial surface, usually without domatia in axils of secondary veins, these when present with shallow, crescent-shaped openings, usually not visible to the naked eye, the terminal blade usually elliptic, 11.1- 27.2 X 3.6-16.1 cm, usually acute (rarely cuneate) at base, with 6-11 secondary veins per side, its petiolule 0.7-2.9 cm long, the lateral blades often elliptic, 6.7-24.7 X 2.1- 11.6 cm, asymmetric at base (usually rounded or obtuse basiscopically and acute acroscopically), with 5-10 secondary veins per side, their petiolules 0.2-1 cm long; petiole 4.7-15.9 cm long. Inflorescence 7.5- 21.5 cm long including a peduncle 7-20 cm long, the internodes of primary rachis not developed, the partial inflorescences borne at apex of peduncle, stalked, dichasial at first node, dichasial or monochasial at higher nodes (as many as four levels observed), the secondary axis 3-65 mm long; pedicels 1.5-4 mm long. Calyx distinctly dentate, 0.8-2 mm long, pubescent with short, appressed or erect trichomes without, glabrous within. Corolla rounded or obtuse in bud, 5-merous, 50-68 mm long at anthesis, pubescent with curved appressed trichomes and some straight erect trichomes without, white, the tube formed by coherent petals 40-54 mm long, 1.7-3 mm wide just above the calyx, 3.6-6 times longer than the lobes, these 8-12.5 X 1.5-2.5 mm, inflexed at apex. Androecium of 5 fertile stamens (in Lima 587 of 4 fertile stamens and 1 staminode); filaments 45.5-54 mm long, coherent for the length of and tightly adherent to the corolla tube, glabrous or sparsely villous adaxially within the corolla tube, the free part 3-6 mm long; anther including sterile base and appendage 3.3-5 mm long, the fertile portion 1.8-2.1 X 0.7-1.1 mm, the basal sterile portion 0.8-1.8 mm long, the appendage 0.1-0.6 mm long, entire or slightly notched. Disc 1-1.1 mm high, slightly shorter than the ovary. Carpels ca. 1.1 mm high, glabrous but becoming ±pubescent after anthesis; style 55-58 mm long. Fruiting mericarps 11-12 X ca. 10 mm, glabrous or minutely erect-pubescent and glabrescent except for adjacent lateral surfaces. Seed (mature not seen).

description: Shrub or tree sometimes unbranched, 1.5- 6 m tall. Leaves 1 foliolate; blade oblanceolate, narrow-obovate, elliptic, or narrow elliptic, acuminate (rarely rounded) at apex, cuneate or acute at base, 15-40 cm long, 5 - 14.3 cm wide, with 9-18 secondary veins per side; petiole terete or flattened adaxially, 3.3-12.8 cm long, glabrescent; smaller leaves below inflorescence wide-elliptic, elliptic, or narrow-obovate, acuminate or acute at apex, rounded, acute or decurrent at base, 3.2- 12.5 cm long, 2.1-5.7 cm wide, with 7-8 secondary veins per side and a petiole 0.9- 4 cm long. Inflorescence imperfectly twice dichotomous; peduncle 6.2-21 cm long, with branches 3.8-13 cm long, densely appressed-puberulent; bracts subtending pedicels very early deciduous, to 6 mm long, appressed-puberulent; pedicels 0.6-0.9 cm in flower, 0.9-1.3 cm in fruit, appressed puberulent. Sepals lanceolate (rarely nar- row-ovate), 2-4.1 cm long, 0.5-1.0 cm wide, in bud minutely appressed-puberulent without, in flower and fruit glabrous or less often puberulent without and tomentulose especially at apex and on margins within, white or greenish white in flower. Corolla zygomorphic, 3.2-4.5 (6) cm long, the tube curved, (1.7) 2.3-2.7 (4) cm long, 0.7-1.0 cm wide at apex, the lobes narrow- to wide- obovate, rounded at apex, 0.8-2 cm long, 0.8-1 cm wide, spreading, the innermost abaxial in uppermost position. Androecium of 2 fertile stamens and 3 or 5 staminodes; fertile filaments adherent to corolla tube for almost their whole length with a free, triangular tip ca 2 mm long, the anthers oblong to lorate, 8.2-10 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, white, the appendages bilobed, fleshy, 0.9- 1 mm long (when rehydrated); staminodes with free tip 7-9 mm long, puberulent. Disc entire or slightly 5-undulate, 0.8-1.5 mm high. Carpels 1.8-2.4 mm high, glabrous or with a few straight thin hairs 0.5-0.7 mm long; style densely spreading-pilose on up- per 2/3 to 3?. Fruiting mericarps 1.4-1.9 cm high, 1.1-1.4 cm deep, glabrous, the wing widest (1-4 mm) at upper outer corner. Seeds 6-9 mm long, 5-6 mm wide, tuberculate on angles, tan to dark brown.

description: Shrub or tree(-let) 1.5-12 m; shoots pale gray to pale brown, sparsely pubescent to glabrous, striate, with many cream-colored lenticels. Leaves densely white-pubescent when young, soon glabrescent or sparsely and minutely puberulous mainly on the petiole apex; petiole 0.5-1.5(-1.8) cm long, semiterete, subwinged or slightly to deeply canaliculate adaxially, minutely puberulous at apex; leaflets conspicuously black-punctate on both surfaces or only abaxially, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, greenish to olivaceous, shiny above, dull and paler beneath, sessile, oblanceolate to narrow-obovate (the lateral ones sometimes wide-obovate), the margin entire, seldom irregularly and sparsely crenulate, flat or revolute, apex obtuse to retuse or emarginate, sometimes subacute, base decurrent or cuneate or in lateral leaflets sometimes acute and sub-symmetric; terminal leaflet 2.5-4(-5.5) X 1-1.7 cm; lateral leaflets 1.6-2.7(-3.2) X 0.7-1.4 cm; midvein slightly raised on proximal part of the blade, secondary veins mostly obscure to sometimes imperceptible. Inflorescence a sessile monothyrse 1-3.5 cm long, usually much shorter than the leaves, densely and minutely pubescent with white, appressed trichomes, sometimes subglabrous; bracts triangular, acute, ca. 1 mm long, pubescent abaxially. Flowers 4-merous; pedicel pubescent to subglabrous, ca. 1.5-2 mm long; bractlets ovate, pubescent. Sepals ovate, acute, pubescent to pu- berulous, ciliolate, ca. 1 mm long, greenish. Petals cream-colored, oblong, 3.2-3.5 mm long, glabrous, obtuse, margin entire or erose. Stamens ca. 1.5 mm long; anthers ovoid, short-apiculate. Disk 4-lobed, slightly shorter than the ovary. Ovary 4-lobed, densely white-pilose with short trichomes; style glandular-punctate, ca. 0.8 mm long; stigma subcapitate, slightly 4-lobed. Fruit of (3-)4 mericarps, glabrous; seed locule ellipsoid, 5-10 mm long; wing ovate to oblong or rounded, 6-15 X 8-10 mm, chartaceous, with slightly prominent veins.

description: Bushy shrubs or small trees, usually with many stems from the base, 2-6 m high; twigs of the season light chestnut brown, finely puberulent, darker reddish-brown and glabrate the second season; older bark red-brown, smooth with prominent lenticels; foliage and bark strongly aromatic or with sharp mephitic odor; leaves rather bright yellow-green, somewhat glossy above, paler and often with a somewhat rusty-yellowish cast beneath, densely to sparsely puberulent, especially beneath, or glabrate, especially above; leaflets oval to elliptic or oblanceolate to obovate, the terminal one (3-) 4-7 (-9) cm long, the width/length ratio (0.30-) 0.35-0.47 (-0.55); blades mostly rounded to obtuse (or acute) at the apices, cuneate at bases; lateral leaflets about 2/3 as long as the terminal, more or less inequilateral at base, the lower margins forming angles of 45 to 600 with the midveins; margins crenate or crenate-serrulate to nearly entire; inflorescences, in flower, about 3-5 cm in diameter; branches relatively short (to long), few to several from short central axes, the branches again more or less eymosely branched, puberulent; flowers 4- or 5- (-6) -merous, mostly unisexual; pistil bodies pubescent to rather coarsely hirsute in both staminate flowers (vestigial pistils) and the pistillate flowers; ovaries broadly to narrowly ovate, the styles in fertile flowers relatively long, up to about 1 mm long, often persistent for some time into the fruiting stage; fruits more or less circular in outline (sometimes pointed at both ends) sometimes tricarpellate; wings emarginate or rounded (rarely pointed) at apices, cordate to rounded (or cuneate) at bases, (1-) 1.5-2 (-2.5) cm broad and about as long; seed-bodies mostly broader than the wings, (2-) 3-4 mm thick in cross section through the narrow diameter, commonly with strongly indented mid-line between the carpels, usually set about the center of the wings (rarely slightly above).
bibliographicCitation: Bailey, Virginia L. 1962. Revision of the genus Ptelea (Rutaceae). Brittonia. 14: 1-45.

description: Deciduous shrubs or small trees. Prickles present. Leaves imparipinnate (reddish- woolly in bud). Leaflets 5-13, opposite to subopposite, oblong to elliptic, ovate, or lanceolate, to 77 mm long, to 45 mm wide, acute apically, cuneate basally, margin crenulate, pellucid-punctate in margin and lamina, pubescent to glabrate. Inflores- cences axillary, umbellate, less than 1 cm long, reddish-tomentose basally. Sepals absent. Petals 5, reddish-tomentose apically. Stamens 5 (absent in carpellate flowers). Ovaries (3) 4 (5), distinct, stipitate. Follicles 1-3 (per flower), distinct, stipitate, glabrous to pubescent.

description: Deciduous shrubs or small trees. Prickles present. Leaves imparipinnate. Leaflets (5) 9-13, opposite, narrowly ovate to lanceolate, to 90 mm long, to 39 mm wide, acute or acuminate apically, markedly oblique basally, margin shallowly crenate to serrulate, pellucid-punctate in margin and lamina, glabrous to occasionally puberulent. Inflorescences terminal, cymose, 4.5-14 cm long, glabrous to rarely puberulent. Sepals 5, distinct, deciduous. Petals 5, glabrous. Stamens 5 (short and staminodial in carpellate flowers). Ovaries (1) 2 (4), connate basally, sessile. Follicles 1-2 (per flower), connate basally, subsessile, glabrous.

description: Evergreen shrubs or small trees. Prickles present. Leaves paripinnate. Leaflets 4-10, opposite and subopposite, obovate to oblong, ovate, or elliptic, to 45 mm long, to 30 mm wide, rounded to truncate and slightly acuminate to emarginate apically, cuneate and attenuate basally, margin entire, pellucid-punctate marginally, glabrous. Inflorescences terminal, cymose, 4.5-6 cm long, glabrous or slightly puberulent. Sepals 3, connate, persistent. Petals 3, glabrous. Stamens 3 (absent in carpellate flowers). Ovaries 3, connate basally, sessile. Follicles 1 (2) (per flower), connate basally, sessile, glabrous.

description: Deciduous shrubs or rarely small trees. Prickles present. Leaves imparipinnate. Leaflets 5-9, opposite to (lowermost) subopposite, oval to ovate, to 40 mm long, to 22 mm wide, obtuse to acute apically, slightly oblique basally, margin crenate, pellucid-punctate in margin and lamina, hirtellous (on primary veins). Inflorescences terminal and subterminal, paniculate, 2.5-5.5 cm long, hirtellous. Sepals 5, distinct, deciduous. Petals 5, glabrous. Stamens 5 (absent in carpellate flowers). Ovaries 2, distinct, sessile. Follicles 1 (2) (per flower), distinct, subsessile, glabrous.

description: Deciduous shrubs. Prickles present. Leaves imparipinnate (reddish-woolly in bud). Leaflets 7-9, opposite, broadly elliptic-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, to 16 mm long, to 11 mm wide, obtuse apically, margin crenulate, pellucid-punctate in margin and lamina, pilosulous. Inflorescences terminal and subterminal, nearly umbellate. Sepals absent. Petals 4, reddish-tomentose apically. Stamens unknown. Ovaries 2-4, connate, stipitate, tomentose. Follicles unknown.

description: Erect shrubs 1-2 m tall with several to many stems from the base, or small slender trees 6-8 m tall; twigs at first green, becoming chestnut brown, glabrous or glabrate; bark of upper stems and branches chestnut brown, smooth, with consipcuous horizontal slit-like lenticels resembling those of cherry; older bark sometimes ridged and dull brown, especially near the bases of old trunks; leafblades herbaceous, dark green above, often paler beneath but not glaucous; margins irregularly and shallowly crenate or crenate-serrate to entire; glands small, usually less than 0.1 mm in diameter, often numerous (10-20 per mm2), not conspicuously raised above the leaf surface; terminal leaflets ovate to ovate-elliptic or obovate, obtuse or rounded at apex, cuneate at base, sessile or sometimes more or less petiolulate, (-4) 6-10 (-15) cm long, about half as broad as long, the width/length ratio (0.40-) 0.45-0.55 (-0.60); lateral leaflets ovate to rhombic-ovate, 2/3 as long to nearly as long as the terminal leaflets, obtuse to acute at the apex, more or less inequilateral at the base, the angle between the lower margins and the midvein averaging usually more than 45-55º; fruits 2 (rarely 3-)-carpellate; wings mostly circular, 20-25 mm in diameter, rounded to cordate at base (rarely cuneate), rounded to emarginate at apex (rarely acute); seed-bodies roundish to obovate, about 4-5 mm wide, 5-7 mm long, the mid-lines scarcely evident, set near the center or above the middle of the wings.
bibliographicCitation: Bailey, Virginia L. 1962. Revision of the genus Ptelea (Rutaceae). Brittonia. 14: 1-45.

description: Shrubs, or tree-like, to about 6 m tall; twigs greenish to dull reddish-brown; older bark dark reddish-brown; leaflets herbaceous, bright green and often glossy above, paler to greenish-glaucous beneath, the margins finely serrate to irregularly serrate-dentate; lateral leaflets nearly equilateral, the angles between the lower margins and the midvein usually not more than 50-600; glands large, commonly 1/6-1/4 mm in diameter, appearing on both surfaces of mature leaves as low swellings, but usually not numerous nor crowded; flowers and fruits variable as in suLbsp. trifoliata, except for a greater tendency towards the tri- carpellate condition of the ovaries and the somewhat thicker seed-bodies which may be 2-3 mm thick in cross section.

description: A nearly glabrous variety differing from the other two varieties of subsp. angucstifolia in having foliage mostly pale yellow green, leaflets thin but firm, with a distinctive luster on both sides, commonly thinly hairy beneath with long slender hairs; veins inconspicuous; glands rather sparse but prominent; terminal leaflets obovate or oblanceolate to lanceolate, usually broadest above the middle, cuneate to sessile at base.

description: Twigs of the season dull brown, covered with fine dense pubescence or velvety-tomentose, often with long and short hairs intermixed, commonly glabrate the second season; older branches dark reddish-brown; leaflets generally thickish or subcoriaceous, dark green above and appearing somewhat polished or becoming dull yellowish-green or discolored in age; upper surface sparsely short- pubescent, at least along the veins, usually with long hairs tufted at the junction with the petiole, strongly gland-dotted, the numerous large glands commonly 1/6-1/4 mm in diameter and visible to the naked eye; lower surface somewhat glaucous and more or less densely villous or tomentose, especially along the mid-veins; veins generally not conspicuous; terminal leaflets elliptic-lanceolate to ovate, obovate, or lanceolate-obovate, cuneate to the base, usually sessile, the apices rounded or obtuse to acute; blades (2-) 4-7 (-8) cm long, the width/length ratio (0.38-) 0.45-0.55 (-0.65); lateral leaflets oval to ovate or obovate-elliptic, about 2/3 as long as or equalling the terminal leaflets, commonly strongly inequilateral at base, the angles between the lower margin and the midvein about (40-) 50-70 (-80) º; margins shallowly crenate to entire; petioles generally stout and relatively short, about half as long as the terminal leaflets; inflores- cences relatively small, with few to several main branches from near the bases; branches and pedicels more or less hirsute with rather coarse hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Bailey, Virginia L. 1962. Revision of the genus Ptelea (Rutaceae). Brittonia. 14: 1-45.

description: Shrub or tree 1.5-15 m tall, to 40 cm dbh, the indument on petioles and peduncles absent or if present not visible to the naked eye, composed of scattered, erect or ascending, usually curved trichomes (the longest 0.05-0.15 mm). Leaflet-blade acuminate at apex, essentially glabrous (sometimes with scattered trichomes to 0.18 mm long on midrib and margin), usually with domatia in axils of secondary veins, these usually with circular or elongate openings, rarely with shallow, crescent-shaped openings, sometimes visible to the naked eye, the terminal blade usually elliptic, (9.3-)14.5-30.2 X 3.2-11.3 cm, usually acute (rarely cuneate) at base, with (6-)9-14 secondary veins per side, its petiolule 0.6-3.5 cm long, the lateral blades usually elliptic, (5.8-)12.5-28 X (2.3-)4.6-9.4 cm, asymmetric at base (usually acute, but un- equally so, both basiscopically and acro- scopically), with 5-11 secondary veins per side, their petiolules 0.2-1.4 cm long; petiole 3-17 cm long. Inflorescence 7.5-21.5 cm long including a peduncle 4.5-19.2 cm long, the internodes of primary rachis not developed, the partial inflorescences at- tached at apex of peduncle, usually sessile, sometimes stalked, dichasial at first node, dichasial or monochasial at higher nodes, the secondary axis 0-45 mm long; pedicels 1-3.5 mm long. Calyx subentire or shallowly 4- or 5-dentate, 0.7-1.7 mm long, subglabrous or sparsely appressed-puberulent without, glabrous within. Corolla almost always apiculate in bud, 4- or 5-merous, (25-)31-42 mm long at anthesis, usually mealy appressed-pubescent toward base and at margins of lobes and subglabrous on surface of lobes without, white, greenish in bud, the tube formed by coherent petals 20-22 mm long, 1.8-2 mm wide just above the calyx, 1.1-1.8 times longer than the lobes, these 12-20 X 2-3 mm, acute and not inflexed at apex. Androecium of 4 or 5 (rarely 2) fertile stamens; filaments 25-34 mm long, free from each other and adherent to the corolla tube, glabrous or villose adaxially within the corolla tube, the free part 7-8 mm long; anther including sterile base and appendage 4-6.5 mm long, the fertile portion 2.5-4 X 0.6-0.8 mm, the basal sterile portion 0.6-1.5 mm long, the appendage 0.4-1.1 mm long, the notch 0.3-1 mm deep. Disc 0.6-0.7 mm high, slightly shorter than the ovary. Carpels 4 or 5, 0.9-1 mm high, glabrous; style 29.5-35 mm long. Fruiting mericarps 10-15 X 9-12 mm, glabrous, sometimes minutely appressed-pubescent on adjacent lateral surfaces. Seed 8.5-10 X 6.5-8 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Kallunki, Jacquelyn A. 1998. Revision of Ticorea Aubl. (Rutaceae, Galipeinae). Brittonia. 50: 500-513.

description: Shrub or tree 1.5-1 3 m tall, the indument of vegetative buds, young twigs and petioles, and inflorescences strigulose. Leaves 3- foliolate; leaflet blade oblanceolate or narrow-elliptic, rarely elliptic or wide-elliptic, acuminate (rarely rounded or emarginate) at apex, cuneate to decurrent and in lateral leaflets asymmetric at base, chartaceous, dull above, usually glabrous, sometimes with sparse appressed trichomes on abaxial surface, especially on midrib, the secondary veins evident, curved, looping at margin, 8- 19 per side, the tertiary veins obscure on adaxial surface, evident and raised on ab- axial surface, the abaxial surface drying dull green, the terminal blade 9.5-34.5 cm long, 2.8-10.7 cm wide, the lateral blade 10.5- 33 cm long, 2.5-9.8 cm wide; petiole (0.8) 1.5-9.2 cm long; petiolule 0-1 mm long. Inflorescence 35-62-flowered, 12.9-26.5 cm long inctuding a peduncle 4-10 cm long; pedicels 0-2 mm long in flower and in fruit Sepals very wide-ovate, rounded at apex, 1.5-4 mm long, 2-5 mm wide, densely stri- gulose without, glabrous within. Corolla 13- 15 mm long at anthesis, densely strigulose without (even at anthesis), green to white, the tube 3-5.3 mm to division of innermost lobe, 5.1-8 mm to division of other lobes, 3.5-5 mm wide, the innermost lobe narrow- ovate, 6.8-11 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, the other 4 lobes ovate, 2.7-5 mm long, 2-2.2 mm wide. Filaments of fertile anthers ad- herent to corolla, ca. 7 mm long; staminodes adnate to corolla, arising at throat, linear, ca. 3 mm long; anthers 3-3.7 (6) mm long, ca. 1.5 mm wide, the sac usually pilose, the connective usually glabrous, rarely pilose, the appendages 0.8-1 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm wide. Disc shorter than ovary. Carpels ca. 1 mm high, sometimes subglabrous in bud but soon densely strigulose; style 7-9.5 mm long, gland-dotted, glabrous. Fruiting mericarps 1-5 (usually only 2 maturing), 15-16 mm long, 9-10 mm wide, strigulose. Seed ca. 11 mm long, ca. 6.8 mm wide, dark brown.
bibliographicCitation: Kallunki, Jacquelyn A. 1994. Revision of Raputia Aubl. (Cuspariinae, Rutaceae). Brittonia. 46: 279-295.

description: Shrub or tree 1-10 m tall. Leaves 3-foliolate; leaflet blade narrow-ovate to oblanceolate, acuminate (acute) at apex, acute or decurrent at base, with 9-16 secondary veins per side, those of uppermost reduced leaves 5.8-9.7 cm long, 2.2-3.4 cm wide, those of larger leaves 20.2-29.3 cm long, 6.9-10.3 cm wide, the terminal leaflet 1.5-4.6 cm longer than lateral leaflets; petiole subterete, 1.8-5.2 cm on uppermost reduced leaves, 15.9-22.8 cm on larger leaves, sparsely puberulent to glabrous; petiolules 0.1-1.7 cm, densely appressed-pubescent. Inflorescence imperfectly twice or 3-times dichotomous; peduncle 13.5-30 cm long, with branches 2.6-4 cm long, densely puberulent; bracts deciduous before anthesis, lanceolate to narrow-elliptic, sometimes subfalcate, 5-10 mm long, 0.2-0.3 cm wide, sparsely appressed-puberulent; pedicels 0.3-1 cm in flower, 0.8-1.3 cm in fruit, densely puber- ulent. Sepals lanceolate, 1.6-2.2 cm long, 0.3-0.7 cm wide, densely puberulent with- out, tomentulose within, pale cream (Camp 999) in flower. Corolla zygomorphic, 2.5- 3.5 cm long, the tube slightly curved, 1.5- 2 cm long, 0.6-0.9 cm wide at apex, tomentulose within, the lobes lanceolate, ob- tuse or acute at apex, 1.6-2 cm long, 0.25- 0.40 cm wide, spreading, the innermost apparently in uppermost position, the 4 others lower. Androecium of 2 fertile stamens and 3 staminodes; fertile filaments adherent to corolla tube for their whole length or with free tip 3 mm long and 3 mm wide, glabrous adaxially, the anthers oblong, 6-7.5 mm long, 1.6-2 mm wide, the appendages bilobed, fleshy, to 0.8 mm long (when rehydrated); staminodes with free tip 5.6-8 mm long, puberulent. Disc entire, 0.8-1 mm high. Carpels angled dorsally, 1.8-2 mm high, glabrous in bud and in flower, densely puberulent soon after anthesis; style 1 1-15 mm long, densely spreading pilose in upper half. Fruiting mericarps 1.2-1.4 cm high, 1.1-1.3 cm deep, minutely puberulent (less so with age) on lateral and dorsal surfaces, the wing widest (3-7 mm) at upper outer corner. Seeds ca 7.8 mm long, 4.4 mm wide, tuberculate, blackish brown.
bibliographicCitation: Kallunki, Jacquelyn A. 1992. A revision of Erythrochiton sensu lato (Cuspariinae, Rutaceae). Brittonia. 44: 107-139.

description: Shrub or small tree 0.75-5 m tall. Leaves 1-foliolate; blade usually elliptic (sometimes narrowly so) to narrow-obovate, rarely narrow-ovate, short-acuminate and with an obtuse tip (rarely rounded or obtuse) at apex, acute at base, 7.5-26.8 cm long, 2.8- 12 cm wide, with 8-23 secondary veins per side; petiole flattened and slightly margined adaxially, 1.5-11.2 cm long, sparsely appressed-puberulent, glabresent. Inflorescence imperfectly twice dichotomous; peduncle (0.5) 6.7-17.8 cm long, with branches 2.5-9.5 cm long, appressed-puberulent; bracts subtending pedicels very early deciduous (leaving scars but not present on any specimens examined), large ones occasionally persisting, narrow-obovate or oblanceolate, 45-60 mm long, 18-27 mm wide; pedicels 0.9-1.5 cm in flower, 1.2-2 cm in fruit, appressed-puberulent. Sepals lanceo- late, 2.5-4 cm long, 0.4-0.9 cm wide, sparsely appressed-puberulent and glabrescent without, tomentulose especially at apex and on margins within, light yellow-green or light green in flower, green in fruit. Corolla subzygomorphic, more or less funnelform, 5.5-6.8 cm long, the tube straight, 2.9-4 cm long, 1.1-1.2 (2.4) cm wide at apex, the lobes unequal, wide-obovate or wideelliptic and rounded at apex (in best pressed mature flowers), 1.2-2.5 cm long, 0.9-1.9 cm wide, spreading, the innermost in upper position. Androecium of 2 fertile stamens and 4 or 5 staminodes; fertile filaments adherent to corolla tube for 2.1 cm with a narrowed, puberulent, free tip 4-4.5 mm long, glabrous adaxially except at densely tomentulose base, the anthers narrow-oblong to lorate, 6.6-7.5 mm long, 1.4-1.8 mm wide, the appendages to 1-1.2 mm long (when rehydrated); staminodes longer than fertile filaments, with free tip 4-7 mm puberulent. Disc entire, 1-1.4 mm high. Carpels 2-2.5 mm high, united ventrally for whole length, glabrous in bud and in flower, densely puberulent soon after anthesis; style densely spreading-pilose for most of length. Fruiting mericarps 1.3-1.5 cm high, 1-1.2 cm deep, densely puberulent, the wings 1- 1.5 mm wide. Seeds 7-9 mm long, 4.5-5 mm wide, tuberculate on angles, brown or dark gray.

description: Shrub 0.5-2 (10) m tall. Leaves 1-folio- late; blade oblanceolate to narrow-obovate, acuminate at apex, acute or cuneate at base, (7.8) 11.2-34 cm long, (3.2) 4-11.9 cm wide, with 10-15 secondary veins per side; petiole flattened or slightly canaliculate adaxially, (0.9) 1.4-9.6 cm long, glabrous. Inflorescence terminal, once or twice dichotomous; peduncle 4.3-16.3 cm long, with branches 1.2-5.5 cm long, appressed-puberulent; bracts subtending pedicels early deciduous, oblanceolate, 8-15 mm long, 2-6 mm wide, sparsely appressed-puberulent; pedicels 0.5 - 1.1 cm long in flower, 1.2-1.6 cm in fruit, densely pubescent or puberulent. Sepals lanceolate to narrow-ovate, 1.8-3.2 cm long, (0.5) 0.7-1.2 cm wide, appressed-puberulent and glabrescent without, tomentulose within, white. Corolla zygomorphic, 4-5.4 cm long, the tube curved, 3-3.9 cm long, 1-1.2 cm wide at apex, the lobes wide-obovate, acute at apex, 1-1.4 cm long, 0.7-0.8 cm wide, spreading, the innermost in upper position. Androecium of 2 fertile stamens and 4 or 5 staminodes; fertile filaments adherent to petals, with narrowed, puberulent, free tip 7-8 mm long, the anthers oblong, 6.7-7 mm long, 3 mm wide, yellow, the appendages bilobed, fleshy, 1.5-1.6 mm long (when rehydrated); the 3 (2) +/- antesepalous staminodes with glabrous, free tip 4-7 mm arising in throat, the 2 antepetalous ones further united to corolla lobe with glabrous, free tip 1-2 mm. Disc entire or slightly undulate, 0.6-1 mm high. Carpels 1-2.2 mm high, glabrous in bud and in flower, densely and minutely puberulent soon after anthe- sis; style to 40 mm long, densely spreading- pubescent for most of length; stigma oblique. Fruiting mericarps 1.2-1.5 cm high, ca 1 cm deep, densely puberulent, sometimes creamy white, the wing ca 1 mm wide. Seeds ca 8 mm long, 4.5 mm wide, tuberculate on angles, dark brown or lead gray.

description: Treelet or tree 3-10(-15) m tall; shoots reddish-brown to grayish, sparsely pubescent to glabrous, suberose, longitudinally fissured and ridged, with many white lenticels. Leaves densely short-pubescent with white, appressed, curved trichomes when young, soon glabrescent or sparsely and minutely puberulous on main veins and on the petiole apex; petiole 1.8-5 cm long, slender, semiterete, flat adaxially to sometimes slightly canaliculate, pale cream-colored; leaflets conspicuously black-punctate on both surfaces, membranous to chartaceous, pale green to pale olivaceous, dull on both surfaces, sessile to sometimes short-petiolulate, narrow-elliptic to elliptic or seldom subobovate, margin entire, flat to slightly revolute, apex obtuse to short-acuminate with a rounded to retuse tip, base acute to cuneate in the terminal leaflet, acute to ob- tuse and mostly asymmetric in the lateral ones; terminal leaflet (3-)4.5-8(-12) X 1.4-3(-5) cm; lateral leaflets 2.8-7.5(-1 1) X 1.3-2 cm; midvein raised on abaxial surface, pale cream-colored, somewhat raised on adaxial surface, secondary veins 5-7 per side, mostly inconspicuous. Inflorescence a diplothyrse 7-15 cm long, longer than the leaves, punctate, glabrous or sparsely short-pubescent with white, curved trichomes; peduncle 0-1.2 cm long; coflorescences 4- 6, mostly subopposite, the proximal ones 1.5-6.5 cm long; bracts triangular to ovate, ca. 0.5 mm long, puberulous. Flowers 5-merous; pedicel pubescent with white, short trichomes, 1-1.5 mm long; bractlets triangular, pubescent. Sepals ovate to oblong, apex acute, sparsely pubescent, ciliolate, ca. 0.7 mm long, greenish. Petals cream-colored to yellowish (or reddish-brown fide Chiang, 1984, in dried specimen?), elliptic, obtuse to subacute, 2-2.5 X ca. 1 mm, margin slightly erose. Stamens ca. 1.5 mm long; anthers heart-shaped, apiculate. Disk 5-lobed, slightly shorter than the ovary. Ovary 5-lobed, minutely white-villous; style glandular-punctate, ca. 0.3 mm long; stigma slightly 5-lobed. Fruit of 4 or 5 mericarps, villous to glabrescent; seed locule ellipsoid, 8-9 mm long; wing oblong to wide-ovate, 13-15 X 10-12 mm, chartaceous, with raised veins.

description: Arbor 3-10-metralis. Ramuli villosuli vel glabrescentes lenticellis albis instructi. Folia chartacea trifoliolata villosula vel glabrescentia; petioli graciles 2-4.5 cm longi; foliola sessilia rhombeo-ovata vel -obovata vel elliptica, terminale (3) 5-8 (12) cm longum, 1.5-3 cm latum, lateralia terminali minora, basi asymmetrice acuta, apice parum acuminato sed ad extremum rotundato vel leviter emarginato. Inflorescentia paniculata laxa terminalis. Flores pentameri. Fructus villosulus vel glabrescens 4-5 alatis, alis inclusis 3-3.5 cm diametro, apice rotundatis.

description: Tree, 3-10 m tall; young branches reddish-brown to grayish, short-villous to glabrous, with white lenticels; buds densely short-villous with whitish to grayish hairs. Leaves opposite, 3-foliolate; petioles slender, 2-4.5 cm long, pellucid-punctate, short-villous to glabrous; leaflets sessile, rhombic-ovate, -obovate or elliptic, chartaceous, conspicuously pellucid-punctate on both surfaces, short-villous to glabrous, base acute, unequal in the lateral leaflets, apex slightly acuminate, with a rounded to slightly emarginate tip; terminal leaflet (3) 5-8 (12) cm long, 1.5-3 cm broad, the lateral ones smaller. Inflorescence terminal, paniculate, lax, 7-15 cm long, main branches 5-6 cm broad, pellucid-punctate, short-villous to glabrous; pedicels 1-1.5 mm long, minutely villous with whitish hairs, glandularpunctate; flowers 4.5-5 mm diam. Calyx 0.75 mm long, pellucid-punctate, minutely villous, with 5 imbricate sepals, united at the base, broadly ovate, with ciliolate margin. Petals 5, free, elliptic, yellowish to reddish-brown, 2 mm long, 1 mm broad, pellucid-punctate, with a hyaline, slightly erose margin. Stamens alternate with and shorter than the petals, inserted at the base of an intrastaminal disc. Ovary semiglobose, papillate, minutely villous, 5-loculed, 5-costate, borne on a disc with an erect edge that follows the shape of the ovary, each locule with 2 ovules; style short, thick; stigma slightly 5-lobate. Fruit 3-3.5 cm diam (including the wings), of 4 or 5 samaroid, indehiscent carpels separating at maturity, each with a dorsal ascending wing, densely to scarcely villous when young, glabrescent to glabrous at maturity, each with a seed approximately 8 mm long.

description: Densely-branched shrub with slender stems to about 5 cm in diameter near the base, 2-5 m high, forming dense, though strict, clusters; twigs and branchlets reddish brown, appressed-pubescent or glabrate after the first season, often thickly set with pustular glands; leaves rather bright dark green above, paler or somewhat greenish-glaucous beneath, mostly subcoriaceous, minutely pubescent, especially on the lower surface, or older leaves sometimes glabrate, the margins crenulate to nearly entire, more or less revolute; petioles minutely pubescent on adaxial side; glands conspicuous under a lens, relatively large, up to about 0.2 mm in diameter, often with smaller glands intermixed; terminal leaflets elliptic to obovate, rounded to acute at apex, cuneate at base or sometimes short-petioluled, (1.5-) 2-4 (-4.5) cm long, mostly slightly less than half as broad as long, the width/length ratio (0.31-) 0.40-0.50 (-0.56); lateral leaflets about the same shape or with broader inequilateral bases,-about 2/3 as long to nearly as long as the terminal one; flowers solitary or few in small clusters at the ends of short branches, 5 (-4)-merous, relatively large; petals broadly elliptic, 5-6 mm long; sepals ovate-lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 1/4-1/3 as long as the petals; filaments and pistils glabrous; ovary roundish-ovate or oval in outline, at first compressed, in fruit becoming turgid and nut-like with hard thick pericarp; fruits oval to ovate or subquadrate-oval, sometimes 3-carpellate, 10-15 mm long, not quite as broad, the seed-bodies 5 mm or more thick in cross-section through the narrower diameter, conspicuously gland-dotted with large glandular depressions, without midlines, the wings very narrow or practically lacking.

description: Arbor circa 22 m alta ramulis ultimis puberulis deinde glabratis. Folia simplicia alterna chartacea. Petiolus 3-4 cm longus glaber basi ineras- satus. Lamina late obovato-lanceolata apice subito angustata acuminataque basi euneata sine sensu attenuata margine integra, 13-30 cm longa 4-8 cm lata; supra glabra nitidula costa plana nervis secundariis paulo notatis reticulo venulorum minuto prominuleque, superficie minutissime impresso-alveolata; subtus pilis minutis crassiusculis sparsis vel glabra costa crassa eminenti striata nervis see- undariis circa 10 utroque latere prominentibus curvato-ascendentibus ad mar- ginem decurrenti-anastomosantibus, nervis tertiis tenuioribus bene prominulis laxum reticulum instructis venulis minute conspicueque reticulatis. Infloreseentiae statu fructifero paniculatae 18-25 em longae ramulis angulatis pilis crassiusculis copiosis vel glabratis. Pedunculi fructiferi circa 5 mm longi robusti glabri. Drupa in sieco pyriformi-globosa obtuse carinato-nervata asym- metrica circa 18 mm longa 16-17 mm lata exocarpio carnosulo in sieco coriaceo fragili 1.5-2 mm crasso. Endocarpium lignosum durum ellipsoideo-brachyceph- alicum nervo dorsale obtuse prominenti superficie sublaevi minute scabridula basi brevissime attenuatum, 1 mm crassum, 14 mm longum, 12 mm latum.

description: Trees or shrubs to 10 m high. Expanded leaf blades mostly linear (narrowly elliptic), (3-)4-16 X 0.3-1.1 cm, entire or serrulate, pubescent (glabrous) with mostly appressed, straight hairs; petioles 0.5-6 mm long. Anthers 0.4-0.8(-1) mm long. Capsules 3-5(-7) mm long, glabrous or pubescent; styles 0-0.2 mm long; stigmas 0.2- 0.4 mm long; stipes 0-1.5(-2) mm long. Floral bracts 1-2.5(-3) mm long. 2n = 38.

description: Woody vine to 17 m long. Stems 5-angular, 6-7-striate, glabrescent, the old stems obtusely angled, with many, small, rounded lenticels arranged in lines along stem. Cross-section of stem with simple stele. Stipules small (ca 1.5 mm), subulate. Leaves temate; petiole not winged, cylindric, adaxially canaliculate, glabrous or puberulent, shorter than leaflets; leaflets coriaceous, glabrous, adaxially shiny, with hair domatia at axils of prominent veins, apex acuminate and mucronate, base rounded, margins remotely serrate with obtuse, glandular teeth, terminal leaflet larger, 9-13 x 4-6.5 cm, ovate, lateral leaflets smaller, 5-6 x 3 cm, ovate- lanceolate and oblique. Inflorescence longer than subtending leaf, densely covered with small (0.2 mm long), recurved, whitish hairs; bracts 1 mm long, subulate; pedicel articulate at its middle. Flowers unknown. Fruit straw-colored, glabrous, chartaceous, oblong to oblanceolate, 5.5-6 x 3 cm; cocci flat with slightly prominent reticulate network, partitioning wall 12 x 1 mm. Seeds lenticular, brown, 8 mm long, with large hilum (3.5 mm), inserted near the base of coccus. Cotyledons erect.

description: Frutex scandens; rami teretes, tomento brevi; corpus lignosum compositum, e centrali et 8 periphericis equimagnis constans; folia pinnatim (3) 5-foliolata; petioli rachidesque nudi, foliolo breviores; foliola coriacea, elliptica vel oblonga, acuta vel acuminata et mucronata, sessilia, margine revoluto, integerrimo vel prope apicem unidentato vel bidentato; fructus badii, lignosi, 3.5-4.5 cm longi; alae 1.6-2.1 cm latae, semi-obovatae, in coccum decurrentes; cocci subglobosi etsi aliquantum lateraliter compressi, 10 mm usque longi, 9 mm lati, 7 mm crassi, nervis prominentibus, cicatrice tam lata quam cocci latitudinem.

description: Woody vine 6-7 m long. Branches terete, slightly striate, shortly tomentose, the hairs multiseptate, reddish becoming white apically. Cross section of stem with central subterete vascular cylinder surrounded by 8 obcordate vascular cyl- inders of equal size. Stipules triangular, tomentose, 1-1.5 mm long. Leaves pin- nately (3) 5-foliolate, 7-10 x 8-12 cm; petiole and rachis unwinged, rufo-to- mentose, adaxially canaliculate, petiole length shorter than leaflet length; leaflets coriaceous, dull green, elliptic to oblong, 4-7 x 2-3 cm, acute to acuminate and mucronate at apex, attenuate to obtuse and sessile at base, margins revolute, entire or with 1 or 2 teeth near apex (mostly terminal one), veins slightly prominent, upper surface glabrous except for a few hairs on veins, lower surface puberulous. Inflorescence axillary, much longer than subtending leaf, rufo-canescent; cincini 6 mm long; bracts ovate, imbricate, ca 1.5 mm long; fruiting pedicel ca 9 mm long, articulate near base; sepals 5, ovate, obtuse, abaxially rufo-tomentose, adax- ially papillose, the external ones ca 4 mm long, the internal ones ca 5 mm long. Fruits green to yellow-brown, 3.5-4.5 cm long; wings 1.6-2.1 cm wide, semiob- ovate; cocci 10 x 9 x 7 mm, woody, glabrous, with prominent veins, subglobose although somewhat laterally compressed, scar as long as wide, partitioning wall 3-4 mm thick; endocarp ferrugineously floccose. Seeds subglobose, attached to base of coccus, hilum semicircular.

description: Frutex scandens, glabriusculus; rami juniores teretes subtiliter 8-sulcati; corpus lignosum compositum, e centrali majore, medulla cavo, et 7 (6) minoribus periphericis constans; folia temata; petioli nudi, adaxialiter pilosi, foliola glabra, chartacea, acuminata vel acuta, vix petiolulata, margine revoluto, pallido; terminale ellipticum integerrimum, basi attenuatum; lateralia lanceolata, prope basim unidentata, dente calloso, basi obtusa; flores 6-7 mm longi; sepala ciliata adaxialiter tomentosa; exteriora 2, 3.5 mm usque longa, ovata et obtusa; interiora 2 obovata, tertio et quinto coalita 6 mm usque longa, quarto 4 mm usque longo; fructus chartacei, 35-38 mm longi; alac 13-14 mm latac; loculi lentiformes, 7 mm longi, 4 mm lati, ala dorsaliter circumcinti.

description: Woody vine to 10 m long. Branches terete, slightly 8-sulcate. Cross section of stem with central, terete vascular cylinder surrounded by 7 (6) terete, smaller vascular cylinders. Stipules subulate, 2 mm long. Leaves trifoliolate, 7-21 x 7-19 cm; petioles not winged, adaxially pilose, shorter than leaflets; leaflets glabrous, chartaceous, dull green, 4-15 x 1.5-5 cm, acuminate or acute at apex, shortly petiolulate, with revolute, ciliate pale margins, the terminal one elliptic, entire with attenuate base, the lateral ones lanceolate, unidentate on outer margins close to the base, the tooth somewhat glandular, the veins prominent on lower surface. Inflorescence axillary, tomentose, longer than subtending leaf; bracts lanceolate, 1 mm long; pedicels 3 mm long, articulate at base. Flowers pale yellow, 6-7 mm long; sepals 4, ciliate, adaxially tomentose, the external two 3.5 mm long, ovate, obtuse, the connate internal one (consisting of third and fifth) 6 mm long, the fourth 4 mm long; petals spathulate, 6 mm long, adaxially papillose, the scales of frontal petals 4 mm long, crown-shaped and fleshy at apex, the scales of lateral petals 3 mm long; torus well developed, the superior glands globose, 1 mm long, the lateral glands oblong, 1.5 mm long; filaments with inflexed hairs. Fruits yellow- green to straw-colored, chartaceous, 3.5-3.8 cm long; wings 1.3-1.4 cm wide; cocci lentiform, 7 x 4 mm, dorsal side with a decurrent wing; partitioning wall up to 7 times longer than wide; endocarp white-pilose. Seed lentiform, attached near to base of locule; cotyledons erect.
bibliographicCitation: Acevedo-Rodríguez, Pedro. 1987. Two new species of Serjania (Sapindaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 39: 348-352.

description: Frutex scandens; rami teretes vel subteretes, flavido-tomentosi, 5-striati; corpus lignosum in corpora partialia 5 libera radiatim divisum; stipulae magnae, 1.5-2.2 cm longae, ovatae amplexicaules; folia pinnatim 5-foliolata; petioli rachidesque nudi, dense flavido-tomentosi; foliola pubescentia, acuminata vel abrupte acuminata; foliolum terminale ellipticum, 6.5-11.5 cm longum, ad basim attenuatum; foliola lateralia lanceolata, oblonga vel obovata, ad basim obtusa vel subcordata; inflorescentia folia aequantes; flores magni (6-7 mm longi); fructus maturi fallunt.

description: Woody vine. Branches terete or nearly so, slightly striate; young branches densely covered with yellowish curled hairs (0.5-1.2 mm); old branches glabrescent and lenticellate, lenticels disposed in line along striae. Cross-section of stem with xylem radially divided into five subequal parts. Stipules puberulous, broadly ovate to oval and oblique, 1.5-2.2 x 1.5-2 cm, base auriculate, clasping the stem, apex acuminate, margins ciliate, with few dentations. Leaves pinnately 5-foliolate; petiole and rachis not winged, both equal to leaflet length, densely covered with small (0.25-1 mm), yellowish, slightly curled, inflexed hairs, terete, striate on adaxial surface; leaflets chartaceous to membranous, apex acuminate to abruptly acuminate, both surfaces covered with minute resinous glands and with two kinds of small yellowish hairs with swollen base, the smaller erect, 0.25 mm long, the larger inflexed, 1 mm long, veins slightly raised and densely sericeous, margins remotely glandular-serrate and ciliate, terminal leaflet ovate, 6.5-11.5 x 2.5-7 cm, attenuate at base, lateral leaflets lanceolate, oblong, or obovate with obtuse or subcordate base, sessile or shortly petiolulate. Inflorescences as long as or longer than subtending leaf, densely covered with small (1 mm or less), yellowish, slightly curled hairs; bracts lanceolate, ciliate, 5-5.7 mm long; cincinni 0.5-1 cm long, 4- 5-flowered; bracteoles overlapping, 2.5 mm long. Pedicel 4-5 mm long, articulated at 1 mm from the base; sepals 5, ovate, obtuse at apex, abaxially covered with small yellowish, inflexed hairs, adaxially puberulent, the external 2, 3.5-4 mm long, the internal 3, 5-5.2 mm long; petals white, obovate, obtuse at apex, 6.5 mm long, adaxially papillose, the scales of frontal petals ca 4.5 mm long, fleshy and crown-shaped, with reflexed part hood-like and pilose-margined, the scales of lateral petals 4 mm long, the apex slightly fleshy, the margin pilose; torus glands well developed, the frontal ones lanceolate, 2 mm long, puberulent, the lateral ones oblong, 1 mm long; filament with inflexed whitish hairs. Fruit (immature) oblong-ovate, 3.5 x 2.2 cm; cocci tomentose, each flat and surrounded by a wing.

description: Woody vine. Stems sharply triangular, the angles covered with stiff, coarse, 1.5-2 mm long, rusty hairs. Cross-section of stem with central, rounded, large vascular cylinder with hollow medulla and 3 peripheral, smaller, rounded vascular cylinders. Stipules oblong, 0.2-0.7 cm long, acute, ciliate at margin. Leaves ternate, 15-20 x 20-21 cm; petioles not winged, much shorter than leaflets, cylindric, slightly swollen at base, adaxially furrowed and covered with small (0.5 mm), curled, ferrugineous hairs; leaflets chartaceous, glabrous except for few hairs on margins and adaxial surface of veins, abruptly acuminate at apex, with repand- denticulate margins, terminal leaflet oval, 11-13 x 7-8.3 cm, base rounded or obtuse, decurrent into a more or less prolonged (1-2 cm) petiolule, lateral leaflets oval-oblong to obovate, sometimes oblique, base rounded, shortly petiolulate. Inflorescence axillary, 3 times longer than subtending leaf, laxly covered with erect, 1 mm long, rusty hairs; bracts narrowly oblong, 5.2 x 1 mm, margins ciliate, apex acuminate; cincinni 1-1.5 cm long, densely covered with small, rusty, curled hairs, usually 5-flowered; bracteoles lanceolate, ca 3 mm long. Pedicel ca 4 mm long, articulate near the base, densely covered with small (0.15 mm), yellowish, inflexed hairs; sepals 5, with same indument as pedicel, especially on adaxial surface, the external 2, ca 4 mm long, ovate, the apex obtuse, the internal 3, 5- 5.5 mm long, ovate-elliptic, the apex obtuse, third and fifth connate at base 1/4- 2/5 of length; petals white, 6.5-7.5 mm long, broadly spathulate, adaxially minutely papillate, the apex rounded; the scales of frontal petals 5 mm long, hood-shaped, with fleshy, crown-shaped apex and ciliate margins, the scales of lateral petals 4 mm long, with slightly fleshy apex and ciliate margins; torus glands 4, the frontal ones 1.5 mm long, broadly ovate and obtuse at apex, the lateral ones reduced, ca 0.7 mm long, annular; filament puberulent; ovary not seen. Fruit and seeds not seen.

description: Plants 5-60 cm in height, not stoloniferous. Stem erect. Basal leaf blades 1-11 cm broad, incisely 5-13-lobed for 1/4-1/2 the blade length; lobes cuneate to subovate or subovate and once or twice dentately to subcrenately toothed. Stipules mem- branous and inconspicuous; margins entire or erose with a few long bristles to rarely sublaciniate. Inflorescence erect, primary and higher order branches per- pendicular to central axis. Calyx narrowly turbinate-campanulate, 1.8-3.3 mm long, 1.2-2.5 mm wide; lobes triangular to triangular-ovate, 0.6-1.7 mm long, 0.6-1.2 mm wide. Petals 2.5-3.1 mm long; blade ovate and abruptly clawed to ovate-lanceolate and gradually narrowed into claw, 1-1.8 mm wide; claw 1/5- 1/4 total petal length. Ovary at least 4/5 inferior. Capsules at maturity cylindric to cylindric-ovate, 3.25-8 mm long, 1.5-4 mm wide. Seeds dark red-brown, 0.9- 1.7 mm long, 0.3-0.6 mm wide, the main body (not including winged-margin) 0.7-1 mm long. 2n = 14.

description: Plants 5-45 cm in height, stoloniferous. Stem erect. Basal leaf blades 1-12 cm broad, incisely 7-11-lobed for 1/3-1/2 length of blade; lobes cuneate to cuneate- oblong and once or twice dentately toothed. Stipules membranous and inconspicuous; margins entire or erose with a few long bristles. Inflorescence erect, primary and higher order branches perpendicular to central axis. Calyx widely turbinate-campanulate, 1.5-2.5 mm long, 2-4.5 mm wide; lobes triangular, 0.9- 1.5 mm long, 0.8-1.2 mm wide. Petals 1.6-2.5 mm long; blades suborbicular and abruptly clawed, 1-1.8 mm wide; claw usually ca '1/5 total petal length. Ovary at least 4 inferior. Capsules at maturity cylindric, 3.8-7.1 mm long, 1.2-2.6 mm wide. Seeds dark red-brown, 1.1-1.7 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide, the main body (not including winged-margin) 0.8-1 mm long. 2n = 14.

description: Plants 5-40 cm in height. Stem erect to oblique. Basal leaf blades 1-12 cm broad, incisely 7-13-lobed for 1/4-1/2 the length of blade to shallowly and somewhat irregularly 7- to many-lobed; lobes cuneate-oblong to crenate and once or twice dentately to coarsely and subcrenately toothed. Stipules membranous, inconspic- uous to slightly expanded; margins erose with a few long bristles to lacinate. Inflorescence erect to decumbent, the primary and higher order branches ascending relative to the central axis. Calyx tubular-campanulate, 1.3-3.2 mm long, 1.2- 2.1 mm wide; lobes triangular-ovate to lanceolate-oblong, 0.8-1.5 mm long, 0.6- 1.1 mm wide. Petals 1.7-3.5 mm long; blade ovate and abruptly narrowed into the claw to lanceolate and gradually narrowed into claw, 0.7-1.6 mm wide; claw ca 1/5-1/3 total petal length. Ovary ca 1/2 inferior. Capsules at maturity cylindric ovate to cylindric-elliptic, 3-7.5 mm long, 1.3-3.2 mm wide. Seeds tan (rarely red-brown), 0.7-1.2 mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm wide, the main body (not including winged-margin) 0.4-0.7 mm long. 2n = 14.

description: Shrubs to 4 m tall, the younger twigs narrowly ridged when dried. Leaf blades narrowly ovate to lanceolate, 5.5-9 X 1.5-3 cm, glabrous, chartaceous, with 11-15 pairs of lateral veins, the midrib salient below, impressed above, the lower orders of venation more or less salient on both sides; apex long acuminate, the acumen 2-2.5 cm long; base acute to obtuse, narrowly decurrent onto the petiole; margins distinctly serrate, with 10-13 teeth on each side. Petioles 7-11 mm long, canaliculate. Stipules ovate to very widely ovate, 0.8-1.6 X 0.9-1.1 mm. Inflorescences racemose, arising from 34 the distance up the blade to the base of the acumen, with 1-3 separate rachises per cluster, the rachis squamose, 2.5-8.5 mm long, the flowers tightly congested, the pedicels 1.5-3 mm long, subtended by a very broadly ovate bract with fimbriate margins, the bracts more or less imbricate. Flowers 2.5 mm diam.; sepals triangular, 0.3 X 0.3-0.4 mm, with 1-several minute teeth on each side; petals triangular to widely ovate, 0.8-1.0 X 0.7-0.8 mm, with an inconspicuous midvein, pale green or greenish-yellow; filaments 0.3 mm long, the anthers +/- globose, 0.3 mm long; ovary with the hypanthium as long or slightly longer than broad, the style bifid, 0.2 mm long. Berry globose, 4 X 4 mm. Seeds oblong, 2.5-2.8 X 1.5-1.7 mm.

description: Leaf petioles 3.0-22.0 (-28.0) cm long, villous with spreading hairs up to about 5.0 mm long, usually brown on senescent leaves or in specimens dried without heat, generally white in well-dried specimens; blades 1.8-10.0 (-11.5) cm long, 1.7-9.0 (-10.0) cm wide, nearly orbicular with a deeply cordate base, the sinus often closed or with overlapping lobes, and 7-9 (-11) shallow, slightly overlapping lobes which are crenate with broad, flat, short-mucronate, finely serrulate teeth; upper surface of the leaves essentially glabrous, shining, bright green, the lower surface gray-green, glabrate and sparsely villous along the veins. Scapes 50.0-110.0 cm high with 1-4 yellowish or searious fimbriate bracts, villous below grading into glandular-puberulent above; panicle (3.5-) 5.5-12.0 (-15.0) cm long, 1.6-1.8 cm wide in flower, 1.9-2.6 cm wide in fruit, sometimes interrupted below; cymules 1-2-flowered; bracts 6.0-9.0 mm long, greenishyellow, fimbriate, often trifid and glandular-puberulent. Receptacle and sepals glandular-puberulent with a few long hairs, bright green; sepal lobes (3.2-) 3.5-4.5 mm long, (1.2-) 1.6-2.3 mm wide; petals usually wanting, if present linear-spatulate and much smaller than the sepals: stamens ineluded, 2.3-3.2 mm long, the filaments about 3 times the length of the anthers; capsule about 1.0 cm long and somewhat exserted.

description: Shrubs to 2 (4) m tall, intricately branched, often stunted and straggly, the bark exfoliating in reddish-brown, papery plates or grayish, fibrous strips; herbage ascending-strigose; leaves petiolate, the petiole (1) 2-20 (45) mm long, the blade ovate to rounded-ovate, (1) 1.3-8 (9.5) cm long, (0.8) 1-5 (8.5) cm wide, cuneate basally, obtuse apically, the margins with (9) 11-51 (69) crenations or teeth, these often with a mucronate or apiculate tip, the primary lateral veins ascending to the tips of the lobes or teeth, green above, with strigose hairs or glabrate, densely grayish- or whitish-pubescent beneath; inflorescence a 5-35-flowered cyme, rarely with a side-branch bearing only 1 or 2 flowers, the pedicels, hypanthia, and sepals densely strigose, the pedicels 1.5-5.2 mm long; hypanthium hemispheric, 1.3-1.8 mm high; sepals 5, lanceolate to deltate-ovate, 1.5-7 (8) mm long, acute to obtuse and sometimes 2- or 3-lobed apically; petals 5, obovate or oblanceolate, (4) 5.5- 11 (11.5) mm long, with a pubescent patch on both surfaces, spreading, white to pink; stamens 10, the petaloid filaments (2) 2.7-10 mm long, unequal in length, white to pink, the anthers 0.7-1.1 mm long, oval; styles persistent, (3) 3.5-6.5 (8) mm long; capsule 3.5-5.5 (7) mm long, ovoid; seeds elliptic-ovoid to fusiform, 0.6-0.8 mm long, longitudinally reticulate, shiny orangish-brown.

description: Leaf petioles 2.0-16.0 (-21.0) cm long, glandular-puberulent to hirsute, occasionaly villous, the long hairs usually minutely gland-tipped up to about 3.0 mm long; blades 1.2-6.5 (-8.5) cm long, 1.0-6.5 cm wide, ovate to nearly orbicular, the base slightly to strongly cordate, the sinus seldom closed, and the principal leaves with 5-7 frequently overlapping lobes which are crenate with rounded or slightly mucronate teeth; leaves gray-green, glandular-puberulent to moderately glandular-hirsute. description: Leaves of the eaudiees cuneate or oblanceolate, 6-15 (-19) mm long, 1.5-4.5 mm wide or up to 6.5 mm including the divergent lateral cusps, a large proportion with three apical teeth, these each tipped with a rigid, usually white, mutero 0.3-1.2 mm long; marginal cilia weak, usually small, but those near the leaf base occasionally to 0.3 mm long, tipped with elongate, red-brown glands; blades flat, usually reddish or occasionally light green, usually somewhat imbricate, but scattered on elongate caudices in shade-grown plants; cauline leaves smaller, the lateral teeth usually small or lacking; flowering stems about 4-10 cm high in very exposed, up to 20-24 cm in more sheltered situations; stems and panicle branches slightly to moderately capitate-glandular especially above; panicle several to many-flowered, occupying 1/6 to 1/3 the height of the plant; sepals ea 1.5-2.8 mm long, 1-1.8 (-2.3) mm wide at base, entire to lightly and finely glandular-ciliate; petals 4-7 mm long, 1.5-3.2 (-3.5) mm wide, -+ elliptic, sometimes narrowed slightly at base but never clawed, white to cream (drying cream to light yellow), the inner face heavily spotted, the lower spots deep yellow, the middle orange and the uppermost deep red; stamens shorter than the mature petals except in occasional small-petaled plants; filaments subulate; mature capsules (4-) 5-8 mm long. description: Leaves of the caudices grayish green to purplish brown, ca. 2-7 mm long, 1-1.8 mm wide, spatulate with obtuse apex with or without a delicate and often concolorous mucro up to 0.2 mm long, sessile and broad-based; marginal cilia small, delicate and crowded, up to ca. 0.15 mm long near the apex and to 0.3 mm toward the leaf base; leaves loosely to very closely imbricate, according to habitat; cauline leaves narrow, delicately ciliate or glandular-ciliate; flowering stems ca. 0.4-0.8 mm thick, 2-6.5 cm high, moderately capitate-glandular below, strongly so above; flowers few, on delicate and strongly capitate-glandular panicle branches; sepals 1.3-2 mm long, 1.2-1.7 mm wide, rounded or acute, often delicately glandular-ciliate; petals 3-5 mm long, 1.2-2.3 (-2.8) mm wide, elliptic, not clawed at base, cream to brownish yellow when dried, a few yellow spots sometimes visible on the inner face in well-dried specimens, rarely a few small red spots at or above the middle, stamens shorter than petals; filaments subulate; mature capsules ca. 3.5-4 mm high, the wdith nearly equal to the height. description: Perennial herb from a branched woody caudex, this surmounting an elongate taproot; sterile stems often present, short and bearing crowded leaves; flowering stems erect to ascending, (2.5) 3-6 dm tall, 1 to few; herbage puberulent, the hairs becoming glandular above; leaves of 2 types, the margins obscurely toothed or entire, the basal and lower cauline leaves 5.5-14 cm long, 3-14 mm broad, linear-oblanceolate, tapered to a sometimes elongated petiole, ascending to spreading, the middle and upper cauline leaves 2.5-4 (6) cm long, 1-3 (7) mm broad, linear to narrow lanceolate, broadest at the sessile and sometimes subcordate-clasping base, spreading nearly at right angles; thyrse 13-30 cm long, of 6-10 widely spaced verticillasters, the cymes 1-2 (3)-flowered, the axis, peduncles, pedicels and calyces glandular-pubescent with whitish hairs; calyx 4-7 mm long, lanceolate, acute to obtuse, more or less straight, the margins herbaceous, not scarious; corolla 16-20 mm long, ventricose-ampliate, glandular-pubescent externally, the throat and limb blue, the tube violet, the tube 6-7 mm long, the throat 2-ridged at the orifice, 5.5-7 mm broad when pressed, the palate pale yellow- to whitish-bearded, the upper lip erect and the lower projecting-spreading; staminode reaching the orifice or slightly exserted, straight with a slightly recurved tip, densely pubescent to near the base, the yellow hairs 0.9-1.4 mm long at the tip and diminishing in length (0.5 mm) basally; fertile stamens included in the throat, the anther-sacs 1.4-1.8 mm long (after dehiscence), remaining nearly parallel after dehiscence, not explanate, dehiscing the full length and across the connective, glabrous except for the papillate-toothed sutures, blue-gray on the sides; capsule ca 10 mm long, ovoid; seeds few, ca 2 mm long, angled.
bibliographicCitation: Holmgren, Noel H. 1980. A new Penstemon [P. distans] (Scrophulariaceae) from northwestern Arizona. Brittonia. 32: 326-329.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Statura brevi, foliis angustis, inflorescentia glandulosa, corolla parva, staminodio glabro necnon antherarum valvulis post dehiscentiam ex parte tantum hiantibus cum P. parvo Pennell congruens, sed foliis glanduloso-papillatis (nec retrorsus puberulis), caulibus basin versus aphyllis (nec dense foliatis), calycis 5-6.6 (nec 3-4, raro 5) mm longi segmentis anguste lanceolatis (nec ovatis) corollaque glabra (nec glanduloso-puberula) diversa.
bibliographicCitation: Holmgren, Noel H. & Shultz, Leila M. 1982. A new species of Penstemon (Scrophulariaceae) from southwestern Utah. Brittonia. 34: 381-383.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herbaceous perennial; stems 0.5-1.5 dm tall, clustered, usually several arising from a buried, branched, woody caudex and ascending or decumbent above the sand surface; herbage and inflorescence glandular-papillate and glutinous with sand grains adhering throughout; leaves entire and crisped-margined, the lower cauline leaves petiolate, 2.5-5.5 cm long, the blade obovate, 4-8 mm wide, the upper cauline sessile, 1.5-4 cm long, 2-5 mm wide, narrowly oblanceolate, rounded apically; thyrse somewhat compressed, of 5-7 verticillasters, racemelike above with 1-flowered cymules, the lower cymules 2-3-flowered, not secund, the peduncles short to absent, small bracted, the pedicels 2-6 mm long; calyx becoming coriaceous, 5-6.5 mm long, the segments narrowly lanceolate or lanceolate, caudate, the broadened base erose-margined; corolla caducous, 14-17 mm long, moderately ampliate, the throat 5-5.5 mm broad when pressed, shallowly 2-ridged ventrally, both lips more or less projecting-spreading, the lower lip 4-5 mm long, slightly exceeding the upper and with slightly larger lobes, the tube 5-6 mm long, the limb lavender to lavender-blue, glabrous within and without; staminode included, white with dark violet papillate hairs on the upper surface; fertile stamens reaching the orifice, the anther cells 0.9-1.2 mm long, dehiscing from the tips to the connective, the valves only slightly spreading apart, the sutures papillose; capsule 3.5-6.5 mm long, broadly ovoid, acuminate; seeds 2-3 mm long, somewhat winged, black.
bibliographicCitation: Holmgren, Noel H. & Shultz, Leila M. 1982. A new species of Penstemon (Scrophulariaceae) from southwestern Utah. Brittonia. 34: 381-383.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herbae perennes prostratae e caudice ramoso, foliis glabris glaucis; thrysus compactus e verticillastris 2-4 compositus, cymulis 1-2-floris; corolla glaberrima, alba vel lilacina; staminodium inclusum vel vix exsertum, fere tota longitudine pilis brevibus sparsis indutum; antherae subdivergentes, ab apice ad basin usque dehiscentes.
bibliographicCitation: O'Kane, Steve & Anderson, John L. 1987. Pentstemon debilis (Scrophulariaceae): a new species from Colorado endemic to oil shale. Brittonia. 39: 412-416.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herbaceous perennial, forming mats. Roots fleshy. Stems arising from a subterranean soboliferous caudex, often branching and sometimes rooting at the nodes; subterranean parts with sessile, subulate, scalelike leaves 1-2.5 (5) mm long and 1.2-1.7 mm wide; above-ground parts glandular-puberulent distally, less so below. Basal leaves lacking; cauline leaves sessile, opposite, succulent, obovate, elliptic, or more commonly oblanceolate, tapering to base, the apex rounded or acute, some mucronate, glabrous, strongly blue-glaucous (olive-green when pressed), with narrow-white margins 0.2 mm wide (becoming greener when dried), entire to minutely erosulate (at 20 x), 1.2-2.5 (3.2) cm long, 0.4-1.2 cm wide. Thyrse compact, of 2-4 verticillasters, cymules 1-2-flowered, subsecund; sepals lanceo- late, 7-11.5 mm long and 1.5-2.5 mm wide, with white, erose and hyaline margins, glabrous; corolla (14) 17.5-20 mm long, slightly bilabiate, the lower lip longer than the upper, light lavender to nearly white, or sometimes deeper lavender, usually with a darker ring at the junction of the tube and throat, funnelform and slightly ampliate, slightly 2-ridged ventrally, glabrous throughout, tube 6-7 mm long, the throat (6) 7-9.5 (11) mm long; staminode 9-9.5 mm long, barely included to scarcely exserted, gradually and slightly expanding toward the truncate apex, sparsely golden-hairy on upper surface for most of its length with a loose tuft at apex, trichomes up to 0.9 mm in length; fertile stamens included; anthers bright magenta at anthesis, 0.9-1.4 mm long, dehiscent from apex to base almost to connective, surface sparsely hispid with white trichomes less than 0.4 mm long, the cells ultimately diverging from filament ca 30-45º; style 9-10.5 mm long, clavate at tip. Capsule 2.5-5 mm wide, 3.5-7.5 mm long, the valves ovate with acute to acuminate tips, purple when fully expanded; seeds 1.5-2.5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: O'Kane, Steve & Anderson, John L. 1987. Pentstemon debilis (Scrophulariaceae): a new species from Colorado endemic to oil shale. Brittonia. 39: 412-416.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Caulibus 1-2 dm altis, pubescentibus; foliis linearibus, lineari-oblanceolatis, vel lineari-lanceolatis, 2-9 cm x 2-5 (8) mm; inflorescentia glanduloso-pubescenti; corolla caerulea, 15-20 mm longa, pubescenti; antheris pubescentibus, ab apice non usque ad basim dehiscentibus.
bibliographicCitation: Dorn, Robert D. 1982. A new species of Penstemon (Scrophulariaceae) from Wyoming. Brittonia. 34: 334, 335.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Stems 1-2 dm high, several to many from root crown, pubescent usually to near base; leaves opposite, entire, linear to linear-oblanceolate or lance-linear, to 9 cm long, mostly 5 (8) mm or less wide, at least the lower mostly glabrous, the middle ones the longest; inflorescence glandular-pubescent, not secund;flowers 3-7 per cymule; sepals lanceolate with long attenuate tips, 6-8 mm long, the margins often narrowly whitish but scarcely membranous; corolla blue, 15-20 mm long, gradually expanded distally or with a short tubular base, the lobes all distinct, pubescent inside and out, the inner hairs long and broad, the outer smaller and mostly glandular; anthers pubescent, dehiscing not quite to base; staminode sparsely bearded at tip; seeds 2-3 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Dorn, Robert D. 1982. A new species of Penstemon (Scrophulariaceae) from Wyoming. Brittonia. 34: 334, 335.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Herba perennis suffruticosa omnino dense glanduloso-pubeseens, basibus caulium molliter ligneis, caulibus altis crassis erectis foliosissimnis; foliis late lanceolatis vel ovatis acuminatis amplexicaulibus non connatis; pedunculis brevibus manifeste bracteolatis 2-5-floris; sepalis late lanceolatis integerrimis; corollis late ventricosis bilabiatis, labiis inferioribus intus dense villosis; antherarum loculis divaricatis confluentibus non explanatis; apicibus staminodiorum dilatatis laevissime barbatis.
bibliographicCitation: Straw, Richard M. 1963. The Penstemons of Mexico. III. Two subsection in the section Fasciculus. Brittonia. 15: 49-64.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Planta nana, ad 12 cm. alta, glabra, prostrata vel suberecta; rhizoma crassum, simplex, radicibus permultis fasciculatis, longissimis, rigidulis, parcissime fibrosis; foliis radicalibus 3-6, petiolis ad 3.5 cm. longa ala praeditis; lamina rotundata vel late ovata, 2-3 cm. longa, 2-3 cm. lata, ad apicem plus minusve rotundata vel obtusa, ad basim subrotundata vel cordulata, ad marginem integra vel raro inconspicue dentata vel subintegra, in sicco papyracea, venis inconspicuis; scapis solitariis, prostratis vel suberectis, ad 12 cm. longis, folia su- perantibus, crassiusculis, spicis densissimis, ad 2.5 cm. longis, 2 cm. crassis; bracteis inferioribus foliaceis compluribus sterilibus sessilibus vel brevipetio- latis, late ovatis vel rotundatis ad 2 cm. longis; bracteis superioribus herbaceis, 4-6 mm. longis, ovatis, ad apicem acutis, calycibus spathaceis, 4-5 mm. longis, tenuissime membranaceis, ad medium divisis, lobis oblongis obtusis, ciliatis; corolla pallide lialicina vel atro-cyanea, circiter 10- 12 mm. longa, corollae tubo 4-5 mm. longo, limbo 6-7 mm. longo, labio superiore lanceolato vulgo integro, 2 mm. lato, labio inferiore duo lineari-lanceolato, 1 mm. lato; staminibus inclusis, filamentis brevissimis; stylo incluso, stigmate capitato integro; capsulis ignotis.
bibliographicCitation: Li, Hui-Lin. 1954. A revision of the genus Lagotis in China. Brittonia. 8: 23-38.

description: Planta nana, ad 12 cm. alta, postrata vel suberecta; rhizoma crassum, simplex, radicibus permultis longissimis, rigidulis; foliis radicalibus 4-5, petiolis ad 3 cm. longa ala praeditis; lamina late ovata, 3-5 cm. longa 2-2.5 cm. lata, ad apicem obtusa, ad basim subrotundata vel late obtusa, ad marginem distincte crenato-serrulata, in sicco papyracea, venis conspicuis; scapis solitariis vel 2-3, prostratis vel suberectis, ad 12 cm. longis, foliis superantibus, crassiusculis; spicis densissimis, 5 cm. raro ad 7 cm. longis, 2.5 cm. crassis, bracteis inferioribus foliaceis compluribus sterilibus sessilibus vel subsessilibus late ovatis vel rotundatis, serratis vel inconspicue serratis, ad 1.5 cm. longis; bracteis superioribus herbaceis, 6_8 mm. longis, ovatis, ad apicem acutis; calyce spathaceo, 6-8 mm. longo, tenuissime membranaceo, breviter bilobato, lobis rotundatis, ciliatis; corolla pallide lilacina, 12-14 mm. longa, corollae tubo 6-7 mm. longo, limbo 7-8 mm. longo, labio superiore oblongo, 3.4 mm. longo, distincte emarginato vel 2 raro 3-lobato, labio inferiore duo, lanceolato, 2 mm. lato; staminibus inclusis, filamentis brevissimis; stylo incluso, stigmate capitato, capsulis ignotis.
bibliographicCitation: Li, Hui-Lin. 1954. A revision of the genus Lagotis in China. Brittonia. 8: 23-38.
