description: Planta nana, 4-5 cm. alta, glabra vel parcissime pubescens, estolonosa, acaulescens, rhizomate crassa, radicibus fasciculatis, brevibus vel longis, crassis, fibrosis; foliis omnino basalibus, numerosis, plus minusve cespitosis, longe petiolatis, petiolis 1-1.3 cm. longis, late alatis, ad marginem glabris vel parce ciliatis, laminis chartaceis, glabris vel parce pubescentibus, oblongis vel oblongo-obovatis, circiter 1-1.2 cm. longis, 5-7 mm. latis, ad apicem late ro- tundatis, ad marginem integris, ad basim in petiolis acute attenuatis; floribus basalibus, singulis vel 2-3, pedunculis nullis vel parvis, ad 5 mm. longis; pedicellis gracilibus, longis, folia superantibus, ad 3 cm. longis, plerumque glabris; bracteis minimis oblongis, 3-5 mm. longis obtusis glabris; calycibus infundibularis, glabris vel parce pubescentibus, 5 mm. longis et latis, ad medium 5-lobatis, lobis triangulari-ovatis, acutis; corolla rosea, 11 mm. longa, extus glabra, intus palato breviter clavato-piloso; tubo circiter 6-7 mm. longo, 3 mm. lato, dimidio superiore ampliato; labio superiore 2-3 mm. longo, anguste triangulari-ovato, rotundato, apice bifido; labio inferiore duplo longiore, circiter 6 mm. longo, 6 mm. lato, infra dimidio trilobo, lobis rotundatis medio quam late-ralibus paulo longiore et subduplo angustiore; filamentis glabris, inclusis vel superiore a fauce paulo exsertis; stylis inclusis; fructis ignotis.
bibliographicCitation: Li, Hui-Lin. 1954. The Genus Mazus (Scrophulariaceae). Brittonia. 8 (1): 29-38.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Shrub or perhaps a tree, with smooth or very finely wrinkled glaucous twigs, these sometimes becoming hollow by degeneration of the large soft pith; leaflets mostly 7-13, entire or obscurely crenulate, ovate or elliptic-ovate, rounded to occasionally acutish at the base, acute to sometimes rounded at the apex, mostly 4-9 cm. long and 2.5-3.5 cm. wide, the lowermost ones much shorter and proportionately broader than the upper ones, all glabrous or nearly so when mature, except for some fine reddish hairs along the midrib and som-etimes also the main veins; young leaflets copiously puberulent with yellowish or reddish hairs; flowers unknown; fruiting infloreseence with reddish-puberulent sepals about 1-2 mm. long, and light greenish petals about 3-4 mm. long; fruiting gynophore short and broad, not lobed, not over 2.5 mm. long; fruit red, about 5-6 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1944. Studies in the Simaroubaceae--IV. Resumé of the American genera. Brittonia. 5: 128-147.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Smnall tree reported to be 5-6 m. high; leaflets about 5-9, glabrous, or more commonly finely velvety or short-hairy on the veins, when mature, evidently reticulate-veiny on both sides, narrowly to broadly elliptic, or ovate, rounded to distinctly acute at the apex, mostly 1-6 cm. long, 5-30 mm. wide; leaf-rachis narrowly and ineonspicuously winged, infloreseence large, open, complex; sepals about 4-5 mm. long, firm; petals about 6.5-9 mm. long, yellowish, delicate; fruit globose or ellipsoid, about 1-1.5 cm. long, red, the thin smooth outer layer readily peeling, in herbarium specimens.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1944. Studies in the Simaroubaceae--IV. Resumé of the American genera. Brittonia. 5: 128-147.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Erect shrub or small tree mostly 2-5 m. high, branches densely short-tomentose, tardily glabrate; sepals deltoid, acute, densely short-hairy, about 1 mm. long; petals firm, densely short-hairy on the back, about 4 mm. long, fairly broad, and narrowed to a short and broad somewhat claw-like base; fruit red, obliquely ovoid, slightly compressed, about 5-8 mm. long, usually rounded ventrally and rounded or obtuse at the apex.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1944. Studies in the Simaroubaceae--IV. Resumé of the American genera. Brittonia. 5: 128-147.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Depressed or aseending shrub up to 1.5 m. high; branches moderately hirsutestrigose, soon glabrate; sepals ovate, acute, moderately strigose, a little over 1 mm. long; petals firm, about 4 mm. long, sparsely or moderately strigose, broad, not at all claw-like at the base; fruit red or greenish, obliquely ovoid, about 6-9 mm. long, a little more compressed than in H. Emoryi, distinctly ridged ventrally, tending to be acute at the apex.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1944. Studies in the Simaroubaceae--IV. Resumé of the American genera. Brittonia. 5: 128-147.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Arbor ad 20 m. alta, trunco prope basin 15 cm. diametro; ramulis teretibus fuscis juventute arete cano-puberulis; foliis 25-40 cm. longis 9-11-foliolatis, petiolis rhachidibusque teretibus arete strigosis; peti-olulis incrassatis 1.5-3 mm. longis; laminis papyraceis ovato-oblongis, 7-13 cm. longis (eis basis brevioribus), 3.5-6 cm. latis, basi inaequi-lateraliter truncatis vel acutis, apice caudato-acuminatis, margine integris, supra costa puberula excepta subglabris, subtus praecipue ad nervos arete puberulis, nervis secundariis utroque 4-6 arcuato-adscen-dentibus cum costa supra prominulis subtus prominentibus, venulis reticulatis utrinque prominulis; ramis floriferis quam foliis paullo brevioribus paniculatis 1-5-ramosis, ramulis cinereo-puberulis; floribus 5 dense glomerulatis subsessilibus; calyce breviter strigoso, lobis 5 ovatis acutis, 1.5 mm. longis, 0.8 mm. latis; petalis 5 membranaceis glabris oblongo-linearibus, 1.3 mm. longis, 0.3 mm. latis; staminodiis oblongis 0.3 longis petalis oppositis; ovario striguloso, stylo 2-fido, lobis recurvatis; ovulis in loculis 2 geminis; baccis demum glabris nigre-centibus ovoideis 8-12 mm. longis.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1936. Plantae Krukovianae. V. Brittonia. 2: 145-164.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Small tree; leaflets about 9-19, ovate to elliptic-lanceolate, broadly rounded to acutish at the base, often somewhat asymmetric, abruptly acuminate at the apex, mostly 4-12 cm. long, 1.5-4.5 cm. wide, the lower ones sometimes markedly smaller than those above, crenulate to near the base, glabrous when mature; filaments, in the staminate flowers at least, sparsely spreading-hairy; hermaphrodite inflorescence of the ordinary size for the genus; fruiting gynophore well developed, often lobed; fruit globose or broadly obovoid, 8-10 mm. long, 7-9 mm. thick.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1944. Studies in the Simaroubaceae--IV. Resumé of the American genera. Brittonia. 5: 128-147.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Species foliis simplicibus, inflorescentiis caulifloris, habitationi in pluviosylva a congeneribus diversa. Arbor 3-15 m. Ramuli glabri. Stipulae deltatae vel lanceolato-deltatae, 0.5-1.5 (2.5) mm longae persistentes. Folia simplicia alterna. Lamina integra glabra elliptica vel ovato-elliptica vel anguste elliptica, 10-32 x 3-11 cm, (2.8) 3-4.5-plo longior quam latior, apici abrupte acuminata, basi valde obliqua. Petiolus 5-15 mm longus. Inflorescentia saepissime cauliflora vel ramiflora paniculata, usque ad 35 x 30 cm autem plerumque multo minor. Pedicelli 1-4 mm longi puberuli. Calyx patens fere ad basim 5-partitus; lobi subaequales rotundati concavi, eburnei vel roseo-aurantiaci, 2.5-4 x 1.5-3 mm. Petala 5 libera cito caduca, alba vel lutea vel aurantiaca, 3.5-5 x 1-1.8 mm. Stamina 10 ad basim articulata, ex annulo 10-lobato enascentia; filamenta 2-3 mm longa, antherae 0.8-1 mm longae. Carpella 2-3 (4) libera, 0.8-0.9 mm longa, e gynophoro 0.5 mm longo enascentia; stylus fere basalis adaxialis, 1.5-2.5 mm longus, stigma capitatum. Fructus de 1-2 carpellis drupaceis e gynophoro tumido enascentibus compositum; drupae sphaericae vel leviter reniformes 1.5-2 cm longae, splendide aurantiaco-rubrae vel rubrae, exocarpium tenue laeve friabile, mesocarpium succulentum reticulato-fibrosum aureum, endocarpium tenue. Semen reniforme.
bibliographicCitation: Wendt, Tom & Lott, Emily J. 1985. A new simple-leaved species of Recchia (Simaroubaceae) from southeastern Mexico. Brittonia. 37: 219-225.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Tree 3-15 m tall, to 35 cm d.b.h. Bark of trunk grayish-brown, irregularly finely roughened by lenticellar warts 1-3 mm in diameter, only mildly bitter, slash dark reddish-brown, sapwood pale cream-yellow. Branchlets grayish- or reddish-brown, glabrous, usually slightly geniculate at the nodes, with irregularly scattered round or oblong lenticels 0.2-0.5 mm long, distal internodes 1.5-8 cm long. Stipules deltate to lance-triangular, 0.5-1.5 (2.5) mm long, at first puberulent with ap- pressed hairs but soon glabrate and indurate, persistent, apex narrowly acute to acuminate. Leaves alternate, distichous, simple; blade elliptic or ovate-elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 10-32 cm long, 3-11 cm wide, (2.8) 3-4.5 times as long as wide, glabrous, dark green above when fresh, dull olive-green when dry, slightly paler beneath, firm-textured when fresh, chartaceous when dry, tip abruptly acuminate from an acute to broadly rounded apex, the drip-tip usually 1-2.5 cm long, extreme tip minutely rounded, base strongly oblique with distal side rounded to subtrun- cate and proximal side acute to cuneate, margin entire, often irregularly weakly wavy, pale yellow-brown, venation brochidodromous, midvein slightly raised above, strongly raised and more prominent beneath, other venation slightly raised above, raised and prominent beneath, secondary veins 1 1-18 per side excluding tip, diverging 55-75? from midrib, arcuately anastomosing 3-5 mm from margin, each areole with several tertiary veins parallel to the secondaries and the rest of the tertiary venation reticulate; petiole 5-15 mm long, 1.2-2.5 mm thick, glabrous, articulate at base, slightly canaliculate adaxially, drying dark brown or reddish- brown and wrinkled. Inflorescence borne on trunk and larger branches, occasion- ally also axillary among the leaves, a very open irregularly many-branched to much contracted panicle, up to 35 cm long and 30 cm wide, short- to long- pedunculate, principal axes becoming somewhat woody, branches to 17 cm, branching irregular and often crowded in certain parts of panicle, branches gen- erally divergent, sometimes reduced (especially in inflorescences among leaves) to a short scaly axis a few mm long with 1 to few flowers; flowers alternate, spaced or crowded; bract and 2 bracteoles subtending each flower, these puberulent, bracts ca 0.4-0.5 mm long, deltate, bracteoles smaller, sterile bracts and bracteoles usually concentrated in basal parts of inflorescence branches; pedicels 1-4 mm long, lightly puberulent, articulated ca 0.2 mm above base. Flowers: calyx spread- ing at anthesis, divided almost to the base, the 5 lobes subequal, rounded, concave, cream to pale yellow-green, or pinkish-orange, 2.5-4 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, glabrous to pilosulous without, glabrous within, lightly ciliate, entire or slightly erose, persistent; petals 5, free, oblong-elliptic, white, cream, yellow or orange, early deciduous, 3.5-5 mm long, 1-1.8 mm wide; stamens 10, articulated at base to a 10-lobed ring surrounding gynophore, early deciduous; filaments 2-3 mm long, free, glabrous; anthers 0.8-1 mm long and wide, versatile, bithecous, opening by lateral longitudinal slits; carpels free, distinct, 2-3 (4), biovulate, 0.8-0.9 mm long, 0.6 mm wide, borne on a gynophore ca 0.5 mm long; style nearly basal, adaxial, 1. 5-2.5 mm long; stigma capitate. Fruit comprising 1 or 2 mature drupe-like carpels arising from the swollen gynophore, each spherical or slightly reniform, 1.5-2 cm long, bright orange-red or tomato red; exocarp thin, papyraceous, smooth, brittle, breaking easily and irregularly; mesocarp of a longitudinally oriented reticulum of fleshy fibers, yellow, sweet; endocarp thin, light brown. Seed 1 per carpel, reniform, 8-10 mm long, 12-15 mm in diam; testa thin, soft; endosperm absent; cotyledons swollen.
bibliographicCitation: Wendt, Tom & Lott, Emily J. 1985. A new simple-leaved species of Recchia (Simaroubaceae) from southeastern Mexico. Brittonia. 37: 219-225.

description: Arbuscula vel arbores glabrescentes usque ad 8-10 m. Folia imparipinnata, 7-9-foliolata; foliola anguste ovata vel ovato-lanceolata, acuminata, serrulata; inflorescentia thyrsiformis, multiflora; sepala 3, inaequalia; petala 5, anguste obovata, leviter unguiculata; fructus globosus.
bibliographicCitation: Williams, Louis O. 1966. New plants from south Mexico and Guatemala. Brittonia. 18: 265, 267.

description: Shrubs or trees 8-10 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves odd-pinnate, with 7-9 leaflets, 10-15 cm long with a relatively long slender petiole, the petiole angled above and with an inconspicuous mammillate gland at the base of each petiolule; leaflets opposite, the lower ones short petiolulate, the upper ones sessile or nearly so, the blade narrowly ovate or ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, with small gland-tooth serrations, paler below than above, 1.5-4.5 cm long and 0.6-1.5 cm broad; inflorescence a many-flowered terminal thyrse, about as long as the subtending leaves; sepals 3, a pair ovate, ca 4 mm long, the third sepal slightly longer and oblong-ovate, ca 5 mm long; petals 5, narrowly obovate, slightly unguiculate; 5-6 mm long and 2.5 mm broad; stamens 5, about as long as the petals, the filaments complanate, inserted outside the disc; disc crenate-lobate; styles connate in flower but separated in fruit; fruit subglobose to obovate, about 10 mm in diameter, with three upright slender styles at the summit.

description: Much-branched shrubs to 3 m tall; branches densely foliaceous, strigulose, internodes 1-5 mm long. Leaves alternate, subsessile or with petioles 1-2 mm long, strigulose; blades oblanceolate to elliptic, 10-14 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, coriaceous, midrib prominent, base cuneate, apex obtuse, lower surface strigulose, the trichomes ca 0.2 mm long, upper surface glabrous, nitid; margins minutely denticulate with 6-10 pairs of mucronulate teeth. Inflorescences solitary, axillary, subsessile or pedicellate, to 3 mm long; bractlets 2, lanceolate to ovate, 2-2.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, glabrous, ciliolate; bracts 3, imbricate, ovate, ca 2.5 mm long, 2.2-2.5 mm wide, glabrous, ciliolate. Flowers pink; sepals 5, basally connate, imbricate, broadly ovate, ca 3 mm long, ca 4 mm wide, the apex obtuse to rounded, ciliolate; petals 6, biseriate, imbricate, connate below to form a short tube, ob- ovate, 6-7 mm long, 5-6 mm wide, the apex rounded; stamens 40-46, connate, 4-6-seriate, adnate to corolla base, the anthers introrse, basifixed, ca 1 mm long, thecae parallel; ovary 3-carpellate, semi-inferior, pilose, the style slender, the stigma 5-lobed. Fruits (immature) drupaceous, crowned by the persistent calyx lobes, cylindric-oblong, terete, ca 10 mm long, ca 4 mm in diam, smooth, glabrous.

description: Subshrub, 0.5-1.5 m tall, slender; roots fibrous from a woody caudex; stems strict, unbranched or dichotomously so above, terete, nearly solid, glabrous to spreading-puberulent, to 7 mm in diameter, naked at base; leaves ascending, sub- coriaceous, cauline, undivided, entire, petiolate, blades ovate to narrowly so, 3-6.5 cm long, 0.8-1.2 cm wide, lustrous dark green on upper side, pallid beneath, the uppermost ones sessile and a little broader, glabrous (Wurdack 1731), ciliate and puberulent on lower side (Wurdack 1427), the petiole 1/3 as long as the blade, clasping, ciliate at base; inflorescence an aggregate dichasium, the terminal branches (3-) 8-15 cm long, 6-10 cm wide in anthesis, the nodes pilosulose, the internodes glabrous, bracts 3-4 mm long; flowers perfect; corolla infundibuliform, 3-4.5 mm long, white, pinkish in throat, glabrous, the lobes 1/3 to 1/2 as long as the gibbous tube; stamens and style exserted; achenes ovate-oblong, ca 4 mm long, glabrous; calyx-limb 11- to 13-fid.

description: Herbaceous perennial, to 2.5 m tall; roots fibrous; stems strict, loosely branched, terete, glabrous, to 6.5 mm thick, fistulose; leaves ascending, subcoriaceous, cauline, undivided, entire to denticulate, petiolate, the blades narrowly to broadly elliptic, 5-9 cm long, 2-3.5 cm wide, glabrous or sometimes sparingly ciliate, acute to short- acuminate, the midvein beneath prominent, the petioles 0.6-2 cm long, abruptly dilated, forming a more or less inflated cup around the stem, the cup glandular- papillose and sometimes sparsely puberulent within, glabrous or sparingly puberu- lent outside; inflorescence an aggregate dichasium, diffusely branched, the terminal branches 6-15 cm long, 9-20 cm wide in anthesis, glabrous or densely pilosulous at the nodes, the bracts linear, 5-6 mm long, sometimes sparsely papillate on margins; flowers perfect or gynodioecious, 3.2-6 mm long in the perfect ones, 2.5-3 mm long in the pistillate; corolla infundibuliform, glabrous or sometimes hairy at the base of the gibbous tube inside, lobes 1/3 to 1/2 as long as the tube; stamens and style exserted; achenes narrowly oblong, 3-3.5 mm long, about 1 mm wide, glabrous; calyx-limb 9- to 11-fid.

description: Herbaceous perennial, voluble or clambering, several meters long; roots unknown; stems slender, lithe, dichotomously branched, terete, fistulose, glabrous, 1-2 mm thick; leaves herbaceous, cauline, ovate, mostly 3-parted, sometimes un- divided in the uppermost, petiolate, the terminal lobe 1.4-2.2 cm long, 4-9 mm wide, serrate-dentate, the upper side green, pallid beneath, the lateral lobes spreading, smaller, the petiole 1-1.7 cm long; inflorescence a compound dichasium, terminal, diffuse, 8-10 cm long and as wide in fruit, the ultimate branches bracteate, pubescent at the nodes; flowers gynodioecious, the pistillate ones 2-2.5 mm long, the perfect ones 3.0-3.5 mm long; corolla white with a pale lavender flush, more or less campanulate-infundibuliform, glabrous, the lobes about half as long as the tube; stamens and style exserted; achenes ovate-oblong, falcate, 2-3 mm long, glabrous; calyx-limb 12- to 15-fid.

description: A deep-seated geophyte of open grassy dituations, 5-19 cm high; foliage grayish with a short microscopic puberulence throughout; rootstock erect, woody, Fending downward slender adventitious roots from the upper portion and larger woody roots from the lower portion, while from the summit spring the radical leaves and stems which are usually short, half their length or even more subterranean, the living plant appearing acauleseent, but in other plants the stems greatly elongated to 15 or even 30 em long with only a small proportion subterranean; radical leaves few or many according to the age of the plant, the lamina varying from ovate or nearly round to ovate or oblong-lanseolate, occasionally a few much wider and shorter than the cauline leaves, decurrent on the petioles which are two to three times as long as the blades and half or more subterranean, the margin ciliate, mostly entire, occasionally irregularly repanddentate; stipules searious, adnate to the petiole producing the wing, the free portion approximately at the surface of the ground, minute, often microscopic or entirely wanting: cauline leaves reduced to searious bracts below the ground, foliaceous above, never rounded but generally with much the same outline and margin as the radical leaves, but varying widely in outline in different localities from ovate to linear-lanceolate, three to six times longer than broad; petioles in the short-stemmed form progressively shorter upwards, leaving cauline as well as radical leaves at about the same height; stipules of cauline leaves foliaceous, narrowly lanceolate to oblong-linear; peduncles cauline, rarely reaching as high as the leaves, the bractlets searious, filiform mostly above the middle, of the peduncle; sepals linear, acute, 6-8 mm long and slightly more than 1 mm wide, the size of the auricles medium, puberulent; corolla yellow, tinged with brown on the backs of the petals, ca. 18 mm in diameter; upper and lateral petals narrow with few dark lines, the lateral with a few clavate beards, the lower petal spatulate, ca. 7 mm wide at the widest point and 14 mm long including the short and blunt spur; stamen-sheath, including the spur appendages, as in all of the Nutttallianae; stigma short-tubular, the style capitate, the head retrorsely bearded at the sides, 2.2 mm long, the ovary glabrous; capsule ovoid, glabrous but microscopically roughened, ca. 6 mm broad by 9 mm long; seeds light brown, ca. 1.6 mm wide and 2.8 mm long, their average weight 3 mg; caruncle large, extending more than 1/3 the length of the seed and completely enclosing the funiculus.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Alexander H. 1957. A contribution toward a monograph of Phaeocollybia. Brittonia. 9: 195-217.

description: Rounded mass of leaves and flowers, 4-16 cm in height and width, glabrate to retrorse-puberulent throughout; winter buds near the surface; rootstock vertical, simple when young, much branched in age; roots many from all parts of the rootstock; stems many in older plants but in most short with few leaves; leaves mostly radical, noticeably thin, ovate to oblong-ovate, occasionally rounded, with conspicuously rounded apex and mostly truncate to subcordate base, the margin entire, averaging 1.8 times as long as broad, 1-2.7 cm wide by 1.3-5 cm long, on petioles up to 7.5 cm long; cauline leaves of similar outline but smaller; stipules of radical leaves inconspicuous, searious, lanceolate to linear, those of the cauline leaves lanceolate, occasionally foliaceous but never conspicuous; flowers mostly from as high as to slightly higher than the leaves; peduncles cauline, mostly from near the ground, 3-11.5 cm long; bractlets minute, filiform, searious, barely visibly with a lens, attached near the flower; sepals linearlanceolate, ciliolate, 5-6 mm long, the auricles conspicuous; corolla yellow with more or less brown tinting on the back, variable in size, 10-13 mm from the short saccate spur to the end of the lower petal in dried well-pressed flowers; petals exceptionally wide and rounded for this group, the beards on the lateral petals few; stamen-sheath with collar opening as in the group; style uncommonly short, 1.9 mm long, ending in a head sparsely bearded on the sides, the stigma tubular with reflexed lower lip, the ovary piuberulent to glabrous; capsiule spherical, glabrate to densely short- puberulent, on downwardly curving peduncles; seeds small, clear tan in color, 1.15 X 2.1 mm, their average weight 1.5 mg; the smallest seeds in the V. nuttallii complex.

description: Viola affinis possesses a distinct suite of micromorphological characters including the seed coat's finely striated outer periclinal walls, reticulate-terete thickenings in the form of semi-rectangular or -circular rings, and plates with blends of foveate, falsifoveate, and scrobiculate surfaces, and one vis- ible layer of mostly linear capillary cuticular folds on the broad cylindrical petal trichomes. These characters are correlated with a suite of macromorphological characters (including narrowly ovate blades, presence of petal trichomes on the spurred petal, prostrate cleistogamous flower peduncle, densely spotted red-purple and often pubescent capsules, moderate orange-yellow seeds), substrate preference (rich loam), and habitat preferences (low shady borders of lakes and steams, low woods, and wet thickets and meadows) that justify maintaining V. affinis as a distinct species. They support neither Cronquist's (in Gleason & Cronquist, 1991) decision to subsume V. affinis into V. sororia nor McKinney's (1992) decision to abolish V. affinis and to erect the combination V. sororia var. affinis (LeConte) L. E. McKinney for the species previously known as V. nephrophylla (cf. Figs. 1D, 3C, 9D & 10A).

description: Low-growing plants appearing as erect tufts of leaves and flowers, approxis mately as wide as high, 3-13 cm above the ground, pubescent to glabrate; rootstock woody, erect, simple or branched, producing a stout, ligneous tap root without adventitious roots; seasonal buds near the surface; stems one to many, remarkably short; radical leaves few, unusually thin, ovate to broadly elliptical or ovate-lanceolate, with parallel venation and narrow cuneate base, 1.5-3 times as long as wide, with entire and usually ciliated margins, on petioles 1.5-10 cm long; stipules searious throughout, adnate, forming winged petioles, their free tips lanceolate, near the surface of the ground; cauline leaves similar in texture, venation, and margin to the radical leaves but narrower, ranging from 2 to 5 times as long as broad on petioles progressively shorter upwards, thus producing together with the radical leaves a more or less flat-topped plant; stipules of the cauline leaves s5-all, lanceolate, searious to foliaceous, scarcely discernible at flowering time, 5-10 mm long; peduncles rarely longer than the leaves, more or less pubescent, occasionally hirsute; bractlets minute, filiform, searious above the middle, often widely separated; sepals narrow, linear-lanceolate, glabrous except for occasional puberulence on the auricles, the lowest usually the longest, 5-9 mm long; corallo clear yellow with or without brown tinting on the back, variable in size but rather small for the nutttaltii complex; petals wide as in V. vallicola, the lateral bearded, the lower petal (in dried flowers) 11-13 mm from the short, blunt spur to the tip; stamen-sheath as in other Nuttallianae; style 2.6 mm in length, the head bearded laterally as is characteristic of the group, the ovary glabrous; capsule s-nall, spherical, glabrous, 4-9-seeded; seeds dark brown, finely mottled, averaging 1.8 mm wide and 3 mm long, their average weight 4.2 mg; caruncle small for the group, extending to but not covering the point of the seed.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Alexander H. 1957. A contribution toward a monograph of Phaeocollybia. Brittonia. 9: 195-217.

description: Spreading plants varying in size with the season, 6-15 cm high during the flowering season, to 16 cm and more at the end of the season of growth, conspicuously hirsute particularly on the stems, petioles, and pedruncles; rootstockshort, erect, woody, often praemorse; roots mostly adventitious from all parts of the rootstock, the lower becoming large and woody in dry situatins; stems few to many, inconspicuous in flowering time but later very evident and up to 30 cm long; leaves thick, small during the flowering period, hirsutely pubeseent but the pubescence variable in amount and individual hairs inereasing greatly in length and in size during the fruiting period; radical leaves few, rounded to ovate, occasionally as wide as or even wider than long, conspicuously rounded at the apex, cuneate to truncate and decurrent at the base, the margins mostly entire, occasionally faintly repand-serrate, 1.9-3.5 cm wide and 2.5-6 cm long on petioles 4.5-9 cm long; upper cauline leaves similar but smaller, on shorter petioles; lower stipules inconspicuous, lanceolate, searious except late in the season on well-developed stems, and then foliaceous, ovate to obovate, 8-13 mm long; early peduncles appearing radical, but from the base of stems raising flowers well above the immature spreading leaves, 5-9 cm long, densely hirsute to the minute searious bractlets at the middle or above, less pubescent above; sepals linear, acute, more or less ciliate, 7-10 mm long; corolla canary-yellow, often without a brownish tinge on the back, ca. 2.2 cm across the face in fresh flowers, the lower petal narrow, ca. 8 mm wide and 18 mm long including the short, blunt spur; stamen-sheath as in other Nuttallianae; stigma tubular, the capitate head retrorsely bearded on the sides, the style 2.6 mm long, the ovary glabrous; capsule glabrous, ca. 9 mm wide and 10 mm long; seeds light tan throughout, their average width 1.9 mm and length 3.1 mm, their average weight 5.2 mg; caruncle large, projecting beyond the point of the seed, and completely enclosing the funiculus.

description: Plants growing on soil, small, reaching 1 cm in height, including the sporophyte, scattered to somewhat clumped; male plants budlike, reddish, separate, but probably originally attached to female plants by rhizoids or protonemata; female plants with very short stem and a basal cluster of leaves; uppermost and perichaetial leaves rather large, reaching 3 mm in length, with a broadly sheathing oval to oblong base ± 1 mm long and 0.4-0.65 mm wide, and with a smooth, opaque, thickened, subulate awn to 2 mm long, consisting largely of the thickened costa, the costa much thinner at leaf base; basal cells long-rectangular or polygonal, yellowish, becoming gradually shorter and smaller toward apex of the sheath and its shoulders, which are suddenly contracted to the awn. Perichaetial leaves gradually intergrading below with vegetative leaves, which are shorter and have a much less sheathing base without shoulders. Seta 4-5 mm long, smooth, stout, flexuous whether wet or dry, but neither bent nor cygneous, yellow; neck of capsule yellowish, cylindrical, provided with numerous large, roundish stomata, 0.9-1.0 mm long; spore case ± 1.0 mm long, ovoid, 0.6 mm wide at widest point; sporesac oval, dark brown; cells of exothecium long-rectangular, the walls mostly thickened, rather irregularly so, much shorter in several rows at capsule mouth; stomata lacking; annulus conspicuous, revoluble, consisting of large thick-walled cells; operculum long-rostrate, straight, 0.7-0.8 mm long; peristome single, yellow, with a smooth basal membrane 3 cells high, the teeth fragile, of varying lengths, some reaching 220 µm, papillose with scattered spicules not arranged in a pattern, not barred, variously divided, perforated and cribrose, with 1-3 divisions. Spores dark brown, spiculose-papillose, ± tetrahedral, 30-40 µm in diameter; calyptra mitrate, brown, with several lobes at base, covering most of the spore case (but not the neck), falling before the operculum.

description: Plants very large; leafy stems up to 1 cm wide, irregularly and little branched, prostrate, glossy with a golden or bronze cast, very complanate; leaves little changed when dry, conspicuously and regularly undulate, lateral leaves somewhat curved and unsymmetrical, narrowly lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, gradually acuminate in the upper half, 3-5 mm long, 0.7-1.0 mm wide at widest part; costae slender, divergent, reaching about half the leaf length; leaf margins not bordered, distantly but sharply serrate in the upper half with often spreading but rarely recurved teeth; leaf cells smooth, elongated throughout, with pointed end-walls, at leaf middle 65-90 µm long, 7-13 µm wide, becoming wider toward base and apex; alar cells frequently larger, shorter and clearer, as are also some basal marginal cells. Dioicous. Perichaetial leaves smaller and much less undulate. Seta long and slender, 2-3 cm long, densely clothed with long (25-30 µm), yellow, single-celled bristles as well as shorter hairs and irregular papillae; capsule erect and symmetric, cylindric, 2 mm long; exothecial cells convex but not mammillose; operculum long-conic, with a shorter rostrate apex, 1.8-2.0 mm long; peristome teeth 1.1 mm long, linear-lanceolate, papillose, white when dry, bordered, zigzag center line indistinct, the lamellae clearly visible, the segments of inner peristome of equal length as teeth or slightly shorter, yellow. Spores small, ca 15 ,um in diameter, punctate; calyptra large, covering the upper 1/2 or 2/3 of capsule, fringed at the base and bearing scattered, spreading and upward-pointing bristles in the upper part.

description: Plants rather stiff, green, reddish or yellowish brown, darkening with age, the secondary stems up to 5 cm long but usually much shorter, branching irregularly pinnate and bipinnate, stem and branches scarcely differing in size; leaves 1.5-2 mm long, conspicuously and regularly reflexed, squarrose, lanceolate, broadest above base, costa smooth at back, percurrent and ending in the apex or excurrent as a smooth, papillose or toothed spine which may be hyaline at apex, margins sharply serrate and dentate in upper 4/5 of leaf, entire only at extreme base, each tooth solid and appearing to be a long sharp papilla and not formed by a projecting cell apex; basal leaf cells much elongated, 50-80 µm long, smooth, extremely incrassate, with the lumina narrower than the surrounding walls, gradually becoming shorter upward; cells in upper part of leaf rectangular, 2-4:1, 18-30 µm long, wider than basal cells, convex to strongly papillose, the lumen irregular to oval, the walls much thickened; marginal row of cells longer than inner cells; all cells, and especially the upper ones, clearly arranged in rows parallel to the long axis of the leaf. Perichaetial leaves numerous, the basal ones reflexed, resembling the vegetative leaves but larger, the inner and upper ones straight and directed upward, forming a conspicuous cluster; seta 5-6 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, somewhat plicate; margins sharply toothed, upper cells strongly papillose; costa excurrent as a long awn. Seta yellow-brown, dark brown with age, 0.7-1.0 cm long, papillose throughout but more strongly so upward; capsule smooth, dark brown to almost black, oval, 1.0-1.2 mm long, 0.25-0.3 mm broad; operculum long-rostrate from a flat base, as long as capsule; peristome yellow, the teeth fused into a cylinder, 0.3 mm high, the teeth sometimes separating irregularly with age; in some capsules an inner cylinder is visible, apparently representing the fused endostome segments. Spores yellow-brown, large, 70-80 µm in diameter, very irregularly papillose; calyptra ca 3 mm long, heavily clothed with erect yellow hairs.

description: Plantae graciles aureae. Caules repentes fragiles; pseudoparaphyllia foliacea; in sectione transversali cellulis omnibus pariete tenuibus. Folia caulina majora et magis acuminata quam folia ramorum, lanceolata gradatim angustata longiacuminata (0.56) 0.63-0.87 X 0.17-0.24 mm; costa circa medium folium attingens, cellulis suis apice emergentibus; margines plani serrulati; cellulae superae laeves longirhombeae, 6-10:1, pariete firmae; cellulae alares quadratae. Folia ramorum sicca apressa, humida erectopatentia, lanceolata, 0.37-0.50 X 0.12-0.15 mm; costa fere medium folium attingens; cellulae superae rhombeae, 5-6:1; cellulae alares quadratae. Autoicae. Setae erectae luteo-vel rubro-brunneae breves, 2.8-4.0 mm longae; capsulae cylindricae, circa 1 mm longae, cellulis exothecii rectangularibus pariete tenuibus, rectis, orem versus brevioribus; annulus nullus; operculum oblique rostratum, circa 0.4 mm longum; peristomium nullum. Calyptra cucullata, nuda, laevis. Sporae sphaericae, subtiliter papillosae, 11-17 µm diam.

description: Plants slender and golden in lax, shiny mats. Stems creeping, fragile, easily broken, sparsely and irregularly branched, the youngest shoots green; pseudoparaphyllia foliose; in cross-section with 3-5 layers of thin-walled cells, the outer layer with slightly thicker walls and a central area of a few small, thinner-walled cells. Stem leaves lanceolate, gradually tapered, long-acuminate, (0.56) 0.63-0.87 X 0.17-0.24 mm; costa ending somewhat below midleaf, the costal cells usually projecting as small spines, especially on the terminal cells; margins plane, serrulate almost to base; upper cells smooth, firm-walled, long-rhomboidal, 6-10:1; alar cells not reaching the costa or reaching it and extending up it by 3-5 cells, extending up the margin in 15-18 rows. Branch leaves ± appressed and subjulaceous when dry, erect-spreading when moist, lanceolate, gradually tapered, acuminate, 0.37-0.50 X 0.12-0.15 mm; costa extending to or just short of midleaf, the terminal cell often projecting as a small spine; margins plane, serrulate almost to base; upper cells smooth, firm-walled, rhomboidal, 5-6:1; alar cells quadrate, reaching the costa and extending up it 1-3 cells, extending up the margins in 10-13 rows. Autoicous. Perigonial bracts lanceolate-ovate, short-acuminate, ecostate, subentire to serrulate, cells thin-walled, rhomboidal above, rectangular below. Perichaetial leaves triangular, ecostate, serrulate to serrate above, subentire below, upper cells long-rhomboidal, median ones broader and long-hexagonal, basal ones short-rectangular to subquadrate. Setae yellow- to red-brown, erect, slightly twisted above, ± smooth, almost imperceptibly roughened near middle, 2.8-4.0 mm long; capsules cylindric, ca 1 mm long, stomata few at extreme base of urn, exothecial cells thin-walled, long-rectangular, straight-walled, becoming shorter and subquadrate at mouth; annulus none; operculum obliquely-rostrate, ca 0.4 mm long; peristome none. Calyptra cucullate, naked, smooth. Spores spherical, finely papillose, 1 1-17 am in diameter.

description: Plants much branched, but irregularly so, not at all regularly pinnate, forming an interwoven mat; newer growth glossy, pale silvery or yellowish-green to golden-green, becoming darker with age; leafy stems to 2 mm wide; branches slightly to clearly complanate; leaves oval to ovate-lanceolate, narrowed and somewhat decurrent at base; margin 0.7-1.0 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm wide, somewhat concave but not strongly so, margins sharply serrulate to finely serrate in upper 1/3-1/2, plane or nearly so throughout; apex obtuse to acute; apex in many leaves formed by 2 fused, divergent marginal cells of equal size producing a bifurcate leaf apex; cells of lamina much elongated and very narrow, 45-55 µm long and ±3 Am wide, shorter at apex; upper end of occasional laminal cells projecting to produce small and inconspicuous papillae; marginal cells elongated and often somewhat wider than laminal cells and thus occasionally forming an indistinct border; each marginal tooth formed by the projecting upper end of one marginal cell; a group of 6-10 alar cells round or oval, not conspicuous; decurrent cells elongate; costa double, clear but very short, not reaching more than 1/4 of the leaf length. Dioicous. Perichaetial leaves slightly longer and much narrower than vegetative leaves. Seta long, slender, reaching 2 cm, smooth at base but gradually becoming more and more strongly mammillose and papillose toward apex; capsule 1.5-2 mm long, long-oval to fusiform, erect and symmetric, mammillose at very base but the remainder of the exothecium is thickly studded with single-celled, hollow, yellow spines up to 25 Am long; operculum rostrate from a mammillose conic base, straight, 0.8 mm long; peristome teeth narrowly lanceolate, from a hyaline basal membrane, pale yellow, drawn out into a long, nodose spine, inconspicuously papillose, perforate or somewhat furrowed at very base, 0.6 mm long, endostome segments linear, 0.35-0.45 mm long, papillose, perforate in upper part, cilia lacking. Spores small, 13-18 Am in diameter, variable in size, spherical; calyptra not seen.

description: Plants in loose tufts, dark green. Stems erect, (2.5) 4-5 cm high, densely leafy. Leaves straight and erect-spreading when wet, cirrhate-crisped when dry, narrowly triangular-lanceolate to linear, subfalcate, 7-8 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide midway between base and tip, long-tapering to a narrowly acute apex, stoutly bordered from base to apex with linear, thick-walled cells; margin strongly and doubly toothed from lower 1/3 of leaf to apex, often colored. Costa spinose on back above. Lamellae (4) 5 (6), low and inconspicuous, confined to the nerve, strictly parallel, 3-4 cells high. Lamina narrow, unistratose except for the border, plane, not undu- late, with a few scattered dorsal teeth, or none. Leaf cells smooth or occasionally with striate papillae near base of leaf, median cells rounded hexagonal, with their longest dimension at right angles to the nerve, 20-25 µm X 16-17 µm, usually with distinct corner thickenings. Monoicous. Bisexual shoots first forming an antheridial disc, then an archegonial bud on an innovation from the center of the disc, after a short interval of vegetative growth; unisexual female shoots more commonly seen; unisexual male shoots not as yet observed. Perigonial leaves similar to the others, but with broader bases, to broadly lanceolate and unbordered in lower 1/2; innermost bracts tiny, obovate, intermingled with the antheridia. Perichaetial leaves narrower and longer than the vegetative leaves. Seta reddish- brown, 3-4 (5) cm long, usually 1 per perichaetium, occasionally 2. Capsule red- dish-brown, finely striate, narrowly cylindric, subarcuate, erect to inclined, 6-8 (10) mm long, 0.8-1 mm in diameter. Operculum long-rostrate from a hemispherical base, beak 2.5 mm long. Peristome teeth 32. Spores finely papillose, 18-20 µm in longest diameter. Calyptra hispid at tip.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Gary L. 1977. Atrichum cylindricum (Polytrichaceae), an overlooked moss in the southeastern United States. Brittonia. 29: 368-375.

description: Dense caespitosum, caespitibus depressis, intricatis, pallide viridibus, opacis. Caulis prostratus, irregulariter ramosus, ramis cum foliis ca. 1 mm latis, valde complanate foliosis. Folia squarroso-patentia, late ovata, breviter acuminata, concava, ecostata, 0.5-0.6 mm longa, 0.3 mm lata; marginibus erectis, subintegris vel superne minutissime crenulatis; cellulis linearibus, valde seriatim papillosis, alaribus nullis. Folia perichaetialia interna ovata, longe tenuiter acuminata; seta 7-10 mm longa, rubella, tenuis, laevis, theca inclinata vel horizontalis, deopercuata 1 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: Bartram, Edwin B. 1957. Mosses of Eastern Papua, New Guinea. Brittonia. 9 (1): 32-56.

description: Gracile, dense caespitosum, caespitibus luteseenti-viridibus, nitidiusculis. Caulis vix 2 cm altus, irregulariter bipinnatim ramosus, ramulinis filiformibus, curvatis, minute foliosis. Folia erecto-patentia, triangulato-acuminata, ecostata, ca. 0.6 mm longa, 0.4 mm lata; marginibus planis, superne minutissime serru- latis; cellulis anguste linearibus, infimis laxioribus, alaribus 3-4 majusculis, rectangularibus, pellucidis. Folia ramulina minora, arete adpressa, ovato-lanceolata, 0.3-0.4 mm longa, cellulis alaribus nullis. Folia perichaetialia erecta, 2.5 mm longa, oblonga, subulato-acuminata, plicata, superne lacerata; seta ad 5 cm longa, rubella, laevis; theca oblonga, horizontalis, deoperculata 2 mm longa brevicollis; operculum conico-rostratum.

description: Autoica, gracilescens, pallide viridis; caulis pinnatimn-ramosus, ramis simplicibus, remotis; folia caulina et ramea sicea contorta, humida late patelntia, oblongo-ovata, apice rotundato-obtusa, vix 1 mm longa, ad 0.4 mm lata; marginibus planis, minutissime crenulatis; costa infra apicem folii evanida; cellulis subhexagonis, diam. 15-18 µ, pellucidis, unipapillosis; seta 1 cm longa, scabra; folia perichaetialia intima filiformiter acuminata, minutissime deiiticulata; calyptra glabra.

description: Plants relatively robust in lax, golden mats. Stems long-creeping, the branches straight, when mature usually over 1 cm long. Branch leaves somewhat imbricate with spreading apices, broadly ovate, (0.55) 0.75-0.95 mm long, (0.25) 0.50- 0.65 mm wide, fairly gradually tapered to a ± long acumen, the margins plane, minutely serrulate above; costa less than 1/4 the leaf length; upper cells long and narrow, 30-50 µm long, 2.5-4.4 µm wide, the papillae moderately prominent; alar cells 1/3-1/2 the leaf length, extending over 50 cells up the margin except in the smallest leaves. Inflorescences and sporophytes unknown.

description: Plants mostly dark reddish-gold. Stems creeping, prostrate except apically erect; branches erect, ca 2-3 mm long, subfalcate, terminating in a leafless apex bearing numerous short-stalked, brown propagulae of 4-8 uniseriately arranged cells, 45-75 jLm long, 22.5 µm wide, the branch tips becoming naked with age. Branch leaves lanceolate, acuminate, concave, 0.40-1.1 mm (mostly ca 0.85 mm) long, 0.20- 0.38 mm (mostly ca 0.25 mm) wide, the margins plane or recurved, entire to slightly serrulate at apex; costa extending about 1/4 the leaf length; upper cells linear, 8-10:1, 30-38 µm long, 3.5-4.0 µm wide, flexuose, the papillae low; differentiated alar cells quadrate to subquadrate, not reaching the costa, extending 15-25 cells up the margin. Perichaetial leaves lanceolate, 1.05-1.13 mm long, 0.15-0.20 mm wide, serrate almost to base; costa double, extending about 1/3 the leaf length; cells as in vegetative leaves. Perigonia and sporophytes unknown.

description: Plants green to dull gold in loose to tightly-woven mats. Stems creeping, the branches slightly curved. Branch leaves ± imbricate with widespreading to recurved apices, broadly lanceolate, 0.4-1.1 mm long, 0.2-0.55 mm wide, plane to slightly concave, gradually tapered to a long acumen, the margins plane, entire to slightly serrulate, especially at the base of the acumen; costa ending about 1/4 the leaf length or less; upper cells linear, 13-33 pum wide, the papillae mostly prominent; alar cells differentiated to about 1/3 the leaf length, extending 30-50 cells up the margin. Perichaetial leaves with an oblong base and then abruptly long acuminate, 1.05-1.25 mm long, 0.25-0.45 mm wide, very serrate, with teeth sometimes multicellular and wide-spreading to reflexed; costa single to double, weak to strong. Exothecial cells quadrate to rectangular, not collenchymatous. Spores 20-30 µm in diam., finely papillose.

description: Plants green to dark gold in mostly dense mats. Stems creeping, the branches commonly curled when dry (as in T. inflexum). Branch leaves imbricate, orbicular to broadly ovate, rarely even wider than long, 0.4-0.75 mm long, 0.32-0.62 mm wide, abruptly and shortly acuminate, slightly concave, the margins plane, entire to slightly serrulate above; costa ending about 1/ the leaf length; upper cells relatively short and broad, 9-19 1tm long, 4-5 ,um wide, the papillae comonly faint and low; alar cells very well developed, extending up the margin 1/23/4 the leaf length. Perichaetial leaves with an oblong base and then abruptly and long acuminate, 1.4-1.9 mm long, 0.42-0.55 mm wide; costa single; cells ± linear. Exothecial cells ± quadrate, slightly to distinctly collenchymatous. Spores 11-15 lum in diam., finely papillose.

description: Plants green to golden in mostly dense mats. Stems creeping, the branches commonly curled when dry, straight when moist, prostrate. Branch leaves imbricate, mostly ovate, 0.4-0.7 mm long, 0.23-0.52 mm wide, apex stout, ? abruptly tapered, slightly concave, the margins plane, serrulate in the upper half, especially below the apex; costa ending 1/3J/2 the length; upper cells long-rhomboidal, ca 6:1, averaging 30 /-cm long, 5 /-cm wide, the papillae very prominent; alar region ending (1/3) ?/2 the leaf length, extending up the margin by 35-60 cells. Perichaetial leaves lanceolate from an ovate base, gradually long-acuminate, 0.6-1.1 mm long, 0.11-0.30 mm wide; costa mostly absent; cells long-rhomboidal. Exothecial cells short-rectangular to short-hexagonal to isodiametric, not at all or only indistinctly collenchymatous. Spores 13-25 µm in diam., finely papillose.

description: Plants golden in loose mats. Stems creeping; branches mostly straight, short. Branch leaves erect-spreading when dry, wide-spreading when moist, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 0.75-1.4 mm (mostly ca 0.9 mm) long, 0.25-0.50 mm (mostly 0.30 mm) wide, ± abruptly tapered above, plane to somewhat concave, the margins slightly serrulate in upper half, plane to occasionally recurved on one side; costa extending (1/3) 1/2 the leaf length; upper cells linear, 40-52 µm long, 4.0-4.5 µtm wide, slightly flexuose, the papillae prominent; quadrate alar cells always reaching costa, extending 25-35 cells up the margin. Inflorescences and sporophytes unknown.

description: Gracile, caespitosum, caespitibus densis, viridibus, intus fuseeseentibus. Caulis ad 2 cm altus, simplex vel parce ramosus, laxe foliosus, haud radiculosus. description: Robustiusculum, caespitosum, caespitibus densis, fuscescentibus, opacis. Caulis 5-6 cm altus, parce ramosus, comoso-foliosus, dense fusco-radiculosus. description: Lutescenti-viride, inferne fuscescens, nitidiusculum. Caulis repens, sat dense ramosus, ramis ca. 5 mm longis, lutescentibus. Folia erecto-patentia, stricta, haud faleata, anguste oblongo-lanceolata, subulato-acuminata, ca. 1.8 mm longa, 0.4 mm lata; marginibus erectis, superne minutissime denticulatis; costa brevis- sima vel nulla; cellulis linearibus, papilla unica instructa, alaribus tribus, vesicu- losis. description: Sat robustum, caespitosum, caespitibus densis, fusceseenti-viridibus. Caulis ca. 4 cm altus, parce ramosus, fusco-tomentosus, dense foliosus. Folia sicea et humida late flexuoso-patentia, 8-9 mm longa, e basi oblonga vix 1 mm lata sensim lineari-lanceolata; marginibus planis, inferne integerrimis, superne argute ser- ratis; costa ad basin 75 µ lata, superne dorso serrata, in artistam longe excurrenti; cellulis superioribus anguste rectangularibus, inferioribus linearibus, ineras- satis, alaribus numerosis, fuscis, oblongis, ad 30 µ latis. Folia perichaetialia erecta, ca. 8 mm longa, oblonga, abrupte longe aristata; setae aggregatae, 6-8, 2 cm longae; theca anguste oblonga, arcuata, 3 mm longa,; operculum e basi conica longe subulato-rostratum; dentes peristomii aurantiaci, 0.6 mm longi, ad medium bifidi.

description: The sporophyte characters are as follows: perichaetial leaves erect, closely convolute, to 1.5 mm long, abruptly aristate; seta solitary, yellow, 3-4 cm long; capsule erect, oblong-cylindric, the urn 4 mm long; operculum slenderly conic- rostrate, 3 mm long; calyptra eucullate, brownish, extending half-way down the urn; peristome teeth 16, inserted below the rim, reddish at base, lanceolate, papillose (not striolate), about 0.5 mm long, split to about the middle into 3-4 papillose forks; spores about 15 ,u in diameter.

description: Caespitosus, caespitibus compactis, fuseeseentibus, opacis. Caulis 6-8 mm altus, dense foliosus. Folia sicea crispata, humida late patentia, 3-3.5 mm longa, e basi ovata lineari-lanceolata, canaliculata, acuminata; marginibus erectis, integerrimis; costa valida, superne angustata, cum pice desinens; cellulis rotundatis, perinerassatis, diam. ca. 8 µ, laevissimis, basilaribus linearibus, inerassatis, porosis. description: Robustus, rigidus, fuscescens, haud nitidus. Caulis erectus, 10-14 cm altus, simplex, dense foliosus. description: Dense caespitosum, caespitibus fuseeseenti-lutescentibus, nitidiuseulis; caulis dense ramosus, ramis ad 5 mm longis; folia late patentia, vel faleatula, oblongo- lanceolata, coneava, ecostata, in subulam loriformen contracta, ad 2 mm longa, 0.3 mm lata; marginibus erectis, superne serrulatis; cellulis linearibus, sat humiliter unipapillosis, alaribus tribus, fusceseentibus; folia perichaetialia longe tenuiter acuminata, superne serrulata; seta 12-14 mm longa, ubique laevissima; theca oblongo-eylindrica, suberecta, laevissima.

description: Laxe caespitosum, flavo-viride, opacum. Caulis ea. 1 cm altus, parce ramosus, fusco-tomentosus. Folia sicea ineurva, humida late patentia, 2.5-3 mm longa, profunde carinato-coneava, e basi oblonga sensim lanceolata, apice acuto, eucullato; marginibus erectis, integerrimis; costa percurrenti, dorso laevi; cellulis superioribus rotundato-sexangulis, parietibus parum inerassatis, minute papillosis, basilaribus inferioribus breviter rectangularibus, parum porosis, marginali- bus subquadratis.

description: Autoica; caespites circa 1.5 cm alti, luteseentes, intus fuseeseentes. Caulis ramosus, dense foliosus. Folia sicea crispatula, humida erecto-patentia, e basi ovata, coneava lineari-lanceolata, acuminata, 2-3 mm longa; marginibus crenulatis, fere planis; costa fusea, in apice soluta; cellulis basilaribus internis linearibus, inerassatis, marginalibus, 4-6 seriebus oblongis, pellucidis, superioribus rotundatis, inerassatis, diam. 8-10 µ. Seta 3 mm longa; theca cum collo 1.5 mm longa, siecitate plicata; calyptra dense pilosa; dentes peristomii bigeminati, papillosi; cilia 16, circa 25 µ lata; spori rotundati vel ovales, virides, diam. 110-130 µ.
bibliographicCitation: Bartram, Edwin B. 1959. Contribution to the mosses of the highlands of eastern New Guinea. Brittonia. 11: 86-98.

description: Perrobustum, densissime caespitosum. Caulis ad 9 cm altus, ramosus, dense foliosus. Folia patentia, haud faleata, 12-15 mm longa, sicea subspiraliter con- torta, e basi oblonga 3-5 mm lata abrupte ligulato-lanceolata, obtrusa, apice dorso scabro, cellulis marginalibus hyalinis (lamina vera) inferne 3-4 seriatis, linearibus. Fructus ignotus.
bibliographicCitation: Bartram, Edwin B. 1957. Mosses of Eastern Papua, New Guinea. Brittonia. 9 (1): 32-56.

description: Sat robustum, lutescenti-viride, nitidiusculum. Caulis ca. 1 cm altus, dense foliosus, inferne radiculosus. Folia sicea contorta, humida erecto-patentia, oblongo-obovata, rotundato-obtusa, breviter cuspidato-acuminata, 2.5 mm longa, 1 mm lata; marginibus planis, integris, ubique anguste limbatis; costa tenui, longe infra apicem evanida; cellulis superioribus sexangulis, ad 15-25 µ longis, basilaribus elongate rectangularibus, 100-120 µ longis. Seta 2 mm longa, laevissima; theca erecta, minute deoperculata 0.5 mm longa; calyptra superne glabra, inferne profunde laciniata.
bibliographicCitation: Bartram, Edwin B. 1957. Mosses of Eastern Papua, New Guinea. Brittonia. 9 (1): 32-56.

description: Stems 1-3 mm long, simple; leaves erect-spreading, somewhat secund, 3-4 mm long, lanceolate at the base, tapering to a long, filiform-subulate acumen, channeled above, entire except at the extreme apex which has a few obscure teeth; basal leaf cells rectangular, 2-4 :1, narrower at the margin; costa occupying nearly all of the leaf base and all of the subula, long-excurrent with only a few stereids ventrally above a single row of guide cells; perichaetial leaves with an oblong sheathing base. Autoicous: antheridia in numerous axillary buds; seta reddish-yellow, up to 1.5 cm long; capsule ovoid, largest in the middle, the urn up to 1 mm long, nearly symmetric, often inclined, sometimes slightly strumose, tapering conspicuously from middle to base; calyptra eucullate, slenderly rostrate; annulus of a single row (rarely two rows) of large cells, partially persistent; operculum conic, obtuse; peristome teeth 0.3 mm long or shorter, scarcely twisted, divided irregularly to the base into 32 filiform segments from a low, papillose basal membrane, spinose-papillose, irregularly perforate; spores 20-26 µ, coarsely and irregularly papillose, maturing March to May.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, Lewis E. & Bryan, Virginia S. 1958. Systematics of the autoicous species of Ditrichum subg. Ditrichum. Brittonia. 10: 121-137.

description: Stems 4-7 mm long, simple; leaves erect anid somewhat crisped or contorted when dry, not secund, 4-5 mm long, linear-subulate, rather abruptly widened below into a short, oblong-ovate base, channeled above with margins erect, slightly denticulate at the extreme apex, smooth at the back; cells of the leaf base laxly oblong-hexagonal, wide near the costa and becoming shorter and subquadrate near the margins, just above the shoulders becoming shorter, thickerwalled, and quadrate, the upper cells quadrate or shortly rectangular, 7-14 X 7-8 µ,; costa broad and flat, percurrent, filling most of the subula; perichaetial leaves subelasping. Autoicous: perigonia numerous; seta orange-yellow to reddish, slender and flexuous, 25-35 mm long; urn of the capsule 2.5-3 mm long, suberect to inclined, slightly asymmetric, ovoid-cylindric, tapered to a small mouth, pale brown, indistinctly suleate when dry and empty; calyptra eueullate, smooth, 4 mm long; annulus large and usually persistent in fragments; opereulum high-conic, blunt, 1.5 mm long; peristome teeth 16, split to a short membrane into 32 filiform, spiculose divisions, pale red, 1-1.3 mm long. Spores nearly smooth, faintly reticulate at higher magnifications, 11-13 , deep yellow in mass.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, Lewis E. & Bryan, Virginia S. 1958. Systematics of the autoicous species of Ditrichum subg. Ditrichum. Brittonia. 10: 121-137.

description: Stems 5-15 mm long, occasionally up to 20 mm, branched; leaves erect, contorted when dry, 2-3 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, channeled, their margins ineurved, indistinctly serrulate, toothed at the apex; leaf base scarcely differentiated, not clasping, gradually narrowed to the short awn; cells of the leaf base rectangular, quadrate or oblong above; laminal cells irregular to subquadrate, inerassate, about 10 µ wide; perichaetial leaves with sheathing with long, linear cells up to 140 µ in length, colored. Autoicous: antheridia terminal on short basal branches; seta yellow, up to 2.5 cm long; capsule 2-3 mm long, erect, ovoid-cylindric, tapering from a broad base to a narrow mouth, somewhat contorted when dry, not furrowed; exothecial cells narrowly linearoblong and pale, the mouth bordered by dark cells; calyptra about 1 mm; annulus of two rows of cells; operculum conic-rostrate; peristome teeth short, bifid to the base, articulate, spinose-papillose; spores smooth, 8-10 a, maturing in spring.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, Lewis E. & Bryan, Virginia S. 1958. Systematics of the autoicous species of Ditrichum subg. Ditrichum. Brittonia. 10: 121-137.

description: Stems 1-3 cm high, densely tomentose below; leaves erect, not secund, twisted when dry, 3-5 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, from a short clasping base; margins entire or faintly serrulate, narrowly ineurved; basal cells narrowly linear, the upper cells linear, walls thickened; costa indistinct below, excurrent, not filling the awn, with a single row of guide cells forming the upper face of the costa and a broad band of stereids below. Autoicous: antheridia in distinct buds, surrounded by 3-5 short, membranaceous perigonial leaves. Seta up to 2.5 cm high, pale, becoming reddish with age; capsules erect or somewhat inclined, 2-3 mm long, slightly curved, tapering to the mouth anld slightly furrowed when dry; annulus broad; peristome teeth erect, pale red, divided to the base irregularly into 2 filiform, densely papillose, niodose forks; basal membrane short; spores smnooth or nearly so, 10-15 µ in diameter, pale, maturing from April to June.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, Lewis E. & Bryan, Virginia S. 1958. Systematics of the autoicous species of Ditrichum subg. Ditrichum. Brittonia. 10: 121-137.

description: Stems short, simple, less than 1 cm, usually 3-5 mm high; leaves crowded, twisted and somewhat recurved when dry, 3-7 mm long, secund, long-filiformsubulate from a short, ovate to lanceolate base, entire except at the apex; basal cells oblong, thin-walled, becoming narrower and linear at the margin, the upper cells short-rectangular; costa broad, nearly filling the awn, with a broad band of stereid cells below and one row of duct cells forming the upper (inner) face; perichaetial leaves sheathing. Autoicous: antheridia in small buds below the perichaetium; seta pale yellow, 1-2 em long; capsules erect to inclined, 1.5-3 mm long, slightly furrowed when dry, the urn narrowly ovoid-cylindric; calyptra large, cucullate and twisted; annulus narrow, dehiseent; operculum short-rostrate; peristome short, rarely exceeding 0.3 mm, scarcely twisted, from a narrow basal membrane; teeth irregularly perforate or divided below, papillose, nodose at the base; spores roughened, brownish, 20-29 µ, maturing in June.

description: Sat robusta, inter alios muscos sparse cresens, ferruginea, opaca. Caules seeundarii flexuosi, dense foliosi, irregulariter ramosi, ad 2 cm longi. description: Pergracile, caespitosum, caespitibus densis, intricatis, laete viridibus, intus pallide fuscescentibus, nitidiusculis. Caulis sat dense subpinnatim ramosus, ramis brevibus, obtusis. Folia perichaetialia intima ad 1.5 mm longa, e basi convoluta, erecta, sensim longe subulato-acuminata, superne minute denticulata; seta 1 cm longa, theca inclinata, deoperculata 1.5 mm longa; calyptra glabra.

description: Caespitosum, eaespitibus densis, fuseis. Caulis 1-1.5 cm altus, dense fusco-radiculosus, interrupte foliatus. Folia sieca arete contorta, rosulata, late obovata, 3-4 mm longa, 2-2.5 mm lata, obtusa, breviter apiculata; marginibus inferne anguste revolutis, superne prope apicem serrulatis; costa validissima, superne multo angustiore, in apiculum brevissimum excurrens; cellulis superioribus elongate rhomboideis, ea. 35 µ longis, 15 µ latis, parietibus tenniusculis, marginalibus 3-4 serialibus linearibus, basilaribus breviter rectangularibus. Caetera ignota.

description: Plants small to +/- medium sized, forming mats, corticolous, ramicolous or lignicolous. Secondary stems commonly spreading, prostrate to occasionally perpendicular to substrate, occasionally ascending, to 2.5 cm or more long. Secondary stem leaves complanate, crowded, occasionally crispate when dry, smooth to undulate, apex often pinched, lateral leaves symmetrical to slightly asymmetrical, erect-spreading to spreading, ovate-oblong to oblong-lingulate, (1.4)1.8-2.5(3) mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm wide, obtuse (rarely truncate), apiculate or shortly and sometimes sharply acute to short acuminate; margins plane, elimbate, mostly serrate in distal 1/3-1/2(2/3), serration blunt or sharp and composed of two adjoining cells; costae weak to +/- strong, 1/3-l/2 lamina length; median cells linear to long-fusiform, 80-155 µm long, 12-14 µm wide, apical cells rhomboidal, marginal cells narrower but not notably differentiated; median leaves ovate to ovate-oblong or lingulate, 1.9-2.2 mm long, 0.8-1.0 mm wide, acute, costae weak, 1/4 - 1/3 lamina length. Dioicous. Setae 6-12 mm long, often rather slender, papillose throughout, papillae both low projecting and spinose; urn 1.0-1.4 mm long; opercula conicrostrate, ca 1.2-1.4 mm long. Spores ca 20 µm in diameter, lightly papillose lyptrae mitrate-campanulate, 1.8-3.0 mm long, plicate, sparsely hairy, often deeply laciniate at base.

description: Plants yellowish to bright green. Stems often with propagula forming a cylindrical cluster on the upper 1/4-1/3, propagula moderately to densely papillose; rhizoids densely papillose throughout. Leaves (2) 3 (3.5) mm long, linear-lanceolate, long-acuminate, widest just above base; margins recurved in lower 2/3, sharply serrate in upper 1/3 or less; costa excurrent, serrate at back to about same level as marginal serrations, laminal tissue extending out along costal excurrency; cells ± isodiametric, or irregularly rounded hexagonal, 10-14 .um long, cells of upper stem leaves (i.e., those among propagula) short rectangular, 3-7:1. description:
Plantae robustae ramosae rufo-brunneae, partibus junioribus lutescentes vel aureo-virides, nitidae. Folia subcrispata, exsiccata passim patentia nec spiralia, madida subregulariter erectopatula, lineari-lanceolata 3-4 mm longa, sensim in apicem acuminatum vel acute acuminatum angustata, basi carinata ac subplicata, margine plana subintegerrima. Costa valida, per- vel breviter excurrens. Cellulae undique laeves lineares, muris per totam folii longitudinem incrassatis porosisque. Folia perichaetialia vix vel haud a vegetativis diversa.

Seta 1.1-1.8 cm longa laevis rufa; capsula oblongo-cylindrica 1.2-1.8 mm longa laevis, operculo rostrato, annulo distincto; persistoma solitarium, dentibus abbreviatis truncatis papillosis. Calyptra plicata, basi fimbriata, nuda.
bibliographicCitation: Steere, William C. & Buck, William R. 1979. Macromitrium crumianum (Musci: Orthotrichaceae), a new species from Guatemala. Brittonia. 31: 395-398.

description:
Plants rather robust, densely foliate, branching freely, older parts reddish brown, the younger growth yellowish to golden green, glossy. Secondary stems long but variable in length, branches also varying from short (0.5 mm) to long (2 cm). Leaves somewhat crispate, irregularly spreading, neither appressed nor spirally arranged when dry, rather evenly erect-spreading when moist, linear-lanceolate, 3-4 mm long, gradually and evenly tapering to the acutely acuminate or acuminate apex, slightly narrowed to the insertlon, keeled and somewhat plicate, especially at base; margins plane, serrulate to subentire, somewhat erose-denticulate near apex. Costa strong, percurrent or short excurrent in terminal leaves. Cells linear and smooth throughout, not at all tuberculate at base, with conspicuously incrassate and porose cells from base of leaf to apex, but wails considerably thicker at base; basal cells 35-70 µm long, 2.0-2.5 µm wide, their walls twice as thick as lumina or thicker, the lumina appearing somewhat sinuous because of pores, the cells slightly but not significantly shorter near the margin and costa; cells at middle of leaf linear but shorter than the basal ones, 40-50 µm long, 2.5-3.0 µm wide; cells near the apex 35-45 µm long, 2.5-5.0 µm wide, their walls less than the width of the lumen but by no means thin. Outer perichaetial leaves not perceptibly differentiated from regular vegetative leaves, but becoming shorter and narrower inward. Phyllodioicous. Male plants dwarf, averaging 1.0 mm tall, with a short stem and about 10 perigonial leaves, which are smaller toward the center, anchored to the leaves of the female plant by long and conspicuous brown rhizoids.

Seta 1.1-1.8 cm long, smooth throughout, twisted when dry, reddish; capsule oblong-cylindric, 1.2-1.8 mm long, smooth to slightly wrinkled when dry, somewhat contracted at mouth, the exothecial cells thick-walled, rectangular, becoming quadrate and then wider than long toward mouth, the stomata few, superficial, confined to the extreme base of the urn; operculum rostrate from a low-conic base, straight to slightly oblique; annulus differentiated, in 1 or 2 rows of firm-walled (but thinner-walled than in exothecial cells), ± quadrate cells, deciduous; peristome apparently single, attached slightly below mouth of urn, the teeth short, 50-150 µm tall, truncate, densely papillose on front surface, smooth at back. Spores spherical, 15-25 µm in diam., moderately papillose. Calyptra covering entire capsule, ca 2.5 mm long, plicate, fringed at bottom third or half, naked, but papillose at apex from projecting, thickened cell ends.

description: Plants reddish-golden in loose mats. Stems creeping; branches prostrate, short. Branch leaves lanceolate-ovate, 0.75-1.25 mm (mostly ca 1.0 mm) long, 0.35- 0.55 mm (mostly ca 0.45 mm) wide, concave, gradually acuminate, the apex frequently fragile, the margins entire to slightly serrulate, plane; costa ending 1/4-1/3 the leaf length; cells linear, 30-40 µm long, 5 1um wide, straight to slightly flexuose, the papillae low and inconspicuous; quadrate alar cells occasionally reaching the costa, 25-35 cells extending up the margin. Inflorescence and sporophyte unknown.

description: Plants medium-sized, in wide, loose to moderately dense mats or cushions, dull or weakly glossy, olive-brown throughout or dark brown below and olive-green to light olivaceous above. Stems prostrate or ascending, to 6 cm long but usually 3-4 cm, sparsely irregularly to subpinnately branched or almost unbranched, rather slender but stiff, dark brown, densely foliate throughout, with the lower leaves usually strongly eroded; in transverse section rounded, composed of 2-3 layers of smaller cortical cells with strongly incrassate, dark orange-brown walls surrounding 7-8 rows of large medullary cells with very thickened, intensely yellow walls, central strand absent. Rhizoids frequent in the lower part of the stem, scattered in clusters along the stem and not forming a tomentum, reddish-brown, smooth, long and sparsely branched. Axillary hairs numerous and frequent in the upper part of the stem, filiform, hyaline throughout, 9-17-celled, composed of short, barrel-shaped lower cells and elongate upper cells. Stem and branch leaves similar in shape, the latter only somewhat narrower, erect, straight or falcate, crowded, appressed to the stem and often with more or less reflexed apices when dry, erect-spreading when moist, indistinctly bluntly plicate below or not, concave, not sharply carinate, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 2- 3 x 0.5-0.7 mm, with distinct, short- to long-decurrent auricles, gradually tapering to a canaliculate acumen, lower leaves blunt and muticous, often slightly cucullate at the apex, the uppermost leaves hair-pointed; hair-points short, to 0.2 mm long, hyaline or yellowish, plane, canaliculate, remotely bluntly serrulate, gradually merging into chlorophyllose apical leaf cells; margins entire or on piliferous leaves often slightly sinuate to bluntly serrulate at the apex, unistratose throughout, plane or broadly recurved to mid-leaf on one side; costa sin- gle, concolorous with the laminal cells but otherwise clearly separated from them, light yellow, 80-100 pm wide at base, gradually tapering upward, 40-50 pm wide above, ceasing well below the apex and imperceptibly merging with apical cells, prominent and strongly flattened dorsally and usually in a deep furrow below, rounded and less convex on the dorsal side above, ventrally canaliculate throughout, in cross section bistratose above with 2-3 ventral and 4-6 dorsal cells, bistratose with occasional tristratose areas and 3-4 ventral and 8-15 dorsal cells in the median part, bistratose below, with 4-6 large ventral cells and 13-18 small dorsal cells below; laminal cells unistratose and rectangular throughout, (15-)20-40(-50) X 4-5 pm, smooth, with very incrassate and nodulose longitudinal walls and thinner, oblique or truncate trans- verse walls; basal cells intensely yellow or yellow-orange, short rectangular to subisodiametric, 15-25(-30) X 10-12 pm, with strongly thickened, porose walls, forming a narrow strip of 1-2 rows along the insertion; alar cells larger, with thick, porose or nonporose walls, yellow, pale yellowish or orange-yellow, forming plane or inflated, decurrent auricles or occasionally similar to the adjacent basal cells; supra-alar margin- al cells undifferentiated from the laminal cells or 2-3(-5) cells slightly differentiated, pellucid, hyaline or yellowish, with moderately thickened, sinuose or esinuose walls. Dioicous. Perigonia bud-like, ca. 2 mm long; outer bracts similar to vegetative leaves but smaller; inner bracts broadly ovate, epilose, obtuse at the apex, concave, orange-brown, ecostate or with a weak costa; antheridia few, 4-6 per perigonium, pale brownish, claviform, short-stalked; pa- raphyses none. Perichaetia and sporophytes unknown.

description: Plants small, golden-green, prostrate in small, loose mats; branches subcomplanate; pseudoparaphyllia foliose. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves oblong-lanceolate, 1.55-1.75 mm long, con- cave, ecostate, margins minutely serrulate above, entire below, cells linear above, rectangular below. Seta red-brown, 1.5-2 cm long, ± straight; capsule suberect, sometimes indistinctly so, ca 2 mm long; exothecial cells ± thick-walled, rectangular, becoming shorter, quadrate and thinner-walled at mouth, stomata few at extreme base of urn; annulus none; peristome double, inserted slightly below the mouth; exostome teeth lanceolate, strongly bordered, on front surface papillose above, papillose-cross-striolate below, on back surface finely papillose, perforate, non-projecting; endostome of a fairly high, papillose basal membrane, segments narrow, papillose, keeled, perforate, as long as the teeth, cilia rudimentary. description: Stems creeping, to ca 4 cm long, often somewhat ascending. description: Plants delicate, creeping, golden; branches erect, curved, terete; leaves imbricate, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, acute to short-acuminate, plane to slightly concave, broadly attached, 0.52-0.81 mm long, 0.21-0.33 mm wide; margins ± crenulate throughout, plane; costa single, extending about 2/3 the leaf length; cells isodiametric to shortly oval, all edges rounded, thick-walled throughout with conspicuous middle lamellae and intercellular spaces, not noticeably differen- tiated in alar region, smooth. description: Plants moderately sized, to ca 3 cm long, in dense yellow-green, occasionally red-tinted tufts. description: Plants small and slender, pale-green or yellowish to brownish-yellow. Stem cortex 1-layered, with few to numerous cells uniporose at their upper ends. Stem leaves 1.2-1.8 mm long, elliptic to oblong, rounded at the apex, somewhat concave; hyaline cells fibrillose throughout, undivided, on the outer surface with many commissural pores in +/- continuous rows, on the inner surface with pores none or occasionally single and small at side corners. Branches in fascicles of 2, both spreading, or 3, with 1 pendent; retort cells with inconspicuous necks. Branch leaves erect (not secund), 1-1.4 mm long, broadly ovate to elliptic, rounded- obtuse and concave, narrowly bordered; hyaline cells +/- bulging on both surfaces, on the outer surface with many rounded to elliptic pores in +/- continuous commissural rows, with occasional connecting fibrils, on the inner surface with pores none or occasionally single and small at side corners; green cells narrowly rectangular to +/- trapezoidal, exposed on both surfaces by thickened end walls, some- times slightly more so on the inner surface.

description: Plants corticolous, slender, golden, freely but irregularly branched, appressed to substrate, with terete branches and stems; pseudoparaphyllia foliose. Leaves imbricate when dry with apices often erect- to wide-spreading giving the plants a shaggy appearance; leaf base ovate and concave, apex long-acuminate, 0.50- 1.0 mm long, 0.15-0.38 mm wide; costa mostly single and extending 1/2 to 2/3 the length of the leaf base, occasionally double and about 1/2 the length of the base, rarely single with two auxiliary costae; margins entire to sparsely serrulate-crenulate, recurved below, plane above; apical cells rectangular to rounded long-hexagonal, smooth; cells adjacent to and above costa long-hexagonal to linear, 4-15: 1, flexuose, papillose, with the papillae located over cell walls at apical ends, but not from projecting cell ends; alar cells differentiated from basal corners to shoulders, round to oval, smooth, occasionally papillose adjacent to longer inner cells, yellow across insertion. Inflorescences and sporophytes unknown.

description: Plantae robustae, parce ramosae, aureo-fuscae. Folia sicca laxe erecto-imbricata, madida erectopatula, anguste ovata vel ligulato-lanceolata 2-2.5 mm longa, in apicem acuminata, cuspidata, incurvata vel recurvata, margine recurvato e basi usque ad acumen. Costa ad medium folium vel paullum supra producta. Cellulae marginales valde distinctae, elongatae, pluri-seriales e basi ad acumen; juxtacostatae marginalibus similes, e basi ad acumen productae; superae angustae rhomboideae, sinuolatae, incrassatae; basales rectangulares, hyalinae. Seta 1.2-1.5 cm longa basi laevis, supra scabra; theca ovoidea 1.5-1.6 mm longa; dentibus lanceolatis, papillosis; sporae subreniformes 15-18 µm, dilute papillosae.

description: Plants rather robust, to 5 cm tall, sparcely branched, golden-brown. Leaves laxly erect-imbricate when dry, erect-spreading when moist, narrowly ovate to ligulate-lanceolate, 2-2.5 mm long x 0.5-0.6 mm wide, tip incurved or recurved, margins revolute from base to slightly below apex, border sharply defined from base to acumen, 8-10 cells wide at base, 10-14 cells wide at mid-leaf, narrowing to 2-3 cells wide in acumen. Costa extending to mid-leaf or slightly above. Cells of border quite elongate, linear, 60-80 ,um long, 6-7 ,um wide with deeply pigmented walls especially at base of leaf; juxtacostal cells similar in size and shape to those of border, forming a conspicuous and broad band along both sides of costa from base to acumen, this band widening above costa and merging with cells of upper lamina; laminal cells of acumen narrowly rhomboidal, somewhat sinuous, 18-35 µm long, 7-10 µm wide; basal laminal cells hyaline, rectangular, 15-30 ,um long, 7-9 ,um wide. Perichaetial leaves ovate, ecostate. Dioicous? Seta 1.2-1.5 cm long, smooth below, scabrous above. Capsule ovoid, 1.5-1.6 mm long, 0.8 mm in diameter, exothecial cells moderately collenchymatous; intact peristome not seen, but from some fragments the following-teeth lanceolate-acuminate, orange below, light yellow to nearly hyaline above, papillose. Calyptra and operculum not seen. Spores subreniform, 15-18 ,um, faintly papillose.

description: Plants medium-sized, forming golden-brown, lax, shiny mats. Stems creeping, branches ca 0.5 mm long, erect, straight to slightly curved, turgid, obtuse. Leaves erect to erect-spreading, spreading when moist, oblong-ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5-2.0 mm long, 0.77-0.88 mm wide, gradually acute, strongly concave; margins plane or usually recurved in lower half, sometimes further up, plane at apex, entire; costa short and double or absent; apical cells rhomboidal to short-hexagonal, 2-3:1, cells at midleaf long-rhomboidal to linear-flexuose, 7-15: 1, becom- ing thicker-walled and somewhat porose below midleaf; alar cells colored across the insertion in 1-2 rows, oblong, firm-walled, to 70 Am long, the cells above mostly quadrate. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves erect, lanceolate to narrowly tri- angular, 1.3-1.8 mm long, gradually acuminate; margins recurved almost through- out, entire; ecostate; cells hexagonal at extreme apex, linear-flexuose at midleaf, colored and long-rectangular at insertion. Setae 7-8 mm long, orange, smooth; capsules erect to suberect, short-cylindric, ca 1.3 mm long, only slightly constricted below mouth when dry; exothecial cells strongly collenchymatous; annulus none; operculum obliquely long-rostrate, about as long as the urn; peristome double, exostome teeth on front surface cross-striolate below, coarsely papillose above, projecting at back; endostome with a high basal membrane, papillose, segments keeled, narrowly perforate, cilia single, about as long as the segments. Spores spherical, 22-27 ,um in diameter, finely and faintly papillose. Calyptrae not seen.
