description: Plants medium-sized, forming golden-green, lax, + shiny mats. Stems creeping, branches ca 1 cm long, erect, straight, turgid, cuspidate. Leaves erect-spreading, scarcely altered when moist, oblong-ovate to obovate, 1.3-2.0 mm long, 0.5-0.66 (0.95) mm wide, gradually or ? abruptly acute to gradually acuminate, concave; margins sometimes recurved above, plane below, serrulate in upper l/3-l/2, entire below; costa short and double, sometimes extending 1/5-1/4 the leaf length; apical cells rhomboidal, 2-3:1, cells at midleaf long-rhomboidal, 6-10:1; alar cells col- ored across the insertion, mostly in 1 row, occasionally in 2 rows in extreme basal angles, oblong, firm-walled, porose toward costa, to 90 Am long, the cells above mostly rectangular. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves erect, lanceolate to narrowly triangular, 1.5-1.9 mm long, gradually acuminate; margins plane, subserrulate at apex; ecostate; cells short-rectangular at extreme apex, linear-flexuose at midleaf, colored and long-rectangular at insertion. Setae 7-9 mm long, orange, smooth; capsules erect to suberect, short-cylindric, 1.0-1.4 mm long, only slightly con- stricted below the mouth when dry; exothecial cells only slightly to strongly col- lenchymatous; annulus none; operculum obliquely long-rostrate, almost as long as the urn; peristome double, exostome teeth on front surface cross-striolate below, coarsely papillose above, projecting at back; endostome with a high basal mem- brane, smooth, segments keeled, not or only very narrowly perforate, cilia none or rudimentary. Spores spherical to oval, 14-22 Am in diameter, finely papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, naked.

description: Plants medium-sized, forming golden-brown, dense, ± shiny mats. Stems creeping, branches to 1 cm long, erect, straight to slightly curved, turgid to subcom- planate, cuspidate. Leaves spreading to wide-spreading, scarcely altered when moist, oblong to ovate, 1.4-1.8 mm long, 0.55-0.88 mm wide, gradually acute to obtuse, strongly concave, sometimes subplicate; margins plane, entire, indis- tinctly bordered above because marginal cells slightly wider than other laminal cells; costa short and double, or often absent; extreme apical cells rhomboidal, 2-4:1, cells at midleaf linear, 10-30:1; alar cells in well defined, abruptly differ- entiated areas, enlarged, inflated, hyaline, in 2-3 rows, rounded-oblong, to 110 ,um long, the cells above mostly short-rectangular. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves erect, lanceolate-ovate, 1.4-2.0 mm long, gradually short-acuminate, apex some- times obtuse; margins plane, entire; ecostate; cells rhomboidal at extreme apex, linear to midleaf, short-rectangular at insertion. Setae 14-17 mm long, orange, smooth; capsules erect, short-cylindric to pyriform, 1.2-1.4 mm long, not at all constricted below mouth when dry, mouth often flaring on older capsules; exothecial cells collenchymatous; annulus none; operculum long-rostrate, ± straight, shorter than the urn; peristome double, exostome teeth on front surface cross- striolate below, coarsely papillose above, projecting at back; endostome with a high basal membrane, finely papillose, segments keeled, not perforate, cilia single or rudimentary. Spores spherical, 22-25 µm in diameter, finely papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, naked.

description: Slender plants to ca 3 cm tall in sparse, golden tufts. Stems yellow-green to reddish-brown, creeping, sparingly and irregularly branched, in cross-section with 4-5 layers of cells with very small lumina and incrassate, colored walls surrounding thick-walled cells with larger lumina, central strand absent; pseudoparaphyllia narrowly foliose. Leaves imbricate when dry, erect-spreading and conspicuously spirally arranged when moist, oblong-ovate, 0.5-1.1 x 0.25-0.5 mm, broadly acute to obtuse; margins recurved below, serrate at apex, entire below; costa single, strong, occasionally forked, extending 1/2-2/3 leaf length, 30-70 µm wide at base; median cells isodiametric to shortly oblong, smooth, strongly and irregularly thick-walled, 11-22 x 10-12 µm, often porose; alar cells transversely elongate to quadrate, extending well up leaf margins and grading into upper laminal cells. Dioicous and synoicous; inflorescences conspicuous along dried stems. Inner perichaetial leaves longer and narrower than stem leaves, to 1.5 mm long, costate, outer leaves ecostate, blunt; gametangia 8-15 per inflorescence, paraphyses present, few to dense and slightly exceeding gametangia. Sporophytes absent.
bibliographicCitation: Stark, Lloyd R. & Buck, William R. 1986. Corrections to Forsstroemia including Bryonorrisia, gen. nov. (Anomodontaceae). Brittonia. 38: 48-54.

description: Robusta, dense caespitosa, caespitibus fuscescentibus, opacis. Caulis secundarius erectus, rigidus, breviter stipatus, usque ad 10 cm altus; folia stipitis erecta lamina fere destructa, superne dense subpinnatim ramosus, ramis patulis, dense foliosis, parcissime ramulosis, obtusis, ad 2 cm longis; folia caulina imbricata, sicea leniter curvata, 4-5 mm longa, e basi ovata, breviter pluri- plicata, oblongo-lanceolata, acuta, dense transverse undulata; marginibus planis, inferne integris, superne undulatis, irregulariter serratis; costa valida, ferruginea, infra apicem soluta; cellulis laminalibus minutis, rotundatis, incrassatis, laevissimis, diam. 7-8 I, basilaribus interioribus anguste linearibus, porosis, marginibus versus minutis, rotundatis, inerassatis, numerosis. Folia ramea minora, 3-4 mm longa. Fructus ignotus.

description: Plants rather small, in pale-brownish tufts. Cortical cells of stems in 2 (-3) layers, elongate, uniporose at the upper ends, lacking fibrils; wood cylinder reddish-brown. Stem leaves similar to branch leaves in most respects, usually about 2.3 mm long, oblong to elliptic, cucullate-concave, bordered by a resorption furrow, very slightly erose and slightly roughened by resorption at the extreme apex; hyaline cells fibrillose and porose throughout, occasionally 1-divided, on the outer surface with 9-14 small, ringed, elliptic commissural pores as well as triple pores at adjacent corners and a few tiny, round pores or pseudopores on cell middles near the leaf apex. Branches in fascicles of 3 (2 spreading); branch cortex of elongated cells, some of them porose at the upper ends, lacking fibrils. Branch leaves imbricate, ovate to oblong-ovate, varying considerably in size (1.1-)1.4-2.5(-3) mm long, cucullate-concave, bordered by a resorption furrow, very slightly erose and roughened at the extreme tip; hyaline cells on the outer surface with 8-16 small, elliptic, ringed commissural pores, as well as triple pores at adjacent corners, and often toward the apex with 1-4 minute, rounded pores or pseudopores in a +/- median position, on the inner surface with few to numerous rounded to elliptic, unringed pores and pseudopores at corners and along the commissures and often cross-connecting fibrils as well, sometimes also with 1-3 tiny, rounded median pores; green cells isosceles-triangular to +/- trapezoidal in section, with curved sides and a broader exposure on the inner surface, the hyaline cells somewhat convex on the inner surface and bulging-convex on the outer.

description: Caules secundarii 25-28 cm alti, superne parce ramosi. Folia conferta, squarroso-patentia, ca. 15 mm longa, e basi vaginanti breviter oblonga sensim-lineari-lanceolata, subulato-acuminata, ubique late limbata; marginibus spinoso- serratis; costa longe excurrenti; cellulis, superioribus irregulariter oblongis, 7-8 µ latis, 10-25 µ longis, parietibus firmis, inferne sensim longioribus, basilaribus linearibus. Folia perichaetialia interna magna, erecta, vaginantia, oblongo-lanceolata, raptim subulato-acuminata, 10-14 mm longa, 2 mm lata, inferne leniter plicata, superne parce denticulata vel integra, elimbata; costa tenui, excurrenti; cellulis anguste linearibus; seta perbrevis, vix 0.5 mm longa; theca immersa, curvata, deoperculata 4 mm longa; operculum conico-rostratum.

description: Gracilis, lutescenti-viridis. Caules secundarii 2-4 cm alti, inferne simplices, squamis arete adpressis, superne densissime ramosi, ramulis erecto-patentibus, dense ramulosis. Folia patentia, oblongo-ovata, coneava, raptim subulato-acuminata, 1-1.6 mm longa; marginibus erectis, integris, prope apicem minutissime denticulatis; costa longe infra apicem folii evanida; cellulis anguste linearibus, laevissimis, infimis brevioribus, fuscis, alaribus nullis. Folia perichaetialia interna erecta, longe oblongo-lanceolata, sensim longissime subulata, ca. 5 mm longa, integra; costa tenuis, in acumen evanida; seta 2 mm longa; theca vix exserta, oblonga, deoperculata 2 mm longa; operculum conico- rostratum, 1 mm longum; dentes peristomii anguste lanceolati, subulato-acuminati, 0.5 mm alti, laevissimi; endostomium imperfectum. description: Plants pale- to golden-green, in fairly stiff, thin mats, mostly tightly adherent to substrate. Stems thick, creeping, to ca 4 cm long, freely but irregularly branched; outer pseudoparaphyllia narrowly foliose, the inner ones filamentous; in crosssection with 2-3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, the outer row often somewhat larger than the 1-2 rows beneath it and occasionally stripping off with dissection, internally with large, thin-walled cells, central strand well developed, of small, thin-walled, nodulose cells. Stem leaves broadly inserted, laxly spaced, imbricate, ovate-triangular, 0.95-1.1 mm long, acute to apiculate; margins plane, serrulate throughout, more strongly so above; costa double, the two forks separated to base, extending to 1/3 the leaf length; upper cells long-hexagonal, ± flexuose, thin-walled, becoming shorter, ± rectangular and thicker-walled at the base; alar cells scarcely differentiated in 2 rows, 2-4 cells extending up the margin, quadrate to shortrectangular, the extreme basal cells enlarged. Branch leaves ± falcate-secund when dry, sometimes contorted, erect-spreading when moist, not at all falcate but sometimes obscurely homomallous, ovate-lanceolate, 0.7-0.95 mm long, sometimes ± asymmetric, concave, gradually acute to short-acuminate; margins plane or irregularly erect to recurved, serrulate throughout, more strongly so above; costa 1/5-1/2 the leaf length, one fork often longer than the other; upper median cells longhexagonal, subflexuose, thin-walled, the apical ones sometimes shorter, at insertion becoming shorter, ± rectangular and thicker-walled (but not porose); alar cells few, 3-5, in 1-2 rows at margin. Inflorescences and sporophytes unknown.

description: Plantae aureo-virides nitentes. Caules repentes radicantes, pseudoparaphylliis foliosis, cortice transverse secto e cellulis parvis incrassatis composito, filo centrali nullo. Folia complanatim disposita lineari-oblonga 0.95-1.85 x 0.18-0.27 mm acuta vel subobtusa, margine apicem versus serrato vel serrulato basem versus dissitiserrulato vel subintegro, cellulis linearibus flexuosis laevibus in laminae apice brevioribus, cellulis alaribus paucis quadratis vel brevirectangularibus. Dioicae? Caetera ignota.

description: Plants golden-green, shiny, in extensive, loose mats. Stems creeping, slender, heavily radiculose, irregularly branched, the branches prostrate, complanate-foliate, mostly short; pseudoparaphyllia foliose; in cross-section with 2-4 rows of small, thick-walled cells surrounding larger, thinner-walled cells, central strand none. Branch and stem leaves similar, those of the stem usually somewhat smaller; branch leaves erect-spreading, complanately disposed, linear-oblong, 0.95-1.85 mm long, 0.18-0.27 mm wide, ± abruptly acute to subobtuse, plane above, somewhat concave at base; margins plane above, sometimes erect below, serrate to serrulate above, distantly serrulate to subentire below; costae short and double, sometimes unequal, rarely to 1/4 the leaf length, mostly shorter; upper cells linearflexuose, smooth, firm-walled, the apical ones shorter and often irregularly shaped, becoming shorter in a few rows across the insertion; alar cells quadrate to shortrectangular in extreme angles, extending up the margins in 1-2 (3) rows. Dioicous? Sporophytes unknown.

description: Plants small, up to 14 mm long, yellow-green, simple or branched, erect to decumbent. Stems with smooth, basal rhizoids and indistinct hyaline axillary nodules, central strands lacking, outer 4 or 5 rows of cells smaller and thickerwalled. Leaves crowded, slightly crisped when dry, up to 30 pairs, broadly lingulate, 1.4-1.8 mm long and 0.5-9.7 mm wide, obtuse, sometimes emarginate or with blunt apiculi; margins entire to crenulate, indistinctly limbate on the lower halves of the perichaetial leaves, limbidia composed of 1 or 2 rows of slightly elongate unistratose cells; costae strong, ending 2-4 cells below leaf apices, with prominent guide cells, two in distal parts and three in proximal parts; dorsal laminae narrowing abruptly, usually ending at the insertion; vaginant laminae 2/3-3/4 the leaf length, slightly unequal; cells smooth to bulging, distinct, irregularly hexagonal, 8-10 µm long. Autoicous; perichaetia terminal on axillary branches, perichaetial leaves not differentiated except for the indistinct limbidia; perigonia bud-like and axillary. Sporophytes one per perichaetium; setae ca 1 mm long, erect; thecae erect and symmetric, ca 0.7 mm long; peristome teeth divided ±2/3 their length, papillose proximally, spirally thickened distally; opercula conic-rostrate, ca 0.3 mm long. Spores minutely papillose, 16-22 µm in diameter. Calyptrae smooth, cucullate.

description: Relatively robust plants to ca 10 cm tall in yellow-green to golden tufts. Primary stems creeping, adnate to substrate, sheathed in leaves with broadly oblong-ovate bases, abruptly narrowed to broadly acuminate apices, eroding with age; secondary stems reddish, erect, mamillose, in cross-section with ca 6 layers of thick-walled, colored cells surrounding thick-walled cells with somewhat larger lumina, central strand absent; pseudoparaphyllia narrowly foliose; leaves narrowly ovate, 2.0- 2.3 x 1.0-1.2 mm, broadly and gradually acuminate, plicate, especially along upper costae, slightly decurrent, margins undulate above, serrate from apex to midleaf, sublimbate, apices becoming cucullate dry or wet due to strongly reflexed margins, usually twisted above; costae single, strong, extending 85-90% of leaf length, sinuose distally, 42-60 µm wide at base, slightly wider above, entire, bulging abaxially; median cells isodiametric to shortly oblong, smooth, walls strongly and irregularly thickened, porose, 9-13 x 5-6 ,um, apical intralaminal cells longer, 19-28 ,um, basal cells porose, 30-60 ,um long; alar cells quadrate in relatively large areas. Dioicous. Perichaetia inconspicuous, inner leaves to 1.4 mm long, with upper cells sublinear, densely porose, paraphyses present, few, as long as archegonia, cells quadrate below, rectangular above. Post-fertilization perichaetial leaves little differentiated in shape, oblong-lanceolate, abruptly nar- rowed to a long, gradually tapered apex, to 2.4 mm long, upper laminal cells 30-50 µm long. Vaginular hairs dense, uniseriate or often multiseriate, to 2 mm long. Setae twisted, scabrous on upper half, smooth to scarcely papillose below, 2.6- 4.3 mm long. Capsules erect-symmetric, papillose at base, cylindric, ca 2.0 x 0.8 mm; exothecial cells thick-walled, subquadrate, 20-28 x 16-18 ,um, becoming quadrate toward mouth; annulus not differentiated; operculum obliquely rostrate; exostome teeth pale yellow, widely spaced, deeply inserted below the mouth, ±smooth; endostome(?) rudimentary. Spores spherical, nearly smooth, 19-32 µm in diameter. Calyptrae cucullate, pilose, the hairs parallel with surface and slightly overtopping apices, ca 2 mm long.

description: Leaves appressed to loosely imbricate when dry, occasionally mildly crisped, erect to wide-spreading when moist, 0.55-1.50 x 0.34-0.82 mm; distal marginal teeth unicellular to occasionally multicellular; costa reaching 76-90% of leaf length, 37-73 µm wide at base; median cells 8.8-16.2 x 5.0-8.5 µm; basal cells becoming larger, to 35 µm long. Dioicous. Pre-fertilization perichaetial leaves lanceolate, 0.5-0.6 mm long, acuminate, serrulate above; ecostate to weakly costate; upper cells long-hexagonal, subflexuose, firm-walled.

description: Plants slender, glossy, green, yellow-green, or reddish-yellow, to 20 cm in length (Fig. 2). Irregularly branched, branches slender, erect to erect-spreading, more or less attenuate at ends. Leaves usually dimorphic; stem leaves (Figs. 1, 11) erect- spreading, oblong-lanceolate, 2.5-3.5 mm long, moderately concave; upper margins erect to incurved; apex acute or bluntly obtuse, entire or serrulate; median cells linear-flexuose, 50-80 x 5-8 ,um; alar cells (Fig. 3) enlarged, oblong to rectangular in well marked groups, hyaline to reddish-brown; branch leaves (Figs. 4-6) erect, ovate-lanceolate, 1.5-2.5 mm long, strongly concave; upper margins incurved; apex acute, serrulate; median leaf cells linear-flexuose, 40-65 x 7 µm; alar cells shortly oblong, moderately developed, not strongly bulging. Paraphyllia absent. Pseudoparaphyllia absent. Axillary hairs 3 per leaf; each hair 5-10 cells, very long and slender; basal cells reddish-brown, quadrate; upper cells hyaline becoming reddish with age, long cylindrical. Dioicous. Perichaetia terminal at the ends of short lateral branches; perichaetial leaves broadly rounded; archegonia 2 per perichaetium; paraphyses absent. Perigonia numerous on short lateral branches; perigonial leaves acute; antheridia 2 per perigonium; paraphyses present. Cap- sules (Fig. 10) cylindrical to subcylindrical, 2-3 mm long, emergent. Seta very short, 0.2 mm long, epidermal cells short and square. Operculum (Fig. 10) bluntly long-conic, 0.5 mm long. Annulus non-revoluble, consisting of several rows of flattened, thinner-walled cells. Exothecial cells thick-walled and more or less quadrate in 10-15 rows below the mouth, firm-walled and long-rectangular below. Stomata absent. Columella thick and fleshy, 320 ,um wide. Peristome diplolepideous, exostome inflexed when dry, reflexed when wet. Exostome teeth (Figs. 8, 9) inserted shortly below the mouth, 0.5-0.6 mm long, bright red, lightly papillose,dorsal lamellae rounded at the corners. Endostome trellis (Fig. 7) 0.7-0.8 mm long, orange, nearly perfect, cilia papillose, latticed 1/2 to 3/4 their length. Spores spherical, lightly papillose, 20-40 µm. Calyptrae not seen.

description: Plantae graciles, laxe caespitosae, sordido-virides vel aurantiaco-fuscescentes. Hyalodermis caulis strato uno; parietes exteriores cellularum uniporosi; cylindrus lignosus pallide luteus. Folia caulina 2.2-2.5 mm longa, concava, elliptica, apice rotundata, anguste limbata, ad basin fibrosa, interiore folii superficie poris ? numerosis in cellularum angulis et pro parte ad commissuras, dorso poris annulatis permultis in series ad commissuras instructa. Rami tumiduli, 2-fasciculati; parietes externi cellularum epidermidis apice poro magno instructi. Folia ramulina 2.5 mm longa, a foliis caulium non diversi nisi cellulis interioribus folii +/- multiporosis; cellulae chlorophylliferae sectione transversali rectangulae, utroque latere foliorum liberae.

description: Plants relatively small though tumid, loosely tufted, dirty-green to +/- orange- brown. Cells of stem cortex in 1 layer, with a large pore or porelike thin spot at the upper ends; wood cylinder pale-yellowish. Stem and branch leaves similar in size, shape, and cellular detail; stem leaves 2.2-2.5 mm long, deeply concave, broadly elliptic, rounded-obtuse, bordered by 1 or 2 rows of hyaline, linear cells; hyaline cells fibrillose throughout, with many connecting fibrils, on the outer surface with many pores in continuous commissural rows. Branches tumid, in fascicles of 2, both spreading; cortical cells uniporose at the upper ends. Branch leaves 2.5 mm long; hyaline cells slightly convex on both surfaces, on the outer surface with many crowded pores along the commissures, on the inner surface with numerous connecting fibrils and 2-8 pores scattered along the commissures; green cells rectangular in cross-section, broadly and equally exposed on both surfaces.

description: Plants pale to dark green or brownish green. Stems with propagula ± hidden among the leaves or only slightly conspicuous, sometimes absent; propagula smooth to slightly papillose; rhizoids lightly to moderately papillose on larger portions, appearing smooth on smaller rhizoidal branches. Leaves 1.5-2 mm long, ca 0.5 mm wide, broadly lanceolate, acute to subobtuse, widest just below the middle; margins occasionally recurved below, serrate to dentate in upper 1/3-1/4; lamina not extending alongside the excurrent costa, back of costa infrequently serrate. Seta elongate, 2-3 cm long; capsule erect to suberect, long-cylindrical, ca 3 mm long, (7) 8-ribbed, with flared mouth; peristome double, exostome lanceolate, papillose on both surfaces, becoming less so distally; endostome with a high, smooth basal membrane, segments narrow, keeled, papillose, slightly shorter than the teeth, cilia papillose, mostly double. Operculum blunt-conic. Spores spherical, 10-15 µm in diameter. Calyptra cucullate, smooth, naked.

description: Medium-sized to relatively robust plants, the secondary stems to ca 30 cm long, irregularly pinnate, the longer branches often branched; in cross-section with 4- 6 rows of small, thick-walled cells surrounding larger, thick-walled cells; axillary hairs with 2 short brown basal cells and 2 elongate hyaline apical cells. Secondary stem leaves loosely erect, oblong to oblong-ovate, abruptly hairpointed, 3.1-3.4 mm long (the hairpoint less than 1/2 the length of the entire leaf), concave, weakly undulate when dry, narrowly decurrent; margins broadly incurved and serrulate from the base of the hairpoint almost to the base; costa single, 1/2-1/4 the length of the leaf base, sometimes shorter; cells linear-flexuose, firm-walled, porose; alar cells subquadrate to short-rectangular, extending up the margins by 4-8 cells, not reaching the costa, when mature strongly thickened and porose, dark-yellow to reddish-orange. Branch leaves strongly 5-seriate, erect, oblong to oblong-ovate, abruptly long-cuspidate (especially on basal portions of branches but sometimes throughout) to hairpointed (on apical portions of branches or rarely throughout), 1.7-2.3 mm long (when hairpointed the hairpoint less than 1/2 the length), concave, short-decurrent; margins incurved and serrulate above; costa single, 1/2-2/3 the length of the leaf base; cells linear-flexuose, firm-walled, porose; alar cells mostly subquadrate to short-rectangular, extending up the margins by 4-8 cells, not reaching the costa, dark-yellow to reddish-orange, when mature somewhat to strongly thick-walled, in extreme cases the lumina almost occluded, porose. Dioicous. Perichaetia conspicuous; leaves convolute, lanceolate, ca 7 mm long gradually acuminate; margins plane, subentire, undulate; costa single, faint, extending about 5/8 the leaf length; cells linear-flexuose, very thick-walled, the walls as wide as the lumina, porose; the basal cells long-rectangular, yellow. Setae ca 0.5 mm long, smooth, from a crispate-hairy vaginula; capsules immersed, broadly cylindric, ca 3 mm long; exothecial cells short-rectangular, becoming oblate toward the mouth, firm-walled; operculum conic-rostrate, ca 1 mm long; peristome inserted slightly below the mouth, exostome teeth smooth, the outer surface thin and hyaline and the back surface yellow and thickened in 2 vertical columns, the teeth thus appearing furrowed, prostome well developed; endostome rudimentary and adhering to the exostome teeth. Spores ovoid to oblong, 48-69 µm long, finely roughened. Calyptrae cucullate, pilose with long, crispate, 1-3-seriate hairs.

description: Plants epiphytic, medium-sized, bright- to golden-green. Stems creeping, to ca 4 cm long, freely but irregularly branched, the branches often ascending, curved; in crosssection with 1-2 (-3) rows of small, thick-walled cells surrounding abruptly larger, thin-walled cells, central strand none; pseudoparaphyllia broadly foliose; axillary hairs with a single, short-rectangular, brown basal cell and (2-) 3-4 elongate, hyaline apical cells. Leaves erect-spreading, little altered when dry, often +/- homomallous, broadly oblong-lanceolate to oblong-ovate, (1.0-) 1.1-1.4 (-1.6) mm long, abruptly short acuminate, somewhat concave; margins entire or subserrulate at extreme apex, narrowly recurved almost throughout or just below; costa short and double or often absent; laminal cells firm-walled, subporose, in the acumen rounded-hexagonal, ca 4:1, at midleaf long-hexagonal, 7-8 (-1 1): 1, becoming more elongate toward the yellowed insertion; alar cells differentiated with a single row of inflated, oblong, yellow cells, 40-55 µm tall, ca 6 on each side of leaf, and with 2-4 rows of small, subquadrate cells above them. Autoicous. Perigonia minute, bracts ovate, ca 0.35 mm long, gradually short-acuminate; margins subserrulate above, bordered by a single row of long-rectangular cells; ecostate; cells at midleaf long-hexagonal; alar cells not differentiated. Perichaetia conspic- uous, leaves erect, oblong-lanceolate, to ca 2 mm long; margins entire, plane; ecostate or with a short, double costa; cells rounded- hexagonal in the acumen, ca 4:1, becoming linear at midleaf and yellow at insertion; alar cells similar to those of vegetative leaves but somewhat smaller and not inflated. Setae erect, 6-14 mm long, twisted, reddish, smooth; urn erect, 1.1-1.8 mm long, abruptly tapered to seta, widest near base, gradually tapering and becoming narrowest just below apex, mouth flaring; exothecial cells with firm vertical walls and thin, wavy horizontal walls, sometimes +/- collenchy- matous, short-rectangular, becoming quadrate to oblate and thin-walled in 1-2 rows at the mouth; annulus not differentiated; operculum obliquely long-rostrate, almost as long as the urn; peristome double, pale, exostome teeth incurved when dry, erect when moist, lanceolate, ca 110-120 µm long, obtuse at apex, often constricted shortly below apex and +/- capitate, scarcely bordered, on the front surface with a zig-zag center line, finely and sparsely papillose, slightly projecting at back; endostome papillose throughout, basal membrane of medium height, segments horizontal over mouth when dry, erect when moist, narrow, keeled, narrowly perforate, longer than the teeth, cilia none. Spores 15-20 Am in diameter, finely papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, naked, smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Buck, William R. & Vital, Daniel M. 1992. Paranapiacabaea paulista, a new genus and species of Sematophyllaceae from southeastern Brazil. Brittonia. 44: 339-343.

description: Plants rather small, soft, yellowish to pale- tawny or flesh-colored. Stems blackish in older portions; cortical cells in (2-)3(-4) layers, without fibrils, often 1 porose at cell ends or middles; wood cylinder greatly differentiated, dark red-brown. Stem leaves 1.2 mm long, oblong or lingulate, plane or +/-  concave at a rounded tip, fringed; hyaline cells not or sometimes 1-divided, on the outer surface fibrillose and porose in the upper 1/4 -1/3, with gaps at the extreme apex and below that 3-5 large, ringed, elliptic pores at adjacent corners and sometimes at commissures, on the inner surface with fibrils or mere vestiges of fibrils in the upper 1/4 and the surface largely resorbed or with 1-2 oblong or rounded gaps. Branches 3-fasciculate (2 spreading); cells of branch cortex without fibrils, often 1 -porose. Branch leaves erect-spreading, not noticeably seriate, cucullate-concave, 2 mm long, ovate, roughened at back of the tip and bordered by a resorption furrow; hyaline cells on the outer surface with large, ringed pores in 3's at adjacent angles and few or none at the commissures or angles, on the inner surface with 2-4 small, elliptic pseudopores at the commissures; green cells central and included, the hyaline cells smooth-walled, nearly plane on the upper surface, slightly convex on the outer.

description: Plants small (about 4 cm high), yellowish. Stems brown; cortical cells in 2 layers, not fibrillose, mostly porose at upper ends; wood cylinder dark brown, distinctly differentiated. Stem leaves 1.5-1.8 mm long, oblong- triangular, bluntly concave and scarcely roughened at the apex, bordered by a marginal resorption furrow; hyaline cells undivided or occasionally 1-divided, on the outer surface imperfectly fibrillose in the upper 1/3 or less, with numerous (3-6), rounded-oblong, porelike gaps in the upper 1/3 and few (1-3) from there to the base, on the inner surface without fibrils or with fibrils only at the apex, without pores or gaps. Branches 3-fascicled; branch cortex in 1 layer, lacking pores and fibrils. Branch leaves 2-2.5 mm long, concave, narrowly ovate and gradually acuminate, bordered by a resorption furrow; hyaline cells fibrillose throughout, on the outer surface with numerous, moderate-sized, rounded-elliptic commissural pores as well as pores inconspicuously grouped in 2's and 3's at adjacent angles, on the inner surface without pores or occasionally with 1-2 pseudopores; green cells isosceles-triangular, exposed on the inner surface, the hyaline cells convex on the outer surface and nearly plane on the inner.

description: Plants small (2-4.5 cm high), yellowish. Stem cortex 2-layered, the epidermal cells rectangular, 3-5:1, often porose at upper ends, rarely with faint spiral fibrils; wood cylinder poorly differentiated, yellowish. Stem leaves 2.2-3 mm long, oblong-ovate, deeply concave, cucullate at the apex, very narrowly bordered by linear cells below and a resorption furrow above; hyaline cells fibrillose to the leaf base, commonly 1 -divided, on the outer surface with many rather small, ringed, elliptic pores in continuous commissural rows and also toward the apex with occasional rounded, median pores of moderate size, on the inner surface with few (1-4) pseudopores at angles and commis- sures (more numerous at the extreme apex). Branches single, 5-6 mm long; branch cor- tex consisting of elongate cells, often uniporose at their upper ends, occasionally with faint spiral fibrils. Branch leaves 2.2-3 mm long, very slightly roughened at back of the apex, oblong-ovate, deeply concave, cucullate at the tip, narrowly bordered by linear cells in 1 row and by a resorption furrow toward the apex; hyaline cells on the outer surface with many rather small, ringed, elliptic pores in continuous commissural rows (and toward the apex occasional rounded, median pores of moderate size), at adjacent angles with pores inconspicuously grouped in 2's and 3's, with gaps none or very few at back of the apex, on the inner surface with few to numerous (2-1 1) pseudopores at angles and along commissures; green cells narrowly triangular, straight-sided, exposed on the inner surface, the hyaline cells smooth-walled, convex on both surfaces, more so on the inner.

description: Plantae minutae, pallido-luteae. Hyalodermis caulis strato uno; cylindrus lignosus pallidolutea. description: Plants very small, up to about 2 cm high, pale greenish or yellowish. Stem cortex 1 -layered, without pores; wood cylinder yel- lowish, poorly differentiated. Stem and branch leaves similar in shape and structure: Stem leaves ca. 3.2-3.5 mm long, oblong-ovate, concave, cucullate at a narrow, rounded apex, very narrowly bordered; hyaline cells fibrillose throughout, on the outer surface with 4-8 elliptic, ringed pores at commissures and angles, on the inner surface with 2-4 small pores or pseudopores at commissures and angles. Branches single, crowded; retort cells slightly differentiated. Branch leaves +/- spreading to subsquarrose when dry, 2.5-3 mm long, oblong-ovate, concave, cucullate at a narrow, rounded obtuse tip, bordered by 1-2 rows of linear cells; hyaline cells on the outer surface with (2-)5-9 elliptic, ringed pores at commissures, on the inner surface with 2-4(-7) small, elliptic pores and pseudopores at commissures and angles, sometimes in very short rows; green cells rectangular to trapezoidal, equally exposed on both surfaces, the hyaline cells convex on both surfaces.

description: Plants up to 8 cm high, soft and delicate, whitish-green above, pale yellow below. Stems very slender; cortical cells 1-layered, without pores; wood cylinder poorly differentiated, pale yellow. Stem leaves 2 mm long, narrowly ovate-acuminate, concave, very narrowly bordered by about 2 rows of linear cells; hyaline cells fibrillose throughout, long and narrow, not or occasionally 1-divided, on the outer surface with many ringed pores in commissural rows, on the inner surface with pores none or occasion- ally 1-2 in corners. Branches in fascicles of 3. Branch leaves 1.5-1.8 mm long, concave, ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, bordered by 2-3 rows of linear cells, on the outer surface with many ringed pores in commissural rows, on the inner surface with pores none or very few; green cells in section narrowly triangular, exposed on the inner surface, the hyaline cells convex on both surfaces, somewhat more so on the inner surface.

description: Stems loosely intertwined, most only basally attached to substrate (bark), olivegreen to brown in the dried condition. Plants robust, 1.0-2.0 cm long, 1-2 mm wide. Rhizoids sparse at underleaf bases. Growth habit deliquescent (i.e., main and secondary branches equal in vigor); ramification pattern irregularly pinnate. Non-innovational branches exclusively of the Lejeunea type; microphyllous branches absent. Stems (100) 125-150 ,tm wide, with strong differentiation between cortex and medulla. Cortex in cross-section composed of 7 large, rectangular cortical cells, 45-50 ,tm long x 20-22 µm wide, surrounding 18-22 smaller isodiametric medullary cells, 16-18 ,tm in diameter. Ventral merophytes two cells broad. Lateral leaves imbricate, widely-spreading, slightly convex. Dorsal lobe ovate to ovate-falcate, ranging in dimensions from 900 ,tm long x 625 ,tm wide to 1200 µm long x 764 µm wide. Margins crenulate, apices rounded to broadly acute, usually revolute. Dorsal attachment of lobe straight, lobe base cuneate, proximal dorsal lobe margins of opposing lateral leaves overlapping by 125-175 ,um. Lobules very small (covering .02 area of dorsal lobe), consistently fully developed and inflated; ovate to elliptical, 125-130 µm long x 110-1 17 µm wide. Lobular free margin normally inrolled, arched when flattened, with 1 single-celled apical tooth at the distal end; apical tooth acute (15) 27-30 µm long, often falcate, with hyaline papilla situated at proximal base. Opening to water sac constricted at distal end of lobule, opening to water sac roughly circular in shape. Marginal and median leaf cells isodiametric; marginal cells 27-34 µm in diameter; median cells 34-38 ,um in diameter. Basal leaf cells isodiametric to slightly rectangular, 22-28 µm long x 18-22 µm wide. Cells thin-walled, trigones large to bulging, intermediate thickenings absent. Ocelli probably present in living plants, based on occurrence of large, round idioblastic cells (42 µm average diameter) with brown residue found scattered in lateral leaves, underleaves and gynoecial bracts and bracteoles. Underleaves imbricate, rectangular, and very large, from 525 µm long x 800 µm wide to 875 µm long x 1200 µm wide, 7 times as wide as the stem; underleaf area hpproximately equalling lateral leaf area. Underleaves emarginate to slightly bifid, sinus descending at most 50-75 µm, broadly obtuse, lobes rounded. Insertion U-shaped, leaf base cuneate (not decurrent or cordate). Specialized means of asexual reproduction lacking. Androecia not seen. Gynoecia on long or leading axes, terminal appendage of gynoecial branch always an underleaf. Gynoecial bracts obovate, lobe 1250-1500 ,um long x 825-1000 ,um wide. Lobule of bract 875-950 µm long x 500-700 ,um wide, keel 375-450 ,um long; keel occasionally with a narrow wing. Bracteole broadly spathulate, 1150-1250 µm long x 800-925 µm wide, entire to slightly emarginate, apex rounded, and fused at base to youngest (second) bract. Margins of bracts and bracteole crenulate. No mature perianths observed. Immature perianths obpyriform with 5 sharp*carinae, all equally developed, extending 1/2 perianth length. Keels not winged or otherwise ornamented. Radula-type innovations consistently present, usually paired. Appendages follow the pycnolejeuneoid sequence on all innovations. Innovational branches are equal in vigor to non-innovational branches and usually terminate in gynoecia after 10-20 leaf cycles. Inflorescence pattern is a dichasium.

description: Plants small, filamentous, in 2-4 cm long, pinnate to bipinnate, the branches rarely becoming flagelliform; lateral branches with the half-leaf subulate, often with a two-celled base, or bifid; ventral branches occasionally branched, flagelliform or leafy or sexual; rhizoids colorless, short, from small basal cells of the underleaves, or the base of a flagelliform branch; stem in transverse section with a cortex of 6-8-12 large cells surrounding the numerous smaller cells of the medulla (the smaller stems with fewer cells); line of leaf insertion transverse; stem leaves spreading, of 2-3 (-4) approximately equal, long filamentous segments, 4-6 cells long, or each segment from a two-cell base, the latter joined for half or all their length and forming a lamina 4-6 (-8) cells across, the cells of the seg- ments just above the base 75-100 µ long or more, the upper cells 60-80 µ long, the cuticle nearly smooth; stem underleaves variable, smaller than the leaves, bifid (sometimes trifid when the leaves are trifid), the segments of 2-4, rarely more, elongate cells, from a base of 4 or more small cells bearing rhizoids; branch underleaves often very small and only 2 cells broad at the base and 2 cells long; plants dioicous and autoicous (Muller 1956) ; male infloreseence terminal on the stem or lateral branch, the bracts and bracteoles in 5-many series, the monandrous bracts like the leaves, the bracteoles like the branch underleaves; antheridia large, spherical, the stalk of 1 row of cells; female in- florescence on a short ventral sexual branch, occasionally terminal on the stem or lateral branch, the bracts and bracteoles in 3 or 4 series, large, quadrate to rectangular in outline, divided to one-half their lengths or less into usually four laciniate laciniae with occasional marginal spines, the cells long, thin-walled; perianth to 1.7 mm long, fusiform, with three rounded keels above, contracted, the mouth of to 12 laciniae terminated by long unbranched cilia, the cells loing as in the bracts and bracteoles; capsule long, ovoid, dark brown, the wall of three layers of cells, with the brown thickenings appearing as knots along the radial walls of the outer surface, and as bands or partial bands on the inner tangential wall; seta in transverse section of 8 (-9-10) very large outer cells surrounding 16-24 smaller, thin-walled cells; foot cone-shaped; elaters long, reddish brown, bispiral; spores brown, 14-16 µ in diameter, finely punctate.

description: Plants small, to ca. 2 mm tall, but innovations somewhat taller; rhizoids numerous, coarsely papillose when mature, finely papillose when young. Leaves broadly lanceolate, somewhat concave, ca. 1.1 mm long, more or less gradually cuspidate; margins plane throughout or narrowly recurved near midleaf, subentire with marginal cell junctions slightly projecting; costa subpercurrent, percurrent, or shortly excurrent; lam- inal cells with firm walls, long-hexagonal to long-rectangular, ca. 7:1, ca. 55-75 x 8-12 ,im, becoming somewhat longer, narrower, and thicker-walled in a single marginal row and forming an obscure border, becoming shorter, broader, short-rectangular, and thinwalled marginally toward the insertion. Leaves of innovations oblong-lanceolate, 0.5-0.7 mm long, more or less abruptly cuspidate, otherwise similar to other leaves. Dioecious. Setae 1-1.5 cm long, orange, smooth, flexuose when dry, cygneous when moist; capsules obpyriform with a small mouth, ca. 2 mm long, somewhat wrinkled; exothecial cells short-rectangular, more or less leptodermous, becoming oblate in ca. 3 rows at the mouth, the stomata numerous in the lower half of the urn; annuli compound, of 2-3 rows of large, small-lumined cells; opercula conic; peristomes single, of endostome only, pale yellow, consisting of a smooth, irregular basal membrane ca. 140 Am tall, segments none. Spores spherical, ca. 15 Am in diam., slightly roughened. Calyptrae not seen.

description: Plants dark green, arising from persistent protonemata, erect, becoming decumbent, unbranched, ca. 2-5 mm long X 1.5-2.5 mm wide. Stems with basal, tan, papillose rhizoids; axillary hyaline nodules undifferentiated; outer 2-3 tiers of cortical cells small, incrassate, inner cortical cells larger, thin-walled, central strand undifferentiated. Leaves pinnately arranged in as many as 10 pairs, lowermost ones scale-like, upper ones oblong, obtuse, apex usually asymmetric because of the dorsal half of the apex extending further upward than ventral half of the apex, 0.8-1.7 mm long X 0.2-0.4 mm wide; margins crenulate-serrulate, limbate and entire in proximal parts of most vagi- nant laminae, limbidium indistinct; costa long-excurrent, 23-36 Rm wide at junction of vaginant laminae, terete in section, bryoides-type (cf. Bruggeman-Nannenga, 1990: 41); dorsal lamina rounded to insertion, not decurrent; vaginant laminae ca. 2/5 leaf length, unequal, homostichous (cf. Norris & Koponen, 1987: 179; Pursell et al., 1988: 203), minor lamina acute, ending about midway between costa and margins; laminal cells firm-walled, guttulate, smooth or slightly bulging, irregularly quadrate to hexagonal, 9-22 Rm long, somewhat smaller at margins, larger and oblong-hexagonal to oblong juxtacostally. Rhizoautoicous; perigonial stems gemmiform, scattered on protonemata among infertile and perichae- tial stems; perichaetia terminal on elongate stems. Sporophytes one per perichaetium; setae ca. 2 mm long; thecae erect, symmetric, ca. 0.5 mm long, stomatose, exothecial cells quadrate, trigonous; peristome of the scarious type (cf. Allen, 1980: 317; Bruggeman-Nannenga & Berendsen, 1990: 200), teeth split about 1/2 their length, with fimbriate trabeculae on the ventral surface. Opercula, spores, and calyptrae not seen.

description: Plants soft-textured, fleshy rather than wiry, consisting of interwoven, pale, whitish green, copiously ramified axes; shoots threadlike, mostly small- and very remote leaved, subisophyllous, indefinite in lengt distally brownish or purplish brown pigmented (androecia often more deeply pigmented; gynoecia when immature whitish green), ca. 235-285 pm wide with leaves (shoot apices rarely to 325-360 pm broad). Branches copious, intercalary branches from all 3 merophyte rows (85% axillary in lateral leaves, 15% in underleaves); terminal branching very rare (1 Acromastigum- type branch seen). Stems terete, fleshy, 105-125 µm (above) to 150-160 µm diam.; cortex in 8-12 rows, feebly thick walled, slightly inflated, ca. 34-38 pm wide X 30-36 pm high; medullary cells in 18- 24 rows, much smaller than the cortical, ca. (12)15-20(22) pm diam., peripheral row somewhat thick-walled but toward the center rather thin-walled; cortical cells in surface view short-rectangular to subquadrate in outline, with up to 6-8 intervening between successive leaves on each side of stem. Rhizoids rather rare, mostly at bases of highly reduced underleaves low on the stem, usually 1 or 2 per underleaf base, sporadically from basal cells of underleaves of normal leafy shoots. Leaves exceedingly remote, small, their width usually not or barely exceeding stem width but some shoots toward apices with leaves appreciably longer, remaining remote; insertion (as seen in dorsal aspect) feebly incubous to transverse, extended to stem midline (to the me- dian-longitudinal cell walls), ventrally somewhat obliquely incubous. Mature leaves concave, suberect, handlike, the lobes erect or more often a little incurved, the leaves when flattened somewhat asymmetrically quadrate-ovate to quadrate-obo- vate, up to ca. 400 pm wide X 450 pm long (dorsal half, the ventral sector shorter, ca. 340 pm long) up to 370 pm wide X 540 µm long (then ventrally 500-5 10 pm long), usually asymmetrically bifid or (less often) trifid for 0.35-0.45 their length; lobes acute (but not longly so), unequal, the dorsal larger, up to 5-9 cells wide at base, formed of up to 20-30(32) cells, usually ending in 2 superposed cells; ventral 1 or 2 lobes usually a little shorter, few-celled, 4-5 cells broad, blunt at the tips or ending in a single cell and acute; lamina to 10-21 cells broad, the dorsal margin gently curved, the ventral equally or less so. Cells ± similar in size throughout leaf, with walls thin in lower half of leaves, a little thickened in the (often pigmented) lobes, devoid of trigones; lobe cells variable in shape and size; median cells quite variable, quadrate and 38-42 to more often rectangulate and 19-30(36) X 52-76 ,um; basal cells oblong-hexagonal, 27-32 µm broad X 40-83 pm long; cuticle smooth or almost so in proximal half of leaf, in lobes papillose. Oil-bodies lacking. Underleaves large, little or not wider than stem, about 0.55-0.65 X area of lateral leaves, up to (260)330-360(430) pm broad X (190)280-350 pm long, usually 15-18 cells broad (but often much smaller), broadly and transversely quadrate-reniform or rounded-oblong, 3-4-lobed to ca. 0.25- 0.35, the lobes few-celled (usually of 7-9, up to 16-20 cells), usually 1 or 2 lobes a little smaller, but not or weakly asymmetric, the lobes usually not ending in slime papillae, mostly ending in 2 cells, side-by-side. Asexual reproduction lacking.

description: Dioicous?, plants up to 3 cm long x 2.5 mm wide, brown in the dried condition, epiphytic on twigs. Stems 90-110 µm in diam, in cross-section composed of 6 cortical cells surrounding 1 medullary cell. Leaves 850 x 400 to 1200 x 450 µm, diverging from stem at an angle of approximately 750, contiguous, upper margin of dorsal lobe plane, arched, entire to irregular, straight at point of dorsal attachment, not overlapping stem; marginal cells of dorsal lobe isodiametric, 15-35 µm in diam, cells of midportion and base of lobe isodiametric to rectangular, 25- 42 x 20-25 µm, trigones present, large and bulging, intermediate thickenings strongly developed, papillae absent, frame composed of 3 elongate, strongly arched and overlapping cells with weak bands of cell wall thickening. Lobules 1-1.2 mm long, up to 1.5 times the lobe length, cylindrical at base, flaring toward sac, sac inflated, rounded, somewhat bulbous, 400-450 x 400 µm, composed of rectangular cells 25-35 x 17-25 µm, cell walls as in leaf lobe, apex without ornamentation; valve broadly ligulate, 138 x 83 µm, composed of 47-50 cells, border cells hyaline, hinge absent. Gemmae not seen. Underleaves with strongly divergent, narrowly triangular lobes 150-250 Am long, with an attenuate apex terminating in a single cell, lobes 4-6 cells broad at base, cells of underleaves isodiametric, 12-20 µm in diam, trigones large but not bulging, intermediate thickenings small. Gynoecia on main stems or short branches, innovations usually present, single, lobe of gynoecial bract ligulate, 400-500 x 150 µm, apex rounded, margins entire, lobule of bract ligulate, 350-400 x 130 µm, apex rounded, margins entire, bracteole similar in shape to underleaves, and only slightly larger, lobes up to 250 µm long. Perianth emergent, shape oblong, inflated, with 5 keels extending 3/4 the perianth length when young, in older perianths, keels extending only 1/3 or less of perianth length, margins of keels entire; androecia not seen.

description: Autoicous, plants rather small, 1-1.5 cm x 0.6-1.0 mm, shiny dark brown in the dried condition, prostrate, growing over other bryophytes, presumably on bark. Growth habit deliquescent (i.e., main and secondary branches equal in vigor); ramification pattern irregularly pinnate. Branches Lejeunea-type exclusively. Stems 125-140 µm in diam, with cells of cortical layer not larger than medullary cells. Cortex in cross-section composed of 10-13 rectangular cells, averaging 20 x 12 µm, surrounding 9-12 isodiametric medullary cells, averaging 20 µm in diam. Ventral merophytes 4 cells broad. Leaves widely spreading when dry, imbricate, with apices often decurved. Dorsal lobe ovate-falcate, 500 x 400 µm to 800 x 500 µm. Margins entire, apices acute to apiculate. Dorsal attachment of lobe following a straight line, not passing the mid-point of the stem. Lobules uniformly inflated, ellipsoid, 250 x 100 µm to 350 x 210 µm. Free margin involute. Apical tooth single-celled, inconspicuous, hyaline papilla not observed. Keel of lobule rounded to obtusely angled. Cells of dorsal lobe rectangular to isodiametric; cells of acroscopic margin quadrate, 10-20 µm; cells of mid-portion of lobe isodiametric, 25-37 µm in diam, cells of lobe base near stem attachment rectangular, 25-43 x 15-20 µm. Trigones large, radiate; intermediate thickenings present. Underleaves contiguous, rarely imbricate, orbicular to obdeltoid, 340 x 380 µm to 380 x 420 µm (3-4 times stem width). Underleaf margins entire, insertion slightly arched, base cuneate. Rhizoids sparse, when present brownish, forming a primary rhizoid disc at underleaf base. Gynoecia on main and secondary branches, gynoecial bracts ovate, apex acute to apiculate, margins sometimes irregularly dentate, lobe 800-1000 x 370-480 µm. Lobule of bract 280-380 x 70-90 µm. Bracteole broadly ovate, 375-500 x 300-400 µm, margin entire. Perianth spherical when young, at maturity emergent, obpyriform, terete, lacking any trace of plication, becked. Innovations usually absent, but when present, elongated Lejeunea-type branches. One or 2 innovations per gynoecium may be produced. Innovations frequently terminate in gynoecia, and though usually diffuse, the inflorescence pattern is sometimes mono- or dichasial. Androecia, which occupy short branches or terminate elongate branches, consist of 4-7 pairs of hypostatic bracts, with bracteoles present throughout the length of the androecium. Antheridia not seen. Capsule valves ovate-lanceolate, 425-475 x 225-250 µm. Outer capsule wall layer composed of cells with hyaline, nodulose walls, inner capsule walls with yellow-brown fenestrate thickenings. Elaters truncate, with cell wall thickenings forming a single spiral. Sporeling Lopholejeunea-type.

description: Plants aquatic, medium-sized, stiff, dark red-brown to blackish below, dark yellow green at extreme tips. Stems to ca. 6 cm long, little branched, brittle when dry; in cross-section with 2-4(-5) outer rows of small thick-lumened cells, surrounding larger thick-walled cells, central strand none; axillary hairs with 3-4 oblate to quadrate basal cells, all hyaline or the basal most one sometimes brown, and 4-7 short-rectangular hyaline apical cells. Leaves crowded, erect, somewhat homomallous, little altered when moist, 1.5-2.4 mm long, to 0.5 mm wide, with a concave, ? sheathing base, short-decurrent; margins plane throughout or erect at base, entire; costa long-excurrent, concolorous, the ex- current portion comprising 1/3-1/2 the leaf length, blunt or abruptly pointed at apex, ca. 140 pim wide at base, 100-125 pim wide just above lamina, in section round above with 6-9 cells in diam., flattened below with a broad dorsal stereid band 2-3 cells thick and 2(-3) rows of larger ventral cells; lamina unistratose except bistratose at extreme apex and juxtacostally, sometimes unequal and extending along costa higher on one side than the other; laminal cells long-rectangular, 20-36 pim long, 4-5 Km wide, somewhat shorter at the extreme apical margins, the walls strongly nodose  thickened, ± smooth, often colored at in- sertion; alar cells differentiated in 1-2(-3) rows at basal margins, extending up the margins by 3-7 cells, short-rectangular, 16- 32 X 6-10 pLm, slightly nodose-thickened. Inflorescences and sporophytes unknown.

description: Autoicous. Plants up to 700 µm wide, dull brownish-green in the dried condition, growing loosely appressed to bark. Stems 85-100 µm in diam, in cross-section composed of 7 epidermal cells surrounding 10- 13 medullary cells, epidermal cells quadrate to rectangular, 20-25 x 13-20 µm, thin walled, medullary cells roughly isodiametric, 15-18 µm in diam, thick-walled, ventral merophytes 2 cells wide. Leaves diverging from stem at an angle of 50-70º, contiguous, somewhat concave, dorsal lobe orbicular to somewhat reniform, 325-450 x 300-400 µm, margins entire to slightly crenulate, apex broadly rounded, acroscopic margin rounded at dorsal base, basiscopic margin cordate-auriculate at point of lobule attachment; marginal cells of dorsal lobe quadrate to rectangular, 13-25 x 10-18 µm, trigones small, intermediate thickenings absent, cells of midportion isodiametric to oblong, 20- 38 x 12-25 µm, trigones small to medium, intermediate thickenings absent or faintly present, cells of leaf base oblong, 20-40 x 12-25 µm, trigones large, not bulging, in- termediate thickenings absent or faintly present. Lobules ovoid, inflated throughout, 150-160 x 100-140 µm, 0.3-0.5 lobe length, apex acute, sometimes somewhat falcate, base rounded, keel strongly rounded, almost semi-circular, not or barely ex- tending beyond tooth of free margin, free margin inrolled, marginal tooth 1-2 cells long, sharply pointed, often curved inward and difficult to see without flattening the lobule, hyaline papilla situated at distal base of tooth, sinus between tooth and lobule apex constricted. Underleaves distant to contiguous, obovate to orbicular, 150-280 x 190-280 µm, 2 x stem width, bifid to 0.5 underleaf length, sinus V-shaped, lobes triangular, 5-6 cells wide at base, apices acutely pointed, margins entire to slightly crenulate, bases cuneate to slightly rounded, insertion straight to slightly arched. Gynoecia on short or long branches, innovations present, single, not observed to be fertile, leaf sequence pycnolejeuneoid, bract lobes oblong to obovate, 450-480 x 300-330 µm, apex rounded, margins entire to slightly irregular, bract lobules ligulate, 330-350 x 150-180 µm, apex obtuse, margins entire to slightly irregular; bracteoles oblong, 500- 550 x 180-200 µm, margins entire, bifid to 0.2 bracteole length, lobe apices obtusely pointed. Perianths emergent, obpyriform, 580-620 x 480-500 µm, somewhat compressed, keels 5 (dorsal keel much weaker than others), extending at least 0.75 perianth length, the lateral ones with a unicel- lular wing, margins somewhat irregular. Androecia (only one observed) on short branch, with 3 pairs of bracts, 1 bracteole at base.

description: Thallus rigid, yellowish green, convex, with deflexed wings, 350-630 µm wide (non-flattened), 700-1015 ,um wide when flattened. Branching copious, dichot- omous, ventral branches sporadic. Costa notably wide for axis width, on vigorous main axes with (8) 10-15 rows of dorsal cortical cells and 11-16 rows of ventral cortical cells, the costa of weaker thalli with fewer cortical cells: 4-8 rows dorsally and 5 or 6 rows ventrally; dorsal cortical cells in surface view 18-24 µm wide, 28-34 µm long, similar in size to and undifferentiated from wing cells, the ventral cortical cells 19-30 µm wide, 25-38 µm long. Costa with cortical cells not differentiated from the medullary in size or wall characters: both types of cells lepto- dermous or slightly thickened, the cortical cells not tangentially flattened; medullary cells of main axis 5-8 rows high, in 25-38 rows (on weak axes as few as 10-15 rows). Wings on strong axes with margins gently deflexed but not revolute, 16-22 cells wide from midrib to thallus margin, the wings of weaker thalli strongly decurved, 7-13 cells wide; wings locally 2-stratose (especially near juncture with costa but sporadically so elsewhere); cells thin walled, trigones small to medium, the median wing cells 19-26 µm wide, 23-30 µm long, the marginal wing cells 20-30 ,um wide, 28-38 ,um long; wing cells in cross section 23-28 µm thick in median sector, the exposed faces straight and not convex. Hairs of thallus present only on wing margins and ventral surface of costa, completely lacking elsewhere, the hairs freely developed on costa of vigorous thalli but sparingly so on costa of weaker thalli; marginal hairs sparing, single, on strong thalli +/- ventrally displaced, on weak thalli strictly marginal. Gemmae lacking. Dioicous (apparently). Known only from unfertilized gynoecia.

description: Autoicous. Plants up to 1-1.7 mm wide, yellow-green when living, yellow-brown in the dried condition, growing on living leaves. Stems 60-85 Am in diam, in cross-section composed of 7 epidermal cells surrounding 8-12 medullary cells, epidermal cells +/- rectangular, 13-18 x 5-10 µm, medullary cells +/- isodiametric, 4-6 µm in diam. Leaves diverging from stem at an angle of 60-750, imbricate to contiguous, flattened, dorsal lobe ovate to ovate-falcate, 800-1000 x 600-700 µm, margins irregularly denticulate, apex broadly rounded, acroscopic margin straight at dorsal base, basiscopic margin weakly to strongly arched distal to lobule attachment; leaf cells isodiametric to rectangular, marginal cells of dorsal lobe quadrate to rectangular, 18-25 x 10-15 µm, trigones small, intermediate thickenings absent, cells of midportion 18-37 x 15-32 µm, trigones small, intermediate thickenings absent, cells of leaf base 30-50 x 30- 37 µm, trigones medium, intermediate thickenings conspicuous. Lobules ovoid, usually inflated, rarely flattened and triangular, 250-300 x 150-290 µm, approxi- mately 0.3 lobe length, apex narrowly acute to attenuate, base cuneate to rounded, keel straight to rounded, extending beyond tooth for ca 30 µm, free margin strongly inrolled and cucullate, hyaline papilla marginal, situated in a notch between 2 cells, both of which may be somewhat differentiated from other marginal cells (and possibly represent reduced marginal teeth). Papilla oriented toward inner surface of lobule, sinus between tooth and distal edge of lobule very shallow or lacking. Underleaves remote, ovate, 200-520 x 190-300 µm,3-4x stem width, bifid to approx. 0.5 underleaf length, sinus U- or V-shaped, lobes triangular, 5- 6 cells wide at base, apices acute to slightly acuminate, margins dentate to spinose on young leaves, irregularly dentate on mature leaves, rhizoid disc strongly developed, cordate, producing a large, circular rhizoid mat at underleaf base. Gynoecia on very short branches, innovations usually absent, but if present single, and usually quite short and sterile, leaf sequence pycnolejeuneoid, bract lobes spathulate, 450-680 x 350-400 µm, apex rounded, margins irregular to denticulate, bract lobules ligulate to obovate, 350- 450 x 100-120 µm, margins entire to ir- regular, bracteole ligulate to obovate, 450- 500 x 250-300 µm, margins irregularly denticulate, bifid to 0.2 bracteole length, lobes acutely pointed. description: Plants bristly-capillaceous, yellowish to whitish green or dark green, in mats or tufts; leafy stems radial, up to 5-6 cm long, pinnate to bipinnate; lat- eral branches frequent, long, with shorter secondary branches, all of the Frul- lania-type, the half-leaf subulate or bifid; ventral branches frequent becoming long flagelliform; rhizoids short, numerous on the scales of the flaoelliform branches and from the bases of the underleaves; stems in transverse section with a cortical row of 12 or 9 large cells, surrounding the numerous smaller cells of the medulla; line of leaf insertion transverse, the stem leaves erect-spreading, bristly, cuneate in outline, 0.65 mm long, 0.18 mm broad at the base, quadrified or trifid (on the branches) to within 1 1/2 cells of the base, uniseriate segments 5 or 6 cells long, straight and stiff, the lower cells 90-100 × 30-40 µ, the tip cell to 65 × 12 ,, the lamina one and one-half rows of cells high, 6-8 cells across, large; stem underleaves similar, the lamina two rows of cells high and with usually 3 segments; plants dioicous; female infloreseence on a short ventral branch or occasionally terminal on a lateral branch, the bracts and bracteoles similar, in 3 or 4 series, ovate to rectangular in outline, divided to one-third their length into 2-4 long-ciliate laciniae, the cells long, thin-walled; perianth lonig, contracted above, the mouth laciniate, the terminal cilia long, simple.

description: Plants whitish to yellowish green, filamentous, in erect tufts or mats; leafy stems 4-6 cm long, radially symmetrical, abundantly bi-or tripinnately branched, often appearing fan-shaped from an almost leafless base, the tips recurved, the lateral branches long with shorter secondary branches, a few becoming flagelli- form; half-leaf bifid or quadrifid; the ventral branches occasional, long, leafy or rarely becoming flagelliform, or coarse with distant leaves but becoming densely leafy above and easily detached from the stem, or short female; rhizoids colorless, from the base of the underleaf; stem in transverse section brownish yellow, the unistratose cortex of 18 or 15 large cells 63 X 42 ,u, surrounding the medulla of many smaller cells; leaf insertion transverse; stem leaves distant to subimbricated, averaging 0.86 X 0.5 mm. subrectangular in outline, erect-spread- ing, 6- or 5-parted to near the middle, the segments uniseriate, 4 or 5 cells long, the lowest averaging 95 ,u in length, the tip cell to 50 ,u, the walls uniformly thin; perianth long, contracted, with three broad lobes above, the mouth crenulate; sporophyte not seen.

description: Plants tiny, whitish green to yellowish, in small patches; stems up to 1 cm long, pinnate, the lateral branches distant, the half-leaf subulate, the ventral branches occasional, interealary; stem in transverse section with a cortical layer of 6-8 large, thin-walled cells, surrounding the numerous small cells of the nedulla; rhizoids from small cells on the base of the underleaf; leaf insertion transverse; stem leaves distant, more or less ascending; ineurved or spreading, quadrate in outline, mostly 0.35 mm long, trifid to within one cell of the base, the lamina one cell high and 6 cells across (two cells for each segment), the segments to 6 cells long, the cells near the base about 70 µ long, those near tip shorter; underleaves much smaller than the leaves, bifid, the segments one or two cells long; infloreseences and sporophyte not seen.

description: Plants small, filamentous, in whitish green tufts, on decaying logs aid humus; leafy stems to 1 or 2 cm long, mrore or less radially symmetrical, regularly pinnately branched, the branches usually short, densely leafy, the half-leaf from a two-celled base, usually bifid; ventral branches mostly short, bearing a female inflorescence; rhizoids colorless, from the basal cells of an underleaf; stem in transverse section with a cortical layer of 12 large cells surrounding the smaller cells of the medulla, the line of leaf insertion transverse; stem leaves distant, ascendant-nerved, quadrate in outline, averaging 0.35 mm long, divided to within a row of the base into 4 uniseriate segments of 4-6 cells 54-70 / long, the lamina 1 row of cells high, 8 cells across, two cells under each segment; stem underleaves similar, the segments usually 3-5 cells long, the lamina con- sisting of one row of 6-8 cells, the cells as in the leaf; or the lamina smaller and several rows high and bearing rhizoids; branch leaves and underleaves with 1 or 2 fewer segments; female infloreseence on a short ventral branch, the bracts and bracteoles and perianth like those of T. sejuncta.

description: Plants long, slender, flaccid, in whitish green to greenish brown or dark brown, mats or tufts; stems more or less radial, to 3 cm or more long, sparingly to abundantly branched; lateral branches scarce, leafy, of the Fructtania and Microlepidozia types; ventral branches more numerous, long, slender, flagelliform, often becoming leafy, or as pale, slender to stout stolons with tiny scale leaves and few rhizoids; stems in transverse section with a unistratose layer of 20-24 cells mostly larger and with thicker walls and deeper brown pigmentation than those of the medulla; cells of the cortex and medulla not so different in size and color in pale spongy stems; leaf insertion transverse; leaves and underleaves distant to imbricated, spreading-concave, strongly ineurved above, subquadrate in outline, averaging 0.50 mm long, 0.56 m wide, the bases rounded, quadrifid to one-third or more of their length, the segments broad, triangular, the base 8-10 cells across, the cells averaging 18-25 µ x 18 µ, the walls uniformly thickened, the trigones inconspicuous, the cuticle faintly verruculose; plants dioicous; male infloreseences frequent, on short ventral branches, or becoming interealary on longer ventral branches, the bracts and bracteoles in 3-10 or more series, the bracts concave, bifid, the bracteoles plane; female infloreseence (only one) ventral on a short ventral branch with several series of smaller leaves and underleaves; bracts and bracteoles similar, in 3 series, more or less keeled, those of the innermost series long-orbicular, concave, the broad apex undivided or with several blunt lobes and occasional projecting cells; perianth long, slender, contracted above, the mouth crenulate. description: Plants small, in lustrous, yellow- to bright-green, extensive, dense mats. Stems suberect to ascending, mostly ca. 5 mm long, usually not branched, dark red. Leaves contorted when dry, readily caducous, leaving naked stems, ± complanate when moist, lateral leaves erect- to wide-spreading, oblong-obovate, 0.65-0.85 mm long; dorsal leaves erect, ± ovate to oblong-ovate, 0.4-0.5 mm long, short-apiculate; margins bordered by (1-)2(-3) rows of narrow, thick-walled, often porose, elongate cells, merging at apex to form a short (ca. 50 µm), few-celled apiculus, remaining distinct at leaf base, subentire to serrulate above, entire below, plane; costa single, slender, often with a short fork near apex, ending ca. 3/4 the leaf length; upper leaf cells rounded rhomboidal to oval, 1 1-15(-17) X 8-9(-10) gim, firm- to thick-walled and usually somewhat porose, ± collenchymatous, basal juxtacostal cells not greatly differentiated, rectangular to elliptical, ca. 28-32 X 8-9 µm, firm-walled, porose. Asexual reproduction presumably by caducous leaves. Autoicous. Pericbaetia small, inconspicuous; leaves few, pale, erect, Ianceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 0.6-0.9 mm long, t abruptly short-acuminate; margins bordered by 1(-2) rows of elongate cells, merging to form the acumen, obscure below, subentire, plane; costa mostly none; cells long-hexagonal above, firm-walled, not porose, long-rectangular below, becoming narrower toward the margins. Setae elongate, smooth throughout, reddish, 7-9 mm long; capsules erect, short-cylindric and gradually tapering to the seta, ca. 1 mm long; exothecial cells rectangular, 3-5:1, thick-walled, porose, becoming subquadrate and collenchymatous in 3-5 rows at mouth; annulus none; operculum not seen; exostome teeth erect recurved when dry, bordered (outer surface much wider than inner surface), on the front surface pale, with a zig-zag median line, finely cross-striolate below, finely and sparsely papillose above, yellowish at back, ± unornamented, slightly trabeculate; endostome pale, papillosespiculose throughout, with a low basal membrane, segments narrow, keeled, with baffle-like crosswalls, not perforate, about as long as the teeth, cilia none. Spores spherical, papillose, 14-17 µm diam. (few seen). Calyptrae mitrate, ca. 0.75 mm long, fimbriate at base, naked, slightly roughened above.

description: Autoicous, plants rather small, 1.5-2 cm X 0.9-1.1 mm wide, shiny greenish brown in the dried condition, prostrate on substrate (bark). Growth habit deliquescent (i.e., main and secondary branches equal in vigor); ramification pattern irregularly pinnate. Non-innovational branches of the Lejeunea-type exclusively. Stems 88-101 gm in diam, with cells of cortical layer slightly larger than those of medullary region. Cortex in cross-section composed of 12 rectangular to isodiametric cells, 15 X 11 µm to 22 X 20 µm, surrounding 12-16 isodiametric medullary cells, averaging 12 µm in diam. Ventral merophytes 4 cells broad. Leaves widely spreading when dry. Lateral leaves imbricate, erect; dorsal lobe orbicular to ovate, 500 X 450 µm to 750 X 875 µm; margins entire, apices rounded. Dorsal attachment of lobe following a straight line, not passing the mid-point of the stem. Lobules complex, uniform in shape, varying in size from 176 X 165 µm to 207 X 187 µm. Proximal portion of lobule ovoid to sphaerical and utriculate, separated from flattened, triangularly shaped distal portion by a deep acute sinus. In proximal portion, free margin of lobule inrolled and strongly cucullate, not visible without dissection; in distal portion free margin flat, straight, or slightly arched. Apical tooth blunt and inconspicuous, near distal edge of cucullate free margin; hyaline papilla on inner surface of lobule, near apical tooth. Basiscopic edge of lobule rounded to obtusely angled. Cells of dorsal lobe rectangular to nearly isodiametric; cells of acroscopic margin 11 X 9 µm to 13 X 17 µm; cells of of lobe 20 X 115 µm to 26 X 26 µm; cells of lobe base 22 X 22 µm to 18 X 33 µm. Trigones large, radiate to slightly cordate in mid-portion of leaf; intermediate thickenings present. Underleaves contiguous, rarely imbricate, orbicular, 225 X 225 µm to 300 X 375 µm (3-4 times stem width). Underleaf margins entire, insertion straight to slightly arched, base cuneate. Rhizoids reddish-brown, forming a primary rhizoid disc at underleaf base. Gynoecia on main and secondary branches, terminal appendage of gynoeciumbearing branch consistently an underleaf. Gynoecial bracts obovate, apex rounded to acute, lobe 475-500 X 625-650 µm. Lobule of bract 375-425 X 125 µm, keel 375-425 µm long; margins entire. Bracteole orbicular to obovate, 475 X 450 µm, margins entire. Perianth emergent, obcordate to obovate, strongly dorsiventrally compressed, 750-1000 X 1000 µm, beak 30-40 µm long, 30-35 µm wide at mouth. Perianth with 2 sharp lateral keels, keels strongly winged (wing 127-154 µm wide) comprising approximately 30% of perianth width; keels smooth. Dorsal surface of perianth plane and smooth, ventral surface smooth, gibbous. Gynoecial innovations absent. Androecia of short branches bearing 2-4 pairs of hypostatic bracts, bracteoles present throughout. Antheridia not seen. Sporophytes not seen.

description: Plants filamentous, in light yellow-green tufts or mats; stems 3-4 cm lonig, more or less radial, often erect, densely leafy above, regularly bi- or tripinnate, the lateral branches long, the half-leaf bifid; ventral branches occasional, leafy or with smaller leaves for some distance and becoming densely leafy above; stems in transverse section with a cortical layer of 18-12 large cells surrounding a medulla of smaller cells; rhizoids from the bases of the underleaves and the female branches; stem leaves distant to approximate, rectangular to obeuneate in outline, divided to two-thirds or four-fifths their length into mostly 4 (sometimes 5 or 6) uniseriate segments of 4 or 5 cells, the segments often curved, the basal cells averaging 73 µ X 21 µ, the lamina two cells high at the margin and 3 or 4 cells high between, or 1 cell high at the margin and 2 or 3 cells high between, usually 8 (-10, -12) cells across, the cells quadrate to rectangular in outline, thin-walled, the cuticle smooth; underleaves similar, the segments 4 or 5 cells long, the lamina mostly 2 cells high throughout, 8 (-10, -12) cells across; branch leaves and underleaves with 1 or 2 fewer segments; plants dioicous; female inflorescence terminal on a leafy branch, more rarely on a short ventral branch, the bracts and bracteoles similar, in 4 series, the outermost series quadrified to one-half their length, the intermediate series divided to one-third into 4 segments, with a few short cilia on the margins, the innermost series divided to one-halft their length into segments; perianth long, cylindrical, the upper part contracted, with three rounded keels above, the mouth long ciliate with simple cilia; capsule oval, brownl, the seta with an outer row of 16 large cells surrounding many smaller cells; male infloreseence not seen.

description: These plants are much smaller than is usual for the species. The stems are delicate, and the leaves and underleaves are bifid and very small, a condition that one might expect to find on branches of depauperate plants. However, these plants do not appear to be depauperate. The leaf segments are uni-seriate from the base or from a "lamina" half a cell high and three or four cells wide (one or two cells-under each segment) as in T. sejuncta, but the cells are shorter, only up to 49 µ long, and only about half as long as usual for the species, although there is considerable variation in the length between the cells of one segment and between leaves of different plants of the latter.

description: Plants small, 9 mm long, 0.5-0.8(-0.9) mm wide, pale green to yellowish brown when dry, bearing conspicuous dark red spots, loosely creeping. Branches of Lejeunea-type. Stem suborbicular in cross section; cortex a hyalodermis of 7-8 outer rows of cells surrounding 9 inner rows of smaller medullary cells; ocelli scattered only among the dorsal cells of the cortex; ventral merophytes 2 cells wide. Leaf lobes ovate, wide spreading, 370-440 µm long, 300-350 µm wide, contiguous to subim- bricate, convex, the apex rounded, recurved, the margin entire; cells subquadrate to rectangular, 10-15 X 15-29 µm, with uniformly thickened walls, lacking trigones, the surface smooth, the cuticle smooth. Lobule ovate, inflated, 1/3 of leaf length, 1.2X longer than wide, 150-190 µm long, 100-140 µm wide; keel convex; margin free, formed by 4 long cells, involute at base and flattened at apex; apex truncate, with a blunt, 1-celled tooth and hyaline papilla on inner side of apical margin, the papilla-bearing cell distal to the tooth. Underleaves entire, orbicular to subquadrate, small, 120-150 µm long, 115- 165 µm wide, 1.2-1.5X stem width, usually as long as wide, the apex truncate to weakly retuse, the insertion line straight to shallowly curved. Ocelli scattered in leaf lobes, lobules, and underleaves, reddish to pale brown, sometimes becoming hardly discernible, but sometimes very clear even in herbarium condition. Gynoecia on short branches, without innovation, the bracteole obovate, entire, the apex rounded, the female bract damaged. Androecia and perianths unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Ilkiu-Borges, Anna L. 2002. Pictolejeunea reginae, a new species of Lejeuneaceae (Hepaticae) from Venezuela. Brittonia. 54: 318-321.

description: Plants slender, deep brown, in tufts or among other bryophytes; stems more or less erect and radial, 4-5 cm long, irregularly branched and bearing long, brown, often branched stolons; lateral branches of the Frultania and Microlepidozia types; ventral branches axillary, interealary, leafy, or flagelliform, or long stolons, or lighter in color, enlarged, turgid with small leaves and long internodes (eventually bearing a female inflorescence); stems in transverse section with 12 longitudinal rows of cortical cells, larger and with thicker walls than the cells of the medulla; leaf insertion transverse; leaves distant to approximate, erect-spreading, up to 0.5 mm long and wide, cuneate, quadrifid to onehalf their length, the segments triangular, more or less divergent, often somewhat ineurved, 6-8 (-10) cells broad at the base, the cells averaging 18 µ x 18 µ, the margins of the lamina entire or occasionally with a small tooth near the base; cells of the lamina averaging 25 µ x 18 µ, the walls uniformly thickened, the trigones unconspicuous, the cuticle faintly verruculose; underleaves similar, scarcely smaller; plants dioicous; male infloreseence forming a short ventral branch, or terminal, or beeoming interealary on a longer ventral branch, the bracts and bracteols in 5-10 series, the bracts bifid or trifid, with 1-2 antheridia, the bracteoles bifid, plane; female infloreseence (only one, immature), terminating a ventral leafy branch, the stem below the perianth enlarged, turgid, with small distant leaves and underleaves, the outer series of bracts and bracteoles (immature) lobed above, the inner series broadly rounded, scarcely lobed; perianth and sporophyte not seen. The distinguishing characteristics of this species are its dark brown color, radial symmetry, long brown stolons, the spreading leaves and underleaves with the segments 5-10 cells across at the base, and the cortical layer of 12 cells in the transverse section of the stem.

description: Plants very slender, in tufts or among other bryophytes, dark brown, the growing tips and branches often greenish to whitish; stems more or less erect, radial, to 2-4 cm long, irregularly branched and bearing long brown to colorless stolons; lateral branches of the Frultania and Microlepidozia types; ventral branches interealary, as long stolons, or flagelliform, or leafy, or enlarged, turgid, lighter in color and bearing a female infloreseence; stem in transverse section of 12 longitudinal rows of cortical cells, larger and with thicker walls than those of the medulla; leaf insertion transverse; leaves and underleaves distant to approximate, erect-spreading cuneate, 0.42-0.48 mm long, 0.36 mm wide at the middle, quadrifid to one-half or two-thirds the length, the segments longlanceolate, divergent, straight, 4 cells broad at the base, the cells 27-36 µ x 18-22 µ, the walls uniformly thickened, the trigones inconspicuous, the cuticle faintly verruculose; plants dioicous; male infloreseence on a short ventral branch, the bracts and bracteoles in 5 or more series, the bracts concave, the bracteoles plane, the antheridia 1-2 in the axils of the bracts; female inflorescence terminal on a long flagelliform branch ending in an enlarged turgid tip, the bracts in 3 series, quadrate to broadly orbicular in outline, the apical portion variously incised into short segments, the lateral margins with an occasional tooth; perianth mouth (undeveloped) undivided; sporophyte not seen.
