description: Plants filiform, dark brown to blackish, in tufts or among other bryophytes; stems slender, more or less erect and radial, to 2-3 cm long, irregularly branched and bearing numerous long stolons; lateral branches of the Frullania and Microlepidozia types; ventral intercalary branches as long stolons with scale leaves and tufts of rhizoids; or long and flagelliform; or leafy and branched; or lighter, enlarged, turgid, with small leaves and long internodes (eventually with a female inflorescence); stem in transverse section with a single layer of 12 rows of larger cortical cells with thicker walls; leaf insertion transverse; leaves and underleaves distant to approximate, synmmetrical, ascendant, ineurved above, cuneate, quadrifid to one-half their length, to 0.36 mm long, 0.27 mm wide at the middle, the segments mostly 4 cells broad at the base, 6-8 cells long, the cells 18 µ x 18 µ, the walls uniformly thickened, the trigones scarcely developed, the cuticle faintly verruculose; plants dioicous; male infloreseence on a short ventral branch or terminal on a longer branch, the bracts and bracteoles in 3-6 series, the bracts mostly trifid, concave, with a toothed lateral margin, the bracteoles bifid, the antheridia 1 or 2 in the axils of the bracts; female infloreseence o0l a short (sexual) branch, or a flagelliform, or leafy ventral or a lateral branch, or the stem, with or without an enlarged turgid axis below, or terminal oln an enlarged turgid ventral branch, the bracts and bracteoles in 3-4 series, tending to be keeled, the outermost series quadrifid to one-fourth their length, the bracts of the iirnermost series broadly ovate with scattered marginal teeth and lobes, the cells thin-walled; perianth to 3 mm long, cylindrical below, contracted and 3-keeled above, the mouth crenulate; the shoot / sporophyte relationship a shoot-calryptra with the unfertilized archegonia on stem tissue around the base of the capsule; the foot cone-shaped, the collar distinct; mature sporophyte not seen. The dark color and small size, the narrow ineurved segmlents of the leaves and underleaves, and the many long stolons will serve to separate this species from others of a similar size and habitat. Stems with both the Frtllania and the Microlepidozia types of terminal branching are frequent and the accompanying half-leaves are conspicuous (Fig. 83).

description: Trees with spiny branches. Leaves 5-7-foliolate, petioles 75-220 mm, leaflets 70-160 x 30-56 mm, elliptic-oblong, acute at apex, decurrent-cuneate at base, glabrous on adaxial surface, glabrous or glabrate or with sparse hairs or glandular papillae on abaxial surface, subsessile on petiolules 3-10 mm long. Flowers borne singly near stout branch tips. Pedicels ca. 17 mm, robust. Calyx ca. 22 mm long, cupuliform, glabrous externally, villous within, apex lobed to 7 mm. Petals ca. 120 x 18 mm, linear-oblong, externally and internally stellate tomentose, reflexed at anthesis. Staminal tube without articulation, ca. 45 mm long, sparsely hairy, with filamentous lobes ca. 40 mm long; upper anther thecae are sessile (free for 4-5 mm of their 11-12 mm length), the lower pair sessile for only about half their length (18-20 mm) and then free, divergent, often spiralled. Ovary densely hairy. Fruit unknown.

description: Tree, 20 m tall, 55 cm diam; wood described in Miller (1991). Stipules 11-18 (26) mm long, 4-8 mm wide, densely tomentose with golden, echinate-fasciculate trichomes; petioles 5-12 cm long, tomentose as the stipules; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, (9) 24-27 cm long, (8) 15-16 cm wide, at base deeply cordate with lobes 8-28 mm deep, at apex obtuse to broadly acute, coriaceous or subcoriaceous, pale yellowish-green (when dry) and nearly glabrous or tomentulose above, dull oli- vaceous-green (when dry) and tomentose below with an indument of golden, echinate trichomes (Fig. 2A); veins to quatemary order prominent below, forming a very conspicuous reticulum; basal veins palmate, 7-9 (including the midvein but not including the 1 or 2 lowermost pairs of obsolete, marginal veins), the upper 2 pairs of basal veins and the 3 or 4 pairs of pinnate secondary veins brochidodromous. Pedicels of flowers 16-33 mm long, 2- or 3-bracteolate; brac- teoles linear-lanceolate, 9-15 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, the lower pair subequally  inserted ca 1/3 of pedicel length above its base, the upper bracteole at ca 2/3 its length; calyx conical to narrowly campanulate, broadly lobed at summit, 35-52 mm long, 11-20 mm diam, densely tomentose with golden, echinate-fasciculate trichomes without; petals spathulate, 60-70 mm long, 18-26 mm wide, pale yellow, pubescent with pale stellate trichomes; staminal column 75-87 (96) mm long (including the five 22-32 mm long apical lobes), tomentose to densely tomentose with golden, stellate trichomes and scattered, brown, uniseriate, multi- cellular, trichomes; thecae ca 30, straight or vermiform, to 12 mm long, 1 mm wide or less, with many foveae per locule; style filiform, equal or subequal to the anther lobes, densely tomentose; stigma capitate, glabrous. Fruit (perhaps immature?) ellipsoid, 45-52 mm long, ca 32 mm diam, at apex depressed and bearing an apiculate tip; exocarp golden-brown, densely tomentulose; pedicel of fruit 30 mm long; calyx of fruit deep-cupulate, 42-52 mm long, 40 mm diam, covering ca 3/4 of the fruit, at margin lobed as when in flower.
bibliographicCitation: Alverson, William S. 1991. A synopsis of Phragmotheca (Bombacaceae), with two new species and a new sub-species. Brittonia. 43: 73-87.

description: Arbor 5-27 m alta. Folia alterna; petioli 7-40 mm longi; laminae ellipticae vel late ellipticae vel obovatae vel late obovatae, integrae, membranaceae, 5-29 cm longae, 3-16 cm latae, (nervulis submarginalibus tenuibus neglectis) e basi 3- vel 5-nerviae; nervi secundarii pinnati brochidodromi, utroque latere 5-10. Flores parum zygomorphi; pedicelli in alabastro 2- vel 3-bracteolati, sub anthesi ebracteolati, 6-12 mm longi; calyx tubulosus vel conicus, 21-31 mm longus; petala 5, spathulata, lutea, 36-40 mm longa, 5-8 mm lata; columna staminalis 37-44 mm longa; lobi staminales 5, lineares, 8-10 mm longi; thecae 20-25, foveatae; foveae paucae vel multae; ovarium 5-loculare. Fructus drupacei, ellipsoidei vel parum obovoidei, 35-90 mm longi, 35-40 mm diametro, plerumque 5-spermi.

description: Tree, 5-27 m tall; trunk orthotropic (sensu Halle et al., 1978), monopodial, 10- 25 cm DBH, producing whorls of 5 horizontal (plagiotropic) branches at regular intervals of 1-2 m, only 1-3 branches persisting at older whorls; young branches tomentose with ferrugineous, echinate trichomes, soon glabrate, rugose, gray or rufous-gray; outer bark ca 12 mm thick, slightly roughened with small verrucae, greenish-gray, bearing scattered, raised, horizontal ridges (expanded leaf scars?) and many, pale lenticels, these 1-2 mm diam; inner bark fibrous, the outer half dark brown, the inner half pale brown with conspicuous rays; wood described in Miller (1991). Stipules linear-lanceolate, 7-19 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, densely tomentose as the young twigs; petioles 7-40 mm long, rugulose, densely echinate- tomentulose; leaf blades elliptic to broadly elliptic, or obovate to broadly obovate, 5-23 (29) cm long, 3-16 cm wide, at base widely rounded or truncate, occasionally cuneate or subcordate (with lobes to 3 mm deep), at apex rounded and sometimes briefly caudate, stiff-membranous, sublustrous, medium to dark green (when fresh) and glabrous or with few, scattered, stellate trichomes above, medium green and sparsely to densely tomentose with golden-brown stellate trichomes below (Figs. 2C, D), or less commonly with peltate-stellate trichomes (in Ecuadorian and some Peruvian specimens); veins to tertiary order prominent below, together with qua- ternary veins forming a reticulum; basal veins palmate, 3-5 (including the midrib but not including the lowermost pair of obsolete, marginal veins); secondary veins (those above all palmate basal veins) pinnate, 5-10 per side, brochidodromous, sometimes barbate (i.e., bearing domatia in the axils formed with the midrib below). Flowers (Fig. 5B) borne on young branches; pedicels 6-12 mm long, apparently ebracteolate at time of flowering; bracteoles 2 or 3, linear-lanceolate, 7-15 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, deciduous from the young buds; calyx tubular to conical, sometimes asymmetric, 21-31 mm long, 7-12 mm diam, broadly 3-5- lobed at summit, dark olivaceous- to ferrugineous-brown, densely tomentose with echinate and echinate-stellate trichomes without; petals spathulate, 36-40 mm long, 5-8 mm wide, at apex bluntly acute or emarginate, recurved or spreading, yellow, nearly glabrous to densely pilose with white, long-rayed stellate trichomes within, densely tomentose with shiny, golden-brown, echinate trichomes without; staminal column (37) 43-44 mm long (including the apical lobes), 1-2 mm diam, creamy yellow (fresh), glabrous or with few, scattered, uniseriate, multicellular trichomes on the lobes and distal portion of the tube; staminal lobes 5, linear, 8- 10 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, recurved, actinomorphic, bearing the thecae on their abaxial surface; thecae 20-25, straight or vermiform, the uppermost parallel, paired, to 7 mm long, the lower mostly less than 5 mm long, all less than 1 mm wide, each bearing few to ca 50 foveae in each of two overlapping, parallel series (each series corresponding to one of the two lateral locules of the theca, Fig. SC); style filiform, zygomorphic, longitudinally 5-sulcate, ca 49 mm long, 1.5 mm diam, exceeding the staminal tube by ca 14 mm, greenish-yellow, densely to- mentose with golden-brown, echinate, trichomes; stigma zygomorphic, 2-3 mm tall, ca 1 mm diam. Fruit ellipsoid to slightly obovoid, 35-90 mm long, 35-40 mm diam, the apex briefly (3 mm) to extremely (20 mm) mammilate and often apiculate; exocarp coriaceous-fibrous, ca 2 mm thick, longitudinally finely striate or rugulose when dry, matte brown to olivaceous-brown, yellowish-brown or pale orange, densely tomentulose with tiny echinate trichomes; mesocarp densely fibrous, relatively thin (<3 mm), pale brown, only slightly moist, without con- spicuous odor or taste in fresh but slightly unripe fruits; endocarp bony-fibrous, 2-4 mm thick, persistent around seeds; pedicel of fruit 9-16 mm long, 3-8 mm thick, ebracteolate; calyx of fruit shallowly cupulate, 18-25 mm long, 35-45 mm diam at apex, covering at most the basal 1/4 of fruit, medium to dark brown or golden-brown, sometimes with many, pale, lenticel-like verrucae, the apical margin straight and entire or slightly erose (the calyx lobes apparently deciduous); seeds ca 23 mm long, 5-8 mm diam, consisting mostly of 2 nearly equal cotyledons. Seedlings (Fig. 5D) cryptocotylar and epigeal (of "durian morphology" sensu Ng, 1978), i.e., the cotyledons achlorophyllous, retained within testa and endocarp, held 3-4 cm above the soil surface; hypocotyl stout, bearing an irregular, ovate, lateral projection near ground level; cotyledons, testa, and endocarp eventually deciduous to expose a shoot meristem at apex of seedling.

description: Tree to 27 m tall. Petioles 7-35 mm long; leaf blades elliptic to broadly elliptic or slightly obovate, 5-16 (29) cm long, 3-11 (16) cm wide, non-barbate or slightly barbate beneath. description: Arbor 10-40 m alta. description: Tree, 10-40 m tall; trunk irregular in cross-section and deeply ribbed or grooved, to 3 m diam, bearing large buttresses; main branches produced in whorls of 5, ascending at a shallow angle. Stipules lanceolate, 4-6 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, densely lepidote with dull brown, peltate trichomes; petioles 54-62 mm long, tomentose with echinate and peltate-stellate trichomes; leafblades of reproductive individuals ovate to broadly elliptic, occasionally subobovate, 13-19 cm long, 8- 16 cm wide, at base truncate to subcordate (the lobes to 10 mm deep), at apex rounded to broadly acute, coriaceous, sublustrous and olivaceous-brown above when dry, dull and of a similar color when nearly glabrous below, or pale, matte, olivaceous-brown when tomentose below with golden, echinate-stellate trichomes (Fig. 2F); leaf blades of saplings and sterile sub-adults often larger and more elongate than those described above, often greenish and fuzzy to the touch below due to the presence of long, stellate trichomes on the veins and the absence of the dense indument of golden, echinate-stellate trichomes that characterize the adult leaves; veins to tertiary order prominent below, forming a conspicuous reticulum; basal veins palmate, 3-7 (including midvein), the lowermost pair much weaker than the acutely-ascending upper pairs; secondary veins (above the palmate basal veins) pinnate, 4-7 per side, brochidodromous. Pedicel of flower ca 6 mm long, ebracteolate at time of flowering, bearing three 1-1.5 mm wide bracteole scars at the junction of the calyx and the pedicel; calyx conical to broadly tubular, 12-14 mm long, 6-7 mm diam, irregularly 3-5-lobed at summit with 1-5 mm long triangular lobes, green, densely tomentulose on outer surface with ochraceous trichomes; petals spathulate, 16-18 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, the apex obtuse or rounded, sometimes emarginate, orange or "intense yellow" (Neill et al. 7577), pubescent with pale stellate trichomes on both faces; staminal column 20-25 mm long (including the 4-8 mm long apical lobes; Fig. 1 B), the proximal half sericeous with pale, pauciradiate-stellate trichomes, the distal half with an indument of scattered, brown, uniseriate, multicellular trichomes over a surface covered with ochraceous, granular tissue (especially on the lobes between the thecae); thecae linear, varied in number and size, typically ca 22, 1.5-2.5 mm long, ca 0.5 mm wide, borne 4 or 5 per lobe on the lateral margins of the lobes, each bearing 3 to 6 foveae in each of two parallel series (each series corresponding to 1 of the 2 lateral locules of the theca), sometimes showing increased fusion and then ca 15, to 6 mm long, borne 1-2 per lobe, each bearing 20-30 foveae (Fig. 1B); style filiform, subequal to the staminal lobes, the portion exsert beyond the staminal tube densely tomentose with pale, stellate trichomes; stigma apparently 5-sulcate or briefly 5-lobed. Fruit broadly ovoid to broadly ellipsoid, 28-39 mm long, 24- 43 mm diam, tapering to a 4-6 mm mammilate apex; exocarp pale, matte-brown and finely longitudinally striate when dry, densely lepidote with peltate-fimbriate trichomes; mesocarp and endocarp typical for genus; pedicel of fruit seemingly short (less than 10 mm) but relatively thick (4-7 mm diam), ebracteolate; calyx of fruit shallowly cupulate, 8-13 mm high, 24-35 mm diam, covering the basal 1/4 of fruit at most, medium brown, glabrate, its margin erose or irregularly toothed; seeds 18 mm long, 5-9 mm diam, retained within persistent endocarp and mesocarp tissue to form a dispersal unit 25-30 mm long, 10-15 mm diam.

description: Tree. Stipules 10 mm long, 3-4 mm wide; petioles 47-86 mm long; leaf blades elliptic to slightly obovate, 21-29 cm long, 9-14 cm wide, at base subcordate, truncate, or rounded, at apex attenuate or cuspidate, thick-membranous, subscabrous, green with a brownish tinge (especially below) due to peltate-stellate tri- chomes (Fig. 2B); veins to tertiary order protruding conspicuously below, the higher order veins forming an inconspicuous reticulum; basal veins palmate, 5 (including midvein but not including the lowermost pair of obsolete, marginal veins), the upper pair very strong; secondary veins (above the palmate basal veins) pinnate, 4 or 5 per side, brochidodromous. Flowers unknown. Fruit depressed globose, 8 cm long, 9-10 cm diam, bluntly mammilate at apex; exocarp densely tomentose with ferrugineous-ochraceous, fasciculate trichomes; endocarp together with persistent inner layers of the mesocarp ca 1 cm thick, bony-fibrous (cf. Fig. 3 in Cuatrecasas, 1971); pedicel of fruit 22-35 mm long, slender, ebracteolate; calyx of fruit shallow-cupuliform, 5-7 cm diam, at margin entire; seeds angular in cross-section, elongate-pyriform, 30 mm long, 8-17 mm diam; testa thin, membranous, reddish-brown.

description: Plants perennial, leaves and stems moderately to densely pubescent; trichomes stellate, the rays (3)6-25(30), symmetrically disposed, or asymmetrically, forming a U-shaped notch (Fig. 1), bases free or fused; taproots woody, simple or branched, to 50 cm long and more; caudices woody, simple to elaborately branched, slender to enlarged, ascending to decumbent or rarely stoloniferous, 0.5-11 cm long (up to 17 cm in erect and 22 cm in stolon); basal leaves 0.5-9 cm long and 0.3-2.5 cm wide, the blades lanceolate to elliptic to oval, obovate, deltate, lyrate, or orbicular, merging gradually to abruptly with the winged petiole, margins entire to remotely dentate or sinuate, leaves broadening with age and turning purple or gray in senescence; fruiting stems ascending, 5-40(76) cm tall, few to several from each caudex branch; cauline leaves 0.5-4 cm long, 2-6 mm wide, entire, elliptic, sessile or short-petiolate; in- florescences dense, buds ellipsoid; sepals pubescent, at anthesis 4-7 mm long; petals 7-14 mm long, white or yellow, the white ones yellowing upon drying, the yellow ones fading, the region of the midvein reflecting near-ultraviolet for the proximal half of its length, fluorescing yellow in long-wave ultraviolet upon drying; paired stamens 6-11 mm long, single stamens 4-8 mm long; pollen elliptical to orbicular, often both pentacolpate and hexacolpate in the same anther; infructescences dense, subcorymbose to racemose and occasionally elongated; description: Perennial with tap-root, rosulate, completely covered with trichomes except for the inner surface of sepals, petals, stamens, and styles; trichomes stellate, the rays mostly forked and fused towards the center; caudex simple, the stems erect, to 1 dm high, arising from below terminal rosette; leaves of rosette erect and curled from the middle of the leaf to the tip, silvery, entire, petiolate, (1.5) 5-7 cm long; cauline leaves 1-5 per stem, oblanceolate, entire, 1-2.5 cm long; inflorescence compact to elongate in fruit, to 1 dm long, the pedicels divaricately ascending, slightly curved, 0.7-1.8 cm long; sepals erect, oblong to linear, 5.5-7 mm long, the outer pair usually more saccate than inner pair; petals spathulate, yellow, not differentiated into a definite blade and claw, 10-14 mm long, 3-4 mm wide; filaments of stamens ca 7 mm long, the anthers oblong, 2 mm wide, not constricted; silique didymous, highly inflated at maturity, 1-1.8 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, with a deep apical sinus, basal not as deep; valves with elliptical orifice; styles 4-6 mm long, glabrous; stigma capitate; replum obovate, obtusely angled at apex, 4-5 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, not constricted; ovules 4 (2-6 for some fruits) in each loculus; seeds oblong to elliptic, brown, thin-margined or not, remaining in the valves after fruit drops, 3-4 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide.

description: Perennial with a long tap-root; caudex simple, enlarged, covered with old leaf- bases, usually buried; leaves rosulate and flat to somewhat ascending, forming a dense crown at apex of the caudex, silvery from a dense covering of stellate trichomes, entire to obscurely few-toothed, 1.5-3.5 cm long, 6-10 mm wide, blade broadly obovate or deltoid to ovate or narrower, usually obtuse but nearly acute in narrower leaves, abruptly to gradually narrowed to a slender petiole; flowering stems few, decumbent, arising laterally from below current season's leaves, 3-8 cm long; cauline leaves 2-5 per stem, entire, oblanceolate to spatulate, nearly petiolate to cuneate at base and acute at apex; flowers 3-6 per stem; sepals erect at anthesis, narrowly oblong to linear, 7-9 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, outer pair slightly saccate, inner pair nonsaccate; petals erect, yellow, spatulate, 10-12 (15) mm long, 4-5 (7) mm wide; stamens strongly tetradynamous, erect; anthers oblong, ca 2 mm long; fruiting pedicels widely spreading to ascending, 7-11 mm long, slightly curved to straight; siliques didymous, coriaceous, not highly inflat- ed, densely pubescent but not silvery, usually purplish when mature, obtuse to truncate below, with a broad sinus to nearly truncate above; valves irregular and somewhat angular, shallowly grooved distally and on the sides, tapered and nar- rowed toward replum, 6-9 mm high, orifice obovate to broadly oblong, 2.5-4 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide; styles glabrous, 5-7 mm long; replum elliptical to obovate, rounded above and below, 2.5-4 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, margin sparsely pu- bescent or glabrous, funiculi at apex of replum; ovules 2 in each loculus; seeds wingless, 1 or 2 in each loculus, nearly orbicular in outline to slightly longer than broad, 2.5-3 mm diam; cotyledons accumbent; radicle slightly exceeding coty- ledons.

description: Small tree, reproductive height 5-15 m; branchlets with a whitish cast, somewhat fleshy (wrinkled when dry), 2.5-3.5 (4.5) mm diam. at 2 cm from apex, with whitish to yellow, short, appressed, simple hairs to 0.15 mm long, soon glabrescent. Leaves 3-4 jugate, 25-45 (50.5) cm long; base markedly pulvinate, fleshy (wrinkled when dry); pet- iole longer than interjuga, 4.6-12 (15) cm x (1.4) 1.6-2.6 mm, glabrous; interijuga long, (2.9) 4-5.8 (7.5) cm long; petiolules long, lateral ones 0.7-1.5 (2) cm, terminal one 3.4-4.5 (6) cm, all with markedly swollen pulvinuli at both ends, interpetiolular region usually swollen also, pulvinuli with whitish cast below; leaflets (narrowly) elliptic (terminal one sometimes obovate), char- taceous, glabrous, basal pair (6.4) 10.6-13 x (2.5) 3-5.2 cm, ultimate pair (7) 11.9-14 (17) x 2.5-5.2 cm, terminal (7) 9.5-12.7 (15.1) x (2.6) 3-5.2 cm, leaflet base obtuse to acute, subequal to slightly oblique (lat- erals), apex long-acuminate, acumen 0.9- 1.6 cm; on both surfaces primary and secondary veins prominent, higher order veins prominulous. Panicles subterminal, lax, long and slender, (9) 15-30 cm x 0.9-1.4 mm, exceeding the petiole, secondary axes (1.6) 2.8-13 cm long, all axes with scattered, appressed hairs to 0.15 mm long; inflorescences bracts lanceolate to ovate, acute to acuminate, those subtending inflorescence (when present) 0.8-1 mm, those on primary axes (0.25) 0.35-0.6 (0.7) mm, mostly fugaceous, those on secondary axes 0.25-0.4 mm; pedicel terete, long and slender, (0.7) 1.5-2.6 x 0.2-0.35 mm. Flowers functionally unisexual, dimorphic, 4-merous, at anthesis 1.4-1.8 mm long (petals reflexed); calyx shallowly cupuliform, 0.35-0.4 (0.5) x (0.85) 1.2-1.4 (1.6) mm overall, exceeded by disk in both sexes, lobes discrete and separated by a sinuous sinus, negligible or very broadly depressed-deltate, 0-0.15 (0.25) mm, glabrous; petals yellow to cream, ovate, 1.75-1.85 (2.25) x 1-1.25 mm, the apex broadly acute to obtuse with inconspicuous apiculum, abaxial surface glabrous, adaxial surface and margin short-papillate; stamens 8, in staminate flowers antepetalous stamens 1.15-1.25 mm long and antesepalous ones 1.25-1.5 mm long, anthers small, in dorsiventral view narrowly elliptic, in lateral profile obliquely rounded-deltate, 0.2-0.25 mm long; disk broad, 0.2-0.4 mm high x 0.25-0.45 mm thick; pistillode only slightly exceeding disk, 0.25- 0.3 x 0.35 mm overall, deeply depressed- ovoid, glabrous, provided with locules and reduced ovules, abruptly contracted into a 4-lobate stylode 0.1-0.15 mm long; in pis- tillateflowers staminodes level with the stigmas, all 1.15 mm long, rudimentary anthers in dorsiventral view obtuse-oblong with lobulate base, in lateral profile reniform, 0.25 mm long; disk 0.25-0.3 mm high x 0.25- 0.3 mm thick; pistil substipitate, 1 mm long, ovary ovoid, glabrous, contracted into a short thick style 0.1 mm long; stigmatal region 0.15 mm high, stigmas globose, oriented upward and outward. Fruiting pedicel terete, 3.5-5.5 (8) x 1.3-1.7 mm; fruit glo- bose, 1.7-2.1 x 1.7-2.1 cm, maturing red, ovary sessile (substipitate in immature fruit), surface glabrous and smooth (wrinkled when dry); arillate structure pulpy, covering all of pyrene except for a laterally elliptic area accounting for 1/5 of ventral surface and corresponding to funicular scar; pyrene 2 x 2 cm (Rodrigues 7377), the dorsiventral view essentially orbicular with truncate base, the lateral profile semi-orbicular on dorsal side and semi-ovate on ventral side with a shal- low subapical depression on ventral side, base obtuse, apex acuminate, pyrene slightly obtusely ridged along both sides, ventral surface with a shallow central vertical sulcus, site of funicle 5/6 distance to apex; cotyledons unknown.

description: Small tree 9-10 m hioh with trunk 15-25 cm in diameter; bark with whitish flat-topped ridges; yoLnng twigs fascicled-hairy to reddish glandular-pubescent, usually conspicuously lepidote; older twigs fascicled-hairy at tips, becoming puberulent and finally essentially glabrous; pith light brown; leaf of medium size, 42-44 cm long and 20 cm broad; petiole usually conspieuously lepidote; rachis reddish glanidular-villous or -pubescent, finally glabrate; leaflets 15-17 (or more?), rather thin, ovate-lanceolate to broadly oblong or ovate, 8-11 cm long and 3.5-5.5 cm wide, sessile or subsessile, rounded at base, abruptly or gradually acuminate at apex, finely and sharply serrate; upper surface with few scattered fascicled hairs and scattered glandular puberuleniee, the lower fascieled-hairy on all veins, sometimes also reddish glandular-pubescent on the midrib, inconspicuously lepidote; very youngest leaflets (3 mm wide) tomentose beneath but soon becoming merely fascicled-pubeseent; staminate catkins 15 cm long and 1.2 cm in diameter; flowers large, the floral bracts very short, obtuse, reduced to a wooly tuft on the back of the flower; stamens 85; appendage of the connective small, deltoid or narrowly deltoid, mostly pointed, not as broad as the loculi; old pistillate spike 7-8 cm lonig, with 5 flowers, their ovaries densely fascieledtomentose; sepals glabrate; stignmas short and broad; an abnormal pistillate branch with large hairy bracts sometimes present at the base of the pistillate spike; immature fruit unknown; mature fruit 5 cm long and 4.5 cm in diameter; husk shining, the hairs rubbed off in all specimens seen; nut blackish with many very narrow interconnecting sharp ridges and deep narrow furrows, 4.5 cm long and 3.4 X 3.1 cm in diameter.

description: Rhizome stout, erect to short-creeping, scales 2-5.5 mm long, bicolorous, sclerotized center reddish brown, surrounded by golden-yellow unsclerotized tissue. Leaves 0.6-3 m long or longer; petiole 1-1.5 cm wide at the base and scaly, generally longer than lamina, completely smooth throughout its length, straw-colored to light brown; rachis generally rough on the abaxial side. Lamina pedate (Fig. IA), at the central portion generally 1 -pinnate-pinnatifid (rarely more divided) (Fig. 1 B), at the lateral portions (basal pinnae) 3-pinnate-pinnatifid; the basal pinnae once divided to form a basal inferior pinnule. Penultimate segments (Fig. 1 C) alternate, opposite, or subopposite, sharply pinnatifid to pinnatisect, widely cuneate at the base, long-acuminate at the apex, glabrous or minutely pubescent beneath. Ultimate segments decreasing uniformly in length from the base to the apex of the penultimate segments (Fig. 1 D), the apex acute with sterile margins serrate, the costae and costules abundantly muricate with long projections (up to 1 mm long), covered mostly with deciduous golden-red hairs (few scales can be found); awns coriaceous on the adaxial side of the costae; ultimate segment  venation completely free with all veins forked, extending from costule to the margin; sinus narrowly acute and uniform; indusium entire; paraphyses present.

description: Shrubs or small trees, to S m high. Year- old branchlets yellow to reddish brown, not pruinose, glabrous; new branchlets green or yellow sometimes becoming reddish brown, glabrous or nearly so. Expanded leaf blades narrowly elliptic, 5-9 X 1-2.2 cm, serrulate or serrate, glabrous, glaucous abaxially; petioles 2-6 mm long; stipules lacking or to 12 mm long and deciduous. Aments pre- cocious or in axils of mature leaves. Sta- minate aments 1-2.5 cm long, sessile or on branchlets to 0.2 cm long; anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long. Pistillate aments 1-3 cm long, sessile or on branchlets to 0.4 cm long. Capsules 2-4 mm long, glabrous; styles 0.2-0.7 mm long; stipes 0.5-1.5 mm long. Floral bracts oblong to obovate, 1-2 mm long, brown (blackish brown), with dense hairs toward base, hairs sparse or none at tip.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 3-6 mm. lonig; blades more or less elliptic, 9.5-10 cm. long, 4.5-5.7 cm. broad, cuneate at base, abruptly short-acuminate and mucronulate at apex, chartaceous, 3-plinerved (midrib and inner principal nerves impressed above, the outer ones prominulous) with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 11-17 mm. from base. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles densely pubescent with fulvous curved hairs; blades beneath with very conspicuous crowded whitish atomic dots, sparsely pubes- cent on nerves and veinlets, more densely so on midrib, especially near base, above smooth and glabrous except for nerves that are sparsely pubeseenlt and for midrib that is densely pubescent, especially near base, leaf-margins sparsely ciliate. Infloreseences in axillary (and terminal) thyrses, up to 2 cm. long, rather densely pubescent with short adpressed curved fulvous hairs, bracts lanceolate and pubescent with subsetulose hairs, pedicels very short or Dlone; calyx-lobes ovate-lanceolate, about 1.3 mum. long, short-acuminate at apex, sparsely pubescent without, and ciliate; corolla-tube 0.7 cm. long, miinutely papillose and glabrous without, pilose within, densely so near throat, corolla- lobes papillose and glabrous without, densely bearded at base within, the indumentum continuous with that within corolla-tube; anthers sessiloid, hidden beneath wool on corolla-lobes; style pilose. Fruits not seen.

description: Liana ( ?), the branchlets slender, einereous, terete, lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles rugose, slender, 6-8 mm. long, the leafblades chartaceous or thin-coriaceous, elliptic-oblong, 6-9.5 cm. long, 2.54 cm. broad, acute at base, subacute or obtusely short-acuminate at apex, entire and narrowly revolute at margins, the costa prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-9 per side, ascending, interspersed with shorter similar nerves, anastomosing near margins, prominulous on both surfaces, the veinlets reticulate, prominulous or subimmersed; inflorescence 2-4.5 cm. long at anthesis, divided from base, pseudodichotomously several times branched, the branchlets slender, the bracts ovate, subacute, about 0.6 mm. long; flowers about 3 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, about 2 mm. long; sepals deltoid, 0.6-0.8 mm. long and broad, subacute and slightly thickened at apex, entire; petals obovate, 2-2.2 mm. long, 1-1.3 mm. broad, rounded at apex, entire or erosulous at margins, minutely farinosepuberulent on both surfaces; disk submembranous, about 0.4 mm. high, 1-1.3 mm. in diameter, slightly undulate at margin; stamens suberect, the filaments membranous, 0.5-0.6 mm. long, the anthers about 0.2 by 0.4 mm.; ovary depressed-subglobose, the style 0.2-0.3 mm. long, the stigmas spreading, about 0.3 mm. long, oblong, conspicuously bilobed, opposite the stamens; ovules 2 per locule, superposed.

description: Liana; branchlets slender, subterete; leaves opposite (rarely subopposite); petioles slender, 7-10 mm. long; leaf-blades thin-coriaceous, brownish when dried, lanceolate-elliptic, 8-11 cm. long, 1.7-2.5 cm. broad, acute at base and decurrent on the petiole, obtusely acute, entire and narrowly revolute at margins, the costa acutely elevated on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 7-9 per side, ascending, short, prominulous on both surfaces or essentially plane above, the veinlets usually immersed, sometimes faintly prominulous beneath; infloreseence 2-3 cm. long, thyrsoid-paniculate, several times branched, the peduncle straight, slender, 7-18 mm. long, the branchlets alternate or subop- posite, the bracts and bracteoles papyraceous, deltoid, subacute, about 0.5 mm. long; flowers subsessile; sepals semiorbicular-ovate, about 1 mm. long and broad, obtuse, minutely ciliolate; petals oblong-obovate, about 2 mm. long and 1.4 mm. broad; disk submembranous, suberect, about 0.3 mm. high and 1 mm. in diameter, entire or faintly undulate; filaments about 0.5 mm. long, the anthers about 0.2 by 0.4 mm.; ovary subtrigonous-globose, about 0.8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style faintly suleate, 0.3-0.4 mm. long, the stigmas spreading, deltoid, about 0.2 mm. long, subacute, alternate with stamens; ovules 4 per locule, in collateral superposed pairs; fruit (ex Gardner) the "size of a large apple," pyriform (ex Miers), stoutly peduneulate, contracted at both ends, the pericarp coriaceous and ligneous, about 8 mm. thick, finely granular, the seeds oblong, angular, about 3 cm. long and 2 cm. broad, imbedded in pulp.

description: Low shrub, probably becoming scandent, the branehes and branchlets usually cinereous, terete; leaves opposite (rarely subopposite); petioles very stout, rugose, 3-7 mm. long; leaf-blades coriaceous, brownish or olivaceous when dried, elliptic, (5-) 7-14 cm. long, (2-) 3-6 cm. broad, obtuse or subacute at base and decurrent on the petiole, rounded to subacute at apex, essentially entire and often narrowly revolute at margins, the costa stout, prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6-10 per side, areuate-aseending, often conspicuously raised on both surfaces, the veinlets usually immersed, sometimes faintly promin- ulous; infloreseence 2-5 cm. long, thyrsoid-paniculate, several times branched essentially from base, the branchlets alternate or pseudodichotomous, the bracts and bracteoles alternate or subopposite, papy- raceous, ovate, obtuse, less than 1 mm. long; flowers subsessile (pedicels less than 1 mm. long) ; sepals papyraceous, semiorbicular-deltoid, 0.7- 0.9 mm. long, 0.7-1.3 mm. broad, rounded at apex, subentire or ob- scurely fimbriate at margins; petals papyraceous, obovate-elliptic, 1.5- 2.6 mm. long, 1.3-2 mm. broad, conspicuously narrowed at base, rounded at apex, entire; disk thin-carnose, suberect, 0.4-0.7 mm. high, 1.2-1.7 mm. in diameter, conspicuously undulate at margin; stamens suberect, the filaments 0.7-1.1 mm. long, the anthers 0.3-0.4 by 0.5-0.7 mm.; ovary trigonous-conical, about 0.7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, often conspicuously suleate, the style stout, carnose, suleate, 0.5-0.8 mm. long, the stigmas deltoid, spreading, obtuse, alternate with stamens; ovules 2 per locule, superposed.

description: Liana; branchlets elongate, slender, terete, often slightly flexuose; leaves alternate (rarely subopposite toward apices of branchlets); petioles rugose, often conspicuously swollen at base, 2-8 mm. long; leaf-blades thin-coriaceous, brownish or dark green when dried, narrowly elliptic-oblong or lanceolate-elliptic, 8-16 cm. long, 1.7-5.5 cm. broad, obtuse to subattenuate at base and decurrent on the petiole, obtuse or subacute at apex, subentire or obscurely undulate-crenate and narrowly revolute at margins, the costa stout, prominent on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 6 or 7 per side, sharply ascending, elevated on both surfaces, the veinlets usually obscure and immersed, sometimes prominulous-reticulate beneath; infloreseence 1.5-6 cm. long, thyrsoid-paniculate (the main rachis not distinguishable), several times branched, the peduncle essentially none or very short, the branchlets alternate or pseudodichotomous, the bracts and bracteoles alternate, deltoid, subacute, about 1 mm. long, often fimbriate; flowers subsessile (pedicels to 0.7 mm. long at anthesis) ; sepals 5 (rarely 6), suborbicular-ovate, 0.4-1 mm. long, 0.9-1.2 mm. broad, obtuse or rounded, seariose and usually fimbriate at margins; petals 5 (rarely 6), spreading at anthesis, thin-carnose or submelm-branous, obovate or subspatulate, 1.7-3.5 mm. long, 1.2-2.6 mm. broad, conspicuously nar- rowed at base, rounded at apex, essentially entire at margins; disk thin- carnose or submembranous, erecto-patent, 0.2-0.6 mm. high, 1.2-1.5 mm. in diameter, undulate and conspicuously crenulate at margin; stamens 3 (rarely 4), the filaments 0.6-1.3 mm. long, the anthers 0.2- 0.4 mm. long, 0.5-0.7 mm. broad; ovary trigonous-depressed (rarely 4-angled), 0.6-0.8 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style often colnspicu- ously suleate, 0.4-0.5 mm. long, the stigmas 3 (rarely 4), spreading, deltoid, subacute, alternate with stamens; ovary-locules 3 (rarely 4), the ovules 2, collateral-superposed.

description: Frutex subscandens, glaber, ramis elongatis, teretibus, partibus ultimis 1-1.5 mm. diametro; foliis chartaceo-coriaceis, oblongis vel late oblongo- lanceolatis, perspicue subcaudato-acuminatis, basi rotundatis, leviter sed distincte cordatis, margine crebre serrato-dentatis, dentibus eirciter 0.5 mm. longis, vix 1 mm. distantibus, 10-12 cm. longis, 2.3-4 em. latis, olivaceis, utrinque subconcoloribus vel subtus paullo pallidioribus, primariis utrinque 7-8, subtus distinctis, elevatis, rectis vel leviter curvatis, fere inter margi- nem costamque utrinque venulam subundulatam longitudinalem efformati- bus; petiolo 6-9 mm. longo; spicis axillaribus, solitariis, 4-9 cm. longis, deorsum saepe subnudis, sursum multifloris, floribus 1-2 mm. distantibus; floribus viridibus vel pallide roseis, 5-6 mm. longis, bracteis 1.5-2 mm. longis, e basi ovatis longe acute acuminatis, bracteolis binis, ovatis, 2 mm. longis, subacutis vel obscure breviter acuminatis; sepalis 4, ellipticis, coneavis, rotundatis, 3 mm. longis; petalis 4, obovatis, rotundatis, eirciter 5 mm. longis et 3.5 mm. latis; staminibus 8, filamentis longioribus 2 mm. brevioribus 1.5 mm. longis; ovario ovoideo, 4-loculari; stylis eirciter 1 mm. longis, stig- matibus capitatis, 1 mm. diametro.

description: Liana, the woody stems at least 1 cm in  diameter, densely and persistently velutinous with the hairs 0.2-0.4 mm long, Y-shaped. Leaves decussate; lamina of larg- er leaves 19-28 cm long, 11.5-18 cm wide, broadly elliptical or more often obovate, broadly cuneate or rounded at base, distally obtuse or rounded and abruptly short-acuminate and often apiculate, eglandular on abaxial surface but bearing a series of small buttonlike glands on distal half of margin, adaxially relatively thinly but persistently velutinous with weak Y-shaped hairs that often collapse in age, abaxially densely and persistently velutinous with the hairs Y- to T-shaped and standing ca. 0.3 mm high, the lateral veins 10-15 and connected by many fine parallel cross-veins 2-4 mm apart, the lateral and cross-veins raised below, slightly impressed above; petiole 20-30 mm long, densely and persistently velutinous like stems, bearing at the apex a pair of swollen glands 1.5-2 mm in diam.; stipules borne on petiole 2-4 mm below apex, 3-5 mm long, curved or bent near middle, tapering from base to apex but more abruptly so in distal half, proximally persistently velutinous, distally subsericeous or glabrescent. Inflorescence a short compact velutinous axillary cyme of 3-7 4-flowered umbels, occasionally 2 cymes, one borne above the other; bracts and bracteoles ca. 1 mm long, broadly ovate, persistent; pedicel 16-25 mm long. Flowers with a "sweet, lemon-like aroma." Sepals 2-2.5 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, ovate, appressed in anthesis, abaxially se- riceous, adaxially glabrous, the anterior eglandular, the lateral 4 bearing 8 elliptical, apically slightly detached glands 3 mm long. Petals "bright yellow, with orangish-red line in middle, older petals pale yellow"; lateral 4 petals spreading to reflexed, with the claw 3 mm long and the limb 5.5-7 mm long, 7 mm wide, orbicular, eglandular, the ante- rior-lateral pair dentate at base and erose distally, the posterior-lateral pair distinctly dentate all around the margin; posterior pet- al with the claw 5 mm long and held nearly erect, the limb 3.5 mm long, 5 mm wide, reflexed, glandular-dentate all around the margin with the divisions short and terminating in small, subspherical glands. Stamens glabrous; filaments connate for ca. 1 mm at base; filaments opposite sepals ca. 3.5 mm long, that opposite anterior sepal erect and straight, the 2 opposite anteriorlateral sepals curved sideways toward posterior petal and inward to center of flower, the 2 opposite posterior-lateral sepals curved sideways toward stamen opposite posterior petal; filaments opposite petals (2) 2.5-3 mm long, always shorter than adjacent fila- ments, erect, straight; anthers 1.6-2 mm long, similar but those opposite sepals with the locules more pendent below insertion of filaments than those opposite petals, the connective bicolored, probably yellow with a reddish center. Ovary hirsute; styles ca. 3.5-4 mm long, sparsely sericeous or glabrate, the anterior slightly bowed outward, the posterior 2 curved strongly from base toward posterior petal and then back toward center of flower, all with a very short dorsal point at the apex. Samara butterfly-shaped; lateral wings membranous, 22-25 mm wide, 34-38 mm high, roughly semicircular, irregularly sinuous or shallowly lobed, thinly sericeous with all hairs fine, sessile, appressed; dorsal wing 1.5 mm wide, 5 mm high; nut globose, 4-5 mm in diam.

description: Liana, the woody stems at least 0.8 cm in diam., initially thinly and loosely sericeous with some hairs sessile but most raised on a short stalk much finer than the straight crosspiece, glabrescent in age. Leaves de- cussate; lamina of larger leaves 16-19 cm long, 7.5-11 cm wide, obovate, rounded at base, short-acuminate to rounded at apex, eglandular on abaxial surface but bearing a series of small buttonlike or short-cylindrical glands on distal half of margin, adaxially glabrous at maturity except velutinous at very base of midrib, abaxially persistently sericeous on midrib, thinly sericeous on lateral veins, otherwise very sparsely sericeous to glabrate, the lateral veins ca. 9 and connected by many fine parallel cross-veins 2- 4 mm apart, the lateral and cross-veins raised below, the finest reticulum visible above in dried leaves; petiole 8-15 mm long, densely and persistently sericeous abaxially, velutinous adaxially, bearing at or just below apex a pair of glands 1.5-2 mm in di- ameter; stipules borne on petiole 2-5 mm below apex, 2.5-5.5 mm long, often de- curved, tapering gradually from base to apex, sericeous or glabrescent. Inflorescence sericeous to subvelutinous, usually seeming to comprise 3 short-stalked 4-flowered um- bels side-by-side in each axil but actually a single cyme of 3 branches whose common stalk is ? completely suppressed; bracts and bracteoles triangular, persistent, the bracts ca. 1.5 mm long, the bracteoles ca. 1 mm long; pedicel 15-17 mm long, thickened at apex, thinly sericeous with fusiform, short- stalked hairs ca. 0.5 mm long. Sepals 2.5- 3.5 mm long, 2.5 mm wide, ovate, rounded at apex, fleshy, appressed in anthesis, abax- ially sericeous, adaxially glabrous, the anterior eglandular, the lateral 4 bearing 8 small flat elliptical glands 1.5-2 mm long. Petals yellow in bud, red in anthesis; lateral petals spreading, with the claw 2-2.5 mm long and the limb 5-6 mm long, 6-7 mm wide, subor bicular, eglandular, the anterior-lateral pair concave and erose, the posterior-lateral pair nearly flat and denticulate or dentate; posterior petal with the claw 3 mm long and held erect, the limb 4-5 mm long and wide, erect but distally bent forward, glandular dentate all around the margin except across the truncate base. Stamens glabrous; filaments free or connate up to 0.6 mm at base; filaments opposite sepals 3-3.5 mm long, that opposite anterior sepal erect and straight, the 2 opposite anterior-lateral sepals curved sideways toward posterior petal and inward to center of flower, the 2 opposite posterior-lateral sepals curved sideways toward stamen opposite posterior pet- al; filaments opposite petals 2-2.5 mm long, always shorter than adjacent filaments, erect, straight; anthers 1-1.5 mm long, the ante- rior 7 larger than the posterior 3, the connective yellow or, in most, proximally yellow and distally dark red. Ovary hirsute; styles 4-4.5 mm long, glabrous or bearing a few hairs proximally, the anterior erect and straight or slightly bowed outward, the posterior 2 moderately bowed toward posterior petal and then back toward center of flower, all with a short acute dorsal projection at the apex. Samara unknown.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 3-7 mm. long; blades elliptic or ovate to lanceolate, 5-14 cm. long, 2.5-6.5 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, usually aeute to short-acuminate at apex, usually shining on both surfaces, often drying a dull olive-ocher yellow, coriaceous or subcoriaceous, 3(5)-plinerved with the inner pair subopposite to conspicuously alternate and diverging at 0-12 mm. from base, reticulation usually intricate and prominent on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles sparsely or well puberulent with pale-rusty or grey, adpressed or suberect hairs, sometimes becoming glabrescent or glabrous in age; blades beneath with crowded whitish atomic dots and puberulent on midrib, often only at base (rarely with a tendency to obscure barbation in axils of the inner principal nerves), otherwise glabrous (scattered, very short hairs present), above tubereulate to smooth, sparsely puberulent on midrib near base, otherwise glabrous. Inflorescences in axillary, usually elongated thyrses, up to 3 cm. long (nodes of opposite eymes along rachis often distant), puberulent with adpressed or ascending, rusty hairs, pedicels about equal to or shorter than calyx; calyx-lobes ovate-lanceolate to somewhat oblong, up to 1.5 mm. long, subacute at apex, glabrous or sparsely puberulent without, ciliate; corollatube up to 0.6 cm. long, papillose and glabrous without, pilose within from near base up to throat, corolla-lobes papillose and glabrous without, densely papillose within and thickly bearded at base; anthers sessiloid, slightly exserted, less than 1 mm. long; style glabrous. Fruits (Smith 2278) immature, globose, about 1.5 cm. in diam., mucronate at apex, shell about 1 mm. thick, shining, smooth, minutely tuberculate; fruit-pedicels about 3 mm. in diam.

description: Rhizome ca. 1.5-2 cm diam., occasionally forking. Frond with droop-tip vernation; basal petiole scales narrow to long-lanceolate, chartaceous, light orangish yellow to light yellowish brown throughout or sometimes with a weakly developed and poorly delimited yellowish brown to deep yellowish brown center, conform, the cilia short to minute, flaccid; distal petiole scales similar; small petiole scales ovate-caudate, broad-lanceolate, or long lanceolate, orang- ish yellow. Lamina 15-45 cm long, 2-pinnate, attenuate, coriaceous, dull green adaxially when fresh; rachis without a proliferous bud, the rachis scales orangish yellow to light orangish yellow. Pinnae 6-12 X 1.1-2.7 cm, acute to acuminate, attached at right angles to rachis, the lowest pinnae often shorter than next distal, never longer; abaxial pinna-rachis scales mostly filiform, orangish yellow, rarely ciliate. Pinnules crenate, often attached at right angles, acute to obtuse, flat, the basal acroscopic pinnules longer than next distal, the basal basiscopic pinnules near lamina base shorter than next distal; veins all free; spinules usually developed on most vein tips. Sorus terminal on vein, the true indusium 0.9-1.3 mm diam., peltate, yellowish brown to pale orangish yellow.

description: Frutex vel arbor gracilis P. dulci et P. laevigatae affinis, foliorum laniinis ad margirieni conspicue et saepe profunde crenato-serratis, venulis utrinque prominulis, floribus paullo minoribus differt; a P. dulce laminis paullo latioribus, infloreseentiis thyrsoideo-paniculatis, ramulis alternatis glabris, a P. laevigata laminis paullo angustioribus, infloreseentiis brevioribus distinguitur.

description: Shrub or slender tree up to 4 m. high; branchlets often rugose, conspicuously lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, the petioles stout, rugose, 9-12 cm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceous, olivaceous or brownish when dried, narrowly elliptic-oblong, 10-21 cm. long, 4-7.5 cm. broad, obtuse to subattenuate at base and decurrent on the petiole, gradually acuminate at apex (acumen 8-12 mm. long, often obtusely callose-apiculate), conspicuously crenate-serrate, often deeply and conspicuously so (serrations 1 or 2 per centimeter) and slightly thickened at margins, the, costa prominent on both surfaces, the sec- ondary nerves 8-11 per side, spreading, ascending and conspicuously anastomosing toward margins, elevated on both surfaces, the veinlets reticulate and prominulous on both surfaces; infloreseence 1-3 cm. long at anthesis, divided essentially to base, compactly thyrsoid- paniculate, glabrous throughout, the branchlets alternate (suboppo- site distally), each subtended by an ovate subacute often fimbriolate bract about 1 mm. long; flowers loosely arranged in clusters of 2 or 3, 2-2.7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, each subtended by 1 or 2 minute bracteoles; sepals papyraceous, broadly ovate or suborbicular, 0.6-1 um. long, 1-1.3 mm. broad, rounded at apex, seariose and irregularly erosulous at margins; petals submembranous, oblong or elliptic- oblong, 1.5-1.8 mm. long, 1-1.2 mm. broad, often recurved, obscurely erosulous; disk submembranous, 0.3-0.4 mm. high, about 1.2 mm. in diameter, crenulate at margin; filaments membranous, 0.6-0.8 mill. long, gradually broadened toward base, with a conspicuous midnerve; anther-locules 0.3-0.4 mm. long, dehiscing by vertical extrorse-lateral clefts, the connective conspicuously thickened, obtuse, exceeding the locules by about 0.1 mm.; ovary about 0.7 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the style 0.2-0.3 mm. long; ovules 2 per locule, collaterally suspended.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Liana, the branehlets elongate, cinereous, terete, often lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles rugose, 8-11 mm. long, the leaf-blades thincoriaceous, elliptic-oblong, olivaceous when dried, 7.5-14 cm. lonig, 3.5-5 cm. broad, obtuse at base, conspicuously cuspidate at apex (acumen 5-10 mm. long, obtuse), subentire and narrowly revolute at margins, the costa slightly elevated above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 7-9 per side, spreading, anastomosing near margins, prominulous on both surfaces, the veiinlets reticulate and prominulous on both surfaces; inflorescence 1-2.5 cm. long at anthesis, pseudo-dichotomously branehed, the peduncle less than 5 mm. long or essentially none, the branehlets farinose-ceriferous, the bracts thin-coriaceous, appressed, ovate, obtuse, less than 1 mm. long; flowers subsessile, congested, about 1.3 mm. in diameter (slightly before anthesis) ; sepals thin-carnose, ovate-deltoid, 0.5-0.7 mm. long and broad, obtuse at apex, obscurely erosulous-fimbriolate at margins, minutely puberulent without; petals thin-carniose, suberect, oblonig-suborbicular, 0.6-0.8 mm. (probably to 1 mm. at anthesis) long and broad, rounded at apex, subentire or obseurely erosulous at margins, minutely farinose-puberulent distally without; disk thin-carnose, suberect, about 0.1 mm. high, undulatecrenulate at margins; stamens suberect, the filanments thin-carnose, very short, the anthers about 0.25 by 0.5 mm.; ovary depressed trigonous, obseurely connate to disk at angles, the style about 0.2 mm. lonig, the stigmatic shield subequally 6-parted, the stigmas opposite the stamens; ovules 2 per locule, superposed.

description: Rhizome scales 4-10 mm long, reddish to orangish (occasionally blackened at point of attachment), lanceolate, ciliate, spreading. Leaves to 110 cm long; petioles 10-40 cm long, 1/3-3/4 the length of the laminae; laminae widest at base or only slightly reduced; pinnae 13-24(-30) X (3.5-)4-6 cm, pairs 3-6(-7), alternate to subopposite, patent, broadly to narrowly elliptic, entire, the base cuneate, occasionally excavate basiscopically, sessile or nearly so, the stalks (when present) to 3 mm long, the apices acuminate; rachises not alate. Fertile pinnae 0.7-2 cm wide; paraphyses often present, consisting of branched, reddish, hair-like scales; annular cells 13-15; spores spiny, the spines 1/2 to as long as the spores.

description: Rhizomate late repente, gracile, paleis rufo-fer- rugineis, 3 mm. longis, 0.7 mm. latis, supra basin peltatis apice in caudam filiformem ciliatam proten- sis persistentibus subappresis vestito; stipitibus validis, 4-10 mm. longis, frondibusque squamulis nminutis albis stellatis deciduis aspersis; frondibus sterilibus 3-6 cm. longis, 7-12 mm. latis, basi rotundatis, apiee minoribus subacutis majoribus divaricato-lobatis, lobis 2-4, rigide coriaceis, aut planis aut margine revolutis, costa praecipue deorsum prominente; frondibus fertilibus apice repetiter dichotomis ramis palmatim divaricatis, hie solummodo soriferis; soris sine ordine eonfertis vel ob angustatem ramorum irregulariter uniseriatis, parvis, undis.

description: Plants with leaves, inflorescences and calyces densely stellate and dendroid- ferrugineous tomentose and glandular-granulose. Calyx lobes rounded to acute apically. Staminate inflorescence usually contorted; staminal tube 1.1-1.3 mm long. Pistillate inflorescence erect or rarely lax; free portion of the filaments 0.7- 0.9 mm long.

description: Frutices 2-20 dm alti, omnino glabri. Caules erecti, teretes, virides, simplices vel superne subramosi. Folia coriacea, oblanceolata usque obovata raro anguste elliptica, basi in petiolum attenuata, apice abrupte breviter acuminata raro acuta 5.8-17.6 cm longa et 1.9-6.6 cm lata, nervis lateralibus inconspicuis, petiolis 0.5-2 cm longis. Inflorescentiae axillares, dichasiales vel thyrsiformes, 1-3-trichotomae, pedunculis ascendentibus, 8-20 cm longis, bracteis ovatis usque late ellipticis, acuminatis, ses- silibus, 0.7-2.9 cm longis et 0.4-1.6 cm latis. Flores nutantes. Calyx 7-11 mm longus, persistens, lobis lanceolatis, ecarinatis, acuminatis, 5-9 mm longis et 1.5-2.5 mm latis margine membranaceis, tubo 1.5-3.5 mm longo. Corolla citrina, persistens, campanulato-tubulosa, leviter ventricosa, parte 1/3 inferiore constricta, tubo 2.7-3.6 cm longo et 0.8-1.1 cm lato, lobis recurvatis, ovati-lanceolatis, acuminatis, 12-20 mm longis et 5-7 mm latis. Stamina exserta, ad 2.1 cm tubum corollae excedentia, filamentis filiformibus, in tubo corollae leviter super apicem calycis insertis, 3-4 cm longis. Styli exserti, ad 2.7 cm tubum corollae excedentes. Capsula persistente corollaque marcescenti circumcincta, 14-16.5 mm longa, apice rostrata.
bibliographicCitation: Weaver, Richard E. 1970. A new Jamaican species of Lisianthus [L. adumsii] (Gentianaceae). Brittonia. 22: 11-13.

description: Suffrutex ad 5-8 (10) cm altus, pauciramosus. Ramuli dense breviter pilosi striati. Folia longe petiolata, petiolo 1-2 cm longo, dense breviter, piloso striato; laminae 3-6 cm longae, 1-1.3 cm latae, supra glabrae, infra dense breviter pilosae. Inflorescentia ad 0.6-1.0 cm longa. Pedunculus filiformis ad 3-5 cm longus. Stamina 3. Pistillum dense breviter pilosum. Stylus brevis crassus in fructo.
bibliographicCitation: Callejas, R. 1990. Studies in neotropical Piperaceae. II. Four new species and a new combination from Colombia and Peru. Brittonia. 42: 70-82.

description: Subshrub, 5-8 (10) cm tall, sparingly branched, the main stem and the branchlets 1.5-2.5 mm diam, internodes 0.5-1.2 (1.7) cm long, striate, glandular-dotted, the glands raised and prominent in fresh and dry condition, orange when dry, the dense, short indumentum of uniseriate 2- to 4-celled, soft, curly, whitish tri- chomes. Shoot apex emergent from within the prophyll and free from the leaf base at nodes subtending inflorescences. Leaves long-petiolate, the petiole 1-2 cm long, striate, glandular-dotted, densely short-pilose, with prominent stipular mar- gins that extend 3/4 of the petiole length, the margins caducous, thin-membranous. Lamina ovate to narrowly elliptic-lanceolate or obovate, 3-6 x 1-1.3 cm, apically short-acute to long-acuminate, basally obtuse to acute and long-decurrent, pinnately veined, the 2 or 3 pairs of secondary veins widely spaced, arising from the lower half of the midvein, raised on both sides, glandular-dotted throughout, glabrous above, short-pilose beneath along the veins, thin-membranous, chartaceous when dry, light green on both faces. Prophylls caducous, ovate, 2.5-3.5 mm long, apically obtuse to truncate, sparsely short-pilose, thin-membranous, green- ish. Inflorescences erect, white in flower, green in fruit; peduncle filiform, 3-5 cm long, glandular-dotted, glabrous; rachis 0.6-1 cm long, 1.5-2 mm diam in fruit, obscured by the flowers, ridged, glandular-dotted, densely short-pilose. Floral bracts triangular to narrowly deltoid as seen from above, 0.8-1.0 mm wide, marginally fimbriate, shortly white-pilose, centrally with prominent glandular dots, not forming bands around the spike. Flowers tightly congested, trimerous; anthers 0.1 mm long, 0.1-0.2 mm broad, laterally dehiscent, the connective protruding above the anthers and glandular-dotted at the apex; pistil with a short, conical style, densely short-pilose to glabrescent. Fruit triangular-ovoid to obovoid, 0.3-0.5 mm long, apically short-styled, glabrous, glandular-dotted, the glands raised.
bibliographicCitation: Callejas, R. 1990. Studies in neotropical Piperaceae. II. Four new species and a new combination from Colombia and Peru. Brittonia. 42: 70-82.

description: Subshrub to 1 m tall; stems greenish, evenly and densely glandular-pubescent and with some stellate hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long. Leaf blades ovate to ovate-lan- ceolate, sometimes elliptic, basally cuneate to rounded, crenate-dentate, apically acute to obtuse, 2.5-4.5 (6) cm long and 1-2 (3) cm wide, gradually reduced upward, somewhat discolorous, with pinnate venation, densely and evenly soft- pubescent above and beneath, the upper surface with uniform stellate hairs ca 0.3 mm in diam, the lower surface more densely covered with stellate hairs 0.3-0.5 mm in diam; petiole 4-15 mm long, with pubescence like that of the stem (or with relatively fewer glandular hairs and more stellate hairs). Pedicels solitary in the upper leaf axils, erect or ascending in flower, in fruit 2-4.5 cm long, slender, with pubescence like that of the stem, articulated 7-10 mm below the flower, slightly thicker and the hairs slightly longer above the articulation, the pedicels spreading to somewhat reflexed, the part above the articulation elongating somewhat and becoming reflexed; hypanthium (at least when dry) ferrugineous in at least some flowers; sepals 5, ovate-acuminate, imbricate in bud, 9-12 mm long at anthesis, deciduous, these and the hypanthium densely stellate-pubescent and with some glandular hairs on the outside; corolla campanulate [?], the petals 5, 1.3-2.5 cm long, cream-colored with maroon bases; corona ca 1 mm long, fim- briate; stamens 5, the filaments 6-7 mm long, the anthers brown, 2.5-3.5 mm long, sagittate, dehiscing longitudinally, the pollen yellow; styles 3, glabrous, slender, 1 cm long, the yellow lacerate stigmas exceeding the anthers by 3-4 mm. Fruits more or less pendant at maturity, ovoid, 7-12 mm long, 6-10 mm diam, obscurely tuberculate, 3-valved, dehiscent, hirsute with simple, bifurcate, and stellate hairs 0.5-1 mm long and with a few shorter glandular hairs; seeds white (immature) becoming dark brown, 2.5-3 mm long, narrowly clavate, slightly curved, reticulate-foveolate, partially covered by a membranous aril.
bibliographicCitation: Koch, Stephen D. & Fryxell, Paul A. 1989. A new species of Piriqueta (Turneraceae) from Oaxaca, Mexico, with a key to the Mexican species of the genus. Brittonia. 41: 109-112.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 1-6 mm. long; blades variable in shape, mllore or less elliptic, 5-13 em. long, 3-7 cm. broad, usually obtusely narrowed or cuneate and decurrent at base on petiole, rounded to obtuse or acute at apex, shilling above, the old ones usually drying a vivid ocher yellow, thick-coriace ous, 5 (7) -plinerved with the inner pair subopposite or conspicuously alter- nate and diverging at 5-20 mm. from base, reticulation intricate and very prominent above. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles very densely ful- vous-pubeseent with curved adpressed or somewhat matted hairs; blades be- neath densely and persistently fulvous-pubeseent with somewhat matted hairs and with fulvous tubercles (the bases of fallen hairs) hidden under indumentum, above more or less tubereulate, glabrous even when young except near base of midrib. Infloreseences in axillary thyrses, usually many-flowered and elongated, up to 4 cm. long, densely fulvous-subsetulose with erect or ascending, short, somewhat matted hairs; pedicels about equal to or shorter than calyx; calyx- lobes ovate-lanceolate, up to 2 mm. long, less than 1 mm. broad, acute at apex, densely subsetulose without and ciliate; corolla-tube up to 0.8 cm. long, papillose without and fulvous-subsetulose with short spreading hairs, pilose within from below middle up to throat, corolla-lobes densely papillose and solmewhat subsetulose without, densely bearded on the lower half within, the ilndumentum continuous with that within corolla-tube; anthers sessiloid, almost entirely ineluded; style pilose. [Fruits, etc. Prog. (26, p. 273) and from Gardner 4273]. Fruits globose, about 1.6 cm. in diam., mucronate at apex, shell less than 0.5 mm. thick, shining, smooth, with minute facets, bitter-astringent, pulp sweet, seeds 1-4, orbicular-oval, convex on one face and concave on the other, about 15 mm. long and 12 mm. broad.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Small tree 3-5 m tall. Leaves obovate, rounded and conspicuously emarginate at apex, cuneately acute at base, shining and drying a lead-gray color above, 4-10 x 1.5-5.2 cm, margins with 6-10 low, rounded crenations on each side; sec- ondary nerves 7-9 on each side of the midnerve, conspicuously elevated above and below, tertiary venation impressed above, subelevated below; petioles 3-4 mm long. Inflorescence consisting of relatively few-flowered (4-10) racemes, usually solitary and axillary in the lower and upper axils, in anthesis 1.8-3.5 cm long, much shorter than the leaves, in fruit shorter than or equaling the leaves and 4-8 cm long; pedicels 1-3 mm long in anthesis, 3-9 mm long in fruit. Sepals subequal or slightly unequal, the outer ones suborbicular, 1 x 0.7-0.8 mm, the inner ones oval-oblong, 1.2 x 0.7-0.8 mm, mostly subentire or obscurely 1-2- crenulate on each side; petals obovate-oblong, 3.8-5.5 x 2-2.1 mm, 4-5 times longer than the sepals; filaments 3-5 mm long; ovary 1.2-2.8 mm long; style 2- 3.2 mm long, equaling or slightly longer than the ovary. Capsule 10-11 mm long, 4-5 mm in diam; seeds castaneous, body 3-4 x 1.8-2 mm, wing 4-5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. & Luteyn, James L. 1980. Revision of the genus Ochthocosmus (Linaceae). Brittonia. 32: 128-143.

description: Herbae perennes usque ad 5 dm altae. Folia petiolata, lamina elliptica vel ovata vel lanceolata, 10-58 x 2-22 mm, 1.7-6. iplo longior quam latior. Dichasia efoliorum axillis orta, 1-3-flora. Bracteolae lineares vel ellipticae vel obovatae, 3-17 mm longae. Calyx 5-lobus, 5-11 mm longus, lobis aequalibus vel inaequalibus. Corolla purpurea et alba, 16.5-40 mm longa, tubo cylindrico, 12.5-33 mm longo. Pollinis granae 4-aperturatae. Capsula 7-11 mm longa, glabra.
bibliographicCitation: Daniel, Thomas F. 1995. Justicia masiaca (Acanthaceae), a new species from northwestern Mexico. Brittonia. 47: 408-413.

description: Herba, caulibus subsuleatis, supra subquadrangularibus, bifariam pubescentibus; laminis foliorum ellipticis, ad apicem rotundatis, obtusis, vel subacuminatis, ad basim angustatis, in petiolum decurrentibus, integris vel undulatis, supra glabris vel parce hirsutis, subtus subglabris, costa venisque prominentibus, venis pubeseentibus; petiolis pubeseentibus; spicais gracilibus, subsessilibus aliquando peniculas terminales formantibus; bracteis oblongis, acutis, imbricatis, glanduloso-puberculentibus, cilatis, interdum pilis raris longioribus, eglanduliferis instructis, venis prominentibus; bracteolis subulatis; calycis segmentis 4, linearibus; corolla purpurea, minute pubeseentis, angusta, bilabiata, labio superiore oblongo, inferiore trilobo, lobis ellipticis rotundatis; staminibus breviter exsertis; antherae loculis valde superpositis, superiore grandiore rotundato, inferiore calcarato; ovario glabro.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Herb up to 1 m. high; stems subsuleate, light green, the upper portions subquadrangular, pubescent in 2 lines, the hairs white, retrorsely curved, 0.5-1 mm. long, the lower portions ot the stem subterete and subglabrous; leaf blades elliptic, 7-12 cm. long, 3.5-6.5 cm. wide at or near the middle (those subtending the inflorescence smaller), rounded, obtuse or subacuminate at tip, narrowed, sometimes abruptly so at base and decurrent on the petiole, entire or undulate, both surfaces drying green, the upper glabrous or sparingly beset with stiff, slightly curved, multicellular hairs, the veins scarcely prominent, the lower surface subglabrous except copta and veins (6 to 10 pairs), these greenish-white, very conspicuous, moderately pubescent with fine, white, curved hairs, the eystoliths straight or slightly curved, slender, 0.5 mm. long, inconspicuous on both surfaces; petioles (unwinged portion) 5 to 20 mm. long, finely pubescent to subglabrous, the hairs curved; flowers borne in slender, subsessile, erect or suberect spikes 2-5 cm. long, these simple, terminal or axillary, sometimes forming a terminal, crowded panicle, the bracts closely imbricate, oblong, up to 7 mm. long and 2.5-3 mm. wide, acute, the pubesence a mixture of scattered, slender, straight or slightly curved hairs 0.5 mm. long and minute, straight, glandular ones, the margin ciliate, the costa and veins prominent; bractlets linear-subulate, 6 mm. long, 0.75 mm. wide, minutely pubescent, the hairs glandular or pointed at tip, sometimes with a few slender ones intermixed; calyx 4.5 omm. long, divided nearly to the base, the seg- ments linear, 0.5-0.75 mm. wide, the pubescence siinilar to that of the bracts and bractlets; corollas bright purple, 10-14 mm. long, minutely pubescent, the tube slender, the lower lip 3-lobed, the lobes elliptic, 4 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide, rounded at tip, the upper lip oblong, entire, about 6 mm. long; stamens exserted slightly beyond the throat of the corolla, the anther lobes strongly superposed, one about 0.75 mm. above the other, the upper lobe elliptic in outline, 1.5 mm. long, and barely 1 mm. wide, the cells rounded at base, the lower anthers much smaller than the upper, these including the short spur, about 1 mm. long and 0.5 mm. wide; filaments glabrous; ovary glabrous; capsules not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1947. Revision of the North American species of Erigeron, north of Mexico. Brittonia. 6: 121-302.

description: Shrub or treelet, 1.5-6 m tall, the indument of vegetative buds and inflorescences strigulose. Leaves 3-foliolate; leaflet blade oblanceolate or narrow-oblanceolate, acuminate at apex, cuneate and especially in most lateral leaflets obliquely auriculate at extreme base, chartaceous, dull above, glabrous, the secondary veins evident, curved, looping at margin, (13) 21-30 per side, the tertiary veins obscure on adaxial surface, evident and raised on abaxial surface, the terminal blade 65.5-71 cm long, 11.5-15 cm wide, the lateral blade (29) 64-76 cm long, (9.3) 10.5-13 cm wide; petiole usually ca. 0.8 (-3.3) cm long; petiolule absent. Inflorescence 8-13-flowered, 3-6.5 cm long including a peduncle 1.5-2.5 cm long; pedicels 2-3 mm long in flower, ca. 4 mm long in fruit. Sepals very wide-ovate, rounded at apex, 2-4 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, sparsely strigulose without, glabrous within. Corolla ca. 30 mm long at anthesis, sparsely pubescent without and less so as corolla enlarges, greenish white, the tube 4.5-5.5 mm to di- vision of innermost lobe, 14-18 mm to division of other lobes, 2.5-3.6 mm wide, the innermost lobe linear, 22-23 mm long, 1- 2 mm wide, the other 4 lobes narrow-oblong, ca. 12 mm long, ca. 3 mm wide. Filaments of fertile stamens adherent to co- rolla, ca. 17 mm long; staminodes adherent to corolla, linear, 20-22 mm long; anthers 6-7.5 mm long, 1.4-1.5 mm wide, villous, the connective villous, the appendages ca. 3 mm long and wide. Disc taller than and completely enveloping ovary, 5-lobed. Carpels ca. 0.9 mm tall, glabrous; style 18-20 mm long, gland-dotted, glabrous. Fruiting mericarps 1-3, ca. 15 mm long, ca. 10 mm wide, densely strigulose. Seed ca. 12 mm long, ca. 8 mm wide, mottled dark brown.
bibliographicCitation: Kallunki, Jacquelyn A. 1994. Revision of Raputia Aubl. (Cuspariinae, Rutaceae). Brittonia. 46: 279-295.

description: Shrub or tree 1-3 m tall, the indument of vegetative buds, young twigs and petioles, and inflorescences hirsute. Leaves 3-foliolate; leaflet blade oblanceolate or rarely narrow-obovate, acuminate (rarely rounded or obtuse) at apex, cuneate (rarely obtuse) and in lateral leaflets asymmetric at base, chartaceous, dull above, long-hirsute on both surfaces, especially on the veins, the secondary veins evident, curved-ascending, obscurely looping at margin, 6-16 per side, the tertiary veins obscure on adaxial surface, evident and slightly raised on abaxial surface, the terminal blade 8-30 cm long, 2.4-8.3 cm wide, the lateral blade 6-26.5 cm long, 2-6.9 cm wide; petiole 1.2-4 cm long; petiolule absent. Inflorescence ca. 3-flowered, to 1.2 cm long in fruit, including a peduncle ca. 0.2 cm long; pedicels to ca. 3 mm long in fruit. Sepals ovate, acute at apex, 3.5-7 mm long, 1.8-4 mm wide, long- hirsute without, glabrous within. Corolla 8- 8.5 mm long at anthesis, glabrous without even at anthesis, green, the tube 2-2.5 mm to division of innermost lobe, 3.5-4 mm to division of other lobes, ca. 3 mm wide, the innermost lobe oblong, ca. 5.7 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, the other 4 lobes oblong, ca. 2.5 mm long, ca. 1.5 mm wide. Filaments of fertile stamens adherent to corolla, ca. 4 mm long; staminodes adnate to corolla, arising at throat, linear, 2.2-2.5 mm long; anthers 2.5-2.6 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm wide, glabrous, the connective glabrous, the appendages ca. 1 mm long, 0.6-0.9 mm wide. Disc enclosing ovary. Carpels ca. 0.5 mm high, glabrous; style 3-4.5 mm long, gland dotted, glabrous. Fruiting mericarps 1-5, 12- 14 mm long (including a beak 3-4 mm long), 6-8 mm wide, densely long-hirsute. Seed 7- 7.6 mm long, 3-3.8 mm wide, dark brown.

description: Frutex ramis terminalibus annotinis griseis glabris hornotinis ochraceo- sericeis. Stipulae in unam intraxillarem crassam villosam ovatam apice plerum- que bidentatam conereseentes. description: Dioecious trees (35) 40 m X 80 cm, with thick, low, symmetric buttresses; outer bark smooth, peeling in large plates toward base; inner bark orange, with red concentric bands and spicy odor. Axes orthotropic; extensions rhythmic; branching sylleptic, basitonic to mesotonic in axils of cataphylls and basal foliage leaves, normally flowering on sylleptic branches after 1 flush, but capable of flowering upon their inception. Branchlets angled and remaining so for at least 2 flushes, then becoming terete, innovations (0.4)2.6-7.6(17.5) cm long, twigs (0.8)1.4-2(2.6) mm diam., sparsely covered with + straight, ascending, very short (up to 0.2 mm long), whitish hairs, soon glabrescent; epidermis drying brown to black; cataphylls present at base of extension, shortly persistent; terminal buds ovoid to ellipsoid, (1.8)2.8-4(5) X 1.4-2.4(3.4) mm, densely covered with straight, ascending, whitish hairs, giving it a silvery appearance. Leaves alternate; petioles channelled, (0.2)0.7-1.1(1.3) cm X (0.8)1.5-1.6(1.8) mm, indument as on branchlets; lamina chartaceous, flat, elliptic to slightly obo- vate, (2.2)4.1-8.7(9.9) X (1.1)1.7-3.3(3.7) cm, base cuneate, symmetric, apex obtuse to shortly acuminate, acumen up to 0.4 cm long, margin slightly recurved, flattening at apex; primary vein above flat to slightly de- pressed, below raised and longitudinally furrowed; secondary veins (4)6-7(9) pairs, equally spaced, on both sides flat, diverging from primary vein at angle of 60-80º, straight, orientation uniform throughout lamina length, brochidodromous, loops 1-2 mm from margin; higher order veins random reticulate, on both sides inconspicuous (visible only in transmitted light), areoles rectangular, up to 1 mm broad, highest order veins 50, irregularly branched; surface on both sides glabrous, brown, primary vein slightly darker (below lighter at base); black glandular dots sparse above. Staminate plant: inflorescences along whole length of flush, erect, thyrsoid, terminal flower present (lacking), peduncle (1.5)3.1- 6.7(7.5) cm X (0.4)0.5-0.6(1.2) mm, hypopodium (0.8)2.1-3.4(4.5) cm long; second order branches 5-7(8), up to 1.5 cm long, highest order branches 40; indument as on branchlets, axes drying brown; bracts and bracteoles deciduous; flowers: pedicels up to 3.4 X 0.4-0.6 mm, gradually enlarging to form an obconical receptacle, ca. 2 X 1.8-2.2 mm; indument as on branchlets; flowers green, drying brown to black; tepals 6, chartaceous, spreading at anthesis, ovate, ca. 1.6 X 1.5 mm (inner tepals slightly wider), apex obtuse, margins slightly recurved, abaxial surface sparsely covered with short (up to 0.1 mm long), straight, adpressed, ascending, whitish hairs, adaxial surface papillose; inside of receptacle hairy; stamens 9, yellow-brown, those of whorls I and II subequal (whorl I slightly larger than whorl II), slightly stipitate, filament transversely flattened, ca. 0.8 X 0.6 mm, anther inflexed, widely trapezoid, ca. 0.4 X 0.45 mm, apex retuse, glabrous, locelli 4, apical, introrse; stamens of whorl III stipitate (filament and anther barely differentiated) filament ca. 0.7 X 0.3 mm, with few erect hairs at base, anther ca. 0.5 X 0.3 mm, locelli 4, apical, upper pair latrorse, lower pair extrorse, paired glands at base up to 0.8 mm broad (see discussion); whorl IV absent or occasionally a filiform staminode present with an incomplete but fertile anther, and glands at base; pistillode teardrop-shaped, up to 1.4 X 0.4 mm, stigma absent (inconspicuous), ovule absent. Pistillate plant: inflorescences similar to those of staminate plants but smaller, with up to 5 second-order branches; highest order branches 3(4)º flowers similar to those of staminate flowers but smaller; pistil teardrop-shaped, ca. 1.5 X 0.7 mm, style ca. 1/3 of total length of pistil, ca. 0.2 mm diam., stigma hemispherical, spreading, locule located toward base of the ovary. Fruits: unknown.

description: Dioecious shrubs to small trees 2-4(10) m X 3(10) cm; bark unknown. Axes orthotropic, extensions rhythmic; branching normally sylleptic, basitonic in axils of foliage leaves and scattered, or in axils of cataphylls and pseudo-verticillate, flowering on sylleptic branches upon their inception. Branchlets terete, innovations (1.1)4-7.3- (12.2+) cm long, twigs 1-1.4 mm diam., densely covered with straight to curved, ± erect, up to 0.5 mm long, yellow-brown to reddish hairs, persisting and becoming dark brown on older growth; epidermis barely visible, greenish yellow turning brown; cataphylls present at base of extension, soon deciduous; terminal buds ovoid, (1.6)2- 3.2(4.4) X (0.8)1-1.6(2) mm, densely covered with ± straight, ascending to ± erect, yellow-brown to reddish hairs. Leaves alternate; petioles hemicircular in cross section, adaxially flattened to slightly concave, (0.5)0.7-1(1.2) cm X (0.8)1-1.2(2.2) mm, indument as on branchlets; lamina coriaceous, flat to slightly bullate, elliptic, (4.8)7.9-11(15.4) X (1.7)3.1-4(6.8) cm, base attenuate, symmetric (slightly asymmetric), apex attenuate to acuminate, acumen (0)0.3-1(1.5) cm long, margin flat throughout; primary vein above slightly raised and rounded, below raised and longitudinally furrowed; secondary veins (3)4(6) pairs, becoming indistinct from higher order venation toward apex, equally spaced, or first pair somewhat distant, above shallowly depressed, below raised, diverging from primary vein at angle of 45- 60º, slowly arching to chordal angle of 20- 30º, orientation nearly uniform throughout lamina length or basal pair with slightly more acute chordal angle, brochidodromous, loops 1-3 mm from margin, intramarginal veins conspicuous in lower 1/3 of lamina; higher order veins random-reticulate, above inconspicuous, below slightly raised, areoles rectangular, up to 3 mm broad, highest order veins 60, irregularly branched; hairs as on branchlets; surface above glabrous, initially shiny yellow-green, turning olive green, primary vein densely hairy, glabrescent apically, slightly lighter, higher order veins inconspicuous, below sparingly hairy, initially opaque yellow-green, turning darker, primary, secondary, and tertiary veins conspicuously lighter. Staminate plant: infiorescences basitonic to mesotonic, in axils of cataphylls or basal foliage leaves, pendulous, thyrsoid, terminal flower present (absent), peduncle (1.2)3.1-5(6.5) cm X 0.2-0.4 mm, hypopodium 0.6- 2.5(3.2) cm long; second order branches 3- 5 below terminal cyme, up to 0.7 cm long; highest order branches 30; indument as on branchlets, but less dense; bracts shortly persistent, up to 1.6 mm long, bracteoles persistent, up to 1 mm long; flowers: ped- icels up to 8 X 0.2 mm, abruptly enlarging to form minute receptacle, 0.4-0.6 X 1.4 mm, buds just before anthesis 2-3 mm diam.; indument as on inflorescence branches; flowers green to red, drying yel low-brown; tepals 6, chartaceous, spreading at anthesis, ovate, ca. 2.5 X 1.5 mm (inner ones slightly wider and thinner), apex obtuse, margin flat, on both sides densely cov- ered with short (up to 0.15 mm long), straight, erect, yellow-brown hairs; inside of receptacle hairy; stamens 9, yellow- green, those of whorls I and II subequal (whorl I slightly larger than whorl II), sessile, anther oblong, laminar, ca. 1.3 x 0.9 mm, glabrous, locelli 4, apical in whorl I, in whorl II arranged almost in 2 pairs, one above the other, introrse; stamens of whorl III columnar, ca. 1.4 X 0.6 mm, glabrous, locelli 4, apical, upper pair latrorse, lower pair extrorse, paired glands at base small (ca. 0.6 mm broad); whorl IV completely absent; pistillode absent. Pistillate plant: infiorescences like those of staminate plant; flowers similar to those of staminate plant but smaller; tepals and androecium dehiscing as ring after anthesis, leaving a small receptacle ca. 2 X 2.5 mm; pistil teardrop shaped, ca. 1.6 X 1.2 mm, style ca. 1/3 of total length of pistil, ca. 0.5 mm diam., stigma hemispherical, spreading, locule located in middle of the ovary. Fruits: unknown.
