description: Dioecious trees 12-15 m X 10-12 cm, with small buttresses; outer bark thin, fragile, finely fissured and chipped, brownish red in section; inner bark 3 mm thick, somewhat fibrous, pale yellow, with slight odor. Axes orthotropic, extensions rhythmic; branching sylleptic, basitonic in axils of cataphylls, flowering on sylleptic branches upon their inception. Branchlets terete, in- novations (1.7)5.5-16.5(22) cm long, twigs (2)2.4-3.4(4.8) mm diam., densely covered with straight to crisped, erect, up to 1 mm long, yellow-reddish persistent hairs, becoming brown on older growth; epidermis drying black; cataphylls present at base of extension, soon deciduous; terminal buds ovoid, (3.8)4.3-5.5(6) X 2.8-3.4 mm, densely covered with ± straight, ascending to ? erect, yellow-reddish hairs. Leaves al- ternate; petioles hemicircular in cross section, (0.5)0.9-1.8(1.9) cm X (1.2)1.8- 2.4(2.8) mm, indument as on branchlets; lamina coriaceous, flat to slightly bullate, narrow-elliptic to elliptic, (6.3)8.5- 17.6(20.2) X (3.2)4.3-7.2(18.8) cm, base attenuate, symmetric, apex attenuate to acu- minate, acumen (0)0.2-1.3(1.5) cm long, margin revolute for (0.2)0.7-1.2(1.5) cm; primary vein above slightly raised and rounded, below prominent; secondary veins 3-6(7) pairs, equally spaced, above slightly raised, below prominent, diverging from the primary vein at angle of 55-60(70)º, slowly arching to chordal angle of 20-30º, orientation uniform throughout lamina length, brochidodromous, loops ca. 1 mm from margin; higher order veins random-reticulate, on both sides slightly raised, areoles rectangular, up to 1 mm broad, highest order veins 6º, irregularly branched; hairs as on branchlets; surface above initially sparingly hairy, becoming glabrous, primary and secondary veins densely hairy on both surfaces, older leaves above olive green, below light green, slightly glaucous, veins yellowish to brown. Staminate plant: inflorescences basitonic to acrotonic, pendulous, thyrsoid, peduncle 12-16.3(17) cm X 1-1.2 mm, hypopodium (5.5)5.8-7.8(9) cm long; second order branches 4-5, termninal flower present (lacking), up to 4.5 cm long, highest order branches 5º; indument as on branchlets but shorter and less dense, axes drying black; bracts and bracteoles persistent, narrowly ovate, spoon-shaped, reflexed, up to 0.9 X 0.3 cm; flowers: pedicels up to 0.7 X 0.6-0.8 mm, abruptly enlarging to form a spherical receptacle, 2-2.6 X 3-4 mm; indument as on inflorescence branches; flowers yellowish, drying gray; tepals 6, chartaceous, erect, forming a cup ca. 6 mm diam. at anthesis, outer tepals transverse ovate, ca. 4.2 X 4.2 mm, inner tepals slight- ly smaller, apex obtuse, adaxially densely covered with short (up to 0.1 mm long), ± straight, erect, yellowish hairs, abaxially sparser and longer (up to 0.2 mm long); in- side of receptacle densely hairy (hairs up to 0.4 mm long); stamens 9, red, those of whorls I and II subequal, sessile, anther transverse-ovate, thickened at center, the "wings" thinner, ca. 1.6 X 3 mm, apex retuse, with a few erect hairs at base, locelli 2, apical, introrse; stamens of whorl III columnar, ca. 1.5 X 0.7 mm, with a few erect hairs at base, locelli 4, apical, upper pair latrorse, lower pair extrorse, paired glands at base large (ca. 1.2 mm broad); whorl IV completely absent; pistillode absent (minute, up to 0.6 mm, teardrop shaped). Pistillate plant: inflorescences as on staminate plant but smaller, peduncle (1.4)2.3-6.8 cm X 0.6-1 mm, hypopodium (0.6)1.2-3.7 cm long; second order branches (2)3-5, terminal flower mostly present, up to 1.2 cm long, highest order branches 30; bracts deciduous, bracteoles persistent;flowers: pedicels up to 4 mm long, receptacle ca. 1.6 X 2.8 mm, tepals in bud similar to those of staminate flowers; developing staminodes of whorls I and II sessile, similar to stamens of staminate flowers but smaller, anthers with 4 apical vestigial locelli; developing pistil teardrop-shaped, ca. 1.7 X 0.8 mm, stigma broad, ca. 1 mm wide, hemispheri- cal, margin recurved. description:
Frutices scandentes vel arbores humiles dioicae. Ramuli teretes indumento rufo persistente praediti. Folia alterna dissita vel pseudo-verticillata; petiolus in sectione transversali hemicircularis; lamina coriacea, anguste-elliptica, apice angustato vel acuminato, nervis secundariis 7-12-jugis ad basem et apicem demum haud distinctus; pagina supra glabra, subtus glabra vel pilosa, in sicco brunnea. Inflorescentiae dissitae, botryoidae, ramis 5-11 et 0(l)-furcatis; bracteis et bracteolis persistentibus. Florum receptaculum minutum; tepala sub anthesi patentia; stamina verticillorum I et II florum staminatorum sessilia, anteris oblongis, crassis, locellis 4 introrsis apicem versus insertis, ea verticilli III columnaria, basi glandulis geminatis compressis parvis interdum confluentibus, locellis 4 extrorsis et latrorsis, verticilli IV nulla; pistillodium nullum. Fructus pedicello parum incrassato, bracteolae persistentes; cupula coriacea hemisphaerica ad marginem tepalis persistentibus.

Dioecious scandent shrubs to small trees 3-5 m X 5 cm; trunk rhomboid in cross section; bark unknown. Axes plagiotropic?, extensions rhythmic; rarely branching, when so normally sylleptic, pseudo-verticillate, basitonic in axils of cataphylls, not flowering on sylleptic branches upon their inception. Branchlets terete, innovations (4.3)5.9-12.5(14.5) cm long, twigs 2.4-3 mm diam., densely covered with + straight, ± erect, up to 1.2 mm long, reddish brown hairs, persisting and becoming dark brown on older growth; epidermis barely visible, brown; cataphylls present at base of extension, persisting for at least 3 flushes; terminal buds with numerous ascending cataphylls, 2-3.2 X 3-4.6 mm, densely covered with straight, ascending, reddish brown hairs. Leaves alternating along the distal half of the flush or pseudo-verticillate at apex of flush; petioles hemicircular in cross section, adaxially slightly concave, 0.4-0.7 cm X 2-3.2 mm, indument as on branchlets; lamina coriaceous, flat to slightly bullate, narrow-elliptic, (9)13.8-16.6(18.5) X (4)6.6-8(9) cm, base acute to blunt, sym- metric, apex attenuate to acuminate, acumen (0)0.4-1.5(2.4) cm long, margin slightly recurved; primary vein above slightly raised and rounded, below raised and longitudinally furrowed; secondary veins (7)8-11(12) pairs, becoming indistinct from higher order venation at the base and the apex, equally spaced, above shal- lowly depressed to inconspicuous, below raised to inconspicuous, diverging from the primary vein at angle of 60-75º, straight, orientation nearly uniform throughout lamina length, brochidodromous, loops 1-3 mm from margin; intersecondaries often present or indistinct from the mostly parallel tertiary venation; higher order veins random-reticulate, above inconspicuous to slightly raised, below slightly raised, areoles rectangular, up to 1 mm broad, highest order veins 6º, irregularly branched; hairs as on branchlets; surface above glabrous, initially shiny olive-green to brown, turning olive green, primary vein glabrous, higher order veins inconspicuous, below indument variable among samples from densely hairy to glabrous, initially opaque light brown, turning darker, primary, secondary, and tertiary veins with denser pubescence. Staminate plant: inflorescences along whole length of the extension, seldom in axils of cataphylls, more often in axils of foliage leaves of current flush or of previous flushes, pendulous, botryoid, peduncle (0.4)2.8- 5.6(10) cm X 1-1.8 mm, hypopodium 0.3- 1.7(3) cm long; second order branches 5- 11, up to 0.2 cm long; highest order branch es 2(3)º; indument as on branchlets, but less dense; bracts persistent, up to 4.0 mm long, glabrous adaxially, densely hairy abaxially, bracteoles persistent, up to 3 mm long; flowers: pedicels up to 1.5 X 0.6 mm, abruptly enlarging to form minute receptacle, 2 X 3.3 mm, buds just before anthesis ca. 3 mm diam.; indument as on inflorescence branches; flowers whitish, drying black; tepals 6, chartaceous, spreading at anthesis, ovate, outer ones ca. 5 X 3.5 mm, inner ones ca. 3.7 X 2.8 mm, apex obtuse, margin slightly inrolled, adaxially glabrous, abaxially densely covered with short (up to 0.3 mm long), straight, ascending, yellow brown hairs; inside of receptacle hairy; stamens 9, those of whorls I and II subequal (whorl I slightly larger), sessile, anther oblong, thickened, ca. 1.2 X 2 mm, glabrous, locelli 4, apical, introrse; stamens of whorl III columnar, partially to completely fused, ca. 2 X 1 mm, glabrous, locelli 4, apical, upper pair latrorse, lower pair extrorse, paired glands at base ca. 1.2 mm broad, sometimes fusing with the adjacent glands and stamens of outer whorls forming a disc; whorl IV completely absent; pistillode absent. Pistillate plant: inflorescences like those of staminate plant; flowers unknown; staminodes persisting on young cupules similar to stamens of staminate flowers but smaller, all 3 staminal whorls dehiscing as ring surrounding the style. Fruits: infructescences bearing 1 fruit each; pedicels slightly thickened, up to 1.3 cm X 3 mm, bracteoles persisting at base, gradually en- larging to form a thick, hemispherical cupule ca. 1.2 X 1.4 cm, chartaceous, red, margin undulate, with persistent tepals; berry elliptic, ca. 12.4 X 1.5 cm, green, maturing blue-black.
bibliographicCitation: Madriñán, Santiago R. 1996. New species of Rhodostemonodaphne (Lauraceae) from north-eastern South America. Brittonia. 48: 45-66.

description: Graffenrieda latifoliae (Naud.) Triana affinis, floribus minoribus antherarum connectivis dorsaliter ad basim non vel vix calcaratis differt. Arbor vel frutex 3-13 m; ramuli teretes sicut folia subtus inflorescentia hypanthiaque sparsiuscule granuloso-glandulosi. Petioli 3-7.5 cm longi; lamina 14-28 X 10-27 cm, late ovata apice hebetiobtuso vel rotundato basi rotundata vel paulo (usque ad 2 cm) cordata, firme membranacea et integra, supra glabra, subtus in venis primariis secundariisque sparse setulosa (pills laevibus usque ad 1 mm longis) alioque esetulosa, (5-)7(-9)-nervata nervis secundariis 0.5-1.5 cm inter se distanti- bus tertiariis venulisque subtus obscure elevatis laxe reticulatis. Panicula 17-30 cm longa lataque multiflora; flores 4-meri, pedicellis 1-1.2 mm longis, bracteolis non visis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 1.4-1.5 mm longum paullulo 8-costulatum; calycis tubus 0.1 mm longus, lobis 0.6-0.7 X 1-1.1 mm ovatis acutis. Petala alba et glabra, 3.2-3.4 mm longa, 1.1-1.3 mm lata, oblongo-lanceolata anguste acuta. Stamina isomorphica glabra; filamenta 2-2.3 mm longa; antherarum thecae 1.7-1.9 X 0.3-0.4 mm oblongo-lanceolatae poro 0.1-0.15 mm diam. ventraliter inclinato; connectivum 0.1-0.3 mm prolongatum dorsaliter ad basin non vel vix (0.02-0.03 mm) appendiculatum. Stigma punctiforme; stylus 5.1-5.4 X 0.2-0.25 mm glaber; ovarium 2-loculare apicem versus modice resinoso-granulosum, apice rotundato non prolongato; semina ca. 0.9 X 0.1 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Wurdack, John J. 1976. Endemic Melastomataceae of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia. Brittonia. 28: 138-143.

description: Inter congeneres proximos foliis 4-foliolatis nectario petiolari destitutis, perianthio parvo vix 7 mm diam., necnon androecio 5-mero insignis; ulterius a Ch. (ser. Bauhinianae) rotundifolia (Persoon) Greene, nectarii defectu androecioque 5-mero comparabili, foliorum foliolis exacte bi-, nec unijugis distantior.

description: Foliorum rachi anguste marginata, foliolis 4-5-jugis ellipticis emarginatis (nec acuminatis) ±5.5 cm usque longis, florum apetalorum calyce ±4.5 mm longo extus sericeo intus glabro, ovarioque toto sericeo notabilis, ab affini S. steyermarkii Cowan foliolorum numero (4- 5-, nec 2-3-jugo), ambitu (apice emarginato, haud acuminato) et magnitudine (±5.5, nec 9-17 cm usque) ulterius staminum filamentis glabris necnon legumine appresse sericeo (nec piloso) diversa; a S. guianensi (Aublet) Urban foliolis subdimidio minoribus sepalisque intus glaberrimis statim separanda.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1996. Neotropical Fabales at NY: Asides and oversights. Brittonia. 48: 174-187.

description: Trees ±4 m with glabrate branches, the leaflets glabrous sublustrous and minutely speckled above, silky-strigulose beneath, the densely brownish-silky racemes of small apetalous flowers supra-axillary to coeval leaves. Stipules linear ± 4-5 X 0.5 mm. Leafstalks to 10-11 cm, the petiole 1.5-2 cm, the longer interfoliolar segments 2-2.5 mm, each segment narrowly winged, the wings distally ±3 mm wide, each replicate against the rachis and produced at each leaflet-insertion into a stiff point 0.7- 1 mm; leaflet-pulvinules ±1 mm, deeply wrinkled; leaflets 9-11 per leaf, ovate-oblong-elliptic from broadly rounded base, not acuminate, shallowly emarginate, the furthest pair 4.5-5.5 X 2-2.5 cm; venation pinnate, submersed on both faces of blade. Raceme-axis 9-13 cm; bracts ± 1.5 mm; pedicels 3.5-4 mm, ebracteolate; calyx 4- merous, densely brown-silky externally, glabrous within, the broad-ovate segments ±4.5 X 3 mm; androecium ± 60-merous, glabrous, the smaller anthers 0.65-0.9 mm diam., the filament of 2 larger stamens 3.5 mm, their anther ± 1.4 mm; gynoecium and fruit densely silky-strigose overall, the gynophore ± 4 X 0.6 mm, the body of the pod plumply ellipsoid, in profile ± 17 X 11 mm, the minute style lateral just below the fruit's apex; seed not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1996. Neotropical Fabales at NY: Asides and oversights. Brittonia. 48: 174-187.

description: Vine 4-5 m long, stems terete, herbaceous parts sparsely strigose, green-purple, woody parts gray-purple. Leaves alternate, trifoliate, broadly trullate in outline; petiole 2-3 cm long, with 2-3 pairs of nectaries; leaflets 7-12 cm long, 1.5-3.5 cm wide, central leaflet longer and wider than lateral leaflets, narrowly ovate to lanceolate, some asymmetrical, pinnately veined, adaxial surface glabrous, shiny dark green, abaxial surface moderately strigose, trichomes hyaline, tapered, curved, especially abundant along veins, creamy green, margins serrulate, apex acuminate, base attenuate; petiolules 3-5 mm long; stipules 1-1.3 cm long, ovate, serrulate. Inflorescence solitary; peduncles 13-15 cm long, sparsely strigose; bracts 3, 1.8-2.2 cm long, ovate, fused at base, margins shallowly serrulate, apex acute to acuminate. Flowers 11-13 cm diam., pendent, red-orange or vermilion, with yellow markings in 3 of the 5 sepals and at base of all petals; hypanthium 1.5 cm long, 1-1.2 cm wide, dilated at base, bright shiny green on outer surface; oper- culum pendent 0.3-0.5 mm long, margin denticulate; sepals elliptic, 5.5-6 cm long, 2-2.2 cm wide; petals subequal to sepals; corona uniseriate, denticulate, teeth 1-1.2 mm long, deep purple to purple-black; androgynophore 3-4 cm long, glabrous; ova- ry ellipsoid, densely puberulent; styles free, glabrous. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Panero, José L. 1996. Passiflora linda, a new species from southern Ecuador. Brittonia. 48: 192-194.

description: Tree 4-6 m tall, the indument of vegetative buds, young twigs and petioles, and inflorescences strigulose. Leaves 1 -foliolate; leaflet blade elliptic or narrow-elliptic, acuminate at apex, acute at base (sometimes ultimately rounded at extreme base), 11-32 cm long, 4-10.5 cm wide, chartaceous, dull above, glabrous, the secondary veins evident, rather straight, looping at margin, 12- 21 per side, the tertiary veins evident on both surfaces, slightly raised on the adaxial surface; petiole 0.5-2 cm long. Inflorescence 24-37-flowered, 19.5-26.5 cm long including a peduncle 4.5-16.5 cm long; pedicels ca. 1 mm long in flower and 0-2 mm long in fruit. Sepals very wide-ovate, rounded at apex, ca. 1 mm long, ca. 1.5 mm wide, stri- gulose without, glabrous within. Corolla 10- 15 mm long at anthesis, densely strigulose without, green or white, the tube ca. 3 mm to division of innermost lobe, 5-6 mm to division of other lobes, ca. 4.8 mm wide, the innermost lobe narrow-ovate, 7-8 mm long, 2-2.1 mm wide, the other 4 lobes wide- ovate, ca. 2.5 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide. Filaments of fertile stamens adherent to co- rolla, 6-7.5 mm long; staminodes adherent to corolla, linear, ca. 7 mm long; anthers ca. 3.8 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, villous, the connective villous, the appendages 1-1.5 mm long, 1.8-2 mm wide. Disc equal to ovary, not enveloping it. Carpels ca. 1 mm high, strigulose; style 7-10 mm long, gla- brous. Fruiting mericarps 1-3, 13-17 mm long, ca. 8 mm wide, strigulose. Seed ca. 12 mm long, ca. 6 mm wide, brown.
bibliographicCitation: Kallunki, Jacquelyn A. 1994. Revision of Raputia Aubl. (Cuspariinae, Rutaceae). Brittonia. 46: 279-295.

description: Tree, 7-20 m tall; stems glabrous. Leaves coriaceous, elliptic or obovate, 6.5-17 x 2.5-5 cm; base attenuate; margin undulate and denticulate; apex acuminate; principal nerve prominent below, the secondary and tertiary nerves anastomosed and sunken; petiole 5-9 mm long. Inflorescences generally terminal, racemose, 8-15 cm long, the peduncle 6-7 mm long. Flowers: sepals 5, free or united in 3-4 parts, coriaceous, ob- long, 5-6 x 2-3 mm; petals 5, membra- nous, ovate, 9 x 7 mm; stamens 10, subsessile, 5 mm long; carpels 6-8; style 5 mm long. Fruiting carpels 1-3, ovoid, 6-8 x 5- 6 mm; carpophore discoid and lobate (in western Amazonia) or conical (in eastern Amazonia and the Guianas).
bibliographicCitation: Sastre, Claude. 1994. Three new taxa of Ouratea (Ochnaceae) from South America. Brittonia. 46: 309-313.

description: Arbor monoecia 20 m alta, ramulis novellis dense stellato-lepidotis. Petiolus 2-2.5 cm longus, crassus, planus supra, stellato-lepidotus; laminae 10.5-14 cm latae, 22-33 cm longae, obovatae, ad apicem rotundae et emarginatae, margine integro, ad basim longe attenuatae, coriaceae, costa parce stellato-lepidota, aliter parcissime stellato-lepidotae, venis 14-15-jugatis, salientibus, costa saliens. Inflorescentiae axillares, cymosae, ca. 12 cm longae, cum floribus stellato-lepidotae; flores feminei ad terminum ramulorum praecipuorum, ovoidei, 6 mm longi, 5 mm lati, tepalis obsoletis, pedicello 2-4.5 mm longo; flores masculi clavati, ca. 6 mm longi, staminibus duobus, subsessilibus, deltoideis, tepalis obsoletis. Fructus immaturus globosus, stellato-lepidotus.
bibliographicCitation: Cowan, Richard S. 1957. New species and new records of plants in Guiana. Brittonia. 8: 231-245.

description: Shrub or small tree to 6 m; branches brown, glabrous or rarely sparingly hispid. Leaves coriaceous, lucid, narrowly obovate to occasionally ovate, 3-17 cm long, 1.5-6 cm broad, more than twice as long as broad, glabrous to rarely hispid on the midrib beneath, pinnately veined; primary veins obscure above, obvious beneath, the ultimate venation finely reticulate; areoles irregular, less than 0.5 mm diam, pellucid; margin entire, sometimes slightly undulate; apex narrowed, obtuse to rounded and occasionally retuse; base cuneate; petiole 0.5-2 cm long, with conspicuous dark pulvinus, glabrous to occasionally hispid. Male inflorescences axillary, solitary or clustered, racemose, much longer than the petiole, ascending to spreading-ascending, filiform to slender, villous; peduncles 0.2-2.3 cm long; rachis 0.15-0.9 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 0.7-1 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, villous; pedicels 0-1 mm long; bractlets 2 or 3, lanceolate to obovate-lanceolate, ca 0.8 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, glabrous to sparsely villous. Flowers greenish-yellow, glabrous; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate, ca 1.2 mm long, ca 0.9 mm broad, the inner broadly obovate to ovate, ca 1.8 mm long, ca 1.2 mm broad; petals 6 in 2 similar series, obovate, ca 1 mm long, ca 0.7 mm broad; stamens 6; filaments ca 0.5 mm long. Female inflorescences axillary, usually solitary, racemose, usually longer than the petiole, ascending to spreading-ascending, slender to stout, villous, becoming glabrate with age; peduncles 0.1-1.5 cm long; rachis 0.02-0.5 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 1-1.2 mm long, ca 0.5 mm broad, villous; pedicels 1-2 mm long. Flowers not seen. Fruit green, globose, glabrous, 9-12 mm long and broad, scarcely compressed, the apex broadly rounded.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Arbor parva; rami grisei lepidibus minutis obsiti; ramuli valde striati, ferruginei, lepidibus multiradiatis obtecti; folia petiolo 2-2.5 cm longo, ovato-cordata, 7.5-9 cm longa, 3-4.5 cm lata, basi profunde emarginata, apice longe acuminata, nervo medio supra impresso, subtus prominulo, nervis lateralibus utroque latere 2 e basi abeuntibus, exterioribus supra obsoletis subtus 2-3 mm a margine distantibus, supra nitida in sicco pallide viridia, subtus rufescentia, lepidibus multiradiatis obtecta, opaca, margine integra plana vel parum recurva, chartacea; inflorescentiae terminales, pauciflorae (3-5), lepidotae; bracteae semilunares, 0.5 mm longae; flores ad apicem ramorum 3, breve pedicellati, laterales 2, pedicello usque 8 mm longo; calycis tubus cylindraceus sub limbo paulo contractus, 7-8 mm longus, limbo 5-6 mm longo, lobis triangulari-subulatis, 4-5 mm longis; petala alba, limbo calycis supero adnata, oblongo-obovata, 10-12 mm longa; stamina 8, filamentis 5 mm longis, antheris supra basim affixis 7-8 longis, non appendiculatis, apice 2-porosis; stylus 1 cm longus; stigma minutum; ovarium biloculare.
bibliographicCitation: Liogier, Alain H. 1968. Novitates Antillanae. III. Brittonia. 20: 148-161.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Young twigs and under side of midrib puberulent; petioles 0.4-2.4 mm long; blades 16-50 (-59) times as long as the petiole, 1.4-2.8 times as long as wide; true pedicels (1.2-) 2-4.4 mm long (-5 mm in fruit); free part of calyx lobes 1.G-2.5 mm long; calyx length from stamen attachment 1.6-3.5 mm; petals 3.6-5.6 mm long, 2.0-3.6 mm wide, 1.2-2.1 times as long as wide; anther sporangia 1.2-1.8 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1971. Geographic Variation in a Widespread Neotropical Species, Mouriri Myrtilloides (Melastomataceae). Brittonia. 23 (4): 413-424.

description: Planta a varietate genuina differt foliis, ramulis, corollis, et calycibus glabrioribus, viridioribus, resinosioribus; foliis, minoribus.

description: Ramis obtuse quadrangulatis glabris; petiolis gracilibus elongatis; laminis membranaceis ovato-ellipticis ad apicem obtusam acuminatis integris vel subintegris basi obtusis 5-pli-nerviis utrinque glabris; panicula sessile trichotoma; floribus 7-meris breviter pedicellatis; hypanthio subgloboso glabro; alabastris acuminatis glabris; ovario 7-loculari; stigmate capitellato.

description: Laminae elongate, 2-3-pinnate-pinnatifid at base and 2-pinnate-pinnatifid above the basal pinna pair; basal pinnae ca. 0.6 times the length of the lamina, not strongly elongate basiscopically; pinna rachises puberulent on both surfaces, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, 1-3 celled; laminar tissue between veins glabrous on both surfaces; veins visible, puberulent on the abaxial surface, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, 1-3 celled, veins glabrous adaxially; lamina margins sparsely ciliate, the hairs ca. 0.1 mm long, 2- or 3-celled; indusia pubescent.
bibliographicCitation: Prado, Jefferson & Moran, Robbin C. 2008. Revision of the neotropical species of Triplophyllum (Tectariaceae). Brittonia. 60 (2): 103-130.

description: Rhizome scales 3-6 mm long, dull reddish brown, narrowly lanceolate, ciliate, spreading. Leaves 30-50(-60) cm long; petioles 15-25 cm long, ca. 1/2 the length of the laminae; laminae reduced basally, with a ter- minal pinna articulate to the rachis; pinnae 7.5-15 X 1.7-3 cm, pairs 4-9, alternate to subopposite, patent, oblanceolate, entire, equilateral or nearly so, narrowly cuneate for 1/2 their length or more, sessile, the apices abruptly caudate; rachises narrowly winged or marginate distally. Fertile pinnae 0.2-0.4 cm wide; paraphyses absent; annular cells 15-19; spores smooth, very pale yellowish.
bibliographicCitation: Moran, Robbin C. 2000. Monograph of the neotropical species of Lomariopsis (Lomariopsidaceae). Brittonia. 52: 55-111.

description: Planta denise ramosa, 1-2 dim. alta, dense strigosa; foliis' brevi- petiolatis, laminis late oblanceolatis et spathulatis, grosse-serratis, 1-2 cm. longis, 3-5 mm. latis; utraque paginarum strigoso-caneseente; hypanthio 9-12 mm. longo; orificio circa 3 mm. lato; sepalis 4 mm. longis, late ovatis, mucronatis; petalis lucide luteis, late obovatis, 7-8 mm. longis.
bibliographicCitation: Rydberg, Per A. 1934. Taxonomic notes on the flora of the prairies and plains of central North America. Brittonia. 1: 79-104.

description: Herba lignosa, suffrutex vel frutex, caulibus subquadrangularibus, ascendentibus, parce hirtellis; foliorum lamina oblongo-elliptica vel oblongo-lanceolata, graciliter acuminata, basi angustata, firma, integra vel undulata, supra glabra vel parce hirtella, subtus glabra, costa et venis lateralibus prominentibus, parce hirtellis; petioli dense hirtelli; spicae terminales et axillares, unilaterales, pedunculis et rhachibus quadrangularibus, glanduloso-puberulis; bracteae et bracteolae virides, subaequales, lanceolatae, intus glabrae vel parce hirtellae, extus aliquanto glanduloso-puberulae, marginibus ciliatis, nervis obscuris; calycis segmenta 5, linearia, glabra vel parce puberula; corolla vivide coccinea, puberula, tubo subcylindrico, aliquanto angustato, bilabiata, labiis erectis, subaequalibus, labio superiore 2-lobato, lobis ovatis, emarginatis, labio inferiore trilobato, lobis ovatis, apice rotundatis; stamina 4, didynama, pari antico biloculari, exserto, antherarum lobis obliquis, leviter superpositis, muticis, pari postico uniloculari, mutico; pollinis granula e typo "Spangenpollen," sphaeroidea, tricolporata, exinio punctata; capsulae clavatae, basi solida gracili, (siccae) brunneae, obscure puberulae; semina 4, brunnea, plana, muricata.
bibliographicCitation: Wasshausen, Dieter C. 1984. Pranceacanthus coccineus (Acanthaceae), a new genus and species from Amazonian Brazil. Brittonia. 36: 1-7.

description: Woody herb, subshrub or shrub, 0.8-2.5 m tall; stems subquadrangular, ascending, moderately hirtellous, the hairs yellowish, upwardly appressed or ascending, 0.5 mm long; leaf blades oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 15-20 cm long and 4.5-7.5 cm wide, slenderly acuminate, gradually narrowed to base, firm, entire or undulate, the upper surface glabrous or sparingly hirtellous, the hairs appressed, the venation obscure, the lower surface glabrous except the costa and lateral veins, these prominent and rather sparingly hirtellous, the hairs yellowish, appressed, the cystoliths more conspicuous above than below; petioles 0.5-2 cm long, densely hirtellous with yellowish, appressed hairs; flowers borne in terminal and axillary, unilateral spikes, these 6-11 cm long and 2-3 cm broad, the peduncle quadrangular, 1.5-2.3 cm long, densely glandular-puberulous, the short hairs spreading, tipped by brownish glands, these interspersed with longer, yellowish, appressed hairs 1 mm long; the rachis similarly glandular-puberulous with a few scattered, appressed, hirtellous trichomes; bracts and bractlets green, subequal, lanceolate, the inner surface glabrous or sparingly hirtellous toward tip, the outer surface moderately glandular-puberulous, the hairs erect, about 0.5 mm long, commonly tipped by brownish glands, the margins ciliate with ascending hairs, the bracts 11-12 mm long and 1.5 mm wide near base, acute, the bractlets slightly shorter than the bracts, 0.8 mm wide, acuminate, both bracts and bractlets obscurely nerved; calyx 9 mm long, the segments 5, linear, 8 mm long, 0.8 mm wide at base, gradually narrowed to a slender tip, glabrous or sparingly puberulous within, glandular-puberulous without, the glands brownish, the hairs yellowish, about 0.3 mm long, the costa and lateral veins obscure, the margins ciliate; corolla bright red or scarlet, 3.5 cm long, puberulous, the hairs erect, 0.3 mm long, the tube relatively slender, 2 mm broad at base, narrowed at 5 mm above base to 1.5 mm thence gradually enlarged to 5 mm at throat, the limb 2-lipped, the lips erect, subequal, 4 mm long, the upper lip 2-lobed, the lobes narrowly ovate, 2 mm long and 1.5 mm wide, emarginate at apex, the lower lip 3-lobed nearly to base, the lobes ovate, 2.5 mm wide, obtuse or rounded at tip; stamens 4, didynamous, anthers of the anterior pair 2-celled, slightly exserted beyond the mouth of the tube, the anther cells equally and somewhat obliquely attached to the connective, 3.25 mm long, muticous, anthers of the posterior pair 1-celled, barely reaching the mouth of the corolla, the anther 3 mm long, muticous, the filaments attached about 2 cm above the base of the corolla tube, flattened, glabrous; pollen grains spheroid or prolate, 47 µm long, 40 µm wide, tricolporate, each colpus flanked by 2 pseudocolpi ("colpoid streaks" sensu Raj 1961), tectum almost complete, psilate-punctate; style somewhat shorter than the anterior stamens, the stigma bilobed, the lobes minute, obtuse; ovary glabrous; capsule clavate, 20 mm long, 4 mm broad, 3 mm thick, drying brownish, obscurely puberulous, the solid stipitate portion 9 mm long, slender; seeds 4, brownish, flattened, about 4 mm in diameter, muricate.

description: Leaves of the caudices 4-10.5 mm long, 1.6-3.3 mm wide, spatulate; apex obtuse to acute, with or without a small mucro up to 0.3 mm long; margins entire or with a small tooth on each side of the apex, sometimes the tooth little more than a large, broad-based cilium; cilia stout, white and pectinate, 0.2-0.5 mm long; lateral teeth never appreciably mucronate; leaves nearly flat and spreading or somewhat ineurved and imbricate; cauline leaves narrow, delicately ciliate; flowering stems 2.5-7.5 (-11.5) cma high, sparingly capitate-glandular; panicle ca. 1.5-4.5 cm high, usually of 3-5 flowers, with the branches moderately capitate-glanidular; sepals 1.5-2 mm long, 1.2-4.5 mm wide at base, rounded (to subacute), entire, glabrous to minutely ciliolate; petals 4-6 mm longf, 1.7-2.3 (-2.8) mm wide, elliptic, not clawed, white (drying cream to brownish yellow), the inner face spotted with yellow, the upper spots sometimes orange or rarely red; stamens usually shorter than the petals; filaments subulate; mature capsules ca 4-5 mm high, 3-4 mm wide. (Fig. 5.)

description: Epiphytic or terrestrial, lianoid shrub; branches stout, terete, glabrous, to 1.5 cm diam. Leaves thick-coriaceous, broadly ovate-oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 12-35 (-44) X 4-15 cm, base rounded to cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire and very narrowly revolute, glabrous, nitid; 3-5-plinerved from near the base with the inner pair of lateral nerves often arising from 2 (-5) cm above the base, midrib raised above and with lateral nerves prominent beneath, reticulate veinlets slightly raised on both surfaces; petiole subterete, stout, 8-20 mm long and to 5 mm diam., glabrous. Inflorescence ramiflorous, sometimes 2 per node, racemose, 6-14-flowered, frequently on leafless branchlets; rachis subterete, stout, 6-17(-30) mm long and to 3 mm diam., glabrous; floral bracts ovate to oblong, acuminate, 2-3.5 x 1-1.5 mm, glabrous or puberulent, marginally glandular- fimbriate; pedicel subterete to angled, 1.5- 3 cm long, glabrous; bracteoles located usually below middle of pedicel, similar to floral bracts. Flowers with calyx 5-6 mm long, glabrous, bright dark orangish red when fresh; hypanthium broadly campanulate or subspherical, ca. 2.5 mm long, weakly apophysate basally when dry; limb spreading-campanulate to rotate, ca. 3.5 mm long; lobes ovate-deltate, subacute, 0.7-2 mm long; sinuses flat; corolla tubular, cylindric although slightly wider at base, 23-40 mm long and to 6 mm diam. when dry, glabrous or minutely puberulous distally, sometimes bearing short-hirsute to setose hairs especially distally near the lobes, red or bright dark orange with the throat and lobes white when fresh, the lobes broadly deltate, acute, 1-2 mm long; stamens alternately 8-11.5 mm and 10.3-12 mm long; filaments connate into a tube 3.5- 5 mm long that is short-pilose marginally; anthers alternately 6-8.7 mm and 7.5-10 mm long, glandular-fimbriate dorsally; tubules dehiscing through broad clefts to ca. 3 mm long. Berry translucent white when fresh.

description: The creeping, calcareous rhizome is clothed with brown lanceolate-acuminate, hair-pointed entire scales, the stipe of fertile leaves (sterile not seen) glossy, brown, 15 cm. long; lamina ovate, impari-pinnate with 3 or 4 pairs of lateral pinnae and a similar terminal one, all linear oblong, ascending, petiolate, cuneate at base, acuminate, quite entire, to 18 cm. long, 2 cm. wide. Veins all raised on both sides, remarkably regularly anastomosing; main veins straight 2/3 of the way- to the margin and there connected by a horizontal and straight or upcurved angular cross-vein, thus forming large rectangular costular areoles, which midway are divided by a weaker cross-vein that bears at the middle a superficial small sorus and above a circular dot of limestone; outside the large areoles in the broader pinnae is a second row of smaller ones, the outer veins mostly parallel at distances of ca. 2 mm. and fused with the cartilaginous margin witlh a semiovate limestone dot above.

description: Large trees 25-35 m tall; tabular buttresses to 6 m tall; trunk above buttresses 0.3-0.5 m diam. Bark beige, smooth, inte- rior cream. Leaf blades 6.5-17 X 4-11 cm, ovate, ovate-lanceolate or oval, the apices acute to short acuminate, the margin entire, weakly revolute, the bases cordate, strongly asynimetrical, glabrous above except occasionally with simple, rarely bifurcate hairs especially on the veins, pubescent below with erect, simple, bifurcate, rarely stellate hairs (immature or shade leaves?), soft to the touch, or glabrous and slightly glaucous (mature or sun leaves?), 5-7-nerved at the base, markedly coriaceous (in the crown, at least); petioles (1.5-)2-3.5 cm long, pubescent or glabrous and glaucous, slightly thickened at both ends; stipular sheaths broadly falcate, 6-7 x ca. 4 mm, the margin entire except for a tuft of hairs apically, extrorsely glabrous and glaucous (or covered with simple hairs, Smith et al. 13569). Inflorescences terminal on leafy branches, paniculate, densely stellate-pubescent. Flower buds pale rose (Smith et al. 13569) or purplish (Gentry et al. 70781), more or less globose. Epicalyx minutely appressed- pubescent. Calyx campanulate, at anthesis 6-8 mm long, the sepals fused to ca. 2/3 of length, the lobes 2-3 X 2-3 mm, one lobe slightly broader than the other four, densely stellate-pubescent without, base of calyx glabrous within, the cup densely villous and the lobes less densely pubescent. Petals pale yellow (Smith et al. 14108) or whitish-cream (Seidel et al. 7302), 15-16 X 3-5 mm, narrowly oblanceolate to spatulate, densely stellate-pubescent without with multi-rayed hairs, glabrous within basally. Staminal tube ca. 7 mm long, sparsely pubescent with simple, hyaline hairs, distally divided into 5, alternisepalous, indistinct phalanges, each of ca. 12-15 stamens, the filaments varying in length, 1-4 mm long. Ovary ovoid, glabrous (?); style ca. 12-13 mm long, erect, densely stellate-pubescent distally; stigma bipartite, the style slightly twisted apically, dividing (?) for several mm at anthesis. Calyx in fruit ca. 2-3 cm long, green with a reddish tint (Smith & Garcia 14339), the free sepal lobes spatu- late, 1-1.5 cm long, 4-6 mm broad, the outer side with short hairs, the inner side with longer hairs; fruit ca. 10 X 6 mm, pericarp ellipsoidal, with appressed hairs; seeds light brown with darker, broad raphe and chalazal region; testa thin; endosperm confined to gaps between the thick, folded cotyledons and the radicle; radicle next to hilum.

description: Plants twining, sparsely to richly branched above, roots fibrous. Shoots succulent, verrucose, glaucous, glabrous, internodes 4-9 cm long, 4-8 mm diam., (grey) blue-green, young shoots with blue-green or grey-green horizontal banding pattern. Leaf scales caducous, with petiole 1 mm long, blade 3 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, ovate, basally rounded, apically acute. In- florescences bostrychoid to sciadioidal, 2- 7-flowered, 1-4 flowers open at time; pe- duncles 1-4 mm long, glabrous. Flowers with a sweet and spicy (thyme) scent; floral bracts 1.5-2 mm long, 1.2-1.5 mm wide at the base, ovate, glabrous; pedicels 1.5-2.5 mm long. Floral buds 5.5-6.5 mm long, 3.5-4 mm diam., conical, with imbricate aestivation. Calyx fused basally, rotate, abaxially apically glandular, glabrous; free calyx lobes 2.5-3 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, ovate. Corolla cyathiform, basally fused, 8-10 mm long, 3-4 mm wide at the base, abaxially bright grey-green, adaxially (ochre-) brown with purplish veins, gla- brous; free corolla lobes incurved, ovate to lanceolate, keeled, apically obtuse, with revolute margins. Gynostegial corona white, urceolate, 3-4 mm long, slightly ex- ceeding the gynostegium, obscuring it except for the top of the stylar head, not vertically articulated (contrary to Descoings, 1971: 110). C(is) consisting of staminal (Cs) and interstaminal parts (Ci) fused for more than 1/2 of total corona height, Cs and Ci differentiated, Ci shorter than Cs. Cs lobes apically erect, with adaxial appendage (ligule), laminar, ca. 2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, with margins covering the guide rails, entire, apically obtuse. Adaxial ap- pendage a little longer than Cs lobe, ca. 2 X 1.2 mm, membranous, ovate to slightly obovate, entire, inflexed. Ci laminar, keeled along the upper 2/3 of corona height, resulting in an erect to reflexed spur with laterally involute margins. Gynostegium sessile, 3.5-3.8 mm high, 3.5-4 mm diam. Stamens with filament of 0.8-0.9 mm height; anthers broader than high, massive, trapezoidal, abaxially convex; anther wings ca. 2 mm long, extending along the whole length of the anther, convergent, adjacent anther wings parallel, centrifugal, basally forming a distinct "mouth" with the basal lateral margin of the anther. Connective append- ages ca. 1 X 1.5 mm, widely ovate to de- pressed ovate equalling the stamen in width, slightly inflexed, papillose, with emarginate margins. Pollinarium: corpusculum 600-700 Rm long; caudicles 200- 250 pm long, flattened, straight, declinate, trapezoidal; pollinia 600-700 Rm long, 400-450 pm wide, ovate in cross section, ovoid, subapically attached to the caudicles, pendulous. Stylar head yellowish, 2.5-4 mm diam., 1.4. mm high; upper part equall- ing the lower part in height, tabular with a slight central depression. Fruits normally 1 per flower, 10 cm long, 5 mm diam., apically shortly beaked, light brown, longitudinally grooved, glabrous. Seeds 4.8-5.2 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide, ovate, light brown, seta and aseta side indistinctly papillose with regularly arranged papillae, marginal with wing 0.7 mm wide, with entire margin; coma ca. 30 mm long.

description: Plants saxicolous, stems 1.5-2 cm wide, scaly; stem scales (7)11-12 mm long, 2 mm wide, non-conform, nearly concolorous, castaneous to bright brown, with slightly lighter border, margins minutely erose, slightly erose at the apex. Leaves 1-pinnate- pinnatifid, petiolate, petioles non-spinose, dark brown, scaly-pubescent, petiole scales flat, slightly clathrate, bright brown, 1.5-3 X 0.5-0.7 mm, hairs 1-1.5 mm long, 8-10 cells long; lamina 20-67 cm long, 4-6.5 cm wide, lanceolate, proximal pair of pinnae slightly reduced, apex gradually reduced; pinnae 12-15 pairs, sessile, alter- nate, narrowly triangular, slightly inequila- teral, basiscopic lobe slightly smaller, 1.7- 3.3 X 0.7-1.2 cm, segments 2-3 mm wide, apex obtuse, hairs limited to the veins, conspicuous on the abaxial side; veins prominent abaxially, simple or furcate, 3-4 pairs of veins/segment, costa prominent with bullate scales 1.5-2 mm long; rachis scaly and pubescent, scales sparse, linear, dark yellow brown, 2 mm long. Sori medial, if on furcate veins then beyond the fork, indusiate, indusia sphaeropteroid, paraphyses present, shorter or the same length as the sporangia.

description: Arbor. Rami foliosi 10-25 mm crassi. Lamina palmatim quinquepartita vel -fida, 30-70 cm longa, 35-70 cm lata, coriacea, basi profunde cordata, apicibus segmentorum acuminato, lamina subtus subhirtella vel subtomentosa, ad venas principales strigosa vel subsericea, ad areolas venasque minimas pilis albis arachnoideis tecta; petiolus 25-60 cm longus; stipulae 15-20 cm longae, persistentes, flavo-villosae vel -hirsutae et pilis densis albis arachnoideis instructae. description: Tree (6 m tall). Leafy twigs 1-2.5 cm thick, pale yellow-hirsute to -villous. Leaves palmately 5-parted to -fid, 30-70 cm long, 35-75 cm wide, coriaceous, apices of lobes acuminate, base deeply cordate with overlapping lobes; upper surface smooth, yellow-hirsute to -hirtellous on the main veins, lower surface yellow-subhirtellous to -subtomentose, on the main veins yellow-strigose to -subsericeous, in the areoles and on the smallest veins with minute arachnoid hairs; veins almost plane above, prominent beneath; free part of the midsegment with 12-18 pairs of lateral veins; petiole 25-65 cm long, sparsely yellow-hirsute to -strigose; stipules 15-20 cm long, subpersistent, outside densely yellow-villous to -hirsute and with dense white arachnoid hairs, inside sparsely hirsute to strigose. Pistillate inflorescence: peduncle 10 cm long, yellow-strigose to -hirsute and with white arachnoid hairs, branches 3, each with 3-5 flowers; pedicel ca 5 mm long, yellow-hirtellous to strigillose and with white arachnoid hairs; immature fruiting perianth 2 cm long, yellow-strigillose and with white arachnoid hairs, at the base hirsute; stigma peltate, 2 mm in diameter.

description: Arbor. Ramuli foliosi 3-5 mm crassi. Lamina integra, ovata vel subovata vel elliptica vel oblonga, 6-14 cm longa, 3-9.5 cm lata, plerumque subacuminata, basi obtusa vel truncata, subtus ad venas majores appresse flavo-puberula vel -strigillosa, praeterea pilis albis arachnoideis instructa; venae laterales 7-12 pro latere, par basale simplex; petiolus 2-9 cm longus; stipulae 1-3 cm longae, caducae, flavo-sericeae et pilis arachnoideis sparsae. Inflorescentia pistillata ramosa; pedunculus 3-5 cm longus; flores 7-10; perianthium appresse flavo-puberulum; stigma bilobum; paranthium fructiferum ovoideum, ca 2 cm longum.

description: Tree (11 m tall). Leafy twigs 3-5 mm thick, glabrous or sparsely and minutely yellow-appressed-puberulous. Leaves ovate or subovate to elliptic or oblong, 6-14 cm long, 3-9.5 cm wide, subcoriaceous, apex shortly subacuminate, base obtuse to truncate, margin entire; upper surface smooth, with a few yellow hairs on the costa and minute red-brown granular hairs on the main veins; lower surface yellow-appressed-puberulous to -strigillose on the main veins, elsewhere with white arachnoid hairs; above costa prominent, the other veins plane, beneath the main veins prominent, the other veins almost plane, 7-12 pairs of lateral veins, distinctly loop-connected, basal pair unbranched; petiole 2-9 cm long, 1-2 mm thick, glabrous or sparsely yellow-appressed-puberulous to -strigillose; stipules 1-3 cm long, caducous, outside yellow-sericeous and with sparse white arachnoid hairs, inside glabrous. Pistillate inflorescence: peduncle 3-5 cm long, sparsely yellow-appressed-puberulous to glabrous, with 3 branches, each bearing 1-5 flowers, usually a single flower at the apex of the peduncle; flowers 7-11; fruiting pedicel 3-6 (10) mm long, yellow-appressed-puberulous; perianth ca 4 mm long, yellow-appressed-puberulous, stigma ca 2.5 mm in diameter, distinctly 2-lobed; fruiting perianth ovoid, ca 2 cm long, almost glabrous.

description: Shrubs or small trees 2.4-4 m tall. Bark beige to gray superficially, dark reddish gray beneath, the indumentum short, pale-ferrugineous, shortly appressed-tomentose toward apices, fading to gray, glabrescent with age; lenticels numerous, inconspicuous, minute (<0.5 mm diam.), granular, raised, pale orange-brown or gray, contrasting somewhat with dark bark. Leaves simple or slightly lobed basally, thin-coriaceous, petiolate, pale green to yellow brown or pinkish brown when dry, the lower surface with minute red specks, the upper surface shiny, glabrous. Petiole well defined, 1-4 cm long X 1.25-3.5 mm broad at mid-length, ca. 1/10-1/5 the length of the lamina, canaliculate; adaxial surface with persistent tomentose indumentum, gradually becoming glabrescent. Lamina (8-)12-19 X (3.5-)4.5-10.5 cm, length:breadth ratio 1.5-2.5:1, oblong or narrowly (to broadly) obovate; base sometimes obscured by folding of lamina on pressing, symmetrical or strongly asymmetrical (specimens with lobed leaf), the sides of the lamina decurrent on petiole and forming an adaxial channel; apex obtuse to rounded and at times retuse, the midvein rarely protruding; margin entire to serrate with 13-29 pairs of serrations on each side, revolute toward base or not; venation plane to frequently sunken, moderately conspicuous above, prominent and conspicuous beneath, craspedodromous to semicraspedodromous; midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins in 6-8 pairs. Inflorescence axillary, unbranched, 14.5-21.5 X ca. 3 cm, short, orange-brown tomentose-pilose; peduncle 10-15 X 2-3 mm with a few sterile bracts at base; common bracts 0.4 X 0.6 mm, broader than long, short, ferrugineous-tomentose; flower-pair axis absent; pedicels very short, 0.2-0.5 X 1 mm, the indumentum as for inflorescence; flower buds 1.2 mm broad at apex, 0.5 mm broad at mid-length, short yellow orange tomentose. Flowers 15-17 mm long, the perianth indumentum as for inflorescence; filaments 0.6-1.3 mm long, attached 8-8.5 mm from base of tepals; anthers 1.8 X 0.5 mm; nectary lobes ca. 0.5 mm long, well separated; ovary laterally compressed, the ovary hairs extending 2.5-3.5 mm from base, covering entire ovary evenly, ferruginous or rufous, appressed, densely puberulent; ovules 0.6 X 0.3 mm. Infructescence 24-30 cm long, glabrous; fruiting pedicel not seen. Fruit (mature ?) 2.8 X 0.8-1.3 cm, grayish brown, glabrous, smooth, the sutured edge curved but flattened at top, the unsutured edge curved, the base and apex not constricted or briefly so, the apex weakly curved; style not persistent.

description: Dioecious small trees, to 12 m tall. Twigs terete or slightly angled, glabrous or with a few appressed hairs near the tip, 1-2 mm diam. 5 cm below the tip. Terminal buds appressed pubescent. Leaves alternate, chartaceous, 10-14.5 X 4-5 cm, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, glabrous on both surfaces, except for a few hairs in the axils of basal lateral veins on the lower surface, the base acute, apex acuminate, acumen 1-2 cm long, lateral veins 4-7, slightly impressed or immersed on the upper surface, loop- connected toward the margin, weakly raised on lower surface, the angle with the midrib blunt, from 60?-90?. Petioles grooved, gla- brous, 4-6 mm long. Inflorescences axillary, branched from the base, sometimes with some appressed hairs near the base, otherwise glabrous, laxly paniculate-cymose, 3-8 cm long. Pedicels glabrous, 1-6 mm long, slender. Male flowers yellowish, ca. 3 mm diam., the tepals spreading at an- thesis, glabrous on both surfaces, 1-1.2 mm long, stamens 9, all 4-celled, the outer 6 opening introrse, the cells arranged in 2 rows, glabrous, 0.6-0.8 mm long, the fila- ments distinct, but shorter than anthers, in- ner 3 stamens ca. 0.8 mm long, filaments with 2 globose glands near the base, the cells lateral-extrorse, staminodia not seen, pistillode slender, glabrous, with a small stigma, receptacle shallow, densely pubes- cent inside. Female flowers not known. Fruit ellipsoid, 2 X 1 cm, cupule shallow, resembling a golf tee, pedicel thickened to- ward the cupule.
bibliographicCitation: van der Werff, Hendrik H. 1997. A new species of Ocotea (Lauraceae) from French Guiana. Brittonia. 49: 189-191.

description: Similar to var. cyltindrica except in the following characters: petioles (0.5-) 1.0-11.0 cm long; blades 0.8-5.0 (-6.0) cm long, 0.6-4.5 (-5.5) cm wide, the base (rounded or) truncate to moderately cordate, the sinus always open, and the lobes of the principal leaves with rounded to obtusely pointed teeth, slightly to conspicuously mueronate; leaves grayish-green, densely glandular-puberulent and with few to many admixed longer hairs especially below. Scapes 22.0-50.0 (-60.0) cm high usually with 1-2 small, yellowish, ciliate bracts; panicle 2.0-10.0 (-13.0) cm long, 1.0-2.0 (-2.5) cm wide; eymules 1-3(-4)-flowered; bracts 2.5-5.0 mm long, 0.5-1.3 mm wide exeluding cilia. Sepals (2.0-) 2.5-4.0 mm long, 1.3-2.0 (-2.5) mm wide; capsules 6.0-8.0 mm long.

description: Ab omnibus speciebus generis foliis deciduis, foliolis sessilibus parvis, utrinque stellatis-tomentosis, et racemis parvis gracilibus floribus paucis 4-meris optime distincta.

description: Shrub or treelet 2-5 m tall, dioecious, deciduous, unarmed, with terminal buds protected by densely tomentose, thick, concave scales; branches glabrescent, unarmed, the bark greyish brown, distally nodulose (with crowded scars conspicuous on previous year's growth). Leaves imparipinnately compound with (4-)7-1 1 pairs of leaflets, 5-8 cm long; the petiole narrowly winged, 8-15 mm long; the rachis narrowly winged, slightly grooved above, 30-45 mm long, unarmed or occasionally sparsely armed with 1-3 straight, small prickles, densely to sparsely stellate-hairy as the petiole. Leaflets membranaceous, densely dotted with pellucid, spherical glands, opposite to subopposite, sessile, oblong (the terminal one sometimes narrowly elliptic), retuse to emarginate at apex, rounded and oblique at base, with revolute margin, adaxially dull green, with sparse, small stellate trichomes, abaxially paler green, densely covered by stellate trichomes much larger than the adaxial ones, the distal leaflets 10-17 x 2-5 mm, the basal leaflets 3-7 x 1.5-3.0 mm; venation brochidodromous, sunken adaxially, weakly raised abaxially, the midvein straight, the secondary veins ca. 5-9 on each  side of midvein, straight, ascending at 60?- 700 from perpendicular. Inflorescence of crowded racemes, appearing on new shoots with first leaves, borne below these or rarely in the axils. Staminate racemes 12-20 mm long, slender, with ca. 9-12 flowers, the axis and bracts densely stellate-pilose, the bracts linear-lanceolate, to 1 mm long. Staminate flowers 4-merous, whitish green, the pedicel ca. 1.5 mm long, densely covered by simple and stellate trichomes; sepals lanceolate ca. 1 mm long, sparsely pilose with simple, erect, subulate trichomes mixed with rare stellate ones; petals linear-oblong, to 1.5 mm long, acute, densely and irregularly pubescent along margins, with scattered simple hairs on abaxial surface; stamens 4, ca. 2 mm long, the filaments subulate with scattered hairs on lower half, the anthers subglobose, glabrous; pistillodium conical and curved, ca. 0.6 mm long, glabrous, with a short style and a small locule with 2 abortive, pendulous ovules, surrounded at the base by the annular, glabrous disc. Pistillate racemes 6- 1 1 mm, the axis, bracts, and pedicels densely stellate-pilose, the bracts lanceolate. Pistillate flowers 4-merous, the pedicel ca. 0.5 mm long; sepals lanceolate, with simple trichomes along margins and small stellate trichomes on abaxial surface; petals ca. 1 mm long, oblong, stellate-pilose; staminodia not seen; disc annular, glabrous; gynoecium of 1 carpel, subglobose, subglabrous (scattered stellate hairs), glandular-foveolate, the style terete, smooth and lateral (on suture of car- pel), erect, with a discoid stigma. Infruc- tescence 10-25 mm long. Fruit an oblique, subglobose follicle, 1-seeded, stipitate, 5-7 mm in diam., glandular-bullate, with both small stellate trichomes with 2-5 arm-cells and simple trichomes; sepals persistent or not; seed subglobose, black, shiny, pendulous.
bibliographicCitation: Pirani, José R. 1993. A new species and a new combination in Zanthoxylum (Rutaceae) from Brazil. Brittonia. 45: 154-158.

description: Perennial herb, hairy throughout, 10-30 (6-38) cm tall, branched at or near the base and in the inflorescence; leaves opposite near the base or alternate through- out, linear-lanceolate or the lower elliptic, overlapping at least near the base of the plant, the larger 8-12 (6-17) mm long, 1.3-1.9 (0.9-3.3) mm wide, sessile, entire or the upper and the floral bracts with marginal glands, acuminate or sharp pointed, sometimes tipped with a dark gland; stipular glands evident, sometimes at the bases of the sepals as well as leaves and floral bracts; sepals lanceolate to narrowly ovate, sharp pointed to acuminate, 3.2-4.0 (2.7-5.0) mm long, with conspicuous glandular teeth, sometimes ending in a dark gland; petals orange-yellow, narrowly oblanceolate, 4-10 mm long, pilose at the base; stamens glabrous or sparsely hairy, filaments broadened at the base, 4-7 mm long; staminodia deltoid or sometimes none; anthers 0.5-1.0 mm long; styles separate, 2.5-6.3 mm long; fruit broadly ovate, 2.4-2.8 (2.3-3.0) mm high, 2.3-3.0 mm in diameter, glabrous; false septa nearly complete; septa ciliate; seeds reddish brown, elliptic to ovate, 1.4-1.7 mm long, 0.8-1.1 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Glabrous, somewhat glaucous annual or more commonly perennial herb, 23-68 cm tall, branched from near the base, the branches rather stiffly ascending-spreading; leaves opposite near the base, alternate above, or occasionally alternate throughout, entire or usually the middle and upper very sparsely and inconspicuously toothed, the larger commonly with two well defined lateral nerves, basal leaves imbricate, oblanceolate, acute or rounded at the apex, middle cauline leaves larger, lanceolate or oblanceolate, the larger 8-19 mm long, 0.7-3.5 mm wide; stipular glands none; inflorescence open, with stiffly spreading-ascending branches; fruits on pedicels up to 3-14 mm long; sepals ovate to lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 3.0-4.5 mm long, the outer entire or sparsely glandular-toothed above the middle, the inner nearly as long, glandular-toothed; petals white or purplish, oblanceolate, glabrous, 5-8 mm long; stamens 2-3 mm long, filaments broadened at the base with "stami- nodia" present as basal shoulders on either side; anthers elliptic, 0.6-0.8 mm long; styles separate, 1.1-2.0 mm long; fruit ovate-pyriform, suffused with purple near the summit, 2.3-2.7 mm high, 2.3-2.8 mm in diameter, easily crushed, readily dehiscing into 10 segments; false septa only partially developed; septa ciliate along the margins; seeds narrowly to broadly ovate, 1.5-1.8 mm long, 0.8-1.1 mm wide, reddish brown.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Coarse perennial herb, 37-73 (27-117) cm tall (or more since small plants were probably collected), branched at the base or more or less throughout; stems glabrous or occasionally with scattered hairs, these more abundant near the base; leaves opposite or sometimes whorled near the base, alternate above, narrowly lanceolate to oblanceolate or lance-ovate, the largest near the center of the stem, 15-32 mm long, 4-11 mm wide, entire or with a few diminutive glandular teeth, narrowed to a short petiole, pinnately veined, with one pair of rather prominent lateral nerves; stipular glands present; inflorescence ample, but branches rather short; sepals ovate to obovate, 2.2-2.6 (1.8-4) mm long, acute or shortly acuminate, glabrous within, usually entire or sometimes with a few marginal glands on the inner or on all, the outer occasionally with a small tuft of hairs at the apex; petals yellow, obovate or obcordate, 3-6 mm long; stamens 2-4 mm long; staminodia when present very slender; anthers 0.2-0.5 mm long, broadly elliptic; styles 0.9-2.0 mm long, united at the base, but occasionally nearly separate or rarely united nearly to the middle; fruit triangular-ovate, 1.8-2.3 mm high, 2.2-2.6 mm in diameter, readily dehiscing into 10 sharp pointed segments, suffused with purple in the upper half; false septa partially developed, the true septa ciliate; seeds elliptic to ovate, 1.1-1.3 mm long, 0.7 mm wide, reddish brown.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Small tree to ca. 10 m high and 10 em in diameter at breast height; older individuals commonly with a strong basal shoot, sometimes becoming somewhat shrubby, often sprouting from the stump; bark thin, light to dark brown, finely checked vertically with fewer cross-checks; angles of young first-year twigs sometimes winged; petioles 1-7 mm long; blade coriaceous, rarely lareeolate to ovate to elliptic or rhombie-elliptic to obovate, 3-10.5 cm long, 1.5-5.5 cm wide; margin often revolute, the base cuneate, attenuate to the petiole, the apex narrowly acute to broadly rounded to slightly emarginate, sometimes mucronulate; midrib usually rounded below, sometimes rectangular at the middle, very rarely with tiny incomplete wings; lateral veins visible above and below in very large leaves, both fresh and dried, usually visible only above; young leaves when fresh a smooth, glossy green above, pale green and scarcely shining below; older leaves less shiny above and dull below; dried leaves sometimes shiny above, dull below, the surfaces smooth or punctulate; stomatal crypts when regularly present 30-170/mm2, their cavities averaging 30-65 µ in diameter; central bodies of foliar terminal selereids typically elongate, 2-4 times as long as wide, but sometimes isodiametric; upper epidermis predominantly single, rarely with up to 40 per cent of the cells doubled, the inner walls of the epidermal cells never mucilage-thickened; fresh leaves without aromatic odor when crushed, faintly speckled when held to the light. Racemes 1-5 per leaf axil, 2-26 mm high to the ovary base of the terminal flower, the joints in the central axis 1-3, the flowers per raceme 1-7, the bracts at the joints (rarely one also at the ovary base) triangular or ovate-triangular, acute to acuininate, 1.0 mm long, soonl deciduous; length of the true pedicel (ovary to first joint below) 1.5-6 mm. Inferior ovary 1.2-1.7 mm high, campanulate to cup-shaped or approaching turbinate, the angle "o" (fig. 6) 120°-155°; length of the calyx (including ovary height) 3.7-5.6 mm (dry measurements 3.5-5.1 mm); ratio of length of calyx to width of calyx-lobe 1.5-3.1; calyx-lobes 0.9-2.1 mm high from the stamen attachment, 1.5-4 mm wide, 0.4-1.05 times as high as wide, truncate with rounded shoulders to broadly rounded to low-triangular to rarely minutely apiculate, the shoulders sometimes expanded into rounded lobes (figs. 10, 11), the margins minutely fringed with short hairs; fusion distance of adjacent lobes above the stamen attachment 0.4-0.9 mm, the ratio of fusioll distance to width of lobe 0.15-0.45; petals yellow, white, pink, or violet, broadly ovate, often crinkled below, 5-8 mm long, 4-7 mm wide, the base rounded to truncate or slightly cordate to a short claw 0.8-1.0 mm long and 1 mm wide, the apex acute; filaments white; pollen sacs yellow; anthers 1.75-2.5 mm long; stamens and style often slightly zygomorphic, most stamens oriented with the gland upward; ovary (2-) 3-5-locular, 9-18-ovuled; ripe fruits yellow to red-orange, 1-4-seeded, approximately globose when 1-seeded, then 12-15 mm in diameter, lobed according to the number of seeds, up to 30 mm in diameter with 2-4 seeds, their dry measurements 3-4 mm less; fruit thinly fleshed, with slightly sweet, insipid flavor.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1957. A Revision of Mouriri, Section Nesophytum. Brittonia. 9 (2): 109-131.

description: Stomatal crypts when regularly present 90-170/mm2, the cavity averaging 30-33 µ in diameter; raceme to the ovary base of the terminal flower 2-9 mm high; flowers per raceme 1-3; length of the true pedicel 1-4.5 mm; length of the calyx ca. 3.7-5.0 mm (dry measurements 3.5-4.7 mm); ratio of length of calyx to width of calyx-lobe 2.1-3.1; ratio of width to heigfht of ovary (not dried) 1.15-1.45; locules 2-4; ovules 9-12.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1957. A Revision of Mouriri, Section Nesophytum. Brittonia. 9 (2): 109-131.

description: Small to medium tree; angles of young first-year twigs with or without narrow wings; petioles usually winged, 2-8 mm long, usually 0.1 or more the blade length when measured to the abrupt curve at the blade base; blade ovate-elliptic to narrowly or broadly elliptic to slightly obovate, 2.5-6.5 cm long, (1.0-) 1.4-3.8 cm wide, usually mnore thall half as wide as long; margin often somewhat revolute, the base usually abruptly aeuminate into the winged petiole, the apex narrowly to broadly rounded to broadly and slightly emarginate, sometimes mucronulate; midrib below flat to rounded to rectangular, often the two angles with very narrow wings; lateral veins sometimes visible above and below in dried material; dried leaf-surface above minutely rugulose or rarely punctulate, the lower surface smoother; stomiatal crypts when regularly present 25-50/mm2, their cavities averaging 55-60 µ in diameter; central bodies of foliar terminal selereids when elongate 2.5-3 times as long as wide, their arms prominent, their length 0.5-1.5 times the body thickness, 5-40 per cent of the selereids having the body very short and with a stellate appearance; upper epidermis predominantly single, rarely with up to 20 per cent of the cells doubled, the inner walls of the epideriilal cells never mucilage-thickened. Racenles 1 per leaf axil, 9-25 mm high to the ovary base of the terminal flower, the joints in the central axis 2 or 3, the flowers per racemne 1-3(-6), the bracts at the joints ovate-triangular, acute, 1.5 mm long, soon (leciduous; length of the true pedicel (ovary base to first joint below) 2.5-5.5 mm. Inferior ovarv 2-2.6 mm high, turbinate, the sides only slightly convex, angle "o" (fig. 6) 158°-166° or more; length of the calyx (ineluding the ovary height) ca. 6.5 mm fresh, 6.0 mm dry; ratio of length of calyx to width of calyx-lobe 3.2-3.6; calyx-lobes 1.7-2.5 mm high from the stamen attachment, 1.7-2.1 mm wide, 1-1.2 times as long as wide, the free ends triangular to half-elliptic (figs. 15, 16), rarely almost truneate, the margins fringed with short hairs; fusion distance of adjacent lobes above the stamen attachment 0.85-1.0 (av. 0.95) mnm, the lobes separating at anthesis; ratio of fusion distance to width of lobe 0.45-0.57; petals white to pale pink, purple on the midrib, ovate-cordate to broadly oblong to orbicular, 6-7 mm long, 4.5-6 mm wide, the base with a claw to 1 mm long and ca. 0.7 mm wide, the apex apiculate or shortly and abruptly acuminate, the margin irregularly crisped below; anthers 2.45-2.7 mm long; ovary 2- or 3-locular, 8-11-ovuled; fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1957. A Revision of Mouriri, Section Nesophytum. Brittonia. 9 (2): 109-131.

description: Glabrous, glaucous annual, or probably perennial, herb, 25-40 cm tall, more or less branched throughout; leaves opposite at the base or alternate throughout, linear to linear-lanceolate, the larger 11-17 mm long, 1-1.7 mm wide; stipular glands sometimes present on lower part of stem, usually absent; inflorescence paniculate, more or less diffuse, the branches slender; sepals narrowly lanceolate, 2-5.6 mm long, sharply acute, sparsely glandular-toothed; petals narrowly obovate or oblanceolate, 4-8 mm long, brownish red upon drying; stamens 2-4 mm long; staminodia in pairs, low, deltoid, or sometimes absent; anthers 0.6-1.0 mm long; styles 1.4-2.4 mm long, varying from nearly free to united about one-half way; fruit broadly ovate, pointed, 2.4-3.3 mm high, 2.3-2.6 mm in diameter, freely dehiscing nearly to the base into 10 segments; false septa incomplete; septa sparsely, but conspicuously ciliate along the margin; seeds 1.6-2 mm long, 1.0-1.2 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Wing-lines on young growing twigs conspicuous; midrib below rectangular, prominent, with or without narrow wings at the angles; height of inflorescence to the ovary base of the terminal flower 11-25 mmn; calyx-lobes triangular (fig. 16), 1.7-2.0 mm long.

description: Small to medium tree, in favorable situations up to 16 m high andl 20 cm in diameter at breast height, sometimes sprouting from the stump, the bark brown, finely corrugated vertically; young first-year twigs consistently winged at the angles; petioles 0.5-3.5 mm long; blade coriaceous, ovate-elliptic to obovate, 2.6-8 cm lonlg, 1.3-4.5 cm wide; margin sometimes revolute, the base acute or attenuate to the petiole, the apex rarely broadly acute to rounded to emarginate, often mucronate; midrib below rectangular or the two angles with very narrow wings at least in the mid-region; lateral veins invisible below, usually visible above only in very large leaves; young leaves when fresh a smooth very shiny dark green above, less shiny and lighter below; older leaves duller; dried leaves only rarely shiny above, dull below, the upper surface minutely rugulose, the lower less so; stolmiatal crypts when regularly present 15-60/mm2, their cavities averaging 40-95 µ in diameter; central bodies of the foliar terminal selereids isodiametric to twice as long as broad, sometimes longer; upper epidermis predominantly double, more than 40 per cent of the cells doubled, the ilnner walls of some of the inner cells mucilage-thickened as well as those of some of the lower epidermlial cells, or only the latter so thickened; fresh leaves not aromatic wheni crushed, faintly speckled when held to the light. Racemes 1-3 per leaf axil, 6-18 mm high to the ovary base of the terminal flower; joints in the central axis 1 or 2, the flowers per raceme 1-3 (-4), the bracts at the joints ovate-triangular, acute, 1-1.5 mm long, soon deciduous; length of the true pedicel (ovary to first joint below) 2-8 mm. Inferior ovary 1.4-2.5 mm high, narrowly cup-shaped to niearly obconic, the anglle "o" (fig. 6) 145°-168°; length of the calyx (ineluding ovary height) 5.0-6.7 mm (dry measurements ca. 4.8-6.5 mm), ratio of length of calyx to width of calyx-lobe 2.7-4.3; calyx-lobes 1.7-3.0 mm high from the stamen attachment, 1.2-2.3 mm wide, 0.85-1.9 times as bigh as wide, the free ends triangular to apiculate to cuspidate to acuminate (figs. 12-14), the margins minutely and irregularly fringed with short hairs; fusion distance of adjacent lobes above the stameln attachment 0.7-1.9 mm, the lobes separating at anthesis; ratio of fusion distance to width of calyx-lobe 0.45-1.25; petals yellow, white, light purple, or red, ovate to narrowly ovate-triangular, 4.5-6.5 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, the margins often irregularly and minutely crenulate, the base truncate or with a short claw ca. 0.7 mm wide and to 0.7 mm long, the apex acute to acuminate; anthers 1.95-2.5 mm long; ovary 1-3-locular, 7-11-ovuled; fruit globose, 1-seeded [Urban in his description of M. rostrata (1926) described its fruits as having 1 or 2 seeds; I have been unable to verify this], its dry measurements 8-10 mm in diameter, 9-12 mm lolng, thinly fleshed.

description: Fruit ovoid, 8 mm diam., 12 mm long, with pericarp 0.6 mm thick, stigmatic remains apical. Pericarp is distinctive for the very large raphide-bearing cells that fill the outer half of the pericarp and for the lack of brachysclereids and tanniniferous cells in the outer pericarp; fibrous bundles large, terete to slightly radially distended, in a single series just below mid-pericarp, vascular bundles somewhat flattened, with moderately thick fibrous sheaths, in a single series along with small, flattened, tanniniferous cells in the inner pericarp; locular epidermis sclerified but thin.

description: A soft-wooded shrub, about 50 cm tall, the upper internodes rather slender, 3-8 cm long, thinly pubescent, glabrescent, glandular-dotted. Leaves "dark-green above, paler below" when growing, elliptic-ovate, rather abruptly acuminate, the base inequilaterally rounded, obtuse or acutish, one side about 2 mm shorter at the petiole, 9-10 cm long and 4-5 cm wide, pale-glandular-dotted on both sides, glabrous above, the nerves beneath thinly appressed-hirtellous, pinnately nerved to the upper fourth or throughout, the nerves about 5 or 6 on each side, submarginally loop-connected, with slender, cross-connecting-anastomosing nervules, finely pellucid-dotted, drying rather thin, subtranslucent, the petioles from 2-3 mm long above to 1 cm on lower leaves, thinly hirtellous, vaginate-winged to the blade on lower leaves. Racemes (?) as yet young, 1.5 cm long and 2 mm thick, apiculate, the peduncle slender, scarcely 1 cm long, thinly hirtellous, the bracts triangular-subpeltate, narrowly fringed; stamens 4, closely appressed about the as yet very immature ovary, the ovary on a hirtellous pedicel.

description: A soft-wooded subshrub, about 50 cm tall, the upper internodes short above, lengthening downward, densely crisp-pubescent, the hairs subreflexed. Leaves oblong-elliptic or lance-elliptic, gradually acuminate, the base somewhat inequilateral, rounded cordulate or the larger leaves cordate, one side about 1-2 mm shorter at the petiole, 10-14 cm long and 3-5 cm wide, glabrous above, the nerves beneath densely crisp-hirtellous, the hairs subappressed, pale-glandulardotted, the margin strongly ciliolate throughout, pinnately nerved to the middle or sometimes throughout, the nerves commonly 5 or 6 on each side, submarginally loop-connected, when nerved to about the middle the uppermost lateral nerves connected with the midrib with cross-connecting nervules upward, drying rather thin, translucent, densely minutely pellucid-dotted, the petiole becoming about 1 cm long, densely crisp-pubescent, vaginate-winged to the blade. Racemes (?) as yet immature, 2 cm long and 2 mm thick, the peduncle about 5 mm long, densely crisp-pubescent, the bracts triangular-subpeltate, marginally fringed; stamens 4, closely appressed about the immature, globose (?) ovary, ovary pedicellate, the pedicel glabrous.

description: Frutex epiphyticus vel terrestris. Ramuli sicut petioli, folia inflorescentia hypanthiaque pilis 0.5-3(-6) mm longis induti. Folia in quoque pari dimorpha papyracea subintegra vel obscure distanterque denticulata elliptica vel elliptico-ovata apice acuminata vel caudato- acuminata basi asymmetrice obtusa vel rotundata 3-5- plinervata. Folia maiora: larnina 7.5-17.2 X 3.5-7.5 cm. Folia minora: lamina 1.8-10 X 1.7-5.4 cm. Flores 6-meri in quoque nodo superiore singuli; bracteae omnino liberae; bracteae exteriores 2.5-3.2 X 1.7-2.6 cm ovatae vel subcordatae; bracteae interiores elliptico-lanceolatae 1.9-2.5 X 0.7-1 cm. Calycis tubus 2 mm longus, lobis 6-7 X 1 mm. Petala 1.6-2.3 X 1.4-1.7 cm obovato-oblonga. Antherarum thecae 5-7.5 X 1 mm subulatae inter se non cohaerentes, dorsaliter bi- porosae; connectivum ad basim per ca. 0.5 mm ele- vatum, calcari hebeti descendenti ca. 1 mm longo. Ovarium 6-loculare et 1/2 inferum, collo 1-1.5 mm longo hebeti-lobulato glabro.

description: Epiphytic or terrestrial shrub 1-2 m tall with spreading branches to 3 m long. Uppermost branchlets rounded. Cauline internodes, vegetative buds, leaf blades (both surfaces), peduncles, floral bracts, hypanthia, and calyx lobes moderately to copiously hirsute with smooth feiruginous hairs mostly 0.5-3(-6) mm long. Mature leaves of a pair typically unequal in size; petioles 0.3-1.5 cm long; blades thin and papery when dry, the larger one at each node 7.5- 17.2 X 3.5-7.5 cm, the smaller one 1.8-10 X 1.7-5.4 cm, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, base obliquely obtuse to rounded, margin denticulate to subentire (sometimes obscurely and remotely so), 3-5-plinerved with the inner- most pair of primary veins diverging from the median vein 1-5 mm above the blade base, the transverse secondary veins spaced 2-6 mm apart at the widest portion of the blade. Flowers erect or horizontally spreading, solitary in the axils of uppermost branches; peduncles 3.5-5.2 cm long, terete. Floral bracts green and entire; outer bracts 2.5-3.2 X 1.7-2.6 cm, free, ovate to subcordate, apex acute to acuminate, trinerved; inner bracts 1.9-2.5 X 0.7-1 cm, the basal half closely appressed to but free from the hypanthium, narrowly elliptic-lanceolate, apex acute to acuminate. Hypanthium (at anthesis) suburceolate when dry, 6-6.5 mm long to the torus and 6 mm diam. Calyx tube 2 mm long and flaring horizontally at anthesis. Calyx lobes (at anthesis) linear oblong, 6-7 mm long and 1 mm wide at the +i deltoid base between sinuses. Petals 6, glabrous, 1.6-2.3 X 1.4-1.7 cm, white flushed with pink distally on the abaxial surface, thin and translucent when dry, obovate, apex rounded, base shortly clawed, entire. Stamens 12, isomorphic, filaments 5-6.5 X 1 mm, declinate, complanate, glabrous; anthers free, 5-7.5 X 1 mm, yellow, oblong-subulate and incurved distally, each with 2 confluent dorsally inclined pores at the truncate apex; connective thickened dorsobasally into a blunt deflexed appendage 0.5-1 mm long. Ovary 1/2-inferior (at anthesis), 6-locular, glabrous at the summit, which is elevated into a lobulate collar 1-1.5 mm high surrounding the style base. Style glabrous, 0.9-1.4 cm long; stigma punctiform. Berry red at maturity, globose, 1-1.7 X 1.3-1.4 cm. Seeds mostly 1 mm long, beige, cuneate to narrowly pyriform, testa smooth.

description: A shrub 5 dm. tall, apparently rooting in humus. Younger stems densely tomentose with slender, yellowish, flexuous hairs up to 2 mm. long, later glabreseent; internodes up to 20 cm. long. Petioles slender, 3 cm. long or somewhat less, pubescent like the stem, also setose on the upper side with stout, subpaleaceous, roughened setae up to 6 mm. long. Leaf-blades thin, broadly ovate, up to 15 cm. long and 11 cm. wide, abruptly acuminate, obscurely crenulate, finely ciliate, cordulate at the base, 7-nerved, above pilose when young, soon glabreseent, beneath sparsely pubeseent on the veins with crooked hairs up to 1.5 mm. long. Pedunele 2 cm. long, short-setose or tomentose; flowers crowded in a cyme 2 cm. long; bracts stoutly subulate, about 1 mm. long. Flowers 5-merous. IHypanthium reddish, suburceolate, 3.3 mm. long, sparsely pubeseent with slender flexuous hairs up to 0.1 mm. long, or considerably longer distally, obscurely 5-ribbed. Calyx-tube somewhat flaring, 0.4 mm. long; sepals broadly round-ovate, 1.4 mm. long from the torus, minutely pubescent, separated by acute sinuses; exterior teeth half adnate, triangular below, subulate above, 2 mm. long, sparsely setose. Petals oblong, 7-7.5 mm. long. Filaments flattened below, thickened above, 3 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, 2.5 mm. long, the pore dorso-terminal; connective simple, slightly gibbous near the base. Ovary four-fifths inferior, 5-celled, glabrous on the rounded summit; style 6.5 mm. long, tapering to a subglobose stigma.

description: A shrub about a meter high, epiphytic or terrestrial. Stems stout, densely reverse-strigose with stout hairs up to 3 mm. long, flattened at the base, pubescent on the sides, underlaid by a thin indument of slender crooked hairs about 0.3 mm. long; internodes about 5 cm. long. Petioles stout, 1-3 cm. long, pubescent like the stem. Leaf-blades firm, broadly ovate, up to 15 cm. long by 10 cm. wide, acute or subacuminate, minutely serrate, broadly rounded to subcordate at the base, 7-nerved, above bullate, hirtellous with stiff hairs nearly 1 mm. long, beneath foveolate, very minutely pubescent on the veins, glabrous on the surface. Cymes crowded, 1-3 cm. long, of which about half is peduncle, densely bristly. Flowers 5-merous, nearly sessile. Hypanthium red, campanulate, 3 mm. long, freely punctate, otherwise glabrous. Calyx-tube prolonged 0.4 mm., erect, sparsely setose with straight stiff hairs up to 3 mm. long; sepals red, erect, firm, triangular-ovate, 1.8 mm. long from the torus, rounded or broadly obtuse; exterior teeth arising above the sinuses, stoutly subulate, 2.5 mm. long from the torus. Petals and stamens lacking. Ovary wholly inferior, 5-celled, its summit slightly concave.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1939. The genus Clidemia in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 3 (2): 97-130.

description: A shrub 3-5 meters high. Younger stems terete, essentially glabrous, but bearing a few short setae, especially near the nodes. Petioles slender, 2-4 cm. long, glabrous beneath, setose along the top with slender hairs up to 3 mm. long. Leaf-blades thin, ovate-elliptic, up to 13 cm. long by 8 cm. wide, abruptly acuminate, minutely crenulate, ciliate with pale hairs 1-2 mm. long, broadly obtuse to rounded at the base, 5-nerved, sparsely setose above, the hairs 1-2 mm. long and 2-4 mm. apart, glabrous beneath. Panicles spreading, trichotomous, 2-4 cm. long, very sparsely and remotely setose; bracts subulate, about 1 mm. long, of which nearly two-thirds is in the terminal seta. Flowers sessile, 4-merous. Fruiting hypanthium globular, sparsely glandular-hirsute, the hairs spreading, about 2 mm. long. Sepals semicircular, 0.4 mm. long from the torus; exterior teeth conic, deflexed from the middle of the sepal, the free portion 0.3 mm. long. Petals and stamens lacking.

description: Shrub about a meter high. Stems slender, reddish, essentially glabrous. Petioles slender, divaricate, very irregular in len-gth, 1-4.5 cm. long, glabrous or nearly so toward the base, toward the summit pubescent with incurved hairs 0.1 mm. long. Leaf-blades thin, dark green, ovate, often very unequal in each pair, the larger up to 12 cm. long by 6 cm. wide, the smaller about a third as large, slenderly acuminate, very obscurely serrulate and minutely ciliate, broadly rounded to slightly cordate at the base, 5-nerved, essentially glabrous above but short-setose at long intervals and closely white-punctate, beneath paler, pubescent on the primaries toward the base with minute hairs like those of the petiole, becoming glabrous distally and on the surface. Panicles loosely branched, up to 10 cm. long, the principal axes minutely and sparsely hirtellous, the very slender elongate branches apparently long-pedicelled, the actual pedicels about 1 mm. long. Hypanthium campanulate, 2.6 mm. long, purple, thin-walled, apparently glabrous and red-punctate, actually closely pubescent with ascending-ineurved hairs 0.04 mm. long. Calyx spreading, its tube 0.3 mm. wide; sepals broadly triangular, 0.7 mm. long from the torus, acute, separated by rounded sinuses; exterior teeth almost free from the sepals, divaricate, about 1 mm. long from the torus. Petals oblongovate, 2.6 mm. long, obtuse, slightly inequilateral. Filaments stout, 1.4 mm. long; anthers oblong, 1.6 mm. long, the pore terminal; connective simple. Ovary wholly inferior, 3-celled, its flat top glabrous; style slender, 4.8 mm. long; stigma truncate.

description: Shrub or small tree 1.3-5 m tall, the trunk 3-6 cm diam; branchlets fasciculate, subterete, grayish.
