description: Scandent shrubs to 3 m tall; stems slender. Leaves bipinnate; pinnae consistently 1-jugate; petioles eglandular, 1.5-5 cm long, glabrous; rachilla with a conspicuous channel adaxially, 2-5.5 cm long, glabrous; leaflets 2 pairs, rarely 1 per pinna, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, cuneate at the base, acuminate to aristate at the apex, (7-)8.8-10.8 X 3.1-4.4 cm, the proximal ones smaller, chartaceous-membranous, usually drying a light green abaxially, lustrous adaxially, glabrous; leaflet venation conspicuous, with a single central, primary vein, primary and secondary veins prominent; stipules caducous. Capitula axillary or arranged in relatively long, simple pseudopaniculate inflorescences; peduncles usually fasciculate at distant nodes, filiform, 5.8 cm long at anthesis. Flowers sessile, pentam- erous, glabrous throughout, aromatic; calyx cup-shaped, ca. 2 mm long, the teeth linear- lanceolate; corolla campanulate, ca. 4 mm long, the lobes lanceolate; filaments fused at base, white; polyads 16-grained, discoid, ca. 90 pLm diam., heteromorphic, with eccentric lens-shaped thickenings on the central grains. Pods elastically dehiscent, linear, with the apex acute, rostellate, thickly membranous, glabrous.

description: Sporophore single to gregarious or concrescent. Pileus up to 8 cm broad, convex to plane, depressed in weathered specimens, lobed, cottony tomentose becoming matted or glabrous towards disc, often pitted or colliculose, white (4A1), yellowish white (4A2), pastel yellow (4A4), dark blonde (5D4), light brown (6C6-6C8), bruised areas grayish violet (19C3) to blackish blue (19E4-19F8), margin (20F4); context up to 1 cm thick, not obviously duplex, zonate (20C5), white (4A1) to yellowish white (4A2), portions grayish violet (19C3) with pastel blue (20A4) zones; taste slightly disagreeable; odor slightly fragrant. Stipe up to 3 x 1.5 cm, central, terete with a slightly bulbous base, tomentose below to matted or glabrous above, concolorous to grayish orange (6B6) or reddish gold (6C7); context duplex, zonate, spongy subsurface layer, hard at center, concolorous. Spines up to 6 mm long, decurrent, crowded, white (6A1), orange white (5A2), light brown (6D8), tan (6E6) to dark brown (6F8) or violet brown (10F8). Chemical reactions: context tissue olive green in KOH or NH4OH. Pileus trama hyphae up to 7 µm diam, uninflated, interwoven in subsurface layer, subparallel below, clamps rare to locally abundant; gloeoplerous-like hyphae up to 7 µm diam. Stipe hyphae up to 7.5 µm diam, some thick-walled, uninflated, interwoven in subsurface layer to parallel at center, clamps not seen; gloeoplerous- like hyphae up to 9 µm diam. Spine trama hyphae up to 6 µm diam, uninflated, clamps not seen. Basidia 29-60 (80) x 6.5-9 (11) µm (x = 52.35 ± 10.78 x 8.76 ± 1.16 µm), clavate, clamps (X= 6.2 ± 0.86 µm). Basidiospores 5-6.2 x 4.5-5.5 gm (x = 5.69 ± 0.23 x 4.77 ± 0.42 µm), subglobose, brownish; ornamentation tuberculate (Fig. 1D), not prominent, rounded to flattened.
bibliographicCitation: Park, Chong Wook. 1986. Nomenclatural changes in Polygonum section Echinocaulon (Polygonaceae). Brittonia. 38: 217-219.

description: Loosely tufted, annual herbs. Stems 16-20 cm, 1-2.5 mm diam., decumbent ascending, glabrate, internodes to 1.5-2 cm; stipules amplexicaul, connate though >1/2 their length, sheath shortly bidentate, adnate to petiole, decurrent, membranous, glabrous, ciliate, 8-10 mm; leaflets 11-13, short-petiolulate, hairs glandular and axillary, opposite to subopposite, distant ca. 1 cm on the rachis, elliptic to ovate, 12-15 X 2.3-2.4 mm, emarginate, base cuneate, glabrous above, white-strigose to glabrate below. Peduncles (2.5-)4 cm long, erect; racemes loosely 7-8-flowered, flowers distant, 0.8-1 cm between them; bracts subulate, glabrous, ciliolate, 3-4 mm; bracteoles 2; pedicels 2.5-4 mm erect, ascending, recurved in age; calyx 4.5-6.5 mm, white and black-strigulose, tube campanulate, 3-4 mm, teeth subulate, 1.5-2.5 mm; petals blue-violet; banner moderately recurved, suborbicular to ovate, emarginate 11-15 X 9-10 mm; wings nearly as long, the claw 3-4 mm, the rectangulate obtuse blades 9 X 3 mm; keel 9-10 mm; the claws 3-4 mm; ovary glabrous, stigma capitellate; ovules 17-21. Fruit spreading to deflexed, subsessile, the stipe concealed in the hypanthial cup, when mature disjointing from the receptacle, elliptic, 1.3-1.5 X 0.3-0.5 cm, straight, rounded at base, abruptly contracted at apex into a 1.5-2 mm cusp, valves smooth, lustrous green, subcamosulus, becoming coriaceous and stramineous with its nerves in an elevated network, not inflexed, carinate dorsally, laterally compressed, the septum extending halfway across the cavity, the long funicles fused with the endocarp; dehiscence unknown. Seed reniform, 2-2.5 X 3-3.5 mm, the smooth testa dark brown, unmottled.

description: Slender wiry microphyll, effusely branched herb 4 dm tall, except for minutely puberulent young branches, leaflets and flower-buds glabrous, the foliage pallid- green, the flowers borne singly in upper leaf-axils. Stipules lanceolate from subequilateral base, 2.5-4 X 0.4-0.6 mm, 4-5- nerved persistent. Leafstalks 7-10 mm, the petiole ±2.5-3 mm, the interfoliolar seg- ments ? 1-1.7 mm; petiolar nectary subsessile, turbinate-campanulate truncate, 0.2- 0.35 x 0.25-0.4 mm; leaflet-pulvinules 0.2-0.3 mm, fuscous; leaflets 4-6 pairs, slightly accrescent distally, in outline fal- cately linear from oblique base, dimidiate, spinulose-apiculate, the longer ones 7-9 X 1.1-1.3 mm, 5-8 times as long as wide; venation of 3(4) nerves from pulvinule, the midrib displaced almost to distal margin, 3-4-branched only on proximal side, the inner primary nerve produced nearly to apex of leaflet, all nerves slenderly prominulous dorsally, less so above. Pedicels filiform 15-18 mm, bracteolate above middle, the bracteoles ±2 mm; flower-buds ovoid-acuminate ±6 mm; calyx-lobes ovate-acuminate, to 6 mm; longest petal ±8.5 mm; longer anthers ±5 mm; ovary white-strigulose; ovules 4; style linear incurved 4.2-5.5 mm, glabrous. Pod minutely stipitate, the body in profile oblong-elliptic from rounded base, 14-19 X 5-7 mm, apiculate, the stiffly papery valves brown, microscopically puberulent; seeds in broad view obliquely obovate 4.1-4.7 X 2.8-3.1 mm, the testa dull brown, pitted.

description: Sparingly branched, erect or decumbent, suffrutescent herbs 5-13 cm tall. Uppermost cauline internodes terete, copiously strigose like the petioles with appressed, partly glandular, terete hairs 1 mm long but typically glabrous with age; nodal hairs flattened (when dry), 2-4 mm long. Principal leaves somewhat unequal in size in each pair; blades membranaceous, crenate-serrulate, ciliate, the inframarginal pair of abaxial leaf veins typically depressed and inconspicuous, the upper surface flat and sparsely to moderately strigose with hairs mostly 1 mm long, the lower surface with appressed hairs mostly 1-2 mm on the primary veins, antrorsely spreading hairs 1-2 mm long on the secondary and higher veins, and a copious cover of minute, pustulate or crystalline excrescences on the epidermal surface. Larger leaf at each node 3.3-9.1 cm long and 1.4-3.5 cm wide, elliptic- ovate to lanceolate, bluntly acute to attenuate at the apex, rounded (often oblique) to cordulate at the base, 5-7- nerved or 5-7-plinerved; petiole 0.5-2.1 cm long. Smaller leaf at each node 2-3 (-3.6) cm long and 1.2-1.7 cm wide, ovate to ovate-elliptic, acute at the apex, rounded (sometimes oblique) at the base, 5- nerved; petiole 0.3-0.6 cm. Inflorescence terminal (rarely axillary), 3-1 1-flowered, 2.1-6.7 cm long, beset with a mixture of appressed simple hairs and shorter glandular hairs. Pedicels (in fruit) 1.5-3.5 mm long with pubescence like that of the inflorescence rachis. Hypanthia (at anthesis) 2 mm long, moderately beset with a mixture of spreading, simple hairs (1-4 mm long) and minute, glandular hairs. Calyx lobes (flowering hypanthia) 0.5 mm long and 0.5 mm wide basally between sinuses, bluntly deltoid, entire, essentially glabrous or sparsely beset with simple hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially; calyx teeth subulate or setiform, 3-4.5 mm long, inserted subapically on the abaxial surface of calyx lobes. Petals glabrous, white, obovate, entire, obtuse to rounded apically, 5-7 mm long and 3-3.5 mm wide. Stamens dimorphic. Antesepalous stamens: filaments 3 mm long; anthers linear-oblong 1.25-1.5 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, the apical pore truncate; connective prolonged less than 0.2 mm below the thecae, the dorsal bifid spur mostly less than 0.25 mm long, the 3 ventral filiform or clavellate appendages 1.5-3 mm long, less than 0.25 mm wide, and typically exceeding the anthers. Antepetalous stamens: filaments 2.2-2.5 mm long; anthers linear-oblong, 1-1.5 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, the apical pore truncate and somewhat ventrally inclined; connective prolonged less than 0.25 mm below the thecae and modified ventrally into an upturned, irregularly lobed appendage mostly 0.25 mm long and 0.5 mm wide. Ovary glabrous, 1/2 inferior. Style 5-6 mm long; stigma subtruncate to subcapitate. Fruiting hypanthia 2.5-3 mm long and 4-6 mm wide on each of 3 sides. Seeds 0.5 mm long.

description: Herba pusilla 5-13 cm alta. Folia in quoque jugo inaequalia; lamina elliptico-ovata vel lanceolata crenato-serrulata, supra sparse vel modice strigosa (pilis 1 mm longis), subtus in venis primariis secundariisque strigillosa (pilis 1-2 mm longis) in superficie dense pustulata. Inflorescentia 2.1-6.7 cm longa, floribus 5-meris unilateralibus 3-11. Petala obovata 5-7 x 3-3.5 mm. Stamina dimorpha glabra; filamenta 3 mm vel 2.2-2.5 mm longa; antherarum thecae oblongae 1-1.5 x 0.5 mm poro ventraliter inclinato. Stamina maiora: appendices ventrales 1.5-3 x 0.25 mm, dente dorsali 0.25 x 0.25 mm. Stamina minora: appendices ventrales 0.25 x 0.5 mm.

description: Stems simple or much branched; hypanthium 2-6.5 mm long, 1.6-4.5 mm wide, colored or not colored within, the ring of hairs 0.6-3.6 mm from the rim; petals fan-shaped, 1-3.4 cm long; outer stamens 7.5-17 mm long, inner stamens 5-13.5 mm long; stigma lemon-yellow or pink-yellow when closed; ovary 2-7 mm long, on pedicels 1-12 mm long, but usually some pedicels on a plant longer than 5 mm, the upper portion of the immature ovaries not swollen; mature capsules subterete or four-sided with a beak 2-6 mm long.

description: Shrub or tree 1.5-14 m tall, 2-6 cm dbh, the indument on petioles and peduncles not visible to the naked eye, composed of erect or ascending, ±straight trichomes (the longest ca. 0.1 mm). Leaflet-blade acuminate (rarely rounded) at apex, glabrous (sometimes bearing scattered, erect or ascending trichomes to 0.13 mm long on abaxial surface of midrib), usually with domatia in axils of secondary veins, these usually with circular openings, usually visible to the naked eye, the terminal blade usually elliptic or narrow-obovate, 11-30 X 4.7-11 cm, cuneate or decurrent at base, with 7-13 secondary veins per side, its petiolule 0.2-1.4 cm long, the lateral blades usually elliptic, 6.8-26.5 X 2.4-10.5 cm, asymmetric at base (usually acute basiscopically and ±decurrent acroscopically), with 5-9 secondary veins per side, their petiolules 0.1-0.6 cm long; petiole 4.5- 18.5 cm long. Inflorescence 16-35 cm long including a peduncle 13.5-31 cm long, the internodes of primary rachis not developed, the partial inflorescences borne at apex of peduncle, stalked, dichasial at first node, monochasial at higher nodes, the secondary axis 3-32 mm long; pedicels (0.3-)1.5-4.5 mm long (3.5-7 mm in FDBG 5529 and Pires & Westra 48850). Calyx usually shallowly dentate (with reflexed lobes longer than tube in FDBG 5529), (1-)1.5-3.9 mm long (4-5.3 mm in FDBG 5529), sparsely appressed-pubescent without, more densely so or glabrous within. Corolla rounded at apex in bud, 5- merous, 17-22 mm long at anthesis, mealy appressed-pubescent especially toward base without, white, the tube formed by coherent petals 9-10 mm long, 2.8-3.8 mm wide just above the calyx, 0.8-1.6 times longer than the lobes, these ca. 12 X 2-2.2 mm wide, inflexed at apex. Androecium of 5 fertile stamens; filaments 13-17 mm long, free from each other and adherent to the corolla tube, essentially glabrous adaxially, the free part 3.5-6 mm long; anther including sterile base and appendage 4.6-6.7 mm long, the fertile portion 4-5.3 X 0.5-1.5 mm, the basal sterile portion 0.25-1 mm long, the appendage 0.5- 0.8 mm long, the notch 0.15-0.65 mm deep. Disc 1-1.4 mm high, slightly shorter than or equal to the ovary. Carpels ca. 1.5 mm high, glabrous but becoming ± pubescent after anthesis; style 18-20 mm long. Fruiting mericarps 10-14 X 7-10 mm (15-17 X 11-12 mm in FDBG 5529 and Pires & Westra 48850), sparsely strigulose and glabrescent except for adjacent lateral surfaces. Seed 9-10.2 X 6.7-7 mm.

description: Trees or tall shrubs, 0.75-(2.5)-6 m tall. Stems erect, possibly forming colonies by root shoots, but information unavailable. Branches reddish brown, not glaucous or flaky, sericeous. Branchlets yellowish or reddish brown, not glaucous, moderately to densely sericeous or villous with appressed (rarely spreading) hairs. Proximal leaves with entire, glandular-dotted, or serrulate margins. Juvenile leaves yellowish green or obscured by moderately to densely sericeous, white indumentum. Largest mature leaf blades linear, narrowly elliptic, or narrowly obovate (rarely elliptic), 5.6-24 mm long, 1.2-3.8 mm wide, length: width 2.1- 13.3, apex acute, base acute, margin glandular-serrulate or glandular-dotted, 6-16 teeth or glands per cm, blades amphisto- matous, abaxial surface non-glaucous, moderately to very densely sericeous with appressed, straight, white hairs, adaxial surface dull, densely to sparsely sericeous, pilose, or glabrescent with white hair, sec- ondary veins rarely evident, if so, then pinnate and straight; petioles 0.2-1.8 mm long, sericeous. Stipules usually foliaceous, rarely minute rudiments, apex acute. Flowering coetaneous (on short, flowering branchlets), or serotinous (on long, flowering branchlets). Floral bracts tawny, 1.8-5.5 mm long, abaxial surface moderately to sparsely hairy, apex acute to obtuse, apex margin toothed or entire, pistillate floral bracts deciduous after flowering. Staminate aments 4-14 mm long on flowering branchlets 4-102 mm long, densely flowered; stamens two, anthers 0.3-0.6 mm long, filaments free, hairy on lower half (or more), staminate abaxial floral nectaries absent, adaxial nectaries one, rod-like, 0.5-0.9 mm long. Pistillate aments 6-22 mm long on flowering branchlets 8-130 mm long, moderately densely to loosely flowered; ovaries densely to sparsely sericeous with straight, white hairs, pyriform, styles 0.2-0.3 mm long, stigma lobes slender, cylindrical, 1-1.6 mm long, capsules 4-7 mm long, hairy or glabrescent, ovules 10-20 per carpel, stipes 0.2-1.2 mm long, abaxial nectaries absent, adaxial nectaries one, rod-like or ovate, 0.7-1.4 mm long, longer than stipes.
bibliographicCitation: Argus, George W. & McJannet, C. L. 1992. A taxonomic reconsideration of Salix taxifolia sensu lato (Salicaceae). Brittonia. 44: 461-474.

description: Arbores 10-15 m altae; rami stipulis binatis caducis induti; folia duplicato-serrata; inflorescentiae racemo- rum brevium in ramis aphyllis compositae; rachides 3-7 mm longae 3-5 florae moderate strigosae; pedicelli ca. 1 mm longi; fructus ovati 2.1-2.2 X 1.2-1.3 cm, ad basim in stipitem 3-4 mm longum angustati, ciliati, in superficie sparse pubescentes, ala ampla cincti.

description: Trees 10-15 m tall with orangish exfoliating bark; younger branches sparsely puberulent, greenish-brown; older branches glabrous, reddish-brown; stipules paired, 4- 9 mm long, ovate to lanceolate, sparsely strigose abaxially, glabrous adaxially, trans- lucent, light green when fresh, drying medium brown, caducous when the leaves ex- pand; axillary buds 2 mm long, obconical, the scales pubescent abaxially, ciliate, light brown. Leaves alternate, pinnately veined; blades ovate, 4.3-9.6 X 2.3-4.6 cm, the apex acute, the base usually cordate, sometimes rounded, symmetrical or oblique, drying coriaceous, dull green to light brown, glabrous and smooth above, puberulent beneath when young becoming glabrous with age; the margins doubly serrate; lateral veins 7-9(-11) pairs, arcuate near margin, 6-10 mm distant, raised and puberulent beneath; petioles 2-5 mm long, puberulent. Inflorescences axillary, short racemes on leafless branches; peduncles 3-7 mm long, sparsely 3-5-flowered, moderately strigose; bracts subtending flowers ovate, ca. 0.5 mm long, caducous; pedicels ca. 1 mm long, pubescent, articulate. Flowers perfect (description from floral remnants attached to fruits); perianth campanulate, 5-lobed, the lobes ca. 1.5 mm long, sparsely pubescent abaxially, glabrous adaxially, free almost to base; stamens apparently 6-9; filaments ca. 2 mm long, slender; anthers ca. 0.8 mm long; ovary not seen. Fruits flattened stipitate samaras, ovate, 2.1-2.2 x 1.2-1.3 cm, tapered at base into stalk 3-4 mm long, ciliate, sparsely pubescent on surface, the wing membranous with reticulate venation, the persistent styles incurved, often over- lapping; seeds 6-7 x 5-6 mm.

description: Large trees (1O-)18-50 m tall; narrow plank buttresses very tall; trunk above buttresses deeply channeled, strongly fenestrate, (0.11-)0.35-2 m diam. Bark gray, granular; sap watery (Neill et al. 8640). Leaf blades 8-27 X 3-10 cm, elliptic, narrowly elliptic or ovate, the apices acuminate to long acuminate, the margin entire, very slightly sinuate, the bases wedge-shaped to truncate, symmetrical to weakly asymmetrical, glabrous above except rarely when minute hairs continue onto the midrib from the petiole, glabrous below, 3(-5)-nerved at the base, coriaceous; petioles 1-1.8 cm long, glabrous or rarely with minute hairs, slightly thickened apically; stipular sheaths acicular to falcate, 4-7 X ca. 1-3 mm, the margin fimbriate, extrorsely glabrous or with a few simple or bifurcate hairs, or densely pubescent (below inflorescences only?). Inflorescences terminal on leafy branches, thyrso-paniculate, densely stel- late-pubescent. Flower buds cream-colored (Aulestia 3648), more or less globose. Epicalyx minutely appressed-pubescent. Calyx campanulate, at anthesis 7-9 mm long, fused to ca. 1/2 of length, lobes 3-4 X ca. 2-3 mm, densely pubescent without with appressed hairs, densely pubescent within with long simple hairs. Petals white (Aulestia 3654; Neill & Aulestia 10421), 10-15 X 5-8 mm, obovate with narrow base, densely pubescent without with appressed hairs, glabrous within except basally. Staminal tube ca. 8 mm long, pubescent with mostly simple, hyaline hairs basally, distally divided into 5 alternisepalous phalanges, each of ca. 10-15 stamens, the stamens yellow (Neill & Aulestia 10421), the anthers subsessile. Ovary ovoid, glabrous; style ca. 8 mm long, erect, pubescent distally; stigma weakly bipartite (Aulestia 3654). Calyx in fruit ca. 5 cm long, greenish to brownish, the free sepal lobes spatulate, 1.5-3.7 cm long, 6-12 mm broad, pubescent; fruit ca. 15 X 5 mm, pericarp oblong-obovate, minutely pubescent; seeds not seen.

description: Slender, herbaceous, perennial vines. Stems twining over shrubs and other plants or growing prostrate on the ground, rooting at the nodes when prostrate, mostly 2-3 m long, 1-1.5 mm diam, green, glabrous or with scattered glandular trichomes; roots perennial, to 1.5 cm diam, with smaller secondary roots. Leaves simple, persistent, petiolate; lamina markedly sagittate, 2.5-9.5 cm long, the terminal lobe 2-7 cm long, 2-4 mm wide, glabrous, the margins entire, the apex acute to acuminate, mucronate, the basal lobes divergent, 1.5-2 cm long, 2-3 mm wide; venation pinnate; petiole terete, 1.5-2 cm long, 0.5-1 mm diam, glabrous or more commonly with glandular trichomes concentrated near the apex. Inflo- rescence cymose, the first branching dichasial, the second monochasial; flowers 2-5; peduncles axillary and terminal, the primary peduncle terete, 2-3 cm long, 1-1.5 mm diam, the secondary peduncles similar, 0-7 mm long, ca 1 mm diam, subtended by linear bracteoles, 2 mm long and up to 1 mm wide, glabrous; pedicels 8-12 mm long, 0.5-1 mm diam, green, smooth, glabrous; bracts linear, 2-3 mm long; sepals unequal, imbricate, pale green, drying tan to brown, the outer oblong, 7-8 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, membranous, glabrous, the margins entire, scarious, the apices obtuse, caudate, the inner obovate, membranous, glabrous, the margins entire, 8-9 mm long, 4 4.5 mm wide, acute, short caudate; corolla funnelform, 3-3.5 cm long, the tube lavender, 1.5 cm long, 6-10 mm diam, dilating gradually, the buds convolute-duplicate, glabrous; the limb 5-lobate, lavender, 2.5-3 cm wide, glabrous; stamens unequal, included, white, 12-15 mm long, the filaments fused to the base of the corolla tube, glandular pubescent on the basal angles, the anthers 3-4 mm long; ovary ovoid, glabrous, the style 16-17 mm long, exceeding the stamens, capitate, 2-globose, white; nectary dark yellow. Fruit a capsule, brown, ovoid, 4-5 mm long, 2-locular, 4-valvular, dehiscent, chartaceous, gla- brous; mature seeds not seen.
bibliographicCitation: McDonald, J. Andrew & Austin, D. F. 1990. Changes and additions in Ipomoea section Batatas (Convolvulaceae). Brittonia. 42: 116-120.

description: Stems prostrate or trailing, minutely pubescent, mostly 1-2 m long. Leaves sessile or subsessile, linear to narrowly linear, mostly 2.5-7 cm long, 1-3 mm wide, rarely slightly wider; apex acute or obtuse; base acute or attenuate; surface slightly to moderately pubescent, with obscure veins except midrib. Inflorescences cymes of 1-5 flowers; peduncles as long as or longer than leaves, mostly 3-7 cm long; central flowers sessile or pedicellate; pedicels of lateral flowers 4-20 mm long; bracteoles leaf-like, mostly 1.5-2.5 cm long, extending beyond sepals or at least reaching sepal tips. Sepals oval or slightly oval-lanceolate, 4-6 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, with obtuse or acute apices with fulvous pubescence on the outside. Corolla white, 1.2-1.8 cm long, more than twice the length of sepals, with subentire or very shallowly lobed margin. Stamens partially exserted; filaments usually glabrous, rarely with scattered hairs near the bases. Ovary densely villous with long hairs; styles fused nearly to the base of stigmas; stylar branches 2-3 mm long, mostly equal or slightly unequal; stylopodia as.long as 3-4 mm, densely villous. Fruits usually 1- or 2-seeded. Cotyledonary petioles fused. Flowering from late May to early August.
bibliographicCitation: Johnson, A. J. 1966. A new species of Porophyllum [P. warnockii] (Compositae: Helenieae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 18: 96.

description: Shrub; branches sparsely puberulent, brown, the branchlets slender, flexuous, subpungent; leaves thinly subeoriaceous, sparsely puberulent, 4-18 mm. long, 4-12 mm. broad, orbicular, obtuse, obscurely dentate at the apex, entire below, the base obtuse; petiole slender, 1-2 mm. long, densely puberulent; infloreseence-axis 2-4 mm. long, several-flowered, puberulent; bracts deltoid, subacute, finely-puberulent on the outer surface, ciliate on the margin with longer hairs; pedicels slender, 1.5 mm. long, sparsely fine-puberulent; sepals deltoid, subacute, sparsely puberulent on the outer surface, ciliate with longer hairs; petals narrowly ovate, truncate, irregular along the upper margin, glabrous; anthers ovate.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, F. A. 1944. Schinus L. Brittonia. 5: 160-198. f. 1-22.

description: Shrub or small tree, 2-5 m. tall; branches glabrous (or at first minutely and sparsely pilose), brown later becoming grayish-maroon, the branchlets few, slender, rigid, spineseent; leaves subcoriaceous or thinly subcoriaceous, glabrous or essentially so, 18-35 mm. long, 9-19 mm. broad, ovate (sometimes broadly oblong or obovate), truncate to obtuse, rarely subacute, mucronate or not, the margin often from entire to crenate-dentate or crenate-serrate at the apex, never near the obtuse to subeuneate base; petiole slender, 2-4 mm. long, glabrate or sparsely pilose; infloreseence-axis 2-3 cm. long, sparsely pilose or glabrate, manyflowered; bracts deltoid, subacute, persistent, glabrous or with a few hairs on the outer surface, sparsely ciliate on the margin or the margin without cilia; pedicels 4-5 mm. long, glabrous or very sparsely short-pilose; sepals deltoid, subacute, glabrous except for the margin which usually is sparsely ciliate; petals ovate, truncate, glabrous except for a few fine cilia on the margin, about 2 mm. long; anthers ovoid; fruit about 5 mm. in diameter, dark purple.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, F. A. 1944. Schinus L. Brittonia. 5: 160-198. f. 1-22.

description: Frutex vel arbor 1-3 m. altus; ramulis pilis brevibus vel glabratis, primo fulvis deinde glau6is, saepe gracilibus, saepe abundantibus, spineseentibus; foliis subcoriaceis, glabris nisi sparse puberulis in media vena infra, 17-38 mm. longis, 4-15 mm. latis, obovatis, acutis vel obtusis et mucronatis, margine integro (nonnumquam irregulariter crenato-serrato, saepe subrevoluto, ad basim angustatis abrupte obtusis; petiolis 1-2 mm. longis, sparse puberulis; infloreseentia glomerata, axi 2-3 mm. longo, glabrato; bracteis deltoideo-ovatis, fere subacutis, extra glabris vel saepe pubeseentibus, margine ciliolato pilis simplicibus brevibusque.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, F. A. 1944. Schinus L. Brittonia. 5: 160-198. f. 1-22.

description: Shrub or tree to 3 m. tall; branches short-pilose to glabrate, tan or brown becoming gray, moderately slender, moderately abundant, spineseent; leaves subcoriaceous, glabrous except for sparse puberulence on the midvein above, 17-38 mm. long, 4-15 mm. broad, obovate, acute or obtuse and mucronate, the margin entire (rarely irregularly crenate-serrate or serrate), slightly subrevolute, narrowed toward the base, abruptly obtuse; petiole 1-2 mm. long, sparsely puberulent; infloreseence congested, many-flowered, the axis 2-3 mm. long, glabrate; bracts deltoid-ovate, mostly subacute, glabrous or sparsely pubescent on the dorsal surface, the margin ciliate with short simple hairs; pedicels slender, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, about 2 mm. long; bracts deltoid-ovate, obtuse, glabrous or very sparsely pubescent on the outer surface, sparsely ciliate with simple hairs; petals about 1.5 mm. long, ovate, truncate, sparsely pubescent toward the base on the outer surface; stamens between the petals exserted; anthers ovate.
bibliographicCitation: Barkley, F. A. 1944. Schinus L. Brittonia. 5: 160-198. f. 1-22.

description: Arbor grandis ramis teminalibus viridibus in sicco brunnescentibus subter- etibus lenticellatis glabris. Folia simplicia alterna crassiuscule coriacea glabra. Petiolus brevis crassus 2-4 mm longus. Lamina obovata oblongo-obovata vel obovato-elliptica, basi paulo attenuata obtuse cuneata vel subrotundata apice late rotundata vel obtusissima, margine integerrima, 11-19 cm longa, 6.5-10 cm lata; supra siccitate brunnescens costa conspicuissima nervis secundariis visibilibus filiformibus venulis minor- ibus subobsoletis; subtus in sicco tabacina costa fusca valde eminenti nervis secundariis 8-10 utroque latere prominentibus subpatulis sed marginem versus arcuato-ascendentibus evanescente anastomosantibus, nervulis prominulis laxe reticulatis. Inflorescentiae terminales paniculatae folia superne non attingentes 6-7 cm longae et latae ramis ramulisque dichotomis articulatis hirtulo-tomentellis brac- teolis deciduis. Pedicelli crassi tomentosi circa 1 mm longi. Alabastra oblonga apicem angustata 5-6 mm longa. Calyx expansus 3 mm diamitens sepalis rotunda- tis basi coalitis extus pubescentibus 1 mm longis. Petala obovato-linearia cras- siuscula 5.5-6 mm longa 2.5 mm lata extus tomentosa. Stamina crebrissima plus minusve triseriata inaequalis filamentis glabris basi 1 mm longitudine coalita. Antherae minutae ovato-rhomboidales quadrilobatae connectivo incrassato sursum attenuato. Discus intrastaminalis cylindricus membranaceus margine eroso-den- tatus 3 mm altus. Ovarium oblongum 3 mm longum apice tantum hirsutum. Stylus filiformis glaber 2 mm longus. Fructus drupaceus subovato-ellipticus basi rotundatus apice paulo attenuatus, in sicco epicarpio extus grisaceo minute velutino-tomentoso, 3.2 cm longus, 2 cm latus. Endocarpium lignosum (circa 3 x 2 cm) basi rotundatum subtruncatum apice acutum superificie sublaevi (minute ruguloso), 5 costis longitudinalibus bene signatis cum 5 valvis oblongo-linearibus 2.5 cm longis 5 mm latis adpresse alternantibus.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1956. Studies in South American plants--IV. Brittonia. 8: 195-200.

description: Herba perennis, erecta, bulbosa; caules sub anthesi 3-15 (raro 30) mm longi, in fructu ad 30 mm longi; folia caulina nulla; folia basalia sub anthesi ad 12 cm longa, in fructu longiora, linearia; spathae valvae tres, 3-4.5 cm longae, 5-9 mm latae; saepe purpurascentes, exterior saepe plicata ad apicem, interdum flores subtendens, interiores 2 ad 6 flores subtendentes; flores erecti, 3-4.5 cm lati; tepala exteriora oblonga vel oblongi-obovata, 12-21 mm longa, 7-13 mm lata, pallide lavendulacea vel lilacini-lavendulacea cum reticulo macularum et linearum albidarum, vel atrolilacinilavendulacea (raro alba) maculis ad laminas restrictis; lamina patens vel deflexa; tepala interiora hastata, ultra glandem abrupte angustata, glande in sulco laminae, lamina margine undulata, aurea clara; filamenta connata, 7-8 mm longa; antherae 7-10 mm longae, exsertae, angustae; styli ramuli antherarum 1/2 longitudinis, 3-4 mm longi, purpureo-rubri, mucro in sinu reducto vel subobsoleto; capsula oblongi-globosa ad 15 mm longa. Florescentia mense Junii et medium Julii.
bibliographicCitation: Cruden, Robert William. 1968. Three new species of Trigidia (Iridaceae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 20: 314-320.

description: Lianas; stems ca. 10 m long, with long and short brownish glandular hairs. Leaves opposite; petioles 4.5-5 cm long with long and short brownish glandular hairs, blades broadly elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 18-26 X 8-16 cm, with long septate, erect to appressed hairs, midvein on abaxial surface with long (1.5-4 mm) and short (0.15-0.2 mm) hairs, secondary veins conspicuous on abaxial surface, base narrowly cordate, ap- parently without glands, apex obtuse and abruptly acuminate. Inflorescences helicoid cymes, subaxillary, 3-4-flowered (only one flower at anthesis at a time), peduncle 1-4.5 cm long, pubescent, rachis 1.8-7 cm long, similarly pubescent, with conspicuous scars, pedicels 1-3 cm long, densely glandular pubescent, dark red. Calyx lobes narrowly elliptic or narrowly ovate-elliptic, 4.7-5 X 2.2-2.4 mm, apex narrowly obtuse to subacute, abaxially pubescent, adaxially glabrous, base without adaxial glands; corolla rotate, 17-18 mm diam., lobes ovate, green with conspicuous reticulate venation, 6-6.5 X 6.5-7 mm, obtuse to rounded and slightly emarginate, adaxially glabrous except for very short hairs at base, abaxially with short erect hairs on the right half (lobe oriented from base to apex); gynostegium stipitate, 2.4-2.5 mm long; stigma head white, 3-3.1 mm diam.; anthers 1.5-1.6 mm wide between wings, the pollinia asymmetrically obovate, 0.66 X 0.5-0.55 mm, upper margin sterile, translator arms ca. 0.17 mm long, the corpusculum broadly sagittate, 0.27 X 0.22-0.23 mm; corona fleshy, yellow, deeply 5-lobed, surrounding base of gynostegium, the lobes irregularly trapezoidal, 1.2-1.4 X 2.5-2.7 mm, rugose-carunculate at base. Fruit (known from a single old fruit) ovate-lanceolate when open, 19 X 8 cm, acute at apex, externally convex, the surface brown and wavy-striate, internally concave, yellow. Seed (known from a single seed) 8 X 6 mm, the end opposite coma erose, coma white.
bibliographicCitation: Morillo, Gilberto N. 1998. Matelea gracieae Morillo, a new species from French Guiana, and Cynanchum gortsianum Morillo, a new record for Suriname. Brittonia. 50: 296-300.

description: Tree 4-5 m tall, much branched, the young branches puberulous, soon becoming glabrous. Leaves broadly obovate to orbicular, 3-8.5 cm long, 2.5-6.5 cm broad, retuse or rounded at apex, rounded to subcuneate at base, glabrous beneath; midrib slightly impressed above at least on lower portion, prominent beneath and with a few stiff appressed hairs only; primary veins 6-8 pairs, arcuate, anastomosing; petioles 1.5-8 mm long, sparsely appressed pubescent when young, becoming, rugose, terete. Stipules triangular, ca 1 mm long, caducous. Flowers hermaphrodite, sessile, borne in few-flowered (2-4) sessile glomerules on midrib just above the junction with the petiole; bracteoles ca 0.5 mm long, ovate, pubescent, persistent. Calyx 5-6 mm long, puberulous on exterior, the lobes extremely unequal with 3 large ones and 2 much smaller. Corolla exceeding calyx lobes, with 2 large bicucullate lobes and 3 smaller, simple lobes, united at base to form a distinct tube, the tube glabrous on exterior, sparsely hirsutulous on inner surface, white turning cream with age. Fertile stamens 3, alternating with corolla lobes and inserted on the corolla tube, 2 staminodes present. Disc circular and lobed, inserted tightly appressed between base of corolla tube and ovary. Ovary trilocular with 2 ovules in each loculus, tomentellous on exterior. Style hirsutulous for entire length, with a trifid apex. Young fruit ovoid, epicarp with short, appressed pubescence.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1984. the rediscovery of Tapura haitiensis (Dichapetalaceae). Brittonia. 36: 15-17.

description: Frutex scandens; ramulis gracilibus, juventute dense adpresso- pubeseentibus, pilis fuscis; petiolis gracillimis 2-3.5 cm. longis ad-presso-pubescentibus; laminis subcoriaceis nitidis lanceolatis 9-15.5 cm. longis, 2.5-5.7 cm. latis, ad apicein longe attenuatis, integris, ad basin retusis vel cordatis, utrinque glabratis.

description: Descrtption: Woody vine; branchlets very slender, densely ap- pressed-pubeseent with brown hairs when young, becoming glabrate in age; petioles very slender, 2-3.5 cm. long, appressed-pubescent, not noticeably inerassate; blades subcoriaceous, nitid on both surfaces, lanceolate, 9-15.5 cm. long, 2.5-5.7 cm. wide, long-attenuate at apex, entire, retuse or cordate at base, essentially glabrous on both surfaces or rarely appressed-pubeseent along the midrib at base, subpinnately veined; midrib slender, flattened above toward base and subpromin- ulent toward apex, prominent beneath; secondaries slender, about 4 per side, prominulent above, prominent beneath, areuate-aseending, short, anastomosing with each other in many loops some distance within the margins, the upper ones anastomosing in similar fashion with the tertiaries, which are prominulent on both surfaces; veinlet reticulation rather abundant and irregular, prominulent on both surfaces; stami- nate infloreseences racemose, 10-16 cm. long, essentially unbranched or with very much abbreviated few-flowered branches; rachis very slen- der, appressed-pubeseent with strigose brownish hairs throughout; staminate flowers: sepals 18, lanceolate or the inner ones elliptic, the outermost ones very small and narrow, about 0.75 mm. long and 0.38 mm. wide, sharply acute at apex, densely strigose-pubeseent on the back with short appressed brownish hairs, the inner ones to 1.5 mm. long and 0.7 mm. wide; petals 6, obovate-elliptic, 0.7-0.8 mm. long, 0.4-0.5 mm. wide, obtuse or subacute at apex, appressed-pnbeseent or strigose on the back, glabrous within; stamens 6, connate at the base; filaments practically obsolete; anthers about 0.2 mm. long, 0.2-0.5 mm. wide.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Moldenke, Harold N. 1938. Studies of American Menispermaceae, with special reference to species used in preparation of arrow-poisons. Brittonia. 3: 1-74.

description: Frutex vel arbor 3-8 m alta; folia lanceolata vel ovato-lanceolata, acuminata, subtus stellato-pubeseentia, quinqueplinervia; infloreseentia thyrsiformis, pauciflora; hypanthium et calyx campanulati, tomentosi; appendices calycis lineares; petala obovata vel subquadrata, retusa, unguiculata.

description: A shrub or small tree 3-8 m tall, diffusely branched, the young branches densely ferruginous-stellate-tomentose, alabrate with age; leaves on slender petioles 0.7-2.5 cm long, ferruginous-pubescent as are the branchlets; leaves of a pair quite unequal in size, the blades lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, acute to the base, glabrous above or nearly so, stellate-pubescent below especially on the nerves and veins, 5-plinerved with the inner nerves arisinog well above the base of the leaf, 6-15 cm long and 2-6 cm broad; inflorescence terminal, thyrsiform, few- to several-flowered, shorter than the leaves; flowers 5-merous; hypan- thium and calyx campanulate, covered with ferruainous stellate tomentum, about 10 mm long, the calyx-lobes short and rounded; calyx appendages borne below the apex of the calyx, stellate-tomentose, terete, linear, 4-6 mm long; petals 5, white, broadly obovate, or subquadrate, often retuse, somewhat unguiculate, 8-10 mm long; stamens ten, 8-9 mm long, the anthers anid filaments of about equal length; style 8-10 mm long, the stig ma globose; summit of the ovary with several scale-like appendages forming a cup which surrounds the base of the style.
bibliographicCitation: Standley, Paul C. & Williams, Louis O. 1963. A New Miconia (Melastomaceae) from Costa Rica. Brittonia. 15 (1): 25-26.

description: Whole plant, except roots, stamens, corolla, and styles, silvery-canescent with a dense pubescence of appressed flattened hairs; taproots (or caudexes) perennial, with thin fuscous-black bark, 1-2 mm thick; crown or caudex occasionally branched; stolons annual, only 1-5 per crown, less than 10 cm long, ca. 0.8 mm thick, not or rarely branched but bearing short lateral shoots with crowded nodes; internodes 5-20 mm long; leaf-blades reniform or roughly triangular, 6-15 mm long, 10-25 mm broad, apically shortly rounded or bluntly pointed, basally truncate to broadly and shallowly cordate, narrowly cuneate where the blade joins the petiole; petioles 1-4 cm long, 0.5-0.9 mm thick, apparently rather weak, curving; pedicels 20-38 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mrm thick, erect but apparently rather weak, curving; calyx narrowly campanulate, 4-5 mm long at anthesis, 5-lobed three-fourths to five-sixths the length, the lobes lance-oblong, acute (the sides at tip forming a 70º-90º angle) to shortly rounded apically; corolla nearly cylindrical or becoming funnelform, 7-8 mm long, whitish ( ?), 5-lobed two-thirds the length, the lobes obovate-elliptic, sericeous on the outside; stamens attached at the sinuses, the filiments free for 3-4 mm, equalling the corolla-lobes; ovary slightly bilobed; styles entirely free, 10-13 mm long (Brandegee says "2.8" mm!), stigmas minute, capitate; capsule?; seeds two per locule.
bibliographicCitation: Fulford, Margaret H. & Taylor, Jane. 1961. Segregate genera of the Lepidozia complex (Hepaticae) Part 2. Two new genera, Bonneria and Paracromastigum. Brittonia. 13: 334-339.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Stems filiform to medium, light yellow to cream colored. Cymes umbelliform of (1-)2-5 flowers; bracts 1-2 at the base of clusters and 0-2 at the base of pedicels, membranous, ovate-lanceolate, lanceolate, margins entire to obscurely denticulate, apex acute; pedicels 0.5-2.5(-3.5) mm. Floral buds acute to acuminate (rarely rounded). Flowers (4-)5-merous, 1.9-3.2 mm long, membranous, sometimes receptacle and base of perianth with fleshy cells; papillae absent; laticifers evident in the calyx, along midveins, arranged in rows, elongate (Fig. 1B). Calyx usually separating easily from corolla when rehydrated flowers are dissected, straw yellow, golden yellow to brownish yellow, reticulate and glistening-shiny, divided ca. 2/3 the length, campanulate to cylindric-campanulate, as long as the corolla tube or somewhat longer, lobes basally overlapping, oblong to obovate-rhombic, margins ± irregularly denticulate, apex acute to acuminate (Fig. iB). Corolla creamy white when fresh, cream colored to brown when dried; tube campanulate, 0.8- 1.6 mm long, lobes suberect to reflexed, ca. equaling the tube or somewhat longer, ovate to oblong, margins entire to irregularly denticulate, apex acute (Fig. 1B). Stamens included or slightly exerted, shorter than corolla lobes; anthers subrotund to elliptic, 0.3-0.4 mm long, filaments 0.2-0.4 mm long; pollen 3(-4)-zonocolpate, subprolate to prolate, 18-21.4 pm long, tectum imperforate or with a few isolated punctae, sexine scabrate with isolated granules. Infrastaminal scales reaching the filament bases, oblong, truncate, uniformly dense-fringed. Styles unequal, uniformly filiform, 0.3-0.8 mm long, 1/3-1/2 as long as the ovary; stigmas capitate, globose. Capsules indehiscent to irregularly dehiscent, usually not persis- tent on peduncles, globose-ovoid to ovoid, 1.4-2.2 x 1.2-1.8 mm, translucent, capped by the withered corolla. Seeds 1 per capsule, usually separate easily from capsules, globose to globose-ovoid, 0.8-1.15 x 0.8- 1.1 mm, chalazal end narrowed to apiculate; hilum terminal, sunken, 0.16-0.21 mm diam., vascular scar of funiculus punctiform, 0.015-0.02 mm long; seed coat alveolate when seeds are dry and papillose when seeds are hydrated, epidermis cells of 35-45 pm diam. (Fig. 2B); embryo globose-enlarged; endosperm entirely consumed at seed maturity.
bibliographicCitation: Costea, Mihai, et al. 2005. Taxonomic status of Cuscuta nevadensis and C. veatchii (Convolvulaceae) in North America. Brittonia. 57 (3): 264-272.

description: Sparingly branched, erect or decumbent, suffrutescent, terrestrial or epipetric herbs 5-40 cm tall. Cauline internodes terete, beset with a mixture of appressed, simple hairs 1 mm long and an inconspicuous ground layer of minute, glandular hairs but becoming glabrate with age; nodal hairs somewhat flattened (when dry), mostly 1-3 mm long. Principal leaves nearly equal to somewhat unequal in size in each pair; blades chartaceous, nearly entire to crenulate-serrulate, ciliate, 4.8- 17.3 cm long and 2.3-8.3 cm wide, ovate to elliptic-ovate, 5-7-plinerved with the innermost pair of primaries diverging from the median nerve 0.2-0.8 cm above the blade base, sparsely to copiously strigose, below strigillose to glabrate on the elevated primaries and secondaries, apex acute to attenuate, base broadly rounded (sometimes inaequilateral) to subauriculate; petiole 0.8-7.7 cm long. Inflorescence short-pedunculate (0.8-2.1 cm), strigose, 3-47-flowered, 2.8-26.6 cm long, borne in the axils of upper leaves. Pedicels (in fruit) 1.5-2.5 mm long, strigose to strigil- lose but typically glabrate with age. Hypanthia (at anthesis) 2-3 mm long, beset with a caducous mixture of appressed, simple hairs (0.2-1 mm) and minute, glandular hairs. Calyx lobes (flowering hypanthia) 0.5 mm long and 0.7-1 mm wide basally between sinuses, deltoid, entire, sparingly beset with appressed simple hairs abaxially; calyx teeth subulate, 1-2 mm long, inserted subapically on the abaxial surface of calyx lobes. Petals glabrous, white or pink, obovate, entire, bluntly acute to rounded at the somewhat thickened apex, 4-5 mm long and 3 mm wide. Stamens essentially similar in size but differing in appendage devel- opment. Antesepalous stamens: filaments 3-3.2 mm long; anthers linear-oblong, 1.7 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, the apical pore truncate to somewhat ventrally emarginate; connective prolonged 0.25 mm below the thecae, the 3 filiform spurs mostly 1.5-2.5 mm long. Antepetalous stamens: filaments 2.5-3 mm long; anthers linear-oblong, 1.5 mm long and 0.5 mm wide, the apical pore as in the antesepalous anthers; connective prolonged at the base 0.25 mm long below the thecae and modified ventrally into an upturned bifid or trifid appendage 0.5 mm long. Ovary glabrous, inferior. Style 5-6 mm long; stigma subtruncate. Fruiting hypanthia 3- 5 mm long and 8-10.5 (12) mm wide on each of 3 sides. Seeds 0.5 mm long.

description: Planta annua, herbacea, 20-30 cm alta, glabra. Folia petiolata, lamina anguste ovata, margine indistincte serrata. Sepala ovata, 2 X 0.7 mm, glabra. Petala spathulata, apice truncata, 2 X 1 mm. Pedicelli fructiferi patuli, 8-10 mm longi. Fructus lineares, 40-50 mm longi, 1.5 mm diametro, glabri. Semina ca. 40 per fructum, ovoidea, aurantiaco-brunnea, 1 X 0.8-0.9 mm.

description: Annual herb 20-30 cm tall; stems branched 1-3 cm above ground, glabrous, the central one about equalling lateral branches. Leaves petiolate, the petioles 5-11 mm long; median leaves 20-30 X 7-10 mm, upper gradually smaller, lamina narrowly obovate or lanceolate from cuneate base, obtuse or acuminate, margin obscurely serrate or repand. Racemes terminal, ebracteate, 10-30-flowered, elongated and lax in fruit. Sepals ovate, acuminate, 2 X 0.7 mm, yellowish green, with narrow white margin, glabrous. Petals spathulate, 2 X 1 mm, truncate, distinctly narrowed toward base but not clawed, white. Filaments 2-2.3 mm long, anthers basifixed, oblong, sagittate at base, 0.3 mm long, yellow. Ovary linear, 1.2 mm long, style 0.3 mm long, stigma obscurely bilobed. Fruiting pedicels divaricate, straight, glabrous, much narrower than fruits, 8-10 mm long, (5-)10-20 mm apart. Fruits subsessile, terete, narrowly linear, straight, 40-50 X ca. 1.5 mm wide; valves glabrous, rounded at both ends, mid-vein conspicuous, lateral veins inconspicuous; septum hyaline; style in fruit 0.8-1 mm long. Seeds ca. 40 per fruit, ovate, orange-beige, 1 X 0.8-0.9 mm.

description: Planta annua, herbacea, 12-20 cm alta, glabra. Folia amplexicaulia; lamina ovata vel ovato-oblonga, margine indistincte irregulariter repando-serrata. Sepala oblongo-ovata, 3.5 X 1.5 mm, glabra, margine late hyalina. Petala spathulata, lamina orbicularis, basi in unguem attenuata, 5 X 2.5 mm. Pedicelli fructiferi oblique erecti, 4-5 mm longi. description: Annual herb 12-20 cm tall; stems glabrous, branched 1.5-3 cm above ground, main stem quickly ending in inflorescence and far overtopped by the 3-5 lateral branches. Cauline leaves sessile, widely lanceolate, 3-5 cm X 1.5-2.5 cm, basally narrowed and finally auriculate with 2 acuminate lobes ca. 3-5 mm long, the apex rounded, the margin repand. Racemes terminal, ebracteate, 30-45-flowered, not elongating in fruit. Sepals oblong-ovate, ± rounded at apex, 3.5 X 1.5 mm, yellowish green, with very wide white hyaline margin. Petals spathulate, 5 X 2.5 mm, distally subcircular tapering into a narrowed base, white with fine and distinctive reticulate veins. Filaments 4 mm long, anthers oblong, sagittate at base, 1 mm long, yellow. Ovary linear, 1.2 mm long, style 0.3 mm long, stigma obscurely bilobed. Fruiting pedicels ascending, straight, glabrous, much narrower than fruits, 4-5 mm long, 1-3 mm apart. Fruits terete, narrowly linear, straight, subsessile, 20-30 X 1.5 mm; valves gla- brous, rounded at both ends, all veins in- visible from outside, septum hyaline. Seeds ca. 10-12 per fruit, ovoid, orange-brown, 2 X 1 mm.

description: A T. eleganti Rich. et T. rigido Sw. frondium lamina glandulis rubris numerosis conspersa, rachide cum costis costulis venisque dorso pubescentibus, soris fere tam longis quam latis, necnon receptaculis breviter exsertis (parte exserta indusium aequante vel ei dimidio breviori) abstans.

description: Rhizomes 2-5 X 0.4-1 cm, erect, bearing numerous thick (1-2 mm) roots on all sides, pubescent, the hairs 1-1.5 mm long, brown, lustrous, 4-7-celled, the cells often collapsed and slightly twisted. Leaves to 25-60 X 10-25 cm, monomorphous, dull brown or brownish green (never black). Petioles to 35 cm X 1-2.5 mm, equaling or slightly surpassing the length of the lamina, with scattered hairs like those on the rhizome, narrowly winged adaxially for most of its length. Laminae 4-pinnate, deltate, gradually tapered to the tip, sometimes iridescent (when living), glabrous adaxially, moderately to densely pubescent abaxially along the rachises, costae, costules, and veins (but not the lamina tissue), the hairs 0.4-1 mm long, coarse, brown, slightly strigose, 3-5-celled. Pinnae 12-16 pairs, opposite or subopposite proximally, becoming alternate distally, apices acute to obtuse, the basal pinnae longer on the basiscopic side, especially toward the base, the medial pinnae subequal. Pinnules anadromic in the basal pinnae, isodromic in the suprabasal ones, slightly ascending, ca. 9-13 pairs in the medial pinnae. Ultimate segments 0.2-0.3 mm wide, entire, single-veined, with a row of red, resinous-punctate glands between the vein and margin, the marginal row of cells clear and translucent (cell contents apparently lost). Rachis winged throughout, the wing ca. 1 mm wide. Sori curved downward, ca. as long as wide, the mouth of the indusium cylindrical to slightly flared, often resinous-glandular along the margin (and therefore sometimes appearing slightly erose), the receptacles slightly exserted, the exserted portion half or equaling the length of the indusium.

description: Annual or weak perennial herb, glabrous except for the villous pedicels and occasional hairs near the nodes and leaf bases, 18-27 (14-40) cm tall, branched below and in the inflorescence; leaves in fours below, opposite and finally alternate above, narrowly oblanceolate to obovate below, narrowly elliptic above, the larger 6-23 mm long, 1.7-6.2 mm wide; stipular glands present at bases of leaves and floral bracts; inflorescence paniculate, commonly occupying more than one-half entire height; fruiting pedicels 2 mm or less long, villous, sometimes sparsely so; sepals lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 2.3-2.8 mm long, with three prominent nerves and conspicuous sessile marginal glands, these present on the upper or all of the floral bracts as well; petals yellow, narrowly obovate, 3-4 mm long; stamens 2-3 mm long, usually with diminutive low, deltoid staminodia; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long; styles separate, quickly withering after anthesis, about 2 mm long; fruit broadly ovate, sharp pointed, sparsely hirsute above the middle, 1.4-2.1 mm high and 2 mm in diameter; false septa poorly developed; true septa with a few short marginal hairs; fruit dehiscing into 10 parts; seeds brownish, ovate, 0.9-1.2 mm long, 0.6-0.7 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Bushes up to ca. 8 dm in diameter; stems at maturity becoming woody toward the base, glabrous; internodes 4-12 mm long (mean 8 mm), 1-2 mm wide (mean 1.5 mm); leaves fleshy and small. but evident at branch tips, usually deciduous below the apical regions, 2-3.5 mm long (mean 3 mm), 1-1.5 mm wide (mean1.3 mm), sessile, acute at apex, the venation inconspicuous; anthesis approximately from July through September; staminate inflorescence with 1 segment and 5-7 flowers (mean 6.0) ; pistillate inflorescence with 1 segment and 2 flowers; fruit pinkish white, 4 mm in diameter, glabrous; n = 14.

description: Shrub or tree 4-8 m tall, the indument on petioles and peduncles not visible to the naked eye, composed of erect or ascending, straight or curved trichomes (the longest ca. 0.2 mm). Leaflet-blade acuminate at apex, glabrous (sometimes bearing scattered, erect trichomes to 0.12 mm long on abaxial surface of midrib), with domatia in axils of secondary veins, these with circular or crescent-shaped openings, usually visible to the naked eye, the terminal blade usually narrow-obovate, 14.7-24[28] X 5-10.6[12.7] cm, acute at base, with 7-9 secondary veins per side, its petiolule 0.2-1.4[2.2] cm long, the lateral blades usually elliptic, 6.5-21 x 2.2-7.2 cm, asymmetric at base (usually acute basiscopically and short-decurrent acroscopically), with 4-7 secondary veins per side, their petiolules 0.2-1 cm long; petiole (2.9-)5.7-13.5[20] cm long. Inflorescence 9-12.5[18-24.3] cm long including a peduncle 4-12.5[17-23.3] cm long, the internodes of primary rachis not developed, the partial inflorescences borne at apex of peduncle, short-stalked, dichasial at first node, type of branching at higher nodes not apparent, the ultimate branches in fruit secund, the secondary axis 2-5 mm long (to 10 mm in fruit); pedicels 0-1 mm long. Calyx shallowly dentate, [1.8-2] 2.2-4 mm long, pubescent without, glabrous within. Corolla rounded or obtuse in bud [sometimes apiculate in Silva & Bahia 3092], 5-merous, 29-33[37] mm long at anthesis, mealy appressed-pubescent without, the tube formed by coherent petals 20-23 mm long, [2]2.3-2.7 mm wide just above the calyx, [1.2]2.2-2.3 times longer than the lobes, these 9-10[16] x 2.3-3.4[3.5-4.2] mm wide, most inflexed at apex. Androecium of 5 fertile stamens; filaments 23-25[28] mm long, free from each other and adherent to the corolla tube, glabrous or sparsely villous adaxially, the free part 3- 5[10] mm long; anther including sterile base and appendage 5.2-5.5[6.1] mm long, the fertile portion 3.5-4[4.4] X 0.6-0.7[1] mm, the basal sterile portion 0.7-1.3 mm long, the appendage 0.5-0.7[0.8] mm long, the notch ca. 0.2 mm deep. Disc 0.5-0.7 mm high, slightly shorter than the ovary. Carpels 0.7-1 mm high, glabrous but becoming pubescent after anthesis; style ca. 22 mm long. Fruiting mericarps 8.5-12 X 7.5-12 mm, with short erect trichomes, glabrescent except for adjacent lateral surfaces. Seed unknown.

description: Shrub or tree ca. 3 m tall, the indument of vegetative buds, young twigs and petioles, and inflorescences strigulose. Leaves 1- foliolate; leaflet blade (narrow-) elliptic or narrow-obovate, acuminate, obtuse, or rounded at apex, acute or decurrent at base, 7.2-23 cm long, 2.4-9 cm wide, chartaceous, dull above, glabrous, the secondary veins evident, curved-ascending, looping at margin, 7-11 per side, the tertiary veins evident and slightly raised on both surfaces; petiole 0.5-2.2 cm long. Inflorescence 7-16- flowered, 0.8-2 cm long including a peduncle 0.3-0.8 cm long; pedicels ca. 2 mm long in flower and in fruit. Sepals very wide- ovate, obtuse to rounded at apex, 1.2-1.5 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, strigulose without, glabrous within. Corolla in bud ca. 5 mm long, very sparsely strigulose toward apex of lobes without, greenish, the tube ca. 1.7 mm to division of innermost lobe, ca. 2 mm to division of other lobes, ca. 2 mm wide, the innermost lobe ovate, ca. 3.5 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide, the other 4 lobes very wide ovate, ca. 2 mm long, ca. 2 mm wide. Filaments of fertile stamens adherent to corolla, ca. 2.4 mm long; staminodes adherent to corolla, lance-subulate, ca. 2.7 mm long; anthers in bud ca. 2.2 mm long, ca. 1.3 mm wide, glabrous, the connective glabrous, the appendages ca. 0.3 mm long, ca. 0.6 mm wide. Disc taller than and completely en- veloping the ovary, 5-lobed. Carpels ca. 0.5 mm high, glabrous at first but soon densely strigulose; style ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous. Fruiting mericarps usually 2, ca. 1 1 mm long, ca. 6 mm wide, strigulose. Seed (immature) ca. 8 mm long, 4.5 mm wide, pale brown.

description: Slender-stemmed perennial, to about 1 m tall, rather leafy thloughout, more or less woody at base, the branehes mostly 1-2 mm in diameter, subterete, finely pubescent, often strigulose; leaves opposite or alternate, rather equable in size, only gradually reduced up the stems, laneeolate to lance-ovate, the blades 1-2 (-3) cm long, subglabrous to pubescent, especially on the veilns beneath, acute, serrulate, about 4- to 6-veined on each side of the midrib; petioles 3-6 (-10) mm long; uppermost leaves gradually passing into lance-linear or lanceolate subsessile bracts mostly 5-10 mm long; pedicels filiform, asceniding to spreading, strigulose, mostly 1-1.5 cm long; sepals red, oblong-linear, obtuse, about 3.5 mm long; upper petals about as long, linear-oblong, purplish, unituberculate, the claw somewhat setulose; lower petals slightly longer, obovate, long-clawed, pale purplish; sterile stamen with a bright red rounded retuse blade; fertile stamen about 3 mm long, the anther almost as lolng as the broad filament; capsule subglobose, about 3-3.5 mm in diameter; seeds about 1 mm long, tuberculate.
bibliographicCitation: Munz, Philip A. 1961. The Lopezieae (Onagraceae). Brittonia. 13 (1): 73-90.

description: Similar to R. mexicana; differs in its larger (6-14 cm. long) leaflets, which are densely velvety beneath, and in its short and congested infloreseence (5-10 cm. long).

description: Liana caulibus dense et pertinaciter sericeis; lamina foliorum majorum 11-14.3 cm longa, 8.4-9.7 cm lata, abaxialiter pertinaciter sericea, margine distali glandulis parvis instructa; petiolus 13-20 mm longus, sericeus; stipulae 0.4-0.6 mm longae, triangulares, basi petioli gestae; inflorescentia panicula axillaris ex 7 umbellis 4-floris constans; bracteae 2-2.5 mm longae, eglandulosae; pedunculus 1.5-2.5 mm longus; bracteolae 1-1.5 mm longae, in quoque pari una bracteola uniglandulifera glandulo excentrico versus centrum umbellae protuberanti; sepala apice revoluta; petala lutea, 4 lateralia laciniata eglandulosa, posticum limbo toto circuitu fimbriato fimbriis distaliter plus minusve glandulosis; samara subcircularis, 48-56 mm lata, 42- 50 mm alta, ala laterali apice usque ad nucem incisa, basi continua, nuce basi collosa.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, W. R. 1994. New species of Hiraea (Malpighiaceae) from the Guianas and adjacent Brazil. Brittonia. 46: 126-133.

description: Liana, the woody stems at least 0.7 cm in diam., densely and persistently sericeous. Leaves decussate with the members of a pair often subopposite; lamina of larger leaves 11-14.3 cm long, 8.4-9.7 cm wide, broadly ovate, rounded or truncate at base, obtuse or abruptly short-acuminate at apex, eglandular on abaxial surface but usually bearing  a series of tiny buttonlike glands on distal half of margin and occasionally 1-2 somewhat larger glands on margin near base, adaxially sparsely sericeous to glabrate at maturity with the midrib usually persis- tently sericeous, abaxially densely and per- sistently sericeous, the lateral veins 7-9 and connected by many fine parallel cross-veins 3-6 mm apart, the veins and reticulum prominent below and visible above in dried leaves; petiole 13-20 mm long, densely and persistently sericeous, bearing at or slightly below apex a pair of glands 1.1-1.8 mm long; stipules borne on petiole at very base, 0.4-0.6 mm long, triangular. Inflorescence densely and persistently sericeous, 2-5 cm long, an axillary panicle of usually 7 short- stalked 4-flowered umbels; floriferous bracts 2-2.5 mm long, triangular or ovate, abax- ially sericeous, adaxially glabrous, eglandular; floriferous peduncle 1.5-2.5 mm long; bracteoles 1-1.5 mm long, ovate, borne at apex of peduncle, 1 of each pair bearing 1 bulging eccentric gland toward center of umbel; pedicle 7-10 mm long in flower, 12- 14 mm long in fruit, thickened at the apex. Sepals 3.5-4.5 mm long, 2.5-3 mm wide, ovate, acute at apex and revolute in anthesis, abaxially sericeous, adaxially glabrous, all eglandular or the anterior eglandular and the lateral 4 bearing 8 elliptical or subcircular glands 1.5-1.8 mm long. Petals yellow; lateral 4 petals with the claw 3-3.5 mm long, the limb 4.5-5 mm long and wide, laciniate, eglandular; posterior petal with the claw 5 mm long, the limb ca. 6 mm long, 7 mm wide, fimbriate with the long slender divisions somewhat glandular-thickened at apex. Stamens glabrous; filaments nearly distinct; filaments opposite sepals ca. 4 mm long, erect but curved distally toward posterior petal; filaments opposite petals 2.5-3 mm long, erect, straight; anthers 1-1.3 mm long, the connective yellow. Ovary sericeous; styles bowed outward (i.e., curved outward from base and then back toward center of flower), sparsely sericeous in proximal half, dorsally acute or apiculate at apex, the anterior style 4 mm long, the 2 posterior styles 4.7 mm long. Samara depressed-circular with the nut positioned below the center, 48-56 mm wide, 42-50 mm high; lateral wing membranous, continuous at base, incised to nut at apex but with the two sides overlapping so that little or no gap is evident, thinly sericeous with very fine white appressed hairs; dorsal wing 3-5 mm wide, 5-7 mm high; nut subglobose, ca. 3 mm in diam., finely sericeous, bearing along each side at base an irregular swelling up to 1 mm thick.

description: Pavonia repens, caulibus minute stellato-pubescentibus atque pilis simplicibus patentibus indutis; foliis flabelliformibus, profunde cordatis, plus latioribus quam longioribus, subacutis vel obtusis; petiolis plerumque laminae longioribus; pedunculis solitariis in axilis foliorum; bracteis involucellorum ca 15, arcuatis, ciliatis, 15-20 mm longis; calycibus involucello brevioribus; petalis 25-30 mm longis; fructibus ignotis.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1980. Malvaceous miscellany, including new species from Mexico and Brazil. Brittonia. 32: 262-268.

description: Plant procumbent and rooting at the nodes. Stems pilose with spreading simple hairs 1.5-2.5 (3) mm long and with underlying minute stellate hairs. Leaf blade flabelliform, symmetrical, simple or weakly 3-lobulate, profoundly cordate, den- tate to subentire, subacute to obtuse, 2-3 cm long, 3.5-5 cm wide, palmately 7- (9)-nerved, evenly stellate-pubescent above and beneath (the hairs 3-7-armed, the arms 0.3-0.5 mm long), slightly denser beneath. Petiole up to 3.5 cm long (usually longer than lamina), with pubescence similar to that of stem. Stipules 3- 5 mm long, usually 2-3-parted (the segments linear), with pubescence like that of stem, more or less persistent. Peduncles solitary in the axils of the leaves, 6.5- 8 cm long (exceeding the leaves), erect, articulated 12-15 mm below the flower, with pubescence like that of stem, the pedicel above the articulation more densely pubescent. Bracts of the involucel ca 15, more or less arcuate, 15-20 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm wide, linear, prominently ciliate (the hairs 2 mm long). Calyx 10 mm long, deeply 5-lobed, densely pubescent, the lobes lanceolate, ciliate. Petals 25- 30 mm long, essentially glabrous externally. Fruits unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1980. Malvaceous miscellany, including new species from Mexico and Brazil. Brittonia. 32: 262-268.

description: Herba annua 4.5-14 cm alta; ramuli quadrangulati sicut hypanthia sparse pilis glanduliferus induti ca. 0.25-0.5 mm longi. Folia inferiora interdum summa conferta 1.5-5.5 X 0.75-2 mm elliptica vel ellipticoobovata integra glabra, uninervia; folia superiora remota essentialiter sessilia 4.5-11.5 X 0.5-1 mm uninervia oblonga vel anguste oblanceolata distanter ciliato- serrulata, ciliis glanduliferis 0.5-0.75 mm longis. Flores semper 4-meri in axillis foliorum superiorium solitarii. Petala 6-8 X 3.5-4 mm obovata. Stamina dimorpha glabra, thecis subulatis, poro ventraliter inclinato. Stamina maiora: thecae 1.5 mm longae; connectivum 3-3.5 mm prolongatum, appendice ventrali 0.5 mm. Stamina minora: thecae 1.25-1.5 mm longae; connectivum 1-1.5 mm prolongatum, appendice ventrali 0.25 mm. Ovarium 2-loculare; semina 0.25-0.5 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: Almeda, Frank. 1999. A new Acisanthera (Melastomataceae: Melastomeae) from Noel Kempff Mercado National Park, Bolivia. Brittonia. 51 (2): 159-162.

description: Erect, wiry, annual herb 4.5-14 cm tall, unbranched from the base, rarely and then only sparingly branched distally. Distal internodes quadrate, narrowly winged to carinate, sparsely beset with spreading glandular hairs 0.25-0.5 mm long. Lowermost cauline leaves chartaceous with distinct or ill-defined petioles; the petioles (when distinct) ± compressed, narrowly winged, 0.25-0.5 mm long, glabrous; the blade 1-nerved, elliptic to elliptic-obovate, 1.5-5.5 x 0.75-2 mm, obtuse to rounded and some- times tipped with a minute smooth hair at the apex, the base acute, essentially gla- brous on both surfaces; the margins entire, eciliate or with 1 or very few scattered glandular hairs. Upper cauline leaves char- taceous and sessile; the blade 1-nerved, lin- ear-oblong to narrowly oblanceolate, 4.5- 11.5 x 0.5-1 mm, rounded and mucronu- late at the apex, narrowly cuneate at the base, the margins remotely glandular cili- ate-serrulate, with hairs 0.5-0.75 mm long; glabrous or with very few spreading glan- dular hairs. Inflorescence reduced to soli- tary, terminal flowers that become pseudoaxillary because of repeated elongation of axillary shoots; flowers 4-merous and ebracteate on glabrous pedicels mostly 1-1.5 mm long when in fruit. Hypanthia (at anthesis) campanulate, sparsely covered with smooth spreading glandular hairs 0.75-1 mm long. Fruiting hypanthia glo- bose and urceolate, 2-2.5 X 2-2.5 mm. Calyx lobes of fruiting hypanthia entire, spreading, narrowly triangular, glabrous adaxially, sparsely covered with spreading glandular hairs abaxially, 1-2 X 0.5-1 mm basally between sinuses. Petals pinkish-pur- ple, obovate, rounded apically, entire, eciliate but typically tipped with a solitary glandular hair, 6-8 x 3.5-4 mm distally. Stamens 8, alike in form but alternately unequal in length, the connective prolonged below the thecae and modified into a knobby somewhat bilobate appendage at the junction with the filament, the thecae narrowly ovate to subulate in outline, somewhat constricted distally just below the cucullate, ventrally inclined apical pore. Larger (antesepalous) stamens: filaments 2-2.5 mm long; anthers 1.5 X 0.5 mm; connective 3-3.5 mm long, appendage 0.5 mm long. Small (antepetalous) stamens: filaments 1.5-2 mm long; anthers 1.25-1.5 x 0.25 mm; connective 1-1.5 mm long, appendage 0.25 mm long. Ovary superior, orbicular, glabrous, 2-locular. Style glabrous, declinate, 3-4 mm long. Capsules 2 x 2.5 mm, fully enveloped by the hypanthium at maturity. Seeds 0.25-0.5 mm long, reniform to subcochleate, foveolate and beige at maturity.

description: Liana or shrub to 4 m tall, the woody stems at least 0.6 cm in diam., initially se- riceous, soon glabrescent. Leaves decussate; lamina of larger leaves 13-23.5 cm long, 6.5-1 0 cm wide, shallowly cordate or rounded at base, obovate, or rounded and often apiculate at apex, eglandular on abaxial surface but bearing a series of small buttonlike glands on distal 2/3 of margin, initially densely sericeous on both sides but nearly or quite glabrate at maturity or with some hairs persisting especially at base of midrib, the lateral veins 9-13, parallel, connected by +/- parallel cross-veins 2-4 mm apart, the lateral veins raised below and slightly sunken above, the cross-veins hardly prominent on either surface; petiole 5-10 mm long, densely and persistently seri- ceous, bearing at or near apex a pair of glands 1.5 mm in diam.; stipules borne on petiole near middle or occasionally nearer base or apex, 5-8 mm long, somewhat flattened, se- riceous or glabrescent. Inflorescence loosely sericeous, usually a short-stalked cyme of 3 4-flowered umbels; bracts and bracteoles triangular, persistent, the bracts 2-3 mm long, the bracteoles 1.5-2.2 mm long; ped- icel 22-34 mm long. Sepals 2.5-3 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, triangular, appressed in an- thesis, abaxially sericeous, adaxially gla- brous, all eglandular or the lateral 4 or all 5 biglandular, the glands (1) 1.5-2.5 mm long, smallest on and beside the anterior sepal. Petals yellow; lateral petals with the claw 3-3.5 mm long and the limb 6-7.5 mm long, 6-8 mm wide, orbicular, eglandular, the anterior-lateral pair concave and erose, the posterior-lateral pair flat and dentate or short-fimbriate; posterior petal with the claw 3.5-4.5 mm long and held erect, the limb 6-6.5 mm long, 5-7 mm wide, glandular- dentate all around the margin with the glands very small, not or hardly wider than the teeth they terminate and occasionally hard- ly glandular. Stamens glabrous; filaments connate at base for ca. 1 mm; filaments op- posite sepals 4-4.5 mm long, that opposite anterior sepal erect and straight, the 2 op- posite anterior-lateral sepals curved side- ways toward posterior petal and inward to center of flower, the 2 opposite posterior- lateral sepals curved sideways toward stamen opposite posterior petal; filaments op- posite petals 2.5-3.5 mm long, always shorter than adjacent filaments, erect, +/- straight; anthers 1.3-1.8 mm long, the connective bicolored, yellow and dark red. Ovary hirsute; styles 4-5 mm long, glabrous or sparsely sericeous proximally, the anterior bowed outward at base and then erect and nearly straight, the posterior 2 curved strongly from base toward posterior petal, then distally straight and ascending at an angle or bent somewhat back toward center of flower, all with a dorsal point or short hook at the apex. Samara unknown, the very young samaras of Cowan 38542 show- ing only that its structure is typical of the genus (2 well-developed lateral wings distinct at base and apex and a narrow dorsal winglet).

description: Large dioecious, evergreen trees to 35 m; trunk with small to large well-formed buttresses to 2 m tall, diameter above buttresses to 150 cm. Bark longitudinally fissured (or with prominent longitudinal warty lines when younger), reddish or grayish brown to dark chocolate brown, the ridges usually ir- regularly shallowly cross-fissured and thus composed of thin to thickish +/- quadrangular scales; total bark thickness usually 4- 23 mm; external bark laminate; internal bark 3-13 mm thick, pale to rich salmon-red, oxidizing to deeper hues, with paler expansions of parenchyma beneath fissures, finely prominently laminate, with white to cream colored viscid exudate immediately appearing in discrete droplets upon cutting; sapwood cream, very pale pink, or white. Pubescence of two types: 1) +/-spreading acicular crisped hairs 02-0.8 mm long; and 2) minute thickly cylindrical to clavate red glandular hairs <0.05-0.1 mm long. Branchlets densely tanto ferrugineous-tomentose, longer hairs soon caducous to ex- pose abundant glandular hairs; twigs soon glabrate, pale gray to tan with numerous prominent paler lenticels. Leaves usually imparipinnate, (5)7-19-foliolate, at first  densely pubescent with both hair types at base of petiole, on and near petiolule bases, and on midvein and secondaries of leaflets abaxially, pubescence scattered to moderately dense elsewhere, most parts soon glabrate; petiole (3)6-19 cm long, terete, 2.5- 4 mm thick, basal pulvinus concave on ad- axial side; rachis (1)6-36 cm long, terete with +/- obscure low ridge along adaxial side; distal leaflets mostly 6-20 x 3-5.5 cm (in shade leaves to >25 x 6.5 cm), 2.3-3.8(4.5) times as long as wide, (narrowly) elliptic with short and blunt to elongate acuminate drip-tip, apical leaflet cuneate at base, lateral ones with base typically oblique, distal side obtuse to rounded, proximal side narrowly acute, when fresh glossy dark green above, distinctly paler beneath, when dry often very dark to blackish and non-glossy above; proximal leaflets similar but smaller (basal pair mostly 4-10 x 2.5-5 cm), relatively broader (1.6-2.8 times as long as wide), and ovate-elliptic; venation brochidodromous, raised beneath, midvein sunken with raised central ridge above, secondaries 7-15 per side (excluding drip-tip) at 60-80º to midvein, usually with scattered strong intersecondaries, secondary and finer venation impressed to flat above; petiolules thickened at base, canaliculate adaxially from decurrent leaflet bases, on apical leaflet (8)12-25(35) mm long, on distal lateral ones (1)4-8 mm long, on basal ones 5-10 mm. Panicles subterminal, arising in axils of coetaneous leaves, conical, grouped into large compound inflorescences; rachis straight, with straight branches arising at 45-90º, all axes sparsely to densely villous with both hair types; bracts 0.5-1.5 mm long, lanceolate to deltate-ovate, cymbiform, villous, ciliate, caducous; flowers borne on congested, few-flowered branchlets or branchlet complexes; staminate panicles 12-31 x 3- 17(20) cm, peduncle (0)2-8(14) cm, lateral branches to 12 cm, tertiary branchlets to 5 cm, usually much shorter, pedicel 0-0.5 mm long but often appearing as long as 2.5 mm when flower solitary on ultimate branchlet, to which it is articulate; pistillate panicles 4-16 x 2-9 cm, less branched, peduncle 0- 5 cm, lateral branches to 5 cm, tertiary branchlets much reduced, pedicel thick, 0.5-0.8 mm long, often appearing longer as described above. Flowers (measurements when fresh or rehydrated) sweetly fragrant; calyx broadly cupular, 5-lobed, slightly fleshy near base, glabrous to very sparsely villous, margins lightly glandular-ciliolate; petals 5, pale greenish cream, 3-5-veined, apex broadly to narrowly rounded; disc pale green, 10- lobed. Staminateflowers: calyx 1.6-2.5 mm wide, 0.6-1 mm long, lobes 0.5-0.7 mm long, apices rounded to obtuse; petals ob- long to narrowly ovate, 1.8-2.6 x 1-1.4(1.6) mm, strongly reflexed; stamens 10, filaments 1.2-2.1 mm long, white, anthers 0.5- 0.7 mm long, pale yellow; disc 1.1-1.7 mm wide; pistillode 0.4-0.6 x 0.5 mm, densely villous. Pistillate flowers: calyx 2.5-3 mm wide, 0.8-1.3 mm long, lobes 0.6-1.3 mm long, apices rounded to acute; petals ellipticovate, (2.2)2.5-3(3.2) x (1.2)1.3-1.7 mm, patent to moderately reflexed; staminodes well-developed, filaments 0.4-1.2 mm long, anthers 0.5-0.6 mm long; disc 1.8-2.4 mm wide; ovary yellow-green, subglobose-ovoid, 1.5-1.8 x 1.5-1.8 mm, villous, fertile locule(s) 1(-2). Fruit (fresh) obliquely oblong or ovoid, 1(2)-seeded, 1.6-2.3 cm long (dry: 1.4-1.9 cm); exocarp at maturity medium to dark reddish purple without, smooth, green within, <1 mm thick, easily sliding off mesocarp; mesocarp at maturity whitish translucent, to >2 mm thick, sweet, slippery-fleshy, before maturity green with white milky resin; endocarp cream-colored, thin, pliable, fibrous. Seed 1.2-1.6 mm long, ellipsoid, slightly curved and with narrow reflexed tip, chalaza large, saddle-like; testa thin, pliable; embryo 1.1-1.5 mm long, composed mostly of massive white cotyledons; endosperm negligible. Germination phanerocotylar, epigeous; hypocotyl with milky resin; cotyledons narrowly hemi-ovoid with falcate beak-like apex, short-petiolate, 1.8-2.5 cm long, green with purplish mark- ings on abaxial surfaces, longitudinally grooved, internally with abundant secretory canals with white milky resin;first two leaves opposite, simple, lance-elliptic to elliptic with prominent narrow drip-tip, bright rosered at first, ca. 5-9 cm long, petioles 3-7 mm long; subsequent leaves alternate, compound.

description: Erect shrubs up to 1 m tall. description: Tough-roped glabrous lianas climbing into the forest canopy, the pistillate inflorescence pendulous cauliflorous, the staminate plant unknown. Petioles +7- 10 x 0.1 cm, scarcely dilated at either end; leaf-blades membranous, in outline broadly ovate +10-11 x 11-14 cm, pedately 7-fid, the lance-elliptic-acuminate entire lobes 5.5-8 x 1.2-2.3 cm, free to within ±1-1.5 cm of midrib, the whole blade palmately 5-plinerved from the obscurely peltate insertion of petiole and the midrib giving rise ±1 cm above that point to 1 pair of major secondary veins, these 6 veins lateral to the midrib each forming the costa of a lobe and in turn giving rise to weak distant pinnate venules, the fine reticulum between these immersed and scarcely discernible on upper face, immersed but discolored be- neath. Pistillate panicle bisracemose, its stout primary axis ±35-40 cm, its secondary ones divaricate 3.5-5 cm and ±6-15-flowered. Perianth unknown. Drupes grapelike broadly ellipsoid ±10 x 7 mm, the outer skin yellow when ripe, the sweet glutinous pulp not fibrous, cleanly peeling from the endocarp, this oblong- ellipsoid a trifle dorsoventrally compressed 9 x 6-6.5 x 4.5 mm, bluntly 3-denticulate at each end, low-carinate and obscurely umbonate dorsally, the crusta- ceous shell 0.15-0.2 mm thick, the condylar aperture irregularly 3-lobed 4 x 2.5 mm.

description: Amply pinnatifoliolate tree 7-18 m tall with terete branchlets, glabrous chartaceous dull-olivaceous leaves, and short efoliate few-branched panicles of small silky-puberulent flowers arising singly from supra- axillary buds, each panicle far surpassed by the associated leaf. Stipules not seen, scars obscure. Leaf-stalks 30-37 cm, the petiole including obese pulvinus 5-10 cm, at middle 3-4 mm diam., the ventral sulcus wide and shallow, the interfoliolar segments of rachis 3-8 cm; a convex or hemispherical nectary ? 3-3.4 mm diam. between each pair of leaflets, but in some leaves smaller or sunk into the petiolar groove; leaflet-pulvinules 8-10 mm, deeply wrinkled; leaflets 5 pairs, a little accrescent distally, the blades obovate or oblong-obovate from either broadly or narrowly cuneate base, abruptly short-acuminate, the larger ones 17-20 X 7.5-9 cm; midrib centric straight, immersed or shallowly depressed ventrally, sharply prominent beneath, giving rise on each side to ±10-15 slender incurved-ascending secondary nerves brochidodrome close within the plane margin, these in turn generating tertiary and reticular venules raised on both faces. Primary axis of panicle ±10-12 cm, secondary ones smaller and simply racemose, some paired with a solitary flower; nectaries of inflorescence few and scattered, resembling those of leaf-stalk but not over 1 mm diam.; bracts ovate ? 1.5 mm, persistent; pedicels 10-14 mm, bracteolate above middle; perianth densely silky-strigulose externally, the indumentum of subcoriaceous sepals brownish, that of corolla golden; sepals subequilong, obovate obtuse 8-9 X 6-7 mm, convex dorsally; petals obovate-cuneate from broad claw, scarcely as long as calyx; anthers sessile, narrowly lance-obovoid 4.5-5 mm, densely tomentulose; pistil thinly puberulent laterally, the body ±6 mm, the style 3.5 mm. Fruit unknown.

description: Slender, macrophyllidious cauliflorous tree ?4 m tall, the young stem-tips sordid-puberulent glabrescent, the hornotinous leaves crowded at end of branchlets. Stipules caducous, not seen. Leaves 2-4(-6)- foliolate, the rachis gradually expanded upward, at insertion of leaflets ±2.5 mm wide and produced on each side into a short obtuse auricle; petiolar nectary between each pair of pulvinules, subsessile, cupular thick-rimmed 1-1.3 mm diam.; pulvinules in dorsal view nearly 2 mm, the leaflet-blade decurrent on each side, appearing sessile against leaf-rachis; blade of leaflets broad-elliptic or elliptic-obovate from subequilateral base, broadly obtuse, 3-5.8 X 2-3 (-3.3) cm, nearly 1.5 times as long as wide; midrib centric, the secondary nerves 5-7 on each side, the tertiary venulation open, all venation more prominent dorsally. Raceiuies 4-6(-7)-flowered, the primary axis 5 mm or less; bracts and bracteoles minute ephemeral; pedicels ±2.5-3 cm; flower- buds nearly glabrous, but the sepals ciliolate, the larger ones lance-oblong ±7-9.5 mm; petals golden-yellow, pubescent dorsally at base, 4 broadly obovate beyond short claw, 16-20 X 9-11 mm, the cucullus broadly oblanceolate, gently falcate, ±21 X 9 mm; anthers subsessile, narrow-oblong 6 X 2 mm, pilosulous overall; ovary subappressed-pilosulous; style ±9 mm; stigma cupular.
