description: Herbaceous vigorous scandent vines, to several meters in length, monoecious. Roots vertical, thickened, probably perennial, terete to almost 5-angled when dry, 3 cm diam., slightly branched. Stems profusely branched, the basal up to 5 cm diam., sulcate, leafless and with corky bark, the upper ones more slender, herbaceous, leafy, sul- cate-angled when dry, glandular-puberulent. Leaves petiolate, alternate; blades very variable in shape even in adjacent leaves on the same individual, those of sterile branches often deeply 5-7-lobed, those of the fertile branches generally 3-5-angled, 5-14(-18) X 6-19 cm, 5-nerved from the base, the lateral nerves soon branched, the margins denticulate, the teeth linear, 1 mm long, both surfaces of the blade rough-pubescent, the adaxial surface with trichomes from a multicellular and slightly widened base, the abaxial surface with short glandular trichomes and sharp, narrow-based trichomes 0.2-0.6 mm long, mainly on the nerves or scattered over the surface; petioles slender, 2.3-10 cm long, pubescent. Tendrils 4-5-parted, the peduncle 4-13 cm long. Flowers not fragrant, those of each sex arranged in separate inflorescences in the same axil. Staminate flowers in racemes or panicles scarcely branched at the base, 2.5-16 cm long, the pedicels slender, 5-20 mm long, densely to sparsely puberulent; flower buds broadly conical, 0.4-0.7 mm wide, invaginated at the insertion of the pedicel; receptacle urceolate, 1-1.5 X 4-4.5 mm, sparsely puberulent to glabrous, with 10 basal pouch-shaped nectaries (2 per petal) sur- rounding the stamens and covered by a ? pentagonal, cushion-shaped or raised-um- brella-shaped structure 5 mm wide; sepals 5, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 2-4 x 0.5-0.6 mm; petals 4-5 (rarely 6), trian- gular to triangular-lanceolate, 5-10 X 3-4 mm, greenish yellow or greenish white to white, with green veins, puberulent to gla- brous; filaments fused, forming a slender column, 1.5-4 mm long; anthers condupli- cate, fused, forming a globose, yellow structure, 1-1.5 X 1.5-2 mm; pollen grains oblate-spheroidal, 73.8 X 78 pm, stephan- ocolpate, generally with 9 (rarely 10) colpi, the colpi very poorly defined, tectate, ech- inate, the spines conical, 4.1-5.2 pm, with a small translucent cavity at the tip, the in- terspiny area microreticulate, the exine <2 p,m thick, the sexine as thick as nexine, the perimeter circular in polar view. Pistillate inflorescence umbelloid; flowers 3-5, sub- sessile on a common peduncle; peduncle 1- 2 cm long, elongating almost to 3 cm in fruit; perianth and nectaries as in the sta- minate flowers but smaller; ovary narrowly ovoid, glabrous, unilocular; ovule one, pen- dulous; style slender, 1-2 mm long; stigma 3-5-lobed. Fruits usually 1-3 (rarely 4), maturing simultaneously, obovoid, slightly compressed, 3.3-4 cm long, 2-2.7 cm diam., truncate to slightly invaginate at the base, obtuse at the tip, light green, with raised greenish white to white spots, and with 5-7 narrow, longitudinal grooves; epicarp coriaceous, thickened; mesocarp fleshy-fibrous, juicy, ca. 8 mm thick, with flavor of cucumber (Cucumis sativus) but slightly bitter; seed compressed, smooth, 2 x 1.6 cm.

description: Herba perennis glabra superne scaberulosa gracilis ramosa ad 3 dm alta; folia laxe rosulata ovato-oblonga 2.5-4 cm longa, 2-3 cm lata pinnata, foliolis 5-9 orbicularibus vel oblongo-cuneatis 3-5-incislobatis lobis oblongis vel ovali- bus mucronatis 1-4 mm longis; petioli graciles 5-6 cm longi basi scarioso- vaginantes; folia caulina similia; inflorescentia terminalis et lateralis pedunculis sub umbellis dense scaberulis 2.5-8 cm longis; bractea involucralis unica foliacea 0.5-1.5 cm longa; radii 5-8 patenti-adscendentes inaequales scaberulosi 0.3-0.8 cm longi; bracteolae involucellorum 3-5 lineares vel oblanceolatae integrae vel trifidae 3-5 mm longae persistentes pedicellos superantes; pedicelli 4-6 patenti- adscendentes inaequales 3-5 mm longi; petala late ovalia obtusa alba; stylo-podium breviter conoideum, stylis patentibus 0.2-0.3 mm longis; fructus late ovoideus 3 mm longus 2.5 mm latus, costis obscure angulatis suberosis valleculis aequalibus, vittis magnis; semine sub vittis canaliculato facie eius parum concava.

description: Slender perennial herb, glabrous below the scaberulous inflorescence and upper cauline leaf sheaths, from a slender taproot, alternately few-branched from above the base, the branches rather stiffly erect-ascending; leaves loosely clustered at the base; petioles gradually dilated and scarious-sheathing below; cauline leaves few, reduced upward, the petioles wholly sheathing; seed conspicuously channeled beneath the vittae, the face shallowly concave.

description: Huilaea mutisianae Uribe affinis, foliorum laminis tenuioribus integris floribus minoribus differt. Ramuli obtuse tetragoni primum sicut foliorum subtus venae primariae pedunculus pedicellique modice pilis crassiusculis pinoideis plerumque 0.2-0.4 mm longis induti demum glabrati. Petioli 1.5- 3 cm longi; lamina 10-14 X 6.5-9.5 cm elliptica vel paulo ovato-elliptica apice late acuto vel obtuso et 0.3-0.5 mm mucronulato basi late obtusa vel rotundata et paullulo (ad 0.5 mm) cordulata, membranacea et integra, supra glabra, subtus in venis secundariis sparse et in venulis superficieque sparsissime puberula (pilis crassis ca. 0.1 mm longis), breviter (usque ad 0.5 cm) 5-plinervata nervis secundariis ca. 3 mm inter se distantibus venulis subtus planis obscuris areolis ca. 0.5 mm latis, subtus in venis primariis circum basim auriculis paucis usque ad 2 X 1 mm armata. Inflorescentiae e foli- orum superiorem axillas singulae triflorae, pedunculo 11-18 X 0.1-0.15 cm arcuato; flores 6-meri, pedicellis 1-1.5 cm longis, bracteolis non visis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 10 mm longum extus densi- uscule furfuraceum; calycis tubus 3 mm longus, lobis interioribus ca. 1 mm altis remotis, dentibus exterioribus ca. 2 X 2 mm crassis divergentibus; torus intus dense ciliolatus pilis 0.3-0.4 mm longis. Petala 13-14 X 8-10 mm oblongo-obovata glabra apicem versus i. s. rugulosa. Stamina in forma isomorphica glabra; filamenta 9.2-9.6 mm vel 8-8.3 mm longa; antherarum thecae 5 vel 4.5-4.7 X 2 X 1.7 mm oblongae poris duobus 0.15-0.2 mm diam., connectivo non prolongato ca. 1.2-1.5 mm supra basim dorsaliter minute tuberculato. Stigma non expansum; stylus 15 X 1.5-1 mm glaber; ovarium ca. 5 mm longum apice conico 0.7 mm alto glabro.

description: Frutex humilis, vix ramosus, ramis 3-6 mm diam. albo-hirtellis, pilis acieularibus, patentibus, subrigidis, acutis, 3-5-cellularibus, internodiis brevibus; folia opposita, mediocria, breviter petiolata, petiolo 2-5 mm longo, albo-pilosulo, lamina late ovali, 3.7-6.5 cm longa, 2-3.5 cm lata, basi rotundata, apice obtusa vel subacuta, rigide coriacea, supra scabro-pilosula, subtuberculata, pili basi tuberculiformi alba persistenti, subtus dense albo-pilosula, pilis patentibus, rigidis, acicularibus, 2-4-cellularibus, supra obscure nervosa, subtus perspicue reticu- lato-venosa, venis et venulis prominentibus, margine regulariter crenata; inflorescentiae in axillis foliorum supremorum longissime pedunculatae, pedunculo 18-35 cm longo, subrubro, albo-hirsutulo, apice bis fureato, floribus numerosis, pedicellis albis, 11-16 mm longis; hypanthium late obconicum 2.5 mm longum, apice ca. 4 mm latum, mintute hirtellum; calycis lobi triangulari-subulati 3 mm longi, basi 2 mm lati, externe minute hirtelli, intus glabri; corolla in calyce erecta, infundibuliformis, ca. 18 mm longa, tubo cylindrico 4 mm diam., externe dense hirtello, limbo patente, ca. 12 mm lato, lobis imbricatis, externe albo-hirtellis, intus glabris; stamina 4, libera, basi corollae adnata, filimentis glabris, antheris oblongis, liberis, 4.5 mm longis, 2.5 mm latis, loculis parallelis, discretis, glabris; ovarium fere omnino inferum, pars libera conicum, pilosulum; stylus parce hirsutulus; stigma stomatomorphum; discus annularis, crassus, glaber, quinquelobulatus; fructus capsularis, hypanthio 5 mm long, 7 mm apice lato, albo-pilosulo, 10-costato, apice rostrato, valvis 4, ca. 5 mm longis, ineurvis.

description: Sect. Cremanium. In systemate Cogniauxii M. setulosae Cogn. affinis, ramis acute quadrangulatis ad nodos stipuliformiter manicatis floribus maioribus differt. Ramuli acute subalato-quadrangulares sicut inflorescentiae rami ramulique sparse caduceque setu- losi pilis p. p. minore caduce glanduliferis; nodi crasse annulati annulo circum petioli basim ca. 4 mm alto. Petioli 1.5-3 cm longi apicem versus sparse setosi pilis laevibus gracilibus 1-2.5 mm longis; lamina 7-13 X 3-6.5 cm elliptico-oblonga apice hebeti-acuto basi rotundata, firme membranacea et obscure ciliato-serrulata, supra sparse appresso-setosa demum glabrata, subtus in venis primariis secundariisque sparse setosa pilis gracilibus 1-3 mm longis in venulis superficieque glabra, 7-nervata (pari inframarginali tenui incluso) nervis secundariis ca. 5 mm inter se distantibus nervulis subtus planis laxe reticulatis (areolis 0.7-1 mm latis). Panicula ca. 14 X 7 cm multiflora; flores 5-meri subsessiles (pedicellis crassis ca. 0.5 mm longis), bracteolis ca. 3-3.5 X 1.5 mm valde caducis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 3.5 mm longum teres basim versus glabrum apicem versus sparse vel sparsis- sime setulosum pilis 0.5-1 mm longis caduce glanduliferis; calycis tubus 0.4 mm altus, lobis interi- oribus 0.7 X 2 mm oblatis, dentibus exterioribus inframarginalibus. Petala 4.6-5 X 3.2-3.4 mm oblongo-obovata asymmetrice retusa ut videtur pruinosa. Stamina paulo dimorphica glabra; fila- menta 4.6 vel 4 mm longa; antherarum thecae 2.8-3 vel 2.7 X 0.8 X 1-1.1 mm obovato-oblongae late biporosae; connectivum ad basim ventraliter bilobulatum dorsaliter vix vel paullulo (ad 0.3-0.4 mm) hebeti-cornutum. Stigma paulo expansum 1.2 mm diam.; stylus 6 X 0.8-1 mm glaber in ovarii apicem 0.4 mm immersus; ovarium 3-4-loculare et 1/3-1/2 inferum, apice libero conico 1.2 mm alto glabro.

description:
Sect. Cremanium. In monographia Cogniauxii speciebus 472-475 affinis, ramulis setosis floribus maioribus differt.

Ramuli primum obscure quadrangulati striati demum teretes sparsiuscule vel modice setosi pilis 1-1.7 mm longis laevibus robustis. Petioli 0.2-0.3 (-0.6) cm longi glabri; lamina 2-3 X 1-1.5 cm oblongo-elliptica apice hebeti-acuto basi late acuta, subrigida et integra, glabra, 3-nervata nervis secundariis 1-1.5 mm inter se distantibus nervulis subtus planis laxe reticulatis areolis ca. 1 mm latis. Inflorescentia 2-3 cm longa submultiflora; flores 5-meri subsessiles (pedicellis 0.1-0.2 mm longis), bracteolis 3 X 1.4-1.7 mm oblongo-ovatis ad anthesim caducis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 3.6 mm longum glabrum; calycis tubus 0.4 mm longus, lobis interioribus 0.6-0.7 mm longis oblatis, dentibus exterioribus minutis inframarginalibus. Petala glabra 4 X 2.9-3.1 mm late obovata, apice asym- metrice retuso. Stamina isomorphica glabra; filmenta 3-3.2 mm longa; antherarum thecae 2-2.2 X 0.7 X 0.9-1 mm obovato-oblongae, apice 0.3-0.5 mm biporoso; connectivum ad basim ventraliter ca. 0.3 mm bilobulatum dorsaliter dente hebeti 0.4-0.5 mm longo descendenti armatum. Stigma paulo expansum 0.9-1 mm diam.; stylus 4.5-5 X 0.3-0.7 mm glaber in ovarii apicem 0.3 mm im- mersus; ovarium 3-loculare et 1/3-1/2 inferum apice setulis paucis glanduliferis 0.2-0.4 mm longis coronato.

description: Suffrutex 20 cm altus. Caulis teres, glaber, decorticans. Ramuli 4-costati, primum punctato-glandulosi demum glabriusculi. Laminae sessiles, patulae, elliptico- lanceolatae, margine crenulato, utrinque densiuscule impresso-punctata, 1-nervae. Flores solitarii. Petala flava, apice acuminata. Ovarium 3-4-loculare. description: Subshrub, ca. 20 cm tall. Stem terete, bark peeling off, without leaves at the base, glabrous. Young branches quadrangular, 4-costate, covered with sessile glands, glutinous, older branches quadrangular, with bark peeling off, leaf scars conspicuous, glabrescent. Leaves sessile, spreading, blade 5-8 X 1-2 mm, elliptic, apex obtuse, base attenuate, margin crenulate, densely covered with sessile glands on both surfaces, slightly glutinous, with only one central vein. Flowers 5-merous, solitary. Pedicels 0.5-1.2 mm. Hypanthium 2.5-3 X 1.5-1.7 mm, oblong-campanulate, 10-costate, covered with sessile glands, calyx lobes 3-4 mm long, subulate, apex acute, not apiculate; petals 5-7 X 3 mm, yellow, oblong, apex acuminate, margin glabrous, slightly undulate. Stamens 10, dimorphic, yellow, large stamens 5, the filaments 2-2.5 mm long, the thecae ca. 1.5 mm long, oval-oblong, corrugate, with rostrum ca. 0.3 mm long, the connective prolonged ca. 1.5 mm, with ventral appendage ca. 1 mm long, ex- panded and slightly acute; small stamens 5, the filaments ca. 2 mm long, the thecae ca. 1.5 mm long, oval-oblong, corrugate, with rostrum ca. 0.2 mm long, the connective prolonged ca. 0.5 mm, with ventral appendage 0.1-0.2 mm long, obtuse. Ovary superior, 3-4-locular, glabrous; style 4-5 mm long, filiform, glabrous, stigma truncate. Capsule not seen.

description: Shrubs, ca. 3 m tall. Twigs slightly to moderately 4-angled, smooth or slightly tuberculate-roughened, ferrugineous, youngest portions densely and ± evenly pubescent with brown unbranched to irregularly branched or ± stellate, matted multicellular hairs; internodes 1.7-4.9 cm long. Leaf blades 3.1-5.5 X 1.8-3.6 cm, elliptic or slightly obovate, coriaceous, slightly to strongly inrolled abaxially; apex obtuse or rounded; base cuneate or rounded; margin slightly to strongly revolute, especially near base, obscurely serrate in distal ca. 3/4; venation essentially basal, with 1-2 pairs of conspicuous secondary veins, the largest joining midvein 0.5-1 mm above lamina base; adaxial surface with midvein, largest pair of secondary veins (less commonly both pairs of secondary veins), and tertiary veins strongly impressed when fresh, but flattening upon drying; abaxial surface with midvein and largest pair of secondary veins raised, smaller intramarginal secondary veins and tertiary veins less raised, the quaternary and higher-order veins slightly raised in dried material, the surface sparsely pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem concentrated along veins, and scattered minute, glandular hairs; persistent axillary hair tufts absent. Petioles 0.6-1.3 cm long, densely pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem. Inflorescences borne in leaf axils and on leafless nodes below leaves, 2.3-5.2 x 0.8-2.4 cm, 1-2- branched, the caducous bracts to ca. 2 mm long, sparsely to densely pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem; peduncle 1.6-2.9 cm long, sparsely to densely pubescent with hairs similar to those on stem. Mature flowers not known. Flower buds with immature hypanthium, ca. 1.6 mm long, 1.6 mm wide, subglobose, essentially glabrous, the portion free from ovary ca. 0.5 mm long; portion of calyx bearing ex- ternal teeth ca. 0.3 mm long. Immature ca- lyx teeth ca. 0.2 x 0.3 mm. Calyptra pre- sent in bud, domelike. Immature petals ca. 0.5 X 0.7 mm, obovate, slightly cupped adaxially, white; apex rounded, emarginate. Immature folded stamens white; filament narrowly ovate, ca. 0.3 X 0.3 mm; anther narrowly obovate, ca. 0.8 x 0.4 mm, the anther sacs ca. 0.4 mm long, apparently opening by a single gaping foramen, septum torn. Immature ovary inferior, ca. 0.8 x 1.5 mm, the apical appendage ca. 0.3 mm high; immature style ca. 0.5 X 0.5 mm, white, straight; stigma ca. 0.6 mm wide. Berries and seeds not known.

description: Stems prostrate, 0.6-1.5 m. long, mostly 1-2 mm thick, sparsely pubescent, rarely rather densely so. Leaves linear, frequently narrow-linear, rarely linearoblong, mostly longer than 7 times the width, 2.5-7 cm long, 2-3 (-5) mm wide, sessile or shortly petiolate; apex acute, obtuse-mucronate or mucronulate; base acute or obtuse, never cordate; surface with sparse hairs or nearly glabrous, rarely densely pubescent. Flowers solitary, very rarely in cymes of 3; peduncles mostly as long as subtending leaved or longer; pedicels 3-8 mm long, slightly thicker than peduncles; bracteoles minute, linear, mostly unequal. Sepals oval-lanceolate, with ciliate or entire margins, usually glabrous, rarely with scattered hairs; apex acuminate, rarely acute. Corolla white, 1.8-2.2 cm long. Stamens included; filaments glandular-villous. Ovary with a brownish disc around the base, villous near the apex, thin-walled; styles fused for not more than a quarter of their length; stylar branches unequal, included. Fruits usually 1- or 2-seeded, rarely 3- or 4-seeded, glabrous except at the apex, mostly with persistent stylopodia as short beaks. Cotyledonary petioles fused. Flowering from May to late July.

description: The cylindrical creeping rhizome and the basal portion of the stipe clothed with castaneous, glossy, lanceolate, nearly hairpointed scales, which are short-ciliate toward the tip and seated on raised points, the rhizome becoming asperous. The stiffly erect stipe ca. 25 cm. long, brown, terete, slightly paleaceous and soon naked. Lamina three times dichotomously branched, rigidly coriaceous, internodes of the primary axis 12-15 cm. long, the nodes with stipulaceous short pin- nules, the secondary axes opposite, 4, the tertiary ones 8 cm. long, both pectinate-pinnate, the ultimate pinnae up to 20 cm. long and 4 cm. wide at the middle, narrowed gradually to both ends, all axes densely clothed beneath with ovate, first brown, soon grayish, densely ciliate scales; ultimate segments all more or less reflexed, contiguous at the slightly dilated base and gradually narrowed toward the subobtuse or subretuse apex, about 2.5 mm. wide at the middle, the margins entire and strongly revolute, the midribs and veins reddish and naked above, the midribs much elevated beneath and densely floccose-paleaceous; sporangia mostly 4 to each sorus, large, superficial, reddish brown, filling out almost the whole space between the revolute margins.

description: Sticherus rhizomate late horizontaliter repente, cylindrico, subflexuoso, atrobrunneo, ca. 2 mm. diametro, paleis castaneis, lanceolatis, minute ciliatis vel integris, 0.4-0.5 mm. basi latis, 1-1.5 mm. longis, sat dense vestito. Lamina uni- vel bifureatia, 25 cm. longa, coriacea, subtus glauca; ramis striete erectis, fere verticalibus, lanceolatis, ad 25 em. longis, versus apicem longe et gradatim attenuatis, infra medium 3-3.5 cm. latis, iis folii unifureati usque ad basin utrinque pectinato-pinnati- fidis, primariis folii bis fureati 2-5 cm. longis, intus pinnatifidis extus ilnterdum nudis; costis superne teretibus, glabris, subtus quadrangu- laribus, prominulis, paleis brunneis, squarrosis, ovatis vel late lanceo- latis, acuminatis, sparse ciliatis, mox deciduis sat dense vestitis; seg- mentis numerosis, densis, faleatis, basi parum dilatata (2 mm. lata) contiguis, linearibus, medio 1.5 mm. latis, marginibus revolutis, integris vel apice solumn leviter crenatis, utrinque nudis glabrisque; costulis subtus promiinulis, venis supra basin fureatis, superne distinctis, ele- vatis; soris medialibus, sporangiis 3-5 in quoque soro, superficialibus, magnis, laete brunneis.

description: A species of the group of G. hirta with narrow ultimate pinnae, mostly under 1 cm. wide, very like those of the American G. revoltuta H.B.K. description: Trunco ex schedula gracili, ad 1 m. alto; foliis subsessilibus 4-5, plane expansis, herbaceis, subtus pallide viridibus, versus basin grada- tim attenuatis, vix 1 m. longis, medio 30 cm. latis, tripinnatis. Rachi ad basin 7-8 mm. lata, dense paleacea et brunneo-tomentosa, paleis partis inferioris lanceolatis, acuminatis, 1 cm. longis, vix 1 mm. basi latis, atris, nitidis, marginibus erosis tenuibus pallidis, sequentibus stramineis apicis medio atratis, superioribus concoloribus, stramineis. Pinnis alternis, sessilibus, 4 cm. inter se remotis, horizontalibus (in- ferioribus reflexis), versus basin laminae sensim abbreviatis, infimis 2-3 cm. longis, medialibus ca. 15 cm. longis, 3-3.5 cm. latis, oblongis, breve acuminatis; costis omnino exalatis, superne pilis brunneis an- trorsis strigosis, inferne ut rachidis parte superiore dense paleaceis (paleis minoribus, stramineis, iis versus apicem costae bullatis), et sub paleis brunneo-hirtis. Pinnis II. ord. sessilibus, alternis, 1 cm. inter se remotis, ad 20-jugis, parum obliquis, oblongis, obtusis, ad 2 cm. longis, 6-7 mm. latis, glaberrimis, costulis paleis albidis bullatis nonnullis subtus praeditis; pinnulis ultimis ca. 6-jugis, infimis liberis, ceteris ala angusta connectis, oblongis vel subspathulatis, integris, ca. 3 mm. longis, 1.5 mm. latis, apice subtruneato-rotundatis; venis 3-4-jugis, simplicibus, rarius fureatis. Soris submedialibus parvis, indusiis semi- cupularibus, membranaceis, integris, persistentibus, receptaculo cylindrico, prolongato, paraphysibus nullis vel paucis brevibus.

description: Trunco ex schedula ad 2 m. alto, 12 cm. diam., superiore parte basibus adpressis stipitum foliorum emortuorum obtecto. Foliis ca. 10, ad 2 m. longis; stipite inermi, basi 2 sursum 1 cm. crasso, 40 mm. longo, paleis stramineis, lanceolatis, acuminatis, 3-4 cm. longis, basi 2 mm. latis, marginibus tenuibus minute erosis densissime vestito, paleis magnis delapsis parce submuriculato, et sub his paleis aliis parvis fer- rugineis, ovatis vel rotundis, pilis atropurpureis, cylindricis, rigidis ciliatis sat dense furfuraceo. Lamina ad basin paulo decreseente, crassa, coriacea, superne obscure viridi, subtus (in sieco) brunneseente, bipinnata-pinnatifida vel subtripinnata. Pinnis alternis, subsessilibus, 8 em. inter se remotis, lanceolatis, 40 cm. longis, ad 15 cm. latis, breve aduminatis; pinnulis sessilibus, alternis, 3 cm. inter se remotis, 15-16- jugis, ad 7 cm. longis, e basi 2 em. lata versus apicem subintegrum acuminatum subgradatim angustatis, fere ad costulam pinnatifidis vel basi pinnatis, basalibus parum abbreviatis; segnientis (vel pinnulis III. ord.) oblongis, subfaleatis, integris vel leviter repandulo-crenatis, obtusis, 2.5 mm. latis. Radhi costisque paleis stramineis iis stipitis similibus sed minoribus et cito delapsis vestitis et aliis brunneis parvis setosis furfuraceis, superficie superiore pinnularum praeter costulas exalatas parce strigosas glabra, inferiore paleis adpressis, rufo-brun- neis, fimbriatis ciliis intertextis, setis atropurpureis praeditis dense obtecta. Venis 8-10-jugis, fureatis, superne impressis subtus valde elevatis tamen sub tomento occultis. Soris subcostularibus, in tomento inimerso, indusio subcoriaceo, cupuliformi, ore integro, receptadulo capitato, paraphysibus nullis ( ?).

description:
Planta H. aconitifolia A. Rich. simulans; caulibus glabris; foliis orbiculari-peltatis, 2-5 cm. diametro, angulate 5-lobatis, lobis lanceo- latis, acutis vel acuminatis, lobis terminalibus lateralibusque quam basalibus longioribus, marginibus inciso-serratis, supra in nervis venisque hirsutulis, subtus sparse hirsutulis, petiolis glabris; pedunculis quam foliis longioribus, glabris; umbellis simplicibus, 50-80-floris, pedicellis 5-8 mm. longis, glabris; fructibus glabris, costis inconspicuis, acutis.

Stems slender, glabrous; leaves orbicular-peltate, 2-5 cm. in diame- ter, hiirsutulous above on the nerves and veins with appressed ascend- ing hairs, sparingly hirsutulous on the nerves and veins beneath with somewhat crispate to divaricate hairs, angulately 5-lobed, the distance from insertion of petiole to sinus 5-15 mm., unequal within the leaf, the lobes lanceolate, acute to acuminate, the apical and lateral lobes usually longer than the basal, the margins incised-serrate, the lobes occasionally trilobulate, the petioles slender, 2-12 cm. long, glabrous; peduncles longer than the leaves, 6-25 cm. long, glabrous; umbels simple, 50-80-flowered, the pedicels 5-8 mm. lolng, reflexed and spread- ing, glabrous; fruit transversely elliptical, 1-1.5 mm. long, 2 mm. broad, glabrous, the ribs obscure, acute, the stylopodium conical.

description: Stipite inermi, ad 30 cm. longo, basi 2 cm. crasso, parte inferiore paleis albido-stramineis anguste lanceolatis, 3-4 cm. longis, 1.5-2 mm. latis, integris, longe acuminatis vestito et ubique paleis brunneis ovatis perparvis, setis atropurpureis rigidis praeditis, tomeiitoso-furfuraceo. Lamina basi parce angustata, papyracea, superne obscuro subtus plumbeo-viridi, bipinnata-pinnatifida. Pinnis sessilibus, alternis, 10 cm. inter se remotis, 40 cm. vel ultra longis, 12-13 cm. latis, acumin- atis; pinnulis sessilibus, alternis, 1.5 cm. inter se remotis, oblongis, acuminatis, 6-7 cm. longis, 12 mm. latis, fere ad costulam ubique exalatum pinnatifidis; segmentis parum obliquis, subcontiguis, 2 mm latis, obtusis, marginibus parallelis, planis, ca. ad medium ineisis, lobulis profunde emarginatis vel bifidis; venis 6-7-jugis, furcatis, superne impressis subtus prominulis. Rachi, costis, costulis venisque ut stipite utrinque dense ferrugineo-furfuraceis, costis ad basin paleis linearibus albidis subtus ornatis. Soris subcostularibus, in segmento 6-6-jugis, totam superficiem fere tegentibus, indusiis rnagnis, brunneis, nitidis, membranaceis, cupuliformibus ore subelauso integro vel serius fissis, paraphysibus nullis ( ?).

description: Alsophila trunco 2.4 m. alto, apice 24 cm. diametro (vide infra schedulam collectoris). Stipite 30 cm. longo 1 cm. crasso, ferociter aculeato (aculeis numerosis, conicis vel mammiformibus, brunneis, sub- ito in apicem pungentem atrum contractis, 3-4 mm. longis, basi 1-2 mm. crassis), basi paleis castaneis, contortis, integris, lanceolato-acumi- natis, ad 5 cm. longis, 2-3 vel interdum 5 mm. basi latis dense vestito, sursum cito denudatis, sub his paleis aliis parvis polymorphis rufis, dense et longe ciliatis, intertextis, facile abrasis, primum lanoso-fur- furaeeo. Lainina basi paulo angustata, coriacea, bipinnata-pinnatifida, rachi ut stipite vestita, tomento delapso minute aspera. Pinnis alternis, 8 em. inter se remotis, breve (1 cm.) petiolatis, 30 cm. vel ultra longis, 12 cm. latis, acuminatis; costis ut rachi utrinque rufo-tomentosis, mox denudatis, omnino exalatis; pinnulis sessilibus, alternis, 2 cm. inter se remotis, obliquis, ca. 8 cm. longis, basi 15 mm. latis, abrupte acuminatis, fere ad costulam pinnatifidis vel parte basali pinnatis, costulis superne sparsius inferne dense rufo-squamoso-tomentosis, paleis iis rachidis similibus, facile abrasis; segmentis faleatis, basi 2 mm. vel ultra latis, obtusis, marginibus arete revolutis integris vel leviter crenatis, superne subnudis subtus ad nervum medianum valde elevatum ut costulis dense vestitis; venis ca. 10-jugis, fureatis, inferne prominulis tamen sub tomento occultis. Soris medialibus, juvenilibus in tomento occultis, exindusiatis, receptaculo elevato, capitato, paraphysibus paucis, brevibus praeditis.

description: Alsophila trunco stipiteque ab collectore infra descriptis. Lamina coriacea, tripinnata, rachidis parte visa 2 cm. crassa, superne sulcata, laete bruinuea, dense aculeata (aculeis conicis, m-laximis 2 mm. altis basi 1-2 imm. crassis, apice castaneis) et paleis (plerisque delapsis) sordide griseis, tenuibus, lanceolatis, longe acuminatis, breve et decidue ciliatis, basi 1-5 mnm. vel ultra latis 2-3 cm. vel ultra longis primum dense vestita, paleis delapsis minute muriculata, pilis destituta. Pinna visa longe (6 cm.) petiolata, 60 cm. longa, breve acuminata, costa sursum anguste alata laete brunnea superne late sulcata et in sulco pilis rufis brevibus dense tomentoso-hirto, subtus tereti, versus basin muriculata (ex paleis delapsis?). Pinnulis ca. 25-jugis, alternis, petiolulatis, iis infra medium pinnae basi recte divaricatis e medio arcuatim reflexis superioribus horizontalibus vel obliquis, maximis (inframedialibus) 16-18 cm. longis, 3 cm. latis, acuminatis, parte tertia basali pinnatis, sursum fere ad costulam pinnatifidis, costulis superne rufo-hirtis, sub- tus paleis parvis, rufis, ovatis verisimiliter dense vestitis, mox denu- datis. Pinnulis III. ord. basi late adnatis, obliquis vel falcatis, 1.5 cm. vel ultra longis, 3 mm. latis, marginibus infra apicem breve acutum parallelis, integris, subrevolutis, superne glabris, subtus ad venas floccoso-hirtis et ad nervum medianum paleis rufis, parvis, ovatis, ciliatis vestitis; venis 14-15-jugis, furcatis (nullis bis fureatis), subtus elevatis. Sonis medialibus, totam superficiem tegentibus, receptaculo parvo pilis basi circumdatis, sporangiis rufo-brunneis, paraphysibus nonnullis intermixtis.

description: Plants soft, yellow-green, often somewhat globular in shape, 2-7 cm high, 5-12 cm in diam; ribs usually absent, podaria rarely elevated but broad and flat; areoles 1-2 cm apart, 2-3 mm in diam; flower 1.3-2.2 cm in diam, 1.3-2.4 cm long; outer perianth segments 1-2 mm broad; inner perianth segments 2-2.5 mm broad, usually white or faintly pink but sometimes appearing yellowish white; pollen 0-6 colpate, 26.1-48.5 ,u in diam (Fig. 4).

description: Stipes up to the much reduced basal pinnae ca. 35 cm. long and nearly 3 cm. thick at base, covered throughout with a thick mass of castaneous, glossy, cylindrical, articulated, rather thin and soft but not at all woolly hairs, all of one kind, the lower ones 3-4 cm. long and mostly reflexed, the upper patently squarrose, their bases considerably thickened and remaining when the hairs are broken off, the stipe becoming densely muricate. Radhis and all main ribs with similar, smaller, patent hairs and asperulous, the hairs of costae and costules paler and not dense. As to other characters hardly different from D. Hieronymi.

description: Amply foliate trees 10 m with trunk +/- 1.5 dm diam, glabrous except for minutely golden-strigulose axes of inflorescence, the stiffly papery, olivaceous subconcolorous leaflets glabrous except for residual puberulence along midrib beneath, the racemes arising singly both from axils of mature leaves and from some defoliate nodes of terete annotinous branches. Stipules not seen, and stipular scars obscure. Leaf-stalks 3-4.5 dm, terete, the petiole including obese pulvinus 2-3.5 cm, the interfoliolar segments 5-8 cm, the proximal leaflet-pairs not quite opposite but distal ones exactly so; leaflet-pulvinules 7-9 mm; leaflets 5-6 pairs and a small terminal one, the penultimate pair largest, all elliptic-obovate or broadly elliptic from equilateral, broad-cuneate base, abruptly contracted into a narrowly lanceolate acute acumen +/-1-1.5 cm, the larger blades 15-21 x 7-10 cm, the margin of all loosely revolute; midrib centric, straight or almost so, cariniform beneath, the slender, widely ascending secondary nerves weakly camptodrome within the margin, ventrally immersed or shallowly depressed, finely prominulous dorsally, not giving rise to a defined reticulum of veinlets. Racemes incurved to vertical, simple or rarely once branched, the primary axis (3)6-13 cm; bracts triangular 1-1.3 mm, deciduous; pedicels 12-17 mm, bibracteolate beyond middle, only a trifle dilated upward, the bracteoles caducous; flower-buds prior to anthesis plumply ellipsoid 8-9 x 6.5-7 mm, obtuse, dark brown and resinous; calyx at anthesis (3)4-cleft, the recurved lobes gla- brous internally; petal yellow, ovate-subcordate, including the short claw 15-18 x 10-11 mm, the margin undulate; sexual or- gans glabrous throughout, the longer stamens 6-7, their filament +/-15 mm and an- ther 1.2-1.5 mm, the shorter stamens more than 100; gynophore 14-18 mm; ovary in profile elliptic 8-9 x 2.5-3 mm; style terminal +/-2 mm, incurved through +/-45º, tapering into a poriform stigma. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1992. Centennial beans: A miscellany of American Fabales. Brittonia. 44: 224-239.

description: Tree to 12 m; unbranched trunk 5 m, terete, to 23.2 cm dbh; crown 8 m diam., branchlets glabrous. Leaves imparipinnately 5-foliolate; stipules ca. 2 X 0.7 mm, persistent, acerose, glabrous; petioles ca. 7.7 mm long, terete, sparsely strigose; rachis 10-12 cm long, terete, stipellate, glabrous to sparsely strigose; petiolules 3 mm long, black; leaflets alternate, elliptic to ovate, 5.5 X 2.5 cm, the lower pairs smaller, the base obtuse, the apex acuminate or sometimes long acuminate, both surfaces green and glabrous, the upper shining, costa and venules equally salient. Inflorescence a raceme or panicle, 5.4 cm long, axillary or arising from leafless branches, the axis strigose; bracts attached to the base of the pedicel, 1.2 X 0.4 mm, triangular-ovate, sericeous, persistent; bracteoles 1.1 X 0.7 mm, attached to the pedicel halfway up from the base, persistent; pedicel 1 cm, dorsiventrally compressed. Buds elliptic, 5-5.5 X 3.8- 4.1 mm, glabrous. Calyx 4-lobed, the lobes irregular, both surfaces glabrous. Petal 1, yellow, glabrous, the claw 2.3 X 3 mm, the blade ovate, 7.4 X 3 mm. Stamens dimorphic, larger ones 2, filaments 4.3-6.5 mm, glabrous, the anthers oblong 2.1 X 0.7 mm, the smaller stamens many and glabrous, the filaments 6.3 mm, the anthers oblong-elliptic, 1.2 X 0.9 mm. Gynoecium glabrous, the gynophore 3.6 mm, the ovary elliptic, ca. 2.5 X 1.3 mm, ovules 8, the style 1 mm long, straight lateral, the stigma punctiform. Fruit unknown.

description: Tree ca. 2 m. Leaf imparipinnately 5-7- foliolate; stipules lanceolate, 1.9 X 0.4 mm, strigose; petiole 4.5-5.7 cm, terete, sparsely strigulose; rachis 7.5-12.3 cm, terete, strigulose; stipels lacking; petiolule 4.4 mm, terete, strigulose; leaflets 5-7, 9-14.8 X 4- 5 cm, terminal elliptic to obovate, the lateral ones oblong to elliptic, the base cuneate, the apex acuminate, upper surface glabrous and the lower surface sparsely strigulose, venation plane above and prominent beneath. Racemes 10 cm, arising from leafless branches, the axis tomentose; bracts lanceolate, 1 X 0.4 mm, attached to the pedicel base, tomentose; bracteoles lacking; pedicel 5.5 mm, sericeous. Buds ovoid, 3.8 X 4.1 mm, sparsely shortly sericeous. Calyx 4-lobed, the lobes heteromorphic, glabrous within. Petals lacking. Stamens dimorphic, larger ones 2, filaments 5.4 x 0.7 mm, golden yellow, sparsely pilose, the anthers oval, 2.6 X 1.3 mm, cream, glabrous; smaller stamens many, the filaments 2.7 mm, yellow, glabrous, the anthers oblate, 0.7 X 0.7 mm, cream, glabrous. Gynophore 2.4 mm, sericeous, ovary elliptic, 3.1 X 1.7 mm, sericeous, style 0.3 mm, lateral, glabrous, the stigma punctiform, glabrous. Fruit unknown.

description: Inter Pachycarpas stipulis maximis ovato-acuminatis circa 2 X 1 cm cum M. regina Barneby et M. rhodostegia Barneby, ambabus in prov. goiasensis altis rupestribus inquilinis, associanda, sed inflorescentia paniculata (nec pseudoracemosa) foliorum caulinorum rachi praelonga 27-33 (nec 10-22) cm usque longa inter pinnas spiculis binis instructa (nec nuda), pinnis minus numerosis usque 16 (nec 25-44)-jugis, folio- lisque subtriplo majoribus 11-12 X 2.3-2.7 mm usque absimilis, ulterius a M. regina pedunculis 2-2.5 (nec 5-8) cm longis corollisque vix 4.5 (nec 7-8) mm longis abstans.

description: Shrub attaining 3 m with notably long multifoliolate cauline leaves and a terminal pyramidal, efoliate but amply bracteate panicle of plumply ellipsoid capitula, the stout stems and inflorescence-axes at once gray-puberulent and densely hispid with yellowish setae of different lengths, the longer ones simply tapering 3-9 mm, the shorter ones capitate-glandular to 3.5 mm, the plane olivaceous leaflets facially glabrous, setulose-ciliolate. Stipules and bracts of inflorescence ovate-acuminate or caudate, to 20-23 X 8-13 mm, imbricate when young, deciduous before anthesis from a fuscous horizontal scar, the blade finely multistriate, subappressed-silky dorsally, glabrous within. Leaf-formula to xvi/34- 38; leafstalks including short petiole 27-33 cm, in lower fourth 3.5-4 mm diam, charged ventrally, between each pair of pinna-pulvinules, with a pair of narrowly lanceolate acute, green spicules 4-5 mm, the longer interpinnal segments ± 1.5-2 cm; pinna-rachises 4.5-8 cm, a little accrescent distally, the longer interfoliolar segments nearly 2 mm; leafletpulvinules fuscous 0.5-0.8 mm diam; blades broad-linear from semicordate base, straight, obtuse apiculate, the larger ones ±11-12 X 2.3-2.7 mm; venation of 5-6 nerves from pulvinule, the midrib a little forwardly displaced, one anterior and 3-4 posterior all weakly prominulous. Infiorescence paniculate, prior to anthesis amply bracteate, ±4 X 2 dm, the lower branches to 2 dm; peduncles solitary, 2-2.5 cm; capitula without filaments ?16 X 12 mm; bracts oblanceolate ?3.5-5.5 X 1 mm, densely setose dorsally and ciliate; flowers 4-merous, many staminate, all subsessile; calyx shallowly turbinate-campanulate ±0.45 X 0.35 mm, glabrous except for 1-2 minute cilia on the undulate rim; corolla membranous, glabrous below the dorsally setulose lobes, the deeply campan- ulate, slenderly 4-ribbed tube contracted at base into a short neck, ?4.2 mm, the ovate lobes 1.2 mm; androecium 8-merous, the filaments pale pink ±2 cm, united at base into a tube nearly 1 mm; anthers 0.4 mm diam. Fruit unknown.

description: Dwarf unarmed, loosely tufted, subacaulescent subshrub from xylopodium, 9-14 cm tall, the leaf-axes and scapiform peduncles thinly strigulose, micropuberulent, and charged with short thickened trichomes but eglandular, the firm plane corneous-marginate leaflets light green concolorous, the capitula long-pedunculate, glabrous. Stems of the year ± 1.5-2.5 cm. Stipules papery, pale orange brown, ovate or lanceolate from inequilateral base, prominently 5-9-nerved, facially glabrous, setulose-ciliate, persistent. Pulvini of petiole and of each pinna corneous at base and apex, soft and sunken at middle. Leafstalks 3.5-4.5 cm, espiculate; pinnae 1 pair, the rachis 2.5-4 cm, the in- terfoliolar segments ±6-10 mm; leaflets 3- 6 pairs, the green pulvinule 0.6-1 mm seated in a cupular pallid base, the leaflet  blades ovate-elliptic from semicordate base, apiculate, the larger ones 14-18 X 5-7 mm; venation of 5 prominent primary nerves from pulvinule, the midrib displaced to divide blade ±1:2, the innermost posterior primary nerve produced nearly to blade apex, the margin continuously corneous, ascending-setulose-ciliate. Peduncles 6-12 cm; capitula without filaments ± 8 mm diam; bracts oblong or spatulate ±2 mm; perianth glabrous or the membranous calyx minutely 1-2-glandular-setulose at orifice the calyx turbinate-campanulate ? 1.6 X 1.2 mm, irregularly 5-toothed, the teeth mostly triangular; corolla vase shaped 5-merous, ±3 mm, the lobes incurved; androecium 6- merous, the fertile filaments to 8.5 mm, the anthers 0.7-0.8 mm diam; ovary 2(3)-ovulate, puberulent. Pod substipitate, of 2 segments, the distal one abortive, the proximal one 9-10 X 6-7 mm, the replum 0.4 mm wide, the thin green valves minutely puberulent; seed in broad view ?5.5 X 4 mm, pleurogrammate.

description: Epiphytic shrub. Uppermost branchlets bluntly quadrate with elevated internodal lines or ridges, but becoming rounded and coarsely striate with age. Young vegetative buds, floral peduncles, young floral bracts, hypanthia, and calyx lobes moderately covered with a caducous indument of scurfy and or stellulate hairs. Mature leaves of a pair equal to somewhat unequal in size, essentially glabrous on both surfaces; petioles 0.9-2.1 cm long; blades coriaceous, 4.2-9.1 X 1.9-4.3 cm, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, apex bluntly acuminate, base acute to obtuse, margin entire, 5-plinerved, the inner- most primaries diverging from the median vein 2-6 mm above the blade base (on abaxial surface) and forming poculate acarodomatia sparsely to moderately beset with barbellate hairs in the angles formed with the median vein, the transverse secondary veins spaced 0.25 mm apart at the widest portion of the blade. Flowers erect, 2-5 per axil in uppermost leafy branches; peduncles 5-7 mm long, lenticellate. Floral bracts free, sometimes recurved at the apex; outer bracts 3-3.5 X 2-2.5 mm, elliptic-ovate, apex bluntly acute to rounded; inner bracts 2-2.5 X 2-2.5 mm, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, apex rounded. Hypanthium (at anthesis) narrowly campanulate, 3-4 mm long to the torus and 2.5-3 mm diam. Calyx tube 1.5-2 mm long, cupulate; free portions of calyx lobes 0.5-1.5 mm long and 0.5-1.5 mm wide basally between sinuses, broadly subtruncate and often apiculate, somewhat callose-thickened at the median apex abaxially. Petals 6, glabrous but sometimes fringed with inconspicuous caducous white hairs, 6-6.5 X 2-3 mm, reportedly white or pink, obovate-rhombic, the apex bluntly long-acuminate and somewhat concave. Stamens 12, isomorphic, filaments 3 mm long, somewhat declinate, complanate, glabrous; anthers free or laterally connate (in part), 2.5 X 0.25 mm, pale yellow (?) and granulose along the lower ventral half of the thecae, subulate, each with a solitary dorsally inclined apical pore; connective thickened dorso-basally and prolonged near the filament insertion into a deflexed caudiform appendage 0.5 mm long. Ovary 1/2-inferior, 6-locular, glabrous and elevated at the apex into a lobulate collar 1 mm high that surrounds the style base. Style glabrous, 5-7 mm long; stigma punctiform. Berry subglobose, 3-7 X 2.5-7 mm. Seeds 0.75-1 mm long, beige, cuneate to obovoid or narrowly pyriform, testa smooth.

description: Epiphytic shrub. Uppermost branchlets bluntly quadrate, becoming rounded with age. Young vegetative buds covered with an amorphous lanate indument. Mature leaves of a pair equal to slightly unequal in size, glabrous on both surfaces but glandular-punctate abaxially; petioles 0.5-1.2 cm long; blades coriaceous, 4.1-7.5 X 1.7-3 cm, elliptic-obovate to obovate, apex bluntly cuspidate, base acuminate, margin entire, 3-5-plinerved, the marginal pair of prima- ries inconspicuous and concealed by the revolute margins when dry, the transverse secondary veins spaced 0.5-1 mm apart at the widest portion of the blade. Flowers erect, solitary in leaf axils of uppermost branches; peduncles 1.2-2 cm long. Floral bracts green flushed with red, entire and glabrous throughout; outer bracts 1.6-2.1 X 1-1.6 cm, free but conspicuously decurrent on, and imparting a winged aspect to the peduncle, elliptic to elliptic-obovate, apex bluntly cuspidate to bluntly acute; inner bracts 1.1-1.5 X 0.3-0.6 cm, free, linear-oblong to narrowly obovate and distinctly concave, apex bluntly acute to obtuse. Hypanthium (at anthesis) cylindric-campanulate and somewhat fluted when dry, 0.6 cm long to the torus and 0.7 cm diam., glabrous. Calyx tube 2 mm long; free portions of calyx lobes 0.5-1 mm long and 3-4 mm wide basally between sinuses, broadly depressed-triangular, margin entire, callose-thickened at the median apex abaxially, glabrous throughout. Petals 6, glabrous, 2.1- 2.7 X 1.2-1.5 cm, reportedly white-pink, thin and translucent when dry, obovate, apically rounded, entire. Stamens 12, isomorphic, filaments 5-6 mm long, declinate, complanate, glabrous; anthers laterally connate for most of their length, 3-5 X 1 mm, yellow, linear-oblong with each anther sac opening by a separate dorsally inclined terminal pore; connective thickened dorsally and dilated dorso-basally into an upturned or deflexed, somewhat flattened, blunt ap- pendage ca. 0.5 X 0.25 mm. Ovary com- pletely inferior, 6-locular, glabrous at the apex, which is elevated into a blunt cone 1- 3 mm high. Style and stigma not seen. Berry subglobose, 0.6-0.7 X 0.7 cm. Seeds mostly 1 mm long, beige, cuneate-clavate, testa smooth.

description: Semi-woody vine. Stems subterete, furrowed, pubescent (hairs whitish, 0.2-0.5 mm long), becoming nearly glabrous with age; cross section of stem with a central, large, obtusely triangular to asymmetric stele, and 3-5 peripheral, terete to elliptic-flattened steles of different sizes (but smaller than the central stele). Stipules triangular, ca. 1 mm long, glabrous, stramineous. Leaves pinnately 5-foliolate; petioles pubescent, 1.1-1.7 cm long, obscurely canaliculate adaxially; rachis pubescent, shorter than the petiole, bicarinate along adaxial surface; leaflets 1.8-4.2 X 0.7-2.4 cm, discolorous, chartaceous, adaxially puberulent, abaxially pubescent especially along veins, the apex obtuse and usually retuse but the main vein ending on a gland-like structure or less often mucronate, the margins re- motely crenate-serrate, cartilaginous and with a notably lighter color than the blade, the veins mixed craspedodromous; terminal leaflet ovate to elliptic, with long-attenuate base; lateral leaflets oblong to elliptic, with obtuse or round, usually asymmetric base. Thyrses axillary, simple, pubescent, longer than subtending leaf; axis nearly terete to 4-angled, 1.7-4.2 cm long; rachis nearly 3- angular in cross section, 2.3-10 cm long; bracts deltate, ciliate, 1.2-2.5 mm long; bracteoles similar to the bracts but smaller; cincinni alternate, (3-)7-9-flowered, 0.5- 1.5 cm long; pedicels articulated ca. 1.5 mm from base. Flowers secund; outer sepals 3-3.2 X 2-2.2 mm, ovate, concave, glabrous with ciliate margins; inner sepals 3.5-4.5 X 2.2-2.4 mm, lanate abaxially, oblong, nearly concave, the third and fifth sepals free; petals white, 5-5.7 mm long, obovate to spatulate, sparsely papillose adaxially, appressed-puberulent abaxially, the apex rounded, usually emarginate and crenate; appendages of central petals ca. 3.7 mm long, hood-shaped, the apex fleshy, bi- fid, yellow; appendage of lateral petals ca. 2.2 mm long, asymmetric; nectary disk 4- glandular, the glands triangular in outline; torus slightly enlarged, glabrous; filaments nearly terete, pilose, 6-8 mm long, the anthers ellipsoid, ca. 1 mm long; pistillode ca. 1.5 mm long, pubescent, trigonous, with ellipsoid outline. Fruits yellowish green, ovate-triangular in outline, cordate at base; mericarps 20-21 X 7-8 mm; cocci nearly globose, chartaceous, with prominent veins; partitioning walls ca. 1 mm wide; endocarp glabrous; wing not constricted below coccus. Seeds lenticular-globose, ca. 4 X 3.5 mm, light brown; hilar scar trigonous, whitish, 1-1.2 mm wide; adaxial cotyledon transversely biplicate, the abaxial cotyledon curved.

description: Caulescent, perennial herb, from a short rootstock usually tightly wedged in small cracks and bullet-hole-like crevices of rock, the stems, petioles, and pedicels densely clustered, often spreading to declining from the vertical face of rock, dried-up foliage of past years dangling beneath, plants without stolons; herbage glabrous; stems 1.5-6.7 cm long; leaves both basal and cauline; petiole 1.5-6 (14) cm long, the basal usually lon- gest; stipules lanceolate, fimbriate; leaf blade broadly ovate-cordate, deltate-cordate, 1.3- 2.9 (4.1) cm long and about as wide, the base sometimes truncate, the apex obtuse to rounded, crenate; peduncle (including the pedicel) 2.5-7 cm long, the longest ones in the lower axils, curved apically, the bractlets at about the middle; sepals lanceolate or narrowly lanceolate, 4-5.7 (6.5) mm long, short-auriculate basally, acute apically; petals pale purple in front, the lateral and posterior pairs violet on back, the median-an- terior petal purple-lined at base, the lateral pair each with a white-bearded patch inside at about the proximal 1/3, the spur petal 10-16 (18) mm long, the spur well developed, 1.6-2.3 (3) mm long, rounded, greenish to pale lime-green; stamens with minute filaments, the anther thecae about 2.5 mm long, the anterior appendages 1.6-2 mm long, the posterior appendages on the ventral stamens (spur appendages or nectaries) well developed, extending into the petal spur; style about 3 mm long, the style head sparsely bearded on the sides of the tip or subglabrous; capsule 3-7 mm long, the valves mucronate tipped; seeds 2.4-2.8 mm long, pale yellow, narrowly ovoid, the caruncle well developed, off-white.

description: Terrestrial shrub 0.5-1 m tall, without lignotuber; stems terete, striate, glabrous; twigs subterete, bluntly and broadly complanate, puberulent to densely short-pilose, glabrate; bark cracking but seemingly not exfoliating; bud scales 2, lanceolate, longacuminate, 5-6 mm long. Leaves coriaceous, imbricate, obovate to more typically oblong-elliptic, 2.5-4.7 X 1.2-1.8(-2.3) cm, basally rounded, apically acute or rounded but with a 1-2 mm long apiculus, marginally indistinctly and minutely serrulate, the margin a lighter color and seemingly a bit thinner than lamina proper, essentially glabrous above except finely whitish, appressed-pilosulous near the base along midrib and inconspicuously ciliate especially proximally, indistinctly and sparingly whitish, appressed-pilosulous beneath basally and also bearing appressed, reddish brown, glandular fimbriae ±0.2 mm long, also provided with 1-2 reddish, circular basal glands, pinnately nerved with 3-4 arcually ascending lateral nerves per side, the midrib slightly thickened and raised proximally but impressed distally, lateral nerves impressed above, all nerves prominent and raised beneath and of a lighter color than lamina proper; petiole thick, rugose, 2-3 mm long, flattened or broadly canaliculate above and slightly winged throughout, moderately puberulous to short-pilose. Inflorescence axillary, sessile, racemose, 10-15-flowered; rachis strongly and sharply angled, 1-2(-4) cm long, pilose with soft, short, white hairs; floral bract appressed, linear to lanceolate, 3-4 mm long, puberulent; pedicel 6-10 mm long, softly pilosulous or puberulous, bearing around apical border a series of glandular fimbriae; bracteoles basal, appressed, linear to narrowly lanceolate, 2-3 mm long, puberulent, marginally glandular-fimbriate, without dorsal glands. Flowers with calyx articulate with pedicel, 4.5-5 mm long; hypanthium campanulate to cylindric, ±2.5-3 mm long and in diam., longer than limb, moderately puberulous with whitish trichomes ±0.1-0.2 mm long; limb slightly flaring, 2-2.8 mm long; lobes triangular, acute, 1.2-1.8 mm long, puberulous externally and internally; sinuses broadly rounded; corolla terete, cylindric, 8-13 X 4-6 mm, appressed- to spreading-puberulous without with moderately abundant hyaline trichomes ±0.4 mm long and moderately to densely pilose with hyaline trichomes within, the lobes strongly reflexed, triangular, 1.5-2 mm long, densely pilosulous both externally and internally, essentially concolorous with the tube pink to red although the lobes sometimes becoming pale pink to whitish; stamens alternately 7 mm and 7.5 mm long; filaments distinct, alternately 3.5 and 4 mm long, glabrous proximally but marginally with appressedpilosulous hyaline trichomes distally; connectives smooth and thin; anthers 4.5-5 mm long; thecae smooth, not coarsely granular, 1.8-2 mm long, basally strongly incurved; tubules 2, separate to the base, 2.5-2.7 mm long, dehiscing by oblique pores ±0.6 mm long; style exserted. Berry spherical, 8-10 mm diam., short-pilose, blue-black.
bibliographicCitation: Luteyn, James L. 2001. Two new species and two new combinations in mesoamerican Ericaceae. Brittonia. 53: 437-446.

description:
Macroscopic: petioles about 3 mm. long; blades elliptic-lanceolate to ovate, 5-15 cm. long, 3.5-8 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, aeute to short-acuminate at apex, shining on both surfaces, drying a dull olive-ocher yellow, coriaceous, 3-plinerved (the basal-marginal nerves sometimes prominent) with the inner pair subopposite or alternate and diverging at 5-10 mm. from base, reticulation intricate and prominent on both surfaces.

Microscopic: petioles puberulent with short adpressed hairs even in age; blades beneath with inconspicuous atomic dots and essentially glabrous (scattered, very short hairs present) but conspicuously fulvous hirtellousbarbate in axils of the inner principal nerves, above sparsely puberulent on midrib near base, otherwise glabrous and smooth. Infloreseences and flowers essentially as in S. Gardneri except that both the tube and lobes of corolla without (mostly toward apex of former and toward base of latter) are not merely densely einereous-papillose but also pubeseent with spreading pale soft hairs. Fruits not seen.

description: Macroscopic: petioles 1-3 mm. long; blades ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1-3.5 cm. long, 0.4-1.8 cm. broad, rounded to obtuse at base, somewhat narrowed to a blunt and mucronulate apex, dull on both surfaces, membranaceous to subeoriaceous, 3-plinerved (principal nerves not prominent beneath) with the inner pair opposite or alternate and diverging at 0.5-3 mm. from base, reticulation obscure on both surfaces. Microscopic: branchlets and petioles densely grey-puberulent with erect or ascending, straight or slightly curved hairs; blades beneath puberulent on midrib and often on margins, becoming sparsely so in age, often barbate with soft pale hairs in axils of the inner principal nerves where a membranaceous pocket is also frequently found, above sometimes puberulent on midrib, otherwise glabrous. Infloreseences in paniculate eymes, corymbose to hemispheric and fewflowered, usually less than 10 mm. long and about as broad, grey-puberulent with erect hairs, bracts ovate to lanceolate, ciliate, otherwise glabrous, peduncles (0-) 5 (-10) mm. long and 0.5 mm. wide, the lateral infloreseencebranches usually distinct, pedicels short but usually distinct, up to 2 mm. long, more or less puberulent; calyx-lobes ovate to ovate-lanceolate, often unequal in length, about 1 mm. long, acute at apex, glabrous (or glabreseent) without, sparsely ciliate; corolla-lobes glabrous and apparently not papillose without, with sparse pili near middle within along an upwardly convex are, above this line of barbation papillose and glabrous, below neither pilose nor papillose; anthers very sparsely barbate or glabrous; ovary and style glabrous. Mature fruits globose, up to 1.8 cm. in diam., shell less than 0.5 mm. thick, orange-yellow, shining, thickly but lightly tuberculate, seed 1, globose or slightly flattened, about 6 mm. in diam., stony and somewhat translucent; fruit-pedicels about 2 mm. in dialn.
bibliographicCitation: Krukoff, Boris A. & Monachino, Joseph V. 1942. The American species of Strychnos. Brittonia. 4: 248-322.

description: Plants slender, 4.5-10 dm high, the foliage glabrous, the inflorescence scaberulous, from a tuberous base; leaves cylindrical, hollow, undivided except near apex, the short blade ovate, in the basal leaves 5-10 cm long, 1-3-ternate, the divisions linear, rigid, quadrangular, abruptly acute, 0.5-5 cm long, entire, the petioles elongate, cylindrical, 10-30 cm long, narrowly sheathing at base, the cauline leaves reduced upward, the uppermost consisting of a dilated sheath and usually a ternate, sessile blade; inflorescence of a terminal and occasionally one or more axillary peduncles, the terminal peduncle 6-10 cm long, scaberulous at apex; involucre of 5-8 linear, acuminate bracts 1-2 cm long, slightly connate at base; fertile rays 8-16, spreading- ascending, unequal, 1.5-3 cm long, scaberulous; involucel of 5-8 bractlets like the bracts, 3-8 mm long, longer than the flowers but mostly shorter than the fruiting pedicels; fertile pedicels 2-8, 4-8 mm long, spreading-ascending; flowers white; petals oblong-oval, ca 1.5 mm long, with a colored midvein, acute; stamens up to 3 mm long, the anthers oval, ca 0.8 mm long; stylopodium low conical, the styles slender, 1.5-2 mm long, spreading or ascending; fruit ovate, rounded at apex, retuse at base, 6-8 mm long, 3.5-5 mm broad, the dorsal ribs prominent, acute, the lateral broadly thin-winged; seed face slightly concave.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1967. Some Umbelliferae of the Andean Paramos of South America. Brittonia. 19: 212-226.

description: Plants stout, 5-9 dm high, glabrous, from a tuberous base; leaves reduced to cylindrical, hollow, septate phyllodes, the basal 2-3.6 dm long, ca 1 cm in diameter, sheathing at base, the sheaths very narrowly scarious-margined, the cauline leaves reduced upward, the uppermost consisting mostly of a dilated sheath; inflorescence of a terminal and often 1-3 axillary peduncles, the terminal peduncle 6-12 cm long; involucre of 5-8 linear, acuminate bracts 1.5-3 cm long, slightly connate at base; fertile rays 19-23, spreading-ascending, unequal, 2.5-4 cm long; involucel of 5-8 bractlets like the bracts, up to 15 mm long, usually exceeding the pedicels; fertile pedicels 3-8, 5-10 mm long, spreading-ascending; flowers ["yellowish-greenish- white"] greenish-white; petals oblong-oval, ca 2 mm long, with a colored midvein, acute; stamens up to 3 mm long, the anthers oval, ca 0.8 mm long; stylopodium lacking, the styles slender, 2-3 mm long, ascending; fruit ovate, truncate at apex, slightly retuse at base, 8-10 mm long, 4-5 mm broad, the dorsal ribs thick, prominent, the lateral thick-winged, the wing much narrower than the body; seed slightly channeled under the vittae, the face slightly concave.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1967. Some Umbelliferae of the Andean Paramos of South America. Brittonia. 19: 212-226.

description: Erect shrubs 3 m tall, the stems coarsely pubescent, the hairs stellate, ferruginous, 0.5-1 mm long. Leaf blades narrowly ovate, to 14 X 6 cm (greatly reduced and narrowed upward to almost bract-like structures 1.5 cm X 2 mm, in the terminal inflorescence), the leaf base slightly cordate (on larger leaves) to more or less truncate or rounded, serrate (the lowermost teeth glandular), acuminate, prominently discolorous, the upper surface green, sparsely pubescent to glabrescent, the lower surface matted-pubescent with interlacing stellate hairs, whitish to markedly ferruginous; petioles coarsely pubescent like stem, 1.5-4.5 cm (shorter upward); stipules inconspicuous, subulate, ca. 3 mm. Inflorescence a narrow terminal panicle of axillary (usually 3-flowered) cymes; peduncles 3-5 mm; pedicels ca. 5 mm, sparsely and minutely pubescent; calyx of 5 deciduous sepals, at anthesis 12-17 mm, minutely and sparsely pubescent, the appendages obsolete; petals yellow, narrowly spatulate, to 16 X 2-3 mm; stamens ca. 15, 12-13 mm; style longer than the stamens, slender, pallid; gonophore with 5 oblong glands. Fruit body spherical, 5-6 mm diam., whitish-pubescent; spines of the fruit ca. 50, stout (0.5-0.8 mm diam. at base), 2-3 mm long, prominently plumose (the hairs 0.5 mm, whitish, somewhat retrorse), with a straight or curved (rarely uncinate) spinelet at tip.

description: Liana, the braniehlets usually cinereous, inconispicuously lenticel- late; petioles 5-10 mm. long, the leaf-blades chartaceo-ts or thin-coria- ceous, elliptic, 5-8 cm. long, 2.5-3.8 cm. broad, obtuse or acute at base, obtuse or obtusely short-cuspidate at apex, entire or inconispicuously crenate at marginis (crenations 1 or 2 per centimeter), the costa slightly raised above, subprominent beneath, the secondary nerves 4-7 per side, erecto-patent, prominulous oni both surfaces; infloreseences 1.5-7 cm. long, usually paniculate-corymbose, 3-5-times bralched, the pedunele slender, terete, up to 3 cm. long, usually continued inito an obvious rachis, occasionally dichotomously branched at apex, the branehes opposite and paired at 2-4 nodes along the rachis or divaricate, the bracts oblong, subacute, about 1.5 mm. long; flowers 2.8-4 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels slender, about 1 mm. long; sepals submembranous, ovate to oblong, 0.5-0.9 mm. long and broad, erosulous or ciliolate at margins, faintly nerved; petals subLbmenbranous or thin- carnose, elliptic-oblong, 1.5-2 mm. long, 0.8-1.1 mm. broad, subentire or distally minutely erosulous at margins, sometimes faintly glandular- lineolate proximally; disk about 0.8 mm. in diameter, 0.1-0.2 nmi. thick; stamens suberect, the filaments ligulate, 0.4-0.6 mm. long, gradually broadened toward base, the anthers about 0.2 by 0.4 mm.; ovary 0.6-0.8 nmni. in diameter at anthesis, the style 0.2-0.3 mm. long; ovules 6 per locule.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, A. C. 1940. Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3 (3): 356-367.

description: Liana, the branchlets slender, cinereous, tuberculate-lenticellate; leaves opposite, the petioles ofteni glaucous, 3-4 mm. long, the leafblades coriaceous, greenish above and glaucous beneath when dried, oblong or ovate-oblong, 3.5-6 cm. long, 2-3.5 cm. broad, rounded or faintly cordate at base, rounded or emarginate at apex, entire and slightly thickened at margins, the costa faintly elevated above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 5-7 per side, spreading, immersed, sometimes slightly raised beneath; infloreseence axillary, crowdedracemose (pseudo-fasciculate, the peduncle stout, 2-4 mm. long), few-flowered, the bracts numerous, papyraceous, ovate, less than 1 mm. long; flowers 7.5-9 mm. in diameter at anthesis, the pedicels glaucous, 4-5 mm. long; sepals broadly imbricate, papyraceous, conspicuously glandular-variegated, broadly ovate, 1.3-1.7 mm. long, 2-3 mm. broad, rounded at apex, scariose and faintly erosulous or deciduously sessile-glandular at margins; petals thin-carnose, glanidular as sepals, obovate-oblong to orbicular, 3.5-4.5 mm. long, 2.8-4.5 mm. broad, seariose and entire at margins; disk pentagonons, 3-3.5 mm. in diamieter, uniformly thick (0.5-0.7 mm.), flattened on upper surface, projecting beyond petal-bases; stamens 3 (rarely 4), spreading, the filaments sparsely glandular, about 1 mm. long, the anthers transversely ellipsoid, about 0.3 by 0.6 mm., dehiscing by horizontal apical confluent clefts; ovary gradually tapering to a short (0.5-0.7 mm. long) style; ovules 6 per locule, 2-ranked.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Strangler epiphytes, becoming trees to 35- 40 m, with buttressed trunks to 2.2 m DBH; trunk and branches with long, conical spines. Leaves 5-6-foliolate, petioles 90-150 mm, leaflets 90-110 x 35-44 mm, oblanceolate, acute at apex, decurrent-cuneate at base, glabrous on adaxial surface, densely tomentose on abaxial surface with golden-brown stellate trichomes; borne on petiolules 3-5 mm long. Flowers borne singly near stout branch tips. Pedicels to ca. 10 mm, robust. Calyx 15-21 mm long, usually cupuliform, finely tomentose-tuberculate externally, sericeous within, apex sinuous to shallowly lobed. Petals 75-85 x 17-19 mm, narrowly lanceolate, obtuse, finely and densely stellate-tomentose. Staminal tube clearly articulated, 45 mm long, lower tube 35 mm long, ca. 10 mm diam, densely grey-sericeous, apical filamentous lobes 18-25 mm long. Fruits pendulous subcylindric capsules (8-)13-18 x ca. 4 cm.

description: Trees 7 m tall (in single known collection). Leaves grouped at tips of short branches, 5-6 foliolate, petioles 70-80 mm, leaflets 40-45 × 18-22 mm, narrowly obovate, subbobtuse or apiculate at apex, cuneate at base, glabrous on adaxial surface, papillate with inconspicuous red glands on abaxial surface, borne on petiolules 2.5-3 mm long. Flowers borne singly at apex of short branches. Pedicels not seen. Calyx 15-17 mm long, ca. 2 cm wide, obconic, minutely tomentose externally, sericeous within, the apex with 6-8 shallow, rounded lobes. Petals 75-85 mm, narrowly linear-lanceolate, covered externally by a dense indument of fine stellate hairs and internally by scattered stellate hairs. Staminal tube without articulation, 45-47 mm long, densely and finely stellate-tomentose, with filamentous apical lobes 25-28 mm long, each bearing sinuose thecae 15-18 mm long. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Gibbs, P. E. & Alverson, William S. 2006. How many species of Spirotheca (Malvaceae s.l., Bombacoideae)?. Brittonia. 58 (3): 245-258.

description: Shrubs +/-  1 m with stiff virgate branches, the young stems densely strigulose with appressed-incurved, sordid hairs less than 0.2 mm but the stiffly chartaceous lustrous leafblades glabrous, the simple or few-branched, spiciform staminate inflorescences axillary and terminal, each spike borne on a short, efoliate but bracteate branchlet. Petioles (8)10-18 mm, shallow-sulcate ventrally, a trifle swollen but not pulvinate at base, unmodified at apex; blades ovate from broadly flabellate base, depressed-deltate-apiculate at tip, the larger ones 4-6.5 x 2-4.5 cm, all 5-plinerved, the outer primary nerves submarginal, the inner pair incurved-ascending through 2/3 - 3/4 the blade's length, the stout midrib giving rise on each side, beyond mid - blade, to 1(2) major incurved secondary nerves and pinnately branched its whole length, the tertiary and reticular venules all sharply prominulous on each face. Flowering branchlets of staminate plant together with the spike-axis 2-3.5 cm; bracts preceding the flowers linear thick-textured +/- 3 mm, those subtending individual flowers subulate 1-1.5 mm; perianth 15-merous, silky-strigulose externally with partly rusty hairs, the outermost sepals +/- 0.7 mm, the narrowly ovate ones of the third cycle +/-2 mm, the 6 petaloid innermost ones a trifle shorter, glabrescent marginally; androecium 6-merous, the stamens all free to base but dimorphic, the filaments of the outer cycle 1.9 mm, abruptly dilated at apex, the terminal transverse anthers looking upward, the filaments of the inner cycle +/- half as long, their anthers rudimentary. Pistillate plant unknown.

description: Shrub to ca. 3 m tall. Indumentum of multicellular, ferrugineous, irregularly stellate-branched hairs, minute globular hairs, and long-stalked, gland-headed hairs to 1.5 mm long (sometimes on leaves to 3 mm long on teeth). Young twigs not ridged, +/- rectangular or square to elliptic in cross section, 1. 5-4.5 mm wide, the indumentum of dense to sparse, stellate-branched to elongate and irregularly branched hairs and usually very sparse to sparse long-stalked, gland-headed hairs, eventually glabrescent; internodes 0.7-10 cm long. Leaves with petiole 0.6-6.3 cm long, the indumentum dense to moderate, ferrugineous, stellate-branched, with a few long-stalked, gland-headed hairs; blade ovate to elliptic or oblong, 2.5-20 x 1.2-9 cm, flat, coriaceous, the apex (acute to) acuminate, the base (acute) obtuse to rounded, the margin plane to very slightly revolute, serrulate to base or nearly so, 0- 20% of margin entire, the largest teeth 0. 1 5- 0.6 mm long, sometimes with long-stalked hairs with or without gland-heads along margin at apex of teeth, these sometimes deciduous; venation acrodromous, slightly suprabasal, with prominent midvein and 4 secondary veins, with 2 conspicuous secondary veins placed 2-13 mm from margin, with 2 inconspicuous secondary veins closer to margin, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented subperpendicular to mid- vein, the tertiary veins joined by percurrent- orthogonal quatemary veins; adaxial surface nearly glabrous or with indumentum of sparse stellate-branched hairs, especially on major veins, sometimes also with a few minute globular hairs, very soon glabrescent, rarely also with a few scattered, long- stalked, gland-headed hairs, the midvein and major secondary veins impressed, the minor secondary veins and tertiary veins slightly impressed to flat, the higher order veins +/- flat, the surface appearing +/-  minutely papillose after drying due to presence of numerous druse crystals; abaxial surface sparsely to densely covered with stellate branched hairs to 0.2-0.5 mm across (and rarely also a few long-stalked, gland-headed hairs) on midvein and major secondary veins, such hairs very sparse to moderate on minor secondary veins, tertiary veins, and sometimes quatemary veins, the hairs persistent, at least on major veins, but sometimes only on the sides of the veins, the highest order veins sometimes with minute globular hairs, the midvein and major secondary veins prominently raised, mi- nor secondary veins and tertiary veins slightly raised to flat, the higher order veins +/- flat. Inflorescences open-paniculate to round-topped cymes, 1.8-9 cm long, 2-6.5 cm across, of 1 to 4 branch-pairs; proximal segment of lowermost inflorescence branch- es 1-2.7 cm long, the distal internodes shorter, the ultimate branches 1-15 mm long, with sparse to dense, stellate-branched hairs, with very sparse to moderate long- stalked, gland-headed hairs; peduncle 1.3- 7 cm, with similar indumentum; each inflorescence branch associated with an early caducous, narrowly oblong-linear, elliptic, or obovate bract 2.5-20 x 0.5-3 mm, the apex acute to acuminate, the lowermost pair sometimes expanded and leaf-like; flowers in dichasia, each subtended by 2 caducous, narrowly elliptic or obovate to linear brac- teoles 1-5 x 0.4-1.2 mm, the apices acute to acuminate. Flowers with pedicel 0-1.5 mm long. Hypanthium cylindrical, the free portion 1-1.7 mm long, the outer surface with sparse to moderate, stellate-branched hairs, these sometimes intergrading with minute globular hairs, sometimes with sparse to moderate long-stalked, glandheaded hairs, although these may be limited to calyx or completely lacking, the inner surface glabrous and clearly to only obscurely ridged, the apices of the ridges not or only slightly projecting, to 0.05-0.1 mm. External calyx teeth (or lobes) 5, 0.3-1.3 x 0.8- 1.6 mm, broadly to narrowly triangular, with acute to acuminate apex, the indumentum of very sparse to sparse stellate-branched hairs, and usually a few long-stalked, gland- headed hairs; internal calyx lobes 5, 0.4-1.6 x 1.2-2.1 mm, broadly triangular to triangular, reddish, often +/- glabrous, or with very sparse stellate-branched hairs, these sometimes intergrading with minute globular hairs, the apex rounded to acute, the margin entire (rarely with a few marginal hairs); calyx tube 0.2-0.5 mm long. Petals 5, broadly ovate to elliptic or orbicular, 3- 4.5 x 2-3.5 mm, glabrous, white, but some- times red tinged on outside, imbricate and apically interlocking in bud, the apex rounded, with an asymmetrically located notch. Stamens 10, geniculate; proximal segment (filament) 1.6-2.2 mm long; distal segment (anther and connective) 2.2-2.8 mm long, with minute dorsal projection, the anther 1.4-2.2 mm long, with fertile portion of anther sacs 1-1.6 mm long, opening by 2 longitudinal slit-like pores, the connective extended 0.6-0.9 mm beyond the base of the anther sacs. Ovary 3-5-locular (N = 10, 12, 14), 3/4-inferior when immature, to 3/4- 4/5-inferior when mature, short-ovoid to subglobose, 1.4-2.5 x 1.6-3.5 mm, glabrous and obscurely to clearly ridged, with fluted apical projection to 0.4-0.6 mm encircling the base of style; style 2.5-4.4 mm long. Berries globose, 5-7 x 5-7 mm, blue, but red when slightly immature, with sparse to moderate, stellate-branched hairs and sometimes very sparse to moderate, long- stalked, gland-headed hairs. Seeds angular obovoid, 0.6-0.8 mm long.

description: Annual or more probably weak perennial herb, 15-50 cm tall, becoming decumbent at the base; stems glabrous below, thinly pilose in the inflorescence and near the nodes; leaves mostly in fours below, finally alternate above, broadly ovate or elliptic, 6-13 mm long, 3.3-8.3 mm wide, glabrous or sparsely hairy above, sessile or narrowed to a very short petiole, obtuse to subacute, apiculate, the lower entire, the upper and the floral bracts toothed with stalked glands; stipular glands present except at the bases of the upper floral bracts; inflorescence paniculate with spreading branches; pedicels villous, the longer 3-6 mm long; sepals 2.4-3 mm long, lanceolate, sometimes rather narrowly so, acute to subacuminate, the inner broader, all appressed short hairy on the inner surface, conspicuously glandular-toothed; petals pale yellow, 4-6 mm long, obovate, glabrous; stamens 3-4 mm long; staminodia slenderly deltoid; anthers very narrowly elliptic, 0.7-1.2 mm long; styles separate, 2.5-4.3 mm long; fruit broadly ovate, thin-walled and easily crushed, usually sparsely hispidulous above the middle, 1.3-1.7 mm high, about 2 mm in diameter; false septa poorly developed; margins of septa without cilia; seeds brown, broadly ovate, ca. 0.8-0.9 mm long, 0.7-0.8 mm wide.

description: Arbores vel frutices 1-5(-8) m usque. Petiolus 1.3- 6.8 mm longus; laminae foliorum ellipticae vel angustate ellipticae, 1.5-5(-5.6) X 0.9-1.8(-2.1) cm, glabra, margine saltem per distales duas tertias partes serrata. Flores amentacei, dioeci. Bracteae secundariae florum d nullae vel unica, lineares vel fasciarae. Bracteae secundariae florum [female] 2-3(-4). Fructus saepe glaber. description: Trees or shrubs 1-5(-8) m tall. Young twigs more or less flattened, sometimes sulcate, glabrous or pubescent, with minute peltate glands. Old branchlets glabrous, with fewer glands, with conspicuous lenticels 0.2-1 mm long. Leaves evergreen; petioles 1.3-6.8 mm long, 0.7-1 mm thick, sulcate and pubescent adaxially, less pubescent abaxially, with glands on both sides. Blade 1.5-5(-5.6) X 0.9-1.8(-2.1) cm, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, glabrous except for veins, with several glands above (that fall off when the leaves become old) and below, coriaceous or subcoriaceous, acute or subacute at the apex, acute at the base, the margin serrate or serrate-dentate, at least in the distal 2/3, with some short pubescence in or between the teeth, the venation brachidodromous, the secondary veins 6-12 on each side, usually impressed above and beneath, puberulent on the midvein above, less so abaxially, sparsely puberulent on the midvein and secondary veins beneath. Dioecious; staminate inflorescence axillary, 0.8-1.5(-1.8) cm long, the rachis flattened, densely to sparsely pubescent, with glands, flowers 10 to numerous. Staminate flowers with only one main bract (seldom with one secondary bract), rhomboid, 1.1-1.7 X 1.3-2 mm, with glands abaxially and sparsely pubescent in apex and margins, glabrous or with sparse pubescence abaxially; secondary bracts (when present) linear or band-shaped, 0.6- 0.8 mm long, sparsely pubescent at apex; staminal column square or rectangular, gla- brous, 0.2-0.4 mm long and equally broad; stamens 1.3-1.8 mm long; filaments 0.5- 1.1 mm long; anthers 0.8-0.9 mm long; pis- tillate inflorescence axillary, (0.9-)1.4-4(- 4.4) cm long, the rachis flattened or terete, densely to sparsely pubescent, glabrate, with glands, flowers 10 to numerous (depending on length of catkin rachis), 2.9-6.7 mm apart. Pistillate flowers with one main bract and 2-3 (-4) secondary bracts, the main bract rhomboid or lanceolate, 0.7- 2.6(-4.4) X 0.5-1.2 mm, with abaxial glands and pubescence on apex and margins, abaxial surface glabrous or sparsely pubescent, the secondary bracts rhomboid, 0.4-0.7 X 0.3-0.7 mm, pubescent in the apex, sometimes on the margins. Pistil 0.3- 0.7 mm long, glabrous, sometimes with glands, with a light white zone near the stigma base; stigma branches 2 (sometimes 3), 0.6-1.1 mm long, glabrous, without glands. Fruit globose, 0.2-0.5 cm diam., glabrous, with warty protuberances ca. 0.2- 0.7 mm long which are glabrous and have glands. Seed cavity 1.8-3.1 mm long.

description: Shrubs or small trees 2-8 m tall; stems densely stellate pubescent with light yellowish-brown hairs, becoming dark, grayish-black and glabrate. Leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 4-18 cm long, 3.7-14.5 cm wide, base oblique, truncate, cordate, or rounded, apex acute to acuminate, margins irregularly crenate or serrate; densely stellate pubescent throughout, becoming sparingly stellate pubes- cent to subglabrate in age; nervation palmately 5-7-nerved, the nerves sparingly stellate pubescent; petiole 1.2-5 cm long; stipules lanceolate, 2-6 mm long, stellate pubescent. Inflorescences 3-6-flowered; pedicels 4-15 (24) mm long, densely stellate pubescent and with gland-tipped hairs; bracts subtending pedicels lanceolate to nearly linear, 1.5-4 mm long, densely stellate pubescent and occasionally with gland-tipped hairs. Calyx in flower broadly campanulate, 7-15 mm long, densely stellate pubescent, with gland-tipped hairs, bright red, rose-pink, salmon-pink, brownish-yellow, or orange-red; lobes triangular, 1-5 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, apices acute or acuminate; calyx in fruit acutely pentagonal, globose, 2-4 cm long, sparingly stellate pubescent, with scattered gland-tipped hairs, bright brick-red, cherry-red, rose-pink, salmon-pink, brownish-yellow, or orange-red fading to brown or yellow, lobes broadly to narrowly triangular, 4-15 mm long, 4-10 mm wide, apices acute, acuminate or long acuminate. Petals included or slightly exserted, oblanceolate, obovate-oblong or spatulate, 6-14 mm long, 1-3 mm broad, with scattered stellate and gland-tipped hairs on both surfaces, pale brick-red, rose- purple, orange-red, or purple-pink with a yellow central band on each lobe. Lon- gistylous flowers: staminal column 5-6 mm long, glabrous; filaments 1-2 mm long; anthers 1.5-2 mm long; staminodes 0.1-1 mm long; ovary 1.5-1.7 mm long, 1-1.5 mm diam, stellate pubescent with scattered gland-tipped hairs; stipe 5-6 mm long; styles 4-6 mm long, with scattered simple and bifurcate or stellate hairs. Brevistylous flowers: staminal column 3-7.5 mm long; filaments 2-5 mm long; anthers 1.8-2.5 mm long; staminodes, when present, 0.2-2 mm long; ovary 1.5- 2 mm long; 1-1.5 mm broad, pubescence as with longistylous flowers; stipe 2-6 (8) mm long; styles 1-1.8 mm long, with simple and bifurcate hairs. Capsules slightly retuse at the apex, 4-8 mm tall, 4-8 mm diam, covered with stellate, gland-tipped, and simple hairs, subtended by a stipe 5-9 mm long; seeds ovate or trigonal, 1 or 2 per carpel, 2.5-4 mm long, 1.8-2.5 mm diam.

description: Liana. Stems subterete, minutely tomentulose; cross-section of stem with a single terete stele. Stipules minute, early deciduous. Leaves biternate; petiole not winged, 2.5-4.7 cm long, puberulent, adaxially canaliculate; rachis narrowly winged, puberulent, shorter than the petiole; leaflets elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 3-8 X 1.5-3 cm, chartaceous, the adaxial surface glabrous, the abaxial surface with minute tufts of hairs in secondary vein axils, rest of surface puberulent or glabrous, the base acuminate to obtuse, the margins bidentate below the lingulate apex; tertiary venation reticulate, inconspicuous. Thyrses axillary, racemiform, longer than subtending leaf, with a pair of watch spring-like tendrils, or inflorescences lacking tendrils and distally congested into a paniculate synflorescence; axis obtusely 4-angled, 5-8 cm long, minutely tomentulose; rachis obtusely angled, 8-11 cm long, minutely tomentulose; bracts deltate, tomentulose, ca. 4 mm long; bracteoles similar to the bracts but smaller; cincinni alternate or subopposite, 5-7-flowered, sessile; pedicels slightly flattened, articulated at the middle. Flowers unisexual; calyx tomentulose, of 4 sepals, outer sepals ca. 1.2 mm long, concave, rounded; inner sepals ca. 2.5 mm long, oblong, rounded at apex, concave; petals white, 2.2-2.5 mm long, obovate, sparsely papillose adaxially, glabrous abaxially, the apex rounded, usually emar- ginate and crenate; appendages ca. 2 mm long, the central ones bifid, yellow, the lateral ones asymmetric; nectary disk 4-glandular, the central glands discoid, ca. 0.8 mm across, the lateral ones much smaller, rounded; filaments slightly flattened, pilose, ca. 1.5 mm long, the anthers ellipsoid-lanceolate, ca. 0.5 mm long. Pollen foveolate, heteropolar, triporate, with triangular equatorial outline, 16.9-20.8 X 27.3-33.8 pm. Fruits and seeds unknown.
