description: Scandent monoecious herb, creeping and climbing by means of tendrils, the stems slender, branched, sulcate, glabrous to sparsely villous, mainly at the nodes. Leaves simple, thin and membranous, ovate-triangular, 5-angulate-lobed, the lobes wide, triangular, the central lobe longer than the lateral ones and strongly acuminate, the lateral lobes slightly acuminate to acute, 1.5-19.1 X 0.4.-15.3 cm, the margin minutely to strongly denticulate, both surfaces strigose, the abaxial surface with the veins more prominent and the trichomes shorter and more abundant; petioles 0.4-11.6 cm long, sulcate, glabrous to densely villous, mainly on the adaxial surface; tendrils longstalked, 0.6-8.6 cm long, striate, 2-3-branched, glabrous to sparsely villous. Staminate inflorescence in the same axil as the pistillate, racemose, 4.5-28.6 cm long, erect, peduncle 3.4-21.4 cm long; rachis sparsely to densely villous, mainly toward the apex, the pedicels slender, 4.0-23.0 mm long, commonly ascendant, occasionally reflexed, glabrous to densely villous. Staminate flower receptacle 5-merous, widely campanulate, 0.6-2.2 X 0.9-2.3 mm; calyx lobes filiform, 0.2-0.8 mm long; corolla greenish white, 5-merous, the lobes ovate- lanceolate, 1.0-4.3 X 0.6-2.0 mm, the margins and inner surface with glandular trichomes, yellow to dark brown or black at anthesis, the external surface glabrous to sparsely villous; stamens 2-3, fused in a column 1.8-4.3 mm long, the filaments forming a central column, the anthers united to the base with abundant connective tissue, the thecae curved, occasionally of different sizes although apparently all of them always fertile. Pistillate inflorescence umbelliform, the peduncle 0.3-3.3 cm long, extending to 7.6 cm in fruit, glabrous to sparsely villous. Pistillate flowers to 7, sub- sessile, rarely with a very short pedicel, 0.5-1.6 mm long, elongating to 4.9 mm in fruit, densely villous; ovary unilocular, ovate-triangular, with some verrucose antrorse projections mainly toward the base, glabrous to puberulent; ovule 1, occupying almost the entire locule; receptacle and perianth smaller than that of the staminate flowers; corolla with 4-5 petals; column of style and stigma 0.7-3.5 mm long; stigmas 3-lobed to rarely 4-lobed, the lobes widely linguiform, reflexed. Fruits 1-7 per inflorescence (commonly one or more not completely developed), dry, 0.2-0.8 cm long, 0.2-0.5 cm diam., triangular-ovoid, unarmed although conserving the verrucose antrorse projections at the base, glabrous, the fruit wall thin, strongly attached to the seed, light to dark brownish. Seed ovoid, compressed, dark brown.

description: Shrub to 2 m tall. Indumentum of multicellular, ferruginous, long-stalked, dendritic-branched hairs to 3.8 mm long, in- tergrading (on hypanthium) with stellate- branched hairs, minute globular-glandular hairs, and (on adaxial leaf surface) very thick-based, short-stalked (rarely long- stalked), eglandular hairs. Young twigs not ridged, square to rectangular in cross sec- tion, 5-8 mm diam., becoming +/- terete with age, the indumentum sparse to moderate; internodes 2-7.5(15) cm long; nodes with a few  prominent lenticels, but lacking U-shaped flanges. Leaves with petiole 1.2- 4.5 cm long, the indumentum sparse to moderate, the lamina ovate to elliptic, 8- 18.6(22.8) x 3.8-9.3(12.5) cm, flat, coriaceous, the apex acute to slightly acuminate, the base obtuse to slightly cordate, the mar gin plane to slightly revolute, serrulate to obscurely and irregularly serrate to base, the teeth to 0. 2-0.5 5 mm long, intergrading with a thick-based, eglandular hair, these +/- persistent and difficult to distinguish from tooth; venation acrodromous, +/- basal, with prom- inent midvein and 6 secondary veins (2 or 4 of these quite conspicuous), with 2 most conspicuous secondary veins placed 8-21 mm in from margin, 2 less conspicuous veins placed 2.5-8.5 mm in from margin, and 2 inconspicuous, +/- intramarginal veins, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented subperpendicular to midvein, the tertiary veins joined by several to numerous quaternary veins, and higher-order veins +/- or- thogonal-reticulate; adaxial surface green, the indumentum of moderate, thick-based, short-stalked (rarely long-stalked), eglandular (very rarely gland-headed) hairs, scattered minute globular hairs, and also a few long-stalked, dendritic hairs along basal portion of midvein (these initially scattered over surface but very quickly deciduous), the midvein through quaternary veins strongly impressed, quinary veins slightly impressed, and higher-order veins slightly impressed to fiat, thus delimiting raised areoles, especially toward margin, each containing 1 to few thick-based, usually short- stalked, eglandular hairs, i.e., bullate with lamina surface intergrading with thick-based hairs, the surface minutely papillose after drying due to presence of numerous druse crystals; abaxial surface light green, +/- moderately covered with long-stalked, dendrit- ic-branched hairs, these 0.4-1 mm long, 0.4- 0.8 mm wide, also scattered with minute- globular hairs, and all hairs +/- persistent, the midvein and major secondary veins prominently raised, minor secondary and tertiary veins moderately raised, quatemary veins slightly to moderately raised, quinary veins fiat to slightly raised. Inflorescences terminal, many-flowered, open paniculate cymes of 3-5 major branch-pairs, 4-13 cm long, 3-6.2 cm across; proximal segment of lowermost inflorescence branches 0.7-1.7 cm long, ultimate branches 2.4-6 mm long, with sparse hairs, these sometimes limited to the nodes, +/- glabrescent; peduncle 3.3- 9.4 cm long; each inflorescence branch associated with a tardily deciduous, ovate to obovate bract, 4-13.5(25) x 3-8(10) mm, reddish, bract apex acute or acuminate to rounded; flowers in dichasia, well-separated from each other, each subtended by 2 tardily deciduous, obovate to elliptic bracteoles, 3-14 x 1.5-8.5 mm, reddish, +/- glabrous, bracteole apex rounded. Flowers with pedicel 0.5-1 mm long. Hypanthium cylindrical, free portion 1.9-2.7 mm long, the outer surface with sparse dendritic to stellate-branched hairs and minute globular hairs, inner surface glabrous and clearly 20- ridged, with 10 strong ridges alternating with 10 weaker ones, the apices of the ridges clearly projecting, to 0.2-0.5 mm. External calyx lobes 5, 0.2-0.9 x 1.8-2.9 mm, broadly triangular, with apex acuminate (acute), indumentum of sparse minute globular hairs; internal calyx lobes 5, 1-2 x 2.3-3.3 mm, broadly ovate-triangular, green to reddish, glabrous, the apex rounded (obtuse), the margin +/- entire; calyx tube 0.3-0.4 mm long. Petals 5, broadly ovate to obovate, 4.9-6.2 x 3.8-5.2 mm, reflexed, glabrous, pink to red, imbricate and apically inter- locking in bud, the apex rounded, with an asymmetrically located notch; margin entire. Stamens 10, geniculate, glabrous; proximal segment 2-3 mm long; distal segment 3.9-4.5 mm long, essentially lacking dorsal projection or with a slight dorsal bump, the anther 2.6-3.3 mm long, with fertile portion of anther sacs 2.4-3.1 mm long, opening by 2 longitudinal slits, the connective extended 0.7-1.5 mm beyond the base of the anther. Ovary 5-loculate (N = 7), ca. 1/2-inferior, subglobose to ovoid or obovoid, 3.6-4.7 x 3.3-4.3 mm, apically glabrous and clearly ridged, with toothed apical projection to 0.5 mm encircling the base of style; style 2.8- 5.5 mm long, terete, glabrous; stigma truncate. Berries not seen but presumably fairly large, globose and pale blue at maturity.

description: Shrub or small tree to ca 8 m tall. Young twigs not ridged, +/- elliptic, 2.5-5 mm wide, sulcate, becoming terete with age, the indumentum dense, +/- glabrescent; internodes 0.8-4.5 (6) cm long. Leaves with petiole 0.3-2 cm long, the indumentum dense; blade ovate to elliptic or slightly obovate, 1.5-6 (6.7) x 1.1- 3.7 (4) cm, flat, coriaceous, the apex rounded (with small mucro) to acute (very shortly acuminate), the base (acute) obtuse to slightly cordate, the margin obscurely to clearly serrate-dentate, the largest teeth 0.3-1 mm long, becoming entire near base (ca 10-50% of margin without teeth), plane; venation acrodromous, very slightly suprabasal with prominent midvein and 4 secondary veins, with 2 conspicuous secondary veins placed 2-8 mm in from margin and 2 inconspicuous secondary veins closer to margin, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented subperpendicular to midvein, the tertiary veins joined by percurrent-orthogonal quatemary veins; adaxial surface dark green, the indumentum dense when young, glabrescent, the midvein and major secondary veins impressed, minor secondary, tertiary veins (and higher order veins) slightly impressed; abaxial surface ferru- gineous, very light golden to dark reddish-brown, densely covered with multi cellular, stellate hairs to ca 0.3 mm across, the midvein and major secondary veins prominently raised, minor secondary, and tertiary veins raised, quaternary and higher order veins slightly to not at all raised. Inflorescences terminal, many- flowered, open, paniculate cymes of usually 2 or 3 (or 4) major branch-pairs, ca 2-5.5 (7.5) cm long, 2.5-6.5 (7) cm across; lowermost inflorescence branches with basal segment 0.7-2.8 cm long, distal internodes increasingly shorter, all with dense pale to deeply ferrugineous indumentum; peduncle 1.5-3.5 cm long; the inflorescence branches associated with a caducous, narrowly ovate to oblong or linear, ca 1. 5-3 mm long (or possibly longer) bract; flowers in dichasia, each flower associated with a pair of caducous, +/- linear bracteoles, ca 1-1.7 x 0.3-0.6 mm, the indumentum dense, the apices acute to obtuse. Flowers with pedicel 0.5-1.5 mm long. Hypanthium +/- cylindrical, free portion ca 2-3 mm long, the outer surface with moderate to dense ferrugineous indumentum, the inner surface gla- brous and irregularly 10-ridged, the apices of the ridges forming lobes or small irregular projections ca 0.1-0.8 mm long. External calyx lobes 0.2-1.1 x 0.8-2.4 mm, broadly to narrowly triangular with acute to acuminate apex, dense ferru- gineous indumentum; internal calyx lobes ca 0.7-2.1 x 1.9-2.9 mm, broadly ovate, the apex rounded, the margin minutely erose, with sparse to dense ferrugineous indumentum on both surfaces; calyx tube 0.2-0.6 mm long. Petals broadly ovate to elliptic or obovate, 3.8-5 x 3.3-4.3 mm, white. Stamens geniculate; proximal segment (filament) 1.9-2.5 mm long; distal segment (anther and connective) 2.6-3.8 mm long, with minute dorsal projection, the anther ca 2.3-3 mm long, with fertile portion of anther sacs ca 2-2.7 mm long, the connective extending ca 0.5-1 mm beyond the base of anther sacs. Ovary 3-loculate, +/- inferior, ovoid, ca 2.8-3.5 x 2-3.3 mm, glabrous and +/- irregularly 10-ridged, with minute apical projections, to ca 0.5 mm long, encircling base of style; style 3-4 mm long; stigma truncate. Mature berries globose, ca 7-10 mm long and wide, blue (red when immature), moderately to sparsely covered with globular-stellate hairs. Seeds angular-obovoid, 0.7-1 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to ca 6 (8) m tall. Twigs +/- square, 4-8 mm wide, with 4 well developed ridges, becoming cylindric with age, the indumentum dense, glabrescent; internodes 1.2-8 (13) cm long. Leaves with petiole 0.5-3.5 cm long, the indumentum dense; blade ovate, elliptic or oblong 7.5-25.5 x 2.2-9 cm, flat, coriaceous, the apex usually acuminate, the base obtuse to acute (rounded), the margin obscurely serrate, the largest teeth 0.2-0.5 (0.6) mm long, becoming entire toward the base (ca 15-50% of margin without teeth), plane; venation acrodromous, basal to slightly suprabasal, with midvein and 4 secondary veins, 2 inner secondary veins conspicuous and ca 2-10 mm in from margin and 2 outer, + intramarginal, less conspicuous secondary veins, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented perpendicular to midvein and separated by composite intertertiary veins (less strongly developed in leaves of rapidly growing sucker-shoots); adaxial surface dark green, the indumentum dense when young, glabrescent, the midvein and major secondary veins prominently impressed, intramarginal secondary veins slightly impressed; abaxial surface pale-ferrugineous, densely (moderately) covered with multicellular, stellate hairs to ca 0.5 mm across, darker ferrugineous along veins, the midvein and major secondary veins prominently raised, minor secondary, and tertiary veins less conspicuously raised, higher order veins slightly to not at all raised. Inflorescences terminal, many-flowered, open, paniculate cymes of usually 4 or 5 (to 6) major branch-pairs, ca 5-15 cm long, 4-15 cm across; lowermost inflorescence branches with basal segment 1.6-4.5 cm long, distal internodes increasingly shorter, all with dense ferrugineous indumentum; peduncle 3-9 cm long; the inflorescence branches associated with a caducous, + linear to narrowly ovate, to ca 6 mm long bract; flowers in dichasia, each flower associated with a pair of caducous, narrowly elliptic to ovate or linear bracteoles, ca 1.5-3 x 0.5-1 mm, the indumentum dense, the apices acute to obtuse. Flowers with pedicel less than 1 mm long. Hypanthium +/- cylindrical, free portion ca 1.2- 2.3 mm long, the outer surface with moderate to dense indumentum, the inner surface glabrous and 10-ridged, the apices of ridges forming minute projections ca 0.1 mm long. External calyx lobes ca 0.5-0.8 x 1 mm, broadly triangular with acute to slightly acuminate apex, dense ferrugineous; internal calyx lobes ca 1.5- 2.7 x 1.7-3.2 mm, broadly ovate, the apex rounded, the margin minutely erose, with sparse to dense ferrugineous indumentum on both surfaces; calyx tube 0.1- 0.4 mm long. Petals broadly ovate to elliptic, 2.5-5.6 x 2.1-4.5 mm, white, occasionally with purple coloration around the margin or near the apices. Stamens geniculate; proximal segment (filament) 1.4-1.7 mm long; distal segment (anther and connective) 2.4-3.5 mm long, with minute dorsal projection, the anther ca 1.9-2.6 long, with fertile portion of anther sacs ca 1.5 mm long, the connective extending 0.7-1 mm beyond the base of anther sacs. Ovary 5-loculate, +/-  half inferior, short-ovoid, ca 1.8-3 x 2-4.3 mm, glabrous and strongly 1 0-ridged, with minute apical projections to ca 0.3 mm long encircling base of style; style 2.5- 3.5 mm long; stigma truncate. Mature berries globose, ca 7-10 mm long and wide, blue (red when immature), moderately to sparsely covered with globular-stellate hairs. Seeds angular-obovoid, 0.6-0.8 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to ca 2.5-5 m tall. Twigs +/- elliptic, 3-7 mm wide, not ridged or rarely with 2 very poorly developed ridges, becoming elliptic with age, the indumentum dense, glabrescent; internodes 1-8.5 cm long. Leaves with petiole 0.4-2.5 cm long, the indumentum dense; blade elliptic, slightly ovate to obovate, or nearly oblong, 4.3-20 x 1-5.5 cm, flat, coriaceous, the apex +/- acuminate (acute), the base acute to obtuse (rounded), the margin minutely serrate, with the teeth 0.1-0.4 (0.5) mm long, becoming entire toward the base (ca 20-60% of margin without teeth), plane; venation acrodromous, basal to slightly suprabasal, with midvein and 4 or occasionally only 2 secondary veins, 2 inner secondary veins conspicuous and ca 0.5-2 (3.5) mm in from margin, and 2 outer secondary veins very inconspicuous and occasionally lacking (or appearing as a thickened margin), and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented perpendicular to mid- vein, and usually separated by composite intertertiary veins, but sometimes with some tertiary veins connected by percurrent-orthogonal quaternary veins; adaxial surface dark green, the indumentum dense when young, quickly glabrescent, the midvein and major intramarginal secondary veins prominently impressed, minor secondary veins slightly impressed; abaxial surface deep red- to pale-ferrugineous, ? densely covered with multicellular, stellate hairs to ca 0.5 mm across, often darker ferrugineous along veins, the midvein and major intramarginal secondary veins prominently raised, minor secondary, and tertiary veins less conspicuously raised, higher order veins slightly to not at all raised. Inflorescences terminal, many-flowered, open, paniculate, cymes of usually 4-6 major branch-pairs, ca 5- 13 cm long, 4-1 1 cm across; lowermost inflorescence branches with basal segment 0.9-5.5 cm long, distal internodes increasingly shorter, all with dense ferrugineous indumentum; peduncle 1-11 cm long; the inflorescence branches associated with a caducous bract; flowers in dichasia, each flower associated with a pair of caducous, obovate or linear bracteoles, ca 2-6 x 1-2 mm, the indumentum dense, the apices rounded to truncate or obtuse. Flowers with pedicel less than 1 mm long. Hypanthium +/- cylindrical, free portion ca 1.4-2.5 mm long, the outer surface with moderate to dense ferrugineous indumentum, the inner surface glabrous and 1 0-ridged, the apices of the ridges forming lobes or small digitate projections 0. 1- 0.8 mm long. External calyx lobes ca 1-2.7 x 1-1.5 mm, broadly triangular with acute to slightly acuminate apices, dense ferrugineous indumentum; internal calyx lobes ca 1.8-2.6 x 1.7-2.6 mm, broadly ovate, the apex rounded, the margin minutely erose, with sparse to dense ferrugineous indumentum on both surfaces; calyx tube lacking or to 0.4 mm long. Petals broadly ovate to elliptic, 4.2-6.2 x 3-4.5 mm, white. Stamens geniculate; proximal segment (filament) 1.8-2.8 mm long; distal segment (anther and connective) 3-4.4 mm long, with minute dorsal projection, the anther ca 2.4-3 mm long, with fertile portion of anther sacs ca 1.8-2.5 mm long, the connective extending 1-1.6 mm beyond the base of anther sacs. Ovary usually 4-loculate (32 flowers; 5-loculate: 12 flowers), half-inferior to inferior, short ovoid, ca 2.4-5 x 3-5.7 mm, glabrous and strongly 10-ridged, with minute apical projections, to ca 0.4 mm long, encircling base of style; style 4.6- 6.2 mm long; stigma truncate. Mature berries not seen; immature berries globose, to ca 7 mm long and wide.

description: Shrub or small tree to ca 6 m tall. Twigs lenticular to narrowly rhombic, 3-6 (7.5) mm wide, with 2 well developed ridges or 2 well developed and 2 weaker ridges, becoming elliptic with age, the indumentum usually dense, glabrescent; internodes 1-5 (7.5) cm long. Leaves with petiole 0.7-3.2 cm long, the indumentum dense; blade obovate, elliptic or nearly oblong, to slightly ovate, (6.5) 7.5- 16 x (1.6) 2-5.8 cm, flat, coriaceous, the apex slightly to clearly acuminate, the base acute or obtuse (rounded), the margin obscurely serrate, with the largest teeth 0.05-0.35 (0.5) mm long, becoming entire toward base (ca 3.5-65% of margin without teeth), plane; venation acrodromous, basal to slightly suprabasal, with midvein and 4 secondary veins, with 2 conspicuous secondary veins placed ca 2- 9 mm in from margin and 2 inconspicuous, + intramarginal secondary veins, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented subperpendicular to midvein and usually separated by composite intertertiary veins (less so on leaves of rapidly growing sucker-shoots); adaxial surface dark green, the indumentum dense when young, glabrescent, the midvein and major secondary veins impressed, intramarginal secondary, and tertiary veins slightly impressed; abaxial surface pale- ferrugineous, densely (moderately) covered with multicellular, stellate hairs to ca 0.4 mm across, the midvein and major secondary veins prominently raised, minor secondary, and tertiary veins less conspicuously raised, higher order veins slightly to not at all raised. Inflorescences terminal, many-flowered, open, paniculate cymes of usually 3 or 4 major branch-pairs, ca 3-8.5 cm long, 3-7.5 cm across; lowermost inflorescence branches with basal segment 1-3.3 cm long, distal in- ternodes increasingly shorter, all with dense ferrugineous indumentum; peduncle 2.5-11 cm long; the inflorescence branches associated with a quickly caducous +/- narrowly elliptic to ovate or linear, ca 3-6 mm long (or possibly longer) bract; flowers in dichasia, each flower associated with a pair of caducous, narrowly elliptic to ovate or linear bracteoles, ca 2-4 x 0.5-1 mm, the indumentum dense, the apices acute to obtuse. Flowers with pedicel 0.4-1 mm long. Hypanthium +/- cylindrical, free portion ca 1.3-1.7 mm long, the outer surface with moderate to dense ferrugineous indumentum, the inner surface glabrous and 10-ridged, the apices of the ridges forming minute projections ca 0.1 mm long. External calyx lobes 0.5-1 x 1 mm, broadly triangular with acute to slightly acuminate apex, dense ferrugineous indumentum; internal calyx lobes ca 1.2-1.9 x 1.2-2.6 mm, broadly ovate-triangular, the apex rounded, the margin minutely erose, with sparse to dense ferrugineous indumentum on both surfaces; calyx tube 0.6-1.2 mm long. Petals broadly ovate to elliptic, 3.4-5 x 2.9-4 mm, white. Stamens geniculate; proximal segment (filament) 1.6-2.8 mm long; distal segment (anther and connective) 1.8-3.1 mm long, with minute dorsal projection, the anther ca 1.5-2.7 mm long, with fertile portion of anther sacs ca 1-2 mm long, the connective extending ca 0.5-1.5 mm beyond the base of anther sacs. Ovary 5-loculate, half inferior, short-ovoid, ca 2.2-3.8 x 2.9-4.8 mm, glabrous and 10-ridged, with minute apical projections, to ca 0.3 (occasionally 0.8) mm long, encircling base of style; style 3-4.5 mm long; stigma truncate. Mature berries globose, ca 8-10 mm long and wide, blue (red when immature), moderately to sparsely covered with globular-stellate hairs. Seeds angular-obovoid, 0.5-1.1 mm long.

description: Shrub to ca 3 m tall. Young twigs elliptic, (2.5) 3-7 mm in diam, sulcate, with very slight nodal ridge, becoming terete with age, usually densely covered with multicellular, ferrugineous, globular to irregularly stellate-branched hairs, gla- brescent; internodes 1-5 (9) cm long. Leaves with petiole 0.9-2.8 cm long, with indumentum similar to that of twigs; blade elliptic to ovate or obovate, 5- 11.4 x 1.8-5 cm (but the pair immediately below inflorescence usually smaller and sometimes intergrading with inflorescence bracts), coriaceous, the apex slightly acuminate to acute or obtuse, the base rounded to obtuse, the margin plane, obscurely to clearly serrate, becoming entire near base, the largest teeth 0.2-0.5 mm long; venation acrodromous, basal, with prominent midvein and 4 secondary veins, with 2 conspicuous secondary veins placed ca 2.5-6.5 mm in from margin (at blade midpoint) and 2 inconspicuous intramarginal secondary veins, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented subperpendicular to midvein, the tertiary veins joined by percurrent-orthogonal quaternary veins; adaxial surface green, sometimes slightly red-tinged near margin, densely covered with minute globular, and irregularly branched, multicellular hairs, glabrescent, the surface +/- papillose after drying due to presence of numerous druse crystals just beneath surface, the midvein and 2 major secondary veins impressed, 2 minor secondary veins and tertiary veins slightly impressed to flat; abaxial surface light green to red-tinged (especially near margin), initially densely covered with minute globular hairs on lamina and ferrugineous, irregularly stellate-branched hairs on veins,  becoming only sparsely globular-pubescent on mature leaves (glabrescent), the midvein and 2 major secondary veins prominently raised, the 2 intramarginal secondary veins and tertiary veins slightly to not at all raised. Inflorescences terminal, many-flowered, open, broadly rounded cymes of 3 or 4 major branch pairs, ca 2.5-5 cm long (as measured from terminal flower to point at which first branch-pair emerges from axis), 3.5-6.5 cm across; proximal segment of lower most inflorescence branches 0.8-1.9 cm long, distal internodes of inflorescence branches increasingly shorter, all glabrous to sparsely covered with minute glob- ular hairs; peduncle, i.e., internode separating cyme from uppermost leaf pair, 1.5-7.5 cm long, with similar indumentum; each inflorescence branch associated with a caducous, broadly ovate to elliptic, often reddish bract, ca 8-18 x 5.5-10 mm, the apices acute to rounded; flowers in dichasia, each subtended by 2 caducous, broadly ovate to obovate, often reddish, bracteoles, ca 4-11.5 x 2.5-9 mm, nearly glabrous but with a few irregularly branched multicellular hairs near margins, their apices rounded. Flowers 5-merous, nearly sessile. Hypanthium +/-  cylindrical, free portion 1.4-2.5 mm long, the outer surface sparsely covered with minute, ferrugineous, globular, multicellular hairs and slightly roughened due to presence of numerous druse crystals, the inner surface glabrous and 10-ridged, the apices of the ridges forming minute projections 0.1-0.2 mm long. External calyx lobes 5, 0.7-1.1 x 1.9-2.6 mm, broadly triangular with acute to slightly acuminate apex, very sparsely covered with indumentum similar to that of hypanthium; internal calyx lobes 5, 1-1.1 x 2.3-2.4 mm, broadly ovate-triangular, pale green, often red-tinged, glabrous on both surfaces, the apex rounded, the margin entire; calyx tube ca 0.3 mm long. Petals 5, imbricate in bud, broadly elliptic to slightly ovate or obovate, 2.4-2.8 x 2.7-3.2 mm, white, glabrous, the apex rounded, emarginate with an asymmetrically located notch, the margin entire. Stamens 10, geniculate, white; proximal segment (filament) ca 1 mm long, glabrous; distal segment (anther and connective) ca 2.7 mm long, glabrous, the anther ca 1.9 mm long, with fertile portion of anther sacs ca 1.4 mm long, opening by 2 longitudinal slit-like pores, with a dorsal bump ca 0.1 mm long, the connective extending beyond bases of anther sacs 0.7-0.8 mm. Ovary 5-loculate, 3/4 to nearly completely inferior, +/- globose, ca 2.7 x 2.5-3 mm, glabrous and 10-ridged, with a ring of minute apical projections, to ca 0.1 mm long, encircling base of style; style 2.5-3.2 mm long, terete, glabrous, slightly sunken into apex of ovary; stigma truncate. Nearly mature berries globose, ca 6-8 mm in diam (possibly larger when fully mature), purple (red when immature), with very sparsely scattered globular hairs. Seeds angular-obovoid, ca 0.5-0.7 mm long; testa +/- smooth.

description: Rami pubescentes, tomnentosi vel hirsuti, juniores saepe vinosi. Folia alterna, petiolata, membranacea, ovata vel lanceolata, apice acuto vel acuminato, base cordata, pubescenti, tomentosa vel hirsuta. Flores lilacini vel purpurascentes; bracteolae nullae; antherae appendicibus connectivi aurantiaco-brunneis; appendices nectariferae filamentorum duorum anticorum no- duliformes vel conicae; ovarium glabrum. Semina pubescentia, pagina dorsali foveolata.

description: Twining herb; stems terete, pubescent, tomentose or hirsute, frequently vinaceous when young. Leaves alternate, membranous, internodes 1.6-4.5(-8) cm long; stipules 3.5-5 X 1 mm, lanceolate, entire, reddish to vinaceous; petiole 5.5-11 mm long; lamina 3.8-6.1 X 1.6-4.2 cm, ovate or lanceolate, apex acute to acuminate, margin serrate, base cordate, pubescent, tomentose, or hirsute, hairs simple. Flowers lilac or purplish, sometimes with darker linear markings, solitary, axillary, pedicel (0.6-)2-3 cm long, articulate, tomentose to hirsute; bracteoles absent. Sepals equal, 3.5-4.5 X ca. 1 mm, lanceolate, apex acuminate, entire, base truncate, pubescent to tomentose. Upper petals 3-4 X 1.5 mm, oblong to elliptic, apex obtuse to rounded; lateral petals 5.5-7.5 X 2-3.5 mm, oblong to spatulate, falcate, apex obtuse to rounded; anterior petal 11-16 mm long, the lam- ina suborbicular to flabelliform. Staminal filaments ca. 0.5-1 mm long; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, the connective appendages orange-brown, acute, sometimes asymmetric, about as long as the anthers, both anterior staminal filaments with noduliform or (sub-)conical nectary appendages, sometimes one or both of the anterior stamens fused with the adjacent posterior stamens by their filaments. Ovary 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous, style 2 mm long, straight or slightly curved. Capsule 1.7-2.1 cm long, 0.8-1.4 cm diam., ellipsoid, chartaceous; seeds 4.5-5 mm long, 3 mm wide, pubescent, the dorsal surface foveolate.

description: Shrub, treelet, root-climbing liana, or hemiepiphyte, glabrous throughout; branchlets quadrangular becoming almost rounded with age. Leaves of a pair equal or subequal; petioles 5-10 mm long; lamina elliptic to ovate-elliptic, 12-21 X 4-7 cm, subpanduriform, somewhat coriaceous, attenuated toward the base to an almost parallel-sided section 1-1.5 X 0.5-1 cm; margins entire, slightly revolute toward the base; base rounded to slightly cordate; apex abruptly acuminate, the acumen 0.5-1.2 cm long; venation strongly 3-plinerved, excluding the tenuous inframarginal nerves which run 0.5-1 mm from the margin; primary nerves inserted 1-2.7 cm above the lamina base; secondary nerves 2-5 mm apart. Flowers erect, 1-4 in each leaf axil, 6-merous; pedicels 5-9 mm long, thick and somewhat complanate; bracts 9-12 X 9-11 mm, thick and hard; external bracts ovate, 1-nerved and faintly keeled, fused at the base for 1-2 mm, apex acuminate, slightly granulose abaxially; internal bracts free, round to ovate, margins eciliate; hypanthium 6-8 mm long to the torus; calyx tube 1.5-2 mm long, calyx lobes ovate, 5-6 X 4.5-5 mm, coriaceous, apex rounded to acute, margins entire; petals white with pinkish margin, 16-17 X 8.5-11 mm, fleshy and somewhat rigid, glabrous, elliptic, apex acuminate, margins entire; stamens 12, subequal; filaments 5-7 mm long, 3-angled, glabrous; anthers 3.8-4.8 X 2.6- 3 mm, laterally connate, with two minute apical pores, connective with a dorso-basal spur protruding for 1.2-1.4 mm, bluntly acute; ovary completely inferior, 6-locular, glabrous; ovary cone 2.6-3.3 mm long; style glabrous 11-12 mm long; stigma not expanded. Mature berries and seeds not seen.

description: Root-climbing shrub or liana; branchlets somewhat quadrangular becoming terete with age, young stems and petioles sparsely covered with a caducous pubescence of short, thickened, basally barbellate hairs; hairs 0.4-0.8 mm long. Leaves of a pair equal to subequal; petioles 1.5-3 cm long; lamina elliptic to elliptic-obovate, 14-17.5 X 8.5-10.5 cm, subcoriaceous; margins entire to shallowly and distantly denticulate in the upper half; base rounded to cuneate; apex shortly acuminate; hairs on adaxial surface scattered, readily deciduous, elongate, roughened, 0.6-0.9 mm long; venation 5-plinerved, excluding the tenuous inframarginal nerves, the outer primary nerves delicate, running 1-3 mm from the margin, the inner primary nerves robust, inserted 5-10 mm above the lamina base; hairs on abaxial side of primary nerves sparse, readily deciduous, short, thickened, basally roughened, 0.5-0.8 mm long; secondary nerves 3-6 mm apart, mostly glabrous. Flowers erect, 1-4 in each leaf axil, sometimes in terminal clusters on stunted lateral leaf-bearing shoots, 6-merous; pedicels 4-7 mm long; hairs on pedicel deciduous, short, thick, basally barbellate, 0.4- 0.9 mm long; external bracts broadly obovate, 1-1.2 X 1.5-1.8 cm, thick, coriaceous, 1-nerved and faintly keeled, free, imbricate, apex acute, externally with caducous hairs similar to those of the pedi- cels; internal bracts similar to the external ones but venation not visible, apex rounded to truncate, margins irregular, externally glabrous or nearly so; hypanthium 6-7 mm long to the glabrous torus; calyx tube 2-3 mm long; calyx lobes broadly ovate, 6 X 6 mm, coriaceous, apex rounded, margins irregular, adaxially with an amorphous lanate pubescence on the upper 1/2; petals white in the center and pinkish toward margin, 16- 17 X 10-12 mm, somewhat fleshy, elliptic, apex rounded to acute, margins entire; sta- mens 12, isomorphic; filaments 5-7 mm long, complanate, glabrous; anthers subulate, 7-8 mm long, with two confluent pores, dorsally inclined, connective with a minute dorso-basal tooth; ovary 1/2 inferior, 6-locular, glabrous; ovary cone deeply and irregularly divided in 12 teeth, 2-3 mm long; style glabrous; stigma not expanded. Mature berries and seeds not seen.

description: Root-climbing shrub or hemiepiphyte, to 10 m tall; branchlets subquadrangular becoming terete with age, the young stems, petioles and peduncles densely covered with thick, curved hairs; hairs minutely barbellate at the base, 0.6-1.2 mm long. Leaves of a pair equal to slightly unequal in size; petioles 2.5-4 cm long; lamina elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 7-13 X 5-7 cm, coriaceous; margins shallowly and distantly denticulate; base rounded to cuneate; apex acuminate; adaxially bullate; each bulla topped by a short, hardened, conic hair; abaxially the bullae completely covered by slender, elongated, light brown hairs, 0.7- 0.9 mm long, with a white, substellate base; venation shortly 3-plinerved, excluding the pair of inframarginal nerves running 0.8- 1.5 mm from the margin; primary nerves inserted 2-5 mm above the lamina base, secondary nerves 3-5 mm apart, all nerves below densely covered with minutely barbellate, light brown hairs. Flowers erect to somewhat pendulous, 1-4(-5) in each leaf axil, 6-merous; pedicels 1-2.5 cm long; external bracts triangular, 11-12 X 10-11 mm, thick and coriaceous, with one main nerve and several parallel secondary veins, faintly keeled, fused at the base for 1-2 mm, apex acute, occasionally recurved, densely covered with light brown, rough- ened hairs abaxially and in the upper half adaxially, margins ciliolate on the lower half; internal bracts triangular-ovate, similar to the external ones but slightly smaller, free and glabrous at the base, apex often recurved; hypanthium 7-8 mm long to the torus; calyx tube 3.5-4 mm long, calyx lobes elliptic-ovate, 6-7 mm X 5 mm, recurved, coriaceous, apex acute, margins irregular, densely covered with roughened hairs on both sides; petals pinkish-white, 17-18 X 11-12 mm, fleshy, obovate, rounded, entire, minutely puberulent adaxially with hairs 0.3-0.6 mm long; stamens 12, isomorphic; filaments 3-4 mm long, complanate, glabrous; anthers subulate, 6- 7 mm long, with one large dorsal pore, connective with a minute dorso-basal tooth; ovary completely inferior, 5-locular, glabrous; ovary cone shallowly and irregularly divided, 4-5 mm long; style glabrous, 7-8 mm long (measured from the apex of the ovary cone); stigma not expanded. Mature berries and seeds not seen.

description: Shrubs or small trees to 10 m tall; stems copiously and densely stellate pubescent with light yellowish to reddish-brown hairs, becoming dark, grayish-black and glabrate. Leaves, petioles, stipules, and ovaries stellate pubescent. Leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 3.5-11.3 (14.8) cm long, 2.3-9.7 (10.9) cm wide, base truncate on very young leaves, soon becoming somewhat oblique to cordate, apex acute, acuminate, or long acuminate, margins remotely serrate to serrulate; indumentum densely stellate pubescent above and below, the hairs persistent; nervation pal- mately 3-5 (7)-nerved, the nerves densely stellate pubescent; petiole 0.7-3.8 cm long; stipules subulate, ca 2 mm long. Inflorescences 2-5-flowered; pedicels 4-15 mm long, densely stellate pubescent and with scattered gland-tipped hairs; bracts subtending pedicels lanceolate to linear, 3-5 mm long, densely stellate pubescent, pentagonal. Calyx in flower subglobose to urceolate, 7-1 1 mm long, densely stellate pubescent, with scattered gland-tipped hairs; lobes narrowly triangular to trian- gular, 1.5-3 mm long, 2.5-4 mm wide, apices acute and somewhat apiculate; calyx in fruit acutely pentagonal, subglobose, 1.4-2.7 cm long, sparingly stellate pubescent, with scattered, gland-tipped hairs, pale purple or pink-yellow (when dry), lobes triangular, 4-11 mm long, 5-10 mm wide, apices acute to acuminate and apiculate. Petals included, oblanceolate to spatulate, 7-10.5 mm long, 1.5-3 mm broad, with scattered stellate hairs, purple to mauve. Longistylous flowers: staminal column 3-4 mm long, glabrous; anthers sessile, 1-5 mm long; staminodes 0.2-0.4 mm long; ovary 1.5-2 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad; stipe 2-3 mm long, styles 2-3 mm long, with scattered stellate hairs. Brevistylous flowers: staminal column 2.5-3.5 mm long; filaments 1-2 mm long; anthers ca 1.5 mm long; staminodes 0.1-0.5 mm long; ovary 1-1.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm diam; stipe 2.5- 3.5 mm long; styles 0.5-1 mm long, stellate. Capsule deeply retuse at the apex, 4-5 mm tall, 4-5 mm diam, densely stellate pubescent, subtended by a stipe 5- 6 mm long; seeds ovate, rounded in cross section, 1 per carpel, 2.5-3 mm long, 1.5-2 mm diam.
bibliographicCitation: Dorr, Laurence J. & Barnett, L. C. 1989. A revision of Melochia section Physodium (Sterculiaceae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 41: 404-423.

description: Plants mnoderately yellowish pubeseent, the hairs stellate, the older parts often subglabrous, the younger parts often densely pubescent; internodes 9-mm long (mean 23 mm), 1.5-4.5 mm wide (mean 2.5 mm); leaves obovate to elliptic-oblong, 18-36 mm long (mean 28 mm), 9-18 mm wide (mean 11.8 mm); inflorescences often distinctly yellowish because of the dense pubeseence; staminate inflorescence with 2-5 segments (mean 3.0), individual segments with 11-26 flowers (mean 19.5); pistillate inflorescence with 2-3 segments (mean 2.3), individual segments with 9-14 flowers (mean 11.0); n = 14.

description: Liana; rami floriferi aphylli. Lamina foliorum majorum 6-10 x 3.5-5 cm, elliptica, supra glabra, subtus tomentosa, pilis T-formibus; petiolus 0.6-0.9 cm longus. Inflorescentia ex pseudoracemo corymboso solitario axillari constans, floribus in quoque pseudoracemo 14-20(-27); pedunculi 7.5-15.5 mm longi, pedicelli (3-)5-10 mm longi. Bracteae 1.4-3 mm longae, eglandulosae; bracteolae inaequales, una bracteola cujusque paris (0.6-)1-1.3(-2) mm longa, linearis vel oblonga vel anguste triangularis, eglandulosa vel uniglandulosa, altera bracteola 1.5-2.2 mm longa, elliptica, ovata, obovata, oblonga, vel obtriangularis, 1-3 glandulis abaxialibus et interdum margine aliquot glandulis minutis instructa. Petala lutea, glabra, limbo abaxialiter carinato. Samara 2.5-3.5 cm diametro, ala laterali basi continua, crista dorsali 6 mm lata.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, C. 2001. Novelties in Mascagnia (Malpighiaceae). Brittonia. 53: 405-415.

description: Vine; branches tomentulose when young, becoming glabrous in age; flowering shoots leafless or bearing expanding leaves. Lamina of the larger leaves 6-10 X 3.5-5 cm, elliptical, apex acuminate to sometimes caudate, base truncate to shallowly cordate, adaxially glabrous or the costa proximally tomentulose, abaxially white-tomentose (sometimes glabrescent in age), the hairs T-shaped, mostly with a stalk to 0.1 mm long or sometimes subsessile, the trabecula (1-)1.2-2.1 mm long, with 0-2 impressed glands near the base and 0-3 additional impressed glands on the abaxial surface, with 2 marginal glands just below the apex; petiole 0.6-0.9 cm long, densely velutinous, eglandular; stipules 0.7-0.8 mm long, linear, interpetiolar. Inflorescence an axillary, solitary, congested corymbose pseudoraceme of 14-20(-27) flowers, borne on an axis (0.6-) 1.2-2.5 cm long, the 2 lowest flowers usually separated a short distance from the aggregate. Peduncles 7.5-15.5 mm long, (1.3-) 1.6-2.6 X as long as pedicels, velutinous- tomentulose; pedicels (3-)5-10 mm long, sparsely sericeous to glabrate. Bracts 1.4-3 X 0.3-0.5 mm, linear to narrowly triangu- lar, eglandular. Bracteoles usually unequal or rarely subequal; of each pair usually one bracteole (0.6-)1-1.3(-2) X 0.2-0.3 mm, linear or oblong to narrowly triangular, eglandular or sometimes with a prominent basal gland, the other 1.5-2.2 X 0.5-1.2 mm, irregularly shaped from elliptical to ovate to obovate to oblong to obtriangular, abaxially with a large basal gland (0.4-0.5 mm diam., to 0.3 mm high) and usually also with 1-2 smaller glands, often also with several minute marginal glands; pair of bracteoles subopposite or sometimes to 3.5 mm apart, inserted usually at or near the apex of the peduncle or sometimes to 5 mm below it. Calyx of 4 biglandular lateral se- pals and 1 eglandular anterior sepal; lateral sepals exceeding the glands by ca. 1 mm, the glands 3-3.5 mm long, decurrent. Petals 5, yellow, glabrous, the limb abaxially car- inate, briefly hastate at base, the margin erose-denticulate, eglandular; lateral petals: claw ca. 1.5 X 0.5-0.6 mm, limb ca. 5.5 X 4-4.2 mm, ovate; posterior petal: claw ca. 1.5 X ca. 0.7 mm, limb ca. 6.5 X ca. 4 mm, oblong. Androecium of 10 subequal stamens; filaments 1.5-2.7 mm long, the anterior one the longest, the posterior one the shortest, slightly connate at base; anthers 1.2-1.3 mm long, glabrous. Styles erect to slightly divergent, subequal, 3.2-3.5 X 0.4-0.5 mm, the anterior one slightly shorter and slenderer than the posterior two, the apex dorsally rounded to acute. Mature samara 2.5-3.5 cm diam., suborbicular to orbicular, the lateral wing continuous at base and at apex except for a distal notch 1-2.2 mm deep, sericeous; central dorsal winglet 6-8 X 2.5-3.3 mm; nut ca. 6 mm high; torus 2.8-3 mm high, surrounded by a wide, glabrous, 3-lobed, disciform outgrowth of the receptacle.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, C. 2001. Novelties in Mascagnia (Malpighiaceae). Brittonia. 53: 405-415.

description: Rhizome long-creeping, ca 3 mm diam; rhizome scales ovate to ovate-lanceolate, pale brown to bicolorous with a central streak of lustrous dark brown, mostly 3-5 mm long, generally entire; scales somewhat deciduous; phyllopodia distinct, 1-2 cm long; fronds 1-2 cm apart, to 40 cm long, 2.9 cm broad; stipe 1/3-1/2 of the frond length, with scattered ovate scales of the rhizome, entire or with occasional weak marginal hairs; blade narrowly elliptic, apex acute to acuminate, base narrowly cuneate; coriaceous; veins obscure, free, simple or once-forked, ca 1 mm apart, running at ca 70º angle; hydathodes lacking; blade surfaces sub- glabrous, with sparse, minute, stellate hairs and occasional broader scales on midvein, especially on the abaxial surface; fertile fronds longer than the sterile fronds, the stipe longer (1/2-2/3 of the fertile frond length) and the blade slightly narrower; scales lacking; spores with low slender crests.

description: Rhizome 1.5-2.3 cm diam., sometimes forking. Frond with droop-tip vernation; basal petiole scales narrow to long-lanceolate, coriaceous (the edge rarely chartaceous), light orangish yellow to light yellowish brown with a well-developed and sharply delimited central deep brown stripe, conform, the cilia short to minute, flaccid; distal petiole scales similar, but broader, chartaceous to papyraceous, light orangish yellow or with a brownish orange to orangish yellow central stripe; small petiole scales ovate-caudate, broad-lanceolate, or long-lanceolate, orangish yellow with or without a brown central stripe. Lamina 30-45 cm long, 2-pinnate, acuminate, coriaceous, lustrous green adaxially when fresh; rachis without a proliferous bud, the rachis scales deep orange to brown. Pinnae 8-14 X 1.5-3.2 cm, attenuate, attached at right angles to rachis, the basal pinnae usually as long as or longer than rest; abaxial pinnarachis scales abruptly contracted to an elongate apex (rarely long-lanceolate to narrow-lanceolate), deep orangish yellow to yellowish brown, with cilia more frequent at scale base. Pinnules crenate, often attached at oblique angles, acute to obtuse, flat, the basal acroscopic pinnules longer than next distal, the basal basiscopic pinnules near lamina base shorter than next distal; veins all free; short spinules usually developed on most vein tips. Sorus terminal on vein, the true indusium 1.0-1.5 mm diam., peltate, deep orangish yellow to yellowish brown.

description: Plants annual, weakly erect, 0.5-3 X 1- 2 dm, grayish to greenish, densely silky-puberulent. Leaves basal; blades obovate to rounded, 0.5-1.5 X 0.5-1.5 cm, sparsely villous and usually greenish on both surfaces; petioles 0.5-2 cm long. Flowering stems erect or nearly so, 0.3-0.8 dm long. Inflorescences open and spreading, 0.5-2.5 dm long; bracts linear to narrowly lanceolate, somewhat foliaceous, 2-5 (9) X 1-2 (2.5) mm, puberulent on both surfaces. Involucral bracts separate and distinct at anthesis; outer three bracts infrequently partially connate in bud, oblanceolate, 0.5-1.2 X 0.1- 0.3 mm, villous abaxially; pedicels glabrous, 1-2 mm long, glabrous; bractlets 0.3-0.8 mm long, glabrous. Flowers white to pale yellow at anthesis, becoming rose or red in fruit, 1-1.5 mm long at anthesis, 1.5-2 mm long in fruit, minutely pustulose basally and along midribs; tepals somewhat dimorphic, those of outer whorl narrowly ovate and slightly auriculate basally with undulate-crisped margins in fruit, those of inner whorl narrowly oblanceolate, often shorter than those of outer whorl; stamens included, 0.8-1.2 mm long. Achenes light brown, trigonous, 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous.

description: Plants annual, spreading, 0.5-3 X 1-3 (5) dm, reddish, thinly silky-puberulent. Leaves basal; blades obovate to rounded or somewhat reniform, 0.5-1.5 X 0.5-1.5 cm, sparsely villous and greenish on both surfaces; petioles 0.5-2 cm long. Flowering stems erect or spreading, 0.3-0.5 dm long. Inflorescences diffuse and spreading, 0.5-2.5 dm long; bracts triangular, scalelike, 1- 2 (2.5) X 1-2 (2.5) mm, glabrous but ciliate on margins. Involucral bracts separate and distinct at anthesis; outer two bracts sometimes remaining partially connate even at anthesis, oblanceolate to obovate, 0.5-0.8 X 0.1-0.3 mm, glabrous but ciliate on margins; pedicels glabrous, 1-2.5 mm long, glabrous; bractlets 0.3-0.6 mm long, glabrous. Flowers white to rose at anthesis, becoming red in fruit, 1-2 mm long at anthesis, 2-2.5 mm long in fruit, glabrous; tepals monomorphic, lanceolate; stamens included, 1.2-1.8 mm long. Achenes light brown, trigonous, 1.3-1.8 mm long, glabrous.

description: Whole plant glabrous except for the reddish fringes along the midribs of the lower leaf-surfaces (rarely even these fringes wanting or rarely a few hairs at the base of the raceme). Foliage leaves mostly 2-3 cm. wide and 4.5-7 cm. long, 1.8-2.3 times as long as wide; leaves on individual plants sometimes smaller, or occasionally up to 4.5 cm. wide and 9 cm. long; l/w ratio more nearly constant in different leaves of the same plant than in P. serotina (typical), but in some plants standing at 2.7 or 2.8. Petioles very short (mostly 5-7 mm. long) in most Arizona material, longer (1-2 cm.) in most New Mexican and Texan plants and some Mexican material; blades with 4-11 (usually 5-7) teeth per cm. of margin. Second floral leaf mostly about 1.7 cm. wide and 3.4 cm. long, the l/w ratio usually about 2.0, but varying from 1.1 to 3.0; petioles averaging 0.7 cm. long (less- in the western part of the range); blades with 3-13 (usually 7) teeth per cm. of margin. Flowering branch averaging about 10 cm. long (longest branch noted was 39 cm.); flowers usually about 30 (greatest number observed, 69); pedicels about 3.5 mm. long in flower, 4.5 mm. in fruit (1.7-10 mm. in individual plants); calyx-lobes 1.2-2 mm. long (usually about 1.4-1.5 mm.); petals mostly about 3 mm. long and wide; longer filaments up to 3.5 mm. long; anthers averaging about 0.8 mm. long; style averaging about 1.4 mm. long (1-2 mm.); fruit about 1 cm. across.
bibliographicCitation: McVaugh, Rogers. 1951. A revision of the North American black cherries (Prunus scrotina Ehrb., and relatives). Brittonia. 7: 279-315.

description: Pleuridium, P. rupestri affinis, frondibus tenuioribus gracilibus et palearum apicibus crinitis distinguendum, rhizomate repente, 2 mm. crasso, paleis fusco-ferrugineis parvis deorsum ciliatis sursum in caudas tortas demum deciduas protensis vestito; stipitibus haud re- motis, fere filiformibus, 4-8 cm. altis; fronde usque ad 12 cm. longa et 6 mm. lata, utrinque attenuata, praecipue sursum more gregis minute inciso-serrata, glabra, subeoriacea, viride; venis immersis, utraque facie inconspicuis, venulis costae parallelis 2 vel 3, liberis in- clusis, fere nullis; soris inter venas biseriatis, in serie quaque 1 vel 2, superficialibus, parvis.

description: Liana. Lamina foliorum majorum 9-18.5 X 4.8-8 cm, elliptica, utrinque velutina, pilis plerumque Y-formibus; petiolus 0.8-1.5 cm longus. Inflorescentia axillaris, aut ex pseudoracemo corymboso solitario constans, aut thyrsiformis, floribus in quoque pseudoracemo (12-)15-26; pedunculi 6.5-11.3 mm longi, pedicelli 3.5-6.5 mm longi. Bracteae 1-1.5 mm longae, eglandulosae; bracteolae 0.6-0.9 mm longae, triangulares vel ovatae, una bracteola cujusque paris vel raro ambae uniglandulosae. Petala lutea, glabra, limbo abaxialiter carinato. Samara ignota.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, C. 2001. Novelties in Mascagnia (Malpighiaceae). Brittonia. 53: 405-415.

description: Vine; young branches velutinous, vesture abraded in age; flowering shoots with expanding leaves. Lamina of the larger leaves 9-18.5 X 4.8-8 cm, elliptical, rugose, apex briefly acuminate to briefly caudate, base shallowly cordate to cordate, adaxially and abaxially velutinous, the hairs Y-shaped, mostly with a stalk to 0.1 mm long or sometimes subsessile and then V-shaped, the arms 0.2-0.7 mm long, with (0-)1-2 impressed glands near the base and 2-5 additional impressed glands distally, with 2 marginal glands just below the apex; petiole 0.8-1.5 cm long, densely velutinous, eglandular; stipules 1.2-1.5 mm long, linear or very narrowly triangular, interpetiolar. Inflorescence unit a congested corymbose pseudoraceme of (12-)15-26 flowers, borne on an axis 0.7-1 cm long, either solitary or several arranged in a thyrse. Peduncles 6.5-11.3 mm long, 1.3-1.8X as long as pedicels, velutinous; pedicels 3.5-6.5 mm long, sparsely velutinous to glabrate. Bracts 1-1.5 X 0.4- 0.6 mm, linear, eglandular. Bracteoles subequal, 0.6-0.7(-0.9) X 0.4-0.6 mm, triangular to ovate, one of each pair with a discoid, thick-margined gland 0.9-1 mm diam., the proximal half of the gland borne on the peduncle and the distal half on the bracteole and obscuring it, the second bracteole eglandular or with an inconspicuous basal gland (0.2 mm diam.) or very rarely with a discoid gland 0.5 mm diam.; pair of bracteoles subopposite or sometimes to 1 mm apart, inserted near the apex of the peduncle or sometimes to 1.5 mm below it. Calyx of 4 biglandular lateral sepals and 1 eglandular anterior sepal; lateral sepals exceeding the glands by ca. 1 mm, the glands 2-2.2 mm long, decurrent. Petals 5, yellow, glabrous, the limb abaxially carinate, briefly hastate at base, the margin erose-denticulate, eglandular; anterior-lateral petals: claw 1 X 0.3-0.4 mm, limb 4.3-4.5 X 3.2-3.5 mm, ovate to suborbicular, not or slightly abaxially carinate; posterior-lateral petals: claw 1-1.2 X 0.3-0.4 mm, limb 4.3-4.5 X 3-3.2 mm wide, elliptical-oblong, abaxially carinate; posterior petal: claw 1.2-1.5 X 0.5 0.6 mm, limb 4.5-4.8 X 2.4-2.8 mm, oblong, abaxially carinate. Androecium of 10 unequal stamens, filaments connate at base, those opposing the posterior-lateral petals stouter than the rest, anthers glabrous; stamen opposite anterior sepal: filament 2 mm long, anther 1.6 mm long; stamens opposite anterior-lateral petals: filaments 1.5 mm long, anthers 1.4 mm long; stamens opposite anterior-lateral sepals: filaments 2 mm long, anthers 1.2 mm long; stamens opposite posterior-lateral petals: filaments 2.1 mm long, anthers 1.6 mm long; stamens opposite pos- terior-lateral sepals: filaments 2 mm long, anthers 1 mm long; stamen opposite posterior petal: filament 1.1 mm long, anther 1 mm long. Styles erect or slightly divergent, subequal, 2-2.2 X 0.3-0.4 mm, the anterior one slightly shorter and slenderer than the posterior two, the apex dorsally rounded. Samara not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, C. 2001. Novelties in Mascagnia (Malpighiaceae). Brittonia. 53: 405-415.

description: Perennial glabrous herb, 15-18 cm tall, branched at the base and in the inflorescence; stems dark purple, slender, wiry; leaves sessile, 1-nerved, the larger 3.5 mm long, 1.3 mm wide, the lower in whorls of 4, the upper alternate, the uppermost with conspicuous marginal glands, but otherwise all entire; stipular glands none; inflorescence of slender, spreading-ascending branches; pedicels slender, the lowermost up to 12 mm long in fruit; sepals lanceolate to ovate, blunt to subacute, up to 1.7-1.8 mm long, the margins glandular-toothed, those of the inner sepals very sparsely so; petals ca. 3-3.5 mm long, lemon-yellow, glabrous at the base; stamens about 2 mm long; stamen tube with a few hairs near the base of filaments; staminodia very small or none; anthers slender, pale, 0.6 mm long; styles separate, contorted soon after anthesis, ca. 1.6-1.7 mm long; fruit glabrous, broadly ovate, pointed, 1.5-1.6 mm high, ca. 1.7 mm in diameter, easily crushed, freely dehiscent into 10 segments; false septa incomplete; true septa sparsely ciliate-margined; seeds pale brown, shining, ovate-elliptic, ca. 0.8 mm long, 0.5 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Rogers, Claude M. 1968. Yellow-flowered species of Linum in Central American and western North America. Brittonia. 20: 107-135.

description: Delicate annual, 22-34 cm tall, glabrous except for a few short hairs near the nodes and bases of the branches; stem simple to about the middle, the very ample inflorescence occupying one-half or more of the height of the plant; leaves in whorls of 4 below, alternate above, thin, entire, obovate below to ovate above, 14-18 mm long, 7.5-9 mm wide, on petioles up to 2 mm long; stipular glands present, but not well developed; inflorescence of slender branches; fruiting pedicels up to 7-17 mm long; sepals ovate, delicate, acuminate, with a few diminutive marginal glands or, especially the inner, entire, 2-2.5 mm long; petals yellow, obovate, about 4 mm long; stamens 3-4 mm long; staminodia filiform, up to 0.5 mm long; anthers ca. 0.4 mm long, broadly elliptic; styles 1.7-2.3 mm long, united almost to the summit; fruit pale, glabrous, broadly ovate, easily crushed, ca. 1.8 mm high and as wide; false septa imperfectly formed, true septa with some marginal hairs; mature seeds not seen.

description: Foliolis adaxialiter pubescentibus fructuque lenti- cellato S. macrocarpae similis, his notulis autem diversa: foliola lateralia (ob)lanceolata vel elliptica (nec falcato-lanceolata) (2.9-)5.2-7.6 X 1.5-2.3 (nec 5-5.6 X 1-1.4) cm, margo crenulata vel subintegra (vs. crenata), nervi secundarii 15-17 (nec 10-15); pedicellus 1.5-1.7 (nec 2.8-3.5) mm; petala 2-2.4 (nec ca. 2.6) mm; fructus (3.8-)4.9-6.3 X 2.3-2.7 (vs. 3.8-4 X 2.1-2.3) cm.

description: Tree to 38 m x 65 cm. Outer bark grayish brown with vertical stripes of raised lenticels; inner bark red- and white-striate. Trichomes of two types: white, flexuous to crispate suberect hairs to 0.3(-0.4) mm long (on leaves); yellow, appressed to suberect, blunt hairs to 0.2 mm long (on inflorescences). Leaves (5-)7-13-jugate, 20-33 cm long; leaflets (sub)opposite; petiole 3.1-5.6 cm long, petiole and rachis densely pubes- cent; lateral petiolules 1-2 mm, terminal one 0.7-1.7 cm; basal leaflets obliquely ovate to broadly elliptic, 2.9-3.8 X 1.5-2 cm, other laterals obliquely elliptic to (ob)lanceolate, 5.2-7.6 X 1.6-2.3 cm; ter- minal leaflet symmetric but otherwise like laterals, 5.5-5.9 X 1.4-1.8 cm; leaflet apex acuminate, acumen 0.4-1.3 cm; base oblique, truncate to obtuse; margin crenulate to subentire; on abaxial surface the midrib and secondary veins densely pubescent, hairs scattered to sparse along higher-order veins, on adaxial surface the midrib densely pubescent, rest of surface with scattered hairs, glands scattered on both sides of lamina; midrib prominent abaxially, prominulous adaxially, secondary veins in 15-17 pairs, prominulous abaxially, flat adaxially. description: Shrub to 3 m tall, stems to 3 cm diam., young branches and shoots minutely puberulous, light brown turning dark brown, without lenticels. description: Plants terrestrial. Rhizomes not seen. Fronds 160-175 X 57-65 cm, 1-pinnate-pinnatisect. description: Plant forming very low, very dense carpet mats (1.5 cm thick); stems dorsiventral, prostrate, crowded, branched, the stem apices and secondary branches ascending, apices involute when dry; rhizophores produced at intervals throughout. Upper leaves oblong or oblong-elliptic, 0.8-1.3 mm long (excluding seta), densely ciliate (9-15 piliform cilia per side), gray-green, erect-ascending on stem, bluntly acute, abruptly narrowed to seta, strongly carinate and beveled at apex, keeled on back near apex; seta elongate (0.2-1.0 mm long in twisted condition), stout, whitish to whitish-translucent to pale yellowish-white, persistent (at least near stem apices), strongly tortuous, sparsely scabrous; leaf bases abruptly ad- nate to stem, distinct from stem in color. Under leaves elliptic-oblong to lanceo- late-oblong, 1.4-1.7 mm long (excluding seta), densely ciliate (15-24 piliform cilia per side), tan, thinner than upper leaves, appressed, imbricate, bluntly acute, abruptly narrowed to seta, hardly or not beveled or carinate at apex, not keeled on back; seta elongate, tortuous. Strobili short (4-6 mm), exceeding mat of stems by only 2-4 mm, strongly quadrangular; sporophylls short (0.9-1.7 mm), broad (0.7-0.8 mm), broadly ovate, broadly acute, carinate and beveled apically, abruptly narrowed to seta, strongly keeled on back near apex; seta stout, whitish, tortuous, persistent; megasporangia few, basal in strobilus, mostly with one large (ca 0.5 mm diameter), yellow, reticulate megaspore but some with one or two large spores and one to three smaller ones; microspores numerous, tiny, orange, of uniform size.

description: Trunk 0.2-0.5 m high, ca. 3 cm in diam., covered with slender lanceolate, brown to tan, lustrous scales, 16 X 4 mm, some with margins lighter coloured or whitish; young croziers with scales of similar color (Fig. 1B). Petiole to 40 cm long, sparsely verrucate to weakly muricate basally (Fig. IB), smooth to tuberculate distally (Fig. IC), dark brown to atropurpureus; scurf of minute white squamules easily abraded (Fig. IC). Petiole scales broad lanceolate to ovate, opaque white to very light brown, sometimes with a dark brown streak at tip, the margins finely serrate (Fig. IC). Lamina to 40 cm long and 24 cm broad, broad ovate to triangular, widest in the region of the second pinna pair, bipinnate-pinnatifid, the apex gradually reduced, long tapering (Fig. IA). Rachis, costae, and costules dull reddish brown, with many short white multicellular hairs adaxially and few white tortuous, evanescent unicellular hairs abaxially; costae base with dark prominent pneumathode (Fig. ID). Pinnae to 8 cm wide, long triangular, acuminate, distally green alate, the basiscope pinnules missing on the three lower ones. Pinnules to 35 mm long and 8 mm wide, petiolulate (1-2 mm) to sessile, acute to short acuminate (Fig. ID), the segments rounded to deltate, obtuse, crenulate (Fig. IE). White hairs adaxially on all veins as well between the veins along the segment margins, these visible from beneath because of revolute margins (Fig. IC); few flattish brown scales with weakly fringed margins abaxially (Fig. IE). Lateral veins of a segment simple, dark and contrasting with the slightly glaucous abaxial lamina surface (Fig. ID, E). Sori costal, situated in furcation of main and lateral vein of a segment (Fig. IE). Indusium completely sphaeropteroid, without umbo, upper parts thin and evanescent, thus indusium appearing cyatheoid or meniscoid at maturity (Fig. IE). Paraphyses as long as sporangia or slightly longer. Spores not examined.

description: Small to medium-sized trees to at least 20 m tall; trunk to at least 38 cm DBH; bark tight, pale gray; young branches lightly pubescent, quickly glabrescent with growth; lenticels obscure, round, the same color as the bark or darker; wood (Alford 3023) diffuse porous, of vessels in radial multiples of 1-3 elements, and of septate fibers, vessel perforations usually simple, rarely with 1-4 scalariform bars, axial parenchyma lacking, growth rings intermediate between distinct and indistinct, prismatic crystals present in pith, intervascular pitting alternate, rays homocellular or heterocellular, if homocellular, of upright ray parenchyma, if heterocellular, of upright ray parenchyma up to 20 cells long or longer, prismatic crystals occasionally present, marginal or alternating with procumbent ray parenchyma, procumbent ray parenchyma 1- or 2-seriate, 4-20 cells long, prismatic crystals occasionally present. Leaves simple, alternate, chartaceous; blade ovate, 10.0-30.3 cm x 6.5-15.0 cm, sometimes smaller when immediately subtending the inflorescence; venation actinodromous, with 3 principal veins from the base, the lateral pair of veins extending about 2/3 of lamina length, (1)2-4 other prominent secondary veins arising from each side of the midvein more distally, tertiary veins more or less perpendicular to the midvein, numerous; adaxial surface sparsely pubescent, quickly glabrescent, venation flat; abaxial surface sparsely pubescent, especially along veins, quickly glabrescent, venation prominently raised; apex abruptly acuminate 'for about 1 cm with a rounded tip of acute with a rounded tip; base truncate to rounded; margin usually entire, the youngest leaves sometimes with very obscure teeth; two conspicuous glands embedded in the adaxial base of the lamina, glands elliptic, 0.5-1 x 1-1.5 mm; petioles 3.5-10.0 cm long, sparsely pubescent to glabrescent, often densely pubescent at the node and surrounding the axillary bud; stipules lanceolate, ca. 2 mm long, densely pubescent, quickly caducous. Inflorescences often very large, from 11 cm high x 16 cm wide at anthesis but poorly collected in largest state (more often collected in bud or with smaller inflorescences/infructescences), compound umbels of the 3rd to 5th order, the compound umbel probably a modified determinate thyrse or less likely an expanded, composite cymoid, 3-5(-9) axes per node, each axis except the central one immediately subtended by a triangular bract, 0.3-1.2 mm long, sparsely to densely pubescent, usually persistent; peduncle 0.3-1.5 cm long, strigillose; secondary axes 3.1-6.2 cm long, strigillose; higher-order axes gradually shorter than the secondary axes and more densely strigillose to puberulent; pedicels 2.5-8.5 mm long, articulated about 0.5 mm above the base, densely strigillose to puberulent, the central pedicel of each umbel apparently lacking a bract or pair of bracteoles, the other pedicels with a triangular, pubescent bract, 0.3-0.4 mm long, and a pair of bracte- oles or buds below the articulation, the bracteoles caducous; flower buds spheroidal, light green, densely pubescent, perianth aes- tivation valvate; flowers hermaphroditic, complete, 2.5-3.5 mm high x 2-4 mm wide at anthesis; sepals ovate to lanceolate, ca. 1.8 mm x 1.2 mm, creamy white, densely pubescent on both surfaces; petals lanceolate to oblong, ca. 2.0 mm x 0.4 mm, creamy white, densely puberulent on both surfaces; receptacle sparsely to moderately short pubescent; disk present between the stamens and the ovary, consisting of about 8 flat, pad-like glands, 0.2-0.3 mm in diameter; androecium of numerous (-30-50) stamens; filaments ca. 2.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers globose, 0.1-0.2 mm in diameter, glabrous, bilocular, longitudinally dehiscent; pollen grains single, isopolar, tricolporate, subprolate to prolate, tectate, reticulate, average polar length P=15-18.6 µm, average equato- rial width E=11.8-13 µm (Morales 6089 [MO], Fig. 2); staminodes absent; gynoecium of one superior (1)2(3)-carpellate syncarpous (paracarpous) ovary, placentation highly intruded-parietal, but appearing axile from an early stage due to the fusion of the placentae into a pseudo-axis, rarely with one parietal placenta, ovules numerous; ovary ca. 1 mm in diameter, with scattered hairs on its surface; style ca. 2.5 mm long at anthesis; stigma forming a T-shape or flattened Y-shape at apex. Fruit a berry, about 4.5 mm in diameter, slightly stipitate to 0.5 mm high, green when young, red (to blackish) when mature, subtended by the persistent perianth and capped by the persistent style; seeds few (<4), shaped like segments of an orange, ca. 4 mm x 2.5 mm, testa dark black, glossy; cotyledons large, foliate, spatulate.

description: Rhizomes 1-1.5 mm wide, horizontal, compact, polystichous; rhizome scales 2-3 mm long, linear-lanceolate, spreading, dark brown, concolorous, lustrous; phyllopodia absent; fronds 6-15 cm long, clumped; stipes ca. 1/10 the sterile frond length, 0.5 mm wide, with moderately abundant, yellowish orange, lanceolate, entire scales 2-4 mm long, with enrolled bases; blades narrowly lanceolate, 5-13 X 1-2 cm, rounded at base, acuminate at apex, membranaceous, lacking white patches; blade scales slightly to fully subulate, scattered to sparse, 0.5-1 mm long, yellowish orange, entire; blade surfaces with scattered, melleous, mostly 5- armed trichomidia; veins free, 1.5-2 mm apart, at ca. 60º angle to costa; hydathodes present; fertile fronds shorter (1/2-2/3) than the sterile, the stipes 2/3-3/4 the fertile frond length, blades narrowly deltate; inter- sporangial scales absent.

description: Plants terrestrial. Rhizomes short-creeping, densely clothed at apices with dark brown lanceate scales 2-3 mm long, the scale margins entire. Fronds erect, to ca. 140 cm long; stipes ca. 2/3 of frond length, up to 4 mm diam., reddish brown, grooved adaxially, smooth, glabrous except for a few linear-lanceate scales at bases; laminae chartaceous, with scattered whitish long hairs, 2-pinnate-pinnatifid at bases, with 4 pinna pairs per frond, the apical portion 1-pinnate-pinnatifid, ending in a broadly based pinnatifid apical pinna; rachises winged distally, pilose, the hairs whitish and septate, with 1-5 cells. Pinnae: proximal pinna pairs stalked (stalks ca. 0.5 cm long), opposite, deeply pinnatifid, furcate, the basiscopic portion of forks 20-25 X 4.5-5.5 cm, the acroscopic portion 20-25 X 5-6 cm; middle pinnae sessile, alternate, deeply pinnatifid, 25-30 X 6-7 cm; distal pinnae sessile, alternate; costae rounded to flattened and lacking awns adaxially, bearing whitish hairs ca. 0.5 mm long on both surfaces; segments subopposite to alternate, oblong, 1.5-4 cm long, falcate, the margins entire at middle to serrulate at apices, the terminal segment of each pinna narrowly deltate, acute or acuminate, longer than the others, the sinuses between segments roundish to mostly biangulate; venation copiously areolate, the costules somewhat prominent especially on abaxial surfaces, with 4 or 5 areoles adjoining costae between two adjacent costules; veins free near margins and apices of segments. Sori inter- rupted at sinuses and absent at apices of segments; indusia brownish, the margins entire; spores tan, trilete, tetrahedral.

description: Robust shrub or small treelet to 2-4 (-5) m tall, often multi-stemmed, or at least densely branched from the base, heavily armed with short, pale yellow, brown-tipped, 1-4 mm long, stramineous, recurved infrastipular and scattered internodal aculei arranged randomly on shoots and serially along dorsal face of leaf and pinnular rachises, at times the aculei crowded and appearing to occur in pairs, the young shoots dark reddish, weakly ridged, furnished with few scattered, erect, 0.4-0.7 mm long spreading setae mixed with fine minute puberulence on younger shoots, the leaf-stalk and peduncles finely puberulent. Stipules linear-lanceolate, 2-5 x 1-1.2 mm, yellow-puberulent dorsally, glabrous ventrally, setose-ciliate, 1-nerved, persistent. Leaf-stalks 2-5.7 cm, deeply sulcate ventrally, the petiole 1.7-4 x 0.06-0.1 cm, the interpinnal segments 3-9 mm; spicules irregularly present, minute, 0.3-0.6 x 0.1-0.25 mm ascending, finely puberulent, usually between the first and the last pinna pairs, but sometimes all pairs or only the last pair, but frequently absent from the majority of leaves on some specimens, and possibly readily de- ciduous; pinnae (2-)3 jugate, all distributed above middle of leaf stalk, irregularly graduated with the apical pair longer, the rachis 3- 7 cm, the longer interfoliolar segments 1.9-4 mm; leaflets of longer pinnae (15-)18-23 pairs, narrowly oblong (the basal pair ovate- acuminate) from oblique base, the tip acute, (6-)8-12 x (2-)3-4.2 mm (the first pair 5 x 2.3 mm), beneath 1-nerved, the nerve weakly or scarcely visible, but at times prominent to middle blade and towards the apex, dorsally setulose, the first pair 0.7-1.7 mm distant from 1-nerved paraphyllidia (0.5-) 0.8-1 x 0.2-0.3 mm, the blade ovate-acuminate. Peduncles 1.3-3.5 cm, minutely pubescent, in fascicles of 1-3 in axils of coevally developing leaves; capitula prior to anthesis moriform, 0.8-1 x 0.9-1 cm, but slightly hispid with emerging bracteal setae; receptacle 2- 4.5 x 0.7-1.7 mm; bracts 2-2.8 x 0.4-0.7 mm, spatulate, the apex acute, 1-nerved dor- sally, the apex pubescent dorsally, setose-ciliate. Flowers 4-merous, 4-androus, the majority bisexual, some staminate flowers at base of inflorescence and occasional capitula of predominantly staminate flowers; calyx hyaline, pappiform 1-2 mm, the tube 0.5 mm; corolla narrowly urceolate 3.2-4 mm, the tube glabrous, the lobules antrorsely puberulent, 1 x 0.75 mm; filaments white, free, exserted 6-6.5 mm (in fresh material the calyx and corolla pale whitish green, the lobe tips tinged darker green, the anthers pale green). Pods 2-6 per capitulum, sessile or subsessile, straight, oblong, 21-37 x 7-8.5 mm (although fully mature pods not seen), 2-5 seeded, the undulate and slightly constricted replum 1 mm wide, armed on sides with stiff, erect, yellow, brown-tipped setae to 1-6 mm, the stiffly papery valves low-convex over each seed, minutely pubescent, with 0.7-1.1 mm long setae over each seed, apparently breaking up into individually indehiscent single-seeded articles 6 x 7 mm. Seeds not seen (Fig. 1).

description: Shrub 1-1.7(-2) m tall, unarmed, the leaves and inflorescence at apex of a tough gnarled woody stem to ca. 1 m tall, the inflorescence a branched efoliate terminal pseudoraceme, far-exserted 40-70 cm above the leaves. Stems stout, reddish brown, or sometimes blackish as though carbonized on surface following fire, the surface cracking, the outer bark very thick, corky, cinnamon-brown, the latex resinous and sticky; young shoots and inflorescence axes, reddish brown or blackish, more or less terete or weakly ribbed, the inflorescence axis, stipules, petiolules of pinnae and leaflets, and floral bracts with scattered, basally dilated, short subappressed gland-tipped setulae, 0.3-0.8 mm, but these virtually absent from leaf stalks and shoots. Stipules persistent, 6-8(-10) x 2 mm, narrow-lanceolate, ventrally glabrous, dorsally short appressed-setose. Leaf-stalks 11.5-22.5 cm, the petiole (3.7- )6.5-10.5 cm, terete or subterete, at middle 2.5-5 mm diam., the interpinnal segments (2.3-)3-4 cm; pinnae 4(-5) jugate, rachis of proximal pinnae 8.5-13.5 cm, distal pinnae 13-18.6 cm, the longest interfoliar segments 1-1.4 cm; leaflets 8-15-jugate, more or less uniform except for smaller first two pairs, ovate, cordate at base, asymmetric, retuse, the larger leaflets 2.4-3.3 x 1.3-2.1 cm, glabrous, 5-8 nerved from short pulvinule, the stout straight midrib more or less central, 2-3 lateral veins almost reaching the apex, the rest shorter to less than mid-leaflet, first pair of leaflets 5.5-8 mm distant from a pair of short spinescent paraphyllidia 0.8-1.5 mm, but these not evident on all herbarium specimens. Inflorescence an effusely branch- ing panicle of globose capitula. Peduncles solitary, or in fascicles of 2-3, setulose or glabrous, 2-3.5 cm, each node subtended by a pair of persistent, narrow, ovate-lanceolate bracteoles, 6-1.2 x 1.2-1.5 mm, dorsally se- tose throughout or at apex and with scattered glandular setulae, ventrally glabrous. Capit- ula conelike in bud, to 2.2 cm diameter at anthesis; bracts 4-6 x 1-1.5 mm, with an acute recurved tip, dorsally glabrous, ventrally with scattered 0.3-1 mm glandular setulae. Flowers 4-merous, 8-androus; calyx pappiform 2.5-3 mm, united into a tube for 0.3-0.4 mm and the setae weakly joined at base into four lobes; corolla 2.5-4.8 mm, the tube externally glabrous, 1.2-3.8 mm, the ovate 1-nerved lobes 1-1.2 x 0.5-0.7 mm, densely setulose externally; filaments pink, very shortly monadelphous at base, exserted 8-10 mm. Pod (only immature pods seen) a flat plano-compressed craspedium apparently breaking up into one-seeded articles, 1-5 per capitulum, subsessile, 7.7 x 1.1 cm (largest pods seen but not fully mature), 3-9- seeded, the articles puberulous, more densely so in center and here with scattered glandular setae, 8-9 x 9 mm, the replum 0.5 mm wide, puberulous with scattered glandular hairs. Seeds not seen. (Fig. 3).

description: Tree ca. 35 m tall, 45 cm diam. at breast height. Bole cylindrical, with 7-8 short buttresses. Bark white. Leaves opposite, simple; petiole 1 cm; blade elliptic to ovate, entire, chartaceous, glabrous, 8-12.5 X 4- 6 cm, base acute or obtuse, apex acuminate; venation brochidodromous, the major lateral veins forming a looping marginal vein 3 mm from the margin except the basalmost lateral vein, which terminates at the margin; midvein sulcate adaxially, raised abaxially; major lateral veins raised abaxially, 3-4(- 6) pairs, 1-2.5 cm apart, inconspicuous adaxially, the basal pair inserted near the petiole and decurrent, the upper lateral nerves nearly patent. Inflorescence racemose, rachis slender, 3-5 cm long, mostly glabrous or with very sparse simple golden hairs but pubescent at nodes; bracts hemiorbicular, ca. 1 mm long, deciduous, leaving raised scar, opposite scars connected across the rachis by a slight raised ridge; flower buds not seen. Flowers zygomorphic, sweetly scented (at 10 A.M.), opposite; pedicel 1 cm, slender, or flowers sessile. Calyx white, sepals 5, fused basally to the inferior ovary, glabrous except for a somewhat sparse fringe of simple golden hairs along the edge; three larger sepals elliptic, the dorsal (uppermost) larger sepal with a red-speckled, pale yellow band along the midrib, sepals somewhat membranous and transparent when dried, 7-10 X 2.5-3 mm, midrib and 6-7 parallel veins somewhat conspicuous, very conspicuous in dried ma- terial; two smaller sepals deltoid-elliptic, green at the base, 1 mm long; spur of fourth sepal cylindric, straight, white, 2-4 X 1- 1.5 mm, tip rounded, greenish or brownish. Corolla white, petals 5, free, readily decid- uous, glabrous, clawed, elliptic, similar in shape to the large sepals but slightly nar- rower, 9.5 X 1.5-2.5 mm, apex subacumi- nate, transparent in dried material. Androe- cium of one fertile stamen inserted at the top of the ovary; filament straight or slight- ly curved, 2-3 X 0.5 mm, glabrous; anther sagittate, 2 mm long, glabrous, connective broad, purple. Staminodes not observed. Ovary inferior, unilocular, glabrous; ovule 1, inserted laterally; style straight or slightly curved, slightly tapered, 3 X 0.5 mm; stigma lateral, oval, 0.5 mm, wet. Fruit inde- hiscent, winged, the body turbinate, ca. 1.5 X 1.5 cm, the 5 wings formed by the accrescent growth of the sepals, three wings large, two small, reflecting the proportions of the sepals; larger wings oblanceolate, 4.5-5 X ca. 1.7 cm.
