description: Evergreen shrubs or small trees to 10 m high; young twigs slightly quadrangular, becoming terete with age, with an indumentum of multicellular multiseriate setae, inconspicuous, sparse stellate hairs, and sessile glandular hairs, the stellate hairs (0.06-)0.08-0.19(-0.25) mm diam., twigs finally glabrous; nodes (2.87-)3.47-5 (-7.67) mm diam., a slightly expanded, inconspicuous interpetiolar ridge present, with sparse to dense multicellular multiseriate setae, the hairs (0.41-)0.8-1.4(-2.07) mm long. Leaf blade coriaceous, ovate to widely elliptic, suborbiculate or orbiculate, (3.4-)4.4-6.8(-9) X (3.2-)3.4-5.2(-8.3) cm, slightly revolute abaxially, apex obtuse, the tip (acute) acuminate; base obtuse and cordate, adaxial surface of young blades with stellate hairs, some slightly sunken in pits and appearing as punctations, and few sessile-glandular hairs (unicellular hairs and multicellular uniseriate hairs), mature leaves with sessile glandular hairs, which are the aged remains of the central stalk and disc of stellate hairs, densest near base and generally appearing as minute punctations, sometimes slightly sunken in pits, sparse stellate hairs and unicellular hairs, abaxial surface of young blades with stellate hairs (0.06-)0.09-0.19(-0.24) mm diam. and sessile-glandular pubescence (0.06-)0.08- 0.11(-0.12) mm diam., with few multicellular uniseriate hairs mostly restricted to midrib, mature leaves with minute punctate-like bases of aged stellate hairs, these frequently slightly sunken in pits, and few stellate hairs, unicellular hairs, and multicellular uniseriate hairs; margin slightly revolute, entire; venation basal with 2 or 3 pairs of secondary veins, and I pair of inconspicuous submarginal secondary veins, the tertiary veins (17-)20-24(-27), intergrading with quaternary veins at base and apex; midrib (slightly raised to flat) impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, the secondary veins (slightly raised to flat) impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, the tertiary veins (slightly raised to flat) impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; the quaternary veins slightly impressed to impressed adaxially, slightly raised to flat or impressed abaxially. Petiole (0.7-)1.2-2.3(-3.6) cm long, canaliculate, moderately pubescent, with multicellular multiseriate hairs, these primarily on the sulcus edges, (0.76-)0.79-1.15(-1.56) mm long. Inflorescence terminal, cymose, loosely corymbose, (3.5-)4.2- 6.8(-9.3) X (2.2-)2.5-3.9(-5.2) cm, with 2-4 orders of branching, the caducous bracts to ca. 2 cm long; peduncle (0.65-) 1.15-2.5(-4.7) cm long, first internode above peduncle (0.85-)0.94-2(-2.3) cm long, first lateral internode (0.81-)1.04-2.1(-2.3) cm long, the flowers (15-)21-38(-45) per inflorescence. Pedicels (2.67-) 3.27-5.6(-8.67) mm long, with stellate hairs (0.03-)0.08-0.18(-0.21) mm diam. and very sparse sessile glandular and unicellular hairs. Hypanthium cylindrical to suborbicular, spreading above ovary, (4-)4.14-4.94(-5.2) mm long as measured from base of hypan- thium to torus, (2.19-)2.5-4.8(-5) mm wide, indumentum of sparse stellate hairs (0.05-)0.06-0.13(-0.18) mm diam. (sessile glandular hairs), the portion of hypanthium free from ovary (1.02-) 1.06-1.38(-1.47) mm long; inner hypanthium smooth (granular textured), torus to calyx apex length (1.66-)1.82-2.38(-2.6) mm, torus to calyx notch length (0.44-)0.47-1.03(-1.32) mm. Calyx lobes 4, (1.13-)1.4-2.13(-2.74) X (3-)3.34-4(-4.34) mm, lobes broadly triangular, the apex acute (acuminate), the indumentum similar to that of hypanthium, the external calyx teeth (0.63-)0.67-0.8(-0.94) mm long, bluntly and broadly rounded. Petals 4, producing nectar in a basal, cuplike depression on the adaxial surface, yellow or red, irregularly wide elliptic to suborbicular; (8.88-)9.5-14.13(-14.63) X (6.63-)6.88-9.38(-10) mm, glabrous, many-veined, imbricate, campanulate and forming a false tube, occasionally shallowly notched at apex. Stamens 8, folded adaxially in bud, in two series, isomorphic, 15-18(-19.5) mm long; filaments cream, slightly tapered toward apex, 12.4-16.6 mm long, with proximal filament segment (0.47-)0.53-1.07 (-1.13) mm wide, distal segment (0.47-) 0.53-0.81(-1) mm wide; anthers yellow, (2.54-)2.6-2.75(-2.91) X (0.66-)0.72- 0.81(-0.95) mm, elliptic, slightly curving, opening by two longitudinal slits (1.84-) 2.04-2.38(-2.47) mm long. Ovary inferior, 4-loculate, (2.44-)2.5-3.27(-3.41) X (1.72-) 2.04-2.32(-2.69) mm, lacking an apical appendage, the placentation deeply intruded axile; style cream, straight to shallowly S- shaped, glabrous, (16-)17-22(-23) X (1-) 1.03-1.07(-1.13) mm; stigma not expanded, papillose. Berries 4-7 mm diam., subglobose to globose, juicy, with persistent calyx lobes. Seeds pyramidal, 0.6-0.8 X ca. 0.4 mm.

description: Herba repens vel scandens. Folia ovato-triangularia valde acuminata. Flores staminati 5-meri, antheris exsertis. description: Scandent monoecious herb, creeping and climbing by tendrils; stems slender, branched, sulcate, glabrous to sparsely villous at the nodes. Leaves simple, thin, membranous to papyraceous, broadly ovate-triangular, 5-7-angulate-lobed, 3.5-17 X 3.3-19.6 cm, the lobes wide, triangular, the central lobe longer than the lateral, strongly acuminate, the margin serrulate-denticulate, both surfaces strigose, abaxial surface with the veins more prominent and the trichomes shorter; petioles 0.7-6 cm long, sulcate, sparsely to densely glandular-villous; tendrils long-stalked, 2.6-10 cm long, sulcate, 3-6-branched, sparsely to densely glandular-villous. Staminate inflorescence in the same axil as the pistillate, panicles, racemes of umbels, or a combination of both, 7.6-40.5 cm long, erect; peduncle 6.2-22.7 cm long; rachis densely glandular-pubescent toward the apex; pedicels slender, 2.9-10.6 mm long, ascendant, densely glandular-pubescent villous; flower receptacle 5-merous, narrowly campanulate, 0.6-2 mm long, 0.8-3 mm wide; calyx lobes subulate, 0.2-0.4 mm long; corolla greenish yellow, 5-merous, the lobes triangular, 1-3 X 0.5-2 mm, the margins and adaxial surface densely glandular-villous; stamens fused into a column 2.5-4.7 mm long, the filaments forming a central column, the anthers united forming a globose head, the thecae curved. Pistillate inflorescence umbelliform; peduncle 1-2.2 cm long, elongating to 5.5 cm in fruit, densely glandular-villous. Pistillate flowers numerous; ovary unilocular, ovoid, slightly rostrate, armed, densely glandular-pubescent villous; ovule 1, occupying almost the entire locule; receptacle and perianth smaller than those of the staminate flowers; corolla with 5-7 petals; column of style and stigma 2.5 mm long; stigmas conspicuously exserted, 3-4-lobed, the lobes rounded to ovoid, reflexed. Fruits numerous, dry, 0.8-1 cm long, 0.3-0.6 cm in diameter, triangular-ovoid, slightly rostrate, densely armed except for the rostrum; fruit wall thin, strongly attached to the seed, light to dark brownish; spines 2-6.3 mm long, acicular, antrorse, caducous, retrorsely barbed, yellowish. Seed ovoid, compressed, dark brown.

description: Rhizomes erect, ca. 3-4 cm in diameter with petiolar bases, densely scaly, scales orange-brown, translucent, linear, 15-25 x 0.5-1 mm, the margins distally toothed; leaves ascending, to ca. 130 cm long; petioles ca. 55 cm X 3-4 mm, red-brown proximally, becoming stramineous toward the rachises, moderately scaly, the scales of two types, the first type mostly spreading, partly involute, translucent, dark brown with sharply defined, reddish brown, translucent margins, width of the translucent portion increasing from basal scales (0.2 mm) to distal ones (1 mm), ovate-lanceolate with elongate apices, 8-14 X 3-7 mm, margins erose to fibrillose, the second type extending onto rachises and costae, orangebrown, translucent, filiform to long-lanceolate, twisted, 1-6 X 0.05-0.3 mm, margins entire to fibrillose; blades ca. 70 X 25 cm, chartaceaous, deltate, bipinnate, usually bearing a scaly bud in the axil of a distal pinna, free pinnae long-lanceolate, acuminate, ca. 35 pinnate pairs, the longest pinnae the 4th to 8th pair, to 15 cm X 22 mm, proximal pinnae ca. to 1/2 the size of the longest pinnae, apices of all pinnae ascending towards blade apices; pinnules to ca. 22(24) free pairs per pinna plus a pinnatifid apex, to 12 x 8 mm, largest at pinna bases, flat, strongly inequilateral at bases with a large acroscopic lobe, apices acuminate, margins shallowly serrate with distinct spinules on the acroscopic lobe and on the apices, and sometimes on a few other serrations; rachises and costae grooved adaxially, sparsely scaly abaxially, the scales orange-brown, translucent, filiform to long-lanceolate, 1-9 x 0.05-1.5 mm, margins fibrillose; laminar tissue adaxially glabrous, abaxially with scattered, filiform scales to 0.5 X 0.02 mm on the basal veins; sori to 12 per pinnule; indusia lacking.

description: Terrestrial. Rhizome 1-3 mm wide, short-creeping, ascending, scaly, brown, resinous; scales 2-A.5 mm long, lanceolate, brown, entire, the apex acute. description: Woody vine to 7 m. Laminas of the larger leaves 6.5-12.5 X 4-8 cm, elliptical to broadly so to suborbicular, apex apiculate to short-acuminate, base truncate to cordate, becoming coriaceous, adaxially glabrous, abaxially very sparsely sericeous to glabrescent to glabrous, the hairs straight or slightly crisped and sessile, usually reddish, (0.1-)0.3-0.9(-1.1) mm long, with (0-)2(-4) impressed glands near the base and 0- 2(-3) additional glands distally, usually with 2 marginal glands just below the apex; petiole 0.7-2 cm long, sericeous, eglandular; stipules 0.5-0.7 mm long, linear to narrowly triangular, interpetiolar. Inflorescence unit a pseudoraceme of 10-22(-35) flow- ers, borne on an axis 0.8-1.5(-3) cm long, sometimes solitary but usually several ar- ranged in an axillary thyrse. Peduncles 3- 5.5 mm long, 0.3-0.6X as long as pedicels, sericeous; pedicels 8-14 mm long, sparsely sericeous. Bracts 0.8-1.3 X 0.3-0.4 mm, narrowly triangular, eglandular or some- times with an inconspicuous callose area at the base. Bracteoles subequal, 0.4-0.9 X 0.2-0.3 mm, linear or narrowly triangular, eglandular or sometimes with an inconspic- uous callose area at the base; pair of brac- teoles subopposite or sometimes to 0.5 mm apart, inserted at about the middle of the peduncle or sometimes near the apex. Calyx of 4 biglandular lateral sepals and 1 eglan- dular anterior sepal; lateral sepals exceed- ing the glands by ca. 1 mm, the glands ca. 2 mm long, decurrent. Petals 5, yellow, gla- brous, the limb abaxially carinate, eglan- dular; lateral petals: claw 1.5-1.8 X 0.5 mm, limb ca. 6 X 6 mm, orbicular, margin denticulate or sometimes erose; posterior petal: claw 1.8-2 X 0.6 mm, limb 6 X 6 mm, orbicular, margin denticulate-erose. Androecium of 10 subequal stamens; fila- ments 1.5-2.3 mm long, the anterior one the longest, the posterior one the shortest, connate at base; anthers ca. 1.4 mm long, glabrous. Ovary tomentose-sericeous; styles erect or slightly divergent, subequal, 2.3- 2.4 X 0.4 mm, the apex dorsally blunt or rounded. Samara (2.5-)3-4 cm diam., suborbicular to orbicular, the lateral wing continuous at base and at apex except for a distal shallow notch 1-2 mm deep or entirely continuous, sericeous; central dorsal winglet 9-15.5 X 3-5.5 mm, sometimes ex- tended into the apical notch as a spur to 0.8 mm long; nut 4-4.5 mm high; torus ca. 3 mm high, surrounded by a wide, glabrous, 3-lobed, disciform outgrowth of the receptacle.

description: Trunk to 8 m high and 22 cm diam., covered with old spiny, black petiole bases (Fig. 2B), giving the trunk a grooved look. Cleared trunks with large oval frond scars as well as short black, upwardly curved spines, and dark scales like those of the petiole. Trunk apices hidden among young petiole bases. Adventitious buds at the base of the trunk large, growing out to short stolons 0.6-0.8 m long, producing large thickets in favorable places. Frond 180-280 X 60-110 cm. Petiole 35-70 cm long, spiny and with scurf, the spines up to 1.5 cm long, black, with the scurf light brown, vanishing with age; petioles greenish yellow when young, turning brown to dark brown abaxially; yellow color normally persistent at least on the sides. Petiole scales linear to narrowly lanceolate, with crested margins and dark brown central stripe, to 10 mm x 1 mm with one black apical seta, 0.4-1 mm long (Fig. 4F). Rhachis light brown to brown abaxially, yellow adaxially, changing to a purplish brown in full sun, with short black spines in the proximal abaxial part and with evanescent scurf. Leaf axes of the same color, but staying yellow adaxially even in full sun. Laminae bipinnate-pinnatifid, apices abruptly reduced, not pinna-like, or some- times apices gradually reduced. Pinnae short-stalked, the basal ones with the first basiscope pinnules missing; pinnules in sterile, shaded and/or juvenile plants only very short stalked to subsessile, in fertile plants notably short-stalked (Fig. 4A); cos- tae distally green-alate, wings narrow and linear (Fig. 4E, arrow). Pinnules linear with truncate to shallowly cordate bases and acute to short acuminate apices; segments slightly falcate, margins finely serrate at least at their tip (Fig. 4B). Indument of lamina of small yellow- to light brown scales (Fig. 4C) with some darker stripes and one to several marginal setae, of many ciliate squamules (Fig. 4G), and uni- and multicellular hairs of light brown color, especially well developed along the costules and larger veins. Sterile veins simple, rarely forked; fertile veins forked or simple. Sori costal (Fig. 4C); indusia discoid to shallowly cyatheoid (Fig. 4D), hardly visible in entire sori, with entire margins and some white, septate hairs (Fig. 4D), these often broken off in mature ones. Paraphyses as long as the sporangia, tufted at the tip of the slightly columnar receptacle (Fig. 4C, D). Spores trilete, perispore in granules or in ridges.

description: Herb on forest floor, to 1.2 m tall. Stem ascending, quadrangular, pilose, the trichomes sordid to yellowish, erect to spreading, 1 mm long. Leaf blades elliptic to oblong to narrowly ovate, 15-25 X 6-11 cm, light green, short-acuminate, attenuate at base, thin and membranous, entire or slightly undulate; upper surface dark green when dry, sparingly sericeous, the trichomes appressed; mid and lateral veins (6-7 pairs) rather obscure above, more prominent on lower surface; cystoliths minute, often obscure on both surfaces; lower surface a lighter yellow green when dry, moderately sericeous, especially on venation, the trichomes appressed and spreading, sordid, to 2 mm long; petioles short or lacking, if present then 5 mm long, sparingly pilose. Inflorescences of terminal spikes, these long- pedunculate, usually paired, 8-15 cm long and 1-1.5 cm broad; peduncles long, 7-16 cm long, these and the rachis subquadrangular, moderately pilose and puberulous; bracts green, heteromorphic; larger bract slightly imbricate, obovate to suborbicular, 8-9 X 7-8 mm, rounded and minutely apiculate at apex with apicula less than 0.25 mm long, abruptly narrowed and cuneate at base, thin, the mid vein and lateral veins rather prominent, both surfaces dotted with glands, pubescent along mid vein, the margin conspicuously ciliate; sterile bract greatly reduced, linear, 6-7 X 0.4-0.6 mm; bracteoles linear, 6 X 0.5 mm, apically long-aristate, puberulous, the margin ciliolate. Flowers sessile to subsessile; calyx 5- lobed, 5.5-6 mm long, the lobes equal, linear-lanceolate, 5-5.5 X 0.5 mm, apically aristate, glabrous, the margin ciliolate; corolla white, 22-22.5 mm long, puberulous and dotted with glands; tube narrowly cylindrical, 19-19.5 mm long, 2 mm diam. at base, enlarged to 3 mm at 2.5 mm above base, then slightly constricted, 2.5 mm wide at mouth, the limb relatively short compared to the long corolla tube, the upper lip erect, narrowly ovate, 5 X 1.75-2 mm, 2- lobed, the lobes 0.5 X 0.5 mm, the lower lip spreading, 4 mm long, the lobes 2 mm long, all narrowly ovate and apically rounded; stamens exserted 4 mm beyond mouth of corolla tube, the anther lobes superposed, subequal, vertically attached to connective, the lower lobe inconspicuously apiculate, the filaments flattened; pistil ± equaling stamens, the stigma bilobed, minute and rounded, the style glabrous. Capsule clavate, 15 X 4 X 3 mm, puberulous, the stipe 6 mm long, the head ovoid to subspheric to ellipsoid-obovoid, often with slight medial constriction, 9 mm long, apically apiculate. Seeds 4, dark reddish brown, lenticular to subspheric, 3 X 2 X 1 mm, the surface and margin covered with knoblike papillae.

description: Herb or creeping herb, 10-30 cm tall. Roots yellowish. Leaf blades elliptic to narrowly ovate, 10-15 cm long and 2.8-5.6 cm wide, acute to acuminate or short-acuminate at apex, attenuate at base, moderately firm, entire or undulate; upper surface dark green when dry, sparingly sericeous, the trichomes appressed; mid and lateral veins (8-10 pairs) rather obscure above, more prominent on lower surface; cystoliths minute, often obscure on both surfaces; lower surface yellowish green when dry, moderately sericeous, especially on venation, the trichomes appressed and spreading, sordid, to 2 mm long; petioles short, 0.5-1 cm long, densely sericeous. Flowers sessile to subsessile; calyx 5-lobed, 6.5-8 mm long, the lobes hyaline, equal, linear-lanceolate, 6-7.5 X 0.5 mm, apically aristate with a tuft of trichomes, otherwise glabrous; corolla white to pinkish, 10-14 mm long, glabrous except the limb which is sparingly puberulous; tube cylindrical, 7-10 mm long, 1-1.5 mm diam. at base, enlarged to 1.5-2 mm at 1-2 mm above base, then slightly constricted and 2-2.5 mm wide at mouth, the upper lip erect, 2-lobed, narrowly ovate, 3 X 2 mm, apically obtuse to retuse, the lower lip erect or spreading, 3-5 mm long, the lobes 2 X 1.75-2 mm, all obovate and apically rounded; stamens exserted 3 mm beyond mouth of corolla tube, the anther lobes superposed, subequal, vertically attached to connective, lower lobe inconspicuously apiculate, the filaments flattened; pollen grains 2-porate, prolate to perprolate, 41 X 20 µm, the pores circular, the membrane reticulate, the trema area studded with 4 rows of 8-10, ± circular insulae (Fig. 2); pistil ± equaling the stamens, the stigma bilobed, minute and rounded, the style glabrous. description: Erect perennial herb or subshrub, 0.3-0.5 m tall, rooting at the nodes. Stem subquadrate, sulcate, pilosulous, the trichomes decussate, erect and recurved or adpressed, sordid. Leaf blades occasionally anisophyllous, elliptic to broadly lanceolate to narrowly ovate, 4-7 X 2-2.7 cm, acute to acuminate at apex, acute to attenuate at base, moderately firm, entire or undulate; upper surface dark green when dry, minutely and inconspicuously puberulous; mid and lateral veins (4-6 pairs) rather obscure above, somewhat more prominent on lower surface; cystoliths minute, often obscure on both surfaces; lower surface drying a lighter green; young blades often reddish to purple below, ± glabrate to sparingly puberulous, the mid vein sparingly pilosulous; petioles short, 3-5 mm long, pilosulous, the trichomes appressed, sordid. Inflorescences of terminal and axillary spikes, these usually solitary or paired, erect, lax, sometimes violet, pedunculate, 3.5-7 cm long and 0.5 cm broad without corollas or capsules; peduncles short, 4-15 mm long, these and the rachis subquadrangular, pilosulous; bracts green, not imbricate, decussate, narrowly lanceolate, 3.5-4 X 0.75 mm, apically mucronulate, glabrate to sparingly puberulous with both eglandular and glandular trichomes, the margin ciliolate; bracteoles linear, 3.5-4 X 0.5 mm, the vestiture similar to that of bracts. Flowers sessile, opposite, in pairs or solitary and accompanied by a rudimentary second flower in axil of bracts; calyx 5-lobed? 4 lobes subequal, narrowly lanceolate, 4 0.5-0.75 mm, the posterior lobe reduced, filiform, 2.5-3 mm long, all lobes glabrate or sparingly puberulous with a mixture of both eglandular and glandular trichomes, the margins ciliolate; corolla white to pale mauve, 11-13(-14) mm long, minutely and sparingly puberulous; tube cylindrical, 6-8 mm long, 0.5 mm diam at base, slightly enlarged to 1.25 mm at 1 mm above base, then slightly constricted and gradually enlarged to 2 mm wide at mouth, the upper lip erect, 2-lobed, narrowly ovate, 5-6 X 1.5-2 mm, apically entire, the lower lip ± erect, 5.5 mm long, the lobes oblong to narrowly obovate, apically rounded, the limb with conspicuous violet striations; stamens exserted 3-4 mm beyond mouth of corolla, the anther lobes superposed, subequal, vertically attached to connective, not conspicuously apiculate, the filaments flattened; pistil equaling the stamens, the stigma minute, bilobed, the style minutely puberulous. Capsule clavate, 7-7.5 X 2 X 1.5 mm, puberulous, especially the head, the stipe 3 mm long, the head ovoid to spheric to ellipsoid-obovoid, often with a slight medial constriction, 4-4.5 mm long, apically minutely apiculate. Seeds 4 or 2 by abortion, reddish brown, subspheric, 2 X 1.75 X 1 mm, the surface and margin covered with knoblike papillae.

description: Herba vel suffrutex; caulibus erectis, quadrangularibus, dense puberulis, foliorum lamina oblonga vel lanceolata, acuta vel acuminata, basi attenuata, firma, utrinque glabra praeter venatia; petioli puberuli; spicae binae, terminales et axillares, pedunculis et rachidibus subquadrangularibus, dense puberulis; bracteae rubellus-brunneae, spatulatae, dense hirtellae, ciliolatae; bracteolae subaequaliae, anguste spatulatae, dense hirtellae, ciliatae; calycis segmenta aequalia, anguste triangulares, parce hirtellae; corolla pallens lavandula, mox cadens, infra glabra, sursum parce puberula, tubo cylindrico, labio superiore erecto, anguste ovato vel triangulares, minute bilobato, labio inferiore trilobato, lobis patulis, anguste obovatis; stamina exserta; lobi antherarum superpositi.

description: Herb or subshrub to 75 cm tall. Stem erect, ascending, quadrangular, densely puberulent, the trichomes sordid, upwardly appressed, 0.25 mm long. Leaf blades oblong to lanceolate, 9-12 X 2.5-3.5 cm, acute to acuminate at apex, the tip obtuse, attenuate at base, moderately firm, the margin entire or somewhat undulate; upper surface dark green when dry, glabrous except sparingly puberulous with short, sordid trichomes along the midvein; lower surface a light green when dry, glabrous except venation which is minutely appressed puberulent with sordid trichomes; mid and lateral veins (4-6 pairs) conspicuous; cystoliths minute, often obscure on both surfaces; petioles 10-20 mm long, minutely and densely puberulous, the trichomes sordid and appressed. Infiorescence of terminal and axillary spikes, these in pairs, densely bracteate, 2-6 cm long and 0.5-1 cm broad, bearing solitary flowers in nodes; peduncles 10-12 mm long, these and the rachis subquadrangular, densely puberulous with both eglandular and glandular trichomes; bracts decussate, imbricate, reddish brown when dry, spatulate, 9-11 X 2-2.5 mm, densely hirtellous with both eglandular and glandular trichomes, the margin ciliolate; bracteoles subequal, narrowly spatulate, 8-9 X 1.5 mm, densely hirtellous, the margin ciliolate. Flowers sessile; calyx 5-lobed, 7 mm long, the lobes subequal, narrowly triangular, 5-6 X 1 mm, sparingly hirtellous, the margin ciliolate; corolla pale lavender, soon falling, 9-10 mm long, the lower portion of the tube glabrous, the upper portion (enlarged part) and the limb sparingly puberulous; tube cylindrical, 6 mm long, 1-1.25 mm diam. at base, slightly enlarged to 2 mm at 1-1.5 mm above base, then slightly constricted and gradually enlarged to 3 mm wide at mouth, the upper lip erect, narrowly ovate to triangular, 3-4 X 2.5 mm, apically minutely bilobed, the lower lip partially spreading to erect, 3-4 mm long, the lobes oblong to narrowly obovate, delicately veined, apically rounded and ciliolate; stamens exserted 4 mm beyond mouth of corolla, the anther lobes superposed, subequal, vertically attached to connective, apiculate (the lower lobe more conspicuously so), the filaments flattened; pistil ± equaling the stamens, the stigma subcapitate, minutely bilobed or rounded, the style glabrous. Capsule clavate, 9-10 X 3 X 2 mm, puberulous, the stipe 5 mm long, the head ovoid to subspheric to ellipsoid-obovoid, 4-5 mm long, apically apiculate. Seeds 4 or fewer by abortion, dark reddish brown, lenticular to subspheric, 2.5 X 2 X 1 mm, the surface and margin glabrous or covered with knoblike papillae.

description: Herba aquatilis, annua, caespitosa, culmis fasciculatis, erectis vel decumbentibus. Vaginae foliares membranaceae, apice acutae. Spicula ovata, obtusa vel subacuta, glumis floriferis ovatis, viridibus vel stramineis, apice et lateribus hyalinis, setis perigonialibus 5-6, staminibus 3. Achaenium 0.9-1(-1.1) mm longum (cum styli basi), 0.6-0.7 mm latum, obovoideum, biconvexum, basi breviter subconstrictum, tuberculo parvo, minuscule apiculato, 0.1-0.15 mm longo, ca. 0.15- 0.35 mm lato.
bibliographicCitation: González-Elizondo, M. Socorro, et al. 2005. An arsenic-tolerant new species of Eleocharis (Cyperaceae) from Chihuahua, Mexico. Brittonia. 57 (2): 150-154.

description: Aquatic, soft-tissued tufted annual herb with slender, delicate, ascendant rootstocks, the roots fibrous, whitish; roots in juvenile plants often with delicate, fusiform, starchy tubers 2-3.5 X 0.8-1.2 mm, covered by persistent red-purple bracts. Culms erect when young but flaccid and reclining at anthesis and then the entire plant covered by mud, very rarely erect when mature. The erect and reclining stages usually submerged in water (only one emergent clump has been observed); mature culms 20-34 (-40) cm X 0.6-1.1 mm (to 1.5 mm wide when flattened); juvenile culms very delicate, translucid, soft, as little as 0.3 mm wide, irregularly flattened and often sulcate when dried, obtusely 4-angled near summit, bright to pale green, whitish at the base; culms of seedlings translucent green, irregularly septate (transverse septa not complete), and minutely pellucid-dotted. Sheaths oblique apically, not inflated, proximal sheaths firm or decaying, the apex acute, usually fragile and fugacious; distal sheaths membranous, hyaline, tapered to an acute apex, the mouth concave, or the sheath splitting ventrally and becoming loose and withered on drying, some sheaths prolonged into a bladelike portidn to 3.6 cm long and abruptly tapered for 1-1.2 mm at the acute, minutely mucronate apex. Spikelets ovoid, 2.7-4.1(-5) X 1.6-2.2 mm, obtuse to subacute, ca. 12-40-flowered; floral scales polystichous, appressed or subappressed, (1.3-)1.6-2 x 0.4-0.7 mm in lateral view, ovate, obtuse, medially chartaceous, green to stramineus, laterally membranous, translucid, the margins and apex scarious, colorless, gradually hyaline, the two proximal scales without flowers, not amplexicaulous, 1.5-2 mm long. Achene body 0.7-0.8 x 0.6-0.7 mm (0.9-1(-1.1) mm long including the base and rostrum), biconvex, not to slightly plump, obovoid, dark brown to nearly black, finely reticulate and very finely striolate, lustrous; rostrum depressed and apiculate or depressed-conic, not spongy to slightly spongy, whitish, 0.1-0.15 X 0.15-0.35 mm, slightly constricted at the base, the sides slightly wider than the top of the achene. Perianth of 5-6 erect bristles appressed to achene, 0.4-1 mm long, reddish, retrorsely spinulose, the spinules translucid, colorless, proximally slightly flattened, the disc to 0.15 mm high at the base of the achene. Style bifid. Stamens 3, filaments translucid, anthers yellow, thecae 0.4-0.5 mm long, the connective not prolonged.

description: Epiphytic; rhizomes 4-8 mm in diam., compact; rhizome scales 15-25(-35)x0.7- 1.2 mm, linear, concolorous, pink-gold to orange, flat, lustrous, with entire margin; fronds (40-) 11 8-1 72 cm long, approximate; stipes 5-16 cm long, (l/7-)l/10- 1/15 of the frond length, stramineous; stipe scales 4- 7 mm long, subulate, gold to brown, sparse, patent, with entire to denticulate margin, mixed with hairs of 0.3-0.7 mm long, gold, with clávate or acute apex; blades (35- )1 10 - 155 x 3.7-5.5 cm, linear-oblanceolate, charta- ceous, narrowly cunéate at the base, acute to acuminate at the apex; costal scales 3-6 mm long, similar to stipe scales, mixed with dense hairs similar to stipe hairs; abaxial blade scales 2-3 mm long, subulate, gold to light brown, sparse, curved to appressed, with entire margin, mixed with dense and gold hairs; adaxial blade scales similar, but com- monly darker, hairs absent; margin scales same as adaxial scales but more dense; hydathodes absent; fertile fronds 25-35 cm long; stipes 5-11 cm long, 1/4-1/3 of the frond length; fertile blades 18-26 x 1.8- 2.6 cm, narrowly elliptic to narrowly oblan- ceolate, cunéate at the base, acute at the apex; intersporangial scales absent.

description: Herba basi lignescens; caule simplici, medullosa, ad 1.1 m alta. Petiolus 3-5 cm longus. Lamina chartacea, (anguste) obovata, 17-31 X 7-11.5 cm, 5(-7)-nervata. Flores axillares, solitarii, 3-5 mm longe pedicellati; calyx 10 mm longus, tubo ca. 2 mm longo, lobis ovato- ellipticis, ca. 8.5 mm longis; corolla lutea, hypocrater- iformis, 50 mm longa, tubo 40 mm longo, lobis ovatis, 10 mm longis; stamina ad 5 mm basin tubi affixa; grana pollinis magna, sine extensionibus lateralibus, index areae polaris (PAI) magnus; ovarium anguste ovoideum, 5 mm longum, stylo 32 mm longo. Fructus ignotus.

description: Herb to 1.1 m tall; stem unbranched, quadrangular with thick ridges at "corners," pithy, woody at base, 0.7 cm diam., internodes ca. 6 cm long. Petioles 3-5 cm long, forming at the base an ochrea (with resin- producing colleters on the inside) around the stem from which the flowers arise; blades chartaceous, (narrowly) obovate, 17-31 X 7-11.5 cm, 5(-7)-veined, pairs of veins sometimes conspicuously uneven, second (upper) pair branching in the lower 1/2 to 1/3 of blade, apex acuminate, base at- tenuate (sometimes asymmetric). Flowers solitary in leaf axil; pedicel 3-5 mm long; calyx 1 cm long, connate approx. Y5 of length, lobes 5, conspicuously ridged, ovate-elliptic, ca. 8.5 x 6 mm, margin slightly erose, rounded, base overlapping, 1 mm long colleters in a single crescent on inner base of calyx lobes; corolla yellow, tubular to funnel-shaped, 50 mm long, tube 40 mm long, lobes 5, ovate, 10 x 6.5-7.5 mm, margin very slightly erose, apex acuminate with a conspicuous thickening just below apex; stamens 5, unequal in length, inserted 5 mm from base of corolla tube, filaments 29-34 mm long, longest one approx. equal to style/stigma in length, as long as corolla tube, anthers white, 3.5 mm long; pollen 3-zonocolporate, usually oblate spheroidal or spheroidal, polar axis ca. 40-45 µm, no or unclear lateral extensions of the endoaperature, costae thin, polar area index (PAI) >0.30 (ectocolpi relatively short), very coarsely reticulate, lumina of reticulum in polar area not or barely smaller than in mesocolpium, lumina decreasing in size toward the colpi; ovary narrowly ovoid to ovoid, 5 X 2-2.5 mm, basal glands 0.8 mm high, style 32 mm long, stigma green, bilamellate, 2.5 mm long. Fruit unknown.

description: Rhizomes ca. 1 mm wide, erect to ascending, polystichous, scaly, the scales 1-1.5 mm long, orange, concolorous, ascending, margin entire to sparsely denticulate; phyllopodia absent; fronds 1-3(-3.5) cm long, 0.3-0.7 cm wide, fasciculate, the sterile spreading, the fertile erect; petioles ca. half the sterile frond length, moderately scaly and glandular, the scales 1-2 mm long, orange, patent, denticulate, the glands 0.1-0.2 mm long, capitate; blades spatulate to elliptic, apices obtuse, bases abruptly narrowed, moderately scaly and glandular on both surfaces, the scales 2-2.5 mm long, orange to dark orange-brown, widely spreading, the glands 0.1-0.2 mm long, capitate; veins not visible; hydathodes present; fertile fronds equaling or slightly shorter than the sterile ones, erect; petioles ca. 4/5 the fertile frond length; blades 1-2 mm wide, orbicular or nearly so, flat (not conduplicate), scaly adaxially, the scales 2-2.5 mm long, denticulate, widely spreading, generally darker than those on the sterile fronds; intersporangial scales lacking.

description: Herba decumbens; folia ad apicem caulis rosulata, decurrentia, margine obscure serrata; inflorescentia erecta; bracteae foliaceae; sepala apice glandulosa; corolla candida, campanulata, ecalcarata, lobis emarginatis; stamina 4, brevia, staminodium parvum.

description: Saxicolous herbs. Stems 10-30 cm long, semiwoody, terete, decumbent, strigose, unbranched, with a few long adventitious roots. Leaves opposite, crowded at apex of stem; blade subsessile, thin, oblanceolate, 7-15 X 3-6 cm; apex acute to obtuse; base long-decurrent; margin obscurely serrate; adaxial side green, with appressed soft hairs, much denser and matted at vein branching; abaxial side paler, with shorter and denser pubescence than seen adaxially; petiole very short or lacking. Inflorescences erect, pedunculate, cymose, few- to many-flowered; peduncles 1.5-4 cm long, erect, densely hirsute to glabrescent; bracts foliaceous, 10-30 X 5-10 mm; pedicels 2-5 cm long, hirsute to glabrous. Calyx actinomorphic; lobes free nearly to base, lanceolate, 7-10 X 2-4 mm, the margin entire, the apex tip hardened (glandular?), hirsute out- side, glabrescent inside. Corolla erect, white; tube campanulate, 5-6 mm long, slightly contracted at throat, with minute pubescence; lobes subequal, oblique and recurved near middle, the ventral lobe spreading, obovate, 3-4 X 3 mm, minutely ciliate, emarginate; stamens 4, included, inserted at base of corolla, free; filaments 1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ovate, 1.5-1.7 X 1.2 mm; staminode 0.5-0.8 mm long, without anther; nectary lacking; ovary globose, 4- 5 mm long, glabrous; style 2-3 mm long, glabrous; stigma slightly capitate. Capsules ovoid, apiculate, 5-6 X 4 mm, glabrous, the style persistent; seeds elliptic, 0.3-0.4 X 0.1-0.2 mm, brown.

description: Herba rupicola; caulis debilis, decumbens; folia bullata, obovata, basi inaequalia; sepala spathulata; corolla coccinea, calcarata, tubo cylindrico, limbo obliquo; stamina basi connata, staminodium dorsale, minutum; glans dorsalis; ovarium tomentosum.

description: Saxicolous herb. Stems 5-10 cm long, decumbent, sappy, terete, hirsute, rooting and branching at nodes. Leaves opposite, unequal in a pair, the larger blade 1.5-5 times (or more) larger than the smaller one, obovate, 6-15 X 3-6 cm; apex round to obtuse, blunt; base asymmetrically acute to rounded; margin crenate to widely serrate; surface bullate; adaxial side hirsute-floccose, with hairs in groups of 3-7 on the bullae, each hair borne on an individual peak or 2-3 on lobed ridges on a bulla, medium green with silvery white to yellowish green area around the midrib; abaxial side hirsute on the veins, with narrow invagi- nations that correspond to the peaks and ridges of the other side; petiole 1.5-10 cm long, hirsute; smaller leaf blade elliptic to obovate, 1-7 X 0.7-4 cm, the petiole 0.7- 3 cm long. Inflorescences axillary, cymose, 2-8-flowered, short-pedunculate and brac- teate, or flowers solitary; peduncles 0.2-0.5 cm long, hirsute; bracts obovate, up to 1 X 0.3 cm; pedicels hirsute, 1-3.5 cm long. Calyx lobes free to base, green, hirsute; dor- sal lobe spreading, linear to oblanceolate, 5-6 X 1.5 mm, entire; apex narrow-round- ed; base narrow; other lobes erect, spathu- late, 10 X 3-4 mm, with 2 glandular teeth distally, the apex truncate to wide-rounded between teeth, the base narrow. Corolla strongly oblique in calyx, red, 3-4 cm long; tube straight, narrow-cylindric, 1.7-3 cm long, long-hirsute outside, short strigose in- side, with glabrous short-conical (2 X 1.5 mm) spur at base, 2 mm wide at base, 1.5 mm wide above base, slightly and gradually inflating to 2-3 mm wide throat; limb oblique, 2-2.5 cm wide; lobes suborbicular, 5-7 X 5-9 mm, the lateral lobes entire, the dorsal lobes serrate, the ventral lobe serrate and emarginate; stamens included, inserted near corolla base, connate at base; filaments glabrous, contorted after pollen is shed; anthers coherent in a tetrad, orbicular; dorsal staminode minute, less than 0.2 mm, glabrous; nectary reduced to a dorsal gland, entire, less than 1 mm long, rounded at apex, glabrous; ovary small, conical, oblique in the calyx, 1.5-2 X 0.8-1 mm, with ascendent, long and wavy pubescence; style glabrous, 18-20 mm long; stigma slightly bilobed, papillose. Capsule globose (probably somewhat laterally flattened), 6 X 5 mm, with scattered hairs; seeds brown, diagonally striate, ellipsoid, 0.6-0.8 X 0.3- 0.4 mm.

description: Epiphytic subshrub. Stems 30 cm long or more, sappy, becoming sarmentose, hanging obliquely, terete, hirsute, branched at base, with some long adventitious roots at nodes (Boom & Samuels 8990). Leaves strongly unequal in a pair, appearing alternate by reduction of one leaf per pair, the larger leaves short-petiolate; blade chartaceous, elliptic to oblanceolate, 3.5-8 X 0.8- 2 cm; apex blunt or acute to acuminate; base cuneate to rounded, usually asymmetric; margin serrate to dentate; adaxial side strigose; abaxial side reddish, villous; petiole 2-7 mm long, hirsute; smaller leaves stipule-like, mostly linear or narrowly elliptic, 2-12 mm including a short petiole, occasionally up to 1/2 the size of the other leaf and then with full-size petiole and subor- bicular blade. Inflorescences axillary, with flowers solitary in larger leaf axils; pedicels hirsute, 1.7-2 cm long. Calyx reddish, the lobes free; 4 lobes erect, lanceolate, 12-18 X 3-5 mm, entire to obscurely 3-5-toothed, acute to acuminate, narrower at base, hirsute inside and outside; dorsal lobe spreading, 10-15 X 2-3 mm. Corolla oblique, cream colored, yellow in throat; tube short-cylindric, slightly widening from base to throat, ca. 2 cm long, outside hirsute, inside minutely verrucose at throat, spurred at base; spur shorter than wide, the ventral lobe not seen, the other lobes rounded, 3 X 4-5 mm, repand at margin; stamens included (?), inserted near base of corolla; filaments connate at base, glabrous; anthers orbicular, each dehiscent by a distal pore (or from a weak area?); staminode not seen; nectary reduced to a dorsal gland, ca. 1.5 mm long, tongue-shaped, curved around back of base of ovary, entire, glabrous; ovary ovoid, 2.5 X 1.5 mm, densely covered with long ascending hairs; style 10-12 mm long, drying flat, glabrous; stigma slightly capitate. Capsule (immature) globose, 5-6 mm diam.; seeds not seen.

description: Epiphytic herbaceous climber. Stems 20 cm or more long, sappy, becoming sarmentose, radicant or pendent, terete, hirsute, branched, with spreading adventitious roots produced along a single line at and between nodes on the side of the stem facing the substrate. Leaves opposite, short-petiolate, equal in a pair; blade succulent, drying chartaceous, lanceolate to rarely oblanceolate, usually one side broader than the other with the midrib straight to slightly curved, 4-5 X 2-2.5 cm, the apex acute, the base rounded to slightly cordate, the margin crenate and ciliate, the adaxial side appressed-pubescent to glabrescent with a few short rigid hairs mostly on the impressed veins, the abaxial side appressed-pubescent on the impressed veins, glabrous between the veins; petiole 0.5-1 cm long, hirsute. Inflo- rescence axillary, 1-4-flowered; peduncles lacking or short, 0.1-0.2 cm long; bracts when present linear, 4 X 0.1 mm, hirsute, entire, rounded at apex; pedicels 0.5-1 cm long, hirsute; calyx lobes free, erect, sube- qual, narrow-lanceolate, 7-10 X 1-2 mm, with 1-4 obscure teeth, with acute apex, hirsute outside, strigose inside, the dorsal lobe slightly curved around corolla spur. Corolla oblique, cream colored; tube short, slightly infundibuliform, 10-13 mm long, with rounded (ca. 2 X 2 mm) spur at base, 3 mm wide above base, 5-6 mm wide at throat, hirsute outside (especially above middle), glabrous inside; limb zygomor- phic, spreading; lobes rounded, glabrous; lateral lobes 2 X 1.5 mm; dorsal lobes 2 X 3 mm; ventral lobe 4 x 4 mm, long-fimbriate, the fimbriae narrow-triangular at base, then filiform, flexuous, 3-7 mm long; stamens slightly exserted, inserted near corolla base; filaments glabrous, 4 connate at base; anthers coherent (?)in tetrads, orbicular, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; staminode filiform, 3 mm long, without anther; nectary glabrous, reduced to a bilobed dor- sal gland, ca. 1 X 1 mm; ovary ellipsoid, 3 X 2.5 mm, densely covered with long ascending hairs; style 7-9 mm long, glabrous; stigma capitate. Fruits and seeds not seen.

description: Shrubs or trees, to 14 m high. Year-old branchlets brown or reddish brown, rarely grayish; new branchlets green or yellowish becoming brown or reddish brown. Expanded leaf blades elliptic to obovate, (3-) 4.5-8.5(-12) X (1.3-)1.9-3.2(-4.8) cm, entire or sometimes serrulate or crenulate, sparsely pubescent to glabrate adaxially, densely (sparsely) silver-sericeous and usually glaucous abaxially, veins not prominently raised abaxially; petioles 3-16 mm long; stipules 0-15 mm long, generally deciduous except on vigorous shoots. Aments mostly  subprecocious, sometimes coetaneous. Staminate aments 1.5-4(-7) cm long, on leafy branchlets to 0.6(-1) cm long; stamens solitary; anthers 0.6-0.8 mm long. Pistillate aments (1.5-)2.2-6.5(-9.5) cm long, on leafy branchlets to 2 cm long. Capsules 3.5-5.6 mm long, pubescent; styles 0.2-1 mm long; stipes 0.4-1.4 mm long. Floral bracts oblanceolate to obovate, 1-2 (-2.5) mm long, mostly brown or tawny, with long, untangled hairs exceeding tip of bract. 2n = 38 (Taylor & Mulligan, 1968).

description: Herba perennis, caulibus dense hirtellis, foliis infimis obovatis; foliis principalibus ellipticis, marginibus hirtellis ad basin integris, apice serratis; inflorescentibis glabris vel glandulosis; sepalis lanceolato-attenuatis integris; corollis ventricosis bilabiatis, antheris naviculatis, staminodiis glabris vel minute barbatis.

description: An erect, perelnnial, somewhat branching herb to 7 dm tall, with a terete stem densely hirtellous (with colorless, flattened, pointed unicellular hairs about 0.5 mm long) up to the inflorescence. The lowest leaves are obovate, the principal leaves elliptical, the largest 40-80 mm long by 20-28 mm wide, basally entire but in the distal half to two-thirds strongly serrate, the mnargins and major veins densely hirtellous and the laminae less densely so; there are minute fascicular leaves on the specimens seen. The inflorescence and its branches are glabrous or very sparingly glandular-pubescent or hirsutulous. The peduncles are aseend- ant-spreading, 10-20 mm long, with two minute lanceolate bracteoles 3-5 mm long, 2- to several-flowered, with pedicels 5-10 mm long. The sepals are narrowly lance-attenuate, entire, glabrous or remotely glandular-pubescent, 8-10 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide. The corolla is ventricose, abruptly inflated above a lnarrow tube about 10 mme long, with a total length of 20-25 mm and width of 8-12 mm (pressed), bilabiate, the upper lip erect, the lower open or spreading, slightly villose on the inner surface. The anthers are included, the sacs divaricate, de- hiseent through the connective, naviculate, with strong central ridges, glabrous and entire, 3 mm long and 1 mm wide. The staminode is dilated distally, glabrous or with a few erect flattened hairs. The capsule is typical for the genus, glabrous, 10 mm long.

description: Herba perennis; caulibus dense puberulentibus, foliis late lanceolatis vel ellipticis, acutis vel acuminatis, mediis marainum serratis, venis marginibusque puberulentibus; inflorescentis glabris vel paulum glandulosis; sepalis lanceolatis attenuatis; corollis abrupte ventricosis; antheris naviculatis; staminodiis minute barbatis.
bibliographicCitation: Straw, Richard M. 1963. The Penstemons of Mexico. III. Two subsection in the section Fasciculus. Brittonia. 15: 49-64.

description: It is probably a perennial herb, at least 4 dm tall, with terete stems densely puberulent up to the inflores- cence with erect flattened hairs about 0.2 mm long. The leaves are broadly lanceolate or more or less elliptical, acute or acuminate, the basal half to one- third and the acuminate tip entire, the remainder of the margin strongly serrate, the veins and margins densely puberulent like the sterni, and the laminae essen- tially glabrous. The largest leaves are 40-60 mm long, 15-25 mm broad, and the axillary fascicles have leaves up to 18 mm long. The infloreseenee is open and spreading, sparingly glandular-pubescent to glabrous above the lowest portion, the lowest bracts little smaller than the leaves, diminishing upward and becoming entire. Peduncles are 18-20 mm long, bibracteolate, (the lanceolate bracteoles to 15 mm long), 2- to 8-flowered, the longest pedicels to 15 mm long and sometimes themselves bibracteolate also. Sepals are narrowly lanceolate, attenuate, spreading, 8-9 mm long, 2-5 mm broad at the base, the basal half or more with a searious, somewhat erose margin. The corolla is broadly ventricose- campanulate, expanding abruptly above the tube of sepal length, 25-28 mm long, 12-15 mm broad (pressed), with the lower lip spreading and somewhat shaggy-villose. The anthers are divaricate, naviculate, with strong median ridges, glabrous, about 3 mm long. The staminode is dilated apically and sparinoly short-bearded.

description: Frutex ramosus 1-3 dm. altus. Caules graciles, 4-angulati, internodiis glabris vel sparsissime setosis, nodis setosis. Petioli 1-3 mm. longi. Laminae tenues, lanceolatae vel oblongo-lanceolatae, 10-17 mm. longae, 3-7 mm. latae, utrinque acutae, supra glabrae vel paucisetosae, subtus sparse setosae praecipue ad venas, levissime crenulatae, conspicuiter ciliolatae, 3-nerviae, venis secundariis obsoletis. Flores 4-meri, flavi, sessiles. Hypanthium 4.5 mm. longum, 8-costulatum, hirsutum setis adscendentibus simplicibus e basibus papillosis. Sepala triangularia, 2.5 mm. longa, seta terminali eglandulosa. Petala ovato-lanceolata, 6 mm. longa, acuminata, seta terminali eglandulosa. Filamenta 6.3 mm. longa; antherae leviter curvatae, 4.1 mm. longae, lineares, basi simplices. Ovarium summo dense hirsutum; stylus 11 mm. longus, stigma punctiforme.
bibliographicCitation: Lasser, Tobias & Maguire, Bassett. 1950. A report on the plant of the Phelps Cerro Yaví expedition of 1947. Brittonia. 7: 75-90.

description: Frutex subramosus, internodiis brevibus, foliis brevissime petiolatis crasse coriaceis confertis parvis obovatis saepissime glanduloso-ciliatis, floribus 4-meris solitariis brevissime pedicellatis; hypanthio anguste campanulato glabro; calycis tubo et lobis subulatis glanduloso-ciliatis; connectivo antheraruin non curvato; ovario 2-loculare semi-infero.

description: Stem woody, slender, marked with swollen leaf-sears, glabrous to thinly pubeseent, the internodes 6-10 mm. long. Petioles very stout, transversely rugose, 1-2 mm. long, glabrous to densely villous. Blades very thick and leathery, ascending or almost appressed, obovateoblong, 8-12 mm. long, 5-8 mm. wide, at apex obtuse to rounded or subtruneate to a minute apiculum, sparsely or densely ciliate or glandular-ciliate, rounded or truncate at base, essentially veinless above, 1-nerved or obscurely 3-nerved beneath, glabrous above or setulose along midvein or sparsely glandular-setose on surface, puLinetate or bullate beneath and glabrous to freely glandular-villous. Flowers 4-nierous, solitary, nearly sessile. Hypanthium narrowly campanulate, about 6 mm. long, obscurely 8-ribbed, thick-walled, glabrous. Calyx tube somewhat flaring, prolonged 1 mm. from torus to broadly convex sinuses, glandular-setose externally at sinuses with hairs 1-2 mm. long, densely glandular-tomentose within with very fine hairs 0.1-0.2 mm. long. Sepals narrowly triangular, 5-5.5 mm. long, erect or somewhat spreading, glandular-ciliate, glandular-hirsute to glabrous on the back. Petals narrowly obovate-oblong, purple, 22 mm. long, 10-11 mm. wide, slightly inequilateral, minutely glandular-apiculate, sparsely, minutely, and irregularly glandular-ciliate in the basal half. Stamens 8, weakly dimorphic. Filaments subterete, nearly straight, 9.4-10 or 10.3-10.7 mnm. long. Anthers stoutly subulate, erect, nearly straight, 5.8 or 7 mm. in total length, opening by a minute terminal pore; connective prolonged straight back 1.1 or 1.7 nim., bearing two erect, ovoid-conic, anterior lobes 1.5 mm. long. Ovary half-inferior, 2-celled, the rounded summit glabrous; style very slender, 17 mm. long; stigma punctiform.

description: Plants epiphytic; rhizomes 2.5-3 mm wide, horizontal, short-creeping; rhizome scales 2 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, sparsely denticulate, brown; phyllopodia absent; sterile fronds 9-15 cm long, 1.7-3 cm broad; stipes ca. 2/5-2/3 of the frond length, tan to stramineous; stipe scales 2-2.5 mm long, subulate, abundant, spreading, denticulate, brown; blades oblong to lanceolate, base truncate or cordate, apex notched with bud; blade scales on the abaxial side absent except for the midvein and margin, subulate, 0.5-3 mm long, denticulate, on the adaxial side scattered to sparse, subulate, 0.5-1.5 (2) mm long; veins distinct, 1.5-2 mm apart running at 60o-70' to the midvein, sometimes the veins bifurcate in different places along the blade; hydathodes evident; fertile frond ca. the same length as the sterile, the blades oblong to lanceolate, with stipe ca. 7/10-8/10 of the frond length, base truncate to rounded, apex obtuse; scales 0.5-1.5 mm long, abundant on the stipe, blade margin and adaxial blade upper surface, brown, toothed, on the abaxial surface only along the midvein; intersporangial scales absent; spores with irregular crests.
bibliographicCitation: Vasco,  Alejandra. 2006. Elaphoglossum gemmatum (Elaphoglossaceae), a new species from Colombia. Brittonia. 58 (1): 1-3.

description: C. anisandrae affinis, foliis angustioribus ovatis, venis lateralibus basi non nudatis, petiolis brevioribus, pilis glandulosis in pedicellis et hypanthio copiosis, eymulis trifloris, floribus pedicellatis, sepalis hypanthium subaequantibus, staminibus et stylo brevioribus differt.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.

description: Stems woody, freely and diffusely branched, deiisely pubescent with simple hairs, densely setose at nodes. Petioles 1-3 mm. long. Leaf blades firm, ovate, up to 14 mm. long and 8 mm. wide, acute, entire, acute at base, 3-nerved, the lateral nerves not marginal at base, setose on both sides. Upper leaves much smaller, sessile, glandular-setose above. Flowers 4-merous, in 3-flowered terminal eymules, each subtended by a pair of small leaves; pedicels glabrous, 1 mm. long. Hypanthium cup-shaped, 2.6-2.8 mm. long to the torus, glabrous on the basal portion, glandular-pubescent above with curved-ascending hairs 0.6 mm. long; calycine setae erect, 1.7 mm. long. Sepals triangular, 2.6 mm. long, ciliate, glandular-pubescent on the back, tipped with a glandular seta 0.8 mm. long. Petals yellow, 6-6.5 mni. long, about 4.5 mm. wide, ovate, acute, the terminal seta glandular, recurved, 0.7 mm. long. Filaments 4.7 mm. long; anthers stoutly subulate, all alike, 2.6 mm. long, the connective simple. Ovary free, rounded at summit, densely pilose with simple hairs, crowned with a eircumstylar ring of 8 stout, erect, simple hairs 1.3 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.

description: Caulibus ramosis, acute quadrangulatis, glanduLloso-pubeseentibus; petiolis brevibus; laminis oblanceolatis acutis, saepe revolutis, ad basin cuneatis, supra pallidis, minute pubeseentibus, subtus einereis glandulosis; glomerulis brevissime pedunculatis axillaribus, saepe unifloris; hypanthio campanulato glanduloso; sepalis lineari-oblongis acutis glandulosis; petalis obovatis. Stems freely branched, the internodes 15-25 mm. long, sharply 4-angled or very narrowly 4-winged, rather sparsely pubescent with short glandular hairs; petioles 2-5 mm. long, pubescent like the stem; blades oblanceolate, 10-15 mm. long, 3-5 m-m. wide, sharply acute, minutely denticulate, frequently somewhat revolute, long-cuneate at base, 3-nerved, the upper surface glaucous-green and sparsely pubescent with simple hairs; lower surface gray, more densely pubescent with short erect glandular hairs; bracts oblanceolate, 6-7 mm. long, pubescent like the leaves; infloreseence mostly 1-flowered, terminating short axillary branches, the peduncle 1-3 mm., the pedicel 1-2 mm. long; hypanthium narrowly campanulate, 3.5 mm. long, sparsely glandular-pubescent; sepals narrowly linear or slightly oblanceolate, 2.5 mm. long, conspicuously hirsute with glandular hairs; petals obovate, 7-8 mm. long; filaments 3.5 mm. long; anthers, including the connective, 4.5 mm. long; style 11 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Plants terrestrial; stems erect, scales ovate  lanceolate, dark brown with paler margin hairs 0.3 mm on surfaces, 2-3 x 1-1.5 mm; leaves few, clustered, 35-45 cm long; blades chartaceous, pinnate-pinnatifid, proximal 4 pinna pairs subabruptly reduced, the lowermost 2-4 mm long; petioles dark brown, 15 cmx 1.5-2 mm, with dense, thin hairs 0.1-0.4 mm, and with scattered, brown ovate lanceolate  scales 1-2 x 0.6-1 mm with hairs 0.2 mm on surfaces; rachises with dense, thin, spreading hairs 0.15-0.25 mm on both sides, many rachis hairs fascicled in groups of three to seven hairs; pinnae sessile, alternate to proximally subopposite, to 6 x 1.2 cm, deeply pinnatifid to approximately 1 mm from costae; aerophores  at pinna bases peglike, 0.3-0.5 mm long; buds lacking; veins prominulous, 4-5 pairs per segment; indument abaxially on costae and veins of sparse, spreading hairs 0.2-0.3 mm long, surfaces between veins with a few appressed hairs 0.1-0.2 mm, indument adax- ially on costae, veins, and surfaces between veins of moderately dense, spreading hairs 0.2- 0.3(-0.4) mm, glands lacking, costal scales ovate, tan, not clathrate, 0.3-1.2 x 0.2-0.6 mm; sori medial to supramedial, round; indusia absent or reduced to a nearly hidden few-celled fragment, receptacles (or indusial fragment) with hairs 0.2 mm; sporangia glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, A. R. & Kessler, Michael. 2008. Sixteen new species of Thelypteris (Thelypteridaceae) from Bolivia. Brittonia. 60 (2): 49-62.

description: Herba annua pumila, simplex vel parce ramosa; caulibus 4-angu- latis, glabris vel tenuiter pubeseentibus pilis eglandulosis; foliis mox deciduis, anguste ovatis, acutis, ad petiolum cuneatis, glabris, 3-nerviis; capitulis 1-10-floris; bracteis obovatis ciliatis glabris; hypanthio tubuloso; sepalis erectis triangularibus; connectivo antheras subaequantibus.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Annual, erect, simple or sparingly branched, 3-40 cm. high; stems nearly or quite glabrous, sharply 4-angled, the internodes 15-25 mm. long; leaves soon deciduous, flat, dark green, narrowly rhombic-ovate, sharply acute, cuneate to a petiole as long as or shorter than the blade, with 2 or 3 sharp teeth on each side, glabrous, faintly 3-nerved; in- florescence sparsely pubescent, or with a ring of hairs at the nodes; peduncles slender, 5-15 mm. long, spreading; heads 1-10-flowered; bracts broadly obovate, 4 mm. long, sessile, broadly rounded at sum- mit, sharply serrate in the upper third, spinulose-ciliate on the sides, entire below, 1-nerved, conspicuously reticulate-veined, glabrous; flowers sessile or on pedicels 0.5-1 mm. long, subtended by narrowly obovate, spinulose-ciliate bracts about 2 mm. long; hypanthium tubu- lar, becoming 4 mm. long in fruit; sepals erect, somewhat saccate at base, triangular, 1.3 mm. long, 3-nerved; anther-tube scarcely devel- oped; connective about as long as the anther and conspicuously bitu- berculate at base; capsule subeylindric, half as long as the hypan- thium, somewhat 2-lobed at the summit, dehiseent by 4 valves; seeds ellipsoid, 0.5 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Herba perennis; caulibus scabridulis non glandulosis; foliis con- fertis persistentibus adpressis sessilibus revolutis, supra scabridulis, subtus glabris, internodos aequantibus; eymis parvis axillaribus brac- teatis resinoso-punctatis; hypanthio campanulato resinoso; sepalis triangularibus acutis; capsula obovoidea. Perennial, erect, 4 dm. high, simple or with a few erect branches; stems purple-brown, obscurely 4-angled, closely scabrous-pubescent; leaves subcoriaceous, erect or appressed, just equaling the internodes, 5-7 mm. long, strongly revolute, broadly rhombic-ovate when un- rolled, cordate at the sessile base, obtuse or subacute, entire or with 1-3 low teeth on each side, obscurely 3-nerved, scabrously pubescent on the upper surface and the midvein beneath, glabrous and promi- nently pitted on the lower surface; infloreseence of 1-6-flowered, bracteate, pedunculate eymes from the upper axils, scabrously pubes- cent throughout and dotted wNAith nunmerous shining resinous globules; peduncles 2-5 mm. long; bracts few, oblong, slightly revolute, 1-3 mm. long; pedicels 2-3 mm. long; hypanthium campanulate, 1.8-2.2 mm. long, scabrously pubescent and sparsely resinolus; sepals triangu- lar, acute, equaling the hypanthium; capsule obovoid, 2-lobed, barely shorter than the hypanthium.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Sect. Eusiphanthera: herba pereninis, caulibus, bracteis, hypanlthio, et calycibus plusminus glandulosis; folia elliptica utrinque acuta, breviter petiolata vel sessilia; bracteae late obovatae; antherae breviter rostratae, connectivis 2-3-plo loingiores.

description: Stems slender, 3-25 cm. tall, simple or branched above, sharply 4-angled, minutely strigose on the angles and freely glandular-setose. Leaf-blades firm, elliptic, 5-10 mm. long, 2-5 mm. wide, acute at both ends, sparsely pubescent on both sides, the lower on petioles up to 4 mm. long, the upper smaller and sessile (in depauperate plants all leaves sessile). Peduncles filiform, 5-10 mm. long. Glomerules 1-4-flowered; bracts obovate to obovate-rotund, 2.8-3.6 mm. long, 1.5-2.4 mm. wide, sharply serrate and glandular-ciliate above middle. Hypanthium subeylindric, 2.4 mm. long, obscurely 8-ribbed. Sepals erect, persistent, trianigular, 1.5 mm. long, acute, glandular-setose on the back. Petals elliptic, slightly unguiculate at base, 1.7 mm. long, very thin, essentially veinless. Sterile filaments 1.3 mm. long. Filaments of the fertile anthers slender, 1.5 mm. long. Anthers quadrate-elliptic, violet, the thecae 0.5 mm. long, the rostrum broadly ovate, 0.2 mm. long, the connective nearly 0.3 mm. long, its basal half dilated and minutely bituberculate. Ovary free, ellipsoid; style 2.8 mm. long, dilated distally. Capsule didymous, flattened, obovate, 2.2 mm. long, retuse; seeds ellipsoid, 0.4 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. & Killip, E. P. 1939. The flora of Mount Auyan-Tepui, Venezuela. Brittonia. 3: 141-204. f. 1-5.

description: Habitus cespitosus. Culmus 2-5 mm diam., 30-80 cm altus, erectus. Folia culmi 1-5 cm longa, vagina persistenti 1-4.5 cm longa, lamina decidua 5-8 mm longa. Ramificatio intravaginalis. Folia per ramulum secondarium 3-15; vagina persistens, plerumque margines versus pubescentes; lamina 1-2.5 cm longa, 1.5-3 mm lata, ratione long./lat. = 8-10: 1, rigida, glabra, lanceolata, marginibus cartilagineis, ad basem 0.3-0.5 mm lata. Inflorescentia 1-2 (-3) cm longa, paniculata, contracta. Spiculae 5.5-7.2 mm longae. Glumae I et II pubescentes; gluma I 0.4-0.7 mm longa; gluma II (0.4) 0.8-1 (1.5) mm longa; glumae III et IV apicem versus pubescentes; gluma III 4- 6 mm longa; gluma IV 5-8 mm longa; lemma 6-8 mm longum, glabrum; palea 5-6 mm longa.
bibliographicCitation: Niño, S. M., et al. 2006. Una nueva especie de Chusquea (Poaceae: Bambusoideae) de la Cordillera de Mérida, Venezuela. Brittonia. 58 (1): 46-51.

description: Bambi cespitoso, perenne. Rizoma delgado, probablemente simpodial. Culmo macizo, erecto, amarillento, 2-5 mm de grosor y 30-80 cm alto; entrenudos teretes, glabros macizos de 1-8.5 cm de largo; ramificaciones laterales intravaginales, casi siempre de primer orden y algunas veces de segundo orden, de menor grosor que el culmo principal, 1-8 ramitas por nudo, subiguales. Hojas del culmo 1-5 cm de largo, estriadas, glabras o ligeramente pubescentes; vaina 1-4.5 cm de largo, persistente, fusionada 0.5-1 mm en la base del nudo, base extendida 1-2 cm de ancho, dipice 2-3 mm de ancho; limina 5-8 mm de largo, triangular, papiricea, glabra, decidua, la base 2-3 mm de ancho, mairgenes lisos; lfgula interna muy corta, 0.1-0.2 mm de alto, con margen apical irregular, hispido o glabro, cartilaginoso. Hojas del follaje 3-15 por rama subsidiaria; vaina 0.9-1.2 cm de largo, persistente, estriada, carticea, minutamente pubescente particularmente hacia el margen, algunas veces glabra, aquillada hacia el aipice, borde liso; ligula externa diminuta ca. 0.1 mm de alta, cartaicea, glabra o hispida, con pelos transliicidos de 0.5-1 mm de largo o sin ellos; ligula interna muy corta, 0.3-0.5 mm de alto, cartaicea, borde irregular, algunas hispidas o glabras, los pelos de 0.5-1 mm de largo; limina 1-2.5 cm x 1.5-3 mm, ancho en la base, L:A = 8-10, rigida, lanceolada, base redondeada, ipice agudo a veces mucronado, glabra, bordes lisos o minutamente estrigosos, cartilaginosos, prominentes en la cara adaxial, 0.3-0.5 mm de ancho; pseudopeciolo muy corta, 0.5-1 mm de largo. Panicula reducida y corta de 1-2 (- 3) cm de largo, cerrada, la porci6n basal en la vaina de la hoja, 7-15 espiguillas; raquis minutamente pubescente, anguloso, 8-12 mm de largo, mais o menos de igual longitud que la panicula; ramitas adpresas, surgiendo en verticilos espiralados de 2-3, en algunas inflorescencias con 1-2 ramitas dividas en dos, cada ramita (pedicelo) con una espiguilla. Espiguillas 5.5-7.2 mm de largo, lateralmente comprimidas. Glumas I y II carticeas, pubescentes; gluma I 0.4-0.7 mm de largo, no mais que 1/10 del largo de la espiguilla, triangular u ovada, borde liso o lig- eramente crenado; gluma II (0.4-) 0.8-1 (-1.5) mm de largo, 1/10-1/8, del largo de la espiguilla, ovada, apice redondeado. Glumas III y IV 3/4-1 el largo de la espiguilla, pubescentes en el aipice; gluma III 4-6 mm de largo, lanceolada, 5-nervada, Aipice agudo y fimbriado, cara adaxial minutamente pubescente, cara abaxial glabra; gluma IV 5-8 mm de largo, igual o poco mayor que la gluma III, ápice agudo y fimbriado, la cara adaxial pubescente o glabritiscula, 2-3 nervada con el nervio medio generalmente prominente en 1/2 distal, la cara abaxial glabra. Lema fértil 6-8 mm de largo, lanceolada, ápice agudo, fimbriado, 7 (-8) nervada, los bordes y el nervio medio en la cara adaxial con cilios blanquecinos, cara abaxial glabra. Palea 5-6 mm de largo, lanceolada, apice agudo, glabra o algo pubescente hacia el dipice, 4 nervada. Lodiculas 3, blanquecinas y diminutas; par anterior 0.6-1 mm de largo; lodicula posterior poco mayor, 0.7-1.2 mm de largo. Estambres 3; filamento delgado y breve, 0.2-0.5 mm de largo; anteras dorsifijas; lineares, 2-3 mm de largo. Ovario pequefio, 0.8-1 mm de largo, glabro, dos estilos plumosos. Fruto desconocido.

description: Shrubs or small trees, to 8 m or more high. Year-old branchlets brown or yellow-brown, not pruinose, pubescent; new branchlets green becoming brown or yel- low-brown, pubescent. Expanded leaf blades elliptic to oblanceolate, 4-10 X 1-2 cm, entire or slightly glandular-serrulate, moderately to densely pubescent on both sides or sometimes glabrous adaxially, glaucous or glaucescent abaxially; petioles 2-13 mm long; stipules lacking or minute. Aments precocious. Staminate aments 1.5- 2.5 cm long, sessile; anthers 0.6-0.8 mm long. Pistillate aments 1.5-3 cm long, ses- sile. Capsules 2.5-4 mm long, pubescent to glabrate; styles 0.2-0.5(-0.8) mm long; stipes 0.1-0.8 mm long. Floral bracts ob- ovate, 1-2 mm long, brown, with dense, long, untangled hairs exceeding the bract tip.

description: Liana, ascending to 2-12 m, glabrous (except flowers), branches terete, sulcate, minutely tuberculate. Leaves opposite; stipules caducous, not seen; petioles 1.3-1.7 cm, canaliculate, drying wrinkled; blades (10.5) 14.7-16.7 x (4.9) 5.6-6.1 (7.6) cm, elliptic or ovate, the base rounded or cuneate, the apex acuminate, the margin slightly sinuous or entire, chartaceous, drying grey-green on the adaxial side, light brown on the abaxial side, venation brochidodromous with veins prominulous on both sides, secondary veins prominulous to inconspicuous. Inflorescence an corymbiform dichasium, 3.8-7.4 x 4.3- 4.5 cm, with more than 1,500 flowers, axillary; bracts 0.4-0.7 mm long, triangular, densely dirty-brown puberulous, frequently somewhat apart from the dichotomy; peduncle 0-0.2 cm long, flattened, densely dirty-brown puberulous; inflorescence branches dichotomous, flattened, densely dirty-brown puberulous; pedicels ca. 0.9 mm long, terete, densely dirty-brown puberulous. Flowers spherical in bud, ca. 2.7 mm wide at anthesis; sepals 5, 0.7-0.8 x 0.7-1 mm, triangular, unequal, carnose, yellowish green, densely dirty-brown puberulous; petals 5, 1-1.3 x 0.8-1.5 mm, elliptic, ± carnose, somewhat reflexed at anthesis, white, densely dirty-brown puberulous; disc annular, short-tubular, 0.23-3 mm high, carnose, connate with ovary lobes; stamens 3, 0.54-0.64 mm long, the filaments flattened, the anthers 0.3- 0.31 x 0.57-0.64 mm, transverse ellipsoidal and emarginated at both larger sides, dorsi-fixed, bilocular, transversely dehiscent; pistil pyramid-shaped, ovary 3-lobed, lobes con- nate with inner side of disk, 3-locular, with 5-6 ovules in each locule, style 0.2-0.23 mm long after anthesis, central, triangular, stigmas deltate, entire, alternate with stamens. Drupes not seen; seeds not seen.

description: Cyathea mediae trunco nudo, lamina pilosa ad apicem gradatim contracta, pinnis planis oppositis vel alternis, pinnulis in marginem duplicato-serratis vel bicrenatis, indusio firmo sphaeropteroideo cum umbone praestans.

description: Trunk to 2-4 m high, to 7-8(-12) cm diam., erect, dull dark brown to blackish; trunks over 1 m high without persistent old petiole bases (Fig. ID), although a skirt of last year's fronds or petioles may be present; the scars not protruding, inconspicuous, similar to the trunk cortex in color; trunk scales concolorous dull brown, present around the scars near the apex. Petioles to 60 cm long, inermous (Fig. ID), smooth to scabrous, livid light green when young, dull brown when mature, scaly scurf lacking, but with a tomentum of stiff, translucent white pluricellular trichomes (0.5-1.0 mm) and scattered dark brown glandular hairs (0.1-0.2 mm) (Fig. IF, arrow). Petiole scales with differentiated margin without marginal teeth or setae, lanceolate, to 3-5 x 22 mm, broad at the petiole base, narrow distally (Fig. lE), concolorous dull to golden brown, or weakly bicolorous with the margins lighter than the center. Lamina to 140 x 80 cm, bipinnate-pinnatifid, broadly ovate, dull green to dark green adaxially, pale grayish green abaxially; lowermost pinna pair not or only weakly deflexed, apex gradually reduced; pinnae to 40 cm long, sessile (Fig. lA), either opposite throughout with a rather short apex or the lamina distally with alternate pinnae/segments, and then the apical rhachis prolonged and bent in a zigzag pattern. Leaf axes inermous, green to dull brown, with white to tan pluricellular hairs 1-2 mm long, often catenate at base. Pinnules to 15 x 75 mm, oblong-linear to oblong-obovate, sessile, cuspidate to short attenuate at tip (Fig. 1A, B); segments patent to curved, with deeply double-serrate margins along the sides, at tip weakly serrate to crenate (Fig. IC), basal segments with pronounced basiscopic lobules that partly cover tween veins on both sides, the trichomes white, erect and to 1 mm long abaxially (Fig. IC), appressed and only 0.5 mm or less long adaxially; with some small scales to 3 mm long, opaque whitish to tan, plane or wrinkled, not bullate (Fig. IC). Sterile veins forked or simple, fertile veins forked (Fig. IB, C). Sori costal to subcostal, in fork of veins (Fig. IC). Indusia sphaeropteroid, firm, with umbo, rupturing irregularly at maturity, one part normally bearing the umbo (Fig. IC); paraphyses as long as the sporangia. Spores trilete, exospore smooth, perispore baculate.

description: Trunk to 4 m high, to 12-16 cm diam., erect and straight, not covered by old petiole bases, the scars pale brown to grey, arranged in horizontal whorls, some oval vermillion pneumathodes below them (Fig. 2C, arrow), to 10 x 5 mm, immersed 1-2 mm into the cortex; the cortex dark brown to blackish, densely scaly towards apex (Fig. 2C); the scales long-lanceolate, dull orange-brown, concolorous or bicolorous with the center darker brown, or the narrow margins lighter orange to whitish. Petioles to 25 cm long, scabrous to finely muricate at base, rarely inermous or with some longer spines; bright green when young, dull light brown when old, with caducous scurf of brown squamellae with strongly crispate margins (Fig. 2E). Petiole scales long lanceolate with elongated tips, to 3.6 x 50.0 mm, narrow at the petiole base, broader in its upper parts, nearly concolorous orange brown to bicolorous with orange brown to castaneous center and orange to whitish narrow margins (Fig. 2D). Lamina bipinnate-pinnatifid, 105-165 x 60-70 cm, the apex gradually reduced (Fig. 2C), firm-chartaceous to subcoriaceous, often glossy adaxially (especially when young), opaque abaxially. Lamina axes inermous, glabrescent except for the adaxial side; rhachis and costae brown adaxially, otherwise bright green to stramineous when dried, densely hairy adaxially; costa base conspicuously swollen and ring-like where it joins the rachis; costules of the same color as the lam- ina, moderately hairy adaxiallly, glabrous or glabrescent abaxially. Pinnae alternate, to 40 cm long, sessile to short stalked (2 cm) (Fig. 3), acute to short attenuate at tip, green alate between distal pinnules and segments. Pinnules linear-lanceolate, 1.0-1.5 x 3.0-7(-8) cm, sessile or rarely short-stalked (to 3 mm), base truncate to subcordate, tip short-acute (Fig. 2A); pinnules turned upwards with respect to the costa and often twisted towards the rhachis, especially in the proximal half of the pinnae; glabrous adaxially except for the hairs on the costae, abaxially glabrous or with few short hairs (to 0.5 mm) on costa and veins, rarely between them, sometimes also small tan flattish squamules; indument more developed with increasing size, fertility, and sun exposure, but always inconspicuous; segments patent with subentire to crenulate or rarely crenate margins; sterile veins forked or simple, fertile veins forked. Sori inframedial to costal, at vein fork. Indusia sphaeropteroid, without umbo, tan, opaque, transparent, fragile, remaining as brown discs at maturity. Paraphyses as long as sporangia. Spores trilete, bright yellow

description: Calyx 5-10 mm long. Petals 40-55 x 5-15 mm, usually markedly reflexed. Staminal tube usually with a distinct articulation 2-5 mm from the base, lower tube densely tomentose, and the upper tube pubescent below, becoming glabrous above.

description: Herba vel suffrutex, caulibus quadrangularibus, dense hirtellis vel subtomentosis; foliorum lamina ovata vel oblongo-ovata, basi angustata, firma, hirtella, costa et venis lateralibus subtus prominentibus; spicae plerumque binae, terminales et axillares, pedunculis et rhachidibus subquadrangularibus, dense hirtellis; bracteae et bracteolae pallide virides, spathulatae, hirtellae et ciliatae; calycis segmenta viridia margine purpurascentia, lanceolata, hirtella et ciliata; corolla lavandula, parce glanduloso-puberula, labio superiore erecto, ovato, bilobato, labio inferiore trilobato, lobis ellipticis, rotundatis; stamina inclusa; lobis antherarum leviter superpositis.

description: Herb or subshrub, 0.75-1 m tall; stems quadrangular, densely hirtellous or subtomentose, the trichomes whitish, mostly erect, to 1 mm long; leaf blades ovate or oblong-ovate, 10-16.5 cm long and 3.3-7.3 cm wide, acute to acuminate or short-acuminate, narrowed at base, moderately firm, entire or undulate, the upper surface drying dark-green, moderately hirtellous, the trichomes whitish, septate, curved, about 0.5 mm long, the costa and lateral veins (6 to 10 pairs) rather obscure above, prominent on the lower surface, the cystoliths minute, often obscure on both surfaces, the lower surface drying yellowish-green, moderately to rather densely hirtellous, especially the venation, the trichomes erect, whitish to 0.5 mm long; petioles short, 1-2 cm long, hirtellous; flowers borne in terminal and axillary, usually paired spikes, 4-6 cm long and 2-3 cm broad; peduncles 0.5-2 cm long, these and the rachis subquadrangular, densely hirtellous, the trichomes white, erect; bracts pale green, spatulate, 15-25 mm long and 5.5-8 mm wide, obtuse or rounded at apex, unguiculate at base, the narrowed portion 5-8 mm long and 0.6 mm wide, the entire bract hirtellous, the costa and lateral veins prominent; bracteoles pale green, spatulate, 11-20 mm long and 2.5-4.5 mm wide, obtuse or rounded at apex, unguiculate at base, the entire bracteole hirtellous, especially along the costa, the margins ciliate; calyx 14 mm long, deeply segmented, the segments 5, green with purplish margins, lanceolate, 12 mm long, 2.5-2.7 mm wide, hirtellous and ciliolate, the trichomes subappressed; corolla 2.3-2.8 cm long, lavender, sparingly glandular-puberulous, especially the upper portion, the corolla tube about 0.5 cm long, 2 mm broad at base, 6 mm broad at mouth, the upper lip erect, ovate, 21 mm long, 12 mm wide, bilobed at apex, the lobes rounded, 1 mm long and 1.75 mm wide, cucullate, enclosing the stamens, the lower lip 15 mm long and 1 cm wide at base of the 3 lobes, these elliptic, 10-13 mm long and 5.5-6.5 mm wide, rounded; stamens 18 mm long, glabrous; anthers 3.5 mm long and 2 mm broad, slightly superposed, the lower lobe terminating in a short apiculum 1 mm long; pollen grains 2-porate, bilateral, 57 x 38 µm, the pores circular, membrane reticulate, trema area studded with more or less circular insulae (Fig. 2B); pistil about equaling the stamens, the stigma bilobed, minute and rounded, style minutely puberulous; capsule green or purplish-green, brown when dry, clavate, glabrous, 1.8-2 cm long, 6 mm broad and 4 mm thick, subobtuse at tip (the solid basal portion 8 mm long); retinacula stout, 3 mm long and 1 mm wide, flattened, rounded at tip; seeds only slightly flattened, almost spherical, glabrate, 3.5 mm in diam, greenish, or dark purple at maturity.

description: Ramuli teretes, dense setosi; folia (12-) 17-50 x 7-14 (-16) cm, elliptica vel ovata; formicaria 1.5-2.5 cm x 0.8-1.3 cm, ovata vel anguste ovata; inflorescentia terminalis primum intra bracteam inclusa; bracteae basilares involucrales caducae, 7.5-11 x 3.5-6 cm, suborbiculares vel ellipticae, intus rubrae; ovarium superius, in apice coronatum.

description: Tree or treelet, up to 6 m tall. Stems terete, densely pubescent, the simple, eglandular trichomes up to 5 mm long, persistent, magenta to crimson. Leaves isophyllous or slightly anisophyllous, (12-)17-50 x 7-14 (-16) cm, 5-nervate (excluding the very inconspicuous marginal veins), elliptic to obovate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, base acute, entire to obscurely serrulate-ciliate, membranaceous, adaxial side appressed-setose, abaxial side densely setose on the primary and secondary veins, the surface sparsely to densely setose, light green; domatia present on both leaves of each node, 1.5-2.5 cm x 0.8-1.3 cm, ovoid to narrowly ovoid, at the apex of the petiole, the apex of the domatia slightly immersed in the leaf blade, with sparse broad-based trichomes up to 3 mm long; petioles 2-5.5 cm long, pubescence as in the stems florescence a terminal panicle, 13-20 cm long, with numerous flowers, the axis fuchsia, flattened, pubescent, the simple eglandular trichomes up to 2.5 mm long; bracts at the base of the inflorescence, branches, and dichasia, the basal most bracts 7.5-11 x 3.5-6 cm, caducous, surrounding the developing inflorescence, sub-orbicular to elliptic with an acuminate apex 2-4 cm long, the abaxial surface red, the adaxial surface white-yellow, both surfaces flat with the nerves obvious towards the apex, and with a mixture of dense short simple trichomes up to 0.6 mm long and sparse simple trichomes up to 2.5 mm long; remaining bracts progressively smaller in size and narrower from the base of the inflorescence to the apex and from the base of the branches to the individual dichasia; bracteoles subtending the flowers 3-9 x 1.2-2.5 mm, lanceolate to linear, caducous. Flowers sessile, 5-merous; hypanthium broadly conical at the base, becoming cylindrical at the apex, 6.5-8 mm long, with a mixture of sparse simple and gland-headed setae up to 3.5 mm long, and occasionally with very sparse dendritic hairs; outer calyx teeth highly reduced, often inconspicuous; inner calyx teeth broadly deltoid, fused almost to the apex, 1.5-2.2 mm long; the ring inside the torus glabrous. Petals 6.5-8 x 4.5-5.5 mm, broadly oblong to ovate, apex emarginate, border entire, often undulate, pruinose to smooth, glabrous, pink to white. Stamens all of the same size, the filaments 5-6 mm long, pink, glabrous; anthers yellow, the connective with a dorsal-basal blunt tooth; thecae 5.0-6.0 (-6.5) mm long, opening by a upright to dorsally inclined pore. Ovary 3-locular, fully to 9/10 superior, terete, the apex with a corona of short, flat setae 1.2-2.1 mm long, partially fused at the base; style glabrous, 11-14 mm long; stigma capitate, 1.5-1.8 mm wide. Fruits globose, 8-14 mm long, black, sparsely glandular pubescent. Seeds numerous, not evident through the pericarp, triangular, 0.6-1.0 mm long, without capitate trichomes in the raphal area, without sculpturing, anticlinal walls straight, periclinal walls convex, boundaries between periclinal walls flat.
