description: Tree or treelet, up to 3 m tall. Stems flattened when young, becoming terete, densely pubescent, the simple eglandular trichomes 3-4.5 mm long, persistent. Leaves isophyllous to moderately anisophyllous, narrowly obovate to narrowly elliptic, the larger leaves 13-21 (-29) x 4-5 cm, the smaller leaves 20-35% smaller, apex acute, caudate, the tip 8-25 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, base acute, adaxial side with a mixture of appressed setae up to 3.5 mm long and sparse glandular trichomes up to 1 mm long, abaxial side with the primary and secondary veins densely setose, the surface with a mixture of sparse to dense eglandular trichomes (up to 2.5 mm long) and sparse glandular (less than 1 mm long) trichomes, 5-nervate, membranaceous, obscurely crenulate, ciliate; domatia present on both leaves of each node, 1.2-2.2 x 0.8-1.1 cm, ovoid to narrowly ovoid, at the apex of the petiole, but free from the leaf blade, with sparse broad-based trichomes up to 3 mm long; petioles 0.8-2.2 cm long, pubescence as in the stems. Inflorescence a terminal condensed raceme, 3-6 cm long, with persistent bracts at the base and the base of the dichasia, 2-3.5 x 2.5-4 cm, broadly obovate, the margins obscurely fimbriate, the abaxial surface glabrous, the adaxial surface with sparse glandular trichomes and sessile glands; bracteoles 6-9 x 0.5-1 mm, lanceolate, persistent. Flowers sessile, 5-merous, the petals, anthers, and stigma only partially visible at anthesis between the bracts; hypanthium campanulate, 8.5-10.5 mm long, with a mixture of sparse glandular trichomes and sessile glands; outer calyx teeth deltoid at the base, 0.9-1.1 mm long, with an acute tip 0.3- 0.5 mm long, not projecting above the inner calyx, with sparse sessile glands and short trichomes (less than 0.3 mm long); inner calyx teeth broadly deltoid, fused 2/3 of the length, 1.5-1.8 mm long; the ring inside the torus glabrous. Petals 3.5-4.5 (-5) x 4-5.5 mm, broadly obovate, apex emarginate to obtuse, margin entire, smooth, glabrous, white with pink borders. Stamens all of the same size, the filaments 6-7.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers yellow; the connective with a dorsalbasal blunt tooth; thecae 7.5-8.5 mm long, opening by a dorsally inclined pore. Ovary 3-locular, inferior, the apex glabrous and even with the hypanthium floor; style glabrous, 14-18 mm long; stigma capitate, 1.5 mm wide. Fruits and seeds unknown.

description: Staminal tube lacking a distinct articulation, variably pubescent, sometimes uniformly so, usually densely pubescent in the lower half and becoming glabrous above, but sometimes uniformly very sparsely hairy or glabrescent. description: Plants terrestrial. Rhizomes short-creeping, nodose, ca. 0.4 cm in diam., scaly, the scales somewhat shiny, essentially concolorous, appressed but spreading at their tips, varying from medium to dark brown, lanceate, sparsely denticulate to short-ciliate at margins. Fronds monomorphic, 2-pinnate, 40-72 x 18-25 cm; stipes approximate, 1/2-2/3 the length of the frond, brown to black, adaxially sulcate, with two kinds of scales, scales appressed at base and spreading at middle and apices, concolorous, brown, 2-4(-5) mm long, linear to narrowly lanceate with a long filiform apex, ciliate at margins and with several processes at the base; and scales 2-3 mm long, arachnoid, basal processes thin, uniseriate, concolorous, light brown; rachises similar to the stipes and with similar indument; pinnae oblong-laceate, slightly narrowed at their base, tapering at the apex, (7-)10-15 x 2.0-2.5 cm, the lateral pinnae 3-4(-6) pairs, ascending alternate, the terminal pinna conform, 1-1.5 times longer than the subtending pinnae; indument of costae like that of stipes and rachises; pinnules (11-)18-21 pairs, ca. 3 times longer than wide, chartaceous, not articulate, freeveined, each without an evident midrib, proximal pairs reduced, somewhat rounded or rhombic, medial pairs dimidiate, oblong to subfalcate, acroscopic base truncate, basiscopic base perpendicular or oblique to costa, sterile apices obtuse to round, sterile margins denticulate, fertile apices round to angular, distal pinnules ca. 1/2 or less as the length of the medial pinnules, adaxial surfaces of pinnules glabrous, abaxial surface with scales and hairs, the scales hairlike, light brown, 1.0-1.5 mm long, similar to those of the stipes, but with fewer processes at the base, the hairs light brown, 1.0-1.5 mm long, septate, glands absent, veins slightly prominulous, idioblasts present between the veins on both surfaces; sori oblong, (1-)5-12(-17) per pinnule, mostly distributed on the acroscopic and distal margins of the pinnules, sometimes also on the basiscopic side; indusia scaly, the scales with long filiform apices and pectinate bases, margins entire to erose, cells well evident; spores not seen.

description: Plants terrestrial. description: Trunks 6-12 m high, (5-) 8-15 cm diam. without petiole bases, to 20 cm diam. with them; petiole bases persistent in small plants and at the base of large plants, deciduous when the trunk height surpasses the frond length; cortex dark brown to brown, inermous, with some narrow lanceolate scales around frond scars; scars ellipitic to ovate, well spaced in lower parts, in higher parts tighter packed and rounder, but not rhomboid; trunk apices hidden in fascicle of the youngest petioles; adventitious buds lacking. Fronds 200-330 cm long, patent to weakly ascending, weakly arching. Petioles to 90 cm long, short- to long-aculeate (Fig. lA), dark green to blackish when fresh, stramineous to lustrous brown when dried, the bases usually dark brown; pneumathodes in one discontinuous line laterally, very narrow, inconspicuous, contracted when dried, hence usually not visible; petiole scurf white to tan, dense to scattered (Fig. 1A), easily detached and vanishing with age, consisting of fragile squamules to 0.3 mm long, with crested margins, in larger squamules the margins laterally convolute (Fig. IB); marginal processes very fragile, with the horizontal cell walls often on one level so that the squamellae may appear trimmed when the marginal processes have fallen off (Fig. IB); petiole scales lanceolate, their bases very narrow to broad (Fig. IC), 17-25 x 1.8-5 mm, at petiole bases nearly concolorous brown to dark brown with the margins paler to white apically, distal petiole parts with scales concordantly bicolorous with dark brown to atropurpureous, often streaked center and yellowish to white margins; scales of the adaxial petiole parts and beneath the upper scale layer on the crosiers discordantly bicolorous with most of the center yellowish to golden like the margins (Fig. IC); scale margins differentiated, without marginal teeth, but sometimes with some brown cells. Lamina elliptic-ovate, dark lustrous green adaxially when fresh, opaque dark olive to blackish when dried, pale grey green and opaque abaxially; apex gradually reduced, basal pinna pair small, deflexed; lamina very often infected by a fungus, notable abaxially as brown to black spots restricted by the veins (Fig. 1D). Rhachis muricate, weakly aculeate, stramineous to pale brown, glabrous in basal parts adaxially, with some short (0.5-0.8 mm) pale brown trichomes distally, glabrous abaxially except for scattered evanescent scurf similar to petiole scurf. Pinnae in 12-19 pairs, to 45-69 cm long (Fig. 2E), distally narrowly green alate. Costae inermous or muricate proximally, stramineous or yellowish brown to brown, their insertions into the rhachis not raised, with two spots abaxially (Fig. 1F), one firm plumbeous to greenish yellow aerophore (to 5 x 2 mm) with brown to rufescent stomata, and one black (when dried) glutinous spot; costules inermous, dark brown adaxially, brown to pruinose or rufescent abaxially; costae and costules with short (0.5-0.8 mm), pale brown to whitish antrorse hairs adaxially, glabrous abaxially except for evanescent scurf similar to petiole scurf. Pinnules (61-) 95-122 x (10-) 18-28 mm, long linear to weakly long obovate (Fig. iG), rarely long triangular, subsessile to short stalked to 2 mm, bases truncate to weakly cordate or rounded, apices long-acute to short attenuate (Fig. G); segments oblong to weakly obovate-oblong, patent to weakly ascending, with acute tips (Fig. ID); basal segments of largest pinnules usually remote from the next segments, articulate or connected by a thin green wing to adjacent segments (Fig. 1G); margins crenulate, especially towards segment tips, subentire to entire towards the sinuses; sinuses acute (except for remote segments); glabrous adaxially or with 1-5 short (to 0.6 mm long) hairs on the midveins distally, without or with scattered white erect hairs (to 0.5 mm long) on the veins, and some whitish to tan flattish to subbullate squamules abaxially (Fig. 1D); the squamules whitish to tan, flat or subbullate (Fig. 1H), with subentire to weakly toothed margins and elongate tips. Veins. brown to pruinose or rufescent, not raised; sterile veins forked or simple, fertile veins forked. Sori costal to subcostal (Fig. 1D), in vein forks; indusia sphaeropteroid, opaque brown to tan, each with an apical umbo (Fig. 1J), fragile, the part bearing the umbo usually shed at maturity; indusia remaining as a shallow cups (Fig. 1J) or irregularly shaped discs, sometimes appearing hemitelioid (Fig. 1J) or vanishing entirely; receptacles globose, paraphyses brown to tan, as long as sporangia, stout and persitent (Fig. 1D). Spores tetrahedral-globose, trilete, ex- ospore smooth, finely porate (Fig. 2A), perispore finely baculate (Fig. 2B).

description: Shrub or small tree to 6 m tall. Indumentum of multicellular, ferrugineous, thick-stalked, irregularly dendritic to elongate-branched hairs, smaller, globular-branched hairs, and minute globular hairs. Young twigs rectangular to rounded-rectangular in cross section, 1.5-3 mm wide, becoming terete with age, the indumentum of moderate to sparse, multicellular, ferrugineous, thick-stalked irregularly dendritic to elongate-branched hairs, and smaller, globular-branched hairs; internodes 1-3.4 cm long. Leaves opposite, with petiole 3-23 mm long, the indumentum sparse to moderate, similar to that of the twigs; blade ovate to elliptic, 1.7-5.9 X 1-3.4 cm, flat, coriaceous, the apex obtuse, acute, to slightly acuminate, the base obtuse to rounded or very slightly cordate, the margin distinctly serrulate to base or nearly so (ca. 0-10% of margin entire basally), plane to revolute, the largest teeth 0.15-0.4 mm long; venation acrodromous, basal, with prominent midvein, two pairs of conspicuous secondary veins placed 1.5-7 mm and 0.5-2.5 mm from margin respectively, and often one pair of inconspicuous intramarginal secondary veins, and with numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented subperpendicular to midvein, the tertiary veins usually connected by quaternary veins; adaxial surface green, essentially glabrous, but some ferrugineous, erect-stalked, often few-branched, dendritic hairs along midvein and major secondary veins, with several rows of stout, conical projections, to 0.15-0.35 mm long, in regions bounded by tertiary veins; the midvein, major secondary veins, and tertiary veins strongly to slightly im- pressed, quaternary veins moderately to very slightly impressed or flat, the surface ?+ bullate, with the conical projections at the apices of the bullations, minutely papil- lose after drying due to presence of numer- ous druse crystals; abaxial surface light green, moderately to sparsely covered with ferrugineous, dendritic to elongate- branched hairs, to 0.4-0.7 mm long, along with smaller globose-stellate hairs and mi- nute-globular hairs on midvein, secondary and tertiary veins, and only minute-globular hairs on quaternary and higher order veins, the midvein, major secondary, and tertiary veins prominently raised, quaternary veins slightly raised to flat, intramarginal second- ary veins slightly raised to flat, the higher order veins flat. Inflorescences terminal, many flowered, pyramidal cymes of 2 to 6 major branch-pairs, 2.5-11 cm long, 1.5- 5.5 cm across; proximal segment of low- ermost inflorescence branches 4.5-21 mm long, distal internodes of inflorescence branches increasingly shorter, ultimate branches 0-0.5 mm long, and flowers ap- pearing in 3- to 5-flowered glomerules, along and terminating inflorescence branch- es, with sparse to moderate, ferrugineous hairs similar to those of twigs; peduncle 1- 3.8 cm long, with similar indumentum; each inflorescence branch associated with a + deciduous, oblong to elliptic bract, 2-3.5 X 0.7-1.5 mm, the bract apex + acute; flowers in dichasia, each subtended by 2 de- ciduous narrowly elliptic to narrowly tri- angular bracteoles 0.7-1.5 X 0.2-0.5 mm, the indumentum sometimes of a few branched hairs along margin, otherwise gla- brous, the apices acute to acuminate; the lowermost inflorescence branches some- times in the axils of leaves. Flowers sessile or nearly so, the pedicel 0-0.3 mm long. Hypanthium cylindrical-orbicular, free por- tion ca. 0.7-0.9 mm long, the outer surface with moderate ferrugineous, minute-globu- lar to globular-stellate hairs, the inner surface glabrous and smooth to shallowly ridged. External calyx teeth 4, 0.3-0.5 X 0.9-1.3 mm, triangular, with acute to obtuse apex, indumentum of a few minute-globular or globular-branched hairs, but frequently glabrous; internal calyx lobes 4, 0.35-0.6 X 0.75-1.1 mm, ovate-triangular, pale green to red tinged, glabrous, the apex rounded, the margin entire; calyx tube 0.1- 0.3 mm long (but one young fruit seen with 5 external calyx teeth and internal calyx lobes, 2 of these closely placed, as if resulting from a division of a single primordium, and thus considered a rare teratological condition). Petals 4, broadly elliptic to suborbicular, 1.4-1.85 X 0.9-1.25 mm, glabrous, white, imbricate and apically inter-locking in bud, with apex rounded, with an asymmetrically located notch; margin ± entire. Stamens 8, geniculate, isomorphic, white, glabrous, and arranged actinomorphically; proximal portion 1.1-1.4 mm long; distal segment (anther and distal portion of filament) 1.55-1.75 mm long, the anther 1-1.15 mm long, with fertile portion of anther sacs 0.75-0.95 mm long, opening by a single, fairly large, terminal pore, with the septum between the anthers sacs clearly visi- ble, the base slightly lobed, extended 0.15- 0.3 mm beyond the anther sacs. Ovary 2- loculate, ca. 1/2-inferior, ± globose, 0.85- 0.95 X 0.85-1 mm, glabrous, non-ridged to shallowly ridged (and these often ending in minute, rounded, apical projections), with crown to 0.5-0.7 mm high encircling the base of style; style 2.5-2.8 mm long, terete, glabrous; stigma distinctly expanded. Berries ± globose, ca. 2.6 X 2.5 mm, purple-blue, with sparse minute-glandular hairs; observed fruits apparently still somewhat immature. Seeds rounded pyramidal, 0.3-0.6 mm long, the testa smooth, of isodiametric cells; hilum ovoid, comprising ca. 3/4 of one face of seed.

description: Terrestrial; rhizome 7-10 mm diam., erect, not arborescent, not stoloniferous, the scales 10-20 x 2-5 mm, ovate to lanceolate, concolorous, light brown to brownish yellow, entire; sterile and fertile fronds dimorphic, the sterile ones curving to involute, the fertile erect and skeletonized; sterile fronds 25-70 cm long; stipe 4.5-40.0 cm long, basally stramineous to atropurpureous, the scales 3-15 x 1-3 mm, lanceolate, yellowish, with an entire to short-ciliate margin; blade 20-35 × 5.5-11.5 cm, pinnate, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, slightly to strongly reduced at the base, without vestigial pinnae, the terminal pinna similar in form to the lateral pinnae; sterile pinnae 1.5-6 x 0.5-1.0 cm, 22-26 pairs, the basal ones commonly retroflex, the medial and distal ones perpendicular to the rachis, sometimes falcate at apex, strongly involute, sessile but not adnate, the margins entire, the veins impressed; rachis without papillae, stramineous to brownish yellow, densely scaly, the scales 1-5 x 0.5-2.0 mm, stellate to lanceolate, yellowish, with dentate to ciliate margins; costa stramineus, densely scaly, the scales 1-3 mm long, similar to the rachis scales; fertile fronds a little longer than the sterile; stipe (10-) 20-45 cm long; fertile pinna 3.0-5.5 x 0.2-0.4 cm, dark brown adaxially, arching at the apex; aerophores present.

description: Plants terrestrial. Rhizomes erect, ca. 100 x 5 cm. Fronds ca. 100-135 cm, 1-pinnate. Stipes 40-50 x 1-1.5 cm, densely scaly, the scales 10-15 x 1-2 mm, concolorous, brown, lustrous, linear-lanceolate, the margins with minute bifid teeth 0.05-0.1 mm long. Laminae 60-95 x 40-48 cm, subcoriaceous, ovate-lanceolate, beyond the middle the pinnae adnate for their entire width, the lamina apex confluent and pinnatifid, consisting of 4-6 pairs of entire segments separated by rounded sinuses. Rachises straight, densely scaly, the scales 5-16 x 0.5-2 mm, brown, the margins with bifid teeth like those of stipes. Free pinnae 3-4 pairs, 20-27 x 5.0-6.5 cm, subequilateral, alternate, oblongelliptic, sessile, apices rounded to acute, margins entire, reflexed, followed by another 3-4 pairs of broadly adnate pinnae, costae nonalate adaxially, densely scaly abaxially, the scales 5-9 mm, like those of the stipes. Veins free, 2-3-forked, running ± parallel to the pinna margins just beyond the basal forks, bearing hyaline, catenate, adpressed hairs mostly 0.5-1 mm long, abaxial surfaces glabrous between veins. Sori 8-11 mm long, diplazioid (back-to-back on both sides of viens), primarily confined to distal pinnae and lobes of apical segment. Indusia linear along the veins, tan, erose. Spores 40-48 × 28-36 µm.

description: Perennial herbs, 60-120 cm high, densely cespitose, forming large tussocks, not rhizomatous. Innovation intravaginal. Culms green, basal third 1.5-2.7 mm thick, scabrous at least near the top, with 2-3 nodes; ligule of culm leaves a fimbriate rim, often slashed, 0.3-1 mm long; lamina conduplicate, rarely flat and then 1-3 mm wide; lamina of the uppermost culm leaf 6-15 cm long, much shorter than its sheath; lower culm leaves with lamina up to 25 cm long and shorter or about equalling its sheath. Sheaths of innovation leaves open to near base, membranaceous, pale green, abaxially antrorsely scabrous, with long cells with undulate walls, frequent short cells usually longer than wide, and sometimes few silica-suberous couples on the ribs and with long cells and scattered short cells usually shorter than wide in between, adaxially glabrous, with long cells with straight or slightly undulate walls. Ligules acute, 1.3-2.5(-3.5) mm long, in the upper half with rather dense, weak, deciduous fimbriae 35-60 µm long, lacking auricles. Laminae erect, filiform, conduplicate, 10-50 cm long, 0.5-1 (in outermost leaves to 1.3) mm in diameter, pungent, abaxially scabrous, adaxially with an indument of lax hairs 30-50 µm long. Abaxial leaf epidermis with frequent prickles, short cells, and silicasuberous couples between successive long cells 70-250 x 12-18 µm adjacent to the sclerenchyma strands, exclusively with long cells 250-400 x 14-20 µm and scattered short cells in between. Adaxial leaf epidermis with a marginal row of lax to rather dense stout, short hairs, long cells (with undulate walls), and scattered short cells, the cell rows next to the center with similar cells but the hairs distinctly more delicate. Short cells otherwise lacking on the adaxial side; guard cells of leaf stomata (38-)42-47(-50) µm. Leaves V-shaped in cross section, with 7-9 veins, 7-9 prominent ribs, and 6-8 deep furrows, most veins connected by sclerenchyma girders with the abaxial and adaxial epidermis, additional free sclerenchyma strands along the leaf edges, along adaxial ribs without girders, and sometimes on the abaxial side below some furrows, rarely abaxial sclerenchyma somewhat decurrent from a girder; adaxial epidermis without bulliform cells in the furrows. Panicles 10-30 cm long, 3-10 cm wide, lax, often somewhat nodding, with 3-8 lateral branches with simple to multiple basal branching, with 20-100 spikelets; panicle branches and pedicels scabrous, the latter (0-)2-7(-30) mm long. Spikelets lanceolate, 11-13.7 mm long (11-12.8 mm to tip of fourth lemma), 4-5-flowered; rachilla scabrous except on the palea side, the prickles often accompanied by short cells. Glumes more or less membranaceous, green with broadly scarious margins, sometimes tinged with rose or purple, abaxially scabrous in the upper two thirds and with frequent silica-suberous couples, the long cells 120-280 x 14-18 µm, the glume edges smooth, sometimes apically slightly scabrous; lower glume lanceolate, 1-veined, 5.5-7.5 x 1-1.3 mm, the upper glume lanceolate or elliptic, 3-veined, 6.5-8.5 x 1.5-2.7 mm, 1-1.3 times as long as the lower. Lemmas more or less membranaceous, green, often tinged with purple or rose, 5-veined, 6.5-8.7 x 3-3.7 mm, with an apical awn (0-)0.2-1.2 mm, scabrous above, the abaxial epidermis with long cells 60-160 x 10-15 Rpm and frequent silica-suberous couples; callus glabrous. Paleae about equalling lemma; apex shortly bifid; keels scabrous at least in the upper three fourths and ciliate in the upper half to three fourths; edges ciliate in the upper third to half. Lodicules shortly bifid, glabrous. Anthers 3, 3.3-4 mm long; pollen grains 32-38 im in diameter. Ovaries apically densely long-hairy; mature caryopsis unknown.

description: Canopy trees, reproductive size ca. 22 m tall, diameter unknown. Trunk and bark not recorded. Resin milky. Trichomes on various organs consisting of three types: thick appressed golden hairs to 0.15 mm long, malpighiaceous hairs, and snail-shaped glandular trichomes. Leaves ca. 7.3-20 cm long, 0-2-jugate; petiole 1.5-6.2cm long, 0.9-1.7 mm diam; interjuga ca. 3 cm long; petiole and rachis with dense appressed hairs; lateral petiolules 0.6-0.8 cm long, deeply canaliculate, pulvinuli not apparent; terminal petiolule ca. 2.6 cm long, the pulvinulus present but inconspicuous; all lateral leaflets 5- 8.1 x 2.4-4.2 cm, (broadly) oblong-elliptic to slightly obovate; terminal leaflet 5.5-0.6 x 3.2-4.6 cm, obovate; leaflet apex rounded and retuse, rarely slightly broadly acuminate and the acumen to 0.1 cm long; leaflet base acutely to obtusely cuneate, subsymmetric on laterals; margin flat; leaflets coriaceous, drying gray-brown; abaxial surface glossy, the midvein and secondaries acutely prominent, remaining veins prominulous, the midvein and some secondaries with scattered appressed hairs, rest of surface with scattered malpighiaceous hairs; adaxial surface glossy, the midvein inconspicuous to flat and sunk in a groove, remaining veins prominulous, the surface entirely glabrous. Inflorescences 2.7-12.6 cm long, 1.2-2.5 mm diam in fruit, usually longer than petiole of subtending leaves, pseudospicate, the axes with dense to sparse appressed hairs and snail-shaped glands. Bracts subtending inflorescences not seen; those on primary axes at least 1 mm long; bracteoles subtending cymules 0.6-0.8(-1) mm long; all bracts broadly subulate to ovate, coriaceous, with dense appressed hairs. Staminate flowers not seen. Pistillate flowers (known from one flower and persistent parts on fruits) with calyx ca. 0.9-1 mm long, taller than the disk, shallowly cupular, pubescence as on inflorescence, the lobes 0.5- 0.7 mm, rounded perdepressed-deltate, the apex acute and papillate; petals (color unknown) 2.2-2.5 x 1.25-1.3 mm (dry), ovate, fleshy, suberect, apex acute, with an inconspicuous inflexed apiculum to 0.2 mm long, the abaxial pubescence as on calyx, the adaxial surface glabrous and not papillate, the margin short-papillate; staminodes in two unequal series but their anthers overlapping in height and both reaching the stigmas, the antesepalous series ca. 1.1 mm long with anthers ca. 0.3 mm long (dry), the antepetalous series 0.85-1.05 mm long with anthers 0.25-0.3 mm long, the filaments narrowly strap-shaped, the anthers dorsifixed, in dorsal view the antesepalous ones lanceolate, the ante-petalous ones oblong to oblong-ovate; disk glabrous (measurements not possible); pistil ca. 0.9 x 0.8 mm, the ovary sessile and broadly ovoid, with dense appressed hairs, the style ca. 0.2 x 0.3 mm, unbranched, glabrous, the stigmatic area ca. 0.2 mm high, the stigmas sub-sessile, lateral, slightly sigmoid-caudiculate and spiculate. Fruits 1.2-1.6 x 1-1.3 cm (to 1.9 cm wide when more than one pyrene develops), borne on a pedicel (0-)0.7-1.1 long and 1.7-3 mm diam, maroon, obliquely ovoid, the apex very slightly acuminate, the base sessile and slightly cordate; surface relatively smooth, with sparse to scattered appressed hairs toward the apex and base; mature pyrenes, seeds, germination, and seedlings unknown.

description: Arbor 7-20 m alta, ramis junioribus ferrugineis tomentosis vel sericeis. Laminae foliorum 8-12 cm longae, 2.7-3.5(-3.8) cm latae, subcoriaceae, anguste ellipticae vel ellipticae vel oblanceolatae, ad marginem integrae, ad basem acutae, ad apicem acuminatae, maturitate supra glabrae, subtus dense sericeae; petiolus 5-9 mm longus. Inflorescentia axillaris, condensatim spicata, bracteis bracteolisque ovatis vel orbicularibus, 1-1.5 mm longis, 1-1.5 mm latis; calyces lobis ovatis, sericeis, 2-3 mm longis, 1-1.2 mm latis; corolla rosea, campanulata, 8-11 mm longa, glabra, basaliter lobis oblanceolatis, 2-3 mm latis; stamina multiseriata; stylus basaliter pilosus, 10-12 mm longus. Fructus pilosus, ellipsoideus vel subglobosus, 6-8 mm longus, 3-5 mm latus, 3-locularis.

description: Trees 7-20 m tall; vegetative buds, juvenile branches, and inflorescences densely sericeous to tomentose, the hairs 0.5-0.8 mm long, reddish brown. Petioles densely to sparsely (on older leaves) sericeous abaxially, 5-9 mm long, ca. 1 mm wide. Leaf blades subcoriaceous, narrowly elliptic or elliptic to oblanceolate, 8-12 x 2.7-3.5(-3.8) cm, margin entire, undulate, apex acuminate, base acute, abaxially densely sericeous with secondary veins elevated, adaxially glabrous with the midvein not impressed, slightly raised. Inflorescences fasciculate, with 10-16 sessile flowers; bracts and bracteoles 1-1.5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, deciduous, broadly ovate to orbicular, sericeous abaxially. Calyx 5-lobed, the lobes ovate, 2-3 mm long, 1-1.2 mm wide at the base, densely sericeous abaxially, margins ciliate (but this obscured by pubescence). Corolla sympetalous, campanulate, 8-11 mm long, 5-lobed, pink; lobes connate basally for 3-4 mm and adnate to the filaments for 3-5 mm at the base, narrowly to broadly oblanceolate, abaxially sparsely sericeous near the apex, apically rounded, 2-3 mm wide, entire to minutely ciliate distally. Stamens 3-4-seriate; filaments connate basally for 4-5 mm, the free portions of outermost filaments linear-oblong, 1-15 × ca. 0.75 mm. Ovary inferior, villous at the summit, sericeous on the sides; style straight, pilose on basal half, 10-12 mm long; stigma irregularly 3-lobed. Fruits drupaceous, densely to sparcely pilose, broadly ellipsoid to subglobose, 6-8 mm long (not including persistent sepals), 3-5 mm diam., 3-celled in cross section with a rounded bony endocarp.

description: Habitus scandens; stipulae 2.5-3.5 mm latae; petioli in parte media vel in parte infra medium biglandulosi; folia peltata, bilobata, basi cordata, lobis lateralibus acutis vel raro attenuatis, lobis centralibus obtusis, marginibus integris; pedicelli ebracteati; stipites fructuum 6.9-8.5 mm longi; fructus ellipsoidei vel globosi; semina 4.6-4.9 x 2.9-3.1 mm, retifoveata, chalaza obtusa vel obsoleta.

description: Vine, pubescent throughout; all surfaces antrorsely appressed-puberulent, trichomes 0.06-0.08 x 0.02 mm; petiole, adaxial leaf surface, and stipules with unicellular curved trichomes 0.28-0.38 x 0.03 mm. Stems terete or somewhat compressed, 1.5-1.8 mm diam. Stipules ovate, acute to acuminate, 6.3-7.5 x 2.5-3.5 mm; petioles 2.3-2.6cm long, commonly bearing 2 nectaries at or just below the middle (0.44-0.5 of the distance from the base toward the apex of the petiole), the nectaries elliptic, opposite to subopposite, sessile, discoid with the rims slightly raised, 1.0-1.1 mm wide (on the widest axis), 0.5-0.6 mm high. Laminas 3.8-5.3 x 12.4-14.2 cm, membranous, slightly peltate (the distance from leaf base to point of petiole insertion 1-1.7mm), transversely elliptic, 3-lobed 0.02-0.1 of the distance to the leaf base at the deepest sinus, the lateral lobes elliptic, acute to attenuate, 6.9-7.5 x 2.6-4.2 cm, the central lobe elliptic or present as an obtuse to rounded tip, the central vein 3.7-5.2cm long (measured from point of petiole insertion to leaf apex), the angle between the lateral lobes 109-130', the ratio of lateral lobe to central vein length 1.4-1.9, the margins entire, hyaline; primary veins 3, diverging and branching above base; laminar nectaries absent; tendril 0.7-0.9 mm wide, present at flowering node. Pedicels 11.9- 13 x 0.5 mm in fruit, paired in the leaf axils; bract(s) absent. Flowers not seen. Stipe 6.9- 8.5 x 0.5-0.6 mm in fruit. Androgynophore 4.1-4.8 x 1.1-1.3mm in fruit. Berry 25- 26 x 24-26 mm, ellipsoid to globose, very dark purple. Seeds ca. 20, obovate in outline, 4.6-4.9 mm long, 2.9-3.1 mm wide, 2- 2.1 mm thick, reticulate-foveate with each face marked with 22-26 foveae, chalazal beak obtuse or obsolete, micropylar beak acute.

description: Plants low, compact, densely matted, densely pubescent, long-lived perennials (0.3-)0.5-3 dm across with reddish stems and gray-green foliage arising from a deepseated taproot terminated by a buried, densely branched caudex system of up to several hundred branches, each ending in a tufted cluster of leaves. Trichomes substipitate, stellate with 8-13 rays, these usually bifurcate, rays not fused at their bases, tuberculate but less so over the low-mounded center. Stems 1(-2) per tufted cluster of leaves, 1-6(-8) cm long, simple. Leaves basal and cauline, cuneate, not significantly differentiated into a blade and petiole but nonetheless petiolate, persistent on the buried caudex branches but branches not densely covered and thickened by persistent leaf-bases; basal leaf-blades narrowly elliptic to narrowly linear-oblanceolate, apically acute, (8-)10-15 x (0.8-)1-1.8 mm, entire, flattened, not repand; cauline leaf-blades similar, sometimes linear and then 0.5-0.8 mm wide. Inflorescences (2-)4-12-flowered. Flowers with sepals 2.5-3.5(-4) mm long, narrowly elliptic, rounded on back, not keeled; petals entire, yellow, 4-7 mm long, narrowly spatulate. Infructescences elongate; fruiting pedicels becoming distinctly sigmoid and horizontal with the siliques erect or nearly so, 5-10 mm long. Siliques ellipsoid, compressed, 4-6 mm long, densely pubescent with appressed trichomes exteriorly, glabrous interiorly; styles 2-3.5 mm long, sparsely pubescent; ovules 1 per locule; seeds 1-2 per silique, oval, yellowish brown to brown, 2-2.5 x 1.5-2 mm.
bibliographicCitation: O'Kane, Steven L., Jr. & Reveal, James L. 2006. Physaria pulvinata (Brassicaceae), a new species from southwestern Colorado. Brittonia. 58 (1): 74-77.

description: Understory or (sub-)canopy trees, reproductive size 8-30 m tall, 12-40 cm diam. Trunk angular, buttresses absent. Bark: outer bark smooth, reportedly gray (Kernan & Phillips 1146) or tan with "long horizontal lenticels" [hoop marks?](Harmon 331); inner bark not recorded. Resin milky. Trichomes on various organs of 6 types: flexuous hairs to 0.3 mm long, fine erect white bristles to 0.1 mm long, snail-shaped glandular trichomes, thick golden appressed hairs to 0.1 mm long, stiff golden erect trichomes to 0.1 mm long, and dense ascending to appressed hairs 0.25-0.3 mm long. Leaves clustered distally on branchlets, 46.5-99.7 cm long, 4-7-jugate (sometimes 3-jugate in new flushes); petiole 9.2-33.7 cm long, 3.5- 5.2 mm diam; interjuga 3.4-8.5 cm long; petiole and rachis with sparse to dense or less often scattered flexuous (rarely ascending) hairs, dense to sparse bristles, and scattered snail-shaped glandular trichomes; lateral petiolules 0.6-1.4 cm long, canaliculate, pulvinuli not evident; terminal petiolule 2.2-5.2cm long, the distal pulvinulus inconspicuous; basal leaflets 13.2-19.1 x 4.2-9.4 cm, (narrowly) ovate or less often oblong-elliptic; other lateral leaflets 16.5-33.5 x 4.6-10 cm, (narrowly) oblong-elliptic or sometimes slightly oblanceolate; terminal leaflet 15.6- 24.5 x 5.6-8.6cm, oblanceolate to (oblong-) elliptic or rarely obovate; leaflet apex abruptly and broadly short-acuminate to abruptly or rather gradually and narrowly long-acuminate, the acumen 0.2-2 cm long, sometimes retuse and usually mucronate; leaflet base obtuse to truncate, subsymmetric on lateral leaflets; margin flat; leaflets chartaceous, drying tan; abaxial surface dull, all veins acutely prominent, the midvein and secondary veins with sparse bristles, scattered thick appressed hairs, and scattered snail-shaped glandular trichomes, sometimes the rest of the surface with a few scattered malpighiaceous hairs; adaxial surface dull, the midvein narrowly prominulous but sunk in a groove, secondaries flat to prominulous, remaining veins narrowly prominent, the surface altogether glabrous. Inflorescences dimorphic: staminate inflorescences 14-39cm long, 2.4-4.5mm diam, longer than the petiole of the subtending leaves, the secondary axes well-developed, to 13.6 cm long; pistillate inflorescences (based only on fruiting specimens) 8.2-17 cm long, 2-4 mm diam, shorter than the petiole, the secondary axes poorly developed; inflorescence axes with dense to sparse bristles and dense ascending to appressed hairs; pedicel on staminate flowers 0.7-1.3 mm, 0.4-0.5 mm diam, sometimes somewhat clavate, pedicel on pistillate flowers not seen. Bracts subtending inflorescences not seen, those on primary axes 0.8-1.7 mm long, subu- late, bracteoles subtending cymules or flowers 0.2-0.25 mm long, subulate to ovate, all with hairs as on inflorescence. Staminate flowers 2.2-2.7 mm long; calyx 0.6-1 x 2-2.4 mm, shallowly cupular, taller than the disk, with dense appressed hairs, the lobes 0.2-0.4 mm long, (rounded) depressed-deltate with slightly acuminate apex; petals greenish-yellow or cream-yellow or white, 1.8- 2.3 x 0.8-1.1mm, narrowly ovate, with a weakly inflexed apiculum 0.1-0.3 mm long, the abaxial surface with dense short appressed hairs, the adaxial surface glabrous and non-papillate; stamens in two unequal series but their anthers overlapping in height, the ante-sepalous series 2-2.25 mm long with anthers 0.6-0.7 mm long, the antepetalous series 1.4- 1.8 mm long with anthers 0.65-0.8 mm long, the filaments relatively broadly strap-shaped at base, the anthers dorsifixed, in dorsal view the antesepalous ones lanceolate, the antepetalous ones lanceolate to narrowly ovate, in lateral view both series oblique-oblong; disk 0.2-0.35 mm high, 0.2-0.3 mm thick, shorter than the pistillode, glabrous; pistillode 0.5-0.65 x 0.35-0.45 mm, (depressed-) ovoid, provided with reduced locules, the surface with dense ascending hairs to 0.1-0.2 mm long, the stylar part 0.2-0.25 mm high, 5-lobulate. Pistillate flowers (known from only one flower and from parts persisting on fruiting specimens) ca. 3 mm long; calyx 0.8- 1 x 2.3 mm, slightly taller than the disk, the lobes ca. 0.3 mm long, depressed-deltate; petals 2.4-2.5 x 1.25-1.5 mm, (broadly) ovate, with a weakly inflexed apiculum 0.1- 0.2 mm long; staminodes strongly dimorphic (anthers of the two series not overlapping in height), the antesepalous series ca. 1.75 mm long with anthers 0.45-0.5 mm long, taller than the pistil, the antepetalous series 1-1.1 mm long with anthers 0.4-0.45 mm long, the filaments relatively broadly strap-shaped at base, in dorsal view the antesepalous anthers lanceolate, the antepetalous ones narrowly ovate; disk ca. 0.35mm high, 0.1- 0.15mm thick, glabrous; pistil ca. 1.1 x 0.65 mm, ovary (depressed-) ovoid, sessile, both ovary and style with dense ascending hairs, the style 0.2 x 0.2mm, the stigmatic area 0.2-0.25 mm high, the stigmas laterally short-sigmoid, bulbous at the base, the lateral length ca. 0.25mm. Fruit 2.8-3.4 x 2.9- 3.5 cm (all known specimens have fruits with more than one locule developed), borne on a terete pedicel 2-3 long and 2.5-3.4 mm diam, brown, depressed-ovoid, the apex usually slightly acuminate but often acute or rarely rounded, the base usually cordate or less often truncate; surface broadly and obtusely rugose- verrucose (more verrucose than rugose), with ridges to 0.7 mm high and with dense golden stiff erect hairs to 0.1 mm long, dense flexuous hairs, and dense snail-shaped glands; valves within pink (one report of red); pseudaril covering pyrene sweet, white, pulpy; pyrene 2.3-2.5 x 1.3-1.4 cm, 0.35-0.45 mm thick, cartilaginous, in dorsiventral view elliptic to lanceolate with acute apex and rounded base, in lateral view the posterior part hemi-elliptic to hemi-ovate, the anterior part hemi-elliptic to hemi-lanceolate, with a negligible cleft at the site of the funicle 28- 30% the distance from the apex; funicular scar semi-circular to slightly oblunate, covering ca. 20% of the anterior surface. Germination and seedlings not seen.

description: Shrubs unarmed, up to branchlets terete, elongate, tomentose, with yellow, spersed trichomes; stipules triangular-lanceolate, rarely lar-lanceolate, usually slightly riaceous, densely sericeous, obscuring the surface, bipinnate; pinnae (3-)4-0.1-0.4 cm long, tomentose, eglandular; rachis (0.7-)1.5-4.2 cm long, tomentose; rachillae (0.9-)1.4-5.2 cm long, tomentose; leaflets 13-38 pairs, 3-5 x 0.6-1.3 mm when fully developed, lanceolate to widely lanceolate, subcoriaceous, the adaxial faces glabrous to sparingly sericeous, lustrous, dark-brown, the abaxial faces sericeous and pale green, the bases usually obliquely-truncate, the margins ciliate, the apices acute. Inflorescences umbellate, with 6-9 flowers; peduncles solitary or fasciculate, axillary, 2.7-5.6 cm long. Flowers homomorphic, sericeous throughout, with soft, long, appressed, white or light-yellow trichomes; pedicels 3-5 mm long; calyx 2-3 mm long, campanulate, the teeth deltate to triangular, membranous; corolla 4.5-6 mm long, campanulate, membranous; filaments ca. 2 cm long at anthesis, red, with the staminal tube included; polyads 8-grained, bisymmetric, with a mucilaginous structure on the basal cell. Pods ascending to descending, to 6.6 x 0.8 cm, linear-oblanceolate, acute at the apex, rostrate, rigidly coriaceous, densely tomentose to velutinous, with white, soft, long, interspersed trichomes. Seeds ca. 6x 4 mm, widely elliptic, dark-brown, with 90% pleurogram.

description: Trunks to 8 m tall, 8-10 cm diam., without old petiole bases, frond scars round, apices hidden in fascicles of petioles; adventitious buds lacking. Fronds 2 -4 m long, presumably arching. Petioles to 40 cm long, prob- ably longer, dull brown to orange-brown, basally blackish, aculeate to muricate, spines with scales on their tips in young petioles; with long elliptic brown pneumathodes to 18 x 1 mm on the sides basally; scruf persistent (Fig. ЗА), white to tan, flakey, consisting of spaced, appressed, round squamules to 0.5 mm diam. with tortuous marginal cilia. Petiole scales 25.0-35.0(-40.0)x 2.5-4. 0(- 5.0) mm, long-lanceolate, shiny, plain deep brown, concolorous or concordantly bicolo- rous with margins paler brown, sometimes yellowish or cream white (Fig. ЗА); scales persistent only on the sides of the petioles. Laminae to 160*70-80 cm, bipinnate-pinnatifid, green to dark green adaxially, often blackish when dried, pale gray-green abax- ially, apices gradually reduced. Rachises inermous or weakly muricate basally, dark yellowish brown to orange-brown, adaxially with whitish to yellowish, antrorsely curved hairs to 0.8 mm long, abaxially glabrous or glabrescent with white to tan squamellae like in the petiole scurf. Pinnae to 45 cm long (Fig. 3B), patent to ascending, basal pinnules only half the size of the medial pinnae, weakly to strongly reflexed. Costae and costules tan, stramineous or dull orange-brown, inermous, short- hairy adaxially, hairs  to 1 mm long, white, antrorsely curved; abaxially glabrescent with white to tan arachnoid scurf and few bright orange-brown flattish scales with undulated, fimbriate margins, most frequently in the axils. Largest pinnules 5.0-6.5x1.1-1.7 cm, linear-oblong to lanceolate, sessile (Fig. 3C) to subsessile (stalked to 1 mm), 1.0-1.5 cm between the stalks, pinnule bases truncate to weakly cuneate, rarely weakly cordate, tips long- acute to attenuate, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, basal segments sometimes remote but not free; segments to 11x3 mm, weakly ascend- ing, falcate, the tips obtuse (Fig. 3D) to round, segment margins crenulate to crenate, often remaining flat when dried; segments with few to many whitish to tan, erect hairs 0.5-0.8(-1.0) mm long on and between the veins abaxially, veins adaxially glabrous or with few short hairs, none between the veins; with relatively few to many small scales abaxially, ranging from broadly ovate, flat ones (to 3.0x2.5 mm) to búllate ones (to 2.5 X 1.0 mm) with broadly flaring or twisted, elongated tips, tan to orange-brown, often with the thin margins paler brown to whitish, fimbriate to lacerate with considerably long processes; sterile veins forked or simple, fertile veins forked. Sori to 1.0 mm diam., subcoastal in forks of veins; indusia absent; receptacles globose to ellipsoid, 0.3-0.4 mm diam, paraphyses thin, hyaline, white to tan, of the same length as or shorter than sporangia (0.3 -0.4 mm). Spores not examined.

description: Epiphytic shrubs, scrambling 2-2.5 m. Twigs and mature branches subterete, bluntly angled, glabrous, the bark of mature branches striate, reddish-brown, somewhat exfoliating; prophylls 2, opposite, valvate, lanceolate, 2- 3.5 mm long, the apex acuminate. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged; petioles subterete, flattened above, (4-)6-8(-10) mm long, glabrous; blades coriaceous, lanceolate, 9- 17x(2- )3- 5.5 cm, the base cunéate, the margin entire and eciliate, the apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; venation pinnate, the midrib thickened and raised in proximal 0.7-2 cm, then impressed distally above, conspicuously raised beneath over entire length, the secondary nerves 2-5 per side, anastomosing near margin, conspicuously to slightly raised above, raised beneath, the tertiary nerves reticulate, conspicuously to slightly raised above, inconspicuously raised beneath. Inflorescences axillary, solitary, racemes, 2-4(-5)-flowered, ramiflorous racemes also sometimes present; bracts   4-8, persistent, ovate, 2-4 mm long, the margin ciliolate with few deciduous hairs, the hairs simple, unicellular and eglandular, the apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; rachises  subterete, angled, 1.5-4.5 cm long, glabrous; floral bract ovate, 1.5^.5 mm long, the margin ciliolate with few, deciduous, simple and multicellular hairs, the apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; pedicels articulate with calyx, 2.6-4.1 cm long, increasing in diameter distally, 1-1.5 mm diam. at base, 4 mm diam. at apex (pedicels shrinking in diameter in dried specimens although the distal swelling still noticeable), glabrous; bracteoles 2, distinct, persistent, nearly basal, subopposite, ovate, 1.5-4.5x0.7 mm, the margin ciliolate with few, deciduous, simple and multicellular hairs, the apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers 5 (-6) merous, diplostemonous. Calyx campanulate overall, terete, 8-11 mm long, green, glabrous, the aestivation valvate; tube cylindric and basally truncate, 4-6 mm long, minutely rugose; limb 4-6 mm long, thinner in texture at margins; lobes reduced to just a tip, 1 x 4- 5.5 mm, the margin eciliate, the apex apiculate; sinuses broadly rounded. Corolla bistratose, very fleshy (up to 3 mm thick distally and 1 mm basally), rose to red with the lobes white, urceolate, inflated at base, 0.8-1.5 cm long, 1-2.2 cm diam. (0.4-1 cm in dried specimens), glabrous without, shortly tomentose within above the throat, the hairs simple, unicellular and wavy, the aestivation valvate; lobes ovate, 3-3.5x3.5-4 mm, the apex acute. Stamens 10, included, alternating in length, 10.5-10.8 and 11-12 mm long; filaments connate into a tube, alternating in length, 4.5-5.5 and 5-6 mm long, glabrous; anthers equal, distinct, 6.3-7.5 mm long; thecae 4.3-5 mm long, prognathous, with or without basal appendage, sometimes with few minute unicellular hairs arising from appendage, otherwise smooth with cells shaped like jigsaw-puzzle pieces; tubules 2, distinct, 2- 3 mm long, smooth, dehiscing by latrorse slits running from tip of tubules into lower half of thecae, 4-4.5 mm long. Ovary 5-locular, placentation axile; style included, 1.4-1.6 cm long. Immature berry, spherical, at least 1 2 mm diam., red.

description: Shrub or treelet to 4 m, upper stems subquadrangular, lower stems not seen, glabrous or bearing few, scattered trichomes. Leaves with petioles 1.5-3.8 cm long, glabrous, cystoliths dense; laminae elliptic to oblanceolate, 10-22 x 3-7.2 cm, 3.1-3.3 times longer than wide, apices acuminate, bases acute, margins entire to repand, both surfaces glabrous or abaxial surface with few scattered trichomes, adaxial veins raised slightly above surface, cystoliths visible on both surfaces, more notable on adaxial surface, very dense along veins, both laminal surfaces with inconspicuous, patelliform glands, drying dark red or black. Inflorescences terminal, of 1-2 pedunculate racemes, peduncles 1.5-4 cm long, densely covered in short, erect, glandular trichomes, racemes to 14 cm long. Bracts paired at each node, elliptic to oblanceolate, greenish-yellow, most proximal pair usually leaf-like, 50-60 x 5-10mm decreasing to ca. half this size toward distal nodes, apices of proximal bracts acuminate, more distal bracts oblanceolate, apically rounded, pubescent as peduncles, one bract per node usually sterile (i.e., only one flower per node), paired bracteoles subtending each flower resembling bracts in color and shape but smaller, 22-27 x (2-)4-7 mm, with scattered often glandular trichomes. Flowers pedicellate, pedicels to 5 mm long, pubescent as peduncles. Calyx pale yellowish-green, (11-)15-18 x 1.5-2.0 mm, fused portions ca. 2 mm long, free portion 9-16mm long, pubescent as bracteoles. Corolla yellow or yellowish-green basally and narrow unexpanded portion tube 30-34x2-3mm (pressed), expanded portion 38-40mmx 12-13mm (pressed) at mouth, lobes ca. 1 cm wide, length uncertain but very short compared to tube, orientation uncertain, with scattered glandular and eglandular trichomes, denser on tube. Stamens strongly didydamous, apex of anther of shorter pair 66-69 mm from base of corolla, apex of anther of longer pair 72-74 mm from base of corolla, free portions of filaments ca. 13 mm long (shorter) and 18 mm long (longer), fused portion of filaments ca. 50 mm long, fused filament sheath ("curtain") enclosing ca. 3/4 of unexpanded portion of tube, anthers 5-6 mm long, dorsal connective with two parallel rows of glandular trichomes, styles ca. 7 cm long, stigmas 2.5-3 mm long, bifid, the dorsal lobe reduced to ca. 1 the length of longer lobe. Fruits clavate, 16-18 mm long x 6 mm wide, stipe 5-6 mm long, seed bearing portion 11-12 mm long, puberulent, trichomes often glandular Seeds not seen.

description: Shrub to 1 m, young stem weakly quadrangular, densely pilose with minute trichomes <0.25 mm long, erect to upwardly ascending, older stems not seen. Leaves with petioles to 10.5 cm long, pubescent as young stem, laminae broadly ovate, 14-24 x 8-16cm, ca. 1.6 times longer than wide, apices acute to acuminate, bases rounded, margins crenate to entire, abaxial surfaces pubescent as stem, mostly along veins, adaxial surfaces essentially glabrous, cystoliths visible on both surfaces but more obvious above, both laminal surfaces with sessile, patelliform glands, drying pale to dark red. Inflorescence axillary, of much branched cymose panicles, peduncles 14.5-17cm long, pubescent as young stems, proximal nodes mostly bearing branches, more distal nodes with flowers either terminally or in one of leaf axils. Bracts subtending first major branches elliptic, 4-5 x 0.7-1.3 cm, bracts at more distal nodes similar but smaller and appearing bracteole-like, these narrowly lanceolate, rounded apically, ±1 mm long, pubescent as leaves, with patelliform glands as on leaves, bracteoles not seen. Flowers with pedicels 1-3 mm long, trichomes pubescent <0.25 mm long, mostly eglandular, few glandular, mixed orientation. Calyx 7-10 × ca. 1 mm, fused portion 1-1.5 mm long, free portions 6-9 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, calyx slightly accrescent in fruit to 10-12 mm long, pubescent as pedicels, often more densely pubescent within. Corolla pale green, outer surface sparcely pubescent with trichomes as on petioles, unexpanded portion of tube 2.1-2.5 cm long, expand portion 1.8-2.0 cm, lobes 4-5 × 4-5 mm, rounded at apex. Stamens extending to mouth of corolla, not strongly didynamous, apex of anthers ca. 45 mm from base of corolla, free portions of filaments 16-18 mm long, long, fused portions of filaments 25-28 mm long, fused filament sheath ("curtain") not seen, anthers 3-4 mm long, basally mucronate, styles nearly 5 cm long, stigma extending just beyond anthers at anthesis, bifid, ventral lobe ca. 2 mm long, dorsal lobe reduced ca. 0.5 mm. Fruits clavate, to 25 mm long x 6 mm wide, 4 mm thick, stipe 15 mm long, seed bearing portion 10 mm long, pubescent with minute erect eglandular and glandular trichomes. Seeds to 8, at least 3 mm in diam, but mature seeds and hygroscopic trichomes not seen.

description: Rhizomes short-creeping, dorsiventral, scaly; the scales 0.2-0.3 cm long, yellowish, lanceolate, the margins conspicuously ciliate. Fronds 10-60 X 1.5-3(-4) cm, with indeterminate growth, pendulous; stipes 1- 3(-4) X 0.05-0.1 cm, dark brown, with conspicuous castaneous setae, to 0.2 cm long; laminae pinnatisect, linear-lanceolate, papyraceous, gradually tapering to both ends; rachises sclerenchymatous, black to dark brown; segments 1.2-2.5 X 0.3-0.5 cm, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, perpendicular to slightly oblique to the rachises, conspicuously asymmetric at the base, decurrent basiscopically and cuneate acroscopically, the apex round to obtuse; indument of simple castaneous setae on the stipe, rachises and laminae, clustered stellate setae on the costae and margins, and scattered, hyaline hairs on the stipes and ra- chises; sinuses narrower than the width of the segments; veins free, 1-furcate, ending submarginally, inconspicuous or visible only at the base of the segments; hydathodes inconspicuous, lime dots lacking. Sori round, arising at the veins apex; sporangia conspicuously ciliate, the cilia 1- 1.5X as long as the sporangia.

description:
Tibouchina limoeirensi Brade affinis, ramulorum pilis basaliter non protractis foliorum laminis mi- noribus cordulatis hypanthiis sparsiuscule strigulosis calycisque lobis brevioribus differt.

Ramuli primum obscure rotundato-quadrangulati mox teretes sicut inflorescentia pilis plerumque 0.3-0.6 mm longis laevibus ad basim non protractis sparsius- cule strigulosi. Petioli 0.5-0.8 cm longi; lamina 2.5-3.5 x 1-1.5 cm lanceolato- oblonga apice acuta basi paullulo (1-2 mm) cordata, coriacea, supra dense bullis setuliferis (setula ca 0.5 mm longa) obsita, subtus in superficie foveolata et pilis laevibus 0.5-1 (in foveolis 0.1-0.2) mm longis densiuscule setulosa, 5-nervata. Panicula 3-4 cm longa submultiflora; flores 5-meri; pedicelli 2-3 mm longi, bracteolis ca 3 x 1-1.2 mm oblongis intus glabris extus sparse strigulosis ante an- thesim deciduis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 4-4.5 mm longum pilis laevibus ca 0.7-1 mm longis sparsiuscule strigulosum; calycis tubus 0.2 mm longus, lobi 4- 4.5 x 1.7-2 mm oblongo-lanceati acuti intus glabri extus sparse strigulosi ciliolati post anthesim decidui. Petala 16-19 x 13-15 mm obovata apice rotundato-truncata apicem versus ciliolata alioque glabra. Stamina dimorpha; filamenta 5.4-5.5 mm vel 4 mm longa basim versus modice glanduloso-setulosa. Stamina maiora: thecae 4.8 x 0.4 mm rectae poro 0.1 mm diam; connectivum 0.7-1 mm prolongatum, lobis ventralibus brevibus 8-10-glandulosis. Stamina minora: thecae 4 mm longae curvatae poro 0.4 mm diam; connectivum 0.4 mm prolongatum, lobis ventralibus ca 0.2 mm longis eglandulosis. Stylus 6 x 0.5 mm glaber; ovarii pili eglandulosi.

description: Trunks absent, rhizomes short-ascending, branching in posterior parts; apices hidden in fascicles of petioles (Fig. 2A). Fronds 45- 110 cm long, erect (Fig. 2 A). Petioles 15- 36 cm long, dark-brown to blackish, weakly shiny, inermous; scurf brown, dense, consisting of variously sized, erect to appressed, ovate to lanceolate squamules with fimbriate margins and brown tortuous hairs to 1 mm long; without pneumathodes; densely scaly proximally, mod- erately to sparsely so in distal parts. Petiole scales to 12.0-20.0x2.0-3.5 mm, lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate (Fg. 2B), shiny, concolo- rous or weakly bicolorous, deep brown with margins yellowish to cream white, the tips elongate, undulate, not twisted, differentiated margins narrow with cells strongly exerted, shortly dentate, without setae or cilia. Laminae to 30-85x25-35 cm, bipinnate to bipinnate- pinnatifid, long-triangular to lanceolate (Fig. 2 A), coriaceous, dark green adaxially, black when dried, gray-green abaxially, apices gradually reduced, tapering. Rachises inermous, dark brown to castaneous, densely hairy on both sides but glabrescent, with brown, twisted, pluricellular hairs to 1.0 mm long, also with scattered, lanceolate to linear scales to 4 mm long. Pinnae to 17 cm long, weakly ascending, stalked to 5 mm, mostly alternate (Fig. 2 A), fully pinnate only in proximal halves, narrowly green alate distally; basal pinnae about the size of the medial pinnae, not reflexed, sometimes opposite. Costae dark-brown to castaneous, inermous, adaxially densely hairy with whitish to tan, antrorsely curved, pluricellular, uniseri- ate hairs to 1 .0 mm long, abaxially glabrescent with sparser twisted hairs and few concolorous brown, lanceolate scales with whitish, shortly fimbriate margins, most frequently in the axils; junctures of rachises and costules not swollen, each abaxially with a circular, prominent pneumathode to 1 mm diam., dark gray to black in dried specimens. Largest pinnules/ultimate segments (10-)20.0-40.0x(4.0-)8.0-14.0 mm, oblong to oblanceolate, subsessile to sessilec ca. 0.7 cm between the midveins, cuneate to weakly cordate at base, tips obtuse to rounded, patent, weakly ascending, straight to distally falcate, margins shallowly to deeply crenate with entire lobes, often revolute when dried; segments with few whitish to tan, erect hairs 0.5-0.8(-1.0) mm long on the veins abaxially, restricted to the midveins/costules adaxially, none between the veins; with few to many dark-brown scales on the mid- veins/costules abaxially, ovate-lanceolate, flat or búllate, to 2.0 x 0.8 mm with weakly dentate-lacerate margins; veins weakly protruding abaxially, planar or sunken adaxially, sterile veins forked or simple, fertile veins forked. Sori to 1.0-1.2 mm diam., subcostal to inframedial, on the back of vein (Fig. 2D); indusia sphaeropteroid, with prominent umbo, shiny dark brown, translucent; receptacles globose, 0.3- 0.4 mm diam, paraphyses thin, hyaline, tan to brown, of the same length as the sporangia (0.4 mm). Spores ca. 0.04 mm diam., exospore verrucate, perispore lacking ( Young 5236 , USM).

description: Unbranched subshrub to 20 cm tall without the scape, 1 m tall with the scape. Stems shortvillous. Stipules lanceolate, caducous, 6.5-7.0 x 1.0-2.0 mm. Leaf whorls 6-7 per node; petiole 2.5-5.0cm long, flattened and broadened at base; blade obovate, coriaceous, 5.5-18.5 x 0.5-5.0 cm, apex obtuse-rounded, emarginate, acute or short-cuspidate, margin entire, base acute, decurrent on the petiole, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface glabrous or subglabrous, sparsely puberulous to villous on midrib; venation brochidodromous; midrib prominent abaxially, secondary veins 10-15 pairs, prominulous on abaxial surface. Synflorescence a terminal thyrse of cincini; 70-97cm long; rachis densely shortvillous or sparsely short-villous to glabrous, cincinnus peduncle 8-12mm long; cincinnus 1-, 2- or multiflorous; pedicel 4-9.5 mm long. Bud straight or curved, 7-15 x 1.5-2.5 mm, apex rounded; spur recurved, apex rounded or obtuse, 3.5-8.5 mm long, smaller calyx lobes unequal, abaxial surface tomentose, adaxial surface glabrous, margin ciliate. Petals 3, both surfaces glabrous, central ones 7-11 mm long, lateral ones 5.5-9.5 mm long. Stamen 1, filament 2-4.5 mm long, anther 8-10.5 mm long, glabrous, boat-shaped, base sometimes sagittate; staminodes 2, glabrous, 0.7-1.3 mm long. Ovary subconical, ferruginous-tomentose, 1-2.5 x 1.5-2 mm. Style 9.5-12 mm long, glabrous, stigma terminal. Fruit to 2.61 x 1.54 cm, the surface verrucose, tomentose. Seed narrowly elliptic, laterally flattened, oily, ca. 13.3 x 4.2 mm, wing ca. 6 mm long, seminiferous core basal, ca. 5.3 mm long, black.

description:
Shrub 1.8-5 m tall and up to 30 cm thick at base. Stems terete, somewhat sulcate after drying; young stems and thorns scabrescent with deltoid tuberculae ca. 0.05 mm long, glabrate in age. Leaves cuneate to triangular, 0.5-1.4 mm long, borne at the base of thorns or buds, caducous. Thorns straight, terete, 17-60 x 1.7-3 mm, occasionally somewhat sulcate upon drying, gradually narrowed to a brownish to black glabrous, spinose apex, glabrate in the upper half, the lower half puberulent-asperous with broadbased trichomes ca. 0.05 mm long. Inflorescence 10-15-flowered raceme, 30-50 mm or more long, the axis irregularly angled, puberulent asperous with broad based trichomes; pedicels 1.4-4 mm long, glabrate, slightly enlarged at the summit; bracts subulate triangular, 0.25- 0.4 mm long, glabrate, each with a pair of linear subulate stipules, 0.1-0.2 long.

Sepals ovate trullate, ca. 0.8 x 0.8 mm, the margins entire to irregularly and obscurely denticulate. Petals white to creamy yellow green to clear green, cymbiform, 2.5-3 x 1- 1.25 mm, 3-5-nerved from the base, apices acute, tending to roll when dried. Stamens 8, the filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, thickest about one-third from the base; anthers 0.8 mm long. Pollen tricolpate, spherical when fresh, 10- 15 im in diameter, normally ellipsoid after drying, the surfaces rugose. Pistil 0.8-1.2 mm long; stipe 0.3-0.5 mm long; ovary ovoid, 0.4-0.5 mm in diameter, the surfaces rugose; style 0.1-0.2 mm long, striate-rugose, straight (erect) in dried condition; stigma trilobed, much wider than the style immediately below it. Berry color unknown, globose, ca. 4 mm in diameter. Seed cochleate, ca. 3-3.5 mm in diameter, ca. 1.8 mm thick, the surfaces reticulate muricate.

description: Shrub or small tree to 5 m tall, with Rauh's architectural model. Indumentum of multicellular, ferruginous stellate-peltate scales (these often with a slightly raised central region and a fringe of radiating cells) and multicellular, stout non-glandular setae 0.7-2.5 mm long (along the leaf margins). Young twigs slightly quadrangular, with the interpetiolar face (in relation to the distally adjacent node) slightly concave, and the adjacent sides slightly convex, becoming terete with age, the indumentum of moderate to dense, appressed, peltate scales, some of these falling with age; internodes 0.4-10.2 cm long, the proximal the longest, and becoming shorter distally. Leaves with petiole 2.5-8(-12) mm long, the indumentum similar to that of the twigs; blade narrowly ovate to elliptic, 1.8-6.3(-9.4)x 0.45-3 cm, 2.1-7 times longer than wide, flat, coriaceous, the apex acute, acuminate, or shortly acuminate, with the tip of the leaf having upturned margins, forming a mucro with an adaxial pocket (acarodomatium), the base narrowly acute to cuneate, the margin plane to sometimes slightly revolute, entire and ciliate, due to presence of stout non- glandular setae, these sometimes deciduous with age; venation acrodromous, suprabasal, with prominent midvein and 4 secondary veins, with the 2 conspicuous secondary veins placed 0.55-3 mm from margin, 2 very inconspicuous ous secondary veins + intramarginal, and numerous percurrent tertiary veins oriented subperpendicular to midvein, the tertiary veins separated by composite intertertiary veins, higher-order veins reticulate; adaxial surface green, the indumentum initially of numerous peltate scales but these quickly deciduous so surface nearly glabrous at maturity, the midvein slightly to strongly impressed, the 2 major secondary veins slightly impressed to flat, the 2 intramarginal secondary veins, tertiary, and higher-order veins flat, the surface smooth and shiny when fresh, but appearing wrinkled and with minute projections (when dry) due to the presence of numerous mostly vertically oriented, megastyloid crystals, their ends subcuticular; abaxial surface pale green, densely covered with peltate-scales (when young) but becoming only moderately covered with such hairs at maturity (with hairs not obscuring the leaf surface), the hairs of two sizes, i.e., large, pale-ferruginous scales 0.15- 0.3 mm across and smaller, dark-ferruginous scales 0.04-0.07 mm across, the midvein prominently raised, major secondary veins prominently to slightly raised, minor secondary veins, tertiary veins, and higher-order veins flat. Inflorescences reduced to a solitary flower, axillary, associated with 1-3 leaf-bearing nodes in the distal portion of the twigs; each flower with two persistent brac- teoles, these ovate to obovate, 5-16 x 2.6- 4.2 mm, the apices shortly acuminate, with an apical pocket domatium on the adaxial surface (formed from the upturned leaf mar- gins), the indumentum similar to that of the leaves. Flowers perfect, actinomorphic, nearly sessile. Hypanthium broadly conic, the free portion 0.5-1.3 mm long, the outer surface with dense, pale-ferruginous peltate-scales, the inner surface glabrous, slightly to clearly 16-ridged, with the ridges extending onto apex of ovary, the apices of the ridges not or only very slightly projecting. External calyx lobes closely associated with internal lobes, each external lobe at the apex of the internal lobe and forming an extension to the length of the lobe, but well demarked from the internal lobe (when viewed on the adaxial surface) because the internal calyx lobes are glabrous adaxially, while the external calyx lobes are densely lepidote adaxially; external calyx lobes 4, extending 0.7-1.6 mm beyond the apex of the internal lobes, narrowly triangular, with acute apex, indumentum of dense peltate scales both adaxially and abaxially; internal calyx lobes 4, 1.4-2.5 x 1.6-4 mm, triangular, densely lepidote abaxially but glabrous adax- ially, the apex acute to shortly acuminate, the margin entire; calyx tube 0.4-1.1 mm long. Petals 4, imbricate in bud, A asymmetrical, ovate-triangular, 3.5-7.2 x2-3.4 mm, glabrous except for a few scales at the apex of the outer petals (in bud), white, apically green-tinged; apex acute, with minute apical projection; margin entire. Stamens 8, the anther ellipsoi- dal, 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous, pale yellow, obscurely sagittate at base, fertile the entire length, and opening by 2 confluent, dorso- apical pores, the filament terete, 2-3 mm long, glabrous, white. Ovary 4-locular, fully inferior, obconic, 1.8-2.7 x 2.9-4 mm, with a glabrous and slightly to moderately ridged apical portion (within hypanthium), and articulated at base of the style, with axile placentation, the placentae extending into the locules; style terete, 3.5- 5.7 mm long, glabrous; stigma + truncate. Berries obconic, 3-4 mm long, 4.5-5.5 mm in diam., reddish (immature), with dense fermrugi- nous peltate scales, with adaxial surface of the calyx lobes also turning red. Seeds angular- obovoid, 0.6-0.8 mm long; testa + smooth, the cells ± isodiametric, with thickened anticlinal walls.

description: Frutex inermis, stipulis ad 11(-15) mm longis, dense sericeis. description: Shrubs unarmed, up to 1.2(-1.5)m tall, erect; branchlets terete, elongate, straight, the younger parts denely tomentose, with white, soft, usually interspersed trichomes, becoming glabrate on the older parts; stipules to 11(-15) mm long, triangular or triangular-lanceolate, usually slightly curved, subcoriaceous, the younger ones densely sericeous, with the vesture obscuring the surface, the older ones losing trichome density, persistent. Leaves bipinnate; pinnae (3-)4-7(-8)-jugate; petioles 0.4-0.8 cm long, eglandular, tomentose; rachis (1.3-)2.3-4.6(-6) cm long, tomentose; rachillae 6-9(-12.5) cm long, tomentose; leaflets 26-38(-50) pairs, (4-)5-9 x (1.5-)2-3 mm when fully developed, narrowly-oblong to lanceolate, sometimes falcate, subcoriaceous, the adaxial faces glabrous and lustrous dark- brown or dark-green, the abaxial faces sericeous and pale-green, the bases usually obliquely-truncate, the margins ciliate, the apices acuminate or acute. Inflorescences umbellate, with 14-26 flowers; peduncles solitary or fasciculate, axillary, (4.6-) 5.4-8.2 cm long. Flowers homomorphic, seri- ceous throughout, with soft, long, appressed, white or light-yellow trichomes; pedicels (2.5-)3-7 mm long; calyx (2-)3-5 mm long, campanulate, the teeth deltate to triangular, sometimes parted toward the base, membranous; corolla 6-10 mm long, tubular-campanulate, membranous; filaments 3-4 cm long at anthesis, red, with the staminal tube included; polyads 8-grained, bisymmetric, with a mucilaginous structure on the basal cell. Pods ascending, to 8.7 cm long, 0.7 cm wide, linear or linear-oblanceolate, acute at the apex, rostrate, rigidly coriaceous, densely tomentose to velutinous, with white, soft, long, interspersed trichomes. Seeds ca. 7 mm long, ca. 3 mm wide, narrowly elliptic, dark brown, with 90% pleurogram.

description: Evergreen tree to ca. 5 m tall, reproductive when less than 2 m tall, the trunk to ca. 7 cm in diameter; bark smooth, gray; exudate scant, clear; pubescence of simple, relatively straight, appressed to semi-erect hairs, mostly 0.15-0.5 mm long; leaf-bearing branchlets terete to somewhat angular in cross-section, 0.8-1. 5 (-2. 5) mm thick, sparsely to densely strigose-pilose. Inflorescences racemose, occasionally 1 -branched, arising from the axils of current leaves, 1 -several- flowered, the flowers more or less spirally arranged, the axes green, more or less terete, (1.4-)2.2-7.8 cmx0.5-0.8 mm, moderately to densely strigose-pilose; bracts elliptic, convex, 0.6-1.2 xca. 0.5 mm, strigose-pilose abaxially, stipulate, the stipules similar to those of the foliage leaves, (0.5-)1. 1-2.2 xCa. 0.1 mm; pedicels terete, 7.5-20 xca. 0.6 mm, moder- ately to densely strigose-pilose; bracteoles lacking; flower buds green, globose to weakly ellipsoid, 5.7-6.7 mm long and nearly as wide, mostly glabrous, sparsely strigose basally. Androecium zygomorphic, glabrous, the stamens of two sizes, the larger stamens 5-7, abaxial, in a single row, the filaments yellow, somewhat compressed longitudinally, tapering apically, 7-9 mm long, ca. 0.4 mm thick near base, the anthers oblong in outline, ca. 2.3 x 1 mm, the smaller stamens 80-90, mostly adaxial, in several rows, the filaments yellow, terete, 4-8 xca. 0.05 mm, the anthers oval in outline, ca. 0.8x0.7 mm. Gynoecium mono- pistillate, light green, glabrous or nearly so, sometimes sparsely pubescent on the stipe, the stipe oval in cross section, dilated basally and apically, 4-4.7 mm long, ca. 0.4 mm thick near middle, the ovary acuate-elliptic in outline, compressed laterally, 3.7-4.2x1.1-1.5 mm, the style lateral or oblique, not well differ- entiated from the ovary, conical, 0.3-0.4 mm long, the stigma punctiform or more or less truncate. Seeds 1 per fruit, maturing black, reniform, adaxially concave, ca. 2.1x1x0.8 cm, the aril adaxial, white, fleshy, fimbriate, convex, ca. 1.8x1.3 cm flattened, covering ca. one-third of seed.

description: Plants terrestrial or saxicolous; rhizomes suberect or erect, stolons absent; rhizome scales 10-15 X 1.0-2.5 mm, linear-lanceolate, ferruginous to castaneous, concolorous to bicolorous with lighter borders, entire or nearly so; sterile and fertile leaves monomorphous; petioles 10-25 cm long, 0.6-0.75 times the length of the leaf, castaneous throughout, lustrous, smooth (not transversely rugulose like the rachis), sparsely scaly especially toward the base, the scales pale brown to tan; laminae 10-18 X 3-7 cm, 1-pinnate, coriaceous, without buds, widest or slightly reduced at the base, tapering toward the apex and terminating in a caudate segment, this 3-5 X 0.5-1.0 cm, usually with a basal lobe; pinnae 1.5-3.6 X 0.4-1.1 cm, 10-14 pairs, oblong with slightly up-curved apices, bases truncate to subcordate, apices obtuse, margins serrulate, revolute; basal pinnae stalked, the stalk to ca. 2 mm long, the suprabasal pinnae becoming sessile, the distalmost 1 or 2 pinnae adnate on the basiscopic side; rachises castaneous, transversely rugulose on both surfaces by short, narrow ridges, sparsely scaly, the scales linear-lanceolate, denticulate, pale brown or tan; aerophores present on the rachis, appearing as inconspicuous, low, dark bumps at the pinna junctures; costae stramineous, smooth (not rugulose), sparsely scaly, adaxially sulcate with a narrow wing on both sides; veins 1-forked, sometimes obscure and slightly sunken, ending in prominent hydathodes; lamina tissue between the veins sparsely and minutely scaly to glabrescent, adaxially glabrous; indusia erose, brown or sometimes black on the inner margin adjacent to the receptacle; spores cream-colored, with raised folds.

description: Plants terrestrial. Rhizomes compact, suberect. Fronds erect, to ca. 115 cm long; stipes ca. 2/3 of frond length, up to 4 mm diam., straw-colored, dark brown at base, grooved adaxially, smooth, glabrous except for a few scales at base; laminae charta- ceous, shiny, 2-pinnate-pinnatifid at base, with 5-7 pinna pairs per frond, the apical portion 1-pinnate-pinnatifid, ending in a broadly based pinnatifid apical pinna; rachises similar to stipes, with scattered hairs adaxially, the hairs reddish brown, 0.1-0.2 mm long, septate. Pinnae: proximal pinna pairs stalked, the stalks ca. 2.5 cm long, opposite, deeply 1-pinnate-pinnatifid, 33 X 20 cm; middle pinnae stalked 1.5 cm, alternate, deeply pinnatifid, short-decurrent on stalks, 24 X 20 cm; distal pinnae sessile, alternate, 7 X 1 cm; costae sulcate adaxially, rounded abaxially, with indument similar to rachises and hairs concentrated in adaxial grooves, lacking awns adaxially; segments subopposite to alternate, oblong, 3.5-9.0 X 0.6-1.0 cm, the margins entire at middle to ser- rulate at apices, the terminal segment of each pinna narrowly deltate, long-acuminate, the sinuses between segments wide, biangulate; venation copiously areolate, the costules prominent especially on abaxial surfaces, with 4-8 areoles adjoining costae between two adjacent costules; veins free near margins and apices of segments. Sori interrupted at sinuses and absent at apices of segments; indusia greenish when young, the margins entire; spores not seen.

description: Arbor 5-10 m alta; ramuli primum paulo rotundato-quadrangulati demum teretes sicut petioli foliorum subtus venae primariae inflorescentiarum axes ramulique modice strigosi pilis laevibus gracilibus 1-2 mm longis. Petioli 3-6.5 cm longi; lamina (7) 11-15.5 X (4) 6-9 cm ovata apice breviter gradatimque hebeti-acuminato basi obtusa, firme membranacea et obscure serrulata incurvo-ciliolata, supra modice bullato-setosa bullis ca 0.5 mm latis altisque seta 1.5-2 mm longa gracili, subtus foveolata et modice setulosa, 7-nervata (pari imframarginali incluso) nervis secundariis ca 3-4 mm inter se distantibus nervulis subtus planis arcte reticulatis (areolis ca 0.2 mm latis). Panicula 5-6 cm longa ramorum paribus 1-2 et ca 1 cm longis plerumque 3-floris; floris 6-meri paululo (1-2 mm) pedicellati, bracteis ca 9 X 5 mm spathulato-obovatis (apice rotundato) extus densiuscule gracili-strigosis intus sparsissime strigulosis deciduis. Hypanthium (ad torum) 5.5 mm longum densiuscule laxiusculeque gracili-strigosum pilis 3-3.5 mm longis; calycis lobi 10-10.5 X 2.7-3 mm lanceolati ad anthesim caduci extus modice gracili-strigosi intus glabri; torus intus sparse glanduloso-setulosus (0.1-0.2 mm). Petala glabra 18.5-20 X 9-9.5 mm obovata apice rotundato. Stamina dimorphica glabra, filamentis 10 mm vel 7.5 mm longis, thecis subulatis ca 1 mm latis, poro 0.3-0.4 mm diam. ventraliter inclinato. Stamina maiora: thecae 7.6 mm longae sub filamenti insertionem 1.6 mm prolongatae et bifurcatae, connectivo ultra thecas 0.3-0.4 mm prolongato. Stamina minora: thecae 5.6-5.8 mm longae sub filamenti insertionem 0.5 mm prolongatae et bifurcatae, connectivo thecas aequanti non eminenti. Stigma expansum 1.5 mm diam.; stylus 8.5 X 0.7-1 mm glaber in ovarii cono 1.5 mm immersus; ovarium 6-loculare et ca 1/3 inferum, cono glabro ad apicem paululo (0.1-0.2 mm) lobulato.

description: Shrub; erect, slender, branched, to 1.5 m tall, bearing many flower heads per stem, densely and softly pilose throughout with horizontal or ascending hairs to 0.3-2 mm long; branches slightly striped lengthwise, minutely tuberculate with small but prominent warts. Stipules narrowly lanceolate or subulate, 3.5-4.6 mm long, persistent, densely to softly pilosulous and charged with blister glands abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Leaves odd-pinnate, 7-14(-17) mm long, short-petiolate, the petiole 1.1-2.8(- 4) mm long; leaflets 4-5 pairs, elliptic to ovate-elliptic, (3-)4-6(-7.5) X (0.8-)1- 1.8(-2.1) mm, flat or shallowly involute, veinless, densely pilose on both sides, the terminal leaflet sessile forming a palmate trefoil with the last pair of leaflets, submarginally glandular-punctate abaxially, the rachis canaliculate; intrapetiolular gland l, linear-lanceolate, 0.5-1.2 mm, reddish brown; post-petiolular glands 2, minute, dark red to dark brown. Infiorescences: pe- duncles terminal on branches, (7-)9-15(- 23) mm long; spikes dense, ovoid, subglo- bose to conelike, 8-10 mm diameter (ex- cluding petals), the axis becoming 4-8 mm long in fruit; bracts ovate-acuminate, 5.5- 6.0 X 1.3-1.7 mm, persistent, dark brown, softly pilosulous with ascending hairs up to 0.5-2 mm long, charged with prominent blister glands abaxially, glabrate adaxially. Flowers: calyx sessile, campanulate, softly pilose throughout, the tube 1.9-2.8 mm long, with a recess 0.4-0.5 mm behind the banner, the ribs salient, the intervals charged with two rows of 2-4 small yel- lowish glands each, these 0.1-0.4 mm long, the teeth aristate, slightly unequal, 3.6-4.0 mm long, charged on the margin with 1-2 spurred glands near the base of each tooth, the back and margins of each tooth with 4- 6 elliptic, dark brown blister-like glands; corolla bicolored at anthesis, the banner white to bright yellow, rubescent with age, the inner petals lilac, all glandless, perched well below the middle of the androecium; banner 5.2-6.0 mm long, the claw 2.6-3.0 mm long, the blade 2.6-3.2 X 3-3.8 mm, ovate to wide-rhombic; wings 5.3-5.6 X 1.6-2.1 mm, the claw 1.7-2.1 mm long, the blade 3.1-3.6 mm long, obliquely obovate; keel 6-7 mm long, the claw 2-2.7 mm long, the blade 4-4.3 X 2.6-3 mm, broadly oblanceolate to obovate; androecium 10- merous, 7.1-7.8 mm long, the filaments free for 1.6-2.5 mm, the connective gland-tipped, the anthers 0.3-0.4 mm long. Fruits: immature pod 2.3-2.7 mm long, obovate, the style base eccentric, latero-terminal, the valves hyaline, distally pilosulous, the ventral suture of pod not thickened distally; seeds unknown.

description: Slender microphyll, annual from taproot; stems radiating from the root crown, 1.5 mm at base, height 12-15 cm, some branches more delicate upward in the stem, thinly pilosulous to pilose in branches, leaflets, inflorescences and calyces. Stipules lance-ovate, 1-1.2 mm, persistent. Leaf stalks in- cluding short petiole 3-4 mm long, the post-petiolular glands ovoid-acute, 0.1-0.2 mm; leaflets 9-17 pairs, 3 X 1.5 mm, the undersurface with 20-25 tiny glands, some flaveolate, obovate-oblanceolar, obtuse, the upper surface glabrous. Peduncle filiform, 15-25 mm; racemes densely 12(-15-20)- flowered, the bracts lance-obovate, to 2 mm long, deciduous at maturity; pedicels very short; calyx externally white-pilose on all the teeth, the tube 1.8-2.2 mm, the teeth narrowly oblong ca. 0.7-1 mm, 2-3- nerved, purple-tipped; petals bicolored, white and purple, the vexillum falling as soon as it expands, 2.2-2.4 mm, open at throat; wings 1.8-2 mm long, the claw 0.2 mm long, the subquadrate blade 1.8 X 0.9 mm; keel blades small, ca. 0.6-0.8 mm; androecium 10-merous, 2.4-2.6 mm long, the longest filament free for at least 1 mm, the yellowish gland-tipped anthers 0.1-0.2 mm long; ovule solitary; pod ca. 2 X 1.5 mm, 1-seeded, charged centrally with large and small glands.

description: Slender microphylous, seemingly perennial herb from taproot ±2.5 mm diam. at apex, radiating from the root-crown, the filiform diffuse or hemifuse repeatedly forked stem attaining 2.5 mm diam., nearly smooth proximally, thinly pilosulous distally. Stipules lance-ovate, 0.7-1.4 mm, per- sistent. Leaf stalks including short petiole 4-8 mm long, the post-petiolular glands ovoid-acute, 0.1-0.25 mm diam.; leaflets 9-15 pairs, oblanceolate-ovate, obtuse, loosely conduplicate, the larger ones 2-2.5 X 0.6-0.8 mm, tuberculate-glandular dor- sally, smooth. Peduncle filiform, 10-20 mm long; racemes loosely (3-)5-7-flowered; bracts narrowly ovate, nearly 1.5 mm long, deciduous at anthesis; flowers short-pedicellate, the glanduliform bracteoles to 0.35 mm long; calyx white-pilosulous below the herbaceous, purple-tipped, dorsally glabrous teeth, the tube prominently 10-nerved, ca. 1.3-1.7 mm long, the narrowly oblong teeth ca. 1 mm long, tipped with a prominent gland; petals bicolored, white and mainly amethyst-purple, the vexillum 2.5 mm long, its subquadrate blade ca. 2 X 1.4 mm, open at throat; keel blades ca. 1 X 1.4 mm, the wings 1.3-1.5 mm long, the claw 0.4-0.5 mm long, the obliquely-obovate blade 0.9 X 0.5 mm; androecium 10- merous, 2.8-3 mm long, the longest filament free for at least 1.2 mm, the yellowish gland-tipped anthers 0.2-0.3 mm long; ovule solitary; pod ±2 X 1.5 mm, membranous at base, charged distally with an oblique crescent of small blister glands; ripe seeds not seen.

description: Astragalo esperanzae Jones similis, sed differt habitu erecto, pedunculis ac pedicellis brevioribus, dentibus calyce brevioribus, vexillis brevioribus, fructibus brevioribus erectis, et distributio geographica dissimilis.
