description: Herbaceous perennial; taproot slender and woody; the caudex partially buried; stems ascending or erect, light green, except greenish brown at the base, branched, 18- 54 cm, 1.8-2.2 mm diam., appressed, pilose with white hairs of two types, the longer ones straight or slightly incurved, 0.4-1 mm, the shorter ones tightly appressed, antrorse, 0.1-0.4 mm long; stipules 1.5-2.3 x 0.4-3.2 mm, basal and median ones connate, ovate, deflexed, whitish, pilose, the upper ones united at base, triangular, whitish, pilose. Leaves (1.2-)1.3-3.5(-4.2) cm long leaflets 15-21, (2.1-)2.2-5.0(-8.2) x (0.6-)1.1-2.3(-2.8) mm, opposite or rarely, opposite and sub-opposite, membranaceous, elliptic to obovate, not folded, pilose on both surfaces, more densely pilose on the abaxial side, the apex rounded or retuse, the base acute. Racemes (2.0-)4-14(-20) mm long, 4-9(-11) flowered, flowers ascend- ing, the peduncles (11-)12-23(-25) mm, elongating in fruit, to 69 mm, erect, persistent (after flowers have fallen); bracts persistent, 1.3-1.4 mm X 0.4-0.6 mm, ovate, acute at apex, densely pilose; pedicels (0.2- )0.3-0.7(-1) mm, elongating to 1.9 mm, not much thickened in fruit; bracteoles none; calyx 4.6-5.1 X 2.0-2.3 mm, campanulate, white pilose hairs, the tube 3.2-3.5 mm long, the teeth 1.2-1.5 mm long, triangular- lanceolate. Petals purple; the banner recurved 35-40, 9.6-10.1 x 5.2-5.4 mm, obovate to spatulate, the apex retuse, the notch 0.25-3.0 mm; the wings 8.2-8.4 x 2.2-2.6 mm narrowly oblique-obovate, claw 3.2-3.6 mm long, blade 5.0-5.3 mm long; the keel 6.0-6.5 mm long, blade oblique-obovate, abruptly incurved, blade 3.2-3.3 mm long, claw 3.3-3.5 mm long. Stamens 10, diadelphous, the vexillare stamen free, its filament 5.2-5.6 mm long, the other stamens fused by their filaments into a sheath 3.3-3.8 mm long, the free portions of the filaments 1.5-1.6 mm long; anthers elliptic, 0.6-0.7 mm long. Ovary sessile, narrow-ovate, 1.9-2.4 mm long, 0.8-1.0 mm diam., unilocular, hispid-pubescent, 9-11 ovulate; the style curved, 3.0-3.3 mm long. Legumes erect, sessile, 10-11 X 3.1-3.8 mm, oblong, slightly incurved, triquetrously compressed, ventrally carinate, dorsally grooved, apical peak 1.2-2.2 mm long, the base rounded, the lateral angles rounded, the septum completely inflexed, 1.0-1.3 mm wide, the valves stiffly papery, white-pilose, delicately cross-reticulate, dehiscent toward the apex, dark-brown at maturity; seeds 9-11, laterally compressed, notched at the hilum, obliquely reniform, light-brown, 1.7-1.9 mm long, the seed coat smooth, lustrous.

description: Seemingly perennial herbs to 40 cm high. Leaves alternate, deeply pinnatifid, pale green, eglandular, 1.5-4.5 cm long, 1-2 cm wide, pubescent on both surfaces. Scorpioid branches congested, 1.5-2.5 cm long. Calyx of 4 oblanceolate sepals, 2-2.5 mm long, separate to the base or nearly so, moderately sericeous with spreading hairs. Corolla tubular, glabrous, pink, ca 3.5 mm long, ca 1.5 mm wide. Stamens included, or nearly so. Capsule spheroidal, ca 2.1 mm high, 2.5 mm wide, hispid-puberulous or somewhat glandular, the persistent style branches ca 1.5 mm long, united below for ca 0.4 mm. Seeds 4, dark brown, 1.5-1.8 mm long, 0.8-1 mm wide, finely alveolate, the ventral "column" broad but uncorrugated.

description: Woody vine. Stems obtusely triangular, striate, the young parts lanate (white, curly hairs 0.2-0.5 mm long), becoming nearly glabrous with age; cross section of stem with a central, obtusely triangular, large stele, and 3 peripheral, smaller subterete steles of similar size. Stipules triangular, ca. 0.7 mm long, pubescent, early-deciduous. Leaves pinnately 5-foliolate; petioles puberulent, 3-4.2 cm long, canaliculate adaxially; rachis puberulent, 2.5-3.2 cm long, bicaniculate and bicarinate along adaxial surface; leaflets 4-7.5 X 2.2-4.7 cm, discolorous, chartaceous, adaxially puberulent, abaxially puberulent along veins and sparsely covered with papilliform, glandular hairs, the apex acuminate-mucronate, the margins coarsely glandular serrate, the veins mixed-craspedodromous, much lighter than the blade, notably prominent abaxially, third-order veins clathrate-reticulate, fourth-order veins darker than the blade; terminal leaflet cuneate, decurrent onto petiolule; lateral leaflets ovate to obovate, with obtuse or round, asymmetric base. Thyrses axillary, simple, puberulent, shorter than subtending leaf; axis obtusely 4-angled, striate; rachis obtusely 3-angular in cross section, striate; bracts and bracteoles deltate, deciduous; cincinni alternate, 2-3-flowered, 3-7 mm long; pedicels puberulent, articulated near the base. Sepals ca. 4 mm long, oblong, lanate, third and fifth sepals free; nectary disk 4-glandular, the central glands with triangular outline, the lateral ones nearly rounded; torus slightly enlarged, glabrous. Fruits pyriform in outline; mericarps 2.5-3 cm long; cocci nearly globose, 1.2-1.5 X 1.2-1.3 cm, coriaceous to subligneous, sparsely covered with papilli- form glandular hairs, wrinkled, dorsally narrowly keeled; partitioning walls 1.5-2 cm wide; endocarp lanate, with septate hairs, ca. 1 mm long; wing smaller than coccus, oblong to attenuate toward the truncate base. Seeds elliptic with a triangular outline in transverse section, 7-8 X 5-6 mm, dark brown; hilar scar trigonous, ca. 2.5 mm wide; adaxial cotyledon nearly transversely biplicate, the abaxial cotyledon curved.

description: Plants low, acaulescent or very short-caulescent, simple or few branched at base, 10- 30 cm tall, from a tuberous root, glabrous except slightly scaberulous in inflorescence and beneath umbel; leaves rosulate, broadly oblong, 3-5 X 2-3 cm, simply pinnate with usually 2-4 pairs of oval to obovate, obtuse, shallowly crenulate leaflets, the terminal often shallowly 3-lobed, sessile, all narrowly callus-margined; petioles slender, 2-4 cm long, slightly dilated and scarious-sheathing below, the sheath 1-2 cm long; peduncles ter- minal, elongate, 5-30 cm long, slightly scaberulous at summit; involucre lacking; rays 2-8, 0.5-2 cm long, stout, unequal, ridged, ascending or spreading-ascending; involucel of 1-5 linear or linear-lanceolate entire bract- lets, 3-5(-6) mm long; fruiting pedicels 1-6, stout, 2-4 mm long; flowers not seen, reportedly white; sepals lacking; styles very slender, to 2 mm, divergent; stylopodium lacking; carpophore stout, bipartite, the halves remaining adpressed; fruit ovoid-globose, 3-4 mm long, 2-3 mm broad, a little narrowed at apex, rounded at base, the ribs filiform; vittae 1-3 in intervals, 3 or 4 on commissure; seed face sulcate.
bibliographicCitation: Constance, Lincoln & Affolter, James M. 1997. A pair of species of Tauschia Schltdl. (Umbelliferae/Apiaceae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 49: 458-462.

description: Herbae perennes ad basim suffruticosae, ramis erectis vel decumbentibus usque ad 40 cm altis parce ramificatis hirsuto-pubescentibus, radicibus fusiformibus crassis. Folia petiolata elliptica vel ovata, 3-6 X 2-3 cm, apice obtusa basi cuneata, utrimque hir- suto-pilosa. Flores pedicellati, solitarii vel geminati, in axillis foliorum terminalium dispositae, pedunculati, bracteolati, bracteolis lanceolatis 3-5 X 1-2 mm. Calycis segmenta linearia ca. 2.5 cm X 2 mm extus pubescentia glandulosa. Flores caerulei 5-6 cm longi. Corollae infundibuliformis tubo 0.5-1 cm longo faucibus breviore, lobis rotundatis 2 cm longis. Antherae inclusae 5 mm longae. Stylus filiformis glabris. Capsula oblonga, 3 cm longa 0.6 cm crassa, glanduloso-puberula, ca. 12-sperma. Semina 4 mm longa, in siccus adpresso-puberula.
bibliographicCitation: Ezcurra, C. 1998. A new species of Ruellia (Acanthaceae) from Paraguay. Brittonia. 50: 339-342.

description: Erect or decumbent perennial herbs, the stems terete, to 40 cm long, hirsute, arising from a small, woody rhizome, with thick, fleshy, fusiform roots. Leaves on petioles to 0.5 cm long, the blades elliptic or ovate, 3-6 X 2-3 cm, obtuse at the apex, cuneate at the base, somewhat serrulate, the lower ones generally smaller, all hirsute-pilose, the hairs sparse, lax, long, shiny and spreading. Flowers pedicellate, in peduncled, 1-2-flowered dichasia in the axils of the terminal leaves, frequently reduced to solitary flowers with bibracteolate peduncles. Peduncles 2-3 cm long, glandular-pilose; bractlets linear-lanceolate, foliaceous, 3-5 X 1-2 mm, acute, glandular pilose; pedicels 1-3 cm long, glandular pubescent. Calyx 2-3 cm long, segments linear-lanceolate, to 2.5 cm X 2 mm, acute, densely glandular pubescent. Corolla pale mauve or blue, 5-6 cm long, basal tube 0.5-1 cm long, throat obconic, 3-4 cm long and 2 cm diam., darker in color toward the base of the throat, the lobes spreading, suborbicular, ca. 2 cm. Stamens included, longer fila- ments ca. 1.5 cm long, shorter 1 cm long, the anthers 5 mm long. Ovary puberulous and style glabrous. Capsule narrowly oblong, 3 cm long, 6 mm thick, broadest at the middle, hollow nearly to the base, densely short glandular-pubescent. Retinacula obtuse, 2 mm long. Seeds ca. 12, flat, suborbicular, 4 X 3.5 mm, appressed pilose when dry.
bibliographicCitation: Ezcurra, C. 1998. A new species of Ruellia (Acanthaceae) from Paraguay. Brittonia. 50: 339-342.

description: Plants somewhat firm, blue-green and occasionally reddish green, often +- flattened on top, 2-6 cm high, 4-11 cm in diam; ribs and furrows usually present and well defined, 4-14 but highly variable and sometimes forming -+ elevated podaria; areoles 0.9 1.5 cm apart, 2-4 mm in diam; flower 1-2.2 cm in diam, 1-2.4 cm long; outer perianth segments 2-3 mm broad; inner perianth segments 2.5-4 mm broad, usually pink; pollen 0-18 colpate, 14.9-63.4 I in diam (Fig 3).
bibliographicCitation: Anderson, Edward F. 1970. The biogeography, ecology and taxonomy of Lophophora. Brittonia. 21: 299-310.

description: Plants erect, with a well-defined main stem, profusely branched, to 25(-40) cm high; rhizome vertical, succulent, tuberform, to 40 cm long, 5(-10) cm diam.; primary stem larger than normal cladodes, thickened, rarely lignified, to 30 cm high but usually shorter, to 6 cm broad. Secondary cladodes olive-green, sometimes reddish around the areoles, glabrous, narrowly lanceolate when young, becoming lanceolate or oblanceolate, flat, 5-12(-17) X 3.5 (-4.5) cm, 3-6 mm thick. Areoles typically 0.8-1.5(-2) cm apart, elliptical, 2-3 mm diam. in their widest portion, with white wool at center. Leaves present only on the younger cladodes and on the pericarpel, green to reddish, succulent, conical, ephem- eral, 2-3 mm long. Spines white to light brown or grey, with yellowish or brown tips, rigid, acicular, of unequal length, usually 3-5(-6) in each areole, 0.5-2(-3.5) cm long. Glochids brown to yellow, 12-30 (-40), 1-4(-6) mm long. Flowers usually emerging from the margins or occasionally from the upper portion of the cladode faces, infundibuliform, 3-5.5 cm long, 2.5-6 cm diam. at anthesis. Pericarpel olive-green, usually tuberculate, narrowly obconical, 1.8-3.3 cm long, 9-16 mm diam. at the apex; areoles sometimes with 1-2 white, caducous spines, with white wool; glochids to 6 mm long, light brown to reddish brown. External perianth segments green to reddish, with the edge yellow-greenish, the larger ones usually with light green or reddish central stripes and yellow-greenish edges, reddish to brownish at the apex, succulent, becoming membranous inward, oblanceolate to spatulate, truncately attenuate at base, acuminate to apiculate at apex, margin entire, to 2.2 cm long; internal perianth segments greenish-yellow, membra- nous, spatulate, truncate-attenuate at base, mucronate at apex, margin entire, to 3 cm long, 1-1.8 cm at the broadest part. Stamens numerous, erect, slightly reclinate toward the pistil; filaments white, light green at the base, sensitive to touch, 4-7 mm long; anthers yellow, dorsifixed, 1-1.5 mm long. Style white, cylindrical, 1-1.8 cm long, 1.5-2.8 mm diam. at base, becoming narrower toward the apex. Stigma light green, capitate, sometimes with the lobes ascending, 2-3.8 mm diam., with 5-6 lobes. Fruits obovoid, truncate at the apex, umbilicate, 2.5 cm long. Seeds yellow-cream-colored, discoid, ca. 4 mm diam.

description: Slender annuals, (12-) 25-45 (-56) cm tall, the widely divergent branches long and slender, sparsely glandular-viscid to almost subglabrous throughout; petioles 1-22 mm long; leaflets narrowly linear to linear-elliptic or oblanceolate, 5-37 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, somewhat fleshy, more or less conduplicate, acute, mucronulate; racemes very open, 4-25 cm long, few-flowered (each with 10-17 flowers and buds); bracts 3-foliolate; sepals lanceolate to obovate, entire to irregularly toothed, aeute, 2.5-3.6 mm long, erect at anthesis; petals broadly spatulate with slender purplish claw, white to pale lemon yellow, very strongly dimorphic, the larger pair (6-) 7-11 mm long, 5.5-6.9 mm wide, palmately laciniate with 5-9 lobes, the smaller pair 4-6 mm long, of similar shape though much more deeply cut into filiform segments, these again often deeply cleft; stamens (6-) 8-13 (-15), pink, the filaments 6-12 mm long; anthers 1.6-2.5 mm long, apiculate; neetary gland tubular, truncate and irregularly toothed and somewhat constricted above, more or less deeply indented abaxially, 3.5-5.5 mm long (or 0.8-1.8 in se Texas), 0.9 mm in diameter, yellow, drying pink-purple; mature siliques narrowly linear-fusiform, hardly inflated, (15-) 25-65 mm long, 1.7-3.5 mm wide, the valves dehiscing nearly to the base; style (2.5-) 3-6 mm long, persistent in fruit, the stigma minute; gynophore (4-) 7-14 mm long or 3-5 mm in se Texas) ; pedicel 12-22 mm long; seeds (6-) 10-30 (-36) in each silique, subspherical to reniform, 1.4-1.7 mm long, dark reddish-brown, uniformly pebbled, the internal invagination of the testa rather deep (approx. 25 of the seed diameter).
bibliographicCitation: Iltis, Hugh H. 1958. Studies in the Capparidaceae--IV. Polanisia Raf. Brittonia. 10: 33-58.

description: Slender, branched, glandular-viscid annuals (or winter-annuals?), 1-9 dm tall; petioles (1-) 5-20 (-33) mm long; leaflets narrowly linear to filiform, 4-52 mm long, 0.5-2.1 mm wide, fleshy and conduplicate, mucronulate, glandular on the margins and midrib or glabrous; racemes few-flowered (each with 3-8 buds and open flowers), very open, 5-15 (-20) cm long; bracts 3-foliate; sepals triangular-lanceolate, acute and mueronate, 1.1-2.5 mm long, strongly reflexed in flower; petals white (rarely diffused with purple), entire, the apex rounded to truncate or shallowly emarginate, strongly dimorphic, very variable in size and(i shape, the larger pair broadly ovate and subsessile to spatulate and clawed, 2.0-7.5 mm long, 1-5 mm broad, the smaller pair spatulate, 1.5-4.0 mm long: stamens 8-13, the filaments 2.2-6.0 rnm long, white, somewhat clavate (with glandular apex?); anthers 1.0-2.2 mm long, rounded at the apex; nectary shallowly obliquely concave, about 0.5-1.0 mm long, 1.2-1.4 mm wide; siliques narrowly linear-fusiform, not inflated, (25-) 40-70 (-84) mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm thick, the valves separating apically for 1 /32/3 their length; style 1.1-3.5 mm long, persistent, the stigma rather strongly capitate and bilabiate; gynophore lacking; pedicel 11-28 mm long; seeds (40-) 65-115 in each silique, subspherical, 0.7-0.9 mm in diameter, rusty- to grey-brown, uniformly minutely roughened (like sharkskin), the internal invagination of the testa very shallow.
bibliographicCitation: Iltis, Hugh H. 1958. Studies in the Capparidaceae--IV. Polanisia Raf. Brittonia. 10: 33-58.

description: Herbaceous annuals, to 24 dm tall, usually puberulent (scabrid when dry), the stems tan, green, or red streaked; leaves yellow-green, gray-green beneath, trifolio- late; leaflets 4-20 (35) mm long, obovate, less than 2.8 times as long as wide; sepals lanceolate, 0.5-1.6 mm long, more than 1.75 times as long as wide; petals 2.5-5 mm long; anthers 1.3-2.5 mm long; pedicel usually shorter than stipe; carpels 1.4-3.4 mm long, with tubercles less than 0.1-0.3 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Kirkbride, M. C. G. 1979. Review of the neotropical Isertieae (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 31: 313-332.

description: Branched subshrubs to treelets 1-3m tall, essentially glabrous or minutely papillate-puberulent to sparsely pilose generally, the hairs rather crispate and whitish - green to ferruginous (depending on length and relative maturity), intermixed with yellowish, minute, sessile or subsessile glandsl; stems, petioles and inflorescence axis glabrous (except in bract and leaf axils) to sparsely pubescent. Leaves almost always 3-foliolate, the lowest one on young shoots sometimes 1- foliolate, those on fast growing sterile shoots sometimes larger and 5- foliolate; petioles 1-15 cm; leaflets elliptic to narrowly oblong- elliptic, the central blade 3-16 x 1-8 cm , acute to short - acuminate, broadly attenuate to cuneate, glabrous or minutely papillate - roughened above, minutely scabrid- papillate or somewhat glandular - puberulent beneath, especially along the veins; main lateral veins 6- 10 per side. Racemes scarcely elongating, 2-10 (-13) cm long, somewhat densely 24-92(-150) - flowered (pedicels plus pedicel scars); peduncle 3-19 mm; rachis to 13 (mostly 3- 8) cm, with 2-22 open flowers (fewer at beginning of pistillate phase) and 0-68 buds present at any one time. Flowers zygomorphic; pedicels short, 3-12(-20) mm, in flower spreading at an angle of 35° (the upper) to 90° (the lower ones) from the axis. Bracts 1-10, 1- foliolate, sometimes the lowest one 2- or 3- foliolate (but the blades no larger), elliptic to narrowly oblong-elliptic, 0.2-9 cm* 0.5- 33 mm, short-acuminate to attenuate, obtuse to cuneate; petioles 0.2-29(^41) mm. Sepals 4, united for ca. 1-3 mm, green, essentially equal in shape and size, the upper (adaxial) some- times 1 mm shorter or the lower (abaxial) sometimes 1 mm longer than the others, oblong or narrowly oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 4-10x1-3 mm, acute, glabrous to sparsely papillate-pilosulous, deciduous. Petals 4, diagonal to each other, ascending, orangish-red (pale pink to pinkish-purple in herbarium material), obovate-spatulate and unguiculate for 1/5—1/2 their length, 7-14x3-5 mm, rounded, attenuate into a broad or ± narrow claw 2-6 mm. Nectary a fleshy, 3-lobed adaxial gland, the central lobe projecting up and out over the androgynophore, the 2 smaller lateral lobes alternating with the adaxial petals, frequently drying to cubical, oblong, or nearly pyramidal in side view when pressed and dried, 1.5-2.5 mm high and wide, 1.0-2.1 mm thick, persisting and somewhat conspicuous in fruit. Staminate flowers: stamens strongly exserted, normally all fertile and equal in length (rarely one markedly smaller or even aborted); filaments coral-color, upcurved, 11-27 mm; anthers 2.4—3.8 mm, the pollen golden-yellow or pinkish-lavender; androgynophore 2-5 (5 collections) or 6-10 (8 collections) mm long, from shorter than to equaling the sepals. Pistillate flowers: ovary narrowly oblong to cylindric, laterally compressed, 7-16x0.5-1 mm, papillate-puberulent; stigma capitellate, inconspicuously bilobed, 0.7-1 mm in diameter, subsessile (style 0.5-1.3 mm); gynophore 5-11 mm; androgynophore 2-7 mm. Capsules 0-9 per raceme, cylindric, 3-15 cm x 3-6 mm thick, attenuate to the tip, cuneate to attenuate at the base, torulose, straight or curved; valves green, glabrous to very sparsely papillate-puberulent; stigma barely differentiated from the style, 0.5-1.2 mm in diameter, the style 04 mm, forming with the seedless apex of the loculus a definite tapering beak 3-11 mm; gynophore 5-15 mm, wiry, continuous and straight with the androgynophore and pedicel, glabrous or scabrid-puberulent; androgynophore 2-8 mm; pedicel 6-18(-23) mm, rather stiffly horizontally divergent to widely down-curved (not reflexed). Seeds black (brown when dried), suborbicular to broadly obovoid in overall shape, ± strongly beveled, bearing flattened spots on various surfaces because of pressure from adjacent seeds, 2.8-4 x 2.1— 3 mm, 1.7-2.1 mm thick, the sides and backs smooth or very faintly undulate.

description: Herba rosulata hiemalis annua. Folia caulina 2-6 mm longa, 1-2 mm lata, subuliformia, parce succosa. Sepala 1.2-2.4 mm longa, ovata-lanceolata, obtusata vel subacuta, glabra, margine scariosa. Petala alba 1-3 mm longa, elliptica-oblonga, apice bifida aut obtusata. Capsula 3 mm (2.5-3.4) longa, conica, dehiscens per 3 suturas. Chromosomatum numerus 2n = 14.

description: Perennis, ca 1 dm alta, partes omnes (stipulis scariosis et bracteis exceptis) pilis brevibus saepe porrectibus dense velatae; caules corymbosi, simplices vel plusmin- usve ramosi, caules et rami utrique basi foliis et bracteis crebris stipatis imbricatis ornati; folia sessilia, linearia, acuta, fere ad caulem adpressa; folia mediocria 5-6 mm longa, vulgo ad stipulas argenteas in longitudine aequiparantia; flores apice ramulorum corymbosi, bracteas et folia manifesto superantes; calyx croceus; calycis lobi ca 2.5 mm longi cum spina brevi erecta apicali; stylus ca 0.5 mm longus.

description: Perennis, a basi ramosa; caules debiles, prostrati, puberuli, laxe ramosi; folia sessilia, linearo-oblonga vel linearo-lanceolata, ad 1 cm longa et 1.5 mm lata, saeta apice alba prominente, minute puberula; folia vetusta conduplicativa et recurvata, vulgo stipulas attenuatas argenteas breviter superantia; flores corymbosi, bracteas argenteas superantes; calycis lobi manifesto albo-marginati, 3 mm longi cum saeta apicali alba recurvata, infra basi saetae crinem ornati, extra manifesto basi tumida pubescentes; stylus brevis.

description: Subherbaceous; stems slender, glabrous or nearly so, subterete, reclining or scrambling over shrubs, etc., loosely branched, at times ? 4 m. long; branches more or less angular. Leaves thin-membranaceous, pale, oblong or oblong- lanceolate, at apex acute to very acuminate, at base acute to rounded, with dis- tinct median but evanescent lateral nerves, glabrous or nearly so, blade mostly 5-9 cm. long, petiole 4-6 mm. long. Panicle 1-5 dm. long, with commonly 5-7 pairs of spreading rays, these sparingly divided and comparatively few-flowered, more or less puberulous or glandular-puberulous as also their subdivisions com- monly are, pedicels finally up to 4 or even 5 cm. long. Bracts of lower portion of axis reduced-f oliaccous. Bractlets subulate or setaceous. Sepals glabrate or minutely puberulous, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, prominently several-nerved near base, at apex caudate-acuminate, at margins often narrowly searious, 4-7 mm. long. Staminodia subulate to linear, at apex bifid, shorter than sepals, gradually or subabruptly contracting from a somewhat broader base. Stamens up to about twice as long as sepals. Styles 3-5, long-exserted. Capsule ovoid, 3-5-valved, not or but slightly exceeding the calyx. Seeds numerous, black, smooth, barely 1 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Stem weak, decumbent, rather herbaceous, about 3 dm. long. Leaves oblong and mucronate or ovate [sic], 2.5-4 cm. long and 12-16 mm. wide, membrano- chartaceous, 1-nerved. Panicle open and short, 5-10 cm. long, with 3-5 nodes, the rays elongate, branching from the middle, few-flowered. Bracts short, linear. Sepals 4 mm. long, shorter than their pedicels, ovate-lanceolate, long-acuminate, scarcely puberulous. Staminodia linear, entire, from a broad, ovate base, some- what shorter than the sepals. Capsule 3- or 4-valved, shorter than the calyx. Seeds tuberculate.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Glabrous, +- 3.5 din. tall, branches mostly ending lanceolate, very thin, acute at apex, clearly 3-nerved or now (at least at base) 5-nerved, abruptly contracted above their connate insertion, upper and median ones ? 2.5 cm. long. Panicle somewhat or scarcely contracted, -+- 1.7 dm. long, peduncles and pedicels filiform and suberect to somewhat spreading, the latter commonly under 1 cm. long. Calyx about 2.5 mm. tall; sepals in age several- nerved, ovate or broadly laneeolate, at apex somewhat obtuse. Capsule about 2.5-3 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: An erect to semi-decumbent underbrush, 1.5 to 4.5 or even about 5 din. tall; stem glabrous, inferiorly terete and woody; branches numerous, more or less erect, at first herbaceous and green but in age soon brittle-woody and more or less stramineous, the numerous thickened nodes now mostly 5-10 mm. apart now more remote. Leaves numerous, glabrous, the principal ones linear to narrow- lanceolate (and commonly with fascicles of narrowly linear leaves in their axils), at apex acuminate to more or less caudate, subeuneately narrowed below to a sessile or wing-petioled base -(the extreme leaf-bases dilated and connate), paler beneath, somewhat thin-chartaceous and flaccid, at last usually marceseent, 3-8 cm. long and 3-11 mm. wide, 3-nerved from near base, minutely crassulate at margins. Infloreseence terminal, thyrsoid, 4-10.5 ecn. tall and 2 to 4 or even to 6 cm. thick, commonly 2-3 times compound, the branches opposite and subtended by much and abruptly reduced leaves (bracts); peduncle 2-5 cm. long (or up to ? 13 cm. long with leafy node near middle). Pedicels suberect, very slender- filiform, minutely and sparsely puberulous to glabrate, 2-7 mm. long, the broad- lanceolate to ovate bractlets 1-2 mm. long and with niarrow, hyaline margins. Sepals ovate, green, thin, glabrate, apically acute or obtuse, externally at first scarcely nerved but in age more or les's clearly ? 7-nerved, about 2.5 cm. long. Staminodia about 0.3-0 .5 the length of the sepals, broad-triangular (but with both sides folded inward and thus appearing ovate-oblong). Stamens in bud with well-developed anthers but short filaments, these latter becoming long- exserted at anthesis while styles are yet short. Styles 3 or 4, finally long-exserted and + 3 mm. long, often marceseent. Ovary small, glabrous. Capsule ovoid- pyramidal, equalling or barely exceeding the persistent calyx. Seed compressed, reniform-orbicular, grayish-black, dull, mostly 0.6-0.9 mm. across, minutely rugulose.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Erect, subherbaceous, glabrous; stems ancd branches anguilate, grayish when dry, moderately foliose, internodes 1-5 cm. long. Leaves elliptic-oblongr to rhomboidal-oblong, or -obovate, at apex abruptly acuminate or even mucronate, fleshy-membranous or when dry membranous, dull, when dry more or less brownish-green, f'aintly 3-nerved (the 2 lateral nerves converging with the median at apex), blade 2-3 cm. long and 7-14 mm. wide, the petiole narrowly margined and 4-6 mm. long. Panicle open, 6-15 em. long, with 3 or 4 pairs of suberect rays (the lowest up to + 5 cm. long.). Bractlets ovate to lanceolate, subulateattenuate. Pedicels delicate, glabrous, up to 2 cm. long. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, attenuate to subulate above, often with 3 or more simple or branched conspicuous nerves, glabrous unless along searious margins, 4-5 mm. long. Staminodia half or according to Hillebrand "about as long" as sepals, linear from a roundish base, bifid at apex. Styles 3 or rarely 4. Capsules as long as sepals. Seeds transversely rugose.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Woody at base, 3 + dm. tall; branches delicate, subdensely foliose below but scarcely foliose above, not hispidulous except toward top; internodes commonly 1-3 cm. long (uppermost, elongate ones up to + 7 cm. long). Leaves linear or narrowly lanceolate, sessile, gradually narrowed almost from the acute base all the way to the very sharp tip, membranous, glabrous on both surfaces, paler beneath, 4-8 cm. long and 3-7 mm. wide, 3-nerved (at times with 2 weak additional nerves near margins), nerves very slender and depressed above but wider and salient beneath. Panicle erect., thyrsoid, pubeseent, consisting, of 14 glomerules, these 1-2.5 cm. in diameter and at distances of 0.5-4.5 cm. Pedicels slender, tomentulose, irregular in length but the longest -+ 13 mm. long. Sepals lanceolate-oblong, tomentulose, obscurely nerved, somewhat attenuate above, 4-5 mm. long. Staminodia equalling or somewhat surpassing the sepals in length, linear, bifid at apex, at base dilated and deltoid-ovate. Stamens becoming much exserted. Styles 4 in the lone instance where counted, doubtless often 3. Capsules and seeds not examined.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Suffruticose, 2-4 din. tall, the short, naked stems prostrate, with branches ascending or erect, these glabrous unless occasionally near top, angulate, densely foliose below and with axillary fascieles, and suddenly becoming subscapose above; the subscape 0.7-3 dm. long, with commonly 1-3 distant pairs of leaves and a dense, terminal, globose eymule, the latter often subtended at one or two nodes immediately below by 1-3 smaller eymules, these constituting with the terminal one an interrupted t.hyrse. Leaves narrowly or moderately linear but commonly narrowed gradually from near base to an elongate, very acute (or in some forms abruptly apiculate) tip, at base broadly sessile and clasping, 1-(rarely sub-3-)nerved, glabrous or glabrate, the principal ones now 3-6, now 5-11 cm. long and 3-8 mm. wide. Infloreseence 1.7-3.8 cm. in diameter as to principal glomerule, this consisting of 2 or 3 closely approximate nodes, the short sub- glomerules compound from near their base; pedicels glandular-puberulous, very slender or (in apparently ill-defined races) more or less thickened near top, mostly 2-6 but sometimes up to 15 mm. long. Sepals moderately to broadly ovate, at apex obtuse or rounded, thin, glabrate to somewhat puberulons, 3-4 mm. long, the several nerves conspicuous or at times obscure. Staminodia ligulate, half the length of the sepals, apically truncate or bifid, basally not dilated. Stamens barely exserted. Styles 3-5, more often 4. Capsule included. Seeds numerous, transversely rugose.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Erect, suffruticose, 3-6 dm. tall, sparingly branched, distantly foliose, inter- nodes 2.5-4 cm. long. Leaves narrow-lanceolate, 5-7.5 cm. long and 4-8 mm. wide, very acute at both ends, with a subulate point, chartaceous, pale, with a transparent midrib. Panicle short but open and continuous, 7.5-10 cm. long, with 4 or 5 nodes, the lowest rays about 5 cm. long, dividing from the middle, the pedicels 8-12 mm. long, the acute and scarious bracts 2-4 mm. long. Sepals lanceolate-acute and strigose, 4 mm. long. Staminodia nearly as long, linear, entire. Stamens shortly exserted. Capsule 3-5-valved, about as long as the sepals. Seeds transversely rugose.
bibliographicCitation: Sherff, Earl E. 1945. Revision of the genus Schiedea Cham. & Schlecht. Brittonia. 5: 308-336.

description: Perennial from a simple or usually branched caudex; stems one to several, 6-25 cm tall; herbage densely retrorsely puberulent, becoming glabrous or nearly so at the base; leaves oblanceolate to linear, opposite, connate especially at the base of the stem, 1-nerved, the basal leaves nearly linear to oblanceolate, 14-40 mm long, (1) 2-4 mm wide, stem leaves in (2) 3-4 pairs, linear, reduced upwards,purple-tipped; flowers (1) 2-4 per stem, the lowermost often remote from the terminal one and not always maturing; pedicels to 5.2 cm long, the terminal one longest; calyx tubular, 6-11.5 mm long, densely retrorsely puberulent, 10-nerved, mostly purple, the nerves and lobes dark green, the lobes 1-1.5 mm long, ciliate; petals ligulate to slightly oblanceolate, entire to slightly emarginate at the tip, 6.7-12.5 mm long, without auricles or appendages, not differentiated into claw and blade, white except for the exserted portion (up to 2 mm) which is pink to light purple or occasionally white, with a few scattered hairs at the base; stamens 10, the antesepalous ones slightly surpassing the calyx at maturity, the antepetalous ones shorter, sometimes not maturing, the filaments with a few scattered hairs at the base, the antepetalous ones fused to the base of the petals for about 1 mm; carpophore less than 1 mm long; styles 3, about 2 mm long, included in the calyx; capsules glabrous, from about 1 mm shorter to 2 mm longer than the calyx, splitting along 6 lines; seeds brown, about 1 mm long, angled, rugose to papillate, the margins more prominently rounded-papillate.

description: Perennis, ad 2.5 dm alta, glabra, calycis basi excepta; caules erecti vel erecto-ascendentes, filiformes, supra ramosi, saepe aliquantum glauci; folia sessilia, linearia, acuta, curvo-adpressa contra caulem, ad 1.5 cm longa; foliis in inflorescentiis cymosis imminuentibus; stipulae argenteae, anguste triangulo-lanceolatae et longo-attenuatae, quam folia multo breviores; flores quam bracteae ovates argenteae et folia contigua imminuta longiores manifesto detectae; calycis lobi albi vel crocei, 2.5-3 mm longi cum saeta apicali brevi leve patula.

description: Perennial; stems from a woody caudex, yellowish, glabrous, 13-30 cm long; primary leaves subulate-linear, bright green, glabrous, strict arcuate, 3-nerved, 3-5 (9) mm long, 0.75-1 mm wide; secondary leaves fascicled in axils of primary leaves; inflorescence cymose, slightly glandular-pubescent, 4-11 cm long; sepals narrowly lanceolate, slightly glandular-pubescent, purplish with scarious margins, 1- to 3-nerved, 4-5 mm long; petals broadly linear to narrowly oblong-elliptic, white, 3.0-3.5 mm long, shorter than the sepals; capsule dehiscent by 3 valves.

description: Arbor grandis ramis terminalibus brunneseentibus lenticellatis glabris. Folia simplicia rigide papyracea subopposita glaberrima. Petiolus 2-5 mm longus laevis supra suleatus. Lamina ovata vel ovato-elliptica basi rotundata vel obtusa apice acuminata, margine integra 6-10 cm longa 3.5-6 cm lata acumine lato at 1 cm longo; supra viridis nitida costa nervis secundariis tertiisque tenui- bus sed prominentibus venulis prominulis; subtus opaca costa elevata, nervis secundariis 4-5 utroque latere curvato-aseendentibus prominentibus, nervis tertiis prominulis venulis laxe reticulatis paulo prominulis. Infloreseentiae axillares cymoso-paniculatae breves, 1-1.5 cm longae; axi brevissimo 2-3-ramoso; ramis ramulisque valde tenuibus angulatis glabris; bracteis bracteolisque ovatis acutis amplectentibus rubeseentibus 1-2 mm longis. Pedicelli tenues apice dilatati circa 1 mm. longi. Calyx cupularis glaber 0.6-0.8 mm altus, 1.5 mm diamitens, 5-lobatus lobis obtusissimis circa 0.2 mm longis. Petala 5 libera elliptica apice obtusiuscula glabra, circa 1.2 mm longa 0.8 mm lata. Stam- ina 5 alternipetala glabra filamento 0.3 mm longo, anthera ovato-cordata 0.2 mm. Discus crassus circa 1 mm diamitens. Ovarium cum disco inmersum paulo pyra- midale biloculare loculis biovulatis. Stylus crassiusculus brevis circa 0.1 mm longus.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1959. Studies in South American plants--V. Brittonia. 11: 163-172.

description: Arbor ad 5 m. Folia 8-13 cm longa, 3.5-5.5 cm lata, elliptica ad oblongo-elliptica, ad apice acuminata, acumine ca 1 cm longo, ad basim obtusa, glabra vel minute pilis stellaris; venae primariae 13-16 paria; petioli 0.6-1.2 cm longi. Inflorescentia racemosa spiciformis, rhachi ad 16 cm longa, densifloribus, pedicellis 2-3 mm longis. Flores parvae, sepalis reflexis, ovato-lanceolatis ad lanceolatis, 4-5 mm longis.

description: Small tree to 5 m, twigs finely ferrugineous or brown stellate pubescent, older branches glabrous. Leaves opposite, entire, 8.0-13.0 cm long, 3.5-5.5 cm wide, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, acuminate, acumen ca 1 cm long, basally obtuse, entirely glabrous above or sparsely and minutely stellate pubescent on costa; primary veins 13-16 pairs, 5.0-8.5 cm apart medially, slightly arcuate near margins, anas- tomosing into a marginal vein, veins depressed above, elevated beneath; petioles 0.6-1.2 cm long, pubescence similar to twigs. Inflorescence racemose, spike-like, solitary at axils from older defoliated nodes, rachis to 16 cm long, densely and minutely stellate pubescent, densely flowered, ca 8 flowers per cm, pedicels 2-3 mm long, shorter than the sepals, pubescence similar to rachis. Flowers small; perianth reflexed at anthesis; sepals 5, subcoriaceous, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 1.0-1.8 mm wide at base, 4.0-5.0 mm long, outer three sepals adaxially stellate pubescent, abaxially glabrous, inner sepals glabrous, petals not seen, sta- mens numerous, filament 0.5-2.0 mm long, anthers 0.5 mm long, terminal ap- pendage glandular and tubular, 1/2-1/3 length of anther; ovary 3 mm long, 1 mm wide; style 1 mm long, stigma conical. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Mcdearman, Will & McDaniel, Sidney T. 1985. Marila spiciformis (Bonnetiaceae), a new species from Peru. Brittonia. 37: 106-108.

description: Dioecious trees, ca. 20 meters tall, mostly less than 10 cm dbh (diameter at breast height); external bark smooth and grayish; branches terete, glabrous; latex yellow; stilt-roots 50-100(-130) cm long. Leaves opposite, decussate, clustered toward upper parts of the braniches with internodes (6-)7-10(-12) mm long; petiole (10-)17-21(--27) Mm long, 2 mm wide, slender, semi-terete with conspicuous transverse striations; blade (8.9-)10.5-11.5(-13.1) X 3.5-4.1(- 437) cm, oblong, coriaceous, basally attenuate to cuneate, apically acuminate to caudate, the margin thinly revolute; midvein conspicuously elevated on both surfaces but quadrangular on upper suerface, the secondary veins all nearly straight, almost per pendicular to the midvein, 1-2 mm apart, the intersecondary veins well developed, a marginal collector vein present; surface with irregularly distributed small black dots. Inflorescence terminal with I-few flowers. Staminate flowers unknown. Bracts caducous, not seen. Pedicels of pistillate flowers (3-)4-6(-7) mm long; flowers 9-12 X 10-14 mm at anthesis; external sepals 2, 7-8 mm long, 5-6 mm wide at base, triangular; internal sepals unknown. Petals 8-11 X 4-5 mm oblong. Staminodes 35-40, 3-4.5 mm long. Ovary 5-6 mm long, the styles 5, distinct, 2.8-3 mm long, the stigmas capitate, 1-1.5 mm diam. Fruit a septicidal capsule, 2.6 long X 1.8 cm diam., ellipsoidal, with persistent stigmas, 5-6 mm long, bright red within. Seeds 1 per locule, 17 X (7-)8 mm, reniform.
bibliographicCitation: García-Villacorta, R. & Hammel, Barry E. 2004. A noteworthy new species of Tovomita (Clusiaceae) from Amazonian white sand forests of Peru and Colombia. Brittonia. 56 (2): 132-135.

description: Stems filiform, light yellow to cream colored. Cymes glomerulate of (1-)2-7(-12) flowers; bracts 1-3 at the base of clusters and pedicels/flowers, membranous, subrotund, ovate, rhombic to ovate-lanceolate; margins entire to denticulate, apex acute to obtuse; pedicels (0)0.5-2.2 mm long. Floral buds rounded (rarely acute). Flowers (4-)5-merous, 1.8-3.1 mm long, membranous, receptacle and base of perianth without fleshy cells; papillae absent; laticifers visible in the midveins of calyx lobes, arranged in rows, elongate (Fig. lA). Calyx separating easily from corolla when rehydrated flowers are dissected, straw-yellow, reticulate and shiny, campanulate to urceolate, as long as the corolla tube or nearly so, lobes basally overlapping, obovate-orbicular, margins denticulate, apex rounded (Fig. lA). Corol- la creamy white when fresh, creamy yellow when dried; tube campanulate, 0.6-1.5 mm long; lobes reflexed, ca. equaling the tube, ovate to broadly elliptic, margins irregularly denticulate, apex rounded (Fig. lA). Stamens included to slightly exerted, shorter than corolla lobes; anthers 0.25-0.4 mm long, subrotund to elliptic; filaments 0.2- 0.4 mm long; pollen 3(-4)-zonocolpate, subprolate, 15-17.5 pm long, tectum  perforate or with a few isolate punctae, sexine scabrate with isolated granules. Infrastaminal scales reaching the filament bases, oblong-ovate, uniformly denticulate or fringed. Styles unequal, evenly filiform, 0.3-0.5 mm long, 1/3-1/2 as long as the ovary; stigmas capitate, globose. Capsules indehiscent to irregularly dehiscent, not persistent on peduncles, globose-ovoid, 1.3-2.1 X 1-2 mm, translucent, capped by the withered corolla. Seeds 1 per capsule, separating easily from capsules, globose to globose-ovoid, 0.85-1.1 x 0.82-1.1 mm, chalazal end rounded; hilum terminal, not sunken, 0.1-0.2 mm diam., vascular scar of funiculus very short, linear to punctiform, 0.02-0.04 mm long; seed coat alveolate when seeds are dry and papillose when seeds are hydrated, epidermis cells of 35-45 µm diam. (Fig. 2A); embryo globose-enlarged; endosperm entirely consumed at seed maturity.
bibliographicCitation: Costea, Mihai, et al. 2005. Taxonomic status of Cuscuta nevadensis and C. veatchii (Convolvulaceae) in North America. Brittonia. 57 (3): 264-272.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Stems filiform to medium, light yellow to cream colored. Inflorescences umbelliform of 1-2(-5) flowers; bracts 1 at the base of clusters and 0-1 at the base of pedicels, membranous, lanceolate, ovate-lanceolate, margins ± entire, apex acute; pedicels (0.5-)2.5-4 mm. Floral buds acute to acuminate. Flowers (4-)5-merous, (2.8- )3-4(-5) mm, creamy white, yellowish brown when dried, membranous but receptacle and base of perianth with fleshy cells that become gelatinized upon rehydratation (Fig. 1 C, E); papillae absent; laticifers evident in the calyx, along midveins, arranged in rows, elongate. Calyx usually difficult to separate from corolla when rehydrated flowers are dissected, golden yellowto brown, reticulate and shiny, divided ca. 2/3 the length, narrow-campanulate, as long as the corolla tube, lobes basally overlapping, lanceolate, margins ? entire, apex acute to acuminate (Fig. IC). Corolla white creamy when fresh, yellow-orange to brownish when dried; tube campanulate, 1.3-2.5 mm long; lobes suberect to reflexed, equaling the tube or somewhat longer, ovate to oblong, margins entire to irregularly denticulate, apex acute (Fig. IC). Stamens included or slightly exerted, shorter than corolla lobes; anthers elliptic to oblong, 0.4-0.7 mm long, filaments (0-) 0.1-0.3 mm long; pollen 3(-4)-zonocolpate, subprolate to prolate, 18-21.3 Rpm long, tectum imperforate or with a few iso- lated punctae, sexine scabrate with isolated granules. Infrastaminal scales reaching the filament bases, broadly-ovate to subrotund, truncate, margins uniformly short fimbriate. Styles unequal, uniformly filiform, 0.5-1 mm, 1/2 to equaling the ovary; stigmas capitate, globose. Capsules indehiscent to irregularly dehiscent, persistent on peduncles, globose-ovoid to ovoid, 1.4-2.1 x 1.2-2 mm, translucent, capped by the withered corolla (Fig. 2 F). Seeds 1 per capsule, adnate to capsules and separating only through abrasion, globose-ovoid, 0.9-1.2 X 0.85-1.08 mm, chalazal end narrowed to apiculate; hilum sunken, 0.17-0.25 mm diam.; vascular scar of fu- niculus punctiform, 0.015-0.02 mm long; seed coat alveolate when seeds are dry and papillose when seeds are hydrated, epidermis cells of 35-45 pm diam. (Fig. 2C); embryo globose-enlarged (Fig. 2E); endosperm entirely consumed at seed maturity.
bibliographicCitation: Costea, Mihai, et al. 2005. Taxonomic status of Cuscuta nevadensis and C. veatchii (Convolvulaceae) in North America. Brittonia. 57 (3): 264-272.

description: Perennial (annual in temperate regions). Herbaceous twining vine, woody at base, 5-30 m long, glabrous or glabrate, producing sarmentose shoots which may root (Fig. 2). Stems usually armed at least toward the base with numerous herbaceous spines or warts 2-4 mm long. Juice milky. Petioles long and slender, 5-20 cm, smooth or muricate. Leaves glabrous or glabrate, thin, 6-20 cm long, 5-16 cm wide with about 7-8 lateral nerves on each side of midrib, ovate or orbicular, seldom oblong to ovate-oblong, cordate at base, acuminate with excurrent midrib at apex simple or 3-lobed (to nearly hastate or several-lobed). Inflorescences axillary, 1-6(-8)-flowered, usually longer than subtending leaves. Peduncles 1-24 cm long, smooth or muricate. Pedicles 7-15 mm long, smooth, thicker toward apex in flower, greatly thickening and somewhat elongating (2 5-30 mm) in fruit. Bracts 2, fugacious, scarious, about 1.5 mm wide, at the base of pedicel. Sepals 5, unequal in length, 2 or 3 exterior ones shorter and thicker (coriaceous), bearing a long thick recurved or patent awn, interior sepals longer, mucronulate with a less well- developed awn, all sepals in flowering stage (excluding awns) 5-15 mm long, 5-6 mm wide, and in fruiting stage enlarging to 15-20 mm long, 8-10 mm wide, awns 2-8 mm long, reflexed in fruit. Corollas salverform, fragrant; tube 7-12 cm long, 3-6 mm in diameter, white, glabrous without, pubescent within on lower half; limb glabrous throughout, 11-14 cm in diameter, white with greenish plaits, rarely deeply five-lobed. Stamens exserted, white, attached to corolla near top of tube, glabrous. Stigmas exserted, overtopping stamens, capitate, 2-lobed. Capsules 2.5-3 cm long, ovoid to turbinate, mucronate by persistent stylar base, thick-walled, longer than calyx, 2-celled, 4-seeded, on thickened, erect pedicels. Seeds 10-12 mm long, 8-9 mm wide, spheroidal, glabrous (minute hairs may be present around hilum), monochrome light ochre, brown, or blackish-brown. Chromosome number: 2n = 30 (King & Bamford, 1937).

description: Herba perennis, prostrata; foliis sessilibus, linearibus, 1-2 cm longis, 2-4 mm latis. Flores solitarii, axillares; pedunculis brevibus; sepala 4-7 mm longa, acuta, extus sericea; corolla 8-13 mm longa, alba; filamenta villosa; ovarium hirsutum; stylus bifidus; stigmata capitata; capsula conica; cotyledonae valde bifidae, petiolarae. description: Perennial, herbaceous, prostrate vines, from deep roots, underground stems, or lower nodes of previous shoots. Stems 1-2(-3) dm long, 0.5-1 mm thick, densely hairy. Leaves narrowly linear-elliptic, narrowly linear-oblong or narrowly linearlanceolate, ca 1-1.8(-2) cm long, 1.5-2(-2.5) mm wide, sessile; apex acute or obtuse; surface densely villous with silvery grey or brown hairs; veins indistinct except midrib. Flowers solitary, on short peduncles; peduncles mostly shorter than leaves; bracteoles linear, leaf-like, 2-5 mm long, ca 1 mm wide, villous. Sepals 4-7 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, mostly half the length of corolla or longer; apex subacute or subacuminate, rarely obtuse; outside surface densely villous. Corolla white, funnelform, 8-13 mm long or slightly longer, mostly shorter than twice the length of sepals. Stamens included; filaments unequal, shorter than styles, villous. Ovary thin-walled, densely villous; styles free almost to the bases; stylar branches unequal, mostly included; stigmas peltate, rarely subglobose. Fruits mostly 1- or 2-seeded, 4-valvular, thin-walled capsules. Cotyledonary petioles free. Flowering from early May to late July.

description: Stems mostly prostrate or twining, usually 1-2.5 m long, rarely slightly longer, nearly glabrous to villous with silvery grey hairs, more densely on the growing regions; upper portions twisted with tendency of twining. Leaves with petioles 1-12 mm long, the blades narrowly oblong to oblong, oblong-elliptic or oblonglanceolate, 3-7.5(-8) cm long, 1.2-3 cm wide; base slightly cordate or obtuse; apex obtuse, acute or obtuse-mucronate. Inflorescences axillary pedunculate cymes of 3-7(-12) flowers, rarely solitary through the abortion of lateral buds. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, glabrous on outside (rearely slightly puberulous near the tips), 6-9 mm long, 3-5 mm wide; margins ciliate. Corolla white, 2-2.3 cm long. Stamens included; filaments filiform, unequal, up to 23 the length of corolla, distinctly shorter than styles, villous near the bases. Ovary with a brownish glabrous basal disc and long-villous apex; stylar branches fused for half their length or more, unequal, slightly shorter than corolla. Fruits mostly 2-seeded, occasionally 1-4-seeded, glabrous except at the apices. Cotyledonary petioles free. Flowering from May to August.

description: Stems twining or prostrate, 0.5-2 m long, 1-2.5 mm thick, villous with grey or brownish haris. Leaves narrowly oblong-lanceolate or narrowly oblong-elliptic, mostly 3-7 cm long, (0.6-) 1-2 cm wide; petioles 3-10 mm long; apex obtuse mucronulate or acute; base obtuse; surface densely villous, rarely thinly so. Inflorescences solitary or cymes of mostly 3-7 (-12) flowers; bracts opposite, mostly equal. Sepals 7-11 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, oval-lanceolate with acuminate or rarely acute apex; outside surface densely villous with grey or brownish hairs. Corolla white, mostly 1.5-2.5 cm long. Stamens inserted, rarely partially exserted; filaments unequal, distinctly glandular villous at least near the base. Ovary villous with long hairs on outside at least near the stylar base; stylar branches fused for lower one-third or more, unequal in length, longer than filaments, usually with long and scattered hairs near the base; stigmas subglobose or peltate. Fruits mostly 1- or 2-seeded, rarely 3- or 4-seeded, 4-6 mm long, 3-4 mm wide with villous walls. Cotyledonary petioles free or slightly fused at the base. Flowering from late April to August.

description: Whole plant sparsely or densely beset with appressed hairs; roots adventitious at the nodes, 0.1-0.2 mm thick; stolons 0.3-0.7 (-0.9) mm thick, sparingly branched, occasionally with short lateral shoots with a few very crowded nodes; internodes usually (0.8-) 1.3-2 (-3.5) cm long; leaf-blades suborbicular, (8-) 11-16 (-20) mm long, (7-) 11-15 (-19) mm broad, apically rounded or usually shallowly emarginate, broadly cordate with shallow to deep sinuses (lower surfaces usually very densely pubescent, giving the whole a silvery sheen contrasted with the much less pubescent green upper surface); petioles (0.5-) 1-2 (-7.0) cm long, 0.3-0.6 (-0.9) mm thick, weak, arcuate or curvilinear; pedicels (5-) 10-20 (-35) mm long, ca. 0.2 mm thick, arching, erect, often slightly nodding or curved in the upper portion but rarely making more than a 90º arc; calyx campanulate; sepals obovate to obovate-spatulate, 1.8-2.5 mm long at anthesis, accreseent to 2.4-3.3 mm in fruit, pubescent outside, about twice as long as broad; corolla shorter than calyx, 1.6-2 mm long, 5-lobed about half the length, the lobes lanceolate, acute, usually greenish-yellow; anthers and filaments extremely short, the anthers often purple; styles ca. 1 mm long; "utricles" 2-3.5 mm long, 1.8-2.5 mm thick, each often falling entire but apparently often half-persistent, and each "utricle" dehiscing loculicidally and half fallino off; seeds pyriform, 1.7-2.1 mm long.

description: Herbaceous vines; stems rather stout, 1.5-3.5 mm diam, glabrescent to densely pubescent, especially when young. Leaf blades broadly ovate, 4-12 cm long and 2-8.5 cm wide, the apex tapering-acute to acuminate and mucronate, the base cordate to truncate, glabrescent to sparsely pubescent above and glabrescent to adpressed-pubescent or velutinous beneath; petioles 3-8 cm long, slender, 0.5-1 mm diam, sparsely to densely pubescent. Inflorescence a capitate cyme; peduncles exceeding the petioles and often the leaf blades, 2.5-17 cm long, stout, 1.5-4 mm diam, glabrescent to densely pubescent; outer bracts broadly to transversely ovate or elliptic, strongly concave, 1.2-2 cm long and 1-2.5 cm wide, the apex obtuse to rounded, slightly mucronate, abaxially velutinous with trichomes less than 1 mm long, the 2 outermost bracts often ? enclosing the inflorescence; inner bracts narrowly ovate or obovate, abaxially sericeous. Sepals 5, subequal, the outer slightly exceeding the inner, narrowly obovate, with acuminate apices, 1.5-2 cm long and 6-9 mm wide, abaxially pilose with trichomes 2-5 mm long, adaxially glabrous; corolla white or pale lavender, 2.5-3.5 cm long, the 5 midpetaline bands densely pubescent with long, spreading trichomes; stamens somewhat unequal, included, inserted on the corolla tube 6-8 mm from the base, the free portions of the filaments 4-6 mm long; style 1-1.5 cm long, equalling the stamens, fre- quently persistent; stigmatic lobes globose, 0.5 mm diam. Capsule enclosed by the sepals and infiorescence bracts, broadly ovoid, 1.2 cm long, thin-walled, black, with scattered upright trichomes, 4-seeded, evidently dehiscing by 2 valves; seeds light reddish-brown, glabrous, smooth, 5.5 mm long and 3 mm wide; embryo lati-longiplicate, surrounded by persistent endosperm.

description: Perennial woody vine, trailing or twining, up to 10 m long, glabrous, without herbaceous spines or warts. Stems covered by a rough, thin, grayish to yellowish bark bearing brown punctations, partially exfoliating on woody portions, sometimes rooting if prostrate. Juice milky. Petioles 3-16 cm long with purple gland on each side at base of lamina. Leaves glabrous above and below, usually bearing brown punctations below, 5-16 cm long, 5-14 cm wide, with 7-8 lateral nerves on each side of midrib, somewhat thick or of a coriaceous texture, broadly ovate or orbicular, cordate at  base, acuminate with excurrent midrib at apex, simple or rarely with 1-3 well- developed lateral lobes. Inflorescences axillary with 1 (rarely 2-3) flowers, usually longer than subtending leaves. Peduncles 0.7-7 (-12) cm long. Pedicels 14-30 mm long, angular, slightly thickened in fruit. Bracts 2, fugacious, minute, inserted at the base of pedicels. Sepals 5, about equal in length, orbicular, outer 2 coriaceous, 15-25 mm long, inner 3 thinner, 18-25 mm long with innermost encircling corolla tube, all broadly rounded, mucronulate, usually rounded or blunt or infrequently deeply to shallowly emarginate at apex (never bearing long appendages), all enlarging (up to 30 mm long) and becoming coriaceous and reflexed in fruit. Corolla salverform, without fragrance; tube 5-12 cm long, 6-10 mm wide, white and glabrous without, white and minutely pubescent within (glabrous below in- sertion of stamens); limb glabrous, 6-7 cm in diameter, white with yellowish or greenish plaits. Stamens included in tube, white, unequal (2 long and 3 short), filaments bearing minute unbranched hairs near insertion near base of corolla tube. Stigma included in tube but overtopping anthers, capitate, 2-lobed. Capsules globose-acuminoid, 2-3 cm in diameter, thin-walled, 2-celled, 4-seeded, on slightly thickened, non-reflexed pedicels. Seeds 10-11 mm long, 8-9 mm wide, spheroidal, dark brown, covered with minute pale hairs, with the longer hairs restricted to margins and hilar region. Chromosome number unknown.

description: Perennial; woody trailing or twining vine, to at least 4 m long, puberulent becoming glabrate with age. Stems woody (at base of plant), covered with brown exfoliating bark, lacking herbaceous spines or warts. Juice clear. Petioles 5-15 cm long, smooth. Leaves glabrous or glabrate above, puberulent to glabrate and covered with minute black glands below, 8-25 cm long and about as wide, with 7-9 lateral veins on each side of midrib, thin, orbicular, cordate at base, shortly acuminate with minute excurrent midrib at rounded or emarginate apex, simple or rarely with a weakly developed lateral lobe midway between base and apex. Inflorescences axillary with 1-3 (-4) flowers, usually shorter than subtending leaves. Peduncles 2-8 cm long, smooth. Pedicels 1-3 cm long, smooth, not thickening at maturity. Bracts 2, fugacious, obovate to oblong, about 1 cm long, inserted at base of pedicel. Sepals 5, subequal, orbicular, densely black-glandular dotted, the outer 2 coriaceous, scarious along margins, puberulent to glabrate, 1-2 cm long, the inner 3 thin, 1-2 cm long, all broadly rounded and usually mucronulate (never bearing long appendages), all usually greatly enlarging (ca. 4 cm) and becoming coriaceous and clasping fruit (never reflexed) at maturity, the epidermis eventually disintegrating to leave only a vascular skeleton. Corolla funnel-shaped, noticeably constricted just above calyx, apparently without fragrance; tube 5-8 cm long, 1.5-2 cm in diameter, yellowish at base becoming crimson toward apex, glabrous bearing black to colorless glands without on 5 plaits, the folds essentially eglandular and each bearing a central crimson nectar guide, eglandular within and bearing 2 well-defined and 3 poorly-defined crimson nectar guides on each plait and a central guide in each fold; limb about 8 cm in diameter, crimson (fading to purple upon drying or disintegrating), glabrous except for 5 patches of marginal cilia centered around minutely excurrent plait tips (margins of folds glabrous) and scattered hairs at apices of plaits especially in bud. Stamens included in tube, white, unequal (2 long and 3 short), filaments bearing purplish red hairs for about 3 mm above insertion on corolla tube. Stigmas purple, included in tube but over- topping anthers, capitate, 2-lobed. Fruit a dry berry, thin-walled, indehiscent, encased by enlarged fleshy sepals, subspherical and obscurely pointed, about 3.5 cm in diameter, 2-celled, 4-seeded, on non-thickened, non-reflexed pedicels. Seeds 10 mm long, 8 mm wide, obovoid, obscurely angular, grayish brown, covered with minute hairs. Chromosome number: 2n = 30 (Darlington & Wylie, 1955).

description: Whole plant except corolla and interior of calyx more or less sparsely pubescent with short slightly raised soft hairs; taproots, if developed, not seen; roots adventitious at the nodes; rhizomes perennial, apparently vernally budding at some nodes, 1-1.7 mm thick, sparingly to profusely branched, often with short lateral shoots with very crowded nodes; internodes (0.5-) 1-2 (-2.5) cm long; blades suborbicular to reniform, (8-) 12-20 (-27) mm long, (15-) 20-30 (-42) mm broad, apically often shallowly emarginate, basally broadly cordate with a shallow sinus on either side of the shortly cuneate portion of the leaf-blade where it joins the petiole, nearly glabrous; petioles (1.2-) 2.5-6 (-10) cm long, 0.3-0.7 (-1) mm thick, weak and arcuate or curvilinear. Pedicels 5-20 (-31) mm long, 0.2-0.4 (-0.6) mm thick, erect but sharply recurved in the upper portion; calyx broadly campanulate, 1.5-2 mm long at anthesis, accrescent to 2-2.3 mm in fruit, pubescent outside, 5-lobed five-sixths the length, the lobes lanceolate-oblong, shortly truncate or rounded apically; corolla funnelform, 3-3.5 mm long (exceeding calyx), glabrous, purplish to reddish (or "crimson" according to one author), 5-lobed about half the length, the lobes lanceolate, acute; anthers and filaments each about 0.2 mm long; ovary slightly bilobed; styles essentially separate, 1.5-1.7 mm long, promptly deciduous; capsules slightly bilobed, 2.8-3.8 mm high, 4.5-5 mm long, 2.1-2.6 mm wide; seeds 2.5-3 mm long, dark brown to black.

description: Plants, except interior of calyx, corolla, stamens, styles and seeds, more or less pubescent with appressed yellow-buffy, somewhat sericeous hairs; tap-root, if developed, not discernible; roots adventitious at the nodes; rhizomes (or occasionally stolons?) apparently vernally budding at the nodes, 1-1.8 mm thick, somewhat branched, often with short lateral shoots with very crowded nodes; internodes (0.5-) 1-2 (-3) cm long; blades suborbicular-reniform, (5-) 10-15 (-22) mm long, (8-) 15-25 (-38) mm broad, apically rounded or shallowly emarginate, basally broadly cordate with a shallow sinus, the upper surface sparsely pubescent, the lower usually more densely pubescent and less green; petioles (1.5-) 2-4 (-7) cm long, 0.4-1.1 mm thick, weak, arenate or curvilinear; pedicels (4-) 8-15 (-20) mm long, erect but sharply recurved in the upper portion; calyx broadly campanulate, 2-3 mm long at anthesis, acereseent to 2.5- 3.7 mm in fruit, 5-lobed three-fourths to four-fifths the length, the lobes nearly equal, broadly obovate, apically rounded, touching or narrowly overlapping, marginally ciliate; corolla campanulate, 2-3 mm long, glabrous, white or green- ish-white, 5-lobed more than half the length, the lobes broadly lanceolate, acute; filaments and anthers each ca. 0.3 mm long; styles nearly equal, ca. 1 mm long, essentially distinct; utrieles 2.5-3.9 mm high, 2.5-3 mm thick, pilose toward the summit, each falling with its seed; seed 2.4-3 mm long, slightly distended at the micropylar end, dark brown when mature.

description: Plants, except interior of calyx, corolla, stamens, styles and seeds, more or less densely pubescent with sericeous tawny hairs; roots adventitious at the nodes; rhizomes perennial, apparently vernally budding at the nodes, 1-1.9 mm thick, somewhat branched, very often with short lateral shoots with very crowded nodes; internodes (1-) 2-3 (-5) cm long; blades suborbicular-reniform, (10-) 20-30 (-51) mm long, (15-) 30-40 (-62) mm broad, apically rounded or shal- lowly emarginate, basally broadly cordate with a shallow sinus, the lower surface and especially the margins densely pubescent, the upper surface much less densely so; petioles (2-) 4-8 (-17) cm long, 0.5-0.9 mm thick, weak, arcuate or curvilinear; pedicels (5-) 9-17 (-13) mm long, erect but sharply recurved in the upper portion; calyx very broadly campanulate, 2.5-3.2 mm long at anthesis, acereseent to 2.9-3.8 mm in fruit, 5-lobed five-sixths to nine-tenths the length, the lobes somewhat unequal, broadly obovate, apically rounded, broadly over-lapping, marginally densely ciliate; corolla campanulate or funnelform, 3.1-4 mm long, glabrous inside and out, 5-lobed a little more than half the length, the tube slightly constricted at the throat, the lobes lanceolate, acute; filaments and anthers each ca. 0.5 mm long; carpels separate; styles commonly slightly unequal, 1.1-1.6 mm long, essentially distinct; utricles 3-4 mm high, 2.8-3.3 mm thick, pilose, each falling with its seed; seed 2.8-3.1 mm long, slightly distended at the micropylar end, dark brown when mature.

description: Whole plant except roots, stamens, corolla and styles silvery-canescent with a dense pubescence of long, silky, usually appressed, flattened hairs; taproots perennial, dark brown, 1.8-4 mm thick; stolons annual, 10-35 from the crown, ca. 0.7-1.1 mm thick, rarely branched; internodes 1-2.5 (-3) cm long; nodes often bearing adventitious roots and occasionally short-shoots with crowded nodes; leaf-blades reniform, 5-13 mm long, 12-20 mm broad, apically often shal- lowly emarginate, basally truneate or broadly and shallowly cordate, with a narrow cuneate base where the blade joins the petiole; petioles (1-) 2-3 (-5) cm long, 0.5-1 mm thick, erect, straight; pedicels 4-6 mm long, 0.5-1 mm thick, basally sharply recurved; calyx broadly campanulate, 2-2.6 mm long at anthesis, acerescent to 2.4-3 mm in fruit, 5-lobed two-thirds to three-fourths the length, the lobes linear-oblong, apically blunt and often somewhat recurved; corolla nearly cylindrical, 3.4-4 mm long, creamy, 5-lobed about half the length or more, the lobes subulate; ovary only slightly bilobed; styles 1-2.3 mm long, slender, entirely free or somewhat coherent a fifth or less; capsule 2.2-2.8 mm high, 3.9-4.4 (-6) mm long, and 2-2.1 mm wide; seeds 1.9-2.4 mm long, slightly distended at the micropylar elnd, dark brown to black when fully mature.
bibliographicCitation: Fulford, Margaret H. & Taylor, Jane. 1961. Segregate genera of the Lepidozia complex (Hepaticae) Part 2. Two new genera, Bonneria and Paracromastigum. Brittonia. 13: 334-339.

description: Whole plant except roots and flowers with a more or less close pubescence of soft, silky hairs, giving the plant a pale tawny-green cast; taproots pale brown, 1.5-2.8 mm thick; stolons annual, 3-11 from the crown, ca. 0.6-1 mm thick, rarely branched; ilnternodes 2-4 (-8) cm long, the nodes often with adventitious roots; blades suborbicular to reniform, (8-) 12-20 (-40) mm long, (10-) 16-30 (-55) mm broad, apically often shallowly emarginate, basally trun- cate or broadly cordate usually with a rather deep sinus oni either side of the narrowly cuneate portion of the leaf-base where it joins the petiole, the upper surface only sparsely pubescent; petioles (1.5-) 2-4 (-15) em long, 0.3-0.5 (-0.9) mm thick, weak and often arcuate or curvilinear; pedicels 5-13 (-26) mm long, 0.6-1 mm thick, sharply recurved, usually in the upper portion; calyx broadly campanulate, 3-4 mm long at anthesis, acereseent to 3.8-5.2 mm in fruit, villous outside, 5-lobed three-fourths to four-fifths the length, the lobes lanceolate, apically acute or in fruit recurved and appearing blunt; corolla narrowly cam- panulate, 3.5-5 mm long, creamy, villous outside, glabrous inside, 5-lobed about two-thirds the length, the lobes lanceolate, acute; ovary slightly bilobed; styles 1.7-2.5 mm long, very slender, in fresh material coherent a fifth their length or less, in dried material appearing quite distinct; capsules nearly spherical, shortly hispid, 3.8-5 mm high, 6-7 mm long, 3-5 mm wide; seeds 2.8-4 mm long, slightly distended at the mieropylar end, dark brown whenl fully mature.

description: Herba volubilis Ipomoeae hederifoliae affinis; laminae ovatae, integrae vel remote dentatae vel trilobae; ramuli inflorescentiae dichasiales, per 50-90% divergentes; pedicelli erecti; sepala interiora 2.5-4 mm longa; aristae sepalorum 4-6 mm longae; anthesis crepuscula; corolla bicolor, rosea et aurantiaca; capsula ovoidea, acuta; semina angulata, tomento homogeneo fulvo et nigro instructa.
bibliographicCitation: Eckenwalder, James E. 1989. A new species of Ipomoea section Quamoclit (Convolvulaceae) from the Caribbean and a new combination for a Mexican species. Brittonia. 41: 75-79.

description: Annual or short-lived perennial, vigorous, glabrous, herbaceous, twining vine climbing to 4 m; stem longitudinally ribbed; leaf blade ovate, entire, with a few remote teeth, or 3-lobed, deeply cordate with a square sinus, (2.5) 7-12 (15) cm long, (1. 5) 6.5-9 (12) cm wide; petiole about equal in length to blade. Inflorescence axillary, (1) 3-9 (13)-flowered, with one or two successive dichasial branchings, the remainder monochasial; peduncle about equalling the subtending petiole, the dichasial branches almost as thick as the peduncle, diverging at 50-90?, (7) 12- 20 mm long, the monochasial branches about equalling them; pedicels erect in fruit, slender, 5-9 mm long. Flowers opening in the evening, lasting until the following afternoon; sepals 2.5-4 mm long, slightly emarginate, aristate, the awn 4-6 mm long; corolla slightly zygomorphic, subhypocrateriform, the tube curved, (25) 28-30 (35) mm long, greenish-pink, the limb slightly cup-shaped, pentagonal, (15) 19-21 (25) mm across, alternating pink and orange; stamens and style sub- equal in length, slightly exserted, white. Capsule ovoid, 6-8 mm long, acute, surmounted by a remnant of the base of the style, this 0.3-0.4 mm long, 4-valved and 4-loculed, the valves persistent after dehiscence, the locules separated by hyaline partitions. Seeds 4-5 mm long, the ventral faces flat, the dorsal convex, with a shallow, narrow, longitudinal groove, brown, covered with a uniform coat of stiff hairs, these 0.3-0.5 mm long, predominantly tan, but with irregular dark mottling. Chromosome number 2n = 28 (from root tips of Eckenwalder 2525).

description: A slender, trailing or twining, perennial vine. Stems to 10 m long, 1-7 mm in diam, lignescent, contorted, striate, glabrous. Leaves simple, petiolate; petiole 4.5-6.5 cm long, 1-2 mm in diam, smooth, glabrous; blade variable, palmatisect to subpinnatisect, 3.5-10.5 cm long, 3.5-12 cm wide, usually divided into 3-7 major lobes, lobes ovate-elongate to elliptic-elongate to linear, 3-8.5 cm long, 1.5-4 cm wide, incised or dentate-sinuate, teeth ovate-elongate to lanceolate or linear, to 7 cm long, 2-25 mm wide, attenuate, basally truncate, glabrous, apices of lobes acute, mucronulate. Inflorescence 1-5-flowered monochasial cymes; peduncles terete, 7-14 cm long, 1-2 mm in diam, smooth, glabrous; pedicels terete, 1-1.2 cm long, 2-4 mm in diam, smooth, glabrous. Sepals equal, elliptic, 1.4-1.7 cm long and ca 8 mm wide during anthesis, to 2.5 cm long and 1.5 cm wide in fruit, coriaceous, glabrous, light green in flower, red and succulent during fruit maturation, reflexed and tan when dry, margins scarious, apex subacute to obtuse. Corolla infundibular, yellow throughout, 2.5-3 cm long, 3-5 mm in diam at base of tube, limb 4-5 cm wide, glabrous; stamens unequal, 1.7-2.2 cm long, white, filaments adnate to lower third of corolla tube, anthers slightly twisted, white; style ca 1.7 cm long, white; stigma capitate, bilobed, ca 1 mm in diam, white. Fruit a subglobose, depressed capsule, ca 1.2 cm long, ca 2 cm wide, locules 2, valves 4, dehiscing irregularly, tan, membranous, translucent. Seeds 4, subglobose, 8-12 mm long, 7-9 mm thick, black, shortly black-tomentose.
bibliographicCitation: McDonald, J. Andrew. 1987. Three new species of Convolvulaceae from northeast Mexico. Brittonia. 39: 106-111.

description: A trailing and twining, woody, perennial vine. Stems ca 1 m long, 2-5 mm in diam, ligneous, contorted, striate, glabrous or sparsely pilose at nodes, new growth green, old growth pale gray to brown. Leaves simple, petiolate; petiole 2.8-5.4 cm long, ca 2 mm in diam, striate, glabrous or sparingly pilose at base and distally; blade variable, ovate to subtrilobate, 3.8-4.5 cm long, 3.4-4.5 cm wide, glabrous, margins sinuate-crenulate, basally auriculate, basal lobes round, 1.2-1.5 cm long, 1.6-2.9 cm wide, apex acute or obtuse. Flowers axillary, solitary; peduncles shorter than petioles, 1.5-2.2 cm long, ca 1 mm in diam, glabrous or basally sparsely pilose; pedicels about equal in length to peduncles, 1.8-2.3 cm long, 1-2 mm in diam, glabrous or sparsely pilose. Sepals equal, elliptic to elliptic-elongate, 1.3- 1.6 cm long, 4-5 mm wide, outer coriaceous, green, with soft, minute appressed hairs, inner coriaceous, with membranous margins. Corolla crepuscular, subhy- pocrateriform, tube expanding gradually distally, 4-5.5 cm long, 5-7 mm in diam at base, purple inside, limb ca 4 cm wide, white, plicae glabrous, interplicae conspicuously pilose; stamens unequal, filaments 5-6.5 cm long, fused to lower third of tube, glandular pubescent at point of adnation. Fruits not seen.
bibliographicCitation: McDonald, J. Andrew. 1987. Three new species of Convolvulaceae from northeast Mexico. Brittonia. 39: 106-111.

description: A slender, climbing, twining vine. Stems terete, 1-2 mm in diam, contorted, striate, often red-pigmented, glabrous; internodes 2.3-3.8 cm long. Leaves simple, petiolate; petioles 1-3 cm long, less than 1 mm in diam, glabrous, smooth; blade variable, ovate to subsagittate, 2.5-4.5 cm long, 1-2.5 cm wide, membranous, basal lobes rounded or subacute, 4-12 mm long, 4-10 mm wide, margins entire, apex acuminate, attenuate, mucronulate. Flowers solitary, axillary; peduncles terete, longer than pedicel, 1.2-3 cm long, ca 1 mm in diam, smooth, glabrous; pedicel terete, 3-11 mm long, ca 1.5 mm in diam, smooth, glabrous, subtended by minute, aristate bracteoles. Sepals unequal, elliptic-elongate, dotted with dark glands, inner 4.5-6 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, tan, membranous, acute or subemarginate, mucronulate, outer elliptic, ca 2 mm long, 3.5 mm wide, chartaceous, obtuse, mucronulate. Corolla infundibular, 4-5 cm long, tube 5-7 mm in diam at base, throat 1.2-1.5 cm in diam, limbs subentire, ca 4 cm wide, red-purple, glabrous; stamens unequal, 9-22 mm long, style exceeding stamens, 2.8- 3 cm long. Fruits not seen.
bibliographicCitation: McDonald, J. Andrew. 1987. Three new species of Convolvulaceae from northeast Mexico. Brittonia. 39: 106-111.

description: Robust, twining, herbaceous or lignescent at base, annual vines. Stems twining, terete, to 6 m long, 2-5 mm diam, smooth, somewhat striate and frequently alate on mature growth, green or purple-pigmented, glabrous. Leaves simple, persistent, petiolate; lamina ovate or rarely subtrilobate, 4.3-10.5 cm long, 2.5-7.5 cm wide, membranous, glabrous, the margins entire, the apex acute or subacuminate, mu- cronate; basally cordate or auriculate, the basal lobes 4-16 mm long, 0.9-3.8 cm wide; venation pinnate; petioles terete, 1-6 cm long, 0.5-1 mm diam, glabrous. Inflorescence a corymbiform cyme, the first branching dichasial, followed by monochasial branching; flowers 3-9; primary peduncle terete, 37-100 mm long, 1.5-3 mm diam, green, alate or smooth, glabrous; secondary peduncle similar, 6-17 mm long, ca 1 mm diam, subtended by squamose bracteoles about 1 mm long and wide; pedicles erect, 7-15 mm long, 1-2 mm diam, dilated at the apex, green, smooth or striate, glabrous; sepals subequal or unequal, imbricate, pale green or drying to pale tan, the outer shorter than the inner, elliptic, orbicular, obovate to ovate, frequently subcochleate, 4-11 mm long, 3-6 mm wide, mem- branous, glabrous, the margins entire, scarious, the apices acute, obtuse or emarginate, occasionally minutely apiculate; corolla infundibular, 3.5-6 cm long, the tube lavender, 2.5-4 cm long, 8-13 mm diam, dilating gradually, the buds con- volute-duplicate, glabrous; the limb sublobate, scarcely 10-lobate, lavender, 5-6 cm wide, glabrous; stamens unequal, included, white, 1.5-3.5 cm long, the fila- ments fused to the base of the corolla tube, glandular-pubescent; the style white  exceeding the stamens, 2.5-4 cm long, glabrous; stigma lavender, capitate, bilo- bate. Capsule, brown, subconical, 7-9 mm long and wide at base, 2-locular, 4-valvular, dehiscent, chartaceous, glabrous; seeds 4, black, rotund, triangular, 3-4 mm long and wide, the lateral angles with fine white trichomes 5-7 mm long, deciduous.
bibliographicCitation: McDonald, J. Andrew & Austin, D. F. 1990. Changes and additions in Ipomoea section Batatas (Convolvulaceae). Brittonia. 42: 116-120.

description: Slender, herbaceous, annual vines. Stems twining, 0.94-1.42 m long, 1-5 mm diam, green or light-purple pigmented, hirsute, trichomes ca 1 mm long; roots fibrous. Leaves simple, persistent, petiolate; lamina ovate to cordate, 2.2-2.9 cm long, hirsute and also with more densely appressed trichomes than the stems, margins entire, apex acuminate, aristate, the base truncate to shallowly cordate; venation palmate; petiole terete, 0.5-2.3 cm long, 0.5 mm diam, hirsute with erect trichomes. Inflorescence capitulate-cymose; flowers 1-3, only one open per inflorescence per day in anthesis; peduncles axillary, terete, 1.8-2.2 cm long, ca 1 mm diam, hirsute; pedicels 1-4 mm long, purple near the base; bracts foliose, broadly ovate, 7-10 mm long, 6-7 mm wide, acute, mucronulate, hirsute; sepals subequal or the outer to 1 mm longer than inner, quincuncial, green, ovate to lanceolate, 6-7.5 mm long, the outer 2 mostly 3-3.5 mm wide, herbaceous, the inner 1.5-2.5 mm wide, herbaceous, hirsute, the margins thin and scarious, the apices acuminate; corolla funnelform, 1.3-2.1 cm long, the tube white, 5-7 mm long, 3-6 mm wide when pressed, dilating gradually; the remotely hirsute limb entire to shallowly 5-lobed, lavender, 1.2-1.4 cm wide; stamens unequal, included, white, filaments 6-14 mm long, fused to the base of the corolla tube, glandular pubescent on the lower 3-4 mm, the anthers 1-1.25 mm long; pollen globose, pantoporate, 107.14-135.71 µm in diam, spinulose, the spines bottle-shaped, 3.57-9.52 µm long; ovary ovoid, 1.5 mm long, glabrous, the style 13-14 mm long, shorter than longest stamens, the stigma capitate, 2-globose, 0.75-1 mm long and wide, white. Fruit a capsule included within the sepals, brown, ovoid, 6-6.5 mm long, 4.5-5.9 mm wide, 2-loculed, 4-valved, dehiscent, the dehisced valves chartaceous, glabrous, 5.2-8.5 mm long, 2.5-4.5 mm wide; seeds 2-4, black to dark brown, ovoid, keeled, 3.0-4.2 mm long, 2.8-3.9 mm wide, puberulent. 2n = 30.
bibliographicCitation: Austin, Daniel F. 1991. Ipomoea sawyeri (Convolvulaceae), a new species from Peru. Brittonia. 43: 93-95.

description: Suffruticose perennial, arising from a taproot. Stems prostrate and branching to form mats, sericeous with 2-armed trichomes, rooting at nodes. Leaves crowded along short internodes, the petioles mostly 1-2 mm long; blades somewhat thickened, elliptic to lanceolate-elliptic, basally rounded to obtuse, apically acute to occasionally retuse, 6-14 x 3-9 mm, sericeous with 2-armed trichomes. Flowers solitary in leaf axils, subsessile, widely spaced in comparison to their size; peduncles absent; bracteoles 2-2.5 x 0.5 mm; pedicels 0.5-1 mm; sepals 5, free to the base, unequal, the outer ovate-lanceolate, apically acute, 3.5-4 x 1.5 mm at anthesis, enlarging in fruit to 5-6 x 3 mm, the inner lanceolate-acuminate, 2.5- 3 mm long, maturing to ca 5 x 1 mm in fruit. Corolla yellow-green to pale yellow, 3-4 mm long, lobed for about half its length, the lobes apically obtuse to rounded- obtuse, the tube glabrous above, the lobes pubescent without on the distal 1/2-1/3 with 2-armed trichomes. Stamens 5; filaments fused to the corolla tube for ca 1 mm below, free above, glabrous throughout; anthers subcircular to ovoid, less than 0.5 mm long; pollen spheroidal, aggrecolpate (4 polar x 4 equatorial x 4 polar), nonspinulose. Ovary ovoid-conical, ca 1 mm long, glabrous on the lower half, densely pubescent with 2-armed or, by reduction, simple trichomes above; styles 2 and separate or connate for half their length, ca 2 mm long; stigmas globose. Fruits capsular, 2-locular, 4-valved, globose, 3-4 mm wide; seeds often 4, trigonous, either glabrous or verruculose, less often appressed-pilose, 1. 5-2 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Austin, Daniel F. & Staples, George William. 1985. Petrogenia as a synonym of Bonamia (Convolvulaceae), with comments on allied species. Brittonia. 37: 310-- 316.
