description: Succulent herbs 14-25 cm tall, glabrous, glaucous; rosettes 3-9 cm diam, with internodes up to 3 mm long; offsets 0-3 (4), borne on branchlets up to 3 cm long; rosette leaves narrowly obovate to spatulate, (2) 3.3-5.3 times as long as wide, (14) 25-60 mm long, 7-16 mm wide at the widest point 6-9 mm from the apex, (1) 2-4 (4.5) mm thick, apically rounded or barely retuse (up to 1 mm), the margins sometimes conspicuously pruinose; cauline leaves narrowly obovate, basally truncate or obtuse, not decurrent, apically rounded, 2.4-4.7 times as long as wide, 14-18 (30) mm long, 3-6 (13) mm wide, 2-3.8 mm thick; inflorescence corymbose or paniculate, 4.5-9.5 cm long, 20-55-flowered, the lower branches 2-5.5 cm long; pedicels 2-5 (8) mm long; sepals two-fifths to three-fifths as long as the petals, 1.7-2.8 times as long as wide, 4-5.5 mm long, 2-2.6 mm wide, apically obtuse or acute; petals 3-4 times as long as wide, 7-9 (10.5) mm long, 2-3 (4.5) mm wide, light yellow, fused basally for 2-3 (4.5) mm, apically obtuse, slightly apiculate, the margins crenulate or erose on the distal one-fourth or one-third; stamens basally epipetalous for 1-3 mm; anthers (0.5) 0.7-1.5 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, 0.3 mim thick, yellow, golden-yellow or reddish-brown; pollen (16) 20-28 microns diam; nectaries 0.4-0.8 mm long, 1.1-1.8 mm wide; stipe of gy- noecium 0.6-1.2 mm long; stigmas ca 0.2 mm diam; follicles 7-9 mm long, green- ish-brown proximally, reddish-brown distally, the stylar beaks 1.4-2.5 mm long; seeds 1-1.2 mm long (total length), the body 0.8-1 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide; n = 15.
bibliographicCitation: Denton, M. 1982. Revision of Sedum section Gormania (Crassulaceae). Brittonia. 34: 48-77.

description: Succulent herbs 7-29 cm tall; offsets 0-4, borne on branchlets up to 4 cm long; rosette leaves 1.8-3.8 times as long as wide, 10-29 mm long, 4-14 mm wide at the widest point ca 6 mm from the apex, 2-4 (4.8) mm thick; cauline leaves broadly ovate, basally rounded or truncate, not decurrent, slightly wider than long or up to 1.9 times as long as wide, (4) 6-17 mm long, 3-9 mm wide, 2-3 mm thick; inflorescence 1.8-7 cm long, 10-26-flowered, the lower branches 1.3-3.5 cm long; sepals three-tenths to two-fifths as long as the petals, 1.7-2.6 times as long as wide, 2-4 mm long, 1.2-1.8 mm wide, apically obtuse or acute; petals dark reddish-pink or pinkish-red, free or fused basally for 1.5 (rarely to 3) mm, apically acute; stamens basally epipetalous for 1.5-3.5 mm; anthers 0.6-1 mm long, light red or light to dark reddish-purple; pollen 22-25 microns diam; stipe of gynoecium 0.5-1 mm long; stigmas ca 0.15 mm diam; follicles ca 8 mm long, the stylar beak 1.5-2.5 mm long; seeds 1.1-1.8 mm long (total length), the body 0.7-1.6 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm wide; n = 30.

description: Succulent herbs 9-24 cm tall; offsets 0-4, borne on branchlets up to 4 cm long; rosette leaves 1.5-4.6 times as long as wide, (11) 15-32 mm long, 5-20 mm wide at the widest point 4-8 mm from the apex, 1-4 mm thick; cauline leaves broadly ovate, basally amplexicaul and auriculate, not decurrent, wider than long or up to 1.3 (1.8) times as long as wide, 5-14 mm long, 5-12 mm wide; inflorescence 2.5-8.5 cm long, 15-33 (60)-flowered, the lower branches 2-5 cm long; sepals three-tenths to three-fifths as long as the petals, 1.8-3 times as long as wide, 2.5-5 (6) mm long, 1.1-2.5 mm wide, apically acute; petals white to light pink, fused basally for (1) 2-4 mm, apically acute to attenuate with a slight apiculate tip; stamens basally epipetalous for 3-4 (5) mm; anthers 0.8-1.2 (1.5) mm long, reddish-brown, reddish-purple, reddish-black or purplish-black; pollen 20-30 microns diam; stipe of gynoecium 0.8-1 mm long; stigmas 0.18 mm diam; follicles 6.5-12 mm long, the stylar beak 1.8-3 mm long; seeds 1-1.4 mm long (total length), the body 0.8-1.1 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide; n = 15.

description: Succulent herbs 23-33 cm tall, beset throughout with glands up to 0.4 mm long; rosettes 2-7 cm diam, the internodes up to 3 mm long; offsets 0-4 (9), borne on branchlets 1-4 cm long; rosette leaves obovate or spatulate, 1.6-4.4 times as long as wide, 17-40 mm long, 8-17 mm wide at the widest point 4-6 mm from the apex, 3-4.2 mm thick, apically rounded; cauline leaves obovate, basally obtuse or truncate, not decurrent, apically rounded, 1.7-3.3 times as long as wide, 9-16 (21) mm long, 4-8 (14) mm wide, 2-4 mm thick; inflorescence 2-3-parted, 6-9 cm long, 19-27-flowered, with long lateral branches, the lower ones 3-8.5 cm long; pedicels 1-4 (5) mm long; sepals two-fifths to one-half as long as the petals, 1.7-3.1 times as long as wide, 5-7 (8.5) mm long, 2-3 (3.8) mm wide, apically acute to attenuate; petals (2.7) 3.3-5.5 times as long as wide, 11-13 (15.8) mm long, 2.5-4.5 (5) mm wide, light to lemon-yellow, fused basally for (1.5) 2.4-3 mm, apically attenuate and sometimes slightly apiculate, the margins glandular; stamens basally epipetalous for 1-3 mm; anthers 1-1.4 mm long, 0.8 mm wide, 0.3 mm thick, tawny, yellow or reddish-brown; pollen 29-34 microns diam; nec- taries 0.4-0.6 mm long, 1.1-1.9 mm wide; stipe of gynoecium 0.5-1.4 mm long; stigmas ca 0.5 mm diam; follicles 9-11 mm long, greenish to purplish distally, the stylar beak 2-3 mm long; seeds 1-1.3 (1.9) mm long (total length), the body 0.9-1 (1.6) mm long, 0.3-0.5 (0.7) mm wide; n = 15.

description: Succulent herbs 7-38.5 cm tall; offsets 0-12, borne on branchlets up to 8 cm long; rosette leaves 1.4-4.6 times as long as wide, 10-41 (50) mm long, 4-19 (24) mm wide at the widest point 3-8 (12) mm from the apex, 1-4.5 (5) mm thick; cauline leaves narrowly obovate, basally obtuse or truncate and slightly decur- rent, 1.9-4.6 (6) times as long as wide, 7-20 mm long, 3-8.5 (14) mm wide, 2.5-4.5 mm thick; inflorescence 2-11 cm long, 14-67 (82)-flowered, the lower branches 1.5-7 cm long; sepals three-tenths to three-fifths as long as the petals, 1.4-3.3 times as long as wide, 2.2-5.5 mm long, (1.2) 1.5-2.5 mm wide, apically acute; petals white with a pinkish tinge, light pink or rarely light yellow, free or fused basally for 1-2 (3.5) mm, apically acute to attenuate; stamens basally epipetalous for 1.5-3.5 mm; anthers (0.6) 0.8-1.5 (3.5) mm long, reddish-brown, reddish-black or purplish-black; pollen 20-32 microns diam; stipe of gynoecium 0.6-1.3 mm long; stigmas ca 0.15 mm diam; follicles 7-10 mm long, the stylar beak 1.3-2.8 mm long; seeds 1.1-2 mm long (total length), the body 0.8-1.6 mm long, 0.3-0.7 mm wide; n = 15.

description: Perennial herb with a cluster of fleshy, usually white roots, 2-9 cm. long; stems tufted, short-spreading, 0.2-1.0 cm. long, 1-2 mm. thick, bearing several or many compact rosettes of closely crowded, spirally arranged leaves which are rhombic spatulate, acute to obtuse or even rounded, dark green, prominently papillose, 2-4 mm. long, 0.5-2.0 mm. wide, and 0.5-1 mm. thick; rosettes 4-8 mm. in diam., greatly elongating at flowering time, producing floral shoots 3-20 cm. high, simple or sometimes much branched, more or less spreading, with the stems finely papillose; leaves of the flowering stems alternate, spreading or somewhat recurved, sessile, linear, elliptic-linear, or linear-oblong, acute or acutish at apex, flat ventrally and almost so dorsally, dark green (if yellow-green, then darker than in S. cockerellii), minutely papillose, 0.2-1.8 cm. long, 0.5-5 mm. wide; infloreseence a two or three- (or more) parted eyme of 4-27 sessile, usually 5-merous flowers, 0.7-1.4 (-2) cm. in diam.; central flower of eyme usually pedicellate; floral bracts linear or oblong-linear, papillose; sepals erect, linear-oblong, abruptly acute or subacute, unequal, papillose, dark green, 4-9 mm. long; petals erect at base for 2-3 mm., rotately spreading for rest of length, lanceolate, acute, or mucronate, 6-8 mm. long, 1 mm. wide, white suffused with plnk towards base; stamens 5-6 mm. long with alithers red or purple and filaments pale pink; nectarscales transversely rectangular, 0.5 mm. long, pale pink or white; carpels 5-6 mm. long, erect, white or pink, with styles erect or somewhat spreading; seeds pyriform, 0.6-0.8 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Merrill, Elmer D. 1943. An attempt to complete the record. Brittonia. 5: 25-32.

description: Perennial herb with long, stout roots, to 24 cm. long; stems 1-3 mm.- in diam., succulent, spreading, to 1.5 dm. or more long, forming diffuse mats, finally erect, 1-3 cm. high, and bearing loose rosettes of yellow-green leaves, spirally arranged, or minutely papillose, 1-10 mm. long, 1-3 mm. wide, and 1.5 mm. thick; the loose rosettes 6-16 mm. in diam., greatly elongating at flowering time; flowering stems from 2-23 cm. high, usually simple, rarely branched, with the stems glabrous and the leaves alternate, ascending, sessile, fleshy, cuneate-obovate, oblong-obovate or rarely oblanceolate, blunt or broadly rounded, convex dorsally, concave ventrally, glabrous or minutely papillose, yellow-green, rarely slightly glaucous, often suffused with pink towards apex (particularly in exposed places), decreasing in size upwards, 3-12 mm. long, 1-6 mm. wide, and 2 mm. thick; flower-buds pink; flowers 10-15 mm. in diam., 1-5 in a two- or rarely three-parted eyme; floral bracts similar to the upper leaves; sepals linear-lanceolate, blunt, erect, 4-5 mm. long; petals lanceolate, carinate, white with a light pinkish or greenish median stripe towards apex; sometimes completely suffused with pink at apex, erect for about 3 mm., spreading for rest of length, 7-11 mm. long, 3 mm. wide; stamens 6-7 mm. long with filaments white and anthers pink (when young) changing to fuscous; nectar scales subquadrate, emarginate, about 0.5 mm. long, whitish; pistils erect, distinct to the base, or almost so, white or pale pink, 6-7 mm. long; seeds oblonglanceolate, 0.9 mm. long.

description: Perennial herb with a cluster of somewhat fleshy, usually white roots, 5-12 cm. long; stems tufted, short-spreading, 0.5-1 cm. long, 1-3 mm. thick, bearing several or many compact rosettes of closely crowded, spirally arranged leaves which are obovate to spatulate, acute to truncate at apex, dark green, minutely papillose, 1-6 mm. long, 1-4 mm. wide, and 1 mm. thick; rosettes 5-12 mm. in diam., greatly elongating at flowering time, producing flowering shoots 2-20 cm. high, simple or rarely branched, with the stems glabrous or papillose upwards; leaves of the flowering stems alternate, ascending or spreading, oblong-oblanceolate, narrowly spatulate or oblong-lanceolate, sessile, usually obtuse or rounded, rarely acute, at apex, flat ventrally, slightly concave dorsally, light green, glabrous or minutely papillose, 0.5-1.8 cm. long, 2-6 mm. wide; infloreseence a three-parted cyme of 5-11 sessile, 5-merous (rarely 4-merous) flowers, 0.8-1.2 cm. in diam.; floral bracts oblong-oblanceolate, papillose; sepals erect, linear-oblong, obtuse or rarely acute, somewhat unequal, sometimes papillose, green, 4-5 mm. long; petals erect at base for 2-3 mm., rotately spreading for rest of length, lanceolate, acute, 6-9 mm. long, 3 mm. wide; white or faintly suffused with pink; stamens 5-7 mm. long, with anthers pink, purple, or red, and filaments white; nectar-scales transversely oblong, 0.5 mm. long, yellowish white; carpels 5-8 mm. long, erect, white, or pink, with styles erect or slightly spreading; seeds oblong-elliptical or almost pyriform, orange-brown, 0.8 mm. long.

description: Herba monoica, per cirrhos scandens. Foliis palmatim pentangularibus vel leniter 5-7-lobatis, cordatis sinibus apertis atque plus minusve acutis; utrinqus pilis scabridis fragilibus praeditis; inflorescentiis staminatis 0.5-2 (7.5) cm longis, plerumque 8-12-floris, corollis tetrameris vel pentameris, staminibus 4, filamentis columnam formantibus, antheris subsessilibus; inflorescentiis pistillatis subcapitatis, 3-6-floris, pedunculis 0.5-2.5 cm longis, corollis pistillatis tetrameris, stigmatibus 4-lobatis; fructibus alatis, 2.5-3 cm longis (alis inclusis), carpara anguste ellipsoideos, alis laciniatis 2 latis atque subsidiariis 2 vel pluribus laciniis vel dentibus glochidiatis; seminibus ignotis.
bibliographicCitation: Lott, Emily J. & Fryxell, Paul A. 1983. A new species of Sicyos (Cucurbitaceae) from Chiapas, Mexico. Brittonia. 35: 34-36.

description: Scandent monoecious herb, climbing by means of tendrils, the stem slender, glabrous. Leaves simple, thin and concolorous, palmately pentangular to shallowly 5-7-lobed, 6-12 cm long, equally wide, pedately 7-9-nerved, basally cordate, the sinus open and more or less acute, the apex acute, the margin remotely and minutely denticulate, the whole adaxial surface scabrid with scattered conical, fragile hairs ca 0.5 mm long, at base ornate with radiating striations, these hairs more or less in the center of each areola, the veins densely scabrid with shorter hairs, the abaxial leaf surface minutely scabrous with scattered hairs, appearing punctate because the bases of hairs of the upper surface are visible beneath: petioles 2-7 (15) cm long, glabrous except for a narrow line of dense minute hairs adaxially; tendrils long-stalked, bifid. Staminate inflorescence sharing a common axil with the pistillate, racemose, 0.5-2 (7.5) cm long, mostly 8-12-flowered, the pedicels 1.5-3 (5) mm long. Staminateflowers whitish, broadly campanulate, ca 2 mm long, 3-4 mm wide; calyx lobes 4 or 5, subulate, ca 0.2 mm long; corolla 4-5-merous, the lobes ovate-triangular, 1.5-1.8 mm long, spreading, papillose within; stamens 4, united, the filaments forming a central column, the anthers 4, free, reniform, subsessile. Pistillate inflorescence axillary, subcapitate, 3-6-flowered, at the apex of a stout peduncle 0.5-2.5 cm long. Pistillateflowers short-pedicellate, the perianth greenish-white, smaller than that of the staminate flowers, ca 1 mm long, cupuliform, 4-merous; calyx lobes subulate, ca 0.2 mm long; corolla lobes ovate, 0.5 mm long; stigma 4-lobed, the ovary winged and armed. Fruit (wings included) 2.5-3 cm long, the body narrowly ellipsoid, 10-14 mm long, irregularly winged with 2 broad longitudinal wings 3-13 mm wide (teeth included) and 2 or more narrower wings, the wings prominently laciniate, the teeth with glochidiate tips, the smaller wings sometimes reduced to a row of spines with glochidiate tips, each spine usually with 4 retrorse barbs. Seeds unknown.

description: Arbuscula ramis terminalibus valde nodoso-articulatis nigrescentibus, juvenilibus pubescenti-hirtulis mox glabris. Folia opposita simplicia rigide coriacea glaberrima. Petiolus 2-3 mm longus basi incrassatus. Lamina obovato-elliptica basi cuneata apice obtusa vel rotundata margine serrato-crenata calloso-revoluta, 10-22 mm longa 6-14 mm lata; supra viridis nitida, in sicco castanea, nervis medio lateralibus prominulis reticulo obsoleto; subtus pallidior costa elevata nervis secundariis circa 8 utroque latere conspicuis ascendentibus prope marginem anastomosatis reliquis nervulis subobsoletis. Gemmae viscoso-resinosae sursum paulo pubescentes. Stipulae ovatae obtusae coriaceae 3-4 mm longae circa 3 mm latae utrinque glabrae. Pseudoracemi oppositi subterminales 2.5-3.5 cm longi axi mediocri rigidi pubescenti hirsutuli, bracteolis ovato-triangularibus minutis. Flores pedicellati praecipue 3-4 in fasciculis interdum solitarii aggregati. Pedicelli graciles rigidi parce puberuli 2-3 mnr longi. Sepala ovato-lanceolata glabra 1.8 mm longa basi concrescentia. Petala orbicularia 2 mm diamitentia glabra. Filamenta staminorum glabra rubescentia 3.5-4 mm longa. Discus hypogynus cupularis striatus crassus 0.5 mm altus. Ovarium oblongum glaberrimum album 1.2 mm longum styli glabri 2 mm longi. Capsulae oblongae acutae 4-4.5 mm longae glabrae rubescenti bruneae.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1956. Studies in South American plants--IV. Brittonia. 8: 195-200.

description: Arbuscula ramis griseis terminalibus crispo-tomentosis denique glabris. Folia opposita imparipinnata coriacea 3-6 cm longa breviter petiolata praeci- pue 2-3-jugis. Petiolus 2-4 mm longus robustus tomentosus. Foliola oblongo-elliptica vel obovato-elliptica terminalia oblongo-obovata, basi obtuse cuneata apice rotundata, margine breviter crenulato-serrata revolutaque lateralia 8-20 mm longa 6-13 mm lata, terminalia latiora; supra griseo-viridia crispo-pubescentia denique glabrata, nervo medio notato tomentoso ceteris nervis reticuloque tenuiter conspicuo, subtus ferruginei-ochracea dense crispo-tomentosa costa elevata, nervis secundariis 67 utroque latere prominulis sed cum tomento plus minusve velatis. Internodia rachis obovato-rhomboidea oblonga 5-9 mm longa 2.5-5 mm lata. Gemmae densissime crasseque tomentosae. Petala suborbicularia alba margine ciliolata 1.5 mm diamitentia. Filamenta staminorum rubra glabra 2-2.3 mm longa. Antherae 4 mm longae mucronatae. Discus hypogynus crassiusculus 0.4 mm altus. Ovarium ovato-acutatum 2 mm longum dense crispo-tomemtosum. Styli 1.4 mm longi deorsum pubescentes sursum glabri.

description: Stem subterranean, dichotomously branching in older plants, up to 30 cm long, 4-8 cm in diam. Cataphylls membranaceous, persistent, base triangular, apex aristate, 4.5 cm long, 1.2 cm at base, yellowish tomentose. Ptyxis inflexed. Leaves 1-5 (-8), 15-45 x 8-20 cm, ascending to spreading, dark brown when emerging; petiole 9-14 cm long, blackish in young leaves, unarmed, terete; rachis subterete, up to 31 cm long, uarmed. Leaflets 20-35 pairs, sessile, papyraceous, elliptic to oblanceolate, alterante to subopposite, apex acute symmetric, base cuneate, margins serrulate along distal third, subrevolute; articulations light brown in young leaflets, 0.3 -0.4 cm wide, median leaflets 5-9 x 1.5 - 4.5 cm. Pollen strobili usually 1-3, erect, conical, 4-6 cm long, 1.5 - 2.2 cm in diam, gray tomentose, apex acute; peduncle yellowish tomentose, 2.8 cm long, 0.9 -1.1 cm in diam; pollen sporangiophores cuneiform, distal face hexagonal-truncate, 0.3 cm long, fertile abaxial surface with 304 bisporangiate synangia per lobe. Ovulate strobili usually 1-2, erect, cylindrical to ovoid, up to 9 cm long, 4.5 cm in diam, brown to reddish tomentulose when young, dark - green and glabrous when mature, apex acute; peduncle brown tomentose, 3 cm long, 1.1 cm in diam; megasporangiophores peltate. distal face hexagonal - truncate when immature, scutiform when mature 0.8 -1.2 cm high, 1.3 -1.9 cm wide. Seed ovoid, 1.6 cm long, 1.3 cm in diam, sarcotesta pink when young and orange at maturity. Chromosome number. - 2n=16 (Marchant, 1968; Moretti et al., 1991; Stevenson et al., 1 995-1 996a).

description: Stem to 3 m or more tall and 40 cm diam, erect or reclining; leaves numerous, crowded, 70-140 cm long, glabrous or temporarily pubescent, light green or transiently glaucous, flat (rarely little keeled), the petioles semiterete; leaflets 80-130 pairs, linear-lanceolate, 6-12 x (0.5) 0.6-0.9 cm, entire, revolute, distant or im- bricated in particular toward the apex, inserted prevalently at right angle to the rachis, spinulose in plantlets or young plants; male strobilus 20-40 x 6-10 cm, obtuse, the microsporophylls with pointed or ovate tips curved upward; female strobilus ovate, 20-35 x 12-20 cm; seeds 4.5-7 cc in volume, the outer fleshy layer of their coat white or yellowish.

description: Foliola 7-12 mm lata, laete viridia, lanceolata vel lineari-lanceolata, falcata vel subfalcata, recto angulo supra semiteretem rachin inserta.
bibliographicCitation: De Luca, Paolo, et al. 1984. Dion tomasellii (Zamiaceae), a new species with two varieties from western Mexico. Brittonia. 36: 223-227.

description: Rhizome thick, nodose; culms 0.5-3.5 m. tall, in large colonies, erect or elongate and vine-like, rigid, essentially glabrous, triquetrous, robust, the angles roughened; leaves 60-80 cm. long, 5-10 mm. wide, rigid, very scabrous on the margins and on the nerves beneath, subcoriaceous, acuminate, flat, overtopping the culm; sheaths very scabrous on the angles, narrowly winged, minutely pilose; ligule depressed-ovate, glabrous, the margin cartilaginous; inflorescence paniculate, dense, pyramidal, rigid, minutely pilose throughout, 2-12 cm. high, the branches short, occasionally with 1 or 2 smaller panicles in the upper axils; bracts at base of the terminal panicle usually 3, large, foliaceous, overtopping the culm; bractlets setaceous, scabrous; pistillate scales ovate-orbicular, abruptly mucronate, the margins ciliate; spikelets short-stalked or sessile; hypogynium 3-lobed, the lobes broad, rounded, reflexed, light-yellow; achene 2-3 mm. long, globose, white, smooth, minutely apiculate.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: Phyllopodic, caespitose; leaves basal, stiff, erect, 2-4 mm wide, apices long attenuate; culms stiff, erect, to 3.5 dm high, longer than the leaves, slightly roughened above; spikes three to six, the terminal staminate, gynaecandrous or carpellate, the lateral all carpellate, spikes both long and short cylindric, short pedunculate, erect, approximate, subtended by a short sheathing, leaf-like bract, shorter to, longer than the inflorescence; perigynia obovate, 2.5 mm long, brown, abruptly short beaked, beaks entire to shallowly bidentate, beaks and upper perigynium margins papillose and spinulose; carpellate scales ovate, to broadly lanceolate, as wide and as long as the perigynia, margins broadly hyaline, apices obtuse, truncate to cuspidate, or acute, midribs conspicuous; multispicate and monoecious (Fig. 8).
bibliographicCitation: Ornduff, Robert. 1969. Limnanthes vinoulans, a new California endemic. Brittonia. 21: 11-14.

description: Rhizome horizontal, elongate, rather stout; culms 20-60 cm. tall or sometimes taller, triangular, slender, glabrous, rigid, sometimes scabrous above; leaves 2 dm. long or less, 2 mm. wide, few, glabrous, often scabrous towards the apex; sheaths glabrous, the lower ones purplish; ligule minute, slightly hairy or glabrous; lower bract of the inflorescence foliaceous, erect, often appearing like a continuation of the culm; inflorescence terminal or often with a remote axillary cluster on a long slender, ancipital peduncle, the clusters small; bract-lets glabrous or the margins minutely ciliolate, purplish, linear-lanceolate, attenuate; spikelets few-flowered, 5 mm. long; staminate scales lanceolate, purplish; pistillate scales long-awned, glabrous, purplish-tinged; hypogynium bearing three entire or 2-lobed tubercles; achene 2-3 mm. long, papillose-verrucose, globular or globose-ovoid, apiculate, white.
bibliographicCitation: Core, Earl L. 1936. The American species of Scleria. Brittonia. 2: 1-105. pl. 1-3.

description: About 15 species, four of which occur in the Americas as introductions. Robust annual or perennial herbs or subshrubs, often tomentose or hispid. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades palmately lobed, crenate or dentate, lacking foliar nectaries. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils; involucel of 4-16 bracts, usually caducous, sometimes persistent; calyx spathaceous, splitting asymmetrically at anthesis and falling with the corolla; corolla large, yellow (sometimes red or lavender) with a dark red center; androecium included, apically 5-toothed; style single with 5 sessile capitate stigmas. Capsules elongate, pubescent or hispid, 5-carpelled, dehiscent, with numerous seeds; seeds reniform, glabrous, pubescent, or squamose. 2n = 58, 66, 72, 130, and 132.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Annual or perennial herbs, prostrate to erect; long taproot fleshy to woody; stems branched, sometimes cespitose or appearing acaulescent, usually viscid-pubescent; leaves opposite, usually unequal, blades entire to lobed; inflorescences capitate, subtended by 5-10 bracts; receptacle conical, without pedicel-like projections; periph- eral flowers of inflorescence usually opening first; perianth 2-parted, upper part deciduous or somewhat persistent, lower part forming the anthocarp; abscission scar between perianth parts a narrow ring surrounding a short tubular projection, the projection 0.2-0.8 mm long on mature anthocarps; flowers perfect, pentamerous, rarely with 7-9 stamens; stigmas linear; perianth lobes flaring, usually deeply emarginate; anthocarps winged to merely ridged, often beaked; wings 2-5, if present, opaque, not surrounding anthocarp, veins not prominent; body of anthocarp indurate to coriaceous, sometimes scarious, body cavity often minutely puberulent; achenes free, narrow obovate, oblong-ovate, elliptic-oblong to oblong.
bibliographicCitation: Galloway, Leo A. 1976. Systematics of the North American desert species of Abronia and Tripterocalyx (Nyctaginaceae). Brittonia. 27: 328-347.

description: About 160 species, mostly neotropical. Subshrubs or shrubs to small trees, glabrescent or pubescent, sometimes glandular-pu- bescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades elliptic, ovate, or cordiform, sometimes lobed or parted, usually crenate or serrate (rarely subentire). Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or aggregated into racemes or panicles, less commonly in umbels; involucel absent; calyx lobes lanceolate, ovate, or cordate; corolla often yellow or orange, less often white, lavender, rose, red, or purplish; an droecium usually included (rarely exserted), the column filamentiferous at apex; styles 5 to many; stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic (but sometimes pseudocapsular); meri- carps 5 to many, twice the length of the column, usually 1-celled, usually apically acute or acuminate to spinescent (rarely rounded), usually with 3-6 seeds each, not inflated, more or less elliptic in cross section, dorsally dehiscent; seeds glabrous or slightly pubescent. Base chromosome numbers x = 7, 8, 14, 28, 36, 42, 72 (see discussion below)
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Nineteen species. Acaulescent perennial herbs from a woody caudex. Leaves petiolate, the blades suborbicular or ovate, basally cuneate, truncate, or cordate, the margin usually crenate, sometimes entire, usually strigose or pubescent, sometimes sub- glabrous; stipules lanceolate, more or less glabrous. Flowers axillary, long- or short- pedicellate; involucel of 2 or 3 lanceolate or filiform bracts; calyx campanulate, 5-lobed; corolla usually exceeding the calyx, white, lavender, purplish (sometimes with a dark center), or sometimes yellow; androecium included, the stamens numerous; styles 8-20, with capitate stigmas. Fruits schizocarpic, included in calyx; mericarps 8-20, dehiscent or indehiscent, apic- ulate or muticous, hirsute or glabrous, smooth or rugulose; seeds solitary. 2n = 10 (one species reported).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Hypanthium campanulate, the sepals minute and triangular; petals ovate or lanceolate, acute or acuminate, and often setose at the apex; stamens isomorphic, or differentiated in size only or slightly dimorphic; connective prolonged but little or not at all and swollen or minutely 2-lobed anteriorly at base; ovary 2-celled; style slender, stigma subcapitate,. Herbs with 4-angled or 4-winged stems, broad thin leaves, and minute 4-merous flowers in terminal, freely branched panicles. The species number about 30 and are widely distributed through tropical America.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Shrubs to small trees; bark smooth, grayish light brown; wood cream-white. Stipules interpetiolar, free at base (not sheathing), connected to the petioles, caducous. Leaves long-petiolate, blades elliptic to ovate, acute or rounded at base, acute at apex; domatia absent. Inflorescences terminal, solitary, cymose, multiflorous. Flowers protandrous, short-pedicellate; hypanthium narrowly obconical. Calyx membranous, 4-5-lobed, persistent. Corolla hypocrateriform, pinkish white, without annular thickening; tube narrowly tubular, puberulent to short-pubescent outside, pilose toward the orifice inside (the rest glabrous); lobes 4-5, rounded; aestivation imbricate. Stamens alternate to the petals, only the tips exserted (mostly included); anthers narrowly elliptic, dorsifixed near the base, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; filaments attached near the mouth, extremely short, glabrous throughout. Style exserted; style branches long, narrowly oblong, opening after complete maturity of the anthers, reflexed at maturity. Ovary 2-celled, with 15-30 seeds per locule inserted on the central placenta; placenta extending throughout the length of the ovary. Capsules narrowly cylindrical, multicostate, dehiscing septicidally, with a persistent calyx. Seeds peltate, vertical, linear-lanceolate, with central hilum, bipolar-winged.
bibliographicCitation: Delprete, Piero G. 1999. The Cuban endemic genera Ariadne, Mazaea, Acunaeanthus, Phyllomelia (Rondeletieae), and Eosanthe (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 51: 217-230.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Hypanthium campanulate to almost tubular, the sepals short or obsolete, the external teeth ranging from mere tubercles to linear and longer than the sepals; petals showy; stamens 10, equal or so-mewhat dimorphic; anthers subulate, usually arcuate; connective prolonged at base into a short, stout, conic spur and bearing on the back a con- spicuous, elongate, dorsal spur, directed forward or parallel to the anther and often ending in 2 or more slender tails; ovary 3-5-celled; seeds linear or filiform, caudate at one or both ends. Climbing woody vines, with oblong to ovate or rotund leaves and flowers in panicled umbels or capitate clusters. Malpighian hairs are usually present. A genus of about 15 species, most abundant in the Amazonian for- ests, but extending north to Mexico and south as far as Bolivia. Its botanical history is somewhat complicated and begins with Aublet''s description of Melastoma scandens from Cayenne in 1775. His plate is excellent and corresponds well with material of A. scandens now extant. Swartz used the same name for a Jamaican species in 1788, which he re-named Melastora adscendens in 1800, either because he had just discovered Aublet's earlier use of the name or because he recognized his species as distinct. In 1828 De Candolle erected the genus Adelobotrys for Aublet's plant. Not knowing Swartz' plant, he left it under Swartz' name among his species dubiae. In the meantimne, a third species had reached Europe, of which a specimen of Patris was made the type of Davya guianensis DC. and a collection of Dombey from Peru was named Davya peruviana DC. This third species was named Sarnientariq decora by Naudin in 1852, based on a sterile specimen from Cayenne, and a fourth species was also de- scribed by him as Davya ctliata. Finally, in 1871, Triana brought together Sarmentaria. Naud., a portion of Davya DC., and Adelo- botrys DC. under the latter name, which has priority. He also added four new species, bringing the total to eight. Several additional species have since been added.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Leaves alternate, simple, notophylls to mesophylls, chartaceous or coriaceous, caducous, oblong, symmetrical, base and apex acute margin denticulate, teeth simple, tooth spacing irregular; cicatricose-crateriform glands present, never paired; marginal glands present; venation pinnatinerved, agrophic veins absent; primary vein moderate to stout, straight; secondary venation brochidodromous, with 7-12 pairs of secondary veins with an acute angle of divergence; tertiary veins opposite percurrent; quaternary veins polygonal reticulate; orders of venation 5, areoles imperfectl veinlets simple to branched more than twice; ultimate marginal venation looped. Midvien and higher order veins with the bundle sheath sclerified, terminal veinlets naked or with sclerenchymatous sheath cells; mesophyll dorsiventral, with dispersed fibers with numerous druses in the mesophyll and also in the phloem parenchyma; without tannins in the spongy parenchyma; epidermis simple, epidermal cells isodiametric in surface view, abaxial anticlinal cell walls undulate; cuticle smooth; stomata in the abaxial surface, paracytic, guard cells without striations; sparsely pubescent, trichomes simple, papillate.
bibliographicCitation: Cervantes, A., et al. 2009. Foliar architecture and anatomy of Bernardia and other genera of Acalyphoideae (Euphorbiaceae). Brittonia. 61 (4): 375-391.

description: Plants small- to medium-sized, usually epiphytic but occasionally subterrestrial or epipetric; rhizome cylindrical, dorsiventral, solenostelic, short or long and repent; rhizome scales eciliate, elongate-triangular or narrowly lanceolate, light to dark brown, concolorous, the apex provided with glands or not; roots dark brown or blackish, usually bearing few branches or epidermal hairs; fronds erect, arching, or pendulous; xylem arcs single or double in each leaf trace at origin, but in the stipe single and U-shaped; foliar trichomes consisting of 1-8-celled, rather weak hairs, usually glandular, the gland an elongate or obpyriform, oil-containing terminal cell, present on all or most parts of the frond or occasionally absent; stipes non-articulate, blackish, terete except for the usually present lateral alae; blades coriaceous to submembranous, simple, lobed, or 1-3 times pinnatifid, mostly linear, lanceolate, or elliptic in outline; veins free; sori dorsal or at times terminal, exindusiate, super- ficial or slightly immersed, round or suboval, including numerous, uniseriate, glandular paraphyses, borne on elliptic receptacles overlying the apices of the clavate fertile veins; sporangia with stalks uniseriate for most of their length, the annulus containing 9-15 thickened bow cells; spores 64 in each sporangium, green, globose, trilete, minutely sculptured, 25-50 pum in diameter; gametophytes elongate-cordate or ribbon-like.
bibliographicCitation: Bishop, L. Earl. 1974. Earl. Revision of the genus Adenophorus (Grammitidaceae). Brittonia. 26: 217-240.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Woody plants; branches and branchlets tetragonal or subterete; leaves simple, usually decussate-opposite (rarely ternate), deciduous, exstipulate; inflorescence cymose, the cymes often so modified as to more closely resemble panicles, false umbels, glomerules, heads, or thyrsi, or even reduced to a few or only a single flower, axillary or terminal; flowers actinomorphic, hermaph- roditic but usually conspicuously diclinous; calyx gamosepalous, more or less campanulate, cyathiform, or tubular, its margin truncate or 4-5-toothed or -lobed, accrescent, becoming greatly incrassate and indurated in fruit; corolla hypogynous, gamopetalous, infundibular or hypocrateriform, its tube cylindric, its limb equally 4- or 5-parted, its lobes imbricate; stamens 4 or 5, equal, isomorphic, perfect, inserted below the mouth of the corolla-tube and above its base, included or ex- serted, alternate with the corolla-lobes; pistil one; style terminal or subterminal, capillary, single; stigma bifid, its branches elongate and awl-shaped; ovary superior, perfectly or imperfectly 4-celled, each cell 1-ovuled; ovules lateral or high-lateral, hemi-anatropous; fruit dru- paceous, typically 4-seeded [1-3-seeded by abortion]; seeds without endosperm.
bibliographicCitation: Moldenke, Richard G. 1934. A monograph of the genus Aegiphila. Brittonia. 1 (5-6): 245-471.

description: Small shrub to large tree 30 m tall and 15 dm in diameter. Bark light gray, brown or dark brown, smooth or scaly. Twig gray, brown or reddish-brown with pale yellow lenticels, glabrous or tomentose; leaf sear obdeltoid with 3-10 vascular bundles arranged in a V- or U-shaped pattern. Leaves deciduous, with 5-11 leaflets; petiole terete or flattened adaxially, glabrous or tomentose; petiolule 0-3 cm long, glabrous or tomentose. Leaflets thin or subcoriaceous, variable in size and shape, the central leaflet usually the largest; margins repand, or rarely entire, or crenate-serrate, serrate, or irregulaly to tomentose or woolly; mesophyll lacking trichoselereids but often with druses or prismatic crystals. Infloreseence a panicle of variable length and shape, the principle elongated axis monopodially and irregularly branched and bearing lateral cincinni, the eincinni subtended by small bracts. Flowers with pedicels 2-15 mm long, glabrous or tomentose, sometimes with stipitate glands. Calyx white, or yellow to red, glabrous, tomentose, or glandular-villous, campanulate or tubular, often oblique and gibbous at the base on the upper side; sepals 5, fused to half or more of their length, the upper and two lower sepals usually the same height and taller than the two lateral ones (occasionally, all five equal, or the upper and two laterals equal and taller than the two lower) ; when irreoularly 1- or 2-lipped, the five lobes very small and at the top of the flower, or the upper lip composed of the top three lobes and the lower lip of the lower two lobes. Corolla white, or yellow to red; petals 4 or occasionally 5, similar or different in size and shape, the fifth usually abortive or of variable size when present; claws of the petals of various lengths, usually villous, sometimes lobed, or crested, at the top, and with margins and/or base of blade involute; blade of petals glabrous, papillose or pubescent with simple hairs or with multicellular, stipitate glands, or both. Stamens 6-8 (rarely 5), exserted or included; filaments white, glabrous or villous on the lower half; anthers yellow, orange or reddish, glabrous or slightly pubeseent, with or without glandular tips at the apex and base of the locules. Disk annlular or usually eccentric and trilobed around the base of the filaments. Fertile pistil glabrous or tomentose, with or without stipitate glands. Fruit smooth, slightly scaly, or spiny, variable in size and shape; pericarp thick or thin, pale to dark brown; seeds usually 1-3 (occasionally 4-6), dark chestnut-brown or light orange-brown, with a pale hilum of variable size.
bibliographicCitation: Hardin, James W. 1957. A revision of the Americana Hippocastanaceae--II. Brittonia. 9: 173-195.

description: Frutices arbusculae arboresve dioicae. Stipulae interpetiolares membranaceae caducae. Folia petiolata, decussata, laminis papyraceis vel coriaceis, venatione brochidodroma. Inflorescentiae terminales, heterogeneae. Inflorescentiae masculinae 3-16-florae, praecipue thyrsiformes. Inflorescentiae femineae 1(-3)-florae. Calyx plerumque truncatus, tubo brevissimo. Discus saepe protrudens (visibilis post anthesin). Corolla vulgo hypocrateriformis, raro infundibuliformis, vulgo glabra extus et intus, extus raro strigosa vel sparse pilosa, lobis sinistrorsum contortis in alabastro. Lobi corollae feminei et corollae masculini vulgo heteromeri. Corolla in flore masculino 4-6-loba, raro 7-loba; corolla in flore femineo 5-7-loba, raro 4-loba. Stamina vulgo tot quot lobi corollae, medio vel supra medium tubi corollae inserta. Pollinis grana vulgo 3-7-porata, raro brevissime colporata. Stylus in flore masculino 2-4-lobus; stylus in flore femineo 4-lobus.
bibliographicCitation: Persson, C. 2003. Agouticarpa, a new neotropical genus of Tribe Gardenieae (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 55: 176-201.

description: Dioecious shrubs, treelets or trees. Stipules interpetiolar, caducous, free or partly fused intrapetiolarly, held flat back to back in bud, membranaceous, often reddish, elliptic to obovate, rarely ovate or oblong, colleters present at base inside. Leaves decussate, petiolate, blades papyraceous to coriaceous, venation brochidodromous, margin entire. Inflorescences terminal, heterogeneous, sessile or pedunculate, male inflorescences 3-16-flowered, thyrse-like or a 3-flowered dichasium, female inflorescences usually 1-flowered, rarely a 3-flowered dichasium. Calyces cup-shaped, usually truncate, margin sometimes wavy, rarely with tiny awns, tube with colleters inside, very short, surrounding a disk which is protruding and usually clearly visible after corolla is shed (particularly in male flowers). Corollas usually salverform, rarely infundibuliform, contorted to the left, probably heteromerous, fleshy or membranaceous, usually glabrous outside and inside, female corollas usually with one more lobe than male corollas. Male corollas 4-6-, rarely 7-lobed; stamens usually as many as corolla lobes, inserted in the middle to upper part of tube, sessile, rarely with a short filament, anthers linear, rarely narrowly oblong, included or rarely tips barely exserted, subdorsifixed or dorsifixed, pollen 3-7-porate, or rarely colpoidorate, exine reticulate; style non-functional, slender, included, glabrous or sparsely hirsute, ridged or smooth on dorsal part of lobes; style branches 2-4; ovary absent. Female corollas (4-)5-7-lobed; stamens non-functional, as many as corolla lobes, included, anthers linear, sessile, inserted in the middle of the tube, dorsifixed or subdorsifixed, pollen absent; style slender, included, glabrous, style branches 4; ovary glabrous, 4-locular; ovules 10-20 in each locule. Fruits indehiscent, globose or rarely somewhat vertically compressed, many-seeded, sessile or shortly pedunculate, glabrous or hirsute, calyx persistent in fruit, at maturity green, coffee-colored or black. Seeds irregularly globose, oblong, or depressed oblong, embedded in a fleshy placental pulp. Exotesta cells smooth, elongate, 5-10 times longer than wide, with thin secondary thickenings in ra- dial walls.

description: Trees with large alternate pinnately compound leaves; infloreseence of numerous eymules arranged in a large open panicle; incompletely dioecious; male trees producing staminate flowers with the carpels abortive or absent; female trees producing hermaphrodite flowers with reduced but functional stamens, or pistillate flowers without stamens; sepals 5-6; petals 5-6; stamens 10-12, or in hermaphrodite flowers sometimes 5-6, or fewer; disk 5-6-lobed, the lobes sometimes indented at the apex; carpels 5-6, separate except for their short columnar common style, or in some species more or less united and with sessile stigmas; stigmas 5-6, firm, divergent; ovules 1 per carpel; fruit of several distinct samaras each with a flattened seed in the center.
bibliographicCitation: Cronquist, Arthur J. 1944. Studies in the Simaroubaceae--IV. Resumé of the American genera. Brittonia. 5: 128-147.

description: Monotypic. Small trees or shrubs minutely stellate-pubescent. Leaves petiolate the blades ovate, truncate, irregularly cre- nate, acute or acuminate, discolorous, sparsely stellate-pubescent above, densely velutinous beneath; stipules filiform, caducous. Flowers in axillary fascicles, the ped- icels slender, tomentulose, articulated in upper third; involucel absent; calyx campan- ulate, ecostate, stellate-tomentulose; petals asymmetrically emarginate, white to bluish, basally biauriculate, the auricles densely pubescent; androecium included; styles 5, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, densely stellate-tomentose; mericarps 5, muticous, apically dehiscent, trigonal in cross section; seeds solitary, reniform, with scattered simple hairs at the apex. Chro- mosome number unknown.

description: Arbor parva vel frutex. Folia subrhombifolia basi cuneata. Inflorescentia fasciculata in axillis foliorum. Corolla caerulea vel alba. Petala biauriculata, densiter stellato-pubescentibus in appendicibus. Fructus schi- zocarpicis, mericarpiis 5, in apex dehiscentibus, in sectione transversali trigonis. Semina solitaria glabra.

description: Small trees or shrubs. Leaves ovate to subrhomboid. Flowers grouped in axillary fascicles. Calyx campanulate, ecostate. Petals white to blue, bi-auriculate, stellate-pubescent, the auricles stellate-pubescent. Fruits schizocarpic, the mericarps 5, trigonal in cross-section, apically dehiscent, 1-seeded.

description: Plants epiphytic, rarely saxicolous or terrestrial; roots non-proliferous; rhizomes short creeping or very short creeping to suberect, usually radially symmetric, with ventral or radial root insertion, branch buds apparently absent, scales present or sometimes absent, setae present or absent, the scales basifixed, concolorous, dull to shiny, yellowish, orang- ish, castaneous or very rarely blackish, with variously colored setae (hyaline to atropurpureous) and/or hyaline to orangish hairs on the margins and sometimes surfaces; blades pendent, of indeterminate growth, not articulate to rhizome; petioles with a single vascular bundle, usually short to very short (<1 cm long), setose and puberulent, the setae simple, spreading, 0.5-3.5 mm, hyaline to castaneous, the hairs 0.1-0.2(-0.3) mm, branched or unbranched; blades proximally gradually reduced, lacking mycelia and black clavate ascomes of the fungus Acrospermum maxonii, pinnatiesect (except in the case of one very deeply pinnatifid species) to 1- ppinnate- pinnatifid, forking in two species, essentially monomorphic, setose and/or puberulent, the setae stramineous, hyaline, yellowish, orangish, castaneous, deep red or atropurpureous, simple, paired, irregu- larly branched or clustered on pinna surfaces, pinna margins, and rachises, or rarely on the abaxial surfaces of the rachises, also growing out of the transverse walls of catenate axes made of basal cells, up to 1.5 mm long, the hairs simple or branched, hyaline to orangish or rarely whitish-sericeous, tubular to globose, sometimes eglandular; veins free, pinnate (Fig. 2E); hydathodes present, sometimes cretaceous (producing whitish lime dots); sori round, not sunken into the blade tissue, without para- physes; sporangia setose or rarely glabrous; spores tetrahedral-globose to ellipsoid or rarely globose, either monolete or trilete; и =37 (Evans, 1963).

description: Approximately 60 species, one of which is introduced into the Americas. Mostly erect annual, biennial, or perennial herbs, with stellate pubescense sometimes mixed with long simple hairs, sometimes glabrate. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades ovate to suborbicular, angled or weakly lobed or deeply palmately parted, crenate or dentate, acute to obtuse, lacking foliar nectaries. Inflorescence racemiform or spiciform, usu- ally leafless; involucel shorter than to equaling the calyx, 5-11-parted, connate below; calyx 5-lobed, more or less pubescent; petals usually >3 cm long, apically notched, pink, white, purple, or yellow, spreading to form a showy, rotate corolla; androecium included, glabrous, filamenti ferous at apex, usually pallid and compact; styles > 15, the stigmatic zone introrsely decurrent. Fruit a disk-shaped schizocarp of >15 mericarps; mericarps laterally compressed and circular with a prominent ventral notch, indehiscent, glabrous or pubescent, variously smooth, wrinkled, winged, furrowed, etc.; seeds solitary, glabrous or pustulate. 2n = 42 (several species).

description: Low, cespitose, herbaceous, acauleseent, glabrous to pubescent perennials from slender to thickened, elongated roots. Leaves petiolate, membranaceous to coriaceous, pinnate or bipinnate, the pinnae linear to ovate, distinct or confluent, often lobed and spinulose-dentate or entire. Petioles sheathing at base, persistent. Inflorescence a loose or compact compound umbel; peduncles terminial, longer or shorter than the leaves. Bracts of involuere usually wanting, if present, solitary, linear, and entire. Rays few to rather numerous, spreading-ascending. Bractlets of involucel subdimidiate, linear or lanceolate, free or connate at base, usually shorter than the flowers. Pedicels absent or short, spreading. Flowers yellow; petals ovate with a narrower inflexed apex; calyx-teeth deltoid-ovate to linear, evident to very conspicuous; styles slender, spreading, the stylopodium lacking; disk present. Carpophore two-cleft to the base, sometimes readily deciduous. Fruit oblong to ovoid-oblong, usually terete at maturity; ribs sub-equal, prominent and corky-winged or inconspicuous; vittae mostly solitary in the intervals, 2 on the commissure, sometimes one in the apex of each rib (accessory: ; seed subterete in transection, at times slightly channeled under the vittae, the face more or less plane; selerenchymatous cells inconspicuous.

description:
Suffruticose lianas. Stems usually terete, glabrous, sparsely lenticillate. Leaves opposite, blade glabrous except the abaxial surface with numerous fusiform glands at base of midrib, petiole short, minutely appendiculate, slightly fused at the base, mostly eglandular in the axils. Inflorescence a dichasial cyme, axillary, glabrous, 2-30- flowered, pedunculate, regularly dichotomously branched, bracts small, conspicuous or inconspicuous. Flowers: sepals 5, imbricate at base, bearing a few colleters within, entire or slightly fimbriate; corolla infundibuliform, glabrous without, lower part of tube straight, sometimes inflated at the base, the upper part (narrowly) campanulate to (narrowly) infundibuliform, the limb 5-parted, actinomorphic, dextrorsely convolute; stamens 5, always included, inserted where the corolla tube widens, infrastaminal indument, anthers connivent and agglu tinated to the pistil head, each consisting of 2 parallel, uniformly fertile thecae borne adaxially near the apex of an enlarged, sagittate, 2-auriculate, peltate connective, auricles short, filaments short, puberulent to pilose; carpels 2, united at the apex, pistil head fusiform, ovules numerous, disk glands 5, somewhat separated to rarely connate at the base and forming a disk. Follicles 2, apocarpous, smooth, terete and thin, seeds numerous, dry, truncate, comose at the micropilar end, usually rugose.

Allomarkgrafia comprises nine species.

description: Four species. Shrubs 1-5 m tall with pubescence of both stellate and simple hairs, sometimes viscid. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades lanceolate or ovate, cordate, crenate, acuminate. Flowers in terminal, more or less leafless panicles or racemes; invol- ucel absent; calyx basally rounded, twisted in bud, the tips of the acuminate lobes divergent; petals white to yellow, with or without a dark basal spot; androecium in- cluded, the column filamentiferous at apex; styles 5-9, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, oblate, of 5-9 mericarps; mericarps essentially indehiscent, more or less rounded dorsally, with relatively fragile walls lacking ornamentation, with or without an apical beak, with a small endoglossum; seeds solitary, glabrous. 2n = 14 (two species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Approximately 12 species, one of which is naturalized in North America. Annual or perennial herbs, more or less stellate-pu- bescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate triangular or palmately 3-5-lobed orparted (juvenile leaves unlobed and often rotund), dentate, acute; stipules subulate. Flowers solitary or grouped in the leaf axils, often forming terminal racemes rising above the leaves; pedicels short or long (up to 3.5 cm); involucel 6-10-parted, basally con- nate; calyx half-divided to deeply 5-parted; petals lavender or pink, less than or equal to 2 cm long; staminal column glabrous, cylindrical; styles 8-25. Fruits schizocarpic, oblate or disciform; mericarps 8-25, semicircular, dorsally channeled, indehiscent, unilocular and 1-seeded. 2n = 28, 42, 50, 70, and 84. (Some of these counts may represent Al- cea!)

description: Shrubs or smiiall-to-medium-sized trees up to 15 m. high; leaves pinnately compound, with niumerous offset leaflets not over 5 em. long; infloreseence of long slender naked racemnes, with small flowers; dioecious; male flowers with 5 united sepals, 5 slender petals alternate with the sepals, or apetalous, and 5 stamens alternate with the sepals, inserted between the lobes of a disk; connective enlarged, the pollen sacs attached to it nearly opposite to the line of dehiseence; female flowers with 5 distinct sepals, and a 3-carpellary ovary inserted on a thin disk; two carpels sterile, the third fertile and bearing two ovules, usually only one ovule maturing; fruit a samara or samaroid capsule, the fertile carpel sometimes winged like the sterile ones, sometimes inconspicuous and partly surrounded by them.

description: Shrubs, when pubescent the hairs incompletely septate; stipules entire or fimbriate. Inflorescences axillary, rarely terminal or subterminal, cymose or subcapitate. Corolla hypocrateriform, its lobes 5, valvate; stamens 5, inserted in the upper half of the corolla tube; stigma bilobate. Ovary bilocular, the ovules numerous on a discoid placenta. Fruit globose; seeds (Fig. 13) 0.3-0.8 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm in diam, foveolate; seed coat (Fig. 14) with irregularly polygonal cells 72-96 (87) x 39-84 (57.6) µm, small pits scattered in the internal walls (Fig. 14), more than 50 pits per cell, less than I ,um in diam, the lateral walls thick, 8-15 µm thick.

description: Indo-China, Turong (=Tourane), Kuntze 3763, type of Bothriochloa anamitica 0. Ktz., Britton Herbarium, New York Botanical Garden. Bothriochloa was proposed by Kuntze as a new genus. Am-philophis Nash (1901) is congeneric with it. For those who recognize the numerous close generic segregates from Andropogon, Bothriochloa should replace Amphilophis as Rydberg has done (Brittonia 1: 81. 1931). Kuntze’s type has been examined by A. Camus, who overlooked the genus and species in the treatment of the Gramineae of Indo-China (Lecomte, FI. Gen. Indo-Chine 7: 202-650. 1922-23), and who refers it to Roxburgh’s species.

description: Caespitose perennials with usually stiffly erect culms, rounded or flattened and keeled sheaths, and flat or folded blades. Inflorescence various, the flowering culm much-branched above and terminating in numerous branchlets bearing 2 to several pedunculate flower clusters or the flowering culm little-branched and terminating in a stiffly erect panicle of 2 (rarely 1) to few spicate branches. Sessile spikelet of the pair fertile and awned. Pedicelled spikelet smaller than the sessile one, often rudi- mentary or absent. Disarticulation in the rachis, the sessile spikelets falling attached to the rachis joint and associated pedicel.

description: Slender lianas with milky latex, the stems sparsely pubescent. Leaves opposite, chartaceous, the blade ovate to elliptic, 5-14 cm long, 2-6 cm broad, contracted at apex into an acumen 0.5-1 cm long, obtuse to truncate at base, upper surface with a sparse indument of forwardly falcate hairs arising from a conspicuous hardened, multicellular base, lower surface glabrous except for falcate hairs along the midvein, strigillose at the margins, appearing punctate where multicellular trichome bases occur on the upper surface; secondary veins about 10 pairs, broch- idodromous; tertiary venation weakly percurrent; midvein shallowly canaliculate above; petiole 1.5-3 cm long, pubescent, glandular in the axils. Inflorescence an axillary 11-15-flowered dichasium, the peduncle 11-30 cm long, puberulent. Flowers borne on pedicels 0.7-4 cm long; calyx pubescent, the lobes 1.5 mm long, lanceolate, acuminate, terminated by a solitary gland at the apex, with 5-9 squa- mellae on the adaxial surface arranged in a somewhat irregular series on the lower part of the sepal; corolla white, salverform, the tube puberulent externally, pu- bescent internally, with indument more dense above the stamens than below, 0.4-1.2 cm long, 1.5 mm broad, slightly expanded at the level of stamen insertion, the lobes spreading, ciliolate, 4.5-5 mm long, 2.5 mm broad, aestivation sinis- trorse; stamens 5, included, inserted about the middle of the corolla tube, the filaments very short, ca 0.5 mm long, the anthers basifixed, triangular, with an enlarged acumen ca 0.8 mm long at apex, round at the base without sterile appendages, dehiscing latrorsely; ovary superior, ovoid, glabrous, 0.8 mm high, surrounded by an annular lobed disc 0.5 mm high; carpels 2, free, with a common style ca 1 mm long, broadest at the distal end; style-head lenticular with 2 papillose appendages at the apex which are about twice as long as the rest of the style-head, and an abbreviated, membranous annulus at the base; ovules 2-6 in each carpel, biseriate. Fruit apocarpous, composed of 2 fusiform, indehiscent, 1-seeded mer- icarps ca 8 cm long, developed into a sterile beak at the distal end, with an indument of recurved hairs which is most dense at the distal end.
bibliographicCitation: Fallen, Mary E. 1983. A systematic revision of Anechites (Apocynaceae). Brittonia. 35: 222-231.

description: Rhizome compact or short-creeping, horizontal or ascending, clothed with dark or orange hairs; fronds generally erect, rarely forming a flat rosette, pinnate to tripinnate, papyraceous to coriaceous; veins free or netted; sporangia usually restricted to the highly dissected lowermost pair of pinnae, but fronds occasionally holodimorphic; fertile pinnae held erect, rarely horizontally or at an angle; sporangia in two rows on ultimate segments of fertile pinnae; spores tetrahedral-globose, striate with parallel smooth or spiny ridges.

description: Twenty-four species. Annual or perennial herbs or subshrubs, erect or decumbent, hispid or stellate-pubescent or -puberulent to glabrate. Leaves petiolate, the blades linear, lanceolate, ovate, cordate, hastately lobed, or palmately divided, crenate or dentate to subentire, usually green, sometimes with an irregular purplish blotch along midvein, sometimes canescent beneath; stipules generally inconspicuous and deciduous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or aggregated in open apical racemes or panicles; invol- ucel absent; calyx sometimes accrescent in fruit, basally rounded, usually 5- or 10-nerved; petals spreading, yellow, white, lavender, or purplish; androecium shorter than to equaling the petals, usually yellowish, filamentiferous at apex; styles 5-20, slender, usually exceeding the androecium, the stigmas usually abruptly capitate, glabrous. Fruits oblate or disklike, schizocar pic, puberulent to hispid; mericarps 5-20, with or without a spur or spine at the dorsal angle, the lateral walls usually disintegrating at maturity; seeds solitary, glabrous or pubescent, sometimes enclosed in a persis- tent reticulate endocarp. 2n = 26, 28, 30, 60, 90 (Bates, 1987; Fryxell & Stelly, 1993).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Description: A woody vine, climbing to the tops of very high trees; bralichlets slender, terete, solid, rather densely strigose-pubescent on younger parts or furfuraceous-pubeseent throughout, the pubescence soon wearing off from the elongated internodes; leaf scars large and prominent; leaves alternate; petioles slender, 3-10 cm. long, appressed strigose-puberulent (the puberulence wearing off on older petioles), inerassate at apex; blades firmly membranous, very nitid on both surfaces, oblong or oblanceolate, 12-31 cm. long. 2.5-10 cm. wide, rather long-acuminate to a very sharp and attenuate point at the apex, entire, regularly and gradually narrowed to the acute base, glabrous above, more or less short-pilose along the midrib beneath (often very sparsely so in age) with brownish or grayish hairs; midrib slender, impressed above, prominent beneath; sec- ondaries slender, pinnate, 9-11 per side, prominulent above, promi- nent beneath; vein and veinlet reticulation very abundant and delicate, equally and beautifully conspicuous to the ultimate divisions on both surfaces and equally prominulent; infloreseelnce and fruit not seen.

description: Lianas, the braniehes stout, terete, einereous, the branchlets usually opposite, elongate, slender, sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, petiolate, the petioles slender, shallowly canaliculate; inflorescence axillary, cymose, 3-6-times dichotomously branched, pedunculate; flowers paired or ternate at apices of ultimate inflorescence-branchlets or solitary in distal dichotomies, each subtended by 2 or 3 minute bracteoles, pedicellate; sepals 5, imbricate; petals 5, spreading, conspicuously serrate at margins; disk carnose, short-cylindric, sub-erect, usually flattened or grooved on margin; stamens 3, suberect, the filaments ligulate, the anthers basifixed, broadly reniform, dehiseing by elongate apical horizontal confluent clefts; ovary depressed-trigonous, the style stout, carnose, the stigmas 3, minute, often obscure, oppo- site the stameins (but sometinies faintly plicate and giving the appearance of being alternate with stamens and emarginate), the locules 3, the ovules 8-14 per locule, imbricate in a mass attached to the inner basal angle; fruiting infloreseence swollen, the fruits probably 1 per inflorescence, flattened, capsular, the capsules 3, spreading, firmly connate at basal margins (sinuses broadly rounded or nearly flattened), convex on both surfaces, sharp and entire at margins, inconspicuously carinate and dehiscing along a median suture (adjacent halves coherent), the pericarp coriaceous, flabellate-costate without (nerves prominulous), sniooth within; seeds 8-14, erect from base, at maturity coni- pletely occupying the capsule-cavity except for a narrow apical flange, closely imbricate, affixed by a basal wing, the embryoniferous portion apical, coriaceous, the wing membranous, with a single longitudinal nerve near center, the raphe conspicuous, greatly thickened distally, ascending along the outer margin.

description: Low shrubs or small trees, sometimes epiphytes. Leaves alternate, subopposite, or verticillate, coriaceous, margin entire, pin- nate or plinerved. Inflorescence axillary, racemose, many-flowered; floral bract to 20 mm long but usually small and inconspicuous. Flowers 5-merous, without odor; aestivation valvate; calyx continuous with ped- icel; hypanthium broadening distally and winged; limb suberect; lobes ovate to del- tate; corolla subcylindric, cylindric-urceolate or subglobose, narrowly to broadly winged, the lobes triangular, subacute to long-acuminate; stamens 10, essentially equal, nearly as long as the corolla, sometimes geniculate; filaments equal, distinct or basally slightly connate, shorter than anthers, lacking spurs; anthers dorsifixed, membranous, lacking disintegration tissue; thecae smooth; tubules longer than the thecae, de- hiscing by short to elongate clefts; pollen lacking viscin threads; ovary inferior; stigma truncate; style filiform, about as long as the corolla; nectariferous disc annular or cupuliform. Fruit a spherical, blue-black berry (where known).

description: Herba annua, monoecia; radices fibrosae; caules repentes; folia ramique glabrati non glandulosi; folia simplicia, ad basim (5-)7-nervia; cirrhi 2- vel 3-partiti; flores minimi, pentameri, corollis usque ad basim 5-partitis, calycum dentibus subnullis: flores staminati racemosi; staminum filamenta in columnam connata; antherarum loculi 5, hippocrepiformes, circum capitulum connectivorum junctorum digesti; con- nectiva non producta; pollen polycolpatum, foveolato-reticulatum, espinulosum; pistil- lodia nulla; flores pistillati in isdem axillis cum staminatis solitarii; staminodia nulla; pedunculi post anthesin multo elongati geotropicique; ovarium ovoideum, erostratum, uniloculare; ovulum solitarium, erectum; fructus subterraneus, obovoideus, siccus, 1- spermus, indehiscens; semen solitarium, compressum.

description: Plants small, caespitose or prostrate to ascending, rosulate or shortly stoloniferous, perennial herbs of high elevations, densely branching, 1-10 cm high; stems pale to reddish-tinged, terete, smooth to striate, with solid pith. Leaves opposite, sessile or shortly petioliform from short fused sheath; blade oblong to elliptical, mostly 1-2 cm long, margins entire to subdentate, apex rounded to obtuse, surfaces glabrous to lanate, with 3 or 5 longitudinal veins from base. Inflorescence with single heads sessile until anthesis, becoming raised at or after anthesis on non-bracteiferous peduncle. Heads broadly campanulate, heterogamous, shortly subradiate, ca. 4 mm high and wide; involucre weakly biseriate, bracts 6-10, subequal, thinly herbaceous, usually becoming yellowish or brownish, broadly ovate or oblong, tips rounded or obtuse, with many longitudinal resiniferous ducts, glabrous or pilose outside; receptacle coni- cal, with pustulate surface, paleaceous; pales chartaceous, linear or subulate, outer pales longer, inner pales often lacking. Ray florets 5-21, pistillate, not wrapped in bases of involucral bracts; corollas yellowish green, with tube hirtellous to villous, limb lacking or short and weakly trilobed, sometimes disciform with 4 or 5 lobes, smooth inside. Disk florets 3-45; corollas greenish to yellowish greenish or pale yellowish, tube hirtellous to villous, throat campanulate, lobes 5, broadly triangular, nearly smooth inside, ducts yellow, paired or often fused into single duct along veins of throat; anther thecae and appendages yellowish to greenish, without glands; style shaft not enlarged below, with ducts inside of veins; branches short, with paired, separate stigmatic lines, appendages rounded or obtuse. Achenes terete, more narrowed below, glabrous, walls black with intervening continuous rows of pale cells, carpopodium sclerified on only one side; pappus lacking. Pollen 25-27 µm diam.

description: Hypanthium small, glandular-pubescent; sepals depressed semicir- cular; petals cuneate-obovate; outer stamens linear-subulate, about equaling their connective; inner stamens obovoid, blunt, half as long as their appendages; ovary 3-celled; style filiform, stigma punctiform. Low herbs, with small flowers in terminal clusters and ovate leaves about 1 cm. long. The following is the only known species.

description: Trees, shrubs, lianas or rhizomatous herbs, armed or unarmed; leaves alternate, one-four-pinnate, the rachis articulated, mostly stipulate; inflorescence terminal, paniculate, corymbose, or umbellate, usually consisting of umbels, capitula, or racemes, occasionally umbels solitary; flowers five eight-merous, with pedicels articulated below; sepals five-eight; petals five-eight, imbricate; stamens five-eight, recurved in buds; ovary inferior, five-eight-locular, occasionally aborted to three; floral disk present; styles distinct, connate at the base or completely; fruit a berry, five-eight-locular, more or less globose.

description: Gramen perenne sylvarum umbrosarum. Culmi herbacei, erecti, sine ramis. Inflorescentia paniculata, paniculis usque ad 8 e nodo productis. Spiculae 1-florae, unisexuales, [female] singularis terminalis et [male] plures infra-apicales. Spicula [female] grandis, albida, spiculis [male] longior, internodio rachillae inter glumas et anthoecium elongato; glumae multi-nervatae, quam anthoecium longiores; anthoecium maturitate indurescens, sericeum; lodiculae 3, carnosae, truncatae; stylus singularis, stigmatibus 2 plumosis; caryopsis hilo lineari. Spicula [male] sine glumis; lemma et palea membranaceae; lodiculae 3, carnosae, truncatae; stamina 3.

(dwarfs 20-25 p) ;. styles exserted, 2.0-4 mm. exceeding the corolla, slender, the tip somiiewhat broadened and flattened, with an inner longitudinal groove, the outer surface papillose, the tip penicillate, revolutely coiled; achenes cylindrical or tapered at both ends, 3.0-10 nm.m. long, 0.7-1.5 mi. thick, more or less distinctly 5-10-nerved, minutely bullate-striate, glabrous, hirsute, or glanidular, with a conspicuous white annulus at the base; pappus bristles slender, varying fron white to tawny, and fromn barbellate to plumose, more or less as longV as disc corolla; leaves opposite, or the upper alternate by disjunction of the nodes, sessile or petiolate; stemiis herbaceous, 1.0-8.5 din. high, simllple or branched from the base; rhizomne perennial, horizontal creeping and branching, or short, erect, and unbranched.

description: Plants epiphytic, occasionally saxicolous (in A. anfractuosa and A. pichinchensis); roots inserted ventrally on the rhizome, proliferous (i.e., producing new plantlets) or non-proliferous; rhizome short-creeping, dorsiventral, bearing fronds along the dorsal side, unbranched, bearing lateral extra-axillary branch buds or not, dictyostelic, the dictyostele perforated or not, the cortex provided with bands of parenchyma darkened by phenolic compounds or not, provided throughout with scales, the scales basifixed, ovate to lanceolate, usually clathrate, sometimes non-clathrate, often clathrate but appearing non-clathrate and concolorous when the lumina are narrow, the cell walls indurate, dark red to blackish, the lumina usually transparent, iridescent or not, flattened (not turgid), dull to sub-glossy, clear to partially occluded, the opacity often variable between lumina within one scale, rarely fully occluded and opaque, the base semi-cordate, the apex acute to attenuate, provided with a single papillate cell held at an oblique angle to the apex, the margin usually setose, sometimes entire or provided only with a single apical seta, the setae ca. 0.1-0.2 mm long, usually translucent and reddish, sometimes hyaline in A. david- smithii, spreading, the abaxial and adaxial scale surfaces usually glabrous, setose in A. oxapampensis; fronds determinate, monomorphic or hemidimorphic, and then the fertile portions of fertile fronds more densely setose than sterile portions of the same frond or than of sterile fronds, distichous, erect, arching, or pendulous, the position apparently determined by the size of the frond, usually provided throughout with the mycelia and ascomes of Acrospermum maxonii, provided with setae and hairs, the setae ca. 0.5-2 mm long, multicellular, uniseriate, simple, terete, spreading, reddish to castaneous, sometimes pale toward the apex or when young, usually found on petioles, rachises, and laminae, the hairs usually ca. 0.1 mm long, usually 3- celled and unequally 1 -furcate, the shorter branch papillate, the longer branch setiform (Fig. 1C), up to 1.0 mm long (in A. angustipes), sometimes the hairs one-or two- celled and simple, usually found on petioles and rachises, rarely on laminae, if so then generally simple and present along the margin or abaxial surface; petiole non-articulate, with a single vascular bundle, or with two bundles and then the bundles quickly fusing, terete or narrowly marginate, the margin ca. 0.1 mm wide, throughout the length of the petiole, or only along the distal portion, the petiole, rachis, and segment costae dark in color, the cortex sclerenchymatous, castane- ous to blackish, the epidermis greenish to hyaline, not sclerified (Fig. 12D); rachis clearly visible on the abaxial side of the lamina, adaxially sometimes covered by parenchyma of the lamina and not visible; laminae chartaceous to membranaceous, nar- rowly elliptic, sometimes nearly linear, 1- pinnatisect to 1 -pinnate, in general more deeply dissected proximally and less dissected distally, with reduced segments at the apex and base; segments narrowly triangular to oblong, usually entire, pinnatifid in A. athyrioides, the base sessile, even-sided or dilated, and then usually decurrent, sometimes surcurrent, the apex rounded to acute, the margins glabrous, setose, or provided with ca. 0.1 mm long simple hairs; segment costae either visible or covered by the parenchyma of the lamina on either side of the blade; veins alternate, simple, green (not darkly colored), usually visible on the abaxial side of the blade, usually not visible on the adaxial side of the blade; hydathodes present, cretaceous or not, the deposit white, sometimes stained red or gray; sori at apices of veins, present throughout the length of the lamina or more commonly confined to the distal portion, usually inframedial, sometimes medial, slightly longer than wide, sometimes provided with receptacular setae; paraphyses absent; sporangia glabrous; spores trilete (Fig. IB), green, composed of one or two cells at the time of sporangial dehiscence (Fig. 1A), the surface ruberculate (Fig IB); chromosome number unknown, presumably x=37 as in most Polypodiaceae.

description: Trees or shrubs from stout-linear to fusiform taproots; twigs glabrous or variously pubescent when young, alternately arranged, with prominent lenticels; leaves membranaceous to coriaceous, estipulate, alternate, deciduous, entire, slightly to prominently revolute; flowers axillary, 1-4 per leaf axil, acereseent, nutant to suberect, on glabrate to tomentose peduncles; calyx-lobes 3 to 4, triangular to deltoid-ovate, equal, distinct nearly to the receptacle, glabrate to persistently hairy without; corolla 3- or 4-merous in two unequal cycles of three or four equal members each, imbricate in the bud, veiny, spreading to erect, the inner saccate-based and with or without an inner, corrugated, nectary zone; stamens numerous, short-columnar, joined when young into a tight ball on the elevated torus; filaments reduced; anther sacs joined into two parallel series on the outer stamen face and surmounted by blunt to sub-spherical or cuboidal connectives; carpels three to several, variously appressed-hairy, sessile on the torus summit, narrowly fusiform placentation in two ventral rows; fruit an oblong-cylindric, few- to many-seeded, pulpy berry; seeds bean-shaped, com- pressed laterally, with tough, brown to castaneous coats; endosperm in plates; cotyledons rudimentary.
bibliographicCitation: Kral, Robert. 1960. A Revision of Asimina and Deeringothamnus (Annonaceae). Brittonia. 12 (4): 233-278.

description: Plants epiphytic. Pseudobulbs stalked, with 2-6 sheathing bracts on the stalk, the bracts often falling as the pseudobulb matures; pseudobulbs long-elliptic to angular-oblong, usually flattened, often furrowed, topped by 1-2 leaves. Leaves lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, acuminate. Inflorescence 1- to 10-flowered, floral bracts small, clasping, triangular, cuspidate. Pedicel much longer than the floral bracts, smooth. Sepals elliptic-obovate to lanceolate, often with an apiculate fleshy emarginate apex, concave, the dorsal sepal adnate to the base of the column; lateral sepals free, spreading or reflexed. Petals elliptic-obovate, lanceolate, often adnate to the base of the column, often with a fleshy apiculate emarginate apex. Lip united with the column by the lateral margins for about one-half the length of the column or less, bent perpendicular to the column at the union, forming a nectary-like cavity between the column and the base of the lip; lip varying from distinctly lobed to al- most entire, often constricted at the middle, the apex entire or emarginate, rarely acuminate at times fimbriate or crenulate, often curved upwards, the lip with 2-4 ridges of callus basally. Column cylindrical, semiterete, rarely slightly arched forward, the area beneath the stigma often channeled, often with two small auricles or projec- tions just below and to the side of the stigma. Anther fleshy, often with a distinct keel, clinandrium rarely faintly fimbriate or denticulate, never hooded over the anther cap; anther cap smooth to papillose, in some species projecting over the viscidium. Viscidium narrowly elliptic; stipe somewhat constricted basally, narrowly angular- obovate, the lateral margins recurved and almost meeting basally; pollinia asym- metrically reniform, the ventral groove very prominent, the surface smooth, yellow. Capsule cylindrical-fusiform, the three ridges prominent. A chromosome number of 2n -58 has been reported for Aspasia principissa (Sinoto, 1962).

description: Small to medium-sized, solitary, unarmed, pleonanthic, monoecious palm. Stem smooth, brown to brownish cream, erect, sometimes basally decumbent, occasionally with basal and/or lateral vegetative branches, unarmed; internodes short; adventitious roots forming a basal cone. Leaves spirally arranged, 6-31, erect to arching, marcescent; sheath brown or cream colored, short, tubular, splitting opposite petiole, the margins stiff fibrous, the tomentum brown to reddish brown; petiole slender, adaxially flat or channeled, glabrous, abaxially rounded or angled, brown tomentose; blade bifid simple, sometimes becoming irregularly split with age or damage caused by wind, narrowly cuneate at base; veins 25-70, emerging at 20-35º angle from midvein (rachis), prominent at one or both surfaces of blade. Inflorescence interfoliar, solitary, branched to one order, rarely spicate or forked, erect at anthesis, becoming pendent in fruit, protandrous; peduncle long, slender, brown to whitish tomentose; prophyll tubular, fibrous, membranous or chartaceous, bicarinate, brown tomentose, inserted near base of peduncle; peduncular bracts 1 or 2, tubular, chartaceous or membranous, inserted 1 to several cm above base of peduncle; inflorescence rachis with short, ovate, pointed bracts, subtending rachillae, salmon to pink at anthesis, brown to reddish brown in fruit; rachillae 1-16, ca. equal in length, ending in a short, sterile apex, same color as inflorescence rachis. Flower pits containing triads comprising two staminate flowers and one pistillate flower, the pits spirally arranged on rachis, covered by a rounded upper lip that overlaps the lower, immersed lip when in bud; floral bracts 3, the largest bract subtending the second sta- minate flower, a medium-sized, 2-keeled bract subtending the pistillate flower, and a small bract representing the prophyll of the pistillate flower. Staminate flowers oblong to oblong-obovoid, borne abaxially to pistillate flowers; sepals 3, unequal, united ba- sally, narrow, elongate, keeled dorsally; petals 3, ca. as long as or longer than sepals, united into a tube for ca. 2/3 their length, distally valvate; stamens 6-27; filaments united into a tube up to midlength, white or yellow, with or without a papillate epidermis; connective bifid, tanniferous, bearing separated thecae, the anthers inflexed toward center of flower and introrse in bud, spread and extrorse at anthesis; pollen asymmetric in shape, monosulcate, the sulcus as long as main axis, the exine tectate and finely perforate-rugulate or perforate-fossulate (Fig. 3A-H); pistillode irregularly 3-lobed (Fig. 12E). Pistillate flowers oblong to oblong-ovoid; sepals 3, unequal, imbricate in bud, dorsally keeled; petals 3, united up to midlength, distally valvate; staminodes 5-22, fused to corolla and united basally, fleshy, with tanniferous tips; gynoecium syncarpous, trilocular, triovulate, the nectary septal; style basal to lateral, elongate; stigmatic branches 3, papillate, reflexed at anthesis; ovule anatropous, inserted at midlength of locule, pendent. Fruit a drupe, ellipsoid to ellipsoid-ovoid, 1-seeded, dorsiventrally compressed, slightly to conspicuously keeled at apex, the remains of the stigma basal; epicarp smooth, purplish black or garnet red at maturity; mesocarp fleshy and juicy, with an inner layer of closely appressed, longitudinal fibers; endocarp thin, crustaceous, and shiny (Uhl and Dransfield, 1987). Eophyll with a bifid simple blade.
