description: Perennial herbs, hemicryptophytes, ligno tubers elongate, stems erect, basally branched or simple. Leaves densely disposed, alternate, spirally arranged, narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, sessile, apex subacute, base attenuate, glandular and woollyvillous on both surfaces, margins entire. Capitula solitary (less commonly 2 or 3), terminal, sessile, heterogamous, radiate. Involucres hemispheric to globose; phyllaries in 5 or 6 series, glandular and villous on both surfaces. Receptacles epaleate. Ray florets 3- or 4- seriate, pistillate, corollas white, true rays with long limbs, style branches linear. Disk florets numerous, bisexual (functionally male), corolla actinomorphic, 5-lobed; anther base slightly sagittate, apical appendages ovate; style branches narrowly triangular to oblong, totally dorsally covered by sweeping hairs. Cypselae flattened, strongly 2-nerved, gradually attenuate towards the apex, glandular throughout its surface and villous mainly on the margins, cypselae of disk florets noticeably thinner, with or without a developed ovule. Pappus of 2 or 3 series of scabrid bristles, sometimes with some outermost bristles very short.

description: Shrubs to subshrubs, multistemmed; bark papery or thin-coriaceous, exfoliating in small pieces; wood white. Stipules interpetiolar, free or shortly connate at base, caducous (persisting on the stem up to the third-fourth node). Blades narrowly elliptic, elliptic, oblanceolate to obovate, not acuminate at apex; domatia absent. Inflorescence terminal, corymbose, with lateral branches terminating in few-flowered cymules. Flowers protandrous, short-pedicel- late, slightly fragrant; hypanthium obconical. Calyx with 5 lobes, persistent. Corolla narrowly funnel-shaped or narrowly tubular, with reflexed lobes, red or white; corolla tube glabrous throughout; corolla lobes 5, reflexed, aestivation imbricate; flower buds pointed at apex. Stamens 5, exserted; anthers narrowly elliptic, dorsifixed, dehiscing by lateral slits; filaments extremely short, attached at the sinuses of the corolla lobes. Style exserted, style branches short, reflexed at maturity. Ovary 2-celled, with central placentation, obconical. Capsules obovoid, obconical or turbinate, dehiscing septicidally. Seeds numerous, tetrahedral, horizontally inserted.

description: Thirteen or more species. Shrubs or small trees 1-8 m tall, densely stellate-pubescent, often ferruginous. Leaves petiolate, the blades broadly ovate, cordate (or narrower and truncate in the inflorescence), entire (or sometimes vestigially dentate), acute or acuminate, minutely stellate-pubescent above and beneath, more densely so beneath, sometimes discolorous. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils or aggregated into axillary or terminal inflorescences; involucel absent; calyx lobes usually prominently ribbed, sometimes twisted in bud; petals usually large (1.5-6 cm long) and showy, white, yellow, or yellow-or- ange, often with a dark reddish spot at base; staminal column included or exserted, filamentiferous at apex, glabrous or pubescent; styles 7-27, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, more or less blackish, stellatepubescent; mericarps 7-27, rounded, often with a lacerate or erose wing on the dorsal margin, 2-7-seeded; seeds reniform, pubescent or glabrate. 2n = 30 (three species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect, glabrous or minutely puberulent, with 1-20 branches. Leaves alternate, sessile, few to many; blades narrow, entire. Involucre thick, bracts herbaceous, arranged in 3-4 series; outer bracts broad, pubescent; inner bracts longer and narrower, glabrous. Inflorescence of 1-20 heads, determinate. Ray flowers 8-25, neutral, yellow, spatulate, trifid at apex; disk flowers 30-190, perfect and fertile, yellow or purple, funnelform. Filaments nearly as long as the anthers, anthers sagittate at base, each with a distinct acute appendage at the apex. Stigmas divergent or recurved at anthesis, exerted beyond the corolla tube. Receptacle deeply alveolate, the 5-6-angled cells with toothed margins, enclosing the obconical, pubescent achenes, pappus of 10-12 lanceolate or obovate-orbicular nerveless scales.

description: Trees or treelets 2-30 m tall, with punctate glands usually visible on all unlignified parts; buds densely sericeous; young shoots appressed-pubescent. Leaves opposite, digitately 3-foliolate, densely glandular-punctate, pubescent to glabrescent; petiole semiterete to canaliculate, with a small, hairy appendage or a tuft of longer trichomes on the adaxial surface proximal to the base of the terminal leaflet; leaflets sessile to petiolulate, conspicuously articulate at the grooved petiole apex, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, the margin entire to seldom slightly crenulate; terminal leaflet symmetnc and larger than the lateral ones, which are asymmetric at base; venation brochidodromous, the midvein usually raised on both surfaces; domatia (small, hairy, 1-4- celled cavities) in the axils of most second- ary nerves. Inflorescence a terminal, polytelic diplothyrse, usually longer than the leaves, pubescent, loose to dense; branches (sub-)opposite, patent; peduncle present or absent; bracts and prophylls (bractlets) linear-lanceolate, usually paired. Flowers tetramerous, perfect, actinomorphic, pedicellate, cream-colored. Sepals imbricate, pubescent or glabrous, persistent in fruit, scarious, ciliolate. Petals free, imbricate in bud, pellucid-punctate, glabrous, hyaline except for the midvein, margin entire to erose, at base attenuate to subunguiculate. Stamens 4, alternipetalous, free, glabrous; filaments subulate, translucent, inserted below the disk, reflexed after anthesis; anthers ovoid, dorsifixed below the middle, versatile, introrse, 2-celled, the cells somewhat divergent at base. Disk intrastaminal, cupular, forming an erect, undulate rim, 4-lobed, each lobe 2-lobulate, glabrous, surrounding the ovary and about level with it. Ovary of 4 connate carpels conspicuously 4-lobed, depressed-globose, minutely glandular-tuberculate, glabrous; ovules 2 per locule, collateral, pendulous; style 1, terete, glabrous; stigma capitate and minutely 4- lobed. Fruit a (3-)4-locular samara with 4 expanded, vertical, rounded to rounded- truncate, subcoriaceous, prominently veined wings, glabrescent or glabrous; seed 1 per carpel, free from the endocarp, oblong, with a thin testa and fleshy endosperm, glabrous; embryo fleshy, with straight, oblong cotyledons and a superior radicle.

description: Arbores vel frutices scandentes. Folia alterna; lamina subtus glandulis impressis instructa; petiolus eglandulosus; stipulae nullae. Inflorescentia terminalis, thyrsiformis, ex cincinnis 1-3-floris composita, pedunculis pedicellisque longis et gracilibus. Flos calyce, corolla, et androecio perigyno, pilis basifixis caespitosis inter sepala et filamenta. Sepala 5 omnia biglandulifera, glandulis obovatis, arcte compressis, aliquot vel omnis in pedicello decurrentibus. Stamina 10, omnia fertilia, filamentis inter se liberis, antheris longitudinaliter dehiscentibus; pollen 3 (-5) poris aequatoriis instructum, sine colpis. Gynoecium ex 3 carpellis uniovulatis compositum, carpellis late connatis per totam longitudinem ovarii; styli 3, liberi, inter se ± aequales, antheras solum 1-1.5 mm superantes, subulati, stigmatibus internis vel paene terminalibus. Fructus siccus, schizocarpicus, ex 3 samaris constans; samarae ala dorsalis longa, margine superiore (adaxiali) incrassata; nux lateribus laevis, sine carpophoro basalidorsali, areola ventrali grandi; samara ex toro trigono decidua, postremo in receptaculo affixa solum per 2 costas coriaceas margine areolae ventralis. Semen cotyledonibus crassis, subaequalibus vel inaequalibus, ±rectis.

description: Trees or woody vines. Leaves alternate, bearing impressed glands 0.3-0.9 mm in diameter below in the lamina; petiole eglandular; stipules none. Inflorescence terminal, the dominant axis terminal and unbranched or with several to many weaker axes arising from near the base, each axis thyrsiform, i.e., a raceme of 1-3-flowered cincinni, the peduncles and pedicels long and slender. Flower with the calyx, corolla, and androecium perigynous, the calyx lobes and petals borne on the rim of a concave receptacle, the filaments departing below the rim, and the ovary borne in the base. Sepals 5, all biglandular, the glands yellow, tightly compressed, obovate, some or all decurrent on the pedicel; sepals broadly round- ed, abaxially glabrous, ciliate on the margin, adaxially glabrous except for a thick band of straight or twisted basifixed hairs at the base, adjacent to the filaments. Petals 5, yellow, with short thick claws 0.6-1 mm long, the posterior petal erect, the lateral 4 ± spreading. Stamens 10, all fertile, yellow; filaments short, alike, glabrous, free from each other, attached to base of connective; anthers in 2 distinctly alternating ranks in bud, the outer opposite sepals and longer, the inner opposite petals and shorter, all with longitudinal dehiscence, the connective dark but not glandular, not or hardly exceeding locules at apex; pollen 22-27 µm in diameter, oblate, with 3 (-5) large equatorial pores and no colpi. Gynoecium of 3 carpels, 1 anterior and 2 posterior, broadly connate for the whole length of the ovary; ovary densely sericeous, with 3 locules, each locule containing 1 ovule; styles 3, free, ± alike, glabrous or hairy only at the base, exceeding the anthers by only 1-1.5 mm, subulate, the stigmas nearly apical to internal. Fruit dry, schizocarpic, comprising 3 samaras (or fewer due to abortion), each samara with an elongated dorsal wing thickened on the adaxial margin, the veins bending away and ending in the thinner abaxial margin; nut large and inflated, with a prominent reticulum but without lateral wings or crests, lacking a basal-dorsal carpophore, with an elongated ventral areole where the 3 nuts fit together, separating from an elongated 3-faced torus, finally attached to the receptacle only by 2 coriaceous ribs at the margin of the areole. Seed with the cotyledons thick, subequal or unequal, ± straight with neither bent back at the apex.

description: Three or four species, possibly more. Herbs or shrubs 0.5-3 m tall, pubescent with stellate, simple, and often glandular hairs. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate, rarely lobulate, cordate-ovate, subentire to crenate-serrate, acute or acuminate; stipules subulate. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils, often aggregated into terminal leafy panicles; involucel absent; calyx divided almost to the base; petals relatively small, yellow; androecium included, pallid; styles 5-8, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic but functionally capsular; mericarps 5-8, apically rounded or apiculate, 1-seeded; seeds minutely pubescent or gla- brous. 2n = 14, 28 (two species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Four species. Shrubs 1-2 m tall, stellate pubescent. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades oblong to ovate-lanceolate, sometimes weakly trilobed, cordate, coarsely crenate, discolorous; stipules filiform to very small or absent. Flowers solitary or clustered in the leaf axils; pedicels slender and elongate; involucel absent; calyx ecostulate, often brownish at least at base; petals bluish lavender, white, or orange (the flowers sometimes cleistogamous); androecium pallid, glabrous, filamentiferous at apex, included or exserted, the pollen yellow-orange; styles 8-16, slightly exceeding the androe- cium, the stigmas capitellate. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 8-16, 1-seeded although 2-celled and 3-ovuled; the lower cell indehiscent, reticulate, enclosing a solitary seed, the upper cell empty, dehiscent, the walls smooth and rounded, separating to form wings; seeds subglabrous, pubescent, or scabridulous. 2n = 32 (two species); 2n = 24 (one species).

description: Flowers large, 5-9-merous, solitary or in small lateral clusters; hypanthium broadly hemispheric; calyx ample, at anthesis splitting into, regular or irregular lobes and often eventually deciduous; stamens isomorphic, with short thick filaments and stout rounded anthers, laterally compressed and more or less connivent in a ring, dehiseent by 2 minute terminal pores, the coinective not appendaged or prolonged; ovary completely inferior, 8-15-celled; style short and stout, with a large capitate stigma. Shrubs or trees, frequently of large size, with broad 3-5-pli-nerved leaves and white or pink flowers; the fleshy fruit is edible.

description: Leaves alternate, simple, nanophylls to mesophylls, rarely leptophylls (B. spartioides (Baill.) Müll. Arg.), mostly chartaceous, rarely coriaceous, fleshy or membranaceous, persistent or caducous, mostly elliptic, sometimes oblong, ovate or obovate, rarely narrowly triangular (B. spartioides), symmetrical, sometimes slightly asymmetrical at the base, base and apex acute or sometimes obtuse, margin serrate or crenate, rarely entire, teeth simple or compound, tooth spacing regular or irregular (Fig. 1 A-E); cicatricose-crateriform glands typ- ically present sometimes paired (Fig. 2A; absent in B. sidoides (Klotzsch) Müll. Arg. and B. lagunensis (M. E. Jones) L. C. Wheeler), marginal glands present (Fig. 2B; absent in B. incana C. V. Morton); most of the species with intermediate venation, a few pinnatinerved, agrophic veins usually present; primary vein moderate to stout, rarely weak, straight; secondary venation craspedodromous or semi- craspedodromous, rarely paralellodromous [in B. spartioides (Fig. IE)], with (3-)5 or 6(- 11) pairs of secondary veins with an acute angle of divergence; tertiary veins opposite percurrent, sometimes mixed (opposite and alternate) percurrent; quaternary veins polygonal reticulate; orders of venation 5 or 6, rarely 4; aréoles imperfect, incomplete or rarely absent (Fig. 2C-E); veinlets simple to branched more than twice, rarely absent; ultimate marginal venation with incomplete loops. Midvein and higher order veins with a parenchymatous or sclerified bundle sheath, terminal veinlets naked or rarely sheathed with sclerenchyma; mesophyll dorsiventral, some species with numerous air cavities (e.g., B. macrocarpa A. Cerv. & Flores Olv.), only five species with dispersed fibers (B. corensis (Jacq.) Müll. Arg., B. hirsutissima (Baill.) Müll. Arg., B. pulchella (Baill.) Müll. Arg., B. spartioides, and B. chinantlensis A. Cerv. & Flores Olv.; Fig. 3A- C), with numerous druses in the mesophyll (Fig. 2D, E) and also in the phloem parenchyma, without tannins in spongy parenchyma; epidermis simple, epidermal cells isodiametric in surface view, abaxial anticlinal cell walls straight or undulate; cuticle smooth or striate; stornata mostly abaxial, sometimes also in the adaxial surface, paracytic, guard cells with short or long striations (absent in B. hirsutissima and B. chinantlensis; Fig. 4A-D); densely to sparsely pubescent, trichomes simple or mixed simple/stellate (Fig. 5), rarely absent, papillate or smooth.

description: Epiphytes, rarely terrestrial or rupicolous plants to 60 cm high. Roots cylindrical, white, glabrous. Rhizome rigid, very short to elongate. Pseudobulbs erect, four-angled, pyramidal, compressed, commonly bearing a black ring at the apex, apically unifoliate, and becoming irregularly wrinkled with age. Leaves membranaceous to coriaceous, plicate, lanceolate to oblong, acuminate, and attenuate at the base into a pseudo-petiole. Inflorescence racemose, lateral, erect or pendent, 1-10 flowered. Bracts subtending the inflorescence brownish, membra- naceous to coriaceous, concave, oblong, acuminate at the apex, truncate. Scape bracts are numerous, concentrated at the inflorescence base. Floral bracts are similar in size and form to the scape bracts or smaller. Flowers resupinate, zygomorphic, fragrant or not, of various colors. Sepals 3, concave, ovate, rarely lanceolate or oblong, truncate, rarely attenuate, mucronate. Lateral sepals parallel to each other or divergent, prolonged into a spur, which is fused to the column foot. Petals obovate, rarely rhombic or lanceolate, slightly asymmetric and al- ways smaller than the sepals. Labellum, mobile, callous, entire to 3-lobed, lanceo- late to obovate, attached to the column foot by a straight, rarely recurved claw, the lat- eral lobes involute, the midlobe recurved, rarely straight, glabrous to pubescent, with entire, undulate or crenate margins. Callus extended from the labellum base up to its median region, along the midvein, as a low, thick rib; the anterior region is protuberant, entire to 3-lobed, glabrous to pubescent. Column clavate, fleshy, arcuate, with an attenuate, rarely apiculate, apex, glabrous to pubescent; the basal portion prolonged into a foot, erect to arched, glabrous to pubescent. Anther helmet-shaped, 4-celled, terminal, incumbent, externally papillose. Pollinarium with 2 pairs of asymmetric, super-imposed, flattened, ovate to round pollinia; stipes strap-like, 2, rarely 1; viscidium prominent, basally acute, cuneate or truncate. Stigma concave; ovary sulcate, erect to curved. Capsules erect or pendent, green, with flower segments persistent to dehiscence.

description: Trees 4-30 m tall and to 80 cm in diameter, glabrous, the crown dense and usually rounded. Bark of young trees light gray-brown and smooth, becoming slightly scaly and brownish with characteristic large lighter areas. Twig terete, dark nr aroon when young, becoming light gray with yellowish lenticels; leaf scar triangular with 3 large bundle scars. Leaf evergreen or deciduous, palrnately trifoliate with petiole terete, 2-15 cm long, often maroon and glabrouis; petiolule 1-10 mm long, glabrous. Leaflets firm and coriaceous, extremely variable in size and shape even on the same twig but the 3 leaflets on one leaf essentially similar, 5-22 cm long and 2-10 cm wide, lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate, elliptic, ovate, or obovate; apex acute or acuminate, often with a prolonged caudate tip (or "drip tip"); base acute or acuminate; margins entire; surfaces essentially glabrous, rarely with isolated white hairs, the upper surface shiny, the lower surface dull with midrib and secondary veins maroon; mesophyll traversed by many trichoselereids which have an irregular course, and which originate from the cylinder of selerenchyma surrounding the veins. Inflorescence a terminal, diffuse, many-flowered panicle which is broad and often corymbiform; central axis 5-25 cm long with opposite and decussate branching; lateral branches paniculate, bearing dichasia at the ends and along the sides, or in part monopodial, glabrous or tomentose; leaves subtending the lateral branches may be a slightly reduced form of the regular trifoliate leaf and found at the lower nodes of the inflorescence, or they may be reduced to a small, triangular, and caducous bract. Flowers with pedicels 5-15 mm long, glabrous or tomentose. Calyx red, purple, greenish, or nearly white, glabrous or tomelitose; sepals essentially free, unequal, 3-12 mm long and 2-5 mim wide, oblong-ovate, obtuse, often with short claws and concave, the included portions nearly membranaceous, the exposed portions firm and thick. Corolla brilliant red or white with yellow or pink base, 8-25 mm long; petals 4, occasionally 5, commonly with a pubescent claw of variable length, often compressed, bent and crested at the top of the claw, the upper 2 petals usually narrower and longer than the lateral 2, the fifth petal usually abortive or of variable size when present. Stamens 6-8, ascending, 20-30 mm long, exserted; filaments red or white, glabrous; anthers yellow, glabrous or slightly pubescent, glandular at the apex and base of locules. Disk eccentric, one-sided or rarely annular, trilobed. Fertile pistil glabrous or pubescent, deep rose-red, with an oblong-fusiform ovary and attenuated stipe at the base. Fruit obovoid to oval, 5-8 cm long, 4-6 cm in diameter; pericarp thick, dark brown, unarmed but slightly scaly; seeds usually 1 to 3, 3-5 cm in diameter, dark brown to nearly black with a small pale hilum.

description: Monotypic. Ascending to procumbent subshrubs generally <0.1 m tall, softly stellate-pubescent more or less throughout. Leaf blades 0.5-1.5 cm long, about as wide, cuneiform, dentate to subentire; petioles mostly 2-6 mm long; stipules subequal to the petioles, prominent, persistent, broadly oblanceolate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, subsessile; involucel absent; calyx deeply divided, the lobes narrowly triangular; petals somewhat exceeding the calyx, yellow; androecium pallid, included, filamentiferous at apex, the column pubescent; styles 5, pallid, subequal to petals, the stig- mas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 5, elliptic in cross section, with dorsal keel and apical spine 1-1.5 mm long; seeds solitary, pendulous. 2n = 16.

description: Tufted monoclinous or monoecious perennials (or sometimes annuals), low and much branched (similar to Munroa in having stems with widely spaced internodes, and spur shoots with short crowded internodes, but forming larger clumps), each culm with a remarkable 2-aristate prophyll. Sheaths open; ligules incipient (with minute hairs) or absent; blades rigid, sharp pointed, flat, plicate or convolute. Inflorescences short, dense, few-flowered, somewhat exserted or more commonly exceeded by the sheaths of the 2 subopposite subtending leaves. Spikelets laterally compressed, subsessile or shortly pedicellate; glumes almost equal, 1-nerved, membranous, hyaline; rachilla disarticulating above the glumes, but not between the 4 florets; only the third floret fructiferous (with a perfect or pistillate flower), the 2 basal flowers staminate or sterile (in the latter case with or without staminodes), and the fourth distal floret abortive. Lemmas 3-nerved, 3-cleft, the 2 basal ones with deeper incisions, the central segment of each aristate, the 2 lateral mucronate; third lemma 3-aristate; fourth lemma reduced to a 3-awned plumose or hairy rudiment. Paleas nearly as long as the lemmas, much reduced in the neutral florets. Lodicules lacking. Flowers perfect or imperfect; stamens 3 or 2 or exceptionally only 1; staminate flowers sometimes with a tiny pistillode; pistillate flowers with minute staminodes; neutral florets reduced to the empty bracts, occasionally with a pistillode; gynoecium with 2 long styles; stigmata almost smooth, scarcely papillate. Caryopsis laterally compressed; hilum linear, basal, very short.
bibliographicCitation: Hunziker, Armando T. & Anton, Ana M. 1979. A synoptical revision of Blepharidachne (Poaceae). Brittonia. 31: 446-453.

description: Caulescent annual herbs, the mature stems covered with conspicuously exfoliating rhytidome; cotyledons glabrous, rounded, their narrow base tardily elongating; leaves subsessile, the lowest glabrous, opposite, and narrowly connate at the base, the remainder spirally arranged and usually pubescent. Inflorescence erect, each flower borne in the axil of a bract more or less similar to the foliage leaves. Hypanthium evident, short or elongate. Sepals 4, erect. Petals 4, deeply emarginate, purplish or pinkish to white. Stamens 8, the episepalous inserted at the mouth of the hypanthium, the epipetalous ones with shorter filainents often inserted below its summit; anthers versatile, attached near the base in small-flowered species; pollen shed in tetrads. Stigma 4-lobed, the inner surface of the lobes invested with short trichomes, or capitate. Ovary 4-loculate. Capsules brownish at maturity, usually slightly torulose, sessile, tardily loculicidal, terete to quadrangular in transection, each valve with a strong brown rib down its center. Partitions between locules partly adnate to the valves at dehiscence, partly to one another forming a 4-winged central column which readily disintegrates except in B. densiflora. Seeds very finely papillose, dark brown, with a conspicuous pellucid ridge at the chalazal end and a smaller pale ridge near the micropyle, somewhat flattened or very narrowly winged. Gametic chromosome numbers, n = 9, 10, 15, 19.

description: Caespitose perennials with erect or decumbent-spreading culms, rounded sheaths and flat blades. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, the spikelets on few to several spicate primary branches, these moderately rebranched in species with large panicles. Pedicels and upper rachis joints with a central groove or membranous area, this most strikingly developed in New World species. Sessile spikelet of a pair fertile and awned, more or less triangular in outline, the first glume dorsally flattened, the second glume with a medial keel. Pedicelled spikelet staminate or sterile, usually well-developed but tending to be more reduced in New World species. Disarticulation in the rachis, the sessile spikelet falling attached to a rachis joint and pedicel.
bibliographicCitation: Gould, Frank W. 1967. The Grass Genus Andropogon in the United States. Brittonia. 19: 70-76.

description: Five species. Herbs or subshrubs 0.5-1.5 m tall, usually with a single erect stem, branching only in the inflorescence, more or less soft-pubescent with stellate and simple hairs. Leaves long-petiolate below to sessile and amplexicaul above (immediately below the inflorescence), the blades broadly ovate, sometimes somewhat lobulate, deeply cordate, serrate to undulate (or even subentire), acute or acuminate. Inflorescence a leafless terminal spike or panicle, the flowers generally subtended by small trifid bractlets; involucel absent; calyx 5-lobed, small; petals yellow; androecium included, pallid, filamentiferous at apex; styles 5-14, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic but pseudocapsular, strigose or glabrate; mericarps 5-14, 2-celled (or upper cell vestigial in the type species), the cells divided by a simple endoglossum, the lower cell 1-seeded, the upper cell 1-2 seeded; seeds more or less pubescent. 2n = 14 (one species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Relatively small plants to ca 2 cm tall in dense, dull, dark-green mats. Primary stems creeping, freely but irregularly branched; secondary stems erect to ascending, branching in clusters, curved when dry, attenuate; diminutive central strand present, with thick-walled pigmented cells surrounding larger, thinner-walled cells; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia broadly foliose, tightly enclosing lateral buds proximal on stems. Leaves ovate-triangular, short-acuminate, sometimes ± obtuse and apiculate, usually recurved below on one or both sides, serrate above, the teeth reflexed toward leaf apices, decurrent; costa single, strong, homogeneous in transverse section, bulging abaxially, sinuose above, decurrent, reaching ca4/5 of leaf length; upper cells subquadrate, rhomboidal or short rectangular, firm-walled, smooth; alar cells transversely elongate; basal juxtacostal cells larger, rectangular. Dioicous. Perichaetial paraphyses few, from shorter than to reaching archegonial apices. Sporophytes and male plants unknown.

description: Gramina perennia dioicia, humilia, valde stolonifera; culmis ad 15 cm longis, [male] erectis, [female] plerumque prostratis; vaginis artis; ligula ad lineam pilorum brevium reducta; laminis planis vel plus minusve laxe-involutis, apice subattenuatis, micro- pilis bicellulariis epidermidis foliorum lineariis; racemis plerumque 3 (saepe 2, raro 1), [male] persistentibus, [female] facile deciduis, rectis vel plus minusve arcuatis; spiculis subsessilibus, pectinatis, 2-seriatis uno latere rhacheos racemi. Spicula masculina: gluma prima subulata, 1-nervo, 1/3-1/2 spicula breviore; gluma secunda latiore, lemmati circiter aequa, plerumque 1-nervo sed saepe valde 2-3-nervis; lemmate membranacea, 3-nervis, apice minute triaristulata; staminibus 3, pistillo abortivo vel nullo; flosculis rudimentariis nullis vel interdum ad unam vel paucas aristas reductis. Spicula feminea: gluma prima angusta, 1-nervo, 1/3 - 1/4 breviore quam gluma secunda, ipsa gluma secunda late lanceolata, lemmati aequa, valde 2-5-nervis; lemmate cartilaginea, 3-nervis, apice brevi triaristata; palea lemmati subaequa, minute biaristata; caryopside anguste elliptica, embryone caryopside subaequo, flosculis rudimentariis plerumque 3, ad airistas scabras reductis, circiter bis glumis longiores. Lodiculis spiculorum ce et 9 similibus, truncatis auriculatis, et compluribus nervis.

description: Low shrub. Time of opening of flowers unknown. Petals rose-purple. Anthers versatile. Sporogfenous tissue continuous. Stigma hemispherical. Capsules 2-seeded, imbedded in long chains in the axis of the stem but distinct from one another. Chromosome number, n = 11 (Raven, unpubl.). Compatibility system unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Raven, Peter H. 1964. The generic subdivision of Onagraceae, tribe Onagreae. Brittonia. 16: 276-288.

description: Plants terrestrial. Rhizomes erect or decumbent, dictyostelic, usually mucilaginous, the apices and petiole bases scaly, the scales lanceolate, shiny, the margins with 1-3 rows of brown or black cells and similarly colored bifid teeth. Leaves fasciculate, to 2.5 m, usually partially dimorphous, the fertile leaves usually with longer petioles and narrower pinnae and more erect habit than the sterile leaves, adult leaves entire to 1-pinnate-pinnatifid, juvenile leaves simple and entire to 1-pinnate-lobate. Petioles with two pneumatophores on each side. Leaf axes sulcate adaxially, on the abaxial surfaces with catenate, tawny to ferruginous hairs (at least in the neotropical species with anastomosing veins). Rachises alate in the distal third, without buds (neotropical species) or buds present in the axils of the pinnae (a few paleotropical species). Pinna stalks (if present) not winged adaxially (except in C. andina). Laminae tapering gradually to a pinnatifid apex or conform (i.e., like the lateral pinnae) in a few paleotropical species, shiny on the adaxial surface, the abaxial surface scaly, the scales lanceolate to elliptic, usually with bifid, black, marginal teeth, the abaxial surface between veins scaly, with or without catenate hairs. Veins free or anastomosing. Sori diplazioid or (in C. rivalis and C. chocoensis) asplenioid, linear, indusiate, the indusium typically membranaceous. Sporangia stalks with 2 rows of cells; annular cells 12-18. Spores monolete. x = 41.

description: Nine species. Annual or perennial herbs or sometimes subshrubs, glabrate, stellate pubescent, or hispid, erect or procumbent, the perennials often with a fleshy rootstock. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades orbicular in outline (and more or less palmately dissected) or triangular and crenate; stipules lanceolate to broadly auriculate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, in erect species often aggregated into terminal inflores- cences; pedicels usually greatly exceeding the subtending leaves; involucel present or absent, the bracts (when present) 3, linear to spatulate; calyx deeply 5-lobed, usually costate; petals showy, often distally erose or fimbriate, deep red or burgundy to pink or almost white; androecium included, yellow- ish, antheriferous at apex; styles 10-28, the stigmatic zone introrsely decurrent. Fruits schizocarpic, oblate; mericarps 10-28, sub- reniform, laterally reticulate and dorsally smooth or rugose, sometimes beaked, in- dehiscent, glabrous or strigose; seeds soli- tary, glabrous. 2n = 28, 30, and sometimes higher polyploids (Bates et al., 1989).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Trees (rarely shrubs), sometimes canopy trees, a few species with small buttresses; bark often exfoliating in long stripes; wood white and very hard. Stipules interpetiolar, free or connate at base, caducous. Blades elliptic, ovate to obovate, obtuse to acuminate at apex. Inflorescences terminal, corymbiform to paniculate, with lateral branches terminating in cymules. Flowers protandrous, often with two small membranous bracts including (or not including) the flowers. Calyx truncate to reduced to minute teeth, persistent; calyx lobes 5 or 6(8); in a few species, one lobe expanded into a cream to yellowish white calycophyll, in some of the flowers. Corolla funnelform to campanuliform and deeply lobed; corolla tube narrowly funnelform; corolla lobes (4)5-6(8), aestivation contorted to narrowly imbricate. Stamens alternate to the petals and exserted; anthers button-shaped, dorsi fixed, dehiscing by lateral slits; filaments attached on the upper part of the tube, very slender, glabrous throughout or with a tuft of pilose to villous hairs at base. Style exserted; style branches opening after complete maturity of the anthers, long, reflexed at maturity. Ovary 2-celled, placentation imbricate, narrowly obovate. Capsules ob- ovoid to narrowly obovoid, slightly laterally compressed, dehiscing septicidally; disk-loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules of some species. Seeds elliptic, with bipolar wing. Pollen tricolporate; exine densely reticulate.

description: Monotypic. Erect well-branched shrubs, with minute stellate pubescence. Leaves petiolate, the blades <4 cm long, ovate to hastately or palmately lobed, coarsely serrate, acute, discolorous, minutely stellate pubescent, more densely so beneath than above; stipules ligulate, 1-2 mm wide. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, slender, the pedicels subequal to the subtending leaf; involucellar bracts 3, broadly cordate- ovate, entire, minutely stellate-pubescent, surpassing and concealing the calyx; calyx deeply 5-parted; petals red (drying purplish), subequal to the involucel, biauriculate at base, the small auriculae densely bearded; androecium subequal to the petals, the column basally hirsute, the anthers orange; styles 13-14, purple, slightly exceeding the column, the stigmas truncate. Fruits schizocarpic, stellate-pubescent, 5 mm diam., oblate; mericarps 13-14, indehiscent, circular and dorsally rugulose (resembling Urocarpidium), minutely puberulent; seeds solitary, reniform, glabrous. 2n = 10
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Perennial herbs, sometimes slightly woody at base. Flowers openi near sunset. Petals yellow, often fading reddish. Aiithers versatile. Sporogenous tissue divided into packets in each locule. Stigma peltate or very shallowly and broadly 4-lobed, the receptive surface inside. Capsule many-seeded. Basic chromlosome number, x = 7. Self-incompatibility known.
bibliographicCitation: Raven, Peter H. 1964. The generic subdivision of Onagraceae, tribe Onagreae. Brittonia. 16: 276-288.

description: Monotypic. Shrubs, the stems reddish, minutely stellate pubescent distally, the hairs ferruginous, glabrescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades elliptic, 3(5)-nerved, truncate to cuneate, basally entire, distally weakly serrate, acute to subobtuse, discolorous, minutely stellate-pubescent (sparsely so above, densely so beneath); stipules falcate, 6-9 mm long, pubescent. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicel to 5.5 cm long, subequal to subtending leaf, stellate-pubescent, with a small, medial (deciduous) bract; involucel a unitary structure (with an apical pore), completely enclosing the young bud, sparsely and minutely stellate-pubescent, torn open by the developing bud and flower leaving irregular remnants at the base of the calyx at anthesis; calyx 2.5 cm long, ca. half-divided, the lobes 1 cm wide, hirsute (hairs 3 mm); corolla rose lavender, 4 cm long, externally glabrous, stellate-pubescent and hirsute on claw; an- droecium half the length of the corolla, filamentiferous at apex, the anthers numerous, the column hirsute; styles 45, slender, the stigmas capitate. Fruits unknown [the ovary hirsute]. Chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Annual or perennial herbs, sometimes slightly woody. Flowers open near sunrise, or more rarely in the late afternoon. Petals yellow, rose-purple, or white. Anthers versatile or basifixed. Sporogenous tissue continuous. Stigma capitate. Capsule many-seeded. Basic chromosome number, x = 7. Self-incompatibility known.
bibliographicCitation: Raven, Peter H. 1964. The generic subdivision of Onagraceae, tribe Onagreae. Brittonia. 16: 276-288.

description: Essentially glabrous shrubs or small trees with numerous highly flexible, leafless, pale green, alternate branches nearly all ending in stout thorns and having minute, shallow, elegantly parallel, longitudinal grooves with the whitish waxy coating alter- nately thicker and thinner, leaving rows of white dots visible under a lens. Leaves represented merely by a few widely spaced caducous deltoid scales 1-2 mm long; stipules apparently absent; cladophylls minute, darkly pigmented, with marginal dark papillose glands, closely clustered at the axils and forming the usually roughly deltoid "gland-fields" (Sargent, 1890; Airy Shaw, 1965) subtending the lateral branches (the base of each branch being ringed by a blackish glandular zone varying in width but usually widest toward the younger internode). Inflorescences lateral, short, cymose or thyrsoid, few-flowered; bractlets numerous, minute, deltoid, each with a few dark stalked glands marginally; pedicels articulate below the middle, 1-2 mm long. Flowers small, radially symmetrical, bisexual, hypogynous; sepals 5, imbricate in bud, roundly to narrowly deltoid, 1 mm long and wide, acute, firm, round-keeled, marginally thinner and with scattered, minute, translucent, stalked glands, tending to persist after anthe- sis; petals 5, free, imbricate in bud, alternate with sepals, oblong to narrowly obovate, slightly fleshy medially, greenish white to yellowish white, indistinctly keeled ventrally, ascending at first, in anthesis in the distal moiety spreading, deciduous promptly after anthesis; stamens 5, alternate with and slightly shorter than the petals, the filaments subulate, gently tapered the full length, inflexed in bud but nearly erect at anthesis, strongly dorsiventrally compressed, whitish, tending to persist at base of fruit; anthers obcordate, 1.2 mm long and wide, each of the 2 thecae oblong, obliquely and individu- ally attached to the adaxial side of the narrow, tapering, laminar connective, completely 2-celled, both cells opening simultaneously by septicidal, longitudinal dehiscence; pollen said to be "3-horned" when moist (Gray, 1877); ovary 1, superior, at an early stage with a conspicuously thickened (but neither glandular nor nectariferous) gyno- base, above this 5-locular, the locules subincomplete (fide Baillon, 1875, 1876) and opposite the petals; style slender, columnar, 2-3 mm long, at apex with 5 deltoid lobes opposite the stamens, ca. 0.2 mm long, stigmatic on the adaxial surface medially; placentas axile, each locule about at the middle bearing 2-6 amphitropous, horizontal ovules in roughly 2 rows. Capsule 5-locular (the upper third constituting a beak), woody, double-walled, dark brown or blackish, splitting (starting at apex) septicidally nearly the full length and subsequently each carpid splitting nearly its full length ventrally and in the beak region also dorsally, the parts persistent for a year or more on the torus, eventually all deciduous except for 5 more or less coalescent columellalike placentas. Seeds 1 or rarely 2 per cell, hard, brownish, oblong, ca. 7-8 mm long, attached medially, much compressed laterally; endosperm thin, fleshy; embryo straight; cotyledons flat, oval; radicle short, inferior.

description: Shrubs or small trees, or rarely scramblers or lianas, densely grayish stellate-tomentose throughout. Leaves 4-10 x 4-10 cm, broadly ovate or ovate-cordate to subrotund or reniform, slenderly petioled, thinly to firmly coriaceous, evergreen to semi-deciduous, with 4-6 main lateral nerves on each side of the midrib, yet at the base of the leaf blade (sub)palmately veined. Flowers few to c. 20, in short, open corymbiform racemes or rarely solitary; calyx uniseriate, reduplicatevalvate, somewhat quadrangular, with a closed aestivation enclosing the flower bud until near anthesis; corolla lemon-yellow or orange; stamens 4-8 (including the 1 to 4 staminodes in C. tweediana). Fruits dehiscent (indehiscent in C. yunckeri?), ovoid to globose, baccate, with thin to leathery but soft and flexible fruit wall; seeds 2-20 plus, small, surrounded by a white to yellowish or orange, fleshy, pulp-derived, hair-infiltrated sarcotesta (Fig. 1); seeds cochleate-reniform, ovoid to round, with a deep seed cleft open only at the mouth, the smooth, coriaceous testa densely covered with many slender, unbranched, unicellular hairs embedded in pulp; embryo snow-white, the cotyledons foliaceous, with one cotyledon involute, the other convolute; they embrace each other half way with half of each one inside the other's fold; embryo axis curved, with only the root apex uncovered. (Observation of hairs, testa, embryo, etc. based in part Franceschini & Tressens 2004: 212, for C. tweediana; Fig. 1A-F).

description: Leaves alternate, simple, notophylls to mesophylls, coriaceous, persistence unknown, oblong, symmetrical, base and apex acute, margin entire; cicatricose-crateriform glands present, sometimes paired; venation pinnatinerved, agrophic veins absent; primary vein stout, straight; secondary venation brochidodromous, with 6-8 pairs of secondary veins with an acute angle of divergence; tertiary veins opposite percurrent; quaternary veins polygonal reticulate; orders of venation 5, aréoles imperfect; veinlets simple or branched more than twice; ultimate marginal venation looped. Midvein and higher order veins with the bundle sheath sclerified, terminal veinlets naked or with sclerenchymatous sheath cells; with dispersed fibers, with tannins and numerous druses in the mesophyll; epidermal cells isodiametric in adaxial surface view, abaxial anticlinal cell undulate; stornata in the abaxial surface, paracytic, guard cells without striations; glabrous.

description: Shrub, stems one to several from thick woody caudex, or vine or shrub with scandent branches; thickly hairy with yellowish green hairs, to glabrate. Leaves alternate, entire, broadly ovate-elliptic. Flowers bisexual, in large terminal or supra-axillary loose umbelliform panicles. Calyx 6-5-parted, segments almost as long as petals; petals 6-5, oblong-lanceolate, fleshy, valvate, tomentose inside, sericeous-hirsute outside, recurved, stamens 6-5, filaments glabrous, anthers ovoid-oblong, dorsifixed, introrsely dehiscent, connective acute, extended be- yond the loculi; ovary ovoid, sessile, thickly hairy, 1 -locular, ovules 2, pendulous, collateral, style 1 rarely 2-3, short, thickly filiform, stigma small, capitate, m/l distinctly 3-lobed. Fruit an ovoid drupe, thickly hairy, exocarp coriaceous, endocarp woody; smooth but densely tomentose inside. Seed 1, pendulous, with thin testa. 7 spp. trop. S. America.

description:
Reportedly suffruticose ? 6 dm, the root unknown, wholly glabrous except for randomly setose-ciliate stipules and leaflets and for appressed-puberulent pedicels and outer face of petals, the stems, petioles and pedicels prominently ribbed, the ample 2-foliolate, reticulately veiny concolorous leaflets pallid-glaucescent.

Stipules stiffly erect, linear-acuminate +/- 10 mm, commonly 3-nerved, charged toward tip with a few fine spreading setae 2-2.5 mm.

Leaves 5-8.5 (-?) cm; pulvinus and pulvinules ellipsoid 3-3.5 mm, wrinkled when dry; petiolar gland 1, erect from between the pulvinules, narrowly ovoid-fusiform 3-3.5 X 1-1.4 mm, purplish; leaflets tilted backward from tip of petiole, turned half face-to-face, to bring the midrib to horizontal, the plane, stiffly chartaceous blades in outline obliquely reniform obtuse, minutely mucronulate, 2.5-5.5 x 5.3-6.6 cm, at base broadly flabellate or truncate, from base 5-nerved by the straight midrib and on its broad side 3, on its narrow side 1 short, incurved-ascending primary nerves, the midrib thence penniveined with 5-8 p,airs of major obliquely ascending secondary veins camptodromous well within the sharp cartilaginous margin, these all again branched into a prominent quaternary reticulum of venules prominulous on both faces.

Peduncles from upper leaf-axils 1-3.5 cm, at apex 2-flowered; bracts broadly subulate +/- 2mm; pedicels at anthesis 1+, in fruit to 2.5 (-?) cm; sepals firmly herbaceous glabrous oblong-obovate obtuse to 8-9.5 mm, from base coarsely 4-6- nerved, the nerves branched distally; petals (presumably yellow) when dry pinkish- brown, subappressed-puberulent dorsally, all broadly obovate and contracted into a narrow claw +/- 2 mm, the vexillum deeply emarginate at apex, 20 x 11 mm, the rest obtuse, slightly longer, the 2 lateral plane, the 2 abaxial concave, enveloping the 3 long stamens; androecium 10-merous of 3 adaxial staminodia 5 mm, 4 intermediate fertile stamens each consisting of short stout filament and forwardly directed thecae 6.5-8 X 2 mm, and 3 abaxial fertile ones with filament +/- 6 mm and incurved thecae 10.5-12 x 2 mm, the 7 fertile all contracted at apex into a biporose beak +/- 0.4 mm; ovary strigulose; style strigulose, +/- 8 mm, slightly dilated and incurved at apex

Pod when half formed narrowly linear +/- 13 cm, the sutures already becoming prominent, probably subquadrangular when mature.

description: More or less thorny or spiny shrubs or small trees with simple alternate leaves mostly less than 5 cm. long;-flowers solitary or few together in the axils; dioecious; sepals 4, or sometimes 5, united at the base; petals 4, or sometimes 5, distinct; stamens about twice as many as the petals, in the pistillate flowers reduced and non-functional; gynophore short and broad; carpels 4 or sometimes 5, weakly unite&, wanting in the staminate flowers; styles joined at the base into a short broad column; stigmas linear, divergent or recurved; ovules solitary in the carpels; fruit of several distinct drupes.

description: Hypanthium ovoid or hemispheric, the calyx closed and conic in bud, deciduous as a calyptra at anthesis; petals large and showy; sta- mens isomorphic; anthers subulate, usually more or less arcuate, the connective briefly prolonged at base, bearing a dorsal spur directed forward, with or without a second posterior basal spur directed back- ward; ovary 3-many-celled, with a stout style. Trees or shrubs, often densely pubescent, with coriaceous leaves and panicled flowers.

description: Shrubs or small trees, with hard, dark-colored wood, rigid, terete branches, and short lateral, spur-like branchlets conspicuously roughened by the crowded scars of fallen leaves. Leaves alternate, simple; serrate, crenate, or entire- margined; short-petioled, evergreen, or tardily deciduous. Stipules 1-10 mm. long, the longer distal portion free, acute, brown-scarious-margined, with a hairy mid- rib, caducous or deciduous, the proximal portion adnate to the petiole, green, per- sistent. Flowers axillary or terminal on short branchlets, solitary or fasciculate, sessile or short-pedicellate, the pedicels sometimes lengthening before maturity of the fruit. Floral tube elongate, cylindrical, usually somewhat enlarged below, persistent; abruptly widening above into a turbinate or campanulate deciduous limb. Sepals 5, broadly to narrowly triangular. Petals none. Stamens 1045, never a definite number, inserted in two or three rows on the limb of the calyx; filaments subulate or filiform, distinct, glabrous; anthers subrotund or broadly elliptic, emarginate at both ends, affixed dorsally above the base, longitudinally de- hiscent, glabrous or hairy. Pistil 1, inserted in the bottom of the floral tube, free; ovary cylindric-fusiform, sessile, one-celled; style terminal, elongate, silky-plumose, exserted; stigma entire, terminal, subclavate, minute. Ovule soli- tary, affixed above the base, ascending, subcylindrical. Fruit cylindric-fusiform, sericeous, tailed by the elongated persistent bent or twisted silky-plumose style, entirely or about two-thirds included in the persistent floral tube. Testa membra- naceous. Seed cylindric; cotyledons linear, elongate; hypocotyl very short; endo- sperm none. (Cercocarpus from KERKOS tail, and KARPOS fruit, referring to the peculiar long-tailed fruit.)
bibliographicCitation: Martin, Floyd L. 1950. A revision of Cercocarpus. Brittonia. 7: 91-111.

description: Hypanthium campanulate; sepals triangular, acute; petals obovate, 8 mm. long; stamens isomorphic, the connective very briefly prolonged and not appendaged; ovary 4-celled. description: Lianas or slender shrubs or trees, usually with the upper branches scandent, glabrous throughout or essentially so, copiously branching, the branches and branchlets opposite; leaves opposite, petiolate; inflorescence axillary, replete throughout with mucilaginous fibers, thyrsoid or corymbose or cymose, the branchlets dichotomously forked, subtended by small bracts; flowers often congested, usually solitary in the ultimate dichotomies or paired or ternate at ends of ultimate inflorescence-branchlets, small; sepals 5 (rarely 4), narrowly imbricate, semiorbicular to deltoid or ovate, often erosulous or fimbriolate at margins; petals 5 (rarely 3, 4, or 6), narrowly imbricate, often thincarnose, usually rounded at apex and entire; disk discontinuous, forming 3 (5 in group Anomala) (rarely 4) saccate carnose staminiferous lips, the lips confluent with the base of the ovary; stamens the same number as disk-lips and inserted within them, ascending or slightly divergent, often small and hardly exceeding the ovary at anthesis; filaments often slightly enilarged toward apex; anthers small, transversely ellipsoid or reniforni-oblong, broader than long, basifixed but extrorsely nutant, the locules 2, dehiscing by horizontal confluent extrorse (apical) clefts; ovary subglobose, trigonous (pentagonous in group Anomala), flattened at the truncate apex or sometimes shallowly depressed, concave on sides, rounded at angles, the stigmas strictly sessile, 3 (5 in group Anomala) (rarely 4), adnate to summnit of ovary, radiating, linear or oblong or deltoid, enitire or emarginate or bilobed, minutely free at apices, opposite the stamens, alternate with the locules; locules 3 (5 in group Anomala) (rarely 4), the ovules 2 or 4 per locule, usually attached to upper portion of interior angles, collateral or superposed or in superposed pairs; fruits small or medium in size, essentially subglobose, the pericarp coriaceous, the dissepiments soon evanescent, the seeds 2-6, imbedded in mucilaginous pulp, oblong, angled.

description: Dioecious, perennial herbs, subshrubs, or shrubs, 5-50 cm tall. Leaves alternate, subsessile to petiolate, entire to dentate. Capitulescences of solitary capitula, borne on distal branchlets or scapose-pedunculate, rarely weakly cymose. Capitula homoga- mous; involucres campanulate, phyllaries uniseriate, monoor dimorphic, subimbricate; receptacle plane, alveolate, glabrous; corollas tubular, actinomorphic, 5-lobed, 10-nerved; functionally staminate florets with anthers sagittate; styles bifid, the branches apically rounded to broadly triangular, dorsally papillose; achenes sterile; functionally pistillate florets with rudimentary or aborted anthers; styles bifid, the branches apically rounded, dorsally papil- lose; achenes fertile, cylindrical, costate, glabrous or occasionally pubescent with trichomes; pappus of capillary bristles, uniseriate, apically slender or clavate, acute to rounded. Achenes cylindrical, costate, glabrous or villous with trichomes 130-185 µm long; pappus white or purple to brown. Chromosome number: 2n = 20.

description: Trees, often canopy trees; bole irregular, with or without buttresses; buttresses sometimes very large, especially in the Amazonian species; bark smooth to deeply fissured; wood yellow and very hard. Stipules interpetiolar, free or connate at base, persistent or caducous. Blades elliptic to ovate to obovate, usually acuminate at apex; doma- tia absent, or tuft of hairs [tuft-pit domatia in C. jamaicensis (Urb.) Steyerm.]. Inforescences axillary on terminal nodes, corymbose and with opposite to subopposite lateral branches terminating in cymules. Flowers protogynous, sessile to pedicellate, very fragrant; hypanthium obconical to turbinate. Calyx extremely reduced, truncate or with barely distinguishable lobes, persistent; calyx lobes 4 or 5(6); one lobe expanded into a white to greenish white ca- lycophyll in a few species (C. brevipes and C. gentryana), in some of the flowers. Corolla funnelform and deeply lobed, with reflexed lobes, white, greenish white or cream-white; corolla tube funnelform to ciatiform, with a ring of pubescent hairs inside on the tube or on the base of the lobes; corolla lobes 4 or 5(6); aestivation narrowly imbricate, superficially resembling valvate aestivation. Stamens exserted; anthers but- ton-shaped to elliptic, dorsifixed, dehiscing by lateral slits; filaments attached on the upper part of the tube, slender and basally flattened, with a tuft of pilose to villous hairs at base. Style exserted; style branches pro- truding above corolla before anthesis, short, rounded to ovate, reflexed at maturity. Ovary 2-celled, placentation peltate on the septum, turbinate to obovate. Capsules globose, oblong or obovoid, dehiscing septicidally; disk-loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules of some species. Seeds sub- orbicular, margin undulate, and with a narrow concentric wing. Pollen tricolporate; exine densely reticulate.

description: Plantae fruticosae, cirris axillaribus apice biramosis scandentes, habitu Serjaniarum et Paulliniarum, succo lacteo foetae; rami thyrsigeri striato-sulcati, glabrescentes; corpus lignosum compositum e corpore centrali majore et periphericis minoribus 3 triangulariter dis- positis. Folia biternata; foliola ovalia vel subrotunda, apice obtusa vel breviter obtuseque acuminata, ter- minali basi longius attenuato, lateralia in petiolum brevem contracta vel subsessilia, omnia integerrima vel raridenticulata, chartaceo-coriacea, supra subtus- que glaberrima vel puberula; venatio brochidodroma; petiolus communis rhachisque nuda; stipulae minutae, deltoideo-ovatae. Thyrsi robusti, solitarii, pedunculati, dense flavo-puberuli; bractae bracteolaeque parvae, filiformi-subulatae. Flores ut in Serjania et Paullinia, magni, longe pedicellati, sepalis extus flavotomentosis, tertio et quinto fere omnino liberis. Fructus tricoccus, exalatus, subsessilis, subapiculatus, extus tomentosus; cocci trigono-globosi, indehiscentes; carpophorum vestigiale in pedicello haud persistens; loculi monospermi, dissepimentis latioribus, maturi septicide secedentes, intus tomentosi. Semina exalbuminosa, basi interno inserta, testa crustacea fusca laevi glabra, hilo lato basilari; embryo curvatus, oleoso-carnosus; cotyledones ut in Serjania, exterior incurva, interior biplicata.

description: Meristems anauxotelic, RGUs either of long shoots or short shoots and thus dimorphic, both shoot-systems floriferous, though the former only their first year; partial inflorescences of both systems metameric, some of them on long-shoots only modified into persistent axillary thorns; axillary branch-buds proleptic. description: Twenty-five species. Perennial herbs or subshrubs (sometimes shrubs) with procumbent, ascending, or erect stems, gla- brous or pubescent, more or less gland-dotted throughout. Leaves petiolate, the blades linear, elliptic, digitately divided, or reni- form, entire or serrate, pubescent to glabrous, with or (in American species) without adaxial foliar nectaries; stipules subulate or lanceolate to foliaceous and clasping. Flowers solitary or sympodial in the leaf axils; pedicels with or without trimerous involucellar nectaries at apex; involucel of ca. 9 bractlets, sometimes reduced to 3 by lateral connation, sometimes absent; calyx 5-lobed, usually more or less promi- nently gland-dotted; corolla yellow (sometimes nearly white), pink, or purple, with or without a dark basal spot; androecium in- cluded, apically 5-dentate, the column pallid or dark red; style single, sometimes divided apically; stigmas 3(5), capitate or decurrent. Capsules usually 3-locular, glabrous or pubescent; seeds densely sericeous to minutely puberulent, several per locule. 2n = 20 for ten American species; 2n = 22 for four African species.

description: Pistillate inflorescence axillary to hornotinous leaves, simply racemose, the axis and short peduncle together ±1 µm; fruiting pedicels ±2.5 cm, clavate at apex; drupe 1 per flower, elevated on and disjointing from one arm of a tripartite, vertically wrinkled carpophore nearly 1 cm tall, plumply oblong-obovoid ±45- 50 x 28 x 33 mm, densely minutely velutino-tomentellous externally, the exocarp and endocarp both ligneous, the former 2.5-3 mm, the latter 1-1.5 mm thick, separated one from another by a layer of thin, when dry flaky pulp ±1.5 mm thick, the inner face of the cavity transversely venulose but unarmed; embryo vermiform, embedded in a massive U-shaped body of laminated endosperm bent around a subvertical vanelike condyle.

description: Annual herbs. Flowers open after sunrise and are mostly strongly protandrous, the stigma often not opening for one or even two days. Stigma 4-lobed, the receptive surface ilnside. Capsule many-seeded. Basic chromosome numbers, x = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. All species self-compatible.

description: Shrubs or small trees, with a conspicuous single stem or profusely branched at soil level; stems terete or angled, or striate, glabrous or strigose. Leaves opposite, sessile or petiolate; blades narrow-lanceolate to broad-ovate, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, 5-50 X 2.5-40 cm, bases attenuate, rounded, or cordate, apices acute, obtuse, or mucronate, margins serrate, serrulate, finely irregularly serrate, dentate-serrate, crenate, or erose, surfaces pilose, strigose, or glabrous, with veins sometimes prominent on abaxial surfaces. Capitulescences cymose, thyrsoid, or paniculiform, capitula organized in open clusters or dense terminal or axillary glomerules, branching opposite, subtending bracts decreasing in size near capitula. Capitula to 600(-819), heterogamous, with peripheral pistillate florets and central functionally staminate florets, sessile or on short peduncles; involucres cupulate or funnelform (occasionally subglobose), phyllaries 2-6, imbricate, subequal, coriaceous; phyllaries ovate or orbicular, 5-12-veined, apices obtuse, acute, or mucronate, upper one-third of margin mostly ciliate; paleae subtending pistillate florets often resembling phyllaries, ovate or orbicular, 3-9-veined; paleae subtending staminate florets (sometimes absent) membranaceous, lanceolate, 1-3-veined, with upper one-third of margin ciliate. Pistillate florets 3-40, usually uniseriate, less often multiseriate, fertile; corollas white or yellow, tubular, 2-4 lobed; styles bifid, with strong marginal stigmatic lines; pappus usually absent, sometimes of tufts of short hairs (C. anceps) or two short awns (C. sylvestre). Staminate florets same number or fewer than pistillate florets, corollas tubular, white, with 5 triangular lobes; anthers black; style undivided. Cypselae obovoid, compressed, biconvex, brown-black. Staminate florets 3-24, corollas white, tubular, 4-5-lobed; anthers pur- plish or black, sagittate at base; styles undivided; ovaries sterile, linear, with a 5- lobed nectary at style base, pilose at apex, pappus absent. Chromosome number, x =16 (Stuessy & Arriagada, 1993).

description: Hypanthium campanulate to tubular or urceolate; sepals triangular or oblong to obsolete, almost invariably with conspicuous exterior teeth which often far exceed them; petals small or minute, obtuse; stamens isomorphic or nearly so, the anthers linear or subulate, the connective not or only minutely prolonged at base, simple or rarely gibbous or short-spurred at base; ovary inferior, mostly 3-5-celled; stigma punctiform to capitellate. description: Perennials, cespitose, short-stemmed, semi-herbaceous. Leaves essentially distichous; leaf sheaths persistent, open down the ventral side from the mouth nearly or quite to the base; leaf blades eventually deciduous by the formation of an abscission zone at the juncture of the blade and sheath; ligule graminioid, consisting of a more or less ciliate band of tissue across the base of the leaf blade. Flowering culms essentially erect, axillary but appearing as if terminal; inflorescences paniculiform, composed of several-numerous clusters of pedicellate spikes borne in the axils of leaf-like bracts; spikes composed entirely of bisexual spikelets, or some of the lower spikelets entirely staminate. Bisexual spikelets 2-3- flowered, consisting of a solitary pistillate flower sessile at the base of a 1-2-flowered spikelet-like cluster of staminate flowers; staminate spikelets similar, usually 2-flowered; glumes in both sorts of spikelets 4-5. Staminate flowers composed of 1-3 stamens subtended by a single glume; filaments elongated, persistent; anthers linear, the connective prolonged beyond the thecae as a minute mucro. Pistillate flowers consisting of a single pistil subtended by a pair of glumes; style short or obsolete, the 3 elongated and eventually deciduous stigmas usually sessile on the apex of the pistil. Achenes thin-walled, trigonous in cross-section, narrowly oblong-ovoid, more or less wing-margined at least above the middle. Perianth composed of a hypogynous ring of simple or short-branched hairs or bristles (see map, fig. 1, for distribution of genus).

description: Trees and shrubs, uncommonly scandent, thorny or unarmed, deciduous or evergreen, usually with pubescent stems. Leaves alternate or opposite, petiolate, penni- nerved or triplinerved from the base, often bearing small rounded glandular spots either in lines roughly parallel to or at the margin or near the base or less commonly merely with glands few and scattered, unlobed, margins entire or serrate or crenate; stipules lateral and basal or rarely interpetiolar, usually caducous. Inflorescences of cymes or usually small thyrses, sessile and umbel-like or short-peduncled, few flowered and corymb-like, with the axis occasionally modified to a thorn, or rarely the flowers solitary at the nodes of a many-noded spur-shoot. Flowers small, in- conspicuously colored (usually yellowish green), perfect, with a floral cup at the rim of which are borne the calyx, corolla, and androecium. Floral cup hemispheric or shallower, soon after pollination abscising in an annular zone near the rim, the lower part strongly accrescent and persistently suffusing the lower fifth to half of the fruit. Sepals 5, usually about as long as the cup, valvate in bud, deltoid, spreading, usually pubescent dorsally, deciduous along with the rim of the cup. Petals 5, yellowish green or greenish yellow or whitish, slightly shorter than the sepals and of a much thinner texture, usually oblanceolate or spatulate, with terminal hood-like and basal claw-like moieties, deciduous along with the rim of the cup. Stamens 5, about as long as the petals, the anthers at some stages usually hooded or clasped by the petals. Disk massive, nectariferous, nearly filling the cup and at early stages hiding the ovary, accrescent along with the cup and adnate to, the lower fifth to half of the fruit. Ovary 3-celled (rarely 4-celled, but never constantly 4-celled in any one specimen); stigmas 3, small, obtuse; styles slender, 3-lobed to trifid. Fruit sub- globose or very shallowly tricoccous, suffused at base by the adnate, accrescent remnants of the cup and disk. Mesocarp thin, dry, leathery to brittle and flaky, loosely coherent to the endocarp at maturity, and breaking more or less irregularly at dehiscence. Endocarp crustaceous or cartilaginous, at maturity the three endo- carpids separating from each o-ther, and each dehiscing along the ventral, axile, longitudinal suture (and in some species also along the mid-dorsal line) thus releasing its seed. Seeds usually dihedral ventrally and strongly convex dorsally, usually lustrous, dark brown or black, with a thick, bony coat and with endosperm; funiculi thick and pedestal-like, occasionally with a slightly flaring apex which has been interpreted as an aril. Embryo flat, the plane of the usually oblong cotyledons perpendicular to a plane passing through the long axis of the fruit; radicle very small.

description: Columnea L. is the largest genus of neotropical Gesneriaceae (150-200 species) with diversity centered in the area from Ecuador to Costa Rica. Kvist and Skog (1993) and Skog (1979) recognized 57 and 50 species in Ecuador and Panama, respectively. In Colombia there are at least 75 species with the following numbers of species in the six sections of Columnea recognized by Kvist and Skog (1993): Bucinellina (2), Collandra (at least 32, of which 26 have so far been named), Columnea s.str. (5), Ortholoma (at least 26, of which 17 are named), Pentadenia (1), and Stygnanthe (7 according to Smith, 1994). The most prominent taxonomic problems in the genus are found mainly in the sections Collandra and Or- tholoma, both of which have their centers of diversity in Colombia, the former apparently along the Pacific coast and the latter in the department of Antioquia. Most species of sect. Ortholoma are rarely collected, but species of sect. Collandra are relatively abundant. Plants of the latter section are particularly noticeable in premontane and lower montane forests by their characteristic dorsiventral shoots with extremely anisophyllous leaves mostly with purple patterns on their lower surfaces. We are focused currently on sect. Collandra, and here three new species from that section are described.

description: Hypanthium campanulate; sepals elongate, conspicuous, oblonlg or subulate'; stamens nearly isomorphic, sometimes well differentiated in size; anthers subulate, straight or arcuate, the connective well prolonged below the anther-sacs and often bent to one side, ending in 2 short lobes or finger-shaped appendages; ovary 2-celled or 4-celled; style filiform with punctiform stigma. description: Dioecious shrubs or small trees, the branchlets subterete, glabrous; leaves glabrous, alternate, petiolate, the blades entire or slightly undulate and often narrowly recurved at margins, the costa raised above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves several, irregularly anastomosing near margins, the tertiary nerves subparallel, nearly perpendicular to the costa, often conspicuous; inflorescences 1 or 2 in leaf axils or on defoliated branchlets, racemose, fasciculate- racemose, or narrowly paniculate; bracts subtending the fascicles or lateral branches small or none bracteoles none; flowers pedicellatel staminate perianth carnose or thin carnose, sometimes puberulent within , 3(rarely or 5) lobed; filaments connate in a carnose eolnmn; anthers 4-10, oblong, 2-celled, dehiscing by extrorse clefts, in the Section Eucompsoneura basifixed and free (rarely partially dorsally connate by inconspicuous connectives), often recurved, in the Section Coniostele dorsally adnate to a carnose truncate-obconical colnective mass, the anther cells separately adnate and often divergent; pistillate perianth usually slightly larger and more carnose than the staminate, the ovary subglobose or ellipsoid, the style short, the stigma peltate or 2-lobed; fruit ellipsoid, glabrous, 2-valved, smooth or obseurely carinate, pedicellate, the pedicel surmounted by the persistent perianth lobes, the pericarp very thin, the aril essentially entire or minutely laciniate at apex with a few short lobes, the seed ellipsoid, the testa conspicuously irregularly splotched with black or purple.

description: Shrubs or rarely small trees with numerous branches with very short internodes, the branches of several sorts, the principal ones (primary branches or "primaries" of the key and descriptions) elongate and arcuate and with or without thorn-tips, bearing numerous, much shorter, divaricate, thorn-tipped branchlets (secondary branches or "secondaries") which in turli bear the "short shoots" (short, many-noded twigs without discernible internodal elonga- tion) and also in some species at right angles some very short thorn-tipped branchlets (tertiary branchlets or "tertiary thorns") less than 1 cm long. Leaves small, alternate, or appearing fasciculate at the short shoots, obovate or spatulate, or in No. 18 linear or rarely ovate or oblong, tapering basally to the short petiole, from which the blade is not easily distinguished; venation pinnate or in No. 18 seemingly reduced to the midvein without laterals; margins entire or in No. 16 and No. 17a not rarely with a few teeth distally; stipules very small acuminate to subulate, never spinose. Flowers small, perfect, perigynous, solitary or seemingly fascicled at the short shoots, on short pedicels. Floral cup or hypanthium ("cup" of the descriptions) with a thin disk which in some species is slightly thickened near the rim but never around the ovary; cup firm, herbaceous, after anthesis becoming flattened and persistent below the drupe. Sepals 5, deltoid, valvate in bud, eventually falling after anthesis. Petals absent except in No. 11 and No. 18, about as long as the sepals, obovate or somewhat clawed, membranous, the blade cupped adaxially, reflexed at anthesis and caducous. Stamens 5, alternate with an about as long as or usually a little longer than the sepals, strongly introrse in bud and usually also at anthesis; anthers minute, 2-celled, dorsifixed, the cells discoid, convex toward the point of attachment and concave away from it, opening by longitudinal marginal slits. Ovary globose-conic and completely free from the disk and cup, strongly constricted basally and thus with a narrow receptacular attachment, completely 2-celled, each cell with one basal placenta and one erect ovule (or one of these suppressed very early in ontogeny, usually in No. 11 and No. 18 and occasionally in No. 1); style shorter than the ovary, teret often with a slight scarcely differentiated, indistinctly 2-lobed, apical capitulation. Fruit small, drupaceous, with a thick to thin dark pulp and a thick-walled stone with two cells and one or two seeds (when one seed aborts fairly early in development the stone may appear to be only one-celled or very unequally 2-celled). Embryo straight; radiele very small; plane of the cotyledons tangential to the stone, not radial (or appearing radial when only one ovule develops).

Amblyarrhena; ovary inferior, 5-many-celled, with short stout style and capitate or peltate stigma. Shrubs or trees, of very diverse aspect, with ample leaves and terminal panicles of white flowers. description: Trees; bark often aromatic; leaflets 1-12rpaired, abruptly pinnate, the members of each pair alternate or opposite, punctate or impunctate, usually glabrous; stipules small, deciduous; bracts small, usually deciduous; bractlets wanting; inflorescence patent-paniculate, the flowers small, numerous, sessile, disposed as spikes on the branches; sepals 4, imbricate or subvalvate, usually hirsute-pubescent within; stamens (8) 10 (13), the filaments elongate, attached in middle of anther, the anthers oblong, glabrous; ovary stipitate, usually hirsute-pubescent, the style elongate, the stigmas truncate at apex, the ovules 2, compressed, ob- long, pendulous; fruit bivalved, turgid, usually smooth, the endocarp subfibrous, the seeds solitary, plump, shiny, the arillus colored, enveloping most of seed.

description: Four species. Medium to large shrubs or even small trees, stellate-pubescent or sublepidote. Leaves petiolate, the blades large, broadly ovate, and more or less lobulate, or small (xerophyllous) and trifoliolate or pinnatifid; stipules small, triangular. Flowers solitary (or paired) in the leaf axils or in subcorymbose or subumbellate axillary inflorescences; involucel absent; calyx cam- panulate, ca. half-divided to subtruncate, the lobes entire; corolla twice the length of calyx or more, usually lavender or purplish to almost white; androecium included, the column apically staminiferous with laminar filaments; styles 5-10, clavate, the stigmas bilaterally decurrent. Fruits schizocarpic, indurate; mericarps 5-10, apically aristate or homed, 3-6-seeded, loculicidally and septicidally dehiscent; seeds smooth. 2n = 16 (two species).

description: Trees; bole regular, without buttresses; bark smooth, light brown; wood reddish. Stipules interpetiolar, free at base, caducous. Leaves long-petiolate, blades elliptic to ovate, acute at both ends; domatia composed of tufts of sparse hairs or absent. Inflorescences terminal and solitary, corymbose and with opposite to subopposite lateral branches terminating in cymules. Flowers protandrous, long-pedicellate; hypanthium obconical. Calyx cupular with minute deltoid lobes, persistent; calyx lobes 4, one lobe expanding into a red pterophyll after anthesis. Corolla funnelform, yellow; corolla tube funnelform, glabrous throughout; corolla lobes 4, ovate and acuminate at apex; aestivation right-contorted. Stamens alternate to the corolla lobes and half-exserted; anthers narrowly elliptic, long-tailed at base, dorsi-fixed near the middle, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; filaments attached on the middle of the corolla tube, slender and basally flattened, glabrous throughout. Style exserted; style branches short, ovate and reflexed at maturity, opening after complete dehiscence of the anthers. Ovary 2-celled, with 1 seed per locule basally inserted. Fruits narrowly cylindrical, woody, multicostate, indehiscent, with 1 foliose pterophyll. Seeds with basal hilum, clavate, fleshy, smooth.

description: Slender, erect, caulescent perennial herbs, often branching in the inflorescence, scaberulous, from a napiform root. Leaves petiolate, the blades ternate-pinnately to pinnately decompound with linear or lanceolate, entire ultimate divisions. Petioles of moderate length, sheathing, those of the upper cauline leaves often wholly sheathing and the sheaths dilated. Inflorescence of loose compound umbels; peduncles terminal and usually also lateral, longer than the leaves. Involucre none or inconspicuous. Rays (fertile) 7-15, spreading-ascending, unequal. Involucel of several linear bract- lets. Pedicels (fertile) 4-15, slender, spreading-ascending. Flowers white, the petals with' a yellowish midvein; calyx obsolete; petals oval, acute, the apex slightly incurved but not sharply inflexed; styles slender, spreading, the stylopodium lacking. Carpophore divided to the base, the halves filiform. Fruit oblong-ovoid, subterete, glabrous, both the dorsal and the lateral ribs subequally winged, the wings a little narrower than the body; vittae rather large, solitary in the intervals, 2 on the com- missure; seed compressed dorsally in transection, channeled under the vittae, the face essentially plane.

description: Terrestrial, caulescent herbs. Leaves opposite decussate; venation pinnate; stomata scattered; petiolate. Inflorescences axillary, pedunculate, bracteate.
