description: Understory shrubs or trees, reproductive height 8-10 (24) m; sometimes provided with plank buttresses; bark smooth and brown or gray; vegetative apices densely pubescent, branchlets slender to somewhat robust, incompletely glabrescent. Trichomes of two types: 1) simple, long, thin, multicellular, uniseriate, acute, ferrugineous, often with thickened base, occurring on all vegetative surfaces (adaxial leaflet surface rarely glabrous) and on pedicel, calyx, corolla, and often ovary; and 2) multicellular snail-shaped glands (Solereder, 1908; Metcalfe & Chalk, 1950), occurring on most vegetative surfaces and inflorescence axes, usually dense on unexpanded leaflets, sometimes present on the pedicels, calyx, and rarely the ovary. Leaves usually clustered at the ends of the branchlets, imparipinnately compound, with lateral leaflets opposite; leaf bases pulvinate, usually broadly and shallowly canaliculate, remainder of the petiole and interjuga terete, striate, rarely evidently lignified; juga (1) 2-5 (7), generally more juga on the first-produced leaves of a shoot extension, the distal interjugum usually longer than the basal; leaflets elliptic to broadly so, the basal pair sometimes ovate and usually broader and shorter than the others, the ultimate pair usually ± as long as the terminal leaflet, the terminal leaflet sometimes obovate; leaflet apices acute to acuminate to rarely cuspidate, often serrulate, bases of lateral leaflets often asymmetrical, margins consistently simply serrulate (teeth up to 1 mm long), teeth acute to obtuse to rarely rounded, ascending. Inflorescence a panicle of racemes, primary and secondary axes indeterminate, inflorescences subterminal, axillary, initiated at the beginning of a new shoot extension and usually congested at the apex, subtended by leaves and by usually fugaceous bracts or by the bracts only; axes terete (sometimes compressed at branching points); bracts subtending the racemes lanceolate to ovate, coriaceous to fleshy, usually fugaceous, bracts subtending the flowers narrowly lanceolate to broadly ovate, chartaceous, persistent or fugaceous; pedicels clavate to subcylindrical, sulcate. Flowers functionally dioecious; calyx synsepalous, cupular, the lobes narrowly triangular to depressed-deltate, lobe apices acute to obtuse, papillate, lobes usually at least as long as the calyx tube; corolla aestivation induplicate-valvate, petals 5, free, usually green abaxially and white to greenish-white to yellowish-green adaxially, fleshy, narrowly elliptic, somewhat asymmetrical, involute, slightly to markedly carinate, apex with thickened fleshy inflexed apiculum, base slightly narrowed, petals at anthesis erect or reflexed from the basal 1/3 to 2/3 of their length, the margin long-papillate, abaxial surface with sparse to scattered often long hairs, usually concentrated along the keel or restricted to it, adaxial surface short-papillate; stamens 10, weakly diplostemonous in two unequal series (in C. goudotianum 5 in [male] and 5 or 10 in [female]), the antesepalous series longer, free or rarely contiguous filaments sometimes ba- sally connate, inserted on the base of the disk; staminate flowers with stamens exceeding the reduced pistil, filaments fleshy and papillate, moderately to broadly compressed-obclavate to less often compressed-subcylindrical; anthers basifixed, those of the antesepalous stamens in dorsiventral view compressed-oblong and obtuse at both ends, those of the antepetalous series usually triangular with lobulate bases, anther apices sometimes apiculate due to overtopping of the anterior spo- rangia by the posterior pair, the anthers concave abaxially and the posterior sporangia separate to the apex; disk fleshy, sulcate, undulate, annular or sometimes concave-discoid; pistillode substipitate, ovoid, longer than broad, contracted into a short, thick 5-sulcate stylode, surrounded by an annular disk or sometimes in a depression in a discoid disk, glabrous or very rarely with scattered hairs, pistillode reduced and weakly 5-lobed or sometimes subcylindrical, provided with locules and reduced ovules or consisting of a parenchymatous structure; stigmas absent, the apex of the stylode narrowly, vertically canaliculate; pistillate-flowers with only the antesepalous staminodes reaching the level of the style; anthers dorsiventrally compressed, flat abaxially, all four sporangia connate and not producing pollen; disk annular, negligibly undulate; ovary globose, densely pubescent or rarely glabrous, gradually contracted into a short thick style; stigmas 5, discoid to obtusely obdeltate or obtriangular, lateral or oriented upward and outward; locules 5, epipetalous, each with two subapical collateral pendulous ovules, at most 1 ovule per locule developing in fruit. Fruit a compound, septicidally dehiscent drupe, 1-2 (3) locules developing into pyrenes, fruit orange to red when mature, obliquely ovoid, ventricose, with as many lobes as developed locules, drying smooth or wrinkled, glabrous or densely pubescent; style and stigma often persistent in fruit; mesocarp fleshy, thick, the pyrenes papery and brittle to cartilaginous, ovoid-trigonous with 1 concave and 2 convex sides, enveloped by a white sugary pulp, after dehiscence suspended by a sub-apical funicle; seed oblique-ovoid, acute, testa papery; embryo fleshy, exalbuminous, J-shaped (subhippocrepiform) to U-shaped (hippocrepiform) (see Fig. 1), cotyledons entire, plano-con- vex, uncinate, transversely replicate the distal 1/6-1/2 their length.

description: About 75 species. Annual or perennial herbs, erect or procumbent, rarely subshrubs, sparsely to densely stellate-pubescent, sometimes with glandular hairs. Leaves petiolate, lanceolate or ovate to orbicular, unlobed to deeply palmately parted or divided, the lobes sometimes secondarily divided; stipules subulate to lance-ovate. Flowers solitary (or paired) in the leaf axils or aggregated apically in racemes or panicles; involucel absent; calyx campanulate, ca. half-divided or more; corolla ca. twice the length of calyx (sometimes smaller), white, lavender, or purple, sometimes with a dark center; androecium shorter than corolla; styles 8-22, the stigmas capitate or truncate. Fruits oblate, glabrous; mericarps 8-22 supported by a concave carpocrater, the lateral walls lacking at maturity, usually with two membranous apical wings, the wings much shorter than the carpel body to twice as long (usually subequal), sometimes erose, whitish or lavender; seeds solitary, retained at maturity by encircling dorso ventral wall. 2n = 12 (one species), 2n = 24 (one species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Erect herbaceous perennial, 3-5 dm tall; sparingly branched. Stems striate, brown to purplish, hirtellous below, puberulent above, somewhat woody at base. Leaves opposite becoming sub-opposite or alternate above; blades glabrous, sessile, entire, narrowly oblong, 2.2-3.7 cm long, 2-4 mm wide, mostly 3-nerved, apex obtuse. Inflorescence a flat terminal corymb ca. 4-6 cm in diameter; pedicels 1-2.5 cm long; heads discoid, erect, ca. 13 mm high, 5-12-flowered; phyllaries ca. 15, imbricated, lanceolate, acute, purple tinged, ca. 8 mm long, ca. 1.5 mm wide; receptacle flat or very slightly convex, naked; florets lavender, purple or pink, narrowly tubular, ca. 6 mm long, 5-lobed, the lobes ca. 1.5 mm long; stamens 5; anthers (including appendages) ca. 2 mm long, ca. 135 µ in diameter; appendages sessile, very broadly ovate, the apex usually deeply cleft, ca. 275 µ long, ca. 90 µ wide; pappus present; style branches 2, greatly exserted at maturity, ca. 3 mm long, ca. 220 µ in diameter; achenes narrowly prismatic, 8-10 ribbed, ribs setose, dark brown, 3.5-5 mm long. Pollen tricolpate, spherical, distinctly spinose, ca. 30 µ in diameter. Chromosome number not determined.

description: Plants: Vines, herbs, or subshrubs; perennial; with a woody rootstock; monoecious or dioecious. Stems procumbent, climbing, or erect; sulcate; not aculeate; variously pubescent. Nodes not geniculate or rarely geniculate (C. aspera). Leaves: Petioles cylindrical or rarely claviform (C. cla- vipetiolata); sulcate or rarely terete (C. jeffreyana) in cross-section; not aculeate; variously pubescent; pubescence a single type or 2 different types uniformly inter- mixed on each petiole. Leaf blades entire, pentalobate, heptalobate, or 5-palmately lobed; with the margin entire or serrate; elliptic, ovate to very broadly so, or shallowly ovate in outline; cordate or rarely obtuse (C. kelleri) at the base; with or rarely without a basal sinus; narrowly acute to broadly so, broadly acuminate, or obtuse at the apex; variously pubescent and never aculeate; not ciliate or rarely antrorse-ciliate on the margins. Central leaf-blade lobe symmetrical; entire or rarely pinnatifid (C. clavipetiolata); elliptic to broadly so, transversely broadly elliptic, shallowly ovate, narrowly obovate to obovate, or triangular to shallowly so in outline. Lateral leaf-blade lobes asymmet- rical or rarely symmetrical; entire or rarely pinnatifid (C. clavipetiolata); elliptic, broadly ovate to very broadly so, shallowly ovate, narrowly obovate to obovate, very broadly triangular to very shallowly so in outline; acute to broadly so or obtuse at the apex. Tendrils: Present or rarely absent (C. reticu- lata); solitary; simple; variously pubescent or rarely glabrous; never aculeate. Inflorescences: Unisexual. Male inflorescences: Fasciculate, racemose, a solitary flower, or pa- niculate; 1-19-flowered; pedunculate or sessile. Maleflowers: Pedicellate; 5-merous. Pedicel variously pubescent; without bracteoles. Hypanthium campanulate or infun- dibular (C. aetheocarpa); variously pubescent or rarely glabrous. Calyx lobes linear to narrowly oblong or narrowly triangular to triangular in outline; narrowly acute at the apex; variously pubescent. Corolla yellow; infundibular; variously pubescent or rarely glabrous outside; puberulent, glabrous, or rarely papillose inside; fused into a basal tube. Corolla lobes elliptic to broadly so, ovate to broadly so, or obovate to broadly so in outline; narrowly acute to broadly so or mucronate and obtuse at the apex. Stamens free; 3; separating from the free portion of the hypanthium above the ovary; two 2-thecate and one 1 -thecate. Filaments glabrous. Anther thecae straight, without bends or bent once at the apex toward the connective into a hook; glabrous with the edges shortly pubescent. Anther connective extended or rarely not extended (C. aetheocarpa); oblong, transversely broadly oblong, ovate, or narrowly obovate to broadly so; unilobate; obtuse or rarely acute at apex; smooth at the apex. Disc cylindrical, fungiform, or rarely trilobate; glabrous. Female inflorescences: A solitary flower or rarely fascicles (C. ritchiei); 1(4)-flowered; pedunculate or sessile. Female flowers: Pedicellate; 5-merous. Pedicel terete or rarely sulcate in outline; variously pubescent. Hypanthium hourglass shaped or rarely obturbinate (C. aetheocarpa); not distinctly ridged or distinctly ridged; from the constricted portion downwards fused to the ovary. Fused portion of hypanthium ellipsoid, ovoid, rarely cylindrical, or rarely obturbinate; not aculeate or rarely aculeate; variously pubescent or rarely glabrous. Aculei soft. Free portion of hypanthium campanulate; never aculeate; variously pubescent outside; puberulent or rarely glabrous inside. Calyx lobes linear, narrowly oblong, narrowly obovate, or narrowly triangular in outline; narrowly acute to acute at the apex; variously pubescent. Corolla yellow; infundibular; variously pubescent or rarely glabrous outside; puberulent, glabrous, or rarely papillose inside. Corolla lobes elliptic to broadly so, broadly ovate, or obovate in outline; acute to broadly so, acuminate, or obtuse and mucronate at the apex. Staminodes present; papilliform; glabrous or rarely puberulent. Style terete in cross-section; glabrous; subtended by a circular disc. Disc glabrous. Stigma cupular; lobate; with 3, 4, or 6 finger-like projections on the margin. Finger-like stigmatic projections papillate or rarely smooth. Fruit: Not geocarpic, ma- turing above ground and readily visible. Pedicel sulcate or rarely terete in cross-sec- tion; variously pubescent. Fruit monochro- mous or bicolored with longitudinal stripes from base to apex; green, red, yellow, white, or orange; with dark green, white, or orange longitudinal stripes; ellipsoid, globose, ovoid, or spindle-shaped to narrowly so; with the pericarp moderately to very thick or thin; not aculeate or rarely aculeate; var- iously pubescent or rarely glabrous; blunt or rostrate at the apex. Aculei terete. Seeds: Yellowish white; elliptic or ovate; glabrous or rarely puberulent with hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long (C. silentvalleyi); with a band of punctations around the edge on both faces or smooth without evident surface sculpturing; emarginate or rarely marginate with the broad margin delineated by a furrow (C. silentvalleyi); unwinged.
bibliographicCitation: Kirkbridejr, J. H. 1994. Revision of Cucumella (Cucurbitaceae, Cucurbitoideae, Melothrieae, Cucumerinae). Brittonia. 46: 161-186.

description: Lianas or shrubs or slender trees with eventually scandent branches, glabrous throughout, the branches and branchlets subterete, slender, slightly swollen at nodes; leaves opposite or subopposite, petiolate, the petioles shallowly canaliculate or narrowly winged distally, the leaf-blades greenish or olivaceous when dried, decurrent on the petiole; infloreseences axillary or aggregated at apices of branchlets or arranged on short leafless branchlets, paniculate-corymbose, usually pedunculate; flowers large for the family, in distal dichotomies or loosely arranged toward apices of ultimate branchlets, pedicellate, subtended by minute bracteoles; sepals 5, imbricate, membranous, rounded at apex, faintly nerved; petals 5, spreading or erecto-patent, membranlous, usually faintly nerved; disk membranous to thin-carnose, erect or suberect, short-cylindric, conspicuous, entire or minutely crenulate at margin; stamens 3, suberect, the filamnents membranous, ligulate, conspicuously broadened toward base, the anthers basifixed, extrorsely nutant, transversely ellipsoid, dehiscing by extrorse-apical horizontal confluent clefts; ovary depressed-trigonous, soon conspicuously 3-lobed, the style carnose, the stigmas 3, sometimes conspictuous, opposite stamens, the locules 3, the ovules 4 or 6 per locule, 2-ranked, ascending from the inner basal angle; fruiting infloreseence swollen, the fruits apparently 1 per inflorescence, capsular, the capsules 3, divergent, separately attached to a swollen receptacle, conspicuously convex on both surfaces, rounded or cuneate at base and abruptly stipitate, rounded or faintly emarginate at apex, obtuse and sometimes faintly undulate at margins, dehiscing along an inconspicuous median suture, the pericarp thin-coriaceous or papyraceous, conspicuously flabellate-costate without (nerves prominulous, freely branching), smooth or minutely rugulose within; seeds 2-6, at maturity completely occupying the capsule-cavity, erect from base, affixed by a basal wing, the embryoniferous portion apical, coriaceous, ellipsoid, the wing thin- coriaceous or papyraceous, oblong, gradually narrowed toward base, traversed by a single longtitudinal nerve near center, extending dis- tally into a narrow flanige along the inner margin of the embryoniferous portion, the raphe thickened, obscurely immersed along the outer margin of wing.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Dioecious palm-like shrubs with aerial or subterranean, pachycaul, cylindrical stems clad with persistent frond bases. Fronds loosely pubescent when young, pinnate, spirally arranged, produced in seasonal growth flushes interspersed with cataphylls, lower pinnae often reduced to spines. Longitudinal ptyxis erect or rarely reflexed, horizontal ptyxis circinate. Pinnae with a single thick midrib and no lateral veins; stomata confined to abaxial surface in most species; individual ptyxis involute (see Stevenson, 1981). Trichomes transparent, branched or simple. Microsporophylls aggregated into determinate cones and bearing numerous microsporangia (pollen-sacs) on abaxial surfaces, with a simple sterile apex, which is often produced into an upturned spine; microsporangia opening by slits; pol- len cymbiform, monosulcate. Megasporophylls spirally arranged in an indeterminate terminal rosette with the central axis continuing vegetative growth. Ovules 2 to many (rarely 1), marginally inserted on the stipe and directed obliquely outward ("ascending"); sporophyll apically dilated into a pinnatifid, pectinate, toothed or entire lamina. Seeds with a yellow, orange or brown sarcotesta, and with or without spongy tissue beneath the sclerotesta. Endosperm haploid, derived from the female gametophyte. Embryo straight; with two cotyledons that are usually united at the tips and a very long, spirally twisted suspensor; seeds platyspermic; germination cryptocotylar.
bibliographicCitation: Hill, Kenneth D. & Yang, S. L. 1999. The Genus Cycas (Cycadaceae) in Thailand. Brittonia. 51 (1): 48-73.

description: Shrubs or small trees, sometimes scandent. Leaves usually with two glands on the lower surface near the base, often with small glands near the apex, the lower surface glabrous or with stiff ferruginous hairs, more rarely with whitish arachnoid or lanate indumentum. Petiole eglandular. Inflorescence a simple raceme or a raceme of zig-zag, usually lax, false racemes, more rarely a subcapitate spike (D. whytei). Bracts and bracteoles not enclosing the flower-buds in small groups, often with stalked or sessile glands. Flowers bisexual, strongly zygomorphic. Receptacle-tube usually elongate and narrowly obconic-tubular, usually longer than the upper pedicel, often slightly gibbous at the base, glabrous inside except near the throat. Sepals 5, rounded or acute, usually spreading or reflexed, often with stalked or sessile marginal glands, the adaxial surface whitish-tomentellous. Petals 5, caducous. Stamens 10-75, coiled in bud, the filaments ligulately connate for most of length, inserted on posterior rim of faucal annulus, far exserted, much longer than combined length of calyx and receptacle-tube. Staminodes short, filiform or denticulate. Ovary monocarpellary, 1-locular, inserted at mouth of receptacle-tube; style filiform, slightly longer than the stamens, slightly 3-lobed at apex. Drupe usually more than 3 cm long, more or less ovoid, but usually markedly tapered towards the pointed apex; epicarp often ferruginous-tomentose and with longer hispid hairs, less often glabrous; mesocarp thin; endocarp thin but hard, with a roughish surface, hairy inside, with no special mechanism allowing seedlings to escape.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. & White, Frank. 1979. Resurrection of the genus Dactyladenia (Chrysobalanaceae). Brittonia. 31: 483-487.

description: Trees, erect or scandent shrubs, or woody lianas. Leaves alternate, unequally imparipinnate, rarely 1-foliolate; stipules various, often small and caducous; stipels absent. Inflorescence racemose, paniculate, sometimes amply paniculate with small leaves intermixed, or cymose with ± flat top, usually with secundiflorous terminal racemes, or fasciculate with small racemes or panicles clustered at the leaf axils. Flowers small and usually numerous, often fragrant; bracts small, usually caducous, rarely persistent; bracteoles small, caducous or persistent. Calyx campanulate, 5-lobed, the upper pair of lobes usually broader than the others and often partially connate, the lowest lobe usually narrower and the longest. Corolla papilionaceous, white, cream, yellow, purple, or violet; standard petal ovate, obovate, orbicular or panduriform, usually emarginate at the apex, its claw long or short; wings oblong, obovate or rarely ± ovate, usually auriculate at the base of the blade; keel-petals very often slightly shorter than wings, their blades obtuse, oblong or sometimes obovate, usually auriculate at the base of the blade, always connate on the lower side of the apex. Stamens 9 or 10, mono-, di-, or triadelphous, in various arrangements and sometimes with the vexillary stamen free; anthers small, erect, didymous, basifixed with short apical dehis- cence, rarely by longitudinal chinks. Ovary stipitate; style long or short, usually incurved; stigma small, terminal; ovules few. Fruit oblong to oblong-elliptical, samaroid, crescent or kidney-shaped, or orbicular to suborbicular, membranaceous, subcoria- ceous or coriaceous, thickened over the seed cavity or thickened throughout. Seed reniform, compressed; radicle inflexed.
bibliographicCitation: Carvalho, A. M. de. 1997. A synopsis of the genus Dalbergia (Fabaceae: Dalbergieae) in Brazil. Brittonia. 49: 87-109.

description: Shrubs or subshrubs; leaves alternate, elliptical, ovate, or suborbicular, sometimes rather lobed; heads homogamous, discoid; flowers 4-30, all perfect, regular; involucre campanulate; phyllaries in 3-4 imbricate series, fimbriate margined; receptacle con- vex, chaffy; corolla 5-lobed, with or without glands; anther appendage small, with reflexed margin; achene 5-ribbed, with setae mostly on the ribs; pappus setae 10-20, slender and deciduous, somewhat to distinctly enlarged apically, scabrous or becoming barbellate; pollen tricolpate, minutely papillose.
bibliographicCitation: King, Robert M. & Robinson, Harold E. 1969. Studies in the Eupatoricae (Compositae). XVI. A monograph of the genus Decachaeta DC. Brittonia. 21: 275-284.

description: Large shrubs with numerous spreading woody branches arising from a woody taproot; leaves cauline, alternate, exstipulate, petiolate, the leaf-blade elliptic, hir- sutulous; flowering branches slender, annually produced from the axils of the previous year's leaves, green and hirsutulous; inflorescences cymose, compact to rather open, with a single, short-pedicellate flower and a single peduncle at each node, and a cluster of 5-10 sessile or subsessile flowers atop the 2- to 5-bracted peduncle; bracts foliaceous, similar to the leaves only reduced, 3-4 at the lowest node, 2-3 above and these ultimately nearly scale-like; peduncles erect, slender, restricted to the axils of the branches, hirsutulous; involucre lacking; flowers yellowish, sessile to subsessile or short-pedicellate, not at all stipitate, hispidulous, the 6 tepals petaloid, slightly united at the base, narrowly lanceolate with the outer whorl of 3 tepals slightly broader and longer than the inner whorl; stamens 9, slightly longer than the tepals at anthesis, the filaments pilose basally, the anthers yellow, oblong; pistil 3-carpellary, the ovary 1-celled, 1-ovulate, the style 3-branched with a small capitate stigma at the tip of each style branch; fruits 3-angled achenes, light reddish-brown, slightly pubescent on the beak at maturity; embryos curved, with abundant mealy endosperm.

description: Shrubs up to 2 dm tall, from stout-linear or fusiform taproots; shoots annual or biennial, arching to semi-decumbent, simple or sparingly branched, reddish or tan with pale lenticels, glabrate; leaves coriaceous, estipulate, alternate, deciduous, prominently revolute, glabrate; calyx lobes usually three, triangular, equal, distinct nearly to the receptacle, glabrate without, glabrous within; flowers axillary, fragrant, acereseent, on glabrate, nodding to sub-erect, ebracteate pedicels; petals 6-15, subequal, linear or oblong, fleshy, impressed-veiny on the inner face; torus flat or slightly convex; stamens 10-20, the anthers extrorse, surmounted by short-cylindric, extruding, blunt connectives, and clustered into a compact, flat-topped mass; carpels 1-5 (-6), narrowly fusiform, glabrate, located on the center of the upper torus surface, the few to several ovules in two placental rows; fruit an unevenly oblong-cylindric, pulpy berry; seeds bean-shaped or ovoid, castaneous, with tough coat; endosperm in plates.

description: Seven species. Shrubs or small trees 3- 10 m tall, stellate-pubescent or puberulent to glabrate. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate or trilobulate, cordate or truncate, crenate or serrate to subentire, acute, stellate- puberulent to glabrescent; stipules subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or in few- flowered axillary umbels, sometimes api- cally congested; involucel absent; calyx prominently to obscurely 10-ribbed and  angled, ca. half-divided; petals yellow or red, 1.5-4 cm long, androecium included, filamentiferous at apex; styles 7-11, slender, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic (pseudocapsular), ovoid, nearly to quite gla- brous; mericarps 7-11, indurate, apically dehiscent; seeds solitary, glabrous. 2n = 42 (one species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Frutex vel arbor, cortice cinereo. Folia petiolata, ovata vel trilobata, leviter crenato- serrata vel subintegra, sparse stellato-pubescentia vel glabrata. Stipulae lineares, caducae. Pedunculi axillares, 1-flori vel umbellati pauciflori. Involucra nulla. Calyces 5-lobati, basaliter 10-angulati, ad medium divisi, lobis triangularibus. Corolla flava, 4-6 cm diametro. Columna staminalis pallida, antherifera apicem versus, antheris numerosis. Styli numero mericarpiorum aequales; stigmata capitata. Fructus schizocarpium, glaber extus; mericarpia 8-11, conformatione illae Sidae praeter 2 spinis apicalibus destitutis et parietibus lateralibus planiusculis et non ornatis. Semina solitaria, pendula, glabra.

description: Herbae cauleseentes; foliis alternis; floribus spicatis; bracteis minutis; sepalis libris, patentibus; petalis lateralibus minoribus quam This sepalis; caleare quam labello longiore, sacculis antherarum parallelis et approximatis; glandulis nudis; polliniis granularibus, breve- caudatis; stigmatibus cum appendicibus tribus oblongis, media appendiee inter glandulas orbiculares sita, ut antheris alta.

description: Flowers 5-merous; hypanthium campanulate-ovoid, villous; sepals triangular, nearly as long as the hypanthium; petals about 1 ecn. long; stamens strongly dimorphic, the larger with connective greatly prolonged, terminated by 2 filiform appendages about 2 mm. long, the smaller with connective not prolonged and bearing 2 linear-clavate appendages; ovary 5-celled. Herbaceous, simple or sparingly branched, densely villous throughout, with ovate-oblong leaves. The following is the only well known species; a second is described from Venezuela.

description: Annual or perennial herbs from tap roots, bulblets, tubers or rhizomes, acauleseent, or the stems 1-10 (-20 or more), erect, ascending or climbing, up to 20 (-30 or more) dm in length, glabrous, occasionally glaucous; leaves basal, or cauline and alternate, usually ternately decompound, occasionally bipinnately decompound, usually long-petioled, the petioles lunate to lunate-suleate or terete in transverse section, usually slightly expanded below; vascular bundles 3-15; leaflets ovate to oblong-lanceolate, often incisely pinnatifid, glabrous, occasionally glaucous, membranaceous to subcoriaceous, estipulate, entire or occasionally crenate to serrate, sessile to short-petiolulate, the stomata on the lower leaf surfaces only, these with no subsidiary cells; infloreseence thyrsoid, paniculate, racemose, corymbose or consisting of a solitary flower, scapose, axillary, extraaxillary or leaf-opposed; flowers bracteate, isobilaterally symmetrical, dimerous, pedicellate, the pedicels 1- to 2-bracteolate or ebracteolate; sepals 2, rudimentary, searious, eaducous; petals 4, the outer pair spurred or gibbous at the base, usually carinate at the apex, the inner petals unguiculate, the blades panduriform to spatulate or sagittate-spatulate with convex inner faces and dorsal membranous tubular crests, the crests and distal extremities connate, the claws linear oblong to oblanceolate; androecium of two phalanges of three stamens each, each phalange opposite an outer petal, the median anthers dithecal, each theca composed of two sporangia, the lateral anthers monothecal; filaments of each phalange united in varying degrees from the base to shortly below the anthers, a nectariferous spur projecting into the saccate outer petal-bases from the base of each median filament, or at least nectariferous tissue present in varying amounts toward the base of each median filament; ovary linear in outline to broadly oblong or obovoid, superior, bicarpellate, unilocular, the ovules anatropous, few to many, the placentae parietal, the style distinct, filiform, rigid, persistent in fruit, the stigma flattened, persistent in fruit, with or without two apical horns or bilabiate, papillate or rarely epapillate; pollen grains subprolate to spheroidal, tricolpate to irregularly rugate, occasionally synaperturate, the exine reticulate to obscurely verrucate; fruit a few- to many-seeded fleshy or membranous capsule dehiseent by two sterile valves or indehiseent; seeds small, with copious endosperm, reniform to suborbicular, the embryo minute, the testa black to brown, lustrous to dull, essentially smooth to deeply reticulate or densely papillate, an elaiosome usually present.

description: Tufted perennials, usually forming a basal rosette of broad blades early in the growing season and later developing erect, few- to many-noded culms, in some the culms scapose, with the nodes remaining aggregated at the base of the plant, in others there is secondary branching that results in the development of clusters of fascicles of reduced leafy flowering branches, these mainly with few-flowered panicles and cleistogamous spikelets. Herbage glabrous or variously hairy. Ligule usually a ring of hairs, infrequently a short membrane or absent. Culm blades broad or narrow, usually flat. Inflorescence typically a small, open panicle but the branches occasionally loosely contracted, the spikelets on short or long ped- icels. Spikelets ovate-elliptic or obovate, awnless, 0.8-4.5 mm long, with 2 flo- rets, the lower one neuter or (infrequently) staminate, the upper one perfect; disarticulation above the glumes. Glumes unequal, the first usually 1/4-1/2 as long as the spikelet but occasionally longer, the second about equalling the spikelet. Lemma of lower floret similar to the second glume in size and texture. Upper floret with a shiny, glabrous, coriaceous lemma and palea, the lemma tightly inrolled over the palea. Palea apex with minute, rounded, simple papillae in longitudinal rows and an apical ridge with few to several large stomata in 1 or more rows.

description: Creeping or sprawling perennial herbs with long-petioled, minutely stipulate leaves with membranous, entire-margined reniform or orbicular-reniform, apically rounded or emarginate blades; pubescence of equally two-armed, longitudinally oriented, medifixed hairs; flowers small, axillary, solitary, pedicellate; sepals united at the base only, acereseent after anthesis; corolla valvate-induplicate in bud, lobed more than half its length, not much if any longer than the calyx at anthesis; staiuelns 5; filamelnts filiform; anthers small; ovary bicarpellate, the ovules two in each carpel, erect, collateral; styles 2, essentially distinct, entire, each with a capitate, rough-surfaced stigma; fruit short, apically broadly rounded, truncate, or eiuarginate, or very deeply bilobed.

description: Medium to very large, unarmed trees, the trunks sometimes having low buttresses; bark reddish-brown, rather thick, separating into thin scales, the elements storied; young branches, buds, and leaves with gray or light brown to chocolate, ascending pubescence; pith light brown. Axillary buds with 2 imbricate scales, rounded or acute to acuminate. Leaves alternate, imparipinnate, the vascular system of the petioles forming a reniform siphonostele with 2 extra ridge-bundles adaxially (Fig. 3, E); stipules soon caducous; leaflets 5-13, alternate, ovate to elliptic, oblong, or obovate, usually becoming larger toward the distal end of the leaf, the apices acute to mostly acuminate and sometimes with a more or less caudate "drip-tip" often the very tip narrowly emarginate and with a small mucro, the bases obtuse to cordate, the margins sometimes revolute; epidermal cells often containing what appear to be siliceous bodies, the surfaces puberulus to pubescent with unicellular hairs which appear to be simply anticlinally elongated epidermal cells, these predominantly acicular but some abruptly hooked, often papillate below and with scattered, dark, clavate, multicellular glands which have some subepidermal development; veins and veinlets vertically transcurrent; stomatal apparatus limited to the lower epidermis, 15-25 y long mostly of the Rubiaceous or parallel-celled type (type C, Metcalfe & Chalk 1950), though some apparently of the Ranunculaceous or irregular-celled type (type A, Metcalfe & Chalk 1950); petiolules 3-12 mm long. Inflorescence a large terminal thyrse, the bracts ovate, concave on the inner surface, mostly soon caducous. Flower-buds spheroid to ellipsoid, on pedicels 4-7 mm long, the development of the flower parts apparently acropetal. Sepals 5, free, unequal, aestivation imbricate, the margins often ciliate, pubescent without, glabrous within, the outer 3 completely enclosing all flower parts, broad ovate, strongly concave on the inner side, rather thick and coriaceous, the lower (abaxial) one always outside the 2 adaxial laterals, the 2 inner sepals abaxial, narrowly ovate to oblong, only slightly concave, thinner and less coriaceous than the other. Petals 3, the aestivation imbricate but the pattern variable; the upper petal somewhat larger, or usually all of about the same size, with the upper one most frequently enclosing the laterals,3 but occasionally the laterals enclosing the upper one, or all simply imbricate, showy, white or rosy-white, the claws darker colored, the blades broadly elliptic or orbicular with crispate margins and often erose to emarginate apices, the inner faces glabrous, the backs pubescent with golden, chocolate-brown, or white 1-2 mm long hairs; all 3 petals falling before the sepals. Stamens 2, free, unequal in size, the longer usually above the pistil, the shorter usually more or less lateral to it, but occasionally these positions reversed; filaments whitish, glabrous, very crassulate, 1-2 mm thick, grooved on the inner face the longer usually about twice as long as the others; anthers about 5 mm long, yellow crustaceous, mostly glabrous but often with fine white papillae in the inter-thecal grooves and a few hairs on the concavity of the inner face, each dehiscing by a V-shaped apical slit, the anther on the shorter filament rather obovoid, 2-3 mm wide, 8-10 thecate at the midpoint, erect, the other oblong, about 2 mm wide, 4-8 thecate at the midpoint, incurved, both anthers finally developing into 2-locellate structures by the breakdown of the inter-thecal walls; pollen grains similar to those of Martiodendron (cf. Koeppen & Iltis 1962. Fig. 3-2), spherical, 18-24 ,u, tricopate, the furrows long and wide but tapered, the germ pore evident as a bulge, the exine smooth or very finely granular. Pistil 1-carpellate, the stigma small, slightly capitate, finely papillate, the style subulate, glabrous or pubescent, caducous in fruit, the ovary sessile, always pubescent with dark brown hairs, 3-6 ovulate from the upper suture (ventral carpellary bundles); ovules anatropous, the micropyle facing the stigmatic end. Fruit a tardily dehiscent follicle eventually opening along the upper suture, obliquely-ovate to oblong-ovate depending upon the number of seeds which develop, strongly compressed laterally, 4-7 mm thick, coriaceous, finely but sparsely pubescent at maturity, the upper suture with a narrow wing, the lower wingless, the seed chamber unilocular and occupying almost all the fruit, but with transverse "septae" developing as seeds mature. Seeds orbicular to reniform with a concavity on the edge opposite the hilum, strongly flattened laterally when dry; testa smooth, very impervious to water; cotyledons light green, very thin, orbicular to subreniform, covered by milky-white, horny endosperm which becomes quite gelatinous after being soaked in water; hypocotyl short, thick, and straight; epicotyl small, three lobed.

description: Basally woody herbs or subshrubs, mostly erect from a xylopodium. Leaves opposite, sometimes alternate distally, proximally or throughout, broadly ovate to suborbicular on distinct petioles to linear and subsessile, glandular-punctate abaxially, 3-nerved from near to well above the base (always 3-nerved from the base in D. lippioides, 1 -nerved in D. reitzii, and D. annuum), usually subpinnately netted to reticulate distally. Heads in loose dichasiiform arrangements at the end of primary and axillary shoots (always solitary in D. humboldtianum, sometimes solitary in D. vestitum). Involucres broadly campanulate (subglobose in D. brasilianum); phyllaries in ca. 3 or 4 series, the outer spreading (mostly erect in D. oblongum, much like the leaves in form and indûment, the inner appressed, indurate at the base and foliaceous at the tip, more scarious toward the center of the head. Receptacles convex; paleae surpassing the involucre before and after anthesis, conduplicate, variously carinatealate (slightly conduplicate and not carinate-alate inD. annuum), falcate in outline, persistent, scarious, tips rounded to subulate or rigid pungent. Ray florets sterile, lacking pistillodes, or pistillate and fertile (wanting in D. retifolium and sometimes in D. brasilianum); corollas liguliform, yellow, lamina oblong to elliptic or obovate, glandular-punctate, usually sparsely setulose abaxially. Disc florets perfect, fertile; corollas cylindrical in the throat above the campanulate base, lack of fiber sheaths along the veins of the corolla throats, lobes 5, deltate, minutely papillate adaxially, glandular punctate and usually sparsely setulose abaxially, slightly thickened at the tip; anther thecae blackish, connective and appendages stramineous, appendages deltate and glandular punctate abaxially; anther collars gibbous; style branches stout, strongly coiled after anthesis, often glandular-punctate abaxially, pillóse distally, appendages short, acute to acuminate, ending with a few trichomes. Cypselae obovate in outline, cunéate toward the base, usually tuberculate on the faces, mostly winged, wings narrow to as broad as the body or lacking, those of the peripheral flowers (ray and outer disc) mostly trigonous, usually 3- winged and 3-awned, the inner laterally flattened or sometimes thickened, subquadrangular, mostly 2-winged and 2-awned. Pappus coroniform, awns with phytomelanin extending from the body of the cypsela to its base, well developed, stout, trigonous, very broad to relatively narrow at the base, tapering, sometimes reduced to tooth-like projections or lacking, crown between awns not constricted, fragile, lacerate to erose, laciniate to fìmbriolate or reduced to a ciliate or entire margin.

description: Open somewhat pubescent shrub with long often remuotely leaved branches. Leaves opposite, subsessile to short-petioled, lance-oblong, subentire or serrulate, pubeseenit oln both sides. Infloreseeniee a dense terminal corymlb becoming racemose in fruit, finely and densely glandular-pubescent; pedicels slender, ascending to spreading. Floral tube short, gradually ampliate. Sepals 4, lanceolate, acute, more or less divergent, deep crimson, glandular and pubeseent. Petals 4, crimson, round-obovate, narrowed to a clawlike base, the 2 posterior larger. Stamenis 2, fertile, free, about as long as petals; filaments broad; an- thers linear-oblong. Style included; stigma small, capitate. Capsule globose, 4-locular, loculicidally 4-valved, the septa adnate to the persistent center. Seeds solitary in the locules, apparently concave-collnTex, much flattened, narrowly wing-margined.

description: Two species. Subshrubs with stellate pu- bescence. Leaves petiolate (except some- times the uppermost sessile), the blades ovate, cordate, crenate-dentate, acute or acuminate, markedly discolorous; stipules filiform. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils; involucel absent; calyx prominently 5-lobed; petals 8-20 mm long, yellowish; androecium included, pallid or yellowish, filamentiferous at apex; styles 12-17, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 12-17, divided into two cells, the lower cell 1-seeded, indehiscent, laterally reticulate, covered by an endoglossum, the upper cell dehiscent, 1-2-seeded, laterally smooth, apically rounded; seeds minutely pubescent. 2n = 14 (one species); 2n = 30 (one species).

description: Leaves alternate, simple, notophylls, membranaceous, persistence unknown, ovate, symmetrical, base obtuse, apex acute, margin serrate, teeth sedation simple, tooth spacing regular; cicatricose-crateriform glands present, never paired; marginal glands present; venation palmatinerved, agrophic veins present; primary vein moderate, straight; secondary venation semicraspedodromous, with 5 or 6 pairs of secondary veins with an acute angle of divergence; tertiary veins opposite percurrent; quaternary veins polygonal reticulate; orders of venation 5; aréoles incomplete; veinlets simple to branched more than twice; ultimate marginal venation with incomplete loops (Fig. IH). Midvein and higher order vein bundle sheaths sclerified, veinlets naked; mesophyll dorsiventral, without fibers (Fig. 3F), with numerous druses in the mesophyll and also in the phloem parenchyma, without tannins in the spongy parenchyma; epidermis simple, epidermal cells isodiametric in surface view, abaxial anticlinal cell walls undulate; cuticle smooth; stornata in the adaxial and abaxial surfaces, paracytic, striations in guard cells not seen; sparsely pubescent, trichomes simple, papillate.

description: Trees or shrubs with simple hairs. Leaves distichous, chartaceous to coriaceous, less commonly membranous, blade often decurrent on base, midvein prominent and usually keeled abaxially. Inflorescence terminal, less frequently leaf-opposed, 1-3-flowered, the flowers borne on slender pendent ebracteolate pedicels, the leaves opposing the pedicels often much reduced in size and the inflorescences then appearing bracteate. Sepals 5-21 mm long, foliaceous, chartaceous to sub- coriaceous, slightly to deeply concave. Petals either large (up to 35 mm long) and free to the base, or smaller, ovate or strap-shaped, and united into a broad tube that is adnate to the torus for most of its length. Stamens oblong to clavate, the connectives depressed-globose and often overhanging the tops of the anther thecae. Carpels numerous, the style usually markedly narrower than the ovary; ovules usually 2, less frequently 1 or 3, attached laterally; style oblong, usually hairy at apex. Torus usually much wider than high, often slightly depressed in the center, often increasing markedly in size in fruit. Fruit an aggregate of sessile thinly fleshy monocarps, each subtended by a separate long stalk derived from the torus (car- pophore), and separated from it by a distinct articulation. Monocarps two-seeded, less frequently one-seeded or rarely three-seeded in D. pulchrum, the monocarp wall separating readily from the seed in the dried condition. Seeds ellipsoid or flattened ellipsoid, surface in contact with adjacent seed flattened, chestnut-brown, glabrous, shiny, the rim of the exostome papery, light colored, and slightly recessed; seed coat with numerous internal plates extending between the ruminations of the endosperm.

description: Calyx tube obscurely articulate with pedicel, cup-shaped or short- cylindric, the limb suberect, 4- or 5-lobed; corolla subeylindric or campanulate-eylindric, 4- or 5-lobed; stamens twice as many as lobes (5 in D. pentandrtm), equal; filaments ligulate, attached to the anthers dorsally near their bases; anthers membranous, produced into 2 tubules, dehiscing by oval introrse clefts; style filiform, about as long as corolla, the stigma truncate; ovary 4- or 5-celled (3-celled in D. pentandrum?), the placenta central, the ovules numerous; disc an- nular, carnose; fruit a coriaceous berry.  Low terrestrial shrubs, often compact and dwarfed, with short densely foliated branchlets; leaves alternate, small, short-petiolate, coriaceous, the venation often obscure; flowers 1-6 in leaf axils, often subsessile, subtended by a few minute subcoriaceous bracts; pedicels sometimes bibracteolate near base, bibracteate at summit, the bracts large, embracing the calyx tube (bracts 4-6 in D. pentandrutm).

description: Woody climbers or small shrubs, with vegetative and reproductive structures usually bearing sparse sessile or short-stalked glands, these more dense and with longer stalks at the branch nodes. Leaves opposite, petiolate, venation acrodromous. Panicles bracteose or frondose-bracteose, terminal, many-flowered. Flowers 6- or 7-merous, pedicellate. Hypanthium with the calyx persistent, with short tube and lobes, these always with dorsal teeth. Petals purple, minutely papillose. Stamens twice as many petals, isomorphic or slightly dimorphic in size, all grouped in a zygomorphic bundle; filaments glabrous, curved (not geniculate); connectives glabrous, dorsally thickened, not prolonged below the thecae, and with a long, dorsal-basal, descendent, filiform, spiraled or coiled appendage; anthers with a single minute apical pore, each one of the thecae shortly lobed at the base. Ovary (2-)3-4-celled, usually basally 1/4 inferior but seldom free, glabrous; style glabrous. Capsule loculicidal, with (2-)3-4 radial slits on the top; seeds cuneate to long-cuneate, with the testa laterally expanded into thin wings.

description: The genus Drymonia Mart. is characterized by having long narrow anthers which are connate at anthesis by their thecae and which shed their pollen through apical pores (Wiehler, 1983). Drymonia is among the larger genera of neotropical Gesneriaceae, with 50-100 species of mostly lianous epiphytes, but the genus has never been revised and is poorly understood. The new species described here is the only known species of Drymonia with extremely unequal leaf pairs and is, therefore, superficially more similar to species in Columnea sect. Collandra than to other species of Drymonia. The plant de- scribed below may also resemble Alloplectus Mart. superficially. Alloplectus is probably closely related to Drymonia and differs mainly in the character of the anthers. Most species of Alloplectus are terrestrial and have equal or subequal leaves, differing from many species of Drymonia and the one described below. The two genera share the character of having a fleshy capsular display fruit, differing from the berry-fruited Columnea. Like Drymonia, Alloplectus has nu- merous but poorly known species. However, because of the anthers that open by pores initially, we feel confident in placing the new species in Drymonia.

description: Lianas (or slender trees with scandent branches), essentially glabrous throughout (inflorescence sometimes puberulent), the branches and branchlets opposite or subopposite, slender, subterete (or distally faintly quadrangular), often conspicuously pale-lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, petiolate, the petioles slender, shallowly canaliculate, the leaf-blades decurrent on the petiole; inflorescence axillary or terminal, many-flowered, paniculate-coryinbose, copiously branching, the pedunele and branches conspicuously quadrangular, the branches opposite or subopposite; disk carnose or thin-carnose, erect, short-cylindric, inconspicuous, often thickened at mnargin; stamens 3, suberect, the filaments meini- branous, ligulate, the anthers basifixed, extrorsely nutaant, transversely ellipsoid, dehiscing by extrorse-apical horizontal clefts, at length flat- tened into one plane; description: Plants small, 2-4 mm tall including the sporophytes. Leaves 1.5-2.5 mm long from an oblong base 1/3-1/2 the leaf length, then long subulate with the costa filling the acute subula; cells rectangular and lax below. Perichaetial leaves not noticeably differentiated from vegetative leaves except longer. Autoicous. Seta about 2 mm long, smooth, yellowish, slightly flexuose; capsule ca 1 mm long, at least half being differentiated as a neck with numerous, large, roundish stomata; spore sac ± globular; exothecial cells rectangular, ± thin-walled; annulus differentiated in 2-3 rows of large, thick-walled cells, deciduous; peristome single, short, the teeth triangular, papillose, rarely vertically barred above; operculum long-rostrate, straight, falling with the calyptra. Spores radially symmetrical, not spherical, 25-32 µm in diam., coarsely papillose. Calyptra mitrate, covering about half the capsule, smooth, naked, lobed at base.

description: Shrubs, with copiously resinous young branches. Stipules a sheathing truncate ring, connected to the petioles, persistent. Leaves subsessile to short-petiolate, blades elliptic to broadly obovate, thick-coriaceous, rounded at base and at apex; domatia absent. Flowers axillary and solitary, 2 per node, protandrous, pedicellate; hypanthium obconical. Calyx papery, with 4 foliose lobes, functioning as a pterophyll at fruit maturity. Corolla tubular with short lobes; tube glabrous throughout; lobes 4, rounded at apex; aestivation imbricate. Stamens alternate to the petals; anthers narrowly oblong, dorsifixed near the base, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; filaments attached near the mouth, extremely short, glabrous throughout. Style exserted. Ovary 2-celled, with one seed per locule basally inserted. Fruits pseudosamaras, obconical, indehiscent, with a 4-lobed pterophyll developed from the persistent calyx. Seeds with basal hilum, obovoid, fleshy, smooth.

description: Three species. Annual erect herbs, usu- ally widely branching, more or less stellate pubescent, the stems apparently hollow. Flowers solitary or grouped in the leaf axils, sometimes crowded apically; involucel trimerous, persistent, the bracts linear; calyx 5-lobed; petals white, pinkish, or rose-purple, often showy; androecium included, filamentiferous at apex, the column glabrous; styles 12-35, exceeding androecium, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizo- carpic, a depressed disk, glabrous; mericarps 12-35, indehiscent, reticulate or ridged laterally and dorsally, brown or blackish; seeds solitary, subglabrous. 2n = 20, 40 (three species).

description: Hypanthium ellipsoid, pubescent (and glandular in our species); sepals triangular to oblong, acute or subulate; stamens strongly  dimorphic, the connective considerably prolonged, with 2 long, filiform appendages on the ventral side which are erect and often curved past the anther and often with a small dorsal spur; flowers 4-5- merous; ovary 3-4-celled, with filiform style and punctiform stigma. description: Shrub or tree 0.5-12 m, often unbranched or few-branched; young shoots appressed  pubescent, early glabrescent. Leaves alternate, 1-foliolate, often clustered at apex of  trunk or branch; blade entire, chartaceous, glabrous; venation brochidodromous with midvein raised on both surfaces; petiole canaliculate or flattened adaxially, +/- swollen and articulate at apex, glabrous. Inflorescence lateral but not obviously axillary, a pedunculate dichasium, in age often perennating, branched, elongate, cauline, and bearing pedicellate flowers on short-shoots, or a sessile, short, epiphyllous cyme (in hypophyllanthus). Sepals 5, valvate, variously connate at anthesis forming a campanulate to tubular calyx, 1.5-4.6 cm long, red, white, or green, usually persistent in fruit. Corolla 3.8-7.9 cm long, white, glabrous (short-pu- bescent in E. trichanthus) without; petals 5, connate forming a +/- straight tube, the lobes imbricate, arranged actinomorphically or zygomorphically. Androecium of(4) 5 fertile stamens or of 2 fertile stamens flanking innermost (always upper?) corolla lobe and (1) 3-5 linear staminodes; filaments connate or free from each other and adnate to the corolla; anthers glabrous or pubescent, usually connate at lower adjacent corners by the basal appendages, the appendages apparently modified bases of the thecae. Disc intrastaminal, tubular, taller than ovary, gla- brous. Ovary of 5 carpels free except at apex where they join the style and sometimes at base; ovules 2 per carpel; style 1; stigma capitate and +/- 5-lobed to 5-sulcate. Fruit of five free mericarps (rarely 1 aborting) rarely connate at base, each dehiscing adaxially to or past the apex, +/- transversely ridged  or reticulate, with bony, elastic, separating en- docarp. Seeds 1 or 2 per carpel, ovoid, reniform, or cuboidal, sometimes slightly beaked above the hilum, tuberculate, tomentulose; cotyledons plicate.

description:
Ray florets i, numerous, 2-several-seriate, the corolla consisting of a short tube and a flattened lamina lobed at apex (lamina sometimes reduced or lacking), the stamens none, the style slender, bifid at apex, the achene obovoid-trigonous, glabrous; disk florets e, numerous, the corolla consisting of a narrow tube and a campanulate 5-lobed limb, the stamens 5, glabrous, attached at the summit of the tube, the filaments slender, the anthers membranous, oblong, sagittate-auriculate at base, deltoid-appendiculate at apex, connate at margins, the style undivided, slender, distally swollen and papillose, surrounded at the base by a membranous sheath about 1 mm. long; paleae which subtend the florets usually membranous, concave, distally pilose.

Shrubs or perennial herbs, often densely lanate, the caudex branching or simple, erect or subterranean; leaves alternate (rarely opposite), expanded at base to a coriaceous sheath, usually subentire, pinnate-veined; infloreseence axillary, corymbose-paniculate, spiciform- cymose, racemose, or simple, the branches usually alternate. subtended by bracts; heads pedunculate, the receptacle plane or con- vex, the involuere composed of numerous 1-several-seriate crowded imbricate phyllaries, the phyllaries subequal in length, the outer ones broadest.

description: Schlechter’s enumeration includes three species of Euphrasia from New Guinea, two from the Nassau Range of western or Dutch New Guinea and one from Mount Victoria in southeastern New Guinea, from all of which our present species is clearly distinct. On Carstensz Peak of the Nassau Range are E. culminicola Wernham and E. scutel-larioicles Wernham,11 the former differing from E. mirabilis (below) in leaf-blades entire, flowers in axillary racemes (1), calyx-lobes obtuse or subacute, and upper corolla-lip scarcely shorter than the lower, the latter in calyx-lobes very obtuse and corolla-lobes less than half as long as the tube. On Mt. Victoria is E. papuana Schltr., differing from E. mirabilis in leaf-blades 3-5-lobed, calyx-lobes narrowly triangular, corolla externally glabrous with lobes as long as or longer than the tube, and anthers glabrous. Our plant would seem to come nearest to E. scutellarioides, but is probably further distinguished therefrom by the strongly indurated revolution of the terminal leaf-segment.

description: Arbor parva glaberrima. Folia inferiora alterna, superiora op- posita ( !) vel subopposita, pedatim 5- ad 3-foliolata, in sieco crasse coriaeea, superne creberrime resinoso-punctata, petiolo robusto ad 12 mm. longo suffulta. Foliola subsessilia vel brevissime petiolulata, basi articulata, latissime obovata usque suborbicularia, obtusissima, basi cuneata, nervo mediano permanifesto subtus inerassato obscuro per- cursa, lateralibus parallelis saltem in sieco conspicuis, reticulo venularurn conjulictis; 1-3 majora 6-10.5 cm. longa et 4-7.5 cm. lata, 2 infima minima " stipelliformia, " 1-3.5 cm. longa et 0.8-3 cm. lata, facile eaduca. Infloreseentiae terminales nee non oppositifoliae, 6-7 cm. longae, eymis 3-floris paniculatis compositae, ramis inferioribus sa t longis singulis vel binis oppositis, ramulis oppositis vel ternatis brevius pedunculati; floribus subsessilibus pedicello perbrevi articulato. Bracteae minutae, late triangulares, eire. 1 mm. longae, margine ciliatae. Flores dioici. Alabastra j ovoideo-conica, quadrangularia. Sepala 4, patentia, 2 exteriora majora latissima subobtusa, 2 mm. longa et 2.7 mm. lata, 2 interiora niinora acutiuscula, 1.8 mm. longa et 2.1 mm. lata, omnia margine ciliata. Petala 4 bina arete connata, valvata, 8-9 mm. longa et eire. 3 mm. lata, e basi lata lanceolata, obtusiuscula, carnosa ad 1 mm. crassa, alba (?), extus minute resinoso-punctata. Stamina 4, 4-4.3 mm. longa, antheris late linearibus, obtusis, 2.9-3.2 mm. longis, 1.2-1.5 mm. latis, filamentis 3 mm. longis. description: Probably monotypic. Herbs or subshrubs 1-2.5 m tall with mixed glandular hairs, stellate-puberulence, and harsh stellate-pubescence. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades broadly ovate or more commonly 3-5- lobed, cordate, crenate-serrate, acute. Flow- ers axillary, solitary, exceeding the sub- tending petiole; involucel 8-9-parted, the bractlets shorter than the calyx, distinct; calyx campanulate, half-divided; corolla bright yellow with conspicuous maroon center and prominent meandering veins; androecium much shorter than corolla, purplish; style single, apically 5-parted, hirsute, the stigmas capitate. Fruits oblate with apical beak, 5-locular, 5-winged, transversely veined, stellate-pubescent and hispid; seeds several per locule, subglabrous. 2n = 34 (one species).

description: Erect annual herbs 10-60 cm tall; stems single from a tap root, not developing a rosette; first leaves opposite, the later ones alternate, all simple, tripartite to biternately dissected, the ultimate divisions ovate to narrowly linear; inflorescence open, a dichotomously branched or subeorymbose eyme of 5 to numerous heads; involucre broadly to narrowly turbinate; involueral bracts mostly in a single series, usually with searious margins and often suffused with purple; rays absent; corollas hermaphroditic with well defined tubes and throats, distinctly irregular, white to pinkish-red or purplish; anther sacs rounded at the base, the apex with ovate appendages; style branches flattenied, with well developed, marginal, stigmatic lines, abruptly terminated by a penicillate cuspidate appendage, otherwise glabrous; achenes obpyramidal, 4-sided, the faces smooth or distinctly 3-ribbed; pappus of 8-10 ovate, obovate or truncate scales, the midnerve only rarely extending to the apex or beyond; chromosome numbers, as determined from counts on 5 of the 8 species, x = 10, 12.

description: Monotypic. Perennial caespitose herbs with stellate pubescence. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades ovate or oblong-lanceolate, serrate or crenate, acute or obtuse; stipules linear. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils; pedicels shorter than the petioles, articulating (and ultimately abscissing) immediately at the base of the calyx; involucel absent; calyx 12 mm long at anthesis, accrescent to 17 mm long and flaring to a rotate form in fruit, when taking on a red/burnt-orange color; petals 15 mm long, orange; androe- cium included, filamentiferous at apex; styles 12, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schiz- ocarpic, 9-10 mm diam., a flattened disk with radiating spines, stellate-pubescent; mericarps 12, laterally reticulate below, smooth above, with an endoglossum; seeds solitary, basal, glabrous except on hilum. 2n= 16.

description: Herbae caespitosae, stellato-pubescentes. Folia petiolata, stipulata, simplicia, non lobata, ovata vel oblongo-lanceolata, serrata vel crenato-serrata. Flores in axillis solitarii, longe pedicellati. Bracteae involucrales nullae. Calyx inflatus, alatus, ad medium late 5-lobatus. Petala 5, flava ut videtur. Columna staminalis inclusa, filamentis terminalibus. Styli ramuli numero carpellis aequales. Stigmata capitata. Carpella 12, singulatim ovulum unum pendulum includentia. Fructus schizocarpicus, mericarpio quoque in partem superiorem leavem, pubescentem, loculicidaliter de- hiscentem, spinis dorsalibus binatis suberectis armatam ac in partem inferiorem reticulato-fenestratam, indehiscentem, ad columellam vena singula media basi-dorsali affixam discreto, parte superiore ab inferiore endoglosso separata.

description: Fourteen species. Annual or perennial herbs, ascending or erect, with stellate pubescence. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate or orbicular, usually palmately lobed or parted, crenate or dentate. Flowers some- times solitary, usually in axillary scorpioid cymes; involucel of 3 filiform bractlets; calyx stellate-pubescent, 5-lobed; corolla purplish (sometimes white), shorter than to slightly longer than the calyx; androecium included, the column glabrous or pubescent, filamentiferous at apex, the anthers sometimes purple, few (sometimes only 5); styles 5-15, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, oblate, glabrous; mericarps 5- 15, indehiscent, horseshoe-shaped, with irregular transverse ridges, sometimes with a small endoglossum; seeds solitary, glabrous. 2n = 10, 20, and 30 (several species).

description: Trees (rarely shrubs), to 25 m tall. Young twigs, petioles, and lower side of lamina and primary vein covered with straight and curly hairs. Petioles canaliculate. Lamina of leaves (elliptic-)oblong-obovate, narrowly obovate to obovate, chartaceous to slightly coriaceous, (greenish) brown above, brown below, apex cuspidate to acuminate, base attenuate (acute to nearly rounded), primary vein impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins regularly curved to almost straight, 10-22 on either side of primary vein, impressed (rarely flat) above, raised below, forming distinct loops at obtuse angles, tertiary venation reticulate to percurrent. Inflorescences in foliate zone (rarely cauliflorous), supra-axillary, 1-5(-11)-flowered. Flowering and fruiting peduncles to 5 mm long. Flowering and fruiting pedicels slightly curved. Lower bract cucullate, enclosing axillary bud, caducous. Upper bract midway along the pedicel, initially cucullate and enclosing the flower bud, ultimately rupturing into two parts and their resembling 2 opposing bracteoles, caducous. Flower buds compressed ovoid, ovoid to broadly ovoid. Flowers pendent, creamy, yellowish brown, or whitish yellow, sometimes tinged reddish-purplish on the inner side. Sepals 3, valvate, initially connate ex- cept for apex, ultimately rupturing into 3 subequal, saccate parts. Petals 6, in 2 whorls of 3 each, imbricate, free or connate for basal 1/3, longitudinally veined, outer side densely to totally covered with whitish to (yellowish) brown, appressed hairs. To- rus flat to convex, with concave centre. Staminodes 30-60, in 1-2 spiral cycles around outermost stamens, (pale) yellow, orange to salmon, densely to totally covered with very short, whitish hairs. Stamens 200-300, pale yellow to yellowish brown, orange to salmon, prolonged connective a 5-7-angled disc with convex apex, densely covered with very short, whitish hairs. Carpels 30-100, immersed into concave part of floral receptacle, ovary with one, basal ovule, style and stigma distinct, ovary and style densely papillate, styles coherent, stigma dark brown to black, densely to totally covered with hairs. Fruit syncarpous, yellowish green to dark purplish outside, yellowish, orange to salmon-pink inside (in vivo), (broadly) ovoid to subglobose with a truncate or cordate base, torus remnants mostly protruding, fertile carpels 30-100, areoles mostly delineated by dark lines or shallow grooves, hexagonal, smooth or tu- berculate. Seeds reddish brown to dark brown, shiny, aril composed of densely packed, fiber-like structures, ruminations lamellate in four equal parts, raphe a flat to slightly raised rib, shallowly canaliculate, straight, indistinct.

description: Gasteranthus Benth. is a genus of ca. 20 species related to Besleria L. but having fleshy capsules rather than berries, leaves with stomata in groups, and a dorsal or dorsally thickened nectariferous disc rather than annular (Wiehler, 1975). Two subgroups within Gasteranthus are easily distin- guished. The first subgroup with subventricose to funnelform, white, yellow, or red corollas apparently comprises 14 species ranging from Costa Rica to Ecuador. The second subgroup with urceolate flowers apparently comprises seven species ranging from Mexico to Peru, all of which are represented in eastern Ecuador except for the new species described here.

description: Perennial herbs, sometimes slightly woody at base, with a more or less spiciform inflorescence. Flowers opeln near sunset. Petals white or yellow, often fadinog reddish. Anthers versatile. Sporogenous tissue divided into packets in each locule. Stigma 4-lobed, the receptive surface mostly inside but the ends of the lobes receptive all around. Capsule woody, indehiscent, few-seeded. Basic chromosome number, x = 7. Self-incompatibility known.

description: Thirty-three species. Erect herbs or sub shrubs, sparingly branched, minutely puberulent, sometimes also pilose. Leaves sometimes distichous, petiolate, the blades ovate to oblong, cordate, crenate, serrate, or subentire, acute, minutely puberulent. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, sometimes nodding; involucel absent; calyx small, basally rounded, more than half-divided, not prominently nerved; petals usually yellow; androecium included, filamentiferous at apex, the anthers yellow or orange; styles 8-30, slender, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, sparsely pubescent to glabrate, subglobose to broadly subconical mericarps 8-30, somewhat inflated, dehiscent, 1-seeded, usually with specialized pectinate endoglossum arising ventrally and encircling the seed; seeds more or less puberulent. 2n = 12 (several species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Slender anllual herbs. Flowers ope-n in the morning. Petals white, fading rose-purplish. Anthers versatile, attached near the base. Sporogenous tissue continuous. Stiama capitate. Capsule many-seeded, bilocular. Basic chromosome number, x = 7. Self-compatible.

description: Annual herbs; stems slender, often filiform above, the cortex usually exfoliat- ing near the base; leaves alternate or the lowest sometimes subopposite, nar- rowly lanceolate, entire, sessile or narrowed to short petioles; flowers axillary, opening in the morning, closing about noon of the same day, abseising at the top of the ovary on the second day; sepals 4, reflexed individually or in pairs at anthesis; hypanthium very short, obscure; petals 4, oblong, about twice as long as broad, entire, white with a yellow or greenish-yellow spot or pair of spots at the base, [becoming pink or red as they close; stamens 8 in 2 series, those opposite the sepals longer and with larger anthers; anthers versatile, the sporogenous tissue continuous in each anther sac; pollen cream or yellow, tricolporate, shed individually; stigma entire, globose or hemispherical; ovary 2-celled; ovules few to many; capsules terete or flattened, 4-valved, subsessile or with conspicuous pedicels, the valves at maturity free from the septum, or two remain- ing attached; seeds ovoid, glabrous or pubescent, without appendages.

description: Annual hemi-parasitic herb, erect and basally branched with 2 to several ascending stems. Primary root diffusely branching and bearing haustorial attachments. Leaves sessile, entire or with one pair of lobes, the basal opposite, the upper alternate. Inflorescence a narrow raceme with few and scarcely overlapping flowers, the flowers short-pedicellate in the axils of sessile semi-clasping bracts. Calyx shorter than the corolla-tube, tubular and somewhat 4-sided, shallowly 4-cleft with a deeper anterior cleft. Corolla narrowly tubular below, strongly galeate above with the enlarged upper lip rounded on the upper surface and curving outward, ending in a pointed or minutely bifid apex, the galea enclosing the anthers and, at least initially, the stigma. Lower lip highly reduced, consisting of 3 small teeth with incurving lateral margins, terminating 3 scarcely inflated folds of the central tube. Anthers didynamous, each anther 2-celled with the upper cell larger and attached mid-dorsally to the filament, the smaller lower cell attached apically. Style slender, arching forward, the shallowly bilobed stigma included to slightly exserted from the galea. Ovary 2-celled, the numerous ovules horizontally disposed. Capsule dehiscing loculicidally, the numerous small seeds with loose reticulate testa.
bibliographicCitation: Breedlove, Dennis E. 1970. Gentrya, a New Genus of Scrophulariaceae from Mexico. Brittonia. 22 (1): 20-24.

description: Herbae annuae. Folia sessilia, integra vel bilobata. Inflorescentia racemosa angusta simplex erecta. Corolla valde galeata, labio supero dorsaliter rotundato extrinsecus curvato, infero valde reducto, dentibus tribus tantum consistente. Antherae didy- namae, bicellulares, theca supera majore filamento mediodorsaliter affixa, infera minore filamento apicaliter affixa. Ovarium bicellulare, ovulis numerosis. Capsula loculicide dehiscens. Semina parva, testa laxe reticulata.

description: Shrub or small tree, epiphytic or rarely terrestrial, to 5 m tall; young branches terete or angled, glabrate to pubescent; older stems with a light-colored bark. Leaves opposite or subopposite, equal or anisophyllous; petioles short, the base persistent as a conspicuous bump on older stems, not conspicuously thickened; blade simple, entire, often elliptic, coriaceous, subcoriaceous, or rarely chartaceous, often gland-dotted, the domatia often present in the axils of the secondary veins and the midvein below. Flowers solitary or cymose, if cymose, often fasciculate; pedicels elongate, usually bracteate, usually thicker above; calyx campanulate, often brightly colored in purples and reds, often 5-winged, persistent and of- ten accrescent in fruit, truncate, with 5 lobe-like lateral enations; corolla tubular to narrowly funnelform, slightly zygomorphic, often brightly colored in shades of purple, pink, magenta, or red, rarely white, 5-lobed, the lobes rounded, subequal, much shorter than the tube; stamens 4, equal or slightly didynamous, included, free, inserted above the base of the corolla tube, the filaments filiform, bent near the apex, the anthers 2, separate, with a broad connective; stami- node 1, usually shorter than the stamens; disk lacking; ovary bilocular, many-ovulate, the style elongate, longer than the stamens, the style capitate. Fruit a globose to subglobose berry, pale green, white, or pale pink; seeds many, the seed coat reticulate, the margins or the reticulae often laciniate or bearing elongate filaments, the endosperm absent in mature seeds, the embryo straight.

description: Annual herb. Time of opening of flowers unknown. Petals mueh shorter than sepals, probably white. Anthers small, attached near the base. Sporogenous tissue continuous. Carlquist, pers. comm.). Chromo- some number and compatibility system unknown. Said to have "milky juice," this unknown elsewhere in the family.

description: Shrubs, when pubescent the hairs incompletely septate; stipules entire. Inflorescences terminal, paniculate-spiciform. Corolla hypocrateriform, pubescent internally at the throat, the corolla lobes 4, their aestivation irregular, 2 or 3 internal valvate and 1 or 2 external imbricate lobes (as Hooker, 1873, and Liogier, 1962, observed); stamens 4, inserted at the middle of the corolla tube; stigma 4-lobed. Ovary 4-locular, the ovules numerous on a discoid placenta. Fruit globose; seeds (Fig. 7) 0.2-0.8 mm long, 0.1-0.2 mm in diam, foveolate; seed coat (Figs. 8, 9) with polygonal cells, 54-150 (144) x 42-84 (58.8) µm, moderately large pits scattered in the internal walls, (Figs. 8, 9) 18-54 pits per cells, 3-6 µm in diam, the lateral walls thick, 3-7 µm thick.

description: Fifty species. Trees and shrubs, usually erect (rarely procumbent, but not among American species), stellate-pubescent to glabrate, more or less gland-dotted throughout. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate, weakly lobed or deeply parted, entire, with 1 or more abaxial foliar nectaries (these rarely absent); stipules subulate to falcate, caducous or persistent, sometimes prominent. Flowers solitary (rarely several) in the leaf axils or in sympodial inflorescences; pedicels usually surmounted by trimerous involucellar nectaries; involucel of 3 bracts that are often cordate, foliaceous, laciniate or dentate (sometimes entire), enclosing the bud and persisting in fruit, the bracts sometimes reduced to linear straps, small scales, or deciduous at anthesis; calyx truncate or 5-dentate (sometimes 5-lobed); corolla campanulate or funnelform, usually large and showy, the petals white, cream, yellow, or rose, sometimes with a dark spot at the base, often gland-dotted; androecium included, apically 5-dentate, the anthers nu- merous; style single, with 3-5 decurrent stigmatic lobes, ± exceeding the androecium. Capsules glabrous (rarely pubescent), often prominently gland-dotted, ovoid, dehiscent, 3-5-loculate; seeds densely lanate (rarely subglabrous). 2n = 26 or 52 (counts for most species have been reported).

description: Vascularization (Fig. 5, A-O). -The vascular pattern of the Grabowskia flower is equivalent to the one described for Lycium. Anyway, some differences in the ovarian bundles can be distinguished (Bernardello, 1986). Calyx. -Thick, tubular or campanulate, with equal or unequal lobes. Normally it does not split when the fruit ripens. Occasionally, it has two rows of opposite lobes: five normal ones, more or less perpendicular to the corolla, and five extra lobes parallel to it (Fig. 5A). The calyx is glabrous or rarely glabrescent, with "type IV" glandular trichomes (Bernardello, 1982a). Anatomically, it is composed of two epidermal layers and 7 to 25 layers of collenchymatous-like cells with walls mainly formed by pectic substances and cellulose. In all species, the inner epidermis, whether single or multi-layered, is secretory, except for the inner face of each lobe and a narrow ring surrounding the corolla base (Figs. 5A, I-L; 6C-E). Cells with thick radial and outer tangential cellulose walls and large vacuoles are elongated at the calyx base and shorten toward the apex, where they are isodiametric or papilla-like. In buds there is much more secretory activity than in open flowers, and the exudate is concealed between the calyx and corolla. I have not observed insects of any kind seeking the exudate. Corolla. -White, yellowish-white or lilac, usually with green, brown, or dark purple veins. The corolla is infundibuliform with a middle-sized tube and long lobes. It abscises from its base without leaving a ring of tissue as in Lycium. Androecium. -Equivalent to that described for Lycium in morphology and anatomy. Anther dehiscence corresponds to "type 1" (Bernardello, 1983b). The suture zone is formed by four or five layers of small isodiametric cells. Although in Lycium and Phrodus the cells of the suture zone do not have crystal sand, in Grabowskia an extremely fine crystal sand is present. Morphological flower type. - Grabowskia species have similar flowers with scarcely any interspecific variation. The calyx is the most variable whorl and the gynoecium is typical due to the presence of two false septa in the ovary apex and has four-ovuled carpels and a circular green or yellowish nectary (Bernardello, 1986).
bibliographicCitation: Bernardello, Luis M. 1987. Comparative floral morphology in Lycieae (Solanaceae). Brittonia. 39: 112-- 129.

description: Flowers 4-5-merous; hypanthium tubular or narrowly campanu- late, the sepals conspicuous and triangular, or the calyx irregularly splitting at anthesis; petals moderate in size; stamens isomorphic or nearly so; anthers subulate, usually with crenulate pollen-sacs, strongly inflexed from the filament and consequently nearly horizon- tal or declined, usually arcuate, the connective prolonged dorsally at the base into a short, sharp spur which is nearly or quite erect and frequently simulates an extension of the filament; stigmna truncate or punctiform.

description: Shrubs to 2.0 m tall, branching from the base; stems unbranched or angularly branched; leaves sclerophyllous, dispersed evenly on stems or clustered at branch tips, spreading to ascendant-erect, occasionally appressed, sessile or short-petiolate, broadly linear, linear-lanceolate, narrowly spatulate, obovate or ovate, dark green to dark yellow-green, bases truncate or cuneate, apices obtuse or acute, apiculate, margins entire or minutely denticulate, glabrous or scabrate, surfaces glabrous, glandular-punctate, usually resinous. Capitulescences densely pa- niculate or corymbose, bracteate or not; peduncles 0-4.0 mm long, glabrous or scabrate-scabridulous, resinous; capitula borne in clusters of 1-5, these clusters borne in racemes or corymbs, these in turn borne paniculately or corymbosely; involucres cy- lindric, turbinate, or narrowly obconic, 3.0- 6.0 mm high, 2.0-4.0 mm wide, phyllaries 13-25 in 3-5 series, linear-lanceolate or ovate, 1.0-4.5 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm wide, with a single central resin-canal, bases char- taceous-coriaceous, whitish yellow-tan, apices herbaceous, acute or acuminate, glandular-pustulate, resinous, margins hyaline- winged; receptacles flat, foveolate to alveolate; ray florets 3-8, corollas white to creamy-white; corollas 3.2-6.5 mm long, tubes 1.8-3.2 mm long, limbs 2.0-3.5 mm long, 1.3-2.0 mm wide; disk florets 3-10, corollas white to creamy-white, funnel- shaped, glabrous or minutely hispid-pilose at juncture of tube and throat, 4.0-5.5 mm high, tubes 1.0-2.2 mm long, throats 3.0- 3.3 mm long, lobes 2.0-2.5 mm long, laxly erect to laxly recurved, rarely acutely so; anthers exserted at anthesis, appendages linear-lanceolate; styles 6.0-7.5 mm long at full anthesis, branches 0.9-1.5 mm long, appendages 0.5-0.8 mm long, lanceolate or narrowly triangular, flat to concave adaxi- ally, slightly convex abaxially, brushing hairs merely papillate. Cypselas cylindric, 1.0-2.5 mm high, 0.3-0.6 mm diam., grayish brown or coppery-bronze, 5-ribbed, sparsely straight-pilose, trichomes 0.2-0.5 mm long, white; pappus of 30-70 fine, minutely barbellate bristles in 1(2) series, 3.5-5.0 mm high, whitish tan, yellowish white, or pinkish coppery.

description: Twenty species. Trees or shrubs, mostly dioecious, glabrate or stellate-pubescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades elliptic, ovate, or weakly lobed, entire, minutely gland-dotted, with 1 or more abaxial foliar nectaries; stipules caducous, not prominent. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or in axillary fascicles, generally in greater abundance in staminate than in pistillate plants, each flower subtended by an involucel of 3 (rarely more) inconspicuous bractlets, some times also by 3 involucellar nectaries; calyx more or less truncate; petals whitish, gland- dotted, reflexed; staminate flowers usually with short (rudimentary) staminal column and numerous exserted anthers, gynoecium absent; pistillate flowers with rudimentary androecium, recurved style, 3-4 decurrent stigmatic lobes. Capsules globose to elongate, dehiscent, 3-4-loculate, densely puberulent; seeds 1 to several per locule, glabrous, arillate, the aril fleshy, white (when fresh), surrounding half of seed. 2n = 26 (five species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.
