description: Unarmed trees or shrubs, mostly dioecious (except sect. Standleya), glabrate or -invested with stellate hairs. Leaves alternate, stipulate, entire, simple or weakly -lobed, minutely punctate, with abaxial foliar nectaries, sometimes having basal auriculate appendages. Flowers fragrant, in axillary fascicles (or in H. micrantha on branched axillary peduncles), each flower subtended by three small involucral brac- teoles and sometimes by three involucral nectaries. Calyx gamophyllous, nectariferous within, truncate or nearly so, usually torn in flower and fruit. Petals 5, white (or yellow), punctate, reflexed. Staminate flowers with numerous exserted anthers, no gynoecium. Pistillate flowers usually with a reduced androecium, a single recurved style, and decurrent stigma (three species with perfect flowers). Capsules stipitate, globose to elongate, densely puberulent, 3- (rarely 4-) celled. Seeds glabrous, arillate. Cotyledons conduplicate, punctate. Chromosome number: n = 13.

description: Tall shrubs or large trees, to 30 m. or more in height. Flowers open at sunset. Petals white, fading pinkish. Anthers versatile. Sporogenous tissue of each locule divided by sterile tissue into staggered packets. Stigma hemispherical. Capsule woody, many-seeded. Seeds broadly winged. Basic chromosome num- ber, x = 10. Self-compatible.

description: Plants annual, biennial, or perennial. Stems one to several, originating from root, unbranched to paniculately branched above, sulcate below, becoming striate above, glabrous to densely pubescent, unwinged or weakly to strongly winged by the decurrent leaves. Peduncles striate, glabrous to variously pubescent, slightly to considerably broadened beneath the receptacle. Leaves linear to lanceolate, elliptic to oblong- elliptic to spatulate, laciniate to pinnatifid; sessile to petioliform sometimes with clasping bases; margins entire to deeply toothed or lobed; apices rounded to nar- rowly acuminate; glabrous to variously pubescent; midrib prominent, lateral veins obscure to obvious; dotted with impressed glands. Heads solitary to numerous, con- vex to globose, ovoid or conical, 4-24 mm high, 4-33 mm wide (excluding rays). Receptacle convex to narrowly conic, alveolate. Involucre of two series of lanceolate bracts, the outer exceeding the inner and united at the base or free, reflexed to spread- ing at anthesis, glabrous to densely pubescent, dotted with impressed glands. Ray florets present or absent, sterile or fertile, 7 to ca. 40 per head; ligules 2-37 mm long, usually 3-lobed, completely yellow, variously tinged at the base with red, or reddish brown to burnt orange, glabrous to densely pubescent on the under surface. Disc florets bisexual and fertile; disc corollas 4- or 5-lobed, cylindrical to cylindric-cam- panulate to urceolate, 1-6 mm long, yellow to yellow-green with yellow, brown, reddish brown or purple lobes. Achenes 0.6-3.0 mm long, glabrous to densely pubescent, ribbed. Pappus of 5-10 scales or absent, 0.05-5.0 mm long, entire to fimbriate, from minute to exceeding the disc corolla in length, obtuse, acute, acuminate, or awned.

description: Shrubs or trees with punctate glands usually visible on all unlignified parts; buds densely sericeous; young shoots pubescent, usually early glabrescent. Leaves (sub-)opposite, digitately 3-foliolate, densely glandular-punctate, velutinous to pubescent to glabrous; petiole semiterete, flat to canaliculate adaxially or sometimes acutely winged, with a reduced, hairy appendage or a tuft of long trichomes adaxially at apex; leaflets sessile or rarely short-petiolulate, conspicuously articulate at junction with the grooved petiole apex, membranous to chartaceous or subcoriaceous, margin entire (seldom irregularly crenulate), terminal leaflet symmetric and larger than the lateral ones, the latter usually asymmetric at base; venation brochidodromous, the midvein usually raised on both surfaces. Inflorescence a terminal polytelic diplothyrse or (in H. parvifolia) monothyrse, longer or shorter than the leaves, lax, the branches (sub-)opposite, patent, peduncle short or absent; bracts and prophylls (bractlets) scale-like, usually paired. Flowers perfect, actinomorphic, 4- 5-merous. Sepals united at base, quincuncial, persistent in fruit, scarious, usually slightly erose or ciliolate. Petals free, imbricate in bud, pellucid-punctate, glabrous, hyaline and erose or ciliolate or entire at margin, spreading at anthesis. Stamens as many as the petals, alternipetalous, free, glabrous; filaments complanate, translucent, inserted below the disk, reflexed after anthesis; anthers ovoid or heart-shaped, dorsifixed below the middle, versatile, introrse, 2-locular, the locules somewhat divergent at base. Disk intrastaminal, cupular, forming an erect, undulate rim, 4-5-lobed, each lobe 2-lobulate, surrounding and of about the same height as the ovary, glabrous. Ovary depressed-globose, of 4-5 connate carpels but conspicuously 4-5-lobed, 4-5-loculed, minutely glandular-tuberculate, glabrous or pubescent; ovules 2 per cell, collateral, pendulous; style 1, terete, glabrous; stigma discoid to capitate, slightly 4-5-lobed. Fruit a samarium of (3-) 4-5 samaroid mericarps, velutinous to glabrous, separating at maturity acropetally, each with an ellipsoid-trigonal seeded body and a dorsal ascending, obtuse, chartaceous to subcoriaceous wing, velutinous to glabrous; seed 1 per carpel, free from the endocarp, oblong, with a thin testa and fleshy endosperm, glabrous; embryo fleshy, with straight, oblong cotyledons and a superior radicle, surrounded by a thin layer of a soft endosperm.

description: Lianas or erect woody plants, the branehes stout, glabrous, terete, the branehlets opposite, slender, terete, sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite, rarely subopposite, petiolate; inflorescences axillary or rarely crowded ill groups of 4-6 at apices of short leafless branehlets, paniculate or pseudoeymose, pedunculate; flowers loosely arranged, usually solitary at apices of ultimate brancehlets, comparatively large for the family, pedicellate; sepals 5, imbricate; petals 5, erecto-patent or spreading; disk thick-earnose, conspicuous, annular-pulvinate, slightly narrowed and entire at margin, glabrous, not obscuring the petal-bases; stamens 3, suberect or spreading, inserted within the disk, the filaments membranous, ligulate, conspicuously broadenied and nearly contiguous at base, the anithers basifixed, transversely ellipsoid, the locules 2, laterally confluenit, dehiscing by extrorse-apical horizonital confluent clefts; ovary carnose, semi-immersed in disk, depressed-glo- bose-trigonous, soon conspicuously 3-lobed, the style carnose, subulate, the stigmas obscure, the locules 3, the ovules 6-8 (often 7) per locule, essenltially 2-ranked, often imbricate; fruiting infloreseeniee swollenl, the fruits few, capsular, the capsules 3, spreadinig in a shallowly cam- panulate cup, connate at basal margins, slightly convex oln both surfaces, emarginate at apex, bluntly cariniate anid dehiscing alonig a median suture (adjacent halves often coherent), the pericarp coriaceous; seeds 6-8, erect from base, at maturity completely occupying the capsule-cavity, affixed by a basal wing, the embryoniferous portion apical, coriaceous, the winlg membranous, with a single longitudinal nerve near center, the raphe conlspicuous, ascending along the outer margin.

description: Hypanthium campanulate; sepals triangular or broadly rounded; petals obovate or oblong, usually apiculate just below the apex; stamens isomorphic, with slender glabrous filaments; anthers linear, attenuate above and 1-pored, the connective not prolonged, simple nearly so; ovary completely inferior, 5-6-celled, the style sometimes pilose, usually somewhat thickened above and bearing a truncate or slightly capitate stigma. Shrubs or trees, with ample, usually plinerved leaves pubescent beneath with stellate hairs and lateral clusters of medium-sized flowers. About 15 species in the tropics from Rio de Janeiro to the West Indies, most abundant in the Amazonian forests.

description: Flowers 4-5-merous; hypanthium campanulate, small; calyx truncate or with short lobes; petals mostly oblong, acute or acuminate; stamens isomorphic; filaments slender, glabrous; anthers short, oblong or linear-oblong, obtuse, the connective neither appendaged nor prolonged; ovary inferior, 4-5-celled; style filiform, with a truncate or punctiform stigma. Trees or shrubs, with clusters of small flowers on the old wood at the scars of the fallen leaves. Nearly 30 species in tropical America, most abundant in the West Indies and extending south to Brazil and Peru.

description: Plantae herbaceae vel suffruticosae ad 1 m altae, ramosae, glabrae, rarius pubescentes. Folia alterna, laminis in petiolum decrescentibus, integris, membranaceis, anguste ovatis vel lanceolatis, acutis. Cymulae 1-aliquot in axillis foliorum dispositae. Flores hermaphroditi, bracteati et 2- bracteolati. Sepala 5, subaequalia, ovata vel lanceolata, acuta vel acuminata. Stamina 5, basi in cupulam membranaceam dilatata, laciniis interjectis nulls, antheris 2-locularibus. Ovarium lenticulari- ovoideum. Stylus erectus, stigmatibus 2. Ovulum 1, funiculo brevi erectum. Utriculus globosus, leviter compressus, perianthio inclusus, indehiscens vel irregulariter dehiscens. Semen erectum, sublenticulare, testa crustacea punctulata nigra nitida, arillo nullo.

description: Six or more species. Herbs, subshrubs, or shrubs, erect or decumbent, pubescent or hirsute, sometimes viscid. Leaves petiolate (sometimes subsessile), the blades ovate, cordate, dentate; stipules minute, subulate, caducous. Flowers often solitary in the leaf axils or borne on several-flowered peduncles; involucel absent; calyx lobes lanceolate or ovate; petals white; androecium included, filamentiferous at apex; styles 10- 14, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, oblate, inflated, pendulous; mericarps 10- 14, pubescent or hispid, with fragile walls, dehiscent, 1-3-seeded; seeds glabrous or minutely scabridulous. 2n = 14 (one spe- cies), 2n = 12 (one species).

description: Herbaceous or somewhat woody climbers. Stems branched, the internodes usually terete, smooth or rarely pubescent, unarmed. Leaves jointed at very apex of the petiole; blades broad, mostly lanceolate, ovate or oval, net-veined with 5-9 costas, of which outermost 1 or 2 pairs running along margins; petioles sheathing at base with narrow wings; tendrils mostly present, arising immediately above the sheathing portion of the petiole. Plants dioecious. Inflorescences a solitary umbel borne at 2 to several basal leaf axils of branches, often the first 1 or 2 subtending leaves reduced to a scale; peduncles non-prophyllate at base, obcom- pressed. Perianths of both staminate and pistillate flowers connate into a bottle-shaped organ, open only at apex with 3 teeth. Staminate flowers with 3, 6 or rarely 9-12 stamens contained in the bottle-shaped perianth; filaments connate below or for the entire length forming a synandrium; anthers free, ovate, introrse, the connective projecting beyond the theca as an acute appendage. Pistillate flowers with up to 3 needle-like staminodia; pistil located at bottom of the bottle-shaped perianth, the ovary ovoidal, 3-locular, containing 1 or 2 ovules in each cell; stigmas 3, short, erect or patent, sessile. Fruits a berry with 1-6 seeds.

description: Low, evergreen, aromatic herbs with essentially glabrous, coriaceous, lustrous leaves, the blades varying from triangular- to ovate- or cordate-sagittate or -sub- hastate, or from cordate to orbicular or reniform, often mottled light green, the petioles much longer than the blades, with a bud in the axil, borne on thick, short rhizomes with scale leaves, each branch bearing one normal leaf each season, this usually persisting into the next season. Roots thick and fleshy with slender branch roots. Flowers solitary, terminal on the branches, subtended by a keel- shaped bract, the pedicels relatively short, often curved. Vestigial petals none. Calyces flask-shaped, cylindric, cylindro-urceolate, or cylindro-campanulate, often with a more or less prominent flare about the middle or above, with three actinomorphic (rarely slightly zygomorphic), obtuse to acute, erect or more or less spreading lobes, the tips sometimes incurved; colored on the outside different shades of brown, purplish to yellowish, mostly light to dark purplish on the in- side of the tube, the lobes purplish to red on the inside and often marked with colorless spots or streaks; glabrous on the outside, more or less pilose inside the lobes and upper part of the tube, sometimes ridged or ridged-reticulate inside the lower part of the tube. Stamens 12 (in 2 whorls), epigynous, sessile or with very short filaments, the outer whorl (i.e. opposite the styles) slightly shorter than the inner, the anther-connective with or without a short, blunt extension (appendage). Ovaries .wholly superior or only partly inferior, 6-celled, the placentae central with relatively few ovules. Styles 6, separate, erect, extending more or less above the orbicular to elliptic, slightly raised, extrorse stigmas, the ex- tension grooved on both sides radially and more or less bifid. Mature ovaries usually dehiscing by general disintegration. Seeds obovate, concave on the upper side with a prominent caruncle.

description: About 200 species. Subshrubs, shrubs, or trees (rarely herbs), glabrescent, pubescent, or hispid. Leaves petiolate, the blades elliptic, lanceolate, ovate, or cordate, sometimes lobed or parted, dentate or less commonly subentire; abaxial foliar nectaries some- times present. Flowers usually solitary (sometimes fasciculate) in the leaf axils, sometimes aggregated apically; pedicels long or short; involucel present (rarely suppressed), the involucellar bracts 8-10(20), distinct or basally connate; calyx symmetrical, 5-lobed; petals yellow (sometimes with a purple spot at base), lavender, red, or other colors, sometimes large and showy; staminal column apically 5-dentate, the anthers numerous; styles 5, distally free, with capitate stigmas. Capsules ovoid or oblong, 5-loculate, glabrous or pubescent, dehiscent; seeds several in each locule, glabrescent to hirsute. Chromosome number extremely variable.

description: Two species. Erect subshrubs with scattered to dense stellate and simple pubescence. Leaves petiolate or sessile, the blades ovate, deeply cordate, serrate-crenate, acute or acuminate, more or less discolorous; stipules filiform, ciliate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or in terminal racemes or lax panicles; involucel absent; calyx pubescent, half-divided (or sometimes more deeply divided), the lobes more or less cordate, acuminate, more or less accrescent; petals yellow, equaling the calyx to 3 times as long as calyx; androecium glabrous, pallid, included, filamentiferous at the apex; styles 10-20, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, pubescent, blackish at maturity; mericarps 10-20, apically acute or aristate, dehiscent, with 2 minute spines or knobs at base on dorsal angle, 5-seeded with an endoglossum positioned below the lowermost seed; seeds essentially glabrous but often minutely and sparsely scabridulous. 2n = 14 (one species).

description: Essentially leafless much-branched shrubs, the branches all spine-tipped; infloreseence a short and dense mixed panicle; dioecious; sepals 5-8; petals 6-8; staminate flowers with 12-16 stamens whose filaments are densely hairy below, the short gynophore or disk present, the carpels absent; pistillate flowers with rudimentary stamens and 6-8 weakly united carpels, these with a short and broad common style and divergent stigmas, the style and stigmas, when viewed from above, resembling a starfish; ovules 1 in each carpel; fruit of several distinct drupes less than 1 cm. long.

description: Four species. Erect herbs or subshrubs, stellate-tomentose or stellate-scabrous. Leaves petiolate, the blades suborbicular, ovate, or lanceolate, obscurely crenate-dentate, obtuse to acute; stipules 2-5 mm long, subulate, deciduous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or paniculately aggregated; involucel absent; calyx 5-lobed; petals 2-3 times the length of the calyx, yellow-orange or lavender, often drying bluish; androecium included, pallid or yellowish, filamentiferous at apex; styles 6-11, exceeding the androecium, the stigmas capitate, purplish. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 6-11, dehiscent and flaring apically, glabrous or slightly pubescent, basally rugose, usually with two prominent apical wings, with a solitary seed in the base and usually also with 1-2 seeds in the upper part; seeds minutely pu- bescent or verruculate. 2n = 30 (three species).

description: Frutices vel arbores parvae. Folia integra oblonga vel oblongo-linearia glabra vel subtus lanato-tomentosa. Flores parvi in inflorescentiis terminalibus vel axillaribus dispositi. Calycis tubus campanulatus, extus puberulus, intus pilosus; lobi 5 acuti imbricati. Petala 5, parva, sessilia, decidua. Stamina 5-9 ad marginem adaxialem calycis tubi disposita, filamentis filiformibus brevibus in annulum connatis; staminodia (stamina ananthera) 3-7 parva staminibus diametricaliter opposita; antherae parvae, basifixae. Ovarium ad medium calycis tubi insertum extus dense puberulum 2-loculare, loculis uni-ovulatis. Stylus basilaris filiformis ut videtur simplex revera e stylis 3 connatis formatus, stigmate truncato, breviter 3-lobo. Fructus drupaceus 1- vel 2-locularis extus laevis intus dense pilosus, endocarpio duro tenui extus laevi longitudinaliter in partes 4-6 dehiscente.

description: Shrubs or small trees with hermaphrodite flowers 1.5-3 mm long. Lower leaf surface glabrous or woolly-tomentose, stomata visible at a magnification of x 25. Inflorescence a few-flowered, terminal or axillary raceme of cymules. Bracts and bracteoles small, persistent, not enclosing the flowers in small groups. Receptacle subcampanulate, slightly asymmetric, shortly puberulous outside, hairy inside throughout, but most hairy at the throat. Sepals 5, acute. Petals 5, small, not exceeding the calyx lobes. Stamens and staminodes inserted on the free margin of the disk; stamens 5-9, included, filaments short, grouped towards one side of the receptacle and with 3-7 vestigial staminodes inserted opposite to them. Ovary monocarpellary, bilocular, inserted mid-way up the receptacle, densely hairy outside. Style truncate but distinctly 3-lobed at apex, hairy at base. Fruit a small, fleshy drupe, bilocular or often with one loculus underdeveloped; epicarp smooth; mesocarp thin, fleshy; endocarp hard, thin, bony with a smooth surface, interior very hairy, with 4-6 longitudinal lines of weakness which allow the seedling to escape.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1979. New genera and species of Chrysobalanaceae from Malesia and Oceania. Brittonia. 31: 79-95.

description: Twining herbs. Leaves serrate, the teeth glandular. stipules 2. Flowers solitary, axillary, sepals 5, free; corolla strongly zygomorphic, petals 5, free, the anterior petal clawed, concave or saccate at base; stamens 5, membranous connective appendages at apex of anthers; carpels 3. Capsule thin-walled, chartaceous, opening by a single longitudinal slit; seeds obovate in dorsal view with two lateral expansions at the base.

description: Low, glabrous or pubeseent, herbaceous perennials with slender creeping stems or rootstocks. Leaves petiolate, peltate or non-peltate, entire or parted to the base; petioles slender. Infloreseence usually a simple umbel, sometimes proliferous, or an interrupted spike; pedun- dles axillary, subsessile to much exceeding the leaves; involuere absent or present; flowers white, greenish or yellow; petals ovate, plane; calyx teeth minute or obsolete; stylopodium depressed to conspicuously coni- cal. Fruit transversely ovate to orbicular, strongly flattened laterally; dorsal surface rounded or acute, the lateral ribs conspicuous, slender, acute, rarely obscure, the dorsal ribs acute, rarely obscure; mericarp orbicular to triangular in cross-section; seed ovate to ovate-oblong in cross-section; seed face plane to convex; oil-bearing cells conspicuous to obsolete; strengtheninog cells surrounding the seed cavity.

description: Lianas or slender trees with scandent branches, glabrous through-out, the branches and branchlets usually opposite, swollen at nodes, sparsely lenticellate; leaves opposite or subopposite, petiolate, the peti- oles shallowly canaliculate; inflorescence paniculate-corymbose or pseudo-cymose, pedunculate, the branchlets sometimes capillaceous; flowers very small (not more than 2 mm. in diameter), sometimes abor- tive sepals 5, membranous, acute or subacute, narrow for the family; petals 5, membranous, rounded at apex; disk membranous to thin-carnose, erect, short-cylindric; stamens 3, suberect or reflexed, the filaments membranous, ligulate, gradually broadened toward base, the anthers basifixed, extrorsely nutant, subglobose or transversely oblong, dehiscing by extrorse-apical horizontal confluent clef ts; ovary depressed-subglobose-trigonous, the style carnose, the stigmas obscure, the locules 3, the ovules 4 or 6 per locule, 2-ranked, ascending from the inner basal angle; fruiting infloreseenee swollen, the fruits probably 1 per infloreseence, capsular, the capsules 3, divergent, separately at- tached to a greatly swollen receptacle, conspicuously convex on both surfaces, rounded and blunt at margins, dehiscing along an obseure median suture, the pericarp coriaceous, woody; seeds 4-6 (or fewer by abortion), at maturity eompletely oceupying the capsule-cavity, erect from base, affixed by a comparatively inconspicuous basal wing, the embryoniferous portion apical, thick-coriaceous, imperceptibly passing into the coriaceous wing; wing with a single obscure longitudinal vein, the raphe thickened, ascending along the outer margin, immersed in wing and hardly apparent.

description: Erect annual or biennial (rarely perennial?) herbs, 30-70 cm tall; stems usually single from a tap root and at first developing an inconspicuous rosette (rarely several stems develop following injury); leaves alternate, biternately or triternately divided into linear divisions; infloreseence a subcorymbose eyme of 5 to numerous heads; involuere turbinate to hemispheric; involueral bracts searious, in 1 or 2 series; rays present in only one species (H. wislizeni), these inconspicuous, 3-4 mm long; disc corollas hermaphroditic, distinctly zygomorphic, white to lavender-pink or pale yellow, the 5 lobes of various lengths; anther sacs rounded at the base, the apex with ovate appendages; style branches flattened to nearly terete (in H. wislizeni) with distinct marginal stigmatic lines, the apex with rather small, conic or swollen, obtuse appendages; achenes obpyramidal, 4-sided, the faces conspicuously nerved to smooth; pappus composed of 12-18 paleaceous scales; mid-nerve of scales conspicuous, extending to the apex and often beyond; basic chromosome number, as determined from counts on 2 species, x-12.

description: Slender to woody lianas, shrubs or trees up to 15 m; branches gray to grayish-brown, usually terete, striate, glabrous to pubescent. Leaves alternate, simple, coriaceous, rarely membranaceous, narrowly oblong, ovate to obovate, glabrous to variously pubescent along midrib and veins; venation camptodromous or rarely actinodromous, ultimately finely reticulate; margin entire to dentate; base cordate to cuneate; petioles glabrous to variously pubescent, usually pulvinate above. Male inflorescences axillary, often clustered, spicate to paniculate, longer to shorter than the petiole, filiform to stout, glabrous to variously pubescent; bracts usually lanceolate; bractlets oblong-lanceolate to obovate. Flowers white to greenish-white, yellow or brownish; sepals usually 6 in 2 series, very rarely fewer, the outer obovate to ovate, usually smaller than the inner, glabrous or rarely sparsely villous, the inner broadly obovate to ovate or orbicular, glabrous or rarely sparsely villous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, very rarely fewer or absent, usually obovate, rarely rhombic or broadly obovate to orbicular; stamens 6, rarely fewer; anthers dehiscing longitudinally and transversely across theca. Female inflorescences usually axillary, solitary to clustered, spicate to paniculate, longer or shorter than the petiole, filiform, slender or stout, glabrous to variously pu- bescent; bracts usually lanceolate; bractlets lanceolate to obovate-oblong or ovate. Flowers white to greenish-white, yellow or brownish; sepals 6 in 2 series, the outer obovate to broadly ovate, usually smaller than the inner, glabrous or rarely villous, the inner broadly ovate to obovate, glabrous or rarely sparsely villous; petals 6 in 2 similar series, rarely fewer, usually obovate; carpels 2-5, obovoid to globose; style absent; stigma laterally displaced or terminal. Fruit a drupe, green, yellow, orange, bluish to reddish purple, or black, globose or nar- rowly to broadly obovoid, the apex broadly rounded, rarely narrowly rounded, glabrous, very rarely villous; exocarp thin, mealy-coriaceous; endocarp inversely U-shaped, turned upon itself over a vertical, long to short septiform condyle; seed inversely U-shaped; cotyledons fleshy; endosperm absent.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Theobald, William L. 1981. A revision of the genus Hyperbaena (Menispermaceae). Brittonia. 33: 81-104.

description: Seven species. Robust perennial herbs from a woody rootstock, sparsely stellate- pubescent. Leaves petiolate, large, palmately 5-7-lobed (aceriform), the lobes triangular, coarsely crenate serrate, more or less acute; stipules inconspicuous, caducous. Inflorescence an interrupted spike or corymbose raceme (the lower flowers occasionally solitary), the pedicels usually short; involucel trimerous, persistent, the bracts distinct, linear or lanceolate; calyx 0.5-2 cm long, half-divided to deeply parted; corolla 1.5-3 cm long, white, pink, or rose-purple, densely pubescent on margins of claw; androecium included (half or less the length of corolla), the column basally pubescent, filamentiferous at apex; styles 10-14, the stigmas obliquely capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, subglobose, coarsely pubescent with stellate and antrorse simple hairs; mericarps 10-14, oblong, thin-walled, dorsally dehiscent, 2-4-seeded; seeds reniform, 2-3 mm long, puberulent or glabrous. 2n = 66 (three species).

description: Plants dark-green and stiff in extensive mats. Stems creeping, not at all complanate-foliate, irregularly branched, the branches simple, erect or ascending; pseudoparaphyllia foliose; in cross-section with small, thick-walled cells surrounding larger, thinner-walled cells, central strand present. Branch and stem leaves similar, oblong-lanceolate, long-acuminate; margins plane, entire to serrulate; costae short and double or absent; upper cells long-hexagonal to linear, thin- to firm-walled; alar cells well developed in conspicuous groups, quadrate to subquadrate. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen.

description: Monoecious (or perhaps sometimes dioecious) shrubs or trees, the inner bark frequently exuding a reddish liquid, the branchlets subterete, when young ferruginous-strigose (hairs usually attached by the middle, i.e., 2-branched, about 0.2-0.3 mm in. in total length), soon glabrous; leaves alternate, petiolate, the blades chartaceous to coriaceous in texture, often fragile when dry, often finely rugose or muinutely papillose on both surfaces, glabrous, entire and usually slightly recurved at margins, the costa prominent beneath, the secondary nerves several to many, anastomosing toward margins; inflorescences 1-3 in leaf axils or on defoliated branchlets (pistillate often on old bark of trunk or branches), fascieulate-racemose or narrowly paniculate, short pedunculate, minutely strigose with hairs like those of branchlets or glabrescent, the pistillate often few-branched from near base; fascicles often sessile on the rachis, subtended by minute inconspicuous ovate deciduous bracts; pedicels bracteolate at summit, the bracteole cupuliform or one-sided; staminate perianth small, usually thin carnose and pubeseent without, glabrous within, 3 (rarely 4) -lobed; filaments connate in a column, the anthers 3 (rarely 4), connate to apex or distally divergent or free to base, obtuse, 2-celled, opening by extrorse clefts, the connectives inconspicuous or carnose, sometimes glandular; pistillate perianth usually slightly larger similar to those of the leaves, 6-9 cm. long at anthesis, the peduncle up ot 5 cm.  long; fascicles alternate, about 3 per inflorescence, the bracts inconspicuous or none; the flowers 10-20 per fascicle , the pedicles slender, up to 7mm. long; perianth carnose, about 5mm. long, 3 - lobed nearly to base, the lobes oblong, obtuse; androecium about 3.5 mm long, the filament column conspicuously swollen near base, the filaments completly  connate, the anthers 3, about 0.8 mm. long, dorsally connate nearly to apex; pistillate and fruiting infloresences not known.

description: Shrubs or trees, glabrous or pubescent, with slender subrotund or thick quadrangular branchlets; leaves opposite, petiolate, membranaceous or coriaceous; stipules 4 and interpetiolar or 2 and intrapetiolar. Inflorescence terminal, thyrsiform-paniculate or thyrsiform-racemose with secondary rachises terminating in dichasia or scorpioid cymes of sessile or pedicellate flowers. Flowers: calyx 4-6- lobate, the lobes small, often indistinct, equal or unequal, persistent; corolla tube cylindrical, short or elongate, the throat villous inside, the lobes 5 or 6 (7), short and spreading, valvate or imbricate in bud; stamens 4-7, inserted in corolla tube near mouth, the anthers dorsifixed, loculate, included or slightly exserted; ovary 2-6 (7)-celled, the style linear, the stigma with 2-6 (7) narrowly oblong lobes, included or slightly exserted, ovules numerous; ovarian disc prominent and pad-like. Fruit a berry or pyrene, globose, 2-6 (7)-celled, many seeded; seeds minute, brownish, angular, the testa deeply foveolate.

description: Trees, when pubescent the hairs incompletely septate; stipules bifid. Inflores- cences terminal, paniculate-thyrsoid with cymose branches. Corolla infundibuliform, densely pubescent internally at the throat, its lobes 5 or 6, their aestivation irregular, 3 internal valvate and 2 external imbricate (as Hooker, 1873, observed); stamens 5 or 6, inserted on the upper half of the corolla tube; stigma 5- or 6-lobed. Ovary 5- or 6-locular, the ovules numerous on a cordiform placenta. Fruit globose; seeds (Fig. 4) 0.5-1 mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm in diam, foveolate; seed coat (Figs. 5, 6) with polygonal cells, 84-150 (119.7) x 66-98 (79.8) jtm, moderately large pits in the internal walls (Figs. 5, 6), 17-45 pits per cell, 3-14 µm in diam, the lateral walls thick, 3-15 µm thick.

description: Branched annual or perennial herbs of shallow water or moist places, rooting at the decumbent lower nodes and with erect or spreading upper internodes, from 0.5 up to ca. 10 dm high; stems thick and hollow or narrower and essentially solid, striate, glabrate to pubescent; leaves opposite, sessile to petiolate, entire to dentate, linear to ovate, glabrous or pubescent, bases connate; peduncles axillary, solitary, generally elongate and considerably more slender than the subtending internode, heads up to ca. 1 cm high and 2.3 cm wide including rays, more or less campanulate; phyllaries free, equal, 1- or rarely 2-seriate but in certain species the outer paleae vaguely resemble an inner second series, mostly readily deciduous, lance-linear, herbaceous, 0-4 nerved, glabrous to pubescent, dorsally flat to convex, ventrally with the lower portion abruptly expanded into hyaline, generally ciliated alae which enclose the ray achenes, or alae rudimentary to lacking; ray flowers female and fertile, the same in number as the phyllaries; ray corollas white, yellow, pink, or purplish, glabrous, up to ca. 12 mm long, linear-oblong to spatulate, tubed or tubeless, generally with a thickened basal ring, entire to 3-lobed at apex, somewhat persistent on the achene or not, ray style bifid, branches recurved, apices obtuse to rounded; ray achenes shiny black when mature, glabrous, minutely striate, turbinate to linear, generally terete, awnless but with a corolla remnant which appears as a low crown; disk florets numerous, perfect, fertile; corollas yellow or yellow-green, generally not persistent on the achenes, up to ca. 3 mm long, 5- or sometimes 4-lobed, tube basally constricted 1/2-1/4 the length, generally densely pilose on the constriction, otherwise the corolla glabrous, the base of the constriction thickened and wider, style bifid, exserted for pollen presentation, branches recurved, more or less flattened inwardly and generally with bulbous cells outwardly, apices obtuse to rounded, anthers loosely connate, with acute sterile, apical appendages and free-sagittate bases, filaments filiform, adnate near the base of the corolla, achenes of the disk very similar to those of the rays but sometimes compressed or angular, also awnless; paleae mono- or heteromorphic, scarious, ciliate, narrow to quite wide, thin to indurate, lanceolate to oblanceolate, more or less enclosing the subtended disk achenes or sometimes very narrowly linear and not at all surrounding the disk achenes, generally more or less persistent on the conical receptacle; basic chromosome no.: x = 9.

description: Herbae caespitosae; caulibus dense ramosis. Folia alterna, rosulata, sessilia, marcescentia, coriacea, oblongo-lanceolata ad lanceolata vel obpyriformae, 3.5-9 mm longa, 0.5-2 mm lata, inferne tomentoso-araneosa, 3-costata, superne glabra, 2-caniculata, margine integra. Capitulescentiae solitaria, ad anthesim sessiles, post anthesin pedunculo sparse araneoso, instructae. Capitula discoidea, heterogama; involucrum ovoideum usque ad campanulatum; phyllaria 2-seriata, aequalia vel subaequalia, scariosa, straminea, ovato-lanceolata vel lanceolata; receptaculum planum. Flores feminei 4-6, corolla filiformi; styli rami lineares, exserti; flores hermaphroditi 2-6, corolla tubulosa, limbo 4-5-lobato; antherae basi sagittatis, appendice apicali lanceolata; styli rami truncati usque ad clavati, papillosi. description: Cespitose herbs; stems branched, densely compact. Leaves alternate, rosulate, sessile, marcescent in age, coriaceous, oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate or obpyramidal, 3.5-9 mm long, 0.5-2 mm wide, lower surface tomentose-arachnose, 3-costate, upper surface glabrous, 2-canaliculate, the margins entire. Capitulescences solitary, sessile at anthesis, becoming pedunculate at maturity, the peduncles 1-5 mm long, sparsely arachnose. Capitula discoid, heterogamous; involucres ovoid to campanulate; phyllaries 2-seriate, equal to subequal, scarious, stramineous, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate; receptacle plane; pistillate florets 4-6, the corolla filiform, the style branches linear, exserted; hermaphroditic florets 2-6, the corolla tubular, the limb slightly expanded, 4-5-lobed, the anthers basally sagittate, the terminal appendage lanceolate, the style branches truncate to clavate, papillose, exserted, the stigmatic lines short and parallel. Achenes ovoid, 4-costate, glabrous; pappus bristles uniseriate, fused basally.

description: Herbs to shrubs to 2 m high, sometimes scandent (without specialized structures), terrestrial, unarmed. Branches erect or spreading, 4- or 5-sided to terete, usually hollow. Vesture of multicellular finger or branchlet-hairs, gland-tipped or not. Leaves alternate or appearing opposite (rarely appearing verticillate), simple, petiolate, estipulate, ovate, ovate-lanceolate or ovate- acuminate, sometimes basally truncate, entire, subentire or toothed, often tapering asymmetrically along distal portion of petiole. Inflorescence axillary or from a stem dichotomy (false dichotomy), pedunculate, umbel-like (Fig. 1E). Pedicels basally artic- ulated after fruit ripens, sometimes angled. Flowers five-merous; bisexual; regular. Calyx enclosing the bud with valvate aesti- vation. Flowering calyx with sepals partially connate, lobes triangular, narrowly triangular or obtuse, rotate with a stellate outline (Fig. 1), or the lobes reflexed. Fruiting calyx conspicuously accrescent, green or purple, spreading behind berry, rotate (Fig. 1 E) to reflexed. Most species having 10-lobed corollas, the five larger lobes alternating with 5 smaller lobules, the latter sometimes inconspicuous. Corolla aestivation with five valvate lobes, each lobe alternating with an inwardly pleated and shorter lobule. Corolla 1-5 cm diam., rotate, broadly infundibular, campanulate, tubular, in one species (J. ven tricosa) the tube urceolate and the limb retrorse (Fig. 1A), if the corolla is non-rotate then the lobes flare. Filaments 5, filiform, markedly enlarged/swollen at base where adnate to base of corolla, the expanded base pubescent with finger hairs, slender part of filament pubescent with finger hairs (Fig. 1 D) or not, filament inserted obliquely into ventral face of anthers in bud. Anthers de- hiscing longitudinally. Ovary superior, bicarpellate, ovules 42-412 (n = 128 ovaries) per ovary. Style slender (Fig. 1 G), exerted or not. Stigma single, bilobed, slightly bilobed, or grooved. Nectary disk annular around base of ovary (Fig. 1 G). Nectar clear to yellowish drops at base of corolla and androecium, or, in several Peruvian and one Bolivian species orange to red, filling base of corolla and visible through corolla. Fruit a juicy globose or oblate berry, 4-25 mm diam., many-seeded, black, purple, green, orange, red or yellow (also white fide Ruiz &Pavon, 1799).

description: Shrubs to 2 (4) m tall, with pale to reddish, exfoliating bark, the young twigs pubescent; leaves deciduous, opposite, petiolate, thin, ovate, pinnately-veined, crenate to serrate, very rarely entire, bright green and sparsely hairy to glabrate above, densely whitish-pubescent beneath, exstipulate; inflorescence of dense, terminal, 1-35-flowered cymose clusters or solitary flowers; flowers perfect, rather large, slightly fragrant, the pedicels, hypanthia, and sepals densely hairy; hypan- thium hemispheric, adnate to the lower part of the ovary; sepals 4 or 5, lanceolate to narrowly ovate; petals 4 or 5, spreading, obovate or oblanceolate, pubescent within, white or pink, showy; stamens 8 or 10, the filaments of varying lengths, broad and flat, tapering from the base to a narrow summit; anthers oblong; ovary about half inferior, conical, partially 3-5-celled at first, becoming 1-celled, the placentation parietal, the styles (2) 3-5, distinct, the stigmas obtuse; fruit long- persistent, conic capsules, beaked by long-persistent styles, 3-5-valved, septicidal, dehiscing in the upper half; seeds many, striate-reticulate.
bibliographicCitation: Holmgren, Noel H. & Holmgren, Patricia K. 1989. A taxonomic study of Jamesia (Hydrangeaceae). Brittonia. 41 (4): 335-350.

description: Plants low, weakly erect to spreading herbaceous annuals with slender, green to reddish, silky-puberulent stems and branches arising from a thin to slender taproot. Leaves basal, alternate, estipulate, petiolate; blades obovate to rounded or somewhat reniform, sparsely villous and greenish or reddish on both surfaces. Flowering stems erect or spreading. Inflorescences open or diffuse and spreading, di- or trichotomously branched at first node, otherwise dichotomous, sparsely to densely silky-puberulent; bracts ternate, connate basally, awnless, scalelike, triangular and glabrous but ciliate along margin or somewhat foliaceous, linear to narrowly lanceolate and puberulent. Peduncles lacking. Involucres reduced to a tight spiral of 4-7 awnless bracts, outer two occasionally partially connate (J. craterior- um) or infrequently outer three connate but becoming separate and individual (J. pub- erula) at full anthesis, each subtending a pedicellate flower and opposite a solitary bractlet; involucral bracts cucullate, oblanceolate to obovate, glabrous but ciliate along upper margin or villous abaxially, translucent or tinged with green; pedicel slender and longer than associated involucral bract, glabrous; bractlets linear, glabrous, sometimes rose to red at anthesis. Flowers pedicellate, not stipitate, white or pale yellowish to rose or red, glabrous, smooth or minutely pustulose proximally and along midribs; tepals monomorphic, oblanceolate and of equal length or slightly dimorphic, those of outer whorl narrowly ovate, slightly auriculate basally with undulate-crisped margins in fruit, those of inner whorl narrowly oblanceolate; stamens 9, included; filaments glabrous; anthers white to pale pink, oblong. Achenes light brown, trigonous, glabrous; embryo curved in thin, mealy endosperm.
bibliographicCitation: Reveal, James L. 2004. Johanneshowellia (Polygonaceae:  Eriogonoideae), a new genus from the Intermountain West. Brittonia. 56 (4): 299-306.

description: Trees, usually small to medium-sized, or shrubs. Leaves decussate, petiolate; stipules interpetiolar, not fused across petiole, held flat back-to-back in bud, ± herbaceous, usually triangular or lingulate to obovate, acute to rounded at apex, precociously withering, but not shed by the formation of an abscission layer; leaf blades membranous to subcoriaceous, margin entire, venation brochidodromus. Inflorescences terminal and lateral, usually pedunculate with principal branches diverging from a dichasial or pseudo-dichotomous branching, the branches monochasial (or branching type obscure in short branches), bracts and bracteoles absent or few and irregularly disposed; inflorescence in one species reduced to solitary flowers or 3-flowered, sessile cymes. Flowers diheterostylous, 4- or 5- merous; calyx campanulate with distinct tube and distinct lobes, or rarely subtrun- cate, or spathaceous; corolla salverform, thick-textured, white or pink, ± densely antrorsely puberulous outside, glabrous inside, tube distinctly longer than lobes, lobes valvate in bud, without distinctly keeled apical portion, with showy petaloid, marginal appendages, glabrous adaxially; stamens attached on corolla tube at ca. 10-70% of tube length, filaments equalling or shorter than anthers, slightly longer in the brevistylous than in the macrostylous flower morph, anthers linear, dorsifixed near base, included; ovary 2-locular, with dis- tinct, elongate placentae that are attached to the septum ± throughout their length, ovules numerous on each placenta, flat- tened, ascendingly imbricate. Capsules septicidal and basipetally dehiscent, often secondarily loculicidally split, at maturity with a distinctly sclerotic endocarp. Seeds ± pla- noconvex, conspicuously winged, hilum located ± centrally on seed body.

description: Plants erect or twining. Stems to 8 mm diam., bluish grey, strongly verrucose, glaucous, glabrous. Leaves reduced to scales, very shortly petiolate, caducous, stipular glands present. Inflorescences 1 per node, extra-axillary, few-flowered, bostrychoid to sciadioidal. Corolla rotate. Gynostegial corona consisting of fused staminal (Cs) and interstaminal (Ci) parts [= C(is)], the staminal parts with strongly differentiated adaxial appendage (ligule). Gynostegium sessile; anthers massive, with apical appendages and prominent lateral anther wings, the latter consisting of a proximal and a distal ridge; space between the ridges filled with upwardly oriented bristles, proximal ridge straight. Pollinia pendulous or erect. Stylar head forming a protrusion at the upper end of the corpusculum, upper part tabular to slightly concave. Fruits erect, fusiform, apically shortly beaked, mottled. Seeds papillose, winged or wingless, comose.
bibliographicCitation: Liede, S. & Meve, Ulrich. 1996. The circumscription of Karimbolea Descoings (Asclepiadaceae). Brittonia. 48: 501-507.

description: Plantae graciles erectae caulescentes ramosae e caudice tumido tuberosoque. Folia petiolata membranacea 2-3-pinnata, foliolis amplis crenato-dentatis minute scaberulis. Inflorescentia ex umbellis laxe constata pedunculis plerumque lateralibus. Involucri bracteae et involucellorum bracteolae plures angustae. Radii pauci patenti-adscendentes. Pedicelli crassi. Flores polygami: floribus marginalibus perfectis, eis centralibus staminatis, petalis albis obovatis apice inflexo laminae angustiore, dentibus calycis evidentibus aequalibus linearibus, stylis gracilibus, stylopodio humili conico. Carpophorum bipartitum. Fructus anguste ovoideus glaber subteres, mericarpiis dorsaliter compressis, costis filiformibus humilibus, vittis 1 vel 2 in intervallis usque 6 in commissura, semine dorsaliter compresso superficie plano-concavo.
bibliographicCitation: Mukherjee, Prasanta K. & Constance, Lincoln. 1986. Two new genera of Indian Umbelliferae/Apiaceae. Brittonia. 38: 145-149.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Two species. Erect subshrubs, stellate pubescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades usually palmately 3-7-lobed (aceriform), truncate to cordate, crenate, acute; stipules present, small. Flowers in congested or lax cymes, aggregated into paniculate inflores cences; involucel of 3 inconspicuous linear bractlets; calyx 5-lobed; petals white, equalling or slightly exceeding the calyx; androecium pallid, included, filamentiferous at apex; styles 7-13, the stigmas capi- tate. Fruits schizocarpic, oblate, more or less glabrous; mericarps 7-13, blackish at maturity, indehiscent, glabrous; seeds soli- tary, glabrous. 2n = 32 (both species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Frutices sine affinitatibus manifestis; folia plerumque lobata; flores in cymis glomeratis vel apertis paniculas amplas formantibus dispositi, bracteis involucralibus praediti, corolla et columna staminali albis, petalis ab medio vel ab basi columnae orientibus, antheris quam 23 paucioribus, stigmatibus capitatis, carpellis 7-13 in verticillo unico, unoquoque ovulum singulum ascendens includente, maturitate laevibus, inermibus, indehiscentibus, parietibus non crassis; numerus chromosomatum gameticus, n = 16.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1967. Some Umbelliferae of the Andean Paramos of South America. Brittonia. 19: 212-226.

description: Erect, soft-woody shrubs, simple or ascendingly to laxly branched above, sparsely to densely pubescent, the hairs mostly stellate, sessile or stalked, radiate-armed, but with simple hairs usually intermixed. Leaf blades large, ovate to transverse- elliptic in outline, shallowly to deeply 3-, 5-, or 7-lobed, sometimes unlobed distally, the lobes deltoid to deltoid-oblong with open or closed sinuses, the apex acute, the base deeply cordate to truncate, the margins obscurely to coarsely crenate-dentate to serrate, the surfaces plane except the major veins raised beneath; petioles gen- erally more than half as long as the blades; stipules linear to subulate or subfalcate. Flowers few to many in glomerate or open cymes, together forming leafy or apically naked, paniculate inflorescences. Involucral bracts 3, free or adnate basally to the calyx tube, appressed, filiform or linear, not surpassing the calyx lobes. Calyx campanulate, 4-7 mm long at anthesis, slightly accrescent, 5-lobed to below the middle, the lobes deltoid-acute to broadly ovate-acuminate, with 3 or 5 principal veins; nectaries 5, distinct or in a closed ring. Petals white, arising from middle or near the base of ovary-cup to form an open-campanulate corolla equaling or slightly exceeding the calyx, obovate to suborbicular, narrowed evenly or abruptly to a very short claw, obliquely rounded at the apex, glabrous or rarely with a few basal hairs. Androecium white, formed of a broadly expanded, glabrous or apically hispidulous ovary-cup terminated by a short tube with elongate, radiate filaments or a slender, elongate tube with short, ascending filaments; anthers 5-23. Style branched only at the apex or nearly to the base, the branches as many as the carpels, glabrous or pubescent, emergent at anthesis; stigmas obliquely to symmetrically capitate, white-papillate. Carpels 7-13 in a single whorl, each with a single, ascending ovule, at maturity thin-walled, reddish-brown to black, glabrous or with a few hairs at the style base or rarely stellate-hairy apically, transversely elliptic- reniform to nearly orbicular, 1.6-2 mm high, 1.8-2.5 mm broad, laterally compressed with the dorso- and baso-lateral edges rounded, the ventro-apical edge sometimes depressed and with a slight crest but otherwise unarmed, the lateral walls smooth, without a venation pattern; midvein present; endoglossum absent; indehiscent. Seeds ovoid-reniform, 1.4-1.7 mm high, 1.2-1.7 mm broad, reddish- to grayish- brown, glabrous or with a few hairs ventrally. Gametic chromosome number, n =16.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1967. Some Umbelliferae of the Andean Paramos of South America. Brittonia. 19: 212-226.

description: Plantae perennes humiles subcaulescentes quasi glabrae simplices vel sparsim ramosae ad 2.5 dm altae e caudice crasso fibrosove. Folia petiolata membranacea plerumque rosulata anguste oblonga 6-7.5 cm longa, 1-1.5 cm lata pinnatisecta, foliolis obovatis in lineari-acuminatis divisionibus dissectis 1-2 mm longis ad 0.5 mm latis, foliis caulinis paucis oppositis vaginantibus. Petioli vaginantes, 1-1.5 cm longi late scarioso-vaginantes. Pedunculus terminalis crassus 1.5-2 dm altus ad apicem hirsutulosus, pedunculis lateralibus debiliter evolutis. Involucri bracteae 5-8 pinnatisectae 1-3.5 cm longae. Radii 10-12 crassi costati inaequales patento-adscendentes 2-7 cm longi. Involucellorum bracteolae 8-10 lineares vel lanceolatae pinnatisectae dissectaeve 5-10 mm longae. Umbellulae 8-12-florae, pedicellis maturis angulatis patento-adscendentibus 2-5 mm longis. Flores non vidi, dentibus calycis lanceolatis, stylopodio conico stylis reflexis subaequali. Carpophorum bipartitum. Fructus late ovoideus glaber subteres apice angustatus basi rotundatus 4-5 mm longus, 2-3 mm latus, mericarpiis laete dorsaliter compressis, costis prominente suberoso-incrassatis aequalibus quam intervallis latioribus, vittis magnis in intervallis solitariis in commissuris 3-5; semen sub vittis canaliculatum superficie planum.
bibliographicCitation: Mukherjee, Prasanta K. & Constance, Lincoln. 1986. Two new genera of Indian Umbelliferae/Apiaceae. Brittonia. 38: 145-149.

description: Seventeen species. Stout erect herbs or subshrubs, often with hispid vestiture, frequently growing in moist habitats. Leaves petiolate, the blades narrowly lanceolate, ovate, cordate, hastate, aceriform, or sagittately parted, with serrate margins, usually coarsely stellate-pubescent, sometimes also with long simple hairs; stipules subulate to filiform. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or aggregated into terminal panicles or racemes; involucel much shorter than to equaling the calyx, of 6-10 linear bracts, usually hispid; calyx deeply 5-lobed; corolla rotate or tubular, whitish, yellow, or pink; androecium equalling petals or (in tubular- flowered species) clearly exserted, apically 5 dentate; styles 5, exceeding androecium, free distally, the stigmas capitate. Capsules depressed, 5-angled or winged, usually scabrid, often transversely rugose or striate, loculicidally dehiscent, the 5 locules each 1-seeded; seeds reniform, glabrous to minutely scabridulous. 2n = 38 (several species, Blanchard, 1974).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Arbores magnae, floribus hermaphroditis 8-12 mm longis. Folia integra, subtus glabra, petiolo glanduloso vel eglanduloso. Bracteae eglandulosae glomerulos florum haud includentes. Flores in paniculis axillaribus et terminalibus pauci-ramosis brunneo-tomentosis dispositi. Calycis tubus late campanulatus vix elongatus vel conicus excavatus intus ubique pilosus extus tomentosus, lobis 5 acutis. Petala 5, 2 ceteris multo majora valde unguiculata, stamina in juventute includentia. Stamina 8-75 exserta, filamentis in ligulam unicam connatis ad receptaculi marginem adaxialem insertis, staminodiis ad receptaculi marginem abaxialem contra stamina dispositis. Ovarium ad os calycis tubi lateraliter insertum, uniloculare; ovula 2; stylus basilaris filiformis. Fructus drupaceus durus, exocarpio crustaceo, endocarpio duro crasso irregulariter dehiscente.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1979. New genera and species of Chrysobalanaceae from Malesia and Oceania. Brittonia. 31: 79-95.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Large trees with hermaphrodite flowers 8-12 mm long. Leaf undersurface glabrous and usually minutely papillate on veins and reticulations, appearing beaded; petioles eglandular. Bracts and bracteoles eglandular, not enclosing groups of young flowers. Inflorescence of unbranched or little-branched terminal or axillary racemes which bear congested cymules proximally and solitary flowers distally. Receptacle shorter than the sepals, broadly campanulate, asymmetric, hollow, hairy throughout, externally tomentellous; calyx lobes markedly unequal. Petals 5, two much larger than the others, markedly unguiculate and enclosing the young stamens in the bud. Stamens 8-75, exserted; filaments connate for half to three-quarters of their length into a short ligule, attached to one side of the receptacle; anthers slightly or very hairy; staminodes 5-8, inserted opposite the stamens on the free margin of the disk. Ovary of 1 (2 or 3) unilocular carpels inserted laterally at the mouth of the receptacle; ovules 2. Fruit a hard drupe; epicarp glabrous, verrucose; endocarp hard, thick, glabrous inside, without a special mechanism of seedling escape. Cotyledons filling the seed, only slightly ruminate.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1979. New genera and species of Chrysobalanaceae from Malesia and Oceania. Brittonia. 31: 79-95.

description: Four species. Procumbent (but not repent), decumbent, or erect perennial herbs, with simple hairs and fine stellate pubescence. Leaves petiolate, distichous, the blades symmetrically lanceovate or oblong-ovate, crenate-dentate; stipules present, small. Flowers solitary or fasciculate in the leaf axils; involucel absent; calyx deeply 5-lobed, accrescent or inflated in fruit, becoming reticulate-membranous by disintegration of all but the finely reticulate vas- culature; petals yellowish (fading rose); androecium included; styles 5-9, the stigmas capitellate. Fruits schizocarpic, the meri- carps 5-9, indehiscent, relatively fragile and unomamented; seeds solitary, glabrous. 2n = 16 (one species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Two species. Trees 15-30 m tall, the twigs (and herbage generally) densely covered with minute stellate (farinose) pubes cence. Leaves petiolate, the blades broadly ovate, basally truncate or cordate, irregularly serrate, weakly lobulate or angled, acute or obtuse, palmately 7-9 nerved, with a prominent nectary on the midrib abaxially; stipules inconspicuous, caducous. Flowers in axillary or terminal panicles; involucel usually 4-parted (rarely 5-6-parted), the bracts briefly connate basally, broadly ligulate or spatulate, obtuse, persistent; calyx 5-parted; petals white, marginally erose. Fruits capsular, oblate, densely pubescent, 3-celled; seeds 2-3 per locule. 2n = 98 (one species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Folia opposita; cymae bracteatae, longipedunculatae, brevipedicellatae; duae nectarii glandes: una dorsalis et una ventralis; ovarium superum; capsula succulenta.
bibliographicCitation: Feuillet, Christian P. G. & Skog, Laurence E. 2002. Novae Gesneriaceae Neotropicarum XI. New genera and species from the Guianas. Brittonia. 54: 344-351.

description: Terrestrial, caulescent herbs, with short internodes. Leaves opposite decussate; venation pinnate; stomata scattered; petiolate. Infiorescences axillary, long-pedunculate, bracteate, short-pedicellate. Flowers with 5 sepals; corolla campanulate, 5-lobed; stamens 4, included, adnate to the corolla base, the thecae dehiscing by a longitudinal slit; nectary ring reduced to 2 large glands, one ventral and one dorsal; ovary superior. Fruit a somewhat fleshy capsule, bivalved, dehiscing loculicidally, opening fully.
bibliographicCitation: Feuillet, Christian P. G. & Skog, Laurence E. 2002. Novae Gesneriaceae Neotropicarum XI. New genera and species from the Guianas. Brittonia. 54: 344-351.

description: Shrubs 1-3 m tall, sometimes small trees, stellate-pubescent to glabrate. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades deeply cordate, palmately 5-7-lobed, the lobes acute or obtuse, serrate or crenate; stipules inconspicuous, lance-ovate to triangular, sometimes re- duced to mere scales. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils; involucel trimerous, more or less gamophyllous basally, the lobes ligulate or triangular; calyx 5-lobed, tubular in flower, more or less enclosing the fruit; petals purple, lavender, or whitish with purple veins; androecium included, filamentiferous at apex; styles 6-10, exceeding androecium, slender, the stigmatic zones introrsely decurrent. Fruits schizocar pic, disk-shaped; mericarps 6-10 semicircular wedges, laterally smooth or reticulate, dorsally smooth, glabrous or more or less pubescent, essentially indehiscent; seeds solitary, glabrous. 2n = 28, 42, 84, 112 (several species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Hypanthium campanulate to hemispheric, pubescent; petals triangular, acute; stamens isomorphic, with slender glabrous filaments and linlear anthers, the -connective not prolonged at base, the appendage, if any, a minute spur; ovary partly inferior, usually 3-5-celled; style slender; stigma usually punctiform. Herbs or low shrubs, almost always conspicuously pubescent and often also glandular; flowers small or minute, numerous in terminal clusters. More than 200 species have been recognized, distributed throughout the American tropics, but most abundant in southern Brazil. Some of them bear a strong superficial resemblance to Miconia, and the two genera are closely related.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Five species. Perennial herbs, erect or decumbent, sometimes rosette-forming, or subshrubs to 0.5 m tall, densely stellate-pubescent to glabrate. Leaves petiolate, the blades palmately divided or parted, the lobes often secondarily divided, the ultimate divisions narrowly linear to lanceolate; stipules subulate to broadly ovate-triangular. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, long-pedicellate, sometimes aggregated into terminal racemes or panicles; involucel absent; calyx campanulate, ca. half-divided or more; corolla 2-3 times the length of calyx, lavender; androecium half the length of co- rolla or less, the filaments often longer than the column; styles 15-22, often purplish, the stigmas capitate or truncate. Fruits oblate or broadly conical, glabrous or nearly so; mericarps 15-22, borne on a concave carpocrater, laterally reticulate, 1-seeded, thin, with a broad apical wing or the wing suppressed. 2n = 12, 24, 36 (four species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: In justifying maintenance of the genus Leichardtia, Bullock (1956) recognizes four species in Australia and New Caledonia, implying that two more species from those areas will also be accepted. In the herbarium at Kew, Bullock also placed with Leichardtia the available material of the Fijian Gymnema stenophyllum A. Gray, but he did not formally propose the implied combination. A comparison of this last taxon with the Australian and New Caledonian species so placed by Bullock confirms its position in Leichardtia; its corolla is more campanulate-subrotate than urceolate, but in habit, foliage, and flower and fruit characters it seems very close to the species recognized by Bullock.

description: Leptoglottis has been adopted by the writer as being the oldest available name. Schrankia has been proposed as a nomen conservandum against Morongita, but not yet adopted as such. See T. A. Sprague, Nomenclature Proposals by British Botanists 63. 1929. The western plant known as Schrankict uncinata is Leptoglottis Nut- tallii DC., the type of the genus Leptoglottis.
bibliographicCitation: Rydberg, Per A. 1934. Taxonomic notes on the flora of the prairies and plains of central North America. Brittonia. 1: 79-104.

description: Plants light yellow or green to dark green, slender, caespitose, in dense to lax tufts. Stems to 3 cm, in cross-section with an outer layer of 1-2 rows of small, thick-walled, rusty red cells, a cortex of 3-4 rows of large, ± thin-walled cells, and a central strand of smaller, thin-walled cells; rhizoids thick to scattered on lower 1/2-1/3 of stem, appearing smooth or lightly to very densely papillose. Propagula usually present in upper 1/2-1/3 of plant, scattered, or in dense rusty-red clusters, sometimes so conspicuous as to hide all but the leaf tips, filamentous, uniseriate, few to many cells long, with walls almost smooth to conspicuously papillose (Figs. 1, 2). Leaves linear to ovate-lanceolate or oval, erect to erectpatent when dry, patent when moist, somewhat clasping the stem, slightly decurrent, usually convex in the middle with the apex ± twisted to one side and incurved; apex ± obtuse or acute to long-acuminate; margins plane to recurved, irregularly dentate to sharply serrate in the upper 1/2; costa strong, shortly excurrent, serrate at back in upper ?2, in cross-section with a medial row of guide cells and both dorsal and ventral stereid bands; cells with incrassate walls, mostly ± isodiametric, occasionally short-rhomboidal or rectangular, basal cells rectangular to quadrate, those adjacent to the costa short to long-rectangular. Dioicous; perichaetial and perigonial leaves mostly linear-setaceous from an enlarged ovate base, basal cells often long-rectangular, somewhat flexuose, perigonial paraphyses filamentous, hyaline, 1/2 again as long as the antheridia. Setae elongate, ± twisted dextrally, rusty red to dull yellow, cells very long-rectangular, in crosssection with an outer layer of 3-4 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortex of 5-6 rows thin-walled, meager central strand of small thin-walled cells; capsule erect or slightly arched, long-cylindric, (7) 8-ribbed, short-necked; exothecial cells short- to long-rectangular; stomata phaneropore, several to many at base of urn and in neck; annulus of 2-3 rows of greatly enlarged, thin-walled cells; peristome double, inserted below the ± flared mouth; exostome teeth lanceolate, on the outer surface with quadrate to short-rectangular plates joined along a median zigzag line below, with the plates becoming less papillose and the median line straight above, on the inner surface with papillose projecting lamellae, in crosssection on the outer layer much thinner than the inner; endostome with a high, smooth basal membrane, segments narrow, keeled, papillose, nonperforate, slightly shorter than the teeth, cilia papillose, mostly double, slightly nodose, not appendiculate. Operculum bluntly conical. Spores spherical, 10-15 µm in diameter, pale yellow in mass, papillose. Calyptra cucullate, smooth, naked, covering about half the urn, falling early.

description:
There is a group of related species belonging to this section, all from western Colombia, that have large leaves with an appressed pubescence on the lower surface. They are L. maritima, L. durifolia and L. macrocarpa. I now have material of two new species belonging to this group, and further material of L. veneralensis showing that it is also a member of the same group. In Prance (1972) L. veneralensis was placed among the imperfectly known species. Since the inclusion of three more species in this part of Licania considerably alters the key for their identification, the differences between these six species are given below in the key and in Table I.

As is common for species of western Colombia most of these species are known only by their type collections or one additional gathering. However, although closely related, they are distinct in a sufficiently large number of characters to be easily recognized and separated. Western Colombia has obviously been an area of con- siderable diversification of this part of the genus Licania where it occupies a wide range of habitats: L. maritima is a lowland species of beaches, L. veneralensis and L. macrocarpa are lowland forest species and L. durifolia, L. cabrerae and L. montana all grow in forest at altitudes over 1300 m in widely separated localities. Licania cabrerae was collected at an altitude of 2550 m. It is a pity that there is not more material available to study more closely related groups of species like this which are centered in the western coastal area of Colombia. The fruit of only two of these species, L. durifolia and L. macrocarpa, is known.

description: Suffruticose perennial herbs; stems erect, spreading to prostrate, rounded to quadrangular or subhexagonal, costate or ribbed, sometimes rooting at the nodes. Leaves opposite, rarely ternate; petioles present and winged or absent and the bases connate-perfoliate; blades chartaceous, subcoriaceous, or somewhat fleshy (L. succulenta), ovate to elliptic, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, rarely deltate or spatulate, entire, margins entire to deeply lobed, serrate or irregularly and coarsely serrate, apex acute to obtuse, both surfaces subglabrous or more often appressed pubescent or hispidulous and scabrous with glutinous dots. Inflorescences terminal with heads solitary or few in cymose clusters. Heads with rays, erect; involucre hemispherical to broadly campanulate; involucral bracts in 2 equal or subequal series of 4-5 bracts each, ap- pressed with scarcely spreading tips, ovate to oblong, green to tan and sometimes pur- ple-tinged near base and along midrib; re- ceptacle paleaceous, the paleae persistent, rigid, erect or arching over florets, weakly conduplicate at anthesis, flatter as achenes mature, obovate to oblanceolate, obtuse to nearly truncate, acute in one species, mu- cronate to apiculate, narrowly keeled and distinctly striate with many longitudinal ribs, sometimes tinged purple toward apex or along midrib, scabrid or asperulous outside, especially toward tip; ray florets 6-16 per head, pistillate and fertile, rays yellow, entire to 3-toothed; disk florets (15-)25-65 per head, hermaphroditic, corolla, 4(-5)- merous, yellow mostly glabrous to scabrid distally, veins without fiber sheath, lobes triangular to longer than wide, anther thecae brownish, apical appendage yellow, ovate. Achenes tuberculate at maturity, flattened to slightly biconvex, in rays obcompressed with median ridge inside, rarely thickened and more triangular, in disk flattened, 2-angled, in rays and disk rounded or sometimes truncate and hispidulous apically, with a small central corolla and pappus attachment, distal hispidulous surface of little or no width, angles with narrow wings 0.3-0.6 mm, often greatly enlarged at maturity, sometimes deeply lobed, sometimes with narrow antrorse projections at upper corners, surface not fleshy; pappus of connate scales forming an uneven corona, sometimes with short sharp or blunt awns and intervening squamellae. Pollen grains ca. 27 lm diam. n = 26.

description: Rhizomes scaly, slightly flattened, long-creeping, climbing, rooting on the ventral side only, bearing 3-5(-6) rows of fronds on the dorsal side, the vascular system dorsi-ventral with a broad ventral meristele notched on the inner side and 1-5 dorsal meristeles, each meristele surrounded by a dark sclerenchymatous sheath; stipes decurrent on the rhizome, not jointed, scaly when young, containing up to 12 vascular bundles, the two adaxial bundles larger then the abaxial ones. Blades 1-pinnate, with a terminal "pinna" resembling the lateral ones; pinnae entire, jointed to the rachis, the joint often appearing as a faint dark line; veins free, simple or branched once near the base, parallel for most of their length, uniting with the (nonvascular) cartilaginous pinna margin; rachises flat to shallowly grooved adaxially, if grooved then the grooves interrupted (not continuous) at the rachis-costa juncture. Fertile leaves dimorphic, their pinnae narrower than those of the sterile; sori acrostichoid; spores smooth, spiny, granulate, minutely papillose, or winged, pale yellow to brown to pale olive-green. x = 41.

description: Annual, or herbaceous or woody perennials, branched freely, leafy. Leaves mostly alternate, ovate to lanceolate, petioled. Flowers symmetrical, usually small, numerous, in bracteate or rarely leafy corymbs that become racemose in age. Pedicels slender, well developed. Floral tuLbe not developed beyond the ovary. Sepals 4, mostly lanceolate. Petals 4, unlike, the 2 upper aseending, more or less clawed and geniculate at the junction of claw and blade, each with 1 or 2 glalndular tubercles at this junction; the 2 lower petals larger, spreading, mostly unguiculate, not bent or tubereled. Stamens 2, basally united with each other alid the style, the posterior one fertile and lying in the infolded expanded sterile distal petaloid part of the alnterior (staminodium). Style slender; stigma subeapitate. Ovary developinog into a 4-valved loculicidal capsule. Seeds many.

description: Aquatic, perennial herbs attached to rocks in river- rapids and waterfalls. Roots prostrate, elongate, flattened to elliptical in cross-section, green and photosynthetic, branched, with an asymmetric root cap and attached to solid substrates via holdfasts (haptera) and adhesive hairs. Stems (shoot system) arising endogenously, opposite or subopposite along flanks of roots, prostrate, surface granulose. Leaves distichous, circinnate, arising from stem margins at 45-90° angle, distinction between leaf base and stem obscure, monothecous (single sheath) or dithecous (two sheaths); simple (young leaves) or repeatedly dichotomously or subdichotomously divided; petiolate, petiole distinctly widened and flattened in cross-section, margin irregularly crenate, 1 several veined; rachis flattened. Spathella davate, oriented vertically, small papillae regularly distributed over surface or crowded apically, rupturing apically or subapically into linear to triangular segments. Flowers solitary, 1 to several per stem, lateral, oriented vertically, hermaphroditic, zygomorphic, pedicellate, covered by sac-like spathella. Tepals 2-5, linear, filiform to flattened, one on either side of stamen filaments, apex acute. Stamens 1-4, filament flattened, wider at base than apex, elongating during anthesis and projecting from ruptured spathella, persisting after anthesis; anthers basifixed, oblong to triangular, thecae fused apically, apex blunt, thecae equal or unequal, helically twisted upon drying or not, dehiscing introrsely and longitudinally. Pollen in monads, dyads or tetrads, incolpate. Ovary 2-carpellate, 2-locular, oval, ellipsoidal to hexagonal in cross-section, anisolobous, oriented subobliquely on pedicel. Ovules numerous, placentation axile, placenta thick. Stigmas 2, free, flattened, semicircular in outline, margin irregularly dentate. Capsules dehiscent, 2- valved, each 3 -ribbed (non-suture), suture margins inconspicuous or rib- like, short (0.1-0.2 mm) gynophore sometimes present in fruit. Seeds orange-brown, obovate.

description: Plants low, with long fusiform roots. Stems solitary or in clusters arising from the same root system, usually rounded above, depressed in the centers; blue-green, yellow-green, and occasionally appearing reddish green; 2-7 cm high, 4-12 cm in diam. Areoles usually linearly arranged along ribs or at the apices of humplike tubercles or podaria, each bearing a tuft of soft, yellowish or whitish trichomes from which the flowers arise, 8-15 mm apart, 1-5 mm in diam; spines absent except in seedlings and then only rudimentary. Flower 1-2.2 cm in diam, 1-2.4 cm long; outer perianth segments with greenish midribs and greenish pink or whitish margins, the largest ones elliptical, 3-12 mm long, 1-3 mm broad, mucronate, marginally minutely ciliate distally; inner perianth segments pink, white, or rarely yellowish white, sometimes with greenish midribs, the largest ones elliptical, 8-22 mm long, 2-4 mm broad, mucronate or occasionally attenuate, margins ciliate or entire; filaments white; anthers yellow; pollen ? spheroidal, 0-18 colpate, 14.9-63 style white, 5-14 mm long; stigmas 4-8 (rarely 3), 1-3 mm long, white though occasionally pinkish; ovary naked. Fruit pinkish red and fleshy at first, becoming brownish white and dry at maturity, naked, clavate, 15-20 mm long, 2-3.5 mm in diam, with the umbilicus large or the perianth parts persistent, emerging rapidly from within the trichomes at maturity. Seeds black, tuberculate (verrucose), pyriform, 1-1.5 mm long, 1 mm broad; hilum large and flattened; cotyledons coalescent. Flowering from March through September. Fruits mature 9-12 months after fertilization.

description: Flowers of medium size, 5-merous, in small lateral clusters below the leaves of the season; hypanthium broadly campanulate or hemispheric; sepals reduced to small teeth; stamens isomorphic, with short filaments and broad rounded anthers as in the preceding genus, but 1-pored; ovary wholly inferior, 5-celled; style elongate, the stigma not conspicuously enlarged. Shrubs or trees, often of large size, with broad, 5-pli-nerved (in our species) leaves-and white or pink flowers. About 7 species of the Amazonian forests, most numerous in the upper Amazon valley.

description: Vascularization (Fig. 1). -The vascular tissue in the pedicels is a continuous ring, an amphiphloic siphonostele, Fig. 1 B. In the receptacle it forms ten distinct bundles; five of these extend outward as the median sepal supplies, and from the other five originate the lateral sepal traces. All of these divergences to the sepals are accompanied by very small gaps (Fig. 1 C, D). In the calyx the traces yield lateral branchings that anastomose with one another forming a network. Above the divergences of the sepal bundles, the remaining vascular tissue is again con- tinuous and forms a star-shaped stele (Fig. 1E). Then five median petal strands diverge, alternating with the median sepal bundles and accompanied by paren- chymatous gaps (Fig. 1 F). The petal strands branch further up giving rise to lateral petal traces. Opposite the median sepal bundles and alternate with those of the petals, five staminal traces then diverge from the outer zone of the remaining vascular tissue without accompanying gaps (Fig. 1G). The central region, which supplies the gynoecium, becomes continuous again and slightly elliptical (Fig. 1 H, I). For the gynoecium, first formed are two large dorsal traces, and then four ventral bundles and a variable number of lateral supplies arise from the inner and outer parts of the vascular cylinder respectively (Fig. 1K, L). The dorsal bundles extend upward through the ovary and the entire length of the style. The ventral bundles ramify to supply the ovules, and the traces corresponding to contiguous carpels fuse at the ovary apex, resulting in two ventral bundles which end at the base of the style (Fig. 1A). Traces for all whorls are amphicribal or bicollateral.

description: Small acaulescent or short-caulescent herbs, or woody at the base, the leaves in terminal rosettes or spirally arranged; flowers crowded at the center or solitary in the axils, sessile or pedicellate, ebracteolate, not inverted; androecium and corolla typically lobeliaceous; capsule unilocular, the placenta parietal and ventral, or the lower part of the capsule divided into two locules by the tangentially flattened placenta; summit of the ovary deciduous from the rim of the hypanthium and detached as an operculum, this and the upper part of the hypanthium unilocular, not divided by the placenta; calyx-lobes often unequal, the dorsal one longest, the lateral and ventral pairs successively shorter.

description: Hypanthium campanulate or ovoid, pubeseent; sepals mostly triangular or subulate; petals medium-sized; stamens dimorphic, the connective conspicuously prolonged and dilated at base into a heartshaped or hoof-shaped appendage; ovary 3-4-celled, free, with a slender style and punctiform stigma. Freely branched shrubs, the thick leaves nearly always densely pubescent, hispid, or scabrous; flowers white to purple, very numerous in terminal panicles. About 25 species, most abundant in the Amazonian savannas, but extending south to southern Brazil.

description: Trees, shrubs, or lianas. Leaves 3-49 cm long; stipules persistent or caducous; leaflets 5-120, ovate, obovate, elliptic or narrowly elliptic, 0.4-29 x 1-12 cm, petiolulate or sessile; midvein conspicuous; secondary venation craspedodromus or camptodromous; tertiary venation reticulate, parallel or absent. Inflorescence an axillary or terminal pseudopanicle, composed of racemose branches, these clustered into fascicles. Flowers papilionoid, 8-20 mm long, pedicellate or sessile; bracteoles persistent or caducous; calyx campanulate, with five obtuse or acute teeth or truncate; corolla white, greenish, yellow, pink or violet; banner with circular blade and narrow claw, often with tomentose indumentum on the adaxial surface, and visible nervation abaxially; wing petals with or without lamellate sculpturing above; stamens 10, monadelphously or diadelphously connate; anthers versatile, elliptic, dorsifixed; ovary brevi-stipitate, 1 or 2 ovulate; style filiform, curved or sometimes straight; fruit compressed, samaroid or lunate, the wing with reticulate nervation; seed solitary, lunate. Chromosomes 9 to 10,  diploid.

description: Flowers 4-5-merous; hypanthium campanulate or tubular, promi- nently ribbed; petals small, often acute; anthers subulate, essentially isomorphic; ovary 3-celled and more or less 3-angled, 3-lobed at the summit; style elongate with punctiform stigma. Delicate low herbs, with leaves rarely more than 3 cm. long, and small flowers in secund spikes or solitary and peduncled. About 7 species in northern South America, some of which are only recently described.
