description: Trees, shrubs or geoxylic suffrutices. Stipules free and lateral and subulate or narrowly deltate to foliaceous, or (subgenus Tolmiella) fused and intrapetiolar. Lower leaf-surface glabrous or with a few strigose or setulose hairs. Inflorescence a simple or branched raceme of cymules or of sessile or subsessile glomerules, sometimes extremely contracted and racemoid, rarely a short simple raceme. Bracts and bracteoles not enclosing flower-buds, sometimes eglandular, in some species with 1 or 2 pairs of sessile glands, and in 1 species (M. glaberrima) with ca 10 shortly stipitate, marginal glands. Flowers bisexual, distinctly zygomorphic, usually sigmoid in bud. Receptacle-tube very variable in shape and size, nearly always curved, or gibbous at the base, or both, very rarely (only in subgenus Tolmiella) turbinate or subcampanulate and neither curved nor gibbous, distinctly oblique at the throat, sometimes markedly so; throat blocked by long retrorse hairs (except in Tolmiella). Sepals 5, unequal, acute (except in M. tamenaka). Petals 5, longer than the sepals, persistent or caducous. Stamens 5-9, usually 7; filaments white, bent or curved through at least 90? at anthesis, scarcely longer than the sepals, inserted opposite the posterior sepal, flattened and expanded towards the base and united for at least 1/3 of length; staminodes very variable in develop- ment and configuration, + completely united to form an elongate tongue-shaped or short denticulate ligule, or partly united to form a comb-shaped ligule, or partly united in two groups of 3 with 2 others completely free. Ovary monocarpellary, 1-locular (2-locular in subgenus Pellegriniella), inserted at or just below mouth of receptacle-tube. Style arcuate, scarcely longer than the sepals, glabrous or hairy in lower half. Drupe fleshy; endocarp densely hairy inside, thick, hard and woody in subgenera Pellegriniella and Tolmiella, otherwise thin and crustaceous or fibrous.

description: Hypanthium narrowly campanulate, surmounted by short sepals; petals small; anthers linear or subulate, the connective neither prolonged nor appendaged; ovary inferior, 3-5-celled; stigma truncate or barely expanded. description: Eight to ten species. Erect herbs or subshrubs, sometimes puberulent, more com- monly hispid, often with urticating hairs. Leaves petiolate, the blades suborbicular to broadly ovate, angular, palmately lobed to digitately divided, truncate, serrate, acute to obtuse, usually pubescent; stipules filiform, relatively persistent. Flowers in condensed, bracteate, headlike racemes, the "heads" axillary or terminal, sessile or pedunculate; specialized bracts subtending the inflorescence broadly cordate-ovate, sessile or subsessile, basally often with prominent nerves alternating with white intercostal tissue, distally green and foliaceous, often dissected or setose basally; involucel absent (except present in M. radiata); calyx small, deeply 5-lobed; corolla white, yellow, or lavender, often inconspicuous; androecium included, the staminal column with 5 apical teeth; styles 10, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, glabrous or puberulent; meri- carps 5, usually smooth or reticulately cos- tate, 1-seeded; seeds glabrous. 2n = 56 (three species), 112 (one species).

description: Eleven species. Spreading or erect shrubs or subshrubs, usually densely stellate-pu- bescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades orbicular to ovate, unlobed to deeply 3-5-lobed, subentire to serrate; stipules subulate to lanceolate or falcate, inconspicuous. Inflorescences paniculate, racemose, or spicate, the flowers more or less congested in cymose clusters in the leaf axils, rarely solitary, subsessile or pedicellate; involucellar bracts 3, usually persistent, subulate to filiform, rarely ovate; calyx shallowly or deeply 5-lobed; petals whitish to rose or lavender; androecium included, filamentiferous at apex, the column glabrous or pubescent, the anthers pallid to deep red; styles 7-14, ex- ceeding the androecium, the stigmas capi- tate. Fruits schizocarpic, subglobose or oblate, apically stellulate-pubescent; mericarps 7-14, more or less reniform, thinwalled, dehiscent to the base; seeds solitary, minutely stellulate-pubescent or rarely gla- brous. 2n = 34 (several species).

description: Herbaceous plants, trailing, ascending, or erect, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves long- petiolate, the blades orbicular or reniform in outline, more or less palmately 5-7- lobed, sometimes deeply dissected; stipules sessile, asymmetrically ovate, usually ciliate, persistent. Flowers solitary or fasciculate in the leaf axils, sometimes grouped in terminal inflorescences; involucellar bracts (2)3, distinct, subulate or foliaceous; calyx 5-lobed, often accrescent and spreading in fruit; petals usually purple, sometimes white, emarginate or with a prominent api- cal notch; androecium included, filamenti- ferous at apex; styles 8-15, filiform, the stigmatic surface introrsely decurrent. Fruits schizocarpic, oblate, pubescent or glabrous; mericarps 8-15, indehiscent, dorsally more or less reticulate, 1-seeded. 2n = 42, 76, 84, 112 (several species).

description: Fifteen species. Perennial shrubs or subshrubs (sometimes annual), erect, with patent or appressed stellate pubescence. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate or lanceolate, usually unlobed, crenate or dentate; stipules lanceolate or falcate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or aggregated in apical spikes or racemes; involucel of 3 filiform or spatulate bractlets; calyx 5-lobed; corolla yellow or orangish, rarely with a red center; androecium included, filamentiferous at apex; styles (5)8-18, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, oblate, setose or pubescent; mericarps (5)8-18, indehiscent, horse- shoe-shaped with a prominent ventral notch, reddish brown, sometimes 2-3-cuspidate, 1-seeded; seeds glabrous. 2n = 12, 24, 36, 48 (several species).

description: Branching shrubs or small trees, sometimes scandent, pubescent or glabrous. Leaves petiolate, the blades elliptic, ovate, or 3-5-lobed, truncate or cordate; stipules subulate, deciduous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or sometimes in apical cymelike groups; bractlets of the involucel linear, lanceolate, or spatulate, usually (5)8-9; calyx campanulate or tubular, 5-lobed; petals red (rarely white), auriculate toward base, forming a tubular corolla; androecium usually exserted, the staminal column with 5 apical teeth, the filaments short and more or less retrorse; styles 10 with capitate stigmas. Fruits a fleshy schizocarp or berry, ob- late, usually red (sometimes white), with 5 carpels, each 1-seeded. 2n = 28, 56, 86.

description: Four species. Prostrate perennial herbs with stellate and lepidote pubescence. Leaves petiolate, distichous, the blades asymmetrical, more or less reniform or flabellate to triangular, dentate or entire; stipules 3-5 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, long-pedicellate; involucel present or absent; calyx lobes ovate or cordate; petals pale yellow fading pale rose; androecium included, glabrous, pallid, filamentiferous at apex; styles 7-10, pallid, glabrous, with capitate stigmas. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 7-10, dorsally rounded, essentially unornamented, essentially indehiscent, 1-seeded; seeds glabrous. Chromosome number uncertain, probably 2n = 32.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Suffruticose shrubs, suffrutescent lianas, or herbs. Stems terete to alate. Leaves opposite or verticillate, adaxial surface with several inconspicuous fusiform glands at the base or distributed along the length of the midrib, rarely eglandular; petiole minutely appendiculate and slightly fused at the base or absent. Inflorescences racemose, axillary, terminal or subterminal, bracteate. Sepals 5, equal or subequal, imbricate, with many colleters at base within. Corolla infundibuliform, subsalverform to salverform; tube exappendiculate, not annulate, straight or somewhat gibbous; limb actinomorphic, 5-parted, dextrorsely convolute. Stamens 5, always included within the corolla; anthers connivent and adnate to the pistil head, of 2 parallel, uniformly fertile thecae borne adaxially near the apex of the enlarged, sagittate, truncate or obtusely 2- auriculate sterile part of the anthers; filaments free, puberulent to pilose. Carpels 2, united apically; pistil head pentagonal-umbraculiform. Ovules numerous; disk glands 2 or 5, rarely absent, separate or somewhat connate at the base. Follicles 2, apocarpous, terete to moniliform. Seeds numerous, dry, truncate, comose at the micropylar end, usually rugose.
bibliographicCitation: Morales Q., J. Francisco. 1998. A synopsis of the genus Mandevilla (Apocynaceae) in Mexico and Central America. Brittonia. 50: 214-232.

description: Hypanthium globose-campanulate; sepals triangular-lanceolate; stamens isomorphic in structure but somewhat unequal in size; anthers linear-subulate, the connective scarcely prolonged below the pollen-sacs, but expanded and 2-lobed; ovary 4-celled; style declined, somewhat sigmoid, stigma punctiform. Low shrubs of heathlike aspect, the leaves (in ours) nearly sessile, revolute, pubescent, and the flowers 4-merous, numerous, nearly sessile among the leaves. About 25 species, mostly in Brazil.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Unarmed trees with buttressed or basally swollen trunks; young branches, buds, petioles and petiolules with golden-brown ascending pubescence; pith light brown to pinkish. Axillary bud-scaleg 2, imbricate, acute to acuminate. Leaves alternate, imparipinnate; stipules early eaducous; leaflets 5-11 (-13), alternate, mostly ovate to elliptic or oblono, the apices acute to acuminate, often slightly emarginate and mucronate, the bases obtuse to cordate; petiolules short, 5 mm long or less; stomata limited to the lower epidermis, 14-20 µ long, of the rubiaceous or parallel-celled type (type C of Metealfe & Chalk 1950). Inflorescence usually a large terminal thyrse, the bracts early eaducous; flower-buds lanecolate, their bases somewhat gibbous on the upper (adaxial) side, the development of the flower parts nonacropetal with the petals last to develop; sepals 5, lanecolate, unequal in width, the lower (abaxial) narrowest, all narrowly imbricate and marginally interlocked in bud, completely en-closinig all flower parts, free and reflexed at anthesis, pubescent on both surfaces but for the glabrous imbricate portion of the margin; petals 5, imbricate in bud, the upper (adaxial) one widest and typically enclosed by the laterals, all showy, yellow or saffron, obovate, more or less clawed, the apices often somewhat erose; stamens free, 4-5 (-7), the 4 lateral ones always present and fuinctional, alternating with the petals, the other 1-3, when present, much reduced in size; staminodes if present 0-5, papilla-like to acicular, without anthers (the total stamen-staminode number 10 or less) ; filaments short and thick, 1-3 mm long, the anthers elongate, narrowly sagittate, often papillate at least along the margins or sutures, glabrous or pubescent, unequal in length, those of the upper 2 lateral stamens somewhat shorter than those of the lower laterals, all initially 4-thecate, becoming 2-thecate with the breakdown of the intrathecal partitions; dehiseence by 2 subterminal pores, these covered by a hygroscopic, hoodlike, terminal pollen-cup (Fig. 3, 3), which, when moistened, closes laterally to cover the pores, the distal part of the lateral anthers with approximately a 90º turn which places the pollen-cup beneath the anther pores; pollen grains spherical, 25-30 µ in diameter, tricolpate, the furrows long, wide but tapered, the germ pore represented by a bulge, the exine smooth or finely granular. Pistil of one carpel (sometimes with 2 nearly free carpels in M. elatum) ; stigma small, slightly capitate, finely papillate; style glabrous, sutulate, eaducous in fruit; ovary sessile, glabrous or pubescent on the sides, uniovulate, the placenta parietal and restricted to the upper (adaxial) stigmatic end of the loculus; ovule anatropous, the micropyle facing towards the stigmatic end. Fruit a samara, elliptic or oblong, strongly compressed laterally, flat and thin (3-8 mm thick at the loculus), indehiscent, winged from the upper and lower sutures, coriaceous, finely but rather sparsely pubescent at maturity in all species except M. excelsum which is always glabrous. Seed 1 in the sole specimen dissected (M. elatum, Krukoff 5401), with the laterally flattened cotyledons covered by a thin layer of gelatinous endosperm (Fig. 5, 5); hypocotyl short thick, and straight; epicotyl small, three lobed.
bibliographicCitation: Keoppen, Robert & Iltis, Hugh H. 1962. Revision of Martiodendron (Cassieae, Caesalpiniaceae). Brittonia. 14: 191-209.

description: Multi-stemmed shrubs (rarely small trees); bark smooth, grayish-light brown; wood cream-white. Stipules interpetiolar, sheathing, connected to the petioles, persis- tent. Leaves short-petiolate, blades narrowly oblong to widely obovate, acute or rounded at base and rounded at apex; dom- atia absent. Infiorescences axillary, 1-2 per node, cymose, pauciflorous. Flowers protandrous, short-pedicellate; hypanthium narrowly obconical. Calyx membranous, (3-)4-lobed (rarely rotate and faintly lobed), persistent but usually breaking off in mature fruits. Corolla salverform, white and without annular thickening, or orange and with annular thickening; corolla tube short and funnelform or long and narrowly tubular, glabrous throughout; corolla lobes 4, oblong and rounded at apex; aestivation imbricate. Stamens alternate to the petals, half-exserted to mostly included (only tips exserted); anthers button-shaped or narrowly elliptic, dorsifixed near the base, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; filaments attached near the mouth, extremely short, glabrous throughout. Style exserted; style branches ovate, opening after complete maturity of the anthers, reflexed at maturity. Ovary 2-celled, with (1-)2 seeds per locule inserted on the central placenta; placenta variable, apically free or extending throughout the length of the ovary. Capsules narrowly cylindrical to narrowly obconical, dehiscing septicidally and loculicidally, with a persistent calyx (often breaking off). Seeds peltate, vertical, linear-lanceolate, with central hilum, bipolar-winged.
bibliographicCitation: Delprete, Piero G. 1999. The Cuban endemic genera Ariadne, Mazaea, Acunaeanthus, Phyllomelia (Rondeletieae), and Eosanthe (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 51: 217-230.

description: Perennial herbs, vines, subshrubs, sometimes shrubs; stems often pale or maculate, quadrangular to subhexagonal, costate, usually sulcate when dry, appressed strigose to asperulate or hispid. Leaves opposite, petioles usually conspicuous, less often lacking or winged; blades herbaceous to chartaceous, ovate or deltate to linear, sometimes strongly trilobed to pinnately lobed, rarely ternately compound, margins remotely to closely serrulate or serrate, often with large teeth or lobes at broadest part, base subtruncate to narrowly cuneate or acuminate, apex acute to narrowly acuminate, upper surface mixed scabrid and scabridulous, lower surface appressed strigose to hispid, without glandular dots, usually trinervate from near base, rarely penninerved with short ascending veins. Inflorescences terminal or from axils of uppermost leaves, with 1-3 heads. Heads with or without rays, erect; involucre hemispherical to broadly campanulate; involucral bracts indurate with somewhat herbaceous tips, appressed with scarcely spreading tips, 10-14 in 1 or 2 subequal series, oblong to narrowly ovate, apex obtuse to acute or attenuate, strigillose outside; receptacle paleaceous, the paleae persistent, chartaceous with membranaceous bases, weakly conduplicate and enfolding the achene, becoming flatter as achene matures, scarcely to narrowly keeled, closely multistriated with longitudinal ribs outside, oblanceolate, tips obtuse to mucronate, or lanceolate, or awned, asperulous or toothed distally. Ray florets 0- 12, neutral or fertile; corollas 5-merous, yellow, tube ca. 1 mm long, glabrous, limb oblong, 2.3-13 mm long, apex bidentate, strigillose below, without glandular dots, papillose above; style absent or present. Disk florets ca. 10-100, bisexual; corollas white or yellow, tube glabrous; throat narrowly campanulate, glabrous outside or scabridulous above and along veins, veins without fiber sheath or with few fibers, lobes triangular to longer than wide, densely scabridulous outside, without glands, papillose inside, papillae often long, often only on margin; anther thecae black, apical appendage yellow, ovate. Achenes 3-angled (disk achenes 4-angled), abruptly narrowed or truncate above, upper surface broad, minutely hispidulous, with small central corolla and pappus attachment, with or without wings on angles or with a pseudopappus of projections on distal corners and edges, surface not fleshy; pappus usually of 1-15(-20) deciduous short bristles, mostly 1-2 mm long. Pollen grains 23-25 jim diam. n = 15.
bibliographicCitation: Wagner, Warren L. & Robinson, H. 2001. Lipochaeta and Melanthera (Asteraceae: Heliantheae subtribe Ecliptinae): Establishing their natural limits and a synopsis. Brittonia. 53: 539-561.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 2-10 m tall; stems terete; pith continuous. Leaves, peduncles, pedicels, calyces, petals, and fruits covered with sessile or subsessile stellate hairs. Pedicels and calyces sometimes also covered with gland-tipped hairs. Stipules caducous. Inflorescences terminal and in the axils of upper leaves, cor- ymbose, the ultimate divisions subumbellate to umbellate, 2-9-flowered. Flowers hypogynous, dimorphic. Calyx in flower campanulate to broadly campanulate or pentagonal and-subglobose to urceolate; calyx in fruit somewhat to acutely pen- tagonal, globose or subglobose, conspicuously accrescent, inflated, and membra- nous. Petals oblanceolate, obovate-oblong, or spatulate, slightly emarginate at the apex. A well-developed ring of nectariferous tissue located between the calyx and corolla. Longistylous flowers: filaments absent or present and borne at the staminal column tip; staminodes absent or present, alternate with the fertile stamens, and tooth-like or obscurely unciform; ovary globose, stipitate; styles erect, free their entire length. Brevistylous flowers: filaments borne at the staminal column tip; staminodes as in longistylous flowers; ovary as in longistylous flowers; styles spreading, free their entire length. Capsule globose, slightly to deeply retuse at the apex, 5-angled, stipitate; seeds ovoid, broadly ovoid or trigonal, rounded in cross- section, 1 or 2 per carpel.
bibliographicCitation: Dorr, Laurence J. & Barnett, L. C. 1989. A revision of Melochia section Physodium (Sterculiaceae) from Mexico. Brittonia. 41: 404-423.

description:
Hypanthium campanulate to hemispheric, the sepals short or elongate, the exterior teeth miiiute to elongate; petals showy; stamens essentially isomorphic; anthers subulate, large, often arcuate; connec- tive with or without a short basal spur or gibbosity, bearing on the back just above the base a linear spur, directed forward and nearly or quite parallel to the anther; ovary 3-5-celled; stigma punctiform.

The species, more than 40 in number, are distributed around two main centers, one in southern and eastern Brazil, the other in the northern Andes, with a few in the West Indies. This distribution bears little or no relation to the division of the species among the 5 sections of the genus.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description:
Racenie solitary, the rachis slender, sometimes broadly winged; spikelets solitary, usually conspicuously hairy, sessile or shortly pedicelled in two rows on one side of the rachis, the first glume turned toward the rachis, hence the back of the fruit turned away from the rachis; first glume more than two-thirds as long as the spikelet, 3- or obscurely 5-nerved, awnless, or in the section Bifaria awned from between the teeth of a minutely toothed apex; second glume 3-7-nerved, equal to or slightly exceeding the fruLit (shorter than the fruit in the section Loliiformnia); lower floret usually sterile, sometimes with a well- developed palea and in some species with a staminate flower, the lemma 5-nerved, exceeding the fruit; fruit usually ventricose on the palea side, the back usually straight, ovoid or obovate, acute, usually minutely striate (smooth and shining in MI. pappophorunt)3 the margins of the lemma flat but rather tightly enclosing the palea; stamens 3; styles 2, plumose.

Slender aninual or perennial grasses, often stoloniferous, with solitary one-sided spikelike racemes.
bibliographicCitation: Swallen, Jason R. 1937. The Grass Genus Mesosetum. Brittonia. 4: 363-392.

description: Frutex vel arbor, inermis, sempervirens. Folia alterna, simplicia vel composita palmata 2-5-foliolata, estipulata. Inflorescentia terminata, paniculata; pedicelli articulati. Flores hermaphroditi; calyx 5-dentatus; petala 5, in alabastra valvata; stamina 5; ovarium 2-loculare, stylis 2. Bacca nigra, compressa; endospermi uniformi.
bibliographicCitation: Wen, Jun & Frodin, David G. 2001. Metapanax, a New Genus of Araliaceae from China and Vietnam. Brittonia. 53 (1): 116-121.

description: Evergreen unarmed shrubs or trees, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves alternate, simple, or sometimes palmately divided or palmately compound with 2-5 leaflets, exstipulate, margin of leaves and leaflets serrate to serrulate in upper 3/4-4/5, entire in lower 1/4-1/5. Inflorescence umbellate with umbels aggregated in a terminal panicle, terminal umbels racemosely arranged; pedicel articulated. Flowers hermaphrodite, sepals 5, petals 5, valvate in bud, stamens 5, anthers oval or oblong, ovary 2- or rarely 3- or 4-locular, styles divided apically. Fruit a berry, black, flattened; endosperm uniform.
bibliographicCitation: Wen, Jun & Frodin, David G. 2001. Metapanax, a New Genus of Araliaceae from China and Vietnam. Brittonia. 53 (1): 116-121.

description: Herbae perennes. Caules foliis subterraneis squamiformibus, oppositis, decussatis prope basin praediti. Involucra anguste campanulata. Phyllaria ovato-oblonga, cum receptaculo secure connexa, aliquantum imbricata. Receptacula leviter convexa alveolataque. Achenia obconica, faciebus quinque convexis (ad maturitatem), apicibus truncatis, omnino callis suberosis tectis. Genus characteribus stylorum antherarumque familiae Compositarum, tribui Eupatoriearum, et subtribui Ageratinarum congruens.
bibliographicCitation: Grashoff, Jerold L. 1975. Metastevia (Compositae: Eupatorieae): a new genus from Mexico. Brittonia. 27: 69-73.

description: Two species. Erect shrubs to 1.5 m tall, minutely stellate-tomentose, with distichous branching. Leaves distichous, short-petiolate, the blades linear-lanceolate, oblong, or lance-ovate, serrate, obtuse or acute; stipules linear, equalling or exceeding the petioles. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils; ped- icels elongate and slender, sometimes exceeding the leaves; involucel absent; calyx small (3-4 mm), basally rounded, ecostate, 5-lobed; petals lavender or purple, small, glabrous throughout (including claw); androecium included, filamentiferous at apex, the column pallid or purple; styles 7-8, divergent, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 7-8, pubescent dorsally, laterally reticulate-fenestrate, partially dehiscent apically between two empty doublewalled "horns"; seeds solitary, glabrous or with a few stellate hairs. 2n = 16 (one species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Flowers 4-8-merous; hypanthium subglobose to narrowly campanulate; sepals elongate to nearly obsolete, frequently with exterior teeth; petals very small to medium in size, oblong to subrotund, often retuse or inequilateral; stamens isomorphic or dimorphic; anthers subulate, linear, oblong, ovoid, or obovate, 2-4-celled; connective not prolonged, or prolonged into 1-few basal appendages or a heartshaped oblique structure; ovary mostly inferior, 2-5-celled, with usually numerous ovules; style terete, straight. or sigmoid, usually elongate; stigma punctiform, truncate, capitate, or peltate. Rarely herbaceous, usually shrubby plants or occasionally trees, the ample leaves sometimes anisophyllous, with numerous fowers in terminal spikes, compound spikes, or panicles, sometimes secund on the branches. The largest genus of the family, with about 780 described species, ranging from Argentina and Bolivia to Cuba and Mexico, and from sea-level to alpine paramos in the Andes.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Caules tenues, erecti, radiales, fusei, irregulariter ramosi; rami laterales, et typo Frullaniae et Microlepidoziae; rami ventrales interealares foliati, vel flagelliformes cum foliis parvulis, vel stoloniformes longi, vel breves d et 9; folia transversalia, quadrifida usque ad medium, segmenta basim 2-10 cellulibus; amphigastria similia; dioica; d infloreseentia interealaris vel in ramis brevibus ventralibus, and antheridia in bractearum axillis; 9 infloreseentia in ramis longis vel brevibus ventralibus, vel in caulibus, vel longis lateralis ramis, sine innovationibus; bracteae et bracteolae foliis dissimiles, in 3-4 ordinibus, subcarinatae; perianthium longum, supra triangulare; sporophyta non vidi.
bibliographicCitation: Fulford, Margaret H. 1962. Segtregate genera of the lepidozia complex (Hepaticae) part. 3. Microlepidozia Jörg. and Micrisophylla gen. nov. Brittonia. 14: 121-136.

description: Dioecious perennials, subarboreseent and semiscandent; stems branched, completely covered by the truncated and long-persistent leaf sheaths. Leaves polycyclic, those bearing blades crowded at the apices of the branches; leaf sheaths of the young leaves tubular and closed to the mouth, later split and broken by the secondary growth of the stem; leaf blades rigid, linear, eventually deciduous by the formation of an abscission zone at the juncture of blade and sheath. Flowering culms axillary; the infloreseence paniculiform, composed of several-numerous clusters of pedicellate spikes borne in the axils of leaf-like bracts. Staminate spikes obovoid, composed of numerous crowded spikelets; staminate spikelets 1-2-flowered, composed of 4 or 5 glumes, the upper 1 or 2 each subtending a flower; staminate flowers composed of 3 stamens, the filaments elongated and persistent, the anthers linear. Pistillate spikes obconic, composed of several-numerous loosely arranged and more or less divergent spikelets; pistillate spikelets 1-flowered, composed of a single pistil surrounded by 2-4 glumes; style short, 2-3-branched, semipersistent. Achenes subeylindrical or rarely obscurely trigonous, more or less falcate, thin-walled and almost entirely filled by the seed. Perianth of 2-5 (but usually 3) hypogynous ciliate-laciniate membranous scales (see map, fig. 1, for distribution of the genus).
bibliographicCitation: Gilly, Charles L. 1943. An Afro-South-American Cyperaceous complex. Brittonia. 5: 1-20. f. 1.

description: Plants small, pale to dark green or brown, caespitose; stems prostrate to ascending, irregularly or regularly pinnate or bipinnate, the secondary branches often short; lateral branches of the Frullania type (the half-leaf dorsal) on one side of the stem, and the Microlepidozia type (the half-leaf ventral) on the opposite side of the stem, leafy, often becoming flagelliform in th outer part; ventral branches interealary in the axils of the underleaves, flagelliform, of short, male or female; stem in transverse section orbicular, with a layer of 12-16 longitudinal rows of cortical cells surrounding the medulla of smaller cells; rhizoids on the scale leaves of the flaglliform branches; leaf insertion transverse with the leaves erect spreading or ineurved, or oblique with the leaves succubous; leaves quadrifid (or trifid) to one-half or three-fourths, the segments equal or unequal, the base of the lamina 8-12 cells wide; underleaves smaller or nearly equaling the leaves in size, symmetrical or asymmetrical, deeply 2-4 divided, the segments unequal (rarely equal) ; plants dioicous; male infloreseence short, ventral, rarely on a long lateral branch or on the stem, dorsiventral, the bracts and bracteoles in 2-6 or more series; antheridia in the axils of the bracts; female infloreseence on a short ventral sexual branch, without innovations, the bracts and bracteoles similar, in 3-5 series, different from the leaves, the innermost series largest, divided to one-fourth into 2-4 segments; perianth long, of one leaves quadrifid (or trifid) to one-half or three-fourths, the segments equal or tracted, crenulate to laciniate-ciliate; capsule reddish brown, the wall of 2-3 layers of cells, with brown knot-like thickenings along the radial walls on the outer surface of the outer layer, and bands or half-rings across the inner tangential wall of the innermost layer; seta in transverse setion with 8 very large cells surrounding 12-16 smaller cells.
bibliographicCitation: Fulford, Margaret H. 1962. Segtregate genera of the lepidozia complex (Hepaticae) part. 3. Microlepidozia Jörg. and Micrisophylla gen. nov. Brittonia. 14: 121-136.

description: Hypanthium campanulate or ureedlate; sepals persisteilt (in our species), triangular, acute or more or less subulate; petals 6-8 mm. long, showy; connective of the large stamens exceeding the anther, the filament attached near its center; connective of the small stamens shorter than the anther, briefly prolonged below the filament into a simple or bilobed appendage. Stems short, fruticulose, slender, strongly 4-angled, with crowded coriaceous leaves exceeding the very short internodes, naked below; flowers nearly sessile, axillary near the tips of the branches.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Monotypic. Trailing herbs, usually with little pubescence. Leaves long-petiolate, the blades 1.5-4 cm long, orbicular in outline, symmetrical, usually palmately 5-7-parted; stipules ovate, 3-4 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels usually shorter than the subtending petioles, more or less pubescent; involucellar bracts 3, distinct, lanceolate; calyx 5-7 mm long, with simple hairs 1-2 mm long; corolla dark orange, often with a red center, 6-8 mm long; androecium included, yellowish, filamentiferous at apex; styles 16- 22, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, setose; mericarps 16-22, 5-6 mm long, green maturing black, with 2 apical spines 1.5-3 mm long, divided into 2 cells by an endoglossum, each cell with 1 seed, the lower cell indehiscent, manifestly rugose, the upper cell dehiscent, smoother, pubescent; seeds ca. 1.5 mm long, with sparse, minute pubescence. 2n = 18.
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Five species. Perennial herbs, decumbent or suberect, the stems more or less hirsute to subglabrous. Leaves long-petiolate, orbicular in outline, more or less deeply palmately lobed or parted, the lobes sometimes secondarily divided, coarsely crenate, acute; stipules lanceolate to ovate, usually persis- tent. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, long- pedicellate (sometimes exceeding the subtending leaf); involucel trimerous, the bracts lanceolate to ovate, subequal to calyx or somewhat shorter; calyx 5-lobed, deeply divided; corolla 1.5-2 times the length of calyx, pale yellow to rose or purple; androecium included, filamentiferous at apex; styles 8-15. Fruits schizocarpic, glabrous or pubescent; mericarps 8-15, laterally rugose, more or less spined apically, usually divided into 2 cells by a rigid endoglossum (sometimes absent), the lower cell 1-seeded, the upper cell empty; seeds reniform, glabrous [?]. 2n = 10, 30, 100 (three species)
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.
rights: Content licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License

description: Flowers 4-merous; hypanthium campanulate or ovoid, almost always pubescent; petals showy, mostly purple; stamens strongly  diinorphic, the connective scarcely prolonged between the anther and the filament, bearing a conspicuous ascending dorsal spur; ovary 4-celled, the style slender with punctiform stigma. Shrubby or suffruticose, mostly freely branched and usually freely pubescent, with conspicuous flowers in ample terminal panicles. In the one species of British Guiana the ovate leaves are sericeous above and the smaller anthers reduced to sterile rudiments. About 40 species, distributed through the higher mountains from Mexico to Peru, extending east into Venezuela and Mount Roraima.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Herba vel suffrutex parce ramosus, foliis trisectis, alternantibus, petiolatis; capitulis in paniculas laxas dispositis; bracteis involucralibus circiter 15, 2- vel 3-seriatis, aequalibus vel subaequalibus, imbricatis; receptaculo glabro, leviter convexo,; capitulis discoideis, 25-30 floribus hermaphroditis fertilibus; corolla infundibuliformi, 5-lobata, intus extusque pilosa, sine stomatibus; antherae appendice parva sed distincta; styli ramis longe exsertis; achaenia prismatica, 5-costata, costis superne hispida, carpopodio brevi, tereti, cellulis longis, parietibus crassis, 1- vel 2-seriatis constituto; pappo ex fimbriis pilis hispidis brevibus et arista unica longa composito.

description: Herbae pusillae glabrae. Folia opposita sessilia estipulata linearia crassiuscula integra. Flores axillares bibracteolati in uno alterove uninscujusque nodi axillo solitarii; calyx quinquilobus lobis lanceolatis marginibus hyalinis; corolla unisaccata bilabiata quinquiloba interius glanduloso-pilosa; aestivatio corollae imbricata labio postico exteriore; stamina didynama thecis globosis vel ovatis separatis; ovarium biloculatum placentatione axiali ovulis anatropis. Capsula globosa pendula septicida; semina exalbuminata reticulato-echinata.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1983. Dragma Hippomanicum IX. A new Astragalus (Leguminosae: Astragalanae) from sandstone rimrock in New Mexico. Brittonia. 35: 109, 110.

description: Small, erect, glabrous herbs. Stems terete, branching. Leaves opposite, sessile, estipulate, slightly thick, entire, only the midvein visible. Flowers axillary, 1 per node; pedicels bibracteolate; calyx 5-lobed, the lobes slightly fused at the base, lanceolate, entire, with a hyaline margin; corolla unisaccate, bilabiate, 5-lobed, glandular-pubescent within, the upper lip 2-lobed, the lateral lobes free, the median lobe flat, without ornamentation, pendent; stamens 4, didynamous, the filaments curved, the thecae globose to ovoid, separate; staminode absent; disk absent; ovary biloculate, the placentation axile, the ovules many, anatropous. Capsule globose, borne on the pendulous pedicel, septicidal, the seeds exalbuminate, borne on the persistent placenta, the exotesta reticulate-echinate.

description: Eight species. Shrubs or subshrubs, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves petiolate or short-petiolate, the blades narrowly elliptic to triangular to broadly ovate (sometimes palmately lobed), coarsely crenate, acute, sparsely to densely pubescent (sometimes harshly so), the hairs simple or stellate; stipules subulate or falcate. Flowers sometimes solitary, but usually in few-flowered axillary inflorescences, these cymose or racemose, sometimes subpaniculate, or subumbellate; involucel trimerous, the bracts ovate-lanceolate; calyx campanulate, 5-lobed; petals exceeding the calyx, sometimes auriculate, apically notched; an droecium included, the column usually basally hirsute, the stamens numerous; styles 10-17, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, hirsute; mericarps 10-17, ventrally and apically dehiscent, laterally smoothwalled; seeds solitary, reniform. 2n = 20 (three species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Annual erect herbs. Leaves opposite, petiolate, simple and ovate to pinnately com- pound. Heads solitary, terminal, pedunculate. Receptacle convex. Paleae conduplicate, scarious, with brown-orange longitudinal lines. Phyllaries multiseriate, lanceolate to narrowly ovate, with the outer bracts herbaceous, with the inner bracts scarious, and with brown-orange longitudinal lines. Ray florets pistillate, fertile, uniseriate; ligules at apex markedly 3-parted, with few to many brown-orange longitudinal lines; fruits obovoid, slightly radially compressed, black, glabrous. Disc florets sterile, hermaphroditic, with corolla lobes 4; anthers black; style undivided; ovary rudi- mentary. Pappus absent. Chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Stuessy, Tod F. 1975. A revision of Moonia (Compositae, Heliantheae, Coreopsidinae). Brittonia. 27: 97-102.

description: Shrubs, when pubescent the hairs incompletely septate; stipules bifid and cadu- cous. Inflorescences terminal, corymbiform. Calyx 5-lobate, one lobe expanded into a foliar structure; corolla infundibuliform, internally pubescent; corolla lobes 5, valvate; stamens 5, inserted at the base of the corolla tube; stigma bilobed. Ovary bilocular; ovules numerous, inserted on a discoid axile placenta. Fruit globose; seeds (Fig. 1) 0.5-1.5 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm in diam, foveolate; seed coat (Figs. 2, 3) with regularly polygonal cells, 91-189 (124.3) x 63-105 (86.2) utm,2 large pits scattered in the internal walls (Figs. 2, 3), 4-14 pits per cell, 7-21 /m in diam, the lateral walls thick, 7-14 µm thick, the external wall smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Kirkbride, M. C. G. 1979. Review of the neotropical Isertieae (Rubiaceae). Brittonia. 31: 313-332.

description: Slender, cespitose bamboo. Culms 0.5-2.5 m tall. Leaves ca. 15 in a terminal complement; sheaths puberulent in lines, the truncate summit slightly auriculate on one side and bearing delicate fimbriae 4-8 mm long, white, delicate; outer ligule 0.1 mm long; blades 15-20 X 0.8-1 cm, linear-lanceolate, cuneate basally, glabrous, the margins and near-marginal veins scabrous. Inflorescences not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Judziewicz, Emmet J. 1998. A revision of Myriocladus (Poaceae: Bambusoideae: Bambuseae). Brittonia. 50: 430-446.

description: Cespitose bamboo from short, sympodial rhizomes, the basal, bladeless sheaths of each shoot shiny, stramineous, and persistent. Culms 1-5 m tall, to 1.2 cm diam., unbranched above the base, hollow with an irregular, pithy lumen; internodes glabrous, smooth, shiny, the lowest apparently to 1 m long, successive nodes crowded, spaced only 3-5 cm apart. Leaves in complements of 5-15, crowded and strongly overlapping; sheaths stramineous, glabrous, shiny, the summit strongly keeled; sheath summit oblique, bearing along its margins a membranous, brownish auricle to 10 mm long that resembles a confluent cluster of sinuous fimbriae, these apparently never splitting; outer ligule 0.2-0.8 mm long, indurate; inner ligule 0.8-2 mm long, puberulent; pseudopetiole absent; blades 35-100 X 1.5-4 cm, tardily deciduous, linear-lanceolate, coriaceous, sometimes splitting longitudinally, the base slightly rounded but not much wider than the apex of the sheath, the apex acuminate, smooth, glabrous, the upper surface with the midrib slightly depressed, the lower surface somewhat nodulose, with the midrib strongly raised, the margins scabrous. Peduncle 30-70 cm long, terete, stout, solid, puberulent. Inflorescence 40-110 X 4-8 cm, a narrowly pyramidal panicle; rachis ridged, pubescent; branches 100-275, pulvinate, divergent to spreading, pubescent, the lowermost 1.5-4 cm long and rather distant, the upper shorter and crowded, all bearing neat rows of spikelets on pedicels 1-2 mm long on their lower sides. Spikelets 2.8-3.8 mm long, elliptical to ovate, 1 (-3)-flowered, smooth, shiny, glabrous or with the awns or summits of the bracts puberulent; glumes brownish, 1-nerved, unequal; glume I 1-1.8 mm long, subulate, acute to subaristate; glume II 2.3- 3.3 mm long, lanceolate, acuminate or more often abruptly awned, the awn to 2.5 mm long; lowest (sterile) lemma 1.8-3 mm long, ovate, acute to abruptly awned, the awn to 1.2 mm long; florets 2.9-3.3 mm long; lemmas ovate-elliptical, obtuse, slightly cucullate, 3- or 5-nerved, only the raised midnerve prominent; paleas usually slightly longer than and protruding from the lemmas; rachilla prolonged past the upper-most floret by 0.5-1 mm, bearing a rudimentary floret 1-2 mm long. Flowers with anthers ca. 1.6 mm long. Fruit not seen.

description: Monotypic. Robust perennial herbs with a dense, fleshy fibrous root system supporting a perennial crown; stems annual, 1.5-3 m tall, minutely and sparsely stellate-pu- bescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades large (to at least 30 X 35 cm), gradually smaller upward, deeply palmately 5-9-divided, the lobes more or less lanceolate, coarsely serrate, acuminate, minutely and sparsely stellate-pubescent, less sparsely so beneath; stipules 2-3 cm long, triangular-lanceolate, 4-9 mm wide at base, persistent. Inflores- cences terminal, paniculate, the subunits umbellate; involucel absent; flowers unisex- ual; calyx small, basally rounded, ca. half divided, sparsely pubescent; petals white, ca. twice length of calyx; staminate flowers with narrow staminal column surmounted by a globular cluster of anthers; pistillate flowers with a rudimentary androecium, 6-9 emergent slender styles with unilaterally decurrent stigmatic surfaces. Fruits oblate, 5-7 mm diam., glabrous; mericarps 6-9, with a small apical beak (or beak obsoles- cent), indehiscent, fragile-walled; seeds sol- itary, reniform, 3 mm long. 2n = 30 (Iltis & Kawano, 1964).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Leaves alternate, simple, notophylls to mesophylls, coriaceous, persistent or caducous, oblong, symmetrical, base and apex acute, margin denticulate, teeth seriation simple, tooth spacing regular; cicatricose-crateriform glands present, never paired; marginal glands absent; venation pinnatinerved, agrophic veins absent; primary vein moderate to stout, straight; secondary venation eucamptodromous, with 8-10 pairs of secondary veins with an acute angle of divergence; tertiary veins opposite percurrent; quaternary veins polygonal reticulate, fifth order veins opposite percurrent or ramified; orders of venation 7, aréoles imperfect; veinlets simple; ultimate marginal venation looped (Fig. IG). Midvein bundle sheath sclerified, higher order veins sclerified, veinlets naked or with sclerenchymatous sheath cells; mesophyll dorsiventral with numerous dispersed fibers (Fig. 3E), with druses in the mesophyll, polygonal crystals along the vascular bundles (Fig. 2F); tannins occluding the lumina of some spongy parenchyma cells; epidermis simple, epidermal cells elongate or isodiametric in surface view, abaxial anticlinal cell walls undulate; cuticle smooth; stornata in the abaxial surface, stomata type not seen, guard cells without striations; sparsely pubescent, trichomes simple, ornamentation not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Cervantes, A., et al. 2009. Foliar architecture and anatomy of Bernardia and other genera of Acalyphoideae (Euphorbiaceae). Brittonia. 61 (4): 375-391.

description: Perennial herbs of small to medium size. Rootstock a bulb. Basal leaves plicate, linear-ensiform. Stem simple or few-branched. Inflorescence few- to several-flowered spathes herbaceous or dry at apex. Flowers stellate; tepals subequal, spreading. Stamens erect, free or the filaments partly to entirely united; anthers longer than fila- ments, linear, occasionally very large, collapsing spirally after anthesis. Style with filiform branching near the apex of filaments, the branches each divided almost to the base and spreading horizontally between the anthers, stigmatic at the apex. Capsule ovate-oblong, truncate. Basic chromosome number: x = 7.
bibliographicCitation: Goldblatt, Peter. 1976. Revision of the bulbous Iridaceae of North America. Brittonia. 27: 373-385.

description: Monotypic. Small shrubs, minutely stellate-pubescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate-oblong, discolorous, the margins prominently undulate-crenate; stipules broadly triangular. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels exceeding the corresponding petiole; involucel absent; calyx 5-lobed, the lobes undulate-crenate (like the leaves) or pinnately divided; petals lavender or pink, exceeding the calyx; staminal column half the length of the petals or less, apically staminiferous; styles 5-8, clavate, pilose [?], the stigmatic zone bilaterally decurrent. Fruits schizocarpic, stellate-pubescent; mericarps 5-8, apically aristate, ventrally and apically dehiscent, each 2-3- seeded. 2n = 16
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Monotypic. Shrubs 2-3 m tall, the stems coarsely stellate-pubescent. Leaves petio- late, the blades 3-5-lobed, cordate, crenate, acuminate, 6-15 cm long; stipules subulate, inconspicuous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, long-pedicellate, the pedicels with more or less retrorse pubescence; involucel absent; calyx 5-lobed, stellate-pubescent, reflexed in fruit; petals 1.5-3 cm long, purple; androecium included, yellowish, filamentiferous at apex, the column pubescent; styles 8-12, slender, the stigmas capitate. Fruits globose-inflated, schizocarpic, densely pubescent; mericarps 8-12, 2-2.5 cm long, dehiscent, fragile-walled, with 2 divergent basal spines 6-14 mm long that are stellate-pubescent; seeds 3 per mericarp, 3 mm long, warty. 2n = 3
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Low, erect, herbaceous, acaulescent, glabrous, cespitose perennials, from tap-roots. Leaves petiolate, pinnate, the pinnae linear, entire or occasionally lobed or toothed. Petioles sheathilng below. Inflorescence of loose compound umbels; peduncles terminal, longer than the leaves. Bracts of involucre wanting. Rays few, spreading, reflexed in flower and fruit. Bractlets of involueel inconspicuous, linlear-laleeolate, sometillmes minutely scaberulous on the margins. Pedicels spreading and reflexed. Flowers yellow; petals inflexed at apex; calyx-teeth evidelnt, deltoid-acute to subacuminate, reflexed and persistent in fruit; styles short, the stylopodium lacking. Carpophore 2-cleft to the base. Fruit oblong, terete in tranlsection, glabrous; ribs prominent but unwinged, the pericarp somewhat corky; vittae numerous, of various sizes, scattered throughout the pericarp; seed slightly flattened dorsally in transection, the face plane or slightly convex.
bibliographicCitation: Theobald, William L., et al. 1964. A revision of Aletes and Neoparrya (Umbelliferae). Brittonia. 16: 296-315.

description: Hypanthium carupanulate, about equaling the acuminate sepals; stamens almost isomorphic, but alternately unequal in length; anthers subulate, the connective well prolonged at base and bearing 2 erect slender anterior appendages; ovary 3-celled; style slender, stigma punctiform. Freely branched herbs, with ovate, serrulate, acuminate, 5-7-nerved leaves and a large branching panicle of small, very numerous, 4-merous flowers. The following is the only species.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Small tree or shrub, 0.5-8 m tall, dioe- cious. Leaves alternate, imparipinnate, estipulate, the leaflets alternate or subopposite, (1- )3- 8, the venation brochidodromous. Inflorescence terminal, subterminal, or axillary, a raceme of glomerules, each glomerule a congested cyme of 1-12 flowers. Staminate flowers maturing and expanding sequentially in the glomerule, few mature at any one time; sepals 5, free, elliptic to ovate or broadly so, 1-1.8 mm long, cymbiform; petals 5, free, elliptic to obovate or broadly so, 1.3-3.2 mm long, the distal half reflexed; stamens 5, united into a columnar androgynophore, the androgynophore terminating in a distal, pubescent rudiment of the pistil; anthers sessile, dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscent with a distal connective. Pistillate flowers: sepals 5, triangular to ovate, 1.2-2.2 mm long, more or less keeled, cymbiform; petals obovate to narrowly so, 2.1-3.3 mm long, the distal half reflexed; androecium and intra- staminal disc not evident; ovary superior, sessile, syncarpous, 2- 4-carpellate, urceolate, pubescent, the stigmas 2-4, sessile, usually recurved, the inner surface papillate. Fruits 1-3 per infructescence, indehiscent, berry- like with a leathery pericarp (an amphisarcum of Spujt, 1994), ellipsoid to globose, the ends rounded or tapering, the surface smooth, slightly striate, or roughly cancellate-wrinkled, puberulent or glabrescent, the pericarp leath- ery, 0.5-4 mm thick, the calyx, corolla, and stigmas persistent or not; seeds 1-4, the cotyledons more or less equal, narrowly elliptic and usually slightly crescent-shaped, dark reddish brown.
bibliographicCitation: Thomas, Wm. Wayt. 2011. Nothotalisia, a new genus of Picramniaceae from tropical America. Brittonia. 63 (1): 51-61.

description: About 100 species. Acaulescent perennial herbs (rarely annuals), usually forming a compact cushion of crowded leaves, the underground stems usually branched, usually covered with persisting leaf sheaths. Leaves petiolate, flabellate to ovate, palmately or pinnately (or bipinnately) dissected, variously pubescent to glabrate (hairs usually stellate, almost always present on upper surface, present or absent on lower surface), with the stipules adnate to the petiole forming a laminar sheath, the stipule tips filiform to broadly ovate. Pedicels adnate to the petiole (inserted on sheath), the flowers sometimes subsessile and crowded among the leaves, sometimes long-pedicellate and overtopping the leaves; involucel absent; calyx gamosepal- ous, ca. half-divided, variously pubescent; petals exceeding calyx, obovate to narrowly linear, variously colored (white, yellow, lavender, blue, purple, red); staminal column usually narrow, glabrous, shorter than the petals, sometimes with a corona-like structure at the base (cf. Chanco, 1992), the anthers forming a globose or oblongoid head at apex of staminal column; styles 7- 14, exceeding androecium, the stigmas clavate. Fruits schizocarpic, hirsute; mericarps 7-14, usually acute or acuminate apically, dehiscent; seeds solitary, glabrous, reniform, often with a longitudinal dorsal furrow. 2n = 10, 20, 30, 40 (many species)
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Herbs robust, basally lignescent. Stems erect, branching, terete, smooth or minutely covered with a crusty exudate. Leaves alternate, narrowly elliptic or lan- ceolate, membranous to subcoriaceous, glabrous; venation pinnate. Inflorescence racemose or spicate, in N. xolocotzii bearing flowers in proximal nodes and short, congested, sterile shoots in distal nodes; flowers initially subsessile, later pedicellate; pedicels terete, smooth or minutely crusty; tepals 5, subequal to unequal, glabrous, green, subcoriaceous, concave or broadly elliptic to spatulate-lanceolate, 3-12 mm long, 1.5-4 mm wide; stamens 7-16, in a single series; gynophore 0.5 mm long extending to 3-15 mm long during maturation, ca 0.5 mm diam, smooth or minutely crusty; ovary green, fleshy, obovoid or obpyriform, carpels 7-9, each carpel terminating in a single style and bearing a single seed, styles basally connate. Maturing fruit a berry, 7-9-lobed or ribbed, obovoid or obpyriform, smooth or rugulate; seeds 7-9.

description: Arbores Mimosaceae tribu Ingeis pertinentes, inermes vel stipulis parvis nonnullis post folium lapsum induratis conicis pungentibus fortuito paratae; folia bipinnata, petiolo nectariis uno vel compluribus obsito, foliolis parvulis oppositis. Flores capitati homomorphi 5-meri polyandri, calycis lobulis valvatis, corolla tubulosa; filamenta in tubum corollae breviorem monadelpha, antheris parvis eglandulosis; pistillum solitarium. Legumen pendulum sessile crasse cylindricum subteres seminibus magnis farctum, valvulis primo laevibus subsucculentis maturis coriaceis rugosis, intus haud septiferis nec coloratis, ambas per suturas sero humi dehiscentibus; semina transversa, funiculo brevi falcato subcamoso sed haud arilliformi gesta, inter se arctissime conferta, perfecta crasse nummularia et imperfecta late cuneiformia, primum et ultimum cum leguminis cavitate sese conformantia obtuse conoidea, omnia leguminis axi verticali horizontaliter versa, testa papyracea laevissima lucida pleu- rogrammate destituta; endospermium nullum; cotyledones plani cornei ebumei virescentes, uterque unam marginem versus attenuatus, alteram versus incrassatus, circacircum truncati. Germinatio epigea.
bibliographicCitation: Barneby, Rupert C. 1989. Obolinga, a new genus of Mimosaceae tribe Ingeae from Hispaniola. Brittonia. 41: 167-172.

description: Small ligneous, glabrous plants, shrubs or trees to 30 meters tall with trunks 10 cm or more in diam, sparsely to much branched. Leaves alternate, subsessile to shortly petiolate; lamina subcoriaceous to coriaceous, suborbicular, obovate, elliptic-oblong to linear or oblanceolate, at the apex obtuse or broadly rounded and emarginate or retuse, at the base rounded, obtuse to acute, entire or remotely dunculate, simple racemes or panicles. Flowers fragrant, pedicellate, the pedicels 1-15 mm long, with bracts 0.4 mm long at the base; sepals 5, slightly connate at the base, reflexed after anthesis, suborbicular, oval, ovate-oblong, or oblong, rounded at the apex, 0.5-3.5 x 0.5-1.6 mm, entire to glandular-crenulate, green to rose-red; petals 5, hypogynous, contorted, persistent, obovate-oblong, rounded at apex, 3.2-6 x 1-3 mm, white to pink; stamens 5, alternate with the petals, the slender filaments dilated at the base where united with the shallow annular disk within the base of the petals; anthers introrsely longitudinally dehiscent, oblong or ovate-oblong, slightly lobed at base, 1-1.5 mm long; ovary superior, ovoid, 5- ridged, 5-celled; ovules 2 in each cell, pendulous; style simple, filiform, equaling or up to 3 times longer than the ovary. Capsule prismatically cylindric, elongated, pointed at apex, 5-valved; seeds fulvous to castaneous, obliquely oblong and curved at the basal end, finely cellular, with a conspicuous, pale, thin wing attached at the distal end which is lanceolate to obliquely ovate, mainly obtuse or rounded at the apex or rarely subacute.
bibliographicCitation: Steyermark, Julian A. & Luteyn, James L. 1980. Revision of the genus Ochthocosmus (Linaceae). Brittonia. 32: 128-143.

description: Robust, herbaceous vines (Fig. 1). Pubescence of rather long, ferruginous or tawny, unbranched trichomes, scattered to densely overlapping on the stems, leaves, pedicels, bracts, sepals, and corolla plicae (Fig. 3). Leaves alternate, petiolate; blades broadly ovate or ovate with mucronate and acute to acuminate apex and cordate to truncate base. Inflorescences axillary, many flowered, capitate cymes; peduncles often equalling or exceeding the leaves, the pedicels very short; bracts numerous, sepaloid, equalling or exceeding the sepals, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous (Figs. 2, 11). Flowers white to lavender; sepals 5, quincuncial in aestivation, unequal in length, abaxially long-villose, adaxially glabrous; corolla of 5 connate petals, campanulate-funnelform, not lobed, indu- plicate-valvate in bud, the 5 midpetaline bands densely pubescent with long trichomes; stamens 5, subequal, included, the filaments inserted near the base of corolla and the adnate portion glandular pubescent, the anthers introrse, slightly curved after dehiscence; pollen 6 (-8) colpate with all colpi equatorial (6-zono- colpate of Austin, 1973b) (Figs. 8-10); style 1, exceeding the stamens; stigmatic lobes 2, subglobose, contiguous; ovary superior, 2-locular, each locule with 2 anatropous ovules. Fruit a 4-seeded capsule, enclosed by the persistent sepals and bracts; seed glabrous, smooth (Fig. 4); embryo lati-longiplicate (Figs. 5-7), surrounded by persistent endosperm.
bibliographicCitation: Buck, William R. 1982. Nematocladia tesserata genus et species novae (Myriniaceae). Brittonia. 34: 414-416.

description: Perennial or rarely annual herbs. Flowers open near sunset but sometimes remain open the next day. Petals yellow, white, or purplish-rose. Anthers versatile. Sporogenous tissue continuous. Stigma deeply 4-lobed, the lobes receptive all around. Capsule many-seeded, sometimes short and more or less indehiseent. Basic chromosome number, x = 7. Self-incompatibility knowil.

description: Erect aquatic annuals from a taproot with fibrous lateral roots; stems immersed for the greater part, green to reddish, simple and glabrous below, branched and capitate-glandular above, the stems fistulous at maturity; leaves alternate, sessile, glabrous, dimorphic (at least in O. tricuspis), linear to lanceolate, the midrib prominent toward the base, the margins faintly revolute; heads few to many, hemispherical, eymose, often subtended by a single bract immediately below the involucre; receptacle flat to slightly convex; peduncles enlargecl below the heads; involucre basally concave, resinous, capitate-glandular, the phyllaries imbricated in about 3 series, united at the base; ray florets pistillate, fertile, yellow, 25-50 in one series, with capitate-glandular throats; disk florets perfect, fertile, 125-250, yellow, the throats capitate-glandular; anthers with apical ovate-lanceolate appendages; anther bases sagittate; style branches of the disk florets appenldiculate, the appendages pubescent without, glabrous within; style branches of the ray florets papillate; pappus of ray and disk of caducous, unequal, antrorsely barbellate bristles; achenes prominently 2- or 3-winged, or 2-nerved, flattened, glabrous, shiny.

description: Dioecious trees, the branchlets subterete, puberulent or glabrous; leaves alternate, petiolate, the blades coriaceous in texture, entire and narrowly revolute at margins, glabrous at maturity, the costa prominent beneath, the secondary nerves several to many, obscurely anastomosing near margins; infloreseences 1-3 in leaf axils or on defoliated branchlets, puberulent, simple or with 1-4 short lateral branches; flowers solitary or fasciculate, subtended by small bracts, pedicellate, the pedicels bracteolate at summit; staminate perianths small, carnose, glabrous within, 3-lobed; filaments connate in a carnose cylindric column, the anthers usually 12 (sometimes 14), 2-celled, linear, subacute at apex, dehiscing by extrorse clefts, dorsally adnate to a carnose cylindrie or narrowly conical connective mass; pistillate perianth slightly larger and more carnose than the staminate; fruit transversely ellipsoid, 2-valved, the pericarp woody, the aril apparently entire, the seed transversely ellipsoid.

description: Subshrubs or rarely herbs, covered with glands. Stems terete to quadrangular, often woody at the base; leaves opposite, lanceolate to obovate, pinnately nerved, with veins sunken in the upper surface and clearly raised beneath, the margins entire to clearly divided. Inflorescence a terminal spike, with solitary subsessile flowers (pedicels to 2 mm long), in the axils of the upper bracteate leaves, bracteoles present in 2 species. Flowers showy. Calyx green, persistent; 5 segments, imbricate, the dorsal sepal ovate, blunt, foliaceous and larger than the other four, which are lanceolate. Corolla violet to blue with a white spot on the base of the lower lip, hypocrateriform, with a long cylindrical tube slightly curved down distally, somewhat villous outside, especially at the apex, inside with a patch of long hairs near the insertion place of the stamens, bilabiate with nearly equal lips with papillose inner side, the upper lip outermost in bud (antirrhinoid aestivation), the lower sometimes slightly 3-lobed, swollen with a convex palate closing the throat. Sta- mens 4, not exserted, inserted at two different heights in the corolla tube, the two posterior sterile, the two anterior fertile and longer; filaments filiform, thickened by a callus at the base, flattened and bent inward at the top. Sterile anthers reniform; fertile anthers dimidiate, coherent by means of the empty inner loculi that form an earlike membranous tissue, the outer loculi fertile and crescent-shaped, very shortly stiped, dehiscing longitudinally by a cleft. Pollen globose or elliptically oblong, tricolporate. Ovary ovoid, pilose, at the base indistinctly surrounded by a disk, bilocular, the placentae paired in the loculi, disjunct, barely touching, peltately stalked. Style filiform, slightly widened at the top; stigma funnel-like, with 2 lobes. Capsule minutely pubescent, ovoid, pointed at the top, septicidal with 2 valves with margins bent inward. Seeds numerous, truncate to nearly ovoid, small, ca. 0.5 mm long, dark brown to black, lengthwise reticulate to minutely pitted, with regular; isodiametric endothelial cells.

description: Approximately 15 species. Annual or perennial herbs, erect or decumbent, usually pubescent, the perennial species often forming a rosette of large leaves at ground level, from which long flowering shoots (sometimes procumbent) arise with heteromorphic, smaller leaves. Leaves petiolate, sometimes ovate, unlobed, and coarsely crenate, sometimes deeply palmately lobed, the lobes pinnately (or bipinnately) dissected; stipules subulate to ovate-sessile, often persistent. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, sometimes aggregated terminally in a leafy raceme, the pedicel sometimes equalling the subtending leaf; involucel absent; calyx 5-lobed (except deeply 3-parted in P. trisepala Hochr.); petals subequal to calyx and inconspicuous (especially in annual species) to large and showy, white, pink, or rose-lavender, often drying purplish; androecium included; styles 30-40, the stigmas clavate. Fruits subglobose, included in calyx; mericarps 30-40, irregularly arranged, each trigonal to reniform, more or less rugose, 1-seeded; seeds glabrous. 2n = 10 (two species)
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Genus Dryopteridearutm habitu peculiare, Jamesoniae subsimile. Rhizoma crassum, erectum, folia dense paleacea, linearia, coriacea, bipinnata, pinnae impari-pinnatae, pinnulae marginibus arcte revolutis bullatae, iis Eugleicheniae similes, sori in cavitate pinnularum occulti, exindusiati, sporae globosae, dense echinati.

description: Capitula homogama pentamera. Involucrum cylindraceum ecaliculatum bracteis 5 subcoriaceis rigidis oblongis basim inerassatis margine in interioribius subseariosis. Flores hermaphroditi 5 in capitulo, corolla tubulosa alba glabra tubulo longo basim versus ampliato limbo usque ad basim 5-fido lobis linearibus. Antherae basi sagittatae vel acutae. Stylus furcatus ramis contortis sursum dorso apiceque subacuto pilosulis. Ovarium oblongum laeve glabrum. Pappus pilis pluriseriatis rigidis strigulosus. Receptaculum planum nudum. Inflorescentiae paniculatae terminales vel axillares. Pedicelli apicem versus bracteolis brevibus. Frutices caulibus vel ramis scandentibus foliis alternis simplicibus coriaceis.

description: Caules erecti, rami foliosi, laterales Frullaniae typo vel ventrales Acrornastigi typo, vel rare ventro-interealares; caulis cum cortice unistratoso ex cellulis partim mnaioribus sistente; folia bifida vel trifida; amphigastria trifida aliquando bifida, magnitudine foliis appropinquantes: [male] et [female] inflorescentiae desunt. Typus: Lepidozia subsimplex Stephani.

description: Trees, ca. 3-15 m; stem simple or few-branched. Leaives alternate, petiolate, abaxial surface commonly with a tomentose or woolly indumentum. Capitulescenices paniculate. Capitula homogamous (except Pa ragynoxys meridanma and P. venezuelae, which usually have heterogamous capitula), discoid; involucre cylindrical, phyllaries 5-8, weakly biseriate or uniseriate, coriaceous or subcoriaceous; receptacle alveolate, denticulate. Florets 5-11(-12), hermaphroditic or, by abortion of the androecium, pistillate; corolla actinomorphic. white, glabrous, limb deeply 5-lobed, lobes linear, revolute, marginal and medial veins prominent; anthers with the base sagittate, caudate, terminal appendage often lanceolate, endothecial tissue with cells oblong-hexagonal, nodes polarized, pollen spheric, tricolpate, echinate, filament collar cylindrical, filament sligthly thickened; style base dilated, style branches linear, contorted. adaxially complanate, stigmatic areas marginal, continuous, thickened, confluent. abaxially papillate-pilose. distally sligthly attenuate, apex more or less thickened, acute or obtuse, conical, central papillae longer, stylopodium denticulate. Achenes homomorphic, oblong, glabrous, 10-veined, 5-10- costate, attenuate towards the base, apex slightly dilated; pappus bristles biseriate, persistent, scabrous, fused at base, stramineous. Chromosome number: 2n = 80 (Nordenstam, 1977).

description: Capitula discoidea homogama plerumque pentamera. Involucrum cylindricum uniseriatum, 5-8 bracteis late oblongis, subcoriaceis. Calyculus parcis (1-5) brevibusque bracteolis vel nuillus. Flores omnes hermaphroditi, vel abortionem causa ferninei polygami. Corolla actinomorpha alba limbo usque ad basim in 5 lacinias lineares fisso. Antherae basi sagittatae. Rami styli longi contorti apice plus minusve incrassati, acute (vel obtuse) conici, dorso praesertirn sursum pilosuli. Receptaculum planum leviter cicatricosum. Arbuscula 5-15 metralia caule simplici vel paulo ramoso cortice resinoso. Folia magna cornosa coriacea rigida simplicia petiolata alterna. Inflorescentiae magnae terminales paniculatae. Achaenia oblonga glabra subtriangulari-compressa leviter lO-costata, pappo stramineo setis biseriatis rigidis strigosisque.

description: Trees, unarmed; inner bark yielding a red exudate; stipules present, caducous; stipels lacking; leaves alternate, imparipinnate, usually with axillary buds; leaflets alternate, subcoriaceous; inflorescences terminal or axillary, paniculate with the lateral branches spicate, the nodes prominent; bracts and bracteoles linear-deltoid to ovate, persistent or caducous; flowers papilionoid; calyx campanulate, the two vexillar lobes mostly connate and slightly longer than the three, essentially separate, carinal lobes; petals glabrous, purple or reddish; stamens 10, monadelphous or, sometimes, becoming diadelphous 5:5, the filaments subequal, the anthers oblong or elliptic, uniform, dorsifixed; ovary (1-3) 4-5-ovulate; style glabrous, slightly curved toward the apex; stigma capitate; fruit sessile, samaroid, indehis- cent, laterally compressed, suboblong with a basal, seminiferous body and a terminal chartaceous wing slightly or well developed; seeds usually 1 or 2, oblong, somewhat sigmoid or deltoid, transverse to the major axis of the fruit; chromo- some number not known.
bibliographicCitation: Rudd, Velva E. 1981. Two new species of Paramachaerium (Leguminosae) [P. krukovii & P. schunkei] and a brief résumé of the genus. Brittonia. 33: 435-440.

description: Sixteen species. Shrubs or subshrubs, erect or decumbent, stellate-pubescent. Leaves short-petiolate, the blades elliptic or ovate to suborbicular, crenate-serrate, acute or obtuse. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils (two species) or more commonly grouped in head-like aggregations subtended by specialized floral bracts, the bracts subsessile, cordate-ovate, serrate, the "heads" subsessile to long-pedunculate; pedicels usually short; involucel of 8-13 bracts, these spatulate or bifurcate; calyx 5-lobed; petals relatively showy, yellow or rose-lavender; androecium included, apically 5-dentate, the anthers distributed more or less throughout the length of the column, sometimes grouped at distinct levels; styles 10, exceeding the staminal column, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 5, glabrous or pubescent, trigonal, more or less smooth and without ornamentation (except winged in one species), essentially indehiscent; seeds solitary, glabrous or pubescent. 2n = 50 (four species), 2n = 100 (one species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: The genus Peltophorum (Vogel) Walpers (nom. cons.) resembles Schizolobium in potentially gigantic stature, abruptly bipinnate leaves, terminal racemose-paniculate inflorescence of handsome yellow flowers, and almost equal calyx-lobes, but differs in grossly peltiform stigma and indehiscent samaroid pod. According to Polhill & Vidal (1981: 90) it contains 7-9 species, five of which are known, either wild or domesticated, in the Americas, the rest being Af- rican or Asian. The taxa recorded from the New World are individually well known and enjoy a stabilized nomenclature, but the morphological differences, both from one another and from deceptively similar exotic species, are less readily apparent. The struc- ture of the flower and fruit of Peltophorum is little diversified and the leaf-formula var- ies too much within the species to offer use- ful characters. Moreover, due to disjunct dispersals, the species have seldom been directly compared. Following review of the material at NY, I here present a key to American species of Peltophorum, whether native or domesticated, and an expanded view of the native P. dubium.

description: Trees with buttresses. Leaves alternate, simple, palmatinerved, petiolate, stipulate. Stipules sheathing, fused on the side opposite the petiole, enclosing the buds, caducous and leaving almost annular scars. Epicalyx (calyptra) entirely enclosing each floral bud, pubescent, opening by a longitudinal slit, caducous before anthesis, leaving an annular scar at the floral base. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals 5, basally fused, the free apical portions slightly quincuncial-imbricate in bud, opening to set the petals free before anthesis, persistent, accrescent in fruit. Petals 5, greatly exceeding the calyx in length, free, connate with the base of the staminal tube, contorted in bud, pubescent at least on the portions of the outer surface that are exposed in bud, caducous. Stamens numerous, forming a staminal tube with 5 more or less distinct alternisepalous phalanges; free filament portions short to several mm long; anthers reniform, monothecal, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary superior, sessile, syncarpous, 2-locular, each locule with 2 axial, basal-ascendent, anatropous ovules; style entire, length equal to or exceeding the staminal tube; stigma discoid. Fruit (as far as is known) indehiscent and 1-seeded by sterility of the second locule and abortion of the remaining ovules, winged by the accrescent, subequal, spatulate, spreading free portions of the sepals ("pseudosamara" sensu Spjut, 1994: 104); basal portion of style persistent; pericarp thin except for apical part, glabrous within. Seeds (as far as is known) glabrous; testa thin except for thickened chalazal region and raphe; endosperm evidently fleshy, possibly reduced during development; cotyledons thin, folded. Pollen grains (Fig. 2) spheroidal to sub-oblate, colporate with short operculate apertures; ora with thickened margins; exine spinulous, microperforate.
bibliographicCitation: Bayer, C. & Dorr, Laurence J. 1999. A synopsis of the neotropical genus Pentaplaris, with remarks on its systematic position within core Malvales. Brittonia. 51: 134-148.

description: Five species. Perennial herbs or sub shrubs, pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate, triangular, or hastate, sometimes 3-lobed, crenate or sub- entire, often with a purple blotch along the midvein; stipules subulate or filiform. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or usually aggregated in terminal panicles or racemes; involucel absent; calyx lobes lanceolate; co- rolla more or less tubular, the petals erect, usually narrow, bright red; androecium ex- serted, filamentiferous at apex, the column more or less pubescent, the anthers yellow or purple; styles 7-15, the stigmas clavate. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 7-15, 1-seeded, umbonate dorsally, the lateral walls evanescent at maturity; seeds solitary, glabrous. 2n = 26 (one species).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1997. The American genera of Malvaceae --- II. Brittonia. 49: 204-269.

description: Stout to slender, erect caulescent perennial herbs, branching in the inflorescence, glabrous or sparsely scaberulous or puberulent, especially in the inflorescence, from a tuberous base probably surmounting a taproot. Leaves petiolate, the blades pin- nately, ternately, or quinately-ternately compound with linear, entire ultimate divi- sions, or the whole leaf reduced to a cylindrical, septate phyllode. Petioles elongate, sheathing, those of the cauline leaves often wholly sheathing and the sheaths con- spicuously dilated. Inflorescence of loose compound umbels; peduncles terminal and usually also lateral, longer than the leaves. Involucre of several pinnatifid, lobed, or entire bracts, somewhat connate at base, shorter than the rays. Rays (fertile) 8-23, spreading-ascending, unequal. Involucel of several bractlets like the bracts. Pedicels (fertile) 2-12, slender, spreading-ascending. Flowers white or greenish-white, the petals usually with a colored midvein; calyx obsolete; petals oblong to oblong-oval or oblanceolate, acute but without an inflexed apex; styles slender to short and stout, ascending to spreading, the stylopodium low conical to lacking. Carpophore divided to the base, the halves filiform. Fruit ovate or oval to oblong-oval, strongly flattened dorsally, glabrous, the dorsal ribs prominent, thickened or thin, obtuse or acute, the lateral with thick or thin wings narrower than the body; vittae rather large, solitary in the intervals, two on the commissure; seed flattened dorsally in transection, channeled under the vittae, the face slightly concave to slightly convex.
bibliographicCitation: Mathias, Mildred E. & Constance, Lincoln. 1967. Some Umbelliferae of the Andean Paramos of South America. Brittonia. 19: 212-226.

description: Shrubs or slender trees with the upper branches usually scandent, or lianas, glabrous throughout or essentially so (inflorescence sometimes pilose), the branches and branchlets alternate or opposite, the branchlets subterete, slightly flattened and swollen at nodes; leaves opposite or subopposite or alternate, petiolate, the petioles canaliculate; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, thyrsoid-paniculate or corymbose or eymose, the branehlets alternate or dichotomously divided, the bracts small; flowers congested or loosely arranged toward apices of ultimate branchlets, small; sepals 5, nar- rowly imbricate, suborbicular to deltoid, often erosulous or fimbriolate at margins; petals 5, narrowly imbricate, usually thin-carnose or sub- membranous, rounded at apex, usually erosulous at margins; disk con- tinuous, free, erect or suberect, short-tubular, memubranous or submem- branous, often crenulate at margin; stamens 3, usually erect, the filaments ligulate, the anthers basifixed, composed of 2 extrorse vertical or oblique locules dorsally adnate to a thickelned connective and later- ally contiguous, the locules dehiscing by longitudinal (or oblique) extrorse clefts, the connective thickened, soluetimes produced into an apiculum; ovary usually depressed-subglobose, often faintly trigonous, the style short, tapering, essentially truncate, the stigmas obscure; locules 3, the ovules 2 or 4 per locule, collateral or somewhat super- posed or in superposed pairs, attached to interior angles near the center, sometimes one erect and the other suspended; fruits small or medium in size, depressed-globose to oblolng-ellipsoid, the pericarp chartaceous or coriaceous, the dissepiments soon evaneseent, the seeds 2-6, imbedded in mucilaginous pulp, oblong, angled.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Suffrutices vel arbores, cicatricibus foliorum conspicuis; laminis foliorum sessilibus gracile-coriaceis, marginum dentibus minutis appressis, costa plerumque utrimque prominente juxta locum articulationis in crassum arthron expandente venis secundariis planis vel leviter prominentibus, parallelis; stipulis deciduis ovoideis vel deltoideis, minutis; floribus in crebrum terminalem racemum dispositis vel solitariis in superiorum foliorum axillibus, rhachidibus rectis, pedicellis elongatis gracilibus loco articulationis plerurnque supra medio, bracteis minutis, deciduis rotundis vel oblongis quam petalis brevioribus, marginibus integris; petalis 5, subaequalibus; staminibus oo in 2 vel 3 ordinibus eircum pistillum semieirculo vel e tribus duobus partibus dispositis, antheris subaequalibus quadrangularibus linearibus cellulis ventralibus paullum dorsalibus longioribus foramine terminale sic lateraliter dorsaliterque disposito filamentis brevibus in unilateralem massam basi ovarii cohaerentibus fructibus persistentibus; pistillis solitariis glabris, triangularibus sub anthesi secundis stylis teretibus brevibus stigmatibus teminalibus gracilibus irregulari-membranaceis vel spongiosis, ovulibus nunierosissimis minutis adscendentibus in nonnullis seriebus in placentis 3-5 formatis intrusisque dispositis; capsulibus rectis vel a basi pendentibus coriaceis-triangularibus fusiformibus leviter faleatis carpellis irregulare-striatis a basi dehiseentibus marginibus gracilibus coriaceis maturitate planis placentis coriaceis sub dehiseentia in colutna ceitrali dispositis denique tripartitis, seminibus. glabris oblongis utroque extreino breviter pellucido-alatis deciduis.
bibliographicCitation: Dwyer, John D. 1944. Philaera, a new genus of the Ochnaceae. Brittonia. 5: 124-127. f. 1.
