description: The Australian species of Spermacoce are usually placed in the genus Borreria G. Meyer, an early segregate from Spermacoce, distinguished by both the cells in the fruit dehiscing, rather than only one in Spermacoce sensu stricto. Borreria, by this definition is a large genus, with a pantropical and subtropical distribution. It is practically indistinguishable from Spermacoce without mature fruit. Within Borreria are variants, some of which may be distinguished by other features of fruit dehiscence that seem at least as significant as that characterizing Spermacoce sensu stricto. At least until these groups within the broad genus can be satisfactorily sorted out, it does not appear practical to maintain more than one genus. Indeed, Dr. Verdcourt of Kew, has recently combined the two (Verdcourt, 1975). Until I know better the rest of the Australian species, I will only treat the two species found on the sand cays, and these will be placed in Spermacoce sensu lato.

description: Low cespitose perennial herbs often with a woody caudex or suffruticose to suffrutescent; leaves alternate, often crowded at the base, pinnately-sometimes bi- or tri-pinnatifid-or pedately divided or simple, usually becoming reduced near the inflorescence, from nearly glabrous to tomentose-canescent with dolabriform hairs; heads apparently discoid, few to several, corymbose to paniculate or subcapitate to solitary; involucre hemispheric to campanulate, the bracts in 2 or 3 series, imbricate to nearly equal, the receptacle conic or concave, naked or pubescent; marginal flowers pistillate and fertile, without ligules; corollas cylindric to lance-ovoid, slightly if at all oblique, nearly glabrous to glandular-granuliferous, rarely pubescent above; disk flowers more numerous, hermaphroditic and fertile, tubular-cylindric to cam- panulate, nearly glabrous to glandular-granuliferous, sometimes pubescent on the 5-parted corolla; anthers with ovate-obtuse to lanceolate or subulate tips; style of the marginal flowers short-exserted, included in the disk flowers or equalling the corolla, the two branches usually longer in the marginal flowers than in the disk where they are truncate and penicillate at the apex; achenes subcylindric and tapering at the base or obovoid and somewhat utricular, usually 5- to 10-ribbed, those in the marginal flowers sometimes 3-angled, glabrous or glandular-granuliferous; pappus usually wanting or somewhat coroniform, rarely of subulate squamellae. Type species, Sphaeromeria capitata Nutt.

description:
Perennial herbs, to 30 cm high. Rootstock a small bulb. Basal leaves plicate, narrow. Stem usually simple, bearing 1 or 2 small leaves. Inflorescence few-flowered, spathes herbaceous or dry above, acute, the inner larger and enclosed by the outer. Fowers secund, blue, with subequally spreading ovate tepals. Stamens free or mon- adelphous, symmetrically disposed. Style declinate, slender below, expanding near apex with 3 short, flat, entire branches. Basic chromosome number not known.

A small genus in northern Florida and Central and South America; about fifteen species.

description: Calyx tube continuous with pedicel, subolobose or obconical, the limb subere(, 4- or 5-lobed; corolla subeylindric, 4- or 5-lobed; stamens as many as or twice as many as the lobes (4, 5, 8, or 10, occa- sionally 6 ol 7), equal or alternately slightly unequal; filaments slender, ligulate, attached to the anthers dorsally near the bases; anthers membranous, produced into 2 tubules as long as or longer than the locules, the tubules dehiscing by oval introrse clefts; style filiform, about as long as corolla, the stigma truncate; fruit subglobose or ellipsoid, the pericarp smooth, brittle, the calyx lobes often per- sistent; locules 4 or 5, the walls soon decaying, the placentation cen- tral; ovules numerous, the basal ones best developed.

description: The position of the genus Sphyrospermnum (including Sophoclesia) within the family Vaceiniaceae has been a matter of disagreement. Bentham & Hooker2 placed the two genera in the tribe Euvaceineae, Drude3 and Hoerold4 in the tribe Thibaudieae. In a recent publica- tion5 the present writer expressed doubt concerning the latter opinion. A more detailed study of the morphology of Sphyrospermrnum strength- ens this doubt. The tribe Thibaudieae rarely has flowers as small as those of Sphyrospermurnm (the genus Themistoclesia is an exception to this statement). The filaments of Sphyrospermurm are usually longer than the anthers, a feature not noted in any member of the Thibaudieae, but common in the tribe Euvaccineae. The fruit of Sphyrospermunt is a globose or ellipsoid berry with a thin and brittle pericarp, much contracted distally to the persistent calyx limb. This fruit becomes very dry and fragile; the fruits of members of the Thibaudieae, upon drying, retain their thick-walled coriaccous aspect. The fruit of Sphyrospermum is so unique that I believe the genus to be of comparatively ancient origin, most closely related, among exist- ing American genera, to Vacciniurn and its allies. In addition to the characteristic fruit, Sphyrosperrnum can be distinguished by its epi- phytic habit, its small subsessile ovate leaves, its axillary, solitary or paired flowers, and its slender cernuous pedicels which are swollen distally, joining the calyx without an articulation. The genus is limited to the American tropics.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1933. The genera Sphyrospermum and Disterigma. Brittonia. 1: 203-232.

description: Epiphytes with strangler capacity, sending down roots and sometimes forming trees of 30 m or more (depending on size of host), or free-standing shrubs or small trees. Trunk, and particularly the branches, usually aculeate. Leaves 3-7-foliolate, petioles 30-220 mm, petiolules 3-10 mm, leaflets obovate to oblanceolate, usually acute and cuneate-decurrent at the base, 30-160 x 15- 56 mm, upper surface glabrous, lower surface glabrous, or somewhat papillose, or sparsely to densely hairy with a mixture of simple and stellate hairs, and usually with prominent venation. Flowers axillary, usually solitary at the ends of branches. Pedicels robust, 10-24 mm, with 3 bracts at the base of the calyx. Calyx robust, persistent, usually cupuliform, sometimes somewhat cone-shaped, externally glabrous, internally densely villous, usually not tightly appressed to the flower bud, entire to irregu- larly 3-5 lobed at margin. Petals 5, narrowly oblong, 40-120 x 5-25 mm, initially whitish-greenish or pink, becoming dark reddish with age, or consistently bright red. Stamens with filaments fused below to form a staminal tube surrounding the ovary, which is usually divided into upper and lower sections by a distinct articulation; when the articulation is present, the lower staminal tube forms a thickened, densely grey sericeous collar, and the tapering upper tube that emerges from it may be sparsely sericeous but becomes mostly glabrous by the point at which five free, sometimes pinkish, filamentous lobes diverge. Each filamentous lobe terminates in two pairs (one pair superposed above the other) of large, bisporangiate thecae (each anther thus tetrathecate and octosporangiate) with partially parallel thecae that are tightly spirally wrapped around staminal tube and its lobes in bud; upper pair of thecae parallel, adjacent, and connate with the connective for most of their length, the lower pair parallel and connate for half or less of their length, then free and divergent, often spiralling. Ovary pyriform, sericeous, with slender style that usually projects the somewhat lobed stigma beyond the level of the anthers. Style may be red, and pubescent towards the base. Fruit a valvate capsule, with endocarp developing cottony fibres ("kapok") that enmesh the blackish seeds.

description: Plants medium size; stems prostrate to ascending, loosely branched, the leafy branches terminal, of the Frullania type (originating in the ventral half of a lateral segment of the apical cell), with the first underleaf of the branch sublate and ventral or nearly so in position, or very rarely bifid and inserted in such a manner that the branch appears to be axillary; intercalary branches ventril in the axils of underleaves; both intercalary and lateral branches leafy or becoming flagelliform near the apices; sexual branches ventral and intercalary, arising in the axils of the underleaves; stem in cross section elliptical, differentiated into an unistratose cortex composed of 18-26, sometimes more, rows of cells, the dorsal often distinctly larger thani the ventral; medulla composed of numerous thin-walled cells of variable size; in longitudinal section of the stem, the medullary cells longer than the cortical cells, with oblique or pointed ends, pits absent; rhizoids colorless, simple or branched at the apices, on the base of the fertilized female bralnch or forming matted tufts on the lamina of the underleaves: leaves incubous, almost longitudinally inserted, small, imbricated to distalnt, asymmetric, with the postical margin longer than the antical and appearing decurrent, more or less quadrate in outline, tridentate, often bidelntate, the lateral margins straight or convex, entire; segments or teeth broadly triangular; sinus lunulate; cells irregularly quadrate-hexagonal in outline, smaller toward the leaf margin, 9-60 µ, in length, 9-27 µ in width, smooth or with small, scattered papillae; underleaves tranversely attached, small, distant, subrectangular to cuneate in outline, quadrifid; branch leaves unlike the stem leaves, larger, rhomboidal, longer than broad, bidentate-tridentate; branch underleaves similar to the stem underleaves but smaller; leaves of the flagelliform branches small, showing a gradual tranlsition to bifid leaves, the juvenile form; dioicous: male branches dorsiventral, the bracts concave and monandrous, to 20 or more pairs, bilobed, an occasional long tooth or slime papilla on each lateral margin; bracteoles much smaller, plane, bifid-trifid, the segments frequently tipped with slime papillae: antheridia in the axils of the bracts, subglobose, the stalk of one row of cells: female branches tending toward a radial symmetry, without innovations, bracts and bracteoles in 3-4 series, increasinig in size toward the archegonia, the bracts of the innermost series quadrifid to four-fifths, the lamina short, broadly rectangular, the segments long, narrowly trianoular-subulate, the margins ciliate or bearing slime papillae; bracteoles similar in outline, two-four-divided, the segments sometimes laciniate, the intermediate series smaller but with longer laminas, the outermost series ovate, bifid to trifid: perianth fusiform, trigonous above, three-layered at the base, two-layered in the median portion, and ulnistratose above, the mouth contracted, bearing long or shorter cilia tipped with slime papillae; calyptra well developed, of one layer of irregularly arranged, thin-walled cells surrounded by about ten archegonia at the base: sporophyte foot simple, seta with an outer layer of eight longitudinal rows of large cells, the interior cells not preserved; capsule not seen. Figs. 1-27.

description: Schweinfurth (1961) recorded only one species of Stenia for Peru, S. guttata Rchb. f. With the removal of S. caudata (Acker- man) Dodson & D. E. Benn. to Ackermania (Dodson & Escobar, 1993) and the addition of new species by Bennett (1992), Dodson & Bennett (1989), and those described here, nine species are known for Peru, and Peru represents the center of distribution for the genus. To aid in the identification of Stenia, a key to the Peruvian species is presented here. It should be noted that Chaubardiella parsonii Jenny (nomen; Jenny, 1989) is S. calceolaris (Garay) Dodson & D. E. Benn.

description: Plants epiphytic or epipetric; rhizomes erect to short creeping, scaly, the scales reddish brown to castaneous, iridescent, deltate to lanceolate, clathrate, glabrous or bearing only an apical cilium; petioles absent to 2 cm long, dark brown, usually sparsely pubescent, the hairs hyaline or reddish simple, 1- or 2- furcate; laminae monomorphic or hemidimorphic, erect or slightly arcuate, linear, characeous to subcoriaceous, 5-10 (-20) x 0.2 - 0.5 (0.8) cm, gradually reduced or truncate at the base, when hemidimorphic, the fertile portion of the lamina less dissected than the sterile; rachises straight, visible or concealed by the laminar tissue, sparsely pubescent, the hairs hyaline or reddish, simple, 1- or 2-furcate; segments linear-deltate to deltate, 1-4(-5)x0.5- 1.5 mm, plane or slightly concave, glabrescent or with hyaline to reddish hairs similar to those of the rachis, present on veins, margins, and laminar tissue, the margin entire, plane or conduplicate, oblique or perpendicular to the rachis, usually widened at the base, decurrent basiscopically and cuneate acroscopically, apex acute to obtuse; veins simple, one per segment, concealed by the laminar tissue on the sterile portion of the lamina, usually visible on the fertile portion of the lamina beneath the sporangia, adaxially with elongate, well-marked hydathodes that lack calcareous secretions; sori basal to medial, rounded to linear- oblong, one per segment, superficial or slightly sunken and embossed on the adaxial side of the segment, sometimes partially covered by the conduplicate laminar margins, sometimes confluent and forming coenosori at the apical portion of the lamina; sporangia glabrous; spores green, trilete, papillate, 20-30 µm long.

description: Creeping or ascending annuals or perennials, all species rooting at nodes. Culms and overlapping leaf-sheaths generally compressed (terete in S. micranthum); blades generally plicate (flat in S. micranthum), abruptly contracted at base; ligule reduced to a line of hairs. Inflorescences mostly terminal, some also axillary, spike-like, dorsiventral or cylindrical, with several to many racemes embedded in pockets on face or sides of main axis; each raceme bearing 1-8 spikelets on a rachis that is usually produced beyond upper spikelet to a subulate tip. Spikelets lanceolate or ovate, awnless, sessile or short pedicelled, falling entire at maturity or with segment of disarticulating main axis. Glumes membranaceous, the lower generally about 1.5 mm long, nerveless (longer and with nerves in S. helferi); upper glume similar to lower in some species, in others 4-5 mm long and with multiple longitudinal nerves. Lower floret staminate or neuter; upper floret bisexual. Sterile (lower) lemma chartaceous to coriaceous, 2.5-5 mm long, acute or acuminate, with 3-9 nerves; fertile lemma similar but slightly smaller and with 3-5 fainter nerves; lemma margins inrolled and embracing palea; palea generally indurated, 2-nerved (absent in sterile florets of S. micranthum). Caryopsis lanceolate to ovate or oblong, 1.5-3.5 mm long, often failing to develop in the perennial species.

description: Plants dioicous, in loose tufts. Leaves erect-spreading, concave, lanceolate from a vaginate base; costa single, subpercurrent, in section with a single row of guide cells with dorsal and ventral stereid bands and enlarged cells on both dorsal and ventral surfaces; margins slightly toothed subapically, strongly serrate apically, entire below, plane or occasionally recurved directly above and below the shoulder; unistratose, cells quadrate to subquadrate and small from leaf shoulder to apex, mamillose; long-rectangular, smooth and thinner-walled in the sheathing base. Perichaetial leaves scarcely differentiated. Seta erect, twisted, somewhat tortuous; capsule suberect to nodding due to a bent seta; exothecial cells short- rectangular, thin-walled, stomata few at extreme base of urn; annulus none; peristome teeth yellow-brown with spiral thickenings their entire length; operculum long-rostrate, oblique. Calyptra cucullate, smooth, only covering the operculum. Spores spherical, 15-18 µm in diameter, very finely papillose, almost smooth.

description: Bush-ropes (rarely shrubs) with stems up to about 55 m. long and 30 cm. in diam. at base, usually provided with tendrils or spines or both; branches opposite, well spaced or sometimes densely crowded into "witches'-brooms," sometimes conspicuously pitted with elliptic or orbicular lenticels; branch- lets terete or flattened, sometimes blackening on drying, often terminating in slender peduncle-like innovations; spines simple and terete, hooked or straight, up to about 3 cm. long, sometimes foliate; tendrils usually issuing from axils of cataphylls, simple, becoming conchoid-coiled, increasing in diam. toward the tapering apex, up to about 10 cm. long; vegetative-butds usually hidden in part or entirely beneath base of petioles, pubescent, with- out imbricated scales; stipule-lines of slightly raised tissue (sometimes becoming leveled in age), straight or convexly or concavely curved; leaf- platforms woody, conspicuously raised giving stems a knobby appearance at nodes, remaining after fall of leaf and torn aside by growth of axillary shoots; leaf-scars shield-shaped, somewhat concave on upper margin; leaves opposite, simple, entire; petioles 0-18 mm. long, smooth or rugose, some- what channeled on upper side and rounded below, often narrowly winged on margins, sometimes blackening on drying; blades variouslv shaped, longest (when mature) at ends of branchlets and shortening toward base where often reduced to cataphylls (and then without leaf-platforms), 1-30 cm. long and 0.4-21 cm. broad, cordate or rounded to acute at base, rounded to long-acuminate at apex and sometimes finely tipped or mucronulate, shining or dull on either or both surfaces, sometimes glauceseent beneath, sometimes drying yellowish, membranaceous to coriaceous, often variously minutely tuberculate on either or both surfaces and leaf tissues aften "roe- egg" celled under high magnification, sometimes with atomic dots beneath, 3-7-plinerved (or rarely pinnately nerved) with inner pair opposite to conspicuously alternate and diverging at 0-30 mm. from base of blade, deeply impressed to slightly raised above, raised beneath, arcuate, the midrib impressed or slightly raised above and raised beneath, reticulation loose or close, faint to prominently raised on either or both surfaces, rarely impressed above. Vegetative-indumentum generally present, the hairs varying in length (from 3 mm. long to barely visible under high magnification), simple and usually consisting of one to several long cells, usually rather uniform in diameter except near apex, sometimes swollen at base, straight (with a tendency to curvature) to markedly curved, spreading to aseending or adpressed with their tips pointing upward, sometimes occurring in double indumentum of spreading straight hairs and shorter adpressed curved hairs, generally brownish, sometimes wholly grey, from very sparsely to very densely distributed and giving a general aspect ranging from microscopic puberulence to thick tomentum, sometimes distributed in lines or wads, sometimes as cilia on margins of blades or petioles, sometimes as minute cilia on the stipule-lines of otherwise glabreseent branchlets, usually denser on under side of blades than above, denser on midrib and nerves than be- tween veins, denser on young growth than oln old, sometimes localized in tufts in axils of principal nerves of blades beneath, usually deciduous with age and often leaving tubercles upon falling, sometimes very minute and universally distributed on blades beneath and then associated with atomic dots. Inflorescences terminal or axillary or both, the axillary flowering branchlets sometimes very slender, sometilmies with all the leaves reduced to cataphylls, or with their axis very much reduced, making the inflores- cences pseudo-axillary, the inflorescence-branches opposite and issuing from axils of bracts, the flower-clusters from about 0.2 to 5 cm. long, corymbose or globose to elongate-thyrsoid, sometimes racemose, densely to loosely flowered (flowers 1 or 3, by reduction, to very numerous), the ultimate components usually in three-flowered eymes with terminal flower sessile or subsessile and lateral flowers on pedicels, the indumentum varying as on the other vegetative parts, bracts and bracteoles present, variously shaped and pubescent, as the calyces which they approximate as they progress up the infloreseent-branches, the peduncles 0-4.5 cm. long, terete or flattened, the pedicels 0-5 mm. long; flowers 5-merous or sometimes 4-ilierous; calyx- lobes more or less imbricate near base and constituting about one-half or almost the entire length of the calyx, broadly ovate to linear, 0.5-6 mm. long, obtuse to long-acuminate at apex, variously pubescent without and sometimes tuberculate or rarely papillose, sometimes pubescent within, usu- ally more or less ciliate on margins, erect or spreading, membranaceous, chartaceous or incrassate; corolla white to yellowish or greenish-white, al- most rotate to salverform, usually carnose and more or less papillose; corolla- tube 0.1-2 cm. long, glabrous and often papillose (the papillae sometimes elongated and hair-like), or variously pubescent without, glabrous within or pilose throughou't (except at the very base) inclusive or exclusive of the throat, rarely containing a shallow corona near throat within; corolla-lobes valvate on aestivation, longer than or equal to or shorter than corolla-tube, ovate-lanceolate or oblong to linear-oblong, erect to reflexed, sometimes cari- nate toward apex within, rarely with a flap of raised tissue near base within, indumentum without as on corolla-tube without, glabrous within or variously pubescent with hairs usually consisting of many short cells, sometimes bearded at base, sometimes pubescent along a curved line near middle; anthers ovate or oblong to linear-oblong or oblanceolate, 0.5-2.75 mm. long, rouinded oni both ends or mucronulate to apiculate at apex, somlietimes acumi- nate at base, glabrous or pilose, inclluded within the corolla-tube to far- exserted, introrse, attached to filaments near their middle or near base; description: Herbs with opposite or alternate simple, entire, 3-nerved, ± pubescent leaves. Inflorescence a number of congested groups of small capitula. Involucre ovoid, multiseriate, its young bracts pale green with dark green apiculate tips, marked with radiating lines, in fruit becoming urceolate and the bracts sclerified and brittle, splitting up along the radiating lines. Ray florets in 1 row, yellow, con- spicuous, neuter, their achenes columnar, sterile, bearing a pappus of minute lacerate scales. Disc florets regular, deeply 5-lobed, the lobes pubescent on the inner surfaces. Anthers pale or translucent. Style branches strap-shaped, acute at the apex, papillose-hairy throughout. Achenes of the disc florets compressed, elliptical, obtuse at apex, black, shining, bearing a pappus of 2 barbellate awns and a ring of very short lacerate scales. Receptacular paleae whitish, stiff, free from the achenes, somewhat shorter than the disc florets.

description: Perennial, commonly herbaceous, rarely suffrutescent, prostrate or twining vines, arising annually from bases of previous shoots, crowns, or from horizontally spreading underground stems. Roots thin, non-tuberous, slightly thicker nearthe origins, deep-penetrating. Stems terete, weak, very thinly to densely villous with 2-armed appressed hairs, light green, light brownish, grey or silvery grey in color. Leaves shortly petiolate to sessile, with entire margins; blade narrowly elliptic, narrowly oblong, oblong-elliptic, narrowly linear-lanceolate, linear or varied forms of these types; base obtuse, acute, attenuate or slightly cordate; apex acute, obtuse, subacuminate or obtuse-acuminate; surface thinly to densely villous, glabrous or with scattered hairs; hairs two-celled (a small stalk-cell and a terminal two-armed cell each), appressed, very fine and soft to long and tough, silvery grey, whitish or brownish in color. Inflorescences axillary, pedunculate, simple or compound dichasial cymes of 1-7(-12) flowers; peduncles usually as long as the leaves or longer; bracteoles 2, at the point of attachment of peduncle to pedicel, scale-like or foliaceous, subopposite, equal or slightly unequal. Sepals herbaceous or subcoriaceous, free or rarely united at the extreme bases, mostly oval or broadly lanceolate, equal or subequal, persistent in the capsules; apex acute, acuminate or obtuse; margin ciliate or entire; outside glabrous or villous with appressed hairs. Corolla funnelform or shortly tubular-campanulate, plicate in bud, with nearly entire or very shallowly lobulate margin, commonly white, occasionally lavender, red or pink, hirsute outside on interplicae (midpetaline bands), glabrous on plicae (infolded areas); hairs on interplicae with 2 unequal arms each (long arms directed toward the apices of petals and short arms frequently not noticeable). Stamens included or partially exserted; filaments straight, unequal or subequal in length, dorsiventrally flattened and widened to the bases, mostly shorter than styles, thinly to densely glandular-villous (hairs with curly arms), frequently villous only on the basal portions (adnate to corolla), occasionally glabrous; anthers oblong, mostly dorsifixed or occasionally appearing to be basifixed, frequently with shallowly sagittate bases, introrse by longitudinally dehiscing slits. Ovary bicarpellate, bilocular, hirsute or villous with 2-armed hairs (both arms of each hair directed toward the mouth of corolla), surrounded by a basal disc; ovules 2 in each loculus; styles almost free to partially united, included or partially exserted; stylar branches (termed stylodia by Jones 1955) nearly equal to unequal in length; stylar base (or stylopodium) distinct or obscure, often persistent in fruits as a short beak; stigmas depressed-capitate, rarely peltate-subglobose. Fruit 1- to 4-seeded valvular capsule with thin wall and a persistent calyx; seeds brownish, smooth, oval or roughly three-angled (then dorsally round), frequently covered with thin membranes derived from arils. Cotyledons thin, narrow, deeply bifid, folded twice against radicles; cotyledonary petioles free or fused. Flowering from April to September.

description: Gramen perenne rhizomatosum aspectu caespitosum sylvis umbrosis incola. Culmi herbacei, erecti, sine ramis, vaginis papyraceis latis persistentibus et radicibus crassis. Laminae apice symmetricae, pagina inferna venetae. Inflorescentia paniculiformis. Spiculae 1-florae, unisexuales, [female] terminales et [male] infra-apicales. Spicula [female]: glumae 2, marginibus cartilagineae, demum tortescentes tessellatae, inferna 5-nervata, superna 3-nervata; anthoecium fusiforme maturitate indurescens; lemma 5-nervata tessellata; lodiculae 3, cuneiformes; stylus singularis, stigmatibus 2 plumosis; caryopsidis hilum lineare. Spicula [male] sine glumis: lemma et palea membranaceae; lemma 3-nervata; palea 2-nervata; lo- diculae 3, cuneiformes; stamina 3.

description: Rhizomatous grass (appearing cespitose) of shaded forests. Culms herbaceous, erect, not branching, with broad persistent papyraceous sheaths and thick prop roots. Blades with a symmetrical apex, green on the upper surface, bluish-green on the lower. Inflorescence paniculiform, the spikelets one-flowered, unisexual, the female terminal and male below. Female spikelets: the two glumes with cartilaginous margins, the whole becoming twisted with age, the lower glume 5- nerved, upper 3-nerved, both tessellate; anthecium fusiform becoming indurate at maturity; lemma 5-nerved, tessellate; lodicules 3, cuneiform; style single with 2 plumose stigmas; fruit a caryopsis with a linear hilum. Male spikelets lacking glumes; lemma and palea membranous, the lemma 3-nerved, palea 2-nerved; lodicules 3, cuneiform; stamens 3.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 1-8 m. high; twigs, leaves, and sepals more or less densely pubescent, many of the hairs gland-tipped; leaves simple, entire, oblanceolate or narrowly oblong, seldom over 4 cm. long; inflorescence of one or a few flowers; sepals 5, lanceolate, acute, persistent, about 6-10 mm. long; petals a, yellow, obovate or elliptical, slightly clawed at the base, erose-dentate at the rounded or truncate summit, about as long as the sepals; stamens 10, 5 commonly larger or better developed than the others; filaments short-hairv below the middle; disk or gynophore very short and adnate to the base of the calyx; carpels 5, distinct; styles deeply lateral; ovules 2 in each carpel; fruit akene-like, the carpels mostlv 4-5 mm. high, pubeseent.

description: Herbaceous epiphyte. Roots fleshy, fascicled, thin, green-tipped. Leaves basal, ovate, persistent at flowering, margin ciliate. Inflorescence capitate, spreading to pendent, several-flowered. Scape ciliate; bracts few, leaf-like, ovate. Flowers erect, lip facing toward center of inflorescence, non-resupinate. Floral bracts leaf-like, ovate, green, margins ciliate. Calyx minutely puberulous, lateral sepals connate, forming a shallow nectar spur. Corolla glabrous. Column foot approximately equal in length to free column portion below stigma and adnate to ovary apex; stigma starting as a spot on each side near bases of staminodes, in maturity confluent and band-like, below anther; rostellum/viscidium absent; anther inserted just above stigma apex; staminodes filament-like; pollinia 4, each clavate.

description: Trees or shrubs; leaves opposite or sometimes alternate, simple, 1-foliolate, or digitately 3-(4-) 5-7-foliolate, the leaflets entire or serrate; indumentum of leaves, petioles and calyx usually similar within a species, often conspicuous, these parts glandular-lepidote, variously pubescent, or glabrous. Inflorescence terminal, short paniculate, very congested to open and much branched; calyx more or less campanulate, bilabiate, 3- or 5-lobed, or subtruncate, glabrous or pubescent, often glandular- lepidote; corolla tubular to campanulate, 5-lobed, slightly bilabiate, yellow, white, purple, red, or pink, glabrous to pubescent without, always somewhat pubescent within; stamens didynamous, included, inserted near base of corolla tube, the anthers glabrous with divergent thecae, longitudinally dehiscent, the staminode small, pos- terior; ovary superior, linear to linear-oblong, glabrous, glandular-lepidote, or pubescent, bilocular, the placentation axile with 2 placentae per locule, the ovules numerous, anatropous; stigma bilamellate; hypogynous disk annular-pulvinate or cupuliform. Capsules ecostate (though sometimes irregularly ridged), pendant, loculicidally dehiscent, linear to linear-oblong, compressed parallel to septum but dehiscing perpendicular to it; seeds biseriate or uniseriate, winged, the wings hyaline and membranaceous, or reduced, corky, and opaque; embryo flattened, the cotyledons foliaceous.

description: About 30 species. Annual herbs or subshrubs, decumbent, ascending, or erect, stellate pubescent. Leaves petiolate, the blades triangular, rhomboid, or suborbicular, simple, lobed, or parted. Flowers usually in scorpioid cymes; involucel of (2)3 usually filiform bracts; calyx more or less accrescent, 5-lobed, stellate-pubescent, the hairs often stipitate (the stipe purplish); corolla purple or blue (rarely white), the petals sometimes biauriculate at base; androecium included, the staminal column glabrous or pubescent, filamentiferous at apex, the anthers few (5-20); styles 6-13, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic; mericarps 6- 13, apically usually aristate (sometimes merely apiculate), indehiscent or ventrally dehiscent, densely covered with stellate hairs, these often stipitate; seeds solitary, glabrous. 2n = 10, 20 (many species).

description: Plants pale green to yellowish green, in mats; stems with leaves radially symmetrical to dorsi-ventral, prostrate to erect, pinnate to bipinnate; lateral branches of the Frtllania-type, leafy, with the half-leaf dorsal, subulate to bifid, rarely becoming flagelliform; ventral branches axillary, interealary, leafy or flagelliform or short sexual; stem in transverse section with a cortical layer of 18-15-12-6 large, thin-walled cells surrounding a medulla of smaller cells; rhizoids few to many, from small basal cells of the underleaves, the base of a ventral branch, or the scale leaves of flagelliform branches; leaf insertion transverse, the leaf wedged between adjacent horizontal rows of cortical cells; leaves divided to one-half their length into 6-5-4 segments or to the base into 3 or 2 segments, each segment a row of 4-8 elongate cells, the lamina 4-3-2-1 rows of cells high, or absent; branch leaves with one or two segments less than the leaves; underleaves as large as and similar to the leaves, or much reduced, bifid and 2-4 cells long. Plants dioicous, or autoicous (Muiller 1956),. Male infloreseence terminal on the stem or long branch, becoming interealary in position, the antheridia in the axils of the male bracts; female infloreseence terminal on the stern or long branch or on a short ventral sexual branch, without innovations, the bracts and bracteoles in three or four series and different from the leaves; perianth long, exserted, of one layer of cells, three-lobed above, the mouth contracted, crenulate to long ciliate; unfertilized archegonia at the base of the calyptra; shoot/sporophyte relationship forming a shoot-calyptra. Capsule cylindrical, reddish brown, the wall of three layers of cells, the seta of 16-8 rows of large cells surrounding many smaller cells. Sporeling protonema of the Nardia type, i.e., a pile of cells developed outside the old exospore.

description: Two species. Shrubs or small trees 1-5 m tall, with minute stellate puberulence. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate to elliptic, subcordate, entire or serrulate, usually acute, stellate-puberulent above and beneath; stipules subulate, inconspicuous, caducous. Flowers in terminal or axillary panicles, the pedicels 0.5-2 cm long; involucel absent; calyx campanulate, ecostate, halfdivided, small; petals exceeding calyx, yellow; androecium included; styles 5-10, the stigmas capitate. Fruits schizocarpic, stellate- pubescent; mericarps 5-10, divided into two cells by a transverse endoglossum or the endoglossum lacking and the upper cell suppressed; seeds one per cell, reniform. description: Seventeen species. Shrubs or more commonly trees, glabrous or pubescent, usually glandular-punctate. Leaves petiolate, the blades ovate or trilobulate, entire, obtuse to acuminate, often with abaxial foliar nectaries. Flowers large and showy, borne single on axillary pedicels (sometimes aggregated apically), sometimes with bracteate articulation; involucel of 3 to many elements, sometimes subtended by trimerous nectaries; calyx truncate to 5-lobed; petals white, yellow, or rose, with or without dark spot at base, staminal column pallid, usually included, apically 5-dentate; style single, the 3-5 stigmatic lobes decurrent. Capsules 3- 5-locular, coriaceous or ligneous, dehiscent or indehiscent; seeds several per locule, glabrous or pubescent. 2n = 24, 26, 28 (four species)

description:
Lianas semiherbiceas; ramitas conspicuamente aplanadas cuando jóvenes, teretes o subteretes en la madurez, glabras, con secreción lechosa; coldteres interpeciolares no evidentes. Hojas opuestas a subopuestas, res, con numerosas flores relativamente aglomeradas, glabras, pedunculadas, brácteas escariosas, inconspicuas; sépalos 5, esencialmente iguales, usualmente no imbricados, escariosos, erectos o con el ápice conspicuamente reflexo, con un colóter solitario opuesto a cada sépalo, subentero a variadamente lacerado apicalmente; corola urceolada a campanulada, glabra o glabrada, con solo los lóbulos ciliados marginalmente, con una corona anular alrededor de la boca, inconspicuamente lobulada o pentalobulada y con cada uno de los lóbulos irregular y levemente lobulados marginalmente, sin una corona epiestaminal interiormente, los 16bulos de la corola erectos a suberectos, con aestivación dextrorsa; estambres apicalmente exsertos, pero envueltos y ocultos por los lóbulos de la corola, insertos en la parte superior del tubo de la corola, las anteras conniventes y firmemente aglutinadas a la cabeza estigmática, sagitadas, fértiles apicalmente, las auriculas estériles basales cortamente acuminadas, los filamentos fusionados en gran parte de su longitud y rodeando el estilo; ovario bicarpelar, los carpelos fusionados apicalmente con el estilo, los óvulos numerosos, la cabeza estigmitica con forma de carrete de hilo, fusiforme, con un collar membranoso presente en la base; nectarios cinco, libres o algunos de ellos levemente fusionados basalmente. Folículos desconocidos.

Este género es endémico a México, con dos especies restringidas a los estados de Oaxaca y Veracruz.

description: Sepala 3, lanceolata aequalia. Corollae tubus elongatus, lobi oblongo-lanceolati majusculi. Tubus stamineus elongatus. Staminodium exterius solitarium, amplum, petaloideum. description: Flowers 4-8-merous; hypanthium mostly campanulate, varying to tubular; sepals well developed and frequLently exceeding the hypanthium; petals often large and brightly colored; stamens weakly to strongly dimorphic; anthers subulate, except in one section of the genus, the connective more or less prolonged below the anther and ending in 2 small or conspicuous tubereles or short spurs; ovary mostly 4-5-celled, with filiform style and punctiform stigma. Herbs or shrubs, simple or freely branched, almost always freely pulbeseent and sometimes strongly lepidote; flowers usually numerous, in terminal panicles. More than 200 species, abundant throughout the American tropics. The genus is weakly distinguished from the preceding, which has a winged hypanthium, the following, which has branched hairs on the hypanthium, and Itatiaia Ule, which differs in its stamens. The section Purpurella, with rounded anthers opening by a large terminal pore, has perhaps better claims to genieric recognition.

description: Shrub or tree 1.5-15 m. Leaves alternate, 3(-4)-foliolate, petiolate; blade entire, chartaceous, dark-glandular-punctate abaxially, often with domatia on abaxial surface in axils of secondary veins. Infiorescence a relatively long-pedunculate, variably branched, usually rounded and shortened thyrse, produced laterally near apex of twig, the partial inflorescences 2-4, usually closely proxi- mate at apex of the peduncle, rarely (in T. diandra) alternate along a primary rachis, dichasial at first node, dichasial or monochasial at higher nodes, the ultimate branches often secund. Calyx subentire or ? dentate, persistent in fruit, the lobes quincuncial in bud. Corolla tubular, actinomorphic, white, greenish in bud, ±pubescent without, tomentulose within, especially in the tube, the petals (4-)5, linear, tightly or weakly coherent in a straight tube, the lobes imbricate in bud, recurved at anthesis. Androecium of (4-)5 fertile stamens or rarely (in T. diandra and an odd individual of T. tubifiora) of 2 fertile stamens and 3 staminodes; filaments flattened, free from or coherent to each other, tightly or weakly adherent to the corolla tube by abaxial woolly pubescence, free and glandular-punctate above; anthers free, glabrous, usually each with a sterile base above its attachment to filament and with a symmetric, entire or notched appendage at base (in T. diandra, appendage lacking), the connective glandular-punctate; pollen grains 6-short-colporate, oblate-spheroidal, very large (sensu Erdtman, 1971), the exine reticulate (Morton & Kallunki, 1993: fig. 1OF-I). Disc cupular, pubescent on rim. Ovary of (4-)5 carpels free laterally, connate axially and basally; style 1, glabrous; stigma capitate, ultimately exserted from the corolla tube. Fruit of 1-5 mericarps, at maturity free except at base, each with a dorsal ridge and often with two lateral ridges along the line of confluence with adjacent carpels, transversely ridged on intervening surfaces, rounded dorsally. Seed 1 per carpel, oblong, smooth, glabrous, the testa papery. Embryo curved, the radicle apical, the cotyledons rounded, conduplicate, plicate, subequal, stiff, glandular-punctate.

description: Flowers 5-6-merous; hypanthium campanulate to conic or subglobose; sepals elongate-triangular to nearly obsolete; petals mostly medium-sized; stamens isomorphic, the filaments slender and glabrous, the anthers linear or linear-subulate, somewhat ineurved at the apex so that the single pore is obliquely introrse; connective not prolonged below the anther, often with a minute dorsal or basal spur or protuberance; ovary partly inferior, 3-5-celled, with stout elongate style and capitate stigma. Shrubs with ample leaves, sometimes anisophyllous and in the commoner species with formicaria on the petiole or base of the blade, and usually ample terminal panicles of white or pink flowers. About 40 species, primarily Amazonian in their distribution, but extending also to Bolivia, southern Brazil, and Central America.
bibliographicCitation: Gleason, Henry A. 1932. A Synopsis of the Melastomataceae of British Guiana. Brittonia. 1 (3): 127-184.

description: Lianas, or slender shrubs or trees with the upper branches scandent, glabrous throughout or essentially so, the branches and branchlets opposite or subopposite, often swollen and slightly flattened at nodes; leaves opposite or subopposite, rarely alternate, petiolate, the petioles canaliculate; infloreseence axillary or arising from defoliate branchlets, often replete with incilaginous fibers, thyrsoid-paniculate or pseudodichotomously branching, occasionally truly dichotomous, the branchlets subtended by small bracts; flowers usually arranged in loose clusters of 2-5 near or at ends of ultimate branchlets, each usually separately subtended by a minute often eaducous bracteole; sepals 5 (rarely 4 or 6), narrowly iimnbricate, semiorbicular to deltoid or ovate, entire to finibriate at iliargins; petals 5 (rarely 6), narrowly imbricate, submembranous to thin-earnose, usually rounded at apex; disk short- tubular, continuous, mieibranous to thin-c4rnose, encireling the ovary but free froin it or sometimes adnate to it by inconspicuous inter- staminal septae, entire or undulate or crenulate at margin; stamens 3 (rarely 4), inserted within the disk, erect to subspreading, usually about equalling the gynaeciuli in length; filaimients ligulate, mem- branous to thin-carnose, sometimes conspicuously broadened toward base; anthers transversely ellipsoid or oblong or reniform, broader than long, basifixed but usually extrorsely nutant, the locules 2, usually subglobose and laterally confluent, dehiscing by horizontal confluent extrorse (apical) clefts; ovary depressed-conical or subtrigonous (or rarely 4-angled), the angles usually rounded and inconspicuous; style short, carnose, terete, sometimes suleate; stigmas 3 (rarely 4), obvious and divaricate, alternate with or opposite to the stamens and locules, deltoid or oblong, entire or emarginate or bilobed (sometimes deeply so), or obscure and negligible on the truncate style; locules 3 (rarely 4), the ovules usually 2 and collateral or superposed, sometimes 4 and superposed in pairs, rarely (in T. cylindrocarpa only) 6 or 8; fruits usually subglobose to ellipsoid, rarely cylindric (in T. cylindrocarpa only, as far as known), often large (reported to 12 cm. in diameter), the pericarp coriaceous, the dissepiments often evanescent, the seeds usually few, rarely many (in T. cylindrocarpa only), angled, imbedded in mucilaginous pulp.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Albert C. 1940. The American species of Hippocrateaceae. Brittonia. 3: 341-555. f. 1-12.

description: Annual or perennial, erect, procumbent, or decumbent, subscapose to leafystemmed herbs (sometimes suffrutescent below) from a single, slender, taproot (rarely with woody, tuberous enlargements), often rooting at the nodes in procumbent and decumbent types; scarcely to sparsely or densely pubescent, puberulent, pilose, hirsute, hispid, or canescent-tomentose (in T. candidissima), often with glandular-tipped trichomes, especially on the peduncles and outer bracts; leaves opposite (rarely alternate above), simple or trilobed to pinnately lobed or divided, the margins entire, serrate, or dentate, to repand; inflorescence solitary or a few- to many-headed cymose panicle; heads discoid or radiate, subcampanulate (urceolate n T. erecta) to broadly campanulate, on slender or stout, elongate peduncles; involucre subuniseriate or 2-3 seriate, the bracts subequal in length, to 4-5 seriate with the bracts conspicuously unequal in length, imbricated, greenish, and usually purple to purple-tinged toward the tips; inner bracts with scarious-purple margins, obscurely to conspicuously vittate; receptacle short- or long-conical to convex or nearly flattened; chaff scarious, persistent (rarely readily deciduous), at least partially enclosing the achenes, yellowish to yellowish-green; ray flowers, when present, pistillate and fertile, tubular at the base, with inconspicuous to conspicuous white, yellow, roseate, or purplish ligules, the ligules obscurely or conspicuously bilabiate, external lip obscurely to conspicuously (2-)3(-4)-lobed or divided, 1 or 2 inner lobelets apparent, merely vestigial, or obsolete; pappus of the ray florets reduced, or like that of the discs (rarely absent); disc florets with regular corollas (except in T. bilabiata and, occasionally, T. coronopifolia), yellow, or less often whitish, partially cyanic, or greenish-yellow, narrowed below into a relatively slender or broad tube, glabrous or pubescent, abruptly or gradually forming a tubular to narrowly funnelform throat, the lobes equal, sublanceolate, acute or obtuse, erect to reflexed or involute at the apex; style branches recurved to revolute, slender and subterete or flattened on the inner surface, with obscure to conspicuous subulate tips, the stigmatic lines on the inner surface weakly defined or obscure; anthers partially to almost completely exserted, obscurely to obviously sagittate at the base, with ovate, cordate, sagittate, or rarely rhombic terminal appendages; achenes turbinate or narrowly obconical to subcylindrical, terete to ridged, often recurved and compressed toward the periphery of the heads, glabrous to densely pubescent with long or short, ascending (rarely matted) hairs; pappus rarely absent, or of 20 (less often 10 or 35-45) plumose or fimbriate, linear-lanceolate (rarely oblong) scales and/or slender bristles; x = 9 and 10.

description: Tuft-forming perennials with much-branched and elongated rhizomatous aerial stems. Leaves 3-ranked; leaf sheaths tubular, closed to the mouth; leaf blades persistent; ligule selerioid, consisting of a prolongation of the ventral surface of the sheath beyond the base of the blade. Flowering culms essentially erect, axillary but sometimes appearing to be terminal; infloreseence paniculiform, composed of several-numerous clusters of pedicellate spikes borne in the axils of leaf-like bracts. Spikes (in the subgenus Afrotrilepis) composed of bisexual spikelets, or (in the subgenus Euttrilepis) composed of unisexual spikelets; in the latter case the spikes may be either entirely staminate, entirely pistillate, or both kinds of spikelets may be aggregated with the pistillate ones terminal in the spike. Bisexual spikelets 2-3-flowered, composed of a single pistillate flower sessile at the base of a 1-2-flowered spikelet-like staminate cluster; staminate and pistillate spikelets both 1-flowered. Staminate flowers composed of 2-3 stamens subtended by a single glume; filaments elongated and persistent; anthers linear, the connective prolonged beyond the thecae as a minute mucro. Pistillate flowers composed of a single pistil subtended by a pair of glumes; style short or obsolete, the 3 elongated and eventually deciduous stigmas sessile on the apex of the pistil. Achenes thin-walled, narrowly oblong-conical or fusiform, terete or sub-terete in cross-section except at the more or less triangular apices; only the lower portion of the achene filled by the seed. Perianth composed of a hypogynous ring of simple hairs, these undoubtedly representing the fimbriated remnants of 3 (or more ?) perianth segments (see map, fig. 1, for distribution of the genus).
bibliographicCitation: Gilly, Charles L. 1943. An Afro-South-American Cyperaceous complex. Brittonia. 5: 1-20. f. 1.

description: The genus Trillium consists of two subgenera. One comprises the pedicellate- flowered species, and the other includes all those with sessile flowers except T. pusillum Michx. var. virginianum Fern. (Fernald, 1943). Pedicellate-flowered species probably preceded the sessile-flowered group phylogenetically. The derivation of the sessile- flowered condition is suggested by the presence of pedicels in the more primitive related genera Paris, Scoliopus, and Medeola, which, together with Trillium, constitute the tribe Parideae sensu Krause (1930) of the Liliaceae, and by the presence of both pedicellate and sessile forms in T. pusillum. In this species some of the northernmost populations contain many plants lacking pedicels. Representing one extreme of the variation in a predominantly pedicellate species, these populations also furnish evi- dence of the probable origin of the sessile-flowered habit from pedicellate progenitors as suggested by Berg (1958).

description: Plants terrestrial or sometimes epipetric. Rhizomes short to o long creeping, scaly, the scales narrowly lanceolate, not clathrate, light to dark brown. Fronds monomorphic, borne approximately to subdistant intervals, not articulate to the stem; stipes at base with few lanceolate scales, in cross section with several rounded meristeles arranged in a ring; laminae deltate, pentagonal, or elongate, 2-5-pinnate pinnatifid, the basal pinnae basiscopically enlarged (more developed) proximally, the ultimate segments asymmetric at their bases, basiscopic side often cuneate, laminar tissue between the veins either glabrous, pubescent and/or glandular, the hairs reddish brown, septate, 1-9-celled (Ctenitis hairs), also with yellowish or brownish glands, these rounded, sessile or stalked, the stalk 1- or 2-celled, the laminae margins sparsely ciliate (glabrous in T glabrum); basal pinnae anadromic; suprabasal pinnae catadromic; rachises and costae adax- ially slightly flattened, ungrooved, puberulent abaxially, puberulent to glabrous adaxially; veins free or (in some Old World species) anastomosing, without free veins in the areoles, easily visible or not, midribs adaxially raised, lacking grooves, pubescent or glandular. Sori round, borne behind or at the vein tips, receptacles somewhat elevated; indusia circular to reniform or (in some Old World species) exindusiate, glabrous or pubes- cent and/or glandular; spores ellipsoid, monolete, the surface bearing thin, wing like ridges; x= 41.
bibliographicCitation: Prado, Jefferson & Moran, Robbin C. 2008. Revision of the neotropical species of Triplophyllum (Tectariaceae). Brittonia. 60 (2): 103-130.

description: Stout somewhat succulent annuals; long fleshy taproot; stems branched, usually viscid, glandular-pubescent to nearly glabrous, usually reddish at least at nodes; leaves opposite, usually unequal at base; blades often undulate, usually longer than petioles; inflorescences capitate, subtended by 5-10 separate bracts; receptacles flat to somewhat conical, surmounted by short pedicel-like projections; flower maturation pro- gressive from one side across inflorescence to the opposite side; perianth 2-parted, upper part deciduous, lower part forming the anthocarp; abscission scar between perianth parts flat, disc-shaped on mature anthocarps; flowers perfect; perianth lobes 4-5, usually emarginate; stamens 4-5, rarely 3; stigmas linear; anthocarps suborbicular to oval in outline, body indurate, fusiform, body completely surrounded by 2-4 thin membranous, nearly transparent wings; wing veins prominent, often dark when mature; body cavity minutely puberulent; achenes free, narrowly elliptical to oblong.
bibliographicCitation: Galloway, Leo A. 1976. Systematics of the North American desert species of Abronia and Tripterocalyx (Nyctaginaceae). Brittonia. 27: 328-347.

description: The five species known from the Fijian Region are twining vines with slender, terete stems, opposite leaves, and slender, canaliculate petioles. The leaf-blades are usually papyraceous, glabrous or soon glabrate, entire, usually obviously glandular on the upper surface at the base, and with a lax veinlet-reticulation that is plane or faintly prominulous on both surfaces. The inflorescences are lateral to a leaf, 1 (or rarely 2) per node, simply (Fig. 31) or compound (Figs. 7, 13) umbelliform-cymose, usually with congested-racemiform umbels. The flowers have membranaceous calyces (Figs. 8, 33) that are campanulate-subrotate at anthesis but have the lobes quincuncial in bud; the sinuses are glandular within (Fig. 8), although sometimes obscurely so. The corollas are essentially membranaceous, glabrous, subrotate at anthesis, with a short cupuliform tube and 5 lobes that are dextrorsely narrowly imbricate in bud. The gynostegium arises from the base of the corolla (Figs. 16, 26, 34), the short filaments being united into a membranaceous tube (Figs. 10, 24) adnate to the corolla-tube. The 5 basifixed anthers are erect, often dorsally thickened (Figs. 10, 15) or even spurred (Figs. 22-24), laterally free or connate and distally fused with the stigma; above the point of fusion the anthers bear membranaceous, imbricate, rounded, cucul- late appendages (Figs. 11, 15, 22) that are proximally thickened within along the midrib, the thickenings being laterally concave and sheltering a pollinium on each margin (Fig. 36). The 5 translators (Figs. 12, 17, 35) are borne on the stigmatic margin between the anthers and have short, slender, curved caudicles (Figs. 18, 27) that are basal or nearly so; the pollinia are erect (Fig. 36) and are attached laterally (Fig. 18) or basally (Fig. 27) to the caudicles. The 2 ovaries are free, with styles that are distally fused to the stigma, this being pentagonal, carnose, thickened in the center, and membranaceous marginally. The fruit is a follicetum, but usually only one of the follicles matures, this being ovoid to slenderly fusiform. The numerous, flattened seeds are ovate, rounded at base, truncate at apex and there copiously comose with hairs 20-25 mm long.

description: Fruticuli debiles; pubes nulla vel e pilis simplicibus eglandulosis vel stellatis constans; pili unicellulares glandula multicellulari praefixis adsunt; flores in fasciculis aggregati, rotati, corollis albis vel eburneis 5-lobatis; pollinis granula fissuris irregularibus perangustis superficiem disperse pererrantibus provisa; calyces fructiferi reticulati, ad orem aperti, ad basem haud invaginatio. Plantae silvae tropicae.

description: Weak shrubs, suffrutescent, trailing, 0.5-7 m tall. Stem fistulose, glabrous or scarcely to densely villose or pubescent with short, brownish, simple, jointed, incurved hairs, glabrescent with age. Petioles glabrous to densely villose, winged by decurrent blade. Leaves alternate or geminate but then one is 1/2 the size of the other, lanceolate to ovate, the margin mostly entire or shallowly sinuate, or with a few angulate lobes, the apex acute to long-acuminate, the base oblique, attenuate and decurrent to acute, glabrescent with sparse jointed and curved hairs, the indument more abundant below, especially along the nerves, the margins ciliate; unicellular hairs tipped with a multicelled gland also present. Inflorescence of axillary fascicles with (1-)2-7 flowers, sometimes only one maturing to fruit. Pedicels glabrous to densely tomentose or villose with jointed hairs, sometimes with a common, simple or several-times branched peduncle, making the aggregation of flowers appear like a compound cyme or pleochasium; pedicels in fruit glabrous, thickened to 4 mm. Calyx acetabuliform, thin-chartaceous, densely pubescent when young, mostly glabrous at anthesis, with short jointed hairs, the margins ciliate, truncate or lobed; fruiting calyx chartaceous, pale green, glabrous or almost so, strongly 5- or 10-angled, strongly reticulate-veined between angles, only partially closed at the mouth. Corolla rotate, with lobes 2/3-34 of the total length, whitish or creamish-white with 5 darker spots near the base of the lobes, rarely without spots, the lobes ovate or lanceolate, the apex acute to shortly acuminate, densely and shortly pubescent on the outside, with simple hairs or their basal remnants, especially on lobes; inside throat and base of lobes pulvinous with branched hairs, branches very fine to filamentous; hairs in 5 more or less confluent pads surrounding and above the insertion of the filaments; lobes ciliate. Filaments blue or purplish, inserted at or near the base of the throat; anthers subdorsifixed and with wide connective, giving a sagittate appearance, bluish or purplish to buff brown. Stigma capitate or bilobate. Berry greenish, spheroidal. Seeds bright dark-orange or bright yellow, flat, reniform, alveolate.

description: Herbaceous annuals to suffrutescent perennials, 12-50 cm tall. Stems terete, dichotomously branched. Peduncles up to 10 (usually 1-5) mm long. Leaves sessile to shortly petiolate, narrowly ovate to lanceolate, 2-10 cm long, 0.4-2.7 cm wide; blades acute at the apex. Mature heads solitary to several, sessile to subsessile (peduncles up to 7 mm long). Receptacle convex, paleaceous.4 Involucre multi- seriate; involucral bracts free; outermost bracts two, ovate, apex acute-acuminate, opaque; inner bracts 5-8, membraneous, margin scarious, apex obtuse-acute. Ray florets with ligules yellow, narrowly oblong, apex rounded, flared at base into an annular disc; style branches filiform, flattened, stigmatic surfaces marginal and enlarged, revolute when fruit maturing, apex obtuse; achenes ovoid, laterally compressed, narrowly keeled on adaxial and abaxial sides, notched at point of receptacle attachment. Disc florets with corollas yellow-orange, regular, 5-lobed, lobe apex narrowly acute, throat narrowly funnelform; anthers partially exserted from corolla ca. 1/2 of length; style linear-capillaceous, unbranched; ovary sterile; pappus absent. Paleae lanceolate, scarious, apex acuminate. Chromosome number, n = 16.

description: Six to eight species. Shrubs 0.5-2 m tall,more or less stellate-pubescent, Leaves petiolate, the blades variable, often 3-5-angled, -lobed, or -parted, less often ovate, oblong, or lanceolate, crenate or serrate, with one or more prominent foliar nectaries on the abaxial side, these often yellow-bordered. Flowers solitary or glomerulate in the leaf axils or forming terminal racemes; pedicels usually short; involucel gamophyllous, 5-lobed, the lobes alternate with the lobes of the calyx; calyx 5-lobed; petals rose or lavender; androecium included, apically 5-dentate, the filaments short or the anthers subsessile; styles 10, slender, the stigmas capitellate. Fruits schizocarpic, 5-lobed, the lobes convex; mericarps 5, prominently glochidiate (in the American species) or smooth, essentially indehiscent; seeds solitary, glabrous. 2n = 28, 56 (two species).

description: Herbae annuae, erectae, glabrae. Folia opposita vel alterna, pinnatifida. Capitula pedunculata, fasciculata. Involucra campanulata, ecalyculata; phyllaria uniseriata, connata, glandibus pellucidis instructa. Radii flosculi pistillati; ligulae inconspicuae. Disci flosculi hermaphroditi, tenues, 5-dentati; styli rami longi, tenues. Pappi squamellae 10, quoque aristis 3-5 instructi. Achaenia tenuia, leviter angulata, parce pubescentia. Typus: Vilobia praetermissa Strother.

description: Herbae repentes vel volubiles. Folia glabra vel raro pubescentia, linearia, oblongo-linearia, lanceolato- elliptica vel oblanceolata ad spathulata, basi sagittata vel truncata vel hastata, lobis basalibus dentatis vel integris, apice acuta, obtusa, truncata vel emarginata, mucronata vel tridentata. Petioli 0.5-3 mm longi. Inflorescentiae cymosae, floribus 1-2(3). Sepala subequalia vel duo externa majora, oblonga vel oblongo-ovata, acuta vel obtusa vel raro basi sagittata, interiora vulgo angustiora, lanceolata vel lanceolato-acuminata. Corollae late infundibuliformes vel campanulatae, 10-23 mm longae, pallide luteae vel fere albae, medio vulgo purpuratae. Granula pollinis pantoporata, laevia. Fructus ovoideus, 4-valvatus, glaber vel supra pubescens. Semina 1-4, 2-3 mm longa, ovoidea, trigona, fusca vel nigra, apicibus obtusis, testis in X. tridentata hypogaeis.

description: Small shrubs, subshrubs, or perennial herbs from a copiously branched caudex atop a woody taproot. Stems branched only at the caudex or branched at the caudex and above, usually white, often tinged with purple, glabrous to variously pubescent. Leaves simple, alternate, with prominent, white midribs, sessile; shape variable, orbicu- lar to narrowly linear; margins spinose-dentate to entire, rarely involute; base attenuate to auriculate and subamplexicaul; apex obtuse, acute, acuminate, or attenuate, mucro- nate to spinose. Heads solitary at the ends of the stems or branches, campanulate to hemispherical, 1-5 cm wide. Involucre tightly to loosely imbricated, the phyllaries herbaceous to largely scarious, narrow or broad, obscurely or distinctly keeled, linear to ovate; apices obtuse, acute, acuminate, or attenuate, never reflexed. Ray flowers pistillate and fertile, 4-85 per head; tube slender, 4-8 mm long; ligule light blue or white, oblong to elliptic, 1.2-3.3 cm long, 2.7-7.2 mm wide, obscurely to distinctly 3-toothed; style branches glabrous, slender, 1.2-3.2 mm long, 0.1-0.4 mm wide, linear with obtuse or acute apices. Disc flowers bisexual and fertile, 30-140 per head; corolla yellow, 3.5-10.5 mm long, gradually ampliate or narrowed below into a slender tube and expanded above into a funnelform or campanulate throat; corolla lobes deltoid, to 1.4 mm long; style branches linear or linear-subulate, 0.7-3.6 mm long, 0.1-0.5 mm wide, the appendages acute to attenuate, 0.3-1.6 mm long. Pappus of ray and disc flowers alike, of about 50-100 stout, unequal bristles, tawny or whitish, the longest bristles 4.5-12 mm long. Achenes fusiform, linear, clavate, or rarely ovate, 3-8 mm long, usually somewhat laterally compressed, woolly or velutinous with long, silky, subappressed hairs, obscurely to distinctly costate. Base chromosome number: x = 6.
bibliographicCitation: Watson, Thomas J., Jr. 1977. The taxonomy of Xylorhiza (Asteraceae-Astereae). Brittonia. 29: 199-216.

description: Stems hypogeous and epigeous, erect to decumbent, sometimes dichotomously branched in mature plants. Cataphylls chartaceous to membranaceous, stipulate, persistent or deciduous, base triangular, apex long acuminate to aristate, tomentose, generally reddish-brown to yellowish. Ptyxis erect to inflexed. Leaves stipulate, ascending to descending to spreading, reddish-brown or green when emerging; petiole sometimes blackish in young leaves, terete or subterete, without prickles or heavily to lightly armed with straight or bifurcate prickles; rachis subterete generally with few prickles along the proximal third or without prickles, with up to 60 pairs of leaflets. Leaflets articulate, sessile, papyraceous to coriaceous, linear, linear-lanceolate, lanceolate, ovate, obovate obpyriform to elliptic, opposite to subopposite, falcate or non-falcate, imbricate to non-imbricate, generally acute at apex and symmetric, attenuate at base, margins entire to dentate along upper third, subrevolute, articulations green, yellowish or dark brown in young leaflets. Pollen strobili usually 1-2 (-4), with sterile tip, erect, cylindrical to conical, light brown to purple, tomenrulose, apex acute to apiculate, generally with densely tomentose peduncles; pollen sporangio- phores cuneiform, distal face truncate hexagonal, 0.3-0.55 cm long, fertile abaxial surface 2 lobed with 2-14 bisporangiate synangia per lobe, sporangia dehiscent by longitudinal slit. Ovulate strobili usually solitary, erect to decumbent, cylindrical to ellipsoid, purple to yellowish, generally tomenrulose, apex acute to apiculate; peduncle densely tomentose; ovulate sporangio- phores cuneiform-peltate to scutiform, distal end truncate-hexagonal when not scutiform. Seeds ovoid, sarcotesta white to pink when immature, red at maturity, sclerotesta smooth but sometimes with several furrows running longitudinally from micropylar end.

description: Deciduous or evergreen shrubs or small trees, dioecious, stems, branches, petioles, and leaf rachises prickly or unarmed. Leaves alternate, imparipinnate or parapinnate, pubescent to glabrous. Leaflets opposite, subopposite, or alternate, oblique, crenate, crenulate, serrulate, or entire, pellucid-punctate. Petioles and rachises alate or not. Inflorescences axillary and shortly spicate or umbellate, or terminal and cymose, paniculate, or umbellate. Sepals 0 or 3-5, distinct or connate, deciduous or persistent. Petals 3-5, distinct. Stamens 3-5 (short and staminodial or absent in carpellate flowers), inserted below disc. Filaments distinct, free, subulate, glabrous. Disc glabrous. Ovaries (1) 2-4 (5) (abortive in staminate flowers), sessile or stipulate; carpels (1) 2-4 (5), distinct or basally connate; ovules 2 per locule; style 1, sub- terminal, distinct, persistent or deciduous; stigmas coherent or connate, capitate or discoid. Follicles (1-3 per flower) distinct or basally connate, sessile or stipitate, ca. 5 mm diameter, valves 2, reddish, pellucid-punctate, glabrous to pubescent. Seeds subglobose or lenticular, 1 per follicle, ca. 4 mm diam., black or reddish, lustrous, minutely foveolate.

description: Annual or perennial herbs or low shrubs; taproots slender or thickened; stems pubescent, striate or smooth, angular to terete, green, but sometimes becoming yellow to purplish; leaves opposite, entire, sessile or short petiolate, the bases connate and sheathing the stem, pubescent; peduncles terete, striate to smooth, hollow, inflated or not, pubescent; heads cylindrical to hemispheric; phyllaries oblong to obovate, imbricate, graduated, the apices mostly rounded and erose and/or ciliated with a darker or discolored summit band at or near the apex; rays mostly present, persistent on the achenes, 1-to 3-lobed, white, lemon, yellow, orange, red, purple, or lilac, tubed or tubeless, pistillate and fertile, often plaited at the throat; ray style bifid, pubescent or glabrous, fili- form, acuminate; ray achenes compressed to 3-angled, glabrous or pubescent, smooth, striate or tuberculate; disk flowers tubular, mostly zygomorphic due to the longer length of one lobe, the tube basally dilated or of uniform width, the lobes acute, smooth, velvety, or densely velutinous within, smooth and mostly glabrous without; anthers loosely connate with acute, sterile, apical appendages, their bases truncate to free-sagittate; filaments ribbon-like, adnate to the thickened corolla base, folded in bud; style bifid, its branches filiform, acuminate and hairy at apex or else penicillately truncate; disk achenes compressed or angular, glabrous or pubescent, awned or awnless or simply bearing horns; chaff persistent on the receptacle, conduplicate, enclosing the achene; apex of chaff rounded to acute, erose, fimbriately lobed or entire cuspidate, bicolorous or not, hyaline to membranaceous, becoming searious; receptacle slightly concave to narrowly conical.

description: Shrubs, subshrubs, or rhizomatous herbs 0.5-2.0 m tall, stems strigose to densely pubescent when young, often becoming gla- brous, brown or gray with age. Leaves opposite or the upper alternate, blades 25-110 mm long, 8-50 mm wide, triplinerved, often the larger with naked basal veins, deltate to ovate, lance-ovate or lanceolate, pubescent adaxially with appressed, septate trichomes from a multicellular base, densely pubescent abaxially with numerous, white, appressed-septate trichomes giving leaf a velvety white appearance or hispid-pilose, subsessile glandular trichomes ("resin dots") absent, apex acute, base cordate to rounded or in uppermost cunéate, margin entire to shal- lowly serrate or dentate; petiole 4-30 mm long, hispid-pilose. Capitula terminal, 2-12 per paracladium, on sericeous peduncles 1.5- 21 cm long. Involucre hemispheric, phyllaries 12-35, in 2-3 (-4) subequal to graduated series, oblong or lanceloate to ovate, obtuse to subacute, puberulent to pilose. Ray florets 6-16, corolla golden-yellow, limb oval- oblong, 10-25 mm long, 3-10 mm wide, often with prominent abaxial veins that darken in color when dried. Disc florets 30- 70, corollas yellow to orange-yellow, nar- rowly campanulate; anthers dark brown, appendage lanceolate, light yellow; styles 5.8-7.0 mm long, tapered with a short appendage; paleae lance-ovate to lanceolate, 6-10 mm long, with an obtuse, acute or acuminate, often dark apex. Disk cypselae black or mottled black and brown, obovate, 3.0-4.8 mm long, sparsely pubescent or glabrous, epappose, or with a pappus of 2 awns and 3-12 deeply lacerated squamellae; awns slender, whitish, 2.5-4.2 mm long, squamellae 0.4-1.2 mm long. Ray ovaries trigonal, 2.5-3.7 mm long, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, pappus of 3 squamellae or absent. Chromosome number x='l (Turner et al., 1962; Schilling & Panero, 1990; Strother & Panero, 2001).

description: Highly branched thorny shrubs or small trees to ca. 10 m tall; branches green, glabrous to puberulent, ending in thorns; leaves alternate, scale-like to lanceolate, (1-) 1.5-2.2(-3) mm long, caducous; inflorescence lateral, umbelliform to racemose, 5-20 (or more)-flowered; flowers perfect, actino morphic; sepals 4, free, green; petals 4, free, white to creamy yellow to greenish; stamens 8, the filaments quadrangular in cross section, thickened at or slightly below the middle; anthers versatile, the dehiscence longitudinal; ovary superior, stipitate, 2-celled; ovules numerous, axile; fruit a globose berry with a thin rostellum; seeds 2-4, cochleate.
